units.la: INTellexi ex literis ad me datis Reverendi admodum Superattendentis Vestri, D. Weinheimeri, Vos Scholae Vestrae in melius emendationem moliri. Non possum non gratulari, optimisque consiliis optimos apprecari successus. Verissimum enim esse illud,
units.tr: I have learned from the letter sent to me by your most reverend Superintendent, Mr. Weinheimer, that you are working toward improving your School. I cannot but congratulate you, and wish you the best success for your best plans. For this is most certainly true:

units.la: FUNDAMENTUM REIPUBLICÆ EST RECTA JUVENTUTIS INSTITUTIO,
units.tr: THE FOUNDATION OF THE COMMONWEALTH IS THE RIGHT TRAINING OF YOUTH,

units.la: nemo dubitat: hoc autem dubitari potest, quænam recta illa sit institutio. Qua de materia quia nobis ab aliquot retrò annis multa cogitandi occasiones datæ fuerunt, repertaque nonnulla existimantur quæ Christianæ Juventuti, & Scholis, prodesse queant, ea nos in unum tandem collecta (sub OPERUM DIDACTICORUM nomine) publico exponere decrevimus. Summa erit, Optando optandum esse, ut omnis Christo sacrata Iuventus ea discat in terris, quorum scientia perseveret in cælos. Ita tamen eos ad æternitatem sapere adsuefaciendo, ut non desipiant hîc etiam. Id quod obtineri potest providendo, ut Scholarum discipuli, tanquam Vitæ candidatuli, nihil discant nisi ad Vitæ usum: adsuescendo de omnibus quæ in Vita obvenient judicare incorruptè, & de rebus rectè intelleintellectis loqui apposite, tandemque (quod maxime quaeritur) agenda agere prudenter: Vitae negotiis ita redditi, quisque suo loco & gradu, idonei, ad serviendum Deo & humanae societati quam maximo usu. Quod esse docendos docemus non verbis duntaxat, aut praeceptis, sed exemplis perpetuis, perpetuoque imitandi conatu, & actionibus vivis. Haec est Didacticorum nostrorum moliminum summa. Aut me omnia fallunt, aut haec erit vera via praestandi, ut Scholae sint quod audiunt, Ecclesiae & Reipublicae seminaria vera. Quae desideria ut obtineamus tandem, videamusque & florentem verè Ecclesiam, & tranquillam undique Rempublicam, fecit misericordia Dei!
units.tr: no one doubts this; but it may be doubted what that right training is. Since for some years now I have had many occasions to think about this matter, and since some things have been found which are thought able to benefit Christian youth and the schools, I have at last decided to gather them together and make them public under the name of Didactic Works. The summary will be this: that we should rightly wish that all youth dedicated to Christ may learn on earth those things whose knowledge will last into heaven; yet so that by training them to be wise for eternity, they do not act foolishly even here. This can be achieved by arranging that the pupils of the schools, as candidates for life, learn nothing except for the use of life: by accustoming them to judge impartially about all things that occur in life, to speak appropriately about things rightly understood, and finally (which is chiefly sought) to act prudently in what they must do; and so, having been made fit for the affairs of life, each in his own place and rank, to serve God and human society to the greatest benefit. That these things should be taught, we teach not by words alone or by precepts, but by constant examples, by a constant effort at imitation, and by living actions. This is the sum of our didactic undertakings. Unless I am altogether mistaken, this will be the true way of ensuring that the schools become what they are called, true seminaries of the Church and the Commonwealth. May the mercy of God grant that we at last obtain these desires, and see the Church truly flourishing and the Commonwealth tranquil on every side!

units.la: Ego interim, dum per hos ipsos dies purioris Latinitatis, & fluidioris styli, subsidiolum hoc, Latino-Latinum Lexicon, prelo exit, honoratissimum nomen Vestrum, Vrbisque & Scholae Vestrae, praefigere volui, ut quanti sapiens Vestrum consilium faciam publicè constet. Benè consulite affectum, Viri sapientes! quos unà cum Schola, Ecclesia, Requepublica Vestra, divinae commendo gratiae. Dabam Amsterdami 21. Julij, 1657.
units.tr: Meanwhile, while in these very days this little aid, the Latin-Latin Lexicon, goes to press for the sake of purer Latin and a more flowing style, I wished to place at its head your most honoured name, and that of your city and School, so that it may be publicly evident how highly I value your wise counsel. Take well the good will of one who wishes you well, wise men! I commend you, together with your School, Church and Commonwealth, to the grace of God. Given at Amsterdam, 21 July, 1657.

units.tr: Elegant formers of minds, of manners, and of the elegance of language, greetings!

units.la: {*}Visquis Latinæ linguæ amore Ianuam Linguarum novissimam, eâ diligentiâ qualem requisivimus, modoque illo quem ostendimus, pertransierit, eum nec circa Res adeò cæcum, nec ad Actiones prorsus inertem, nec in Sermone omnino elinguem, fore speramus. Quia tamen Deus Hominem undiqueversus amussitatum, elegantemque, fecit, subserviendum est hâc etiam parte Divino consilio, ut in humanitatis studio accuratioribus futuris; plenius etiam Rerum ad invicem rationes, Actionumque nostrarum formæ ac normæ, cum occultioribus Sermonum artificiis, commonstrentur, eôque ipso ad humanam & divinam sapientiam verius ac plenius intelligendam fores recludantur. Quo fine nos Atrium linguarum construximus: in quo eadem Rerum & Actionum, quasi omnium, historiola quam Ianua linguarum Verbis propriis simplicissimè enarraverat, sic iteratur, ut cum Rerum & Actionum artificia, tum & Sermonum Ornamenta, patescant melius. Vbi tametsi (Rerum & Actionum symbolicâ pertractatione, Sermonisque exornatione) diffundendi sese materia dabatur uberrima, diffundi tamen non libuit. Ideò primùm, quia fundamentalem Methodi legem (quæ Authores τὸ πᾶν facit, & ad illos viam explanari vult brevem & facilem) violare non libuit: neque Discentium obsistere aviditati, quæ in eosdem Authores (ritè sibi commendatos) proculdubio immitti, quam circumduci, mavolet. (Naturale est ad desiderii finem cum impetu ferri, ut interdum ipsa quoque media remora videantur.) Nec denique nostrum fuit omnia Authorum (Phrases, Adagia & c.) exhausta & huc congesta velle: sed sed gustum tantum dare verum, directorioque instruere vero, quo adjuti utiliter Authorum campos pervolitare, apicularumque instar Elegantiarum & Sapientiae flosculos ipsimet comportare, condocefiant. Maluimus igitur, & ex lege Methodi debuimus, Regularum adjungere (imo praejungere) Syntagma: quo reclusos ante se videntes Elegantiarum fontes, rivulos inde velut infinitos diducere queant, quibus idforet volupe.
units.tr: Whoever, out of love for the Latin tongue, has gone through this newest Gate of Languages with the diligence we required and in the manner we have shown, we hope will be neither blind to things, nor wholly idle in action, nor entirely tongue-tied in speech. Yet since God made man upright and graceful on every side, it is fitting that in this respect too we serve the divine plan, so that those who are more diligent in the study of humanity may also see more fully the relations of things to one another, and the forms and norms of our actions, together with the more hidden arts of speech, and so the doors may be opened to understand human and divine wisdom more truly and fully. To this end we have built the Atrium of Languages, in which the same little history of things and actions, which the Gate of Languages had narrated very simply in proper words, is repeated, so that both the arts of things and actions and the ornaments of speech may be displayed more clearly. Here, although abundant matter for expansion was offered (in the symbolic treatment of things and actions, and in the embellishment of speech), we did not wish to expand. First, because we did not wish to violate the fundamental law of the Method (which makes the authors the whole [τὸ πᾶν] and wants a short and easy road to them); nor to resist the eagerness of the learners, which would rather be sent straight into those authors (properly commended to them) than led round about. (It is natural to rush with force toward the end of one's desire, so that sometimes even the means seem to be obstacles.) Nor was it ever our purpose to want all the phrases, proverbs and so on of the authors exhausted and heaped together here; but only to give a taste and to furnish a true guide, by which, aided, they may learn to fly usefully over the fields of the authors and to gather for themselves, like bees, the little flowers of elegance and wisdom. We preferred therefore, and the law of the Method required, to add (indeed to put first) a Syntagma of rules, so that, seeing before them the springs of elegance opened, they may draw from them, as it were, countless little streams, by which the thing would be pleasant.

units.la: Ne tamen sibi permissi elegantiarum loco monstra forte pariant, detinendi etiamnum intra cancellos sunt: nempe ut non ad lubitum phrases, tropos, adagia, fingere sibi licere putent, sed loquendi formulis receptis, Authorum bonorum, conceptus mentis efferre consuescant. Quo fine illis praesens hoc paravimus subsidium, Latino-Latinum Lexicon: quod hucusque progressos discipulos minus Latina Latinioribus commutare, vere Latina vero Latinissimè etiam variare, doceat.
units.tr: Yet, lest the freedom allowed them should perhaps produce monsters in place of elegance, they must still be kept within bounds: namely, they must not think they may invent phrases, tropes and proverbs at their pleasure, but should accustom themselves to express the concepts of their minds in the accepted forms of speech of good authors. For this purpose we have prepared this present help for them, the Latin-Latin Lexicon, which teaches those who have progressed so far to exchange less Latin words for more Latin ones, and to vary what is truly Latin in the most Latin manner.

units.la: Latino-Latinum Lexicon ideo appellamus: quia quicquid rerum & conceptuum Ianuales discipuli Latine proprie, & Vocum nativo significatu, efferre jam didicerunt, hic pro themate stat: quomodo autem unumquodque horum efferendum sit Latinius, ad elegantioris styli formam, exemplis mox subjectis ostenditur. Quae pure Latina esse ut nequis dubitet, Authores allegamus antiquos, initialibus saltem nominum literis: sed quibus nulla additur allegatio, illa ex recentiorum periphrasibus, aut etiam ex Atrio nostro, desumta esse intelligi debet.
units.tr: We call it a Latin-Latin Lexicon because whatever things and concepts the pupils of the Gate have already learned to express in Latin properly, and in the native meaning of the words, stand here as the theme; how each of these is to be expressed more Latinly, in the form of a more elegant style, is shown in the examples set out below. So that no one may doubt that these are purely Latin, we cite ancient authors, at least by the initial letters of their names; but where no citation is added, those expressions should be understood to be taken from recent periphrases, or even from our Atrium.

units.la: Quae allegatorum Authorum no mina ut legere, simulque quorum phrases & formulas rectius imitari liceat attendere, consuescant Discipuli, libet hic initia illa Nominum integris commutare nominibus, eaque recensere Alphabeti serie: addito, quinam eorum Historici, Oratores, Poëtae, aut de his omnibus Censores, fuerint.
units.tr: So that the pupils may become accustomed to reading the names of the cited authors, and at the same time to noting whose phrases and formulas they may more correctly imitate, it pleases us here to replace those initial names with the full names, and to list them in alphabetical order, adding which of them were historians, orators, poets, or critics of all these.

units.la: Hæc de Lexici hujus structura. Vsus illius erit primùm ad tanto magis alliciendum ingenia ad suavitatum sermonis, & Eloquentiæ, amorem: intelligendumque Plinianum illud, Magna pars studiorum amœnitates quærimus. (Ubique nimirum naturæ humanæ palatum est delicatum, ubique varietatem & suavitates captat.) Deinde, ad comparandam sibi sic etiam facilius initialem (antequam in Authores veniatur) Orationis copiam, stylumque fluidum. Demum ad styli securitatem, dum se cum Authoribus loqui certum habebunt.
units.tr: So much for the structure of this Lexicon. Its use will be, first, to attract minds all the more to a love of the charm of speech and of eloquence, and to understand that saying of Pliny: "We seek the pleasures of study as the greater part of it." (Human taste, of course, is everywhere delicate, and everywhere it seeks variety and charm.) Next, to acquire more easily in this way, even before one comes to the authors, an initial stock of expression and a fluent style. Lastly, to gain security of style, since they will be sure that they are speaking with the authors.

units.la: Quibus autem exercitiis adhæc perpoliri debebunt Discipuli? Offerendum illis quidvis Latinum seu ex Ianuæ seu ex Atrii Textu, aut undecunque desumtum erit, cui illi Lexici hujus ductu novos induere, eosque decoros, tentabunt vultus. Idque tam diu, donec recte imitari, Authorumque allegatas phrases, vel adagia, proposito suo apte accommodare sciant: quæres attentionem, & continuatam aliquousque diligentiam, requiret. Quicquid enim agimus; magisterium relinquendum est praxi: quia solus usus facit artifices.
units.tr: But what exercises must the pupils also practise in order to be polished? Some Latin text, whether from the Gate or the Atrium or taken from anywhere, shall be offered to them, and under the guidance of this Lexicon they will attempt to give it new and seemly faces. They will do this until they know how to imitate correctly, and to fit to their own purpose the phrases or proverbs of the authors that are cited. This will require attention and continued diligence over some time. For whatever we do, teaching must give way to practice, because practice alone makes craftsmen.

units.la: Sicubi circa has iterum minutias defecisse videbitur diligentia nostra (agnosco autem, & fateor) condonetur quaso: defectus intervenire humanis rebus, humana sors est. Placeat cuique bono benignum Varronis judicium: Non omnes cœpisse (magna in sylva) feras, nemini unquam fraudi fuit.
units.tr: If, again, our diligence should seem to have failed in these small matters (I acknowledge and confess it), please pardon it: it is the human lot that failings intrude upon human affairs. Let Varro's kindly judgment please every good reader: that not everyone who has set out to hunt in a great forest has caught game, and that this has never been a fault for anyone.

units.la: Vtinam vero Eruditorum aliquis tale Latino-Latinum Lexicon omnibus numeris perfectum elaborare, eaque re Scholis melius ac per nos potuit gratificari, animum inducat! Vale.
units.tr: Would that some one of the learned would take it upon himself to produce such a Latin-Latin Lexicon, perfect in every respect, and so could oblige the schools better than we have been able to! Farewell.

units.la: A.
units.tr: A.

units.la: ABECEDE.] Augustino, & Coel. Rhod. dicitur. Sed purioribus Scriptoribus Alpha & Beta Inv. Vulgo Alphabetum. Primæ literæ, Vlp. Elementa puerorum, Cic. Prima literarum elementa. Quint. Elementariæ literæ, Iul. Cap.
units.tr: ABECEDE.] Used by Augustine and by Coelius Rhodiginus. But among purer writers, Inv. has Alpha and Beta. Commonly called the alphabet. First letters, Vlp. Children's elements, Cic. First elements of letters, Quint. Elementary letters, Iul. Cap.

units.la: Abecedarius v. Alphabetarius.
units.tr: Abecedarius see Alphabetarius.

units.la: A, AB, ABS.] Ab, etiam consonis præponitur, si non dura faciat collisionem, maximè verò Liquidis, L. R. Item S. I. & D. N. Ab regione, ab radice, Plin. Ab Septentrione, Var. Ab Syllâ, Ab Duce. Ab Domo, Ab Nobilitate Cic. Abs etiam Vocalibus & literæ R præjungitur. Absædibus Plaut. Abs Rege. Tacit.
units.tr: A, AB, ABS.] Ab is also placed before consonants, if it does not make a harsh collision, especially before the liquids L and R. Likewise before S, I, D and N. From the region, from the root, Plin. From the north, Var. From Sulla, from the leader. From the house, from nobility, Cic. Abs is also placed before vowels and before the letter R. From the houses, Plaut. From the king, Tacit.

units.la: Abacus in triclinio] Abacium. Mensa Pythagoræ. Organum Arithmeticum Cal. Rhod.
units.tr: Abacus in triclinio] Abacium. The table of Pythagoras. An arithmetical instrument, Cal. Rhod.

units.la: Abacus lusorius] Alveolus Cic. Alveus lusorius, Plin. Tabula latruncularia, Sen.
units.tr: Abacus lusorius] A gaming board (alveolus), Cic. A gaming trough (alveus lusorius), Plin. A draughts board (tabula latruncularia), Sen.

units.la: Abaculus] Numulus calculatorius, Calculi supputatorii, Hermol.
units.tr: Abaculus] A small counter, a reckoning counter, a set of counting pebbles, Hermol.

units.la: Abamita] Amita major, Fest.
units.tr: Abamita] A great aunt (amita major), Fest.

units.la: Abavus] Quartus Pater, Persius.
units.tr: Abavus] The fourth father, a great-great-grandfather, Persius.

units.la: Abbreviatura] Compendia vocum, Manil. Notæ literarum, Valer. Prob. Compendia scribendi, Recent.
units.tr: Abbreviatura] Abbreviations of words, Manil. Marks of letters, Valer. Prob. Methods of abbreviated writing, Recent.

units.la: Abbreviaturis scribere] Notis scribere, Var. Scribere per compendia, Solin. Litera mihi verbum est Manil. vide Scribere.
units.tr: Abbreviaturis scribere] To write with marks, Var. To write by abbreviations, Solin. "A letter is a word to me," Manil. See Scribere.

units.la: Abdere] Abscondere in latebras Plaut. Natura veritatem in profundo abstrusit. In tenebras retrusus. Occulere, removere ab oculis. Conjicere in latebram, se vel aliquid Cic. Recondere se in aliquem locum Quintil.
units.tr: Abdere] To hide away in lurking places, Plaut. Nature has concealed the truth in its depths. To thrust back into darkness. To hide, to remove from sight. To throw oneself or something into a hiding place, Cic. To retreat into some place, Quintil.

units.la: Abdicare se] Deponere imperium. Exuere. Renunciare magistratui. Abire magistratu, Cic. Ejurare imperium, Tac. vide Deponere.
units.tr: Abdicare se] To lay down power. To strip off. To renounce office to the magistrate. To leave office, Cic. To abjure power, Tac. See Deponere.

units.la: Abdite] Clanculum Ter. Latebrosè, Clandestinò Plaut. In angulis otium Philosophi consumunt, Furtim: In sinu gaudere Cic. Angulatim, Diomed. & Sidon. Furtivè, Vlp. Arcanò, Caf. Clanculò, Celatim. Secretim. Amm. Per occultum. Tac. Celatè, Amm.
units.tr: Abdite] Secretly, Ter. In a hidden manner, privately, Plaut. Philosophers spend their leisure in corners; furtively, to rejoice in one's bosom, Cic. Corner by corner, Diomed. and Sidon. Stealthily, Vlp. Secretly, Caf. Privately, covertly, in secret, Amm. In concealment, Tac. Hiddenly, Amm.

units.la: Abditus, v. Arcanus.
units.tr: Abditus, see Arcanus.

units.la: Abducere à] Deterrere ab officio. Detorquere, Cic. Subducere pugnæ militem, Virg. Avertere, Cic.
units.tr: Abducere à] To turn someone aside from duty. To divert, Cic. To withdraw a soldier from battle, Virg. To turn away, Cic.

units.la: Abduci] Auferri alienis consiliis. Abripi æstu ingenii. Persuasum est ei. Prolabi cupiditate. Induci promissis, Cic. Capi specie. Deliniri voluptate, Quint. Provehi spe, Liv.
units.tr: Abduci] To be carried away by other people's counsels. To be swept away by the heat of one's mind. He is persuaded. To slip away through desire. To be led on by promises, Cic. To be captured by appearance. To be softened by pleasure, Quint. To be carried away by hope, Liv.

units.la: Aberrare] Deviare, Macrob. In falsum jacere tela, Tac. In ventum effundere vires, Virg. Fefellit eum. Deerravit à patre puer. Non est assecutus. Non expressit exemplar. Præter scopum jacit. Decollavit spes, Plaut. Declinare de statu suo, Cic. Deflectere de via. Exorbitare, Aug.
units.tr: Aberrare] To deviate, Macrob. To throw weapons wide of the mark, Tac. To spend strength on the wind, Virg. He missed him. The boy strayed from his father. He did not attain it. He did not copy the model. He shoots beside the mark. His hope has failed, Plaut. To depart from one's condition, Cic. To turn aside from the way. To wander off course, Aug.

units.la: Abesse] Quid eum quæras, qui fuit? Plaut. Defuit bello. Unum jam & alterum diem desideratur. Extra est. Solitudo est ab oratoribus in foro, Cic. Ne musca quidem: scilicet intus, est, Suet. Amici nulli erant, Gell.
units.tr: Abesse] Why do you seek him who has gone? Plaut. He was absent from the war. One day and another are now missed. He is away. It is a relief from the orators in the forum, Cic. Not even a fly: of course, he is within, Suet. He had no friends, Gell.

units.la: Abhinc] A modò, Apul. vid. Exinde.
units.tr: Abhinc] From now, Apul. See Exinde.

units.la: Abhorrere] Exsecrari. Detestari tanquam auspicium malum. Respuere aliquid, Cic. Aversari, Liv. Odium me cepit alicujus, Ter. Fastidire, nauseare aliquid, Cic. Odi profanum vulgus & arceo, Horat.
units.tr: Abhorrere] To curse. To detest as an ill omen. To reject something, Cic. To shrink from, Liv. A hatred of someone has seized me, Ter. To loathe, to feel nausea at something, Cic. I hate the profane crowd and keep it away, Horat.

units.la: Abi] Apage à me, & te à me, Plaut. Aufer te hinc. Concede hinc, Ter. Abi tu tacitus, tuam viam. Ultrò istum à me. Facesse hinc. Fugin' hinc ab oculis? Foras lumbrice. Quin abis quò dignus es, Plaut. Ultra Sauromatas fuge, Iuve. Abi pastum corvos, Hor. Exesto. Fest. Non hinc vos propere amolimini? Pacuv. Abi Morboniam, Suet.
units.tr: Abi] Away from me, and you away from me, Plaut. Get yourself out of here. Withdraw from here, Ter. Go, you silent one, on your own way. Away with that fellow from me. Clear off from here. Are you running out of sight? Out, earthworm. Why not go where you deserve, Plaut. Flee beyond the Sauromatians, Juv. Go and feed the crows, Hor. Get out. Fest. Will you not quickly move yourselves from here? Pacuv. Go to Morbonia, Suet.

units.la: Abjectus] Contemptus, contemptissimus, Jacet. Jacens homo. Jacet in silentio. Despicatissimus, Cic. Despectissimus, Suet. Projectus, Tacit. Inhonorus, Plin. Frustra habitus, Tacit. Jocus, absolutè. Jocum me putat esse Mœcha turpis. Catul. Sterquilinio, fimo, abjectior, Eraf.
units.tr: Abjectus] Despised, most despised, lying low. A man lying low. He lies in silence. Most contemptible, Cic. Most despised, Suet. Cast down, Tacit. Without honour, Plin. Held in vain, Tacit. A jest, absolutely. The filthy adulteress thinks I am a joke, Catul. More abject than dung or manure, Erasm.

units.la: Abigere] Repellere aliquid. Depellere famem. Propellere periculum. Fugare hostes, Cic. Propulsare hostem, Cæf. Si quis non defendit injuriam neque propulsat à suis, cùm potest, injustè facit, Cic. Pellere metum, Idem. Protelare, Fest.
units.tr: Abigere] To drive off something. To drive away hunger. To ward off danger. To put enemies to flight, Cic. To repel an enemy, Caes. If anyone does not defend another from injury, nor ward it off from his own people when he can, he acts unjustly, Cic. To drive out fear, Idem. To put off, Fest.

units.la: Abjicere] Abjicere onus : voluntatem discendi : cogitationem de. Projicere inhumatum aliquem, Cic. Projicere arma, Cæs.
units.tr: Abjicere] To cast off a burden; to abandon the will to learn; to put aside a thought about. To cast out an unburied man, Cic. To throw down weapons, Caes.

units.la: Abire] Facessere ab aliquo. Discedere. Abscedere. Discessionem facere, Cic. Digredi. Avolare. Idem. Tergum ostendere, Val. Max. Occipitium alicui ostendere, Varro. Auferre se, Plaut. Relinquere comites, Ovid. Recedere. Decedere, Plaut.
units.tr: Abire] To take oneself off from someone. To depart. To go away. To make a departure, Cic. To go off. To fly away, Idem. To show one's back, Val. Max. To show the back of the head to someone, Varro. To carry oneself off, Plaut. To leave one's companions, Ovid. To withdraw. To go away, Plaut.

units.la: Abitio] Abitus ; Ter. Discessus ab Urbe. Abscessus solis. Recessus à rebus pestiferis. Discessio, Cic. Secessus avium, Pacuv. Decessus Nili, Plin.
units.tr: Abitio] A going away; Ter. departure from the city. Setting of the sun. Withdrawal from pestilent matters. A departure, Cic. A flight of birds, Pacuv. The retreat of the Nile, Plin.

units.la: Abjudicare aliquid ab aliquo.] Abdicere aliquid ab aliquo, Pomp. IC. Abdicare regno, Pacuv. Regno expellere, Id. Abnego aliquem comitem, Horat. Præteritus suffragiis. Repulsam tulit à populo, Cic.
units.tr: Abjudicare aliquid ab aliquo.] To disown something from someone, Pomp. IC. To disinherit from a kingdom, Pacuv. To drive out from a kingdom, Id. To refuse a companion, Horat. Passed over in the votes. He received a rejection from the people, Cic.

units.la: Abjugare] Abjungere juvencos, Virg. Disjungere boves ab opere, Col. Solvere juga tauris, Virg. Dejugare, Plaut.
units.tr: Abjugare] To unyoke calves, Virg. To separate oxen from the work, Col. To loose the yoke from bulls, Virg. To unyoke, Plaut.

units.la: Abjurare] vide Abnegare.
units.tr: Abjurare] See Abnegare.

units.la: Ablactare] Depellere agnum à matre, Var. Depellere lacte, Suet. Initiare puerum Eduliæ, Poticæ, Cubæ, Varro. (N. Gentilium erant figmenta, Dea Cuba, Edulia, Potica, quibus curam esse puerorum eduliis assuescendorum, somniabant) Disjungo à mammâ agnos, Var. Subduco lac agnis, Virg. Removere infantem, Plin.
units.tr: Ablactare] To drive a lamb from its mother, Var. To wean from milk, Suet. To initiate a boy into Edulia, Potica and Cuba, Varro. (Note: these were pagan figments; the goddess Cuba, Edulia and Potica, who were supposed to have charge of accustoming children to food.) I separate lambs from the ewe, Var. I withdraw milk from the lambs, Virg. To remove the infant, Plin.

units.la: Ablactatus, scil. infans] Exuber Iof. Scal Fest. Isid. Lacte depulsus. Depulsi à mamma porci. Non jam lactentes, sed delici, Var. Abrumus agnus, Palmer. Taubm.
units.tr: Ablactatus, scil. infans] Weaned: Iof. Scal. Fest. Isid. Separated from milk. Pigs separated from the teat. No longer sucklings but dainty ones, Var. A weaned lamb, Palmer. Taubm.

units.la: Ablegare aliquem] Ablegare foras, Plaut. Amovere, Tacit. Mandare in ultimas terras. Amandare hominem à, in. Cic. Hunc Argum si potes amolire. Nescio uti eum amittam à me. Hic utcunque est extrudendus aliquô, Eras.
units.tr: Ablegare aliquem] To send someone away, to send out, Plaut. To remove, Tacit. To send to the furthest lands. To send a man away from or into a place, Cic. If you can drive off this Argus. I do not know how to get him away from me. This fellow must somehow be thrust out somewhere, Erasm.

units.la: Abligurire] Obligurire, Ter. Obsorbent fores quicquid venit intra pessulos, Plaut. Urunt cultæ capellæ, Virg. Absorbere aliquid, Plin. Sorbere, Ovid.
units.tr: Abligurire] To lick up, Ter. The doors swallow up whatever comes within the bolts, Plaut. The tended goats browse, Virg. To swallow up something, Plin. To sip, Ovid.

units.la: Abluere] Eluere sordes. Luere scelus sanguine, Cic. Abdere undis, Virg. Elavi in mari :/: lavi me, Plaut.
units.tr: Abluere] To wash off filth. To expiate a crime with blood, Cic. To hide under the waves, Virg. I washed in the sea: I have washed myself, Plaut.

units.la: Abnegare] scil. depositum Plin. Fraudare creditum, Fest. Abjurare, si quid creditum est, Plaut. Fallere depositum, Ovid. Inficiari, Absol. Fest. Cic. Inficias ire, Ter. Gell. Denegare crimen, Cic. Pernegare. Diffiteri, Id. Si authoritatem postea defugeris, ego pendeam, Plaut.
units.tr: Abnegare] Namely a deposit, Plin. To defraud of a loan, Fest. To abjure, if anything was lent, Plaut. To betray a deposit, Ovid. To deny, absolutely, Fest. Cic. To deny, Ter. Gell. To deny a charge, Cic. To deny flatly. To disown, Id. If you afterwards escape from the agreement, I shall be the one to pay, Plaut.

units.la: Abnuere] Assensum denegare. Renuere, Cic. Renutare, Lucr. Oculo renuente negare, Ovid. Renutu respondere, Plin. Iun. Superciliis criminis renuentes, Cic. Assensus suos sustinere, cohibere. Non audio, nec Homerum audio. Repugno. Non assentior tibi hoc, vel de hoc, Cic.
units.tr: Abnuere] To refuse assent. To refuse, Cic. To shake the head in refusal, Lucr. To deny with a nodding eye, Ovid. To answer by a shake of the head, Plin. Iun. Refusing with a raised eyebrow of accusation, Cic. To hold back and restrain one's assent. I do not listen, nor do I listen to Homer. I oppose. I do not agree with you on this, or about this, Cic.

units.la: Abolere :/: ad nihilum redigere.] Tollere è rerum natura. Exstinguere memoriam alicujus. Afferre perniciem, exitium alicui, Cic. Perdere, Sepelire, Id. Facere perniciem. Dare exitio, Tacit. Perditum ire, Ter. Obliterare memoriam, Liv. Ad vanum & irritum redigere, Id. Disperdere, Amm. Obsolefacere, Arnob. vid. Perdere. Amittere.
units.tr: Abolere :/: ad nihilum redigere.] To take away from the nature of things. To extinguish the memory of someone. To bring ruin, destruction upon someone, Cic. To destroy, to bury, Id. To bring about ruin. To give over to destruction, Tacit. To go to perdition, Ter. To blot out the memory, Liv. To reduce to vanity and nothing, Id. To destroy utterly, Amm. To make obsolete, Arnob. See Perdere. Amittere.

units.la: Abominandus] Aspernabilis, Gell. Odium terrae, Plaut. Exsecratus, Plin. Putidus, Cic. Sceleratus campus, Liv. Scelerata terra (in qua scelus commissum) Virg.
units.tr: Abominandus] Detestable, Gell. The hatred of the earth, Plaut. Accursed, Plin. Foul, Cic. A wicked plain, Liv. A wicked land (in which a crime was committed), Virg.

units.la: Abominari] Respuere malum. Exsecrari aliquem. Detestari aliquem tanquam auspicium malum. Cic. Aversari aliquem, Cic.
units.tr: Abominari] To reject as evil. To curse someone. To detest someone as an ill omen, Cic. To shrink from someone, Cic.

units.la: Aboriri] Abortire, & i, Plin. Abortum facere, pati, Plin. Iun. Abortare, Var. Elidere partum Celf. Ejicere partum : Vlp.
units.tr: Aboriri] To miscarry, and to be born prematurely, Plin. To cause or suffer an abortion, Plin. Iun. To abort, Var. To destroy the birth, Celsus. To expel the birth, Ulp.

units.la: Abortivum] Abortivus foetus, Suet. Partus ejectus, ejectitius, Plin. Abditivus Fest. & Scal. Abortum, Fest. Semiformis pullus, Col.
units.tr: Abortivum] A miscarried offspring, Suet. A birth cast out or thrown out, Plin. A thing dropped, Fest. and Scal. An abortion, Fest. A half-formed chick, Col.

units.la: Abortus.] Abortio, Cic. Abortus fit circa conceptionem. Abortus circa pariendi tempus, Non. Blapsigonia dicitur in apibus. Plin. v. Embryum.
units.tr: Abortus.] A miscarriage, Cic. An abortion happens around conception. An abortion around the time of giving birth, Non. The bees' blapsigonia is so called, Plin. See Embryum.

units.la: Abradere] vid. Deradere.
units.tr: Abradere] See Deradere.

units.la: Abrogare] Rescindere conventa. Dictaturam aequare solo. Antiquare legem. Refigere, Tollere legem. Obrogare legi, Cic. Irrita facio facta alicujus, Id. Infectum aliquid quid facio, Plaut. Infectum reddere, Hor. Rescindo quod sit factum legibus, Ter. Rescindo leges, Lucr. Obliterare legem. Hæc lex abiit in desuetudinem. Nunquam tui beneficii memoria intermorietur. Eraf. Demoliri jus, Plaut.
units.tr: Abrogare] To annul agreements. To level the dictatorship with the ground. To abolish a law. To unfix, to remove a law. To repeal a law, Cic. I make void the deeds of someone, Id. I make undone something that was done, Plaut. To render undone, Hor. I annul what has been done by the laws, Ter. I annul laws, Lucr. To obliterate a law. This law has fallen into disuse. The memory of your kindness will never die out, Erasm. To demolish a right, Plaut.

units.la: Abruptus, v. Interruptus.
units.tr: Abruptus, see Interruptus.

units.la: Abscindere] Præsecare cultello favum, Varr. Resecare membra. Amputare ramos. Præcidere ancoras. Exscindere. Resecare. Præruncare linguam, Cic. Truncare, Plin.
units.tr: Abscindere] To cut the honeycomb off with a knife, Varr. To cut off limbs. To lop off branches. To cut through anchor cables. To cut out. To cut back. To cut out the tongue, Cic. To truncate, Plin.

units.la: Abscissum] Abscissio, Amm. Fructum avulsum. Abruptum.
units.tr: Abscissum] Abscission, Amm. A fruit plucked off. Broken off.

units.la: Absconditus] Reconditus. Seclusus à communi luce Cic. In præcordiis penitus nutriunt invidiam. Apul. In sinu gaudium, Cicer. Abstrusus. Remotus à sensibus. Occulta res, Cic.
units.tr: Absconditus] Hidden away. Shut off from common light, Cic. They nurse envy deep in their hearts, Apul. Joy in the bosom, Cicer. Concealed. Removed from the senses. A hidden matter, Cic.

units.la: Absens] Absentaneus, disjunctus, Cic. Dissitus, Apul.
units.tr: Absens] Absent, separated, Cic. Remote, Apul.

units.la: Absit] Avertat Deus, Vopisc. Dii melius, Sen. Quod Dii prohibeant. Atque hoc quidem detestabile omen avertat Jupiter, Cic. Ne Dii siverint. Melius ominare, Plaut. Sed dira avertite Divi, Sil. Dii averruncassint amentiam Varr. Te Æsculapi, atque Te Salus, ne quid sit hujus, oro, Ter. Absit, longeque absit. Hostibus eveniat. Eraf.
units.tr: Absit] May God avert it, Vopisc. Rather, may the gods prevent it, Sen. What the gods forbid. And may Jupiter avert this dreadful omen, Cic. May the gods not permit it. Rather prophesy good, Plaut. But avert these dreadful things, O gods, Sil. The gods have turned away madness, Varr. Aesculapius, and you, Salus, I pray that nothing of this comes to pass, Ter. Let it be far off, far away. Let it fall upon the enemies. Eraf.

units.la: Absit jactantia dicto] Absit verbo invidia, Livi. Nec verò hoc arroganter à me dictum existimari velim, Cic. Ambitione relegatâ dicere possum. Hor. Præfiscini (hoc nunc dixerim) Plaut. Deus habeat hoc decus, Plato. Liceat mihi de me loquenti hoc absque invidiâ dicere. Quod accipi quasi arroganter dictum, nolim. Dicam non formidans jactationis suspicionem. Defendendi non gloriandi causâ id loquor.
units.tr: Absit jactantia dicto] Let there be no envy in the word, Livi. Nor would I wish this to be thought to have been said by me arrogantly, Cic. Setting ambition aside, I can say, Hor. With fascination averted (I say this now), Plaut. May God keep this honour, Plato. May I be allowed, speaking of myself, to say this without envy. I would not like what is said to be taken as arrogant. I will speak without fear of the suspicion of boasting. I say this in defence, not in self-glorification.

units.la: Absolvere (1) vinculis liberare] vid. Solvere.
units.tr: Absolvere (1) to free from chains] see Solvere.

units.la: (2) Reum justum pronunciare] Adserere. Vindicare, Cic. Noxâ & nexu solvere, Eraf.
units.tr: (2) To pronounce the accused just] To assert. To vindicate, Cic. To release from liability and bond, Eraf.

units.la: (3) Absolvere negotium.]Ad exitum, ad summum perducere. Fastigium operi imponere. Cursum conficere. Emereri, Cic. Accessit operi manus extrema, Id. Ad culmen perducere, Liv. Consummare opus, Plin. Imponere summam manum, Sen. Profligare bellum, perpetrare, Tacit. Incipere multò est, quàm impetrare, facilius, Plaut. Ad umbilicum deducere ; Non recedere sine corollario. Fabulæ extremum actum addere. Circulum complere. Supremam manum addere. Colophonem addere. Apicem imponere, Eraf. Depugnatum est. Perdoluit. Deserbuit. Defunctus est. Desiit artem. Depuduit. Desultavit canticum, Suet. v. Defungi aliquâ re.
units.tr: (3) Absolvere negotium.] To bring to the end, to the highest point. To set the crown upon the work. To complete the course. To earn, Cic. The final hand was put to the work, Id. To bring to the summit, Liv. To finish the work, Plin. To put on the finishing touch, Sen. To carry a war through to the end, to accomplish it, Tacit. To begin is far more than to accomplish; the easier task, Plaut. To lead down to the navel. Not to withdraw without a corollary. To add the last act to the play. To complete the circle. To add the final hand. To add the colophon. To place the apex, Eraf. It has been fought out. It has been grieved through. It has been ended. He has finished. He has ceased the art. He has been ashamed. He has danced the song through to the end, Suet. See Defungi aliqua re.

units.la: Non absolvere solenniter cœpta] Cadere in cursu.
units.tr: Not to bring solemnly begun things to completion] To fall in the course.

units.la: Absolutio] Tabula absolutoria, Suet. Formula indulgentior, quæ plus habet æquitatis & minus rigidi & stricti juris, Bud. Salutaris litera, Cic. (scil. A. quia illa est prima in voce absolvi.)
units.tr: Absolutio] An acquittal certificate, Suet. A more indulgent formula, which has more equity and less rigid and strict law, Bud. A saving letter, Cic. (that is, A, because it is the first letter in the word absolvi.)

units.la: Absolutus in judicio.] Noxâ & nexu solutus, Eraf.
units.tr: Acquitted in court.] Released from liability and bond, Eraf.

units.la: Absque] Citra fastidium, Plin. Scorsum animâ. Orbus pedum, Lucr. Viduata loca pruinis. expers consilii, Cic. v. Citra, intrà.
units.tr: Absque] Without tedium, Plin. Lifeless, without spirit. Bereft of feet, Lucr. Places bereft of frosts. Lacking counsel, Cic. see Citra, intrà.

units.la: Abstemius] Invinius, Apul. Prandium caninum, quod caret temeto, Plaut.
units.tr: Abstemius] Without wine, Apul. A dog's dinner, which lacks wine, Plaut.

units.la: Abstergere] Defricare aliquid pumice, Plin. Extergere spongiâ. Detergere fletus, Claud. Siccare lumina lanâ impresså, Proper. Tergere vasa, Cic. Tergeo vasa, Iuv. Circumfricare, Cato.
units.tr: Abstergere] To rub clean with pumice, Plin. To wipe off with a sponge. To wipe away tears, Claud. To dry the eyes with a pressed woollen cloth, Propert. To wipe vessels, Cic. I wipe vessels, Juv. To rub round about, Cato.

units.la: Abstterrere aliquem à vel ab] Deterrere aliquem ab aliquâ re, Cic. Proterrere aliquem hinc, Plaut. Ter. Armis, viris, periculoque mortis repellere, fugare, avertere, Cic.
units.tr: Abstterrere aliquem à vel ab] To deter someone from a thing, Cic. To drive someone away from here, Plaut. Ter. To repel, put to flight, or turn away by arms, men, and the danger of death, Cic.

units.la: Abstinere se ab aliqua re] Reprimere se. Abstinentem esse, Cic. Abstineo quo minùs, Suet. Temperare sibi. Adducere habenas. Tenere se (scil. ab aliqua re). Imperare cupiditati. Comprimere animam. Sedare arrogantiam. Moderari animo. Parcere dolori. Abstinere manus, oculos, animum à conjugibus, liberis, auro, Cic. Domitas habere libidines. Coërcere omnes cupiditates, Cic. Nullo dedecore se se abstinent. Id.
units.tr: Abstinere se ab aliqua re] To restrain oneself. To be abstinent, Cic. I refrain from doing, Suet. To govern oneself. To draw in the reins. To hold oneself (namely from some thing). To master one's desire. To check one's spirit. To curb arrogance. To moderate one's mind. To spare one's grief. To keep hands, eyes, and mind away from wives, children, and gold, Cic. To keep one's lusts tamed. To restrain all desires, Cic. They abstain from no disgrace, Id.

units.la: Abstinentia] Innocentia, Affectio animi quæ nemini noceat, Cic. Integritas & continentia, Id. Moderatio, Id. Est virtus placitis abstinuisse bonis, Ovid.
units.tr: Abstinentia] Innocence, a disposition of mind that harms no one, Cic. Integrity and self-restraint, Id. Moderation, Id. Virtue lies in having abstained from pleasing goods, Ovid.

units.la: Abstinens] Temperans, Cic. Qui se in libidine continet. Continens linguæ. Fuerunt Romani hac quondam abstinentiâ, Cic.
units.tr: Abstinens] Temperate, Cic. Who restrains himself from lust. Restraining his tongue. The Romans were once men of this abstinence, Cic.

units.la: Abstrahere] v. Retrahere.
units.tr: Abstrahere] see Retrahere.

units.la: Absumere]Depascitur ignis. Depascitur febris artus, Virg. Exedere, Ter. Depasci, consumere, comedere patrimonium. Expromere industriam, Cic. Abuti caseum, Cato. Præconsumere vires, Ovid. Fortunas suas abligurierunt. Exhaurire, Decoquere. Eluere, Plaut.
units.tr: Absumere] The fire feeds upon. The fever feeds upon the limbs, Virg. To eat up, Ter. To feed on, consume, devour one's patrimony. To express diligence, Cic. To misuse cheese, Cato. To use up one's strength beforehand, Ovid. They have licked up their fortunes. To exhaust, to boil down. To wash out, Plaut.

units.la: Absurda agere] Mutus maledixerit surdo. Ab asino lanam petere. Aquam in mari quærere. Aquilam volare doces. Arcem in cloaca facere. Asino dare ossa, cani paleas. Asinum tondere. Athenas noctuas (scil. portare) Bovi saccharum; Psittaco fœnum. Bove venari leporem. Cœcus de coloribus, & surdus de tenore. Camelo transmissło, culex in cribro deprehensus hæsit. Mulgere hircum. Conglomerare inconglomerabilia. Ebur atramento candefacere. Fimo suffitum facere. Fontes ipsi sitiunt. Imberbis senes doces. Imbrem in cribrum ingerere. In aere piscari. In mari venari. Lutum luto purgare. In aqua sitire. In frigidum furnum panem injicere. Luscinia deest cantio. Mercurius infans.
units.tr: Absurda agere] A dumb man has cursed a deaf one. To ask an ass for wool. To seek water in the sea. You teach an eagle to fly. To build a citadel in a sewer. To give bones to an ass and chaff to a dog. To shear an ass. Athens to owls (that is, to carry). Sugar to an ox; hay to a parrot. To hunt a hare with an ox. Blind in colours and deaf in pitch. When the camel has passed through, the gnat sticks fast, caught in the sieve. To milk a he-goat. To heap together things that cannot be heaped. To make ivory white with ink. To make a fumigation with dung. Springs themselves thirst. You teach beardless old men. To pour rain into a sieve. To fish in the air. To hunt in the sea. To cleanse mud with mud. To thirst in water. To throw bread into a cold oven. The nightingale lacks song. Mercury an infant.

units.la: Absurdè] Ab re consulere, Plaut. Ab orbita, Varr. Longius à vera ratione ferri, Lucr. Non cohæret, Ter.
units.tr: Absurdè] To consult away from the matter, Plaut. Off the track, Varr. To be carried further from true reason, Lucr. It does not cohere, Ter.

units.la: Absurdus] Perabsurdum quod dicitis. Auribus, animis absurdum. Ineptum, Cic. Alienum, Cæs. Nihil ad rem, Plaut. Nihil ad fides, vel ad chordam. Er.
units.tr: Absurdus] Something very absurd that you say. Absurd to the ears and minds. Inept, Cic. Foreign, Caes. Nothing to the point, Plaut. Nothing to do with the strings or the chord, Er.

units.la: Abundè] v. Effusè. Abundare, v. Copia.
units.tr: Abundè] see Effusè. To abound, see Copia.

units.la: Abusus] Malus rei usus. Abusio, Sipont. Abusus rerum res tollit.
units.tr: Abusus] A bad use of a thing. Abuse, Sipont. The abuse of things destroys the thing.

units.la: Abuti] Malè operam locare, Plaut. Abuti, & conterere operam, Ter. Luxuriosè & insolenter uti, Bud. Depravare naturam, Cic. Malè collocare horas, Mart. Spargere tempus, Sen. Lacerare diem, Plaut. Frustra habere, Id.
units.tr: Abuti] To spend effort badly, Plaut. To use up and waste effort, Ter. To use luxuriously and insolently, Bud. To corrupt nature, Cic. To spend the hours badly, Mart. To squander time, Sen. To tear the day apart, Plaut. To have in vain, Id.

units.la: Abyssus] Eluvies, Cic. Voragines Id. Barathrum, Virg. Sorbet in abruptum, Id.
units.tr: Abyssus] A flood, Cic. Whirlpools, Id. An abyss, Virg. It swallows into the chasm, Id.

units.la: Academia] Scholarum apex. Emporium Sapientiæ.
units.tr: Academia] The summit of the schools. The marketplace of wisdom.

units.la: Accedere] Coaccedere, Plaut. Accessionem facere. Adire propius, Ter. Descendere ad. Aggredi ad, Cic.
units.tr: Accedere] To come up together with, Plaut. To make an approach. To come nearer, Ter. To descend to. To attack at, Cic.

units.la: Accendere] Flammas admoto fomite excitare. Festinare ignes. Moliri ignes, Virg. Ignem facere. Immittere, subjicere ignem fornacibus, Vlp. Succendere aliquid, Liv.
units.tr: Accendere] To kindle flames by applying tinder. To hasten fires. To set fires in motion, Virg. To make a fire. To put, to set fire under furnaces, Vlp. To kindle something, Liv.

units.la: Accendi] Ignitionem pati. Excipere flammam. Exardescere, Cic. Inardescere, Horat. Corripi flamma, Ovid. Concipere flammam, Cæf. Degustant ligna ignes, Lucr.
units.tr: Accendi] To suffer ignition. To receive the flame. To blaze up, Cic. To burn fiercely, Horat. To be seized by flame, Ovid. To catch fire, Caes. The logs taste the fires, Lucr.

units.la: Accentus] Tenor, Tonus, Quint. Vocalior sonus, Gell. Sonus pronuntiandi. Intervallum sonorum & vocis in loquendo. Contentio vocis, Cic. Vocis moderamenta. Voculationes, Gell. Impressiones vocum. Percussiones numerorum, Cic.
units.tr: Accentus] Tenor, tone, Quint. A fuller sound, Gell. The sound of pronunciation. The interval between sounds and the voice in speaking. Tension of the voice, Cic. Modulations of the voice. Vocal inflections, Gell. Impressions of the voices. Beats of rhythm, Cic.

units.la: Accentus, nota distinctionum in scriptione] Apex, Quint. Interpunctio, Interductus, Cic.
units.tr: Accentus, a mark of distinctions in writing] Apex, Quint. Punctuation, interpunction, Cic.

units.la: Acceptus] Plausibilis, Sen. Probabilis specie & odore rosa, Plin. Probabilis in vita re, Spart. Favorabilis, Plin. Venustus, Cic. Arbor gratiosa umbra. Est illi gratia, Plin. Omnia in illo sunt ad gratiam, Liv. minimè aspernandus. vide Gratus.
units.tr: Acceptus] Pleasing, Sen. Agreeable in appearance and in the scent of roses, Plin. Approved in life, Spart. Favourable, Plin. Charming, Cic. A tree pleasant for its shade. He has grace. Everything in him is for favour, Liv. By no means to be scorned. See Gratus.

units.la: Accidens] Attributio loci, Cic. Qualitates, Celf. v. Casus.
units.tr: Accidens] An attribute of place, Cic. Qualities. Celsus. See Casus.

units.la: Accidens essentiam non variat.] Pumilio, licet in monte, non est magnus. Pygmæus in collo Gigantis magnus sibi videtur.
units.tr: Accidens does not alter the essence.] A dwarf, though on a mountain, is not big. A pygmy on the neck of a giant seems big to himself.

units.la: Accidere, præter spem evenire] Insperato mihi cecidit, evenit, contigit, Cic. Usu venit, Ter. Quod si successerit alienari mente, Plaut. Incidunt tempora. Cum incidunt causæ, Cic. Incidit casus, aliquid mali civitati, Id.
units.tr: Accidere, to happen beyond hope] It befell me unexpectedly, happened, came to pass, Cic. It comes about in practice, Ter. If it should happen that someone is alienated in mind, Plaut. Occasions fall out. When causes arise, Cic. A misfortune befell the state, Id.

units.la: Accinere] Accantare alicui, Stat. Succinere, Var. Admodulari, Claud. Jungere vocem fidibus, Quint. Carmina nervis aptare, Prop. Digiti cum voce loquuntur, Tib. Adsonat Echo, Ovid.
units.tr: Accinere] To sing to someone, Stat. To sing in response, Var. To sing along, Claud. To join the voice to the strings, Quint. To fit songs to the strings, Propert. Fingers speak with the voice, Tib. Echo resounds, Ovid.

units.la: Accipere] Percipere fructus terræ, Cic. Sumere in manum. Assumere, Id. Adscisicere sibi aliquem comitem, Id.
units.tr: Accipere] To gather the fruits of the earth, Cic. To take into the hand. To assume, Id. To take someone as a companion, Id.

units.la: Accitare] v. Vocare.
units.tr: Accitare] see Vocare.

units.la: Acclamare] Succlamatum est à militibus. Clamoribus excipere, Cic. Favere linguis, Horat. Ore, Virg.
units.tr: Acclamare] The soldiers shouted out. To receive with shouts, Cic. To favour with the tongue, Horat. With the mouth, Virg.

units.la: Acclamatio] Applausus. Admurmuratio secunda, Cic. Plausus. Plausus multiplex à toto concessu alicui datus. Clamor secundus, Virg.
units.tr: Acclamatio] Applause. A second murmur of approval, Cic. Clapping. Repeated applause given to someone by the whole assembly. A second shout, Virg.

units.la: Acclinare] Demittere se ad aurem alicujus. Propendere. Incumbere, Cic. Inclinata fortuna, Caes. Inclinat se sol, Liv. Proclinari, Col. Vergere ad imum, Horat. Impellere aliquem eo ut incumbat, Plaut. Conquiniscere, Id.
units.tr: Acclinare] To lower oneself to someone's ear. To lean forward. To lean upon, Cic. Fortune inclined, Caes. The sun inclines itself, Liv. To bend over, Col. To slope down to the bottom, Horat. To drive someone to lean over, Plaut. To crouch down, Id.

units.la: Acclivis] Mollis ascensus, Liv. Declivis locus, collis, Caes. Proclivum solum, Var. Devexus molliter collis ad meridiem, Col. Inclinatus, Pallad. Scalaris forma, Vitruv.
units.tr: Acclivis] A gentle ascent, Liv. A sloping place or hill, Caes. Sloping ground, Var. A hill gently sloping towards the south, Col. Inclined, Pallad. Of stair-like form, Vitruv.

units.la: Accommodare] Attemperare. Moderari vires suas ad inferiorum debilitatem, Sen. Comparare se. Conformare animum. Aptare virtutibus. Aptum reddere. Velificari alicui, Cic.
units.tr: Accommodare] To adapt. To moderate one's strength to the weakness of inferiors, Sen. To make oneself agreeable. To conform one's mind. To fit to virtues. To make fit. To sail with the wind for someone, Cic.

units.la: Accommodare se omnibus] Scenæ servire. Popularem auram captare, Hor.
units.tr: Accommodare se omnibus] To serve the stage. To catch the popular breeze, Hor.

units.la: Accrescere] Accessionem recipere. Adaugescere, Lucr. Augescere, Cic. Creverunt opes animique hostium, Id. Grandescit aliquid hilari adauctu, Luc.
units.tr: Accrescere] To receive an addition. To grow larger, Lucr. To increase, Cic. The enemy's power and spirits grew, Id. Something grows larger with a cheerful increase, Luc.

units.la: Accumbere] Discumbere mensis, Gell. (N. Accumbere, de uno & multis; discumbere de multis tantùm dicitur.) Recumbo conviva, Horat. Considere mensis, Virg.
units.tr: Accumbere] To recline at table, Gell. (Note: accumbere is said of one person and of many; discumbere is said only of many.) To recline as a dinner guest, Hor. To sit down at table, Virg.

units.la: Accumulare] Coacervare pecuniam, cadavera. Congerere omnia in unum, Redigere in unum, Cic. Acervare aliquid, Plin. Contrahere in acervum, Caes. Cumulare benefacta, Bona, mala, ad satietatem usque, Plaut. Constipaverunt se sub vallo hostes, Caes. Conglobare, Liv. Agglomerare, Virg. Coadunare, Plin. Iun. Conglomerat in me fortuna omnia mala, Enn.
units.tr: Accumulare] To heap up money or corpses. To gather everything into one, to bring back into one, Cic. To pile up something, Plin. To draw into a heap, Caes. To heap up good deeds, goods, or evils to the point of satiety, Plaut. The enemy crowded together beneath the rampart, Caes. To form into a ball, Liv. To pile together, Virg. To add together, Plin. Iun. Fortune heaps all evils upon me, Enn.

units.la: Accurare] Advigilare rei. Incumbere in aliquid, Cic. Enixam operam navare, Amm. Ad perpendiculum exigere, Id.
units.tr: Accurare] To attend closely to a matter. To apply oneself to something, Cic. To exert great effort, Amm. To bring to the plumb line, Id.

units.la: Accuratè] Exquisitè. Conquisitè, Scitè. Politè, Cic. Ad amussim, Varr. Ad lineam. Ad libellam. Ex amussi, Plaut. Scrupulosè referre. Ex tempore, quàm à cura, præstantior, Suet. Pensim atque enucleatè, Cell. Usque ad exemplum, Quint. Ad unguem, Hor. Ad nummum convenit ratio. Exactè. Elaboratè. Divinitùs dicta. Presfiùs agamus, Er. Nunc cominus agamus. Quæ verò accuratè cogitatéque scripsisset, Cic.
units.tr: Accuratè] Exquisitely. Carefully, skilfully, cleverly. Elegantly, Cic. To the exact measure, Varr. By the line. By the level. By the rule, Plaut. To report scrupulously. More excellently done extempore than with care, Suet. Weighed and clearly explained, Gell. Exactly after the model, Quint. To the fingernail, Hor. The account tallies to the last penny. Exactly. With elaborate care. Divinely spoken. Let us press on more closely, Erasm. Let us now come to close quarters. But what he had written with careful and thoughtful attention, Cic.

units.la: Accuratissimè rem expendere] Ad vivum resecare. Sagaciter pervestigare, Cic.
units.tr: Accuratissimè rem expendere] To cut to the quick. To investigate keenly, Cic.

units.la: Accuratus] Exquisitus. Exquisitissimus. Elaboratus. Limatus, Cic. Excuratus, Plaut. Quæsitissimi honores, Tacit. Amussitatus, Plaut. Exactus, Pompo. Lucernam olet. Adag.
units.tr: Accuratus] Sought out with care. Most carefully sought. Elaborated. Polished, Cic. Careful, Plaut. Most sought-after honours, Tacit. Ruled exactly, Plaut. Exact, Pompo. He smells of the lamp. Adag.

units.la: Accusare] Reum agere, facere, Citare. Vocare in crimen. Inferre alicui crimen. Arcessere judicio. Arcessere capitis. Deferre. Litem inferre, Cic. Deferre impietatis, Tacit. Postulare reum repetundarum, Suet. Insimulare proditionis. In jus vocare, ducere, Trahere. Dicam scribere, Er. Ad tres viros deferam tuum nomen, Plaut. Incusat senis parsimoniam. Causatur Tutorum perfidiam, Id. Culpam in aliquem conferre, Derivare, Conjicere, Eraf.
units.tr: Accusare] To bring a suit against, to prosecute. To cite, to summon. To lay a charge. To call to account for a crime. To bring a charge against someone. To summon to a trial. To bring to a capital trial. To denounce. To bring an action, Cic. To denounce for impiety, Tacit. To demand the prosecution of a defendant for extortion, Suet. To accuse of treason. To summon to court, to drag before it. I will draw up an accusation, Erasm. I will lay your name before the three men, Plaut. He accuses the old man of stinginess. He alleges the treachery of the guardians, Id. To lay blame on someone, to shift it, to throw it, to impute it, Erasm.

units.la: Accusari] Reum esse ab aliquo. Lege de vi teneri. Nomen meum delatum, Cic. Dies mihi dicta est, Plaut. Pendere vel pependisse, Suet. Quot reorum nomina in tabella suspendebantur. Postulatus est repetundarum. Teneri læsæ Reipublicæ, Cic.
units.tr: Accusari] To be a defendant at the suit of someone. To be held under the law on violence. My name has been laid before the court, Cic. A day has been fixed for me, Plaut. To hang, or to have hung, Suet. How many names of defendants were hung up on the tablet. He has been charged with extortion. To be held guilty of treason against the state, Cic.

units.la: Accusatio] Delatio, Cic. Tac. Insimulatio criminis. Criminatio, Cic.
units.tr: Accusatio] Denunciation, Cic., Tac. Charging with a crime. Accusation, Cic.

units.la: Accusatio sæpe frivola] Si accusare satis, nemo innocens.
units.tr: Accusatio sæpe frivola] If one accuses enough, no one is innocent.

units.la: Accusator] Inquisitor. Sector. Quadruplator, Cic. Persecutor, Ovid. Delator, Suet. Accusatrix, Plaut. Arcessitor, Ammian.
units.tr: Accusator] Investigator. Hunter after. Informer, Cic. Pursuer, Ovid. Informer, Suet. Woman accuser, Plaut. Summoner, Ammian.

units.la: Accusatus] Nocens. Citatus. Is qui causam dicit. Ille unde petitur, Cic. Qui arguitur. Reus ambitus, Id. Defensor. De cujus re disceptatur. Item Advocatio properfonis, Id. Vid. Reus.
units.tr: Accusatus] Guilty. Summoned. The one who pleads his case. The one against whom an action is brought, Cic. The one who is charged. A defendant on a charge of bribery, Id. Defender. The one whose cause is being disputed. Likewise the advocacy of persons, Id. See Reus.

units.la: Acer & Acris] Vehemens, Cic. Argutus sapor, Plin. Vehementi sapore. Id. Acetum acerrimum, Celf. Aceto acrius.
units.tr: Acer & Acris] Vehement, Cic. Sharp flavour, Plin. With a vehement taste. Id. Very sharp vinegar, Celsus. Sharper than vinegar.

units.la: Acredo] Acrimonia. Acritudo succi. Vitr. Acumen saporis, Plin. Durus sapor vini, Virg.
units.tr: Acredo] Sharpness. Sharpness of juice, Vitr. Keenness of flavour, Plin. Harsh taste of wine, Virg.

units.la: Acerbus, aspero sapore] Adstrictus gustus. Vis adstrictoria ria foliorum, Plin. Austerum vinum, Col. Sapore linguam morsicans. Immitior uvâ acerbâ, Eras.
units.tr: Acerbus, aspero sapore] Astringent taste. Astringent power of leaves, Plin. Austere wine, Col. Biting the tongue with its flavour. Harsher than an unripe grape, Erasm.

units.la: Acere, Acescere] Acorem concipere. Acore vitiari, Col. Fermentescit terra nivibus diutinis, Plin. Exacere. Exacescere, Col. Coacescere, Cic. inacescere, Apul. Peracescere, Plaut. Fermentari, Plin.
units.tr: Acere, Acescere] To turn sour. To be spoiled by sourness, Col. The ground turns sour from long-lasting snows, Plin. To make sour. To grow very sour, Col. To turn sour, Cic. To grow sour, Apul. To become quite sour, Plaut. To ferment, Plin.

units.la: Acervare] Acervos construere, Cic. Adaggerare, Id. vide Accumulare.
units.tr: Acervare] To build heaps, Cic. To heap up, Id. See Accumulare.

units.la: Acervatim] Globatim, Amm. Conglobatim, Plin. Uno grege, Curt. Glomeratim, Macrob. Congestim, Fartim, Apul.
units.tr: Acervatim] In clusters, Amm. In balls, Plin. All in one crowd, Curt. In heaps, Macrob. Heaped together, Apul.

units.la: Acervus] Turba voluminum : Chorus virtutum, Cic. Strues lignorum, Liv. Strues malorum. Nav. apud Jerv. Silva rerum. Quint. Agmen aquarum, Virg. Glomeramen. Lucr. Torus graminis, Apul. Quis fons? Quis torrens verborum? Eras.
units.tr: Acervus] A crowd of books. A chorus of virtues, Cic. A pile of firewood, Liv. A heap of evils, Nav. in Jerv. A forest of things, Quint. A flock of waters, Virg. A clump, Lucr. A bed of grass, Apul. What a fountain! What a torrent of words! Erasm.

units.la: Acidula] Vini vicarii suppromus, Plaut.
units.tr: Acidula] The steward's deputy for the wine, Plaut.

units.la: Acies, acuta extremitas] Mucro gladii, dentium, Cic. Vertex acutissimus, Col. Fastigium tenue mucronis, Lucr. Acumen rostri, Plin. Cuspis hastæ, Ovid.
units.tr: Acies, acuta extremitas] The point of a sword or of teeth, Cic. A very sharp tip, Col. The fine tip of a point, Lucr. The point of a beak, Plin. The point of a spear, Ovid.

units.la: Acinaces] Acinacis. Curvus culter. Sen. Harpe. Gladius Persicus, apud Xenoph. Copis. Gladius Turcicâ formâ.
units.tr: Acinaces] A curved knife, Sen. A dagger. A Persian sword, in Xenoph. A sword of Turkish shape.

units.la: Aquiescere] vide. Contentum esse.
units.tr: Aquiescere] See. To be content.

units.la: Aquirere] Assequi honorem. Consequi famam. Nancisci imperium, Cic. Parere libertatem. Invenire pecuniam bono modo. Plin. Parare. Comparare. Quærere rem, Cic. Compotem fieri, Liv. Potiri, Virg. Adipisci gloriam, Plaut. Conquirere opes quæstu Plin. Obtinere urbem armis, Liv. Ad eam laudem aspirare non possunt, Cic.
units.tr: Aquirere] To win an office. To attain fame, Cic. To seize power, Cic. To obtain liberty. To find money by honest means, Plin. To procure, to acquire. To seek wealth, Cic. To come into possession of, Liv. To take possession of, Virg. To win glory, Plaut. To gather wealth by gain, Plin. To take a city by force of arms, Liv. They cannot aspire to that praise, Cic.

units.la: Acquisitum Vid. Partum.
units.tr: Acquisitum: See Partum.

units.la: Acredula] Philomela Virg. Luscinia, Var. Aëdon. Virg. Attis, vel Atthis, Mart. Luscioniola, Plaut.
units.tr: Acredula] The nightingale, Virg. Luscinia, Var. Aëdon, Virg. Attis or Atthis, Mart. Little nightingale, Plaut.

units.la: Acta publica] Tabulæ publicæ, Cic. Acta forensia. Ovid. Libri actorum, Iuv. Acta. Tacit. Instrumentum imperii, Suet. Publicum, Var. In publico Ardeæ scriptum exstat. Tabularium, Cic. Tablinum, Plin. Protocollum, Sipont.
units.tr: Acta publica] Public records, Cic. Court proceedings, Ovid. Books of proceedings, Juv. Acts, Tacit. The instrument of government, Suet. Public, Var. The writing is extant in the public place at Ardea. An archive, Cic. The tablinum, Plin. A protocol, Sipont.

units.la: Actio, agentis motus] Facinus, Cic. Functio operis. Curatio, Administratio rerum, Id. Molimen Liv. vid. Accusatio.
units.tr: Actio, agentis motus] A deed, Cic. The performance of a task. The management and administration of affairs, Id. An enterprise, Liv. See Accusatio.

units.la: Actio in distans nulla] Absens hæres non erit.
units.tr: Actio in distans nulla] No action at a distance: an absent heir will not be an heir.

units.la: Actio non fit sine repafsione] Percutiens idem & percussus.
units.tr: Actio non fit sine repassione] No action happens without reaction: the one who strikes is also the one struck.

units.la: Activus vir] Briarei manus in exsequendo. vid. Industrius.
units.tr: Activus vir] Hands of Briareus in carrying things out. See Industrius.

units.la: Actor] Qui vocat aliquem in jus, Cic. Qui ad judicium provocavit. Accusator, Petitor, Id. Petitrix, Paul. IC. Inquisitor, Cic.
units.tr: Actor] One who summons someone to court, Cic. One who has appealed to judgment. An accuser, a plaintiff, Cic. A female plaintiff, Paul. IC. An investigator, Cic.

units.la: Actor, qui & effector] v. Factor.
units.tr: Actor, qui & effector] See Factor.

units.la: Actum est] Deploratus est, Liv. Tabula evanuit. Occidi. Nullus sum, Ter. Ecce autem perii, Plaut. Nulla est cistella, neque ego sum usquam perdita, perdidit me. Id. Occisa hæc res est. Id. Occisissimus sum omnium qui vivunt, Id. Sepulta est fama, Ovid. Occidit spes omnis, Horat.
units.tr: Actum est] He has been given up for lost, Liv. The tablet has vanished. I am undone. I am nothing, Ter. But look, I am ruined, Plaut. There is no box, and I am utterly lost; she has ruined me, Id. The matter is lost. I am the most undone of all who live, Id. Fame is buried, Ovid. All hope has perished, Hor.

units.la: Acuere] Exacuere furcas. Virg. Præacuere furculum. Cat. Aspirare saxo pugionem, ossibus sagittas, Tacit. Atterere cote gladium, Plin. Cotes trahunt, excitant aciem Id. Samiare, Non. Attrito cogunt gladios juvenescere saxo, Stat. Aciem temperare. Aciem trahere. Plin.
units.tr: Acuere] To sharpen forks, Virg. To sharpen a little fork, Cat. To whet a dagger on stone, and arrows on bone, Tacit. To rub a sword on a whetstone, Plin. Whetstones draw out and sharpen the edge, Id. To polish, Non. They force swords to grow young again by rubbing on stone, Stat. To temper the edge. To draw out the edge, Plin.

units.la: Aculeus] Spiculum apum, Virg. Aculeolus, Mart.
units.tr: Aculeus] The sting of bees, Virg. A little sting, Mart.

units.la: Acuminare] Cuspidare. Fastigiare, Plin. Ducere ferrum, procudendo in tenuia & acuta mucronum fastigia, Lucr. Cacuminare, Ovid.
units.tr: Acuminare] To point, to furnish with a point. To taper to a point, Plin. To draw out iron, forging it into the thin and sharp points of swords, Lucr. To sharpen to a peak, Ovid.

units.la: Acupingere] Acu variare, Mart. Intexere gemmas vestibus. Distinguere vestem segmentis, Plin. Lentum filis immittere aurum, Ovid.
units.tr: Acupingere] To embroider with a needle, Mart. To set gems into garments. To decorate a garment with bands, Plin. To weave gold into cloth with threads, Ovid.

units.la: Acupictus] Acu variatus, segmentatus, Iuv. Pictura-tus, Stat. Variatus figuris, Luc. Intertextus pluribus notis, Quint.
units.tr: Acupictus] Embroidered, decorated with bands, Juv. Painted, Stat. Varied with figures, Luc. Interwoven with many marks, Quint.

units.la: Acute videre] Lynceis oculis contemplari.
units.tr: Acute videre] To look closely with lynx eyes.

units.la: Acutus] Præacutus, Cæs. Cultellatus, Plin. Cultratus. Id. Samiatus, Vopisc. Dentatus, Cic. Chrysippo acutior.
units.tr: Acutus] Sharpened beforehand, Caes. Knife-shaped, Plin. Like a knife, Id. Scimitar-shaped, Vopisc. Toothed, Cic. Sharper than Chrysippus.

units.la: Adagium] Tritum vetustate proverbium. v. Proverbium.
units.tr: Adagium] A proverb worn with age. See Proverbium.

units.la: Adamare, amare incipere] Incidere in amorem. Concipere, suscipere amorem, Cic. Adjungere, appellere animum ad, Ter. Adjicere oculos cupiditatis ad, Cic. Capi amore, Amplexare, Id. Amascere, Isid.
units.tr: Adamare, amare incipere] To fall into love. To conceive, to take up love, Cic. To join, to turn the mind to, Ter. To cast longing eyes upon, Cic. To be captured by love, to embrace, Id. To begin to love, Isid.

units.la: Adaptare] Vide Accommodare.
units.tr: Adaptare] See Accommodare.

units.la: Adaquare] Dare potionem alicui, Quintil. Potionatus medicamento amatorio, Suet. Do potatum bubus medicamentum, Col. Salivare ægrum pecus medicamine. Potandum medicamentum præbere, Colum.
units.tr: Adaquare] To give someone a drink, Quint. Given a love potion, Suet. I give a drugged drink to oxen, Col. To drench a sick animal with medicine. To offer a medicine to be drunk, Col.

units.la: Addere] Adhibere ad, Cic. Coaddere, Cato. Superaddere alicui, superdare, Cel. Coadjicere, subjicere, Col. Superadjicere, Pallad. Adstruere alicui, Plin. Accudere tres minas, Plaut. Subnectere, Quint. Subjungere alicui, Id. Subtexere alicui, Id. Affodere cespitem fundo, Plin. Augere, Plaut. Adaugere, Appingere, Cic. Adjicere cibo, Celf. Adjicere ad, Cic. Cumulare, Id.
units.tr: Addere] To apply to, Cic. To add together, Cato. To add over and above to someone, Cels. To throw in beneath, to subjoin, Col. To add over and above, Pallad. To bestow upon someone, Plin. To add three minae, Plaut. To tack on, Quint. To subjoin to someone, Id. To weave in for someone, Id. To dig a turf into the bottom, Plin. To increase, Plaut. To add to, to append, Cic. To add to food, Cels. To add to, Cic. To heap up, Id.

units.la: Addiscere] Consequi scientiam, Cic. Condiscere, Plin. Mandare memoriæ. Lud. Viv.
units.tr: Addiscere] To attain knowledge, Cic. To learn thoroughly, Plin. To commit to memory. Lud. Viv.

units.la: Additamentum] Appendix. Corollarium. Coauctio, Accessio, Cic. Accessorium, Iust. Parergum, Plin. Mantissa, Lucil. Superpondium, Apul. Sequela, Vlp. Auctarium, Id. Mantissa, Scal.
units.tr: Additamentum] Appendix. Corollary. Addition, accession, Cic. Accessory, Iust. Parergon, Plin. Mantissa, Lucil. An extra weight, Apul. Sequel, Vlp. Supplement, Id. Mantissa, Scal.

units.la: Additicius] Adventitia res, Cic. Insitus civis. Insitdef, Id. Insititius hæres. Sen. Extrinsecus additus & consarcinatus, Gell. Affictitius, Var. Adscitus lepos, Corn. Adjicialis cœna, Plin. Impositivum nomen, Cic.
units.tr: Additicius] An adventitious thing, Cic. An adopted citizen. Adopted, Id. An adoptive heir, Sen. Added from outside and patched on, Gell. Fictitious, Var. Borrowed wit, Corn. An added dinner, Plin. An imposed name, Cic.

units.la: Adducere](1) Obducere exercitum ad oppidum, Plaut.
units.tr: Adducere] (1) To lead an army up against a town, Plaut.

units.la: (2) Citare authores]Laudare aliquem authorem certissimum, religiosissimum, Cic. Recitare alicujus testimonium. Proferre legem. Producere authorem, testes, Id. Allegare, Plaut.
units.tr: (2) Citare authores] To praise an author as most certain and most trustworthy, Cic. To recite someone's testimony. To bring forward a law. To produce an author or witnesses, Id. To allege, Plaut.

units.la: Adeo tam valde]Adeóne hospes es? adeò ut. Tam palàm. Cic. In tantum, ut, Plin. Æquè, Suet. Adæquè, Plaut. Tam mane, vesperi, Ter. Tam amat, Plaut. Tanta mira intus vidi (i.e. tam, vel tot mira) Id. Tantopere dissentiunt, Cic. Opere tanto. Tantum quantum quis (potes) fuge, Plaut. Usquead ut. Eatenus ut, Cic. Ita animus stupet, Ter. Tamne, Fest.
units.tr: So very much]Are you really such a stranger? Yes, so much. So openly. Cic. To such a degree that, Plin. Equally, Suet. Equally, Plaut. So early in the morning, in the evening, Ter. He loves so much, Plaut. I have seen so many wonders within (that is, so or so many marvels), Id. They disagree so greatly, Cic. With such great effort. Flee as far as you can, Plaut. Up to the point that. To that extent, so that, Cic. So the mind is astonished, Ter. Surely not? Fest.

units.la: Adesse] Præsto esse, Cic. Præs-sum. Præs-est, Plaut. Adeeram præsens. In re præsenti esse, Id. Coràm adesse. Præsentem adesse. Interesse sermoni, Cic. Adesse ad, Cat.
units.tr: To be present] To be at hand, Cic. I am in front, he is in front, Plaut. I would be present in person. To be present in the matter, Id. To be present in person. To be present before someone. To take part in a conversation, Cic. To be present at, Cat.

units.la: Adest, de quo loquimur] Lupus in fabula, Ter. Etiamsi lupi meminisses.
units.tr: He of whom we speak is present] The wolf in the fable, Ter. Even if you had been remembering the wolf.

units.la: Adhærere] Adhærescunt homines ad aliquid. Cic. Auri coma stirpibus adhærescit,Apul. Adcorporari, Solin. Affigi, Cic. Picis in morem ad digitos lentescit. (scil.terra) Virg. Mordicus tenere. Cic.
units.tr: To cling to] Men cling to something, Cic. Gold-coloured hair clings to the stalks, Apul. To grow into the body, Solin. To be fastened, Cic. It sticks to the fingers like pitch (sc. the earth), Virg. To hold on with the teeth, Cic.

units.la: Adhortari] Admonere aliquem. Admonere ad aliquid faciendum, Cic. Admonere alicujus rei. Liv. Commonere aliquem officium suum,Plaut. Commonefacere publicæ utilitatis aliquem,Gell. Hortari aliquem aliquid,ad aliquid de aliquâ re. Exhortari aliquem ad virtutis studium, Cic. Plin. Monere aliquem aliquid,Ter. Solea objurgare rubra. Perf. Commonefacere monimentis bubulis, Plaut. Aurem vellere,Virg. Aurem pervellere, Sen.
units.tr: To exhort] To remind someone. To remind someone to do something, Cic. To remind someone of a matter, Liv. To remind someone of his duty, Plaut. To remind someone of the public good, Gell. To urge someone to something, or to something concerning some matter. To exhort someone to the pursuit of virtue, Cic. Plin. To warn someone of something, Ter. To scold with a red sandal, Pers. To remind with cowhide memoranda, Plaut. To tug at the ear, Virg. To pull the ear hard, Sen.

units.la: Adhortatio] v. Admonitio, huc transfer.
units.tr: Exhortation] See Admonition; transfer it here.

units.la: Adhortator] Monitor, Ter. Cic. Admonitor. Hortator, Cic. Intimator, Iul. Cap.
units.tr: Exhorter] A monitor, Ter. Cic. An admonisher. An encourager, Cic. A spur, Iul. Cap.

units.la: Adhuc] Etiamnum ? Etiam nunc ? Nunc etiam, Cic.
units.tr: Still] Even now? Even yet? Now also, Cic.

units.la: Adhuc, de futuro] Amplius, Ter. Etiam. Etiam denuo. Id.
units.tr: Still, of the future] Further, Ter. Also. Also again. Id.

units.la: Adhuc ne?] Adhuccine ?
units.tr: Still not?] Even till now?

units.la: Adigere. v. Inducere.
units.tr: To drive. See To induce.

units.la: Adimere alicui aliquid]Subtrahere.Præcidere libertatem, Cic. Auferre. Plin. Demere, Liv. v. Demere.
units.tr: To take something away from someone] To subtract. To cut off liberty, Cic. To carry off, Plin. To remove, Liv. See Remove.

units.la: Adire] Aditare. v. Accedere.
units.tr: To go to] To frequent. See To approach.

units.la: Aditum parare] Struere gradum ad altiora.
units.tr: To prepare access] To build steps to higher things.

units.la: Aditus]Aggressio. Janua patefacta ad,Cic. Accessus,Ovid.
units.tr: Approach] An attack. An open door to, Cic. Access, Ovid.

units.la: Aditus difficilis] Non cuivis homini contingit adire Corinthum, Horat.
units.tr: Difficult access] It is not given to every man to go to Corinth, Horat.

units.la: Aditus patet] Aditus facilis ad. Aditus lati ducunt. Noctes atque dies patet atri janua Ditis. Virg.
units.tr: The approach is open] Easy access to. Broad roads lead there. Night and day the gate of dark Dis stands open, Virg.

units.la: Adjudicare alicui causam] Secundum aliquem judicium facere.Addicere alicui bona,fundum,Cic.Addicere totam familiam,Plaut. Pecuniam ex edicto meo auferendi illi fuit,Cic.
units.tr: To adjudge a case to someone] To give judgement in someone's favour. To award goods and a farm to someone, Cic. To assign the whole household to someone, Plaut. He had the right to take the money from him under my edict, Cic.

units.la: Adjumentum] v. Auxilium.
units.tr: Help] See Aid.

units.la: Adjungere aliquid alicui] Adjungi ad authoritatem senatus. Adjungere provincias ad imperium. Aggregare aliquid ad. Aggregare se ad amicitiam alicujus. Congregare in eundem numerum aliquem. Adsciscere sibi socium, Cic. Jungere se alicui, Virg. Jungere se ad aliquem, Aliquid ad aliud,
units.tr: To join something to someone] To be joined to the authority of the senate. To join provinces to the empire. To add something to. To attach oneself to someone's friendship. To group someone into the same number. To take someone as a companion, Cic. To join oneself to someone, Virg. To join oneself to someone; to add one thing to another,

units.la: liud, Cic. Associare aliquid, Stat. Claud. Adjugare, Pacuv. Agglomerant se. Addunt se socios, Virg. Attexere aliquid ad aliquid, Cic. Accorporare bona aliena suis, Ammian.
units.tr: ...else, Cic. To associate something, Stat. Claud. To yoke together, Pacuv. They gather together. They add themselves as allies, Virg. To interweave one thing with another, Cic. To incorporate other men's goods into one's own, Ammian.

units.la: Adjurare] Jurejurando aliquem obstringere, Cæs. Adigere jusjurandum, & ad jusjurandum, Liv. Objurare, Fest.
units.tr: To adjure] To bind someone by an oath, Caes. To make someone swear an oath, and to an oath, Liv. To swear against, Fest.

units.la: Adjuvare] Adesse alicui auxilio. vide Juvare.
units.tr: To help] To be present to someone with aid. See Juvare.

units.la: Admirari] Stupescere ob aliquid. v. Mirari.
units.tr: To admire] To be amazed at something. See Mirari.

units.la: Admirator omnium] Omnem lapidem nitidum adorat.
units.tr: An admirer of everything] He worships every polished stone.

units.la: Admiscere] Allinere sordes sententiis, Cic. Intermiscere, Liv.
units.tr: To mix in] To smear filth on sentences, Cic. To intermix, Liv.

units.la: Admittere] Dare alicui admissionem, Plin. Haud gravatim facit sui copiam. Er. vid. Copiam sui facere.
units.tr: To admit] To give someone admission, Plin. He grants access to himself without reluctance, Er. See Copiam sui facere.

units.la: Admonere v. Adhortari.
units.tr: To admonish: see Adhortari.

units.la: Admonitio] Admonitus, ûs. Monitus, Adhortatio. Cohortatio. Compellatio. Admonitum. Monitio. Hortatio. Hortatus, ûs, Cic. Commonitio, Quint. Hortamen, Liv. Monimentum, Plaut.
units.tr: Admonition] A warning. Admonition, exhortation, encouragement, appeal. Exhortation, Cic. Reminder, Quint. Encouragement, Liv. Reminder, memorial, Plaut.

units.la: Adnasci] Membra adnata animalibus. Increscit verruca, Plin. Supercrescit, Quintil. Vid. Copiam sui facere.
units.tr: To grow on] Limbs grown onto animals. A wart grows on, Plin. It grows further, Quintil. See Copiam sui facere.

units.la: Adniti v. Eniti.
units.tr: To strive: see Eniti.

units.la: Adolescens] Juvenculus, Cat. Juvenis imberbis, Hor. Puber filius, Cic. Visticeps, Gell. Tiro, Hor. Ephebus, Ter. v. Ephebus.
units.tr: Young man] A young lad, Cat. A beardless youth, Hor. A grown son, Cic. A young man with a shaven head, Gell. A recruit, Hor. A youth in training, Ter. See Ephebus.

units.la: Adolescere] Pubescere, Ulp. Ad plenitudinem crescere, Plin. Justam maturitatem capere, Col. Excedere ex ephebis, Ter. Manum ferulæ subducere, Juv. Paulatim gradus ætatis adultæ scandere. Summum alescendi cacumen tangere, Lucr. Jam excessit mihi ætas ex magisterio tuo, Plaut. Tempus adest cum meo more mihi vivendum, Ter.
units.tr: To grow up] To reach puberty, Ulp. To grow to full size, Plin. To attain proper maturity, Col. To pass out of boyhood, Ter. To withdraw one's hand from the ferule, Juv. To climb gradually the steps of adult age. To reach the highest peak of growing, Lucr. My age has now passed out of your tutelage, Plaut. The time has come when I must live in my own way, Ter.

units.la: Adoptare aliquem] Arrogare eum qui sui juris est, Gell. Assumere in nomen aliquem, Plin. Jun. Parentelâ suâ dignum putare, Jul. Cap.
units.tr: To adopt someone] To adrogate one who is his own master, Gell. To take someone into one's name, Plin. Jun. To think someone worthy of one's kin, Jul. Cap.

units.la: Adoptio] Adoptatio. Arrogatio, Gell.
units.tr: Adoption] Adoptation. Arrogation, Gell.

units.la: Adorare] Aris honores imponere, Virg. v. Supplicare.
units.tr: To worship] To place honours on the altars, Virg. See Supplicare.

units.la: Adscribere] Appingere aliquid scripto, Cic. Allinere, Hor.
units.tr: To write in addition] To add something in writing, Cic. To smear on, Hor.

units.la: Adstare] Assistere, Ovid. Ter.
units.tr: To stand by] To assist, Ovid. Ter.

units.la: Advehere aliquid] Advectare copiam rei frumentariæ, Tacit. Tacit. Supportare frumentum alicui, Caj. Commeatus sub-vehebatur, Liv. Subvectare virgas rure, Plaut. Ad nos pervehitur, Plin. Importare longe fructus, Var.
units.tr: To bring something] To convey a supply of corn, Tacit. Tacit. To bring grain to someone, Caj. Supplies were brought up, Liv. To carry branches up from the countryside, Plaut. It is brought to us, Plin. To import fruit from afar, Var.

units.la: Advena] Adventitium genus. Adventor, Plaut. vid.Peregrinus. Item Hospes.
units.tr: Stranger] A foreign kind. An incomer, Plaut. See Foreigner. Likewise, Guest.

units.la: Advenire] v. Venire.
units.tr: To arrive: see Venire.

units.la: Adventus] Accessus. Accessio, Appulsus, Cic. Quid tibi huc ventio est ? Plaut.
units.tr: Arrival] Approach. Approach, landing, Cic. Why have you come here? Plaut.

units.la: Adversari] Contraire alicujus sententiæ, Tacit. Reclamare. Admurmurare. Refragari. Obtrectare, Cic. Stare contrà, Mart. Tendere contrà, Ter. Obstrigillare, Var. Obvertere cornua alicui, Plaut. Apul. v. Obsistere.
units.tr: To oppose] To be contrary to someone's opinion, Tacit. To protest. To murmur against. To gainsay. To disparage, Cic. To stand against, Mart. To strive against, Ter. To oppose with objections, Var. To turn one's horns against someone, Plaut. Apul. See Obsistere.

units.la: Adversarius] Obtrectator, Æmulus, Cic. Adversator, Apul. Contradictor, Vlp. Obstrigillator, Var. Refragator, Ascon.
units.tr: Adversary] A disparager, a rival, Cic. An opponent, Apul. A contradictor, Vlp. An objector, Var. A refuter, Ascon.

units.la: Adversus, a, um] Adversans, Cic. Adversissimi venti, Cæs. Repugnantes inter se naturæ, Cic. Controversa, & repugnantia, & naturâ communionem abhorrentia, Macrob.
units.tr: Adverse] Opposing, Cic. The most adverse winds, Caes. Natures that are inconsistent with one another, Cic. Conflicting and opposed things, and by nature shrinking from union, Macrob.

units.la: Adversùs] Contrà naturam. In Antonium dicere, Cic.
units.tr: Against] Against nature. To speak against Antony, Cic.

units.la: Ex adverso] E regione & è contrariâ parte nobis est, Cic. Ex adversum est fabrica. Exadversus ei loco erat. Ter. Ex diverso cœli, Virg. Stat contrà, Id.
units.tr: Opposite] It is on our side and on the opposite side, Cic. The building is opposite. It was opposite that place, Ter. From the opposite quarter of the sky, Virg. He stands opposite, Id.

units.la: Adversaria, orum] Libellus memorialis, Suet. Hypomnema, Cic. Libelli liturarii, Ausonn. Silvæ, Gell. Stat. Confusanea doctrina, varia, miscella, Gell. Pratum, Id. Spicilegia, Palmer. Animadversiones, Adrian. Iun.
units.tr: Notebooks] A memorial book, Suet. Notes, Cic. Little books for erasing, Ausonn. Miscellanies, Gell. Stat. A miscellaneous, varied, mixed learning, Gell. A meadow, Id. Gleanings, Palmer. Annotations, Adrian. Iun.
