units.la: Adulari] Non re factisque, sed linguâ tantùm & verbotenus gratiâ gratificari, Salust. Lenocinari alicui. Sermonem ad alterius gratiam fingere & commutare. Ad gratiam alicujus loqui. Gratiæ causâ dicere. Auribus dare aliquid. Ne assentatiunculâ quâdam gratiam tuam aucupari videar. Ad voluntatem seu sensum alicujus loqui, Cic. Auribus servire, Cæs. Palpari. Parasitari. Supparasitari alicui, Plaut. Partes tractare secundas, Horat. Quicquid dixisset sequi, & secundas agere, Sen. Ad omnem auram evanuit. Dicis causâ, dicis gratiâ facit. Palpo percutere. Palpum obtrudere. Er. Caudâ blandiri, Id.
units.tr: To flatter] To gratify someone in word only, not in deeds, Salust. To pander to someone. To shape and change one's speech for another's favour. To speak to win favour. To speak for the sake of favour. To give ear to something. Lest I seem to be angling for your favour with some small flattery. To speak according to someone's will or feeling, Cic. To serve the ears, Caes. To be fawned upon. To play the parasite. To play the sycophant to someone, Plaut. To take the second parts, Horat. To follow whatever was said and play second fiddle, Sen. He vanished at every breath of favour. You say it for form's sake; he does it for form's sake. To strike with a pat. To thrust out a palm, Er. To fawn with the tail, Id.

units.la: Adulanti fides non adhibenda] Nec te quæsiveris extrà.
units.tr: No credit should be given to a flatterer] Do not seek yourself outside yourself.

units.la: Adulatio] Assentatiuncula, Cic. Adulatorius sermo, Tacit. Aufer hinc palpationes, Plaut. Palpamenta, Ammian. Vernilitas, Plin. Comitas assentatrix. Officiorum blanditiæ malitiosæ.
units.tr: Flattery] A little flattery, Cic. A flattering speech, Tacit. Away with these pattings, Plaut. Sweet words, Ammian. Servility, Plin. A fawning courtesy. The malicious caresses of duty.

units.la: Adulator] Eruditus ad assentationem, Cic. Palpator, Plaut. Palpo, Var. Arrisor divitum, Sen. Quibus linguæ gratia facta est, Ovid. Quibus sunt pictæ tentoria linguæ, Pers. Cane adulantior. Hæredipetis, Gnathone adulantior, Er. Adulatore & amico non potes eodem uti.
units.tr: Flatterer] One trained for flattery, Cic. A patter, Plaut. A patter, Var. A mocker of the rich, Sen. Those whose tongue has been made a favour, Ovid. Those whose tongue is painted like a tent, Pers. More fawning than a dog. A fortune-hunter, more fawning than Gnatho, Er. You cannot use a flatterer and a friend as one and the same.

units.la: Adulatoribus credere potius, quàm sibi] Extrà quærere sese.
units.tr: To trust flatterers rather than oneself] To seek oneself outside oneself.

units.la: Adulter] Nobilitatus adulterio, Plin. Pater alicujus vitio, Ovid. Subsessor alieni matrimonii, Val. Max. Clodius, Cic. Mulierum omnium vir, Suet. Plaut. Mœchus, Ter.
units.tr: Adulterer] Made notorious by adultery, Plin. The father of someone through vice, Ovid. A lurker in another's marriage, Val. Max. Clodius, Cic. The husband of all women, Suet. Plaut. An adulterer, Ter.

units.la: Adultera] Succuba alieni lecti, Ovid. Clytemnestra, Agamemnonis uxor infida. Pellex, Salust. Pallace, Suet. Mœcha, Catul.
units.tr: Adulteress] A succubus of another's bed, Ovid. Clytemnestra, the faithless wife of Agamemnon. A concubine, Salust. A mistress, Suet. An adulteress, Catul.

units.la: Adulterare] Peccare in adulteria, Sen. Lectum temerare jugalem, Ovid. Adulterare matronam, Suet. Adulterari Cic. Committere adulterium, Quint. Alienum cubile inire, Cic. Stuprare, pro adulterare, Sueton. in Nerone. Mœchari. Catul. Permolere alienas uxores, Horat.
units.tr: To commit adultery] To sin in adultery, Sen. To defile a marriage bed, Ovid. To commit adultery with a married woman, Suet. To be an adulterer, Cic. To commit adultery, Quint. To enter another's bed, Cic. To debauch, that is, to commit adultery, Sueton. in Nerone. To play the adulterer, Catul. To grind other men's wives, Horat.

units.la: Adulterium] Stuprum, Plaut. Stupri argui à viro, Bud. Probrum, Cic. Pellicatus, Id. Mœchimonium, Beroald.
units.tr: Adultery] Debauchery, Plaut. To be accused of debauchery by one's husband, Bud. Dishonour, Cic. Concubinage, Id. Adultery-mongering, Beroald.

units.la: Adulterator pecuniæ] Stellio monetarius, Æruscator, Gell.
units.tr: Adulterator of money] A coiner, a money-changer, Gell.

units.la: Adultus] Maturus, Liv. Maturus sponsæ, Stat. Grandis, Cic. Exoletus, Fest.
units.tr: Adult] Mature, Liv. Ripe for a bride, Stat. Full-grown, Cic. Outgrown, Fest.

units.la: Adunare. vid. Coadunare.
units.tr: To unite: see Coadunare.

units.la: Adunatio] Unitas facta est, Quint. Unius corporis esse, Liv. Unum esse corpus, Tacit. Colliquescere & unum fieri, Col. Coalescere in unum, Liv. Corpora connexa. Condenso. Conciliatus, Lucr. Unitas, Sen. Unio animorum, Sipont.
units.tr: Union] Unity has been made, Quint. To be of one body, Liv. To be one body, Tacit. To melt together and become one, Col. To grow together into one, Liv. Connected bodies. Condensed. Reconciled, Lucr. Unity, Sen. Union of minds, Sipont.

units.la: Aduncus] Uncus unguis, Lucr. Hamatus, Ovid. Inflexa in se cornua, Plin. Recurvum rostrum, Claud. Scalpratum ferramentum, Col.
units.tr: Hooked] A hooked claw, Lucr. Hooked, Ovid. Horns bent inwards, Plin. A curved beak, Claud. A scraping iron tool, Col.

units.la: Advocare, vid. Vocare.
units.tr: Advocare, see Vocare.

units.la: Advocatio] Revocatio ad, Cic. Introvocatus ad, Amm. Accitus, us, Virg.
units.tr: Advocatio] A calling to, Cic. A summoning in to, Amm. A summoning, accitus, -us, Virg.

units.la: Advocatus] (1) generaliter causæ defensor] Patronus causarum. Actor causarum. Orator, Cic. Procurator litis, Paul. IC. Forensis homo, Quint. Qui linguam causis acuit, Hor. Et mitia sub judice bella movet, Lucan. Natus ad arma clamosi fori, Ovid.
units.tr: Advocatus] (1) in general, a defender of a cause] A patron of causes. An advocate of causes. A speaker, Cic. A manager of a lawsuit, Paul. IC. A man of the forum, Quint. One who sharpens his tongue for causes, Hor. And stirs up gentle wars before the judge, Lucan. Born for the arms of the noisy forum, Ovid.

units.la: (2) Advocatus accusatoris] Actor. Petitor. Accusator. Cic.
units.tr: (2) Advocate of the accuser] A plaintiff. A petitioner. An accuser, Cic.

units.la: (3) Advocatus Rei] Defensor. Patronus. Ab reo, Cic.
units.tr: (3) Advocate of the defendant] A defender. A patron. On behalf of the accused, Cic.

units.la: (4) Advocatus in malam partem] Causidicus. Pugnaciter loquens, Fest. Proclamator, Cic. Rabula, Id. Latrator. Altercator, Quint. Ad lites (scil. homo) Propert. Prævaricator. Vocem in quæstum conferens : venalem linguam habens, Cic. Vitilitigator, Cato. Concinnator litium. Consarcinator causarum, Vlp. Togatus vulturius, Apul. Vendens jurgia fori, & verba locans, Sen. Loquendo pugnans, Ovid. Vendere verba solitus. Martial.
units.tr: (4) Advocate in a bad sense] A pettifogger. Speaking combatively, Fest. A bawler, Cic. A ranter, Id. A barker. A wrangler, Quint. Driven to lawsuits (of a man), Propert. A prevaricator. One who turns his voice to profit, having a tongue for sale, Cic. A fomenter of lawsuits, Cato. A stitcher-together of lawsuits. A patcher-up of causes, Ulp. A toga-clad vulture, Apul. One who sells the brawls of the forum and hires out words, Sen. One who fights with words, Ovid. One accustomed to selling words, Martial.

units.la: Advolvere] Admoliri rupem, Curt.
units.tr: Advolvere] To struggle to move a rock, Curt.

units.la: Adurere, leviter urere] Ignes cœlestes levi afflatu vestimenta adusserunt, Iul. Obseq. Amburere, Plaut. Præurere, Virg. Ignis degustavit tigna celeri flammâ. Suburere, Sueton. Glabrare sues ex tenuibus lignis factâ flammulâ, Col.
units.tr: To burn, to scorch lightly] Heavenly fires with a light breath scorched the garments, Iul. Obseq. To burn around, Plaut. To burn in front, Virg. The fire tasted the beams with swift flame. To burn from below, Suet. To singe pigs with a little flame made from thin sticks, Col.

units.la: Aduri à Sole] Colorari sole, Cic. Nigrum colorem trahere, Ovid.
units.tr: To be scorched by the sun] To be tanned by the sun, Cic. To take on a dark colour, Ovid.

units.la: Adustus à Sole] Solatus, Plin. Præustus, Plin. Sole torridus. Cui discolor à sole cutis. Cui sole usta cutis, Plin. Decolor Indus, Ovid. Incoctus Maurus, Sisl. Exustus in sole, Celsi. Solibus perustus, Hor. Adustioris coloris homo ex recenti via, Liv.
units.tr: Scorched by the sun] Sun-tanned, Plin. Scorched beforehand, Plin. Parched by the sun. One whose skin is discoloured by the sun. One whose skin is burnt by the sun, Plin. A dark-hued Indian, Ovid. A Moor baked dark, Sisl. Burnt in the sun, Celsus. Burnt by the sun, Hor. A man of darker complexion from a recent journey, Liv.

units.la: Adustus] Afflatus incendio, Liv. Allambentibus flammis ereptus. Quint. Inustus vapore fulminis, Lucr. Levi afflatu ignis adustus, Iul. Obseq. Sudes obusta, Ovid. Ambesus flammis, Virg. Semiustus, Lucr. Semiustulatus, Cic. Semi ambustus, Suet. Ustulatus, Vitruv. Tosti parietes, stant defordeformati, Cic. Indufata flammis robora, Stat. Ambustulatus, Plaut. Semicrematus, Ovid.
units.tr: Scorched] Fanned by fire, Liv. Snatched from the licking flames, Quint. Branded by the blast of lightning, Lucr. Burnt by a light breath of fire, Iul. Obseq. Charred stakes, Ovid. Singed by flames, Virg. Half-burnt, Lucr. Half-scorched, Cic. Half-burnt, Suet. Charred, Vitruv. Walls scorched, standing disfigured, Cic. Oaks wrapped in flames, Stat. Slightly burnt, Plaut. Half-cremated, Ovid.

units.la: Adytum vid. Sacrarium.
units.tr: Adytum, see Sacrarium.

units.la: Ædificare] Excitare ædificium, Sen. Fabrefacere vel fabrè facere, Liv. Architectari. Condere urbem. Texere Basilicam. Exstruere sepulchrum, Cic. Substruere Capitolium, Liv. Construere ædificium, navim, Cic. Struere, Hor. Moliri portam, Tac. Conficere porticum, Cic. Plin.
units.tr: To build] To raise a building, Sen. To construct, or build skilfully, Liv. To act as architect. To found a city. To weave a basilica. To erect a tomb, Cic. To lay the foundations of the Capitol, Liv. To construct a building, a ship, Cic. To build, Hor. To construct a gate, Tac. To complete a portico, Cic. Plin.

units.la: Ædificandi ars] Architectura, Cic. Architectonice, Quint. Machinalis scientia, Plin. Ars Mechanica Archimedis, Firm.
units.tr: The art of building] Architecture, Cic. Architectonics, Quint. Knowledge of machines, Plin. The mechanical art of Archimedes, Firm.

units.la: Ædificator] Architector, Plaut. Officinator, qui exstruit. Architectus, qui designat, Philard. Machinator. Liv. Mechanicus, Suet. Fabricarum peritus. Vopisc. Ædifex, Tertull.
units.tr: A builder] A master builder, Plaut. A workman, one who erects. An architect, one who designs, Philard. A machinist, Liv. A mechanic, Suet. One skilled in construction, Vopisc. A builder, Tertull.

units.la: Ædificatio] Fabricatio rei alicujus. Molitio, Cic. Molimentum, Liv. Structio cum fundamenta ad structuram jaciuntur, Col. vid. Exstructio.
units.tr: Building] The making of anything. A construction, Cic. A structure, Liv. The erection, when foundations are laid for a structure, Col. See Exstructio.

units.la: Ædificium] Fabrica. Opus, Cic. Pendent opera interrupta, minæque murorum, Virg. structura surgens, Lucan.
units.tr: A building] A structure. A work, Cic. Unfinished works hang, and the threatening walls, Virg. A rising structure, Lucan.

units.la: Ædificium magnæ molis aliquod] Semiramidis murus.
units.tr: Some building of great bulk] The wall of Semiramis.

units.la: Ædilis] Fabricarum tribunus, Amm. Tutelarius, Plin. Curator sartorum tectorum.
units.tr: An aedile] Tribune of the workshops, Amm. A guardian, Plin. Overseer of the repair of roofs and buildings.

units.la: Ædilitas] ædilitium munus] Cura ædium, Var. Ædilatus, Fest. Ædilitatus, Sipont.
units.tr: Aedileship] the aedilician office] Care of buildings, Var. Aedileship, Fest. Aedileship, Sipont.

units.la: Ædituus] Æditimus, Var. Hierodulus. Neocorus, Firm. (Sacristianus minimè Latinè dicitur) Custos sacrarum ædium, Er.
units.tr: A temple-keeper] A temple-keeper, Var. A temple servant. Neocorus, Firm. (sacristanus is by no means Latin) A guardian of the sacred buildings, Er.

units.la: Æger] Invalidus. Obnoxius. Morbidus. Morbosus. Causfariæ in animo partes, quibus adhibenda curatio est, Sen. Vitiosæ oves, Col. Corpus malè affectum, Liv. Sanitatis dubiæ.
units.tr: Sick] Infirm. Liable. Diseased. Morbid. Parts of the mind in which a cure must be applied, Sen. Faulty sheep, Col. A body badly affected, Liv. Of doubtful health.

units.la: Ægre facere alicui] Facere omnia ut incommodet, Ter. Quod eum remordeat. Id. Ultrò malè facere. Lædendi studio facere.
units.tr: To trouble someone] To do everything to inconvenience him, Ter. What gnaws at him, Id. To do harm unprovoked. To act with a desire to injure.

units.la: Ægre ferre] Acerbè ferre. Cic. Malè me id habet, Ter. Indignè ferre, Plin. Iniquissimè ferre, Suet. Ingratè ferre, Tacit. Indignanter ferre, Amm. Iniquâ mente ferre, Ovid.
units.tr: To take ill] To bear bitterly, Cic. That galls me, Ter. To bear with indignation, Plin. To bear most unfairly, Suet. To bear ungratefully, Tacit. To bear indignantly, Amm. To bear with an ill mind, Ovid.

units.la: Ægrè mihi est aliquid, Plin. Graviter hoc audio, Ter. Ægrè est aliquid animo meo, Plaut. Subirascor. Submolestè fero. Durius accipere hoc mihi visus est, quàm vellem. Est mihi id stomacho. Ex hac re molestiâ affectus sum, Cic.
units.tr: It grieves me that something..., Plin. I hear this with grief, Ter. It grieves my mind that something..., Plaut. I am somewhat angry. I take it rather ill. He seemed to take this harder than I would have wished. It sticks in my craw. I was troubled by this matter, Cic.

units.la: Ægrescere] Tentari aliquâ valetudine, Cic. Mentis vitio laesa figura est, Ovid. Facit amor maciem, Id. Consternari anima, Salust. Fragescit animus miseriis, Pacuv. Commarcet miles, Amm. vide Male est mihi. Deficere viribus.
units.tr: To grow sick] To be afflicted by some illness, Cic. The form is harmed by a fault of the mind, Ovid. Love makes one wasted, Id. To be dismayed in spirit, Sallust. The spirit grows weak under misfortunes, Pacuv. The soldier droops, Amm. See It is bad with me. To fail in strength.

units.la: Ægrotare] Morbo affici, urgeri, laborare, Cic. Morbus cum tenet, Plaut. Graviter se habet. Vis morbi vagatur, Liv. Conflictari morbo. Male est mihi. Morbo tentari, Cic. In morbo cubat, Plaut. Afflictari morbo, Liv. Conflictari iniquâ valetudinę, Plin. Laborare aliquo morbo, in morbo esse, Cic. Minus commodâ valetudine uti, Caes. Jacere, Cic.
units.tr: To be sick] To be affected, oppressed, labouring with a disease, Cic. When sickness holds him, Plaut. He is seriously ill. The force of the disease wanders about, Liv. To be wrestled with by disease. It is bad with me. To be tried by disease, Cic. He lies sick in bed, Plaut. To be afflicted by disease, Liv. To be struggling with poor health, Plin. To labour under some disease, to be in ill health, Cic. To enjoy less good health, Caes. To lie prostrate, Cic.

units.la: Æmulari] Æmulatus agere, Tacit. Æmulationem infensam exercere, Id. Decertare cum aliquo contentione dicendi, Cic. Cùm omnes certatim, aliusque alio gravius atque ornatius de salute meâ dixissent, Cic. Æmulari cum aliquo, Liv. Alter alteri non cedit, Altera ad alterius invidiam facit. Certare illos credas. Splendorem eorum æmulatio excitat.
units.tr: To emulate] To act in emulation, Tacit. To carry on a hostile rivalry, Id. To contend with someone in a contest of speaking, Cic. When all had vied with one another, one speaking more weightily and elegantly than another about my safety, Cic. To emulate someone, Liv. One does not yield to the other; the one stirs the other's envy. You would believe they were competing. Rivalry kindles the brilliance of them.

units.la: Æmulatio] Æmulatus, Tacit. Certamen, Cic. Ambitiosa æmulatio, livida, Bud.
units.tr: Emulation] Rivalry, Tacit. A contest, Cic. Ambitious emulation, spiteful, Bud.

units.la: Æmulus] Æmulator Catonis, Cic. Æmulus ejusdem Musæ, Gell. Sæpe nomen ejus, quem imitamur, nobis attribuitur, ad exprimendum æmulandi studium. Ut apud Quint. Brutius Antoniaster dicitur, imitator Antonii. Philotimus Fulviniaster, Fulvinii, &c. Terent. Parasitaster à parasito.
units.tr: A rival] An emulator of Cato, Cic. A rival of the same Muse, Gell. Often the name of the one whom we imitate is given to us, to express the zeal of emulating. As in Quint., Brutius is called Antoniaster, an imitator of Antony. Philotimus is called Fulviniaster, of Fulvinius, etc. Terent. Parasitaster from parasite.

units.la: Ænigma] Nodus. Nodosa quæstio, Macrob. Perobscura quæstio, Cic. Apologus. Apologatio. Quint. Griphus, Gell. (à reti intricato, ὁ γρίφος dicto) Glossa: Lingua secretior, Quint. Scirpi, Sirpi, Gell. Flexiloqua & obscura oracula, Cic. Bæotia ænigmata, i.e. Sphingis.
units.tr: A riddle] A knot. A knotty question, Macrob. A very obscure question, Cic. A fable. An apologue, Quint. A puzzle, Gell. (so called from an intricate net, Greek [ὁ γρίφος]) A gloss: a more secret tongue, Quint. Scirpi, Sirpi, Gell. Ambiguous and obscure oracles, Cic. Boeotian riddles, i.e. of the Sphinx.

units.la: Æqualis, æquè tantus] Æqui par, Ausón. Geminus, Cic. Æquilaterus angulus, Firm. Mei loci & ordinis, Ter. Æquiparabilis, Plaut. Similis. Ex æquo. Æqualis amore, staturâ Æquus, Ter. Æquabilis. Par studium, momentum. Pares in amore & æquales, Cic.
units.tr: Equal, equally great] Equal in pairs, Ausonius. Twin, Cic. An equilateral angle, Firm. Of my place and rank, Ter. Comparable, Plaut. Like. On equal terms. Equal in love, even in stature, Ter. Uniform. Equal in zeal and weight. Equal and alike in love, Cic.

units.la: Æqualis ætate] Synephebus. Coævus, Cic. Ætate pares, Plaut. idem ætatis, Tacit. ejusdem ætatis. Parili ætate homo, Ovid.
units.tr: Equal in age] A fellow youth. Coeval, Cic. Equal in years, Plaut. Of the same age, Tacit. Of the same age. A man of equal age, Ovid.

units.la: Æqualis ætati alicujus] Conjunctus ætati, Cic. Synchronos, Var. Contemporaneus, Sipont. Æquævus, Virg. Coætaneus, Port. Lat. Suppar ætati. (Qui eodem tempore vixit, sed junior) Cic.
units.tr: Contemporary with someone] Joined in age, Cic. Synchronous, Var. Contemporary, Sipont. Of equal age, Virg. Coetaneous, Port. Lat. Almost equal in age (one who lived at the same time but was younger), Cic.

units.la: Æqualitas] Æquilibritas. Æqualis tributio. Isonomia, Cic. Æquipollentia. Æquilatatio, Vitruv. Æquitas portionum, Sen. Æquabilitas juris, Cic. Æquiparatio, & Parilitas, Gell. Paritas. Assimilis ratio, Lucr.
units.tr: Equality] Equilibrium. Equal distribution. Isonomy [ἰσονομία], Cic. Equipollence. Equal breadth, Vitruv. Fairness of shares, Sen. Equality of law, Cic. Equal comparison and parity, Gell. Parity. A similar reckoning, Lucr.

units.la: Æqualiter] Ex æquo partiri, Tacit. Ex pari coëunt, Quint. Nihilo plus, minus, Ter. Æque ambo pares, Plaut. Æquâ lance.
units.tr: Equally] To divide equally, Tacit. They come together on equal terms, Quint. No more, no less, Ter. Both equally matched, Plaut. On an even balance.

units.la: Æquare, æquum facere] Ad æqualitatem redigere, Plin. Coërcere incrementa, Col. Complanare, Ulp. Ad planum reducere. Explere cicatrices. Emarginare ulcera, Plin. vid. Coæquare.
units.tr: To make equal, to make level] To reduce to equality, Plin. To check growth, Col. To level, Ulp. To bring to a flat surface. To fill up scars. To trim the edges of ulcers, Plin. See Coæquare.

units.la: Æquè ac] Æquè ac si collega ejus. Æquè atque ea, Cic. Æquè quasi, Ulp. Quasi si. Tantidem est quasi si, Plaut. Non aliter quàm si. Ulp. Æquè ut, Cic. Adæquè ut, quasi, si, Plaut. Non secus ac si, Cic. Haud secus atque, Sallust. Haud secus quàm si, Liv. Pariter ac si hostes adessent, Sallust. Pariter atque, Gell. Pariter ac, Liv. Pariter ut, Plaut. Perinde ac, Caes. Perinde ac si, Cic. Perinde atque, Id. Perinde atque si, Ulp. Perinde quàm, Suet. Perinde veluti, Just. Perinde uti ego, Plaut. Perinde ut, Cic. Perinde prout, Plin. Proinde ac, Plaut. Var. Cic. Proinde atque, Pomp. Proinde quasi, Cic. Proinde ut, Fest. Non minus atque, Catul. Nihilominus quasi, Liv. Varr. Non magis quàm si, Virg. Similiter ac, atque. Similiter ut, Cic. Simili ratione, Col. Similiter item ut coquus, Plaut. Juxta ac meus frater esses. Nihil aliter ac. Itidem fui, ut Cic. Juxta rem mecum tenes, Plaut. Itidem quasi, Plaut. Non minus, quàm si. Non aliter ac, atque, Cic.
units.tr: Æquè ac] Just as if he were his colleague. Just as that, Cic. Just as if, Ulp. As if, Ulp. It is just as if, Plaut. Not otherwise than if, Ulp. Just as, Cic. Just as if, Plaut. Not otherwise than if, Cic. Just as, as if, Plaut. Not otherwise than if, Cic. Just as if enemies were present, Sallust. Just as, Gell. Just as, Liv. Just as, Plaut. Exactly as, Caes. Exactly as if, Cic. Exactly as, Cic. Exactly as if, Ulp. Exactly as much as, Suet. Exactly as, Just. Exactly as I, Plaut. Exactly as, Cic. Exactly as the situation requires, Plin. Just as, Var. Cic. Just as, Pomp. As if, Cic. Just as, Fest. No less than, Catul. Not otherwise than as if, Liv. Not more than if, Virg. In the same way as, Cic. In a similar way, Col. Just as the cook, Plaut. You were as my brother. Nothing otherwise than. I was just as, Cic. You hold the matter just as I do, Plaut. Just as if, Plaut. No less than if. Not otherwise than, Cic.

units.la: Æquilibrium] Pondus æquum, Pallad. Æquatum examen, Virg. Æquali examine dividere, Plin.
units.tr: Equilibrium] An equal weight, Pallad. A balance of equal weight, Virg. To divide with an equal balance, Plin.

units.la: Æquinoctium] Æquidiale & æquinoctiale,(scil. tempus) Fest. Nodus anni. Fretus anni, Lucr.
units.tr: Equinox] Equal-day and equinoctial (sc. time), Fest. The knot of the year. The strait of the year, Lucr.

units.la: Æquatio. vid. Exæquatio.
units.tr: Equation. See Exæquatio.

units.la: Æquator] Æquinoctialis circulus, Plin. Æqui dies, Archit.
units.tr: Equator] The equinoctial circle, Plin. Equal days, Archit.

units.la: Æquipollere] Æquivalere, Sipont. Respondere majoribus suis, Cic.
units.tr: To be equivalent] To be of equal value, Sipont. To answer to one's ancestors, Cic.

units.la: Æquum iniquum] Fas & nefas.
units.tr: Fair and unfair] Right and wrong.

units.la: Ex æquo & bono] De plano aliquid cognoscere, arbitrari, censere. Æquitatem habe, serva. Æquitate utere. Remisso, non summo jure contende. Ne ad summa & inimicissima jura decurras, Cic. Ne quid iniquum exigas, incoeptes. Ne quid præter æquum & bonum. Æquum bonumque ora.
units.tr: In equity and good conscience] To judge something on the plain facts, to decide and to give an opinion. Keep to equity, observe it. Use equity. Contend on the milder rather than the strictest law. Do not run to the highest and most hostile rights, Cic. Do not demand anything unfair; do not begin. Nothing beyond what is fair and good. Pray for what is fair and good.

units.la: Æquum est] vid. Fas est.
units.tr: It is fair] See Fas est.

units.la: Aer] Aeres, Lucr. Cœlum, crassum, tenue, in quo nubes, imbres, ventique coguntur. Cœli (cœlestis) spiritus. Communis spiritus; & absolutè, Spiritus, Animalis spirabilisque natura circumfusa undique, Cic. Æther. Æthra, Virg. Refocillator rerum. Arrosor rerum. Aura ætherea.
units.tr: Air] Airs, Lucr. The sky, thick or thin, in which clouds, rains and winds are gathered. The spirit of heaven (heavenly). A common spirit; and absolutely, Spirit: the animal and breathable nature spread around on every side, Cic. Ether. Aethra, Virg. The refresher of things. The moistener of things. Ethereal breeze.

units.la: Aer salubris] Salubritas aeris, Pallad. Cœlum bonum habet ager, Cic. Temperatura cœli, Var. Temperies cœli, Ovid.
units.tr: Healthy air] The healthfulness of the air, Pallad. The field has a good climate, Cic. The temperature of the sky, Var. The mildness of the sky, Ovid.

units.la: Aer insalubris] Inimicus aer membris, homini, Lucr. Cujus pestilens & gravis est spiratio, Cic. Gravitas cœli ac loci. Calamitosum cœlum, Cic. Morbus cœli, Virg.
units.tr: Unhealthy air] Air hostile to the limbs and to man, Lucr. Whose breathing is pestilential and heavy, Cic. The unhealthiness of sky and place. A calamitous sky, Cic. A sickness of the sky, Virg.

units.la: Aercus] Æthereus, Virg. Ætherius.
units.tr: Aerial] Ethereal, Virg. Heavenly.

units.la: Æramenta] Ærificia, Non. ex Vart.
units.tr: Bronze implements] Works in bronze, Non. ex Varr.

units.la: Ærana] Æris fodina, Plin.
units.tr: Copper mine] A bronze mine, Plin.

units.la: Æraria officina] Æraria fornax, Plin.
units.tr: Bronze foundry] A bronze furnace, Plin.

units.la: Ærarium, loculamentum æris publici] Gaza, Mela. Ærarium sanctius, Cic. Cimiliarchon, Bud. Gazophylacium, Lucr.
units.tr: Treasury, a chest for public money] A treasure, Mela. The more sacred treasury, Cic. Treasurer, Bud. Treasure-house, Lucr.

units.la: Ærarius faber] Faber æris. Flator æris, Pomp. Excusor, Quint. Faber ærarius, Plin.
units.tr: Coppersmith] A worker in bronze. A bronze beater, Pomp. A bronze embosser, Quint. A bronze-smith, Plin.

units.la: Æreus] Æneum vas, Col. Aheneus murus, Hor. Ærinas compedes, Var. Mortarium Cyprium, seu cuprium, Plin. Cuprini clavi, Pallad.
units.tr: Bronze] A bronze vessel, Col. A brazen wall, Hor. Bronze fetters, Var. A Cyprian, or copper, mortar, Plin. Copper nails, Pallad.

units.la: Æratus] Inærata puppis, Val. Argon.
units.tr: Bronzed] A ship's stern not sheathed in bronze, Val. Argon.

units.la: Ærosus] Ærifex, Ovid. Plin. Ærosus lapis, cum ære mixtus, Plin.
units.tr: Full of bronze] Bronze-working (artificer), Ovid. Plin. A bronze-bearing stone, mixed with copper, Plin.

units.la: Ærugo] Æruca, Vitruv. Viride æris, Philand. Ærugo æris, Plin.
units.tr: Rust, verdigris] Verdigris, Vitruv. The green of bronze, Philand. Rust of bronze, Plin.

units.la: Ærumnæ] Ærumnulæ, Plaut. Furcæ, vel Furca, Id. Furcillæ viatorum, Fest.
units.tr: Hardships] Little hardships, Plaut. Yokes, or a yoke, Id. Travellers' little forks, Fest.

units.la: Æs] Ærumen, & Ærimen, Fest. Scal. Cuprum, Plin. Rudus,& Rudusculum, est æs infectum. At rudus est conflatum, Fest.
units.tr: Bronze, copper] Aerumen and Aerimen, Fest. Scal. Copper, Plin. Rudus and rudusculum are unwrought bronze. But rudus is cast bronze, Fest.

units.la: Æs alienum, Solvere ære alieno] Versuram facere. Versurâ aliquid solvere, Cic.
units.tr: Debt; to pay off debt] To take out a loan to pay another debt. To pay something off by borrowing, Cic.

units.la: Æstas] Fervens æstas, Virg. Æstivi Soles. Formosa messibus æstas, Poëtica sunt. Frugum maturatrix.
units.tr: Summer] Burning summer, Virg. Summer suns. Summer beautiful with harvests (poetic expressions). Ripener of crops.

units.la: Æstate] Mediâ, adultâ æstate, Col. Per ætatem, Col.
units.tr: In summer] In midsummer, in high summer, Col. Through life, Col.

units.la: Æstimare] Constituere pretium. Spectare aliquem ex censu, Cic. Taxare tanti aliquid. Sumptus funeris arbitrantur pro facultatibus defuncti, Vlp. Judicare, Ter. Pensare amicos factis, Liv. Pensare unum ex alio, Val. Max. Ponderare. Existimare alios suis moribus. Spectare aliquem ex vita. Describere jura prætio, non æquitate. Metiri, Er. Vulgus amicitias utilitate probat, Ovid. Parvi pretii deputare, Terent.
units.tr: To value] To fix a price. To judge someone by his property, Cic. To rate something at so much. They reckon the cost of a funeral by the means of the deceased, Vlp. To judge, Ter. To weigh friends by their deeds, Liv. To weigh one against another, Val. Max. To weigh up. To judge others by one's own morals. To judge someone by his life. To define rights by price, not by fairness. To measure, Er. The crowd approves friendships for their usefulness, Ovid. To count as of little worth, Ter.

units.la: Æstimari] Esse in numero, Cic.
units.tr: To be valued] To be counted among, Cic.

units.la: Nihil æstimari] Esse nullo numero, Id.
units.tr: To be valued at nothing] To be of no account, Id.

units.la: Æstimatio] Censio, Fest. Æstimia, Id. Taxatio latifundii, unionum, Plin.
units.tr: Valuation] Assessment, Fest. Estimate, Id. Appraisal of an estate, of pearls, Plin.

units.la: Æstuans] Æthna æstuantior, Er. Flagras. Flagrantissimus sol, Plin. Torridus aër, Propert. Torrentissimus axis, Stat. Æstuosus auster, Plin. Æstuosissimum animal, sus, Col. Æstifer ignis, Cic. Præfervida mundi declinatio. Præfervidus cœli status, Col. Referens, Plin. Ardens, Id.
units.tr: Seething, blazing] Hotter than Etna, Er. Blazing. The most blazing sun, Plin. Scorching air, Propert. Most scorching axle, Stat. Sultry south wind, Plin. The most sultry animal, the pig, Col. Heat-bringing fire, Cic. The overheated turning of the world. An overheated state of the sky, Col. Glowing, Plin. Burning, Id.

units.la: Æstuare à sole] Æstu laborare, Col. Fervescere sole, Lucr. Ardore solis torreri. Uri calore, Cic. Exæstuare igne, Lucr. Æstuare caloribus, Col.
units.tr: To swelter from the sun] To labour in the heat, Col. To boil in the sun, Lucr. To be parched by the sun's blaze. To be burnt by heat, Cic. To glow with fire, Lucr. To seethe with heat, Col.

units.la: Æstuare ab aquâ] Æstuat mare, Liv. Fervet æquor, Virg. Effervescit pontus, Cic. Turbat mare, Var. Subhor-rescit mare, Sisin. Hom.
units.tr: To surge, of water] The sea surges, Liv. The sea seethes, Virg. The sea boils up, Cic. The sea is stirred, Var. The sea shudders, Sisin. Hom.

units.la: Æstus aëris à sole] Ardor solis, Cic. Verbera radiorum solis. Fervor solis, Lucr. Æstivus fervor, Plin. Excanduit radiis dies, Amm. Assus sol, Cic. Turneb. Herbarum para-lysis.
units.tr: Heat of the air from the sun] The burning of the sun, Cic. The lashing of the sun's rays. The heat of the sun, Lucr. Summer heat, Plin. The day blazed with rays, Amm. Parched sun, Cic. Turneb. The paralysis of herbs.

units.la: Æstus maris] Accessus & recessus maris, Cic. Accremen-tum maris. Æstus reciproci: crescentes, Plin. Refluum mare, Id.
units.tr: Tide of the sea] The advance and retreat of the sea, Cic. The increase of the sea. Alternating tides: flowing, Plin. The sea ebbing back, Id.

units.la: Ætatem mutare] Calceos mutare.
units.tr: To change one's age] To change one's shoes.

units.la: Ætas] Spacium ætatis. Tertiam hominum ætatem vi-vebat, Cic.
units.tr: Age] A span of life. He lived the third age of men, Cic.

units.la: Æternare] In æternum durare, Quint. Immensum vi-vere, Tacit. Infinito tempore cessare, Cic. Perpetuitare, Enn.
units.tr: To make eternal] To last for ever, Quint. To live immensely, Tacit. To cease for infinite time, Cic. To perpetuate, Enn.

units.la: Æternitas] Ævum sempiternum. Infinitum ætatis tem-pus. Perennitas, Cic. Sempiternitas, Cato.
units.tr: Eternity] Everlasting age. Infinite span of time. Perpetuity, Cic. Sempiternity, Cato.

units.la: Æternitati consecrare] Perpetuitatis honore mactare, Arnob. Æternare aliquem, Hor.
units.tr: To consecrate to eternity] To honour with the glory of perpetuity, Arnob. To make someone eternal, Hor.

units.la: Æternò, & æternùm] In perpetuum, Cic. In tempus sem-piternum. In omne ævum. In omne tempus, Cic. Perpe-tuò, Ter. Infinito tempore, Cic.
units.tr: Eternally] For ever, Cic. For everlasting time. For all ages. For all time, Cic. Continually, Ter. For infinite time, Cic.

units.la: Ab æterno] Ab omni æternitate. A sempiternis seculo-rum ætatibus, Cic. Ab infinitâ innumerabilium seculorum multitudine, Id.
units.tr: From eternity] From all eternity. From the everlasting ages of the centuries, Cic. From the infinite, countless multitude of ages, Id.

units.la: Æternus] Eâ exstructione, quæ sit ad memoriam æterni-tatis. Ab omni æternitate vivens. Ex omni æternitate fluens fatum. Perennis fama. Sempiternus mundus, Cic. Æviter-nus, Enn. Perpetuus, Lucr. Mulio perpetuarius, Sen.
units.tr: Eternal] A structure of such a kind as to be for the memory of eternity. Living from all eternity. A fate flowing from all eternity. An everlasting fame. An everlasting world, Cic. Age-long, Enn. Perpetual, Lucr. A muleteer for ever, Sen.

units.la: Æthiops] Incoăti corpora Mauri, Sil. Tincti colore no-ctis, Petron. Quibus in corpore color est noctis, Apul.
units.tr: Ethiopian] Moorish bodies scorched, Sil. Dyed with the colour of night, Petron. Those whose bodies have the colour of night, Apul.

units.la: Æthiopia] Mauritania, Cic.
units.tr: Ethiopia] Mauretania, Cic.

units.la: Ævum] Ævitas, Var. Seculum, Cic. In longum durare ævum, Ovid. Ætas, Cic. undeni decies anni, Hor.
units.tr: Age] Age-long time, Var. A century, Cic. To last for a long age, Ovid. A lifetime, Cic. Eleven times ten years, Hor.

units.la: Affabilis] Benignus vir, Cic. Liquidiusculus, quàm ven-tus Favonius, Plaut. Civilissimus in colloquiis, Spart. Quint. Omnibus affabilem se esse vult. Philologus in omni ser-mone, mone,Cic. Liquidus homo,Cic.Plaut. Comis vir,Cic. Commodus conviva, Plaut. Blanda lingua, Cic.
units.tr: Affable] A kindly man, Cic. Smoother than the west wind, Plaut. Most courteous in conversation, Spart. Quint. He wishes to be affable to all. Fond of learning in every conversation, Cic. A pleasant man, Cic. Plaut. A courteous man, Cic. A genial dinner-guest, Plaut. A soft tongue, Cic.

units.la: Affabilitas]Benigna oratio,Cic. Charientissimus,Donat. Comitas, Philologia, Cic.
units.tr: Affability] Kindly speech, Cic. Most gracious, Donat. Courtesy, love of learning, Cic.

units.la: Affabiliter] Affabilissimè dicebat, Gell. Placidè accepta oratio, Liv. Indulgenter loqui, Cic. Comiter appellare aliquem, Liv. Benedicè alliciebas ad te, Plaut.
units.tr: Affably] He spoke most affably, Gell. A speech received calmly, Liv. To speak kindly, Cic. To address someone courteously, Liv. You used to win people over to you with fair words, Plaut.

units.la: Affabre] vid. Artificialiter.
units.tr: Skilfully] See Artificialiter.

units.la: Affectare, solicitè quærere] Adspirare ad magistrum, Vlp. in summum ambitionis eniti. In consummutationem dignitatis erepere, Sen. Ultimo animo contendere, Cic. Captare laudem. Venari gloriam. Accersere sibi malum. Aucupari famam, Er.
units.tr: To aspire to, to seek anxiously] To aspire to an office, Vlp. To strive for the height of ambition. To creep into the highest dignity, Sen. To strive with utmost effort, Cic. To catch at praise. To hunt for glory. To bring trouble on oneself. To fish for fame, Er.

units.la: Affectare] affectatè agere] Ambitiosius agere aliquid, Cic. Affectator sum nimius, Quint. Et gratiam rei nimiâ coop-tatione consumpsimus, Fab. i.e. affectatione nimiâ.
units.tr: Affectare, to act affectedly] To act something with more ambition, Cic. I am too much of an affecter, Quint. And we have spoiled the grace of the thing by excessive over-elaboration, Fab. that is, by excessive affectation.

units.la: Affectate] Ambitiosè agere, Cic. Putidè loqui, Sen. Putidè literas exprimere, Cic. Jactanter, Tacit. Certatim, Quint. Ad certamen, Vitruv. Noli jactantius mœrere Germanicum.
units.tr: Affectedly] To act ambitiously, Cic. To speak affectedly, Sen. To write letters affectedly, Cic. Boastfully, Tacit. Competitively, Quint. In rivalry, Vitruv. Do not mourn Germanicus too ostentatiously.

units.la: Affectatio] Ambitiosus declamandi sudor,Quint. Ambitiosa diligentia,Vlp. Contentiosa simultas. Livida æmulatio.
units.tr: Affectation] The ambitious sweat of declamation, Quint. Ambitious diligence, Vlp. Quarrelsome rivalry. Envious emulation.

units.la: Affectatus, oppositus ingenio] Ambitiosæ amicitiæ declamationes, Cic. Putida oratio, Id. Adpetita, vel appetita verba, Ter. Adulatio quæsitior. Composita dicta, Acci. Imaginarius, Liv. Quæsitus, Tacit. Ascitus ornatus. Ascititius decor, Er.
units.tr: Affected, opposed to natural talent] Ambitious declamations of friendship, Cic. Affected speech, Id. Sought-after words, Ter. A more studied flattery. Composed sayings, Acci. Feigned, Liv. Far-fetched, Tacit. Borrowed ornament. Borrowed grace, Er.

units.la: Affectuosus] Patheticus, Macrob. Tragicus orator, Cic.
units.tr: Emotional] Pathetic, Macrob. A tragic orator, Cic.

units.la: Affectus] Affectio animi. Mentis motus.Animi impetus. Pathos. Divina mentis incitatio, Cic. Irritatio animorum naturalis, Sen.
units.tr: Affection, emotion] A disposition of the mind. A movement of the mind. An impulse of the soul. Pathos. A divine stirring of the mind, Cic. A natural arousing of the spirits, Sen.

units.la: Affectum moderare] Ama tanquam osurus. Oderis tanquam amaturus.
units.tr: To moderate one's feelings] Love as one who will one day hate. Hate as one who will one day love.

units.la: Affectus præsens fallax] Animo dolenti nihil oportet credere.
units.tr: A present feeling deceives] One ought to believe nothing when the mind is grieving.

units.la: Afferre, secum ferre] Apportare nuncium,Ter. Importare adjumenta, incommoda,Cic. Conciliare. Conflare. Comparare. rare. Creare. Procreare. Conscisцere. Conficere alicui malum. Cic.
units.tr: To bring, to carry with oneself] To bring a message, Ter. To bring in help, troubles, Cic. To procure. To kindle. To prepare. To make ready. To create. To beget. To be party to. To bring evil upon someone, Cic.

units.la: Afferre nihil Symbolæ] Immunem venire.
units.tr: To bring nothing to the shot] To come without contributing.

units.la: Afficere animum mærore vel gaudio] Perculit me timor, Cic. Invasit me dolor, Ter. Occupat animos terror, Cæf. Percussit me pulchritudo istius rei, Sen. Percepit me odium vitæ, Lucr. Commovet me desiderium. Movet me aliquid, Cic. Percutit animum, Lucr.
units.tr: To affect the mind with sorrow or joy] Fear has struck me down, Cic. Grief has come upon me, Ter. Terror seizes the minds, Caes. The beauty of that thing has struck me, Sen. Hatred of life has taken hold of me, Lucr. Longing stirs me. Something moves me, Cic. It strikes the mind, Lucr.

units.la: Affigere] Figere clavo aliquid, Cic. Offigantur ei (in cruce) tis pedes, bis brachia, Plaut.
units.tr: To fasten] To fix something with a nail, Cic. On the cross his feet are fastened, and his arms twice, Plaut.

units.la: Affinitatem jungere cum aliquo] Devincire se affinitate, Cic. Innecti alicui per affinitatem, Tacit. Congermanescere cum aliquo, Dar.
units.tr: To form a marriage alliance with someone] To bind oneself by affinity, Cic. To be tied to someone by marriage, Tacit. To become like brothers with someone, Dar.

units.la: Affirmare] Ajere. Asserere. Asseverare firmissimè. Omni asseveratione affirmare. Arbitrari (verbum testis jurati) Cic. Pro comperto afferre, Liv. Instare factum, Ter.
units.tr: To affirm] To say yes. To assert. To swear most firmly. To affirm with every solemn assurance. To declare (a word of a sworn witness), Cic. To bring forward as certain, Liv. To insist on the deed, Ter.

units.la: Neque affirmare, neque negare] In medio aliquid relinquere, Cic. Quod discrepat, in medio sit, Suet. In medium relinquere, Gell. Nihil statuere. Sed de hoc ut tu videris. Viderint ista viri boni, Cic. Tu videris. Tuum judicium esto. Nihil definire, Id.
units.tr: Neither to affirm nor to deny] To leave something undecided, Cic. What differs, let it stand in the middle, Suet. To leave in the middle, Gell. To decide nothing. But as for this, see to it yourself. Let good men see to those things, Cic. You must see to it. Let it be your judgement. To define nothing, Id.

units.la: Afflare] Afflare ore, Ovid. Afflari ore alicujus. Adflare calidum vaporem, Lucr. Adhalare. Inhalare. Inspirare, Gell. Necare afflatu aliquem.
units.tr: Afflare: to breathe upon with the mouth (Ovid.); to be breathed upon by someone; to breathe warm vapour upon (Lucr.); to breathe in; to inspire (Gell.); to kill someone by breath.

units.la: Afflatus] Inhalatus oris, Apul.
units.tr: Afflatus: breathed upon by the mouth (Apul.).

units.la: Afflatus divinus] Vid. Inspiratio divina, Cic.
units.tr: Afflatus divinus: see Inspiratio divina, Cic.

units.la: Affliction & Afflictatio] Ægritudo cum vexatione corporis, Cic. Calamitas. Cruciatus animi. Cruciamentum. Ærumna. Angor. Ægritudo premens. Aculeus & scrupulus solicitudinum. Stimulus doloris. Tormentum suspicionis. Anxietudo prona ad luctum & mœrores, Ipsaque semper se solicitans, Cic. Cordolium, Plaut. Manes patimur quisque suos, Virg.
units.tr: Affliction & Afflictatio: sickness together with bodily torment (Cic.); calamity; torment of the mind; torture; distress; anguish; oppressive grief; the sting and prick of anxieties; the goad of pain; the torment of suspicion; anxiety inclined to mourning and sorrow, always troubling itself (Cic.); heartache (Plaut.); each of us endures his own ghosts (Virg.).

units.la: Afflictus] Fractus animus calamitate. Ægritudine debilitatus. Omnisque spe salutis orbatus. Vexatus contumeliis. Jactatus injuriis. Male, graviter affectus. Æger, & animo confectus angoribus. Prostratus. Mœrore profligatus. Lacrymis crymis ac mœrore perditus, Cic. Miser animi, animo, &, ab animo, ex animo, Plaut. Æger animi, Liv. Animo, Plin. Ab animo, Plaut. Lassus animi, Id.
units.tr: Afflictus: spirit broken by calamity; weakened by sickness; deprived of all hope of safety; harassed by insults; battered by injuries; badly and grievously affected; sick, and worn down in spirit by anxieties; prostrate; ruined by grief; ruined by tears and sorrow (Cic.); wretched in spirit (Plaut.); sick in spirit (Liv.); in spirit (Plin.); from the spirit (Plaut.); weary in spirit (Id.).

units.la: Affligere] Afflictare sese; aliquem. Afficere corpus calamitate. Conficere angore. Vexat eum conscientia scelerum, Republica divexata, Cic. Habere aliquem miserrimum omnibus molestis. Tentare hominis solitudinem, Infirmitatem. Exercere. Suffocare, Cic. Cruciare. Excarnificare, Ter. Macerare, Sen. Ærumna me exercitum habet, Plaut.
units.tr: Affligere: to harass oneself or someone; to afflict the body with calamity; to wear down with anguish; a guilty conscience torments him (Cic.), the republic is torn apart; to make someone most wretched with all kinds of troubles; to test a man's solitude and weakness; to exercise; to suffocate (Cic.); to torture; to tear to pieces (Ter.); to waste away (Sen.); distress holds me in its grip (Plaut.).

units.la: Affligi] Tabescere calamitate. Vid. Angi.
units.tr: Affligi: to waste away with calamity. See Angi.

units.la: Affluere, fluendo pervenire] Bis affluunt, bisque remeant, Plin. Adnare oris terræ, Virg.
units.tr: Affluere, fluendo pervenire: they flow in twice and return twice (Plin.); to swim up to the shores of the land (Virg.).

units.la: Affulgere] Illucescere. Vox & authoritas Consulis in tantis tenebris illuxit, Resplenduit, Cic. Refulsit sol. Ovid. Exsplenduerunt in puero dotes animi & corporis, Suet. Infulgere, Plaut.
units.tr: Affulgere: to dawn upon. The voice and authority of the consul shone out in such great darkness (Cic.); the sun has shone out again (Ovid.); gifts of mind and body shone forth in the boy (Suet.); to shine upon (Plaut.).

units.la: Agaricum] Fungus larignum, & aliarum arborum, Plin. Matthiol.
units.tr: Agaricum: a fungus of the larch and of other trees (Plin., Matthiol.).

units.la: Agaso] Agitator asselli, Virg. Stimulator, Cic. Asinarius, Casaub.
units.tr: Agaso: the driver of a little ass (Virg.); a goader (Cic.); a donkey-keeper (Casaub.).

units.la: Age !] Age licemini! Plaut. Age, age, Cic. Ter. Agedum procedat, Liv. Agedum conferte, Cic. Vos age! Val. Argon. Vos agedum! Propert. Eja, Ter. Eja age, Virg. Agite pugnis, Plaut. Agite dum, ite mecum, Liv. Pergite, agite, Virg. Age sis ergo, Cic. Perge in virum, Plaut. Fac honestis studiis incumbas, Eras.
units.tr: Age!: come on! (Plaut.); come, come (Cic., Ter.); let him come forward now (Liv.); come on, bring together (Cic.); you, come on! (Val. Argon.); you, come on now! (Propert.); come on! (Ter.); come on, come on (Virg.); fight with your fists (Plaut.); come on, go with me (Liv.); press on and come on (Virg.); come then, please (Cic.); press on against the man (Plaut.); see that you apply yourself to honourable studies (Erasm.).

units.la: Age strenue] Vires tuas explica. Virtutem omnem excita.
units.tr: Age strenue: display your strength; rouse all your virtue.

units.la: Agat quisque sua] Colo quod aptasti, ipsi tibi nendum est. Fabri fabrilia tractent. In suo regno quisque sit. Quam quisque novit artem, in ea se exerceat.
units.tr: Agat quisque sua: let each do his own work. I cultivate what you have fitted; the spinning is not yet yours. Let smiths handle smith's work. Let each be in his own kingdom. Let each practise the art he knows.

units.la: Agendo discimus agere] Dicendo dicere discunt. Errando non errari discitur. Ex libro miser gubernator. Fabricando fabricamur.
units.tr: Agendo discimus agere: by speaking we learn to speak; by erring one learns not to err; a steersman learns from a book, and is a wretch; by making we become makers.

units.la: Agere inutile quid] Actum agere. Aciem cædere, ferire, Vid. Inutiliter aliquid agere.
units.tr: Agere inutile quid: to do what is already done (actum agere); to cut down or strike the battle line. See Inutiliter aliquid agere.

units.la: Age, quod cœpisti, perage] Domum cum cœpisti, ne delinquas imperfectam. In cursu esse.
units.tr: Age, quod cœpisti, perage: when you have begun a house, do not leave it unfinished. To be in the course.

units.la: Agere sic res, quomodo patiuntur se agi] Conto navigare.
units.tr: Agere sic res, quomodo patiuntur se agi: to sail with a pole.

units.la: Agere stulta] Nebulas diverberare. Vid. Inutiliter.
units.tr: Agere stulta: to beat the clouds. See Inutiliter.

units.la: Agere sibi contraria] Calidum & frigidum ex eodem ore effiare.
units.tr: Agere sibi contraria: to blow hot and cold from the same mouth.

units.la: Ager] Agellus, Cic. Aratio, Cic. Aratiuncula. Plaut.
units.tr: Ager: a little field (Cic.); ploughing (Cic.); a little ploughed land (Plaut.).

units.la: Agilis] Liv. Velox, Plin. Citus, Virg. Citissimus, Plaut. Citatus. Citatissimus. Concitatus, Liv. Concitatissimus, Quint. Praeceler. Praevelox, Plin. Pernix, Lucr. Plin. Praepes, Cic. Incitus. Incitatus & Incitatissimus, Id. Volucer, & volucris. Rapidus equus, Ovid. Praerapidus, Sil. Mobilis, Lucr. Mens mire mobilis. Effusus cursus, Liv. Expromptus, Ter. Levipes, Var. Pegaseo fertur volatu, Ocyor. Ocyssimus, Plin. Volaticus impetus, Cic. Ales, adnom. Sil.
units.tr: Agilis: nimble (Liv.); swift (Plin.); quick (Virg.); quickest (Plaut.); hurried; quickened (Liv.); very quick (Quint.); very swift; Praeceler; very fast (Plin.); nimble, active (Lucr., Plin.); flying ahead (Cic.); rapid horse (Ovid.); very rapid (Sil.); mobile (Lucr.), a wonderfully restless mind; a rushing course (Liv.); spontaneous (Ter.); light-footed (Var.); he is carried on with Pegasean flight, swifter; swiftest (Plin.); a flying onset (Cic.); winged (Sil., a play on words).

units.la: Agitare perpetuo] Esse in jugi agitatione.
units.tr: Agitare perpetuo: to be in constant motion.

units.la: Agnatus] Frater cognatione. Patruelis, Cic.
units.tr: Agnatus: a brother by kinship; a paternal cousin (Cic.).

units.la: Agnoscere seipsum] In se descendere.
units.tr: Agnoscere seipsum: to go down into oneself.

units.la: Agnus] Agnellus, Plaut. Agnus tener, Virg. Lactens, Ovid. Novella agna, Id. Avilla, Fest.
units.tr: Agnus: a little lamb (Plaut.); a tender lamb (Virg.); a suckling (Ovid.); a young ewe (Ovid.); a little ewe (Fest.).

units.la: Agrarius] Lex agraria, Liv. Agrosus homo, Var. Glebarius bos, Id. Arvales fratres. Sacerdotes pro frugibus arvorum. Sacra procurantes apud Ethnicos.
units.tr: Agrarius: an agrarian law (Liv.); a man devoted to the land (Var.); an ox for breaking clods (Id.); the Arval brothers, priests for the fruits of the fields; those who performed sacred rites among the heathen.

units.la: Agrestis] Silvestris herba (opposita hortensi), Plin. Fera vitis, Silen. Turneb. Scal. Agrestis arbor, Cic. Campester & campestris, Cic. Agrios, Graeca voce saepe utitur Plinius.
units.tr: Agrestis: wild herb, opposed to garden herb (Plin.); wild vine (Silen., Turneb., Scal.); a wild tree (Cic.); campester and campestris, of the plain (Cic.). Agrios: Pliny often uses this Greek word.

units.la: Agricola] Arator, Cic. Agricultor. Cultor agrorum, Liv. Cultor terrae, Cic. Liv. Colonus, Cic. Virg. Moderator aratri, Lucr. Politor (scil. agrorum) Cato Vlp. Subarator, Plin. Sulcator, Silius transtulit alio. Obstetricator terrae. Foenerator Deo. Imporcitor, Fest.
units.tr: Agricola: a ploughman (Cic.); a farmer; a tiller of the fields (Liv.); a tiller of the earth (Cic., Liv.); a husbandman (Cic., Virg.); a steerer of the plough (Lucr.); a polisher (sc. of fields) (Cato, Ulp.); an under-ploughman (Plin.); a furrower, transferred elsewhere by Silius; a midwife of the earth; a usurer to God; an imporcitor (Fest.).

units.la: Agricolaris] Georgicus. Colonius, Col. Agricolare opus, Pallad. Aratricus, Varr. Aratrica corona.
units.tr: Agricolaris: georgic; a farmer's (Col.); agricultural work (Pallad.); of the plough (Varr.); a plough-crown.

units.la: Agricultura] Agricultura nil dulcius, Cic. Doctores agricolationis non cognovi, Col. Agricultio, Cic. Ars agriculturae, Varr. Rusticationis scientia.
units.tr: Agricultura: nothing is sweeter than agriculture (Cic.); I have not known teachers of husbandry (Col.); husbandry (Cic.); the art of agriculture (Varr.); the knowledge of country life.

units.la: Ah!] Aha, Plaut. Eheu, Cic. Hei, heu, Atat, Ter. Pro vel Proh, Ovid. vid. Heu Miserum.
units.tr: Ah!: aha (Plaut.); alas (Cic.); oh, alas, atat (Ter.); pro or proh, oh (Ovid.). See Heu Miserum.

units.la: Ajunt] Traditur, Cic. Liv. Fertur, Cic. Virg. Produnt. Proditur. Refertur. Pronunciatur. Narrant solvi metum, Plin. Memorant. Fama fert, Liv. Nunciatur. Dicitur. Ferunt. Perhibent. Perhibentur fuisse. Jactatur vulgò. Multus sermo est. Prædicant. Increbuit sermo nonnullorum. Percrebuit sermone omnium. Perferuntur sermones. Perfertur sermone. Sermo monet. Sermo est, Cic. Sunt quidam authores Liv. Dispersus sine authore sermo Quint. Sermo promanaverat, Sen. Sunt, qui authores sint, Liv.
units.tr: Ajunt: it is handed down (Cic., Liv.); it is reported (Cic., Virg.); they put forward; it is made known; it is brought back; it is proclaimed; they tell that fear was relieved (Plin.); they relate; rumour reports (Liv.); it is announced; it is said; they say; they assert it was so; it is commonly bandied about; there is much talk; they declare; the talk of some has grown; the talk has spread among everyone; reports are spread about; the talk warns; it is said (Cic.); there are certain authors (Liv.); talk spread without an author (Quint.); talk had spread abroad (Sen.); there are those who are the authors (Liv.).

units.la: Ala] Alæ, Virg. Pennæ. Pinnæ apum, infectorum. Membranaceæ pinnæ vespertilionum. Crusta, tutela pennis scarabæorum, Plin. Remigium alarum.
units.tr: Ala: wings (Virg.); feathers; the wings of bees and insects; the membranous wings of bats; the shell or protective wing-case of beetles (Plin.); the rowing-bench of the wings.

units.la: Alabastrites] Lapis ex marmoris genere, Plin. Onyx, Id.
units.tr: Alabastrites: a stone of the marble kind (Plin.); onyx (Id.).

units.la: Alacer] Promptus & alacris animus ad aliquid. Vegetus ad. Ardens & erectus ad, Cic. Accinctus, Petron. Strenuus, Col. Strenuissimi milites, Col. Plin. Impiger, Plaut. Gnavus, Ovid. Navus, Cic. Excitatus, Id. Benignus, Cic. Alte cinctus. Cursu valet.
units.tr: Alacer: a mind ready and eager for something; lively towards; burning and roused towards (Cic.); girded (Petron.); vigorous (Col.); very vigorous soldiers (Col., Plin.); tireless (Plaut.); keen (Ovid.); active (Cic.); aroused (Id.); kind (Cic.); girded high; strong in running.

units.la: Alacritas] Navitas. Impigritas, Cic. Vigor inest juventæ, Liv. Alacris animus. Animi incitatio & alacritas innata hominibus, Cæf. Strenuitas, Ovid.
units.tr: Alacritas: readiness; eagerness (Cic.); vigour is in youth (Liv.); a lively mind; the stirring and liveliness innate in men (Caes.); vigour (Ovid.).

units.la: Alacriter] Alacrè compellare, Plaut. Promptissimè, Plin. Acri ac prompto ore ac vultu. Studiosè. Non gravatè. Benignè aliquid polliceri. Benignissimè communicare. Prolixè, libenter, celeriter facere. Strenuè accepi tuas literas. Officiosè parere. Pleno gradu ingredi. Ingenti alacritate sublatus clamor, Liv. Prosequi sedulò faciebat, Ter. Pro se quisque omnes per æqua, & iniqua loca pervadant, Liv. Non ingratè, Plin. Calet res. Actuosè agere, Cic.
units.tr: Alacriter: to address cheerfully (Plaut.); most readily (Plin.); with a keen and ready face and look; eagerly; not reluctantly; to promise kindly; to share most generously; to do a thing lavishly, willingly and quickly; I have received your letter with zeal; to obey dutifully; to walk with a full step; a shout raised with great eagerness (Liv.); he was accustomed to attend to him diligently (Ter.); each man presses on through level and rough places alike (Liv.); not ungraciously (Plin.); the matter is heating up; to act actively (Cic.).

units.la: Alapa] Colaphus, Spart. Plaga incussa colapho. Os hominis palmâ excussissimâ pulsat, Petron. (Alapa fit palmâ :/: explicatâ manu : Colaphus digitis in pugnum compressis.)
units.tr: Alapa: a cuff (Spart.); a blow struck with a clenched fist; he strikes a man's face with an outstretched palm (Petron.). (An alapa is made with the open palm; a colaphus with the fingers closed into a fist.)

units.la: Alaris, ad alas spectans] Alariæ cohortes, Liv. Alaris, Tacit.
units.tr: Alaris, ad alas spectans: wing cohorts (Liv.); of the wings (Tacit.).

units.la: Alatus] Pennatus equus, Plin. Penniger, Cic. Pinnatus Cupido, Id. Aliger amor. Aligerum agmen, Virg. Alifer currus, Ovid. Alipes equus, Virg. Ales equus, Ovid. Pegasus ales, Hor. Pennipes, Catul. Præpes victoria, Ausón. i. e. pennata.) (Prisci enim victoriam pinxere pennatam.) Pterotos calix, Plin. :/: ansatus.
units.tr: Alatus: a winged horse (Plin.); feather-bearing (Cic.); winged Cupid (Cic.); winged love; a winged host (Virg.); a winged chariot (Ovid.); a wing-footed horse (Virg.); a winged horse (Ovid.); Pegasus the winged (Hor.); wing-footed (Catul.); winged Victory (Ausonius), that is, feathered (for the ancients painted Victory winged). A pterotos cup (Plin.), winged, that is, with handles.

units.la: Alauda] Non cristata, Aldrovand. Gesner.
units.tr: Alauda: not crested (Aldrovand., Gesner).

units.la: Albare] Dealbare, Cic. Inalbare, Apul. Incretare, Petron. Candidare, Pompon. Candificare, Næv. Candefacere, Plaut.
units.tr: Albare: to whiten (Cic.); to whiten over (Apul.); to whiten with chalk (Petron.); to make white (Pompon.); to make bright (Naev.); to make white (Plaut.).

units.la: Albedo] Albitudo, Plaut. Albor, Var. Candor nivis, Virg.
units.tr: Albedo: whiteness (Plaut.); whiteness (Var.); the snowy whiteness (Virg.).

units.la: Albere] Albicare, Plin. Inalbere, Apul. Candicare, Plin. Candet ebur, Catul. Canescit flos, Plin. Canet herba gelu, Sil.
units.tr: Albere: to grow whitish (Plin.); to whiten over (Apul.); to glow white (Plin.); ivory gleams white (Catul.); the flower greys (Plin.); the grass whitens with frost (Sil.).

units.la: Albidus] Albidulus, Pallad. Exalbidus. Subalbidus, Plin. Subalbicans, Var. Albineus color equi, Pallad.
units.tr: Albidus: whitish (Pallad.); somewhat white (Plin.); slightly white (Var.); a whitish colour of a horse (Pallad.).

units.la: Alburnum] Adeps arboris. Caro arboris. Pulpa arboris, Plin.
units.tr: Alburnum: the fat of a tree; the flesh of a tree; the pulp of a tree (Plin.).

units.la: Alea] Sonat alea fritillis, Mart. Tessera, Cic. Jacere tesseras. Numeri eburni, Ovid. Lepusculi. Jacula, Isid.
units.tr: Alea: the dice rattle in the dice-box (Mart.); a die (Cic.); to throw dice; ivory counters (Ovid.); little hares; missiles (Isid.).

units.la: Aleator] Aleo, Fest. Deditissimus aleæ, Suet. Aleâ lendi artifex, Plutar. Tesserarius, Amm. Effusus in lusum.
units.tr: Aleator: a gambler (Fest.); most addicted to dice (Suet.); skilled in dice-playing (Plut.); a dice-player (Amm.); given over to play.

units.la: Alembicum] Æolipyla, Vitruv. (ἡ αἰολικπύλη, quasi venti porta, Philord. Cardan.) Vesica metallica, Matthiol. Clibanus, Bud. Turbo, Jun. Meta furnaria, Id. Nola vitrea. Conceptaculum, Cardan. Diploma, Caes. Jun. Balneum maris, Offic. Balneum Mariæ, Cardan. & Matthio.
units.tr: Alembicum: an aeolipile (Vitruv.), from the Greek, as if the gate of the wind (Philord., Cardan.); a metal bladder (Matthiol.); a still-head (Bud.); a whirl (Jun.); a furnace-cap (Id.); a glass flask (Cardan.); a receptacle (Cardan.); a double vessel (Caes., Jun.); a sea-bath (Offic.); a Mary's bath (Cardan. and Matthiol.).

units.la: Alere] Nutrire, Ovid. Pax nutrit Cererem. Sustentare, Cic. Sustineo milites piscæ, Liv. Educat aliquem ager, Martial. Alere & majus facere aliquid, Cic. Alere facundiam, vires augere eloquentiæ, Quint. Memoriam, ingeniumque assidua exercitatio alit. Corporis vires labor modicus alit. Lenis alit flammas, grandior aura necat, Ovid.
units.tr: Alere: to nourish (Ovid.); peace nourishes Ceres; to sustain (Cic.); I sustain the soldiers with fish (Liv.); the land feeds someone (Martial.); to nourish and make something greater (Cic.); to foster eloquence, to increase the strength of eloquence (Quint.); constant exercise nourishes memory and talent; moderate labour nourishes bodily strength; a gentle breeze feeds flames, a stronger wind kills them (Ovid.).

units.la: Alescere] Alescendo roborari, Var. Adolescere, Tacit.
units.tr: To grow up] To be strengthened by nourishing, Var. To grow up, Tacit.

units.la: Alga] Fucus marinus. Alga marina, Plin. Theriaca maris, Plin.
units.tr: Alga] Sea-weed. Sea-weed, Plin. Sea theriac, Plin.

units.la: Algere] vid. Frigere.
units.tr: Algere] See Frigere.

units.la: Alias] Sed de hoc alias, Cic. (Alteras, pro alias, Fest. priscum) Alio die, tempore, congressu. Alia, vel altera vice, Liv. Hor.
units.tr: Alias] But of this, another time, Cic. (Alteras, for alias, is an old usage, Fest.) On another day, at another time, at another meeting. Another time, or a second turn, Liv. Hor.

units.la: Alias-alias] Aliquando quidem. Aliquando vero. Modo huc, modo illuc. Modo unum, tum autem plures Deos dicere. Alias beatus, alias miser, Cic. Interdum relinquere, concludere alias. Nonnunquam. Aliquando. Interdum, Cic. Interim interim, Quint.
units.tr: Alias-alias] Sometimes indeed. Sometimes truly. Now here, now there. Now to say there is one god, now several gods. Sometimes happy, sometimes wretched, Cic. To leave off now and then, to shut up at other times. Not infrequently. Sometimes. Now and then, Cic. Meanwhile, meanwhile, Quint.

units.la: Alibi] Aliubi, Plin. Rubus in Ida non alias nascitur, Id. Alibi gentium & Civitatum, Apul.
units.tr: Alibi] Elsewhere, Plin. The bramble on Ida does not grow anywhere else, Id. Elsewhere among the nations and states, Apul.

units.la: Alicubi] Nonnusquam, Plin. Est ubi, Hor.
units.tr: Alicubi] Somewhere or other, Plin. There is a place where, Hor.

units.la: Aliena vitia videns, non sua] In alienis vitiis oculatus, in propriis Tiresia caecior. Alienas observans papulas, ipse ulceribus obsitus. Aliorum medicus, ipse vulneribus scatet, Er. Cum tua pervideas oculis mala lippus inunctis, Cur in amicorum vitiis tam cernis acutum? Hor.
units.tr: Aliena vitia videns, non sua] Sharp-eyed for others' faults, blinder than Tiresias for his own. Inspecting others' pimples, himself covered with sores. A physician to others, he himself is full of wounds, Er. When with bleary eyes smeared with ointment you can see through your own faults, why are you so keen-sighted over your friends' faults? Hor.

units.la: Alieni arbitrii] Ab alieno pendet suffragio, Sen. Arbitrio carens suo. Semiliber, Cic.
units.tr: Alieni arbitrii] Depending on another's vote, Sen. Lacking his own judgement. Half-free, Cic.

units.la: In Aliena se ingerere] Falcem in alienam messem mittere. In alieno choro pedem ponere. Ne sutor ultra crepidam, Er. Adag.
units.tr: In Aliena se ingerere] To put one's sickle into another's harvest. To set one's foot in another's dance. Let the cobbler stick to his last, Er. Adag.

units.la: Alienis uti pro suis] Petere ex alieno littore gemmas.
units.tr: Alienis uti pro suis] To seek gems on another's shore.

units.la: Alienus] Alienum, Subst. Salust. Externa causa, Cic. Exter honos, Stat. Extrarius canis, Suet. Extraneus heres, Id.
units.tr: Alienus] Something belonging to another, Sallust. A foreign cause, Cic. Foreign honour, Stat. A stranger's dog, Suet. A foreign heir, Id.

units.la: Alibilis, vim alendi habens] Alibile lac. Var. Altilis sanguis. Robustus cibus. Firmior ex frumento potio, quo firmius ipsum frumentum fuit. Valentissimum voco, in quo plurimum est nutrimenti, Cels.
units.tr: Alibilis, vim alendi habens] Nourishing milk, Var. Rich blood. Robust food. A drink made from grain, the stronger the more strongly the grain itself was. I call most powerful that in which there is most nourishment, Cels.

units.la: Alimentum] Alimonium apum, mel, Varr. Annona latis, Id. Res frumentaria, Cic. Copiae. Val. Max. Victus, Virg. Hor. Sal, elementum necessarium, i. e. alimentum, Plin. Omni frugalitate absumptâ, Apul. i. e. frugibus, victu. Cibaria. Commeatus, Cic. Utensilia, quae apes in alvearia congerunt, Col. Utensile non nascitur, Var. i. e. eduliae, Bud. ex Liv. Utensilia, ex quibus alitur hominum genus, Col Pabulum, Lucr. Pastus, Cic. Esca, Liv.
units.tr: Alimentum] Food of bees, honey, Varr. Grain supply, Id. Provisions of corn, Cic. Supplies, Val. Max. Victuals, Virg. Hor. Salt, a necessary element, that is, nourishment, Plin. With all thrift used up, Apul. that is, with grain and victuals. Provisions. Supplies, Cic. Stores which bees gather into the hives, Col. Necessaries do not grow, Var. that is, edibles, Bud. from Liv. Necessaries by which the human race is fed, Col. Fodder, Lucr. Pasture, Cic. Food, Liv.

units.la: Alimentis opus est] Aurâ victitare non licet.
units.tr: Alimentis opus est] It is not possible to live on air alone.

units.la: Alimentarius] Victualis, Apul.
units.tr: Alimentarius] Relating to victuals, Apul.

units.la: Alimonia in certum tempus admensa] Diurnum, Sen. Diarium, Mart. Cibus diurnus, Claud. Justa, orum. Colum. Demensum, Plaut. Sportula, (pro cibo in sportulam imponi solito) Mart. Visceratio populo data. id est, Carnis distributio facta, Cic. Sipont.
units.tr: Alimonia in certum tempus admensa] Daily allowance, Sen. Daily pay, Mart. Daily food, Claud. Due measures, Colum. Food measured out, Plaut. Dole (food customarily put into the basket), Mart. A distribution of meat given to the people, that is, a distribution of flesh made, Cic. Sipont.

units.la: Alio] Alio transferre, Cic. Aliorsum, Alioversum, Plaut. Altrorsus, & Alterorsus discludere, Apul.
units.tr: Alio] To transfer elsewhere, Cic. In the other direction, Plaut. To separate in opposite directions, Apul.

units.la: Alioqui] Alio clarus, Tacit. Alias res est impensè improbus, Plaut. Vitruv. Cætera egregium secutus, Liv. Cætera, Hor. Cæterum. Cæteroqui. De cætero, Cic. Reliquum, Plaut. Vir alias doctissimus, Macrob.
units.tr: Alioqui] Famous for other things, Tacit. He is otherwise utterly wicked, Plaut. Vitruv. Otherwise following an outstanding course, Liv. In other respects, Hor. Otherwise. Otherwise. For the rest, Cic. What remains, Plaut. A man otherwise most learned, Macrob.

units.la: Aliquandiu] Aliquantisper, Plaut. Paulisper, Cic. Paululum, Ter. Ad tempus: Cic. Ad breve, & ad brevissimum tempus. Ad punctum temporis. Parumper, Cic. Nunc te marmoreum pro tempore fecimus, Virg. Paulò amplius. Tantisper. Perpusillum, Cic.
units.tr: Aliquandiu] For a little while, Plaut. For a short while, Cic. A little, Ter. For the time being, Cic. For a short and the shortest time. At a point of time. For a little, Cic. Now for the moment we have made you marble, Virg. A little longer. For so long. Very little, Cic.

units.la: Aliquando] Quandoque. Quandocunque. Aliquando tandem. Nonnunquam, interdum, Cic. Quondam etiam victis redit in præcordia virtus, Virg. Est quando, (sicut, est ubi, est cur, est unde) Cic. Est cùm, Lucr. Si forte, si quando, &c. Temporis progressu, Cic.
units.tr: Aliquando] At some time. Whenever. At last, at some time. Now and then, sometimes, Cic. Sometimes even virtue returns to the hearts of the conquered, Virg. There is a time when (as there is a place where, a reason why, a place whence), Cic. There is when, Lucr. If perchance, if ever, etc. In the course of time, Cic.

units.la: Aliquantum] Paululum, Aliquantulum æris, Cic. Non nihil, Id. Haud nihil, Liv. Aliquammultum, Apul. Nonnihil, Vopisc. Aliquantillum, Plin. Non ita multum, Cic. Aliquid fessus, Plin. Hillum, hilum, En. C.Aliquo multum, Apul.
units.tr: Aliquantum] A little; a little money, Cic. Not nothing, Id. Not nothing at all, Liv. Somewhat much, Apul. Somewhat, Vopisc. A little, Plin. Not so very much, Cic. Somewhat weary, Plin. A hair's breadth, a jot, Enn. Somewhat much, Apul.

units.la: Aliquantò] Paulò amplius. Paulum immutatus, Cic. Nec nimio plus, Lucr. Non ita multò post, Liv. Non ita diu post. Nec ita longo intervallo venit, Cic. Non nimio post, Lucr. Exiguò post, Plin.
units.tr: Aliquantò] A little more. Changed a little, Cic. Not much more, Lucr. Not so very long after, Liv. Not so long afterwards. He came not after so long an interval, Cic. Not long after, Lucr. A little after, Plin.

units.la: Aliquid] Quidpiam, vel Quippiam, Ter. Quicquam, Cic. Quicque. Quint. Ne quid, Hor. Neque nihil, neque omnia.
units.tr: Aliquid] Something, Ter. Anything, Cic. Whatever, Quint. Lest anything, Hor. Neither nothing nor everything.

units.la: Aliquid, cum Emphasi] Est quiddam, Cic. Aliquid est, Plaut. Quod certè est, Virg. Scilicet aliquid magnum est. Haud nihil.
units.tr: Aliquid, cum Emphasi] There is something, Cic. Something exists, Plaut. Which surely is something, Virg. Surely something great it is. Not nothing.

units.la: Aliquis] Quis, Plin. Iun. Aperite quis, Plaut,Ter. Quisquam. quam. Si ullus me vocabit,Ter. Nonnullus,Cic. Quisquam omnium,Id. Quisquam unus, Liv. Quò quisque est ingeniosior, Cic. Nemo; Contigit tibi, quod haud scio an nemini, id est, alicui, Cic. Si quis me quæret, inde vocatote aliqui, id est, aliquis, Plaut. Est qui, Hor. Unus aliquis. Quodpiam, aliquod membrum, Cic. Quispiam. Nescio quis, Plaut.
units.tr: Aliquis] Anyone, Plin. Iun. Open up, whoever you are, Plaut., Ter. Anyone at all. If anyone at all will call me, Ter. Some, Cic. Anyone at all of them, Id. One alone, Liv. The more ingenious each one is, Cic. No one. It has happened to you, which I know not whether has happened to anyone, that is, to someone, Cic. If anyone asks for me, call me from there, someone, that is, aliquis, Plaut. There is one who, Hor. Some single one. Some part, some member, Cic. Someone or other. I know not who, Plaut.

units.la: Aliquorsum] Aliquò militatum profugiet, Ter. Si deducta est usquam gentium, Plaut. Nec usquam discedebam, Cic. Iturane es quopiam? Ter. Quoquam. Uspiam, Cic.
units.tr: Aliquorsum] He fled to serve somewhere as a soldier, Ter. If she has been taken anywhere in the world, Plaut. I did not go away anywhere, Cic. Are you going anywhere? Ter. Whither? Anywhere, Cic.

units.la: Aliquot] Aliquos viginti dies, Plaut. Aliquammulti, Cic. Aliquotfariam, Var. Sex aut septem, Ter. Horat. (Numerus certus, pro incerto, sed proportiones habente. Nam pro aliquot centenis, dicunt Latini sexcenti, sex aut septem centuriæ &c. vel sexies aut septies deni, centeni.) Aliquantis diebus refrigerentur, pro aliquot, Pallad.
units.tr: Aliquot] Some twenty days, Plaut. Several, Cic. Some, in parts, Var. Six or seven, Ter. Hor. (A definite number used for an indefinite one, yet keeping proportions. For the Latins say sexcenti, six hundred, for some hundreds, and so six or seven centuries, or six or seven times ten, a hundred.) Let them be cooled for some days, for some, Pallad.

units.la: Aliquoties] Semel atque iterum.
units.tr: Aliquoties] Once and again.

units.la: Aliquousque] Usque eò, quò opus erit, Cic. Eâtenus, quâ, Col. Eâtenus quoad licebit. Quatenus fieri poterit, Er.
units.tr: Aliquousque] As far as there is need, Cic. As far as, Col. As far as it will be permitted. As far as it can be done, Er.

units.la: Aliter] Secus ac, Cic. Secius, Var. Tacit. Fingere alia omnia, Sallust. Diversè, Gell. Alio pacto, Plaut. Aliuta, pro aliter, Fest. Plaut.
units.tr: Aliter] Otherwise than, Cic. Otherwise, Var. Tacit. To feign everything else, Sallust. Differently, Gell. In another way, Plaut. Otherwise, for aliter, Fest. Plaut.

units.la: Aliter quàm] Secus quam, Cic. Secus ac, atque. Aliter ac, atque, Id. Aliorsum, atque ego feci, accepit, Ter. Aliter olim & nunc, Var. Contrà ac liceret. Contrà atque oporteret. Contrà quàm fas erat, Cic. Adversum quod me obsecravit, Plaut.
units.tr: Aliter quàm] Otherwise than, Cic. Otherwise than, as. Otherwise than, Id. He received it differently from how I did, Ter. Otherwise then and now, Var. Contrary to what was permitted. Contrary to what was right. Contrary to what was lawful, Cic. Against what he begged of me, Plaut.

units.la: Aliter atque aliter] vid. Diversè.
units.tr: Aliter atque aliter] See Diversè.

units.la: Aliunde] Aliunde accersitus. Foris assumere, Cic. Peregrè accire, Liv.
units.tr: Aliunde] Summoned from elsewhere. To take in from outside, Cic. To summon from abroad, Liv.

units.la: Alius] Alius es multò quam soles. Præter te neminem habeo reliquum, Cic. Et cætera ejusdem generis, Id. Alia his, Plaut.
units.tr: Alius] You are far other than you usually are, Cic. I have no one left besides you, Id. And other things of the same kind, Id. Others besides these, Plaut.

units.la: Alia aliis conveniunt] Alia alios delectant. Equus quadrigis, aratro bos.
units.tr: Alia aliis conveniunt] Different things delight different people. A horse suits the chariot, an ox the plough.

units.la: Alii alios instruere possumus] Ferrum ferro acuitur.
units.tr: We can instruct one another] Iron is sharpened by iron.

units.la: Alius modi] Non alius essem, atque nunc sum, Sallust. Multùm mutatus ab illo, Virg. Multùm distat ab illo, qui, Cic. Alimodi, Fest. Alter, Horat. Te speculo videris alterum, Lamb.
units.tr: Alius modi] I would not be other than I am now, Sallust. Much changed from that man, Virg. He is far different from him who, Cic. Of another kind, Fest. Another, Hor. You see yourself in the mirror as another, Lamb.

units.la: Allatrare] vide Oblatrare.
units.tr: Allatrare] See Oblatrare.

units.la: Allegare scil. exempla] Citare authores, Liv. Cito Senatum Philosophorum. Recitare alicujus testimonium. Proferre legem, Cic. Laudo testem Jovem, Plaut. Afferre rationem. Producere authores, testes, Cic.
units.tr: Allegare scil. exempla] To cite authors, Liv. I summon a senate of philosophers. To recite someone's testimony. To bring forward a law, Cic. I call Jove to witness, Plaut. To adduce a reason. To produce authors and witnesses, Cic.

units.la: Allegatio] Prolatio exemplorum, Cic.
units.tr: Allegatio] The adducing of examples, Cic.

units.la: Allegoria] Ambages allegoricæ, Arnob. Allegoricum genus, Id.
units.tr: Allegoria] Allegorical circumlocutions, Arnob. The allegorical kind, Id.

units.la: Allevare] In altum tollere. Vidi multos, quorum supercilia ad singulos vocis conatus allevarentur, Quint.
units.tr: Allevare] To lift up on high. I have seen many whose eyebrows were raised at every effort of the voice, Quint.

units.la: Alleviare] Levius reddere, Er.
units.tr: Alleviare] To make lighter, Er.

units.la: Allicere] Allectare, Col. Captare aliquem aliquo emolumento, Cic. Solicitare ad se aves, Plin. Invitare, Cic. Præclara ingenia gloriâ invitantur. Allicefacere, Suet. Admulcere illecebris ciborum aliquem. Devocare cœlo sidera, Hor. Delicere, Non. Trahere mentes artificio, Plin. Inescare homines, Ter.
units.tr: Allicere] To entice, Col. To win someone over by some advantage, Cic. To lure birds to oneself, Plin. To invite, Cic. Brilliant minds are invited by glory. To make attractive, Suet. To soothe someone with the allurements of food. To call the stars down from heaven, Hor. To charm, Non. To draw minds by art, Plin. To ensnare men, Ter.

units.la: Allidere] Illidere foribus caput, Suet. Offensare capita, Liv. Fligere, Lucr. Adstringere parieti, saxo, Stat.
units.tr: Allidere] To knock one's head against the doors, Suet. To bruise heads, Liv. To strike down, Lucr. To press against a wall or a rock, Stat.

units.la: Alligare] Deligare, Cic. Plaut. Adalligare aliquid brachio, Plin. Religare aliquid ad currum, Cic. Jugo ramus illigatur, Col. Superilligare, Plin. Annectere, Adstringere, Cic. Stringam te ad carnarium. Devinciam ad taurum, Plaut. Destinare aliquid loro ad ansulam, Apul. Areæ catenis destinandæ firmiter, Vitruv. Adjugare palmites. Injungere, Col.
units.tr: Alligare] To bind up, Cic. Plaut. To bind something to the arm, Plin. To tie something to a chariot, Cic. A branch is tied to the yoke, Col. To bind above, Plin. To join, to bind fast, Cic. I will bind you to the butcher's stall. I will tie you to the bull, Plaut. To fasten something to a little ring with a thong, Apul. Floors to be firmly fastened with chains, Vitruv. To yoke vine shoots. To enjoin, Col.

units.la: Allium] Alum, est allium sponte nascens in arvis, Plin. Allietum, Vlp. Col. Plin.
units.tr: Allium] Wild garlic: garlic growing of itself in the fields, Plin. A garlic bed, Vlp. Col. Plin.

units.la: Alloqui aliquem] Appellare. Compellare. Affari, Cic. Adire aliquem blandis verbis. Tecum ago. Tibi dico, Plaut. Adorat populum causidicus, Apul. Reus orat ad. Sermones dare. Lacessere.
units.tr: Alloqui aliquem] To address. To accost. To speak to, Cic. To approach someone with flattering words. I am speaking to you. I am saying it to you, Plaut. The advocate addresses the people, Apul. The accused pleads with... To hold conversations. To provoke.

units.la: Allocutio] Alloquium, Plin. Compellare, Cic, Affatus alicujus, Virg. Affamen, Apul.
units.tr: Address: a speaking to (Plin.); a calling to, addressing (Cic.); a speaking to someone (Virg.); an accosting (Apul.).

units.la: Alphabeta] vid. Abecede.
units.tr: Alphabet: see Abecede.

units.la: Alphabetarius puer ] Syllabarius. Hieron. Elementarius, Sen.
units.tr: Alphabet boy: a child at the syllabary, a beginner in spelling (Hieron.); a child in the rudiments, an elementary pupil (Sen.).

units.la: Alphabeticus ordo] Elementorum serie dispositus. Alphabeti ordine textus, Seneca vero dicit: Digerere in literas. pro Alphabeti ordine conscribere.
units.tr: Alphabetical order: arranged in the sequence of the letters. A text in alphabetical order; but Seneca says: to arrange under letters, to write down in alphabetical order.

units.la: Altare ] vid. Ara.
units.tr: Altar: see Ara.

units.la: Alte] Alte extollere, Cic. Altius efferre caput. Excelsius scandere. Sublimitate volitare, Caes. Sublime putrescere, Cic.
units.tr: High, on high: to raise on high (Cic.); to lift the head higher; to climb more loftily. To fly aloft with lofty flight (Caes.); to rot on high (Cic.).

units.la: Altercari] Altercari cum aliquo, Cic. Dum hujusmodi altercârunt sermonem. Alternant secum, Apul. Altercabilem conferre sermonem, Arnob. Conflictari verbis, Cic. Serram ducere cum aliquo. Quàm diu per hanc lineam serram contentionis reciprocabimus ? Contendere voce, verbis, Ter. Funem contentionis ducere, Hieron. Velitari verbis, Turpil. Labris inter se velitari, Afran. vid. Contendere.
units.tr: To dispute: to dispute with someone (Cic.); while they were disputing in this way; they argue among themselves (Apul.); to hold a contentious discourse (Arnob.); to clash in words (Cic.); to drag a saw with someone (to wrangle with someone). How long shall we keep sawing back and forth along this line of contention? To contend with voice or words (Ter.); to drag the rope of contention (Hieron.); to skirmish in words (Turpil.); to skirmish with lips against one another (Afran.); see Contendere.

units.la: Altercatio] Concertatio verborum, Amm. Estque benevolorum : Jurgium inimicorum.
units.tr: Dispute: a contest of words (Amm.). It is a thing of friends; a quarrel of enemies.

units.la: Alternare, per vices agere] Alternare vices, Ovid. Alternis agere. Alternatis nervis, vicibus, redire, Plin. Variare otium labore, laborem otio, Plin. Iun. Exercere, variare vices, Virg. Ducite sorte vices, Prop. Mutitamus, vel Mutitamur. Mutuamus, vel mutuamur ira, Plaut. Alternatione tractare, Macrob.
units.tr: To alternate, to act in turns: to alternate turns (Ovid.); to act alternately. To return with the sinews, the turns, alternately (Plin.); to vary leisure with labour and labour with leisure (Plin. Iun.); to exercise and vary turns (Virg.); draw lots for turns (Prop.); let us exchange, or let us be exchanged; let us lend, or let us borrow in anger (Plaut.); to handle by alternation (Macrob.).

units.la: Alternatim] Alternis annis, diebus, vicibus : & absolutè, Vicibus, Plin. & absol. Alternis. Alternis Catones, alternis Vatinii, Sen. Vicissim terra floret : Deinde horret, Cic. Per vices, Plin. Inque vicem, Virg.
units.tr: Alternately: in alternate years, days, turns; and absolutely, by turns (Plin.), and absolutely, alternately. Alternately Catos, alternately Vatinii (Sen.). The land blooms in turn, then freezes (Cic.); by turns (Plin.); in turn (Virg.).

units.la: Alternatio] Vices loquendi, Quint. Gratâ vice veris & Favonii, Hor. Vicissitudines laboris & voluptatis: dierum ac noctium, Cic.
units.tr: Alternation: turns of speaking (Quint.); the welcome turn of spring and the west wind (Hor.); the changes of labour and pleasure, of days and nights (Cic.).

units.la: Alternus] Alterna requies, Ovid. Alternata series, Sen. Alternans aqua, Prop. Alternis vicibus, vel alternâ vice contingens, faciens. Vicissitudinem habens. Vicissim respondens. Amoebaeum carmen, Fest. Successio per vices.
units.tr: Alternating: a alternating rest (Ovid.); an alternating series (Sen.); alternating water (Prop.); happening or doing in alternate turns, having a change, responding in turn. An antiphonal song (Fest.); succession by turns.

units.la: Alteruter] Alter vel alteruter, Absol. vel Alteruter ve-strûm, Cic. Alter è duobus, Quint. Si uter velit, Cic.
units.tr: One or the other: either, or one of the two (absolutely); or either of the two (Cic.); one of two (Quint.); if either wishes (Cic.).

units.la: Altilis, passivè] Altilis gallina, Plin. Saginatus, opimus bos, Var. Cellaris columbus, Col. Pafcualis, Douza. Pastus aper, Mart. Fartilis anser, Plin. Corpora pinguescere coacta, Sen. Fertus, Perf. (Altilia, sunt animalia, quæ inclusa aluntur, Var.)
units.tr: Fattened, in the passive sense: a fattened hen (Plin.); an ox fattened and rich (Var.); a cellar-fed pigeon (Col.); a pasture-fed (Douza); a fed boar (Mart.); a stuffed goose (Plin.); bodies forced to grow fat (Sen.); plump (Pers.). (Altilia are animals which are kept and fed while shut up, Var.)

units.la: Altitudo] Proceritas arborum, Excelsitas, Cic. Celsitudo corporis, Paterculus. Sublimitas cellæ, Col. Sublime. Aspice hoc sublime cadens, Col. Celsa montium, Amm. In cœlo sum, Cic. Celsum.
units.tr: Height: the tallness of trees, loftiness (Cic.); the height of the body (Paterculus); the height of a cell (Col.). Lofty. Behold this thing falling from on high (Col.); the heights of mountains (Amm.); I am in heaven (Cic.). High.

units.la: Altissimum quid] Cœlo tenus altum.
