units.tr: Something highest: lofty as far as heaven.

units.la: Alta captare] Humum vitando nubes & inania captare, Adag.
units.tr: To seize lofty things: avoiding the ground, to grasp at clouds and empty things (Adag.).

units.la: Altiora captu ne quæsiveris] Quæ supra nos, nihil ad nos.
units.tr: Do not seek things too high for your understanding: what is above us has nothing to do with us.

units.la: Alta sunt præcipitia] Plus habent ponderis ad ruinam, quæ sunt cæteris altiora.
units.tr: Heights are precipices: those things which are higher than the rest have more weight for the fall.

units.la: Altus] Præaltus. Celsus vertex montis, Cic. Excelsus mons, Plin. Præcelsus locus, Cic. Procerus, Cic. Elevatus, Capitol. Conspicuus, Quint. Colosseus, Suet. Sublimis vertex saxi, Cic. Prolixa arbor, Var. Sublimè fixus, Cic. Celsum caput, Sen.
units.tr: High: very high. A lofty mountain peak (Cic.); a high mountain (Plin.); a very lofty place (Cic.); tall (Cic.); raised up (Capitol.); conspicuous (Quint.); colossal (Suet.); the lofty peak of a rock (Cic.); a long-stretched tree (Var.); fixed on high (Cic.); a lofty head (Sen.).

units.la: Altus tonus in Musica] Symphoniæ pars puberum voce canenda. Symphoniæ pars, suprema virili voce cani solita.
units.tr: High tone in music: the part of a harmony to be sung with boys' voices. The part of a harmony usually sung with the highest male voice.

units.la: Altista] Occentorem vocat Iun. Qui Altum canit.
units.tr: Altus singer: Juvenal calls him a noisy singer, one who sings the high part.

units.la: Alvear] Alveare, Col. Alvearium, Var. Alveus, Plin. Congregatio apum mellificantium, Val.
units.tr: Beehive: a beehive (Col.); an apiary (Var.); a hive-trough (Plin.); a gathering of honey-making bees (Val.).

units.la: Alvearium] Locus qui multos habet apum alveos, Er. Vid. Apiarium.
units.tr: Apiary: a place that has many beehives (Erasm.). See Apiarium.

units.la: Alveolus] Tabula lateruncularia, Sen. Latruncularia, Pincian. Alveus lusorius. Alveolum, Plin. Abacus, Macrob. Abaco & latrunculis conterunt diem.
units.tr: Small board: a draughtboard for counters (Sen.); a counting-board for the game of latrunculi (Pincian.); a game-board. A little board (Plin.); an abacus (Macrob.). They wear out the day with the abacus and the draughtsmen.

units.la: Alveus in navi] Alveus, Salust. Liv. Carina, Cic. Virg. Tropis, Martial.
units.tr: Hold of a ship: a hold (Sall.; Liv.); the keel (Cic.; Virg.); the hull (Mart.).

units.la: Alveus, cavum terræ, per quod flumen decurrit] Nilus se condit alveo, Virg. Pleno fluit alveo, Quint. Fossa gurgitibus abundans, Cic.
units.tr: Channel, the hollow of the earth through which a river runs: the Nile hides itself in its channel (Virg.); flows in a full channel (Quint.); a ditch abounding in currents (Cic.).

units.la: Alumen] Stypteria, Vlp. Trichitis. Chalcitis, Plin. Lapis scissilis, Celf. Strongyle, Plin. Inertioris aluminis genus. Melinum optimum, à Melo insulâ, Plin.
units.tr: Alum: stypteria (Ulp.); trichitis; chalcitis (Plin.); a splitting stone (Cels.); strongyle (Plin.), a kind of less pure alum. The best melinum, from the island of Melos (Plin.).

units.la: Aluminatus] Exaluminatus, Plin.
units.tr: Alumed: thoroughly alumed (Plin.).

units.la: Alumnus] Altus alieno sumptu, Var. Merendarius, Sen. Nutrimenta, quae in exitium suae patriae converterentur, digna, Val. M. De filiis Annibalis.
units.tr: Foster-child: one reared at another's expense (Var.); one who eats a meal at another's table (Sen.); nourishments that would be turned to the ruin of their own country, worthy (Val. Max., concerning the sons of Hannibal).

units.la: Alvus] vid. Venter.
units.tr: Belly: see Venter.

units.la: Alvus cita] Alvus liquida, Celf. Profluvium alvi, Col. Resolutio alvi, Celf. Lienteria, Id. Diarrhoea. Praeceps alvi exinanitio Plin. Coeliacus morbus Celf. Rheumatismus ventris, Plin. Proluvies alvi, Lucr. Pantices, Fest. Fluxus ventris, Sipont. Laxamentum ventris comitatum timorem, Macrob. Facilis uterus.
units.tr: Quick bowel (diarrhoea): a liquid bowel (Cels.); a flux of the bowels (Col.); a loosening of the bowels (Cels.); lientery (Id.), diarrhoea; a headlong evacuation of the bowels (Plin.); celiac disease (Cels.); a rheumatism of the belly (Plin.); a washing out of the bowels (Lucr.); pantices (Fest.); a flux of the belly (Sipont.); an easing of the belly with accompanying fear (Macrob.); an easy belly.

units.la: Alvus dura] Hor. Alvus adstrictior. Venter suppressus, Celf.
units.tr: Hard bowel (constipation): Horace: a more constricted bowel. A suppressed belly (Cels.).

units.la: Alvi causa aliquid dare alicui] Decoctum ad catapotia, solvendae alvi gratiâ, Plin.
units.tr: To give something to someone for the sake of the bowels: a decoction into pills, for the sake of loosening the bowels (Plin.).

units.la: Alvum bonam facit] Alvum aliquid movet, ciet, Plin. Cato. Purgat, solvit alvum, Plin.
units.tr: Makes the bowels good: moves or stirs the bowels (Plin.; Cato); purges, loosens the bowels (Plin.).

units.la: Alvum dejicere] Purgari per alvum, Plin. Perpurgat se cervae herbulâ, Cic. Alvum clysmo trahere, Scribon. Perluit se Ibis, Plin. Ducere, Subducere, Movere alvum, Celf. Ciere, Inanire alvum, Plin. vid. Exinanitio alvi.
units.tr: To void the bowels: to be purged through the bowels (Plin.); a deer purges itself with a little herb (Cic.); to draw the bowels with an enema (Scribon.); the ibis washes itself (Plin.); to draw, to withdraw, to move the bowels (Cels.); to stir up, to empty the bowels (Plin.). See Exinanitio alvi.

units.la: Amabilis à primo conspectu] In ostio formosus.
units.tr: Lovable at first sight: handsome in the doorway.

units.la: Amabilis] Gratiosus apud omnes. Cic. Inspirans tacitum amorem, Claud. Jactans è toto pectore amorem, Lucr. Omnes attrahens, ut Magnes lapis ferrum, vel Caecias nubem.
units.tr: Lovable: agreeable to all (Cic.); breathing a silent love (Claud.); pouring forth love from the whole breast (Lucr.); drawing all to itself, as the magnet stone draws iron, or amber draws a cloud.

units.la: Amabilitas] Amantia, Plaut. Venus. Venustas. Lepor, Illecebra, in bonam partem, Cic.
units.tr: Lovableness: lovingness (Plaut.); Venus; charm; grace, allurement, in a good sense (Cic.).

units.la: Amanter] Peramanter. Amantissimè, Cic. Non ingratè nominare aliquem, Plin. Favorabiliter, Quint. Amabiliter, Hor.
units.tr: Lovingly: very lovingly. Most lovingly (Cic.); to name someone not ungratefully (Plin.); favourably (Quint.); lovably (Hor.).

units.la: Amanuensis] Amanuensis, Suet. Ab Epistolis, Id. A Commentariis, Hier. Commentariensis, Ascon. Librarius, Cic. Literae librarii manu. Librarius ad manum, Lavin. Librariolus, riolus, Cic. Scriptor & lector alicujus. Domesticarum rerum scriptores, Cic. Scriba Regis, Liv. Servus à manu, Suet.
units.tr: Amanuensis: amanuensis (Suet.); secretary for letters (Id.); secretary of records (Hier.); commentariensis (Ascon.); a copyist, a scribe (Cic.); a writing in a copyist's hand; a scribe at hand (Lavin.); a little copyist (Cic.); a writer and reader of someone. Writers of domestic affairs (Cic.); the king's scribe (Liv.); a slave for the hand (Suet.).

units.la: Amare] Amore amare. Amare oculitus, Cic. In oculis gerere. In sinu habere. Teneri alicujus amore, Ovid. Amore prosequi, amplecti. Habere amorem in, erga, aliquem. Amplexari. Carum habere. In manibus habere. Fovere. Diligere. Colere, Cic. Complecti charitate, Liv. Piare, id est, pie amare, Non. In charitate est apud me, Liv. Residet in me amor erga te, Cic. Oculi mei habitant in aliquo, Er. Unice te diligit. Amat effusissime. Charissimum habet. Admirandâ quadam charitate prosequitur. Animo toto te complectitur. Oculis atque animo fert hominem. Ex animo tibi bene vult, bene cupit. Te habet in deliciis, oblectamentis, Er. Affectus est illi, Suet. Pronus, Id. Omnia exosculatur. Amantissimus est tui. Effusissime te diligit, Er.
units.tr: To love: to love with love; to love with the eyes (Cic.); to keep in the eyes; to hold in the bosom; to be held tenderly by someone's love (Ovid.); to pursue with love, to embrace. To have love for, towards, someone. To embrace. To hold dear; to hold in the hands; to cherish; to delight in; to cultivate (Cic.); to embrace with affection (Liv.); to love piously, that is, to love devotedly (Non.); you have a place in my affection (Liv.); my love towards you dwells in me (Cic.); my eyes dwell upon someone (Erasm.). He loves you singularly. He loves most abundantly. He holds him most dear. He pursues him with a certain wondrous affection. He embraces you with his whole soul. He bears the man in his eyes and mind. He wishes you well from the heart, desires your good. He holds you in delights and pleasures (Erasm.). He was attached to him (Suet.); inclined (Id.). He kisses everything. He is most fond of you. He loves you most devotedly (Erasm.).

units.la: Amare perditè aliquem] Vide deamare.
units.tr: To love to ruin someone: see deamare.

units.la: Amans aliquid, non benè judicat] Nævos non videt amor, quia oculis captus.
units.tr: A lover does not judge well of something: love does not see the blemishes, being blinded in the eyes.

units.la: Amari tutius, quàm metui] Amor optimum satellitium, Lud. Viv.
units.tr: Safer to be loved than feared: love is the best bodyguard (Lud. Viv.).

units.la: Amarescere] Inamarescere, Hor. Amarorem concipere, ex Græco, Amaricari, Apoc. 10. 10.
units.tr: To become bitter: to become very bitter (Hor.); to conceive bitterness, from the Greek, to be made bitter (Apoc. 10.10).

units.la: Amarior, quàm dulcior] Plus aloës, quàm mellis habet.
units.tr: More bitter than sweet: has more aloes than honey.

units.la: Amaror] Amaritudo, Plin. Amarities, Catul. Amaritas, Vitr. Virus, Cic. Plin.
units.tr: Bitterness: bitterness (Plin.); bitterness (Catul.); bitterness (Vitr.); poison (Cic.; Plin.).

units.la: Amarus] Amaricans, Gaz. Tristis succus, Virg. Triste absinthium, Ovid. Gelli. Amarulentus. Sardois herbis amarior. Helleboro amarior, Er.
units.tr: Bitter: bitter-tasting (Gaz.); a bitter juice (Virg.); bitter wormwood (Ovid.; Gell.); somewhat bitter; bitterer than Sardinian herbs; more bitter than hellebore (Erasm.).

units.la: Amator] Tuus non tantùm amicus, sed amator. Inflammatus amore in patriam, Cic. Dilector, Apul. Cultor Minervæ, Hor. Cupidus. Cupidissimus. Studiosus, studiosissimus mei, Cic. Sauciusamore.
units.tr: Lover: your not only friend, but lover. Inflamed with love of the fatherland (Cic.); a devotee (Apul.); a worshipper of Minerva (Hor.); eager; most eager; a devoted follower of mine (Cic.); wounded with love.

units.la: Ambages] Circuitu ad aliquid pervenire, Quint. Nihil circuitione usus es, Ter. Anfractus, vel amfractus orationis, Cic. Ambago viarum, Prud. Mæander, vel Mæandrus, Col. Mæandri more, i.e. flexuosè. (A fluvio hujus nominis minis flexuoso.) Quos tu Mæandros, quas flexiones quæsisti? Flexio viarum, Cic.
units.tr: Circumlocutions: to arrive at something by a roundabout way (Quint.); you have used no circumlocution (Ter.); a winding of speech (Cic.); a maze of roads (Prud.); a meander, or meandrus (Col.); in the manner of a meander, that is, winding (from a river of this name, winding). What meanders, what windings have you sought? A bending of roads (Cic.).

units.la: Ambedere] Ambadedere, Plaut. Capra ambadedit aliquid, Virg. Ammianus vocat Ursas sævas hominum ambestrices. Abedere, Tacit. Obedere, Sipont. Adedere, Liv. Adesa exta, Virg. Ambest (unius tantum tertiæ personæ apud Fest.) Dudum circumrodo quod devorandum est,Cic.
units.tr: To eat away: to eat around (Plaut.); a goat has eaten away something (Virg.). Ammianus calls wild bears man-eaters. To eat off (Tacit.); to eat up (Sipont.); to eat to (Liv.); eaten entrails (Virg.). Ambest (found only in the third person in Festus). I have long been gnawing around what is to be devoured (Cic.).

units.la: Ambesus] Ambesæ mensæ, Virg. Adesus, Liv. Obesus, i. e. Circumrosus, Næv. apud Gell. Exesæ literæ, Cic. Semesa ossa, Virg.
units.tr: Gnawed: gnawed tables (Virg.); eaten away (Liv.); gnawed round about, that is, nibbled round (Naev., in Gell.); eaten letters (Cic.); half-eaten bones (Virg.).

units.la: Ambidexter] Æquimanus, Ausón. Isid. Utrâque manu (pede) ceu dextrâ utens.
units.tr: Ambidexter: Equimanus, Ausón. Isid. Using both hands (or feet) as if each were the right.

units.la: Ambisinister] Ambilævus, Henr. Steph. Ambifariam lævus, Cæl. Rhodius.
units.tr: Ambisinister: Ambilaevus, Henr. Steph. Left-handed on both sides, Cael. Rhodius.

units.la: Ambifariam] Ambiformiter, Arnob. Utroque vel alterutro modo.
units.tr: Ambifariam: Ambiformiter, Arnob. In either or both ways.

units.la: Ambigere] Vid. Dubitare.
units.tr: Ambigere: See Dubitare.

units.la: Ambigua sententia] Æquales calculi.
units.tr: Ambigua sententia: Evenly balanced counters.

units.la: Ambiguitas, vid. Dubietas.
units.tr: Ambiguitas: see Dubietas.

units.la: Ambiguus, vid. Dubius.
units.tr: Ambiguus: see Dubius.

units.la: Ambire, (1) circa aliquid ire]Ambit terram Oceanus,Ovid. Circumire aliquid, Cæs. Liv. Circuitu ad aliquid pervenire, Quint. Circumcingere. Cingere, Ovid. Oberrare,Perf. Circinare auras, Ovid.
units.tr: Ambire, (1) to go around something: The ocean encircles the earth, Ovid. To go around something, Caes. Liv. To arrive at something by a roundabout way, Quint. To surround, to encircle. To gird, Ovid. To wander about, Pers. To wheel through the breezes, Ovid.

units.la: Ambire (2) idem quod affectare in se honores] Contendere Magistratus. Inservire honoribus, Cic. Deservire honoribus, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Ambire, (2) the same as to seek honours for oneself: To contend for magistracies. To serve honours, Cic. To devote oneself to honours, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Ambitio (1) circumcirca itio] Ambitus stellarum rotundi, Cic. Æther terram circumspectu amplectitur, Id. Circumrotundatio, Vitruv. Ignominiæ cinctus indagine,Bud. Circuitus solis. Circumvectus. Circumvectio. Conversio solis annua, Cic. Orbita lunæ minor, quàm solis, Virg. Ambitudo, Apul. Obitus civitatum multarum, Id.
units.tr: Ambitio, (1) going about: The round orbits of the stars, Cic. The aether embraces the earth with its circuit, Id. Circular rounding, Vitruv. Girt with the net of disgrace, Bud. The circuit of the sun. A going round. A circular course. The yearly turning of the sun, Cic. The orbit of the moon is smaller than that of the sun, Virg. A going around, Apul. The circuit of many cities, Id.

units.la: Ambitio (2) ] Honorum cupiditas,Cic. Ambitus,Quint. Prensatio :/: petitio consulatus &c. Occursatio & blanditio popularis, Cic. Affectati honoris crimen, Fest.
units.tr: Ambitio, (2): Desire for honours, Cic. Canvassing, Quint. Prensatio: the seeking of the consulship, etc. Courting and popular flattery, Cic. The charge of affected honour, Fest.

units.la: Ambitiosus in honoribus petendis] Ambitor, Lampr.
units.tr: Ambitiosus in honoribus petendis: Office-seeking, Lampr.

units.la: Ambitiosus in gestibus] Pompæ plenus, Cic. Affectatus, Plin. Iun. Affectator, Quint. Putidus orator, Cic. Candidâ veste indutus. Herostrato ambitiosior, Er.
units.tr: Ambitiosus in gestibus: Full of pomp, Cic. Affected, Plin. Iun. An affecter, Quint. A flashy orator, Cic. Dressed in a white toga. More ambitious than Herostratus, Erasm.

units.la: Ambo] Uterque, Cic. (Ambo dicitur de iis, qui uno tempore aut simul quid faciunt. Uterque de iis, qui diverso tempore & separatim.) Alter uterque, Plin. Utrumvis, Plato.
units.tr: Ambo: Each of two, Cic. (Ambo is used of those who do something at one time or together; uterque of those who do so at different times and separately.) Either of two alike, Plin. Whichever you like of the two, Plato.

units.la: Ambrosia] Deorum cibus. Ambrosiæ dapes, Mart. Ambrosius succus, Col.
units.tr: Ambrosia: The food of the gods. Ambrosial feasts, Mart. Ambrosial juice, Col.

units.la: Ambulacrum] Ambulatio, Vitruv. Tecto ambulatiunculâ addenda est, Cic. Deambulatorium, Iul.Cap. Sipont. Spatia Academiæ, in quibus Philosophi docentes deambulant, Xyst. Cic. Inambulatio subdialis, Plin. Peridromus, Vitruv.
units.tr: Ambulacrum: A walk, Vitruv. A little covered walk must be added to the building, Cic. A place for strolling, Iul. Cap. Sipont. The grounds of the Academy, in which philosophers walk about while teaching, Xyst. Cic. An open-air walk, Plin. A peristyle, Vitruv.

units.la: (1) Ambulare] In-ambulare. Incedere. Grassari, Plaut. Usurpare pedibus aliquid, Id.
units.tr: (1) Ambulare: To walk about. To go on foot. To stride, Plaut. To use something with one's feet, Id.

units.la: (2) Ambulatio] Ambulatus, Arnob. Incessus, Cic. Quis noster itus ac reditus, Pallad. Ambulatiuncula, Cic. Inambulatio, Id. Deambulatio, Ter. Obambulatio hominum, ad Heren.
units.tr: (2) Ambulatio: A walking, Arnob. A going, Cic. Our going out and coming back, Pallad. A short walk, Cic. A walking about, Id. A stroll, Ter. A crowd of people milling about, ad Heren.

units.la: (3) Ambulatorius, & -tilis] Ambulatoriæ porticus, Hirt. Circumforaneæ domus, Apul. Confixilis machina, Id. Subliciæ turres, Id. Pegma, Sen. Suet.
units.tr: (3) Ambulatorius, and -tilis: Covered walkways, Hirt. Houses that move about the market, Apul. A sliding machine, Id. Towers on piles, Id. A stage, Sen. Suet.

units.la: Amburere, Ambustus] vid. Adurere.
units.tr: Amburere, Ambustus: see Adurere.

units.la: Amens, Amentem esse] Animi impos, Plaut. Qui non est sani animi. Donat. Male sanus, Cic. Animo parum valet, Sallust. Non constat alicui animus, Sen. Ubi sum, ibi non sum; ubi non sum, ibi est animus meus, Plaut. Qui animum suum in potestate non habet, Fest. Neque mens, neque vox, neque lingua consistit, Cic. Demens. Dementissimus. Excors. Vecors. Vecordissimus. Delirus. Insanus. Permotus mente, Vesanus, Cic. Vacerra, Fest. Vacerrosus, Suet. Captus corde, Plaut. Captus animo, Sen. Captus animi, Tacit. Captus mente, Cic. Exiit è potestate, Id.
units.tr: Amens, being out of one's mind: Not master of one's mind, Plaut. One who is not of sound mind, Donat. Ill in mind, Cic. Weak in spirit, Sall. One's mind does not hold together, Sen. Where I am, I am not; where I am not, there is my mind, Plaut. One who does not have his mind under his control, Fest. Neither mind, nor voice, nor tongue holds steady, Cic. Demented. Most demented. Witless. Senseless. Raving. Delirious. Insane. Moved in mind; crazed, Cic. A fool, Fest. A complete fool, Suet. Seized in the heart, Plaut. Seized in spirit, Sen. Seized in mind, Tac. Seized in mind, Cic. Gone out of control, Id.

units.la: Amentia] Dementia. Insanitas, & Ægritudo animi. Defectio à recta ratione; Totâ mente & ratione, Cic. Vecordia, cordia, Salust. Valetudo mentis, Suet. Alienatio mentis, Plin. Impotentia mentis, Suet.
units.tr: Amentia: Madness. Insanity, and sickness of the mind. Departure from right reason; with the whole mind and reason, Cic. Witlessness, Sall. Ill health of mind, Suet. Derangement of mind, Plin. Loss of control of the mind, Suet.

units.la: Amicè] vid. Familiariter.
units.tr: Amicè: see Familiariter.

units.la: Amicire] Amiciebat se, dum salutatur, Suet. Tunicare, Var. Circumamicire, Psal. 44. Incingi laurum. Incingi pictis vestibus, Ovid.
units.tr: Amicire: He wrapped himself up while being greeted, Suet. To clothe in a tunic, Var. To wrap around, Ps. 44. To be girt with laurel. To be clothed in embroidered garments, Ovid.

units.la: Amicitia] Amicities, Lucr. Necessitudo amicitiæ cum aliquo. Vinculum amoris, conjunctionis. Necessitas, Cic. Conjunctio gratiæ cum aliquo, Id. Gratia mihi cum illo magna est, Id. Factio, Cato ap. Sosip. Nodus amicitiæ, Cic.
units.tr: Amicitia: Friendship. Friendliness, Lucr. The bond of friendship with someone. A bond of love or union. Necessity, Cic. A union of favour with someone, Id. I have great favour with him, Id. Faction, Cato, cited by Sosip. The knot of friendship, Cic.

units.la: Amicitiæ specimen, pericula] Amicus certus in re incerta cernitur, Ennius.
units.tr: Proof of friendship is danger: A sure friend is seen in an uncertain matter, Ennius.

units.la: Amicorum unus animus] Idem velle, & idem nolle, ea demum firma amicitia, Salust. Amicorum communia omnia, Ter. Cic. Eurip. Arist.
units.tr: One mind among friends: To wish the same and to refuse the same: that alone is firm friendship, Sall. All things are common among friends, Ter. Cic. Eurip. Arist.

units.la: Amicitiam sibi parare] Amicitias aliquorum sibi adjungere, Comparare, Conciliare, Connectere, Conglutinare. Applicare se ad amicitiam alicujus. Conjungere cum aliquo necessitudinem. Inire summam gratiam cum omnibus bonis. Recipere in necessitudinem. Adjungere ad necessitudinem suam aliquem, Cic. Venire in amicitiam alicujus. Accipere in amicitiam aliquem, Liv. Devovere se alicujus amicitiæ, Caes.
units.tr: To make friendship for oneself: To join to oneself the friendships of certain people; to procure, to win over, to connect, to glue together. To attach oneself to someone's friendship. To join with someone in a bond. To enter into the highest favour with all good men. To receive into a bond. To add someone to one's own circle, Cic. To come into someone's friendship. To receive someone into friendship, Liv. To devote oneself to someone's friendship, Caes.

units.la: Amicitiam habere cum aliquo] Uti aliquo familiariter. Est mihi cum illo arctissima necessitudo. Sum illi summâ familiaritate conjunctus. Sum illi amicus. Summa mihi cum illo familiaritas intercedit. Multus mihi cum homine quondam usus fuit. Mutua quædam benevolentia jampridem inter nos est, Ter.
units.tr: To have friendship with someone: To treat someone on familiar terms. I have a very close bond with him. I am joined to him in the greatest intimacy. I am his friend. A very great familiarity lies between me and him. I have had much dealings with the man for a long time. A certain mutual goodwill has long existed between us, Ter.

units.la: Amicitiam dimittere] Amicitias dissuere, diluere, deponere, præcidere, dissociare, divellere. Removere se ab amicitiâ alicujus, Cic. Nodum amicitiæ tollere. Venire ad inimicitias. Dirimere, dirumpere societatem. Disjungere se ab amicitia alicujus. Disjungere aliquem à se, & se ab aliquo, Ter. Remittere amicitiam, Liv. Refugere ab institutâ consuetudine. Nuncium remittere. Facere divortium. Multam salutem dicere. Valere, & plaudere dicere, Cic.
units.tr: To dismiss friendship: To unstitch, dissolve, lay aside, cut off, dissociate, tear away friendships. To withdraw oneself from someone's friendship, Cic. To remove the knot of friendship. To come to enmities. To break off, to rend asunder a partnership. To part oneself from someone's friendship. To separate someone from oneself and oneself from someone, Ter. To give up friendship, Liv. To depart from an established custom. To send back a message. To make a divorce. To bid a long farewell. To say farewell and clap hands, Cic.

units.la: Amicus] Amicus tuus antiquissimus. Necessarius, Cic. Pernecessarius, Id. Tuus, pro amico. Unus de Tuis. Abes à Tuis. Habet mecum conjunctionem gratiæ. Conjunctissimi inter se. Studiosissimus mei, suus, Cic. Studiosa cohors, Hor. Summus, (subaudi amicus) Ter. Amiculus, Cic. Amicabilis, Plaut. Amicitior, pro amicior, Apul. Achates, fidus comes Æneæ. Conjunctus amicitiâ, gratiâ, officiis.
units.tr: Amicus: Your oldest friend. A close friend, Cic. A very close friend, Id. "Yours", for friend. One of yours. You are absent from your friends. He has a bond of favour with me. Most intimately joined with each other. Most devoted to me, his own, Cic. A devoted band, Hor. The best (friend, understood), Ter. A little friend, Cic. Friendly, Plaut. More friendly, for amicior, Apul. Achates, the faithful companion of Aeneas. Joined by friendship, favour and services.

units.la: Amicus insincerus] Amicus ollæ, mensæ. Amicos multos habet felicitas. Fervet olla, fervet quoque amicitia. Diffugiunt cadis cum fæce siccatis amici, Hor. Felicium multi sunt amici, inopis nullus. Mensa amicorum procreatrix.
units.tr: Insincere friend: a friend of the pot, of the table. Good fortune has many friends. The pot boils, and friendship boils too. Friends scatter like the lees dried from the jars, Hor. Of the fortunate there are many friends, of the needy none. The table of friends is the begetter of friendship.

units.la: Amicus non est adulator] Amicus Plato, Amicus Aristoteles; sed magis amica veritas. Non potes eodem amico & adulatore uti.
units.tr: A friend is not a flatterer: Plato is a friend, Aristotle is a friend, but truth is a greater friend. You cannot use the same man as friend and flatterer.

units.la: Amicus alter ego] Cum amico non certandum æmulatione.
units.tr: A friend is another self: One must not contend with a friend in rivalry.

units.la: Amicus eligendus circumspectè] Quem diligas, delige. Nulli temerè manum imponito, Pythag.
units.tr: A friend is to be chosen with care: Whom you love, choose. Lay your hand on no one rashly, Pythag.

units.la: Amicus non ludendus] Injuria solvit amorem.
units.tr: A friend is not to be trifled with: Injury dissolves love.

units.la: Amicus præstat pecuniæ] Papæ! quanto satius est amicis, quam pecuniis abundare, Er.
units.tr: A friend is better than money: Oh! how much better it is to abound in friends than in money, Erasm.

units.la: Amici sunt rari] Amicus fidus rara possessio. Amicus esto, neque nullis, neque multis.
units.tr: Friends are rare: A faithful friend is a rare possession. Be a friend to none, nor to many.

units.la: Amicos plures admittere convenit] Deus unus, amici plures.
units.tr: It is fitting to admit several friends: God is one; friends, many.

units.la: Amicum ama] Amicus cum vitiis ferendus. Amici vitia noveris, non oderis. Qui me amat, amat & canem meum,
units.tr: Love your friend: A friend is to be borne with his faults. Know a friend's faults, and do not hate them. He who loves me loves my dog too.

units.la: Amictus] Amicimen, Apul. Cultus, Liv. Inducula. Plaut. Habitus, Quint. Apparatus cultusque visendus, Cic. Tyrios induta paratûs, Ovid. Encomboma, Varr.
units.tr: Amictus: A covering, Apul. Dress, Liv. An undergarment, Plaut. Attire, Quint. Equipage and dress worth seeing, Cic. Clothed in Tyrian garments prepared, Ovid. An encomboma, Varr.

units.la: Amissio] Amissus Corn. Nep. Orbitas luminis, Plin. Orbatio, Sen. Perditio, Id. Tædia exquisita perditione, potatu, vel portatu, Turneb. Legit. Perditio nepotatu.
units.tr: Amissio: Loss. Amissus, Corn. Nep. Loss of sight, Plin. Bereavement, Sen. Destruction, Id. Exquisite weariness from ruin, drinking or carrying, Turneb. Read: destruction through squandering.

units.la: Amita] Patris mei soror, Fest.
units.tr: Amita: My father's sister, Fest.

units.la: Amittere] Perdere gratiam, Cic. Deperdere honestatem, vel, de honestate aliquid. Naufragium facere alicujus rei, Cic. Pereo à re. Res mea perit, Plaut. Orbari, amico. Facere jacturam equi pretiosi. Cic. Miserum istud verbum est, habuisse, & nihil habere, Plaut. Excidere uxore, Ter. Excidit è manibus victoria, Cic.
units.tr: Amittere: To lose favour, Cic. To lose honour, or to lose something of one's honour. To suffer shipwreck of something, Cic. I perish through the thing. My property is lost, Plaut. To be bereaved of a friend. To suffer the loss of a valuable horse, Cic. That word is wretched: to have had and to have nothing, Plaut. To lose one's wife, Ter. Victory slipped from one's hands, Cic.

units.la: Amittere aliquid per incuriam] Avolat pullus de nido.
units.tr: Amittere aliquid per incuriam: The chick flies away from the nest.

units.la: Amittere fidem] Decoquere fidem.
units.tr: Amittere fidem: To squander credit.

units.la: Amittere meliora, deterioribus retentis] Nucleum amisisse, putamina retinere, miserum est, Plaut.
units.tr: To lose the better things while keeping the worse: To have lost the kernel and kept the shells is wretched, Plaut.

units.la: Amitinus] Fratris vel sororis filii vel filiae, Non. Matruelis, Ulp. Sobrinus, Cic. Consobrinus, Id.
units.tr: Amitinus: Son or daughter of a brother or sister, Non. A cousin on the father's side, Ulp. A cousin, Cic. A cousin of the same grandparents, Id.

units.la: Amnis] Vid. Fluvius.
units.tr: Amnis: see Fluvius.

units.la: Amœne] Amœniter, Gell. Amplissimè habitare, Plin. Iun. Suaverubens, Virg.
units.tr: Amoene: Pleasantly, Gell. To live most splendidly, Plin. Iun. Sweetly blushing, Virg.

units.la: Amœnitas] Apricitatis inclytæ regia, Plin. Genialitas, Amm. Hilaritas, Cic.
units.tr: Amoenitas: The royal seat of famous sunshine, Plin. Genial character, Amm. Cheerfulness, Cic.

units.la: Amœnus] Apricum pratum, Hor. Aprici montium recessus, Plin. Festivus locus, Plaut. Luculentum ambulacrum, Plaut. Floridus color, Plin. Geniale rus, Ovid. Læta pascua, Horat. Arbor gratiosæ umbræ. Est illi gratia, Plin. Distinctus vario lepore, Lucr.
units.tr: Amoenus: A sunny meadow, Hor. Sunny recesses of the mountains, Plin. A pleasant place, Plaut. A splendid walk, Plaut. A flowery colour, Plin. A pleasant countryside, Ovid. Happy pastures, Hor. A tree of pleasant shade. He has charm, Plin. Adorned with varied charm, Lucr.

units.la: Amor] Pietas erga Deos, parentes, patriam, propinquos. Perquàm sanguine conjunctis, patriæque benevolis officium & diligens cultus tribuitur, Cic. Affectio, Plin. Affectus parentis, Quint.
units.tr: Amor: Piety towards the gods, parents, country and kin. Duty and diligent care are owed to those joined by blood and well disposed to the fatherland, Cic. Affection, Plin. The affection of a parent, Quint.

units.la: Amor diffusivus] Qui amat me, amat & canem meum.
units.tr: Love that spreads abroad] He who loves me loves my dog too.

units.la: Amor seipsum prodit] Tussis amorque non celatur.
units.tr: Love betrays itself] A cough and love cannot be concealed.

units.la: Amor res spontanea] Amari non extorquebis; sed elicies amore & officiis!
units.tr: Love is a spontaneous thing] You will not extort being loved; but you will draw it out by affection and kindness!

units.la: Amor artifex] Musicam docet amor.
units.tr: Love is an artist] Love teaches music.

units.la: Amor cæcus] Amor cæcus est, naves non videt.
units.tr: Love is blind] Love is blind; it does not see ships.

units.la: Quisquis amat ranam, ranam putat esse Dianam.
units.tr: Whoever loves a frog thinks the frog is Diana.

units.la: Quisquis amat cervam, cervam putat esse Minervam.
units.tr: Whoever loves a doe thinks the doe is Minerva.

units.la: Amor sui omnibus inest]
units.tr: Self-love is in everyone]

units.la: Est amor & rerum cunctis tutela suarum.
units.tr: Love is also the guardian of everyone's own possessions.

units.la: Athenienscm Athenis laudare haud difficile.
units.tr: To praise the Athenians at Athens is not difficult.

units.la: Amorem tuum non meretur] Indignus tuo amore. Indignus quem ames. Indignus, ut abs te diligatur. Indignus abs te amari.
units.tr: He does not deserve your love] Unworthy of your love. Unworthy to be loved by you. Unworthy that you should love him. Unworthy to be loved by you.

units.la: Amovere] Dimovere laborem. Propulsare famem, suspi-cionem. Removere se à suspicione, Cic. Submovere, Col. Ablegare, Cic. Segregare à se culpam. Semovere, Plaut. Amoliri periculum. Arcere fascinum, Fest.
units.tr: To remove] To drive away trouble. To repel hunger or suspicion. To remove oneself from suspicion, Cic. To push away, Col. To send away, Cic. To set a fault apart from oneself. To put aside, Plaut. To ward off danger. To keep off the evil eye, Fest.

units.la: Amphibium] Anceps bestia, in utraque sede vivens, Cic. Duplicis vitæ animans, Col. Amphibius, a, um, Id. Quæ & terrestria & aquatilia pabula desiderant, Id. Vibium animal, Stat.
units.tr: Amphibian] A doubtful creature, living in either element, Cic. A creature of double life, Col. Amphibious, Id. Which need both land and water for food, Id. An amphibious animal, Stat.

units.la: Amphora Romana] Mensura duas urnas capiens, Varr. Quadrantal, & Cubus, Ian. Cybium, Fest. Trimodium, Plaut. Semimedimnus, Agricol. Philand. Henr. Steph.
units.tr: Roman amphora] A measure holding two urns, Varr. A quadrantal, or cube, Ian. A cybium, Fest. A trimodium, Plaut. A semimedimnus, Agricola, Philander, Henr. Steph.

units.la: Ample] Sublatè ampleque dicere. Amplissimè, Magnificentissimè. Honorificè. Honorificentius. Honorificentissimè. Elatè. Rhetoricè & tragicè aliquid ornare. Augustè. Magnificè, Cic. Generosè, Hor. Tragicum spirare, Id. Ampliter, Plaut. Amplificè, Catul.
units.tr: Ample] To speak loftily and amply. Most amply, most magnificently. Honourably. More honourably. Most honourably. Loftily. To adorn something in rhetorical and tragic style. Nobly. Magnificently, Cic. Generously, Hor. To breathe of tragedy, Id. Amply, Plaut. Amplifiedly, Catul.

units.la: Amplecti] Amplexari aliquem, Cic. Amplexantur inter se, Plaut. Jungi amplexu mutuo, Plin. Amplexu tenere aliquem, Lucr. Ruere in amplexus alicujus, Sen. Complectere. Complecti inter se. Complexu recipere. Complexu jungi, Cic. Ire in amplexus, Ovid. Venire in colla, Prop. Mutare brachia alterno amplexu, Id. Involare in collum, Afran. apud Non.
units.tr: To embrace] To embrace someone, Cic. They embrace one another, Plaut. To be joined in mutual embrace, Plin. To hold someone in an embrace, Lucr. To rush into someone's embrace, Sen. To enfold. To enfold one another. To receive in an embrace. To be joined in an embrace, Cic. To go into the arms, Ovid. To come into the neck, Prop. To exchange arms in mutual embrace, Id. To fling oneself on the neck, Afran., cited in Non.

units.la: Ampliare] Amplificare Remp. Cic. Proferre imperium, Tacit. Proferre in immensum aliquid, Sen. Propagare laudem, Cic. Accessionem ædibus adjungere.
units.tr: To enlarge] To enlarge the commonwealth, Cic. To extend dominion, Tacit. To extend something immeasurably, Sen. To spread fame, Cic. To add an annex to a building.

units.la: Amplificare orationem] Dilatare, Exaggerare rem oratione. Diffusiùs & latiùs aliquid dicere. In majus ferre, Claud. Fundere se latiùs, Cic. Magnificare, Gell. Longiùs prosequi, Cic. Latiùs prosequi, Quint. Altiùs prosequi, Plin. Longiùs excurrit oratio, Cic. Exspatiari, Quint. Infinitè fertur, ut flumen, oratio, Cic. Amplificatio. Vid. Dilatatio.
units.tr: To amplify a speech] To expand and magnify a matter in speech. To speak of something more fully and broadly. To carry to a greater size, Claud. To spread oneself more widely, Cic. To magnify, Gell. To pursue at greater length, Cic. To pursue more broadly, Quint. To pursue more deeply, Plin. The speech runs on at greater length, Cic. To range freely, Quint. The speech is carried on without limit, like a river, Cic. Amplification. See Dilatatio.

units.la: Amplitudo] Vastitas, laxitas terræ, viarum, Col. Superficies areæ. Capacitas, Cic. Laxamentum, Id. Apertum, Lucr.
units.tr: Breadth] The vastness and width of land or of roads, Col. The surface of a courtyard. Capacity, Cic. Room, Id. An open space, Lucr.

units.la: Amplius] Ultrà, Cic. Porrò, Lucr. Porrectius, Amm.
units.tr: Further] Beyond, Cic. Moreover, Lucr. More extended, Amm.

units.la: Amplus] Vid. Latus. Magnificus.
units.tr: Ample] See Broad. Magnificent.

units.la: Ampulla] Guttus, Mart. Guttulus, Plaut. Nimbus vitreus, Mart.
units.tr: Flask] A small jar, Mart. A little bottle, Plaut. A glass vessel, Mart.

units.la: Amputare] Vid. Abscindere.
units.tr: To cut off] See To cut away.

units.la: Amuletum] Religiosum gestamen amoliendis periculis, Plin. Sipont. Præbia, Fest. Remedia in collis puerorum, Scal. Ligaturis curare, Fab. Vict. Samothracius annulus Isid.
units.tr: Amulet] A religious charm for warding off dangers, Plin. Sipont. Praebia, Fest. Remedies hung about the necks of children, Scal. To cure by bindings, Fab. Vict. The Samothracian ring, Isid.

units.la: Amurca] Magma, Plin. Fraces, Vitr. Sanies, Cat. Retrimenta, Plin. Cerda, Fæx olei, Plin.
units.tr: Amurca] Dregs, Plin. Lees, Vitr. Gore, Cat. Refuse, Plin. Sediment, the dregs of oil, Plin.

units.la: Amussis] Linea, Vitruv. Album, Sen. Epist. 59 Rubrica, Pers. Stat. Amussium, Bernar. Bald. in Vitruv.
units.tr: Plumb-line] A line, Vitruv. A white board, Sen. Epist. 59. Red chalk, Pers., Stat. A rule, Bernard, Bald. on Vitruv.

units.la: Amygdalum] Nux Græca, Col. Plin. Nux Thasia, Plin. Macrob.
units.tr: Almond] A Greek nut, Col., Plin. A Thasian nut, Plin., Macrob.

units.la: An?] Nunquid? Ter. Nunquidnam non novi? Id. Anne? Cic. Num furis? Hor. Ecquid attendis? Cic. Vid. Ne, Enclitic.
units.tr: Whether?] Surely? Ter. Surely not, Id. Or? Cic. Are you mad? Hor. Are you paying attention? Cic. See Ne, enclitic.

units.la: Ana libras, Drachmas] Singulas libras, vel uncias binas, ternas, vel singulorum tres uncias.
units.tr: Ana of pounds, of drachmas] Each a pound, or two, three ounces, or three ounces of each.

units.la: Analecta] Reliquiæ mensarum. Collectanea, Cic. Vid. Reliquiæ.
units.tr: Analecta] Scraps from tables. Collections, Cic. See Remnants.

units.la: Analogia] Proportio, Var. Comparatio, Cic.
units.tr: Analogy] Proportion, Varr. Comparison, Cic.

units.la: Analysis] Resolutio, Gell. Examinatio, Arnob.
units.tr: Analysis] Resolution, Gell. Examination, Arnob.

units.la: Anaphora] Repetitio, Cic. Epanaphora aliis.
units.tr: Anaphora] Repetition, Cic. Epanaphora in others.

units.la: Anas] Anaticula, Plaut. Quassagipennæ & Tremipedæ, Anatum epitheta apud Varr. (quòd quassis agantur pennis, & tremant pedibus.) Tetrinnit anas.
units.tr: Duck] A little duck, Plaut. Swift-winged and trembling-footed, epithets of ducks in Varr. (because they are driven with shaking wings and tremble on their feet.) The duck quacks.

units.la: Anathema] Vid. Execratus, & atio.
units.tr: Anathema] See Cursed, and the like.

units.la: Anatocismus, usura supra usuram] Usuræ in singulos annos renovatio. Fœnoris anniversaria renovatio, Bud. & Cic. apud quem est, Renovatio singulorum annorum I. 6. ad Att. de usurâ. Mergentes sortem usuræ, Liv. Usuræ usurarum, ex Græco, Fœnorum fœnora. Fœnoris pensiuncula.
units.tr: Compound interest, usury upon usury] The renewal of interest every year. The yearly renewal of interest, Bud., and Cic., in whom it occurs as a yearly renewal, Att. I.6, on usury. Usury swallowing the principal, Liv. Usury of usuries, from the Greek; interest on interest. A small payment of interest.

units.la: Anatomia] Incisio membrorum, Celsi. Ars anatomica, Henr. Steph. Laniena Hippocratica. (Prudentius paulò aliter sumit pro medicinâ, quæ urit vel secat.)
units.tr: Anatomy] Cutting up of limbs, Celsus. The anatomical art, Henr. Steph. Hippocratic butchery. (Prudentius takes it somewhat differently, for medicine, which burns or cuts.)

units.la: Anatomicus]Profector, Tert. Dissectionis corporum peritus, Henr. Steph. Medici, qui ista aperta & patefacta viderunt, (scil. vias ad oculos, aures) Cic. Qui homines incidit, Celsi.
units.tr: Anatomist] A dissector, Tert. Skilled in the dissection of bodies, Henr. Steph. Physicians who saw those things opened and laid bare (namely the passages to the eyes and ears), Cic. One who cuts up men, Celsus.

units.la: Anceps] (1) Ambiguum ferrum, Eurip. in Hippol. In utramque partem valet, Cic. Bipennis:/: securis, Var.
units.tr: Doubtful] (1) An ambiguous blade, Eurip. in Hippol. It holds in either direction, Cic. A double-headed axe, Var.

units.la: (2) Idem quod Dubius.
units.tr: (2) The same as Dubius.

units.la: Anchora] Ancora, Virg. Uncus,Val. Argon. Servaculum apud Vlp. anchoram interpretatur Hotoman.
units.tr: Anchor] An anchor, Virg. A hook, Val. Argon. Hotoman interprets servaculum in Ulpian as anchor.

units.la: Anchorale] Anchorarius funis, Cæf. Camelus, Rhodius.
units.tr: Anchor-rope] A cable for anchoring, Caes. A camel, Rhodius.

units.la: Ancilla] Ministra. Famula. Pedissequa, Cic. Scandaligerulæ. Flabelliferæ. Vestispicæ. Cistellatrices, Plaut.
units.tr: Maidservant] An attendant. A female servant. A handmaid who follows, Cic. Bearers of fans and mirrors, fan-bearers, dress-watchers, box-carriers, Plaut.

units.la: Ancillula] Quasillariæ, Petron. (quæ quasillos & calathos, lanæ & pensis aptos, gestant, Passerat.)
units.tr: Little maidservant] Spinning-maids, Petron. (who carry spindle-baskets and bowls suited to wool and yarn, Passerat.)

units.la: Ancus] Qui justo breviorem habet cubitum.
units.tr: Crooked-armed] One who has a cubit shorter than the proper length.

units.la: Andabatæ] Celetizontes, Plin. Homines in tenebris vel clausis oculis, vel operto capite, equis aut curribus concurrentes, Turneb.
units.tr: Blindfolded fighters] Those who race in the dark, or with eyes shut or heads covered, running with horses or chariots, Turneb.

units.la: Anfractus] Flexus itineris, Cic. Mæander, Id. Flexuræ vicorum, Suet. Flexus labyrintheus, Catul. Inversura adituum theatri, Vitruv. Cornua maris, Ovid. Curvor, Var.
units.tr: Winding] A bend in a road, Cic. A meander, Id. Turnings of streets, Suet. A labyrinthine twist, Catul. The inward curve of the entrance passages of a theatre, Vitruv. The horns of the sea, Ovid. A curving, Var.

units.la: Angelus] Ciceroni Dæmon seu Lar. Nuntii Deorum, Hor. Nuntius Dei, Minut. Felic. Cœlestes mentes, Ovid. Genios etiam multi vocant; sed melius, Cœlestes animos, mentes beatas, corporibus semper vacantes. Mentes ab omni concretione mortali segregatas.
units.tr: Angel] For Cicero, a demon or household god. Messengers of the gods, Hor. A messenger of God, Minut. Felix. Heavenly minds, Ovid. Many also call them genii; but better, heavenly spirits, blessed minds, always free from bodies. Minds set apart from all mortal composition.

units.la: Angelus custos] Prisciis Ethnicis Genius alicujus, Ter. Genius familiaris, Marcel. Empir. Lar familiaris, Cic. Actorum & cogitatorum testis, Apul. Pædagogus à Deo datus, Sen. Custos vitæ, Plaut.
units.tr: Guardian angel] Among the pagans, the genius of a person, Ter. A household genius, Marcel. Empir. A household god, Cic. A witness of deeds and thoughts, Apul. A tutor given by God, Sen. A guardian of life, Plaut.

units.la: Angelica, radix] Panaces angelicum. Costos niger. Radix Sancti Spiritus. Sirin. Offic. Panax Heracleum, Iun.
units.tr: Angelica, root] Panax angelicum. Black costus. Root of the Holy Spirit, Sirin., Offic. Panax Heracleum, Iun.

units.la: Angi corpore vel animo] Angi curis, Cic. Angor faucis occupat, Plin. Confici angoribus. Torqueri. Excedit me cura. Ægritudo lacerato exest, conficit animum meum. Est mihi unguis in ulcere, Cic. Cruciari, Pungi, Exerceri, Laborare hostibus domesticis. Suffocari, Cic. Coquit me hoc, Id. Mordet me id, Ter. Remordent me peccata, Lucr. Urit me dolor. Uror doloribus, Ovid. Cordolium est mihi. Cor stimulis foditur. Miserum me habet miseris modis, Plaut. Fodicat mihi animum, Id. Est (edit) me animi exercitus, Afran.
units.tr: To be distressed in body or mind] To be troubled by cares, Cic. A choking grief seizes the throat, Plin. To be worn down by anguish. To be tormented. Care gnaws at me. Grief eats away the torn heart, wears down my spirit. I have a claw in a wound, Cic. To be racked, pricked, harassed, to suffer from domestic enemies. To be choked, Cic. This cooks me, Id. This gnaws at me, Ter. Sins gnaw at me, Lucr. Pain burns me. I am burned with sorrows, Ovid. My heart is pained. My heart is pierced with goads. He holds me wretched in wretched ways, Plaut. It pricks my spirit, Id. An army of feelings eats at me (or gnaws me), Afran.

units.la: Afran. Suffocat me aliquid. Conflictari molestiis. Hæc me refricant, Cic. Vid. Solicitum esse.
units.tr: Afran. Something chokes me. To be struggled against by troubles. These things rub my wounds raw, Cic. See To be anxious.

units.la: Angor] Vid. Afflictio.
units.tr: Distress] See Affliction.

units.la: Angiportus, & um) Limes, Liv. Extra latos vicos urbis, semita transversa, Bud. Laura, Suid.
units.tr: Back alley] A narrow path, Liv. A cross-path outside the broad streets of the city, Bud. A lane, Suid.

units.la: Angiportus impervius] Angiportum non pervium, Ter. Fundulæ, Varro (à fundo quia exitum habent, Turneb.)
units.tr: Impassable alley] An alley not passable, Ter. Little blind alleys, Varro (from fundus, because they have an outlet, Turneb.).

units.la: Angina] Angor faucium hominis, Plin. Synanche, es, Cels. (proprie suum angor.)
units.tr: Quinsy] The choking of human throats, Plin. Synanche, Cels. (properly, a choking of the throat.)

units.la: Angularis] In flexu viæ sita domus. In flexu vici eminens. Angularius, Procul. IC.
units.tr: Corner] A house set at a bend in the road. Standing out at a bend of a street. Angularius, Procul. IC.

units.la: Angulus] (1 Interne) Versura porticûs, Vitruv.
units.tr: Corner] (1) Internal: the recess of a portico, Vitruv.

units.la: (2) Externe] Angulus intimus, Ovid. Lateris angulus, qui ad orientem spectat, Cic.
units.tr: (2) External: the innermost corner, Ovid. The corner of a side facing east, Cic.

units.la: Angustia] Angustitas, Accibec. Non. Angusta viarum, Virgil. Via angusta ædium, urbis. Coarctatio, Liv. Contractura columnarum, Vitruv.
units.tr: Narrowness] Narrowness, Accib., Non. A narrowness of roads, Virg. A narrow way of a house, or a city. Constriction, Liv. Contraction of columns, Vitruv.

units.la: Angustare] Coarctare, Liv. Coangustare, Var. In angustum claudere, concludere, deducere, Cic. In angustum cogere, Ter. In angustias compellere, Coarctare, Cic. Introrsus agere, Sen. Coactare, Lucr. Coërcere, Cic. Addensere, Virg.
units.tr: To narrow] To constrict, Liv. To narrow greatly, Var. To shut up, enclose, or lead into a narrow place, Cic. To drive into a narrow space, Ter. To compel into straits, to constrict, Cic. To drive inward, Sen. To crowd, Lucr. To confine, Cic. To press together, Virg.

units.la: Angustari] Arctè accubare, Plaut. Urgeri angustiis, Cic. Inter cuneos mihi accubare videor, Plaut. In puteo constringi. In angusto esse. In angustum includi. Constipari in locum unum tantus numerus nequit, Cic.
units.tr: To be pressed in] To lie down cramped, Plaut. To be pressed by straits, Cic. I seem to lie among wedges, Plaut. To be bound in a well. To be in a narrow place. To be shut up in a narrow space. So great a number cannot be packed into one place, Cic.

units.la: Angustè] Vid. Arctè.
units.tr: Narrowly] See Closely.

units.la: Angustus] Arctum theatrum, Hor. Arctus annulus, Amm. Per angustum fretum, Cic. Præten uis pons. Contractus, Col. Confer Arctus.
units.tr: Narrow] A cramped theatre, Hor. A tight ring, Amm. Through a narrow strait, Cic. A bridge that is too narrow. Contracted, Col. Compare Tight.

units.la: Anguis] Serpens, Plin. Python, Ovid. Coluber, Virg.
units.tr: Snake] A serpent, Plin. A python, Ovid. A snake, Virg.

units.la: Anguinus] Anguineus, Cic. Anguigena,& Serpentigena, Ovid.
units.tr: Snaky] Snake-like, Cic. Born of snakes, and serpent-born, Ovid.

units.la: Anhelare propr.] Boves anhelant, Ovid. Crebras auras reducere, Lucr. Vix sufferre anhelitum, Plaut. Vehementer & crebrò spirare, morbi testimonium, Cels. Ducit anhelitum ex cursurâ, Plaut. Ilia ducere, Plaut. Ilia trahere re, Plin. Spiritum difficulter reddere, Celf. Spiritus est gra-vis. Interclusus spiritus arcte meat, Id. Raris turbatus vo-cibus hisco, Virg. Circumgemit ursus ovile, Hor.
units.tr: To pant, properly] Oxen pant (Ovid). To draw back frequent breaths (Lucretius). To scarcely bear the breath (Plautus). To breathe vehemently and often, a sign of illness (Celsus). He draws breath from running (Plautus). To heave the flanks (Plautus). To drag the flanks (Pliny). To breathe out with difficulty (Celsus). The breath is heavy. A breath held in narrow passages passes with difficulty (Celsus). Troubled in voice, I gape with rare words (Virgil). The bear growls around the sheepfold (Horace).

units.la: Anhelitus] Creber anhelitus, Virg. Spiritus gravis, Celf. Anhelatio, Plin. Dyspnoea, Celf. Plin. Peripneumonia, Celf. Difficultas spirandi, Id. Angustiae spiritus. Angustus spiritus, Cic. Suspirium, Sen. Cavitatum pulmonis angustia. Ob humorem ingestum, vel ulcus, tuber enatum, Ger.
units.tr: Panting] Rapid breathing (Virgil). Heavy breath (Celsus). Panting (Pliny). Dyspnoea (Celsus, Pliny). Peripneumonia (Celsus). Difficulty in breathing (Celsus). Shortness of breath; narrowness of breath (Cicero). A sigh (Seneca). Narrowing of the cavities of the lungs, from swallowed moisture, or an ulcer, or a growth that has sprung up (Ger.).

units.la: Anhelus] Anhelator, Plin. Anhelatus, Cic. Ilia trahens jumentum, Id. Ilia ducens, Horat. Dyspnoeicus. Suspi-riosus. Peripneumonicus. Pulmonarius, Plin.
units.tr: Short of breath] One who pants (Pliny). Panted (Cicero). A beast of burden drawing in its flanks (Cicero). Heaving the flanks (Horace). Dyspnoeic. Sighing. Peripneumonic. Pulmonary (Pliny).

units.la: Anima] Anima dum aegroto est, spes esse dicitur, Cic. Ani-mos immortales credo, pro anima, Id. Animo sapimus. Animo fruimur. Sine animo anima est debilis, Accius. Spi-ritus, Ovid. Mens cingitur corpore externo, Cic. Animu-la, Id. Hospes comesque corporis. Divinae particula au-rae, Horat.
units.tr: Soul] While the sick man lives, it is said there is hope (Cicero). I believe souls are immortal, as for the soul (Cicero). We are wise in mind; we enjoy with the spirit. Without spirit the soul is weak (Accius). Breath (Ovid). The mind is enclosed by an outward body (Cicero). A little soul (Cicero). Guest and companion of the body. A particle of divine air (Horace).

units.la: Animadvertere] Intendere animum, sensum. Vid. Di-spicere.
units.tr: To notice] To direct one's mind or senses. See Dispicere.

units.la: Animal] Animans, Cic. Belua, Bestiae, Ciceroni etiam a-ves & pisces. Natura animantum, i.e. animans, Lucr. Plan-ta ambulatilis.
units.tr: Animal] A living thing (Cicero). A beast, beasts; for Cicero also birds and fish. The nature of living things, that is, living creatures (Lucretius). A walking plant.

units.la: Animalia omnia armata] Natura animantium sua cuique dedit arma, Er.
units.tr: All animals are armed] Nature gave each kind of living thing its own weapons (Erasmus).

units.la: Animalis] Animale genus. Animalia corpora, Quint. Spirans, Cic. Mundum animantem dixerunt, Cic. Spirita-lis. Pneumaticus, Vitruv. Vitaliter animata, Lucr.
units.tr: Animal (adj.)] A kind of living thing. Animal bodies (Quintilian). Breathing (Cicero). They called the world a living being (Cicero). Spiritual. Pneumatic (Vitruvius). Animated with life (Lucretius).

units.la: Animalis facultas] Animabilis spirabilisque facultas, Cic. Animatu carent insecta, Plin.
units.tr: Animal faculty] A faculty capable of giving life and breath (Cicero). Insects lack animation (Pliny).

units.la: Animalculum] Bestiola, Cic. Plin.
units.tr: Little animal] A small beast (Cicero, Pliny).

units.la: Animare, animosum reddere] Addere animos. Addere cor-nua. Erigere animos, Cic. Confirmare animum trepi-dum, Iuv. Facere alicui animum; animos. Facere hosti armipotenti spiritus. Facere ardorem animi, Liv. Excitare animum, Sen.
units.tr: To animate, to make bold] To add spirit. To add horns. To raise the spirits (Cicero). To strengthen a trembling mind (Juvenal). To give someone courage, or spirit. To give an enemy mighty in arms spirit. To kindle the ardour of the mind (Livy). To rouse the mind (Seneca).

units.la: Animose] Animosissime, Suet. Praesenti animo, Cic. Fi-denti animo, Confidenter, Cicer. Fidentissime dimican-tes, ter, Amm. Animosissimè, Suet. Audacter, Ter. Audacissimè, Cæs. Vid. Audenter.
units.tr: Boldly] Most boldly (Suetonius). With presence of mind (Cicero). With a confident mind, confidently (Cicero). Fighting most confidently (Ammianus). Most boldly (Suetonius). Boldly (Terence). Most audaciously (Caesar). See Audenter.

units.la: Animositas] Magnitudo animi. Animus erectus, fortis, alacer, amplus, regius, invictus. Ad omnes casus ferendos paratus animus. Præsentia animi, Cic. Præsens animus, Quint. Vid. Audentia, Fortitudo.
units.tr: Boldness, spirit] Greatness of mind. A mind raised, brave, lively, ample, kingly, unconquered. A mind ready to bear all chances. Presence of mind (Cicero). A ready mind (Quintilian). See Audentia, Fortitudo.

units.la: Animosus] Nam & animosos, & bene animatos dicimus, robusti animi, Cic. Animi plenus, Liv. Prodigus animæ, Hor. Ingentis spiritûs, Virg. Liv. Armatus animis, Cic. Nimius animus, Liv. Adest mihi animus, Plaut. Adsum animo, Cic. vid. Audens, Fortis.
units.tr: Spirited] For we say spirited and well-minded, of a robust mind (Cicero). Full of spirit (Livy). Prodigal of breath (Horace). Of great spirit (Virgil, Livy). Armed in mind (Cicero). Excessive mind (Livy). I have the courage (Plautus). I am present in mind (Cicero). See Audens, Fortis.

units.la: Animus] Mens animi vigilat, Lucr. Mala mens, malus animus, Ter.
units.tr: Mind] The mind of the spirit keeps watch (Lucretius). A bad mind, a bad spirit (Terence).

units.la: Anniculus] Unius anni. Annotini ungues palmitum, Col. Annua vita uxoris, Plaut.
units.tr: A year old] Of one year. Shoots of vines a year old (Columella). The yearly life of a wife (Plautus).

units.la: Annosus] Maturus annis. Vergens annis virgo, Tacit. Maturus ævi, Virg. Longiùs ætate provectus. Ingravescente, affectâ ætate, Cic. Grandævus. Non gravis Acestes, Virg.
units.tr: Aged] Ripe in years. A maiden advancing in years (Tacitus). Ripe in age (Virgil). Advanced further in age. In failing, weakened age (Cicero). Aged. Not heavy Acestes (Virgil).

units.la: Annotare. Vid. Enotare.
units.tr: To annotate. See Enotare.

units.la: Annotatio] Adnotatio, Sipont. Annotatiuncula. Annotamentum, Gell.
units.tr: Annotation] Annotation (Sipontinus). A little annotation. A note (Gellius).

units.la: Annuere] Annuere toto capite, Cic. Annuere nutum, Liv. Adnutare, Plaut. Verbis nutum accommodare; ut, quod nollem, rejecto capite; quod vellem, relato monstrarem, Apul.
units.tr: To nod assent] To nod assent with the whole head (Cicero). To assent by a nod (Livy). To nod (Plautus). To fit a nod to words: so that by a head thrown back I might show what I did not want, and by a head raised what I wanted (Apuleius).

units.la: Annularis digitus] Medicinalis, Macrob. Sipont. Medicus digitus, Gerræ Alex. Neapol. (quòd ob munditiem, pharmaca eo misceantur commodè.)
units.tr: Ring finger] The medicinal finger (Macrobius, Sipontinus). The physician's finger (Gerra of Alexandria, Neapolitanus), because medicines are conveniently mixed with it for cleanliness.

units.la: Annulus] Annellus, Cic. Condulus. Condalus, Cor. Condalium, Fest. Ungulus, Pacuv.
units.tr: Ring] A little ring (Cicero). Condulus. Condalus (Cor.). Condalium (Festus). Ungulus (Pacuvius).

units.la: Annumerare] Annumerare alicui pecuniam. Numerare militibus stipendium. Numerare à se. Attribuere pecuniam. Enumerare pretium, Cic. Dinumerare. Renumerare, Ter. Pernumerare alicui pecuniam, Liv.
units.tr: To count out] To pay money to someone. To count out pay to soldiers. To count out from oneself. To assign money. To count out a price (Cicero). To count again. To count again (Terence). To pay out money in full to someone (Livy).

units.la: Annus] Annuum spatium, Plin. Annuum intervallum, Liv. Annale tempus, Var. Natales sex ierant mihi, Ovid. Post aliquot aristas, Virg. Æstas septima, Sen. Ver, bruma, Ovid. Messis, Petron. Ætatem decimam ingressus, Var. Lustra solis, vocat annos, Lucr. Quadriga mundi. Anni nodi, Lucr.
units.tr: Year] A yearly space (Pliny). A yearly interval (Livy). Annual time (Varro). Six birthdays had gone by for me (Ovid). After some ears of corn (Virgil). The seventh summer (Seneca). Spring, winter (Ovid). Harvest (Petronius). Having entered the tenth year of age (Varro). The lustra of the sun, which he calls years (Lucretius). The chariot of the world. The knots of the years (Lucretius).

units.la: Sub anni finem] Exeunte anno, Vid. Finis.
units.tr: Towards the end of the year] Near the year's end. See Finis.

units.la: Annus est, à] Annus interjectus. Annus est,& repulsam tulit. Anni multi sunt, cùm, &c. Intersunt anni tres, decem, Cic. Hanc domum jam multos annos est cùm possideo. Annus septimus est postquam, Plaut. Septimo ab hinc anno obiit. Septimus est annus, Ter. Mensis agitur septimus, postquam venit, Liv.
units.tr: It is a year since] A year intervening. It is a year, and he has suffered rejection. There are many years since, when, etc. Three or ten years lie between (Cicero). I have owned this house these many years. It is seven years since (Plautus). He died seven years ago from now. It is the seventh year (Terence). The seventh month is passing since he came (Livy).

units.la: Annum ago 50] Annus 50 vitæ meæ completur, Virg. Contiguus anno 50, Ammian. Centesimus tibi premitur annus, Sen. 50 annos vitæ numero.
units.tr: I am fifty years old] Fifty years of my life are completed (Virgil). Close to fifty years (Ammianus). The hundredth year presses upon you (Seneca). I count fifty years of life.

units.la: Anno Christi]Anno virginei partûs. Anno à Christo nobis coelitùs misso. Anno Domini. Anno à nato Christo. Anno salutiferi virginis partûs. Anno incarnationis divinæ. Anno humanæ Redemptionis. Anno quo divina majestas humanâ in specie, ad salutem nostram coelitus sese demisit. Guagninus.
units.tr: In the year of Christ] In the year of the virginal birth. In the year since Christ was sent to us from heaven. In the year of the Lord. In the year from Christ's birth. In the year of the saving virginal birth. In the year of the divine incarnation. In the year of human redemption. In the year in which the divine majesty came down from heaven in human form for our salvation. Guagninus.

units.la: Semel in anno] Semel per annum.
units.tr: Once a year] Once through the year.

units.la: Anniversarius, annuo spatio revertens] Dies anno redeunte festus, Hor. Anniversariæ vicissitudines coeli, Cic.
units.tr: Yearly, returning at a yearly interval] A festal day returning with the year (Horace). The yearly returns of the heavens (Cicero).

units.la: Annuatim] In annos singulos, Cic. Quotannis, Plaut. Cic. Quotquot annis, Var. Annuâ vice, Col. Annuis vicibus, Id.
units.tr: Yearly] For each single year (Cicero). Every year (Plautus, Cicero). As many times as each year (Varro). By annual turn (Columella). In yearly turns (Columella).

units.la: Annuus] Annuus sumptus, Cic. Annuum est quadrupedibus pilos cadere & subnasci, Plin. Etesius,a,um, Lucr. Annifer juniperus. Restibile vinetum, Col.
units.tr: Annual] An annual expense (Cicero). It is annual for four-footed animals that hair falls out and grows again (Pliny). Yearly (Lucretius). Juniper bearing fruit each year. A vineyard renewed each year (Columella).

units.la: Annona] Annuum, Sen. i. e. annuum alimentum. Vitus annuus, Plin. Res frumentaria,Cic. Frugalitas, Apul. Canon. Alimentum publico datum, Cæl. Rhodig. Annonaria provisio, Spartian.
units.tr: Grain supply] Yearly (Seneca), that is, yearly food. Annual vine (Pliny). Corn supply (Cicero). Frugality (Apuleius). Canon. Food given out publicly (Caelius Rhodiginus). Provision of the grain supply (Spartianus).

units.la: Annonarius] Annonæ manceps, Plin. Dardanarius, Cujac. Flagellator annonæ.
units.tr: Grain contractor] Contractor for the grain supply (Pliny). Dardanarius (Cujacius). Scourger of the grain supply.

units.la: Annona præfectus]Pabulator, Cæf. Frumentator, Liv. Curatores. Rei frumentariæ præpositi. Pabularius, Col. Agens in rebus, Amm. Annonæ gravitas] Caritas annonæ, difficultas, penuria, inopia annonæ, Cic. Sævitia annonæ, Tacit. Compressa annona, Liv. Incendium annonæ, Quint. Grave pretium, Salust.
units.tr: Prefect of the grain supply] Forager (Caesar). Grain provider (Livy). Curators. Set over the grain business. Fodder-man (Columella). Agent in affairs (Ammianus). The dearness of the grain supply: the high price, difficulty, scarcity, want of grain (Cicero). The savagery of the grain supply (Tacitus). The grain supply restricted (Livy). The fire of the grain supply (Quintilian). A heavy price (Sallust).

units.la: Annonam excandefacere] Incendere annonam, Var. Caritatem annonæ infero. Flagello annonam, Plin. Vexo & exonero annonam, Vlp. Augere, accendere pretium, Plin. Intendere pretium, Tacit. Candefacere annonam, Var.
units.tr: To inflame the price of grain] To set fire to the grain supply (Varro). I bring on dearness of grain. To whip up the grain price (Pliny). To shake and unload the grain (Ulpian). To increase, to kindle the price (Pliny). To stretch the price (Tacitus). To heat up the grain price (Varro).

units.la: Ansa, vasis manubrium] Manubrium trullæ, Cic. Ansula, Val. M. Tenaculum, Ter. Vid. Manubrium. Occasio.
units.tr: Handle of a vessel] The handle of a ladle (Cicero). A little handle (Valerius Maximus). A grip (Terence). See Manubrium, Occasio.

units.la: Ansatus] Amentatus, Cic. Subtentus lectus loris, Cat. Cum manubrio, Cic.
units.tr: Having a handle] Having a handle (Cicero). A couch held up by straps (Cato). With a handle (Cicero).

units.la: Ante, Præpos.] Ante triennium. Abhinc triennium, Ter. Stabat pro templo, i.e. ante templum, Tacit. Sub exitu vitæ, Suet. i. e. ante exitum.
units.tr: Before, preposition] Three years before. Three years ago (Terence). He stood before the temple, that is, in front of the temple (Tacitus). At the end of life (Suetonius), that is, before the end.

units.la: Ante, Adverb.] Anteà. Jam anteà. Anteà cùm. Anteà quàm, Cic. Antehac nunquam, Ter. Tantum hodie dixi, quantum antehac nunquam. Id miraculi vidi, antehac nunquam, Er. Priùs, Tibul. Dudum, Plaut.
units.tr: Before, adverb] Formerly. Already before. Before when. Before that (Cicero). Never before (Terence). Today I have spoken as much as never before. I saw a miracle, never before (Erasmus). Earlier (Tibullus). Long ago (Plautus).

units.la: Antecedere] vid. Præcedere.
units.tr: To go before] See Praecedere.

units.la: Antecellere] Superare aliquem doctrinâ, Cic. Vincere authoritate. Excellere ingenio. Præterire aliquem ætate. Præstare cæteris prudentiâ, Cic. Supergredi aliquem, Stat. Antevenire aliquem, Salust. Antepollere cunctis, Apul. vide Eminere.
units.tr: To surpass] To surpass someone in learning (Cicero). To conquer by authority. To excel in talent. To outstrip someone in age. To excel others in prudence (Cicero). To go beyond someone (Statius). To come before someone (Sallust). To outshine all (Apuleius). See Eminere.

units.la: Antecessor] Præcursor, Cic. Antecursor, Cæs. Anteambulo, Mart. Præventor, Amm. Præminister, Macrob. Prodromus, Cic. Præclamator, Fest. Antecursorius, Apul. Præcidaneus, pro Præcedaneus, Gell.
units.tr: Predecessor] Forerunner (Cicero). Advance guard (Caesar). Walker before (Martial). Anticipator (Ammianus). Pre-minister (Macrobius). Herald (Cicero). Crier before (Festus). Going before (Apuleius). Præcidaneus, for Præcedaneus (Gellius).

units.la: Anteferendus omnibus] Primus omnium, Ter. Primarum partium actor, Cic Primiceps, Var. In jure civili, in Astrologia princeps, Cic. Vir in eloquentia præcipuus, Quint. In principibus est, Cic. Apud Reges Rex perhibetur, Plaut. Alpha penulatorum, Mart. Regulus sutorum cerdo, Id. Deus. In hoc tu mihi Deus videris, Cic. Flos Poëtarum, Plaut. Optimæ notæ vinum, Col. Primæ pressuræ oleum, Id. Eminentissimus in eloquentia, Quint. Vid. Primarius.
units.tr: To be preferred above all] First of all (Terence). Leader of the first rank (Cicero). First head (Varro). In civil law, in astrology, a prince (Cicero). A man pre-eminent in eloquence (Quintilian). He is among the chiefs (Cicero). Among kings he is called king (Plautus). The alpha of cobblers (Martial). The little king of shoemakers (Martial). A god: in this you seem to me a god (Cicero). The flower of poets (Plautus). Wine of the finest quality (Columella). Oil of the first pressing (Columella). Most eminent in eloquence (Quintilian). See Primarius.

units.la: Anteferre] Anteponere aliquid alicui, Cic. Antehabe-re, Tac. Habere potiùs, Cæf. Dare palmam alicui, Cic. Primas, priores tribuere. Præponere, Cic. Præver-tere, Plaut. Antiquius habere, Cic. Ducere, Bud. Præoptare, Liv. Præferre aliquid alicui, Cic.
units.tr: To prefer] To put one thing before another (Cicero). To hold in higher regard (Tacitus). To hold rather (Caesar). To give the palm to someone (Cicero). To give first, prior places. To set before (Cicero). To turn aside (Plautus). To hold more dear (Cicero). To lead (Budaeus). To choose before (Livy). To prefer one thing to another (Cicero).

units.la: Antelucano tempore] Sublucanis temporibus, Plin. Ante primitias lucis. Principio lucis. Prope confinia lucis, Amm. Appetente luce, Tacit. Priusquam lucescat, Plaut. Ante-lucano. Antelucio. Anteluculo, Apul.
units.tr: Before dawn] In the dim times of daylight (Pliny). Before the first breath of light. At the beginning of light. Near the borders of light (Ammianus). As the light draws near (Tacitus). Before it grows light (Plautus). Before dawn (Apuleius).

units.la: Antelucanus] Antelucana lucubratio. Sublucanus, Plin.
units.tr: Done before dawn] Work done by lamplight before dawn (Pliny).

units.la: Antequam] Priusquam, & Prius quàm. Prius de probro, quàm de re, Cic.
units.tr: Before: priusquam, and prius quam. "First the disgrace, then the matter" (Cic.).

units.la: Anterior] Adversus, Cic. Adversæ cicatrices. Anticus, Fest.
units.tr: Former: opposed to, Cic. Scars on the face. Anticus, Fest.

units.la: Anterior pars] Priora & terga, Plin. In primum (aciei) infestis hastis involabant, Liv. Frons libri, Ovid. Caput je-cinoris, Liv. Primores ungues, Lucil. Primores dentes, Plin. Principia, i. e. primus ordo in acie, Tacit.
units.tr: Front part: the front and back parts, Plin. They rushed upon the first line with hostile spears, Liv. The front of a book, Ovid. The head of the liver, Liv. The foremost claws, Lucil. The front teeth, Plin. The principes, that is, the first rank in battle, Tacit.

units.la: Anterius] In antè ponere aliquid, Prop.
units.tr: To set in front: to place something in front, Prop.

units.la: Antesignanus] Campigenus, Veget. Antepilani, Liv. Hastati ante Triarios, Turneb.
units.tr: Standard-bearer: a fighter in the front rank, Veget. Forward troops, Liv. The hastati before the triarii, Turneb.

units.la: Antilena, Lorum ante pectus jumenti] Antela, Isid. Phaleræ, Virg. Iuv. interprete, Lypf. qui Phaleras planas, ad pectus equi demissas, pendere ait.
units.tr: Breast-strap, a strap before the animal's chest: Antela, Isid. Trappings, Virg. and Juv., as Lipsius explains it, saying the flat trappings hang down to the horse's chest.

units.la: Antipodes] Antichtones, Plin. Qui adversi nobis stant. Qui adversi nobis urgent vestigia. Antipodes, Cic. Circum-fundi undique terræ homines, conversisque inter se pedibus stare, ait Plin.
units.tr: Antipodes: antichthones, Plin. Those who stand opposite us; those who press their soles against ours. Antipodes, Cic. Pliny says men are spread round the earth on every side and stand with their feet turned towards one another.

units.la: Antiquè, more antiquo] Antiquo opere. Antiquissimo artificio factus. Obsoletè vestitus. Priscè agere. Cic. Moribus antiquis vivere, Plaut. More majorum, severè, graviter, Cic.
units.tr: In the old manner, after the ancient custom: in an old style; made with the most ancient craft; dressed in old-fashioned clothes; to act in the old way, Cic. To live by ancient customs, Plaut. In the manner of our ancestors, strictly and seriously, Cic.

units.la: Antiquitas] Antiquitas generis, Cic. Antiqui mores, vel Prisca vivendi forma. Vetustas, Cic. Cana antiquitas, Caf.
units.tr: Antiquity: antiquity of birth, Cic. Old customs, or the ancient way of life. Age, Cic. Hoary antiquity, Caf.

units.la: Antiquitùs] Antiquitùs duravit mos, Quint. Vetustissimè in usu est, Plin. A prisci s Majoribus, Amm. Opinio inde usque ab Heroicis temporibus ad nos deducta, Cic. Ab Aborigenum seculo, Er.
units.tr: In ancient times: the custom has lasted from antiquity, Quint. It is in use from the most ancient times, Plin. Handed down from our ancestors, Amm. The opinion handed down to us from the heroic times, Cic. From the age of the Aborigines, Er.

units.la: Antiquus] Antiquior memoriâ nostrâ. Antiquissimum vetustate municipium, Cic. Vetusta disciplina, Id. Ex vetustate verba, Quint. Fundatissima familia. Tua nobilitas, Servi Sulpici, hominibus literatis & historicis est notior; populo vero obscurior, Cic. Vetus prosapia, Salust. Aborigenes, de quavis gente antiquissimâ, Sipont. Terrâ orti, Quint. Antiquior quàm Chaos & Saturnus, Er. Vid. Priscus.
units.tr: Ancient: older than our memory. The most ancient town by age, Cic. Old discipline, Id. Words from antiquity, Quint. A very well-established family. Your nobility, Servius Sulpicius, is better known to learned men and historians, but more obscure to the common people, Cic. An old lineage, Sall. Aborigines, of any most ancient people, Sipont. Born of the earth, Quint. Older than Chaos and Saturn, Er. See Priscus.

units.la: Antiqui, ante hoc ævum] Veteres illi. Veteres & prisci viri superiori memoriâ cives, Cic. Antiquorum auctoritas. Patres, majoresque nostri. Fuit vir eruditus apud Patres nostros, Cic. Ut ab instituto superiorum non recedatur, Id. Priores nostri, Plin. Antiquitas, fabulosa narravit, Id. Priscus mos. Prisca Religio, Ovid. Antiqua fides, virtus, Er.
units.tr: The ancients, those of earlier ages: those old men. Old and ancient men, citizens of earlier memory, Cic. The authority of the ancients. The fathers and our forefathers. There was a learned man among our fathers, Cic. That one should not depart from the practice of our predecessors, Id. Our predecessors, Plin. Antiquity has told fabulous stories, Id. Ancient custom. Ancient religion, Ovid. Ancient faith and virtue, Er.

units.la: Antiquitatem sermonis imitari] Cum Evandri matre loqui, Gell.
units.tr: To imitate the antiquity of speech: to speak with the mother of Evander, Gell.

units.la: Anus, i] Ima excrementorum via, Cic. Et Plinius de Ibi ave, per eam se partem proluens, quâ onera ciborum reddi maximè salubre est. Exitus naturalis, Col. Posticum, Arnob.
units.tr: Anus, the fundament: the lowest passage of the excrement, Cic. Pliny, of the ibis, which washes out that part through which it is most healthful to void the load of food. Natural exit, Col. Back passage, Arnob.

units.la: Anus, us] Annua, i, anus, Scal. Vetula, Plaut. Accedo aniculam quandam, & rogo, inquam, mater, nunquid scis, &c. Petron.
units.tr: Anus, an old woman: annua, anus, Scal. An old woman, Plaut. "I approached a certain old woman and asked, Mother, do you know anything, etc.," Petron.

units.la: Anxius vid. Solicitus. Anxietas, Solicitudo.
units.tr: Anxious: see Solicitous. Anxiety: solicitude.

units.la: Apage. Vid. Abi.
units.tr: Begone: see Go away.

units.la: Aper] Silvaticus sus, Var.
units.tr: Boar: a wild pig, Var.

units.la: Aprinus] Aprugnum callum, Plaut. Apraria retia, Paul. IC.
units.tr: Of or like a boar: a hard boar's hide, Plaut. Boar-hunting nets, Paul. IC.

units.la: Aperire] Adaperire literas, Cic. Patefacere portam, Liv. Totum ostium patefacere. Fores longè reducere. Refupinare valvas, Propert. Pandere januam, Plaut. Relinere dolium, Ter. Recludere armarium, Plaut. Referare fores, Ovid. Resignare literas, Cic. Admittere lucem totis fenestris, Ovid. Quod non in calcarium suum latis specularibus diem admiserat, Sen. Explicare volumen, Evolvere, Cic. Returare aures, Var. Rescindere os ulceris, Virg. Restringere dentes, Plaut. Repandere fores januæ, Apul.
units.tr: To open: to open a letter, Cic. To throw open a gate, Liv. To open a door completely. To draw the doors wide apart. To push back the folding doors, Propert. To throw open a door, Plaut. To unstop a cask, Ter. To unlock a cupboard, Plaut. To unbar the doors, Ovid. To unseal a letter, Cic. To admit light through all the windows, Ovid. He had not let daylight into his corner through wide windows, Sen. To unroll a scroll, to unfold, Cic. To unstop the ears, Var. To open the mouth of a wound, Virg. To unclench the teeth, Plaut. To spread open the doors of a gate, Apul.

units.la: Aperte] Patenter, Cic. Omnia aperta habeo, i, aperte ago.
units.tr: Openly: openly, Cic. I have everything open, that is, I act openly.

units.la: Aperte loqui in publico] Cœlo ac terræ loqui.
units.tr: To speak openly in public: to speak to heaven and earth.

units.la: Apertilis] Adapertilis, Ovid. Apertissimum, promptis-simumque, Cic.
units.tr: Open: open, Ovid. Most open and most ready, Cic.

units.la: Aperte, sine fuco] Latinè loqui. Summo pectore.
units.tr: Openly, without pretence: to speak plain Latin. With full heart.

units.la: Apertura] Apertura in pariete, Vitruv. Pator, oris, Apul. Ad amplitudinem & patorem narium. Illatebra, Plaut.
units.tr: Opening: an opening in a wall, Vitruv. The opening and width of the nostrils, Apul. A hiding place, Plaut.

units.la: Apertus] Patens porta, Virg. Patulæ fenestræ, Ovid. Reclusæ fores, Ovid.
units.tr: Open: an open gate, Virg. Open windows, Ovid. Unlocked doors, Ovid.

units.la: Apes] Bugones Var. (i. bovis soboles, quòd ex bobus mortuis nascantur.) Mater mellis, Var. Melissa, Rhodius.
units.tr: Bees: bugones, Var. (that is, offspring of cattle, because they are born from dead oxen.) Mother of honey, Var. Melissa, Rhodius.

units.la: Apex. vid. Accentus, Cacumen.
units.tr: Apex: see Accent, Summit.

units.la: Apexabo] Intestinum sanguine & pingui plenum, Sipont. Longabo, Langano, onis Var. Longavo, Arnob.
units.tr: Apexabo: an intestine full of blood and fat, Sipont. Longabo, Langano, Var. Longavo, Arnob.

units.la: Apiana vitis] Muscatula, Sipont. Stica vitis, Plin. Vinum Falernum, Mart.
units.tr: Apiana vine: muscatel, Sipont. Stica vine, Plin. Falernian wine, Mart.

units.la: Apiarium] Alvearium. Mellarium, Var. Mellifica loca, Pallad. Mellitotrophium, Var. Apum cubilia, Pabulationes. Pastiones, Col. Apum statio, Castra, Pallad.
units.tr: Apiary: a beehive. A place for honey, Var. Places producing honey, Pallad. Honey-house, Var. Beds of bees, their feeding grounds. Pastures, Col. Station or camp of bees, Pallad.

units.la: Apiarius] Mellarius. Melliturgus, Var. Curator apum, Scal. ex Var.
units.tr: Beekeeper: a honey-keeper. A honey-worker, Var. A keeper of bees, Scal., from Var.

units.la: Apocha] Apodixis, Petron. Acceptilatio, Vlp.
units.tr: Receipt: a proof of payment, Petron. Acceptilation, Ulp.

units.la: Apologus] Mythistoria, Iul. Cap. Mythistorica volumina, Vopisc.
units.tr: Fable: a mythical story, Jul. Cap. Mythical histories, Vopisc.

units.la: Apophthegma] Dictum breve & sententiosum, Camer. Sententia breviter enunciata, Bud. Breviter & acutè dictum, Er.
units.tr: Apophthegm: a short and pithy saying, Camer. A sentence briefly stated, Bud. A briefly and sharply spoken remark, Er.

units.la: Apoplecticus] Sideratus, Plin. Sidere percussus, Mart. Sidere afflatus, Gorr.
units.tr: Struck by apoplexy: struck by a star, Plin. Smitten by a star, Mart. Blasted by a star, Gorr.

units.la: Apoplexia] Resolutio membrorum totius corporis, Celf. Attonitus. Stupor. id. Sideratio, Scribon. Ictus sanguinis, Sext. Aurel. Victor. Solstitialis morbus, Plaut. Patagus, Fest.
units.tr: Apoplexy: loss of movement of the limbs of the whole body, Cels. Stunned; stupor, id. Blasting by a star, Scribon. A stroke of blood, Sext. Aurel. Victor. The summer sickness, Plaut. Patagus, Fest.

units.la: Apostata] Desertor, Cic. Defector, Suet. Fœdifragus. Profugus, Ovid. Transfuga, Cic.
units.tr: Apostate: deserter, Cic. Defector, Suet. Breaker of faith. Fugitive, Ovid. Renegade, Cic.

units.la: Apostema, vid. Suppuratio. Vomica.
units.tr: Abscess: see Suppuration. Boil.

units.la: Apostolus] Legatus Christi ad Gentes.
units.tr: Apostle: an envoy of Christ to the Gentiles.

units.la: Apparare] Comparare cœnam, Ludos, Ter. Præstruere, Apul. Instituere dapes, Virg. Obsonare prandium, Plaut. i.comparare. Instruere epulas, Liv. Adornare nuptias, Plaut. Dapinare victum, Plaut. Præsternere aliquid, Plin. Machinari aliquid, Cic.!
units.tr: To prepare: to prepare a dinner or games, Ter. To set in order beforehand, Apul. To lay out a feast, Virg. To provide a meal, Plaut., that is, to arrange. To set out a banquet, Liv. To get a wedding ready, Plaut. To prepare food, Plaut. To lay something out, Plin. To contrive something, Cic.!

units.la: Apparatus] Paratus regius, Principalis, Tacit. Instrustus. Ornatus scenæ, fori. Instrumentum triumphi, oratoris, aulæ, regni, Cic, Apparatio. Præparatio. Comparatio, Id. Pararium, Sen. Instructio balnei, Plin. Munimen ad imbres, Col. Scenâ minore, i. apparatu. Habitus triumphalis, Quint.
units.tr: Equipment: a royal or princely retinue, Tacit. Furnishing. The stage or forum fittings. The trappings of a triumph, of an orator, a court or a kingdom, Cic. Preparation. Comparison, Id. A storehouse, Sen. The furnishing of a bath, Plin. Protection against rain, Col. With a smaller stage, that is, with less equipment. Triumphal dress, Quint.

units.la: Apparere] Comparet vestigium. Vestigia exstant. Paret, pro Apparet, Cic. Visebantur ornamenta, quorum exigua pars comparet, Liv. Occurrunt oculis tot paludes, tot campi, Col. Elucere. Enitere. Eminere. Patere. Objici, Cic. Spectari, Plaut.
units.tr: To appear: a trace appears; traces remain. It appears, for apparet, Cic. Ornaments were seen, of which a small part is visible, Liv. So many marshes and so many fields meet the eye, Col. To shine forth. To strive. To stand out. To lie open. To be exposed to view, Cic. To be seen, Plaut.

units.la: Apparere non facit esse] Barba non facit Philosophum. Non omnes Sancti, qui calcant limina templi. Barbâ tenus vir, vel Philosophus. Formosus sine pulchritudine. Plumas video, aves non video.
units.tr: Appearance does not make the thing: the beard does not make the philosopher. Not all who tread the threshold of the temple are saints. A man only in his beard, or a philosopher. Handsome without beauty. I see feathers, I do not see the bird.

units.la: Apparitor] Apparitio, pro Apparitoribus, Amm. Officialis, Apul. Servus publicus, Cic. Lictor, Cic. Plaut. Submotor, Liv. Virgator, Plaut. Accersitor, Plin. Officiorum tristium minister, Amm. Mastigophorus, Bud. Locarius, Gell.
units.tr: Attendant, apparitor: the attendants, Amm. An official, Apul. A public servant, Cic. A lictor, Cic., Plaut. An usher, Liv. A whipper, Plaut. A summoner, Plin. A minister of unpleasant duties, Amm. A staff-bearer, Bud. A porter, Gell.

units.la: Appellare, vid. Nominare.
units.tr: To call: see To name.

units.la: Appellare ad Superiorem] Appellare Tribunos, Prætorem, Plebem. A Prætore ad Tribunos, Cic. Cum alter ad Tribunos, alter ad Senatum provocâssct, Id.
units.tr: To appeal to a superior: to appeal to the tribunes, the praetor, the people. From the praetor to the tribunes, Cic. When one appealed to the tribunes and the other to the senate, Id.

units.la: Appellatio est libera] Appellare & mendicare cuilibet liberum.
units.tr: An appeal is free: anyone is free to appeal and to beg.

units.la: Appellere] Adigere oris, Plaut. Vis ventorum navem coëgit. Necessitas nos detrusit, Cic.
units.tr: To drive ashore: to drive a ship to land, Plaut. The force of the winds drove the ship on. Necessity drove us on, Cic.

units.la: Appendere] Affigere, Cic. Suspendere aliquid collo, Col. Suspendere ex cervice aliquid, Plin. Librare: Librat corpus in alas avis, Ovid. Affigere in aliquo, Cic. Figere in æde, Liv. Figere postibus, Virg. Affigere alicui, Plin.
