units.tr: To hang on: to fasten, Cic. To hang something on the neck, Col. To hang something from the neck, Plin. To balance: the bird balances its body on its wings, Ovid. To fix on something, Cic. To fix in a temple, Liv. To fasten to posts, Virg. To attach to someone, Plin.

units.la: Appendix, vid. Additamentum.
units.tr: Appendix: see Addition.

units.la: Appetere, in specie cibum] Palatum exacuere, Ovid. Obsonare sonare famem ambulando, Cic. Solicitat stomachum meum aliquid, Plin. Accenditur desiderium panis, Id. Lassum pervellunt stomachum sifer, alec, Hor. Salivam commovere.
units.tr: To desire food by appearance: to sharpen the palate, Ovid. To make hunger sound by walking about, Cic. Something stirs my stomach, Plin. Desire for bread is kindled, Id. Sharp and bitter things rouse the weary stomach, Hor. To stir the saliva.

units.la: Appetere nimia, noxium] Camelus cornua desiderans, & aures amisit.
units.tr: To desire too much, harmful: the camel, desiring horns, lost its ears.

units.la: Appetitus] Appetentia, Appetitio. Declinatio naturalis. Cupido. Impetus animi. Libido. Stomachus, Cic. Cupiditas cibi, Celf. Orexis, Iuv. Conatus ad naturales pastus capessendos, Cic. Affectio animi, Cic.
units.tr: Appetite: appetency, appetition. Natural inclination. Desire. Impulse of the mind. Lust. Stomach, Cic. Craving for food, Cels. Orexis, Juv. An effort to seize natural food, Cic. A disposition of the mind, Cic.

units.la: Applaudere] Adhinnire ad orationem alicujus. Admurmurare, Cic. Excipere plausu, strepitu. Approbare plausu. Clamore comprobare. Una voce approbent omnes, Cic. Plausum dare, Impertiri, Id. Adstrepere huic alacre vulgus, Tac. Succlamare, Cic. Favere linguis, Horat.
units.tr: To applaud: to murmur approval at someone's speech. To murmur in assent, Cic. To receive with applause and noise. To approve by applause. To confirm with a shout. Let all approve with one voice, Cic. To give applause, to bestow it, Id. The eager crowd applauded him, Tac. To shout out in support, Cic. To favour with the tongue, Hor.

units.la: Applausus] Acclamatio populi, Cic. Plausus multiplex a toto consessu datus, Id. Secundus clamor, Virg. Admurmuratio secunda, Cic.
units.tr: Applause: acclamation of the people, Cic. Repeated applause given by the whole assembly, Id. A second shout, Virg. A second murmur of approval, Cic.

units.la: Applicare] Adhibere ad Cic. Apprimere carnem ad offa, Plin. Admovere. Adferere, Fest.
units.tr: To apply: to bring to, Cic. To press meat onto morsels, Plin. To bring close. To bring forward, Fest.

units.la: Apponere] Applicare, Horat. Superponere medicamentis aliquid, Plin.
units.tr: To put on: to apply, Hor. To put something on top of medicines, Plin.

units.la: Appositè, vid. Aptè.
units.tr: Appositely: see Aptly.

units.la: Approbare] Attestari. Subscribere in crimen, Cic. Adstipulari alicui, Plin. Gratulatur mihi gestu accusator, Cic. Album calculum addere. Creta, vel cresså notare. Cursu vadere in sententiam, Cic. Utroque pollice laudare. Pollicem premere, Hor. Vid. Cedere authoritati.
units.tr: To approve: to bear witness. To join in an accusation, Cic. To agree with someone, Plin. The accuser congratulates me with a gesture, Cic. To add a white pebble. To mark with chalk or white chalk. To pass over to an opinion by moving across, Cic. To praise with both thumbs. To press the thumb down, Hor. See To yield to authority.

units.la: Approbator] Confirmator.
units.tr: Approbator] A confirmer.

units.la: Appropinquare] Imminet bellum, Liv. Impendet fatum. Instat dies. Adventat tempus. Proximat alicui, Cic. Appetit nox, Liv. Ingruit frigus, Col.
units.tr: Appropinquare] War is imminent, Liv. Fate hangs over. The day presses on. The time is at hand. He draws near to someone, Cic. Night approaches, Liv. Cold sets in, Col.

units.la: Apricari] Soli aperto se committere, Celf. Soliculari, & Solicitari, Casaub.
units.tr: Apricari] To expose oneself to the open sun, Celf. To bask in the sun, and to be warmed, Casaub.

units.la: Apricus] Expositus locus solis, Plin. Ostentus soli ager, Cato. Insolatæ vites, Col. Apricum, pro loco aprico, Hor.
units.tr: Apricus] A place exposed to the sun, Plin. A field open to the sun, Cato. Vines warmed by the sun, Col. Apricum, for a sunny place, Hor.

units.la: Aptare] Comparare se, Conformare mentem aliquâ cogitacogitatione, Cic. Attemperat sibi gladium, Sen. i. e. accommodat aptè ad feriendum, vel ut feriatur ipse.
units.tr: Aptare] To prepare oneself, to fit one's mind to some thought, Cic. He fits the sword to himself, Sen. that is, he adjusts it suitably for striking, or so that he himself may be struck.

units.la: Aptare omnia omnibus] Eodem collyrio mederi omnibus. Omni pedi eundem calceum induere. Uno calopodio omnes calceare.
units.tr: Aptare omnia omnibus] To heal everyone with the same eye-salve. To put the same shoe on every foot. To shoe everyone with one sandal.

units.la: Apta aptis conveniunt] Dignum patellâ operculum. Quaere uxorem aptam tuis moribus, Aptam ad tuos mores.
units.tr: Apta aptis conveniunt] A lid that fits its pan. Seek a wife suited to your morals, suited to your manners.

units.la: Aptè] Appositè. Accommodatè, Cic. Probè, Id. Cadit aptè in rem. Scitè factum. Macte, Cic. Ex pictura adstitit, Plaut. Ad propositum, Ulp. Ad rogata respondere, Cic. Hic agit magis ex argumento, Plaut. Habiliter, Paul. IC. Aptè quadrat. Commodè, Cic. Accommodissime jungi poterit, Quint. Cohaerentius, Gell. Congruenter ad id quod agitur. Idoneè accommodans oratio ad, Cic. E re natâ fieri me huic haud potuit. (quasi è re natum,) Ter.
units.tr: Aptè] Fittingly. Suitably, Cic. Properly, Id. It fits the matter well. Done cleverly. Well done, Cic. He stood there as if from the picture, Plaut. To the point, Ulp. To answer the questions to the point, Cic. Here he argues more from the case itself, Plaut. Skilfully, Paul. IC. It fits exactly. Conveniently, Cic. It can be joined most fittingly, Quint. More coherently, Gell. Congruently with what is being done. A speech suitably adapted to, Cic. In this matter it could not have happened more fittingly for me (as if from a matter born), Ter.

units.la: Aptitudo] Commoditas ad faciendum idonea. Facultas ingenii. Habilitas corporis, Cic. Facilitas ingenii, Quint. Qualitas ingenii mediocris, Diomed. Opportunum. Opportuna locorum, Tac. Opportunitas loci, membrorum, Cic.
units.tr: Aptitudo] Suitability for doing something; a capacity for it. Natural ability. Bodily fitness, Cic. Facility of mind, Quint. A moderate quality of mind, Diomed. Opportuneness. Opportunity of places, Tac. Opportunity of place, of limbs, Cic.

units.la: Aptus] Accommodatum tempus ad aliquid. Appositus locus. Valet ad aliquid. Natus ad aliquid: huic rei, Cic. Idoneus est qui impetret. Idoneus est, ut impetret. Commoda via, Cic. Peridoneus castris locus, Caes. Ad pedem. (scil. quadrat.) Natus rebus agendis. Natus publico bono. Tempestivum mare, Cic. Oculus perturbatus, non est benè affectus ad suum munus fungendum. Habilis homo, Cic.
units.tr: Aptus] A suitable time for something. A well-placed location. Useful for something. Born for something: for this business, Cic. He is fit to obtain it. He is fit so that he may obtain it. A convenient road, Cic. A very suitable place for a camp, Caes. Fitting to the foot (sc. fits). Born for conducting affairs. Born for the public good. A sea suitable for sailing, Cic. An eye that is disturbed is not well disposed to perform its function. A capable man, Cic.

units.la: Apud] Ad me fuit, Cic. Ad exercitum manere, Caes. In vulgus nomen retinere. Penes me erat, Cic. Et id gratum fuisse adversum te, habeo gratiam, i. e. apud te, Ter. Pro foribus religato cane, Suet.
units.tr: Apud] It was with me, Cic. To remain with the army, Caes. To keep a name among the common people. It was in my keeping, Cic. And that it was pleasing to you, I am obliged to you, that is, with you, Ter. The dog being tied up before the doors, Suet.

units.la: Aqua] Lympha, Lucr. Unda, Id. Lues, apud Petron. pro aquâ liquidâ, oppositâ glaciei, Turneb. Fontibus obruere. (Fontibus pro aquâ.) Pulveris terreni glutinamentum. Sitis levamentum. Refectrix rerum & putrefactrix: Rerum molimentum.
units.tr: Aqua] Water: lymph, Lucr. wave, Id. Lues, in Petron. for liquid water, as opposed to ice, Turneb. To overwhelm with springs (springs for water). The glue binding earthy dust. The relief of thirst. The restorer and destroyer of things. The mover of things.

units.la: Aquagium] Hydraulica machina, Vitruv. Aquae ductus, Cic. Inductio, Id. Aquae ductio, Ulp. Aquaelicium, Fest. Canalis structilis, Vitr. Rivus, Vlp. Cuniculus rivi ad piscinam perducatur, Col.
units.tr: Aquagium] A hydraulic machine, Vitruv. A water-channel, Cic. Introduction of water, Id. Conduction of water, Ulp. Rain-making, Fest. A built channel, Vitr. A stream, Ulp. Let a conduit be led to the pool, Col.

units.la: Aqualiculus] Canaliculus,Col. Alveolus,Id. Linter, Cat.
units.tr: Aqualiculus] A small channel, Col. A trough, Id. A tub, Cat.

units.la: Aqualis,scil. Vrceus] Guttus, Liv. Gutturnium, Fest. Trulleum, Non. Urceus manalis, Sipont.
units.tr: Aqualis, sc. Urceus] A jug, Liv. A pitcher, Fest. A basin, Non. A flowing jug, Sipont.

units.la: Aquaria mola] Hydraula, Vitruv. Hydromyla, Iun. Molinæ, Amm.
units.tr: Aquaria mola] A water-mill, Vitruv. A water-mill, Iun. Mills, Amm.

units.la: Aquari pecudes] Dare potatum bubus, Col. Salivare ægrum pecus medicamine, Id.
units.tr: Aquari pecudes] To give drink to oxen, Col. To treat a sick flock with medicine to make it salivate, Id.

units.la: Aquarium, (1) ubi jumenta aquantur] Aquatio, Col. Pabula & aquationes pecudum mutare. Canalis aquationi destinatus, Id.
units.tr: Aquarium, (1) where beasts are watered] Watering, Col. To change the pasture and watering places of the cattle. A channel set apart for watering, Id.

units.la: (2) Latrina, quâ sordes effluunt] Lavatrina. Urinarium, Var. Labrum. Eluacrum, Cato. Aquariolum,Iun. Fusoria coquinæ procul sint apibus, Pallad.
units.tr: (2) A latrine, through which filth drains away] A washing-trough. A urinal, Var. A basin. A drain-trough, Cato. A little drain, Iun. Kitchen melting-pots should be kept far from the bees, Pallad.

units.la: Aquarius] Aquator, Cæs. Utrarius, Liv. Astronomis Amphora.
units.tr: Aquarius] A water-carrier, Cæs. A bucket-carrier, Liv. To astronomers, the Water-pot (Amphora).

units.la: Aquaticus] Aquatilis mus, Plin. Aquatilis bestia, Cic.
units.tr: Aquaticus] A water mouse, Plin. An aquatic beast, Cic.

units.la: Aquatile] Æquoreum genus. Natantum genus, Virg. Natatilia, Rob. Steph. Iun.
units.tr: Aquatile] A sea-kind. A kind of swimming creatures, Virg. Swimming things, Rob. Steph. Iun.

units.la: Aqueus,aquæ similis] Undatus, Plin. Undatim crispus,Id. Aquosa crystallus, Propert. Vitreus, Horat. Vitro æmulus fluvius, Apul. Hyalus color. Hyali fucatus colore. Plumbeus color. Thyles, Glaucinus, Mart. Galbineus, Veget. Color cæruleus dilutior, Id.
units.tr: Aqueus, similar to water] Waved, Plin. rippling in waves, Id. Watery crystal, Propert. Glassy, Horat. A river rivalling glass, Apul. A hyaline colour. Coloured with a hyaline hue. A lead colour. Thyles, glaucous, Mart. Galbineus, Veget. A paler blue colour, Id.

units.la: Aquila] Regalis avis, Apul. Jovis ales,Virg. Avis magna, Plaut. Aquila, Vultur,Turneb. Avis præpes, Virg. Præpes, Val. Argon. Rex alitum.
units.tr: Aquila] The royal bird, Apul. Jove's bird, Virg. A great bird, Plaut. Eagle, vulture, Turneb. A swift bird, Virg. Swift, Val. Argon. King of the birds.

units.la: Aquilex] Indagator aquarum, Col. Librator, Plin. Aquarius, Front. Præfectus castello aquæ. Castellarius, Meurs. ex Veter. inscript.
units.tr: Aquilex] A seeker of water, Col. A surveyor, Plin. A water-carrier, Front. A prefect of a water-castle. A castellarius, Meurs. from old inscriptions.

units.la: Aquilus color] Luridus, Hor. Pullus, Vitruv. Fuscus. Infuscatus, Col. Impluviatus, Plaut. Hispanum. Thyles. Suasum, Plaut.
units.tr: Aquilus colour] Sallow, Hor. Dark, Vitruv. Dusky. Darkened, Col. Impluviatus, Plaut. Spanish. Thyles. Suasum, Plaut.

units.la: Aquosus] Aquosa nubes, Virg. Undosum æquor, P. Virg. Aquaticus Auster, Ovid. Aquatus, Plin.
units.tr: Aquosus] A watery cloud, Virg. The wavy sea, P. Virg. The watery south wind, Ovid. Watery, Plin.

units.la: Ara] Altare, Cic. Altare, Diis superis. Ara, Diis inferis, Fest.
units.tr: Ara] An altar, Cic. An altar for the gods above; an altar for the gods below, Fest.

units.la: Aranea] Araneola, Cic. Araneus, Col. Vermis aëris, Isid. Phalangium, & us, Plin. Myrmecion capite formicino, Id. Lupus, Id. Araneus cavernarum. Lycus, Rhagion. Muscarum venatrix.
units.tr: Aranea] A little spider, Cic. Spider-like, Col. A worm of the air, Isid. Phalangium, Plin. A myrmecion with an ant-like head, Id. Lupus, Id. A cave spider. Lycus, Rhagion. A catcher of flies.

units.la: Aranea marina] Maja, Gaz. Cancer rotundus, araneæ similis. Pagurus, Plin. Squilla parva. Pinnoteres, Cic. Annophylax, Plin.
units.tr: Aranea marina] Maja, Gaz. A round crab like a spider. Pagurus, Plin. A small squilla. Pinnoteres, Cic. Annophylax, Plin.

units.la: Arare] Inarare. Subarare, Plin. Subigere terram, Cic. Perarare, Ovid. Proscindere agrum, Col. Colere agrum, Cic. Vertere agrum, Plin. Excolere rura, Claud. Recolere terram desertam, Liv. Infindere sulcos telluri. Sollicitare terram, tellurem, Virg. Rostrare vomere superiora terræ, Plin.
units.tr: Arare] To plough in. To plough under, Plin. To subdue the soil, Cic. To plough through, Ovid. To cut open a field, Col. To tend a field, Cic. To turn over a field, Plin. To cultivate the countryside, Claud. To recultivate deserted land, Liv. To cut furrows into the earth. To stir up the ground, Virg. To break the upper surface of the earth with the ploughshare, Plin.

units.la: Aratio] Cultus, Cultio, Cultura agri, Cic. Politio, Cat. Proscissio terræ, Col. Sulcamen, Apul.
units.tr: Aratio] Tillage, cultivation, the cultivation of fields, Cic. Polishing, Cat. The turning up of earth, Col. A ploughed furrow, Apul.

units.la: Arator, vid. Agricola.
units.tr: Arator, see Agricola.

units.la: Arbiter] Honorarius arbiter. Sequester. Finium regendorum præfectus. Editititius autem Judex est, quem una pars eligi, Cic. Diæteta, vel Diætetes, Rhodius. Bud. Discéptator, Vlp. Strictus judex, Fest. Pacator, Sen. Vid. Pacificator.
units.tr: Arbiter] An honorary arbiter. A sequester. A prefect for settling boundaries. An editicius judge, however, is one whom one party chooses, Cic. A dietetes, or Diaetetes, a Rhodian, Bud. A mediator, Ulp. A strict judge, Fest. A pacifier, Sen. See Pacificator.

units.la: Arbitrari, vid. Censere.
units.tr: Arbitrari, see Censere.

units.la: Arbitrario, pro lubitu] Arbitratu suo loqui. Ad arbitrium suum navigare. Ad libidinem aliquid fingere. Quantum libido tulit, tantum relictum est, Cic. Suopte ingenio, Liv. Sponte suâ vivere, Lucr. Suo stomacho vivere, Plin. Meis auspiciis, Virg. i. meo arbitratu. Tua facultas. Tua potestas ejus rei est, Cic.
units.tr: Arbitrario, at pleasure] To speak at one's own discretion. To sail as one wishes. To invent something as one pleases. As much as desire carried, so much was left, Cic. By one's own nature, Liv. To live of one's own accord, Lucr. To live by one's own temper, Plin. By my own auspices, Virg. that is, at my own discretion. It is your ability, your power over that matter, Cic.

units.la: Arbitrarius] Arbitralis judicatio, Macr. Pacificatorius. Pacificatoria legatio, Cic.
units.tr: Arbitrarius] A judgement by arbitration, Macr. Pacificatory. A pacificatory embassy, Cic.

units.la: Arbitrium, arbitri judicium] Arbitrarium decretum, Sipont. Arbitramentum, Id. & Vlp.
units.tr: Arbitrium, the judgement of an arbiter] An arbitrary decree, Sipont. An award, Id. & Vlp.

units.la: Arbitrium, arbitrandi voluntas] Liberum arbitrium, Liv. Libera hominis voluntas, Cic. vid. Liberum est.
units.tr: Arbitrium, the will to decide] Free choice, Liv. The free will of a man, Cic. See Liberum est.

units.la: Arbitrii alient. vid. Alieni arbitrii.
units.tr: Arbitrii alient., see Alieni arbitrii.

units.la: Arbor] Arbos, Virg. Robur, Plin. Humanum humo fixum corpus.
units.tr: Arbor] A tree, Virg. Oak, hardwood, Plin. A human body fixed in the ground.

units.la: Arborator] Putator, Plin. Frondator, Virg. Plin. Consitor uvæ, Ovid. Inoculator. Colum.
units.tr: Arborator] A pruner, Plin. A stripper of leaves, Virg. Plin. A planter of vines, Ovid. A grafter, Colum.

units.la: Arbuscula] Arboris abortus. Arboris pumilio, Plin.
units.tr: Arbuscula] A stunted tree. A dwarf tree, Plin.

units.la: Arca] Cista, Cic. Scrinium, Iuv. Plin. Horat, Loculi recondendæ pecuniæ aut vesti, Mart. Septum aquarium, Bud.
units.tr: Arca] A chest, Cic. A coffer, a box, Iuv. Plin. Horat. Compartments for storing money or clothes, Mart. A water enclosure, Bud.

units.la: Arcanum] Mysterium: Hoc tacitum tanquam mysterium teneas, Cic. Secretum, Iuv. Celare operta magnifica sacrificiorum, Apul. Et qui solet ebrius fieri, non dari tacitum, Sen.
units.tr: Arcanum] A mystery: "keep this silent as a mystery," Cic. A secret, Iuv. To conceal the great mysteries of the sacrifices, Apul. And one who is wont to get drunk should not be given what must be kept silent, Sen.

units.la: Arcanum silendum] Ne interula quidem arcani conscia.
units.tr: Arcanum silendum] Not even the undershirt is privy to the secret.

units.la: Arcanus] Mystica sacra, Mart. Reconditá natura. Secretus locus. Obscurus. Intimus sermo. Tacitus sensus. Compressum odium. Abditus. Latens, Cic. Opertanea sacra, Plin.
units.tr: Arcanus] Mystic rites, Mart. A hidden nature. A secluded place. Obscure. Intimate speech. A hidden meaning. Suppressed hatred. Concealed. Lurking, Cic. Covered sacred rites, Plin.

units.la: Arcere] Abarcere vel abercere, Plin. Abigere à se. Depellere. Propellere. Repellere, Cic. Propulsare hostem ab aliquo loco, Id. Serva cives. Defende hostes, Enn. Protelare cladem. i, propulsare, Apul.
units.tr: Arcere] To keep away, Plin. To drive away from oneself. To thrust off. To push back. To repel, Cic. To drive the enemy from a place, Id. Save the citizens. Defend against enemies, Enn. To delay ruin, that is, to ward it off, Apul.

units.la: Archidux] Dux maximus. Regulus, Iun.
units.tr: Archidux] A chief leader. A petty king, Iun.

units.la: Archiepiscopus] Primas, in Iure Canonico.
units.tr: Archiepiscopus] A primate, in canon law.

units.la: Archimagirus] Prægustator culinæ, Arnob. Magister culinæ, Cromer.
units.tr: Archimagirus] A taster of the kitchen, Arnob. A master of the kitchen, Cromer.

units.la: Archithalassus] Trierarchus, Cic. Archigubernus, Iavolen. Dux præfectusque classis, Cic. Præpositus classi, Suet. Navarchus, Veget. Thalassiarchus, Horat.
units.tr: Archithalassus] A trierarch, Cic. A chief helmsman, Iavolen. A commander and prefect of the fleet, Cic. One set over the fleet, Suet. A navarch, Veget. A lord of the sea, Horat.

units.la: Architriclinus] Symposiarchus, Donat.
units.tr: Architriclinus] A master of the feast, Donat.

units.la: Archivum, vulgò Cancellaria] Tabularium, Cic. Officina diplomatica. Officina scribendorum & obsignandorum diplomatum. Indulgentiæ regiæ promptuarium. Juris æquitatisque promptuarium, & oraculum, Bud. Grammatophylacium, & Chartophylacium, Id.
units.tr: Archivum, commonly called Cancellaria] A record office, Cic. A office for drawing up and sealing documents. A workshop for writing and sealing diplomas. A storehouse of royal grants. A storehouse and oracle of law and equity, Bud. A keeper of writings and charters, Id.

units.la: Arcte] Angustè. Pressè. Compressè. Conserte, Contexte. Restrictè. Adstrictè, Cic. Conferte, Plin. Pressulè, Apul. Contentè habere aliquem, Cic. Strictissimè, Gell. Conjunctè, ius, issimè amare, Cic.
units.tr: Arcte] Narrowly. Closely. Compressed. Densely packed. Tightly woven. Restrictively. Tightly bound, Cic. Crowded together, Plin. Somewhat pressed, Apul. To hold someone closely and contentedly, Cic. Most strictly, Gell. Most intimately united, to love most closely, Cic.

units.la: Arctus] Restrictus, Tac. Adstrictus, Pressus, Cic. Constrictus, strĩctus, Plin. Strĩctus homo, Firm. Pilatus, Var. Arſtæ leges, Plin. Angusta pauperies, Hor.
units.tr: Arctus] Restricted, Tac. Bound tight, pressed close, Cic. Constricted, Plin. A tight-fisted man, Firm. Cramped, Var. Narrow laws, Plin. Narrow poverty, Hor.

units.la: Arcularius] Arcarius. Arcarum faber, Cæl. Rhodius. Capsarius. Levin. Hotoman. ex Suet. Capsarum opifex, Iun. Levin.
units.tr: Arcularius] A coffer-maker. A maker of chests, Cæl. Rhodius. A box-maker, Levin. Hotoman, from Suet. A craftsman of boxes, Iun. Levin.

units.la: Arcus] Vid. Iris. Fornix.
units.tr: Arcus] See Iris. Fornix.

units.la: Ardelio] Qui facillimè quidvis incipit & mox abjicit. Qui omnia & nihil agit, Sipont. Celocem regere nescit, & onerariam petit. Falcem in alienam messem immittens.
units.tr: Ardelio] One who very easily begins anything and soon drops it. One who does everything and accomplishes nothing, Sipont. He does not know how to steer a skiff, yet he makes for a freighter. Putting his sickle into another man's harvest.

units.la: Ardens] Flammans fax, Val. Argon. Flammatus Jupiter, Cic. Æstifer ignis, Lucr. Torridus aër, Prop. Ardentes oculos suffusus sanguine & igni, Virg.
units.tr: Ardens A flaming torch (Val. Argon.). Jupiter ablaze (Cic.). Heat-bearing fire (Lucr.). Torrid air (Prop.). Eyes burning, suffused with blood and fire (Virg.).

units.la: Ardere] Ardescit palea, Cic. Uri, Plin. Peruri, Ovid. Ignescit mundus. Torreri succensis ignibus, Cic. Torrescere flammis, Lucr. Debacchantur ignes, Horat. Populatur flamma capillos. Comprehendere ignem crinibus. Adolescunt ignibus arae. Dominatur flamma. Induitur flammis tota regio, Sil. Flagrare, Plin.
units.tr: Ardere Chaff catches fire (Cic.). To be burned (Plin.). To be burnt up (Ovid). The world catches fire. To be scorched by kindled fires (Cic.). To be parched with flames (Lucr.). The fires rage (Hor.). The flame lays waste the hair. To catch fire in the hair. The altars grow hot with fire. The flame prevails. The whole region is engulfed in flames (Sil.). To blaze (Plin.).

units.la: Ardescere, vid, Exardescere.
units.tr: Ardescere See Exardescere.

units.la: Ardor] Flagrantia, Cic. Æstuatio, Plin. transfulit ad animum.
units.tr: Ardor Burning (Cic.). Heat (Plin.). Transferred to the mind.

units.la: Arduus] Difficilis adscensu, Cic. Difficilis aditus, Ovid. Præceps saxum, Id.
units.tr: Arduus Hard to climb (Cic.). Difficult of access (Ovid). A steep rock (Id.).

units.la: Area] Cavum ædium testudinatum, Vitruv. Cavaedium, Plin. Iun. Hypæthrum. Locus subdialis. Loca in urbe pura, Vitruv. Testudo dicitur, si non tegitur, Rhodius.
units.tr: Area A vaulted hall of a house (Vitruv.). A courtyard (Plin. Iun.). An open-air space. An uncovered place. Places in the city kept clear (Vitruv.). It is called a testudo if it is not roofed (Rhodius).

units.la: Area, in horreis] Area frumento terendo, Cato. Area ad trituraм habilis, Col.
units.tr: Area, in barns A threshing floor for grinding corn (Cato). A floor suitable for threshing (Col.).

units.la: Arena] Glarea, Cic. Sabulum, Plin. Arenacea terra. Saburra, Vitruv. Sabuletum, Plin. Solum sitiens, siticulosum, siccaneum, Peraridum, Sabulosum, Col.
units.tr: Arena Gravel (Cic.). Sand (Plin.). Sandy ground. Gravel (Vitruv.). A sandy patch (Plin.). Thirsty, dry, parched, very dry, sandy ground (Col.).

units.la: Arere] Arescit lacryma, Cic. Adarere, Cat. Aridum fieri, Ovid. Exarescere, Cic. Obarescere, Lact. Assiccescere, Col. Exsiccescere, Vitr. Exsudat humor, Vitr. Serescunt in sole vestes, Lucr. Sitit tellus, Ovid. Siti necari. Siderationem sitire, Celf.
units.tr: Arere A tear dries up (Cic.). To dry up (Cato). To become dry (Ovid). To dry out thoroughly (Cic.). To parch (Lact.). To dry (Col.). To wither (Vitr.). Moisture evaporates (Vitr.). Clothes dry in the sun (Lucr.). The earth thirsts (Ovid). To die of thirst. To thirst from a blasting chill (Celsus).

units.la: Argentarius] Abaci custos, Cromer. Ab argento, (scil. servus.) Fulvius, Vrsin. Argen-
units.tr: Argentarius A keeper of accounts (Cromer.). From silver (sc. a slave). Fulvius (Ursin.). Argen-

units.la: Argentatus] Argentosus, Plin. Inargentatus, Id.
units.tr: Argentatus Rich in silver (Plin.). Unsilvered (Id.).

units.la: Argenteus] Electrei nummi, Lamprid. Electrina patera, Trebell. Pollio. Argennus Scal. ex Fest.
units.tr: Argenteus Coins of electrum (Lamprid.). A bowl of electrum (Trebell. Pollio). Argennus (Scal., from Fest.).

units.la: Argenti fodina] Argentaria, Liv. Scaptesula, Lucr. Argenteus puteus. Argentei fontes.
units.tr: Silver mine A silver mine (Liv.). A tunnel (Lucr.). A silver well. Silver springs.

units.la: Argentum] Massa argenti, Serv. Subterranea Luna.
units.tr: Argentum A mass of silver (Serv.). The underground moon.

units.la: Argentum vivum] Vomica liquoris æterni. Rerum omnium venenum. Dirâ tabe permanans omnia vasa. Exest. Plin. Hydrargyrum, Id.
units.tr: Quicksilver The vomit of an eternal liquid. The poison of all things. Seeping through everything with a dire corruption, it eats through all vessels (Plin.). Hydrargyrum (Id.).

units.la: Argilla] Lutum, Col. Lutum figulare, Plin. Terra figularis, Col. Creta figularis. Lutum paleatum, subactum, Plin.
units.tr: Argilla Mud (Col.). Potter's clay (Plin.). Potter's earth (Col.). Potter's chalk. Clay mixed with chaff, kneaded (Plin.).

units.la: Argillaceus] Luteus scyphus. Fictilis urna, Cic. Testaceum operimentum, Plin. Testeum corpus, Macrob. Samius, Cic. (à loco celebri)
units.tr: Argillaceus An earthenware cup. An earthen urn (Cic.). An earthen lid (Plin.). An earthen body (Macrob.). Samian ware (Cic.), from a famous place.

units.la: Argillosa terra] Solum pingue, ubereque glebâ, Virg.
units.tr: Clayey soil Rich soil with fertile clods (Virg.).

units.la: Arguere verbis] Redarguere, Castigare segnitiem alicujus. Objurgare molli brachio. Accusare de negligentiâ, vel negligentiæ, Cic. Aures mordaci radere vero. Atterere aures, Perf.
units.tr: Arguere verbis To rebuke, to chastise someone's sloth. To scold with a gentle hand. To accuse of negligence (Cic.). To scrape the ears with biting truth. To wear down the ears (Pers.).

units.la: Argumentum] Inventum in rem aliquam probabile aut necessarium, Cic. Documentum, Sal. Rationibus exquisitis disputare. Ratiuncula, Cic. Amentata hasta (i. e. argumentum validum,) Cic.
units.tr: Argumentum Something found to prove a matter probable or necessary (Cic.). Proof (Sal.). To dispute with sought-out reasons. A little argument (Cic.). A spear with a thong (that is, a strong argument) (Cic.).

units.la: Argumentum, summaria indicatio alicujus scripti] Lemma, Mart. Scena totius rei, Cic. Sententia concionis, Id. Periocha. Caput literarum, Cic. Substantia Orationis, Plin.
units.tr: Argumentum, a summary indication of some writing A heading or epigram (Mart.). The scene of the whole matter (Cic.). The gist of a speech (Id.). A summary (Periocha). The heading of a letter (Cic.). The substance of an oration (Plin.).

units.la: Argumentatio] Ratiocinatio. Inductio. Oratio, rebus non dubiis captans assensionem. Conclusio, Cic. Probatio, demonstratio, Bud. Collectio, Sen.
units.tr: Argumentatio Reasoning. Inference. A speech seeking assent with matters not in doubt. A conclusion (Cic.). Proof, demonstration (Bud.). A collection (Sen.).

units.la: Argutè] Artificiosè. Scitè, Cic. Tacitâ arte nocere, Ovid. Scrupulosè, Col. Acutè respondere, Er.
units.tr: Argutè Cunningly. Skilfully (Cic.). To harm by a hidden art (Ovid). Scrupulously (Col.). To answer sharply (Er.).

units.la: Argutie, vid. Sophisma.
units.tr: Argutie See Sophisma.

units.la: Argutus] Acutulæ conclusiones, Cic. Non inarguta sententia, Vlp. Nebulosum syrma, Fulg. OEdipus, (homo calidus, ænigmatibus solvendis idoneus.) Argutator, Er. Argutulus, Id.
units.tr: Argutus Sharp little conclusions (Cic.). An opinion not lacking subtlety (Ulp.). A cloudy phrase (Fulg.). Oedipus (a clever man, fit for solving riddles). A subtle debater (Er.). Somewhat subtle (Id.).

units.la: Aridè, Ariditas. Aridus, vid. Siccè &c.
units.tr: Aridè, dryness See Siccè etc.

units.la: Arietare] Arietant inter se, Sen. Caput opponis cum eo coruscans, Quint. Inter se adversi cornibus hædi, Virg. Coruscant agni, Lucr. Adversis concurrere frontibus, Hor.
units.tr: Arietare They butt against each other (Sen.). You set your head against him, flashing (Quint.). Kids butting each other with their horns (Virg.). Lambs frisk (Lucr.). To run together with opposed foreheads (Hor.).

units.la: Arista] Spica contra morsus avium munitur vallo aristarum, Cic. Arista est, quæ ut acus tenuis longa eminet è gluma, Var. Apex glumæ. Cornua spicarum, Id.
units.tr: Arista The ear of grain is protected against the bites of birds by a rampart of awns (Cic.). The awn is the thin, long, needle-like part projecting from the husk (Var.). The tip of the husk. The horns of ears of grain (Id.).

units.la: Arithmetice] Numerorum ratio, disciplina, Isid. Ars calculatoria. Scientia ratiociniorum, Henr. Steph. Numeralis scientia, Sipont.
units.tr: Arithmetice The reasoning and discipline of numbers (Isid.). The art of calculation. The science of reckoning (Henr. Steph.). Numerical science (Sipont.).

units.la: Arithmeticus] Calculator, Hart. Arenarius numerorum, Tert.
units.tr: Arithmeticus A calculator (Hart.). A sand-reckoner of numbers (Tert.).

units.la: Arma bellica] Armatura varia, Cic. Armatus, ûs, Liv. Arma mortis moras vocat, Sen. Universitas armorum, Amm.
units.tr: Arma bellica Varied armour (Cic.). Armed force (Liv.). Death calls the weapons of war delays (Sen.). The whole body of arms (Amm.).

units.la: Arma diversa] His lingua, illis dentes.
units.tr: Arma diversa The tongue for these, the teeth for those.

units.la: Armare] Cingi armis. Induere arma, Virg.
units.tr: Armare To gird oneself with arms. To put on arms (Virg.).

units.la: Armarium] Pegma, Cic. Promptuarium. Armarium. Promptuarium, Cat. Armarium librorum. Armille, Apul. Armillum, Id.
units.tr: Armarium A cabinet (Cic.). A storeroom. A cupboard (Cato). A bookcase. Bracelets (Apul.). A bracelet (Id.).

units.la: Armatus] Scutis, telisque paratus, ornatusque, Cic. Gravis armaturæ miles, Id. Armiger, Mart. Sil. Succinctus armis, ferro. Loricatus, Liv. Thoracatus, Plin. Armaturarum rector, i. e. Armatorum, Amm. Cataphractus, Liv. Clibanarius, instar clibani ferro tectus, Curt. Gravis armatura, tanquam murus ferreus stabat, Veget. Laminis ferreis, in modum plumæ contectus miles, Salust. Ferratæ catervæ, per singula membra densis laminis tectæ, ut junctúræ rigentes compagibus artuum convenirent. Incedebat ordo armatorum clypeatus atque cristatus corusco lumine radians, nitidis loricis indutus. Equites thoracum tegminibus & limbis ferreis cincti. Quos laminarum circuli tenues ambiebant, Ammian.
units.tr: Armatus Prepared and equipped with shields and weapons (Cic.). A soldier of heavy armour (Cic.). An arms-bearer (Mart., Sil.). Girded with arms and iron. Clad in a cuirass (Liv.). Breastplated (Plin.). The commander of armoured troops (Amm.). Cataphract (Liv.). Clibanarius, covered with iron like an oven (Curt.). Heavy armour stood like an iron wall (Veget.). A soldier covered with iron plates like feathers (Sall.). Iron-clad companies, covered with dense plates over every limb, so that the joints fit with the stiff framework of the limbs. A line of armed men advanced, shielded and crested, gleaming with a flashing light, clad in shining breastplates. Horsemen girt with breastplates and iron borders, whom thin circles of plates surrounded (Ammian).

units.la: Armentum] Grex armentorum, Var. Grex armentitius, Id. Pecus equinum, Col.
units.tr: Armentum A herd of cattle (Var.). A herd of cattle, pastoral (Id.). Horse cattle (Col.).

units.la: Armiger] Clavator. Puer telifer, Sen. Scutigerulus, Plaut. A pugione, Lamprid. Cacula, Plaut. Galearius, Veget. Calo. Calones. Galearii militum, Serv.
units.tr: Armiger A club-bearer. A boy carrying javelins (Sen.). A little shield-bearer (Plaut.). Armed with a dagger (Lamprid.). An attendant (Plaut.). A helmet-bearer (Veget.). Camp-followers (calones). The helmet-bearers of soldiers (Serv.).

units.la: Armilla] Viriæ, & Viriolæ. Brachiale spathalium, Plin. Spathale, Claud. Spinther, Plaut. Conveniunt tenues scapulis ometides altis, Ovid.
units.tr: Armilla Bracelets, and small bracelets. A bracelet of armlets (Plin.). An armlet (Claud.). A bracelet (Plaut.). The thin shoulder-blades meeting high (Ovid).

units.la: Armilustrium] Armilustrium, Var. Recensus, ûs, Suet. Transvectio equitum ante conspectum Ducis, Val. Max.
units.tr: Armilustrium The armilustrium (Var.). A review (Suet.). A parade of horsemen before the general's gaze (Val. Max.).

units.la: Armis versis pugnare] Abjectis lusoriis armis transfire ad vera, Lips. Ad certum dimicare, Tertull. Versis gladiis depugnare, Plaut. Ponite jam gladios hebetes, pugnetur acutis, Ovid. Decretoriis armis pugnare, Sen.
units.tr: Armis versis pugnare Putting aside playful weapons, to pass to real ones (Lips.). To fight to a decision (Tert.). To fight with swords reversed (Plaut.). Now lay down your blunt swords, and let the fight be with sharp ones (Ovid). To fight with decisive weapons (Sen.).

units.la: Armorum ars ludicra, Cic.] Certamen curule, Lamprid. Decursus, Gell. Decursio prætorianis indicta in foro, Suet. Ludicri concursus, Lips. Ludicrum certamen, Sen. Ludicrum, Mart. Trebel. Militia imaginaria, Suet. Hostici ludi, Id. Curules dimicationes, Amm. Equiria, Fest.
units.tr: The art of arms, playful (Cic.) A curule contest (Lamprid.). A running drill (Gell.). A drill ordered for the praetorian guard in the forum (Suet.). A playful charge (Lips.). A playful contest (Sen.). A playful sport (Mart., Trebel.). Imaginary soldiering (Suet.). Mock battles (Id.). Curule combats (Amm.). Horse races (Fest.).

units.la: Armorum Doctor] Campidoctor. Campiductor, Veget. Lamp. Amm. Tribunus armaturarum. Rector armaturarum, Amm. Armidoctor Gloss. Dux secundarius.
units.tr: Teacher of arms A field-teacher. A field-leader (Veget., Lamp., Amm.). A tribune of armed troops. The ruler of armed troops (Amm.). An arms-teacher (Gloss.). A second-in-command.

units.la: Aroma] Diapasmata, Plin. Mart. Stymmata. Magma, Plin. Pastillus, Hor. Aromata, Col. Odoramentum, Sipont. Hedysmata, Plin. Species, Macrob.
units.tr: Aroma Perfumed powders (Plin., Mart.). Scented ointments (stymmata). A paste (Plin.). A pastille (Hor.). Spices (Col.). A perfume (Sipont.). Sweet-smelling confections (hedysmata) (Plin.). Kinds of spice (Macrob.).

units.la: Arrha] Hunc arrhabonem amoris à me accipe, Plaut. Minis triginta puellam sibi destinat, datque arrhabonem, Id. Auctoramentum. Pignus, Cic.
units.tr: Arrha "Take this pledge of love from me" (Plaut.). He betroths the girl to himself for thirty minae and gives an earnest (Id.). Hire-money. A pledge (Cic.).

units.la: Arridere] Arridere dentibus, Horat. Ridere illi, Plaut.
units.tr: Arridere To smile with the teeth (Hor.). To smile favourably upon him (Plaut.).

units.la: Arrodere] Præroserunt mures oleas, Cic. Admordere, Virg. Figere dentem in aliquid, Ovid. Abscindere dentibus, Id.
units.tr: Arrodere Mice have gnawed the olives (Cic.). To nibble at (Virg.). To fix a tooth in something (Ovid). To bite off with the teeth (Id.).

units.la: Arrogans] Arrogantiæ plenus, Cic. Inflatus opinione, Id. Ferox formâ, Plato. Tumidus homo, Hor. Nimius animi, Liv. Vid. Superbus.
units.tr: Arrogans Full of arrogance (Cic.). Puffed up with opinion (Id.). Proud of beauty (Plato). A swollen-headed man (Hor.). Excessive in spirit (Liv.). See Superbus.

units.la: Arroganter, vid. Superbè.
units.tr: Arroganter See Superbè.

units.la: Ars] Facultas oratoris, Cic. Solertia cogitandi & agendi. Machinatio & solertia quædam in araneolis, Id.
units.tr: Ars The skill of the orator (Cic.). Cleverness in thinking and acting. A certain contrivance and cunning in little spiders (Cic.).

units.la: Ars deluditur arte] Pulchrè fallit vulpem.
units.tr: Ars deluditur arte He cleverly fools the fox.

units.la: Artes variæ obsunt] Septem artes, quatuordecim calamitates. Qui multiplicat scientiam, multiplicat dolorem.
units.tr: Artes variae obsunt Seven arts, fourteen calamities. He who multiplies knowledge multiplies sorrow.

units.la: Artem propriam tracta] Quam quisque novit artem, in ea se exerceat. Spartam, quam nactus es, hanc orna.
units.tr: Artem propriam tracta Let each exercise himself in the art he knows. Adorn the lot you have been given.

units.la: Ars mechanica] vid. Opificium.
units.tr: Ars mechanica See Opificium.

units.la: Arteria] Arteriæ micantes, Cic. Arteriace, Plin. Semita spiritūs, Id. Nervi pulsatiles, Arnob. Venæ audaces. Avicen. Pulsus venarum, Plin.
units.tr: Arteria Shining arteries (Cic.). Arteriace (Plin.). The path of the breath (Id.). Pulsing nerves (Arnob.). Bold veins (Avicen.). The pulse of the veins (Plin.).

units.la: Arteria aspera] Trachea, Gell. Canalis animæ, Plin. Fistula, per quam spiritus reciprocatur, Gell. Spiritalis fistula, Lactant. Vitales vias & respiramina, & vias vocis vocat Ovid. 2. Metam.
units.tr: Arteria aspera The windpipe (Gell.). The channel of the breath (Plin.). The pipe through which the breath goes back and forth (Gell.). The breath-pipe (Lact.). Ovid calls these the vital passages and breathing-spaces, and the passages of the voice, in the second book of the Metamorphoses.

units.la: Artes liberales] Literatura. Literarum scientia, Cic. Doctrinæ ingenuæ. Studia humanitatis. Mansuetiores Musæ. Bona studia artesque. Politior humanitas, Id. Studia disciplinarum, Quint.
units.tr: Artes liberales Literature. Knowledge of letters (Cic.). Liberal learning. The studies of humanity. The gentler Muses. Good studies and arts. A more refined humanity (Id.). The studies of the disciplines (Quint.).

units.la: Artes scire, utile] Artem quævis terra alit. Ars census, opera vita. Ars portus inopiæ.
units.tr: Artes scire, utile Every land nourishes some art. Art is wealth, and work is life. Art is a harbour against want.

units.la: Artes subtiles] Literæ interiores & reconditæ ac exquisitæ. Artes difficillimæ, gravissimæ. Summæ, perfectæ, spinosæ. Spinæ differendi, definiendi, Cic. Scientiæ omnium magnarum rerum & artium. Magna quædam scientiæ. Majorum rerum scientia, Cic.
units.tr: Artes subtiles Inner, hidden and exquisite letters. The most difficult, most weighty arts. The highest, most perfect, thorny arts. The thorns of distinguishing and defining (Cic.). The sciences of all great things and arts. Certain great sciences. The science of greater things (Cic.).

units.la: Artes magicæ] Præstigiæ, Cic. Sceleratæ preces, & nefaria vota nocturna, Id. Artes secretæ, Amm. Artes nefandæ, Id. Funestæ artes, Vopisc. Zoroastræi susurri, Prud. Magica sacra, Virg.
units.tr: Artes magicae Deceptions (Cic.). Wicked prayers and nefarious nightly vows (Id.). Secret arts (Amm.). Unspeakable arts (Id.). Baleful arts (Vopisc.). Zoroastrian whisperings (Prud.). Magic rites (Virg.).

units.la: Arthritis] Articulorum, Artuum dolor, Cic. Articularis, Articulanus dolor, Plin. Articulamentorum dolor, Scribon.
units.tr: Arthritis Pain of the joints and limbs (Cic.). Pain of the joints (Plin.). Pain of the articulations (Scribon.).

units.la: Articulatè dicere] Syllabatim, Cic. Explanatius. Enodatè, Id. Signatè & proprie, Macrob. Significanter dicere, Quint.
units.tr: To speak articulately] Syllable by syllable, Cic. More explicitly. Clearly, Id. Distinctly and precisely, Macrob. To speak with significance, Quint.

units.la: Articulatus] Articulata vox, Apul. Explanabilis, Sen.
units.tr: Articulate] An articulate voice, Apul. Capable of being explained, Sen.

units.la: Artifex] Fabricator, Cic. Technicus, Quint. Concinnator, Col. vid. Opifex.
units.tr: Artificer] A maker, Cic. A skilled worker, Quint. A contriver, Col. See Craftsman.

units.la: Artifici bono, omnis materia bona] Proba materia probo artifici. Proba sit materia, si probum adhibeas artificem.
units.tr: For a good craftsman, every material is good] Good material for a good craftsman. Let the material be good if you employ a good craftsman.

units.la: Artificiosè] Ex arte. Summâ arte. Singulari artificio. Fabrè, affabrè factum, Cic. Argutè. Perbelle, Id. Artificialiter, Quint. Faberrimè politus thorax, Amm. Perbellè, Scitè, Id. Ars est occultare artem, Cic. Lepidè id efficiam. Per doctos dolos aliquid auferre, Plaut.
units.tr: Skilfully] By art. With the greatest skill. With singular craft. Finely, well-made work, Cic. Cleverly. Very beautifully, Id. Artificially, Quint. A breastplate polished most finely, Amm. Very beautifully, neatly, Id. Art is to conceal art, Cic. I shall bring this about cleverly. To carry off something by learned tricks, Plaut.

units.la: Artificiosus] Opus artificiosum & divinum. Artis plenus, Cic. Arte laboratus, Virg. Artifex dimicatio, ingeniosa, Plin. Acutulus. Argutus. Operosus, Cic. Scitus, Quint. Faber. Fabra ars, Ovid. Affabrum, Fest. Machinosa navis. Dædala tecta, Virg. Omnia ingenia illi sunt, Plaut. Minervæ opus. Novem Musis cælatum opus. Dædali opera. Dædalus ipse.
units.tr: Skilful] A skilful and divine work. Full of art, Cic. Wrought with art, Virg. A skilful, ingenious contest, Plin. Sharp-witted. Cunning. Laborious, Cic. Clever, Quint. Crafty. An art wrought by a craftsman, Ovid. Made by craftsmen, Fest. A ship skilfully rigged. Daedalian roofs, Virg. He has every talent, Plaut. A work of Minerva. A work engraved by the nine Muses. The works of Daedalus. Daedalus himself.

units.la: Artificium] Specimen ingenii, Cic. Opum magnificium, Mirabili opere perfectum, Id. Opus elegantioris alicujus. (scil. Artificis) Diligentissimè perfecta ex ebore argumenta, Id.
units.tr: Work of art] A specimen of talent, Cic. A magnificent treasure. Finished with wonderful workmanship, Id. A work of some more elegant craftsman (namely, the artist). Figures of ivory most carefully finished, Id.

units.la: Artocreas] Crustulata caro. Ut perna crustulata, apud Spartian.
units.tr: Pastry-crust meat] Meat in a pastry crust. Like a ham in a crust, in Spartian.

units.la: Artus] Artuatim. vid. Membrum.
units.tr: Joints] Limb by limb. See Limb.

units.la: Arvisium vinum] Vinum Creticum, Iun. Chium, Serv. Malvaticum, & Malvisium, Cæl. Rhodig.
units.tr: Arvisian wine] Cretan wine, Juv. Chian wine, Serv. Malmsey and Malvisian wine, Caelius Rhodiginus.

units.la: Arundo] Calamus, Plin. Canna, Col.
units.tr: Reed] A pen-reed, Plin. A cane, Col.

units.la: Arvum] Seges. Humus subacta. Subactus ager, Cic. Arvus ager, Var. Pinguia culta, Virg. Mollitus ager, Cic. Pastinum, Pallad. Repastinatum solum, Emotum, Effossum, Col. Vervactum, (q. d. vere proscissum,) Plin. Proscissum segeti arvum, Serv.
units.tr: Ploughland] Standing crop. Turned-over ground. Ground that has been worked, Cic. Arable land, Varro. Richly tilled fields, Virg. Softened land, Cic. Ground dug over with a spade, Pallad. Ground turned over again, dug out, dug up, Col. Ground ploughed in spring, Plin. A field cut open for the crop, Serv.

units.la: Arvum requietum] Novale, quod alternis annis seritur, Plin. Novalis ager, Var. Vervactum, Id. Ager requietus, Ovid.
units.tr: Resting arable land] Fallow land that is sown in alternate years, Pliny. Fallow field [novalis ager], Varro. Ploughed fallow [vervactum], Id. Rested field, Ovid.

units.la: Arx] Castellum natura munitum. Propugnaculum. Munitio. Opus. Præsidium, Cic.
units.tr: Citadel] A fortress made strong by nature. A bulwark. A fortification. A work. A garrison, Cic.

units.la: Ascendere] Ascensionem facere, Plaut. Gradum ad aliquid facere. Scandere malos, Cic. Escendere in summum, Plaut.
units.tr: To climb] To make an ascent, Plaut. To take a step towards something. To climb the masts, Cic. To climb to the top, Plaut.

units.la: Ascensus] Difficilis atque arduus ascensus. Gradus. Aditus, Cic.
units.tr: Ascent] A difficult and steep ascent. A step. An approach, Cic.

units.la: Asciare, vid. Deasciare.
units.tr: To hew, see To hew off.

units.la: Asilus] OEstrum, Virg. Musca, quæ fervente sole, acrius agit, Scal.
units.tr: Gadfly] A gadfly, Virg. A fly that bites more fiercely in the heat of the sun, Scaliger.

units.la: Aspectus] Obtutus Oculorum. Intuitus, Species, Conjectus oculorum, Cic. Respectu me terruit, Plaut. Inspectio, Col. Injectus oculorum, Arnob.
units.tr: Sight] A gaze of the eyes. A look, appearance, a glance of the eyes, Cic. He frightened me with a look, Plaut. A viewing, Col. A casting of the eyes, Arnob.

units.la: Aspectu tantum terret] Visu, non re terribilis.
units.tr: He frightens only by his look] Terrible in appearance, not in reality.

units.la: Asper] Peraspep, Cels. Scaber cortex, Plin. Rugosus, Id. Scabrata vitis, Col. Scabrosus unguis. Scrupulosa cortex. Tergum ulceribus oftreatum, Plaut. Fragosus, Quint. Confragosus, Lucan. Squarosus, Lucill. Rigens. Scythâ asperior, Er. Rusco horridior, Id.
units.tr: Rough] Very rough, Celsus. A rough bark, Plin. Wrinkled, Id. A rough vine, Col. A rough nail. A scaly bark. A back covered with sores, Plaut. Broken, Quint. Full of rubble, Lucan. Scaly, Lucilius. Bristling. Rougher than a Scythian, Erasmus. More bristly than butcher's broom, Id.

units.la: Asperè, propr.] Asperiter, Non. Scabrè, Robert. Stephan. Fragosè fragosiùs, Plin.
units.tr: Roughly, literally] Roughly, Nonius. Scrabbly, Robert Stephanus. More and more broken, Pliny.

units.la: Aspere, translat.] Acutè dicere. Acriter. Acerrimè vituperare. Acerbè dicere. Vehementer aliquem accipere. Fastidiosè. Duriùs differere. Severè, Cic. Inclementer in aliquem dictum, Ter. Scrupulosè probare, Col. Infectanter vituperare, Gell.
units.tr: Harshly, figuratively] To speak sharply. Fiercely. To condemn most bitterly. To speak bitterly. To treat someone violently. Disdainfully. To argue more harshly. Severely, Cic. Said unmercifully against someone, Ter. To prove with scrupulous care, Col. To condemn with spite, Gell.

units.la: Aspergere] Irrigare. Respergere, Cic. Perspergere, Tacit. Adaquare arbores, Plin. Offundere, Obsipare alicui aquam, Plaut. Irrorare aliquid oleo, Col. Tingere poculis, Hor. Inspergere vinum. Spargere saxa tabô, Cic.
units.tr: To sprinkle] To water. To sprinkle over, Cic. To sprinkle through, Tac. To water trees, Plin. To pour over, to pour water over someone, Plaut. To moisten something with oil, Col. To wet with drinks, Hor. To sprinkle wine. To strew stones with gore, Cic.

units.la: Asperitas] Aspretum, Liv. Aspredo. Aspritudo, Cels. Scabricia cutis. Scabrities. Scabrum, Plin. Scabredo, Hieron. Salebra, Plaut. Scabies, Cic. Virg.
units.tr: Roughness] Roughness, Livy. Roughness. Roughness of the skin, Cels. Scabrousness. Scabby roughness, Plin. Roughness, Jerome. An uneven place, Plaut. Mange, Cic., Virg.

units.la: Aspernari] Despicere aliquem. Despicatui ducere aliquem. In minimis, in extremis res aliquas ponere. Pro nihilo ducere, habere, putare aliquid. Parvi ducere. Negligere minas alicujus. Nauci habere aliquem, Cic. vid. Contemnere.
units.tr: To despise] To look down on someone. To hold someone in contempt. To set certain things among the smallest or lowest. To count, hold, or think something as nothing. To value little. To disregard someone's threats. To hold someone as worth a nut, Cic. See To scorn.

units.la: Aspersio] Aspersus. Respersus. Respersio, Irrigatio, Cic. Riguum. Perfusio, Plin. Aspergo, inis. Sparsio aquæ, Sen.
units.tr: Sprinkling] A sprinkling. A wetting. A watering, Cic. Irrigation. A soaking, Plin. A sprinkle, Aspergo. A splashing of water, Sen.

units.la: Aspicere] Aspicere ad, aspicere inter se, Cic. Contemplari oculis. Contueri ad, Id. Conspicere aliquid lumine cupido, Catul. Spectare oculis devorantibus, Mart. Obtueri, Plaut. Pascere oculos, Ter. Adspectare aliquem, Cic. Respicere ad, Ter.
units.tr: To look at] To look at, to look at one another, Cic. To gaze upon with the eyes. To look toward, Id. To catch sight of something with eager eyes, Catull. To gaze with devouring eyes, Mart. To stare at, Plaut. To feast the eyes, Ter. To look on someone, Cic. To look back at, Ter.

units.la: Aspis] Cerastes, Plin. Excetra, Cic. Serpens cornutus, Stat.
units.tr: Asp] A horned serpent, Plin. A viper, Cic. A horned serpent, Stat.

units.la: Assare] Torrere succensis ignibus, Cic. Mollire cibum flamma, Lucr. Adolere. In veru coquere, Var. Coquere aliquid asso igne. Sicut Cicero assus sol, dixit.
units.tr: To roast] To scorch with kindled fires, Cic. To soften food by flame, Lucr. To burn up. To cook on a spit, Varro. To cook something over a fire. As Cicero said, the sun roasts.

units.la: Assatura] Tosta caro. Assura, Var. Assum, Cic. Assum vitulinum. Assa bubula, Assariæ dapes, Id.
units.tr: Roast meat] Roasted flesh. Roast, Varro. A roast, Cic. Roast veal. Roast beef, roast dishes, Id.

units.la: Assatus] Inassatus, Plin. Assarius, Cat. Tostus. Indura-tus flammis, Ovid.
units.tr: Roasted] Not roasted, Plin. Roasted, Cato. Toasted. Hardened by flames, Ovid.

units.la: Assecla] A pedibus servus. Circum pedes, Cic. Aulicum famulitium, Capitol. Anteambulo, Suet.
units.tr: Attendant] A servant on foot. Around the feet, Cic. Court service, Capitolinus. A runner before, Suet.

units.la: Assensus] Assensio, Cic. Assertatio, Id. Assentatio, Petron. Pater.
units.tr: Assent] Assent, Cic. Affirmation, Id. Flattery, Petronius.

units.la: Assentatio] Mercenarium præconium. Comitas assen-tatrix, Cic.
units.tr: Flattery] A hired proclamation. Obliging courtesy, Cic.

units.la: Assentator, vid. Adulator.
units.tr: Flatterer, see Sycophant.

units.la: Assentatores mutui] Mulus mulum scabit.
units.tr: Mutual flatterers] A mule scratches a mule. One hand washes the other.

units.la: Assentiri] Assentire, Cic. Assentaris huic? Assensione comprobare. Assensionem animi adjungere. Sum alicui assensor. Concedere, Id. Annuere, Virg. Ire in sententiam alicujus, Cic. Defensionem facere in sententiam alicujus, Id. Pedibus venio in sententiam tuam, Id. Accedere senten-tiam, Vlp. Subscribere, Acquiescere consilio, Sen. Subsequi alicujus judicium, Ovid.
units.tr: To assent] To assent, Cic. Do you agree with him? To confirm by assent. To add the assent of the mind. I am a supporter of someone. To yield, Id. To nod, Virg. To go into someone's opinion, Cic. To make a defence in accordance with someone's opinion, Id. I come to your opinion with both feet, Id. To come round to an opinion, Ulpian. To subscribe, to acquiesce in counsel, Sen. To follow someone's judgment, Ovid.

units.la: Assequi] Consequi cursu. Persequi te triginta diebus non potui, Cic. Æquare aliquem cursu, Liv. Adæquare cursum alicujus, Cæs.
units.tr: To overtake] To overtake in a run. I could not catch up with you in thirty days, Cic. To match someone in running, Livy. To match someone's pace, Caes.

units.la: Asserere, vid. Affirmare.
units.tr: To assert, see To affirm.

units.la: Assertio] Asseveratio. Affirmatio, Cic. Nuncupatio. Parata ipsam nuncupationem tabulis probare, Plin.
units.tr: Assertion] An asseveration. An affirmation, Cic. A dedication. To prove the dedication itself by ready documents, Plin.

units.la: Assidue] Assiduus, pro assidue, Cic. Assiduissimè mecum fuit. Perpetuò, Id. Continuò. Continenter. Continuatè. Jugiter, Plaut. Perpetim, Plin. Usque & usque, Mart. Protinus, Plin. Noctes & dies. Noctu & diu, Plaut. Continuato protelo, Cic. In totum, Col. Perenne fabricari, Id. Sempiterno inumbrantur foliis, Solin.
units.tr: Constantly] Constant, for constantly, Cic. He was with me most constantly. Continually, Id. Without interruption. Continuously. Continuously. Ceaselessly, Plaut. Perpetually, Plin. Always and ever, Mart. Immediately, Plin. Night and day. By night and by day, Plaut. In continuous delay, Cic. Wholly, Col. To be built perpetually, Id. They are shaded by everlasting leaves, Solinus.

units.la: Assiduitas] Perpetuitas, Cic.
units.tr: Constancy] Perpetuity, Cic.

units.la: Assiduitas incredibilia præstat] Aquilam testudo vincit. Assidua stilla saxum excavat.
units.tr: Constancy achieves incredible things] The tortoise overcomes the eagle. A constant drop hollows out a stone.

units.la: Assiduus] Continuatus. Jugus. Perpetuus sumptus,Cic. Continuus. Continens cursu, Liv. Perdius. Pernox, Gell. Perennis rivus, Plin.
units.tr: Constant] Continuous. Unbroken. Perpetual expense, Cic. Continuous. Continuing in a course, Livy. Through the day. Through the night, Gell. A perennial stream, Plin.

units.la: Assignare] Annotare, & adnotare. Denotare, Cic. Præfinire diem. Constituere locum, tempus, Prodicere, & Prodere diem, Cic. Determinare limites, Plaut. Designare locum, Liv. Signare differentiam duarum rerum, Quint. Præstituere tempus, locum Cic. vid. Definire aliquid.
units.tr: To assign] To note down, and to annotate. To denote, Cic. To fix a day beforehand. To appoint a place or time. To name and proclaim a day, Cic. To determine boundaries, Plaut. To designate a place, Livy. To mark the difference between two things, Quint. To fix a time or place beforehand, Cic. See To define something.

units.la: Assignatio.] Designatio, Cic. Annotamentum, Gell.
units.tr: Assignment] Designation, Cic. An annotation, Gell.

units.la: Assilire] Contingere aliquid saltu, Stat.
units.tr: To leap upon] To touch something by a leap, Stat.

units.la: Assimilare] Similem judicare,Cic. Configurare ad similitudinem alterius. Fingere se ad. Accommodare se ad arbitrium & nutum aliorum. Conformare se ad alicujus voluntatem. Servire tempori, scenæ,Id. Assimilare aliquem alicui,Tac. Utcunque res sunt, ita animum habere, Plaut. Alienum sumere vultum, Juv.
units.tr: To assimilate] To judge to be similar, Cic. To shape oneself to the likeness of another. To feign oneself to. To accommodate oneself to the will and nod of others. To conform oneself to someone's will. To serve the time, the stage, Id. To make someone like another, Tac. However things are, so to have one's mind, Plaut. To assume a foreign countenance, Juv.

units.la: Assimilare se aliis] Balare cum ovibus. Ululare cum lupis, Hinnire cum equis. Insanire cum insanientibus.
units.tr: To assimilate oneself to others] To bleat with the sheep. To howl with the wolves. To neigh with the horses. To rage with the madmen.

units.la: Assuefacere] Adducere ad consuetudinem. Afferre alicui consuetudinem, Cic. Consuescere juvencum aratro. Consuefacere ut, Ter. Insuevit me Pater, ut Hor. Insuefacti equi, Cæs.
units.tr: To accustom] To bring to a habit. To bring a habit to someone, Cic. To train a young bullock to the plough. To accustom so that, Ter. My father has accustomed me to it, as Horace says. Horses trained, Caes.

units.la: Assuescere] Assiduitate quotidianâ & consuetudine oculorum assuescunt animi. Consuetudinem alicujus rei nancisci. In consuetudinem venire. Obdurescere consuetudine. Consuetudo callum obduxit, Cic. Consuetudo in me vitium altius fixit, Sen. Adduxerunt se in eam consuetudinem, Cæs. Vertit mihi aliquid in consuetudinem, Tacit. Venire in usum alicujus rei,Plin. Condiscere aliquid, Id. Colligere usum patiendi, Ovid. Naturam alicujus rei sibi facere, Quint. Leviora, quibus assuevimus.
units.tr: To become accustomed] Minds become accustomed through daily repetition and the habit of the eyes. To acquire the habit of something. To come into a habit. To grow hardened by habit. Habit has made a callus, Cic. Habit has fixed a fault more deeply in me, Sen. They brought themselves into that custom, Caes. Someone has turned something into a custom for me, Tac. To come into the use of something, Plin. To learn something thoroughly, Id. To gain the practice of suffering, Ovid. To make the nature of something one's own, Quint. Lighter things, to which we have become accustomed.

units.la: Assuetus] Suetus alicui rei, Cic. Duratus laboribus, usu armorum, Lucan.
units.tr: Accustomed] Used to something, Cic. Hardened by labours, by the use of arms, Lucan.

units.la: Assula] Hastula, Plin. Fragmenta ligni, Philand. Defomitatum,Fest.(à fomitib.) Segmen minutum ligni, Sipont.
units.tr: Splinter] A small spear, Plin. Fragments of wood, Philander. Tinder-like, from tinder, Festus. A small chip of wood, Sipontinus.

units.la: Assumere] Adscisere sibi, Cic. Sumere secum, Liv. Secum rapere, agere, ferre, ducere, Virg.
units.tr: To take up] To take to oneself, Cic. To take along with oneself, Livy. To snatch, drive, carry, or lead away with oneself, Virg.

units.la: Assurgere] Consurgere in altitudinem, Col. Exsurgere, Liv. Cano capiti assurgere adolescentem decet, Er.
units.tr: To rise] To rise up to a height, Col. To rise up, Livy. It becomes a young man to rise up before a grey head, Erasmus.

units.la: Asteriscus] Stellula, Rob. Steph.
units.tr: Asterisk] A little star, Robert Stephanus.

units.la: Asthma, vid. Anhelitus.
units.tr: Asthma, see Breathlessness.

units.la: Astrologia] Prædictio & notatio vitæ ex natali die, Cic. Superstitiosa ex astris vaticinatio, Val. M.
units.tr: Astrology] The foretelling and reading of a life from the day of birth, Cic. Superstitious prophecy from the stars, Val. Max.

units.la: Astrologus] Chaldæos, cæterosque divinos, Cic. vocat. Planetarius, Celf. Genethlialogus. Genituræ peritissimus, Philard. Fatorum per genituras interpres, Amm. Genethliacus, Gell. Mathematicus, Iuv. Venerarius, (quia Planetas veneratur) Tertull.
units.tr: Astrologer] Cicero calls the Chaldaeans and other diviners... Planetary, Celsus. Genethlialogist. Most skilled in nativities, Philardus. Interpreter of fates through nativities, Ammianus. Genethliac, Gellius. Mathematician, Juvenal. A worshipper of Venus (because he worships the planets), Tertullian.

units.la: Astronomia] Astrorum scientia, Cic.
units.tr: Astronomy] Knowledge of the stars, Cic.

units.la: Astronomus] Interpres cœli, astrorum, Cic. Inspector siderum, Plin. Studiosus rerum cœlestium, Col.
units.tr: Astronomer] An interpreter of the heavens and the stars, Cic. An observer of the constellations, Plin. One devoted to heavenly things, Col.

units.la: Astus] Malitia. Versuta & fallax nocendi ratio, prudentiæ similis, Cic. Astutia, & æ, Ter. Offuciæ. Panurgia, Plin. Præstigiæ, Cic. Circulatoria jactatio, Quint. Stellionatus, Vlp. Manticulatio, Sipont.
units.tr: Cunning] Malice. A crafty and deceitful way of harming, resembling prudence, Cic. Shrewdness, Ter. Deceits. Roguery, Plin. Tricks, Cic. Charlatan's boasting, Quint. Stellionate (fraud), Vlp. Trickery, Sipont.

units.la: Astutè] Dolosè. Vafrè. Fallaciter. Veteratorie, Cic. Astu. Subdolè, Plaut. Perfidè, Var. Sycophanticè, Plaut.
units.tr: Cunningly] Deceitfully. Craftily. Fallaciously. Slyly, Cic. Shrewdly. Craftily, Plaut. Treacherously, Var. Sycophantically, Plaut.

units.la: Astutus] Versutus. Versutiloquus, Cic. Astutam servans sub pectore vulpem, Perf. Astutulus. Peraštutulus, Apul. Nasutulus, Id. Vulpes, Vulpio, Id. Nasutissimus, Sen. Vulpinus animus, Plaut. Præstigiosus, Gell. Vulpinum ingenium, Er. Dolosus. Argutus. Subdolus, Plaut. Callidus, Ter. Cic. Alterplex, Isid. Callidulus, Arnob. Vafer, Cic. Vafellus, Fest.
units.tr: Cunning] Wily. Speaking with guile, Cic. Keeping a sly fox under the breast, Pers. Somewhat cunning. Very cunning, Apul. A little sharp-nosed, Id. A fox, a sly one, Id. Very sharp-nosed, Sen. A foxy mind, Plaut. Given to tricks, Gell. A foxy disposition, Erasm. Deceitful. Sharp-witted. Sly, Plaut. Clever, Ter., Cic. Twice-folded, Isid. Rather clever, Arnob. Crafty, Cic. Somewhat crafty, Fest.

units.la: Atavus] Quintus pater, Perf. Abavi pater. Proavi avus. Patris abavus.
units.tr: Great-grandfather] The fifth father, Pers. The father of a great-great-grandfather. The grandfather of a great-grandfather. The great-great-grandfather of a father.

units.la: Atheus] Cui nec ara, nec fides.
units.tr: Atheist] One who has neither altar nor faith.

units.la: Athletica, vid. Pugillatus.
units.tr: Athletics, see Boxing.

units.la: Atomus] Corpus individuum, Cic. Pulvisculus, Plaut. Corpus insecabile, Quint. Corpusculum. Elementum. Principium. Primordium. Minimum, parvissimum corpus. Corpus primum. Semen rerum. Principiorum corpus. Materiai corpus, Lucret.
units.tr: Atom] An indivisible body, Cic. A little dust, Plaut. An indivisible body, Quint. A tiny body. A element. A first principle. A beginning. The smallest, very tiny body. The first body. The seed of things. The body of first principles. The body of matter, Lucr.

units.la: Atrocitas, vid. Crudelitas. Atrociter, vid. Crudeliter.
units.tr: Atrocity, see Cruelty. Atrociously, see Cruelly.

units.la: Atrox] Crudelis in aliquem. Truculentus homo. Gens immanitate barbara. Efferatus immanitate, Cic. Teter. Terrimus homo. Immanis homo. Immanissima natio. Toto pectore immanitatem anhelat. Feritas & immanitas belluæ in figura hominis. Laborat crudelitate, Id. Sævus, Sævissimus Tyrannus, Liv. Homo cum gemitu nominandus, Amm. Cassianus judex. Sanguinarius homo. Cyclops alter, multò importunior, Cic. Immitis Achilles, Virg. Inclemens dictator, Liv. Vid. Crudelis.
units.tr: Atrocious] Cruel towards someone. A savage man. A people barbarous in its brutality. Brutalized by savagery, Cic. Foul. A most dreadful man. A monstrous man. A most monstrous nation. He pants with monstrous cruelty in his whole breast. The wildness and brutality of a beast in human form. He suffers from cruelty, Id. A savage, most savage tyrant, Liv. A man to be named with a groan, Amm. A Cassian judge. A bloodthirsty man. Another Cyclops, far more savage, Cic. Pitiless Achilles, Virg. Merciless dictator, Liv. See Cruel.

units.la: Attamen] Etsi, attamen. Tametsi tamen. Etsi, verùm tamen, Cic. Tamen, Ter. Etsi, sed tamen. At, Cæs. Sed etsi, nihilominus, Vlp. Etiamsi, tamen, Cic. Sed tametsi antea scripsi, tamen hoc tempore breviter commonendum putavi.
units.tr: Nevertheless] Although, nevertheless. Even though, yet. Although, but still, Cic. Yet, Ter. Although, but yet. But, Caes. But although, nonetheless, Vlp. Even if, yet, Cic. But although I wrote before, yet at this time I thought it right to give a brief warning.

units.la: Attemperatè] Pro ratâ parte. Proportione, Cic. Pro ratâ (Absol.) ejus, quod cuique debebatur.
units.tr: Proportionately] In proportion to the part. In proportion, Cic. In due proportion (absolutely) to what was owed to each.

units.la: Attendere] Attento animo excipere. Attentissimis animis audire, Cic. Advertere animum, animos, Liv. Age, quod in manu est. Quod agis, agas, Plaut. Hoc age, Plutarch. Intendere oculos in scopum. Mens videt. Mens audit, vid. Audire.
units.tr: To attend] To receive with an attentive mind. To listen with the most attentive minds, Cic. To turn one's mind, minds, Liv. Do what is in your hand. Do what you are doing, Plaut. Do this, Plutarch. To fix the eyes on the mark. The mind sees. The mind hears; see Hear.

units.la: Attentè] Maturo judicio & consideratè, Cic. Vigilatè, Gell. Arrectis auribus. Fixis oculis, Ter. Rebus relictis. Purgatis auribus, Er.
units.tr: Attentively] With mature judgement and consideration, Cic. Watchfully, Gell. With ears pricked up. With eyes fixed, Ter. With other matters set aside. With ears cleansed, Erasm.

units.la: Attentio] Intentio, adjunctio, applicatio, inductio animi, Cic. Oculorum cura.
units.tr: Attention] The intention, joining, application, and bending of the mind, Cic. The care of the eyes.

units.la: Attentio Heri proficua] Oculus Domini saginat equum. Oculus domûs est præsentia Domini.
units.tr: Attention to the Master is profitable] The Lord's eye fattens the horse. The eye of the house is the Master's presence.

units.la: Attenuare] In angustam subtilitatem tenuare, Plin. Diducere vocem, Pomp. Subter-tenuare, Lucr.
units.tr: To thin out] To make thin to a narrow fineness, Plin. To stretch out the voice, Pomp. To make somewhat thin beneath, Lucr.

units.la: Attenuatè] Tenerrimè derasus cortex. Presse, Pressius dicere. Tenuiter. Tenuiùs differere. Argutè. Argutissimè dicta, Cic. Peracutè. Acutè, Id Minutius & scrupulosiùs scrutari, Quint.
units.tr: Finely] A bark scraped very thinly. Closely, to speak more closely. Subtly. To discourse more subtly. Keenly. Things said most keenly, Cic. Very sharply. Sharply, Id. More minutely and scrupulously to examine, Quint.

units.la: Attenuatio] Tenuitas animi tanta, ut fugiat aciem. Exilitas in dicendo, Cic. Acumen Hyperidis. Parvitas oculorum, Id.
units.tr: Subtlety] Such fineness of mind that it escapes the sight. Slenderness in speaking, Cic. The sharpness of Hyperides. Smallness of the eyes, Id.

units.la: Atterere] Limare aliquid cum aliquo, Plaut. Conterere, Var. Collidere aliqua, Sil.
units.tr: To wear down] To file one thing against another, Plaut. To grind together, Varro. To crush some things together, Sil.

units.la: Attestatio] Astipulatio, Quint. Adstipulatus, Plin.
units.tr: Attestation] Corroboration, Quint. A corroborating witness, Plin.

units.la: Attingere, prensando tractare] Tango aliquid, aliquem, Cic. Ter. Plaut. Contingere aliquid, Cic. Col. Tractare vulnere, Cic. Perstringere portam urbis. Continens est aliquid alicui, Id. Tractare aliquid manu, Col. Attrectare signum, Liv. Contrectare pocula, Col. Libare, Petron.
units.tr: To touch, handle by grasping] I touch something or someone, Cic., Ter., Plaut. To come into contact with something, Cic., Col. To handle with a wound, Cic. To graze the city gate. Something is adjacent to someone, Id. To handle something with the hand, Col. To touch a statue, Liv. To handle cups, Col. To sip, Petron.

units.la: Attingere, leviter agere] Digito attingere aliquid. Extremis digitis. Primoribus labris, Cic. Degustare, Id. Perstringere aliquid breviter. Tangere aliquid leviter. In transitu aliquid attingere, Plin. Movere, inferre mentionem de re aliquâ, Liv. Libare aliquid, Virg. Lambere. Delibare partem humoris ab æquore, Lucr.
units.tr: To touch, act lightly] To touch something with a finger. With the tips of the fingers. With the first of the lips, Cic. To taste, Id. To touch something briefly. To touch something lightly. To touch something in passing, Plin. To move, to bring in mention of some matter, Liv. To sip something, Virg. To lick. To draw off a part of the moisture from the sea, Lucr.

units.la: Attollere aliquid] Sublevare aliquem. Extollere caput. Erigere afflictum, Cic. Allevare afflictum, Quint. Arrigere comas, Virg. Relevare corpus, Ovid. Levare animum, Quint. Tollere in sublime aliquid, Plin. Sustollere aliquem, Plaut. Subducere cataractam, Liv. Elevare lapidem, Plaut. Sublimare facem, Enn.
units.tr: To lift something up] To raise someone up. To lift up the head. To raise the afflicted, Cic. To relieve the afflicted, Quint. To raise the hair, Virg. To relieve the body, Ovid. To lift up the spirit, Quint. To lift something on high, Plin. To raise someone up, Plaut. To draw up a portcullis, Liv. To lift a stone, Plaut. To raise a torch on high, Enn.

units.la: Attollere se] Erigere se. Sublevare se. Tollere se, Cic. Assurgere, Virg. Consurgere in altitudinem, Quint. Surgunt æquora, Virg. Attolluntur colles, Plin. Insurgere, Virg.
units.tr: To lift oneself up] To raise oneself. To lift oneself up. To rise, Cic. To rise up, Virg. To rise to a height, Quint. The waters rise, Virg. The hills are raised, Plin. To rise up, Virg.

units.la: Attonitus] Obtutu in uno defixus hæret, Virg. Oculos patentes tenet, Lucr. Demens.
units.tr: Astonished] Fixed and held by one gaze, Virg. Holding the eyes open, Lucr. Mad.

units.la: Attrahere] Protrahere ad, Cic, Pertrahere, Liv.
units.tr: To draw] To draw forth to, Cic. To draw through, Liv.

units.la: Attrectare] Tentare aliquid digitis. Manticulari, Plaut. Tractare aliquid. Sollicitare manu aliquid, Mart. Pertractare, Petron.
units.tr: To handle] To try something with the fingers. To fumble, Plaut. To handle something. To stir something with the hand, Mart. To handle thoroughly, Petron.

units.la: Attritus] Mentum simulacri attritius, Cic. Detrita tegmina, Gell. Defloccatus, Plaut. Obsoletus, Cic.
units.tr: Worn] A statue's worn face, Cic. Worn-out coverings, Gell. Threadbare, Plaut. Obsolete, Cic.

units.la: Avare] Sordidè. Per avaritiam. Spe & avaritiâ bona alicujus devorare, Cic. Avariter, Plaut. Avidè, Hor.
units.tr: Greedily] Meanly. Through avarice. To devour someone's goods out of hope and greed, Cic. Greedily, Plaut. Eagerly, Hor.

units.la: Avaritia] Sordes, Cic. Cupido, Hor. Avaritiès, Lucr.
units.tr: Avarice] Meanness, Cic. Desire, Hor. Greed, Lucr.

units.la: Avaritia insatiabilis] Inexplebilis avaritia. Crescentem sequitur cura pecuniam, Hor. Crescit amor nummi, Juv. Crescunt opes, & opum crescit furiosa libido. Et cum pos-sideant sideant plurima, plura petunt. Quo plus sunt potæ, plus sitiuntur aquæ, Ovid. Loculi mendicorum semper inanes. Hydropico nihil siccius. Non mittit cutem, nisi plena cruoris hirudo, Hor. Multa desideranti desunt multa, Id. Avarus semper eget. Argentea fames.
units.tr: Insatiable avarice] Avarice that cannot be filled. Care follows money that keeps growing, Hor. The love of money grows, Juv. Wealth grows, and the frenzied lust for wealth grows with it. And though they possess very much, they seek more. The more they drink, the thirstier they are for water, Ovid. The purses of beggars are always empty. Nothing is drier than a dropsy patient. The leech does not let go of the skin unless it is full of blood, Hor. Many things are lacking to one who desires many things, Id. The avaricious man always lacks. A silver hunger.

units.la: Avaritia corrumpit judices] Auro conciliatur amor. Auro loquente, nihil pollet quævis oratio. Qui dare scit, non qui dicere, Rhetor erit, Oven.
units.tr: Avarice corrupts judges] Love is won with gold. When gold speaks, no speech at all has weight. He who knows how to give, not he who knows how to speak, will be the orator, Ovid.

units.la: Avarus] Ardens avaritiâ. Hiante avaritiâ homo. Illiberalis & sordidus, Cic. Præ pretio, lucro, prædaque, non authoritas, non gratia cujusquam valet, Id. Attentus ad rem, Ter. Accipiter pecuniæ. Procax. Rapax. Trahax. Polypus. Hiulca gens, Plaut. Sordis infimæ homo, Apul. Gluto sorbens salivam Mercurialem, Perf. Cui pecunia vita est. Pumice aridior. Obolum supra Deos evehit. Res est inexplebilis.
units.tr: Avaricious] Burning with avarice. A man gaping with avarice. Mean and sordid, Cic. Authority and favour of no one count for anything before price, gain and plunder, Id. Intent on money, Ter. A hawk for money. Greedy. Rapacious. Grasping. A polypus. A gaping race, Plaut. A man of the lowest meanness, Apul. A glutton swallowing Mercury's spittle, Pers. For whom money is life. Drier than pumice. He raises a halfpenny above the gods. He is an insatiable thing.

units.la: Avari sumus omnes] Omnes ad rem attentiores, Ter.
units.tr: We are all avaricious] All are more attentive to business, Ter.

units.la: Auceps] Aucupator, Sipont. Lanista rixosarum avium, qui alites certaminibus præparabat, Col.
units.tr: Fowler] A bird-catcher, Sipont. A trainer of quarrelsome birds, who prepared winged creatures for fights, Col.

units.la: Auctarium] Vid. Additamentum.
units.tr: Extra payment] See Addition.

units.la: Auctio] Venditio bonorum, sectio, Cic. Hastæ subjectio, Id. Promercium, Vlp. Suspensa bona, Sen.
units.tr: Auction] The sale of goods, confiscation, Cic. Putting up for the spear, Id. Sale of goods, Ulp. Goods held in suspense, Sen.

units.la: Auctionari] Auctionem facere, proponere. Vid. Vendere.
units.tr: To auction] To hold or advertise an auction. See Sell.

units.la: Auctorare militem] Obligare aliquem sacramento militiæ, Cic. Adstringere, obstringere donis, Id. Militem conscribere.
units.tr: To enlist a soldier] To bind someone by the military oath, Cic. To bind or oblige by gifts, Id. To enrol soldiers.

units.la: Auctoramentum] Vid. Pignus. Arrha. Obligatio.
units.tr: Enlistment bounty] See Pledge. Earnest. Obligation.

units.la: Auctor sum alicui] Ansam do. Materiam præbere, Cic. Auctoritatem afferre, Id. Patefacere alicui viam, aditum, ad aliquid, Id. Fenestram alicui ad nequitiam patefacere, Ter. Sternere viam, Stat.
units.tr: I am the cause of something for someone] I give occasion. I provide material, Cic. I bring authority, Id. To open a way or access for someone to something, Id. To open a window for someone to wickedness, Ter. To pave the way, Stat.

units.la: In auctorem mali recidit malum] Malum consilium consultori pessimum. Faber compedes quas fecit, ipse gestat. Flagellum ipse paravit, quo vapularet. Sæpe in magistrum scelera redire suum. Quicquid intrivit, ipsi excedendum erit.
units.tr: The evil returns upon its author] A bad plan is worst for the one who devised it. The smith wears the fetters he made himself. He prepared the whip himself with which he would be beaten. Often wickedness returns upon its own master. Whatever one has rubbed in must be rubbed out again.

units.la: Auctores legere] Bonos auctorare. Nocturnâ, diurnâque manu versare, Er. Manibus terere, Cic.
units.tr: To read authors] To profit from good authors. To turn over with night and day hand, Erasm. To wear down with the hands, Cic.

units.la: Auctoritas] Majestas, dignitas personæ. Granditas verborum, Gravitas personæ. Pondus verborum. Supercilium Campanum, Cic. Frons duri severa Catonis, Mart. Oris dignitas, Bud. Aut erit is sibi nimium arrogans. Ipse dixit.
units.tr: Authority] Majesty, dignity of person. Weight of words, gravity of person. The weight of words. The Campanian brow, Cic. The stern brow of harsh Cato, Mart. The dignity of the face, Budé. Or he will be too arrogant in his own eyes. He himself has spoken.

units.la: Audacia] Projecta audacia. Confidentia. Licentia. Petulantia. Contumacia responsi. Temeritas furiosa. Ferocitas. Protervitas, Cic. Audentia, Vlp.
units.tr: Boldness] Reckless boldness. Confidence. Licence. Impudence. Obstinacy in answering. Frenzied rashness. Ferocity. Wilfulness, Cic. Boldness, Ulp.

units.la: Audacia non semper succedit] Qui nimis est audax, sæpe infeliciter audet.
units.tr: Boldness does not always succeed] He who is too bold often dares unhappily.

units.la: Audacter] Audenter, Vlp. Audentius, Tacit. Prælicenter, Gell.
units.tr: Boldly] Boldly, Ulp. More boldly, Tac. Very freely, Gell.

units.la: Audaculus ad magna] Catulus leonem allatrans. Confidentia Herculis, vel Herculea. Aquilam cornix provocat.
units.tr: Bold toward great things] A puppy barking at a lion. The confidence of Hercules, or Herculean confidence. A crow challenges an eagle.

units.la: Audax] Projectus ad audendum. Animis armati, Cic. Confidentissimus, Id. Nimius animis, Sen. Columen audaciæ, Plaut. Præsumptor, Amm. Animos leonum præferentes. Calidi omnia turbant. Icaro audacior, Er.
units.tr: Bold] Driven to dare. Armed in spirit, Cic. Most confident, Id. Too spirited, Sen. The pillar of boldness, Plaut. Presumptuous, Amm. Carrying the spirit of lions before them. Hotheads disturb everything. Bolder than Icarus, Erasm.

units.la: Audacem non debere esse] Cedendum multitudini. Cedendum casui. Ne Hercules quidem contra duos. Cui cerebrum est vitreum, vitet pugnam lapideam.
units.tr: A bold man should not be] One must yield to the crowd. One must yield to chance. Not even Hercules against two. He whose brain is glass should avoid a stone fight.

units.la: Audes, vinces] Audaces fortuna juvat, timidosque repellit, Virg. Fortes fortuna adjuvat.
units.tr: Dare, and you will conquer] Fortune favours the bold and drives away the timid, Virg. Fortune helps the brave.

units.la: Audere] Adesse animo, Cic. Nec quisquam tanto ausu essel, Plaut. Quod an fieri possit, interrogate audaciam vestram, Petron.
units.tr: To dare] To be present in spirit, Cic. Nor was anyone so bold, Plaut. Ask your boldness whether it can be done, Petron.

units.la: Audientia] Silentium. Dare copiam senatui, Tac. Dare senatum legatis, Cic. Auritum populum face præeo, Plaut.
units.tr: Hearing] Silence. To give the senate a hearing, Tac. To grant the envoys an audience with the senate, Cic. To make the people all ears, Plaut.

units.la: Audire] Attendere diligenter. Operam dare aurium: auscultando : sermoni, Cic. Plaut. Aures dare, Tac. Aures arrigere, Ter. Operari auditioni, Plin. Aures dare, adhibere alicui. Auribus accipere mandata. Admovere aures, Ter. Excipere quæ alii loquuntur, Plaut. Excipere verba alicujus, Cic. Mandata, voces excipere, Tac. Legere sermonem alicujus. Vacare sermoni alicujus, Curt. Pendere ab ore narrantis, Ovid. Devorare dicta, Plaut. Usurpare auribus. Advertere animum, Er.
units.tr: To hear] To attend carefully. To give one's attention: to listen to a speech, Cic. Plaut. To lend ears, Tac. To prick up the ears, Ter. To apply oneself to hearing, Plin. To lend an ear, to give heed to someone. To receive orders by ear. To bring the ears near, Ter. To catch what others say, Plaut. To catch someone's words, Cic. To catch commands and voices, Tac. To gather someone's speech. To have leisure for someone's speech, Curt. To hang on the lips of the speaker, Ovid. To devour words, Plaut. To take in with the ears. To turn the mind to, Er.

units.la: Audire de aliquâ re] Ter. Audire aliquid, Id. Audivi è, ex, de, ab aliquo. Audivi dici: dicere sæpe majores nostros audivi, abs. Sic à majoribus nostris accepimus. Accipere multa aurib. Aures accipiunt. Accipe orationem. Auditionem de aliquâ re accipere. Accipere auditione & famâ: de aliquo aliquid. Non exaudimus nos metipsos. Venit, pervenit, accidit, permanavit ad aures meas, Cic. Pervenit ad me, Plaut.
units.tr: To hear about something] Ter. To hear something, Id. I have heard it from, out of, about, or from someone. I have heard it said: I have often heard our elders say, abs. Thus we have received it from our ancestors. To take in many things by ear. The ears receive. Receive the speech. To receive a report about a matter. To get word by hearing and by report of something about someone. We do not hear ourselves. It came, reached, befell, and seeped to my ears, Cic. It reached me, Plaut.

units.la: Auditur aliquid novi] Cic. Affertur nuntius. Nuntii literæque celebrant. Constanti famâ atque sermone omnium celebratum est. Perfertur nunciis, literis, sermone omnium. Percrebuit vox, intonuit. Increbuit, increpuit aliquid. Est & nonnullus odor dictaturæ. Emanat fama, Cic. Sermo permanaverat quòd, Sen. Ea res in compitis agitatur, Liv. Apparet, i.e. auditur. Sonitûs ungularum appareant, Plaut. Sentite sonorem, Id. Ad nos vix tenuis rerum perlabitur aura. Virg.
units.tr: Something new is heard] Cic. A message is brought. Messages and letters spread it abroad. It was made known by the constant rumour and talk of all. It is carried by messengers, letters, and the talk of all. The voice spread, thundered. Something grew, rang out. There is also some scent of a dictatorship. Rumour spreads, Cic. A talk had spread that, Sen. The matter is discussed at the crossroads, Liv. It appears, i.e. it is heard. The sound of hooves appears, Plaut. Feel the noise, Id. Only a faint breeze of events glides to us, Virg.

units.la: Audivi obscurè] In strepitu exaudiisse videor, Cic. Insidet imis auribus. Quasi per nebulam audivi, Plaut.
units.tr: I have heard indistinctly] I seem to have caught it amid the din, Cic. It lodges in the innermost ears. As if I had heard it through a mist, Plaut.

units.la: Audire benè, vel malè sc. de se] Secundiore famâ esse, Suet. Minûs commodè audit, Cic. Vid. Infamis & Sermones.
units.tr: To be well or ill spoken of (sc. of oneself)] To be in better repute, Suet. He is less favourably spoken of, Cic. See Infamous and Rumours.

units.la: Auditio] Auscultatus, Apul. Acroasis, Varro.
