units.tr: Hearing] A listening, Apul. A lecture, Varro.

units.la: Auditor] Auscultator. Concionatorius populus, Cic. Auritus populus, Plaut. Humanum genus est avidum auricularum (i.e. auditorum) Lucr.
units.tr: Hearer] A listener. An audience fond of oratory, Cic. An audience all ears, Plaut. The human race is greedy for little ears (i.e. hearers), Lucr.

units.la: Auditorium] Acroaterium. Vid. Schola.
units.tr: Lecture hall] A lecture room. See School.

units.la: Auditus gravis] Audiendi sensus hebes, Cic. Gravitas, Tarditas aurium, Plin. Gravitas audiendi, Id.
units.tr: Dull hearing] Dullness of the sense of hearing, Cic. Heaviness and slowness of the ears, Plin. Heaviness of hearing, Id.

units.la: Ave] Vid. Salve.
units.tr: Hail] See Salve.

units.la: Avellana] Corylus edura, Virg. Nux coryli, Pontica, Prænestrina, Prænestica, calva, Macrob.
units.tr: Hazelnut] Hard hazel, Virg. The nut of the hazel: Pontic, Praenestine, Praenestic, bald, Macrob.

units.la: Avere] Ardere cupiditate incredibili. Cupiditate incendi. Cupere ardenter. Cupide appetere. Discupere. Prægestire. Anhelare. Inhiare. Efferri studio. Æstuare. Mori desiderio, Cic. Perfixus sum desiderio, Lucr. Imminet exitio vir conjugis, Ovid.
units.tr: To long for] To burn with an incredible desire. To be inflamed with desire. To desire ardently. To seek eagerly. To long for keenly. To be eager. To pant. To gape. To be carried away with zeal. To seethe. To die of longing, Cic. I am pierced through with longing, Lucr. The husband threatens the wife with ruin, Ovid.

units.la: Avertere] Expiare. Detorquere, Cic. Averruncare, Pacuv.
units.tr: To avert] To expiate. To turn aside, Cic. To avert by charms, Pacuv.

units.la: Aufugere] Vid. Profugere.
units.tr: To flee away] See To flee forth.

units.la: Augere] Facere sibi accessionem magnam. Afferre incrementum. Locupletare. Cumulare, Cic. Exaugere. Auctare, Plaut. Augmentare thesauros, Firm. Adauctare, Acci. Auctitare, Tacit. Augmen addere. Augmine donare, Lucr. Geminare, Ingeminare, Ovid. In majus ferre. Prohibere. Multiplicare æs alienum, Caf. Dare pabula morbo, Ovid.
units.tr: To increase] To make a great addition to oneself. To bring an increment. To enrich. To heap up, Cic. To increase greatly. To enlarge, Plaut. To augment the treasures, Firm. To add to, Accius. To increase, Tac. To add an augmentation. To endow with increase, Lucr. To redouble, to double again, Ovid. To carry to a greater extent. To hold back. To multiply debt, Caes. To give food to a disease, Ovid.

units.la: Augescere] Affluunt opes, copiæ, Liv. Sumunt augmina noctes, Lucr. Gliscit invidia, Tac. Crescit dies, Lucr. Ingeminant curæ, Virg.
units.tr: To grow] Wealth and resources flow in, Liv. The nights gain in length, Lucr. Envy grows, Tac. The day grows, Lucr. Cares redouble, Virg.

units.la: Augmentum] Accessio honoris. Adjunctio virtutis, Cic. Auctus aquarum, Plin. Augmen noctium, Lucr. Accretio lunæ. Incrementum rerum, Liv.
units.tr: Increase] An addition of honour. An addition of virtue, Cic. The swelling of the waters, Plin. The lengthening of the nights, Lucr. The waxing of the moon. The growth of things, Liv.

units.la: Augur] Pullarius. Interpres auguriorum. Qui avium cantum intelligunt: magisque ex alieno jecore sapiunt, quam suo, Pacuv.
units.tr: Augur] A keeper of the sacred chickens. An interpreter of omens. One who understands the song of birds, and who knows more from another's liver than from his own, Pacuv.

units.la: Augurari] Augurare. Augurium agere. Auspicari. Auspicium agere, gerere, capere, Cic. Auspicium mittere, facere, Liv.
units.tr: To augur] To practise augury. To take the auspices. To take omens. To take, hold, or get the auspices, Cic. To send out or make the auspices, Liv.

units.la: Augurium] Auguratio. Auguratus. Prædictio augurum, Cic. Auspicium, Id. Plaut. Tripudium pullorum, Cic. Solistimum tripudium, Id.
units.tr: Augury] The art of augury; the office of augur. The prediction of augurs, Cic. Auspices, Cic. Plaut. The dance of the chickens, Cic. A solitary dance of the chickens, Id.

units.la: Avidè] Cupidè. Ardenter. Sitienter. Ad insaniam concupiscere, Cic. Flagranter. Flagrantissimè, Tac. Cupidissimè, Cæf. Effusè diligere, Plin. Effusis habenis, Val. Max.
units.tr: Eagerly] Greedily. Ardently. Thirstily. To desire to the point of madness, Cic. Blazingly. Most blazingly, Tac. Most greedily, Caes. To love lavishly, Pliny. With loosened reins, Val. Max.

units.la: Aviditas] Vid. Cupiditas.
units.tr: Eagerness] See Desire.

units.la: Avidus laudis] Laudis avarus. Avens gloriæ. Cupiens famæ. Famelicus gloriæ. Famam sitit. Esurientissimus laudis. Mira gloriæ fames habet hominem. Ambit honores. Nullius rei, quàm gloriæ ambitiosior. Appetens honoris, Er.
units.tr: Greedy for praise] Greedy of praise. Desiring glory. Longing for fame. Hungry for glory. Thirsts for fame. Most hungry for praise. A wondrous hunger for glory possesses the man. He courts honours. More ambitious for nothing than for glory. Seeking after honour, Er.

units.la: Avis] Ales, Plin. Volucris, Virg. Cantatrices aves, Var. Præpetes, Fest.
units.tr: Bird] A winged creature, Plin. A flying thing, Virg. Singing birds, Varro. Swift-flying birds, Fest.

units.la: Avius] Vid. Invius.
units.tr: Pathless] See Trackless.

units.la: Aula] Ædes aulicæ, Lamprid. Domus aulica, Spartian. IC. Vid. Area.
units.tr: Court] Courtly buildings, Lamprid. A courtly house, Spartian. Jurists. See Area.

units.la: Aulicus] Aulico fastigio ornatus, Iul. Cap. Aulam lambens, Lipf.
units.tr: Courtier] Adorned with courtly eminence, Iul. Cap. Licking the court, Lipsius.

units.la: Aulici miseri] Aulica vita splendida miseria.
units.tr: Courtiers are wretched] Court life is splendid misery.

units.la: Aulici impii] Exeat ex aulâ, qui volet esse pius.
units.tr: Courtiers are impious] Let whoever wishes to be pious leave the court.

units.la: Aulicorum honor inconstans] Aulici sunt calculis Arithmeticis similes; qui pro collocantis arbitrio, alias centum millia, alias teruncium valent.
units.tr: The honour of courtiers is inconstant] Courtiers are like arithmetical counters, which are worth now a hundred thousand, now a farthing, according to the will of the one who places them.

units.la: Aura] Ventulus, Ter. Aurarum leves animæ, Lucr. Flatus lenissimus, mollissimus. Fluxus aëris placidus & æquabilis, Plin.
units.tr: Breeze] A little wind, Ter. Light breaths of the winds, Lucr. A very gentle, very soft blast. A calm and even flow of air, Plin.

units.la: Aurà victitare] Vento pasci. Vento vivere. Rore pasci.
units.tr: To live on the breeze] To be fed by the wind. To live on the wind. To feed on dew.

units.la: Auratus] Vid. Deauratus.
units.tr: Gilded] See Gilded.

units.la: Aurifaber] Aurifex, Cic. Faber auri, Hor. Argenti cælator, Plin.
units.tr: Goldsmith] A goldworker, Cic. A smith of gold, Hor. An engraver of silver, Plin.

units.la: Aurifodina] Auraria, Tacit. Arrugia, Plin.
units.tr: Gold mine] A gold-bearing mine, Tac. An ore-pit, Plin.

units.la: Auriga] Aurigandi arte clarus, Suet. Restiarius, Front. Bigarum agitator, Apul. Fex terræ, Lud. Viv. Vector, Cic.
units.tr: Charioteer] Famous for the art of driving, Suet. A net-fighter, Front. A driver of a two-horse chariot, Apul. The dregs of the earth, Lud. Viv. A carrier, Cic.

units.la: Aurigari] Sustinere currum equosque, Cic. Vecturam facere, Quint. Factitare vecturam, Gell. Vecturis vivere, Var. Vellaturam facere, Id.
units.tr: To drive a chariot] To hold the chariot and horses, Cic. To carry passengers for hire, Quint. To ply a carriage trade, Gell. To live by carrying, Varro. To carry for hire, Id.

units.la: Auris] Auricula, Cic.
units.tr: Ear] A little ear, Cic.

units.la: In aurem dicere] Ad aurem referre. Admonere ad aurem. Obloqui alicui, Cic. Suffla re aliquid alicui, Amm. Stillare in aurem aliquid, Iuv. Garrire in aurem, Mart.
units.tr: To speak into the ear] To report in the ear. To admonish in the ear. To contradict someone, Cic. To whisper something to someone, Amm. To drip something into the ear, Juv. To chatter in the ear, Mart.

units.la: Aurora] Aurora prima, Crastina, Lutea, Virg. Mater, Matuta, Fest. Eos, Ovid.
units.tr: Dawn] Early dawn, tomorrow's dawn, golden dawn, Virg. Mother, Matuta, Fest. Eos, Ovid.

units.la: Aurum] Metallorum sol. Intus mera puritas, foris merum pretium.
units.tr: Gold] The sun of metals. Pure purity within, pure price without.

units.la: Auscultare] Aurium operam dare, Cic. Vid. Attendere.
units.tr: To listen] To give heed with the ears, Cic. See To attend.

units.la: Auspicatus] Vid. Felicitatem ferens.
units.tr: Auspicious] See Bringing happiness.

units.la: Austeri mores à solitudine sunt] Austeritas solitudinis socia & comes.
units.tr: Austere manners come from solitude] Austerity is solitude's companion and comrade.

units.la: Authenticus] Vid. Fide dignus.
units.tr: Authentic] See Worthy of trust.

units.la: Autographum] Idiographum, Gell. Meâ manu scripsi. Manus mea, tua, sua, Cic.
units.tr: Autograph] An idiograph, Gell. I wrote it with my own hand. My hand, your hand, his hand, Cic.

units.la: Automatum] Automataria, Plp. Pegmata per se surgentia.
units.tr: Automaton] Self-moving machines, Plp. Figures rising of themselves.

units.la: Autumnus] Tempestas autumna, Plin. Autumnitas, Cic. Horreum anni. Autumnat semper in Italiâ, Plin. i. e. autumnus est.
units.tr: Autumn] Autumn weather, Plin. Autumnal season, Cic. The granary of the year. It is always autumn in Italy, Plin., i.e. it is autumn.

units.la: Auxiliari] Ferre opem. Opitulari. Subvenire. Succurrere alicui. Subsidio alicui venire, currere. Lapso dexteram porrigere, Cic. Suppetias ferre, offerre alicui, Plaut. Tempore adveni tibi suppetias, Id. Afferre alicui opem, auxilium, Ter. Suppetias alicui ire, ferre, mittere, Caes. Auxilio alicui esse, Ter. Item, Adesse alicui, Cic. Suffragari alicujus cupiditati, Afferre alicui auram favoris, Id. Adstipulari alicui, Plin.
units.tr: To help] To bring aid. To lend a hand. To come to the rescue. To succour someone. To come or run to someone's support. To stretch out a right hand to one who has fallen, Cic. To bring reinforcements or offer them to someone, Plaut. I have come to help you in time, Id. To bring help or assistance to someone, Ter. To go, bring, or send reinforcements to someone, Caes. To be of help to someone, Ter. Likewise, to stand by someone, Cic. To support someone's desire, to lend someone a breath of favour, Cic. To back someone, Plin.

units.la: Auxiliator] Adstipulator, Cic. Adscriptor dignitatis meae. Suffragator, Id. Secundanus. Secundarum partium, Cic. Secundarum, (Abfol.) Tertiarum partium, Id. Non assertor gloriae ejus, sed auctor. Adminiculator, Gell. Cooperator, Apul.
units.tr: Helper] A fellow supporter, Cic. One who adds his name to my dignity. A supporter, Cic. A second, one of the secondary party, Cic. Of the second rank, of the secondary party (absolutely), of the third party, Id. Not a champion of his glory, but its author. An assistant, Gell. A co-worker, Apul.

units.la: Auxilium] Adjutorium, Cic. Causae adjuvantes. Adjuvantia causarum. Adminiculum. Praesidium. Subsidium. Momentum, Id. Suppetiae, Caes. Suppetiatus, Non. Ops, Hor. Opera. Instrumentum virtutis, Cic. Levius reddunt onus multae manus. Levamen, Sipont.
units.tr: Help] Assistance, Cic. Causes that help. Things that aid a cause. A prop. A protection. A reserve. A support. A weight, Cic. Reinforcements, Caes. Assistance rendered, Non. Aid, Hor. Labour. An instrument of virtue, Cic. Many hands lighten the burden. Relief, Sipont.

units.la: Auxilium inspiratum] Deus ex improviso apparens. Deus ex machina.
units.tr: Help sent from above] A god appearing unexpectedly. A god from the machine.

units.la: Auxilium insufficiens] Lunae radiis non maturescit botrus.
units.tr: Insufficient help] The cluster does not ripen in the rays of the moon.

units.la: Auxilium est necessarium in magnis] Ope opus est ad opus. Levius reddunt opus manus multae.
units.tr: Help is necessary in great matters] Work needs help for the work. Many hands lighten the work.

units.la: Auxilium implorare] Suppetiatum inclamare, Apul. Quiritare, Var. Fidem alicujus implorare, Cic. Ter. Caes. Hominum fidem obtestari, Liv.
units.tr: To implore help] To call out for assistance, Apul. To cry for help, Varro. To implore someone's faith, Cic. Ter. Caes. To call on the faith of men, Liv.

units.la: Auxilium militare] Supplementum, Cic. Auxiliarius miles. Auxiliariae cohortes, Id. Subsidiaria cohors, Liv. Auxiliaria manus, Volcat. Subitarii milites, Liv. Ferentarius, Var. Adscensi, Veget.
units.tr: Military help] Reinforcement, Cic. An auxiliary soldier. Auxiliary cohorts, Cic. A reserve cohort, Liv. An auxiliary band, Volcat. Reserve soldiers, Liv. Light-armed troops, Varro. Rear-guard, Veget.

units.la: Axioma] Vid. Sententia.
units.tr: Axiom] See Maxim.

units.la: Axis] Verticulum, Var.
units.tr: Axis] A little pivot, Varro.

units.la: Axis caelestis] Vertex, cardo coelorum, Vitruv. Centrum coeli, Plin.
units.tr: Heavenly axis] The pole, the hinge of the heavens, Vitr. The centre of the heavens, Plin.

units.la: B.
units.tr: B.

units.la: Bacchari] Bacchanal exercere. Bacchanal facitis in cellâ vinariâ, Plaut. Bacchanalia vivere, Iuv. In illâ vitâ turpissimè perbacchatus es, Cic. Furere & Bacchari, Id. Temulento agmine commessabundus incessit. Commessantium modo agere, Liv. Parentare luxuriæ, Sen. Effundi in luxum, epulas, nocturnos coetus, Tacit. Lustris perire, Lucr. Luculentè habere diem, Plaut. Tuburcinari de suo, si quid domi sit, Id. Profusissimè celebrare dies festos, Suet. Popinari, Iul. Capit. Luculentè habere diem, Plaut.
units.tr: To revel] To carry on like a Bacchanal. "You carry on like Bacchanals in the wine-cellar" (Plaut.). "To live a Bacchanalian life" (Juv.). "In that life you have revelled most shamefully" (Cic.). "To rave and revel" (Id.). "He advanced in a drunken troop, carousing." "To act like revellers" (Liv.). "To pay funeral rites to luxury" (Sen.). "To give oneself up to luxury, feasts and nocturnal gatherings" (Tacit.). "To waste away in brothels" (Lucr.). "To make a splendid day of it" (Plaut.). "To gobble up one's own property, if there is anything at home" (Id.). "To celebrate festival days most lavishly" (Suet.). "To haunt cookshops" (Iul. Capit.). "To make a splendid day of it" (Plaut.).

units.la: Bacchanalia] Liberalia. Dionysia, Cic. Hilaria, Bud. Agonalia, Ovid. Jus luxuriæ publicæ datum est. Exuenda est toga, dum hilarius in voluptates omnis turba procumbit, Sen. Floralia, Henr. Steph. Pridie cinerum, Cic.
units.tr: Bacchanalia] Liberalia. Dionysia (Cic.). Hilaria (Bud.). Agonalia (Ovid.). Licence for public debauchery was granted. "The toga must be cast off, while the whole crowd more cheerfully gives itself up to pleasures" (Sen.). Floralia (Henr. Steph.). "The day before Ash Wednesday" (Cic.).

units.la: Baculus] Scipio, Liv. Pedum, Virg.
units.tr: Staff] Scipio (Liv.). Pedum (Virg.).

units.la: Bajulare] Attollere humeris. Subigere feretro, Virg. Succollare aliquid. Vecturas corpore factitare, Plin.
units.tr: To carry] To lift on the shoulders. "To bear on a bier on the shoulders" (Virg.). To carry something on one's back. "To make carrying trips with the body" (Plin.).

units.la: Bajulus] Phalangarius, & Palangarius, Non. Cistifer, Mart. Vectiarius, Vitruv. Clitellarius homo, Plin. Gerulus, Hor. Portitor, Stat. Vecturas corpore factitans, Gell. Dossuarius, Var.
units.tr: Porter] Phalangarius and Palangarius (Non.). Cistifer (Mart.). Vectiarius (Vitruv.). A man who carries like a pack-animal (Plin.). Gerulus (Hor.). Portitor (Stat.). One who makes carrying trips with his body (Gell.). Dossuarius (Var.).

units.la: Balæna] Cetus, Plaut. Cete immania, Virg. Cetos, Celf. Bellua marina, Fest. Bellua Ponti, Horat.
units.tr: Whale] Cetus (Plaut.). "Monstrous whales" (Virg.). Cetos (Celf.). A sea monster (Fest.). "Monster of the sea" (Horat.).

units.la: Balare] Balitare, Plaut. Belare, Var. Blacterare arietum est, Auth. Philon.
units.tr: To bleat] Balitare (Plaut.). Belare (Var.). Bleating is the cry of rams (Auth. Philon.).

units.la: Balbus] Atypus, Gell. Qui inexplanatâ est linguâ, Plin. Pfellus, Cæl. Bambalio, Cic. Titubans linguâ, Ovid. Infracta loquelâ vox. Traulus, Cæl. Rhod. Os balbum pueri, Hor. vid. Hæsitans.
units.tr: Stammering] Atypus (Gell.). One whose tongue is not free (Plin.). Pfellus (Cæl.). Bambalio (Cic.). Faltering in speech (Ovid.). A voice with a broken utterance. Traulus (Cæl. Rhod.). "The stammering mouth of a boy" (Hor.). See Hesitant.

units.la: Balbuties] Titubantia linguæ, Macrob. Nodus linguæ & spiritûs vinculum, Gell. Debilitas linguæ, Mart. vid. Hæsitatio.
units.tr: Stammering] Faltering of the tongue (Macrob.). "A knot of the tongue and a bond of the breath" (Gell.). Weakness of the tongue (Mart.). See Hesitation.

units.la: Balbutire] Fringultire. Tertiatò & quartatò dicere verba, Sen. Infringere linguam, Lucr. Vid. Hæsitare.
units.tr: To stammer] To stutter. To say words three and four times over (Sen.). "To break the tongue" (Lucr.). See To hesitate.

units.la: Balbutire data operâ, ut delicati quidam] Verbis sonat plorabile rabile quiddam, ultra nequitiam fractis, Claud. Supplanta-re verba palato, Perf. Balba feris annoso verba palato, Hor. Frangere vocem, Quint. Blanda atque infracta loquela, Lucr. Ut mulsa loquitur! Plaut. Nimium lepidè fabulata est. Veneris mera est oratio, Id. Eliquare vocem, Perf Balbutientem linguam in dimidiata verba moderari, Hieron. Ad muliebres blanditias vocem extenuare, Sen.
units.tr: To stammer on purpose, as some affected people do] "With words she makes a sound to be wept over, a babble, broken beyond wantonness" (Claud.). "To trip over words on the palate" (Pers.). "To lisp words with an aged palate" (Hor.). "To break the voice" (Quint.). "A soft and broken speech" (Lucr.). "How sweetly she talks!" (Plaut.). "She has told the story far too charmingly. Her speech is pure Venus" (Id.). "To melt the voice" (Pers.). "To hold the stammering tongue to half-words" (Hieron.). "To thin the voice into womanly coaxing" (Sen.).

units.la: Balneum] Caldarium, Sen. Lavatrina, Var. Latrinum, Id. Lavacrum, Gell.
units.tr: Bath] Caldarium (Sen.). Lavatrina (Var.). Latrinum (Id.). Lavacrum (Gell.).

units.la: Balnea] Balneae publicae, Cic. Res quadrantaria, Sen. (quia ibi quadrante lavabantur) Sudatoria cella. Balineae, Plaut. Nymphaeum, Plin. Nymphaea, Id.
units.tr: Baths] Public baths (Cic.). "A cheap-bath business" (Sen.), because people bathed there for a quadrans. A sweating-room. Balineae (Plaut.). Nymphaeum (Plin.). Nymphaea (Id.).

units.la: Baptismus] Salutare lavacrum. Salutaris aqua, ablutio. Sancta tinctura.
units.tr: Baptism] A saving washing. Saving water, ablution. Holy dipping.

units.la: Baptizare] Tingere, Cypr. Intingere, Tert. Sacro baptismate abluere. Sacro lavacro tingere.
units.tr: To baptize] To dip (Cypr.). To immerse (Tert.). To wash with holy baptism. To dip in a holy washing.

units.la: Baptisterium] Fons sacer, Paul.
units.tr: Baptistery] Holy font (Paul.).

units.la: Barba] Barbitium, Apul. Honor aetatis. Ornamentum viri. Virilis praerogativa.
units.tr: Beard] Barbitium (Apul.). The mark of age. The ornament of a man. The manly prerogative.

units.la: Barbare] Cyclopum more.
units.tr: Barbarously] In the manner of the Cyclopes.

units.la: Barbarus] Cyclops. Cyclopica vita, agrestis, Cic. InCultus & horridus vir. Inconditus. Barbarus moribus, Id. Ferox. In crasso aere natus, Hor. Abnormis rusticus, Id. Rusticitati quam deliciis propior, Plin. Barbaricis moribus, Apul. Vid. Incultus.
units.tr: Barbarian] Cyclops. Cyclopean life, rustic (Cic.). An uncultivated and rough man. Unpolished. Barbarous in manners (Cic.). Fierce. "Born in thick air" (Hor.). "A boorish countryman" (Id.). "Nearer to rusticity than to luxury" (Plin.). "In barbarian manners" (Apul.). See Uncultivated.

units.la: Barbatus] Barbatulus, Cic. Barbiger, Lucr. Multibarbus, Apul. Tectus lanugine malas, Ovid. Tu, qui stas cum hirquina barba, Plaut. Homo barba promissa, Liv. Summissa, Suet. Homo maxima barba, Cic.
units.tr: Bearded] Slightly bearded (Cic.). Bearing a beard (Lucr.). Much-bearded (Apul.). "Cheeks covered with down" (Ovid.). "You who stand with a goat's beard" (Plaut.). "A man with a beard allowed to grow" (Liv.). With the beard let down (Suet.). "A man with a very great beard" (Cic.).

units.la: * Bardus] Bos, tardum pecus. Ad clitellas natus. Tardus & indocilis. Tardus & indocilis. Tardo ingenio, Cic. Retusum ingenium, hebes. Plumbeus homo, Id. Baeotica auris. Baeoticum ingenium, Non. Obesae navis, Hor. Iners ingenium, Ovid.
units.tr: Dull] An ox, a sluggish beast. Born for the pack-saddle. Slow and unteachable. Slow and unteachable. Of sluggish mind (Cic.). A blunted, dull wit. "A leaden man" (Id.). "A Boeotian ear, a Boeotian mind" (Non.). "A sluggish ship" (Hor.). "A lazy mind" (Ovid.).

units.la: Basilica] Palatium, Mart. Regia, Virg. Augustale, Quint. Praetorium, Ioh. 18.
units.tr: Basilica] Palace (Mart.). Royal hall (Virg.). Augustale (Quint.). Praetorium (John 18.).

units.la: Basis] Spira, Vitruv. Stylobata, Var. Scamilli, Vitruv. Stereobatae, Id.
units.tr: Base] Torus (Vitruv.). Stylobata (Var.). Scamilli (Vitruv.). Stereobatae (Id.).

units.la: Beatissime] Reddidisti me mihi, Cic. Reddidisti mihi animum, Id.
units.tr: Most blessed] "You have restored me to myself" (Cic.). "You have restored my spirit to me" (Id.).

units.la: Beatitudo] Secretis malis omnibus cumulata bonorum complexio, Cic. Deorum felicitas, Vita, Ter.
units.tr: Blessedness] "A combination of goods heaped together, with every evil removed" (Cic.). The happiness of the gods, life (Ter.).

units.la: Nemo Beatissimus] Nihil ab omni parte beatum.
units.tr: No one is most blessed] Nothing is blessed in every respect.

units.la: Beatus sum] In coelo sum. Deus sum.
units.tr: I am blessed] I am in heaven. I am a god.

units.la: Belgium] Gallia Belgica, Hirt. Celtica, Plin.
units.tr: Belgium] Belgic Gaul (Hirt.). Celtic (Plin.).

units.la: Bellaria] Mensæ secundæ. Tragemata, Pemmata, Gell. Epiphonemata, Rhod. Mactea, Suet. Trogalia, Cassian. Coluthea, Plaut.
units.tr: Dessert] Second course. Tragemata, Pemmata (Gell.). Epiphonemata (Rhod.). Mactea (Suet.). Trogalia (Cassian.). Coluthea (Plaut.).

units.la: Bellator] Belligerator. Præliator, Tac. Pugnator, Liv. Ares, Plaut.
units.tr: Warrior] A bearer of war. A fighter (Tac.). A fighter (Liv.). Ares (Plaut.).

units.la: Bellicosus] Bellicosa civitas, natio, Liv. Pugnax Centurio, Cic. Pugnacissimæ legiones, Sen. Belliger, Mart. Stat. Spectatus bello, Tacit. Præstans bellis, Sil. Omnibus belli dotibus eminentissimus sui seculi, Paterc. Bello durus, egregius, intractabilis, Virg. Militiæ gnarus, acer, impiger, Tacit. Bello bonus, Salust. Sciens pugnæ, Horat. Belli potens, Enn. Bellosus, Cæcil. Armipotens, Stat. Armisonus, Claud. Martialis. Sub Martis stellâ natus, Sipont. Marte bellacior, seu pugnacior, Er.
units.tr: Warlike] A warlike state, a warlike nation (Liv.). A fighting centurion (Cic.). Most combative legions (Sen.). War-bearing (Mart., Stat.). Distinguished in war (Tac.). Excelling in wars (Sil.). Most eminent of his age in all the gifts of war (Paterc.). Hard in war, outstanding, intractable (Virg.). Skilled in soldiering, keen, untiring (Tac.). Good in war (Sall.). Knowing the fight (Hor.). Powerful in war (Enn.). War-loving (Caecil.). Mighty in arms (Stat.). Arms-sounding (Claud.). Martial. Born under the star of Mars (Sipont.). More warlike, or more pugnacious, than Mars (Er.).

units.la: Bellicus] Militaris, Cic. Castrensis ratio, Id. Militarius. Præliaris, Plaut. Pugnatorius, Suet. Martius miles, Ovid. Bellatorius stylus, Plin. Belliger labor, Valer. Bellifera Italia, Claud. Bellicrepa saltatio, Fest. Ars duellica, Plaut.
units.tr: Military] Military (Cic.). A military plan (Id.). Military. Concerned with battle (Plaut.). For fighting (Suet.). A martial soldier (Ovid.). A warlike style (Plin.). Warlike toil (Valer.). War-bearing Italy (Claud.). A war-dance (Fest.). The art of war (Plaut.).

units.la: Bellum] Arma, Cic. Bellica res, Id. Mars, Virg.
units.tr: War] Arms (Cic.). The business of war (Id.). Mars (Virg.).

units.la: Bellum domesticum] Bellum civile, intestinum, Cic.
units.tr: Civil war] Civil war, internal war (Cic.).

units.la: Bellum parare] Ad saga ire. Ad arma ire, Venire. Saga sumere, parare, Cic. Moliri bellum. Capere arma, Cæs. Esse in armis, Cic.
units.tr: To prepare for war] To go to the military cloak, to go to arms, to come to arms. "To put on and prepare the military cloak" (Cic.). To plan war. To take up arms (Caes.). To be under arms (Cic.).

units.la: Bellum suscitare] Bellum canere. Classicum canere. Bellum commovere, conflare. Lacessere aliquem bello, Cic. Facere bellum patriæ, Tacit. Intendere bellum in aliquem. Concitare alicui bellum, Liv.
units.tr: To stir up war] To sound war. To sound the trumpet-call. To stir up and kindle war. "To provoke someone with war" (Cic.). "To make war on one's country" (Tac.). To wage war against someone. "To stir up war against someone" (Liv.).

units.la: Bellum res innovat] Bellum omnium pater.
units.tr: War brings change to things] War is the father of all.

units.la: Bene, approbando dictum aut factum] Macte, Cic. Præclarè. Sapienter. Maturè. Expeditè. Versutè. divinè. Bellè. Festivè. stivè. Non potest melius, Id. Optimum est, Plaut. Et recte & vera dicis, Id. Bene habet, Liv. Effoetè. Graviter. Citò. Euge. Beatè, Mart. Laudo fortunas tuas, Plaut. Recte factum. Recte sanè. Rectum est, Er. Factum puta, Ter.
units.tr: Well, approving a word or deed] "Well done!" (Cic.). Excellently. Wisely. In good time. Promptly. Shrewdly. Divinely. Finely. Charmingly. Festively. "It could not be better" (Id.). "It is best" (Plaut.). "You speak both rightly and truly" (Id.). "It is well" (Liv.). Splendidly. Seriously. Quickly. Well done. Happily (Mart.). "I praise your good fortune" (Plaut.). Well done. Quite right. It is right (Er.). Consider it done (Ter.).

units.la: Bene esse] Delectatus est, ac libenter fuit. Recte ei est. Bene habet, Cic. Bene sumus. Melius mihi hoc anno non fuit domi. Nusquam fui bene (pro melius) minore dispendio, Plaut. Bene agitat, Gell.
units.tr: To be well] He was delighted and gladly was. It goes well with him. It is well with him (Cic.). We are well. I was not better at home this year. "I have never been better (instead of 'better') at less expense" (Plaut.). "He is doing well" (Gell.).

units.la: Bene mihi est] Commodè hic sum. Vos isthic commodissimè spero esse, Cic. Commoda mihi hic est sedes.
units.tr: I am well] I am comfortable here. "I hope you are most comfortable there" (Cic.). My dwelling here is comfortable.

units.la: Bene tibi est? Maneto.] Domi manere oportet bellè fortunatum.
units.tr: Are you well? Stay put] One who is splendidly fortunate ought to stay at home.

units.la: Bene est] Bene res habet. Bene sese res habet. Optimè est. Bene tibi habent principia. Optimo in loco res est, Er.
units.tr: It is well] Things are well with him. Things are going well. Things are very well. Your beginnings are going well for you. "The matter is in the best place" (Er.).

units.la: Bene esse non semper potest] Ipsa dies quandoque parens, quandoque noverca.
units.tr: It cannot always be well] The day itself is sometimes a mother, sometimes a stepmother.

units.la: Bene sit ad votum] Jupiter plue mel.
units.tr: May it be as one wishes] May Jupiter rain honey.

units.la: Bene & citò] Non quàm diu, sed quàm benè. Sat citò, si sat benè.
units.tr: Well and quickly] Not how long, but how well. Quick enough, if well enough.

units.la: Bene sibi consuluit] Benè de se meruit, Sen. Bonum consilium coepisti. Optimo consilio usus es. Nimium scis sapere.
units.tr: He has provided well for himself] "He has deserved well of himself" (Sen.). You have begun a good plan. You have used the best counsel. You know too much to be wise.

units.la: Bene-dicere] Dicere bona verba alicui, Ter.
units.tr: To speak well] To say good words to someone (Ter.).

units.la: Benedicere Deo] Deum cum laudibus & gratiis venerari, Tacit. Deus benedictionibus celebretur, Apul.
units.tr: To bless God] To honour God with praise and thanksgiving (Tacit.). God is to be celebrated with blessings (Apul.).

units.la: Benefacere] Benè mereri de aliquo, Cic. Beneficia dare, non fœnerari debemus, Sen. Rectè facere alicui, Plaut. Benigne facere alicui, Ter. Meritus erga me quod vellem, Id. Beneficium apud aliquem ponere. Conferre in aliquem, Cic. Figere beneficium clavo trabali.
units.tr: To do good] To deserve well of someone (Cic.). "We ought to give benefits, not lend them at interest" (Sen.). To do right by someone (Plaut.). To do kindness to someone (Ter.). "Deserving of me, whatever I might wish" (Id.). To place a benefit upon someone. To confer on someone (Cic.). To fix a favour to a beam of the cross.

units.la: Benefacere male facturus] Luporum catulos alere. Serpentem in sinu fovere.
units.tr: To do good while about to do harm] To feed the whelps of wolves. To cherish a serpent in one's bosom.

units.la: Benefactor] Beatificus Deus, Apul. Benè meritus de aliquo, Cic. Is fundus est mihi, Plaut. Rex meus, Plaut. Hor.
units.tr: Benefactor] The blessing-giving God (Apul.). One who has deserved well of someone (Cic.). "This estate is mine" (Plaut.). "My king" (Plaut., Hor.).

units.la: Beneficium] Benefactum. Gratia. Promeritum, Cic. Officium, Cic.
units.tr: Benefit] A good deed. A favour. Merit (Cic.). Service (Cic.).

units.la: Beneficium non erit irrecompensatum] Sere beneficium, ut metere possis.
units.tr: A benefit will not go unrepaid] Sow a benefit so that you may be able to reap.

units.la: Beneficium exhibere] Devincire sibi aliquem officiis, Cic. Demereri aliquem beneficio, Liv. Facere beneficii sui aliquid. Vid. Benefacere.
units.tr: To show a benefit] To bind someone to oneself by services (Cic.). "To win someone over by a benefit" (Liv.). To make something part of one's kindness. See To do good.

units.la: Beneficium provocat gratiam] Gratia ducit gratiam.
units.tr: A benefit calls forth favour] Favour leads on to favour.

units.la: Beneficium cum detrimento alterius] Nudato Petro, Paulum tegere.
units.tr: A benefit with another's loss] Stripping Peter to cover Paul.

units.la: Beneficium imperfectum] Panis sine sale.
units.tr: An incomplete benefit] Bread without salt.

units.la: Beneficium sit promptum] Qui citò dat, bis dat.
units.tr: Let a benefit be prompt] He who gives quickly gives twice.

units.la: Beneficium citò dare] Manu brevi dare, Vlp. Qui citò dat, bis dat.
units.tr: To confer a benefit quickly: to give with a short hand, Vlp. He who gives quickly gives twice.

units.la: Beneficium spontaneum] Bis datur, quod ultrò offertur.
units.tr: A spontaneous benefit: That is given twice which is offered unasked.

units.la: Beneficium insidiosum] Panis lapidosus, hamatus.
units.tr: An insidious benefit: Bread full of stones, baited with a hook.

units.la: Beneficia conferre in dissitos, praeteritis proximis] Fluvius, quae procul absunt, irrigat, proxima praeterit.
units.tr: Conferring benefits on distant people while passing over near ones: A river waters the things that lie far off and passes by those that are near.

units.la: Beneficiarius] Beneficium accipere, libertatem vendere est. Beneficii sui Centuriones, Suet.
units.tr: Beneficiarius: To accept a benefit is to sell one's freedom. Centurions of his own favour, Suet.

units.la: Bene meritus] In beneficiis. Ad aerarium delatus.
units.tr: Well deserving: In benefits. Brought to the treasury.

units.la: Bene valet] Recte ei est, Cic.
units.tr: Bene valet: It goes well with him, Cic.

units.la: Benevole] Placido vultu, Prop. Placidâ mente, Ovid. Secundis auribus accipere, Liv.
units.tr: Benevole: With a calm face, Prop. With a calm mind, Ovid. To hear with favourable ears, Liv.

units.la: Benevolentia] Favor. Gratia, Cic. Aura popularis, Id. Voluntas vestra si ad Poëtam accesserit, Ter.
units.tr: Benevolence: Favour. Grace, Cic. A popular breeze, Id. If your goodwill has come to the poet, Ter.

units.la: Benevolus] Benevolus animus. Affectio amicabilis, Vlp.
units.tr: Benevolent: A benevolent mind. A friendly disposition, Vlp.

units.la: Benignè] Benignissimè communicare cum aliquo, Cic. Cum bonâ gratiâ. Amabiliter in aliquem cogitare, Id. Benigniter patrocinari, Non.
units.tr: Kindly: To share most kindly with someone, Cic. With good grace. To think lovingly of someone, Id. To defend kindly, Non.

units.la: Benignitas] Benefica voluntas, Cic. Vid. Clementia. Liberalitas.
units.tr: Kindness: A beneficent will, Cic. See Clemency. Liberality.

units.la: Benignus, vid. Affabilis, Liberalis.
units.tr: Kind: see Affable, Liberal.

units.la: Bibax] Magnitudine poculorum bibendo, totam Asiam superavit, Cic. Vindemia huic non satis est soli, Plaut.
units.tr: Given to drinking: He surpassed all Asia in the size of his cups when drinking, Cic. This vintage is not enough for him alone, Plaut.

units.la: Bibendo respondere] Bibere more Graeco, Cic. Bibere optimâ fide, Plin. Bibere ad numeros, Ovid.
units.tr: To answer by drinking: To drink in the Greek manner, Cic. To drink in the best faith, Plin. To drink to the rhythm, Ovid.

units.la: Bibere] Sumere meracius, Cic. Accipere, bibere potionem, Quint. Bibere pocula, Tibul. Onerare gulam potione, Plaut. Haurire poculum, Liv. Potionem, Plin. Sumere mere Bacchi haustus, Ovid. Ducere pocula, Propert. Ducere sextarium, Iuv. Bibere haustum, vid. Haustim.
units.tr: To drink: To take neat wine, Cic. To receive and drink a potion, Quint. To drink cups, Tibul. To load the throat with drink, Plaut. To gulp down a cup, Liv. A potion, Plin. To take the draughts of Bacchus' wine, Ovid. To lead cups, Propert. To lead a sextarius, Juv. To drink a draught: see Draught.

units.la: Bibere in orbem] Dare cantharum circùm, Plaut. Ab summo bibere, Id. Cursoria potatio ut primùm labiis contigerat, Apul.
units.tr: To drink round: To pass the tankard round, Plaut. To drink from the top, Id. A hasty drinking, as soon as it had touched the lips, Apul.

units.la: Bibere largiter] Duĉtim invergere in se liquores, Plaut. Ingurgito in me merum avariter, faucibus plenis, Id. Pluet credo hodie, bibit arcus, Id. Vid. Haustim.
units.tr: To drink heavily: To pour liquor into oneself in a stream, Plaut. I gulp down neat wine greedily with a full throat, Id. I think it will rain today, the bow is drinking, Id. See Draught.

units.la: Bibere pro salute] Da puer auguriis Murænæ, i. e. pro salute, Hor. Benè mihi, benè vobis, benè amicis. Benè qui non invidet mihi, & ei, qui hoc gaudet, gaudeo, Plaut. Annosque precantur quot sumunt cyathos, Ovid. In alienum honorem intemperantem esse, Sen.
units.tr: To drink for health: Boy, give to the omens of the lamprey, that is, for health, Hor. Well for me, well for you, well for friends. Well for him who does not envy me, and I rejoice with him who rejoices in this, Plaut. And they pray for as many years as the cups they drink, Ovid. To be intemperate at another's honour, Sen.

units.la: Bibulus] Arenis sitientior. Spongiâ bibacior. Cornu siccior. Pumice aridior. Uvis passis aridior. Thracibus bibacior. Hirundine bibacior, Er.
units.tr: Given to drink: Thirstier than sand. More absorbent than a sponge. Drier than horn. Drier than pumice. Drier than raisins. More drinking than Thracians. More drinking than a swallow, Er.

units.la: Biblia] Sacri libri, Dionys. Codex sacer. Oracula divina.
units.tr: The Bible: Holy books, Dionys. A sacred codex. Divine oracles.

units.la: Bibliopegus] Compactor librorum. Concinnator librorum. Glutinator, Cic.
units.tr: Bookbinder: A binder of books. A compiler of books. A glue-man, Cic.

units.la: Bibliopola] Librarius, Gell.
units.tr: Bookseller: A bookseller, Gell.

units.la: Bibliopolium] Taberna libraria, Cic. Libraria, Gell.
units.tr: Bookshop: A bookshop, Cic. A bookshop, Gell.

units.la: Bibliotheca] Cicero Amaltheam appellat libris instructam, ad Attic. 1. Mutum concilium. Congregatio demortuorum sapientum. Pharmacopœum animi.
units.tr: Library: Cicero calls it Amalthea, furnished with books, in Att. 1. A dumb assembly. An gathering of dead wise men. A pharmacy for the mind.

units.la: In Bibliotheca versari] Conversari cum mortuis.
units.tr: To live in a library: To keep company with the dead.

units.la: Bibliotheca sine usu] Murium condimentum, pulveris receptaculum, Libri sine lectore. Tinearum habitaculum.
units.tr: A library without use: A seasoning for mice, a receptacle for dust. Books without a reader. A dwelling for moths.

units.la: Biceps] Bifrons, Virg. Anceps Janus, Ovid.
units.tr: Two-headed: Two-faced, Virg. Janus, two-faced, Ovid.

units.la: Bicorpor] Bicorporeus, Firm. Bimembris, Ovid. Biformatus, Cic. Ambiguus infans, Suet.
units.tr: Two-bodied: Two-bodied, Firm. Two-limbed, Ovid. Of two forms, Cic. An ambiguous infant, Suet.

units.la: Bidens] Bipalum, Var. Pastinum. Capreolus. (Bicorne ferrum, quo terra commovetur.) Col.
units.tr: Two-pronged: A two-pronged hoe, Var. A mattock. A hoe with a fork. (An iron with two points, with which the earth is stirred.) Col.

units.la: Bifera arbor] Bifera ficus, Col. Gemellæ vites. Bis utilis pomis arbor, Virg.
units.tr: A tree bearing twice: A fig tree bearing twice, Col. Twin vines. A tree useful twice over for its fruit, Virg.

units.la: Bilis] Cos ingeniorum. Iræ susceptaculum.
units.tr: Bile: The seat of the temper. The receptacle of anger.

units.la: Bimus] Biennis, Plin. Bimulus, Cat. Bidens ovis, Gell.
units.tr: Two years old: Two years old, Plin. A little two-year-old, Cat. A two-year-old sheep, Gell.

units.la: Bipartiri] Bifariam dispertiri, Plaut. Dividere æqualiter in duas partes, Cic. Tribuere in duas partes, Id. Bicipitem civitatem fecit, Var. Dimidium facere, Ter.
units.tr: To divide in two: To divide into two parts, Plaut. To divide equally into two parts, Cic. To assign into two parts, Id. He made the state two-headed, Var. To make half, Ter.

units.la: Bis coctus panis] vid. Panis bis coctus.
units.tr: Twice-baked bread: see Twice-baked bread.

units.la: Bis peccare] Impingere ad eundem lapidem, vel, offendere ad &c.
units.tr: To sin twice: To stumble against the same stone, or to offend, and so on.

units.la: Bis peccare non licet] Iteranti culpam venia non datur. Bis idem peccare, non est viri sapientis.
units.tr: It is not allowed to sin twice: Pardon is not granted to one who repeats a fault. To commit the same fault twice is not the part of a wise man.

units.la: Bivium] Compitum, Cic. Divortium viarum, Tacit.
units.tr: Crossroads: A crossroads, Cic. A parting of roads, Tacit.

units.la: Blesus] Traulus. Inexplanata lingua, Rhodig.
units.tr: Lisping: A stammerer. A tongue not yet unfolded, Rhodig.

units.la: Blande] Perblandè, Mart. Leniter agere, Liv. Molliter facere aliquid. Lenè, Mart. Molli articulo, Quint. Suaviter respondere, Cic.
units.tr: Flatteringly: Most flatteringly, Mart. To treat gently, Liv. To do something softly. Gently, Mart. With a soft joint, Quint. To answer sweetly, Cic.

units.la: Blandiloquus] Blandiloquens, Macrob. Blandiloquentulus. Blandidicus. Delinificus, Plaut.
units.tr: Flattering in speech: Flattering in speech, Macrob. A little flatterer. Honey-tongued. Soothing, Plaut.

units.la: Blanditiæ] Mollitudo humanitatis. Mollitia animi. Illecebræ. Lenocinium, Cic. Dulcedo, Gell. Hoc placamento blandiuntur terræ, Sen. Blandimentum, Plin. Blanditus, Liv. Blanditiés, Apul.
units.tr: Flatteries: Softness of manner. Softness of mind. Enticements. Coaxing, Cic. Sweetness, Gell. With this placating the lands are coaxed, Sen. A coaxing, Plin. Coaxing, Liv. Caresses, Apul.

units.la: Blandiri] Leniter arridere. Molli brachio, molliter facere. Delinire animum alicujus blanditiis, Cic. Demulcere caput. Dulce promere ex pectore. Loqui dicta mulsa, Plaut. Blanditer alloqui, Id. Oblinire. Mollire animos dictis, Virg. Mulcere, Plin. Addere blanditias, Ovid. Alludere alicui, Sen. Jactare popello caudam.
units.tr: To flatter: To smile gently. To stroke softly with the arm. To soothe someone's mind with flatteries, Cic. To stroke the head. To draw sweetness from the breast. To speak honeyed words, Plaut. To address someone sweetly, Id. To coax. To soften minds with words, Virg. To soothe, Plin. To add caresses, Ovid. To play with someone, Sen. To wag the tail at the crowd.

units.la: Blandiri tibi noli]Suffenus aut Mœvus tibi non sis. (Utreque fuit Poëta ineptus, & tamen sui admirator maximus.)
units.tr: Do not flatter yourself: Be not Suffenus or Maevius to yourself. (Both were inept poets, and yet great admirers of themselves.)

units.la: Blandum malum] Mellitum venenum.
units.tr: A flattering evil: Honeyed poison.

units.la: Blandus] Perblandus homo, Cic. Animula blandula, Spart. Agnâ mollior, Mart. Thaide blandior, Er.
units.tr: Flattering: A most flattering man, Cic. A charming little soul, Spart. Softer than a lamb, Mart. More flattering than Thais, Er.

units.la: Blandus sermo] Oratio ad gratiam & lenocinium elaborata, Cressot. Oratio vinula, venustula. In melle sunt sitæ linguæ vestræ, atque orationes, lacteque Corolla felle & acetolita. Libidinosa eloquentia, Quint. Oratio papavere ac sesamo sparsa, & ex mellitis verborum contexta globulis, Muret. Melleum laqueum, vocat Diog. Verba byssina, Rhodig. Suavitas decocta orationis, Cic.
units.tr: Flattering speech: A speech elaborated for favour and enticement, Cressot. A speech charming and pretty. Your tongues and speeches are set in honey, and your cups of milk are mixed with gall and vinegar. Wanton eloquence, Quint. A speech sprinkled with poppy and sesame and woven of honeyed little balls of words, Muret. Diogenes calls it a honeyed noose. Words of fine linen, Rhodig. The sweetness of a well-boiled-down speech, Cic.

units.la: Blasphemia] Verba impia in Deos dicta, Tibul. Impietas tas verborum, ex Græc. Chrysost. Sacrilega obtrectatio, Bud.
units.tr: Blasphemy: Impious words spoken against the gods, Tibul. Impiety of words, from the Greek, Chrysost. Sacrilegious slander, Bud.

units.la: Blasphemare] Impia in Deum verba profundere, jacere. Divinum numen verbo, lingua scelesta violare. Exsecrari cælites. Devotare cœlites. Tu Diis nec recte dicis, Plaut.
units.tr: To blaspheme: To pour out and hurl impious words against God. To violate the divine majesty with a word and a wicked tongue. To curse the heavenly ones. To devote the heavenly ones. You do not speak rightly of the gods, Plaut.

units.la: Blasphemus] Probrosi in Deum Divosque maledicti reus vel convictus, Bud.
units.tr: Blasphemer: One accused or convicted of abusive words against God and the gods, Bud.

units.la: Blaterare] Nugari, Cic. Ineptire, Ter. Centones alicui farcire, Plaut. Nugalia proferre alicui, Gell. Deblaterare. Deblacterare, Fest. Vid. Nugari.
units.tr: To babble: To trifle, Cic. To play the fool, Ter. To stuff someone with patchwork, Plaut. To utter trifles to someone, Gell. To babble on, Fest. See Trifle.

units.la: Blatero, onis] Nugator, Cic. Plaut. Futilis homo, Cic. Nugivendus, Plaut. Nugator graphicus, Id. Ridiculum caput, Ter. Nugo, Apul. Balatro, Hor. Homo ineptitudinis cumulatissimus, Cæcil.
units.tr: Babbler: A trifler, Cic. Plaut. A futile man, Cic. A seller of trifles, Plaut. A painted trifler, Id. A laughable head, Ter. A prattler, Apul. Balatro, Hor. A man most full of silliness, Caecil.

units.la: Boare, vid. Mugire.
units.tr: To bellow: see To bellow.

units.la: Boarius] Bubulus, Plin. Bovillus, Id.
units.tr: Of oxen: Of cattle, Plin. Of young oxen, Id.

units.la: Bona, vid. Facultates.
units.tr: Goods: see Property.

units.la: Bona exhausta alicujus] Adesæ fortunæ, Tacit. Attritæ opes, Liv. Comminutæ & depressæ opes. Diminuta prædia, Cic. Extenuatissimæ copiæ. Iufracta res, Cic. Lacinata bona, Catul. Accisæ res, Liv.
units.tr: A person's goods exhausted: Fortune worn away, Tacit. Resources worn out, Liv. Resources diminished and reduced. Estates diminished, Cic. The most meagre means. A broken estate, Cic. Tattered goods, Catul. Affairs shattered, Liv.

units.la: Bonares sine usu] Lucerna sub modio.
units.tr: Good things without use: A lamp under a bushel.

units.la: Bona res usui exposita] Lucerna super candelabro.
units.tr: A good thing set out for use: A lamp upon a lampstand.

units.la: Bona mixta malis] Nihil tam mali, cui non boni quidpiam adjunctum. Sunt bona mixta malis; sunt mala mixta bonis. Omnis commoditas sua fert incommoda secum. Malum nullum sine aliquo bono.
units.tr: Good mixed with evil: Nothing is so bad that some good is not joined to it. Some goods are mixed with evils; some evils are mixed with goods. Every advantage brings its disadvantages with it. No evil without some good.

units.la: Boni consulere] Accipere amicè, æquo animo, Cic.
units.tr: To take in good part: To receive in a friendly way, with an equable mind, Cic.

units.la: Bona causæ fiducia mihi est] Arbitrum quemvis cedo.
units.tr: I have confidence in my good cause: I will yield to any judge whatever.

units.la: Bona causa male agendo perditur] Bona nomina fiunt mala, si nunquam interpelles.
units.tr: A good cause is lost by bad pleading: Good debts become bad if you never call them in.

units.la: Bonum laudat seipsum] Vino vendibili non opus est hederâ. Merx bona reperit emptorem facilè, etiamsi in abstrusò sita sit, Plaut.
units.tr: A good thing praises itself: Saleable wine has no need of ivy. Good wares find a buyer easily, even if they lie in some hidden place, Plaut.

units.la: Bonum non facile fasti ditur] Bis aut ter quod pulchrum.
units.tr: A good thing is not easily repeated: Twice or three times what is beautiful.

units.la: Bonum spontaneum] Boni ad bonorum convivia ultro accedunt. Bonum præsens, & cumulatum] Horna messis, Plaut.
units.tr: A spontaneous good: The good come unbidden to the feasts of the good. A present and abundant good: A harvest of this year's grain, Plaut.

units.la: Bonum consilium utile] Bene consulta bonos eventus pa-riunt.
units.tr: A good counsel is useful: Well-considered counsels bring forth good outcomes.

units.la: Bonarum rerum habenda ratio]Generosus frutex fulciendus.
units.tr: Account must be taken of good things: A noble shrub must be propped up.

units.la: Boni sunt obsequiosi] Generosus equus umbrâ quoque regitur. Imperium facile est in bonos.
units.tr: The good are obliging: A noble horse is steered even by its shadow. Rule over the good is easy.

units.la: Bonis bene fit] Animi tranquillitas virtutis præmium. Bona cum bonis navigatio. Boni principii bonus finis. Bonitas mirum vitæ miraculum. Bonum fuisse te non pœniteat.
units.tr: Good is done to the good: Tranquillity of mind is the reward of virtue. A voyage with good companions. A good beginning, a good end. Goodness is a wonderful marvel of life. May it never grieve you to have been good.

units.la: Bonis parcendum] Peccat in publica commoda, Viros publicè utiles qui lædit.
units.tr: The good must be spared: He sins against the public interest who injures men who are useful to the public.

units.la: Bonis nocet, qui parcit malis] Clementia in malos, crudelitas in bonos est.
units.tr: He harms the good who spares the bad: Clemency towards the wicked is cruelty towards the good.

units.la: Bonus] Bellus, Cic. Perbonus. Probatissimus vir. Summâ bonitate præditus. Frugi homo, Id. Probus, Ter. Optimis proximus. Bonæ frugis homo, Gell. Homo de meliori notâ, melioris notæ, Cic. Quibus de meliore luto finxit præcordia Titan, Juv. Bonos viros omnia decent. Bonum manere, difficile est.
units.tr: Good: Handsome, Cic. Very good. A most approved man. Endowed with the highest goodness. A worthy man, Cic. Upright, Ter. Nearest to the best. A man of good worth, Gell. A man of better repute, of better standing, Cic. Those whose hearts Titan fashioned from better clay, Juv. All things become good men. To remain good is difficult.

units.la: Non adeo bonus] Meliora, quàm deterrima hæc sunt.
units.tr: Not so good: These things are better than the worst.

units.la: Bonus dies, vel, bonam diem precor] Felix tibi illucescat hæc dies. Matutinum Ave porto tibi, Mart Bonum manè, sicut clarum manè, Perf. Sis felix, Catul. Virg.
units.tr: Good day, or, I pray for a good day] May this day dawn happily for you. I bring you a morning greeting, Mart. A good morning, as a bright morning, Perf. Be happy, Catul. Virg.

units.la: Bos] Tardum pecus, Tib. Bucerum pecus, Fest. Grex magnus, Virg.
units.tr: Ox] A slow herd, Tib. A herd of oxen, Fest. A large flock, Virg.

units.la: Botrus] Botryon, Mart. Racemus, Virg. Uva, Col. Corymbus, Virg. Bumastus, Plin. Vinum pendens, Cat.
units.tr: Bunch of grapes] Botryon [βότρυον], Mart. A cluster, Virg. A grape, Col. A corymb, Virg. Bumastus, Plin. Wine hanging on the vine, Cat.

units.la: Brabium] Præmium victori, Virg. Palmarium, Vlp.
units.tr: Prize] A reward for the victor, Virg. A palm, a prize, Vlp.

units.la: Brachiatus] Ansatus incedit.
units.tr: Brachiatus] He walks with his arms tucked up.

units.la: Braxator] Cerevisiarius. Factor cerevisiæ.
units.tr: Brewer] A maker of beer; a brewer.

units.la: Breve gaudium] Ignis ex arundine conflatus.
units.tr: Brief joy] A fire kindled from reeds.

units.la: Breviarium] Hypomnemata. Commentarius, Cic. Recensio, Id.
units.tr: Breviary] Notes, memoranda. A commentary, Cic. A revision, Id.

units.la: Brevis, ratione longitudinis] Breve curriculum. Compendiaria via. Curta sententia. Capitalis scriptor, (qui capita rerum scribit) Pressus, Cic. Breviariæ rationes, Scæv. Parcus somnus, Plin. Pigmæo brevior, Er.
units.tr: Brief, in respect of length] A short course. A shortcut. A short saying. A writer of headings (one who writes the heads of matters). A compressed account, Cic. Brief accounts, Scæv. Sparing sleep, Plin. Shorter than a pygmy, Er.

units.la: Brevis, ratione profunditatis] Breves undæ. Brevia, Virg. Brevia dorsuosa, Amm. Brevitas fluminis, Solin. Humilis fossa, Virg. Vid. Vadum.
units.tr: Shallow, in respect of depth] Shallow waters. Shallows, Virg. Shallows with ridges, Amm. The shallowness of a river, Solin. A low ditch, Virg. See Ford.

units.la: Brevis, ratione durationis] Perexiguum tempus, Cic. Brevis ævi, Sal. Momentaneus, Sipont. Momentarius, Lamp. Oligochronius, Firmic.
units.tr: Brief, in respect of duration] A very short time, Cic. Of brief life, Sal. Momentary, Sipont. Momentary, Lamp. Short-lived, Firmic.

units.la: Brevitas] Contractio, Cic, Compendium viæ, orationis, Plaut. Exiguitas temporis, Liv.
units.tr: Brevity] A contraction, Cic. A shortening of a journey or of a speech, Plaut. Scantiness of time, Liv.

units.la: Breviter] Perbreviter, Strictim dicere. Breviter. Compressiùs loqui. Cum brevitate. Presse, Cic. Summatim,Var. Paucis, Lucr. Tribus verbis, Plaut. Capitulatim,per capita, Plin. Circumcisè, Macrob.
units.tr: Briefly] Very briefly; to speak in a nutshell. Briefly. To speak more compactly. With brevity. Concisely, Cic. In summary, Var. In a few words, Lucr. In three words, Plaut. Point by point, by heads, Plin. Tersely, Macrob.

units.la: Breviter agere] Compendiis scribendi uti. Notis verba subsequi. Compendiariò te ducam, Suet. Minore finire pomœrio.
units.tr: To deal briefly] To use shorthand in writing. To follow words with signs. I will lead you briefly, Suet. To end within a smaller boundary.

units.la: Breviter loqui] Uno verbo complectar. Strictim dicam. Quid multa ? Ne multa. Ne multis. Ne plura. Ne agam de singulis. Ne longiùs abeam. Quid quæris? summam faciam. Ad summam,summatim exponam. Ne longus sim. Breviter perstringam, Cic. Summa sequar fastigia rerum, Virg. Uno fasce complecti, Plin. Nihil opus est verbis. Rem in pauca conferam, Plaut. Ut ad pauca redeam, Ter. Mirâ verborum parsimoniâ perstringere aliquid. Paucissimis loqui verbis. Ut semel dicam. Ut finiam, Er.
units.tr: To speak briefly] I will sum it up in one word. I will speak in brief. Why say more? Not to say much. Not at length. Not more. Let me not go through each thing. Let me not wander further. What do you ask? I will make it a summary. In sum, I will set it out in outline. Let me not be long. I will touch on it briefly, Cic. I will follow the chief heights of things in summary, Virg. To embrace in one bundle, Plin. There is no need for words. I will bring the matter into a few words, Plaut. To return to a few points, Ter. To touch on something with wonderful sparingness of words. To speak in the fewest possible words. To say it once. To finish, Er.

units.la: Brevi pòst] In brevi, Cic. Perbrevi. Propediem. Paucis diebus interpositis, Id. Cis paucos dies. Cis paucas tempestates, Plaut. Vid. Exiguum tempus.
units.tr: Shortly afterwards] In a short time, Cic. Very shortly. Soon. With a few days intervening, Id. Within a few days. Within a few seasons, Plaut. See Short time.

units.la: Breviloquentia] Laconismus, Cic. Contracta & adstricta eloquentia, Cic. Compendium dicendi, Quint.
units.tr: Brief speech] Laconic speech, Cic. Eloquence contracted and compressed, Cic. A short way of speaking, Quint.

units.la: Breviloquentia grata] In re apertâ piget esse prolixum.
units.tr: Brevity pleasing] In a plain matter it is tiresome to be long-winded.

units.la: Breviloquentia, Sapientis character] Intelligenti pauca. Pauciloquus, sed eruditus.
units.tr: Brevity, the character of the wise] A word to the wise is enough. Few words, but learned.

units.la: Brutus] Vid. Stupidus.
units.tr: Dull] See Stupid.

units.la: Bubo] Strix nocturna, Lucr. Noctiluges, i. e. Bubones, Fest.
units.tr: Owl] A night screech-owl, Lucr. Night-shiners, that is, owls, Fest.

units.la: Bubulcus] Bubsequa, Sidon. Jugarius, Col. Busequa, Apul.
units.tr: Ox-herd] A ploughman's servant, Sidon. One who yokes oxen, Col. An ox-driver, Apul.

units.la: Bubulus] Bubulum lac, Col. Bovillus, Plin. Boarium forum, Fest.
units.tr: Of oxen] Ox milk, Col. Of a young bull, Plin. The cattle market, Fest.

units.la: Bucca] Rictus. Rostrum, de homine, Plaut.
units.tr: Cheek] The mouth, the gaping jaws. The snout, said of a man, Plaut.

units.la: Bucco] Buccis fluentibus homo, Cic. Bucculentus, Plaut, Masticus, Fest. Vid. Tubicen.
units.tr: Cheeky fellow] A man with flowing cheeks, Cic. Full-cheeked, Plaut. Chewing, Fest. See Trumpeter.

units.la: Buccina] Cornu, Var. Triton, Buccini concha excavata, perforata sonat, Higin. Tuba, in variis usibus, Sen. Quint. Classicum, (extra bellum) Liv. Classico ad concionem vocat.
units.tr: Trumpet] A horn, Var. A triton; a trumpet shell hollowed and pierced sounds, Higin. A trumpet, used on various occasions, Sen. Quint. A bugle call (outside war), Liv. He summons to the assembly with a bugle call.

units.la: Buccinare] Inflare buccinam, Var. Canere tubâ, Virg. Dare signum tubâ, Cæs. Occanere tubas, cornua, Tac. Implere cornu bombis, Pers. Terribilem sonitum ære canoro increpuit, Virg. Stridulum aërem elidere lituis. Concipere classica cornu, Lucan. Æneatorum occentu signo dato, Ammian. Occinere, Diomed.
units.tr: To blow the trumpet] To blow a trumpet, Var. To sound the trumpet, Virg. To give the signal with a trumpet, Cæs. To sound trumpets and horns, Tac. To fill the horn with booming, Pers. He blared a dreadful sound on the ringing bronze, Virg. To break the shrill air with curved trumpets. To sound the bugle calls on the horn, Lucan. With the trumpeters' blare, the signal being given, Ammian. To sound, Diomed.

units.la: Buccinator] Cornicen, Iuv. Cornuarius, Fest. Flator, Id. Tubicen, Sen. Liticen, Enn. Non. Æneator, Suet. Classicines, Varr. Incentor tubarum, Ammian.
units.tr: Trumpeter] A horn-player, Iuv. A horn-maker, Fest. A blower, Id. A trumpeter, Sen. A trumpeter, Enn. Non. A brazen-trumpeter, Suet. A bugler, Varr. A leader of trumpets, Ammian.

units.la: Bulimea] Canina appetentia, Gorr. Milvina orexis, ex Plaut. Camer. Magna fames, Gell. Phagedæna, Plin. Milvina appetentia, Turneb.
units.tr: Bulimia] Dog-like appetite, Gorr. Kite-like hunger, ex Plaut. Camer. Great hunger, Gell. Phagedaena [φαγέδαινα], Plin. Kite-like appetite, Turneb.

units.la: Bulla] (1) Sufflatio bullantium aquarum, Plin.
units.tr: Bubble] (1) The bubbling up of bubbling waters, Plin.

units.la: (2) Libris affixus globus] Umbilicus librorum, Hor. Martial.
units.tr: (2) A knob fixed to books] The navel of books, Hor. Martial.

units.la: Bullire] Effervescunt aquæ, Col.
units.tr: To bubble] The waters foam up, Col.

units.la: Bullire desiit] Desiit spumare, Plin.
units.tr: To cease bubbling] It ceased to foam, Plin.

units.la: Bura] Dentale, Virg. Dens aratri, Var. Buris, Virg. Curvum aratri, Var.
units.tr: Plough-beam] The ploughshare, Virg. The tooth of the plough, Var. The plough-beam, Virg. The curved part of the plough, Var.

units.la: Butyrum] Spuma lactis, Plin.
units.tr: Butter] The froth of milk, Plin.

units.la: C.
units.tr: C.

units.la: Cccare] Vid. Oletare.
units.tr: Cccare: See Oletare.

units.la: Cachinnari] Risu crepare, Cic. Crassum ridere, Pers. Dissilire risu, Sen. Majore cachinno concuti. Pulmonem risu agitare, Iuv. Ridere ore Catuli Gallicani, Catul. Emori risu.
units.tr: To guffaw: To burst with laughter, Cic. To laugh at Crassus, Pers. To split one's sides laughing, Sen. To be shaken by a greater guffaw. To set the lungs heaving with laughter, Juv. To laugh with the mouth of Catulus Gallicanus, Catul. To die of laughter.

units.la: Cachinnus] Cachinnatio. Risus maximus, mirus, Cic. Effusus, Claud. Exsertus, Liberalis cachinnus. Latissimo cachinno ad usque intestinorum dolorem redactus, Apul.
units.tr: Guffaw: Loud laughing. A very great laugh, wonderful, Cic. Unrestrained, Claud. An open, unrestrained guffaw. Reduced by the broadest guffaw even to pain in the bowels, Apul.

units.la: Cacodæmon] Genius ater. Genius salax, Hor. Genius sinister, Perf. Orcus, Cic. Vejovis, Id. Læva numina, Virg. Satan, & Satanas, ap. S.S. scriptores.
units.tr: Evil spirit: A black spirit. A lustful spirit, Hor. A sinister spirit, Pers. Orcus, Cic. Vejovis, Id. Powers of the left hand, Virg. Satan, and Satanas, in the writers of Holy Scripture.

units.la: Cacumen] Columen mentis, Catul. Apex montis, Sil. Supercilium montis, Liv. Vertex, Virg. Jugum, Cæs.
units.tr: Summit: Pillar of the mind, Catul. Peak of a mountain, Sil. Brow of a mountain, Liv. Top, Virg. Ridge, Caes.

units.la: Cadaver] Corpus animâ cassum, Lucr. Mortuale & Morticinium, Hier. Funus, Ter. Reliquiæ hominis.
units.tr: Corpse: A body bereft of life, Lucr. A dead body and carrion, Hier. A funeral, Ter. The remains of a man.

units.la: Cadere] Cadere deorsum, Lucr. Accidere ad terram, Plaut. Prolabi in caput, Liv. Pluit glans de ilice, Virg. Labitur lacryma, Ovid. Collabi, Id. Procidere, Liv. Concidere, Liv. Succidere, Gell.
units.tr: To fall: To fall down, Lucr. To come down to the ground, Plaut. To slip headlong, Liv. Acorns rain down from the holm oak, Virg. A tear slides down, Ovid. To collapse, Id. To sink down, Liv. To fall down, Liv. To fall down, Gell.

units.la: Cadere præcipitem] Decidere in præceps, Ovid. Ire præcipitem de ponte in lutum per caput pedesque, Catul. Abire præcipitem, Sal. Ferri præcipitem, Cic. Præcipitem ruere, cadere, Virg. Cadere pronum in pectus, Ovid. Præcipitare se de turri, Liv. In flumen, Cæs. Præcipitant pondera, Lucr.
units.tr: To fall headlong: To drop headlong, Ovid. To go headlong from a bridge into the mud, head and feet, Catul. To depart headlong, Sal. To be carried headlong, Cic. To rush headlong and fall, Virg. To fall forward on the chest, Ovid. To throw oneself down from a tower, Liv. Into the river, Caes. Weights plunge headlong, Lucr.

units.la: Caduca bona] Caduca hæreditas, Cic. Caducum, Vlp. Bona intestabilium, Paul. IC.
units.tr: Forfeited goods: A forfeited inheritance, Cic. Something forfeited, Ulp. Goods of the intestable, Paul IC.

units.la: Caducarium jus] Caducaria lex, Vlp. Jus publici ærarii vel fisci.
units.tr: Right of forfeiture: A law of forfeiture, Ulp. The right of the public treasury or the fisc.

units.la: Caduceator] Caducifer, Ovid. Fecialis, Var. Legatus pacem petens, Fest. Orator pacis petendæ, Liv. Orator fœderum, Cic. Pater-patratus, Liv.
units.tr: Herald: A bearer of the caduceus, Ovid. A fetial, Var. An envoy seeking peace, Fest. A speaker who seeks peace, Liv. A spokesman for treaties, Cic. Pater patratus, Liv.

units.la: Caduceum] Cerycium, Rhod. Supplicia, Fest. Ramus oleæ, Plaut. (Virga Mercurii erat.)
units.tr: Caduceus: A herald's staff, Rhod. Punishments, Fest. A branch of olive, Plaut. (It was the wand of Mercury.)

units.la: Caducus] Vid. Labilis.
units.tr: Falling: See Labilis.

units.la: Caducus morbus] Morbus comitialis, Plin. Morbus major, Celf. Morbus sonticus, Plin. Divinus, Apul. Sacer. Herculeus, Iun. Lues sacra, Deifica, Aurel. Epilepsia.
units.tr: Falling sickness: The comitial disease, Plin. The greater disease, Celsus. The sonticus disease, Plin. The divine disease, Apul. The sacred disease, the disease of Hercules, Iun. A sacred plague, a deified plague, Aurel. Epilepsy.

units.la: Cadurcum] Vas, quo aquam haurimus è puteo aut piscinâ, jumento rotam versante, Vall.
units.tr: Bucket: A vessel by which we draw water from a well or pool, with a beast turning the wheel, Vall.

units.la: Cæcitas] Cæcitas Cyclopis, Tiresiæ, Cic. Orbitas luminis. Caligo oculorum, Scotomia, Plin.
units.tr: Blindness: The blindness of the Cyclops, of Tiresias, Cic. Loss of light. A darkness of the eyes, scotomia, Plin.

units.la: Cæcutiens] Parum videns sæpe offendit, Lusciosus, Vall.
units.tr: Dim-sighted: Seeing poorly, often stumbling; purblind, Vall.

units.la: Cæcutire] Cœcultare, Fest. E duobus tria videns. In sole caligare. Parum prospicere. Tenebris crassis circumfundi, Cic. Falli visu. Caligo ob oculos obsistit, Plin.
units.tr: To be dim-sighted: To see double, seeing three out of two. To be dazzled by the sun. To see poorly. To be wrapped in thick darkness, Cic. To be deceived in one's sight. Mist stands before the eyes, Plin.

units.la: Cæcus] Cœcior Ægyptiis, Tiresiâ, Talpâ, Ipsâ cœcitate cœcior, Er. Captus oculis. Non constat oculis. Orbus luminibus, Plaut.
units.tr: Blind: Blinder than the Egyptians, than Tiresias, than a mole, blinder than blindness itself, Erasmus. Deprived of sight. Lacking sound eyes. Bereft of light, Plaut.

units.la: Cædere hostem] Profligare copias, Cic. Facere, edere stragem, Id. Conficere hostes, Id. Prosternere aciem, Liv. Fundere exercitus. Sternere omnia ferro, Id.
units.tr: To slay an enemy: To rout forces, Cic. To make a slaughter, Id. To destroy enemies, Id. To lay low the battle line, Liv. To rout armies. To strike all down with the sword, Id.

units.la: Cædere exitialiter] Ad internecionem cædere. Occisione occidere. Exstinguere, Cic. Perdere ac delere omnes ad unum, Id. Internecione disperdere, Amm. Degrassari. Exitialem cladem inferre, Stat. Cæsar fulgurat Euphratem. Ne nuncius quidem relictus.
units.tr: To slaughter utterly: To slaughter to extermination. To kill with a massacre. To wipe out, Cic. To destroy and blot out everyone to a man, Id. To destroy by slaughter, Amm. To cut to pieces. To inflict a deadly disaster, Stat. Caesar lightning across the Euphrates. Not even a messenger left behind.

units.la: Cædua silva] Renascens. Regerminans. Restibilis, Plin.
units.tr: Coppice wood: Sprouting again. Regerminating. Restibilis, Plin.

units.la: Cælare] Incidere in æs aliquid. Formata in muliebrem figuram statua, Cic. Animare aurum impressis figuris, Stat. P. Scalpere, Cic. Sculpere, Hor. Cælare in poculis aliquid, Plin. Exscalpere, Cat. Exsculpere ex quercu, Cic. Fingere, Effingere fingendo, vel pingendo corpora, Quint.
units.tr: To engrave: To cut something into bronze. A statue formed in the figure of a woman, Cic. To bring gold to life with impressed figures, Stat. P. To scrape, Cic. To sculpt, Hor. To engrave something on cups, Plin. To carve out, Cat. To hew out of oak, Cic. To fashion or form bodies by modelling or painting, Quint.

units.la: Cælator] Cælator in ære, Cic. Excusor in ære, Quint. Scalptor. Plin. Sculptor. Anaglyptes, Sipont. Statuarius, Quint. Crustarius, Plin. Faber æris, Hor. Eborarius, in Cod. Politor gemmarum, Firm. Fictor sculptilium. Gemmarius, in SS.
units.tr: Engraver: An engraver in bronze, Cic. An embosser in bronze, Quint. A carver, Plin. A sculptor. An anaglyptes, Sipont. A statuary, Quint. A crustarius, Plin. A smith of bronze, Hor. A worker in ivory, in Cod. A polisher of gems, Firm. A maker of carved images. A gem-cutter, in SS.

units.la: Cælatura] Scalpturatus. Scalptura seu sculptura. Sectura gemmarum, Plin. Anaglyptice, Sipont. Anaglyphice, Cal. Rhod. Diaglyphice, Id. Ars politurae, Plin.
units.tr: Engraving: Carving. Carving or sculpture. The cutting of gems, Plin. Anaglyptics, Sipont. Anaglyphics, Cal. Rhod. Diaglyphics, Id. The art of polishing, Plin.

units.la: Cælatum opus] Argumenta ex ebore confecta. Dolatus ex robore, Cic. Cælatura, Plin. Cælamen, Ovid. Sculptile opus, Id. Typi, Cic. Scriptiles formæ elementorum, incisæ. Atria spirantia figmentis signorum, Amm. Ancæsa vasa, Fest. Columna res gestas loquens, Enni. Phidiacæ artis opus. Phidiaco cælo formatum, Mart. Scalptus ex, Cic. Scalpturatus, Plin. Scaptus, Varr. Sigillatus, Trebel. Effigiatus, Sculptilis, Amm. Crater impressus signis, Virg.
units.tr: Engraved work: Figures made of ivory. Turned from oak, Cic. Carved work, Plin. Chased work, Ovid. Sculptured work, Id. Types, Cic. Written forms of letters, incised. Halls breathing with figures of statues, Amm. Embossed vessels, Fest. A column telling of deeds done, Ennius. A work of Phidian art. Formed with Phidian chasing, Mart. Carved from, Cic. Carved work, Plin. Scaptus, Varr. Sealed, Trebel. Fashioned, sculptured, Amm. A bowl stamped with figures, Virg.

units.la: Cæmentum] Lapis ordinarius, Vitruv. Lapis operarius, Plin. Saxum è monte revulsum, Ovid.
units.tr: Rubble: Ordinary stone, Vitr. Building stone, Plin. Stone torn from the mountain, Ovid.

units.la: Cementitius] Saxeus pons, Lucan. Lapidata templa, Suet. Vivo saxo sedilia & ostia, Virgil.
units.tr: Built of rubble: A stone bridge, Lucan. Temples built of stone, Suet. Seats and doors of living rock, Virg.

units.la: Cæsar] Augustus, Suet. Rector Imperii Romani, Amm. Princeps Principum Imperator, Cic.
units.tr: Caesar: Augustus, Suet. Ruler of the Roman Empire, Amm. Prince of princes, emperor, Cic.

units.la: Cæsus, Vid. Verbero.
units.tr: Beaten: See Verbero.

units.la: Cæsio, Vid. Sectura.
units.tr: Cutting: See Sectura.

units.la: Et Cetera] Reliqua ejusmodi. Et similia horum, Cic. Et alia hujus notæ, Sen. Aliaque ejus generis, Plin. Multaque præterea, Lucr. Cæteraque alia, & alia cætera, Arnob. Deinde quæ assolent. Et quæ sequuntur. Itemque cæteri, vel cætera, Cic.
units.tr: And so on: Other things of this kind. And similar things of these, Cic. And others of this sort, Sen. And other things of that kind, Plin. And many more besides, Lucr. And other things, and other things besides, Arnob. And whatever else is customary. And what follows. Likewise the rest, the others, Cic.

units.la: Calamarium] Theca calamaria. Theca pennaria, graphiaria, Er. ex Vall.
units.tr: Pen-case: A pen-case. A case for pens or styluses, Erasmus, from Vall.

units.la: Calamistratus] Calamistrata homo comâ, Cic. Vibratus. Cirriger, Lucr. Intonsus deliciarum causâ, Juv.
units.tr: Curled: A man with hair curled with tongs, Cic. Waved. Curly-haired, Lucr. Unshorn for the sake of luxury, Juv.

units.la: Calamitas] Pestis. Pernicies, Cic. Fortuna afflicta, adversa, misera, Id. Crux mala maxima, Plaut. Occasio virtutis.
units.tr: Calamity: Plague. Ruin, Cic. Fortune afflicted, adverse, wretched, Id. The greatest evil cross, Plaut. An occasion for virtue.

units.la: Calamitas extrema] Niobes mala. Via ad meliora calamitas. Sæpe mala sors futuri boni occasio.
units.tr: Extreme calamity: The misfortunes of Niobe. Calamity is a road to better things. Often a bad fate is the occasion of a future good.

units.la: Calamitatum cumulus] Moles mali, Cic. Thesaurus mali, Plaut. Abyssus malorum, laborum. Abyssus abyssum invocat, Psal. 42.
units.tr: Heap of calamities: A mass of evil, Cic. A treasury of evil, Plaut. An abyss of evils and troubles. Deep calleth unto deep, Ps. 42.

units.la: Calamitosi omnium præda] Arbore defecta (cadente quercu) quivis ligna colligit.
units.tr: The prey of all: When the tree has been felled (the oak having fallen), anyone gathers wood.

units.la: Calamitosus homo] Ærumnosus, quem miseriæ & ærumnæ omnes premunt, Cic. Equum Sejanum habet, solem aversum. Ventum adversum habet. Calamitate calamitosior, Fr.
units.tr: Unfortunate man: A distressed man, whom all miseries and troubles press down, Cic. He has the horse of Sejanus, the sun turned away. He has the wind against him. More calamitous than calamity, Fr.

units.la: Calcaneum] Calx, Cic. Calcaneus, Sipont.
units.tr: Heel: A heel, Cic. A heel, Sipont.

units.la: Calcar] Aculeus calcis, Col. Calx ferrata, Sil.
units.tr: Spur: The point of a spur, Col. A heel of iron, Sil.

units.la: Calcari pungere] Adhibere calcaria, Cic. Concitare equum calcaribus, Liv. Calcari agitare quadrupedem, Plaut. Subdere calcar equo, Ovid. Auferre calcaribus equum. Ferratâ calce cruentat cornipedem, Sil.
units.tr: To prick with spurs: To apply spurs, Cic. To urge a horse on with spurs, Liv. To drive a quadruped with the spur, Plaut. To put spurs to a horse, Ovid. To take the spurs from a horse. With an iron-shod heel he bloodies the hoofed horse, Sil.

units.la: Calcare] Calcatu solidare terram, Pallad. Recalcare terram. Supercalcare, Col. Prosubigere, Virg. Augutari pedibus, Titin. Depsere, Condepsere, Cat.
units.tr: To tread: To make the ground firm by treading, Pallad. To tread the earth again. To tread over, Col. To plough under, Virg. To be trodden under foot, Titin. To trample down, Cat.

units.la: Calcarius lapis] Lapis Thracius.
units.tr: Spur-stone: Thracian stone.

units.la: Calceamentum] Calceamen, Plin. Calceatus, Suet. Tegmina pedum, Col. Pedalia, Fest. Solea objurgabere rubra, Pers. Cothurnus, calceus utrique pedi aptus, Serv. Phaecasium, Hesych. Sen.
units.tr: Footwear: Footwear, Plin. Shod, Suet. Coverings for the feet, Col. Pedalia, Fest. You will be scolded in red sandals, Pers. A cothurnus, a shoe fitting either foot, Serv. Phaecasium, Hesych. Sen.

units.la: Calceare se] Inducere calceum sibi, vel pedi, Cic.
units.tr: To shoe oneself: To put a shoe on oneself, or on one's foot, Cic.

units.la: Calceare equos] Inducere soleas jumentis, Plin. Calceare solea equum, Liv.
units.tr: To shoe horses: To put shoes on beasts of burden, Plin. To shoe a horse with a sole, Liv.

units.la: Calcitrare] Petere pedibus, Luc. Adversus stimulos calcare, Ter.
units.tr: To kick: To strike out with the feet, Lucan. To kick against the goads, Ter.

units.la: Calefacere] Concalefacere aliquem, Cic. Calefactare, Hor. Excalefacere algores, Plin. Incalefacere, Ovid. Fovere, Cic. Confovere oleas, Cat. Refovere, Ovid. Recalfacere, Recalefacere, Ovid. Fovere fomentis calidis, Cels. Tepidare, Plin. Tepefacere, Cic. Temperare ignibus aquam, Hor. Vaporat sol latus montis, Lucr.
units.tr: To warm: To warm someone thoroughly, Cic. To warm, Hor. To drive out chills, Plin. To heat up, Ovid. To foment, Cic. To warm the olive oils, Cat. To warm again, Ovid. To warm again, Ovid. To foment with warm poultices, Cels. To make lukewarm, Plin. To make tepid, Cic. To temper water with fire, Hor. The sun warms the side of the mountain, Lucr.

units.la: Calefactio] Calefactus. Excalefactio, Plin. Focillatio, Fest.
units.tr: Warming: A warming. A thorough warming, Plin. A fomentation, Fest.

units.la: Calefieri] Concalefieri, Varr. Excalefieri, Plin. Percalefieri, Lucr. Fervescere, Id. Corpora concalescunt. Recalescunt motu, Cic. Tepescere; Id. Recalefieri, Scrob. Calescere flamma. Percalescere, Ovid. Intepescere comae radiis, Id.
units.tr: To be warmed: To be heated through, Varr. To be heated up, Plin. To be thoroughly warmed, Lucr. To ferment, Id. Bodies grow warm. They grow warm again by motion, Cic. To grow lukewarm, Id. To be warmed again, Scrob. To glow with flame. To be thoroughly heated, Ovid. Hair grows warm in the rays, Ovid.

units.la: Calendarium] Fasti. Libri computationem dierum continentes, Serv.
units.tr: Calendar: Fasti. Books containing the reckoning of days, Serv.

units.la: Calendae] Neomenia, Isidor.
units.tr: Calends: The new moon, Isid.

units.la: Calidus] Tepens cinis, Stat. Formus, Fest. Formidus, Cato. Vaporeus, Arnob. Vaporosa balnea, Apul. Vaporifera fornax, Stat. Vaporatus, Col. Egelidus, Ovid.
units.tr: Warm: Warm ashes, Stat. Hot, Fest. Hot, Cato. Steaming, Arnob. Steaming baths, Apul. A furnace producing steam, Stat. Vaporous, Col. Warm, Ovid.

units.la: Calet hic] Caletur hic maxime, Plaut. Est hic caloris satis. Est nunc calor foris.
units.tr: It is hot here: It is very hot here, Plaut. There is enough heat here. Now there is heat outside.

units.la: Caliendrum, capilli factitii] Capillamentum, Suet. Externi crines, Prop. Externo tincta colore caput, Id. Captivos miscet Germania crines, Ovid. Captivis comis cultior, Mart. Comis uti emptis, Id. Appositis caput emutare capillis. Coma adulterina, Bud.
units.tr: Wig, false hair: A hairpiece, Suet. Foreign hair, Prop. A head dyed with a foreign colour, Id. Germany mixes captive hair, Ovid. More elegant with captive locks, Mart. Using bought hair, Id. To change one's head by attaching false hair. Adulterated hair, Bud.

units.la: Caligare, Vid. Caecutire.
units.tr: To be dim-sighted: See Caecutire.

units.la: Caligo, Vid. Nebula. Tenebrae.
units.tr: Darkness: See Nebula. Tenebrae.

units.la: Calix. Vid. Poculum. Callescere :/: callos nancisci] Concallere, Cic. Occallescere, Plin. Durari ad plagas, Quint. Induruit usu corpus, Ovid. Duritiem contra sensum inducere, Plin.
units.tr: Cup: See Poculum. To grow hard: to get calluses: To harden, Cic. To grow callous, Plin. To be hardened to blows, Quint. The body grows hard through use, Ovid. To induce hardness against feeling, Plin.

units.la: Callidus] Recoctus homo, Catul. Exquisito judicio, Cic. Emunctae naris. Acutis naribus. Cernit acutum, Hor. Habet sal. Ter. Acetum acre habet in pectore, Plaut. Sesquilysses, Var. Sesculysses, Plin. Rerum humanarum aestimator callentissimus, Bud. Vetulus lupus, de Annibale Lucil.
units.tr: Crafty: A man cooked through, Catul. By exquisite judgment, Cic. Of a clean nose. Sharp-nosed. He perceives what is keen, Hor. He has salt, Ter. He has sharp vinegar in his breast, Plaut. Sesquilysses, Var. Sesculysses, Plin. A most skilled assessor of human affairs, Bud. An old wolf, said of Hannibal, Lucil.

units.la: Calor] Caldor, Var. Calidus vapor, Lucr. Æstuantium dissolutio ac distensio.
units.tr: Heat] Warmth, Var. A hot vapour, Lucr. The melting and swelling of things that seethe.

units.la: Calorem efficiens] Calorificum vinum, Sipont. Concalefactoria, Excalefactoria vis. Calidum fidus, Ovid. Calidarius, Plin. Vaporifera fornax, Stat.
units.tr: Producing heat] Heat-giving wine, Sipont. A power that warms and heats through. A warm star, Ovid. A heating-room attendant, Plin. A steam-giving furnace, Stat.

units.la: Calumnia] Contumelia. Falsum crimen. Criminatio falsa. Maledictum conjectum in alicujus vitam, Cic. Dictum. Non me latet in quem dicta ista jaculeris. Contorsi in eum dictum, quod illi perpetuo doleat, Er.
units.tr: Calumny] Insult. A false charge. A false accusation. A slander aimed at someone's life, Cic. A saying. I am not unaware at whom you aim these words. I have aimed at him a saying that will always pain him, Er.

units.la: Calumniari] Maledicti loco, vel, In maledicto aliquid alicui objicere. Criminari odio factum aliquod, Cic. Crimen in aliquem confingere, Fest. Inquinare famam alicujus, Liv. Insimulare, Fest. insimulare aliquem falsum facinus, Plaut.
units.tr: To calumniate] To use as slander, or to throw something at someone in abuse. To charge someone with a deed out of hatred, Cic. To invent a crime against someone, Fest. To stain someone's reputation, Liv. To accuse, Fest. to accuse someone of a false crime, Plaut.

units.la: Calumniator] Insimulator, Apul. Criminator. Delator, Plin. Quaelibet in quemvis opprobria dicere saevus, Hor.
units.tr: Calumniator] An accuser, Apul. A slanderer. An informer, Plin. One who in a savage spirit hurls abuse at anyone, Hor.

units.la: Calvaria] Cælum capitis, Plin.
units.tr: Crown of the head] The top of the head, Plin.

units.la: Calvescere] Calvere, Plin. Calvefieri, Var.
units.tr: To grow bald] To go bald, Plin. To become bald, Var.

units.la: Calvities] Calvitium, Cic. Lævitas capitis, Sen.
units.tr: Baldness] Baldness, Cic. Smoothness of the head, Sen.

units.la: Calvus] Calvatus, Cato. Calvitio deformis, Suet. Calvaster, Sipont. Calvena, Cic. Deflloccatus senex, Plaut.
units.tr: Bald] Shaved bald, Cato. Disfigured by baldness, Suet. A little bald man, Sipont. Bald-pated, Cic. A balding old man, Plaut.

units.la: Calvus anteriore tantum parte] Præcalvus, Suet. Recalvus, Plaut. Recalvaster, Valla. Relicinia frons, Apul. Calidus fronte equus, Isid. Lunata fronte, Virg.
units.tr: Bald only at the front] Bald in front, Suet. Receding at the brow, Plaut. A little receded, Valla. A forehead bared of hair, Apul. A horse bald on the forehead, Isid. With a crescent-shaped brow, Virg.

units.la: Calx] Ferrumen cæmentorum, Plin. Coctus pulvis, Stat. Cæmentum, SS. Lit.
units.tr: Lime] The iron-scale of mortars, Plin. Baked dust, Stat. Mortar, SS. Lit.

units.la: Calx nondum macerata] Calx viva, Isid. Recens, Vitruv.
units.tr: Unslaked lime] Quicklime, Isid. Fresh lime, Vitruv.

units.la: Calx macerata] Calx tempore macerata & fermentata, Philand. Intrita, Plin. Trima, Id.
units.tr: Slaked lime] Lime steeped and fermented over time, Philand. Steeped, Plin. Thrice-steeped, Id.

units.la: Calx exstincta] Calx aquâ perfusa, Isid.
units.tr: Slaked lime] Lime drenched with water, Isid.

units.la: Cambire] Cambire aliquid cum aliquo, Apul.
units.tr: To exchange] To exchange something with someone, Apul.

units.la: Cambium, vid. Collybus.
units.tr: Cambium, see Collybus.

units.la: Camelus] Dromas, Liv.
units.tr: Camel] A dromedary, Liv.

units.la: Camerare] Concamerare. Fornicare, Plin. Confornicare, Vitruv. Lacunare, Ovid. Caminare, Plin.
units.tr: To vault] To arch over, Plin. To vault, Vitruv. To panel a ceiling, Ovid. To make arches, Plin.

units.la: Caminus] Infumibulum, Sipont. Fumi spiraculum, Id. Nares fornaculæ, Vitr. Spiramentum exhalans flammam, Ovid.
units.tr: Chimney] A flue, Sipont. A vent for smoke, Id. The nostrils of a small furnace, Vitr. A vent breathing out flame, Ovid.

units.la: Campana] Campanum æs, Stat. Æramentum sonorum. Ærea pelvis, Alciat.
units.tr: Bell] Bell-bronze, Stat. A sounding bronze. A bronze basin, Alciat.

units.la: Campanarum agitator] Motor æramenti campani. Æris tinnuli pulsator. Tintinnaculus, Plaut. A campanis, Bud.
units.tr: Bell-ringer] A mover of the bell-bronze. A striker of the ringing bronze. A bell-ringer, Plaut. From the bells, Bud.

units.la: Campanam pulsare] Pulsare tintinnabulum, Iuv. Sonat æs, Mart. Titinnire, & Titinnare, Item. Tintinire, & Tintinnare, Non. Scalig. Pulsare æra tinnula. Percussu æris sonum elicere.
units.tr: To ring a bell] To strike a little bell, Juv. The bronze sounds, Mart. To tinkle, and to tinkle again, Item. To tinkle, Non. Scalig. To strike ringing bronze. To produce a sound by striking bronze.

units.la: Campus] Æquor campi, Virg. Planissimi campi area, Ovid. Immensitates camporum. Immensa camporum spatia, Cic.
units.tr: Plain] The surface of a level plain, Virg. The area of a perfectly flat plain, Ovid. The vastness of plains. The vast spaces of plains, Cic.
