units.la: Cancellare] Cancellos circumdare, Cic. Præfigere cancellos. Clathrare, Col. Objecti clathri caveæ, Hor.
units.tr: To fence with bars] To surround with lattice-work, Cic. To set up a grating. To fence with bars, Col. A cage of barred gratings, Hor.

units.la: Cancellaria] Diplomatica officina. Officina scribendorum & obsignandorum Diplomatum. Indulgentiæ Regiæ promptuarium. Juris æquitatisque promptuarium, Bud. Tabularium, Cic. Archivum. Grammatophylacium. & Chartophylacium, Bud.
units.tr: Chancery] A office for drawing up and sealing charters. A workshop for writing and sealing charters. The storehouse of royal favour. The storehouse of law and equity, Bud. A record-office, Cic. An archive. A place for keeping writings [γραμματοφυλάκιον] and papers [χαρτοφυλάκιον], Bud.

units.la: Cancellarius] A Libellis, Suet. Ab ore Principis, Vrsin. Proximus Libellorum, Amm. Scriniorum princeps, Cognitorum, Causarum ad Principem devolutarum, Crom. Magister memoriæ, Meurf. Scriba Regis, Liv.
units.tr: Chancellor] Secretary of petitions, Suet. From the prince's own mouth, Ursin. Next to the secretary of petitions, Amm. Chief of the registers, of cases, of causes referred to the prince, Crom. Master of records, Meurs. Royal scribe, Liv.

units.la: Cancellarii officium] Annuli cura, Iustinian. Regalis, aut Reip. Diplomatum scribendorum aut obsignandorum munus. Codicillaris magistratus, Lamprid.
units.tr: Office of chancellor] Care of the signet ring, Iustinian. The duty of writing or sealing royal or public documents. A magistracy of codicils, Lamprid.

units.la: Cancellatus] Clathratus, Plin. Cratitius, Vitruv. Fenestratus, Cassiod.
units.tr: Latticed] Barred, Plin. Trellised, Vitruv. Windowed, Cassiod.

units.la: Cancelli] Cancri, Apul. Craticula, Mart. Interseptum ligneum instar retis. Reticula, Paulin.
units.tr: Lattices] Lattice-bars, Apul. A little grating, Mart. A wooden partition like a net. Small nets, Paulin.

units.la: Candela] Noctiluca, Var. Lugubrum, Isid. Ancilla lucernæ, Cicindelæ, Mart. Aliis inserviendo consumor, Hieroglyph.
units.tr: Candle] A night-light, Var. A mourning light, Isid. A servant of the lamp, a wick, Mart. I am consumed in serving others, Hieroglyph.

units.la: Candelabrum] Lychnuchus, Suet. Lychonpodas, Lucil.
units.tr: Candlestick] A lampstand, Suet. A lampstand on feet, Lucil.

units.la: Cadens] Prunitius torris, Ovid.
units.tr: Burning] A glowing brand from the fire, Ovid.

units.la: Candére, candentem esse] Scintillare, Plin.
units.tr: To glow, to be white-hot] To sparkle, Plin.

units.la: Candidatus] Officiosissima candidatorum natio. Candidâ veste indutus. Candidatus consulatûs, Cic. Plin. Petitor, Hor. Competitor, Suet. Honoripeta, Apul.
units.tr: Candidate] A most dutiful breed of candidates. Dressed in a white robe. A candidate for the consulship, Cic. Plin. A seeker, Hor. A rival, Suet. One who seeks honours, Apul.

units.la: Candidè] Sincerè. Ex fide bonâ agere. Aperte atque ingenuè fateri, Cic. Sincerâ fide agere, Liv. Aperto pectore. De summo pectore, Plin. Iun. vid. Sincerè.
units.tr: Candidly] Sincerely. To act in good faith. To confess openly and frankly, Cic. To act with honest faith, Liv. With an open heart. From the bottom of the heart, Plin. Iun. see Sincerè.

units.la: Candidus] Niveus, Virg. Nivalis, Id. Eburneus, Ovid. Candidior nive, Er.
units.tr: White] Snowy, Virg. Snow-like, Id. Ivory-white, Ovid. Whiter than snow, Er.

units.la: Candidus, Transl. vid. Sincerus.
units.tr: White, Transl. see Sincerus.

units.la: Canere, vid. Cantare.
units.tr: To sing, see Cantare.

units.la: Canescere] Canet ætas, Claud. Incanesco, Virg, Tempora mea cygneas imitantur plumas, Ovid. Sparguntur canæ per caput, Id. Canis ætas. Candescit annis, Propert.
units.tr: To grow grey] Age grows grey, Claud. I grow grey, Virg. My temples imitate swans' feathers, Ovid. Grey hairs are scattered over my head, Id. Grey age. He grows white with the years, Propert.

units.la: Cani] Canities, Cic. Canitudo, Plaut. Senium, Pompon. Capitis nives, Hor.
units.tr: Greyness] Greyness, Cic. Greying, Plaut. Old age, Pompon. Snows of the head, Hor.

units.la: Canicula, sidus] Syrius, Virg.
units.tr: Dog-star] Sirius, Virg.

units.la: Caniculares dies] Caprificiales dies, Plin.
units.tr: Dog-days] The days of caprification, Plin.

units.la: Canis] Custos, Plaut. Custos hominis. Excubitor canis. Custos mutus, Id.
units.tr: Dog] A guard, Plaut. A guardian of man. A watchdog. A silent guard, Id.

units.la: Canis venaticus] Canis nare sagaci, Lucan. Sagax, Fest. Odorans ex vestigiis sagacius, Cic. Canis inquisitor, Plin. Odora canum vis, Virg. Ichnobates, vestigia sequens, Ovid.
units.tr: Hunting dog] A dog with a keen nose, Lucan. Keen-scented, Fest. Following the tracks more keenly, Cic. A dog that searches out, Plin. The keen power of a dog's scent, Virg. Ichnobates, following tracks, Ovid.

units.la: Canistrum] Sporta, Vitr. Cophinus, Iuv. Messoria corbis, Prisc. Scirpea, vel Sirpea, Cato. Cista viminea, Plin. Ex vimine texta, Ovid. Fiscina ex viminibus, Varr.
units.tr: Basket] A basket, Vitr. A pannier, Juv. A reaping basket, Prisc. A rush basket, Cato. A wicker basket, Plin. Woven of osiers, Ovid. A basket of wicker, Varr.

units.la: Canon, vid. Regula.
units.tr: Canon, see Regula.

units.la: Canonicus] Amplissimo sacerdotio præditus, Cic. Sacerdos à consiliis Episcoporum.
units.tr: Canon (clergyman)] Endowed with a very high priesthood, Cic. A priest who sits on the councils of bishops.

units.la: Cantare] Percrepat lucus cantu Symphoniæ. Personat vicinitas cantu vocum, Cic. Dare, Edere cantus. Fundere cantus gutture, Id. Canere voce, Tibul, Concanuerunt, Apul.
units.tr: To sing] The grove resounds with the song of harmony. The neighbourhood rings with the singing of voices, Cic. To give forth songs. To pour out songs from the throat, Id. To sing with the voice, Tibul. They sang together, Apul.

units.la: Cantitare, Ter. Incino ore varios modos, Prop. Vernant aviculæ, Ovid. Dant canoros modos, Virg. Modulari, Id.
units.tr: To sing often, Ter. I sing various tunes with my mouth, Prop. Birds sing in spring, Ovid. They give out tuneful melodies, Virg. To modulate, Id.

units.la: Cantitat gallus] Favent faucibus galli noctis silentia, Enn. Cic. Cucurrit gallus, Schol.
units.tr: The cock crows] The cocks' throats break the silence of the night, Enn. Cic. The cock crew, Schol.

units.la: Cantillare, submisse canere] Adsonare, Perf. Succinere, Var. Tu calamos inflare leves, Virg.
units.tr: To sing softly, to sing under the breath] To sing softly in accompaniment, Perf. To sing in response, Var. You blow light reeds, Virg.

units.la: Cantare modulate, vid. Modulari.
units.tr: To sing in measure, see Modulari.

units.la: Cantharis] Impetigo. Parvus scarabæus, Plin.
units.tr: Cantharis] Impetigo. A small beetle, Plin.

units.la: Canus] Canosus, Flav. Incanus, Plaut.
units.tr: Hoary] Greyish, Flav. Grey, Plaut.

units.la: Capax est] Capiet nos domus. Unâ domo capiemur, Cic. Barathro capacior, Enn.
units.tr: It is capable] The house will hold us. We shall be held in one house, Cic. Larger than the pit, Enn.

units.la: Capere] Capere in manum, Plaut. Prehendere, Petron. Comprehendere aliquem, Tacit. Excipere, Cic.
units.tr: To take] To take into the hand, Plaut. To grasp, Petron. To seize someone, Tacit. To receive, Cic.

units.la: Capi] Incidere in casses, Ovid.
units.tr: To be caught] To fall into snares, Ovid.

units.la: Capilli] Coma, Virg. Frontis integumentum, Athen. Crines, Tacit. Capillitium inaffectatum, Apul.
units.tr: Hair] Hair, Virg. A covering of the forehead, Athen. Locks, Tacit. Unaffected hair, Apul.

units.la: Capilli factitii] vid. Caliendrum.
units.tr: False hair, see Caliendrum.

units.la: Capillus alienis ornatus] Calvus comatus. Graculus Æsopicus.
units.tr: Hair adorned with another's hair] A bald man with long locks. Aesop's jackdaw.

units.la: Capilli densi] Silva horrida condi, Juv.
units.tr: Thick hair] A bristling forest hidden, Juv.

units.la: Capilli decidui] Defluvium capitis, Plin. Alopecia, Id.
units.tr: Falling hair] Loss of hair, Plin. Alopecia, Id.

units.la: Capillis trahere aliquem] Comâ arripere aliquem. Capillo pertrahere in viam. Capillo me de curru deripuit, Plin.
units.tr: To drag someone by the hair] To seize someone by the hair. To drag someone into the street by the hair. He dragged me from the chariot by the hair, Plin.

units.la: Capistrum] Fiscella, Cato. Reticulus densus adjectus capiti, Plin. Camus, Plaut.
units.tr: Halter] A basket, Cato. A dense net fitted over the head, Plin. A muzzle, Plaut.

units.la: Capistrare] Præfigere ora ferratis capistris, Virg. Frænare ora capistris, Ovid. Incapistrare, Apul.
units.tr: To halter] To fix muzzles on the mouths with iron muzzles, Virg. To bridle the mouths with muzzles, Ovid. To muzzle, Apul.

units.la: Capitalis causa] Res capitis est. Res capite agitur, Plin. Agitur caput. Causa capitis in jure versatur. In judicium capitis vocatur. De capite suo causam dicere. Capitis certamen cum aliquo agere. Agitur alicujus salus. Causam capitis orare, Cic.
units.tr: Capital case] It is a matter of life. The matter is one of life, Plin. The head is at stake. The case of life lies in law. To be summoned to a trial for life. To plead one's own case for life. To contend with someone in a contest for one's head. The safety of someone is at stake. To plead a case for life, Cic.

units.la: Capitis periculum subire] Capitale id est, Cic. Capital facinus, Fest. Capital feceris, Plaut. Capitali noxa id habetur, Liv. Nunc crinibus capitique capitalem fraudem creas, Plaut.
units.tr: To incur danger to life] That is a capital matter, Cic. A capital crime, Fest. You would make it a capital matter, Plaut. It is held to be a capital offence, Liv. Now you make a capital fraud against hair and head, Plaut.

units.la: Capitatio] Exactio capitum, Epicephalium, Cic. Tribu-tum tum in singula capita imperatum, Caes. Capitalis census, Iustin. Æs capitarium. Tributorum collatio in capita, Fest.
units.tr: Poll-tax] A levy of heads, a head-tax, Cic. A tribute imposed on each head, Caes. A capital assessment, Justin. Money for heads, Fest. A collection of taxes per head, Fest.

units.la: Capitaneus] Præfectus regius. Præfectus urbi, Gell. Præses urbi, Cic.
units.tr: Captain] A royal prefect. The prefect of the city, Gell. The governor of the city, Cic.

units.la: Capitaneatus] Præfectura, Cic. Satrapia, Plin, Præsidatus, Vopisc.
units.tr: Captaincy] A prefecture, Cic. A satrapy, Plin. A presidency, Vopisc.

units.la: Capitatus] Capitulatus surculus, Cels. Magni capitis brassica, Col. Bulbosa, Bulbacea radix, Plin.
units.tr: Headed] A cut shoot, Cels. Cabbage with a large head, Col. A bulbous, bulb-like root, Plin.

units.la: Capitellum] Capitulum, Var. Epistylium, Vitruv.
units.tr: Little head] A little head, Var. The capital of a column, Vitruv.

units.la: Capito] Tuditanus, qui caput magnum, tuditis instar, habet, Fest.
units.tr: Capito] Tuditanus, one who has a large head like a mallet, Fest.

units.la: Capo] Gallus spado, Petron. Gallus castratus, Var. Capus, Id.
units.tr: Capon] A gelded cock, Petron. A castrated cock, Var. A capon, Id.

units.la: Capra] Mater hœdorum, Virg. Barbigeræ pecudes capræ, Lucr.
units.tr: Goat] The mother of kids, Virg. Bearded she-goats, Lucr.

units.la: Caprone] Crines propenduli, Apul. Ante-penduli, Ovid.
units.tr: Fringe of hair] Hanging locks, Apul. Hanging forelocks, Ovid.

units.la: Captare] Appetere manibus aliquid, Cic. Aucupari verba alicujus, Id. Auribus aucupium facere. Captare aliquem loquentem, Id. Consectari umbras falsæ gloriæ. Aucupari famam, Plin. Sequi gratiam Cæsaris, Caes. Colligere gratiam, famam, Er. Prensare aliquos, Cic.
units.tr: To catch at] To reach for something with the hands, Cic. To catch at someone's words, Id. To fish for favour with the ears. To catch someone while he speaks, Id. To pursue the shadows of false glory. To hunt for fame, Plin. To follow Caesar's favour, Caes. To gather favour and fame, Er. To importune some people, Cic.

units.la: Captator] Auceps sermonis. Auceps auribus alienis. Venator cum auritis plagis, Plaut.
units.tr: Catcher] A catcher of talk. A fowler of other people's ears. A hunter with eared snares, Plaut.

units.la: Captio, captiuncula] Aucupium. Tendicula, Cic. Præstigiæ & captiones in oratione. Laqueus verborum, judiciorum, Legum, Id. Decipula fraudis, Apul.
units.tr: Trap, little trap] A fowling, a snare, Cic. A little snare, Cic. Tricks and traps in speech. A noose of words, of judgements, of laws, Id. A bait of deceit, Apul.

units.la: Captiosus] Captiosum genus orationis, Cic. Captatrix, Apul. Captatorius, Paul.IC.
units.tr: Captious] A captious kind of speech, Cic. One who deceives, Apul. Deceptive, Paul IC.

units.la: Captivare] Onerare vinculis. Mandare vinculis, Cic. Capere vinculis aliquem, Virg. Capere bello, Cic. Abducere in servitutem, Caes. Captivum ducere, Claud.
units.tr: To capture] To load with chains. To bind in chains, Cic. To take with chains, Virg. To take in war, Cic. To lead away into slavery, Caes. To lead as a captive, Claud.

units.la: Captivari] Exceptus est, Cic. Capi ab hoste, Ovid. Venit in manus, scil. hostiles, Sal. Potitus est hostium Rex, Plaut. Captus. (Subintellige vi hostium.)
units.tr: To be captured] He was received, Cic. To be taken by the enemy, Ovid. He came into the enemy's hands, Sall. The king of the enemy took possession, Plaut. Taken. (Understand: by the force of the enemy.)

units.la: Captivitas] Comprehensio, Cic.
units.tr: Captivitas: seizure, apprehension, Cic.

units.la: Captivus] Potitus hostium, Plaut. Captivitas, Ephes.4.
units.tr: Captivus: one who has fallen into the enemy's hands, Plaut. Captivity, Ephes.4.

units.la: Captura] Captus piscium, Pompon.IC. Piscatus bonus obveobvenit, Plaut. Aucupium, pro re captâ, Sen. Piscatio, Non.
units.tr: Captura: a catch of fish, Pompon.IC. A good catch of fish turns up, Plaut. Bird-catching, used of the thing caught, Sen. Fishing, Non.

units.la: Captus] Indagine cinctus, Virg.
units.tr: Captus: surrounded by a net, Virg.

units.la: Caput] Synciput, Plaut. Corporis arx.
units.tr: Caput: the front of the head, Plaut. The citadel of the body.

units.la: Carbo] Pruna restincta.
units.tr: Carbo: an extinguished coal.

units.la: Carbunculus] Apyrotus, Plin. Ignis lapideus, Petron. Ignis maris rubri, Claud.
units.tr: Carbunculus: Apyrotus, Plin. Stony fire, Petron. The fire of the Red Sea, Claud.

units.la: Carcer] Custodia. Vincula, Cic. Poenalia claustra, Amm. Ferriterium, quod ferrum ibi teratur, Plaut. Ergastulum. Claustrum poenale, Amm.
units.tr: Carcer: custody. Chains, Cic. Penal confinement, Amm. A place where iron is ground down, because iron is worn away there, Plaut. A workhouse. A penal prison, Amm.

units.la: Carcerarius] Ergastularius, Col. Manceps carceris, Bud. Magister claustrorum, Cassiodor. Praefectus carceris, Bud. Phylacista, Plaut.
units.tr: Carcerarius: a slave kept in a workhouse, Col. Keeper of a prison, Bud. Master of the prisons, Cassiodor. Prefect of the prison, Bud. Jailer, Plaut.

units.la: Carceres] Limen, Virg. Linea, Tertul.
units.tr: Carceres: a threshold, Virg. A starting line, Tertul.

units.la: Cardinalis] Cardinalis Antistes, Sipont. Summum Ecclesiae consilium. Supremus Ecclesiae Senatus. Patres purpurati. Summum orbis Christiani collegium : ita apud Pontificios audiunt. vid. Principalis.
units.tr: Cardinalis: a cardinal bishop, Sipont. The highest council of the Church. The supreme senate of the Church. The purple-robed fathers. The highest college of the Christian world; so the Papists call it. See Principalis.

units.la: Cardojanuae] Tacitis cardinibus, Propert. Quia clausâ januâ tacent.
units.tr: Cardojanuae: with the hinges silent, Propert. Quia clausâ januâ tacent. (because with the door shut they are silent).

units.la: Carduus] Lactuca asinorum.
units.tr: Carduus: donkeys' lettuce.

units.la: Carére] Nihil mihi suppetit, Cic. Non est copia, Plaut. Egeo pudoris, Id. Deficior lacte, Col. Vaco pecuniâ, Liv. Laborare re frumentariâ, Salust. Procul habere, Id.
units.tr: Carére: I have nothing left, Cic. There is no supply, Plaut. I am in want of shame, Id. I lack milk, Col. I am without money, Liv. To suffer a shortage of grain, Salust. To keep far off, Id.

units.la: Carere] Pectere ferreis hamis stupam, Plin.
units.tr: Carere: to comb tow with iron hooks, Plin.

units.la: Caritas, vid. Annonae gravitas.
units.tr: Caritas: see Annonae gravitas.

units.la: Carmen, instrumentum] Ferreus hamus, Plin.
units.tr: Carmen, instrumentum: an iron hook, Plin.

units.la: Carmen] Poëma, Plaut. Poësis, Horat. Pictura tacita, Loquens, Lemon. Vorsa facundia, Apul.
units.tr: Carmen: a poem, Plaut. Poetry, Horat. A silent picture, a speaking one, Lemon. Turned eloquence, Apul.

units.la: Carminare] Plin. Carmine trahere lanam, Lucr. Putare lanam, Scal.
units.tr: Carminare: Plin. To card wool with a comb, Lucr. To pick wool, Scal.

units.la: Carnifex] Tortor. Spiculator, Cic. Exactor supplicii, Liv. Tintinnaculus, (à tinnitu plagarum, quas inferebat reo, vel tintinnabulis, quibus ornabat reum) Plaut.
units.tr: Carnifex: a torturer. An executioner, Cic. One who carries out a punishment, Liv. A tintinnaculus (named from the ringing of the blows he inflicted on the accused, or from the little bells with which he adorned the accused), Plaut.

units.la: Caro] Corpus, Cic. Lutum sanguine maceratum.
units.tr: Caro: the body, Cic. Mud steeped in blood.

units.la: Carpathus mons] Altissima juga montis Carpathi, Iun.
units.tr: Carpathus mons: the highest ridges of Mount Carpathus, Iun.

units.la: Carpentaria] Carpentaria fabrica, Plin.
units.tr: Carpentaria: carpentry work, Plin.

units.la: Carpentarius] Plaustrarius, Lampr. Traharius, Sidon. Rhedarius, & Vehicularius fabricator, Capitol.
units.tr: Carpentarius: a wagon-maker, Lampr. A cart-maker, Sidon. A maker of carriages and wagons, Capitol.

units.la: Carpentum] Lectica, Cic. Pilentum, Virg. Hexaphorum, Mart. Octophorum, Cic.
units.tr: Carpentum: a litter, Cic. A two-wheeled carriage, Virg. A six-bearer, Mart. An eight-bearer, Cic.

units.la: Carpere] (1) Decerpere fructus, Hor. Legere poma ab arbore, Tibul. Deligere ficus, Fest. Lectitare flores, Arnob. Vellere poma manu, Tibul. Stringere glandes, Plin. Cogere oleam, Cato.
units.tr: Carpere: (1) to pluck fruit, Hor. To gather apples from a tree, Tibul. To pick figs, Fest. To pluck flowers, Arnob. To pick fruit by hand, Tibul. To strip acorns, Plin. To press olives, Cato.

units.la: Carpere (2) sugillare] Pervellere. Cerâ miniatâ notare, Cic. Sugillare opinionem alicujus, Vlp. Obtrectare legi, Cic. Obtrectare lautitiam alicujus. Vitilitigare aliquid, Plinio. Vellicare opus alicujus, Var. Notare carbone, Horat. Cavillari artem, Quint.
units.tr: Carpere (2) sugillare: to carp at, to pick apart. To mark with red wax, Cic. To disparage someone's opinion, Vlp. To find fault with a law, Cic. To carp at someone's extravagance. To pick holes in something, Plinio. To nibble at someone's work, Var. To mark with charcoal, Horat. To cavil at an art, Quint.

units.la: Carptim] Vellicatim, Sisen. Digitulis duobus primoribus sumere aliquid, Plaut. Digitis eminulis modicum salis tangere, Prud. Tribus digitis prehendere, Plin.
units.tr: Carptim: piece by piece, Sisen. To take something with two front fingers, Plaut. To touch a little salt with the tips of the fingers, Prud. To take hold with three fingers, Plin.

units.la: Carptor] Improbator, Apul. Momus, Cal. Rhod. Vitupero, Gell. Obstrigillator, Var. Vitilitigator, Plin.
units.tr: Carptor: a disparager, Apul. A scoffer, Cal. Rhod. One who censures, Gell. A rebuker, Var. A carper, Plin.

units.la: Carrum] Birotum vehiculum, Non.
units.tr: Carrum: a two-wheeled vehicle, Non.

units.la: Carus] Multorum nummorum. Durior annonâ. Malè empta domus. Pretiosus. Pretii magni, Cic. Maximo pretio, Id. Impenso coëmptus, Hor. Habet pretium, Plin. Antecedit pretio aliquid, Id. Magno pretio, Stat.Hor. Magnò est, Sen. Multinummus asinus, Varr. Nihil carius pensiusque nobis est, Gell. Carus est auro contrà, Plaut. Poma veneunt contra aurum, Id,
units.tr: Carus: costing many coins. Dear because of scarcity of food. A house badly bought. Precious. Of great price, Cic. At the highest price, Id. Bought at a great outlay, Hor. It has a price, Plin. Something surpasses another in price, Id. At a great price, Stat.Hor. It costs a great deal, Sen. A many-coined ass, Varr. Nothing is dearer or more weighty to us, Gell. Dear as gold, on the contrary, Plaut. Apples sell for their weight in gold, Id.

units.la: Care vendere] Quàm plurimô vendere. Magnô vendere. Plure venit, Cic. Valdè carè æstimare, Id. Grandi pecuniâ mercari, Plaut. Luculentè vendere, Id. Die vendere, Cato. Avarè statuere pretium mercis, Ter.
units.tr: Care vendere: to sell for as much as possible. To sell at a high price. It sells for more, Cic. To value very dearly, Id. To trade for a large sum of money, Plaut. To sell splendidly, Id. To sell by the day, Cato. To fix the price of goods greedily, Ter.

units.la: Carè emere] Sumtuosiùs emere. Immenso mercari quid, Plin. Impenso parare pretio, Caes. Malè emere. Malè conciliatus, Plaut.
units.tr: Carè emere: to buy more expensively. To trade for something at an immense price, Plin. To acquire at a great outlay, Caes. To buy badly. Badly bargained for, Plaut.

units.la: Casa] Gurgustium, Cic. Tugurium. Aggrestum manus. Magalia, Virg. Mapalia, Cato. Taberna pauperum, Hor. De cannâ straminibusque domus, Ovid.
units.tr: Casa: a hut, Cic. A hovel. A band of rustics. Huts, Virg. Mapalia, Cato. The poor man's inn, Hor. A house of reeds and straw, Ovid.

units.la: Caseus] Caseum, Plaut. Meta lectens, & lactis, Mart. Lac pressum, Virg. Lac passum. Lactis coacti massa, Ovid. Caseus manu pressus, Suet.
units.tr: Caseus: cheese, Plaut. A cake of cheese and milk, Mart. Pressed milk, Virg. Dried milk. A mass of curdled milk, Ovid. Cheese pressed by hand, Suet.

units.la: Cassis] Rete, Virg. Plagae, Ovid. Panthera, omnis generis feras capiens, Cerda. Tendicula, Sipont. Viscum, Id.
units.tr: Cassis: a net, Virg. Snares, Ovid. A panther, catching wild beasts of every kind, Cerda. A snare, Sipont. Birdlime, Id.

units.la: Castigare] Arguere aliquem avaritiae. Coercere, Cic. Incessere monitis amaris, Sil. Concastigare, Plaut. Admonere monimentis bubulis, Id. Corripere peccatum, Ovid. Objurgare flagris, ferulis, Suet. Corrigere natum, Ter.
units.tr: Castigare: to charge someone with greed. To restrain, Cic. To assail with bitter warnings, Sil. To chastise thoroughly, Plaut. To admonish with ox-hide whips, Id. To rebuke a sin, Ovid. To scourge with rods and switches, Suet. To correct a son, Ter.

units.la: Castigaberis] Non hoc sic abibit, Ter. Non inultum aufferes, Id.
units.tr: Castigaberis: you will not get away with this, Ter. You will not carry it off unpunished, Id.

units.la: Castitas] Castimonia, Cic. Castusanimus, Id. Castitudo, Non. Castus, ûs, Var. Soror sobrietatis.
units.tr: Castitas: chastity, Cic. A chaste mind, Id. Chastity, Non. Chastity, Var. The sister of sobriety.

units.la: Castitas suspecta] Foris Helena, Intus Hecuba.
units.tr: Castitas suspecta: Helen outside, Hecuba inside.

units.la: Castra] Stativa, Liv. Sepimentum militare, Varr. Munitio. Operibus munitionibusque cingere urbem, Cic. Castra stativa, Id.
units.tr: Castra: standing camps, Liv. A military fence, Varr. A fortification. To surround the city with works and fortifications, Cic. Standing camps, Id.

units.la: Castra metari] Castra alicubi locare, ponere, habere, collocare castra, tabernaculum, Cic. Castra facere, Caes. Carraginem facere, Treb.
units.tr: Castra metari: to pitch a camp somewhere, to set up or place a camp or tent, Cic. To make a camp, Caes. To make a palisade, Treb.

units.la: Castrare] Virilitatem amputare, Plin. Privare parte virilitatis, Fest. Genitalia incidere, Id. Privare sexu, Arnob. vid. Evirare.
units.tr: Castrare: to cut off virility, Plin. To deprive of part of one's virility, Fest. To cut the genitals, Id. To deprive of sex, Arnob. See Evirare.

units.la: Castratio] Eviratio, Sen. Detestatio, Apul. Castratura, Plin.
units.tr: Castratio: emasculation, Sen. Detestation, Apul. Castration, Plin.

units.la: Castratus] Exsectus, Cic. Excastratus caper, Gell. Eviratus, Plaut. Praecisus, Lampr.
units.tr: Castratus: cut off, Cic. A castrated goat, Gell. Emasculated, Plaut. Cut short, Lampr.

units.la: Castrum] Castrum natura munitum, Cic. Burgus, Veget.
units.tr: Castrum: a fortress fortified by nature, Cic. A fort, Veget.

units.la: Castus] Purus. Integer, Cic. Abstinentissimus Veneris. Abstinentissimus rebus Venereis, Col. Perintegrae castitatis, Gell. Lucretiâ, Penelope castior. Vestarum toro purior.
units.tr: Castus: pure. Untouched, Cic. Most abstinent from love. Most abstinent from sexual matters, Col. Of perfect chastity, Gell. Chaster than Lucretia or Penelope. Purer than the bed of the Vestals.

units.la: Casus](1) Prolapsio, Lapsio: Proclivitas ad lapsionem, Cic. Lapsus, Sil. Procidentia, Plin. Petitus terra, Lucr.
units.tr: Casus: (1) a falling down, a slipping. A tendency to slip, Cic. A fall, Sil. A prolapse, Plin. Thrown to the ground, Lucr.

units.la: Casus] (2) Pro fortuna accidentibus frangi. Casus repentinus, Cic. Eventus, Id. Doleo vicem tuam, Id. Communem belli Martem, casumque. Alea, Id. Humanam sortem, Ovid. Fortunâ. Forte cecidit, Ter. Accidentiam naturae morari, Plin. Fortuitus eventus, Id.
units.tr: Casus: (2) to be broken by the accidents of fortune. A sudden chance, Cic. An outcome, Id. I grieve for your plight, Id. The common Mars and chance of war. A game of dice, Id. The human lot, Ovid. By fortune. It fell out by chance, Ter. To delay the accident of nature, Plin. A fortuitous event, Id.

units.la: Casibus omnes subjacemus] Accidere cuiquam potest, quod cuiquam accidit. Fors domina campi.
units.tr: Casibus omnes subjacemus: what has happened to anyone can happen to anyone. Chance is mistress of the field.

units.la: Casus inopinato veniunt] Accidit in puncto, quod non speratur in anno.
units.tr: Casus inopinato veniunt: what is not hoped for in a year happens in a moment.

units.la: Casu aliquo delatus] Fatis adactus. Fatis imputandum.
units.tr: Casu aliquo delatus: driven by the fates. To be imputed to the fates.

units.la: Casus conscientiæ] Doctrina de finibus bonorum & malorum in re Christianâ. Quæstiones de conscientiâ ex lege Christi moderandâ. Controversiæ ad conscientiam pertinentes. Fori interni quæstiones. Ars exsolvens animos nodis religionum, Lucr.
units.tr: Casus conscientiae: the doctrine of the ends of good and evil in Christian matters. Questions about governing the conscience by the law of Christ. Controversies pertaining to conscience. Questions of the inner forum. An art that frees minds from the knots of religions, Lucr.

units.la: Catalogus] Album, Sen. Tacit. Matricula, Iuv.
units.tr: Catalogus: a list, Sen. Tacit. A register, Iuv.

units.la: Cataphractus] vid. Armatus.
units.tr: Cataphractus: see Armatus.

units.la: Catapulta] Pilum, catapultarium, Plaut.
units.tr: Catapulta: a javelin, a catapult-thrower, Plaut.

units.la: Catechesis] Religionis capita, Bud. Imitatio in sacris. Initia sacra. Capita rerum de Deo credendarum. Institutio sacra. Initiamenta. Elementa, Rudimenta Christiana. Schola de religionis Christianæ rudimentis.
units.tr: Catechesis: the heads of religion, Bud. Imitation in sacred things. Sacred beginnings. The main points of what is to be believed about God. Sacred instruction. Initiation. The Christian elements and rudiments. A school for the rudiments of the Christian religion.

units.la: Catechizare] Docere rudimenta religionis. Elementa Christiana tradere. Initiare sacris Christianis. Instituere præceptis Christianis.
units.tr: Catechizare: to teach the rudiments of religion. To hand on the Christian elements. To initiate into the Christian sacred rites. To instruct in Christian precepts.

units.la: Caterva] Turba hominum, Cic. Agmen, grex hominum. Fluctus barbariæ. Unda, Cic. Globus armatorum, Liv. Turba confertissima, Id. Stipati hominum, Plin.
units.tr: Caterva: a crowd of men, Cic. A throng, a flock of men. A surge of barbarians. A wave, Cic. A ball of armed men, Liv. A very dense crowd, Id. Crowded men, Plin.

units.la: Catervatim] Gregatim, Cic. Acervatim se præcipitarunt, Caes. Uno grege, Curt. Globatim. Amm. Effusoriè egressi. Undatim. Agminatim, Id. Conglobatim, Liv. Centuriatim currant, Pompon. Glomeratim excurrit, Mart. Confertim, Liv. Effusè fugere. Effusissimis habenis, Liv. Profusè tundentibus in castra, Virg.
units.tr: Catervatim: in flocks, Cic. They threw themselves down headlong in heaps, Caes. In one flock, Curt. In clusters, Amm. Pouring out in disorder. In waves. In columns, Id. In bands, Liv. They run in centuries, Pompon. He rushes out in clumps, Mart. In close ranks, Liv. To flee in disorder. With reins loosened, Liv. Pouring violently against the camp, Virg.

units.la: Cathedra] Suggestum, Cic. Suggestus, Plin. Ambo, Var. Concio, Liv. Superior locus. Rostra, Cic. Prorostra, Ifid.
units.tr: Cathedra: a platform, Cic. A raised platform, Plin. A pulpit, Var. An assembly, Liv. A higher place. The rostra, Cic. The prorostra, Isid.

units.la: Catholicus] Universalis, Cic. OEcumenicus, Sipont.
units.tr: Catholicus: universal, Cic. Ecumenical, Sipont.

units.la: Cavare aliquid] Cavatur in vasa lapis, Plin. Excavant ripas hirundines, Id. Incavare aliquid cultro, Col. Concavati nidi, Id. Exsculpere foramen in ligno, Cato.
units.tr: Cavare aliquid: stone is hollowed out into vessels, Plin. Swallows hollow out the banks, Id. To hollow something out with a knife, Col. Hollowed nests, Id. To carve a hole in wood, Cato.

units.la: Cauda] Muscarium, Veget. Peniculamentum canterii, Arnob. Penis, (à pendeo) Afran. Gubernaculum. Velamen pudendorum.
units.tr: Cauda: a fly-whisk, Veget. A wiper for a cup, Arnob. The penis (from pendeo), Afran. A rudder. A covering for the private parts.

units.la: Caudex arboris] Codex, stylus, Col. Crus arboris, Id. Ramorum mater, Plin. Truncus, Cic. Stipes, Virg. Unistirpia, pl. Plin.
units.tr: Caudex arboris: a wax tablet, a stylus, Col. The leg of a tree, Id. The mother of branches, Plin. A trunk, Cic. A stump, Virg. A single-stemmed plant, plural, Plin.

units.la: Cave, rem malam] Etiam atque etiam vide quid agas, Cic. Tu videris, Id. Cave malo. Discaveas malo, Plaut. Ne tibi hercle haud longè est os ab infortunio, cave, Id. Disperisti, ni feceris, Id. Adverte sis, Var. Vide sis, Perf. Vide quid agas. Fac sis apud te, Ter.
units.tr: Cave, rem malam: look again and again at what you are doing, Cic. See to it yourself, Id. Beware of evil. Take care, your mouth is not far from misfortune, Plaut. You are ruined if you do not do it, Id. Pay attention, please, Var. See to it, please, Perf. See what you are doing. Please keep it to yourself, Ter.

units.la: Cave ab ignotis] A cane muto, & aquâ silenti cave tibi.
units.tr: Cave ab ignotis: beware of the silent dog and the still water.

units.la: Cavendum est] Præcauto opus est.
units.tr: Cavendum est: caution is needed.

units.la: Cavere] Cavere à veneno. Cavere malum, Cavere omnia, Cic. Subterfugere pericula. Refugere, Id. Cavere sibi ab aliquo, Ter. Discavere malo, Plaut. Fugere, Vitare mala, Er.
units.tr: Cavere: to beware of poison. To beware of evil, to be wary of everything, Cic. To avoid dangers. To flee, Id. To beware of someone, Ter. To be on one's guard against evil, Plaut. To flee and avoid evils, Er.

units.la: Cavere alicui] Cavere hæredi. Tu mihi meisque multa sæpe cavisti, Cic. Damni infecti satisdare, promittere, Id. Excipere aliquid fœdere. Obligare se nexu, Id. Cavere alicui obsidibus, i.e. dando obsides, Cas. Cavere capiti, Plin. Cavere de evictione, Vlp. Excipere in emptionibus aliquid, Var. Autor sum alicui, Plaut. Mancipio aliquid dare, vendere, Plaut. (i. e. periculum evictionis in se recipere.) Præstare cautelam alicui, Paul. IC. Idoneos sponsores dare, Bud.
units.tr: To give security to someone: to be surety for an heir. "You have often given security for me and mine," Cic. To promise and give surety against threatened damage, Id. To except something by treaty. To bind oneself by a bond, Id. To secure someone with hostages, that is, by giving hostages, Caes. To take care of one's life, Plin. To give guarantee against eviction, Ulp. To make an exception in sales, Varr. I stand as guarantor for someone, Plaut. To give or sell something by formal conveyance, Plaut. (that is, to take the risk of eviction upon oneself). To provide security for someone, Paul. IC. To give suitable sureties, Bud.

units.la: Caverna] Specus, Plin. Spelunca, Cic. Antrum, Virg. Desidiabulum, Plaut. Successus terrarum, Arnob. Cavamen rupis, Solin.
units.tr: Caverna: a cave, Plin. A cavern, Cic. A cave, Virg. A lazy-hole, Plaut. A hollow of the earth, Arnob. A hollow in a rock, Solin.

units.la: Cavillari] De plaustro loqui. Conscindere aliquem. Authoritatem senatus in conspectu populi concidere. Differre aliquem maledicendo, Lucil. Allatrare aliquem, Mart. Jocari in capitis alicujus lævitatem, In staturam, Sen. Carpere inimico dente. Responsione inimica me laccessivit, Cic. Frigidam suffundere, Plaut.
units.tr: Cavillari: to talk about a wagon. To tear someone apart. To overthrow the authority of the senate in the sight of the people. To slander someone with abuse, Lucil. To bark at someone, Mart. To joke about someone's baldness, or about his stature, Sen. To nip with a hostile tooth. He provoked me with a hostile reply, Cic. To pour cold water over someone, Plaut.

units.la: Cavillatio] Ludificatio senatûs, Cic. Ludibrium, Ter. Cavillatus, Apul. Dicteria, Var. Mart. Irridiculum. Ludus, Plaut. Dicacitas scurrilis & scenica, Quint. Nasus, Mart. Nasus Atticus, Sen. Cavillem, Fest. Scomma, Macrob. Postica sanna, Perf. Ronchus, Mart.
units.tr: Cavillatio: mockery of the senate, Cic. Derision, Ter. Jeering, Apul. Gibes, Varr., Mart. Ridicule. Play, Plaut. Scurrilous and stage wit, Quint. A sneer, Mart. Attic wit, Sen. A jibe, Fest. A taunt, Macrob. A backward sneer, Pers. A snort of scorn, Mart.

units.la: Cavillator] Dicax. Scurra, Cic. Lusor, Plaut. Ludificator, cator, Id. Deludam lusorem meum. Exagitator Rhetorum, Plato. Cic. Balatro. Suspendens omnia naso, Hor. Verna, Mart. Vernula, Sen. Puer subdolae vernilitatis, Plin. Apinarius, Trebell. Rhinocerotis nasum habet, Mart.
units.tr: Cavillator: a witty mocker. A buffoon, Cic. A joker, Plaut. A mocker, Id. I will make a fool of my joker. A critic of rhetoricians, Plato, Cic. A jester. Sniffing at everything, Hor. A household jester, Mart. A little household jester, Sen. A boy of sly slavish wit, Plin. A buffoon, Trebell. He has a rhinoceros's nose, Mart.

units.la: Caula] Præsepe, Virg. Præsepes, Cat. Præsepia, Sipont. Catablum, clausura animalium, Papia, vel as, Gloss. Anastas. Meurs.
units.tr: Caula: a manger, Virg. Mangers, Cat. Stalls, Sipont. A pen, an enclosure for animals, Gloss. Anastas. Meurs.

units.la: Caulescere] Caulem facere, Col. Erigi in caulem, Pallad. In articulum it seges, Col. Coles agere, coliculum agere, Id. In cymam prosilit brassica, Id.
units.tr: Caulescere: to make a stalk, Col. To rise into a stalk, Pallad. The crop runs into the joint, Col. To put forth cabbage shoots, to put forth little cabbage shoots, Id. The cabbage shoots up into a head, Id.

units.la: Caupo] Tabernarius, Cic. Copa, Virg. Cupa, Cic. Caupona, de muliere, Apul. Priscian.
units.tr: Caupo: a tavern-keeper, Cic. A barmaid, Virg. A tavern, Cic. A female innkeeper, Apul., Prisc.

units.la: Caupona] Taberna meritoria, Sipont. Meritorium, Iuv. Bacchanal, Plaut. Cauponula, Cic. Synoecium, Petron. Copona, Festo. à copiis dicta.
units.tr: Caupona: a tavern let by the night, Sipont. A lodging-house, Juv. A drinking-shop, Plaut. A small inn, Cic. A lodging-house, Petron. An inn, Festus. So called from supplies (copiae).

units.la: Cauponari] Cauponam exercere, Vlp. Cauponariam artem exercere, Iustin.
units.tr: Cauponari: to keep an inn, Ulp. To practise the innkeeper's trade, Justin.

units.la: Causa] Nomen, Cic. Ratio, Ter. Causula, Cæs. Occasio, Plaut. Elogium. Tres gladios Marti addito elogio consecravit, i. e. addita causa, Suet.
units.tr: Causa: a name, Cic. A reason, Ter. A little case, Caes. An opportunity, Plaut. An inscription. He dedicated three swords to Mars with an inscription added, that is, with a reason added, Suet.

units.la: Causa capitis] Causa & contentio de capite. Capitis certamen, lis, causa. Dimicatio capitis. Res capitalis, Cic. Actio criminosa, vel civilis, Bud. Iudicium capitis. Discrimen salutis. Capitale facinus, Cic. Actio criminalis, & judicium criminale, ICtis.
units.tr: Capital case: a case and contest over life. A contest, suit or case for life. A fight for life. A capital matter, Cic. A criminal or civil action, Bud. A trial for life. Peril to life. A capital crime, Cic. A criminal action and a criminal trial, Jurists.

units.la: Causa de homicidio] Judicium caedis, vid. de Cede. De parricidio causa dicitur, Cic.
units.tr: Case concerning homicide: a trial for killing, see under de Cede. The case is pleaded concerning parricide, Cic.

units.la: Causa dissidii] Pomum dissidii. Malum Eridis.
units.tr: Cause of dissension: an apple of discord. The apple of Eris.

units.la: Causa certa & evidens] Omnibus judicibus vincit. Omnium calculis.
units.tr: A clear and evident case: it wins before all judges. By the votes of all.

units.la: Causa facti dissimulata, post deprehensa] Hinc illae lacrymae.
units.tr: A deed concealed, afterwards discovered: hence those tears.

units.la: Causa tua nunc agitur] Ferrum tuum nunc in igni est. Comitia de tuo capite aguntur. De tuo corio luditur.
units.tr: Your case is now being heard: your iron is now in the fire. The assembly is being held about your life. Your hide is being played for.

units.la: Causa injudicata] Indicta causa, Cic.
units.tr: Undecided case: a case not yet judged, Cic.

units.la: Causam amittere] Cadere causa in judicio. Perdere litem, Cic. Cecidisse lite, Fest. Cadere formula, Sen. Excidere formula, Suet.
units.tr: To lose one's case: to fall in a case at law. To lose the lawsuit, Cic. To have lost the suit, Fest. To fall by the formula, Sen. To fall out of the formula, Suet.

units.la: Causam fingere facile] Canem ut cædas facilè invenies fustem.
units.tr: It is easy to invent a case: to beat a dog you will easily find a stick.

units.la: Nihil sine causâ] Absque Vulcano non fit incendium.
units.tr: Nothing without a cause: there is no fire without Vulcan.

units.la: Causa ante effectum] Ignominiam protervia præcedit.
units.tr: Cause before effect: insolence goes before disgrace.

units.la: Qualis causa, talis effectus] Ad semen nata respondenti. Non imbellem feroces progenerant aquilæ columbam, Hor. Mali corvi, malum ovum. Non procul à proprio stipite poma cadunt. Hæc Arabia, hoc thus olet. Inanium inania consilia.
units.tr: As the cause, so the effect: born to answer the seed. Fierce eagles do not beget a timid dove, Hor. Bad crows, bad egg. Apples do not fall far from their own trunk. This is Arabia, this smells of frankincense. Empty plans belong to empty men.

units.la: Causam dicere (1)] Purgare se alicui de aliquo. Respondere de suo officio alicui. Evocare aliquem ad causam dicendam, Cic. Reddere alicui rationem, Plaut.
units.tr: To plead a case (1): to clear oneself to someone of something. To answer to someone for one's duty. To summon someone to answer a charge, Cic. To render account to someone, Plaut.

units.la: Causam dicere (2) i. e. causam agere, vel habere orationem] Agere orationem. Orationem ad populum habere. Habere orationem contra aliquem, Quint. Orationem dicere, recitare. Perorare causam aliquam. Dicere ad judices, apud judices, Cic. Orare causam, Quint.
units.tr: To plead a case (2), that is, to act a case, or to make a speech: to deliver a speech. To make a speech to the people. To make a speech against someone, Quint. To deliver and recite a speech. To plead a cause to the end. To speak to the judges, before the judges, Cic. To plead a case, Quint.

units.la: Causari] Ætatem adferre, Cic. Causam fingere. Causam dicere nescio quam, Ter. Prætexere culpam nomine conjugii, Virg. Obtentus est mihi hoc, Sal. Causam rei gestæ afferre. Afferre impedimenta, Er. Ardea natandi nescia, causatur aquas natatui non esse idoneas.
units.tr: To allege: to bring forward one's age, Cic. To invent a pretext. To plead some pretext or other, Ter. To cover a fault under the name of marriage, Virg. This was my excuse, Sall. To give a reason for the deed. To bring forward hindrances, Erasm. The heron, not knowing how to swim, pleads that the waters are not fit for swimming.

units.la: Causidicus, vid. Advocatus.
units.tr: Causidicus, see Advocatus.

units.la: Caute] Cautiùs. Cautissimè, Cic. Cautim, Ter. Custodìte, Plin. Circumspectè, Quint. Curiosè fodito, ne lædas, Col. Tanquam super spinas incedere.
units.tr: Cautiously: more cautiously. Most cautiously, Cic. Warily, Ter. Keep watch, Plin. Circumspectly, Quint. Dig carefully, so as not to harm, Col. To walk as on thorns.

units.la: Caute agendum semper] Abundare in cautela, non nocet. Præcautô opus est. Viso, cautô opus est, Plaut. Oculatâ die eme, Id.
units.tr: One must always act with caution: to be too cautious does no harm. Precaution is needed. Look, caution is needed, Plaut. Buy by daylight with your eyes open, Id.

units.la: Cautela, vid. Conditio.
units.tr: Cautela, see Conditio.

units.la: Cautio] Circumspectio, Cic. Circumspicientia. Circumspectus, Apul. Observatio, Cic.
units.tr: Caution: circumspection, Cic. Watchfulness. Circumspection, Apul. Observance, Cic.

units.la: Cautus] Percautus, Cic. Consideratus. Præacutus. Præcaveus, animum intentum tanquam arcum habebat, Cic. Circumspectissimus, Suet. Cautores sui, Amm. Catus, Plaut. Album & nigrum novit.
units.tr: Cautious: very cautious, Cic. Considerate. Very shrewd. Very wary; he held his mind taut like a bow, Cic. Most circumspect, Suet. Careful of themselves, Amm. Shrewd, Plaut. He knows white from black.

units.la: Carum] Cayus Leoninus, Plaut. Caula palati, Lucr.
units.tr: Carum: Plautus's Leonine cavity. The cavity of the palate, Lucr.

units.la: Successus, Arnob. Cavius, Varr. Lacuna, Lucr. Cavum terræ, Virg. Cavamen rupis, Solin. Recessus spelunæ, Ovid.
units.tr: A hollow, Arnob. Hollow, Varr. A pit, Lucr. A hollow of the earth, Virg. A hollow in a rock, Solin. A recess of a cave, Ovid.

units.la: Cavus] Lacunosus, Cic. Concavus, Id. Lacunatus torus nuclei, Plin. Loculosus, Id. Conchata cauda pavonis, Id. Alveatus, Cat.
units.tr: Hollow: full of pits, Cic. Concave, Id. A couch of kernels full of hollows, Plin. Full of little pockets, Id. A peacock's tail hollowed like a shell, Id. Trough-shaped, Cat.

units.la: Cecidit, Vid. Evenit.
units.tr: Cecidit, see Evenit.

units.la: Cedens annis] Fugiens vinum, ætatem ferre non potest, Cic. Fugax, Plin. Intolerans, Liv. Intolerantissima laboris corpora. Impatiens hiemis, Plin. Vitrea fama, Horat.
units.tr: Yielding to the years: one who shuns wine cannot bear old age, Cic. Fleeting, Plin. Unable to endure, Liv. Bodies least able to endure toil. Impatient of winter, Plin. A fragile reputation, Hor.

units.la: Cedit bene] Succedit, absol. Cic. Succedit ex sententia. Procedit aliquid bene, prosperè, pulcherrimè, ex sententia. Incipit res melius ire quàm putàram. Prorsus res ibat. Fluunt ad voluntatem nostram res prosperæ. Respondet fortuna optatis meis, Id. Succedit cœptis, Liv. Procedunt consilia, Id. Benè prosperèque hoc operis processit mihi, Plaut. Benè vertit, Ter. Bellè, feliciter cecidit. Inclinat se fortuna ad aliquem. Nunc secundi sunt venti, Cic. Habet res fortunam, Liv. Subscripsit fortuna votis meis, Col. Omnibus feliciter hic locus se dedit, Sen. Provenit benè, Plaut. Vid. Evenit.
units.tr: It goes well: it succeeds, absol. Cic. It succeeds as one wished. Things go well, prosperously, most beautifully, as one wished. Matters are going better than I thought. Matters were going quite well. Prosperous things flow according to our will. Fortune answers my wishes, Id. It succeeds in one's undertakings, Liv. Plans go forward, Id. This work has gone forward well and prosperously for me, Plaut. It turned out well, Ter. It went well and happily. Fortune leans toward someone. Now the winds are favourable, Cic. Fortune favours the matter, Liv. Fortune has smiled on my prayers, Col. This place has come out well for everyone, Sen. It turns out well, Plaut. See Evenit.

units.la: Cedere alicui] Decede peritis, Hor. Da locum melioribus, Plaut. Decedere loco, Tac. Dare transitum, Plin. Iun. Concedere, Cic. Concedere alicui primas partes. Deferre palmam. Fasces submittere, Id. Arenâ cedere. Herbam porrigere. Lampada tradere. Cedere de jure suo. Decedere de jure, Cic.
units.tr: To yield to someone: leave the skilled to decide. Give way to the better, Plaut. To withdraw from a place, Tac. To give passage, Plin. Jun. To grant, Cic. To yield first place to someone. To award the palm. To lower the fasces, Id. To yield in the arena. To hold out the grass. To hand over the torch. To give up one's right. To withdraw from a right, Cic.

units.la: Non cedere] Nemini concedere ne tantillum in aliquâ re, Cic. Negare, Sen. Certare cum aliquo vitiis, Vid. Æmulari.
units.tr: Not to yield: to concede nothing to anyone in any matter, however small, Cic. To refuse, Sen. To contend with someone in vices, see Aemulari.

units.la: Cedere authoritati] Descendere in partes alicujus, Tac. Venire in partes alicujus, Liv. Affigi alicui, tanquam magistro, Cic. Ire in sententiam alicujus manibus pedibusque, Cic. Vid. Assentiri.
units.tr: To yield to authority: to go over to someone's side, Tac. To come over to someone's party, Liv. To attach oneself to someone as to a master, Cic. To go over to someone's opinion with hands and feet, Cic. See Assentiri.

units.la: Cedria] Cedrium, Vitruv. Oleum Cedrinum, Plin. Cedrius liquor, Col.
units.tr: Cedria: cedar resin, Vitruv. Cedar oil, Plin. Cedar liquor, Col.

units.la: Celaté, Vid. Abdite.
units.tr: Secretly, see Abdite.

units.la: Celare] Celare aliquem aliquid, de aliquâ re, Cic. Celare aliquid alicui, Ter. Occultare consilium, Cic. Tegere commissa, Hor. Habere aliquid tacitum, Plaut. Tacitè, Lucr. Continere audita, Ter. Velare aliquid, Plin. Iun. Obscurè ferre aliquid, Cic. Occultè ferre, Ter. Habere aliquid occultum, Sallust. Intra me futurum est, Plin. Tacitum tectumque habere aliquid, Ter. Strangulare aliquid alienum, Petron. Mihi in sinu est, neque ego discingor, i. e. effutio, Cic.
units.tr: To conceal: to conceal something from someone, or about some matter, Cic. To conceal something from someone, Ter. To keep a plan hidden, Cic. To keep secrets, Hor. To keep something quiet, Plaut. Quietly, Lucr. To keep heard things to oneself, Ter. To veil something, Plin. Jun. To bear something obscurely, Cic. To bear something secretly, Ter. To keep something hidden, Sall. It will stay between me and you, Plin. To keep something silent and covered, Ter. To strangle something belonging to another, Petron. It is in my bosom, and I do not unbelt myself, that is, I blurt it out, Cic.

units.la: Celebrare] (1) Celebrare diem religione debitâ, Plin. Agere diem festum, Cic.
units.tr: To celebrate: (1) to celebrate a day with due religious observance, Plin. To keep a feast day, Cic.

units.la: (2) Celebrare alicujus famam, &c.] Prædicare alicujus virtutem. Prædicare de aliquo multa honorificè. Prædicare multis laudibus aliquem. Præconium alicui deferre, tribuere. Ornare gloriolæ insignibus aliquem, Cic. In cœlum evehere aliquem, Juv. Magnificare aliquem, Plin. Hominis alicujus memoriam ad immortalitatem consecrare, Cic. Quos egregium nomen insignes fecit, Sen. Facere alicui nomen, Liv. Nobilem facere, Plin.
units.tr: (2) To celebrate someone's fame, etc.: to proclaim someone's virtue. To speak of someone's deeds in many honourable terms. To praise someone with many commendations. To bestow or award praise on someone. To adorn someone with the marks of a little glory, Cic. To raise someone to heaven, Juv. To magnify someone, Plin. To consecrate the memory of a man to immortality, Cic. Those whom a distinguished name has made famous, Sen. To make a name for someone, Liv. To make someone noble, Plin.

units.la: Celebratio] Prædicatio, Cic. Dispiciunt prædicationem nobilitatemque Philosophi. Prædicatio de laude alicujus, Id.
units.tr: Celebratio] Praise, Cic. Philosophers despise praise and renown, Cic. Praise of someone's merit, Id.

units.la: Celebris] Ad sidera usque notus. Nomen ejus longè atque latè vagatur. Magno theatro spectatus, Cic. Volitat per ora virûm, Id. Magnum habet nomen, Id. Illustri laude celebratur, omniumque sermone. Ad maximam laudem insignis. Decantatur, Inclytus, Id. Per ora hominum magnificè incedit, Sallust. Celebrata in vulgus laus ejus, Tac. Famosus, Id. Est in sermonibus, Sen. Memoratissimus, Gell. Cymbalum mundi. Famâ super æthera notus, Virg.
units.tr: Celebris] Known even to the stars. His name wanders far and wide. Watched in a great theatre, Cic. Flies about on the lips of men, Id. Has a great name, Id. Is celebrated with illustrious praise and on everyone's lips. Distinguished for the highest praise. Sung about; renowned, Id. Walks proudly on the lips of men, Sallust. His praise is spread abroad among the common people, Tac. Famous, Id. Is in people's talk, Sen. Most remembered, Gell. The cymbal of the world. Known beyond the heavens by fame, Virg.

units.la: Celer] Celere telum, Val. Arg. Celeris fœmina, Ovid. Perceler interitus, Cic. Vid. Agilis.
units.tr: Celer] A swift weapon, Val. Arg. A swift woman, Ovid. A very swift death, Cic. See Agilis.

units.la: Celerare] Incitare celeritatem, Cic. Accelerare opus, Stat. Accelerare venire, Amm. Tollere moras, Virg. Admaturare aliquid, Cs. Celeritatem facere, Plaut. Addere celeritati, Celsus. Instare operi, Virg. Omni festinatione properare, Cic. Intendere mobilitatem, Lucr. Vid. Festinare.
units.tr: Celerare] To stir up speed, Cic. To hasten a work, Stat. To hasten coming, Amm. To remove delays, Virg. To hurry something on, Caes. To make haste, Plaut. To add speed, Celsus. To press on with the work, Virg. To hurry with all speed, Cic. To increase nimbleness, Lucr. See Festinare.

units.la: Celeritas] Volubilitas linguæ, mobilitas, velocitas corporis. Impigritas, Cic. Celeri ludo, Var. Pernicitas pedum, Liv. Agilitas navium, Liv. Celeritudo, Caf.
units.tr: Celeritas] Nimbleness of tongue, mobility, swiftness of body. Activity, Cic. A swift game, Varro. Speed of feet, Liv. Agility of ships, Liv. Celerity, Caf.

units.la: Celeriter] Dictum factum, Ter. Citis quadrigis, Apul. Celeriuscule. Velociter, Velocissime. Rapidè. Mobiliter, Cic. Perniciter, Plin. Ocyùs, Ter. Puncto temporis, Lucr. Caduciter ruentes aquæ, Var. Citatim contendit, Hirt. Sub manu, Sen. Pegaseo volatu ferri, Catul. Tollunt se celeres, Virg. Tantâ citatione fertur, ut celeritas ejus quanta sit, ne cogitari possit, Cic. Immissis habenis, Lucr. Citiùs cogitatô. Jovis quadrigis. Apua vidit ignem, (vel Aphia ad ignem) Priùs, quàm asparagi coquantur.
units.tr: Celeriter] Said and done, Ter. With swift chariots, Apul. Rather quickly. Speedily, very speedily. Rapidly. Nimbly, Cic. Swiftly, Plin. Faster, Ter. In a moment of time, Lucr. Waters rushing headlong, Varro. Hurries on, Hirt. At hand, Sen. To be borne on a Pegasean flight, Catul. The swift ones lift themselves up, Virg. It is carried with such speed that its swiftness cannot even be conceived, Cic. With reins loosened, Lucr. Faster than thought. With the chariots of Jupiter. Apua saw the fire (or Aphia to the fire). Before the asparagus is cooked.

units.la: Cella vinaria] Horreum (vinarium) Hor. Taberna vinaria, Iun. Apotheca, Colum.
units.tr: Cella vinaria] A granary (wine store), Hor. A wine tavern, Juv. A storeroom, Colum.

units.la: Celsitas, Vid. Altitudo.
units.tr: Celsitas, See Altitudo.

units.la: Censere] Statuere quanti sit aliquid. Spectare aliquid ex censu, Cic. Pensare, Val. M. Deputare parvi pretii operam alicujus. Censuram facere. Censoriâ virgulâ notare. Cerulâ miniatâ scripta alicujus notare. Notam ponere ad versum, Cic. Recensere, Causab. Censorem agere. Librum alicujus censorio animo examinare. Sumere censoris personam, vel animum, Hor. Censorium stylum, vel censoris styli mucronem exacuere, Cic.
units.tr: Censere] To state how much something is worth. To look at something by its assessment, Cic. To weigh, Val. Max. To reckon the work of someone as of little worth. To hold a censorship. To mark with the censor's rod. To note someone's writings with blue and red ink. To put a mark against a verse, Cic. To revise, Casaubon. To act as censor. To examine someone's book with a censor's mind. To assume the censor's role or spirit, Hor. To sharpen the censorial stylus or the point of the censor's pen, Cic.

units.la: Censor] Judices ac censores poëmatum, Quint. Spectator formarum, Ter. Existimator acerrimus. Existimator alieni artificii. Arbiter, Cic. Ratio, arbitra est bonorum & malorum, Sen. Criticus, Cic. Judex, Id. Canon scriptorum, Cic. i. e. Censor.
units.tr: Censor] Judges and censors of poems, Quint. An observer of forms, Ter. A most keen assessor. An assessor of another's craft. An arbiter, Cic. Reason is the arbiter of good and evil, Sen. A critic, Cic. A judge, Id. The canon of writers, Cic., that is, a censor.

units.la: Censor acutus] Aristarchus, Palæmon scriptorum, Cic. Aristophanis & Cleanthis lucerna.
units.tr: Censor acutus] Aristarchus, the Palaemon of writers, Cic. The lamp of Aristophanes and Cleanthes.

units.la: Censor prudens] Cato sui temporis. Cato rigidus.
units.tr: Censor prudens] The Cato of his time. Cato the stern.

units.la: Censor rigidus] Critici nimis Critici. Criticus antiquus judicaturus sum, Cic. Magister veteris disciplinæ & severitatis. Censorius homo, Id.
units.tr: Censor rigidus] Critics who are too much critics. "I shall judge as an ancient critic," Cic. A master of old discipline and severity. A censorious man, Id.

units.la: Censura] Censorium judicium ac notatio. Censorius stylus. Mucro styli censorii, Cic. Virga censoria, Quint.
units.tr: Censura] Censorial judgment and reproof. A censorial stylus. The point of a censorial stylus, Cic. A censorial rod, Quint.

units.la: Censuram incipere à seipso, vel domesticis] A lare ordiri. (A ritu tu gentilium id ortum est, qui sacrificiorum primitias. Lari domestico offerebant.)
units.tr: Censuram incipere à seipso, vel domesticis] To begin from one's own hearth. (This came from the rite of the Gentiles, who offered the first fruits of their sacrifices to the household Lar.)

units.la: Census] Pensio. Pensiuncula, Col. Pensitatio, Ascon. Censio populi, Val. Max. Æstimatio censûs, Cic. Recensus populi, Suet. Recensio, Cic. Recensitio, Vlp. Censitio, Spart. Professio agrorum, Cic.
units.tr: Census] A tax. A small tax, Col. A payment of tribute, Ascon. A census of the people, Val. Max. An assessment of property, Cic. A review of the people, Suet. A revision, Cic. A census-taking, Ulpian. A registration, Spart. A declaration of lands, Cic.

units.la: Census, qui per focos solvitur] Census colonicus. Colonarium, Cic. Caes. Columnarium. Ostiarium, Caes. Pro agello tributum, Apul. Canon glebæ debitus, Sidon. Capitatio, ICtus.
units.tr: Census, qui per focos solvitur] A tenant's rent. A hearth-tax, Cic., Caes. A column-tax. A door-tax, Caes. A tribute for a little field, Apul. A ground-rent owed on land, Sidon. A poll-tax, jurists.

units.la: Cento] Pannucia vestis, Victor. Pannucium, Id. Peniculamenta, Enn. Mendicula vestis, Plaut. Toga, quæ passa est furias & cornua tauri, Mart. Centunculus, Apul.
units.tr: Cento] A patched garment, Victor. A little patchwork, Id. Ragged clothing, Ennius. A beggar's rag, Plaut. A toga that has suffered the furies and the horns of a bull, Mart. A little patchwork garment, Apul.

units.la: Centenarius] Ager centuriatus, Fest. i. e. 100 civibus assignatus.
units.tr: Centenarius] Land divided into centuries, Fest. that is, assigned to a hundred citizens.

units.la: Centum] Centuria equitum, Cic. Centeni anni, Plin. Seculum, Paul.
units.tr: Centum] A century of horsemen, Cic. Hundred-year periods, Plin. An age, Paul.

units.la: Centuriare] Centuriatim distribuere, Describere, Cic.
units.tr: Centuriare] To distribute by centuries; to describe, Cic.

units.la: Cerdo] Unius cujusdam operis homo, Cic. Vilis opificus. Mango, Plin. Veteramentarius, Suet. Rudiarius, Fest. Interpolator, Sipont. Iun.
units.tr: Cerdo] A man of one particular work, Cic. A cheap craftsman. A botcher, Plin. A dealer in old clothes, Suet. A rough-work craftsman, Fest. An interpolator, Sipont. Iun.

units.la: Cerebrum] Cerebellum. Vitalia capitis, Plin.
units.tr: Cerebrum] A little brain. The vital parts of the head, Plin.

units.la: Cerebrosus, Vid. Pertinax.
units.tr: Cerebrosus, See Pertinax.

units.la: Ceremonia] Mos solemnis sacrorum, Lucr. Solennia ac justa ludorum, Cic. Rites, is, Stat. Ritus, Fest.
units.tr: Ceremonia] The solemn custom of sacred rites, Lucr. The solemn and proper observances of the games, Cic. Rites, Stat. Ritual, Fest.

units.la: Ceremonialis] Ritualis, Fest. Ceremoniosus, Amm.
units.tr: Ceremonialis] Ritual, Fest. Ceremonious, Amm.

units.la: Sine Ceremoniâ] Non ritè. Non servato ritu. Nihil more institutoque. Omissis ceremoniis, Cic.
units.tr: Sine Ceremoniâ] Not properly. Without observing the rite. Nothing according to custom and institution. With the ceremonies omitted, Cic.

units.la: Cerevisia] Potus vini æmulus. Aqua tritico incocta. Potio ex tritico, Vlp. Vinum cereale. Potus è fruge, Plin. Fruges madida. Zythum, Id. Bacchus cerealis. Vinum hordeaceum. Triticeus Bacchus, cicerinus. Lympha cerealis. Humor ex hordeo aut frumento in similitudinem corruptus, Tacit. Pocula vitea fermentô imitantur, Virg.
units.tr: Cerevisia] A rival of wine as a drink. Water boiled with wheat. A drink made from wheat, Ulpian. Grain wine. A drink from the crop, Plin. Moistened grain. Zythum, Plin. Cereal Bacchus. Barley wine. Wheaten Bacchus; chickpea-Bacchus. Cereal water. A liquor made from barley or wheat, fermented to resemble wine, Tac. Cups of grape fermented to imitate wine, Virg.

units.la: Cernere (1) de frumento] Incernere, absol. Vitr. Subcernere cribro farinario, Plin. Excreti à farinâ furfures, Plaut. Decutere farinam, Virg. Decussa farina, Perf. Castrare, Plin. Castrata siligo, Id.
units.tr: Cernere (1) de frumento] To sift grain. To sift absolutely, Vitr. To sift under a flour sieve, Plin. Bran sifted out of flour, Plaut. To shake the flour out, Virg. Sifted flour, Pers. To castrate, Plin. Sifted fine wheat, Id.

units.la: (2) de visu] Cernere acutum, Hor. Acerrimi visûs sum, Plin. Deprehendere aliquid visu, Val. Argon. Terminare oculis campos, Liv. Si tantis intervallis species nostra potest id animadvertere, Vitru.
units.tr: (2) de visu] To discern keenly, Hor. I have the keenest sight, Plin. To make out something by sight, Val. Arg. To mark the plains with the eye, Liv. If our sight can perceive that at such distances, Vitr.

units.la: Certamen] Decursio, Suet. Ludicri concursus, Lipf. Ars ludicra armorum, Cic. Ludicrum certamen, Sen. Militia imaginaria, Suet. Hastici ludi, Suet. Curules dimicationes, Amm. Certamen curule, Lamp.
units.tr: Certamen] A running course, Suet. A meeting in sport, Lipsius. The art of mock arms, Cic. A game contest, Sen. Imaginary warfare, Suet. Javelin games, Suet. Curule combats, Amm. A curule contest, Lamp.

units.la: Certamen imparium] Sus cum Minervâ certamen suscipit.
units.tr: Certamen imparium] A pig takes up a contest with Minerva.

units.la: Certamen classicum, Vid. Classicum certamen.
units.tr: Certamen classicum, See Classicum certamen.

units.la: Certare (1) rei certitudine pignore contendere] Sponsionem facere cum aliquo, Plin. Sponsione contendere, Macrob. Deponere aliquid cum aliquo, Virg. Contendere pignore, Catul. Sacramentô contendere, Cic. i. e. Depositis pignoribus, magnâ sponsione litigare) Sponsione aliquem lacessere, Cic. Sponsionem facere cum aliquo de aliquâ re duobus millibus, Id. Dare pignus cum aliquo. Ponere aliquid pignori. Ni matris filia est, in meum nummum, in tuum talentum pignus da. Opponere pallium, Plaut. Dic quo pignore certes? Virg.
units.tr: Certare (1) rei certitudine pignore contendere] To make a wager with someone, Plin. To contend by a stake, Macrob. To deposit something with someone, Virg. To contend by a pledge, Catul. To contend by oath, Cic. that is, having deposited pledges, to dispute under a great wager. To provoke someone by a wager, Cic. To make a wager with someone about a matter for two thousand, Id. To give a pledge with someone. To stake something as a pledge. If she is not my mother's daughter, put up my coin, your talent, as a pledge. To put down a cloak, Plaut. Tell me what pledge you contend for? Virg.

units.la: (2) Armis vel verbis] Decertare. Per disceptationem contendere. Certare cum aliquo dicacitate, Cic. Certare minaciis, Plaut. Disceptare armis, conditionibus, jure de aliquâ re. Conflictari judicio, Cic. Colluctari. Confligere, Id. Cernere de aliquâ re, Plaut. Leges inter se colliduntur. Quis te cum illo commisit homine? Concertare. Conferre pedem. Conferere manum. Congredi cum, Vitruv. Vid. Disceptare.
units.tr: (2) Armis vel verbis] To fight it out. To contend by debate. To contend with someone in wit, Cic. To contend with threats, Plaut. To dispute about a matter by arms, terms, or law. To contend at law, Cic. To wrestle. To clash, Id. To dispute about a matter, Plaut. The laws clash with one another. Who brought you into conflict with that man? To contest together. To join battle. To join hand to hand. To engage with, Vitr. See Disceptare.

units.la: Certatur de hoc] Id agitur. Hoc pugnatur. In eo cardo vertitur, Cic. In eo res vertitur. In eo spes civitatis vertitur, Liv. Ea res in discrimen adducitur. De hac re certamen est inter illos. Id in certamen adducitur, Cic. Certatur aliquâ re foro, Hor.
units.tr: Certatur de hoc] This is what is at issue. This is what is fought over. On this the hinge turns, Cic. On this the matter turns. On this the hope of the state turns, Liv. That matter is brought into peril. There is a dispute between them about this. It is brought into contention, Cic. The matter is contested in the forum, Hor.

units.la: Certatim currere] Contendere occupare aliquid. Præcurrere, Antevertere alicui. Præripere alicui ne sit primus. Occupare suffragium, Curt. Intercipere fortunam, regnum, &c. Plin. Iun. Antecapere pontem fluminis, Tacit.
units.tr: Certatim currere] To strive to seize something first. To run ahead; to get in front of someone. To snatch something from someone so as not to be first. To seize the vote, Curt. To intercept fortune, a kingdom, and so on, Plin. Iun. To get ahead to the bridge over the river, Tac.

units.la: Certe] Quidem certè, Cic. Et ea certò est, Certè hercle, Ter. Revera, aut re verâ, Cic. Sanè. Sanè, quidem, Cic.Ter. Profectò, Ter. Plane. Planissimè. Verissimè, Næ, Id. Quidem. Equidem doleo, Cic. Enim me nominat, Plaut. Ter. Dii boni! Sen.
units.tr: Certe] Indeed, certainly, Cic. And this is certain; certainly, by Hercules, Ter. In truth, or in very fact, Cic. Surely; indeed, Cic., Ter. Assuredly, Ter. Plainly. Most plainly. Most truly. Yes, Id. Indeed. I grieve indeed, Cic. For he names me, Plaut., Ter. Good gods! Sen.

units.la: Certitudo] Fides promissi, testimoniorum, Cic. Constantia dictorum, Id.
units.tr: Certitudo] The reliability of a promise or of testimony, Cic. The consistency of words, Id.

units.la: Certò] Ad liquidum explorata veritas, Liv. Exploratè. Certò certius, Vlp. Nimirum, pro certè. Planè, Ter.
units.tr: Certò] A truth explored to the clear, Liv. Surely; certainly. Most surely of all, Ulpian. Surely, in place of certainly. Plainly, Ter.

units.la: Certò scire] Tanquam digitos unguesque tenere. Tanquam in speculâ, Tanquam in tabulâ, Tanquam meum nomen noyi.
units.tr: Certò scire] To hold it as one holds one's fingers and nails. As if from a watch-tower; as if on a tablet; as if I knew my own name.

units.la: Certò vincere] Vel Momô judice vincere.
units.tr: Certò vincere] Or to win with Momus as judge.

units.la: Certum est] Certa fides, res, Hor. Certæ fidei res, Plin. Definitum, Constitutum, Deliberatum est. Liquet id inter nos. Controversia non est. Constat inter omnes. Solidum est. Pro explorato est. Pro certo, pro facto habeo. Ex oraculo Apollinis dictum puta. Persuasissimum mihi est. Rectum est. Stat mihi. Stet nobis illud. Stat sententia, Cic. Stabile est. Istud mihi exquisitum est tam satis, quàm nunquam hoc invenies secus, Plaut. Satis acceptum, Id. Fecimus periculum. Extra dubitationis aleam positum est. Extra controversiam est. In animo fixum est. Compertum est mihi. Comperi. Exploratum est mihi. Tua fides mihi satis explorata est, Er.
units.tr: Certum est] A matter of sure faith, Hor. A thing of certain trust, Plin. It is decided, settled, resolved. It is clear between us. There is no controversy. It is agreed by all. It is solid. It is taken as proven. I hold it for certain, as a fact. Take it as if spoken by an oracle of Apollo. I am thoroughly persuaded of it. It is right. It stands with me. Let that stand for us. The opinion stands, Cic. It is firm. I have considered this enough; you will never find it otherwise, Plaut. Well enough accepted, Id. We have made the test. It has been placed beyond the dice of doubt. It is beyond controversy. It is fixed in my mind. It has been ascertained by me. I have found it out. It has been proved to me. Your good faith is sufficiently proved to me, Er.

units.la: Certum, & indubitatum quid] Folium Sibyllæ. Ex tripode dicta.
units.tr: Something certain and indubitable: the leaf of the Sibyl. Said from the tripod.

units.la: Certum, vel certiorem aliquem facere] Significare aliquid alicui, vel de aliquâ re, Cic. Nunciare aliquid alicui. Renunciare alicui de aliquâ re; alicui aliquid. Denunciare alicui aliquid, de aliquâ re, Id. Deferre nuncium, Id. Internunciare, Liv. Perferre consilium alicujus ad alium. Certius alicui aliquid facio, Plaut. Certum alicui facio ubi habitet quis, Id. Facere notum alicui, Plin. Iun. Notificare aliquid alicui, Ovid. Docere aliquem de aliquâ re literis, Cic. Manifestare, Justin. Manifestum facere. Indicare, Cicer.
units.tr: To make someone certain, or better informed: to signify something to someone, or about some matter, Cic. To announce something to someone. To report to someone about some matter, or something to someone. To denounce something to someone, or about some matter, Id. To bring word, Id. To carry news between parties, Liv. To convey one person's plan to another. I make something certain to someone, Plaut. I make known to someone where a man lives, Plaut. To make known to someone, Plin. Iun. To notify something to someone, Ovid. To inform someone of some matter by letter, Cic. To make manifest, Justin. To make plain. To indicate, Cic.

units.la: Certus] Certæ fidei, Plin. Iun. Exploratus, Cic. Locuples testis. Ratus. Fidelis ager, Id. Status fidei cursus, Firm. Stabilis quæstus, Cat. Credulæ rates, (quibus tuò te credas,) Sen. Præsentissimum remedium, Col. Præsentaneum, Plin. Authenticus, Vlp. Paul.IC. Pistrinum scribam in mundo, si id faxem, mihi, Plaut. i. e. certum. Testata dicere, Cic.
units.tr: Certain: of trustworthy faith, Plin. Iun. Explored, Cic. A credible witness. Reckoned. A faithful field, Id. A steady course of faith, Firm. A stable gain, Cat. Trusting boats (on which you may trust yourself), Sen. The most ready remedy, Col. Ready at hand, Plin. Authentic, Ulpian, Paul. IC. "May I be a slave at the mill in the world, if I do this," Plaut.; i.e. certain. To speak as one who has witnessed, Cic.

units.la: Certissimè] Certò certius.
units.tr: Most certainly: more surely than surely.

units.la: Certus alicujus rei] Certus reliquendæ vitæ. Certus mori, Sili.
units.tr: Certain of something: certain to leave life behind. Certain to die, Sil.

units.la: Cervical] Pulvinus, Plin. Culcitra plumea, Cic. (Ab inculcando,) Culcitella, ex Plaut. Lipf. Culcitula, Lucil.
units.tr: Cervical: a pillow, Plin. A feather mattress, Cic. (from inculcating) a little mattress, from Plaut.; Lipsius. A small cushion, Lucil.

units.la: Cervicosus] Duræ cervicis, Er. Vid. Contumax.
units.tr: Stiff-necked: of a hard neck, Er. See Contumax.

units.la: Cervix] Corpus à cervicibus demittere, Cic.
units.tr: Neck: to let the body hang down from the neck, Cic.

units.la: Cerussa] Psimythium, Plin. Melinum, Id. Annulare, vel, Anulare, Id. Fucus splendens, Tibul. Medicamen faciei, Juv. Lomentum, Plin. Sputum tenue, Juv.
units.tr: White lead: a white lead pigment, Plin. A white clay, Id. A ring-shaped pigment, Id. A shining cosmetic, Tibul. A face-paint, Juv. A cosmetic paste, Plin. A thin spittle, Juv.

units.la: Cæspes, & cespes] Cutis terræ, Plin. Fructum terræ herbidum, ex Græc.
units.tr: Turf: the skin of the earth, Plin. A grassy growth of the earth, from the Greek.

units.la: Cespitator, equus] Equus suffosus. Cernicus, Virg.
units.tr: A stumbling horse: a horse with a hollowed hoof. A cernicus, Virg.

units.la: Cessare] Abire inceptò, Liv. Facere intercapedinem scribendi, Cic. Deserere suscieptum officium. Intermittere studia. Interponere moram. Silent leges, Id. Pausare. Pausam facere. Concessare, Plaut. Quiescebant edicere, Gell. Supersedere loqui, Liv. Cessator sum, Er. Vid. Desinere.
units.tr: To cease: to depart from a beginning, Liv. To make a break in writing, Cic. To abandon a duty undertaken. To break off studies. To interpose a delay. The laws fall silent, Id. To pause. To make a pause. To lie idle, Plaut. They were quiet in announcing an edict, Gell. To stop speaking, Liv. I am an idler, Er. See Desinere.

units.la: Cessatio] Intercapedo scribendi. Pausa loquendi. Intermissio ab actione. Interspiratio. Vacatio laboris, Cic. Concessatio. Requies forensium negotiorum, Col. Intervallum. Silentium, Liv. Sine intermissu cantùs, Plin. Interstitio & cessatio juris, Gell.
units.tr: Cessation: a break in writing. A pause in speaking. An interruption from action. A breathing space. A rest from labour, Cic. An idling. A rest from legal business, Col. An interval. Silence, Liv. Singing without a break, Plin. An interruption and suspension of law, Gell.

units.la: Cessator] Tardus. Segnis. Piger, Cic. Lentus gradus, Val.Max. Tardior, quàm corbita in tranquillo mari. Cum pedicis condidicisti hoc grassari gradu. Cochleam tarditate vincit. Tandem si podagrosis esset pedibus, jam rediisse oportuit. Formicinum gradum movet. Testudineus gradus. Pulmoneis qui esset pedibus, prius venisset. Pulmo prius venisset, Plaut. Veternosus senex, Ter. Asino pigrior, Mart. Cete, Vid. Balæna.
units.tr: Idler: slow, sluggish, lazy, Cic. A slow pace, Val. Max. Slower than a merchant ship on a calm sea. You learned to walk that way with fetters on. He beats a snail for slowness. If he had gouty feet, he should have been back long ago. He moves at an ant's pace. A tortoise's step. Had he feet like a lung, he would have come sooner. A lung would have arrived first, Plaut. A drowsy old man, Ter. Lazier than a donkey, Mart. See Whale.

units.la: Ceu, Vid. Tanquam.
units.tr: Ceu: see Tanquam.

units.la: Chalybs] Nucleus, Acies ferri, Plin. Stomoma, Matthiol.
units.tr: Steel: the core, the edge of iron, Plin. A kind of steel, Matthiol.

units.la: Chalybe firmare] Roborare chalybe, Trahere aciem, Plin. Acie ferrum temperare, Id.
units.tr: To strengthen with steel: to fortify with steel, to draw an edge, Plin. To temper iron to an edge, Id.

units.la: Chaos] Confusio temporum. Perturbatio vitæ. Conturbatio, Tempestas popularis. Fluctus concionum. Tenebræ Reip. Offusa animis caligo. Procella. Turbidæ res. Turba, Cic. Vid. Confusio.
units.tr: Chaos: a confusion of times. A disturbance of life. An upheaval, a popular storm. The surging of assemblies. The darkness of the commonwealth. A fog spread over minds. A tempest. Troubled affairs. A crowd, Cic. See Confusio.

units.la: Character] Signum pecori impressum, Virg. Quadrupedia characte signari debent, Col. Stigmata saxorum, Mart.
units.tr: Character: a mark impressed on livestock, Virg. Four-footed beasts ought to be marked with a brand, Col. Marks on rocks, Mart.

units.la: Charitas] Pietas erga propinquos, &c. Patriæque benevolis officium, & diligens cultus, Cic. Affectus, Quint.
units.tr: Charity: duty toward kin and so on; the dutiful and diligent cultivation of goodwill toward one's country, Cic. Affection, Quint.

units.la: Charta] Scheda, Mart. Folium, Iuv.
units.tr: Paper: a sheet, Mart. A leaf, Juv.

units.la: Charta bibula] Transmittens literas, Plin.
units.tr: Blotting paper: letting letters through, Plin.

units.la: Chartaria officina] Locum confecturæ chartarium, Plin.
units.tr: Paper workshop: a place for making paper, Plin.

units.la: Chartopæus] Chartarius, Plin. Chartopola. Chartoprates. Papyropola, Bud.
units.tr: Paper-maker: a paper-maker, Plin. A paper-seller. A paper-dealer. A papyrus-seller, Bud.

units.la: Charus] Hoc nihil charius, nihil antiquius habeo. Suavitatem filii apud me obtinet. Tanta est apud omnes tui charitas. Mellitus. In amore est mihi, Cic. Percharus alicui, Tacit. Oculissimus. Mellillus, Plaut. Oculis charior. Luce magis dilectus, Er. Quo nihil charius propensiusque quisque æstimantur, penduntur accurate. Tota vita, Plato. Pro re cara, vitâ & animâ, Ex Græc. Ambobus oculis charior, Catul. Affectus pro his, qui magno affectu amantur, Suet.
units.tr: Dear: I hold nothing dearer, nothing more important. He keeps the sweetness of his son with me. Such is your affection among all. Honeyed. He is dear to me, Cic. Very dear to someone, Tacit. Dearest to the eyes. Sweet little one, Plaut. Dearer to the eyes. Loved more than light, Er. Those things than which nothing is esteemed and weighed more dearly by each person. Whole life, Plato. For a dear thing, life and soul, from the Greek. Dearer than both eyes, Catul. Affection for those who are loved with great affection, Suet.

units.la: Charybdis] Vorago, Cic. Virg. Gurges profundissimus, Cicer.
units.tr: Charybdis: an abyss, Cic. Virg. A very deep whirlpool, Cic.

units.la: Chasma] Nubium antrum, lucisque privata profunditas. Vastus hiatus, Sen. Cœli recessus, Id. Chasma & hiatus cœli, Plin. Hiatus terræ. Discessus cœli, Cic. Chasmatias, Bud. Labes, Cic.
units.tr: Chasm: a cave of clouds, a depth deprived of light. A vast gaping, Sen. A recess of the sky, Id. A chasm and gaping of the sky, Plin. A gap in the earth. A parting of the sky, Cic. Chasmatias, Bud. A fall, Cic.

units.la: Chasmate perire] Haurire urbes terræ hiatibus, publicum malum est. Hiatus sorbuit aliquid, Plin. Desidere hiatu, Val. In subitam cavernam concidentis soli lapsus. Abduxit urbem, Sen. Dehiscit alicui terra, Virg. Vid. Desidere.
units.tr: To perish in a chasm: for cities to be swallowed up in gaps of the earth is a public calamity. A gap swallowed something, Plin. To sink into a gaping pit, Val. A sinking of the ground into a sudden cavern. He drew the city away, Sen. The earth yawns open for someone, Virg. See Desidere.

units.la: Chasmaticus] Dissipabilis & maximè cedens aër, Cic. Diffusilis æther, Lucr.
units.tr: Chasmatic: air that scatters and yields most readily, Cic. Diffused ether, Lucr.

units.la: Chiliarcha] Chiliarchus, Bud. Tribunus militiæ vel militaris, Cic. Legionarius dux. Præfectus alæ, Suet. Pro magistro equitum agens. Pro magistro equitum militem regens, Amm. Primipilus, Caes. Liv. Primopilus, Manut Centurio primipili, Liv. Præsul militum, Vopisc. Primipilarius, Spart.
units.tr: Chiliarch: a chiliarch, Bud. A military tribune, Cic. A legionary commander. A prefect of a wing, Suet. Acting as master of horse. Commanding soldiers as master of horse, Amm. A chief centurion, Caes., Liv. A first-rank centurion, Manut. A centurion of the first rank, Liv. A commander of soldiers, Vopisc. A chief of the first rank, Spart.

units.la: Chimice] Chimica ars, Card. Alchimia, Firm. Argenti conficiendi scientia, Col. Chrysopœja, Delrio, Spagyria, Paracelf.
units.tr: Chemistry: the chemical art, Card. Alchemy, Firm. The science of making silver, Col. Chrysopoeia, Delrio; spagyria, Paracelsus.

units.la: Chimicus] Chimisticæ facultatis magister, Mattheol. Chimicus, Scal. Chrysopœjus, Delrio.
units.tr: Chemist: a master of the chemical faculty, Matthiol. A chemist, Scal. A gold-maker, Delrio.

units.la: Chirographum] Cautio chirographi. Tabulis obsignatis mecum agis. Per singraphām credere, Cic. Cautio, Absol. Tabulæ chirographi, & Tabulæ, Absol. Ictis ex Plaut. Symbolus, Plaut.
units.tr: Bond: a bond of handwriting. You deal with me by sealed tablets. To entrust by a written bond, Cic. A security, Absol. The tablets of a bond, and tablets, Absol. Struck from Plautus. A token, Plaut.

units.la: Chirurgia] Iatraleptice, Plin. Unguentaria, Dalecamp.
units.tr: Surgery: healing by touch, Plin. Ointment-making, Dalecamp.

units.la: Chirurgus] Vulnerarius, Plin. Iatraliptes, Celf.
units.tr: Surgeon: a wound-healer, Plin. A rubber of wounds, Celsus.

units.la: Choragus] Chorostates. Chorodidascalus. Magister chori, Bud. Præsultor, Cic. Liv. Præsul, Lucil.
units.tr: Chorus-leader: a leader of the chorus. A master of the chorus, Bud. A leader of the dance, Cic., Liv. A leader, Lucil.

units.la: Chorda] Fides, Cic. Nervus, id. Nervia, Var. Filum, Ovid. Nervinus funis, Veget.
units.tr: String: a lyre-string, Cic. A sinew, Id. Sinews, Varro. A thread, Ovid. A sinewy rope, Veget.

units.la: Chorea] Versus, Plaut. Si isthoc me versu viceris, alio provocato. Saltatorius orbis, Cic. Ebrietatis comes, sobrius nemo saltat. Chorus, Virg.
units.tr: Dance: a verse, Plaut. "If you surpass me in this verse, I challenge another." A whirling round of dancers, Cic. The companion of drunkenness: no one dances sober. A chorus, Virg.

units.la: Choreas ducere] Choros exercere, agitare, Virg. Celebrare, Sen. Pedibus plaudere choreas. Indulgere choreis. In numerum ludunt Fauni, feræque, Virg. In numerum procedere, & mollia membra movere, Lucr. Orbes saltatorios vertere, Arnob. Saltare ad modos Tibicinis, Quint. Ad numeros se movere; non molliter se infingendo. Virilem in modum tripudiare, Sen. Saltitare, Macrob. Choros ducere, Hor. Saltare, Cic.
units.tr: To lead dances: to conduct choruses and stir them, Virg. To celebrate, Sen. To clap the feet to dances. To indulge in dances. Fauns and wild beasts play in rhythm, Virg. To step in time and move soft limbs, Lucr. To turn the dancing rings, Arnob. To dance to the flute-player's tunes, Quint. To move to the measure, not softly. To dance in a manly way, Sen. To skip, Macrob. To lead choruses, Hor. To dance, Cic.

units.la: Christianus] Christianis sacris imbutus. Qui Christo nomen dedit.
units.tr: Christian: steeped in Christian rites. One who has given his name to Christ.

units.la: Christianismus] Christiana Respub. Res Christiana.
units.tr: Christianity: a Christian commonwealth. Christian affairs.

units.la: Christus] Unctus, Lucr. Horizo[?] humanitatis & divinitatis. tatis. Gigas geminæ substantiæ. Sequester Dei & hominum.
units.tr: Christ: anointed, Lucr. The horizon of humanity and divinity. A giant of two substances. A mediator between God and men.

units.la: Chronicon] Chronica, Plin. Chronici libri, Gell. Annales, Cic. Annales, Cic. Annalium monumenta, Id.
units.tr: Chronicle: chronicles, Plin. Chronicle books, Gell. Annals, Cic. Annals, Cic. Records of annals, Id.

units.la: Chronographia] Descriptio temporum, Cic.
units.tr: Chronography: a description of times, Cic.
