units.la: Chronographus] Annalium scriptor, Cic. Chronologus.
units.tr: Chronographer: a writer of annals, Cic. A chronologer.

units.la: Cibalis] Cibarius, Macrob. Escarius, Plin.
units.tr: Of food: of food, Macrob. Relating to food, Plin.

units.la: Cibare] Pascere, Virg. Nutricari, Cic. De manu dare pabulum, i.e. domi pascere, Col. Dapinare cibum alicui, Plaut.
units.tr: To feed: to pasture, Virg. To be nourished, Cic. To give fodder by hand, that is, to feed at home, Col. To provide food to someone, Plaut.

units.la: Cibaria res] Edulium, Varr. Cibarium, Sen. Cibaria, orum, Annona macelli, Cic. Esculentum, Plin. Conviviatus & cibatus. Obsonatus, Plaut. Copiæ, Val. Facultas. Lamprid.
units.tr: Foodstuffs: food, Varro. Food, Sen. Market provisions, Cic. Edibles, Plin. Feasting and eating. Purchased provisions, Plaut. Supplies, Val. Means, Lamprid.

units.la: Cibus] Cibatus hominis. Focula, Plaut. Esca, Cic. Pastus, Plin. Copiæ, Apul. Nutritia, orum, Arnob. Res cibi, pro cibo, Bud.
units.tr: Food: a person's food. Victuals, Plaut. Bait, Cic. Pasture, Plin. Supplies, Apul. Nourishments, Arnob. Things of food, for food, Bud.

units.la: Cibus sapidus] In mensarum honore est.
units.tr: Savoury food: it is held in honour at tables.

units.la: Cibus tenuis] Jejunium olet, Adag.
units.tr: Plain fare: lean fare smells of fasting, Adag.

units.la: Cibus diurnus, vid. Alimonia.
units.tr: Cibus diurnus, see Alimonia.

units.la: Cicatricare] Senescunt vulnera, Col. Obducere cicatricem, Cic. Coit cicatrix, Celf. Ducere cicatricem, Liv. Solidare nervos abscissos, Plin. Inducere citatricem vulneri, Celf. Contrahit vulnerum cicatrices aliquid, Plin.
units.tr: Cicatricare: Wounds grow old (Col.). To draw over a scar (Cic.). The scar forms (Celf.). To produce a scar (Liv.). To strengthen severed sinews (Plin.). To induce a scar on a wound (Celf.). Something draws together the scars of wounds (Plin.).

units.la: Cicatrix] Vestigium plagæ, Cic. Obducta cicatrix, Id. Cicatricula, Celf. Cæcum vulnus habes.
units.tr: Cicatrix: A mark left by a blow (Cic.). A covered-over scar (Id.). A little scar (Celf.). You have a hidden wound.

units.la: Ciconia] Concordia, Iuv. Quæque salutato crepitat concordia nido, Ovid. Ipsa sibi plaudat crepitante ciconia rostro. Crotaliistria. Avis hospita, peregrina. Pietatis cultrix. Exul hiemis. Titulus tepidi temporis, Petron.
units.tr: Ciconia: Harmony (Iuv.). And the harmony that rattles in the nest it greets (Ovid). The stork itself applauds itself with its rattling beak. A clatterer. A guest bird, a foreign bird. A cultivator of dutifulness. An exile from winter. A sign of mild weather (Petron.).

units.la: Cicur] Mansuetus, Cic. Mansuefactus, Plin. Mitigatâ feritate bestia. Mitigatum ferum pecus, Col. Manum patiens, Virg. Mansues ursa, Apul.
units.tr: Cicur: Tame (Cic.). Tamed (Plin.). A beast with its ferocity softened. A tamed wild flock (Col.). Patient of the hand (Virg.). A tame bear (Apul.).

units.la: Cicurare] Traducere ex feritate ad mansuetudinem, Cic. Lenire leones, Hor. Mansuefacere, Var. Cicurem reddere, Mart. Pacare feras, Claud. Efferatam mitigare saevitiem, Val. Max. vid. Mansuefacere.
units.tr: Cicurare: To lead from wildness to tameness (Cic.). To soothe lions (Hor.). To tame (Var.). To make tame (Mart.). To pacify wild beasts (Claud.). To soften a savage cruelty that has grown wild (Val. Max.). See Mansuefacere.

units.la: Cicuratio] Tractatio pelluarum, Cic.
units.tr: Cicuratio: The handling of hides (Cic.).

units.la: Ciere] Agitare aliquid motibus, Cic. Conciere æstum, Lucr. Solicitare aliquid de suis sedibus, Id. Vegete aliquid motibus, Var.
units.tr: Ciere: To stir something with motions (Cic.). To stir up heat (Lucr.). To drive something from its seat (Id.). To rouse something into motion (Var.).

units.la: Cilicium] Vela cilicia. Cilicina vestis, Plin. Trichoria, pl. Cæl. Rhod. Vestis ex pilis confecta, Hen. Steph.
units.tr: Cilician cloth: Cilician sail-cloths. Cilician garment, Plin. Triple-woven hair cloth, pl. Cael. Rhod. A garment made of woven goat's hair, Hen. Steph.

units.la: Cilo, vid. Fronto.
units.tr: Cilo: see Fronto.

units.la: Cincinnatus, vid. Calamistratus.
units.tr: Cincinnatus: see Calamistratus.

units.la: Cincinnus] Cirrus, Var. Intorti capilli, Mart. Contortus crinis, Sen. Annuli comarum, Mart.
units.tr: Cincinnus (curl): A ringlet, Var. Twisted locks, Mart. A twisted tress, Sen. Curls of hair, Mart.

units.la: Cinefacere] In cinerem redigere, Lucr. In cinerem cremata purgamenta. Ad cinerem ambustus, Plin.
units.tr: To reduce to ashes: To turn into ash, Lucr. Rubbish burnt to ash. Scorched to ashes, Plin.

units.la: Cinereus] Cineraceus, Plin, Marinus color, Col. Leucopseus, Plin.
units.tr: Ash-coloured: Ash-like, Plin. Sea-coloured, Col. Grey-white, Plin.

units.la: Cingere] Præcingere, Horat. Succingere. Incingere, Ovid. Cingere copiis, vid. Obsidere.
units.tr: To gird: To gird round, Hor. To gird up. To gird on, Ovid. To surround with troops: see Besiege.

units.la: Cingula] Zonâ cinge uterum equi, Claud. Incingulum, Non.
units.tr: Girth: Gird the belly of the horse, Claud. A girth, Non.

units.la: Cingulum] Zona, Mart. Cestus, Var. Cinctus, Plin. Semicinctum (Zona semilata) Petron.
units.tr: Girdle: A belt, Mart. A girdle, Var. A band, Plin. A half-girdle (a half-width belt), Petron.

units.la: Cingulum bullatum] Balteus, Virg. Baltea, pl. Liv. Balteolus. Succingulum, Iul. Cap. Cingulum è corio bullatum, Var.
units.tr: Studded belt: A baldric, Virg. Baldrics, pl. Liv. A small baldric. A sash, Iul. Cap. A leather belt studded with bosses, Var.

units.la: Ciniflo] Concinnator capillorum, Col. Cinerarius, Val.
units.tr: Hairdresser: One who arranges hair, Col. A keeper of ashes, Val.

units.la: Cinis] Lix, cis, (cinis foci) Sipont. Combustæ rei incombustibiles reliquiæ.
units.tr: Ashes: Lye, the ash of a hearth, Sipont. The incombustible remains of a burnt thing.

units.la: Cippus (1) Lapis, cui appendebantur insignia demortuorum] Mensa super tumulum. Summum sepulchri, Collumellæ, Cic. Lapis memoriæ Othonis inscriptus, Suet.
units.tr: Cippus (1), a stone on which the insignia of the dead were hung: A table above a tomb. The top of a tomb or column, Cic. A stone inscribed in memory of Otho, Suet.

units.la: (2) carceris genus] Numella, Vinculum ligneum, caput & pedes stringens, Non. Area robusta, Fest. Codex robustus, Plaut. Soleæ ligneæ, Cic.
units.tr: (2), a kind of prison: A wooden bond binding head and feet, Non. A sturdy enclosure, Fest. A sturdy wooden stock, Plaut. Wooden shoes (stocks), Cic.

units.la: Circa] Circum tribus. Ob os. Cis Euphratem ad Castoris. (idem) Cic.
units.tr: Around, about: Around the three. In front of. On this side of the Euphrates, at the temple of Castor, Cic.

units.la: Circiter] Circiter tertiam vigiliam, Apul. Citra diem, Suet. Plus minus triginta, Mart. Quasi ad quindecim, Ter. Instar quinque, Col. Aliquos viginti dies, i. e. circiter. Triduum non interest, Plaut. Circa vicies sestercium, Suet. Ad quindecim homines, Cic. Præterpropter, Gell. Facilè decem.
units.tr: About, approximately: About the third watch, Apul. Less than a day, Suet. More or less thirty, Mart. As if about fifteen, Ter. Roughly five, Col. About twenty days, that is, about. Three days make no difference, Plaut. Some twenty thousand sesterces, Suet. About fifteen men, Cic. Just about, Gell. Easily ten.

units.la: Circuire] Lustrare, Virg. Obire provincias. Peragrare, Id. Obambulare urbem, Plaut. Circuitu ad aliquid pervenire, Quint.
units.tr: To go round: To survey, Virg. To travel through the provinces. To wander over, Virg. To stroll round the city, Plaut. To reach something by a roundabout route, Quint.

units.la: Circuitio] Circuitio viarum, Apul. Ambages, Virg. Mæander, Col. Gyrus milvii in aëre, Ovid. vid. Ambitio.
units.tr: Circuit: A winding of roads, Apul. Windings, Virg. A meander, Col. The circling of a kite in the air, Ovid. See Ambition.

units.la: Circulatio] Claudere, cingere indagine, Plin.Iun. vid. Circumactio.
units.tr: Circulation: To enclose or surround with a net, Plin. Iun. See Circumaction.

units.la: Circulatim] In orbem, Liv. Orbiculatim, Macrob. Rotare aliquem more fundæ. In gyros ire coactus equus, Ovid. In turbinem versari, Sen. Vertigine ambulat, Iuv. Zonatim, Lucil.
units.tr: In a circle: In a ring, Liv. In little rounds, Macrob. To whirl someone like a sling. A horse forced to go round in circles, Ovid. To spin like a whirlwind, Sen. He walks in a dizzy whirl, Juv. Girdle-wise, Lucil.

units.la: Circulator] Circumforaneus homo, Gell. Suet. Ostentarius, Macrob. Nugivendus, Plaut. vid. Impostor.
units.tr: Mountebank: A fellow who performs in the open street, Gell., Suet. A showman, Macrob. A trifle-seller, Plaut. See Impostor.

units.la: Circulus] Sphæra, Cic. Rota solis, Vitruv. Orbis, Cic.
units.tr: Circle: A sphere, Cic. The sun's disc, Vitruv. An orb, Cic.

units.la: Circumcirca] Circumsecus, Apul. Omnia circa defecerunt, Liv.
units.tr: All around: On all sides, Apul. All the things round about failed, Liv.

units.la: Circumactio] Conversio annorum, mensium, Cic. Circumactus rotarum. Circulatio. Versatio rotæ, Vitr. Versura foliorum, Var. Vertigo rotarum, Plin. Conversus, Macr. Rotatio, Diom. Vid. Revolutio.
units.tr: Revolution: The turning round of years and months, Cic. The revolving of wheels. Circulation. The turning of a wheel, Vitr. The turning over of leaves, Var. The whirling of wheels, Plin. A turning round, Macr. Rotation, Diom. See Revolution.

units.la: Circumagere] Æther stellas contorquet. Torsit in orbem Deus mundum, Cic. Versare in orbem, Id. Rotare aliquid more fundæ, Ovid. Volvere orbem, Liv. Celeri volumine torquere, Ovid.
units.tr: To turn round: The sky whirls the stars. God set the world turning in a circle, Cic. To turn round and round, Id. To whirl round like a sling, Ovid. To roll the sphere round, Liv. To twist with a swift coil, Ovid.

units.la: Circumcidere] Circum-secare, Col. Resecare, Ponere ungues, Horat.
units.tr: To circumcise: To cut round, Col. To cut away, to pare the nails, Hor.

units.la: Circumcisio] Circumcisura membrorum. Circumcæsura, Lucr.
units.tr: Circumcision: A paring away of the members. A cutting round, Lucr.

units.la: Circumcisus] Circumsectus, Suet. Apella, Hor. Curtus Judæus, Id. Recutitus, Mart.
units.tr: Circumcised: Cut round, Suet. Apella, Hor. A clipped Jew, Hor. Recut, Mart.

units.la: Circumcurrere] Circumcursare, Ter. Hâc, illac circumcursa.
units.tr: To run around: To run about, Ter. Here and there, running round.

units.la: Circumdare] Circumdare aliquid, & alicui aliquid. Claudere, ex omni aditu clausus. Intercludere fugam, aditum, viam. Circumcludere, Cic. Includere aliquem septis, Ovid.
units.tr: To surround: To put something round, and to put something on someone. To shut in, closed off on every side. To cut off flight, access, and way. To enclose, Cic. To shut someone in with fences, Ovid.

units.la: Circumire, circumvenire, circumsedere, circumretire, Cic. Circumfusus consul multitudine, & multitudo consuli, circumvadere, circumsepire, circumjacere, vel circumjicere vallos. Succingere, septus ab armis, Liv. Septus nebulâ, Virg. Obsident pericula, Sen. Percingere, Col. Circumcingere, Sil. Redimire Ovid. Ambire Id. Vallare armis, Val. M. Circumvallare, Ter. Circumfluere, Var. Circumgredi, Tac. Circumplecti, Gell. Obretire, Lucr.
units.tr: To go round, to surround, to besiege, to entangle in a net, Cic. A consul surrounded by a crowd, and a crowd round a consul. To attack on all sides, to fence round, to lie around, or to throw up ramparts about. To hem in, shut in by arms, Liv. Enclosed by cloud, Virg. Dangers beset, Sen. To hem in completely, Col. To encircle, Sil. To crown, Ovid. To go round, Id. To fortify with arms, Val. Max. To wall round, Ter. To flow round, Var. To go round, Tac. To embrace, Gell. To enclose, Lucr.

units.la: Circumducere, stolidum] Naribus trahere. Ductare aliquem dolis, Frustra habere, Plaut. vid. Contemnere.
units.tr: To lead round, a fool: To lead by the nose. To lead someone on by tricks, to make a fool of him, Plaut. See Despise.

units.la: Circumfodere] Circumdare fossulas arbori. Ablaqueare vineam, vites, Col. Excodicare vites, Isid. Præducere fossas, Tacit.
units.tr: To dig round: To put little trenches round a tree. To loosen the soil round the vines, Col. To dig out vines, Isid. To run ditches in front, Tac.

units.la: Circumfundere] Obspare alicui aquulam Offundere aquulam alicui, Plaut. Circumluere, Liv. Cingere amne, Virg.
units.tr: To pour round: To pour a little water over someone, Plaut. To flow round, Liv. To surround with a river, Virg.

units.la: Circumgelatus] Obductus gelu. Vestitus gelu, Claud. vid. Gelatus
units.tr: Frozen round: Covered with frost. Clothed in ice, Claud. See Frozen.

units.la: Circumlinire] Oblinire, Col. Lutare. Delutare habitationem, Cato. Prælinire, Gell. Illinire crates parietum luto, Plin. Gypsare, Petron.
units.tr: To smear round: To smear over, Col. To plaster. To plaster a dwelling with mud, Cato. To smear beforehand, Gell. To daub the wattle of walls with mud, Plin. To plaster with gypsum, Petron.

units.la: Circumloqui] Circuitione uti, Ter. Pluribus verbis explicare, quod paucioribus dici potest, Quint.
units.tr: To speak round about: To use a roundabout way of speaking, Ter. To explain in many words what could be said in few, Quint.

units.la: Circumlocutio] Periphrasis. Circuitus loquendi, Quint.
units.tr: Circumlocution: Periphrasis. A roundabout way of speaking, Quint.

units.la: Circumluere] Cingit urbem fluvius, Caes. Cingitur amni urbs, Virg.
units.tr: To flow round: A river surrounds the city, Caes. The city is girt by a river, Virg.

units.la: Circummunire se] Induere se vallis, Caes. vid. Vallare
units.tr: To fortify oneself: To throw up trenches, Caes. See To fortify.

units.la: Circumponere] Circumaggerare, Plin. Opimare mensam agrestibus, Vopisc. Aggerare, Plaut. Suffarcinare, Apul.
units.tr: To heap round: To pile up an embankment round, Plin. To stuff a table with country folk, Vopisc. To heap up, Plaut. To cram, Apul.

units.la: Circumsepire, vid. Sepire,
units.tr: To fence round: See To fence.

units.la: Circumspectè, vid. Cautè.
units.tr: Circumspectly: See Cautiously.

units.la: Circumspectus] Capreà oculatior. Oculatissimus. Oculatus ad omnia. Oculatus à fronte simul & occipitio. Oculatior Argo. Dormiens vigilat, Er.
units.tr: Circumspect: Keener-eyed than a roe. Most watchful. Watchful in everything. Watchful from front and back. Sharper-eyed than Argus. Sleeping, he keeps watch, Erasm.

units.la: Circumspectè agendum] Gubernatorem prudentem nox terret.
units.tr: Circumspection must be used: A night frightens a prudent pilot.

units.la: Circumspicere] Circumferre oculos, Liv. Circumaspicere, Plin. Ad omnem strepitum circumagenda cervix, Sen. Retrospicere. Retorquere oculos. Referre aspectum in curiam, Cic. Reflectere visum, Valer.
units.tr: To look round: To carry the eyes round, Liv. To look about, Plin. At every noise the neck must be turned round, Sen. To look back. To turn the eyes back. To direct the gaze to the senate-house, Cic. To turn the sight back, Val.

units.la: Circumstare] Circumsistere aliquem, Caes. Ingenti turbâ circumdatus, Prop. Circumfudere Dianam Nymphæ. Turba latus cingit, Ovid. Rarâ muros cinxêre coronâ, Virg. Stipare, Cic. Circumstipare, Claud.
units.tr: To stand round: To crowd round someone, Caes. Surrounded by a great crowd, Prop. The nymphs thronged round Diana. A crowd encircles his side, Ovid. They girt the walls with a thin crown, Virg. To press round, Cic. To crowd round, Claud.

units.la: Circumfuere] Obfuere, Ovid. Præfuere, Plin.
units.tr: To be round, to be against: To stand in the way, Ovid. To preside over, Plin.

units.la: Circumtegere] Obtegere, Cic. Circumvestitur arbor, Plin. Convestiuntur herbis prata, Cic.
units.tr: To cover round: To cover over, Cic. The tree is clothed round, Plin. The meadows are covered with grass, Cic.

units.la: Circumtexere] Obtexere, Plin. Sirpo dolia quassa, Varr. i. e. Colliga.
units.tr: To weave round: To weave over, Plin. To bind broken jars with rush-work, Varro, that is, to bind together.

units.la: Circumvolvere] Circumplicare, Cic. Coronæ in modum circumdare, Col.
units.tr: To wrap round: To fold round, Cic. To set round in the manner of a crown, Col.

units.la: Circus] Orbis. Ambitus rotundus. Planities rotunda, Cic. Circumferentia, Apul. Corona, Virg. Circumflexus ambiens, Plin. Linea circumcurrens, Quint.
units.tr: Circle: A ring. A round compass. A round plain, Cic. A circumference, Apul. A garland, Virg. A curve encircling, Plin. A line running round, Quint.

units.la: Citare aliquem] Vocare in jus, judicium. Accersere aliquem capitis. Arcessere judicio, in judicium. Persequi aliquem judicio. Postulare de repetundis. Dare, & dicere diem alicui, Cic. Rapere in jus, Plaut. Convenire aliquem, Vlp. Convenire in jus, Plaut. Postulare repetundarum, Suet.
units.tr: To summon someone: To call to law, to a trial. To summon someone on a capital charge. To summon for judgment. To prosecute someone at law. To demand repayment of extortion. To give and name a day to someone, Cic. To drag into court, Plaut. To bring before a court, Ulp. To summon to court, Plaut. To sue for extortion, Suet.

units.la: Citatio] Vocatio in jus, judicium, Gell. Bud.
units.tr: Summons: A calling to law or trial, Gell., Budé.

units.la: Cithara] Chelys, Sen. Testudo, Cic. Hor. Cava testudo, Virg. Fides, Fest. Barbitus, Hor. Barbitos, Ovid. Barbiton, Ausson. Cinyra, Lorin.
units.tr: Lyre: A harp, Sen. A tortoise-shell lyre, Cic., Hor. A hollow tortoise, Virg. Lyre-strings, Fest. A barbitos, Hor. A barbitos, Ovid. A barbiton, Ausonius. A cinyra, Lorin.

units.la: Citharœdus] Citharista, Cic. Chorocitharista. Psallocitharista, Suet. Citharistria, Ter.
units.tr: Lyre-player: A lyre-player, Cic. A player on lyre and chorus. A singer and lyre-player, Suet. A female lyre-player, Ter.

units.la: Citò] Citis quadrigis. Jovis quadrigis. Citiùs cogitari. Citiùs, quàm asparagi coquantur. Dicto citiùs, Liv. Ventis remisque, Cic. Dictum factum, Ter. Quàm ocyssimè, Id. Quadrigis albis. Quàm primùm. vid. Celeriter.
units.tr: Quickly: With swift chariots. With Jupiter's chariots. Quicker than thought. Quicker than asparagus can be cooked. Quicker than the word, Liv. With wind and oars, Cic. No sooner said than done, Ter. As quickly as possible, Id. With white chariots. As soon as possible. See Speedily.

units.la: Cito efficere] Manus Briarei injicere.
units.tr: To accomplish quickly: To lay on the hands of Briareus.

units.la: Citra] Absque me, te, illo, &c. Sine rivali. Expers consilii, Cic. Otiosus à metu. Seorsum animâ nec aures, nec pedes esse potest. Seorsum corpore toto nequit ullam rem despicere oculus, Lucr. Orbis pedum, Id. Defectus aliquâ re, Plin. Viduata loca pruinis, Virg. Viduus pharetrâ, Horat.
units.tr: Without, on this side of: Without me, you, him, and so on. Without a rival. Lacking counsel, Cic. Free from fear. A soul cannot exist apart from the body, nor ears nor feet. The eye cannot perceive anything apart from the whole body, Lucr. Bereft of feet, Id. Lacking something, Plin. Places widowed by frost, Virg. Bereft of the quiver, Hor.

units.la: Citra delictum] Clausis oculis aliquid agere, Ter.
units.tr: Without fault: To do something with eyes closed, Ter.

units.la: Citra laborem nihil fit] Lutum nisi tundatur, non fit testa, Absque labore gravi non possunt multa parari. Qui vitat molam, vitat & farinam.
units.tr: Nothing is made without labour: Unless clay is pounded, no pot is made. Many things cannot be got without hard labour. Whoever avoids the mill avoids the flour too.

units.la: Cives] Corpus Civitatis, Liv.
units.tr: Citizens: The body of the state, Liv.

units.la: Civilis, Vid. Moratus.
units.tr: Civil: See Mannerly.

units.la: Civilitas] Morum elegantia, Tacit. Morum suavitas, Paterc. Mores humanissimi, suavissimi, Commodi. Urbanitas, Cic. Mores gratissimi, modestissimi, Id.
units.tr: Courtesy: Elegance of manners, Tac. Sweetness of manners, Paterc. Most humane, most agreeable, most pleasant manners. Urbanity, Cic. Most gracious and most modest manners, Id.

units.la: Civis] Oppidanus, Caes. Urbanus, Cic. Municeps, Juv. Civis adventitius.
units.tr: Citizen: A townsman, Caes. A city-dweller, Cic. A burgess, Juv. An incoming citizen.

units.la: Civis illegitimus] Furatus civitatem. Qui irrepsit in censum civitatis. Qui imprudenter surripuit civitatem, Cic. Peregrinitatis reus, Suet. Esse pro cive, qui non sit civis, non licere ait, Cic.
units.tr: Illegitimate citizen: One who has stolen citizenship. One who has crept into the citizen roll. One who unwittingly usurped citizenship, Cic. Accused of being a foreigner, Suet. He says that one who is not a citizen may not be counted as a citizen, Cic.

units.la: Civitas] Astu, τὸ ἄστυ, accus. utitur, Ter in astu venit. Urbs, Cic. Municipium, Plin. Corpus civitatis, Liv.
units.tr: State, city: Astu [τὸ ἄστυ], used in the accusative, Ter.: "he came into the city." City, Cic. A municipality, Plin. The body of the state, Liv.

units.la: Civitate donare] Adscribere in civitatem, civitati. Compotem facere civitatis. Civitati recipere. Ascisccre civem. Aliquem in civitate legibus constituere, Cic. Communicare cum aliquo civitatem, Liv.
units.tr: To grant citizenship: To enrol as a citizen. To make someone a sharer in citizenship. To receive into citizenship. To admit as a citizen. To establish someone among the citizens by law, Cic. To share citizenship with someone, Liv.

units.la: Clades] Calamitas, Cic. Internecio. Occidio. Strages, Liv. Deletio exercitus ad unum, Lucil. Internecinum bellum, Liv. Plin. Populi fugia, Macrob.
units.tr: Disaster: A calamity, Cic. Slaughter, destruction. Massacre, Liv. The destruction of an army to the last man, Lucil. A war of extermination, Liv., Plin. The flight of a people, Macrob.

units.la: Clam] Clam me. Me insciente, Plaut. Inconsciis aliis, Liv. Clanculum patrem facere aliquid, Ter. Insciô & inconsultô Dominô, Varro. In angulo. Sub tunicâ & sinu, Tertull. Vid. Occultè.
units.tr: Secretly: Secretly from me. Without my knowledge, Plaut. Others being unaware, Liv. To do something secretly from one's father, Ter. Without the master's knowledge or consent, Varro. In a corner. Under the tunic and in the bosom, Tertull. See Secretly.

units.la: Clamare] Tollere clamorem. Clamitare. Facere clamores. Clamorem edere. Voce contendère, Cic. Personant clamoribus tecta, Plin. Lacerat diem loquens, Plaut. Voce m tollere, Lucr. Attollere vocem, Sen. Tragœdias agere, excitare. Latrare. Bacchari, Cic. Vociferari, Id. Vociferare, Var.
units.tr: To cry out: to raise a shout; to clamour; to make outcries; to utter a cry; to strive with the voice (Cic.). The roofs ring with shouting (Plin.). He wears out the day by talking (Plaut.). To lift up the voice (Lucr.; Sen.). To play tragedies, to rant. To bark. To rave like a Bacchant (Cic.). To shout out (Id.). To vociferate (Var.).

units.la: Clamator] Proclamator, Cic. Stentore clamosior. Stentorea vox, Ter.
units.tr: Clamourer: a proclaimer (Cic.); louder than Stentor; a Stentorian voice (Ter.).

units.la: Clamor] Contentio vocis. Exclamatio acuta. Vociferatio, Cic. Vociferatus, Plin.
units.tr: Clamour: a straining of the voice; a sharp outcry; vociferation (Cic.); a shouting (Plin.).

units.la: Clamitatio] Plaut. Intentio vocis, Quint. Jubilatio, Apul.
units.tr: Clamouring: (Plaut.) a straining of the voice (Quint.); jubilation (Apul.).

units.la: Clamosus] Acutus & excitatus sonus. Clamatorius, Cic. Clamosus altercator, Quint. Argutus olor. Arguta fistula, Virg. Querulus, Hor. Tumultuosus, Plaut. Orthium carmen, Gell. Subtilissima vox, Id. Ejulabilis plangor, Apul.
units.tr: Clamorous: a sharp and raised sound; clamorous (Cic.); a noisy disputant (Quint.); a shrill swan; a shrill pipe (Virg.); plaintive (Hor.); tumultuous (Plaut.); an Orthian song (Gell.); a most subtle voice (Id.); a wailing lament (Apul.).

units.la: Clancularius] Umbraticus homo, Plaut. Umbratica turba, Sen. Umbratilis vita. Clandestinum colloquium. Furtivum iter. Lucifugus, Cic. Timidus lucis, Sen.
units.tr: Skulking: a shadowy fellow (Plaut.); a shady crowd (Sen.); a life lived in the shade; a secret conversation; a furtive journey; a light-shunning man (Cic.); one who fears the light (Sen.).

units.la: Clara voce] Voce contentâ, exsertâ, summâ, Cic. Vid. Sonore.
units.tr: In a loud voice: with the voice raised, strained, at full pitch (Cic.). See Sonore.

units.la: Clare] Liquidò, liquidius, dilucidè, perspicuè, plane explicare aliquid. Explanatiùs luculentè, Cic. Illustrissimè describere. Demonstrativè, Macrob. Expositè, Gell. Nudè, Sipont. Sole clarius. Laternâ magis perlucidus, Er.
units.tr: Clearly: to explain something plainly, lucidly, distinctly, perspicuously, openly. To explain more fully and brightly (Cic.). To describe most brilliantly. Demonstratively (Macrob.). Expounded (Gell.). Bare, without ornament (Sipont.). Clearer than the sun. More transparent than a lantern (Er.).

units.la: Clarescere] Effulsit sol in nubes. Dilucere, Liv. Elucidare lumen, Cic. Exsplendere, Plin.
units.tr: To grow bright: the sun has broken through the clouds. To shine forth (Liv.). To shed light (Cic.). To gleam forth (Plin.).

units.la: Claritas] Candentia Lunæ. Prominentia in picturis. Eminentia, Vitr. Claror, Plaut. Fulgor, Cic. Claritudo, Fest.
units.tr: Brightness: the gleam of the moon; projections in paintings; prominence (Vitr.); brightness (Plaut.); radiance (Cic.); clarity (Fest.).

units.la: Clarus] Splendidus. Candidus candor. Purus aër, Cic. Claror merus. Luculentus dies, Plaut. Illustris nox. Prænitens Luna. Prælucidus candore lunæ circulus. Occulatissimus locus, Plin. Liquidum lumen. Liquidissima cœli tempestas, Lucr. Pura luna, Cels. Veri luminis purpura, Trebel. Insolatus dies, Colum. Oculata dies, Plaut. Lucida gemma, Ovid. Percandidus, Cels.
units.tr: Bright: shining; gleaming white; pure air (Cic.); unmixed brightness; a bright day (Plaut.); an illustrious night; a shining moon; a circle very bright with the moon's whiteness; a most sunny place (Plin.); clear light; the clearest weather of the sky (Lucr.); a clear moon (Cels.); the purple of true light (Trebel.); a sunny day (Colum.); an open day (Plaut.); a bright gem (Ovid.); very white (Cels.).

units.la: Classicum certamen] Navalis pugna. Navale bellum, Cic. Navale prælium, Plin. Naumachia, Mart.
units.tr: Naval battle: a sea fight; a naval war (Cic.); a naval engagement (Plin.); a mock sea-battle (Mart.).

units.la: Classicum canere] Bellicum canere, Cic. Signum dare buccinâ, Curt. Inflare classicum, Virg. Convocatur classicò exercitus ad concionem, concrepantibus lituis. Processui canere, Amm. Insonant tubæ, Lucan. Classicum sonat, Seneca.
units.tr: To sound the call to battle: to sound the war-trumpet (Cic.); to give the signal with a horn (Curt.); to blow the classicum (Virg.). The army is summoned to an assembly with the sound of trumpets and horns. To sound the march (Amm.). The trumpets resound (Lucan.). The classicum sounds (Seneca).

units.la: Classis navium] Castra navalia, Cæs. Navales copiæ, Tacit. Disjecta classis toto æquore, Virg.
units.tr: Fleet of ships: a naval camp (Caes.); naval forces (Tacit.); a fleet scattered over the whole sea (Virg.).

units.la: Claudere] Adducere ostium cellæ, Petron. Obserare ostium. stium. Objicere fores portæ, Ter. Obtrudere fores, Plaut. Operire ostium, Ter. Occludere, Oppilare, Cic.
units.tr: To shut: to draw the door of the room to (Petron.); to bar the door; to bolt the door; to throw the doors of the gate shut (Ter.); to push the doors to (Plaut.); to cover the door (Ter.); to close, to block up (Cic.).

units.la: Claudicare] Alternum facere pedem, Stat.
units.tr: To limp: to make one foot lame (Stat.).

units.la: Claudus utroque pede] Neutro pede utilis, Plin. Cleppus, Scal.
units.tr: Lame in both feet: useless with either foot (Plin.); Cleppus, Scal.

units.la: Clava] Sparus, Saluft. Virg. Sparum, Lucil. Mateola, Caton.
units.tr: Club: a cudgel; Sparus, Saluft. Virg.; Sparum, Lucil.; Mateola, Caton.

units.la: Clavis] Dens. Referare fores dente, Tibul.
units.tr: Key: a tooth. To unbar the doors with a tooth (Tibul.).

units.la: Clavis falsa] Clavis adultera, Ovid. Adulterina, Taub. Clavis Laconica, Id. ex Plaut.
units.tr: False key: an adulterous key (Ovid.); an adulterine key (Taub.); a Laconian key (Id. ex Plaut.).

units.la: Claustrum (1) i.e. Sera] Claustrum Januæ, Catul. Clostrum, Cat. ant. Serraculum Palem. IC. Clostellum, Petron.
units.tr: Claustrum (1), that is, bar: the bar of a door (Catul.); clostrum (Cat. ant.); serraculum (Palem. IC.); clostellum (Petron.).

units.la: Claustrum] (2) Cœnobium, Gell. Monasterium, Philon. Ascaeterium, in Cod.
units.tr: Claustrum (2): a convent (Gell.); a monastery (Philon.); ascaeterium (in Cod.).

units.la: Claustrum virginale] Parthenon. Gynæceum sacrum, Bud. Sacrarum virginum collegium. Cœnobium virginum, Isid.
units.tr: Nunnery: a Parthenon; a sacred women's apartment (Bud.); a community of consecrated virgins; a convent of virgins (Isid.).

units.la: Clausula] Exitus. Determinatio orationis Epilogus. Peroratio. Extrema oratio, Cic. Coronis, Mart. Colophon, Fest.
units.tr: Close: the end; the conclusion of a speech; an epilogue; a peroration; the final part of a speech (Cic.); a coronis (Mart.); a colophon (Fest.).

units.la: Clausulam impono, Vid. Absolvere.
units.tr: To put an end to: see Absolvere.

units.la: Clausus] Inclusus, Conclusus, Cic. Clausa domorum, Lucr. Intraclusus, Aggen.
units.tr: Shut: shut up, enclosed (Cic.); closed-up houses (Lucr.); shut in (Aggen.).

units.la: Clavus] Clavulus, Var. Claviculus, Sipont.
units.tr: Nail: a little nail (Var.); a small peg (Sipont.).

units.la: Clemens] Æquum & bonum amans, sequens. Justus, Ter. Æqualem tenet juris rationem. Æquabilis in suos, Tacit. Æquabilem se præbet, Cic. Incruentus Princeps, Amm.
units.tr: Merciful: loving and following what is fair and good; just (Ter.); keeping an even measure of right (Tacit.); even-handed towards his own (Tacit.); showing himself even-tempered (Cic.); a bloodless prince (Amm.).

units.la: Clementer] Benevolè. Benignè. Benignissimè. Cum bonâ gratiâ. Amabiliter in aliquem cogitare, Cic. Indulgenter. Placidè, Liv. Indulgentissimè. Humanè, Sen. Dignanter, Vopisc. Placido vultu, Prop.
units.tr: Mercifully: kindly; benignly; most benignly; with good will. To think kindly of someone (Cic.); indulgently; gently (Liv.); most indulgently; humanely (Sen.); graciously (Vopisc.); with a gentle countenance (Prop.).

units.la: Clementia] Facilitas. Placabilitas. Indulgentia. Lenitas. Mansuetudo imperii, Æquitas, Cic. Benignitas, Plaut. Semper-lenitas, Terent.
units.tr: Mercy: readiness to forgive; placability; indulgence; leniency; the mildness of government and equity (Cic.); kindness (Plaut.); constant gentleness (Ter.).

units.la: Clericus] Initiatus sacris, Iun. Qui est in clero, Tertul.
units.tr: Clergyman: one initiated into sacred rites (Iun.); one who belongs to the clergy (Tertul.).

units.la: Clerus, collegium Clericorum] Res Clerica & Ecclesiastica. Jus sacrosancti capitis, Bud.
units.tr: Clergy, the body of clerics: clerical and ecclesiastical affairs; the right of the inviolable person (Bud.).

units.la: Cliens alicujus] Clienta, Plaut. Qui in fide & clientelâ est. Cic. Sub umbrâ alicujus dilitescens. Commendatus in clientelam, Cic.
units.tr: Client of someone: a clienta (Plaut.); one who is in the trust and clientship of another (Cic.); one hiding under another's shade; one commended into clientship (Cic.).

units.la: Clientela] Clientela, Cic. Curatio, Vlp.
units.tr: Clientship: clientship (Cic.); care, management (Ulp.).

units.la: Clima] Ora, Cic. Inclinatio, Vitr. Declinatio, Col. Devergentia, Gell. Segmenta mundi, terrarum, Plin.
units.tr: Zone: a region (Cic.); an inclination (Vitr.); a declination (Col.); a divergence (Gell.); the segments of the world and of the lands (Plin.).

units.la: Clitella] Sagmata asinorum, Scal.
units.tr: Pack-saddle: the packs of asses (Scal.).

units.la: Clitellarius equus] Dorsuarius, Var. Sarcinarius, Cæs. Sagmarius, Rhod.
units.tr: Pack-horse: a horse for burdens (Var.); a baggage horse (Caes.); a sumpter horse (Rhod.).

units.la: Clivus] Jugum montis, Virg. Declivitas montis, Sipont. Pes montis, Iun. Radix montis, Cæs. Acclivitas, Id. Proclivitas. Proclive, Cic.
units.tr: Slope: the ridge of a mountain (Virg.); the descent of a mountain (Sipont.); the foot of a mountain (Iun.); the base of a mountain (Caes.); the ascent (Id.); a downward slope; sloping downward (Cic.).

units.la: Cloaca publica] Forica, Iuv. Aumarium, Petron. Automatium, Gotfred.
units.tr: Public sewer: a forica (Juv.); an aumarium (Petron.); an automatium (Gotfred.).

units.la: Cloaca domestica] Latrina, Apul. Sella familiarica, Var. Sella familiæ, Cat. Quo saturi ire solent, Plaut. Secessus, Isid. Culina, Petr. Cloacula, Lampr.
units.tr: Domestic sewer: a privy (Apul.); a household stool (Var.); the family seat (Cato); where full men are wont to go (Plaut.); a retreat (Isid.); the kitchen (Petron.); a little privy (Lampr.).

units.la: Clunes] Sedes, Plin. Postica pars corporis, Lucil. Posticum, Arnob. Posteriora, Ovid.
units.tr: Buttocks: the seat (Plin.); the hinder part of the body (Lucil.); the posterior (Arnob.); the hinder parts (Ovid.).

units.la: Clypeus] Umbo, Liv. Pectorale militum, Plin. Phalanx. Parma, Cæs.
units.tr: Shield: the boss (Liv.); the breastplate of soldiers (Plin.); a phalanx; a small shield (Caes.).

units.la: Clyster] Clysmus acris, Scrib.
units.tr: Enema: a sharp enema (Scrib.).

units.la: Clysterum adhibere] Ab inferiore parte alvum evocare, Cels. Cremorem in alvum inferiorem indere, Id. Clystere purgari, Cæs.
units.tr: To administer an enema: to draw the bowels out from below (Cels.); to pour gruel into the lower bowel (Id.); to be purged by an enema (Caes.).

units.la: Coactio] Necessitas. Coactus, Cic. Adactio ad aliquid, Liv.
units.tr: Compulsion: necessity; one who is compelled (Cic.); being driven to something (Liv.).

units.la: Coactus fecit] Vi ac necessitate, metu ac malo coactus, Cic. Expressit hoc necessitas patribus. Per ultimam necessitatem, Liv. Ex necessitate facere, Id.
units.tr: He did it under compulsion: compelled by force and necessity, by fear and misfortune (Cic.). Necessity wrung this from the senators (Liv.). By the last necessity (Liv.). To act out of necessity (Liv.).

units.la: Coadunare] Redigere in unum. Provinciæ aliquot uno imperio conjunctæ, Cic. Vid. Adunatio.
units.tr: To bring together: to bring into one. Several provinces joined under one rule (Cic.). See Adunatio.

units.la: Coæquare] Adæquare virtutem cum fortunâ. Exæquare omnia. Paria in utramque partem reddere omnia. Infima summis paria facere, Cic. Componere dicta cum factis, Sallust.
units.tr: To make equal: to match virtue with fortune; to equalise all things; to make all things equal on both sides; to make the lowest equal to the highest (Cic.); to match words with deeds (Sallust.).

units.la: Coagmentare] Concorporare, Plin. Coadunare statuæ brachium, Consolidare, Vlp.
units.tr: To join together: to join into one body (Plin.); to join the arm of a statue together, to consolidate (Ulp.).

units.la: Coagulare] Cogere lac in duritiem. Contrahere lac, Plin. Congelare, Col.
units.tr: To curdle: to force milk into hardness; to contract milk (Plin.); to congeal (Col.).

units.la: Coagulari] Spissatur lac igni, Plin. Glaciat unguentum, Id.
units.tr: To be curdled: milk thickens with fire (Plin.); ointment freezes (Id.).

units.la: Coit sanguis, Virg. In densitatem coit, Plin. Concrescit, Lucr.
units.tr: Blood clots (Virg.); it coagulates into density (Plin.); it grows together (Lucr.).

units.la: Coagulatum lac] Coactum lac, Ovid. Spissatum, Plin.
units.tr: Curdled milk: milk made to curdle (Ovid.); thickened (Plin.).

units.la: Coalescere] Implicantur inter radices, & unitatem faciunt, Col. Concorporari, Plin. Concrescere, Lucr.
units.tr: To grow together: they become entangled among the roots and make one unity (Col.); to grow into one body (Plin.); to grow together (Lucr.).

units.la: Coarctare] In arctum cogere. Claudere, Cic. Vid. Angustare.
units.tr: To constrict: to drive into a narrow space; to shut in (Cic.). See Angustare.

units.la: Coaxare] Quoaxare. Quaxare, Fest. Quassare, Scal.
units.tr: To croak: quoaxare; quaxare (Fest.); quassare (Scal.).

units.la: Cochlea] Strombus pluviatilis, Gesner. Limax, Plin.
units.tr: Snail: a river snail (Gesner); a slug (Plin.).

units.la: Cochleæ concha] Domus cochleæ. Calix cochleæ. Testa limacis, Plin.
units.tr: Snail shell: the house of the snail; the cup of the snail; the shell of the slug (Plin.).

units.la: Cocles] Unoculus, Plaut. Monoculus, Firm. Luscus, Cic. Defioculus, Mart. Oculum persolum habet, Id. De coelitum prosapia est, Plaut.
units.tr: One-eyed: one-eyed (Plaut.); one-eyed (Firm.); squinting (Cic.); blind in one eye (Mart.); he has only one eye (Id.); he is of the race of the heavenly ones (Plaut.).

units.la: Coctus, Vid. Elixus.
units.tr: Cooked: see Elixus.

units.la: Cælebs] Exsors matrimonii, Plin. Nuptiarum expers. Litibus carens homo. Extra conjugium vivens.
units.tr: Unmarried: without a share in marriage (Plin.); lacking wedlock; a man free of quarrels; living outside marriage.

units.la: Cælibatus jucundus] Libero lecto nihil jucundius.
units.tr: A pleasant single life: nothing is more pleasant than a bed of one's own.

units.la: Cælum] Altissimum domicilium. Orbis coelestis extimus. Cic. Polus. Olympus, Virg. Æther, Ovid. Altum, Lucr. Lucida templa coeli. Mœnia mundi. Coelestium templa, Lucr.
units.tr: Heaven: the highest dwelling; the outermost sphere of the heavenly world (Cic.); the pole; Olympus (Virg.); the ether (Ovid.); the height (Lucr.); the bright temples of heaven; the walls of the world; the temples of the heavenly beings (Lucr.).

units.la: Cælestis] Supera & cœlestia cogitare. Æthereus locus, Cic. Coelitibus regnis pulsus, Ovid.
units.tr: Heavenly: to think of things above and heavenly; an ethereal place (Cic.); driven from the heavenly kingdoms (Ovid.).

units.la: Cælites] Superi. Concilium cœlestium, Cic. Cœlicolæ, Divi indigetes, Virg.
units.tr: The heavenly ones: the gods above; an assembly of the heavenly ones (Cic.); the heaven-dwellers, the native gods (Virg.).

units.la: Cælitus] Divinitus. De cœlo delapsus, Lucr.
units.tr: From heaven: divinely; fallen down from heaven (Lucr.).

units.la: Cœna lauta] Cœna deorum. Ambrosia & Nectar.
units.tr: A sumptuous dinner: the feast of the gods; ambrosia and nectar.

units.la: Cœna frugalis] Cœna sine sanguine, Diphil. Cœna terrestris, Cynica, Petron. Dapes inemptæ, Hor.
units.tr: A frugal dinner: a dinner without blood (Diphil.); an earthly, Cynic dinner (Petron.); uninvited feasts (Hor.).

units.la: In cœna] Sub horam cœnæ.
units.tr: At dinner: about the dinner hour.

units.la: Cænaculum] Cœnatio, Col. Tabulinum, Varr. Diæta seu Cœnatiuncula, Plin. Iun. Zeta, Lampr. Sigma, Mart. Diætula, Plin. Iun. Zeticula, Rhod. Hormil.
units.tr: Dining room: an upper dining room (Col.); a study (Varr.); a small dining room or diaeta (Plin. Iun.); a zeta (Lampr.); a sigma (Mart.); a small diaeta (Plin. Iun.); a zeticula (Rhod.); hormil.

units.la: Cæpi, Vid. Incipere.
units.tr: To begin: see Incipere.

units.la: Cænosus, Vid. Lutosus.
units.tr: Muddy: see Lutosus.

units.la: Cæpta non deserenda] Ante mysteria discedere. Filum nervi, & acu opus est. Cœpta deserere] Infecta sacra relinquere. Incepta fila relinquere, Ovid.
units.tr: Things begun not to be abandoned: to withdraw before the mysteries. A thread of sinew and a needle are needed. To abandon things begun: to leave the rites unfinished; to leave the threads begun (Ovid.).

units.la: Cœpta alterius perficere] Hic telam texuit, alter deduxit.
units.tr: To finish another's undertaking: one wove the web, another finished it off.

units.la: Coërcere] Comprimere impetum. Reprimere furorem. Inhibere aliquem. Frenare. Injicere frenos. Refrenare licentiam. Moderari iræ, Cic. Frangere furorem, Id. Compescere, Ovid. Vid. Cohibere.
units.tr: To restrain: to check an onset; to curb rage; to hold someone back; to bridle; to put on the reins; to rein in licence; to moderate anger (Cic.); to break fury (Id.); to check (Ovid.). See Cohibere.

units.la: Coercitio] Cohibitio, Cic. Refrenatio, Sen. Coërctio alicujus, Cels.
units.tr: Restraint: a checking (Cic.); a curbing (Sen.); the restraining of someone (Cels.).

units.la: Cœtus] Corona. Congregatio. Concilium. Confessus, Frequentia virorum. Panegyris, Celebritas. Concio, Circulus hominum. Chorus juventutis, Cic. Corpus, Liv.
units.tr: Gathering: a crowd; a meeting; an assembly; a council; a throng; a company of men; a festive assembly; a celebration; a sermon; a circle of people; a chorus of young men (Cic.); a body (Liv.).

units.la: Cogere] Adigere. Subigere aliquem, Plaut. Compellere ad. Jungere necessitatem, Plin. Iun. Afferre necessitatem, Virg. Vi cogere, Cic. Capillis trahere, Plaut.
units.tr: To drive: to force; to compel someone (Plaut.); to compel to; to lay necessity upon (Plin. Iun.); to bring necessity (Virg.); to compel by force (Cic.); to drag by the hair (Plaut.).

units.la: Cogitabundus] Defixus in cogitatione, Altius aliquid cogitans, Cic. Cogitationibus magnis attonitus, Amm.
units.tr: Lost in thought: fixed in thought; thinking something more deeply (Cic.); stunned by great thoughts (Amm.).

units.la: Cogitare] Cogitare saxa & montes. Versare mente. Cogitatione complecti. Conquirere. Insidet mihi cogitatio. Injecta est mihi cogitatio de. Suscipere cogitationem, quiddam, &c. Obversatur animo species. Animus est in hortis, in patinis. Commentari aliquid secum. Meditor mecum ipse. Mente contrectare, complecti. Ratione animoque lustrare, Cic. Cogito in animo, Ter. Cogitationes volvere. Animum cogitationibus volutare, Liv. Agitare aliquid cum animo, Sallust. Immorari cogitationibus, Plin. Figere mentem in aliquâ re.
units.tr: To think] To think of rocks and mountains. To turn over in the mind. To embrace in thought. To search out. A thought sits on me. A thought has been put into my mind about... To take up a thought about something, etc. An image presents itself to the mind. The mind is in the gardens, in the dishes. To rehearse something to oneself. I meditate with myself. To handle and embrace in the mind. To survey with reason and mind, Cic. I think in my mind, Ter. To roll thoughts over. To toss the mind about with thoughts, Liv. To turn something over with the mind, Sallust. To dwell on thoughts, Pliny. To fix the mind on some matter.

units.la: Cogitavi idem] Meum mihi narras somnium.
units.tr: I thought the same] You tell me my own dream.

units.la: Cogitatè, vid. Præmeditatè. Consultò.
units.tr: Thoughtfully, see Premeditatively. Deliberately.

units.la: Cogitatio] Motus cogitatione celeriter agitatus. Commentatio. Mentis agitatio. Mentis sensus. Animi sensus & motus. Sermo intimus. Meditatio, Cic. Meditamentum, Tacit. Animus, Ter. ut, Advertere animum.
units.tr: Thought] A motion of the mind swiftly stirred. Reflection. Stirring of the mind. Sense of the mind. Feeling and movement of the soul. Inner speech. Meditation, Cic. A contrivance, Tacit. Mind, Ter. as in: to turn the mind to something.

units.la: Cogitationes varia] Aliam rem ex alia cogito, Ter. Animum huc, illuc verso, Virg.
units.tr: Various thoughts] I pass from one thing to another in thought, Ter. I turn my mind this way and that, Virg.

units.la: Cogitationes alterius nemo novit] Cogitationis pœnam nemo patitur. Cognatio] Gentilitas. Necessitudo liberorum fraterna. Germanitas, Cic. Necessitas, Gell. Propinquitas, Cæs. Parentela, Iul. Cap.
units.tr: No one knows another's thoughts] No one suffers punishment for a thought. Kinship] Clanship. Brotherly bond of blood. Blood-brotherhood, Cic. Necessity, Gell. Nearness of kin, Caes. Kindred, Iul. Cap.

units.la: Cognatus] Attingit me necessitudine, cognatione. Est illi conjunctus propinquitate, Gentilis alicui, Cic. Contingit propinquitatem regiam, Liv. Cognatus sanguis, Virg. Charitate sanguinis sociati, Amm. Arctissimo contingere gradu, Suet.
units.tr: Kinsman] He touches me by blood tie and kinship. He is closely related to him by kinship. A clansman of someone, Cic. He attains royal kinship, Liv. Blood kin, Virg. Joined by the affection of blood, Amm. To be related in the closest degree, Suet.

units.la: Cognatis abundans] Cognatione amplissima homo, Cic. Pollens genus. Factiosus, Plaut.
units.tr: Abounding in kinsmen] A man of very wide kinship, Cic. Powerful in family. Partisan, Plaut.

units.la: Cognitio] Perspicientia veri, Agnitio alicujus rei, Cic.
units.tr: Knowledge] Clear perception of truth. Recognition of some thing, Cic.

units.la: Cognitus, vid. Notus.
units.tr: Known, see Notus.

units.la: Cognomen] Agnomen, Cæs. Ovid. Esse cognominis alicujus, Plin.
units.tr: Surname] A second name, Caes. Ovid. To bear the same surname as someone, Pliny.

units.la: Cognoscere] Venit aliquid in cognitionem meam, Quint. Primum in notitiam venit, Plin. Assequi. Tum primùm noscuntur partes philosophiæ, cùm &c. Cic.
units.tr: To know] Something comes into my knowledge, Quint. It first comes into notice, Pliny. To attain. Then for the first time the parts of philosophy are known, when etc., Cic.

units.la: Cognoscere leviter] De facie nosse.
units.tr: To know slightly] To know by face.

units.la: Cohabitare] Pariter habitare, Var. Unà habitare. Commanere, Macr.
units.tr: To cohabit] To live together on equal terms, Varro. To live together. To stay together, Macr.

units.la: Cohærentia] Concatenatio laborum. Continentia. Continuatio Regionum, Macr. Compactio membrorum. Colligatio. Copulatio rerum, Cic. Junctura artis latens, Plin. Consortio, Arnob. Compositura, Lucr.
units.tr: Coherence] A chain of labours. Continuity. Continuous stretch of regions, Macr. Joining of limbs. Binding together. Joining of things, Cic. A hidden joint of art, Pliny. Association, Arnob. Arrangement, Lucr.

units.la: Cohærere] Congruere. Quadrare, Cic.
units.tr: To cohere] To agree. To fit exactly, Cic.

units.la: Cohibere] Reprimere se à. Reprimere iracundiam. Revocare, & Reflectere animum, ad ulciscendum incitatum. Contrahere vela. Adducere habenas. Tenere iracundiam. Remittere spiritum aculeorum plenum. Comprimere manum. Sedare iram. Iræ moderans & ori. Iracundiam dimittere. Injicere frenos, Cic. Resp onsare cupidinibus, Hor. Supprimere iram, Ovid. Comprimere se. Vincere animum, Plaut. Temperare sibi, manibus, Liv.
units.tr: To restrain] To check oneself from. To curb anger. To call back and turn the mind, roused to vengeance. To furl the sails. To draw in the reins. To hold back anger. To let go of a spirit full of stings. To press down the hand. To calm anger. Governing anger and the mouth. To give up anger. To put on the bit, Cic. To curb one's desires, Hor. To suppress anger, Ovid. To restrain oneself. To overcome the mind, Plaut. To control oneself, one's hands, Liv.

units.la: Cohibitio, vid. Coërcit.
units.tr: Restraint, see Coërcitio.

units.la: Cohors militum] Globus virûm. Manus juvenum ardens, Virg. Ordo. Cohorticula, Cic.
units.tr: Cohort of soldiers] A band of men. A burning band of young men, Virg. A rank. A small cohort, Cic.

units.la: Colaphus, vid. Alapa.
units.tr: Blow with the fist, see Slap.

units.la: Colaphizare] Infligere, Infringere alicui colaphum. Incutere, Iuv. Porrecta palma ferire. Ducere colaphum, Plaut.
units.tr: To strike with the fist] To deal a blow with the fist to someone. To strike with an open palm held out. To receive a blow, Juv. To take a blow, Plaut.

units.la: Colare] Exprimere per linteum. Sacco frangere, Castrare vina, Plin. Liquare vinum, Col. Ttanscolare. Defaecare, Lucr. Cernere percribrum. Percolare, Cat.
units.tr: To strain] To press out through linen. To break with a sack; to strain wines, Pliny. To strain wine, Col. To filter through. To clear of dregs, Lucr. To sift through a sieve. To strain through, Cat.

units.la: Colere aliquem] Advenerari, Sil. Percolere honore, Tacit. Devenerari, Ovid. Vid. Honorare. Ornare.
units.tr: To honour someone] To pay reverence to, Sil. To honour greatly, Tacit. To revere, Ovid. See To honour. To adorn.

units.la: Collabascere] Collabi, Ovid. Collabescere, Lucr. Collabefieri, Caf. Prolabi, Liv. Labi, Cic. Procidere, Hor. Procumbere, Liv. Submissi petimus terram. Decidunt turres casu, Hor. Vid. Cadere.
units.tr: To collapse] To fall down, Ovid. To sink, Lucr. To be brought down, Caf. To slip away, Liv. To slide, Cic. To fall prostrate, Hor. To lie down, Liv. We seek the ground as suppliants. Towers fall by chance, Hor. See To fall.

units.la: Collateralis] Laterarius, Vitruv.
units.tr: Collateral] Of the side, Vitruv.

units.la: Collatio] Collecta, Var. Symbola, Plaut.
units.tr: Contribution] A collection, Varro. Shares, Plaut.

units.la: Collaudare, vid Dilaudare.
units.tr: To praise highly, see To extol.

units.la: Collectaneus] Collectitius exercitus, Cic. Collatitia instrumenta, Sen.
units.tr: Collected] A levied army, Cic. Borrowed tools, Sen.

units.la: Collega] Contubernalis in consulatu, Cic.
units.tr: Colleague] A fellow in the consulship, Cic.

units.la: Collegium] Curia, Plaut. Corpora omnium omnino artium, Lampr. Sodalitium, Sodalitas, Cic. Corona. Coetus senatorum, Sen.
units.tr: College] A senate house, Plaut. The bodies of all the arts together, Lampr. A fellowship, company, Cic. A crown. A gathering of senators, Sen.

units.la: Collidere] Confligunt agmine, Claud. Complodere manus. Arietantur inter se tela, Sen. Concrepare digitis, Cic.
units.tr: To clash] They clash in a body, Claud. To clap the hands. Weapons strike one another, Sen. To snap the fingers, Cic.

units.la: Colligare] Connectere nodum. Copulando jungere. Constringere catenis, Cic. Colligere in fasciculos, Plin. Ansis ferreis vincire, Vitruv. Fibula conjungere, Id. Cohibere crinem nodo, Ovid. Circumplectere, Cat. Fibulare, Col.
units.tr: To bind] To tie a knot. To join by fastening. To bind with chains, Cic. To gather into bundles, Pliny. To bind with iron clamps, Vitruv. To join with a clasp, Id. To hold hair in a knot, Ovid. To embrace, Cat. To fasten with a brooch, Col.

units.la: Colligere] Libare ex omnibus excellentissima quaeque. Conficere pecuniam, Cic. Cogere undique auxilia, Virg. Contrahere. Legere spolia, Liv. Recolligere ova, Col.
units.tr: To gather] To pick out the choicest things from all. To raise money, Cic. To bring together help from everywhere, Virg. To draw together. To gather spoils, Liv. To collect eggs again, Col.

units.la: Colligere se] Colligere animum, Liv. Sumere animos, Ovid. Sumere confidentiam, Plaut. Colligere se ex timore, Caes.
units.tr: To collect oneself] To collect one's courage, Liv. To take heart, Ovid. To take confidence, Plaut. To recover oneself from fear, Caes.

units.la: Collimare] Collineare hastam aliquo. Intendere machinam. Petere caput alicujus. Vulnerabant, quem locum destinassent, Cic. Dirigere spiculum, Ovid. Dirigere ad metam, Var. Id semper feriet, quodcunque minabitur arcus, Hor. Perlibrare jaculum ad aliquid, Stat.
units.tr: To aim] To aim a spear at something. To level a machine. To seek someone's head. They would wound whatever spot they had chosen, Cic. To direct a dart, Ovid. To direct at the goal, Varro. It will always strike whatever the bow threatens, Hor. To aim a javelin thoroughly at something, Stat.

units.la: Collimatio] Directio lineæ. Temperatura ballistarum, Scorpionum, Catapultarum. Libratio, & Perlibratio, Vitruv.
units.tr: Aiming] Direction of a line. The setting of ballistae, scorpions, catapults. Levelling, and careful levelling, Vitruv.

units.la: Colliquefacere, vid. Liquare.
units.tr: To melt together, see To melt.

units.la: Calliquefieri, vid. Liquefieri.
units.tr: To be melted together, see To be melted.

units.la: Collis] Colliculus, Mart. Tumulus civitatis excellens. Globus terræ leviter eminens, Cic. Dorsuosa prominentia, Id. Verruca, Gell. ex Lat. Grumus, Non.
units.tr: Hill] A little hill, Mart. A mound rising above a town. A slightly raised mass of earth, Cic. A ridged projection, Id. A wart, Gell. from the Latin. A clod, Non.

units.la: Collocare, vid. Locare.
units.tr: To place, see To set.

units.la: Colloqui cum aliquo] Colloquium cum aliquo facere. Sermonem conferre, habere, facere, instituere. Fit sermo inter nos. Sermo mihi est cum aliquo, de. Communicare cum aliquo de. Communicare sermones. Frui sermone alicujus. Sermocinari cum aliquo de aliquâ re, Cic. Serere cum aliquo colloquium. Rem agitare sermonibus, Liv. Copulare cum aliquo sermonem, Plaut. Cædere sermonem, Ter. Viam sermone levabant, Virg. Variare cœnulam sermone. Verba commutare, Varr. Confabulari aliquid cum aliquo. Fabulari, conferre, Plaut.
units.tr: To converse with someone] To hold a conversation with someone. To carry on, hold, make, begin a discussion. A conversation takes place between us. I have a talk with someone, about something. To share talk with someone about something. To exchange talk. To enjoy someone's conversation. To discuss something with someone, Cic. To enter into conversation with someone. To deal with a matter in talk, Liv. To engage someone in talk, Plaut. To cut short a conversation, Ter. They lightened the road with talk, Virg. To vary a little supper with talk. To exchange words, Varro. To discuss something with someone. To chat, to converse, Plaut.

units.la: Colloquium] Sermo, Sermonis communicatio cum aliquo. Præclara Synodia, Cic. Communio sermonis, Suet. Commercia linguæ, Lucr. vid. Dialogus.
units.tr: Conversation] Talk, the sharing of speech with someone. An excellent gathering, Cic. Sharing of talk, Suet. Intercourse of language, Lucr. See Dialogue.

units.la: Colluctari, vid. Luctari.
units.tr: To wrestle together, see To wrestle.

units.la: Colludere cum aliquo] Collusoriè agere, Litigare, Vlp. Prævaricatorem sibi apponere, Bud.
units.tr: To collude with someone] To act collusively, to dispute, Ulp. To set a prevaricator against oneself, Bud.

units.la: Collusio] Compactum, Suet. Pactio, Cic. Colludium actionum in judicio, Amm. Prævaricatio, Bud.
units.tr: Collusion] A secret agreement, Suet. A bargain, Cic. Collusion of actions in a trial, Amm. Prevarication, Bud.

units.la: Colluvies] Confluvium, Sipont. Confluentia, Macrob. Purgamentorum receptaculum, Liv. Eluvies, Plin. Illuvies, Varr.
units.tr: Filth] A place where waters meet, Sipont. A confluence, Macrob. A receptacle for refuse, Liv. A washing away, Pliny. A soiling, Varro.

units.la: Collybista] Argyrognomon (i e. pecuniæ spectator) Bud. Pecuniæ venditor, Id. Campsoria.
units.tr: Money-changer] A watcher of money (i.e. one who watches money), Bud. A seller of money, Id. A moneychanger.

units.la: Collybus] Cambium, Lævin.
units.tr: Exchange] Exchange of money, Lævin.

units.la: Coloniam instituere] Occupare, Complere coloniis aliquam regionem. Deducere colonos aliquò. Collocare in aliqua civitate colonos. Colonorum numerum in aliquam civitatem scribere. Mittere in coloniam. Assignare novos colocolonos: Dare, dividere agrum novis colonis. Collocare in aliquo loco novos colonos. Instituere civitatem, Cic. Coloniam in agro ponere, Liv.
units.tr: To establish a colony] To occupy or fill a region with colonies. To lead colonists somewhere. To settle colonists in some city. To enrol a number of colonists in some city. To send into a colony. To assign new colonists. To give or divide land to new colonists. To settle new colonists in some place. To found a city, Cic. To place a colony in the countryside, Liv.

units.la: Color dilutus] Color lentus, surdus, obsoletus, languidus, Plin.
units.tr: Faded colour] A dull, dim, worn, faint colour, Pliny.

units.la: Color floridus] Color suavis, Cic. Color satur, Virg. Color vivus, Mart.
units.tr: Bright colour] A pleasant colour, Cic. A rich colour, Virg. A lively colour, Mart.

units.la: Color purpureus] Color diffusus sanguine. Rubor, Cic. Rubor in malis, Plin. Candor purpureo sanguine diffusus, Stat. Verecundus color, Hor. Sanguinolentus color, Ovid.
units.tr: Purple colour] A colour spread with blood. Redness, Cic. Redness among apples, Pliny. Whiteness spread with purple blood, Stat. A modest colour, Hor. A bloody colour, Ovid.

units.la: Colore ambiguo] Inclinans ad luteum colorem. Languescente colore in suspectu refulgens. Candicans è rufo. Color violas sentiens, Plin. Albicans ex rutilo. Ex auro flavus. Ex aureolo varius, Col. Viridis communicatio coloris cum, Plin. Ambiguo colore nitens, Amm.
units.tr: Ambiguous colour] Leaning towards a yellow colour. Shining in a fading colour, under suspicion. Whitish from red. A colour feeling its way to violet, Pliny. Whitish from ruddy. Yellow from gold. Varied from golden-brown, Col. The green mixing of colour with, Pliny. Shining with an ambiguous colour, Amm.

units.la: Colorem mutare] Non constat ei color, Liv. Errant varii colores in vultu, Virg. In varios colores transfire. Trahit colorem croci. Descendit ad &c. Plin. Variat sol ortum maculis, Virg. Migrare in alius colorem, Lucr.
units.tr: To change colour] The colour does not stay with him, Liv. Varied colours wander over the face, Virg. To pass into various colours. It takes on the colour of saffron. It sinks to etc., Pliny. The sun varies its rising with spots, Virg. To pass into another colour, Lucr.

units.la: Colorare] Colorem inducere, Vitr. Inficere colore, Plin. Tingere, Mart. Fricare lanam, Virg. Sufficere lanam, Cic. Rutilare comam, Amm.
units.tr: To colour] To bring in colour, Vitr. To stain with colour, Pliny. To tinge, Mart. To dye wool, Virg. To dye wool, Cic. To make the hair reddish, Amm.

units.la: Coloratus] Tinctus, Ovid. Contactus colore croci, Lucr. Colorea vestis, Causab. Colorius, Metiens colorem, Virg. Suffecta sole nubes, Sen. Infectus, Plin. Fucatus, Virg.
units.tr: Coloured] Dyed, Ovid. Touched with the colour of saffron, Lucr. A coloured garment, Casaubon. Coloured, measuring colour, Virg. A cloud tinted by the sun, Sen. Stained, Pliny. Painted over, disguised, Virg.

units.la: Colossus] Statua colossea, Spart. Colossicum signum, Colosseus Nero, Plin.
units.tr: Colossus] A colossal statue, Spart. A colossal figure; the colossal Nero, Pliny.

units.la: Colum, vid. Qualus.
units.tr: Sieve, see Qualus.

units.la: Columbus ferus] Columba agrestis & saxatilis, Var. Turricola, Scal. Venago, Gaz.
units.tr: Wild pigeon] A rural and rock-dwelling dove, Varro. A tower-dweller, Scal. A wild pigeon, Gaz.

units.la: Columbarium] Columbaria, orum, Varr. Latibula columbarum, Id.
units.tr: Dovecote] Dovecotes, Varro. Hiding-places of doves, Id.

units.la: Columna in aedificiis] Tibicen, Iuv. Pila, Plin.
units.tr: Column in buildings] A prop, Juv. A pillar, Pliny.

units.la: Coma] Capillamentum, Suet. Coma plicata, nexa. Subtilia & textilia capillamenta, Ter. Caesaries, Serv. Frontis tegumentum, Athen. Capilli, Cic. Capillitium, Apul. Comam alere] Promittere barbam, Tacit. Submittere, Sen. Pascere crinem, Virg.
units.tr: Hair] A wig, Suet. Plaited, knotted hair. Fine and woven tresses, Ter. Long hair, Serv. A covering for the forehead, Athen. Hair of the head, Cic. Hair, Apul. To grow hair] To let the beard grow, Tacit. To let it grow long, Sen. To nourish the hair, Virg.

units.la: Combibo] Compotor alicujus, Cic. Compotrix, Ter.
units.tr: To drink up] A drinking companion of someone, Cic. A female drinking companion, Ter.

units.la: Comburere] Scripta ustulanda lignis infelicibus da tardipedi Deo, i.e. Vulcano, Catull. Concremare igni. Cinefacere, Lucr. Exurere puppes, Virg. Deurere vicos, Liv. Vulcano tradere.
units.tr: To burn] Writings to be burnt with unlucky wood, to the lame god, that is Vulcan, Catull. To burn with fire. To reduce to ashes, Lucr. To burn up ships, Virg. To burn down villages, Liv. To hand over to Vulcan.

units.la: Comburi] In cinerem crematus. Ad cinerem ambustus, Plin. [Cinefactus, Lucr. Deflagrare. Deflagrare incendio, ardore, flammâ. Conflagrare, flammâ, Cic. Consumi incendio. Hausit multos flamma, Liv. Haustus igni, Tacit. Abiit in flammas, Ovid. Consedit in ignes, Virg. Conflagratæ sunt naves, Vitruv.
units.tr: Comburi] To be reduced to ashes. Burnt to ashes, Plin. Reduced to ashes, Lucr. To be set on fire. To burn up with fire, heat or flame. To be utterly burnt by flame, Cic. To be consumed by fire. The flame swallowed up many, Liv. Swallowed up by fire, Tacit. Went up in flames, Ovid. Sank into the fires, Virg. The ships were burnt up, Vitruv.

units.la: Combustio] Exustio. Cic.
units.tr: Combustio] Burning up. Cic.

units.la: Comedere] Consumere, Cic. Commanducare, Plin. Comesum, epotum, exunctum, elotum, &c. Fecisti prandio, Plaut. Epasci, Ovid.
units.tr: Comedere] To consume, Cic. To chew up, Plin. Eaten, drunk up, licked clean, washed away, etc. You have made a meal of it, Plaut. Devoured, Ovid.

units.la: Comedo] Heluo, Cic. Catillo, Fest. Gluto, Perf. Glutus, Scal. Lurco, Plaut. Lurcones capacis gulæ homines. Venter, Lucil. Rapo, Ulp. Comestor viscerum. Devorator, Var. Mando. Phago, Id. Barathrum, macello. Gurges atque heluo, natus abdomini suo. Patinarius, Suet. Quasi lupus esuriens, Plaut. Homo profundæ & intempestivæ ac sordidæ gulæ, Suet. vid. Edax.
units.tr: Comedo] A glutton, Cic. A dish-licker, Fest. A gobbler, Pers. A guzzler, Scal. A gorger, Plaut. Men of a gullet that can hold a great deal. A belly, Lucil. A gobbler, Ulp. One who eats up his own entrails. A devourer, Varro. A chewer. A phagus, Id. A gulf, a shambles. A whirlpool and a glutton, born for his own belly. A dish-hunter, Suet. Like a hungry wolf, Plaut. A man of bottomless, untimely and filthy gluttony, Suet. See Edax.

units.la: Comes] Comes itineris, Cic.
units.tr: Comes] A companion on a journey, Cic.

units.la: Comes jucundus] Facundus comes in via pro vehiculo est.
units.tr: Comes jucundus] An agreeable companion on the way is, in place of a carriage, a pleasant comfort.

units.la: Comessari] Propinari, Iul. Cap. Vacare epulis. Indulgere abdomini, Suet. Obsonare pollucibiliter, Plaut. Convivia sumptuosa apparare, Mart. Convivia lauta, sumptuosa de die facere, Catul. Cùm funereis illis epulis sepeliisset, quasi sibi parentaret, Sen. Non convivantur, sed justa sibi faciunt, Id.
units.tr: Comessari] To drink to someone's health, Iul. Cap. To be at leisure for feasting. To indulge the belly, Suet. To provide victuals lavishly, Plaut. To prepare sumptuous banquets, Mart. To hold lavish and sumptuous feasts by day, Catul. When he had buried him with those funeral feasts, as if he were holding his own funeral rites, Sen. They do not feast, but perform their own funeral rites, Id.

units.la: Comessatio] Heluatio. Intempestivum convivium, Cic. Tripatinum, summa cœnarum lautitia, Fenestel. Epulas trifariam semper, interdum & quadrifariam dispartiebat, in jentacula, prandia, cœnas, & comessationes, Suet. in Vitel.
units.tr: Comessatio] Revelry. An untimely banquet, Cic. A Tripatinum, the greatest luxury of dinners, Fenestel. He always divided his feasts into three parts, and sometimes into four: into breakfasts, lunches, dinners and revels, Suet. in Vitel.

units.la: Comessator] Popino, Suet. Natta, (& nacca) discinctus, Perf. Tabernarius, Apul. Mapalia, Sen. Mera mapalia fecistis, i. dissolutè vixistis, Lurco, Plaut. Asotus, Cic. Lustro, Næv. vid. Comedo.
units.tr: Comessator] A reveller, Suet. Loose, ungirdled, Pers. A tavern-hanger, Apul. Huts, Sen. You have made pure huts, that is, you have lived dissolutely. A glutton, Plaut. A spendthrift, Cic. A debauchee, Naev. See Comedo.

units.la: Cometa] Crinita stella, Cic. Stella comans, Ovid. Stellæ cincinnatæ, magnarum calamitatum prænuntiæ, Cic. Flamma comas imitata, tenuesque capillos, Manl. Regnorum eversor rubuit letale cometes, Lucan. Crinemque timendi sideris, & terris mutantem regna cometem, Val. Argon. Ferales calamitatum nuntii, Regnorumque eversores horrifici.
units.tr: Cometa] A comet, a star with hair, Cic. A hairy star, Ovid. Curled stars, heralds of great calamities, Cic. A flame imitating hair and thin locks, Manl. The comet, destroyer of kingdoms, blushed with deadly light, Lucan. And the comet, a dreaded star with hair, changing kingdoms on the earth, Val. Argon. Deadly messengers of calamities, and dreadful destroyers of kingdoms.

units.la: Comicus] Scenicus artifex, Cic. Scenilis, Lucr.
units.tr: Comicus] A stage performer, Cic. Of the stage, Lucr.

units.la: Cominus] Ad pila ubi ventum est. Propè intueri, Cic. De proximo, Plaut. Ex vicino, Col. E proximo, Plaut. Ad manum intueri, Vitr. De prope, apud Ter.
units.tr: Cominus] At spear-range, where it came to the javelins. To look on closely, Cic. From close at hand, Plaut. From a neighbour, Col. From nearby, Plaut. To look at by hand, Vitr. From near, in Ter.

units.la: Comis] Nemo Catone commodior, nemo comior fuit. Commodis moribus homo, Cic. Liquidus homo. Liquidiusculus quàm ventus Favonius, Plaut. Liquidus animus, Id. Oleo tranquillior, Er.
units.tr: Comis] No one was more courteous than Cato, no one more affable. A man of courteous manners, Cic. A smooth man. Smoother than the west wind, Plaut. A smooth mind, Id. Calmer than oil, Erasm.

units.la: Comitari] Comitem se præbere. Prosequi. Ornare frequentiâ egressum alicujus. Deducere in domum, Cic. Ire ad latus. Comitari iter alicujus, Virg.
units.tr: Comitari] To show oneself a companion. To accompany. To honour someone's departure with a crowd. To escort home, Cic. To go at someone's side. To accompany someone's journey, Virg.

units.la: Comitas] Facilitas. Popularitas. Humanitas. Affabilitas. Benignitas, Er.
units.tr: Comitas] Affability. Popularity. Humanity. Friendliness. Kindness, Erasm.

units.la: Comitatus] Commeatus, cuneatim stipatus, Apul.
units.tr: Comitatus] Provisions, crowded together in wedges, Apul.

units.la: Comitatus, a, um] Benè comitatus conscendit. Magno comitatu, Cic. Uno puero sum comitatior, Id.
units.tr: Comitatus, a, um] Well accompanied, he mounted. With a great retinue, Cic. I am more accompanied than with a single boy, Id.

units.la: Comiter] Blandè, Ter. Perblandè, Mart. Benigniùs. Perbenigne. Suaviter respondere, Cic. Leniter. Placidè accepta oratio, Liv. Affabiliter, Macrob. Affabilissimè, Gell. Placabiliter, Id. Mitiùs, Ovid. Mitissimè, Cæf. Molliter. Molli brachio, Mansuetè, Indulgenter. Civiliter, Cic.
units.tr: Comiter] Flatteringly, Ter. Very flatteringly, Mart. More kindly. Very kindly. To answer pleasantly, Cic. Gently. A speech received calmly, Liv. Affably, Macrob. Most affably, Gell. Appeasingly, Id. More mildly, Ovid. Most mildly, Caes. Softly. With a soft arm. Gently, meekly, indulgently. Civilly, Cic.

units.la: Comitia] Deorum concio. Comitiatus. Concilium, Cic.
units.tr: Comitia] An assembly of the gods. An assembly of the people. A council, Cic.

units.la: Comitia habere] Concilium habere. Comitia gerere, facere, obire, peragere, Cic.
units.tr: Comitia habere] To hold an assembly. To hold, carry out, conduct and complete elections, Cic.

units.la: Commeatus] Æsopicum onus. Pabulum, Tac. Condita. Annonaria provisio, Spart.
units.tr: Commeatus] An Aesopian burden. Fodder, Tac. Stored goods. Provision of the public stores, Spart.

units.la: Commemorare, vid. Memorare.
units.tr: Commemorare, see Memorare.

units.la: Commendabilis] Habet commendationem, Cic.
units.tr: Commendabilis] Has a recommendation, Cic.

units.la: Commendare aliquid] Commendare aliquem alicui diligentissimè. Commendationem facere. Me, & meos commendatos habe, vel habebis. Omnibus rebus eos habeas à me commendatissimos. Tibi omnia commendatissima esse cupio. Munus augere verbis. Rem laudando augere. Commendare aliquem alicui de meliori notâ, Cic. Ornare verbis munus, Ter. Insinuare aliquem alicui, Suet. Lenocinari, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Commendare aliquid] To commend someone to someone most diligently. To make a recommendation. Hold me and mine commended, or you will hold them so. In all matters hold them most highly commended by me. I wish that everything be most commended to you. To increase a gift with words. To increase a thing by praising it. To commend someone to someone with the best credentials, Cic. To adorn a gift with words, Ter. To insinuate someone to someone, Suet. To flatter, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Commendare male] Colorare in pejus. Vertere aliquid in pejorem partem, Cic. Vertere in crimen, Liv. Mittere aliquem in sermones & fabulas, Quint. In deterius augere, Tacit. Insimulans homines fraudandi causa discessisse, Cic.
units.tr: Commendare male] To colour for the worse. To turn something into the worse sense, Cic. To turn into a charge, Liv. To send someone into gossip and tales, Quint. To increase for the worse, Tacit. Accusing men of having left in order to defraud, Cic.

units.la: Commentarius] Libellus memorialis, Diurni commentarii. Ephemeris, Suet. Libri liturarii, Ausn. Scholion, Cic.
units.tr: Commentarius] A memorial booklet. Daily commentaries. A journal, Suet. Account-books, Ausonius. A scholium, Cic.

units.la: Commentator] Interpres rerum obscurarum. Explanator. Explicator, Cic. Paraphrastes, Gell. Scholiastes. Glossematicus, Cæl. Rhod.
units.tr: Commentator] An interpreter of obscure matters. An explainer. An expounder, Cic. A paraphrast, Gell. A scholiast. A glossator, Cael. Rhod.

units.la: Commentitius] Res fictæ & adumbratæ. Simulatus. Fucatus, quæsitus, Cic. Imaginarius, Liv.
units.tr: Commentitius] Matters invented and sketched out. Feigned. Painted over, sought out, Cic. Imaginary, Liv.

units.la: Commentum] Ingenium, Plin. Iun. Figmentum, Plin. Portenta Poëtarum. Machinatio & solertia, Cic.
units.tr: Commentum] Invention, Plin. Iun. A fabrication, Plin. The monstrosities of the poets. Contrivance and cleverness, Cic.

units.la: Commilito] Commiles, Cæs. Contubernalis militiæ, Cic. Turmalis, Liv. Commanipulo, Bud. Commanipularis. Ejusdem commilitii, Tacit. Conturmalis, Amm, Centurialis, Fest.
units.tr: Commilito] A fellow soldier, Caes. A comrade in arms, Cic. A soldier of the same troop, Liv. A fellow of the same maniple, Budé. A fellow of the same maniple. Of the same military service, Tacit. A fellow of the same squadron, Ammian. A fellow of the same century, Fest.

units.la: Comminisci] Effingere aliquid animo. Excogitare ingenio. Depromere ex suo sensu aliquid. Fingere aliquid cogitatione. Depingere cogitatione. Architectari. Commoliri dolum, aut machinam, Cic. Ut cito commentatus es, Plaut. Machinari, Lucr. Consomniare, Plaut.
units.tr: Comminisci] To form something in the mind. To devise by ingenuity. To draw something out of one's own sense. To invent something in thought. To depict in thought. To contrive. To plot a trick or a device, Cic. As quickly as you have contrived it, Plaut. To scheme, Lucr. To dream up, Plaut.

units.la: Comminuere] Frangere in micas, Plin. Minutatim comminuere. Destringere. Refringere. Concidere minutim, & minutè, Col. Concidere in minuta, Plin. Friare terram, Var. Frendere fruges saxo altius, Seren.
units.tr: Comminuere] To break into crumbs, Plin. To crush into small pieces. To split. To break up. To cut up small and finely, Col. To cut into little pieces, Plin. To break up the earth, Varro. To grind grain with a stone more deeply, Seren.

units.la: Commissere, vid. Miscere.
units.tr: Commissere, see Miscere.

units.la: Commiseratio] Miseratio. Misericordia, Cic. Cordolium, Plaut. Motus misericordiæ, Vlp.
units.tr: Commiseratio] Pity. Compassion, Cic. Grief, Plaut. An impulse of pity, Ulp.

units.la: Commiseratio seria] Cruciatum proprium in aliena miseria quærit.
units.tr: Commiseratio seria] Seeks its own torment in another's misery.

units.la: Commiseratio simulata] Crocodili lacrymæ. Ad novercæ tumulum flere.
units.tr: Commiseratio simulata] Crocodile tears. To weep at a stepmother's tomb.

units.la: Commiseratio facile transit] Cito arescit lacryma in alienis malis, Cic. Curt.
units.tr: Commiseratio facile transit] A tear dries quickly at another's misfortunes, Cic.; Curt.

units.la: Commiserescere] Miserēri alicujus. Miseret me alicujus. Affici alicujus casu. Moveri, commoveri misericordia. Ex tuis incommodis magnam animo capio molestiam. Misericordia me alicujus tenet. Frangi misericordia. Allici ad misericordiam. Misericordiam alicui tribuere, impertiri, Cic. Commiseror alicujus interitum, Gell. Commiserescit me alicujus, Ter. Duci misericordia. Exercere misericordiam, Vlp. Dii nos respiciant, Cic. Aspicere. Jupiter aspice nos, Virg. Indolere malis alicujus, Ovid.
units.tr: Commiserescere] To pity someone. It moves me with pity for someone. To be affected by someone's misfortune. To be stirred, moved to compassion. I take great vexation in my mind from your troubles. Pity for someone holds me. To be broken by pity. To be drawn to compassion. To grant, bestow pity on someone, Cic. I pity someone's death, Gell. It moves me to pity someone, Ter. To be led by pity. To exercise mercy, Ulp. May the gods look upon us, Cic. To behold. Jupiter, look upon us, Virg. To grieve at someone's misfortunes, Ovid.

units.la: Commissarius vox ficta, vid. Delegatus Iudex.
units.tr: Commissarius, an invented word, see Delegatus Iudex.

units.la: Committere aliquid alicui] Committere aliquid potestati alicujus. Commendare. Permittere alicui negotium. Deferre, dare negotium alicui. Delegare curas, laborem, provinciam. Imponere, dare partes alicui, Cic. Transmittere alicui bellum, Id. Credere summam belli puero, Virg. Dedere alicui negotium. Tradere provinciam, Ter. Lampada tradere, Varr. vid. Delegare aliquid.
units.tr: Committere aliquid alicui] To entrust something to someone's power. To commend. To grant someone a business. To hand over, give a business to someone. To delegate cares, labour, a province. To impose, to give a part to someone, Cic. To pass a war on to someone, Cic. To entrust the command of a war to a boy, Virg. To give someone a business. To hand over a province, Ter. To hand over the torch, Varro. See Delegare aliquid.

units.la: Commodare aliquid alicui] Dare utendum aliquid, Cic. Dare foras aliquid, Plaut. Accommodare ædes ad nuptias, Cic. Commoditare, Catul.
units.tr: Commodare aliquid alicui] To give something to someone for use, Cic. To lend something out, Plaut. To fit out a house for a wedding, Cic. To lend, Catul.

units.la: Commode] Percommodè cadit. Non incommodè accidit. Nihil fieri potest commodius & aptius, Cic. Vid. Opportunè.
units.tr: Commode] It falls out very conveniently. It does not happen inconveniently. Nothing can be done more conveniently and fittingly, Cic. See Opportune.

units.la: Commoditas, vid. Opportunitas.
units.tr: Commoditas, see Opportunitas.

units.la: Commodum, vid. Vtilitas.
units.tr: Commodum, see Utilitas.

units.la: Commodum omne, habet suum incommodum] Omnis commoditas sua fert incommoda secum. Non est piscis sine spinâ. Non est triticum sine paleâ. Non apis sine acu-leo. leo. Non prodest quod non laedere possit idem, Ovid.
units.tr: Commodum omne, habet suum incommodum] Every advantage brings its own disadvantage with it. There is no fish without a spine. There is no wheat without chaff. There is no bee without a sting. What does not harm cannot profit, the same thing, Ovid.

units.la: A quo nihil Commodi, ab eo non sit incommodum] Non me adurat ignis qui me non calefacit.
units.tr: A quo nihil Commodi, ab eo non sit incommodum] The fire that does not warm me does not burn me.

units.la: Commodus, vid. Opportunus.
units.tr: Commodus, see Opportunus.

units.la: Commotio] Commotiuncula è morbo. Conquassatio valetudinis corporis, Cic. Motiuncula, Sen.
units.tr: Commotio] A slight disturbance from illness. A shaking of the body's health, Cic. A slight movement, Sen.

units.la: Communis] Promiscuus usus. Compascuus ager, Cic. Publicus, Plaut. Obvius, expositus, Plin. Collativus favor aliquorum, Macr. Mutua voluntas, Cic.
units.tr: Communis] Common use. A common field, Cic. Public, Plaut. Open to all, exposed, Plin. A favour shared by some, Macrob. Mutual goodwill, Cic.

units.la: Communia mala] Commune naufragium. Commune solatium. Gaudia sunt miseris, socios habuisse doloris. Miserum est ex aliena miseria solatium, Cic.
units.tr: Communia mala] A common shipwreck. A common comfort. Joys are for the miserable, to have had companions in grief. It is a comfort in another's misery to be wretched, Cic.

units.la: Communia leviora] Facile fertur, quod omnibus commune est.
units.tr: Communia leviora] What is common to all is easily borne.

units.la: Communitas] Ad civilem communitatem conjuncti sumus. Commune, Cic. Universitas, Bud. Corpus, Liv. Communio est inter eos legis, Cic. Commercium, communicatio utilitatum inter, Id.
units.tr: Communitas] We are joined in civil community. The common good, Cic. The whole body, Budé. A body, Liv. There is a common bond of law between them, Cic. Exchange, a sharing of advantages between, Id.

units.la: Communiter, vid. Vulgò, Mutuo.
units.tr: Communiter, see Vulgo, Mutuo.

units.la: Comædia] Scena. Spectaculum, Suet.
units.tr: Comoedia] A stage. A spectacle, Suet.

units.la: Comædus] Scenicus artifex. Tragoedus, Cic. Actor scenicus, Quint. Persona de mimo, Cic.
units.tr: Comoedus] A stage performer. A tragic actor, Cic. A stage actor, Quint. A mime's character, Cic.

units.la: Compages] Coagmentatio. Constructio corporis hominis. Compactio membrorum. Concretio corporum. Commissura ossium. Colligatio naturalis. Cohaerentia mundi, Cic. Coagmentum parietum, Vitr. Compago laterum, Stat. Contextio, Boët. Junctura artis latens, Plin. Textura. Compositura, Lucr. Coagulum, Var.
units.tr: Compages] A joining together. The construction of the human body. The fitting together of limbs. The knitting of bodies. The joining of bones. A natural bond. The cohesion of the world, Cic. The joining of walls, Vitr. The joint of bricks, Stat. A weaving together, Boëthius. A hidden joint of art, Plin. A texture. A composition, Lucr. A coagulum, Varro.

units.la: Comparare, assimilare] Contentionem aliquorum hominum facere. Contendere rem aliam cum alia, Cic. Contendere vetera & praesentia, Tacit. Assimilare parvis grandia, Ovid. Magna componere parvis, Virg. Aequiparare aliquem alicui, Liv. Conferre exempla, Ter. Componere aliqua inter se, Quint.
units.tr: Comparare, assimilare] To make a comparison of certain men. To set one thing against another, Cic. To set ancient and present things against each other, Tacit. To liken great things to small, Ovid. To compare great things with small, Virg. To match someone with someone, Liv. To bring examples together, Ter. To set things side by side, Quint.

units.la: Comparari cum illo nequit] Indignus, qui illi calceos detrahat.
units.tr: Comparari cum illo nequit: He is not worthy to unloose his shoes.

units.la: Non me comparato huic aut illi] Non sum unus ex istis heroibus.
units.tr: I am not to be compared with this man or that: I am not one of those heroes.

units.la: Comparata res talis, vel talis] Absente graculo corvus pul-cher.
units.tr: Comparata res talis, vel talis: With the jay absent, the raven is fine.

units.la: Comparatio inaequalium] Formica camelus.
units.tr: Comparatio inaequalium: An ant compared with a camel.

units.la: Comparare sibi aliquid] Conficere, Emere, Parare aliquid alicui. Cic. Auctorare sibi mortem, Paterc.
units.tr: Comparare sibi aliquid: To procure, buy, or prepare something for oneself or another. Cic. To procure death for oneself. Paterc.

units.la: Comparere] Sistere se, Vlp. Respondere citatum, Vadimonium obire, sistere. Obire diem, Cic. Respondere ad nomina, Liv. Obire ad vadimonium, Plin. Ad constitutum venire, Varr.
