units.tr: Comparere: To present oneself. Vlp. To answer a summons, to give bail and appear. To answer a day. Cic. To answer the roll call. Liv. To appear for bail. Plin. To come to an appointment. Varr.

units.la: Compedes injicere] Indere alicui compedes, catenas, Plaut. Compedibus coercere, Suet. Compedire pedes corrigiis, Varr. Impingere alicui compedes, Plaut.
units.tr: Compedes injicere: To put fetters on someone. Plaut. To restrain with shackles. Suet. To fasten feet with thongs. Varr. To clap fetters on someone. Plaut.

units.la: Compedibus liberare] Exsolvere compedes, Stat. Expedire aliquem. Adimere compedes, Plaut.
units.tr: Compedibus liberare: To loosen fetters. Stat. To release someone. To remove fetters. Plaut.

units.la: Compeditus] Compede vinctus, Ovid. Cruricrepidae. Ferriteri, Compedium tritor, Plaut. Innexus compedibus, Col.
units.tr: Compeditus: Bound in fetters. Ovid. Leg-rattling. Iron-worn, one who wears down fetters. Plaut. Fastened in fetters. Col.

units.la: Compellare, vid. Alloqui.
units.tr: Compellare, see Alloqui.

units.la: Compendium] Summarium, Sen. Breviarium, Plin. Epitome, Cic. Summa rerum ad titulos opposita, Firm. Aphorismus, Gal. Praecisa narratio, Quint.
units.tr: Compendium: A summary. Sen. An abridgement. Plin. An epitome. Cic. A summary of matters set under headings. Firm. An aphorism. Gal. A condensed narrative. Quint.

units.la: Compendium utile] Magnus liber magnum malum.
units.tr: Compendium utile: A big book is a big evil.

units.la: Compensare] Rependere gratiam facto, Ovid. Repensare, Patere, Resarcire damnum, Col. Exsarcire, Ter. Reconcinnare detrimentum, Caes. Impendium usque ad assem reddere, Plin. Praestare damnum alicui, Cic. Paria facere, Sen. Reficitur, Var. Repraesentat laborem, Bud. vid. Pensare.
units.tr: Compensare: To repay a favour with a deed. Ovid. To repay. Patere. To make good a loss. Col. To make amends. Ter. To make up a shortfall. Caes. To repay an outlay to the last as. Plin. To make good a loss to someone. Cic. To make equal. Sen. He restores it. Varr. He makes up for the labour. Bud. See Pensare.

units.la: Compensatio] Pensatio, Papin. Pensitatio, Plin. Hostimentum, Plaut.
units.tr: Compensatio: A weighing against. Papin. A paying back. Plin. Recompense. Plaut.

units.la: Comperendinare, vid. Differre.
units.tr: Comperendinare, see Differre.

units.la: Comperire] Reperire causas verissimas. Manifesto comperi & manu teneo, Cic. Invenire causam, Ter. Experimentis deprehendere, Quint. Percognoscere, Plin. Perspicere fidem alicujus.
units.tr: Comperire: To find the truest causes. I have clearly ascertained it and hold it in my hand. Cic. To discover the cause. Ter. To detect by experiment. Quint. To learn thoroughly. Plin. To perceive someone's loyalty.

units.la: Compescere] Domare, Cic. Otiosum aliquem reddere. Sedare arrogantiam. Comprimere audaciam. Reprimere furorem. Frangere furorem & petulantiam. Retundere improimprobitatem, Cic. Perdomare provinciam, Liv. Resteda- re morbos, Plin. Edomare, Incidere alicujus nervos, Cic. Constringere alicujus superbiam, Tit. Detonsus est, Claud. Habenas injicere.
units.tr: Compescere: To tame. Cic. To make someone idle. To calm arrogance. To curb audacity. To rein in rage. To break fury and wantonness. To blunt wickedness. Cic. To subdue a province. Liv. To cure diseases. Plin. To cut the sinews of someone thoroughly. Cic. To curb someone's pride. Tit. He has been shorn. Claud. To put on the reins.

units.la: Competenter, vid. Decenter.
units.tr: Competenter, see Decenter.

units.la: Competit hoc illi] Spectat aliquid ad bene vivendum. Pertinet aliquid ad me, tc, &c. Pertinet eo, Cic. Facit ad bonos mores, Ovid. Habet in hac re (vel hic) partes, Ter. Attinet. Hoc te non attingit, Cic.
units.tr: Competit hoc illi: It bears on living well. It pertains to me, etc. It pertains to that. Cic. It promotes good morals. Ovid. He has a part in this matter. Ter. It concerns. This does not touch you. Cic.

units.la: Competitor] Rivalis, vid. Candidatus.
units.tr: Competitor: A rival, see Candidatus.

units.la: Compilare] Expilare fanum, Cic. Effringere thesaurum, Plin. Iun. Refringere cellas, Plaut. Perfringere domum alicujus, Tacit. Spoliare fanum, despoliare templum. Diripere domum. Depeculari aliquem, Cic. Expugnare domum, Horat.
units.tr: Compilare: To plunder a temple. Cic. To break open a treasury. Plin. Iun. To break open storerooms. Plaut. To break into someone's house. Tacit. To despoil a shrine, to despoil a temple, to ransack a house. To strip someone of money. Cic. To storm a house. Horat.

units.la: Compilatus] Suppilatus. Furtum passus, Non.
units.tr: Compilatus: Pilfered. Robbed. Suffered theft. Non.

units.la: Compingere] Conglutinare, Plin. Glutinatur vulnus, Id. Coagmentare, Cic. Conjungere cerâ calamos, Virg. Committere aliquid alicui, Cæs. Solidare fracta, Plin. Iun. Concorporare aliquid. Agglutinare. Ferruminare, Plin. Coadunare. Consolidare, Ulp.
units.tr: Compingere: To glue together. Plin. A wound is glued. Id. To fit together. Cic. To join reeds with wax. Virg. To entrust something to someone. Caes. To make broken things whole. Plin. Iun. To join a body together. To cement. To weld. Plin. To unite. To consolidate. Ulp.

units.la: Compitum] Divortium viarum, Tacit. Quadrivium, Serv. Gruma, Non.
units.tr: Compitum: The parting of roads. Tacit. A crossroads. Serv. Gruma. Non.

units.la: Complanare] Redigere ad æqualitatem, planum. Vid. Æquare. Coæquare. Deplanare.
units.tr: Complanare: To reduce to equality, to level. See Aequare, Coaequare, Deplanare.

units.la: Complementum] Supplementum legionum, Cic. Cæs. Explementum ventris, Sen.
units.tr: Complementum: A supplement of legions. Cic. Caes. A filling of the belly. Sen.

units.la: Complere] Complere ad summum, Col. Supplere, Cat. Explere, Cic. Succenturiare. Integrare, Fest. vid. Implere.
units.tr: Complere: To fill to the top. Col. To supply. Cat. To fill up. Cic. To reinforce with a reserve. To make whole. Fest. See Implere.

units.la: Completus] Expletus omnibus suis partibus & numeris, Cic. Terminata oratio, Id. vid. Plenus.
units.tr: Completus: Complete in all its parts and numbers. Cic. A finished speech. Id. See Plenus.

units.la: Complicare] Plicare chartam, Plin.
units.tr: Complicare: To fold a paper. Plin.

units.la: Complodere] Manus collidere, Quint. Insonare flagello, Virg. vid. Collidere.
units.tr: Complodere: To strike hands together. Quint. To resound with the whip. Virg. See Collidere.

units.la: Componere] Construere. Contexere. Struere verba, Cic.
units.tr: Componere: To construct, to weave together. To arrange words. Cic.

units.la: Componere litigantes] Constituere concordiam. Ad concordiam rem adducere. In pristinam concordiam distractos stos adducere. Sedare, Tollere, Dissipare discordiam, Cic. Reconciliare, Id. Conjungere rursus amantes, Prop. Unum cum alio in gratiam reducere, Quint.
units.tr: Componere litigantes: To establish concord. To bring the matter to agreement. To bring those who were torn apart back into their former concord. To calm, remove, or scatter discord. Cic. To reconcile. Id. To bring lovers together again. Prop. To lead one party back into favour with the other. Quint.

units.la: Compos] Particeps, cic Ter. Consors laboris, Cic. Socius doloris & periculorum, Id.
units.tr: Compos: A sharer. Cic. Ter. A partner in toil. Cic. A sharer of grief and dangers. Id.

units.la: Compositus] Constat ex, Conflatus ex &c. Cic.
units.tr: Compositus: Consisting of, made up of, etc. Cic.

units.la: Compotatio] Concoenatio. Epulatio. Accubatio epularis amicorum. Symposium, Cic. Pollutum. Pollutura, Plaut. Domium, Lucil.
units.tr: Compotatio: A dining together. A feast. A reclining at table of friends. A symposium. Cic. A polluted banquet. Plaut. Domium. Lucil.

units.la: Comprimere] Stringere manu aliquid. Coarctare, Cic. Interprimere, Plaut. Premere capita mordicus, Cic.
units.tr: Comprimere: To grip something in the hand. To confine. Cic. To press between. Plaut. To press heads with the teeth. Cic.

units.la: Comprobare, vid. Approbare.
units.tr: Comprobare, see Approbare.

units.la: Comprobator] Laudator, Approbator, Probator rationis, Cic. Adstipulator vanae opinionis, Val. M. Applausor. Attestator, Plin. Iun. Acceptor, Plaut. Plausor, Hor.
units.tr: Comprobator: A praiser, approver, or approver of an argument. Cic. A supporter of a vain opinion. Val. M. An applauder. An attester. Plin. Iun. An acceptor. Plaut. An applauder. Hor.

units.la: Compromittere] Boni viri arbitrio facere, Cato. Compromissum facere. Arbitrium sumere, Cic.
units.tr: Compromittere: To leave a matter to the judgment of a good man. Cato. To make a compromise. To take up arbitration. Cic.

units.la: Computare] Subducere numerum, summam, calculos alicujus rei, rationem. Ad calculos aliquid reducere. Dimetiri in digitis. Numerum censere, Cic. Rationem inire, Cat. Calculum ponere, Col. Mittere in digitos, Rhod. Dispungere vitae dies, Sen. Numero commetiri, Cic. Comprehendere, Virg. Definire, Cic.
units.tr: Computare: To work out the number, sum, or calculations of a matter; to take account. To reduce something to calculation. To count on the fingers. To assess a number. Cic. To make an account. Cat. To set down the reckoning. Col. To send on the fingers. Rhod. To strike off the days of one's life. Sen. To count up by number. Cic. To comprehend. Virg. To define. Cic.

units.la: Computatio recta] Summa rationum quadrat. Ratio constat, Bud. Ratio argenti comparet, Plaut. Putata ratio, Fest. Numerus est ad amussim, Varr. Convenit ad numerum. Rationes expeditae. Confectae, consideratae, subductae, illatae in aerarium rationes, Cic. Convenit numerus quantum debuit, Ter. Rationibus villici herus subscripsit, Apul. Rationes expunctae & subscriptae, Hermogen.
units.tr: Computatio recta: The sum of the accounts balances. The account stands. Bud. The account of the silver appears. Plaut. The reckoning set down. Fest. The number is exact. Varr. The number agrees. Accounts settled, completed, examined, and entered in the treasury. Cic. The number agrees as much as it should. Ter. The master signed off the steward's accounts. Apul. Accounts struck out and signed. Hermogen.

units.la: Conari] Manibus pedibus, Ter. Magno conatu studioque agere. Contendere nervos. Contendere in aliquâ re. Nervis contendere. Adhibere omnem machinam. Adniti. In hoc laboro, ut. Desudare & elaborare in aliquâ re, Cic. Vid. Eniti.
units.tr: Conari: To try with hands and feet. Ter. To act with great effort and zeal. To strain every nerve. To strive in some matter. To strain with the nerves. To bring every device to bear. To exert oneself. To labour to bring something about. To toil and labour in some matter. Cic. See Eniti.

units.la: Conari non frustra] Agnum lupo eripere.
units.tr: Conari non frustra: To snatch a lamb from the wolf.

units.la: Conatus] Impetus animi, Applicatio, Intentio, Cic. Nervus. vus. Nervulus, Id. Nisus vehemens, Plin. Molimentum, Sisen. Pertinax studium, Intensio, Quint.
units.tr: Conatus: An impulse of mind, application, attention. Cic. A sinew. A little sinew. Id. A vehement effort. Plin. A contrivance. Sisen. A persistent zeal, an intensity. Quint.

units.la: Conatus sine re] Parturiunt montes, nascetur ridiculus mus.
units.tr: Conatus sine re: The mountains are in labour; a ridiculous mouse will be born.

units.la: Concedere libenter] Non invitis manibus dare aliquid. Per me licet. Per me nulla est mora.
units.tr: Concedere libenter: To give something with hands not unwilling. As far as I am concerned, it is allowed. There is no delay on my part.

units.la: Concedamus hoc] Fiat. Sine sic habere, Plaut. Licet. Pone, Ter. Esto. Fac esse. Fac ita esse. Fiat velle. Esto sane. Fac potuisse facile. Positum sit, Cic. Sed fingamus hoc aliter esse, Apul. Finge hominem vivere. Fac ita esse. Ut donemus ita esse. Ut hoc interim tibi concedamus. Ut hoc interim tibi largiar, Er.
units.tr: Concedamus hoc: Let it be so. Let it be thus. Plaut. It is allowed. Suppose it so. Ter. Let it be so. Let it be made so. Let it be willed. Certainly, let it be so. Let it be made easily possible. Let it be laid down. Cic. But let us imagine this to be otherwise. Apul. Suppose a man lives. Suppose it is so. Let us grant that it is so. Let us grant you this for now. I bestow this upon you for the moment. Er.

units.la: Conceptus mentis] Perceptio animi. Comprehensiones rerum. Species & cogitatio. Notio, Cic.
units.tr: Conceptus mentis: A perception of the mind. Comprehensions of things. Image and thought. Notion. Cic.

units.la: Concessio, Vid. Permissio.
units.tr: Concessio, see Permissio.

units.la: Concidere, Vid. Scindere.
units.tr: Concidere, see Scindere.

units.la: Conciliare, Vid. Componere.
units.tr: Conciliare, see Componere.

units.la: Conciliare gratiam sibi vel alicui] Parare sibi gratiam alicujus. Benevolentiam hominum sibi adjungere, colligere. Conciliare animos ad benevolentiam. Facere aliquem alicui propitium. Ponere se, vel aliquem, in gratia vel in gratiam apud aliquem, Cic.
units.tr: Conciliare gratiam sibi vel alicui: To procure someone's favour for oneself. To attach men's goodwill to oneself and gather it. To win minds to goodwill. To make someone well disposed to someone. To put oneself, or someone, in favour with another. Cic.

units.la: Conciliatio] Compositio. Decisio. Pacificatio. Concordia, Cic. Ita res concordia coaluit.
units.tr: Conciliatio: A composing, settling, pacifying. Concord. Cic. Thus the matter has grown together into concord.

units.la: Conciliator] Proxeneta, Mart. Pararius. Intercessor, Sen.
units.tr: Conciliator: A go-between. Mart. A pander. An intercessor. Sen.

units.la: Conciliatrix ] Conciliatricula, Cic. Sequestra stupri, Apul. Quaestuaria mulier, Vlp.
units.tr: Conciliatrix: A little go-between. Cic. A procuress of seduction. Apul. A woman who sells her body for gain. Vlp.

units.la: Concilium] Orbis terrae consilium, Cic. De Romano senatu. Amphyctionum confessus, Er. in Chil.
units.tr: Concilium: The counsel of the whole world. Cic. Of the Roman senate. The assembly of the Amphictyons. Er. in Chil.

units.la: Concinnus] Euterpe concinnior, Er.
units.tr: Concinnus: Euterpe more elegant. Er.

units.la: Concipere aliquid mente] Capit animus aliquid. Comprehendere mente. Complecti, percipere animo, Cic. Intellectum rei capere, Quint.
units.tr: Concipere aliquid mente: The mind takes something in. To comprehend in the mind. To embrace and perceive with the mind. Cic. To grasp the understanding of a thing. Quint.

units.la: Concitare aliquem ad iram] Bilem movere alicui. Oestro concitare aliquem. Adducere aliquem ad indignationem, Cic. Facere, Movere stomachum alicui, Iof. Movere indignationem, Liv.
units.tr: Concitare aliquem ad iram: To stir up someone's bile. To goad someone with a gadfly. To lead someone to indignation. Cic. To make someone's stomach rise. Iof. To move indignation. Liv.

units.la: Concitatus] Turbatus, Turbidus, Perturbatus animi motus. Offensus, Offensior animus, Cic. Turbidus animi, Tacit. Tactus dolore, Ovid.
units.tr: Concitatus: Disturbed, agitated, a perturbed motion of mind. Offended, a more offended mind. Cic. Troubled in mind. Tacit. Touched by grief. Ovid.

units.la: Conclave] Conclavium, Plaut. Seclusorium, Varr. Conseptum, Apul.
units.tr: Conclave: A little chamber. Plaut. A secluded room. Varr. An enclosure. Apul.

units.la: Concludere, Vid. Claudere.
units.tr: Concludere, see Claudere.

units.la: Concludere, conclusionem inferre] Probare, Lucr. Convincere, Colligere, Vincere, Cic. Rationibus confirmare, Quint.
units.tr: Concludere, conclusionem inferre: To prove. Lucr. To convince, to gather, to conquer. Cic. To confirm by reasons. Quint.

units.la: Conclusio] Collectio, Sen. Complexio. Consectarium. Consequentia, Id. Vid. Clausula.
units.tr: Conclusio: A collection. Sen. A complex, a corollary, a consequence. Id. See Clausula.

units.la: Concoquere cibum] Coquere cibum. Perficere. Stomachi calore concoquere, Cic. Conficere. Vincere cibum. Coctionem facere, Plin. Digerere, Celf. In succum & sanguinem convertere.
units.tr: Concoquere cibum: To cook food. To complete. To digest by the warmth of the stomach. Cic. To finish. To overcome food. To cause digestion. Plin. To digest. Celf. To turn into juice and blood.

units.la: Concoquere bene] Stomacho valere, Quint.
units.tr: Concoquere bene: To be healthy in the stomach. Quint.

units.la: Concoctu difficilis] Alienus à stomacho. Parum obsequens stomacho. Cibus valentis materiae, Celf. Difficulter perficiuntur in cibis acria. Vivunt pepones in stomacho, Plin.
units.tr: Concoctu difficilis: Disagreeable to the stomach. Little compliant with the stomach. Food of strong matter. Celf. Sharp foods are digested with difficulty. Melons live in the stomach. Plin.

units.la: Concordare] Bene convenit inter nos, Ter. Concorditer congruere inter se, Plaut. Concordissime cum aliquo vivere. Conjunctis sententiis, Cic. Mutuas operas tradunt. Pariter remum ducunt.
units.tr: Concordare: He gets on well with us. Ter. To agree together harmoniously. Plaut. To live in great harmony with someone. With minds joined. Cic. They offer mutual services. They row together in step.

units.la: Concordia] Mutua defensatio tutissima. Concentus, Trop. Hor. Unanimitas. Consensus atque unitas, Plaut. Conspiratio & concordia. Consensus omnium, Naturae vox est. Consensio omnium, lex naturae, Cic. Unio animorum, Sipont. Mutua opera & officia muniunt amicitiam.
units.tr: Concordia: Mutual defence is the safest protection. Harmony, Trop. Hor. Unanimity. Agreement and unity, Plaut. Common accord and harmony. The agreement of all is the voice of nature. The agreement of all is the law of nature, Cic. A union of minds, Sipont. Mutual services and duties strengthen friendship.

units.la: Concordia res firmat] Funiculus triplex indissolubilis. Concordia res parvae crescunt, discordia maximae dilabuntur.
units.tr: Concordia res firmat: A threefold cord is not quickly broken. Harmony makes small things grow, and discord brings the greatest things to ruin.

units.la: Concorditer] Sine controversia, Ter. Omnes uno ore, Cic. Conspiratius ad arma concurrunt, Iust.
units.tr: Concorditer: Without dispute, Ter. All with one voice, Cic. They rush to arms together in harmony, Iust.

units.la: Concors] Concordia conjunctissimi. Consentiens fama. Consentaneae sibi disciplinae. Congruens. Conspirans consensus. Convenientia inter se omnia, Cic. Consonus interrogationi, Amm. Concinentes inter se mundi partes, Coharentes & aptae inter se res, Cic.
units.tr: Concors: Very closely united in harmony. Agreeing in report. Disciplines consistent with themselves. Corresponding. Harmonious and agreeing. Everything agreeing with one another, Cic. Consistent with the question, Amm. The parts of the world harmonising with one another; things cohering and fitting together, Cic.

units.la: Concredere aliquid alicui] Credere animum suum alicui, ConConsilia sua, Ter. Mandare aliquid fidei alicujus. Concredere aliquid taciturnitati alicujus, Plaut. In fide & religione alicujus aliquid deponere, Cic. Deponere tutis auribus, Hor. Curarum mearum arcana expromo, Lucan. Adscisc-ere aliquem in conscientiam facinoris, Tac.
units.tr: Concredere aliquid alicui: To entrust one's mind to someone. Consilia sua, Ter. To commit something to another's good faith. To entrust something to someone's silence, Plaut. To deposit something in another's trust and loyalty, Cic. To lay it in attentive ears, Hor. I disclose the secrets of my cares, Lucan. To admit someone into the knowledge of a crime, Tac.

units.la: Concrepare] Insonare. Concrepuêre obnixi remi, Virg. Perstrepere, Claud. Increpuit verberis ictu, Ovid. Mutire, vel Muttire, Plaut.
units.tr: Concrepare: To resound. The straining oars creaked loudly, Virg. To rattle, Claud. It cracked with the blow of the whip, Ovid. To mutter, or to mutter softly, Plaut.

units.la: Concrescere, Vid. Coalescere.
units.tr: Concrescere: See Coalescere.

units.la: Concubina] Pellex, Cic. Succuba alieni lecti, Ovid.
units.tr: Concubina: A mistress, Cic. A bedfellow of another man's bed, Ovid.

units.la: Conculcare] Proterere, Cic. Pessum dare, premere, Plaut. Proculcare, Ovid. Opprimere pede aliquid, Cat.
units.tr: Conculcare: To trample underfoot, Cic. To destroy and press down, Plaut. To tread down, Ovid. To crush something under foot, Cat.

units.la: Concupiscentia] Impetus animi non rectus. Ardor cupiditatum. Æstus gloriæ. Libido, Cic. Vid. Cupiditas.
units.tr: Concupiscentia: An impulse of the mind that is not right. Ardour of the desires. Heat of glory. Lust, Cic. See Cupiditas.

units.la: Concupiscere, Vid. Desiderare.
units.tr: Concupiscere: See Desiderare.

units.la: Concurrere] Concursare. Concursus est factus. Convolant multi, confluunt, Cic.
units.tr: Concurrere: To gather in crowds. A crowd has formed. Many flock together and flow in from all sides, Cic.

units.la: Concursus] Concurso rerum fortuitarum. Concursatio puerorum, Cic.
units.tr: Concursus: A chance meeting of events. A crowd of boys running together, Cic.

units.la: Concursus fit] Concurrunt plures. Concursabant noctes diesque armati. Confluunt ad nos causæ. Convolant multi. Affluunt literæ. Celebrantur viæ multitudine legatorum, Cicer.
units.tr: Concursus fit: Many run together. They were running about armed, night and day. Cases flow in to us. Many flock together. Letters pour in. The roads were thronged with the crowd of envoys, Cic.

units.la: Concussio] Contusio, Col. Conquassatio, Cic. Concussura, Tert.
units.tr: Concussio: A bruising, Col. A shaking to pieces, Cic. A violent shaking, Tert.

units.la: Condemnare] Decernere contra rem alicujus. Judicare, Pronunciatio contra aliquem. Configere aliquem. Pronunciavit fecisse videri. Damnare aliquem capitis. Addicere morti. Adjudicare in servitutem alicui aliquem, Cic. Ducijubere, imperare, Suet. Plin. Jun. Statuere de aliquo, Tac. Pronunciare reum capitis videri, Cic.
units.tr: Condemnare: To decide against someone's cause. To judge, a pronouncement against someone. To condemn someone. He pronounced that he seemed to have done it. To sentence someone to death. To hand someone over to death. To adjudge someone to slavery, Cic. To order, to command, Suet., Plin. Jun. To decide about someone, Tac. To pronounce someone to seem liable to a capital charge, Cic.

units.la: Condemnatio, Vid. Damnatio.
units.tr: Condemnatio: See Damnatio.

units.la: Condemnatus] Addictus morti, Cic. Damnatus morti, Lucr. Judicatus debiti, Gell.
units.tr: Condemnatus: Handed over to death, Cic. Condemned to death, Lucr. Adjudged liable for a debt, Gell.

units.la: Condescendere inferioribus] Demittere se ad aliorum mediocritatem, ex Cic.
units.tr: Condescendere inferioribus: To lower oneself to the middling level of others, from Cic.

units.la: Condicere alicui] Oblocare operam suam ad, Just. Locare operam, Gell. Vendere operam: Plaut. Addicere se, vel operam suam alicui mercede, pretio, Cic. Pacisci cum aliquo mercede, Liv. Locare se ad ludos pro manduco, Plaut. Vid. Pacisci.
units.tr: Condicere alicui: To hire out one's labour to someone, Just. To let out one's services, Gell. To sell one's labour, Plaut. To bind oneself to someone, or to hire one's labour to someone for wages or a price, Cic. To bargain with someone for a wage, Liv. To hire oneself out for the games as a fodder-man, Plaut. See Pacisci.

units.la: Condictum, Vid. Pactio.
units.tr: Condictum: See Pactio.

units.la: Condimentum] Conditio ciborum, Cic. Conditura, Sen. Confectura mellis, Col.
units.tr: Condimentum: The seasoning of foods, Cic. A preserving, Sen. A preparation of honey, Col.

units.la: Condire] Imbuere aliquid sapore, Quint. Sapidissimis intrimentis pulmenta condita, Apul. Temperare. Diluere, Plin. Concinnare aquam marinam, Cato, Componere aliquâ conditurâ olivas, Col.
units.tr: Condire: To imbue something with flavour, Quint. Dishes seasoned with very savoury sauces, Apul. To temper. To dilute, Plin. To mix sea water, Cato. To preserve olives with some pickling, Col.

units.la: Condiscipulus] Doctus eodem in ludo. Musæ ejusdem æmulus. Condiscipulatu utens.
units.tr: Condiscipulus: One taught in the same school. A rival of the same Muses. One who shares in the same schooling.

units.la: Conditio] Exceptio contra quam, &c. Cautio. Adjunctio, Cic. Satisdatio, Id. Plin. Cautela, Paul. IC. Infecti damni promissio, Hotom. Evectio, Caj.
units.tr: Conditio: An exception against which, etc. A security. An addition, Cic. A surety, Id., Plin. A precaution, Paul. IC. A promise of indemnity against harm not yet done, Hotom. A removal, Caj.

units.la: Condonare, Vid. Ignoscere.
units.tr: Condonare: See Ignoscere.

units.la: Conducere] In rem esse. Vid. Prodesse.
units.tr: Conducere: To be to one's advantage. See Prodesse.

units.la: Conducere operarium] Conducere mercede diurnâ, Hor. Emere operam alicujus pretio. Locare agrum fodiendum, Plaut.
units.tr: Conducere operarium: To hire a labourer for a day's wage, Hor. To buy someone's labour for a price. To let out a field to be dug, Plaut.

units.la: Conductitius, Vid. Meritorius.
units.tr: Conductitius: See Meritorius.

units.la: Conductus] Mercede conductus, Hor. Cujus opera conducta est. Pretio compositus, Sal.
units.tr: Conductus: Hired for wages, Hor. Whose labour has been hired. Bargained for a price, Sal.

units.la: Confessionarius] A confessionibus.
units.tr: Confessionarius: Of confessions; one who hears confessions.

units.la: Conficere, Vid. Absolvere. Facere.
units.tr: Conficere: See Absolvere and Facere.

units.la: Confidenter, Vid. Animosè.
units.tr: Confidenter: See Animose.

units.la: Confidens] Ipsâ confidentiâ confidentior. Phormione confidentior, Ter. Vid. Audax.
units.tr: Confidens: More confident by his very confidence. More confident than Phormio, Ter. See Audax.

units.la: Confidere in aliquo] Niti viribus alicujus. Ne te urbi committas, Cic. Tantum illi in virtute ejus fiduciæ fuit, Liv. Fidere præsidio, Hor. Spe destinare, Liv. Benè præsumere, Lampr.
units.tr: Confidere in aliquo: To rest on another's strength. Do not entrust yourself to the city, Cic. He had so much confidence in his courage, Liv. To trust in a guard, Hor. To destine by hope, Liv. To presume well in advance, Lampr.

units.la: Configere] Figere aliquid clavis, Plin. Cuneare, Sen. Compaginare pontes, Amm.
units.tr: Configere: To fasten something with nails, Plin. To wedge, Sen. To join bridges together, Amm.

units.la: Confingere aliquid] Confingere crimen in aliquem. Fingas verba, & ea dicas, quæ non sentias. Contexere crimen, Cic.
units.tr: Confingere aliquid: To fabricate a charge against someone. Let your words be made up, and say what you do not think. To weave a charge, Cic.

units.la: Cic. Consarcinare crimina, falsitatem, mendacia, Amm. Componere mendacia, falsitatem, Plaut. Fraudem, Liv. Concriminari adversus aliquem aliquid, Plaut. Ementiri aliquid in aliquem, Cic. Imitari chirographum alicujus, Id.
units.tr: Cic. To patch together accusations, falsehoods and lies, Amm. To invent lies and falsehoods, Plaut. To invent a fraud, Liv. To bring a charge against someone in addition, Plaut. To lie about someone, Cic. To counterfeit someone's handwriting, Id.

units.la: Confirmare] Ratum habere, facere. Ratum, firmum, fixum est, Cic. Vid. Firmare.
units.tr: Confirmare: To hold or make something valid. What is valid, firm and fixed, Cic. See Firmare.

units.la: Confirmatio] Approbatio argumenti, Cic. Adstipulatio gestu rerum, quæ dicuntur, Quint.
units.tr: Confirmatio: Approval of an argument, Cic. Support by gesture for the things being said, Quint.

units.la: Confirmator] Adstipulator. Firmator pacis, Cic. Approbator. Fundus subscritorque legis, Gell. Auctor, Bud.
units.tr: Confirmator: A supporter. A firm establisher of peace, Cic. An approver. A founder and co-signer of a law, Gell. An author, Bud.

units.la: Confiscare bona] Redigere bona alicujus in publicum, in ærarium, Liv. Publicare bona, Cic. Redigere in fiscum, Spart. Fisco applicare, Insulan.
units.tr: Confiscare bona: To bring a person's goods into the public treasury, into the exchequer, Liv. To make goods public, Cic. To bring into the fisc, Spart. To apply to the fisc, Insulan.

units.la: Confiscatus] In commissum, vel in commissi causam cecidit, Ulp. In publicum commissa sunt prædia, Cod.
units.tr: Confiscatus: Fell into forfeiture or into the cause of forfeiture, Ulp. Estates were forfeited to the public, Cod.

units.la: Confisus aliquo] Fretus conscientia. Feci fiduciā tuā. Per rationem fiduciæ, Cic. Fretus Diis, Sal.
units.tr: Confisus aliquo: Relying on one's conscience. I have trusted in your good faith. By the reasoning of trust, Cic. Relying on the gods, Sal.

units.la: Conflagrare] Consumi incendio, Liv. Vid. Comburi.
units.tr: Conflagrare: To be consumed by fire, Liv. See Comburi.

units.la: Conflictus, Vid. Prælium.
units.tr: Conflictus: See Proelium.

units.la: Confluere] Corrivantur torrentes, Plin.
units.tr: Confluere: Torrents flow together, Plin.

units.la: Confœderatus] Fœderatæ civitates, Cic. Fœderi adscriptus. Obligatus fœdere, Liv. Fœdere junctus, sociatus, Ovid.
units.tr: Confoederatus: Confederate states, Cic. Enrolled in an alliance. Bound by a covenant, Liv. Joined and allied by a covenant, Ovid.

units.la: Confringere, Vid. Frangere, Comminuere.
units.tr: Confringere: See Frangere, Comminuere.

units.la: Confugere aliquò] Refugere ad. Conferre se ad præsidium alicujus. Confugere ad sinum alicujus. Uti aliquò perfugio. Ad aliquem tanquam ad aram confugere. In asylum confugere, Cic.
units.tr: Confugere aliquo: To flee for refuge to. To betake oneself to someone's protection. To flee to someone's bosom. To use some place of refuge. To flee to someone as to an altar. To flee to a sanctuary, Cic.

units.la: Confugium, Vid. Refugium.
units.tr: Confugium: See Refugium.

units.la: Confundere] Mutum reddere. Conturbare aliquem. Deturbare aliquem de mente. Dejicere de statu adversarium, Cic. Differre aliquem oratione, dictis, Plaut. Eripere mentem alicui, Virg. Vid. Pudefacere.
units.tr: Confundere: To render speechless. To disturb someone. To throw someone out of his wits. To knock an opponent from his position, Cic. To baffle someone in speech or words, Plaut. To snatch the mind from someone, Virg. See Pudefacere.

units.la: Confuse] Absque ordine sparsim ferri. Permixtè. Confusius, Cic. Confusim, Plin. Incompositè, Liv. Per Satyram abrogare, Fest. Mixtim, Lucr.
units.tr: Confuse: To be carried about scattered without order. Mixedly. More confusedly, Cic. In a heap, Plin. Without arrangement, Liv. To repeal by satire, Fest. Mixed together, Lucr.

units.la: Confusio] Perturbatio vitæ. Conturbatio. Tempestas popularis. pularis. Tumultus. Turbidæ res. Turba. Nox rebus offusa, Cic. Interturbatio animi, Plin. Tragœdias excitare. Turbella, Plaus.
units.tr: Confusio: Disorder of life. Disturbance. A popular storm. Tumult. Troubled affairs. A crowd. Night spread over things, Cic. Inner disturbance of the mind, Plin. To stir up tragedies. A little tumult, Plaut.

units.la: Confusus] Incompositus, Liv. Commistus, Virg. Passiva congeries frumenti, Apul.
units.tr: Confusus: Disordered, Liv. Mixed, Virg. A passive heap of grain, Apul.

units.la: Confutare verbis] Refellere alicujus dicta argumentis. Refutare aliquem re, verbis, testibus. Redarguere. Dissolvere alicujus mendacium. Coarguere errorem. Diluere objecta. Evertere adversaria. Confirmare sua. Frangere, infirmare aliquid. Retundere sermones alicujus. Profligare. Repugnare alicui. Reprimere sermones, impetus, Cic. Revincere crimen, Liv. Repercutere dicta alicujus, Quint.
units.tr: Confutare verbis: To refute someone's words by arguments. To refute someone by deed, words or witnesses. To expose. To dissolve someone's lie. To point out an error. To answer objections. To overthrow the opponent's case. To confirm one's own. To break down and weaken something. To beat back someone's speeches. To overthrow. To oppose someone. To check speeches and attacks, Cic. To refute a charge, Liv. To rebut someone's words, Quint.

units.la: Confutatio] Depressio, Infirmatio actionis. Refutatio. Dissolutio criminum. Reprehensio, Cic. Replicatio, Vlp.
units.tr: Confutatio: A suppression, a weakening of an action. A refutation. A dissolving of charges. A reproof, Cic. A rejoinder, Ulp.

units.la: Congelascere, Vid. Gelascere.
units.tr: Congelascere: See Gelascere.

units.la: Congenitus] Congenus & naturalis honor, Gell. Natalis & ingenita sterilitas, Col. Innata, ingenerata ei probitas. Nativus, Cic. Genitiva nota, Suet. Congeneratus, Varr.
units.tr: Congenitus: A congenial and natural honour, Gell. A natal and inborn barrenness, Col. Innate, inborn uprightness. Native, Cic. A birth mark, Suet. Congenerate, Varr.

units.la: Congerere] Frumentum in tuta loca comportatur, Cic. Regerere culmos in acervum, Col. Densare, Virg. Compilare, Fest. Conglobare, Liv. Vid. Accumulare.
units.tr: Congerere: Grain is carried into safe places, Cic. To heap stalks into a pile, Col. To crowd together, Virg. To plunder, Fest. To gather into a ball, Liv. See Accumulare.

units.la: Congiarum] Donativum, Plin. Sportula, Suet. Corollaria Præmia, Id. Charasticum, Callistr. Panarium. Panariolum, Mart.
units.tr: Congiarum: A donative, Plin. A dole, Suet. Garland prizes, Id. A gift of money, Callistr. A bread basket. A small bread basket, Mart.

units.la: Congredi cum aliquo] Congredi alicui quotidianâ consuetudine, Caf. Congredi aliquem, Plaut. Conferre, contollere gradum, Id.
units.tr: Congredi cum aliquo: To meet someone in daily intercourse, Caf. To meet someone, Plaut. To match one's pace with another, Id.

units.la: Congregare se] Colligunt se ad aciem, Hirt. Locus conventu celebratur. Condensant. Affluunt, Cic. Orbem facere, Salust.
units.tr: Congregare se: They gather themselves into battle line, Hirt. The place is crowded with an assembly. They condense. They flow together, Cic. To form a circle, Sall.

units.la: Congruere] Consonat moribus oratio. Consentaneum est. Respondent paria paribus. Omnia omnibus. Dextra dextris. Quadrat in aliquem, alicui, ad aliquid. Principiis exitus consentiunt. Cor cum oculorum aspectu consentit, Cic. Videsne, ut hæc concinant? Ter. Competit aliquid cum exitu, Tacit. Ars & natura conjurat amicè, Hor.
units.tr: Congruere: The speech agrees with the character. It is consistent. Equal things answer to equal things. All things to all. Right to right. It fits someone, something, or some matter. The endings agree with the beginnings. The heart agrees with the sight of the eyes, Cic. Do you see how these things harmonise? Ter. Something suits the outcome, Tac. Art and nature conspire amicably, Hor.

units.la: Congruentia] Convenientia. Concentus, Consensus naturæ. Conspiratio virtutum, Cic.
units.tr: Congruentia: Agreement. Harmony. Concord of nature. Conspiracy of virtues, Cic.

units.la: Congruus] Consentaneus : Accommodatum aliquid naturæ, ad naturam. Proprium est epistolæ, Cic. Justa ætas, Vlp. Legitima ætas legibus præscripta, Liv. Competens, Vlp.
units.tr: Congruus: Consistent. Something fitted to nature, or adapted to nature. It is proper to a letter, Cic. A fitting age, Ulp. A legal age prescribed by law, Liv. Suitable, Ulp.

units.la: Conjectura] Conjectio, Cic. Conjectatio, Plin.
units.tr: Conjectura: A conjecture, Cic. A guessing, Plin.

units.la: Conjicere] Conjecturam de aliquâ re facere. Conjecturâ duci ad suspicandum. Suspicione assequi. Conjecturâ, animo & cogitatione prospicere. Argumentari & conjecturâ persequi, Cic. Subolet patri. Subsensit, Ter. Colligere ex animo suo, Ovid. De meis venatur verbis. Scire quod nescias, Plaut.
units.tr: Conjicere: To make a conjecture about some matter. To be led by conjecture to suspect. To grasp by suspicion. To foresee by conjecture, mind and thought. To argue and pursue by conjecture, Cic. It is suspected by the father. He had an inkling, Ter. To gather from one's own mind, Ovid. He hunts for meanings in my words. To know what you do not know, Plaut.

units.la: Conjugalis, Vid Matrimonialis.
units.tr: Conjugalis, see Matrimonialis.

units.la: Conjugium] Connubium, Cic. Jugum, Plaut. Conditio, Caj Matrimonium, Cic.
units.tr: Conjugium] Wedlock (connubium), Cic. Yoke, Plaut. Condition, Caj. Matrimony, Cic.

units.la: Conjunctim, Vid. Simul.
units.tr: Conjunctim, see Simul.

units.la: Conjungere, Vid. Compingere. Colligare.
units.tr: Conjungere, see Compingere. To bind together.

units.la: Conjurare] Conjurare in ruinam alicujus, Claud. Conjurationem facere contra aliquem, Cic. Fœderari. Piaculô quôdam fœderantur de Christianis, Oclav. Ap. Minut. Jurare in facinus aliquod, Ovid. Dare & accipere fidem, ex Gr.
units.tr: Conjurare] To conspire to someone's ruin, Claud. To form a conspiracy against someone, Cic. To bind by oath. They bind themselves by some sacrilegious oath against the Christians, Octav. ap. Minut. To swear to some crime, Ovid. To give and receive a pledge, from the Greek.

units.la: Conjuratio, Vid. Conspiratio.
units.tr: Conjuratio, see Conspiratio.

units.la: Conjuratus] Conjuratorum manus permagna. Juratus, Cic. Conspirati, Suet.
units.tr: Conjuratus] A very large band of conspirators. Sworn, Cic. Conspirators, Suet.

units.la: Conjux, Vid. Maritus.
units.tr: Conjux, see Maritus.

units.la: Connivere] Dissimulare. Indulgere, Cic. Apertis oculis transilire, Sen. Vid. Indulgere.
units.tr: Connivere] To dissemble. To indulge, Cic. To overlook with eyes open, Sen. See Indulgere.

units.la: Conniventia] Dissimulatio, Cic. Vid. Indulgentia.
units.tr: Conniventia] Dissimulation, Cic. See Indulgentia.

units.la: Connubia à Deo] Connubia sunt fatalia.
units.tr: Connubia à Deo] Marriages are fated.

units.la: Conqueri, Vid. Queri.
units.tr: Conqueri, see Queri.

units.la: Conquiescere, Vid. Quiescere:
units.tr: Conquiescere, see Quiescere.

units.la: Conquirere] Perquirere vasa, Cic. Pervestigare omnia. Ubi quicquid est, Cic.
units.tr: Conquirere] To search out vessels, Cic. To investigate everything thoroughly. Wherever anything is, Cic.

units.la: Conquisitus] Lecti juvenes, Virg. Delecti viri. Exercitus superbissimo delectu & durissima conquisitione collectus. Vir à viro lectus, Cic.
units.tr: Conquisitus] Picked young men, Virg. Chosen men. An army gathered by a most arrogant levy and the harshest conscription. A man chosen from among men, Cic.

units.la: Consanguineus] Consanguinitate propinquus, Virg. Attingit tingit me sanguine. Conjungi alicui sanguine, Cic.
units.tr: Consanguineus] Related by blood, Virg. He touches, he stains me with blood. To be joined to someone by blood, Cic.

units.la: Consanguinitas] Communio sanguinis, Cic. Vinculum sanguinis, Prop. vid. Prosapia.
units.tr: Consanguinitas] Community of blood, Cic. Bond of blood, Prop. See Prosapia.

units.la: Conscendere currum] Inscendere currum, quadrigas. Corpus saltu subjicere in equum, Virg. Ascendere equum, Suet. In equum, Cic. Escendere vehiculum, Sen.
units.tr: Conscendere currum] To mount a chariot, a four-horse chariot. To throw one's body up by a leap onto a horse, Virg. To mount a horse, Suet. Onto a horse, Cic. To climb into a vehicle, Sen.

units.la: Conscientia] Mille testes.
units.tr: Conscientia] A thousand witnesses.

units.la: Conscientia bona] Conscientia recte factorum. Fides bona. Mens bona. Mens idonea cui credatur, Cic. Murus aheneus nil conscire sibi, nulla pallescere culpa, Hor. Bona conscientia, dulcis nutricula senectutis, Plat. Conscia mens recti, juge convivium. Nullum theatrum virtuti majus conscientia.
units.tr: Conscientia bona] Consciousness of right deeds. Good faith. A good mind. A mind worthy of trust, Cic. An iron wall: to have nothing on one's conscience and to turn pale at no fault, Hor. A good conscience, the sweet nurse of old age, Plat. A mind conscious of right is a continual feast. No theatre is greater for virtue than conscience.

units.la: Conscientia mala] Conscientia maleficiorum, peccatorum, scelerum, Cic. Dolo malo possidere, Hotom. Furiae aliquem agunt. Furiae domesticae assiduae. Mens conscelerata. Mens conscia facinoris, Cic. Conscio animo nihil miserius. Conscientia animum exulcerat. Conscientia crimen prodit.
units.tr: Conscientia mala] Conscience of wrongdoing, sins, crimes, Cic. To possess with evil intent, Hotom. The Furies drive someone. The Furies of the household, constantly. A guilty mind. A mind conscious of a crime, Cic. Nothing is more wretched than a guilty mind. Conscience festers in the soul. Conscience betrays crime.

units.la: Conscientia dubia] Angor conscientiae, Cic. Scrupulus animi, vel in animo, Ter. Scrupulositas, Col. Scrupea religio, Varr.
units.tr: Conscientia dubia] Anguish of conscience, Cic. A prick of the mind, or in the mind, Ter. Scrupulosity, Col. Scrupulous religion, Varr.

units.la: Conscientia accusatrix] Improbum virum vel mus mordeat. Mentem exagitat conscientia.
units.tr: Conscientia accusatrix] Let even a mouse bite the wicked man. Conscience harasses the mind.

units.la: Conscientiam alicui movere] Injicere, Afferre alicui religionem, Cic. Objicere religionem, Plaut. Incutere religionem. Trahere, Vertere in religionem, Liv. Percutere animum suspicione religionis, Sen. Injicere scrupulum, Ter.
units.tr: Conscientiam alicui movere] To cast, to bring religious scruple upon someone, Cic. To throw religion in someone's way, Plaut. To stir up religious scruple. To turn into a matter of religion, Liv. To strike the mind with suspicion of religion, Sen. To put a scruple in, Ter.

units.la: Conscientia tangi] Religionem habere. Habere religioni aliquid. Venit mihi in religionem, Cic. Religio mihi est, Plaut. Incessit me religio, Tacit. Religiosum est id facere. In religionem ea res versa est. Offusa religio oculis & animis Sacerdotum, Liv. Dicebant sibi id nefas esse. Se summa religione teneri, Cic. Constringi religione. Salva conscientia consentire non possum, Sen. Bona fide, Plaut.
units.tr: Conscientia tangi] To have religious scruple. To hold something as a matter of religion. It comes into my scruples, Cic. It is a scruple to me, Plaut. Religious scruple has come upon me, Tacit. It is scrupulous to do that. The matter has turned into a scruple. Religion, spread over the eyes and minds of the priests, Liv. They said it was unlawful for them. That they are held by the greatest religious scruple, Cic. To be bound by religion. Without violating my conscience I cannot consent, Sen. In good faith, Plaut.

units.la: Conscientia liberare] Eximere alicui religionem. Exsolvere aliquem religione, Liv. Tollere religionem. Eximere scru-
units.tr: Conscientia liberare] To take religious scruple away from someone. To release someone from religion, Liv. To remove religion. To remove the scru-

units.la: scrupulum. Evellere alicui scrupulum ex animo, Cic. Exonerare conscientiam, Curt. Exsolvere animum nodis religionum, Lucr. Levare animum religionis, Liv. Rejicere à se religionem, Varr.
units.tr: ple. To pluck a scruple out of someone's mind, Cic. To unburden one's conscience, Curt. To loose the mind from the knots of religions, Lucr. To lighten the mind of religious scruple, Liv. To cast religion off from oneself, Varr.

units.la: Conscientiâ inquietari] Morderi conscientiâ. Conscientiae animi me terrent, Cic. Conscius animus me mordet. Praeteritis admissa annis peccata remordent, Luc. Conscientiam hujus rei ferre non possum, Suet.
units.tr: Conscientiâ inquietari] To be gnawed by conscience. Qualms of conscience terrify me, Cic. A guilty mind bites me. Sins committed in past years gnaw back at me, Luc. I cannot bear the knowledge of this matter, Suet.

units.la: Conscientiam examinare, vid. Descendere in se.
units.tr: Conscientiam examinare, see Descendere in se.

units.la: Conscientiâ aliquem obligare] Illigare aliquem conscientiâ, Tacit. Obstringere aliquem religione, Cic.
units.tr: Conscientiâ aliquem obligare] To bind someone by conscience, Tacit. To bind someone by religion, Cic.

units.la: Conscientiosus] Scrupulosus, Plin. Infixa animo illius est religio, Liv.
units.tr: Conscientiosus] Scrupulous, Plin. His religion is fixed in his mind, Liv.

units.la: Conscius] Conscius culpae facinoris, de re aliquâ, Cic. Conscio mihi aliquid, Hor. Conscius facinori, Cic. Numina veri conscia. Conscia sidera, Conscia silva, Ovid. Vid. Gnarus.
units.tr: Conscius] Conscious of the fault of a crime, concerning some matter, Cic. Conscious of something in me, Hor. Conscious of a crime, Cic. Divinities conscious of the truth. Conscious stars, a conscious forest, Ovid. See Gnarus.

units.la: Conscribere] Regerere res in commentarios, Quint. In literas aliquid dare, Macrob. In literas tradere, mittere, Spart. vid. Scribere.
units.tr: Conscribere] To set things down in commentaries, Quint. To commit something to writing, Macrob. To hand down, to send in writing, Spart. See Scribere.

units.la: Conscriptio] Breviarium, Suet. Breviarium rationum, Vopisc. Inauditiuncula, Gell. Recensio, Cic.
units.tr: Conscriptio] Summary, Suet. Summary of accounts, Vopisc. A little unheard-of thing, Gell. Review, Cic.

units.la: Consecrare] Delubra sanatissimis religionibus consecrata. Facere religiosum. Religare religionibus. Religione devincire. Adstringere sacris, Cic. Inaugurare locum aliquem, Liv. Sacrare Deo, Plin. Initiare ac devovere sacris. Devovere DEO, Cic.
units.tr: Consecrare] Shrines consecrated with the most sacred rites. To make religious. To bind with religious observance. To bind by religion. To bind with sacred rites, Cic. To inaugurate a place, Liv. To consecrate to God, Plin. To initiate and devote with sacred rites. To devote to God, Cic.

units.la: Consecratio] Dedicatio templi, Cic. Sacratio, Macrob. Initia, pl. Liv. Encaenia, pl. Aug. Sanctificatio, in SS.
units.tr: Consecratio] Dedication of a temple, Cic. Consecration, Macrob. Beginnings, pl., Liv. Encaenia, pl., Aug. Sanctification, in SS.

units.la: Consecratus] Religiosum propter sanctitatem depositum, Cic. Magno ritu sacrum est aliquid, Plaut. Consecraneus, Iul. Cap. Initiatus sacris, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Consecratus] Something set apart as sacred because of its holiness, Cic. Something is made sacred by a great rite, Plaut. Consecraneus, Iul. Cap. Initiated into the sacred rites, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Consectio, vid. Sectura.
units.tr: Consectio, see Sectura.

units.la: Consensus] Consensio voluntatum. Convenientia. Conjunctae sententiae, Cic. Unitas, Sen.
units.tr: Consensus] Agreement of wills. Harmony. Joined opinions, Cic. Unity, Sen.

units.la: Consensus sit cum seipso] Qui secum dissentit, nullo modo alio consentiet.
units.tr: Consensus sit cum seipso] One who dissents from himself will agree with no one else in any way.

units.la: Consentire] Uno ore omnes consentiunt. Unâ mente & voce Stoici cum Peripateticis concinere videntur. Convenit inter nos, Cic. vid. Assentiri.
units.tr: Consentire] All agree with one voice. With one mind and voice the Stoics seem to harmonise with the Peripatetics. It is agreed between us, Cic. See Assentiri.

units.la: Consentiens] vid. Congruus, Concors.
units.tr: Consentiens, see Congruus, Concors.

units.la: Consequens] Subsequens annus,Plin. Insequens hora,Cic. Consectarius, Id. Undis sequacibus, Virg. Succenturiatus,Ter. Successorius, Vlp. Instans bellum. Cic. Postprincipia,pl. Var. Reliquum deincipe, vel deincipiti die perlecturum, Apul.
units.tr: Consequens] The following year, Plin. The next hour, Cic. Consectary, Id. Waves following one another, Virg. Reserve, supplementary, Ter. Successive, Vlp. The war at hand, Cic. Postprincipia, pl., Var. The remainder to be read through the next day, or the day after, Apul.

units.la: Consequens est] Colligitur, conficitur, sequitur, concluditur, subsequitur, consectarium est, Cic. Consequentia, pl. Cic.
units.tr: Consequens est] It is gathered, concluded, follows, is inferred; it is a corollary, Cic. Consequences, pl., Cic.

units.la: Consequenter] Subsequenter, Messal. Corvin. Successivè, Spart. Deinceps, Cic.
units.tr: Consequenter] Consequently, Messal. Corvin. Successively, Spart. In turn, one after another, Cic.

units.la: Ex Consequente colligitur antecedens] Ex culmo spica colligitur.
units.tr: Ex Consequente colligitur antecedens] From the consequent the antecedent is inferred. The ear of grain is inferred from the stalk.

units.la: Consequentia, vid. Conclusio.
units.tr: Consequentia, see Conclusio.

units.la: Consequi] Res rem consequitur. Insequi. Succrescere aetati alicujus. Succedit ætas ætati, Cic. Digni succedere in pugnam. Excipit nox diem, Liv. Morbi subeunt, Virg. Subire per vices,Plin, Iun. alicui, Liv. Eventus laetus secutus,Plin. Iun. Supervenit alicui aliquid, Celf.
units.tr: Consequi] One thing follows another. To pursue. To grow up along with someone's age. Age succeeds age, Cic. Worthy to succeed one another into battle. Night takes over from day, Liv. Diseases come on, Virg. To come in turn, Plin. Iun. To someone, Liv. A happy outcome followed, Plin. Iun. Something comes upon someone, Celf.

units.la: Conferere agrum] Obserere, Cic. Perserere, Plaut. Inserere hortos, Col. Omnibus seminibus arvum complere.
units.tr: Conferere agrum] To sow a field, Cic. To sow through, Plaut. To plant gardens, Col. To fill the ploughland with every kind of seed.

units.la: Conservare] Sustentare valetudinem,notitiâ corporis sui & observatione. Sustinere dignitatem ac decus civitatis. Esse saluti alicui, Cic. Præsto me incolumem, Lamb. Parcere vitam alicui, Gell. Sospitare, Plaut. Salvare, Sipont. Servare incolumes & integros cives, Cic.
units.tr: Conservare] To maintain health by knowledge and observance of one's body. To sustain the dignity and honour of the state. To be the safety of someone, Cic. I present myself unharmed, Lamb. To spare someone's life, Gell. To keep safe, Plaut. To save, Sipont. To preserve citizens safe and whole, Cic.

units.la: Considerare] Ratiocinari. Reputare aliquid. Æstimare. Recolo ipse mecum aliquid. Retractare diligenter, Cic. Recogitare secum, Col. Volvere aliquid in corde. Exputare, Plaut. Volvere cum animo. Agitare cum animo. Trahere animis aliquid,Salust. Putare rem,Ter. Librare,Apul. Pendere. Expendere aliquid. Intendere in aliquid animum, Cic. Ire in cogitationem & dispicere,Sen. Pensare, re, Curt. Penficulare, Gell. Contemplari. Lustrare. Perlustrare. Ponderare aliquid, Cic.
units.tr: Considerare] To reason. To reckon something up. To estimate. I recall something to myself. To review carefully, Cic. To think over with oneself, Col. To turn something over in the heart. To weigh up, Plaut. To turn over in the mind. To revolve in the mind. To take a thing into the mind, Sall. To reckon a matter, Ter. To balance, Apul. To weigh. To weigh something out. To direct the mind to something, Cic. To go into thought and examine, Sen. To weigh a matter, Curt. To scrutinise, Gell. To contemplate. To survey. To survey thoroughly. To ponder something, Cic.

units.la: Considerate] Providè. Judicio & consideratè aliquid factum. Maturo judicio, diligenter, Cic. Perspectè, Plaut. Penficulatè. Vigilatè atque attentè, Gell. Dextrè, Liv.
units.tr: Considerate] Prudently. Something done with judgement and deliberation. With mature judgement, carefully, Cic. Clearly, Plaut. Carefully. Watchfully and attentively, Gell. Skilfully, Liv.

units.la: Consideratio] Ratiocinatio. Contemplatione dignissima res. Circumspectio, Cic. Pensatio, Gell. Reputatio, Plin. Dispectus, Sen. Examinatio parium momentorum, Arnob.
units.tr: Consideratio] Reasoning. A matter most worthy of contemplation. Circumspection, Cic. Weighing, Gell. Reckoning, Plin. Survey, Sen. Examination of equal weights, Arnob.

units.la: Consideratus] Prudens. Perspicax, Cic. Multum videt. Providus. Providens, Id. Sensatus, Firm. Providentissimus, Plin. Iun. Provisor, Hor.
units.tr: Consideratus] Prudent. Perceptive, Cic. Sees much. Provident. Foreseeing, Id. Sensible, Firm. Most provident, Plin. Iun. Provider, Hor.

units.la: Consignare] Consignare aliquid literis, literis publicis. Commendare monumentis ad memoriam, Cic. Signare stylo, Paterc. Excipere notis, Suet.
units.tr: Consignare] To record something in writing, in public records. To commit to memory in monuments, Cic. To mark with a stylus, Paterc. To note down with signs, Suet.

units.la: Consignatio] vid. Assignatio.
units.tr: Consignatio, see Assignatio.

units.la: Consiliarius] Consiliorum socius, Moderator, Dux, Cic. Consultor, Sal. Consiliator, Plin. Iun. A consiliis, In consilio Imperatori est, Lampr.
units.tr: Consiliarius] Companion in counsels, adviser, leader, Cic. Consultant, Sal. Counsellor, Plin. Iun. Of the council: he is in the emperor's council, Lampr.

units.la: Consilium] Tua ratio est, ut, &c. mea, ut. Consiliarium senatum in corde convocabo, Plaut.
units.tr: Consilium] Your reasoning is that, etc.; mine is that. I will summon a council of senators in my heart, Plaut.

units.la: Consilium ante opus]Ante, quàm incipias, consulito, Salust.
units.tr: Consilium ante opus] Before you begin, take counsel, Sall.

units.la: Consilium post factum ferum] De praeteritis non est deliberandum. Praeterita reprehendi possunt, corrigi non possunt.
units.tr: Consilium post factum] One should not deliberate about past things. Past things can be censured but cannot be corrected.

units.la: Consilium bonum utile] Benè consulta bonos eventus pariunt.
units.tr: Consilium bonum utile] Well-considered counsels bring forth good outcomes.

units.la: Consilium malum noxium] Consilio perit ipse suo consultor iniquus.
units.tr: Consilium malum noxium] The unjust adviser perishes by his own counsel.

units.la: Consilium & auxilium jungenda] Fortuna artem amat, ars fortunam.
units.tr: Consilium & auxilium jungenda] Fortune loves skill, and skill fortune.

units.la: Consilio & vi] Arte & Marte.
units.tr: Consilio & vi] By skill and by might.

units.la: Consistere] Subsistere. Inhibere cursum, Ovid. Subsidere in via. Sustentare se, Cic. Sistunt amnes. Hærere in vestigio, Plin. Reprimere, figere pedem, Virg. Reprimere cursum, Caes. Remorari gradum, Plaut.
units.tr: Consistere] To stand still. To check one's course, Ovid. To settle down on the road. To hold oneself up, Cic. Rivers stand still. To remain fixed on the track, Plin. To hold back and plant one's foot, Virg. To check one's course, Caes. To delay one's step, Plaut.

units.la: Consociare, vid. Iungere.
units.tr: Consociare, see Iungere.

units.la: Consolari, vid. Solari.
units.tr: Consolari, see Solari.

units.la: Consolatio] Levatio doloris ac ægritudinis, Cic. vid. Solatium.
units.tr: Consolatio] Relief of pain and distress, Cic. See Solatium.

units.la: Consolatio medicina] Oratio pharmacum optimum. Oratio medicus.
units.tr: Consolatio medicina] A speech is the best medicine. A speech is a physician.

units.la: Consors negotii] Idem trahimus jugum. In eadem es navi.
units.tr: Partner in business] We pull the same yoke. You are in the same boat.

units.la: Conspicillum] Conspicilium, Plaut. Ocularium specillum, Iun. Specillum quo specimus, Var. Iun. (Perspicillia, non est Latin.)
units.tr: Spyglass] A spyglass, Plaut. An ocular instrument, Iun. An instrument through which we look, Var. Iun. (The plural form is not Latin.)

units.la: Conspicuus (1) de re] Apparens. Spectabilis undique, Ovid. Propatulus locus, Cic. Fons in planitie conspicuus, Plin.
units.tr: Conspicuous (1), of things] Apparent. Visible on all sides, Ovid. An open place, Cic. A spring conspicuous on the plain, Plin.

units.la: Conspicuus (2) de persona] Ab aspectu decorus, Col. Spectabilis, Val. Argon. Monstrabilis homo probitate, Plin. Ostensionales milites, Lampr. Præclarus ad aspectum. Ad speciem magnifico ornatu. Eminens effigies virtutis. Speciosa causa, Cic. Conspectior, Liv. Prospicuus, Sen.
units.tr: Conspicuous (2), of persons] Comely in appearance, Col. Notable, Val. Argon. A man remarkable for uprightness, Plin. Conspicuous soldiers, Lampr. Outstanding in appearance. Magnificent in splendid adornment. An eminent image of virtue. A splendid cause, Cic. More conspicuous, Liv. Prominent, Sen.

units.la: Conspirare] Facere conspirationem. Consociare cum aliquo arma, consilia, Liv. Coire. Coitum facere. Coire de alicujus bonis, Cic. Inita factione illum ceciderunt. Factionem cum militibus facere, Iul. Cap. vid. Conjurare.
units.tr: Conspirare] To form a conspiracy. To join with someone in arms and plans, Liv. To come together. To assemble. To gather together over someone's goods, Cic. Having formed a faction, they struck him down. To make a faction with soldiers, Iul. Cap. see Conjurare.

units.la: Conspiratio] Coitio. Conspiratio sceleratissima contra dignitatem alicujus. Consensio scelerata, Cic. Conspiratus, Gell. Factio, Capitol.
units.tr: Conspiratio] A coming together. A most wicked conspiracy against someone's dignity. Wicked agreement, Cic. Conspiracy, Gell. Faction, Capitol.

units.la: Conspuere, vid. Spuere.
units.tr: To spit upon, see Spuere.

units.la: Constans] Perpetua & constans voluntas. Firmus amicus. Stabilis sententia. Constat sibi, Cic. Tenax propositi, Hor. Pertinax recti, Tacit. Perseverantissimus, Col. Solida felicitas, Plaut. Certus consilii. Manent illi semper placita, nec ulla in decretis ejus litura est, Sen.
units.tr: Constans] A perpetual and steadfast will. A firm friend. A stable opinion. He is consistent with himself, Cic. Holding fast to his purpose, Hor. Stubborn in what is right, Tacit. Most persevering, Col. Solid happiness, Plaut. Settled in his plan. Those things that please him always remain, and there is no erasure in his decrees, Sen.

units.la: Ille velut pelagi rupes immota resistit.
units.tr: Like a rock of the sea, he stands unmoved and resists.

units.la: Constans esto] Cubus esto propriæ basi innixus, moveri nescius. Destinatus obdura, Catul.
units.tr: Constans esto] Be like a cube resting on its own base, knowing not how to be moved. Hold firm, resolved, Catul.

units.la: Tu ne cede malis sed contrà audentior ito.
units.tr: Do not yield to misfortunes, but on the contrary go forth more boldly.

units.la: Perpetuo eam opinionem retineas, Cic. Injurias non dejectus, ne motus quidem gradu, sustine, Sen.
units.tr: Keep that opinion steadfastly, Cic. Undismayed by injuries, not even moved from your step, endure, Sen.

units.la: Constanter] Fortiter facta. Perseverantissimè, Plin. Iun. Statim rem gerunt, Plaut.
units.tr: Constanter] Acting bravely. Most persistently, Plin. Iun. They carry out the matter at once, Plaut.

units.la: Constantissimus] Eundem cursum constantissimè tenet. Habet stabilitatem. Constat sibi in sententiâ. In neutram partem movetur, Cic.
units.tr: Constantissimus] He keeps the same course most steadily. He has steadiness. He is consistent in his opinion. He is moved in neither direction, Cic.

units.la: Constellatio] Positura stellarum, Gell.
units.tr: Constellatio] The position of the stars, Gell.

units.la: Consternare] De gradu dejicere. Perpavefacere, Plaut. Exanimare metu, Ter. Perstringere horrore, Liv. Percel-lere pavore pectus. Percutere, Tacit.
units.tr: Consternare] To knock from one's footing. To frighten thoroughly, Plaut. To stun with fear, Ter. To strike with horror, Liv. To strike the breast with fear. To strike down, Tacit.

units.la: Consternari] Expavescere, Cic. Præter modum exterre-ri, Id. Compavescere, Macrob.
units.tr: Consternari] To be alarmed, Cic. To be frightened beyond measure, Id. To be utterly terrified, Macrob.

units.la: Consternatio] Exanimatio, Cic. Cataplexis, Lucr. Hy-drophobos, Cels.
units.tr: Consternatio] Stupefaction, Cic. Cataplexy, Lucr. Hydrophobia, Cels.

units.la: Consternatus, vid. Territus.
units.tr: Dismayed, see Territus.

units.la: Constituere aliquid (1)] Statuere jus, Cic. Cernere. Rogare, Irrogare legem sancire legem, Cic. Præscribere jura civi-bus, Id. Sciscere legem. Scitum facere. Ferre. Destinare. Præsinire. Figere, Id.
units.tr: Constituere aliquid (1)] To lay down a law, Cic. To decide. To propose a law, to impose a penalty by law, to sanction a law, Cic. To prescribe laws to citizens, Id. To pass a law. To make a decree. To bring forward. To appoint. To define. To fix, Id.

units.la: Constituere aliquid apud se (2)] Proponere sibi aliquid. Proponere apud animum. Est mihi propositum. Statuere cum animo, Cic. Propositum habeo ostendere, Varr. Pro-ponere aliquid animô, Liv. Statuere apud animum, Salust. Destinare aliquid agere, Cas. Constitutum, deliberatum, decretum, statutum est mihi, sedet, stat animo sententia, Er. Animum inducere. Suadere sibi, Cic. Decernere, Mart. Cernere, Lucil.
units.tr: Constituere aliquid apud se (2)] To propose something to oneself. To propose in one's mind. I have a purpose. To resolve in one's mind, Cic. I intend to show, Varr. To propose something to the mind, Liv. To determine in the mind, Sallust. To intend to do something, Caes. It is decided, resolved, determined and settled by me; my mind is set on it, Er. To make up one's mind. To persuade oneself, Cic. To decree, Mart. To decide, Lucil.

units.la: Constringere aliquid] Constringere quadrupedem, Ter. Religare, Col. Devincire. Connectere. Coërcere, Ovid. Adstringere, Cic. Plaut. Fraus adstringit, non dissolvit per-jurium, Id. Stringere, Apul. vid. Ligare.
units.tr: Constringere aliquid] To bind a four-footed beast, Ter. To tie up, Col. To bind fast. To connect. To restrain, Ovid. To bind tightly, Cic. Plaut. Fraud binds; it does not dissolve perjury, Id. To draw tight, Apul. see Ligare.

units.la: Consuescere, vid. Assuescere.
units.tr: To become accustomed, see Assuescere.

units.la: Consuetudo] Consuetudo quasi altera natura. Vetus con-fuetudo, institutumque Majorum. Mos. Usus frequens, Cic. Assuetudo, Ovid. Servemus solemne nostrum, Cic. Anti-quum hoc tuum obtines, Plaut. Facere sibi naturam ali-cujus rei, Ter.
units.tr: Consuetudo] Custom is a second nature. Ancient custom and the institution of ancestors. Manner. Frequent use, Cic. Habit, Ovid. Let us keep our solemn custom, Cic. You hold on to this old custom of yours, Plaut. To make the nature of a thing one's own, Ter.

units.la: Consuetudinis magna est vis] A teneris assuescere multum est, Ter. Veteres canes non facilè assuescunt loro. Usus fre-quens omnium magistrorum præcepta superat, Cic. Con-fuetudo altera natura. Ciconia reversa priores repetit ni-dos. dos. Quo semel est imbuta recens servabit odorem testa diu, Hor. Quod nova testa capit, inveterata sapit.
units.tr: Consuetudinis magna est vis] To accustom oneself young is a great thing, Ter. Old dogs do not easily get used to the leash. Frequent practice surpasses the precepts of all teachers, Cic. Custom is a second nature. The stork, returned, seeks its former nests. What the fresh jar has once been steeped in will keep its smell long, Hor. What a new jar takes in, the old jar tastes of.

units.la: Consuetudo est] Est hoc in more positum, institutoque majorum. Mos est, Cic. Moris est plerisque, Quint. More fit, Plaut. Habet hoc moris, Plin. Iun. In patris est moribus. Consuetudo patitur. Comparatum est more majorum. Fert usus eorum. Venit in consuetudinem. Usitatum est, Cic. Receptum est, Lucr. Fert consuetudo, Cæs. Solenne est, Suet. In observatione quondam erat, Plin.
units.tr: Consuetudo est] It is placed in custom and in the institution of ancestors. It is the custom, Cic. It is the custom of most people, Quint. It happens by habit, Plaut. He has this habit, Plin. Iun. It is in the father's manner. Custom allows it. It has been acquired by the custom of ancestors. The practice of those people brings it. It has come into custom. It is usual, Cic. It has been received, Lucr. Custom brings it, Caes. It is solemn, Suet. It was once observed, Plin.

units.la: Pro consuetudine] Moribus. Ut mos est. Moribus antiquis. Usitato more. Usitatè, Cic. Ut assolet, Liv. Solita peccare nolunt, Sen. De more, Virg. Solemnia insanire, Horat.
units.tr: Pro consuetudine] In the manner of. As is the custom. In ancient fashion. In the usual manner. Usually, Cic. As is customary, Liv. They do not wish to sin as usual, Sen. In the customary way, Virg. To go mad in solemn fashion, Horat.

units.la: Consuetus] Consuetissima verba. Familiaris. Pro cætera (consueta) diligentiâ facis, Plin. Usurpatus, Cic. Ordinarius, Suet. Sueta adulatio, Tacit. Solennis, Col. Moribus constitutum, Bud. Solitus mos, Ovid.
units.tr: Consuetus] Most customary words. Familiar. You act with your usual diligence, Plin. Used, Cic. Ordinary, Suet. Customary flattery, Tacit. Solemn, Col. Established by custom, Bud. Accustomed manner, Ovid.

units.la: Consul] Major Magistratus, Fest. Tutor Reip. legitimus. Rector urbis, Amm. Legum præses, Rectorque civitatis, Sen.
units.tr: Consul] A greater magistrate, Fest. A lawful guardian of the commonwealth. Ruler of the city, Amm. President of the laws and ruler of the state, Sen.

units.la: Consulem agere] Gerere consulatum, Cic. Inire tribunatum, Val. Max. Esse consulem, Cic.
units.tr: To be consul] To hold the consulship, Cic. To enter upon the tribunate, Val. Max. To be consul, Cic.

units.la: Consulere aliquem] Consilium alicujus exquirere, petere, interrogare. Adhibere consiliis, in consilium. Referre ad aliquem de re aliquâ, Cic. Adhibere ad consilium, Cæs.
units.tr: Consulere aliquem] To seek, ask for or question someone's counsel. To take counsel with someone. To bring into council. To refer a matter to someone, Cic. To bring into council, Cæs.

units.la: Consulere alicui] Facere copiam consilii alicui. Afferre aliquid consilii. Dare consilium alicui. Censere, Cic. Suadere. Auctor tibi sum, Ter.
units.tr: Consulere alicui] To give someone an opportunity to counsel. To offer some counsel. To give someone counsel. To advise, Cic. To persuade. I counsel you, Ter.

units.la: Consultò] Cogitatò fit aliquid. Studiò. Dedità operâ: de industriâ, Cic. Ex industriâ, Liv. Industriâ, ob industriam, Plaut. Ex præparato, consiliò, Liv. Datâ operâ, Vlp. Consultâ operâ. Professò, Amm. Ex professo, Quint. Destinatò, Suet. Ex destinato; ex proposito, Sen. Ex dispositο, Macrob. Volentes tenuant arma, Virg.
units.tr: Consultò] Something is done by deliberate thought. Carefully. Purposely. By set design, Cic. By diligence, Liv. For the sake of diligence, Plaut. From a prepared plan, from deliberate counsel, Liv. By design, Vlp. Deliberately, Amm. Professedly, Quint. Resolutely, Suet. From settled purpose; from design, Sen. By arrangement, Macrob. Willingly they hold their arms, Virg.

units.la: Consultare de re aliquâ] Consultare & deliberare de, Cic. Consultare aliquid, Liv. alicui, Sallust. Consilium habere, capere de. De consilii sententiâ aliquid facere. Ex consilio alicujus facere. Uti consiliis. Ire in consilium. Consilia conferconferre, Cic. Consociare, agitare, Liv. In secreto cum amicis aliquid volutare, Id. Inire consilium. Communicare alicui, cum aliquo, inter fe aliquid, de. Considerare de, cum aliquo. Conferre capita, Agere cum populo, Cic. Appellare aliquem de &c. Plaut. Consulere in commune, Ter. In publicum, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Consultare de re aliquâ] To consult and deliberate about, Cic. To consult about something, Liv. or someone, Sallust. To hold counsel about. To take counsel. To act on the opinion of counsel. To act on someone's advice. To make use of counsels. To go into council. To confer counsels, Cic. To consult together, to debate, Liv. To turn something over in secret with friends, Id. To form a plan. To share something with someone, or with one another, about. To consider about, with someone. To put heads together. To deal with the people, Cic. To address someone about this and that, Plaut. To consult for the common good, Ter. For the public, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Consultare religiosè] Apud aram consultare.
units.tr: Consultare religiosè] To consult at the altar.

units.la: Consultatio] Consilii capiendi ratio, deliberatio, Cic. Consilium, Virg. Consilium, Virg. Consilium maguis de rebus habebant.
units.tr: Consultatio] The method of taking counsel, deliberation, Cic. Counsel, Virg. Counsel, Virg. They held counsel about great matters.

units.la: Confultus] Consilii plenus. Amicus consiliarius, Plaut. Compos consilii, Cic. Sciens, peritus, à quo consilium petas, Er.
units.tr: Confultus] Full of counsel. A friend who gives counsel, Plaut. Possessed of counsel, Cic. One who knows and is skilled, from whom you may seek counsel, Er.

units.la: Consumere] Absumere vinum, Ter. Depasci possessionem. Expromere industriam, Cic. Præconsumere vires, Ovid. Prodigere, Fest. Perdere rem paternam, Plaut.
units.tr: Consumere] To use up wine, Ter. To graze away an estate. To bring forth one's diligence, Cic. To use up one's strength beforehand, Ovid. To squander, Fest. To lose one's paternal estate, Plaut.

units.la: Confuere] Committere futuris ora vulneris, Celf. Consarcinare, Amm. Suturis crebris aliquid durare, Id.
units.tr: Confuere] To bring the lips of a wound together for future healing, Celf. To patch together, Amm. To make something firm with frequent stitches, Id.

units.la: Contagium] Contagio, Cic. Plaut. Contages, Lucr. Tabes, Salust. Lues morbi, (laud. Gangræna, Varr.
units.tr: Contagium] Contagion, Cic. Plaut. Contagion, Lucr. Wasting, Salust. Plague of disease, (laud. Gangrene, Varr.

units.la: Contagium inficit] Morbida facta pecus totum corrumpit ovile.
units.tr: Contagium inficit] A sickly flock corrupts the whole sheepfold.

units.la: Contaminare] Deformare. Maculare dignitatem suam, Cic. Fœdare, Cat. Lutulare mores majorum, Plaut. Deturpare, Suet. Devenustare pulchritudinis insignia, Gell. Turpare aram sanguine, Lucr. Denormare, Hor. Infuscare maculis aliquid, Virg. Inficit caput senecta, Tibull. Inquinare, Plaut. Decolorare, Suet. Collinere, Plaut. Pulchrum ornatum mali mores pejus luto collinunt, Id. Obsolefacere, Arnob.
units.tr: Contaminare] To deform. To stain one's dignity, Cic. To defile, Cat. To corrupt the morals of the ancestors, Plaut. To disfigure, Suet. To strip a thing of the adornments of beauty, Gell. To stain the altar with blood, Lucr. To make foul, Hor. To darken something with spots, Virg. Age has greyed the head, Tibull. To defile, Plaut. To discolour, Suet. To smear, Plaut. Bad morals smear a fine adornment worse than mud, Id. To make obsolete, Arnob.

units.la: Contaminatio]Inquinamentum. Dehonestamentum, Gell. Deformatio, Liv.
units.tr: Contaminatio] Pollution. Dishonouring, Gell. Deformation, Liv.

units.la: Contemnere] Aspernari aliquem. Per jocum & risum contemnere. Despicere. Negligere Respuere, Cic. Medium unguem alicui ostendere, Mart. Minimo digito provocare aliquem, habere despicatui aliquem, Plaut. Nihil pensi mihi est, Liv. Jubere plorare aliquem, Hor. Mandare alicui laqueum, queum, Iuv. In levi habere, Tacit. Fastidire, Virg. Susque de-que ferre, Plaut. Despectare, Tacit. Despuere mores alicujus, Claud. Dedignari aliquem amicum, Ovid. Conspernari veterem discipulum, Tacit. Despernere opus alicujus, Col. Non pluris illius convitia facio, quàm culicem elephantus Indicus. Pili non facio. Nauci non facio. Pro nihilo ducis. Ne hujus quidem facit. Non hettæ te facio, Fest. Insuper habere. Teruncii non facere, Plaut. Vid. Vilipendere, Nihili facere.
units.tr: Contemnere] To despise someone. To scorn with jest and laughter. To look down upon. To neglect. To spurn, Cic. To show the middle finger to someone, Mart. To challenge someone with the little finger, to hold someone in contempt, Plaut. It is nothing to me, Liv. To bid someone weep, Hor. To hand someone a noose, Iuv. To hold in light regard, Tacit. To disdain, Virg. To take lightly, Plaut. To look down on, Tacit. To spit upon someone's manners, Claud. To disdain a friend, Ovid. To scorn an old pupil, Tacit. To despise someone's work, Col. I value his insults no more than an Indian elephant values a gnat. I do not care a hair for him. I do not care a fig. You take him for nothing. He does not think much of you. I do not value you a rush, Fest. To set aside. I do not care a farthing, Plaut. See To hold cheap and To make of no account.

units.la: Contemni] Jacere in silentio, in oblivione, In nullo numero esse, Cic. Venire in contemptum, in contemptionem, Caes. Jacere in occulto, Plaut. Contemptu apud aliquem laborare. Sordere suis, & contemni ab iis, Liv. Inter inquilinos censeri.
units.tr: Contemni] To lie in silence, in oblivion. To be of no account, Cic. To come into contempt, Caes. To lie hidden, Plaut. To suffer contempt from someone. To be despised by one's own, Liv. To be counted among the lodgers.

units.la: Contemplari] Lustrare. Perlustrare. Omni acie ingenii contemplari acerrimè, intentis oculis, Cic. Speculari ortus signorum, Virg. Noscitabundus accedo, Gell. Obtueri, Plaut. Intueri sagaciter, Quint.
units.tr: To contemplate] To survey, to scan thoroughly. To look over with the full keenness of one's mind and eyes fixed, Cic. To watch the rising of the stars, Virg. I approach looking about me inquisitively, Gell. To gaze upon, Plaut. To look upon sharply, Quint.

units.la: Contemplari se in speculo] Speculum consulere, Ovid. Inspicere in speculum, Ter. Formam suam explorare spectaculo assiduo, Apul. Cantharus & lanx ostendent tibi te, Hor. Faciem quaerere in speculo, Macrob. In littore se videre, Virg.
units.tr: To contemplate oneself in a mirror] To consult the mirror, Ovid. To look into the mirror, Ter. To study one's own appearance by constant looking, Apul. The cup and the dish will show you yourself, Hor. To seek one's face in the mirror, Macrob. To see oneself on the shore, Virg.

units.la: Contemplatio] Animus in hac unâ contemplatione defixus, Plin. Suspectus donorum, Ovid. Ad tantæ rei speculam me praeparem, Apul. Spectaculum rerum coelestium, Cic.
units.tr: Contemplation] A mind fixed upon this one contemplation, Plin. One who is suspicious of gifts, Ovid. I prepare myself to stand as a lookout over so great a matter, Apul. A spectacle of heavenly things, Cic.

units.la: Contemplator] Spectator naturæ, Cic. Contemplativus, Sen. Admirator, Id.
units.tr: Contemplator] An observer of nature, Cic. Contemplative, Sen. An admirer, Id.

units.la: Contemptus] Contemptio. Despectus. Despicatus. Despicatio, Cic. Fastidium, Quint. Despicientia, Cic. Dedignatio, Quint.
units.tr: Contempt] Disdain, scorn. Contemptio. Despectus. Despicatus. Despicatio, Cic. Disdain, Quint. Despicientia, Cic. Scorn, Quint.

units.la: Contemptus, a, um, vid. Abjectus.
units.tr: Contemptus, a, um, see Abjectus.

units.la: Contendere] Altercari cum altero, In contentionem & discrimen venire. Vocas aliquid in controversiam, in disceptationem, in contentionem, Cic. Altercare. Commutare verba, Ter. Controversari. Certare cum aliquo de. Certare inter se. Concertare cum aliquo. Confligere cum aliquo. Conflictari verbis, Cic. Habere certamen cum aliquo. quo. Facere controversiam, Liv. In disceptationem venire, Id. Dissertare de aliquâ re, Gell. vid. Altercari.
units.tr: To contend] To quarrel with another, to come into conflict and danger. You bring a matter into dispute, into debate, into contention, Cic. To wrangle, to exchange words, Ter. To dispute about something. To strive with one another. To struggle with someone. To clash with someone. To fight with words, Cic. To have a contest with someone. To make a controversy, Liv. To come into debate, Id. To discourse on some matter, Gell. See Altercari.

units.la: Contentio] Concertatio. Altercatio. Disceptatio. Certamen. Controversia. Certatio. Discrimen, Cic. Dissertatio, Plin. Disputatio litigiosa, Cic.
units.tr: Contention] Strife. Wrangling. Debate. Combat. Controversy. Struggle. Peril, Cic. Discourse, Plin. A quarrelsome disputation, Cic.

units.la: Contentio est de eo] Venit aliquid in controversiam, in contentionem, in certamen. Est aliquid in controversiâ. Cadit in disceptationem. Certamen est inter &c. Ambigitur, Cic. Venit aliquid in disceptationem. Factantur disceptationes. Vertitur utrum &c. Liv. Vocatur in contentionem, controversiam, Cic.
units.tr: There is contention about it] A matter comes into controversy, into contention, into conflict. It is under dispute. It falls into debate. There is a contest between etc. It is in question, Cic. A matter comes into debate. Debates are stirred up. It is turned whether etc., Liv. It is called into contention, into controversy, Cic.

units.la: Contentiosè] Pugnacissimè, Cic. Pugnaciter, Quint. Controversè, Litigiosè, Sipon.
units.tr: Contentiously] Most pugnaciously, Cic. Pugnaciously, Quint. Controversially, litigiously, Sipon.

units.la: Contentiosus] Concertatorius. Refractariolus. Pugnax, Controversus. Litigiosus homo, perpugnax, repugnans, Cic. Altercabilis sermo, Arnob.
units.tr: Contentious] Fond of strife. Stubborn. Pugnacious, controversial. A litigious man, very combative, resisting, Cic. A contentious discourse, Arnob.

units.la: Contentum esse] Æqui bonique consulere, facere. Contentum esse suis rebus, maximæ sunt divitiæ. Conquiescere, Cic. Parvo naturæ dimittitur, Sen. Æquum discedere. Æqui placatique discesserunt, Quint. Abeat per gratiam. Habere satis, Plaut.
units.tr: To be content] To take things in good part and make the best of them. Being content with one's own lot is the greatest wealth. To rest content, Cic. He is dismissed with little of nature, Sen. To depart on fair terms. They departed fairly and reconciled, Quint. Let him go with goodwill. To have enough, Plaut.

units.la: Contentum esse præsentibus] Contenti simus hoc Catone, Aug. Cæs.
units.tr: To be content with present things] Let us be content with this Cato, Aug. Caes.

units.la: Continere se] Continentia. Continens. Vid. Abstinere.
units.tr: To restrain oneself] Continence. Continent. See Abstinere.

units.la: Conterere in pulverem] Deterrere frumenta. Subterere salem. Distringere, Col. Terendo in minutiam redigere, Sen. Dispulverare, Nev. Pulverationem facere. In pulverem resolvere, Col. Terere in farinam, Plin. Perfriare, perterere baccas, Col.
units.tr: To grind to powder] To crush grain. To grind salt under. To tear apart, Col. To reduce to fine bits by wearing down, Sen. To pulverise, Nev. To make into powder. To dissolve into powder, Col. To rub into meal, Plin. To crush and thoroughly rub berries, Col.

units.la: Contigit] Accidit aliquid alicui. Accidit ut. Evenit aliquid alicui, Evenit ut. Forte evenit ut. Vereor ne id eveniat in meas literas. Obtingit, Evenit mihi aliquid. Incidit tempus. Fit sæpe ut. Cadit aliquid. Sæpe concurrit ut. &c, Cic. Usus venit, Ter. Objectus est error, Cic. Succedit, Plin.
units.tr: It happens] Something befalls someone. It happens that. Something turns out for someone. It turns out that. It happens by chance that. I fear this may happen in my letters. It falls to me. The time comes. It often happens that. Something falls out. It often chances that, etc., Cic. The occasion arises, Ter. An error is objected, Cic. It succeeds, Plin.

units.la: Contingere, i.e. ferire] Collimare, Cic. Tangere metam, Ovid. Ferire, Hor.
units.tr: To touch, that is, to strike] To aim at, Cic. To touch the goal, Ovid. To strike, Hor.

units.la: Contingunt non omnibus omnia] Corinthum adire non cuivis contingit.
units.tr: Not everything falls to everyone] It is not given to everyone to go to Corinth.

units.la: Continuare] Perpetuare, Plaut. Usque & usque agere, Mart. Nec absistit facere donec, Col. Cursu continenti sequi fugientem, Liv. Perstare incoepto. Persequi incoepta, Liv. Pertexere orsa. Pergere, Cic. Urgere iter, Ovid. Lineæ insistere. Lineas producere.
units.tr: To continue] To keep up, Plaut. To drive on without cease, Mart. Nor does he stop doing it until, Col. To follow the fleeing man at a continuous run, Liv. To persist in what has been begun. To pursue undertakings, Liv. To carry the beginnings through to the end. To go on, Cic. To press on the journey, Ovid. To keep to the line. To extend lines.
