units.la: Continuatur] Alius post alium interiêre, Amm. Gaudium gaudiis suppeditat. Alius super alium, Plaut. Continuantur dapes, Hor.
units.tr: It is continued] One after another perished, Amm. Joy supplies joy. One upon another, Plaut. Feasts are kept going, Hor.

units.la: Continuanda sunt cæpta] Non uno ictu cadit arbor. Nulla res consummata est, cum incipit, Sen. Nihil omnium est, quod possit in suis primordiis perfici, Apul.
units.tr: What has been begun must be continued] A tree does not fall with one blow. No thing is finished at the moment it begins, Sen. There is nothing of all things that can be perfected in its beginnings, Apul.

units.la: Continuò] Continuato protelo, Lucr. Assiduò. Assiduissimè, Cic. Tractim, Virg. Continenter, Cæs. Irrequieto cursu, Amm. Indesinenter, Var. Nec mora nec requies interdatur ulla fluendi, Lucr.
units.tr: Continually] With an unbroken prolongation, Lucr. Constantly. Most constantly, Cic. Drawn out, Virg. Without interruption, Caes. With restless course, Amm. Unceasingly, Var. Neither delay nor rest is allowed to the flowing, Lucr.

units.la: Continuus] Continens oratio. Perpetua historia, Cic. Ictus contigui, Gell. Inabruptus, Stat. Irruptus, Hor.
units.tr: Continuous] A continuous speech. An unbroken history, Cic. Contiguous blows, Gell. Unbroken, Stat. Unbroken, Hor.

units.la: Contorquere] Torquere aliquid in varias partes, Plin. Torquere huc & illuc ora. Convibrare linguam. Circumrotare machinam, Amm.
units.tr: To twist] To turn something in various directions, Plin. To turn the face this way and that. To shake the tongue. To rotate a machine round, Amm.

units.la: Contorsio] Vertigo tenebrarum, Arnob. Implicatio nervorum, Cic. Complexio. Implicabilis series, Quint. Volumina vinculorum, Virg.
units.tr: Contortion] A whirl of darkness, Arnob. An entanglement of sinews, Cic. An intertwining. A series hard to unravel, Quint. Coils of chains, Virg.

units.la: Contortus] Tortuosus visus. Contortulus. Involutus, Cic. Perplexus, Quint. Intortus caudex, Plin. Retortus, Col. Contortuplicata volumina, Plaut.
units.tr: Twisted] A tortuous appearance. Somewhat twisted. Involved, Cic. Perplexed, Quint. A twisted trunk, Plin. Bent back, Col. Coils folded many times over, Plaut.

units.la: Contrà] Contrariè, E, ex contrario. Ex parte contrariâ, Cic. E diverso. E contrario. Ex adverso, Plin. Viceversâ, Vlp. Adversè, Gell. Controversum, Solin.
units.tr: On the contrary] Contrariwise, on the other hand. On the opposite side, Cic. On the other side. Opposite, Plin. Vice versa, Ulp. Adversely, Gell. Opposed, Solin.

units.la: Contractio] Contractione brevius, Præcisio orationis, Cic. Breviarium culturæ, Epitome, Hor. Cic. Vid. Compendium.
units.tr: Contraction] A briefer thing by contraction, a cutting short of speech, Cic. An abridgement of cultivation, an epitome, Hor. Cic. See Compendium.

units.la: Contradicere] Contra aliquem dicere, disputare. Contrà pugnare. Resistere & repugnare contra. In contrariam partem afferre. Ex contrario aliquid contendere. Refragari alicui. Adversari alicui in disputando. Oppositum aliquid afferre, Cic. Contra verum niti, Salust. Contra aliquem venire, Cic.
units.tr: To contradict] To speak or dispute against someone. To fight against. To resist and oppose. To bring forward on the opposite side. To put something forward on the contrary side. To gainsay someone. To oppose someone in argument. To bring forward an opposing point, Cic. To strive against the truth, Sall. To come against someone, Cic.

units.la: Contradicere vehementer] Pleno velo, obversaque resistere prora.
units.tr: To contradict vehemently] With full sail, and resisting with prow turned against.

units.la: Contrahere] Contrahere orationem. Breviter summatimque dicere, Cic. Abbreviare sparsa, Veget. Breviare, Quint. Decurtare, Plin. Curtare, Hor. Imponere modum temporeri, Liv. Compendefacere operam orationis. Compendium alicujus rei facere, Plaut. Praecidere aliquid ex oratione, Cic.
units.tr: To contract] To contract speech: to speak briefly and in summary, Cic. To abridge scattered matters, Veget. To shorten, Quint. To cut short, Plin. To clip, Hor. To set a limit to time, Liv. To make the labour of speech short. To make a summary of something, Plaut. To cut something out of a speech, Cic.

units.la: Contraniti] Adversus tendere. Adverso flumine. Adversis ventis. Adversum ire, venire, fieri, alicui.
units.tr: To strive against] To strain against. Against the current. Against the winds. To go, come or happen against someone.

units.la: Contraniti illis, quos vincere nequeas] Contra stimulos calcare.
units.tr: To strive against those whom you cannot overcome] To kick against the goads.

units.la: Contrarium] Contraria pars, res. Contrarium caput. Adversum, Cic.
units.tr: Contrary] The opposite part or thing. The opposite head. Adverse, Cic.

units.la: Contra alium] Sentire suffragio mei improbo. Refragari alicui, Cic.
units.tr: Against another] To vote against me dishonestly. To oppose someone, Cic.

units.la: Contrarius] Adversarius. Adversans, Cic. Controversa sibi & repugnantia, & natura communionem abnegantia promisceri, Macrob. Adversus alicujus vel alicui, Tacit. Pugnantia loqui, Cic.
units.tr: Contrary] Adversary. Opposing, Cic. Contradictory and repugnant things, denying fellowship with nature, to be mixed together, Macrob. Opposed to someone, Tacit. To speak contradictions, Cic.

units.la: Contraria in contraria degenerant] Fratrum irae acerbissimae. Fratrum quoque gratia rara est, Ovid. Pusillum malum ingens bonum esse solet, Plin. Magno bono magni mali periculum vicinium. Profundus risus lacrymas parit. Vid. Extrema in se.
units.tr: Contraries degenerate into their contraries] The anger of brothers is most bitter. Favour among brothers, too, is rare, Ovid. A small evil is wont to be a great good, Plin. There is the danger of great evil close beside great good. Deep laughter brings forth tears. See Extrema in se.

units.la: Contrarietas] Repugnantia rerum. Oppositio. Adversans & repugnans natura, Cic. Adversitas. Antipathia, Plin. Dissociatio corporum, Id. Repugnatio, Apul.
units.tr: Contrariety] Opposition of things. Opposition. A nature opposing and contradicting, Cic. Adversity. Antipathy, Plin. Separation of bodies, Id. Repugnance, Apul.

units.la: Contribuere] Dare symbolam, Ter. Conferre in medium, Suet. Conferre in commune. In partem impensae venire. Congerere, Cic. Intribuere, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: To contribute] To give a share, Ter. To bring into the common stock, Suet. To bring into a common fund. To come into a share of the expense. To gather together, Cic. To distribute, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Contristare aliquem] In luctum conjicere aliquem. Offerre alicui moerorem alicui, Ter. Plaut. Inferre moestitiam alicui. Detrudere in luctum aliquem. Conturbare aliquem. Contrahit animos cantus, Cic. Funestare, Id.
units.tr: To sadden someone] To throw someone into mourning. To bring sorrow to someone, Ter. Plaut. To bring sadness upon someone. To thrust someone into grief. To disturb someone. Song draws in the spirits, Cic. To make mournful, Id.

units.la: Controversia, Vid. Contentio.
units.tr: Controversy, see Contentio.

units.la: Controversus] Controversa causa, res. Litigiosum prædium, Cic. In disputationem cadit. Habet res controversiam, Quint. Habet res certamen. Id in controversiâ est, Cicer.
units.tr: Controversial] A controversial cause or matter. A disputed estate, Cic. It falls into dispute. The matter has controversy, Quint. The matter has a contest. It is in controversy, Cic.

units.la: Controvertere, Vid. Contendere.
units.tr: To dispute, see Contendere.

units.la: Contubernalis] Eodem igne & aquâ utentes. Homocapni, Arift.
units.tr: Tent-mate] Those who use the same fire and water. Homocapni, Arist.

units.la: Contumacia] Pervicacia. Pertinacia. Obstinatio sententiæ. Obstinata voluntas. Duritia animi, Cic. Contumacia pervicax, Col. Obstinatio inflexibilis, Plin. Iun. Destinatio pertinax, Amm. Confidentia, Plaut. Perduellis spiritus, Amm. Pugnacitas, Plin.
units.tr: Stubbornness] Obstinacy. Pertinacity. Obstinacy of opinion. An obstinate will. Hardness of mind, Cic. Stubborn obstinacy, Col. Unyielding obstinacy, Plin. Iun. Persistent resolve, Amm. Self-assurance, Plaut. A hostile spirit, Amm. Combativeness, Plin.

units.la: Contumaciter] Præfractè. Mordicus tenere, Cic. Pertinacissimè, Quint. Obfirmatè. Obstinatissimè hærens, Suet. Obstinato animo, Liv. Edurè negare. Certâ mente prælia geris, Ovid. Enixim, Sifon. Districtim nolle ire, Sen. Tenaciter, Ovid.
units.tr: Stubbornly] Obstinately. To hold on with the teeth, Cic. Most pertinaciously, Quint. Firmly. Clinging most obstinately, Suet. With an obstinate mind, Liv. To deny stoutly. You wage battles with a fixed mind, Ovid. Eagerly, Sipon. To refuse stubbornly to go, Sen. Tenaciously, Ovid.

units.la: Contumax] Pertinax. Pertinacissimus. Præfractus. Nimium sui juris ac sententiæ est. Obstinatæ voluntatis. Pugnax in vitiis. Durus, Cic. Improbus labor. Virg. Pervicax, Tac. Rebellis flamma, Stat. Durus capite, Plaut. Obfirmatus. Negans stimulus equus, Cic. Refractarius, Sen. Mens obnixa malo. Percontumax, Stat. Tenax, Virg.
units.tr: Contumacious] Pertinacious. Most pertinacious. Headstrong. Too much his own master and set in his opinion. Of an obstinate will. Pugnacious in vices. Hard, Cic. Unworthy toil, Virg. Stubborn, Tac. A rebellious flame, Stat. Hard-headed, Plaut. Hardened. A stubborn horse that refuses the spur, Cic. Refractory, Sen. A mind stubborn in evil. Very contumacious, Stat. Tenacious, Virg.

units.la: Contumelia] Ignominia (Est nominis tantùm nota) Non. Dedecus. Labes. Macula. Probrum, Nota, Sen. Opprobrium, Hor. Indignitas, Liv. Dehonestamentum, Justin. Tac. Flagitium, Plaut. Contaminatio, Vlp. Deformatio tantæ majestatis, Liv.
units.tr: Contumely] Ignominy (it is only a mark of the name), Non. Dishonour. Stain. Blemish. Disgrace, a mark of shame, Sen. Reproach, Hor. Indignity, Liv. Dishonouring, Justin. Tac. Shameful crime, Plaut. Defilement, Ulp. Defacing of so great a majesty, Liv.

units.la: Contumeliam inferre] Contumeliâ aliquem onerare, insequi, operire. Contumeliam, Probra in aliquem jacere. Contumeliis verborum lacerare. Inferre probrum. Objicere ut probrum, Cic. Vid. Conviciari.
units.tr: To inflict contumely] To load someone with contumely, to pursue, to heap upon. To hurl reproaches at someone. To tear someone with verbal insults. To bring disgrace. To throw in someone's face as a reproach, Cic. See Conviciari.

units.la: Contumeliosè, Vid. Probrosè.
units.tr: Contumeliously, see Probrosè.

units.la: Contumeliosus] Probrosus. Beneficium contumeliosum. In sociis contumeliosum & injuriosum est. Probro est alicui. Insigni turpitudine notatus, atque oppressus dedecore & infamiâ. Cum probro & dedecore sumptus, Cic. Ignominiosus. miniosus. Pudori est alicui, Liv. Dedecore plenus, Plaut.
units.tr: Contumelious] Reproachful. A contumelious benefit. Among allies it is insulting and injurious. It is a reproach to someone. Marked with notable baseness and overwhelmed with dishonour and infamy. Taken up with reproach and disgrace, Cic. Ignominious. It is a shame to someone, Liv. Full of dishonour, Plaut.

units.la: Contundere] Conterere pistillo. Conquassare, Col. Confringere, Plaut. Concutere, Ovid.
units.tr: To bruise] To crush with a pestle. To shatter Col. To break in pieces Plaut. To shake Ovid.

units.la: Conturbare] De statu mentis deturbare. Deturbare de mente, Cic. Vid. Turbare. Perturbare.
units.tr: To disturb] To drive out of one's state of mind. To drive out of the mind Cic. See Turbare. Perturbare.

units.la: Conturbatio] Perturbatio, Motus animi nimius. Turbida mens, Cic. Æstus. Turbidi animorum excitatique motus, Id. Æstus mentis, Lucr. Confusio, Val. Max.
units.tr: Disturbance] Perturbation; excessive agitation of the mind. A troubled mind Cic. Turmoil. Turbulent and stirred-up movements of the spirits Id. Turmoil of the mind Lucr. Confusion Val. Max.

units.la: Convalescere] Levari morbo. Recreari è morbo. Confirmata è morbo valetudo. Emergere ex incommodâ valetudine. Evadere. Melius mihi est, fit, Cic. Incipit refici æger, Plin. Recolligit se, vires, Id. Assurgit è morbo, it in melius valetudo, Tac. Revalescere, Ovid. Relevatur æger, Id. Recipere vires. Consanescere, Celf. Meliuscule esse coepit, Id. Resumere vires, Ovid. Redintegrare vires, Cæs.
units.tr: To recover] To be relieved of sickness. To be restored from illness. Health made firm after sickness. To rise out of poor health. To escape. I am better, it goes better with me Cic. The sick man begins to be restored Plin. He gathers himself and his strength Id. He rises from sickness, and his health improves Tac. To grow well again Ovid. The sick man is relieved Id. To recover strength. To grow sound again Cels. He has begun to be a little better Id. To take back strength Ovid. To restore strength Caes.

units.la: Convenientia, Vid. Congruentia.
units.tr: Agreement, see Congruentia.

units.la: Convenire alicubi] Confluere. Concurrere. Conventus agere, facere, celebrare, Cic. Vid. Congregari.
units.tr: To meet somewhere] To flow together. To run together. To hold assemblies Cic. See Congregari.

units.la: Convenire cum] Sine controversia esse. Concordare, Cic. Vid. Congruere.
units.tr: To agree with] To be beyond dispute. To be in harmony Cic. See Congruere.

units.la: Convenire super aliquâ re] Pax in eas conditiones convenit, Liv. Convenit, mihi cum illo de hac re. Concordant utriusque judicia de, Cic. Res est composita, Ter.
units.tr: To agree upon something] Peace was agreed on those terms Liv. It is agreed between me and him about this matter. The judgements of both agree about it Cic. The business is settled Ter.

units.la: Conventio] Stipulatio, Cic. Condictum, Fest. Constitutum, Cic. Auctoramentum. Formula, Sen.
units.tr: Agreement] A stipulation Cic. A condition agreed Fest. An appointment Cic. A bond of hire. A formula Sen.

units.la: Conversio] Receptus à malis consiliis, Liv. Mutatio, morum, Sen. Melior mens, Cic.
units.tr: Conversion] A return, a withdrawal from wicked counsels Liv. A change of manners Sen. A better mind Cic.

units.la: Convertere errantem] Revocare lapsum. Perducere ad frugem, Quint. Hæreticum Ecclesiæ restituere.
units.tr: To turn a wanderer] To call back one who has fallen. To bring to virtue Quint. To restore a heretic to the Church.

units.la: Convertere in aliquid] Vertere homines in lupos, Plin. Vertere feria ludo, Hor. Anhelitus terræ induunt se in nubem. Redacta vina in speciem mellis, Cic. Redigere in sordidissimam turbam nobiles, Sen.
units.tr: To change into something] To turn men into wolves Plin. To turn holidays into play Hor. The breath of the earth takes on the form of a cloud. Wines reduced to the appearance of honey Cic. To reduce nobles to the most squalid crowd Sen.

units.la: Converti in aliquid] Vertere se in faciem alterius, Plaut. Ossa traxerunt figuram lapidis, Ovid. Abiit oppidum in villas, Plin. Recidere ex, in, Cic.
units.tr: To be changed into something] To turn oneself into another's appearance Plaut. Bones took on the shape of stone Ovid. The town turned into farmsteads Plin. To relapse from, into Cic.

units.la: Converti] Conversus ad pœnitentiam, Suet. In melius consilia referre, Virg.
units.tr: To be converted] Converted to repentance Suet. To turn one's plans toward something better Virg.

units.la: Conviciari] Lacerare infesto ore aliquem. Vulnerare, Violare voce. Foedare nefando scelere, Cic. Occentare. Dente Theonino rodere. Perstringere aliquem asperioribus, Percellere, Pungere, Carpere, Aculeum testimonii in me convertit. Dicere in aliquem acerbè, Id. Proscindere conviciis, Plin. Iun. Conscindere, Cic. Conviciis os verberare, Consectari. Convicium alicui grande facere, Id. Incessere verbis amaris, Sil. Defricare sale aliquem, Hor. Dicere quod doleat. Differre dictis aliquem. Admordere, Plaut. Insequi aliquem morsibus, Ovid. Auriculas teneras mordaci radere vero, Pers. Genuinum infligere, Hier.
units.tr: To revile] To tear someone with a hostile mouth. To wound, to violate with the voice. To defile with a nefarious crime Cic. To rail at. To gnaw with a Theonine tooth. To assail someone with harsher words; to strike down, to prick, to carp at. He turned the sting of testimony against me. To speak bitterly against someone Id. To tear to pieces with insults Plin. Iun. To rend with insults Cic. To beat someone's mouth with insults, to pursue. To heap a great insult upon someone Id. To attack with bitter words Sil. To rub someone with salt Hor. To say what hurts. To put someone off with words. To bite Plaut. To pursue someone with bites Ovid. To scrape tender ears with a biting truth Pers. To deal a blow to the cheek Hier.

units.la: Conviciator, Vid. Dicax.
units.tr: Reviler, see Dicax.

units.la: Convivari] Convivere. Pollucere, Plaut. Concelebrare convivia, Cic. Mensas exquisitis epulis exstruere, Tacit.
units.tr: To feast together] To live together at table. To entertain lavishly Plaut. To hold banquets together Cic. To lay tables with choice dishes Tac.

units.la: Convivator] Conditor instructorque convivii. Dominus convivii, Varr. Arbiter bibendi. Coenae pater, Hor. Rex mensae, Macr. Summus magister in poculis, Cic. Rex convivii, Tac.
units.tr: Host] The one who arranges and furnishes a banquet. The master of the feast Varr. The judge of drinking. Father of the dinner Hor. King of the table Macr. Chief master in the cups Cic. King of the feast Tac.

units.la: Convivium opiparum] Coenae Deorum. Saliares dapes, Hor. Geniales epulae, Claud. Mensa Sicula Saliaris coena pollucibilis, Macr. Opiparè apparatum convivium, Id. Adipalis coena, Er. Coena popularis, Plaut. Adjicialis, Plin. Cerealis pompa, Var. Mensa Asiana, Macr. Coena dubia, in quâ quod prius sumas, dubites, Ter. Turneb. Dapsilis, Plaut. Sybaritica mensa. Epulum, Cic.
units.tr: A sumptuous banquet] Feast of the gods. Salian dishes Hor. Festive banquets Claud. A Sicilian table, a Salian dinner worthy of Pollux Macr. A banquet splendidly furnished Id. A fatty dinner Er. A common dinner Plaut. Adjicialis Plin. A Cerealian procession Varr. An Asian table Macr. A doubtful dinner, in which you hesitate over what to take first Ter. Turneb. Lavish Plaut. A Sybaritic table. A public feast Cic.

units.la: Convocare] Concire multitudinem, Liv. Convocare in unum, Cic.
units.tr: To call together] To rouse a crowd Liv. To call together into one place Cic.

units.la: Convolvere] Glomerare in orbes, Ovid. In spicam se colligit, Convolvit terga serpens, Virg. Conspirare se, Plin. Seneca.
units.tr: To roll together] To coil into circles Ovid. It gathers itself into a spike; the serpent rolls its back together Virg. To conspire together Plin. Seneca.

units.la: Cooptare] Cooptare Senatorum, in Collegium, in ordinem. Adscribere aliquem ad, in numerum, Cic. Allegare in ordinem, Vlp. inter Praetorios, Plin. Iun. Adscisce re in, Spartian.
units.tr: To co-opt] To co-opt senators into a college, into an order. To enrol someone among the number Cic. To assign someone to the order Vlp. Among the praetorians Plin. Iun. To admit into Spartian.

units.la: Copia] Facultas nummorum. Ubertas frugum. Foetus oratorum uber. Sylva rerum, Cic. Opimitas. Fructus, Solin. Largitas. Flumen verborum. Profluentia loquendi. Opiparae paræ res. Affluentia, Cic. Messis malorum, Plaut. Proventus poëtarum, Plin. Iun. Paratus principalis, regius, Tacit. Amplitudo opum, Plin. Copiæ cornu, aut cornu copiæ, Hor. Plin. Ovid. Amaltheæ cornu, Adag.
units.tr: Abundance] Means of money. Fertility of the crops. The rich fruitfulness of an orator. A forest of matter Cic. Richness. Fruit Solin. Generosity. A flood of words. Fluency of speech. A sumptuous supply of goods. Affluence Cic. A harvest of evils Plaut. The outpouring of poets Plin. Iun. A ready supply, royal Tac. Abundance of wealth Plin. The horn of plenty Hor. Plin. Ovid. The horn of Amalthea Adag.

units.la: Copiam alicujus rei habere] Abundare, circumfluere rebus omnibus, redundare, Cic. Abundè esse alicui, Cels. Superabundare, Vlp. Affluere divitiis, Lucr. Scatere irarum, Gell. Superfluere, Plin. Fluit auro terra. Exuberat promis arbor, Virg.
units.tr: To have plenty of something] To abound, to overflow with all things, to be redundant Cic. To have enough of something Cels. To have more than enough Vlp. To flow with riches Lucr. To teem with anger Gell. To overflow Plin. The land flows with gold. The tree overflows with fruit Virg.

units.la: Copiam sui facere] Præbere se conspiciendum. Dare aditum alicui ad se, Cic. Copiam mei facio, Plin. Iun. Copiam efficere alicui ad aliquem. Facere alicui copiam conveniendi. Viam planam facere ad aliquid, Plaut. Facere sui potestatem, Cic. Dare accessum, Ovid. Vid. Admittere.
units.tr: To make oneself available] To offer oneself to be seen. To give someone access to oneself Cic. I make myself available Plin. Iun. To give someone the chance of meeting someone. To give someone the chance to meet. To smooth the way to something Plaut. To make one's power available Cic. To give approach Ovid. See Admittere.

units.la: Copiosè] Affatim. Affluenter, Profluenter. Plenè & cumulatè, Cic. Abundanter, Plin. Abundè, Cic. Refusè, refusius, Col. Cumulatim, fluxe, Varr. Claud. Horreo ipsò, Luculento sinu, Plaut. Largè comparavit pastum, Cic. Copiosissimè nascitur herba. Fertilius provenit, Plin. Ubertim, Claud. Uberius, uberrimè tractare, Cic.
units.tr: Abundantly] Enough, plentifully. Copiously, fluently. Fully and in full measure Cic. Abundantly Plin. Enough Cic. More lavishly, most lavishly Col. Heaped up, flowingly Varr. Claud. I have store in a rich bosom Plaut. He provided food lavishly Cic. The grass grows most abundantly. It springs up more richly Plin. Plentifully Claud. To handle more richly, most richly Cic.

units.la: Copiosus] Abundans. Redundans, Superfluens. Affluentissimus variarum rerum, copiis. Lautus. Locuples. Ferax. Præditus opibus. Luculentus, Cic. Opimus, Plaut. Præscatens doctrinis liber, Gell. Effertissima opimitas, Plaut. Dapsilis proventus, Col. Macta munera, Sal. Felix ævi, Apul. Largifluus, Lucr. Munifex mamma, Plin. Torrens, copia dicendi, Iuv. Prodigus multæ herbæ locus, Hor.
units.tr: Abundant] Abounding. Overflowing, superfluous. Most abundant in various things, in resources. Sumptuous. Rich. Fertile. Endowed with means. Splendid Cic. Rich Plaut. Full of learning, free Gell. Most abounding in riches Plaut. A lavish yield Col. Bountiful gifts Sal. Happy in age Apul. Flowing with abundance Lucr. A bountiful breast Plin. A flowing torrent of eloquence Iuv. A place lavish with much grass Hor.

units.la: Copula matrimonialis] Benedictio nuptiarum. Coronatio, Eucholog. Fides, Ovid. Fides sacrata conjugii, Sen. Fœdus conjugale. Jura conjugialia. Connubialia jura, Ovid. Fœderatori, Lucr. Coëmptio, Cic. Confarreatio, Tacit. Farreatio, Boët. Confarreationis vinculum. Confarratio, Plinius.
units.tr: Matrimonial bond] The blessing of a marriage. Crowning Eucholog. Faith Ovid. The sacred faith of marriage Sen. A conjugal covenant. Conjugal rights. Marital rights Ovid. Covenanting Lucr. Coemption Cic. Confarreation Tac. Farreation Boët. The bond of confarreation. Confarreation Plinius.

units.la: Copulare novos nuptos] Connubio jungere, Virg. Coronare novos nuptos, Eucholog.
units.tr: To join newly married couples] To join in wedlock Virg. To crown the newly married Eucholog.

units.la: Coquere] Coquinari, Plaut. Percoquere carnes, Plin. Mitigare cibum igne, Cic. Mollire pulmenta vapore, Apul. Madere facere, Plaut. Foculari, Fovere, Non. Concoquere cibos in foco, Varr. Elixare, Sipont.
units.tr: To cook] To work as a cook Plaut. To cook meats thoroughly Plin. To soften food with fire Cic. To soften dishes with steam Apul. To make moist Plaut. To warm at the hearth, to cherish Non. To cook food at the hearth Varr. To boil Sipont.

units.la: Coquus] Cocus, Cic. Magirus, Lampr. Cui notitia palati Domini est, Sen. Namque coquus Domini debet habere gulam, Mart. Coquinarius, Sipont. Culinarius, Scrib. Gulae magister.
units.tr: Cook] Cook Cic. Cook Lampr. One whose knowledge of the palate belongs to the master Sen. For a master's cook ought to have a gullet Mart. Kitchen cook Sipont. Of the kitchen Scrib. Master of the gullet.

units.la: Coqua] Cocula, Non. Focaria, Hier.
units.tr: Cook (woman)] Female cook Non. Kitchen-woman Hier.

units.la: Cor] Vitae principium ac coloris. Primum vivens & ultimum moriens, Arist. Fons nativi caloris, Sacrarium cordis.
units.tr: Heart] The source of life and of colour. The first to live and the last to die Arist. The fount of natural heat, the sanctuary of the heart.

units.la: Coram] Si coràm me praesente dixisset. Praesens tecum egi, Cic. Coràm in os laudare, Ter. Coràm praesens praesentem vides, Plaut. In re praesenti fuit, Id. Liv. Impraesentiarum, pro in praesens, Cato. Gellius verò, in praesentiarum.
units.tr: In the presence of] If he had said it in my presence. I dealt with you face to face Cic. To praise someone to his face Ter. You see the present one face to face with you present Plaut. He was in a matter at hand Id. Liv. Impraesentiarum, for "in praesens", Cato. Gellius however has "in praesentiarum."

units.la: Corbis, vid. Sporta.
units.tr: Basket, see Sporta.

units.la: Coriarius] Confector coriorum, Firm. Cerdo, Mart.
units.tr: Tanner] One who dresses hides Firm. Craftsman Mart.

units.la: Corium] Pellis, Virg. Exuviae leonis, &c. Id. Spolium ferarum, Lucr.
units.tr: Hide] Skin Virg. The hides of a lion, etc. Id. The spoils of wild beasts Lucr.

units.la: Cornix] Augur aquae, Avis imbrium augur, Hor.
units.tr: Crow] The augur of water; a bird, the augur of rains Hor.

units.la: Cornu] Ungulae, Virg.
units.tr: Horn] Hooves Virg.

units.la: Cornutus] Armatus cornibus, Col. Corniger, Virg.
units.tr: Horned] Armed with horns Col. Horn-bearing Virg.

units.la: Corona] Odoratis sertis innectere tempora, Ovid. Sextae coronae, Arnob. Floies serti, Apul. Verno florentes coronamine, Apul. Strophium olim, Quint.
units.tr: Garland] To bind the temples with fragrant wreaths Ovid. Sixth crowns Arnob. Flowers of a wreath Apul. Flowering with a spring garland Apul. A strophium formerly, Quint.

units.la: Corona regia] Diadema, Cic. Insigne regium, Tacit.
units.tr: Royal crown] A diadem Cic. Royal insignia Tac.

units.la: Coronatio Regis] Dies capiendo diademati delectus, Tacit.
units.tr: Coronation of a king] The day chosen for taking up the diadem Tac.

units.la: Coronare] Diadema imponere, Cic. Insigni regio evincire, Tacit.
units.tr: To crown] To place a diadem upon Cic. To bind with royal insignia Tac.

units.la: Corpulentia] Corporatura. Corporatio, Col. Bona corporis habitudo, Plaut. Lacertorum tori, Cic. Actus corporis, Col. Augmen corporis, Lucr.
units.tr: Corpulence] Bodily build. Bulk of body Col. A good physical constitution Plaut. The muscles of the arms Cic. Movement of the body Col. An increase of body Lucr.

units.la: Corpulentus] Corporatus, Cic. Corpore curatus, Cat. Carnosus. Carnosissimus, Plin. Carnulentus, Solin. Habitior, Plaut. Pulposus, Apul. Collum torosum, Col.
units.tr: Corpulent] Stout Cic. One who takes care of his body Cat. Fleshy. Very fleshy Plin. Full of flesh Solin. Rather plump Plaut. Pulpy Apul. Thick-necked Col.

units.la: Corpus] Ergastulum animae, Sepulchrum, quod circumfertur, Trismegist. Nobis in carunculae hujus folliculo constitutis, Arnob. Saccus es, (scil. tu homo) Sen. Saccus stercoreus, Hugo. Cortex corporeus, Varr. Caducum vasculum.
units.tr: Body] The prison of the soul. A sepulchre that is carried about Trismegist. Placed in the little sack of this flesh of ours Arnob. You are a sack (namely you, man) Sen. A dung-sack Hugo. A bodily husk Varr. A fragile little vessel.

units.la: Correctio] Emendatio temeritatis, Cic. Refectio, Col.
units.tr: Correction] The correction of rashness Cic. Repair Col.

units.la: Correctum opus] Elimatum opus. Opus, quod multa litura coërcuit, Ovid.
units.tr: A corrected work] A polished work. A work that has been reined in by much erasing Ovid.

units.la: Corrector] Emendator, trix, Cic. Refector, Col.
units.tr: Corrector] A corrector, an emender, feminine Cic. A restorer Col.

units.la: Corrigere] Emendare consilium. Correctionem adhibere. Reficere. Instaurare aliquid, Cic. Recorrigere, Sen. Castigare carmen, Horat. Retexere scripta, Id. Retractatum opus, Bud. Reddere incudi versus male tornatos, Hor. Recoquere, Quint. Sarcire, Cato. Quod jactu cecidit, arte corrige. Huic incommodo paulo mederi possis. Huic malo illud erit remedio. Mendum litura tollitur. Animi morbos sanat Philosophia. Corporis vitia ingenii dotibus pensantur. Orationis vitia Grammatica castigat. Philosophia morbos animi pellit medicaturque, Er. Vid. Emendare. Denuo agere.
units.tr: To correct] To amend a plan. To apply correction. To repair. To restore something Cic. To correct again Sen. To polish a poem Horat. To revise writings Id. A reworked work Bud. To return verses badly turned to the anvil Hor. To cook again Quint. To patch Cato. What has fallen by a throw, correct by skill. This inconvenience can be somewhat remedied. That will be a remedy for this evil. A blemish is removed by erasure. Philosophy heals the diseases of the mind. Defects of the body are balanced by gifts of the mind. Grammar corrects faults of speech. Philosophy drives out the diseases of the mind and cures them Er. See Emendare. Denuo agere.

units.la: Corripere, vid. Arguere.
units.tr: To rebuke, see To reprove.

units.la: Correptio] Corrigi non vult stultus. Vid. Pæna.
units.tr: Rebuke] A fool does not want to be corrected. See Punishment.

units.la: Corrugare frontem] Contrahere frontem, Plaut. Ducere vultum. Corrugat alicui nares mappa sordida, Mart. Caperare vultum, Var. Caperat illi frons severitudine, Plaut. Demere supercilio nubem. Trahere rugas & vultum, cogere rugas. Rugis anilibus perarare ora, Ovid. Senili tristitia striatam gero frontem, Apul. Deturpare rugis aliquid, Plin. Asseverare frontem, Apul. Rugat palliolum, pro rugatur, Plaut. Irrugari, Gell. Torpescere rugis, Plin.
units.tr: To wrinkle the brow] To draw the brow together, Plaut. To pull a face. A dirty napkin wrinkles one's nose, Mart. To wrinkle the face, Var. His brow is wrinkled with severity, Plaut. To remove a cloud from the eyebrow. To draw wrinkles across the face; to gather wrinkles. To plough the face with old women's wrinkles, Ovid. I bear a brow furrowed with senile sadness, Apul. To disfigure something with wrinkles, Plin. To make the brow stern, Apul. The little cloak is wrinkled (for "is wrinkled"), Plaut. To be wrinkled, Gell. To grow stiff with wrinkles, Plin.

units.la: Corrumpere] Vitiare, Ovid. Depravare naturam, Conficere, Consumere, Cic. Infestare, Plin. Pecuniae illudere, Tacit. Imbuere vitiis, Quint. Inconciliare aliquem, Plaut. Cur nobis perdis adolescentem, Ter. Adolescentem nobilitare flagitiis, Cic. Præcorrumpere donis, Ovid. Transtundere in aliquem vitium, Cic. Confringere consilia, jura. Abuti viribus, Id.
units.tr: To corrupt] To spoil, Ovid. To deprave nature; to destroy, to consume, Cic. To infest, Plin. To make sport of money, Tacit. To imbue with vices, Quint. To alienate someone, Plaut. Why are you ruining the young man for us? Ter. To make a young man notorious by disgraceful deeds, Cic. To corrupt beforehand with gifts, Ovid. To transfer a fault onto someone, Cic. To break plans and laws. To misuse strength, Id.

units.la: Corrumpi] Corruptela depravari. Capere, concipere vitium, Cic. Facere vitium. Abire pessum, Plaut. Collanus affert suo beneficio, Sen. Conteritur ferrum, vita, Ovid.
units.tr: To be corrupted] To be depraved by corruption. To catch or conceive a fault, Cic. To become faulty. To go to ruin, Plaut. Collanus brings it to ruin by his favour, Sen. Iron and life are worn away, Ovid.

units.la: Corruptibilis] Dissolubilis. Corruptioni obnoxius, Cic.
units.tr: Corruptible] Dissoluble. Liable to corruption, Cic.

units.la: Corruptio à primariis incipit] Piscis primùm à capite fœtet.
units.tr: Corruption begins with the leading men] A fish stinks first from the head.

units.la: Corruptor] Corruptrix provincia, Cic. Perditor Reipub. Id. Contritor compedum, Plaut. Tritor stimulorum, Id. Confector cardinum, Lucil.
units.tr: Corrupter] A corrupting province, Cic. A ruiner of the Republic, Id. A crusher of fetters, Plaut. A grinder of goads, Id. A destroyer of hinges, Lucil.

units.la: Corruptus] Vitiatus, profligatus, profligatissimus homo. Prolapsus. Constuprata judicia, Cic. Perditissimus homo. Vitiosus, Id. Vitiosissimus, Paterc.
units.tr: Corrupted] Spoiled, ruined, a thoroughly ruined man. Fallen. Corrupted judgments, Cic. A most lost man. Vicious, Cic. Most vicious, Paterc.

units.la: Corruptus muneribus] Argentanginam patitur. Bos in lingua. Percorrumpere donis aliquem, Ovid. Placatus muneribus.
units.tr: Corrupted by bribes] Suffers from a silver quinsy. An ox on the tongue. To corrupt someone thoroughly with gifts, Ovid. Appeased by gifts.

units.la: Coruscare, vid. Nitere.
units.tr: To glitter, see To shine.

units.la: Cortex] Cutis arborum, Plin. Induviæ palmæ arboris, Id. Tunica, Id.
units.tr: Bark] The skin of trees, Plin. The covering of the palm tree, Id. A tunic, Id.

units.la: Corvus] Corax, Cic. Ales Satyria, Flor.
units.tr: Raven] A crow, Cic. A bird of Satyria, Flor.

units.la: Coticula] Lapis Heraclius, Plin. Lapis Lydius. Cotes aurificum, Id. Exhebenus, Id. Index, Ovid. Metallorum examinator.
units.tr: Whetstone] A Heraclean stone, Plin. A Lydian stone. The whetstones of goldsmiths, Id. Exhebenus, Id. An indicator, Ovid. An examiner of metals.

units.la: Cras] Crastinò, Gell. Secundum hunc diem, Cic.
units.tr: Tomorrow] On the next day, Gell. The day after this one, Cic.

units.la: Crastinus] Jam Cras hesternum consumpsimus, etit aliud Cras, Perf.
units.tr: Of tomorrow] Now we have used up yesterday's tomorrow, and there will be another tomorrow, Pers.

units.la: Crassus] Pinguis toga, Suet. Altus, Cat. Concretus, Cic. Spissus, Virg. Duplex Spina dorsum, i. crassum, Id. Pinguis saliva, Sen.
units.tr: Thick] A thick toga, Suet. High, Cat. Curdled, Cic. Dense, Virg. Double. A thorn of the back, that is, thick. Thick saliva, Sen.

units.la: Crassus (2) vid. Barbarus.
units.tr: Thick (2), see Barbarous.

units.la: Crasse, vid. Impolite.
units.tr: Thickly, see Impolitely.

units.la: Crassescere, vid. Grandescere.
units.tr: To thicken, see To grow large.

units.la: Crater] Patera. Trulla, Cic. Phiala, Juv. vid. Poculum.
units.tr: Bowl] A dish. A ladle, Cic. A cup, Juv. See Cup.

units.la: Crates] Cancelli, Cic. Cancri, Apul. Clathri cavæ, Hor. Arcus pellucidâ transsennâ, Paul. Interseptum ligneum instar retis, Euseb.
units.tr: Lattice] Railings, Cic. Gratings, Apul. Hollow lattice-work, Hor. An arch with a transparent screen, Paul. A wooden partition like a net, Euseb.

units.la: Creare] Natura creat & fingit, Cic. Plasmare, in SS.
units.tr: To create] Nature creates and shapes, Cic. To form, in the Scriptures.

units.la: Creator] Procreator, molitor, Effector mundi. Sator cœlestium omnium. Conditor ævi Christus, Claud.
units.tr: Creator] Begetter, maker, author of the world. Sower of all heavenly things. Christ, founder of the age, Claud.

units.la: Creatura] Res creatæ, Cic.
units.tr: Creature] Created things, Cic.

units.la: Creber] Frequens, Quint. Multus, Cic. Crebro crebrius.
units.tr: Frequent] Frequent, Quint. Many, Cic. More and more often.

units.la: Credere] Aliquid credo fore, Plaut. Persuasissimum mihi est de. Sic habeo persuasum. Pro certo habere, Cic. Ac-credere aliquid, Col.
units.tr: To believe] I believe something will happen, Plaut. It is most firmly persuaded to me that. So I hold it persuaded. To hold for certain, Cic. To entrust something, Col.

units.la: Credere alicui Credere fidei alicujus. Fidem habere, adhibere, tribuere testimonio, Cic. Fidem alicujus sequi, Vlp. Adcredere alicui, Lucr. Fidem alicui arbitrari, Plaut. Fides illi nuncianti fuit, Liv.
units.tr: To believe someone] To trust someone's good faith. To have, apply or give faith to testimony, Cic. To follow a person's faith, Ulp. To entrust to someone, Lucr. To consider someone trustworthy, Plaut. He had faith in the one announcing it, Liv.

units.la: Credere firmiter Credere fide divinâ. Si isti formidas credere, meâ fide crede, Plaut. Qui huic non credit, Deo non credit.
units.tr: To believe firmly] To believe with divine faith. If you fear to believe him, believe on my word, Plaut. Whoever does not believe this one does not believe God.

units.la: Non credere Cras credam, hodie nihil. Fidem non adhibere, non tribuere, Cic. Negare fidem, Sen. Pro falsis ducere, Salust. Respuit hoc sapientissimi cujusque fides, Plaut. Credat Judæus apella, non ego, Hor. Vid. Incredibile.
units.tr: Not to believe] I will believe tomorrow, nothing today. Not to give faith, Cic. To deny faith, Sen. To hold as false, Sallust. The trust of every wise man rejects this, Plaut. Let the Jew Apella believe it, not I, Hor. See Incredible.

units.la: Credat qui vult Ex ingenio quisque suo addat vel demat fidem, Tacit. Fides penes authores fit, Sal. Fides tantum auctores apellet, Plaut. Fidem auctor vindicet, Val. M.
units.tr: Let him believe who will] Each person adds or subtracts faith according to his own temperament, Tacit. Credit rests with the authors, Sal. Trust should appeal only to authorities, Plaut. Let the author vindicate the faith, Val. M.

units.la: Credulitas noxia Artus & nervi Sapientiæ sunt, non facilè credere, Epichar. Bonorum virorum morbus credulitas.
units.tr: Harmful credulity] Not to believe readily is the sinew and nerve of wisdom, Epichar. Credulity is the disease of good men.

units.la: Cremare, vid. Vrere, Comburere.
units.tr: To burn, see To scorch, to set on fire.

units.la: Cremor lactis Flos lactis. Pingue lactis, Iun. Spuma lactis, Lac spumosum, Gerr. Pingue lac, Plin.
units.tr: Cream of milk] The flower of milk. Fatty milk, Juv. Foam of milk; frothy milk, Gerr. Rich milk, Plin.

units.la: Crena Scissuræ pennarum, Plin.
units.tr: Notch] Cuts in feathers, Plin.

units.la: Crepidæ Gallicæ, Cic. Crepidulæ, Gell. Solea objurgabere rubrâ, Pers.
units.tr: Gallic sandals] Cic. Little sandals, Gell. You will be scolded with a red sole, Pers.

units.la: Crepitus ventris Flatum ventrem emittere, Suet. Pedi-tum, Catul. Venter (ventus) injuriam facit, Petron. Visum, Scal.
units.tr: Breaking wind] To let out wind, Suet. To break wind, Catul. The belly (wind) does wrong, Petron. Visum, Scal.

units.la: Crepusculum Extremum diei, Fest. Lux dubia, Non. Primæ tenebræ, Liv. Lucis & noctis confinium, Ovid. Prima fax noctis, Gell. Crepusculascens hora, Sidon.
units.tr: Twilight] The end of the day, Fest. Doubtful light, Non. The first darkness, Liv. The border between light and night, Ovid. The first torch of night, Gell. An hour growing dusky, Sidon.

units.la: Crescere Augescunt femina, Cic. Incrementis augescere, Liv. Grandescere, Lucr. Gignitur capillus, Gell. Capere incrementum, Col. Augmen sumere, Lucr.
units.tr: To grow] Women grow, Cic. To grow by increments, Liv. To grow large, Lucr. Hair grows, Gell. To take increase, Col. To take on augmentation, Lucr.

units.la: Crescere in alieno solo Hos[illegible, ~4 letters] ^ nescit castanea.
units.tr: To grow in a foreign soil] Hos[illegible, about 4 letters] ^ the chestnut does not know.

units.la: Creta Terra Cretica, Gerr.
units.tr: Chalk] Cretan earth, Gerr.

units.la: Cribrum Cribrum excussorium. Incerniculum, Plin. Cribernículum, Sipont. Cribrare, vid. Cernere.
units.tr: Sieve] A sieve for sifting, Plin. A little sieve, Sipont. To sift, see To sieve.

units.la: Crimen] Culpa mea, tua, Plaut. Vitium. Noxia. Fraus. Meritum. Capitale facinus, Cic. Noxa, Liv. Piaculi contracta commissio, Arnob.
units.tr: Crime] My fault, your fault, Plaut. A fault. A wrong. A misdeed. A merit. A capital crime, Cic. An offence, Liv. A committed sin that calls for expiation, Arnob.

units.la: Criminalis actio] Judicium capitis. Causa de capite, capitis. Certamen capitis & famæ. Res capitalis. Judicium damnatorium. Lis capitis, Cic. Capitale judicium, Quint. Criminaliter actio intenditur, Bud. Actio criminosa, Id.
units.tr: Criminal action] A trial for life. A case concerning life or head. A contest of life and reputation. A capital matter. A judgment of condemnation. A suit involving life, Cic. A capital judgment, Quint. A criminal action is brought, Bud. A criminal action, Id.

units.la: Criminari aliquem] Crimen alicui movere, Suet. Objicere alicui probrum, Crimen objectare, inferre. In magnis criminibus, vel, criminis loco aliquid objicere. Vocare in crimen, Cic. Insimulare falsis criminibus, Ovid. Crimen alicui intentare, Quint. Intendere crimen in aliquem, Liv. Arguere de crimine. Incusare aliquem probri, Plaut. Raptare pro scelesto, Prop. Increpabantur hæc in eum, Sallust. Pulsari falso crimine, Claud. vid. Accusare.
units.tr: To accuse someone] To bring a charge against someone, Suet. To object a disgrace to someone; to lay a charge; to bring a charge. To object something as a grave crime or in place of a charge. To summon into accusation, Cic. To charge falsely with crimes, Ovid. To bring a charge against someone, Quint. To lay a charge against someone, Liv. To argue about a charge. To accuse someone of disgrace, Plaut. To seize someone as a villain, Prop. These things were cried out against him, Sallust. To be struck by a false charge, Claud. See To accuse.

units.la: Criminator] Momus, vid. Accusator.
units.tr: Accuser] Momus, see Accuser.

units.la: Crines, vid. Capilli.
units.tr: Hair, see Hairs.

units.la: Crispare] Frangere in gradus comam, Plin. Calamistris inurere, Cic. Ustulare ardente ferro crines, Pacuv. Vibrare, Virg.
units.tr: To curl] To break the hair into curls, Plin. To singe with curling irons, Cic. To scorch the hair with a burning iron, Pacuv. To brandish, Virg.

units.la: Crispatus] Calamistrata coma, Cic. Vibrati calido ferro crines, Virg.
units.tr: Curled] Hair curled with the curling iron, Cic. Hair brandished with a hot iron, Virg.

units.la: Crispitudo] Annuli comarum, Mart. vid. Cincinnus.
units.tr: Curliness] Rings of hair, Mart. See Ringlet.

units.la: Crispus] Bene capillatus, Cic. Criniger, Lucan. Cirratus, Pers. Crispulus, Mart. Subcrispus, Var. Crinibus in nodum tortis homo, Mart.
units.tr: Curly] Well-haired, Cic. Hairy, Lucan. Ringleted, Pers. Little-curled, Mart. Slightly curled, Var. A man with hair twisted into a knot, Mart.

units.la: Crista (1)] Cirrus. Apex, Plin. Insigne cristatum pavonis, Pallad.
units.tr: Crest (1)] A tuft. A top, Plin. The crested ornament of a peacock, Pallad.

units.la: (2) Plumeus apex] Cerda, Virg. Capitis summi insigne, Lucr.
units.tr: (2) Feathered crest] A bristle, Virg. The ornament of the highest part of the head, Lucr.

units.la: (3) in Gallo] Juba Gallinaceorum, Col.
units.tr: (3) in a cock] The comb of a cock, Col.

units.la: Crocus] Croci, plu. Ovid. Spica Cilissa, Propert. Scal. Fila croci, Ovid. Crocum, Plaut.
units.tr: Saffron] Saffrons, plural, Ovid. A Cilician spike, Propert. Scal. Threads of saffron, Ovid. Saffron, Plaut.

units.la: Cruciabiliter] Per tormenta, Suet. Lateribus fodicatis, sulcatis, Amm.
units.tr: Painfully] By torments, Suet. With flanks pierced and furrowed, Amm.

units.la: Cruciare tormentis] Cruciatu afficere, Caes. Supplicio assi-cere, cere, discruciare. Torquere. Exprimere confessionem facinoris. Extorsisti ut fateor. Tormentis cogere, confiteri, Cic. Excruciare aliquem pessimis exemplis, Plaut. Tortare, Pompon. Habere quaestionem tormentis, Liv.
units.tr: To torture with torments] To inflict agony, Caes. To subject to punishment, to torment greatly. To torture. To extract a confession of a crime. You extracted it, as I confess. To compel by torments to confess, Cic. To torment someone with the worst examples, Plaut. To torture, Pompon. To hold an examination by torment, Liv.

units.la: Cruciari, vid. Excruciari.
units.tr: To be tormented, see Excruciate.

units.la: Crucifigere] Suffigere cruci. In crucem tollere, Cic. In cruce figere. In crucem agere, Suet. Crucibus suspendere, Col. Cruci dare aliquem, Plaut.
units.tr: To crucify] To fasten to a cross. To raise to the cross, Cic. To fix on a cross. To put to the cross, Suet. To hang on crosses, Col. To give someone to the cross, Plaut.

units.la: Crudelis] Immanis, ferox, atrox, teter, Cic. Truculentus, barbarus, Liv. Dirus, Ovid. Tyrannicus. Infandus, Cic. Tragicus, Liv. Trux ira, Val. Argon. Immitis, Virg. Efferus, Sen. Inclemens, Liv. Cruentus, Salust. Immanior Medea. Alter Atreus, Scytha barbarior. Phalaride crudelior, Er.
units.tr: Cruel] Monstrous, fierce, savage, foul, Cic. Brutal, barbarous, Liv. Dire, Ovid. Tyrannical. Unspeakable, Cic. Tragic, Liv. Fierce in anger, Val. Argon. Merciless, Virg. Wild, Sen. Pitiless, Liv. Bloody, Sallust. More monstrous than Medea. Another Atreus. More barbarous than a Scythian. More cruel than Phalaris, Er.

units.la: Crudelem esse] Exuere humanitatem. Exuere hominem ex homine, Cic.
units.tr: To be cruel] To cast off humanity. To strip the man from the man, Cic.

units.la: Crudelitas] Immanitas. Saevitas. Feritas. Diritas, Atrocitas, Cic. Barbaries, Id.
units.tr: Cruelty] Monstrousness. Savagery. Wildness. Harshness. Atrocity, Cic. Barbarity, Id.

units.la: Crudeliter tractari] Indignissimè, atrociter, tetrè, teterrimè, hostilem in modum, servilem in modum cruciari. Omni crudelitate lacerare, Cic. Indignum in modum, Liv. Cruciabiliter. Poenaliter interire, Amm. Foedum in modum verberibus lacerari, Liv. Tyrannicè statuere, Cic. Binis tonderi forcibus. Impotenter regnare, Hirt. Gladiatorie, Lamp. Insatiabilem crudelitatem in aliquo exercere, explere, saturare, Cic. Foedè interemptus, Cic.
units.tr: To be treated cruelly] To be tormented most unworthily, atrociously, foully, most foully, in the manner of enemies or of slaves. To tear to pieces with all cruelty, Cic. In an unworthy manner, Liv. To be tortured painfully. To die a penal death, Amm. To be foully torn with blows, Liv. To rule tyrannically, Cic. To be shorn with two pincers. To rule without restraint, Hirt. In the manner of gladiators, Lamp. To exercise, satisfy and glut insatiable cruelty on someone, Cic. Foully slain, Cic.

units.la: Cruentare] Cruentari, Cic. Cruentare morsu, Tibul. Sanguinare, Quint. Facere sanguinem, Liv.
units.tr: To make bloody] To be made bloody, Cic. To stain with a bite, Tibul. To bloody, Quint. To make blood flow, Liv.

units.la: Cruentus] Cruentus gladius, Cic. Cruentati oculi, Plin. Sanguinolentus, Var. Perfusus sanguine, Quint. Foedatus sanguine, Ovid.
units.tr: Bloody] A bloody sword, Cic. Bloodshot eyes, Plin. Bloodstained, Var. Drenched in blood, Quint. Defiled with blood, Ovid.

units.la: Crumena] Marsupium, Succulus, Plaut. Funda, Macrob. Locellus, & Locelli, Mart. Pasceolus, Plaut. Bulga, Var.
units.tr: Purse] A money-bag, Plaut. A small pouch, Macrob. A sling, Macrob. A little purse, Mart. Little purses, Mart. A pouch, Plaut. A leather bag, Var.

units.la: Crus] Tibia, Cels. Internodium, Ovid.
units.tr: Shin] A leg-bone, Cels. A joint between stems, Ovid.

units.la: Crustare, vid. Incrustare.
units.tr: To encrust, see To incrust.

units.la: Crystallus] Glacies lapidescens.
units.tr: Crystal] Ice turning to stone.

units.la: Cubare] Discubare, Plaut. Recubare, Virg. Decumbere, re, Col. Decubare, Apul. Accubare eodem lecto, Liv. Re-cumbere, Cic. Jacere ad quartam, Hor. Accumbere, Plaut. Incubare, Id.
units.tr: To lie down] To recline at table, Plaut. To lie down beside, Virg. To lie down, Col. To lie down, Apul. To lie together on the same couch, Liv. To recline, Cic. To lie until the fourth hour, Hor. To recline at table, Plaut. To lie upon, Id.

units.la: Cubare in latus] Incubitus lateris dextri valetudini conducit, Plin. Cubitus in latera conducunt adversum destillationes, Id.
units.tr: To lie on the side: Lying on the right side is good for health, Plin. Lying on the sides helps against defluxions, Id.

units.la: Cubitum ire, vid. Ire cubitum.
units.tr: Cubitum ire, see Ire cubitum.

units.la: Cubiculum] Conclave, Cic. Dormitorium, Plin.
units.tr: Cubiculum: A bedchamber, Cic. A dormitory, Plin.

units.la: Cubicularius] Præpositus cubiculo, Suet. Super somnum servus, Curt. A cubiculis.
units.tr: Cubicularius: One set over the bedchamber, Suet. A slave who waits on the sleeper, Curt. A chamberlain.

units.la: Cubitus] Ossa cubita, Hippoc. Ulnis complecti, Claud.
units.tr: Cubitus: The bones of the forearm, Hippoc. To embrace with the arms, Claud.

units.la: Cuculus] Coccyx, Plin. Cucus, Plaut.
units.tr: Cuculus: The cuckoo [κόκκυξ], Plin. The cuckoo, Plaut.

units.la: Cudere] Procudere ensem, Hor. Ducere ære effigiem, Apul. Igni res tractare, Lucr. Stringere ferrum, Plin.
units.tr: Cudere: To forge a sword, Hor. To beat a bronze likeness into shape, Apul. To work material in the fire, Lucr. To hammer iron, Plin.

units.la: In formam calidæ percussit pondera massæ, Lucr.
units.tr: He beat the weight into the shape of the hot lump, Lucr.

units.la: Cudere monetam] Signare argentum, Cic. Nummos figurare, Lamp. Percutere nummos unâ formâ, Sen. Ferire pecunias, Plin.
units.tr: Cudere monetam: To stamp silver, Cic. To shape coins, Lamp. To strike coins from one die, Sen. To strike money, Plin.

units.la: Cujas? ] Cujatis? Plaut. Unde es gentium? Id. Qui genus? Unde domo? Virg.
units.tr: Cujas?: Whose are you? Plaut. What country are you from? Id. What family, and from what house? Virg.

units.la: Culcitra] Substramen, Var. Culcitrula, Plaut. Culcitella, Lipf.
units.tr: Culcitra: An underlay, Var. A little cushion, Plaut. A little mattress, Lipf.

units.la: Culex] Culex aculeatus. Conopœorum æstiva animalia, Plin. Scal. Centrines, Plin. Humoris alumnus, Virg. Sanguisuga, Hor.
units.tr: Culex: A stinging gnat. Summer creatures of the mosquito-nets, Plin. Scal. A kind of gnat, Plin. Nourished by moisture, Virg. A bloodsucker, Hor.

units.la: Culina] Coquina, Non. Coquinula, Sipont. Fœdissimum patrimoniorum exitium, Sen.
units.tr: Culina: A kitchen, Non. A small kitchen, Sipont. The most shameful ruin of an inheritance, Sen.

units.la: Culinarius] Focarius, Sipont. Coquinarius culter, Var. Coquinatorius, Vlp.
units.tr: Culinarius: Of the hearth, Sipont. A kitchen knife, Var. Relating to cookery, Vlp.

units.la: Culmus] Culmus cerealis, fragilis, Virg. Calamus avenæ. Avena, Plin. Stipula, culmen fabæ, Ovid.
units.tr: Culmus: A brittle cereal stalk, Virg. A stalk of oats. Oats, Plin. Straw, the stalk of a bean, Ovid.

units.la: Culpa, vid. Crimen.
units.tr: Culpa, see Crimen.

units.la: Culpam pœna sequitur] Peccati pœna sæva satelles.
units.tr: Culpam pœna sequitur: Punishment is the cruel attendant of wrongdoing.

units.la: Culpa in eo est] In culpâ, in crimine est. In noxiâ est. Acceptum illi referendum. Tenetur culpâ. Resider in eo culpa hujus rei. Culpam ejus rei sustinet. Est in vitio, Cic. Per testetit, quo minus fierent hæ nuptiæ. Ipse sibi injurius rius est. Meritum meum est. Penes te culpa est. Hæret in eo culpa, Ter. Tu es huic noxæ obnoxius, Attius. Admisit in se culpam castigabilem, Plaut. Admittere in se delictum : noxiam, Ter. Culpam, Liv.
units.tr: Culpa in eo est: He is at fault, he is in blame, in the charge. He is guilty. It is to be put down to his account. He is held to blame. The fault in this matter rests with him. He bears the blame for that. He is in the wrong, Cic. He stood in the way through a witness, so that these marriages did not take place. He does himself an injury. It is my merit. The blame lies with you. The fault clings to him, Ter. You are liable for this offence, Attius. He incurred a punishable fault, Plaut. To incur guilt for an offence, Ter. To incur a fault, Liv.

units.la: Culpandus] Reprehensione dignus. Castigabilis, Plaut. Accusandus, Ter. Obelisco dignus, Er. Culpabilis, Apul.
units.tr: Culpandus: Worthy of reproof. Punishable, Plaut. To be accused, Ter. Worthy of the obelisk (the mark of censure), Er. Blameworthy, Apul.

units.la: Culpare, vid. Vituperare.
units.tr: Culpare, see Vituperare.

units.la: Culter] Cultellus, Var. Machærium, Plaut.
units.tr: Culter: A small knife, Var. A dagger, Plaut.

units.la: Cultus, vid. Religio.
units.tr: Cultus, see Religio.

units.la: Cumulatè, vid. Effusè.
units.tr: Cumulatè, see Effusè.

units.la: Cunctari] Restitare, Ter. Cunctanter prodire. Tergiversari, Cic. Dubitas dicere? Plaut. Hærere. Muginari, Cic. Tardari, Cæs. Tardè conari, Fest.
units.tr: Cunctari: To hold back, Ter. To advance hesitantly. To shift about, Cic. Do you hesitate to speak? Plaut. To stick fast. To mutter, Cic. To be slow, Caes. To try slowly, Fest.

units.la: Cunctanter] Tergiversanter, Pater. Restitando, Plaut. Manu longâ, Iavol. Cunctabundi & restitantes, Liv. Retractans, Col. Strigosus (à bubus, qui strigant, i. quiescunt.) Lucil.
units.tr: Cunctanter: Evasively, Pater. By hanging back, Plaut. With a long hand, Iavol. Hesitating and holding back, Liv. Drawing back, Col. Sluggishly (from oxen that strigant, that is, rest), Lucil.

units.la: Cunctator negotii] Diphilus ædificat, Cic. (qui architectus fuit tardissimus) Fabio cunctantior, Er. vid. Impromptus.
units.tr: Cunctator negotii: Diphilus builds, Cic. (who was the slowest of architects). Slower than Fabius, Er. See Impromptus.

units.la: Cuniculus sub terra] Suffosio, Sen. Fossura, Vitr. Specus agere, Id. Subruere mœnia cuniculis, Liv.
units.tr: Cuniculus sub terra: A digging under the ground, Sen. A trench, Vitr. To dig a tunnel, Id. To undermine walls with mines, Liv.

units.la: Cupedia] Cupedia, orum, Plaut. Crustula, pl. Scitamenta mellita, Apul. Dulcia, Lamp. Macteolæ suaves, Arnob. Pulpamentum, Cic. Popinæ potiùs, quàm epulæ, Id. Vinum, pemma, Var. Irritamenta lassæ voluptatis, ultra necessitatem lacessentia, Sen. Popinalis luxuria, Apul.
units.tr: Cupedia: Cakes, Plaut. Small sweet biscuits, Pl. Sweet, honeyed delicacies, Apul. Sweetmeats, Lamp. Soft dainties, Arnob. Relishes, Cic. Taverns rather than feasts, Id. Wine, a sweet cake, Var. Enticements of a tired pleasure, provoking beyond necessity, Sen. Tavern luxury, Apul.

units.la: Cupedinarius] Crustularius, Sen. Scriblitarius, Afran.
units.tr: Cupedinarius: A confectioner, Sen. A maker of little cakes, Afran.

units.la: Cupere] Habeo audire quid vellem, Cic. Percupidus est tui. Poscere aliquid. Optare & expetere, Id. Pervelle, Cic. Plaut. Curæ est quid sit, Id. Concupere, Capit. Avemus aliquid audire, & discere, Cic. Vellem salvam Remp. Id. Nimis vellem dari tibi fundam, Ter. Nunc ut veniret miles velim, Plin. Affectus sum in illum, Cic. Affectus alicui, Suet. vid. Avere. Desiderare.
units.tr: Cupere: I have it in mind to hear what I wish, Cic. He is very eager for you. To ask for something. To wish for and seek, Cic. To wish very much, Cic. Plaut. It is a concern to know what it is, Id. To desire, Capit. We long to hear and learn something, Cic. I would wish the Commonwealth safe, Id. I very much wished you a sling, Ter. Now I would like the soldier to come, Plin. I am well disposed toward him, Cic. Disposed toward someone, Suet. See Avere, Desiderare.

units.la: Cupidè, vid. Avidè.
units.tr: Cupidè, see Avidè.

units.la: Cupiditas] Cupiditas dominatrix animi, projecta ac effrenata. Cupiditatis sitis, Cic. Cupido habendi. Aviditas inexhausta. exhausta. Flamma, Id. Inhiatio, Capit. Amor, Cic. Prolubium, Laërt.
units.tr: Cupiditas: Desire, the mistress of the mind, headlong and unbridled. Thirst of desire, Cic. Desire to have. Inexhaustible greed. A flame, Id. Gaping, Capit. Love, Cic. Inclination, Laërt.

units.la: Cupidus] Hians avaritiâ. Appetens, Avidus, studiosus. Ardens cupiditate, Cic. Cupientissimus alicujus rei. Cupitor, Tac. Arrectæ mentes, Virg. Procax manus, Sen. Multivolus, Omnivolus, Catul. Calidus redemptor, Hor. Multicupidus, Var. Libidinosus gloriæ, Ter.
units.tr: Cupidus: Gaping with greed. Eager, greedy, keen. Burning with desire, Cic. Most desirous of something. A desirer, Tac. Aroused minds, Virg. A grasping hand, Sen. Wanting much, wanting everything, Catul. A hot contractor, Hor. Very desirous, Var. Lustful for glory, Ter.

units.la: Cur, vid. Quare.
units.tr: Cur, see Quare.

units.la: Cura] Curatio & administratio rerum. Consectatio, Cic.
units.tr: Cura: The care and management of affairs. Pursuit, Cic.

units.la: Curabo] Est mihi antiquissimum. Nihil habeo antiquius. Id mihi in oculis animoque versatur. Excubat ad me cura Reipub. Tantæ curæ mihi id est, ut me nolim admoneri. Dies noctesque nihil curo, nisi ut. Hoc animo sum, ut si in hac cura atque administratione vita mihi ponenda sit, præclarè mecum actum putem, Cic. Hæc res neutiquam negletui est mihi, Ter. Intentus alicui negotio, Sal. Cordi est mihi, Lucil. Suscipere curam, conferre curam ad. Ponere in aliqua re curam. Curas referre ad. Versari in cura aliqua, Cic. Habere in cura, Plin. Tangit me cura, Virg. Intendere curam in aliquid, Liv. Laborare ut, de famâ laborare. Consulere, providere, dare aliquid. Aucupari. Agere ut, Cic. Insistere rei, Celf. Has res studeo, Plaut. Advigilare alicui, Tac. Laborari alicui rei, Sen.
units.tr: Curabo: It is my most pressing concern. I have nothing more pressing. It is constantly before my eyes and in my mind. The care of the Commonwealth keeps watch over me. It is of such concern to me that I would not want to be reminded of it. Day and night I care for nothing but that. I am so disposed that if my life had to be spent in this care and administration, I should think I had been well treated, Cic. This matter is by no means neglected by me, Ter. Intent on some business, Sal. It is dear to my heart, Lucil. To take up a care, to devote care to. To set one's care on a matter. To refer one's cares to. To be engaged in some concern, Cic. To hold in care, Plin. Care touches me, Virg. To bend one's attention to something, Liv. To labour that, to be anxious about one's reputation. To take thought, to provide, to give something. To lie in wait for. To act so that, Cic. To apply oneself to a matter, Celf. I am keen on these things, Plaut. To keep watch over someone, Tac. To be busied with a matter, Sen.

units.la: Curato] Da operam. Enitere Adnitere totis nervis. Illud totis viribus agito. Pro virili conatus sum. Hoc unum stude, ut te in Regis benevolentiam insinues. Literis incumbas. In hæc studia incumbito. Ad id eluctare. Ad hoc advigila. Vigilandum est, qui sua negotia velit tempore conficere. Manibus pedibusque connitere. Eò velis equisque contendit. Huc remis velisque festinat. Hoc studium parvi properemus & ampli. In ea re vehementer est sudatum. In id plurimum laboris est exhaustum, exantlatum. Rem arduam molimur. Summô nixu, summâ ope, summâ vi, quantum potes adlabora, Er.
units.tr: Curato: Give your effort. Strive with all your strength. Press on with all your might. I have done what I could to the utmost of my power. Make it your one aim to insinuate yourself into the King's goodwill. Apply yourself to letters. Give yourself to these studies. Strive towards that end. Keep watch for that. Whoever wishes to finish his business on time must be vigilant. Strive with hands and feet. He hastens there with sails and oars. Let us hurry, small and great, to this study. In that matter there has been great sweating. Much labour has been spent and endured on it. We undertake a hard task. With the utmost effort, with the utmost power, with all your force, strive as hard as you can, Er.

units.la: Curare valetudinem] Dare operam valetudini. Servire, Inservire, Indulgere valetudini. Sustentare valetudinem, Cic. Curare ægrotos. Curare se & ætatem suam, Plaut.
units.tr: Curare valetudinem: To attend to one's health. To serve and indulge one's health. To sustain one's health, Cic. To treat the sick. To look after oneself and one's age, Plaut.

units.la: Non curare] Nihil morari. Nulla me hujus cupiditas te-net. Facile id transco. Non laboro de hac re. Per me ista pedibus trahantur. Modice me id tangit. Ne digitum quidem porrigendum in eam utilitatem dicebant, Cic. Manum non verterim, quid de me sentiat, Apul. Haud in magno pono discrimine, Liv. Nihil pensi habere, Quint. Mea causa quaeras vel in medio mari. Alias res agere, Ter. Dum pereas, nihil interdico, dicant vivere, Plaut. Illud mea nihilo pluris refert, quam si ad sepulchrum mortuo dicas jocum, Id. Ranarum palustrium major est mihi cura, quam rerum istarum. Nihil moveri, Prop. Nullarum rerum candidatus est, Sen.
units.tr: Non curare: To hold nothing back. No desire of this holds me. I pass that over easily. I am not troubled about this matter. Let those things be dragged by the feet for all I care. It touches me slightly. They said that not even a finger should be lifted for such an advantage, Cic. I would not lift a hand over what he thinks of me, Apul. I do not put it in great peril, Liv. To have no scruple, Quint. Seek me even in the middle of the sea. I am busy with other things, Ter. Provided you perish, I forbid nothing; let them say you live, Plaut. That matters no more to me than if you told a joke to a dead man at his tomb, Id. The care of marsh frogs means more to me than those affairs. To be moved by nothing, Prop. He is a candidate for nothing, Sen.

units.la: Curat quisque sua] Sagittario pharetra curae est.
units.tr: Curat quisque sua: The quiver is the archer's concern.

units.la: Curabo res meas ipsemet] Mihi curae erit hoc negotium. Mihi ipse balneum ministrabo.
units.tr: Curabo res meas ipsemet: This business will be my own concern. I will serve my own bath myself.

units.la: Curas interdum remittere] Miscere gaudia curis.
units.tr: Curas interdum remittere: To mix joys with cares.

units.la: Cura alia post aliam] Fluctus fluctum excipit.
units.tr: Cura alia post aliam: One wave follows another.

units.la: Curatio] Procuratio aedium sacrarum alicui commissa. Provisio posteri temporis, Cic. Procuratio hortorum Veneris est, Var.
units.tr: Curatio: The management of a sacred building entrusted to someone. Provision for a later time, Cic. The management of gardens belongs to Venus, Var.

units.la: Curia] Praetorium. Sedes ac templum publici consilii. Senatus, Cic. Senaculum, Val. Max.
units.tr: Curia: A council chamber. The seat and temple of a public council. The senate, Cic. A small senate house, Val. Max.

units.la: Curio] Magister curiae, Plaut. Hetaeriarcha, Bud. Caput contubernii, Alc. ex Cic. Magister contubernii, Crom. Praefectus sodalitio. Tribunus & tribuum magister, Henr. Steph.
units.tr: Curio: Master of the curia, Plaut. Leader of a club, Bud. Head of a fellowship, Alc. from Cic. Master of a fellowship, Crom. Prefect of a sodality. Tribune and master of the tribes, Henr. Steph.

units.la: Curiositas] Appetitus rerum novarum, Amm. Panurgia, Quint. Curiosum est ea scire velle, quae ad nos non pertinent, pro curiositas est, Cic.
units.tr: Curiositas: Desire for new things, Amm. Panurgia, Quint. It is curiosity to wish to know those things that do not pertain to us, Cic.

units.la: Curiosus] Curiosulus, Apul. Percuriosus, Cic. Musca est pater meus, Plaut. Philotheoros, Cupidus spectaculorum, Cicer.
units.tr: Curiosus: A little inquisitive, Apul. Very inquisitive, Cic. My father is a busybody, Plaut. Philotheoros, a lover of spectacles, Cic.

units.la: Curiosus circa aliena] Agros alienos irrigas tuis sitientibus. Jupiter quomodo duxerit Junonem novit. Peregrinum negotium ad suas molestias trahere. Alieno choro pedem inferre. Alienum fundum arare. Alias prospiciens, non sibi.
units.tr: Curiosus circa aliena: You irrigate other men's fields for your own thirsty ones. Jupiter knows how he has led Juno. To drag a foreign business into one's own troubles. To set foot in another's dance. To plough another man's field. Looking out for others and not for oneself.

units.la: Curiosus loquax] Curiosus idem & garrulus.
units.tr: Curiosus loquax: Inquisitive and also a chatterbox.

units.la: Curiosi exploratores] Curiosus idem ac delator.
units.tr: Curiosi exploratores: Inquisitive is the same as informer.

units.la: Currere] Cursum aliquò tendere, Liv. Contendere cursum, Plaut. Contendere ad, in. Contendere iter. Ferri, Cic. Ferri rapidè, Virg. Meare, Lucr. Ingredi cursim.
units.tr: Currere: To direct one's course somewhere, Liv. To make haste on the course, Plaut. To hasten to or into. To hurry on a journey. To be carried along, Cic. To be borne swiftly, Virg. To flow, Lucr. To go quickly.

units.la: Currere certatim] Vid. Certatim.
units.tr: To run eagerly, vying with one another] See Certatim.

units.la: Curriculo currere] Volare. Rapere se. Inflammato studio rapitur classis, Cic. Contendere magnis itineribus, Caf. Passibus rapidis ferri, Virg. Cursu magno, Cic. Admisso passu sequi, Ovid.
units.tr: To run at full speed] To fly. To hurry oneself. "The fleet is swept along by inflamed zeal," Cic. To press on with great marches, Caes. To be carried with rapid steps, Virg. With great speed, Cic. To follow with a quickened pace, Ovid.

units.la: Curriculum] Stadium, Cic. Xystus, Vitr. Curriculum stadii, Gell. Circus, Cic. Agonium, Scal. Campus Martius, Caf. Stadiodromus, pro loco Robert. Heptastadium, Amm. Hiera, Sen. Media linea in stadio.
units.tr: Racecourse] A stadium, Cic. A xystus, Vitr. The course of a stadium, Gell. A circus, Cic. An arena for contests, Scal. The Campus Martius, Caes. Stadiodromus, for the place, Robert. Heptastadium, Amm. Hiera, Sen. A middle line in the stadium.

units.la: In Curriculo currere] Curriculum conficere. Abire curriculo. Stadium currere, Cic.
units.tr: To run the course] To complete the course. To depart from the course. To run the stadium, Cic.

units.la: Currus] Rheda, Cic. Quadrigæ, Hor. Quadrijugus currus, Virg. Bijuge curriculum, Suet. Sarracum, Juv.
units.tr: Chariot] A carriage, Cic. A four-horse chariot, Hor. A four-horse chariot, Virg. A two-horse chariot, Suet. A wagon, Juv.

units.la: Cursus] Curriculum lunæ, Cic. Cursura, Varr. Meatus, Lucr.
units.tr: Course] The course of the moon, Cic. Cursura, Varr. Passage, Lucr.

units.la: Cursor publicus] Gerulus literarum, Plaut. Servus à pedibus, Cic. Hemerodromus, Liv. Armillati cursores.
units.tr: Public courier] A bearer of letters, Plaut. A servant on foot, Cic. Hemerodromus, Liv. Runners with armlets.

units.la: Curtus, Vid. Brevis.
units.tr: Curtus: See Brevis.

units.la: Curvare] Inflectere ferrum, Caf. Lentare arcum, Ovid. Arcuare, Plin. Cornuare, Varr. Concurvare, Macr. Obliquare, Stat. Lunare, Ouid. Detorquere, Virg. Delimare, Varr.
units.tr: To curve] To bend iron, Caes. To bend a bow, Ovid. To arch, Plin. To make horned, Varr. To curve together, Macr. To make oblique, Stat. To crescent, Ovid. To twist aside, Virg. Delimare, Varr.

units.la: Curvatio] Curvatura. Incurvatio. Pravitas & distorsio membrorum. Obliquitas lineæ, Plin. Flexus pulli, Col. Flexura vicorum, Suet. Distortio, Cic. Flexuosa radicum, Pallad. Anfractus viarum, Caf. Curvor, Varr. Cornua maris, i. curvitates, Ovid.
units.tr: Curvature] Curvature. Incurvation. Crookedness and distortion of the limbs. Obliquity of a line, Plin. Bending of a colt, Col. Winding of streets, Suet. Distortion, Cic. Twisting of roots, Pallad. Windings of roads, Caes. Curvature, Varr. The horns of the sea, that is, curves, Ovid.

units.la: Curvus] Incurva arbor, Plin. Flexuosus, Cic. Obliquus, Hor. Sinuosus, Ovid. Distortus, Cic. Obstipus, Col. Indirectus, Quint. Torvus, Perf. Procurvus, Virg. Conflexum jugum montis. In anfractum convoluta cornua, Plin. Pravus. Pandus, Ovid. Enormis, Tacit. Limulus, Plaut. Limus, & Limis, Fest.
units.tr: Curved] A tree bent inward, Plin. Winding, Cic. Oblique, Hor. Sinuous, Ovid. Distorted, Cic. Slanting, Col. Indirect, Quint. Grim-looking, Pers. Bent forward, Virg. A yoke bent together; a mountain ridge bent. Horns curled into a coil, Plin. Crooked. Bent, Ovid. Excessive, Tac. Limulus, Plaut. Limus and Limis, Fest.

units.la: Cuspidatus] Mucronatus. Cacuminatus fastigio. Muricatus. Faftigiatus in mucronem vomer, Plin.
units.tr: Pointed] Sharpened to a point. Topped with a peak. Bristling with spikes. A ploughshare tapering to a point, Plin.

units.la: Cuspis | Fastigium tenue mucronis, Luc. Vid. Acies.
units.tr: Point] The slender tip of a point, Lucan. See Acies.

units.la: Cuspidare, Vid. Acuminare.
units.tr: To point: See Acuminare.

units.la: Custodia] Excubitus, Hirt. Speculatus, Plin. Custodi-tio, Sipont. Excubatio, Val. Max. Custodela, Fest. Vigilia, Cic.
units.tr: Guard] Watch, Hirt. Lookout, Plin. Custody, Sipont. Watching, Val. Max. Guarding, Fest. Vigil, Cic.

units.la: Custodia rerum non cuivis committenda] Canis canistri malus custos.
units.tr: Custody of things not to be entrusted to just anyone] A bad dog is a guard for a basket.

units.la: Custos] Excubitor. Vid. Vigil.
units.tr: Guardian] A watchman. See Vigil.

units.la: Custos rei invidu] Canis in præsepi.
units.tr: Guardian of envied property] A dog in the manger.

units.la: Custodire] Advigilare ad custodiam, Cic. Incubare thesauris, Quint. Inservare volucres, Stat.
units.tr: To guard] To keep watch for the sake of custody, Cic. To brood over treasures, Quint. To keep birds in captivity, Stat.

units.la: Cutis] Corium, hominis vivi, Plaut. Cutis superficies, Gal. Cuticula, Celf.
units.tr: Skin] The hide of a living man, Plaut. The surface of the skin, Gal. The cuticle, Celsus.

units.la: Cynosura] Septemtriones, Plaut. Triopes, Virg. Ursa major, Sen. Arctos, Virg. Helice, Lucan. Plaustrum, Sen. Sarracum, Iuv.
units.tr: Cynosure] The Septentriones, Plaut. Triopes, Virg. The Great Bear, Sen. Arctos, Virg. Helice, Lucan. A wagon, Sen. Sarracum, Juv.

units.la: D.
units.tr: D.

units.la: Dæmon] Spiritus insincerus, Minut. Malus genius. Genius sinister, Perf. Genius ater, Hor. Vid. Cacodamon.
units.tr: Daemon] An insincere spirit, Minut. An evil genius. A sinister genius, Perf. A black genius, Hor. See Cacodaemon.

units.la: Damnabilis] Vituperabilis, improbabilis, accusabilis turpitudo. In pejus notabilis. Cadit in vituperationem. Est in vitio. In vitio ponitur. Tu tibi hoc criminosum fore nunquam putasti, Cic. Improbatus, Vlp. Accusandus, Ter. Culpabilis, Apul. Damnandus, Ovid. Condemnabilis, Pallad. Obelisco dignus.
units.tr: Damnabilis] Blameworthy, reprehensible, censurable baseness. Notable for the worse. It falls into reproach. It lies in fault. It is placed in vice. "You never thought this would be a crime for yourself," Cic. Disapproved, Vlp. To be accused, Ter. Culpable, Apul. Deserving condemnation, Ovid. Condemnable, Pallad. Worthy of the obelisk.

units.la: Damnare, Vid. Condemnare.
units.tr: Damnare, See Condemnare.

units.la: Damnatio] Condemnatio, Vlp. Damnatus, Plaut. Tristis sententia. Ovid. Tristis litera, (fil. C. nam læta est, A; quia inscriptione illius, rei condemnabantur, hujus vero, absolvebantur.) Cic. Sententia sanguinaria, Plin. Iun. Tristior nota, Liv. Theta mortiferum, Mart. Theta nigrum, Perf. Judicium damnatorium, Cic. Tabula damnatoria, Suet.
units.tr: Damnatio] Condemnation, Vlp. Damnation, Plaut. A sad sentence, Ovid. A sad letter (that is, C; for A is the joyful letter, since by the inscription of the one the accused were condemned, but by that of the other they were acquitted), Cic. A bloody sentence, Plin. Iun. A sadder mark, Liv. The deadly theta, Mart. The black theta, Perf. A condemnatory judgment, Cic. A condemnatory tablet, Suet.

units.la: Damnatus] Addictus morti, Cic. Damnatus morti, Lucr. Judicatus pecuniæ, Liv. Judicatus debiti, Gell. Gehennæ mancipium.
units.tr: Damnatus] Given over to death, Cic. Condemned to death, Lucr. Adjudged to pay money, Liv. Adjudged for a debt, Gell. A slave of Gehenna.

units.la: Damnatus voti] Damnata voti Civitas, Sisen. Damnatus voto. Ejus devotionis me esse convictum, lætor, Cic. Voti reus, Virg. Debitor voti, Mart. Damnabis tu quoque votis, Virg. Voto ac promisso tenetur. Debet votum, Cic. Convoti (ejusdem voti) obligatio, Fest.
units.tr: Damnatus voti] A state condemned by its vow, Sisen. Bound by a vow. "I rejoice that I have been convicted of that devotion," Cic. Liable on a vow, Virg. A debtor of a vow, Mart. "You too will be condemned by your vows," Virg. He is bound by vow and promise. He owes a vow, Cic. An obligation of the same vow, Fest.

units.la: Damnosè] Damnosè libere, Hor. Perniciosè & pestiferè multa in civitate scisçuntur, Cic. Nocenter armata crura, Col.
units.tr: Damnose] Ruinously, freely, Hor. Perniciously and destructively, many things are torn apart in the state, Cic. Legs harmfully armed (with spurs), Col.

units.la: Damnosus] Damni conciliabulum. Damnigerulus, Plaut. Scopulus & vorago Reip. Calamitas, pestis, beluo patriæ, Labes & pernicies provinciæ. Bustum Reip, Cic. Fractor ferularum, Sidon. Noxa, Scal. Vid. Nocivus.
units.tr: Damnosus] A meeting-place of loss. A bringer of harm, Plaut. A rock and whirlpool of the commonwealth. A calamity, a plague, a beast of the fatherland, a blight and ruin of a province. A tomb of the commonwealth, Cic. A breaker of rods, Sidon. Harmful, Scal. See Nocivus.

units.la: Damnum] Detrimentum. Incommodum. Jactura. Magnâ mercede (damno) experiri, Cic. Intertrimentum, Plaut. Noxa, Ovid. Noxia, Ulp. Dispendium, Ter. Malefactum, ruina fortunarum. Naufragium bonorum. Calamitas, vulnus, clades Reip. Cic. Transire sine maleficio, maleficentia, Caes. Lucrum malum æquale dispendio.
units.tr: Damnum] Detriment. Inconvenience. Loss. To try something at a great price (loss), Cic. Loss, Plaut. Harm, Ovid. Harmful, Ulp. Expense, Ter. A wrong done, the ruin of fortunes. The shipwreck of goods. Calamity, wound, disaster to the commonwealth, Cic. To pass without injury, mischief, maleficence, Caes. A bad gain equal to the expense.

units.la: Damnum tolerabile] Cum sarcinis enatare. Præstat lanam quam oves amittere.
units.tr: Damnum tolerabile] To swim out with one's baggage. It is better to lose the wool than the sheep.

units.la: Damnum multiplicatum] Cum cane simul & lorum. Manubrium ad perditam securim abjicere.
units.tr: Damnum multiplicatum] The dog and the leash too, together. To throw away the handle along with the lost axe.

units.la: Damnum partiale] Prælio victus, non bello.
units.tr: Damnum partiale] Beaten in a battle, not in the war.

units.la: Damnô meo] Expensum mihi feras. Fraudi mihi erit, Cic. Periculo meo, Plaut. Mea fiduciâ opus conduxi, Id.
units.tr: Damno meo] Let it be entered against me as expense. It will be to my detriment, Cic. At my risk, Plaut. I hired the work on my own confidence, Id.

units.la: Damno accepto prudentior] Flammam passus, metuit flammam. Piscator ictus sapiet. Quæ nocent, docent. Mus piscem gustat. Malo accepto stultus sapit. Post acerba prudentior. Tranquillas etiam, naufragus horret aquas.
units.tr: Damno accepto prudentior] Having suffered a fire, he fears fire. A fisherman who has been stung will be wise. What harms, teaches. The mouse tastes the fish. Having received a bad loss, the fool becomes wise. Wiser after bitter experience. Even calm waters the shipwrecked man dreads.

units.la: Qui semel est læsus fallaci piscis ab hamo;
units.tr: He who has once been wounded by the deceptive hook of a fish,

units.la: Omnibus unca cibis æra subesse putat, Ovid.
units.tr: Thinks that every bait has a hook hidden beneath it, Ovid.

units.la: Damnum ab aliquo avertere] Indemnem servare, Paul. IC. Indemnitati alicujus consulere. Indemnitatem præstare, Ulp. Prohibere aliquem detrimento, calamitate. Consulere samax, fortunæ alicujus. Parcere famæ alicujus, Cic. Habere rationem alicujus, Liv. Defensare à calamitate aliquem. Defendere civium pericula, Cic. Levare injuriam, Cæs. Contueri pecus, Col.
units.tr: Damnum ab aliquo avertere] To keep someone unharmed, Paul. IC. To look after someone's interests. To provide indemnity, Ulp. To keep someone from loss or calamity. To look after someone's fortunes. To spare someone's reputation, Cic. To have regard for someone, Liv. To defend someone from calamity. To defend citizens from dangers, Cic. To relieve an injury, Caes. To look after the flock, Col.

units.la: Damnum dare alicui] Damno esse alicui, Plin. Dare malum alicui, Ter. Afferre, Inferre alicui detrimentum, Cæs. Afficere aliquem incommodo. Dare incommodum. Nocere alicui, aliquid, in aliquâ re, Cic. Nocere noxam. Committere noxam, Paul. IC. Incommodare alicui, Ter. Esse noxæ alicui, Liv. Exitium afferre alicui. Attondere aliquem, Plaut. Pauperare. Admordere, Admutilare aliquem, Id. Oblimare rem patris. Limare commoda, Hor. Arrodere rempubl. Cic.
units.tr: Damnum dare alicui] To be a loss to someone, Plin. To give someone trouble, Ter. To bring detriment upon someone, Caes. To inflict inconvenience on someone. To give harm. To harm someone, or something, in some matter, Cic. To do harm. To commit a wrong, Paul. IC. To inconvenience someone, Ter. To be a harm to someone, Liv. To bring ruin upon someone. To clip someone's wings, Plaut. To impoverish. To bite at and maim someone, Id. To squander a father's property. To whittle away advantages, Hor. To gnaw at the commonwealth, Cic.

units.la: Damnum pati] Detrimentum accipere, capere, facere. Damnum facere, contrahere. Plagam, calamitatem, cladem accipere. Jacturam rei familiaris facere. Obest mihi aliquid, Cic. Accipere jacturam. Est mihi id noxæ. Vertit mihi id in perniciem, Liv. Evenit mihi incommodum. Capere incommodum, Cic. Noxam contrahere, Col. Pati jacturam, Id. Evenit mihi damnum. Disconducit, Plaut. Obnoxium esse, Plin.
units.tr: Damnum pati] To receive a loss, to take it, to suffer it. To incur a loss. To receive a blow, a calamity, a defeat. To suffer a loss in household property. Something is harmful to me, Cic. To receive a loss. It is a ruin to me. It turns to my destruction, Liv. An inconvenience befalls me. To take an inconvenience, Cic. To incur harm, Col. To suffer a loss, Id. A loss befalls me. It is unprofitable, Plaut. To be liable to harm, Plin.

units.la: Dapes, Vid. Cibus.
units.tr: Dapes, See Cibus.

units.la: Dapsilis, Vid. Opiparus.
units.tr: Dapsilis, See Opiparus.

units.la: Dare] Deferre, tribuere, largiri, præbere, impertiri alicui laudem, vel, tantum laudis, quantum meretur. Impertitur illi laus. Contribuere laudem alicui. Largiri, conferre aliquid ad aliquem. Facere copiam consilii. Mandare alicui honores. Concedere alicui primum locum, Cic. Præstare alicui salutem, Sen. Propinare aliquid alicui, Enn. Irrigare, Quint.
units.tr: Dare] To bestow, attribute, grant, provide, or impart praise to someone, or as much praise as he deserves. Praise is imparted to him. To contribute praise to someone. To grant, to confer something upon someone. To supply advice. To entrust honours to someone. To grant someone the first place, Cic. To grant someone safety, Sen. To pour out something for someone, Enn. To water, Quint.

units.la: Non dare] Denegare aliquid alicui, Cic. Denegare dare, Ter. Negare, Ovid. Mihi fortuna divitias invidit, Apul. Per me egebit, Plaut.
units.tr: Non dare] To deny something to someone, Cic. To refuse to give, Ter. To say no, Ovid. Fortune has grudged me riches, Apul. He will go in want because of me, Plaut.

units.la: Non dabo] Non dare, definitum est. Quod dedi datum non vellem, quod reliquum est non dabo. Aliud quidvis impetrari à me facilius perferam, quam ut non, &c. Non remissurus es? pro me responsas tibi. Non remittes? scis jamdujamdudum meam sententiam, Plaut. Non do, Terent.
units.tr: Non dabo] "Not to give" is settled. What I have given, I would not wish to have given; what remains, I will not give. I would more easily bear anything else being obtained from me than that I should not... "You will not release it? I have already answered for myself to you." "You will not remit it? You know my opinion, which I have long held," Plaut. "I do not give," Terent.
