units.la: Si dabis, dabo] Da simul & accipe. Datatim dare se.
units.tr: Si dabis, dabo] Give and take at once. To give oneself in turn.

units.la: Dabam, formula in literis] Data Idibus Juniis Cypro. Quarto Calendas ex castris (subaudi, dabam.) Hæc ad te die &c. Hæc ad te meâ manu. Habes epistolam plenam festinationis, Cic.
units.tr: Dabam, a formula in letters] Given at Cyprus on the Ides of June. Given at the camp on the fourth day before the Kalends (understand "dabam"). Written to you on this day, etc. Written to you in my own hand. You have a letter full of haste, Cic.

units.la: Dapifer] Structor mensæ, Crom.
units.tr: Dapifer] Steward of the table, Crom.

units.la: Datio] Sine meo datu, Plaut. Præstatio fiscalis, Firm. Datum, Cic.
units.tr: Datio] Without my giving, Plaut. A fiscal payment, Firm. A gift, Cic.

units.la: Dator] Largitor. Præbitor, Cic. Tributor, Præstitor, Apul.
units.tr: Dator] A giver. A provider, Cic. A distributor, a bestower, Apul.

units.la: Datum, in literis] Dies literis adscripta, Cic. Subscripta, Bud.
units.tr: Datum, in letters] A date added to letters, Cic. Subscribed, Bud.

units.la: Dea] Diva, Virg. Hor.
units.tr: Dea] A goddess, Virg. Hor.

units.la: Dealbare] Nitorem inducere, Plin. Vid. Albare.
units.tr: Dealbare] To induce brightness, Plin. See Albare.

units.la: Dealbatus] Calicatus. Calce politus, Fest. Calcatus, Sipont. Opere tectorio exornatus, Cic. Tectorio prælitus, Gell. Albarium è calce pura, Vitr.
units.tr: Dealbatus] Whitewashed. Polished with lime, Fest. Trodden in lime, Sipont. Adorned with plaster work, Cic. Coated with plaster, Gell. Whitewashed with pure lime, Vitr.

units.la: Deamare] Amare ut cùm maximè, Ter. Amare plus oculis suis, Catul. Effundi in aliquem. In oculis ferre. Summo studio esse in, Cic. Effusè diligere. Perire aliquem. Perire afflictim aliquem. Deperire, Demori aliquem. Amicus es mihi germanum in modum, Plaut. Deperire amore, Liv. Ardere aliquem, Virg. Usque in delicias amare, Sen. Effundi in amorem alicujus, Tacit. Amore alicujus pectus terere, Prop. Amore flagrare, insanire, Hor.
units.tr: Deamare] To love as much as possible, Ter. To love more than one's own eyes, Catul. To pour oneself out upon someone. To hold someone in one's eyes. To be deeply devoted to someone, Cic. To love someone to distraction. To pine away for someone. To be utterly undone for someone. "You are a friend to me as a brother would be," Plaut. To be consumed with love for someone, Liv. To burn for someone, Virg. To love to excess, Sen. To pour oneself out in love for someone, Tacit. To wear out one's breast for love of someone, Prop. To blaze with love, to be mad with love, Hor.

units.la: Deambulare] Inambulare domi, Plaut. Adambulare ad ostium, Id. Obambulare, Ovid. Facere spacia, Cic. Spatiari in Xysta, Id. Spatiari per, Plin. Cornicari secum, i. e. solum ambulare, Casaub.
units.tr: Deambulare] To walk about indoors, Plaut. To walk up to the door, Id. To walk around, Ovid. To take exercise, Cic. To stroll on the xystus, Id. To stroll through, Plin. To croak to oneself, i.e. merely to walk alone, Casaub.

units.la: Deambulatio] Ambulatio. Inambulatio. Ambulatiuncula, Cic. Obambulatio hominum, ad Heren.
units.tr: Deambulatio] Walking, strolling, walking about indoors, a little stroll, Cic. A crowd of people walking about, ad Heren.

units.la: Deargentare] Incoquere argentum alicui rei. Inargentatus, Plin.
units.tr: Deargentare] To fuse silver onto something. Silver-plated, Plin.

units.la: Deartuare] Membratim cædere, dividere, Plin. Articulatim membra dividere, Cic. Artuatim concidere, Firm.
units.tr: Deartuare] To cut the limbs up piece by piece, to divide them, Plin. To divide the limbs joint by joint, Cic. To cut to pieces at the joints, Firm.

units.la: Deasciare] Dedolare partes putridas, Col. Dolabrâ abradere, dere, Col. Derimcinare, Plaut. Polire ascià, Cic. Circumdolare, Plin.
units.tr: Deasciare] To hew away putrid parts, Col. To scrape away with an axe, Col. To trim away, Plaut. To polish with an adze, Cic. To hew around, Plin.

units.la: Deaurare, Vid. Inaurare.
units.tr: Deaurare, See Inaurare.

units.la: Deauratus, Vid. Inauratus.
units.tr: Deauratus, See Inauratus.

units.la: Debacchari in aliquem] Invehi in aliquem. Insatiabilem crudelitatem in aliquo exercere. Depromere, saturare crudelitatem suam. Omni crudelitate aliquem lacerare, Cic. Protelare saevis dictis aliquem, Ter. Intonuit perniciosa voce collega. Saevire in aliquem, Liv. Fulminat armis Æneas, Virg. Grassari in aliquem, Plaut. Grassari adversus aliquem, Suet. Desævire in aliquem, Claud. Expleri crudelitas alicujus aliqua re non potest, Cic.
units.tr: Debacchari in aliquem] To rage against someone. To exercise insatiable cruelty upon someone. To unleash and glut one's cruelty. To tear someone apart with every cruelty, Cic. To hound someone with savage words, Ter. The colleague thundered with a deadly voice. To rage against someone, Liv. Aeneas thunders with arms, Virg. To rage upon someone, Plaut. To rage against someone, Suet. To storm furiously against someone, Claud. The cruelty of someone cannot be satisfied by anything, Cic.

units.la: Debellare aliquem] Subigere bello aliquem, Lucr. Liv. Expugnare oppida, Plaut. Profligare hostes. Facere stragem, edere. Conficere & opprimere hostes. Effligere aliquem, Cic. Fœdant & proterunt hostium copias, Plaut. Dare stragem. Sternere catervas hostium, Prosternere aciem, Liv. Fundere copias, Cæs.
units.tr: Debellare aliquem] To subdue someone in war, Lucr. Liv. To storm towns, Plaut. To rout enemies. To make a slaughter. To crush and overwhelm the enemy. To lay someone low, Cic. They crush and trample the enemy forces, Plaut. To inflict a slaughter. To scatter the enemy bands, to lay the line low, Liv. To rout the forces, Caes.

units.la: Debellato] Debellatum est, Liv. Depugnato prælio, Plaut. Sub hac pessimi exempli victoria, Liv. Confecta res est, Cicer.
units.tr: Debellato] It has been decided by war, Liv. The battle having been fought out, Plaut. After this victory of the worst example, Liv. The business is finished, Cic.

units.la: Debere] Laborare ex ære alieno, Cæs. Laborare fœnore, Liv. In nummis esse alicujus. Nomina facere. Grandem pecuniam debere, Cic.
units.tr: Debere] To be struggling with debt, Caes. To be labouring under usury, Liv. To be in someone's books for money. To run up debts. To owe a great sum of money, Cic.

units.la: Debere alicui multa] Magnopere illi debeo. Debeo illius omnia. Animam illi debeo. Devinctum, obstrictum me habet. Obligavit me sibi. Acceptum illi refero, quod vivam, Cic. Oculos alicui debere, Catul. Debitor sum vitæ, Ovid. Obnoxii sibi erimus propter hanc rem, Plaut.
units.tr: Debere alicui multa] I owe him a great deal. I owe him everything. I owe him my life. He holds me bound and obligated. He has bound me to himself. I credit to him that I am alive, Cic. To owe someone one's eyes, Catul. I am a debtor to life, Ovid. "We shall be bound to them over this matter," Plaut.

units.la: Qui debet, solvat] Qui non habet in ære, luat in corpore.
units.tr: He who owes, let him pay] He who has nothing in his purse, let him pay with his body.

units.la: Debilis] Imbecillis natura. Perimbecillus. Imbellis. Perinfirmus. Remissus. Languidus. Vacillans amicitia. Impotens & insanus, Cic. Debile homo, Enn. Laxus, Virg. Vacuus virium, Plaut. Fluidi lacerti, Ovid. Virium modicarum, Paterc. Delumbis. Fragilis. Fluidus. Dilabidus. Obnoxius, Plin. Invalidus, Liv. Enervis, Quint. Vietus senex, Ter. Ter. Quassabile munimen. Lucr. Lapsabunda fundamenta, Sen. Elumbis, Elumbus, Fest. Ficulnus gladius. Tenuis spes. Tener animus, Cic. Fictilis homo. Languidior tenerâ betâ,Catul. Plumbeo gladio jugulare. Debile homo,Lipf. ex Enn.
units.tr: Weak] Weak by nature. Very feeble. Unwarlike. Very infirm. Slack. Languid. Wavering friendship. Powerless and mad, Cic. A feeble man, Enn. Loose, Virg. Empty of strength, Plaut. Limp arms, Ovid. Of modest strength, Paterc. Weak in the loins. Frail. Fluid, limp. Crumbling. Vulnerable, Plin. Feeble, Liv. Enervated, Quint. A worn-out old man, Ter. Ter. A defence that can be shaken. Lucr. Crumbling foundations, Sen. Weak in the loins, Fest. A fig-wood sword. A slender hope. A tender spirit, Cic. A man of clay. More drooping than a tender beet, Catul. To cut one's throat with a leaden sword. A feeble man, Lipsius, from Ennius.

units.la: Debilitare] Enervare vires, Hor. Languorem afferre. Membra solvere. Incidere vires, pennas. Dare ad languorem, Cic. Infirmare, Liv. Subnervare, Apul. Labefacere, Ter. Convellere vires,Celf. Vires infringere, Prop. Solvere, Ovid. Collabefactare, Id. Nervos frangere, Quint. Delumbare, Plin.
units.tr: Weaken] To sap the strength, Hor. To bring on languor. To loosen the limbs. To cut off strength, as one clips wings. To bring to languor, Cic. To weaken, Liv. To unnerve, Apul. To shake, Ter. To overthrow the strength, Celsus. To break the strength, Prop. To loosen, Ovid. To overthrow utterly, Id. To break the sinews, Quint. To weaken the loins, Plin.

units.la: Debilitari] Labare, Deficere me incipiunt vires. Vacillat. Frigere, Cic. Labascere, Lucr. Lentescunt tempore curæ, Ovid. Flaccessere, Col. Fragescere, Non. Frangi. Infirmari. Inveterascit fervor, Cic. Inclinatæ sunt vires. Torpere, Liv. Relentescit amor, Ovid. Succidunt genua, Plaut. Infuscatur vox, Plin. Exolescere, Tacit. Rapidè se habere, Suet. Resolvuntur homines vino, Celf.
units.tr: Be weakened] To totter; my strength begins to fail me. It wavers. To grow cold, Cic. To grow faint, Lucr. Cares grow slack with time, Ovid. To wither, Col. To grow feeble, Non. To be broken. To be weakened. Ardour grows old, Cic. Strength is bent down. To grow numb, Liv. Love grows cold, Ovid. The knees give way, Plaut. The voice becomes dim, Plin. To fade away, Tacit. To be in a rapid state, Suet. Men are loosened by wine, Celsus.

units.la: Debilitas] Imbecillitas. Infirmitas. Infractio animi. Fragilitas, Cic. Impotentia, Ter. Invalentia, Apul. Languor corporis, animi, Cic.
units.tr: Weakness] Feebleness. Infirmity. Breaking of spirit. Fragility, Cic. Powerlessness, Ter. Lack of vigour, Apul. Languor of body or mind, Cic.

units.la: Debiliter] Languidè procedere, Col. Infirmè animatus. Imbecillius assentiri. Remissè agere. Remissius dicere. Jejunè disputare, Cic. Infœcundè & jejunè laudare, Gell. Leviter eruditus, Cic. Vapidè se habere, Suet. Digitulis primoribus tenere aliquid, Plaut.
units.tr: Weakly] To proceed languidly, Col. Feebly spirited. To assent with too little conviction. To act in a slack manner. To speak in too slack a way. To argue dryly, Cic. To praise barrenly and dryly, Gell. Slightly learned, Cic. To conduct oneself flatly, Suet. To hold something only with the tips of the fingers, Plaut.

units.la: Debitor] Æratus homo. Nomen, pro debitore, Omnia debet præter animam, Cic. Animam debet, Ter. Trico nummarius, Lucil.
units.tr: Debtor] A man in debt. A noun for a debtor. He owes everything except his soul, Cic. He owes his soul, Ter. A petty money-changer, Lucil.

units.la: Debitum] Æs alienum. Nomen, Cic. Creditum, Credita pecunia, Sen.
units.tr: Debt] Another's money, borrowed. A noun, Cic. Money lent, borrowed money, Sen.

units.la: Debitum contrahere] Æs alienum facere, cogere, conflare. Alieno ære opprimi. Incidere in æs alienum, Cic.
units.tr: To incur debt] To make, compel, or pile up other people's money. To be overwhelmed by borrowed money. To fall into debt, Cic.

units.la: Debitum exigere] Nomen vel nomina exigere. De nomine compellare aliquem, Cic.
units.tr: To collect a debt] To call in a debt or debts. To press someone for payment of a debt, Cic.

units.la: Debitum solvere] Ære alieno se liberare. Ære alieno exire. Levare æs alienum. Nomina explicare, expedire, dissolvere, vere, Cic. Luere æs alienum, Curt. Nominibus respondere, Sen. Nomina expungere, Plaut.
units.tr: To pay a debt] To free oneself from borrowed money. To get out of debt. To lift debt. To settle, clear, or dissolve accounts, Cic. To pay off a debt, Curt. To answer to one's creditors, Sen. To strike off the accounts, Plaut.

units.la: Decalogus] Decem verba, Isid. Duæ tabulæ legis. Duarum tabularum lex, ut apud Romanos duodecim tabularum leges. Testamenti tabulæ. Tabulæ lapideæ, scriptæ digito Dei, ex Gr.
units.tr: Decalogue] The ten words, Isid. The two tables of the law. The law of the two tables, as among the Romans the laws of the twelve tables. The tables of the covenant. Tables of stone, written with the finger of God, ex Gr.

units.la: Decantatus, Vid. Notus.
units.tr: Decantatus, see Notus.

units.la: Decem] Deni humores, Cic. Bis quinque. Bis quini, Virg. Mart. Decas, Sipont. Decussis, Vitr. Decuria, Trebell.
units.tr: Ten] Ten humours, Cic. Twice five. Twice five each, Virg. Mart. A decade, Sipont. A cross-grid, Vitr. A group of ten, Trebell.

units.la: Decemvir]Decem primi, Cic. Decaproti, Vlp. Demiurgus, Liv.
units.tr: Decemvir] The first ten, Cic. Ten magistrates, Ulp. A demiurge, Liv.

units.la: Decemviratus] Collegium decimvirale, Cic. Decemprimatus, Bud. Decaprotia, Id.
units.tr: Decemvirate] A college of decemvirs, Cic. The first ten, Bud. The office of ten magistrates, Id.

units.la: Decus] Congruens. Consentaneus. Perappositus. Forma apposita ad dignitatem. Idoneum dignitate tuâ, Cic. Perdecorum, Plin.
units.tr: Fitness] Agreeing. Consonant. Very well suited. A form suited to dignity. Fitting your dignity, Cic. Very becoming, Plin.

units.la: Decenter] Decentissimè. Decorè. Ad rerum dignitatem aptè loqui. Minimè indecore. Convenienter. Ritè. Bono modo, Cic. Competenter. Competentissimè, Apul. Condignè. Condecenter. Condecore, Gell.
units.tr: Becomingly] Most becomingly. Decorously. To speak fittingly to the dignity of the matter. Not at all unseemly. In harmony. Duly. In a proper manner, Cic. Suitably. Most suitably, Apul. Worthily. Becomingly. Decently, Gell.

units.la: Decentia] Decentiam oculi judicant. Decorum. Condetentia, Cic. Congruentia, Plin.
units.tr: Decency] Judges of decency by the eye. Propriety. Seemliness, Cic. Harmony, Plin.

units.la: Deceptio] Fructratio, Varr. Fraudatio. Captio. Fucus. Circumscriptio, Cic. Prævaricatio, Plin. Circumductio argenti, Plaut. Fallacies, Apul.
units.tr: Deception] Frustration, Varr. Fraud. Trickery. Deceit. Trickery, Cic. Prevarication, Plin. The shifting about of silver, Plaut. Fallacies, Apul.

units.la: Deceptor] Defraudator, Sen. Fraudator. Circumscriptor. Ex fraude, fallaciis, mendaciis constat totus, Cic. Impostor, Vlp. Præstigiator, Plaut. Præstrigiator, Camer. Callens miris modis ad fallendum, Amm. Architector, Vlp. Vid. Dolosus. Veterator.
units.tr: Deceiver] A defrauder, Sen. A cheat. A swindler. Made wholly of fraud, falsehoods and lies, Cic. An impostor, Ulp. A juggler, Plaut. A juggler, Camer. One skilled in wondrous ways of deceiving, Amm. A contriver, Ulp. See Dolosus. Veterator.

units.la: Deceptor deceptorum decipit] Cretensis Cretensem.
units.tr: The deceiver deceives the deceivers] A Cretan deceives a Cretan.

units.la: Decernere]Pronunciare. Pronunciare sententiam, judicium, Cic. Edicto sancire. Edictum edicere. Decreto statuere, Cic. Interloqui, Vlp.
units.tr: To decree] To pronounce. To pronounce a sentence or judgement, Cic. To sanction by edict. To issue an edict. To determine by decree, Cic. To give an interlocutory ruling, Ulp.

units.la: Decerperefructus] Decerpere fœtus arborum, Plin. Legere mala ex arbore, Virg. Deligere ficus, Fest. Ovid. Vellere mala, Tibull. Intervellere poma, Col. Stringere glandes, Plin. Cogere oleam, Cat.
units.tr: To pick fruit] To pluck the fruit of trees, Plin. To gather apples from a tree, Virg. To pick figs, Fest. Ovid. To pluck apples, Tibull. To pluck apples off, Col. To strip acorns, Plin. To gather olives, Cato.

units.la: Decet] Simulare non dedecet. Convenit in me aliquid. Consonum est, Consentaneum est, quæ personis consentiunt. Rectum est. Est humanitatis vestræ. Boni judicis est. Cadit, vel non cadit in illum, Cic. Addecet. Condecet. Aliam ætatem aliud factum convenit, Plaut. Competit illi, Suet. Meum est, Ter. Facias, quod te dignum est, Id.
units.tr: It is fitting] It is not unseemly to pretend. Something suits me. It is consonant; it is consistent, when things agree with the persons. It is right. It befits your courtesy. It befits a good judge. It falls, or does not fall, upon him, Cic. It is becoming. It is suitable. Another age suits another deed, Plaut. It suits him, Suet. It is mine to do, Ter. Do what is worthy of you, Id.

units.la: Decidere] Vid Cadere.
units.tr: To fall] See Cadere.

units.la: Decidere] Vid Dijudicare.
units.tr: To decide] See Dijudicare.

units.la: Decidunt folia] Folia arboribus decidunt. Nudatur arbor foliis. Deperdunt arbores folia. Cadunt arbori folia. Arbor folia amittit. Plin. Ex arboribus cadunt folia, Plaut.
units.tr: The leaves fall] The leaves fall from the trees. The tree is stripped of its leaves. The trees lose their leaves. The leaves drop from the tree. The tree sheds its leaves, Plin. The leaves fall from the trees, Plaut.

units.la: Deciduus] Cornua cervorum decidua. Capilli defluì, Plin.
units.tr: Deciduous] The horns of stags are deciduous. The hair falls out, Plin.

units.la: Decima] Decuma. Decuma pars, Cic. Decima pars, Plaut.
units.tr: Tenth] A tithe. A tenth part, Cic. A tenth part, Plaut.

units.la: Decimus] Posterior nono est, undecimóque prior.
units.tr: Tenth] It comes after the ninth and before the eleventh.

units.la: Decimus octavus] Duodevicesimus. Octavus decimus, Plin.
units.tr: Eighteenth] Eighteenth. Eighth tenth, Plin.

units.la: Decipere aliquem] Fallere aliquem, Cic. Caf. Dare verba alicui. In errorem inducere. Fucum facere. Fraudare. Imponere alicui. Ludere, deludere aliquem. Pervertere aliquem aliquo artificio. Circumvenire, Circumscribere aliquem, Cic. Defraudare. Sublinere os alicui. Intervenire aliquem. Verba alicui per diverticulum dare. Adire manum alicui. Tangere aliquem bolo. Palpum alicui obtrudere. Perfabricare aliquem, Plaut. Supplantare, Sipont. Quasi pedem supponere, Non. Eludere aliquem, Hor. Obrepere alicui, Ulp. Ille contrà calvi se ratus, Salust. Circumducere aliquem per dolos. Fucum facere alicui, Plaut.
units.tr: To deceive someone] To mislead someone, Cic. Caf. To throw dust in someone's eyes. To lead into error. To make a fool of. To cheat. To defraud. To impose upon someone. To play with, to mock someone. To pervert someone by some trick. To circumvent, to outwit someone, Cic. To defraud. To smear someone's face. To take someone in. To give someone words through a side-passage. To lay a hand on someone. To touch someone with a morsel. To push a fob upon someone. To put someone through his paces, Plaut. To trip up, Sipont. To place a foot as it were, Non. To mock someone, Hor. To creep up on someone, Ulp. Thinking himself bald, Sall. To lead someone astray by tricks. To make a fool of someone, Plaut.

units.la: Decipi] Falli opinione. Duci errore. Labi per errorem. In magno errore esse, versari. Objectus est mihi error. Inducì, rapi in errorem. Hallucinari, Abs. Hallucinari aliquid. Fefellit me, vel spem meam aliquid. Rapi in fraudem, in errorem. Inferri in fraudem. Decepit exspectationem meam. Optatis meis non respondit, Cic. Imprudenti mihi obrepsit, Plaut. Deerravi sententia, Col. In cassum hiavit, Apul. Procul avius erras. Longè avius à verâ ratione vagaris, Lucr. Excidit uxore, Ter. Spe præsumptâ frustratus, Amm. Murem cepit decipula, Adag.
units.tr: To be deceived] To be mistaken in one's opinion. To be led by error. To slip through error. To be in great error, to be caught in it. Error has been thrown at me. To be led on, carried away into error. To wander in mistake, Abs. To be wrong about something. Something has deceived me, or disappointed my hope. To be carried away into fraud or error. To be brought into fraud. It has disappointed my expectation. It has not answered my wishes, Cic. It crept up on me when I was unaware, Plaut. I have strayed from the opinion, Col. It gaped in vain, Apul. You stray far away. You wander far from the true reasoning, Lucr. He lost his wife, Ter. Cheated by a hope taken in advance, Amm. The mouse was caught by the trap, Adag.

units.la: Decipi facilis] Cui verba dare facilè est, Ter.
units.tr: Easily deceived] One to whom it is easy to give fair words, Ter.

units.la: Declarare] Illustrare dubia. Illuminare. Lumen verbis adhibere. Afferre lucis aliquid rei. Afferre lumen memoriæ. Dilucidare rem, Cic. Dare lumen rei, Quint. Clarificare, Sipont. Gaudeo me nactum esse opportunitatem, quâ meum erga te amorem declarare possim, Er.
units.tr: To declare] To clear up doubtful matters. To illuminate. To bring light to words. To shed light on a thing. To bring light to the memory. To make a matter clear, Cic. To give light to a matter, Quint. To make clear, Sipont. I rejoice that I have found an opportunity by which I may declare my love for you, Er.

units.la: Declaratio] Illustramentum. Illustratio, Quint. Lumen. Lux, Cic.
units.tr: Declaration] An illustration. An illustrating, Quint. Light. A light, Cic.

units.la: Declinare ab aliquo] Retrahere se ab ictu, Ovid. Declinare ictum, Liv. Refugere tela. Subterfugere periculum, Cic. vid. Vitare.
units.tr: To decline from someone] To draw oneself back from a blow, Ovid. To decline a blow, Liv. To flee from missiles. To escape danger, Cic. See Vitare.

units.la: Declivis] Proclivum solum, Varr. Devexus molliter collis. Clivosus locus, Col. Cliva loca, Cat. Inclinatus, Pallad.
units.tr: Sloping] Sloping ground, Varr. A gently sloping hill. A hilly place, Col. Sloping places, Cat. Inclined, Pallad.

units.la: Declivitas] Devexitas loci, Plin. Proclive. Proclivitas. Clivus, Cic. Terræ libramentum in alteram partem propensius, Col.
units.tr: Slope] The sloping of a place, Plin. A slope. Steepness. A hill, Cic. The levelling of the ground tilting more to the other side, Col.

units.la: Decoctum] Decoctura, Plin.
units.tr: Decoction] A decoction, Plin.

units.la: Decollare] Capite plectere aliquem. Obtruncare puerum. Jugulare aliquem. Securi aliquem ferire, Cic. Decidere alicui collum, Plaut. Decutere ense caput, Ovid. Capite punire, Plin. Iun. Truncare, Val. Argon. Demutilare virgarum cacumina. Præcidere uno ictu arborem, Col. Detruncare caput, Ovid. Caput ense auferre, Virg. Capite diminuere.
units.tr: To behead] To punish someone by the head. To cut off a boy's head. To cut a man's throat. To strike someone with an axe, Cic. To cut off the neck, Plaut. To strike off the head with a sword, Ovid. To punish by beheading, Plin. Iun. To cut off, Val. Argon. To lop off the tips of branches. To cut through a tree with one blow, Col. To cut off the head, Ovid. To take off the head with a sword, Virg. To diminish by beheading.

units.la: Decollatus] Jugulatus, Ovid.
units.tr: Beheaded] Having its throat cut, Ovid.

units.la: Decolor, vid. Deformis.
units.tr: Discoloured, see Deformis.

units.la: Decoquere] Defervefacere, Plin. Usque coquitare, dum dimidium excoquas, Cat.
units.tr: To boil down] To make boil away, Plin. To keep boiling until you have boiled half away, Cato.

units.la: Decorare, vid. Ornare.
units.tr: To adorn, see Ornare.

units.la: Decor] Decus senectutis. Decora fanorum. Lumen. Splendor. Ornamentum, Ornatus. Exornatio, Cic. Decoramen majorum, Sil. Decoramenta, Arnob. Honestamento virtus non eget, Sen. Color, Venus, Quint.
units.tr: Ornament] The adornment of old age. The adornments of temples. Brightness. Splendour. Ornament, decoration. Embellishment, Cic. The glory of ancestors, Sil. Adornments, Arnob. Virtue needs no embellishment, Sen. Colour, charm, Quint.

units.la: Decoratus[ Cultus, politus, perpolitus in dicendo. Perornatus, expolitus, exornatus. Quo nihil potest esse pictius. Tinctus elegantia, literis, Cic. Decoribus armis, Salust. Speciosa eloquentia, Quint. vid. Pulcher.
units.tr: Adorned] Cultivated, polished, perfectly polished in speaking. Highly embellished, refined, decorated. Than which nothing can be more finely painted. Steeped in elegance and letters, Cic. With splendid arms, Sall. Eloquence that is fair to look upon, Quint. See Pulcher.

units.la: Decorè] Ornatè : Concinnè, politè, splendidè dicere. Luculentè scribere, Cic. Comtè, Fest. vid. Pulchrè.
units.tr: Becomingly] To speak elegantly, neatly, polished, splendidly. To write brilliantly, Cic. Neatly, Fest. See Pulchre.

units.la: Decorus] Decori perquam studiosus. Omnia accuratè, decenter, ad amussim agit. Homo è palæstra. Palæstrâ constitutus.
units.tr: Becoming] Very keen on propriety. He does everything carefully, becomingly, exactly by the rule. A man from the wrestling-school. Trained in the wrestling-ground.

units.la: Decrementum] Detrimentum sentit dies, Sen. Decrescentia, Senium lunæ, Vitr.
units.tr: Decrease] The day feels the loss, Sen. A waning; the old age of the moon, Vitr.

units.la: Decrescere, vid. Minuitur.
units.tr: To decrease, see Minuitur.

units.la: Decretorius, vid. Irrevocabilis, Hor.
units.tr: Decretorius, see Irrevocabilis, Hor.

units.la: Decretum] Sententia. De consilii sententiâ pronunciant, Cic. Pronunciatio, Edictum, Id.
units.tr: Decretum] A sentence or decision. They announce by the opinion of the council, Cic. A proclamation, an edict, Id.

units.la: Decretus] Decreta supplicatio. Indictum funus, Cic.
units.tr: Decretus] A decreed thanksgiving. A funeral appointed by public decree, Cic.

units.la: Decumbere] Collocare se in cubili. Ponere se toro, Ovid. Componere se thalamo, Virg. Sternere corpus somno, Liv. Dare corpus somno, Ovid. Quin lectis nos actutum commendamus? Plaut.
units.tr: Decumbere] To lay oneself down in bed. To place oneself on a couch, Ovid. To lie down in the bridal chamber, Virg. To stretch the body out in sleep, Liv. To give the body to sleep, Ovid. Why do we not commit ourselves to our beds at once? Plaut.

units.la: Decuria] Contubernium, Amm.
units.tr: Decuria] A tent-group, a company sharing a tent, Amm.

units.la: Decurio] Decanus. Caput Contubernii, Veget. Decarchus, Vall.
units.tr: Decurio] A dean. The head of a tent-group, Veget. A decarch, Vall.

units.la: Decurrere] Cursum conficere. Ad callem decurrere, Cic. Contingere cursu metam, Horat. Tangere metam, Ovid.
units.tr: Decurrere] To complete a course. To run down to the narrow path, Cic. To touch the goal in the race, Horat. To touch the turning-post, Ovid.

units.la: Decurtare, vid. Contrahere.
units.tr: Decurtare, see Contrahere.

units.la: Decussare] Ducere lineas duas obliquas in decusses, Plin. In tetrantem devidere, Aggun.
units.tr: Decussare] To draw two oblique lines crossing like an X, Plin. To divide into four parts, Aggun.

units.la: Decussatim] In crucem expansa vela, Fest. Cancellatim reticulatus, Cancellato implexu brachiorum, Plin.
units.tr: Decussatim] Sails spread out in the form of a cross, Fest. Latticed like a net or grating; with arms crossed in a lattice, Plin.

units.la: Decedet] Indignus es, qui faceres. Non est mea simulatio, Ter. Non cadit in bonum virum mentiri. Si quid decedeat in illis, vitemus & nos, Cic. Indecet, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Decedet] You are unworthy to do it. It is not my pretence, Ter. It does not befit a good man to lie. If anything in them is unbecoming, let us also avoid it, Cic. It is unbecoming, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Dedecus] Ego has indignitates diutius patiar? Liv. Flagitium. Magnum pauperies opprobrium, jubet & quidvis facere, & pati, Horat. vid. Contumelia.
units.tr: Dedecus] Shall I endure these indignities any longer? Liv. A disgraceful act. Poverty is a great reproach; it bids a man to do and suffer anything, Horat. See Contumelia.

units.la: Dedere se] Deditionem facere, Quint. Subire, Caes. Concedere in deditionem alicujus, Liv. Dedere manus, Lucr. Dare manus; Cic. Arma submittere. Vitam rogare, Sen. Emancipare se alicui, Plaut. Substernere, Val. M. Submittere tere fasces, Cic. Dare, porrigere alicui herbam, Fest. id est, palmam, vel victoriam, Non.
units.tr: Dedere se] To make a surrender, Quint. To submit, Caes. To yield oneself into someone's surrender, Liv. To give up one's hands, Lucr. To give one's hands; Cic. To lay down one's arms. To beg for one's life, Sen. To hand oneself over to someone, Plaut. To prostrate oneself, Val. M. To lower the fasces, Cic. To offer someone a herb, Fest. that is, the palm or victory, Non.

units.la: Dedicare librum alicui] Dicare opus nominatim, Plin.
units.tr: Dedicare librum alicui] To dedicate a work to someone by name, Plin.

units.la: Dedicatio] Dicatura. Nuncupatio, Plin. Devotio. Consecratio ædis, Cic. Encoenia, August. Sacratio, Macr. Initia, Liv.
units.tr: Dedicatio] A dedication. A public declaration, Plin. A devotion. The consecration of a temple, Cic. Encaenia, August. A hallowing, Macr. A beginning, Liv.

units.la: Dedignari, vid. Contemnere.
units.tr: Dedignari, see Contemnere.

units.la: Dediscere] Desuescere, Liv. Desuefieri, Varr. Sublata est consuetudo ignoscendi, Cic.
units.tr: Dediscere] To grow unaccustomed to, Liv. To be disaccustomed, Varr. The custom of forgiving has been abolished, Cic.

units.la: Deditiius] Nulla servitus infelicior, quàm meretricum deditium esse. Is plane liber esse desiit, qui vitiorum esse deditius coeperit, Er.
units.tr: Deditiius] No slavery is more wretched than to be given over to harlots. He who has begun to be given over to vices has plainly ceased to be free, Er.

units.la: Deditus] Submissus alicui. Nulli naturæ subjectus est Deus, Cic. Qui in ditione, potestate, imperio alterius est. Mancipatus alicui, Id. Obnoxius alicui, Plaut. Sapiens nullius mali patiens est, Sen. Emancipatus miles fœminæ, Hor. Devotus, Cæs. Obnoxiosus, Plaut.
units.tr: Deditus] Submitted to someone. God is subject to no nature, Cic. One who is in another's power, authority or command. Bound over to someone, Id. Bound to someone, Plaut. The wise man is never subject to any evil, Sen. A soldier enslaved to a woman, Hor. Devoted, Caes. Obliged, Plaut.

units.la: Dedocere] Desuefacere aliquem ab, Cic. Defueo & desuesco aliquem, Titin. apud Non.
units.tr: Dedocere] To wean someone from something, Cic. To disaccustom someone, Titin. apud Non.

units.la: Deducere aliquem in viam] Inducere in viam, Var. Reducere in viam, Plaut. Reducere errantem, Plin.
units.tr: Deducere aliquem in viam] To lead someone into the way, Var. To bring someone back to the way, Plaut. To bring back one who has gone astray, Plin.

units.la: Deducere aliquem domum] Prosequi aliquem abeuntem usque ad. Ornare & celebrare egressum alicujus frequentiâ. Comitari alicui: & Comitari aliquem ad, Cic. Comitem se præbere alicui, Id. Comitari iter alicujus, Virg. Traducere pompam, Ter.
units.tr: Deducere aliquem domum] To accompany someone as he departs, all the way to his home. To adorn and honour someone's departure with a crowd. To escort someone; and to escort someone to a place, Cic. To offer oneself as someone's companion, Id. To accompany someone's journey, Virg. To escort a procession, Ter.

units.la: Deerrare, vid. Aberrare, deviare.
units.tr: Deerrare, see Aberrare, deviare.

units.la: Deesse] Defit mihi aliquid, Plaut. Deficit illum fides. Deficiunt me omnia. Carere est egere eo, quod habere velis. Egere rebus omnibus. Indigere alicujus rei, & aliquâ re, Cic. Quid illi abest? Arbitrabantur non defore, Id. Deficitur aquâ salienti hæc amœnitas, Plin. Iun. Deficior rebus omnibus, Col. Egere rationis, Mart. Desideratur aliquid, Cæs. Deliquum est, Plaut. Carere aliquâ re, Cic. Carere alicujus rei, Ter. Carere aliquam rem, Plaut. Non ad numerum sunt coloni. Partem abesse numero sensit, Liv.
units.tr: Deesse] Something is lacking to me, Plaut. Faith fails him. Everything fails me. To be without is to lack what one would wish to have. To lack everything. To need something, and to need it with something, Cic. What is lacking to him? They thought nothing would be wanting, Id. This pleasant place lacks water for its fountain, Plin. Iun. I am failing in all things, Col. To lack reason, Mart. Something is missed, Caes. It is a lack, Plaut. To be without something, Cic. To be without a thing, Ter. To lack a thing, Plaut. The farmers are not up to their number. He perceived that a part was missing from the count, Liv.

units.la: Deest cuique aliquid] Nemo mortalium omnibus horis sapit. pit. Nemo sine crimine, Cat. Nulli sunt visi, qui caruere Nisi.
units.tr: Deest cuique aliquid] No mortal is wise at every hour. No one is without fault, Cat. None have been seen who were without, except...

units.la: Defæcatur vinum] Subsidunt fæces in fundis vasorum, Col. Eliquatur à fæcibus vinum. Omni fæce carens. Vinum vetustatis saporem sumit. Fæculentum redditur limpidum. Deliquantur turbida. Consident, Id. Defæcare senectutem vini, Tertull.
units.tr: Defæcatur vinum] Dregs settle to the bottoms of vessels, Col. The wine is strained free of its lees. Free of all lees. Wine takes on the flavour of age. Cloudy wine is made clear. Turbid things are clarified. They settle, Id. To clarify the old lees of wine, Tertull.

units.la: Defæcatum] Eliquatum à fæcibus vinum. Mustum eliquatum. Fœcibus carens, Col.
units.tr: Defæcatum] Wine strained free of its lees. Strained must. Free of lees, Col.

units.la: Defalcare, barbare] Deducere ex salario, Cat. Deductionem facere, Cic.
units.tr: Defalcare, barbare] To deduct from a salary, Cat. To make a deduction, Cic.

units.la: Defatigare, & ri, vid. Fatigare.
units.tr: Defatigare, & ri, see Fatigare.

units.la: Defatigatio, defatigatus, vid. Fatigatio.
units.tr: Defatigatio, defatigatus, see Fatigatio.

units.la: Defectio] Rebellio, Cæs. Rebellium, Liv, Rebellatio, Val. Max. Defectus legionum, Capit.
units.tr: Defectio] Rebellion, Caes. Rebellion, Liv. Rebellion, Val. Max. Desertion of the legions, Capit.

units.la: Defector, vid. Apostata.
units.tr: Defector, see Apostata.

units.la: Defendere] Tutari. Tegere alicujus salutem præsidio. Protegere. Defendere, conservare, propugnare commoda patriæ. Vindicare à. Causam alicui tutari. Sustinere. Adesse alicui contra aliquem, Cic. Partes alicujus agere, sustinere, Id. Tutari præsidio, Hor. Tueri aliquem, Cic. Patrocinari alicui, Plin. Defenso aliquem injuria, Plaut.
units.tr: Defendere] To protect. To shelter someone's safety with a guard. To shield. To defend, preserve and champion the interests of the homeland. To vindicate from. To uphold someone's cause. To sustain. To stand by someone against another, Cic. To play someone's part, to maintain it, Id. To protect with a guard, Hor. To guard someone, Cic. To patronise someone, Plin. To defend someone from injury, Plaut.

units.la: Defensio] Tuitio sui. Propugnatio dignitatis. Patrocinium suscipere, vel repudiare alicujus. Apologismus, Cic. Apologia, Apul. Causæ dictio, Cæs. Dicæologia, Rutil. Lupo.
units.tr: Defensio] The protection of oneself. The championing of one's dignity. To take up or refuse someone's patronage. An apologia, Cic. An apology, Apul. The pleading of a case, Caes. Dicaeologia, Rutil. Lupo.

units.la: Defensor] Propugnator. Patronus civitatis. Conservator urbis. Servator mei capitis, Cic. Protector, Firm. Spart. Tutor finium, Hor. Tutanus, Varr. (Deus, qui laborantes tutari putabatur] Manstator, Plaut. Assertor, Suet. Defenstrix, Cic. Patrona, Id. Vindex honoris, Plaut.
units.tr: Defensor] A champion. The patron of a state. The preserver of a city. The saviour of my life, Cic. A protector, Firm. Spart. A guardian of the borders, Hor. Tutanus, Varr. (a god thought to protect the distressed). A protector, Plaut. An asserter, Suet. A defender (feminine), Cic. A patroness, Id. An avenger of honour, Plaut.

units.la: Deferre aliquid aliquò] Perferre aliquid ad aliquem, alicui nuncium. Asportare aliquid ad locum aliquem, Cicer. Mea ornamenta clam me ad meretrices degerit, Plaut.
units.tr: Deferre aliquid aliquò] To convey something to someone, to bring a message to someone. To carry something off to a place, Cicer. He secretly carried my ornaments off to the courtesans behind my back, Plaut.

units.la: Deficere viribus] Defici viribus, Cic. Effluunt vires lassitudine, Liv. Deficit anima per æstum, Cels. Linquere animam, mam, Lucr. Linqui animô, Suet. Reliquit me animus, Plaut. Sopiri, Liv. Per lætitiam linquitur animus, Var. Male est mihi.
units.tr: Deficere viribus] To be deprived of strength, Cic. Strength ebbs away from weariness, Liv. The breath fails in the heat, Cels. To give up the ghost, Lucr. To be overcome and fall senseless, Suet. My spirit leaves me, Plaut. To faint away, Liv. The spirit faints away for joy, Var. I feel faint.

units.la: Definire aliquid alicui] Statuere locum colloquio. Destinare tempus & locum alicui rei, Liv. Prodere diem judicii. Describere duodena jugera in homines singulos, Cic. Dicere diem nuptiis, Ter. Attribuere alicui negotium, Caes. Constituere locum. Designare fines. Præstituere tempus, Cic. Notare locum, Virg.
units.tr: Definire aliquid alicui] To appoint a place for a meeting. To fix a time and place for a matter, Liv. To announce the day of judgment. To assign twelve iugera of land to each man, Cic. To name the day for a wedding, Ter. To assign a task to someone, Caes. To appoint a place. To mark out boundaries. To prescribe a time beforehand, Cic. To mark a place, Virg.

units.la: Definitè, vid. Expressè.
units.tr: Definitè, see Expressè.

units.la: Definitio] Descriptio. Designatio temporum. Perscriptio legis. Determinatio mundi. Præscriptio naturæ. Terminatio rerum expetendarum. Circumscriptio temporis, Cic. Si extra hos cancellos egrediar, quos ipse mihi circumdedi, Id. Descriptiuncula, Sen. Finitio, Quint. Limites, Col.
units.tr: Definitio] A description. A designation of times. A written prescription of law. The determination of the world. The prescription of nature. The limit of things to be sought. The circumscription of time, Cic. If I go beyond these bounds which I have myself drawn around me, Id. A short description, Sen. A definition, Quint. Limits, Col.

units.la: Definitum est, vid. Certum est.
units.tr: Definitum est, see Certum est.

units.la: Deflagrare. vid. Comburi.
units.tr: Deflagrare. see Comburi.

units.la: Deflectere, vid. Aberrare.
units.tr: Deflectere, see Aberrare.

units.la: Deflere] Deplorare calamitatem. Lugere vitam hominum. Patriam eluxi jam & gravius & diutius, quàm ulla mater unicum filium, Cic. Nondum complorată morte, Id. Comploratu prosequi mortuos, Liv. Complorare fortunam, Quint. Vide Flere.
units.tr: Deflere] To lament a calamity. To mourn the life of men. I have now bewailed my country both more bitterly and for longer than any mother her only son, Cic. Before death had been wept over, Id. To attend the dead with lamentation, Liv. To bewail one's fortune, Quint. See Flere.

units.la: Defluere] Defluit aqua, Virg. Destillat humor ex capite. Cels. Col. Superlacrymat, Col.
units.tr: Defluere] Water flows down, Virg. Moisture drips from the head, Cels. Col. It weeps over, Col.

units.la: Defodere in terram aliquid] Obruere thesaurum alicubi, Cic. Obruere aliquid tellure, Ovid. Obruere aliquid in terra, Sarmenta infodere, Cat. Humare talcas, Col. Inhumare taleas, Plin. Præfodere aurum. Demersa humi dolia, Col.
units.tr: Defodere in terram aliquid] To bury a treasure somewhere, Cic. To cover something with earth, Ovid. To cover something in the ground; to bury cuttings, Cat. To bury vine-cuttings, Col. To inhume cuttings, Plin. To dig up gold. Jars sunk into the ground, Col.

units.la: Deformare, vid. Contaminare.
units.tr: Deformare, see Contaminare.

units.la: Deformatus in facie, vid Stigmaticus.
units.tr: Deformatus in facie, see Stigmaticus.

units.la: Deformis] Turpis, deformis aspectus. Distortus. Distortissimus homo, Fœdus. Maculosus. Improbiorem non vidi faciem mulieris. Insignis ad deformitatem. Monstrum hominis, Cic. Invenustus, Col. Decolor cutis, Plin. Decul-patum & dehonestum verbum, Gell. Improbus amor, Virg.
units.tr: Deformis] Foul, unsightly appearance. Distorted. A most distorted man. Foul, filthy. Blemished. I have not seen a more shameless face in a woman. Remarkable for ugliness. A monstrous man, Cic. Unlovely, Col. Discoloured skin, Plin. A word disgraced and dishonoured, Gell. Shameful love, Virg.

units.la: Fœdum monstrum, Cic. Informis, Virg. Cadaverosus, Ter. Cadaveris instar formosus. Teter color, Lucr.
units.tr: A foul monster, Cic. Shapeless, Virg. Cadaverous, Ter. Beautiful as a corpse. A foul colour, Lucr.

units.la: Deformitas] Fœditas vultus, Plin. Decoloratio, Cic. Pravitas in actionibus, Id. Maculatio, Apul.
units.tr: Deformitas] Foulness of countenance, Plin. Discolouring, Cic. Perversity in conduct, Id. Staining, Apul.

units.la: Deformiter, vid. Turpiter.
units.tr: Deformiter, see Turpiter.

units.la: Defraudari, vid. Decipere.
units.tr: Defraudari, see Decipere.

units.la: Defraudator] Circumforaneus homo, Suet. Circulator. Planus, Cic. Circumventor, Lamp. Bispellio, Plin. Versipellis, Plaut. Veterator, Ter. Veteratrix, Apul. Ærusca-tor, Gell. Calophanta, Plaut. Halapanta, Fest. & Holophanta. Callens miris modis ad fallendum, Amm. Agyrtes, Rhod. vid. Deceptor.
units.tr: Defraudator] A wandering fellow, Suet. A peddler. A plain deceiver, Cic. A circumventer, Lamp. A two-faced man, Plin. A shape-shifter, Plaut. A trickster, Ter. A trickstress, Apul. A haggler, Gell. A cheat, Plaut. Halapanta, Fest. and Holophanta. One skilled in deceiving in wondrous ways, Amm. Agyrtes, Rhod. See Deceptor.

units.la: Defricare aliquid] Effricare rubiginem, Sen. Depolire, Plin. Insplendorem dare, Plaut. Extergere rubiginem, Id. Extergere. Exterere cutem in facie, Plin. Exterere literam, Var. Atterere, Virg.
units.tr: Defricare aliquid] To scrape off rust, Sen. To polish off, Plin. To give a shine, Plaut. To wipe off rust, Id. To wipe away. To rub the skin off the face, Plin. To rub out a letter, Var. To wear away, Virg.

units.la: Defugere aliquid. vid. Recusare.
units.tr: Defugere aliquid. see Recusare.

units.la: Defunctus, vid. Mortuus.
units.tr: Defunctus, see Mortuus.

units.la: Defungi aliquâ re] Perfungi bello, curâ, laboribus, periculis, Cic. Perfunctus sum opellâ, Lucr. Amittere, Ter. vid. Finire.
units.tr: Defungi aliquâ re] To perform war, care, labours or dangers, Cic. I have finished the little task, Lucr. To lose, Ter. See Finire.

units.la: Degener ad rem aliquam] Degener virtutis patrum, Sil. Degener patrii oris, Ovid. Indignus majoribus, Cic. Abortivi Senatores, Suet. Paterni nominis oblitus. Paternam cantionem non canit, Adag. Teterrimis ignaviæ ac nequitiæ sordibus imbuta nobilia portenta, Val. Max. Dii boni, quas tenebras ex quo fulmine nasci passi estis? Deformes umbras in imo gurgite turpitudinis suæ jacere sinam? Id.
units.tr: Degener ad rem aliquam] Degenerate from the virtue of the fathers, Sil. Degenerate from one's native shore, Ovid. Unworthy of one's forebears, Cic. Senators who are abortions, Suet. Forgetful of one's father's name. He does not sing his father's song, Adag. Noble monsters steeped in the basest filth of idleness and wickedness, Val. Max. Good gods, what darkness did you allow to be born from which lightning? Shall I let deformed shadows lie in the depths of their own baseness? Id.

units.la: Degenerare] Degenerare à gravitate paternâ; à moribus majorum. Desciscere à consuetudine majorum, Cic. Heroum filii noxæ, Adag. vid. Desciscere.
units.tr: Degenerare: to degenerate from a father's dignity, from the customs of one's ancestors. To depart from the customs of one's ancestors, Cic. The sons of heroes are a disgrace, Adag. See Desciscere.

units.la: Degeneravit] Ab animo periit. Argentum versum est in scoriam. Exuto homine in feram transiit.
units.tr: Degeneravit: He has perished in spirit. Silver has been turned into dross. Having put off his humanity, he has passed into a beast.

units.la: Deglubere, vid. Excoriare.
units.tr: Deglubere, see Excoriare.

units.la: Deglutire] Sorbere ovum, Plin. Delingere plenum cochleare, Celf.
units.tr: Deglutire: to swallow an egg, Plin. To lick off a full spoonful, Celf.

units.la: Degere alicubi, vid. Habitare.
units.tr: Degere alicubi, see Habitare.

units.la: Degradare, barbarè, vid. Deponere ab officio.
units.tr: Degradare, barbarè, see Deponere ab officio.

units.la: Dehinc] In posterum prospicere. In reliquum tempus sancit. Ad posterum. De reliquo jam nostra culpa fuerit, Cic. De cætero, Sen. In reliquum, abf. Quint. Dehinc cæterum valete, Plaut. Deinceps. In posteritatem, Post hac, Cic. In futurum, Liv. Cetera parce puer bello, Virg. Cæterò, Plin.
units.tr: Dehinc: to look ahead to the future. To ordain for the time to come. For the future. "From now on the fault will be ours," Cic. From now on, Sen. For the rest, abl. Quint. "Farewell for the rest," Plaut. Henceforth. Into posterity. Hereafter, Cic. In the future, Liv. "Spare the rest, boy, from war," Virg. Henceforth, Plin.

units.la: Dehiscere] Dehiscit cœlum, Ovid. Dissiluêre loca, Virg. Discedit, Cic. Fatiscit area, Virg. Hiat humus vasta & profunda, Sal Labes terræ vastas video in immensum discedere, Bud.
units.tr: Dehiscere: "The sky gapes," Ovid. "The places burst apart," Virg. It parts, Cic. "The threshing floor cracks," Virg. "The ground gapes vast and deep," Sal. "I see the ruin of the earth spreading out into the immensity," Bud.

units.la: Dehortari aliquem ab aliquâ re] Dissuadere aliquid alicui. Dissuadere de re. Depellere aliquem sententiâ. Detrudere. Dejicere de sententiâ. Deducere de mente & consilio aliquem. Revocare ab incœpto, à consilio, Cic. Demovere aliquem de sententiâ, Plaut. Movere aliquem de sententiâ, Liv.
units.tr: Dehortari aliquem ab aliquâ re: to dissuade someone from something. To dissuade someone about a matter. To drive someone from his opinion. To thrust him down. To throw him off his opinion. To lead someone away from his purpose and counsel. To call back from a start, from a plan, Cic. To move someone from his opinion, Plaut. To move someone from his opinion, Liv.

units.la: Dejectus, vid. Demissus.
units.tr: Dejectus, see Demissus.

units.la: Dejerare, vid. Iurare.
units.tr: Dejerare, see Iurare.

units.la: Dejicere aliquem] Dejicere araneas de foribus, Plaut. Dejicere equo, Liv. Projicere se ex navi, Caes. Abjicere se è muro in mare. Jacere se in profundum, Cic. Vid. Præcipitari.
units.tr: Dejicere aliquem: to flick spiders off the doors, Plaut. To throw someone from a horse, Liv. To throw oneself from a ship, Caes. To cast oneself from a wall into the sea. To throw oneself into the depths, Cic. See Praecipitari.

units.la: Deinde] Posthac. Dein, tum, postea, Exin, Exinde. Pòst aliquanto. Posteriùs ista videbimus. Secundùm ea quæro. Secundo loco. Deinceps, Cic. Post hinc, Virg. Post inde, Suet. Posteriùs, post hoc, Lucr. Postmodum, Ter. Postmodo, Liv. Post illa, Plaut. Post id locorum, Id. Subinde. Non, si malè nunc, & olim sic erit, Horat. Exhinc, Lucr.
units.tr: Deinde: Posthac. Then, thereafter, afterwards, after that, thence, thenceforth. Some time after. We shall see those things later. I inquire next about these matters. In the second place. Next, Cic. Hence afterwards, Virg. Thereupon, Suet. Afterwards, after this, Lucr. Afterwards, Ter. Presently, Liv. After those things, Plaut. After that, in that place, Id. Thereupon. "If it is bad now, it will one day be so," Horat. Hence, Lucr.

units.la: Dejugare, vid. Abjugare.
units.tr: Dejugare, see Abjugare.

units.la: Delabi, vid. Incidere.
units.tr: Delabi, see Incidere.

units.la: Delebilis] Deletitius, Vlp.
units.tr: Delebilis: Deletitius, Vlp.

units.la: Delectabilis] Delicatus sermo. Delicatissimi versus. Habet ea res delectationis, quantum voles. Habet ea res delectationem. Mellitus puer, Cic. Voluptarium prædium, Vlp. Delectatior motio, Gell. Voluptabilis nuncius, Plaut. Voluptuosum est invisere, Plin. Iun. Deliciæ pueri, Plaut.
units.tr: Delectabilis: a witty speech. Very witty verses. That thing has as much delight as you like. That thing has delight. A honeyed boy, Cic. A pleasant estate, Vlp. A more delightful movement, Gell. A pleasing messenger, Plaut. It is a pleasure to visit, Plin. Iun. The darling of a boy, Plaut.

units.la: Delectabiliter] Delicatè cœnare, Varr. Jucundè, jucundissimè dissimè vivere, Cic. Molliter se curare, Ter. Malacum in modum. Lepidè stratus lectus, Plaut. Genialiter agere festum, Ovid. Voluptuosè.
units.tr: Delectabiliter: to dine daintily, Varr. To live pleasantly, most pleasantly, Cic. To take one's ease softly, Ter. In a soft manner. A couch elegantly spread, Plaut. To keep a festival joyfully, Ovid. Voluptuously.

units.la: Delectamentum] Delectatio. Animi libera oblectatio. Oblectamentum puerorum. Animi causa fecit. Jucunditas. Est mihi aliquid voluptati. Solatium magnum est vacare culpâ, ocellus. Deliciarum causâ loris aliquem in convivio cædere, Cic. Magis in decoris armis, & militaribus equis, quàm in scortis & conviviis libidinem habebant, Salust.
units.tr: Delectamentum: delight. A free refreshment of the mind. A pastime of boys. He did it for the sake of amusement. Pleasantness. I have some pleasure in it. Solace is great, to be free from fault, ocellus. To beat someone with thongs at a banquet for the sake of pleasure, Cic. "They had more desire for fine arms and military horses than for harlots and banquets," Salust.

units.la: Delectare aliquem] Delectationem alicui afferre. Oblectare aliquem. Exhaurire sermone solicitudines. Reddidisti me mihi, Cic. Me depositum ac mœrentem repentino nuncio alacrem reddidisti, ac me ex luctu in latitudinem excitasti, Accius, Non. Ego illos lubentiores faciam, quàm lubentia est. Creare alicui voluptatem, Plaut. Beare aliquem, Hor. Reddere alicui animum, Ter. vid. Exhilarare.
units.tr: Delectare aliquem: to bring delight to someone. To divert someone. To drain away his cares by conversation. "You have restored me to myself," Cic. "You made me cheerful with the sudden news, when I was dejected and sorrowful, and lifted me out of grief into open space," Accius, Non. "I shall make them more willing than willingness itself," Plaut. To create pleasure for someone, Plaut. To make someone happy, Hor. To give someone back his spirit, Ter. See Exhilarare.

units.la: Delectari] Delector hac re. In hac re. Est mihi in deliciis, in amore, in amoribus. Oblector hac re. Delectationi mihi est, Perstudiosus sum musicorum, Cic. Oblectat me aliquid, Plaut. Habeo voluptati aliquid, Sallust. Gaudeo carmine, Hor. Amo silvas, Ovid. Capior jocis, Virg. vid. Delinire.
units.tr: Delectari: I take delight in this thing. In this thing. It is in my delights, in my love, in my loves. I am diverted by this thing. It gives me delight. "I am exceedingly fond of music," Cic. "Something diverts me," Plaut. "I have pleasure in something," Sallust. "I rejoice in song," Hor. "I love the woods," Ovid. "I am captivated by jests," Virg. See Delinire.

units.la: Delectus, a, um] Lecti juvenes. Lecta juventus. Exercitus superbissimo delectu, & durissimâ conquisitione collectus. Conquisiti milites. Vir à viro lectus, Cic.
units.tr: Delectus, a, um: chosen young men. A chosen youth. An army gathered by a most proud levy and the harshest recruitment. Picked soldiers. A man chosen from among men, Cic.

units.la: Delectus] Electus necis, Ovid. Selectio rerum. Optio, delectus & discrimen rerum, Cic. Tros Tyriusque mihi nullo discrimine, Virg. Magnâ diligentiâ eligi oportet, Veget.
units.tr: Delectus: chosen for death, Ovid. A selection of things. Choice, selection and discrimination among things, Cic. "Trojan and Tyrian alike to me, without distinction," Virg. One must choose with great care, Veget.

units.la: Delectu opus] Delige quod diligas.
units.tr: Delectu opus: choose what you love.

units.la: Delegare officium suum alicui] Demandare vicem suam alicui, Suet. Transcribere nomina, fundum, jus suum in aliquem, Liv. Vlp. Transfundere jus, IC. Laudem, Liv. vid. Committere aliquid alicui.
units.tr: Delegare officium suum alicui: to entrust one's duty to someone, Suet. To transfer names, land or right to someone, Liv. Vlp. To transfer a right, IC. To transfer praise, Liv. See Committere aliquid alicui.

units.la: Delegatus judex] Recuperator, Prædiator, Cic. Juris prædiatorii vel prædialis peritus, Bud. Arbiter regundis finibus, Lipsius. Regundorum finium præfectus, Cromer.
units.tr: Delegatus judex: a recuperator, a prediator, Cic. Skilled in predial law, Bud. An arbiter for fixing boundaries, Lipsius. An officer for fixing boundaries, Cromer.

units.la: Delere] Lituraм facere, inducere, Cic. Delitæ literæ, Prisc. Spongiâ corrigere, Lipsius. Vid. Abolere. Perdere. Delator] Confector & consumptor. Exstinctor conju-rationis. Perditor Provinciæ. Exterminator Reipubl.Cic.
units.tr: Delere: to make an erasure, to draw a line through, Cic. Letters erased, Prisc. To correct with a sponge, Lipsius. See Abolere. Perdere. Delator: a finisher and consumer. A stamper-out of conspiracy. A destroyer of the province. An exterminator of the Commonwealth, Cic.

units.la: Deliberare] Deliberationem de aliquâ re habere. Cogitationem suscipere. Spatium deliberandi habere. Deliberandum & concoquendum tibi est. Te adhibe ad consilia, Cic. Rem secretis cogitationibus agitare, Tac. Argumenta in corde constituere. Convocare in animum consilia. Senatum consilii in cor convocare, Consiliarium senatorem in corde convocare, Plaut. Etiam atque etiam cogitare, Ter.
units.tr: Deliberare: to hold deliberation about some matter. To take up consideration. To have time for deliberation. It must be weighed and digested by you. Bring yourself to counsels, Cic. To turn a matter over in secret thoughts, Tac. To set arguments in the heart. To summon counsels into the mind. To summon the senate of counsel into the heart; to summon a counsellor senator into the heart, Plaut. To think again and again, Ter.

units.la: Deliberare in utramque partem] Calculos utrimque ponere. Pensiculare utrumque, Gell.
units.tr: Deliberare in utramque partem: to place pebbles on both sides. To weigh each side, Gell.

units.la: Deliberatio] Nulla tibi hic jam consultatio est, Ter. Cunctatio decora in sermone, Plin. Consilii capiendi deliberatio, Cic.
units.tr: Deliberatio: "There is no more consultation for you here," Ter. A becoming hesitation in speech, Plin. Deliberation in taking counsel, Cic.

units.la: Deliberator] Contemplativus, Sen. Speculativus, Quint. Nunquamcunctabundus nisi cum in senatu loqueretur, Tac. Speculator, Cic. Cunctator, Liv. Ephectici Philosophi, (i.e.) Cunctatores, qui nihil definiebant, sed amplius se deliberaturos dicebant) Scepticí, Bud. Opinatores, Cic.
units.tr: Deliberator: contemplative, Sen. Speculative, Quint. Never hesitating except when speaking in the senate, Tac. A speculator, Cic. A delayer, Liv. Ephectic philosophers (that is, delayers, who defined nothing but said they would deliberate further): sceptics, Bud. Opinionists, Cic.

units.la: Delibare, Vid. Gustare.
units.tr: Delibare, see Gustare.

units.la: Delibrare] (i. e. Libra expendere) Dependere aliquid libra. Rependere aliquid argento, Plin. Repensum auro caput. Repensum aurum pro capite, Cic. Expendere aliquem auro, Plaut. Pensare aliquid argento, Col.
units.tr: Delibrare (i.e. Libra expendere): to pay out something by weight. To repay something in silver, Plin. A head repaid in gold. Gold repaid in place of a head, Cic. To weigh someone out in gold, Plaut. To pay something in silver, Col.

units.la: Delibutus, Vid. Vnctus.
units.tr: Delibutus, see Vnctus.

units.la: Delicate vivere] Molliter & delicatè, Cic. Molliter se curare, Ter. Facere sibi voluptatem. Facere animo suo volupe, Plaut. Provocare Apitium coenis, Sen. Molliter, Turpiter, effœminatè vivere, Apul. Vid. Delectabiliter.
units.tr: Delicate vivere: to live softly and daintily, Cic. To take one's ease softly, Ter. To give oneself pleasure. To make one's soul pleasant, Plaut. To provoke the appetite with dinners, Sen. To live softly, shamefully, effeminately, Apul. See Delectabiliter.

units.la: Delicatus] Fastidii delicatissimi homo. Malacus, Plaut. Tenerae mentes nimis asperioribus formandae studiis, Hor. Valdè jam lautus es, Cic. Vinulus, Fest. Abrodiætus, Rhod. Vid. Voluptarius.
units.tr: Delicatus: a man of most fastidious delicacy. Soft, Malacus, Plaut. "Tender minds to be formed by too harsh studies," Hor. "You are now very elegant indeed," Cic. Pampered, Fest. Luxurious, Rhod. See Voluptarius.

units.la: Delicati morbis obnoxii] Dolor voluptatis comes. Dolor libenter apud eos manet à quibus alitur & augetur.
units.tr: Delicati morbis obnoxii: pain is the companion of pleasure. Pain stays willingly with those by whom it is fed and increased.

units.la: Delicia] Molities, Molitia animi, (est dolor & fuga laborum.) Mollisvictus. Voluptuarius sensus. Blanditiæ. Blandimendimentum. Lenocinium cupiditatum, Cic. Jovis lac. Jovis cerebrum. Nectar & Ambrosia,
units.tr: Delicia: softness, softness of mind (it is grief and avoidance of labour). Soft living. A voluptuous sense. Caresses. Flattery. The enticement of desires, Cic. Milk of Jove. Brain of Jove. Nectar and ambrosia.

units.la: Delicere, Vid. Allicere.
units.tr: Delicere, see Allicere.

units.la: Delictum] Commissum, Cic.
units.tr: Delictum: a thing committed, Cic.

units.la: Delicus, Vid. Ablactatus.
units.tr: Delicus, see Ablactatus.

units.la: Deligare, Vid. Alligare.
units.tr: Deligare, see Alligare.

units.la: Deligere, Vid. Eligere.
units.tr: Deligere, see Eligere.

units.la: Delimare, Vid. Limare.
units.tr: Delimare, see Limare.

units.la: Delineare] Deformare operis speciem. Deformare lineis imitationem aedificiorum, Vitru. Primas lineas ducere, Quint. Adumbrare. Extremas umbrae lineas circumscribere, Id. Ita informatum, anticipatum est mentibus nostris.
units.tr: Delineare: to outline the appearance of a work. To outline in lines the imitation of buildings, Vitru. To draw the first lines, Quint. To sketch in shadow. To trace the outermost lines of a shadow, Id. Thus is it shaped and anticipated in our minds.

units.la: Delinimentum] Scitamentum orationis, Gell. Color, Fr. Quint. Pigmenta orationis, Cic. Fucus Poetae, Id. Lenocinium, Quint. Pictae tectoria linguae, Perf.
units.tr: Delinimentum: an elegance of speech, Gell. Colour, Fr. Quint. The paints of speech, Cic. The poet's rouge, Id. An enticement, Quint. "Painted plaster of the tongue," Perf.

units.la: Delinire] Lenire miseriam. Severitatem acerbam condimentis humanitatis mitigare, Cic. Oblenire, Sen. Mollire animos dictis, Virg. Mulcentur cervi fistula, Plin. Addere lenimen, Ovid. Permulcere plebem, Liv. Complacare, Gell. Litare saevitiae, Id. Interconciliare, Quint. Vid. Placare.
units.tr: Delinire: to soothe misery. To soften harshness with the seasonings of humanity, Cic. To soothe, Sen. To soften minds with words, Virg. "Deer are charmed by the pipe," Plin. To add a soothing balm, Ovid. To win over the common people, Liv. To placate, Gell. To appease cruelty, Id. To win over, Quint. See Placare.

units.la: Deliniri aliquâ re] Duci laude, gloria, quaestu. Capi amore assentatione. Avocat me voluptas. Attrahit commodum. Trahi studio laudis. Prolabi cupiditate. Aufert me aliquid. Pecunia ejus contra meam fidem, apud me nihil valuit. Induci promissis. Persuasum est ei magnitudine pecuniae. Rapimur in errorem opinionibus vulgi, Cic. Provexit me spes, Liv.
units.tr: Deliniri aliquâ re: to be led by praise, glory or gain. To be captured by love or flattery. Pleasure draws me away. Advantage attracts. To be drawn by zeal for praise. To slip away through desire. Something takes me away. His money, against my good faith, had no weight with me. To be induced by promises. He was persuaded by the size of the sum. "We are carried into error by the opinions of the crowd," Cic. "Hope has carried me forward," Liv.

units.la: Delinquere, Vid. Peccare.
units.tr: Delinquere, see Peccare.

units.la: Deliquium animi] Defectus animi, Plaut. Defectio animi, virium. Subita defectione stare, ingredi, vix posset, Suet. Vid. Deficere viribus.
units.tr: Deliquium animi: failure of spirit, Plaut. Failure of spirit or strength. He could scarcely stand or walk after a sudden collapse, Suet. See Deficere viribus.

units.la: Delirare] Errore mentis affici, Cic. Nihil pro sano facere, Caes. Cerebro laborare, Plaut. Vesanire, Catul. A mente consilioque deduci, Cic. Exire à se, Petron. Desipere mentis, Plaut. Desiit inter homines morari, (stultè agere) Suet. Si quod vestigium in vecordi pectore sensus fuisset, Valer. Maxim.
units.tr: Delirare: to be affected by an error of mind, Cic. To do nothing as one sane, Caes. To labour in the brain, Plaut. To be out of one's wits, Catul. To be drawn away from mind and counsel, Cic. To go out of oneself, Petron. To be out of one's mind, Plaut. He ceased to live among men (acting foolishly), Suet. "If any trace of feeling had been in that frenzied breast," Valer. Maxim.

units.la: Delirium] Deliramentum, Plaut. Alienatio mentis, Plin. Deliratio, Cic. Amentia. Mania. Insania, Id. Vesania, Plin. Phrenesis, Id. Desipientia, Lucr. Vid. Amentia.
units.tr: Delirium: a raving, Plaut. Alienation of mind, Plin. Derangement, Cic. Amentia. Madness. Insanity, Id. Unsoundness of mind, Plin. Frenzy, Id. Senselessness, Lucr. See Amentia.

units.la: Delirus] Captus animi, vel animo. Homo plusquàm insanus, Er.
units.tr: Delirus: having the mind seized or disordered. A man more than insane, Er.

units.la: Dilitescere, Vid. Latere.
units.tr: Dilitescere, see Latere.

units.la: Delubrum, Vid. Templum. Fanum.
units.tr: Delubrum, see Templum. Fanum.

units.la: Deludere, Vid. Decipere.
units.tr: Deludere, see Decipere.

units.la: Delutare, Vid. Circumlinere.
units.tr: Delutare, see Circumlinere.

units.la: Demandare] Tibi provinciam hanc delegamus, Vid. Committere aliquid alicui.
units.tr: Demandare: We entrust this province to you. See Committere aliquid alicui.

units.la: Demens] Alienatus mente, Plin. Alienatus homo sensibus. Alienatus sensu animus, Liv. Attonitus visis, Virg. Lapsus mente, Suet. Lapsus animi. Delinitus, Plaut. Mente captus, Fest. Mente non constat, Val. Max. Vid. Amens.
units.tr: Demens: out of one's mind, Plin. A man out of his senses. A mind estranged from sense, Liv. Stunned by what it saw, Virg. Having lost one's wits, Suet. Lost in spirit. Beguiled, Plaut. Out of one's mind, Fest. Not in possession of one's mind, Val. Max. See Amens.

units.la: Dementare] Erroris ac dementiae aliquem complere. Objicere alicui glaucoma ob oculos. Frustrationem noxiam injiciam in hanc familiam, Plaut. Perstringere oculos animi, ingenii. Infatuare aliquem. Offundere tenebras, noctem. De mente deturbare, Cic. Mentem alicui excutere, Plin. Iun. Exsternare aliquem, Pacuv. De statu mentis aliquem deturbare, Plaut. Occaecat animos Scipionis mors, Liv.
units.tr: Dementare: to fill someone with error and madness. To throw a blinding film before someone's eyes. To cast a harmful delusion upon this family, Plaut. To dull the eyes of the mind, of the intellect. To infatuate someone. To pour darkness over, to cloud the night. To drive out of one's mind, Cic. To knock someone's wits out of him, Plin. Iun. To astound someone, Pacuv. To throw someone off his mental balance, Plaut. The death of Scipio blinded their minds, Liv.

units.la: Dementia, Vid. Delirium. Amentia.
units.tr: Dementia, see Delirium. Amentia.

units.la: Demere] Subtrahit vires timor. Deflorare, Liv. Deponere aliquid ex levitate. Deducere aliquid. Deductionem facere pecuniae. Detrahere ex summâ. Decerpsit aliquid jocus de gravitate. Imminuere summam. Decessionem de summâ facere. Delibare de gloriâ alicujus. Nil libatum de corpore cernas, Cic. Limare commoda alicujus, Hor. Derogare alicui gratiam, Plin.
units.tr: Demere: fear saps his strength. To strip of bloom, Liv. To lay aside something of one's lightness. To deduct something. To make a deduction from the money. To subtract from the sum. A joke has taken something from the dignity. To reduce the sum. To make a reduction from the total. To take a little from someone's glory. You could see nothing diminished from the body, Cic. To file down someone's advantages, Hor. To take away someone's favour, Plin.

units.la: Demereri sibi aliquem] Bene mereri de aliquo, erga aliquem. Promereri bene de multis. Gratificari aliquid alicui. Devincire sibi aliquem officiis. Gratiam alicujus colligere, aucupari. Inire gratiam aliquo facto ab omnibus. Beneficium apud aliquem bene ponere, collocare. Ampletti aliquem officiis, Cic. Ad gratiam facere aliquibus, Amm. Volentia plebi facere, Sallust. Sensi sedulò bonam operam mihi dare, Plaut.
units.tr: Demereri sibi aliquem: to deserve well of someone, towards someone. To deserve well of many. To do a favour for someone. To bind someone to oneself by services. To gather, to court someone's favour. To win favour from everyone by one deed. To place a kindness well with someone. To surround someone with services, Cic. To win favour with some people, Amm. To make oneself pleasing to the common people, Sallust. I perceived that he was diligently doing me a good turn, Plaut.

units.la: Demetiri] Demetiri. Limitare vineas, Plin. Determinare limites, Plaut. Metari vineas, Col. Demetiri cursus solis, Cic.
units.tr: Demetiri: to measure out. To mark out vineyards, Plin. To fix boundaries, Plaut. To measure out vineyards, Col. To measure out the course of the sun, Cic.

units.la: Demirari, Vid. Mirari
units.tr: Demirari, see Mirari.

units.la: Demissa loca] Depressior locus, Caes.
units.tr: Demissa loca: a lower-lying place, Caes.

units.la: Demisse] Tenuiter æstimare. Abjectè aliquid facere. Exiliter, Cic. Leviter ornatus. Humiliter & demissè sentire, Id. Obscurè natus, Macrob.
units.tr: Demisse: to value slightly. To do something meanly. Plainly, Cic. Lightly adorned. To think humbly and modestly, Id. Born in obscurity, Macrob.

units.la: Demissus vultus] Dejectus in humum vultus, Ovid. Obstipus. Obstipum caput. Tristis ac severus philosophus, Cic. Obstipo capite stare, Hor. Stupentibus in terram oculis, Hier. Tristis Erynnys, Diva solo fixos oculos immota tenebat, Virg. Tristis severitudo inest in vultu, Donat. Si nihil mittitur, quo supercilio spicit! Plaut.
units.tr: Demissus vultus: a face cast down to the ground, Ovid. Bent over. A head bowed down. A grave and severe philosopher, Cic. To stand with head bowed, Hor. With eyes fixed on the ground, Hier. The grim Fury held her eyes fixed on the ground, motionless, Virg. Grim severity is in the face, Donat. If nothing is sent, how haughtily he looks down! Plaut.

units.la: Demittere] Dejicere elatam securim in caput alicujus, Liv. Demittere manus, Plaut. Remittere aures, Plin. Submittere oculos, Ovid. Fasces, Cic.
units.tr: Demittere: to bring down a raised axe on someone's head, Liv. To let fall the hands, Plaut. To lower the ears, Plin. To drop the eyes, Ovid. To lower the fasces, Cic.

units.la: Democratia] Imperium populare, Cic. Cum res ad summam secem turbamque redit, Lucr.
units.tr: Democratia: popular rule, Cic. When affairs fall back into utter confusion and turmoil, Lucr.

units.la: Demoliri, Vid. Destruere.
units.tr: Demoliri, see Destruere.

units.la: Demolitio, Vid. Destructio.
units.tr: Demolitio, see Destructio.

units.la: Demolitor, Vid. Destructor.
units.tr: Demolitor, see Destructor.

units.la: Demonstrare aliquid] Apertissimè colligere, Plin. Ratione docere, Lucr. Argumentatione firmare, Quint. Rationibus conquisitis confirmare. Signis omni luce clarioribus probare. Fidem facere. Planum facere. Concludere aliquid ratione. Amentatas hastas oratoris lacertis torquebit, Cic. Amentare sententiam, Tertull. Rem, auctorem dare, Plaut. Pervincere aliquid dictis, Lucr. Argumenta rei, & ad rem, dicere, Plaut.
units.tr: Demonstrare aliquid: to gather most clearly, Plin. To teach by reasoning, Lucr. To confirm by argument, Quint. To confirm with carefully sought reasons. To prove by signs clearer than daylight. To make good one's case. To make plain. To conclude something by reason. The orator will hurl his javelins, fitted with throwing-thongs, with the strength of his arm, Cic. To set forth an opinion fitted with its thong, Tertull. To give the matter and its author, Plaut. To overcome something with words, Lucr. To state the arguments about the matter and relevant to it, Plaut.

units.la: Demonstratio] Probatio, Sen. Documentum, Sallust. Rationes conquisitæ. Amentata hasta. Argumentum. Oratio rebus non dubiis captas assensionem alicujus, Cic. Evidens probatio, Apodixis, Quint. Amentatæ sententiæ non manipulares, Ambros.
units.tr: Demonstratio: proof, Sen. Evidence, Sallust. Carefully sought reasons. A javelin fitted with a thong. Argument. A speech which, from matters not in doubt, wins the assent of someone, Cic. Evident proof, apodixis, Quint. Opinions fitted with thongs, not of the common sort, Ambros.

units.la: Demonstrative] Comperta oculis proferre, Liv.
units.tr: Demonstrative: to bring forward things seen with one's own eyes, Liv.

units.la: Demum] Nunc demum. Tunc demum, Cic. Tum denique nique nostra intelligimus bona, Plaut. Jam primum, Ter.
units.tr: Demum: now at last. Then at last, Cic. Then at last we understand our goods, Plaut. First of all, Ter.

units.la: Denarrare, Vid. Enarrare.
units.tr: Denarrare, see Enarrare.

units.la: Denegare] Negare præcisè. Abnuere. Renuere convivium. Recusare postulanti. Sine ullâ exceptione præcidere. Repulsam alicui afferre, Cic. Abnegare alicui dotem, Virg. Cùm sæpe replicasset, tandem persuasit, Plin. Per me egebit, Plaut.
units.tr: Denegare: to deny flatly. To refuse. To decline an invitation. To refuse someone who asks. To cut off without any exception. To bring a rebuff to someone, Cic. To deny a dowry to someone, Virg. When he had often repeated the refusal, he at last persuaded, Plin. He may go without for all I care, Plaut.

units.la: Denegatur mihi] Repulsam fero, accipio, refero, Cic. Rpulsam patior, Ovid.
units.tr: Denegatur mihi: I bear, accept and carry back a rebuff, Cic. I suffer a rebuff, Ovid.

units.la: Denigrare] Nigrore suffundere, Plin. Infuscare vellera, Col. Fuscare, Ovid.
units.tr: Denigrare: to suffuse with blackness, Plin. To darken fleeces, Col. To make dusky, Ovid.

units.la: Denique] De reliquo. Quod superest. Extremò. Novissimè, Cic. Ad extremum, Tac. Ad postremum, ad ultimum, Liv. Ultimò, Suet. Demum, Pacuv.
units.tr: Denique: for the rest. What remains. At the end. Lastly, Cic. To the end, Tac. At the last, at the final point, Liv. Finally, Suet. At last, Pacuv.

units.la: Denodare, Vid. Laxare arcum.
units.tr: Denodare, see Laxare arcum.

units.la: Denominari ab aliquo] Nomen ex aliquâ re capere, Caf. Trahere, Cic. Nomen usurpare alicujus civitatis. Nominare se ex altero. Inducere sibi nomen alicujus, Id. Cognomentum alicujus accipere, Tac. Etymon ab aliquo habere, Col. Adoptare sibi aliquod nomen, Mart.
units.tr: Denominari ab aliquo: to take a name from some thing, Caes. To draw a name, Cic. To assume the name of some city. To be named after another. To take someone's name for oneself, Id. To receive someone's surname, Tac. To have one's etymology from someone, Col. To adopt some name for oneself, Mart.

units.la: Denominatio] Agnominatio, Quint. Denominatione similis, Bud.
units.tr: Denominatio: paronymy, Quint. Similar by paronymy, Bud.

units.la: Dens] Nucifrangibula, Plaut.
units.tr: Dens: a nutcracker, Plaut.

units.la: Densare] Condensare, Col. Quia se condenseat aër, Lucr. Spissare. Conspissare, Plin. Addensare, Id. Cogere, Virg.
units.tr: Densare: to condense, Col. Because the air condenses, Lucr. To thicken. To make dense, Plin. To add density, Id. To compress, Virg.

units.la: Densatio] Ignis ex aëris condensitate, conflatur, Apul. Spissamentum, Colum.
units.tr: Densatio: fire is kindled from the condensed density of air, Apul. A thickening, Colum.

units.la: Dense] Spisse, Col. Spissius. Arctissimè serere, Plin. Confertim, Liv. Cohors crebrò operta stramentis, Varr. Litera alia aliam scandit, Plaut. Continuatum lateri latus, Ovid.
units.tr: Dense: thickly, Col. More thickly. To plant most closely, Plin. In crowds, Liv. A cohort often covered with straw, Varr. One letter climbs over another, Plaut. Side pressed continuously against side, Ovid.

units.la: Densere] Coire in densitatem. Addensari. Crassescere. Cogitür in bitumen humor, Plin. Concrescere, Lucr. Spissescere, Celf.
units.tr: Densere: to come together into density. To thicken. To grow thick. Moisture hardens into bitumen, Plin. To grow together, Lucr. To become dense, Celf.

units.la: Densitas] Spissitudo, Spissitas. Condensa arborum, Plin. Crassitudo, Celf. Crassamen, Col. Stipatio, Quint.
units.tr: Densitas: thickness. The thickness of trees, Plin. Thickness, Celf. Thickness, Col. Crowding, Quint.

units.la: Densus] Perdensus, Col. Prædensus. Spissus, Plin. Solidus, Ovid.
units.tr: Densus: very dense, Col. Very dense. Thick, Plin. Solid, Ovid.

units.la: Dentale, vid. Bura.
units.tr: Dentale, see Bura.

units.la: Dentarpaga] Odontagra. Iun. Forficula, Plin. Forfi-ces, Celf. Forfices dentarpagæ, Var.
units.tr: Dentarpaga: toothache, Iun. A small pair of pincers, Plin. Pincers, Celf. Tooth-pulling pincers, Var.

units.la: Dentatus] Broccus. Bronchus. & Brochus, Broncus. Brocus, Non. Dento, Mart. Rhinoceros (dente eminulo) Id. Oxyodontas, Lucil.
units.tr: Dentatus: broccus, bronchus, brochus, broncus, brocus (variant forms of the one word for protruding-toothed), Non. Toothed, Mart. A rhinoceros (with a small projecting tooth), Id. Sharp-toothed, Lucil.

units.la: Dentes nudare] Riftum diducere, Hor. Restringere den-tes. Irridet me albis dentibus. Canem irritatam imitari, Plaut. Immodicus hiatus ri�único ftum distendit, Quint.
units.tr: Dentes nudare: to draw back the lips, Hor. To draw the teeth back. He laughs at me with white teeth. To imitate a dog provoked, Plaut. An excessive gaping distends the gash of the mouth, Quint.

units.la: Dentes maxillares] Dentes molares, Isid.
units.tr: Dentes maxillares: grinding teeth, molars, Isid.

units.la: Dentes primores] Adversi dentes, Cic. Incisores, Isid. Ge-lasini, Cal. Rhod. Mordices, Plaut.
units.tr: Dentes primores: front teeth, Cic. Incisors, Isid. The laughing teeth, Cal. Rhod. Nibblers, Plaut.

units.la: Denticulatus] Denticulata falx, Plin. Dentata cornua scarabæi bisulcis forpicibus, Id. Tribulata falcicula, Pallad.
units.tr: Denticulatus: a serrated sickle, Plin. Horns toothed like a beetle's, with two-grooved pincers, Id. A sickle with three spikes, Pallad.

units.la: Dentiscalpium] Cuspis frondea. Penna dentes levans, Mart. Spina argentea, Petr. Acus arundinea, Marcell.
units.tr: Dentiscalpium: a leafy point. A feather for cleaning the teeth, Mart. A silver pin, Petr. A reed needle, Marcell.

units.la: Denudare, vid. Nudare.
units.tr: Denudare, see Nudare.

units.la: Denunciare hostilitatem alicui] Denunciare alicui, Abs. Denunciare inimicitias, iram, dimicationem. Indicere ali-cui arma, funus, Cic. Sanguinarium nuncium alicui mitte-re, Plin. Clarigare, Id. Clarigationem exercere, Serv.
units.tr: Denunciare hostilitatem alicui: to announce hostilities to someone, Abs. To declare enmities, anger, battle. To declare war on someone with arms and death, Cic. To send a bloody message to someone, Plin. To proclaim war, Id. To carry out a formal declaration of war, Serv.

units.la: Denunciatio] Clarigatio, Quint. Inimicitiæ indictæ. Ob-nunciatio, Perduellia. Odia professa, Id.
units.tr: Denunciatio: a formal declaration of war, Quint. Declared enmities. Denunciation, treason. Hatreds openly professed, Id.

units.la: Denuo] Iterum, Plaut. Revertor rursus denuo, Id. Rur-sus, Cic. Ab integro, Virg. De integro, Ter. Ex integro, Plin. Ab inchoato, Col.
units.tr: Denuo: again, Plaut. I return again and again, Id. Again, Cic. From the beginning, Virg. Anew, Ter. From the start, Plin. From the outset, Col.

units.la: Denuo aliquid tentare, agere, aggredi] Integrare pugnam, certamen, Virg. Retexere, Hor. Recomponere lapillos. Reconducere domum, Vlp. Recreare Consules, augu-res, Cic. Refervescit sanguis in terram fusus. Reponere dia-dema quod ille abjecerat. Recidunt in terram omnia, Id. Redordiri. Resorbere, quæ evomimus, Plin. Resumere tela, Ovid. Repolire, Col. Reddere incudi, Hor. Revende-re, Vlp. Sub incudem revocare.
units.tr: Denuo aliquid tentare, agere, aggredi: to renew the battle, the contest, Virg. To unweave again, Hor. To rearrange the little stones. To lead home again, Vlp. To elect consuls and augurs again, Cic. Blood poured on the ground heats up again. To put back the diadem which he had cast away. All things fall back to the ground, Id. To warp again. To swallow back what we have vomited, Plin. To take up weapons again, Ovid. To polish again, Col. To put back on the anvil, Hor. To sell again, Vlp. To call back under the anvil.

units.la: Deorsum, vid. Infra.
units.tr: Deorsum, see Infra.

units.la: Depangere] Pangere malleolos, Col. Repangere. Infere-re surculos. Ponere vites, Defigere. Deponere. Demer-gere. gere. Deprimere sarmentum, surculum, Immergere terræ vitem. Ingenerare terræ, Id.
units.tr: Depangere: to plant young vine-shoots, Col. To plant again. To set in offshoots. To put vines in. To fix in. To put down. To sink. To press down a twig or shoot. To plunge the vine into the earth. To bury in the earth, Id.

units.la: Depasci alicujus bona] Herbas depaverunt, Col. Hirci pascuntur sylvas, Virg. Quid te futurum censes, quem assiduè exedent? Ter. Comedere bona alicujus, Cic. Comedere aliquem, Ter. Attondere bona alicujus, Plaut.
units.tr: Depasci alicujus bona: they have grazed the grass bare, Col. Goats graze the woods, Virg. What do you think will become of you, whom they will eat up constantly? Ter. To eat up someone's goods, Cic. To eat someone up, Ter. To strip someone's goods bare, Plaut.

units.la: Depauperare, vid. Pauperare.
units.tr: Depauperare, see Pauperare.

units.la: Depeciere, vid. Vellere.
units.tr: Depeciere, see Vellere.

units.la: Depeculari, Depeculator, vid. Compilare, compilator.
units.tr: Depeculari, Depeculator, see Compilare, compilator.

units.la: Depellere, vid. Abigere, Arcere.
units.tr: Depellere, see Abigere, Arcere.

units.la: Deperire, vid. Deamare.
units.tr: Deperire, see Deamare.

units.la: Depilis, vid. Glaber.
units.tr: Depilis, see Glaber.

units.la: Deplanare] Ad planum reducere, Plin. Coæquare terram cylindro, Pallad. Degrumare. Degrumari viam, Lucil. Explere cicatrices, Plin. Inæquare. Fossas perducere, Cæs. Vid. Æquare.
units.tr: Deplanare: to bring back to level, Plin. To level the ground with a roller, Pallad. To smooth. To smooth a road, Lucil. To fill up scars, Plin. To make even. To carry trenches through, Caes. See Aequare.

units.la: Deplorare, vid. Deflere.
units.tr: Deplorare, see Deflere.

units.la: Deploratus, vid. Depositus.
units.tr: Deploratus, see Depositus.

units.la: Deponere à se officium aliquod] Decedere magistratu, Cic. Exuere senatorium ordinem. Exutâ dignitate, Tac. Abdicare magistratum, Sallust. Abdicavit se consulatu, Liv. Exaugurare sacerdotium, Gell. Vid. Abdicare se.
units.tr: Deponere à se officium aliquod: to step down from an office, Cic. To strip off the senatorial rank. With dignity laid aside, Tac. To give up the magistracy, Sallust. He resigned from the consulship, Liv. To lay down the priesthood, Gell. See Abdicare se.

units.la: Deponere officio aliquem] Tollere ab officio aliquem, Cic. Abdicare, Plin. Abrogare alicui magistratum. Movere aliquem senatu, Cic. Val.M. Depositus imperio, Suet. Discingere. Spoliare cingulo, Bud. Imminuere alicujus imperium, Liv. De coelo detractus, Bud. Demovere aliquem magistratu, Tac. Defecrare, (ex sacro profanum facere) Sipont. Exaugare aliquem, Capitol. Exauctorare, Iul. Cap. Episcopum removit à sacramento quod habebat, Amm. Dejicere aliquem ædilitate, honore. Dejicere senatum gubernaculis, Cic. Eradere albo judicum aliquem, Suet.
