units.tr: To depose someone from office] To remove someone from office, Cic. To dismiss, Plin. To repeal someone's magistracy. To remove someone from the senate, Cic. Val. Max. Deprived of command, Suet. To ungird. To strip of the belt, Bud. To diminish someone's authority, Liv. Dragged down from heaven, Bud. To remove someone from a magistracy, Tac. To desecrate (to make the sacred profane), Sipont. To deprive someone of augurship, Capitol. To discharge from service, Iul. Cap. He removed the bishop from the sacred office he held, Amm. To unseat someone from the aedileship or from an honour. To remove the senate from the helm of government, Cic. To strike someone from the roll of judges, Suet.

units.la: Deponere cum aliquo, vid. Certare.
units.tr: To lay down with someone: see To contend.

units.la: Depopulari, vid. Vastare.
units.tr: To lay waste: see To devastate.

units.la: Deportare aliquid] Devehere aliquem in ultimas terras, Liv. Transportare in insulam aliquem, Sen.
units.tr: To carry off something] To carry someone off to the farthest lands, Liv. To transport someone to an island, Sen.

units.la: Deposcere] Efflagitare. Urgere præfecturam. Pugnare aliquid. Et hoc pugnatum, ut. Postulare aliquid, Cic. Depostulare sibi aliquid, Tac.
units.tr: To demand urgently] To press insistently. To press for a prefecture. To fight for something. And this was fought for, that... To ask for something, Cic. To demand something for oneself, Tac.

units.la: Depositum] Fiducia. Creditum aliquid, Cic. Hor. Fidei commissum, Vlp.
units.tr: Deposit] A trust. Something entrusted, Cic. Hor. A trust bequest, Ulp.

units.la: Depositus à medicis] Deploratus, Plin. Conclamatus, Lucan.
units.tr: Given up by the physicians] Despaired of, Plin. Given up for dead, Lucan.

units.la: Depositus ab officio] Erasus, Plin. Abactus, Fest. Exutus honoribus, Id.
units.tr: Deposed from office] Erased, Plin. Driven out, Fest. Stripped of honours, Id.

units.la: Depraedatio, vid. Spoliatio.
units.tr: Plundering: see Spoliation.

units.la: Depraedari, vid. Praedari.
units.tr: To plunder: see To pillage.

units.la: Depravare] Destruere aliquem, Plin. Praecorrumpere donis, Ovid. Perdere amando, Ter. Transfundere in aliquem vitium, Cic. Facere vitium, Vitruv. Conteritur ferrum, vita, Ovid. Infringere spem, Cic. Manus affert suo beneficio, Sen. Diffingere aliquid, Hor. Vid. Corrumpere.
units.tr: To corrupt] To destroy someone, Plin. To corrupt beforehand with gifts, Ovid. To ruin by loving, Ter. To transfer a vice to someone, Cic. To make faulty, Vitruv. The iron, the life is worn away, Ovid. To break hope, Cic. To lay hands on one's own benefactor, Sen. To mar something, Hor. See To corrupt.

units.la: Deprecari] Veniam irarum exposcere, Liv. Ignoscendi venia petenda, Cic. Vid. Intercedere.
units.tr: To deprecate] To seek pardon for anger, Liv. To ask for the pardon of forgiveness, Cic. See To intercede.

units.la: Deprecari culpam] Depellere crimen, aversari, abominari, rejicere, refellere, negare, inficiari, propulsare, Er.
units.tr: To deny a fault] To ward off a charge, to shun, abominate, reject, refute, deny, disavow, repel, Erasmus.

units.la: Deprecatio] Deprecatio veniae, facti. Ignoscendi postulatio, Cic.
units.tr: Deprecation] A deprecation of pardon for a deed. A request for forgiveness, Cic.

units.la: Deprehendere aliquem] Inopinantem deprehendere, Caes. Texentem tela studiose offendimus. Decipula murem cepit. Sorex suo indicio periit, Adag.
units.tr: To catch someone] To catch someone unawares, Caes. We have eagerly caught him weaving his nets. The trap caught a mouse. The shrew perished by its own betrayal, Adag.

units.la: Deprehendere (2) i. cognoscere] Ad sensum & opinionem alicujus rei penetrare. Rem non conjectura, sed oculis ac manibus tenere, Cic.
units.tr: To detect (2), that is, to recognise] To penetrate into the sense and opinion of some matter. To hold a thing with the eyes and hands, not by conjecture, Cic.

units.la: Depressus locus, vid. Inferior.
units.tr: A lowered place: see Lower.

units.la: Deprimere] Submittere fasces, Quint. Vim dicendi tantis comparatam laboribus, ad unum auditorem demittere, est quaedam tacita indignatio, Cic. Infimata ad miserias ingenia, Apul.
units.tr: To press down] To lower the fasces, Quint. To bring down to a single listener the power of speech won by such great labour is a kind of silent indignation, Cic. Minds brought low to miseries, Apul.

units.la: Depromere, vid. Promere.
units.tr: To bring forth: see To produce.

units.la: Depsere farinam] Condepsere, subigere far, massam, Cat. Massare, id est, massam facere, Lucr.
units.tr: To knead flour] To knead together, to work flour into a mass, Cato. To make into a mass, that is, to form a lump, Lucr.

units.la: Depudere] Perfricare faciem, Plin. Frontem, Mart. Os, Cic. Pudori nuncium remittere. Depuduit, Ovid. Pudere dedidicit.
units.tr: To feel shame] To rub the face clean, Plin. The forehead, Mart. The mouth, Cic. To send back the messenger of shame. He became shameless, Ovid. He has unlearned how to be ashamed.

units.la: Describere aliquid] Definire verbis. Deformare, depingere, Persequi. Pingere rem suis coloribus. Definitione quam vim res habet, exprimere. Informare, Cic. Tractare copiosissimè, Quint.
units.tr: To describe something] To define in words. To shape, portray, pursue. To paint a thing in its own colours. To express by definition the force a thing has. To sketch, Cic. To treat very fully, Quint.

units.la: Descriptio, vid. Definitio.
units.tr: Description: see Definition.

units.la: Deserere] Derelinquere. Derelictui habere. Desertum esse pati. Destituere aliquem. A causa alicujus recedere. Aliquem non solùm relinquere, sed etiam prodere. Postmittere aliquid. Defecit illum spes. Migrare ea, quæ pertinent ad veritatem & fidem, & non servare, Cic. Longum valere jussit. Dimittit dolor aliquem, Celf. Remittere nuncium mundo & hujus miseriis, Basil. Rebus humanis valere & plaudere dixit, Apul. Emanere, Scal. Linquere, Cic. Virg.
units.tr: To desert] To abandon. To hold in abandonment. To allow to remain deserted. To leave someone in the lurch. To withdraw from someone's cause. To not only leave someone but even betray him. To give up something. Hope fails him. To migrate from those things which pertain to truth and faith and not to keep them, Cic. He bade a long farewell. Pain dismisses someone, Celsus. To send a message to the world and its miseries, Basil. He said farewell and applauded human affairs, Apul. To flow out, Scal. To leave, Cic. Virg.

units.la: Desertio] Destitutio. Relictio Consulis. Derelictio utilitatis. Prætepmissio alicujus rei,Cic. Derelictus,ûs, Gell.
units.tr: Desertion] Abandonment. The leaving of a consul. The abandoning of advantage. Giving up of some thing, Cic. Abandonment, Gell.

units.la: Desertor, vid. Miles, & Profugus.
units.tr: Deserter: see Soldier and Fugitive.

units.la: Desertum] Desertæ solitudines. Cultu vacantes regiones, Cic. Soli loci. Solæ terræ,Ter. Vastitas soli sterilis,Sen. Deserta & inhospita tesqua, Hor. Vastitudo inculta, Pacuv. Ferus ager, Fest. Eremus, Isid.
units.tr: Desert] Deserted solitudes. Regions empty of cultivation, Cic. Lonely places. Lonely lands, Ter. The barrenness of sterile soil, Sen. Deserted and inhospitable wastes, Hor. An uncultivated wilderness, Pacuv. Wild land, Fest. A wilderness, Isid.

units.la: Desertus locus] Solus locus. Orba civitas. Relicta possessio. Derelicta regio, Cic. Desolati penates, Tac. Vacuefacta possessio, Æmil. Prob. Solus ager, Virg. Vastus locus à natura & humano cultu, Salust. Adespota bona, (quæ in nullius dominio sunt), Bud. Locus nullo hominum cultu, Tac. Incultum & derelictum solum, Cic. Desolata loca, Plin.
units.tr: A deserted place] A lonely place. A bereft city. Abandoned property. An abandoned region, Cic. Desolate household gods, Tac. An emptied possession, Aemil. Prob. A lonely field, Virg. A waste place, empty of nature and human cultivation, Sall. Goods without an owner (which belong to no one), Bud. A place without human cultivation, Tac. Uncultivated and abandoned soil, Cic. Desolate places, Plin.

units.la: Desiderabilis] Optatus. Optatissimus. Exoptatus. Expetendus. In desiderio est civitatis. Est in optatis, Cic. Cupitus, Plaut. Votivus conspectus alicujus, Apul. Exoptabilis, Sil. Ego te, mea vota quàm primum videre cupio, Ter. Appetibilis, Macrob.
units.tr: Desirable] Wished for. Most wished for. Longed for. To be sought after. He is in the city's longing. It is among things wished for, Cic. Desired, Plaut. The longed-for sight of someone, Apul. Desirable, Sil. I long to see you, my wishes, as soon as possible, Ter. Worth seeking, Macrob.

units.la: Desiderare] Esse in desiderio alicujus rei. Teneri, moveri desiderio. Tenet me tui desiderium. Concupiscere mortem, opes. Appetere mortem. Avere aliquid audire & discere. Expetere aliquid, Cic. Est aliquid in desiderio, Id.
units.tr: To desire] To be in want of something. To be held and moved by longing. Longing for you holds me. To long for death, wealth. To seek death. To have an eagerness to hear and learn something. To seek after something, Cic. Something is in longing, Id.

units.la: Insidet mihi desiderium alicujus rei, Lucr. Cupio te videre, Plaut. Optare & expetere aliquam fortunam, Cic. Exoptare aliquem exitum, Id. Peroptare filiam alicujus nuptiis, Cornel. Nep. Est in votis aliquid, Perf. Vota facere ut, Cic. Exposcere audire, Virg. Percupere, postulare, Ter. Apposcere plus, Hor.
units.tr: A longing for something sits within me, Lucr. I wish to see you, Plaut. To wish for and seek a certain fortune, Cic. To long for a certain end, Id. To desire a daughter in marriage with someone, Cornelius Nepos. Something is among one's prayers, Persius. To make vows that, Cic. To long to hear, Virg. To desire greatly, to demand, Ter. To ask for more, Hor.

units.la: Desiderare vehementer] Ardere cupiditate incredibili. Inflammari cupiditate honoris. Rapi studio inflammato ad. Flagrare amore. Laborare ex desiderio. Efferri studio videndi aliquem. Inhiare alicui rei, Cic. Corvus hians. Perfixus desiderio, Er. Vid. Avere.
units.tr: To desire greatly] To burn with incredible desire. To be inflamed with the desire of honour. To be carried away with an inflamed eagerness to. To be aflame with love. To labour from longing. To be carried away with eagerness to see someone. To gape after something, Cic. A gaping crow. Transfixed with longing, Erasmus. See To crave.

units.la: Desidere, in fundum delabi] Sidere ad ima, Plin. Subsidere. Pessum ire, Col. Cum ad infinitam altitudinem terra descedisset. Si montes resedissent, Cic. Multis locis labes facta sit, Liv. Subsedit pondere humus, Ovid. Terra in profundum abiit, Iul. Obseq.
units.tr: To sink, to slip down to the bottom] To settle to the lowest depths, Plin. To subside. To go to ruin, Col. When the earth had sunk to an infinite depth. If the mountains had subsided, Cic. The ground gave way in many places, Liv. The earth subsided under the weight, Ovid. The earth went down into the depths, Obseq.

units.la: Desidere hiatu] Hauriri urbes terrae hiatibus, publicum malum est. Hiatus sorbuit aliquid. Perire chasmate, Ulp. In subitam cavernam concidentis soli, lapsus abduxit urbem, Sen. Multa moenia in terris ceciderunt magnis motibus, & multae per mare pessum subsedere suis pariter cum civibus urbes, Lucr. Pedibus raptim tellus subtracta fertur in barathrum. Abeant per inane profundum, Id. Dehiscit alicui terra, Virg. Hiscere nempe tibi terra neganda foret, Ovid.
units.tr: To sink into a chasm] That cities should be swallowed up by yawning earth is a public calamity. A gulf swallowed something. To perish in a chasm, Ulp. When the ground collapsed into a sudden cavern, the sliding earth carried the city away, Sen. Many walls have fallen on the earth in great quakes, and many cities have sunk into the sea together with their citizens, Lucr. The earth was hurriedly withdrawn from under their feet and carried into the pit. Let them vanish through the empty deep, Id. The earth gapes open for someone, Virg. Surely the earth would have been forbidden to gape open for you, Ovid.

units.la: Desidere, otiosum esse] Desideo reses, Pacuv. Marcescere desidiâ, Liv. Residere, Plaut. Sedere, Virg. Sedere ferias, Plaut. Torpescere socordiâ, Sallust. Marcet animus, Liv. Turdescere, Lucr. Pigrescere, Plin. Deponere studium. Lentere, Lucil. Vid. Otio torpere.
units.tr: To sit idle] I sit idle, at rest, Pacuv. To waste away in idleness, Liv. To sit back, Plaut. To sit, Virg. To sit out the holidays, Plaut. To grow numb with sloth, Sall. The spirit withers, Liv. To grow sluggish, Lucr. To become lazy, Plin. To lay aside one's study. To grow slack, Lucil. See To languish in leisure.

units.la: Desidendo nihil proficimus] Nec currimus, nec navigamus.
units.tr: By sitting idle we make no progress] We neither run nor sail.

units.la: Desiderium] Optatio. Optatum. Desideratio. Votum. Appetentia, Cic. Est in votis, Perf. Desiderii flamma, ardor, Er.
units.tr: Desire] Wishing. A thing wished for. Longing. Vow. Appetite, Cic. It is among one's prayers, Persius. A flame of longing, a burning, Erasmus.

units.la: Desideria cuique sua] Canis panes somnians, Adag.
units.tr: Each person has his own desires] A dog dreams of bread, Adag.

units.la: Desidia] Desidies. Socordia. Segnities, Ter. Inertia laboris. Ignavia. Veternus civitatem occupavit. Pigritia. TardiTarditas. Desidiosissimum otium,Cic. Inertia. Animi torpedo, Sal. Torpor mentis, Firmic. Torpor corporis, Virg. Exercitus marcore ducis circumventus, Paterc. Tarditudo, Plaut.
units.tr: Idleness] Sloth. Lethargy. Sluggishness, Ter. Idleness from work. Indolence. A drowsiness has taken hold of the city. Laziness. Sluggishness. Most idle leisure, Cic. Inertia. Numbness of spirit, Sall. Torpor of mind, Firmicus. Torpor of body, Virg. An army surrounded by its leader's languor, Paterc. Slowness, Plaut.

units.la: Desidiosus] Desidiæ indormit, Plin. Deses, Liv. Supinus,Iuv. Reses & Residuus,Acci. apud Fest. Reses populus animus, Virg. Subbasilicanus. Marcidus,Plaut. Subrostranus. Ignavus. Segnis, Cic. Oscitans, Ter. Persegnis, Liv. Socordissimus, Apul. Endymion,Varr. Vid.Otiosus,Piger.
units.tr: Idle] Dozes off in idleness, Plin. Slothful, Liv. Lazy, Juv. Idle and remaining, Accius, cited in Festus. An idle people, a sluggish spirit, Virg. Lying low under the basilica. Withered, Plaut. Lying under the rostra. Shiftless. Sluggish, Cic. Yawning, Ter. Very sluggish, Liv. Most lazy, Apul. Endymion, Varro. See Leisurely, Lazy.

units.la: Designare, vid. Definire.
units.tr: To designate: see To define.

units.la: Designator hospitiorum] Epistathmus,Bud. Metator,Brissonius. Mensor,Veget. Epidemeticus,Cæl. Rhod.
units.tr: Billeting officer] Quartermaster, Bud. Surveyor, Brissonius. Measurer, Vegetius. Hospitable host, Caelius Rhodiginus.

units.la: Desinere] Abire incepto, Liv. Abstistere, Abscedere incepto, Id. Canere receptui. Discedere à contentione. Facere intercapedinem scribendi. Desistere facere. Desistere sententiâ, à sententia, de sententiâ. Desitus est vocari Papisius. Intermissionem à re aliquâ facere. Modum lugendi facere. Modum inimicitiarum statuere. Interponere moram. Reprimere objurgationem, Cic. Cesso dicere. Postquam aurora est, nunquam concessavimus lavari. Finem facere orandi. Quiescere. Mitte male loqui. Neque defetiscar experiri donec, Ter. Rescindere beneficium, Sen. Vacare à scribendo, Plin. Iun. Si unquam fatiscar facere quidpiam boni, Pac.
units.tr: To cease] To depart from a undertaking, Liv. To withdraw, to retire from an undertaking, Id. To sound the retreat. To withdraw from a dispute. To make a break in writing. To stop doing. To desist from an opinion, from a view. He ceased to be called a Papist. To make a pause from something. To make an end of mourning. To set a limit to enmity. To interpose a delay. To check a rebuke, Cic. I hesitate to speak. Since dawn, we have never delayed bathing. To make an end of praying. To rest. Stop speaking ill. Nor will I tire of trying until, Ter. To cancel a kindness, Sen. To be free from writing, Pliny the Younger. If ever I flag in doing something good, Pacuvius.

units.la: Definit, vid. Terminatur.
units.tr: It ends: see It is bounded.

units.la: Despipere] Fatuari, Sen. A mente deseri. Dementem esse. Mente capi, Cic. Morari (stultè agere) inter homines desiit, Suet, Exire à se. Vid. Delirare.
units.tr: To be out of one's mind] To be foolish, Sen. To be abandoned by one's mind. To be mad. To be seized by madness, Cic. He has ceased to live among men (acting foolishly), Suet. To go out of oneself. See To rave.

units.la: Desolare, vid. Vastare.
units.tr: To lay waste: see To devastate.

units.la: Despectus, vid. Contemptio.
units.tr: Contempt: see Scorn.

units.la: Desperare] Desperare honores. Desperare saluti. Desperare se. Sibi ipse desperat. A se ipso desperatus. Abjicere spem aliquid faciendi. Abjicere spem alicujus rei, & de aliquo. Perdere spem. Orbari spe. Spes extenuatur, evanescit. Deserit me spes. Frangi animo. Concidere mente. Animo contrahi, & animum contrahere. Abjicere clypeum. Jacet. Diffidit. Abjicit hastas, Cic. Conclamatum est. Decidere spe, de spe, Ter. Deficit me spes. Depelli de spe. Deturbari spe, & ex spe, Cic. Labi spe. Pervenire ad desperationem. Deserere sese, Caes. Diffidere rebus suis. Praedamnatâ spe dimicandi. Cadere animis. Succumbere animo. Abjicere se & prosternere, Liv. Demittere mentes, Virg. Despondere animum, Plaut.
units.tr: To despair] To despair of honours. To despair of salvation. To despair of oneself. He despairs of himself. Abandoned by himself. To give up hope of doing something. To abandon hope of something, and concerning someone. To lose hope. To be bereft of hope. Hope is weakened, vanishes. Hope forsakes me. To be broken in spirit. To collapse in mind. To be drawn together in spirit, and to draw oneself together in spirit. To cast away the shield. He lies prostrate. He loses faith. He throws away his spears, Cic. It is given up for lost. To fall from hope, from expectation, Ter. Hope fails me. To be driven from hope. To be thrown down from hope and out of hope, Cic. To slip from hope. To come to despair. To abandon oneself, Caes. To distrust one's own affairs. With hope of fighting already condemned. To fall in spirit. To succumb in spirit. To cast oneself down and prostrate, Liv. To lower the spirits, Virg. To despond in spirit, Plaut.

units.la: Desperandum non est] Adhuc coelum volvitur. Adhuc aliquis Deus nos respicit. Aegroto dum anima est, spes est. Dum spiro, spero. Nihilne a Deo speremus opis? Nullum ne auxilium coelitus exspectandum est? Haeccine Deum aut nescire, aut negligere? Nullane Deo nostri cura? Quid si hoc Deus avertat, aut in melius convertat? Eventum a Deo exspectemus. Fata viam invenient. Desperatio contumelia est in bonitatem Dei. Non dum omnium dierum sol occidit.
units.tr: One must not despair] The heavens are still turning. Some God still looks upon us. While the sick man has breath, there is hope. While I breathe, I hope. Shall we expect no help at all from God? Must no aid be looked for from heaven? Can we suppose that God either does not know of this or neglects it? Does God have no care for us? What if God turns this aside, or changes it for the better? Let us wait for the outcome from God. The fates will find a way. Despair is an insult to the goodness of God. The sun has not yet set on all days.

units.la: Desperabundus] In statum inemendabilem adductus, Sen. Ad ultima salutis detrusus. Desperatissimus latro extremae poenae certus, Apul.
units.tr: Desperabundus] Brought into a state that cannot be mended, Sen. Thrust to the furthest edge of safety. A most desperate robber, certain of the extreme penalty, Apul.

units.la: Desperabundus quid vis tentat] Desperatio facit Monachum. Flectere si nequeo superos, Acheronta movebo, Virg.
units.tr: Desperabundus quid vis tentat] Despair makes a monk. If I cannot bend the gods above, I will stir Acheron, Virg.

units.la: Desperanter] Perdite se gerere, Cic. Gladiatorio animo ad me affectat viam, Ter. Aperto ore in mare desilire, Sen.
units.tr: Desperanter] To act recklessly, Cic. He is trying to reach me with a gladiator's courage, Ter. To leap into the sea with open mouth, Sen.

units.la: Desperatio] Projecta audacia, Cic.
units.tr: Desperatio] Audacity thrown away, Cic.

units.la: Desperatus] Exspes, Hor. Depositus, Virg. Stat. Conclamatum est, Ter. Res conclamata & perdita, Amm. Actum & conclamatum est, Id. Res illi ad restim rediit.
units.tr: Desperatus] Without hope, Hor. Abandoned, given up for dead, Virg. Stat. It has been given up, Ter. A matter given up and lost, Amm. It is done and given up, Id. His affair has come back to the noose.

units.la: Despicere, vid. Contemnere.
units.tr: Despicere, see Contemnere.

units.la: Despicere, (2) deorsum spectare] Aspicere ex alto, Sen. Ad terram aspice, & despice. Demittere oculos, Plaut. Despectare regionem oppido, (id est, ex oppido) Liv. Prospicere ex speculâ. Identidem ex altissima rupe speculabundus, Cic.
units.tr: Despicere, (2) deorsum spectare] To look down from on high, Sen. Look down at the earth and despise it. To lower the eyes, Plaut. To survey the region from the town (that is, from the town), Liv. To look out from a watchtower. Gazing again and again from a very high rock, Cic.

units.la: Despondere sponsam] Pacisci filiam alicui, Cic. Pacisci nuptias filiae cum aliquo, Justin. Spondere alicui aliquam uxorem, Plaut. Destinare alicui filiam, Plin. Iun. Dicta est inter nos nuptiarum dies, Afran.
units.tr: Despondere sponsam] To contract a daughter to someone, Cic. To arrange a daughter's marriage with someone, Justin. To promise a wife to someone, Plaut. To destine a daughter to someone, Plin. Iun. The day of the wedding has been fixed between us, Afran.

units.la: Desponsata] Pacta conjux, Ovid. Pacto jugali destinata, ta, Apul. Desponsa, Cic. Sperata antè quàm petatur & promittatur, deinde pacta promissa dicitur, Plaut.
units.tr: Desponsata] A wife pledged, Ovid. Destined by a marriage contract, Apul. Betrothed, Cic. Hoped for before she is sought and promised; afterwards she is called pledged and promised, Plaut.

units.la: Desponsatio] Pactio connubialis, Liv. Sponsalia, Cic. Sponsus, Varr. Sponsionum contractus. Stipulationum contractus, Gell.
units.tr: Desponsatio] A marriage agreement, Liv. Betrothal, Cic. A betrothed man, Varr. A contract of pledges. A contract of stipulations, Gell.

units.la: Despumare] Detergere spumam, Plin.
units.tr: Despumare] To wipe off the foam, Plin.

units.la: Desquamare] Depurgare pisces, Plin. Oppectere, (id est, digitis ceu pectine purgare) Lambin.
units.tr: Desquamare] To clean fish of their scales, Plin. To scrape off (that is, to clean with the fingers as with a comb), Lambin.

units.la: Destillans humor] Catarrhus, Vall. Defluxio, Henr. Steph. Destillatio, Cels. Rheumatisma, Cæl. Rhod. Gravedo, Lambin.
units.tr: Destillans humor] Catarrh, Vall. A flux, Henr. Steph. Distillation, Cels. Rheumatism, Cael. Rhod. A cold in the head, Lambin.

units.la: Destillare aquam, oleum &c.] Aquas stillatitias ex herbis calore ignis elicere, Matthiol. Sublimare, Iul. Scal. est tenuissimas partes vi ignis à crassioribus, sublatas secernere.
units.tr: Destillare aquam, oleum &c.] To draw distilled waters from herbs by the heat of a fire, Matthiol. Sublimating, Iul. Scal., is the separating, by the force of fire, of the finest parts from the grosser ones, lifting them away.

units.la: Destructio] Demolitio. Dejectus arborum, Plin. Excisio tectorum, Cic. Ruina, Sal.
units.tr: Destructio] Demolition. Felling of trees, Plin. Pulling down of roofs, Cic. Ruin, Sal.

units.la: Destructor] Demolitor, Vitruv. Eversor, Cic.
units.tr: Destructor] A demolisher, Vitruv. An overthrower, Cic.

units.la: Destruere] Demoliri. Demolitione aliquid tollere. Evertere civitatem. Inferre tectis eversionem. Deturbare tectum, ædificium. Revellere crucem, quæ fixa est. Affligere statuam, Edere ruinas. Subvertere molem, Cic. Dejicere mœnia, Ovid. Dare ruinas. Disturbare ædes, Lucr. Proruere urbem. Sternere ariete muros, Liv. Destruere mœnia. Convellere turres, Virg. Prosternere oppida. Consternere mœnia, Sil. Percellere arietem, Varr.
units.tr: Destruere] To demolish. To remove something by demolition. To overthrow a city. To bring overthrow upon roofs. To pull down a roof or building. To tear up a cross that is fixed in the ground. To knock down a statue. To bring about ruins. To overturn a mass, Cic. To throw down walls, Ovid. To bring about ruin. To pull down houses, Lucr. To tear down a city. To level walls with a battering-ram, Liv. To destroy walls. To tear down towers, Virg. To lay towns flat. To strike down walls, Sil. To shatter the ram, Varr.

units.la: Desuefieri, & Desuefacere, vid. Dediscere, dedocere.
units.tr: Desuefieri, & Desuefacere, see Dediscere, dedocere.

units.la: Desuper] Supernè volvitur amnis. Insuper imposita Ætna. Superpremor, Virg. E sublimi jacere, Plin. Deinsuper, Sallust. Exsupero, Lucr. Super è vallo prospectat.
units.tr: Desuper] From above: the river rolls down from on high. Etna piled upon above. I am pressed from above, Virg. To lie from on high, Plin. From above, Sallust. To rise above, Lucr. He looks out from above the rampart.

units.la: Detegere aliquid] Revelare caput, Arnob. Aperire, patefacere, Cic. Nudare viscera, Virg. Retegere scrinium, Juv. Adaperire, Plin.
units.tr: Detegere aliquid] To uncover the head, Arnob. To open, to lay open, Cic. To bare the entrails, Virg. To unlock a chest, Juv. To open up, Plin.

units.la: Detentio] Retentio currus vel equorum, Cic. Retardatio, Id. Continentia, Suet. Moratio terræ, Firmic.
units.tr: Detentio] Holding back of a chariot or horses, Cic. Delay, Id. Restraint, Suet. Stopping of the earth's motion, Firmic.

units.la: Detergere, vid. Abstergere.
units.tr: Detergere, see Abstergere.

units.la: Deterrere, vid. Absterrere.
units.tr: Deterrere, see Absterrere.

units.la: Determinare, vid. Terminare.
units.tr: Determinare, see Terminare.

units.la: Detestari, vid. Abhorrere. Detinere aliquem, aliquid] Demorari aliquem, Retinere. Ventus nos tenuit. Reprehendere manu aliquem, Retardare. Spes me obtentabat, Cic. Infrenare navigia anchoris pluribus, Plin. Retrahere fugitivum, Varr. Inhibere tela, Liv. Premere carmen in annum novum, Hor. Sustinere manum, Ovid. Restringit nauseam hæc herba, Plin.
units.tr: Detestari, see Abhorrere. Detinere aliquem, aliquid] To delay someone: to keep someone back. The wind kept us back. To hold someone back by the hand, to delay him. Hope kept me back, Cic. To check ships with several anchors, Plin. To drag back a runaway slave, Varr. To check weapons, Liv. To hold a poem back until the new year, Hor. To hold back the hand, Ovid. This herb checks nausea, Plin.

units.la: Detorquere, vid. Dirigere.
units.tr: Detorquere, see Dirigere.

units.la: Detrahere] Deripere aliquem capillo de curru, Plaut.
units.tr: Detrahere] To snatch someone by the hair from a chariot, Plaut.

units.la: Detrectare laborem] Restitare, Ter. Resistere, Liv. Cunctanter procedere, Col. Tergiversari. Muginari, id est, tardè conari, Cic. Dubito dicere aliquid, Plaut. Tardari, Cæs.
units.tr: Detrectare laborem] To resist, Ter. To oppose, Liv. To proceed reluctantly, Col. To shirk, to dodge. To mutter, that is, to try slowly, Cic. I hesitate to say something, Plaut. To be held up, Caes.

units.la: Detrimentum, vid. Damnum.
units.tr: Detrimentum, see Damnum.

units.la: Detritus] Trita vestis, Hor. Subtritus. Vid. Attritus.
units.tr: Detritus] A worn garment, Hor. Worn down. See Attritus.

units.la: Detrudere aliquem de] Deturbare aliquem de fortunis, Cic. Proturbare à solio, Val. Arg.
units.tr: Detrudere aliquem de] To drive someone out of his fortunes, Cic. To thrust from a throne, Val. Arg.

units.la: Detumescere] Desedit tumor, Celf. Recessit venter. Deturget Nilus, Plin. Deferbuit mare. Sternuntur fluctus. Conflaccescunt, Gell. Abire in profundum, Cic. Subsidunt undæ, Virg.
units.tr: Detumescere] The swelling has subsided, Celf. The belly has receded. The Nile subsides, Plin. The sea has ceased to boil. The waves are laid low. They wilt, Gell. To go down into the depths, Cic. The waves sink, Virg.

units.la: Deturpare, vid. Contaminare.
units.tr: Deturpare, see Contaminare.

units.la: Devehere aliquid]Convehere æs plaustris ad ærarium, Liv. Convectare prædas, Virg.
units.tr: Devehere aliquid] To carry money in wagons to the treasury, Liv. To carry off plunder, Virg.

units.la: Devenit res eò] In eum casum veneram, ut, Cic. In eum casum res deducta est. Res ad pugnam venit. Eò recidit. In eum locum adducta res est. Rem huc deduxi, Id. Eò res devoluta est, Liv. Adeo res rediit, Ter. Eò res recidit, Quint. Eò insolentiæ furorisque processit, Plin. Iun. In eam fortunam deveni, Cic. Ventum juxta seditionem, Tac. Progredi in, Cic.
units.tr: Devenit res eò] I had come to such a pass that, Cic. The matter has been brought to such a state. The matter came to battle. The matter fell back there. The matter has been led to that point. I have brought the matter to this point, Id. The matter has rolled down to that point, Liv. So the matter has come round again, Ter. The matter has fallen back to this, Quint. He advanced to such a height of insolence and frenzy, Plin. Iun. I have come to such a fortune, Cic. We came close to sedition, Tac. To advance into, Cic.

units.la: Devexus, vid. Declivis.
units.tr: Devexus, see Declivis.

units.la: Deviare] Deerrare itinere, Quint. Decessit viâ errabundus, Suet. Flexiones, diverticula persequi, Cic. Exorbitare, Aug. Exspatiari à viâ diversissimè, Sipont. Vid. Aberrare.
units.tr: Deviare] To stray from the road, Quint. He wandered off the road, Suet. To pursue bends and byways, Cic. To go beyond the bounds, Aug. To wander far from the road, Sipont. See Aberrare.

units.la: Devincire] Vita coërcebat capillos, Ovid. Nectere brachia, Id. Prævincire, Gell. Vid. Alligare. Colligare.
units.tr: Devincire] Life held back her hair, Ovid. To knot arms together, Id. To bind fast, Gell. See Alligare. Colligare.

units.la: Devinctus alicui] Obstrictus maximis beneficii vinculis. Addictum, deditum sibi ac liberis suis habere aliquem. Obligatus. Servus. Mancipatus alicui, Cic. Obnoxius sum illi, Plaut. Tenetur jurejurando, voto, legibus. Auctoratus, Liv. Offrenatus unius prædæ offulâ, Apul.
units.tr: Devinctus alicui] Bound by the greatest chains of a benefit. To hold someone devoted and given over to oneself and one's children. Obliged. A servant. Bound to someone, Cic. I am beholden to him, Plaut. He is bound by oath, vow, or laws. Hired, Liv. Caught by the bait of a single prey, Apul.

units.la: Devium] Secessus, Virg. Seductus recessus, Ovid. Diverticula, flexiones, anfractus, Cic.
units.tr: Devium] A secluded retreat, Virg. A remote recess, Ovid. Byways, bends, windings, Cic.

units.la: Devius] Devius, Cic. Devia gens, Liv. Devia rura, Ovid.
units.tr: Devius] Out of the way, Cic. An out-of-the-way people, Liv. Remote countryside, Ovid.

units.la: Devolvere aliquid] Provolvo subter jugum saxa. Infesto pondere saxa volvere. Detrudere naves scopulo, Virg. Proturbare hostes in præceps, Liv. Demovere aliquid, Cic. Commoliri, Lucr.
units.tr: Devolvere aliquid] To roll stones down under a yoke. To roll rocks with a heavy weight. To drive ships onto a reef, Virg. To drive enemies headlong, Liv. To move something away, Cic. To contrive, Lucr.

units.la: Devorare] Abligurire, Obligurire, Cic. Ter. Absorbere, Plin. Vid. Vorare.
units.tr: Devorare] To lick up, Cic. Ter. To swallow up, Plin. See Vorare.

units.la: Devotio, Vid. Dedicatio.
units.tr: Devotio, see Dedicatio.

units.la: Devovere] Devotare, Cic. Devovere se pro aliquo, Id. Livius.
units.tr: Devovere] To devote, Cic. To devote oneself for someone, Id. Livius.

units.la: Deus] Mens, Cic. Mens mundum fabricata est. Numen. Numen divinum, Lucr. Incorporalis ratio. Ingentium operum artifex, Sen. Causa causarum, Id. Circulus æternus, cujus centrum ubique, circumferentia nusquam. Author omnium & fons, Er. Artifex, Fabricator, Effector mundi. Molitor mundi, Cic. Opifex, Id. Conditor ævi, Claud. Qui nobis omnia solus est, Varr.
units.tr: Deus] Mind, Cic. Mind fashioned the world. Divine power, Lucr. Incorporeal reason. Artificer of mighty works, Sen. Cause of causes, Id. An eternal circle whose centre is everywhere and whose circumference is nowhere. Author and fountain of all, Erasm. Artificer, maker, producer of the world. Builder of the world, Cic. Maker, Id. Founder of the age, Claud. He who alone is all things to us, Varr.

units.la: Deus est ubique] Jovis omnia plena. Omnia Deo plena.
units.tr: Deus est ubique] Jupiter's presence fills all things. All things are full of God.

units.la: Deus omniscius] Deo nihil clausum. Oculus Dei fortissimus.
units.tr: Deus omniscius] Nothing is closed to God. The eye of God is most keen.

units.la: Deus regit omnia] Fatum rotat omnia. Cum Deo quisque & gaudet, & flet. Consilia humana divinitus gubernantur. Sors nostra in manu Dei.
units.tr: Deus regit omnia] Fate turns all things. Each person both rejoices and weeps with God. Human counsels are governed by divine power. Our lot lies in the hand of God.

units.la: Deus est longanimis] Deus natura cunctabundus. Deus tolerat malos, ut exerceat bonos. Dii laneos habent pedes. Dii lenti, sed certi vindices. Deorum molæ tardè quidem molunt, sed tenuissimè. Lento gradu ad vindictam sui divina procedit ira, tarditatemque supplicii gravitate compensat, Val. Max.
units.tr: Deus est longanimis] God is slow by nature. God bears with the wicked in order to test the good. The gods have woolly feet. The gods are slow but sure avengers. The mills of the gods grind slowly, but very finely. With slow step divine anger advances to avenge itself, and it makes up for its tardiness by the severity of the punishment, Val. Max.

units.la: Deus dat cui vult] Dormienti Dii conficient. Dormientis rete trahere.
units.tr: Deus dat cui vult] The gods will accomplish it for the sleeper. To drag in the net of a sleeper.

units.la: Deus fortunet] Adsint Dii beati. Dii fortunent tuum patrimonium. Bene hæc verruncent populo. Bene venire velim quod, Cic. Quæ res bene vertat mihi & vobis. Bene sit, Plaut. Ter. Macte virtute ac pietate in patrem patriamque esto, perge, & nomen invictum Diis juvantibus præsta, Liv.
units.tr: Deus fortunet] May the blessed gods be present. May the gods bless your patrimony. May these things turn out well for the people. I would gladly have it turn out well, Cic. May this turn out well for me and for you. Let it go well, Plaut. Ter. Be blessed in valour and piety towards your father and your country; go on, and with the gods' help, win an unconquered name, Liv.

units.la: Deo favente] Si Deus annuerit, Plin. Iun. Deo prosperante. Spondente Deo prospera. Deo vobisque fautoribus, Amm. Sperat quidem animus, quò eveniat, Diis in manu est, Plaut. Modo Jupiter adsit, Si qua viam dederit fortuna. Si qua fata sinant, Virg. Diis bene volentibus. Si Diis placet. Si Dii volunt, Plaut. Nos dicemus: Deo volente. Si Deus volet.
units.tr: Deo favente] If God consents, Plin. Iun. With God prospering. With God promising prosperity. With God and your favourers, Amm. The mind hopes, indeed, but how it turns out is in the hands of the gods, Plaut. If only Jupiter is present, if fortune gives a way. If the fates allow, Virg. With the gods well disposed. If it pleases the gods. If the gods will, Plaut. We shall say: God willing. If God wills.

units.la: Cum Deo] In Deo virtutem faciemus, Psal. 60. Cum Musis.
units.tr: With God: "In God we shall do valiantly," Ps. 60. With the Muses.

units.la: Deo adhæreamus semper] Animam potiùs deseramus, quam Deum.
units.tr: Let us always cling to God: Rather let us give up our life than God.

units.la: Deo id committamus] Viderit Deus.
units.tr: Let us commit that to God: God will see to it.

units.la: Deo non resistendum] Cum Diis non pugnandum. Fato non repugnandum.
units.tr: One must not resist God: One must not fight against the gods. One must not struggle against fate.

units.la: Cum Deo superamus omnia] Obex nullus officit Deo præeunte.
units.tr: With God we overcome all things: No obstacle stands in the way when God goes before.

units.la: Dei voluntas immutabilis] Fatum inevitabile. Fatum rotat omnia.
units.tr: God's will is unchangeable: Inevitable fate. Fate turns all things.

units.la: Dei dona semper bona] Coelitus sublimia dantur, Sigismundi III. Regis Polon. Symbolum.
units.tr: God's gifts are always good: Sublime gifts come down from heaven, Sigismund III, King of Poland. A motto.

units.la: Deum colere] Venerari, Advenerari Deum, Varr.
units.tr: To worship God: To venerate, to approach God in reverence, Varro.

units.la: Deum esse credere] Constringi sensu numinis. Piare pietatem, Plaut.
units.tr: To believe that God exists: To be bound by the sense of divinity. To keep up piety, Plautus.

units.la: Vt Deum segerere] Jovi paria intonat.
units.tr: How to conduct oneself towards God: He thunders things equal to Jove.

units.la: Dextera] Dextra. Dextella, Cic. Dextrabus manibus, Liv.
units.tr: Right hand: The right hand. Little right hand, Cic. With right hands, Liv.

units.la: A Dextrâ parte] Dextrâ illum assedit, Salust. Dexter assedit, Cic. Quo dexter abis? Virg. A dextrâ, Cic. Ad dextram, Ter. Sepulchrum in via Appiâ dextrùm euntibus, Spart.
units.tr: On the right-hand side: He sat down on his right, Sallust. The man on the right sat down, Cic. Where are you going, on the right? Virg. On the right, Cic. To the right, Ter. A tomb on the Appian Way for those going to the right, Spart.

units.la: Dextram versus] Dextrorsum, Cic. Dextrorsus, Liv. Ad dextram, Plut. Plin. Dextroversum, Plaut. Dextra levaque] A lateribus.
units.tr: Towards the right: Rightward, Cic. Rightward, Liv. To the right, Plut. Plin. Turning to the right, Plaut. On the right and on the left: from the sides.

units.la: Diabolicus] Dæmonicus, Lactant.
units.tr: Devilish: Demonic, Lactant.

units.la: Diabolus, Vid. Demon. Calumniator.
units.tr: The devil: See Demon. Calumniator.

units.la: Diadema] Insigne regium, Tac. Corona aurea, Cic.
units.tr: Diadem: A royal emblem, Tac. A golden crown, Cic.

units.la: Dialectica] Ratio disserendi. Ars disserendi. Judicandi via. Veri & falsi disceptatrix & judex. Contracta & constricta eloquentia. Logice, Cic. Disputatrix virtus, Quint. Culter veritatis anatomicus.
units.tr: Dialectic: The art of reasoning. The art of disputing. The way of judging. The arbiter and judge of true and false. Eloquence compressed and condensed. Logic, Cic. A virtue that disputes, Quint. The knife of truth that dissects.

units.la: Dialecticus clarissimus] Chrysippus.
units.tr: The most famous dialectician: Chrysippus.

units.la: Dialogus] Collocutio. Disputatio. Scholæ, pro disputationibus, Cic. Dialogismus, Rufin. Fabula. Lupus est in fabula, Ter. Diverbium, Liv. Alloquium, Hor. Sermocinatio, Quint. Affatus, Sen.
units.tr: Dialogue: Conversation. Debate. Schools, for disputations, Cic. Dialogue, Rufin. Story. There is a wolf in the story, Ter. Exchange of words, Liv. Address, Hor. Speech, Quint. Utterance, Sen.

units.la: Diarium] Diurnum, Tac. Ephemeris. Commentarius, Cic. Quotidiana, pl. Vopisc.
units.tr: Daily record: Daily news, Tac. Ephemeris. Journal, Cic. Daily things, plural, Vopisc.

units.la: Diarrhæa, Vid. Alvus cita.
units.tr: Diarrhoea: See Rapid bowel.

units.la: Dic] Cedo, Ter. Cedo dic mihi, Cic. Dic bonâ fide. Plaut. Age loquere. Eja dicito. Loquere porrò. Dic tandem. Dic age sis, Ter. Ain tu? Dicisne hoc, quod te rogo? Possumne ego hodie ex se exsculpere verum? Taces. Monstrum hominis, non dicturus? Dic mihi verò serio, Plaut.
units.tr: Say: Give it here, Ter. Give it here, tell me, Cic. Tell me in good faith, Plaut. Come, speak. Come on, say it. Speak further. Tell me at last. Come on, tell me, please, Ter. Do you say so? Do you say this, which I am asking you? Can I today draw the truth out of him? You are silent. Monster of a man, will you not speak? Tell me truly and seriously, Plaut.

units.la: Dica] Libellus forensis, Schard. ex Ict. Formula, Quint. Vadimonium, Plaut.
units.tr: Writ: A legal pamphlet, Schard. from the jurists. A formula, Quint. A bail bond, Plaut.

units.la: Dicacitas. Vid. Garrulitas. Cavillatio.
units.tr: Dicacity: See Garrulity. Quibbling.

units.la: Dicacula] Lingulaca, Plaut. Lingulata, Turneb. Sermocinatrix, Apul. Garrula, Ter. Oblatratrix. Argulatrix, Plaut. Citeria, Fest.
units.tr: Chatterbox: Tattler, Plaut. Tattler, Turneb. Talker, Apul. Garrulous, Ter. Barking at people, nagging. Nagging woman, Plaut. Gossip, Fest.

units.la: Dicax] Homo mordax. Maledicus convitiator. Criminosus orator, Cic. Maledicentissimus liber, Gell. Petulans verbum, Ovid. Diasyrticum dictum, Spart. Petulantissima verba, Sal. Famosus libellus, Suet. Acida lingua, Sen. Cùm aculeo & maledicto facetus, Cic.
units.tr: Sharp-tongued: A biting man. A slanderous, abusive reviler. An accusing orator, Cic. The most slanderous book, Gell. A wanton word, Ovid. A scornful saying, Spart. Most wanton words, Sal. A defamatory pamphlet, Suet. A sour tongue, Sen. Witty with sting and slander, Cic.

units.la: Dicere] Verbis exponere. Expedire, Lucr. Edere, exsequi verbis. Oratione persequi, referre, edisserere, Cic.
units.tr: To say: To set out in words. To explain, Lucr. To express and set forth in words. To pursue, relate, and expound in speech, Cic.

units.la: Dicere paucis] Paucis dare, Ter.
units.tr: To speak briefly: To give in few words, Ter.

units.la: Dicere planius] Rudius ac planius dicere. Crassâ, pinguiore Minervâ dicere.
units.tr: To speak more plainly: To speak more roughly and plainly. To speak with plain, heavier wisdom.

units.la: Dicis causâ] Dicis gratia auxilium ferre, Vlp. Ut careas reprehensione, Bud. Verbotenus. Ut possit dicere se emisse. Ad speciem & usurpationem veritatis, Cic. In speciem preces jactantur. Juris usurpandi causâ, Liv. Moris causâ ingemiscunt, Sen. Verbo poscebat, re verâ autem, &c. Cic. Specie recusantis, flagrantissime poscebat, Tac. Quasi joco dicere, Spart.
units.tr: For show: To give help for form's sake, Ulp. So that you may escape blame, Budé. In word only. So that he can say he bought it. For the sake of appearance and pretence of the truth, Cic. Prayers are put forward for show. For the sake of claiming a right, Liv. They groan from custom, Sen. He demanded it in words, but in fact, etc., Cic. Specie. Pretending to refuse, he demanded it most vehemently, Tac. As if speaking in jest, Spart.

units.la: Dicitur, Vid. Ajunt.
units.tr: They say: See Ajunt.

units.la: Dictare alicui] Præire alicui voce, Cic. scil. scribenti. Præire aliquem de scripto, Plin.
units.tr: To dictate to someone: To speak the words to someone, Cic. scil. scribenti. To dictate to someone from a written text, Plin.

units.la: Dicterium] Scomma, Macrob. Asteismus, Donat. Salsum dictum. Amari sales, Quint. Vellicatio, Sen. Styli nasus, Plin. Sugillatio, Id. Aculeus, Cic. Morsus figuratus, Macr. Opprobrium linguæ, Hor. Conviciolum, Lampr.
units.tr: Witticism: Scomma, Macrob. Asteismus, Donat. A witty saying. Bitter wit, Quint. Teasing, Sen. The nib of the stylus, Plin. Disparagement, Id. A sting, Cic. A figurative bite, Macr. A reproach of the tongue, Hor. A little insult, Lampr.

units.la: Dictitare] Crebris sermonibus aliquid usurpare. Crebrò aliquid usurpare. In ore tibi semper esse solet. In omnibus dictis aliquid usurpare. In ore semper habere aliquem authorem. Creberrimè commemorare aliquid, Cic.
units.tr: To keep repeating: To keep using something in frequent talk. To use something again and again. To be always on your lips. In every saying to keep using something. To keep an authority always in mouth. To mention something very often, Cic.

units.la: Dicturire, gestire dicere] Quidquid illos urit, in quaslibet aures exonerant, Sen.
units.tr: To be eager to speak: Whatever burns them, they pour out into any ears, Sen.

units.la: Diducere] Diffundere vitem in orbem. Dispensare. Digerere crines. Dispergere, diradiare vitem, Col. Divaricari taleas, Cat Explicare acies, Liv.
units.tr: To spread out: To spread the vine in a circle. To distribute. To arrange the hair. To scatter, spread out the vine, Col. To spread out the stakes, Cat. To unfold the battle lines, Liv.

units.la: Die aut Nocte] Luce rediisse, Cic. Nocte ac Die, Plin. Nocte dieque, Ovid. Noctesque & dies, Ter. Diu noctuque Sallust. Noctes atque dies, Lucr. Dies noctesque, Plaut. Ter. Cic. Diem noctemque, Cic. Sub ipsa die, Plin. Luce clara. De die portare, Plaut. Interdiu, Cat. Cæs. Ter.
units.tr: By day or by night: To have returned in daylight, Cic. Night and day, Plin. Night and day, Ovid. Nights and days, Ter. Day and night, Sallust. Nights and days, Lucr. Day and night, Plaut. Ter. Cic. Day and night, Cic. Right under the daylight, Plin. In clear light. To carry in daylight, Plaut. By day, Cat. Cæs. Ter.

units.la: Dies] Diurnum spatium. Spatium diei, Cic. Lumen. Tertia te tempestas in portu locabit, Id. Lux, Mart. Lampas solis, Lucr. Quotidianum principium, æternaque commutatio. Revolutio diei.
units.tr: Day: A span of daytime. A span of day, Cic. Light. The third weather will set you down in port, Cic. Light, Id. Light, Mart. The lamp of the sun, Lucr. The daily beginning and eternal change. The revolution of the day.

units.la: Dies periculosus à Medicis dictus] Dies decretorii, Plin. Criticus dies, Cels. Crisimus, Id.
units.tr: Dangerous days, so called by physicians: Decretory days, Plin. Critical day, Cels. Crisimus, Id.

units.la: Diffamare] Infamare aliquem, Sen. Lædere, atterere famam alicujus. Inurere, inferre, conflare alicui infamiam. Spergere aliquem infamiâ. Detrahere de famâ alicujus. Inurere alicui famam superbiæ, Cic. Infamem aliquem facere, Cic. Infamiâ lædere, Quint. Inquinare, lacerare famam alicujus. Per ora hominum aliquem traducere, dare sermonem per civitatem de aliquo, Liv. Sauciare famam alicujus. Pipulo differre, Plaut. Pipulo poscere, Scal. Stigma alicui imponere, Suet. Mittere in sermones & fabulas, Quint. Infligere vulnus infamiæ, Firm. Notare infamiâ. Sugillare famam alicujus, Ulp. Differre.
units.tr: To defame: To defame someone, Sen. To harm and wear down someone's reputation. To brand, inflict, and fix infamy on someone. To sprinkle someone with infamy. To take away from someone's good name. To brand someone with the mark of pride, Cic. To make someone infamous, Cic. To injure with infamy, Quint. To stain and tear someone's reputation. To carry someone through the mouths of people, to spread talk about someone through the city, Liv. To wound someone's reputation. To put off with a little rumour, Plaut. To demand by rumour, Scal. To brand someone, Suet. To send into talk and stories, Quint. To inflict a wound of infamy, Firm. To mark with infamy. To bruise someone's reputation, Ulp. To spread about.

units.la: Diffamatus] Infamatus, Ovid. Flagitatus, Cat. Notatus, abs. Notatissimus omnium scelerum, flagitiorum maculis. Opertus infamiâ, Cic. Vid. Infamis.
units.tr: Defamed: Defamed, Ovid. Demanded, Cat. Marked, abs. Most marked with the stains of every crime and disgrace. Covered with infamy, Cic. See Infamous.

units.la: Differens] Diversus ab illo. Diversi inter se. Longissimè inter se diversa sunt. Dissimilis alicui, sui. Dissimiles inter se. Dissimillimi suorum, Cic. Diversus quàm, Plin. Dissimiles inter se re aliquâ, Hor. Dispar ætas, fortuna, color. Dispares inter se. Dispar sui. Disparilis aspiratio terrarum. Dissociabilis, Cic. Dispares viribus, Liv. Discolor calculus, Mart. Dissonæ moribus gentes, Liv. Alterius notæ pisces, Col.
units.tr: Differing: Different from that one. Different from one another. Their natures are very far apart. Unlike someone, or oneself. Unlike one another. Most unlike their own kind, Cic. Different from what, Plin. Unlike one another in some respect, Hor. Unequal in age, fortune, colour. Unequal with one another. Unequal to oneself. The uneven breathing of lands. Incompatible, Cic. Unequal in strength, Liv. A stone of different colour, Mart. Nations discordant in customs, Liv. Fish of a different kind, Col.

units.la: Differentia] Dissimilitudo morum. Discrimen rerum. Distinctio & dissimilitudo causarum. Dissidium, varietas, Diversitas ingeniorum, Plin. Variatio sententiarum, Liv. Variantia, Lucr. Disparilitas diversarum rerum, Macrob. Distinctus pennarum à cæteris avibus, Tacit.
units.tr: Difference: Unlikeness of character. Distinction of things. Distinction and dissimilarity of causes. Disagreement, variety, diversity of minds, Plin. Variation of opinions, Liv. Variety, Lucr. Inequality of different things, Macrob. A feather distinct from other birds, Tacit.

units.la: Differentia est] Differt inter locum & locum. Interest inter locorum naturas.
units.tr: There is a difference: It differs from place to place. There is a difference between the natures of places.

units.la: Differre ab alio] Res cum re differt. Apparet in aliquibus distinctio. Distat aliquid ab alio. Distant aliqua inter se. Est inter eos distantia. Habet ab aliquo dissimilitudinem. Interest inter nos & illos, Cic. Distinguuntur inter se, Plin. Discordet parcus avaro, Hor.
units.tr: To differ from another: One thing differs from another. A distinction appears in some cases. One thing stands apart from another. Some things are different from one another. There is a distance between them. He has a dissimilarity from someone. There is a difference between us and them, Cic. They are distinguished from one another, Plin. The thrifty man disagrees with the miser, Hor.

units.la: Differre negotium] Differre tempus, horam. Rejicere aliquid in mensem. Retrudere, reservare in aliud tempus. Proferre diem, opus. Procrastinare. Prorogare diem, Prolatare. Sustento ædificationem in adventum tuum, Cic. Diem de die differre, ducere. Sustinere rem in noctem. Suspendere rem. Extrahere in annum, Liv. Recrastinare, Cic. Col. Promovere nuptias, Ter. Producere rem, Cæf. Protol‐lere, Plaut. Prolongare diem mortis, Sen. Negotium paxil‐lo suspendere.
units.tr: To postpone a matter: To postpone a time or an hour. To push something back to a month. To hold back, keep for another time. To put off a day or a work. To delay. To prolong a day. To defer. I am holding back the building until your arrival, Cic. To put off and lengthen a day from one day to the next. To hold a matter over until night. To suspend a matter. To drag it out to a year, Liv. To put off again, Cic. Col. To delay a marriage, Ter. To prolong a matter, Cæs. To hold back, Plaut. To prolong the day of death, Sen. To suspend the business with a little pause.

units.la: Differre judicium] Diffindere diem. Trajicere negotium ad novos magistratus, Liv. Comperendinare reum. Trans‐ferre causam in annum proximum. Dirimere tempus. Am‐pliare rem, hominem, causam. Dimisit illo die quæstio‐nem, Cic. Protelare causam, Vlp.
units.tr: To defer a trial: To postpone the day. To transfer the business to new magistrates, Liv. To keep the accused waiting for a further hearing. To transfer the case to the following year. To divide the time. To adjourn the matter, the man, the case. He dismissed the court on that day, Cic. To delay a case, Ulp.

units.la: Differamus] In crastinum seria. In nocte consilium.
units.tr: Let us defer: Put it off until tomorrow. Plan for the night.

units.la: Differre aliquod suo malo] Echinus partum differt.
units.tr: To postpone something to one's own harm: The hedgehog delays giving birth.

units.la: Difficilis] Difficilis & multum sæpe quæsita res. Magni laboris est. Infinitus, operosus, & molestus est labor. Ope‐rosa res, ars, opus. Provincia negotiosa. Perdifficilis. Per‐obscura quæstio. Spinosa oratio, Cic. Id in difficili est, Liv. Perdurum, Quint. Laboriosus, Quint. Parum ex fa‐cili fluens res, Sen. Inimitabile opus, Quint. Hoc opus, hic labor est, Virg. Malignus aditus, Id. Scrupulosa res, Fest. Ardua res, via, Cic. Res multi laboris & operæ, Cæf. Ardui operis est, Plin. Insuperabiles moles. Inest nodus. Gravius, quàm sit Trojam capere. Difficile naturam mutare. Difficile est tacere, cùm doleas. Difficile est simul sorbere & flare.
units.tr: Difficult: A thing difficult and often much sought after. It is of great toil. The labour is endless, laborious and troublesome. A laborious matter, art, or work. A troublesome business. Very difficult. A very obscure question. A thorny speech, Cic. That is hard to do, Liv. Hard to endure, Quint. A laborious matter, Quint. A matter that flows with little ease, Sen. A work that cannot be imitated, Quint. This is the work, this is the toil, Virg. A grudging approach, Id. A scrupulous matter, Fest. A steep matter, a steep road, Cic. A matter of much toil and effort, Cæs. It is a work of great difficulty, Plin. Insurmountable masses. There is a knot. Heavier than taking Troy. It is hard to change one's nature. It is hard to keep silent when you are in pain. It is hard to sip and blow at the same time.

units.la: Difficilia tentare] Extorquere clavam Herculi. Cursum fluvii detorquere. Contra torrentem niti. Isthmum per‐fodere. Admovere manus deploratis vulneribus. Contra stimulum calcitrare. Ire per extentum funem.
units.tr: Difficilia tentare] To attempt difficult things: to wrench the club from Hercules; to turn the course of a river; to struggle against a torrent; to dig through an isthmus; to apply hands to hopeless wounds; to kick against the goad; to walk along a stretched rope.

units.la: Difficultas] Negotium, Plin. Multum negotiorum fe‐runt negotia; Sen. Iniquitas temporum. Nodus, Cic. Mo‐les curarum, Tac. Nodus Herculeus, Sen. Incitæ, Tricæ, Plaut.
units.tr: Difficultas] Business, Plin. Business brings much business, Sen. Unfavourable state of the times. A knot, Cic. A burden of cares, Tac. A Herculean knot, Sen. Tangles and vexations, Plaut.

units.la: Difficultatem tollere] Nodum solvere.
units.tr: Difficultatem tollere] To untie the knot.

units.la: Difficulter] Difficile. Difficiliter, perdifficiliter, vel per‐difficulter. Difficillimè fit aliquid. Inveterata vitia ægrius depelluntur. Laboriosè. Laboriosius, Cic. Non sine ne‐gotio, Plin. Facilius clavam Herculi extorqueas. Facilius ex illo excuteres ignem, Adag.
units.tr: Difficulter] With difficulty. Difficultly, very difficultly, or with great difficulty. Something is done most difficultly. Long-rooted vices are driven out with more pain. With labour. More laboriously, Cic. Not without trouble, Plin. You would more easily wrest the club from Hercules. You would more easily strike fire from him, Adag.

units.la: Diffidere] Diffidere alicui & de aliquo. Subdiffidere, Cic. Levi momento fides (alicujus) pendet, Liv. Ne fidci qui‐dem dem credere. Ne Catoni quidem crederem, Adag. Vid. Desperare.
units.tr: Diffidere] To distrust someone and in someone. To distrust slightly, Cic. A person's trust hangs on a slight moment, Liv. Not even to believe in good faith. I would not even believe Cato, Adag. See Desperare.

units.la: Diffidentia] Incredulitas. Credendi difficultas, Sipont. Incredibilitas, Martian. IC.
units.tr: Diffidentia] Unbelief. Difficulty of believing, Sipont. Incredibility, Martian.

units.la: Difflare] Differt favillam ventus, dissipat, Lucr.
units.tr: Difflare] The wind scatters the spark and disperses it, Lucr.

units.la: Diffluere] Diffluit extra ripas, dilabitur, funditur fluvius. Diffunditur glacies liquefacta & dilapsa, Cic. Evagatur Nilus, Plin.
units.tr: Diffluere] The river overflows its banks, runs away, and spreads out. The melted and slipping ice spreads out, Cic. The Nile spreads over the land, Plin.

units.la: Diffluens] Diffluus, Macr. Incontinens sui aqua, Sen.
units.tr: Diffluens] Overflowing, Macr. Not containing its water, Sen.

units.la: Diffugere] Dilabuntur in agros, in oppida milites. Discurrit juventus, Liv. Dispalantur. Dispalata multitudo, Sallust.
units.tr: Diffugere] Soldiers scatter into the fields and towns. The youth run off in all directions, Liv. They scatter. A scattered crowd, Sallust.

units.la: Digerere aliquid] Disponere semina, plantas, Sen. Dissecrit olitor in aream aliquid, Varr. Serere, Plin.
units.tr: Digerere aliquid] To arrange seeds and plants, Sen. The gardener scatters something over the bed, Varr. To sow, Plin.

units.la: Digitalis, id est, digiti crassitudine] Digitalis crassitudo, gracilitas, Plin. Unciarius, Col. Uncialis altitudo. Pollicarius, (i. pollicem crassius, vel latius) Plin. In pollicem tondeatur vitis, Col.
units.tr: Digitalis, id est, digiti crassitudine] Thickness of a finger; slenderness, Plin. An inch thick, Col. A height of an inch. Pollicarius (that is, thicker or wider than a thumb), Plin. The vine should be pruned to the thickness of a thumb, Col.

units.la: Digitis stare] In summis ambulans digitis, Sen. In plantas exsurgere, Id. Primoribus digitis stare, ut in littore cancri, Varr.
units.tr: Digitis stare] Walking on the tips of the toes, Sen. Rising up onto the plants, Id. Standing on the tips of the toes, as crabs do on the shore, Varr.

units.la: Digitus index] Digitus salutaris, Suet. Digitus silentii (quia ori appresso, Harpocrates silentium indicabat), Juven. Demonstratorius, Isid.
units.tr: Digitus index] The saving finger, Suet. The finger of silence (because Harpocrates indicated silence by holding it to the mouth), Juv. Demonstrative, Isid.

units.la: Digitus medius] Infamis digitus, (quia tantum probrosa res correctione hujus digiti indicabantur), Perf. Sipont. Impudicus, Mart. Verpus, Iun. Gerr. Famosus (quia, quando porrigebatur, signum derisionis erat,) Iunio.
units.tr: Digitus medius] The infamous finger (because disgraceful matters were indicated by raising this finger), Perf. Sipont. Shameless, Mart. Verpus, Iun. Gerr. Notorious (because when it was held out it was a sign of derision), Junius.

units.la: Digitus annularis] Medicinalis, Mart. Medicus digitus, (quia ob munditiem pharmaca eo miscentur commode) Gerrae.
units.tr: Digitus annularis] The medicinal finger, Mart. The physician's finger (because medicines are conveniently mixed with it, for cleanliness), Gerrae.

units.la: Digitus auricularis] Digitus minimus, Plin.
units.tr: Digitus auricularis] The smallest finger, Plin.

units.la: Digladiari] Rotare ensem, Virg. Licitari machæra contra aliquem, Non. Pugillatu decertare. Cestu pugnare, Plaut.
units.tr: Digladiari] To brandish the sword, Virg. To fight with a blade against someone, Non. To contend with the fists. To fight with the cestus, Plaut.

units.la: Dignitas] Est honesta, & cultu & honore, & verecundia digna authoritas. Amplitudo, Cic. Dignatio, Tac. Axioma familiae.
units.tr: Dignitas] Authority that is honourable in both bearing and honour, and worthy of reverence. Eminence, Cic. Dignatio, Tac. The family's motto.

units.la: Dignari aliquem aliquâ re] Te unum ex omnibus voluit Venus magnificare, Plaut. Mactare aliquem honore, Cic.
units.tr: Dignari aliquem aliqua re] Venus wished to exalt you alone above all others, Plaut. To honour someone with an honour, Cic.

units.la: Dignoscere] Internoscere. Dignum & indignum secernere. Iudicare oculorum sensu aliquid. Iudicare quid interfit. Discernere alba & atra. Distinguere civem & hostem, Cic.
units.tr: Dignoscere] To distinguish between. To separate the worthy from the unworthy. To judge something by the sense of sight. To judge what differs. To tell white from black. To distinguish citizen from enemy, Cic.

units.la: Dignus] Dignissimum donum. Idoneus auctor. Idonei atque integri homines. Ad omnia summa natus. Honoribus amplissimis perfunctus. Summa est in eo dignitas. Summae est dignitatis. Magnâ dignitate praeditus, Cic. Condignum donum. In eam rem si quid habebo, Plaut. Luculentus Auctor.
units.tr: Dignus] A most worthy gift. A suitable author. Suitable and upright men. Born for all the highest things. Having discharged the highest offices. In him there is the highest dignity. It is of the highest dignity. Endowed with great dignity, Cic. A fitting gift. If I shall have anything for that purpose, Plaut. A distinguished author.

units.la: Dignus honore] Dignus obelisco. Statuâ dignus. Meritus es cui laurea imponatur. Promeritus es ut tibi decernatur triumphus, Er.
units.tr: Dignus honore] Worthy of an obelisk. Worthy of a statue. You deserve to have the laurel placed upon you. You have earned that a triumph be decreed for you, Erasmus.

units.la: Dignus longâ vitâ] Dignus qui quàm diutissimè vivat. Dignus ut quàm diutissimè vivat. Longissimâ vitâ dignus. Dignus quàm diutissimè vivere, Er.
units.tr: Dignus longa vita] Worthy to live as long as possible. Worthy that he should live as long as possible. Worthy of the longest life. Worthy to live as long as can be, Er.

units.la: Digna dignis] Invenit gladius se dignam vaginam. Dignum patellâ operculum. Similes habent labra lactucas. Mala malis conveniunt. Stramenta asino, non aurum, Adag.
units.tr: Digna dignis] The sword has found a sheath worthy of it. A lid worthy of the dish. Lips have lettuces like themselves. Apples suit apples. Straw for the donkey, not gold, Adag.

units.la: Dignis indigni quandoque praeferuntur] Corvi luscinis honoratiores.
units.tr: Dignis indigni quandoque praeferuntur] Sometimes the unworthy are preferred to the worthy. Crows are more honoured than nightingales.

units.la: Digredi à proposito, vid. Evagari.
units.tr: Digredi à proposito, see Evagari.

units.la: Dijudicare] Disceptare controversias aliorum. Distrahere controversias. Decidere de negotio, dirimere controversiam, Cic. Cernere, Pacuv. Disceptare inter aliquos, Liv. Secare litem. Secare res, Hor.
units.tr: Dijudicare] To settle the disputes of others. To resolve controversies. To decide a matter, to settle a dispute, Cic. To discern, Pacuv. To arbitrate between persons, Liv. To cut through a lawsuit. To cut matters apart, Hor.

units.la: Dilacerare] Discerpere. Diripere, Lucan. Dilaniare, Cic. Diversum actis cruribus distrahere, Sen. Dilancinare, Ammian. Differre in diversa quadrigis, Virg.
units.tr: Dilacerare] To tear apart. To pull to pieces, Lucan. To tear to shreds, Cic. To pull apart with the legs spread, Sen. To mangle, Ammian. To drag in different directions by chariots, Virg.

units.la: Dilapidare, vid. Dissipare.
units.tr: Dilapidare, see Dissipare.

units.la: Dilatare, in amplius spatium diducere] Propagare fines, laudem, religionem. Amplificare gloriam, dignitatem, Rempubl. Collatare, Cic. Prolatare agros. Proferre imperium, Tacit. Ampliare plagam scalpello, Celf.
units.tr: Dilatare, in amplius spatium diducere] To spread the borders, praise or religion. To magnify glory and dignity, Rempubl. To enlarge, Cic. To extend fields. To extend an empire, Tac. To widen a wound with the scalpel, Celsus.

units.la: Dilatare, sermonem prolongare] Amplificare aliquid dicendo. Amplificare rem orando, dolorem, orationem, verbis aliquid. Exaggerare verbis aliquid, oratione rem. Fundit se latius orator, Cic. Augere peccati atrocitatem; aliquid verbis; rem laudando. In majus vulgare, Tacit. Rem parvam attollere, Celf. In majus aliquid provehere, Hor. Ultra verum aliquid ferre, Sen. Vid. Amplificare orationem.
units.tr: Dilatare, sermonem prolongare] To amplify something by speaking. To magnify a matter in pleading, pain or speech; to amplify something in words. To exaggerate something in words, a matter in speech. The orator spreads himself more widely, Cic. To increase the enormity of a sin; to amplify something in words, a matter by praising. To spread a report more widely, Tac. To raise a small matter, Celsus. To carry something further, Hor. To carry something beyond the truth, Sen. See Amplificare orationem.

units.la: Dilatatio] Propagatio. Amplificatio. Exaggeratio, Cic. Paraphrasis, Quint.
units.tr: Dilatatio] Propagation. Amplification. Exaggeration, Cic. Paraphrase, Quint.

units.la: Dilatio alicujus rei] Procrastinatio in rebus agendis. Cunctatio. Sustentatio. Mora supplicii, Cic. Prolatatio victoriae inimica, Tac. Frustratio, Liv.
units.tr: Dilatio alicujus rei] Procrastination in carrying things out. Hesitation. Holding back. Delay of punishment, Cic. A victory's postponement is hurtful, Tac. Frustration, Liv.

units.la: Dilatio juris] Comperendinatio. Comperendinatus. Advocatio, Prorogatio, Mora. Prolatio judicii, Cic. Amplificatio, Ascon. Sufflamen litis, Juv. Exceptio dilatoria, Vlp. Diffissio, Gell.
units.tr: Dilatio juris] Adjournment to the third day. Adjourned. Pleading, postponement, delay. Postponement of a judgment, Cic. Amplification, Asconius. A drag upon the lawsuit, Juv. A dilatory plea, Ulp. Delay, Gell.

units.la: Dilatio parit ignaviam] Qui non est hodie, cras minus aptus erit.
units.tr: Dilatio parit ignaviam] He who is not ready today will be less ready tomorrow.

units.la: Dilaudare aliquem, i. valde laudare] Celebrare aliquem laudibus. Celebrare laudes alicujus. Tollere, ferre aliquem in coelum. Tollere aliquem laudibus. Tollere famâ in coelum. Tollere laudes alicujus in astra. Extollere aliquem in coelum laudibus. Ferre in astra, ad coelum aliquem, Cic. Tonare laudes alicujus, Plin. In coelo est Bibulus, (id est, laudatur) Cic. Laudare maximis laudibus, Cato. Elaudare, Varr. Tollere in altum gloriam Viri, Ariftoph.
units.tr: Dilaudare aliquem, i. valde laudare] To celebrate someone with praises. To celebrate someone's praises. To lift someone up to heaven. To raise someone with praises. To raise someone's fame to heaven. To raise someone's praises to the stars. To extol someone to heaven with praise. To carry someone to the stars, to heaven, Cic. Bibulus is in heaven (that is, he is praised), Cic. To praise with the greatest praises, Cato. To praise greatly, Varr. To raise the glory of a man to the heights, Aristoph.

units.la: Dilectus] Deliciae, deliciolae nostrae Tullia. In amore & deliciis alicui est, Cic. In intimis meis est, de alicujus delectu, complexu, sinu est. Anima. Alter ille est, vel Alter idem, Id. Hi sunt deliciae & amores tui, Virg. Primus apud aliquem est, Ter. Homines à latere, Curt. Liv. Continuus Principis, Tacit. Mea voluptas. Mea delicia, Plaut. Deliciolum meum es, Sen. Delicies mea Critias, Apul. Col. Dimidium animae alicujus est, Hor. Pars animae alicujus, Id. Meus. Mea lux. Meum desiderium. Vos meae charissimae animae, Cic.
units.tr: Dilectus] Our delights, our little delight Tullia. He is in someone's love and delights, Cic. He is in my innermost heart, in the embrace and bosom of someone's favour. Soul. He is another self, or another same, Id. These are your delights and loves, Virg. He is first with someone, Ter. Men at one's side, Curt. Liv. Constant companion of the Prince, Tac. My pleasure. My delight, Plaut. You are my little delight, Sen. My delight, Critias, Apul. Col. He is half of someone's soul, Hor. Part of someone's soul, Id. Mine. My light. My longing. You, my dearest souls, Cic.

units.la: Dilectio, vid. Amor.
units.tr: Dilectio, see Amor.

units.la: Dilemma] Cornutus syllogismus. Complexio, in qua utrum concesseris, reprehenditur, Cic. Argumentum ab utraque parte concludens.
units.tr: Dilemma] A horned syllogism. A complex argument in which whichever alternative you concede is refuted, Cic. An argument that concludes from either side.

units.la: Diligens] Studiosus. Assiduus. Curiosus famae suae. Sedulus, Cic. Intentus ad, Tacit. Multus in opere, Sal. Propenso animo in hoc incumbens, Er.
units.tr: Diligens] Zealous. Assiduous. Careful of his reputation. Painstaking, Cic. Intent upon, Tac. Busy at work, Sall. Bending to this with a ready mind, Er.

units.la: Diligens nimium] Perdiligens. Perattentus, Cic. Nimius in aliqua re, Id. Anxiè diligens, Macrob. Cleanthes. Librorum heluo, Cic.
units.tr: Diligens nimium] Overly diligent. Very attentive, Cic. Excessive in some matter, Id. Anxiously diligent, Macrob. Cleanthes. A glutton for books, Cic.

units.la: Diligens semper habet quod agat] Homini diligenti semper aliquid superest.
units.tr: Diligens semper habet quod agat] For the diligent man there is always something left to do.

units.la: Diligentem esse in aliqua re] Adhibere curam, contentionem, studium. Incumbere alicui rei, Cic.
units.tr: Diligentem esse in aliqua re] To apply care, effort and zeal. To devote oneself to a matter, Cic.

units.la: Diligenter] Perdiligenter. Vigilanter. Perquisitius. Perattentè. Etiam atque etiam considera, Cic. Solicitissimè, Sen. Observanter, Macr. Observatè, Gell. Excusse, Sen. Enixâ operâ, diligentiâ. Examinatius, Amm. Sedulè, Gell. Sedulò, Cic. Inquisitius, Gell. Curiosiùs, Col. Rebus relictis, Plaut. Ter. Lucr. Acceptâ candelâ. Levato velo de causa cognoscere. Oculis fixis, immobilibus intueri. Omnibus vestigiis inquirere. Passim & effusè. Passis velis. Nihil obiter.
units.tr: Diligenter] Very diligently. Vigilantly. More carefully. Very attentively. Consider again and again, Cic. Most anxiously, Sen. Observantly, Macr. Observantly, Gell. Thoroughly, Sen. With strenuous effort and care. More closely, Amm. Assiduously, Gell. Assiduously, Cic. More inquisitively, Gell. More carefully, Col. With other things set aside, Plaut. Ter. Lucr. With a candle lit. Lifting the veil to examine the case. Looking with fixed, unmoving eyes. To search every track. Everywhere and freely. With sails spread. Nothing by the way.

units.la: Diligentia] Navitas. Sedulitas. Assiduitas. Mira observatio operis. Accuratio, Cic. Intentio discentis, Quint. Intentissima cura, Id. Fervet opus.
units.tr: Diligentia] Eagerness. Diligence. Assiduity. Wonderful attention to one's work. Accuracy, Cic. The attention of the learner, Quint. Most intent care, Id. The work glows.

units.la: Diligentia inversa frigescens] Principium fervet, medium tepet, ultima frigent.
units.tr: Diligentia inversa frigescens] The beginning glows, the middle is lukewarm, and the end grows cold.

units.la: Diligentia errantium] Bene currunt, sed extra viam.
units.tr: Diligentia errantium] They run well, but off the road.

units.la: Diligere, vid. Amare.
units.tr: Diligere, see Amare.

units.la: Diluci dare] Accendere facem, vid. Declarare.
units.tr: Diluci dare] To give light: to kindle a torch, see Declarare.

units.la: Diluculo] Primulo diluculo, Plaut. Cum prima luce, Ter. Cic. Primo diluculo, Cic. Suet. Manè obscuro, Col. Primâ luce, Ter. Liv. Coeptâ luce, Tacit. Primo manè, Col. Principio lucis, Tacit. Benè manè scripsi. Multo mane, Cic. Maturrimè, Cæs. Maturissimè, Cic. Vid. Antelucano tempore.
units.tr: Diluculo] At first dawn, Plaut. At first light, Ter. Cic. At early dawn, Cic. Suet. In the dim morning, Col. At first light, Ter. Liv. At the first light of day, Tac. In the first morning, Col. At the beginning of the light, Tac. I wrote early in the morning. In the morning, Cic. Very early, Caes. Very earliest, Cic. See Antelucano tempore.

units.la: Diluere] Diluvium facere. Ad diluvium revocantur glebæ imbriimbribus, Lucr. Miscere vinum aquâ, Plaut. Temperare merum lymphâ, Tibul. Infucare vinum, Plaut. Turneb. Infusçare, Lamb.
units.tr: Diluere] To make a flood. Clods are brought back to a flood by the rains, Lucr. To mix wine with water, Plaut. To temper neat wine with water, Tibul. To adulterate wine, Plaut. Turneb. To pour in, Lamb.

units.la: Dilutum vinum] Vinum lymphatum, Iuv. Diluta potio, Celf. Infucatum vinum, Plaut. Aquâ mixtum, Plin.
units.tr: Diluted wine: wine mixed with water, Juv. A diluted drink, Cels. Wine adulterated, Plaut. Wine mixed with water, Plin.

units.la: Diluvium] Cataclysmus, Varr. Vid. Eluvio.
units.tr: Flood: a cataclysm, Varr. See Eluvio.

units.la: Dimensio] Metatio vinearum, Col. Limitatio, Vitruv. Centuriatio. Cancellatio. Typus, Sicul. Flacc. Normatio agri per angulos, Aggen. Vrbic. Pedatura, (pedibus facta dimensio) Veget, Podismus, Id. Mensio, Cic.
units.tr: Measurement: the measuring out of vineyards, Col. Surveying, Vitruv. Division into centuries. Division into squares. Type, Sicul. Flacc. Laying out a field by its angles, Aggen. Urbic. Pacing out (measurement made by feet), Veget. Podismus, Id. Measuring, Cic.

units.la: Dimetiri] Dimetari. Limitare vineas, Plaut. Collibrare, Cat. Determinare regiones, Plaut. Liv. Metari agros, Virg. Dimensa verba, Cic.
units.tr: To measure out: to measure out again. To mark out vineyards, Plaut. To measure with a level, Cat. To fix the boundaries of regions, Plaut. Liv. To measure fields, Virg. Measured words, Cic.

units.la: Dimicare, vid. Digladiari, Præliari.
units.tr: To fight: see Digladiari, Praeliari.

units.la: Dimicatio, vid. Prælium.
units.tr: Fighting: see Prælium.

units.la: Dimidium] Dimidia pars, Cic. Dimidia circuli forma, Plin. Media pars, Casaub. Semis, Col. Semissis, Lampr. Cic.
units.tr: Half: a half part, Cic. A half-circle shape, Plin. The middle part, Casaub. A half, Col. A half, Lampr. Cic.

units.la: Dimidiatus] In partem dimidiatam decoquere, Col. Ex parte dimidiâ hæres, Cic. Decoquere ad dimidias, ad tertias, ad quartas, Col.
units.tr: Halved: to boil down to a half part, Col. To be heir to a half share, Cic. To boil down to halves, thirds, quarters, Col.

units.la: Diminuere, vid. Minuere.
units.tr: To diminish: see Minuere.

units.la: Dimissione non factâ abire] Vasis non conclamatis abire, Cic.
units.tr: To depart without dismissal: to depart without the vessels being called out, Cic.

units.la: Dimittere] Solvere coetum, Ovid. Missos facere. Ablegare, Cic. Domuitionem dare alicui, Pacuv. Missionem dare militibus, Tac. Amittere aliquem à se, Ter.
units.tr: To dismiss: to break up an assembly, Ovid. To release, to send away, Cic. To give someone leave, Pacuv. To grant soldiers their discharge, Tac. To send someone away from oneself, Ter.

units.la: Directè] Recta. Rectè feruntur atomi. Directo deorsum ferri. Ad lineam ferri. Rectis lineis subvolare. Protinus, Cic. In rectum jacit, Sen. Normaliter è regione stare, Amm. Proversus, vel Provorsus, Varr.
units.tr: Directly: straight. Atoms are carried straight. To be carried straight down. To be carried along a line. To fly along straight lines. Straight on, Cic. He throws straight ahead, Sen. To stand upright opposite the region, Amm. Forward, or Provorsus, Varr.

units.la: Dirigere] Circumflectere cursum navis, Torquere proras ad littora, Virg. Contorquere aliquo gubernaculum, Lucr. Flectere currum. Convertere navem ad. Clavum tenere. Gubernacula tractare. Detorquere voluntatem alicujus. Obvertere proram, Cic. Obflectere navem, Plaut. Obtorquere proram. Obliquare equos, Stat. Strigare mulas dextrâ. id. in Catul. Virg.
units.tr: To direct: to turn the course of a ship, to turn the prows to the shore, Virg. To turn the helm towards something, Lucr. To bend a chariot. To turn a ship towards. To hold the tiller. To handle the rudder. To turn someone's will aside. To turn the prow against, Cic. To bend a ship, Plaut. To twist the prow. To guide horses sideways, Stat. To guide mules with the right hand, id. in Catul. Virg.

units.la: Dirimere rixas] Sedare lites. Componere, Liv. vid. Componere litig.
units.tr: To settle quarrels: to calm disputes. To settle, Liv. See Componere litig.

units.la: Diripere aliquid] Membra direpta, Ovid. Disturbare vitæ societatem. Discindere amicitias. Dirumpere societatem, Cic.
units.tr: To tear something apart: torn limbs, Ovid. To break up the fellowship of life. To sever friendships. To break a partnership, Cic.

units.la: Diruere aliquid] Disturbare tecta. Edere ruinas, Cic. Dare ruinas, Virg. Vid. Destruere aliquid.
units.tr: To destroy something: to disturb roofs. To bring down ruins, Cic. To lay in ruins, Virg. See Destruere aliquid.

units.la: Dirus, vid. Crudelis, Atrox.
units.tr: Dire: see Crudelis, Atrox.

units.la: Discedere, vid. Abire.
units.tr: To depart: see Abire.

units.la: Disceptare cum aliquo] Dimicare cum aliquo de fortunis. Decertare cum aliquo de aliqua re; manu, vi, armis. Decernere pro suo sodali. Controversia est mihi cum aliquo de aliquâ re. Controversias habere inter se de. Litem habere cum aliquo. Litigare cum aliquo. Contendere cum aliquo de aliquâ re. Contendere jure. Vitam ferro, non auro cernamus. Habere cum aliquo contentionem de. Confligere ratione cum alicujus ratione. Causæ inter se confligunt. Conflictari judicio, Cic. Certare multum, Liv.
units.tr: To dispute with someone: to contend with someone over fortunes. To fight with someone over a matter, by hand, by force, by arms. To decide for one's companion. I have a dispute with someone about a matter. To have disputes among themselves about. To have a lawsuit with someone. To litigate with someone. To contend with someone about a matter. To contend by law. Let us decide life by iron, not by gold. To have a contest with someone about. To clash in argument with someone's reasoning. Causes clash with one another. To be contested in judgment, Cic. To contend hard, Liv.

units.la: Disceptator, vid. Arbiter.
units.tr: Arbitrator: see Arbiter.

units.la: Discere] Dare studium alicui rei. Eruditi in scholis, Quint. Dare operam Præceptori, Suet. Studere literas, literis, artibus. Imbuere se studiis literarum. Subdoceri alicujus labore. Accipere ab aliquo disciplinam. Adhærescere ad aliquam disciplinam, Cic. Perdiscere literas, Plin. Adjungere animum ad aliquod studium, Ter. Uti aliquo magistro, Cic. Vid. Studere.
units.tr: To learn: to give attention to a subject. Trained in the schools, Quint. To take pains with a teacher, Suet. To study letters, literature, the arts. To steep oneself in the study of letters. To be taught by another's labour. To receive instruction from someone. To adhere to a discipline, Cic. To learn letters thoroughly, Plin. To apply one's mind to a study, Ter. To have a particular teacher, Cic. See Studere.

units.la: Discere à doctiori] A bove majori discit arare minor.
units.tr: To learn from one more learned: the smaller ox learns to plough from the larger.

units.la: Discendum semper] Ætas nulla ad discendum sera. Nulla est sera ad bonos mores via.
units.tr: Learning is always to be done: no age is too late for learning. No road is too late to good morals.

units.la: Discenda utilia solum] Dementia est discere supervacanea in tanta temporis inopia.
units.tr: Only useful things are to be learned: it is madness to learn superfluous things when time is so scarce.

units.la: Disce, qui nescis] Auscultare disce, qui nescis loqui.
units.tr: Learn, you who do not know: learn to listen, you who do not know how to speak.

units.la: Discerpere, vid. Dilacerare.
units.tr: To tear apart: see Dilacerare.

units.la: Discessus, vid. Abitio.
units.tr: Departure: see Abitio.

units.la: Discinctus] Recinctus, Virg. Tunicis demissis ambulat, Hor. Tu, qui zonam non habes, Plaut. Solutis tunicis semper in urbe incessit, Sen. Effluit effuso cui toga lapsa sinu, Tibull. Discingere aliquem] Ego non discingor, Cic. Recingor. Plin. Ire solutis zonis, Ovid. Solvere zonam ligatam, Catull.
units.tr: Ungirded: girt, Virg. He walks with his tunic let down, Hor. You who have no belt, Plaut. He always walks about the city with his tunic loosened, Sen. The toga slipping from its loosened fold, Tibull. To ungird someone: I am not ungirded, Cic. I am ungirded again, Plin. To go with belts loosened, Ovid. To loosen a tied belt, Catull.

units.la: Disciplina] Animadversio in sceleratos. Castigatio. Pœna. Supplicium. Fraudi esse, Cic. Punitio, Gell. Noxa, Liv. Multatio bonorum, Cic. Vexat censura columbas, Iuv. Censio bubula. Malum. Iniqua hæc patior cum pretio tuo, Plaut. Luela sceleris, Lucr. Vindicta legis, Ovid.
units.tr: Discipline: punishment of wrongdoers. Chastisement. Penalty. Execution. To be a cause of loss, Cic. Punishment, Gell. Harm, Liv. Confiscation of goods, Cic.
