The censor harries the doves, Juv. A bovine tax. Evil. I suffer these unjust things at your expense, Plaut. The penalty for crime, Lucr. The vengeance of the law, Ovid.

units.la: Disciplina est salubris] Castigans unum, emendat centum.
units.tr: Discipline is wholesome: by chastising one, it amends a hundred.

units.la: Disciplinam deserere] Pullus de nido avolat. Ferulæ manum subducere, Id.
units.tr: To abandon discipline: the chick flies from the nest. To withdraw one's hand from the rod, Id.

units.la: Disciplina exolescit, vid. Mollescere.
units.tr: Discipline grows obsolete: see Mollescere.

units.la: Disciplina labens] Lapsi ad mollitiem mores. Mollis disciplina, Cic. Nusquam est disciplina ignavior, Plaut. Dissolutio, Spart. Vid. Licentia.
units.tr: Discipline lapsing: morals fallen into softness. Soft discipline, Cic. Nowhere is discipline more slack, Plaut. Dissolution, Spart. See Licentia.

units.la: Discipulus inchoat à vitio] Nihil sine peccato discitur. Errando non errare discimus.
units.tr: A pupil begins with a fault: nothing is learned without sin. By erring we learn not to err.

units.la: Discordare] Disconvenit inter me & te, Hor. Discrepare, dissidere ab aliquo, Cic. Dissonare, Col. Facilius inter horologia convenit. Tanta mihi tecum concordia, quanta agnis cum lupo, Hor.
units.tr: To disagree: it does not suit between me and you, Hor. To differ, to dissent from someone, Cic. To sound discordant, Col. Clocks agree more easily. Our agreement is as great as that between lambs and wolves, Hor.

units.la: Discordia] Dissensio. Dissidium. Discrepantia, Cic. Dissidentia. Dissensus, Plin.
units.tr: Discord: dissent. Disagreement. Discrepancy, Cic. Dissidence. Dissent, Plin.

units.la: Discordia sibi suisque nocet] Navem, quâ vehuntur, perforant.
units.tr: Discord harms itself and its own: they bore holes in the ship in which they are carried.

units.la: Discors] Malè concors, Lucan. Dissonus, Liv. Dissentaneus, Cic. Insociabilis. Tac.
units.tr: Discordant: ill-matched, Lucan. Dissonant, Liv. Dissentient, Cic. Unsociable, Tac.

units.la: Discrimen] Variatio, Liv. Variantia, Arnob. Vid. Differentia.
units.tr: Distinction: variation, Liv. Variance, Arnob. See Differentia.

units.la: Discrimen rerum vilium & pretiosarum nosse] Novit quid distent æra lupinis, Hor.
units.tr: To know the difference between cheap and precious things: he knows how far bronze coins differ from lupins, Hor.

units.la: Discrimina sunt rerum] Alia res sceptrum, alia plectrum.
units.tr: There are differences between things: one thing is a sceptre, another a plectrum.

units.la: Discrepare, vid. Discordare.
units.tr: To differ: see Discordare.

units.la: Discurrere] Cursare huc atque illuc, ultro ac citro. Volitare per forum. Pervagari, Cic. Vagari tota urbe, Virg. Discursare, Quint. Percursare, Liv. Intercursare. Ultro citroque pervolare, Plin. Cursitare sursum deorsum. Cursatur sursum prossum, Ter. Volitare totâ acie, Tac.
units.tr: To run about: to rush hither and thither, back and forth. To flit about the forum. To wander, Cic. To roam the whole city, Virg. To run to and fro, Quint. To run through, Liv. To run between. To fly back and forth, Plin. To scurry up and down. He scampers up and down, Ter. To flit about the whole line of battle, Tac.

units.la: Discutere] Diverberare aliquid ictu, Lucr. Elidere caput, Excutere cerebrum alicui. Dispertiri cerebrum alicui, Plaut. Aperire caput fuste, Juv. Dispercutere, Lambin. Displodere capita ossibus perfractis, Amm. Displanare caput rastro, Varr.
units.tr: To shake, to knock about: to strike something with a blow, Lucr. To dash out someone's brains. To knock out someone's brains, Plaut. To split open a head with a club, Juv. To strike apart, Lambin. To smash heads with broken bones, Amm. To flatten a head with a rake, Varr.

units.la: Disertus] Copiosus ad dicendum. Cujus quasi torrens fertur oratio. Omnibus naturae & doctrinae praesidiis ad dicendum paratus. A natura solutus ad dicendum. Celeriter verba volvens. Volubilis orator. Non est illi oratio. Vir omnium eloquentissimus. Pereloquens, Cic. Disertissimus, Mart. Facundus. Perfacundus, Justin. Orandi validus, Tacit.
units.tr: Eloquent: copious in speech, whose oratory flows like a torrent. Equipped for speaking with all the resources of nature and learning. Free by nature in speaking. Rolling out words quickly. A fluent orator. He has no lack of words. The most eloquent man of all. Very eloquent, Cic. Most eloquent, Mart. Fluent. Very fluent, Justin. Strong in oratory, Tac.

units.la: Disjicere] Disjectat mare carinas. Dispergere corpus passim per agros. Disturbare domum, Cic. Dissipare cumulos, Pallad. Dispulverare montes, Nav.
units.tr: To throw apart: the sea scatters the keels. To scatter a body here and there over the fields. To throw a house into disorder, Cic. To scatter heaps, Pallad. To grind mountains to dust, Nav.

units.la: Disjunctio, vid. Separatio.
units.tr: Separation: see Separatio.

units.la: Disjungere aliquid ab aliquo] Distrahere. Divellere. Distinguere. Disjugare. Sejugare, Cic. Dejungere. Abjungere, Plaut. Disjungere, Var. Disparare, Gell. Vid. Separare.
units.tr: To separate one thing from another: to pull apart. To tear away. To distinguish. To unyoke. To unyoke, Cic. To disjoin, Plaut. To disjoin, Var. To part, Gell. See Separare.

units.la: Dispar, in aliquo alicui] Inaequalis varietas. Inaequatum onus, Tibul. Impar intervallum. Nihil ad Persicum, Cic. Injustus fascis, Virg. Majus ferens onus, Sen. Nihil ad nostram hanc, Ter. Ad sapientiam hujus ille nimius nugator fuit, disparat, Plaut. Incomparabilis, Plin. Comparatio Bithi cum Bacchio.
units.tr: Unequal, one thing to another: unequal variety. An unequal burden, Tibul. An unequal interval. Nothing like the Persian, Cic. An unjust bundle, Virg. Bearing a greater load, Sen. Nothing like this one, Ter. That man was too great a trifler to match this one's wisdom, Plaut. Incomparable, Plin. A comparison of Bithus with Bacchius.

units.la: Disparere] Evanescunt hirundines, Plin. nubes, Ovid. Ex oculis tenuem ceu fumus in auram evanuit, Virg. Vanescere in auras, Ovid. Rapi ex oculis, Liv. Oblituit cometes, Sen.
units.tr: To vanish: swallows vanish, Plin. clouds, Ovid. He vanished from sight like thin smoke into the air, Virg. To vanish into the breezes, Ovid. To be snatched from sight, Liv. The comet faded, Sen.

units.la: Dispellere aliquid] Dissipare hostes, Caes. Digerere humorem, Cels. Discutere fuliginem, advocationem. Fugare inermes homines, somnum, Cic. Resolvere nebulas, tenebras, Ovid. Dispersa per agros agmina, Plin. Dispalantur milites, Gell.
units.tr: To dispel something: to scatter enemies, Caes. To disperse moisture, Cels. To shake off soot, a summons. To put unarmed men to flight, to drive away sleep, Cic. To dissolve mists and shadows, Ovid. Troops scattered across the fields, Plin. Soldiers are dispersed, Gell.

units.la: Dispensare] Arbitrio ejus omnia tractantur, Cic. Non ex fide versare pecuniam, Suet.
units.tr: To manage: everything is handled at his discretion, Cic. To handle money dishonestly, Suet.

units.la: Dispensatio] OEconomia, Sipont. Digestus opum, Stat. Erogatio pecuniae, Cic. Dispensator] Promus, Plaut. Actor summarum, Suet. Vid. Quæstor.
units.tr: Management: economy, Sipont. The distribution of wealth, Stat. The disbursement of money, Cic. Steward: a cellarer, Plaut. A keeper of accounts, Suet. See Quaestor.

units.la: Dispergere, vid. Disjicere.
units.tr: To scatter: see Disjicere.

units.la: Disperse, vid. Sparsim.
units.tr: Scattered: see Sparsim.

units.la: Dispescere] Interpungere, Cic. Interstinguere, Stat. Distinguere caput acu, Claud. Discludere, Cæs. Intervenit aliquid, ex Col.
units.tr: To punctuate: to put in punctuation, Cic. To mark off, Stat. To fasten a head with a pin, Claud. To shut off, Caes. Something intervened, ex Col.

units.la: Dispicere aliquid] Prospicere longè animo aliquid. Prospicere mente & cogitatione aliquid. Prospicere multò ante. Providere quid futurum sit. Spectari in judice debet fortuna & dignitas, Cic.
units.tr: To foresee something: to look far ahead in mind. To foresee something by mind and thought. To foresee long beforehand. To provide for what is going to happen. Fortune and dignity must be considered in a judge, Cic.

units.la: Displicere] Injucundum esse alicui, Odiosum. Memet mei pœnitet, Cic. Gravis sum mihi, Vall. Laborare fastidio sui, Sen.
units.tr: To displease: to be unpleasant to someone, odious. I am ashamed of myself, Cic. I am a burden to myself, Vall. To suffer weariness of oneself, Sen.

units.la: Displicet palato] Non est mei stomachi, Cic. Non juvat. Non facit ad stomachum. Nec cœlum nec aquæ faciunt, nec terra, nec auræ, Ovid.
units.tr: It displeases the palate: it is not to my stomach's liking, Cic. It does not delight. It does not suit the stomach. Neither sky nor waters, nor earth nor breezes agree, Ovid.

units.la: Disponere] Digerere aliquid in partes. Distribuere. Dispensare, Cic.
units.tr: Disponere] To arrange something into parts. To distribute. To dispense, Cic.

units.la: Disputabilis] Omnia, quæ tractantur ab oratoribus, dubia sunt & incerta. Habet dubium res. Habet dubitationem sordus. Venit, vocatur in dubium aliquid, in controversiam. Versatur in controversia. Controversa res. Jus controversum. Revocatur in dubium. Habet aliquid quæstionis. Habet res deliberationem, Cic. Est in quæstione, in dubio, Plin. Controversiosa res, Liv.
units.tr: Disputabilis] All matters handled by orators are doubtful and uncertain. The matter has doubt. The matter has hesitation. Something comes into doubt and is called into question or controversy. It is engaged in controversy. A controversial matter. A disputed law. It is called back into doubt. It has some question in it. The matter admits of deliberation, Cic. It is in question, in doubt, Plin. A controversial matter, Liv.

units.la: Disputare] Differere cum aliquo. Decertare per disceptationem. Contendere verbis, non pugnis. Certare cum aliquo dicacitate, Cic.
units.tr: Disputare] To argue with someone. To contend by debate. To fight with words, not fists. To vie with someone in wit, Cic.

units.la: Disputatio] Disceptatio. Altercatio. Pugna doctissimorum virorum. Contentio dicendi. Conflictus & concursus rationibus ac firmamentis. Decertatio, Cic.
units.tr: Disputatio] Debate. Dispute. A contest of the most learned men. A contest of speaking. A clash and meeting of reasons and proofs. A contest, Cic.

units.la: Disquirere] Exquirere aliquid ab aliquo, Inquirere; & de aliquo; in aliquem, Cic. Habeo quæstionem alicujus rei, de aliquâ re. Sciscitari sententiam alicujus, Id. Aliquid ex aliquo, de aliquo exquirere. Investigare aliquid, de aliquo diligenter. Expiscari aliquid ab aliquo. Explorare futura.
units.tr: Disquirere] To seek out something from someone, to inquire; and about someone, into someone, Cic. I have a question about something, concerning some matter. To ask for someone's opinion, Id. To seek out something from someone, or about someone. To investigate something carefully about someone. To fish out something from someone. To explore the future.

units.la: Perscrutari voluntatem alicujus, Plaut. Vocare in disquisitionem, Suet. Inscrutari aliquid altius, Macrob. Mittimus scitatum oracula Phoebi, Virg. Requirere res novas, Plaut. Vise redieritne domum, Ter.
units.tr: To search out someone's will, Plaut. To summon into investigation, Suet. To probe something more deeply, Macrob. "We send to inquire of the oracles of Phoebus," Virg. To seek new things, Plaut. See whether he has returned home, Ter.

units.la: Dissecare] Secare in partes, Cic. Dirigere gallinam cultro. Diribere, Fest. Anatomen exercere. Anatomas facilitare, Henr. Steph.
units.tr: Dissecare] To cut into parts, Cic. To cut up a hen with a knife. To dissect. To practise anatomy. To make anatomies easier, Henr. Steph.

units.la: Dissentire] Discrepare, dissidere ab aliquo. Dissonare. Pugnat oratio ejus cum vita, Cic. Abludere, Hor. Non ad exemplar orationis suae vivit, Sen. Diversus animi; in diversum abire. Ego longe diversa sentio. Multò aliter, atque tu, sentio. Ei sententiae refragabuntur omnes. Isti sententiae nemo non reclamabit. Mihi tua sententia neutiquam probatur. Magnopere nostra cum tua pugnat opinio. Variatum est sententiis. Id unum nobis est controversum. Multum à tua mea discrepat sententia. Longe secus atque tu, sentio. Haud mediocriter à tua mea dissidet opinio. Nimium inter tuam atque meam interest opinionem. Mihi secus videtur, Er.
units.tr: Dissentire] To differ from, to disagree with someone. To be discordant. His speech is at odds with his life, Cic. To differ, Hor. He does not live according to the pattern of his own speech, Sen. Of a different mind; to go over to the opposite side. I think quite differently. I think quite otherwise than you do. All will oppose that opinion. No one will fail to protest against that opinion. Your opinion by no means pleases me. My opinion strongly conflicts with yours. There has been disagreement in opinions. This one point is disputed among us. My view differs much from yours. I think quite otherwise than you. My opinion is by no means small in disagreement with yours. There is too great a difference between your opinion and mine. It seems otherwise to me, Er.

units.la: Diffidere] Discessit in duas factiones civitas. Fovere partes, Tacit. In alia omnia senatus transiit, Cic. Tendunt in diversum sententiae, Liv. Scinditur in contraria studia vulgus, Virg.
units.tr: Diffidere] The state has split into two factions. To support a party, Tacit. The senate went over entirely to the other side, Cic. Opinions tend in opposite directions, Liv. The common people are divided into opposing pursuits, Virg.

units.la: Dissidium] Distractio animorum. Secessio non bellum. Exstinctae amicitiae, Cic. Studium in partes diductum, Plin. Iun. Divortium, Factio, Cic, Partes, Tac. Renunciatio societatis, Vlp.
units.tr: Dissidium] A distraction of minds. A secession, not a war. Friendships extinguished, Cic. A pursuit split into parties, Plin. Iun. Divorce, faction, Cic. Parties, Tac. A renunciation of partnership, Ulp.

units.la: Dissilire] Dissultare, Lucr. Rumpuntur inflata, Virg. Dirupi me penè, Cic.
units.tr: Dissilire] To leap apart, Lucr. Swollen things burst, Virg. I was almost torn apart, Cic.

units.la: Dissimilis, vid. Differens.
units.tr: Dissimilis, see Differens.

units.la: Dissimilia non cohaerent] Morum dissimilitudo amicitias dissociat.
units.tr: Dissimilia non cohaerent] Dissimilarity of character separates friendships.

units.la: Dissimilia comparare] Aquilam noctuae comparas. Cygno fulicam.
units.tr: Dissimilia comparare] You compare an eagle with an owl. A coot with a swan.

units.la: Dissimulare] Apertis oculis transilire, Sen. Obscurè aliquid ferre. Condere iram; simulationem. Fronte & vultu facilè sustinere, Cic. Spem vultu simulat, premit alto corde dolorem, Virg. Se laetum assimulat. Tu, si sapis, quod scis, nescis, Ter.
units.tr: Dissimulare] To pass over with eyes open, Sen. To bear something covertly. To hide anger; to feign. To bear it easily with brow and countenance, Cic. He conceals hope in his face and buries deep grief in his heart, Virg. He feigns a cheerful look. If you have sense, pretend not to know what you know, Ter.

units.la: Dissimulare artem, Ars artium] Dissimulare artem, summi artificis.
units.tr: Dissimulare artem, Ars artium] To conceal one's art: the art of a supreme craftsman.

units.la: Dissimulatio] Hypocrisis, Bud. Fallaciloquentia, Cic. Loligo. Hic nigrae succus loliginis, haec est aerugo mera, Hor. Vid. Simulatio.
units.tr: Dissimulatio] Hypocrisy, Bud. Deceitful speech, Cic. Cuttlefish. "Here is the juice of the black cuttlefish, here is pure verdigris," Hor. See Simulatio.

units.la: Dissipare] Disturbare ac dissipare omnia. Disseminare, Cic. Disparare, Plaut. Vid. Prodigere.
units.tr: Dissipare] To throw everything into confusion and scatter it. To disseminate, Cic. To squander, Plaut. See Prodigere.

units.la: Dissociare, Vid. Disjungere.
units.tr: Dissociare, see Disjungere.

units.la: Dissociari, Vid. Amicitiam dimittere.
units.tr: Dissociari, see Amicitiam dimittere.

units.la: Dissolvere] Resolvere nodos, Plin. Relaxare, Cic. Restringere, Apul. Exsolvere nodos, Liv. Nexus, Lucr. Nexos artus, Virg. Abnodare, Col. Solvere nodum, Hor. Enodare, Non.
units.tr: Dissolvere] To untie knots, Plin. To loosen, Cic. To tighten, Apul. To untie knots, Liv. Bonds, Lucr. Bound limbs, Virg. To unfasten knots, Col. To loosen a knot, Hor. To disentangle, Non.

units.la: Dissolvere subtiliter] Resecare ad vivum.
units.tr: Dissolvere subtiliter] To cut to the quick.

units.la: Dissoluta vita] Licentia. Effusa licentia, Ter. Immoderata libertas. Effrenatio impotentis animi. Lapsi ad mollitiem mores. Bacchatio. Dissoluta consuetudo, & licentia impudens, Cic. Dissolutio, Spart. Desidentes mores, Liv. Bacchanalia.
units.tr: Dissoluta vita] Licence. Unbridled licence, Ter. Immoderate freedom. The unbridling of an uncontrolled mind. Morals fallen into softness. Revelry. A dissolute way of life and shameless licence, Cic. Dissolution, Spart. Morals sinking away, Liv. Bacchanalia.

units.la: Dissolutus] Licentiosus miles, Ter. Cui quod libet, licet, Cic. Vid. Licentiosus.
units.tr: Dissolutus] A licentious soldier, Ter. One who may do whatever he pleases, Cic. See Licentiosus.

units.la: Dissuadere, Vid. Dehortari.
units.tr: Dissuadere, see Dehortari.

units.la: Dissuere] Resuere, Suet.
units.tr: Dissuere] To unstitch, Suet.

units.la: Distare] Locorum & temporum intervallo disjuncti sumus. Abesse spatio bidui. Dirimuntur oppida itinere diei. Distinguunt nos duo millia passuum, Mart. Longius a mari recedit, Curt. Tanta intercapedine dispescuntur, Apul. Diametro distare.
units.tr: Distare] We are separated by an interval of place and time. To be two days' journey apart. Towns are divided by a day's journey. Two thousand paces separate us, Mart. He withdraws farther from the sea, Curt. They are parted by so great a gap, Apul. To be apart by a diameter.

units.la: Distanter longinque] Quantum distat coelum a terra.
units.tr: Distanter longinque] As far as heaven is from earth.

units.la: Distantia] Longinquitas, Cic. Intervalla siderum, Quint. Spatium, Ovid. Interjecta non mediocri, Amm. Vid. Intervallum.
units.tr: Distantia] Remoteness, Cic. The distances between the stars, Quint. Space, Ovid. An interval of no small extent, Amm. See Intervallum.

units.la: Distendere] Expandere, Plin. Extendere vites. Prolixare aciem ferramenti. Porrigit radices arbor. Exporrigere crura. Prolongare. Dispandere, Plin. Protendere brachia. Tendunt vela Noti, Virg. Pandere alas ad solem, Id. Contendere poplitem, Hor. Producere pelles dentibus, Mart.
units.tr: Distendere] To spread out, Plin. To stretch out vines. To lengthen the edge of a blade. The tree puts out roots. To stretch out the legs. To lengthen. To spread out, Plin. To stretch out the arms. The south winds stretch the sails, Virg. To spread wings to the sun, Id. To stretch the knee, Hor. To stretch skins over teeth, Mart.

units.la: Distinguere] Discernere alba & atra, Cic. Vid. Dignoscere.
units.tr: Distinguere] To separate white from black, Cic. See Dignoscere.

units.la: Distractus animo] Distractissimus negotiorum onere, Pater. In plura studia distrahi industriam. Distentus operâ & animo. Alias res agit, Cic. Diversæ animum trahunt curæ, Ter. Dividit huc illuc animum, Virg. Nos alio mentes, alio divisimus aures, Catul.
units.tr: Distractus animo] Most distracted by the burden of business, Pater. Diligence is drawn into too many pursuits. Occupied with work and mind. He does other things, Cic. Divided cares draw the mind different ways, Ter. He turns his mind this way and that, Virg. "I have divided my minds elsewhere, my ears elsewhere," Catul.

units.la: Distractus sensus impeditur] Duos insequens lepores, neutrum capit. Nusquam est, qui ubique est. Pluribus intentus minor est ad singula sensus.
units.tr: Distractus sensus impeditur] Chasing two hares, one catches neither. He who is everywhere is nowhere. A mind intent on many things is less keen for each one.

units.la: Distribuere] Dispartiri. Dilargiri, Cic. Dividere argentum in vivos, Plaut. Dispensare officia, Sen.
units.tr: Distribuere] To share out. To distribute lavishly, Cic. To divide money among the living, Plaut. To dispense duties, Sen.

units.la: Distribuendum prudenter] Manu serendum, non thylaco.
units.tr: Distribuendum prudenter] One should sow with the hand, not with a purse.

units.la: Ditare aliquem] Augere aliquem divitiis. Locupletare. Collocupletare, Cic. Opulentare, Col. Luculentos reddit lucrum, Plaut. Multos annos est possideo,
units.tr: Ditare aliquem] To enrich someone with riches. To make wealthy. To make very wealthy, Cic. To make rich, Col. Gain makes people rich, Plaut. For many years I have possessed ...

units.la: Ditescere] Rem, opus augere. Amplificare rem familiarem. Pervenire ad nummos, opulentiam. Confirmare potestatem opibus & copiis. Fundare opes. Consequi opum potentiam, Cic. Convalescunt opes alicujus, Liv. Crescere in multas opes, Id. Facere rem, Ter. Emergere ad summas opes, Lucr.
units.tr: Ditescere] To increase one's property or work. To enlarge one's estate. To attain money and wealth. To secure power by means of resources and forces. To establish wealth. To achieve the power of riches, Cic. A person's wealth grows, Liv. To grow into great wealth, Id. To make a fortune, Ter. To rise to the greatest wealth, Lucr.

units.la: Diu] Perdiu. Longo spatio. Multum. Plurimum ætatis, Cic. Diutinè. Ætatem velim servire. Seculum est, Plaut. Mille annorum. Perpetuò vivunt. A seculo ad seculum. Non longum lætabere, Virg. Annus est dum comuntur, Ter. Longinquuum, Longum nimis loquor. Per longinquum est, Plaut. Longum est explicare, Cic. Peilongè est, Ter.
units.tr: Diu] For a long time. For a long span. Much. The greater part of life, Cic. For a long time. I would gladly serve for a lifetime. It is an age, Plaut. For a thousand years. They live forever. From age to age. You will not rejoice for long, Virg. It is a year while they are being combed, Ter. Too long, I speak at too great length. It is far off, Plaut. It is a long business to explain, Cic. It is very far, Ter.

units.la: Divaricare] Dilaxare crura, Porphyr. Cossigerare. Dispendere, Accius.
units.tr: Divaricare] To stretch the legs apart, Porphyr. To spread wide. To stretch out, Accius.

units.la: Divendere] Distrahere, Suet. Hastæ subjicere, Cic. Vid. Vendere.
units.tr: Divendere] To sell off, Suet. To put up for auction, Cic. See Vendere.

units.la: Diversorium, Vid. Hospitium.
units.tr: Diversorium, see Hospitium.

units.la: Diversus] Longissimè diversi sunt. Alius longè. Aliud melle, Col. Res dissociabiles miscere, Tac. Alienigenæ res, Lucr. Vid. Differens. Diversis diversa conveniunt] Insania non omnibus eadem. Facta juvenum, Consilia mediocrium, vota senum. Consilia senum, juvenum lanceæ. Equis quadrigis, aratro bos.
units.tr: Diversus] They are very different. Another far away. Another thing entirely. To mix incompatible things, Tac. Foreign things, Lucr. See Differens. Diversis diversa conveniunt] Madness is not the same for everyone. The deeds of the young, the counsels of the middle-aged, the prayers of the old. The counsels of the old, the spears of the young. Horses for the chariot, an ox for the plough.

units.la: Diversos diversa juvant] Alia aliis pulchra. Alia apud alios bona. Alia vita, alia diæta. Aliam ætatem alia decent. Alia æstate, alia hieme.
units.tr: Diversos diversa juvant] Different things please different people. Some things are beautiful to some, good to others. One life, one diet. Different ages suit different things. Some things suit summer, others winter.

units.la: Diversi diversa possunt] Consilio pollet, cui vim natura negavit.
units.tr: Diversi diversa possunt] He who nature denied strength is strong in counsel.

units.la: Divertere, Vid. Hospitari.
units.tr: Divertere, see Hospitari.

units.la: Dives] Opulentus, prædives, perdives. Copiosus, Divitior. Pecuniosus. Lautus, Cic. Luculentus, Plaut. Præpollens divitiis, Liv. Rem habet. Cic. Largæ sunt illi facultates, Plin. Unctum patrimonium, Catul. Æris alicujus homo. Croesus. Croeso ditior. Plutone. Mido ditior. Multorum nummorum. Tantali opes assecutus, Er.
units.tr: Dives] Wealthy, very rich, exceedingly rich. Abundant, richer. Moneyed. Sumptuous, Cic. Flourishing, Plaut. Powerful in riches, Liv. He has means, Cic. His resources are ample, Plin. An anointed inheritance, Catul. A man made of bronze. Croesus. Richer than Croesus. Richer than Pluto. Richer than Midas. Of many coins. Having attained the riches of Tantalus, Er.

units.la: Dives fundis, seu prædiis] Locuples, Cic., (Qui locorum plenus.) Bene peculiatus, Cic. Bene prædiatus, Apul.
units.tr: Dives fundis, seu praediis] Rich in land, Cic. (full of places). Well provided with property, Cic. Well endowed with estates, Apul.

units.la: Dives avarus] Fontes ipsi sitiunt.
units.tr: Dives avarus] The springs themselves thirst.

units.la: Dives rudis] Deauratus stipes. Simia purpurata. In eburnea vagina, plumbeus gladius. Midas Rex auriculas asini habet. Aureum pecus. Ovis aurea. Aureus asinus. Stultitiam patiuntur opes, Hor.
units.tr: Dives rudis] A gilded stump. A purple-clad monkey. A lead sword in an ivory scabbard. King Midas has the ears of an ass. A golden flock. A golden sheep. A golden ass. Wealth makes stupidity endurable, Hor.

units.la: Dives superbus] Superbia divitiarum comes.
units.tr: Dives superbus] Pride is the companion of riches.

units.la: Dividere] Tribuere in partes membra; partiri. Facere partes, Cic. Dispertiri. Dispertire aliquid aliquibus. Orbis certis passibus dimensus. Dividuum facere, Plaut. Dispendere curam alicujus. Dispensare æquâ portione sucum. Contribuere in regna Tetrarchias. Discernere aliquid forte, Col. Diducere in particulas aliquid, Sen. Æquare laborem, Justin. Ercisci, & Ercisceri hæreditatem, Fest.
units.tr: Dividere] To divide into parts or limbs; to share. To make parts, Cic. To distribute. To distribute something among several. To measure the world with fixed paces. To make something divisible, Plaut. To dispense someone's care. To dispense juice in equal portions. To distribute into kingdoms and tetrarchies. To separate something by chance, Col. To break something into small pieces, Sen. To equalise labour, Justin. To divide an inheritance, Fest.

units.la: Dividere unam rem ab alia] Disterminare aliquid ab aliquo, Cic. Dirimere, Plin. Iun. Librare, Col. Discludere, Virg. Discriminare, Cic. Dissepire, Sen. Dispescere, Plin. Cernere, Bud. Discernere, Stat. Limitari vineas, Plin. Limitare, Fest.
units.tr: Dividere unam rem ab alia] To separate one thing from another, Cic. To divide off, Plin. Iun. To weigh out, Col. To cut off, Virg. To distinguish, Cic. To partition off, Sen. To divide, Plin. To separate, Bud. To discern, Stat. To mark out vineyards, Plin. To mark out boundaries, Fest.

units.la: Divinare] Augurari conjectura. Hariolari, Cic. Viam restaminstare. Rem acu tangere, Plaut. Addivinare. Omnia facere, Plinius. Inaugurare, Livius. Ominari, Bud.
units.tr: To divine] To augur by conjecture. To prophesy, Cic. To block the way. To hit the matter with the needle, Plaut. To guess at. To do everything, Plinius. To inaugurate, Livius. To foretell from omens, Bud.

units.la: Divinatio] Ars divinationis. Auguratus scientia. Ars exstispicum, Cic.
units.tr: Divination] The art of divination. The science of augury. The art of the haruspices, Cic.

units.la: Divinator] Dissector nodorum Gordiorum.
units.tr: Diviner] One who unties the Gordian knots.

units.la: Divitiæ] Res. Opulentitas. Bonæ res, Plaut. Opes. Copiæ, Fortuna, Cic. Opulentia, Virg. Midæ opes. Croesi opes. Arabum gazæ. Stimuli in corde. Sudes in oculis. Tantali opes. Tantali talenta. Census, Iuv.
units.tr: Riches] Goods. Wealth. Good things, Plaut. Resources. Plenty, fortune, Cic. Affluence, Virg. The wealth of Midas. The riches of Croesus. The treasures of the Arabs. Goads in the heart. Stakes in the eyes. The riches of Tantalus. The talents of Tantalus. Property, Juv.

units.la: Divitiæ pariunt stultitiam] Misera est magni custodia census.
units.tr: Riches breed folly] Wretched is the guarding of great wealth.

units.la: Divortium, Vid. Repudium.
units.tr: Divorce, see Repudiation.

units.la: Dium] Divum, Hor. Sub Jove frigido. Subdialis locus, Plin. Hypæthrum, Vitr. Aperta promptaque coeli, Lucr. Loca retecta, Plin.
units.tr: Under the open sky] Under the open sky, Hor. Under cold Jove. An open-air place, Plin. Hypaethral, Vitr. Open and clear to the sky, Lucr. Places laid bare, Plin.

units.la: Divulgare aliquid] Publicare reticenda, Iustin. Vulgatum hoc vestrâ voce est. Pervulgare atque edere aliquid populo. Percelebrare. Dissipare famam, rumores, sermones. Spargere famam, disseminare. Edere in vulgus aliquid. Decantare aliquid, Cic. Vulgare famam per omnes. Rem vulgo ferre, Liv. Dare aliquid famæ. Rumoribus aliquid differre, Tac. Tradere famæ, Curt. Invulgare aliquid, Gell. In vulgum vulgas, quæ scis, Enn. Mittere aliquid in ora populi, Quint. Dispergere famam, Plin. Spargere aliquid in vulgus, Virg.
units.tr: To divulge something] To make public what ought to be kept secret, Justin. This has been made common talk by your voice. To publish and put something before the people. To make widely known. To scatter fame, rumours, talk. To spread abroad, to disseminate. To send something out among the common people. To sing something abroad, Cic. To spread a report among everyone. To bring a matter before the common people, Liv. To give something to fame. To put off something with rumours, Tac. To hand something down to fame, Curt. To make something common knowledge, Gell. You publish to the crowd what you know, Enn. To put something into the mouths of the people, Quint. To disperse fame, Plin. To scatter something among the crowd, Virg.

units.la: Docere] Artem docendi tradere. Tradere scientiam alicui. Dare alicui præcepta. Et rationes dicendi. Instituere aliquem artem. Tradere vias artium. Erudire aliquid ad aliquam disciplinam. Perdocere aliquem aliquid, Cic. Instruere aliquem scientia, Quint. Imbuere ingenium artibus, Plaut. Formare studiis mentes, Hor. Instillare præcepta auriculis, Id. Formare juventutem, Plin. Præcipere artem, Quint. Peritum aliquem facere, Propert. Edocere. Addocere artes, Salust.
units.tr: To teach] To hand on the art of teaching. To hand knowledge on to someone. To give someone precepts, and rules of speaking. To instruct someone in an art. To hand down the ways of the arts. To train someone up in a discipline. To teach someone something thoroughly, Cic. To furnish someone with knowledge, Quint. To steep the mind in the arts, Plaut. To form minds by study, Hor. To instil precepts into the ears, Id. To form the youth, Plin. To prescribe an art, Quint. To make someone skilled, Propert. To teach thoroughly. To teach arts in addition, Sall.

units.la: Docendum aut discendum semper] Doce vel audi.
units.tr: One must always either teach or learn] Teach or listen.

units.la: Doctrina] Ars doctior quàm natura. Disciplina juris. Ingenuarum artium scientia. Facultas oratoris, Cic. Ratio vivendi, Id.
units.tr: Learning] An art more learned than nature. The discipline of law. Knowledge of the liberal arts. The skill of the orator, Cic. The method of living, Id.

units.la: Doctr] Doctè] Literatè respondere. Literatius, Eruditius, Cic. Perdoctè, Plaut.
units.tr: Learnedly] To answer in a literate manner. More literately, more learnedly, Cic. Very learnedly, Plaut.

units.la: Doctor] Doctor Sapientiæ. Magister artium. A studiis, Suet. Præmonstrator, Ter. Formator, Gell. Exercitator hominis vel artis, Plin. Literator linguæ, Gell. Præceptor, Cic. Institutor, Lampr. Eruditor, Tertul.
units.tr: Teacher] Teacher of wisdom. Master of the arts. Secretary of studies, Suet. Instructor, Ter. Former, Gell. Trainer of a man or of an art, Plin. Teacher of language, Gell. Preceptor, Cic. Instructor, Lampr. Educator, Tertul.

units.la: Doctor juris] Interpres legum, Cic. Sic. Theologiæ interpres.
units.tr: Doctor of law] Interpreter of the laws, Cic. Likewise. Interpreter of theology.

units.la: Doctor indoctus] Asinus portans mysteria.
units.tr: Unlearned doctor] An ass carrying mysteries.

units.la: Doctrina, Vid Eruditio.
units.tr: Learning, see Erudition.

units.la: Doctus] Instructus artibus ingenuis. Politus literis. Sunt in eo literæ plurimæ. Tinctus arte. In omni recto studio, & humanitate versatus, Cic. Doctiloquus, Varr. Madet arte, Lucr. Vivum Musæum. Bibliotheca obambulans, animata, Er. Proceres & antesignani literarum, Polian. Docere posse, signum est scientis. Minervâ doctior. Aristarcho doctior, Er. Vid. Eruditus.
units.tr: Learned] Furnished with the liberal arts. Polished by letters. He has very many letters in him. Tinctured with art. Versed in every right study and culture, Cic. Speaking learnedly, Varr. He is steeped in art, Lucr. A living museum. A walking library, animated, Erasm. Leaders and vanguard of letters, Polian. To be able to teach is the sign of one who knows. More learned than Minerva. More learned than Aristarchus, Erasm. See Erudite.

units.la: Doctus quidem, sed malè moratus] Vir est doctrinâ quidem egregiâ, verùm moribus illaudatis.
units.tr: Learned indeed, but ill-mannered] He is a man of outstanding learning, but of unpraiseworthy morals.

units.la: Docti sunt humani] Commisce Gratias Musis.
units.tr: The learned are humane] Mix the Graces with the Muses.

units.la: Documentum, Vid. Argumentum.
units.tr: Document, see Argument.

units.la: Dolere] Dolorem capere, habere, suscipere. Dolore angi, Cic. Distrahi, diripi doloribus, Ter. Dolore urgeri, cruciari, Celf. Concruciari, Lucr. Dolori operam dare, Sen. Caput condoluit, Tibul. Doleo ab oculis, Plaut. Confligari capitis doloribus, Celf. Dolitat mihi aliquid, Cat. Indolere. Indolescere, Justin.
units.tr: To grieve] To take, have, or undergo pain. To be distressed by pain, Cic. To be torn apart and seized by pains, Ter. To be pressed and tormented by pain, Cels. To be racked, Lucr. To take trouble over pain, Sen. My head has ached, Tibul. I ache in my eyes, Plaut. To be struck down by headache pains, Cels. Something gnaws at me, Cat. To begin to feel pain. To begin to hurt, Justin.

units.la: Dolor] Motus asper in corpore à sensibus alienus. Ægritudo crucians, Cic. Voluptatis comes.
units.tr: Pain] A harsh bodily motion, foreign to the senses. Tormenting distress, Cic. The companion of pleasure.

units.la: Dolor justus diu durat] Temperare justum dolorem difficilè.
units.tr: A just pain lasts long] It is hard to moderate a just pain.

units.la: Dolosè] Insidiosè, Fallaciter. Fraudulentèt, Col. Per dolum, Hor. Per fas & fidem deceptus, Liv. Perfidiosè, Plaut. Ex insidiis, Cic. Vid. Astutè.
units.tr: Deceitfully] Insidiously, deceptively. Fraudulently, Col. By trickery, Hor. Deceived through right and faith, Liv. Treacherously, Plaut. From ambushes, Cic. See Craftily.

units.la: Dolosus] Fraudulentus. Insidiosus, Cic. Fraus, Ter. Callidus in fraudem, Amm. Ulysse dolosior, Er. Vid. Decep-tor, Astutus.
units.tr: Deceitful] Fraudulent. Insidious, Cic. Fraud, Ter. Skilled in fraud, Amm. More deceitful than Ulysses, Erasm. See Deceiver, Crafty.

units.la: Dolus] Fallacia, Ter. Fraudes. Fraudatio. Perfidia, Cic. Techna, Ter. Impostura, Gell. Dolus doctus. Dolus malus. Vid. Deceptio.
units.tr: Guile] Deceit, Ter. Frauds. Cheating. Treachery, Cic. Trickery, Ter. Imposture, Gell. Skilled guile. Wicked guile. See Deception.

units.la: Dolus adversus dolum] Laqueus laqueum cepit. Ars deluditur arte. Vulpinari cum vulpe.
units.tr: Guile against guile] The snare caught the snare. Art is deluded by art. To fox it with a fox.

units.la: Dolos struere] Dolos nectere. Dolare dolum. Dolos texere. Fabricare fallaciam. Fabricam fingere, Plaut.
units.tr: To lay plots] To weave plots. To contrive guile. To weave tricks. To devise deceit. To invent a fabrication, Plaut.

units.la: Domesticus] Penetralis. Dii penetrales. Vernaculus. Familiaris, Cic. Privatus, Lucr. Gentilis mos, tessera, Amm.
units.tr: Domestic] Inner, private. The household gods. Native. Familiar, Cic. Private, Lucr. A native custom, token, Amm.

units.la: Domi meae] Intra sepes meas.
units.tr: In my home] Within my hedges.

units.la: Domi suae quisque Dominus] Gallus in suo sterquilinio multum potest.
units.tr: Each is master in his own house] The cock has much power on his own dunghill.

units.la: Domi optime] Domus amica. Domus optima.
units.tr: Very well at home] A friendly home. The best of homes.

units.la: Domi desidere] Cochleae vitam agit. Umbraticus homo, Plaut. Incubator domi suae, Macrob. Non facile hunc quisquam non modo extra tectum, sed ne extra lectum quidem vidit. Ipse tanquam cochlea abscondens & retentans sese, Tacit. Lucem conventumque hominum vitat. Tectis ac tenebris continetur. Omnes solitudines persequitur. Januâ se ac parietibus tegit. Publico caret. Quae vitatio oculorum ? lucis, urbis, fori ? Solitudo ei pro frequentiâ, nox pro die, Cic. Ipsa domus puerum quem videt, ipsa senem, Claud. Microspicus, Mart. (qui parum conspicitur foris) Nimis urbanus es, nisi concupiscis secessum, Plin.Iun. Claudus sutor.
units.tr: To stay at home] He lives the life of a snail. A stay-at-home, Plaut. One who broods in his own house, Macrob. Hardly anyone has seen him outside the roof, nor even outside his bed. Like a snail he hides himself away and holds himself back, Tac. He shuns the light and the gathering of men. He keeps himself under roofs and in shadows. He pursues every solitude. He hides himself behind door and walls. He has no part in public life. What is this avoidance of the eyes? of light, city, forum? Solitude is his company, night his day, Cic. The house itself sees the boy, the house itself the old man, Claud. A man of small visibility, Mart. (one who is seen little abroad). You are too much a townsman unless you long for seclusion, Plin. Jun. A lame cobbler.

units.la: Domina] Dominatrix, Cic. Herois, Mart. Optimates matronae, Cic. Summates matronae, Plaut. Summates Deae, Apul. Hera major.
units.tr: Mistress] A ruling lady, Cic. A heroine, Mart. Matrons of the optimates, Cic. Matrons of the highest rank, Plaut. Goddesses of the highest rank, Apul. Greater Hera.

units.la: Dominari] Potiri rerum. Imperare. Imperium in aliquem tenere. Tenere in dicione, Cic. Divitiae meae sunt, Sen. Imperitare, Lucr.
units.tr: To rule] To hold command of affairs. To command. To hold power over someone. To keep in one's sway, Cic. My riches are mine, Sen. To domineer, Lucr.

units.la: Dominium, vid. Imperium.
units.tr: Dominion, see Empire.

units.la: Dominus] Dominus in suos. Dominus in bonis alicujus. Dominus rerum suarum. Dominus juris sui, sui municipii. Nemini mancipatus. Dominationem habens in aliquos, Cic. Herus, Ter. Dominator, Plin.
units.tr: Lord] Lord over his own people. Lord over someone's goods. Lord of his own affairs. Lord of his own right, of his own town. Bound to no one. Having authority over some, Cic. Master, Ter. Ruler, Plin.

units.la: Domus] Tectum. Ædes, Cic. Nidus, Hor.
units.tr: House] Roof. Dwelling, Cic. Nest, Hor.

units.la: Domus lapidea] Domus lateritio opere structa.
units.tr: Stone house] A house built of brickwork.

units.la: Donare] Condonare alicui munuscula, Cic. Dare dono aliquid, Liv. Offerre, mittere munera, Quint. Munerare &, ri,) aliquem aliquâ re, Cic. Ter. Dare in peculium, Plaut. Dare alicui mancipio aliquid, Lucr. Perscribere pecuniam, Id.
units.tr: To give] To make small gifts to someone, Cic. To give something as a gift, Liv. To offer and send presents, Quint. To reward someone with something, Cic., Ter. To give as a private fund, Plaut. To give something to someone as property, Lucr. To assign money, Id.

units.la: Donec, vid. Quàm diu.
units.tr: Donec, see As long as.

units.la: Donum] Munus, Cic. Donarium, Macrob. Aureæ compedes. Aureæ catenæ.
units.tr: Gift] A present, Cic. A votive offering, Macrob. Golden fetters. Golden chains.

units.la: Dona magna à non magnis frustra exspectes] Dii parvi parva dant.
units.tr: Do not vainly expect great gifts from small givers] Little gods give little things.

units.la: Donis ne inhia] Non omnia, nec passim, nec ab omnibus accipienda dona.
units.tr: Do not gape after gifts] Not all gifts are to be accepted, nor indiscriminately, nor from everyone.

units.la: Dona sponsalitia] Dona propter nuptias, ICt.
units.tr: Betrothal gifts] Gifts on account of marriage, Jurists.

units.la: Dona strictim non examinanda] Donum quodcunque aliquis dederit probato.
units.tr: Gifts not to be examined superficially] Accept whatever gift someone has given, as approved.

units.la: Dormiens interdiu] Antipodes nostri.
units.tr: Sleeping by day] Our antipodes.

units.la: Dormire] Operam dare somno, Plaut. Quieti se dare, Cæs. Somnum capere. Imaginem mortis quotidie inducere, Cic. Nocturnâ quiete diurnum laborem relaxare, Curt. Sopor me habet, Virg. Tota mihi dormitur hiems, Mart.
units.tr: To sleep] To devote effort to sleep, Plaut. To give oneself to rest, Caes. To take sleep. To bring before oneself daily the image of death, Cic. To relax the day's labour by night's rest, Curt. Sleep holds me, Virg. I sleep through the whole winter, Mart.

units.la: Dormire altùm] Gravi somno premi, Plin. Somno vinoque sepultus, Virg. Gravi sopore membra devinxit somnus, Lucr. Temulento sopore profligatus, Quint. Arctè & graviter dormitare. Arctior me somnus amplectitur. Somno solutus, Cic. Altus sopor illum habet, Virg. Sorbet dormiens, Plaut. Totum diem stertere, Hor. Vigilanti sterte-re naso, Iuv.
units.tr: To sleep soundly] To be pressed by heavy sleep, Plin. Buried in sleep and wine, Virg. Sleep has bound my limbs in heavy slumber, Lucr. Overcome by drunken slumber, Quint. To doze firmly and heavily. A deeper sleep embraces me. Loosed from sleep, Cic. A deep slumber holds him, Virg. He sips while asleep, Plaut. To snore the whole day, Hor. Snoring with a wide-awake nose, Juv.

units.la: Dormire leviter] Intervigilare, Sen. Dormitio nostri pectoris vigilabilis, Varr. Semisomnus vel semisomnis sum, Cic. Corybantiare, (dormire patentibus oculis) Plin.
units.tr: To sleep lightly] To half-wake, Sen. The sleep of our breast is wakeful, Varr. I am half asleep, Cic. To Corybantiate (to sleep with eyes open), Plin.

units.la: Dormire parcè] Non quantùm lusciniæ dormiunt.
units.tr: To sleep sparingly] Not as much as nightingales sleep.

units.la: Dormire stando] Cantherino more somniare.
units.tr: To sleep standing] To dream in the manner of a horse.

units.la: Dormiturire] Dormitare, Plaut. Soporari, Plin. Obrepsit mihi somnus, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: To be drowsy] To doze, Plaut. To be drowsy, Plin. Sleep has crept upon me, Plin. Jun.

units.la: Dotalia dona] Super dotem aliqua accepta, Liv. Præter dotem accepta, Cic. Paraphena, pl. Paraphernalia, pl. Ulp. Paraphernica, pl. Sidon. Dona peculiaria uxoris, Vlp. Dotalitia, ICti. Accessio dotis praeter profectionem, Vlp.
units.tr: Dowry gifts] Something received over and above the dowry, Liv. Received apart from the dowry, Cic. Paraphena, pl. Paraphernalia, pl., Ulp. Paraphernica, pl., Sidon. The wife's own gifts, Ulp. Dotalitia, Jurists. An addition to the dowry beyond what was brought, Ulp.

units.la: Dotem dare] Dotare filiam, Suet. Dicere doti pecuniam. Largiri dotem. Dote locupletare, Cic.
units.tr: To give a dowry] To endow a daughter, Suet. To pledge money as dowry. To bestow a dowry. To enrich with a dowry, Cic.

units.la: Dubiè] Dubitanter. Ambiguè, Cic. Perplexum, & perplexè loqui, Plaut. Suspensa manu commendare, Plin. Iun. Incertè, Gell.
units.tr: Doubtfully] Hesitantly. Ambiguously, Cic. Perplexedly, and to speak perplexedly, Plaut. To commend with the hand held in suspense, Plin. Jun. Uncertainly, Gell.

units.la: Dubitare] Dubium habere. Dubitatione æstuare. Injectus est mihi scrupulus. In dubitationem venire. Hærere, hæsitare in aliqua re. Pendere animi, animis. Pendere, Abs. Incertus sum. Suspensus & incertus pendeo. Suspensas habeo rationes. Ambigere de aliquâ re. Ambiguum habere, Cic. In dubio ponere, Liv. In dubio est animus, Ter. Totâ vitâ pendent, Sen. Fluctuari animo, Curt. In salo stare, Apul. Revocare in dubium. Scrupulam commeare viam, Id. Res in ambiguo est. Non dum satis constitui. Adhuc anceps animi sum. Non dum huc aut illuc inclinat sententia. Adhuc in æquilibrio vacillat animus utroque nutans. Hactenus suspendo decretum animi. Nondum liquet, Er.
units.tr: To doubt] To hold as doubtful. To be tossed about by doubt. A scruple has been put into me. To come into doubt. To stick and hesitate in some matter. To hang in one's mind. To hang, Abs. I am uncertain. I hang suspended and unsure. I hold my reckonings in suspense. To be uncertain about some matter. To hold as ambiguous, Cic. To put in doubt, Liv. The mind is in doubt, Ter. They hang their whole life, Sen. To waver in mind, Curt. To stand on the sea, Apul. To call into question. A scruple to travel the road, Id. The matter is in ambiguity. I have not yet settled. I am still of two minds. My opinion does not yet incline one way or the other. Up to now my mind wavers, nodding both ways. Thus far I suspend my decision. It is not yet clear, Erasm.

units.la: Dubitare valde] In magna quæstione aliquid habere, Plin. Hæc me res in diversum trahit, Cic. Incertior multo sunt, quàm dudum. Longa dies meum incertat animum, Plaut.
units.tr: To doubt greatly] To hold something in a great question (Plin.). This matter draws me in a different direction (Cic.). I am far more uncertain than I was a while ago. A long day wears down my mind (Plaut.).

units.la: Dubitatio] Dubium. Ambiguitas. Addubitatio. Hæsitatio. Quæstio anceps, perobscura, Cic. Fluctuatio animorum, Liv. Suspensio animi, Hirt. Dubietas, Ammian. Salum mentis & cogitationum, Apul.
units.tr: Doubt] Doubt. Uncertainty. Ambiguity. Hesitation. A question that is doubtful and very obscure (Cic.). Wavering of minds (Liv.). Suspension of mind (Hirt.). Dubiety (Ammian.). The sea of the mind and of thoughts (Apul.).

units.la: Dubitatione liberare] Scrupulum evellere, eximere.
units.tr: To free from doubt] To pluck out a scruple, to remove it.

units.la: Dubitatur adhuc] Sub judice lis est, Hor. In incerto est. In quæstione est. In quæstionem, disceptationem vocatur. In quæstione versatur, Cic. Er.
units.tr: It is still doubted] The case is before the judge (Hor.). It is uncertain. It is in question. It is brought into question and dispute. It is in question (Cic. Er.).

units.la: Sine dubio, vid. Procul dubio.
units.tr: Without doubt, see Undoubtedly.

units.la: Dubium movere alicui] Scrupulum injicere. Adducere alicui dubitationem. Injicere, facere animum alicui dubium, Cic. Dubietatem facere, Amm.
units.tr: To raise a doubt in someone] To throw in a scruple. To bring doubt upon someone. To put a doubt into someone's mind (Cic.). To make doubtful (Amm.).

units.la: Dubius] Anceps eventus rei. Ambiguus futuri, Tacit. Suspensus spensus animi. Incertus sententiae, Liv. Peranceps labor, Amm. Ancipitis consilii res, Cic.
units.tr: Doubtful] An uncertain outcome of a matter. Ambiguous as to the future (Tacit.). Suspended in mind. Uncertain in opinion (Liv.). Labour fraught with peril (Amm.). A matter of doubtful counsel (Cic.).

units.la: Ducere] Manu ducere. Praebere alicui ducem, Cic. Praeducere, Tacit. Ducatum alicui praebere, Hor. Perductare, Plaut.
units.tr: To lead] To lead by the hand. To furnish someone with a guide (Cic.). To lead before (Tacit.). To give someone leadership (Hor.). To lead along, to conduct through (Plaut.).

units.la: Ductum Dei sequamur] Quo fata trahunt retrahuntque sequamur.
units.tr: Let us follow the leading of God] Wherever the fates draw us and draw us back, let us follow.

units.la: Dudum] Pridem, Olim, Jam pridem, jam olim, Tanto intervallo. Longo intervallo, Cic. Diu. Jam dudum. Jam dudum aetatem sunt inter nos, Ter. Jam diu, Perdudum, In multos annos est cum possideo, Plaut. Annò, Id.
units.tr: Long since] Formerly, of old, long ago, a long time since. After a long interval (Cic.). For a long time. Already for a long time. Already for ages between us (Ter.). For a long time now, for many years: I have held it for many years (Plaut.). For years (Id.).

units.la: Duellum] Pugna singularis, Macrob. Monomachia, Caes. Rhod. Singulare praelium, Ausón. Gladiatorium certamen. Gladiatoria pugna, Cic.
units.tr: Duel] A single combat (Macrob.). Monomachy [μονομαχία] (Caes. Rhod.). A single battle (Ausón.). A gladiatorial contest. A gladiatorial fight (Cic.).

units.la: Dulcis] Dulcior melle, Ambrosiâ. Nectareus, Mart. Ambrosius. Mulseus. Musteus, Col. Mellifluus, Sipont.
units.tr: Sweet] Sweeter than honey or ambrosia. Nectar-like (Mart.). Ambrosial. Honeyed (Mulseus). Of new wine (Musteus, Col.). Honey-flowing (Sipont.).

units.la: Dulce-amarus] Plus aloës quàm mellis habet.
units.tr: Bittersweet] It has more aloes than honey.

units.la: Dulciculus] Languidè dulcis. Subdulcis, Plin.
units.tr: Mildly sweet] Faintly sweet. Somewhat sweet (Plin.).

units.la: Dum, vid. Quam diu,
units.tr: While, see As long as.

units.la: Duo] Tot, quot ego & tu sumus, Plaut. Geminus ictus, Plin. Geminatus sol, Cic. Paribus equis, id est, duobus. Binae literae, Cic.
units.tr: Two] As many as you and I are (Plaut.). A double blow (Plin.). The sun doubled (Cic.). With equal horses, that is, two. Two letters (Cic.).

units.la: Duo non sunt idem] Dominus domino, servus servo praestat.
units.tr: Two are not the same] A master excels another master, and a servant excels another servant.

units.la: Duo plus possunt uno] Melius duo defendunt retinacula navem.
units.tr: Two can do more than one] Two hawsers hold a ship more securely.

units.la: Duplum] Bis tanto valeo, Plaut. Dupla pars alicujus. Altero tanto, Cic.
units.tr: Double] I am worth twice as much (Plaut.). A double share of someone. Twice as much (Cic.).

units.la: Durabilis] Firmus. Stabilis ad diuturnitatem, Cic. Vivax oliva, Col. Tenax morbus, Suet. Pertinax certamen, Liv. Duratrix firmitas, Plin. Bene fert aetatem, Macr. ex Cic. Contumax emori, Plin. Perseverans, Col.
units.tr: Durable] Firm. Stable for a long duration (Cic.). A long-lived olive (Col.). A tenacious disease (Suet.). A persistent contest (Liv.). Hardening firmness (Plin.). Bears age well (Macr., from Cic.). Stubborn about dying (Plin.). Persevering (Col.).

units.la: Durabilis parum, vid. Cedens annis.
units.tr: Scarcely durable, see Yielding to the years.

units.la: Duracinus] Servabilis uva, Plin. Fert aetatem vinum. Fert vetustatem, Cic. Fert annos; non fugit vinum, Quint. Stabilia mala. Lupinum patitur aevum in granario, Col. Servant poma nomen. Conservat notas vinum, Virg. Non perdit nomen vinum, Cat.
units.tr: Long-keeping] A grape that keeps (Plin.). Wine bears age. Wine bears old age (Cic.). It bears the years; wine does not flee (Quint.). Apples that last. Lupine endures age in the granary (Col.). Apples keep their name. Wine keeps its marks (Virg.). Wine does not lose its name (Cat.).

units.la: Durare diu] Durare pertinacissimè , Quint. Perennant fructus diutius, Col. Imber continuus tendit, Liv. Expetit ætatem aliquid, Plaut. Perstat hiems, Ovid. Viguit ad nostram ætatem. Manet mos memoriæ, Cic. Stat Troja, Virg. Prorogant tempus vestes, Plin. Pervigere, Tac. Annare, Macr. Continuare, Celf.
units.tr: To last long] To last most persistently (Quint.). Fruits last longer (Col.). A continuous rain stretches on (Liv.). Something seeks to last an age (Plaut.). Winter persists (Ovid.). It has flourished down to our age. Custom remains in memory (Cic.). Troy still stands (Virg.). Garments prolong their time (Plin.). To keep vigil through (Tac.). To last through the year (Macr.). To continue (Celsus).

units.la: Durescere] Guttæ durantur in grana. Lapidescere in duritiem. Duritiem induere. Usque in duritiem pumicis crassescente limo. Spissari duritie, Plin. Semen diuturnitate obdurescit, Varr. Subdurescunt grana, Col. Præduratur terra, Gell. Rigere ferro, Virg. Rigidari, Sen. Obducere callem, Cic. Solidari, Celf.
units.tr: To harden] Drops harden into grains. To turn to stone in hardness. To put on hardness. Until the mud thickens into the hardness of pumice. To become solid in hardness (Plin.). Seed hardens with age (Varr.). The grains harden somewhat (Col.). The ground is hardened beforehand (Gell.). To stiffen with iron (Virg.). To grow rigid (Sen.). To form a hardened path (Cic.). To solidify (Celsus).

units.la: Durities] Duritia adamantina. Centrum, in lignis & marmore partes duriores, Plin. Duritas, Cic. Soliditas tophi, Vitr. Robur saxi, Lucr. Duramen aquarum. Rigor auri, Id.
units.tr: Hardness] Adamantine hardness. The core, the harder parts in wood and marble (Plin.). Hardness (Cic.). The solidity of tufa (Vitr.). The strength of stone (Lucr.). The frozen hardness of waters. The stiffness of gold (Id.).

units.la: Durus] Edurus, Virg. Durus ad tactum. Solidum robur. Rigida quercus. Spissus ager, Id. Prædura gemma, Plin. Impenetrabilis silex, Lucr. Adamantinum saxum, Id. Intractabiles lapides, Plutar. Respuit secures, ictum ferri. Contumacius transmittit ferrum. Centrosum lignum, Plin. Materina terra, Cato. Callosa ova, Hor. Corneus, Perf. Fossore durior. Adamantinus. Adamante durior. Totus saxeus, Er.
units.tr: Hard] Very hard (Virg.). Hard to the touch. Solid strength. Stiff oak. A dense field (Virg.). A very hard gem (Plin.). Impenetrable flint (Lucr.). Adamantine stone (Lucr.). Intractable stones (Plutarch). It refuses axes and the blow of iron. It transmits iron more stubbornly. Centrose wood (Plin.). Hard earth of the mother (Cato). Callous eggs (Hor.). Horny (Pers.). Harder than a digger. Adamantine. Harder than adamant. Wholly stony (Er.).

units.la: Dux] Coryphæus, Cic. Caput, Ter.
units.tr: Leader] A chief, a head (Cic.). A head (Ter.).

units.la: Dux exercitus] Ductor, Imperator castrorum, Cic. Rector exercitus, Suet. Campiductor, Amm. Magister militiæ, Virg.
units.tr: Commander of an army] A leader, commander of the camp (Cic.). Ruler of the army (Suet.). Field-leader (Amm.). Master of the soldiery (Virg.).

units.la: Dysenteria] Dysenterica passio, Pallad. Tormina, Cic. Profluvium alvi. Morbus edacitatis, Cic. Vid. Alvus cita.
units.tr: Dysentery] A dysenteric affliction (Pallad.). Gripes (Cic.). A flux of the bowels. A disease of voracity (Cic.). See Swift bowels.

units.la: Dysuria] Urinæ cum difficultate cupiditas, Celf. Urinæ difficultas, Plin. Vesicæ morbus, Cic. Dysuricum pathos, Id.
units.tr: Dysuria] A desire to urinate with difficulty (Celsus). Difficulty in urinating (Plin.). A disease of the bladder (Cic.). A dysuric affliction (Cic.).

units.la: Dysuriacus] Cui ægre lotium it, Cato.
units.tr: Dysuriac] One for whom urine comes with difficulty (Cato).

units.la: E.
units.tr: E.

units.la: E Vid. Ex.
units.tr: E: See Ex.

units.la: E conspectu] E regione, & è contrariâ parte nobis est, Cic. Ex adverso, Plin. Ex adversum est fabrica. Ex adverius ei loco erant, Ter. Adversum, Plin. Ex adverso cœli. Contrà, Virg. Diversum cœli, Id. Erga, Plaut. Exante porticum, Apul.
units.tr: E conspectu: from the opposite side, on the other side from us, Cic. Opposite, Plin. The workshop lies opposite. Those were opposite to that place, Ter. Opposite, Plin. Opposite the sky. Against, Virg. Across the sky, Id. Towards, Plaut. In front of the portico, Apul.

units.la: E parvis initiis magna rerum incrementa] De parvâ scintillâ magnum sæpe concitatur incendium.
units.tr: E parvis initiis magna rerum incrementa: A great fire is often kindled from a small spark.

units.la: Ebenum] Hebenus, Virg.
units.tr: Ebenum: Ebony, Virg.

units.la: Ebibere] Exhaurire poculum, Liv. Terpotare laticem, Lucr. Epotare poculum. Obducere. Obbibere. Exsorbere sanguinem, Cic. Age effunde hoc citò in barathrum. Propere prolue cloacam. Medullam mihi lassitudo perbibit. Educere cirneam vel hirneam vini. Exantlare submerum, Plaut. Ducere pocula Lesbii, Hor. Exsiccare amphoram, Sen. Siccare poculum avidè, Mart.
units.tr: Ebibere: To drain a cup, Liv. To gulp down the liquor, Lucr. To drink off a cup. To drink up. To swallow down. To drink up blood, Cic. Come, pour this out quickly into the pit. Quickly wash out the sewer. Weariness has drunk up my marrow. To draw off a cask of wine. To empty the cask, Plaut. To drink the cups of Lesbian wine, Hor. To drain the jar, Sen. To gulp down a cup greedily, Mart.

units.la: Eblandiri aliquid] Blanditiis elicere aliquid. Eblandita suffragia, Cic. Electare, Plaut. Pellicere, Col. Expalpare aliquid ab aliquo, Pompon. Plaut.
units.tr: Eblandiri aliquid: To coax something out by flattery. Votes won by flattery, Cic. To entice, Plaut. To wheedle, Col. To wheedle something out of someone, Pompon. Plaut.

units.la: Ebrietas] Vinolentia. Vinarium crimen, Cic. Temulentia, Plaut. Crapula, Lucr. Potatus, Sen. Hilaris insania. Voluntaria insania, Lud. Viv.
units.tr: Ebrietas: Drunkenness. The charge of wine-bibbing, Cic. Intoxication, Plaut. Surfeit, Lucr. Heavy drinking, Sen. Merry madness. Voluntary madness, Lud. Viv.

units.la: Ebriosus qui libenter inebriatur] Vinosus, Plaut. Bibax. Bibosus, Gell. Bibulus, Hor. Doliaris anus. Lagenam dicas. Vinosissima est. Merobibus. Potator, Plaut. Crapulosus, Firm. Merobibulus, Sipont. Multimeri, Hor. Potor, Plin.
units.tr: Ebriosus qui libenter inebriatur: A drunkard, one who gladly gets drunk: a heavy drinker, Plaut. A wine-bibber. A tippler, Gell. A toper, Hor. An old woman who lives in the wine-cask; you might call her a flagon. She is a great drinker. A wine-guzzler. A drinker, Plaut. A glutton for drink, Firm. A wine-swiller, Sipont. A man who drinks many cups, Hor. A drinker, Plin.

units.la: Ebrius, potu plenus] Ebriolus. Ebriacus. Potus. Appotus. Madidus, Plaut. Vinolentus, temulentus, Cic. Benè potus, Var. Crapulæ plenus, Liv. Vini plenus, Ter. Potulentus, Suet. Crapulentus, Amm. Mersus vino, Sen. Hesterno vino sauciati, Justin. Vino sepultus, Virg. Vertigine tectum ambulat, & geminis exsurgit mensa lucernis, Juv. Caminus semper fumans.
units.tr: Ebrius, potu plenus: Tipsy, full of drink. Half-drunk. Drunk. Soaked in drink. Sodden, Plaut. Drunk with wine, sottish, Cic. Well drunk, Var. Full of carousing, Liv. Full of wine, Ter. Given to drink, Suet. Besotted, Amm. Drowned in wine, Sen. Wounded by yesterday's wine, Justin. Buried in wine, Virg. He walks about with his head reeling, and the table rises before him with twin lamps, Juv. A chimney always smoking.

units.la: Ebrius incautus] In vino veritas. Quod in animo sobrii, id in lingua ebrii.
units.tr: Ebrius incautus: In wine there is truth. What a man has in mind when sober, he has on his tongue when drunk.

units.la: Ebullire] Effervescit aqua, Cic. Circumfunditur, Plin.
units.tr: Ebullire: The water boils up, Cic. It spreads around, Plin.

units.la: Ebulum] Ebulus. Chamæacte. Helion. Actæa, Plin.
units.tr: Ebulum: Dwarf elder. Chamaeacte. Helion. Actaea, Plin.

units.la: Eburnus] Eburneus, Cic. Eburatus lectus, Plaut. Eburneolus, Cic. Eboreus codex, Vlp. Eborata sella, Lamp.
units.tr: Eburnus: Made of ivory, Cic. An ivory-inlaid couch, Plaut. A little ivory thing, Cic. An ivory book-case, Ulp. An ivory chair, Lamp.

units.la: Ecce] En ecce, Apul. Ecce autem. Ecce tibi. En hic est ille, Cic. Eccere atque, Plaut. Vah, Diomed. Habes, quæ tota mente petisti, Virg.
units.tr: Ecce: Behold, Apul. But behold. Look here. Here he is, that man, Cic. Lo and behold, Plaut. Bah, Diomed. Here you have what you sought with all your heart, Virg.

units.la: Eccum] Eccos. Eccistam. Ellum. Eccillum. Eccam, Plaut. Hem Davum tibi, Ter. Habemus hominem ipsum, Id.
units.tr: Eccum: Look there him. Look there her. Look there it. Look there that one. Look at her, Plaut. Here is Davus for you, Ter. We have the man himself, Id.

units.la: Echeneis, piscis] Remora, Plin. Odinolyon, Id. Remeligo, Fest. & Remiligo, Lamb.
units.tr: Echeneis, piscis: The remora fish, Plin. Odinolyon, Id. Remeligo, Fest., and Remiligo, Lamb.

units.la: Echo] Echea sonantia, Vitr. Sonorum imagines, Var. Filia aëris & linguæ, Auf. Repercussus vocis, Plin. Resultat vox. Respondent silvæ, Virg. Repercussæ clamoribus valles, Liv.
units.tr: Echo: Echoing places, Vitr. Images of sounds, Var. Daughter of air and tongue, Auf. The reflection of a voice, Plin. The voice resounds. The woods answer back, Virg. Valleys made to echo with shouts, Liv.

units.la: Eclipsis] Defectio solis, lunæ. Defectus solis, lunæ, Cic. Deliquium, obscuratio solis, lunæ. Labores siderum, Plin. Labores lunæ, Virg.
units.tr: Eclipsis: An eclipse of the sun or moon. A failing of the sun or moon, Cic. A fainting, an darkening of the sun or moon. The labours of the stars, Plin. The labours of the moon, Virg.

units.la: Ecquid audis? vid. Heus.
units.tr: Ecquid audis?: Do you hear? See Heus.

units.la: Ecstasis] Alienatio mentis (divinitus facta) Celf. Plin.
units.tr: Ecstasis: Alienation of mind (brought about by a god), Celf. Plin.

units.la: Ecstasin pati] Vis eum quædam abstraxisse à sensu mentis videtur. Cum à corpore animus abstractus divino instinctu concitatur. A mente discedit, Cic.
units.tr: Ecstasin pati: Some force seems to have drawn him away from the sense of his mind. When the soul, drawn away from the body, is stirred by divine impulse. It departs from the mind, Cic.

units.la: Eculeus, instrumentum examinandi sceleratos] Fidiculæ, Suet. Catasta, Prudent. Lectus ferreus, Isid. Tabularia, Sen. Tortum, Pacuv. Rota. Fabrica, Amm.
units.tr: Eculeus, instrumentum examinandi sceleratos: The rack, an instrument for examining criminals: torture cords, Suet. A scaffold, Prudent. An iron bed, Isid. A tablet, Sen. A twisting, Pacuv. A wheel. A machine, Amm.

units.la: Edacitas] Gula, Ovid. Implacata gula, Sallust. Immensa gula, Mart. Ingeniosa gula, Cic. Ingluvies, Ter. Liguritio vel Liguritio, Cic. Peredia, Plaut. Voracitas, Gulositas, Sipont.
units.tr: Edacitas: Gluttony, Ovid. Insatiable gluttony, Sallust. Immense gluttony, Mart. Ingenious gluttony, Cic. Greed, Ter. Gluttony or daintiness, Cic. Voracity, Plaut. Voraciousness, gluttony, Sipont.

units.la: Edax] Gulosus, Mart. Vorax, Ovid. Improbus anser, Virg. Ingluviosus, Fest. Multi cibi homo. Profundæ, intempestivæ, & sordidæ gulæ homo, Suet. Cui modulus vitæ est culina, Var. Intemperatus. Intemperatissima pe-ns, Cic. Maximæ escæ est, Plaut. Ventri & veneri deditus, tus, Cornel. à Lap. Parasito edacior. Vulture edacior, Er. Vid. Comed.
units.tr: Edax: Gluttonous, Mart. Voracious, Ovid. A greedy goose, Virg. Gorging, Fest. A man of many dishes. A man of profligate, untimely and filthy gluttony, Suet. One whose measure of life is the kitchen, Var. Intemperate. Most intemperate food, Cic. He is for eating only, Plaut. Given over to belly and lust, Cornel. à Lap. More greedy than a parasite. More greedy than a vulture, Er. See Comed.

units.la: Edentare] Everberare, Excutere, Elidere dentes, Cic. Exossare alicui os pugnis. Dentilegum aliquem facere, Plaut.
units.tr: Edentare: To knock out, shake out, or drive out the teeth, Cic. To break someone's jaw with blows of the fist. To make someone a tooth-picker, Plaut.

units.la: Edentulus] Exedentulus, Tertull. Edentatus, Macr. Defectus dentibus, Plin.
units.tr: Edentulus: Toothless, Tertull. Without teeth, Macr. Lacking teeth, Plin.

units.la: Edere, vid. Comedere. Esitare.
units.tr: Edere: See Comedere. Esitare.

units.la: Edere libros] Divulgare libros. Emittere aliquid dignum suo nomine. Pervulgare, Cic. Publicare librum, Plin. Iun. Dare in publicum aliquid ; in manus hominum, Plin. Juri humano publicare versus, Arnob. Vid. Exeunt libri.
units.tr: Edere libros: To publish books: to make a book known. To put forth something worthy of one's name. To spread abroad, Cic. To publish a book, Plin. Iun. To bring something before the public, into men's hands, Plin. To publish verses to human judgement, Arnob. See Exeunt libri.

units.la: Edicere aliquid] Imperare alicui tributum, Plaut. Irrogare alicui tributum, Hirt. Indicere tributum. Pronunciare bellum, Liv. Denunciare judicium. Decernere alicui supplicationem, Cic. Imponere alicui frumentum, Hirt. Imputare civitati terna millia, Plin. Iun. Injungere alicui onus, munus, Liv. Damnare aliquem tributis, Tacit.
units.tr: Edicere aliquid: To impose a tax on someone, Plaut. To levy a tax on someone, Hirt. To proclaim a tax. To declare war, Liv. To give notice of a trial. To decree a thanksgiving for someone, Cic. To impose corn on someone, Hirt. To charge a city with three thousand, Plin. Iun. To lay a burden or duty on someone, Liv. To condemn someone to taxes, Tacit.

units.la: Edictum] Diploma Cæsaris. Decretum, Cic. Edictio basilica, Plaut. Codicilli, Macr. Mandatum, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Edictum: An imperial charter. A decree, Cic. A basilica edict, Plaut. Documents, Macr. A command, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Ediscere artem] Rudem accipere, Cic. Rudem mereri, Mart. Edoctus belli artes sub magistro, Liv.
units.tr: Ediscere artem: To receive the discharge (from a trade), Cic. To earn a discharge, Mart. Trained in the arts of war under a master, Liv.

units.la: Ediscere memoriter] Mandare aliquid memoriæ : animis ac mentibus mandare. Perdiscere tanquam dictata. Ediscere ad verbum. Consequi artium scientiam. Addiscere, Cic.
units.tr: Ediscere memoriter: To commit something to memory: to entrust it to the mind and soul. To learn thoroughly as if dictated. To learn word for word. To acquire knowledge of the arts. To learn in addition, Cic.

units.la: Edisserere, vid. Enarrare.
units.tr: Edisserere: See Enarrare.

units.la: Edormire] Edormiscere somnum, Plaut. Satiari somno.
units.tr: Edormire: To sleep off, Plaut. To have one's fill of sleep.

units.la: Educare] Eduxit eam mater pro sua, Ter. Locus, ubi ille altus & edoctus est, Cic.
units.tr: Educare: She brought her up as her own, Ter. The place where he was reared and taught, Cic.

units.la: Educatio] Disciplina, Cic. Curatura, Ter. Alitura, Gell. Educatus, Ter. Nutrimentorum ejus locus, Suet. Nutritus pius, Sen.
units.tr: Educatio: Training, Cic. Care, Ter. Upbringing, Gell. A person brought up, Ter. The place of his nourishment, Suet. A devoted upbringing, Sen.

units.la: Educator] Altor. Alumnus pacis. Auctor pacis, Cic.
units.tr: Educator: A foster-father. A nursling of peace. A promoter of peace, Cic.

units.la: Educatrix] Nutrix. Altrix, Cic. Alumna omnium rerum terra, Plin. Alma tellus, Col.
units.tr: Educatrix: A nurse. A foster-mother, Cic. The earth, the nurse of all things, Plin. The kindly earth, Col.

units.la: Educere aliquem] Producere aliquem in prospectum populi, Cic. Ter.
units.tr: Educere aliquem: To bring someone forth into the view of the people, Cic., Ter.

units.la: Edulcare] Imbuere aliquid sapore, Quint. Indulcare, Eccles. 12.
units.tr: Edulcare: To season something with flavour, Quint. To sweeten, Eccles. 12.

units.la: Edulium, vid. Cibaria res. Ferculum.
units.tr: Edulium: See Cibaria res. Ferculum.

units.la: Edulis] Escaria uva, cibaria. In pabulo est. Est vescendo aliquid, Plin. Esculenta frusta,Cic. Ad escam uva,Col. Vescum papaver, Virg. Pabularis, Plin.
units.tr: Edulis: Edible grapes, food. It is in the fodder. It is good to eat something, Plin. Edible morsels, Cic. Grapes for eating, Col. The eating poppy, Virg. Fodder, Plin.

units.la: Edurare, molestum quid] Durare laborem, superare, Virg. Exantlare clades. Pertolerare. Exigere ærumnam, Plaut. Exsorbere difficultatem. Devorare molestiam,Cic. Concoquere, Liv. Sufficere dolori, Sen.
units.tr: Edurare, molestum quid: To endure trouble, to overcome, Virg. To go through disasters. To bear to the end. To bear to the end hardship, Plaut. To swallow down difficulty. To swallow down annoyance, Cic. To digest, Liv. To suffice for grief, Sen.

units.la: Effarcire aliquid] Confercire. Saburrare, Plin. Infercire, Suet. Differcire, Tac. Refercire libros fabulis, Cic. Distendere ventrem, Plaut. Stipare, Virg.
units.tr: Effarcire aliquid: To stuff, to cram. To fill with sand, Plin. To cram full, Suet. To stuff full, Tac. To cram books with fables, Cic. To distend the belly, Plaut. To crowd, Virg.

units.la: Effarcire se cibis] Ingurgitare se cibis, confertus cibo. Onustus cibo & vino, Cic. Implere se. Implere se nimium, Celf. Distentus coenâ, pabulô, Quint. Obsaturari alicujus rei, Ter. Gravis cibo & vino, Liv. Vino se & epulis sepelire, Sen.
units.tr: Effarcire se cibis: To gorge oneself with food, crammed with food. Loaded with food and wine, Cic. To fill oneself. To overfill oneself, Celf. Distended with dinner and fodder, Quint. To have one's fill of something, Ter. Heavy with food and wine, Liv. To bury oneself in wine and feasts, Sen.

units.la: Effatum] Enunciatum, quicquid enunciatur. Enunciatio. Pronunciatum. Pronunciatio, Cic.
units.tr: Effatum: Whatever is uttered. Utterance. Statement. Pronouncement, Cic.

units.la: Effectio] Factio testamenti, Cic. Cùm ab actu recesserunt, Quint.
units.tr: Effectio: The making of a will, Cic. When they have withdrawn from action, Quint.

units.la: Effector, vid. Factor.
units.tr: Effector: See Factor.

units.la: Effectus] Vires ad effectum dare, Prop. Effectas res vocat, Cic. Consilia primum, deinde Acta, posteà Eventus expecta. Res ipsa loquitur. Vis erumpit in actum. Eventus, &c. Eventum, Cic.
units.tr: Effectus: To give strength to an effect, Prop. He calls things effects, Cic. Consider the plans first, then the deeds, and afterwards wait for the outcome. The thing speaks for itself. Force breaks out into action. The outcome, etc. The result, Cic.

units.la: Ex effectu cognoscitur causa] Ex cantu dignoscitur ales. Ex ungue leo. Ex auribus asinus. Ex tinnitu olla. Ex vestigio Hercules. Ex fimbria vestis. Ex culmo spica.
units.tr: Ex effectu cognoscitur causa: The bird is known by its song. The lion by its claw. The ass by its ears. The pot by its ring. Hercules by his footprint. The garment by its fringe. The ear of corn by its stalk.

units.la: Effeminatè, vid. Effæminatè, &c.
units.tr: Effeminatè: See Effæminatè, etc.

units.la: Efferari] Degenerare in feritatem.
units.tr: Efferari: To degenerate into savagery.

units.la: Effervescere] Infervefieri, Scrib. Confervescere, Col. Infervescere. Inservere, Cat. Bullare, Id. Inæstuat bilis praecordiis, Hor.
units.tr: Effervescere: To begin to boil, Scrib. To boil up together, Col. To boil up. To seethe, Cat. To bubble, Id. Bile seethes in the breast, Hor.

units.la: Effetus, vid. Effætus.
units.tr: Effetus: See Effætus.

units.la: Efficacia] Efficacitas virium, Efficientia solis, Cic.
units.tr: Efficacia: The efficacy of powers, the effective power of the sun, Cic.

units.la: Efficaciter] Efficienter. Incantatione quàvis efficacius, Cic.
units.tr: Efficaciter: Effectively. More effectively than any incantation, Cic.

units.la: Efficax] Efficacissimum ; Præsentaneum remedium. Plin. Præsens remedium, Col. Efficiens causa, Cic. Operosa herba, Ovid.
units.tr: Efficax: Very effective; a ready remedy, Plin. A present remedy, Col. An efficient cause, Cic. A useful herb, Ovid.

units.la: Efficere] Perficere ; præstare aliquid, Cic. Effectum dare, Ter. Effectum propositum obtinere, Plin. Iun. Ad effectum adducere, Liv.
units.tr: Efficere: To accomplish; to bring something about, Cic. To give effect to, Ter. To attain the purpose proposed, Plin. Iun. To bring to effect, Liv.

units.la: Effigies] Ectypum, Sen. Forma ab exemplari sumpta, & operi imposita, Id.
units.tr: Effigies: A copy in relief, Sen. A form taken from a pattern and impressed upon the work, Id.

units.la: Effigiare] Exprimere exemplar, Plin. Iun. Conformare columnam, Vitr. Imitari penicillo, Cic. In exemplum operis aliquid assumere, Quint.
units.tr: Effigiare: To express a model, Plin. Iun. To shape a column, Vitr. To imitate with the brush, Cic. To take something as a pattern for a work, Quint.

units.la: Effingere] Manu fingere. Exprimere imitando. Informare aliquid, Cic. Exprimere similitudinem è membris alicujus, Plin. Assimulare aliquid, Quint. Vid. Comminisci.
units.tr: Effingere: To shape by hand. To express by imitating. To form something, Cic. To express a likeness from someone's limbs, Plin. To make something resemble, Quint. See Comminisci.

units.la: Efflagitare, vid. Deposcere.
units.tr: Efflagitare: See Deposcere.

units.la: Efflagitatio] Efflagitatus. Postulatio. Desiderium. Postulatum, Cic. Postulatus, Liv. Votum, Virg. Hinc respondere votis alicujus. Subscribere votis, Virg. Ovid.
units.tr: Efflagitatio: A vehement demand. A request. A longing. A thing demanded, Cic. A demand, Liv. A prayer, Virg. Hence to answer someone's prayers. To subscribe to prayers, Virg., Ovid.

units.la: Effictim] Intimè. Perliberaliter, Cic. Enixè, Cæs. Toto pectore amare aliquem ; ex animo. Medullitus amplecti aliquem. Oculitus, corde, animo, Viribus aliquid persequi, Plaut. Plus oculis meis amo aliquem, Catul. Te pectore toto accipio, Virg. Addictius, Tacit.
units.tr: Effictim: thoroughly, heartily. Very liberally (Cic.). Eagerly (Cæs.). To love someone with the whole breast, from the heart. To embrace someone from the marrow. With the eyes, with the heart, with the mind. To pursue something with all one's strength (Plaut.). I love someone more than my eyes (Catul.). I receive you with my whole breast (Virg.). More devotedly (Tacit.).

units.la: Efflorescere, vid. Florere.
units.tr: To blossom forth, see To flourish.

units.la: Effluentia] Effluvium humoris è corpore, Plin. Effluxio, Bud.
units.tr: Effluentia: a discharge of fluid from the body (Plin.). An effluxion (Bud.).

units.la: Effluere] Emanare. Exstillare. Exsaniari baccam olivæ patimur, Col. Eliquescere, Varr. Effunditur oculus ictu, Vlp.
units.tr: To flow out: to emanate, to drip out. We allow the berry of the olive to be drained (Col.). To melt away (Varr.). The eye is spilled by a blow (Vlp.).

units.la: Effodere] Eruere aurum terrâ, Ovid. Defodere, Col. Refodere, Plin. Excodicare, Fest. Exobruere, Apul.
units.tr: To dig out: to dig gold out of the earth (Ovid.). To bury (Col.). To dig up again (Plin.). To dig out (Fest.). To bury under (Apul.).

units.la: Effœminatè] Muliebriter ; animo fracto. Molliter ; abjectè. Parum fortiter ferre aliquid, Cic.
units.tr: Effeminately: in a womanish way, with a broken spirit. Softly, abjectly. To bear something with little courage (Cic.).

units.la: Effœminare aliquem] Enervare aliquem, Cic. Muliarare, Varr. Malacissare aliquem, Plaut. Mollire & resolvere aliquem, Sen. Frangere deliciis, Juv.
units.tr: To effeminate someone: to enervate someone (Cic.). To make someone womanish (Varr.). To soften someone (Plaut.). To melt and relax someone (Sen.). To break someone with pleasures (Juv.).

units.la: Effœminari] Puellascere, Pacuv. Fœmineo imperio regi; Non.
units.tr: To become effeminate: to behave like a girl (Pacuv.). To be ruled by a woman's authority (Non.).

units.la: Effœminatus] Effœminatissimus, Apul. Fractus, Plin.lun. Uxorius, Virg. Enervatus, Victor. Mulierosus, Malacut. Tymbanotriba, Plaut. Muliebris animus, Enn. Enervis, Enervus, Quint. Semivir, Liv. Eviratus, Mart. Spado tener, Iuv. Animi fluxioris, Suet. Elumbis, Fest. Delumbis, Pers. Mollitia & fluxu fluit, Mollis, omnia ad voluptatem corporis referens. Mulierarius. Cic. Mollis ac fœminei corporis animique homo, Plin. Mollitiâ vincens quamlibet mulierem, Hor. Moribus gallinis, Mart. Fluxiore cinctura cingitur. Male præcinctus, Suet. Plumâ, auriculâ infimâ, spongiâ mollior, Er.
units.tr: Effeminate: most effeminate (Apul.). Broken (Plin. iun.). Uxorious (Virg.). Enervated (Victor.). Womanizing (Malacut.). Tambourine-thumper (Plaut.). A womanish spirit (Enn.). Enervous (Quint.). Half a man (Liv.). Unmanned (Mart.). A tender eunuch (Juv.). Of a flabby spirit (Suet.). Loin-less (Fest.). Limp-loined (Pers.). Soft and flowing, referring everything to bodily pleasure. A man of women (Cic.). A man soft in body and mind, like a woman (Plin.). Conquering any woman by softness (Hor.). Hen-hearted in his ways (Mart.). Girt with a loose belt. Badly girded (Suet.). Softer than down, than a little ear, than a sponge (Erasmus).

units.la: Effœtus] Defœta senio arbor. Defatigatum solum, Col. Exoleta stirps. Expartæ pecudes. Exsuctiores solent esse segetes, Varr.
units.tr: Effete: a tree worn out by old age. Exhausted ground (Col.). A worn-out stock. Spent cattle. Crops are wont to be more exhausted (Varr.).

units.la: Effœtum fieri, vid. Sterilescere.
units.tr: To become effete, see To become sterile.

units.la: Effrenis] Infrenatus equus, Liv. Infrenis, Gell. Infrenus cursus, Col. Effrenatus, Cic. Defrenatus, Ovid.
units.tr: Unbridled: a horse not bridled (Liv.). Unbridled (Gell.). An unbridled course (Col.). Unbridled (Cic.). Unbridled (Ovid.).

units.la: Effringere] Perfringere repagula. Revellere fores. Vincula carceris rumpere, Cic. Refringere portas, Cæs. Perrumpere limina, Virg. Molliri fores, Tac. Discutere claustra, Petron.
units.tr: To break open: to burst through bars, to tear off doors. To break the chains of a prison (Cic.). To break open gates (Cæs.). To burst through thresholds (Virg.). To loosen doors (Tac.). To shake off bolts (Petron.).

units.la: Effrons, vid. Impudens.
units.tr: Shameless, see Impudent.

units.la: Effugere] Subducere se de circulo. Ducere se. Evolare ex insidiis. Subtrahere se. Colligere se de alicujus regno, Cic. Subterducere se. Promigrare, Plin. Suffugere ex stationibus. Prævertere fugâ metum supplicii, Liv. Nunquam evadere. Exauspicari è vinculis. Concedere à foribus, Plaut. Custodiis elapsus. Elabi pugnam, vincula, Tac. Secedere à lusu, Propert.
units.tr: To escape: to withdraw oneself from the circle, to lead oneself away, to fly out of ambushes, to withdraw oneself. To withdraw from someone's kingdom (Cic.). To slip away underneath. To emigrate (Plin.). To flee from posts. To avert by flight the fear of punishment (Liv.). Never to evade. To get free of chains. To withdraw from the doors (Plaut.). Escaped from custody. To slip away from battle and chains (Tac.). To withdraw from play (Propert.).

units.la: Effundere] Profundere lacrymas, Cic. Urna refundit aquas, Prop. Effutire, Donat. Quod montes nullos evergerent rivos, Liv. Progeritur urceis oleum. Frons aquas eliquans, Apul. Vergitur in terras solis ardor, Lucr. Efflat nimbas balæna, Plin.
units.tr: To pour out: to shed tears (Cic.). The urn pours forth its waters (Prop.). To blurt out (Donat.). Which mountains, not being there, would pour out streams (Liv.). Oil is poured out from jugs. Melting waters over the brow (Apul.). The heat of the sun is poured down upon the lands (Lucr.). The whale spouts forth clouds (Plin.).

units.la: Effuse] Ampliter. Affatim iisdem & homines vescuntur. Cumulatè explere, Cumulatissimè gratiam referre. Accumulatissimè gratiam polliceri. Eleganter acceptus est. Magnificè & splendide ornare convivium. Largè effuseque donare. Liberaliter, lautè vivere. Perliberaliter. Opiparè. Prolixè promittere. Pleno modio. Plenâ manu, Cic. Abundè, Lucr. Genialiter, Ovid. Rectè & dapsilè convivari. Abundantissimè coenam præbet, Suet. Largiter auferre, Hor. Pascuè, Apul. Lepidè accipiemur, Plaut. Locupletissimè muneratus, Spart. Opimè, Plaut. Munificè. Utraque manu. Soluto sinu, Sen. Benignè præbere, Ter.
units.tr: Lavishly: abundantly, plentifully. Men feed on the same things in plenty. To fill up copiously, to repay a favour most abundantly. To promise a favour most abundantly. He was entertained graciously. To adorn a feast magnificently and splendidly. To give generously and lavishly. To live generously and sumptuously. Very liberally. Richly. To promise at length.
