By the full measure. With a full hand (Cic.). Abundantly (Lucr.). Genially (Ovid.). To dine well and generously. He provides a most abundant dinner (Suet.). To carry off in large amounts (Hor.). Pasturally (Apul.). We shall be welcomed charmingly (Plaut.). Most richly rewarded (Spart.). Richly (Plaut.). Bountifully. With both hands. With loosened fold (Sen.). To give kindly (Ter.).

units.la: Egenus[ Egens. Egentissimus in suâ re. Egens omnibus rebus. Indigens. Egestate perditus & præditus, Cic. Defectus aquâ ciboque, Quint. Egens omnium rerum, Liv. Sis. Indigus alicujus rei, Virg.
units.tr: Needy: lacking, in want. Most needy in his affairs. Lacking all things. Wanting. Ruined by poverty and burdened with want (Cic.). Lacking water and food (Quint.). Lacking all things (Liv. Sis.). In need of something (Virg.).

units.la: Egenus extremè] Nec obolum habet, unde restim emat. Pedem ubi ponat, non habet.
units.tr: Utterly needy: he does not have a halfpenny with which to buy a rope. Where to set his foot, he does not have.

units.la: Egenus inter egentiores eminet] Inter cæcos regnat Strabus. Luscus in regione cæcorum rex est. Inter indoctos, qui semidoctus est, doctissimus habetur. Inter mendicos,qui paululum habet nummorum, Croesus est. In urbe cæcorum regnat lippus.
units.tr: Among the needy, the needier stands out: among the blind, Strabo reigns. A one-eyed man is king in the land of the blind. Among the unlearned, the half-learned is held most learned. Among beggars, whoever has a few coins is a Croesus. In the city of the blind the bleary-eyed rules.

units.la: Egere] Indigere consilii, adjumento. Desiderare. In egestate esse. In mendicitate vivere, Cic. Egetur acriter, Plaut. Opus est mihi dux, Cic. Opus sunt milites, Ter. Opus habere aliqua re, Col. Vid. Opus habere, miseria premi.
units.tr: To lack: to need counsel or help, to desire. To be in want. To live in beggary (Cic.). He badly needs a leader (Plaut.). I need a leader (Cic.). Soldiers are needed (Ter.). To have need of something (Col.). See To have need, to be pressed by misery.

units.la: Egere dat valere] Indigentia mater sanitatis.
units.tr: Want gives health: want is the mother of health.

units.la: Egestas] Defectus, Liv. Inopia. Egestas. Indigentia. Angustiæ rei familiaris, ærarii. Penuria amicorum. Necessitas, Cic. Coactus rerum necessitudine, Salust. Viduitas opum, copiarum, auxilii, Plaut.
units.tr: Poverty: lack (Liv.). Want. Penury. Need. Straitened circumstances of a household or treasury. Lack of friends. Necessity (Cic.). Compelled by the pressure of circumstances (Salust.). Being bereft of wealth, forces, help (Plaut.).

units.la: Egredi, vid. Exire.
units.tr: To go out, see To exit.

units.la: Egregiè, Egregius, vid. Eximiè, Eximius.
units.tr: Remarkably, remarkable, see Exceptionally, exceptional.

units.la: Eja, vid. Age.
units.tr: Come on, see Come on.

units.la: Eja autem.] Quid? malum! Quid? domum vestram! Ain' tandem carcer?Plaut. Cur non introeo in nostram domum, Mercur. Autem. Eja autem inimicos. Ego non tanquam meam? Tuam autem, furcifer? Pergin' malè loqui hero , homo impurissime ? Terentius.
units.tr: But come on.: What? Bad luck! What? Your house! Do you say so, prison? (Plaut.). Why should I not go into our house? (Mercur.). But, come on, the enemies! Am I not treating it as my own? Yours, rather, you gallows-bird? Will you keep speaking ill of your master, most filthy fellow? (Terentius.)

units.la: Ejaculari] Emittere arcu sagittam, Plin.
units.tr: To hurl: to shoot an arrow from a bow (Plin.).

units.la: Ejectio] Ejectus, us, Lucr. Exactio regum, Cic. Egestus, us, Sen. Egeries, Solin.
units.tr: Ejection: ejection (Lucr.). Expulsion of kings (Cic.). Voiding (Sen.). Excrement (Solin.).

units.la: Ejicere] Ejectare, Ovid. Extrudere furcâ. Projicere foras. Explodere aliquid: Evomere conchas. Exterminare, Cic. Eructat fluvius arenas, Virg. Expungere pupillum, Perf. Evallare. Evallefacere, Varr.
units.tr: To eject: to drive out (Ovid.). To thrust out with a fork. To throw forth. To hiss out something. To banish (Cic.). The river belches out sand (Virg.). To dispossess a ward (Perf.). To uproot (Varr.).

units.la: Ejulatio] Ejulatus. Vociferatio muliebris, Cic. Planctus fœmineus; cum planctu fœmineo mixtus clamor, Sen. Plangor fœmineus. Ululatus fœmineus, Virg. Ovid. Conclamatio & lamentatio, Tac.
units.tr: Wailing: women's shouting (Cic.). Women's lamentation; a shout mixed with women's lamentation (Sen.). Women's wailing, howling (Virg. Ovid.). Outcry and lamentation (Tac.).

units.la: Ejulare] Magnitudine dolorum ejulare. Ululare, Lucan. Complere auras ejulatibus, Ovid. Quiritare, Quint. Edere ploratum, Cic.
units.tr: To wail: to cry out from the greatness of one's pains. To howl (Lucan.). To fill the air with wailing (Ovid.). To shriek (Quint.). To utter lamentation (Cic.).

units.la: Elabi. vid. Evadere.
units.tr: To slip away, see To evade.

units.la: Elabitur verbum alicui] Excidit. Verbum ab aliquâ cupiditate prolapsum. Solet hoc ebullire nonnunquam. Effutita aliqua temere, Cic. Elapsa sunt verba, Ovid.
units.tr: A word slips from someone: it falls out. A word slipped out from some passion. This is wont to boil over at times. Something said rashly (Cic.). Words have slipped out (Ovid.).

units.la: Elaborare aliquid industriâ] Elucubrare aliquid, Cæs. Elucubrari. Elimare. In quadrum redigere orationem, sententiam. Procudere linguam. Quadrare orationem, Cic. Expolire, exasciare opus aliquod, Plaut. Evigilare aliquid, Ovid. Polire agrum, Enn. Ad unguem facere, castigare, Hor.
units.tr: To work out something by diligence: to polish something by lamplight (Cæs.). To lucubrate, to refine. To reduce a speech or sentence to a square. To hammer out one's tongue. To square a speech (Cic.). To smooth out a work (Plaut.). To keep watch over something (Ovid.). To polish a field (Enn.). To finish to the nail, to correct (Hor.).

units.la: Elaboratio] Elaborata concinnitas, Cic. Interpolatio. Politura telæ, Plin. Politio frumenti, Cat. Depolitio agri, Varr.
units.tr: Elaboration: elaborate neatness (Cic.). Interpolation. The polishing of a web (Plin.). The polishing of grain (Cat.). The clearing of a field (Varr.).

units.la: Elaboratum aliquid industriâ] Elaborata diligenter oratio. Diu multumque in manibus fuit liber. Præcultus & præparatus habitus. Retractatus liber, oratio. Limatus, Cic. Multæ operæ & laboris res, Cæs. Quadrata compositio orationis, Quint. Decoctus, Perf. Laboratus arte, Virg. Everganeus, Vitr. Amussitatus, Plaut. Emussitatus, Fest. Ad amussim factus, Gell. Politus ager, Enn. Expolitum frumentum, Col.
units.tr: Something worked out by diligence: a speech elaborated with care. The book was for a long time and much in hands. A carefully prepared and prearranged appearance. A book or speech gone over again and again. Filed (Cic.). A matter of much work and labour (Cæs.). A squared composition of speech (Quint.). Boiled down (Perf.). Wrought by art (Virg.). Everganeus (Vitr.). Smoothed by the rule (Plaut.). Planed (Fest.). Made exactly to the rule (Gell.). A polished field (Enn.). Polished grain (Col.).

units.la: Elapidare agrum] Lectionem lapidum expedire, Col. Exossare terram, Perf. Delapidare, Cat.
units.tr: To clear a field of stones: to pick out the stones (Col.). To free the earth of bones (Perf.). To remove stones (Cat.).

units.la: Elargiri alicui] Totum se in aliquem profundere. Largitiones maximas facere. Ærarium vel patrimonium effundere in aliquem, Cic. Si ignotis impertit, eluet facilius, Iun.
units.tr: To lavish on someone: to pour oneself wholly out upon someone. To make very great largesses. To pour out one's treasury or patrimony upon someone (Cic.). If he bestows on strangers, he will the more easily be washed clean (Juv.).

units.la: Elatio, Elatus. vid. Superbia. Superbus.
units.tr: Elation, elated, see Pride. Proud.

units.la: Electio] Electus necis,Ov. Lectio senatus, Suet. Optio, Cic.
units.tr: Election: a chosen death (Ov.). The selection of the senate (Suet.). Option (Cic.).

units.la: Electio plurium] Calculis omnium. Plurium calculus vicit.
units.tr: Election by the majority: by the votes of all. The vote of the majority has prevailed.

units.la: Elector Imperii] Septemvir, Lipf.
units.tr: Elector of the Empire: a Septemvir (Lipf.).

units.la: Electus] Selectus. Cunctorum suffragiis factus consul, Cic. Optivus, Hor.
units.tr: Elected: chosen. Made consul by the votes of all (Cic.). Preferred (Hor.).

units.la: Eleemosyna] Stips, Ovid. Sportula, Rader. Collecta, Id. Collatitia, vel Collectitia pecunia. Collatitia stips, Amm.
units.tr: Alms: a coin (Ovid.). A dole (Rader.). A collection (Id.). Money collected by contribution. A contributed dole (Amm.).

units.la: Elegans] Excultus homo, omni vitâ & cultu lautus, mundus homo, Politus, Cic. Lautiusculus, Apul. Praetersus, Plaut. Excuratus homo, Id. A Deo factus. Concinnus. Scitus, Cic.
units.tr: Elegant: a cultivated man, refined in all his life and manner, a neat and polished man (Cic.). Rather finely dressed (Apul.). A dandy (Plaut.). A carefully groomed man (Plaut.). Made by God. Neat. Knowing (Cic.). Groomed man (Id.).

units.la: Eleganter] Pereleganter. Enucleatè & Atticè, Cic. Lautè, munditer vestitus, Plaut. Conversè, Cat. Purgatè. Non. Mundulè, Apul. Mundè, Titinn.
units.tr: Elegantly: most elegantly. Neatly and in the Attic manner (Cic.). Carefully dressed (Plaut.). Conversely (Cat.). Purely (Non.). Neatly (Apul.). Neatly (Titinn.).

units.la: Elegantia] Munditia. Vitae cultus cum elegantia & copiâ delectat, Cic. Mundities, Catul. Lautitia, est munditia in vestitu & cibo, Plin.
units.tr: Elegance: neatness. A cultivated way of life delights with elegance and abundance (Cic.). Neatness (Catul.); luxury is neatness in dress and food (Plin.).

units.la: Elegantia sermonis] Atticus sal. Vid. Sermo elegans.
units.tr: Elegance of speech: Attic wit. See Elegant speech.

units.la: Elegantiæ nihil] Nullo apparatu.
units.tr: Nothing elegant: without any display.

units.la: Non est in tanto } corpore mica salis. Nulla in tam magno est }
units.tr: There is not a grain of salt in so great a body. In one so large there is none.

units.la: Elementa] Prima, genitalia corpora, Lucr. Quatuor naturæ, ex quibus omnia constant. Corpora principiorum. Rerum matrices, nutrices, populatrices. Elementaris mundi rotæ quatuor.
units.tr: Elements: first, generating bodies (Lucr.). The four natures from which all things are made. Bodies of the principles. Mothers, nurses and destroyers of things. The four wheels of the elemental world.

units.la: Elephas] Elephantus, Cic. Barrus, Hor. Bos luca, Plin. Turres armatorum, Id.
units.tr: Elephant: an elephant (Cic.). A barrus (Hor.). A Lucanian ox (Plin.). Towers of armed men (Id.).

units.la: Elevare, vid. Attollere.
units.tr: To raise, see To lift up.

units.la: Elicere aliquem] Elicere aliquem ad aliquid præmiis. Invitare voluptatibus, Cic. Electare aliquid (scil. ab aliquo) Plaut. Carminibus clausas excantare puellas, Propert. Evocare aliquem præmiis, Quint. Delectare hostem, Non. Extrahere serpentes cantu, Plin.
units.tr: To entice someone: to entice someone to something by rewards. To invite with pleasures (Cic.). To lure something from someone (Plaut.). To charm enclosed girls with songs (excantare) (Propert.). To summon someone with rewards (Quint.). To lure an enemy (Non.). To draw out serpents by song (Plin.).

units.la: Elices, vid. Lira.
units.tr: Elices, see Lira.

units.la: Elidere, vid. Excudere.
units.tr: Elidere, see Excudere.

units.la: Eligere] Legere locum, tempus idoneum,Ovid. Deligere ex omni numero. Adoptare sibi patronum. Adhibere delectum. Seligere,Cic. Præoptare aliquam rem alteri, Liv. Ut ex collegis optaret, quem vellet. Desumere sibi aliquem, Id. Censuram facere, Plin. Secernere nucleos, Col. Capere locum oculis.
units.tr: Eligere] To choose a place or a suitable time, Ovid. To pick out from the whole number. To take a patron for oneself. To hold a selection. To select, Cic. To prefer one thing to another for someone, Liv. So that he might choose from among his colleagues whomever he wished. To take someone for oneself, Id. To hold the census, Plin. To separate the kernels, Col. To seize a place for the eyes.

units.la: Eligere ad munus] Deligere magistratum. Legere in senatum aliquem. Creare consulem, magistratum. Facere consulem, Cic. Cooptare sibi collegas, Suet. Designare consulem, Salust. Dicere Dictatorem, Liv.
units.tr: Eligere ad munus] To choose for an office: to appoint a magistrate. To enrol someone in the senate. To create a consul, a magistrate. To make someone consul, Cic. To co-opt colleagues for oneself, Suet. To designate someone consul, Sall. To name a dictator, Liv.

units.la: Eliminare aliquem, vid. Extrudere.
units.tr: Eliminare aliquem, see Extrudere.

units.la: Elinguis, sine lingua] Elinguatus,Cornel.Front. vid.Mutus.
units.tr: Elinguis, without a tongue] Elinguatus, Cornel. Front.; see Mutus.

units.la: Eliquare aliquem humorem] Defæcare vinum, Plin. Fæculentum liquorem clarum reddere, Pallad. Examurcare oleum, Apul. Liquare. Hor. Depurare, Sipont.
units.tr: Eliquare aliquem humorem] To clarify wine, Plin. To make a cloudy liquid clear, Pallad. To strain oil, Apul. To melt down, Hor. To purify, Sipont.

units.la: Eliquescere, humorem emittere] Delacrymat vitis. Exsudat amurcam oliva. Exsaniatur bacca olivæ, Col. Succescit terra madida imbribus, Arnob.
units.tr: Eliquescere, humorem emittere] The vine weeps. The olive sweats out its lees. The olive berry is drained, Col. Earth soaked with rain grows moist and gives off water, Arnob.

units.la: Elixare. vid. Coquere.
units.tr: Elixare. see Coquere.

units.la: Elixum] Coctum, Fest.
units.tr: Elixum] Boiled, Fest.

units.la: Elixus] Madidus, Plaut. Jurulentus, Celf. Jussulentus, Apul. Percoctus, Plin.
units.tr: Elixus] Sodden, Plaut. Brothy, Cels. Full of broth, Apul. Thoroughly cooked, Plin.

units.la: Elocare filiam] Locare in matrimonio. Collocare filiam alicui; in matrimonium; in matrimonio, Cic. Collocare filiam nuptui, Cæs. Dare filiam nuptum. Dare alicui in manum virginem, Ter. Dare in nuptias, Id. Dare in matrimonium, Liv. Locare nuptu filiam,Plaut. nuptiis, ad Her. Maritare filiam, Suet.
units.tr: Elocare filiam] To place a daughter in marriage. To marry a daughter to someone, into marriage, in wedlock, Cic. To give a daughter in marriage, Caes. To give a daughter to be married. To give a virgin into a husband's hand, Ter. To give in wedlock, Ter. To give in marriage, Liv. To give a daughter in marriage, Plaut. To give in marriage with a wedding, ad Her. To marry off a daughter, Suet.

units.la: Elocare fundum. vid. Locare.
units.tr: Elocare fundum. see Locare.

units.la: Eloquens] Architectus verborum, Logodædalus. Perfectus Orator, Cic. Tam facundus, ut nemo sit ei conferendus. Quis hoc uno facundior? Eloquentiæ princeps. Alter Cicero, Er. Rhetor. Dicendi artifex, opifex. Cic. Opifex persuadendi. Elocutrix. Quint. Orandi validus, Tac. Vid. Disertus. Facundus.
units.tr: Eloquens] An architect of words, a craftsman of speech. A perfect orator, Cic. So eloquent that no one can be compared with him. Who is more eloquent than this man? Prince of eloquence. Another Cicero, Er. Rhetor. A master of speaking, a craftsman, Cic. A craftswoman of persuasion. A female speaker, Quint. Strong in speaking, Tac. See Disertus. Facundus.

units.la: Eloquentia] Rhetoris ars. Copiosè loquens sapientia. Eloquendi vis. Copia dicendi. Facultas dicendi singularis. Summa vis dicendi Vis oratoria. Ratio dicendi, Cic. Facundia, Tac. Scientia orandi. Ars oratoria, Quint. Vid. Loquentia.
units.tr: Eloquentia] The art of the rhetorician. Wisdom speaking fluently. The power of speaking. Abundance of speech. Unusual ability to speak. The highest power of speaking; oratorical power. A method of speaking, Cic. Fluency, Tac. Knowledge of oratory. The art of oratory, Quint. See Loquentia.

units.la: Eloquentia magnam vim habet] Citò persuadebis, si benè dicas.
units.tr: Eloquentia magnam vim habet] You will persuade quickly if you speak well.

units.la: Eloquentiæ studere] Imbuere linguam lepore eloquentiæ.
units.tr: Eloquentiæ studere] To steep the tongue in the charm of eloquence.

units.la: Eloquentia singularis] Attica eloquentia. Eloquium liquidum, melleum, Ausón.
units.tr: Eloquentia singularis] Attic eloquence. A smooth, honeyed eloquence, Ausonius.

units.la: Eloquentia vana, vid. Loquentia.
units.tr: Eloquentia vana, see Loquentia.

units.la: Eloqui] Efferre aliquid non indecenter. Depromere verba, Quint. Promere voces, Cic. Expromere quid sentiam, Liv. Enunciare. Proloqui. Effari, Cic.
units.tr: Eloqui] To bring something out without impropriety. To bring out words, Quint. To utter sounds, Cic. To express what I think, Liv. To announce. To speak forth. To speak, Cic.

units.la: Elucere, in lucem & conspectum venire] Elucet lumen ingenii. Enitet acumen alicujus. Pellucet honestum ex virtutibus. Vultus mores indicat, Cic. Eminet foras animus, Id. Proditur furor, Vitr. Sen. Prorumpit cupiditas, Cic.
units.tr: Elucere, in lucem & conspectum venire] The light of talent shines forth. The keenness of someone gleams. Honour shines through from virtues. The face reveals the character, Cic. The mind projects outward, Id. Madness is revealed, Vitr. Sen. Desire bursts forth, Cic.

units.la: Eluctari difficultates] Eluctari per multa impedimenta. Ereptare ex pecuniâ, Sen. Erepere ruinis domus, Id. Emergere de paludibus; Liv. Emergere se ex malis, Corn. Nep. Replicare tricam, Plaut. E scopulis emergere. Enavigare. Vid. Extricare aliquid.
units.tr: Eluctari difficultates] To struggle through many hindrances. To wrest oneself free from money, Sen. To snatch a house from its ruins, Id. To emerge from marshes, Liv. To extricate oneself from evils, Corn. Nep. To unravel a tangle, Plaut. To emerge from the rocks. To sail clear. See Extricare aliquid.

units.la: Eludere aliquem] Te verò quemadmodum elusurus sit, videre jam videor. Fingere causas, Ter. Nectere causas, Virg. Incertis responsis aliquem implicare, Liv. Vid. Evitare.
units.tr: Eludere aliquem] And indeed I seem already to see how he will slip away from you. To invent excuses, Ter. To weave excuses, Virg. To entangle someone in uncertain answers, Liv. See Evitare.

units.la: Elugere, vid. Lugubris.
units.tr: Elugere, see Lugubris.

units.la: Elutriare vinum] Transfundere vinum in alia vasa, Cato. Defundere in vasa oleum. Deliquare vinum in alia vasa, Col. Diffundere vinum. Decapulare oleum, Plin. Detrullare, Apit. Trajicere in alia vasa, Varr. Deplere, Cat. Iun.
units.tr: Elutriare vinum] To pour wine into other vessels, Cato. To pour oil into vessels. To decant wine into other vessels, Col. To pour out wine. To skim oil, Plin. To draw off, Apic. To transfer into other vessels, Varr. To empty, Cat. Iun.

units.la: Eluvio] Eluvies; Alluvio. Proluvies, Cic. Exundatio, Plin. Proluvium, Ter. Interluvies fluminis, Amm. Restagnatio, Plin.
units.tr: Eluvio] Flood-wash; alluvion. A washing away, Cic. An overflowing, Plin. A flood, Ter. A flooding between the banks of a river, Amm. A stagnation, Plin.

units.la: Em, vid En.
units.tr: Em, see En.

units.la: Emaceratus] Peresus languoribus, Catul. Quem amor tabe peredit, Virg. Fœdior corporis habitus. Pallore & macie peremti, Liv.
units.tr: Emaceratus] Worn out by sicknesses, Catul. Whom love has consumed with decay, Virg. A more hideous state of body. Destroyed by pallor and leanness, Liv.

units.la: Emaciare] Emacrare. Ad maciem reducere obesum corpus, Plin. Ad maciem ultimam redigere, Col. Tenuare vultum, Propert. Macerare fame, Liv. Permacerare, Enn. Tenuare armenta macie, Virg.
units.tr: Emaciare] To make lean. To reduce a fat body to leanness, Plin. To reduce to the utmost leanness, Col. To thin the face, Propert. To waste with hunger, Liv. To waste away completely, Enn. To thin the herds with leanness, Virg.

units.la: Emancipare, vid. Subjicere.
units.tr: Emancipare, see Subjicere.

units.la: Emancipatio] Mancipatio, Vlp. Traditio rei, mancipi, aut nexu, Cic.
units.tr: Emancipatio] Mancipation, Ulp. The transfer of a thing, whether by mancipium or by nexum, Cic.

units.la: Emanare, vid. Effluere.
units.tr: Emanare, see Effluere.

units.la: Emanere] Abesse, Cic. Abstinere curia, Suet. Emansorem agere.
units.tr: Emanere] To be absent, Cic. To keep away from the senate-house, Suet. To act as an emansor.

units.la: Emax] Coëmptionalis, Plaut.
units.tr: Emax] Relating to buying, Plaut.

units.la: Præstat esse emacem, quàm vendacem] Vendacibus resperciunt.
units.tr: It is better to be a haggler than a liar] Liars are caught out by their own tricks.

units.la: Emblema] Pictura loquens. Pictura poësis tacita.
units.tr: Emblema] A speaking picture. Poetry is a silent picture.

units.la: Embolimus mensis] AdditITIUS, Bud. Intercalaris, Macr.
units.tr: Embolimus mensis] Additional, Bud. Intercalary, Macr.

units.la: Embryum] Mola. Partus inchoatus, Plin. Tumor carneus, Actuar. Pecus, Firmic. (Veteres, quicquid non erat homo, id pecus appellabant.)
units.tr: Embryum] A mass. An incipient birth, Plin. A fleshy swelling, Actuar. Cattle, Firmic. (The ancients called whatever was not a man "pecus," cattle.)

units.la: Emedullare, vid. Exprimere per vim.
units.tr: Emedullare, see Exprimere per vim.

units.la: Emendabilis] Capax ad præcepta animus, Ovid. Bonâ disciplinâ exercitus, Cic. Disciplinosus, Cat. apud Gell.
units.tr: Emendabilis] A mind receptive to precepts, Ovid. Trained by good discipline, Cic. Disciplined, Cato apud Gell.

units.la: Emendare aliquem] Meliorem facere, Sen. Ad frugem perducere, corrigere. In viam reducere, Plaut. Reparare in melius vetustate sublapsâ. Reformare mores, Plin. Restaurare, Tac. Corrigere aliquem ad frugem, Plaut.
units.tr: Emendare aliquem] To make someone better, Sen. To bring someone to honest living; to correct. To lead back onto the way, Plaut. To restore to a better state after it has decayed with age. To reform morals, Plin. To restore, Tac. To correct someone to uprightness, Plaut.

units.la: Emendari] Ad bonam frugem se recipere. Mutare mentem, (scil. malam). Frugi jam factus est. Redire in viam. Ad bonitatem venire. Revocare se ad mediocritatem, Cic. Applicare se ad frugem, Plaut.
units.tr: Emendari] To return to good living. To change one's mind (namely from a bad one). He has now become honest. To return to the right way. To come to goodness. To recall oneself to moderation, Cic. To apply oneself to uprightness, Plaut.

units.la: Emendationem à se ipso ordiri] A laribus inchoandum. Medice cura teipsum. Increpa te ipsum. Vir bonus ipse sibi spongia.
units.tr: Emendationem à se ipso ordiri] Begin from the household hearth. Physician, heal yourself. Reprove yourself. A good man is a sponge to himself.

units.la: Emere] Emptitare, Plin. Mercari aliquid à; de aliquo pretio. Nundinari, Cic. Comparare aliquid carius, Suet. Conciliare benè vel malè, Plaut. Empturire, Varr.
units.tr: Emere] To haggle, Plin. To buy something from someone at a price. To haggle over prices, Cic. To buy at a higher price, Suet. To procure well or badly, Plaut. To buy up, Varr.

units.la: Emerere] Meritare, Plin. Emereri stipendium, Plaut. Per-merere, Stat. Magna operæ pretia mereri. Stipendia facere, Liv.
units.tr: Emerere] To earn, Plin. To earn one's pay, Plaut. To earn fully, Stat. To earn great worth of service. To serve in campaigns, Liv.

units.la: Emergere] Emersit, totumque se ejecit, atque extulit, Cic. Efferre caput undis, Col. Submersus equus non exstitit, Cic. Superenatare, Lucan.
units.tr: Emergere] He rose up, threw himself clear and lifted himself out entirely, Cic. To raise the head above the waves, Col. The drowned horse did not come up again, Cic. To swim above the surface, Lucan.

units.la: Emeritum stipendium] Enavatæ operæ premium, Tac. Præmia meritorum, Hor. Præmium pro industriâ, Cic. Pecu-lium castrense, Vlp. Parta labore militiæ, Iuv. Operæ pretium, Liv. Vid. Stipendium.
units.tr: Emeritum stipendium] The reward of service fully performed, Tac. Rewards of merit, Hor. A reward for diligence, Cic. Military savings, Ulp. Won by the labour of soldiering, Juv. The worth of the service, Liv. See Stipendium.

units.la: Emeritus] Emeritus Marte (miles) Lucan. Emeritus est stipendiis. Accepit rudem, Cic. Rudem meritus est, Mart. Donatus rude, Hor. Rudiarius, Suet. Exauctoratus, Tac.
units.tr: Emeritus] A soldier who has earned his discharge by Mars, Lucan. He has completed his term of service. He has received the wooden sword, Cic. He has earned the wooden sword, Mart. Given the wooden sword, Hor. A discharged gladiator, Suet. Dismissed from service, Tac.

units.la: Emicare] Erumpit ignis. Exoritur honestum ex virtu-tibus, Cic. Renitent gemmæ. Eluctatur flamma fornaci-bus, Plin. Erumpunt se radii inter nubila, Virg.
units.tr: Emicare] Fire bursts forth. Honour rises out of virtues, Cic. Gems gleam. Flame struggles out of the furnaces, Plin. Rays break through the clouds, Virg.

units.la: Emigrare, vid. Migrare.
units.tr: Emigrare, see Migrare.

units.la: Eminens] Eminulus. Prominulus, Var. Iul. Cap. Prominens, Liv. Protectus, Bud. Perf. Protentus, Priscian. Pro-stans, Lucr. Extumidus, Varr. Extuberans, Plin. Vid. Prominens.
units.tr: Eminens] Slightly projecting. Protruding, Var. Iul. Cap. Projecting, Liv. Jutting out, Bud. Perf. Stretched out, Prisc. Standing forth, Lucr. Swollen, Varr. Bulging, Plin. See Prominens.

units.la: Eminens. (2.) vid. Conspicuus.
units.tr: Eminens. (2.) see Conspicuus.

units.la: Eminere] Prominere, Supereminere extra aquam, Plin. Exstare è terrâ : super terram, Col. Exserit herba cacumen ex humo, Ovid. Exstare ab humo, Plin. Exsistit corpore sudor, Lucr.
units.tr: Eminere] To project, to stand up above the water, Plin. To stand out from the earth, above the ground, Col. The herb thrusts its top out of the soil, Ovid. To stand out from the ground, Plin. Sweat breaks out of the body, Lucr.

units.la: Eminere, esse notabilem] Præminere, vel Præeminere aliis. Signa ferre, Sen. Digito monstrari, Plaut. Excellere præ-ter cæteros. Enitere cunctis, Cic. Supereminet omnes vi-ros, Virg. Vid. Antecellere.
units.tr: Eminere, esse notabilem] To stand out above others. To carry the standards, Sen. To be pointed at with a finger, Plaut. To excel beyond the rest. To stand out above all, Cic. He towers above all men, Virg. See Antecellere.

units.la: Eminentia] Prominens littoris, Tac. Exstantia, Col. Ecpho-ra, Vitr. Umbo montis, Stat. Procursus urbis angulo-sus, Plin.
units.tr: Eminentia] A jutting headland of the shore, Tac. Projecting parts, Col. A projection, Vitr. The bulge of a mountain, Stat. A jagged projection of a city, Plin.

units.la: Eminentissimus] Primæ classis, Gell. Flos populi. Præcel-lentissimus omnium. Omnium gentium, & omnis memo-riæ clarissimum lumen, Cic. Optimæ, primæ notæ, Col. Primarius vir, Plaut. Potissima nobilitas, Stat. Prima laus illi est, Plin. Apprimus, Virg. Vid. Anteferendus.
units.tr: Eminentissimus] Of the first class, Gell. The flower of the people. The most excellent of all. The brightest light of every nation and of all memory, Cic. Of the best and first repute, Col. A leading man, Plaut. The chief nobility, Stat. He has the first praise, Plin. Foremost, Virg. See Anteferendus.

units.la: Eminus] Deprocul aspicere, Plaut. E longinquo, Plin. Longè prospicere, Cic. Intervallo magno sequi, Caf. Procul de rupe videre aliquem, Virg. A limine salutare disciplinas, Sen.
units.tr: Eminus] To see from a distance, Plaut. From afar, Plin. To look far ahead, Cic. To follow at a great interval, Caes. To see someone from a cliff far off, Virg. To greet the disciplines from the threshold, Sen.

units.la: Emissarius, vid. Explorator.
units.tr: Emissarius, see Explorator.

units.la: Emittere ex aliquo loco] Dimittere reum, Plin. Effundere carcerem (incarceratos) in aliquem. Emittere è custodiâ, de carcere, è manibus, Cic.
units.tr: Emittere ex aliquo loco] To release an accused man, Plin. To pour out prisoners into a place. To send out of custody, out of prison, out of the hands, Cic.

units.la: Emollire] Mollire cibum dentibus, Cic. Præmollire femina, mentes, Quint. Remollire terram, Col. Ah nimium ferus es! malacissandus es, Plaut. Commitigare caput alicui, Ter. Inflectere sensus alicujus, Virg. Inflectere aliquem lacrymis, Stat.
units.tr: Emollire] To soften food with the teeth, Cic. To soften women and minds beforehand, Quint. To soften the earth, Col. Ah, you are too savage! You must be tamed, Plaut. To soothe someone's head, Ter. To bend someone's feelings, Virg. To move someone to tears, Stat.

units.la: Emolumentum, vid. Commodum.
units.tr: Emolumentum, see Commodum.

units.la: Emungere, vid. Mungere.
units.tr: Emungere, see Mungere.

units.la: Emphatica verba] Fulmina verborum.
units.tr: Emphatica verba] Thunderbolts of words.

units.la: En] Ecce, Ter. Ecce tibi. Em hic est ille, Cic.
units.tr: En] Look, Ter. Look there. Here, this is that famous man, Cic.

units.la: En tibi] En sume, Cornel. Gall. Cape hoc flagellum, Ter. Accipe, Plaut. Capsis, Cic. Cape hoc sis. Accipe sis argentum, Tene sis, Plaut. Sume Catelle tibi, Hor. Accipin' argentum? Plaut.
units.tr: En tibi] Here, take it, Cornel. Gall. Take this whip, Ter. Receive it, Plaut. Take it, Cic. Take this, if you please. Take the money, please; hold it, Plaut. Take this, little dog, Hor. Do you take the money? Plaut.

units.la: Enarrabilis] Explicabilis res, Cic. Effabilis, Apul.
units.tr: Explicable: a matter that can be explained, Cic. Expressible, Apul.

units.la: Enarrare] Denarrare aliquid alicui, Ter. Hor. Exponere rem ordine, Prosequi rerum ordinem. Edisserere aliquid, Digerere mandata alicujus. Explicare causas rerum. Exprimere sensus animi. Efferre aliquid. Eloqui cogitata mentis. Enunciare, Effingere aliquid verbis. Expromere alicujus crudelitatem, odium, Cic. Omnem rem modò Seni, quo pacto se haberet, enarravimus ordine, Ter. Edissertare. Expedire capita rerum, Plaut.
units.tr: To relate: to tell something to someone, Ter. Hor. To set out a matter in order; to follow the order of things. To explain something at length; to set out a person's commands in order. To explain the causes of things. To express the feelings of the mind. To bring something out. To utter the thoughts of the mind. To announce; to give something form in words. To bring out someone's cruelty or hatred, Cic. We have just related to old Senex, in order, how everything stood, Ter. To explain fully. To unravel the main points of a matter, Plaut.

units.la: Enarratio] Explicatio rerum. Enodatio nominum. Explicatus difficilis naturæ Deorum. Interpretatio juris. Explanatio portentorum. Expositio, Cic. Commentarium. Interpretamentum Latinæ linguæ, Gell. Commentum, Prisc.
units.tr: Explanation: an explanation of things; an unfolding of names; an explanation of the difficult nature of the gods; the interpretation of law; an explanation of portents. Exposition, Cic. Commentary. An interpretation of the Latin language, Gell. Invention, Prisc.

units.la: Enatare] Enare, Liv. Denatare alveo, Hor.
units.tr: To swim out: to swim away, Liv. To swim away from the channel, Hor.

units.la: Encomium, vid. Laudatio.
units.tr: Encomium, see Praise.

units.la: Encyclopædia] Orbis doctrinæ, Quint. Encyclios disciplina, Vitr.
units.tr: Encyclopaedia: a circle of learning, Quint. Encyclic discipline, Vitr.

units.la: Enervis, vid. Debilis.
units.tr: Enervated, see Weak.

units.la: Enervare, vid. Debilitare,
units.tr: To enervate, see To weaken.

units.la: Enim, vid. Nam.
units.tr: Enim, see Nam.

units.la: Eniti] Adhibere nervulos; omnem machinam, Omnia facere, ut. Obniti, Cic. Omnia experiri, Id. Cæs. Adniti omni ope, Plin. Summa omnia facere, Lucil. Intendere animum in rem aliquam, Liv. Intendere animum & studium. vid. Curato.
units.tr: To strive: to bring up the little sinews; to do every machine's work, to do everything so that. To strive against, Cic. To try everything, Id. Cæs. To strain with every resource, Plin. To do everything in full, Lucil. To direct one's mind to some matter, Liv. To direct one's mind and zeal. See Take care.

units.la: Enixè] Quam ego credo, manibus pedibusque obnixè omnia facturum, Ter. Enixissimè juvare, Suet. Magno conatu studioque agere aliquid. Omni ope atque opere eniti. Toto corpore, atque omnibus unguiculis. Contentius. Contento studio. Intensius petere. Remis velisque. Velis equisque. Equis & quadrigis. Summis viribus, medullitus contendere. Omnibus nervis; Cic. Summâ ope niti, Salust. Omnibus opibus experiri. Ex summis opibus ire mihi te opitulatum. Pro se quisque. Remigio veloque, quantum potes, Plaut. Tenaciter urget fortuna, Ovid. Certatim me omnes amant. Instanter petere. Instantissimè, Plin. Iun. Totius corporis nixu, Quint.
units.tr: Earnestly: I believe he will do everything with hands and feet, Ter. To help most earnestly, Suet. To act on something with great effort and zeal. To strive with all one's resources and work. With the whole body and every fingernail. More keenly. With eager zeal. To seek more intently. With oars and sails. With sails and horses. With horses and chariots. To strive with all one's strength, to press on from the depths. With all one's sinews, Cic. To strive with the greatest resources, Sall. To try with all one's means. You came to help me with your utmost resources. Each for himself. With oar and sail, as hard as you can, Plaut. Fortune presses on relentlessly, Ovid. All men love me eagerly. To seek urgently. Most urgently, Plin. Iun. With the effort of the whole body, Quint.

units.la: Enixus] Impensus, Suet. Preces impensissimæ. Intentus animus. Contentus cursus, Cic.
units.tr: Strained: applied with force, Suet. Most urgent prayers. An intent mind. A strained course, Cic.

units.la: Enormiter aliquid facere] Offendere ad montes.
units.tr: To do something outrageously: to stumble against the mountains.

units.la: Enotare aliquid] Adnotare aliquid cursim, Plin. Iun. Subscribere, Suet. Subnotare aliqua verba; Mart. Notare ad memoriam aliquid, Cic. Excerpere, Cic.
units.tr: To note something: to jot something down hastily, Plin. Iun. To subscribe, Suet. To mark some words beneath, Mart. To note something for memory, Cic. To excerpt, Cic.

units.la: Enucleatè. vid. Expresse.
units.tr: Clearly, see Expressly.

units.la: Enumerare] Enumerare per singula. Percensere numerando, Cic. Persequi numeris aliquid, Quint. Recensere ad numerum, Col. Percensere numerum legionum, Tac. Obire numero, Cic. Traloqui tuas impuritias nemo potest, Plaut. Retexere noxas, Stat.
units.tr: To enumerate: to enumerate one by one. To count over by numbering, Cic. To pursue by number, Quint. To review by number, Col. To count over the number of legions, Tac. To go through in number, Cic. No one can recite your impurities, Plaut. To unfold offences, Stat.

units.la: Enumeratio] Dinumeratio, Cic. Consectatio in numerum generum, Plin. Recensio, Bud.
units.tr: Enumeration: a counting over, Cic. A pursuit of kinds into a number, Plin. A review, Bud.

units.la: Enunciatum, vid. Effatum.
units.tr: Pronouncement, see Saying.

units.la: Eò, vid. Illuc.
units.tr: Thither, see Thither.

units.la: Ephebus] Adolescentulus. Extremâ pueritiâ adolescens, Cic. Miracidium, Fest. Parectatus, Lucil. Catastus, Vitr.
units.tr: Youth: a young lad. A young man at the very end of boyhood, Cic. Miracidium, Fest. Parectatus, Lucil. Catastus, Vitr.

units.la: Ephemeris, vid. Diarium.
units.tr: Diary, see Journal.

units.la: Ephippiatus, qui epipphio utitur.] Sagmarius, Isid. lustra-tus, Virg.
units.tr: Saddled, one who uses a saddle-cloth: a pack-horse, Isid. Lustratus, Virg.

units.la: Ephippium] Sella equestris, Sidon. Sagma, Rhodin. Scordiscus, Turneb.
units.tr: Saddle: a riding seat, Sidon. A pack-saddle, Rhodin. Scordiscus, Turneb.

units.la: Epicedium] Nenia, Varr. Cantus funebris, Cic. Elegus, Hor. Elegia, Ovid. Elegidion, Perf. Mortualia, Plaut. Mortuaria glossaria. Præficarum voces, Gell. Monodia, Iun. Rob.
units.tr: Funeral song: a dirge, Varr. A song for the dead, Cic. Elegus, Hor. Elegia, Ovid. Elegidion, Perf. Words of mourning, Plaut. Mourning glossaries. The cries of hired mourners, Gell. A monody, Iun. Rob.

units.la: Epicureus, vid. Voluptuarius.
units.tr: Epicurean, see Pleasure-seeker.

units.la: Epigramma, vid. Inscriptio.
units.tr: Epigram, see Inscription.

units.la: Epilepsia, vid. Caducus morbus.
units.tr: Epilepsy, see Falling sickness.

units.la: Epilepticus] Comitialis homo, Plaut. Caducus, Firm. Morbus, qui sputatur interdum, ei venit. Eum morbum mihi esse, ut qui me opus sit insputarier, Plaut.
units.tr: Epileptic: a man struck by a fit, Plaut. One who falls down, Firm. A disease in which one at times spits. I have that disease, so that I need to be spat upon, Plaut.

units.la: Epilogus, vid. Clausula.
units.tr: Epilogue, see Conclusion.

units.la: Episcopa, sedes Episcopi] Episcope, Crom. Episcopium, Bud.
units.tr: Bishop's see: Episcope, Crom. Episcopium, Bud.

units.la: Episcopalis] Pontificius, Pontificialis, Cic.
units.tr: Episcopal: pontifical, papal, Cic.

units.la: Episcopatus] Pontificatus, Cic. Antistitium, Mart. Pontificium, Gell.
units.tr: Episcopate: pontificate, Cic. Office of the priesthood, Mart. Pontificate, Gell.

units.la: Episcopus] Pontifex, Cic, Protomysta, Sidon. Antistes legis Christianæ, Amm.
units.tr: Bishop: pontiff, Cic. Protomysta, Sidon. A leader of the Christian law, Amm.

units.la: Epistola] Literæ, Literulæ. Libellus. Libelli, Cic. Tabellæ, Plaut. Epistolium, Catul. Charta salutatrix, Mart.
units.tr: Letter: a missive, a short note. A pamphlet. Pamphlets, Cic. Writing tablets, Plaut. A little letter, Catul. A greeting card, Mart.

units.la: Epistolicè] Per literas colloqui. Literis appellare. Absens exponam audacius, Cic. Scripto adire, Tac. Tabellis obsignatis agere.
units.tr: By letter: to converse by letter. To address by letter. I shall speak more boldly in absence, Cic. To approach in writing, Tac. To transact business with sealed tablets.

units.la: Epitaphium] Eloquium sepulchri, monumenti. Laus mortui sepulchro versibus incisa. Sepulchrum, Cic. Titulus sepulchri, Sil. Titulus monumenti, Plin. Iun. Nomen signatum saxo, Ovid.
units.tr: Epitaph: the words of a tomb or monument. Praise of the dead cut into the tomb in verse. A sepulchre, Cic. The inscription of a tomb, Sil. The title of a monument, Plin. Iun. A name carved in stone, Ovid.

units.la: Epithalamium] Nuptiale carmen, Catul. Fescennini versus, Fest. Liv. Hymen, Stat. Hymenæus, Ter. Talassio, Talassius, Talassus, Catul. Mart.
units.tr: Epithalamium: a wedding song, Catul. Fescennine verses, Fest. Liv. Hymen, Stat. Hymenaeus, Ter. Talassio, Talassius, Talassus, Catul. Mart.

units.la: Epotare, vid. Ebibere.
units.tr: To drink off, see To drink up.

units.la: Epulari] Saliarem in modum epulari. Hilarem in modum epulari. Apparare, instituere convivia, Cic. Agitare convivia. Hilarem sumere diem, Ter. Obsonare pollucibiliter, Plaut. Obsonitare, Cat. Vid. Convivari.
units.tr: To feast: to feast in the manner of the Salii. To feast in a merry way. To arrange and hold banquets, Cic. To spend a merry day, Ter. To provide a lavish spread, Plaut. Obsonitare, Cat. See To dine together.

units.la: Epularis] Convivalis, Liv. Coenatorius, Mart. Genialis dies, Iuv. Genianum triclinium, Varr.
units.tr: Festive: of a banquet, Liv. Of the dining room, Mart. A festive day, Juv. A dining room, Varr.

units.la: Epulatio, vid. Compotatio.
units.tr: Feasting, see Drinking party.

units.la: Epulo, vid. Convivator.
units.tr: Feast-giver, see Host.

units.la: Equa] Equila, Varr.
units.tr: Mare: a little mare, Varr.

units.la: Equorius medicus] Veterinarius. Veterinariae medicinae peritus, Col. Mulcenedicus, Firmic.
units.tr: Horse doctor: a veterinarian. One skilled in veterinary medicine, Col. A horse physician, Firmic.

units.la: Eques] Equestris ordinis homo. Equestri loco ortus, natus, Cic. Eques auratus; à rege creatus, & calcaribus aureis donatus, vid. Nobilis.
units.tr: Knight: a man of the equestrian order. Born of equestrian rank, Cic. A gilded knight, created by the king and presented with golden spurs; see Noble.

units.la: Equidem, vid. Certè.
units.tr: Indeed, see Certainly.

units.la: Equiso] Domitor, agitator equorum, Cic. Exercitator equorum. Equitarius, Firm. Desultor, Varr.
units.tr: Horse-breaker: a tamer, a driver of horses, Cic. A trainer of horses. Equitarius, Firm. Desultor, Varr.

units.la: Equitare] Vehi in equo, Cic. Vehi equo, Fest. Invehi equo. Ferri equo, Virg.
units.tr: To ride: to be carried on a horse, Cic. To be carried on horseback, Fest. To ride on horseback. To be borne on a horse, Virg.

units.la: Equitabilis] Vectarius equus, Varr.
units.tr: Rideable: a horse for riding, Varr.

units.la: Equitatio] Atterere equitatu femina, Plin. Peragratio itinerum. Profectio, Cic. Vectatio equi, Suet.
units.tr: Riding: to wear down a woman by riding, Plin. A journeying over distances. A setting out, Cic. Riding a horse, Suet.

units.la: Equitatus] Copiæ equestres, Cic. Equites, Plin.
units.tr: Cavalry: cavalry forces, Cic. Horsemen, Plin.

units.la: Equus] Equinum genus, pecus, Col. Celsior in campo sonipes, Luc.
units.tr: Horse: the equine kind, livestock, Col. A swift-hoofed steed high on the plain, Luc.

units.la: Eradicare] Exstirpare radices. Explantare. Exherbare. Radicitus effodere, Col. Evellere fibras radicum. Stirpitus radicem exigere, Cic. Evellere radicitus, Vlp. Cum imis stirpibus evellere. Ab radice altâ revellere, Virg.
units.tr: To root out: to pull up the roots, to tear out the roots. To weed out. To dig up by the roots, Col. To pluck out the fibres of the roots. To draw out the root completely, Cic. To tear up by the roots, Ulp. To pull out with the deepest stumps. To tear away from the deep root, Virg.

units.la: Eradicatio] Exstirpatio filicum frequens, Col.
units.tr: Eradication: frequent rooting out of ferns, Col.

units.la: Eradere] Distringere & eradere muscum, Col. Radere nomen alicujus in fastis, Tac.
units.tr: To scrape out: to scrape and wipe away moss, Col. To erase someone's name from the calendar, Tac.

units.la: Erasus, vid. Depositus ab officio.
units.tr: Erased, see Removed from office.

units.la: Eremita] Anachoreta, Isid.
units.tr: Hermit: an anchorite, Isid.

units.la: Erga] Ad. Adversum. Ad se versum, Cic. Supernè tendit non in terram, Suet. Versus. Horsum, Cic. Advorsum, Virg.
units.tr: Towards: toward; against. Turned toward oneself, Cic. Stretches upward, not to the ground, Suet. Turned. Hither, Cic. Against, Virg.

units.la: Ergastulum] Fustitudinæ. Ferricrepinæ insulæ. Pistrinum, Plaut.
units.tr: Workhouse: a place of the cudgel; the island of the clanking chains. A mill, Plaut.

units.la: Ergo] Proinde. Proin. Igitur, Ter. Quamobrem. Quapropter. Quocirca. Quas ob rēs. Itaque, Cic. Ergo igitur, Apul.
units.tr: Therefore: accordingly. Therefore, Ter. For which reason. Wherefore. On account of which. Hence, Cic. Therefore, then, Apul.

units.la: Erigere] Sublevare ad pedes stratum, Ovid. Arrigere comas, Virg. Levare in sublime, Plin. Subrigere, vel Surrigere, Liv. Suberigere, Sil.
units.tr: To raise: to lift up what has been laid low, Ovid. To raise the hair on end, Virg. To lift on high, Plin. To set upright, Liv. To raise up, Sil.

units.la: Eripere aliquid] Extorquere arma è manibus. Exprimere pecuniam, Cic. Exsculpere prædam leoni, Plaut. Mordicus evellere aliquid, Hor. Vid. Extorquere.
units.tr: To snatch away: to wrest weapons from the hands. To extract money, Cic. To wrench prey from a lion, Plaut. To pull something away with the teeth, Hor. See To extort.

units.la: Erogare, vid. Impendere. Expendere.
units.tr: To spend, see To expend. To lay out.

units.la: Erogatio, vid. Dispensatio. Quastura,
units.tr: Distribution, see Dispensing. Quaestorship.

units.la: Errabundus] Erraticus. Erroneus, Col. Homo de viâ, Catul. Vid. Vagus.
units.tr: Wandering: roaming. Erroneous, Col. A man off the road, Catul. See Vagrant.

units.la: Errare] Decipi, duci errore. Labi per errorem. In errore esse. In errorem induci, rapi. Objectus est mihi error, Cic. Decerravi sententiâ, Col. Errore labi, Quint. Errore teneri. Falli opinione. Rapi, inferri in fraudem. Hallucinari. Delirare in aliquâ re, Cic. Frustrari se, Hor.
units.tr: To err: to be deceived, to be led astray by error. To slip by mistake. To be in error. To be led into error, to be carried off. A mistake has been charged against me, Cic. I have strayed from my opinion, Col. To slip through error, Quint. To be held in error. To be misled in judgement. To be drawn into deceit. To be mistaken. To rave about some matter, Cic. To deceive oneself, Hor.

units.la: Errare valdè] Errare toto cœlo. Errare totâ regione. Longè avius à verâ ratione vagaris. Procul avius erras.
units.tr: To go far wrong: to err across the whole sky. To err over the whole region. You wander far from sound reason. You stray far from the way.

units.la: Errare errorem alicujus] Laborat morbo Manichæi, &c.
units.tr: To hold someone's error: he labours under the disease of Manichaeus, etc.

units.la: Errare humanum est] Cuique mortalium suus attributus est error.
units.tr: To err is human: each mortal has his own error allotted to him.

units.la: Errantium diligentia] Benè currunt, sed extra viam.
units.tr: The diligence of wanderers: they run well, but outside the road.

units.la: Erro, vid. Vagabundus.
units.tr: To wander, see Vagabond.

units.la: Error] Erratum. Erratio. Mendum. Menda, Cic. Vitium, Plin. Hallucinatio, Non. Senticetum errorum.
units.tr: Error: a mistake. A wandering. A blunder. Blemishes, Cic. A fault, Plin. Hallucination, Non. A thicket of errors.

units.la: Errorem agnosco] Non putâram, Cic.
units.tr: I acknowledge the error: I had not thought so, Cic.

units.la: Erubescere] Erubescere malis, Ovid. Ruborem mihi aliquid evocat, Sen Vehementer erubesco, rubeo, Cic. Hærere humo. Vid. Pudesieri. Pudet me.
units.tr: To blush: to blush at evils, Ovid. Something calls a blush to my face, Sen. I blush vehemently, Cic. To cling to the ground. See To be ashamed. I am ashamed.

units.la: Erubescendus, vid. Pudendus.
units.tr: Shameful, see Disgraceful.

units.la: Eruca, vid. Volvox.
units.tr: Rocket, see Volvox.

units.la: Eructare, vid. Ructare.
units.tr: To belch, see To belch up.

units.la: Erudire aliquem] Exercere, Excolere, Informare ad humanitatem manitatem. Inficere artibus. Expolire & hominem reddere. Elaborare in aliqua re. Recoquere hominem, Cic. Recolere ingenium, Plin. Procudere ingenium, linguas, Amm. Mercurium sculpere. Vid. Docere. Exercere.
units.tr: To train someone: to exercise, to cultivate, to form to humanity. To imbue with the arts. To polish and make a man. To labour at some matter. To re-cook a man, Cic. To restore talent, Plin. To hammer out talent and languages, Amm. To sculpt Mercury. See To teach. To train.

units.la: Eruditio, pro habitu] Ars liberalis. Doctrina. Scientia Dialecticorum. Studium agri colendi. Facultas oratoris. Disciplina juris civilis. Ratio bene vivendi, Cic.
units.tr: Learning, as a state: the liberal arts. Learning. The science of the dialecticians. The study of tilling the fields. The skill of the orator. The discipline of civil law. The way of living well, Cic.

units.la: Eruditio, pro actu erudiendi, vid. Institutio.
units.tr: Education, as the act of teaching, see Instruction.

units.la: Eruditor] Exercitator, Plin. Exercitor, Plaut.
units.tr: Trainer: one who exercises, Plin. A trainer, Plaut.

units.la: Eruditulus, vid. Semidoctus.
units.tr: Half-learned, see Semi-learned.

units.la: Eruditus] Pereruditus. In omnibus artibus politus. Instructus magnarum artium disciplinis. In arte & facultate excellit. Vir praeclara eruditione atque doctrina. Est ingenio praestanti, & eruditione perfecta, Cic. Animata Bibliotheca. Vid. Doctus.
units.tr: Learned: very learned. Polished in all the arts. Furnished with the disciplines of the great arts. Excelling in art and skill. A man of outstanding learning and erudition. He is of outstanding talent and perfect learning, Cic. A living library. See Learned.

units.la: Eruditus potest esse, licet vili vestitu amictus] Saepe sub obscuro palliolo latet sapientia.
units.tr: He may be learned although he is wrapped in shabby clothing: wisdom often lies hidden under a plain cloak.

units.la: Eruere aliquid occulti] Ego in hoc triduo, aut terra aut mari alicunde evolvam id argentum tibi. Exterebrare, Id. Conruspari consilia in pectore, Plaut. Evestigare, Sen.
units.tr: To dig out something hidden: In these three days I will somehow dig up that money for you, from land or from sea. To bore out, Id. To ferret out plans from the breast, Plaut. To track out, Sen.

units.la: Erumpere] Proripere se foras. Projicere se ex urbe. Ejicere se e sylvis. Evolare & impetum facere, Cic. Provolare, Liv. Proruere se foras, Ter. Dare se foras, Lucr. Eruptionem facere, Caes. Prosilire ex, Liv. Effundi, Id. Excursionem facere. Ruere portis, Virg.
units.tr: To burst forth: To rush out of doors. To throw oneself out of the city. To hurl oneself out of the woods. To fly out and make an attack, Cic. To rush forward, Liv. To dash outside, Ter. To come out of doors, Lucr. To make a sortie, Caes. To leap forth from, Liv. To pour out, Id. To make a sally. To rush through the gates, Virg.

units.la: Eruncare, vid. Runcare.
units.tr: Eruncare: see Runcare.

units.la: Eruptio] Excursio militum, hostium. Decursionibus vastat loca, Cic. Procursus militum temerarius, Liv. Procursatio, Id. Procursio, Quint. Discursio praedatoria, Amm.
units.tr: Sally: A sortie of soldiers or of the enemy. He lays waste the places with raids, Cic. A rash rush of soldiers, Liv. A running out, Id. A running forward, Quint. A plundering raid, Amm.

units.la: Eruptor] Procursator. Excursator, Liv.
units.tr: Sallier: A skirmisher. A raider, Liv.

units.la: Esca] Illecebra, Cic. Illicium, Varr. Cibus, Plaut. Cibarium, Col.
units.tr: Bait: An allurement, Cic. A lure, Varr. Food, Plaut. Fodder, Col.

units.la: Esculentus, vid. Edulis.
units.tr: Edible: see Edulis.

units.la: Esitare] In pabulo alicui est aliquid, Plin.
units.tr: To feed upon: Something is fodder to someone, Plin.

units.la: Esse] Tenere aliquam personam, sustinere. Agere Pastorem &c. Gerere consulatum, &c. Sustinere aliquid muneris. Fungi officio, Cic.
units.tr: To be: To hold a certain character, to sustain it. To act as shepherd, etc. To hold the consulship, etc. To bear some office. To discharge a duty, Cic.

units.la: Est pro] Habet vicem antidoti. Adimplet vicem. Supplet, obtinet, explet, reddit, efficit vicem alicujus rei. Obtinet vim medicamenti. Valet pro antidoto, Plin. Cedit pro, Col. Est tanti, Cic. Complet tres duces, Claud. Pensat, Repræsentat vicem olei, Plin.
units.tr: Stands for: It takes the place of an antidote. It fills the role. It supplies, holds, fulfils, renders, or effects the place of something. It has the force of a medicine. It serves as an antidote, Plin. It gives way for, Col. It is worth so much, Cic. It makes up three commanders, Claud. It balances, or represents the place of oil, Plin.

units.la: Esto, quod esse possis] Aulœdus sit, qui Citharœdus esse non possit. Est aliquid prodire tenus, si non datur ultrà. Bovem si nequeas, asinum agas.
units.tr: Be what you can be: Let him be a lute-player who cannot be a harpist. It is something to go forward as far as one may, if no further is granted. If you cannot get an ox, drive an ass.

units.la: Esuriens] Esurio. Esurialis, Plaut. Esuritor, Mart. Latrans stomachus, Hor. Ipsâ fame esurientior, Esuritione esurientior, Er. Famelicus, Plaut. Vid. Famelicus.
units.tr: Hungry: To be hungry. Ravenous, Plaut. Ravening, Mart. A barking stomach, Hor. Hungrier than hunger itself, hungrier than starvation, Erasm. Famished, Plaut. See Famelicus.

units.la: Esuries] Esuritio, Mart. Esurigo, Varr. Rabies ventris, Poëticè.
units.tr: Hunger: Starvation, Mart. Craving, Varr. The raging of the belly, poetically.

units.la: Esurire] Adesurire. Hunc hominem curculio exercet. Huic homini curculio est exercitor, Plaut. Urgeri fame, Liv. Fame laborare, Col. Fames appellat, Sen. Latrat ei stomachus, vel, Latranti est stomacho, Hor. Fatigat aliquem edendi rabies, Virg.
units.tr: To be hungry: To be very hungry. A weevil plagues this man. A weevil is his tormentor, Plaut. To be pressed by hunger, Liv. To suffer from hunger, Col. Hunger drives him on, Sen. His stomach barks at him, or, his stomach is barking, Hor. The raging of appetite harasses someone, Virg.

units.la: Esurire diu molestum] Fames & mora bilem in naso conciunt.
units.tr: Hunger and delay are hard to bear: Hunger and delay stir up bile in the nose.

units.la: Et] Que. Atque. Ac. Juxta, &c. Æquè, ac, perinde. Cum. (Remo cum fratre Quirinus.) Item. Itemque. Et autem. Quoque. vel, Cic.
units.tr: And: Que. Atque. Ac. Along with, etc. Equally, as, just as. With (Remus with his brother Quirinus). Likewise. And likewise. And moreover. Also, or, Cic.

units.la: Et, &, ex, &c. Et doctus, & pius] Est vir tam doctus, quam probus. Vir est doctus juxtà ac bonus. Vir est non minùs probus, quàm literatus. Vir est non inferior literis quàm moribus. Vir est ex æquo probus atque doctus. Vir est non minore probitate quàm aliâ doctrinâ præditus. Vir est quemadmodum doctus, ita & integer. Vir est haud secius eruditus ac probus. Vir est ut doctus, ita & probus. Vir est optimus, idemque doctissimus. Vir est pari vel doctrinâ, vel probitate præditus. Vir est non tantùm eruditus, sed & integer. Vir est præter summam eruditionem etiam optimus. Vir est de quo dubites doctior ne sit an melior. Vir est, qui literas æquavit cum vitæ sanctimonia. Vir est, cujus eruditioni respondet morum sanctimonia, Erasm.
units.tr: And, &, from, etc. Learned and pious: He is as learned as he is upright. The man is learned just as he is good. He is no less upright than he is literate. He is not inferior in learning to his morals. He is equally upright and learned. He is endowed with no less uprightness than with other learning. He is not only learned, but also upright. He is, beyond his great learning, also the best of men. He is a man of whom one may doubt whether he is the more learned or the better. He is one who has matched his letters with holiness of life. He is one whose holiness of conduct matches his learning, Erasm.

units.la: Et dives, & probus] In hoc fortuna cum probitate facit paria. Et deformis, & vitiosus] Parùm erat deformem esse, nî mores formâ dignos addidisset. Nihil erat deformi esse vultu, nisi moribus etiam esset deterrimis, Erasm. Vid. Tamquàm.
units.tr: Rich and upright: In this case fortune matches uprightness. And ugly and vicious: It was not enough to be ugly unless he had added morals worthy of his looks. It was nothing to have an ugly face, unless one also had the worst morals, Erasm. See Tamquam.

units.la: Et catera, vid. Catera.
units.tr: And the rest: see Catera.

units.la: Etesiæ] Etesiarum prodromi flatus, Gell. Aquilones, quos prodromos appellant, Plin. Etesia flabra Aquilonum, Gell.
units.tr: Etesian winds: The blasts which are the forerunners of the Etesian winds, Gell. The north winds, which they call forerunners, Plin. The Etesian gusts of the north winds, Gell.

units.la: Ethica] Philosophia moralis. Pars Philosophiæ de moribus. Ethice, Cic.
units.tr: Ethics: Moral philosophy. The part of philosophy concerning morals. Ethics, Cic.

units.la: Ethnicus] Gentilis, Isid. Gentes. Nationes, Arnob. Gentilitas, Sipont.
units.tr: Heathen: Gentile, Isid. The Gentiles. The nations, Arnob. Heathenism, Sipont.

units.la: Etiam] Quoque, Cic. Ergo, Plaut.
units.tr: Also: Likewise, Cic. Then, Plaut.

units.la: Etiam si sic] Ne sic quidem male.
units.tr: Even if it is so: Not even so is it bad.

units.la: Etsi, vid. Quamvis.
units.tr: Although: see Quamvis.

units.la: Evacuare] Exinanire naves. Exhaurire aerarium. Eversum & extersum fanum, Cic. Exinanire corpus morbidum fluvio sanguinis, Plin. Exenterare marsupium, Plaut.
units.tr: To empty: To drain ships. To exhaust the treasury. A temple overturned and swept clean, Cic. To drain a diseased body by a flood of blood, Plin. To empty out a purse, Plaut.

units.la: Evadere, vid. Evitare.
units.tr: To escape: see Evitare.

units.la: Evagari] Vagor quocunque volo, Cic. Exspatiantur equi, nulloque inhibente per auras ignotae regionis eunt. Populatur flamma capillos, Ovid. Exspatior equis oblitis ad metam tendere, Id. Bacchari, Lucr.
units.tr: To wander: I wander wherever I wish, Cic. The horses range freely and go through the air of an unknown region with no one to restrain them. The flame ravages the hair, Ovid. I, having let loose my horses, race to the turning-post, Id. To rave, Lucr.

units.la: Evagari longius à proposito] Digredi à causa, de causa, de cursu orationis. Digredi ab eo, quod propositeris. Egredi à proposito. Recedere paululum à causa. Deflectere & declinare à proposito. Aberrare à proposito, Cic. Divertio Redeamus, unde divertimus, Id. Averti, Liv.
units.tr: To wander far from the subject: To depart from the cause, from the matter, from the course of the speech. To digress from what was proposed. To go out from the subject. To withdraw a little from the case. To turn aside and deviate from the subject. To stray from the subject, Cic. Let us return to where we turned aside, Id. To be turned away, Liv.

units.la: Evagatio] Digressio à proposito, à proposita oratione. Excursio orationis, Cic. Excursus, Plin. Egressus, Tac. Egressio, Quint. Diverticulum, Juv. Diverticulum fabulae. Ecbasis, Serv.
units.tr: Digression: A departure from the subject, from the course of the speech. A running out of the speech, Cic. A digression, Plin. A going out, Tac. An outgoing, Quint. A byway, Juv. A digression in a story. An episode, Serv.

units.la: Evaginare ensem] Educere gladium è vagina. Distringere gladium, Cic. Nudare gladium. Expedire tela, Liv. Stringere gladium, Virg. Exuere ense vaginà. Exserere ensem, Stat. Ducere ensem, Sen.
units.tr: To unsheathe a sword: To draw a sword from its scabbard. To bare a sword, Cic. To strip a sword, to bare a sword. To draw weapons, Liv. To brandish a sword, Virg. To strip the sword from its scabbard. To unsheathe the sword, Stat. To draw the sword, Sen.

units.la: Evanescere] Vanescit aliquid diuturnitate. Dilabitur res familiaris. Consenescere moerore. Emori. Tabescit humor. mor. Extabuit opinio. Ad nihilum recidere, venire. In nihilum occidere. In nihilum interire. Exstingui, Cic. Consumi mœrore, incendio, senio. Dilabuntur vectigalia negligentia, Liv. Obsolescere. Exolevit disciplina, Tac. Deflorescere, Heren. Ad nihilum funditus res redeunt, Lucr. Labitur res, Plaut.
units.tr: To vanish: Something vanishes through long duration. The estate dwindles away. To waste away with grief. To die. The moisture dries up. The opinion has been destroyed. To return to nothing, to come to nothing. To perish into nothing. To be annihilated, Cic. To be consumed by grief, fire, or old age. Revenues slip away through neglect, Liv. To fall into disuse. Discipline has faded, Tac. To lose its bloom, Heren. Things return utterly to nothing, Lucr. The estate slips away, Plaut.

units.la: Evanescere ex oculis, vid. Disparere.
units.tr: To vanish from sight: see Disparere.

units.la: Evanidus] Exeat in tenues evanidus auras, Ovid. Tabificus, Liv. Evanescens memoria. Sen. Occidunus, Plin. Ventosa ratio favoris, Claud.
units.tr: Vanishing: Let him depart, vanishing into thin air, Ovid. Wasting away, Liv. A fading memory, Sen. Setting, Plin. The windy reasoning of favour, Claud.

units.la: Evannare, vid. Vannare.
units.tr: To winnow away: see Vannare.

units.la: Evaporare] Evanescit vetustate vinum, Cic. Evaporatione exprimitur aura tenuissima, Macrob. Evaporatio trahit saporem, Sen. Remittere saporem, Id. Moritur unguentum, (evaporat), Plin.
units.tr: To evaporate: Wine goes flat with age, Cic. The finest air is drawn out by evaporation, Macrob. Evaporation takes away the flavour, Sen. To lose its savour, Id. The ointment dies away (evaporates), Plin.

units.la: Evellere] Eruere herbam. Ruere herbas, Plin. Vellere aliquid radicitus, Col. Runcare spinas, Cat. Convellere funem à terra, Virg. Intervellere barbam, Sen. Vid. Eradicare.
units.tr: To pluck out: To root up a herb. To pull up herbs, Plin. To pluck something up by the roots, Col. To weed out thorns, Cat. To tear a rope from the ground, Virg. To pluck out the beard, Sen. See Eradicare.

units.la: Evenire] Peropportunè cecidit. Ita cadit, ut prædictum, Cic.
units.tr: To happen: It fell out most opportunely. It turns out just as foretold, Cic.

units.la: Evenit bene vel male] In bonum exibit, quicquid aget, Sen. Benè vel malè ei vertit, Plaut. Evadet in aliquid magnum malum hæc licentia, Ter. Ea ei fama pro bono cessit, Suet. In bonum abibit, Sen. Præter sententiam & spem evenit. Nequiter expedivit prima parasitatio, Plaut. Irritum cecidit. Non sponte illius, Tacit. Hac non successit, aliâ aggrediemur viâ, Ter. Non ex sententia eventus processit. Multa sunt, quæ illi stomachum concitant. Alienum id institutis meis. Alienissimum rationibus meis, Cic. Præter votum, Bud. Vid. Cedit benè.
units.tr: To turn out well or badly: Whatever he does will turn out for the good, Sen. It has turned out well or badly for him, Plaut. This license will end in some great evil, Ter. That reputation turned to his good, Suet. It will turn out for the good, Sen. It turned out beyond his opinion and hope. The first parasite's undertaking went badly, Plaut. It came to nothing. Not by his own will, Tacit. This did not succeed; we shall try another way, Ter. The outcome did not proceed according to opinion. There are many things which stir his bile. That is alien to my customs. Most alien to my reasoning, Cic. Beyond wish, Bud. See Cedit bene.

units.la: Eventus] Exitus, Cic. In bonum exibit.
units.tr: Outcome: The end, Cic. It will turn out for the good.

units.la: Eventus in fine patet] Duello durante, dubius eventus est.
units.tr: The outcome is open at the end: While the war lasts, the outcome is uncertain.

units.la: Eventus ostendet] Mox sciemus melius vate.
units.tr: The outcome will show: Soon we shall know better than the seer.

units.la: Eventus rerum varii, incerti] Animo quicquid statueris, non eveniet. Consilii & cursus non est idem exitus. Non in eadem potestate initium & finis. Eventus non prospicere stultum est] Eventus stultorum magister.
units.tr: Outcomes of things vary and are uncertain: Whatever you decide in your mind, it will not come to pass. The end of a plan or course is not the same as the outcome. The beginning and the end are not in the same power. It is foolish not to foresee the outcome: The outcome is the teacher of fools.

units.la: Eventus belli incertus] Mars communis.
units.tr: The outcome of war is uncertain: Mars is common to all.

units.la: Everrere] Deverrere, Col.
units.tr: To sweep: To sweep away, Col.

units.la: Evertere aliquid] Subvertere decretum, Salust. Transvertere consilia alicujus, Firm. Explantat ventus arbores, Col.
units.tr: To overturn something: To overthrow a decree, Salust. To divert the plans of someone, Firm. The wind uproots trees, Col.

units.la: Evertere urbem] Excidere urbes hostium. Delere & perdere. Exstinguere urbem, Tac. Expugnare oppidum, Plaut. Dare excidioni, Liv. Vertere arces, Virg. Convellere statum civitatis, Cic. Subruere arces, Propert. Eruere urbem, Virg.
units.tr: To overthrow a city: To destroy the cities of the enemy. To demolish and ruin. To lay a city waste, Tac. To storm a town, Plaut. To give over to destruction, Liv. To overturn citadels, Virg. To shake the state of a commonwealth, Cic. To undermine citadels, Propert. To tear up a city, Virg.

units.la: Euge!] Evox. Io! Plaut. Evohe, Ovid. Evæ, Catul. Benè factum, macte. Rectè. Præclare, Cic. Optimum est. Patrone salve! Nunc places. Ædepol. Mortalem graphicum! Plaut. Laudo. Vir es. Virum te judico, Ter. Euge beate! Mart. Tanto fortior, tanto felicior, Sen. Io Pæan! Ovid. Vid. Benè.
units.tr: Well done!: Evoe! Io! Plaut. Evohe, Ovid. Evae, Catul. Well done, bravo. Rightly. Excellently, Cic. It is best. Greetings, patron! Now you please. Surely! A true painter of mortals! Plaut. I commend you. You are a man. I judge you a man, Ter. Well done, happy man! Mart. So much the braver, so much the happier, Sen. Io Paean! Ovid. See Bene.

units.la: Evidens] Probabilis, Cic. Authenticus, Vlp. Authenticæ rationes. Argumento patet, Quint. Explicitus locus, Cic.
units.tr: Evident: Probable, Cic. Authentic, Vlp. Authentic reasons. It is clear from the argument, Quint. An explicit passage, Cic.

units.la: Evidenter] Liquidè. Liquentius, Gell. Perspicuum, Cic. Vid. Clarè.
units.tr: Evidently: Clearly. More clearly, Gell. Plainly, Cic. See Clearly.

units.la: Evigilare] Expergisci, Virg. Expergefieri, Suet. Excita juventus, Ovid. Excutior somno, Virg. pro, Excutio somnum. Somnus me reliquit.
units.tr: To wake up: To awake, Virg. To be roused, Suet. Rouse the young men, Ovid. I am shaken out of sleep, Virg. For, to shake off sleep. Sleep has left me.

units.la: Evirare] Castrare, Claud. Eunuchare se, Varr. Eunuchum se facere, Iuv. Adimere virilitatem, Tacit. Excidere virilitatem, Quint. Eunuchare, Hieron. Emasculare, Serv. Moecho adimere abdomen, Plaut. Onus inguinis auferre, Ovid. Demetere ferro caudam salacem, Hor.
units.tr: To geld: To castrate, Claud. To make oneself a eunuch, Varr. To make oneself a eunuch, Juv. To take away manhood, Tacit. To cut off manhood, Quint. To make a eunuch, Hieron. To emasculate, Serv. To take the belly away from an adulterer, Plaut. To remove the burden of the groin, Ovid. To cut off the lustful tail with iron, Hor.

units.la: Eviratus] Exsectus ab aliquo, Cic. Gallus, Quint. Præcisus, Lampr. Spoliatus viro. Exmas, Arnob. Ademptæ virilitatis homo, Tac. Excisâ virilitate puer, Quint. Semivir, Iuv. Semimas, Varr. Spado, Plin. Deliaci manu recisus, Petron. Eunuchus, Iuv. Desperatio barbæ, Id. Castratus hæres. Ambiguus mas, Claud. Vir non vir.
units.tr: Gelded: Cut off by someone, Cic. A eunuch, Quint. Cut off, Lampr. Stripped of manhood. Stripped of manhood, Arnob. A man deprived of manhood, Tac. A boy with his manhood cut out, Quint. Half-man, Juv. Half-male, Varr. Castrated man, Plin. Cut off by the hand of the Deliacan, Petron. Eunuch, Juv. Despair of a beard, Id. Castrated heir. Ambiguous male, Claud. A man who is not a man.

units.la: Evitare] Evadere ex periculo. Evitare dolorem. Exire ærumnâ. Vitare fabulam. Elabi suspicione, è, ex, de manibus nibus alicujus, Cic. Transmittere discrimen, Plin. Iun. Fallere retia. Eluctari laqueum, effugere. Subducere se nimbo, animam morti, Ovid. Defungi fatalibus malis, Suet. Præterire malum, Ter.
units.tr: To avoid: To escape from danger. To avoid pain. To get out of trouble. To shun a rumour. To slip away from suspicion, from someone's hands, Cic. To come safely through a crisis, Plin. Iun. To evade the nets. To wriggle out of a noose, to escape. To withdraw oneself from the storm, to snatch one's life from death, Ovid. To get free of fated evils, Suet. To pass by an evil, Ter.

units.la: Evitatio] Devitatio incommodorum, Cic. Fuga. Effugium, Id.
units.tr: Avoidance: Avoiding of troubles, Cic. Flight. Escape, Id.

units.la: Eunuchus, vid. Eviratus.
units.tr: Eunuch, see Gelded.

units.la: Evocare] Evocare foras, excire, Plaut. Sevocare in privatam domum de communi, Cic. Devocare aliquem, Liv.
units.tr: To call out: To call out of doors, to summon, Plaut. To call someone aside from the public into a private house, Cic. To call someone away, Liv.

units.la: Evolare] Evolitare, Col. Provolant omnes apes, si dies mitis futurus est, Plin. Superevolare, Lucan.
units.tr: To fly out: To fly out, Col. All the bees swarm out if the day is going to be mild, Plin. To fly over, Lucan.

units.la: Evolvere, vid. Explicare.
units.tr: To unroll, see To explain.

units.la: Evolutio] Explicatio rudentis, Cic. Explicatus, ûs, Plin.
units.tr: Unfolding: Explanation of a rope, Cic. An unfolding, Plin.

units.la: Eurus] Eurinus ventus, Col.
units.tr: East wind: An eastern wind, Col.

units.la: Evulgare secreta, vid. Prodere.
units.tr: To divulge secrets, see To betray.

units.la: Ex] A, ab, è, de aliquo audire, Plaut. Cic. Unde empta est? Plaut. Id unde te audivisse dicis? Cic.
units.tr: From: From, away from, out of someone: to hear from someone, Plaut. Cic. From whom was it bought? Plaut. From whom do you say you heard that? Cic.

units.la: Exacerbare, vid. Irritare.
units.tr: To exacerbate, see To irritate.

units.la: Exactè, vid. Accuratè.
units.tr: Exactly, see Accurately.

units.la: Exactio] Exactus mercis, Quint. Efflagitatio Consulatus insulsa, Cic. Coactio argentaria, Suet. Efflagitatus, ûs, Cic.
units.tr: Exaction: Exaction of goods, Quint. A foolish demanding of the consulship, Cic. Forced collection of money, Suet. Exacting, Cic.

units.la: Exactor] Exactor studiorum, operis, recte loquendi, Quint. Flagitator aëris assiduus. Coactor, Cic. Collectarius, Acron in Horat. Repetitor nuptæ ademptæ, Ovid. Reciperator, Fest.
units.tr: Exactor: An exactor of studies, of work, of correct speaking, Quint. A constant dunner for money. A compeller, Cic. A tax collector, Acron in Horat. One who demands back a wife who has been taken away, Ovid. A recoverer, Fest.

units.la: Exactus, vid. Accuratus.
units.tr: Exact, see Accurate.

units.la: Exacuere, vid. Acuere.
units.tr: To sharpen, see To whet.

units.la: Exæquatio] Æquatio juris Civium. Æquatio Civitatis, Cic. Temperatio juris, Reip. Temperamentum, quo alii cum aliis æquantur, Id. Libratio, & perlibratio aquarum, Vitruv.
units.tr: Equalising: Equalising of the rights of citizens. Equalising of the state, Cic. Regulation of law, of the commonwealth, Id. A balancing, and thorough balancing, of waters, Vitruv.

units.la: Exæstuare, vid. Æstuare.
units.tr: To boil over, see To seethe.

units.la: Exaggerare, exaggeratio, vid. Dilatare, Dilatatio.
units.tr: To exaggerate, exaggeration, see To enlarge, enlargement.

units.la: Exaggerare nimis] Elephantum ex musca facit.
units.tr: To exaggerate too much: He makes an elephant out of a fly.

units.la: Exagitare aliquem] Versare, Quint. Ego te exercebo hodie, uti dignus es. Solicitum habere aliquem, Ter. Solicitudo vexat impios, Cat. Exal-
units.tr: To harass someone: To turn over, Quint. I will exercise you today as you deserve. To keep someone troubled, Ter. Anxiety torments the wicked, Cat. Exal-

units.la: Exaltare] Tollere in sublime aliquid, Plin. Sustollere aliquem, Plaut. Sublimare aliquid, Non. Levare in sublime aliquid, Plin. Extollere caput, Cic. Relevare corpus à terra, Ovid. Attollere pedes, Quint.
units.tr: To exalt: To raise something on high, Plin. To lift someone up, Plaut. To elevate something, Non. To lift something up on high, Plin. To hold up the head, Cic. To raise the body from the earth, Ovid. To lift up the feet, Quint.

units.la: Exaltatio] Elevatio, Quint.
units.tr: Exaltation: Elevation, Quint.

units.la: Examen apum] Grex apum. Pulli apum. Apum pullities. Populus. Una, Col. Globus apum. Uber, Pallad.
units.tr: Swarm of bees: A flock of bees. Young bees. The brood of bees. A people. One, Col. A ball of bees. A udder, Pallad.

units.la: Examen seu probatio alicujus rei] Periclitatio longi temporis. Experientia. Periculum, Cic. Experimentum. Specimen sumere, Plin. Exploratio, Macrob. Spectamen, Plaut. Tentatio perseverantiæ, Liv. Tentamen, Ovid. Tentamentum, Virg.
units.tr: Examination or testing of something: A long trial over time. Experience. Danger, Cic. Experiment. To take a sample, Plin. Investigation, Macrob. A specimen, Plaut. A test of perseverance, Liv. A trial, Ovid. An attempt, Virg.

units.la: Examinant apes] Vernant apes. Exundant novis fœtibus apes, Col.
units.tr: Bees swarm: Bees are in spring. Bees overflow with new offspring, Col.

units.la: Examinare] Tentare alicujus scientiam, Cic. Extentare vires, Plaut. Facere periculum innocentiæ alicujus, Cæs. Experimentum facere, capere, Quint. Explorare animum alicujus, Ovid.
units.tr: To examine: To test someone's knowledge, Cic. To stretch one's strength, Plaut. To put someone's innocence to the test, Caes. To make an experiment, to take one, Quint. To explore someone's mind, Ovid.

units.la: Exardescere] Incandescere. Corripi flammâ, Ovid. Flammescere, Sipont. Excandescere, Cat. Inflammari. Excipere flammam, Cic. Inardescere, Hor. Concipere ignem, Lucr.
units.tr: To blaze up: To glow hot. To be seized by flame, Ovid. To become aflame, Sipont. To flare up in anger, Cat. To be set on fire. To catch the flame, Cic. To burn fiercely, Hor. To take fire, Lucr.

units.la: Exarmare] Dearmare, Liv. Inermare, Fest. Spoliare armis, Virg. Nudare armis, Ovid.
units.tr: To disarm: To disarm, Liv. To make unarmed, Fest. To strip of arms, Virg. To bare of arms, Ovid.

units.la: Exauctorare] Missionem dare militibus, Tac. Dimittere exercitum. Missum facere militem, Cic. Auctoratum militem dimittere, Liv.
units.tr: To discharge: To give soldiers their discharge, Tac. To dismiss the army. To release a soldier, Cic. To dismiss a soldier who has been enlisted, Liv.

units.la: Exauctoratus miles] Sacramento solutus, Cic.
units.tr: Discharged soldier: Released from the oath, Cic.

units.la: Exaudire aliquem] Concedere petitioni alicujus. Deduci preces ab aliqua re. Exorabilis sum alicui. Præbere se exorabilem, Cic. Dare aliquid precibus alicujus, Plin. Flecti precibus, Virg. Vinci precibus, Sen. Moveri, frangi precibus. Dare manus precibus. Accipere preces alicujus, Ovid. Audire precantem, Id. Preces ratas facere, Bud. Cedere precibus alicujus. Cic.
units.tr: To grant someone's request: To yield to someone's petition. Prayers can be obtained from something. I am open to someone's entreaty. To show oneself open to entreaty, Cic. To grant something to someone's prayers, Plin. To be bent by prayers, Virg. To be overcome by prayers, Sen. To be moved, to be softened by prayers. To lift up the hands to prayers. To accept someone's prayers, Ovid. To hear one who prays, Id. To make prayers effective, Bud. To yield to someone's prayers, Cic.

units.la: Excæcare] Obcæcare. Privare oculis, Cic. Exoculare caput alicujus. Exturbare alicui oculos, Plaut. Lumine oculorum privare. Consciscere alicui cæcitatem. Effodere aciem luminis solis radiis, Gell. Elufcare,Vlp. Caecitatem inferre. Offundere oculis pulverem. Officere luminibus.
units.tr: To blind: To make blind. To deprive of the eyes, Cic. To gouge out someone's eyes. To knock out someone's eyes, Plaut. To deprive of the light of the eyes. To bring blindness upon someone. To throw dust in the eyes. To block the light of the eyes.

units.la: Excæcatio] Elufcatio, Vlp. Occæcatio, Isid.
units.tr: Blinding: Dimming, Vlp. Blinding, Isid.

units.la: Excellens] Excellenti animo ac virtute vir. Illustris. Præstans. Præstabilis, Præclara indoles. Excellens omni generelaudis, (& in omni genere) ornatiss. & splendidissimus vir. Ampliss. Nobilis, Cic. Divinus vir. Magna anima, Tac. Animæ, quales neque candidiores terra tulit. Instar multorum unus. Inter paucos. Cedro dignus. Problema Archimedeum.
units.tr: Excellent: A man of outstanding spirit and virtue. Illustrious. Distinguished. A man of notable disposition. A man most adorned and most splendid in every kind of praise. Most illustrious. Noble, Cic. A divine man. A great soul, Tac. Souls such as the earth has never brought forth more radiant. One among many. Among few. Worthy of cedar. An Archimedean problem.

units.la: Excellentissimus negligit vilia] Elephantus non captat murem.
units.tr: The most excellent disdains trifles: The elephant does not chase the mouse.

units.la: Excellere, vid. Eminere. Antecellere.
units.tr: To excel, see To stand out. To surpass.

units.la: Excellentia] Splendor nominis. Præstantia virtutis, Cic. Claritudo familiæ, Tac. Claritas personarum, Plin. Iun. Nobilitas morum, animi, Ovid.
units.tr: Excellence: The splendour of a name. Excellence of virtue, Cic. The fame of a family, Tac. The brightness of persons, Plin. Iun. The nobility of manners and of mind, Ovid.

units.la: Exceptio, vid. Conditio.
units.tr: Exception, see Condition.

units.la: Excerpere] Tu id, quod boni est, excerpis. Ex variis ingeniis excellentissima quæque libavimus. Depromere aliquid de libris, Cic. Vid. Enotare.
units.tr: To select: You pick out what is good. From various minds we have gathered the most excellent of each. To draw something from books, Cic. See To note down.

units.la: Excidere] Exscindere silvam. Exsecare,Cic. Exputare vitem. Explantare arbusculam, Col. Recidere vepres, Cat.
units.tr: To cut down: To cut down a wood. To cut out, Cic. To prune a vine. To uproot a small tree, Col. To cut back brambles, Cat.

units.la: Excidere, cadere] Fluunt arma è manibus. Erumpit repente risus, Cic. Excussi manibus radii, Ovid. Vid. Elabitur.
units.tr: To fall out, to fall: Weapons fall from the hands. Laughter suddenly bursts out, Cic. Rays shaken from the hands, Ovid. See To slip away.

units.la: Excidium urbis] Excidio. Eversio tectorum. Disturbatio Corinthi. Disperditio, Cic. Excidio, Fest.
units.tr: Destruction of a city: Ruin. Overthrow of roofs. The wrecking of Corinth. Destruction, Cic. Ruin, Fest.

units.la: Excipere aliquid in emptione] Exceptione cavere. Exceptum est aliquid fœdere, Cic.
units.tr: To except something in a purchase: To guard oneself by an exception. Something was excepted in the treaty, Cic.

units.la: Excitare è somno] Suscitare è quiete, Catul. Exsuscitare quietum, Cic. Abrumpit somnos cura, Virg.
units.tr: To wake from sleep: To rouse from rest, Catul. To rouse the one at rest, Cic. Care breaks sleep, Virg.

units.la: Excitare ad alacritatem, vid. Incitare.
units.tr: To rouse to eagerness, see To incite.

units.la: Exclamatio] Excitus vocis, Apul. Proclamatio.
units.tr: Exclamation: A outburst of voice, Apul. A proclamation.

units.la: Excludere] Excludere aliquem foras, Ter. Excludere domo. Præcludere alicui aditum. Intercludere alicui omnes aditus, Cic. Secludere curas, Virg. Prohibere aliquem domo, Ter. Arcere aliquem aditu, Liv.
units.tr: To exclude: To shut someone out of doors, Ter. To shut out of the house. To block someone's access. To cut off all access to someone, Cic. To drive away cares, Virg. To keep someone from the house, Ter. To keep someone from access, Liv.

units.la: Excludere ova] Excudit gallina ovum. Excudit pullos, Var. Excludit gallina, absol. Virg.
units.tr: To hatch eggs: The hen hatches the egg. She hatches chicks, Var. The hen hatches, absol., Virg.

units.la: Excogitare aliquid] Effingere animo. Depromere ex suo sensu aliquid. Fingere cogitatione, depingere aliquid. Commoliri dolum, machinam. Promere à se aliquid, Cic. Comminisci, Liv. Investigare cum animo, Plaut. Excoquere malum, Id. Consequi cogitatione aliquid. Architectari, Cic. Machinari, Lucr.
units.tr: To devise something: To form in the mind. To draw something from one's own understanding. To imagine something in thought, to depict something. To plot a trick, a contrivance. To bring something forth from oneself, Cic. To invent, Liv. To search out with the mind, Plaut. To brew mischief, Id. To grasp something by thought. To plan, Cic. To contrive, Lucr.

units.la: Excogitatio] Machinatio, & Solertia, Cic.
units.tr: Contrivance: Scheming and ingenuity, Cic.

units.la: Excolere, vid. Exercere.
units.tr: To cultivate, see To exercise.

units.la: Excommunicare] Sacrificiis alicui interdicere. In numero sceleratorum ac impiorum aliquem habere. Devovere hominis caput. Anathemate plectere caput. Animam alicujus inferis sacrare. Ultimæ animadversionis exempla statuit in aliquem Pontifex, Bud. Anathema alicui dicere. A sacris amovere. A piorum societate & communione secludere. Ab Ecclesiæ communione repellere.
