Communione multare, secludere. Anathemate percellere, jugulare. Communionem alicui interdicere. Dirum anathema alicui intorquere.
units.tr: To excommunicate: To forbid someone the sacrifices. To count someone among the wicked and impious. To devote a man's head. To punish a head with anathema. To consecrate someone's soul to the dead. The Pontiff set down the examples of the last punishment against someone, Bud. To pronounce anathema on someone. To remove from holy things. To cut off from the fellowship and communion of the pious. To drive out from the communion of the Church. To penalise with the loss of communion, to shut out. To strike down and slaughter with anathema. To forbid someone communion. To hurl a dire anathema at someone.

units.la: Excommunicato] Exclusio, Macrob. Vid. Proscriptio.
units.tr: Excommunication: Exclusion, Macrob. See Proscription.

units.la: Excommunicatus] Exclusus à communione ecclesiæ. Cui interdictus est ingressus templi, & consortium, ac communicatio cum omnibus. Abstentus, Cyprian. Sacer homo, Hor. Exsecrandus ac detestabilis, Cic. Dirâ proscriptione, vel, diris programmatibus (ecclesiæ, episcopi) per compita confixus, Bud. Extorris domo, penatibus, foro, congressu æqualium, Id.
units.tr: Excommunicated: Shut out from communion of the Church. One to whom entry to the temple, and association and communication with all, is forbidden. Held apart, Cyprian. A sacred man, Hor. Accursed and detestable, Cic. Fixed up at the crossroads by a dire proscription, or by dire notices of the Church or bishop, Bud. Banished from home, household gods, forum, and the company of equals, Id.

units.la: Excoquere, vid. Decoquere.
units.tr: To overcook, see To boil down.

units.la: Excoriare] Deglubere pecus, Suet. Despoliare dorsum, Plaut. Exasperat fauces aliquid, Plin.
units.tr: To flay: To skin cattle, Suet. To strip the back, Plaut. Something chafes the throat, Plin.

units.la: Excors, vid. Demens.
units.tr: Senseless, see Mad.

units.la: Excrementa] Retrimenta cibi, Varr. Reliquiæ cibi, Cic. Fimus. Fimum, Plin. Stercus, Plaut. Egeries, Solin. Merda, Hor. Sordes aurium, Cic. Coactaalvi, Celf. Foria, pl. Non. Oletum, Fest. Purgamenta, quæ homines corporibus edunt. Proluvies ventris, Col.
units.tr: Excrements: Leftovers of food, Varr. Remnants of food, Cic. Dung. Manure, Plin. Dung, Plaut. Discharge, Solin. Ordure, Hor. Earwax, Cic. Hardened bowel matter, Celsus. Refuse, pl. Non. Oletum, Fest. The refuse which people pass from their bodies. The outflow of the belly, Col.

units.la: Excrescere] Exire in herbam. Repullulare è radicibus. Assurgere in altitudinem, Plin. Tollunt fe altiùs à terra vites,Cic. Prosiliunt in altitudinem frutices, Col. Crescere in altitudinem, Liv. Exit in cœlum ramis, Virg.
units.tr: To grow up: To go into grass. To sprout again from the roots. To rise to a height, Plin. The vines lift themselves higher from the earth, Cic. Shrubs shoot up to a height, Col. To grow up to a height, Liv. It rises to heaven with its branches, Virg.

units.la: Excruciare, vid. Cruciaretormentis.
units.tr: To torture, see Cruciare, with tortures.

units.la: Excruciari] Difcrutiari animi, Plaut. Ter. Percruciari, Plaut. Rumpi inediâ, Rumpi, Abf. Mart. Quàm magis id reputo, tam magis uror. Omnibus exemplis cruciari. Maceror, quòd sim tibi causa doloris. Ipsus fe comest. Exenteror miser. Angere fe animi. Cordolium mihi est. Dolere ab animo, ab ægritudine. Exest animam ægritudo. Excedor exspectando,Plaut. Conficere fe. Moderi conscientia, Cic. Mandendo sese conficit ipsa. Invidia aliquem macerat,Lucr. Fremere, Cic. Ringi,Ter.
units.tr: To be tormented] To be tormented in mind, Plaut. Ter. To be utterly tormented, Plaut. To be consumed by hunger, Abl. Mart. The more I consider it, the more I burn. To be tormented by every kind of example. I am worn down with grief that I am the cause of your pain. He eats himself up. I am wretched, my insides are being torn out. To gnaw at oneself in mind. I have heartache. To grieve in mind, from distress. Sorrow eats away the soul. I am worn out by waiting, Plaut. To wear oneself out. To be restrained by conscience, Cic. She wears herself out by biting herself. Envy wears someone down, Lucr. To rage, Cic. To snarl, Ter.

units.la: Excubare] Agere excubias, Ovid. Vigilias agere. Stare in vigilia urbis. Agere stationem. In specula esse, observare. Advigilare ad custodiam ignis, Cic. Excubare pro portis in muris, Liv. Agrarias facere, Veget.
units.tr: To keep watch] To keep watch, Ovid. To stand guard. To stand watch over the city. To maintain a picket. To be on the lookout, to observe. To keep watch over the fire, Cic. To lie awake by the gates and on the walls, Liv. To make night patrols, Veget.

units.la: Excubiæ] Vigiliæ. Custodiæ. Præsidium stativum, Cic. Statio militum, Suet. Procubitores, Cato. Velites ante castra excubantes, Fest.
units.tr: Watches] Night watches. Guards. A standing garrison, Cic. A post of soldiers, Suet. Outposts, Cato. Light troops keeping watch before the camp, Fest.

units.la: Excubitor] Vigil nocturnus, Plaut. Vigiles castrorum, Lucan. Vigiliarius, Sen.
units.tr: Night watchman] A night watchman, Plaut. The watchmen of the camp, Lucan. A watchman, Sen.

units.la: Excudere ignem] Excutere, Elidere ignem è silice, Plin. Elicere ignem conflictu & ictu lapidum, Cic. Procudere ignem, Lucr.
units.tr: To strike fire] To knock out, to strike fire from flint, Plin. To draw fire by the clash and striking of stones, Cic. To beat out fire, Lucr.

units.la: Excultus] Excultus ad humanitatem ex agresti immaniqué vitâ. Expolitus homo. Subactum ingenium,Cic. Exuit animum silvestrem, Virg. Exercitus vario & assiduo motu & dissidiis. Depexus, Ter.
units.tr: Refined] Refined to humanity out of a rustic and savage life. A polished man. A tamed disposition, Cic. He has put off his savage nature, Virg. An army with varied and constant movement and disputes. Combed, Ter.

units.la: Excurrere ex aliquo loco] Evolare ex senatu, è carcere, Cic. Exspatiari longè equis, Ovid. Procurrere in publicum, in vias, Liv. Longius, Virg. In pugnam, Col.
units.tr: To run out of a place] To fly out of the senate, out of prison, Cic. To range far and wide on horseback, Ovid. To run out into public, into the streets, Liv. Farther, Virg. Into battle, Col.

units.la: Excursio, vid. Eruptio.
units.tr: Sally, see Eruption.

units.la: Excusare aliquem] Excusare aliquem alicui,apud aliquem. Elevare noxam alicujus. Extenuare crimen,Cic. Cuncta ad imperatorem in mollius relata, Tac.
units.tr: To excuse someone] To excuse someone to someone, before someone. To lessen someone's fault. To extenuate a crime, Cic. All matters referred to the commander in a milder light, Tac.

units.la: Excusare seipsum] Afferre excusationem. Uti excusatione, Cic. Causari, Virg. Plaut. Extra omnem culpam se ponere. Crimen dissolvere, diluere, purgare. Ex culpa se eximere. Exsolvere se suspicionibus. Levare se infamiâ. Purgare se alicui: de aliqua re. Expedire se de peripetasmatis, Cic. Levare facinus. Liberare se culpa, Liv. Lavare peccatum, Ter. Expurgare se, Plaut.
units.tr: To excuse oneself] To offer an excuse. To make use of an excuse, Cic. To plead, Virg. Plaut. To place oneself entirely beyond blame. To dissolve, dilute, or clear a charge. To free oneself from guilt. To rid oneself of suspicions. To lift the disgrace from oneself. To clear oneself to someone, concerning some matter. To extricate oneself from a hanging, Cic. To lighten a crime. To free oneself from blame, Liv. To wash away a sin, Ter. To clear oneself, Plaut.

units.la: Excusare se, id est, causam dicere] Excusari morbi causa. Afferre excusationem oculorum. Uti excusatione valetudinis &c. Defendere vitia excusatione adolescentiae. Excusatio necessitatis, aetatis &c. aliquem satis defendit: a labore vindicat, Cic. Causam dicere, fingere, Ter. Excusare mare & flatus, Quint. Vires, Ovid. Causari, afferre aetatem, Cic. Causari ignorantiam, &c. Vlp. Praetendere ignorantiam, Quint. Verba culpae, Ovid. Praetexere culpam nomine conjugii, &c. Virg. Obtentui est mihi aliquis, vel aliquid, Sal. Paupertatis obtentu se excusare, Paul. IC.
units.tr: To excuse oneself, that is, to plead a cause] To be excused on account of illness. To offer an excuse about one's eyes. To make use of an excuse of ill health, etc. To defend faults by the excuse of youth. The excuse of necessity, of age, etc. Something sufficiently defends someone: it frees him from toil, Cic. To plead a cause, to invent one, Ter. To excuse the sea and the winds, Quint. Strength, Ovid. To plead, to offer age as a reason, Cic. To plead ignorance, etc., Ulpian. To pretend ignorance, Quint. Words of blame, Ovid. To cloak a fault under the name of marriage, etc., Virg. Someone or something has served me as a pretext, Sall. To excuse oneself on the pretext of poverty, Paul. IC.

units.la: Excusatio] Causa. Diverticulum quaerere peccatis, Cic. Causatio aegri corporis, Gell. Transcriptio. Color, Quint.
units.tr: Excuse] A reason. To seek a bypath for one's sins, Cic. A plea of bodily sickness, Gell. A transcription. A colour, Quint.

units.la: Excusatio justa] Causa sontica, Tac. Impedimentum legale, Ict.
units.tr: Just excuse] A guilty cause, Tac. A legal impediment, Jurists.

units.la: Excusatio ficta] Excusatio calva. Causa non causa. Praetextus. Fucus, Cic.
units.tr: Feigned excuse] A bald excuse. A cause that is no cause. A pretext. A pretence, Cic.

units.la: Excusatus] Excusabilis, Ovid. Excusatissimus est. Excusate fieri videtur, Quint. Excusatius facies, Plin. Iun. Excusationem habens, Bud.
units.tr: Excused] Excusable, Ovid. He is most excusable. It seems to be done excusably, Quint. You make it more excusable, Plin. Iun. Having an excuse, Bud.

units.la: Exdorsuare, vid. Exenterare.
units.tr: To strip off the back, see To disembowel.

units.la: Exedere, vid. Depasci.
units.tr: To eat away, see To graze upon.

units.la: Exemplar] Archetypus. Proplasma, Plin. Species, Cic. Vid. Idea.
units.tr: Exemplar] An archetype. A model, Plin. A kind, Cic. See Idea.

units.la: Exemplaris vir] Gnomon & regula. Exemplum continentiae, Ter. Exempli rari; Singularis, Quint. Exemplar vitae morumque, Hor.
units.tr: Exemplary man] A gnomon and rule. An example of self-restraint, Ter. Of rare example; singular, Quint. A pattern of life and conduct, Hor.

units.la: Exemplum] Me sibi habeat documentum. Specimen virtutis, Cic. Parsimoniae disciplina aliis eram, Plaut. Exemplare, Lucr. Paradigma, Donat.
units.tr: Example] Let him take me as his lesson. A specimen of virtue, Cic. I was a model of thrift to others, Plaut. A copy, Lucr. A paradigm, Donat.

units.la: Exemplum statuere] Documentum in posterum statuere, ne quis, &c. Cic. Curabo ut omnibus exemplo sis. Edere exempla in aliquem. Malis exemplis perdere, Ter.
units.tr: To set an example] To set down a lesson for the future, so that no one, etc., Cic. I will take care that you are an example to all. To make examples of someone. To ruin with bad examples, Ter.

units.la: Exempli causâ] Verbi causâ, Verbi gratiâ, Cic. Exempli gratia, Plin. Ut puta, Vlp.
units.tr: For example] By way of reason, for instance, Cic. For example, Pliny. Let us suppose, Ulpian.

units.la: Exemplo alieno cautum fieri] Alienâ insaniâ frui optimum. Alieno periculo cautus. Alieno discere periculo. Alienum vulnus nostra cautio. Felix, quem faciunt aliena pericula cautum.
units.tr: To be made cautious by another's example] It is best to profit from another's madness. Cautious by another's danger. To learn from another's danger. Our caution is another's wound. Happy is he whom the dangers of others make cautious.

units.la: Exenterare] Exdorsuare piscem, Plaut. Exossare, Id. Evi-scerare, Virg.
units.tr: To disembowel] To strip the back of a fish, Plaut. To bone, Id. To eviscerate, Virg.

units.la: Exercere corpus] Exercere vires. Exerceri in venando. Modicis exercitationibus utendum, Cic.
units.tr: To exercise the body] To exercise one's strength. To exercise oneself in hunting. Moderate exercises should be used, Cic.

units.la: Exercere se in aliqua re] Exerceri ad pugnam, Fab. Recolere ingenium, Plin. Iun. Elaborare in aliqua re, Cic. Ponere alicubi tyrocinium, Liv. Rudimenta virtutis sub aliquo ponere, Quint. Expoliendum limandumque se alicui docto viro permittere, Plin. Procudere ingenium, linguam, Amm. Meditor me ad cursuram, Plaut.
units.tr: To train oneself in some matter] To be trained for battle, Fab. To cultivate one's talent, Plin. Iun. To labour at some matter, Cic. To place oneself somewhere as an apprentice, Liv. To put oneself under someone as a student of the rudiments of virtue, Quint. To entrust oneself to a learned man to be polished and filed, Plin. To hone one's talent and tongue, Amm. I prepare myself for the race, Plaut.

units.la: Exercere aliquem in aliquo studio] Excolere aliquem doctrinâ, disciplinâ. Erudire aliquem artibus, laboribus. Informare ad humanitatem. Formare pueros. Inficere artibus. Instituere. Expolire aliquem & hominem reddere. Recoquere hominem, Cic. Erudire aliquem artes, Ovid. Exercitator sum alicujus artis vel hominis, Plin. vid. Docere.
units.tr: To train someone in some study] To cultivate someone with learning and discipline. To teach someone the arts, through labours. To form someone for humanity. To form boys. To imbue with the arts. To instruct. To polish someone and make him a man. To refine a man, Cic. To teach someone the arts, Ovid. I am a trainer in some art or man, Pliny. See To teach.

units.la: Exercitatio] Exercitium. Meditatio. Rudimentum. Usus assiduus. Commentatio, Cic. Tyrocinium, Plin. Meditamenta puerilia. Disceptatiunculae memoriarum, Gell. Exercitus, Plaut. Studium, Ovid.
units.tr: Exercise] Practice. Meditation. A rudiment. Constant use. A commentary, Cic. An apprenticeship, Pliny. Childish exercises. Little disputations for memory, Gell. An army, Plaut. A study, Ovid.

units.la: Sine exercitio nihil fit] Testa non fit, nisi lutum tundatur.
units.tr: Nothing is made without practice] A pot is not made unless the clay is pounded.

units.la: Exercitatus] Exercitatissimus. Nemini parere animus, bene a natura informatus, vult, Cic. Exercitatus ad rem aliquam, Ter. Disciplinosus gladiator, Cato. Recoctus scriba, Hor. Exercitus, ti, Lucr.
units.tr: Trained] Highly trained. A mind well formed by nature wants to obey no one, Cic. Trained for some task, Ter. A disciplined gladiator, Cato. A scribe well seasoned, Hor. Trained, Lucr.

units.la: Exercitus] Copiae. Manus, Cic. Res, Liv. Armatae hominum caterva, Catul. Miles, Ter.
units.tr: Army] Forces. A band, Cic. Affairs, Liv. An armed throng of men, Catul. A soldier, Ter.

units.la: Exercitus instructus] Acies, Liv. Acies instructa, Cic.
units.tr: Army drawn up] A battle line, Liv. An army drawn up in battle order, Cic.

units.la: Acies deposita, Tacit. Instructæ copiæ. Agmen composi-tum, Liv. Procinctum. Acies procincta. Procincta acies, Fest.
units.tr: A battle line laid down, Tac. Forces drawn up. A column arranged, Liv. Ready for action. A line ready for battle. A battle line ready for action, Fest.

units.la: Exeunt libri] Eduntur libri, Libellus excidit. Pervenit in manus hominum. Versantur scripta inter manus, Cic. Enotescit, Plin. Iun. Venit in manus hominum liber, Quint. Data est in publicum scripta oratio. Edita est in lucem. Vid. Edere libros.
units.tr: Books come out] Books are published, a little book comes out. It reaches the hands of men. Writings circulate among hands, Cic. It has become known, Pliny the Younger. The book comes into the hands of men, Quint. The written speech is given to the public. It is published to the light. See To publish books.

units.la: Exhalare] Exspirat amnis auras. Vaporant aquæ, Plin. Respirat terra malignum vaporem, Stat. Exæstuat æstum tellus, Lucr. Exsudat gravis halitus faucibus. Perf. Halant alæ sertis, Enn.
units.tr: To exhale] The river breathes out its breezes. The waters give off vapour, Pliny. The earth breathes out a harmful vapour, Stat. The earth glows with heat, Lucr. A heavy breath exhales from the throat, Pers. The wings breathe out with garlands, Enn.

units.la: Exhalationes] Halitus terræ, Plin. Halitus retorridi. Exspiratio terræ. Respiratio aquarum, Cic. Spiritus fœdi odoris, Cel. Anhelitus vini, Cic.
units.tr: Exhalations] Vapours of the earth, Pliny. Dried-up vapours. The breathing out of the earth. The respiration of waters, Cic. Breath of a foul smell, Cels. The fumes of wine, Cic.

units.la: Exherbare, vid. Runcare.
units.tr: To weed out, see To hoe.

units.la: Exheredare] Exheredem scribere filium. Excludere ab hereditate, Cic.
units.tr: To disinherit] To write a son as disinherited. To exclude from an inheritance, Cic.

units.la: Exhereditatus] Exheres, Plaut. Abstentus, Vlp.
units.tr: Disinherited] Disinherited, Plaut. Withheld, Ulpian.

units.la: Exhilarare aliquem] Traducere à severitate ad hilaritatem. Remittit animos cautus. Afficere aliquem voluptate, gaudio, lætitia. Integrare animum, Cic. Concire in lætitiam aliquem, Ter. Permulcere aliquem jucunditate, Quint. Lubentiores vos faciam, quàm lubentia est. Faciam ut gaudeas, Plaut. Discutere vultu nubila, Stat. Discutere tristes cogitationes, Cels. Afferre alicui hilaritatem, jucunditatem, Plin. Objicere lætitiam alicui, Ter. Facere lætitiam, Cic. Vid. Lætificare.
units.tr: To cheer someone] To move from severity to cheerfulness. The cautious man relaxes his spirits. To affect someone with pleasure, joy, gladness. To refresh the mind, Cic. To stir someone into gladness, Ter. To soothe someone with delight, Quint. I will make you more glad than gladness itself. I will make you rejoice, Plaut. To dispel clouds from the face, Stat. To dispel sad thoughts, Cels. To bring cheerfulness, delight to someone, Pliny. To bring gladness to someone, Ter. To give gladness, Cic. See To gladden.

units.la: Exhinc, vid. Deinde.
units.tr: Thenceforth, see Then.

units.la: Exhorrescere, vid. Horrescere.
units.tr: To shudder, see To bristle.

units.la: Exhortari, vid. Incitare.
units.tr: To exhort, see To incite.

units.la: Exigere, vid. Pellere.
units.tr: To exact, see To drive out.

units.la: Exigere (2) id est, reposcere suum] Cogere pecuniam à Civibus statuarum nomine. Repetere res suas. Recuperare suum judicio, Cic. Coactiones argentarias facere, Suet. Vid. Reposcere.
units.tr: To exact (2), that is, to demand back what is one's own] To compel payment from citizens in the name of statues. To reclaim one's property. To recover what is one's own by judgment, Cic. To carry out financial exactions, Suet. See To demand back.

units.la: Exiguitas] Parvulum ligni, Plin. Iun. Paululum agelli. Pauxillum. Perpauxillum. Aliquantillum cibi, Plaut. Guttula argenti, consilii. Perpusillum rogare, Id. Pauca loquitur, Ter. Perpauca mutare. Perpauculi passus, Cic. Aliquantum nummorum. Aliquantulum æris, Id. Modicum. Parvum, Subst. Hor. Non est in toto corpore mica falis, Catul.
units.tr: Smallness] A little wood, Plin. Iun. A little field. Very little. Very, very little. A small amount of food, Plaut. A drop of silver, of counsel. To ask for a very small thing, Id. He speaks few words, Ter. To change very few things. A very few paces, Cic. Some money. A little bronze, Id. A moderate amount. A small thing, a substantive, Hor. There is not a grain of salt in the whole body, Catul.

units.la: Exiguum temporis] Exiguo post. Exiguum dormire, Plin. brevi, Gell. Parum diu. Parumper conticere. Paulum abesse. Paulisper commorari. Paulo ante. Paulo post. Paulo amplius. Aliquamdiu. Pusillum laxamenti, Cic. Parumper operire. Paululum opperiri aliquem, Ter. Aliquantisper hinc concede, Plaut.
units.tr: A small amount of time] A little after. To sleep briefly, Pliny. In a short time, Gell. For a short while. To be silent for a little while. To be a little distant. To stay awhile. A little before. A little after. A little more. For some time. A small relief, Cic. To cover up for a little while. To wait a little for someone, Ter. Withdraw from here for a little while, Plaut.

units.la: Exiguus, vid. Parvus.
units.tr: Small, see Little.

units.la: Exilis] Junceus. Juncidus. Ejuncidus, Varr. Monogrammos, Cic. Perexilis, Col. Petilus, Plaut.
units.tr: Slender] Rush-like. Rushy. Quite rushy, Varr. Single-lined, Cic. Very slender, Col. Thin, Plaut.

units.la: Exilitas] Gracilitas corporis, Cic. Tenuitas caudæ, Plin. Gracilitudo staturæ, Acci. Non. Contractus, & Contractura columnarum, Vitr.
units.tr: Slenderness] Slimness of body, Cic. Thinness of a tail, Pliny. Slimness of stature, Accius, Non. Contraction, and the contraction of columns, Vitr.

units.la: Exilium] Exulatio, Flor. Exportatio, Sen. Insularis pœna, Amm. Relegatio in insulam. Deportatio, Vlp.
units.tr: Exile] Banishment, Flor. Expulsion from the country, Sen. Punishment of island exile, Amm. Relegation to an island. Deportation, Ulpian.

units.la: Exilii venia] Restitutio exulum; damnatorum, Cic.
units.tr: Pardon of exile: Restoration of exiles; of condemned persons, Cic.

units.la: Eximere] Excipere femina pomis, Plin. Expedire agrum lectione lapidum, Col.
units.tr: To pick out: A woman catching fruit, Plin. To clear a field by gathering the stones, Col.

units.la: Eximiè] Præclarè gessit negotium. Divinitus disputata. Apprimè, egregiè, insigniter, excellenter. Nihil suprà. Ita ut nihil possit suprà. Ut nihil ultrà possit cogitari, Cic. Divinè omnia exsequitur, Tull. Quint.
units.tr: Especially: He carried out the business outstandingly. Discussed in a divine manner. Particularly, nobly, remarkably, excellently. Nothing beyond. So that nothing more can be imagined, Cic. He carries out everything divinely, Tull. Quint.

units.la: Eximius] Singularis vir. Egregia indoles. Insignis res, Cic. Exceptus sorti. Exsors equus, Virg. Edecimatus, Fest. Unicus, Afran. Conquisitus, exquisitus, lectus, Cic. Auro hunc expendi decet. Aurea gens. Auro contrà non carus est, Plaut. Superba aulæa, Virg. Unus instar omnium.
units.tr: Outstanding: An extraordinary man. A distinguished disposition. A remarkable thing, Cic. Chosen by lot. A horse not allotted, Virg. Tenth-born, Fest. Unique, Afran. Sought out, choice, picked, Cic. He deserves to be weighed in gold. A golden race. Not dear even for gold, Plaut. Splendid hangings, Virg. One who is equal to all.

units.la: Exinanire] Inanire, Plin. Vacuare sulcum, Col. Vacuefacere aliquid, Col. Egeitur dolor lacrymis, Ovid. Deplere vitam supervacuis querelis, Manil. Vid. Evacuare.
units.tr: To empty: To make empty, Plin. To empty a furrow, Col. To make something empty, Col. Grief is drained away with tears, Ovid. To fill up life with superfluous complaints, Manil. See Evacuare.

units.la: Exinanitio alvi] Purgatio alvi. Detractio consumpti & confecti cibi, Cic. Dejectio, Celf. Egestus ventris, Sen.
units.tr: Evacuation of the bowels: Purging of the bowels. The removal of consumed and digested food, Cic. Dejection, Celsus. Discharge of the belly, Sen.

units.la: Exinde] Ex illo. Ex illo tempore, Virg. Post unquam, quam, Ter. Inde loci fecla creavit, Lucr. Ex tunc, Apul
units.tr: Thereafter: From that. From that time, Virg. Ever since, when, Ter. Thence the ages created the places, Lucr. From then, Apul.

units.la: Exire] Exire foràs, Ter. Exire domo à patria, è portu. de triclinio. Ex Italia. In solitudinem. Egredi urbe, è portu, ex provincia, ad bellum, extra fines. Prodire in publicum. Procedere è prætorio in publicum, in solem. Excedere urbe, ex urbe. Efferre pedem portâ, Cic. Exire limen, Ter. Exire intùs, i. e. domo, Plaut. Progredi. Provenire in scenam, Id. Excedere, abf. Cic. Evadere limen, Col. Facessere ædibus, Pacuv.
units.tr: To go out: To go out of doors, Ter. To leave home or country, to leave port, to leave the dining room. To go out of Italy. Into the wilderness. To leave the city, leave port, leave the province, go to war, go beyond the borders. To come forward in public. To proceed from the praetorium into public, into the sun. To withdraw from the city, out of the city. To set one's foot outside the gate, Cic. To cross the threshold, Ter. To go out inside, that is, out of the house, Plaut. To advance. To come forward onto the stage, Id. To depart, abs. Cic. To pass beyond the threshold, Col. To clear out of the house, Pacuv.

units.la: Existimare] Videor mihi perspexisse aliquid, Cic. Videor videre illum diem, Ter. Optimum factu ratus, Sallust. Videtur ita mihi, Plaut. Hoc primùm sentio, Cic. Vid. Opinari.
units.tr: To think: I seem to myself to have grasped something, Cic. I seem to see that day, Ter. Thinking it the best course of action, Sallust. It seems so to me, Plaut. This is the first thing I feel, Cic. See Opinari.

units.la: Existimatio, vid. Opinio.
units.tr: Judgement: see Opinio.

units.la: Exitium] Interitus. Pernicies. Internecio aratorum. Occasus urbis, hominis, Reip. Interitio, disperditio, Cic. Occidio, Col. Pestis, Liv. Perditio, Sipont. Mors æterna, Lucr.
units.tr: Destruction: Ruin, perdition. Slaughter of ploughmen. The overthrow of a city, a man, a commonwealth. Destruction, ruin, Cic. Massacre, Col. Plague, Liv. Perdition, Sipont. Eternal death, Lucr.

units.la: Exit, vid. Terminatur.
units.tr: Exit: see Terminatur.

units.la: Exitialis] Exitiabilis dies, Plaut. Exitiosum bellum. Perniciosus morbus, Cic. Damnosus, Hor. Funestus, Sen. Lævus, Virg. Perniciosa lex, Cæf. Hostis studiorum perniciosissima, Quint. Dispendiosus, Col. Decretorius dies. Sonticus morbus. Maleficus, Plin. Detrimentosus, Cæf. Damnificus, Plaut. Obnoxius, Enn.
units.tr: Deadly: A deadly day, Plaut. A deadly war. A pernicious disease, Cic. Harmful, Hor. Mournful, Sen. Ill-omened, Virg. A pernicious law, Caes. The most pernicious enemy of studies, Quint. Ruinous, Col. A decisive day. A sickly disease. Harmful, Plin. Detrimental, Caes. Damaging, Plaut. Liable, Enn.

units.la: Exitus ridiculus] Pro amphora urceus exit, Hor.
units.tr: A ridiculous outcome: Instead of a jar, a jug comes out, Hor.

units.la: Exitus omnium idem] Omnia mors æquat.
units.tr: The outcome is the same for all: Death levels all things.

units.la: Exlex] Lege solutus ac liber, Cic.
units.tr: Lawless: Freed and released from the law, Cic.

units.la: Exolescere] Vetustate aliquid exolescit, Quint. Defectus senio, Col. Coacescit ætas vetustate. Obsoleverunt res propter vetustatem. Exarescere, Cic. Abiit res longè in desuetudinem, ICtus.
units.tr: To fall into disuse: Something fades away with age, Quint. Worn out by old age, Col. Things have grown obsolete through age. To wither, Cic. The matter has fallen far into disuse, jurist.

units.la: Exoletus] Obsoletus. Literarum oblivio, Cic.
units.tr: Obsolete: Out of use. The forgetting of letters, Cic.

units.la: Exoptabilis, vid. Desiderabilis.
units.tr: Desirable: see Desiderabilis.

units.la: Exoptare, vid. Desiderare.
units.tr: To desire: see Desiderare.

units.la: Exorabilis] Venia deprecationis facilior, Quint Impetrabilis, Plaut. Facilis impetrandæ veniæ, Claud. Facilis rogantibus. Facilis veniæque paratus, Ovid. Facilis ad concedendum, Cic.
units.tr: Placable: More easily moved to pardon by entreaty, Quint. Obtainable, Plaut. Easy to win pardon, Claud. Easy for those who ask. Ready to grant pardon and easily persuaded, Ovid. Easy to bring to a concession, Cic.

units.la: Exorabilis sum, vid. Exaudire.
units.tr: I am placable: see Exaudire.

units.la: Exorare aliquem] Impetrare aliquid ab aliquo. Impetrare veniam precibus, Cic. Obtinere, Id. Exorare aliquid ab aliquo, Plaut. Exorator sum, Ter. Litare. Impetratum aliquid reddere; auferre ab aliquo, Plaut. Impetrassere, Id. Flectere aliquem prece, Sen. Valere rogando, Ovid. Cogere precibus aliquem, Hor. Precibus evincere aliquem, Sen.
units.tr: To entreat someone: To obtain something from someone. To obtain pardon by prayer, Cic. To secure, Id. To obtain something from someone, Plaut. I am one who gains by entreaty, Ter. To win favour by sacrifice. To give back, or take away from someone, what has been obtained, Plaut. To obtain, Id. To bend someone by prayer, Sen. To prevail by asking, Ovid. To compel someone by prayers, Hor. To overcome someone with entreaties, Sen.

units.la: Exorbitare] Decedere officio, ab officio, Liv. De officio, Cic. Flexiones, diverticula persequi, Cic. Extra chorum saltare. Extra callem ire, errare est. Extra curriculum ferri. Extra oleas ferri. Extra scopum jaculari. Extra viam currere. Extra orbitam ruere. Vid. Deviare.
units.tr: To go astray: To depart from duty, Liv. From one's duty, Cic. To pursue digressions and byways, Cic. To dance outside the chorus. To go beyond the path is to wander. To be carried outside the racecourse. To be driven outside the lanes. To throw wide of the mark. To run outside the road. To rush out of the track. See Deviare.

units.la: Exordiri, vid. Incipere.
units.tr: To begin: see Incipere.

units.la: Exordium] Exorsum orationis, Cic. Introitus defensionis. Ingressio dicendi. Orsus, Cic. Orsa. Exorsa, plu. Virg. Vestibulum artis, Quint. Proœmium. Præfatio, Cic. Vid. Initium.
units.tr: Beginning: The opening of a speech, Cic. The introduction of a defence. The entrance into speaking. A beginning, Cic. Beginnings, Cic. Openings, plural, Virg. The vestibule of an art, Quint. A prologue. A preface, Cic. See Initium.

units.la: Exordium rei parvæ magnum] De pusillis magna proœmia.
units.tr: A small matter has a grand beginning: Great prologues for small things.

units.la: Exoriri, vid. Oriri.
units.tr: To arise: see Oriri.

units.la: Exornare, vid. Ornare.
units.tr: To adorn: see Ornare.

units.la: Exos] Exossis, Apul. Exossatus, Lucr. Anguimanus, Id. De Elephan.
units.tr: Without bones: Boneless, Apul. Deboned, Lucr. With snake-like hands, Id. Said of the elephant.

units.la: Exossare, vid. Exenterare.
units.tr: To bone: see Exenterare.

units.la: Exosus, vid. Odiosus.
units.tr: Hated: see Odiosus.

units.la: Expalpare, vid. Eblandiri.
units.tr: To flatter: see Eblandiri.

units.la: Expandere, vid. Distendere.
units.tr: To spread out: see Distendere.

units.la: Expavescere] Pavefieri, Ovid. Gell. Expavere ad aliquem tumultum, Plin. Percussit animum illico, Ter. Incessit eum timor, terror, Liv. Pertimescere. Extimescere. Territi & consternati animis hostes. Exterreri aspectu. Præter modum exterreri. Submittere animum periculo, Cic. Comparescere, Mart. Consternari, Salust.
units.tr: To be terrified: To be struck with fear, Ovid, Gell. They were alarmed at a tumult, Plin. It struck his mind at once, Ter. Fear and terror seized him, Liv. To be greatly afraid. To be utterly afraid. Enemies terrified and dismayed in spirit. To be startled at the sight. To be frightened beyond measure. To lower one's spirit before danger, Cic. To appear, Mart. To be dismayed, Sallust.

units.la: Expedire negotium] Conficere negotium. Confectum relinquere. Tantum recipies, quantum obire possis, Cic. Facessere jussa, Virg. Transactum reddere aliquid, Plaut. Factum & curatum dare, Ter.
units.tr: To carry out a task: To finish a task. To leave it finished. You will undertake only as much as you can manage, Cic. To carry out orders, Virg. To return something done, Plaut. To give a thing done and attended to, Ter.

units.la: Expedire se ab occupationibus] Expedire se, abs. Relaxare se occupationibus. A nimia necessitate faciendi aliquid se relaxare. Eximere tempus è suis occupationibus, Cic.
units.tr: To free oneself from business: To free oneself, abs. To relax from one's business. To release oneself from the pressing need of doing something. To take time out of one's occupations, Cic.

units.la: Expedit] Fructuosum est de jure suo nonnunquam decedere. Confert ad aliquid. Rationes meae ita ferunt. Operæ pretium est,Cic. Fœnerat hoc mihi. Quod erit mihi bonum ac commodum. Ex usu nostro erit, Ter. In rem est, Tacit. Pretium curæ visum est, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: It is advantageous: It is sometimes profitable to give up one's right. It contributes to something. My reckonings bear this out. It is worth the trouble, Cic. This lends itself to me. It will be good and convenient for me. It will be to our advantage, Ter. It is to the purpose, Tac. The matter seemed worth the care, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Expedite, vid. Facile.
units.tr: Readily: see Facile.

units.la: Expeditio bellica] Apparatus belli, qui fit publico consensu, Bud.
units.tr: Military expedition: The equipment of war, made by public consent, Bud.

units.la: Expeditus] Expeditissimus ad aliquid, in aliqua re. Perexpeditus, Cic. Vid. Facilis.
units.tr: Unencumbered: Most ready for something, in some matter. Wholly unencumbered, Cic. See Facilis.

units.la: Expellere, vid. Pellere.
units.tr: To expel: see Pellere.

units.la: Expendere aliquid libra] Expendere aurum auro, Plaut. Pensare aliquid libra, Col. Rependere aliquid argento, Plin. Dependere aliquid libra, Id. Librare coenas, Gell.
units.tr: To weigh something on a scale: To weigh gold against gold, Plaut. To weigh something with a balance, Col. To pay back something in silver, Plin. To weigh out something, Id. To balance dinners, Gell.

units.la: Expendere pecuniam] Erogare pecuniam. Erogare in sumptum. Effundere patrimonium in salutem Reipub. Facere sumptum in rem militarem. Impendere laborem & sumptum ad incertum casum. Insumere sumptum in aliquid magnum. Impensas facere, Cic. Expromere heminas octo in urceum, Plaut. Expensare argumentum,Id. Prodere aliquid, Ter. Dependere in aliquid multum, plus. Onerare rationes, Col. Conferre in aliquid impendia, Quint.
units.tr: To spend money: To pay out money. To disburse for expenses. To pour out one's patrimony for the safety of the commonwealth. To make outlays for military affairs. To lay out labour and expense on an uncertain chance. To devote great outlay to something. To make expenditures, Cic. To pour eight hemina out of a jug, Plaut. To reckon an argument as expenditure, Id. To hand over something, Ter. To spend much, or more, on something. To load up the accounts, Col. To contribute outlays to something, Quint.

units.la: Expensi codex] Codex accepti & expensi. Tabulae accepti & expensi,Cic. Rationarius codex,Suet. Ratio expensi,Plaut. Calendarium versat, Sen. Magnus calendarii liber evolvitur, Id. (Calendarium proprie est codex pecuniae fœnori datae, calendis exigi solitae, Bud.)
units.tr: Ledger of expenditure: The ledger of receipts and expenditure. Tablets of receipts and expenditure, Cic. An account book, Suet. The account of expenditure, Plaut. He turns over the calendar, Sen. A great calendar book is unrolled, Id. (A calendar is properly a ledger of money lent at interest, usually called in on the Kalends, Bud.)

units.la: Expensi ratio] Ratio, calculus. Subductio, Cic. Ratiuncula, Plaut. Computatio, Plin. Iun. Ad digitos venit, Et hoc venit in computationem. Ratiocinium,Col. Discussiones rationales, Firm. Disputatio rationum, Vlp.
units.tr: The reckoning of expenditure: Account, calculation. A subtraction, Cic. A little reckoning, Plaut. A computation, Plin. Iun. It comes down to the fingers, and this comes into the reckoning. A reckoning, Col. Rational discussions, Firm. A disputation of accounts, Ulp.

units.la: Expensas acceptis metire] Messe tenus propriâ vive.
units.tr: Measure your outlays by your receipts: Live within your harvest.

units.la: Expensare, vid. Expendere.
units.tr: To weigh out: see Expendere.

units.la: Expergefacere] Inquietare aliquem, Suet. Excitare aliquem de, e ex somno,Cic. Excitare cubilibus,Liv. Vid.Excitare.
units.tr: To wake someone: To disturb someone, Suet. To rouse someone from sleep, Cic. To rouse from beds, Liv. See Excitare.

units.la: Expergefieri, vid. Evigilare.
units.tr: To wake up: see Evigilare.

units.la: Experiens, vid. Peritus.
units.tr: Experienced: see Peritus.

units.la: Experientia] Experimentum,Plin. Periclitatio longi temporis, Cic. Exploratio, Macr.
units.tr: Experience: An experiment, Plin. A long-term trial, Cic. An investigation, Macr.

units.la: Experimentum non fit sine periculo] Empyricus periculosè in corpore humano facit pericula.
units.tr: An experiment is not made without danger: The empiric makes dangerous experiments on the human body.

units.la: Experiri] Experimentum capere, Liv. Experimentum facere. Periclitari. Tentare quid possim. Pertentare. Attentare fidem alicujus. Degustare & experiri vitam aliquam, Cic. Tentare experientiâ, Varr. Probare boves, Col. Facere periculum, Cæs. Ter. Usu explorare, Cels. Prætentare chordas. Aurum in ignibus spectatur, Ovid. Extentare vires, Plaut.
units.tr: To try: To make an experiment, Liv. To make an experiment. To put to the test. To try what I can do. To test. To try someone's loyalty. To taste and try a way of life, Cic. To test by experience, Varr. To test oxen, Col. To make the trial, Caes. Ter. To explore by use, Cels. To try the strings. Gold is tested in the fire, Ovid. To stretch one's strength, Plaut.

units.la: Expers alicujus rei] Exsors, Plaut. Immunis malis, Plin. Inconscius, Liv.
units.tr: Without share in a thing: Having no share, Plaut. Free from evils, Plin. Unaware, Liv.

units.la: Expertus, vid. Peritus. Gnarus.
units.tr: Experienced: see Peritus. Gnarus.

units.la: Expertus melius rem intelligit] Credendum peritis in sua arte. Experto crede Ruperto. Artifici in sua arte credendum. Quisque suæ artis actor & professor optimus, Val. M.
units.tr: The one who has experience understands the matter better: One must trust experts in their own art. Trust the experienced Rupert. The craftsman must be trusted in his own art. Each person is the best practitioner and professor of his own art, Val. M.

units.la: Expetendus, expetere, vid. Desiderabilis, desiderare.
units.tr: To desire: see Desiderabilis, desiderare.

units.la: Expiabilis] Lustralis, Ovid. Lustricus dies, Macrob. Lustrificus, Val. Argonau. Piacularis, Liv. Piaculus porcus, Cato.
units.tr: Expiable: Lustral, Ovid. A lustral day, Macrob. Purifying, Val. Argon. Expiatory, Liv. An expiatory pig, Cato.

units.la: Expiare piaculum] Piare culpam morte, Virg. Luere stuprum morte, Cic. Lustrare urbem, homines, Virg. Diluere peccata, Ovid. Purificare, Suet. Februare, Varr.
units.tr: To expiate a crime: To atone for a fault with death, Virg. To pay for a defilement with death, Cic. To purify the city, men, Virg. To wash away sins, Ovid. To purify, Suet. To cleanse with the februa, Varr.

units.la: Expiatio] Lustratio, Col. Lustratus, Symmach. Piamentum, Plin. Averruncatio, Henr. Steph. Religiosa purificatio, Mart.
units.tr: Expiation: Purification, Col. Purified, Symmach. Means of atonement, Plin. Averting, Henr. Steph. Religious purification, Mart.

units.la: Expilare, expilator, vid. Compilare, compilator.
units.tr: To plunder, plunderer: see Compilare, compilator.

units.la: Expiscari, vid. Disquirere.
units.tr: To search out: see Disquirere.

units.la: Explere] Complere, Tac. Adimplere, Plin. Vid. Implere.
units.tr: To fill: To fill up, Tac. To fill, Plin. See Implere.

units.la: Explicare] Evolvere quod involutum est, Cic. Exsinuat collectos amictus, Virg. Expandit florem. Mittit folia, Plin.
units.tr: Explicare] To unfold what is rolled up, Cic. She shakes out her gathered cloak, Virg. It expands a flower; it puts forth leaves, Plin.

units.la: Explicare obscura] Explanare rem obscuram. Interpretari. Enodare. Exponere. Enucleare. Aperire, quæ in obscuritate latuerunt; Planum facere, Cic. Substernere notioni omnium, Arnob. Deplanare aliquid. Liquidum facere, Non.
units.tr: Explicare obscura] To explain an obscure matter: to explain, to interpret, to unravel, to expound, to bring out. To open up what has lain hidden in obscurity, to make plain, Cic. To lay it open to everyone's understanding, Arnob. To level something out, to make it clear, Non.

units.la: Explicatio] Explicatus difficilis. Explanatio interpretum. Expositio. Enodatio, Cic. Enarratio poëtarum. Paraphrasis, Quint. Commentarium. Interpretamentum Gell. Commentum, Priscian.
units.tr: Explicatio] A difficult explication. The explanation of interpreters. Exposition. Unravelling, Cic. The exposition of poets. Paraphrase, Quint. Commentary. Interpretation, Gell. Comment, Priscian.

units.la: Explicator] Interpres rerum obscurarum. Explanator, Cic. Commentator, Bud.
units.tr: Explicator] An interpreter of obscure things. An explainer, Cic. A commentator, Bud.

units.la: Explorare] Noctu ventitabat, ut omnia specularetur, Cic. Speculandi causâ missus. Prospeculatum mittere aliquem. Liv. Acutissimè indagare & odorari quid &c. Odorari & degustare aliquem, Cic. Scrutari mentem alicujus, Ovid. Introspicere voluntates, Tac. Tentare animos nuntiis, Caes.
units.tr: Explorare] He used to go about at night so as to spy on everything, Cic. Sent out for the purpose of scouting. To send someone ahead to reconnoitre, Liv. To investigate most keenly, to sniff out what... To smell out and taste someone, Cic. To probe the mind of someone, Ovid. To look into people's wills, Tac. To test minds with messages, Caes.

units.la: Explorator] Speculator, Cic. Lustrator orbis Hercules, Apul. Missis visoribus, Tac. Emissarius. Canes venatici. Cibyratici. Cibyrathæ pantheræ. Qui cuncta odorantur, pervestigant, venantur, Cic. Conquisitores, Plaut. Inquisitores, Suet.
units.tr: Explorator] A spy, Cic. Hercules, the scourer of the world, Apul. By sending out observers, Tac. An emissary. Hunting hounds. Cibyratic hounds. Cibyrathean panthers. Those who sniff out, track down and hunt out everything, Cic. Searchers, Plaut. Inquisitors, Suet.

units.la: Expolire, vid. Polire.
units.tr: Expolire, see Polire.

units.la: Expolitio] Politio, Fest. Politura marmoris, Plin. Perpolitio sermonis, Ad Heren. Vltima lima scriptis deficit, Ovid.
units.tr: Expolitio] Polishing, Fest. The polish of marble, Plin. Thorough polishing of style, Ad Heren. Writings lack the final file, Ovid.

units.la: Expolitus, vid. Elaboratus.
units.tr: Expolitus, see Elaboratus.

units.la: Exponere aliquid] Proponere vexillum, Caes. Collocare tabulas bene pictas in bono lumine, Cic. Efferre, vel extollere signum, Virg.
units.tr: Exponere aliquid] To set up a standard, Caes. To place well-painted pictures in a good light, Cic. To raise or lift up a standard, Virg.

units.la: Exportare aliquid] Efferre aliquid è navi. Inter manus accipere aliquem. Facere exagogam, Plaut. Tollere ex aliquo loco aliquid. Inter manus è convivio auferre aliquem, Cic. Egero prædam ex hostium tectis, Liv. Proferre foras aliquid, Col. Progerunt formicæ defunctas, Plin. Extra ferre, Quint.
units.tr: Exportare aliquid] To carry something out of a ship. To take someone up in one's arms. To make an exagoge, Plaut. To take something away from some place. To carry someone off from a banquet in one's arms, Cic. To carry off plunder from the enemy's houses, Liv. To bring something forth out of doors, Col. Ants carry out their dead, Plin. To carry outside, Quint.

units.la: Exportatio rerum] Egestio opum, Plin. Iun. Exagoga, Plaut.
units.tr: Exportatio rerum] The draining away of wealth, Plin. Iun. Exagoga, Plaut.

units.la: Expositio, vid. Explicatio.
units.tr: Expositio, see Explicatio.

units.la: Expositivus] Projecta, Projectitia puella, &c. Plaut.
units.tr: Expositivus] A foundling girl, an exposed child, Plaut.

units.la: Expostulare cum aliquo] Expostulationem habere, facere cum aliquo. Conqueror apud te de injuriâ mihi à te factâ, Cic.
units.tr: Expostulare cum aliquo] To have a remonstrance with someone, to make one. I complain to you about the injury done to me by you, Cic.

units.la: Expresse] Enucleatè dicere. Definitè dare potestatem alicui. Enucleatius. Enodatè. Enodatius dicere. Articulatè dicere, Præcisè negare. Syllabatim dictare, Cic. Signatè & proprie loqui, Macrob. Significanter dicere, Quint. Significantius. Consignantius, Consignatissimè, Gell. Corporaliter aliquid explicare, Arnob.
units.tr: Expresse] To speak clearly and distinctly. To grant someone a power in precise terms. More clearly. To speak more plainly and in detail. To speak articulately. To deny flatly. To dictate syllable by syllable, Cic. To speak in a marked and proper sense, Macrob. To speak significantly, Quint. More significantly. Most significantly, Gell. To explain something in bodily terms, Arnob.

units.la: Exprimere per vim] Elicere sanguinem, Cic. Emoliri. Pondere presssam baccam velut exsaniari, Col. Emedullare, Plin. Emungere alicui oculos, Elidere. Exculcare furfures, Plaut. Exurgere succum, Cat. Prælo supponere olivam, vehementerque premere, ut exsudet quantulumcunque habeat amurcæ, Col.
units.tr: Exprimere per vim] To draw out blood, Cic. To force out. To squeeze a pressed berry as if wringing out its juice, Col. To take out the marrow, Plin. To gouge out someone's eyes. To crush out. To tread out bran, Plaut. To wring out the juice, Cat. To put an olive under the press and press it hard, so that it sweats out whatever little oil-lees it has, Col.

units.la: Exprobrare aliquid alicui] Exprobrandi causa dicere. Objicere alicui furta, Cic. Opprobrare, Plaut. Imputare, Suet.
units.tr: Exprobrare aliquid alicui] To say something for the purpose of reproach. To throw thefts in someone's face, Cic. To upbraid, Plaut. To impute, Suet.

units.la: Expromere aliquid] Depromere pecuniam ex arcâ. Promere pecuniam ex ærario. Expedire pyxidem, virgas. Argumenta eruere, Cic. Distringere amaritudinem carminum, Plin. Intendere eruditionem, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Expromere aliquid] To take money out of a chest. To bring money out of the treasury. To unpack a box, the rods. To bring out arguments, Cic. To unwrap the bitterness of songs, Plin. To display learning, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Expugnare] Potiri armis, Virg. Potiri oppidi, regni, Cic. Obtinere urbem armis, Liv.
units.tr: Expugnare] To take by arms, Virg. To gain possession of a town or kingdom, Cic. To hold a city by arms, Liv.

units.la: Expungere] Albo eradere, Tac. Interlinere. Tollere alicujus nomen ex omnibus scriptis. Eximere ex, vel de reis aliquem, Cic. Abolere, Suet. Spongiâ mederi, Id. Exsculpere aliquem versum, Amil. Prob. Radere nomen alicujus fastis, Tac.
units.tr: Expungere] To erase from the roll, Tac. To cancel by writing between the lines. To remove someone's name from all records. To strike someone off from among the accused, Cic. To abolish, Suet. To heal with a sponge, Id. To cut out a verse, Amil. Prob. To scrape someone's name off the calendars, Tac.

units.la: Exquirere, vid. Disquirere. Anquirere, Cic.
units.tr: Exquirere, see Disquirere. Anquirere, Cic.

units.la: Exquisitum quid] Cibi conquisitissimi, Cic. Attica bellaria, Lautæ cupediæ, (Athenienses enim omnia voluerunt exquisita) vid. Eximius.
units.tr: Exquisitum quid] Most exquisite foods, Cic. Attic dainties, fine delicacies (for the Athenians wanted everything exquisite), see Eximius.

units.la: Exsanguis] Incruentus, Liv. Incruentatus, Tacit.
units.tr: Exsanguis] Bloodless, Liv. Unstained with blood, Tacit.

units.la: Exscindere] Exsecare, Cic. Vid. Excidere.
units.tr: Exscindere] To cut out, Cic. See Excidere.

units.la: Exscribere] Describere librum ab aliquo. E libris exscribere, Cic. Vid. Enotare. Transcribere.
units.tr: Exscribere] To copy a book from someone. To copy out from books, Cic. See Enotare. Transcribere.

units.la: Exscriptum] Exemplar literarum. Apographum, Cic. Exemplar Chirographi, Id. Exsculpere, vid. Cavare.
units.tr: Exscriptum] A copy of a letter. A transcript, Cic. A copy of a bond, Id. Exsculpere, see Cavare.

units.la: Exsecrari aliquem] Malè precari alicui. Omnibus precibus detestari. Devincire exsecrationibus aliquem, Cic. Diram exsecrationem alicui componere, & ei furias invocare. Sacrare caput alicujus, Liv. Diris exsecrationibus incessere, Suet. Imprecari diras poenas alicui. Defigere diris deprecationibus, Plin. Devovere, Tibul. Iram Dei in caput alicujus detestari, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Exsecrari aliquem] To curse someone. To execrate someone with every prayer. To bind someone with curses, Cic. To compose a dire curse against someone and invoke the Furies upon him. To consecrate someone's head, Liv. To assail someone with dire curses, Suet. To pray dire punishments upon someone. To pierce someone with dire prayers, Plin. To devote to destruction, Tibul. To call down the wrath of God upon someone's head, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Exsecratio] Diræ, Cic. Preces, Cæs. Iratæ. præces, Hor. Devotio, Apul. Anathema, Hieron. Vota exsecrantia alicujus nomen, Ovid.
units.tr: Exsecratio] Curses, Cic. Prayers, Caes. Angry prayers, Hor. Devotion, Apul. Anathema, Hieron. Vows cursing someone's name, Ovid.

units.la: Exsecrandus] Detestabilis & exsecrandus homo, Exsecratus. Devotus. Abominatus, Hor. Exsecratione devinctus, Cic. Exsecrabilis, Porphyr. Sacer homo, Plaut. Anathema, Bud. Vivite devoto fœmina virque toro, Ovid.
units.tr: Exsecrandus] A detestable and accursed man. Cursed. Devoted. Abominated, Hor. Bound by a curse, Cic. Execrable, Porphyr. A man made sacred (forfeit to the gods), Plaut. Anathema, Bud. Live on, devoted woman and man, in the marriage bed, Ovid.

units.la: Exsecutio] Confectio, Cic. Patratio pacis, Paterc. Peractio, Fest.
units.tr: Exsecutio] Accomplishment, Cic. The establishing of peace, Paterc. Completion, Fest.

units.la: Exsecutor] Exactor operis, Liv. Patrator necis, Tac. Agens in rebus, Amm.
units.tr: Exsecutor] A supervisor of works, Liv. An executor of a killing, Tac. An agent in affairs, Amm.

units.la: Exsequi] Perficere instituta, Cic. Patrare necem, Tacit. Perpetrare omnia, quæ pertinent ad, Liv. Conata peragere, Iuv. Exserere manum, & quæ meditata sunt, ad verum perducere, Profectus in opere tentare. Sen.
units.tr: Exsequi] To carry out what has been resolved, Cic. To carry out a murder, Tacit. To carry through everything that pertains to..., Liv. To accomplish what has been attempted, Iuv. To stretch out the hand and bring what has been planned to the truth; to try in action what has been begun, Sen.

units.la: Exsequiæ] Justa funebria, Liv. Justa funerum, exsequiarum, Cic. Justa exsequialia, Stat. Solenne funeris: officia suprema, Suprema abs.Tac. Funebria sacra. Mos parentalis, Ovid. Ferale, inferiale officium, Apul. Supremus mortalium honos, Val. Max. Sepultura. Funus. Humatio, Cic.
units.tr: Exsequiæ] Due funeral rites, Liv. The due rites of funerals, Cic. Due funeral observances, Stat. The solemn rites of a funeral: the last duties, abs. Tac. Sacred funeral rites. The custom of parental rites, Ovid. The funeral, the rite of the dead, Apul. The last honour paid to mortals, Val. Max. Burial. Funeral. Interment, Cic.

units.la: Exsequias celebrare] Parentare alicui. Justa facere. Justa solvere funeri. Memoriam nominis epulis celebrare, Cic. Suprema alicui solvere, Tac. Libitinam exercere, Val. M. Exsequi funus, Gell. Feralia officia peragere, Apul.
units.tr: Exsequias celebrare] To perform rites for a parent. To pay due rites. To discharge the due rites of a funeral. To honour the memory of a name with feasts, Cic. To pay the last tribute to someone, Tac. To carry on the trade of Libitina, Val. M. To conduct a funeral, Gell. To perform the funeral duties, Apul.

units.la: Exsequialis] Libitinensis porta, Lamp. Funebris concio, Cic. Funebris pompa, Quint. Sepulchralis fax. Parentalis mos, Ovid. Funerea fax, Mart. Feralis, Inferialis. Inferalis, Apul.
units.tr: Exsequialis] The gate of Libitina, Lamp. A funeral address, Cic. A funeral procession, Quint. A sepulchral torch. Ancestral custom, Ovid. A funeral torch, Mart. Funereal, belonging to the dead, Apul.

units.la: Exserere caput] Prominet vulgus ex tectis, Stat. Emerger gere se, Cic. Proferre caput, Ovid. Protendunt cornua cochleæ, Plin. Exsertantem ora latebris, Virg. Ab exsertare.
units.tr: Exserere caput] The crowd peeps out from the houses, Stat. To raise oneself up, to emerge, Cic. To put out one's head, Ovid. The snail thrusts out its horns, Plin. Thrusting its face out of its hiding place, Virg. Ab exsertare.

units.la: Exspectans alicujus rei] Candidatus dignitatis, mortis, æternitatis. Est in exspectatione magistratus. Spes ei facta est à Rege dignitatis obtinendæ, Cic.
units.tr: Exspectans alicujus rei] A candidate for dignity, for death, for eternity. He is awaiting the magistracy. Hope of obtaining the dignity was held out to him by the King, Cic.

units.la: Exspectare] Præstolari. manere aliquem, Opperiri aliquem, Ter. Esse in exspectatione alicujus rei, Exspectatione pendere, Cic. Sum in exspectando, Gell. Respectare aliquid ab aliquo, Cic.
units.tr: Exspectare] To wait for, to stay for someone. To await someone, Ter. To be in expectation of something, to hang in suspense, Cic. I am in the act of waiting, Gell. To look for something from someone, Cic.

units.la: Exspectatio diuturna & frustranea molesta est] Fœdum est & mansisse diu, vacuumque redire.
units.tr: Exspectatio diuturna & frustranea molesta est] It is a shameful thing to have waited long and to return empty-handed.

units.la: Exspuere] Remittere ore aquam, Col. Respuit equus frenos, Stat.
units.tr: Exspuere] To let water out of the mouth, Col. The horse spits out the bit, Stat.

units.la: Exstans] Editus collis, Cæs. In immensum aditus, Col. Editus in altitudinem, Liv. Elatus, elatior, Ov. Col. Superlatus pileus, Val. M. Superedita luna, Lucr. Extumidus, Var. Minantur in cœlum scopuli, Virg.
units.tr: Exstans] A raised hill, Cic. An approach rising to an immense height, Col. Raised to a height, Liv. Lifted up, higher, Ov. Col. A cap set high, Val. M. The moon rising high, Lucr. Swollen, Var. The cliffs threaten the sky, Virg.

units.la: Exstimulare] Stimulare aliquem ad arma, Hor. Adjicere stimulos alicui, Ovid. Adhibere stimulos, Lucr. Admovere calcar, stimulor alicui. Bellicum canere, Cic. Addere calcar alicui, Hor. Sufflare aliquem, Amm. Agere mentes ad omne scelus & libidinem, Liv.
units.tr: Exstimulare] To spur someone on to arms, Hor. To add goads to someone, Ovid. To apply goads, Lucr. To apply the spur; I spur someone on. To sound the war-trumpet, Cic. To add a spur to someone, Hor. To fire someone up, Amm. To drive men's minds to every crime and lust, Liv.

units.la: Exstimulator, vid. Instigator.
units.tr: Exstimulator, see Instigator.

units.la: Exstinguere] Restinguere incendium, Cic. Stinguere, Lucr. Ferre auxilium tignis ardentibus, Id. Deflammare tædas, Apul. Explere diuturnam sitim, restinguere, Cic.
units.tr: Exstinguere] To put out a fire, Cic. To extinguish, Lucr. To bring help to burning beams, Id. To extinguish torches, Apul. To satisfy a long thirst and quench it, Cic.

units.la: Exstingui] Stinguitur, Interstinguitur ignis, Luc.
units.tr: Exstingui] The fire is put out, quenched, goes out, Luc.

units.la: Exstirpare. vid. Eradicare.
units.tr: Exstirpare, see Eradicare.

units.la: Exstruere, vid. Ædificare.
units.tr: Exstruere, see Ædificare.

units.la: Exstructio] Exædificatio. Fabrica. Fabricatio alicujus rei. Ædificatiunculæ, Cic. Structura, Col. Constructio, Plin. Iun. Structio, Firm.
units.tr: Exstructio] A building up. Construction. The making of a thing. Little buildings, Cic. Structure, Col. Construction, Plin. Iun. Structure, Firm.

units.la: Exsuctus, vid. Sterilis.
units.tr: Exsuctus, see Sterilis.

units.la: Exsudare, vid. Sudare.
units.tr: Exsudare, see Sudare.

units.la: Exsultare, vid. Gaudere. Tripudiare.
units.tr: Exsultare, see Gaudere. Tripudiare.

units.la: Exsultatio. vid. Tripudium.
units.tr: Exsultatio, see Tripudium.

units.la: Exsuperantia] Exsuperatio,Cic. Exuberatio,Vitruv. Redundantia, Cic. Superfluitas, Plin. Enormitas, Spart.
units.tr: Exsuperantia] Excess, Cic. Overflow, Vitruv. Redundancy, Cic. Superfluity, Plin. Excessiveness, Spart.

units.la: Extabescere, vid. Macere.
units.tr: Extabescere, see Macere.

units.la: Extemporaneus ] Extemporalis, Mart. Schedicus, Apul. Subitaria dictio, Gell. Incogitatus, Sen. Verba inopinata, Plin. Calidum mendacium (ex tempore natum) Incoctum non expromet, bene coctum dabit, Plaut.
units.tr: Extemporaneus] Extempore, Mart. Improvised, Apul. A speech made on the spur of the moment, Gell. Unthought-out, Sen. Unexpected words, Plin. A hot lie (made up on the spot) will not come out half-baked; it will give you one well cooked, Plaut.

units.la: Extendere , vid. Distendere.
units.tr: Extendere, see Distendere.

units.la: Extenuare aliquid] Extenuare verbis munus. Elevare offensiones, Cic. Haud parva res sub titulo prima specie minime atroci circumferebatur, Liv. Cuncta in mollius relata, Tac. Magna attenuare, & ad minima deducere, Sen. Omnia ejus vel vanitate vel fumis vendebat, Lampr.
units.tr: Extenuare aliquid] To belittle a service with words. To lighten offences, Cic. A matter of no small importance was passed around under a title that at first sight looked least atrocious, Liv. All things were reported in a milder light, Tac. To belittle great things and reduce them to the smallest, Sen. He sold all of him either for vanity or for smoke, Lampr.

units.la: Extenuari] Tenuari, Ovid. Tenerescere, Plin.
units.tr: Extenuari] To be thinned, Ovid. To grow thin, Plin.

units.la: Extenuatio] Attenuatio Suspicionis. Levatio vitiorum, Cic.
units.tr: Extenuatio] Lessening of suspicion. The lightening of faults, Cic.

units.la: Exterebrare] Efforatus stipes, Col. Vid. Terebrare
units.tr: Exterebrare] A stump bored through, Col. See Terebrare

units.la: Extergere, vid. Defricare.
units.tr: Extergere, see Defricare.

units.la: Exterior] Extrariae res, Cic. Superficiarius, Bud. Personata, bracteata felicitas, Sen.
units.tr: Exterior] External things, Cic. Superficial, Bud. A mask-like, gilded happiness, Sen.

units.la: Exteriora fallunt] Fronti nulla fides.
units.tr: The outward appearances deceive] There is no trusting the brow.

units.la: Exterminare, vid. Pellere.
units.tr: To exterminate, see to drive out.

units.la: Externus, vid. Alienus.
units.tr: External, see foreign.

units.la: Exterrere aliquem ] Percellere, Liv. Perterrefacere aliquem, Tremefacere. Conterrere, exterrere aliquem, Cic. Percutere pectus alicujus pavore, Tacit. Perterrere valde. Examinare aliquem metu, Ter. Complere formidinis aliquem, Plaut. Perpavefacere aliquem, Id. Conjicere in metum, Consternare, Perstringere horrore aliquem, Liv.
units.tr: To terrify someone] To strike down, Liv. To make someone thoroughly afraid; to make someone tremble. To frighten thoroughly, to terrify someone, Cic. To strike someone's breast with fear, Tacit. To terrify greatly. To harass someone with fear, Ter. To fill someone with dread, Plaut. To make someone terribly afraid, Id. To throw someone into fear; to dismay; to strike someone with horror, Liv.

units.la: Exterreri, vid. Expavescere.
units.tr: To be terrified, see to be alarmed.

units.la: Extollere, vid. Exaltare.
units.tr: To extol, see to exalt.

units.la: Extorquere] Elicere alicui lacrymas. Exsculpere in quaestione aliquid. Eripere agnum lupo. Plaut. Exterebrare, Id. Emungere aliquem, Ter. Extorquere per vim suffragium, Liv. Exprimere, Cic. Mordicus evellere, Hor.
units.tr: To extort] To draw tears from someone. To wring something out under questioning. To snatch the lamb from the wolf, Plaut. To bore out, Id. To blow someone's nose, Ter. To extort a vote by force, Liv. To squeeze out, Cic. To tear away with the teeth, Hor.

units.la: Extra, vid. Praeter.
units.tr: Outside, see beyond.

units.la: Extrahere] Trahere de medio aliquem. Subducere è puteo teo sursum. Intertrahere aquam omnem, Plaut.
units.tr: To extract] To draw someone out from the midst. To haul something up out of a well. To draw off all the water, Plaut.

units.la: Extraneus, vid. Peregrinus.
units.tr: Foreign, see stranger.

units.la: Extremum quid] Herculis columnae. Ultima Thule.
units.tr: An extreme thing] The Pillars of Hercules. Ultima Thule.

units.la: Extrema spes] Anchora sacra. Ad casum extremum deductus, Hirt.
units.tr: Last hope] The sacred anchor. Brought down to the final disaster, Hirt.

units.la: Extrema tentare] Ad sacram anchoram confugere. Ultima experiri. Summae rei periculum facere, Tac. Ad extrema descendere, Ad novissima auxilia. Extremam belli aleam experiri. Descendere in dimicationem vitae. Decernere de omnibus fortunis uno judicio, Cic. Si ad ultima periculi pervenietur, (ubi ultima necessitas denunciabitur] hoc agam.
units.tr: To attempt extremes] To flee to the sacred anchor. To try the last resources. To make trial of the peril of the whole matter, Tac. To go down to extremes; to the last aids. To try the final throw of war. To go down into the struggle for life. To decide all one's fortunes in a single judgment, Cic. If we come to the utmost peril (when the final necessity is announced), I will do this.

units.la: Ad extremum redactus] Ad incitas redactus.
units.tr: Reduced to the last extremity] Driven to straits.

units.la: In extremis malis] Inter malleum & incudem. Inter sacrum & saxum.
units.tr: In the greatest evils] Between the hammer and the anvil. Between the sacrifice and the rock.

units.la: Ab extremo ad extremum] A coelo usque ad terram.
units.tr: From one extreme to the other] From heaven to earth.

units.la: Extrema prospicienda] Si sapis, extrema prospectes. Quicquid agis, prudenter agas, & respice finem.
units.tr: Extremes to be foreseen] If you are wise, look to the end. Whatever you do, do it prudently, and keep the end in view.

units.la: Extrema in se transeunt, cohaerent] Commoditas quaevis sua fert incommoda secum. Compendium dispendium. Contrariorum eadem disciplina. Comes voluptatis dolor. Comitatur ruina proterviam, humiliationem gloria. Commodum sine aliquo incommodo esse nequit.
units.tr: Extremes pass into one another and cohere] Every advantage carries its disadvantages with it. Gain is loss. The same discipline governs opposites. Pain attends pleasure. Ruin accompanies arrogance; humiliation, glory. A benefit cannot exist without some drawback.

units.la: Extricare aliquid] Retriplicare plicam. Extricabor aliquâ. Facere expeditum aliquem ex impedito, Plaut. Evolvere complicata. Expedire aliquem nodum, Cic. Eluctari difficultates, Tacit. Expedire aliquem illigatum, Hor. Expedire impeditum, Ter. Vid. Eluctari.
units.tr: To disentangle something] To unfold a fold again. I will get myself out of it somehow. To free a man from hindrance, Plaut. To unroll what is folded. To untie a knot for someone, Cic. To struggle out of difficulties, Tacit. To free someone who is entangled, Hor. To free the entangled, Ter. See Eluctari.

units.la: Extrinsecus] Extra. Forinsecus. A foris, Plin.
units.tr: Outwardly] Outside; from without; from outside, Plin.

units.la: Extrudere aliquem] Extrudere aedibus, ex aedibus, Plaut. Expellere & exturbare aliquem domo. Proturbare extra tecta aliquem, Col. Proturbare domo, Apul. Eliminare aliquem, Varr. Quatere, Excludere aliquem foras, Ter. Exigere ex civitate aliquem, Cic. Emovere plebem de medio, Liv. Explodere aliquem in Arpinos.
units.tr: To thrust someone out] To thrust out of the house, out of the house, Plaut. To drive out and expel someone from home. To drive someone out from under the roof, Col. To turn someone out of doors, Apul. To banish someone, Varr. To shove someone out of doors, Ter. To expel someone from the state, Cic. To remove the common people from the midst, Liv. To hiss someone off to Arpinum.

units.la: Extusfire] Emoliri tussi aliquid, Celf. Edere tussi aliquid, Lucr.
units.tr: To cough out] To expel something by coughing, Celf. To bring up something by coughing, Lucr.

units.la: Exuberare, vid. Abundare.
units.tr: To overflow, see to abound.

units.la: Exul] Extorris à solo patriæ, Liv. Submotus patriâ, Ovid. Exclusus, Cic.
units.tr: Exile] One cast far from the soil of his fatherland, Liv. Removed from his fatherland, Ovid. Shut out, Cic.

units.la: Exulare] Vagus & exul error, & undique exclusus. Insulari solitudine damnari, Amm. Proficisci exilium, Atti. apud Non. Ire exilium, Catul.
units.tr: To be an exile] A wandering exile and outcast on every side. To be condemned to banishment on a lonely island, Amm. To set out into exile, Atti. in Non. To go into exile, Catul.

units.la: Exulcerare, vid. Irritare.
units.tr: To ulcerate, see to irritate.

units.la: Exundatio, vid. Eluvies.
units.tr: Overflow, see inundation.

units.la: Exundare] Stagnat Nilus, Virg. Undat. Redundat lacus, Cic. Inundat. Exspatians lacus, Plin. Restagnat locus, Col. Refusus pontus, Virg. Superfusus Tiberis, Liv, Exspatiatum flumen, Ovid. Excessit alveum Tiberis, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: To overflow] The Nile stagnates, Virg. It surges. The lake overflows, Cic. It inundates. The spreading lake, Plin. The place stagnates again, Col. The sea poured back, Virg. The Tiber poured over, Liv. The spreading river, Ovid. The Tiber left its bed, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Exuere] Exuere habitus regales, Stat. Hominem ex homine exuere. Ponere tunicam, Cic. Exsuvias facere, Plaut.
units.tr: To put off] To put off royal robes, Stat. To strip a man of his humanity. To put off a tunic, Cic. To make spoils, Plaut.

units.la: F.
units.tr: F.

units.la: FAba] Fabula, Plaut. Fabulus, Cato.
units.tr: Bean] Story, Plaut. Storyteller, Cato.

units.la: Fabale] Fabalia, Scal. Fabulum, Lucil. Fabale acus. Fabales alæ. Fabaginum acus, Cat. Fabalis stipula. Culmen fabæ, Ovid. Scapi fabarum. Caules fabarum, Plin.
units.tr: Of beans] Of beans, Scal. Fable, Lucil. Bean-stalk needle. Bean wings. Bean-stalk needle, Cat. Bean straw. The top of the bean, Ovid. Bean stalks. Bean cabbages, Plin.

units.la: Fabalis] Fabarius, fabaginus, fabatus, Cat. Fabales, Cato. Scalig.
units.tr: Of beans] Bean-like, bean-shaped, Cat. Of beans, Cato. Scalig.

units.la: Faber ærarius, vid. Ærarius.
units.tr: Bronze-smith, see coppersmith.

units.la: Faber ferrarius] Ferrarius, abs. Firm.
units.tr: Iron-smith] Blacksmith, abs. Firm.

units.la: Fabrica] Officina ferraria.
units.tr: Workshop] A smithy.

units.la: Fabula] Fabella. Apologus, Cic. Næniæ aniles, Iul. Cap. Fabularis historia, Suet. Mythistoria, Iul. Cap.
units.tr: Fable] A little story. A fable, Cic. Old wives' tales, Iul. Cap. A historical legend, Suet. Mythical history, Iul. Cap.

units.la: Fac ita esse, vid. Concedamus hoc.
units.tr: Suppose it is so, see let us grant this.

units.la: Facile aliquid] Creare fastidium, Plin. Præstare tutum iter, Cic. Faxo, Ter. Effectum habere, Cæs. Habeo rem factam, Mart.
units.tr: To make something easy] To create weariness, Plin. To provide a safe journey, Cic. I will do it, Ter. To have it done, Cæs. I have the thing done, Mart.

units.la: Facere aliquem talem vel talem] Reddere amicitiorem, otiosum, Cic.
units.tr: To make someone such or such] To make someone more friendly, more idle, Cic.

units.la: Facesse hinc, vid. Abi.
units.tr: Get away from here, see go away.

units.la: Facessere alicui negotium] Exhibere alicui molestiam. Negotium facere, Cic. Exhibere alicui laborem, Col. Objicere alicui laborem. Conjicere aliquem in malum. Injicere alicui scrupulum, Ter. Cic. Objicere alicui solicitudinem, Parere aegritudinem. Conjicere aliquem in tricas, Plaut.
units.tr: To give someone trouble] To cause someone annoyance. To make trouble, Cic. To cause someone toil, Col. To cast trouble upon someone. To throw someone into evil. To put a scruple into someone, Ter. Cic. To cast anxiety upon someone; to bring on distress. To throw someone into a tangle, Plaut.

units.la: Facete] Perfacete dicta. Persalsè & humaniter gratias egit. Festivè aliquid dissolvere, Cic. Lepidè, Plaut. Festiviter, festivissimè, Gell. Jocosè satis eum risi, Cic. Salsè; salsissimè dicere. Facetè & urbane irridere, Id.
units.tr: Wittily] Things said very wittily. He thanked him with great wit and courtesy. To dissolve something elegantly, Cic. Charmingly, Plaut. Wittily, most wittily, Gell. I laughed at him quite a lot in jest, Cic. To speak wittily, most wittily. To mock with wit and courtesy, Id.

units.la: Facetia] Urbanitas facetorum hominum. Lepos urbanitatis. Color urbanitatis. Facetia politissima. Festivitas sermonis. Lepos sermonis, facetiarum. Sal, & Sales facetiarum, Cic.
units.tr: Wit] The urbanity of witty men. The charm of urbanity. The colour of urbanity. Most polished wit. Liveliness of speech. The charm of speech and of wit. The salt and savour of wit, Cic.

units.la: Facetus] Facetus & dulcis festivique sermonis. Urbanus, falsus homo, Multa in homine jucunditas, & magnus in jocando lepos. Urbanitate limatus. Affluit omni lepore & venustate. Perfacetus. Tempestivus. Perlepidus, Cic. Fluit facetus. Graphicè facetus, Plaut. Merum sal, Lucr. Facetiis conditus. Disertus leporum & facetiarum, Catul. Jocosus, Hor.
units.tr: Witty] Witty and sweet and pleasant in speech. Urbane, a witty man. Much charm in the man, and great charm in jesting. Polished with urbanity. Overflowing with every charm and grace. Very witty. Opportune. Very charming, Cic. Flows wittily. Wittily witty, Plaut. Pure salt, Lucr. Seasoned with wit. Eloquent in charm and wit, Catul. Jesting, Hor.

units.la: Facies] Vultus animi imago, Cic. Oris species, Non. Os placidum, Ovid. Forma virginea, virilis, Ovid. Filum, Gell. Scitum filum mulieris, Plaut.
units.tr: Face] The image of the mind's expression, Cic. The appearance of the mouth, Non. A calm countenance, Ovid. A maidenly form, a manly form, Ovid. A thread, Gell. The clever thread of a woman, Plaut.

units.la: Facile] Perfacile. Expedite. Nullo labore, negotio, Perlevi momento, Procliviter est, quatenus amicitiae venia dari possit. Digitorum percussione haeredem fieri, Cic. Momento parvo. Faciliter, Vitr. Sine negotio, Plin. De praefacili, Plaut.
units.tr: Easy] Very easy. Readily. With no labour or business, in a very slight moment. It is easy enough, as far as pardon can be granted to friendship, Cic. To become heir by a snap of the fingers, Cic. In a small moment. Easily, Vitr. Without trouble, Plin. Concerning very easy things, Plaut.

units.la: Facile est] Hoc nihil est negotii. Nihil est negotii hoc facere. Ad manum est. In manu est. Praesto id est. Hoc in promptu mihi est, Cic. In expedito est. Expeditum est, Plin. In proclivi est. Ter. In facili est, Ter. Proclivi est, Plaut. In procinctu habeo, Quint. In numerato habeo, Vlp. Factu facile est, Lucr. Quam facile canis exsta edit, Tam in proclivi, quam imber. Tam facile, quam vulpes pyrum comest.
units.tr: It is easy] This is no trouble. It is no trouble to do this. It is at hand. It is in hand. This is ready to hand for me, Cic. It is ready, Plin. It is downhill, Ter. It is easy, Ter. It is downhill, Plaut. I have it in readiness, Quint. I have it in hand, Vlp. It is easy to do, Lucr. As easily as a dog eats the entrails; as downhill as rain; as easily as a fox eats a pear.

units.la: Facile aliena pericula spectare] E terrâ spectare naufragium.
units.tr: To watch others' dangers in safety] To watch a shipwreck from the land.

units.la: Facile intellectu] Puer quivis intelligat. In perfacili negotio versatur, Cic.
units.tr: Easily understood] Any boy would understand it. He is engaged in a very easy matter, Cic.

units.la: Facilia impera ] Factu proclivia jube.
units.tr: Easy commands] Order things that are easily done.

units.la: Facilis] Perfacilis. Proclive dictu. Facilis & prompta res. Facilis & expeditus ad dicendum; ad explicandum expeditissima. Nullâ re implicatus, Cic. Explicitus, Cæs. Minimi negotii, Suet. Inpulvis victoria, Vitr. Præfacilis, Plaut.
units.tr: Easy] Very easy. Easy to say. An easy and ready matter. Easy and ready in speaking; most ready in explaining. Entangled in nothing, Cic. Unfolded, Cæs. Of very little trouble, Suet. A victory won in the dust, Vitr. Very easy, Plaut.

units.la: Facilitas] Facultas pariendi, Ter.
units.tr: Facility] Ability to bear children, Ter.

units.la: Facinorosus] Scelestus, Flagitiosus. Nefarius. Improbitate & vitiis notus. Omnium scelerum maculis notissimus. In ore vulgi, atque in communibus proverbiis ejus nequitia versatur. Omnibus turpitudinis notis insignis. Post homines natos longè improbissimus. Perdità nequitiâ homo. Pilum viri boni non habet, Cic. Dedecore maculosus, Tac.
units.tr: Wicked] Villainous; shameful; impious. Known for wickedness and vices. Known by the stains of every crime. His wickedness is current on the lips of the common people and in common proverbs. Notable for every mark of baseness. By far the most wicked of all men born. A man of desperate wickedness. He has not the hair of a good man, Cic. Spotted with disgrace, Tac.

units.la: Facinus] Nefarium facinus, facinoris crimen. Malefactum, Cic. Cœptum immane.
units.tr: Crime] An impious deed; the charge of a crime. A misdeed, Cic. An enormous undertaking begun.

units.la: Facinora Magnanimi] Herculei labores.
units.tr: Deeds of the magnanimous] The labours of Hercules.

units.la: Factio] Distractio animorum humanorum. Divortium, Cic. Secessio, Id. Studium in partes diductum, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Faction] A division of human minds. A divorce, Cic. A secession, Id. A zeal split into parties, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Factiosus] Evocator servorum. Concitator & stimulator seditionis, Cic. Rerum novarum avidus concitator. Incentor & incensor turbarum. Turbulentus seditionum concitator, Amm. Turbator, Liv. Novarum rerum molitor, Sen.
units.tr: Factious] An inciter of slaves. An agitator and goader of sedition, Cic. An eager agitator for revolution. An inciter and inflamer of disturbances. A turbulent instigator of sedition, Amm. A disturber, Liv. A deviser of new things, Sen.

units.la: Factitius] Structilis,Col. Arte laboratus, Virg. Vid. Medicatus.
units.tr: Artificial] Built, Col. Wrought by art, Virg. See Medicated.

units.la: Factor] Auctor profectionis, Cæs. Suasor & author deditionis. Administer. Transactor. Artifex, fabricator. Effector. Molitor. Confector negotiorum. Creator, Cic. Machinator belli; Liv. Tu es huic rei caput, Ter. Conditor, Claud. Patrator, Tacit.
units.tr: Maker] Author of a departure, Cæs. Adviser and author of a surrender. Administrator. Negotiator. Artificer, fabricator. Effecter. Contriver. Accomplisher of affairs. Creator, Cic. Machinator of war, Liv. You are the head of this matter, Ter. Founder, Claud. Perpetrator, Tacit.

units.la: Factori in opus suum potestas est] Figulis ollis ansas pro voluptate ponit.
units.tr: The maker has power over his work] The potter puts handles on his jars as he pleases.

units.la: Facta Virum ostendunt] Facere Virorum est, loqui mulierum. lierum. Factis vult inspectari Græcia, non verbis.
units.tr: Deeds show men] It belongs to men to act and to women to talk. Greece wishes to be judged by deeds, not words.

units.la: Factum infectum non fit] Ab inferis nullus reditus. Quod periit, periit.
units.tr: What is done cannot be undone] There is no return from the dead. What has perished has perished.

units.la: In ipso facto] Recenti re, tempore, negotio. Calent rumores. Dum res calet, Cic. Nihil est nisi dum calet, id agitur, Plaut.
units.tr: In the very act] In a fresh matter, at a fresh time, in fresh business. Rumours are hot. While the thing is hot, Cic. There is nothing but while it is hot; that is what is at stake, Plaut.

units.la: Facultates] Possessio. Bona. Bona patria. Copiæ. Res. Vir magnâ cum re, sed plenus fidei. Post quam iam habere cœpit, est mortuus. Opes, Cic. Substantia, Quint. Tenere suum, Sen. Familia (pro ædibus & bonis) Suet. Pecunia, Plaut.
units.tr: Facultates] Possession. Goods. Patrimony. Resources. Property. A man of substance, but full of good faith. Soon after he had begun to be rich, he died. Wealth, Cic. Estate, Quint. To keep one's own, Sen. Household (for house and goods), Suet. Money, Plaut.

units.la: Facundè] Facundissime, Gell. Sen. Diserte, Cic. Eloquentissime, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Facundè] Most eloquently, Gell. Sen. Fluently, Cic. Most eloquently, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Facundus] Perfacundus, Iustin. Facundiosus, Gell. Facundiâ validus, Plin. Iun. A facundia multum potest, Ter. Nestoria Eloquentia. Mercurio facundior. Demosthene, Nestore facundior, Er.
units.tr: Facundus] Very eloquent, Iustin. Rather eloquent, Gell. Strong in eloquence, Plin. Iun. He has great power through eloquence, Ter. Nestorian eloquence. More eloquent than Mercury. More eloquent than Demosthenes or Nestor, Er.

units.la: Feces] Fæx, Apul. Crassamen in fundo liquidorum subsidens, Col.
units.tr: Feces] Dregs, Apul. Thick sediment settling at the bottom of liquids, Col.

units.la: Faculentus] Fæciniæ uvæ; multum fæcis afferentes, Col. Fæcinum vinum, Id. Fæcatum vinum, Cat. Nimius fæce, Plin. Tryginum atramentum, Id.
units.tr: Faculentus] Full of lees. Grapes yielding much lees, Col. Wine with lees, Id. Wine clouded with lees, Cat. Too full of lees, Plin. Thick ink, Id.

units.la: Fallacia] Techna, Ter. Perfidia. Fucus, Cic. Impostura, Vlp. Fraudulentia. Præstigiæ, Captio, Er. Vid. Deceptio.
units.tr: Fallacia] Trickery, Ter. Treachery. Pretence, Cic. Imposture, Vlp. Fraudulence. Tricks, deceit, Er. See Deceptio.

units.la: Fallacia elusa] Rete hoc nihil attraxit.
units.tr: Fallacia elusa] This net has caught nothing.

units.la: Fallax] Falsus. Mendosus. Adumbrata Comitia. Fucosus, fucatus, Cic. Falsiloquus, falsidicus, Plaut. Laborat à veritate, Liv. Adulterinus nidus, Plin. Nulla fide, Plaut. Coloratum crimen, Amm.
units.tr: Fallax] False. Faulty. Sham elections. Feigned, painted over, Cic. Speaking falsely, Plaut. Strays from the truth, Liv. A counterfeit nest, Plin. Without faith, Plaut. A coloured charge, Amm.

units.la: Fallaci nunquam credendum] Cavendum ab eo, qui semel imposuit.
units.tr: Fallaci nunquam credendum] One must never trust a deceiver; beware of the man who has deceived once.

units.la: Fallentem fallere licet] Cretiza cum Cretensi.
units.tr: Fallentem fallere licet] One may deceive the deceiver: to play the Cretan with a Cretan.

units.la: Fallere aliquem] Fucum facere alicui. Fallaciam intendere. Vid. Decipere.
units.tr: Fallere aliquem] To make a dupe of someone. To set a snare. See Decipere.

units.la: Fallendi causæ variæ] Fallacia alia aliam trudit.
units.tr: Fallendi causæ variæ] The reasons for deceiving are various: one deceit drives on another.

units.la: Fallere volentem nemo evitare potest] Sycophantarum morsus inevitabilis.
units.tr: Fallere volentem nemo evitare potest] No one can avoid one who is set on deceiving; the bite of the sycophants is unavoidable.

units.la: Fallere alicujus desideria] Corvum delusit hiantem.
units.tr: Fallere alicujus desideria] He cheated the gaping crow.

units.la: Fallere velle] Advocare artes. Omnes adhibere machinas ad tenendum aliquem. Commoliri dolum, Cic. Astutiam instituere. Dolare dolum. Procudere, confuere dolos. Fabrefacere fallaciam, facere technas adversum aliquem, Fallaciam in aliquem intendere, Plaut. Suere aliquid alicujus capiti, Ter. Intendere dolum, Curt. Manticulari, Pacuv. Adire manum alicui, Vid. Decipere.
units.tr: Fallere velle] To summon arts. To bring every contrivance to bear to hold someone fast. To plot a trick, Cic. To set up cunning. To hew out a trick. To forge and stitch together tricks. To fashion deceit, to make tricks against someone, to aim deceit at someone, Plaut. To sew something onto someone's head, Ter. To lay a trap, Curt. To cheat, Pacuv. To approach someone's hand. See Decipere.

units.la: Falli] Errare. Decepit exspectationem meam, Non respondit votis, Cic. Vid. Errare.
units.tr: Falli] To err. It disappointed my expectation; it did not answer my prayers, Cic. See Errare.

units.la: Ni fallor] Cic. Nisi longe fallor opinione. Nisi me mea fallit opinio. Nisi meam opinionem res fallit. Nisi me fallo. Nisi me omnia fallunt. Nisi quid me fallit, Cic. Nisi me animus fallit, Ter. Nisi fallor. Si quid veri mens augurat, Virg.
units.tr: Ni fallor] Cic. Unless I am far wrong in my opinion. Unless my opinion deceives me. Unless the facts disappoint my opinion. Unless I deceive myself. Unless everything deceives me.
