Unless something escapes me, Cic. Unless my mind deceives me, Ter. Unless I am mistaken. If my mind divines anything true, Virg.

units.la: Falli & labi humanum est] Quandoque bonus dormitat Homerus. Humanum est errare; sed diabolicum in errore perseverare. Vid. Decipi.
units.tr: Falli & labi humanum est] Sometimes good Homer nods. To err is human, but to persist in error is devilish. See Decipi.

units.la: Falsare] Adulterare jus, Cic. Supponere falsa testamenta. Corrumpere literas, chirographa, Vlp. Vitiare, fucare, interlinere, Cic. Nummos cudere plumbeos, Plaut.
units.tr: Falsare] To corrupt the law, Cic. To substitute false wills. To corrupt letters and handwritings, Vlp. To vitiate, paint over, interline, Cic. To coin leaden money, Plaut.

units.la: Falsarius] Adulterator monetae, IC. Interversor. Conturbator rationum, Turneb. Testamentarius, Cic. Adulterator testamenti, Bud. Reus falsi in C.
units.tr: Falsarius] A counterfeiter of coin, IC. An embezzler. A disturber of accounts, Turneb. A forger of wills, Cic. A falsifier of a will, Bud. Accused of forgery in C.

units.la: False] Falso. Mendose, fallaciter, Cic. Fabulose, Plin. Procul vero, Col. Perperam insimulari, Plaut. Non ex fide.
units.tr: False] Falsely. Mendaciously, deceitfully, Cic. Fabulously, Plin. Far from the truth, Col. To accuse wrongly, Plaut. Not in good faith.

units.la: Falsitas] Falsum, fidem non habet. A rei veritate distat. Vanitati veritas cedat, fallaciloquentia. Absonum fidei, Cic. Procul vero, Col. Procul a vero, Ovid. Remotum longe a vera ratione. Reclamat ratio vera, Lucr. Majora, vel minora vero, Tac. Abhorret vero, Liv. Non cohaerent, Ter. Falsimonium, Plaut. Cavillatio, Quint.
units.tr: Falsitas] What is false has no credit. It is far from the truth of the matter. Let truth give way to vanity and lying speech. Discordant with faith, Cic. Far from the truth, Col. Far from the truth, Ovid. Removed far from sound reasoning. True reason protests, Lucr. Greater or less than the truth, Tac. Clashes with the truth, Liv. Do not cohere, Ter. Deceit, falsehood, Plaut. Quibbling, Quint.

units.la: Falx] Falx messoria, Vlp. Denticulata, Col. Stramentaria, Cat. Falcula, Id. Vid. Secula.
units.tr: Falx] A reaping-hook, Vlp. Toothed, Col. For cutting straw, Cat. A little sickle, Id. See Secula.

units.la: Fama, i.e. claritas nominis] Famella, Fest. Gloria. Gloriola, Nomen, Cic. Titulus, Ovid. Adorea, Claud. Claritudo, tudo, Sisen. Euclea (herba, concilians bonam famam eâ perun-ctis,) Plin.
units.tr: Fama, i.e. claritas nominis] Little fame, Fest. Glory. A little glory, a name, Cic. Title, Ovid. Honour, Claud. Brightness, clarity, Sisen. Euclea (an herb which wins a good reputation for those anointed with it), Plin.

units.la: Fama, id est, vulgi sermo, vid. Rumor.
units.tr: Fama, id est, vulgi sermo, see Rumor.

units.la: Fama incerta, vid. Rumor incertus.
units.tr: Fama incerta, see Rumor incertus.

units.la: Fama de remotis major] Minuit praesentia famam. Advena fama venit semper majoribus alis.
units.tr: Fama de remotis major] Presence diminishes fame. A rumour that arrives from afar always comes on greater wings.

units.la: Fama communis non semper falsa] Rumor publicus non omnino frustra. Vox populi, vox Dei.
units.tr: Fama communis non semper falsa] Public rumour is not altogether groundless. The voice of the people is the voice of God.

units.la: Fama bonae studendum] Famae bonae patrocinium deserere, dissoluti est, Polit.
units.tr: Fama bonæ studendum] To abandon the defence of one's good name is the mark of a dissolute man, Polit.

units.la: Famâ adversâ] Infamissimè, Iul. Cap. Parum secundâ famâ, Asiam administrans, Suet.
units.tr: Famâ adversâ] Most infamously, Iul. Cap. With not very favourable repute, administering Asia, Suet.

units.la: Famam benè meriti diffamare] De possessione aliquem dejicere.
units.tr: Famam benè meriti diffamare] To dispossess someone of his property.

units.la: Fama alicujus derogare aliquid] Detrahere de famâ, de laudibus alicujus. Obterere laudem alicujus res gestas. Imminuere laudem alicujus. Cic. Obtrectare laudes, & laudibus alicujus, Liv. Elevare famam, Tac. Atterere famam alicujus, Salust. Demere aliquid laudi, Ovid. Forcillare, furcillare, vel furcilare fidem alicujus, Plaut. Vid. Diffamare.
units.tr: Fama alicujus derogare aliquid] To take something away from someone's reputation, from his praises. To crush someone's praise for his achievements. To diminish someone's praise, Cic. To disparage someone's praises, Liv. To lower a reputation, Tac. To wear away someone's fame, Salust. To take something from someone's praise, Ovid. To undermine someone's credit, Plaut. See Diffamare.

units.la: Fame comprimere aliquem] Inferre famem civibus, Cic. Compescere fame, Sen. Perduci ad exitiabilem famem, Paterc. Abstinere aliquem, Sen. Celf.
units.tr: Fame comprimere aliquem] To bring hunger upon the citizens, Cic. To curb by hunger, Sen. To be brought to deadly famine, Paterc. To keep someone from food, Sen. Celf.

units.la: Fame perire] Inediâ consumi. Fame confici, enecari, Cic. Esurigo findit costas, Varr.
units.tr: Fame perire] To be consumed by starvation. To be worn down and done to death by hunger, Cic. Hunger splits the ribs, Varr.

units.la: Fame confectus] Fame enectus, Cic. Corpus aridum esuritione, Catull.
units.tr: Fame confectus] Killed by hunger, Cic. A body dried up by hunger, Catull.

units.la: Famelicus] Fame laborat, Col. Esuritor, Hor. Miserabile vulgus in pecudum cecidit cibos. Plurima humanis incognita mensis diripit, Lucan. Neque jejuniosiorem neque magis effartum fame vidi, Plaut.
units.tr: Famelicus] Suffers from hunger, Col. A hungry man, Hor. The wretched crowd fell upon the food of beasts. He tears at many things unknown to human tables, Lucan. I have seen neither a more famished nor a more wasted man with hunger, Plaut.

units.la: Famelico omnia sapiunt] Fames praeter seipsam edulcat omnia. Fames suavissimum cibi condimentum. Esurienti omnis panis dulcis. Jejunus stomachus raro vulgaria temnit, Hor.
units.tr: Famelico omnia sapiunt] Hunger sweetens everything except itself. Hunger is the sweetest seasoning of food. To the hungry every bread is sweet. An empty stomach seldom scorns common fare, Hor.

units.la: Fames] Esuriales feriae, Plaut. Rabies, Poët. Esurigo findens costas, Varr.
units.tr: Fames] Fasting days, Plaut. Madness, Poët. Hunger splitting the ribs, Varr.

units.la: Fames magistra] Fames malesuada. Venter ingeniosa corporis pars, Varr.
units.tr: Fames magistra] Hunger the bad counsellor. The belly, the ingenious part of the body, Varr.

units.la: Fames magna] Saguntina fames.
units.tr: Fames magna] Saguntine famine.

units.la: Fames non sedatur verbis] Venter caret auribus. Famem non sedat splendida coena, sed solida, Molestus interpellator venter.
units.tr: Fames non sedatur verbis] The belly has no ears. A splendid dinner does not appease hunger, but a solid one does. The belly is an annoying interrupter.

units.la: Famem sedare] Fami dentes excutere.
units.tr: Famem sedare] To knock out one's teeth for hunger.

units.la: Familia] Famulitium, Varr. Famularis turba, Suet. Servitia, Cic.
units.tr: Familia] Service, Varr. A household crowd of servants, Suet. Servants, Cic.

units.la: Familia (2)] Domus nobilis. Genus, Cic. Prosapia vetus, Salust.
units.tr: Familia (2)] A noble house. Lineage, Cic. Ancient stock, Salust.

units.la: Familiaris alicujus] De ejus sinu, delectu, Cic. Fidelis, Lamp. Homines à latere, Curt. Peculiaris alicujus, Suet. Continuus alicujus, Tac. Alter ille. Ut larem familiarem colere aliquem. Ex intimis ejus est. In intimis ejus est. Intercedit mihi cum illo amicitia. Vid. Dilectus. Socius.
units.tr: Familiaris alicujus] One of his inner circle, his choice, Cic. Faithful, Lamp. Men at one's side, Curt. A personal friend of someone, Suet. Constant companion of someone, Tac. The other self. To honour someone as one's household god. He is among his intimates. He is among his intimates. Friendship exists between me and him. See Dilectus. Socius.

units.la: Familiaritas, vid. Societas.
units.tr: Familiaritas, see Societas.

units.la: Familiariter] Amicè. Amicissimè & conjunctissimè vivere cum aliquo. Intra parietes disceptare & experiri, Cic.
units.tr: Familiariter] Amicably. To live with someone most amicably and intimately. To discuss and try things within the walls, Cic.

units.la: Familiariter uti aliquo] Familiaris, familiarissimus sum alicui. Valdè familiariter, familiarissimè cum aliquo vivere. Multùm uti aliquo, familiarissimè. Versari in familiaritate alicujus. Magno usu familiaritatis cum eo conjunctus sum. Familiaritate est mihi, vel, ego sum illi, conjunctus. Nihil est familiaritate nostrâ conjunctius. Est mihi cum illo usus, consuetudo, societas. Feci, inivi cum eo omnium rerum societatem. Multa & jucundâ consuetudine inter nos conjuncti sumus. Inter se conjunctissimi sunt. Multum est mecum Epicrates. Implicare se societate aliquorum. Implicare se aliquibus. Implicor familiaritatibus, Cic. Omnia mihi sunt cum illo, Id. Neminem cum quo plura sint mihi, Plaut.
units.tr: Familiariter uti aliquo] I am intimate with someone, most intimate. To live with someone on very familiar terms, most intimately. To make great use of someone on the most intimate terms. To move in someone's intimacy. I am joined to him by long and close familiarity. I am bound to him in familiarity, or he is bound to me. Nothing is more closely joined than our familiarity. I have dealings, custom and fellowship with him. I made with him, and entered into, a partnership in all things. We are joined by much and pleasant intercourse. They are most closely joined to one another. Epicrates is much with me. To entangle oneself in the fellowship of some. To involve oneself with some people. I am entangled in intimacies, Cic. I have everything in common with him, Id. There is no one with whom I have more in common, Plaut.

units.la: Famosus libellus] Famosum carmen. Famosum epigramma scriptum. Infame carmen, Ovid. Criminosus liber, Suet. Impleantur meæ fores elogiorum carbonibus, Plaut. Felcennini versus, Macrob.
units.tr: Famosus libellus] A defamatory poem. A written defamatory epigram. A disgraceful poem, Ovid. An accusatory book, Suet. Let my doors be covered with charcoal scrawls of verses, Plaut. Fescennine verses, Macrob.

units.la: Famulari] In famulatu esse. Deservire alicui. Ancillari alicui, Cic. Servire, Ter. Servire apud aliquem. Dare operam Domino, Plaut. Locare operam suam alicui, Gell.
units.tr: Famulari] To be in service. To be at someone's service. To wait upon someone as a maid, Cic. To serve, Ter. To serve with someone. To give service to one's master, Plaut. To hire out one's labour to someone, Gell.

units.la: Famulus] Stator. Administer. Victus quotidiani puer. Familiaris. Pedisequus. Assecla. Assectator alicujus. Ministrator. Minister, Cic. Præminister, Macrob.
units.tr: Famulus] An attendant. A helper. A boy who lives on daily bread. A household member. A lackey. A follower. A follower of someone. A servant. A minister, Cic. A chief servant, Macrob.

units.la: Famulitium] Famulatus, Comitatus, Cic. Famuletium, Fest. Ministerium, Plin. Iun. Nobile servitium, Stat. Ministeria, Paul. IC. Ambacti, Caes.
units.tr: Famulitium] Service, retinue, Cic. Small service, Fest. Ministry, service, Plin. Iun. Noble servitude, Stat. Services, Paul. IC. Retainers, Caes.

units.la: Fanum] Idolium, Tertull. Delubrum, Cic. Lararium, Lamp.
units.tr: Fanum] A temple of idols, Tertull. A shrine, Cic. A household shrine, Lamp.

units.la: Farcire] Infarcire, Plin. Infercire, Bud. Lambin. Infulcire, Suet. Offercire, Sipont. Obesare, vel obescare pane triticeo avem, Colum.
units.tr: Farcire] To stuff in, Plin. To stuff in, Bud. Lambin. To cram, Suet. To stuff, Sipont. To fatten a bird with wheaten bread, Colum.

units.la: Fari, vid. Loqui.
units.tr: Fari, see Loqui.

units.la: Farina] Far, Col. Far salsum, Ovid. Mola salsa. Plaut. Far molitum, Dou.
units.tr: Farina] Spelt, Col. Salted spelt, Ovid. Salted meal, Plaut. Ground spelt, Dou.

units.la: Farina aqua subacta] Farina subacta, Cat. Conspersa, Id. Pistrinarum opera, Plin.
units.tr: Farina aqua subacta] Flour kneaded with water. Kneaded flour, Cat. Sprinkled, Id. The work of bakeries, Plin.

units.la: Farinaceus] Farinulentus, Apul. Farreus, Turneb. Farraceus, Id. Farrarius, Cato.
units.tr: Farinaceus] Mealy, Apul. Of spelt, Turneb. Of spelt, Id. Of spelt, Cato.

units.la: Fartilis, vid. Altilis.
units.tr: Fartilis, see Altilis.

units.la: Fartum] Fartile, Subst. Plin. Fartura, Col.
units.tr: Fartum] Stuffing, as a noun, Plin. Stuffing, Col.

units.la: Fartus] Farctus ventriculus, Plin. Confertus cibo. Refertus, Cic. Offertus. Offertissimus aliquâ re. Collativus venter, Plaut. Stipatus, Ovid. Effertissimus, Lambi.
units.tr: Fartus] A distended stomach, Plin. Crammed with food. Stuffed full, Cic. Overfilled. Most overfilled with something. A bloated belly, Plaut. Packed tight, Ovid. Most stuffed, Lambi.

units.la: Fas est] Æquum est. Æquum & bonum. Æquitas causæ. Jus postulas. Optimum atque æquissimum oras. Verum est, Cic. Æquum bonum, Ter. Fas & jura sinunt, Virg. Rationabile est, Pompon. Par est, Lucr.
units.tr: Fas est] It is right. It is fair and good. The fairness of the case. You ask for what is just. You ask for what is best and most equitable. It is true, Cic. A fair and good thing, Ter. Divine law and justice allow it, Virg. It is reasonable, Pompon. It is fitting, Lucr.

units.la: Fascia] Incunabula, Plaut. Sunt involucra lanea vel linea, Taubm.
units.tr: Fascia] Swaddling clothes, Plaut. They are wrappings of wool or linen, Taubm.

units.la: Fasciculus] Scopa manualis herbæ, Plin. Fasces viminei, Plaut. Mataxa, Kitr.
units.tr: Fasciculus] A hand-broom of herbs, Plin. Bundles of twigs, Plaut. A bundle of rods, Kitr.

units.la: Fasti] Libri computationem dierum continentes, Serv. Fastus, ûs. Scal. Lucan.
units.tr: Fasti] Books containing the reckoning of days, Serv. Fastus, ûs. Scal. Lucan.

units.la: Fastidire] Odium atque fastidium ad aliquem habere. Non posse fastidium alicujus. Nauseare aliquid, Cic. Damnare. Bilem movere præfastidio, stidio, Plaut. Abhorret alicui animus à vel, ab. Tædet me eadem audire millies, Ter. Vid. Abhorrere.
units.tr: Fastidire] To have hatred and disgust toward someone. To be unable to stomach someone. To feel nausea at something, Cic. To condemn. To stir up bile through disdain, Plaut. The mind shrinks from something or someone. I am sick of hearing the same things a thousand times, Ter. See Abhorrere.

units.la: Fastidienti nihil ad palatum] Febricitanti omnia amara.
units.tr: Fastidienti nihil ad palatum] To one with a fever, everything is bitter.

units.la: Fastidium] Nausea, Col. Nauseola, Cic. Fœditas spectaculi, Liv. Horror, Apul.
units.tr: Fastidium] Nausea, Col. A slight nausea, Cic. The foulness of a spectacle, Liv. Horror, Apul.

units.la: Fastidium movere alicui] Fastidium, tædium, alicujus rei facere, Liv. Fastidium alicui afferre, Cic. Adducere aliquid in fastidium. Fastidium alicui creare, gignere, Plin. Fastidium stomacho movere, Hor.
units.tr: Fastidium movere alicui] To cause someone loathing and weariness of something, Liv. To bring disgust upon someone, Cic. To bring something into disgust. To create and beget disgust in someone, Plin. To stir disgust in the stomach, Hor.

units.la: Fastigium] Summum alicujus rei, Plaut. Vertex, Lucr. Culmen, Virg. Cacumen, Plin. Apex, Ovid. Caput arboris, Sen. Vid. Cacumen.
units.tr: Fastigium] The top of something, Plaut. A peak, Lucr. A summit, Virg. A tip, Plin. An apex, Ovid. The crown of a tree, Sen. See Cacumen.

units.la: Fastuosus, vid. Superbus.
units.tr: Fastuosus, see Superbus.

units.la: Fastus] Tumor animi & sublatio. Supercilium Campanum, Cic. Campana superbia. Vid. Superbia.
units.tr: Fastus] Swelling and elation of spirit. A Campanian eyebrow, Cic. Campanian pride. See Superbia.

units.la: Fastum alicui demere] De pulmone revellere, Pers. (Animi enim tumorem in pulmone locant.)
units.tr: Fastum alicui demere] To tear out someone's lung, Pers. (For they place the swelling of the spirit in the lung.)

units.la: Fatalis] Inevitabilis, Plin. Iun. Indeclinabilis, Sen. Gell. Indeclinatus, Ovid. Ineluctabilis, Virg.
units.tr: Fatalis] Unavoidable, Plin. Iun. Unalterable, Sen. Gell. Not to be turned aside, Ovid. Inescapable, Virg.

units.la: Fateri] Confiteri de maleficio. Fateor etiam atque etiam profiteor, & præ me fero. Hoc non solum confiteor, sed etiam profiteor. Cognoscere manum suam, Cic. Haud cunctanter de se ipso fassus, Liv. Agnoscere debitum, Paul. IC. Ignosci orat. Confitetur, Ter.
units.tr: Fateri] To confess a crime. I admit it again and again, and openly profess it and display it. I not only confess this but also openly profess it. To know one's own hand, Cic. Having spoken of himself without hesitation, Liv. To acknowledge a debt, Paul. IC. To beg for pardon. He confesses, Ter.

units.la: Fatigare] Defatigare judices, Cic. Lassare aliquem, Mart. Delassare, Hor. Concitatè agere pecus, eò usque dum anhelat, Col. Nervos eligat omnes, Lucil.
units.tr: Fatigare] To wear out judges, Cic. To tire someone out, Mart. To weary, Hor. To drive a flock hard until it pants, Col. Let him choose all the sinews, Lucil.

units.la: Fatigari] Defatigari laboribus, Cic. Lassescere in labore, Plin. Lassari in arena. Lassari artus, Ovid. Fatigari æstu, Cas. Nos defessi quærere, vos reperire, i. e. quærendo, Plaut. Fatiscere sudore, Stat. Succumbere. Frangere nervos mentis & corporis, Cic. Neque [illegible, ~2 letters] ctiscar, Ter.
units.tr: Fatigari] To be worn out by labours, Cic. To grow weary at work, Plin. To be tired in the arena. Limbs grow tired, Ovid. To be exhausted by the heat, Cas. We, weary, seek; you find, that is, by seeking, Plaut. To faint with sweat, Stat. To give way. To break the sinews of mind and body, Cic. Neque [illegible] ctiscar, Ter.

units.la: Fatigatio] Lassitudo. Defatigatio corporis, Cic.
units.tr: Fatigatio] Weariness. Wearing out of the body, Cic.

units.la: Fatigatus] Defatigatus animus. Defessus labore, negotiis. Fessus de via, Cic. Defessus qui sit eundo. Lassus opere faciundo. Lassus de via, Plaut. [illegible, ~6 letters] , Effluxere vires lassilassitudine, Liv. Lassatus aliquâ re, Iuv. Lassulus, Catul. Exantlatus, Cic.
units.tr: Fatigatus] A worn-out mind. Worn out with toil and business. Tired from the road, Cic. Worn out with going on. Weary from working. Tired from the road, Plaut. [illegible] , strength has drained away through weariness, Liv. Wearied by something, Juv. A little weary, Catul. Exhausted, Cic.

units.la: Fatis non resistendum] Queri mollitia est, reluctari insania, fatis, Lipf.
units.tr: Fatis non resistendum] To complain is weakness, to struggle against fate is madness, Lipf.

units.la: Fatiscere, vid. Dehiscere, fatigari.
units.tr: Fatiscere, see Dehiscere, fatigari.

units.la: Fatum] Inevitabile fatum. Æternale, Sen.
units.tr: Fatum] Unavoidable fate. Eternal, Sen.

units.la: Fatuus] Perfatuus, Mart. A bona mente abest. Naviget Anticyras, Hor. Morus, Plaut. Si quando fatuo delectari volo, non longè mihi quærendus est, me video, Sen. Ep. 36, Excors, Vecors, Cic. Cor illi abest, Mart. Bliteus. Betaceus, Er.
units.tr: Fatuus] Utterly foolish, Mart. Lacking good sense. Let him sail to Anticyra, Hor. A fool, Plaut. If ever I want to amuse myself with a fool, I need not look far; I see myself, Sen. Ep. 36. Witless, senseless, Cic. He has no heart, Mart. Bliteus. Betaceus, Er.

units.la: Favens] Studiosus, studiosissimus mei. Deditus fuit gratiæ & voluntati eorum. Fautor, Cic. Fautrix, Ter. Auspicabilis, Id. Devotus. Devotissimus Reipub. Sen.
units.tr: Favens] Eager, most eager on my behalf. Devoted to their favour and will. A patron, Cic. A female patron, Ter. Auspicious, Id. Devoted. Most devoted to the Republic, Sen.

units.la: Favere alicui] Cupere alicui, Cæs. Alicujus causâ vehementer cupere. Tuâ causâ omnia magnopere volo. Libentissimè alicui tribuere. Deditus sum alicui. Studere alicui, Cic. Afflare alicui auram, Id. Subscribere votis alicujus, Ovid. Annuere cœptis alicujus, Virg. Premere pollicem, Hor. Ex animo benè velle alicui, Ter. Gremio complecti, fovere aliquem.
units.tr: Favere alicui] To wish someone well, Caes. To desire intensely for someone's cause. I wish everything greatly for your sake. To grant most willingly to someone. I am devoted to someone. To be zealous for someone, Cic. To breathe a breeze upon someone, Id. To subscribe to someone's wishes, Ovid. To nod assent to someone's undertakings, Virg. To press the thumb, Hor. To wish someone well from the heart, Ter. To embrace someone in one's lap, to cherish someone.

units.la: Favet mihi] Gratiosus sum apud illum. Teneo illius gratiam. Æquo, benigno illo utor. Facilem habeo. Propendet in me inclinatione voluntatis. Persequitur me benevolentiâ. Animatus erga me, Cic. Valeo apud illum gratiâ, Plin. Iun. Indulgentissimè in me confert omnia, Sen.
units.tr: Favet mihi] I am in his good graces. I hold his favour. I enjoy his kind and gentle disposition. I have him well disposed. He leans toward me with an inclination of his will. He pursues me with goodwill. He is well disposed toward me, Cic. I have influence with him through favour, Plin. Iun. He bestows everything upon me most indulgently, Sen.

units.la: Favilla] Vivus cinis.
units.tr: Favilla] Living ash.

units.la: Faunus] Satyrus, Cic. Semifer, Virg. Semihomo, Col.
units.tr: Faunus] A satyr, Cic. Half-beast, Virg. Half-man, Col.

units.la: Favonius] Zephyrus, Sen.
units.tr: Favonius] Zephyr, Sen.

units.la: Favor] Affectus amoris. Favonius gratiæ. Secunda voluntas, Cic. Vid. Benevolentia.
units.tr: Favor] Affection of love. The west wind of grace. Goodwill, Cic. See Benevolentia.

units.la: Favor fortunam sequitur] Quò se fortuna, eò & favor hominum inclinat. Omnes inclinamus in felicem parietem.
units.tr: Favor fortunam sequitur] Wherever fortune turns, there the favour of men also leans. We all lean toward the wall of the fortunate man.

units.la: Faustè, vid. Feliciter.
units.tr: Faustè, see Feliciter.

units.la: Faustus, vid. Felix.
units.tr: Faustus, see Felix.

units.la: Fax] Tæda candens, Cic. Facula, Propert. Lampas, Pers. Facem præferens] Daduchus, Mart. Faxo] Faxit, Plaut. Faxis, Ter. Faxitis, Liv. Faxint,Ter. Faciam cavebunt, Plaut.
units.tr: Fax] A shining torch, Cic. A little torch, Propert. A lamp, Pers. Carrying a torch: a torch-bearer, Mart. Faxo: he will make it so: faxit, Plaut.; faxis, Ter.; faxitis, Liv.; faxint, Ter.; they will take care, faciam cavebunt, Plaut.

units.la: Febricitare] Febrire, Cels. Jactari febri. Habere febrim, Cic. Calere febre,Iuv. Est febris,Id. Febris illum habet, Sen. Aduri, decoqui ardore febris, Firm. Ardore febrili æ-stuat, Apul. Depascitur artus febris, Virg. Peruri febri, Plin.lun.
units.tr: Febricitare] To have a fever, Cels. To be tossed about by fever. To have a fever, Cic. To be hot with fever, Juv. He has a fever, Id. The fever has him, Sen. To be burned and boiled by the heat of fever, Firm. He seethes with feverish heat, Apul. Fever devours his limbs, Virg. To be burned by fever, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Febris ardens] Causodes scil. febris, Cels. Flagrans febris, Firm. Acuta febris, vehemens. Intentio febris, Cels. Ardor febrilis, Apul. Ardor febrium incredibilis, Plin. Incendium absque Vulcano.
units.tr: Febris ardens] A burning fever, Cels. A blazing fever, Firm. A sharp, violent fever. The intensity of a fever, Cels. Feverish heat, Apul. The heat of fevers is incredible, Plin. A fire without Vulcan.

units.la: Febris continua] Febris continuata, continens. Continuant febres. Continuatur febris, Cels.
units.tr: Febris continua] A continued, unbroken fever. Fevers continue. The fever continues, Cels.

units.la: Febris intermittens] Intervallata febris biduo, triduo, Amm.
units.tr: Febris intermittens] A fever interrupted by an interval of two or three days, Amm.

units.la: Febris tertiana] Tertiana abs. Plin. Semitertiana febris, Cels. Hemitritaeus, qui hanc patitur, Mart.
units.tr: Febris tertiana] A tertian fever, Plin. A semitertian fever, Cels. A hemitritaeus, one who suffers from it, Mart.

units.la: Febris quartana] Quartana, Cic. Febris quadrini circuitus, Plin. Febris quartis diebus recurrens, Gell.
units.tr: Febris quartana] A quartan fever, Cic. The cycle of a quartan fever, Plin. A fever returning every fourth day, Gell.

units.la: Febris oritur] Corripior febri, Plin. Tentor febri, Cic. Concipit sese febris, Cels. Cooritur febris, Lucr. Init me febris, Plaut.
units.tr: Febris oritur] I am seized by fever, Plin. I am afflicted by fever, Cic. The fever takes hold of itself, Cels. The fever arises together, Lucr. The fever seizes me, Plaut.

units.la: Febris remittit.] Inclinat se febris, decrescit levatur, minuitur, remittit se, remittitur ex toto, levior fit, finitur, quiescit, conquiescit, evanescit, crescere desiit, Cels. Decedit febris. Quartana a te discessit, Cic.
units.tr: Febris remittit] The fever bends down, decreases, is lightened, diminished, relaxes, is remitted altogether, grows milder, ends, rests, subsides, vanishes, and has ceased to increase, Cels. The fever departs. The quartan fever has left you, Cic.

units.la: Fecialis, vid. Caduceator.
units.tr: Fecialis, see Caduceator.

units.la: Felicitas, vid. Fortuna.
units.tr: Felicitas, see Fortuna.

units.la: Felicitas securos facit] Res secundae securitatem pariunt.
units.tr: Felicitas securos facit] Prosperity produces security.

units.la: Felix] Fortuna illi felicitatem dedit. Felicitate semper utitur. Summa ejus est felicitas. Fortunatus homo. Nihil est illo fortunatius, Cic. Vid. Fortunatus.
units.tr: Felix] Fortune gave him happiness. He always enjoys good fortune. His chief good is his happiness. A fortunate man. Nothing is more fortunate than he, Cic. See Fortunatus.

units.la: Felix, i. felicitatem ferens] Boni, optimi ominis. Secundus ventus. Faustus dies, Cic. Bene ominatus. Candidus favonius, Hor. Auspicatus, Plin. Nec auspicatior in Lesbo arbor. Auspicatissimum exordium, Quint.
units.tr: Felix, i.e. bringing happiness] Of good, best omen. A favourable wind. A lucky day, Cic. Well omened. A bright west wind, Hor. Auspicious, Plin. Nor was any tree more auspicious on Lesbos. A most auspicious beginning, Quint.

units.la: Felix temeritas, vid. Temeritas.
units.tr: Felix temeritas, see Temeritas.

units.la: Felix insolens] Sequitur stultitia opes. Ferociam satietas parit.
units.tr: Felix insolens] Folly follows wealth. Satiety breeds arrogance.

units.la: Feliciter] Jovis taxilli semper feliciter cadunt. Vid. Fortunatè.
units.tr: Feliciter] The dice of Jupiter always fall happily. See Fortunatè.

units.la: Feliciter cedant omnia] Quod agis bene fortunent superi. Quod agis bene vertat. Feliciter cadat, quod instituisti. Dii coepta secundent. Bene vertat. Sit felix, faustum, bonumque Reipub. Feliciter cedat nobis omnibus. Hanc affinitatem, precor, ut Deus nobis omnibus laetam esse velit. Feliciter exeat, quod coepisti. Prosperè succedat, quod agis. Ex animi sententia procedat, quod aggressus es. Deum optimum maximum precor, ut istud consilium, quàm est honestum, tam sit etiam auspicatum. Precor ut bonis avibus Italiam adeas, melioribus redeas. Precor ut hic annus tibi laetis auspiciis ineat, laetioribus procedat, laetissimis exeat. Bonis auspiciis anchoram solvas. Faxint superi, ut alba tibi contingant omnia, Er.
units.tr: Feliciter cedant omnia] May the gods of heaven bless what you do. May what you do turn out well. May what you have begun end happily. May the gods favour your undertakings. May it turn out well. May the Republic be happy, auspicious and good. May it turn out happily for us all. I pray that God will wish this kinship to be joyful for us all. May what you have begun go forth happily. May what you are doing succeed prosperously. May what you have undertaken proceed according to your mind. I pray to God, best and greatest, that this counsel, as honourable as it is, may also be auspicious. I pray that you may go to Italy under good birds and return under better. I pray that this year may begin for you with joyful auspices, proceed more joyfully, and end most joyfully. May you loose your anchor under good auspices. May the gods grant that all things turn out white for you, Er.

units.la: Fenerari, vid. Faenerari.
units.tr: Fenerari, see Faenerari.

units.la: Fenestra] Angustiæ fenestrarum. Luminaria, Cic. Lumen, Id. Lumina sex, scamna tria, Vitr. Transsenna, Salust. Specular, Mart. Foricula, Varr.
units.tr: Fenestra] The narrowness of windows. Lights (luminaria), Cic. Light, Id. Six openings, three benches, Vitr. A crossbar, Salust. A pane of mica, Mart. A small door, Varr.

units.la: Ferax, vid. Fertilis.
units.tr: Ferax, see Fertilis.

units.la: Ferculum] Esculentum. Mensa pinguis. Mittere alicui de mensâ. Capit coenæ, Cic. Edulium, Vlp. Obsonium vel Opsonium, Plaut. Sipont. Manducium, Var. Dapis, Pulmentum, Hor.
units.tr: Ferculum] Food. A rich table. To send something to someone from one's table. It takes its place at dinner, Cic. A dish, Ulp. A viand, obsonium or opsonium, Plaut. Sipont. A manducium, Varr. A feast, a dish, a stew, Hor.

units.la: Fere] Prope, Liv. Propius, pene, ferme. Parum abfuit quin. Nihil admodum sciebat literarum. Prorsus, Cic. Propemodum. Septem prorsum mensibus. Usque me occidit. Perreptavi usque omne oppidum, Ter. Plerique omnes, Id. Vix teneor quin, Plaut. Benè pleno lumine luna, Lucr. Facilè princeps, Cic. Annis sex minus paucis diebus, Vopisc.
units.tr: Fere] Nearly, Liv. Closer, almost, nearly, about. It fell little short of. He knew almost nothing of letters. Entirely, Cic. Almost. Almost seven months. He has almost killed me. I roamed through the whole town, Ter. Almost all, Id. I can scarcely keep from, Plaut. The moon with its light nearly full, Lucr. Easily first, Cic. Six years, less a few days, Vopisc.

units.la: Feretrum] Sandapila, Mart. Capulum, Plaut. Ferculum, Suet.
units.tr: Feretrum: a bier; Mart. a sandapila (litter); Plaut. a capulum (coffin-bier); Suet. a ferculum (stand for carrying).

units.la: Feriæ] Dies otiosus, feriatus, Cic. Vid. Festum.
units.tr: Feriae: a leisure day, a day of rest, Cic. See Festum.

units.la: Ferinus] Animalis sonus, Cic. Belualis educatio, Macrob. Beluinus furor, Sipont.
units.tr: Ferinus: the cry of an animal, Cic.; the upbringing of a beast, Macrob.; brutish rage, Sipont.

units.la: Ferire] Percutere lapidem, Cic. Impingere alicui pugnum, Plaut. Replaudere frontem, Apul. Plangere pectora palmis, Ovid. Intorquere hastam tergo, Virg. Icere, Plaut.
units.tr: To strike: to strike a stone, Cic.; to deal someone a blow with the fist, Plaut.; to slap the forehead, Apul.; to beat the breast with the palms, Ovid.; to hurl a spear at someone's back, Virg.; to strike, Plaut.

units.la: Fermentare] Fermentum modicum totam desipit conspersionem. Tertull.
units.tr: To ferment: a little leaven spoils the whole mass, giving it its taste. Tertull.

units.la: Fermentescere] Fermento intumescere, Plin.
units.tr: To swell with leaven, Plin.

units.la: Fermentum] Farriculum, Pallad.
units.tr: Leaven: a leavening agent, Pallad.

units.la: Ferocia] Temeritas furiosa. Feritas, Cic. Cornua, Hor. Leonina ferocia, Er.
units.tr: Ferocity: reckless, furious boldness; savageness, Cic.; horns, Hor.; lion-like ferocity, Erasm.

units.la: Ferociter] Centauricè. Cyclopicè, Er. Vid. Proterve.
units.tr: Fiercely: like a centaur; like a Cyclops, Erasm. See Impudently.

units.la: Ferox] Animo ferocior, Plaut. Præferocis animi, Liv. Eone es ferox, quia habes imperium in belluas? Cic. Fœnum in cornu habet.
units.tr: Fierce: fiercer in spirit, Plaut.; of very fierce spirit, Liv.; Are you proud because you have power over the beasts? Cic. He has hay on his horn (proverb: he is dangerous).

units.la: Ferre] Portare, Cic. Vid. Bajulare.
units.tr: To carry: to bear, Cic. See To carry on the back.

units.la: Ferreus] Genus ferratile, Plaut. Ferruginus, Lucr. Ferratus, Plin.
units.tr: Iron (adj.): a kind of ironwork, Plaut.; rust-coloured, Lucr.; iron-clad, Plin.

units.la: Ferrum] Mars terræ indomitus. Omnium propè instrumentorum materia.
units.tr: Iron: the untamed Mars of the earth; the material of almost all tools.

units.la: Fertilis] Fœcundus, ferax, opimus, Cic. Præfœcundus, Plin. Felix hortus, Mart. Fructuosus. Benè natus ager, Var. Frugiferum solum, Plin. Uberrima regna, Virg. Prodiga tellus. Genitale arvum, Ovid. Fœcunditate præstat, Col. Fœtificus, fœtifer, Plin. Generabilis rerum naturæ spiritus. Nube fœcundior, Scrophâ fœcundior albâ Er.
units.tr: Fertile: fruitful, fecund, rich, Cic.; very fruitful, Plin.; a happy garden, Mart.; productive. A well-born field, Varr.; fruit-bearing soil, Plin.; rich kingdoms, Virg.; a bountiful earth. A generative field, Ovid.; excels in fertility, Col.; fruitful, fruit-bearing, Plin.; the generative breath of nature. More fruitful than a cloud, more fruitful than a white sow, Erasm.

units.la: Fertilitas] Ubertas agrorum, fœcunditas, bonitas, Cic. Felicitas terræ, Plin. Uber glebæ, Virg. Semen terræ, Varr. Indoles, Liv.
units.tr: Fertility: the richness of fields, fruitfulness, goodness, Cic.; the happiness of the land, Plin.; the richness of the soil, Virg.; the seed of the earth, Varr.; natural disposition, Liv.

units.la: Fertiliter] Fœcundè, fœcundius, Plin.
units.tr: Fertilely: fruitfully, more fruitfully, Plin.

units.la: Fervens] Fervidus, Hor. Æstuans, Plin. Præfervidus, Col. Vid. Æstuans.
units.tr: Fervent: fervid, Hor.; glowing, Plin.; very hot, Col. See Glowing.

units.la: Fervere] Collyræ fac madeant, Plaut. Undat aqua calefacta, Pallad. Fervescunt aquæ, Lucr.
units.tr: To boil: let the cakes soak, Plaut.; the heated water surges, Pallad.; the waters boil, Lucr.

units.la: Ferunt, vid. Ajunt.
units.tr: They say: see They say.

units.la: Ferus] Nuper à silva Elephas, Flor.
units.tr: Wild: an elephant lately from the forest, Flor.

units.la: Fessus, vid. Fatigatus.
units.tr: Weary: see Tired.

units.la: Festinanter] Propere, Plaut. Properatò, Tac. Properanter, ter, Acc. Festinatò, Id. Festinè. Omni festinatione. Progressu firmo venire. Properato opus est. Velis equisque. Remisque velisque. Plenis velis. Equis & quadrigis, Cic. Magnis itineribus, Cæs. Navibus atque quadrigis, Hor. Maturatè, Liv. Maturato opus est, Id.
units.tr: Quickly: speedily, Plaut.; hurriedly, Tac.; speedily, Acc.; hastily, Id.; in haste. With all haste. To come with steady progress. The work needs haste. With sails and oars. With oars and sails. With full sails. With horses and chariots, Cic.; by long marches, Caes.; with ships and chariots, Hor.; promptly, Liv.; the work needs haste, Id.

units.la: Festinanter festina, ubi opus est] Propera propere. Etiam celeritas in desiderio mora est, Publ.
units.tr: Make haste quickly, hasten where there is need: hurry hastily. Even speed is a delay when one longs for something, Publ.

units.la: Festina tentè] Celeritate & morâ. Ita fugias, ne præter casam. Festinans initio serius absolvit. In arduis cunctanter agendum. Canis festinans cæcos parit catulos. Nimium properans serius absolvit. Nihil cautè simul & celeriter agi potest. Multa dicere & opportuna non est ejusdem.
units.tr: Make haste carefully: with both speed and delay. So flee, lest you pass by the hut. One who hurries at the start finishes later. In difficult matters one must act with caution. A dog in haste bears blind puppies. One who hastes too much finishes later. Nothing can be done both carefully and quickly at once. To say many things and to say them at the right time is not the same person's gift.

units.la: Festinare] Incitare celeritatem. Accelerare. Properare. Approperare. Maturare. Omni festinatione properare, Cic. Citare, Col. Removere moram, Plaut. Admaturare, Cæs. Addere celeritati, Cels. Præcipitare cursum, Juv. Præfestinare, Liv. Maturatè properare, Plaut, Sumere, intendere mobilitatem, Lucr. Addere gradum. Contento gradu aliquem petere. Pegasum conscendere. Pegaseo volatu ferri.
units.tr: To hasten: to stir up speed; to accelerate; to hurry; to make haste; to ripen. To hurry with all haste, Cic.; to urge on, Col.; to remove delay, Plaut.; to press on, Caes.; to add speed, Cels.; to quicken one's pace, Juv.; to hasten beforehand, Liv.; to hurry promptly, Plaut.; to take up and put forth mobility, Lucr.; to add a step. To seek someone with a stretched stride. To mount Pegasus. To be borne on Pegasean flight.

units.la: Festinatio] Properatio, Cic. Maturatio. Acceleratio, ad Her. Properantia, & properatus rei rusticæ, Gell.
units.tr: Haste: hurrying, Cic.; ripening; acceleration, ad Her.; hurrying, and the hurried business of farming, Gell.

units.la: Festinus] Plenus festinationis. Properans, Cic. Properus. Maturatum malum, Plaut. Festinata maturitas, Quint. Præfestinatus ictus, Ovid. Properatus gressus, Sil. Properatus stylus, Quint.
units.tr: Hasty: full of haste; hurrying, Cic.; hasty. An evil ripened too soon, Plaut.; hastened ripeness, Quint.; a blow struck too soon, Ovid.; a hurried step, Sil.; a hasty style, Quint.

units.la: Festivè, festivitas, vid. Facetè, facetiæ.
units.tr: Wittily, wit: see Wittily, wit.

units.la: Festivus, vid. Facetus.
units.tr: Witty: see Witty.

units.la: Festum] Festus dies. Feriæ, Cic. Feriæ festæ, Fest. Memoriæ. Hilaria, Vopisc. Feriæ conceptivæ, Macrob. Solennia, Tacit. Feriaticus, dies, Ulp. Feriatus dies, Plin.
units.tr: Feast: a festal day. Holidays, Cic.; festal holidays, Fest.; of memory. Hilaria, Vopisc.; conceived holidays, Macrob.; solemnities, Tac.; a holiday, Ulp.; a day of rest, Plin.

units.la: Festa anniversaria] Feriæ stativæ, Macrob. Statæ feriæ, Fest.
units.tr: Annual feasts: fixed holidays, Macrob.; fixed holidays, Fest.

units.la: Fiber] Castor, Plin. Canis ponticus, Serv. Cerd.
units.tr: Beaver: a beaver, Plin.; a Pontic dog, Serv. Cerd.

units.la: Fibra] Vena. Nervus, Plin. Striæ, Vitruv. Striges, cavitates, Plin.
units.tr: Fibre: a vein; a sinew, Plin.; grooves, Vitruv.; channels, hollows, Plin.

units.la: Fibulare] Colligare fibulis. Fibulâ conjungere, Vitr. Infibulare, Cels. Ansis ferreis vincire, Vitr. Constringere catenis, Cic.
units.tr: To clasp: to fasten with clasps; to join with a clasp, Vitr.; to fasten with a bolt, Cels.; to bind with iron hoops, Vitr.; to fasten with chains, Cic.

units.la: Ficte,
units.tr: Fictly,

units.la: Fictè, vid. Simulatè.
units.tr: Feignedly: see Pretendedly.

units.la: Fictilis, vid. Argillaceus.
units.tr: Earthen: see Clayey.

units.la: Fictio, vid. Ironia.
units.tr: Fiction: see Irony.

units.la: Fictor] Plastes, Plin. Plasticus, Firm. Plasmator, apud Theol.
units.tr: Sculptor: a modeller, Plin.; a plastic artist, Firm.; a moulder, in Theology.

units.la: Fictus] Fictitius,seu factitius,Sipont. Simulata tristitia,Cic. Commentitius. Infucata vitia, Id. Fabulosus,Hor. Vid. Simulatus.
units.tr: Feigned: fictitious, or made by art, Sipont.; feigned sadness, Cic.; invented; vices without varnish, Id.; fabulous, Hor. See Pretended.

units.la: Ficus] Fici arbor,Cic. Ficulnea arbor,Col. Ficaria,Pallad.
units.tr: Fig: a fig tree, Cic.; a wild fig tree, Col.; a fig tree, Pallad.

units.la: Fide jubere, vid. Spondere.
units.tr: To pledge one's word: see To pledge.

units.la: Fidelis] Fidelis alicui. Qui animo fideli in aliquem est. Fidissima uxor. Fidissimi socii. Incorruptus & integer testis, Religiosus, Religiosissimus, Cic. Incorruptissimus custos, Hor. Bonæ fidei homo, Suet. Juratissimus,Plin.Iun. Conspicuus fide,Ovid. Dignus quicum in tenebris mices.
units.tr: Faithful: faithful to someone; one who is of a faithful mind towards someone. A most faithful wife. Most faithful companions. An incorrupt and upright witness; conscientious, most conscientious, Cic.; a most incorruptible guardian, Hor.; a man of good faith, Suet.; most sworn, Plin. Iun.; conspicuous for loyalty, Ovid.; one with whom you could share the dark.

units.la: Fidelitas] Fides. Dictorum, factorumque constantia. Religio, Cic. Attica fides, Paterc.
units.tr: Fidelity: faithfulness; steadiness in word and deed. Conscientiousness, Cic.; Attic good faith, Paterc.

units.la: Fideliter] Ex fide scribere, Plin. Sanctissimè observare, quæ promiseris, Cic. Religiosè, Col. Bonâ fide, Cato.
units.tr: Faithfully: to write in good faith, Plin.; to observe most scrupulously what you have promised, Cic.; conscientiously, Col.; in good faith, Cato.

units.la: Fides, is, vid. Chorda.
units.tr: Strings: see Cord.

units.la: Fides, ium] Lyra, Hor. Lyrion, Cæl. Rhod.
units.tr: Lyre: a lyre, Hor.; a lyre, Cael. Rhod.

units.la: Fidibus canere] Scire fidibus, Ter. Canere tibiis. Inflat tibicen, Cic. Ludere. Psallere. Incinit tibicen,Gell. Pulsare chelyn. Concinere lyrâ, Ovid. Concinere aliquid plectro, Hor. Inflare, calamos. Ludere calamo agresti, Virg. Organo modulari, Lamp. Citharizare, Æmil. Assis tibiis canere, Scal.
units.tr: To play on strings: to know the strings, Ter.; to play the pipes. The piper blows, Cic.; to play; to pluck. The piper strikes up, Gell.; to strike the lyre. To sing to the lyre, Ovid.; to sing something to the plectrum, Hor.; to blow reeds; to play on a rustic reed, Virg.; to play a tune on the organ, Lamp.; to play the cithara, Aemil.; to sing with pipes at the ready, Scal.

units.la: Fides ei, vid. Fidelitas.
units.tr: Their faith: see Fidelity.

units.la: Fides dubia] Fidei lubricum, Macrob. Fides Græca, Punica.
units.tr: Doubtful faith: slipperiness of faith, Macrob.; Greek faith; Punic faith.

units.la: Fidem amittere] Percoquere fidem. Sum incredibilis. Nullâ fide est, Plaut. Abiit fides, Liv. Caret res fide, Plin. Carent verba fide,Ovid. Concidit fides. Defecit aliquem fides. Fidem non habet res, Cic. Fides apud te nulla mihi. Parum mihi habet fidem, Ter.
units.tr: To lose faith: to spoil one's credit. I am not to be believed. There is no trust in it, Plaut.; faith has gone, Liv.; the thing lacks credit, Plin.; words lack faith, Ovid.; faith has fallen. Faith has failed someone. The thing does not win belief, Cic.; you have no credit with me. He gives me little credit, Ter.

units.la: Fidem amisisse, magna jactura] Fides ut anima est, unde abiit, non revertitur.
units.tr: To have lost faith is a great loss: faith is like life; once it has departed, it does not return.

units.la: Fidem spes sequitur] Quod quisque sperat, facilè credit.
units.tr: Hope follows faith: what each man hopes for, he readily believes.

units.la: Fidem negare, vid. Credere non.
units.tr: To deny faith: see Not to believe.

units.la: Fides sit penes auctores, vid. Credat, qui vult.
units.tr: Let the authors answer for it: see Let him believe who will.

units.la: Fide tibi, non aliis] Oculis magis habenda fides, quàm auribus. Plus est oculatus testis unus, quàm auriti decem.
units.tr: Trust yourself, not others: trust is to be placed more in the eyes than in the ears. One eyewitness is worth more than ten earwitnesses.

units.la: Fide dignissimus] Authenticus, Vlp. Omni exceptione major. Incorruptus & integer testis. Locuples testis. Sanctissimum testimonium, Cic. Constat ei fides, Arnob.
units.tr: Most worthy of trust: authentic, Ulp.; beyond all exception. An incorrupt and upright witness. A wealthy witness. A most holy testimony, Cic.; trust is established in him, Arnob.

units.la: Fidendum caute] Fide, sed cui, vide. Fiduciâ pecunias amisi. Modius salis absumendus priùs, quàm credas. (id est, non facilè credendum.)
units.tr: Trust with caution: trust, but see whom you trust. I lost money through overconfidence. A peck of salt is to be eaten through before you believe. (That is, one is not to believe readily.)

units.la: Fide, vid. Credere.
units.tr: Trust: see To believe.

units.la: Fidicen] Psaltes, Hieron. Psaltria, Cic. Fidicina, Ter.
units.tr: Lyre-player: a psalter-player, Jerome; a female lyre-player, Cic.; a female lyre-player, Ter.

units.la: Fiducia] Fidentia. Confisio, Cic. Confidentia, Plaut.
units.tr: Confidence: trust; reliance, Cic.; boldness, Plaut.

units.la: Fieri potest] Potest, abs. Plaut. Fieri potest, Arnob. Si forte ita fert natura locorum, Lucr. Si impetrari potest. Fortasse, Plaut. Licebit bibas, Cat.
units.tr: It is possible: it can be, Plaut. (absolutely); it can be, Arnob.; if the lie of the land allows it, Lucr.; if it can be obtained; perhaps, Plaut.; you may drink, Cat.

units.la: Figere] Configere tabulas inter se. Desuere cupam, Cato. Vid. Configere.
units.tr: To fasten: to fasten boards together. To stitch a cask together, Cato. See To join.

units.la: Figlinum opus] Fictile, testaceum opus, Plin. Figularis rota, Plaut.
units.tr: Earthenware work: a fired or earthen work, Plin.; a potter's wheel, Plaut.

units.la: Figmentum, vid. Commentum.
units.tr: Fabrication: see Invention.

units.la: Figura] Forma. Species. Effigies, Cic. Corporatura, Col. Factura corporis, Gell. Schema, Plaut. Facies, Tac. Simulacrum, Quint. Typus faciei, Plin.
units.tr: Figure: form; appearance; likeness, Cic.; bodily build, Col.; the make of the body, Gell.; shape, Plaut.; face, Tac.; image, Quint.; the cast of the face, Plin.

units.la: Figurare] Formare in muliebrem habitum & figuram, Cic. Conformare in speciem, Col. Configurare, Macrob. Informare effigiem. Modificari membra, Sil. Deformare, Varr.
units.tr: To shape: to form into a woman's dress and figure, Cic.; to form into an appearance, Col.; to fashion, Macrob.; to form a likeness; to shape the limbs, Sil.; to deform, Varr.

units.la: Figuratio] Informatio. Conformatio, Cic. Modificatio, Sen. Formatura, formamentum, Lucr. Deformatio, Firm. Fictura, Gell.
units.tr: Shaping: forming; conformation, Cic.; modification, Sen.; formation, Lucr.; deformation, Firm.; fashioning, Gell.

units.la: Filia] Nata, Virg. Hera minor, Plaut.
units.tr: Daughter: a born child, Virg.; a little mistress, Plaut.

units.la: Filius] Natus. Gnatus, Cic. Herus minor, Plaut.
units.tr: Son: one born; begotten, Cic.; a little master, Plaut.

units.la: Filii] Columna domus liberi masculi, Eurip.
units.tr: Sons: the pillar of the house; male children, Eurip.

units.la: Fimbria, vid. Lacinia.
units.tr: Fringe: see Hem.

units.la: Fimetum] Sterquilinium, Col. Fimus] Bolbitum. Saturitas, Plin. Fimum bubulum, caballinum, Id. Editus boum, Vlp. Vid. Excrementum.
units.tr: Dunghill: a manure heap, Col. Dung: a kind of dung; abundance, Plin.; cattle and horse dung, Id.; the droppings of oxen, Ulp. See Excrement.

units.la: Findere] Diffindere vitem, Cat. Profindere, Stat. Discuneare, Plin. Scindere quercum cuneis, Virg Cuneare. Secare arborem in pulpam. Assulosè frangere, Plin.
units.tr: To split: to split a vine, Cato.; to split apart, Stat.; to split with wedges, Plin.; to split an oak with wedges, Virg.; to wedge; to cut a tree into chips; to break into splinters, Plin.

units.la: Fingere]Confingere rumorem, comminisci, Apul. Commentari. Confabulari fabulam. Contechnari aliquid, Plaut. Texere causam leti, Propert. Contexere crimen, Cicer. Mentiri causam, Ovid.
units.tr: To feign: to invent a rumour, to devise, Apul.; to contrive; to make up a tale. To devise something by craft, Plaut.; to weave the cause of death, Propert.; to weave a charge, Cic.; to allege a reason, Ovid.

units.la: Fingis] Ex te ipso hæc audis. Campas dicis, abi, abi, Scal.
units.tr: You are making it up: you hear these things from yourself. You say "campas"; go away, go away, Scal.

units.la: Finire negotium] Concludere multa uno die. Ad exitum pervenire. Expedire exitum orationis. Curriculum conficere. Facere finem. Extrema lineamenta addere, Cic. Perficere. Confectum relinquere, Curt. Clausulam, summam manum imponere, Sen. Finem imponere, Plin. Exigere opus, Hor. Coronidem addere. Manum de tabulâ. Vid. Absolvere.
units.tr: To finish a business: to conclude many things in one day; to come to the end; to bring a discourse to its conclusion; to complete the course; to make an end; to add the final touches, Cic.; to bring to completion and leave finished, Curt.; to put on the final touch, Sen.; to set an end, Plin.; to finish the work, Hor.; to add the crown; to take the hand from the picture. See To complete.

units.la: Finis] Terminus. Terminatio, Cic. Termen. Extremum. Extremitas. Exitus. Calx, Fastigium, Varr. Coronis. Umbilicus libri, paginæ, Mart, Eras. Colophon, Fest. Meta, Ovid. Eventus, Plin Postremitas, Macrob. Extrema linea. Extremus actus fabulæ. Clausula fabulæ.
units.tr: End: a boundary; termination, Cic.; a limit; the extremity; the outcome; the summit, Varr.; the crown; the navel of a book or page, Mart., Erasm.; the turning-post, Ovid.; the outcome, Plin.; the last part, Macrob.; the final line; the last act of a play; the close of a play.

units.la: Finis laborum delectat] Jucundi acti labores.
units.tr: The end of labours delights] Labours once completed are pleasant.

units.la: Finis rem ostendit] Finis coronat opus. In fine cognoscitur, cujus toni. Epulum à bellariis commendatur. Diem vesper commendat. Consilia ab eventu probari solent.
units.tr: The end reveals the thing] The end crowns the work. The tone of a piece is known at its close. A feast is recommended by its sweets. Evening recommends the day. Plans are usually judged by their outcome.

units.la: Sub finem anni, veris, &c.] Exeunte anno. Extremâ hieme, Cic. Exitu superioris anni, Liv. Sub exitu vitæ, Suet. Extremo anni, Tac. Senescente hieme. Affecta æstate. Inclinata die, Cic. Præcipiti autumno, Amm. Ver inclinatum in æstatem, Sen. Ruit ver, Virg.
units.tr: Towards the end of the year, of spring, etc.] As the year runs out. In late winter, Cic. At the close of the previous year, Liv. Near the end of life, Suet. At the year's end, Tac. As winter wanes. With summer spent. With the day declining, Cic. In late autumn, Amm. Spring leaning towards summer, Sen. Spring rushes on, Virg.

units.la: Ad finem venire] Ad calcem pervenire. Ad ultimum fidem præstare, Liv Extrema me vocant. Ad metas venit finita voluptas, Sil. Nunc ad metam festinat oratio.
units.tr: To come to the end] To reach the close. To keep faith at last, Liv. The last things call me. Pleasure that has run its course comes to the turning-post, Sil. Now the speech hastens to its goal.

units.la: Ad finem properare] Contrahere vela. Manum de tabula.
units.tr: To hasten towards the end] To furl the sails. To take one's hand off the picture.

units.la: In fine quies] Ad finem ubi perveneris, ne velis reverti.
units.tr: In the end is rest] When you have arrived at the end, do not wish to turn back.

units.la: In fine deficere] Ab ipsa messe discedere. In summo clivo deficere. In portu impingere. Devorato boye in cauda deficere.
units.tr: To fail at the end] To quit just at the harvest. To give out at the top of the hill. To run aground in harbour. To stop at the tail after the ox has been eaten.

units.la: Finem non assequi] Operam ludere. Operam & oleum perdere. Excidere fine, Quint.
units.tr: Not to attain the end] To waste one's effort. To lose both labour and oil. To fall outside the end, Quint.

units.la: Finitimus] Confinis, Plin. In confinio positus, Vlp. Conterminus, Col. Collimitatus, Salin. Affines potentioribus, Sallust.
units.tr: Neighbouring] Bordering, Plin. Situated on the boundary, Ulp. Adjoining, Col. Bordering on the same limit, Salin. Neighbours of the more powerful, Sallust.

units.la: Finitor] Persector. Confector, Cic.
units.tr: Surveyor] Pursuer. Completer, Cic.

units.la: Firmamentum] Firmamen trunci, Ovid. Stabilimen regni, Cic. Stabilimentum, Plaut. Duramentum virtutis necessitas, Sen. Solidamentum, Lactant. Statuminatio, Vitruv.
units.tr: Support] A prop for the trunk, Ovid. A stay of the kingdom, Cic. A support, Plaut. The hardness of virtue that comes from necessity, Sen. A solid base, Lactant. A propping, Vitruv.

units.la: Firmare] Clavo trabali figere. Corroborare, Cic. Stabilire, Plaut. Roborare. Rigorare. Statuminare, Plin. Consolidare, Vlp. Affirmare armis virtutem alicujus, Tac. Confirmare. Constabilire rem, Ter. Indurare, Sen. Fundare, Virg.
units.tr: To make firm] To fix with a beam-nail. To strengthen, Cic. To establish, Plaut. To make robust. To stiffen. To prop up, Plin. To consolidate, Ulp. To confirm someone's virtue by arms, Tac. To confirm. To establish a matter, Ter. To harden, Sen. To found, Virg.

units.la: Firmè] Valenter. Firmiter, Col. Prævalidè, Plin. Nervosè. Clavo trabali figere, Cic. Omni pede stare, Quint.
units.tr: Firmly] Vigorously. Firmly, Col. Very strongly, Plin. Sinewily. To fix with a beam-nail, Cic. To stand on the whole foot, Quint.

units.la: Firmitas] Firmitudo animi. Soliditas. Stabilitas. Nervus, Cic.
units.tr: Firmness] Firmness of spirit. Solidity. Stability. Sinew, Cic.

units.la: Firmus] Fixus. Stabilis. Defixus altissimis radicibus. Nunquam dimoveri loco potest. Labefactari non potest, Cic. Infrangibilis rigor animi, Sen. Infrangibilis animus, Ovid. Potens argumentum, Quint. Vid. Immobilis. Robustus.
units.tr: Firm] Fixed. Stable. Fastened by the deepest roots. Can never be moved from its place. Cannot be shaken, Cic. Unbreakable rigour of mind, Sen. Unbreakable spirit, Ovid. Strong argument, Quint. See Immovable. Robust.

units.la: Fissura] Fissus,ûs. Vitium ædis, parietis, Cic. Fissum, Celf. Scissura, Rima, Plin. Segmen & rima parietis, Vitruv. Spiramentum, Virg.
units.tr: Crack] A splitting. A defect of a building or wall, Cic. A split, Celsus. A cleft or fissure, Plin. A cleft and crack in a wall, Vitruv. A breathing-hole, Virg.

units.la: Fissus, vid. Rimosus.
units.tr: Split: see Cracked.

units.la: Fistucare] Fistucis pavire, Plin. Fistucationibus solidare, Vitr. Fistucis fustibusque calcare, Cat. Pavire, Pavimentare, Circumpavire, Plin. Configere locum congestitium, Vitr.
units.tr: To ram] To pave with a rammer, Plin. To make solid by ramming, Vitruv. To tread down with rammers and clubs, Cato. To pave, to floor, to pave around, Plin. To set a site with packed fill, Vitruv.

units.la: Fistucatio] Pisatio, Sen. Palatio, Vitr.
units.tr: Ramming] Pounding, Sen. Paving, Vitruv.

units.la: Fistucatus] Pavitus, Glutus, Subactus, Plin. Glittus, Fest. Pavidatum solum rudere, Pallad. Occulcatus, Varr. Palatum.
units.tr: Rammed] Trodden, pressed down, trampled, Plin. Trodden, Fest. Ground paved with rubble, Pallad. Trampled, Varr. Paved.

units.la: Flagellare] Flagellis terrere, Lucr. Cædere, Hor. Urilo- ris, Id. Variare virgis & loris. Pinsere aliquem flagro. Facere aliquem ferventem flagris, Plaut. Verbere in aliquem sævire. Scindere latus flagello, Ovid. Verberibus te cæsum in pistrinum dedam, Ter. Verberare aliquem virgis. Castigare verberibus aliquem, Cic. Multare aliquem virgis, Liv. Lacerare terga alicujus verbere, Ovid. Monumentis commonefacere bubulis. Ne in te bubuli cottabi crepent, Plaut.
units.tr: To whip] To frighten with whips, Lucr. To beat with rods, Hor. To flog with thongs, Id. To vary blows with rods and straps. To lash someone with a scourge. To make someone smart with whips, Plaut. To rage against someone with blows. To cut someone's side with a whip, Ovid. I will have you beaten and sent to the mill, Ter. To beat someone with rods. To chastise someone with blows, Cic. To punish someone with rods, Liv. To tear someone's back with a lash, Ovid. To admonish with ox-hide monuments. Lest the ox-hide cottabus rattle against you, Plaut.

units.la: Flagellum] Flagrum, Suet. Scutica, Hor. Mastyx, Sipont.
units.tr: Whip] A scourge, Suet. A lash, Hor. A switch, Sipont.

units.la: Flagitare, vid. Postulare. Reposcere.
units.tr: To demand: see Ask. Reclaim.

units.la: Flagitiosus] Libidinosus. Impurus. Intemperans. Perflagitiosus. Animus libidini deditus. Maculosus homo. Cic. Perturpis & flagitiosus, Id. Vid. Scelestus.
units.tr: Shameful] Lustful. Impure. Intemperate. Thoroughly shameful. A mind given over to lust. A stained man, Cic. Utterly foul and shameful, Id. See Wicked.

units.la: Flagitium] Scelus atrox, audax, impium, inauditum. Factum flagitii & dedecoris plenum. Crimen atrocissimum, nefarium, immane. Malefictum, maleficium simile portenti ac prodigii, Cic. Capital, Plaut. Nefas immane, Virg.
units.tr: Shameful deed] A fierce, bold, impious, unheard-of crime. A deed full of shame and disgrace. A most atrocious, nefarious, monstrous crime. A wrong, a misdeed like a portent or prodigy, Cic. A capital offence, Plaut. Monstrous wickedness, Virg.

units.la: Flagranter, vid. Cupidè.
units.tr: Ardently: see Eagerly.

units.la: Flagrare, vid. Ardere.
units.tr: To blaze: see To burn.

units.la: Flamma] Splendor pinguedinis in aërem & lucem se resolventis.
units.tr: Flame] The brightness of fat dissolving into air and light.

units.la: Flammescere, vid. Exardescere.
units.tr: To flare up: see To blaze up.

units.la: Flare] Perflare, follicare, Virg.
units.tr: To blow] To blow through, to puff, Virg.

units.la: Flatus] Flatura, Arnob. Inflatus tibicinis, Cic. Flamen venti. Boreæ flabra, Proper.
units.tr: Blast] A blowing, Arnob. The breath of a flute-player, Cic. A gust of wind. The blasts of Boreas, Propert.

units.la: Flavus, vid. Luteus.
units.tr: Yellow: see Golden-yellow.

units.la: Flebilis] Miserandus, miserabilis. Perluctuosum funus. Acerbissimus interitus, Cic. Deplorandus, Id. Lamentabilis, Virg. Illacrymabilis, Levin. Ærumnabilis, Lucr. Funesta querela, Propert. Tristis ad recordationem, Liv. Lugubres res, Cic.
units.tr: Mournful] Pitiable, wretched. A funeral full of tears. Most bitter death, Cic. To be lamented, Id. Lamentable, Virg. Tearless, Levin. Wretched, Lucr. A sorrowful lament, Propert. Sad to remember, Liv. Mournful matters, Cic.

units.la: Flebiliter] Flebile canere, Ovid. Lacrymosè, Plin.
units.tr: Mournfully] To sing a dirge, Ovid. Tearfully, Plin.

units.la: Flectere, vid. Curvare. Dirigere.
units.tr: To bend: see Curve. Direct.

units.la: Flere] Fit fletus. Lacrymare, Lacrymari. Lacrymas effuneffundere. Jacere in lacrymis, Cic. Flere lacrymis argen-teis, Plaut. Indulgere lacrymis, Ovid. Indulgere luctibus, Lucret. Absumere lumina in fletus, Catul. Opplorare auri-bus alicujus, ad Heren. Effundi in lacrymas. Fletus ciere, excitare, Cic. Virg. Vid. Lacrymari.
units.tr: To weep] To shed tears. To pour out tears. To lie in tears, Cic. To weep silver tears, Plaut. To indulge in tears, Ovid. To give oneself to grief, Lucr. To spend one's eyes in weeping, Catul. To beg with tears at someone's ears, ad Herennium. To be poured out in tears. To raise weeping, to stir up lamentation, Cic. Virg. See To lament.

units.la: Flere mortuum] Illacrymari alicujus morti. Collacryma-re casum alicujus. Lessum habere. Prosequi lacrymis abeuntem, Cic. Illacrymare alicui. Lugere fratrem adem-ptum, Ovid. Plangere aliquem, funera alicujus, Stat. Les-sum facere filio, Plaut. Plorare, Sen.
units.tr: To mourn the dead] To weep over someone's death. To mourn someone's misfortune with tears. To hold a lament. To escort the departing with tears, Cic. To mourn a brother taken away, Ovid. To lament someone's funeral, Stat. To make a lament for a son, Plaut. To wail, Sen.

units.la: Fletus] Ploratus. Plangor. Ejulatio. Ejulatus. Collacry-matio, Lessus, Cic. Lacrymatio, Plin. Comploratio. Com-ploratus, Liv.
units.tr: Weeping] Wailing. Lamentation. Keening. Ululation. Shared weeping, lament, Cic. Tears, Plin. Common lamentation, Liv.

units.la: Flexibilis] Flexilis, Plin. Ovid. Lentus, Plaut. Vietæ virgæ, Hor. Vitilis vagina cucurbitæ, Plin.
units.tr: Flexible] Pliant, Plin. Ovid. Supple, Plaut. Pliant twigs, Hor. A pliant gourd-sheath, Plin.

units.la: Flexio, vid. Curvatio. Inclinatio.
units.tr: Bending: see Curving. Inclination.

units.la: Flexuose] Torte, Lucr. Intortius. Oblique, Plin. Vage decerant amnes, Lucr. Mæandri more, Col.
units.tr: Winding] Twistingly, Lucr. Tortuously. Obliquely, Plin. The rivers had wandered off, Lucr. In the manner of the Maeander, Col.

units.la: Flexuosus, vid. Tortuosus.
units.tr: Winding: see Tortuous.

units.la: Floccifacere, vid. Contemnere.
units.tr: To despise: see To scorn.

units.la: Floccus] Flocculus, Plin. Villus ovium, Col.
units.tr: Flock] A small tuft, Plin. The wool of sheep, Col.

units.la: Florere] Florescere. Efflorescere, Cic. Reflorescere. Exhilarantur flore arbores. Pubescit virtus. Præflorere. Superflorere. Superflorescere, Plin. Vernant arbores, Plin. Vigere, Lucr.
units.tr: To flower] To come into flower. To blossom forth, Cic. To flower again. Trees rejoice in their flowers. Virtue comes to its bloom. To flower early. To flower over. To flower over greatly, Plin. Trees grow green, Plin. To be vigorous, Lucr.

units.la: Floridus] Floridulus, Catul.
units.tr: Flowery] Somewhat flowery, Catul.

units.la: Flos] Flosculus, Cic.
units.tr: Flower] A little flower, Cic.

units.la: Fluctus] Motus & agitatio fluctuum, Cic. Fluctus decumanus, Fest. Unda præcelsis crescit molibus. Montes aquarum, Ovid.
units.tr: Wave] The motion and agitation of waves, Cic. A tenth wave, Fest. A wave swelling with towering masses. Mountains of water, Ovid.

units.la: Fluentum] Agmen aquarum, Lucr. Impetus fluminis.
units.tr: Flow] A host of waters, Lucr. The force of a river.

units.la: Fluere] Manare, Ovid. Scatere. Profluere, Cic. Volvitur amnis, Virg.
units.tr: To flow] To ooze, Ovid. To gush. To flow forth, Cic. The river rolls on, Virg.

units.la: Fluidus] Fluxus succus. Torrens flumen, Virg. Profluens aqua, Cic. Manans, Hor. Manalis fons, Fest. Vivum flumen, Liv. Fons vivus, Ovid. Profluus amnis, Col.
units.tr: Fluid] A flowing juice. A rushing river, Virg. Running water, Cic. Trickling, Hor. A running spring, Fest. A living river, Liv. A living spring, Ovid. A flowing stream, Col.

units.la: Fluvialis] Fluvatilis, Cic. Fluviaticus. Rivalis alecu-la, la, Col. Fluminens, Ovid. Amicus, Plaut. Flumentana porta, Fest.
units.tr: Of rivers] Of the river, Cic. River-dwelling, Col. Flowing by, Ovid. Companion, Plaut. The river gate, Fest. Note: "Rivalis alecula" as in Col., river-fish.

units.la: Fluvius] Aquæ ductus naturalis. Aquarum natatio. Cursus indeficiens. Regionum aquatio. Flumen, Virg. Profluens, Subst. Cic.
units.tr: River] A natural conduit of water. A swimming of waters. An unceasing course. The watering of regions. A river, Virg. A flowing stream, Cic. (as a noun).

units.la: Fluxio] Scaturigo. Fluxura, Col. Fluor, Celf. Meatus fluminis, Claud. Flumen, Virg. Scatebræ, Id. Interluvies, Solin. Fluentia, Solin. Scaturies, Sipont. Vid. Profluvium.
units.tr: Flux] A spring. A flow, Col. A flow, Celsus. The course of a river, Claud. A river, Virg. Gushings, Virg. Overflow, Solin. A flowing, Solin. A welling up, Sipont. See Discharge.

units.la: Fodere] Fodiri, Col. Perducere fossas in altitudinem, Cæs. Interfodere aliquid, Lucr. Scrutari abdita terræ, Id. Ducere fossam, Liv. Facere fossam, Cat. Sulcare fossam, Varr.
units.tr: To dig] To be dug, Col. To sink trenches to a depth, Caes. To dig into something, Lucr. To search the hidden places of the earth, Id. To dig a ditch, Liv. To make a ditch, Cato. To plough a furrow, Varr.

units.la: Fœcunditas, fœcundus, vid. Fertilitas, fertilis.
units.tr: Fertility, fertile: see Fruitfulness, fruitful.

units.la: Fœdare, vid. Contaminare.
units.tr: To defile: see To contaminate.

units.la: Fœdè] Putidè. Sordidè. Impurissime, teterrimeque violasti. Impurè ac tetrè : nequiter & turpiter facere aliquid, Cic. Impurè vivere, Id. Rancidè, Gell. Deformiter, Quint.
units.tr: Foully] Stinkingly. Squalidly. You have violated most foully and hideously. Impurely and hideously: to do something wickedly and basely, Cic. To live impurely, Id. Rancidly, Gell. Deformedly, Quint.

units.la: Fœderatus] Fœderi adscriptus, fœdere obligatus, Liv. Fœdere junctus, sociatus, Ovid.
units.tr: Bound by treaty] Enrolled in a treaty, bound by a covenant, Liv. Joined by a covenant, allied, Ovid.

units.la: Fœditas, vid. Turpitudo.
units.tr: Foulness: see Baseness.

units.la: Fœdus, i] Bipedum & quadrupedum impurissimus, Cic. Turpis amor, Hor. Turpissimus homo, Cic. Turpitudine notabilis. Maculosus homo dedecore, Tac. Maculosum nefas Hor. Tetrum facinus, Sen. Vid. Deformis, Impurus
units.tr: Foul] The most foul of two-footed and four-footed creatures, Cic. Base love, Hor. A most base man, Cic. Marked by baseness. A man stained with disgrace, Tac. A stained wickedness, Hor. A foul deed, Sen. See Ugly. Impure.

units.la: Fœdi pulchra non curant] Nihil sui cum amaracino. Amica luto suus, Hor.
units.tr: Beautiful things do not care for foul ones] Nothing in common with marjoram. One's own love is mud, Hor.

units.la: Fœdus, eris] Induciæ, Liv. Feriæ belli, Varr. Pax castrensis paucorum dierum, Gell.
units.tr: Covenant] Truces, Liv. Wartime truces, Varr. A camp peace of a few days, Gell.

units.la: Fœdus facere] Ferire, icere, sancire fœdus cum aliquo. Facere fœdus inter se. Inducias facere. Cavere fœdere de aliquâ, Cic. Percutere fœdus, Hirt. Pangere inducias, fœdere alicui jungi. Jungere fœdera, Liv. Inire inducias, Plin. Iun. Fœderare aliquem, Tacit.
units.tr: To make a covenant] To strike, make and ratify a covenant with someone. To make a covenant between themselves. To make a truce. To take care about something by covenant, Cic. To strike a covenant, Hirt. To agree a truce, to be joined to someone by covenant. To join covenants, Liv. To enter into truces, Plin. Iun. To bind someone by covenant, Tac.

units.la: Fœnerare, id est, mutuari alicui, ut pendat usuram] Dare fœnori pecunias. Fœnerare pecuniam, Cic. Dare in fœnus, Varr. Locare alicui argentum. Locare fœnori argentum, Plaut. Ponere in fœnore nummos, Hor. Accipere fœnus ab aliquo, Id. Pecuniam in quæstu relinquere.
units.tr: To lend at interest, that is, to lend to someone so that he pays interest] To give money out at interest. To lend money at interest, Cic. To give at interest, Varr. To place silver with someone. To place silver at interest, Plaut. To put coins out at interest, Hor. To receive interest from someone, Id. To leave money out at profit.

units.la: Foliatus] Foliosus. Pampinatus, Plin.
units.tr: Leafy] Full of leaves. Tendrilled, Plin.

units.la: Fomes] Suscitabulum, Non. Sulfurata. Fungi aridi. Alimentum ignis. Materia aridi fomitis,Plin. Lucubrum,Prisc. Scal. Esca ignis, Liv. Nutrimentum ignis, Virg.
units.tr: Tinder] A kindler, Non. Sulphur-treated. Dry fungus. Fuel of the fire. Material of dry tinder, Plin. Lamp-wick, Prisc. Scal. The food of fire, Liv. The nourishment of fire, Virg.

units.la: Fons] Aquae perennes, Cic. Latices perennes, Lucr. Rivus perennis, Plin. Iun. Caput fluminis,Virg. Caput aquae. Eruptio subita amnis ex abdito, Sen. Scaturigo perennis, Plaut. Aqua viva,Varr. Subterreae abyssi. Vivus canalis. Naturalis Sipho.
units.tr: Fountain] Perennial waters, Cic. Perennial springs, Lucr. A perennial stream, Plin. Iun. The head of a river, Virg. The source of water. A sudden bursting forth of a river from a hidden place, Sen. A perennial spring, Plaut. Living water, Varr. Subterranean abysses. A living channel. A natural siphon.

units.la: Fontem malo quàm rivos] Dulcius ex ipso fonte bibuntur aquae.
units.tr: I would rather have the spring than the streams: Water is drunk more sweetly from the spring itself.

units.la: Foramen] Apertura, Vitruv. Cavum terrae, Virg.
units.tr: Foramen: An opening, Vitruv. A hollow in the ground, Virg.

units.la: Foraminosus] Pertusum vas, Lucr. Fenestrata domus. Tot meatibus distinctus est, & interpatet rimis, Macrob. Pellucet crebrius quam cribrum. Pellucidus quasi laterna Punica, Plaut. Rimosa cymba, Virg. Perforatus & transmittens quicquid acceperat, Sen.
units.tr: Full of holes: A vessel pierced through, Lucr. A house full of windows. Divided by so many passages and interrupted by gaps, Macrob. Shining through more thickly than a sieve. Transparent like a Punic lantern, Plaut. A leaky boat, Virg. Pierced through, letting through whatever it has received, Sen.

units.la: Forare, vid. Terebrare.
units.tr: Forare: see Terebrare (to bore).

units.la: Foràs] Extrà excedere, Cic.
units.tr: Foràs: To go out, to go beyond the outside, Cic.

units.la: Forceps] Lupi, Veget. Tenaculae,Turneb. Tenaces,Pallad.
units.tr: Forceps: Of a wolf, Veget. Tongs, Turneb. Pincers, Pallad.

units.la: Fores] Foris crepuit. Ostium,Ter. Janua, Cic.
units.tr: Fores: The door creaked. A door, Ter. A door, Cic.

units.la: Forfex] Forficula, Plin.
units.tr: Forfex: A little pair of shears, or an earwig, Plin.

units.la: Forfex pro dentibus, vid. Dentarpaga.
units.tr: Forceps for teeth: see Dentarpaga (tooth-puller).

units.la: Foris] Forinsecus, Col. Extrinsecus,Perf. A foris, Plin.
units.tr: Foris: Outside, Col. Externally, Perf. From outside, Plin.

units.la: Forma externa, vid. Figura.
units.tr: External form: see Figura.

units.la: Formam habet juxta virtutem] Corporis formam animi dotibus æquiparat, Er.
units.tr: He has beauty alongside virtue: He matches the beauty of the body with the gifts of the mind, Er.

units.la: Formare, i. formam rei inducere, vid. Figurare.
units.tr: Formare, that is, to give a thing its form: see Figurare.

units.la: Formator, vid. Pædagogus, Doctor.
units.tr: Former: see Pædagogus (tutor), Doctor (teacher).

units.la: Formatura, vid. Figuratio.
units.tr: Formation: see Figuratio.

units.la: Formica] Formicula, Arnob. Solpuga, Cic. Solpunga, Lucan. Solifuga, Sipont.
units.tr: Formica: A little ant, Arnob. A solpuga, Cic. Solpunga, Lucan. Solifuga, Sipont.

units.la: Formidare, vid. Timere.
units.tr: Formidare: see Timere (to fear).

units.la: Formosus] Venustus. Cultus. Eximia facie, Ter. Formâ scitâ, Plaut. Spectatâ, Ovid. Speciosior & coloratior homo,Cels. Floridus. Floridulus,Catul. Præsignis facie,Ovid. Formâ conspicuus, Plin.
units.tr: Formosus: Charming, elegant. Of striking appearance, Ter. Of skilled form, Plaut. Of notable beauty, Ovid. A man handsomer and of fresher complexion, Cels. Flowering. A little flower, Catul. Outstanding in face, Ovid. Conspicuous in form, Plin.

units.la: Formula, apud ICtos] Pactio verborum. Juris praescriptum & norma. Conceptio. Concepta verba, Cic. Praescripta verba, Vlp. Praescriptum. Actio, Paul. IC. Sermo de re formatus, Suet.
units.tr: Formula, among the jurists: An agreement in words. The prescribed rule and norm of law. A drafting. Words set down, Cic. Prescribed words, Ulp. A prescription. A legal action, Paul, IC. A speech shaped to a subject, Suet.

units.la: Ad formulam] Pejerare conceptis verbis. Praescriptis verbis agere, Cic.
units.tr: By formula: To swear in set words. To plead in prescribed words, Cic.

units.la: Forsan] Forte, forsitan, Ter. Fortassis. Haud scio an. Si forte, Cic. Fortean, Meurs. Fortassean, Apul.
units.tr: Perhaps: Perhaps, perchance, Ter. Perhaps. I do not know whether. If perchance, Cic. Perhaps, Meurs. Perhaps, Apul.

units.la: Forte, vid. Fortuito.
units.tr: Forte: see Fortuito (by chance).

units.la: Fortis] Fortis & magnus animus. Robustus. Viri propriusanimus, Cic. Non victum fatis caput, Lucan. Achilles alter. Hiccine Achilles est, Plaut. Virilis animus, Ter. Masculus, Hor. Generosus ac potens. Magnanimus, Cic. Animi ingentis foemina, Animi validus, Tac. Milone fortior, Er.
units.tr: Brave: A brave and great spirit. Sturdy. A man's own spirit, Cic. A head not conquered by the fates, Lucan. Another Achilles. Is this Achilles?, Plaut. A manly spirit, Ter. Manly, Hor. Noble and powerful. Great-souled, Cic. A woman of great spirit. Strong in spirit, Tac. Stronger than Milo, Er.

units.la: Fortis debiles non timet] Lanius unus non timet multas oves.
units.tr: The brave do not fear the weak: One butcher does not fear many sheep.

units.la: Fortiter] Viriliter & magno animo aliquid facere. Praebere se virum, Cic. Generosius perire, Hor. Vicit hui perfortiter! Ter. Commasculare frontem, Macr.
units.tr: Bravely: To do something manfully and with a great spirit. To show oneself a man, Cic. To die more nobly, Hor. He has conquered, by heaven, very boldly!, Ter. To make the brow manly, Macr.

units.la: Fortitudo] Robur, magnitudo animi. Magnanimitas. Generosa virtus, Cic. Virtus, Lucr.
units.tr: Courage: Strength, greatness of spirit. Magnanimity. Noble virtue, Cic. Virtue, Lucr.

units.la: Fortitudo pervincit] Fortitudo de adversis triumphat.
units.tr: Courage prevails: Courage triumphs over adversity.

units.la: Fortuito] Forte, forte fortuna, fortuitu. Temere. Non temere creati sumus. Temeritate omnia regi opinabantur, Cic.
units.tr: By chance: By chance, by lucky chance, accidentally. Rashly. We were not created by rash chance. They thought all things were governed by chance, Cic.

units.la: Fortuitus] Obvius. Uti quisque obvius fuit, Sallust. Caecus casus, Cic. Incogitatus, Plaut.
units.tr: Accidental: Met by chance. As each man happened to meet, Sallust. Blind chance, Cic. Unthought-of, Plaut.

units.la: Fortuna] Fors fortuna, Ter. Sors, Sallust. Fors domina campi. Mars belli, communis omnibus, Cic. Genius, Perf. Plaut. Divinitus adjuncta fortuna, Cic.
units.tr: Fortune: Chance, fortune, Ter. Lot, Sallust. Fortune is mistress of the field, and Mars of war, common to all, Cic. Genius, Perf., Plaut. Fortune joined to us by divine providence, Cic.

units.la: Fortuna favens] Felicitas, fortunata fortuna. Secunda admurmuratio, fortuna, Cic. Albus calculus. Niveus lapillus, Ovid. Secundus exitus. Auspicatus impetus. Candidus favonius, Hor. Prosperitas. Beatitudo, & Beatitas, Cic.
units.tr: Favourable fortune: Happiness, fortunate fortune. A second murmur of approval, Cic. A white pebble. A snowy little stone, Ovid. A successful outcome. A favourable start. A bright west wind, Hor. Prosperity. Blessedness and beatitude, Cic.

units.la: Fortuna favente] Temporibus secundis. Prosperis rebus. Bonis meis rebus. Cum secundo flatu fortunae utimur, Cic.
units.tr: With fortune favouring: In favourable times. In prosperous circumstances. In my good circumstances. When we enjoy the favourable breeze of fortune, Cic.

units.la: Fortuna favente uti] Ad felicius latus, aut felicem parietem tem inflectere. Felici diplomate uti, felicitate uti, Cic. Ad-dicunt aves. Album diem agere. Cœlum digito attingere. Deum fieri. Navigare cum felicibus in aëre.
units.tr: To enjoy favourable fortune: To turn toward a more fortunate side or a lucky wall. To use a fortunate diploma, to enjoy good fortune, Cic. The birds declare favourable. To spend a white day. To touch heaven with a finger. To become a god. To sail with the fortunate through the air.

units.la: Fortuna nulla perpetua] Nullus ubique potest felici ludere dextrâ. Heri servus, hodie liber, hodie nullus, cras maximus.
units.tr: Fortune is never constant: No one can play with a lucky hand everywhere. Yesterday a slave, today free, today nobody, tomorrow greatest.

units.la: Fortunæ non fidendum] Fortuna Euripus, citò & variè reciprocans. Fortuna vitrea est, cùm maximè splendet, frangitur.
units.tr: One must not trust fortune: Fortune is an Euripus, quickly and variously reversing its tide. Fortune is glass: when it shines most, it breaks.

units.la: Fortuna sequitur mores] Fortunæ faber est quisque suæ: fortunam sui cuique mores fingunt, fortunatus sapiens, fortunæ victrix sapientia.
units.tr: Fortune follows character: Each man is the smith of his own fortune. Their own character shapes each one's fortune. The wise man is fortunate; wisdom conquers fortune.

units.la: Fortunatè] Addicentibus auspiciis, Tac. Bono auspicio. Salvis auspiciis. Optimis ominibus. Ex sententia. Virgulâ divinâ. Secundo vento, Cic. Felicibus pennis, Prop. Bonis, secundis avibus, Liv. Hercule dextro, Perf. Prosperrimè, Suet. Secundo Aquilone, Hor. Jovis quadrigis. Prosperè. Fauste, Cic.
units.tr: Fortunately: With auspices favourable, Tac. With good omen. With auspices secure. With the best omens. According to one's wish. With a divine rod. With a favourable wind, Cic. With happy wings, Prop. With good birds, Liv. With the right hand of Hercules, Perf. Most prosperously, Suet. With a north wind, Hor. With Jove's chariot. Prosperously. Auspiciously, Cic.

units.la: Fortunatus] Amplissimis fortunæ muneribus ornatus. Fortuna illi divinitus adjuncta est ad res agendas. Nihil illo fortunatius. Florens opibus, honoribus, amicis. Boni, optimi ominis, Cic. Albus dies, Prosper, Suet. Benè ominatus, Hor. Quis vidit homines beatiores? Quis Venerem auspicatiorem? Catul. In quem quicquid conferri potuit, dii homînesque contulerunt, Sen. Natus est vittatus, vel pileatus. Albæ gallinæ filius. Fortunâ ipsâ fortunatior. Polycrate fortunatior, Er. Perbeatus homo, Cic. Sospes cursus, Hor. Secundus exitus, Id.
units.tr: Fortunate: Adorned with the greatest gifts of fortune. Fortune has been joined to him by divine favour for carrying out his affairs. Nothing is more fortunate than he. Flourishing in wealth, honours and friends. Of good, best omen, Cic. A bright day, prosperous, Suet. Well-omened, Hor. Who has seen men happier? Who has seen Venus more auspicious?, Catul. Whatever could be bestowed on him, gods and men have bestowed, Sen. He was born with a ribbon, or with a cap of liberty. Son of a white hen. More fortunate than fortune itself. More fortunate than Polycrates, Er. A most blessed man, Cic. A safe course, Hor. A successful outcome, Id.

units.la: Fortunatum seculum] Aureum seculum.
units.tr: Fortunate age: The golden age.

units.la: Fortunet Deus, vid. Feliciter cedant.
units.tr: May God grant fortune: see Feliciter cedant (may things turn out well).

units.la: Forum] Circus, Cic.
units.tr: Forum: A circus, Cic.

units.la: Forum judiciale] Competens tribunal, Vlp.
units.tr: Court of law: A competent tribunal, Ulp.

units.la: Fovere] Focillare, Suet. Focillari, Varr. Fovere fomentis calidis, Celf. Refovere corpus, Ovid.
units.tr: To cherish: To warm gently, Suet. To warm, Varr. To foment with warm poultices, Celf. To revive the body, Ovid.

units.la: Fraces, vid. Retrimen.
units.tr: Fraces: see Retrimen.

units.la: Fragilis] Vitro fragilior. Vitreus. Vid. Debilis.
units.tr: Fragile: More fragile than glass. Glassy. See Debilis.

units.la: Fragilitas humana] Homo bulla. Homo dei ludibrium. Umbræ somnium.
units.tr: Human frailty: Man is a bubble. Man is God's plaything. Man is the dream of a shadow.

units.la: Fragor] Aridus sonus, Lucr. Silvifragus ventus. Dare sonitu magno stragem, Id. Tonitrua, Sili. Fragrare, vid. Olere.
units.tr: Crash: A dry sound, Lucr. A wind that breaks the forests. To make a great din, Lucr. Thunderclaps, Sil. Fragrare: see Olere (to smell).

units.la: Frangere] Confringere aliquid. Diffringere. Offringere, Plaut. Interfringere, Plin. Perfringere, Cic. Præfringere, Liv.
units.tr: To break: To break something to pieces. To break apart. To break off, Plaut. To break into pieces, Plin. To break through, Cic. To break off in front, Liv.

units.la: Frater] Frater germanus, Cic. Germanus, Ter. Germanissimus frater. Geminus meus frater, Plaut. Uterinus, IC. Fraterculus, Iuv. Fratellus, Scaur.
units.tr: Brother: A full brother, Cic. A brother of the same parents, Ter. A most true brother. My twin brother, Plaut. A brother on the mother's side, IC. A little brother, Juv. A little brother, Scaur.

units.la: Fraternè] Germanè rescribere, Cic. Germanitus, Pompon. Germanum in modum, Plaut.
units.tr: Brotherly: To write back as a brother, Cic. Brotherly, Pompon. In the manner of a brother, Plaut.

units.la: Fraternitas] Germanitas, Cic.
units.tr: Brotherhood: Brotherhood, Cic.

units.la: Fraudare] In fraudem deducere, fraudem facere, Cic. Nectere dolum alicui, Liv. Lacere in fraudem, Lucret. Vid. Decipere.
units.tr: To defraud: To lead into fraud, to commit fraud, Cic. To weave a snare for someone, Liv. To entangle in fraud, Lucr. See Decipere (to deceive).

units.la: Fraudulenter] Fraudulentiùs, Plaut. Pelasgâ arte. (Pelasgi, id est, Graeci, pro fraudulentis habiti, & in fabricando equo, Trojae exitio, id ostenderunt.)
