units.tr: Fraudulently: More fraudulently, Plaut. By Pelasgian art. (The Pelasgians, that is the Greeks, were held to be deceitful, and they showed this in building the wooden horse, to the ruin of Troy.)

units.la: Fraudulentus] Vulpe fraudulentior, Er. Vid. Dolosus.
units.tr: Fraudulent: More cunning than a fox, Er. See Dolosus.

units.la: Fraus] Fraus quasi vulpeculae; fraudatio, Cic. Techna, Ter. Impostura, Gell.
units.tr: Fraud: Fraud, as if of a little fox. Cheating, Cic. Trickery, Ter. Imposture, Gell.

units.la: Fraude sua sibi nocuit] Laqueo suo captus est.
units.tr: He harmed himself by his own fraud: He was caught in his own snare.

units.la: Fremere] Halare naribus, Lucr. Proflare iras, Plin. Follicare naribus, Apul. Mussare, Virg. Et fremitum patulis sub naribus edit ad arma, Lucr. Confremuere omnes, Virg.
units.tr: To roar: To snort through the nostrils, Lucr. To breathe out anger, Plin. To puff through the nostrils, Apul. To mutter, Virg. And from wide nostrils he gives a snort to arms, Lucr. All of them roared together, Virg.

units.la: Fremitus] Strepitus, Cic. Tremor, Virg.
units.tr: Roaring: Noise, Cic. Trembling, Virg.

units.la: Frendere] Horrendum stridens bellua. Infrendens dentibus, Virg. Instrepere dentibus, Claud.
units.tr: To gnash: A dreadful, grinding beast. Gnashing with the teeth, Virg. To grind with the teeth, Claud.

units.la: Frenare equos] Capistrare, Plin. Incapistrare, Apul.
units.tr: To bridle horses: To put a halter on, Plin. To bridle, Apul.

units.la: Frequens, vid. Populosus.
units.tr: Crowded: see Populosus (populous).

units.la: Frequentia] Pompa lictorum. Grex amicorum, Stipatio. Concursatio. Si modò tecti satis estis, ad comitatum nostrum recipiendum. Cohors, Cic. Circumfusi omnis generis hominum frequentiâ, Liv. Caterva, Lucr.
units.tr: Crowd: A train of lictors. A troop of friends. A throng. A press. If only you are enough under cover to receive our company. A cohort, Cic. Surrounded by a crowd of men of every kind, Liv. A throng, Lucr.

units.la: Friabilis] Fragilis dentibus. Crustosus, Plin.
units.tr: Brittle: Brittle to the teeth. Crusty, Plin.

units.la: Friare] Frangere in micas, Plin. Minutatim comminuere. Refringere, Col. Resolvere in pulverem. Interere cyminum, Cato.
units.tr: To crumble: To break into crumbs, Plin. To grind into tiny pieces. To break back, Col. To reduce to powder. To crush cumin, Cato.

units.la: Fricare] Perfricare caput. Defricare in balneis, Cic. Circumfricare, Cato. Scalpere digito, Iuv. Scarificare dolorem, rem,Plin. Scabere se,Plaut. Scarificare gingivas,Plin. Suffricare palpebras,Cels.
units.tr: To rub: To rub the head thoroughly. To rub down in the baths, Cic. To rub around, Cato. To scratch with a finger, Juv. To scarify the pain, Plin. To scratch oneself, Plaut. To scarify the gums, Plin. To rub the eyelids, Cels.

units.la: Fricatio] Friction,Cels. Laceratio genarum,Cic. Linteum exersui, Plaut. Tersus : linteum tersui, Apul.
units.tr: Rubbing: Friction, Cels. A tearing of the cheeks, Cic. A linen cloth for sweating, Plaut. A cloth for wiping, Apul.

units.la: Frigere] Frictum reddere, Plaut.
units.tr: To fry: To serve up fried food, Plaut.

units.la: Frigere] Frigescere, rigescere frigore. Sustineo vim frigorum tectis urbis, Cic. Inalgescere, Cels. Adstringi frigore, Plin. Adurit frigus, Virg. Excruciat me frigus. Gelidum de corpore frigus anhelat. Tremulum quatitur frigore corpus, Lucr. Laborare frigore, Col. A frigore, Plin.
units.tr: To be cold: To grow cold, to stiffen with frost. I withstand the force of the cold with the roofs of the city, Cic. To grow chilled, Cels. To be bound by cold, Plin. The cold burns, Virg. The cold tortures me. It breathes chill from the body. The trembling body is shaken with cold, Lucr. To suffer from cold, Col. From the cold, Plin.

units.la: Frigidus] Frigidulus, Catul. Præfrigida tempestas. Gelidum flumen, Cic. Egelidum, Virg. Prægelidus, Col. Algidus, Catul. Rigidus, Ovid. Alsiosus, Plin. Glacie frigidior, Er.
units.tr: Cold: A little cold, Catul. A cold storm. A cold river, Cic. Cold, Virg. Very cold, Col. Chilly, Catul. Stiff, Ovid. Chilly, Plin. Colder than ice, Er.

units.la: Frigus] Frigiditas, Sipont. Algor, Salust. Algus, ûs, Plaut. Rigor aquæ, Ovid. Frigedo Aquilonica, Varr. Stipatio rigescentium, & se intra se comprimentium.
units.tr: Cold: Coldness, Sipont. Chill, Sallust. Chill, Plaut. The stiffness of water, Ovid. The northern cold, Varr. A crowding together of things stiffening and pressing in upon themselves.

units.la: Fritinnire, cantillare ut aves] Merulæ fringultiunt, Apul. Queruntur in silvis aves, Hor. Minuriunt palumbes, Spart. Argutatur cicada, Næv. Pipilabat passer,Catul. Garrire, Donat. Canturire, Fest.
units.tr: To chirp, to sing as birds do: Blackbirds chirp, Apul. Birds complain in the woods, Hor. Doves coo, Spart. The cicada chirrups, Naev. The sparrow chirped, Catul. To chatter, Donat. To sing, Fest.

units.la: Frivolus] Lusoria quæstio,Plin. Sputatilicus. Futilis. Nugatorius. Ridiculus, Cic. Ludicer, Col. Deridiculus, Gell.
units.tr: Frivolous: A playful question, Plin. Trifling. Futile. Empty. Ridiculous, Cic. Playful, Col. Ridiculous, Gell.

units.la: Frondes] Frondium foliatura. Capillamenta arboris. Tabulata arborum, Col.
units.tr: Leaves: The leafage of fronds. The foliage of a tree. The boards of trees, Col.

units.la: Frons] Animi janua, Cic.
units.tr: Forehead: The gate of the mind, Cic.

units.la: Fronto] Frontosus, Sipont. Cilo, Fest. Latâ fronte, Liv.
units.tr: Brazen-faced: Brazen-faced, Sipont. Cilo, Fest. With a broad forehead, Liv.

units.la: Fructifer] Fructuarius, Plin. Pomifer, Ovid, Pomosus, Prop.
units.tr: Fruit-bearing: Fruit-bearing, Plin. Apple-bearing, Ovid. Abounding in fruit, Prop.

units.la: Fructuosus] Est de pane lucrando. Commodis meis aptum. Fœcunda quæstura, Cic,
units.tr: Fructuosus] It concerns earning one's bread. Suited to my own means. A fruitful quaestorship, Cic.

units.la: Fructus] Fruges, Varr. Fœtus arborum, Plin.
units.tr: Fructus] Crops, Varr. The fruit of trees, Plin.

units.la: Frugalis] Curius, exactiss. frugalitatis civis Romanus. Crassus elegantium parcissimus. Scævola parcorum elegantissimus. Parcissimus colonus, Cic. Frugi victus, Quint. Concinnatitia mensula,Apul. Tenuis cultus,Cic. Tenuiculus apparatus. Qui parvo contentus, tenui cultu victuque delectatur. Frugalissimus vir,moderatus & temperans. Siccum,frugi,continentem virum!Cic. Vini parcus,cibi parcissimus, mus, Catul. Qui singulas esNcas indies edunt. Mihi quidvis sat est, Plaut. Aridus victus, Cic. Coena sine sanguine.
units.tr: Frugalis] Curius, a Roman citizen of most exact thrift. Crassus, the most sparing of elegant men. Scaevola, the most elegant of sparing men. The most sparing farmer, Cic. Plain food, Quint. A neatly contrived little table, Apul. Modest dress, Cic. A rather meagre equipment. One who is content with little and takes pleasure in plain dress and fare. A most frugal man, moderate and temperate. A sober, thrifty, self-restrained man! Cic. Sparing of wine, most sparing of food, a mouse, Catul. Those who eat single beans each day. Anything is enough for me, Plaut. Dry fare, Cic. A dinner without meat.

units.la: Frugaliter] Parcè ac frugaliter vivere, Ter. Exiguo vivere, Claud. Laconicè coenare. Modicè uti liberalitate, Liv. Parcè victitare, Plaut.
units.tr: Frugaliter] To live sparingly and thriftily, Ter. To live on little, Claud. To dine Spartan-fashion. To use generosity in moderation, Liv. To live sparingly, Plaut.

units.la: Frugalitas] Temperies fruendi, Stat. Parsimonia in victu, Cic. Natura paucis contenta. Boni amici fabâ & sale contenti sunt. Natura conservatrix sui. Naturæ necessitas exiguo placatur.
units.tr: Frugalitas] A measure in enjoying, Stat. Thrift in diet, Cic. Nature content with few things. Good friends are content with beans and salt. Nature preserves itself. The need of nature is satisfied with little.

units.la: Fruges] Frugalitas, Apul. Cerealia dona. Messis spicea. Sata læta, Virg. Seges farris, Liv. Adorea, Plaut. Fœnus, Fest. Far in spicis, Varr. Farra lætissima, Virg.
units.tr: Fruges] Frugality, Apul. Gifts of Ceres. A harvest of ears of corn. Joyful sown fields, Virg. A crop of spelt, Liv. Adorea (spelt), Plaut. Hay, Fest. Spelt in the ear, Varr. Most joyful spelt, Virg.

units.la: Frugalitate opus] Cogitato quàm longa sit hiems. Magnum os anni. Asse carum est, quod opus non est.
units.tr: Frugalitate opus] Consider how long the winter is. The mouth of the year is large. What is not needed is dear even at a penny.

units.la: Frui bonis] Potiri pace & pacem. Fungi fortuna. Pasci bibliotheca alicujus. Perfrui otio voluptatis. Vesci voluptatibus, Cic. Frui usura alicujus rei, Quint. Perfuncta satis sum, satias me jam tenet, Ter. Fruisci gloria, Gell. Rem aliquam, Non. Uti-frui, IC. Potior patria commoda, Ter.
units.tr: Frui bonis] To possess and enjoy peace. To discharge one's fortune. To feed on someone's library. To enjoy the leisure of pleasure. To take pleasure in delights, Cic. To enjoy the use of a thing, Quint. I have had my fill, and satiety now holds me, Ter. To enjoy glory, Gell. A thing, Non. Use and enjoyment, IC. I prefer the advantages of home, Ter.

units.la: Frumentarius] Dardanarius, Vlp. Annonæ flagellator. Frumentorum negotiator. Frumentarius negotiator, Plin.
units.tr: Frumentarius] A dealer in grain (Dardanarius, Vlp.). A scourge of the grain market. A dealer in corn. A corn merchant, Plin.

units.la: Frumentaria negotiatio] Dardanaria ars.
units.tr: Frumentaria negotiatio] The Dardanarian trade.

units.la: Frumentum] Far, Sipont. Adoreum semen, Cat. Res frumentaria, Cæs. Annona, Cic. Tac.
units.tr: Frumentum] Spelt, Sipont. Seed of spelt, Cat. The grain supply, Caes. The corn supply, Cic. Tac.

units.la: Frustatim] Frustillatim. Offatim, Plaut. Per partes, Vlp. Incisè. Incisim, Cic. Visceratim dissipant membra, Enn. Laciniatim, Apul.
units.tr: Frustatim] Piecemeal. Morsel by morsel, Plaut. Part by part, Vlp. Cut up. Cut into pieces, Cic. They tear the limbs apart piece by piece, Enn. In shreds, Apul.

units.la: Frustra] Inaniter. Nequicquam volo, Cic. In cassum. Ex vano habere spem, Liv. Futilè provenisti, Plaut. Vanè, Sipont. Apud novercam queri, Plaut. Non si te ruperis.
units.tr: Frustra] In vain. I wish in vain, Cic. To no purpose. To have hope in vain, Liv. You were born to no purpose, Plaut. Vainly, Sipont. To complain to a stepmother, Plaut. Not even if you burst yourself.

units.la: Frustra laborare] Ludere operam in re aliqua. Malè operam locare, Plaut. Oleum & operam perdere. Profundere & perdere vires, vocem, Cic. Ventis verba profundere, Lucr. Inaniter aquam consumere. Leonem larvâ territare. Lapidem elixare. E Tantali horto fructus colligere. Arenæ semina mandare. Nihil agere. Numerare fluctus. Actum agere. In silvas ferre ligna. Lateram lavare. Ex arena funiculum nectere.
units.tr: Frustra laborare] To squander one's effort on something. To spend effort badly, Plaut. To lose both oil and labour. To squander and waste strength and voice, Cic. To pour words to the winds, Lucr. To use up water to no purpose. To frighten a lion with a mask. To boil a stone. To gather fruit from Tantalus's garden. To entrust seeds to sand. To do nothing. To count the waves. To do what has already been done. To carry wood into the forests. To wash a brick. To weave a rope out of sand.

units.la: Frustra conatus sine re] Parturiunt montes, nascetur ridiculus mus.
units.tr: Frustra conatus sine re] The mountains labour, and a ridiculous mouse is born.

units.la: Frustraneus, vid. Irritus.
units.tr: Frustraneus, see Irritus.

units.la: Frustulum] Frustillum, Sipont. Massula salis, Col. Buccella. Ofella carnis, Mart. Offula, Varr.
units.tr: Frustulum] A little fragment, Sipont. A lump of salt, Col. A small morsel. A morsel of meat, Mart. A little bit, Varr.

units.la: Frustum] Fragmentum, Cic. Fragmen. Massa ferri. Offa panis, Col. Crustum (panis) Virg. Quadra panis, Sen. Raudus & Rodus plumbi, Serv.
units.tr: Frustum] A fragment, Cic. A splinter. A lump of iron. A piece of bread, Col. A crust (of bread), Virg. A quarter of a loaf, Sen. A scrap of lead, Serv.

units.la: Fruticare] Fruticari. Propagari : vera gloria radices agit & propagatur, Cic. Fruticescere. Pullulare. Proserpit herba. Plin. Pullulascere, Col. Congerminare, Gell.
units.tr: Fruticare] To put forth shoots. To spread: true glory takes root and spreads, Cic. To grow into bushes. To sprout. The herb creeps forth, Plin. To sprout up, Col. To put forth buds, Gell.

units.la: Fruticetum, vid. Virgetum.
units.tr: Fruticetum, see Virgetum.

units.la: Fucare] Fuco circumlinire, Lucr. Ad placendum fuco aliquid subornatur, Sen. Nitorem cuti inducere, Plin. Mentiri colorem fuco, Virg. Fuco splendente genas ornare, Tibul.
units.tr: Fucare] To smear over with rouge, Lucr. Something is decked out with paint to please, Sen. To put a shine on the skin, Plin. To feign colour with paint, Virg. To adorn the cheeks with glittering paint, Tibul.

units.la: Fucatus] Fuco illitus. Coloratus. Fucosæ merces. Infucata vina, Cic. Insincerus cruor, Virg.
units.tr: Fucatus] Smeared with paint. Coloured. Painted wares. Unadulterated wines, Cic. Impure blood, Virg.

units.la: Fucus] Pigmentum. Offucia, Plaut. Tentipellium, Titin. Tectorium, Iuv. Medicamentum faciei, Sen.
units.tr: Fucus] Pigment. Paint, Plaut. Cosmetic, Titin. Plaster, Iuv. A medicine for the face, Sen.

units.la: Fucus rebus detergendus] Nunquam mihi Mango, Medicus; nunquam muscerda, piper erit.
units.tr: Fucus rebus detergendus] Never for me, Mango the doctor; never shall there be muscerda, there will be pepper.

units.la: Fuga]Fugela, Apul. Præsidium fugæ, Amm. Effugium. Cic.
units.tr: Fuga] Flight, Apul. A means of escape, Amm. A way of escape, Cic.

units.la: Fugare] Vertere, agere in fugam aliquem. Avertere in fugam hostes, Liv. Facere fugam alicui Plaut. Retroagere aliquem. Retro ire cogere, Plin. Dispalare milites, Sisen. Dispergere, Sil. Dissipare, Cæs. Injicere fugam alicui, Plaut.
units.tr: Fugare] To turn someone and drive him into flight. To rout the enemy, Liv. To put someone to flight, Plaut. To drive someone back. To force back, Plin. To scatter soldiers, Sisen. To disperse, Sil. To dissipate, Caes. To put someone to flight, Plaut.

units.la: Fugax] Fugacissimus, Sen. Lepore, Parthis fugacior, Er.
units.tr: Fugax] Most fleeting, Sen. Swifter in flight than the Parthians, Er.

units.la: Fugere]Fugere è manibus. In fugam se conferre, conjicere, Cic. Fugam capessere, Liv. Dimissis manibus fugere, Plaut. Conscisccre sibi fugam, Tac. Conjicere se in pedes. Penetrare se in fugam, Plaut. Ab inermibus pedibus auxilium petere, Salust. Effundi in fugam. Terga dare, vertere, Liv. Mandare se fugæ. Exsequi fugam, Cic. Occipitium & armos ostendere, Prop. Fuga salutem petere, Cæs. Ambobus pedibus fugere. Fugere utroque velo. Apparare fugam. Maturare fugam.
units.tr: Fugere] To flee out of someone's hands. To betake oneself to flight, Cic. To take to flight, Liv. To flee with hands let down, Plaut. To take flight for oneself, Tac. To throw oneself on one's feet. To rush into flight, Plaut. To seek help from unarmed feet, Sall. To pour out in flight. To turn one's back, Liv. To commit oneself to flight. To pursue a flight, Cic. To show the back of one's head and shoulders, Prop. To seek safety by flight, Caes. To flee on both feet. To flee with full sail. To prepare a flight. To hasten a flight.

units.la: Fugere ad aliquem, vid. Confugere.
units.tr: Fugere ad aliquem, see Confugere.

units.la: Fugere citra necessitatem] Nemine persequente fugere.
units.tr: Fugere citra necessitatem] To flee with no one pursuing.

units.la: Fuge, ubi necesse est] Fuga tutior. Fugere satiùs, quàm malè manere.
units.tr: Fuge, ubi necesse est] Flight is the safer course. It is better to flee than to stay on badly, Plaut.

units.la: Fuit, non est] Fuere quondam strenui Milesii. Fui & ego quondam. Fuimus Troës. Omne ego pro nihilo esse duco, quod fuit, quando fuit, Plaut. Habui filiam. De omnibus meis habui dicendum.
units.tr: Fuit, non est] Once there were brave Milesians. I too once was. We were Trojans. I count everything as nothing, what once was, when it was, Plaut. I had a daughter. I have had to speak about all my affairs.

units.la: Fulcire] Fulcire labefacta. Labentem & propè cadentem Rempub. Sustentare officiis. Sustinere humeris Rempub. Adminiculari aliquid. Præfulcire, sublevare adjumento, Cic. Suffulcire aliquid, Lucr.
units.tr: Fulcire] To prop up things that are tottering. To prop up a falling commonwealth. To sustain with services. To bear the commonwealth on one's shoulders. To lean on something. To prop up beforehand, to help with aid, Cic. To prop something from below, Lucr.

units.la: Fulcrum] Fultura ædificii. Statumen vitis. Pedamentum, Col. Fulmentum, Vitruv. Fulcimentum, Apul. Fulcimen, Sipont. Adminiculum, Cic. Stabilimentum, Plaut. Columen rerum. Columna civitatis, Hor. Destina, & Tibicen cœli, Atlas, Arnob.
units.tr: Fulcrum] The support of a building. The prop of a vine. A stake, Col. A brace, Vitr. A support, Apul. A prop, Sipont. A support, Cic. A stay, Plaut. The pillar of things. The column of the state, Hor. The prop and supporter of heaven, Atlas, Arnob.

units.la: Fulgere] Effulgere. Radiare, Virg. Fulgurat auro domus, Stat. Clarescunt luminibus tecta, Tac. Confulgent ædes, Plaut. Stellare, Mart. Ardex apex capiti, Virg. Scintillant templa cœli, Lucr.
units.tr: Fulgere] To shine forth. To radiate, Virg. The house glitters with gold, Stat. The roofs gleam with lights, Tac. The buildings blaze, Plaut. To sparkle like stars, Mart. A fiery peak on the head, Virg. The temples of heaven glitter, Lucr.

units.la: Fulgor] Claritas solis. Splendor cœli, Plin. Claror, Plaut. Candescentia, Vitr. Claritudo, Fest. Non.
units.tr: Fulgor] The brightness of the sun. The splendour of the sky, Plin. Brightness, Plaut. Glow, Vitr. Clearness, Fest. Non.

units.la: Fulgur] Jovis fulgor, Cic. Fulguratio, Sen. Fulgetrum, fulgetra, æ, Plin. Fulminea fax, Val. Arg. Corusçamen, Apul. Abrupti nubibus ignes, Lucr. Missilia ignita Dei. Muta fulmina.
units.tr: Fulgur] The lightning of Jove, Cic. A flash of lightning, Sen. A thunderbolt, Plin. A flaming torch of lightning, Val. Arg. A flashing, Apul. Fires broken out of the clouds, Lucr. Missiles of God, kindled. Silent thunderbolts.

units.la: Fulgurat] Præfulgurat, Val. Arg. Flamma inter nubes corusçat, Cic. Nubila micant, Ovid. Fulgurivit Jupiter, Non.
units.tr: Fulgurat] It flashes before, Val. Arg. Flame flashes between the clouds, Cic. The clouds gleam, Ovid. Jupiter has flashed lightning, Non.

units.la: Fuligo] Cinis ater volaticus. Materiæ ustæ scoria. Camini agglutinamentum.
units.tr: Fuligo] Black flying soot. The dross of burnt matter. The sooty crust that clings to a chimney.

units.la: Fulmen] Sulfur sacrum, Pers. Nubes ardens, Lucan. Fulmineus ignis, Ovid. Conflictu nubium ardor expressus, Cic. Fulminatio, & manubia fulminis prima, secunda, tertia, à Jove missa, Sen. Vortex igneus, Lucr. Alatum Jovis telum, ex Aristophan. Trisulca Jovis tela. Elisi nubibus ignes. Antè ferit, quam flamma micat.
units.tr: Fulmen] Sacred sulphur, Pers. A burning cloud, Lucan. Lightning fire, Ovid. The heat expressed from the collision of clouds, Cic. A thunderstroke, and the first, second and third thunderbolts sent from Jove, Sen. A fiery whirl, Lucr. The winged weapon of Jove, from Aristophanes. The three-forked weapons of Jove. Fires struck out of the clouds. It strikes before the flame gleams.

units.la: Fulminat] Feriunt fulmina montes, Hor. Fulmine percutio. Fulminis ictu deflagravit, Cic. Jaculatur Jupiter orno. Repentino fragore nubium fulmen excussum, Amm. Fulminant inferiora, Sen. pro Fulminantur, Muret.
units.tr: Fulminat] Thunderbolts strike the mountains, Hor. I strike with lightning. He was burned down by a stroke of lightning, Cic. Jupiter hurls lightning at the ash tree. A thunderbolt was shaken loose by a sudden crash of clouds, Amm. They thunder below, Sen. for: they are struck by lightning, Muret.

units.la: Fulmine percussus] Fulmine ictus, fulminatus, Plin. De coelo tactus, Cic. Fulgure afflatus, Plaut. Bidental, Pers. de homine.
units.tr: Fulmine percussus] Struck by lightning, Plin. Stricken by a thunderbolt, Plin. Touched from heaven, Cic. Struck by a flash of lightning, Plaut. A bidental, Pers., said of a man.

units.la: Fumare] Fumigare, Var. Fumificare, Plaut. Insumare, Plin. Transfumat aliquid, Stat.
units.tr: Fumare] To smoke, Varr. To make smoke, Plaut. To smoke over, Plin. To smoke through something, Stat.

units.la: Fumidus] Fumosa ligna, Cat. Fumifer ignis, Virg. Fumificus coquus, Plaut. Fumeus Acheron, Val. Arg.
units.tr: Fumidus] Smoky wood, Cat. Smoke-bearing fire, Virg. A smoky cook, Plaut. The smoky Acheron, Val. Arg.

units.la: Fumus] Volumina fumi, Ovid. Vapor flammae, Sen. Flocci sursum evolantes, Val. Arg.
units.tr: Fumus] Coils of smoke, Ovid. The vapour of a flame, Sen. Flakes rising upward, Val. Arg.

units.la: Funambulus] Schoenobates, Iuv. Neurobates. Petaminarius, Firm. Funirepus, Apul. Qui it per extentos funes, Hor. Ephelmator, Firm.
units.tr: Funambulus] A rope-walker, Iuv. A rope-dancer. A tightrope walker, Firm. A rope-dancer, Apul. One who walks on stretched ropes, Hor. Firm.

units.la: Funebris, vid. Exsequialis.
units.tr: Funebris, see Exsequialis.

units.la: Funis funambulorum] Petaurum, Lucil. Extentus funis, Hor. Catadromus, Suet.
units.tr: Funis funambulorum] The tightrope of rope-walkers: a high rope, Lucil. A stretched rope, Hor. A rope for descending, Suet.

units.la: Funis] Restis. Schoenus, Plaut. Serta, Varr. Linum tortum. Linum, absol. Ovid. Stupa, Gell. Tormentum stupeum, Apul. Funis e stupa tortus, Scal. Cannabis torta.
units.tr: Funis] A rope. A cord, Plaut. A rope of rushes, Varr. Twisted flax. Flax, simply, Ovid. Tow, Gell. A twisted tow-rope, Apul. A rope twisted from tow, Scal. Twisted hemp.

units.la: Funda] Fundibalum, Hier. Lipf. Fustibalus, Veget. Petraria, Lipf.
units.tr: Funda] A sling, Hier. Lipf. A sling, Veget. A stone-thrower, Lipf.

units.la: Fundare] Fundamenta jacere, Suet. Locare, Plin. Ponere, Cic. Ordiri fundamenta ex depressiori loco, Col. Agere fundamenta, Cic.
units.tr: Fundare] To lay foundations, Suet. To set in place, Plin. To put down, Cic. To begin the foundations from lower ground, Col. To carry out the foundations, Cic.

units.la: Fundatio] Fundamentorum positio, Cic. Positio urbis, Muret. Conditus coloniae novus, Apul.
units.tr: Fundatio] The laying of foundations, Cic. The founding of a city, Muret. The new founding of a colony, Apul.

units.la: Funditus] Imitus, Apul. A fundamento, Plaut. Imo fundi, Virg. Evertere fundo, Lucr. Radicibus, Cic. A stirpe, Liv.
units.tr: Funditus] From below, Apul. From the foundation, Plaut. Right down to the bottom, Virg. To overthrow from the bottom, Lucr. From the roots, Cic. From the stock, Liv.

units.la: Fundum] Solum fossae, Caes. Basis columnae, Sipont. Vadum, Plin.
units.tr: Fundum] The bottom of a ditch, Caes. The base of a column, Sipont. A shallow, Plin.

units.la: Fundus] Solum agri, Caes. Terrenum, Col.
units.tr: Fundus] The ground of a field, Caes. Soil, Col.

units.la: Funerare, vid. Humare. Exsequias celebrare. Fungi officio] Gerere potestatem. Sustinere munus. Obtinere partes. Obire rem, Cic.
units.tr: Funerare, see Humare. Exsequias celebrare. Fungi officio] To hold the funeral rites; to celebrate the obsequies. To perform a duty: to exercise power, to sustain an office, to fill a role, to discharge a task, Cic.

units.la: Fungus] Fermentum terræ. Plantæ rudimentum. Callus terræ, Plin.
units.tr: Fungus: the ferment of the earth. The first beginning of a plant. The crust of the earth, Plin.

units.la: Funus] Funebria justa, vid. Exsequiæ.
units.tr: Funeral: the due rites of burial; see Exsequiae.

units.la: Fur] Trium literarum homo. Vesperi suo vivens. Homines cum senis manibus, Plaut. Furunculus, Cic. Perfossor, Apul. Directarius, Vlp. Vecticularius & Effractor, ICt. Compilator, Isid. Lavernio, Fest.
units.tr: Thief: a man of three letters. One who lives by night. Men with six hands, Plaut. A little thief, Cic. A borer through walls, Apul. A directarius, Vlp. One who uses a crowbar, and a housebreaker, ICt. A plunderer, Isid. A Lavernio, Fest.

units.la: Fur notorius] Trifur. Trifurcifer, Plaut. Manifestarius fur.
units.tr: Notorious thief: a thrice-thief. A thrice-rogue, Plaut. A thief caught in the act.

units.la: Fur obvia rapit] Lupus non curat numerum
units.tr: The thief seizes whatever lies in his way: The wolf does not count the sheep.

units.la: Furari] Furari aliquid alicui, vel ab aliquo. Furtum facere. Depeculari aliquem argento, Cic. Admittere furtum, Vlp. Clepere, Plaut. Subducere alicui annulum. Subtrahere aliquid alicui. Suffurari. Suppilari aliquid, Id. Subtrahere aliquid furto, Liv. Sublegere, Virg. Tollere aliquid furtim, Id. Surripere aliquid alicui, Plin. Auferre alicui aliquid Plaut. Ter.
units.tr: To steal: to steal something from someone, or from someone's possession. To commit theft. To rob someone of money, Cic. To admit to theft, Vlp. To filch, Plaut. To slip a ring off someone's finger. To take something away from someone. To pilfer something, Id. To remove something by stealth, Liv. To pick up furtively, Virg. To lift something secretly, Id. To snatch something from someone, Plin. To take something away from someone, Plaut., Ter.

units.la: Furax] Piceatâ manu homo Mart. Milvinis, aut, aquilinis est ungulis. Harpax. Accipiter pecuniarum. Trahax. Rapax. Rapacidæ. Summanus. Vulturius homo. Scio te facilè abstinere posse, si nihil, Plaut. Tax, Id. Tagax, Cic. Manu sinistra non rectè utitur, Catul.
units.tr: Light-fingered: a man with a pitch-smeared hand; with kite's or eagle's talons. A grabber. A money-hawk. A snatcher. A rapacious person. A plunderer. A vulture-like man. I know you can easily refrain, if you take nothing, Plaut. Tax, Id. Tagax, Cic. He uses his left hand badly, Catul.

units.la: Furca] Furcæ bicornes, Virg. Furcula, Sipont Furcilla, Catul. Ferramentum bifurcum, Col. Vari. Bacillum furcillatum, Varr. Ærumnula, Scal. Merga, Col. Bidens, Iuv.
units.tr: Fork: two-pronged forks, Virg. A little fork, Sipont. A small fork, Catul. A two-pronged tool, Col. Vari. A forked staff, Varr. A little hook-like tool, Scal. Merga, Col. Bidens, Juv.

units.la: Furenter] Dementer. Furiose, Cic. Insanè, Varr. Perditè, Ter. Furialiter, Ovid. Bacchatim, Apul.
units.tr: Madly: senselessly. Furiously, Cic. Insanely, Varr. Recklessly, Ter. Furiously, Ovid. In Bacchic frenzy, Apul.

units.la: Furere] Bacchari, Cic. Perfurere, Lucr. Inflammari furore. Furiæ me agitant & insectantur, Cic. Furibundum ruere, Ovid. Agitari furiis, Virg. Intemperiæ agunt aliquem. Non sanum est synciput. Non pro sano agit, loquitur, Plaut. Rabie ferri, Plin.
units.tr: To rage: to rave like a Bacchant, Cic. To rage thoroughly, Lucr. To be inflamed with madness. The Furies harass and pursue me, Cic. To rush about in a frenzy, Ovid. To be driven by the Furies, Virg. Intemperate passions drive someone. His head is not sound; he does not speak or act as one in his right mind, Plaut. To rage with the madness of iron, Plin.

units.la: Furiosus] Furialis, furibundus, fanaticus, Cic. Furiis captus, actus, furiatus, Virg. Lymphaticus. Atrâ bili percitus, Plaut. A furiis oriundus. Furiâ furiosior.
units.tr: Furious: frenzied, raging, possessed, Cic. Seized, driven, or maddened by the Furies, Virg. Crazed. Stirred up by black bile, Plaut. Sprung from the Furies. More furious than a Fury.

units.la: Furor] Furiæ, Cic. Lymphatus, Plin. Lymphaticus error, Sen. Intemperiæ, Plaut.
units.tr: Fury: frenzy, Cic. Madness, Plin. A raving error, Sen. Excess, Plaut.

units.la: Furtim] Furtivè ingressus possessionem, Vlp. Furacissimè, Apul.
units.tr: Stealthily: having entered into possession secretly, Vlp. Most stealthily, Apul.

units.la: Furtum] Detractio alieni, Cic. Furatrinæ artificium, Apul.
units.tr: Theft: the removal of another's property, Cic. The craft of a thief, Apul.

units.la: Futare] Confutare truâ, Titin.
units.tr: To confute: to refute with a trua (a ladle), Titin.

units.la: Futilis, vid. Frivolus.
units.tr: Futile: see Frivolous.

units.la: Futurum omne incertum] Multa cadunt inter calicem, extremaque labra. Nescis quid serus vesper vehat. Vid. Eventus incerti.
units.tr: All the future is uncertain: Many things fall between the cup and the lips. You do not know what the late evening will bring. See Uncertain events.

units.la: G.
units.tr: G.

units.la: Albula, avis] Chlorio. Chlorion, Plin. Vireo. Icterus. Luteus, luridus ales. Picus nidum suspendens, Plin.
units.tr: Albula, a bird] Chlorio. Chlorion, Plin. Vireo. Icterus. A yellow, sallow-coloured bird. A bird that hangs its nest, Plin.

units.la: Galea] Cassis, Mart. Cassida, Virg. Cassila, Fest.
units.tr: Galea] A helmet, Mart. A cassida, Virg. A cassila, Fest.

units.la: Galerus] Galericulus, Suet. Galericulum, Mart.
units.tr: Galerus] A little cap, Suet. A little cap, Mart.

units.la: Gallina] Pecus volatile. Gallinaceum genus. Gallinaceus grex, Col.
units.tr: Gallina] A winged flock animal. A kind of barnyard fowl. A flock of barnyard fowl, Col.

units.la: Gallopavus] Meleagris, Varr. Plin. Gallina Africana, Varr. Avis Lybica. Avis Numidica. Avis guttata, Mart. Pavo Indicus, Longol. Card. Ales ab Indis, Ovid. Æmulus pavi, Iul. Scal.
units.tr: Gallopavus] A turkey, Varr. Plin. An African hen, Varr. A Libyan bird. A Numidian bird. A spotted bird, Mart. An Indian peacock, Longol. Card. A bird from the Indies, Ovid. A rival of the peacock, Iul. Scal.

units.la: Gallus] Gallus gallinaceus, Cic. Gallinaceus, Plin. Maritus gallinarum, Iuv. Prænuncia lucis ales, Ovid. Avis lucis cristata, Mart. Pyctes. Gallinaceus. Gallinacei mares, Col. Canora avis. Nocturnus vigil. Familiæ excitator. Horologium vivum. Gallinacei gregis dux fidelis.
units.tr: Gallus] A cock, Cic. A barnyard cock, Plin. The husband of the hens, Juv. The bird that announces the dawn, Ovid. A crested bird of the daylight, Mart. Pyctes. Gallinaceus. Male barnyard fowl, Col. A singing bird. The night watchman. The rouser of the household. A living clock. The faithful leader of the barnyard flock.

units.la: Ganeo, vid. Scortator.
units.tr: Ganeo, see Scortator.

units.la: Gangræna] Cancer, Celf. Carcinoma, Suet. Cacoëthes. Phagedæna, Plin.
units.tr: Gangræna] A cancer, Celf. A carcinoma, Suet. A malignant ulcer. A phagedaena, Plin.

units.la: Garrire] Verba funditare, Plaut. Garriditare. Gargaridiare, Var. Oblatrare assanias, Apul. Friguttire, Fulgen. Blaterare, Fest. Argutari, Non.
units.tr: Garrire] To pour out words, Plaut. To babble. To gargle words, Var. To bark nonsense, Apul. To chirp, Fulgen. To prattle, Fest. To chatter, Non.

units.la: Garrulitas] Multiloquium, Plaut. Loquacitas, Cic. Verbositas, Firm. Loquendi temeritas. Petulantia loquendi, Gell. Larga copia fandi, Virg. Sartago loquendi, Pers.
units.tr: Garrulitas] Wordiness, Plaut. Loquacity, Cic. Verbosity, Firm. Rashness of speech. Pertness of speech, Gell. A ready flow of speech, Virg. A frying pan of talk, Pers.

units.la: Garrulitas noxia] Garrulum os intricat omnia. Oris infreni finis est calamitas.
units.tr: Harmful talkativeness] A talkative mouth tangles everything. The end of an unbridled mouth is calamity.

units.la: Garrulus] Futilis. Verbosa epistola, Cic. Verborum forum, Hor. Nimius sermonis, Non. Largiloquus. Multiloquus. Morbus loquendi illum tenet. Dicaculus, Plaut. Larga tibi copia fandi, Virg. Oratio ei in ore, non in pectore nascitur, Gell. Satis eloquentiae, sapientiae parum, Salust. Homo non laquacissimus, sed ipsa loquacitas. Ipsa loquacitate loquacior, Er. Cicada muta, miraculum. Dicenda tacenda loquens. Dodonæum æs. Garrire optimus. Loquaculus.
units.tr: Garrulus] Trifling. A wordy letter, Cic. A marketplace of words, Hor. Excessive in talk, Non. Long-winded. Full of words. A disease of speech holds him. A chatterbox, Plaut. A ready flow of speech is yours, Virg. His speech is born in his mouth, not in his heart, Gell. Rich in eloquence, poor in wisdom, Sallust. A man not so much talkative as talkativeness itself. More talkative than talkativeness itself, Erasm. A silent cicada, a marvel. Speaking what should be said and what should be kept silent. The Dodonean bronze. Best at chattering. A little chatterbox.

units.la: Gaudere] Immortaliter, Vehementer, in sinu gaudere. Tam excellenti bono gaude, Cic. Mecum tacitus gaudeo. Id gaudeo, Ter. Gaudere in se, Catul. Sibi gaudere, Lucr. Gaudere animo, gaudio, Plaut. Gaudere facto, Ter. Gaudium capio, Plin. Iun. Ex re aliqua gaudium capere animis. Compleri gaudio, efferri, exsilire, exsultare gaudiis. Cumulari gaudiis. Lætari triumphis de hac re. Illud in primis lætandum mihi esse jure video. Lætitiâ efferor, excitor, perfruor. Lætitiam apertissimè ferre. Lætitiis omnibus incessi. Lætitiam percipere, capere. Exsultare lætitiâ. Capere animo voluptatem. Affici voluptate. Triumphare gaudio. Voluptate perfundi. Gestire lætitiâ, Cic. Hilaror mirum in modum, Plin. Indulgere gaudio, Plin. Iun. Exporrigere frontem, Ter. Quantâ in voluptate debacchabere? Cic. Explicare frontem, Hor.
units.tr: Gaudere] To rejoice immortally, to rejoice vehemently, to rejoice inwardly. To rejoice in so excellent a good, Cic. I rejoice silently with myself. I rejoice at this, Ter. To rejoice in oneself, Catull. To rejoice in oneself, Lucr. To rejoice in mind and joy, Plaut. To rejoice in a deed, Ter. I take joy, Plin. Jun. To take joy in some matter with one's mind. To be filled with joy, to be carried away, to leap, to exult with joys. To be heaped with joys. To exult in triumph over this matter. I see that I have every right to rejoice above all in this. I am carried away, roused, and enjoy to the full with gladness. To show gladness most openly. I have gone forth with all gladness. To perceive and take gladness. To exult with gladness. To take pleasure in the mind. To be affected by pleasure. To triumph with joy. To be steeped in pleasure. To be eager with gladness, Cic. I am wonderfully cheerful, Plin. To indulge in joy, Plin. Jun. To unbend the brow, Ter. In how great a pleasure will you rave? Cic. To smooth the brow, Hor.

units.la: Gaudium] Effusio animi. Lætitia, Cic. Ter.
units.tr: Gaudium] An outpouring of the mind. Gladness, Cic. Ter.

units.la: Gaudium magnum] Lætitia gestiens, Cic. Effusa lætitia, Liv.
units.tr: Great joy] Gladness eager with delight, Cic. Gladness poured out, Liv.

units.la: Gaudium novum] Nova lux effulsit.
units.tr: New joy] A new light has shone forth.

units.la: Gaudium præmaturum] Ante victoriam encomium, triumphus.
units.tr: Premature joy] Praise before victory, a triumph.

units.la: Gavia] Fulica. Phalaris, Plin.
units.tr: Gavia] A coot. A phalaris, Plin.

units.la: Gausape] Penula gausapina. Endromis, Mart. Stragulum villosum, crassum, Steph. Penula mulonia, Cic. Sagum, Veget. Coactilia, Vlp. Subcoactio, Cæs. Toral villosum, Plin.
units.tr: Gausape] A shaggy cloak. An endromis, Mart. A thick, shaggy covering, Steph. A muleteer's cloak, Cic. A soldier's cloak, Veget. Felts, Ulp. A felt undercovering, Caes. A shaggy couch covering, Plin.

units.la: Gelare] Glaciat aqua, Plin. Urunt montana nives, Lucan.
units.tr: Gelare] Water freezes, Plin. The mountain snows burn, Lucan.

units.la: Gelascere] Congelat aqua, Col. Rigere gelu, Liv. Rigere frigore, Lucr. Concrescere glacie, Ovid. Perfrigere, gere, Mart. Glaciari. Adstringi frigore, Plin. Conglaciat frigoribus aqua, Cic. Præirigere, Tacit.
units.tr: Gelascere] Water freezes, Col. To stiffen with frost, Liv. To stiffen with cold, Lucr. To grow together into ice, Ovid. To be thoroughly chilled, Mart. To turn to ice. To be stiffened by cold, Plin. Water freezes with the cold, Cic. To stiffen beforehand, Tac.

units.la: Gelidus] Glacians aura, congelans. Gelatus, congelatus, Col. Glaciatus, perstrictus gelu humor. Conglaciatus. Glacie duratus. Præusta nive membra, Plin. Adstrictus frigore, gelu. Duratus frigore, stantia vina gelu, Ovid. Mare pigrum, colligatum, Apul. Rugosus frigore campus, Hor. Torrida gelu membra; frigore pecora, Liv. Rigentia gelu animantia, Lucr. Aggeribus & alto gelu informis terra, Virg. Crustatus. Hieme humus crustata frigoribus. Gelu duratus, Amm.
units.tr: Gelidus] A freezing, congealing breeze. Congealed, frozen, Col. Water stiffened and bound by frost. Frozen solid. Hardened into ice. Limbs seared by snow, Plin. Bound by cold, by frost. Hardened by cold; wines standing hardened by frost, Ovid. A sluggish sea, bound fast, Apul. A field wrinkled by frost, Hor. Limbs numbed by frost; cattle numbed by cold, Liv. Creatures stiffened by frost, Lucr. The earth shapeless with ridges and deep frost, Virg. Crusted over. Ground crusted over by winter frosts. Hardened by frost, Amm.

units.la: Gelu] Gelatio, Plin. Gelicidium, Cato. Frigoris partus. Aquarum condensator. Herbarum persequutor.
units.tr: Gelu] Freezing, Plin. An icy frost, Cato. The offspring of cold. The condenser of waters. The persecutor of herbs.

units.la: Gemere] Ciere gemitus, Virg. Dare, edere gemitus. Gemitu testari dolores, Ovid. Gemiscere, Claud.
units.tr: Gemere] To raise groans, Virg. To give forth, to utter groans. To attest one's pains by groaning, Ovid. To moan, Claud.

units.la: Gemini] Fratres gemini, Cic. Geminus partus, Liv. Gemelli. Proles gemina, Virg. Gemelli fratres, Ovid.
units.tr: Gemini] Twin brothers, Cic. A twin birth, Liv. Twins. A twin offspring, Virg. Twin brothers, Ovid.

units.la: Geminus] Duplus, Cic. Vid. Duplum.
units.tr: Geminus] Double, Cic. See Duplum.

units.la: Gemma, in arbore] Oculi in arborum furculis, qui germinant, Col. Germen, Id.
units.tr: Bud, on a tree] The eyes on the twigs of trees, which sprout, Col. A shoot, Id.

units.la: Gemma, lapis pretiosus] Lapilli, Hor. Lapillus pretiosus, Curt. Cylindrus, Plin. Lapillus oblongus, Briten. Sidus subterraneum. Summi saxorum. Indicus lapillus.
units.tr: Gem, precious stone] Little stones, Hor. A precious little stone, Curt. A cylinder, Plin. An oblong little stone, Brit. An underground star. The highest of rocks. An Indian little stone.

units.la: Gemmare] Gemmascere, germinare, progerminare, Plin. Turgent gemmæ in palmite, Virg.
units.tr: Gemmare] To put forth buds, to sprout, to bud forth, Plin. The buds swell on the vine-shoot, Virg.

units.la: Non gemmat, (germinat) arbor] Silent arbores. Silens flos. Gemmæ se nondum movent, & surculi silent, Col.
units.tr: The tree does not bud (sprout)] The trees are silent. A silent flower. The buds do not yet stir, and the shoots are still, Col.

units.la: Gemmatio] Germinatio, germinatus, Plin.
units.tr: Gemmatio] A sprouting, a budding forth, Plin.

units.la: Gena] Mala, Lucr. Maxilla, Gerr. Molli vestit lanugine malas juventus, Lucr.
units.tr: Gena] Cheeks, Lucr. A jaw, Gerr. Youth clothes the cheeks with soft down, Lucr.

units.la: Generalis] Communis. Universalis. De omni genere lex, Cic. Catholicus, Quint. Perpetuus, Celf. Oecumenicus, Sipont.
units.tr: Generalis] Common. Universal. A law concerning every kind, Cic. Catholic, Quint. Perpetual, Celf. Ecumenical, Sipont.

units.la: Generaliter] Universe loqui. Generatim quærere. Communiter. Sine designatione personarum & temporum. De toto genere disputare. Acervatim dicere, Cic. In commune de pluribus rebus dicere, Plin. Communitus, Varr. In universum dicere, Quint. Per satyram dicere, Fest.
units.tr: Generaliter] To speak universally. To inquire by kinds. In common. Without specifying persons and times. To discuss a whole kind. To speak in heaps, Cic. To speak of many things in common, Plin. In common, Varr. To speak in general, Quint. To speak in satire, Fest.

units.la: Generare] Procreare. Producere. Profundere,Cic. Progerminare, Plin. Creat terra fructum, Quint. Citat materiam planta, vitis radices, Col. Fœtum facere, Plin. Gignere, Cic. Vid. Fœtificare.
units.tr: Generare] To procreate. To produce. To pour forth, Cic. To sprout forth, Plin. The earth brings forth fruit, Quint. The plant, the vine's roots draw in matter, Col. To make offspring, Plin. To beget, Cic. See Fetificare.

units.la: Generatio] Genitura & origo conchæ. Germinatio. Exortus, Plin.
units.tr: Generatio] The birth and origin of a shell. A sprouting. A rising, Plin.

units.la: Genitor] Procreator, generator, Cic. Auctor generis,sanguinis, Virg.
units.tr: Genitor] A procreator, a begetter, Cic. The author of a race or of a bloodline, Virg.

units.la: Genitrix] Procreatrix, Cic.
units.tr: Genitrix] A procreatrix, a mother, Cic.

units.la: Generosè, vid. Fortiter. Ample.
units.tr: Generosè, see Fortiter. Ample.

units.la: Generositas] Forma & species liberalis. Dignitas vultus & oris, Cic. Forma ad dignitatem apposita, ad Heren.
units.tr: Generositas] Noble form and appearance. The dignity of face and countenance, Cic. A form suited to dignity, ad Herenn.

units.la: Generosus] Ingenuus. Liberali formâ,Plaut. Speciosus, Val.Arg. Liberalis facies. Perliberalis fœmina,Ter. Formâ ad dignitatem appositâ Vir,ad Heren. Ab ore honestissimus, Apul. Mulier omnibus simulacris emendatior. Nulla vox est, quæ formam ejus comprehendere possit, Petron.
units.tr: Generosus] Freeborn. Of noble form, Plaut. Handsome, Val. Arg. A noble face. A very noble woman, Ter. A man of form suited to dignity, ad Herenn. Most honourable in appearance, Apul. A woman more perfect than all statues. No word exists that could comprehend her form, Petron.

units.la: Genius] Deus naturæ. Natalis Deus, Plaut. Genealis Deus, Enn.
units.tr: Genius] A god of nature. A god of birth, Plaut. A genealis god, Enn.

units.la: Genius malus, vid. Dæmon.
units.tr: Evil genius, see Daemon.

units.la: Gens] Sanguis, longo sanguine censeri. Gentilitas, Cic. Natales, Plin. Semen generosum, Ovid. Stemma, Perf. Vid. Natio.
units.tr: Gens] Blood; to be reckoned by long blood. Clanship, Cic. Birth, Plin. Noble stock, Ovid. A pedigree, Pers. See Natio.

units.la: Genti cuique sui mores] Mores regioni respondent.
units.tr: Each nation has its own customs] Customs correspond to the region.

units.la: Gentilis] Gentilitius, Plin. Iun. Genitalis, Stat. Natalis, Col. Generalis macula, Lucr. Tribulis meus, Cic.
units.tr: Gentilis] Of the clan, Plin. Jun. Of birth, Stat. Natal, Col. A stain common to the family, Lucr. My fellow tribesman, Cic.

units.la: Genua flectere] Procumbere in genua. Excipere se, vel corpus poplitibus, Curt. Submittere flexum genu. Flectere genu. Poplite deciduo genua intremuere,Ovid. Excipere se in pedes. Niti genibus, Liv. Excipere se in pedibus, Sen. Congeniculare,Cæcil. Congenulare, Sis. Desidere in imos poplites, Apul. Provolvi genibus, Tac. Pinsere terram genibus, Enn. Adstare in genua, Plaut.
units.tr: To bend the knees] To fall to the knees. To support oneself, or the body, on the knees, Curt. To lower the bent knee. To bend the knee. The knees trembled as the joints gave way, Ovid. To support oneself on the feet. To lean on the knees, Liv. To support oneself on the feet, Sen. To kneel, Caecil. To kneel, Sis. To sink down upon the lowest knees, Apul. To throw oneself at the knees, Tac. To strike the ground with the knees, Enn. To stand upon the knees, Plaut.

units.la: Genus] Genitorum series.
units.tr: Genus] A succession of ancestors.

units.la: Geometria] Linea�ris ratio,Quint. Terræ partitio. Ars metiendi.
units.tr: Geometria] Linear reasoning, Quint. The division of land. The art of measuring.

units.la: Geraria navis, vid. Navis.
units.tr: Transport ship, see Navis.

units.la: Gerere] Gestitare, Plaut. Gestare, Tac. Portitare, Gell.
units.tr: To carry] To carry about, Plaut. To bear, Tac. To convey, Gell.

units.la: Geram officium meum] Non deero officio meo. Nunquam cessabo in officio meo, Er.
units.tr: I will carry out my duty] I shall not fail in my duty. I shall never cease in my duty, Erasm.

units.la: Germanè, vid. Fraternè.
units.tr: Germanely, see Fraternally.

units.la: Germanus, de gente] Teuto. Strabo Teutonus, Plin.
units.tr: Germanus, of the people] A Teuton. Strabo the Teuton, Plin.

units.la: Germen, vid. Gemma.
units.tr: Germen, see Gemma.

units.la: Germinare, vid. Gemmare.
units.tr: Germinare, see Gemmare.

units.la: Gesticularia] Ludia, Mart. Mima, mimula, Cic.
units.tr: Gesticularia] A female mime, Mart. A little mime, a female mime, Cic.

units.la: Gesticulator, vid. Histrio.
units.tr: Gesticulator, see Histrio.

units.la: Gestire, i, velle] Gestio ludere, Perf. Gesturire, Amm. Libido (mihi) est irridere, Plaut. Tenet me aviditas; cupiditas dimicandi; studium alicujus rei. Intemperans sum in ejus rei cupiditate. Ardebat cupiditate sic, ut &c. Cic. Acuit animum aliqua cupiditas. Salivam mihi movet aliquid, Sen. Capiuntur porcelli sequi matrem, Varr.
units.tr: Gestire, to desire] To frolic in play, Pers. To be eager, Amm. I have a desire (to) mock, Plaut. Desire holds me; eagerness for fighting; zeal for some matter. I am immoderate in my desire for that thing. He burned with such desire that etc., Cic. Some desire sharpens the mind. Something makes my mouth water, Sen. Piglets are caught following their mother, Varr.

units.la: Gestus] Motus corporis. Actio, pronunciatio, Cic. Flexus & motus. Eurythinia, Quint. Gesticulus, Non.
units.tr: Gesture] Movement of the body. Delivery, action, Cic. Bending and motion. Eurythmy [εὐρυθμία], Quint. Gesticulation, Non.

units.la: Gestu uti] Gestum agere, Cic. Gesticulari, Suet. Digiti cum voce loquuti, Tibul.
units.tr: To use gesture] To perform a gesture, Cic. To gesticulate, Suet. Fingers speaking along with the voice, Tibull.

units.la: Gibbus] Gibber. Tuber Cameli, Plin.
units.tr: Gibbus] A hunchback. A camel's hump, Plin.

units.la: Gibbosus] Gibber. Gibberosus, Firm. Suet.
units.tr: Gibbous] Humped. Gibberous, Firm. Suet.

units.la: Gigas] Partu terra nefando Coeumque Japetumque creat, sævumque Typhæa, Virg. Extrapeli (id est, prodigioso incremento augescentes,) Plin.
units.tr: Giant] By the cruel earth she bore Coeus and Iapetus, and savage Typhoeus, Virg. Extrapeli (that is, growing to a prodigious size), Plin.

units.la: Gigantæus] Colossicus, & Colosseus homo, Plin. Colosseros homo, Suet.
units.tr: Gigantic] A man of colossal and Colosseus size, Plin. A Colosseros man, Suet.

units.la: Gignere] Generare hominem. Progignere. Procreare. Fœtum producere. Ferre, Cic.
units.tr: To beget] To beget a man. To bring forth. To procreate. To produce offspring. To bear, Cic.

units.la: Gilvus] Flavus. Flavens arena, Virg. Flavidus. Melleus color Cerinus. Cereus, Plin. Cirthus, Gell. Hilvus, Varr. Helvolus. Helveolus, Cato, Varr. Ravus, Fest.
units.tr: Gilvus] Yellow. Yellow sand, Virg. Yellowish. Honey-coloured, the colour of wax, Plin. Cirthus, Gell. Hilvus, Varr. Helvolus, Helveolus, Cato, Varr. Reddish-yellow, Fest.

units.la: Gingiva] Gingivula, Apul. Epulis excrescens caro ad molares, Rhodig.
units.tr: The gum] A little gum, Apul. A fleshy growth on the molar teeth, Rhodig.

units.la: Gingras, tibia stridula] Gingrica tibia. Gingros, Rhodig. Gingrinæ, Fest.
units.tr: Gingras, a shrill pipe] A shrill pipe. Gingros, Rhodig. Gingrinae, Fest.

units.la: Glaber] Glabellus corpore. Cucurbitâ glabrior. Depilis, Varr. Deplumis, implumis, Plin. Subvulsus, Gell.
units.tr: Smooth] Smooth in body. Smoother than a gourd. Hairless, Varr. Featherless, unfledged, Plin. Plucked, Gell.

units.la: Glabrare] Deglubere pecus, Suet. Excoriare, Sipont. Despoliare virgis dorsum alicujus, Plaut.
units.tr: To make smooth] To flay cattle, Suet. To skin, Sipont. To strip a man's back with rods, Plaut.

units.la: Glabrescere] Lævigari, Varr.
units.tr: To become smooth] To be made smooth, Varr.

units.la: Glacies] Crystallum. Concreta in flumine crusta, Virg. Aqua gelu concreta. Duramen aquæ, Lucr.
units.tr: Ice] Crystal. A crust of ice formed on a river, Virg. Water congealed by frost. The hardness of water, Lucr.

units.la: Gladiarius] Gladiator, Bud. Machæropæus, Cæl. Rhod. Gladiorum artifex, Treb.
units.tr: Gladiator (adj.)] A gladiator, Bud. A sword-fighter, Cael. Rhod. A maker of swords, Treb.

units.la: Gladiatorius ludus] Gladiatorium certamen, munus, pugna. Gladiatorium, abs. It. Gladiatores, Cic. Vid. Pugil.
units.tr: Gladiatorial games] Gladiatorial contest, show, fight. Gladiatorial, abs. It. Gladiators, Cic. See Pugil.

units.la: Gladius] Ensis, Lucan. Machæra, Cæl. Spatha, Apul. Mucro, Virg.
units.tr: Sword] Sword, Lucan. A short Greek sword, Cael. A broadsword, Apul. The point of a sword, Virg.

units.la: Glandulæ] Antiades. Tumor faucium, Vlp. Strumæ, Cels. Mammosus pannus, Plin. Phygethlon, Cels. Iun.
units.tr: Glands] Swellings of the glands. A swelling of the throat, Ulp. Scrofulous swellings, Cels. A breast-shaped flap, Plin. Phygethlon, Cels. Iun.

units.la: Glans] Balanus, Plin. Fruges roburneæ, Col.
units.tr: Acorn] Acorn, Plin. Oak-fruit, Col.

units.la: Glarea] Glareola, Plaut.
units.tr: Gravel] Gravel, Plaut.

units.la: Gleba] Grumus terræ, Col.
units.tr: Clod] A clod of earth, Col.

units.la: Glebosus] Glebulentus. Glebiosior terra, Plin. Crassis glebis, Id.
units.tr: Clodded, clayey] Full of clods. Earth more clodded, Plin. In heavy clods, Id.

units.la: Gliscit ignis] Convalescit flamma magnâ congerie, Quint. Volvit globos flammarum aliquid. Furit æstus ad auras, Virg. Ardet in immensum geminatis ignibus Æthna, Ovid.
units.tr: The fire grows] The flame gathers strength from a great heap, Quint. It rolls balls of flame. The heat rages up to the sky, Virg. Etna blazes beyond measure with redoubled fires, Ovid.

units.la: Globus] Sphæra, Cic. Soliditas rotunda, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Ball] A sphere, Cic. A round solidity, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Glocire, gallinarum] Sequitur grex gallinam singultientem. Singultientem matrem sequuntur pulli, Col. Singultus nutricis sequuntur pulli. Singultu pullos convocat, Pallad. Gracillat gallina, Aut. Philom.
units.tr: Clucking, of hens] The flock follows the clucking hen. The chicks follow their mother as she clucks, Col. The chicks follow the nurse's clucking. She calls the chicks with a cluck, Pallad. The hen cackles, Aut. Philom.

units.la: Glomerare fila] Conglomerari posset ejus textura, Lucr. In glomum cogi, Lambin.
units.tr: To wind thread into balls] Its texture could be wound into a ball, Lucr. To be gathered into a ball, Lambin.

units.la: Glomus] Glomulus, Apul.
units.tr: Ball of thread] A little ball, Apul.

units.la: Gloria] Fama perpetua. Nomen. Gloriola, Cic. Adorea, Claud. Claritudo, Sisen.
units.tr: Glory] Lasting fame. Name. A little glory, Cic. Honour won in war, Claud. Renown, Sisen.

units.la: Gloriatio, vid. Iactantia.
units.tr: Boasting, see Iactantia.

units.la: Gloriam captare ex frivolis] In mustaceo laureolam quærere.
units.tr: To seek glory from trifles] To look for a little laurel in a honey cake.

units.la: Gloriari, vid. Iactare se.
units.tr: To boast, see Iactare se.

units.la: Gloriosus] Illustri laude celebratus. In gloria est. Est illustris lustris honore ac nomine vir. Prædicabilis. Magno honore spectatus. Gloriosus in vulgus, Cic. Vid. Celebris.
units.tr: Glorious] Celebrated with illustrious praise. Held in glory. A man illustrious for years and honour. Praiseworthy. Esteemed for great honour. Glorious among the common people, Cic. See Celebris.

units.la: Gloterare] Gloctorare. Crepitante rostro plaudit, Ovid. Ore crepitare, & sonum non vocem edere.
units.tr: To chatter] To clap with a crackling beak, Ovid. To crackle with the mouth and make a noise, not a voice.

units.la: Glubere] Delibrare corticem, Col. Decorticare arborem, Plin. Cingere arborem, Vlp. Deglabrare, Paul. IC.
units.tr: To peel] To strip the bark, Col. To decorticate a tree, Plin. To girdle a tree, Ulp. To make smooth, Paul. IC.

units.la: Gluma] Utriculus Zeæ. Vagina grani. Vaginula, Plin. Theca grani, Varr.
units.tr: Husk] The husk of maize. The sheath of a grain. A little sheath, Plin. The case of a grain, Varr.

units.la: Gluten] Asphaltum, Hermol. Glux, Ausonn. Glutinum, Plin. Colla, Sipont.
units.tr: Glue] Asphalt, Hermol. Glue, Ausonn. Glue, Plin. Size, Sipont.

units.la: Glutinare aliquid] Bitumihare. Conglutinare. Solidare. Concorporare, Plin. Coagmentare. Compingere, Cic. Coadunare statuæ brachium, Vlp. Massare, Lucr.
units.tr: To glue something] To cement with bitumen. To join together. To make firm. To fuse into one body, Plin. To fasten together, Cic. To join an arm back onto a statue, Ulp. To knead, Lucr.

units.la: Glutire] Degulare, Plaut. Trajicere cibum. Transmittit guttur alimenta.
units.tr: To swallow] To gulp down, Plaut. To send food down. The throat passes food along.

units.la: Glycyrrhiza] Glycyrrhizon. Adipsos. Scythice. Scythica, Plin.
units.tr: Liquorice] Liquorice root. Sweet root. Scythian root, Plin.

units.la: Gnarus] Prudens locorum, Liv. Conscius mihi in privatis omnibus. Intelligentia alicujus rei præstat, Cic. Expertus, Liv. Scitus lyræ, Ovid. Expertor turbarum, Sil. Notus. Novi, notis prædicas, Plaut. Sagacissimus naturæ, Col. Experiens. Experientissimus, Cic. Sciens latinæ linguæ, Gell. Scius, Macrob. Multarum rerum usum habet. Peritus ad disciplinam, Cic.
units.tr: Knowing] Acquainted with the places, Liv. Aware of all my private affairs. Knowledge of a matter excels, Cic. Experienced, Liv. Skilled at the lyre, Ovid. Experienced in uproars, Sil. Known. You proclaim things that are known, Plaut. Most perceptive of nature, Col. Experienced. Most experienced, Cic. Knowing Latin, Gell. Learned, Macrob. Has practical knowledge of many things. Skilled in discipline, Cic.

units.la: Gnomen] Solis umblicus, Plin. Indagator umbræ, Vitr. Veruculum in medio amusio stans ad umbras cognoscendas, Philand.
units.tr: Gnomon] The navel of the sun, Plin. A tracer of shadows, Vitr. A small pin standing in the middle of a sundial to show the shadows, Philand.

units.la: Gossampinus] Gosipinus: Linum gossipinum: è gossipio seu Xylo frutice. Linum Xylinum, Plin. Lana lignea, Vlp.
units.tr: Cotton (adj.)] Cotton thread: from the gossypium or xylon shrub. Linen from the xylon, Plin. Wooden wool, Ulp.

units.la: Gossipium] Xylon. Lanigera arbor. Gossampinus arbor, Plin.
units.tr: Cotton] The xylon. A wool-bearing tree. The cotton tree, Plin.

units.la: Gracilescere, vid. Macere.
units.tr: To grow thin, see Macere.

units.la: Gracilis] Gracile corpus. Substricta crura Exiles artus, Ovid. Prætener, Cic. Perexilis, Col. Gracilipes ciconia, Petron. Junceus, Ter. Monogrammos, Cic. Petilus, Lucil.
units.tr: Slender] A slender body. Thin legs. Slim limbs, Ovid. Slender, Cic. Very slender, Col. A thin-legged stork, Petron. Rush-like, Ter. Of a single line, Cic. Lean, Lucil.

units.la: Gracilitas] Exilitas vitis, Col. Tenuitas caudæ, Plin. Gracilitudo statuæ, Acci. Non. Contractus, ûs, & contractura columnarum, Vitr.
units.tr: Slenderness] Thinness of a vine, Col. Slightness of a tail, Plin. Slenderness of a statue, Accius, Non. The tapering of columns, Vitr.

units.la: Graculus] Gracus, Varr. Monedula, Cic. Cornicula, Hor.
units.tr: Jackdaw] Jackdaw, Varr. Daw, Cic. Little crow, Hor.

units.la: Gradarius equus] Tolutarius, Sen. Asturco, Plin. Astur equus, Mart. Ad numerum colligens ungulas, Id. Tolutim incedens, Plaut. Tolutim carpens incessus. Glomeratim incedens, Non. Sinuans volumina crurum. Gressus glomerans superbos, Virg.
units.tr: Ambling horse] An ambler, Sen. A hackney, Plin. A trotter, Mart. Gathering its hooves into rhythm, Id. Ambling along, Plaut. An ambling gait. Walking in a bunched step, Non. Swaying the legs in coils. Gathering proud steps, Virg.

units.la: Gradatim] Gradibus ascendere, Cic. Ad modum scalæ. Scalari formâ.
units.tr: Step by step] To climb by steps, Cic. Like a ladder. In the form of a ladder.

units.la: Gradi] Tollere gradum, Plin. Facere gradum, Cic. Plaut. Gradi gradum. Grandiorem facere gradum. Grandi gradu properare. Grallatorio ire gradu. Militari metari gradu. Vegrandi gradu ire, Id. Proceros passus proferre, Lucr. Ingenti venire gradu, Ovid.
units.tr: To step] To raise a step, Plin. To take a step, Cic.; Plaut. To step step by step. To take a longer step. To hurry with a long stride. To go with a stilt-walker's stride. To measure with a soldier's stride. To go with a very long stride, Id. To bring forward lofty paces, Lucr. To come with a huge stride, Ovid.

units.la: Gradus] Vestigium, Cic. Passus, Lucr.
units.tr: Step] A footprint, Cic. A pace, Lucr.

units.la: Græce loqui] Græcissare. Atticissare, Plaut.
units.tr: To speak Greek] To Grecize. To Atticize, Plaut.

units.la: Græcus] Græcanicus. Græciensis. Græculus, Cic.
units.tr: Greek (adj.)] Greekish. Grecian. A little Greek, Cic.

units.la: Græcus sermo] Græcanicus sermo, Plin. Græcæ literæ, Cic. Hellenismus, Priscian.
units.tr: Greek language] Greek-style speech, Plin. Greek letters, Cic. Hellenism, Priscian.

units.la: Gramen] Boves cum viride comedunt, Col.
units.tr: Grass] Cattle eat the green grass, Col.

units.la: Grammatica] Literatura. Literarum scientia. Literarum cognitio. Rectæ loquelæ, rectæque Scripturæ. Literæ, abs. Cic.
units.tr: Grammar] Literature. Knowledge of letters. Knowledge of letters. Of correct speech and correct writing. Letters, absolutely, Cic.

units.la: Grammaticus] Grammatista. Literator. Literatus, Suet. Filii Grammaticorum.
units.tr: Grammarian] A schoolmaster. A teacher of letters. Literate, Suet. Sons of grammarians.

units.la: Granarium] Cella & horreum Romanorum. Cella frumentaria, Cic. Veterarium, Sen. Veteris frumenti theca. Conditorium frugum, Amm.
units.tr: Granary] The cellar and barn of the Romans. A grain-store, Cic. A store, Sen. A store for old grain. A storehouse of produce, Amm.

units.la: Grandescere] Ingrandescere, Col. Turgescere, Ovid. Crassescere, Plin. Grandere, Col.
units.tr: To grow large] To grow larger, Col. To swell, Ovid. To thicken, Plin. To grow, Col.

units.la: Grandinat] Grando decidit, Zenod.
units.tr: It hails] Hail falls, Zenod.

units.la: Grandinare definit] Degrandinat, Ovid.
units.tr: Hail stops] It stops hailing, Ovid.

units.la: Grandis] Grandior virgo, grandiuscula, Ter. Grandiculus. Statutus homo, Plaut. Adulti artus, Stat. Generosus, Ovid. Incrementi majoris, Col. Quadricubitus, Iun.
units.tr: Tall] A taller girl, rather tall, Ter. A man of stature, Plaut. Full-grown limbs, Stat. Noble, Ovid. Of greater growth, Col. Four cubits tall, Juv.

units.la: Granditas] Auctus arboris. Augmen corporis perfectum, ītum, Lucr. Generositas surculorum, Pallad. Majestas boum, Varr.
units.tr: Size] The growth of a tree. The full increase of a body, Lucr. The vigour of shoots, Pallad. The majesty of cattle, Varr.

units.la: Grando] Glacies suspensa, Sen. Calamitas olera non attigit, Plaut. Calamitosa tempestas, Cic. Guttæ aquæ concretæ solito grandiores, Firm. Congelata pluvia. Grandine concussum, calamitosum frumentum.
units.tr: Hail] Suspended ice, Sen. A calamity that did not touch the vegetables, Plaut. A calamitous storm, Cic. Drops of water frozen larger than usual, Firm. Congealed rain. Grain beaten by hail, a ruined crop.

units.la: Granum] Nucleus pomi, uvæ, Plin.
units.tr: Kernel] The core of an apple or grape, Plin.

units.la: Grassari, violento gressu ferri] Cursu magno ferri. Incitatus feror, Cic. Effusissimis habenis invadere, Cic.
units.tr: To rush, to be carried with violent step] To be carried along at great speed. I am carried away, Cic. To rush in with loosened reins, Cic.

units.la: Grate] Grata memoria. Grato animo prosequi aliquid, Cic. Gratanter accipere aliquem, Capitol. Secundâ voluntate hominum, Cic.
units.tr: Pleasantly] A pleasing memory. To follow something with a grateful mind, Cic. To receive someone gladly, Capitol. With the goodwill of people, Cic.

units.la: Gratia] Propensior voluntas. Secunda voluntas, Cic. Favor, Claud.
units.tr: Grace, favour] A more favourable will. A favourable will, Cic. Favour, Claud.

units.la: Gratia non potest referri par parenti, ne malo quidem] Nemo parem gratiam referre parenti potest, ne malo quidem. Nec malo parenti quisquam referre gratiam potest. Non potest par gratia rependi patri vel malo.
units.tr: Grace cannot be repaid equally to a parent, not even with evil] No one can repay a parent with equal kindness, not even with evil. Nor can anyone repay a parent's kindness even with evil. An equal kindness cannot be returned to a father, even with evil.

units.la: Gratia sit constans] Immortales sunt gratiarum horti, Sen.
units.tr: Grace is constant] The gardens of kindness are immortal, Sen.

units.la: Gratias agere] Grates alicui habere, Plaut. Amplissimis verbis gratias agere. Immortales, incredibiles, mirificas, ingentes gratias agere. Amo te de hac re. Multum te amamus quòd. Utinam illum diem videam, quo tibi agam gratias. Summâ gratiarum actione complector officium tuum. Quibus officiis tua beneficia remunerabor? Ago tibi gratias singulares. Partem meritorum alicujus referendâ, aut cogitandâ gratia consequi, Cic. Tui beneficii in perpetuum praedicator ero. Maximas gratias tibi ago, majores etiam habeo, Id. Quod tam officiosè me commendaris, gratiam & habeo, & habiturus immortalem. Quòd tantâ fide mea negotia procuraris, pares gratias agere vix possum, referre nequaquam. Quòd me passim amantissimè praedicas, video quantum debeam tuo in me studio. Quòd meis commodis tantopere studes, & habetur à me gratia, & habetur semper. Quòd nos pro tua virili tueris, gratum est. Grates persolvere dignas non opis est nostræ. Fateor me tibi devinctum vinctum esse. Hoc nomine plus tibi debeo, quàm ut unquam solvendo esse possim. Hic officio arctius me tibi adstrinxisti, obligatiorem reddidisti, magis obnoxium effecisti, quàm ut vel verbis agere gratias possim, Er.
units.tr: To give thanks] To owe thanks to someone, Plaut. To give thanks in the warmest words. To give thanks immortal, incredible, wonderful, and great. I love you for this. We love you very much because... I wish to see that day on which I may give you thanks. I embrace your service with the fullest thanks. With what services shall I repay your benefits? I give you my special thanks. To obtain a share of someone's merits by repaying or by intending gratitude, Cic. I shall be a perpetual proclaimer of your kindness. I give you the greatest thanks, and I have even greater, Id. Since you commend me so dutifully, I have thanks and shall have them forever. Since you handle my affairs with such faithfulness, I can scarcely give equal thanks, and cannot repay at all. Since you praise me everywhere so lovingly, I see how much I owe to your zeal for me. Since you take such pains for my advantage, I have thanks, and always shall. Since you defend us with your manly strength, it is welcome. Thanks worthy of payment are beyond my power. I confess myself bound to you. On this account I owe you more than I could ever repay. By this service you have bound me to you more tightly, made me more obliged, and made me more indebted than that I could give thanks even in words, Er.

units.la: Gratia Dei] Est diis gratia unde hæc fiant, Ter. Deûm virtute multa bona penè parta habemus, Plaut. Diis volentibus magni & opulenti estis, Sallust. Divina gratiâ, liberalitate, benignitate. Quæ benignitas Dei est. Quod divinæ benignitati tribuo. Quod volente & largiente Deo accidit, Dei munere.
units.tr: The grace of God] It is by the grace of the gods that these things come about, Ter. We have many good things almost won by the power of the gods, Plaut. By the gods' will you are great and rich, Sallust. By divine grace, generosity, kindness. This is the goodness of God. What I attribute to divine goodness. What happens by God's willing and bountiful gift, by the gift of God.

units.la: Gratiam inire, vid. Mereri de aliquo bene.
units.tr: To win favour, see To deserve well of someone.

units.la: Gratificari alicui] Beasti me. Respondere voto alicujus, Plin. Iun. Ex voluntate alicujus agere, Quint. In gratiam, honorem alicujus agere, Sen. Ad voluntatem loqui. Gratiam quærere, Cic. Volentia plebi facere, Non.
units.tr: To gratify someone] You have made me happy. To answer someone's wish, Plin. Iun. To act according to someone's will, Quint. To act in someone's favour or honour, Sen. To speak to someone's liking. To seek favour, Cic. To make things pleasing to the people, Non.

units.la: Gratis] Gratiis. Per beneficium & gratiam alicui concedere aliquid, Cic. Gratiis, Ter. Ex pari gratia eccam tibi, Plaut. Gratiâ, Flor.
units.tr: Free of charge] Freely. To grant something to someone as a favour and kindness, Cic. Freely, Ter. I give it to you on equal terms, Plaut. By favour, Flor.

units.la: Gratitudo] Gratus animus. Gratia & memoria officiorum, beneficii &c. Cic.
units.tr: Gratitude] A grateful mind; gratitude and remembrance of kindnesses, of benefits, etc. Cic.

units.la: Gratuitus] Voluntarius amicus, Cic. Ultroneus, Sen. Spontaneus, Macr. Spontalis, Apul. Beneficiarius, Sen.
units.tr: Gratuitous] A willing friend, Cic. Unbidden, Sen. Spontaneous, Macr. Spontaneous, Apul. Bestowed as a favour, Sen.

units.la: Gratulari alicui, hoc vel illud] Gaudeo te nobis optantibus incolumem esse redditum. Gratulamur tibi victoriam, Suet. Gratulor vicisse te. Quod victor redieris, vehementer gaudeo. Te novâ prole esse auctum, gaudeo. Salvum te advenire volupe est. Lætor tuo nomine, quòd uxor feliciter peperit. Voluptati mihi est, quòd tibi res ex sententia cesserit. Tuâ gratiâ gaudeo, quòd res præter spem bene verterit, Er.
units.tr: To congratulate someone on this or that] I am glad that you have returned safe, as we hoped. We congratulate you on your victory, Suet. I congratulate you on having conquered. I am very glad that you have returned as a victor. I am glad that you have been blessed with a new child. It is a pleasure to see you arrive safe. I rejoice on your account that your wife has given birth successfully. It gives me pleasure that things have turned out as you wished. I am glad on your behalf that matters have turned out well beyond expectation, Er.

units.la: Gratulatio] Congratulatio, Cic. Faventia, Val. Max. Bona ominatio, Fest.
units.tr: Congratulation] Congratulation, Cic. Good wishes, Val. Max. A favourable omen, Fest.

units.la: Gratus, i. e. acceptus] Pergratus. Gratus in vulgus, Tac. Grati generis, Plaut. Habet gratiam, Plin. Vid. Acceptus. Suavis.
units.tr: Pleasing, that is, acceptable] Very pleasing. Popular with the crowd, Tac. Pleasing of kind, Plaut. Is held in favour, Plin. See Acceptable. Pleasant.

units.la: Gratus beneficii] Gratus ac memor beneficii. Gratus in aliquem. Respondet officiis, Cic. Bene apud memores veteris teris stat gratia facti, Virg. Quod beneficium haud sterili te obsevisse, in segete cognosces, Acci.
units.tr: Grateful for a benefit] Grateful and mindful of a benefit. Grateful towards someone. He repays kindnesses, Cic. The grace of a deed well done stands firm among those who remember it, Virg. You will know that you have sown a benefit not in barren soil, from the harvest, Acc.

units.la: Gravare] Aggravare, Quint. Deprimere, Plaut. Prægravare, Plin. Coonerare, Tac.
units.tr: To burden] To weigh down more heavily, Quint. To press down, Plaut. To weigh down greatly, Plin. To overload, Tac.

units.la: Gravari] Urgeri onere. Urget onus, Cic. Gravat me iste labor. Urgetur corpus mole, Virg. Est mihi oneri, Liv.
units.tr: To be burdened] To be pressed by a load. The load presses, Cic. This toil weighs upon me. The body is pressed by its weight, Virg. It is a burden to me, Liv.

units.la: Gravatim, vid. Invitè.
units.tr: Heavily, see Unwillingly.

units.la: Gravedo] Destillatio, Cæs. Rheumatisma, Cæl. Rhod. Destillans humor, Cels.
units.tr: Catarrh] A dripping, Caes. Rheumatism, Cael. Rhod. A dripping humour, Cels.

units.la: Gravida mulier] Prægnans fœmina, Cic. Repleta, Justin. Gravida puero mulier, Plaut. Fœta, Col. Virg. Gravis utero, Plin.
units.tr: A pregnant woman] A pregnant woman, Cic. Filled, Justin. A woman heavy with a child, Plaut. Breeding, Col. Virg. Heavy in the womb, Plin.

units.la: Gravidant se animalia] Faciunt gravida, Plaut. Implent fœmellam, Col. Ter. Implevit uterum generoso sanguine, Ovid.
units.tr: Animals become pregnant] They make her pregnant, Plaut. They fill the female, Col. Ter. He filled her womb with noble blood, Ovid.

units.la: Graviditas] Alvus gravida, Fest. Prægnatio animalium, arborum, Varr.
units.tr: Pregnancy] A pregnant belly, Fest. The conception of animals and of trees, Varr.

units.la: Grave quid] Onus Æthnâ gravius sustinere. Oneris magni. Gravior quàm ut ferri possit.
units.tr: A heavy thing] To bear a burden heavier than Aetna. Of great weight. Heavier than can be borne.

units.la: Gravis] Ponderosus. Onerosus, gravida manus, Plaut. Multas manus poscit. Ingestabilis. Prægravis, Plin. Pondus habens, Ovid. Injustus fascis, Virg. Contrarium æs, Fest.
units.tr: Heavy] Ponderous. Burdensome; a hand heavy with a load, Plaut. It demands many hands. Hard to carry. Very heavy, Plin. Having weight, Ovid. An unjust bundle, Virg. Bronze of the opposite kind, Fest.

units.la: Gravis vir] Auctoritate gravis. Magnæ auctoritatis. Magna auctoritate. Habet auctoritatem. Valet auctoritate. Præditus auctoritate. Vir in quo summa est auctoritas & amplitudo. Serius & gravis vir. Dignitatis retinens. Locuples auctor, Cic. Amplissimus auctor, Tac. Plin.
units.tr: A serious man] Weighty in authority. Of great authority. With great authority. Has authority. Has influence. Endowed with authority. A man in whom there is the highest authority and dignity. A serious and grave man. Keeping his dignity. A wealthy authority, Cic. A most distinguished authority, Tac. Plin.

units.la: Graviter] Graviter concidit, Virg. Prægraviter, Cic. Gravatim cadere, Lucr.
units.tr: Heavily] He fell heavily, Virg. Very heavily, Cic. To fall heavily, Lucr.

units.la: Gregatim] Frequenter, frequentissimi venerunt, Cic. Cæs. Catervatim volant sturni, Plin. Acervatim, Id. Uno grege, Curt. Globatim dispersi prædones, Amm. Conglobatim, Liv. Congestim, fartim, coacervatim, Apul. Congestè, Iul. Cap. Numerosissimè, Apul. Glomeratim eunt, Macrob.
units.tr: In flocks] Frequently; very many came, Cic. Caes. Starlings fly in flocks, Plin. In heaps, Id. In one herd, Curt. Robbers scattered in bands, Amm. In crowds, Liv. In heaps, in clusters, in piles, Apul. Crowded together, Jul. Cap. Very numerously, Apul. They go in clusters, Macrob.

units.la: Gremium] Sinus. Complexus, Cic.
units.tr: Lap] A fold. An embrace, Cic.

units.la: Gremium vestis] Lacinia, Plaut. Ala vestis, Scal. Alaria, pl. Grumusterra] Gleba, Cic. Panes æris, Granum, Plin. Massa, Virg.
units.tr: Fold of a garment] A hem, Plaut. The wing of a garment, Scal. Wings, plural. Clod] A clod of earth, Cic. Lumps of bronze, grain, Plin. A mass, Virg.

units.la: Gubernare navem] Gubernare, abs. Clavum tenere. Gubernacula tractare. Sedere ad gubernacula. Moderari navigium, Cic.
units.tr: To steer a ship] To steer, absolutely. To hold the tiller. To handle the helm. To sit at the helm. To control a vessel, Cic.

units.la: Gubernator] Moderator & gubernator ventorum, Cic. Auriga carinæ, Carif. (Proreta in prora, Gubernator in puppi) Servaculus, Varr. Proreus, Ovid.
units.tr: Steersman] Controller and steersman of the winds, Cic. Charioteer of the keel, Carif. (the look-out at the prow, the helmsman at the stern) A little servant, Varr. A bowman, Ovid.

units.la: Gula, vid. Guttur.
units.tr: Gullet, see Throat.

units.la: Gubernatio, vid. Moderamen.
units.tr: Government, see Moderation.

units.la: Gulosus] Heluo. Gurges, natus abdomini suo. Virago, Cic. Catillo, guttur, gutturosus. Ingluviosus. Curculio, Fest. Comedo, Varr. Gluto, Perf. Lurco, Plaut. Venter, Lucil. Barathrum macelli, Hor.
units.tr: Greedy] A glutton. A whirlpool, born for his own belly. A shrew, Cic. Gullet-bound, throaty. Gluttonous. A weevil, Fest. He eats up, Varr. A guzzler, Pers. A gobbler, Plaut. A belly, Lucil. The pit of the market, Hor.

units.la: Gummi] Lacryma arborum, Plin. Gumma, gumen, Pallad. Gummis, Col.
units.tr: Gum] A tear of trees, Plin. Gum, Pallad. With gum, Col.

units.la: Gurges] Vorago, Cic. Charybdis, Virg.
units.tr: Whirlpool] An abyss, Cic. Charybdis, Virg.

units.la: Gurgulio] Summum gulæ. Fauces, Plin. Frumen, Donat.
units.tr: Uvula] The top of the throat. The jaws, Plin. A windpipe, Donat.

units.la: Gustare] Degustare. Facere vini censuram, Plin. Explorare gustu epulas, Tac. Tentare gustu. Explorare maturitatem uvarum, Col. Delibare cibos, Claud. Libare, Virg. Primis labris attingere, Cic. Pitissare, (modicè bibendo gustare) Ter. Prolibare, Plin.
units.tr: To taste] To sample. To make a judgement of wine, Plin. To test a feast by taste, Tac. To try by taste. To test the ripeness of grapes, Col. To nibble at food, Claud. To sip, Virg. To touch with the first lips, Cic. To sip, drinking moderately, Ter. To taste beforehand, Plin.

units.la: Gustatio] Præcibatio, Fest. Prolibatio. Libamentum, Sen. Degustatio, Vlp. Gustatus, Cic.
units.tr: Tasting] A foretaste, Fest. A tasting beforehand. An offering, Sen. A sampling, Ulp. A tasting, Cic.

units.la: Gustus] Gula, Col. Intellectus saporum est in palato, Plin. Palatum, Ovid. Ingeniosa gula, Mart.
units.tr: Taste] Appetite, Col. The perception of flavours is in the palate, Plin. The palate, Ovid. A clever palate, Mart.

units.la: Gutta] Ros, Ovid. Cum tot possideret flumina in suo orientia, in suo cadentia, mendicavit stillicidia, Sen. Stilla, Plin. Aspergo, inis, Amm.
units.tr: Drop] Dew, Ovid. Though he possessed so many rivers, rising in his own land and falling in it, he begged for drippings, Sen. A drop, Plin. A sprinkling, Amm.

units.la: Guttatim] Per stillicidia, Sen.
units.tr: Drop by drop] By dripping, Sen.

units.la: Guttatus] Rorans poculum, Cic. Guttans, Plin.
units.tr: Spotted] A cup dripping with dew, Cic. Dripping, Plin.

units.la: Guttur] Gula, Plin. Gluttus, vel Glutus, Perf. Cibaria fistula, Lact. Rumen, Fest. Stomachus, Cic.
units.tr: Throat] Gullet, Plin. Gullet or throat, Pers. A food-pipe, Lact. The gullet, Fest. Stomach, Cic.

units.la: Gymnasium, vid. Schola.
units.tr: Gymnasium, see School.

units.la: Gynæceum, vid. Virginal.
units.tr: Women's quarters, see Virginal.

units.la: Gyrare, vid. Rotundare.
units.tr: To turn round, see To make round.

units.la: Gyrus, vid. Circuitio.
units.tr: Circle, see Circuit.

units.la: H.
units.tr: H.

units.la: Habena] Habena curulis. Lorum, Trop. Virg. Retinaculum, Id.
units.tr: Rein] Curule rein. Thong, Trop. Virg. Tether, Id.

units.la: Habe tibi hoc] Tene tibi. Apage istiusmodi salutem cum cruciatu quæ advenit. Solum eum, licet ames, me æmulum non habebis. Serva tibi, Plaut.
units.tr: Keep this to yourself] Hold on to it. Away with such a greeting, which comes with torment. Although you love him, you will not have me as a rival. Keep it for yourself, Plaut.

units.la: Habeo] Est mihi, Possideo, Cic. Obtineo aliquid, Ter. Occupo, Lucr. Inest mihi, Plin.
units.tr: I have] I have it; I possess, Cic. I hold something, Ter. I occupy, Lucr. It is in me, Plin.

units.la: Habeo te] Captus es.
units.tr: I have you] You are caught.

units.la: Habitaculum] Domicilium. Commoratio. Sedes, Cic. Habitatio, Col. Mansio, Pallad. Tabernaculum.
units.tr: Dwelling] Abode. Lodging. Seat, Cic. Habitation, Col. Dwelling, Pallad. Tabernacle.

units.la: Habitare] Nunc hic habet, Salust. Inhabitare in, Plin. Incolere aliquem locum. Colere urbem. Commorari in vita. Morari in Italia. Manere domi. Degere inter feras. Versari in, Cic. Demorari alicui, Vlp. Tenere se alicubi, Plin. Iun. Agitare in tuguriis, Sal. Agemus illic. Circumcolere aliquem locum, Liv. An superne agentes humana negligant? Non. Stabulari, Serv. Intermanere, Lucan.
units.tr: To dwell] Now he has it here, Sall. To dwell in, Plin. To inhabit a place. To cultivate a city. To linger in life. To stay in Italy. To remain at home. To live among wild beasts. To be occupied in, Cic. To stay with someone, Ulp. To keep oneself somewhere, Plin. Iun. To dwell in hovels, Sal. We shall live there. To surround a place, Liv. Do those who live on high neglect human affairs? Non. To stable, Serv. To remain between, Lucan.

units.la: Habitant ibi] Habitatur & colitur ea pars frequentissimè. Habitabilis est regio, Cic.
units.tr: They live there] That part is very thickly inhabited and cultivated. The region is habitable, Cic.

units.la: Habitudo corporis] Constitutio. Habilitas. Affectio corporis firma, Cic. Temperamentum, Firm. Temperatura, Plin.
units.tr: Habit of body] Constitution. Fitness. A firm condition of the body, Cic. Temperament, Firm. Temperature, Plin.

units.la: Hac] Istac, Ter.
units.tr: This way] That way, Ter.

units.la: Hactenus] Adhuc. Usque. Usque eò donec, Plaut. Usque eò dum. Ad id locorum, Liv. Tantisper dum. Tam diu quàm diu. Tam diu dum. Eatenus, Cic. Tantisper quoad, Vlp. Eousque, Colum. Usque adeo dum. Usque dum, Ter. Tam diu donec, Col. Tam diu quoad, Vlp.
units.tr: Hitherto] Until now. Up to. Up to the point that, Plaut. Up to the time when. Up to that place, Liv. For just as long as. As long as ever. As long as while. So far, Cic. For just so long as, Ulp. Up to this point, Colum. Just as long as at once. Until, Ter. As long as until, Col. As long as, Ulp.

units.la: Hæmorrhois, vid. Menstrua.
units.tr: Haemorrhois, see Menstrua.

units.la: Hærere] Inhærescere in. Implicari aliquâ re. Inhærere. Illaqueari. Irretiri. Valdè implicatus hæreo, Cic. Hæsitare, Liv. Innecti, Tac. Impedivit se in plagas, Plaut. Obhæret equus, Lucr. Impeditus ac penè constrictus sum.
units.tr: To cling] To stick to something. To become entangled in something. To cling, be ensnared, be caught in a net. I am very much entangled and cling fast, Cic. To hesitate, Liv. To be bound fast, Tac. He entangled himself in the snares, Plaut. The horse sticks fast, Lucr. I am hindered and almost bound fast.

units.la: Hærere ubi prius] Hærere in iisdem scopulis. In eodem luto. In hoc mihi aqua hæret.
units.tr: To cling where before] To stick on the same rocks. In the same mud. In this, the water sticks for me.

units.la: Hæresiarcha] Qui populari blandiente favore, sensim calum pertinaciæ ubi obduxit, deplorata arrogantia decreta sua adstruxit, Bud. Rerum novarum in disciplina Christiana reus. Pravarum religionum virus spargens. Antichristi multi sunt ex 1 Joh. 2. 18. August. Pravi alicujus dogmatis primus auctor, seminator, ac magister.
units.tr: Heresiarch] One who, flattered by popular favour, gradually drew over his eyes the veil of obstinacy, and, with arrogance made desperate, built up his own decrees, Bud. Guilty of novelties in Christian discipline. Spreading the poison of perverse religions. There are many antichrists, from 1 John 2:18, Aug. The first author, sower and teacher of some perverse doctrine.

units.la: Hæresis] Cato est in ea hæresi, id est, opinione, Cic. Vid. Secta.
units.tr: Heresy] Cato is in that heresy, that is, that opinion, Cic. See Sect.

units.la: Hæreticus] Pestiferis de religione opinionibus imbutus. Catholicæ Ecclesiæ dogmata impugnans. Qui illum, aut istum profitetur, Bud.
units.tr: Heretic] Imbued with pestilent opinions about religion. Attacking the doctrines of the Catholic Church. One who professes this or that, Bud.

units.la: Hæsitans] Elucutantium verborum homo, Tac. Singulas syllabas singultiens, Apul. Titubans lingua, Ovid. Vid. Balbus.
units.tr: Hesitant] A man of faltering speech, Tac. Stuttering out each syllable, Apul. Tongue-tied, Ovid. See Stammering.

units.la: Hæsitantia] Hæsitatio linguæ. Titubatio, Cic. Titubantia linguæ, Macrob. Titubantia oris, Suet. Nodus linguæ, Justin. Offensantis linguæ fragmen. Blæsum os tibi debilisque lingua est, Manut. Obligatio linguæ, Justin.
