units.tr: Hesitancy] Hesitation of the tongue. Stammering, Cic. Faltering of the tongue, Macrob. Faltering of the mouth, Suet. A knot in the tongue, Justin. A fragment of a stumbling tongue. Your mouth is lisping and your tongue weak, Manut. A tying up of the tongue, Justin.

units.la: Hæsitare] Titubare, & Titubare verbo. Titubante lingua loqui. Pisoniano vitio teneri, (qui tertiata verba vix profert, & tamen loqui non cessat, quod Pisoni objicit Cicero.) Labi sermone. Resorbere vocem carptim, Plin. Adhæsè loqui, Gell. Fringultire, Apul. Fremens & semianimi voce substrepens ait, Petron. Infringere linguam, Lucr.
units.tr: To hesitate] To stammer, and to falter in words. To speak with a faltering tongue. To be afflicted with the Pisonian fault (one who scarcely utters three-times-repeated words, yet never stops talking, which Cicero objects to Piso). To slip in speech. To swallow back the voice in fragments, Plin. To speak in a clinging way, Gell. To gasp out, Apul. Trembling and muttering in a half-dead voice, he speaks, Petron. To break the tongue, Lucr.

units.la: Halare] Halitare, Enn. Reddere animam, Lucr. Spiritum, Celf. Anhelare, Cic. Prospirare, Cato.
units.tr: To breathe] To breathe out, Enn. To give up the spirit, Lucr. To breathe out the breath, Celf. To pant, Cic. To breathe forth, Cato.

units.la: Halcyon] Halcedo, Plaut.
units.tr: Halcyon] Kingfisher, Plaut.

units.la: Halitus] Spiritus, Animam continere, Cic.
units.tr: Breath] Breath; spirit. To hold back the breath, Cic.

units.la: Halo] Corona circa sidera, Sen. Circulus circa sidera, Plin. Area, Bud.
units.tr: Halo] A crown around the stars, Sen. A circle around the stars, Plin. Area, Bud.

units.la: Hara] Suile. Vivarium suum, Plin.
units.tr: Pigsty] Pig-yard. Their own piggery, Plin.

units.la: Harmonia, vid. Melodia.
units.tr: Harmony, see Melody.

units.la: Hasta] Cuspis, Ovid. Falarica, seu Phalarica, Liv.
units.tr: Spear] A point, Ovid. A falarica or phalarica, Liv.

units.la: Hastatus] Phalanx (equites hastati sunt.) Antesignani. Postsignani, Lipf. Contarius, Capit. Contophorus, Rhod.
units.tr: Spearman] Phalanx (the cavalry are hastati). Front-line soldiers. Rear-line soldiers, Lipsius. Pikeman, Capit. Lancer, Rhod.

units.la: Haud, vid. Non.
units.tr: Haud, see Non.

units.la: Haurire] Antlare, Fest.
units.tr: To bale out] To draw up with a ladle, Fest.

units.la: Haustim bibere] Dustim bibere, Plaut. Uno impetu, Plin. Uno spiritu poculum immane exhaurire, Cic. Amystide bibere. Trahere poculum, Hor. Raptim & sine interspiratione potare, Plin. Uno haustu, duƈtu, poculum evacuare. Vini poculum continuo produxit haustu, id est, eduxit. Grandissimum calicem uno haustu perhausi, Apul.
units.tr: To drink in gulps] To drink in gulps, Plaut. At one rush, Plin. To drain a huge cup in one breath, Cic. To drink amystis-fashion. To drag the cup, Hor. To drink hastily and without pausing for breath, Plin. To empty a cup at one draught. He drew off a cup of wine in one continuous draught. I drank off a very large cup in one draught, Apul.

units.la: Hebes] Obtusus vomer. Obtusa acies, Virg. Plumbeus, Cic. Præpilatus, Plin. Hebetatus, Suet. Retusa securis, Plaut. Obesæ naris, Horat.
units.tr: Blunt] A blunted ploughshare. A blunt edge, Virg. Leaden, Cic. Without a point, Plin. Dulled, Suet. A blunt axe, Plaut. Of a flat nose, Hor.

units.la: Hebescere] Hebescere, Liv. Hebetetscere, Plin. Stupescere, Hor.
units.tr: To grow dull] To grow dull, Liv. To grow blunt, Plin. To become stupefied, Hor.

units.la: Hebetare] Retundere. Perstringere aciem, Cic. Refringere. Obtundere, Plin.
units.tr: To blunt] To beat back. To dull an edge, Cic. To break off. To make blunt, Plin.

units.la: Hebetudo] Hebetatio, Plin.
units.tr: Bluntness] A blunting, Plin.

units.la: Heluari] Bacchari. Bacchanalia vivere, Iuv. vid.
units.tr: To revel] To live riotously. To live Bacchanalian lives, Juv. See.

units.la: Heluamini] Bibite. Pergræcamini, Effercite vos. Sagi-nam cudite. Dies noƈtesque bibite. Pascite parasitos. Obso-nate pollucibiliter. Estur, bibiturque semper, neque quis-quam parsimoniam adhibet. Sagina plane hic est, Plaut.
units.tr: Revel away] Drink. Carouse like the Greeks. Work yourselves into a frenzy. Beat out a sausage-stuffing. Drink day and night. Feed the parasites. Feast sumptuously. People eat and drink without ceasing, and no one practises thrift. This is plainly a fattening-place, Plaut.

units.la: Heluo] Decoƈtor, Cic. Sen. Gurges & vorago patrimonii. Naufragus patrimonio, Cic. Obliguritor, Firm. Degula-tor, Apul. Vappa, Hor. In ventrem illi correpserunt ædes. Omnia comedit, quod fuit, quod non fuit, Plaut. Sumit, consumit, perdit. Imò age ut lubet, ede, bibe, disperde rem, &c. Id.
units.tr: Glutton] A spendthrift, Cic. Sen. A whirlpool and gulf of one's inheritance. Shipwrecked on his patrimony, Cic. A licker of dishes, Firm. A squanderer, Apul. A sot, Hor. His house crept into his belly. He ate up everything that was and everything that was not, Plaut. He takes, consumes, loses. Come, do as you please: eat, drink, squander the property, etc., Id.

units.la: Hem] Ehem! Hui! Papæ! Vah consilium callidum, Ter. Atat! Euge. Eugepæ! Viden? Ecceve, Plaut.
units.tr: Hem] Ehem! Hui! Bravo! Vah, a clever plan, Ter. Aha! Well done! Bravo! Do you see? Look there, Plaut.

units.la: Hepar] Jecur, Plaut. Venarum radix, & sanguinis thesaurus, Hipp. Sedes amoris, Plato.
units.tr: Liver] Liver, Plaut. The root of the veins and the storehouse of the blood, Hipp. The seat of love, Plato.

units.la: Hepaticus] Jecinorosus, Scribon.
units.tr: Hepatic] Full of liver, Scribon.

units.la: Hera, vid. Domina.
units.tr: Hera, see Mistress.

units.la: Heraclius lapis, vid. Coticula.
units.tr: Heraclean stone, see Whetstone.

units.la: Herbidus] Herbosus. Herbifer mons, Ovid.
units.tr: Grassy] Full of grass. A grass-bearing mountain, Ovid.

units.la: Hereditas] Familiam primus habeto. Hereditas commissa. Obvenientia. Applicatio, vel, jus applicationis, Cic. Diatheca, Mart. Obventio, Vlp.
units.tr: Inheritance] Let him first have his household. An entrusted inheritance. Things falling to one. Application, or the right of application, Cic. A will, Mart. A coming into property, Ulp.

units.la: Heredem facere] Scribere, constituere, relinquere testamento mento aliquem hæredem. Vocare in partem hæreditatis, Cic.
units.tr: To make someone heir] To write, appoint or leave someone as heir in one's will. To call someone to a share of the inheritance, Cic.

units.la: Heredipeta] Captator, Iuv. Vultur, Sen.
units.tr: Legacy-hunter] A fortune-hunter, Juv. A vulture, Sen.

units.la: Hereditarie] Hereditario jure.
units.tr: By inheritance] By hereditary right.

units.la: Heri] Hesterno die, Catul. Hesternâ luce, Ovid. Hesternò, Lipf.
units.tr: Yesterday] On the previous day, Catull. In yesterday's light, Ovid. Yesterday, Lipsius.

units.la: Heri filius] Filius familias, Cic. Herilis filius, Ter. Herus minor, Plaut.
units.tr: Son of the house] A son under the authority of his father, Cic. The master's son, Ter. The younger master, Plaut.

units.la: Hermaphroditus] Ambigui generis homo. Androgynus. Hermathena, Cic. Infans incertus, masculus an fœmina esset, Liv. Ambiguus: modò vir, modò fœmina, Ovid. Diphyis, Plin.
units.tr: Hermaphrodite] A person of ambiguous sex. Androgyne. Hermathena, Cic. A child uncertain whether it was male or female, Liv. Ambiguous: now man, now woman, Ovid. Diphyes, Plin.

units.la: Hernia] Enterocela, Celf. Hydrocela, Mart. Ramex, Plin.
units.tr: Hernia] Enterocele, Cels. Hydrocele, Mart. Ramex, Plin.

units.la: Herniosus] Enterocelicus. Ramicosus. Hydrocelicus, Plin.
units.tr: Herniated] Suffering from enterocele. Ramicose. Suffering from hydrocele, Plin.

units.la: Heroina] Herois, Mart.
units.tr: Heroine] A heroine, Mart.

units.la: Heroicus] Heroicæ personæ. Herous, Cic.
units.tr: Heroic] Heroic characters. A hero, Cic.

units.la: Herpes, vid. Hulcus.
units.tr: Herpes, see Ulcer.

units.la: Herus] Paterfamilias. Dominus in suis ædibus. Dominus in suos, Cic. Paterfamiliæ, Mart. Pater domus, Hor. Herus major, Plaut. Vid. Dominus.
units.tr: Master] Father of the family. Master in his own house. Master over his household, Cic. Head of the household, Mart. Head of the house, Hor. Senior master, Plaut. See Lord.

units.la: Hesperus] Vesper, Catul. Vesperugo, Plaut. Venus. Stella veneris, Cic. Noctiluca Venus, Catul.
units.tr: Hesperus] Evening star, Catull. Vesperugo, Plaut. Venus. The star of Venus, Cic. Night-shining Venus, Catull.

units.la: Heu mihi] Hei misero mihi. Me miserum, Ter. Heu mihi, nequeo, quin fleam, Plaut. Rem miseram, Cic. Infandum! Virg. Proh dolor, Liv. O meum malum grave! Heu infortunium meum! Heu heu! Plaut.
units.tr: Alas for me] Alas, wretched me. Wretched me, Ter. Alas, I cannot help weeping, Plaut. A wretched affair, Cic. Unspeakable! Virg. Alas! Liv. O my grievous ill! Alas, my misfortune! Alas, alas! Plaut.

units.la: Heus] Heus tu. Heus adolescens. Ecquid audis? Ecquid attendis? Cic. Audin? Eho. Eho tu. Tibi ego dicam annon? Ter.
units.tr: Hey] Hey you. Hey, young man. Do you hear? Are you paying attention? Cic. Do you hear? Hey. Hey you. Am I not speaking to you? Ter.

units.la: Hiare] Hiscere, Plaut. Hiascere, Cato. Oscitare folia, Plin. Inhiare. Rimas agere, Cic. Segmina fiunt in pariete, Vitruv. Rimis fatiscere, Virg. Vitium facit domus, Cic. Rimosa fiunt tectoria, Vitr. Scindunt se, Cato.
units.tr: To gape] To open the mouth, Plaut. To gape open, Cato. Leaves gape, Plin. To gape wide. To make cracks, Cic. Seams form in the wall, Vitruv. To split with crevices, Virg. The house develops a fault, Cic. Plaster becomes cracked, Vitr. They split apart, Cato.

units.la: Hiatus] Derupta hiatuum vorago ac præcipitium.
units.tr: Gap] A steep, broken chasm and a precipice of gaping abysses.

units.la: Hiberna] Hibernacula, Liv. Hiemalia, Vopisc.
units.tr: Winter quarters] Winter quarters, Liv. Wintry places, Vopisc.

units.la: Hibernare] Hiemare. Tolerare hyemem, Cic. Agere hiemem sub tectis, Liv. Perhyemare, Col.
units.tr: To winter] To spend the winter. To endure the winter, Cic. To spend the winter under cover, Liv. To winter through, Col.

units.la: Hic, hæc, hoc] Hoc morbi. Hoc hominis, pro, hic homo, Ter. Hoc literarum. Hic iste. Hic ille, Cic. Is, iste, isthic, isthæc, isthoc, Ter. Hoc genus, Varr. Id genus, Col.
units.tr: This, this, this] This of disease. This man, for "hic homo", Ter. This of letters. This one here. That famous one, Cic. That one, this one, that one there, Ter. This kind, Varr. That kind, Col.

units.la: Hiemalis] Brumalis dies. Hibernus mensis, Cic.
units.tr: Wintry] A winter day. A winter month, Cic.

units.la: Hieme] Per hiemem navigare, Cic. Hiberno, Venul. ICt.
units.tr: In winter] To sail in winter, Cic. In winter, Venul. ICt.

units.la: Hiems] Hiemes, Caf. Bruma, & brumis, plur. Cic. Terræ requies.
units.tr: Winter] Winters, Caes. Winter, and winters (plural), Cic. The rest of the earth.

units.la: Hiemsest] Hiemat. Fidicula exoritur. Hiemat & pluit. Hiemat tempus, Plin.
units.tr: It is winter] It is wintering. The little lyre rises. It is wintry and it rains. The season is wintry, Plin.

units.la: Hieme finitâ] Sub hiemem statim. Hirundine primâ, Hor. Abruma sata, quadragesimo die vix exsistunt, Plin. Hieme extremâ. Senescente, Cic.
units.tr: When winter is over] Straight after winter. At the first swallow, Hor. Crops sown late in winter scarcely come up before the fortieth day, Plin. At the very end of winter. As it wanes, Cic.

units.la: Hieroglyphica] Ægyptiæ literæ, sculpturæ, Effigies, Apul. Ignorabiles literæ, Lucr. Primi Ægyptii per figuras animalium sensus mentis effingebant, Tacit. Emblemata.
units.tr: Hieroglyphics] Egyptian letters, carvings, images, Apul. Unknown letters, Lucr. The first Egyptians expressed the meanings of the mind through figures of animals, Tac. Emblems.

units.la: Hilaris] Hilaritate plenus. Hilarulus. Hilarula, Cic. Festus, Quint. Defæcatus animus, Macrob. Liquido animo, Plaut. Lubens, Ter. Remissus, Sen. Frons erugata, exporrecta. Hilarus homo, Ter.
units.tr: Cheerful] Full of cheerfulness. Light-hearted, Cic. Festive, Quint. A purified mind, Macrob. With a clear mind, Plaut. Willing, Ter. Relaxed, Sen. A brow smoothed and unwrinkled. A cheerful man, Ter.

units.la: Hilarem esse] Proferre gaudia oculis, Plin. Diffundere vultum, Ovid. Explicare frontem. Demere nubem supercilio, Hor. Laxare animum. Sustuli animum, Exporrigere frontem, Cic. Soluto liberoque animo esse.
units.tr: To be cheerful: to bring joy to the eyes (Pliny). To spread joy over the face (Ovid). To smooth the brow. To remove the cloud from the eyebrow (Horace). To relax the mind. To lift up the spirit, to unfold the brow (Cicero). To be free and unburdened in mind.

units.la: Hilaritas] Hilaritudo, Cic. Lubentia, Plaut. Jucunditas vitæ. Festivitas sermonis, Cic. Vid. Jucunditas.
units.tr: Cheerfulness: cheerfulness of spirit (Cicero); willingness (Plautus); enjoyment of life; gaiety of speech (Cicero). See Pleasantness.

units.la: Hilariter] Hilarius. Remissè tractare res tristes. Hilarem in modum. Hilari atque læto vultu. Jucundè vivere cum remissis, Cic. Hilarissimè. Hilaritus. Porrectiore fronte, Plaut. Læte, Quint. Lætanter, Lamp. Amplissimè habitare, Plin. Iun. Laxatis curis. Hilarè, Cic.
units.tr: Cheerfully: cheerfully (Hilarius). To treat sad matters lightly. In a cheerful manner. With a cheerful and happy face. To live pleasantly with easy-going people (Cicero). Most cheerfully. Hilaritus. With a more open brow (Plautus). Gladly (Quintilian). Joyfully (Lampridius). To live most splendidly (Pliny the Younger). With cares laid aside. Cheerfully (Cicero).

units.la: Hinc] Inde est quòd, Plin. Iun. Aufer abhinc lacrymas, Lucr.
units.tr: Hence: it is for this reason that (Pliny the Younger). Take tears away from here (Lucretius).

units.la: Hinc inde, vid. Sparsim. Vndique.
units.tr: Hence and thence: see Scattered. From every side.

units.la: Hinnire] Hinnilitare, Lucil.
units.tr: To neigh: to whinny (Lucilius).

units.la: Hinnitus] Fremitus equorum, Virg. Sonus equi, Propert.
units.tr: Neighing: the neighing of horses (Virgil). The sound of a horse (Propertius).

units.la: Hircus] Vir gregis. Caper. Dux & maritus pecoris. Vir capellarum, Mart.
units.tr: He-goat: the man of the flock; a goat; the leader and husband of the herd; the man of the she-goats (Martial).

units.la: Hirsutus] Villosus. Vestitissimum pecus. Lanatus, Col. Hispidus. Lanuginosus, Plin. Hispidosus, Capitol. Vibratus, Plin. Pilosus. Capillatus. Horridus, Cic. Comans. Comatus, Mart. Caesariatus, Plaut. Urso hispidior, Er. Rusco horridior, Er.
units.tr: Shaggy: hairy; the most thickly clothed flock; woolly (Columella); bristly; downy (Pliny); fluffy (Pliny); bushy (Capitolinus); shaggy (Pliny); hairy; bristling (Cicero); long-haired; hairy (Martial); curly-haired (Plautus); more bristly than a bear (Erasmus); bristlier than butcher's broom (Erasmus).

units.la: Hirudo] Sanguisuga. Alabeta & Alabetes, Plin.
units.tr: Leech: a bloodsucker. Alabeta and alabetes (Pliny).

units.la: Hirundo] Avis hospita, Var. Avis exul hiemis.
units.tr: Swallow: a foreign bird (Varro); a bird exiled from winter.

units.la: Historia] Monimenta antiquitatis, rerum gestarum; annalium, Cic. Gesta, Tac. Acta, Luv. Speculum prudentiae. Magistra vitae, Cic.
units.tr: History: records of antiquity and of deeds done; annals (Cicero); deeds (Tacitus); acts (Juvenal); a mirror of prudence; the teacher of life (Cicero).

units.la: Histrio] Ludius. Mimus. Ethologus, Cic. Scenicus jocu-lator. Mimologus. Orchestopalarius, Firm. Chironomus. Pantomimus, Bud. Gesticulator, Col. Gesticularis puer, Amm. Scenicus. Thymelicus, Vitruv. Ventilator, & Pilarius, Quint. Ludio, Liv.
units.tr: Actor: a player; a mime; a mimic (Cicero); a stage jester; a mimologus; a dancing mime (Firmicus); a chironomus; a pantomime (Budaeus); a gesticulator (Columella); a boy who gesticulates (Ammianus); a stage performer; a thymelicus (Vitruvius); a ventilator and a pilarius (Quintilian); a ludio (Livy).

units.la: Histrionalis] Mimicus, Cic. Pantomimicus, Sen. Ludicer, Plaut. Ludius, Catul. Ludianus, Varr.
units.tr: Theatrical: mimic (Cicero); pantomimic (Seneca); playful (Plautus); of the stage (Catullus); of actors (Varro).

units.la: Histrionica] Histrionia, Plaut. Histrionale studium, Tac. Ars histrionum, Cic. Ars ludicra, Plaut.
units.tr: The acting profession: the art of acting (Plautus); the study of acting (Tacitus); the art of actors (Cicero); the theatrical art (Plautus).

units.la: Hoc ad me non pertinet] Mihi isthic nec scritur, nec metitur.
units.tr: That does not concern me: that is neither sown nor reaped by me.

units.la: Hoc est] Id est, Cic. Quod dico tale est, Sen. Quod est, Fest. Hoc illud est, quod dicitur, Catul.
units.tr: That is: that is (Cicero). What I say is this (Seneca). What is (Festus). This is that which is said (Catullus).

units.la: Hodie] Hodiernè, Tibul.
units.tr: Today: today; of today (Tibullus).

units.la: Hodieque] In hunc diem, Plaut.
units.tr: And today: up to this day (Plautus).

units.la: Homicida] Parricida civium. Percussor. Thrax, Interfector, Cic. Cui hominum mors omnis in usu est, Lucan. Patrator necis, Tac. Necator hominum, Macr. Interemptor. Maestator senum, Sen. Sicarius, Cic.
units.tr: Murderer: a murderer of citizens; a killer; a cutthroat, a slayer (Cicero); one for whom the death of men is everyday business (Lucan); the perpetrator of a killing (Tacitus); a killer of men (Macrobius); a destroyer; a slayer of the aged (Seneca); an assassin (Cicero).

units.la: Homicidium] Multorum civium neces. Parricidium civis, fratris, Reipub. Cic. Internecidium, Isidor.
units.tr: Murder: the killing of many citizens; the murder of a citizen, a brother, or of the commonwealth (Cicero); mutual slaughter (Isidore).

units.la: Homicidium patrare] Parricidam esse. Reum esse homicidii. Nefario se alicujus parricidio obstringere, Cic.
units.tr: To commit murder: to be a murderer; to be guilty of homicide; to bind oneself by a wicked murder of someone (Cicero).

units.la: Homo] Caput, Cic. Persona, Plin. Anima, Tac. Microcosmus, Sipont. Mortalis, Plaut. Animal divinum. Ambulatilis planta. Coadjutor Dei. Collusor Dei. Dei ludibrium. Dominus creaturarum. Imago Dei.
units.tr: Man: a head (Cicero); a person (Pliny); a breath of life (Tacitus); a microcosm (Sipontinus); a mortal (Plautus); a divine animal; a walking plant; a co-worker of God; a playmate of God; the plaything of God; the lord of creatures; the image of God.

units.la: Homines] Genus humanum, vel, hominum, Cic. Mortales, Plin. Capita, Nomina, Sen. Animæ, Hor. Mentes albas, vocat Lipf. homines simplices.
units.tr: Men: the human race, or men (Cicero); mortals (Pliny); heads, persons (Seneca); souls (Horace); white minds, as Lipsius calls them; simple men.

units.la: Homines sibi invicem humanitatem debent] Homo sacra res homini. Homo homini Deus.
units.tr: Men owe one another humanity: man is a sacred thing to man; man is a god to man.

units.la: Hominis vita] Concatenatio laborum.
units.tr: Human life: a chain of toils.

units.la: Honestas] Honestum. Dignitas. Ingenuitas, Cic. Respectus honesti, Lucan. Honorificentia, Capitol. Honor verborum, Quint. Majestas loci, Liv. Rectum trahat ad amicitias, Hor.
units.tr: Honourableness: the honourable; dignity; good birth (Cicero); regard for what is honourable (Lucan); honouring (Capitolinus); the honour of words (Quintilian); the majesty of a place (Livy); let what is right draw friendships (Horace).

units.la: Honeste] Ingenuè educatus, Liberaliter, Cic. Venerabundè templum ingressi, Liv. Pudicè actum ævum, Ovid. Pudicius. Reverenter, Plin. Iun. Reverentissimè, Suet. Dignanter audire loquentem, Vopisc.
units.tr: Honourably: brought up nobly, liberally (Cicero); entering the temple with reverence (Livy); a life spent chastely (Ovid); more chastely; reverently (Pliny the Younger); most reverently (Suetonius); to listen to a speaker with courtesy (Vopiscus).

units.la: Honestus] Honoratus. Honorabilis vir, spectatus vir, Cicer. Venerabilis vir, Plin. Veneranda effigies, Val. Argon. Reverendus, Claud. Speciosus, Hor. Pudicus thalamus, Ovid.
units.tr: Honourable: honoured; an honourable man, a distinguished man (Cicero); a venerable man (Pliny); a venerable image (Valerius Flaccus); reverend (Claudian); splendid (Horace); a chaste bedchamber (Ovid).

units.la: Honor] Dignitas, Cicer. Titulus, Ovid. Dignatio, Suet. Amplitudo, Cic. Majestas, Fest. Honos, Cic. Decus, Id.
units.tr: Honour: dignity (Cicero); title (Ovid); distinction (Suetonius); greatness (Cicero); majesty (Festus); honour (Cicero); ornament (Id.).

units.la: Honos onus] Corona fulgidum ærumnarum auctoramentum. Fasces sunt fasces.
units.tr: Honour is a burden: a shining crown, the reward of hardships. The fasces are fasces.

units.la: Ad honores provehi] Ascendere in Capitolium, Adscendere ad honores, in honorem. Capessere honorem senatorium, Tacit. In altissimo dignitatis locari gradu. In sedem honoris ascendere. Provenire ad dignitatem. Procedere honoribus. Honoribus decorari, Cic. In dignationem pervenire, Liv.
units.tr: To be promoted to honours: to climb to the Capitol; to rise to honours, to office. To assume the senatorial honour (Tacitus). To be placed on the highest step of dignity. To mount to the seat of honour. To come forward to dignity. To advance through honours. To be adorned with honours (Cicero). To attain dignity (Livy).

units.la: Honores affectare] Inservire honoribus, Cic. Laborare in famam, Sen. Deservire honoribus, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: To aspire to honours: to serve honours (Cicero); to strive for fame (Seneca); to devote oneself to honours (Pliny the Younger).

units.la: Honorum exspectans] Candidatus, Officiosissima candidatorum natio. Tribunitius. Candidatorium munus, Cic. Candidâ veste indutus, Hor.
units.tr: One awaiting office: a candidate; the most obsequious nation of candidates; of the tribunes. The duty of a candidate (Cicero); dressed in the white robe (Horace).

units.la: Honoris causa multa fiunt] Honos alit artes. Honos virtutis alimentum, Val. M.
units.tr: Many things are done for the sake of honour: honour nourishes the arts; honour is the nourishment of virtue (Valerius Maximus).

units.la: Honore dignus] Venerandus. Venerabilis, Augustus, Serv. Vid. Honestus.
units.tr: Worthy of honour: venerable; venerable, august (Servius). See Honest.

units.la: Honorare] Afficere, ornare honore, honoribus. Facere, augere, deferre, dare, præstare, habere alicui honorem. Habere in honore. Perhibere honorem. Dignare aliquem, & dignari. Colere, observare, venerari hominem; observantiâ colere. Cohonestare. Mactare honore, Cic. Veneratione prosequi, Paterc.
units.tr: To honour: to grant honour or honours to someone; to do, increase, confer, give, render, or have honour for someone; to hold in honour; to pay honour; to deem someone worthy, and to deign; to cherish, observe, or revere a man, cherishing him with regard; to grace; to honour with honour (Cicero); to pay veneration (Paterculus).

units.la: Honorarium] Honor. Honoris aliquid habere alicui, Cic. Lautia, pl. Liv. Dautia, quæ dabantur Legatis, Scal. Xenia, Plin. Voluntarium munus.
units.tr: Honorarium: honour; to give someone something as an honour (Cicero); the lautia (Livy); the dautia, given to envoys (Scaliger); gifts (Pliny); a voluntary gift.

units.la: Hora] Horarium spatium, Suet.
units.tr: Hour: a space of hours (Suetonius).

units.la: Hordeaceus] Hordearius, Fest.
units.tr: Barley-like: of barley (Festus).

units.la: Hordeum] Molâ mactatus porcus, i.e. hordeo auctus, Scal.
units.tr: Barley: a pig sacrificed with meal, that is, fattened with barley (Scaliger).

units.la: Horizon] Finiens, Cic. Finitor, Sen. Cortina cœli corporei cærulea, Enn. Concha cærulea, Hemisphærium superius, Varr.
units.tr: Horizon: the boundary (Cicero); the limiter (Seneca); the blue vault of the corporeal heaven (Ennius); the blue shell, the upper hemisphere (Varro).

units.la: Horrendè] Formidolosè, Cic. Monstrificè, Plin. Ferale gemiscunt, Claud.
units.tr: Dreadfully: fearfully (Cicero); monstrously (Pliny); they groan mournfully (Claudian).

units.la: Horrendus] Truculentus, & terribilis aspectu. Metuendus. Formidolosus. Horridus, Cic. Perhorridus, Lucil. Tristis ad recordationem, Id.
units.tr: Dreadful: fierce and terrible to behold; to be feared; fearful; horrible (Cicero); very horrible (Lucilius); sad to recall (Id.).

units.la: Horrescere] Cohorrere. Perhorrescere toto corpore, omnibus artubus. Contremiscere corpore. Exhorrescere vultum alicujus. Exhorrescere metu. Exiguntur capilli, Cic. Inhorrescere, Plin. Perterritus contremui. Perfudit me horror. Cic. Membra reformidant, Ovid. Arrigitur coma, Virg. Horrent capilli, Tibul. Erectus horret crinis, Sen. Rigent coma, Ovid.
units.tr: To shudder: to shiver; to shudder over the whole body, in every limb; to tremble in body; to shrink from someone's face; to shudder with fear. The hair stands on end (Cicero); to bristle (Pliny); I trembled, terrified; horror came over me (Cicero); the limbs shrink (Ovid); the hair stands up (Virgil); the hair bristles (Tibullus); the erect hair stands on end (Seneca); the hair stiffens (Ovid).

units.la: Horribile aliquid] Horribile dictu videtur. Dii immortales, quis me horror perfudit? Quod nemo unquam aspicere non horruit, Cic. Horrendum dictu. Horresco referens. Animus meminisse horret. Mihi frigidus horror membra quatit, Virg. Horreo postquam aspexi, Ter. Insanum quantum, Plaut. Immane quantum exarsere animi. Immane dictu, Sallust.
units.tr: Something horrible: it seems horrible to tell. Immortal gods, what horror has come over me? Which no one ever looked upon without shuddering (Cicero). Dreadful to tell. I shudder to speak of it. The mind shrinks from remembering. A cold horror shakes my limbs (Virgil). I shudder since I saw him (Terence). How insanely (Plautus). How monstrously their minds blazed up. Monstrous to tell (Sallust).

units.la: Horridus, vid. Hirsutus. Rudis.
units.tr: Bristly: see Hairy; Rough.

units.la: Hortari] Admonere, Cic. Exhortari, Adhortari, Cic. Monere, Ter. Vid. Adhortari.
units.tr: To urge: to admonish (Cicero); to exhort, to encourage (Cicero); to warn (Terence). See To Exhort.

units.la: Hortulanus] Olitor, Varr. Cultor virentis agelli, Hor. Lachanopola. Olerum venditor.
units.tr: Gardener: a gardener (Varro); a tiller of a green little field (Horace); a vegetable grower; a seller of greens.

units.la: Hortus] Hortulus, Plin. Virens agellus, Hor. Hortum agricolae succidiam alteram appellant, Plin. Alterum macellum. Successio necessaria, Non.
units.tr: Garden: a little garden (Pliny); a green little field (Horace); farmers call a garden the second pork-larder (Pliny); another market; a necessary succession (Nonius).

units.la: Hortus amœnus] Adonidis horti. Item, Alcinoi horti.
units.tr: Pleasant garden: the gardens of Adonis; likewise, the gardens of Alcinous.

units.la: Hospes activus] Stabularius, Apul. Diversitor, Petron.
units.tr: A host who is active: a stable-keeper (Apuleius); an innkeeper (Petronius).

units.la: Hospes passivus] Diversor, Cic. Interventor, Id. Adventor, Plaut. Diversitor, Petron.
units.tr: A guest who is passive: a lodger (Cicero); an intervener (Id.); a visitor (Plautus); a lodger (Petronius).

units.la: Hospes non invitatus] Umbra, translatè Hor. Locus est & pluribus umbris.
units.tr: An uninvited guest: a shadow, figuratively (Horace). There is room for even more shadows.

units.la: Hospes caute agat] Domi alienæ surdus & mutus esto.
units.tr: Let a guest behave with caution: be deaf and dumb in another's house.

units.la: Hospitalis homo] Homo hospitalissimus & amicissimus nostrorum hominum, Cic. Perhospitalis, Id.
units.tr: A hospitable man: a most hospitable and most friendly man of our people (Cicero); very hospitable (Id.).

units.la: Hospitalis (2) id est, ad hospites pertinens] Diversorius, Plaut. Adventorius, Mart. Metatoria epistola, Sidon. Scal.
units.tr: Hospitable (2), that is, pertaining to guests: pertaining to lodging (Plautus); pertaining to arrivals (Martial); a letter of introduction (Sidonius, Scaliger).

units.la: Hospitalitas] Hospitio amicitiaque conjungi. Hospitii jus, necessitudo, Cic. Contesseratio hospitalitatis, Tertul. Hospitalis amicitia.
units.tr: Hospitality: to be joined by hospitality and friendship; the right of hospitality, a bond (Cicero); the mutual sealing of hospitality (Tertullian); friendship of hospitality.

units.la: Hospitari alicubi] Hospitium est mihi cum eo. Hospes meus est. Feci cum illo hospitium, Cic. Hospitor apud aliquem, in aliquo loco, vel, Hospitari soleo, ex Sen. Hospitalis mihi tessera cum illo est, Plaut. Diversari apud aliquem. Accipi ab aliquo hospitio. Divertere ad aliquem in hospitium, Cic. Divertere apud aliquem, Liv.
units.tr: To lodge somewhere: I have a hospitable bond with him; he is my host. I made a bond of hospitality with him (Cicero). I lodge with someone, in some place, or, I am accustomed to be a guest, from Seneca. The token of hospitality is between me and him (Plautus). To lodge with someone. To be received as a guest by someone. To turn aside to someone as a guest (Cicero). To lodge with someone (Livy).

units.la: Hospitium] Diversorium. Diversorium, Taberna, Cic. Hospitiolum, Vlp. Hospitale, Vitr. Hospitium, Plaut. Vlp. Diverticulum, Liv.
units.tr: Lodging: a lodging-house. An inn, a tavern (Cicero); a small lodging (Ulpian); a guest-house (Vitruvius); lodging (Plautus, Ulpian); a side-lodging (Livy).

units.la: Hostia] Victima, i. hostia post victo Libamen, Cic. Virg. Piaculum, Hor.
units.tr: Victim: a victim, that is, a sacrifice after it has been slain; a libation (Cicero, Virgil); an atoning sacrifice (Horace).

units.la: Hostilis, vid. Inimicus.
units.tr: Hostile: see Unfriendly.

units.la: Hostiliter] Hostilem in modum, Cic. Per hosticum venire, Spart.
units.tr: In a hostile manner: in the manner of an enemy (Cicero); to come through enemy territory (Spartianus).

units.la: Hostis] Hostili animo adversus Remp. animatus, Vlp. Hostis capitalis alicujus. Apertus inimicus. Qui alicui inimicitias micitias denunciant, Cic. Professus inimicum alicui. Qui sanguinarium nuncium alicui misit, Plin.
units.tr: Enemy: animated with a hostile mind against the commonwealth (Ulpian); the mortal enemy of someone; an open enemy; those who declare enmity against someone (Cicero); one who has professed himself someone's enemy; one who sent a bloody message to someone (Pliny).

units.la: Hostilitas] Inimicitiæ, Cic. Ter. Inimicitia, Id.
units.tr: Hostility: enmities (Cicero, Terence); enmity (Id.).

units.la: Hostilitatem denunciare, vid. Denunciare.
units.tr: To declare hostility: see Declare.

units.la: Hostem habere domi] Anguem, colubrum in sinu fovere.
units.tr: To have an enemy at home: to nurse a snake, to cherish a viper in one's bosom.

units.la: Hostium interitus gratus] Luporum interitus ovium salus.
units.tr: The death of enemies is welcome: the death of wolves is the safety of sheep.

units.la: Huc] Huc locorum; huc vicinię. Horsum pergunt, Ter.
units.tr: Hither: hither of place; hither of nearness. They are going this way (Terence).

units.la: Huc & illuc] Huc illuc, Tac. Huc & huc, Hor. Rursus proꝛsus, Varr. Sursum deorsum, Ter. Diversè, Id. Ultro citróque. Vagè, Cic. Ultra citráque, Plin. Hac illac, Ter. Discursim, Macrob. Sparsim. Rapit huc, rapit impetus illuc, Stat.
units.tr: Hither and thither] Hither and thither, Tac. Here and here, Hor. Forward and forth, Varr. Up and down, Ter. In different directions, Id. Back and forth. Wanderingly, Cic. Beyond and on this side, Plin. This way and that, Ter. Running in all directions, Macrob. Scattered here and there. Impulse drags him here, impulse drags him there, Stat.

units.la: Huc usque] Eatenus. Adhuc. Usque eò, Plaut. Ad id locorum, Sal. Adusque, Virg. Vid. Hactenus.
units.tr: Up to here] Thus far. Up to now. Right up to that point, Plaut. To that place, Sal. Right up to, Virg. See Hitherto.

units.la: Hulcerosus] Hulceribus plurimis obsitus, Sen. Pulmoneus, Plaut.
units.tr: Ulcerous] Covered with very many ulcers, Sen. Diseased in the lungs, Plaut.

units.la: Hulcus] Suppuratum. Colleƈtio, Plin. Vomica, Cic. Petimen, Lucil. Petumen, Gloss.
units.tr: Ulcer] Suppurated matter. A collection (of pus), Plin. A boil, Cic. Petimen, Lucil. Petumen, Gloss.

units.la: Hulcus serpens] Herpes, Gorr. Zona, Scribon.
units.tr: Creeping ulcer] Herpes, Gorr. Zona (shingles), Scribon.

units.la: Humanè] Humaniter. Comiter monstrare viam erranti. Officiosè, Cic. Hospitaliter invitati per domos, Liv.
units.tr: Humanely] In a humane way. Courteously showing the way to a wanderer. Dutifully, Cic. Hospitably, as guests invited through houses, Liv.

units.la: Humanitas] Dexteritas quædam, benevolentiaque erga omnes homines promiscua, Gell.
units.tr: Humanity] A certain graciousness, and a benevolence towards all men alike, Gell.

units.la: Humanus] Humanissimus. Perhumanus. Humanitate perpolitus. Excultus ad humanitatem. Hospitalis. Comis. Percomis; habet comitatem, Cic. Comissimus, Suet. Plus humani est vulturio, (scil. quàm huic homini) Plaut. Ipsis Gratiis humanior. In Gratiarum hortis educatus. Gratiosa res homo est, si homo est.
units.tr: Humane] Most humane. Very humane. Refined by culture. Trained to humanity. Hospitable. Courteous. Very courteous; he has courtesy, Cic. Most courteous, Suet. A vulture has more humanity (namely than this man), Plaut. More humane than the Graces themselves. Brought up in the gardens of the Graces. A man is a pleasant thing, if he is a man.

units.la: Humanitus] Humano modo. More omnium, scil. hominum, Cic. More hominum, Ter. Humani ingenii more, Sal.
units.tr: Humanly] In a human manner. After the manner of all (men), Cic. After the manner of men, Ter. In the manner of human nature, Sal.

units.la: Humare]Tradere sepulturæ, Apul. Inferre mortuum, Vlp. Condere in sepulchro, Cic. Terram terræ reddere, Id. ex Eurip. Condere terrâ, monumento, Plin. Tumulare. Contumulare, Mart. Mandare humo, Virg. Componere tumulo, Ovid. Contegere tumulo, Liv. Sepelire, Cic. Editus terrâ terræ redditur. Inhumare, Plin.
units.tr: To bury] To give to burial, Apul. To carry in a dead body, Vlp. To lay in a tomb, Cic. To return earth to earth, Cic. from Eurip. To lay in the earth, in a monument, Plin. To entomb. To entomb again, Mart. To commit to the ground, Virg. To lay in a mound, Ovid. To cover with a grave-mound, Liv. To bury, Cic. Brought forth from earth, it is returned to earth. To inter, Plin.

units.la: Humatio, vid. Exsequiæ.
units.tr: Burial, see Funeral rites.

units.la: Humatus, vid. Sepulcrus.
units.tr: Buried, see Sepulchred.

units.la: Humectare] Humidare lavacro siccitatem, Vindician. Udare, Macrob.
units.tr: To moisten] To wet the dryness with a bath, Vindician. To soak, Macrob.

units.la: Humere]Humescere. Arbor humet lacrymis, Ovid. Uvescere, Lucr. Humificum succum ex aëre ducere, Cic. Madescere humore, Quint.
units.tr: To become damp] To become moist. A tree grows damp with tears, Ovid. To grow wet, Lucr. To draw moisture-bearing juice from the air, Cic. To become soaked with moisture, Quint.

units.la: Humidus] Humens, humidulus. Uvidus cœli status. Udus, Ovid. Humectus locus. Victus locus, Varr. Cat. Succosus, Col. Succidus homo, Plaut. Vaporifer, Stat. Vaporosus, Apul.
units.tr: Moist] Wet, slightly damp. Wet state of the sky. Dripping, Ovid. A damp place. A place of living, Varr. Cat. Juicy, Col. A juicy man, Plaut. Vapour-bearing, Stat. Vaporous, Apul.

units.la: Humiliare se] Submittere se in humilitatem, Liv. Cedere alicui. Abjicere se. Submissius se gerere. Remittere spiritus. Comprimere animos, Cic. Ponere superbiam, Hor. In planum deferre fortunam suam. Descendere in æquum, & detrahere pompam muneri. Detrahere superbiam rebus superbis, Sen. Demittere cristas. Exuere arrogantiam, Tac.
units.tr: To humble oneself] To submit oneself to humility, Liv. To yield to someone. To cast oneself down. To behave more submissively. To lower one's spirits. To curb one's spirit, Cic. To lay aside pride, Hor. To bring one's fortune down to the level. To come down to the level, and strip the show from the office. To strip pride from proud things, Sen. To lower one's crest. To cast off arrogance, Tac.

units.la: Humiliare aliquem] Redigere in sordidissimam turbam nobiles, Sen. In infimum agere, Apul. Traducere ad plebem. De cœlo aliquem detrahere. Diminuere capite. In ærarios referre. Conjicere in ordinem, Cic. Apul. In cæritum tabulas referre, Gell. Dejicere aliquem de suo statu. Movere senatu, tribu, Cic.
units.tr: To humble someone] To reduce nobles to the most wretched crowd, Sen. To drive into the lowest rank, Apul. To bring down to the common people. To pull someone down from heaven. To diminish someone's status. To enter in the treasury records. To put into the order, Cic. Apul. To enter in the censors' lists, Gell. To throw someone down from his position. To remove from senate or tribe, Cic.

units.la: Humiliatio actl.]Diminutio capitis. Traductio ad plebem, Cic.
units.tr: Humbling] Diminution of status. Transfer to the common people, Cic.

units.la: Humiliatus] Capitis minor, Hor.
units.tr: Humbled] Of diminished status, Hor.

units.la: Humiliora tutiora] Qui alta quærit, præcipitium quærit, quia plus habent ponderis ad ruinam, quæ sunt cæteris altiora. Rebus parvis alta quies, Sen. Procul à Jove, procul à fulmine. Qui jacet in terra, non habet unde cadat. Qui quærit alta, malum videtur quærere.
units.tr: Lower things are safer] He who seeks high things seeks a precipice, because those things that are higher than the rest carry more weight for the fall. Quiet in small things is a high thing, Sen. Far from Jove, far from the thunderbolt. He who lies on the ground has nowhere to fall from. He who seeks high things seems to seek harm.

units.la: Humilis] Supplex, Cic. Infimus, Liv.
units.tr: Humble] Suppliant, Cic. Lowest, Liv.

units.la: Humilitas] Submissio animi. Submissus animus. Despicientia sui. Demissio animi, Cic.
units.tr: Humility] Submission of mind. A submissive mind. Self-contempt. Lowering of spirit, Cic.

units.la: Humiliter] Demisse, submisse, submissius, Cic. Demississime & subjectissimè, Cæl. Velatis manibus, Plaut. Suppliciter respondere. Demisso atque humili animo, Cic.
units.tr: Humbly] Humbly, submissively, more submissively, Cic. Most humbly and most subjectly, Cael. With hands veiled, Plaut. To answer in a suppliant manner. With a humble and lowly spirit, Cic.

units.la: Humor] Uvor, Varr. Succus terræ. Exspiratio terræ, Cic. Halitus terræ, Plin. Humidum. Tac.
units.tr: Moisture] Wetness, Varr. Juice of the earth. Exhalation of the earth, Cic. Breath of the earth, Plin. Moisture, Tac.

units.la: Humus] Tellus, Virg. Tergum terræ, Lucr. Solum, Cic. Terrenum, Col.
units.tr: Ground] Earth, Virg. The back of the earth, Lucr. Soil, Cic. Earthly matter, Col.

units.la: Hungaria] Pannonia.
units.tr: Hungary] Pannonia.

units.la: Hungarus] Pannonius.
units.tr: Hungarian] Pannonian.

units.la: Hyacinthus herba] Purpureum. Vaccinium, Virg. Turneb.
units.tr: Hyacinth (plant)] Purple (flower). Bilberry, Virg. Turneb.

units.la: Hyacinthinus] Violaceus, Plin. Amethystinus, Id. Ferrugineus pileus, Plaut. Purpureus. Janthinus, Plin.
units.tr: Hyacinthine] Violet-coloured, Plin. Amethyst-coloured, Id. A rust-coloured cap, Plaut. Purple. Violet, Plin.

units.la: Hydrargyrum] Vomica liquoris æterni. Vid. Argentum vivum.
units.tr: Quicksilver] The vomit of the eternal liquid. See Quicksilver.

units.la: Hydrops] Hydropisis, Plin. Aqua intercus, Cic. Aquosus albo corpore languor, Hor. Tumor assurgens, Celf.
units.tr: Dropsy] Dropsy, Plin. Water in the belly, Cic. A watery languor with a pale body, Hor. A rising swelling, Cels.

units.la: Hydropicus] Veternosus cùm plurimum bibit, tum maximè sitit, Cato.
units.tr: Dropsical] A dropsical man, who, when he has drunk much, thirsts most of all, Cato.

units.la: Hypocaustum] Triclinium hybernum. Hybernaculum, Plin. Vaporarium, Cic. Hibernum cubiculum, Manut. Tepidarium, Vitruv.
units.tr: Hypocaust] A winter dining-room. A winter room, Plin. A steam room, Cic. A winter bedroom, Manut. A warm room, Vitruv.

units.la: Hypocrisis] Hypocriseos larva. Hic nigræ succus loliginis. Hæc mera ærugo est. Loligo, Hor. Simulatio, dissimulatio. Fallaci loquentia, Cic. Duplicitas animi, Lact. Alia dicunt, alia faciunt. Aliud in ore, aliud in corde. Aliud in titulo, aliud in pyxide.
units.tr: Hypocrisy] The mask of hypocrisy. Here is the juice of black cuttlefish. This is pure verdigris. Cuttlefish, Hor. Pretence, dissimulation. Deceitful speech, Cic. Duplicity of mind, Lact. They say one thing and do another. One thing in the mouth, another in the heart. One thing on the label, another in the box.

units.la: Hypocrita] Sub persona vivens. Personatus, Sen. Alienas observans papulas, ipse hulceribus obsitus, Id. Alieno in oculo festucam videns, in proprio trabem non animadvertit. In alienis vitiis oculatus, in propriis Thyresia cæcior. Apparere, quàm esse malunt. Colantes muscas & deglutientes camelos. Culicem colant. Hypocrita est histrio personatus. Personam mavult, quàm faciem, seil. perdere. Salutator est comis, sed virulentus obtrectator, Er.
units.tr: Hypocrite] Living under a mask. Masked, Sen. Watching others' spots, himself covered with ulcers, Id. Seeing a splinter in another's eye, he does not notice the beam in his own. Sharp-eyed in others' faults, blinder than Tiresias in his own. They prefer to seem rather than to be. Straining out gnats and swallowing camels. He strains out a gnat. A hypocrite is an actor in a mask. He would rather lose his mask than his face. He is a courteous greeter, but a venomous detractor, Erasm.

units.la: Hypocrita se fallit, non Deum] Deum fallere volenti multa scienda.
units.tr: The hypocrite deceives himself, not God] He who wants to deceive God must know many things.

units.la: Hypotheca, vid. Pignus.
units.tr: Pledge, see Pledge.

units.la: Hystrix] Herinaceus Æthiopicus, Sol. Herinaceus Indicus, & Africanus, Plin. Mus Africanus, Plaut.
units.tr: Porcupine] Ethiopian hedgehog, Sol. Indian and African hedgehog, Plin. African mouse, Plaut.

units.la: I.
units.tr: I.

units.la: in rem malam, vid. Abi.
units.tr: to the devil, see Away.

units.la: Ibi] Istic, Cic. Illic, Ter. Ibi loci, Plin. Illic ibi. Ini-bi, Plaut. Interibi, Gell.
units.tr: There] There, Cic. Yonder, Ter. There in that place, Plin. Right there, Plaut. Inibi, Plaut. Meanwhile there, Gell.

units.la: Icere, vid. Ferire.
units.tr: To strike, see To strike.

units.la: Icon, vid. Effigies.
units.tr: Image, see Likeness.

units.la: Ictericus] Arquatus, Celf. Arcuatum pecus, Col.
units.tr: Jaundiced] Jaundiced, Cels. Jaundiced cattle, Col.

units.la: Icterus] Morbus arquatus, Celf. Morbus regius. Bilis suf-fusio, Plin. Aurugo, Celf. Aurigo, Sipont. Morbus icteri-cus, Cæl. Rhod.
units.tr: Jaundice] Jaundice, Cels. The royal disease. Suffusion of bile, Plin. Aurugo, Cels. Aurigo, Sipont. Icteric disease, Caelius Rhod.

units.la: Ictus] Incussus, Tac. Illisus, Plin. Punctio. Verbera-tus, Id. Petitio. Percussio. Plaga venit vehementior. Im-petus, Cic. Impactio nubium, Sen. Pulsus, Virg.
units.tr: Blow] Struck, Tac. Dashed against, Plin. A pricking. Beaten, Id. An attack. A striking. A stronger blow arrives. Impetus, Cic. Impact of clouds, Sen. A push, Virg.

units.la: Id ago] In hoc sum. Totâ mente in curam aliquam in-cumbere. Hoc ago, Cic. Totus in hoc sum, Hor.
units.tr: I am doing this] I am set on this. To throw oneself wholly with the whole mind into some care. I do this, Cic. I am wholly set on this, Hor.

units.la: Id agitur] Hoc pugnatur. In eo cardo vertitur. Ea res in discrimen adducitur. De hac re certamen est. Hoc solùm pugno, Cic. In eo res vertitur. In eo spes civitatis verti-tur, Liv.
units.tr: The matter at stake] This is being fought over. On this the hinge turns. The matter is brought into danger. This is the subject of contest. I fight only this, Cic. On this the affair turns. On this turns the hope of the state, Liv.

units.la: Idea] Exemplar, Figura, Species, Deformatio operis, Vitr. Designatio operis. Formula quædam constituenda est, quam si sequemur, non aberrabimus. Species rei animo concepta. Ratio, Cic. Si proponatur instar quoddam, & facies quasi operis facta, Sympos.
units.tr: Idea] Pattern, figure, appearance, the design of a work, Vitr. The sketch of a work. Some formula must be fixed, which if we follow, we shall not go astray. The appearance of a thing conceived in the mind. Reason, Cic. If some model is set forth and the face of the work, as it were, made, Sympos.

units.la: Idem] Idem ille. Ille ipse Gorgias in illo ipso libro, Cic.
units.tr: The same] That very same. That very Gorgias in that very book, Cic.

units.la: Idem est, qui ante] Antiquum obtinet. Vulpes pilum mu-tat, non naturam.
units.tr: It is the same that was before] It keeps to the old ways. The fox changes its coat, not its nature.

units.la: Ideò] Propterea. Id eâ gratiâ, ut. Eâ re quòd. His de causis. Ex eo, quòd. Hoc nomine. Idcirco quia. Eo quod. Hæc causa est. Iis de causis. Propter eam causam quod. Propter nostram causam, Cic. Ad eum finem, Tac. Hac re, Val. M. Ad hoc, Paul. IC. Eâ causâ, Salust. Hac pro-pter, Varr.
units.tr: Therefore] For that reason. For this favour, that. For this reason, that. For these causes. From this, that. On this account. Because. Therefore, because. For that cause, that. For our cause, Cic. To that end, Tac. For this reason, Val. M. For this, Paul. IC. For this cause, Sall. For this reason, Varr.

units.la: Non ideo] Non continuò, si me in gregem sicariorum con-tulì, sum sicarius, Cic.
units.tr: Not for that reason] Not immediately: if I have joined a band of assassins, I am not therefore an assassin, Cic.

units.la: Idiota] Nullis literis homo. Illiteratus, vid. Rudis. Illiteratus.
units.tr: Layman] A man with no letters. Unlettered, see Rude, Unlettered.

units.la: Idolum] Divum simulacra, Virg. Signum æneum Cupidinis. Statua, Cic. Imago macra, Iuv. Lapides divi, Lamp.
units.tr: Idol] Images of the gods, Virg. A bronze figure of Cupid. A statue, Cic. A lean image, Juv. Stone gods, Lamp.

units.la: Idololatræ] Adorantes omnem lapidem nitidum.
units.tr: Idolaters] Those who worship every shining stone.

units.la: Idoneus] Aptus ad aliquid. Accommodatus. Habilis. Opportunus. Ad hoc nati, sculpti, facti, Cic. In eam rem si quid habebo, Plaut. Vid. Aptus.
units.tr: Fit] Apt for something. Suited. Able. Convenient. Opportune. Born, shaped, made for this, Cic. If I shall have anything for that purpose, Plaut. See Apt.

units.la: Igitur, vid. Ergo.
units.tr: Therefore, see Hence.

units.la: Ignarus] Inscius rerum omnium. Inscitia in illo est. Laborat ex inscitia. Inscitus faciendi, Cic. Inconscius. Ignorans Quid pro Quo sumendum, Liv. Nescius rerum, facti, Virg.
units.tr: Ignorant] Ignorant of all things. Ignorance is in him. He suffers from ignorance. Ignorant of doing, Cic. Unaware. Not knowing what should be taken for what, Liv. Ignorant of things and of deeds, Virg.

units.la: Ignarus rerum temerarius] Inscientia confidentiam parit.
units.tr: Ignorance of things breeds rash confidence] Ignorance gives birth to confidence.

units.la: Ignavè] Ignaviter, Cic. Socordiùs. Per socordiam, Liv. Segniter, Plin. Vigilans dormit, Plaut.
units.tr: Idly] Lazily, Cic. More carelessly. Through carelessness, Liv. Sluggishly, Plin. Awake, he sleeps, Plaut.

units.la: Ignavia] Inertia laboris, Cic. Animi torpedo, Sallust. Vid. Desidia, Pigritia.
units.tr: Idleness] Disinclination for labour, Cic. Torpor of mind, Sall. See Sloth, Laziness.

units.la: Ignavus] Iners. Segnis, Cic. Plumbeus homo. Laboris fugiens.
units.tr: Idle] Inert. Sluggish, Cic. A leaden man. One who flees labour.

units.la: Ignavi amant feriας] Ignavis semper feriæ.
units.tr: The idle love holidays] For the idle there are always holidays.

units.la: Ignavus infelix] Ignavus equus suo defraudator pabulo.
units.tr: The idle are unhappy] The idle horse defrauds itself of its own fodder.

units.la: Igneus] Ignitus, Gell. Ignescens, Plin. Ignifluus, Claud. Igniferum fulmen, Lucr.
units.tr: Fiery] Ignited, Gell. Glowing, Plin. Fire-flowing, Claud. A fire-bearing thunderbolt, Lucr.

units.la: Ignis] Fotor & vastator omnium. Motor moventium, Fotor nascentium, Excoctor maturescentium.
units.tr: Fire] The warmer and destroyer of all things. The mover of moving things, the warmer of things being born, the ripener of things coming to maturity.

units.la: Ignem elicere] Excutere ignem, scintillam silicis, Virg. Excutere ignem, Plin. Elicere ignem conflictu & ictu lapidum. Procudere ignem. Semina ardoris creant incendia sylvis, Lucr.
units.tr: To strike out fire] To strike out fire, a spark from flint, Virg. To strike out fire, Plin. To strike out fire by striking and hitting stones. To forge fire. The seeds of heat kindle fires in the woods, Lucr.

units.la: Ignitabulum] Igniarium, Plin.
units.tr: Tinderbox] A tinderbox, Plin.

units.la: Ignobilis] Homo ex familia ignobili. Ignobili loco natus. Obscurus. Obscuro, infimo loco natus. Obscuris ortus parentibus. Quem nemo propter ignobilitatem nominat, Cic. Nullis majoribus ortus, Hor. Obscurè natus, Macr. Inter agros & armenta natus, Tibul. De plebejâ fæce sellulariorum, Cic. Vid. Plebejus.
units.tr: Ignoble] A man of an ignoble family. Born in a humble place. Obscure. Born of low and obscure rank. Born of obscure parents. The man whom no one names because of his lowliness, Cic. Born of no notable ancestors, Hor. Born in obscurity, Macr. Born among fields and herds, Tibul. From the plebeian dregs of the stall-keepers, Cic. See Plebejus.

units.la: Ignobilitas] Humilitas generis. Obscuritas generis. Abjectio animi, Cic.
units.tr: Ignobility] Lowliness of birth. Obscurity of family. Abjectness of spirit, Cic.

units.la: Ignominia, vid. Contumelia.
units.tr: Ignominy, see Insult.

units.la: Ignorans, vid. Ignarus.
units.tr: Ignorant, see Ignorant.

units.la: Ignorare] Non me pudet fateri nescire, quod nesciam. In summa rerum ignoratione versari, Cic. Non didici. Juxta cum ignarissimis scire, Plaut.
units.tr: To be ignorant] I am not ashamed to confess that I do not know what I do not know. To be engaged in a total ignorance of things, Cic. I have not learned. To know things alongside the most ignorant, Plaut.

units.la: Ignorantia] Ignoratio, inertia, inscitia, inscientia, Cic. Amusia, Varr. Tirocinium, Plin.
units.tr: Ignorance] Ignorance, lack of skill, unskilfulness, lack of knowledge, Cic. Lack of culture, Varr. Inexperience, Plin.

units.la: Ignoscere] Vitio ignoscere, Ovid. Parcere. Veniam dare, tribuere. Concedere alicujus dicto. Dare impunitatem peccatorum, Cic. Concedere impunitatem. Condonare peccatum, Caes. Amittam tibi hanc unam noxiam, Plaut. Unam hanc noxiam mitte, Ter. Remittere adolescentiae alicujus, Plin. Iun. Gratiam culpae facere, Plaut. Connivere ad vitia alicujus, Er. Eximere aliquem noxae, Liv. Exsolvere aliquem poenâ, Tac. Pietati dare peccatum, Amm. Veniam alicui prosperare, Plaut.
units.tr: To pardon] To pardon a fault, Ovid. To spare. To grant forgiveness, to bestow it. To yield to someone's word. To grant impunity for wrongs, Cic. To grant impunity. To pardon a fault, Caes. I will let go this one offence for you, Plaut. Pass over this one offence, Ter. To remit the youthful fault of someone, Plin. Iun. To make a favour of a fault, Plaut. To wink at someone's vices, Er. To take someone out of harm's way, Liv. To release someone from punishment, Tac. To grant a sin to piety, Amm. To let someone's pardon succeed, Plaut.

units.la: Ignotus] Incognitus alicui. Ignorabilis. Obscurus. Nescius. Illum ego omnino natum nesciebam. Albus aterve fuerit ignoro, Cic. Ignarus, Tac. Ignoratus, Id. Incompertus, Plin. Inexploratus, Liv. Qui me ne vivum quidem novisset. Quem ego hominem nullius coloris novi, Plaut.
units.tr: Unknown] Unknown to someone. Unknowable. Obscure. Not known. I did not know him at all. I do not know whether he was white or black, Cic. Ignorant, Tac. Unknown, Id. Not ascertained, Plin. Unexplored, Liv. One who would not even have known me while I was alive. What man of no known colour do I know, Plaut.

units.la: Ignoti nulla dijudicatio] Nihil coeco coloratum. In tenebris etiam contrariis coloribus bene convenit. Asinus stramenta mavult, quàm aurum. Ars non habet contemptorem nisi ignorantem.
units.tr: No judgment of the unknown] Nothing is coloured to a blind man. In darkness even opposite colours agree well. The ass prefers straw to gold. Skill has no despiser except the ignorant.

units.la: Ile] Ilium, Enn. Intestinum tenue, Caes.
units.tr: Groin] The groin, Enn. The small intestine, Caes.

units.la: Illabi, vid. Incidere.
units.tr: To slip in, see To fall upon.

units.la: Illaesus] Infractus, Plin. Infragilis animus. Incorrupta integritas. Illibatus, Ovid. Innoxius, Col. Intemeratus, immotus, Virg. Intactus, Liv. Vid. Indemnis.
units.tr: Unharmed] Unbroken, Plin. An unbreakable spirit. Uncorrupted integrity. Unspoiled, Ovid. Harmless, Col. Untouched, unmoved, Virg. Untouched, Liv. See Undamaged.

units.la: Illaqueare aliquem] Injicere laqueum alicui, Liv. Implicare aliquem laqueis, Firm. Inducere se in laqueos. Irretire, Cic. Circumretire aliquem. Illicere. Obretire, Lucr.
units.tr: To entangle someone] To throw a noose around someone, Liv. To entangle someone in snares, Firm. To lead oneself into snares. To catch in a net, Cic. To surround someone with a net. To entice. To trap, Lucr.

units.la: Ille] Ollus, a, um, Varr. Ipse, Cic. Homo, eleganter ponitur loco ille. Aggredior hominem, Plaut. Videbitis hominem, Cic.
units.tr: That] The old form ollus, Varr. Itself, Cic. The word homo is elegantly used in place of "that." I approach that man, Plaut. You will see that man, Cic.

units.la: Illecebra] Perlecebra. Pellecebra, Plaut. Invitamentum. Pabulum studii, Cic. Lenocinium, Quint. Blandimentum, Tac. Incitamentum. Illectamentum, Apul.
units.tr: Allurement] Enticement. Enticement, Plaut. Inducement. Food for study, Cic. Flattery, Quint. Coaxing, Tac. Incitement. Lure, Apul.

units.la: Illecebrare se] Lotum gustasti.
units.tr: To entice oneself] You have tasted what is washed.

units.la: Illegitimus] Nothus. Non legitimus, Quint. Adulterinus, Plin. Apocryphus liber, Hieron.
units.tr: Illegitimate] Bastard. Not lawful, Quint. Adulterine, Plin. An apocryphal book, Hieron.

units.la: Illepidus] Agrestis, Cic. Impolitus. Rudis homo. Inconcinnus, inornatus, invenustus, Subhorridus, & incultus vir. Barbarus moribus. Incompositis moribus, Quint. Barbaricis moribus, Apul. In crasso aere natus. Naris obesae, Hor.
units.tr: Uncouth] Rustic, Cic. Unpolished. A rough man. Ungainly, unadorned, unlovely, and uncultivated man. Barbarous in manners. Of unrefined manners, Quint. Of barbarian manners, Apul. Born in thick air. With a flat nose, Hor.

units.la: Illiberalis, vid. Avarus, Parcus.
units.tr: Illiberal, see Greedy, Stingy.

units.la: Illicere] Lactare, Ter. Pellicere ad se. Prolectare egentes spe largitionis, Cic. Prolicere, Plaut. Trahere mentes artificio, Plin. Vid. Allicere.
units.tr: To allure] To coax, Ter. To entice to oneself. To lure the needy with hopes of largesse, Cic. To lure away, Plaut. To draw minds by art, Plin. See Allure.

units.la: Illicite, vid. Inique.
units.tr: Illicitly, see Unjustly.

units.la: Illicitus] Inconcessus, Quint. Impermissus, Hor. Negatus, Ovid.
units.tr: Unlawful] Not granted, Quint. Not permitted, Hor. Forbidden, Ovid.

units.la: Illidere ad aliquid] Frangere aliquid ad saxum. Offensare capita, Liv. Infringere liminibus lumbos, Hor. Impingere caput parieti, Plin. Iun. Offendere ad stipitem, Col. Incutere pollicem limini, Plin. Impingere se in columnam, Sen. Detundere digitos pedum ob lapides, Apul.
units.tr: To dash against something] To break something against a rock. To knock heads, Liv. To bruise the loins against thresholds, Hor. To knock the head against a wall, Plin. Iun. To strike against a post, Col. To strike the thumb against a threshold, Plin. To throw oneself against a column, Sen. To bruise the toes on stones, Apul.

units.la: Illinc] Illim, Pompon. prisce. Isthinc emanant mala. Indidem, Cic. Inde redeo, Ter. Inde loci, Enn.
units.tr: From there] From there, Pompon. (archaic). From here evils flow. From the same place, Cic. I return from there, Ter. From that place, Enn.

units.la: Illinere] Linere pice aliquid, Liv. Superlinere viscum pennis, Sen. Superillinere butyrum ovinum cum melle, Plin. Collinere, Col. Lutare, Lampr. Perlinere pice hulcus, Col.
units.tr: To smear] To smear something with pitch, Liv. To smear birdlime over the wings, Sen. To smear sheep's butter with honey over something, Plin. To smear over, Col. To plaster, Lampr. To smear a sore with pitch, Col.

units.la: Illiteratus] Illiteratissimus, Plin.Iun. Agrammatos. Amusus, Vitr. Nullis literis vir, Plin. Alienus a literis. Sine ulla bona arte; sine literis homo. Aversus a Musis, Cic. Profanus literarum, Marc. Analphabetus, Prud. Pulverem eruditum ne quidem attigit. Ne pilum sapientiae habet, Er.
units.tr: Unlettered] Most illiterate, Plin. Iun. Unlettered. Unmusical, Vitr. A man with no letters, Plin. Estranged from letters. Without any good art; a man without letters. Turned away from the Muses, Cic. Ignorant of letters, Marc. Unable to read, Prud. He has not even touched learned dust. He does not have a hair's breadth of wisdom, Er.

units.la: Illotus] Illautus, illutus, Plaut.
units.tr: Unwashed] Unbathed, unwashed, Plaut.

units.la: Illuc] Eo, illo, istorsum. Istoc, Ter. Isto, Plin.Iun. Illorsum, Fest.
units.tr: Thither] To that place, thither, in that direction. To that, Ter. To that, Plin. Iun. Thither-ward, Fest.

units.la: Illucere] Allucescit, Suet. Reluxit stella, Cic. Interluxit, nocte, Liv. Præluxêre faces, Mart.
units.tr: To shine] It dawns, Suet. The star shone again, Cic. It shone between in the night, Liv. Torches shone forth, Mart.

units.la: Illucescere, vid. Lucescit.
units.tr: To grow light, see It grows light.

units.la: Illudere, vid. Ludificare.
units.tr: To mock, see To delude.

units.la: Illuminare] Collustrare aliquid luce, Cic. Illustrare, Hor. Lustrat sol lampade terras, Virg. Convestit omnia profundens lucem sol. Percussa radiis solis luna, Luna.
units.tr: To illuminate] To light up something with light, Cic. To illustrate, Hor. The sun sweeps the lands with its torch, Virg. The sun covers all things, pouring out light. The moon struck by the rays of the sun, Luna.

units.la: Illunis] Interlunis nox, Amm. Illunæ caliginis, Apul.
units.tr: Moonless] A moonless night, Amm. Of moonless darkness, Apul.

units.la: Illusio, vid. Cavillatio.
units.tr: Mockery, see Jesting.

units.la: Illustris] Perillustris. Splendidus eques, Cic. Prælustris, Ovid. Speciosa miracula, Hor. Præmicans nitore galea, Apul. Superbus ornatus, Virg. Nihil pompabilius visum, Trebel.
units.tr: Illustrious] Very illustrious. A distinguished knight, Cic. Very bright, Ovid. Splendid marvels, Hor. Shining with brightness from a helmet, Apul. Proud adornment, Virg. Nothing more splendid was seen, Trebel.

units.la: Illustrissimus] Splendidus. Splendidissimus. Clarus. Clarissimus, Cic.
units.tr: Most illustrious] Splendid. Most splendid. Famous. Most famous, Cic.

units.la: Illuxit dies] Illuxit, abs. Liv. Diluxit dies, Hor. Dilucu-lavit, Gell. Elucescit.
units.tr: The day has dawned] It dawned, abs. Liv. The day has broken, Hor. The day has grown light, Gell. It grows bright.

units.la: Imaginari[ Fingere sibi alicujus rei speciem. Speciem alicujus rei cogitatione percipere. Imaginationibus aliquid agitare, Cic. Vanæ finguntur species, velut ægri somnia, Hor. Vid. Cogitare.
units.tr: To imagine] To form for oneself the appearance of something. To perceive the appearance of something in thought. To turn something over in the imagination, Cic. Empty appearances are imagined, like the dreams of the sick, Hor. See To think.

units.la: Imaginarius, vid. Fictus. Affectatus.
units.tr: Imaginary, see Feigned. Affected.

units.la: Imago] Effigies patris. Forma. Simulacrum. Sancta Jovis species, Cic. Icon, Sipont.
units.tr: Image] The likeness of a father. Form. Statue. The sacred appearance of Jupiter, Cic. Icon, Sipont.

units.la: Imago propriè expressa] Imago ad vivum repræsentata. Ethica imago, Cel. Rhod. Spirantia signa, Virg. Vivi de marmore vultus. Spirantia æra, Amm. Viva species, Prop. Vivida, animosa signa, Id. Speciem oris ita formavit, ut in ea reconditos mores penitus effingeret, Cic. Iconicum simulacrum, Suet.
units.tr: An image closely expressed: an image represented to the life. An ethical image, Cel. Rhod. Statues that breathe, Virg. Living faces from marble. Bronzes that breathe, Amm. A living likeness, Prop. Lively, spirited statues, Id. He so formed the features of the face that they fully expressed the character hidden within, Cic. A portrait statue, Suet.

units.la: Imaguncula] Icuncula, Suet. Tabellæ pictorum, Plin. Sigillum, Cic. Oscillum, Macrob.
units.tr: Little image] A little image, Suet. Painters' panels, Plin. A seal, Cic. A little mask, Macrob.

units.la: Imbecillis, imbecillitas, vid. Debilis, debilitas.
units.tr: Weak, weakness, see Feeble, feebleness.

units.la: Imber] Ruit cœlum imbribus, Virg.
units.tr: Rain] The sky falls down in showers, Virg.

units.la: Imberbis] Impubis communiter, Impuber, Cic. Investis, Apul.
units.tr: Beardless] Generally under-age; not yet grown, Cic. Unbearded, Apul.

units.la: Imbuere] Sufficere lanam medicamentis. Natura impressit animis Deorum notitiam, Cic.
units.tr: To imbue] To soak wool with medicines. Nature has impressed on minds the knowledge of the gods, Cic.

units.la: Imbui] Imbibere malam opinionem. Concipere vitium, maculam, odium. Sugere cum lacte nutricis errorem. Combibere artes, Cic. Perbibisti nequitiam, Sen. Lana bibit colorem, Plin. Potat lana, Id. Arena bibula est, Virg. Insumere, Tac.
units.tr: To be imbued] To soak up a bad opinion. To take in a fault, a stain, hatred. To suck in error with the nurse's milk. To take in the arts, Cic. You have drunk in wickedness, Sen. Wool takes up colour, Plin. Wool drinks, Id. Sand is absorbent, Virg. To take in, Tac.

units.la: Imitari aliquem] Imitari exemplum alicujus. Vestigiis alicujus insistere, Plin. Iun. Imitatione exprimere; Consequi studio. Consectari genus dicendi alicujus. Consectari aliquem imitando. Persequi alicujus vestigia. Ingredi patris vestigiis, Cic. Idem istud faciamus. Idem imitemur, Plaut. Exemplo alicujus facere. Exemplum de aliquo capere, Ter. Ad aliquod exemplar vitam dirigere, Sen.
units.tr: To imitate someone] To imitate someone's example. To tread in someone's footsteps, Plin. Iun. To express by imitation; to attain by zeal. To pursue someone's style of speaking. To follow someone by imitating. To pursue someone's tracks. To walk in a father's footsteps, Cic. Let us do the same thing. Let us imitate the same, Plaut. To act by someone's example. To take an example from someone, Ter. To direct one's life towards some model, Sen.

units.la: Imitatio] Imitamentum, Tac.
units.tr: Imitation] An imitation, Tac.

units.la: Imitatio inepta] Cacozelia. Mala affectatio, Quint. Imitatio depravata, Cic.
units.tr: Clumsy imitation] Cacozeal. Bad affectation, Quint. Corrupt imitation, Cic.

units.la: Imitatione dignus] Expositus ad imitandum, Cic.
units.tr: Worthy of imitation] Set forth to be imitated, Cic.

units.la: Imitator] Sectator. Affectator alicujus eloquentiae, Plin. Æmulus. Non duces, sed comites consiliorum, Cic. Sequax Aristippi, Sen. Secutor, Apul.
units.tr: Imitator] A follower. A pursuer of someone's eloquence, Plin. A rival. Not leaders but companions in counsels, Cic. A follower of Aristippus, Sen. A pursuer, Apul.

units.la: Imitator ineptus] Cacozelus, Quint. Suet. Simius, Hor. Simiolus, Cic.
units.tr: Clumsy imitator] A clumsy imitator, Quint. Suet. An ape, Hor. A little ape, Cic.

units.la: Immanis] Cyclope immanior. Vid. Crudelis.
units.tr: Monstrous] More monstrous than the Cyclops. See Cruel.

units.la: Immansuetus] Intractabilis animus, Sen. Intractatus & novus equus, Cic. Indomitus, Col. Indomabilis, Plaut. Ferox sonipes, Virg. Incicor, pro Incicur, Pacuv.
units.tr: Untamed] An intractable spirit, Sen. An untamed and new horse, Cic. Unbroken, Col. Unconquerable, Plaut. A fierce steed, Virg. Incicor, for incicur, Pacuv.

units.la: Immaturus] Immitis uva, Hor. Crudus, Cic. Semiacerbæ uvæ, Pallad.
units.tr: Unripe] Unripe grapes, Hor. Raw, Cic. Half-sour grapes, Pallad.

units.la: Immedicabilis, vid. Insanabilis.
units.tr: Incurable, see Incurable.

units.la: Immensus, vid. Infinitus.
units.tr: Immense, see Infinite.

units.la: Immerito] Injuriâ, injuriosè, iniquè. Nullo jure. Contra jus, fas, Cic. Immeritò accusari ac immeritissime omnium. Præter æquum & bonum. Indignissimè, Ter.
units.tr: Undeservedly] Wrongfully, unjustly, unfairly. By no right. Against law and right, Cic. To be accused undeservedly, and most undeservedly of all. Beyond what is fair and good. Most unworthily, Ter.

units.la: Immeritus] Immeritæ opes, Mart. Immerita gratia, Id.
units.tr: Undeserved] Undeserved wealth, Mart. Undeserved favour, Id.

units.la: Imminere] Instat, impendet aliquid. In procinctu mortem habere, Cic. Ingruit alicui, Virg. In cervicibus bellum, lum, Liv. In conspectu & sub ictu habere aliquid, Sen. Ante pedes posita. Vid. Appropinquare.
units.tr: To hang over] Something threatens, something hangs over. To have death at hand, Cic. War threatens someone, Virg. War is at the neck, Liv. To have something before one's eyes and within striking distance, Sen. Placed before the feet. See To approach.

units.la: Imminuitur aliquid] Decedit de summa, Liv. Decrescit dies, Plin. Defluxit unus e numero, Cic. Imminuit se dolor.Minuuntur vires,Ovid. Decoquitur aurum in igne,Liv. Diminuitur aliquid ex potestate regia, Liv. Lentescunt tempore curæ, Ovid. Minuuntur luces. Tabescunt noctes, Lucr. Detrimentum sentit dies, Sen.
units.tr: Something is diminished] It falls away from the sum, Liv. The day grows shorter, Plin. One is taken away from the number, Cic. Pain subsides of itself. Strength wanes, Ovid. Gold is consumed in the fire, Liv. Something is reduced from royal power, Liv. Cares slacken with time, Ovid. The lights grow fewer. The nights waste away, Lucr. The day feels its loss, Sen.

units.la: Imminuere, vid. Minuere.
units.tr: Imminuere, see Minuere.

units.la: Immisericors] Quis fuit tam durus ac ferreus, qui non converteretur, Cic.
units.tr: Immisericors] Who was ever so hard and iron-hearted as not to be moved? Cic.

units.la: Immittere] Intromittere aliquem ad aliquem, Ter. Indere vini guttulam in os, Plaut. Impescere in lætam segetem. Pascendi gratia mittere, Fest.
units.tr: Immittere] To let someone in to another person, Ter. To pour a drop of wine into someone's mouth, Plaut. To let cattle loose to graze on a flourishing crop. To send out for the sake of pasture, Fest.

units.la: Immobilis ] Inagitabilis & iners aër, Sen. Incitus, Bud. Templa incita sunt, Varr. Scal. Statuâ immobilior, Er.
units.tr: Immobilis] Still and sluggish air, Sen. Motionless, Bud. Temples are motionless, Varr. Scal. More immovable than a statue, Erasmus.

units.la: Immobilia bona ] Res immobiles. Res soli, Macer. IC. Immobilia bona dicuntur invadi : Mobilia rapi, Iustin. Opes fundatæ ac benè constitutæ, Cic. Fundata illis pecunia, Hor.
units.tr: Immobilia bona] Immovable property. Landed property, Macer, jurist. Immovable goods are said to be seized, movables to be carried off, Justin. Wealth well founded and securely established, Cic. Money invested, Hor.

units.la: Immoderatè] Extra modum agere aliquid, Hor. Infinitè concupiscere, Cic. Infinitè præstat cæteris. Immensum attolli, Tac. In immensum crescere, Liv. In infinitum extendere. Effusè petulans, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Immoderatè] To do something beyond measure, Hor. To desire without limit, Cic. He excels all others beyond measure. To rise up immensely, Tac. To grow without limit, Liv. To extend without bound. Wantonly playful without restraint, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Immoderatus] Vehemens in utramque partem, Ter. Immodicus, Col. Immoderatissimus. Nepotinus sumptus, Suet. Nepotalis luxus, Apul. Redundans copia. Profusus. Multus in aliqua re quispiam. Luxuriosa lætitia, Cic. Effusus in luxum homo, Tac.
units.tr: Immoderatus] Vehement in either direction, Ter. Immoderate, Col. Most immoderate. Extravagant expenditure like a spendthrift's, Suet. Spendthrift luxury, Apul. Overflowing abundance. Lavish. Someone excessive in some matter. Luxurious joy, Cic. A man poured out into luxury, Tac.

units.la: Immodestè] Intemperanter, intemperantius uti opibus, intemperatè & immoderatè vivere. Insolenter se efferre. Jactare se insolentius, Cic.
units.tr: Immodestè] Intemperately; to use one's wealth more intemperately; to live intemperately and immoderately. To carry oneself insolently. To boast more insolently, Cic.

units.la: Immodestia] Intemperies, importunitas, Cic.
units.tr: Immodestia] Intemperance, unruliness, Cic.

units.la: Immodestus] Insedatus, Cic. Incommodus, importunus, Plaut.
units.tr: Immodestus] Unsettled, Cic. Unsuitable, troublesome, Plaut.

units.la: Immolare, vid. Sacrificare.
units.tr: Immolare, see Sacrificare.

units.la: Immori alicui rei] Inemori spectaculo, Hor. Mori in studio dimetiendi cœli, Cic. Alicui rei intabescere. Consumere ætatem in aliquâ re, Cic.
units.tr: Immori alicui rei] To die while watching a spectacle, Hor. To die in the pursuit of measuring the heavens, Cic. To waste away over something. To spend one's life on something, Cic.

units.la: Immortalis] Nullis delebilis annis vivet, Mart. Vivax virtus expersque sepulchri, Ovid. A mortalitate se vindicare, Sen.
units.tr: Immortalis] Will live, undestroyed by any years, Mart. Living virtue, free from the tomb, Ovid. To free oneself from mortality, Sen.

units.la: Immunis] Vacuus à sumptu. Lege solutus ac liber. Exlex, Cic. Vid. Liber.
units.tr: Immunis] Free from expense. Released and free by law. Outside the law, Cic. See Liber.

units.la: Immunitas] Vacatio muneris publici, Cic. Vid. Privilegium.
units.tr: Immunitas] Exemption from public duty, Cic. See Privilegium.

units.la: Immunitas locus] Urbs nuda præsidio, Cic. Hæc pars patet ictibus, Sen.
units.tr: Immunitas locus] A city bare of its garrison, Cic. This part lies open to blows, Sen.

units.la: Immutabilis] Ratum, firmum, fixum, Cic. Inflexibilis obstinatio. Irrevocabilis constantia, Plin. Iun. Tenax propositi, Hor.
units.tr: Immutabilis] Settled, firm, fixed, Cic. Unbending obstinacy. Irrevocable steadfastness, Plin. Iun. Holding fast to one's purpose, Hor.

units.la: Immutatio] Mutatio, permutatio, commutatio morum, Cic. Transmutatio, Lucr. Inclinatio, Liv.
units.tr: Immutatio] Change, alteration, transformation of manners, Cic. Transmutation, Lucr. Inclination, turn, Liv.

units.la: Imo, vel immo] Quin imo. Quin potius, Plaut. Atque adeo. Quin etiam. Imo etiam, Cic. Imo vero. Imo enimvero, Ter.
units.tr: Imo, vel immo] Nay rather. Rather, Plaut. Indeed, and even. Nay, even, Cic. Nay, truly. Nay indeed, Ter.

units.la: Impar viribus] Ne Hercules quidem contra duos. Cedendum multitudini.
units.tr: Impar viribus] Not even Hercules against two. One must yield to numbers.

units.la: Imparatè, id est, irreverenter] Illotis manibus, pedibus ingredi.
units.tr: Imparatè, id est, irreverenter] To enter with unwashed hands and feet.

units.la: Imparatus] Discinctus miles, Liv.
units.tr: Imparatus] A soldier with his belt undone, Liv.

units.la: Impassibilis] Apathes, Plin. Qui respuit omnis mali sensus. Impatiens animus. Quibus summum bonum visum est animus impatiens, Sen. Nullius mali patiens, sapiens. Obduruit usu, & incaluit incredibilis alicujus patientia, Id. Invulnerabilis animus, Extra omnem patientiam positus, Id.
units.tr: Impassibilis] Apathes, Plin. One who rejects every sense of evil. An insensible mind. Those for whom an insensible mind seemed the highest good, Sen. One who suffers no evil, the wise man. Through practice a mind has grown hard, and an incredible endurance of something has grown warm, Id. An invulnerable mind, placed beyond all suffering, Id.

units.la: Impassibilitas] Apathia.
units.tr: Impassibilitas] Apathy.

units.la: Impatiens] Intractabilis animus. Mollior in dolore, Cic. Qui nullum malum ferre potest, Sen. Mollissimum & indignantissimum servitutis genus, Col. Facile fit, quod illi doleat, Ter. Imbecilla, si tangantur, lædi se putant. Molliter fert injurias. Nihil molestum æquo animo ferre potest. Totus ulcus est. Quicquid in eo attigeris, ulcus est. Vel ad plumæ contactum exhorrescit. Impatientiæ manus dedit.
units.tr: Impatiens] An unmanageable mind. Softer in pain, Cic. One who can bear no evil, Sen. The softest and most indignant kind of slavery, Col. It is easy for someone who is hurt to feel pain, Ter. Weak people, if touched, think themselves harmed. Bears injuries softly. Cannot bear anything annoying with an equal mind. He is all sore; whatever you touch on him is a sore. Shrinks even at the touch of a feather. Has surrendered to impatience.

units.la: Impatienter] Intoleranter dolere. Immoderatè aliquid ferre. Immodicè ferre aliquem casum. Repugnanter, Cic. Impatientiùs dolere, Justin. Molliter ferre ægritudinem, Sallust.
units.tr: Impatienter] To grieve intolerantly. To bear something immoderately. To bear a misfortune excessively. Reluctantly, Cic. To grieve more impatiently, Justin. To bear sickness softly, Sallust.

units.la: Impatientia] Animus extra omnem patientiam positus, Sen. Abjectio patientiæ. Victa dolore patientia.
units.tr: Impatientia] A mind placed beyond all patience, Sen. Abandonment of patience. Patience overcome by grief.

units.la: Impavidus] Intrepidus, Plin. Tac. Interritus, Quint. Imperterritus, Virg. Otiosus à metu, Gell.
units.tr: Impavidus] Fearless, Plin. Tac. Undaunted, Quint. Unterrified, Virg. Free from fear, Gell.

units.la: Impedimentum] Obstaculum, Sipont. Obex, Virg. Objectaculum, Varr. Incommodum, incommoditas, Cic. Præpedimentum, Plaut. Obnunciatio, Bud.
units.tr: Impedimentum] Obstacle, Sipont. Bar, Virg. Obstruction, Varr. Inconvenience, inconvenience, Cic. Hindrance, Plaut. Obnunciatio, Bud.

units.la: Impedire] Impedimento esse alicui. Incommodare. Commodis alicujus officere, & obstare, Cic. Remorari alicujus commodum, Ter. Obstrigillare, Sen. Interpellare victoriam, Cæs. Accidere alas. Incidere pennas.
units.tr: Impedire] To be a hindrance to someone. To cause inconvenience. To thwart someone's advantages and stand in their way, Cic. To delay someone's advantage, Ter. To hold back, Sen. To interrupt a victory, Caes. To clip the wings. To cut the feathers.

units.la: Non impediam te] Non obsistam: non fuero impedimento. Non obturbabo. Non reluctabor. Non obstrepam tuis conatibus. Non renitar. Non reclamabo. Non remorabor institutum tuum, Er.
units.tr: Non impediam te] I will not oppose you; I will not be a hindrance. I will not disturb you. I will not struggle against you. I will not drown out your efforts. I will not resist. I will not object. I will not delay your undertaking, Erasmus.

units.la: Impeditè] Tanquam super spinas incedere.
units.tr: Impeditè] As if walking on thorns.

units.la: Impeditio] Interturbatio, Plaut.
units.tr: Impeditio] Disturbance, Plaut.

units.la: Impellere, vid. Inducere.
units.tr: Impellere, see Inducere.

units.la: Impendere in aliquid] Facere impensam vel impensas, sumptum. In rem aliquam insumere sumptum. Ponere alicubi sumptum. Sustinere sumptum. Sustentare sumptibus aliquem, Cic. Conferre in aliquid impendia, Quint.
units.tr: Impendere in aliquid] To make an outlay or expense. To spend money on some matter. To put expense somewhere. To bear expense. To support someone with money, Cic. To devote outlays to something, Quint.

units.la: Impenetrabilis] Nullo forabilis ictu. Imperfossus, Ovid.
units.tr: Impenetrabilis] Not pierceable by any blow. Unpierced, Ovid.

units.la: Impensa] Impendium, sumptus, Cic.
units.tr: Impensa] Outlay, expense, Cic.

units.la: Impensæ in res nihili] Bracteis aureis inaurare juglandium putamina. Asini caput sapone, nitro lavare.
units.tr: Impensæ in res nihili] To gild walnut shells with gold leaf. To wash an ass's head with soap and nitre.

units.la: Impensè, vid. Enixè.
units.tr: Impensè, see Enixè.

units.la: Imperare] Imperitare pro jure suo, Plaut. Imperium exercere, Virg. Summam imperii tenere, Cic. Imperium in aliquem tenere, Cic.
units.tr: Imperare] To rule arbitrarily by one's own right, Plaut. To exercise command, Virg. To hold the chief command, Cic. To hold command over someone, Cic.

units.la: Imperare mihi noli] Eme cui imperes.
units.tr: Imperare mihi noli] Buy someone to command.

units.la: Imperator, vid. Cæsar.
units.tr: Imperator, see Cæsar.

units.la: Imperator bellicus, vid, Dux exercitus. Imperfecte] Non perfecte, Cic.
units.tr: Imperator bellicus, see Dux exercitus. Imperfecte] Not perfectly, Cic.

units.la: Imperfectus] Inelaboratus, vel, illaboratus, Quint. Infabricata robora, Virg. Informatus, Id. Abest a perfectione. Absolutionem & perfectionem in eo desidero. Manca cognitio, Cic. Incompletus, Firm. Semifactus, Tac. Semiperfectus, Suet. Truncus sermo, Stat. Affecta aedificia, Gell. Sacra infecta relinquere. Lima ultima operi defuit. Summa manus abfuit scriptis, Ovid.
units.tr: Imperfectus] Unwrought, or unlabored, Quint. Unfinished timbers, Virg. Unshaped, Id. Lacking perfection. I miss completion and perfection in it. Incomplete knowledge, Cic. Incomplete, Firm. Half-made, Tac. Half-finished, Suet. Truncated speech, Stat. Unfinished buildings, Gell. To leave sacred rites unperformed. The final polish was lacking to the work. The finishing touch was missing from the writings, Ovid.

units.la: Imperiosus] Nimius imperii, Liv.
units.tr: Imperiosus] Excessive in command, Liv.

units.la: Imperite] Inerudite, inscitissimè, Gell. Inscite, indocte, inscienter, Cic. Inscie, Apul.
units.tr: Imperite] Unlearnedly, most ignorantly, Gell. Ignorantly, unlearnedly, unskilfully, Cic. Ignorantly, Apul.

units.la: Imperitus] Imprudens religionis, Liv. Rudis rei militaris, Cicer. Rerum nescius, Virg. Inguinis & capitis quae sint discrimina nescit. Ne Æsopum quidem trivisti. Monacho imperitior, Er. Inexpertus, Hor. Inscius omnium rerum, Cic.
units.tr: Imperitus] Ignorant of religion, Liv. Inexperienced in military affairs, Cic. Ignorant of affairs, Virg. He does not know the difference between groin and head. You have not even rubbed up Aesop. More ignorant than a monk, Erasmus. Inexperienced, Hor. Knowing nothing of anything, Cic.

units.la: Imperium] Dominium, ICt. Dominatio, Liv. Principatus, Cic. Rerum nos summa sequetur, Lucan. Summa imperii, Caef. Potentatus, Id. Potestas. Ditio, Cic.
units.tr: Imperium] Dominion, jurist. Domination, Liv. Principate, Cic. Whatever is the highest of things will follow us, Lucan. Supreme command, Caes. Power. Potestas. Rule, Cic.

units.la: Impertinens] Nihil ad rem. Nihil ad rhombum. Nihil ad versum. Nihil ad Dionysium. Nihil sui cum amaracino. Anser inter olores. Caeco quid speculum? Nihil ad farinas. Non est fori tui.
units.tr: Impertinens] Nothing to the point. Nothing to the rhombus. Nothing to the verse. Nothing to Dionysius. Nothing to do with marjoram. A goose among swans. What is a mirror to the blind? Nothing to do with the meal. It is not of your forum.

units.la: Impertinentia agere] Chordas non movendas movere.
units.tr: Impertinentia agere] To move strings that should not be moved.

units.la: Impertire aliquid alicui] Impertiri. Derivare partem alicujus rei in aliquem, Cic.
