units.tr: Impertire aliquid alicui] Impertiri. To transfer a part of something to someone, Cic.

units.la: Impervius] Insuperabilis transitus Alpium. Impenetrabilis exercitus, Liv. Viae incommeabiles, Amm. Impeditissima silva, Caef.
units.tr: Impervius] An impassable crossing of the Alps. An impenetrable army, Liv. Impassable roads, Amm. The densest forest, Caes.

units.la: Impetere aliquem] Impetum in aliquem facere. Irruere, invehi in aliquem, Cic. Adpugnare classem, Tacit. Adoriri. Intentare manus alicui, Liv. Invadere in aliquem inusitatâ rabie, cum ferro, effrenatius, Cic. Involare aliquem, Apul. Involare in capillum alicujus, Ter. Incursionem facere in hostes, Liv. Incursare agros, Id.
units.tr: Impetere aliquem] To make an attack upon someone. To rush at, to assail someone, Cic. To attack a fleet, Tac. To assault. To threaten someone with the hands, Liv. To fall upon someone with unusual fury, with a sword, more unbridled, Cic. To swoop upon someone, Apul. To fly at someone's hair, Ter. To make an incursion against enemies, Liv. To raid fields, Id.

units.la: Impetrare, vid. Exorare aliquem.
units.tr: Impetrare, see Exorare aliquem.

units.la: Impetratio] Impetratus, Scal.
units.tr: Impetratio] Obtaining, Scal.

units.la: Impetrabilis, vid. Exorabilis.
units.tr: Impetrabilis, see Exorabilis.

units.la: Impetuosè] Impetu, incitatiùs, Cic. Impete magno, Lucr. Effufiffimis habenis invadere hostem, Liv. Incitatus fe-ror, Cic. Grassor, Hor.
units.tr: Impetuosè] With impetus, more swiftly, Cic. With great force, Lucr. To attack the enemy with reins loosened as far as possible, Liv. Impetuous rage, Cic. I rush forth, Hor.

units.la: Impetus] Inc tatus. Flumen orationis, Cicer Violen-tia ventorum, Plin. Rapido ictu decurrentes fluvii, Amm. Incitus mundi assiduus, Plaut. Agmine ingref-fi, Liv.
units.tr: Impetus] Impulse. The flow of speech, Cic. Violence of winds, Plin. Rivers running down with a rapid stroke, Amm. The constant rush of the world, Plaut. To enter in column, Liv.

units.la: Impetus periculosus] Mala cuncta ministrat impetus.
units.tr: Impetus periculosus] Impulse brings every kind of evil.

units.la: Impexus] Impexa coma,Ovid. Intactum caput buxo,Juv. Vid. Incomptus.
units.tr: Impexus] Unkempt hair, Ovid. A head untouched by a boxwood comb, Juv. See Incomptus.

units.la: Impietas] Irreligiositas, Fab. Vict.
units.tr: Impietas] Irreligion, Fab. Vict.

units.la: Impius] A pietate, à religione remotus, Cic. Sacrilega lingua, Ovid.
units.tr: Impius] Remote from piety and religion, Cic. A sacrilegious tongue, Ovid.

units.la: Implacabilis] Implacatus, Ovid. Inexpiabilis, Liv. Nullis affatibus delinitus, Amm. Implacidus, Hor. Durus & ferreus homo, Cic. Nullis precibus, officiis, rationibus, spe, metu, pretio adduci potest, Cic. Inflexibilis, Plin.
units.tr: Implacabilis] Unappeased, Ovid. Not to be atoned for, Liv. Soothed by no words, Amm. Implacable, Hor. A hard and iron-hearted man, Cic. Cannot be moved by any prayers, services, reasons, hope, fear or price, Cic. Inflexible, Plin.

units.la: Implacabilitas] Duritia animi, Cicer. Rigor naturae inflexibilis, Plin. Obstinatio inflexibilis, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Implacabilitas] Hardness of mind, Cic. Unbending rigour of nature, Plin. Inflexible obstinacy, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Implere] Complere horrea messe, Lucan. Replere domos exhaustas. Opplere. Referserunt omnia libris. Frequentare orationem luminibus, Cicer. Replere aliquem unguentorum, Plaut. Augustus Italiam coloniarum numero frequentavit, Suet. Stipare. Opulentare, Col. Opimare, Vopisc.
units.tr: Implere] To fill barns with the harvest, Lucan. To refill emptied houses. To fill up. They filled everything with books. To crowd a speech with lights, Cic. To fill someone with ointments, Plaut. Augustus filled Italy with a large number of colonies, Suet. To crowd. To enrich, Col. To fatten, Vopisc.

units.la: Impletio] Expletio, Cic. Repletio, f. a. v.
units.tr: Impletio] Filling up, Cic. Repletion, f. a. v.

units.la: Implicare aliquem] Involvere, Plin. Intricare aliquem. Conjicere in tricas aliquem, Plaut. Irretire aliquem veste, Cic. Nexare, Virg. Innectere, Id. Impedire aliquem, Ter. Illigare, Hor.
units.tr: Implicare aliquem] To wrap up, Plin. To entangle someone. To throw someone into snares, Plaut. To ensnare someone in a garment, Cic. To bind, Virg. To entwine, Id. To hinder someone, Ter. To bind, Hor.

units.la: Implicari] Involvere se laqueis. Induere se in laqueos, Cicer. Convolvi, Plin. Innecti, Virg. Præpediri aliquâ re, Plaut.
units.tr: Implicari] To entangle oneself in snares. To put oneself into nooses, Cic. To be rolled up, Plin. To be entwined, Virg. To be hindered by something, Plaut.

units.la: Implumis, vid. Impubes.
units.tr: Unfledged, see Impubes.

units.la: Impolite] Crasse, inornatè, inculte, horridè, vastè, Rustice loqui. Pingui Minervâ agere. Inconditè, inelegantèr, squalidè, Cic. Crasâ Minervâ,Hor. Crassiore Musâ,Quint. Invenustè, inconcinniter, Gell. Insciè,Plaut. Illepidè. Infice-tissimè, Plin. Inficetè, Solin. Mapalia mera fecisti,Sen.
units.tr: Impolite: to speak coarsely, plainly, inelegantly, uncouthly, roughly, rustically; to act with a clumsy Minerva. To speak carelessly, inelegantly, squalidly, Cic. With a crude Minerva, Hor. With a heavier Muse, Quint. Without charm, without harmony, Gell. Unskilfully, Plaut. Without wit. Most unwittily, Plin. Unwittily, Solin. You have made mere hovels, Sen.

units.la: Impolitus, vid. Incultus.
units.tr: Unpolished, see Uncultivated.

units.la: Imponere] Indere ignem in aram, Plaut. Ingerere ligna foco, Tibull. Ponere in caput, in capite, coronam, Gell.
units.tr: To put on: to throw fire on the altar, Plaut. To heap wood on the fire, Tibull. To place on the head, or on the head as a crown, Gell.

units.la: Importunè] Instanter dicere, Quint. Infectanter, Gell. Molestè rogare, Cic.
units.tr: Importunately: to speak insistently, Quint. To pester, Gell. To ask troublesomely, Cic.

units.la: Importunitas]Instantia, Gell. Solicitatio, Ter. Cic. Efflagitatio. Efflagitatus. Nunquam tuo odio vinces me. Compellatio, Cic. Odium, Ter. Protelum, Lucr.
units.tr: Importunity: insistence, Gell.; solicitation, Ter. Cic.; urging, pressing. Never will you conquer me by your hatred. Accusation, Cic. Hatred, Ter. Delay, Lucr.

units.la: Importunus] Urgens, Cic. Coccyge importunior, Er. Molestus. Odiosus. Submolestus. Permolestus, Cic.
units.tr: Importunate: pressing, Cic. More importunate than a cuckoo, Er. Troublesome. Odious. Somewhat troublesome. Very troublesome, Cic.

units.la: Impossibile est] Non erit ut distent. Non erat ut fieri posset, Lucr. Fieri non potest, Cic. Citius terra ætherem conscendet. Facilius ex illo excutias ignem. Muti citius loquentur. Prius cavum à convexo disjunxeris.
units.tr: It is impossible: it will not be that they are apart. It was not possible for it to happen, Lucr. It cannot be done, Cic. Sooner shall the earth climb up to the sky. Sooner would you strike fire from him. Dumb men will speak sooner. Sooner will you separate the hollow from the convex.

units.la: Impossibilia tentare] Aquam igni miscere. Arenam metiri. Calvum vellere. Cancrum rectâ ingredi docere. Exurere, exhaurire mare. Ferrum natare doces. Nudo vestem detrahere: Lupi alas quærere. Hippocrates desperatis vult medicinam adhibere. Aquam è pumice postulas. Calvum pectere. Colligere uvas è spinis. Metari mare.
units.tr: To attempt the impossible: to mix water with fire; to measure sand; to pluck a bald man; to teach a crab to walk straight; to burn up or drain the sea; you teach iron to swim; to strip clothing from the naked; to seek wings of wolves; Hippocrates wants medicine applied to the hopeless; you ask water from pumice; to comb a bald man; to gather grapes from thorns; to measure the sea.

units.la: Ad impossibilia nemo obligatur] Impossibilium nulla obligatio. Ultrà posse viri non vult Deus ulla requiri.
units.tr: No one is bound to the impossible: there is no obligation to the impossible. God does not wish anything to be required of a man beyond his power.

units.la: Impostor, vid. Deceptor.
units.tr: Impostor, see Deceiver.

units.la: Imprecari, vid. Exsecrari.
units.tr: To imprecate, see To curse.

units.la: Impressor] Excusor, Quint. Typographus, Iuv. Librarius, Cic. Liv. Bibliographus, Scal.
units.tr: Printer: publisher, Quint. Typographer, Iuv. Bookseller, Cic. Liv. Bibliographer, Scal.

units.la: Imprimere] Exprimere, Mart. Excudere, ex Cic. Prelo subjicere, Col.
units.tr: To print: to press out, Mart. To strike off, Cic. To put under the press, Col.

units.la: Impressus] Ectypus, Plin. Informatus in animis nostris, i. e. impressus. Insignitæ veritatis notæ, Cic.
units.tr: Impressed: an impression, Plin. Formed in our minds, that is, impressed. Marks of truth stamped in, Cic.

units.la: Imprimis, vid. Primò.
units.tr: Especially, see First.

units.la: Improbabilis] Probabile non est, Cic. Probationem non habet, Sen.
units.tr: Improbable: it is not probable, Cic. It has no proof, Sen.

units.la: Improbandus] Improbatus, Vlp. Damnabilis, Polli. In pejus notabilis, Quint.
units.tr: Not to be approved: disapproved, Ulp. Condemnable, Pollio. Noticeable for the worse, Quint.

units.la: Improbare] Reprobare aliquid. Cerâ miniatâ notare, Cic. Damnare, Ovid. Carbone notare, Hor. Vid. Vituperare.
units.tr: To disapprove: to reject something. To mark with red wax, Cic. To condemn, Ovid. To mark with charcoal, Hor. See To find fault with.

units.la: Improbus, vid. Nequam.
units.tr: Wicked, see Worthless.

units.la: Improbum esse facile est] Compendiaria res improbitas.
units.tr: It is easy to be wicked: wickedness is a shortcut.

units.la: Improles] Orbus senex, Cic. Orbæ natis matres, Col. de Ovib.
units.tr: Without offspring: an old man bereft of children, Cic. Mothers bereft of their sons, Col. on sheep.

units.la: Impromptus] Fastidiosus in causis recipiendis. Languens: languidus : alienior & languidior. Lentus & frigidus in dicendo. Frigidus homo. Frigidissimus. Intermortua concio. Jacens oratio, animus, Cic. Stataria comœdia, Don. Tepidus, instrenuus, Plaut. Animo cunctantiore. Cunctator & segnis. Cunctabundus, Liv.
units.tr: Unready: fastidious in accepting cases. Languid, sluggish; more alien and more languid. Slack and cold in speaking. A cold man. Very cold. A dead sermon. A lifeless speech or spirit, Cic. A standing comedy, Donatus. Lukewarm, inactive, Plaut. With a more hesitant spirit. Dawdling and sluggish. Hesitating, Liv.

units.la: Improprie] Minùs proprie, Cic. Abusivè, Quint.
units.tr: Improperly: less properly, Cic. Abusively, Quint.

units.la: Improprius] Figurata verba, Quint. Vagi nominis aliquid, Plin. Spurius versus, Ausen. Extraria defensio, ad Heren.
units.tr: Improper: figurative words, Quint. Something of a vague name, Plin. A spurious verse, Ausonius. A foreign defence, ad Herennium.

units.la: Improsper, vid. Infelix.
units.tr: Unprosperous, see Unhappy.

units.la: Improvidè] Imprudenter peccare. Imprudentiùs ad flammam accessit, Ter. Per imprudentiam, incautè, inconsideratè, Cic. Incautiùs, improvisò, Liv. De improviso, Plaut. Cic.
units.tr: Improvidently: to sin imprudently. He approached the flame too imprudently, Ter. Through imprudence, carelessly, inconsiderately, Cic. More carelessly, unexpectedly, Liv. Unawares, Plaut. Cic.

units.la: Improvidens] Mens improvida, inconsiderans, inconsideratus. Parum videt. Inconsultus, Cic. Occipiti cœco vivens, Persi. Imprudens, Ter. In diem vivens.
units.tr: Improvident: a improvident, inconsiderate mind; inconsiderate. Sees little. Inconsiderate, Cic. Living with a blind back of the head, Persius. Imprudent, Ter. Living from day to day.

units.la: Imprudens] Parum prudens, Ovid. Neque gutta consilii. Plus cimex sanguinis, quàm ille rationis habet, Er.
units.tr: Imprudent: not very prudent, Ovid. Not a drop of counsel. The bedbug has more blood than that man has reason, Erasmus.

units.la: Imprudens prudentia] Malum malo qui tegit, cumulat.
units.tr: Imprudent prudence: he who covers evil with evil piles it up.

units.la: Imprudentia] Mentis occultum delirium.
units.tr: Imprudence: a hidden madness of the mind.

units.la: Impubes] Implumis, Hor. Impube corpus, impuber filius, imberbis, Cic. Impubis puer, Plin. Impubescens cortex arboris, Id. Depubes, Fest. Investis, Pallad.
units.tr: Immature: unfledged, Hor. A body not yet mature, an immature son, beardless, Cic. A boy not yet grown, Plin. A bark of a tree not yet mature, Id. Depubes, Fest. Unclothed, Pallad.

units.la: Impudens] Impudicus. A pudore longissimè remotus. Oscus. Inverecundus. Petulans dictum. Insigniter impudens. Inverecundum animi ingenium possidet. Perfricuit os. Impudentiusculus. Virtutem, fidem, existimationem pudoris amisit. Durissimo ore est, Cic. Effrons, Popisc. Irreverens, verens, Spart. Perfricæ frontis. Musca impudentior. Frons ferrea. Frons illi periit. Propudianus porcus. Nihil pudet. Dedidicit pudorem. Oblitus est pudoris. Nescit pudescere. Exuit pudorem. Nihil habet oris. Quo ore? Quâ fronte? Er. Vid. Depuduit.
units.tr: Shameless: unchaste. Far removed from modesty. Impudent. Immodest. Insolent in speech. Insolently shameless. Possesses an immodest disposition of mind. Has hardened his face. Rather shameless. Has lost virtue, faith, and reputation of modesty. Has a very hard face, Cic. Brazen, Popisc. Irreverent, reverent, Spartianus. Of hardened brow. A more shameless pig than a fly. Iron brow. His brow has perished. Shameless hog. Nothing shames him. He has unlearned modesty. He has forgotten modesty. He does not know how to blush. He has cast off modesty. He has no face. With what face? With what brow? Erasmus. See Ashamed.

units.la: Impudenter] Parum pudenter rogare, Cic. Nudo capite, ex Chrysost. Aperto capite, Plaut. Hor. Operto capite. Fuge atque operi caput, Plaut. Deposito pudore. Cynicè vivere. Caninis moribus vivere. Oscè loqui. Inconsultè. Temerè, Cic.
units.tr: Shamelessly: to ask rather unbecomingly, Cic. With bare head, from Chrysostom. With uncovered head, Plaut. Hor. With covered head. Flee and cover your head, Plaut. With modesty laid aside. To live like a Cynic. To live with dog's habits. To speak obscenely. Without deliberation. Rashly, Cic.

units.la: Impudentia] Inverecundia, impudica impudentia Petulantia, Cic. Pudor præmortuus, Liv. Projectus, Ovid. Prostitutus, Firm. Os impudens, durum, Ter. Os ferreum, & os, abs. Cic. Frons dura. Duritia oris. Firmitas frontis, Sen. Frons ferrea, Plin. Iun. Prostrata pudicitia.
units.tr: Impudence: immodesty, unchaste impudence, wantonness, Cic. Modesty dead beforehand, Liv. Cast out, Ovid. Prostituted, Firmicus. A shameless, hard face, Ter. An iron face, and a face, Cic. A hard brow. Hardness of face. Firmness of brow, Sen. An iron brow, Pliny the Younger. Prostrate chastity.

units.la: Impugnare aliquid] Facere in hostes impressionem, Varr. Dare impressionem. Incessere aliquem saxis, pilis. Instare ferociter alicui. Carpere agmen, Liv. Incursare aciem, Tacit. Urgere aliquem litteris. Incurrere impetu in aliquem. Premere verbo aliquem. Impugnare terga hostium, Cic. Infestare, infestantur Pygmæi à gruibus, Plin.
units.tr: To attack something: to make an assault on enemies, Varro. To give an onset. To pelt someone with stones or javelins. To press fiercely upon someone. To seize the column, Liv. To run over the battle line, Tac. To press someone with letters. To rush violently upon someone. To press someone with words. To assault the rear of the enemy, Cic. To harass, the Pygmies are harassed by cranes, Plin.

units.la: Impulsio, impulsor, vid. Incitatio. incitator.
units.tr: Impulse, instigator, see Incitement, inciter.

units.la: Impunè ferre] Impunitus dimissus est. Impunitum hoc illi fuit. Impunitatem consecutus est, Cic. Impunè fecit, impunè habet, impunè abiit. Tulit inultum, Ter. Impunè id illi est, impunissimè licuit, Plaut. Tacitum tulit, Cic. Impunitè aliquid committere, Amm.
units.tr: To go unpunished: he was dismissed unpunished. This was unpunished for him. He obtained impunity, Cic. He did it with impunity, he has it with impunity, he went away with impunity. He bore it unavenged, Ter. It is unpunished for him, it was most unpunished permitted, Plaut. He bore it in silence, Cic. To commit something unpunished, Ammianus.

units.la: Impunis] Impunitus, inultus, Cic. Incastigatus, Hor.
units.tr: Unpunished: unpunished, unavenged, Cic. Not chastised, Hor.

units.la: Impurè] Sordidè, Plin. Iun. Turpiter. Spurè. Spurcissimè. Obscœnè. Causa agetur fœdissimè. Sutorio atramento absolutus, Cic. Fœdè admissum aliquid, Lucr.
units.tr: Impurely: meanly, Plin. Iun. Shamefully. Foully. Most foully. Obscenely. The case will be pleaded most foully. Acquitted with a cobbler's ink, Cic. Something foully committed, Lucr.

units.la: Impuritas] Verborum, rerum obscœnitas. Fœditas. Labes turpitudinis, Cic. Impuritia, Plaut.
units.tr: Impurity: obscenity of words and things. Foulness. The stain of baseness, Cic. Impurity, Plaut.

units.la: Impurus] Immundus, Plaut. Immundissimus, Suet. Spurcus : Spurcissimus. Sputatilicus. Lutulentus sus, Cic. Obscœnus, Ovid. Inquinatus, inquinatissimus. Maculosa vestis, Cic. Sordida mappa, Hor. Contaminatus parri- cidiis, Cic.
units.tr: Impure: unclean, Plaut. Most unclean, Suet. Filthy; most filthy. Spitty. Most muddy. A muddy pig, Cic. Obscene, Ovid. Defiled, most defiled. A stained garment, Cic. A dirty towel, Hor. Contaminated by parricides, Cic.

units.la: Imputare alicui culpam] Adscribere alicui negligentiam. Assignare aliquid imprudentiae, Cic. Vertere aliquid stultitiae alicui, Plaut. Attribuere alicui culpam, causam. Arrogare sibi sapientiam. Non sumo mihi tantum neque arrogo; Cic. Adjudicare alquid alicui, Plin. Vid. Tribuere.
units.tr: To impute blame to someone: to ascribe negligence to someone. To assign something to imprudence, Cic. To turn something into folly for someone, Plaut. To attribute blame or cause to someone. To claim wisdom for oneself. I do not claim so much for myself, nor arrogate it, Cic. To adjudge something to someone, Plin. See To attribute.

units.la: Imus] Infimus, Plaut.
units.tr: Lowest: the lowest, Plaut.

units.la: Inaccessus] Inascensus locus, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Inaccessible: a place that cannot be climbed, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Inaequalis] Inaequabilis varietas, inaequatum onus, Tibul. Impar intervallum. Nihil ad Perfium, Cic. Dispar certamen, Ovid. Injustus fascis, Virg. Major, Sen. Incomparabilis, Plin. Ne comparandus quidem ad illum, Ter. Disparat, Plaut.
units.tr: Unequal: uneven variety, an unequal burden, Tibullus. Unequal interval. Nothing compared to Persius, Cic. An unequal contest, Ovid. An unjust bundle, Virg. Greater, Sen. Incomparable, Plin. Not even to be compared with him, Ter. Unequal, Plaut.

units.la: Inaequalia comparare] Elephanti culicem conferre. Formica camelus.
units.tr: To compare unequal things: an elephant compared with a gnat. An ant with a camel.

units.la: Inaequalis societas, vid. Societas.
units.tr: Unequal partnership, see Partnership.

units.la: Inaequalitas] Imparilitas, Gell. Iniquitas loci, Liv. Anomalia, Gell.
units.tr: Inequality: disparity, Gell. Unevenness of place, Liv. Anomaly, Gell.

units.la: Inaequaliter] Inaequabiliter, Col. Iniquè comparata certatio, Ter. Justo longius aliquid, Cic. Impariter juncti versus, Hor. Injuria dispertivisti, Plaut.
units.tr: Unequally: unevenly, Col. An unfairly matched contest, Ter. Something too far beyond what is just, Cic. Verses joined unequally, Hor. You have divided unjustly, Plaut.

units.la: Inaestimabilis] Extra pretium est. Auro contrà non est carus. Auro expendi hunc hominem decet, Plaut.
units.tr: Inestimable: beyond price. It is not dear even at gold. This man deserves to be bought with gold, Plaut.

units.la: Inanis] Vanus ictus, Liv. Supervacanea operositas, Quint. Supervacuus metus, Ovid. Irritus labor, Id. Vid. Vacuus.
units.tr: Empty: a vain blow, Liv. Superfluous labour, Quint. Needless fear, Ovid. Fruitless toil, Id. See Empty.

units.la: Inanitas] Jejunitas & fames, Cic. Inanimentum, Plaut. Inane profundum, Lucr. Cassa palearum, Lucan.
units.tr: Emptiness: fasting and hunger, Cic. An empty thing, Plaut. An empty deep, Lucr. A vain husk of chaff, Lucan.

units.la: Inaratus] Incultus ager, Cicer. Ferus ager, Fest.
units.tr: Unploughed: uncultivated field, Cic. Wild field, Festus.

units.la: Inardescere, vid. Exardescere.
units.tr: To grow hot, see To blaze up.

units.la: Inarticulatus] Inexplanata lingua, Plin. Incertae vocis sonitus, Non. Mutae quadrupedes, Nævi.
units.tr: Inarticulate: tongue not made plain, Plin. Sounds of an uncertain voice, Nonius. Dumb four-footed creatures, Naevius.

units.la: Inaudire aliquid] Auditiunculâ aspersus & de, Gell. Non satis exaudiebam, nec fallebar sermonis tamen, Plaut.
units.tr: To hear something: sprinkled with a little hearing, and from, Gell. I did not hear well, nor was I deceived by the speech, Plaut.

units.la: Inaudita causa] Inexorata causa, vel res, Cic.
units.tr: Unheard cause: a cause or matter not yet pleaded, Cic.

units.la: Inauditus] Inauditum omni memoria. Ne fando quidem auditum est. Nullo exemplo factum, Cic. Fando inauditus, Plin. Immemoratus, Lucr. Exemplo carens nefas, Sen. Novo exemplo, Cic. Neque fando unquam accedit quisquam. Neque usquam fictum, neque pictum, neque scriptum in poëmatis, &c. Plaut.
units.tr: Unheard of: unheard of in all memory. Not even heard of by report. Done with no precedent, Cic. Unheard of by report, Plin. Unremembered, Lucr. A crime without precedent, Sen. Of unprecedented novelty, Cic. Nor does anyone ever approach by report. Nor is anything fictional or painted or written in poems, etc., Plaut.

units.la: Inaugurare aliquem sacris] Initiare aliquem. Initiare aliquem sacris. Augustè sanctéque aliquem consecrare. Deorum religione aliquem consecrare, Cic. Creare sacerdotem, Liv. Vid. Consecrare.
units.tr: To consecrate someone with sacred rites: to initiate someone. To initiate someone into sacred rites. To consecrate someone reverently and solemnly. To consecrate someone with the sanctity of the gods, Cic. To create a priest, Liv. See To consecrate.

units.la: Inaurare] Aurare, Sipont. Incoquere alicui rei aurum, Plin. Illinere aurum tectis, Sen.
units.tr: To gild: to gild, Sipontinus. To pour gold onto something, Plin. To smear gold on roofs, Sen.

units.la: Inauratus] Auratus currus, Cic. Obauratus, Apul. Aureolus. Auro similis, Varr. Imbracteatus auro, Amm. Contactus ab auro, Ovid. Auratilis pulviculus, Solin. Circumlitus auro, Ovid Subæratus, Perf. Subauratus annulus, Petron. Incrustatus auro.
units.tr: Gilded: a gilded chariot, Cic. Overgilded, Apul. Golden-like. Like gold, Varro. Covered with gold leaf, Ammianus. Touched by gold, Ovid. Gold-dusted, Solinus. Smeared with gold, Ovid. Gilded with bronze, Persius. Gilded ring, Petronius. Encrusted with gold.

units.la: Inauspicatò, vid. Infeliciter.
units.tr: Inauspicato, see Unluckily.

units.la: Incantare] Cantare, Virg. Sacra facere, Ovid. Malum carmen occentare, Plin. Devotare fortes, Plaut. Sopire magicis artibus.
units.tr: Incantare: to chant, Virg. To perform sacred rites, Ovid. To sing an evil charm, Plin. To doom the brave, Plaut. To lull to sleep by magic arts.

units.la: Incantatio] Incantamenta carminum, Plin. Carmina & devotiones aliaque maleficia, Tac. Indigitamenta, Fest. Deliramenta, Liv. Zoroastræi susurri, Prud. Præcantatio, Quint. Incentio, Amm. Vota nefaria. Vid. Venificium.
units.tr: Incantatio: charms, Plin. Songs, curses and other sorceries, Tac. Invocations, Fest. Ravings, Liv. Zoroastrian whisperings, Prud. Preliminary charming, Quint. Enchantment, Amm. Wicked vows. See Witchcraft.

units.la: Incautè, incautus, vid. Inconsideratè, inconsideratus, improvidè.
units.tr: Incautè, incautus: see Inconsiderately, inconsiderate, improvidently.

units.la: Incedere] Ire bene comitatum. Inferre se in templum, Cic. Agere se, Plaut. Molli incessu suspendere gradum, Sen. Ducere se, Ter. Junonium ingredi, Athen.
units.tr: Incedere: to go with a good escort. To enter a temple, Cic. To conduct oneself, Plaut. To pause with a soft gait, Sen. To lead oneself, Ter. To walk in the manner of Juno, Athen.

units.la: Incendere] Incendium facere, excitare. Ignes Capitolio injicere, inflammare naves, templum; inflammationem inferre urbibus, inferre tectis faces, ignes. Jactare accensas faces. Offerre incendium, Cic. Ignis immissus, Sen. Succendere, Cic.
units.tr: Incendere: to make a fire, to kindle one. To set the Capitol alight; to set ships and a temple on fire; to bring conflagration upon cities, to put torches to roofs and fires. To hurl burning torches. To offer a fire, Cic. A fire let loose, Sen. To set alight, Cic.

units.la: Incendiarius] Incensor messium, Vlp.
units.tr: Incendiarius: one who sets fire to the harvests, Ulp.

units.la: Incendium] Incensio urbis, Cic. Ignis immissus, Sen.
units.tr: Incendium: the burning of a city, Cic. A fire let loose, Sen.

units.la: Incendium restinguere] Vulcanum compescere. Alimenta ignis dissipare.
units.tr: Incendium restinguere: to subdue Vulcan. To scatter the fuel of a fire.

units.la: Incertitudo] Incertum, Cic. Incertum salutis, Apul. Alea, Paul. Pomp. IC.
units.tr: Incertitudo: uncertainty. Something uncertain, Cic. Uncertainty of safety, Apul. A gamble, Paul. Pomp. IC.

units.la: Incertò] Incertè, Gell. In incerto sita res. Per nebulam scire, Plaut. Per caliginem cernere, Cic.
units.tr: Incertò: uncertainly, Gell. The matter lies in doubt. To know through a mist, Plaut. To discern through darkness, Cic.

units.la: Incertum est] In incerto sita res est. Nescias cui credas, Plaut. Haeret haec res, Id. In disquisitionem venit, Liv. In disquisitione positum est, ad Her. Auctoritate id semper eguit. Nescitur utrum, an, Cic. Non traditur, Plin. Non satis mihi liquet. Parum mihi liquet. Minùs compertum habeo, Er.
units.tr: Incertum est: the matter lies in doubt. You would not know whom to trust, Plaut. This matter sticks, Id. It comes into question, Liv. It is placed under inquiry, ad Her. It has always lacked authority. It is not known whether it is so, or not, Cic. It is not handed down, Plin. I am not quite clear about it. I have little clear understanding of it. I have less certain knowledge of it, Er.

units.la: Incertus] Infida pax. Ambiguus favor, fides. Vanus auctor, Liv. Perincertus, Sal. Dubius rumor, Plin. Iun. Levisidus, Plaut. Vagi nominis est Ambrosio, & circa alias herbas fluctuantis, Plin.
units.tr: Incertus: an unfaithful peace. A wavering favour, loyalty. An unreliable author, Liv. Very uncertain, Sal. A doubtful rumour, Plin. Iun. Fickle, Plaut. The name "ambrosia" is vague and wavers among other herbs, Plin.

units.la: Incessus, vid. Ambulatio.
units.tr: Incessus: see Walking.

units.la: Incessus tolutarius] Glomeratio crurum mollis, Plin. Tolutilis gradus, Varr.
units.tr: Incessus tolutarius: a soft swaying of the legs, Plin. A trotting step, Varr.

units.la: Incessus tardus] Grallatorius, aut testudineus gradus, Plaut.
units.tr: Incessus tardus: a stilted or tortoise-like step, Plaut.

units.la: Incestare] Incesto flagitio aliquem polluere, Cic.
units.tr: Incestare: to defile someone with an incestuous disgrace, Cic.

units.la: Incestus] Incestum, Non. Sanguis mistus, Lucan.
units.tr: Incestus: incest, Non. Mixed blood, Lucan.

units.la: Incestuosus] Incestae virilitatis homo, Tac. Incestus, Cic. Incestificus, Sen.
units.tr: Incestuosus: a man of incestuous manhood, Tac. Incestuous, Cic. Causing incest, Sen.

units.la: Inchoare, vid. Incipere.
units.tr: Inchoare: see Begin.

units.la: Incidere, in aliquid cadere] Decidere in, Plaut. In plagas cervus cecidit, Ovid. Delabi in flumen, in morbum. Incurrere in fraudem, irruere in malum. Venire, devenire, pervenire in manus alicujus. Conjicere se in plagas. Inducere se in laqueos, Cic. Labi in adulationem, Tac. Praecipitari in insidias, Lucr. Illabi, Cic.
units.tr: Incidere, to fall upon something: to fall down into, Plaut. The stag fell into the nets, Ovid. To slip into a river, into sickness. To run into deceit, to rush into evil. To come, or arrive, into someone's hands. To throw oneself into snares. To lead oneself into nooses, Cic. To slide into flattery, Tac. To be hurled headlong into ambushes, Lucr. To glide in, Cic.

units.la: Incidit in hoc tempus] Incidunt in eum diem mysteria. Solutio cadit in eum diem. Ea res in eum diem incurrit, Sic.
units.tr: Incidit in hoc tempus: the mysteries fall on that day. The settlement falls on that day. That matter falls on that day, Sic.

units.la: Incidere] Insecare olivam, Col. Fisficulare, Apul. Infindere, Virg.
units.tr: Incidere: to cut into an olive tree, Col. To split, Apul. To cleave, Virg.

units.la: Inceptio] Susceptio. Commissio, Cic. Aggressus, Firm. Prima operis aggressio, Bud.
units.tr: Inceptio: an undertaking. A taking up, Cic. An attempt, Firm. The first beginning of a work, Bud.

units.la: Inceptio cantionis] Præcentio, Cic. Incentio, Gell.
units.tr: Inceptio cantionis: the leading of a song, Cic. A start to singing, Gell.

units.la: Incipere] Inceptare. Occipere, Ter. Incipissere, Plaut. Inchoare. Ordiri altius, à capite. Exordium ducere, sumere, dare. Principia ducere. A diis immortalibus sunt nobis agendi capienda primordia, Cic. Initium facere, ducere, dare, capere, Quint. Capessere principium, Tac. Facere principium. Inire prælium. Ciere pugnam. Committere ludos, Liv. Aggredi dicere, ad dicendum. Ingredi disputationem. Instituere, suscipere aliquid, Cic. Auspicari, Plin. Indipisci pugnam, Gell. Exordiri telam. Ponere initium, Cic.
units.tr: Incipere: to make a beginning. To begin, Ter. To begin, Plaut. To start, to take up. To begin from higher up, from the head. To take up a beginning, to make a start, to give one. To make a beginning: "From the immortal gods we must take the first beginnings of our undertakings," Cic. To make a beginning, to lead off, to give one, to take one, Quint. To seize the beginning, Tac. To make a beginning. To enter battle. To raise a battle. To open the games, Liv. To begin to speak, for speaking. To enter upon a discussion. To undertake, to take up something, Cic. To begin with auspices, Plin. To join battle, Gell. To begin a web. To lay down a beginning, Cic.

units.la: Incipere canere] Incinere, inceptare canere, Gell. Inceptare cum aliquo, Ter. Præcipere. Præire voce alicui, Cic. Auspicatus est cantare, Suet.
units.tr: Incipere canere: to begin to sing. To begin to sing, to start singing, Gell. To begin singing with someone, Ter. To lead with one's voice before another, Cic. He began to sing under good auspices, Suet.

units.la: Incipit, vid. Oritur.
units.tr: Incipit: see It rises.

units.la: Incitamentum] Incitabulum, Gell. Suscitabulum. Protelum. Delectatio protelum ad discendum, Varr. Celeuma, Hieron. Celeusma, Mart Irritamentum. Incentivum belli, Plin. Iun. Irritamen, Ovid. Invitamentum, illicium, illecebra. Pabulum. Stimulus. Calcar. Tuba belli, Bellicum. Fax seditionis, Cic. Fomes ingenii, Gell. Concitamentum, Sen. Thyrsus. Thyrso laudis percutere, Lucr.
units.tr: Incitamentum: an incentive. A spur, Gell. A stimulus. A lure. A delight that leads to learning, Varr. A shout of encouragement, Hieron. The same, Mart. An incitement. An incentive to war, Plin. Iun. A provocation, Ovid. An invitation, an enticement, an allurement. Fodder. A goad. A spur. A trumpet of war, a war-cry. A torch of sedition, Cic. Tinder for the wit, Gell. An incitement, Sen. A thyrsus. To strike with the thyrsus of praise, Lucr.

units.la: Incitare] Suscitare, exsuscitare, exciere, excitare. Impellere. Dare vel injicere alicui mentem. Inflammare, præferre facem ad aliquid. Addere alacritatem. Admovere calcar, stimulos alicui. Bellicum canere. Ventilare concionem flabello seditionis, Cic. Accendere, addere faces flagrantibus militum animis, Tacit. Addere ardorem mentibus, Virg. Addere alas. Inspirare occultum ignem, Id. Injicere ardorem. Acuere animos, Liv. Proritare, Plin. Sufflare aliquem, exstimulare dictis, Ovid. Subjicere faces.
units.tr: Incitare: to rouse, to rouse up, to stir up, to excite, to arouse. To impel. To give or put a mind into someone. To inflame, to bring a torch to something. To add eagerness. To apply spurs or goads to someone. To sound the war-trumpet. To stir up an assembly with the fan of sedition, Cic. To kindle and add torches to the blazing minds of soldiers, Tac. To add ardour to minds, Virg. To add wings. To breathe in a hidden fire, Id. To inject ardour. To sharpen minds, Liv. To urge on, Plin. To puff someone up, to goad with words, Ovid. To put torches beneath.

units.la: Incitatio] Invitatio, invitatus, impulsio, impulsus. Motus animorum, Cic. Instigatus, Vlp. Instinctus, Plin. Stimulatio, Tac.
units.tr: Incitatio: an invitation, an incitement, an urging. A stirring of spirits, Cic. An instigation, Ulp. An instinct, Plin. A stimulation, Tac.

units.la: Incitator ] Instinctor, concitor belli, Tacit. Concitator & stimulator. Impulsor. Fax incendiorum, Cic. Irritator, Sen. Incensor, incentor belli, Amm. Iustin. Incentivus, Firmic.
units.tr: Incitator: an instigator, one who stirs up war, Tac. An agitator and stimulator. An impeller. A torch of fires, Cic. An irritator, Sen. An inciter of war, Amm. Iustin. An incentive, Firmic.

units.la: Incitatus, vid. Agilis.
units.tr: Incitatus: see Nimble.

units.la: Incivilis, vid. Inurbanus.
units.tr: Incivilis: see Unmannerly.

units.la: Inclamare ] Inclamitare. Occlamitare alicui. Clamore hominem poscere, Plaut. Clamore insequi, Cic. Persona-re aurem alicui, Hor. Accipere aliquem clamore, Liv.
units.tr: Inclamare: to shout at. To cry out at, to shout at someone. To demand a man with a shout, Plaut. To pursue with clamour, Cic. To sound in someone's ear, Hor. To greet someone with a shout, Liv.

units.la: Inclementer, vid Crudeliter.
units.tr: Inclementer: see Cruelly.

units.la: Inclinare] Propendere inclinatione voluntatis in aliquid. Incumbere ad bonitatem. Demittere se ad, Cic. Inclinare animum ad rem aliquem. Inclinare in hoc consilium, Liv. Proclinari, Col. Vergere ad imum, Hor. Acclinare se ad aliquem, Ovid.
units.tr: Inclinare: to lean towards something, to incline by the bent of the will. To lean towards goodness. To bend oneself down to, Cic. To incline one's mind to a matter. To incline to this plan, Liv. To lean forward, Col. To slope down to the bottom, Hor. To lean towards someone, Ovid.

units.la: Inclinatio Flexus aetatis. Nutus, Cic. Proclinatio structurae, Vitr. Devergentia. Declinatio mundi, Gell. Devexitas, loci, Plin. Iun. Inflexio, flexio laterum, Cic. Deflexus, Col.
units.tr: Inclinatio: the bending of age. A nod, Cic. A leaning forward of a structure, Vitr. A downward slope. The tilt of the world, Gell. The descent of a place, Plin. Iun. A bending, a bending of the sides, Cic. A deflection, Col.

units.la: Inclinatus] Proclinatus, Vitr. Deflexa aetas. Proclivis, Cic. Pronus ad meridiem locus, Varr.
units.tr: Inclinatus: leaning forward. Advanced in age. Sloping, Cic. A place sloping towards the south, Varr.

units.la: Inclytus, vid. Celebris.
units.tr: Inclytus: see Famous.

units.la: Incoctus, i, non coctus] Semicoctus, Semicrudus, Col.
units.tr: Incoctus, not cooked: half-cooked, half-raw, Col.

units.la: Incaenatus] Incaenis, Plaut.
units.tr: Incaenatus: having not dined, Plaut.

units.la: Incogitans, vid. Inconsideratus.
units.tr: Incogitans: see Inconsiderate.

units.la: Incogitanter] Incogitato animo, Plaut.
units.tr: Incogitanter: with an unthinking mind, Plaut.

units.la: Incogitantia] Temeritas, inconsulta ratio, Cic. Praecipitantia. Praecipitatio, Sen.
units.tr: Incogitantia: rashness, unadvised reasoning, Cic. Headlong haste. Precipitation, Sen.

units.la: Incognitus, vid. Ignotus.
units.tr: Incognitus: see Unknown.

units.la: Incola] Habitator, Cic. Inhabitator, Vlp. Viri loci, Ovid. Diique virique loci succurrite.
units.tr: Incola: an inhabitant, Cic. A dweller, Ulp. The men of the place, Ovid. "Gods and men of this place, come to our aid."

units.la: Incolere, vid. Habitare.
units.tr: Incolere: see Dwell.

units.la: Incolumis, vid. Sanus.
units.tr: Incolumis: see Sound.

units.la: Incommodare, vid. Impedire.
units.tr: Incommodare: see Hinder.

units.la: Incommodatio] Incommodum, Cic.
units.tr: Incommodatio: inconvenience, Cic.

units.la: Incommode] Alieno, alienissimo, adverso tempore aliquid agere. In alienissimum tempus adventus meus cadet. Im-portuportunè. Intempestivè, Cic. Advorsum tempori venire> Plaut. Perincommodum est id mihi, Liv.
units.tr: Incommode: to do something at an inconvenient, most unsuitable or adverse time. My arrival will fall at the most inconvenient time. Importunately, unseasonably. Untimely, Cic. To come at an adverse time, Plaut. This is most inconvenient for me, Liv.

units.la: Incommodus] Perincommodus, Liv. Importunus, Cic.
units.tr: Incommodus: very inconvenient, Liv. Importunate, Cic.

units.la: Incompti capilli] Incomptum caput, Hor. Horridæ comæ, Iuv. Sine lege capilli; scissi. Soluti crines. Disjecta comas fœmina; Resoluta capillos. Neglecta coma, Ovid. Nulla lege jacens coma, Sen. Dederat comas diffundere ventis, Virg. Sparsus humeris capillus, Hor. Capillus horrore implexus, Apul. Impexus, Scal.
units.tr: Incompti capilli: an unkempt head, Hor. Bristling locks, Juv. Hair without order, torn. Loose tresses. A woman with hair scattered and unbound. Neglected hair, Ovid. Hair lying in no order, Sen. She had let her locks stream to the winds, Virg. Hair sprinkled over the shoulders, Hor. Hair entangled with horror, Apul. Uncombed, Scal.

units.la: Inconsiderantia] Irrationabilitas bonorum hominum, Apul. Imprudentia, inconsulta ratio, inconsideratissima temeritas. Cupiditas inconsiderata, Cic. Inconsulta amentia, Quint.
units.tr: Inconsiderantia: the unreasonableness of good men, Apul. Thoughtlessness, unadvised reasoning, most inconsiderate rashness. Unconsidered desire, Cic. Unadvised madness, Quint.

units.la: Inconsideratè] Inconsultè procedere, Sal. Incogitato animo, Plaut. De summo pectore dicere, Gell. Nullo consilio, sine judicio, & modo facere aliquid, Cic.
units.tr: Inconsideratè: to proceed without counsel, Sal. With an unthinking mind, Plaut. To speak from the top of the breast, Gell. To do something without plan, without judgement and without measure, Cic.

units.la: Inconsideratus] Incautus, Cic. Inconsultus homo. Præceps consiliis. Cœci consules. Nunc demum scio me fuisse excordem, cœcum, incogitabilem, Id. Incogitans, Ter. Incogitatus, Plaut.
units.tr: Inconsideratus: heedless, Cic. An ill-advised man. Headlong in counsels. Blind consuls. "Now at last I know that I was senseless, blind and unthinking," Id. Not thinking, Ter. Unconsidered, Plaut.

units.la: Inconstans] Volubilis. Mobilis, Vacillans animus. Ventosus homo. Fluxus. Pluma & folio facilius movetur, Cic. Instabilis. Ambiguus, Plin. Diversus animi, Tac. Incertus sui, Sen. Desultorius, Bud. Miscellio, Fest. Profluviâ fide homo, Priscian. Animo nunc huc, nunc fluctuat illuc. Nihil ipsi constantius inconstantiâ. Claudicat claudicans utroque. Aliud stans, aliud sedens. Amicitia desultoria. Amicitia, quæ desiit, nunquam vera fuit. Cœpisti melius, quàm desinis. Cardine versatilior. Chamæleonte mutabilior. Cothurno versatilior. Euripus homo. Hydrâ magis varius Pilâ volubilior. Turbine versatilior. Cortice levior. Plumâ levior, subere, ramento levior. Vento instabilior. Vertumno inconstantior, Er. Versatilior quàm rota sigulatis, Plaut.
units.tr: Inconstans: fickle. A mobile, wavering mind. A windy man. Fluid. A feather and a leaf are moved more easily, Cic. Unstable. Ambiguous, Plin. Of divided mind, Tac. Uncertain of himself, Sen. Restless, Bud. A mixed-up thing, Fest. A man of flowing faith, Priscian. Now he leans here, now he wavers there in his mind. Nothing is more constant than inconstancy itself. He limps, limping on both feet. Standing for one thing, sitting for another. A desultory friendship. A friendship that ceases was never true. You began better than you end. More turning than a hinge. More changeable than a chameleon. More turning than a buskin. A man like the Euripus. More varied than the Hydra. More spinning than a ball. More whirling than a whirlwind. Lighter than bark. Lighter than a feather, cork, or wood shaving. Less stable than the wind. More inconstant than Vertumnus, Er. More turning than a wheel on a lathe, Plaut.

units.la: Inconstantem esse] De statu demigrare. De toga ad palium. Polypi mentem obtincre.
units.tr: Inconstantem esse: to move away from one's station. From the gown to the cloak. To take on the mind of a polyp.

units.la: Inconstantia] Instabilitas, Plin. Volubilitas fortunæ.
units.tr: Inconstantia: instability, Plin. The fickleness of fortune.

units.la: Mobilitas & levitas hominis. Vanitas, Cic. Levitas mentis, Sil.
units.tr: The mobility and levity of a man. Vanity, Cic. Lightness of mind, Sil.

units.la: Inconsulte] Inconsultò. Temerè, imprudenter aliquid facere, Cic. Vid. Temerè.
units.tr: Inconsulte: without deliberation. To do something rashly or carelessly, Cic. See Rashly.

units.la: Inconsultus] Qui nullo consilio aliquid administrat. Expers consilii, Cic. Inopiosæ res consilii, Plaut.
units.tr: Inconsultus: one who manages something without any plan. Lacking counsel, Cic. Matters that are without counsel, Plaut.

units.la: Incontaminatus] Intaminatus, Hor. Impollutus, Sil. Integer, Virg. Illutus pes, Arnob.
units.tr: Incontaminatus] Untainted, Hor. Unpolluted, Sil. Whole, Virg. A foot unsoiled, Arnob.

units.la: Incontinens] Impotens amoris, Tac. Intemperans in alicujus rei cupiditate, Cic. Dolio pertuso licentiosior. Acolastus, Gell. Projecta & effrenata cupiditas, Cic.
units.tr: Incontinens] Mastered by love, Tac. Intemperate in the desire for something, Cic. More unrestrained than a leaking cask; Acolastus, Gell. Headlong and unbridled desire, Cic.

units.la: Incontinenter] Intemperanter. Effrenatè, Cic. Impotenter, Liv. Insedabiliter sitis urit corpora, Lucr.
units.tr: Incontinenter] Intemperately. Unbridledly, Cic. Without restraint, Liv. Thirst burns bodies insatiably, Lucr.

units.la: Incontinentia] Impotentia animi. Intemperantia, Cic.
units.tr: Incontinentia] Lack of self-control of mind. Intemperance, Cic.

units.la: Inconveniens] Incongruens aliquid alicui, Gell. Ineptus, Cic.
units.tr: Inconveniens] Not agreeing with something for someone, Gell. Unfitting, Cic.

units.la: Inconventia] Calceus major pede. Cum Cerdone inepto parvo pedi magnum inducere calceum. Vid. Inepta agere.
units.tr: Inconventia] A shoe bigger than the foot. To put a big shoe on a small foot, as with the fool Cerdo. See Inepta agere.

units.la: Incorporeus] Incorporalis, Sen. Quint. Expers corporis. Nullius corporis est Deus, Cic.
units.tr: Incorporeus] Incorporeal, Sen. Quint. Free of body. God is of no body, Cic.

units.la: Incorrupte] Incorruptiùs judicare, Cic. Vid. Justè.
units.tr: Incorrupte] To judge more incorruptly, Cic. See Juste.

units.la: Incorruptus] Integer, Ter. Illibatus, intactus, Liv. Infractus, Plin. Illæsus, Stat. Sanctum jus. Sana Resp. Salvus. Virgo, Philosophia, virtus indepravata, Cic. Constat pietasque fidesque, Sen. Aristide incorruptior, Eras.
units.tr: Incorruptus] Whole, Ter. Unblemished and untouched, Liv. Unbroken, Plin. Unharmed, Stat. Inviolable law. Sound state. Safe. A virgin; philosophy; undefiled virtue, Cic. Integrity and faithfulness endure, Sen. More incorruptible than Aristides, Erasm.

units.la: Incredibilis, e, est] Absurdum & incredibile. Nihil mihi unquam tam incredibile accidit, quàm, &c. Hoc omnibus incredibile, & falsò memoriæ proditum. Aliquis tibi ex inferis excitandus est, qui hæc approbet, Cic. Difficile ad credendum. Procul est (non est) ut credere possis, Lucr. Difficile ad fidem. Fidei absonum, Liv. Fide caret, Ovid. Fidem excedit. Respuit hoc sapientissimi cujusque fides, Plin. Etiamsi Cato dicat. Fando inauditum.
units.tr: Incredibilis, e, est] Absurd and incredible. Nothing ever happened to me so incredible as, etc. This is incredible to everyone and falsely handed down to memory. Someone must be raised from the dead for you, who would approve these things, Cic. Hard to believe. It is far (not) possible for you to believe, Lucr. Hard to trust. Discordant with faith, Liv. Lacking credit, Ovid. Exceeds belief. The faith of the wisest of every kind rejects this, Plin. Even if Cato says so. Unheard of by report.

units.la: Incredulitas, vid. Diffidentia.
units.tr: Incredulitas, see Diffidentia.

units.la: Incredulus] Incredibilis, Apul. Diffidens, Cic. Ne genio quidem credit suo, Plaut.
units.tr: Incredulus] Incredible, Apul. Distrustful, Cic. He does not even trust his own genius, Plaut.

units.la: Incrementum, vid. Augmentum.
units.tr: Incrementum, see Augmentum.

units.la: Increpare] Increpitare aliquem moræ, Sil. Incusare vehementer aliquem, Cæs. Incessere monitis aliquem, Sil. Cantare alicui ocyma, Perf. Lucilius urbem defricuit sale multo, Hor. Confricare servos injuriis ac criminationibus imperiosis, Gell. Os tuum ferreum Senatus convicio verberari voluisti, Cic. in Pison. Accipere aliquem malè vehementer, Cic. Vid. Objurgare.
units.tr: Increpare] To chide someone for delay, Sil. To accuse someone vehemently, Caes. To assail someone with warnings, Sil. To sing ocyma to someone, Pers. Lucilius rubbed the city down with much salt, Hor. To rub down slaves with injuries and imperious accusations, Gell. You wished your iron face to be battered with the reproach of the Senate, Cic. in Pison. To receive someone very badly, Cic. See Objurgare.

units.la: Incruentus, vid. Exsanguis.
units.tr: Incruentus, see Exsanguis.

units.la: Incrustare] Sincerum vas incrustare, Hor. Trulissare. Inducere parieti marmor. Nucleum inducere (pavimento) Ruderare pavimentum, Vitr. Loricare parietes marmorato, opere tectorio, Varr. Albarii operis nitore decorare. Frequentare inductionem, Pallad.
units.tr: Incrustare] To encrust a clean vessel, Hor. To plaster with a trowel. To lay marble on a wall. To lay a floor of rubble-work. To pave the floor with rubble, Vitr. To line walls with marble and with stucco work, Varr. To adorn with the gleam of whitewashed work. To apply the coating frequently, Pallad.

units.la: Incrustatio] Loricatio pavimenti. Trulissatio. Ruderatio. Directio è grano marmoreo. Directura exarenato, Vitruv. Inductio parietis, inductio calcis, grani marmoris, Pallad.
units.tr: Incrustatio] Lining of a pavement. Plastering with a trowel. Rubble-work. A layer of marble grain. A plastered surface of sand, Vitruv. The laying of a wall, of lime, of marble grain, Pallad.

units.la: Incubare ovis] Incubare, abs. Incubare fœtibus. Excubant gallinæ, Col. Sedet in ovis polypus. Fovent ova volucres, Plin.
units.tr: Incubare ovis] To brood, used absolutely. To brood over the young. Hens sit on their eggs, Col. The octopus sits on its eggs. Birds warm their eggs, Plin.

units.la: Incubatio] Incubitio, incubitus, incubatus, cubatio gallinæ, Plin.
units.tr: Incubatio] Incubition, incubitus, incubatus: a hen's brooding, Plin.

units.la: Incubus] Faunorum ludibria. Suppressio nocturna, Plin. Ephialtes, Macr. Incubo, Serv. Genius salax, Lipf.
units.tr: Incubus] The mockeries of the Fauns. Nocturnal suppression, Plin. Ephialtes, Macr. Incubo, Serv. A lustful genius, Lipsius.

units.la: Inculpatus] Candidus. Abest à reprehensione, Cic. Irreprehensibilis, Firm. Irreprehensus, Ovid.
units.tr: Inculpatus] Spotless. Free from reproach, Cic. Irreproachable, Firm. Not reproached, Ovid.

units.la: Incultus, vid. Inaratus.
units.tr: Incultus, see Inaratus.

units.la: Incultus, transl.] Impolitus, inconcinnus, inornatus, inven ustus actor. Subhorridus & incultus. Barbarus servus. Verrucosus orator. Rusticanus. Vastus & Agrestis in vultu motuque corporis, Cic. Crassior Musa, incompositis moribus, Quint. Vid. Barbarus.
units.tr: Incultus, transl.] Unpolished, unrefined, unadorned; an actor without grace. Somewhat rough and uncultivated. A barbarous slave. A warty orator. Rustic. Coarse and rural in look and bodily movement, Cic. A Muse too rough, with uncouth manners, Quint. See Barbarus.

units.la: Incuria] Non curantia, Cic. Omissus animus, Ter. Negligentia, Cic. Supina negligentia, Mart. Iuv.
units.tr: Incuria] Not caring, Cic. A neglected mind, Ter. Negligence, Cic. Lazy negligence, Mart. Juv.

units.la: Incuriosus] Expers curæ, Liv. Socors futuri, Tac. Nullarum rerum candidatus est, Sen. Negligens sui, Id. Instudiosus alicujus rei, Apul. Vid. Negligens.
units.tr: Incuriosus] Free of care, Liv. Careless of the future, Tac. He is a candidate for nothing, Sen. Negligent of himself, Id. Uninterested in something, Apul. See Negligens.

units.la: Incuriosus sui nec Deo est cura] Qui domi suæ complui-tur, ejus ne Deum miseret.
units.tr: Incuriosus sui nec Deo est cura] He whose own house lets in the rain, God does not pity him.

units.la: Incurrere] Introrumpere, Ter.
units.tr: Incurrere] To rush in, Ter.

units.la: Incursio, vid. Invasio.
units.tr: Incursio, see Invasio.

units.la: Incurvare, vid Curvare & Pandari.
units.tr: Incurvare, see Curvare & Pandari.

units.la: Indagare] Vestigare. Pervestigare, Cic. Premere alicujus vestigia, Tac. Stringit canis leporis vestigia, Ovid. Instare vestigiis. Persequi aliquem ipsius vestigiis. Insistere in vestigium alicujus, Cic. Sequi vestigia, Quint. Scrutari vestigia alicujus, Plin.
units.tr: Indagare] To track. To trace out thoroughly, Cic. To press upon someone's tracks, Tac. The dog follows the hare's trail closely, Ovid. To press on the footsteps. To pursue someone in his very footsteps. To step into someone's footprint, Cic. To follow the traces, Quint. To search out someone's tracks, Plin.

units.la: Indagatio] Pervestigatio, Cic. Indago, Plin. Vid. Inquisitio.
units.tr: Indagatio] Thorough tracing, Cic. A hunting net, Plin. See Inquisitio.

units.la: Indagator] Vestigator, Col. Indagatrix, investigator, Cic. Ichnobates, Ovid. Quæsitor ferarum canis, Non.
units.tr: Indagator] Tracker, Col. Female investigator, Cic. Ichnobates, Ovid. A dog that seeks out game, Non.

units.la: Inde, vid. Illinc.
units.tr: Inde, see Illinc.

units.la: Indecens] Indecorus, inconveniens factum, Cic. Dedecorus, Plaut. Indignus, Ter.
units.tr: Indecens] Unbecoming; an unseemly deed, Cic. Disgraceful, Plaut. Unworthy, Ter.

units.la: Indecenter] Indecorè, indignè, illiberaliter, Cic. Irreverenter, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Indecenter] Unbecomingly, unworthily, illiberally, Cic. Irreverently, Plin. Jun.

units.la: Indecentia] Indignitatem rei exponere, Cic.
units.tr: Indecentia] To set forth the unworthiness of a matter, Cic.

units.la: Indemnis] Innoxius à pecoribus, Col. Illæsus evasit, Sen. Innocuus, Virg. Nunquam obnoxius, Plin. Indemnitati consulens, Vlp.
units.tr: Indemnis] Unharmed by cattle, Col. Escaped unhurt, Sen. Harmless, Virg. Never liable, Plin. Looking to indemnity, Ulp.

units.la: Indicare] Monstrare aliquid indice, digito, Hor. Digitum intendere ad frontem. Enunciare mysteria alicui, Cic. Indicio ipse de se erit, Ter. Per indicium enunciata res, Cas.
units.tr: Indicare] To show something by a sign or finger, Hor. To point a finger at the forehead. To disclose mysteries to someone, Cic. He will be the informer about himself, Ter. A matter disclosed through information, Cas.

units.la: Indicare pretium, vid. Pretium.
units.tr: Indicare pretium, see Pretium.

units.la: Indicatio, vid. Proditio.
units.tr: Indicatio, see Proditio.

units.la: Indicere, vid. Edicere.
units.tr: Indicere, see Edicere.

units.la: Indicium] Oculi indices animi. Argumentum accipere certissimum. Significatio virtutis, Cic. Insignia morbi, Hor. Vid. Signum.
units.tr: Indicium] The eyes are indicators of the mind. To receive the most certain proof. A sign of virtue, Cic. The symptoms of a disease, Hor. See Signum.

units.la: Index libri] Elenchus, Plin. Syllabus, Cic.
units.tr: Index libri] Table of contents, Plin. Syllabus, Cic.

units.la: Indifferens] Adiaphorus, Varr. Neutralis, Quint. Medii & neutrius alterius partis homines, Cic. Et benè & male facere tenet. Improbus cum improbis est, bonus bonis. Utcunque res sit, ita animum habet. Eum patinarium vel assum vorses ; quo pacto lubet. Utroque versum rectum est ingenium meum, ad te atque ad illum, Plaut. Pro rota me uti licet ; vel ego huc, vel illuc vertar, quò imperabitis, Id. In utrumque paratus, Virg. Ambiguæ fidei vir, Liv. Nec utilis, nec inutilis.
units.tr: Indifferens] Adiaphorus, Varr. Neutral, Quint. Men of a middle sort, belonging to neither party, Cic. He keeps to both doing good and doing ill. A bad man is with the bad, a good man with the good. However the matter stands, he takes on that disposition. You may turn him like a stew or a roast, whichever way you please. My nature is bent straight both ways, to you and to him, Plaut. I may be used like a wheel: I shall turn here or there, wherever you command, Id. Ready for either, Virg. A man of doubtful loyalty, Liv. Neither useful nor useless.

units.la: Indifferenter] Indiscriminatim, Varr.
units.tr: Indifferenter] Indiscriminately, Varr.

units.la: Indifferentia]In contrarias partes facultas. Adiaphoria, Cic.
units.tr: Indifferentia] The ability to go to opposite sides. Adiaphoria, Cic.

units.la: Indigena] Oriundus hinc, Plaut. Indidem homo, Cic. Hinc civis, Ter.
units.tr: Indigena] Native from here, Plaut. A man from the same place, Cic. A citizen from here, Ter.

units.la: Indigens, indigere, vid. Egenus, egere.
units.tr: Indigens, indigere, see Egenus, egere.

units.la: Indigestio] Cruditas stomachi, Cic. Vid. Concoctu difficile.
units.tr: Indigestio] Upset of the stomach, Cic. See Concoctu difficile.

units.la: Indigestus prop.] Indistinctus, Quint.
units.tr: Indigestus prop.] Undistinguished, Quint.

units.la: Indigestus cibus] Inconsumptus, Ovid.
units.tr: Indigestus cibus] Unconsumed, Ovid.

units.la: Indignari] Indignè ferre, pati aliquid, Cic. Indignissimè ferre, Capit. Labra movere, Aristop. Inflare buccas, Hor. Atrociter ferre.
units.tr: Indignari] To bear with indignation, to suffer something, Cic. To bear it most indignantly, Capit. To move the lips, Aristoph. To puff out the cheeks, Hor. To bear fiercely.

units.la: Indignanter, vid Iracundè.
units.tr: Indignanter, see Iracunde.

units.la: Indignè] Aliquem non pro dignitate ejus tractare, Cic.
units.tr: Indigne] To treat someone not according to his dignity, Cic.

units.la: Indignè ferre, vid. Sinistrè accipere.
units.tr: Indigne ferre, see Sinistre accipere.

units.la: Indignus] Tanto nato indignissimus, Stat. Non dignus, Ter. Ligula non dignus. Ne crepitu quidem digiti dignum.
units.tr: Indignus] Most unworthy of so great a son, Stat. Not worthy, Ter. Not worth a shoelace. Not worth even the snap of a finger.

units.la: Indiligens, vid. Negligens.
units.tr: Indiligens, see Negligens.

units.la: Indiligenter, vid. Negligenter.
units.tr: Indiligenter, see Negligenter.

units.la: Indiscretus] Indiscretæ similitudinis effigies. Indiscreta propè specie similes, Plin. Promiscuus, Liv.
units.tr: Indiscretus] The image of an indistinguishable likeness. Almost alike in appearance, Plin. Promiscuous, Liv.

units.la: Indisertus] Ineloquens, Lact. Infacundus, Liv. Strigosus orator. Jejunus, jejunior in orationibus. Infans. Nihil illo infantius, infantissimus. Elinguis, Cic.
units.tr: Indisertus] Not eloquent, Lact. Inarticulate, Liv. A meagre orator. Dry, drier in speeches. Infant-like. Nothing more infantile than that, most infantile. Tongue-tied, Cic.

units.la: Indispositè, indispositus, vid. Inordinate, inordinatus.
units.tr: Indispositè, indispositus, see Inordinate, inordinatus.

units.la: Indissolubilis] Insolubilis, indivulsus comes, Macrob. Indissociabilis unitas, Lactant. Continuus, Hor. Velut umbra, quoquo ibis, te sequar, Plaut. Irresolubilis nexus, Amm. Inseparabilis, Priscian.
units.tr: Indissolubilis] Insoluble; an inseparable companion, Macrob. An indissociable unity, Lact. Continuous, Hor. Like a shadow: wherever you go, I will follow you, Plaut. An irresoluble bond, Amm. Inseparable, Prisc.

units.la: Indissolubiliter] Non tenaciter tantùm, sed insolubiliter etiam uniuntur. Quæ inseparabiliter natura vinxit, Macr.
units.tr: Indissolubiliter] They are not only held fast but joined insolubly. What nature has bound inseparably, Macr.

units.la: Indissolutus] Irresolutus, Ovid. Inevolutus, Mart.
units.tr: Indissolutus] Not loosed, Ovid. Unrolled, Mart.

units.la: Indistinctè] Indigestè, Gell. Congestè, Iul. Cap. Permixtè, Promiscuè. Confusè. Confusim, Cic.
units.tr: Indistincte] Undigested, Gell. Heaped together, Jul. Cap. Mixed, promiscuously. Confusedly. In confusion, Cic.

units.la: Indistinctus] Indigestus, Plin.
units.tr: Indistinctus] Undigested, Plin.

units.la: Indivisibilis] Individuus, Cic. Indivisus, Fest.
units.tr: Indivisibilis] Individual, Cic. Undivided, Fest.

units.la: Indivisus] Indiscretus, Sil.
units.tr: Indivisus] Undistinguished, Sil.

units.la: Indere aliquid alicui] Speciem sui clypeo inclusit. Illigare. Cic. Inserere fenestras, Virg. Adindere, Cat. Imprimere tabulam parieti, Plin. Incorporati repagulis funes, Anim.
units.tr: Indere aliquid alicui] He enclosed the likeness of himself in his shield. To bind on, Cic. To insert windows, Virg. To fix to, Cat. To press a tablet against a wall, Plin. Ropes fastened with bars, Anim.

units.la: Indocilis] Obtusa acies animi. Tardus & indocilis. Tardo ingenio. Retusum ingenium. Plumbeus homo, Cic. Hebes homo, ingenium, Acci. Homo naris obesae, Hor. Iners ingenium, Ovid. Stipite tardior. Plumbo stupidior. Caudice stolidior, Er.
units.tr: Indocilis] A blunt edge of mind. Slow and unteachable. Of dull intellect. A blunted wit. A leaden man, Cic. A dull man, a dull mind, Acc. A man with a flat nose, Hor. A sluggish mind, Ovid. Slower than a log. More stupid than lead. More stolid than a stump, Erasm.

units.la: Indocte, vid. Imperte.
units.tr: Indocte, see Imperte.

units.la: Indoctus] Amusus, Vitr. Aversus à Musis. Iners, qui caret arte. Idiota. A doctrina parum instructus, Politioris humanitatis expers, Cic. Ne Æsopum quidem (seu Donatum) trivit. Vid. Illiteratus.
units.tr: Indoctus] Untaught, Vitr. Averse to the Muses. Idle, lacking skill. Ignorant. Poorly instructed in learning, lacking refined culture, Cic. He has not even worn down Aesop (or Donatus). See Illiteratus.

units.la: Indoctus inter doctos] Graculus inter Musas. Anser inter olores.
units.tr: Indoctus inter doctos] A jackdaw among the Muses. A goose among swans.

units.la: Indolentia] Vacuitas, privatio doloris, Cic.
units.tr: Indolentia] Emptiness; absence of pain, Cic.

units.la: Indoles, vid. Ingenium.
units.tr: Indoles, see Ingenium.

units.la: Indomitus, vid. Immansuetus.
units.tr: Indomitus, see Immansuetus.

units.la: Indormire] Incumbere lecto, Ovid. Supercubare, Col. Incubare stramentis, Hor. Incubare super tomentum, Sen.
units.tr: Indormire] To lie down on a bed, Ovid. To lie upon, Col. To lie on straw, Hor. To lie on a cushion, Sen.

units.la: Indubitatè, vid. Procul dubio.
units.tr: Indubitate, see Procul dubio.

units.la: Indubitatus] Indubitabilis, Quint. Vid. Certus.
units.tr: Indubitatus] Indubitable, Quint. See Certus.

units.la: Inducere aliquem in aliquod factum] Perducere aliquem in discrimen. Impellere aliquem ad aliquid. Deducere aliquem in fraudem. Illicere conjugem in stuprum, Cic. Adigere aliquem ad suspendium. Perdere capitis aliquem, Plaut. Compellere aliquem ad laqueum, Plin. Conficies filio aliquid mali. Redigere aliquem ad inopiam, Ter. Redigere aliquem ad interitum, Lucr.
units.tr: Inducere aliquem in aliquod factum] To lead someone into danger. To drive someone on to something. To lead someone into fraud. To entice a wife into debauchery, Cic. To drive someone to the noose. To bring someone to the block, Plaut. To force someone to the halter, Plin. You will bring some harm upon your son. To reduce someone to poverty, Ter. To reduce someone to ruin, Lucr.

units.la: Inducia] Belli feriae, Varr. Pax castrensis paucorum dierum, Gell. Pax sequestra, Virg. Feriale officium, Apul.
units.tr: Inducia] Holidays of war, Varr. A camp peace of a few days, Gell. A sequestered peace, Virg. A festal duty, Apul.

units.la: Induere vestem] Induere se veste. Ter. Indui vestem, Plin. Sumere vestem, Ovid. Cic. Superinduere penulam, Suet. Incingi, Ovid.
units.tr: Induere vestem] To put on clothes. To clothe oneself, Ter. To put on clothing, Plin. To take up clothing, Ovid, Cic. To put a cloak on over, Suet. To gird oneself, Ovid.

units.la: Indulgenter] Indulgentissimè, Sen. Molliter. Molli brachio. Leniter. Mansuetè, Cic. Blande, Ter. Mitius ferre aliquid, Ovid. Molli articulo, Quint.
units.tr: Indulgenter] Most indulgently, Sen. Softly. With a soft arm. Leniently. Gently, Cic. Blandly, Ter. To bear something more mildly, Ovid. With a soft joint, Quint.

units.la: Indulgentia] Remissio. Relaxatio. Dissimulatio, Cic.
units.tr: Indulgentia] Remission. Relaxation. Dissimulation, Cic.

units.la: Indulgentia corrumpit pueros] Nocet indulgentia nobis, Ovid. Blanda patrum segnes facit indulgentia natos. Facilitas multa mala docet.
units.tr: Indulgentia corrumpit pueros] Indulgence harms us, Ovid. A father's flattering indulgence makes his sons lazy. Easiness teaches many evils.

units.la: Indulgere] Indulgere alicui, vel aliquem nimis, Sil. Relaxat pater nimis indulgens, quicquid ego adstrinxi. Suffragari alicujus cupiditatibus. Blandiri alicui, Cic. Blandiendo dulce malum nutrit, Sen. Sustentare vitia alicujus, Sal. Permittere licentiam. Lenocinari alicui, Cic. Nimis liberaliter habere aliquem, Sal. Addere blanditias. Agere blanditiis, Ovid. Laxare frena, Lucan. Effundere habenas, Virg. Connivere, Cic.
units.tr: Indulgere] To indulge someone, or to indulge someone too much, Sil. A father who indulges too much undoes whatever I have tightened. To favour someone's desires. To flatter someone, Cic. Sweet flattery nourishes a sweet evil, Sen. To uphold someone's vices, Sall. To allow licence. To pander to someone, Cic. To treat someone too liberally, Sall. To add flattery. To work by flattery, Ovid. To loosen the reins, Lucan. To pour out the reins, Virg. To connive, Cic.

units.la: Indurare] Durare ungulas. Edurare, Col. Condurat ferrum humor, Lucr. Perfolidat imbres Boreas, Stat. Callum alicui obducere. Lapire. Lapit cor cura, Pacuv. i.e. Obdurefacit Non. Obdurare, Hor.
units.tr: Indurare] To harden hooves. To harden thoroughly, Col. Moisture hardens iron, Lucr. Boreas hardens the showers, Stat. To make a callus grow over someone. To harden. Care hardens the heart, Pacuv.; that is, makes it hard, Non. To harden, Hor.

units.la: Indurari, vid. Durescere.
units.tr: Indurari, see Durescere.

units.la: Induratus] Duratus, Liv. Præduratum vas, Plin. Robustus vetustate, Cic.
units.tr: Induratus] Hardened, Liv. A hardened vessel, Plin. Made robust by age, Cic.

units.la: Indurata durant] Frangas potiùs, quàm corrigas, quæ in pravum induruerunt.
units.tr: Indurata durant] Rather break than correct those things that have hardened into wickedness.

units.la: Indusium] Intusium, Non. Indusiata vestis, Plaut. Interrula, Apul. Tunica intima, Gell.
units.tr: Indusium] Intusium, Non. A garment with an undergarment, Plaut. Interula, Apul. An inner tunic, Gell.

units.la: Industria] Virtus ad obeundas res plurimas cum celeritate. Ad res multas aggressio, earumque actio, ex Gell. Negotialis status, Cic.
units.tr: Industria] Vigour in undertaking many tasks quickly. The undertaking of many affairs and their carrying out, from Gell. A busy, business-like condition, Cic.

units.la: De industriâ aliquid agere] Sola industria præstat ut sperare possis indiviam.
units.tr: De industriâ aliquid agere] Industry alone makes it possible to hope for endive.

units.la: Industriè, vid. Ingeniosè.
units.tr: Industriè, see Ingeniosè.

units.la: Industrius] Acer & industrius in rebus agendis. Homo navus. Pragmaticus. Negotii bene gerens, Cic. Strenui, boni, factiosi, Sal. Muret. Rebus agendis natus, Hor. Activus, Quint. Industriosus, Val. Max.
units.tr: Industrius] Keen and industrious in carrying out affairs. A man of energy. Practical. Competent in business, Cic. Vigorous, good, active, Sall., Muret. Born for doing business, Hor. Active, Quint. Industrious, Val. Max.

units.la: Indutus] Vestitissimus, Col. Inebrians , vim inebriandi habens] Vinolenta medicamina , Cicer. Lyncestis aqua , Plin. Lyncesius amnis, Ovid.
units.tr: Indutus] Most clothed, Col. Inebrians , vim inebriandi habens] Intoxicating, having the power to intoxicate: wine-laced medicines, Cic. Lyncestian water, Plin. The Lyncestian river, Ovid.

units.la: Inebriare aliquem ] Deponere aliquem vino. Conficere aliquem poculis, vino. Invitare aliquem magnis poculis. Facere ut sit madidus aliquis, Plaut. Vino sepelivit illum ad somnum. Poculis crebris grandibusque singulos ingurgitat, Apul. Urgere culullis, Hor.
units.tr: Inebriare aliquem] To lay someone low with wine. To finish someone off with cups of wine. To invite someone to large cups. To make someone drunk, Plaut. He put him to sleep with wine. He gulps down each one with frequent large cups, Apul. To press with ladles, Hor.

units.la: Inebriari] Obruere se vino , Cic. Ingurgitare ingenium poculis, Gell. Invitare se largissimè. In multum vini processerunt, Liv. Madere mero, Tib. Vino te devincis, Plaut. Vicit (me) vinum quod bibi. Vino inundamur, Petron. Incaluit quoties saucia vena mero, Mart. Accessit fervor icto capiti, humerusque lucernis, Hor. Incalescere mero. Mergi, sauciari vino, Liv.
units.tr: Inebriari] To drown oneself in wine, Cic. To swamp one's wit with cups, Gell. To drink very heavily. They went far into the wine, Liv. To be soaked in neat wine, Tib. You are overcome by wine, Plaut. The wine I drank has beaten me. We are flooded with wine, Petron. My vein is warmed whenever it is wounded by neat wine, Mart. Heat has come to my struck head and to my shoulder from the lamps, Hor. To grow warm with neat wine. To be drowned, to be wounded by wine, Liv.

units.la: Inedia] Abstinentia mitigatur febris, Cic. Apastia, Cæl. Rhod.
units.tr: Inedia] Abstinence moderates a fever, Cic. Apastia, Caelius Rhodiginus.

units.la: Ineffabilis ] Inenarrabilis. Enarratu difficilis , inexplicabile dictu est, Plin. Inenarratus, Gell. Indictus & innominabilis Deus, Apul. Nec relatu effabilis, nec, &c. Amm. Quicquid dixero minus erit, Petr. Vincitur sermo rei magnitudine , & minus est eo quod dicitur, Hieron.
units.tr: Ineffabilis] Unspeakable. Unutterable. Hard to tell, impossible to explain in words, Plin. Not told, Gell. The unnamed and unnameable God, Apul. Not expressible in speech, nor etc., Amm. Whatever I say will be less, Petron. Speech is overcome by the greatness of the thing, and is less than what is said, Hier.

units.la: Ineffabiliter ] Inenarrabiliter , Liv. Inexplicabiliter, Apul.
units.tr: Ineffabiliter] Indescribably, Liv. Inexplicably, Apul.

units.la: Inefficaciter] Frigidissimè, Quint.
units.tr: Inefficaciter] Most coldly, Quint.

units.la: Inefficax] Frigidum solatium, Ovid. Lentus, Cic. Inelaboratus, vid. Imperfectus.
units.tr: Inefficax] Cold comfort, Ovid. Slack, Cic. Inelaboratus, see Imperfectus.

units.la: Inelegans] Incultus, inornatus, indotatus. Incomitata, incompta ars, Cic.
units.tr: Inelegans] Uncultivated, unadorned, without a dowry. An art without company, unadorned, Cic.

units.la: Ineloquens, vid. Indisertus.
units.tr: Ineloquens, see Indisertus.

units.la: Inemendabilis] Inemendabilis pravitas, Quint. Irredivivus pons, Catul. Corrigi non potest, Cic. Nullus hunc recudat Vulcanus ; Nullus refingat Mercurius.
units.tr: Inemendabilis] Incorrigible wickedness, Quint. A bridge that cannot be restored, Catull. It cannot be corrected, Cic. No Vulcan will recast this, no Mercury will remake it.

units.la: Inemendabile pereat] Inemendabile vulnus ense recidendum, ne pars sincera trahatur, Ovid.
units.tr: Inemendabile pereat] Let an incurable wound be cut out with the sword, lest the sound part be dragged along with it, Ovid.

units.la: Inenodabilis, vid. Inexplicabilis.
units.tr: Inenodabilis, see Inexplicabilis.

units.la: Inepte] Putidè. Odiosè, Cic. Frigidè, subfrigidè. Inconcinniter, Gell. Infabrè sculptum, Hor. Perridiculè, Cic. Nugatoriè responsum, ad Heren.
units.tr: Inepte] Foolishly. Offensively, Cic. Coldly, rather coldly. Awkwardly, Gell. Clumsily carved, Hor. Very ridiculously, Cic. Answered in a trifling way, ad Herenn.

units.la: Ineptia] Ineptitudo, Non. Insulsitas, Cic.
units.tr: Ineptia] Ineptitude, Non. Insipidity, Cic.

units.la: Ineptus homo] Fœnum. Abnormis, Hor. Caudex, stipes asinus, Ter. Insulsus, Cic. Frustra est, Sal. Mala merx, Frutex, Plaut. Asinus ad lyram. Dispeream si tu Pyladi præstare matellam dignus es, Mart.
units.tr: Ineptus homo] Hay. Abnormal, Hor. Blockhead, stump, donkey, Ter. Insipid, Cic. It is useless, Sall. Bad goods, a shrub, Plaut. A donkey at the lyre. May I die if you are worthy to hold Pylades' chamber-pot, Mart.

units.la: Inepta agere] Adaptare capiti ocream, tibiæ galeam, Herculis cothurnos infanti. Adhibere sanæ corporis parti scalpellum. Asinum sub freno currere doces. Bovi clitellas. Bove leporem venari. Clave findere ligna & securi fores aperire.
units.tr: Inepta agere] To fit a greave on the head and a helmet on the shin, to put Hercules' buskins on a baby. To apply a scalpel to a healthy part of the body. You teach a donkey to run under the bridle. Panniers for an ox. To hunt a hare with an ox. To split wood with a key and open doors with an axe.

units.la: Ineptire, vid. Nugari.
units.tr: Ineptire, see Nugari.

units.la: Inermis] Inermus, inermis ac nudus, Cic. Inarmatus, Propert.
units.tr: Inermis] Unarmed and naked, Cic. Unarmed, Propert.

units.la: Iners, vid. Segnis.
units.tr: Iners, see Segnis.

units.la: Ineruditus] Indoctus. Tiro ac rudis. Rudis literarum. Rudis in re civili. Iners. Expers eruditionis, Cic. Pulverem eruditum ne quidem attigit. Bipes asellus, Hieron.
units.tr: Ineruditus] Untaught. A raw novice. Raw in letters. Raw in civic affairs. Idle. Without learning, Cic. He did not even touch the learned dust. A two-legged donkey, Hier.

units.la: Inescare, vid. Allicere, instruere.
units.tr: Inescare, see Allicere, instruere.

units.la: Inevitabilis] Indeclinabilis, Sen. Indeclinatus, Ovid. Inaversabilis, Apul. Ineluctabilis, Virg.
units.tr: Inevitabilis] Unavoidable, Sen. Not to be turned aside, Ovid. Not to be averted, Apul. Inescapable, Virg.

units.la: Inexcitabilis, vid. Somnus profundus.
units.tr: Inexcitabilis, see Somnus profundus.

units.la: Inexcusabilis] Impurgabile crimen, Amm. Carens purgatione.
units.tr: Inexcusabilis] A crime that cannot be purged, Amm. Without any excuse.

units.la: Inexercitatus] Inexercitus, Macrob.
units.tr: Inexercitatus] Untrained, Macrob.

units.la: Inexorabilis] Indeprecabilis, Gell. Mollescere nescius alloquiis. Adeo ingenio est duro & inexorabili, ut neque misericordia, neque precibus molliri queat, Ter. Inflexibilis, Plin. Nullis precibus adduci potest, Cic. Silice durior. Lapide surdior. Cote durior. Æquore surdior, Er. Obduruerunt, occaluerunt aures.
units.tr: Inexorabilis] Not to be entreated, Gell. Knowing not how to be softened by pleading. So hard of nature and inexorable that neither pity nor prayers can soften him, Ter. Inflexible, Plin. Cannot be moved by any prayers, Cic. Harder than flint. Deafer than stone. Harder than whetstone. Deafer than the sea, Erasm. Their ears have grown hard and deaf.

units.la: Inexpertus] Expers periculorum. Hospes in aliqua re, peregrinus, tiro. Ne umbram quidem hujus rei vidit, Cic. Imprudens maris, Liv. Insolens bellorum, Tac. Homo recens, nuperus & novitius, Plaut.
units.tr: Inexpertus] Without experience of dangers. A stranger or foreigner in some matter, a novice. He had not even seen the shadow of this thing, Cic. Ignorant of the sea, Liv. Unused to wars, Tac. A new man, fresh and untried, Plaut.

units.la: Inexpertus qualia scit? ] Dulce bellum inexpertis. Dulcis inexpertis cultura potentis amici, expertus metuit, Hor.
units.tr: Inexpertus qualia scit? ] War is sweet to the inexperienced; the friendship of a powerful man is sweet to the untried, but he who has tried it fears it, Hor.

units.la: Inexplebilis, vid. Insatiabilis.
units.tr: Inexplebilis, see Insatiabilis.

units.la: Inexplicabilis] Insolubilis, Quint. Inexplicitus, Mart. Ineluctabile fatum, Stat. Inexputabilis, (qui supputari nequit,) Gell. Indissolubilis nodus, Plin. Inenodabilis res, Cic. Inexpedibilis mora, Amm. Inextricabilis, Virg.
units.tr: Inexplicabilis] Not dissolvable, Quint. Not unfolded, Mart. Inescapable fate, Stat. Not to be reckoned up, Gell. An indissoluble knot, Plin. A matter that cannot be unravelled, Cic. An inexpedient delay, Amm. Inextricable, Virg.

units.la: Inexploratus] Inexaminatus, Firm. Si quid inexpertum scenae committis, Hor. Intentatus, Sen.
units.tr: Inexploratus] Unexamined, Firm. If you entrust anything untried to the stage, Hor. Untouched, Sen.

units.la: Inexpugnabilis, vid. Invictus.
units.tr: Inexpugnabilis, see Invictus.

units.la: Infacetus] Inficetus, insulsus, Cic. Frigidus, ineptus, Id. Illepidus, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Infacetus] Inelegant, dull, Cic. Cold, clumsy, Id. Unpleasant, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Infacundus, vid. Indisertus.
units.tr: Infacundus, see Indisertus.

units.la: Infamare, vid. Diffamare.
units.tr: Infamare, see Diffamare.

units.la: Infamia] Adversa fama, Sen. Vulnus famae. Nota. Dedecus, Cic. Flagitium, Plaut. Stigma. Dysphimia. Parum secunda fama, Suet. Traductio, Sen. Fama, abs. Ter. Virg.
units.tr: Infamia] Adverse reputation, Sen. A wound to one's name. A mark. Disgrace, Cic. A shameful deed, Plaut. A brand. Dysphimia. Not very favourable reputation, Suet. Slander, Sen. Fame (absolute), Ter., Virg.

units.la: Infamis] Infame nomen, Ovid. Famosus, Sal. Adverso in vulgus rumore fuit, Tac. Male audit. Infamia laborat, flagrat. Habet infamiam. Minus commode audit, Cic. Pessima ejus fama in vulgus est, Liv. Laborat infamiae nota, Vlp. Vid. Diffamatus.
units.tr: Infamis] An infamous name, Ovid. Notorious, Sall. Was held in adverse rumour among the people, Tac. Is ill spoken of. Suffers from infamy, is branded. Has infamy. Is spoken of less well, Cic. His very bad reputation is among the people, Liv. Suffers the mark of infamy, Ulp. See Diffamatus.

units.la: Infandus] Nefandus amor, Val.M. Innominabilis, Gell. Ne fando quidem cognoscendus, audiendus. Ne fando quidem dignus, Cic.
units.tr: Infandus] Unspeakable love, Val. Max. Unnamable, Gell. Not even to be known or heard of by report. Not even worthy of mention, Cic.

units.la: Infans] Nefrens, Liv. Animal nondum rationale, Sen. Puellus, Lucil. Pupus, Varr.
units.tr: Infans] Unbridled, Liv. A creature not yet rational, Sen. A little boy, Lucil. A little child, Varr.

units.la: Infantia] Exordium vitae.
units.tr: Infantia] The beginning of life.

units.la: Ab infantia] Ab unguibus, a teneris unguiculis. A prima aetate. A pueris. Ab ineunte aetate. A parvis. Ab initio aetatis, Cic. A puero parvulo, pusillo. A cunabulis, Plaut. Ab infantibus, Celf. Ab infante, a tenero, Col. A parvulis, Caes. A teneris, Virg. A rudibus annis. Ab ipsis crepundiis, Er. Hoc discunt omnes ante alpha & beta puellae, Iuv. Cum lacte bibere errorem, Prudent.
units.tr: Ab infantia] From the nails, from tender little nails. From the first age. From boys. From the beginning of one's age. From little ones. From the start of life, Cic. From a small boy, from a little one. From the cradle, Plaut. From infancy, Cels. From infant, from tender, Col. From the little ones, Caes. From the tender years, Virg. From one's raw years. From the very rattles, Erasm. All girls learn this before alpha and beta, Juv. To drink error in with one's milk, Prudent.

units.la: Infantilis, vid. Puerilis.
units.tr: Infantilis, see Puerilis.

units.la: Infatuare, vid. Dementare.
units.tr: Infatuare, see Dementare.

units.la: Infectus] Infabricata robora, Virg. Æs rude, Plin. Æs grave, Liv. Æs rudum, Sipont. Raudusculum, vel Rudiusculum. Adrudus. Æs conflatum, infectum, contrarium, grave, Fest.
units.tr: Infectus] Unwrought timbers, Virg. Raw bronze, Plin. Heavy bronze, Liv. Raw bronze, Sipont. A little raw bronze, or a little rough piece. Unmelted bronze. Bronze that is cast, unwrought, opposite, heavy, Fest.

units.la: Infectus peste, vid. Pestis.
units.tr: Infectus peste, see Pestis.

units.la: Infecunditas] Sterilitas, Cic. Segnites camporum, Plin.
units.tr: Infecunditas] Sterility, Cic. Barrenness of the fields, Plin.

units.la: Infecundus] Infecunda natura, Stat. Sterile virtutum seculum, Tac. Laborans sterilitate, Col. Male natus ager, Varr. Infelix arbor, Cic. Cœlebs arbor, Plin. Spadonia laurus, Id.
units.tr: Infecundus] Barren nature, Stat. A sterile age of virtues, Tac. Labouring under sterility, Col. A badly born field, Varr. An unfruitful tree, Cic. A childless tree, Plin. A spayed laurel, Id.

units.la: Infelicitas] Infortunium, Ter. Adversa, misera, afflicta, infesta fortuna. Calamitas. Ærumna adversa. Res adversæ, contrariæ, miseræ, Cic. Mala fors, Cæs. Summum infelicitatis genus est, Sen. Fatum, Cic. Vicem alterius dolere, Cic. id est, sortem malam.
units.tr: Infelicitas] Misfortune, Ter. Adverse, wretched, afflicted, hostile fortune. Calamity. Bitter adversity. Adverse, opposed, wretched circumstances, Cic. Bad luck, Caes. The greatest kind of unhappiness is..., Sen. Fate, Cic. To grieve for another's lot, Cic., that is, a bad lot.

units.la: Infeliciter] Improspere, Col. Inauspicato. Malis omnibus. Nullis, vel, malis auspiciis. Funestis omnium omnibus. Auspicio non captato, Cic. Haud auspicato, Ter. Adverso flumine, ex Gr. Malâ avi. Adversis austris. Mala alite, Hor. Cum malo auspicio nomen conjunctum est, Plaut. Contrario amne.
units.tr: Infeliciter] Unprosperously, Col. Without auspices. With all things bad. With no auspices, or with bad ones. With fatal omens for all. Without taking the auspices, Cic. Not with good auspices, Ter. Against the current, from the Greek. With a bad omen. With adverse south winds. With an ill-omened bird, Hor. A name joined with an ill omen, Plaut. Against the stream.

units.la: Infeliciter tentare aliquid] Invitâ deliâ venari. Tu nihil invitâ dices faciesve Minervâ.
units.tr: To attempt something unsuccessfully: to hunt with Diana unwilling. You will say or do nothing with Minerva unwilling.

units.la: Infeliciter laborare] Alienâ manu laborare.
units.tr: To labour unsuccessfully: to labour with another's hand.

units.la: Infelix] Infortunatus, invenustum ac infelicem hominem. Genio ad miseriam natus. Cui bonæ felicitates omnes adversæ sunt, Ter. Improsper, Tac. Infaustus, Ovid. Lævum tempus, Hor. Nefastus dies, Id. Scævus. Atri dies, Gell. Sinister, Virg. Funestus dies, Cic. Parum felix, Plin. Jun. Nati infelicibus ovis. Quartâ lunâ natus. Næ ego infelix homo sum. Ipso infortunio infortunior, Er. Inauspicatus, Plin. Inauspicatissimus, Id. Non auspicatus, inominatus. Malè ominata verba, Hor.
units.tr: Unhappy: an unfortunate, graceless and unlucky man, born under an unlucky star for misery. One for whom all good fortune is adverse, Ter. Unprosperous, Tac. Ill-omened, Ovid. An unlucky time, Hor. An unlucky day, Id. Sinister, Gell. Black days, Gell. Sinister, Virg. A deadly day, Cic. Scarcely fortunate, Plin. Jun. Born of unlucky eggs. Born under the fourth moon. Alas, I am an unhappy man. More unfortunate than misfortune itself, Erasmus. Inauspicious, Plin. Most inauspicious, Id. Not auspicated, nameless. Ill-omened words, Hor.

units.la: Infelix donum] Malo asino vehitur.
units.tr: An unhappy gift: he rides on a bad donkey.

units.la: Infensè, vid. Iracundè.
units.tr: Hostilely: see Angrily.
