units.la: Infensum esse alicui] Malè sum affectus erga aliquem, Maleyolus. Maleyolentiâ in aliquem suffusus sum, Cic. Malè favere alicui. Malo esse in aliquem animo, Ovid. Vertere pollicem, convertere, Iuv. tract. à gladiatorib. Quasi infensantibus diis, Tac. Malè in aliquem consulere, Ter.
units.tr: To be hostile to someone: I am ill disposed towards someone, ill-willed. I am filled with ill will against someone, Cic. To favour someone ill. To be ill-minded towards someone, Ovid. To turn the thumb down, to turn it, Juv., a figure taken from the gladiators. As if the gods were hostile, Tac. To counsel ill against someone, Ter.

units.la: Inferialis, vid. Exsequialis.
units.tr: Funereal: see Funeral.

units.la: Inferior] Infernus. Depressus, depressior locus, Col. Demissa loca, Cic. Submissa planities, ima terra, infernum limen, Varr.
units.tr: Lower: infernal. A sunken place, a lower and more sunken spot, Col. Low-lying ground, Cic. A sunken plain, the lowest ground, the lower threshold, Varr.

units.la: Infernalis] Infernus Rex, Virg. Orcinianus, Mart. Avernus. Avernalis. Tartareus, Ovid. Acheronticus, Plaut. Acherusia templa, Lucr. Orcinus, Gell. Orchius, & Orchivus, Id.
units.tr: Infernal: King of the Underworld, Virg. Of Orcus, Mart. Avernus. Avernian. Tartarean, Ovid. Acherontic, Plaut. The Acherusian temples, Lucr. Orcine, Gell. Orchian and Orchivan, Id.

units.la: Infernus] Umbrarum locus. Orcus. Tartarus. Tartara, pl. Virg. Tartarea domus, Ovid. Tartarea plaga. Erebus. Inferi. Sceleratorum sedes atque regio. Vita mortuorum sub terra; Ubi impii supplicia perferunt, Cic. Carcer infernus; & perpetuâ nocte oppressa regio, Sen. Avernus, Claud. Orcum, Enn. Acherontica regio, Plaut. Acherusia templa, Lucr.
units.tr: Hell: the place of shades. Orcus. Tartarus. Tartara, plural, Virg. The Tartarean home, Ovid. The Tartarean region. Erebus. The underworld. The seat and region of the wicked. The life of the dead beneath the earth, where the impious undergo punishment, Cic. A hellish prison, and a region oppressed by perpetual night, Sen. Avernus, Claud. Orcus, Enn. The Acherontic region, Plaut. The Acherusian temples, Lucr.

units.la: Inferre] Introferre, Cic. Invehere mala, Id. Importare frumentum, Caes.
units.tr: To bring in: to carry in, Cic. To bring evils upon, Id. To import grain, Caes.

units.la: Infestare] Premit fortuna infesta, Varr. Infestare ferociter, Liv. Urgere crebris assultibus, Virg. Incursare, Tacit. Incurrere impetu in aliquem, insectari aliquem acerbius. Calefacere aliquem, Cic. Urere hominem, Ter. Exercitor sum alicujus, Plaut.
units.tr: To harass: fortune presses hard, Varr. To harass fiercely, Liv. To press with frequent assaults, Virg. To run against, Tac. To rush at someone with force, to pursue someone more bitterly. To heat someone, Cic. To burn a man, Ter. I am the trainer of someone, Plaut.

units.la: Infestus] Incursitans, Sen. Vid. Molestus.
units.tr: Hostile: running about in attack, Sen. See Troublesome.

units.la: Inficere aliquid] Infuscare, Cic. Mali quidpiam alicui affla-re ad Her. Temerare venenis fluvios, Vitiare auras, praevitiare, Ovid. Importare aliquò contagionem, Plin. Inspirare venenum, Virg. Penetrant contagia, Lucan. Venenare aliquid, Lucr. Coinquinare, Col.
units.tr: To infect something: to darken, Cic. To breathe some harm upon someone, ad Her. To poison rivers with venom; to taint the air, to pollute beforehand, Ovid. To carry contagion to a place, Plin. To breathe in poison, Virg. Contagions penetrate, Lucan. To poison something, Lucr. To defile, Col.

units.la: Infici] Contaminare se contagione societatis, Cic. Ducere vitium, Plin. Trahere periculum à flatu, Sen. Vitiari odoribus, Ovid. Laedi odore, Plin. Concipere morbum, Col.
units.tr: To be infected: to contaminate oneself with the contagion of a society, Cic. To catch a fault, Plin. To draw danger from a breath, Sen. To be tainted by odours, Ovid. To be harmed by a smell, Plin. To take in a disease, Col.

units.la: Inficiatio, vid. Negatio.
units.tr: Denial: see Negation.

units.la: Infidelis] Infidus amicus, infidelissimi socii. Perfidus. Perfidissimus. Fidem venalem habet, Cic. Homo nullâ fide, Plaut. Non ex fide versans pecuniam nummularius, Suet. Male fidus, Ovid, Fallit promissum, Curt. Cribro infidelior, Er.
units.tr: Unfaithful: a faithless friend, most faithless allies. Treacherous. Most treacherous. He has a faith that is for sale, Cic. A man with no good faith, Plaut. A money-changer who does not deal in good faith, Suet. Badly trustworthy, Ovid. He breaks his promise, Curt. More untrustworthy than a sieve, Erasmus.

units.la: Infidelitas] Istius fide, ac potius perfidia deceptus sum, Cic. Lubricum fidei, Macrob. Vid. Perfidia.
units.tr: Unfaithfulness: I was deceived by that man's good faith, or rather by his treachery, Cic. The slipperiness of faith, Macrob. See Treachery.

units.la: Infidelitas inter homines crebra] Homo homini lupus.
units.tr: Unfaithfulness is frequent among men: man is a wolf to man.

units.la: Infideliter] Perfide, Vlp. Non ex fide agere, Suet. Non cum fide inferunt frumentum, Col.
units.tr: Unfaithfully: treacherously, Ulp. To act not in good faith, Suet. They bring in grain not in good faith, Col.

units.la: Infigere] Defigere cultrum in corde alicujus, Liv. Telum sedet in corpore, Sen. Figere mucronem in aliquo. Gladium hosti in pectus infigere, Cic.
units.tr: To thrust in: to plunge a knife into someone's heart, Liv. The weapon sticks in the body, Sen. To fix a point in someone. To thrust a sword into an enemy's breast, Cic.

units.la: Infimus] Imus, Plaut. Nullo non inferior, Er.
units.tr: Lowest: the lowest, Plaut. Inferior to none, Erasmus.

units.la: Infinitae rei quaestio est] Multi sermonis sunt ista. Res longi subsellii est, Cic. Dies deficiat si velim numerare; Id. Tardum dictu est, Plaut. Immensae quaestionis est. Immensum referre, Plin. Si prima repetens ab origine pergam; ante diem clauso componet vesper Olympo, Virg. Longum est, si percensere velim, Macrob.
units.tr: The matter is one of infinite inquiry: that is a matter for much discussion. It is the business of a long bench, Cic. The day would fail if I wished to count, Id. It is hard to say, Plaut. It is a question of immense scope. To relate what is immense, Plin. If I should go on from the very beginning, the evening would close the Olympian gate before the day ends, Virg. It would be long if I wished to go through them all, Macrob.

units.la: Infinitas] Infinitio, Cic. Indefinitio, Non.
units.tr: Infinity: unboundedness, Cic. Indefiniteness, Non.

units.la: Infinite] Dempto fine, Ovid. Infinitis vicibus, temporibus.
units.tr: Infinitely: with the end removed, Ovid. Infinitely many times, at infinite times.

units.la: Infinitus] Interminatus, immensus. Nullis terminis circumscriptus aut finitus. Cujus nullus est terminus, Cic. Viduatus fine, Apul. Immanis numerus, Varr. Effusus risus, Claud.
units.tr: Infinite: unbounded, immense. Not limited or bounded by any boundaries. One whose limit is none, Cic. Deprived of an end, Apul. An immense number, Varr. Unbounded laughter, Claud.

units.la: Infirmare, vid. Debilitare.
units.tr: To weaken: see To debilitate.

units.la: Infirmus, vid. Debilis.
units.tr: Weak: see Feeble.

units.la: Inflammare, vid. Incendere.
units.tr: To inflame: see To kindle.

units.la: Inflare] Sufflare buccas, Plaut. Inflare vehementer. Intendere sonorum gradus, Cic. Implere tubam flatu. Adhibere, addere pulmonibus, lateribus vim. Explere mensuram soni.
units.tr: To blow into: to puff out the cheeks, Plaut. To blow vigorously. To raise the pitch of sounds, Cic. To fill the trumpet with breath. To apply and add force to the lungs and sides. To fill out the measure of sound.

units.la: Inflatio] Inflatus, Cic. Sufflatio, Plin.
units.tr: Inflation: a blowing into, Cic. A puffing up, Plin.

units.la: Inflexibilis] Rigida quercus, Ovid. Rigor ferri, Col.
units.tr: Inflexible: a stiff oak, Ovid. The rigidity of iron, Col.

units.la: Inflexio, vid. Inclinatio.
units.tr: Bending: see Inclination.

units.la: Inflexus, vid. Aduncus.
units.tr: Bent: see Hooked.

units.la: Influere] Subinfluunt aquae, Sen. Interfusus Oceanus intrat per tot maria. Amnis mari illabitur, immergitur, immeat meat Nilo. Evolvitur in mare flumen. Evomit se Nilus. Funditur in Rhenum fluvius, Plin. Tiberis flumen vomit in mare, Enn. Intimatur mari Nilus, Sol. Ingurgitat se paludi fluvius, Amm.
units.tr: To flow into: the waters flow beneath, Sen. The Ocean, poured round, enters through so many seas. The river glides into the sea, is plunged into it, passes into the Nile. The river rolls out into the sea. The Nile pours itself out. The river is poured into the Rhine, Plin. The Tiber pours its stream into the sea, Enn. The Nile is poured into the sea, Sol. The river pours itself into the marsh, Amm.

units.la: Influxus stellarum] Influentia, influxio, Firm. Vis coelestis ad eos, qui in terra gignuntur, pertinens. Adspiratio coeli gravis & pestilens. Affectio astrorum, coelorum valeat ad res quasdam. Efficientia solis, Cic.
units.tr: Influence of the stars: influence, influx, Firm. The heavenly power that acts upon those who are born on the earth. The heavy and pestilent breath of heaven. The disposition of the stars and heavens, which has power over certain things. The efficacy of the sun, Cic.

units.la: Infœcunditas, vid. Infecunditas.
units.tr: Barrenness: see Infecundity.

units.la: Informare] Conformare in speciem, Col. Modificari membra, Gell. Membrari, Cens. Vid. Figurare.
units.tr: To shape: to form into a figure, Col. To mould the limbs, Gell. To give limbs, Cens. See To fashion.

units.la: Informis] Ineffigiatus, Gell.
units.tr: Shapeless: without an image, Gell.

units.la: Infortunium] Mala fortuna, Cic. Vid. Infelicitas.
units.tr: Misfortune: bad luck, Cic. See Unhappiness.

units.la: Infortunia vitanda] Navis scopulos deprecatur.
units.tr: Misfortunes to be avoided: the ship prays to avoid the rocks.

units.la: Infortunii sui causam existere] Consilia sana spernere, & malum sibi ultrò accersere. Mali fontem ipse sibi reperit. Jumento suo sibi malum accersere. Quisque suae fortunae faber.
units.tr: To be the cause of one's own misfortune: to scorn sound counsel and voluntarily bring trouble upon oneself. He finds the source of evil himself. To bring trouble upon oneself by one's own beast. Each man is the smith of his own fortune.

units.la: Infrà] Deorsum feror, Cic. Pessum eo, Plaut. Infrà scripsi, Cic.
units.tr: Below: I am carried downwards, Cic. I go to ruin, Plaut. I wrote below, Cic.

units.la: Infra, præp. Vid. Sub.
units.tr: Below, preposition: see Under.

units.la: Infrenatus, vid. Effrenis.
units.tr: Unbridled: see Unbridled.

units.la: Infrequens, vid Rarus.
units.tr: Infrequent: see Rare.

units.la: Infriare aliquid] Interere, Cat. Inradere, & irradere, Id. Infricare, Col.
units.tr: To rub something in: to grind down, Cato. To shave and shave again, Id. To rub in, Col.

units.la: Infricare aliquid alicui] Perfricare caput unguentis, Cic. Affricare, Plin. Fricare corpus oleo, Mart. Defricare aliquid salivâ, Celf.
units.tr: To rub something on something: to rub the head with ointments, Cic. To rub on, Plin. To rub the body with oil, Mart. To rub something off with saliva, Celsus.

units.la: Infringere] Perfringere, Lucr. Præfracta lingua, id est, in summo cortice fracta, Lamb. Si quid ventus interfregerit, Cat.
units.tr: To break into: to break through, Lucr. A tongue broken off in front, that is, broken at the outermost bark, Lamb. If the wind has broken anything through, Cato.

units.la: Infucare, vid. Diluere.
units.tr: To stain: see To dilute.

units.la: Infucatus, vid. Imaginarius.
units.tr: Stained: see Feigned.

units.la: Insumare] Suspendere in fumo, Plin.
units.tr: To smoke: to hang up in smoke, Plin.

units.la: Infumatus] Fumosa perna, Hor. Caro inveterata, vel arefacta, in fumo.
units.tr: Smoked: a smoked ham, Hor. Meat that has grown old, or dried, in smoke.

units.la: Infundere] Fundere vina, implere pateram mero, Virg. Illiquefacere, Cic. Miscere alicui poculum, Ovid. Invergere lac, Id.
units.tr: To pour in: to pour out wine, to fill the cup with unmixed wine, Virg. To melt, Cic. To mix a cup for someone, Ovid. To pour in milk, Id.

units.la: Infundibulum] Infudibulum, Cat. Epichysis, Plaut.
units.tr: Funnel: a little funnel, Cat. A pipe, Plaut.

units.la: Infuscare, vid. Denigrare.
units.tr: To darken: see To blacken.

units.la: Infusio] Infusus, Cic.
units.tr: Infusion: a poured-in thing, Cic.

units.la: Ingeminare, vid. Repetere.
units.tr: To repeat: see To repeat.

units.la: Ingemiscendus, vid. Miserandus.
units.tr: To be lamented: see To be pitied.

units.la: Ingemiscere] Ingemere. Trahere suspirium, Ovid. Suspirare. Alte petere suspirium, Plaut. Ingentem dare gemitum. De imo pectore ducere gemitus, Virg. Adgemere alicui, Stat. Graviter gemere aliquid. Congemuit Senatus, Cic. Quid congemis & fles? Lucr.
units.tr: To sigh: to groan. To draw a sigh, Ovid. To sigh. To breathe a deep sigh, Plaut. To give a great groan. To draw groans from the depths of the heart, Virg. To groan to someone, Stat. To groan heavily over something. The Senate groaned together, Cic. Why do you groan and weep together? Lucr.

units.la: Ingeniosè] Sagaciter, sagacissimè. Solerter, solertissimè. Acutè, acutissimè. Argutè conjicere, Cic. Industriè, Cæs.
units.tr: Ingeniously: shrewdly, most shrewdly. Skilfully, most skilfully. Keenly, most keenly. To conjecture shrewdly, Cic. Diligently, Caes.

units.la: Ingeniosus] Ingenio acutissimus. Peringeniosus, ingenii plenus. Summo ingenio præditus. Præstans ingenio. Versutus, Cic. Præsens ingenio, Plin. Extra omnem ingenii aleam positus, Id. Promptus ingenio, Liv. Valet ingenio. Capitali ingenio, Ovid. In numerato habet ingenium, Sen. Ingeniatus, Plaut. Omnia ingenia mihi sunt, Id. Mercurialis vir, Hor. Non inargutus, Vlp. Cerebri felicis. Daedalo ingeniosior, Er.
units.tr: Ingenious: most keen in wit. Full of wit. Endowed with the highest talent. Excelling in talent. Crafty, Cic. Ready in wit, Plin. Placed beyond all the risk of wit, Id. Quick of wit, Liv. Strong in wit. Of the highest talent, Ovid. He holds his wit in ready money, Sen. Clever, Plaut. I have all the wit in the world, Id. A man of Mercury, Hor. Not unwitty, Ulp. Of a fortunate brain. More ingenious than Daedalus, Erasmus.

units.la: Ingenium] Ingeniolum, Arnob. Indoles. Mentis acumen & acies. Mars. Minerva. Acumen, Cic.
units.tr: Wit: a little talent, Arnob. Natural disposition. The keenness and sharpness of mind. Mars. Minerva. Acuteness, Cic.

units.la: Ingenium stupidum in formoso corpore] Gladius plumbeus in eburnea vagina. Æquale caput & cerebrum non habet. Pistillo retusius ingenium, Er.
units.tr: A stupid mind in a handsome body: a leaden sword in an ivory scabbard. He has no head and brain level with each other. A mind blunter than a pestle, Erasmus.

units.la: Ingenium excellens] Aquila in nubibus, Lipf.
units.tr: An excellent mind: an eagle among the clouds, Lipsius.

units.la: Ingenium distortum ægrè corrigitur] Lignum tortum haud unquam rectum.
units.tr: A distorted mind is corrected with difficulty: a twisted piece of wood is never straight.

units.la: Ingenii perversi] Improbus ab ingenio, improbus impensè, Plaut.
units.tr: Of a perverse mind: wicked by nature, wicked to excess, Plaut.

units.la: Ingens, vid. Magnus.
units.tr: Huge: see Great.

units.la: Ingenuè, vid. Sincerè.
units.tr: Ingenuously: see Sincerely.

units.la: Ingerere se] Admiscere se, Ter. Immiscere, Liv. Intrudere, inserere. Cur te interponis invitissimis iis, &c. Cicer.
units.tr: To thrust oneself in: to mix oneself in, Ter. To intermingle, Liv. To push in, to insert. Why do you put yourself in among those who are most unwilling, etc.? Cicero.

units.la: Inglorius] Ignobilis mors, Liv. Obscurus. Umbratilis, Cic. Illaudatus, indictus alicui, Virg. Incelebratus, Tac. Incelebris, Sil. Umbratica turba, Sen.
units.tr: Inglorious: an ignoble death, Liv. Obscure. Living in the shade, Cic. Unpraised, unnamed to someone, Virg. Uncelebrated, Tac. Little celebrated, Sil. A shadowy crowd, Sen.

units.la: Ingluviosus, vid. Gulosus. Heluo.
units.tr: Gluttonous: see Greedy. Glutton.

units.la: Ingratè, vid. Injucundè.
units.tr: Ungratefully: see Unpleasantly.

units.la: Ingratitudo ] Ingratus animus, Sen. Ingrati animi crimen.
units.tr: Ingratitude: an ungrateful mind, Sen. The offence of an ungrateful mind.

units.la: Ingratus] Ingratus in aliquem, Cic. Alicui, Sen. Ingratus adversùm Deos, Gell. Malè gratus, Ovid. Immemor beneficii, Cic. Gratior officiis quò sis. Magè carior esto. Ne nomen subeas, quod dicitur officiperda, Cat. Beneficia hauriens perforato animo, Sen. Tesseram confregit.
units.tr: Ungrateful: ungrateful towards someone, Cic. To someone, Sen. Ungrateful towards the gods, Gell. Badly thankful, Ovid. Mindless of a kindness, Cic. Be more grateful for favours the more you are; be dearer the more so. Do not take on the name that is called "ruiner of services", Cato. Drinking in kindnesses with a pierced mind, Sen. He broke the tessera.

units.la: Ingratus ne sis] Adversus solem ne loquitor. Adversus solem ne mejito. Tesseram hospitalem ne confringas, Plaut.
units.tr: Do not be ungrateful] Do not speak against the sun. Do not make water against the sun. Do not break the hospitable token, Plaut.

units.la: Ingravescere] Crudescit morbus, Virg. Crescit, Cic. Exasperatur, Celf. Convalescunt mala, Ovid. Gliscit invidia, Tacit. Aggravescit morbus, integratur malum.
units.tr: To grow worse] The disease grows fiercer, Virg. It increases, Cic. It becomes more severe, Celsus. The evils grow strong, Ovid. Envy flares up, Tacit. The disease gets worse; the evil is renewed.

units.la: Ingredi viam] Convertere, suscipere iter aliquò. Dare se in viam. Committere se viæ. Capessere se domum, Plaut. Flectere iter ad, Liv. Instituere iter, Cat. Insistere aliquam viam, Plaut. Intendere iter ad, in, aliquò, Liv. Petere, petissere cœlum, terras. Contendere. Tendere aliquò, Cic. Quò profectus intenderat, Salust.
units.tr: To enter upon a road] To turn toward, to set out on a journey to a place. To set oneself on the road. To entrust oneself to the road. To hasten home, Plaut. To bend one's journey toward, Liv. To begin a journey, Cato. To take up a path, Plaut. To aim one's journey at, Liv. To seek, to make for heaven or the lands. To strive. To head for a place, Cic. He had set out and aimed for where he was going, Sall.

units.la: Ingruit, vid. Imminet.
units.tr: To rush in, see To hang over.

units.la: Ingurgitare, vid. Influere,
units.tr: To gulp down, see To flow into.

units.la: Ingustatus] Ingustabilis, Plin.
units.tr: Untasted] Not to be tasted, Pliny.

units.la: Inhabilis, vid. Ineptus.
units.tr: Unfit, see Unsuitable.

units.la: Inhabitare, vid. Habitare.
units.tr: To inhabit, see To dwell.

units.la: Inhærere, vid. Hærere.
units.tr: To cling to, see To cling.

units.la: Inhalare alicui] Afflari ore alicujus, Ovid. Adhalari aliquem, Plin. Adflare calidum vaporem membris, Lucr.
units.tr: To breathe upon someone] To be breathed upon by someone's mouth, Ovid. To be breathed upon by someone, Pliny. To blow warm vapour upon the limbs, Lucr.

units.la: Inhalatus] Afflatus, Ovid.
units.tr: Breathed upon] Inspired, Ovid.

units.la: Inhiare] Inhiare alicui, imminere cupiditate in aliquid. Excubare. Erigi exspectatione, Cic. Inhiare aliquid, Plaut. Vid. Insidiari.
units.tr: To gape after] To gape after someone; to press eagerly upon something with desire. To keep watch. To be roused with expectation, Cic. To gape after something, Plaut. See To lie in wait.

units.la: Inhibere, vid. Cohibere.
units.tr: To hinder, see To restrain.

units.la: Inhibitio, vid. Retrocessus.
units.tr: Hindrance, see Retreat.

units.la: Inhonestè] Irreverenter, Plin. Iun. Indignis modis, Ter.
units.tr: Dishonourably] Irreverently, Pliny the Younger. In unworthy ways, Terence.

units.la: Inhonestus] Inhonorus. Obnoxius, Plin. Illiberalis quæstus. Famosus. Sordidum aliquid ad famam, Cic. Indecorus quæstus. Inhonoratus triumphus, Liv.
units.tr: Dishonourable] Without honour. Liable, Pliny. Illiberal gain. Infamous. Something sordid as regards reputation, Cic. Unseemly gain. A triumph without honour, Liv.

units.la: Inhospitalis] Fores habet tritas, ut pastorum casæ. (Iron. Pastores foris habitantes quis invisat?) Scythotauris inhospitalior, Er.
units.tr: Inhospitable] It has worn-out doors, like the huts of shepherds. (Ironically: "Who would visit shepherds who live outside?") More inhospitable than the Scythian Taurians, Erasmus.

units.la: Inhumanè] Inhumaniter. Morosè, Cic. Inciviliter, Apul.
units.tr: Inhumanly] Without humanity. Peevishly, Cic. Uncivilly, Apuleius.

units.la: Inhumanitas] Barbaries, Morositas. Diritas in homine, Cic.
units.tr: Inhumanity] Barbarity, peevishness. Savagery in a man, Cic.

units.la: Inhumanus] Omnem humanitatem exuit. Expers humanitatis, inofficiosus in aliquem. Durus oratione ac moribus. Misanthropus. Ferus ac ferreus, Cic. Morosus, Id. Omni generi humano insociabilis, Liv. Minimè humanus, Sen. Paucorum hominum homo. Timone inhumanior, Er.
units.tr: Inhuman] Stripped of all humanity. Lacking humanity, unkind toward someone. Harsh in speech and manners. A misanthrope. Wild and iron-hearted, Cic. Peevish, Cic. Unsociable toward the whole human race, Liv. Least humane, Seneca. A man of a few men only. More inhuman than Timon, Erasmus.

units.la: Inhumare, vid. Defodere. Humare.
units.tr: To inter, see To bury. To inter.

units.la: Inibi, vid. Ibi.
units.tr: Therein, see There.

units.la: Injectio] Injectus, Lucr.
units.tr: Injection] Something thrown in, Lucr.

units.la: Injicere] Conjicere in ignem, Cic. Inferre aliquid in aliquid, Quint. Injectare, Stat. Corruere spicas in corbem, Varr. Impingere. Qui beneficium aut superbè injecit, aut iratus impegit, Sen.
units.tr: To throw in] To cast into the fire, Cic. To bring something into something, Quint. To hurl at, Stat. To pour grain-ears into a basket, Varro. To push in. He who bestows a kindness either arrogantly or, angry, flings it at a man, Seneca.

units.la: Inimicari] Inimicitias capessere, concipere, contrahere, gerere alicui, cum aliquo, Cic. Liv. Cæs. Abalienare se ab aliquo, Cic.
units.tr: To make enemies] To take up, form, contract, or carry on enmities toward someone or with someone, Cic., Liv., Caes. To alienate oneself from someone, Cic.

units.la: Inimicus, adjectn.nom.] Hostilis animus, infestus & inimicus auditor. Infesta mater, inimicior, inimicissimus mihi, infensus homo, Cic. Iniquus, Virg. Sidus iniquum, Tac. Inimicitiis capessendis facilis, Tacit.
units.tr: Hostile, as adjective] A hostile mind; a hostile and unfriendly listener. A hostile mother, more hostile, most hostile to me; a man of hostile disposition, Cic. Unfriendly, Virg. An unfavourable star, Tacit. Easy to take up enmities, Tacit.

units.la: Inimicus. Subst. vid. Hostis.
units.tr: Enemy, as noun, see Enemy.

units.la: Inique] Iniquissimè, injuriâ, injuriosè. Nullo jure. Contra jus, legem, factum, fas. Improbè parta, Cic. Indignè, indignissimè. Præter æquum & bonum. Immeritò accusari, & immeritissimo omnium, Ter. Illicitè, Vlp.
units.tr: Unjustly] Most unjustly, wrongfully, injuriously. By no right. Against law, custom, deed, or divine law. Gained by dishonest means, Cic. Unworthily, most unworthily. Beyond what is fair and good. To be accused undeservedly, and by the most undeserving of all, Terence. Unlawfully, Ulpian.

units.la: Iniquitas] Habet ea res iniquitatem. Fas non est. Iniquum est, indignitas, injuriæ, indignissimum est, Cic. Injurium est, Plaut. Injuriosum est rapto vivere, Sen. Perinjurium injurium est, Apul. Periniquum est, Cic. Præjudicium, Vlp.
units.tr: Unfairness] The thing has unfairness in it. It is not right. It is unfair, unworthy, an injury; it is most unworthy, Cic. It is wrong, Plaut. It is wrong to live by plunder, Seneca. A great wrong is a wrong, Apuleius. It is very unfair, Cic. Prejudice, Ulpian.

units.la: Iniquus] Res indigna. Flagitiosus. Periniquus. Habet ea res iniquitatem, Cic. Injurus, illex, gis. Plaut. Ipse sibi injurius est, Ter.
units.tr: Unjust] An unworthy thing. Shameful. Most unjust. The thing has unfairness in it, Cic. Injuring, enticing, Plaut. He injures himself, Terence.

units.la: Initium] Primordia agendi. Origo, ortus. Coeptus. Exordium. Principatus. Exorsus. Incunabula. Stirps, cubilia avaritiæ, Cic. Primordia prima. Prima viæ. Prima linea, Lucr. Prima, abs. Liv. Exorsa, Virg. Orsus, ingressus, introitus, Cic. Orsa, pl. Plin. Vestibulum, Quint. Elementum, Iuv. Metropolis. Summus puteus, Plaut. Caput. Nativitas, Ter. Exordium mundi, Virg. Initus motus, Lucr. Radix, Varr. Fontes rerum. Principium juris, Cic.
units.tr: Beginning] The first stages of doing. Origin, source. A start. Opening. Preface. Beginning. Cradle. Stock, the seedbed of avarice, Cic. First beginnings. The first part of the road. The front line, Lucr. The first, Liv. Opening, Virg. A start, entry, entrance, Cic. Beginnings, plural, Pliny. Vestibule, Quint. Rudiment, Juvenal. Metropolis. The top of the well, Plaut. Head. Birth, Terence. The beginning of the world, Virg. The beginning motion, Lucr. Root, Varro. The sources of things. The principle of law, Cic.

units.la: Initium bonum opus repræsentat] Dimidium facti, qui benè coepit, habet. Dimidium plus toto.
units.tr: A good beginning represents the work] He who has begun well has half the deed done. Half is more than the whole.

units.la: Initium factum est] Alea jacta est.
units.tr: The beginning is made] The die is cast.

units.la: Initia malorum non sentiuntur] Cùm parvula est, bona videtur spina.
units.tr: The beginnings of evils are not felt] While it is small, the thorn seems harmless.

units.la: Ab initio] A primo. De principio, Cic. A primordio. A prima linea, Tac. Ab ovo, à fonte, à capite arcessere.
units.tr: From the beginning] From the first. From the origin, Cic. From the source. From the front line, Tacit. To derive from the egg, from the spring, from the head.

units.la: Ab initio ad finem] Ab origine ad exodium, Varr. A capite ad calcem. A carceribus ad metam. Ab ovo usque ad mala.
units.tr: From beginning to end] From the origin to the outcome, Varro. From head to heel. From the starting-gates to the turning-post. From the egg to the apples.

units.la: Ab initio anni, mensis, &c.] Incipiente vere. Inter initia, Plin. Ineunte vere, Cic. Vere novo, Virg. Inchoantibus canicularibus, Pallad. Primâ vindemiâ, Col. Primo progressu; primordiis, Cic. Principio lucis, Tac.
units.tr: From the beginning of the year, month, etc.] At the start of spring. Among the beginnings, Pliny. At the opening of spring, Cic. In new spring, Virg. As the dog-days begin, Palladius. At the first vintage, Columella. At the first progress; in the beginnings, Cic. At the dawn of light, Tacit.

units.la: Ab initio mox errare] Deficere à lineis. A lineis excidere.
units.tr: To go astray at the beginning] To fail from the lines. To fall out of the lines.

units.la: Ad initia rei venire] Ostii limen tetigisti.
units.tr: To come to the beginnings of a matter] You have touched the threshold of the door.

units.la: Injucundè] Injucundius actæ res. Insulsè. Submolestè. Duriter, Cic. Absonè pronunciare, Apul. Invenustè, insubidè, Gell. Ingratè, Tac.
units.tr: Unpleasantly] A matter done more unpleasantly. Insipidly. Somewhat annoyingly. Harshly, Cic. Discordantly in pronunciation, Apuleius. Without charm, without flavour, Gellius. Unpleasingly, Tacitus.

units.la: Injucunditas] Insulsitas. Asperitas rustica orationis. Habet invidiam, Cic.
units.tr: Unpleasantness] Insipidity. Rustic harshness of speech. It has odium, Cic.

units.la: Injucundus] Inamabilis, Plin. Ingratus jocus, Ovid. Insuavis vita. Invenustus. Absonus. Absurdus sonus. Frigidus. Insulsus. Ab ipsa oculorum auriumque comprobatione abhorret, Cic. Sine Venere & gratiâ, Donat. Illepidus homo, Cic. Insipidus. Subidus, Gell.
units.tr: Unpleasant] Unlovable, Pliny. An unpleasing joke, Ovid. A joyless life. Without charm. Discordant. A discordant sound. Frigid. Insipid. Flat. It is repugnant to the very approval of eyes and ears, Cic. Without Venus and grace, Donatus. A man without wit, Cic. Insipid. Tasteless, Gellius.

units.la: Injuria, vid. Iniquitas.
units.tr: Injury, see Unfairness.

units.la: Injuriam pati] Injuriam accipere, Quint. Injuriâ laborare, affligi, jactari, &c. Cic.
units.tr: To suffer injury] To receive an injury, Quint. To labour under, be afflicted with, or buffeted by injury, Cic.

units.la: Injuriam facere alicui] Inferre, injungere injurium, injurium esse, Cic. Injuriosè facere, Vlp. Iniquè injurius es, Plaut. Non æquum facis, Ter. Injuriari. Deterius facere jus alicujus, Sen. Violari jus, Cic.
units.tr: To do injury to someone] To inflict, to impose injury; to be unjust, Cic. To act injuriously, Ulpian. You are unjustly injurious, Plaut. You are not doing right, Terence. To injure. To make someone's right worse, Seneca. To violate a right, Cic.

units.la: Injurius] Injuriosus in aliquem, Cic. Injurus, Lamb.
units.tr: Injurious] Injurious toward someone, Cic. Injurious, Lambinus.

units.la: Injustè] Maximâ injuriâ vinctus adsto, Plaut. Vid. Iniquè.
units.tr: Unjustly] Bound with the greatest injustice I stand, Plaut. See Unfairly.

units.la: Injustitia] Nefandum, Virg. Iniquitas. Nefas. Fas non est. Iniquum est, Cic.
units.tr: Injustice] Unspeakable wrong, Virg. Unfairness. Wrong. It is not right. It is unfair, Cic.

units.la: Injustus] Iniquus. Nam quid hoc iniquius aut indignius dici potest? Cic. Nefandus sanguis, Liv.
units.tr: Unjust] Unfair. For what can be said to be more unfair or more unworthy than this? Cic. Unspeakable blood, Liv.

units.la: Innasci, vid. à Natura.
units.tr: To be born, see From Nature.

units.la: Innatus, vid. Naturalis. Fluitare, Liv.
units.tr: Innate, see Natural. To float, Liv.

units.la: Innatare] Innare aquæ, Liv. Supernatare, Col. Obnatare, Virg. Fluctuare, Plin. vel, ri.
units.tr: To swim in] To swim in water, Liv. To float above, Columella. To swim against, Virg. To surge, Pliny. Or, to float.

units.la: Inniti] Incumbere ad arborem, Plin. Acclinare se ad aliquem, Liv. Nititur arbor radicibus, Cic. Reclinatis in aliquod adminiculum obrepit somnus, Sen.
units.tr: To lean upon] To lean against a tree, Pliny. To recline against someone, Liv. The tree rests on its roots, Cic. Sleep creeps upon a man who has leaned back on some support, Seneca.

units.la: Innocens] Innoxius, insons, Plaut. Inculpatus, Gell. Immerens, Hor. Remotus à culpa. Extra culpam est. Abest culpa ab illo. Abest à culpa. In causa non est, Cic. Nullius criminis reus, Ovid. Exsors culpæ, Liv. Caret noxiâ, Plaut. Indignos & immerentes examinat, Lucr.
units.tr: Innocent] Harmless, blameless, Plaut. Unblemished, Gellius. Undeserving, Horace. Free from fault. Outside of blame. Blame is far from him. Not in the wrong. Not guilty of any crime, Ovid. Free from guilt, Liv. Lacking harm, Plaut. He examines the unworthy and the innocent, Lucr.

units.la: Innocentem accusare] Agnus aquam turbat.
units.tr: To accuse an innocent person] The lamb muddies the water.

units.la: Innocentia] Integritas, Cic. Immeritum, Plaut. Castitas, Vitr. Calumniam refutare satius est re, quàm verbis. Vacare culpâ magnum est solatium.
units.tr: Innocence] Integrity, Cic. Blamelessness, Plaut. Chastity, Vitruvius. It is better to refute a slander by deeds than by words. To be free from fault is a great consolation.

units.la: Innocuè] Inoffensè, Gell. Inviolatè, Cic. Innocenter, Plin. Sine ulla noxa, Suet. Innoxiè, Vopisc. Immeritò, immeritissimò, Terent. Innocentissimè. Castè & integre versari in, Cic.
units.tr: Innocently] Without offence, Gellius. Inviolately, Cic. Innocently, Pliny. Without any harm, Suetonius. Harmlessly, Vopiscus. Undeservedly, most undeservedly, Terence. Most innocently. To conduct oneself chastely and uprightly in, Cic.

units.la: Innodare, vid. Nodare.
units.tr: To knot, see To tie in knots.

units.la: Innominabilis, vid. Ineffabilis, infandus.
units.tr: Unnameable, see Unspeakable, accursed.

units.la: Innotescere] Nomen petere ex otio, Sen. Inclarere, Plin.
units.tr: To become known] To seek a name from leisure, Seneca. To become famous, Pliny.

units.la: Innotescet omnibus] Toto cantabitur orbe.
units.tr: It will become known to all] It will be sung throughout the whole world.

units.la: Innovare, vid. Renovare.
units.tr: To renew, see To renew.

units.la: Innumerabilis] Innumerus numerus, Lucr. Innumeratus, inexputabilis numerus,Col. Indimensus populus, Amm. Superat arenæ numerum, foliorum, pluviæ, stellarum, capillorum, &c. Iun.
units.tr: Innumerable] A number without number, Lucr. Uncounted, an inexhaustible number, Columella. An unmeasured people, Ammianus. It surpasses the number of sand, of leaves, of rain, of stars, of hairs, etc., Juvenal.

units.la: Innumerabilitas] Infinitas, Cic.
units.tr: Innumerability] Infinity, Cic.

units.la: Innuere] Innuere alicui. Annuere toto capite, Cic. Nutare, Plaut. Annuere nutum, Liv. Adnutare, Plaut. Appellare aliquem capite, vultu, Cic. Nutanti mento percutere pectus. Manu loqui, superciliis loqui, Ovid. Digitis concrepare, Cic. Verbis nutum accommodare, ut quod nollem, rejecto capite, quod vellem, relato monstrarem, Apul. Digiti locuti, Tibul.
units.tr: To nod] To nod to someone. To assent with the whole head, Cic. To nod, Plaut. To give a nod, Liv. To nod again, Plaut. To address someone by the head or expression, Cic. To strike the breast with a nodding chin. To speak with the hand, to speak with the eyebrows, Ovid. To snap the fingers, Cic. To fit a nod to words, so that by turning my head away I showed what I did not want and by turning it back what I wanted, Apuleius. The fingers have spoken, Tibullus.

units.la: Innupta] Cœlebs mulier, Plaut. Expers nuptiarum, Hor. Innuba, Ovid.
units.tr: Unmarried] A woman living single, Plaut. Without marriage, Horace. Unwed, Ovid.

units.la: Innutrire, vid. Instruere.
units.tr: To bring up, see To instruct.

units.la: Inobediens] Nulli obediens, nec obediens. Contumax in superiores, Cic. Inobsequens, Sen. Imparens, Fest. Homo imperii inhibiti, detrectator, Bud. Jactat jugum, Hor. Immorigerus, Bar.
units.tr: Disobedient] Obedient to no one, nor obedient. Stubborn toward superiors, Cic. Disobedient, Seneca. Unruly, Festus. A man of restrained command, a refuser, a rebel, Budé. He shakes off the yoke, Horace. Unyielding, Barth.

units.la: Inobedientia] Impatientia, Gell. Lipf. Parendi dedignatio, Plin. Iun. Contumacia, Cic.
units.tr: Disobedience] Impatience, Gellius, Lipsius. Disdain of obeying, Pliny the Younger. Stubbornness, Cic.

units.la: Inobservabilis] Improvisa nobis, Cic. Inobservatus. Minus observabilis, indeprehensibilis, Quint. Improvida tela, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Unobservable] Unforeseen by us, Cic. Unobserved. Less observable, not easily detected, Quint. Unforeseen weapons, Pliny the Younger.

units.la: Inoccare, vid. Occare.
units.tr: To hoe, see To harrow.

units.la: Inofficiosus, vid. Inhumanus.
units.tr: Undutiful, see Inhuman.

units.la: Inopia, vid. Egestas.
units.tr: Want, see Poverty.

units.la: Inopinatus, vid. Insperatus.
units.tr: Unexpected, see Unhoped for.

units.la: Inopportunus] Intempestivus, importunum tempus, Cic. Importuna mors, Ovid.
units.tr: Inopportune] Unseasonable; an unseasonable time, Cic. An untimely death, Ovid.

units.la: Inordinate] Incomposite. Tumultuose; tumultuosissime. Nullo ordine, Liv. Indisposite, Sen. Inordinatim incedebant, Amm. Passim. Turbate; turbide; turbulente; turbulenter; confuse, incondite. Præposterè, Cic. Turbatè aguntur omnia, Cæs. Temerè jacentes, Virg.
units.tr: Disorderly] Without arrangement. In a tumultuous way; most tumultuously. Without any order, Liv. Without arrangement, Seneca. They advanced in disorder, Ammianus. Everywhere. Confusedly; in disorder; turbulently; in confusion; without form. Back to front, Cic. Everything is carried on in confusion, Caesar. Lying about rashly, Virgil.

units.la: Inordinatio] Perturbatio ordinis, Cic. Permutatus ordo, Quint.
units.tr: Disorder: disturbance of order, Cic. Reversed order, Quint.

units.la: Inordinatus] Cic. Inconditus. Tumultuosus, Liv. Indispositus, Tac. Vitiosus magistratus. Vitiosè creatus. Præposterus, Cic. Inconsequens, Carif.
units.tr: Disordered: Cic. Unarranged. Tumultuous, Liv. Ill-arranged, Tac. A magistrate improperly chosen. Wrongly appointed. Topsy-turvy, Cic. Inconsistent, Carif.

units.la: Inornatè & inornatus, vid. Impolitè, incomptus.
units.tr: Unadorned and unadorned: see Unpolished, uncombed.

units.la: Inquietare] Turbare alicujus quietem, Prop. Obturbare, interturbare aliquem, Ter. Interpellare. Obstrepere alicui, in aliqua re. Perturbare otium Reip. Cic. Infestam facere alicui quietem, Lucr.
units.tr: To disquiet: to disturb someone's rest, Prop. To harass or disturb someone, Ter. To interrupt. To make a noise at someone, over some matter. To disturb the peace of the commonwealth, Cic. To make someone's quiet uneasy, Lucr.

units.la: Inquictari, vid. Perturbari.
units.tr: To be disquieted: see To be disturbed.

units.la: Inquietatio] Odium, Ter. Vexatio alicujus, Cic. Interturbatio, Liv. Maleficium ; maleficentia, Cæf.
units.tr: Disquieting: hatred, Ter. The harassing of someone, Cic. Disturbance, Liv. Mischief; wrongdoing, Caes.

units.la: Inquietudo] Inquies, Gell. Otii sui tristis ac ægra patientia. Nusquam residentis animi volutatio, Sen.
units.tr: Restlessness: unease, Gell. A sad and sickly endurance of one's leisure. A mind wandering restlessly, never settled, Sen.

units.la: Inquietus] Inquies, Sal. Turbidus motus, turbulentus. Tumultuosa vita, Cic. Solicitus motus, Lucr. Nusquam residens animus, Sen. Infesta regio, Varr.
units.tr: Restless: uneasy, Sall. Turbid, turbulent motion. A stormy life, Cic. Anxious motion, Lucr. A mind that never settles, Sen. A hostile region, Varr.

units.la: Inquilinus] Inhabitator. Cœnacularius, qui conduxit cœnaculum, Vlp. Proletaneus, Fest.
units.tr: Lodger: a dweller within. A tenant who has rented an upper room, Ulp. Proletaneus, Fest.

units.la: Inquinare] Spurcare, Celf. Collinere, Plaut. Sordidare, Firm. Tetrare, Pacuv. Polluere, Ovid. Contaminare, Paul. IC. Conspurcare, Col. Infuscare pectus illuvie, Cic. Confœdare, Apul. Inbubinare, Lucil.
units.tr: To defile: to foul, Celsus. To smear, Plaut. To make filthy, Firm. To stain, Pacuv. To pollute, Ovid. To contaminate, Paul. IC. To befoul thoroughly, Col. To darken the breast with filth, Cic. To defile, Apul. To make muddy, Lucil.

units.la: Inquinatio] Inquinamentum, Gell. Contaminatio, Bud. Maculatio, Firm. Pollutio, Sipont.
units.tr: Defilement: a stain, Gell. Contamination, Bud. A spotting, Firm. Pollution, Sipont.

units.la: Inquinatus, vid. Impurus.
units.tr: Defiled: see Impure.

units.la: Inquirere] Anquiretur in eum quomodo vivat. Quærere in aliquem. Quæstionem inter aliquos exercere, Cic. Inquirere in vitia alicujus, Amm. Instituere, habere quæstionem, Quint.
units.tr: To inquire: he is to be inquired into as to how he lives. To make inquiry against someone. To hold an examination among certain persons, Cic. To inquire into someone's faults, Amm. To set up and hold an inquiry, Quint.

units.la: Inquisitio] Scrutinium, Apul. Examinatio civilis, Vlp. Anacrisis. Indagatio veritatis in judicio de reo, Plaut. Quæsitio, Plaut. Conquisitio rationis, Cic.
units.tr: Inquiry: a search, Apul. A civil examination, Ulp. Anacrisis [ἀνάκρισις]. A search for the truth in a trial concerning the accused, Plaut. A questioning, Plaut. A seeking out of reason, Cic.

units.la: Inquisitor] Quæsitor, Cic. Scrutator causarum. Cognitionum scientissimi scitatores, Amm.
units.tr: Inquisitor: an examiner, Cic. A searcher into causes. The most skilled investigators of cases, Amm.

units.la: Insalubris] Infaluberrimum vinum, Plin. Morbum faciens, ciens, Cels. Gravissimus & pestilentissimus annus, Cic. Tempus anni gravissimum. Pestilens & gravis ora, Plin. Intempestus, Virg. Aliena salutis, Lucr. Incutere, afferre morbum, Plaut.
units.tr: Unhealthy: very unwholesome wine, Plin. Causing or bringing on disease, Cels. A most grievous and pestilential year, Cic. The most grievous season of the year. Pestilential and heavy air, Plin. Untimely, Virg. Hostile to health, Lucr. To bring on or inflict disease, Plaut.

units.la: Insanabilis] Immedicabilis. Vulnus quod nec Chironia manus levârit, Virg. Irremediabilis, insuperabilis valetudo, Plin. Nullis herbis medicabilis, Ovid. Vomicus morbus Civitatis, Sen. Recusantia perpeti sanitatem ulcera, Arnob.
units.tr: Incurable: beyond remedy. A wound which not even the hand of Chiron could have eased, Virg. A sickness that cannot be remedied or overcome, Plin. Curable by no herbs, Ovid. A festering disease of the commonwealth, Sen. Ulcers that refuse to receive health, Arnob.

units.la: Insania] Defectus à recta ratione. Egestas rationis. Vid. Amentia.
units.tr: Madness: a departure from right reason. A lack of reason. See Insanity.

units.la: Insanire] Hilarem insaniam insanire, ac per risum furere, Sen.
units.tr: To be mad: to be mad with a cheerful madness and to rage through laughter, Sen.

units.la: Insanus] Non sanum tibi est synciput, Plaut. Non satis sanus es. Non pro sano agit. Discedit à mente. Helleborum bibe. Non consistit mente. Pol homo tu non es sobrius. Delirat ; desipit ; insanit. Non est integrae mentis. Non est compos mentis. Non constat animo. Laborat errore mentis. Motae, vel commotae mentis est. Mente lapsi sunt. Defectus animo. Mente excidit. Laborat ab animo. Destituit illum vis animi. Ajace insanior, Er.
units.tr: Mad: your skull is not sound, Plaut. You are not sane enough. He does not act as a sane man. He has departed from his mind. Take hellebore. He does not keep his mind. Good heavens, you are not sober. He raves; he is out of his wits; he is mad. He is not of sound mind. He is not master of his mind. He does not hold to his senses. He is of disturbed mind. They have slipped from their minds. He has fainted in spirit. He has lost his wits. He suffers in the mind. The force of his mind has left him. More mad than Ajax, Er.

units.la: Insatiabilitas] Insatietas, Plaut.
units.tr: Insatiability: insatiety, Plaut.

units.la: Insatiabilis] Inexsaturabilis, inexpletus, Virg. Insaturabilis, inexplebilis. Vorax. Charybdis. Profundus venter, Cic. Insatiatus, Stat. Abdomen insaturabile. Mendici pera non impletur.
units.tr: Insatiable: not to be sated, unfilled, Virg. Insatiable, unfillable. Greedy. Charybdis. A bottomless belly, Cic. Never satisfied, Stat. A belly that is never full. A beggar's bag is never filled.

units.la: Insatiabiliter] Insaturabiliter, Cic.
units.tr: Insatiably: Cic.

units.la: Insitia, vid. Ignorantia.
units.tr: Ignorance: see Ignorance.

units.la: Insicus, vid. Ignarus, imperitus.
units.tr: Ignorant: see Unskilled, inexperienced.

units.la: Inscribere] Referre aliquid in codicem, commentarium. Mandare, commendare monimentis. Adscribere in numerum. Perscribere in tabulas. Inducere in rationes, Cic. Inferere, Plin. Committere literis aliquid. Adscribere ad numerum. Perscribere in tabulis, in monumentis. Perscribere usuras, Cic. Referre, inferre rationibus, Suet. Regerere aliquid in commentarios, Quint.
units.tr: To inscribe: to enter something in a register or commentary. To commit to records, to commend to memorials. To enrol in a number. To write down on tablets. To enter in the accounts, Cic. To enter, Plin. To commit something to writing. To enrol in a number. To write down on tablets or in records. To write down interest, Cic. To enter in the accounts, Suet. To put something into notes, Quint.

units.la: Inscriptio] Titulus libri, Mart. Inscriptum libri, Gell. Index libri, Cic. Epigramma, Id.
units.tr: Inscription: the title of a book, Mart. The inscription of a book, Gell. The index of a book, Cic. An epigram, Id.

units.la: Inscriptus, i. e. nonscriptus] Illiterata pax, Fest. Illiterata vox, Priscian. Pura charta, Ulp.
units.tr: Unwritten, that is, not written: an unwritten peace, Fest. An unwritten voice, Priscian. Blank paper, Ulp.

units.la: Insectari, vid. Persequi, insequi.
units.tr: To harass: see To pursue, to follow.

units.la: Infedatus, vid. Immodestus.
units.tr: Defiled: see Immodest.

units.la: Insensibilis] Insensilis, Gell. Suffugit sensus, Lucr. Nullo sensu percipi potest, Cic.
units.tr: Insensible: Gell. Sense escapes, Lucr. Can be perceived by no sense, Cic.

units.la: Insensibiliter] Sensim, Plin. Sine sensu.
units.tr: Insensibly: gradually, Plin. Without feeling.

units.la: Inseparabilis, vid. Indissolubilis.
units.tr: Inseparable: see Indissoluble.

units.la: Insepultus] Inhumatus, Virg. Inconditus, Lucan. Intumulatus, Ovid. Ossa inhonora, Pers.
units.tr: Unburied: unentombed, Virg. Unburied, Lucan. Not laid in a tomb, Ovid. Bones without honour, Pers.

units.la: Insequi aliquem] Sectari leporem, Hor. Persequi terrâ, mari. Consequi, Cic. Consectari. Prosequi, Caes. Persectari, Lucr.
units.tr: To pursue someone: to chase a hare, Hor. To pursue by land and sea. To overtake, Cic. To go after closely. To follow up, Caes. To pursue, Lucr.

units.la: Inserere] Deserere semen in terram. Immittere vitem, Varr. Defigere sarmentum in terram. Ingerere solo surculum, semen, Col. Indere, Plaut. Infulcire aliquod verbum omnibus locis, Sen. Vid. Depangere humi.
units.tr: To plant in: to sow seed in the earth. To set a vine, Varr. To fix a shoot in the ground. To set a slip or seed in the soil, Col. To insert, Plaut. To cram some word into every place, Sen. See To plant in the ground.

units.la: Inservire alicui] Subservire alicui, Plaut. Praeservire patri, Liv.
units.tr: To serve someone: to be subservient to someone, Plaut. To serve a father first, Liv.

units.la: Insidere, vid. Sedere.
units.tr: To sit upon: see To sit.

units.la: Insidiae] Subsessae, Veget.
units.tr: Ambushes] Ambuscades, Veget.

units.la: Insidiari alicui] Insidias alicui facere, comparare, locare, collocare, instruere, parare, ponere, opponere, moliri, tendere, Cic. Statuere insidias, Tac. Sustendere alicui insidias, Sal. Petere insidiis, Liv. Expandere rete. Circumponere escam hamo. Incumbere ad, in perniciem alicujus. Appetere vitam alicujus insidiis. Imminet in fortunas nostras, Cic. Intentare alicui periculum, Quint. Petere caput alicujus, Id. Oppugnare caput alicujus. Deposcere aliquem ad supplicium, Cic. Morti, Tac. Capite ac fortunis aliquem oppugnare, Cic.
units.tr: To lie in wait for someone: to set, prepare, place, arrange, contrive, plan, lay, oppose, devise or spread ambushes for someone, Cic. To set up an ambush, Tac. To lay traps for someone, Sall. To seek by ambush, Liv. To spread a net. To put bait on a hook. To lean toward someone's ruin. To seek someone's life by treachery. He hangs over our fortunes, Cic. To threaten someone with danger, Quint. To seek someone's head, Id. To attack someone's life. To demand someone for punishment, Cic. For death, Tac. To assail someone's life and fortune, Cic.

units.la: Insidiator] Subsessor alieni matrimonii, Val. M. Altera manu fert lapidem, altera panem ostendit. Panem & pugnum dat. Altera manu trahit, altera repellit. Altera scabit, altera ferit. Caduceum alterā, alterā hastam. Homo homini lupus. Panem praeferre manu, praefigere puppibus arma.
units.tr: Ambusher: one who lies in wait for another's marriage, Val. M. He carries a stone in one hand and shows bread in the other. He offers bread and a fist. He draws with one hand and repels with the other. He scratches with one and strikes with the other. A herald's staff in one hand, a spear in the other. Man is a wolf to man. He carries bread in one hand and sets weapons on the prows.

units.la: Insidiosa munera] Panis lapidosus. Hamatum beneficium. Pileum donat, ut pallium accipiat. Pauper diviti dans petit.
units.tr: Treacherous gifts: bread full of stones. A barbed kindness. He gives a cap so that he may receive a cloak. The poor man gives to the rich and asks in return.

units.la: Insidiosè] Ex insidiis aliquid facere. Per insidias, Cic.
units.tr: Treacherously: to do something out of ambush. By treachery, Cic.

units.la: Insignia vetusta gentis] Imagines majorum, Cic. Stemmata, Plin. Famosæ imagines.
units.tr: Ancient insignia of a family: images of ancestors, Cic. Family trees, Plin. Famous likenesses.

units.la: Insignia nobilium] Symbolum, Plin. Signum, Cic. Insignia imperii, Sallust.
units.tr: Insignia of nobles: an emblem, Plin. A sign, Cic. Insignia of empire, Sall.

units.la: Insignis, vid. Eximius, Notabilis.
units.tr: Conspicuous: see Outstanding, notable.

units.la: Insimulare, vid. Calumniari.
units.tr: To accuse falsely: see To slander.

units.la: Insincerus] Bilinguis animus, Firm. Vespertilio, Er. Malè sarta gratia, Hor. In fronte promptus. Gerens amicitiam atque inimicitiam, Enn. Maligni sunt cati, qui anterius lambunt, posterius laniant. Mel in ore, fel in corde. Vid. Hypocrita.
units.tr: Insincere: a double-tongued mind, Firm. A bat, Er. Ill-stitched favour, Hor. Ready on the forehead. Bearing both friendship and enmity, Enn. Malicious are the cats that lick in front and tear behind. Honey in the mouth, gall in the heart. See Hypocrite.

units.la: Insinuare se alicui] Insinuo me in familiaritatem alicujus. Blanditiis & assentationibus se in consuetudinem alicujus immergere. Adrepere ad amicitiam alicujus. Irrepere in sensus ; in mentes hominum ; in opinionem gratiæ. Inculcare se auribus alicujus. Intrare penitus ad familiaritatem alicujus. Influere in animos hominum. Dare se alicui, Cic. irrepere animo alicujus, Quint. Adrepere animo, Tac. Facere se intimum apud aliquem. Insinuare in amicitiam, Plaut. Adoptare seipsum. Obrepsisti ad honores errore hominum, Cic.
units.tr: To insinuate oneself with someone: I insinuate myself into someone's intimacy. To plunge into someone's habits by flattery and fawning. To creep up to someone's friendship. To slip into someone's feelings, into men's minds, into the opinion of favour. To push oneself into someone's ears. To enter deep into someone's intimacy. To flow into men's spirits. To give oneself to someone, Cic. To creep into someone's mind, Quint. To steal into the mind, Tac. To make oneself someone's intimate. To insinuate oneself into friendship, Plaut. To adopt oneself. You crept into honours through men's error, Cic.

units.la: Insipare] Insipitare, Cat. Fundere segetem, Liv. Corruere, Varr. Insipere, Id.
units.tr: To be foolish: Insipitare, Cat. To pour out a crop, Liv. To fall down, Varr. To be foolish, Id.

units.la: Insipidus] Infuscatus, Col. Fatuus, Mart. Teter sapor. Tristi sapore, Lucr. Tristis sapor, Ovid. Betâ magis insipidus, Er. Sine sale panis.
units.tr: Insipid: mouldy, Col. Foolish, Mart. A foul taste. With a sad taste, Lucr. A sad taste, Ovid. More insipid than beet, Er. Bread without salt.

units.la: Insipiens, vid. Stolidus.
units.tr: Foolish: see Stupid.

units.la: Insistere, vid. Restitare.
units.tr: To persist: see To resist.

units.la: Insitio, vid. Plantatio.
units.tr: Grafting: see Planting.

units.la: Insititius] Insitiva pyra, Hor. Insita pyrus, Virg.
units.tr: Grafted: a grafted pear, Hor. A grafted pear tree, Virg.

units.la: Insolare] Insolem producere aliquid, Col. Maturare aliquid sole, Plin. Candefacere ebur, Plaut.
units.tr: To expose to the sun: to bring something forth into the sun, Col. To ripen something by the sun, Plin. To whiten ivory, Plaut.

units.la: Insolator] Candidans vestes, Pompon.
units.tr: Bleacher: one who whitens garments, Pompon.

units.la: Insolitè] Insolenter, inusitatè. Novo more. Nullo exemplo, plo, Cic. Præter morem, Ter. Præter consuetudinem, Cic. Præter solitum, Virg.
units.tr: Unusually: out of the ordinary, in an unaccustomed way. In a new manner. With no precedent, Cic. Contrary to custom, Ter. Beyond habit, Cic. Beyond what is usual, Virg.

units.la: Insolitus] Inusitatus, insuetus mos. Non cadit in consuetudinem, Cic Infolentiffimum nomen, insolens verbum. Extra vulgarem usum politus, Quint. Alieni temporis flores, Capitol.
units.tr: Unusual: an unfamiliar custom, an unaccustomed practice. It does not fall into common use, Cic. A most unfamiliar name, an unusual word. Polished beyond ordinary use, Quint. The flowers of another age, Capitol.

units.la: Insolita nos afficiunt] Pulchra ac nova stupescimus.
units.tr: Unusual things move us: we are amazed at what is beautiful and new.

units.la: Insolubilis, vid Inexplicabilis.
units.tr: Insoluble: see Inexplicable.

units.la: Insomnia] Vigilia, Cic. Pervigilia, Iustin. Noctuma inquies, Plin. Excubatio, Val. M.
units.tr: Sleeplessness: wakefulness, Cic. Vigil, Just. Restlessness at night, Plin. A watch, Val. M.

units.la: Insomnis] Pervigilis, Mart. Exsomnis, Paterc. Pernox, Gell. Somnus abest ab oculis.
units.tr: Sleepless: wakeful, Mart. Without sleep, Paterc. Awake through the night, Gell. Sleep is absent from the eyes.

units.la: Insons, vid. Innocens.
units.tr: Innocent: see Innocent.

units.la: Inspector] Spectator officiorum alicujus diligens. Curator. Episcopus, Cic. Provisor, Hor. Epistata, vel Epistates, Bud. Lustrator, Apul. Antistes operarum in vineis. Procurator apum, Col. Arbiter, Plaut. Tutelarius, Plin. Visitator.
units.tr: Overseer: a diligent observer of another's duties. A curator. A bishop, Cic. A provider, Hor. Epistata or Epistates, Bud. A purifier, Apul. A supervisor of workers in the vineyards. A keeper of bees, Col. An arbiter, Plaut. A guardian, Plin. A visitor.

units.la: Insperans] Inopinans, Cæs. Nec opinans, Cic.
units.tr: Unexpecting: not anticipating, Caes. Not supposing, Cic.

units.la: Insperate] Inopinatè, & inopinatò. Ex insperato, Liv. Nec opinatò. Ex inopinato. Præter opinionem, exspectationem, spem, optatum. Insperanti mihi cecidit, Cic. Insperante me, Ter. Ante exspectatum, Virg. Postico falle clientem, Hor.
units.tr: Unexpectedly: unanticipated and unforeseen. Beyond expectation, Liv. Not supposed. Beyond opinion, expectation, hope or wish. It fell upon me when I did not hope for it, Cic. While I did not expect it, Ter. Before it was looked for, Virg. He deceives the client from behind, Hor.

units.la: Insperatus] Inopinatus, improvisus, Cic. Nec opinatus, Lucr. Inopinus, Virg. Inopinabilis, Gell. Inexspectatus hostis, Ovid. Insperabilis, Gell.
units.tr: Unhoped for: unanticipated, unforeseen, Cic. Not supposed, Lucr. Unlooked for, Virg. Not to be expected, Gell. An enemy not awaited, Ovid. Not to be hoped for, Gell.

units.la: Insperatum elabendi consilium] Dædaleis ferri remigiis. Dædaleis adjuti alis. Dædali alæ.
units.tr: An unexpected plan of escape] With Daedalean oars of iron. Aided by Daedalean wings. The wings of Daedalus.

units.la: Inspicere] Introspicere mentes hominum ; in omnes partes, Cic. Inspectare per impluvium, Plaut. Vid. Speculari.
units.tr: To look into] To look into the minds of men on every side, Cic. To peer through the impluvium, Plaut. See Speculari.

units.la: Inspirare] Afflatu divino mentem alicujus concitare. Oracula instinctu afflatuque divino tunduntur, Cic.
units.tr: To breathe into] To stir someone's mind by divine breath. Oracles are stirred by divine instinct and inspiration, Cic.

units.la: Inspiratio divina] Inflatus & afflatus divinus. Afflatus ita mentem movens, ut eam providam rerum futurarum efficias. Cœlestis instinctus mentis. Impetus divinus, Cic. Enthusiasmus, Cæl. Rhod. Vis, quæ mentem divino afflatu concitabat, Cic.
units.tr: Divine inspiration] A divine breathing into and upon. A breath that moves the mind so that you make it foresee future things. A heavenly impulse of the mind. A divine impetus, Cic. Enthusiasm, Cæl. Rhod. A power that stirred the mind with divine breath, Cic.

units.la: Inspiratus divinitus] Inspiratus vates. Deo impletus, Iustin. Deo plenus, Virg. Deo repletus, Iul. Capit. Tactus divino spiritu, Liv. Entheus, Firm. Entheatus, Mart. Furore sacro mens instincta, Lucan.
units.tr: Inspired by God] An inspired prophet. Filled by God, Iustin. Full of God, Virg. Filled by God, Iul. Capit. Touched by the divine spirit, Liv. Possessed by God, Firm. Possessed, Mart. A mind pricked by sacred frenzy, Lucan.

units.la: Instabilis] Hamaxobio instabilior. Vid. Inconstans.
units.tr: Unstable] More unstable than a Hamaxobius. See Inconstans.

units.la: Instante aliquo aliquid facere] Urgente amico facere. Id facias gratia, & gratiae causa, Cic. Mitte hanc mea gratia, Plaut.
units.tr: To do something while a friend presses] To act at a friend's urging. Do it as a favour and for the sake of favour, Cic. Let this go for my sake, Plaut.

units.la: Instanter] Instantissime, Gell. Vid. Importune.
units.tr: Urgently] Most urgently, Gell. See Importune.

units.la: Instantia, vid. Importunitas.
units.tr: Urgency, see Importunitas.

units.la: Instar] Instar montis, Virg. Ad instar filii, scoparum, Apul. Vice poetae. Sardanapali vice in lecto mori. More gigantum. Ritu latronum: pecudum, Cic. Ad speciem sideris. In modum pilae. Modo sagittae, Plin. Ad morem alicujus rei, Quint. In morem fluminis. More ferae vivere, Virg. Facie humani vestigii, Salust.
units.tr: Like, in the manner of] Like a mountain, Virg. In the manner of a son, of brooms, Apul. In place of a poet. In the place of Sardanapalus, to die in bed. In the manner of giants. In the manner of robbers; of cattle, Cic. In the likeness of a star. In the shape of a ball. In the manner of arrows, Plin. In the custom of a thing, Quint. In the manner of a river. To live in the manner of a wild beast, Virg. With the appearance of a human footprint, Salust.

units.la: Instare, vid. Urgere.
units.tr: To press upon, see Urgere.

units.la: Instaurare, instauratio, vid. Renovare, renovatio.
units.tr: To restore, restoration, see Renovare, renovatio.

units.la: Insternere] Superinsternere. Stramentis aliquid exaggerare, Col. Vid. Sternere.
units.tr: To spread over] To spread over, to heap straw over something, Col. See Sternere.

units.la: Instigare] Inflammare mentes aliorum in aliquem, Cic. Sufflare aliquem, Amm. Frigidam suffundere, Plaut. Subjicere faces invidiae. Subjicere ignem. Incitare, concitare aliquem in alium. Acuere ad crudelitatem, Cic. Instimulare, Ovid. Subdere stimulos alicui, Liv.
units.tr: To incite] To inflame the minds of others against someone, Cic. To blow upon someone, Amm. To pour cold water on, Plaut. To put firebrands of hatred under. To set fire under. To stir up, rouse one against another. To sharpen to cruelty, Cic. To goad, Ovid. To apply spurs to someone, Liv.

units.la: Instigatio] Ex suggestu alicujus facere, Vlp. Instinctus, Firm. Insufurratio, Capit.
units.tr: Incitement] To act from someone's platform, Vlp. Prompting, Firm. Whispering, Capit.

units.la: Instigator] Fax accusationis, Plin. Iun. Exstimulator acerrimus, Tac. Incentivum apud patulas aures alicujus. Suffiantes adulatores, Amm. Fornacula totius calumniae iste est, Apul.
units.tr: Instigator] A torch of accusation, Plin. Iun. A most fierce goader, Tac. A spur to someone's open ears. Fawning flatterers, Amm. This fellow is the little furnace of all calumny, Apul.

units.la: Institor] Propola. Obsessor fori. Caupo, Plaut. Coactor, Cic. Manceps annonae, Plin. Annonarius, Alciat.
units.tr: Retailer] A petty dealer. A besieger of the forum. An innkeeper, Plaut. A collector, Cic. A contractor for the grain supply, Plin. A corn dealer, Alciat.

units.la: Institoria taberna] Taberna, Hor. Tabernula, Suet.
units.tr: Shop] A shop, Hor. A little shop, Suet.

units.la: Instituere, vid. Statuere, instruere.
units.tr: To appoint, see Statuere, instruere.

units.la: Institutio] Disciplina, Eruditio alicujus. Doctrina puerilis. Cultura animi. Exercitatio. Praeceptio. Praeceptum. Documentum, mentum, Cic. Doctrinæ pretium triste magister habet, Ovid. Vid. Exercitatio.
units.tr: Instruction] The training and education of someone. Childhood teaching. Cultivation of the mind. Practice. Precept. Rule. Lesson, Cic. The reward of learning is bitter; the teacher keeps it, Ovid. See Exercitatio.

units.la: Instruere ] Initiare infantem Eduliæ, Varr. Inolescere, Mart. Innutrire, innutritus disciplinis, Sen. Exercere equos, Virg. Instituere aliquem ad aliquid, Cic. Inescare homines, Ter.
units.tr: To instruct] To initiate an infant into food, Varr. To grow up, Mart. To nourish; one brought up in the disciplines, Sen. To train horses, Virg. To instruct someone in something, Cic. To lure men, Ter.

units.la: Instrumentum res operandi] Organum ad agros dividendos. Parsimonia non mediocre telum ad virtutem, Cic. Machina, Virt. Arma coquinaria, tonsoria, Mart.
units.tr: Instrument, a thing for working with] A tool for dividing fields. Thrift is no small weapon toward virtue, Cic. A machine, Virt. Kitchen and barber's implements, Mart.

units.la: Insuavis, vid. Injucundus.
units.tr: Unpleasant, see Injucundus.

units.la: Insuetudo] Insolentia loci, Cic. Sermonis, Liv.
units.tr: Unaccustomedness] The strangeness of a place, Cic. Of speech, Liv.

units.la: Insuetus] Inconsuetus, Sili. Indocilis alibi nasci arbor, Plin. Insolens contumeliæ, Tac. Infamiæ, Cic. Insolitus ad laborem, Cæs. Inassuetus equus, inassueta manus, Ovid.
units.tr: Unaccustomed] Not used to, Sil. A tree that will not grow elsewhere, Plin. Unused to insult, Tac. Unused to disgrace, Cic. Unused to labour, Caes. An unbroken horse, an untrained hand, Ovid.

units.la: Insulsè, vid. Stolidè.
units.tr: Foolishly, see Stolidè.

units.la: Insultare alicui] Ludificari mala alicujus, Plin.Jun.
units.tr: To mock someone] To make light of someone's misfortunes, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Insultatio] Opprobrium, Hor. Lœdoria. Exprobratio ad directam contumeliam, Macrob. Incavillatio, Fest.
units.tr: Mockery] Reproach, Hor. Scorn. Rebuke amounting to direct insult, Macrob. Ridicule, Fest.

units.la: Insuper, vid. Præterea.
units.tr: Besides, see Præterea.

units.la: Insuperabilis, vid. Impervius, invictus.
units.tr: Insuperable, see Impervius, invictus.

units.la: Insurgere, vid. Attollere se.
units.tr: To rise up, see Attollere se.

units.la: Insurgere adversus aliquem ] Consurgere in arma, Virg. Vertere iras in aliquem. Vertere arma adversus aliquem, ex Liv. Rebellare alicui, Id. Convertere se in aliquem, Cic.
units.tr: To rise up against someone] To rise up in arms, Virg. To turn anger upon someone. To turn arms against someone, ex Liv. To rebel against someone, Id. To turn oneself against someone, Cic.

units.la: Insusurrare, vid. Susurrare, Murmurare.
units.tr: To whisper, see Susurrare, Murmurare.

units.la: Intactus] Diana intactior, Er. Vid. seqq.
units.tr: Untouched] More untouched than Diana, Er. See what follows.

units.la: Integer] Integellus, Catul. Salva Respub. Incolume & salvum est aliquid, illibatus cortex. Sartum, tectum, integrumque corpus. Sacrosanctus, Cic. In integro est vobis fortuna, Tac. Solidum beneficium, Ter. Inattenuata fames, Ovid. Sospes navis ab ignibus, Hor. Intactus, Plin. Vid. Incorruptus.
units.tr: Whole] A little whole thing, Catul. The commonwealth safe. Something unharmed and safe; an unbroken bark. A whole, intact and unharmed body. Sacrosanct, Cic. Fortune is open to you, Tac. A solid kindness, Ter. Hunger undiminished, Ovid. A ship saved from the fires, Hor. Untouched, Plin. See Incorruptus.

units.la: Integrè, vid. Probè, Sincere.
units.tr: Uprightly, see Probè, Sincere.

units.la: Integritas] Salus Reipub. Incolumitas civitatis, Cic.
units.tr: Integrity] The welfare of the commonwealth, the safety of the state, Cic.

units.la: Integrum] Cum ramento reddere. Cum tota ærugine. Cum pulvisculo. In totum. Per omnia, Col.
units.tr: Entire] To return with the rust removed. With all the verdigris. With the dust. Wholly. In every respect, Col.

units.la: Integrum est, vid Liberum est.
units.tr: It is open, see Liberum est.

units.la: Integumentum, vid. Tegumentum.
units.tr: Covering, see Tegumentum.

units.la: Intellectus] Rationis & intelligentiæ particeps. Mens, Cic. Animus, Iuv. Speculum imaginum plenum.
units.tr: Understanding] A sharer in reason and intelligence. Mind, Cic. Spirit, Iuv. A mirror full of images.

units.la: Intellexi faciam] Factum puta, Ter.
units.tr: I will make it so] Consider it done, Ter.

units.la: Intelligenter ] Luculentè, accommodatè ad intelligentiam dicere. Planè & dilucidè loqui. Apertissimè & planissimè explicare, Cicer. Plani loquus sum, Plaut.
units.tr: Intelligently] To speak clearly and suitably for understanding. To speak plainly and lucidly. To explain most openly and plainly, Cicer. I speak plainly, Plaut.

units.la: Intelligentia]Cognitio veritatis, Perceptio, intellectus disciplinarum, Cic. Intellectio, ad Heren.
units.tr: Understanding] Knowledge of the truth; perception; grasp of the disciplines, Cic. Comprehension, ad Heren.

units.la: Intelligere] Intelligentiam alicujus rei habere. Putatur intelligens in hac re, Cic. Tenes, quid dicam? Ter. Pervidere, Col.
units.tr: To understand] To have an understanding of something. He is thought to understand this matter, Cic. Do you grasp what I mean? Ter. To see through, Col.

units.la: Non intelligere ] Parum, vel minùs intelligere. Parum accipere. Non comprehendere animo, mente. Quæso quid agitur, mihi enim sunt tenebræ, Cic. Non sum divinus, Oedipus. Fugit me ratio, Plaut. Oratio ejus à multitudine devoratur, i. non intelligitur, Cic. Scot. Nihil horum recipit mens, Lucr. Animus non capit, Cic. Non sum divinator. Non sum vates.
units.tr: Not to understand] To understand little or less. To take in little. Not to grasp with the mind or intellect. Please, what is going on? For to me it is darkness, Cic. I am not the divine Oedipus. Reason escapes me, Plaut. His speech is swallowed up by the crowd, that is, it is not understood, Cic. Scot. The mind takes in none of these, Lucr. The mind does not grasp it, Cic. I am no diviner. I am no seer.

units.la: Non intelligere se mutuò] Alter de cœpis, alter de alliis.
units.tr: Not to understand one another] One speaks of onions, the other of garlic.

units.la: Intelligibilis ] Comprehensibilis. Cognitionem habens facilem. In intelligentiam cadit. Opinabilis, Cicer. Facilis ad intelligendum, Quint. Disciplinalis scientia, ad Heren.
units.tr: Intelligible] Comprehensible. Having an easy knowledge. Falls within understanding. Conjectural, Cicer. Easy to understand, Quint. Knowledge that can be taught, ad Heren.

units.la: Intemeratus, vid. Inviolatus.
units.tr: Inviolate, see Inviolatus.

units.la: Intemperans] Immoderatus pastus, potus, Cic. Luxuriæ immodestissimæ, Suet. Vehemens in utramque partem. Immodicus, Ter.
units.tr: Intemperate] Immoderate food and drink, Cic. The most immodest luxuries, Suet. Vehement in either direction. Immoderate, Ter.

units.la: Intemperanter] Intemperantius, intemperatè, & immoderatè vivere. Insolenter se efferre, Cic. Extra numerum modumque, Hor. Intemperantissimè, Apul.
units.tr: Intemperately] To live more intemperately, that is, without restraint and immoderately. To carry oneself insolently, Cic. Beyond number and measure, Hor. Most intemperately, Apul.

units.la: Intemperantia ] Nimietas pabuli, Immoderatio, Col.
units.tr: Intemperance] Excess of fodder; immoderation, Col.

units.la: Intemperantia plures perimit, quàm gladius] Marte ipso fortior Bacchus.
units.tr: Intemperance kills more than the sword] Bacchus is more dangerous than Mars himself.

units.la: Intempestas, vid. Tempestas.
units.tr: Untimely, see Tempestas.

units.la: Intempestivè, vid. Incommodè.
units.tr: Unsuitably, see Incommodè.

units.la: Intempestivè agere] Inter lugentes gaudere.
units.tr: To act untimely] To rejoice among mourners.

units.la: Intempestivè diligens] In otio tumultuosi, in bello segnes.
units.tr: Untimely diligent] Stirred up in peacetime, sluggish in war.

units.la: Intempestivè fortes] In prælio cervi, in pace leones.
units.tr: Untimely brave] Stags in battle, lions in peace.

units.la: Intempestivus, vid. Serus, inopportunus.
units.tr: Untimely, see Serus, inopportunus.

units.la: Intendere arcum] Contendere ballistam, Cic. Adducere arcum, Virg. Tormentum, Cic.
units.tr: To bend a bow] To bend a crossbow, Cic. To draw the bow, Virg. A siege engine, Cic.

units.la: Intentatum nihil relinquere] Extrema, ultima experiri. Omnem movere lapidem.
units.tr: To leave nothing untried] To try the last and final means. To move every stone.

units.la: Intentum esse negotio] Intendere animum in aliquid, Liv. Satagere rerum suarum. vel, Agere sat, ut, Egi satis, & sui homo exercitus, Plaut. Quod agis, agas. Age quod in manu est, Plaut. Sudare pro aliquo, Cic. Semper tibi pendeat hamus, Ovid. Hoc age. Vid. Conari.
units.tr: To be intent on business] To direct the mind to something, Liv. To attend to one's own affairs, or: enough, as in "I have done enough," and a man busy with his own affairs, Plaut. Do what you are doing. Do what is at hand, Plaut. To sweat for someone, Cic. Let your hook always hang ready, Ovid. Mind this business. See Conari.

units.la: Inter] Inter nos, illos, &c. Nisi in bonis (i. inter bonos) amicitiam esse non posse, Cic.
units.tr: Between] Between us, them, and so on. Unless friendship can exist only among the good, Cic.

units.la: Intercalare] Interserere, Macr. Inter duos menses, mentem, diem, interjicere, Suet.
units.tr: To intercalate] To insert, Macr. To put in a month or a day between two months, Suet.

units.la: Intercalaris mensis] Intercalarius, Suet. Embolimus, Cæl. Rhod. Additicius, Bud.
units.tr: Intercalary month] An intercalary month, Suet. An embolimus, Cæl. Rhod. An additional month, Bud.

units.la: Intercapedo, vid. Cessatio.
units.tr: Interval, see Cessatio.

units.la: Intercedere pro aliquo] Deprecari pro sodali. Supplicare alicui pro aliquo. Operam suam pro aliquo interponere. Juvare aliquem apud aliquem, Cic. Postulare pro aliquo, Gell. Interponere se, Cic.
units.tr: To intercede for someone] To entreat on behalf of a companion. To plead with someone for someone. To put one's own effort in for someone. To help someone with someone, Cic. To demand on someone's behalf, Gell. To interpose oneself, Cic.

units.la: Intercessio] Suffragatio pro salute. Allegatio. Deprecatio, Cic. Intercursus, Tac.
units.tr: Intercession] Support for someone's safety. Pleading. Entreaty, Cic. An intervening course, Tac.

units.la: Intercessor] Deprecator, Cic. Precator, Ter.
units.tr: Intercessor] One who entreats, Cic. A supplicant, Ter.

units.la: Intercidere, vid. Perire.
units.tr: To perish, see Perire.

units.la: Intercidere, vid. Intersecare.
units.tr: To cut off, see Intersecare.

units.la: Intercipere aliquid] Præripere consilia hostium, Cic.
units.tr: To intercept something] To snatch away the plans of the enemy, Cic.

units.la: Intercus] Intercutia vitia, Gell. Subcutaneus, Subtercutaneus, Sip.
units.tr: Under the skin] Diseases under the skin, Gell. Subcutaneous, subtercutaneous, Sip.

units.la: Interdicere rem aliquam, & re aliquâ] Vetare, Cavere lege aliquid. Publicis exsecrationibus aliquid sancitum est, Cic. Interminari, interminatus sum ne faceres, Ter.
units.tr: To forbid a thing, and to forbid from a thing] To prohibit, to guard by law against something. Something was sanctioned by public curses, Cic. I forbade you to do it, Ter.

units.la: Interdictum] Interdictio ignis & aquæ. Vetitum, Cic.
units.tr: Interdict] Prohibition from fire and water. Forbidden, Cic.

units.la: Interdiu, vid. Die.
units.tr: By day, see Die.

units.la: Interdum, vid. Aliquando.
units.tr: Sometimes, see Aliquando.

units.la: Interest, vid. Refert. Nihil interest.
units.tr: It matters, see Refert. Nihil interest.

units.la: Interfari] Interrumpere sermonem, Plaut. Obsonare alicui sermone, Id. Dirimere colloquium, Caes. Interpellare aliquem. Obloqui, Cic. Interloqui alicui. Obturbare. Davus interturbat, Ter. Intercipere medium sermonem, Quint. Appellare aliquem, Hor.
units.tr: To interrupt] To interrupt a conversation, Plaut. To break in on talk, Id. To break off a discussion, Caes. To interrupt someone. To object, Cic. To speak against someone, Cic. To disturb. Davus interrupts, Ter. To seize the middle of a speech, Quint. To address someone, Hor.

units.la: Interfector, vid. Homicida.
units.tr: Killer, see Homicida.

units.la: Interficere, vid. Occidere.
units.tr: To kill, see Occidere.

units.la: Interjacere] Jacere inter, interjectus inter mare & coelum, intermedius est, Cic. Intercedunt silvae, Caes. Intercest amnis, Liv. Interveniente flumine, Plin. Intersita agnis praedia, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: To lie between] To lie between: what lies between sea and sky is the middle, Cic. Forests lie between, Caes. A river lies between, Liv. With a river intervening, Plin. Estates lying between the sheep-pastures, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Interim] Inter haec. Per id tempus. Per illa tempora. Interjecto spatio, Liv. Interea. Hoc interim spatio. Tantisper, Cic. Sub hoc tempus, Hor. Medio tempore, Suet.
units.tr: Meanwhile] In the meantime. At that time. In those times. With an interval intervening, Liv. Meanwhile. In this interval. For so long, Cic. At this time, Hor. In the meantime, Suet.

units.la: Interior] Intimus angulus, Hor. Intestinus dolor. Penetrales & abditi foci, Cic. Penitae medullae, Apul.
units.tr: Interior] An innermost corner, Hor. Inward pain. Inmost and hidden hearths, Cic. Inmost marrows, Apul.

units.la: Interitus, vid. Exitium.
units.tr: Interitus, see Exitium.

units.la: Interlinere] Inducere nomina. Multa erant deleta & inducta. Interlitus codex. Circumscribere, Cic. Litura coercere aliquid, incomptis allinet atrum transverso calamo signum. Vertere stylum, Hor. Liturare, Sidon.
units.tr: Interlinere] To insert names. Many things were deleted and inserted. A codex interlined. To cross out around, Cic. To correct something by blotting it out: a black mark is drawn across it with a crooked pen, allinet, Hor. To turn the stylus (to erase), Hor. To blot out, Sidon.

units.la: Interlocutio] Interpellatio, Cic.
units.tr: Interlocutio] Interruption, Cic.

units.la: Interloqui, vid. Interfari.
units.tr: Interloqui, see Interfari.

units.la: Interlunium] Corbis lunae. Coelum sine luna. Silentium lunae. Luna aversa, tacens, Virg. Luna silens, cava, intermenstrua, Varr. Concursus solis & lunae, Cels. Luna synodica, Firm. Sicca luna, Propert.
units.tr: Interlunium] The basket of the moon. A sky without a moon. The silence of the moon. The moon turned away and silent, Virg. The moon silent, hollow, between the menses, Varr. Conjunction of the sun and moon, Cels. The synodic moon, Firm. The dry moon, Propert.

units.la: Intermittere, vid. Cessare.
units.tr: Intermittere, see Cessare.

units.la: Internecio, vid. Clades.
units.tr: Internecio, see Clades.

units.la: Ad internecionem cadere] Occisione occidere copias alicujus, Cic. Internecino bello certatur. Uno praelio occidit res Vestinorum, Liv. Occidione copiae occubuerunt, Tacit. Ne nuncius quidem relictus. Vid. Cadere exitial.
units.tr: Ad internecionem cadere] To destroy someone's forces by slaughter, Cic. A war of extermination is fought. In a single battle the power of the Vestini was destroyed, Liv. The forces perished by slaughter, Tacit. Not even a messenger was left. See Cadere exitial.

units.la: Internuncius] Commeator. Mediator, Apul. Loquelaris servus, ex Fest. Interventor, Vlp.
units.tr: Internuncius] A go-between. A mediator, Apul. A servant who carries messages, ex Fest. An intervener, Vlp.

units.la: Interpellare, vid. Interfari.
units.tr: Interpellare, see Interfari.

units.la: Interpolare] Reconcinnare vestem. Denuo fingere,Plaut.
units.tr: Interpolare] To patch up a garment. To remake anew, Plaut.

units.la: Interpolator] Rudiarius, Fest. Mango, Plin. Interpolatrix, Pompon.
units.tr: Interpolator] A rough amateur, Fest. A dealer who doctors his wares, Plin. A female interpolator, Pompon.

units.la: Interpolatus] Interpolis, Plaut. Redivivus, Cic.
units.tr: Interpolatus] Refurbished, Plaut. Restored to life, Cic.

units.la: Interponere] Interserere, Plaut. Interjicere, Caes. Intergerere, Fest. Intertexere, includere orationem in literas, Cic. Inserere, Ovid.
units.tr: Interponere] To insert, Plaut. To throw in between, Caes. To thrust in, Fest. To interweave, to work a speech into a letter, Cic. To insert, Ovid.

units.la: Interpositio] Interpositus, interjectus, Cic. Parenthesis, interjectio, interclusio, Quint.
units.tr: Interpositio] Interposed, interjected, Cic. A parenthesis, an interjection, an interruption, Quint.

units.la: Interpres] Communis Mercurius. Metaphrastes.
units.tr: Interpres] The common Mercury. A translator.

units.la: Interpretari] Communem agere Mercurium. Convertere è Graeco in Latinum. Reddere aliquid Latinè. Vertere de Graecis aliquid, Cic. Transferre Graecos authores: ad verbum aliquid, Quint.
units.tr: Interpretari] To act as the common Mercury. To turn from Greek into Latin. To render something into Latin. To translate something from the Greeks, Cic. To transfer Greek authors, word for word, Quint.

units.la: Interpretatio] Metaphrasis, Rhodig.
units.tr: Interpretatio] A metaphrase, Rhodig.

units.la: Interpunctio, vid. Intervallum.
units.tr: Interpunctio, see Intervallum.

units.la: Interpungere, vid. Dispescere.
units.tr: Interpungere, see Dispescere.

units.la: Interrex, vid. Prorex.
units.tr: Interrex, see Prorex.

units.la: Interrogare] Rogare aliquem aliquid, de aliquo. Scisci tari aliquid ex aliquo, inquirere de aliquâ re. Quaestionem habere. Contari; percontari, de aliqua re: aliquid ab aliquo. Quaerere, requirere aliquid ex aliquo, Cic. Rogitare aliquem, Ter. Vocare ad sermonis exiguam responsionem, Arnob.
units.tr: Interrogare] To ask someone something, about something. To inquire of someone about something, to look into a matter. To hold an inquiry. To question someone about something; to ask something of someone. To seek, to ask someone something, Cic. To question someone repeatedly, Ter. To call someone to a brief answer in conversation, Arnob.

units.la: Interrogatio] Interrogatiuncula. Quaestio. Quaestiuncula. Percontatio. Rogatio, Cic. Quaesitum, Ovid.
units.tr: Interrogatio] A little question. An inquiry. A small inquiry. An enquiry. A question, Cic. A matter asked, Ovid.

units.la: Interrumpere] Intercipere iter, Liv. Praecidere sermonem. Distrahere judicium, Cic. Incidere verba, Stat. Intercidere, rescindere pontem, Caes. Vid. Impedire.
units.tr: Interrumpere] To cut off the course, Liv. To cut short a speech. To break off a trial, Cic. To break off words, Stat. To cut off, to demolish a bridge, Caes. See Impedire.

units.la: Interrupte] Incisim, incisè, caesim, membratim dicere, Cic. Singultim loqui, Hor. Interjectibus capere fructum, Col.
units.tr: Interrupte] To speak in broken clauses, in short phrases, piece by piece, limb by limb, Cic. To speak with sobs, Hor. To take pleasure in interjections, Col.

units.la: Interruptio] Abruptio. Rumentum, Fest. Ruptio, Ulp.
units.tr: Interruptio] A breaking off. A ruin, Fest. A rupture, Ulp.

units.la: Interruptus] Solutus sopor clamore, Ovid. Intervigilus somnus, Sen. Abruptus, Liv.
units.tr: Interruptus] Sleep broken by a shout, Ovid. Sleep broken by waking, Sen. Broken off, Liv.

units.la: Intersecare] Intercidere venas, Plin. Interscindere vinculum, Gell. Distruncare aliquem medium. Transcindere aliquid, Plaut. Scindere os hulceris, Virg. Persecare, Cic. Praecidere. Discindere ferro aliquid in partes, Lucr. Intertrigo] Attritus, Plin. Copulæ tritura, Apul.
units.tr: Intersecare] To cut out the veins, Plin. To sever a bond, Gell. To cut someone in two through the middle. To cut through something, Plaut. To cut the mouth of a sore, Virg. To cut through, Cic. To cut off in front. To cut something into pieces with iron, Lucr. Intertrigo] Chafing, Plin. Rubbing of the joints, Apul.
