units.la: Interturbare, vid. Inquietare.
units.tr: Interturbare, see Inquietare.

units.la: Intervallum] Discidium orbis, Solin. Interpunctio, interpunctum verborum, interduƈtus, interjectus, interpositus terræ. Mons divisus aquarum divortiū. Discrimen, Cic. Divisura, Plin. Interstitiis elementa separantur, Macrob. Fretus anni. Freta ætatis, Lucr.
units.tr: Intervallum] A division of the globe, Solin. A punctuation, a space between words, an interval, a strip of land lying between. A mountain dividing the waters, a watershed, divortium. A distinction, Cic. A dividing line, Plin. The elements are separated by intervals, Macrob. The strait of the year. The straits of life, Lucr.

units.la: Intervenire] Supervenire, Liv. Obvenit vitium. Intercurrere, Cic. Intercessit casus, Cæs.
units.tr: Intervenire] To come upon, Liv. A defect comes in the way. To run in between, Cic. An accident intervened, Caes.

units.la: Interventus] Superventus, Plin. Obitus sermo. Adventus tuus, Ter. Intercessione unâ morbos centum sanabat, Arnob. de Christo.
units.tr: Interventus] A coming upon, Plin. A report of a death. Your arrival, Ter. By one intervention he healed a hundred diseases, Arnob. of Christ.

units.la: Interula, vid. Indusium.
units.tr: Interula, see Indusium.

units.la: Intestatus] Intestato mortuus, Cic. Ab intestato, Afran. Intestabilis, Vlp.
units.tr: Intestatus] Died intestate, Cic. From intestacy, Afran. Disqualified as a witness, Vlp.

units.la: Intestina] Interanea, Plin. Annulus in præcordiis piscis inventus est, Cic.
units.tr: Intestina] The entrails, Plin. A ring was found in the heart-region of a fish, Cic.

units.la: Intimè] Toto pectore, ex animo, medullitus, Cic. Oculitus, corde, animo, viribus prosequi aliquid. Effictim, Plaut. Plus oculis suis aliquem amare, Catul.
units.tr: Intimè] With the whole heart, from the soul, to the marrow, Cic. To pursue something with eyes, heart, soul and strength. Entirely, Plaut. To love someone more than one's own eyes, Catul.

units.la: Intimus] De tuis unus. Hic fervor in venis medullisque insedit. Quicum joca seriaque, quicum arcana occultaque omnia (sunt mihi communia) Cic. Devotus est, deditus est alicui cliens, Iuv. Devotissimus alicui, Sen.
units.tr: Intimus] One of your own circle. This ardour has settled in my veins and marrow. With whom I share jests and serious matters, with whom all secrets and hidden things are held in common (are common to me), Cic. He is devoted, a client attached to someone, Juv. Most devoted to someone, Sen.

units.la: Intinctus, us] Tinctura, Plin.
units.tr: Intinctus, us] A dipping, Plin.

units.la: Intingere] Intingere aliquid, Cat. Tingere, & tingi, in aliquo, Celf. Tingere ferrum sanguine, Ovid.
units.tr: Intingere] To dip something, Cato. To tinge, and to be tinged, with something, Celsus. To stain iron with blood, Ovid.

units.la: Intolerabilis] Intolerandus, impatibilis pœna. Non ferendus. Nemini tolerabilis. Toleratu difficilis. Odor oris & corporis tæterrimus, quem ne bestiæ quidem ferre possunt. Tantus dolor &c. ut jam ista non modò homines, sed ne pecudes quidem mihi passuræ videantur, Cic. Intolerans, intolerantior servitus, Tac. Gravis, Suet, Insustentabilis dominatio, Lactant.
units.tr: Intolerabilis] An intolerable punishment, not to be borne. Not bearable to anyone. Hard to endure. A foul breath from mouth and body, which even beasts cannot bear. Such great pain, etc., that now these things seem likely to affect not only men but not even beasts, Cic. Intolerant, more intolerable slavery, Tac. Heavy, Suet. An unbearable dominion, Lactant.

units.la: Intoleranter] Intolerantissimè, Cicer. Intolerabiliter, Col.
units.tr: Intoleranter] Most intolerantly, Cicer. Intolerably, Col.

units.la: Intorquere] Intorquere mentum. Cervices oculosque torquere. quere, Cic. Torquere collum, Liv. Obtorquere collum alicui, Plin. Gulam, Cic. Retorquere, Plin. Iun. Prætorquere caput, Col. Replicare, Cato.
units.tr: Intorquere] To twist the chin. To turn the necks and eyes, Cic. To twist the neck, Liv. To wring someone's neck, Plin. To twist the throat, Cic. To twist back, Plin. Iun. To turn the head aside, Col. To unfold again, Cato.

units.la: Intractabilis] Intactilis. Suffugit tactum manum, Lucr. Incontiguus tactu Deus, Arnob. Difficilis, morosus, durus & ferreus homo, Cic. Inflexibilis, Plin.
units.tr: Intractabilis] Not tangible. He shrinks from the touch of a hand, Lucr. God, not to be touched by contact, Arnob. A difficult, morose, hard and iron-hearted man, Cic. Inflexible, Plin.

units.la: Intrare] Ingredi, inire domum, introire in, inferre pedem, Cic. Initare, Pacuv. Introgredi, Virg. Introitum facere, Col. Facere se intra limen, Apul. Subire tectum, Caes. Penetrare, penitus intrare, Fest. Penetrare se in, Gell. Succedere urbi, Virg. Invehitur victor in Capitolium, Cic.
units.tr: Intrare] To go in, to enter a house, to go into, to set foot in, Cic. To go in, Pacuv. To go into, Virg. To make an entrance, Col. To make oneself within the threshold, Apul. To enter under the roof, Caes. To penetrate, to go deeply in, Fest. To penetrate into, Gell. To approach a city, Virg. He rides victorious into the Capitol, Cic.

units.la: Intrepide] Impavide, Liv.
units.tr: Intrepide] Fearlessly, Liv.

units.la: Intrepidus, vid. Impavidus.
units.tr: Intrepidus, see Impavidus.

units.la: Intricare] In tricas conjicere. Perplexari, Plaut. Solvas quod male implicuisti, Sen.
units.tr: Intricare] To throw into tangles. To be perplexed, Plaut. You may untie what you have tangled badly, Sen.

units.la: Intricatum negotium] Contorta oratio. Contortulae conclusiunculae, inextricabilis, inenodabilis, Cic. Pertricosus, Mart. Inexplicabilis error, Plin. Res involutissimae, Sen. Nec caput, nec pedes habet. Labyrintho intricatior. Vid. Perplexus.
units.tr: Intricatum negotium] A twisted speech. Twisted little arguments, inextricable, inexplicable, Cic. Full of snares, Mart. An inexplicable error, Plin. Most involved affairs, Sen. It has neither head nor feet. More intricate than a labyrinth. See Perplexus.

units.la: Introducere] Inducere personam: novum verbum in linguam, Cic. Isocratem Plato facit laudari à Socrate, Id.
units.tr: Introducere] To introduce a character; to bring a new word into the language, Cic. Plato makes Isocrates praised by Socrates, Id.

units.la: Introitus] Ingressio, Cic. Ingressus, Quint. Initus, Lucr. Ephodos, Firm.
units.tr: Introitus] Entrance, Cic. Entering, Quint. Going in, Lucr. Approach [ἔφοδος], Firm.

units.la: Intromittere, vid. Immittere.
units.tr: Intromittere, see Immittere.

units.la: Introrsum] Intro ferre, Cic. Interius pergens, Amm. Introrsus, Varr. Intra tecta vocare, Virg. Intus compellere, Cels.
units.tr: Introrsum] To bring inward, Cic. Proceeding further inward, Amm. Inwards, Varr. To call within the roof, Virg. To drive inside, Cels.

units.la: Intrudere aliquid] Infulcire, Sen. Detrudere. Detrudi ac compingi in pistrinum, Cic.
units.tr: Intrudere aliquid] To cram something in, Sen. To thrust down. To be thrust down and shut up in the mill-house, Cic.

units.la: Intueri, vid. Speculari.
units.tr: Intueri, see Speculari.

units.la: Intumescere] Invaserunt misero in genua flemina, Plaut. Intumuit caput, Ovid. Obturgescit pes, Lucr. Tumere, Plaut. Obturgere, Lucil. Inflari, Cic. Extumescere. Extuberat aliquid, Plin.
units.tr: Intumescere] Rheums invaded his wretched knees, Plaut. The head swelled, Ovid. The foot swells up, Lucr. To swell, Plaut. To swell up, Lucil. To be inflated, Cic. To swell out. Something bulges out, Plin.

units.la: Inturbatus] Inturbidus, Tac. Imperturbato, ore bibit venenum, Ovid.
units.tr: Inturbatus] Undisturbed, clear, Tac. Unperturbed, with steady face he drank the poison, Ovid.

units.la: Intus] Intrà, Col. Intrinsecus, Plin. Interius, Sen. Introrsus, Liv. Penitus in visceribus, Cic. Intrò, Cat.
units.tr: Intus] Within, Col. Inwardly, Plin. More inwardly, Sen. Inwards, Liv. Deep within the bowels, Cic. Inside, Cato.

units.la: Intutus, vid. Periculosus.
units.tr: Intutus, see Periculosus.

units.la: Invadere aliquem] Petere caput alicujus, Quint. Incursare fortunas omnium, ad Her. Infestus fertur in suos, Cic. Incursitare, Sen. Infesta latrociniis pascua, Liv. Vexare urbem Legionibus, Claud. Irruere in aliquem, Cic. Impetere aliquem, Tac. Impetum in aliquem facere, Cic. Dare, Liv. Adpugnare classem, Tac. Grassari in aliquem, Liv. Involare aliquem, Apul.
units.tr: Invadere aliquem] To seek the head of someone, Quint. To attack the fortunes of everyone, ad Her. He is borne hostile against his own people, Cic. To run at repeatedly, Sen. Pastures infested with robbers, Liv. To harass a city with legions, Claud. To rush upon someone, Cic. To assail someone, Tac. To make an attack upon someone, Cic. To make a charge, Liv. To storm a fleet, Tac. To rage against someone, Liv. To fly at someone, Apul.

units.la: Invalescere] Convalescunt opes alicujus, Liv. Potentiam consequi. Obdurescere. Firmitatem nancisci, Cic. Robur accipere, Col. Invalere, Lucr. Aggravescit vulnus. Latescit aliquid, Cic. Serpit consuetudo, Id. Evagatur vis morbi, Gliscit seditio, Liv.
units.tr: Invalescere] Someone's resources grow strong, Liv. To attain power. To harden. To gain firmness, Cic. To receive strength, Col. To grow strong, Lucr. A wound grows worse. Something spreads, Cic. Custom creeps in, Id. The force of the disease spreads abroad. Sedition flares up, Liv.

units.la: Invaletudo, vid. Morbus.
units.tr: Invaletudo, see Morbus.

units.la: Invasio] Incursio in agros hostium, incursus militum. Aggressio, Cic. Impressio in castra facta, Varr. Insultura, Plaut. Assultus, Virg. Impressus, us, Amm. Pedatus. Nisi pedatu tertio omnes afflixero, Cat. Aggressura, Vlp. Incursitatio, Iuv. Insultus.
units.tr: Invasio] A raid into the enemy's fields, a sally of soldiers. An assault, Cic. An attack made on a camp, Varr. A leaping on, Plaut. An assault, Virg. Impressus, us, Amm. A stepping: unless I shall have struck down all with a third step, Cato. An attack, Vlp. An onset, Juv. Insult.

units.la: Invehi in aliquem, transl.] Invehi in aliquem asperè, graviter, vehementer, infestum esse in aliquem, vel, alicui. Infestus feror in aliquem, infestis signis inferri in hostes. Oppugnare aliquem clàm, palàm, Cic. Contra aliquem venire, Id. Protelare sævis dictis aliquem. Bacchari, &, debacchari in aliquem, Ter. Intonat alicujus perniciosa vox, Liv. Fulminat Æneas, Virg.
units.tr: Invehi in aliquem, figurative] To attack someone harshly, bitterly, vehemently; to be hostile towards someone. I am carried hostile against someone; to be borne with hostile standards against the enemy. To assail someone openly or secretly, Cic. To come against someone, Id. To hound someone with savage words. To rave and rage against someone, Ter. The deadly voice of someone thunders, Liv. Aeneas thunders, Virg.

units.la: Invenire] Qui ortus stellarum comperit, Catul. Reperire. Deprehendere. Indagare omnibus vestigiis, Cic. Adinvenire, Plaut. Quærendo investigare, Ter.
units.tr: Invenire] He who discovered the risings of the stars, Catul. To find out. To detect. To track down by every trace, Cic. To discover in addition, Plaut. To investigate by inquiry, Ter.

units.la: Invenire consilium] Exordium invenire.
units.tr: Invenire consilium] To find an opening.

units.la: Inventa sua alienis exornare] Panno suo alienam assuere purpuram.
units.tr: Inventa sua alienis exornare] To sew another's purple onto one's own cloth.

units.la: Inventio] Excogitatio rerum, inventum, Cic. Inventiuncula, Quint. Reperta pulcha, Lucr. Repertu novo, Apul. Conquisitio piaculorum, Liv. Inventus, ut, Plin.
units.tr: Inventio] The devising of things, a discovery, Cic. A small invention, Quint. Fine discoveries, Lucr. By a new discovery, Apul. A search for expiations, Liv. A finding, Plin.

units.la: Inventio inventori perniciosa] Perilli taurus. Vid. In auctorem mali recidit malum.
units.tr: Inventio inventori perniciosa] The bull of Perillus. See The evil recoils upon its author.

units.la: Inventio prima habet laudem ] Facilè est inventis addere.
units.tr: The first invention has its praise ] It is easy to add to inventions already made.

units.la: Inventor] Repertor, Quint. Investigator. Auctor Architectus. Machinator. In rebus inveniendis acer, Cic. Indagator aquarum. Commentor uvæ Bacchus, Ovid. Commentator omnium falsorum, Apul. Monstrator aratri, Virg. Molitor novarum rerum, Suet.
units.tr: Inventor: a discoverer, Quint.; an investigator; an author, an architect; a contriver. Keen in discovering things, Cic. A finder of waters. Bacchus, the inventor of the grape, Ovid. The author of all falsehoods, Apul. The teacher of the plough, Virg. A maker of new things, Suet.

units.la: Invenustè, vid. Injucundè.
units.tr: Invenustè, see Injucundè.

units.la: Invenustus, vid. Injucundus. Deformis.
units.tr: Invenustus, see Injucundus. Ugly.

units.la: Inverecundia, inverecundus, vid. Impudentia, &c.
units.tr: Inverecundia, inverecundus, see Impudentia, etc.

units.la: Investigare, vid. Quærere.
units.tr: Investigare, see Quærere.

units.la: Invertere, vid. Pervertere.
units.tr: Invertere, see Pervertere.

units.la: Inveteratus] Veternosus, Plin. Veternus, Apul. Veterna macies, Col.
units.tr: Inveteratus: lethargic, Plin.; sluggish, Apul.; a wasting of long standing, Col.

units.la: Invictus] Insuperabilis, Virg. Inexsuperabilis homo. Indomitus Achilles, Sen. Inexpugnabilis homo, Cic. Non est superabilis ulli, Ovid. Arma Achillea.
units.tr: Invictus: unconquerable, Virg.; a man who cannot be overcome; untamed Achilles, Sen.; a man who cannot be stormed, Cic.; he cannot be overcome by anyone, Ovid.; the arms of Achilles.

units.la: Invidere ] Subinvidere. Æmulantis est angi alieno bono, quod ipse non habeat. Rumpi invidiâ, Cic. Torqueri invidiâ, Hor. Pulsari invidiâ, Cassiod. Invidiâ flagrare, premi.
units.tr: Invidere: to envy. The rival is vexed at another's good which he does not himself possess. To burst with envy, Cic.; to be tormented by envy, Hor.; to be struck by envy, Cassiod.; to blaze with envy, to be pressed.

units.la: Invidet habenti non habens] Edentulus vescentium dentibus invidet.
units.tr: Invidet habenti non habens: the toothless man envies those who have teeth.

units.la: Invideat quantum libet] Rumpantur ilia Momo.
units.tr: Invideat quantum libet: let Momus burst his bowels.

units.la: Invidere nescit virtus] Non invidet virtuti alienæ, qui suæ confidit, Cic.
units.tr: Invidere nescit virtus: he who trusts in his own virtue does not envy the virtue of another, Cic.

units.la: Invidetur alicui] Maximam habet invidiam aliquis. Est in invidia, Cic. Prætendit nubila livor alicui, Stat. Invidiæ subjectus, Hor. Invidiosa possessio, Cic.
units.tr: Invidetur alicui: someone has very great envy against him. He is in ill odour, Cic.; envy spreads clouds over him, Stat.; subject to envy, Hor.; an envied possession, Cic.

units.la: Invidetur pulchris ] Invidia non serpit humi. Livor summa petit. Quicquid eximium est, Momum habet suum.
units.tr: Invidetur pulchris: envy does not creep along the ground; spite seeks the heights. Whatever is outstanding has its own Momus.

units.la: Invidetur vivis] Pascitur in vivis livor, Ovid. Vivos invidia fatigat, Sal.
units.tr: Invidetur vivis: spite feeds on the living, Ovid.; envy wears out the living, Sall.

units.la: Invidia] Invidentia, invidiola. Livor, Cic. Loligo, Hor. Animi hulcus invidia, Plaut. Jactantiæ comes. Carpet citiùs aliquis, quàm imitabitur. Virtutis comes.
units.tr: Invidia: envying, little envy. Spite, Cic.; a squid, Hor.; a canker of the mind, envy, Plaut.; companion of boastfulness. Someone will sooner carp at a thing than imitate it. Companion of virtue.

units.la: Invidia est inter propinquos] Figulus figulo invidet: Mendicus mendico. Invidus vicini oculus.
units.tr: Invidia est inter propinquos: the potter envies the potter, the beggar the beggar. The envious eye of a neighbour.

units.la: Invidia sibi ipsi nocet] Genuinum frangere.
units.tr: Invidia sibi ipsi nocet: to break one's own jaw.

units.la: Invidia invido nocet] Viperam fœtus suus dilacerat, Cic.
units.tr: Invidia invido nocet: the viper's own offspring tears it apart, Cic.

units.la: Invidia cum morientibus moritur] Livor post fata quiescit.
units.tr: Invidia cum morientibus moritur: envy rests after death.

units.la: Invidus ] Lividus. Malevolus, Cicer. Lividulus, Juv. Quos livoris tinea comest. Rubigo subrodit invidiæ, Politian. Qui gloriam alterius suam pœnam, felicitatem alterius suam carnificinam faciunt. Profectu contabescit alieno, Id. Cordolium est tibi, Plaut.
units.tr: Invidus: envious. Spiteful, malevolent, Cic.; somewhat envious, Juv.; those whom the moth of envy eats. The rust of envy gnaws at them, Politian. Those who make another's glory their own punishment and another's happiness their own torture. He wastes away at another's success, Id. It is a heartburn to you, Plaut.

units.la: Invido aliena magis placent] Fertilior seges est alienis semper in agris, vicinumque pecus grandius uber habet.
units.tr: Invido aliena magis placent: the envious find other people's things more pleasing. The crop in another's field is always richer, and the neighbour's cattle have the fuller udder.

units.la: Inviolabilis ] Sanctus. Sacrosanctus, Cicer. Impenetrabilis pudicitia, Tac. Intemerandus, Val. Arg. Capitalis locus. Religiosus, Fest.
units.tr: Inviolabilis: holy; most sacred, Cic.; unassailable chastity, Tac.; inviolable, Val. Arg.; a place of sanctuary; sacred, Fest.

units.la: Inviolatus] Invulneratus, Ovid. Intemerata fides. ex Virg. Pudica est à me, Plaut.
units.tr: Inviolatus: unwounded, Ovid.; unbroken faith, from Virg.; she is chaste so far as I am concerned, Plaut.

units.la: Invisere, vid. Visitare.
units.tr: Invisere, see Visitare.

units.la: Invisus, vid. Odiosus.
units.tr: Invisus, see Odiosus.

units.la: Invitare aliquem] Vocare aliquem ad cœnam; domum. Invitare tecto, domo, Cic. Vocare convivam, Plaut. Invitare hospitio, &, in hospitium. Hodie sis apud me volo, Ter.
units.tr: Invitare aliquem: to invite someone to dinner, to invite him home. To invite under one's roof or house, Cic.; to invite a guest, Plaut.; to invite to hospitality, or into hospitality. "I want you to be at my house today," Ter.

units.la: Invitatio] Quærunt in triviis vocationem, Catul.
units.tr: Invitatio: they seek an invitation at the crossroads, Catul.

units.la: Invitè] Gravatè, repugnanter, fastidiosè, fastidiosius aliquid facere. Repugnante, adversante naturâ, Cic. Gravatim, Liv. Reluctante natura, Sen.
units.tr: Invitè: reluctantly, unwillingly, with distaste, to do something grudgingly. Against one's inclination and against nature, Cic.; grudgingly, Liv.; with nature reluctant, Sen.

units.la: Invitus] Perinvitus; alienus, alienissimus, aversus, aversissimus à vel ab, Cic. Alienus hujus rei, Col. Male animatus erga aliquem, Suet. Instudiosus Medicinæ, Apul.
units.tr: Invitus: very unwilling; alien, most alien, averse, most averse to, Cic.; alien to this matter, Col.; ill-disposed towards someone, Suet.; not inclined to the study of medicine, Apul.

units.la: Invita actio non bene succedit] Luscinia minùs bene canit in cavea.
units.tr: Invita actio non bene succedit: a nightingale does not sing well in a cage.

units.la: Invito ingenio] Invitâ Minervâ. Invitâ Deliâ venari. Repugnante natura, ingratiis, Cic. Invitis canibus non est venandum, invita Venere.
units.tr: Invito ingenio: with an unwilling talent; with Minerva unwilling. To hunt with Diana unwilling. Against nature, against one's will, Cic. One must not hunt with unwilling dogs, nor love against one's will.

units.la: Invitus eò deveni] Huc me adegit inopia. Huc redegit fortuna. Ad hæc traxit necessitas. Huc fatis pertrahor. Huc obtorto collo trahor, Er.
units.tr: Invitus eò deveni: want drove me here; fortune brought me here; necessity drew me to this. Fate drags me here. I am dragged here by the neck, twisted against my will, Erasm.

units.la: Invitum retinere] Penulum detinere, Adag.
units.tr: Invitum retinere: to hold back an unwilling man by his cloak, Adag.

units.la: Invius] Avius. Sal. Avia, pl. Tac.
units.tr: Invius: trackless, Sall. In the plural, avia, Tac.

units.la: inumbrare, vid. Obscurare.
units.tr: inumbrare, see Obscurare.

units.la: Inundare] Inundatio urbes abscondit, Sen. Tiberis au-ctus plana urbis stagnaverat, Tac. Montano flumine torrens sternit agros, sternit sata læta, boumque labores, Virg. Tiberis demissioribus ripis altè superfunditur. Premit valles, innatat campis. Quâque planum salum pro solo cernitur, aquis operit agros, Plin. Iun. Natare campos fecere imbres, Lucret. Undare, Cic. Restagnat lacus, Col. Redundat amnis campis, Lucr. Refunditur, Virg. Exgurgitare, Plaut. Superstagnare, Varr. Intumescit, æstuat, accedit mare, Curt. Accrescit flumen, Cic. Excessit alveum Tiberis, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Inundare: a flood hides cities, Sen.; the swollen Tiber had flooded the level parts of the city, Tac.; from the mountain a torrent lays low the fields, the happy crops and the labours of the oxen, Virg.; the Tiber is poured deep over its low banks; it presses down the valleys and swims over the plains; wherever the flat sea is seen in place of land, it covers the fields with water, Plin. Iun.; the rains have made the plains swim, Lucr.; to overflow, Cic.; the lake overflows, Col.; the river overflows the plains, Lucr.; it is poured back, Virg.; to gush out, Plaut.; to stand over, Varr.; the sea swells, surges and advances, Curt.; the river rises, Cic.; the Tiber has left its channel, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Inundatio, vid. Eluvio.
units.tr: Inundatio, see Eluvio.

units.la: Invocare] Implorare Deos immortales, Cic. Poscere opem, Hor. In vota vocare. Vocare, abs. Virg. Preces precari, Cat. Invocare ad, Cic. In auxilium. Quint.
units.tr: Invocare: to implore the immortal gods, Cic.; to ask for help, Hor.; to call to vows; to call, without an object, Virg.; to offer prayers, Cat.; to invoke, to call upon for help, Quint.

units.la: Invocatio] Imploratio. Contestatio, Cic. Vocatus meos nunquam frustrata hasta, Virg.
units.tr: Invocatio: imploring; calling to witness, Cic.; "my spear, once invoked, never failed me," Virg.

units.la: Involvere] Circumvolvere, Plin. Circumplicare, Cic. Obvolvere, Id. Coronæ in modum circumdare coles arbori, Col. Velare aliquid, Sil. Intorquere circum, Liv.
units.tr: Involvere: to roll around, Plin.; to wrap around, Cic.; to enfold, Id.; to wind around a tree, as a vine does, Col.; to veil something, Sil.; to twist around, Liv.

units.la: Involutus, vid. Perplexus.
units.tr: Involutus, see Perplexus.

units.la: Inurbanè] Parum urbanè, incivilius, Cic.
units.tr: Inurbanè: not very urbanely, more uncivilly, Cic.

units.la: Inurbanus] Incivilis, Gell. Inficetus, Catul. Malè moratus. Rus merum, Plaut.
units.tr: Inurbanus: uncivil, Gell.; dull, Catul.; ill-mannered. Pure countryside, Plaut.

units.la: Inusitatus, vid. Insolitus.
units.tr: Inusitatus, see Insolitus.

units.la: Inutilis] Infructuosus, Plin. Nulli usui est. Nullum usum habet. Nulla ex eo utilitas est, Cic. Nullum mihi operæ pretium, Juv. Nullum in eo momentum ad aliquid, Liv. Achrestus, Ausón. Ficulnus truncus, Hor. Ab re mea est, Plaut. Campana sine pistillo. Calvo pecten. Oleum & operam perdidi.
units.tr: Inutilis: unproductive, Plin.; of no use; it has no use; there is no benefit from it, Cic.; no worthwhile task for me, Juv.; no weight in it for anything, Liv.; useless, Ausón.; a fig-tree trunk, Hor.; it is no concern of mine, Plaut.; a pestle-less mortar; a comb for a bald man. I have wasted my oil and my labour.

units.la: Rem inutilem agere] Aërem ferire, verberare. Æthiopem lavare, dealbare. Laterem lavare, in cassum tela jacere, Liv. Frustrà operam sumere. Perdere laborem, Cic. Ludere operam, Plaut. Ventis verba profundere, Lucr. Annosam arborem transplantare. Apud novercam queri. Aquam cribro haurire. Aquam è pumice postulare. Aquam in mortario tundere. Aranceae telas texere. Arare littus. Cæco lumen præferre. Canes vetulos loris assuefacere. Dormienti loqui. Fluctibus obloqui. Fluctus numerare. Ignem dissecare, in aqua scribere, in aqua sementem facere. Cœlo addere sidera quid opus? Ignes horrari ut caleant. Juxta fluvium puteum fodere. Utrem mergere vento plenum. Utre territare. Vento loqui. Ventis tradere. Verba facere oleribus.
units.tr: Rem inutilem agere: to strike and beat the air. To wash an Ethiopian, to whiten him. To wash a brick; to throw darts in vain, Liv.; to take pains to no purpose; to lose one's labour, Cic.; to play at working, Plaut.; to pour out words to the winds, Lucr.; to transplant an old tree; to complain before a stepmother; to draw water with a sieve; to demand water from pumice; to pound water in a mortar; to weave spiders' webs; to plough the shore; to hold a light before the blind; to accustom old dogs to the leash; to speak to a sleeper; to talk to the waves; to count the waves; to cut fire in pieces; to write in water; to sow seed in water. Why add stars to the sky? To shake the fires so that they may warm up. To dig a well beside a river. To dip a bladder full of wind. To frighten a bladder. To talk to the wind. To hand things over to the winds. To make speeches to cabbages.

units.la: Inutilitas] Incommoditas, Ter. Incommodum, Lucr.
units.tr: Inutilitas: inconvenience, Ter.; disadvantage, Lucr.

units.la: Inutiliter] Parum utiliter, Plin.Iun. Vid. Supra, Rem inutil.
units.tr: Inutiliter: not usefully, Plin. Iun. See above, under Rem inutilem.

units.la: Ipse] Ipse ego, ipse egomet, Plaut. Tute ipse, Ter. Tutemet in culpa es, Lucr. De suâ sententiâ, Plaut. Ipse per se, Cic. Solus per se, Liv. Ipsipsus, Plaut.
units.tr: Ipse: I myself, Plaut.; you yourself, Ter.; you yourself are to blame, Lucr.; by his own opinion, Plaut.; by himself through himself, Cic.; alone by himself, Liv.; he himself, Plaut.

units.la: Ira] Bilis. Rabies animi, acerbitas. Stomachus, Cic. Acris acrimonia animi & ingenii feri, Nævi. Excandescentia, Apul. Irarum ardor, iracundia, Cic. Indignatio, Plin. Sine Vulcano flamma.
units.tr: Ira: bile; the rage of the mind; bitterness; temper, Cic.; sharp bitterness of spirit and a fierce nature, Naev.; excitement, Apul.; the heat of anger, Cic.; indignation, Plin.; a flame without Vulcan.

units.la: Ira inveterata] Ira vetus, Ovid. Ira memor, Virg.
units.tr: Ira inveterata: old anger, Ovid.; anger that remembers, Virg.

units.la: Ira excæcat] Impedit ira animum, ne possit cernere verum, Cato.
units.tr: Ira excæcat: anger hinders the mind so that it cannot see the truth, Cato.

units.la: Ira non facile defervet] Ira ægrè senescit, iræ regum plumbeæ.
units.tr: Ira non facile defervet: anger grows old slowly; the anger of kings is leaden.

units.la: Ira decedit] Defervescit ira, Cic. Deflagrant iræ, Liv. Despumat, Apul.
units.tr: Ira decedit: the anger cools, Cic.; angers burn out, Liv.; it foams away, Apul.

units.la: Ira est inter hunc & illum] Intercedit ira inter eos, iræ sunt inter, &c. Ter.
units.tr: Ira est inter hunc & illum: anger stands between them; there are angers between them, etc., Ter.

units.la: Iram effundere] Erumpere in aliquem stomachum. Aliquid in aliquem evomere, Cic. Iram evomere in aliquem, Ter. Bilem effundere, Liv.
units.tr: Iram effundere: to burst out in anger against someone. To pour something out on someone, Cic.; to vent anger on someone, Ter.; to pour out bile, Liv.

units.la: Irâ, furore, ultionem moliri] Montes ardentes in alios jacere tentat.
units.tr: Irâ, furore, ultionem moliri: he tries to hurl burning mountains at others.

units.la: Iracundè] Per iram. Non sine stomacho. Stomachans,Cic. Furibundus venit, Id. Indignabundè, indignanter ; Amm. Impotenter, Quint. Indignabundus, Liv. Infensè invectus,Tac.
units.tr: Iracundè: in anger; not without spleen. Spitefully, Cic.; he came in a fury, Id.; indignantly, Amm.; without restraint, Quint.; indignantly, Liv.; fiercely attacked, Tac.

units.la: Iracundus] Iracundissimus. Prærabidus,Sen. Rabiosus, Id. Iræ plenus, Liv. Impatiens iræ,Ovid. Immodicus iræ,Stat. Impotens iræ, animi, Curt. Stomachosiores literæ. Effervescens sæpe stomacho iracundiaque vehementius, irritabilis, Cic. Non habet iram in potestate, Sen. Iniquus animus,Ter. Facilis irasci, Amm.
units.tr: Iracundus: most irascible; very furious, Sen.; raging, Id.; full of anger, Liv.; impatient of anger, Ovid.; immoderate in anger, Stat.; not in control of his anger or mind, Curt.; more irritable letters. Often boiling over more violently with spleen and anger, quick-tempered, Cic.; he does not have his anger under control, Sen.; a hostile mind, Ter.; quick to anger, Amm.

units.la: Irasci] Irascor tibi istud dictum. Uxor tua in fermento jacet. Turget. Sufflare se alicui, Plaut. Indignari , stomachari alicui. Mordere labra. Stomacho est mihi aliquid. Infensus illi sum, indignè ferre, pati. Succensere alicui. Cor mihi turgescit tristibus iris. Fremere, Cic. Tangi irâ, Lucr. Carpi irâ, Id. Inflare buccas iratum. Bile tumet jecur, Hor. Indulgere iræ, Liv. Iras gerere. Ringi, Ter. Intumescere , intumesco alicui, Ovid. Fervere, Ter. Infenso animo esse in aliquem.
units.tr: Irasci: I am angry at you for saying that. Your wife lies in the leaven; she swells up. To puff oneself up against someone, Plaut.; to be indignant with someone, to be resentful of someone. To bite one's lips. Something is bile to me. I am hostile to him; to take it ill; to suffer. To be aggrieved with someone. My heart swells with sad anger. To roar, Cic.; to be touched by anger, Lucr.; to be seized by anger, Id.; to puff out one's cheeks in anger. The liver swells with bile, Hor.; to indulge anger, Liv.; to bear grudges. To growl, Ter.; to swell up, to swell against someone, Ovid.; to seethe, Ter.; to be hostile in mind towards someone.

units.la: Irasci valde] Ardere iracundia , Ter. Inflammari, efferri iracundiâ. Exardescere stomacho, & iracundiâ incendi in aliquem. Furere & insanire in aliquem,Cic. Ignescunt iræ, Virg. Coquere iras,Sil. Inæstuat bilis præmordiis meis,Hor. Plumbeas iras gerere, Plaut. Iracundia effervescere , exardescere, Cic. Excandescere. Excandescere irâ. Exardere irâ. Cumulatum cor irâ , incitari irâ. Permoveri iracundiâ,(ic. Exacerbescere, Apul. Accendi iră , odio, Plin. Succendi irâ, Sil. Peracescere , ita mihi pectus peracuit, Plaut. Lamb. Tandem.
units.tr: Irasci valde] To burn with anger, Ter. To be inflamed and carried away by anger. To blaze with rage and be fired with anger against someone. To rage and be frenzied against someone, Cic. Anger flares up, Virg. To boil with wrath, Sil. Bile seethes in my vitals, Hor. To bear leaden anger, Plaut. To grow hot with anger, to blaze up, Cic. To be excited. To flare up with anger. To burn with anger. A heart heaped up with anger; to be roused to anger. To be stirred by rage, Cic. To grow more bitter, Apul. To be kindled by anger or hatred, Plin. To be set on fire by anger, Sil. To grow sour: "so my breast has gone sour," Plaut. Lamb. Tandem.

units.la: Irasci impotenter ridiculum] Vana sine viribus ira, Hor.
units.tr: Irasci impotenter ridiculum] "Anger without strength is vain," Hor.

units.la: Iratus] Incitatus irâ , irato & percito animo. Ardens iracundiâ, (ic. Obiratus, Liv. Succensus irâ, Sil.
units.tr: Iratus] Roused to anger, with an angry and agitated mind. Burning with rage, Cic. Provoked, Liv. Inflamed with anger, Sil.

units.la: Iratus facilè arma invenit] Ira telum facit. Furor arma ministrat. Facilè fustem invenit, qui vult canem cædere.
units.tr: Iratus facilè arma invenit] Anger makes a weapon. Fury supplies arms. Whoever wants to beat a dog easily finds a stick.

units.la: Ire] Venio ad Veneris visere , incedere viam, per vias, insistere viam. Proficisci, Plaut. Insistere , & ingredi viis. Conferre se ad aliquem. Contendere in ædes. Capessere se domum. Capessere cursum ad aliquem. Recipere se Romam. Iter conficere ; aliquò conferre iter. Iter facere, dirigere, habere. Pergere iter aliquò, Romam. Petere Athenas. Tendere Venusiam. Vadere, Abs. Vadere ad aliquem, Cic. Incedere ad urbem. Intendere iter aliquò. Pergunt domos. Tendere cursum aliquò. Tendere ad aliquem, Liv. Recipere se ad aliquem, Caes. Grassari ad gloriam virtutis via, Sal. Ducere se, Ter. Quò iter inceptas? Pergere ad aliquem, Plaut.
units.tr: Ire] To come to visit Venus; to walk the road, to go along the ways, to set foot on the road. To set out, Plaut. To enter upon and go along roads. To betake oneself to someone. To make for the house. To hasten one's course to someone. To return to Rome. To complete a journey; to direct a journey somewhere. To make, direct or keep a journey. To press on a journey somewhere, to Rome. To make for Athens. To head for Venusia. To go, Abs. To go to someone, Cic. To proceed to the city. To direct one's journey somewhere. They make for their homes. To aim one's course somewhere. To go to someone, Liv. To betake oneself to someone, Caes. To press on by the way of virtue's glory, Sal. To lead oneself, Ter. Where have you set out on your journey? To hasten to someone, Plaut.

units.la: Ire cubitum] Ire dormitum, Plaut. Proficisci ad dormiendum. Dare se somno. Proficisci ad somnum, Cic. Mandare quieti fessum corpus. Abire in somnum. Dabantur in lectum, Lucr. Ire in somnum, Plaut.
units.tr: Ire cubitum] To go to bed. To go to sleep, Plaut. To set out for sleep. To give oneself up to sleep. To set out for sleep, Cic. To commit the weary body to rest. To go off into sleep. "They were given over to bed," Lucr. To go into sleep, Plaut.

units.la: Iris] Arquus, Non. Arcus coelestis, Iuv. Arcus pluvius, Hor. Imbrifer, Tibul.
units.tr: Iris] Arquus, the bow, Non. The heavenly bow, Juv. The rain-bow, Hor. The rain-bringing bow, Tibul.

units.la: Ironia] Fictio, Lact. Fabulositas poetica, Plin. Dissimulantia. Dissimulatio, Cic. Imitamentum, Gell. Figura, quâ quidam rejiciunt, quae magis ad se volunt attrahere, Sen.
units.tr: Ironia] Pretence, Lact. Poetic fabulousness, Plin. Dissembling. Dissimulation, Cic. Imitation, Gell. A figure by which some reject what they rather wish to draw to themselves, Sen.

units.la: Irrationalis] Irrationabilis, Quint. Expers rationis. Temerarius, Cic.
units.tr: Irrationalis] Irrational, Quint. Lacking reason. Rash, Cic.

units.la: Irreconciliabilis] Lupos ovem prius ducat uxorem. Ne via quidem eadem vult cum illo ingredi. Prius unda cum flammâ redibit in gratiam.
units.tr: Irreconciliabilis] Let the wolf first marry the sheep. He will not even walk the same road with him. Sooner shall water return to friendship with fire.

units.la: Irreparabilis] Nunquam pensabile damnum, Amm.
units.tr: Irreparabilis] A loss that can never be made good, Amm.

units.la: Irrepere] Subrepere sub tabulas, Cic. Tabulis, Col. Erepere in sublimitates rupium, Amm. Inscendere, ascendere in aliquid. Immergere se in ganeum, Plaut. Inserpit somnus, Stat. Vid. Insinuare.
units.tr: Irrepere] To creep under the boards, Cic. Under the boards, Col. To creep up to the heights of the cliffs, Amm. To climb up, to ascend onto something. To immerse oneself in a gutter, Plaut. Sleep creeps in, Stat. See Insinuare.

units.la: Irretire, vid. Illaqueare.
units.tr: Irretire, see Illaqueare.

units.la: Irretiri, vid. Hærere.
units.tr: Irretiri, see Hærere.

units.la: Irreverenter] Illotis manibus vel pedibus ingredi.
units.tr: Irreverenter] To enter with unwashed hands or feet.

units.la: Irreverentia] Imminutio dignitatis, Cic. Mala tractatio, Arnob. Turneb.
units.tr: Irreverentia] A diminishing of dignity, Cic. Rough handling, Arnob. Turneb.

units.la: Irrevocabilis] Irrevocandus error, Claud. Decretorius dies mortis, Sen. Irrevocatus, Ovid. Irremeabilis error, Virg. Irredux via, Lucan.
units.tr: Irrevocabilis] An error that cannot be recalled, Claud. The fated day of death, Sen. Not recalled, Ovid. An unreturnable wandering, Virg. A road with no return, Lucan.

units.la: Irridere errores] Sales aspergere scabiei. Vid. Ludificare. Irrigare, vid. Aspergere.
units.tr: Irridere errores] To sprinkle wit on a sore. See Ludificare. Irrigare, see Aspergere.

units.la: Irrigatio, vid. Aspersio.
units.tr: Irrigatio, see Aspersio.

units.la: Irrisio ] Irrisus, us, Tacit. Derisus, us, Suet. Deridiculum, Tac.
units.tr: Irrisio] Mockery, Tacit. Derision, Suet. A laughing-stock, Tac.

units.la: Irrisor, vid. Derisor.
units.tr: Irrisor, see Derisor.

units.la: Irritare] Exulcerare animum alicujus. Refricare dolorem oratione. Facere, movere alicui stomachum. Lacessere injuriâ aliquem, Cic. Concire iram. Asperare iram alicujus. Facere ægrè alicui, Ter. Exacerbare aliquem, Suet. Obacerbare, Fest. Retractare vulnera cruda, Ovid. Frigidam suffundere. Stomacho esse alicui. Lacessere aliquem, Ter. Non expedit exasperatas apes lacessiri. Exasperare animos, Col. Vexare aliquem verbis, Lucr. Asperare iram alicujus. Accendere offensiones, Tac. Inflammare odiis, Stat. Acerbare vulnus scil. animi, Claud. Inconciliare aliquem, Plaut.
units.tr: Irritare] To gall someone's spirit. To rub a grief raw by speech. To stir up, to provoke someone's bile. To provoke someone with an injury, Cic. To rouse anger. To sharpen someone's anger. To vex someone, Ter. To exacerbate someone, Suet. To embitter, Fest. To reopen raw wounds, Ovid. To pour cold water over. To be a thorn in someone's side. To provoke someone, Ter. It is not advisable to provoke angry bees. To exasperate minds, Col. To vex someone with words, Lucr. To sharpen someone's anger. To kindle offences, Tac. To inflame with hatreds, Stat. To make a wound sharper, namely of the mind, Claud. To alienate someone, Plaut.

units.la: Irritare denuo] Obductam cicatricem refricare.
units.tr: Irritare denuo] To reopen a healed scar.

units.la: Irritare malevolos] Crabrones irritare.
units.tr: Irritare malevolos] To stir up hornets.

units.la: Irritare eum, qui retaliare potest] Cornutam bestiam petere.
units.tr: Irritare eum, qui retaliare potest] To attack a horned beast.

units.la: Irritator malorum] Vexator furoris Clodii Milo, Cic. In ulcere unguis.
units.tr: Irritator malorum] Milo, the tormentor of Clodius's madness, Cic. In the ulcer of a nail.

units.la: Irritatus] Exasperatus animo, Liv. Efferatus irâ odioque, Id.
units.tr: Irritatus] Embittered in mind, Liv. Roused to fury by anger and hatred, Id.

units.la: Irritus] Infectum foedus, Virg. Irritum promissum, Ter. Pro infecto habendum, Cic. Nihil agit, Paul.IC. Non procedit hoc in servo, Ulp. Frustraneus, (S.A.V.)
units.tr: Irritus] A covenant set aside, Virg. An empty promise, Ter. To be held as not done, Cic. He achieves nothing, Paul.IC. This does not hold in the case of a slave, Ulp. Vain, frustrate, (S.A.V.)

units.la: Irrogare, vid. Edicere.
units.tr: Irrogare, see Edicere.

units.la: Irruere, vid. Invadere.
units.tr: Irruere, see Invadere.

units.la: Irrumpere] Invadere in urbem vi. Irrumpere in, Cic. Irrumpere oppidum, Caes. Irrumpere intrò, Ter. Introrumpere in. Irruptionem facere in, Plaut. Penetrare, Cic. Penetro me, Gell. Incurrere in hostes, Sal.
units.tr: Irrumpere] To burst by force into a city. To break into, Cic. To break into a town, Caes. To burst inside, Ter. To break in upon. To make an incursion into, Plaut. To penetrate, Cic. I penetrate myself, Gell. To rush upon the enemy, Sal.

units.la: Irruptio] Incursus militum, Liv.
units.tr: Irruptio] A raid of soldiers, Liv.

units.la: Is, vid. Hic.
units.tr: Is, see Hic.

units.la: Ischuria] Lotii retentio, suppressio, Iun. Suppressa urina, Franc. Val.
units.tr: Ischuria] Retention or suppression of urine, Iun. Suppressed urine, Franc. Val.

units.la: Isthmus] Collum peninsulæ, quo continenti cohæret.
units.tr: Isthmus] The neck of a peninsula, by which it clings to the mainland.

units.la: Ita ] Sic. Hoc modo. Ad hunc modum, Cic. Hac re. Eo pacto, Ter. Taliter, Plin. Etiam, Plin.Iun. Adeò, Cic.
units.tr: Ita] Thus. In this manner. In this way, Cic. For this reason. In that way, Ter. Thus, Plin. Also, Plin. Iun. So far, Cic.

units.la: Ita res procedunt] Sic fortuna rotam suam versat.
units.tr: Ita res procedunt] So fortune turns its wheel.

units.la: Ita est, affirmando] Ita dico, loquor, ita enim verò, ita inquam, ita profectò, Plaut. Ita prorsus: est ita. Sanè quidem. Verò, ac libenter quidem. Etiam. Certè, Cic. Sic. Admodum. Oppidò. Rectè. Maximè. Factum: tuam vestem detraxit tibi? factum, Ter. Sic est. Sic res est. Vera prædico. Nempe sicut dicis. Pro me responsas vel responsas tibi, Plaut. Tuas tibi voces reddo, Petron. Tu dicis: tu dixisti, in SS. Scilicet, Ter. Quippini. Immo etiam, Plaut.
units.tr: Ita est, affirmando] "So I say, I speak; indeed so, so I say, certainly so," Plaut. Just so; it is so. Certainly. Truly, and gladly indeed. Yes. Certainly, Cic. Thus. Quite so. Exactly. Right. Most certainly. It is done: did he strip your clothes off you? Done, Ter. That is so. The matter stands so. I declare true things. Just as you say. I answer for you, or I give back your words to you, Plaut. I give your own words back to you, Petron. You say so; you said so, in SS. Of course, Ter. Why not. Indeed, even so, Plaut.

units.la: Ita est, Ironicè] Rectè sanè. Sanè quia verò, Ter. Eja, verò, Plaut. Vid. Quasiverò.
units.tr: Ita est, Ironicè] Quite right, indeed. Indeed, since truly, Ter. Oh yes, truly, Plaut. See Quasiverò.

units.la: Itane?] Itane verò? Siccine? Ain'? Ter.Cic. Ain' verò? Ain' tu? Ain' tandem? Plaut.Cic. Itane est? Siccine agis? Ter.Cic.
units.tr: Itane?] Is that so, really? Is it so? Do you say so? Ter. Cic. You say so, really? You say so? So at last? Plaut. Cic. Is that how it is? Are you acting like that? Ter. Cic.

units.la: Iter] Iter longum, & via inepta, Cic.
units.tr: Iter] A long journey and an awkward way, Cic.

units.la: Iterare] Duplicare & iterare verba, Cic. Geminare, Ter. Repetere audita, Ovid. Congeminare sonitus, Sili. Integrare pugnam, Liv. Instaurare bellum, Cic.
units.tr: Iterare] To double and repeat words, Cic. To redouble, Ter. To repeat what has been heard, Ovid. To redouble sounds, Sil. To renew the battle, Liv. To renew a war, Cic.

units.la: Iterare idem sæpe, vid. Repetere eadem.
units.tr: Iterare idem sæpe, see Repetere eadem.

units.la: Iterare arationem] Repastinare agrum. Aratro subvertere lupinum, Col. Offringere. Secundâ aratione renovare, Varr. Novare, Bud. Recolere humum, ex Ovid. Tertiâ vice arare, Pallad. Tertiare agrum, Col.
units.tr: Iterare arationem] To plough a field again. To turn up lupins with the plough, Col. To plough over. To renew with a second ploughing, Varr. To renew, Bud. To till the ground again, from Ovid. To plough for a third time, Pallad. To plough a field a third time, Col.

units.la: Iteratio, vid. Repetitio.
units.tr: Iteratio, see Repetitio.

units.la: Iterum, vid. Denuo.
units.tr: Iterum, see Denuo.

units.la: Itidem] Item, Ter. Perinde felix, Plin Iun. Ad eundem modum. Eodem modo. Uno, & eodem modo. Æquè. Pariter, Cic.
units.tr: Itidem] Likewise, Ter. Equally happy, Plin. Iun. In the same way. In the same manner. In one and the same way. Equally. Alike, Cic.

units.la: J.
units.tr: J.

units.la: Jacere] Jacere humi; ad pedes alicujus, Cic. Accumbere in via, Plaut. Procubat umbra, Virg. Vid. Cubare.
units.tr: To lie] To lie on the ground; at someone's feet, Cic. To recline in the road, Plaut. The shade lies down, Virg. See Cubare.

units.la: Jacere] Facere jactum, Hirt. Projicere, librare telum, jactare lapides, Virg. Vibrare hastam, Cic. Jaculari saxa, Ovid. Ingerere tela, Liv.
units.tr: To throw] To make a throw, Hirt. To hurl forward, to poise a spear, to throw stones, Virg. To brandish a spear, Cic. To hurl stones, Ovid. To hurl weapons, Liv.

units.la: Jactanter] Gloriosè. Sublatè, Cic. Gloriabundus aspicit, Gell. Vid. Affectatè.
units.tr: Jactanter] Boastfully. Proudly, Cic. He looks about in a boastful way, Gell. See Affectatè.

units.la: Jactantia] Jactatio. Ostentatio. Gloriatio, Cic. Vid. Sermo jactabundus.
units.tr: Jactantia] Showing off. Ostentation. Vainglory, Cic. See Sermo jactabundus.

units.la: Jactare se & sua] Jactare caudam popello, Perf. Jactant miracula dictis. Monstra & portenta loqui, Lucr. Efferre se insolenter. Sublatè de se dicere. Tragœdias agere. Venditare se. Ostentare, quod re verâ nullo pacto fieri potest. Ebullire virtutes & sapientias. Exsultare juveniliter. Eructare aliquid, Cic. Ampullari. Ampullas loqui. Projicit ampullas, & sesquipedalia verba, Hor. Deblaterare, Gell. Elatum & opulentum spirare, ex Philostr. Crepare. Basilica facinora loqui. Ipse semet canit.
units.tr: Jactare se & sua] To flaunt oneself and one's possessions: to wag one's tail among the crowd, Perf. They boast of wonders in their words. To speak of monstrous and portentous things, Lucr. To carry oneself insolently. To speak of oneself haughtily. To play the tragedian. To push oneself forward. To make a show of what in truth can by no means be done. To bubble over with virtues and wisdoms. To exult like a youth. To belch out something, Cic. To puff oneself up. To talk bombast. He throws out bubbles and words a foot and a half long, Hor. To babble on, Gell. To breathe out lofty and rich things, ex Philostr. To crow. To talk of lofty deeds. He sings his own praises himself.

units.la: Ne jacta verbis, ostende factis] Hic Rhodus, hic salta.
units.tr: Do not boast in words, show in deeds] Here is Rhodes, leap here.

units.la: Jactator] Jactans, Cic. Jactantissimus, Spart. Jactator proprii honoris, Claud. Tumidus ac sui jactans, Quint. Bucco, Isidor. Magniloquus, Mart. Magnidicus, Plaut. Venditator in prædicandis doctrinis suis, Gell. Gloriator, Apul. Ostentator, Liv. Animal gloriæ. Ipse. Thrasone gloriosior, Er.
units.tr: Jactator] A boaster, Cic. Most boastful, Spart. A boaster of his own honour, Claud. Puffed up and boasting of himself, Quint. A braggart, Isidor. A big talker, Mart. Loud-mouthed, Plaut. A peddler of his own teachings in proclaiming them, Gell. A seeker of glory, Apul. A show-off, Liv. A creature of glory. Himself. More boastful than Thraso, Er.

units.la: Jaculari] Jaculum mittere. Solicitare arcu feras, Ovid. Sagittare, Justin. Arcu sagittas emittere, Cic. Ire in aliquem sagittis, Stat. Contendere in auras telum, Virg. Ignes tormentis jacere, Vopisc.
units.tr: Jaculari] To throw a dart. To hunt wild beasts with a bow, Ovid. To shoot arrows, Justin. To shoot arrows from a bow, Cic. To attack someone with arrows, Stat. To aim a weapon into the air, Virg. To hurl fire from engines, Vopisc.

units.la: Jaculatio] Emissio teli tormento, Cic. Excussio, Vibratio, Sipont. Missus sagittæ, Lucr.
units.tr: Jaculatio] The discharge of a missile from an engine, Cic. A shaking out, a brandishing, Sipont. The sending of an arrow, Lucr.

units.la: Jaculator] Sagittarius, Cic. Doctus sagittarum, Aurel. Vict. Fistulator, Recent.
units.tr: Jaculator] An archer, Cic. Skilled with arrows, Aurel. Vict. A piper, Recent.

units.la: Jaculum] Sagitta, Cicer. Spiculum. Telum. Arundo, Virg. Sagittula, Apul. Ferrum missile volvere, pennatum, Plin.
units.tr: Jaculum] An arrow, Cicer. A small spear. A missile. A reed, Virg. A little arrow, Apul. To whirl a feathered iron missile, Plin.

units.la: Janitor] Ostiarius. Admissionum liberti, Plin. Atrienses, Cic. Submotor aditus. Clausftritimus, Liv. Qui salutationem publicam exercet, Sen. Ad limina custos, Virg. Ad limina. abs. IC. Admissionum magister, Vopisc.
units.tr: Janitor] Doorkeeper. A freedman in charge of admissions, Plin. Attendants of the atrium, Cic. One who keeps people from access. Keeper of the bolts, Liv. One who conducts the public salutations, Sen. Guardian of the threshold, Virg. At the threshold. abs. IC. Master of admissions, Vopisc.

units.la: Janua] Ostium, Sipont. Rectum ostium, (i.e. anterius) Plaut. Porta, Cic. Apertura. Vacuum ostii, Vitr.
units.tr: Janua] Door, Sipont. A straight door (that is, facing forward), Plaut. Gate, Cic. An opening. The empty space of a doorway, Vitr.

units.la: Januâ clausâ] Tacitis cardinibus, Propert. Non mutit cardo, Plaut. Dormiunt pessuli, Id.
units.tr: With the door closed] With silent hinges, Propert. The hinge does not creak, Plaut. The bolts sleep, Id.

units.la: A januâ aberrare] De curru delapsus. De asino delapsus. A calcaria in carbonariam. Deficere à limine. A lineis excidere.
units.tr: To stray from the door] Fallen from a chariot. Fallen from a donkey. From the spurs to the charcoal-burner's. To fall short of the threshold. To fall out of the lines.

units.la: Jecur, vid. Hepar.
units.tr: Liver, see Hepar.

units.la: Jejunare] Jejunium servo magis, quàm Judæus Sabbatha, Suet. Jejunia annua celebrare, Claud. Longa domant illos inopi jejunia victu, Ovid.
units.tr: To fast] He kept his fast more strictly than a Jew keeps the Sabbath, Suet. To keep yearly fasts, Claud. Long fasts subdue those men with their meagre food, Ovid.

units.la: Jejunium] Esuriales feriæ, Plaut. Ubi laniones frigent, & salsamentarii regnant, Er.
units.tr: Fast] Holidays of hunger, Plaut. Where the butchers grow cold and the salt-fish sellers reign, Er.

units.la: Jejunium absolvere] Solvere jejunium meridie, Vespere. Solvere jejunium tribus granis, Ovid. Boët. Solvere abstinentiam. Abstinentiæ rigorem prandiis relaxare, Isidor.
units.tr: To break a fast] To break the fast at midday; in the evening. To break the fast with three grains, Ovid. Boët. To relax the abstinence. To relax the rigour of abstinence with lunches, Isidor.

units.la: Jejunus] Jejuna oris saliva, Plin. Jejuna saliva, Col. Siccus. Impransus, Hor. Expers undæ & cibi, Ovid. Jejunus & abstemius, Apul. Famem integram ad cibum adferre, Cic. Jejuniosior, Plaut. Deprandius leo, Non. apud Fest.
units.tr: Fasting] Dry saliva of the mouth, Plin. Fasting saliva, Col. Dry. Unfed, Hor. Without water and food, Ovid. Fasting and abstemious, Apul. To bring a whole hunger to one's food, Cic. More hungry, Plaut. A lion that has dined, Non. apud Fest.

units.la: Jentaculum] Jentatio, Firm. Præguftativa comestio, Id. Prandiolum, Sipont. Prandiculum, Lipf.
units.tr: Breakfast] Breakfasting, Firm. A taking of food before tasting, Id. A little luncheon, Sipont. A little breakfast, Lipf.

units.la: Jentare] Jentaculum sumere, Mart.
units.tr: To breakfast] To take breakfast, Mart.

units.la: Jocari] Joco dicere. Per jocum dicere, Plaut. Per ludum. Ludere, jacere, mittere ridiculum. Cavillari & jocari familiariter cum aliquo, Cic. Delicias, facetias facere, Plaut. Delicias dicere, Catul. Jocari in aliquem, vel in aliquid, Hor. Lepore elevare objecta ab aliquo. Facetiis venustè eludere aliquid. Facetè eludi ab aliquo, Cic.
units.tr: To joke] To say in jest. To say by way of a joke, Plaut. In play. To play, to throw out, to make a witticism. To banter and joke familiarly with someone, Cic. To make sport, to crack jokes, Plaut. To speak playfully, Catul. To joke at someone or about something, Hor. To lighten objections raised by someone with wit. To parry something elegantly with witticisms. To be wittily mocked by someone, Cic.

units.la: Joco] Per jocum, per ludum. Animi causa. Ludibundus, jocandi causâ. Facetiis eludere. Facetè. Per risum & jocum, Cic. Joculariter, Plin. Jocabundus, Val.M. Ad jocum constitutæ aquilæ, Capitol.
units.tr: In jest] In play, in fun. For the sake of amusement. Playing, for the sake of a joke. To parry with witticisms. Wittily. With laughter and jest, Cic. Jokingly, Plin. Jesting, Val.M. An eagle set up for a joke, Capitol.

units.la: Jocosus] Lepore & humanitate præstat omnibus. Habet sermonis festivitatem. Festivus sermo. Aptissimus ad jocandum. Facetiis & sale conditus. Persalsus. Urbanitate colorata oratio. Omnes sale facetiisque superavit, Cic. Ridiculus, Ridiculosissimus, Ridiculissimus parasitus, Plaut. Plenus joci, Ovid. Vid. Facetus.
units.tr: Witty] He surpasses all in charm and courtesy. He has a festive manner of speech. Festive speech. Most apt for jesting. Seasoned with wit and salt. Very salty. A speech coloured with urbanity. He surpassed everyone in wit and witticisms, Cic. Ridiculous, most ridiculous, the most ridiculous parasite, Plaut. Full of jest, Ovid. See Facetus.

units.la: Jocus] Jocatio. Ludus. Dicta bona. Dictum acutè, facetè. Dicacitas, Cic. Joculo aliquem fallere, jocos ridiculos vendo. Dictum ridiculum, Plaut. Joculatio, Firm. Logi, Cic. Joca plena facetiarum, Id. Vid. Facetiæ.
units.tr: Jest] Jesting. Play. Good sayings. A saying put sharply and wittily. Raillery, Cic. To deceive someone with a jest, offering ridiculous jokes. A ridiculous saying, Plaut. Jesting, Firm. Witty speeches, Cic. Jests full of wit, Id. See Facetiae.

units.la: Jocus mordax] Sales dentati, amari.
units.tr: Biting jest] Biting, bitter witticisms.

units.la: Jocus in feria tendat] Jocandum ut feria agas.
units.tr: Let jesting be kept within the feast] Jest in such a way that you keep the holiday.

units.la: Jocandi nimia consuetudo mala] Jocus aufert reverentiam.
units.tr: Excessive habit of joking is bad] Jest takes away reverence.

units.la: Jocus nimius, theatricus] Triscurria, pl. Juv. Lepos, jocus scurrilis, mimicus. Dicacitas scurrilis, Cic. Jocus nequam.
units.tr: Excessive, theatrical jesting] Buffooneries, plural, Juv. Wit, scurrilous and mimicking jokes. Scurrilous raillery, Cic. A wicked joke.

units.la: Juba] Capronæ, Fest.
units.tr: Mane] Goat's hair, Fest.

units.la: Jubere] Imperare quid facto opus sit. Præcipere conservis aliquid, jubeo, cogo, atque impero, Ter. Vid. Mandare.
units.tr: To order] To command what needs to be done. To instruct fellow slaves to do something: "I bid, I compel, and I order," Ter. See Mandare.

units.la: Jubilare] Ovare, Liv. Ululare lætis triumphis, Lucan. Personare festis clamoribus, Plin. Iun. Reclangere, Amm.
units.tr: To rejoice aloud] To shout for joy, Liv. To howl with joyful triumphs, Lucan. To resound with festive shouts, Plin. Iun. To cry out again, Amm.

units.la: Jubilatio] Jubilum, Sil. Jubilatus, Vall. ex Varr. Vid. Acclamatio.
units.tr: Jubilation] A shout of jubilation, Sil. Jubilation, Vall. ex Varr. See Acclamatio.

units.la: Jubileus annus] Jubileum. Annus remissionis, Isid. Rectè etiam dici potest, Annus secularis. Annus scalaris, ex septem septenniis constans, Franc. Valef.
units.tr: Jubilee year] Jubilee. A year of remission, Isid. It may also rightly be called a secular year. A ladder year, made up of seven sevens of years, Franc. Valef.

units.la: Jucundè, vid. Hilariter.
units.tr: Pleasantly, see Hilariter.

units.la: Jucundè vitam agere] Album diem agere, Plaut.
units.tr: To live pleasantly] To have a white-letter day, Plaut.

units.la: Jucunditas] Animus. Solatium. Oblectamentum. Delectamentum. Animi oblectatio, Cicer. Lubentia, Plaut. Genialitas, Amm. Delenimentum, Tac. Apricitas diei, Col. Amœnitas loci, Cic.
units.tr: Jucunditas] Cheer. Comfort. Enjoyment. Delight. Gratification of the mind, Cicer. Pleasure, Plaut. Geniality, Amm. Soothing, Tac. Sunny brightness of the day, Col. Pleasantness of a place, Cic.

units.la: Jucundus] Festivus, Lepidus, Mellitus puer. Res plena delectationis, Cic. Magnam habet delectationem, Id. Tangit sensus bellè, jucundè.
units.tr: Jucundus] Festive, charming, a honey-sweet boy. A thing full of delight, Cic. It gives great pleasure, Id. It touches the senses nicely and pleasantly.

units.la: Judæus] Judæus recutitus. Sabbatarius, Mart. Hebræus, Hieron. Apella, Hor. Verpus, Juven.
units.tr: Judæus] A circumcised Jew. A keeper of the Sabbath, Mart. A Hebrew, Hieron. Apella, Hor. A circumcised man, Juven.

units.la: Judaicus] Hebræus liquor, Stat.
units.tr: Judaicus] Hebrew liquor, Stat.

units.la: Judex] Juridicus, Sen. Prætor, Cic. Condemnator, Tac. Subsellia, pro judicibus ponit Mart.
units.tr: Judex] A judge of law, Sen. A praetor, Cic. A condemner, Tac. Benches, which Mart. uses to stand for judges.

units.la: Judex severus & incorruptus] Areopagita. Minos. Rhadamantus.
units.tr: Judex severus & incorruptus] An Areopagite. Minos. Rhadamanthus.

units.la: Judex corruptus] Argentariam patitur. Bos in lingua.
units.tr: Judex corruptus] He submits to bribery. An ox on the tongue.

units.la: Judicis rigor] Censorium supercilium, judicium nactus acutum.
units.tr: Judicis rigor] A censorious brow, having obtained a sharp judgement.

units.la: Judicare] Judicium facere. Arbitrium facere. Statuo & judico, Cic. Judicium profiteri.
units.tr: Judicare] To make a judgement. To make a decision. I state and judge, Cic. To profess a judgement.

units.la: Judicare (2) i. e. jus dicere] judicium de aliquo pronunciare, jus dicere alicui. Agere forum, judicium exercere inter aliquos. Cognoscere causas. Fit, committitur judicium. Litem suam facere. Dat operam judex alicui, judex in aliquem sedeo, Cic. Reddere judicium, ad Heren.
units.tr: Judicare (2) i.e. jus dicere] To pronounce a judgement about someone; to dispense justice to someone. To hold court, to exercise judgement between certain persons. To hear causes. The case is brought, the judgement is committed. To make the suit one's own. He gives his attention to someone as judge; I sit in judgement on someone, Cic. To render judgement, ad Heren.

units.la: Judicare ex parte de toto] E fimbria de texto judicare. Leonem ex unguibus aestimare. Ex sonitu ollas, aure probamus asellos.
units.tr: Judicare ex parte de toto] From the fringe to judge the cloth. To estimate the lion from its claws. We judge the pots by their sound, the donkeys by the ear.

units.la: Judica incorrupte] Audi utramque partem.
units.tr: Judica incorrupte] Hear both sides.

units.la: Judicialis, vid. Iuridic.
units.tr: Judicialis, see Iuridic.

units.la: Judiciosus] Auribus acutis homo, Calpurn. Magni consilii vir. Qui intelligens & prudens habet judicium, Cic. Acutis auribus. Emunctae naris homo, Hor. Acetum ei peracre est in pectore. Aquila in nubibus, Lipf.
units.tr: Judiciosus] A man with sharp ears, Calpurn. A man of great counsel. He who understands and is prudent has judgement, Cic. With keen ears. A man of clean nostrils, Hor. Vinegar is very sharp in his breast. An eagle among the clouds, Lips.

units.la: Judicium] Cognitio. Quaestio, jurisdictio, Cic. Judicatio, Id.
units.tr: Judicium] Knowledge. Inquiry, jurisdiction, Cic. Judging, Id.

units.la: Judicium, (2) judicandi acumen] Animi judicium. Sapientia ad judicandum. Prudentia in judicando, judicatus, us, Cic. Dispectus rerum agendarum, Sen.
units.tr: Judicium (2), the keenness of judging] Judgement of mind. Wisdom in judging. Prudence in judging; judgement, Cic. A survey of the things to be done, Sen.

units.la: Judicium iniquum] Dat veniam corvis, vexat censura columbas.
units.tr: Unfair judgement] He grants pardon to crows; censure harasses the doves.

units.la: Judicium justum] Judicium, aequum, bonum: vel, ex aequo & bono.
units.tr: Just judgement] A fair and good judgement: or, in equity and good conscience.

units.la: Judicium severum] Rhadamantheum judicium. Amphictyonum consessus. Areopagus.
units.tr: Severe judgement] A Rhadamanthine judgement. The assembly of the Amphictyons. The Areopagus.

units.la: Judicium praeceps, immaturum] Ante barbam senes doces. Ante pilos sapit. Antequam pisces ceperis, muriam misces. Judicium praeceps insani judicis index.
units.tr: Hasty, premature judgement] You teach old men before their beards grow. He is wise before his hairs. Before you have caught the fish, you mix the brine. Hasty judgement is the sign of a foolish judge.

units.la: Judicium inter paria faciendum] Purpura juxta purpuram dijudicanda.
units.tr: Judgement to be made between equals] Purple is to be judged beside purple.

units.la: Judicium de ignotis] Caecus parietem palpat. Caecus de coloribus. Vid. Ignoti nulla dijudicatio.
units.tr: Judgement about unknown things] The blind man feels his way along the wall. The blind man on colours. See Ignoti nulla dijudicatio.

units.la: Judicium de rebus futile] Apud pueros simia pulchra.
units.tr: Judgement about trivial things] Among children a monkey is beautiful.

units.la: Judicio non servili] Nullius addictus in verba jurare magistri, Hor.
units.tr: Independent judgement] Not bound to swear to the words of any master, Hor.

units.la: Ad judicium aliquem admittere] Accipere judicium pro aliquo. Dare alicui judicium. Dare alicui rei actionem. Admittere; Reus ad causam agendam admissus, Cic. Judicium constituere, edere. Edere actionem, Budæ.
units.tr: To admit someone to trial] To accept a trial on someone's behalf. To give someone a trial. To give someone the right of action. To admit: a defendant admitted to plead his case, Cic. To set up a trial, to bring an action, Budæ.

units.la: Judicium capitis, de cæde, vid. Causa capitis, &c. Capitalis.
units.tr: Capital trial, concerning murder, see Capital case, &c. Capital.

units.la: Jugamenta] Cubilia fenestrarum, Exemplo Vitr. qui cubilia tignorum vocat, in quibus tigna conquiescunt, Philand.
units.tr: Jugamenta] The beds of windows, following the example of Vitr., who calls the beds of beams the cradles in which the beams rest, Philand.

units.la: Jugare] Jungere tauros, Virg. Subdere jugo leones, Plin. Conjugare. Jungere equis rhedam, Cic. Conjungere boves, Cat. Sociare juvencos impositio aratro, Stat. Adjugare, Pacuv. Jungere equos ad currum, Plin. Agere sub juga tauros, Propert.
units.tr: To yoke: to join bulls, Virg. To subject lions to the yoke, Plin. To yoke together. To harness a carriage to horses, Cic. To yoke oxen together, Cat. To join young bulls by putting the plough on them, Stat. To yoke to, Pacuv. To harness horses to a chariot, Plin. To drive bulls under the yoke, Propert.

units.la: Jugarius] Conjugator, Catul.
units.tr: Jugarius: one who yokes together, Catul.

units.la: Jugis, jugiter, vid. Assiduè.
units.tr: Jugis, jugiter, see Assiduè.

units.la: Juglans] Nux juglans, Varr. Nux regia, basilica, Persica, vel, Persicum, basilicum caryon. Mollusca nux, Plin. Fructus nucis juglandis, Id. de arbore.
units.tr: Juglans: the walnut, Varr. The royal, basilican or Persian nut; also called the Persian basilican nut. A soft-shelled nut, Plin. The fruit of the walnut, Id. de arbore.

units.la: Jugulum] Jugulus præbendus erat, Quint.
units.tr: Jugulum: the throat was to be offered up, Quint.

units.la: Jumentum] Pecus operarium, Col. Veterinum genus. Veterina, pl. Plin. Jugatorius bos, Varr. Subjugis, Plin. Jugalis, Virg. Ovid.
units.tr: Jumentum: working livestock, Col. A kind of draught animal. Veterina, pl. Plin. A draught ox, Varr. Beasts placed under the yoke, Plin. Used for yoking, Virg. Ovid.

units.la: Junceus] Caudeus. Scirpeus, Plin. Juncinus, Id. Sirpeus, Scal.
units.tr: Junceus: of stems. Made of rushes, Plin. Of rushes, Id. Made of rushes, Scal.

units.la: Junctim, vid. Gregatim.
units.tr: Junctim, see Gregatim.

units.la: Juncus] Scirpus, Ter. Sirpus, Lamb. Scirpiculus, vel Sirpiculus, Varr.
units.tr: Juncus: a bulrush, Ter. A rush, Lamb. A little rush, or little bulrush, Varr.

units.la: Jungere] Conjungere diversa. Consociare consilia cum aliquo. Connectere. Sociare sapientiam cum eloquentia. Conjugare. Conciliare, Cic. Complectere manus, Sen. Nectere brachia, Ovid. Componere manibus manus. Committere se probis, Virg. Geminare, Hor.
units.tr: Jungere: to join different things together. To share counsels with someone. To connect. To join wisdom with eloquence. To couple. To win over, Cic. To clasp hands, Sen. To entwine arms, Ovid. To place hand against hand. To attach oneself to good men, Virg. To double, Hor.

units.la: Junior] Minor natu, Cic. Juvenilior annis, Ovid. Minor annis, Vlp. Minor à quinque annis. Minor quimo, quàm quimus, quàm quinque annorum, quàm quinque annos natus, Saturn.
units.tr: Junior: younger by birth, Cic. Younger than one's years suggest, Ovid. Younger in years, Vlp. Younger than five years. Younger than five, than we are five, than five years old, than one who is five years old, Saturn.

units.la: Jupiter] Stella Jovis. Phaëton, Cic. Mundi jecur.
units.tr: Jupiter: the star of Jove. Phaethon, Cic. The liver of the world.

units.la: Juramentum] Jusjurandum, Plaut. Jurandum jus, Pacuv. Sanctiora aditis juranda jura, Sen. Sacramentum, Liv. Affirmatio religiosa, Cic. Mantile, quo quotidianæ sordes exterguntur, Pacuv. Juratio, Macrob.
units.tr: Juramentum: an oath, Plaut. A law of swearing, Pacuv. Oaths more sacred than those one approaches, Sen. A sacrament, Liv. A religious affirmation, Cic. A cloth with which daily dirt is wiped away, Pacuv. Swearing, Macrob.

units.la: Jurare] Jurejurando affirmare. Affirmatè Deo teste promittere. Firmare diis immortalibus interpositis. Sanctè adjurare. Dare jusjurandum, Cic. Jure jurare, Liv. Dare fidem & jusjurandum. Obstringere se jurejurando, Cæs. Concipere jusjurandum, Tac. Interponere jusjurandum, Liv. Dicere sacramentum, Hor. Religione adjectâ affirmare. Religionum fidem dictis addere, Amm. Juramento spondere, jurare conceptis, Plaut. Dejerare persanctè, & dejerare, Ter. Dejurare, i. e. valdè jurare, Plaut. Jurandi fidem addendo firmare aliquid, Ammian. Jurandi exsecratione permittere, Id.
units.tr: Jurare: to affirm by oath. To promise firmly, calling God as witness. To confirm by invoking the immortal gods. To swear solemnly. To give an oath, Cic. To swear by right, Liv. To give one's word and oath. To bind oneself by oath, Caes. To take an oath, Tac. To put forward an oath, Liv. To speak the oath, Hor. To affirm with religious sanction added. To add the faith of religious oaths to one's words, Amm. To pledge by oath, to swear to what has been agreed, Plaut. To swear most solemnly, and to swear to the uttermost, Ter. To swear vehemently, that is, to swear with great force, Plaut. To confirm something by adding the pledge of an oath, Ammian. To allow by the curse of an oath, Id.

units.la: Jurare per vindicem Deum] Jovem lapidem jurare, jurare per Deos, Cic. Per Deos & Deas omnes, Plaut.
units.tr: To swear by the avenging God: to swear by the stone of Jove, to swear by the gods, Cic. By all gods and goddesses, Plaut.

units.la: Juratò] Sacramento rogatus es, Sen. Sub consecratione jurisjurandi promisère, Amm. Obstricto religionum consecratione colloquio, Id.
units.tr: Juratò: you were asked under oath, Sen. They promised under the sanction of an oath, Amm. In a conference bound by the solemn sanction of religious oaths, Id.

units.la: Jurator] Comitiales homines, Plaut. Subbasilicani, Id. Subrostrani. Comicus testis, Cic. Ordinarius homo, Fest. Præjurator, Sipont.
units.tr: Jurator: men of the assembly, Plaut. Men under the basilica, Id. Men under the rostra. A comic witness, Cic. An ordinary man, Fest. One who swears beforehand, Sipont.

units.la: Juratus] Juratissimus auctor, Plin. Sacramento imbutus miles, Tac. Sacramento tenetur, Suet. Sacramento rogatus, Quint. Qui sacramentum dixit, Hor. Jurejurando comprobatus, obstrictus, adstrictus, Recent.
units.tr: Juratus: a most sworn authority, Plin. A soldier bound by oath, Tac. Held by oath, Suet. Asked under oath, Quint. One who has spoken the oath, Hor. Confirmed, bound and tied by an oath, Recent.

units.la: Jure agere] Agere pro jure. Lege agere. Eo jure quo qui optimo, Cic. Ex jure, ex lege, per legem, justo sacramento. Eo jure, ut qui optimo, Id. Legibus, Ter. Legitimè, justis vindiciis & sacramentis, Bud.
units.tr: To act by law: to act on behalf of right. To proceed by statute. By that right by which the best man..., Cic. By right, by law, through statute, by a lawful oath. By that right, so that the best man..., Id. By the laws, Ter. Lawfully, by just claims and oaths, Bud.

units.la: Jure disceptare cum aliquo] Contendere, certare, disceptare jure. Decernere, confligare judicio. Persequi bona lite, judicio, jus de aliqua re adire. Litigare cum aliquo. Litem in aliquem, vel, alicui inferre. Intendere litem alicui. Habere litem cum aliquo. Summo jure experiri, Cic. Jure agere, Lucr. Lites sequi, Ter. Contendere lite, Quint. Agere litem adversus aliquem, Id. Jurgare, est de jure agere & contendere, Sipont.
units.tr: To dispute with someone at law: to contend, struggle, or argue on the basis of right. To decide, to fight out in court. To pursue goods by a lawsuit or by judgment; to approach the law concerning some matter. To go to law with someone. To bring a suit against someone, or to lodge one with someone. To bring a suit against someone. To have a lawsuit with someone. To prosecute with the utmost legal right, Cic. To act by law, Lucr. To pursue lawsuits, Ter. To contend in a lawsuit, Quint. To bring a suit against someone, Id. To quarrel is to act and contend on the basis of law, Sipont.

units.la: Jurgium, vid. Rixa.
units.tr: Jurgium, see Rixa.

units.la: Juridicialis] Judicialis, judiciarius quaestus. Forensis causa, actio. Fasti dies, Cic. Comitiales dies, Varr. Juridicus conventus, Plin. Legalis quaestio, tractatus, Quint.
units.tr: Juridicialis: judicial, of the courts. A judicial or judiciary business. A forensic cause or action. Fasti days, Cic. Comitial days, Varr. A juridical assembly, Plin. A legal inquiry or treatment, Quint.

units.la: Juris consultus] Pragmaticus, jure consultus. Interpres juris, juris peritus. Prudens in jure civili. Instructus à jure civili, &, in jure civili. Interpres legum. Versatus in causis. Valet in causis. Consultus juris. Qui consulitur, & respondet in jure. Qui legum, & consuetudinis ejus, quâ privati in civitate utuntur, & ad respondendum, & ad agendum, & ad cavendum peritus est, Cic. Jure peritus, Lucil. Prudens juris, Claud. Responsor, Hor. Formularum ac usus forensis callentissimus, Bud. Qui jura & leges tenet, Plaut.
units.tr: Jurisconsult: a practical lawyer, a jurisconsult. An interpreter of law, one skilled in law. Learned in civil law. Versed in civil law, and in civil law. An interpreter of the laws. Experienced in cases. Strong in cases. A consulted expert in law. One who is consulted and gives opinions on law. One who knows the laws and customs by which private citizens live in the state, and who is skilled in giving advice, in acting for others, and in giving security, Cic. Skilled in law, Lucil. Expert in law, Claud. One who gives responses, Hor. Most practised in forms and forensic usage, Bud. One who holds the laws and rights, Plaut.

units.la: Jurisprudentia] Jus, juris nodos solvere, Juvenal. Studium juris, Quint.
units.tr: Jurisprudence: to untie the knots of the law, Juvenal. The study of law, Quint.

units.la: Jus] Justum & jus colere, Cic. Judicium acre. Summum jus, Id. Rigor juris, jus exactius duriusque, Bud. Strictum, IC.
units.tr: Right: to cultivate the just and the right, Cic. A sharp judgment. The strictest right, Id. The rigour of law, a law more exact and harsher, Bud. Strict law, IC.

units.la: Jus & æquum immutabile sit] Fiat justitia, & pereat mundus. Patere legem, quam ipse tulisti.
units.tr: Let right and equity be unchanging: Let justice be done though the world perish. Abide by the law you yourself have passed.

units.la: Juste] Justissimè facere. Optimo jure. Incorruptè, castè judicare, Cic. Secundum jus fasque, Liv. Ex æquo facere, Tac. Ex justitia, Plin. Iun. Æquâ lance, Sen. Eâdem trutinâ pensare. Vid. Fas est.
units.tr: Justly: to act most justly. By the best right. To judge uncorruptly and chastely, Cic. According to right and divine law, Liv. To act with equal fairness, Tac. From justice, Plin. Iun. With an even balance, Sen. To weigh with the same scales. See Fas est.

units.la: Justitia] Æquitas, jus, Cic. Æquum, Quint. Servantissimus æqui, Virg.
units.tr: Justice: fairness, right, Cic. Equity, Quint. Most observant of equity, Virg.

units.la: Justitium] Res prolatæ. Rerum prolatio, Cic. Jurisdictionis intermissio, Liv. Juris cessatio, Gell. Tristi justitio clausa fora, Lucan.
units.tr: Justitium: things deferred. A postponement of affairs, Cic. A suspension of jurisdiction, Liv. A cessation of law, Gell. The courts closed by a gloomy suspension of justice, Lucan.

units.la: Justitium edicere, id est, differre judicia] Justitium indicere, edicere, jurisdictionem intermittere, judicia tollere. Obnunciatio interposita est. Prolatis rebus, id est, indicto justitio, Cic. Justitium servare, ut, justitium servatum est, Liv. Favere justitio, & omnium rerum licentiæ, Gell. Justitium est, ex Cic. qui dixit. Justitium futurum videbatur. Differre judicium, Quint.
units.tr: To proclaim a justitium, that is, to defer trials: to declare a justitium, to proclaim, to suspend jurisdiction, to abolish trials. A notice has been issued. With matters deferred, that is, with a justitium declared, Cic. To observe a justitium, as "a justitium was observed," Liv. To favour a justitium and the licence of all things, Gell. A justitium is..., from Cic., who said it. A justitium seemed likely to come. To defer a judgment, Quint.

units.la: Justus] Æquus, Cic. Justitiæ tenax. Ex justitia est nostrorum temporum, Plin. Iun. Servantissimus æqui, Virg. Nullum denarium intra limen suum admittit malè intrantem, Sen. Trutinâ, Phocione justior, justitiâ justior, Er. Aristides, (civis Atheniensis, justitiæ exemplar.)
units.tr: Just: fair, Cic. Tenacious of justice. Of the justice of our times, Plin. Iun. Most observant of equity, Virg. He admits no penny that enters his threshold dishonestly, Sen. More just than Phocion in the balance, more just in justice, Erasmus. Aristides, (a citizen of Athens, a model of justice.)

units.la: Juvamen, vid. Auxilium.
units.tr: Juvamen, see Auxilium.

units.la: Juvare aliquem] Adjuvare. Adjutare onus alicui. Adjumento esse. Subsidio alicui venire. Ferre opem, aliquid opis. Ferre labenti Reip. præsidium. Navare operam & studium alicui. Digitum porrigere in rem aliquem. Asservire alicui. Magnum momentum afferre ad. Suffragari alicui, prodesse, Cic. Operam mutuam dare, Gell. Auxiliari, Ter. Auxilia afferre, Id. Auxilio esse. Adjutor sum alicui auxilio. Mecum id militat. Subvenire alicui. Præstare operam alicui adjutabilem. Civis civi commodat operam, Plaut. Particeps sum alicui in operibus ruris, Quint. Sublevare laborem alicujus. Suppetias alicui ferre, ire, mittere, Cæs.
units.tr: To help someone: to assist. To share someone's burden. To be of help. To come to someone's aid. To bring help, to give some support. To come to the aid of a falling commonwealth. To lend effort and zeal to someone. To extend a finger to someone in a matter. To be devoted to someone. To bring great weight to. To back someone, to be of profit, Cic. To give mutual service, Gell. To lend aid, Ter. To bring aid, Id. To be of help. I am an aid to someone. This works in my favour. To come to someone's support. To render service to someone that can be assisted. One citizen lends service to another, Plaut. I share with someone in the work of the countryside, Quint. To relieve someone's labour. To bring, go with, or send aid to someone, Caes.

units.la: Juvenilis] Juvenilis dies, Suet. Juvenes anni, Ovid. Ephebicus, Apul.
units.tr: Juvenilis: youthful days, Suet. Youthful years, Ovid. Of the ephebe, Apul.

units.la: Juvenilibus annis] Dum genua virent. Intra juventam raptus, Tac.
units.tr: In youthful years: while the knees are still green. Snatched away within youth, Tac.

units.la: Juvenis] Juvenculus, Catul. Tenera ætas, Cic. Juventus primævo flore. Vid. Adolescens.
units.tr: Juvenis: a young fellow, Catul. Tender age, Cic. Youth in its first bloom. See Adolescens.

units.la: Juvenum est non posse seipsos regere] Vitium juvenile, non posse regere impetum, Sen.
units.tr: It is characteristic of the young not to be able to govern themselves: it is a youthful fault not to be able to restrain one's impulse, Sen.

units.la: Juvenibus labor, senibus quies] Quære adolescens, utere senex.
units.tr: Labour for the young, rest for the old: seek as a youth, enjoy as an old man.

units.la: Juvenis adj.] Tener puer. Novella arbor, Mustus, Cic. Musta virgo, Plaut. Musteus caseus. Infans boletus, pomum, Plin. Pubens herba, Virg. Juvencæ aves, juveniles anni Ovid. Juvenilior semper suis annis, Silen. Primævo flore, Virg.
units.tr: Young, as adjective: a tender boy. A young tree, fresh and new, Cic. A young maiden, Plaut. Fresh cheese. A young mushroom, a young fruit, Plin. Growing grass, Virg. Young birds, youthful years, Ovid. Always younger than his years, Silen. In first bloom, Virg.

units.la: Juventus pro pueris] Juventa, Mart. Omnem Italiæ pubem ei commiserat, Cic. Juventus, pro ætate] Ætatis ver breve, juventa, Non. Pubertas, Col. Pubes. Bona ætas, Cic. Flos ævi, ætatis, Lucr. Multicupida juventilitas, Varr. Lubricum ætatis, Vlp. Lubricum ætatulæ virentis, Apul. Juventas, Lucr. Juventas est Dea præses juventutis, Hor. Liv. Flos ætatis, Cic.
units.tr: Youth for boys: youth, Mart. He had entrusted all the youth of Italy to him, Cic. Juventus, pro ætate] A brief spring of life, youth, Non. Puberty, Col. Adolescence. A good age, Cic. The flower of life and age, Lucr. Eager youthfulness, Varr. The slipperiness of age, Vlp. The slipperiness of flourishing youth, Apul. Youth, Lucr. Youth is the goddess presiding over young people, Hor. Liv. The flower of age, Cic.

units.la: Juxta] Secundùm mare ire. Proximus Pompejum sedebam, Cic. Prope oppidum. Propter ædem Vulcani, Cic.
units.tr: Juxta: to go along the sea. I was sitting next to Pompey, Cic. Near the town. Beside the temple of Vulcan, Cic.

units.la: Juxtà tempus] Pro ratione temporis. Ut ratio temporis postulabit, Cic. Ad rationem temporis, Plin. Iun. Prout tempus patiebatur, Liv.
units.tr: According to the time: in proportion to the time. As the reason of the time will demand, Cic. According to the circumstances of the time, Plin. Iun. As the time allowed, Liv.

units.la: Juxta rem ac locum] Pro re ac loco, Salust. Prout res ac locus, ex Liv. Ad rationem loci, Plin.
units.tr: According to the matter and place: for the matter and place, Sallust. As the matter and place, from Liv. According to the reason of the place, Plin.

units.la: L.
units.tr: L.

units.la: Labans] Lapsabundus, Sen. Casabundus, Enn. Succiduus gressus, Claud. Prociduus, Plin. Vertilabundus, Varr. Labens domus, Virg.
units.tr: Labans (tottering, sliding): slipping, Sen.; tottering, Enn.; a faltering step, Claud.; falling forward, Plin.; reeling, Varr.; a house sinking into ruin, Virg.

units.la: Labascere] Vacillare. Toto corpore in utramque partem vacillans. Labare, Nutare. Fluctuare, Cic. Vacillat ex vino, Quint. Minatur & nutat ornus accisa, Virg. Collabascere, Lucr. Collabescieri, Caes.
units.tr: To begin to totter [labascere]: to be unsteady. Swaying with the whole body this way and that. To totter [labare], to nod [nutare]. To fluctuate Cic. He reels from wine Quint. The cut ash tree threatens and nods Virg. To collapse [collabascere] Lucr. To collapse [collabescieri] Caes.

units.la: Labefacere, vid. Debilitare.
units.tr: Labefacere: see Weaken [Debilitare].

units.la: Labefactare] Infringere lilia, Ovid. Infirmare. Frangere alicujus opes. Violare amicitiam, existimationem. Exulcerare gratiam alicujus, Cic. Delumbare, Plin. Delibare aliquid, Varr.
units.tr: To shake [labefactare]: to crush lilies Ovid. To weaken. To break someone's power. To violate friendship or reputation. To sore someone's favour Cic. To weaken the loins Plin. To nibble at something Varr.

units.la: Labefieri, vid. Debilitare.
units.tr: Labefieri: see Weaken [Debilitare].

units.la: Labeo] Labiosus, Lucr. Labrosus. Broccus, Plin.
units.tr: Thick-lipped [labeo]: thick-lipped [labiosus] Lucr. Thick-lipped [labrosus]. Projecting-toothed [broccus] Plin.

units.la: Labes] Labecula, Cic. Macula, Plin. Sordes luxuriæ, Juven.
units.tr: Stain [labes]: a little stain [labecula] Cic. A spot [macula] Plin. The filth of luxury Juven.

units.la: Labi, vid. Cadere.
units.tr: Labi: see Fall [Cadere].

units.la: Labilis] Caducus. Ruinosus. Præcipitans Resp. Ad terram fertur, Cic. Vid. Labans.
