units.tr: Slippery [labilis]: falling [caducus]. Ruinous. Hurtling headlong. Carried down to the ground Cic. See Tottering [Labans].

units.la: Labium] Labrum, labellum, Cic. Suavium, vel, Savium, Plaut. Lacuna, Lactant. Nympha, Iun. Valvæ oris.
units.tr: Lip [labium]: a lip [labrum], a little lip [labellum] Cic. A kiss [suavium, or savium] Plaut. A hollow [lacuna] Lactant. A nymph Iun. The doors of the mouth.

units.la: Labor] Labos, Plaut. Elaboratio operæ. Sudor, Cic. Res multæ operæ, Plaut. Opella, Hor. Fallimentum temporis optimum, Anon.
units.tr: Toil [labor]: toil [labos] Plaut. The working out of effort. Sweat Cic. A matter of much effort Plaut. A little work Hor. The best waste of time Anon.

units.la: Labor omnia superat] Quod natura negat, labor præbet. Perrumpit Acheronta Herculeus labor, Hor. Labor improbus omnia vincit, Virg. Omnia diligentiæ subjiciuntur. Omnia pulchra laborans consequitur. Omnia conando docilis solertia vincit.
units.tr: Labour overcomes all things [labor omnia superat]: What nature denies, labour supplies. Herculean labour breaks through Acheron Hor. Unrelenting toil conquers all Virg. All things are subject to diligence. Whoever labours at all fine things attains them. Nimble skill, learned by striving, conquers all.

units.la: Labor irritus] Ovem agglutinans. Canem vetulum loris assuefacere difficile. Cani cum balneo nihil. Semitam quærere, cùm sit via. Frustraneus labor. Vid. Inutilem rem.
units.tr: Vain labour [labor irritus]: gluing a sheep. It is hard to train an old dog with straps. Nothing is gained by bathing a dog. Seeking a path when there is already a way. Fruitless labour. See Useless thing.

units.la: Labor etiam parvus, fatigat] Etiam palea longo ex itinere oneri est.
units.tr: Even small labour wearies [labor etiam parvus, fatigat]: even a straw is a burden on a long journey.

units.la: Qualis labor fuerit, talis & merces] Ut sementem feceris, ita & metes. Quicquid seminaverit homo, hoc & metet. Quicquid intrivisti, hoc tibi exedendum est. Ut quisque est meritus, præmium ferat.
units.tr: As the labour, so the reward [qualis labor fuerit, talis et merces]: as you sow, so shall you reap. Whatever a man sows, that he shall also reap. What you have ground in, you must eat up. Each should receive the reward he has earned.

units.la: Labor vegetat] Labore vigent artus.
units.tr: Labour gives life [labor vegetat]: the limbs thrive through labour.

units.la: Labore uno duplex opus conficere] Apros duos in uno saltu capere. Unâ fidelià duos dealbare parietes.
units.tr: To do a double task with one labour: to catch two boars in one leap. To whitewash two walls with one brush.

units.la: Labori debetur præmium] Omnis labor optat præmium. Ingratus ille labor, quem præmia nulla sequuntur.
units.tr: Reward is due to labour [labori debetur praemium]: every labour desires its reward. That labour is thankless which no rewards follow.

units.la: Labori ne parcat, qui fructum quærit] Qui nucleum esse vult, nucem frangat oportet. Dii laboribus vendunt omnia, Hesiod. Ora, & labora, dabit Deus omnia bona. Vigilantibus & non dormientibus jura subveniunt. Lutum nisi tundatur, non fit testa. Molam qui vitat, vitat farinam. Non tibi per ventos assa columba venit. Affundat oleum, qui indiget lucerna.
units.tr: Let him who seeks the fruit not spare his labour: whoever wants the kernel must crack the nut. The gods sell all things for labour Hesiod. Pray and work, and God will give all good things. Laws help the watchful, not the sleepers. Unless clay is beaten, it does not become a pot. He who avoids the millstone avoids the flour. A roast pigeon does not fly to you through the winds. He who needs a lamp must pour in oil.

units.la: Per labores ad honores] Fugiens labores fugit honores, Thucyd. Per templum virtutis, ad templum honoris. Scandit per ardua virtus.
units.tr: Through labours to honours [per labores ad honores]: whoever flees labours flees honours Thucyd. Through the temple of virtue to the temple of honour. Virtue climbs by steep paths.

units.la: Labores interminabiles] Sisyphi labores.
units.tr: Endless labours: the labours of Sisyphus.

units.la: Laborem immensum suscipere] Harenam metiri.
units.tr: To undertake an immense labour: to measure the sand.

units.la: Labor diurnus infelix] Acum invenisses.
units.tr: A day's labour that comes to nothing: you might as well have found a needle.

units.la: Labore & quiete] Otiari strenuè & actuosè.
units.tr: By labour and rest: to take one's leisure vigorously and actively.

units.la: Sine labore] Citra arationem. Citra sementem. Citra pulverem. Impulvis, Gell.
units.tr: Without labour: without ploughing. Without sowing. Without dust. Without dust Gell.

units.la: Laborare] Sudare pro communibus bonis. Frangere se laboribus. Exercere se labore. Sustinere, ferre laborem. Consumere multum operæ & laboris in aliqua re. Exantlare labores. Suscipere labores. Noctes & dies in opere aliquo urgeri. Impendere, insumere multum laboris in aliqua re. Exsudare laborem, Liv. Exercete corpus viri. Impendere laborem, operam, Cic.
units.tr: To labour: to sweat for the common good. To break oneself with labours. To exercise oneself in labour. To endure and bear labour. To spend much effort and toil on something. To go through labours. To take up labours. To be driven night and day at some task. To expend much labour on something. To sweat out one's labour Liv. Exercise the body of a man. To expend labour and effort Cic.

units.la: Laborare in incertum] Committere se fortunæ. Permittere sententiis judicium vitam, Cic. Dare ratem fluctibus. Casum ducem sequi, Sen. Aleam sequi, Varr. Permittere vela ventis, Quint. Rem, se, in casum dare, Tac. Liv. In dubiam aleam irc, Liv. Jacere aleam, Adag.
units.tr: To labour at an uncertain thing: to commit oneself to fortune. To entrust one's judgment and life to opinions Cic. To give one's ship to the waves. To follow chance as one's guide Sen. To follow the dice Varr. To entrust the sails to the winds Quint. To put a matter, or oneself, to chance Tac. Liv. To go into a doubtful throw Liv. To cast the die Adag.

units.la: Laborare alternatim] Operam vicariam alicui impendere, Quint. Partes alicujus agere. Transferre in se alterius maledicta. Pro aliquo sufferre aliquid, Ter. Officium & partes alicujus, pro aliquo, suscipere. Supponere se pro aliquo. Sustinere partes alicujus. Fungi officio alicujus. Præstare aliquem: alicujus factum, Cic. Vicem alterius implere. Subire vices alicujus, Plin. Præstare vicem alicujus, Ovid. Fungi vicem alterius, Liv. Fungi officium alicujus, Ter. Munus alicujus, Plaut.
units.tr: To labour in turn: to lend vicarious effort to someone Quint. To play another's part. To take another's slanders upon oneself. To bear something on behalf of someone Ter. To take up another's duty and role on his behalf. To put oneself in someone's place. To sustain another's parts. To perform another's office. To represent someone, or someone's deed Cic. To fill another's place. To undertake someone's place Plin. To perform someone's turn Ovid. To fulfil another's turn Liv. To perform someone's office Ter. Someone's duty Plaut.

units.la: Laborare frustra, vid. Frustra.
units.tr: To labour in vain: see Vain [Frustra].

units.la: Laboriosè] Operosè, actuosè. Multo sudore ac labore. Cum labore operoso ac molesto. Nimiâ cum cura & opera, Cic. Laboriosius, Id.
units.tr: Laboriously [laboriose]: industriously, actively. With much sweat and toil. With laborious and troublesome effort. With great care and effort Cic. More laboriously Id.

units.la: Laboriosus] Senectus operosa & semper aliquid agens. Actuosa virtus. Laboris amans. Ab agendo non cessans. Nunquam in studio & opere suo cessavit. Studiosus, Cic. Sedula apis, Tibul. Patiens operum juventus, Virg.
units.tr: Laborious [laboriosus]: an active old age, always doing something. Active virtue. Loving toil. Not ceasing from doing. Never ceased in his study and work. Diligent Cic. The busy bee Tibul. A youth patient in work Virg.

units.la: Labrum, vas] Lavabrum, Lucr.Turneb. Lavacrum, Claud. Solium, Celf. Fest. Suet. Lutra, Rhodig.
units.tr: Basin, vessel [labrum, vas]: a washbasin [lavabrum] Lucr. Turneb. A bath [lavacrum] Claud. A tub [solium] Celf. Fest. Suet. A trough [lutra] Rhodig.

units.la: Labrusca] Vitis fera, Non. Ampellos agria. Vitis silvestris. Oenanthe. (Hinc Oenanthinum vinum.) Massaris, idis. Plin.
units.tr: Wild vine [labrusca]: a wild vine [vitis fera] Non. A wild grape [ampelos agria]. A forest vine. Oenanthe. (Hence oenanthine wine.) Massaris, idis. Plin.

units.la: Lac] Ros vitalis, Cic. Mulctra, Col. Spuma sanguinis, Varr.Cat.
units.tr: Milk [lac]: vital dew Cic. A milk pail [mulctra] Col. The foam of blood Varr. Cat.

units.la: Lactis cremor] Flos lactis. Pingue lactis, Iun. Pinguc lac, Plin.
units.tr: Cream of milk [lactis cremor]: the flower of milk. Fat of milk Iun. Thick milk Plin.

units.la: Lacer, vid. Pannosus. Vulneratus.
units.tr: Torn [lacer]: see Ragged, Wounded.

units.la: Lacerare] Discerpere unguibus. Conscindere. Concerpere. Radere, Cic. Carpere, Serv. Sauciare, Ovid. Collaceratum corpus, Tac. Laniare tunicam, distringere, Ovid. Divellere. Diloricare, Cic.
units.tr: To tear [lacerare]: to tear with the nails. To cut to pieces. To tear apart. To scrape Cic. To mangle Serv. To wound Ovid. A mangled body Tac. To rip a tunic, to pull apart Ovid. To pull apart. To strip of armour Cic.

units.la: Lacerna] Tegillum, Apul. Tunica, Cic. Plebejus amictus, Propert. Famularis vestis, Val. M. Encomboma, Varr.
units.tr: Cloak [lacerna]: a little covering Apul. A tunic Cic. A plebeian cloak Propert. A servant's garment Val. M. A cloak [encomboma] Varr.

units.la: Lacerta] Lacertus, Plin.
units.tr: Lizard [lacerta]: a lizard, or the muscle of the arm [lacertus] Plin.

units.la: Lacertus] Brachium, Cic. Humerus, Cels.
units.tr: Arm [lacertus]: the upper arm [brachium] Cic. The shoulder [humerus] Cels.

units.la: Lacessere, vid. Irritare.
units.tr: To provoke [lacessere]: see Irritate.

units.la: Lacinia vestis] Ora vestimenti, Fest. Extremum vestimenti. Fimbria vestis, Plin. Peniculamentum, Lucil. Vid. Gremium vestis.
units.tr: Fringe of a garment [lacinia vestis]: the border of a garment Fest. The extremity of a garment. The fringe of a garment Plin. A dust-cloth [peniculamentum] Lucil. See Lap of a garment.

units.la: Laconicus] Paucorum verborum. Breviloquens, Cic.
units.tr: Laconic [laconicus]: of few words. Brief in speech Cic.

units.la: Laconismus, vid. Breviloquentia.
units.tr: Laconism [laconismus]: see Brevity of speech.

units.la: Lacryma] Lacrymula, Cic. Pumiceos oculos habet, nequit exorare lacrymam, ut exspuat unam modo. Genus siccoculum, i. e. non lacrymans, Plaut.
units.tr: Tear [lacryma]: a little tear [lacrymula] Cic. He has eyes of pumice; he cannot be prayed into shedding a tear, not even to spit out just one. A dry-eyed kind, that is, one not weeping Plaut.

units.la: Lacrymari] Indulgere lacrymis. Lacrymas effundere. Lacrymis confici. Lacrymæ oboriuntur, erumpunt, volvuntur, Ovid. Vim lacrymarum profundere. Dedere se lacrymis. Iacere in lacrymis, Cic. Vid. Flere.
units.tr: To weep [lacrymari]: to indulge in tears. To pour out tears. To be worn down with tears. Tears well up, burst forth, roll down Ovid. To pour out a flood of tears. To give oneself up to tears. To lie in tears Cic. See Weep [Flere].

units.la: Lacrymosè, vid. Flebiliter.
units.tr: Tearfully [lacrymose]: see Tearfully [Flebiliter].

units.la: Lacrymosus] Plorabundus. Largus lacrymarum, Plin. Flebilis gemitus, Cic. Lacrymabile tempus. Lacrymosum carmen, Ovid.
units.tr: Tearful [lacrymosus]: weeping, tearful [plorabundus]. Abounding in tears Plin. A mournful sigh Cic. A time for tears. A tearful song Ovid.

units.la: Lactare]Nutrire mammis fœtum, Plin. Nutricare, Plaut. Alere fœtum ubere. Indulgere lac, Virg. Mammam dare, Plaut.
units.tr: To suckle [lactare]: to nourish the young at the teat Plin. To nurse [nutricare] Plaut. To feed the young at the breast. To give milk Virg. To give the teat Plaut.

units.la: Lactarius] Lactaria bos, Col. Lactans, Gell.
units.tr: Suckling [lactarius]: a milch cow Col. Suckling Gell.

units.la: Lactere] Sugere, abs. Cic. Sugere ubera, Ovid. Trahunt agni maternum alimentum, Col.
units.tr: To suck [lactere]: to suck, absolutely Cic. To suck the breasts Ovid. Lambs draw their mother's nourishment Col.

units.la: Lacteus] Lacteus porcus. Lacte pastus, Mart. Subrumus agnus, Var. Nefrens, Liv.
units.tr: Milky [lacteus]: a suckling pig. Fed on milk Mart. A suckling lamb Var. Unweaned Liv.

units.la: Lactitinia, barb.] Lactaria, pl. Lamp. Lactantia, pl. Cels. Bud. Lactarii cibi, Bud.
units.tr: Milk-foods [lactitinia, barbarous]: milk-fed things [lactaria], plural Lamp. Milk-things [lactantia], plural Cels. Bud. Milk foods Bud.

units.la: Lactuca] Lactucula, Suet. Astylis, Meconis, Plin. Lacuna] Lacus, Varr. Coeni confluges, ex Sipont.
units.tr: Lettuce [lactuca]: a little lettuce Suet. Astylis, Meconis Plin. Pool [lacuna]: a lake [lacus] Varr. Muddy pools ex Sipont.

units.la: Ledere, vid. Offendere.
units.tr: To offend [ledere]: see Offend.

units.la: Latari] Lætitiam percipere. Lætitiâ efferri, excitari, perfrui, gestire. Explicare, exporrigere frontem. Sustollere manum, Cic. Lætum esse de aliquâ re, Ter. Lætificari in aliqua re, Plaut. Hilarescere, Varr. Vid. Gaudere.
units.tr: To rejoice [latari]: to receive joy. To be carried away with gladness, stirred, to enjoy fully, to be eager. To unfold and smooth the brow. To raise the hand Cic. To be glad about something Ter. To be cheered in something Plaut. To grow cheerful Varr. See Rejoice [Gaudere].

units.la: Latè, vid. Hilariter.
units.tr: Widely [late]: see Cheerfully [Hilariter].

units.la: Latificare aliquem] Afficere aliquem lætitiâ. Animum integrare, renovare, Cic. Beare, Plaut. Diffundere animum alicujus, Ovid. Diffundere faciem alicui, Sen. Hilaritate confspergere, Cic. In lætitiam conjicere, Ter. Vid. Exhilarare.
units.tr: To gladden someone [latificare aliquem]: to affect someone with joy. To renew and refresh the mind Cic. To make happy Plaut. To pour out someone's spirit Ovid. To spread cheerfulness over someone's face Sen. To sprinkle with cheerfulness Cic. To throw into joy Ter. See Cheer [Exhilarare].

units.la: Latitia, vid. Gaudium.
units.tr: Gladness [latitia]: see Joy [Gaudium].

units.la: Latus] Gestiens lætitiâ. Lætus omnibus lætitiis. Lætus animus, Cic. Lætus animi, Paterc. Plenus lætitiæ, Hor. Immodicus lætitiæ, Tac. Lubens, Ter. Remissus, Suet. Renidens os, Ovid. Floridus color, Plin. Lætafter, Fest.
units.tr: Glad [latus]: exulting with joy. Glad in all joys. A glad spirit Cic. Glad of mind Paterc. Full of joy Hor. Immoderate in joy Tac. Willing Ter. Relaxed Suet. A smiling face Ovid. A flourishing colour Plin. Joyful Fest.

units.la: Læva, vid. Sinistra.
units.tr: Left [laeva]: see Left [Sinistra].

units.la: Lævigare aliquid] Læware exasperata, Celf. Allævare ferro furculum, Cat. Delævare cultro plagam, Col. Dolare robur, Cic. Edolare, Non. Despumare cote pavimentum, Vitr. Pumice expolire, Catul. Pumicare, Tibul.
units.tr: To smooth something [laevigare aliquid]: to smooth what is rough Celf. To smooth a forked stick with iron Cat. To smooth a wound with a knife Col. To hew oak Cic. To shave down Non. To smooth a pavement with pumice Vitr. To polish with pumice Catul. To pumice Tibul.

units.la: Lævis] Lenis locus. Politus, Cic. Perpolitum aurum tritu, Plin. Rasilis fibula, Col. Edolatus, Id. Exasciatus, Plaut. Ad unguem factus, Hor.
units.tr: Smooth [laevis]: a smooth place. Polished Cic. Gold polished by rubbing Plin. A smoothed brooch Col. Smoothed with the axe Plaut. Made exactly to the nail Hor.

units.la: Lævitas] Lævor spectatur in chartis, Plin.
units.tr: Smoothness [laevitas]: smoothness is seen on papers Plin.

units.la: Lævorsum, vid. Sinister.
units.tr: Leftwards [laevorsum]: see Left [Sinister].

units.la: Lagena] Laguna, Pallad. Oenophorum, Mart. Lagunc-ula, Plin. Ampulla, Suet.
units.tr: Flask [lagena]: a flask [laguna] Pallad. A wine jar [oenophorum] Mart. A little flask Plin. A bottle Suet.

units.la: Laicus] Homo è vulgo Christianorum, Crom. Popularis, sacris non initiatus, Bud.
units.tr: Lay [laicus]: a man from the common crowd of Christians Crom. Of the common people, not initiated into sacred rites Bud.

units.la: Lambere] Allambere, Quint. Delambere, Stat. Lingere. Delingere, Plaut. Lambitare, Solin.
units.tr: To lick [lambere]: to lick over Quint. To lick off Stat. To lick, to lick clean Plaut. To lap Solin.

units.la: Lamentabilis comploratio] Quæribundâ voce dicebat, Cic. Amarus luctus, Ovid. Effusus in lacrymas, Tac. Effusus ad lacrymas. Amarulentus, Gell.
units.tr: Lamentable wailing] Speaking in a plaintive voice, Cic. Bitter grief, Ovid. Dissolved in tears, Tac. Dissolved into tears. Bitterly lamenting, Gell.

units.la: Lamentari] Lamentis vacare. Lacrymis se muliebribus lamentisque dedere. Lamentabili voce aliquid deplorare. Commiserari. Conqueri,Cic. Ejulare,Plaut. Miserari,Non. Plangore & lamentatione complere forum. Edere plora-tum,Cic. Plangere. Deplangere, Ovid. Pectus percutere manu, Virg. Ululare ,Lucan. Obvagulari, &, obvagula-tum ire, Fest. Occentare ostium, Plaut.
units.tr: To lament] To give oneself up to lamentation. To give oneself over to womanish tears and wailing. To deplore something in a lamenting voice. To commiserate. To complain, Cic. To wail, Plaut. To pity, Non. To fill the forum with beating of breasts and lamentation. To utter a loud weeping, Cic. To beat the breast. To lament bitterly, Ovid. To strike the breast with the hand, Virg. To howl, Lucan. To wail aloud, and to go about wailing, Fest. To serenade the door, Plaut.

units.la: Lamentatio] Lamentum. Ejulatus. Ejulatio. Percussio pectoris, capitis. Laceratio genarum, Cic. Planctus, Stat. Pipulum, Plaut.Fest. Vagulatio, Fest. Lessus,Cic. Plaut.
units.tr: Lamentation] Lamenting. Wailing. Howling. Beating of the breast or head. Tearing of the cheeks, Cic. Lamentation, Stat. Mourning, Plaut., Fest. Wailing, Fest. Dirge, Cic., Plaut.

units.la: Lamia, vid. Lemures.
units.tr: Lamia, see Lemures.

units.la: Lampas] Trulla ferrea, Liv. Iun. Lychnuchus, Suet.
units.tr: Lamp] An iron pan, Liv., Iun. A lamp-stand, Suet.

units.la: Lana] Lanula, Celf. Lanicium, Plin. Vellus,Cic. Coma ovium, Col. Lana puta, Titin.
units.tr: Wool] Fine wool, Celsus. Wool-work, Plin. A fleece, Cic. The hair of sheep, Col. Wool, you may say, Titin.

units.la: Lana impura] Lana succida, osca, Varr. Oesypum. Lana cum sudore & sordibus, Plin. Solox lana, Titin.
units.tr: Unwashed wool] Wool that is greasy, or from the Oscans, Varr. Yolk-wool. Wool with sweat and dirt, Plin. Wool that is dirty, Titin.

units.la: Lanaria] Lanosus. Lanatus, Col. Lanatior canities foliorum. Lanifera arbor, Plin. Lanifer grex, Virg.
units.tr: Woolly] Covered with wool. Woolly, Col. A woollier whiteness of leaves. A tree bearing wool, Plin. A flock bearing wool, Virg.

units.la: Lancea] Romphaea. Hasta velitaris , Liv. Hasta velitis, Ovid. Sibyna, Gell.
units.tr: Lance] A broadsword. A light javelin, Liv. A light spear, Ovid. A Sibyna, Gell.

units.la: Laneus] Lanatus pileus, Fest. Velleus , Ascon. Lane-stris, Flav. Vopisc.
units.tr: Woollen] A cap made of wool, Fest. Of wool, Ascon. Woollen garments, Flav., Vopisc.

units.la: Lancinare, vid. Vellicare.
units.tr: To tear to pieces, see To pluck.

units.la: Languere] Languescere corpore. Debilitari. Deficiunt vires. Vacillare memoriâ. Esse remissum,Cic. Languidior sum tenerâ beta, Catul. Lentet opus, Lucil. Inflaccebunt conditiones, Enn. Conflaccescere, Gell. Torpent consilia,Liv. Senescit pugna, Id. Ægrotant in te artes antiquae , Plaut. Infirmatur transactio,Vlp. Vid. Debilitari, Lassari.
units.tr: To languish] To grow faint in body. To be weakened. Strength fails. To waver in memory. To be slackened, Cic. I am more languid than a tender beet, Catul. The work drags on, Lucil. The terms will grow weak, Enn. To wither away, Gell. Plans grow numb, Liv. The battle flags, Id. The ancient arts are sick in you, Plaut. The agreement is weakened, Ulp. See To be weakened, To be wearied.

units.la: Languidè, languidus, languor. vid. Debilis, &c.
units.tr: Languidly, languid, languor, see Weak, etc.

units.la: Laniare, vid. Lacerare.
units.tr: To mangle, see To tear.

units.la: Laniena] Laniarium. Taberna lanigna, Varr. Lanionia mensa, Suet. Lanea, Liv.
units.tr: Butchery] A slaughterhouse. A butcher's shop, Varr. A butcher's table, Suet. A butchery, Liv.

units.la: Lanio] Lanius ,Ter. Carnarius , Iun. Liv. Conciliator carnis suillae,Varr. Qui concinnant (i. reddunt) oves liberis orbas, Plaut. Bucaeda, vel Bucida, Id. & Lamb.
units.tr: Butcher] A butcher, Ter. A meat-seller, Iun., Liv. A broker of pork, Varr. Those who make sheep bereft of their children, Plaut. Bucaeda, or Bucida, Id., and Lamb.

units.la: Lanista] Gladiatorum princeps, magister, Cic. Doctor, Val. Max.
units.tr: Gladiator-trainer] The chief, master of gladiators, Cic. A teacher, Val. Max.

units.la: Lanuginosus, vid Hirsutus.
units.tr: Downy, see Hairy.

units.la: Lanugo] Fibrae radicum, Cic. Capillamenta. Villi radicis, Plin. Hirsutiae, Sol. Lanositas, Tertull.
units.tr: Down] The fibres of roots, Cic. Small hairs. The fuzz of a root, Plin. Hairiness, Sol. Woolliness, Tertull.

units.la: Lapicida] Lapidarius, Firm. Marmorarius, Sen. Faber marmoris, Hor. Latomus, Cael.Rhod. Quadratarius, Sidon. Caementarius, Sipont.
units.tr: Stonecutter] A stone-mason, Firm. A marble-worker, Sen. A marble craftsman, Hor. A quarryman, Cael. Rhod. A hewer of square stone, Sidon. A builder of rubble walls, Sipont.

units.la: Lapicidinae] Latomiae, latumiae, Lautumiae, Plaut. Varr. Lautumiae lapidariae, Plaut.
units.tr: Quarries] Latomiae, latumiae, lautumiae, Plaut., Varr. Stone quarries, Plaut.

units.la: Lapidare aliquem] Lapidibus obruere, cooperire,Cic. Petere aliquem saxis, Ovid.
units.tr: To stone someone] To overwhelm or cover someone with stones, Cic. To attack someone with rocks, Ovid.

units.la: Lapidescere ] Trahere duritiam, figuram lapidis, Ovid. Vid. Durescere.
units.tr: To turn to stone] To take on the hardness and shape of stone, Ovid. See To harden.

units.la: Lapideus ] Lapidata templa, Suet. Saxeus mons, Virg. Pumiceus, Stat. Domus caementitia, Vitr. Vlp.
units.tr: Stony] Temples paved with stone, Suet. A rocky mountain, Virg. Of pumice, Stat. A house of rubble, Vitr., Ulp.

units.la: Lapidosus] Saxosus,Virg.Calculosus ager,Col. Scruposus, Apul. Petrosus,Plin. Scrupea spelunca,Virg. Saxetum,Cic.
units.tr: Stony] Rocky, Virg. A field full of pebbles, Col. Craggy, Apul. Gravelly, Plin. A rocky cave, Virg. A rocky place, Cic.

units.la: Lapis ] Ossa terrae, Ovid. Saxum manuale, Plin. Tacit. Calx, (unde Calculus) Fest. Isid.
units.tr: Stone] Bones of the earth, Ovid. A hand-stone, Plin., Tacit. Lime (whence calculus, a pebble), Fest., Isid.

units.la: Lapsus, vid. Casus.
units.tr: Fall, see Chance.

units.la: Laquear]Lacunar, Cic. Coelum contignationum, Serv. Philand. Imum coelum camerarum, Vitr. Laqueare,Virg.
units.tr: Ceiling] A panelled ceiling, Cic. The sky of floors, Serv., Philand. The lowest sky of vaulted rooms, Vitr. A ceiling, Virg.

units.la: Laqueus ] Pedica, Virg. Transsenna, Plaut. Tenus, ûs, & Tenum, Id. Tendicula, Sipont. Cippus, Meurs.
units.tr: Snare] A fetter, Virg. A net, Plaut. A noose, Id. A small snare, Sipont. A trap, Meurs.

units.la: Lardum Laridum, Plaut. Taxea, Afran.
units.tr: Lard] Bacon, Plaut. Salted pork, Afran.

units.la: Large, vid. Liberaliter. Copiosè.
units.tr: Generously, see Liberally. Copiously.

units.la: Largiri, vid. Dare.
units.tr: To bestow, see To give.

units.la: Largus, vid. Copiosus. Liberalis.
units.tr: Generous, see Copious. Liberal.

units.la: Largitio] Donatio. Condonatio, Cic. Muneratio, Vlp.
units.tr: Largess] A gift. A bestowing, Cic. A present, Vlp.

units.la: Larva} Persona adjicitur capiti. Persona cerea, Gell. Lucr. Oraque corticibus sumunt horrenda cavatis, Virg.
units.tr: Mask] A persona fitted to the head. A wax mask, Gell., Lucr. And they take on horrible faces made of hollowed bark, Virg.

units.la: Lascivia] Lascivia Veneris, Ovid. Conjunctionis appetitus. Mulierositas. Libido procreandi, Cic. Petulantia, Col. Salacitas, Plaut. Mulierariae voluptatis cupiditas, Trebell. Libido commiscendorum corporum. Venerea voluptas. Res Venereae, Cic. Veneris damnosa voluptas, Ovid.
units.tr: Lasciviousness] The wantonness of love, Ovid. Desire for union. Lust for women. Lust for procreation, Cic. Wantonness, Col. Lewdness, Plaut. Desire for the pleasure of women, Trebell. Lust for mingling bodies. Venereal pleasure. Matters of love, Cic. The ruinous pleasure of love, Ovid.

units.la: Lascivire ] Catullire uxorem, Plaut. Adhinnire puellis, Prudent. Gestire, Cic.
units.tr: To be wanton] To play the lecher with one's wife, Plaut. To neigh after girls, Prudent. To delight, Cic.

units.la: Lascivus] Salax, Catul. Libidinosus. Mulierosus vir. Admissarius, Cic. Inexstinctæ libidinis homo, Ovid. Projectissimus ad libidinem, Tac. Pronus in Venerem, Ovid. Venereus, vel, Venerius. Tenax equus. Hircosus senex, Plaut. Petulcus, Lucr. Procax, Cic. Procacior in fœminas, Col. Passere verno salacior. Satyrion bibit, Petron. Mulierarius, Capit. Delphino lascivior, Er.
units.tr: Lascivious] Lustful, Catul. Lecherous. A man given to women. A stallion, Cic. A man of unquenched lust, Ovid. Most abandoned to lust, Tac. Inclined to love, Ovid. Lustful, or of Venus. A tenacious horse. A goatish old man, Plaut. Wanton, Lucr. Forward, Cic. Too forward towards women, Col. More lustful than a sparrow in spring. He drinks satyrion, Petron. Fond of women, Capit. More playful than a dolphin, Erasm.

units.la: Lassari ] Lassescere, Plin. Relanguescere, Ovid. Elanguescere, Remittere ardorem pugnæ, Liv. Remittere aliquid de voluntate. Oblanguerunt tui desiderio literæ nostræ. Exolevit ætas tua, Cic. Elassescere, Plin.
units.tr: To grow weary] To grow faint, Plin. To grow faint again, Ovid. To grow faint, to lose heat. To lessen the ardour of battle, Liv. To relax something of one's will. Your letters have grown faint through longing for you. Your youth has faded away, Cic. To grow weary, Plin.

units.la: Lassus] Cursu exhaustus equus, Lucan. Vid. Fatigatus.
units.tr: Weary] A horse exhausted by running, Lucan. See Tired.

units.la: Late] Latius, latissime patet. Perlate. Fuse. Diffuse. Verbose dicere, Cic. Vaste, vastius tumet, Cels. Laxe, Varr. Laxissime pererrare. Spatiose fruticat, Pli. Effuse vastare regnum, Liv.
units.tr: Widely] More widely, most widely spreading. Extensively. Spread out. Diffusely. To speak wordily, Cic. It swells vastly, more vastly, Celsus. Loosely, Varr. To wander most widely. It spreads out luxuriantly, Plin. To lay waste a kingdom far and wide, Liv.

units.la: Latebra] Latibulum. Opertum, Cic. Abditum, Plin. Occultum. Desidiabulum, Plaut. Secretum dulce, Plin. Iun. Abstrusum, Amm. Adytum cordis, Lucr. Secretarium terræ, Apul.
units.tr: Hiding-place] A hiding place. Covered, Cic. Hidden, Plin. Concealed. A hiding-hole, Plaut. A sweet secret, Plin., Iun. Concealed, Amm. The inner sanctum of the heart, Lucr. The secret chamber of the earth, Apul.

units.la: Latebrose, vid. Abdite.
units.tr: Secretly, see Obscurely.

units.la: Latenter, vid. Occulte.
units.tr: Hiddenly, see Covertly.

units.la: Later] Later, m. Cic. Later aureum, Varr. Laterculus coctilis, Plin.
units.tr: Brick] A brick, masc. Cic. A golden brick, Varr. A baked small brick, Plin.

units.la: Latere] Latere in occulto. Latitare. Oblitescere. Tegere se latibulis. Occultare se. Occultare se latebris. Delitescere, Cic. Latibulare, sublatere, Var. Latibulari, Non. Acc. Copiam sui non facere, Vlp. Delitere, exPli. Latebrose se occultare, Plaut.
units.tr: To lie hidden] To lie hidden in secret. To lurk. To slip out of mind. To cover oneself with hiding-places. To hide oneself. To hide oneself in lurking-places. To lie concealed, Cic. To lurk, to lie hidden, Varr. To hide, Non., Acc. Not to make oneself available, Ulp. To lie hidden, ex Pli. To conceal oneself in a hiding-place, Plaut.

units.la: Lateritius] Domus lateritio structa, coctilis murus, Ovid.
units.tr: Of brick] A house built of brick, a wall of baked brick, Ovid.

units.la: Laterna] Laterna cornea, Mart. Punica, Plaut. Cornu. Qui Vulcanum in cornu conclusum geris, Id.
units.tr: Lantern] A horn lantern, Mart. A Punic lantern, Plaut. A horn. You who carry Vulcan shut up in a horn, Id.

units.la: Latescere, vid. Invalescere.
units.tr: To grow strong, see To grow strong.

units.la: Latina lingua] Latinitas. Sermo Latinus. Sermonis Latini integritas, Cic. Sermo Latialis, Plin. Latinum, Vertere in Latinum, Quint.
units.tr: Latin language] Latin. The Latin tongue. The purity of the Latin tongue, Cic. The Latial speech, Plin. Latin. To translate into Latin, Quint.

units.la: Latinitas simplex] Vernacula Latinitas.
units.tr: Plain Latin] Native Latin.

units.la: Latinus] Latiniensis, Cic. Latialis, Plin.
units.tr: Latin] Of Latium, Cic. Latial, Plin.

units.la: Latitudo] Laxitas viarum. Vastitas terræ, Col. Superficies areæ. Capacitas, Cic. Amplitudo stadiorum sexaginta, Plin.
units.tr: Breadth] The width of roads. The vastness of the land, Col. The surface of a threshing-floor. Capacity, Cic. The breadth of sixty stadia, Plin.

units.la: Latium] Italia, Cic. Hesperia. Ausonia. Oenotria, Virg.
units.tr: Latium] Italy, Cic. Hesperia. Ausonia. Oenotria, Virg.

units.la: Latrare] Personare latratu aliquem locum,Virg. Implere ternis latratibus auras, Ovid.
units.tr: To bark] To resound with barking at a place, Virg. To fill the air with threefold barking, Ovid.

units.la: Latratus ] Gannitus. Gannitibus improbis lacessere aliquem, Mart.
units.tr: Barking] Yelping. To assail someone with shameless yelping, Mart.

units.la: Latro] Latrunculus. Grassator. Spartacus, Cic. Aggressor, Vlp. Praedonulus, vel, Praedonculus, Scal. Qui in caede atque ex caede vivunt, Cic. Hodoedocus, Fest. Insidiator viae, Cic.
units.tr: Robber] A little robber. A highwayman. Spartacus, Cic. An assailant, Ulp. A little pirate, or a little pirate, Scal. Those who live by slaughter and from slaughter, Cic. A road-thief, Fest. An ambusher on the road, Cic.

units.la: Latrocinium] Grassatura, Suet. Piratica, Cic. Latrocinatio, Plin. Aggressura, Vlp. Direptus, us, Spart. Grassatio, Beroald.
units.tr: Robbery] Highway robbery, Suet. Piracy, Cic. Brigandage, Plin. An assault, Ulp. Plunder, Spart. Highway robbery, Beroald.

units.la: Latus, ti,] Laxa domus, Plin. Amplus locus, ad Her. Vastus orbis. Sinuosa vestis, Ovid. Spatiosus, Col. Patulus campus,Claud. Longe lateque diffusus. Late patet. Longe & late pervagata anteponuntur angustis. Diffusus. Late se pandunt illa bona. Fusus. Late fusus, Cic. Praelargus pulmo, Perf. Longe pertinet, Caes. Vegrandis. Grallatorius gradus,Plin. Latissime continuatus, Cic.
units.tr: Wide] A roomy house, Plin. A spacious place, ad Her. A vast circle. A flowing garment, Ovid. Spacious, Col. A wide plain, Claud. Spread far and wide. Spreads out far and wide. Things that have spread far and wide are preferred to narrow ones. Diffused. Those good things spread out widely. Spread out. Spread widely, Cic. A very large lung, Pers. It extends far, Caes. Very large. A stilt-walker's stride, Plin. Most widely continued, Cic.

units.la: Latus, eris] Lateramina vasis, Lucr.
units.tr: Broad] The broad sides of a vessel, Lucr.

units.la: Lavacrum, vid. Labrum.
units.tr: Bath, see Basin.

units.la: Lavare] Abluere se, Virg. Perluere manus unda, Ovid. Dare aquam manibus. Ferre aquam pedibus,Plaut. Piscina uti, Lampr. Perfundere se aqua, ex Col.
units.tr: To wash] To wash oneself, Virg. To wash the hands in water, Ovid. To give water to the hands. To bring water for the feet, Plaut. To use a pool, Lampr. To pour water over oneself, from Col.

units.la: Lavatio] Ablutio corporis, Macrob. Piscina, Plin. Cic. Lotio. Lotura, Plin.
units.tr: Washing] Washing of the body, Macrob. A pool, Plin., Cic. Lotion. A bath, Plin.

units.la: Laudabilis] Laude dignus, Hor. Celebrandus. Gloriosus, Cic. Inclytus, Plaut. Praedicabilis. Laudandus. Praedicandus. Gloriabile ac praedicandum est aliquid. Gloriosum aliquid. Gloriandus. Prae se ferendus. Probabilis Orator, Cic. Omne tulit punctum, Hor.
units.tr: Praiseworthy] Worthy of praise, Hor. To be celebrated. Glorious, Cic. Renowned, Plaut. To be proclaimed. To be praised. To be proclaimed. Something is to be gloried in and proclaimed. Something glorious. To be gloried in. To be displayed before others. A probable orator, Cic. He won every vote, Hor.

units.la: Laudare aliquem] Laude afficere, celebrare, ornare aliquem. Laudi aliquid dare,tribuere, concedere. Efferre aliquem verbis, sermonibus, laudibus, Cic. Ponere aliquid in laude alicujus. Habere in laudibus aliquid, Plin. Habere alicui laudem. Cumulare aliquem laudibus. Tac. Laudare laudibus, Plaut. Vid. Dilaudare.
units.tr: To praise someone] To honour, celebrate, adorn someone with praise. To give, assign, or grant praise. To extol someone with words, speeches, praises, Cic. To set something in someone's praise. To hold something in esteem, Plin. To hold someone in praise. To heap praises upon someone, Tac. To praise with praises, Plaut. See To extol.

units.la: Laudatio] Præconium. Prædicatio de laude alicujus. Gloriatio. Celebratio, Cic. Elogium, Turn. Encomium, Cel. Rhod.
units.tr: Praise] Proclamation. Declaration in someone's praise. Boasting. Celebration, Cic. Eulogy, Turn. Encomium, Cel. Rhod.

units.la: Laudator] Approbator. Comprobator, probator rationis, Cic. Adstipulator vanæ opinionis, Val. M. Acceptor, Plaut. Attestator, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Praiser] An approver. A commender. A judge of reason, Cic. A supporter of vain opinion, Val. Max. An accepter, Plaut. A witness, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Laudet nemo seipsum] Ne præcones quidem ipsi se prædicant, Ex. Cic. contra jactat.
units.tr: Let no one praise himself] Not even the heralds proclaim themselves, from Cic., against boasting.

units.la: Laudes tuas non agnosco] Magnus sum, si ita est ut res.
units.tr: I do not recognise your praises] I am great, if things are as they are.

units.la: Laurea] Laureola. Cic. Lorea, Cat.
units.tr: Laurel] A little laurel, Cic. A laurel, Cat.

units.la: Laureatus] Laurifer, Lucan. Lauriger, Mart.
units.tr: Laureled] Laurel-bearing, Lucan. Laurel-bearing, Mart.

units.la: Laureus] Laurinus, Plin. Lauricomus mons, Lucr. Loreus, prisc. Cat.
units.tr: Of laurel] Of laurel, Plin. A laurel-crowned mountain, Lucr. Of laurel, Prisc., Cat.

units.la: Laurus] Janitrix Cæsarum & Pontificum, Plin.
units.tr: Laurel] The doorkeeper of the Caesars and of the Pontiffs, Plin.

units.la: Laus] Gloria, Gloriola, Cic. Adorea, Fest.
units.tr: Praise] Glory, a little glory, Cic. Honour for valour, Fest.

units.la: Lautè, vid. Effusè.
units.tr: Elegantly, see Lavishly.

units.la: Lautus, vid. Purus. Copiosus.
units.tr: Refined, see Pure. Abundant.

units.la: Laxamentum, vid. Levamen.
units.tr: Relief, see Alleviation.

units.la: Laxare aliquid] Permittere equo habenas, Tibull. Remittere frena equo, Ovid. Effundere habenas, Virg. Laxare pedem ab adstricto nodo, Liv. Laxare aliquid ex eo, quo adstricti sumus, Cic.
units.tr: To loosen something] To give the horse its reins, Tibull. To slacken the reins for a horse, Ovid. To pour out the reins, Virg. To loosen the foot from a tight knot, Liv. To loosen something from that by which we are bound, Cic.

units.la: Laxare arcum] Denodare arcum, Apul. Remittere, ex Hor. Retendere, Ovid.
units.tr: To slacken a bow: to unstring it (Apul.); to let it go (ex Hor.); to draw it taut again (Ovid).

units.la: Laxus] Laxata membrana, Plin. Vid. Latus.
units.tr: Loose: a loosened membrane (Plin.). See Broad.

units.la: Leæna] Lea, Lucr.
units.tr: Lioness: (Lucr.).

units.la: Lebes] Cucuma, Mart. Cocula, pl. Fest. Cortina, Plaut. Ahenum, Virg. Tepidarium. Caldarium, Vitr. Miliarium, vel milliarium, Vlp. Marcell. Don.
units.tr: Cauldron: a kettle (Mart.); a cooking pot (pl. Fest.); a bronze pot (Plaut.); a bronze vessel (Virg.); a hot-room, a heated chamber (Vitr.); a milestone (Vlp. Marcell. Don.).

units.la: Lectio] Recitatio literarum. Evolutio poëtarum frequens, Cic.
units.tr: Reading: a reading aloud of letters. Frequent perusal of poets (Cic.).

units.la: Lectio non intellecta inutilis] Qui non intelligit, frustra legit. Legere, & non intelligere, est negligere.
units.tr: Reading that is not understood is useless: one who does not understand reads in vain. To read without understanding is to neglect.

units.la: Lector] Anagnostes. Prælector. Recitator, Cic.
units.tr: Reader: a reader [ἀναγνώστης]. A lecturer. A reciter (Cic.).

units.la: Lectus] Lectulus. Cubile, Cic. Lectica, Plin. Torus, Virg. Vid. Stratum.
units.tr: Couch: a little bed. A bed (Cic.). A litter (Plin.). A bed (Virg.). See Bedding.

units.la: Legalis, vid. Iuridic.
units.tr: Legal: see Juridical.

units.la: Legatio] Jus legationis. Mandatum, Cic, Nuncium, Varr.
units.tr: Embassy: the right of embassy. A commission (Cic.). A message (Varr.).

units.la: Legationem expedire] Legatos, mandata mittere. Legationem alicui dare. Oratores ad aliquem mittere, Cic. Legationem ad aliquem mittere, Quint. Legare aliquem ad aliquem, Caes.
units.tr: To discharge an embassy: to send envoys and instructions. To give someone an embassy. To send ambassadors to someone (Cic.). To send an embassy to someone (Quint.). To send someone as envoy to someone (Caes.).

units.la: Legationem obire] Legationem habere, accipere. Legatus ad aliquem venio de, Venire cum mandatis, Cic. Esse in legatione. Legationem gerere, Quint. Orator ad aliquem venio, Ter. Agere legationem, Ascon.
units.tr: To carry out an embassy: to hold and receive an embassy. To come to someone as envoy, coming with instructions (Cic.). To be on an embassy. To conduct an embassy (Quint.). To come to someone as an ambassador (Ter.). To act as envoy (Ascon.).

units.la: Legator] Testans. Testator. Testatrix, Vlp.
units.tr: Bequeather: a testator. A testatrix (Vlp.).

units.la: Legatus] Legatus de maximis rebus. Nuncius. Legatio, properson. Cic. Orator, Varr.
units.tr: Envoy: an envoy on weighty matters. A messenger. An embassy (properson. Cic.). An orator (Varr.).

units.la: Legati inviolabiles] Nuncio nihil imputandum.
units.tr: Envoys are inviolable: nothing is to be charged against the messenger.

units.la: Legere] Sequi scripta oculis, Quint. Lectitare, Cic. Lectare, Hor.
units.tr: To read: to follow writings with the eyes (Quint.). To read repeatedly (Cic.). To read often (Hor.).

units.la: Legibilis] Legi facilis, Gell.
units.tr: Legible: easy to read (Gell.).

units.la: Legio] Cohors Praetoria, Tac. Commanipulatio, Spart. Phalanx, Caes. Curt. Caterva, Cic. Vexillatio, Lavin.
units.tr: Legion: a praetorian cohort (Tac.). A combined maniple (Spart.). A phalanx (Caes., Curt.). A troop (Cic.). A detachment of soldiers (Lavin.).

units.la: Legislator] Lator legis. Legum scriptor, Cic. Legum lator, Liv. Legum conditor, Plaut. Legifer, Virg.
units.tr: Lawgiver: a proposer of law. A writer of laws (Cic.). A proposer of laws (Liv.). A founder of laws (Plaut.). Law-bringing (Virg.).

units.la: Legitime, vid. Merito.
units.tr: Lawfully: see Deservedly.

units.la: Legitimus] Legitimum jus. Justa causa, excusatio. Aequa postulatio: Aequa postulare, Cic. Causaria omissio. Competens judex, Vlp. Verus, Virg. Sontica causa, Nev. Fest.
units.tr: Lawful: lawful right. A just cause, a valid excuse. A fair demand: to make a fair demand (Cic.). An omission in a suit. A competent judge (Vlp.). True (Virg.). A criminal case (Nev. Fest.).

units.la: Legumen] Legarium, Varr. Legumenta, Gell. Cerealia femina, Gorra.
units.tr: Pulse: a leguminous plant. Pulses (Gell.). A cereal-like grain (Gorra).

units.la: Lemures] Lemures nocturni, Hor. Lemurales larvae, Fest. Lemures nigri, Perf. Spectra. Larvae, Plaut. Umbrae, Suet. Occursaculum noctium. Terriculamenta sepulchrorum. Formidamina bustorum. Lamia. Empusa, Apul. Monstra, Plaut. Lymphatio nocturna, Plin. Maniae, Scal.
units.tr: Lemures: nocturnal spirits (Hor.). Lemurian ghosts (Fest.). Black lemures (Pers.). Phantoms. Spectres (Plaut.). Shades (Suet.). Night apparitions. Terrors of the graves. Frights of the tombs. A lamia. An empusa (Apul.). Monsters (Plaut.). Nocturnal madness (Plin.). Frenzies (Scal.).

units.la: Lenimen] Lenimentum. Mitigatorium, Plin. Delinimentum, Liv.
units.tr: Solace: a remedy. A soothing remedy (Plin.). An appeasement (Liv.).

units.la: Lenire] Delinire. Delinire animum blanditiis. Severitatem acerbam condimentis humanitatis mitigare, Cic. Oblenire, Sen. Addere lenimen, Ovid. Mollire animos distis, Virg. Mulcere, Plin.
units.tr: To soothe: to coax, to charm. To coax the mind with flattery. To soften harsh severity with the seasoning of kindness (Cic.). To soothe (Sen.). To add a solace (Ovid). To soothe minds with words (Virg.). To caress (Plin.).

units.la: Lenis] Mites mores, Col. Mollis animus. Facilis & lenis, nis, Cic. Indulgens. Perindulgens. Agnâ mollior, Mart. Mitione mitior, Er. Mitificus, Apul.
units.tr: Gentle: gentle manners (Col.). A soft spirit. Easy and gentle (Cic.). Indulgent. Very indulgent. Softer than a lamb (Mart.). Milder than mildness itself (Er.). Soothing (Apul.).

units.la: Lenitas, vid. Clementia.
units.tr: see Clemency.

units.la: Leniter, vid. Blandè.
units.tr: see Gently.

units.la: Leno] Lenunculus, lenullus, Plaut. Conciliator, Ballio, Vopisc. Lupanarius, Lampr.
units.tr: Pimp: a little pimp (Plaut.). A go-between, Ballio (Vopisc.). A brothel-keeper (Lampr.).

units.la: Lenocinium, vid. Illecebra, Deliniment.
units.tr: see Allurement, Enticement.

units.la: Lens, tis] Lenticula, Plin.
units.tr: Lentil: a little lentil (Plin.).

units.la: Lentè] Suspenso gradu, Ter. Passu tardo, anili, inerti, Ovid. Pedatim, Plin. Desìde passu ire, Stat. Celerius elephanti pariunt. Furis passu progredi. Pedem struere. Talipedare, Lucr.
units.tr: Slowly: with a measured step (Ter.). With a slow, old woman's, listless step (Ovid). Step by step (Plin.). To walk with a languid step (Stat.). Elephants bear young more quickly. To walk with a thief's step. To set one's foot down. To shuffle along (Lucr.).

units.la: Lentus, vid. Flexibilis.
units.tr: see Flexible.

units.la: Lepidè, vid. Facetè.
units.tr: see Wittily.

units.la: Lepos, vid. Suavitas.
units.tr: see Charm.

units.la: Lepus] Lepusculus, Cic. Inauspicati ominis animal, Pier. Valer.
units.tr: Hare: a little hare (Cic.). An animal of ill omen (Pier. Valer.).

units.la: Lessus, vid. Lamentatio.
units.tr: see Lamentation.

units.la: Letalis] Internecinum bellum, Liv. Fatale, Cic. Funesta dies. Mortifer, Id. Feralis, Lucan. Pernicialis, Liv. Perniciabilis rigor nivis, Curt. Insuperabilis novissima valetudo, Plin. Peremptorium venenum, Apul. Praesentaneum, Gell. Capitalis morbus, Id. In mortem vulnus, Tac. Letifer ensis, Virg. Mortalis circumventio Cypri. Letabilis morbus, Amm.
units.tr: Deadly: a war of extermination (Liv.). Fatal (Cic.). A fatal day. Deadly (Cic.). Deadly, funereal (Lucan.). Destructive (Liv.). The destructive cold of snow (Curt.). An incurable final illness (Plin.). A deadly poison (Apul.). Immediately fatal (Gell.). A capital disease (Gell.). A wound to death (Tac.). A death-bearing sword (Virg.). A deadly ambush of Cyprus. A mortal disease (Amm.).

units.la: Letaliter] Mortificè vulneratus, Vlp.
units.tr: Mortally: mortally wounded (Vlp.).

units.la: Lethargicus] Veternosus, Fest. Lethargo laborat.
units.tr: Lethargic: drowsy (Fest.). Suffers from lethargy.

units.la: Lethargus] Dormiendi necessitas inexpugnabilis, Celf. Morbus lethargicus, Plin. Lethargia, Quint. Veternus, Plin. Plaut. Perpetuus sopor, Hor. Cataphoricus somnus, Paul. Ægin.
units.tr: Lethargy: an irresistible need to sleep (Cels.). A lethargic disease (Plin.). Lethargy (Quint.). Drowsiness (Plin., Plaut.). Perpetual sleep (Hor.). Cataphoric sleep (Paul. Aegin.).

units.la: Levamen] Levamentum doloris, Plin. Iun. Allevamentum in adversis. Allevatio doloris, Tac. Levatio doloris. Relaxatio. Laxamentum. Remissio senescentis morbi, Cic. Mollimentum calamitatum, Sen. Allenimentum tumultûs, Amm.
units.tr: Relief: relief from pain (Plin. Iun.). Support in adversity. Alleviation of pain (Tac.). Relief of pain. Relaxation. Easing. Remission of an ageing illness (Cic.). Easing of calamities (Sen.). Quieting of a tumult (Amm.).

units.la: Levare aliquem onere, &c.] Levare alicujus calamitatem. Levamento esse. Relevare curam. Mitigare laborem. Levationi mihi est aliquid. Allevare onus. Remittere de, Cic. Levare alicui dolorem, Virg. Levamentum praestare. Collevat aliqua herba renes, Plin. Laxare aliquid ex studio, Sen. Exonerare animum solicitudine, Curt.
units.tr: To relieve someone of a burden, etc.: to relieve someone's calamity. To be a relief. To relieve care. To ease toil. It is a relief to me. To lighten a burden. To grant some concession from (Cic.). To relieve someone of pain (Virg.). To provide relief. Some herb relieves the kidneys (Plin.). To relax something from one's study (Sen.). To unburden the mind of anxiety (Curt.).

units.la: Levidensis pannus &c.] Rarum textum, Quint. Ralla tunica (a rarus) Non. Rarum cribrum, Ovid. Rara retia, Virg.
units.tr: Thinly woven cloth: a loose weave (Quint.). A thin tunic (Non.). A sieve with wide mesh (Ovid). Loose nets (Virg.).

units.la: Levis] Perleve momentum. Leviculus, levidense munus, Cic. Leviusculus, Plin. Levior tipula, subere, Er.
units.tr: Light: a very slight consideration. A rather small gift (Cic.). Rather light (Plin.). Lighter than a gnat, lighter than cork (Er.).

units.la: Leviter] Duobus digitis. Primoribus, supremis labris, Summis digitis. Strictim. Levi brachio & molli. Per transfennam aspicere, Cic. Suspensa manu. Superficie tenus.
units.tr: Lightly: with two fingers. With the tips, with the top lips, with the fingertips. Grazing. With a light and gentle arm. To look sideways (Cic.). With the hand held aloft. Superficially.

units.la: Lex] Lex regula juris & injuriae. Decretum, Scitum, Institutum, juris publici. Regula, norma, praescriptio rationis, naturae. Sanctiones foederum, Cic. Rogatio. Promulgatur ab eo rogatio de mea pernicie, Id.
units.tr: Law: law is the rule of right and wrong. A decree, an enactment, an institution of public law. A rule, a norm, a prescription of reason and nature. The sanctions of covenants (Cic.). A bill. A bill is proposed by him concerning my ruin (Cic.).

units.la: Lex Dei] Lex divina & coelestis, Cic. Decalogus. Decem verba, Isid. Lex divina per Mosen data. Vetus testamentum. N.T. Praecepta Deum, Virg.
units.tr: Law of God: divine and heavenly law (Cic.). The Decalogue. The Ten Words (Isid.). The divine law given through Moses. The Old Testament. N.T. The precepts of God (Virg.).

units.la: Legi communi pare] Publica via ingredi.
units.tr: To obey the common law: to walk the public road.

units.la: Ad legem vivere] Extra circinum & regulam nescire quicquam.
units.tr: To live by the law: to know nothing beyond compass and rule.

units.la: Lexicon] Onomasticon. Nomenclator.
units.tr: Lexicon: Onomasticon. Nomenclator.

units.la: Libatio, vid. Sacrificium.
units.tr: see Sacrifice.

units.la: Libens, vid. Lubens.
units.tr: see Willing.

units.la: Libenter] Animo libentissimo facere aliquid. Animo gaudenti ac libenti. Libentissime. Perlibenter. Propensè. Non repugnanter. Non gravatè. Magnâ, summâ voluptate, Cic. Volenti animo agere, Sallust. Propenso animo, Liv. Lubens, Ter. Studiosè ludere pilâ, Cic. Ex animo facere, Sallust. Aventer suscptus, Amm. Lubenter, Plaut. Enixè, Perofficiosè, Perstudiosè, Cic. Libenter, vide plus in Lubenter.
units.tr: Willingly: to do something with a most willing mind. With a joyful and willing spirit. Most willingly. Very willingly. Gladly. Not reluctantly. Not unwillingly. With great pleasure and highest delight (Cic.). To act with a willing mind (Sallust). With a ready spirit (Liv.). Gladly (Ter.). To play ball eagerly (Cic.). To do from the heart (Sallust). Eagerly undertaken (Amm.). Gladly (Plaut.). Zealously, most dutifully, most eagerly (Cic.). For more, see Gladly.

units.la: Liber, bri] Pellicula arboris interior. Membrana tenuis arborum inter corticem & lignum, Isid. Tunica, Plin. Torus, Col.
units.tr: Book: the inner bark of a tree. The thin membrane of trees between bark and wood (Isid.). A tunic (Plin.). A bulge, a swelling (Col.).

units.la: Libri] Codices. Muti Magistri, Gell. Muti Praeceptores.
units.tr: Books: codices. Dumb masters (Gell.). Dumb teachers.

units.la: Libri raptim scripti] Rhapsodi, (quales Homerici.
units.tr: Books written hastily: rhapsodies (such as the Homeric ones).

units.la: Libri magni] Elephantini libri.
units.tr: Large books: elephantine books.

units.la: Libri sapientes] Libros thesauros esse oportet.
units.tr: Wise books: books ought to be treasuries.

units.la: Liber, beri] Vacuus, laxatus curis, Cic. Solutus lege. Exlex. Libero solutoque animo est, Caes. Suae spontis. Liberum caput, Cels. Meus sum, Bud. Sese utens, Plaut. Arbitrio suo vivens. Sui juris homo. Mancipatus nemini. Integrae libertatis & solidae; solutus & sui juris est sapiens, Sen. Ad arbitrium suum vivens. Arbitrio suo omnia agens, faciens. Qui in potestate sua est. Jus habet sui, Cic.
units.tr: Free: empty, released from cares (Cic.). Released from law. Lawless. Free in mind and spirit (Caes.). Of one's own will. A free head (Cels.). I am my own (Bud.). Living by one's own choice (Plaut.). Living at one's own discretion. A man under his own right. Belonging to no one. Whole in freedom and solid; the wise man is released and his own master (Sen.). Living at one's own pleasure. Doing everything at one's own will. Being in one's own power. Having a right over oneself (Cic.).

units.la: Liberalis] Largus. Beneficus; beneficentissimus. Munificus in dando. Benignus, Cic. Munifex, Lucil. Praelargus, Perf. Prona manus.
units.tr: Generous: open-handed. Beneficent; most beneficent. Munificent in giving. Kind (Cic.). Munificent (Lucil.). Very generous (Pers.). An open hand.

units.la: Liberalis nimis] Largitio non habet fundum. Magis promus, quam condus.
units.tr: Too generous: lavish giving has no bottom. More a dispenser than a keeper.

units.la: Liberalem esse] Aperit rem familiarem alicujus benignitas. Referare rem familiarem ita, ut omnibus pateat, Cic.
units.tr: To be generous: the kindness of someone opens up his estate. To lay open one's estate so that it lies open to all (Cic.).

units.la: Liberalitas] Animus liberalis. Magnificentia libertatis. Beneficentia. Liberalis, benefica voluntas. Effusio Caesaris in aliquem. Benignitas ne sit major, quam facultas, Cic. Largitas, Ter. Munificentia, Tac.
units.tr: Generosity: a generous spirit. The magnificence of freedom. Beneficence. A generous, beneficent will. The outpouring of Caesar's favour towards someone. Kindness that is not greater than one's means (Cic.). Largess (Ter.). Munificence (Tac.).

units.la: Liberalitas decet divites] Dives opum, sit largus opum.
units.tr: Generosity becomes the rich: let the rich, being rich in means, be open-handed.

units.la: Liberaliter] Effuse. Large. Laute. Opiparè. Ampliter. Amplissimè. Plena manu. Liberalissimè ac accumulatissimè polliceri, Cic. Largiter, Hor. Munificè, Liv. Genialiter, Ovid. Divite manu. Locupletissimè, Spart. Utraque manu, Sen. Benignissimè. Affatim, Cic.
units.tr: Generously: lavishly. Largely. Sumptuously. Splendidly. Abundantly. Most abundantly. With full hand. To promise most generously and most copiously (Cic.). Largely (Hor.). Munificently (Liv.). Genially (Ovid). With a rich hand. Most abundantly (Spart.). With both hands (Sen.). Most kindly. Enough (Cic.).

units.la: Liberare] Vindicare aliquem in libertatem, Cic. Asserere aliquem, Sen. Eximere in libertatem, Liv. Expedire è servitute filium, Plaut. Eximere vinculis, Id. Eximere è vinculis, ex obsidione. Vindicare aliquem à molestiâ. Exsolvere aliquem occupationibus, Cic. Absolvere aliquem suspicione. Exonerare metu aliquem, Liv. Excludere aliquem servitute, Amm. Servitutem excludere, Lucil. Non.
units.tr: To free: to set someone free (Cic.). To claim someone for freedom (Sen.). To bring someone into freedom (Liv.). To rescue a son from slavery (Plaut.). To take out of chains (Plaut.). To take out of chains, out of a siege. To free someone from annoyance. To release someone from business (Cic.). To clear someone of suspicion. To relieve someone of fear (Liv.). To shut someone out of servitude (Amm.). To shut out servitude (Lucil.).

units.la: Liberatio] Vindicatio, Cic. Absolutio, Suet. Assertio à servitute in libertatem, Priscian. Vindiciae, Liv.
units.tr: Liberation: vindication (Cic.). Acquittal (Suet.). An assertion of freedom from servitude (Priscian). Claims to freedom (Liv.).

units.la: Liberator] Assertor, Liv. Vindex alienae libertatis, Don. Qui ex obsidione, &c. eximit. Soter, Cic. Servator, Sen. Sospitator, Arnob. Qui salutem dedit, ex Cicer. Salvator.
units.tr: Liberator: a champion (Liv.). A defender of another's freedom (Don.). One who takes someone out of a siege, etc. A saviour [σωτήρ] (Cic.). A preserver (Sen.). A deliverer (Arnob.). One who has given safety (ex Cic.). A saviour.

units.la: Libere] Libero corde, linguâ uti, Plin. Verba edere libera, Tibull. Solutè ac liberè movetur animus. Ingenuè fateri, Cic. Sponte suâ vivere, Lucr.
units.tr: Freely: to use the heart and tongue freely (Plin.). To utter free words (Tibull.). The mind moves freely and unrestrained. To confess openly (Cic.). To live of one's own accord (Lucr.).

units.la: Liberi] Soboles, Plin. Pignora, Tac. Carissimi affectus, Apul. Prognati, Plaut.
units.tr: Children: offspring, Plin.; pledges, Tac.; dearest affections, Apul.; begotten ones, Plaut.

units.la: Liberi parentum solicitudo] Liberi labores, Liberi amarissima voluptas, Tertull.
units.tr: The anxiety of parents for their children: the toils of children; the most bitter pleasure of children, Tertull.

units.la: Libertas] Libertas licita, publica, propria. Voluntas libera. Facultas. Licentia. Suum jus, Cic. Pileus. Arbitrium liberum, Liv. Potestas quidlibet audendi, Hor. Liberiùs vivendi potestas, Ter. Ingenuitas poëtarum, Cic. Res inaestimabilis. Delicatissimum mortalium bonum.
units.tr: Liberty: lawful, public and private liberty; free will; facility; licence; one's own right, Cic.; the freedman's cap; free judgement, Liv.; the power to dare anything, Hor.; the power of living more freely, Ter.; the freedom of poets, Cic.; an inestimable thing; the most precious good of mortals.

units.la: Libertate donare] Ad pileum vocare servos, Sen. Caput liberum facere, Plaut. Vindicias dare. Rude donare. Rudem dare. Vid. Vindicare.
units.tr: To grant liberty: to call slaves to the cap of liberty, Sen.; to make a head free, Plaut.; to give a vindicta (the rod of liberty); to give a wooden sword. See Vindicare.

units.la: Liberatus à muneris functione, vid. Officio dimittere.
units.tr: Released from the performance of a duty, see Dismiss from office.

units.la: Libertus] Liberta, Hor. Vindicta emissus manu, Tac. Manumissus, Vlp.
units.tr: Freedman: freedwoman, Hor.; sent forth by the rod, Tac.; manumitted, Ulp.

units.la: Liberum est mihi, vel alicui] Arbitrii mei est, Cat. Integrum est mihi. Integra est mihi potestas. In medio est sitrum. Optio soluta nobis est eligendi. Omnia sunt mihi solutissima. Habeo concessam licentiam. Patent haec omnibus ad visendum. Habeo in potestate, Cic. Habeo arbitrium, Pallad. Arbitrarium est. Copia est faciendi, Plaut. In manu mea est, Plaut. Vid. In potestate habere.
units.tr: It is free for me, or for someone: it is at my discretion, Cat.; it is open to me; the power is unimpaired for me; it lies in the middle; the choice is left free to us; all things are wholly loose for me; I have a licence granted; these things are open to everyone to see; I have it in my power, Cic.; I have discretion, Pallad.; it is optional; there is opportunity for doing it, Plaut.; it is in my hand, Plaut. See In potestate habere.

units.la: Libet. vid. Placet.
units.tr: Libet: see Placet.

units.la: Libidinari] Scortari. Habere foeminam. Rem habere cum aliqua, Ter. Amare, abs. Id. Volutari in stupris, in scortis, cum scortis. Consuescere alicui. Complexu Venereo jungi. Miscere corpus, Cic. Jungere Venerem, Tibul. Furtivis rebus operam dare. Lustrari, Plaut. Consuescere cum aliquo, vel, cum aliqua, Id. Ter. Meretricari, Col. Persequi turpia, Catul. Ludere, Id. Petron. Moechari, Catul. Congressu foeminarum pollui. Volutari cum aliqua, Plin. Habere fœminæ notitiam, Cæs. Tangere mulierem, Hor. Habere amicam, Plaut. Ductare mulierem, Ter.
units.tr: To indulge lust: to whore; to have a woman; to have intercourse with someone, Ter.; to love, absolutely, Id.; to wallow in debauchery, among whores, with whores; to consort with someone; to be joined in a venereal embrace; to mingle bodies, Cic.; to join in Venus, Tibul.; to take pains over furtive affairs; to consort, Plaut.; to consort with someone, or with a woman, Id. Ter.; to play the harlot, Col.; to pursue shameful things, Catul.; to play, Id. Petron.; to commit adultery, Catul.; to be defiled by intercourse with women; to wallow with a woman, Plin.; to have acquaintance with a woman, Caes.; to touch a woman, Hor.; to have a mistress, Plaut.; to take a woman as wife, Ter.

units.la: Libidinosè] Incestè, Lucr. Meretricië, Plaut. Amatoriè scripta epistola, Cic. Lenocinè, Lamp. Lascivè. Lasciviter, Sosip.
units.tr: Lustfully: incestuously, Lucr.; like a harlot, Plaut.; a letter written amorously, Cic.; pandering, Lamp.; wantonly. Lasciviously, Sosip.

units.la: Libidinosus] Animus libidini deditus impurus. Flagitiosus, Cic, Lastaurus, Suet. Nepos Veneris. Nepotulus Venereus. Salacior passere. Hirco libidinosior, Er. Hircum olet, Hor. Patrans oculus libidinosi, Marsil. Morsicantes oculi, Apul.
units.tr: Lustful: a mind impure and given over to lust; shameless, Cic.; a debauchee, Suet.; a grandson of Venus; a little venereal grandson; more salacious than a sparrow; more lustful than a he-goat, Er.; he smells of the goat, Hor.; an eye that is sinking into lust, Marsil.; biting eyes, Apul.

units.la: Libido] Petulantia mollis oculorum, Petron. V. Lascivia.
units.tr: Lust: soft wantonness of the eyes, Petron. See Lasciviousness.

units.la: Libra] Trutina, Philand.
units.tr: Scales: a balance, Philand.

units.la: Librare ] Ponderare granum. Pensitare æquâ lance aliquid, Plin. Delibrare, Gell. Trutinare, Hier.Sip. Suspendere lance, Perf. Staterâ, trutinâ examinare, Cic. Pendere aliquid, Id. Pensare, Liv. Expendere aliquem quot pondo sit, Plaut.
units.tr: To weigh: to weigh a grain; to weigh something on an even scale, Plin.; to weigh out, Gell.; to weigh in a balance, Hier. Sipont.; to hang something on the scale, Pers.; to examine with steelyard or balance, Cic.; to weigh something, Id.; to pay out, Liv.; to weigh someone, to find how many pounds he is, Plaut.

units.la: Libratio] Pensura, Varr. Exagium, Col. Examinatio, Vitr.
units.tr: Weighing: weighing, Varr.; a weight, Col.; examination, Vitr.

units.la: Libripens] Pensator, Plin. Pensitator, Gell.
units.tr: Balance-holder: a weigher, Plin.; a weigher, Gell.

units.la: Libum ] Mellitum, Suet. Dulciaria, vel, Dulcia, Lampr. Mellita bellaria, Varr. Mellitæplacentæ, Plaut. Strues, Fest. Fertum. Subucula, Id. Mellitum edulium, Apul.
units.tr: Cake: honeyed cake, Suet.; sweetmeats, or sweet things, Lampr.; honeyed dainties, Varr.; honey cakes, Plaut.; a heap, Fest.; a kind of pastry, Id.; a honeyed dish, Apul.

units.la: Libum piperatum ] Laterculus, Apul. Copta, Trallian. Secium, Fest. Sipont.
units.tr: Peppered cake: a small brick-shaped cake, Apul.; a cake of the kind called copta, Trallian.; a cake called secium, Fest. Sipont.

units.la: Licenter] Licentiùs dicere. Licentiosum est hoc, Quint. Nimiùm familiariter. Temerè, Plaut. Vid. Audacter.
units.tr: Licentiously: to speak more licentiously; this is licentious, Quint.; too familiarly; rashly, Plaut. See Boldly.

units.la: Licentia] Autonomia. Immoderata libertas. Mollis disciplina. Infinita, impudens, intoleranda, nimia licentia. Insolentia militum. Dissoluta consuetudo, Cic. Effusa licentia, Tac.
units.tr: Licence: self-rule; unrestrained liberty; lax discipline; unlimited, shameless, intolerable, excessive licence; the insolence of soldiers; loose custom, Cic.; unbridled licence, Tac.

units.la: Licentia nimia noxia]Cui, quod libet, licet, plerumque libet, quod non licet. Infelix cui omnia licent. Licentiâ reddimur deteriores. Peccat semper, qui semper, quod potest, facit.
units.tr: Excessive licence is harmful: he to whom whatever he pleases is permitted mostly pleases what is not permitted. Unhappy is he to whom all things are allowed. By licence we are made worse. He always sins who always does what he can.

units.la: Licentiosè conviciari] De plaustro loqui.
units.tr: To abuse licentiously: to speak of a cart.

units.la: Licentiosus] Solutior, Liv. Dissolutus. Effrenatus. Effusè petulans, Cic. Suopte ingenio vivens. Floralibus licentiosior, Er.
units.tr: Licentious: looser, Liv.; dissolute; unbridled; wantonly petulant, Cic.; living by his own nature; more licentious than at the Floralia, Er.

units.la: Licere, de pretio ] Pendere, Pendet drachmas decem. Implet libras sedecim modius grani, Plin. Pendo, Tantundem pendere par est, Lucr. Valet. Denarii denos aeris valent, Varr. Quot pondo sis, Plaut.
units.tr: To be worth (of price): to weigh, to cost. It weighs ten drachmas. A peck of grain makes sixteen pounds, Plin. I weigh; it is fitting to weigh as much, Lucr. To be worth. Ten asses are worth a denarius, Varr. As many pounds as you weigh, Plaut.

units.la: Liceri] Licitationem facere, Cic. Licitari, Curt. Licere. Venibunt omnia, quiqui licebunt, praesenti pecuniâ. Poscere, Plaut.
units.tr: To bid: to make a bid, Cic.; to bid, Curt.; to be sold. Everything will be sold to whoever bids, for ready money. To demand, Plaut.

units.la: Licet ] Licitum est. Jus est. Jus habeo. Per leges licet. Appellare & mendicare cuilibet liberum, integrum est, &c.
units.tr: It is permitted: it is lawful; it is right; I have the right; it is allowed by the laws. To beg and to appeal is free and lawful for anyone, and so on.

units.la: Lichen, vid. Mentagra.
units.tr: Lichen: see Mentagra.

units.la: Licitator] Nundinator. Illicitator. Inlicitator, Fest.
units.tr: Auctioneer: a dealer at market; a bidder; a bidder, Fest.

units.la: Lictor, vid. Apparitor.
units.tr: Lictor: see Attendant.

units.la: Ligare] Vincire. Constringere. Alligare. Illigare sententiam verbis. Copulando jungere, Cic. Obligare manipulos, Col. Vincula indere, Tac. Evincire manus, Ovid. Nodare vites, Col.
units.tr: To bind: to tie; to constrict; to fasten; to bind a sentence in words; to join by coupling, Cic.; to tie up bundles, Col.; to put on chains, Tac.; to bind the hands, Ovid.; to tie up vines, Col.

units.la: Ligatio] Ligatura in vitibus locum mutare debet, Pallad. Subligatio uvarum, Id. Pedatio, Col. Arundulatio, Varr. de vineis.
units.tr: Binding: the binding of vines should be moved to another place, Pallad.; the tying up of grapes, Id.; the propping of vines, Col.; the staking of vineyards with canes, Varr.

units.la: Lignatio] Lignatum ire, Plaut. Materiari, Caes. Lignatio-nis causa in silvas discedere, Id.
units.tr: Wood-gathering: to go out for wood, Plaut.; to cut timber, Caes.; to go away into the forests for the sake of wood-gathering, Id.

units.la: Ligneus ] Materiatus. Ligneolus lychnuchus, Cic. Materiarius, Plin. Ex intestino opere, factus, Varr. Philand.
units.tr: Wooden: made of timber; a small wooden lamp-stand, Cic.; timber-worked, Plin.; made from interior woodwork, Varr. Philand.

units.la: Lignosus ] Surculosa radix, Plin. Materia lignea, Cic. Surculaceus, Plin.
units.tr: Woody: a root full of shoots, Plin.; wooden material, Cic.; full of twigs, Plin.

units.la: Ligo] Marra, Col. Scapane, Rhod. Scaphium, Cel. Rhod. Ligurire, vid. Vorare.
units.tr: Hoe: a mattock, Col.; a spade, Rhod.; a small spade, Cel. Rhod. To lick up, see Devour.

units.la: Lima] Limula. Scobina, Varr. Serraculum, Vlp.
units.tr: File: a small file; a rasp, Varr.; a saw-file, Vlp.

units.la: Limare] Perterere limâ, Plaut. Delimare, Plin. Elimare, Ovid.
units.tr: To file: to wear down with a file, Plaut.; to file down, Plin.; to file off, Ovid.

units.la: Limatè, vid. Politè.
units.tr: Filed carefully: see Polished.

units.la: Limatus, vid. Politus. Elaboratus.
units.tr: see Polished. Elaborated.

units.la: Limbus, in veste] Instita, Hor. Fimbria, Plin.
units.tr: Border, on a garment: a hem, Hor.; a fringe, Plin.

units.la: Limbus, navicula] Monoxylum. Navis piscatoria, Linter, Liv. Cymba, Cic. Alveus, Virg. Alveus cavatus, Paterc. Remunculus, Salust. Oria, Plaut. Baris, idos, Propert. Lenis, Mart. Cujac.
units.tr: Boat: a dugout canoe; a fishing boat; a skiff, Liv.; a small boat, Cic.; a trough-boat, Virg.; a hollowed boat, Paterc.; an oar-boat, Salust.; a light craft, Plaut.; a canoe, Propert.; a light boat, Mart. Cujac.

units.la: Limes ] Terminus. Fines provinciarum. Regionibus aliquid quid circumscriptum, Cic. Meta, Virg. Confinium, Col. (Trifinium, quadrifinium, concursus tot finium.)
units.tr: Boundary: a limit; the borders of provinces; something marked off by regions, Cic.; a goal, Virg.; a frontier, Col. (three-boundary, four-boundary: the meeting of so many borders.)

units.la: Limitaneus] Terminalis lapis, Sipont. Finalis lapis, Frontin.
units.tr: Boundary stone: a terminal stone, Sipont.; a stone marking the border, Frontin.

units.la: Limitare] Terminare, constituere, pangere fines, terminos. Finibus circundare, Cic. Facere limites, Col. Determinare regiones, limites, confinia, Plaut. Partiri campum limite. Litem discernere arvis, Virg. Termino certo definire. ad Heren.
units.tr: To mark boundaries: to set out boundaries, to fix limits and marks; to surround with borders, Cic.; to make boundaries, Col.; to determine regions, borders and frontiers, Plaut.; to divide a field by a boundary line; to settle a dispute over fields, Virg.; to define by a fixed limit, ad Heren.

units.la: Limitatio, vid. Dimensio.
units.tr: see Measurement.

units.la: Limpidus, vid. Pellucidus.
units.tr: see Clear.

units.la: Limus] Crassamen in imo aquae, Col. Prima terra, Ovid. Prima tellus, Virg.
units.tr: Mud: the sediment at the bottom of water, Col.; the first earth, Ovid.; the first soil, Virg.

units.la: Limus, adj. vid. Curvus.
units.tr: see Curved.

units.la: Linctus] Ecligma, Plin.
units.tr: Linctus: a medicinal electuary, Plin.

units.la: Linea] Lineamentum, Cic. Lineola, Gell. Filum, Varr. Nota in marmore incisa, Hor.
units.tr: Line: an outline, Cic.; a small line, Gell.; a thread, Varr.; a mark cut in marble, Hor.

units.la: Lineare opus] Exigere ad lineam, ad regulam. Ad libellam collocare, Vitr. Ad regulam dirigere. Ad perpendiculum exigere aliquid. Ad normam rationis vitam dirigere, Cic. Ad amussim examinare. Revocare ad rectum robora, Sen.
units.tr: Work made by line: to square to the line, to the rule; to set by the level, Vitr.; to direct by the ruler; to test by the plumb-line; to guide one's life by the norm of reason, Cic.; to examine exactly; to bring crooked timbers back to straight, Sen.

units.la: Lingere, vid. Lambere.
units.tr: see Lick.

units.la: Lingua, pro sermone] Os. Ore duarum & viginti gentium loquebatur Mithridates, Plin. Sermo Graecus, Cic. Latinus, Quint.
units.tr: Tongue, for speech: the mouth. Mithridates spoke with the mouth of twenty-two nations, Plin.; Greek speech, Cic.; Latin speech, Quint.

units.la: Linere, vid. Illinere.
units.tr: see Smear.

units.la: Linquere, vid. Deserere.
units.tr: see Forsake.

units.la: Linter] Canalis, Virg. Alveus, Liv. Navia. Nauftibulum, Fest. Lacus salsurae, Col. Milliarium, Sen.
units.tr: Trough: a channel, Virg.; a hollow, Liv.; a small boat; a skiff, Fest.; a salt-pan, Col.; a milestone, Sen.

units.la: Linteum] Pannus linteus, Sipont. Tela, Cic. Textum, Ovid.
units.tr: Linen cloth: a piece of linen, Sipont.; weaving, Cic.; a woven fabric, Ovid.

units.la: Linteus] Linea vestis, Plin.
units.tr: Linen: a linen garment, Plin.

units.la: Lippire] Suffunduntur oculi ad alienam lippitudinem, Sen.
units.tr: To be bleary-eyed: the eyes are moistened at another's bleariness, Sen.

units.la: Lippitudo] Epiphora. Fluxio oculorum. Delacrymatio, Plaut. Acre malum semper stillantis ocelli, Iuv.
units.tr: Bleariness: a watering of the eyes; a flux of the eyes; a weeping, Plaut.; a sharp affliction of an always-running eye, Juv.

units.la: Liquefacere] Liquare. Colliquefacere, Cic. Liquidum facere. Dissolvit glaciem sol. Tabescere cogit radiis. Conferves facit fulmen aurum, Lucr. Resolvere aliquid, Id.
units.tr: To liquefy: to melt; to melt completely, Cic.; to make liquid. The sun dissolves ice and forces wax to melt with its rays; lightning makes gold melt, Lucr.; to dissolve something, Id.

units.la: Liquefactio] Liquatio, Flav. Vopisc.
units.tr: Liquefaction: a melting, Flav. Vopisc.

units.la: Liquescere] Eliquescere Varr. Colliquescere, Col. Intabescit cera, Ovid. Tabescit cera, Lucr. Liquefieri, Cic. Ovid. Hinc liquefactus.
units.tr: To melt: to melt away, Varr.; to melt completely, Col.; wax melts, Ovid.; wax wastes away, Lucr.; to become liquid, Cic. Ovid. Hence "liquefied."

units.la: Liquidè, liquidò, vid. Clarè. Perspicuè.
units.tr: see Clearly. Plainly.

units.la: Liquidus] Tenuis, aër, Cic. Rarus, Lucr. Sorbilis cibus, sorbile ovum, Col. Fluidus liquor, Virg. Fluvidus, Lucr. Diluta potio. Jurulentus cibus, Cels. Jureus, Plaut. Jussulentus, Apul. Subtilissimus succus, Plin.
units.tr: Liquid: thin, of air, Cic.; rare, Lucr.; food to be sipped; a sipped egg, Col.; flowing liquid, Virg.; flowing, Lucr.; a diluted drink; brothy food, Cels.; brothy, Plaut.; soupy, Apul.; the most subtle juice, Plin.

units.la: Liquor] Succus lactis. Unda preli (ex prelo fluens liquor.) Margaritas in tabem resolvere, Plin. Succus in corpore, Cic. Liquamen, Col. Liquidum, Subst. Hor.
units.tr: Liquor: the juice of milk; the flow from a press (liquid running from the press). To dissolve pearls into a paste, Plin.; juice in the body, Cic.; a fish sauce, Col.; liquid, as a noun, Hor.

units.la: Lira] Sulcus, aquarius, Col. Porca, Fest. Elix, Col. Ulp. Fossa, quâ aqua pluvia delabitur, Varr.
units.tr: Furrow: a watering furrow, Col.; a ridge, Fest.; a drain, Col. Ulp.; a ditch down which rainwater runs, Varr.

units.la: Liratim] Tabulatim inserere surculos, Pallad. Castellatim serendum allium, Plin.
units.tr: In furrows: shoots inserted in layers, Pallad.; garlic planted in clusters, Plin.

units.la: Lirare] Sulcum altius imprimere, Cic. Infindere sulcos telluri, Virg. Imporcare. Sulcare. In liras redigere jugerum proscissum, Col.
units.tr: To furrow: to press a furrow deeper, Cic.; to cut furrows into the earth, Virg.; to ridge; to groove; to reduce a ploughed acre into furrows, Col.

units.la: Lis] Litigium, Plaut. Vid. Rixa.
units.tr: Strife: a lawsuit, Plaut. See Quarrel.

units.la: Litare, Litatio, vid. Sacrificare.
units.tr: see Sacrifice.

units.la: Lites concire in alios] Lites creare, serere. Litigium contrahere inter aliquos, Plaut. Committere inter se aliquos, Suet. Serere certamina, discordias, Liv. Inferre certamen aliquibus, Id. Discordias facere, Plin.
units.tr: To stir up quarrels among others: to create quarrels, to sow them; to bring about a lawsuit between some people, Plaut.; to set some against one another, Suet.; to sow contests and discords, Liv.; to bring a contest upon some, Id.; to make discords, Plin.

units.la: Litigare] Litem habere, contendere cum aliquo. Digladiari. Tricari cum aliquo. Conterere aetatem in litibus, Cic. Contendere lite, Quint. Exercere discordias, Liv.
units.tr: Litigare] To have a suit, to contend with someone. To fight it out. To quibble with someone. To wear out one's life in lawsuits, Cic. To contend in a suit, Quint. To stir up quarrels, Liv.

units.la: Litigator, vid. Rixosus.
units.tr: Litigator, see Rixosus.

units.la: Litigiosus, vid. Rixosus.
units.tr: Litigiosus, see Rixosus.

units.la: Littoralis] Littoreus, Stat. Littorarius, Isid. Orarius, Plin. Iun. Riparius, Plin. Actaeus, Virg. Riparensis, Alciat.
units.tr: Littoralis] Of the shore, Stat. Of the shore, Isid. Of the coast, Plin. Iun. Of the riverbank, Plin. Of the strand, Virg. Of the riverbank, Alciat.

units.la: Littus] Acta, ae, Cic. Crepido maris, Cic. Col. Ora, Cels.
units.tr: Littus] Strand, Cic. The edge of the sea, Cic. Col. Shore, Cels.

units.la: Litura] Deletio, Lucil. Maculatio, Firm. Superinductio, Ulp.
units.tr: Litura] Erasing, Lucil. Staining, Firm. Overlaying, Ulp.

units.la: Lituus] Classicum, Virg. Recto cantare aere, Iuv. Non tuba directi non aeris cornua flexi, Ovid. Buccinum, Plin. Livere] Livescere, Lucr. Lividum fieri, Fest. Livorem ducere, Luv.
units.tr: Lituus] A trumpet call, Virg. To sound the bronze straight, Iuv. Neither the straight trumpet nor the curved bronze horn, Ovid. A horn, Plin. Livere] To grow livid, Lucr. To become bluish, Fest. To draw a bruise, Luv.

units.la: Lividus] Plumbeus. Sugillatus. Luridus, Plaut.
units.tr: Lividus] Leaden. Bruised. Sallow, Plaut.

units.la: Livor] Plumbeus color, Plin. Plumbago. Plumbum, Id. Livedo, Apul.
units.tr: Livor] A leaden colour, Plin. Lead-ore. Lead, Id. Bluish discolouration, Apul.

units.la: Lixivium] Lixivia cinis. Lixivia calda, Col. Cinis lixivius, vel, lixivus, Varr. Lixivum, Pallad. Cinis, Decalem, pro lixivio.
units.tr: Lixivium] Lye-ash. Hot lye, Col. Lye-ash, or lye, Varr. Lye, Pallad. Ash, Decalem, for lye.

units.la: Locare aliquid alicui] Elocare fundum, Cic. Locitare foras agrum, Ter. Ablocare domum, Suet. Exercere cænaculariam, Vlp.
units.tr: Locare aliquid alicui] To let out an estate, Cic. To let out a field abroad, Ter. To let a house, Suet. To run a boarding-house, Vlp.

units.la: Locator] Locatarius, Sipont.
units.tr: Locator] Lessee, Sipont.

units.la: Loco] In loco alicujus esse, Cic. Invicem, Virg. Vice cotis, Hor. Pro Domino possidere, Liv. Nomine præmii, Quint.
units.tr: Loco] To be in someone's place, Cic. In turn, Virg. In the manner of a whetstone, Hor. To hold as owner, Liv. By way of reward, Quint.

units.la: Locuples] Benè peculiatus, Cic. Benè prædiatus, Apul. Multa bona benè parta habet, Plaut. Omnes te in lauta & benè aucta parte putant, Ter.
units.tr: Locuples] Well endowed with private property, Cic. Well supplied with estates, Apul. He has many goods well acquired, Plaut. Everyone thinks you are in a rich and well-increased position, Ter.

units.la: Locus] Spatium loci, Lucr. Spatium, abs.Ovid. Receptaculum rerum. Receptator locus, ex Cic.
units.tr: Locus] A space of place, Lucr. Space, abs. Ovid. A receptacle of things. A place that receives, ex Cic.

units.la: Locus desertus] Locus nullo hominum cultus, Sen.
units.tr: Locus desertus] A place untouched by human cultivation, Sen.

units.la: Suo quodque loco se contineat] Fulmenta lectum scandunt, Turneb.
units.tr: Suo quodque loco se contineat] Let each keep to its own place. Props climb onto the couch, Turneb.

units.la: Locusta] Iræ Deorum pestis, Plin. Messium depopulatrix.
units.tr: Locusta] A plague, the wrath of the gods, Plin. A ravager of crops.

units.la: Locutulejus] Locutor. Linguax. Blatero, Gell. Tractator, Spartian. Aretalogus, Suet.
units.tr: Locutulejus] A speaker. A chatterer. A babbler, Gell. A discusser, Spartian. A teller of marvels, Suet.

units.la: Logica] Logice. Flabellum animi. Frenum rationis. Scientiarum clavigera. Vid. Dialectica.
units.tr: Logica] Logic. A fan of the mind. A bridle of reason. The key-bearer of the sciences. See Dialectica.

units.la: Logicus] Profligator errorum. Sophistarum mastix. Venator veritatum.
units.tr: Logicus] A destroyer of errors. A scourge of sophists. A hunter of truths.

units.la: Loliaceus] Ærina farina, Plin. Loliarium cibrum, Col.
units.tr: Loliaceus] Flour of darnel, Plin. A sieve for darnel, Col.

units.la: Lolium] Æra, Plin. Zizania. Zizanium, Suid.
units.tr: Lolium] Darnel, Plin. Tares. Tares, Suid.

units.la: Longævitas] Cervina senectus. Hesiodi senectus. Mathusalæ vivacitas.
units.tr: Longævitas] A stag's old age. The age of Hesiod. The long life of Methuselah.

units.la: Longævus] Polychronius, Firm. Macrobius, Mela. Perdiuturnus, Cic. Anus famæ, Catul. Vivax cervus, Virg. Expers sepulchri virtus, Ovid. Cornice vivacior.
units.tr: Longævus] Lasting for ages, Firm. Of great age, Mela. Very long-lasting, Cic. An old woman of fame, Catul. A long-lived stag, Virg. A virtue that the tomb does not claim, Ovid. Longer-lived than a crow.

units.la: Longè remotus] Immane quantùm distat, Er. Remotiffi- mus. Longissimè remotus, Cic.
units.tr: Longè remotus] Immensely far apart, Er. Most remote. Furthest removed, Cic.

units.la: Longè post] Multò pòst, Cic. Intervallo magno tempo- ris. Intersunt tot anni, Er.
units.tr: Longè post] Much later, Cic. After a great interval of time. So many years lie between, Er.

units.la: Longinquè] Longe abire. Longè procul. Procul à. Lon- gè gentium. Longè lateque, Cic.
units.tr: Longinquè] To go far away. Far off. Far from. Far among the nations. Far and wide, Cic.

units.la: Longitudo loci] Prolixitas locorum, Vlp. Longinquitas locorum, Cic.
units.tr: Longitudo loci] Extent of places, Vlp. Remoteness of places, Cic.

units.la: Longitudo temporis] Diuturnitas, Liv. Longinquitas tem- poris, Cæf. Ætatis, Ter.
units.tr: Longitudo temporis] Long duration, Liv. Length of time, Cæf. Of age, Ter.

units.la: Longius, vid. Vlterius.
units.tr: Longius, see Vlterius.

units.la: Longus duratione] Longa ætas, Hor. Diuturnus, Cic. Lon- ginquus morbus, Liv. Spatiosus, Ovid. Prolixus, Sipont. Diutinus, Cic.
units.tr: Longus duratione] Long life, Hor. Lasting, Cic. A protracted illness, Liv. Extended, Ovid. Prolonged, Sipont. Long-drawn-out, Cic.

units.la: Longus extensione] Longus sex pedum. Spatiosus. Lon- ginquum iter. Perpetuus canaliculus. Productus, Col. Pro- lixa arbor, Varr. Procerus numerus, Cic. Promissa bar- ba, Cornel. Nep. Prælongus gladius, Liv. Demissitius, Plaut. Demissa ad talos tunica, Varr. Cic. Projecta insula. Multus in laudando, Id.
units.tr: Longus extensione] Six feet long. Spacious. A long journey. A continuous channel. Extended, Col. A tall tree, Varr. A tall number, Cic. A beard grown long, Cornel. Nep. A very long sword, Liv. Hanging down, Plaut. A tunic reaching down to the ankles, Varr. Cic. A jutting island. Lavish in praise, Id.

units.la: Loquacitas] Inanis, citraque delectum congesta, verbo- rum & sententiarum turba, Er. Vid. Garrulitas.
units.tr: Loquacitas] A crowd of words and sentences heaped together without selection, Er. See Garrulitas.

units.la: Loquax] Loquacior cornice, turture. Ad vinum disertus. Lingua non habet frenum, lingua quò vadis? Vid. Garrulus.
units.tr: Loquax] More talkative than a crow or a turtle-dove. Eloquent over wine. The tongue has no bridle: tongue, where are you going? See Garrulus.

units.la: Loquax ne sis] Cum aliis pauca, tecum multa, cum D E o plurima. Vis loqui? disce tacere prius.
units.tr: Loquax ne sis] Use few words with others, many with yourself, and most of all with GOD. Do you want to speak? First learn to be silent.

units.la: Loquela, vid. Sermo.
units.tr: Loquela, see Sermo.

units.la: Loquentia] Profluentia loquendi. Redundantia juvenilis (in dicendo) Cic. Fluentia loquendi, Amm. Satis eloquen- tiæ, Salust.
units.tr: Loquentia] Flow of speech. Youthful exuberance (in speaking), Cic. Fluency of speech, Amm. Enough eloquence, Salust.

units.la: Loquentia vana] Mare verborum, gutta rerum.
