units.tr: Loquentia vana] A sea of words, a drop of things.

units.la: Loqui] Agere aliquid. Verba facere. Differere de aliqua- re. Operam dare sermoni. Uti voce. Fari. Vocem mittere. Promere voces. Pronunciare uno spiritu. Sermocinari, Cic. Profundere verba, Lucr. Satis jam dictum habeo, Plaut. Profari, Virg.
units.tr: Loqui] To do something. To make speeches. To discourse on a matter. To give attention to talk. To use the voice. To speak. To send forth the voice. To bring out words. To pronounce in one breath. To converse, Cic. To pour out words, Lucr. I have now said enough, Plaut. To speak forth, Virg.

units.la: Loqui ad populum] Orationem agere, dicere, habere. Pero- ran rare causam, dicere, apud, ad judices. Ad populum agere, Cic. Orationem recitare, Id. Orare causas, Quint. Agere causas apud aliquem, Plin. Oratio est mihi cum aliquo, Cic.
units.tr: Loqui ad populum] To deliver, say, or hold a speech. To plead a case before judges. To speak to the people, Cic. To recite a speech, Id. To plead cases, Quint. To plead cases before someone, Plin. I have a speech with someone, Cic.

units.la: Loqui & agere suo cuique modo fas est] Doribus Doricè loqui fas est.
units.tr: Loqui & agere suo cuique modo fas est] It is right for each to speak and act in his own way. It is lawful for the Dorians to speak in the Doric manner.

units.la: Loqui non intellecta] Dare sine mente sonum.
units.tr: Loqui non intellecta] To give out sound without mind.

units.la: Loqui frustra] Littori loqueris. Surdo loqueris. Fabulam narras.
units.tr: Loqui frustra] You speak to the shore. You speak to the deaf. You tell a tale.

units.la: Loquitur res ipsa] Opus commendat artificem.
units.tr: Loquitur res ipsa] The work itself commends the craftsman.

units.la: Lora] Vinum secundarium, operarium. Deuteria, & deuterias, Plin. Vinum eructum, Gell. Acinatitium, Pallad. Lorea, Cat. Vinum praeliganeum, Id. Acinacium, vel Acinaticum, Hotom.
units.tr: Lora] Second-quality wine, workmen's wine. Deuteria and deuterias, Plin. Belched wine, Gell. Grape-wine, Pallad. Lorea, Cat. Wine that is left over, Id. Acinacium or Acinaticum, Hotom.

units.la: Lorarius, vid. Apparitor.
units.tr: Lorarius, see Apparitor.

units.la: Lorica, ferrum indusium] Thorax nexilis, Stat. Ferrea texta, Lucr. Tunica ex annulis ferrea, Varr. Lorica hamis conserta, Virg. Lorica hamata, Lipf. Lorica è ferreis circulis contexta, Isid. Laminarum circuli tenues apti corporis flexibus, Amm.
units.tr: Lorica, ferrum indusium] An iron shirt: a knotted breastplate, Stat. Woven of iron, Lucr. An iron tunic of rings, Varr. A breastplate linked with hooks, Virg. A mail breastplate, Lipf. A breastplate woven of iron rings, Isid. Thin circles of plates fitting the bends of the body, Amm.

units.la: Loricatus, vid. Armatus.
units.tr: Loricatus, see Armatus.

units.la: Lorum] Loramentum, Iust. Corium, Cic.
units.tr: Lorum] A leather strap, Iust. Hide, Cic.

units.la: Lotium, vid. Vrina.
units.tr: Lotium, see Vrina.

units.la: Lotura] Lotio, Plin.
units.tr: Lotura] A washing, Plin.

units.la: Lubens] Perlubens. Libentissimus. Perstudiosus alicujus rei. Benevolentissimus. Perbenevolus alicui. Incensus studio ad aliquid. Inflammatus ad gloriam. Affectus in aliquem, erga aliquem, ad aliquid. Propendet in aliquem inclinatione voluntatis. Propensior in aliquem voluntas. Studiosus venandi. Prolixus animus. Prolixus in aliquem, Cic. Studiosus eloquentiae, Quint. Plurimus in Junonis honorem, Hor. Volens, Salust.
units.tr: Lubens] Very willing. Most willing. Very eager for something. Most kindly disposed. Well disposed towards someone. Fired with zeal for something. Inflamed with desire for glory. Inclined towards someone, towards someone, towards something. Leans towards someone by an inclination of the will. A will more inclined towards someone. Keen on hunting. A generous spirit. Generous towards someone, Cic. Eager for eloquence, Quint. Very much in honour of Juno, Hor. Willing, Salust.

units.la: Lubenter] Libenter. Vid. Libenter.
units.tr: Lubenter] Gladly. See Libenter.

units.la: Lubentia] Prolubium, Non. Prolubies. Prolubido, Var. Non.
units.tr: Lubentia] Inclination, Non. Inclination, Non. Desire, Var. Non.

units.la: Lubricitas] Bud. Lubricum, Lubrica viarum, Tac.
units.tr: Lubricitas] Bud. Slipperiness. Slippery roads, Tac.

units.la: Lubricus] Labidus, Vitr. Anguillâ lubricus magis, Er.
units.tr: Lubricus] Slippery, Vitr. More slippery than an eel, Er.

units.la: Lubricum tractare negotium] Caudâ tenes anguillam.
units.tr: Lubricum tractare negotium] You hold an eel by the tail.

units.la: Lucanica] Lucanicus botulus. Lucanica hira, Isid. Meurs. Botulus. Botellus, Mart. Farcimen, Varr.
units.tr: Lucanica] A Lucanian sausage. A Lucanian gut, Isid. Meurs. A sausage, Mart. Stuffed meat, Varr.

units.la: Lucere] Collucere. Splendere. Fulgere, Cic. Claret candidum lumen, Enn. Internitet cœli fulgor, Curt. Interlucet, Lucan.
units.tr: Lucere] To shine together. To gleam. To glitter, Cic. A bright white light shines clear, Enn. The brilliance of the sky gleams through, Curt. It shines through, Lucan.

units.la: Lucerna] Lychnus, Cic. Lychnuchi pensiles, Lavin. Lumen, Plin. Noctiluca, Varr.
units.tr: Lucerna] A lamp, Cic. Hanging lamps, Lavin. A light, Plin. A night-light, Varr.

units.la: Lucescit] Luciscit, Ter. Dilucescit, Cic. Diluculat, Gell. Diluculascit, Plaut. Promicat lux, Amm. Vid. Diluculum.
units.tr: Lucescit] It grows light, Ter. It dawns, Cic. It is dawning, Gell. Plaut. Light darts forth, Amm. See Diluculum.

units.la: Lucidus, vid. Clarus.
units.tr: Lucidus, see Clarus.

units.la: Lucifer] Stella Veneris, vid. Venus, Cic. Phosphorus, Mart. Iubar, Apul. Fest.
units.tr: Lucifer] The star of Venus, see Venus, Cic. Phosphorus, Mart. Morning star, Apul. Fest.

units.la: Lucius] Lupus fluvialis, Col. Fluviatilis, Gesn. Caudā placens, Plin.
units.tr: Lucius] River-wolf (pike), Col. River-fish, Gesn. Pleasing by its tail, Plin.

units.la: Lucrari] Lucrifacere, Mart. Lucrifit aliquid. Facere rem meliorem, Cic. Facere lucrum, quæstum, frugem. Compendifacere, Plaut. Rem facere. In lucro deputare, Ter. Facere operæ alicujus pretium, Liv.
units.tr: Lucrari] To make profit, Mart. To gain something. To make a thing better, Cic. To make gain, profit, or yield. To make a little profit, Plaut. To make money. To reckon as profit, Ter. To make it worth someone's while, Liv.

units.la: Lucrosus] Lucrosa eloquentia, Tac. Lucrosissimum aliquid, Plin. Quæstuosum damnum, Cic. In lucro est, Ovid. Lucri est aliquid, Ter. Lucro est, Plaut. Compendiosus, Col. Mancipium quæstuarium, Ulp.
units.tr: Lucrosus] Profitable eloquence, Tac. Most profitable as something, Plin. A loss that brings gain, Cic. It is profitable, Ovid. Something is a gain, Ter. It is profitable, Plaut. Lucrative, Col. A slave who earns money, Ulp.

units.la: Lucrum] Lucellum. Quæstus & compendium. Quæsticulus. Accessio, Cic.
units.tr: Lucrum] A small gain. Profit and advantage. A little profit. An addition, Cic.

units.la: Lucrum iniquum] Dispendio æquale, malum lucrum.
units.tr: Lucrum iniquum] A gain equal to a loss; a bad gain.

units.la: Lucrum damnosum] Cadmæa victoria.
units.tr: Lucrum damnosum] A Cadmean victory.

units.la: Lucro inhiare] Quæstui habere. Conferre in quæstum. Quæstum in aliquâ re facere, Cic. Præmiari, Suet.
units.tr: Lucro inhiare] To hold for profit. To turn to profit. To make profit in some matter, Cic. To be rewarded, Suet.

units.la: Luctari] Colluctari cum aliquo, Plin. Confictari doloribus, Cels. Deluctari. Depugnare cum animo suo, Plaut. Certare secum, Plin. Iuv. Obluctari, Col. Illuctari, Stat.
units.tr: Luctari] To wrestle with someone, Plin. To struggle with pains, Cels. To fight it out. To fight with one's own mind, Plaut. To contend with oneself, Plin. Iuv. To struggle against, Col. To wrestle in opposition, Stat.

units.la: Luctatio] Lucta, Sipont. Colluctatio, Col. Luctatus, Plin. Luctamen, Virg. Certamen cum aliquo. Certatio, Cic. Certatus, Stat. Confluctatio, Gell.
units.tr: Luctatio] Wrestling, Sipont. Wrestling together, Col. A struggle, Plin. A struggle, Virg. A contest with someone. A contest, Cic. A striving, Stat. A violent struggle, Gell.

units.la: Luctator] Palæstrita. Valet viribus ad certandum Athleta, Cic. Palæstricus, Quint. Arenarius, Iul.cap. Gymnasiarchus, chus, Cic. Palæstes, Lamprid. Hysticus. Confector ferarum, Suet. Bestiarius, Cic.
units.tr: Luctator] Wrestler. An athlete who is strong enough to contend, Cic. A wrestling-master, Quint. A sand-fighter, Iul.cap. A gymnasiarch, Cic. A wrestler, Lamprid. Hysticus. A slayer of wild beasts, Suet. A fighter with beasts, Cic.

units.la: Luctuosus, vid. Flebilis.
units.tr: Luctuosus, see Flebilis.

units.la: Luctus ] Ægritudo ex ejus, qui carus fuit, interitu acerbo. Sordes. Mæror. Squalor. Denicales feriæ, quibus residentur mortui, Cic.
units.tr: Luctus] Grief from the bitter death of one who was dear. Mourning dress. Sorrow. Squalor. Funeral days on which the dead are mourned, Cic.

units.la: Lucubrare] Lucubratum opus noctibus. Per lucubrationem. Ad lucubrationem. In lucubratione aliquid conficere, Cic. Nocturnus legit, Hor.
units.tr: Lucubrare] A work written by night. By lamplight. For night-work. To finish something by lamplight, Cic. A night reader, Hor.

units.la: Lucubratio] Lucubratiuncula, Gell. Opusculum contra-ctioribus noctibus lucubratum, Cic. Lucubratoria lecticula, Sen.
units.tr: Lucubratio] A little night-work, Gell. A little work written in the shortened nights, Cic. A lamp-stand for night work, Sen.

units.la: Ludere] Ludere par impar, Hor. Ludere pilâ, Cic. Ludere ducatus & imperia. (cum fingunt reges & potestatespueri.) Ludo se oblectare, Suet. Alludere alicui, Sen. Ad aliquem, Ter. Perludere campis, Propert.
units.tr: Ludere] To play at odd and even, Hor. To play ball, Cic. To play at leaders and commands (when boys play at kings and magistrates). To amuse oneself with play, Suet. To play with someone, Sen. To joke with someone, Ter. To play over the fields, Propert.

units.la: Ludi] Ludicrum, Liv. Agon gymnicus, Plin. Iun. Ludorum certamen, Ovid. Edidit spectacula varii generis munus gladiatorium, ludos etiam, &c. Ludi juvenales, Suet. Iuvenalia, Cap. Sid. Ludi juvenalium, Tac.
units.tr: Games: a sport, Liv.; a gymnastic contest, Plin. Iun.; a contest of games, Ovid.; he gave spectacles of various kinds, a gladiatorial show, games also, etc.; the youthful games, Suet.; the Juvenalia, Cap. Sid.; the games of the young, Tac.

units.la: Ludibrio esse ] In ridiculo esse, haberi. Irridiculum sumus, &, irridiculo, Plaut. Debere risum alicui, Lambin. In ora hominum pro ludibrio abit, Liv. Esse in fabulis. Esse ostentui alicui, Suet. Deridiculo fuit senex, Tac. Rideris. Traduceris, Mart.
units.tr: To be a laughingstock: to be held in ridicule; we are made a laughingstock, Plaut.; to owe someone laughter, Lambin.; he becomes a byword on people's lips, Liv.; to be the talk of stories; to be a show for someone, Suet.; the old man became a laughingstock, Tac.; you are laughed at, you are made a spectacle of, Mart.

units.la: Ludibriosè] Scurriliter, Plin. Per deridiculum, per ridiculum, Plaut. Per ludibrium consulere aliquem, Tac. Per cavillationem, Liv. Per ludum & jocum aliquem fortunis evertere. Ludibundus, Cic.
units.tr: Mockingly: scurrilously, Plin.; by way of derision, by way of ridicule, Plaut.; to consult someone mockingly, Tac.; by sarcasm, Liv.; to ruin someone's fortunes by mockery and jest; playfully, Cic.

units.la: Ludibriosè tractare aliquem ] Ab Herode ad Pilatum mittere.
units.tr: To treat someone mockingly: to send him from Herod to Pilate.

units.la: Ludicer, vid. Scurrilis.
units.tr: Playful: see Scurrilous.

units.la: Ludibrium]Ludificatio senatus. Illusio. Ridiculum. Ironia, Cic. Deridiculum. Irridiculum, Plaut. Cavillatus, Apul. Dicteria, Var. Dicacitas scurrilis & scenia, Quint. Dictum vernile, Tac. Vernilitas, Sen. Cavillatio, Cic. Sanna, Pers. Postica sanna, Britan. Rhonchus, Mart.
units.tr: Mockery: a making a fool of the senate; illusion; a laughingstock; irony, Cic.; derision, a laughingstock, Plaut.; taunting, Apul.; gibes, Varro; scurrilous and buffoonish wit, Quint.; a servile jibe, Tac.; servility, Sen.; jeering, Cic.; a sneer, Pers.; a backward sneer, Britan.; a snort of scorn, Mart.

units.la: Ludificare aliquem] Ludificari aliquem, Cic. Ludos face re aliquem. Ludere aliquem. Ludibrio habere. Frustra ha bere aliquem. Subleƈtare os alicui. Sublinere os offuciis Versare aliquem, Plaut. Irridere per jocum. Carpere mi mico dente, Cic. Ludos sibi facere ex malis alicujus. Iocar in staturam alicujus, Sen. Illudere aliquem, &, in aliquem Eludere, Cic. Dicteria dicere in aliquem, Mart. Naso ad unco suspendere, Hor. Insultare fenis patientiam, Tac. Il ludere alicui, Virg. Iactitare ridicula, Liv. Adag. Ab He rode ad Pilatum mittere. Barbam vellere. Quasi pilam ha bere aliquem.
units.tr: To make a fool of someone: to be made a fool of, Cic.; to make sport of someone; to hold someone in mockery; to hold someone up to ridicule; to deceive someone in vain; to pull a face at someone; to smear someone's face with paint; to turn someone about, Plaut.; to mock by jest; to tease someone with a sharp tooth, Cic.; to make sport of another's misfortunes; to joke about someone's height, Sen.; to mock someone, Cic.; to scoff at someone, Cic.; to hurl taunts at someone, Mart.; to hang up one's nose at someone, Hor.; to insult an old man's patience, Tac.; to make fun of someone, Virg.; to bandy jests, Liv. Proverb: to send someone from Herod to Pilate; to pluck someone's beard; to handle someone like a ball.

units.la: Ludio, vid. Histrio.
units.tr: Stage-player: see Actor.

units.la: Ludus] Lusus puerorum, Plin. Lasciviæ lususque, Col. Lusio pilæ, Cic. Collusio cum aliquo, Solin.
units.tr: Game: the play of children, Plin.; wantonness and frolic, Col.; a game of ball, Cic.; playing together with someone, Solin.

units.la: Luere, vid. Abluere, Pœnas dare.
units.tr: To wash away / to pay the penalty: see To wash; to pay penalties.

units.la: Lues, vid. Contagium.
units.tr: Plague: see Contagion.

units.la: Lugere] Residere mortuos. Lessum facere. Iacere in mœ rore, Cic. Prolugere, est solito diutius lugere, Fest.
units.tr: To mourn: to sit beside the dead; to make lamentation; to lie in grief, Cic.; to mourn for longer than is customary, Fest.

units.la: Lugubris habitus] Lugubria, Ovid. Vestimentum fune bre. Mœror funebris. Lugubris ornatus. Sordes lugubres. Pulla toga, Cic. Vestis funesta, Catul. Mortualia, Næv. Fu nerea lana, Lucan, Vestes lugubris, Ter. Pulla vestis. Sor des, & squalor, Cic.
units.tr: Mourning dress: mourning garments, Ovid.; funeral clothing; funereal sorrow; mourning attire; mourning dirt; a dark toga, Cic.; a funereal garment, Catul.; garments of death, Naev.; funereal wool, Lucan; mourning garments, Ter.; a dark robe; filth and squalor, Cic.

units.la: Lugubrem habitum induere] Lugubria induere, Ovid. Mu tare vestem. Pullatum esse. In squalore & luctu esse. Squa let civitas velte mutatâ. Innumerabilis multitudo ad eum sordidata venerat, Cic. Induere habitum dolentium, Tac.
units.tr: To put on mourning dress: to put on mourning garments, Ovid.; to change one's clothes; to be dressed in dark robes; to be in squalor and grief; the city, its clothing changed, is in squalor; a countless crowd came to him in mourning dress, Cic.; to put on the garb of mourners, Tac.

units.la: Lugubrem habitum exuere] Insignia doloris deponere, Val. Max. Ad suum vestitum redire, Cic. Elugere, Liv.
units.tr: To lay aside mourning dress: to lay down the marks of grief, Val. Max.; to return to one's ordinary clothing, Cic.; to cease mourning, Liv.

units.la: Lumbricus] Colubra cœca, Col. Tænia, à fimil. Plin.Ium. Animal ventris ; intestinorum, Plin. Vermes innati, Id.
units.tr: Earthworm: a blind snake, Col.; a ribbon-worm, from its likeness, Plin. Iun.; a creature of the belly, of the intestines, Plin.; worms bred within, Id.

units.la: Lumen, vid. Lux.
units.tr: Light: see Lux.

units.la: Lumen majus obscurat minus] Smaragdus in luce obscurus.
units.tr: The greater light obscures the lesser: an emerald is dim in the light.

units.la: Luminaria cæli] Luminis nostri diribitores.
units.tr: Lights of heaven: distributors of our light.

units.la: Luna] Soror æmula Phœbi. Diva Menstrua. Tenebrarum fax. Noctis honor. Humorum præsul. Mundi cerebrum Noctiluca, Varr.
units.tr: Moon: the sister and rival of Phoebus; the monthly goddess; the torch of darkness; the honour of night; the lord of moisture; the brain of the world; Noctiluca, Varr.

units.la: Luna crescens] Luna crescens gibbosa, Firm. Cornicula, Apul. Major dimidiata, Martian. Capel.
units.tr: Waxing moon: the gibbous waxing moon, Firm.; the little horn, Apul.; the half-grown moon, Martian. Capel.

units.la: Luna decrescens] Luna extrema senescens, Varr. Luna deficiens, Plin. Luna minuens, Pallad. Senium lunæ, Plin. Decrescentia lunæ, Vitr.
units.tr: Waning moon: the moon growing old at its end, Varr.; the failing moon, Plin.; the diminishing moon, Pallad.; the old age of the moon, Plin.; the waning of the moon, Vitr.

units.la: Lupanar] Stabulum, Plaut. Ganeum, Ter. Meritorium, Firm. Fornix, Iuven. Lustrum, Cic. Ianua orci, Plaut.
units.tr: Brothel: a stable, Plaut.; a bawdy-house, Ter.; a place for hire, Firm.; a vault, Juv.; a haunt of vice, Cic.; the gate of the underworld, Plaut.

units.la: Lupulus] Lupus solitarius, Plin.
units.tr: Lupulus: a solitary wolf, Plin.

units.la: Lurco, vid. Heluo.
units.tr: Glutton: see Gourmand.

units.la: Luridus, vid. Lividus, Pallidus.
units.tr: Livid / pale: see Livid, Pale.

units.la: Luscinia] Lusciniola, Plaut. Philomela. Aedon, Virg. Acredula, Cic. Isid. Attis, Mart.
units.tr: Nightingale: a little nightingale, Plaut.; the philomel; the songstress, Virg.; the little singer, Cic., Isid.; Attis, Mart.

units.la: Lusciosus] Lolio victitat, Plaut. Male oculatus, Suet. Male luminatus, Apul. Nyctalops, Plin. Myops, Bud. Caeculus, Ser. Microspicus.
units.tr: Purblind: living on darnel, Plaut.; badly sighted, Suet.; ill-sighted, Apul.; night-blind, Plin.; short-sighted, Bud.; squinting, Ser.; weak-eyed.

units.la: Luscus] Cocles, Plin. Unoculus, Plaut. Monoculus, Firm. Defioculus, Mart. Oculum persolum habet. Catapulta alter oculus ictus est, Plaut.
units.tr: One-eyed: Cyclops, Plin.; one-eyed, Plaut.; monocular, Firm.; blind in one eye, Mart.; he has only one eye; the other eye was struck by a catapult, Plaut.

units.la: Lusoria pugna] Pugnant volsellis non gladiis.
units.tr: Fight with tweezers: they fight with pincers, not swords.

units.la: Lusorius] Ludicer. Ludicrus, Gell. Ludiae coronae, Plin.
units.tr: Playful / sportive: playful; see Ludicer; playful, Gell.; garlands for games, Plin.

units.la: Lustrare] Perlustrare oculis. Prospeculari, Liv. Circumspicere. Contemplari, Cic. Visere, Plaut. Convisere oculis, Lucr. Oculis obire, Plin. Perspectare, Plaut. Vid. transl. Expiare.
units.tr: To survey: to survey with the eyes; to look out, Liv.; to look about; to contemplate, Cic.; to visit, Plaut.; to look over with the eyes, Lucr.; to go over with the eyes, Plin.; to examine closely, Plaut.; see To expiate.

units.la: Lustricus] Expiabilis, Cic. Piacularis, Liv. Piaculus porcus, Cic. Lustralis aqua, Ovid. Lustrificus, Val. Arg. Purgatoriae virtutes, Macrob.
units.tr: Lustral: expiable, Cic.; expiatory, Liv.; a pig offered for expiation, Cic.; lustral water, Ovid.; purifying, Val. Arg.; cleansing virtues, Macrob.

units.la: Lutare] Lutulare, Plaut. Collutulare aliquem, Limare caput limo, Id. Lambin. Vestimenta elevit luto, Non.
units.tr: To bemire: to splash with mud, Plaut.; to daub someone thoroughly with mud; to smear one's head with mud, Plaut.; she lifted her garments out of the mud, Non.

units.la: Luteus de colore] Luteola viola, Col. Silaceus color. Calthulus, Melleus, Plin. Fulvum aurum. Flavus crinis, Virg. Floridi crines, Id. Serv. Col. Galbus, & Galbeus, Lævin.
units.tr: Yellow in colour: yellowish violet, Col.; the colour of silphium; honey-coloured; golden; tawny gold; yellow hair, Virg.; flowing locks, Virg., Serv., Col.; yellow and golden-yellow, Lævin.

units.la: Luteus, de luto, vid. Argillaceus.
units.tr: Made of mud: see Clayey.

units.la: Lutosus] Limosus, Virg. Lutulentus, Ovid. Lutensis. Luto nutritus. Dialutensis purpura, Plin. Labosum & lutosum iter, Lucil. Luto lutulentior, Er.
units.tr: Muddy: slimy, Virg.; full of mud, Ovid.; miry; nurtured in mud; purple dyed twice over, Plin.; a toilsome and muddy road, Lucil.; muddier than mud, Erasm.

units.la: Lutum] Coenum. Limus, Virg. Volutabrum porcorum, Lux] Lux] Lumen, Lucr. Luminare, Cic. Collyrium oculorum. Revelator omnium.
units.tr: Mud: filth; slime, Virg.; a wallow of pigs, Lux. Light: a light, Lucr.; a lamp, Cic.; eye-salve; the revealer of all things.

units.la: Luxare membrum] Intorquere talum, Plin. Extorquere articulum, Sen. Convellit bos armum, Col.
units.tr: To dislocate a limb: to twist the ankle-bone, Plin.; to wrench a joint out, Sen.; an ox dislocates the arm, Col.

units.la: Luxatio] Luxum, Cat. Exarticulatio, Cel. Rhod.
units.tr: Dislocation: a dislocation, Cat.; disarticulation, Cel. Rhod.

units.la: Luxatus] Luxus pes, Non. Cat. Eluxatus, Decalemp. ex Plin.
units.tr: Dislocated: a dislocated foot, Non. Cat.; put out of joint, Decalemp., from Plin.

units.la: Luxuria] Profusa luxuries. Insolentia, Cicer. Luxus populator opum, Claud. Blandum malum. Mellitum venenum.
units.tr: Luxury: lavish luxury; insolence, Cicer.; luxury, the plunderer of wealth, Claud.; a pleasing evil; a honeyed poison.

units.la: Luxuria noxia] Serviet æternum, qui parvo nescient uti, Hor.
units.tr: Harmful luxury: he will be a slave forever who does not know how to make do with little, Hor.

units.la: Luxuriari] Diffluere luxuriâ, Tac. Mollitia & luxu fluere, Cic. Luxuriant animi rebus plerumque secundis. Mollescunt pectora, Ovid. Indulgere gaudio, Plin. In longinquum mittere cupiditates, Sen.
units.tr: To indulge in luxury: to melt away in luxury, Tac.; to flow with softness and extravagance, Cic.; minds grow luxurious amid prosperity, for the most part; hearts grow soft, Ovid.; to give oneself up to joy, Plin.; to let one's desires range far afield, Sen.

units.la: Luxuriosus] Adolescens luxu perditus, Ter. Luxuriæ immoderatissimæ, Trebel. Effusus in luxum, Tac. Æsopo luxuriosior, Er.
units.tr: Luxurious: a young man ruined by luxury, Ter.; luxury beyond all measure, Trebell.; poured out into luxury, Tac.; more luxurious than Aesop, Erasm.

units.la: Lynx] Lupus cervarium, Plinius, Sipont. Gesnerus. Chaus, Id.
units.tr: Lynx: a wolf of the deer kind, Plin., Sipont., Gesner.; the chaus, Id.

units.la: M.
units.tr: M.

units.la: Macellum] Tabernacarnaria, Varr. Carnarium, Plaut. Macer] Macilentus, Plaut. Ossa atque pellis totus. Exta inspicere in sole etiam vivo licet. Ita pellucet, quasi laterna Punica, Id. Macie peremptus, Liv. Exsuccus, Quint. Emaceratus, Sen. Scutilus. Vescculus, Fest. Vescus; corpore vesco, Plin. Torridus macie, Cic. Ossa pelle amicta lurida, Hor. Vix ossibus hæret, Virg. Monogrammos. Macellus, Non. Male habitus, Gell. Petilus, Varr. Aëre & rore pastus. Tam pinguis, quàm cor.
units.tr: Macellum] a meat-market: a butchers' stall, Varr. A meat-larder, Plaut. Macer] lean, thin: gaunt, Plaut. All bones and skin. One may inspect his entrails in the sun even while he is alive; he is so transparent, like a Punic lantern, Id. Worn to death by leanness, Liv. Juiceless, Quint. Wasted away, Sen. Shrivelled. Wizened, puny, Fest. Thin of body, Plin. Parched with leanness, Cic. Bones covered with discoloured skin, Hor. Scarcely clinging to the bones, Virg. A bare outline [μονόγραμμος]. Lean, Non. In poor condition, Gell. Slender, Varr. Fed on air and dew. As fat as a heart.

units.la: Macerare] Præmacerare mala, Scribon. Madefacere, Virg. Madidare, Arnob. Imbuere liquoribus. Sinere aliquid in aqua, Col. Vid. Emaciare.
units.tr: To soak] To soak apples beforehand, Scribonius. To moisten, Virgil. To wet thoroughly, Arnobius. To steep in liquids. To let something lie in water, Columella. See Emaciate.

units.la: Macere] Macescere, Plaut. Extabescere macie. Contabescere bescere luctu. Amittere corpus, Cic. Emacrari, Plin. Cibum non sentire, Id. Nihil corpori per alimenta accedit, Cels. Ad ultimam maciem redigi, Col. Remacrescere, Suet. Perdere carnem, Mart. Per tenues ossa numerantur cutes, Propert.
units.tr: To waste away] To grow thin, Plautus. To waste away with leanness. To pine away with grief. To lose flesh, Cicero. To become emaciated, Pliny. To not feel food, Id. Nothing reaches the body through nourishment, Celsus. To be reduced to utmost leanness, Columella. To grow thin again, Suetonius. To lose flesh, Martial. Through thin skin the bones are counted, Propertius.

units.la: Maceratus] Madefactus, Virg. Insuccatus, Col. Fluviatus, Plin.
units.tr: Soaked] Moistened, Virgil. Steeped in brine, Columella. Of river water, Pliny.

units.la: Machina]Machinamentum, Tac. Machinatio, Cic. Machinatus, Apul. Praecipua naturae architectio. Architectatio, Plin. Artificium simulationis, Cic.
units.tr: Machine] A contrivance, Tacitus. Machination, Cicero. Contrived, Apuleius. The outstanding construction of nature. Construction, Pliny. A device of pretence, Cicero.

units.la: Machinari] Omnes adhibere machinas ad tenendum aliquem. Commoliri machinam ad aliquem. Advocare artem, Cic. Fingere ad aliquem fabricam, Ter. Apparare, admovere fabricas, Plaut.
units.tr: To contrive] To use every device to seize someone. To set a plot against someone. To call in skill, Cicero. To devise a scheme against someone, Terence. To prepare and bring up contrivances, Plautus.

units.la: Machinatione occulta] Cuniculis oppugnare.
units.tr: By secret machination] To attack by tunnels.

units.la: Macies] Macror, Pacuv. Macritudo, Plaut. Maceries, Non. Malus corporis habitus, Cels. Coriago, in jumentis, Col.
units.tr: Leanness] Thinness, Pacuvius. Thinness of body, Plautus. Thinness, Nonius. A poor state of body, Celsus. Galled back, of beasts of burden, Columella.

units.la: Mactare sacrificandum] Caedere hostias, Cic. Victimas, Liv. Supponere cultros, Virg.
units.tr: To sacrifice for slaughter] To strike down victims, Cicero. Sacrificial animals, Livy. To place knives beneath, Virgil.

units.la: Mactè, vid. Euge.
units.tr: Mactè: see Euge.

units.la: Macula] Macula, Labes in veste. Naevus, Varus in facie. Lentigo in charta. Taenia, Plin. Area (ubi defluxere pili) Cels. Labecula, Cic.
units.tr: Stain] A stain, a blemish on a garment. A mole, a blemish on the face. A freckle on paper. A streak, Pliny. A bald patch (where the hair has fallen out), Celsus. A small stain, Cicero.

units.la: Maculare aliquid] Polluere dapes ore. Commaculare sanguine alicujus manus. Vultus foedare, Virg. Facere maculas in veste, Plin. Contemerare torum alicujus, Ovid. Caedes decoloravere mare, Hor.
units.tr: To stain something] To soil a feast with the mouth. To stain someone's hands with blood. To defile the face, Virgil. To make stains on a garment, Pliny. To defile someone's marriage bed, Ovid. Slaughter has stained the sea, Horace.

units.la: Maculosus] Respersus guttis. Interstinctus aureis guttis. Distinctus punctis, Plin. Stellantibus oculis interstinctus amictus, Martian. Varia pelle, vel versicolore, ut panthera, Plin. Guttata avis, Martial. Litus guttis, Virg. Vid. Versicolor.
units.tr: Spotted] Sprinkled with drops. Speckled with golden drops. Marked with dots, Pliny. A cloak speckled with starry eyes, Martial. Of variegated skin, or many-coloured, like a panther, Pliny. A spotted bird, Martial. A shore spotted with drops, Virgil. See Many-coloured.

units.la: Madefacere, vid. Macerare.
units.tr: To moisten: see To soak.

units.la: Madere]Madescere. Madefieri, Ovid. Commadere, Cat. Immadescere, Plin. Macerescere, Cat.
units.tr: To be wet] To become moist. To be made wet, Ovid. To be soaked through, Catullus. To become very wet, Pliny. To become soaked, Catullus.

units.la: Madidus] Madens, Cic. Uvida vestis, Plaut. Riguus hortus, Ovid. Irriguus, Hor. Subriguus, Plin. Vid. Humidus.
units.tr: Wet] Dripping, Cicero. Wet clothing, Plautus. A well-watered garden, Ovid. Irrigated, Horace. Well watered, Pliny. See Damp.

units.la: Magia ] Magice. Ars Magica, Plin. Dardanariæ artes. (A Dardanario inventore.)
units.tr: Magic] Magic arts. The magic art, Pliny. Dardanian arts (from Dardanus, the inventor).

units.la: Magicus] Veneficus aspectus, Plin.
units.tr: Magical] A baleful gaze, Pliny.

units.la: Magis] Impendio magis animus gaudebat mihi,Ter. Magis magisque, Sen. Plus plusque. Impensius. Magis ac magis. Amplius. Plus quàm. Pluris æstimo quam. Plusculum largiare, quam, Cic. Ter tanto pejor, Plaut. Dulcior magè, Boët. Magis magis irascor, Catul.
units.tr: More] I rejoiced in my mind all the more, Terence. More and more, Seneca. Still more and more. More intensely. More and more. Further. More than. I value more highly than. You bestow a little more than, Cicero. Three times worse, Plautus. Sweeter, Boethius. I grow more and more angry, Catullus.

units.la: Magis propriùs, quàm alienis afficimur] Omne domesticum afficit.
units.tr: The more closely we are affected by what is near than by what is alien] Everything domestic affects us.

units.la: Magister] Magister luxuriæ, Cic. Officinator, Vitr. Magister officinæ, vel Fabrorum. Vid. Doctor.
units.tr: Master] Master of luxury, Cicero. A craftsman, Vitruvius. Master of a workshop, or of the smiths. See Teacher.

units.la: Magister bonus] Bonus dux, bonum reddit comitem.
units.tr: A good master] A good leader makes a good companion.

units.la: Magister ineptus] Cœcus cœcorum dux. Tortor ingeniorum.
units.tr: An incompetent master] A blind leader of the blind. A torturer of talents.

units.la: Magistratus] Potestas. Imperium summum, clarissimum, Consulare, Prætorium, Extraordinarium. Munus Reip. Magistratus mutus, lex ; & lex, mutus Magistratus, Cic.
units.tr: Magistracy] Authority. Supreme, most distinguished, consular, praetorial, extraordinary power. A duty of the commonwealth. A magistrate who is silent is a law; and a law is a silent magistrate, Cicero.

units.la: Magistratum inire ] Ascendere dignitatis gradum, in honorem, ad honorem. Venire in summum locum, Cic. Magistratum ingredi, Salust. Magistratum occipere, Tac. Inire Consulatum, Cæs. Capessere honorem, Tac.
units.tr: To enter upon a magistracy] To climb a step of dignity, to honour, to office. To come into the highest place, Cicero. To enter a magistracy, Sallust. To begin a magistracy, Tacitus. To enter upon the consulship, Caesar. To seize an office, Tacitus.

units.la: Magistratum gerere] Magistratum habere, Peragere, sustinere munus Consulare. Fungi munere maximo. Potestatem gerere, In ordinibus sedere. Prætextatus & in magistratu sum, Cic.
units.tr: To hold a magistracy] To have a magistracy. To carry out, to sustain the consular office. To discharge the greatest duty. To exercise authority. To sit among the orders. I am even in office, wearing the purple-bordered robe, Cicero.

units.la: Magnanimitas, magnanimus, vid. Animosítas, Fortitudo, &c.
units.tr: Magnanimity, magnanimous: see Courage, Fortitude, etc.

units.la: Magnanimus, sed non magnipotens] Aut minus animi, aut plus potentiæ.
units.tr: Magnanimous but not mighty] Either with less spirit, or with more power.

units.la: Magnanimus non invidet] Sol non invidet vesperæ.
units.tr: The magnanimous man does not envy] The sun does not envy the evening.

units.la: Magnanimus nihil metuit ] Incus maxima non metuit strepitus. Incus robusta non timet malleum.
units.tr: The magnanimous man fears nothing] The largest anvil does not fear the noise. A sturdy anvil does not fear the hammer.

units.la: Magnanimi labores] Herculea facinora.
units.tr: Magnanimous labours] Herculean deeds.

units.la: Magnates] Optimates. Columina Reip. Cic. Proceres, Liv. Primores, Virg. Summates Viri, Apul. Megistanes, Tac. Potentes, Lucan. Magna-
units.tr: Great men] Best men. Pillars of the commonwealth, Cicero. Leaders, Livy. Foremost men, Virgil. Men of the highest rank, Apuleius. Magnates, Tacitus. The powerful, Lucan.

units.la: Magnatum preces, mandata] Potestas dum supplicat, imperat. Preces armatæ.
units.tr: The entreaties and commands of the great] Authority, while it begs, commands. Armed entreaties.

units.la: Magnes] Lapis siderites è ferro vitam trahens.
units.tr: Magnet] A siderite stone that draws life from iron.

units.la: Magnificè, vid. Amplè.
units.tr: Magnificently: see Amply.

units.la: Magnificus, Subst.] Potens Vir. Potentissimus. Vir fortunatus & potens. Clarissimus. Amplissimus, Cic. Illustrissimus. Spectabilis, Amm. Clementissimus. Providentissimus, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Magnificent (noun)] A powerful man. Most powerful. A man of wealth and power. Most distinguished. Most noble, Cicero. Most illustrious. The honourable, Ammianus. Most merciful. Most provident, Pliny the Younger.

units.la: Magnificus, adj.] Augustus, Virg. Ovid. Augustior, Liv. Superbus vestitus, Virg. Amplus. Amplissimus. Splendidus. Splendidissimus. Magnificentius & splendidius genus. Grandis & tragicus orator. Regius, Cic. Sublimis, Hor. Ambitiosus, Amm. Basilicus, Plaut.
units.tr: Magnificent (adjective)] Majestic, Virgil, Ovid. More majestic, Livy. Proud clothing, Virgil. Ample. Most ample. Splendid. Most splendid. A more magnificent and splendid kind. A grand and tragic orator. Royal, Cicero. Lofty, Horace. Ambitious, Ammianus. Kingly, Plautus.

units.la: Magnitudo] Amplitudo signi modica. Vis mellis maxima, Cic. Moles immensa, Virg. Res suo molimine gravis, Liv. Enormitas pedum, Sen. Vastitas beluarum, Col. Vastities corporis, Apul. Vastitudo leonis, Gell. Immanitas pretii, Plin. Mons aquarum, Virg. Maximitas, Lucr.
units.tr: Greatness] Moderate amplitude of a figure. Very great strength of honey, Cicero. Immense mass, Virgil. A matter heavy with its own weight, Livy. Enormous size of feet, Seneca. Vastness of beasts, Columella. Vastness of body, Apuleius. Vastness of a lion, Gellius. Monstrous price, Pliny. A mountain of waters, Virgil. Greatest size, Lucretius.

units.la: Magnus] Grandis, pergrandis, prægrandis. Amplus, peramplus. Infinitæ molis. Vastus, Cic. Ingens moles. Plurimus collis. Montes nimborum, Virg. Decumanus (quia decima magna sunt) Fest. Conspicuus magnitudine cæseus. Colosseus. Colossicus, Plin. Permagna res, Cic. Machinosum navigium. Enormis Colossus, Suet. Vis divina, Vlp. Decumani malorum fluctus. Moles mali, (magnum malum) Lucr. Mare & pelagus malorum, Lucr. Ilias malorum, Er.
units.tr: Great] Large, very large, exceedingly large. Ample, very ample. Of infinite mass. Vast, Cicero. A huge mass. A most numerous hill. Mountains of clouds, Virgil. Decumanus (because they are great tenths), Festus. Conspicuous for greatness of stone. Colosseus. Colossal, Pliny. A very great matter, Cicero. A ship with many engines. A huge Colossus, Suetonius. Divine power, Ulpian. The swelling waves of evils. The mass of evil (a great evil), Lucretius. The sea and the deep of evils, Lucretius. An Iliad of woes, Erasmus.

units.la: Magna non nisi cum mora fiunt] Res magnæ cunctationem requirunt.
units.tr: Great things do not come about except with delay] Great matters require deliberation.

units.la: Magnis magna] In mari magni capiuntur pisces.
units.tr: Great things for great] In the great sea fish are caught.

units.la: Magnos magna decent] Aquila non captat muscas. Culicem non curat Elephantus Indicus.
units.tr: Great things befit great persons] The eagle does not catch flies. The Indian elephant does not care for a gnat.

units.la: Magus] Sinistras literas edoctus.
units.tr: Magus] Learned in sinister letters.

units.la: Majestas, vid. Honor.
units.tr: Majesty: see Honour.

units.la: Major] Pluisculus, Ter. Magis majores, Plaut. Majusculus, Plin. Subgrandis, Cic.
units.tr: Greater] Somewhat more, Terence. Greater and greater, Plautus. Rather large, Pliny. Somewhat large, Cicero.

units.la: Majora evidentiora] Cum adsit via, semitam quæris.
units.tr: Greater things are more evident] When the way is open, you seek a footpath.

units.la: Majori cede] Cùm sis nanus, cede. Fluvius cum mari certas?
units.tr: Yield to the greater] Since you are a dwarf, give way. Do you contend with the sea, O river?

units.la: Majorennes] Major natu. Ætate præcurrit alterum, anteit, antecellit, alteri præstat, Cic. Natu grandior, Ter. Senior, Plaut. Cic. Ex potestate exiit. Vid. Adolescere.
units.tr: Elder] Older by birth. He outstrips the other in age, goes before him, surpasses him, is superior to him in years, Cicero. Older by birth, Terence. Senior, Plautus, Cicero. He has come out of parental authority. See Grow up.

units.la: Majores] Superiores. Superiori memoriâ cives, Cic. Priores nostri, Plin. Iun. Majores & parentes, Vlp. Vid. Antiqui.
units.tr: Ancestors] Superiors. Citizens of former memory, Cicero. Our predecessors, Pliny the Younger. Ancestors and parents, Ulpian. See Ancients.

units.la: Majores inferioribus infesti] Grandibus exigui pisces sunt piscibus escæ.
units.tr: Greater ones hostile to lesser ones] Small fish are food for larger fish.

units.la: Maliacia, vid. Tranquillitas, Mollitia.
units.tr: Mildness: see Tranquillity, Softness.

units.la: Male] Depravatè, & corruptè judicare, Vitiosè, perperam, Cic. Vapidè se habere, Suet. Secus, Sallust. Sinistrè, Hor. A malo quærere æs, Plaut. De malo, Apul. Pravè, Liv.
units.tr: Badly] To judge in a depraved and corrupt manner. Faultily, amiss, Cicero. To be in a flat condition, Suetonius. Otherwise, Sallust. Sinisterly, Horace. To seek bronze from a bad source, Plautus. From an evil source, Apuleius. Wrongly, Livy.

units.la: Male sit, quod male regitur] Plaustri rota malè uncta stridet.
units.tr: Whatever is badly governed is ill] A wagon wheel badly greased creaks.

units.la: Male parta, male dilabuntur] De malè quæsitis non gaudet tertius hæres.
units.tr: Ill-gotten goods are ill-spent] A third heir does not rejoice in what was badly acquired.

units.la: Male est mihi, vel alicui] Malè animo est. Factum male est animo alicujus. Doleo ab animo; ab ægritudine. Nescio quid malè factum nostræ familiæ. Perire ab animo. Cordolium mihi est. Ægrè est ab animo. Quid tibi ægrè est? Plaut. Ægrescit animus, Lucr.
units.tr: I am unwell, or someone is] I am in bad spirits. A thing has gone badly with someone's mind. I grieve in my heart; from distress. Something has gone badly with our family. To perish in one's mind. I have heartache. It goes badly with me in my mind. What is troubling you? Plautus. The mind grows sick, Lucretius.

units.la: Maledicere alicui] Malè loqui alicui. Loqui alicui non rectè. Maledictis aliquem onerare, differre, Plaut. Dicere mala plurima alicui, Catul. Maledictis insectari, figere, Maledicta in aliquem conjicere, dicere, Cic. Congerere, Quint. In caput tuum (scil. redeat malum) Scal. Gell. Deprecari mala, Catul.
units.tr: To speak evil of someone] To speak ill of someone. To speak wrongly to someone. To burden someone, put off with reproaches, Plautus. To say many evil things to someone, Catullus. To harass, fix someone with reproaches. To hurl reproaches at someone, Cicero. To heap up, Quintilian. Let the evil return upon your own head, Scaliger, Gellius. To pray down evils, Catullus.

units.la: Maledicere qui audet, audet & male facere] Maledicus à malefico non distat, nisi occasione.
units.tr: Whoever dares to speak evil also dares to do evil] The slanderer differs from the evildoer only in opportunity.

units.la: Maledictio] Maledictum. Convicium, Cic. Vid. Calumnia.
units.tr: Slander] A reviling word. Abuse, Cicero. See Calumny.

units.la: Maledicus] Maledicentiorem novi neminem, Plaut. Maledicentissimus, Cic. Maliloquax lingua, P. Mimus.
units.tr: Slanderer] I know no one more slanderous, Plautus. Most slanderous, Cicero. A tongue of evil speech; a mime.

units.la: Maledicum scriptum] Dentata charta.
units.tr: Libellous writing] Paper with teeth.

units.la: Malefacere, vid. Damnum inferre.
units.tr: To do harm: see To inflict loss.

units.la: Maleficium] Nefas committere, Cic. Vid. Flagitium.
units.tr: Wrongdoing] To commit a crime, Cicero. See Disgrace.

units.la: Maleficus] Maleficentissimus, Suet. Reus noxens. Reus maximis plurimisque criminibus. Reus capitalis, Cicer. Omnibus reis noxior, Noxiosissimus, Sen. Noxiissimus, Curt. Noxialis, Prudent.
units.tr: Wrongdoer] Most harmful, Suetonius. A guilty defendant. A defendant charged with the gravest and most numerous crimes. A capital defendant, Cicero. More harmful than all defendants, most harmful, Seneca. Most guilty, Curtius. Hurtful, Prudentius.

units.la: Malevolentia ] Voluptas ex alieno malo. Mala gratia. Aliena & offensa voluntas, Cic. Malignitas, Plaut.
units.tr: Malevolence] Pleasure taken in another's misfortune. Ill will. A hostile and offensive will, Cicero. Malice, Plautus.

units.la: Malevolus] Malevolentia suffusus, infuscatus, Cic. Infavorabilis sententia, Cels. Sinistris sermonibus carpere aliquem, Plin. Iun. Malevolens genius, Plaud.
units.tr: Malevolent] Filled with malevolence, tainted, Cicero. A judgement unfavourable, Celsus. To carp at someone with sinister talk, Pliny the Younger. A malevolent spirit, Plautus.

units.la: Maligne] Malitiosè. Per malitiam fingere, &c. Dicto aut facto protervo alicui nocere, Cic. Maligna mente facere, Catul. Protervè, Ter. Per nequitiam facere, Vlp.
units.tr: Maliciously] Wickedly. To feign out of malice, etc. To harm someone by an insolent word or deed, Cic. To act with a malicious mind, Catul. Insolently, Ter. To act out of wickedness, Vlp.

units.la: Malignitas] Malitia. Pravitas animi. Malevolentia, Improbitas. Vitiositas, Cic. Nequitia, Vlp. Sinisteritas, Plin. Iun. Vitium, Hor.
units.tr: Malignity] Malice. A depraved mind. Ill will, wickedness. Viciousness, Cic. Naughtiness, Vlp. Sinisterness, Plin. Iun. A vice, Hor.

units.la: Malignus] Maligna mens, Catul. Malitiosus homo, sceleratus, nequam, protervus, Cic. Malignissima capita, Sen. Scelus, Plaut. Improbus. Plenus sceleris, Cic.
units.tr: Malignant] A malicious mind, Catul. A malicious, wicked, worthless, insolent man, Cic. The most malignant heads, Sen. A crime, Plaut. Wicked. Full of crime, Cic.

units.la: Maligni] Maleferiati homines sunt non solùm otiosi, sed etiam otia malè collocantes.
units.tr: Idle men] Men who are ill-employed are not only idle but also spend their leisure badly.

units.la: Malle ] Multò malle, Cic. Magis velle. Præoptare aliquid, Ter. Liv.
units.tr: To prefer] To prefer by far, Cic. To wish more. To choose one thing in preference, Ter., Liv.

units.la: Malleus] Tudites mallei, Scal. Tudis malleus, Isid.
units.tr: Mallet] Hammers of the tudes, Scal. A hammer for tudes, Isid.

units.la: Malum] Moles mali. Tetra, & horribilis, infesta Reipub. pestis. Pestis & pernicies. Labes, calamitas, Cic. Mala crux. Thesaurus mali, Plaut. Pessimum, Varr. Ilias malorum, Er.
units.tr: Evil] A mass of evil. A foul and dreadful plague, hostile to the commonwealth. Pest and ruin. Disaster and calamity, Cic. A wretched cross. A storehouse of mischief, Plaut. Worst, Varr. An Iliad of woes, Erasm.

units.la: Malum esse, res facilis] Improbitas compendiaria res. Facilis descensus Averni, Virg. Noctes atque dies patet atri janua Ditis.
units.tr: To be bad is an easy matter] Wickedness is a short road. The descent to Avernus is easy, Virg. Night and day the gate of dark Dis stands open.

units.la: Malum commovere] Ruspari sterquilinium.
units.tr: To stir up evil] To rummage in a dunghill.

units.la: Malum non perit ] Malum vas non frangitur. Mala herba non perit.
units.tr: Evil does not perish] A bad vessel is not broken. A bad herb does not die.

units.la: Mala cumulare] Morbum morbo addere.
units.tr: To heap up evils] To add disease to disease.

units.la: Malum cum annis fit deterius ] Vulpes cum annis fit astutior.
units.tr: Evil grows worse with the years] The fox grows craftier with the years.

units.la: Malum cito transeat ] Celeritas in malis optima.
units.tr: Let evil pass quickly] Speed is best in evils.

units.la: Malum hoc, malum illud] Mali tripes, mali ipes: Malum hoc, nec illud melius.
units.tr: This evil, that evil] Mali tripes, mali ipes: this evil, nor is that better.

units.la: Malum malo non corrigitur] Convicium convicio regerere, est lutum luto purgare.
units.tr: Evil is not corrected by evil] To answer abuse with abuse is to cleanse mud with mud.

units.la: Malum bene positum non est movendum] Ebrius dormiens non est excitandus.
units.tr: An evil well placed is not to be moved] A drunk man sleeping is not to be woken.

units.la: Malum malo non augendum] Ignem igni ne addas.
units.tr: Evil is not to be increased by evil] Do not add fire to fire.

units.la: Malum malo oppositum] Duro nodo durus cuneus. Crudelem medicum intemperans æger facit.
units.tr: Evil set against evil] A hard wedge against a hard knot. An intemperate patient makes a cruel doctor.

units.la: Mala mixta bonis] Dulce amaro mixtum. Dulcia non meruit, qui non gustavit amara. Malum nullum sine aliquo bono, Plin.
units.tr: Evils mixed with goods] Sweet mixed with bitter. He does not deserve sweets who has not tasted bitter. No evil without some good, Plin.

units.la: Mala diutius meminimus, quàm bona] Cui placet, obliviscitur; cui dolet, meminit.
units.tr: We remember evils longer than goods] He who is pleased forgets; he who grieves remembers.

units.la: Mala præterita non terrent] Jucunda malorum præteritorum memoria.
units.tr: Past evils do not terrify] The pleasant memory of past evils.

units.la: Mala malis pelluntur] Amaris pharmacis amara bilis proluitur.
units.tr: Evils are driven out by evils] Bitter bile is washed away by bitter drugs.

units.la: Malus] Pravus. Deterrima mulier, Cic. Pravissimus, Tac. Alter, pro malo, Fest. Alius, itidem, Si quid cogitarent aliud, Apul. Hic niger est, Hor. Vitiosa nux. Perditi animi homo, Plaut. Parentem habeo illepidum, in liberos difficilem, qui nec te amet, nec studeat tui. Injuriosissimis aliquibus uti, Cic. Durus pater, Ovid. Mala, sæva, injusta noverca mihi est, Virg.
units.tr: Bad] Depraved. The most depraved woman, Cic. The most depraved, Tac. The other, for bad, Fest. Another, likewise: if they were thinking something else, Apul. Here is the black one, Hor. A bad nut. A man of ruined spirit, Plaut. I have a father who is unpleasant and difficult with his children, who neither loves you nor cares for you. To make use of some very wrongful persons, Cic. A harsh father, Ovid. A bad, cruel, unjust stepmother is mine, Virg.

units.la: Malus semper malus] Pardus maculas non deponit. Qui niger est nullâ candorem ducit ab arte.
units.tr: A bad man is always bad] A leopard does not lose its spots. Whoever is black draws no whiteness from any art.

units.la: Malus malum bene instruit] Aspis à vipera venenum mutatur. Malorum doctorum malæ sunt disciplinæ.
units.tr: A bad man instructs evil well] The asp takes its venom from the viper. The teachings of bad teachers are bad.

units.la: Mali sui author] Sibi ipsi vincula cudit. Sibi malum arcessit jumento suo. Sibi parat malum, qui alteri parat. Technam in teipsum struxisti.
units.tr: Author of one's own evil] He forges chains for himself. He brings evil on his own beast. He prepares evil for himself who prepares it for another. You have built a trap for yourself.

units.la: Malo nuncio mala præmia] Vates secum auferat omen.
units.tr: Bad news, bad rewards] Let the seer carry the omen away with him.

units.la: Malo quidvis noceat] Malum virum vel mus mordeat. Vel capra mordeat nocentem.
units.tr: Let anything harm the bad man] Let a mouse bite the bad man. Let a goat bite the guilty one.

units.la: Cum malo ne ingrediaris] Viro malo ne comes viæ fueris.
units.tr: Do not go with a bad man] Do not be a companion on the road to a bad man.

units.la: Mali malùs raro nocent] Corvus corvo oculum non eruit. Canis caninam non est.
units.tr: Bad men rarely harm bad men] A crow does not pluck out a crow's eye. A dog does not eat dog's flesh.

units.la: Malis male] Mali bibunt improbitatis secem. Malitia veneni maximam partem sui bibit. Malis fortuna parcit in poenam. Tolluntur in altum, ut lapsu graviore ruant. Nemo malus felix. Nocentem reperit Deus.
units.tr: The bad to the bad] The wicked drink the dregs of wickedness. The malice of poison drinks the greater part of itself. Fortune spares the wicked for their punishment. They are lifted on high so that they may fall with a heavier crash. No bad man is happy. God finds out the guilty.

units.la: Male artis artifex pessimus] Aleator quanto in arte est melior, tanto est nequior.
units.tr: The worst craftsman of a bad art] A gambler: the better he is in his art, the more wicked he is.

units.la: Mamilla] Mamma, Ter. Mammula, Cels. Uber, Virg. Ovid. Sumen lactans foeminae, Lucil. Fons sanctissimus corporis, Humani generis educator, Gell.
units.tr: Breast] A breast, Ter. A little breast, Cels. An udder, Virg., Ovid. The suckling of a woman, Lucil. The most holy fountain of the body, nurse of the human race, Gell.

units.la: Mammosus] Mammeatus, Plaut. Mammatus, Sipont.
units.tr: Big-breasted] Big-breasted, Plaut. Mammatus, Sipont.

units.la: Manalis, vid. Fluidus.
units.tr: Flowing, see Fluid.

units.la: Manare, vid. Fluere, Scatere.
units.tr: To ooze, see To flow, to spurt.

units.la: Manceps] Conductor aedificii, Cat. Coenacularius, (qui coenaculum conducit) Ulp.
units.tr: Contractor] The contractor of a building, Cat. The tenant of an upper room (one who rents a coenaculum), Ulp.

units.la: Mancipium, vid. Servus.
units.tr: Slave, see Servant.

units.la: Mancus] Unimanus, Liv.
units.tr: One-handed] One-handed, Liv.

units.la: Mandare] Imponere partes, provinciam alicui. Dare alicui negotium, Cic. In mandatis dare, Plaut. Vid. Committere, Iubere.
units.tr: To entrust] To assign parts, to give a province to someone. To give someone a task, Cic. To give in commission, Plaut. See To commit, to order.

units.la: Mandatum] Jussus, Plaut. Jussum. Imperio parere, Virg. Imperata peragere, Sen.
units.tr: Command] A command, Plaut. Commanded. To obey an order, Virg. To carry out what has been commanded, Sen.

units.la: Mandere] Mansitare, Plaut. Dentibus manditur, extenuatur, & mollitur cibus, Plaut. Conficere cibum, Liv. Manducare, Varr. Commanducare aliquid, Val. Max.
units.tr: To chew] To munch, Plaut. Food is ground, softened and made tender by the teeth, Plaut. To break down food, Liv. To chew, Varr. To chew something thoroughly, Val. Max.

units.la: Mane] Diluculo primo, Plaut. Bene mane. Multo mane. Maturissime, Cic. Mane obscuro, primo, Col. Cum prima luce, Ter. Coepta luce. Principio lucis, Tac. Maturrime, Caes. Matutino, Plin.
units.tr: Morning] At daybreak, at first light, Plaut. Very early in the morning. Early in the morning. Very early, Cic. In the dim early morning, Col. At first light, Ter. At the beginning of light, Tac. Very early, Caes. In the morning, Plin.

units.la: Mane, nomen] Diei principium, Varr. Matutinum, Quint. Aurora Musis amica.
units.tr: Morning, noun] The beginning of the day, Varr. The morning, Quint. Dawn, friend of the Muses.

units.la: Manere] Remanere alicubi, Caes. Residere. Redundat aliquid in sequentem annum. Exstat memoria, Cic. Haerescere, Lucr.
units.tr: To remain] To remain somewhere, Caes. To stay behind. Something overflows into the following year. Record of it survives, Cic. To cling, Lucr.

units.la: Manes] Umbrae volantes nocte, Virg. Tenues sine corpore vitae, Id.
units.tr: Shades] Shades flying about at night, Virg. Thin lives without bodies, Id.

units.la: Mango] Ornator, Firm. Exornator, Cic. Concinnator capillorum, Col. Cosmeta, Iuv. Vlp.
units.tr: Dresser] A decorator, Firm. An adorner, Cic. A curler of hair, Col. A cosmetic worker, Juv., Vlp.

units.la: Manica] Manulea, Lamb. Taub.
units.tr: Sleeve] A sleeve, Lamb., Taub.

units.la: Manicatus] Manclatus, Coler. Chirodotæ vestes, Lampr. Tunicæ habentes manicas, Virg. Manuleátus, manuleata tunica, Plaut. Suet.
units.tr: Sleeved] Sleeved, Coler. Sleeved garments, Lampr. Tunics having sleeves, Virg. Sleeved, a sleeved tunic, Plaut., Suet.

units.la: Manifestare] Aperire futura, Virg. Revelare, Sipont. Manifestum facere. Facere rem palàm, Plaut. Recludere operta, Hor.
units.tr: To make manifest] To reveal future things, Virg. To reveal, Sipont. To make manifest. To make a thing plain, Plaut. To uncover hidden things, Hor.

units.la: Manifestare se] In solem & pulverem prodire.
units.tr: To show oneself] To come forth into the sun and dust.

units.la: Manifestatio] Revelatio per, &c. Firm.
units.tr: Manifestation] Revelation through, etc., Firm.

units.la: Manifeste] Manifestò. Publicè dicere. In ore, in oculis omnium gestum. Luce & palàm. Aperte, Cic. Non obscurè, Cæs. Palàm populò, Liv. Propalam, Tac. Detectâ fronte, Quint.
units.tr: Manifestly] Plainly. To speak publicly. Done in full view and before the eyes of all. In the light and openly. Openly, Cic. Not obscurely, Caes. Openly before the people, Liv. Publicly, Tac. With forehead uncovered, Quint.

units.la: Manifestum] Confessa res. Vel puero clarum. Vel cœco apparet. Vid. Palam est.
units.tr: Manifest matter] An admitted matter. Clear even to a boy. Apparent even to a blind man. See It is plain.

units.la: Manifestus] Apertus. Palàm adversarius. Perspicua causa. Res clara & testata, Cic. Manifestarius fur, Plaut. Res in confessum venit, Plin. Iun. Confessa res, Col. Professus, Sen.
units.tr: Manifest] Open. Openly an adversary. A clear cause. A clear and attested matter, Cic. A manifest thief, Plaut. The matter came into the open, Plin. Iun. A confessed matter, Col. Professed, Sen.

units.la: Manna] Mel aëreum roscidum, Virg. Saliva siderum, Plin. Ros Syriacus, Cels.
units.tr: Manna] Airy, dewy honey, Virg. The spittle of the stars, Plin. Syrian dew, Cels.

units.la: Mansuefacere] Traducere ex feritate ad mansuetudinem. Ex feris & immanibus mites & mansuetos reddere, Cic. Lenire leones, Hor. Cicurare, Varr. Cicurem reddere, Mart. Pacare feras, Claud. Commulcere sensus judicum, Gell. Circummulcere. Mitigare, mitificare, Plin. Tractare aliquemarte, Ter.
units.tr: To tame] To lead from wildness to gentleness. To make wild and savage creatures mild and gentle, Cic. To soothe lions, Hor. To make tame, Varr. To make tame again, Mart. To pacify wild beasts, Claud. To soothe the feelings of judges, Gell. To stroke around. To mitigate, to make gentle, Plin. To deal craftily with someone, Ter.

units.la: Mansuefactus, vid Cicur.
units.tr: Tamed, see Tame.

units.la: Mansuete, vid. Comiter.
units.tr: Gently, see Courteously.

units.la: Mansuefieri] Mansuescere. Deponere ingenium silvestre, Col. Assuefieri ad homines, Cæs. Mitescere, Liv. Mitificare, Plin. Mansuetum fieri, Varr. Exuere ferociam, Tac. Mitigari. Demitigari, Cic. Deponere feritatem. Mollita feritas, Ovid.
units.tr: To be tamed] To become tame. To lay aside a wild nature, Col. To grow accustomed to men, Caes. To grow mild, Liv. To become gentle, Plin. To become tame, Varr. To cast off ferocity, Tac. To be softened. To be made milder, Cic. To lay aside savagery. Softened ferocity, Ovid.

units.la: Mansuetudo] Placiditas hominis, Gell. Lenitas. Suavitas tas hominis. Lenitas animi. Lenitudo, mollitudo, Cic. Vid. Clementia.
units.tr: Gentleness] A placid disposition of a person, Gell. Mildness. Sweetness of a person. Gentleness of spirit. Softness, tenderness, Cic. See Clemency.

units.la: Mansuetus] Mitis. Lenis, facilis, placidus, Cic. Permitis, Col. Mitificus, Apul.
units.tr: Gentle] Mild. Gentle, easy, placid, Cic. Quite mild, Col. Making mild, Apul.

units.la: Mantile] Chiromaétrum, Ludov.Viv. Mantellum, Lucil. Mantelium, Scal. Manterium, Varr. Linteum extersui, Plaut.
units.tr: Napkin] A hand towel, Ludov. Viv. A napkin, Lucil. Mantelium, Scal. Manterium, Varr. A linen cloth for wiping, Plaut.

units.la: Mantissa, vid. Additamentum.
units.tr: Addition, see Addition.

units.la: Manualis] Qui manum implet, Plin. Pugillaris, Iuv. Pugillatorius, Plaut. Manuarius, Iabolen.
units.tr: Handy] That which fills the hand, Plin. Palm-sized, Juv. Of the writing tablet, Plaut. Manuarius, Iabolen.

units.la: Manubiæ] Spolium, Plin. Ovid. Spolia, Cicer. Vid. Præda.
units.tr: Spoils] Booty, Plin., Ovid. Spoils, Cic. See Plunder.

units.la: Manubrium] Manubriolum, Celf. Capulus gladii, Cic. Virg. Capulum, Fest. Tenaculum, Ter. Ansa scuti, Amm. Capistrum, Cato. Amites basternarum (lecticarum) Pallad.
units.tr: Handle] A small handle, Celsus. The hilt of a sword, Cic., Virg. A hilt, Fest. A holder, Ter. A handle of a shield, Amm. A halter, Cato. The shafts of litters, Pallad.

units.la: Manumittere] Manu mittere aliquem, Plaut. Donare libertate servos, Cic. Vid. Libertas.
units.tr: To manumit] To send away from the hand, to set free. To give slaves their freedom, Cic. See Liberty.

units.la: Manupretium] Manipretium, Plin. Operæ pretium, Lucan. Æs manuarium, Gell.
units.tr: Wages] Hand-money, Plin. Worth the labour, Lucan. Hand-money, Gell.

units.la: Manus] Instrumentum instrumentorum. Organon artificiosissimum.
units.tr: Hand] The instrument of instruments. The most skilful organ.

units.la: Mappa] Mensale linteum, Lampr.
units.tr: Table-cloth] A table linen, Lampr.

units.la: Mappula] Mappela, Isid. Mantele, Plin. Decalemp.
units.tr: Small cloth] Mappela, Isid. A tablecloth, Plin., Decalemp.

units.la: Marcens] Vietus, Col. Exsuccus, Sen.
units.tr: Withering] Wilted, Col. Dried up, Sen.

units.la: Marcere] Marcescere. Exspirat flos ad austros, Stat. Sole & vento exarescere, & siccari. Flavescit fœniculum, Col. Commarcere fervore, Amm.
units.tr: To wither] To become withered. The flower breathes out in the south winds, Stat. To dry up and be parched by sun and wind. Fennel yellows, Col. To wilt from the heat, Amm.

units.la: Marcidus, vid. Vapidus.
units.tr: Withered, see Flat.

units.la: Marcor, vid. Desidia.
units.tr: Languor, see Idleness.

units.la: Mare] Pelagus. Salum, Cic. Altum. Æquor, Virg. Profundum, Lucr. Comitia aquarum. Hospitium fluminum. Terræ limes. Regionum divisor. Imbrium fons.
units.tr: Sea] The open sea. Brine, Cic. The deep, the high sea. The main, Virg. The depths, Lucr. The assembly of waters. The inn of rivers. The boundary of the land. The divider of regions. The source of rains.

units.la: Margarita] Margaritum, Varr. Tac. Uniones. Exalumi-natus. Nucleus concharum, Plin. Pretiosus calculus in carne conchæ, Isid. Ocellatum, Varr. Rubri maris grana pretiosissima, Vlp. Rubentis maris gratia candentia, Hieron. Bac ca conchea, Virg.
units.tr: Pearl] Pearl, Varr., Tac. Pearls. Polished. The kernel of shells, Plin. A precious little stone in the flesh of a shellfish, Isid. Little eyes, Varr. The most precious grains of the Red Sea, Vlp. The shining grace of the Red Sea, Hieron. Shell-berries, Virg.

units.la: Marinus] Maritimus, Plin. Pelagius,Varr. Pelagicus,Col. Caeruleus piscis, Iuv. Iof. Scal. Permarinus, Liv. Æquoreus, Virg.
units.tr: Marine] Maritime, Plin. Of the open sea, Varr. Pelagic, Col. A blue fish, Iuv. Iof. Scal. Wholly marine, Liv. Of the deep sea, Virg.

units.la: Marita] Nupta, Ovid. Matrona, Cic. Hor.
units.tr: Married woman] A wife, Ovid. A matron, Cic. Hor.

units.la: Maritus] Compar, Plaut. Hor. Vir, Ter. Consors tori, Ovid. Conjux apertus, Propert.
units.tr: Husband] A mate, Plaut. Hor. A man, Ter. A partner of the bed, Ovid. An open spouse, Propert.

units.la: Mars] Mavors. Mundi fel. Stella Martis, Cic.
units.tr: Mars] Mavors. The gall of the world. The star of Mars, Cic.

units.la: Marsupium, vid. Crumena.
units.tr: Purse, see Purse.

units.la: Martialis, vid. Bellicosus.
units.tr: Martial, see Warlike.

units.la: Martyres] Qui non dubitarunt capite cavere, quæ repromisit Dominus, vel interminatus est, Bud.
units.tr: Martyrs] Those who did not hesitate to risk their heads for what the Lord promised or threatened, Bud.

units.la: Martyrium] Fortissima pro Christo, ad necem usque dimicatio. Gloriosissimâ Christi causâ cædes.
units.tr: Martyrdom] The bravest struggle for Christ, even unto death. A slaying for the most glorious cause of Christ.

units.la: Mas] Masculus, Varr. Mascula proles, Hor. Vir. Plin. Sexus melior, Stat. Virilis proles, Virg. Virilis sexûs puer, Liv. Homo, pro masculo, Plaut. Beneficia fœminis hominibusque portabant, Arnob. Maritus perdicis, Plin.
units.tr: Male] Masculine, Varr. A masculine offspring, Hor. A man, Plin. The better sex, Stat. Manly offspring, Virg. A boy of the male sex, Liv. Man, used for male, Plaut. They brought benefits to women and men, Arnob. The male of the partridge, Plin.

units.la: Mastix] Mastiche, Plin. Masticum, Pallad.
units.tr: Mastic] Mastic, Plin. Mastic gum, Pallad.

units.la: Materialis] Corporeus. Corporatus. Constans ex materia. Factus è materia, Cic.
units.tr: Material] Corporeal. Embodied. Consisting of matter. Made of matter, Cic.

units.la: Matrimonialis] Conjugalis, Sen. Conjugialis,Ovid. Iugalis torus. Genialis,Virg. Maritalis,Iuv. Connubialis,Stat. Conjugulus, Cat.
units.tr: Matrimonial] Conjugal, Sen. Of marriage, Ovid. A yoked bed. Genial, Virg. Marital, Iuv. Connubial, Stat. Conjugal, Cat.

units.la: Matrimonium, vid. Conjugium.
units.tr: Matrimony, see Marriage.

units.la: Matta; vid. Storea.
units.tr: Mat; see Rush-mat.

units.la: Matula] Matella, Mart. Matellio, Iun. ex Varr. Scaphium, Iuven. Lasanum, Hor.
units.tr: Chamber-pot] Chamber-pot, Mart. Chamber-pot, Iun. from Varr. Bowl, Iuven. Pot, Hor.

units.la: Maturatè, vid. Festinanter.
units.tr: Maturely, see Quickly.

units.la: Maturè, vid. Tempestivè.
units.tr: Maturely, see Timely.

units.la: Maturescere] Maturari. Maturant arbores. Ematurescere. Mitescunt poma. Coquitur fructus. Percoquit sol messem, Plin. Devenit ad maturitatem. Permaturescit pomum. Percoquuntur uvæ, Col. Pervenit ad maturam frugem aliquid, Quint. Præcocem maturitatem trahere, Col. Spectat ad aream seges, Sen.
units.tr: To ripen] To be ripened. Trees ripen. To be fully ripe. Fruit mellows. Fruit is cooked. The sun ripens the harvest, Plin. It has come to maturity. The fruit has fully ripened. The grapes are thoroughly ripened, Col. Something has reached mature fruit, Quint. To draw on early maturity, Col. The crop nears the threshing floor, Sen.

units.la: Maturitas] Pubertas uvæ,Plin. Alescendi cacumen,Lucr. Plenitudo, Plin. Maturus] Permaturæ uvæ, Virg. Percoctus, Plin.
units.tr: Maturity] The bloom of the grape, Plin. The summit of growth, Lucr. Fullness, Plin. Mature] Fully ripe grapes, Virg. Thoroughly cooked, Plin.

units.la: Maxilla] Mandibula, Macrob. Sip. Mandibulum, Scalig.
units.tr: Jaw] Jawbone, Macrob. Sip. Jawbone, Scalig.

units.la: Maxime] Cùm maximè, Sen. Vel maximè. Imprimis. Præcipuè. Maximopere. Maximo te orabant opere, Cic. Potissimùm, Ter. Maximùm, Plaut.
units.tr: Most] Especially, Sen. Above all. Chiefly. Especially. Most of all. They begged you with the greatest effort, Cic. Above all, Ter. Most of all, Plaut.

units.la: Maximus] Ulteriorem accessionem non recipiens, Sen. Giganteâ mole sumus, Ter. Supremus, Virg. Ultimus, Cic. Vix jam ultrà, quò progrediatur habet, Ovid. Decimus. Decumanus, Fest.
units.tr: Greatest] Admitting no further increase, Sen. We are of gigantic bulk, Ter. Highest, Virg. Last, Cic. It scarcely has room to advance further, Ovid. Tenth. Tenth, as in the tenth legion, Fest.

units.la: Meâ sententiâ] Pro mea quidem sententia. Ut ego quidem sentio. Ut mea fert opinio. Meo quidem animo, meo judicio. Ut mihi quidem videtur. Ni fallor. Si quid judico. Meo quidem suffragio, calculo, Er.
units.tr: In my opinion] For my part indeed. As I myself think. As my opinion goes. In my mind, in my judgment. As it seems to me. Unless I am mistaken. If I judge anything. In my vote indeed, in my ballot, Er.

units.la: Meatus] Spiramina naris, Lucan. Oscula in cerebro animantis, quibus pituita destillat, Plin.
units.tr: Passage] Breathing-holes of the nose, Lucan. Little openings in the brain of a creature, through which phlegm drips, Plin.

units.la: Mechanica] Mechanica ars, Firm. Illiberalis labor, Cic. Vid. Opificium.
units.tr: Mechanical] Mechanical art, Firm. Illiberal labour, Cic. See Workmanship.

units.la: Mechanicus] Homo operarius, Cic. Vid. Opifex.
units.tr: Mechanic] A working man, Cic. See Craftsman.

units.la: Medela, vid. Sanatio.
units.tr: Healing, see Cure.

units.la: Mederi] Mederi aliquas res. Medicari alicui, Ter. Medicinam facere, afferre, adhibere. Adhibere curationem alicui. Admovere curationem ad aliquem. Sanare vulnera, dolores. Adhibere remedium, Cic. Medicari ictum cuspidis, Virg. Medicare oves, Pall. Curare ægros, Plaut. Sana faciet ulcera omnia, Cat. Ad sanitatem perducere ulcus, Cels.
units.tr: To heal] To heal something. To treat someone. To apply medicine: to bring, to administer. To apply treatment to someone. To bring treatment to someone. To heal wounds and pains. To apply a remedy, Cic. To treat a spear-thrust, Virg. To doctor sheep, Pall. To treat the sick, Plaut. He will make all sores healthy, Cat. To bring an ulcer to health, Cels.

units.la: Medianus] Centralis terra, Plin. Vid. Medius.
units.tr: Median] Central land, Plin. See Middle.

units.la: Medicamentum] Medicina, Plaut. Medicamen. Remedium, Cic. Medela, Quint. Pharmacum, Caj.
units.tr: Medicament] Medicine, Plaut. Medicament. Remedy, Cic. Healing, Quint. Drug, Caj.

units.la: Medicatus] Præmedicatus, Ovid. Condimentarium genus cibi, Plin. Infucata vina. Fucatus nitor, Cic. Oliva conditanea, Varr. Conditus, Col.
units.tr: Medicated] Previously medicated, Ovid. A seasoned kind of food, Plin. Unmixed wines. Adorned polish, Cic. Preserved olives, Varr. Seasoned, Col.

units.la: Medicè vivere] Vivere miserrimè.
units.tr: To live medically] To live most wretchedly.

units.la: Medicina] Ars medica, Tibul. Ars valetudinis, Cic. Ars medicinalis, Cels.
units.tr: Medicine] The medical art, Tibul. The art of health, Cic. The medicinal art, Cels.

units.la: Medicina experimentalis] Empirice, Plin. Ars muta, Virg.
units.tr: Empirical medicine] Empiricism, Plin. The silent art, Virg.

units.la: Medicina catholica ] Panacea. Panchrestum medicamentum, Cic.
units.tr: Universal medicine] Panacea. A remedy for all ills, Cic.

units.la: Medicinalis] Medicus usus, Ovid. Remedialis vis, Macrob.
units.tr: Medicinal] Medical use, Ovid. Healing power, Macrob.

units.la: Medicus] Felices Medici, quorum successus sol videt, errores terra opprimit, Plin. Doctus medicinæ, Id.Hor. Antagonista mortis. Colluctator morborum. Custos sanitatis.
units.tr: Physician] Happy physicians, whose success the sun sees and whose errors the earth covers, Plin. Learned in medicine, Id. Hor. Antagonist of death. Wrestler with diseases. Guardian of health.

units.la: Medicus imperitus malum reddet pejus] Acesias medicatus est, Aristoph.
units.tr: An unskilled physician makes the malady worse] Acesias was treated by a physician, Aristoph.

units.la: Medicorum magna libertas] Solis Medicis licet impune occidere.
units.tr: The great freedom of physicians] Only physicians may kill with impunity.

units.la: Mediocris] Modicus, Plin. In mediocribus oratoribus habitus. Temperatus. Habet modum, Cic. Moderatus,Ovid. Commodus, Celf. Justa magnitudo dierum, Suet. Tempestivus, Hor. Stata forma, Enn. Neque pessimus, neque optimus.
units.tr: Moderate] Modest, Plin. Held among moderate orators. Temperate. Keeps measure, Cic. Moderate, Ovid. Suitable, Celf. A just length of days, Suet. Timely, Hor. A standard form, Enn. Neither worst nor best.

units.la: Mediocritas] Modus benignitatis, Ter. Modus in dicendo, Cic. Modulus, Hor. Mensura beneficii, Plin.
units.tr: Mediocrity] A measure of kindness, Ter. A measure in speaking, Cic. A little measure, Hor. The measure of a benefit, Plin.

units.la: Mediocritas optima] Modus in re est optimus. Est modus in rebus, sunt certi denique fines ; quos ultra citraque nequit consistere verum, Hor.
units.tr: The golden mean is best] The middle course in a matter is best. There is a measure in things; there are fixed limits, beyond or short of which the truth cannot stand, Hor.

units.la: Mediocritatem transgredi] Ultra septa transilire.
units.tr: To go beyond the mean] To leap over the fence.

units.la: Mediocriter] Moderatè, modicè. Intra modum. Modo aliquid facere, Cic. Mediè, Apul. Moderatis rationibus, Lucr. Indifferenter, Suet. Medioxumè, Varr. Temperanter haberi, Tacit. Temperatè tepet, Cat. Moderatim tribuere. Moderanter habere habenas, Lucr.
units.tr: Moderately] Temperately, modestly. Within measure. To do something only moderately, Cic. Mediocrely, Apul. By moderate reasoning, Lucr. Indifferently, Suet. Half-well, Varr. To be held in check, Tacit. Lukewarm in temperature, Cat. To distribute in moderation. To hold the reins with moderation, Lucr.

units.la: Meditari, meditatio, vid. Cogitare, &c.
units.tr: To meditate, meditation, see To think, etc.

units.la: Mediterraneum] Meditullium, Fest.
units.tr: Inland] Middle of the land, Fest.

units.la: Medium ] Medius locus alicujus rei. Centrum solis. Meditullium. Medietas, Cic. Umbilicus diei, Plaut. Sinus urbis, Sallust. Mediocritas inter nimium & parum.
units.tr: Middle] The middle place of something. The centre of the sun. The midpoint. The mean, Cic. Noon, Plaut. The heart of the city, Sallust. The mean between too much and too little.

units.la: Medium utrique tutissimum ] Dimidium plus toto. Mediâ via quæstionem dirimit. Medium tenuere beati. Medio tutissimus ibis. Mediam viam elige. Modus in re est optimus omni.
units.tr: The middle course is safest for both] Half more than the whole. He settles the question by a middle way. The blessed have kept to the middle. You will go most safely by the middle. Choose the middle way. Measure in all things is best.

units.la: Medium sectare] Tenuem cypressum delige.
units.tr: Keep to the middle] Choose the slender cypress.

units.la: Medium (2) via,] Bono literarum absentes utemur, Cic. Beneficio aetatis, Quint. Vid. Per.
units.tr: Middle way] We shall make do without the benefit of literature, Cic. By the benefit of age, Quint. See Through.

units.la: Medius] Intermedius. Interjectus inter duos. Interjectus aliis. Constans aetas, quae dicitur Media, Cic. Medianus, Vitruv.
units.tr: Middle] Intermediate. Placed between two. Placed among others. The stage of life called middle, Cic. Median, Vitruv.

units.la: Medulla] Ossa arboris. Cerebrum arboris. Vitalis anima, Plin.
units.tr: Marrow] The pith of a tree. The heart of a tree. The vital spirit, Plin.

units.la: Mejere] Aquam petere, Petron. Aquam sumere, Ovid. Levare vesicam, Spart. Facere, reddere, edere, expellere urinam. Reddere humorem, Plin.
units.tr: To urinate] To fetch water, Petron. To take water, Ovid. To ease the bladder, Spart. To make, return, give out, expel urine. To return moisture, Plin.

units.la: Mel] Nectar. Dulci distendunt nectare cellas, Virg.
units.tr: Honey] Nectar. With sweet nectar they fill the cells, Virg.

units.la: Melancholia] Furor, Cic. Displicentia sui. Otii sui tristis ac aegra patientia, Sen. Balneum diaboli.
units.tr: Melancholy] Madness, Cic. Displeasure with oneself. The sad and sickly patience of idleness, Sen. The devil's bath.

units.la: Melancholicus] Ipse suum cor edens, Cic. Agelastus, Plin. Atra bili percitus. Ipsus se comest, Plaut.
units.tr: Melancholic] Eating his own heart, Cic. Never laughing, Plin. Driven by black bile. He eats himself up, Plaut.

units.la: Melior] Meliusculus. Pensior, Plaut. Satior, Plin. Potior mors servitute. Praestantior, Cic. Bellior, Varr. Melius se habet, quam, Cic. Melioris notae.
units.tr: Better] Somewhat better. More weighty, Plaut. More satisfying, Plin. Death is preferable to slavery. More excellent, Cic. Better, Varr. It is better than, Cic. Of better repute.

units.la: Melius est] Satius est. Praestat, Cic. Praevalet ista non tacere, Catul. Pro meliore nobis fuit effugere, Tac. Meliusculè est. Sapias magis, si, &c. Plaut.
units.tr: It is better] It is more satisfying. It is preferable. It is better not to keep silent, Catul. It was better for us to escape, Tac. It is a little better. You would be wiser if, etc., Plaut.

units.la: Melius hoc illo] Mel est, cum illo comparatum.
units.tr: This is better than that] It is honey compared with that.

units.la: Melius regredi, quam male progredi] Recurrere satius, quam male currere.
units.tr: Better to go back than to go on badly] It is better to run back than to run badly.

units.la: Meliora praeoptanda] Cum aquila esse queas, inter graculos primas ne opta.
units.tr: Better things are to be preferred] Since you may be an eagle, do not wish to be first among jackdaws.

units.la: Meliora pejoribus mutare] Aurea aereis permutare. Glauci cum Diomede permutatio.
units.tr: To exchange worse things for better] To exchange gold for bronze. The exchange of Glaucus with Diomedes.

units.la: Meliorem habere successum] Aves meliores nancisci. Effugi malum, inveni bonum.
units.tr: To have a better outcome] To find better birds. I escaped evil and found good.

units.la: Mellitus] Melleus, melligenus succus, Plin. Mellillus, Plaut.
units.tr: Honeyed] Honeyed juice, Plin. Honeyed, Plaut.

units.la: Melodia] Concentus. Concentio. Harmonia. Dissimilium sonorum, aut vocum concordia. Symphonia. Symphoniae cantus, Cic. Plin. Consonantia vocum. Concentu sibi conveniens consonantia, Vitr. Concordia discors vocum. Modulamen avium, Ovid. Symphonia discors, Hor. Modulatum canticum. Modulatio, Quint. Modulamentum, Gell. Modulatus canorus, Sen. Concinentia, Macrob. Chroma. Consonantia, Boët. Modi musici, Quint. & absol. Modi, Cic. Moduli, Plin.
units.tr: Melody] Harmony. Concord. Concert. Agreement of unlike sounds or voices. Symphony. Symphonic song, Cic. Plin. Harmony of voices. Harmony that agrees with itself in concord, Vitr. Discordant concord of voices. The song of birds, Ovid. Discordant symphony, Hor. A modulated song. Modulation, Quint. Modulation, Gell. Melodious modulation, Sen. Harmony, Macrob. Chroma. Consonance, Boët. Musical modes, Quint. and absolutely. Modes, Cic. Melodies, Plin.

units.la: Melon] Pepo, Plin. Melopepo, Id. Matthiol.
units.tr: Melon] Pumpkin, Plin. Melopepo, Id. Matthiol.

units.la: Membratim] Incisim, Incisè, articulatim dividere, Cic. Artuatim concisum pecus, Firm.
units.tr: Limb by limb] To divide piece by piece, joint by joint, Cic. Cattle cut up limb by limb, Firm.

units.la: Membrum] Pars corporis. Artus, Cic.
units.tr: Limb] A part of the body. A joint, Cic.

units.la: Memento ] Memineris meminisse. Sine, Dixisti in me, sine, Plaut. Maneat altâ mente repostum, Virg. Me specta modò. Sine modò, Plaut.
units.tr: Remember ] "Remember to remember" (memineris meminisse). "Let it be; you said it against me, let it be" (Sine, dixisti in me, sine), Plaut. "Let it remain stored deep in the mind," Virg. "Only look upon me," Virg. "Just let it be," Plaut.

units.la: Meminisse] Memoriter meminisse. Memoria est. In mente est mihi, &c. Plaut. Commeminisse aliquid. Tenere aliquid. Tenere memoria, vel, Teneri memoriâ alicujus rei. Retinere memoriam alicujus, &, memoriâ aliquid. Servare, conservare memoriam. Custodire, completi memoriâ. Insidet aliquid in memoria, haeret. Haeret rei memoria, Cic. Infixum est animo. Insidet memoriae, Quint. Memini probè, Ter.
units.tr: To remember] To remember by heart. It is in memory. It is in my mind, etc., Plaut. To recall something fully. To hold something. To hold in memory, or to be held in someone's memory for something. To retain the memory of someone, and to keep something in memory. To keep and preserve the memory. To guard it, to be filled with memory. Something lingers in the memory and sticks fast. The memory of a thing clings, Cic. It is fixed in the mind. It sticks in the memory, Quint. I remember it well, Ter.

units.la: Memor ero] In mente insculpam. Non solùm dum animâ spirabo meâ, sed etiam cum mortuo, monimenta beneficii tui permanebunt. Nullum erit tempus, quo tui memoria moriatur. Id tabulis mandabo, ad memoriam posteri temporis sempiternam. Immortalitatis memoriâ prosequar. Quae fortuna? quis casus, tui memoriam potest delere? Quae unquam vetustas obruet? aut quae tanta tui memoriam delebit oblivio? Nulla obscurabit oblivio, Cic. Adamante notabo, Claud.
units.tr: I will remember] I will engrave it on my mind. Not only while I breathe, but even when I am dead, the monuments of your kindness will endure. There will be no time when the memory of you dies. I will commit this to tablets, for the everlasting memory of later times. I will pursue it with the memory of immortality. What fortune, what chance could destroy the memory of you? What age will ever overwhelm it? What oblivion will so blot out the memory of you? No oblivion will obscure it, Cic. I will mark it with adamant, Claud.

units.la: Memorabile quid] Memoria dignus. Dignum cedro, Cic. Insigne aliquid ad memoriam, Liv. Res ad memoriam crudelitatis insignis, Cicer. Dignum memoratu aliquid, Plin. Memorandus, Virg. Memoratissimus scriptor, Gell.
units.tr: Something memorable: worthy of remembrance. Worthy of cedar (oil), Cic. Something notable for memory, Liv. A deed notable for the memory of cruelty, Cicer. Something worth relating, Plin. Memorable, Virg. A most memorable writer, Gell.

units.la: Memorare] Commemorare, aliquid, & de. reducere in memoriam. Suggerere. Excitare aliquem ad memoriam alicujus rei. Revocare animos ad memoriam rei, Cic. Submonere alicujus. Redigere in memoriam alicui, Ter. Facere cere mentionem. Inducere aliquem in memoriam rei, Plaut. Inculcare & ingerere, Sen. Subjicere, Ter. Renovare memoriam, Quint. Aurem vellere, Virg. Pervellere, Sen. Vid. Mentionem facere.
units.tr: To mention: to call something to mind again, to bring back into memory. To suggest. To stir someone to the memory of something. To recall the minds of people to the memory of a thing, Cic. To remind someone of something. To bring something to someone's memory, Ter. To make mention. To bring someone into the memory of a thing, Plaut. To inculcate and inject, Sen. To subjoin, Ter. To renew the memory, Quint. To tug at the ear, Virg. To pluck sharply, Sen. See To make mention.

units.la: Memoria] Mens. Venit mihi in mentem. Memoriola, Cic. Rerum actarum retinentia, Lucr.
units.tr: Memory: mind. It comes into my mind. A little memory, Cic. The retention of things done, Lucr.

units.la: Memorialis liber, vid. Adversaria.
units.tr: A memorial book, see Notebooks.

units.la: Memoriter addiscere, vid. Ediscere.
units.tr: To learn by heart, see To learn thoroughly.

units.la: Memoriter recitare] Ex memoria exponere. Reddere aliquid sine scripto, Cic. Quae cogitaverat, ad verbum in agendo retulit. Complectamur animo, quae reddi fideliter possint, Quint. Meditatè tenere, Plaut.
units.tr: To recite from memory: to set forth from memory. To give back something without a written text, Cic. What he had thought out he delivered word for word in his speaking. Let us grasp in our minds what can be faithfully reproduced, Quint. To hold in mind by meditation, Plaut.

units.la: Mendacium] Mendaciunculum. Mentitio. Vanitas orationis, Cicer. Vanitudo, Plaut. Cedat vanitas veritati, Cic.
units.tr: Lie: a small lie. Lying. Falsity of speech, Cicer. Vanity, Plaut. Let vanity yield to truth, Cic.

units.la: Mendacium seipsum refellit] Mendacem oportet esse memorem. Mendacium aranea tela pellunt.
units.tr: A lie refutes itself: a liar ought to have a good memory. Lies are driven off like a spider's web.

units.la: Mendacia non durant ] Nullum mendacium veterascit. Parum virium habet falsitas.
units.tr: Lies do not last: no lie grows old. A falsehood has little strength.
