units.la: Mendax ] Expers veritatis, Cicer. Falsiloquus, falsidicus, mendaciloquus. Nullà fide es, Plaut. Insolens veri, Sen. Ex se fingit veluti araneus. Vir omnibus instructus dolis. Vir ex meris mendaciis conflatus atque compositus. Cretensi mendacior, Er.
units.tr: Liar: one devoid of truth, Cicer. Speaking falsely, lying, speaking lies. You are of no faith, Plaut. Unaccustomed to the truth, Sen. He makes things up out of himself, like a spider. A man furnished with every trick. A man built and put together out of pure lies. More lying than a Cretan, Erasmus.

units.la: Mendax est perjurus ] Qui mentiri solet, pejerare consuevit.
units.tr: A liar is a perjurer: one who is accustomed to lie is accustomed to forswear himself.

units.la: Mendicare] Precarium quaestum facere. Cogere stipem. Precariò rogare. Alienâ misericordiâ vivere, Cic. Colligere stipem, Liv.
units.tr: To beg: to make a living by begging. To collect alms. To ask as a favour. To live on another's pity, Cic. To collect alms, Liv.

units.la: Mendicus] Mendiculus, Cic. Mendicabulum circumforaneum, Apul. Ut rogator ostiatim petam, Plaut. Egens, Cic. Qui manum ad stipem porrigit, Sen. Fortunae decermina, in triviis stipem erogantia, Lipf. Col. Ad manticam res illi rediit.
units.tr: Beggar: a poor little beggar, Cic. A street-corner beggar, Apul. That I might go from door to door as a begging petitioner, Plaut. Needy, Cic. One who holds out his hand for alms, Sen. Fortune's decrees, dispensing alms at the crossroads, Lipsius, Cent. His affairs came down to the beggar's wallet.

units.la: Mendosus, vid. Vitiosus.
units.tr: Faulty, see Defective.

units.la: Mendum, vid. Error.
units.tr: Fault, see Error.

units.la: Mens] Animus, Tac. Mens animi vigilat, Lucr.
units.tr: Mind: spirit, Tac. The mind of the spirit keeps watch, Lucr.

units.la: Mente alienari] Alienari sensibus. Discedere à se, à sensi-bus. Effluit mihi mens. Vis eum quædam à sensu mentis abstraxit. Non constat mente, lingua, oratione, Cic. Sen-sibus ereptis mens excidit, Catul. Labi mente, Celf. Labi cerebro, Plaut. Exire de potestate, Cicer. Exire à se, Pe-tron.
units.tr: To be out of one's mind: to be estranged from one's senses. To depart from oneself, from one's senses. My mind slips away from me. Some force drew him away from the perception of his mind. He is not consistent in mind, tongue, or speech, Cic. With his senses snatched away, the mind fails, Catul. To slip from the mind, Celsus. To slip from the brain, Plaut. To go out of one's power, Cicer. To go out of oneself, Petron.

units.la: Mentis alienatio] Diminutio mentis, Suet. Stupor hominis, cordis, Cic.
units.tr: Derangement of mind: a lessening of the mind, Suet. The stupefaction of a man's heart, Cic.

units.la: Mentis compos] Compos animo. Sanus homo. Sanæ mentis homo. Mentis suæ est. Integer animi. Integrâ mente cæterisque sensibus. Constat mente, Cicer. Constat auribus, oculis, Liv. Constat mens in aliquo. Compos sui, Celf. Integer mentis. Penes te es? Hor. Sanus sim, ante insaniam. Fac apud te sis, Ter. Mentis sanæ compos, Ovid.
units.tr: Of sound mind: master of one's mind. A sane man. A man of sound mind. He is in his right mind. Whole in spirit. With a whole mind and the other senses. He is consistent in mind, Cicer. He is consistent in his ears and eyes, Liv. The mind stands firm in someone. Master of himself, Celsus. Whole of mind. Are you in your right mind? Hor. May I be sane before madness. See that you keep yourself in hand, Ter. Master of a sound mind, Ovid.

units.la: Mensa escaria] Mensa, abs. Cic. Cibilla, Varr. Gustatorium. Sigma, Mart. Stibadium, Plin. Sipont.
units.tr: Dining table: a table, Cic. A little food tray, Varr. A table for tasting. A semicircular couch, Mart. A couch for reclining at table, Plin.

units.la: Mensalis] Mensarius, Liv. Tricliniaris lectus. Escaria vasa, Plin. Escale argentum, Paul. Mod. Pransorium candelabrum, Quint.
units.tr: Of the table: of the bank-table, Liv. A dining couch. Dishes for food, Plin. Silver for the table, Paulus Modestinus. A lamp-stand for lunch, Quint.

units.la: Mensio, vid. Dimensio.
units.tr: Measuring, see Measurement.

units.la: Mensor] Geometres, Cic. Geodætes, Bud.
units.tr: Surveyor: a geometer, Cic. A land-measurer, Budé.

units.la: Menstrua, pl.] Hæmorrhois, Celf. Menses. Profluvium fœminarum, Plin. Lunare virus, Ovid. Muliebria, Hieron.
units.tr: Menses, pl.: haemorrhoids, Celsus. Menstruation. The flow of women, Plin. Lunar poison, Ovid. Female matters, Jerome.

units.la: Menstruatus, a, f. a. v.] Hæmorrhoicus, Firm. Menstruale animal mulier, Plin. Menstruans mulier, Pallad.
units.tr: Menstruating, adj.: suffering from haemorrhoids, Firm. A woman is a menstruating animal, Plin. A menstruating woman, Pallad.

units.la: Mensura] Modus agri, Plaut. Modulus calcei est pes, Hor. Spatium hominis à vestigio ad verticem, Plin.
units.tr: Measure: the size of a field, Plaut. The foot is the measure of a shoe, Hor. The span of a man from the sole to the crown, Plin.

units.la: Mensurare] Metiri agrum. Dimetiri terram. Demetari. Permetiri. Admetiri, Cic. Commetiri agrum, mensuras agrorum inire, Col.
units.tr: To measure: to measure a field. To measure out land. To measure off. To measure through. To measure up to, Cic. To measure a field together, to enter upon the measuring of fields, Columella.

units.la: Menta] Mintha. Hediosmos, Plin.
units.tr: Mint: mint. Sweet-smelling mint, Plin.

units.la: Mentagra] Mentigo, Col. Impetigo. Lichen. Fœdus cutis furfur. Impetix, Plin. Petigo, Lucil. Scabies est, tenui squammâ per corpus serpens, Gorr. Lichene laborare.
units.tr: Mentagra: a mentigo, Columella. Impetigo. Lichen. A foul skin scurf. Impetix, Plin. Petigo, Lucilius. It is a scab creeping over the body in a thin scale, Gorr. To suffer from lichen.

units.la: Mentionem alicujus rei facere] Mentionem facere de aliqua re, Cic. Inducere mentionem de aliquâ re. Inferre mentionem alicujus rei, Liv. Mentionem habere, Quint. Meminisse rei, Id. Memorare aliquid, de aliqua re. Refricare animum: memoriam pulcherrimi facti: aliquid dicendo, oratione. Incidere in mentionem alicujus. Renovare commemorando. Attingere nomen alicujus. Commemorare aliquid : de aliquâ re, Cic. Habere in sermonibus aliquid, Liv. Redigere aliquid in memoriam, Ter.
units.tr: To make mention of a thing: to make mention of some matter, Cic. To bring in mention of some matter. To bring in mention of a thing, Liv. To have mention, Quint. To remember a thing, Id. To recall something concerning some matter. To refresh the mind, the memory of a most noble deed, by saying something, in speech. To fall into mention of someone. To renew by recalling. To touch on someone's name. To call to mind something concerning some matter, Cic. To keep something in conversation, Liv. To bring something back to memory, Ter.

units.la: Mentionem facere hominis alicujus singularis ] Mentionem alicujus honorificam facere. Memoriæ alicujus operam dare. Memoriam alicujus cum charitate usurpare. Nec tui mentionem intermitti sinimus. Nos posterorum sermo colet, ac frequentabit. In assidua commemoratione est omnibus. Honoratorum virorum laudes memorentur. Colere absentem memoriâ. Virtutem alicujus gratâ memoriâ prosequi, Cic. Mentionem alicujus cum summo honore prosequi, Plin. Iun. Colere sermone, Sen.
units.tr: To make mention of a singular person: to make an honourable mention of someone. To take pains for someone's memory. To use someone's memory with affection. We do not allow mention of you to be dropped. The talk of posterity will honour and frequent us. He is constantly mentioned by everyone. Let the praises of honoured men be remembered. To cherish the absent by memory. To pursue someone's virtue with grateful memory, Cic. To pursue someone's mention with the highest honour, Plin. Jun. To cherish by speech, Sen.

units.la: Mentiri ] Mendacium facere, Quint. Mendacium dicere, mendacio fallere, facere centones, mendaciis onerare aliquem, Cic. Mentiri alicui ; in aliquem ; adversùs aliquem, Plaut.
units.tr: To lie: to make a lie, Quint. To tell a lie, to deceive by a lie, to make patchwork, to load someone with lies, Cic. To lie to someone; against someone; in opposition to someone, Plaut.

units.la: Mercatio. Mercator, vid. Negotiatio, &c.
units.tr: Trade, merchant, see Business, etc.

units.la: Mercenarius ] Mercenariorum omnium illiberales & sordidi quæstus, Cic. Ambactus, Fest. Conductitiæ operæ, Var. Conductæ operæ, Cic. Lucellaris, Lucellarius servus, Fest. Vid. Conductus.
units.tr: Hired, mercenary: all the mean and sordid gains of hired men, Cic. A dependant, Festus. Hired labour, Varro. Hired work, Cic. A slave who works for hire, a hireling slave, Festus. See Hired.

units.la: Merces] Pretium. Præmium. Mercedula. Arbitria funeris. Remuneratio, Cic. Ultrotributum, Sen. Enavatæ operæ præmium, Tac.
units.tr: Wage: a price. A reward. A small wage. A fee for arranging a funeral. A repayment, Cic. An extra tax, Sen. The reward of labour finished, Tac.

units.la: De mercede convenire ] Pacisci mercedem cum aliquo, Cicer. Statuere mercedem alicui. Statuere stipendium, Liv.
units.tr: To agree on a wage: to bargain a wage with someone, Cic. To fix a wage for someone. To fix a stipend, Liv.

units.la: Mercurius] ♆. Mundi pulmo.
units.tr: Mercury: ☿. The lung of the world.

units.la: Merda. Merdare, vid. Excrementum. Oletare.
units.tr: Dung. To dung, see Excrement. Befoul.

units.la: Merè, vid. Sincere.
units.tr: Purely, see Sincerely.

units.la: Merenda] Antecoenium, Apul. Ante coenam, Isid.
units.tr: Snack: a light meal before dinner, Apul. Before dinner, Isid.

units.la: Mereri ] Promerere & ri, malum, Plaut. Emereri honores, Propert. Commereri æstimationem, Cic. Meum meritum est. Quid commerui? Terent. Meritissimo ejus, meritum est. Quid commerui ? Terent. Meritissimo ejus, quæ volet, faciemus, Plaut. Committere pœnam, Cic. Manut.
units.tr: To deserve: to earn by service, to deserve evil, Plaut. To earn honours, Propertius. To deserve esteem, Cic. It is my merit. What have I deserved? Terence. We shall do whatever he most deservedly wishes, Plaut. To incur punishment, Cic., Manutius.

units.la: Mereri bene de aliquo] Promereri bene de aliquo. Gratiam alicujus inire, quærere, colligere, aucupari. Facere omni studio, ut, Ampletĉi officiis aliquem. Inire gratiam apud aliquem. Devincire sibi aliquem officiis. Beneficium collocare, ponere, Cic. Bonam operam alicui dare. Bene mereri, erga aliquem, Plaut. Demereri beneficio aliquem, Liv. Facere alicui volentia, Sallust. Vid. Benefacere.
units.tr: To deserve well of someone: to deserve well of someone. To win someone's favour, to seek, gather, or court it. To take every pains that... To bind someone to oneself by services. To bestow, place a benefit, Cic. To do someone a good service. To deserve well of someone, Plaut. To oblige someone with a benefit, Liv. To do someone welcome services, Sallust. See To do good.

units.la: Merentem bene, demereri convenit] Fricantem refrica.
units.tr: One who deserves well ought to be well deserved by: a rubber rubs the one rubbed.

units.la: Meretricè, vid. Libidinosè.
units.tr: Like a prostitute, see Lustfully.

units.la: Meretricius]Meritorius puer. Amatorius sermo. Incestum os, Cic. Fœmina propudiosa, Plaut. Vetitus amor, Ovid.
units.tr: Harlot-like: a boy for hire. Amatory speech. A shameless mouth, Cic. A shameless woman, Plaut. Forbidden love, Ovid.

units.la: Meretrix] Lupa. Propudiosa fœmina. Prostibulum, Prostituta fœmina. Quæ corpus alit corpore, Plaut. Mulier vulgata omnibus. Quæ se omnibus pervulgat, Cic. Omnium virorum mulier, Suet. Propudium. Quæstuosa mulier. Proseda, Plaut. Publicatâ pudicitiâ fœmina, Tac. Quæstuaria mulier, Sen. Scortum, Cic. Scortillum, Catul. Meretricula, Cic. Monstrum mulieris.
units.tr: Harlot: a she-wolf. A shameless woman. A brothel, a woman who is a prostitute. She who feeds her body with her body, Plaut. A woman common to all. She who gives herself up to everyone, Cic. A woman of all men, Suet. A shameless creature. A woman who earns by her trade. A proseda, Plaut. A woman whose chastity has been made public, Tac. A woman who works for gain, Sen. A whore, Cic. A little whore, Catul. A little harlot, Cic. A monster of a woman.

units.la: Meretrix formosa] Thais.
units.tr: Beautiful harlot: Thais.

units.la: Mergæ, vid. Furca.
units.tr: Forks, see Fork.

units.la: Mergere] Immergere aliquid ponto, Virg. Mergere se in mari, Cic. In flumen, Varr. Mersitare, Solin. Mersare, ex Col.
units.tr: To plunge: to plunge something into the sea, Virg. To plunge oneself into the sea, Cic. Into a river, Varro. To keep sinking, Solinus. To drown, from Columella.

units.la: Mergi] Mersari fluctibus, Catul. Haustæ mari naves, Liv. Submergi, Cic. Naufragus intereo, Ovid. Degravat meum unda caput. Implicat pedes, Propert.
units.tr: To be plunged: to be drowned by waves, Catul. Ships swallowed by the sea, Liv. To be submerged, Cic. I perish shipwrecked, Ovid. The wave weighs down my head. It entangles my feet, Propertius.

units.la: Merges] Manipulus frumenti, ex Serv. Virgil.
units.tr: Sheaf: a handful of corn, from Servius on Virgil.

units.la: Meridianus, de die] Meridialis hostia, Fest. Vid. Somnus pomeridianus.
units.tr: Of midday, of the day: a midday sacrifice, Festus. See Afternoon sleep.

units.la: Meridianus, de plagâ mundi] In meridiano orbe præcipuam obtinet nobilitatem. Meridiana orbis pars. Austrinus flatus, Col. Austrinum cœlum. Notius, Plin. Australis orbis. Antarcticus Polus, Cic. Ad meridiem spectans, Cic. Prona ad solem loca, Varr.
units.tr: Southern, of a region of the world: holds a chief place of nobility in the southern hemisphere. A southern part of the world. A south wind, Columella. A southern sky. The south-west wind, Plin. The southern world. The Antarctic Pole, Cic. Facing towards the south, Cic. Places sloping towards the sun, Varro.

units.la: Meridiè] Meridianò, Plin. Per medium diem repertus est. Medio diei, Tac.
units.tr: At midday: at midday, Plin. It was found in the middle of the day. In the middle of the day, Tac.

units.la: Meridies] Dies medius. In medios dormire dies,Hor. Sol adultus,Petron. Umbilicus diei, Plaut.
units.tr: Midday: the middle of the day. To sleep through the middle of the day, Hor. The sun grown up, Petron. The navel of the day, Plaut.

units.la: Meridies (2) Plaga meridionalis] Media diei regio, Lucr. Medius dies. Stabula ad medium conversa diem, Id.
units.tr: Midday (2), southern region: the region of the middle of the day, Lucr. The middle of the day. Stalls turned towards midday, Id.

units.la: Merito] Meritissimo Jure, jure & merito. Non injuriâ. Juste, justissimè. Ritè potest appellari sapientia. Legitimè, Cic. Nec injuriâ, Liv. Recte, Ter.
units.tr: Deservedly: most deservedly, by right. Rightly and deservedly. Not unjustly. Justly, most justly. One may rightly call it wisdom. Lawfully, Cic. Nor unjustly, Liv. Rightly, Ter.

units.la: Meritorius] Mercenarius testis. Vectigalis equus, Cicer. Conductitius, Varr.
units.tr: Meritorious: a mercenary witness. A horse paying tax, Cicer. Hired out, Varr.

units.la: Meritum] Meritissimum, Plaut. Promeritum, Lucr.
units.tr: Merit: most deserving, Plaut. Earned in advance, Lucr.

units.la: Meritus bene] Optimè de aliquo meritus. In beneficiis ad ærarium delatus, Cic. Beneficiarius, Veget.
units.tr: Having deserved well: having deserved very well of someone. Brought before the treasury for benefits, Cic. A beneficiary (a soldier excused from duties), Veget.

units.la: Mersio] Demersio, Macrob.
units.tr: Immersion: a sinking under, Macrob.

units.la: Merus, vid. Purus putus.
units.tr: Pure, see Pure, clean.

units.la: Merx] Res promercales, Col.Gell. Mercimonium, Plaut. Species, Amm.
units.tr: Merchandise: goods for sale, Col.Gell. Wares, Plaut. Kinds, Amm.

units.la: Meßis] Messio, Varr.
units.tr: Harvest: reaping, Varr.

units.la: Meta] Meta spatii novissima, Sen. Metula, Plin. Calx. Flexus, Cic. Cursor. Cretam prior contingit, Sen. Mors ultima linea rerum, Hor.
units.tr: Goal: the last turning-post of a course, Sen. A small turning-post, Plin. A limestone mark. A bend, Cic. A runner. He reaches Crete before the other, Sen. Death, the final goal of things, Hor.

units.la: Metam non attingere] A lineis excidere, Er.
units.tr: To not touch the goal: to fall off the lines, Er.

units.la: Metam fœni facere] In metas fœnum exstruere. Fœnum siccatum coarctare in struem. In metas exstruere, easque ipsas in angustissimos vertices exacuere. Exstruere in acervum stramenta, Col.
units.tr: To make a haystack: to pile hay into stacks. To press dried hay into a heap. To build up stacks and sharpen them to narrow peaks. To pile straw into a heap, Col.

units.la: Metallicus, subst.] Scrutator auri, Lucr.
units.tr: Metalworker, noun: a seeker of gold, Lucr.

units.la: Metallum] Fluida terra, solidataque aqua. Viscera terræ.
units.tr: Metal: liquid earth and solidified water. The bowels of the earth.

units.la: Meteora] Res superæ, Lucr.
units.tr: Heavenly phenomena: things above, Lucr.

units.la: Meteora ignita] Flammantia ostenta.
units.tr: Fiery meteors: blazing portents.

units.la: Metere] Facere messem. Supponere falcem maturis, Col. Demetere arva, Catul. Frumenta tempestivè decisa sunt. Secare Medicam, Col. Herbas, Virg. Succidere segetes, Virg. Desecare segetem cum stramentis, Liv.
units.tr: To reap: to make a harvest. To put the sickle to ripe crops, Col. To cut down fields, Catul. The grain was cut down at the right time. To mow clover, Col. To cut grass, Virg. To cut down crops, Virg. To cut the crop along with the straw, Liv.

units.la: Methodus] Modus, Ratio, Via ad aliquid, Cic. Breve compendium aliquid inveniendi, discendi, tractandi, docendi. Habitus, Keck. Ordo, Scal.
units.tr: Method: a manner, plan, or way to something, Cic. A brief shortcut for finding, learning, handling, or teaching something. Disposition, Keck. Order, Scal.

units.la: Metropolis] Mater urbium, Solin.
units.tr: Metropolis: mother of cities, Solin.

units.la: Metuendus, vid. Terribilis.
units.tr: Fearful, see Terrible.

units.la: Metuere] In metu esse. In metu aliquid ponere. Habere metum. Exanimari metu, Cic. Metum capere. Liv. Permetuere, Virg. Tentari metu. Præmetuere, Lucr. Madere metu, Plaut.
units.tr: To fear: to be in fear. To put something in fear. To have fear. To be paralysed by fear, Cic. To take fright, Liv. To fear greatly, Virg. To be seized by fear. To fear beforehand, Lucr. To be drenched with fear, Plaut.

units.la: Non metuo te ] Antea putabam te habere cornua. Hostes semper tales ne insequantur.
units.tr: I do not fear you: I used to think you had horns. Let enemies never pursue such men.

units.la: Metum pellere] Deponere timorem. Abstergere, depellere, pellere metum. Abjicere timorem, Cic. Pellere animo timorem, Plaut. Colligere se ex timore, Cæs. Mittere timorem, Virg.
units.tr: To drive out fear: to lay aside fear. To wipe away, drive off, or banish fear. To cast off fear, Cic. To drive fear from the mind, Plaut. To collect oneself from fear, Caes. To send away fear, Virg.

units.la: — Metus, vid. Timor.
units.tr: — Fear, see Dread.

units.la: Meum est] Ad me attinet, pertinet. Attingit me. Refert meâ, nostrâ, Cic.
units.tr: It is mine: it concerns me, it pertains to me. It touches me. It matters to my or our interest, Cic.

units.la: Mica] Momentum resinæ, Plin. Fragmina favorum, Col. Segmentum arenæ, Plin. Detrimentum, Varr.
units.tr: Crumb: a particle of resin, Plin. Fragments of honeycomb, Col. A grain of sand, Plin. A loss, Varr.

units.la: Micare ] Palpitat ignis, Stat. Vibrat mare. Perstringit aliquid aciem oculorum, Cic. Nictantia fulgura flammæ, Lucr. Coruscare, Virg. Vid. Promicare.
units.tr: To flicker: the fire flickers, Stat. The sea quivers. To strike the sight of the eyes, Cic. Flashing flames of lightning, Lucr. To glitter, Virg. See To flash out.

units.la: Migrare] Demigrare ex agris in urbem, Liv. Commigravit habitatum huc, Plaut. Commutare locum, Lucr. Mutare sedem, solum. Mutari civitate. Transferre se in aliam domum Transire. Vertere solum, Cic. Mutare sedem ex sede, Plin. Transmigrare, Suet. Mutes te cum omni familiâ, Varr.
units.tr: To migrate: to move away from the fields into the city, Liv. He has moved his home here, Plaut. To change place, Lucr. To change one's seat or soil. To be changed in citizenship. To transfer oneself to another house. To cross over. To change one's country, Cic. To change one's seat from one seat to another, Plin. To transmigrate, Suet. May you move with your whole household, Varr.

units.la: Migratio] Demigratio, Æmil. Prob. Mutatio loci, Cic.
units.tr: Migration: emigration, Aemil. Prob. A change of place, Cic.

units.la: Miles] Manus, Virg. Auctoratus spoliorum venator. Homo de castris. Nulla fides pietasque viris, qui castra sequuntur, Lucan. Mactatores hominum.
units.tr: Soldier: a hand, Virg. A hired hunter of spoils. A man from the camp. No loyalty or piety among men who follow the camp, Lucan. Slaughterers of men.

units.la: Milespugnax] Mars, Marticola, Martis pullus, Ovid. Militiæ gnarus. Impiger, Tac. Martialis. Sub Martis stellâ natus, Sipont.
units.tr: Warlike soldier: Mars, a worshipper of Mars, a chick of Mars, Ovid. Skilled in war. Tireless, Tac. Martial. Born under the star of Mars, Sipont.

units.la: Miles emanens] Desertor miles, Cæs. Emansor, Scal. Infrequens miles, Fest. Erro, Virg.
units.tr: Deserting soldier: a soldier who deserts, Caes. A runaway, Scal. A rare soldier, Fest. A wanderer, Virg.

units.la: Militem conscribere] Centuriare. Decuriare, Cic. Delectum militum instituere, Cæs. Censere. Censionem facere, Plaut. Delectum facere, Quint. Agere, habere, Plin. Conscribere exercitum, Cæs.
units.tr: To enlist soldiers: to draw up into centuries. To draw up into decuries, Cic. To institute a levy of soldiers, Caes. To take a census, Plaut. To hold a levy, Quint. To hold, have, Plin. To enrol an army, Caes.

units.la: Militare] Mereri equo. Mereri in bello stipendia. Mereri, facere stipendia, Cic. Tolerare militiam & grave Martis onus, sub aliquo Magistro, Virg. Militare militiam, militiâ, Plaut. Militiam colere. Præmia militiæ pulverulenta sequi, Ovid. Navare operam militarem, Liv.
units.tr: To serve as a soldier: to earn pay as a horseman. To earn one's pay in war. To earn, to serve out one's term, Cic. To endure soldiering and the heavy burden of Mars under some commander, Virg. To serve as a soldier, Plaut. To cultivate soldiering. To follow the dusty rewards of soldiering, Ovid. To perform military service, Liv.

units.la: Militaris] Militarius, Plaut. Duellica proles, Lucr. Manipularius, Suet.
units.tr: Military: martial, Plaut. Warlike offspring, Lucr. Of the maniple, Suet.

units.la: Militaris scientia] Res militaris. Rei militaris scientia, virtus. Res, Disciplina, Virtus bellica, Cic. Militiæ disciplina, Id. Ars duellica, Plaut. Armatura, Veget. Ars armaturæ. Armorum gestus, Amm. Militia, Tac. Castrensis ratio, Cic.
units.tr: Military science: military affairs. The science and virtue of military affairs. The matter, discipline, and warlike virtue, Cic. The discipline of soldiering, Id. The art of war, Plaut. Armament, Veget. The art of arms. The handling of weapons, Amm. Soldiering, Tac. The military method, Cic.

units.la: Militia] Labor militiæ, Ovid. Decora militiæ, Liv. Latrocinium, Plaut. Sacramentum, Iuv.
units.tr: Soldiering: the toil of soldiering, Ovid. The glories of soldiering, Liv. Brigandage, Plaut. The military oath, Juv.

units.la: Milium] Miliaria herba, Plin.
units.tr: Millet: a millet-like grass, Plin.

units.la: Milliare] Milliarium, mille passuum, millia quadraginta abesse, (scil. passuum) Cic. Milliarense, seu milliarium spatium, Vopisc. Milliarium aureum, Suet.
units.tr: Mile: a milestone; a thousand paces. To be forty miles away, Cic. A mile-long stretch, Vopisc. A golden milestone, Suet.

units.la: Millus] Millum, Varr. Collare canum, Id. Armilla, Passer. ex Propert. Armillati canes colla.
units.tr: Collar: a dog's collar, Varr. An armlet, Passer, from Propertius. Dogs with armlets on their necks.

units.la: Milvus] Milvius, Plaut. Ter. Milvus, Lamb. Circanea avis, Fest.
units.tr: Kite: a kite, Plaut. Ter. A kite, Lamb. A Circaean bird, Fest.

units.la: Mimus, vid. Histrio.
units.tr: Mime, see Actor.

units.la: Mina] Comminatio, minatio. Intentus palmarum, minæ, Cic. Eminatio, minaciæ, Plaut.
units.tr: Threat: a warning or menace. A threatening gesture of the palms, Cic. A threatening, Plaut.

units.la: Minæ præcedunt pugnam] Imbrem tonitus antecedit.
units.tr: Threats come before battle: thunder goes before the rain.

units.la: Minaciter] Minanter, Ovid. Minitabundus petebat, Liv.
units.tr: Threateningly: menacingly, Ovid. He sought to attack with threats, Liv.

units.la: Nec tam minaciter] Bona verba quæso, melius ominare. Dii meliora.
units.tr: Not so threateningly: I beg you, good words; speak better omens. May the gods grant better things.

units.la: Minari] Jactare minas. Insectari aliquem minis. Minitari alicui mortem, flammam. Ferro ignique patriæ minitari. Proponere alicui minas, periculum, Cic. Intendere minas alicui, Ter. Eminari. Interminari vitam alicui, Plaut. Præminari, Apul. Minas spirare. Intentare arma, Liv. Intentare & minari, Cic.
units.tr: To threaten: to brandish threats. To harass someone with threats. To threaten someone with death or fire. To threaten the fatherland with sword and fire. To hold out threats or danger to someone, Cic. To aim threats at someone, Ter. To threaten. To threaten someone's life, Plaut. To threaten in advance, Apul. To breathe threats. To hold out arms, Liv. To hold out and threaten, Cic.

units.la: Minari extrema] Ignem spirare. Igni ferroque minari, Cic.
units.tr: To threaten the utmost: to breathe fire. To threaten with fire and sword, Cic.

units.la: Minax] Minacissimus, Suet. Minatorius, Amm. Terriloquus, Lucr.
units.tr: Threatening: most threatening, Suet. Menacing, Amm. Speaking terror, Lucr.

units.la: Minaces timidi] Canes timidi vehementius latrant.
units.tr: Timid threateners: timid dogs bark most fiercely.

units.la: Minerval] Didactrum magistro, Cel. Rhod.
units.tr: School fee: a fee paid to the teacher, Cel. Rhod.

units.la: Mingere ] Micturire, Priscian. Hunc perminxere calones, Hor. Reddere humorem, Plin. Vid. Mejere.
units.tr: To urinate: to pass water, Priscian. The camp-followers urinated on him, Hor. To release moisture, Plin. See To pass water.

units.la: Miniaceus] Miniarius, Plin.
units.tr: Vermilion-coloured: of red lead, Plin.

units.la: Miniatus] Minianus, Varr. Miniatula cera, Cic. Mineus circulus in collo, Apul. Minius, Beroald.
units.tr: Painted with red lead: painted red, Varr. Painted wax, Cic. A red-lead circle on the neck, Apul. Red-lead, Beroald.

units.la: Minimè gentium, vid. Nullatenus. Saltem.
units.tr: By no means, see Not at all. At least.

units.la: Minimum quid] Mica, Catul. Guttula argenti consilii, Plaut.
units.tr: A very little thing: a crumb, Catul. A drop of silver judgement, Plaut.

units.la: Minimum] Minimè probandum, Cic. Minimopere, Priscian. Paucissima septem ova, Col. Vid. Saltem.
units.tr: Least: not to be approved in the least, Cic. In the least degree, Priscian. Very few, seven eggs, Col. See At least.

units.la: Minimus] Pumilia mole. Parvissimus, Lucr. Momentosus, Quint.
units.tr: Smallest: of tiny bulk. Very small, Lucr. Of small moment, Quint.

units.la: Ex minimis maxima] Minutula pluvia imbrem parit.
units.tr: Greatest from the smallest: a tiny drizzle produces a shower.

units.la: Minister] Administer. Ministrator. Administrator, Cic. Præminister, Macrob.
units.tr: Minister: an assistant. A servant. An administrator, Cic. A chief servant, Macrob.

units.la: Minister publicus] Actor publicus,Tac. Accensi Magistratuum, apud Rom. Varr. Liv. Officialis, Apul. Stator. Viator. Servus publicus. Ex cohorte Prætoris, Cic.
units.tr: Public minister: a public agent, Tac. Attendants of magistrates among the Romans, Varr. Liv. An official, Apul. An usher. A messenger. A public slave. From the praetor's cohort, Cic.

units.la: Ministerium]Ministratio. Servile officium facere. Supremum officium, Tac. Obsequium, Cic.
units.tr: Ministry: service. To perform servile duty. The last duty, Tac. Obedience, Cic.

units.la: Ministrare] Ministrum se præbere in. Ministratorem alicui exhibere. Operam alicui navare. Egregiam operam alicui dare. Officium præstare, exsequi,Cle. Enavare operam, Ter. Operam alicui impendere. Optimè alicui operam locare, Col. Optimam alicui dare operam,Plaut. Obsequium præstare alicui, Plin. Iun. Subire ministerium, Virg. Administrare alicui, Spart. Præministrare alicui, Gell. Obsequor tibi in hoc, Bud. Supremo officio in aliquem fungi, Curt.
units.tr: To minister: to show oneself a minister to someone. To render service to someone. To devote effort to someone. To give someone excellent effort. To perform a duty, carry it out, Cic. To devote effort, Ter. To expend effort on someone, Plaut. To render obedience to someone, Plin. Iun. To undertake a ministry, Virg. To administer to someone, Spart. To minister to someone beforehand, Gell. I obey you in this, Bud. To discharge the final duty to someone, Curt.

units.la: Minor natu] Minor annis,Vlp. Minor annorum tot,Var.
units.tr: Younger by birth: under so many years of age, Vlp. Under so many years old, Var.

units.la: Minor etiam nocere potest] Et meum telum cuspidem habet acuminatum. Et mihi sunt vires,& mea tela nocent. Ingenio pollet, cui vim natura negavit.
units.tr: The lesser can still do harm: my weapon too has a sharp point. I too have strength, and my weapons do harm. He excels in wit, to whom nature has denied strength.

units.la: Minorum non est æstimatio,nisi majora absint] Lampyrides non sunt conspicuæ, nisi nocte.
units.tr: Small things are not seen unless larger ones are absent: fireflies are not conspicuous except at night.

units.la: A minori ad majus] Ab armis lusoriis, ad decretoria.
units.tr: From the less to the greater: from playing weapons to deadly ones.

units.la: Ad minora inhabili, majora imponi non possunt ] Capram portare non possum, & imponitis bovem.
units.tr: What is unsuited to small things cannot be laid on larger ones: I cannot carry a goat, and you put an ox on me.

units.la: Minuere aliquid] Diminuere numerum, Caes. Imminuere summam. Derogare aliquid de dignitate alicujus. Redigere ad paucos. Ad pauciores reducere. Subtrahere materiam, Cic. Demere aliquid de cibo, aut, ex cibo, Cels. Extenuare famam, Liv. Attenuare curas, Ovid. Curtare rem, Perf. Deintegrare aliquid, Cæcil.
units.tr: To diminish something: to lessen the number, Caes. To reduce the sum. To detract something from someone's dignity. To bring down to a few. To reduce to fewer. To withdraw material, Cic. To take something from food, or from the diet, Cels. To weaken a reputation, Liv. To lessen cares, Ovid. To curtail a matter, Perf. To take a part away from something, Caecil.

units.la: Minuitur aliquid] Decedit de summa, opibus, Liv. Decrescit dies, morbus, Cels. Minuuntur curæ, Ovid. Experientibus quarta pars decocta erat, Liv. Quæ nata sunt, ea omnino denasci ajunt, Non. Varr. Vid. Imminuitur.
units.tr: Something is diminished: it falls from the sum or from resources, Liv. The day, or a disease, decreases, Cels. Cares diminish, Ovid. For those who had tried it, a quarter had been boiled away, Liv. Those things that have been born, they say, are altogether unborn again, Non. Varr. See It is lessened.

units.la: Minùs] Deliquum. Delicuum, Fest. Plaut. Secius, Apul.
units.tr: Less: a failing. A failing, Fest. Plaut. More moderately, Apul.

units.la: Minus promittere, plus dare ] Præstat lucem dare è fumo, quàm fumum è luce.
units.tr: To promise less and give more: it is better to give light out of smoke than smoke out of light.

units.la: Minus qui non potest, nec majus poterit ] Qui celocem regere nequit, onerariam petit?
units.tr: He who cannot do less will not be able to do more: he who cannot steer a light boat, does he make for a freighter?

units.la: Minùs necessarium] Minùs in usu necessarium, Cic. Parergon, & Parergum, Vitr.
units.tr: Less necessary: less necessary in use, Cic. A by-work, and a by-work, Vitr.

units.la: Minutal] Isitium, vel Incium, Macrob. Insicium, Apul. Tucetum, Id. Perf. Protrimentum. Intritum, Apul.
units.tr: Minced meat: or minced, Macrob. Minced, Apul. Ground, Id. Perf. Crushed. Ground up, Apul.

units.la: Minute] Minutiùs, minutatim. Incise. Incisim, Cic. Minutim, minutissimè, Col. Cæsuratim, Suet. Concisè, Quint. Assulatim, Plaut.
units.tr: Minutely: more minutely, bit by bit. Cut up. Cut into pieces, Cic. Bit by bit, very minutely, Col. In small pieces, Suet. Concisely, Quint. In chips, Plaut.

units.la: Minutio] Attenuatio suspicionis. Extenuatio oratoria rerum. Decessio aliquarum rerum, de summa, Detractio molestiæ. Diminutio civium: de bonis privatorum. Imminutio corporis. Levatio vitiorum. Deductio pecuniæ, Cic.
units.tr: Diminution: a weakening of suspicion; a rhetorical softening of things; a withdrawal of some part from the total; a removal of annoyance; a diminishing of citizens, or of private property; a lessening of the body; a relief from faults; a deduction of money. Cic.

units.la: Minutus] Tenuis pluvia, Virg. Concisus. Perminutus, Cic. Vegrandes oves, Varr. Articulosus, Quint. Incrementi parvi animalia, Col. Incrementi minuti pisces, Pallad. Minutulus, Plaut. Minutissimus, Suet.
units.tr: Small: a fine rain, Virg. Cut up, broken into pieces. Very small, Cic. Very small sheep, Varr. Jointed, Quint. Small animals in growth, Col. Small fish in growth, Pallad. Rather small, Plaut. Very small, Suet.

units.la: Mirabilis] Mirus, mirificus, permirus. Admirabilis. Mirandus. Habet admirationem. Visendus ornatus. Monstrosus, Cic. Mirificissimus, Ter.
units.tr: Wonderful: marvellous, wonderful, very wonderful. Admirable. To be marvelled at. Worthy of admiration. A splendour worth seeing. Monstrous, Cic. Most wonderful, Ter.

units.la: Mirabiliter] Mirè, mirificè. Admirabiliter. Mirum in modum, Cic. Mirius, Varr. Mirum quantum, Liv. Miris modis, Plaut. Nihil tam monstrosum cogitari potest, Id. Monstrosè, Cic. Insanum! bonam, Plaut.
units.tr: Wonderfully: marvellously, wonderfully. Admirably. In a wonderful manner, Cic. More wonderfully, Varr. Wonderfully much, Liv. In wonderful ways, Plaut. Nothing so monstrous can be imagined, Id. Monstrously, Cic. Madness! Good heavens, Plaut.

units.la: Miraculum] Prodigium. Portentum, ostentum, Cic. Triportenta Deorum, Varr.
units.tr: Miracle: a prodigy. A portent, an omen, Cic. The three portents of the gods, Varr.

units.la: Miracula non in cujusvis gratiam patrat Deus] Fluvius non semper fert secures.
units.tr: God does not work miracles for the sake of everyone: A river does not always carry axes.

units.la: Mirari] Mirari aliquid; mirari si; mirari quòd. Admirari aliquem; de aliquo; aliquid in aliquo. Satis admirari non queo. Admiratione affici. Incessit, cepit me admiratio. Suspicere eloquentiam. Permirum mihi accidit, Cic. In admiratione esse. In admirandis, in admiratione ponere, Plin. Demirari, Ter. Emirari, Hor. Caput quassare. Oculis attonitis cernere. Intentis oculis contemplari. Oculis immobilibus contueri.
units.tr: To wonder: to wonder at something; to wonder if; to wonder that. To admire someone; for something; something in someone. I cannot wonder enough. To be struck with admiration. Amazement seized me. To look up to eloquence. It happened to me most wonderfully, Cic. To be in admiration. To place among things to be admired, Plin. To be astonished, Ter. To marvel at, Hor. To shake the head. To look with astonished eyes. To gaze with fixed eyes. To behold with motionless eyes.

units.la: Miratio] Mirabilitas. Admirabilitas. Admiratio, Cic. Suspectus sui, Sen.
units.tr: Wondering: wonderfulness. Admirableness. Admiration, Cic. One who is suspicious of himself, Sen.

units.la: Mirator] Admirator antiquitatis, Quint. Miratrix vetustas sui, Lucan. Mirabundi Pœni, Liv. Mirio, Tertull.
units.tr: Admirer: an admirer of antiquity, Quint. Antiquity, admiring of itself, Lucan. The Carthaginians, marvelling, Liv. Wondering, Tertull.

units.la: Miratus id sum valde] Id mihi me penè eripuit.
units.tr: I was greatly amazed at this: That nearly took me out of myself.

units.la: Mirè, vid. Mirabiliter.
units.tr: Wonderfully: see Wonderfully above.

units.la: Mirum!] Mirum quantum! Liv. Immane! quantum discrepat, Hor. Immensum! quantum memoria vigens, Amm. Mirum quin grex venalium in cistella infuerit una, Plaut. Habet, quod exclamet admiratio, Arnob.
units.tr: How strange!: How wonderful! Liv. Monstrous! How much it differs, Hor. Immense! How much vigour of memory, Amm. It is strange that a flock of slaves for sale was not in one little basket, Plaut. Wonder has something to cry out, Arnob.

units.la: Miscere] Permiscere aliquid cum aliquo. Admiscere hæc cum illis nolo. Confundere, Cic. Remiscere vera falsis, Hor. Futare vinum, Fest. Emiscere vinum, Manil. Interponere aquam vino, Mart. Interjicere sagittarios inter equites, Cæs. Commiscere aliquid cum aliquo, Cic. Promiscere, Macrob.
units.tr: To mix: to mix something together with something. I do not want to mix these things with those. To confuse, Cic. To blend truth with falsehood, Hor. To stir wine, Fest. To mix wine, Manil. To add water to wine, Mart. To place archers among the cavalry, Caes. To mingle something with something, Cic. To mix indiscriminately, Macrob.

units.la: Miser] Calamitosus, miserandus, miserabilis, prostratus, afflictus. In miseria est. Nihil fieri potuit miserius. Fortuna egens. Ærumnosus. Quem miseriæ & ærumnæ omnes premunt. Misellus, Cic. Coopertus miseriis, Sallust. Fessi rerum, Virg. Miserula anima, Seren. Diom. Omnium copiarum, atque opum, auxilii, præsidii viduitas nos tenet, nec ulla specula est, quæ salutem afferat, Plaut. Acherusia vita stultorum, torum, Lucr. Genio malevolente natus, Plaut. Genio ad miseriam natus. Natus ferendis miseriis, Ter. Vid. Afflictus.
units.tr: Wretched: calamitous, pitiable, miserable, prostrate, afflicted. He is in misery. Nothing could be more wretched. Fortune in need. Full of woe. Whom all miseries and hardships press down. Poor little, Cic. Covered with miseries, Sallust. Weary of affairs, Virg. A poor little soul, Seren. Diom. The lack of all resources, wealth, help and protection holds us, and there is no lookout that brings safety, Plaut. The Acherusian life of fools, Lucr. Born under a malevolent genius, Plaut. Born to misery under a genius. Born to bear miseries, Ter. See Afflicted.

units.la: Miserum ne irriseris] Calamitoso risus etiam injuria est.
units.tr: Do not mock the wretched: Laughter is an injury even to the calamitous.

units.la: Miserandus] Vel hosti miserandus, Suid. Miserabilis casus. Deploranda calamitas. Illacrymabilis, Lev. Ingemiscenda clades, Amm. Hostis miseraturus, si vidisset.
units.tr: Pitiable: pitiable even to an enemy, Suid. A pitiable accident. A calamity to be lamented. Not to be wept over, Lev. A disaster to be groaned over, Amm. An enemy who would have pitied, had he seen.

units.la: Misera est vita] Homo a miseria vitam auspicatur.
units.tr: Life is wretched: Man begins his life with misery.

units.la: Misere] Miserabiliter, miserandum in modum. Calamitose. Indigne nunc eges, quondam felix, Cic. Miseris modis, Lucr. Miseriter, Catul.
units.tr: Wretchedly: pitiably, in a pitiable manner. Calamitously. Now you are in need undeservedly, once happy, Cic. In wretched ways, Lucr. Wretchedly, Catul.

units.la: Misereri] Miserari aliquem; sortem alicujus. Affici alicujus casu; moveri, commoveri misericordia. Ex tuis incommodis magnam animi capio molestiam. Misericordia adductus fecit. Frangi misericordia. Allici ad misericordiam, misericordiam capere aetatis alicujus, misericordiam alicui tribuere, impertiri, Cic. Miseret me, miseresct me, commiseresct me alicujus, Ter. Commiserari interitum alicujus, Gell. Dii nos respiciunt, Ter. Cic. Jupiter aspice nos, Virg. Indolere malis alicujus, Ovid. Vellem, quae velles, Sen. Lipf.
units.tr: To pity: to pity someone; someone's lot. To be affected by someone's misfortune; to be moved, stirred with compassion. I feel great distress of mind at your troubles. Led by compassion, he did it. To be broken by compassion. To be drawn to compassion, to feel compassion for someone's age, to show compassion to someone, to grant, bestow, Cic. I pity me, it pities me, he pities me, Ter. To lament someone's death, Gell. The gods look upon us, Ter., Cic. Jupiter, look upon us, Virg. To grieve at someone's misfortunes, Ovid. I would wish what you would wish, Sen., Lips.

units.la: Miseri homines] Huc homunculi quanti estis! Horum aliquanti sunt, dum recogito! Diis nos homines, quasi pilas habent, Plaut. Ludus Deorum homo, Plaut. Hoccine seculum? O Jupiter, hanccine vitam! Ter.
units.tr: Wretched men: Oh, how great you are, little mannikins! Some of them are, as I consider! Men, the gods have them as if they were balls, Plaut. Man is the plaything of the gods, Plaut. Is this the age? O Jupiter, is this the life! Ter.

units.la: Miseria] Calamitas, Cic. Profundum calamitatis, Apul. Miserrimorum labes, Non. Miseritudo, Accius.
units.tr: Misery: calamity, Cic. The depth of calamity, Apul. The downfall of the most wretched, Non. Wretchedness, Accius.

units.la: Miseria premi] Infesta fortuna; inopia premi, Varr. Col. Te miseriae & aerumnae premunt omnes. Tabescere in calamitate. Comminutae sunt opes ejus. Venit in calamitatem. Comminutus re familiari. Extenuatissimae sunt meae copiolae. Infracta res, Cic. In egestate esse propter inopiam. Degere vitam in egestate. Duriore fortuna conflictari. Multis & magnis incommodis conflictari. Egere rebus omnibus. In summa mendicitate esse, Id. Defectus, lapsus facultatibus, Vlp. Egetur acriter. Ab re perire, Plaut. Lassae resejus, Ovid. Vid. Pauperari. MiserICordia ] Ægritudo ex alterius miseriâ. Miseratio. Commiseratio, Cic. Miserycordiæ motus, Vlp. Cordolium, Plaud.
units.tr: To be oppressed by misery: hostile fortune; to be oppressed by want, Varr., Col. Miseries and hardships press upon you all. To waste away in calamity. His resources are diminished. He comes to ruin. Reduced in property. My small means are very much reduced. A ruined condition, Cic. To be in want because of poverty. To pass life in want. To be struggled with by harsher fortune. To be beset with many great troubles. To lack everything. To be in utter beggary, Id. Deprived, having lost one's means, Ulp. He is sorely in need. To perish from want, Plaut. Weary of his affairs, Ovid. See To be poor. Pity: distress at another's misery. Compassion. Sympathy, Cic. Motion of pity, Ulp. Heartache, Plaud.

units.la: Misericors] Misericors in aliquem. Qui misericordiâ commovetur. Qui alienis miseriis commovetur, Cic. Misericordior, Plaut. Boni viri lacrymabiles. (Facile lacrymantur.)
units.tr: Compassionate: compassionate towards someone. One who is moved by compassion. One who is moved by others' miseries, Cic. More compassionate, Plaut. Good men are easily moved to tears. (They weep easily.)

units.la: Miserum! ] Miserabile! Navibus, infandum! amissis Ah silice in nuda connixa reliquit, Virg. Indignum! Ovid. Rem miseram!
units.tr: Pitiful!: Pitiable! With the ships lost, unspeakable! She left him, clinging to the bare rock, Virg. Shameful! Ovid. A wretched affair!

units.la: Missio ] Missus, caf.
units.tr: Dismissal: a dismissed one, Caes.

units.la: Miftim, vid. Confusè.
units.tr: Mixed: see Confusedly.

units.la: Miftura ] Permistio. Congeries variarum rerum. Silva rerum & verborum, Cic. Miscellanea, pl. Iuv. Farrago libelli, Id. Colluvio rerum, Liv. Satuta, Fest. Commistum, Cat.
units.tr: Mixture: a blending together. A heap of various things. A forest of things and words, Cic. A miscellany, Juv. A medley of a little book, Id. A heap of things, Liv. A satura, Fest. A mixed thing, Cat.

units.la: Miftura rerum] Sunt bona mixta malis; sunt mala mista bonis. Mel nulli sine felle datur.
units.tr: A mixture of things: Good things are mixed with bad; bad things are mixed with good. Honey is given to no one without gall.

units.la: Mistus] Miscellus, Suet. Miscellaneus, Apul. Promiscua connubia. Confusaneus, Gell. Conseminalis, &, conseminea vinea, Col.
units.tr: Mixed: miscellaneous, Suet. Miscellaneous, Apul. Marriages of mixed kind. Confused, Gell. Sown together, and a vine sown together, Col.

units.la: Mitescere, vid. Mansuefieri.
units.tr: To grow mild: see To become tame.

units.la: Mitigare, vid. Placare.
units.tr: To soothe: see To appease.

units.la: Mitis] Permitis, Col. Columbâ mitior. Vid. Mansuetus.
units.tr: Mild: very mild, Col. Milder than a dove. See Gentle.

units.la: Mites vexantur] Mitissimus & afflictissimus Moses.
units.tr: The meek are harassed: Moses, the meekest and most afflicted.

units.la: Mittere ] Missum facere, Cic. Mandare alicui salutem, Ovid. Legare famulum aliquò, Catul. Vid. Dimittere. Ablegare. Omittere.
units.tr: To send: to give up, Cic. To send greetings to someone, Ovid. To send a servant somewhere, Catul. See To dismiss. To send away. To omit.

units.la: Mobilis] Qui semper movetur, ut cœlum, Cic. Motorius, Donat. Ambulatorius, Hort. Ambulatilis, Vitr. Agitabilis ager, Ovid.
units.tr: Mobile: that which is always in motion, like the heavens, Cic. Moving, Donat. Walking, Hort. Movable, Vitr. A field that can be ploughed, Ovid.

units.la: Mobilitas, mobiliter, vid. Celeritas, &c.
units.tr: Mobility, mobilely: see Swiftness, etc.

units.la: Moderamen] Gubernatio. Administratio rei familiaris. Tractatio vocis. Temperatio Reip. Rectio rerum. Gubernaculum. Clavus. Habenæ, Cic. Regimen, Liv. MagistVerium, Col. Ordinatio orientis, Suet.
units.tr: Control: direction. Management of household affairs. Handling of the voice. Regulation of the state. Governance of affairs. Helm. Rudder. Reins, Cic. Government, Liv. Management, Col. Ordering of the east, Suet.

units.la: Moderari] Moderare, Salust. Modum unicuique rei statuere, constituere, definire. Sententiam tanquam aliquod navigium ex Reip. tempestate moderari, non est inconstantis. tis. Moderari alicui rei, & aliquid. Modum quendam & ordinem in vita adhibere. Facere modum lugendi. Dirigere utilitatem honestate. Exigere jus ad veritatem. Aures vocem modulantur. Omnia gubernes ac moderere tuâ prudentiâ. Temperare æqualiter aliquid, Cic. Imponere rei modum, Liv. Modificari, Gell. Præmoderari, Id. Ad mediocritatem aliquid revocare. Tenere mediocritatem, Cic. Adhibere temperamentum, Plin.
units.tr: To moderate: to moderate, Sall. To set, establish, or define a limit for each thing. To steer one's opinion like a ship through the storm of the commonwealth is not the mark of an inconstant man. To govern something and to control a thing. To bring some measure and order into life. To set a limit to mourning. To direct usefulness by honour. To direct right towards truth. The ears regulate the voice. Govern and rule all things by your prudence. To temper something evenly, Cic. To impose a limit on a matter, Liv. To be modified, Gell. To moderate beforehand, Id. To bring something back to the mean. To keep the mean, Cic. To apply a restraint, Plin.

units.la: Moderatè] Moderatissimè. Intra modum. Finitè. Intra legem epulari, Cic.
units.tr: Moderately: most moderately. Within measure. Finitely. To feast within the law, Cic.

units.la: Moderata omnia] Moderata durant. Modico frui, mera suavitas. Extra cachinum sit risus. Boni pastoris est tondere pecus, & non deglubere. Nullum violentum diuturnum.
units.tr: All moderate things: Moderate things endure. Enjoy a little; pure sweetness. Let laughter be short of uproar. It is the duty of a good shepherd to shear the flock, not to flay it. No violence is lasting.

units.la: Moderatio] Temperatio vitii. Modus in perturbationibus. Modus lugendi. Tractio vocis, Cic. Temperamentum linguæ, Liv.
units.tr: Moderation: restraint of a fault. Measure in emotions. Measure in mourning. Regulation of the voice, Cic. Self-control of the tongue, Liv.

units.la: Moderator, vid. Rector.
units.tr: Moderator: see Ruler.

units.la: Modestè] Moderatè dictum. Sedatè, temperatè, temperatius, moderatius. Tenere se suis finibus. Servare modum, tenere. Modicè facere, Cic. Composite, Col. Compositius, Tac. Circumcisè, Suet.
units.tr: Modestly: said in moderation. Calmly, temperately, more temperately, more moderately. To keep oneself within one's bounds. To keep measure, to hold back. To act with moderation, Cic. Neatly, Col. More neatly, Tac. Concisely, Suet.

units.la: Modeste age] Modulo te ac pede metire tuo. Intra pellicu-lam tuam te contine. Intra proprios limites consiste. Noris quàm sit tibi curta supellex. Pedibus ingredere, si natare non didicisti. Fluvius cum mari certat?
units.tr: Behave modestly: Measure yourself by your own rule and foot. Keep yourself within your own skin. Stand within your own limits. You know how short your baggage is. Walk on foot if you have not learned to swim. Does a river contend with the sea?

units.la: Modestia] Moderatio dicendi, in dicendo. Comitas in moribus. Urbanitas, Cic. Temperies morum, Stat.
units.tr: Modesty: moderation of speech, in speaking. Courtesy in manners. Urbanity, Cic. Good temper of manners, Stat.

units.la: Modestus] Modestissimus adolescens. Moderatus vir. Temperati mores. Permodestus homo. Sedatus animus, Cic. Verecunda translatio, Id. Modicum gaudium, domiti oculi, Plaut.
units.tr: Modest: a most modest young man. A moderate man. Temperate manners. A very modest man. A calm mind, Cic. A modest figure of speech, Id. Small joy, subdued eyes, Plaut.

units.la: Modicè] Perpaulum declinare. Leviter saucius. Leviter inflexum. Perleviter commotus. Aliquantulùm deflectere. Paulùm differunt inter se, Cic. Permodicè, Col. Aliquantùm es timida, Plaut. Vid. Mediocriter.
units.tr: Moderately: to deviate a very little. Slightly wounded. Slightly bent. Slightly disturbed. To deflect a little. They differ little from one another, Cic. Very moderately, Col. You are a little timid, Plaut. See Moderately.

units.la: Modicum, vid. Exiguitas.
units.tr: Moderate: see Smallness.

units.la: Modicus, vid. Parvus, modestus.
units.tr: Moderate: see Small, modest.

units.la: Modò, vid. Nunc. Tantùm. Modulari, i. e. modulatè canere] Incinere ore varios modos, Propert. Ad harmoniam, symphoniâ, modulatè canere, Cic. Canere in modum, Catul. Doctissimè & gratissimè cantillare, Apul. Personat vicinitas cantu vocum, Cic. Ædes pulsu nervorum & articulorum, flatilique sonitu resonant, Amm. In numerum ludere, Virg.
units.tr: Only, merely: see Now. Only. To modulate, i.e. to sing in measured tones: To sing various tunes with the mouth, Propert. To sing melodiously in harmony and symphony, Cic. To sing in the manner of, Catul. To sing most learnedly and most pleasantly, Apul. The neighbourhood resounds with the song of voices, Cic. The buildings resound with the striking of strings and joints and the sound of flutes, Amm. To play in rhythm, Virg.

units.la: Modulatio] Modulatum canticum, Quint. Vid. Melodia.
units.tr: Modulation] A modulated song, Quint. See Melody.

units.la: Modus] Ratio dicendi. Via ad aliquid. Via litigandi. Latronum ritus. Conditio. Consilium de toto genere belli. Genus vitæ. Mos, Cic. Tenor, Liv. Genus dicendi, Quint.
units.tr: Manner] A way of speaking. A way to something. A way of disputing. The custom of robbers. A condition. A plan concerning the whole kind of war. A way of life. Custom, Cic. Tenor, Liv. A style of speaking, Quint.

units.la: Mœcha. &c. vid. Adulter, &c.
units.tr: Adulteress, etc. See Adulterer, etc.

units.la: Mœchari, vid. Libidinari, Adulterare.
units.tr: To commit adultery, see To indulge lust, To commit adultery.

units.la: Mœrere] In mœrore jacere. Mœrore se conficere; confici, affligi, urgeri. In mœstitia esse. In luctu est senatus. Contrahere animum, Cic. Incessit mœstitia animos, Liv. Confecta est senio; squallet tota civitas. Contrahi animo. Dolere. In dolore esse, Cic. In fermento esse, Plaut. Vid. Tristari.
units.tr: To grieve] To lie in grief. To wear oneself out with sorrow; to be worn down, afflicted, oppressed. To be in sadness. The senate is in mourning. To draw in the spirit, Cic. Sadness has seized their minds, Liv. She is worn out by old age; the whole city is squalid. To be drawn in spirit. To feel pain. To be in pain, Cic. To be in a ferment, Plaut. See To be sad.

units.la: Mœror] Mœstitia. Ægritudo est contractio animi, Cic. Senium, Id. Mœstitudo, Acci. Contractiuncula animi, Cic.
units.tr: Grief] Sadness. Distress is a contraction of the spirit, Cic. Old age, Id. Sorrow, Acc. A slight contraction of the spirit, Cic.

units.la: Mœstè] Mœstiùs lacrymis Simonideis, Catul. Tristiùs, Cic.
units.tr: Sadly] More sadly than with Simonides' tears, Catul. More sadly, Cic.

units.la: Mœstus] Mœrens. Mœrore profligatus, perditus. Os in mœstitiam flexum, Cic. Immodicus mœroris, Tac. V. Tristiu.
units.tr: Sorrowful] Grieving. Crushed and ruined by sorrow. A face turned to sadness, Cic. Immoderate in grief, Tac. See Sad.

units.la: Mola] Machina frumentaria, Vlp. Ubi lapis lapidem terit, Plaut.
units.tr: Mill] A machine for grinding grain, Ulp. Where stone grinds stone, Plaut.

units.la: Mola alata] Mola pneumatica, En. Mola pinnata, Philand. Machina spiritalis.
units.tr: Winged mill] A pneumatic mill, En. A feathered mill, Philand. A spiritual machine.

units.la: Mola manuaria] Incusus lapis, Virg. Mola trusatilis, Gell. Suspensa, Col. Vlp. Trapetum suspensum, Id. Trapes. Mola olearia, Varr.
units.tr: Hand mill] A stone anvil, Virg. A hand-turned mill, Gell. Hanging, Col. Ulp. A hanging press, Id. A press. An olive mill, Varr.

units.la: Molere] Molâ aliquid frangere, terere, Plin. Molæ operam dare, Cic. Commolere, Col. Emolere. Frendere fruges, Pacuv. Permolere, Hor. Lapidem lapide terere, Lucr.
units.tr: To grind] To break or rub something down with a mill, Plin. To work at the mill, Cic. To grind together, Col. To grind down. To gnash the grain, Pacuv. To grind thoroughly, Hor. To rub stone with stone, Lucr.

units.la: Moles, vid. Magnitudo.
units.tr: Mass, see Magnitude.

units.la: Molestare aliquem] Molestiam alicui afferre, aspergere, exhibere. Sum gravis alicui. Habeo aliquem acerbum, Cic. Urere aliquem, Liv. Facere ægrè alicui. Odiosus esse alicui pergo. Ter. Excruciare animi aliquem. Interere aliquem. Stimulus ego nunc sum tibi, Plaut. Ducere serram, Varr.
units.tr: To trouble someone] To bring trouble to someone, to inflict or cause annoyance. I am a burden to someone. I hold someone in bitterness, Cic. To burn someone, Liv. To cause someone displeasure. I persist in being tiresome to someone, Ter. To torment someone's mind. To ruin someone. Now I am a goad to you, Plaut. To draw a saw, Varr.

units.la: Molestè, vid. Importunè, &c, Molestum mihi est.
units.tr: Troublesomely, see Importunately, etc. It is troublesome to me.

units.la: Molestia] Præmolestia. Asperitas rerum. Acerbitas sententiarum. Stridor ferræ cùm acuitur. Stomachus, Cic. Cordolium, Plaut. Asperitudo sermonis, Apul. Dividia mentis, Plaut. Lamb. Fest. Acerbum, Ovid. Hulcus, Cicer. Senium, Titin. Sartago loquendi, Pers.
units.tr: Annoyance] Foretaste of trouble. Harshness of things. Bitterness of opinions. The screech of a saw being sharpened. Irritation, Cic. Heartburn, Plaut. Harshness of speech, Apul. Distress of mind, Plaut. Lamb. Fest. Bitterness, Ovid. An ulcer, Cicer. Old age, Titin. A frying pan of speech, Pers.

units.la: Molestum mihi est] Molestiam capio, traho ex. Molestiâ afficior ex hac re. Afficit me ex te solicitudo. Molestè, permolestè, atrociter ferre aliquid, Cic. Indignissimè ferre, Iul. Cap. Hæres vitæ me saturant. Dividiæ est mihi illæc res. Hoc peracescit. Cerebrum mihi misero excutiunt tua dicta. Lapides loqueris, Plaut. Quod me mactat, Lamb.
units.tr: I am annoyed] I take offence, I am vexed by it. I am disturbed by this matter. Anxiety from you troubles me. To bear something with annoyance, very much so, fiercely, Cic. To bear it most indignantly, Iul. Cap. The clinging things of life sate me. This business is a torment to me. This is galling me. Your words shake my wretched brain. You speak stones, Plaut. What is killing me, Lamb.

units.la: Molestus] Permolestus homo. Odiosus labor. Submolestus. Acerbus interitus. Importunus. Perodiosus, Cic. Amari sales, Quint. Dividiæ magnæ res, Plaut. Importunissimus homo, Cic. Crambe recoctâ molestior, Fr.
units.tr: Troublesome] A very troublesome man. Tedious labour. Somewhat troublesome. A bitter death. Importunate. Very hateful, Cic. Bitter wit, Quint. Vexing matters are great, Plaut. The most importunate man, Cic. More troublesome than cabbage reheated, Fr.

units.la: Moliri aliquid] Conceptare aliquid, Amm. Res magnas movere. Struere mendacium. Struere odium in aliquem. Versare mentem ad omnem malitiam & fraudem, Cicer. Vid. Machinari.
units.tr: To contrive something] To plot something, Amm. To set great matters in motion. To devise a lie. To stir up hatred against someone. To turn the mind to every malice and fraud, Cicer. See To devise.

units.la: Moliri occultè malum] Monstrum alere. Struere aliquid, Ter. Versare mentem ad malitiam, Cic. ut supr.
units.tr: To plot evil secretly] To nurse a monster. To devise something, Ter. To turn the mind to malice, Cic. as above.

units.la: Molitor] Molendinarius, Paul. IC. Magister molarius, vel molæ, ex Varr.
units.tr: Miller] A man who works a mill, Paul. IC. A master of the millstone, or of the mill, from Varr.

units.la: Mollescere] Lentescit cicer. Remollescit cera, Cic. Tenerescere, Plin. Macerescere. Flaccescere, Col. Ponere, deponere duritiem.
units.tr: To grow soft] Chickpeas soften. Wax softens, Cic. To grow tender, Plin. To grow soft and weak. To wither, Col. To lay aside hardness.

units.la: Mollire] Emollire, Plin. Præmollire femina, Quint. Malaciffare, Plaut. Sen. Commitigare caput alicui, Ter. Inflectere sensus alicujus, Virg.
units.tr: To soften] To soften, Plin. To soften a woman beforehand, Quint. To make soft, Plaut. Sen. To soothe someone's head, Ter. To bend someone's feelings, Virg.

units.la: Mollis] Præmollis. Lentus calamus, Plin. Lentus ut cera. Infimâ auriculâ mollior, Cic. Tener, præter, Virg. Plin. Vitilis cucurbita, Id. Edurus, Virg. Casaub. Cereus, Hor. Malacus, Plaut. Molliculus, Id. Molliccllus, Catul. Moliusculus, Plin. Iun. Somno mollior, Clem. Alex.
units.tr: Soft] Very soft. A pliant reed, Plin. Soft as wax. Softer than the lowest ear, Cic. Tender, Virg. Plin. A pliant gourd, Id. Hard, Virg. Casaub. Waxen, Hor. Soft, Plaut. Rather soft, Plaut. Delicate, Catul. Somewhat soft, Plin. Iun. Softer than sleep, Clem. Alex.

units.la: Mollitia] Mollities. Teneritudo, Plin. Mollitudo, Cic. Teneritas, Id. Malacia lecti. Plaut. Lentor, Col.
units.tr: Softness] Softness. Tenderness, Plin. Softness, Cic. Tenderness, Id. The softness of a bed, Plaut. Sluggishness, Col.

units.la: Momentaneus, vid. Brevis ratione durationis.
units.tr: Momentary, see Brief in respect of duration.

units.la: Momento] Uno momento. Puncto temporis. Uno puncto, Cic. Tempore puncto. Parvo momine, Lucr. Momento fusi, Liv. Momento horae, Hor. Perlevi momento, Cic. Oculi ictu. Puncto temporis maximarum rerum momenta vertuntur. In ipso articulo temporis.
units.tr: In a moment] In one moment. In a point of time. In one instant, Cic. In a moment of time. In a small moment, Lucr. In a moment poured out, Liv. In the moment of an hour, Hor. In a very slight moment, Cic. In the blink of an eye. In a point of time the course of the greatest matters is turned. At the very joint of time.

units.la: Momentum]Momen, Lucr. Unum punctum temporis, Cic.
units.tr: Moment] A moment, Lucr. One point of time, Cic.

units.la: Momenti res magni] Permagni, maximi momenti. In hoc fortunae Graeciae sitae sunt, Cic. Grande operae pretium est. Iuv. Propter quod vadimonium deseri possit, Plin. Mare & pelagus, (pro re longe lateque diffusa) Lucr. Moles mali, Id. Mons aquae, Virg.
units.tr: Matters of great moment] Of very great, very highest importance. On this hang the fortunes of Greece, Cic. It is a great reward for the labour, Juv. On account of which a recognizance may be forfeited, Plin. The sea and the deep (for a thing spread wide and far), Lucr. A mass of evil, Id. A mountain of water, Virg.

units.la: Momus] Improbator, Apul. Carptor. Vitupero, Gell. Vitilitigator, Plin. Litigator, Cato. Obstrigillator, Varr.
units.tr: Momus] A censurer, Apul. A carper. A critic, Gell. A quibbler, Plin. A litigator, Cato. A hair-splitter, Varr.

units.la: Monarcha] Orbis terrae princeps. Principum princeps. In cjus unius potestate ac moderatione vertuntur omnia. Cujus dominatu omnia tenentur. Ad unum omnia deferunt, Cic. Uni omnia tribuere, Id.
units.tr: Monarch] Ruler of the world. Prince of princes. In his single power and control all things turn. By whose lordship all things are held. They refer all things to one, Cic. To attribute all things to one, Id.

units.la: Monarchia] Dominatio, Cic.
units.tr: Monarchy] Lordship, Cic.

units.la: Monarchia optimum regimen] Imperatorum multitudo Cariam perdidit.
units.tr: Monarchy the best form of government] A multitude of commanders destroyed Caria.

units.la: Monasterium, vid. Claustrum.
units.tr: Monastery, see Cloister.

units.la: Monere, vid. Adhortari.
units.tr: To admonish, see To exhort.

units.la: Monere seipsum] Balneator ero mihi ipsi.
units.tr: To admonish oneself] I shall be my own bath attendant.

units.la: Monere facilius est, quam moneri] Facile, cum valemus, recta consilia aegrotis damus.
units.tr: It is easier to admonish than to be admonished] When we are well, we readily give sound advice to the sick.

units.la: Moneta] Concisum argentum in titulos faciesque minutas, Iuv.
units.tr: Money] Silver cut into small pieces, with inscriptions and little faces, Juv.

units.la: Monitio, vid. Admonitio.
units.tr: Admonition, see Admonition.

units.la: Monitor, vid. Adhortator.
units.tr: Admonisher, see Exhorter.

units.la: Monitorius] Hortatorius, Bud. Hortativus, Quint. Protrepticus sermo, Id. Ausion.
units.tr: Admonitory] Exhortatory, Bud. Exhortative, Quint. A protreptic speech, Id. Ausion.

units.la: Monoculus, vid. Cocles.
units.tr: One-eyed, see Cocles.

units.la: Mons] Jugum, Tac. Montium praecelsa juga.
units.tr: Mountain] A ridge, Tac. The lofty ridges of the mountains.

units.la: Monstrare aliquid alicui] Commonstrare, Cic. Demonstrare re villam, Plaut. Præter monstrare, Gell. Ostendere aliquid digitis, Ovid. Digitum, dextram ad aliquid intendere, Cic. Vid. Ostendere.
units.tr: To point something out to someone] To show in addition, Cic. To point out a farm to someone, Plaut. To show besides, Gell. To show something with the fingers, Ovid. To point a finger or right hand at something, Cic. See To show.

units.la: Monstratio, vid. Ostensio.
units.tr: Showing, see Display.

units.la: Monstrator] Index regionum, Amm. Stylus horologii solaris, Macrob.
units.tr: Guide] An indicator of regions, Amm. The gnomon of a sundial, Macrob.

units.la: Monstrose]Prodigiosè, monstrificè, Plin. Prodigialiter, Hor.
units.tr: Monstrously] Prodigiously, monstrously, Plin. Prodigiously, Hor.

units.la: Monstrosus] Portentosus, Cic. Prodigiosus. Monstrifer, Monstrificus. Portentosissimus, Sen. Prodigialis, Claud. Monstrificabilis, Non. Lucil. Quovis monstro monstrosior, Er. Pro monstro est, Plaut. Inter monstra numerandus, Petron. Monstri simile est, Ter. Pro monstro accepit, Val. M. Monstruosus, ut aliqui.
units.tr: Monstrous] Portentous, Cic. Prodigious. Monstrous. Most portentous, Sen. Prodigious, Claud. Monstrous, Non. Lucil. More monstrous than any monster, Erasm. It is a monster, Plaut. To be counted among the monsters, Petron. It is like a monstrosity, Ter. He took it as a monster, Val. M. Monstruosus, as some write.

units.la: Monstrum] Hominum pecudumque portenta præter naturam. Portentosa ex homine & pecude nata, Cic. Prodigiosus partus. Adulterium naturæ, Plin. Ostentum. Contra naturam aliquid genitum, Vlp.
units.tr: Monster] Prodigies of men and beasts beyond nature. A portentous thing born of man and beast, Cic. A prodigious birth. An adultery of nature, Plin. A portent. Something born contrary to nature, Ulp.

units.la: Montanus] Monticola. Ovid. Montivagus, Lucr. Montigena, Sipont. Petro, Fest. Rupices, Tertul.
units.tr: Mountain-dwelling] A little mountaineer, Ovid. Wandering on mountains, Lucr. Mountain-born, Sipont. A rock-dweller, Fest. Cliff-dwellers, Tertul.

units.la: Montosus] Montosa regio, Cic. Montana, (scil. loca) Liv. Ardua, pl. Virg.
units.tr: Mountainous] A mountainous region, Cic. Mountain (sc. places), Liv. Steep (in the plural), Virg.

units.la: Monumentum] Monimentum virtutis, sapientiæ, crudelitatis, &c. Cic. Memoria, Tac. Memoriæ, Gell. Memoraculum, Apul.
units.tr: Monument] A monument of virtue, wisdom, cruelty, etc., Cic. A memorial, Tac. Memorials, Gell. A memorial, Apul.

units.la: Mora] Exigui temporis usura. Intervallum temporis, Cic. Interjectus, Tac. Tractus temporis, Paterc. Morula, Sipont.
units.tr: Delay] The use of a short time. An interval of time, Cic. An interval, Tac. A stretch of time, Paterc. A little delay, Sipont.

units.la: Mora in negotiis noxia] Diligentia profuit, mora semper obfuit. Nocuit semper differre paratis.
units.tr: Delay is harmful in business] Diligence has always profited; delay has always been a hindrance. Delay has always harmed those who are ready.

units.la: Moralitas] Ethologia. Ethopœia, Quint. Morum & affectuum effectio, Robert.
units.tr: Morality] Ethology. Ethopoeia, Quint. The shaping of manners and affections, Robert.

units.la: Moratus bene] Vir moribus domesticis, ac nostrorum hominum urbanitate limatus. Urbanus homo, Cic. Ingenuatus, Plaut. Moribus commodis, antiquis, Er.
units.tr: Well-mannered] A man polished by domestic manners and the courtesy of our people. A courteous man, Cic. Well-bred, Plaut. Of agreeable, old-fashioned manners, Erasm.

units.la: Morbidus] Morbosus, Cat. Valetudinarius. Opportunus morbis. Opportunum corpus morbis, Cels. Corpore affecto, Liv.
units.tr: Sickly] Diseased, Cat. Valetudinarian. Prone to illness. A body prone to illness, Cels. With the body affected, Liv.

units.la: Morbus] Invaletudo. Ægra valetudo. Valetudo, abs. &, ValcValetudo incommoda, mala, infirma, valetudinis gravitas, vitium, Cic. Pertinax valetudo, Plin.Iun. Ingravescens, Vlp. Infensa, Tac. Ægritudo corporis, Plin. Affectus, Celf.
units.tr: Disease] Ill health. Sickly health. Bad, unsound, weak health; the seriousness of ill health, a fault, Cic. Persistent ill health, Plin. Iun. Growing worse, Ulp. Hostile, Tac. Sickness of the body, Plin. An affliction, Cels.

units.la: Morbo affici, vid. Ægrotare.
units.tr: To be affected by disease, see To be sick.

units.la: Morbo eodem laborare] In eodem valetudinario jacere.
units.tr: To suffer from the same disease] To lie in the same sickroom.

units.la: Mordax] Ipso Momo mordacior, Er.
units.tr: Biting] More biting than Momus himself, Erasm.

units.la: Mordere] Arrodere morsu, Sidon. Laniare dentibus, Liv. Lacerare morsu, Cic. Petere, mandere morsu. Suspensis dentibus catulos tractat canis, Lucr. Morsicare, Apul. Admordere aliquem, Propert. Imprimere notam labris. Illidere dentem alicui rei, Hor. Figere dentem in aliquid, Ovid.
units.tr: To bite] To gnaw with the teeth, Sidon. To tear with the teeth, Liv. To lacerate with a bite, Cic. To seize and chew with a bite. The dog handles its puppies with teeth held carefully, Lucr. To nibble, Apul. To bite at someone, Propert. To press a mark with the lips. To dash the teeth against something, Hor. To fix a tooth in something, Ovid.

units.la: More fit] More. De more, Virg. Ex more, Ovid. Mos habetur, Tac. Solet scribi, Cic. Usitatissimum est, Vlp. Pro more patrio. More hominum facit. Non insolens istud facis. Pro vetere consuetudine, solens meo more facere. Nihil praeter solitum. Usu publico receptum est, Eraf. Hoc apud Scythas solenne est, Suet. Obtinuit consuetudo. Usus recepit. Vertit in morem. Vid. Pro consuetudine, sub consuetudo.
units.tr: It is the custom] By custom. According to custom, Virg. According to custom, Ovid. It is observed, Tac. It is usually written, Cic. It is most common, Ulp. According to ancestral practice. It is like the custom of men. You do not do this unusually. According to old custom, accustomed to do as I usually do. Nothing beyond the ordinary. Received by public use, Erasm. This is solemn among the Scythians, Suet. Custom has prevailed. Use has received it. It has become a custom. See According to custom under Custom.

units.la: Mores boni, vid. Civilitas.
units.tr: Good manners, see Civility.

units.la: Mores mali] Mores feri. Mores lapsi ad mollitiem, Cic. Ingenii, Id. Suo ingenio vivere coepit, Liv. Desidentes mores, Id.
units.tr: Evil manners: Fierce manners. Manners sunk into softness, Cic. Of disposition, Id. He began to live according to his own disposition, Liv. Declining morals, Id.

units.la: Mores non semper respondent natalibus] Vir, ut est optimis prognatus majoribus, ita pessimis praeditus moribus.
units.tr: Manners do not always match birth: A man born of the best ancestors may be endowed with the worst manners.

units.la: Mori] Mortem obire. Occumbere morti, mortem, morte. Obire diem suum. Demori. Emori. Emigrare è vita. Demigrare hinc : ex vita : ab hominibus. Migrare ex hac vita : de vitâ : in coelum. Exire de vita. Excedere vitâ ; à vita ; de vitâ. Recedere, desciscere à vita. Cedere vitâ, è vita. Discedere à vita ; ex vita. Ad inferos proficisci. Decedere. Vitam cum morte commutare. Conficere extremum diem morte. Conficere cursum vitae Vinculis corporis se relaxare. E vinculis corporis, tanquam è carcere evolare. Occidere & exstingui. Ponere vitam. Satisfacere naturae. Reddere vitam pro Rep. Reddere spiritum patriae. Naturam satietate viven-di explere. Potiri fatorum. Abire è vita. Profundere, edere animam, vitam. Edere, effundere extremum spiritum. Effla-re animam ; extremum halitum, Cic. Abire è medio, Ter.
units.tr: To die: To meet death. To succumb to death. To go to one's end. To go to one's day. To die off. To die out. To emigrate from life. To depart hence, from life, from men. To migrate from this life, out of life, to heaven. To go out of life. To withdraw from life, from life, out of life. To give way to life, out of life. To depart from life, out of life. To set out for the underworld. To pass away. To exchange life for death. To finish the last day by death. To finish the course of life. To loosen oneself from the bonds of the body. To fly out of the bonds of the body as out of a prison. To perish and be extinguished. To lay down life. To satisfy nature. To give life for the state. To give up one's spirit to one's country. To fill nature by satiety of living. To take possession of one's fates. To depart from life. To pour out, to give forth the soul or life. To breathe out one's last spirit, one's last breath, Cic. To go out of the way, Ter.

units.la: Obire, occubare morte, Suet. Excedere è medio, Ter. Abire in communem locum. Anima abest. Vitam corpore seclu-dere. Animum amittere, Plaut. Concedere, & Concedere vitâ. Agere inter homines desiit. Finire vitam. Mortalita-tem ; supremum diem explere, Tac. Concedere fato, Plin. Iun. naturæ, Salust. Placidâ compôstus pace quiescit, Virg. Ad plures penetrare, Plaut. Efflare vitam, Sil. Mortis adire iter, Proper. Calcare viam leti, mortis gradum, Hor. Ultimum spiritum reddere, Paterc. Exspirare, Liv. Exspirare animam, Virg. Digredi vitâ, mundo, Amm. Denasci, Varr. Exuere animam, Ovid. Exuere se animo, Sen. Occidere morte æternâ, Val. Arg. Recedere ab oculis, Plin. Absumi morte, Tac. Anima illum defecit. Animam edidit, amisit reliquit, Cic. Facere finem vitæ, Lucr. Fato functus est. In fata concessit, Liv. Implere finem vitæ, Tac. Ad finem mortalitatis concedere, Suet. Curriculum animæ decurrere. Fabulæ extremum actum addere. Fungi diem Fungi fato &c. Perfungi fato, Liv.
units.tr: To meet death, to fall in death, Suet. To pass out of the midst, Ter. To go to the common place. The soul is gone. To shut life off from the body. To lose one's spirit, Plaut. To yield, and to give way to life. He has ceased to be among men. To end life. To fill out mortality or the last day, Tac. To yield to fate, Plin. Iun., to nature, Salust. Composed in peaceful calm he rests, Virg. To penetrate to many, Plaut. To breathe out life, Sil. To set out on the path of death, Propert. To tread the way of death, the step of death, Hor. To give up the last breath, Paterc. To breathe out, Liv. To breathe out the soul, Virg. To depart from life, from the world, Amm. To be born again, Varr. To cast off the soul, Ovid. To strip oneself of the mind, Sen. To perish in eternal death, Val. Arg. To withdraw from the eyes, Plin. To be consumed by death, Tac. His soul failed him. He gave up the soul, lost it, left it, Cic. To make an end of life, Lucr. He has performed his fate. He has yielded to fate, Liv. To fulfil the end of life, Tac. To yield to the end of mortality, Suet. To run through the course of the soul. To add the last act to the play. To perform the day; to perform by fate, etc. To finish one's fate, Liv.

units.la: Moribundus] Vicinus morti. Animam agit. Capularis est. Capulo adhæret, Er.
units.tr: Dying: Near to death. He is breathing his last. He is fit for the bier. He clings to the bier, Er.

units.la: Morositas] Intolerantia morum, Suet. Rusticitas, Quint. Rus merum, Plaut. Immodestia, Id. Ruditas morum.
units.tr: Peevishness: Intolerance of manners, Suet. Rusticity, Quint. Pure countryside, Plaut. Immodesty, Id. Roughness of manners.

units.la: Morosus] Submorosus. Difficilis, Cic. Intractabilis animus, Sen. Totus echinus, asper. Ipsa morositate morosior, Er. Vid. Rudis moribus.
units.tr: Peevish: Somewhat peevish. Difficult, Cic. An intractable spirit, Sen. A hedgehog all over, prickly. More peevish than peevishness itself, Er. See "Rude in manners."

units.la: Mors] Mortes. Fatum. Exstinctio. Excessus fatalis è vita. Dissolutio. Obitus, Cic. Letum, Lucr. Ultimus fati dies, Val. Max. Exitus, ultima necessitas, suprema, Tac. Mortalitas, Vlp. Supremitas, Amm. Fatalis mora, Petron. Decretoria hora. Finis miseriæ. Cineres, Mart.
units.tr: Death: Deaths. Fate. Extinction. The fated departure from life. Dissolution. Decease, Cic. Death, Lucr. The last day of fate, Val. Max. The exit, the final necessity, the supreme hour, Tac. Mortality, Vlp. Finality, Amm. The fated delay, Petron. The decisive hour. The end of misery. Ashes, Mart.

units.la: Mors malorum finis] Mortui non dolens, mors molestiarum remedium.
units.tr: Death is the end of evils: The dead man does not grieve; death is the remedy for troubles.

units.la: Mortem precedere] Folia cadunt, post cadent arbores.
units.tr: To precede death: Leaves fall, afterwards the trees will fall.

units.la: Mors semper exspectanda] Omnem crede diem tibi diluxisse supremum, Hor.
units.tr: Death is always to be expected: Believe that every day has dawned for you as your last, Hor.

units.la: Vsque ad mortem] Usque ad rogos. Usque ad extremum spiritum.
units.tr: Unto death: Even to the funeral pyres. Even to the last breath.

units.la: Mortales sumus omnes] Commorandi non habitandi locus datur, Sen. Homines foliis similes. Homines quoque moriuntur. Cui nasci contigit, mori restat. Fata manent omnes. Flos, cinis, omnis caro. Quis fluvius est, quem non recipiat mare? Plaut. Omnia orta occidunt, Salust. Mors sceptra ligonibus aequat, Hor. Aequat omnes cinis. Impares nascimur, pares morimur, Sen. Nascentes morimur, finisq; ab origine pendet, Manil. Mors etiam saxis, marmoribusq; venit, Auson. Omnium versatur urna. Mors est indeclinabile nomen. Leti via calcanda semel. Tros Rutulusve suat, nullo discrimine.
units.tr: We are all mortal: A place is given for sojourning, not for dwelling, Sen. Men are like leaves. Men too die. He to whom it has been granted to be born, it remains for him to die. The fates await all. Flower, ash, all flesh. What river is there that the sea does not receive? Plaut. All things that arise also fall, Salust. Death levels sceptres with mattocks, Hor. Ash levels all. We are born unequal, we die equal, Sen. We are born dying, and the end depends on the origin, Manil. Death comes even to rocks and marbles, Auson. The urn of all is shaken. Death is an indeclinable noun. The path of death must be trodden once. Whether Trojan or Rutulian, he sews, with no distinction made.

units.la: Mortalis] Animal mortale, dissolubile, dividuum. Caducum corpus, Cic. Commortalis natura, Col. Capularis senex, Lucil. Occiduus, Ovid.
units.tr: Mortal: A mortal, perishable, divisible animal. A frail body, Cic. A mortal nature, Col. An old man ready for the bier, Lucil. Setting in the west, Ovid.

units.la: Mortuis maledicere] Mortuos rursus occidere. Flagellare mortuum. Cum larvis luctari. Mortuo leoni insultare.
units.tr: To speak ill of the dead: To kill the dead again. To flog a dead man. To wrestle with ghosts. To insult a dead lion.

units.la: Mortuus] Morte absumptus, Tac. Demortuus. Morte deletus. Funus, Cic. Intermortuus, Suet. Perfunctus fato, Liv. Exsors vitae. Exanimis. Cinis, Virg. Exanimatus, Liv. Conclamata corpora, Lucan. Positus. Ereptus, Ovid. Absentes. Plures, Plaut.
units.tr: Dead: Taken away by death, Tac. Dead and gone. Destroyed by death. A funeral, Cic. Half-dead, Suet. Discharged by fate, Liv. Without life. Lifeless. Ashes, Virg. Breathless, Liv. Bodies given up for lost, Lucan. Laid out. Snatched away, Ovid. The absent. Many, Plaut.

units.la: Mortuus est] Fuit. Vixit, Plaut. Caret vita Catone, Lucan. (i. e. mortuus est Cato.)
units.tr: He is dead: He was. He lived, Plaut. Cato lacks life, Lucan. (that is, Cato is dead.)

units.la: Mos] Mos est hominum, ut nolint eundem in pluribus excellere. Quae est tua natura, Cic. Ingenium soli, Plin. Mores equi, Col. Vid. Consuetudo.
units.tr: Custom: It is the custom of men that they do not want the same person to excel among many. What is your nature? Cic. The nature of the soil, Plin. The temper of a horse, Col. See Custom.

units.la: Motus] Actio & agitatio mentis. Motio animi, Cic. Agitatus spontaneus, Macrob. Diverso numine ad locum quaeque suum tendunt, Lucr. Vegetatio ambulationis, Apul.
units.tr: Motion: The action and agitation of the mind. Movement of the spirit, Cic. Spontaneous agitation, Macrob. Each thing tends by a different power to its own place, Lucr. The vitality of walking, Apul.

units.la: Motus (2) quo movent] Alieno pulsu, impulsu moveri, Cic. Motio alicujus ab ordine, Ulp. Paulo momento huc illuc impellitur, Ter. Momine parvo possunt impulsa moveri, Lucr. Numine capitis quatientes cristas, Ovid.
units.tr: Motion by which things move: To be moved by another's push or impulse, Cic. The moving of someone out of order, Ulp. Is pushed hither and thither by a slight momentum, Ter. Things struck by a small momentum can be moved, Lucr. Shaking their crests with a nod of the head, Ovid.

units.la: Motus fit successive] Primo quoque die nemo fit doctus.
units.tr: Motion happens successively: On the very first day no one becomes learned.

units.la: Movere ] Motare latus, Ovid. Commovere alas, Virg. Dimovere de loco. Cière, agitare motibus, Cic.
units.tr: To move: To flap the side, Ovid. To shake the wings, Virg. To remove from a place. To rouse, to stir with motions, Cic.

units.la: Mox, vid. Statim.
units.tr: Soon, see Immediately.

units.la: Muccinium] Sudarium, Catul. Strophiolum, Er. Orarium, Popisc. Lucil. Sudariolum, Apul. Linteolum, Plaut. Col. Panniculus, Celf. Mucco-
