units.tr: Handkerchief: A sweat-cloth, Catul. A little band, Er. A scarf, Popisc. Lucil. A little sweat-cloth, Apul. A little linen cloth, Plaut. Col. A small rag, Celsus. Mucco-

units.la: Maccofus] Muculentus, Arnob. Blennus, Plaut. Muccidus, vel, Mucidus, Plaut. Qui sæpe, vel, nimium emungitur, Iuv.
units.tr: Snotty: Snotty, Arnob. Blennus, Plaut. Snotty, or mucid, Plaut. One who often, or too much, blows his nose, Juv.

units.la: Muccus] Pituita nasi, Catul. Crassior pituita, Gorr.
units.tr: Mucus: Phlegm of the nose, Catul. Thicker phlegm, Gorr.

units.la: Mucescere] Mucere, Cat. Mucorem situ contrahere, Col. Canescunt situ tecta, Ovid. Situm ducere, Quint. Situ corrumpi, Plaut. Situm trahere, Plin.
units.tr: To grow mouldy: To mould, Cat. To contract mould by mustiness, Col. Houses grow white with age, Ovid. To take on mustiness, Quint. To be spoiled by mustiness, Plaut. To take on a musty smell, Plin.

units.la: Mucidus] Cariosus, Mart. Nemo illâ vivit carie cariosior, Afran. Emucida vitis, Plin. Mucorum contraxit situ, Col.
units.tr: Mouldy: Decayed, Mart. No one lives more decayed than she, Afran. A mouldy vine, Plin. Has contracted mustiness from mould, Col.

units.la: Mucor] Caries vini, Plin. Situs croci, Id. Situs araneosus, Catul.
units.tr: Mould: Decay of wine, Plin. Mustiness of saffron, Id. Cobwebby mustiness, Catul.

units.la: Mucro, vid. Acies.
units.tr: Point, see Edge.

units.la: Mucronatus, vid. Cuspidatus.
units.tr: Pointed, see Tipped.

units.la: Mugire] Mugilant onagri, Auth. Philom. Remugit vacca, Admugit, Ovid. Immugire. Fremit leo, Virg. Boat, boit, &, bovat bos, Varr. Demugitæ paludes, Ovid. (à demugio) Reboare, Virg.
units.tr: To bellow: Donkeys bray, Auth. Philom. A cow lows back, lows at, Ovid. To bellow. A lion roars, Virg. An ox moos, Varr. Marshes resounding with lowing, Ovid. (from demugio) To re-echo, Virg.

units.la: Mulcere] Demulcere caput, Ter. Permulcere manu aliquem. Palpare, Ovid. Subblandiri, Lucil. Pertractare mullulos, Cic. Plaudere equum, Stat.
units.tr: To stroke: To stroke the head, Ter. To caress someone with the hand. To pat, Ovid. To coax, Lucil. To handle small fish, Cic. To pat a horse, Stat.

units.la: Mulcta, vid. Multa.
units.tr: Fine, see Penalty.

units.la: Mulgere] Pressare ubera. Immulgere lac mulctræ, Virg. Emulgere, Col.
units.tr: To milk: To press the udders. To pour milk into the pail, Virg. To milk out, Col.

units.la: Mulier] Puella experta virum, Hor. Muliercula, Cic.
units.tr: Woman: A girl experienced with men, Hor. A little woman, Cic.

units.la: Mulier mala] Excetra. Mala merx tu es. Mulier es, Plaut. Monstrum mulieris. Mulier plus quàm pessima, &, Pessimâ pejor, Er. Erinnys, Virg.
units.tr: Bad woman: A viper. You are a bad bargain. You are a woman, Plaut. A monster of a woman. A woman more than most wicked, and worse than the worst, Er. A fury, Virg.

units.la: Mulsum] Aqua mulsa. Hydromeli, Plin.
units.tr: Mead: Honeyed water. Hydromel, Plin.

units.la: Multa] Mulcta. Irrogatio multæ, Cic. Condemnatio pecuniaria, Vlp. Æstimata poena, Fest. Censio, Id. Æra, plur. Plaut. Accipere ab aliquo pecudem æraque. Depensum, Paul.IC.
units.tr: Fine: A penalty. The imposition of a fine, Cic. A pecuniary condemnation, Vlp. A penalty fixed by estimate, Fest. An assessment, Id. Bronze money, plural, Plaut. To receive a sheep and bronze from someone. Paid out, Paul. IC.

units.la: Multare] Multare aliquem pensione. Multam alicui dicere, irrogare, Cic. Censionem faciebat censor, cùm multam equitibus irrogabat, Fest.
units.tr: To fine: To fine someone by payment. To impose a fine on someone, Cic. The censor made an assessment when he imposed a fine on the knights, Fest.

units.la: Multi] Pars magna, bona, multa, maxima, Hor. Complures. Permulti. Frequentissimi. Vis militum: magna vis auri, Cic. Numerosi, Plin. Quàm plures mali. Magna res argenti. Decem animi in pectore certant, Plaut. Immodicæ imagines, nes, Mart. Crebri lapides è cœlo cecidére, Liv. Centum, Hor. Mille colores iridis, Virg. Trecenti. Sexcentæ causæ. Quingentos coquos, i. multos, Plaut. Numerus, magnum numerum frumenti advexit, Cic. Decies centena, Hor. Catena negotiorum, Catenati labores. Colluvio ciborum. Cumulos meritorum.
units.tr: Many: A great part, good, much, very great, Hor. Several. Very many. Most frequent. A force of soldiers; a great quantity of gold, Cic. Numerous, Plin. How many evils. A great amount of silver. Ten minds struggle in the breast, Plaut. Countless images, Mart. Frequent stones fell from heaven, Liv. A hundred, Hor. A thousand colours of the rainbow, Virg. Three hundred. Six hundred reasons. Five hundred cooks, i.e. many, Plaut. A number; he brought a great number of grain, Cic. Tens of hundreds, Hor. A chain of business; chained labours. A heap of food. Heaps of merits.

units.la: Multifariam, vid. Variè.
units.tr: Manifoldly, see Variously.

units.la: Multiplex ] Multijugis. Multiformis, Cic. Multijugus, Apul. Multimodus, Lucr. Multifarius, Gell. Multigenus, Lucr. Multigenæ figuræ, Plin. Multigeneris, Robert. Step. Sed multigener, potest etiam dici, ut; Degener, Congener.
units.tr: Manifold: Many-yoked. Multiform, Cic. Many-yoked, Apul. Many-fashioned, Lucr. Multifarious, Gell. Of many kinds, Lucr. Figures of many kinds, Plin. Of many kinds, Robert. Step. But "multigener" may also be said, as "degener" and "congener."

units.la: Multiplicare] Propagare genus. Proseminatæ sunt familiæ, Cic. Ad maximum numerum perducere aliquid. Multiplicare summas inter se, vel, in se, Col. Auctare, Lucr.
units.tr: To multiply: To propagate a race. Families have been spread abroad, Cic. To bring something up to a very great number. To multiply sums among themselves, or into themselves, Col. To increase, Lucr.

units.la: Multiplicatio ] Incrementum populi, Ovid. Propagatio rerumpubl. Cic.
units.tr: Multiplication: the increase of a people (Ovid.); the propagation of the commonwealth (Cic.).

units.la: Multiplicativi numeri] Bis bina, sunt quatuor, &c. Tabula Cebetis. Mensa Pythagoræ.
units.tr: Multiplicative numbers: "twice two are four," etc. The Tablet of Cebes. The table of Pythagoras.

units.la: Multitudo ] Vis magna. Numerus magnus. Frequentia magna. Turba voluminum. Manus conjuratorum. Magnitudo fructuum, Cic. Nubes equitum peditumve, Lucr. Numerositas innumerabilis, Macr. Exercitus corvorum. Nimbus peditum, Virg. Magnum pondus artificum, Varr.
units.tr: Multitude: great force; a great number; a large crowd; a throng of volumes; a band of conspirators; abundance of fruits (Cic.); a cloud of horsemen or foot soldiers (Lucr.); countless numbers (Macr.); a flock of crows; a storm of foot soldiers (Virg.); a great weight of craftsmen (Varr.).

units.la: Multò ] Multis partibus plures. Longè longeque plurimùm. Permultò clariora. Nimiò multò, Plaut. Multò tanto nequior, Lucr. Multis rebus melior, Id. Impendiò loquacior, Gell. Infinitò præstat cæteris, Plin.
units.tr: Much (by much): many parts more; by far the most; far clearer; far too much (Plaut.); by so much more wicked (Lucr.); better in many things (Id.); more talkative by far (Gell.); far surpasses the rest (Plin.).

units.la: Multoties, vid. Sæpe.
units.tr: Multoties, see Often.

units.la: Multùm ] Plurimùm jucunditatis. Moles molestiarum. Magnum, grave pondus auri, &c. Cic. Quàm plurimam brassicam edere, Cat. Maria & montes polliceri, Salust. Montes auri, Ter. Aquarum, Ovid. Saltus mali, Plaut. vid. Seqq.
units.tr: Much (multum): the greatest pleasure; a mass of troubles; a great, heavy weight of gold, etc. (Cic.); to eat as much cabbage as possible (Cat.); to promise seas and mountains (Sall.); mountains of gold (Ter.); of waters (Ovid.); a wood of troubles (Plaut.); see what follows.

units.la: Multùm bonorum] Bonorum acervus, glomi.
units.tr: Much good: a heap, a ball of goods.

units.la: Multùm malorum ] Thesaurus mali. Montes mali, Plaut. Ilias, Mare, Lerna malorum. Lernea hydra. In apes irruisti. Pyxis Pandoræ. Panegyris miseriarum.
units.tr: Much evil: a treasury of evil; mountains of evil (Plaut.); an Iliad, a sea, a Lerna of evils; the Lernaean hydra; you have rushed into a hive of bees; Pandora's box; a festival of miseries.

units.la: Multùm augere] Cumulis augere. Cumulare officiis, &c. Multa convicia] Naves onustæ conviciis.
units.tr: To increase much: to augment with heaps; to load with favours, etc. Many insults: ships laden with insults.

units.la: Multus] Multus sermo. Frequens senatus, Cic. Plurimus labor. Tergeminus honor. Solutus risus,Hor. Impensissimæ preces, Suet. Major quàm pro numero hominum editur pugna, Liv. Numerosa cohors, Plin. Impensa libido, Lucr. Vid. Longus. Magnus.
units.tr: Much: much talk; a crowded senate (Cic.); very great toil; a threefold honour; loose laughter (Hor.); most urgent prayers (Suet.); a battle fought on a larger scale than the number of men warrants (Liv.); a numerous cohort (Plin.); lavish lust (Lucr.). See Long, Great.

units.la: Mundanus ] Cosmicus, Mart.
units.tr: Mundane: cosmic (Mart.).

units.la: Mundare, vid. Purgare.
units.tr: To cleanse, see To purge.

units.la: Mundè, vid. Eleganter.
units.tr: Cleanly, see Elegantly.

units.la: Mundus, a, um, vid. Purus. Elegans.
units.tr: Mundus, a, um, see Pure, Elegant.

units.la: Mundus] Orbis terrarum. Universitas rerum. Universitatis corpus. Universa natura. Universum, Cic. Orbis,Virg. Omne, Lucr. Æterna ratio Toti indita,Sen. Summa. Summa totius ; immensi ; rerum ; summarum , Lucr. Amphitheatrum spectaculis refertissimum. Domus omni supellectile instructa. Vanitatis speculum. Satanæ caupona.
units.tr: World: the orb of lands; the totality of things; the body of the universe; universal nature; the universe (Cic.); the orb (Virg.); all things (Lucr.); eternal reason implanted in the whole (Sen.); the sum; the sum of the whole, of the immense, of things, of totals (Lucr.); an amphitheatre crammed with spectacles; a house furnished with all its household goods; a mirror of vanity; Satan's tavern.

units.la: Mundus opinione regitur]Opinio plus valet,quàm res ipsa.
units.tr: The world is governed by opinion: opinion carries more weight than the thing itself.

units.la: A mundo condito ] Post homines natos. Post hominum memoriam. Ab omni æternitate vixit animus,Cic. Ab orbe condito. A primordio sui,Tac.
units.tr: From the foundation of the world: after men were born; after the memory of men; the soul has lived from all eternity (Cic.); from the founding of the world; from its own beginning (Tac.).

units.la: Mungere nares] Emungere se, ad Her. Emungere nares, ex Hor. Emungeris, ab emungor, Iuv.
units.tr: To blow the nose: to blow one's own nose (ad Her.); to blow the nose (from Hor.); you are blown (from emungor, Juv.).

units.la: Municeps ] Municipalis homo, Vlp. Tribulis, Cic. Popularis, Ter.
units.tr: Citizen of a municipality: a municipal man (Vlp.); a fellow tribesman (Cic.); a fellow countryman (Ter.).

units.la: Munificus, vid. Liberalis.
units.tr: Munificent, see Liberal.

units.la: Munire] Circummunire aliquid macerie. Emunire arborem cavea,Col. Præmunire locum aliquem,Tacit. Præmunire & effulcire. Sepimento vallare. Mirificis molibus munire aditus,Cic. Circumfirmare vineam. Præsepire aditus trabibus , Cæs. Tutari fundum , Varr. Circumstruere undique lapidibus, Plin. Circumdare muros igni, Virg.
units.tr: To fortify: to wall a thing round with a rampart; to enclose a tree with a cage (Col.); to fortify a place in advance (Tacit.); to fortify and prop up; to enclose with a hedge; to fortify approaches with marvellous structures (Cic.); to strengthen a vineyard all round; to block approaches with beams (Caes.); to guard an estate (Varr.); to build up on all sides with stones (Plin.); to surround walls with fire (Virg.).

units.la: Munitio] Munimen, Virg. Munimentum, Tac. Tutamentum, Liv.
units.tr: Fortification: a defence (Virg.); a bulwark (Tac.); a protection (Liv.).

units.la: Munitus] Permunita castra. Emunitus in modum arcis, Liv. Arx munitissima. Urbs muris armata, Cic.
units.tr: Fortified: a strongly fortified camp; raised up in the manner of a citadel (Liv.); a most strongly fortified citadel; a city armed with walls (Cic.).

units.la: Munus]Donatum aliquid.Munusculum,Cic. Dono aliquid datum,Plaut. Pugnus aureus. Xeniolum,Vlp. Vid.Donum.
units.tr: Gift: something given as a present; a little gift (Cic.); something given as a gift (Plaut.); a golden fist; a small present (Vlp.). See Gift.

units.la: Munus, (2) vid. Officium.
units.tr: Munus (2), see Duty.

units.la: Murarius faber] Structor, Cic. Officinator, Vitr. Faber cæmentarius, Sipont. Machiones, vid. Machinones, Lipf. ex Isid.
units.tr: Mason: a builder (Cic.); a constructor (Vitr.); a cement worker (Sipont.). Machiones, see Machinones (Lipsius, from Isidore).

units.la: Muratus] Mœnitus divinâ manu, Plaut. Saxo structus. Lateritio opere structus, Col.
units.tr: Built of stone: walled by a divine hand (Plaut.); built of stone; built of brick (Col.).

units.la: Murmur, vid. Strepitus, & seqq. hic.
units.tr: Murmur, see Noise, and the following entries here.

units.la: Murmurare propr. ut aqua, &c.] Fremunt venti. Obmurmurat ventus meis precibus. Obstrepitur locus aquis, Ovid. Insusurrat favonius. Perfremere, Cic. Obstrepente pluviâ, nihil sensêre, Liv. Immurmurat auster, Virg. Remurmurat pinus, Stat. Sonant alicui aures, Celf.
units.tr: To murmur, properly of water: the winds roar; the wind murmurs at my prayers; the place is drowned by waters (Ovid.); the west wind whispers; to roar through (Cic.); with the rain roaring, they noticed nothing (Liv.); the south wind murmurs in (Virg.); the pine murmurs back (Stat.); the ears ring for someone (Celsus).

units.la: Murmurare transf.] Fremit provincia. Commurmurare secum, Cic. Gannire alicui in aurem. Cornicare secum quid grave clausō murmure, Perf. Contractis rugatis naribus, concava verba trutinantur, Hieron. Videas illum barbato rostro commentari, & unum quodque verbum staterâ auriâ pendere, Varr. Immurmurare aliquid sub linguâ, Perf. Commurmurant inter se, Plin. Murmurillare. Ut scelesta sola secum commurmurat, Plaut. Obmurmurare, Ovid. In occulto mussare, Enn. Mussitare, Plaut. Respònsare, Id.
units.tr: To murmur, figuratively: the province grumbles; to murmur among themselves (Cic.); to whisper into someone's ear; to mutter something to oneself with a closed murmur (Pers.); with nostrils wrinkled, hollow words are weighed (Hieron.); you may see him with a bearded beak pondering, and every single word weighed on a golden balance (Varr.); to mutter something under the tongue (Pers.); they mutter among themselves (Plin.); to mumble; as the wicked fellow mutters to himself alone (Plaut.); to mutter at (Ovid.); to mutter in secret (Enn.); to mutter (Plaut.); to answer back (Id.).

units.la: Murmuratio] Murmur tacitum, Ovid. Secretum, Iuv. Murmuratio querula, Plaut. Mussitatio, Apul. Vid. Strepitus.
units.tr: Murmuring: a silent murmur (Ovid.); secrecy (Juv.); a complaining murmur (Plaut.); muttering (Apul.). See Noise.

units.la: Murus] Mœri (orum, unde pomœrium) Serv. Mœnia, Cic. Structa saxorum, Lucret. Opus factum structurâ cæmentitiâ, &, structura, absol. Vitr.
units.tr: Wall: moeri (whence pomerium) (Serv.); walls (Cic.); a structure of piled stones (Lucret.); a work made of mortared construction, and structure, absolutely (Vitr.).

units.la: Muros exstruere] Ædificare muros. Mœnia constituere, ponere. Ducere muros, Ovid. Struere templa saxo. Cingere muro, Virg.
units.tr: To build walls: to construct walls; to set up and lay down city walls; to draw walls (Ovid.); to build temples of stone; to surround with a wall (Virg.).

units.la: Musca] Muscula, Arnob. (Deriv. Muscinus, Sipont. ex Plauto.)
units.tr: Fly: a little fly (Arnob.). (Derivative: muscinus, Sipont., from Plautus.)

units.la: Muscosus] Lanuginosus, Plin. Lanatæ vites, Col. Pubens herba, Virg.
units.tr: Mossy: downy (Plin.); woolly vines (Col.); a grass in full bloom (Virg.).

units.la: Musculosus] Pulposis torulis obesa terga, Apul. Musculorum toris numerosum pectus, Col.
units.tr: Muscular: a back fat with plump lumps (Apul.); a chest abundant with knots of muscle (Col.).

units.la: Musculus] Lacertus, Gor. Torulus, Apul.
units.tr: Muscle: the upper arm (Gor.); a muscle knot (Apul.).

units.la: Muscus] Lanugo, Plin. Herbeæ nationis initiamentum.
units.tr: Moss: down (Plin.); the beginning of the grassy kind.

units.la: Museum] Penetrale, Virg. Conclave, Ter.
units.tr: Museum: an inner sanctum (Virg.); a room (Ter.).

units.la: Musica] Musica ars, Ter. Musica, pl. Cic.
units.tr: Music: the art of music (Ter.); music, in the plural (Cic.).

units.la: Musicus] Symphoniacus, Cic. Hymnologus, Firm. Hymnifer, Ovid. Musurgus, Iun.
units.tr: Musician: a player of instruments (Cic.); a hymn singer (Firm.); a hymn bearer (Ovid.); a singer (Iun.).

units.la: Musicus excellens] Amphion. Luscinia Musarum.
units.tr: Outstanding musician: Amphion; the nightingale of the Muses.

units.la: Mussare] Mutitare. Ne hiscere quidem, vel mutire audeo, Plaut. Mittere vocem, Cic. Emittere, Liv. Facere mu. Ne mu quidem facere auderet, Lucil. In occulto mussabant, En.
units.tr: To mutter: to murmur. I dare not even open my mouth or mutter (Plaut.); to send forth a voice (Cic.); to emit (Liv.); to make a mu. He would not dare even make a mu (Lucil.). They muttered in secret (Enn.).

units.la: Mustum] Vinum novitium, Plin.
units.tr: Must: new wine (Plin.).

units.la: Mutabilis] Varians coelum. Commutabilis, Cic. Versabilis motus fortunae, Amm. Vertumnus, Passerat. Proteo mutabilior. Chamaeleontem imitatur. Vid. Inconstans.
units.tr: Changeable: a varying sky; interchangeable (Cic.); the shifting motion of fortune (Amm.); Vertumnus (Passerat.); more changeable than Proteus. He imitates the chameleon. See Inconstant.

units.la: Mutabilia omnia] Omnium rerum vicissitudo est.
units.tr: All things are changeable: there is a succession of all things.

units.la: Mutabilitas] Volubilitas fortunae, Cic. Volumen sortis humanae, Plin.
units.tr: Changeableness: the fickleness of fortune (Cic.); the turning of the human lot (Plin.).

units.la: Mutare] Immutare, commutare vultum. Novare aliquid, Cic. Remutare formam orationis, Tac. Alterare faciem, Ovid. Transmutare, Lucr. Variare vocem, Cic. Alium facere, Plaut. Omnia migrat & commutat natura, Lucr. Transfigurare, Plin.
units.tr: To change: to alter, to change the countenance; to make something new (Cic.); to recast the form of speech (Tac.); to alter the face (Ovid.); to transform (Lucr.); to vary the voice (Cic.); to make into another (Plaut.); nature changes and transforms all things (Lucr.); to transfigure (Plin.).

units.la: Mutare factum] Reducere calculum. Decedere, desistere de sententia. Retrahere se, Cic. Calculum a linea movere. Vertere stylum, Hor. Revocare promissum, Sen. Demutare animum, Plaut.
units.tr: To change a decision: to reverse the vote; to withdraw from, desist from an opinion; to draw oneself back (Cic.); to move the counter off the line; to turn the stylus (Hor.); to revoke a promise (Sen.); to change one's mind (Plaut.).

units.la: Mutare statum] De toga ad pallium, &c. Acus Aciasque reliquere.
units.tr: To change one's station: from the toga to the pallium, etc. They left behind needles and needle-cases.

units.la: Mutandum est factum] Ad metamorphosin Ovidii res revocanda.
units.tr: A deed to be changed: the matter is to be brought back to Ovid's Metamorphoses.

units.la: Non est statim mutandum propositum] Etiam post malam messem metendum.
units.tr: A purpose should not be changed at once: one must reap even after a bad harvest.

units.la: Mutantur res in melius] Flebile principium, melior fortuna secuta.
units.tr: Things change for the better: a tearful beginning, followed by a better fortune.

units.la: Mutari in deterius] Leonem prius, nunc leporem agit.
units.tr: To change for the worse: he played the lion before, now the hare.

units.la: Mutatio] Permutatio rerum. Immutatio ordinis. Commutatio studiorum, vitae, Cic. Transmutatio, Lucr. Inclinatio, Liv. Catastrophe fabulae, Donat.
units.tr: Change: an exchange of things; an alteration of order; a change of studies, of life (Cic.); transmutation (Lucr.); inclination (Liv.); the catastrophe of a play (Donat.).

units.la: Mutatio crebra inutilis] Lapis saepe volutus non obducitur musco.
units.tr: Frequent change is useless: a stone often rolled does not gather moss.

units.la: Mutatus] Quantùm mutatus ab illo, Virg. Non cognoscas eandem esse, Ter. Alium esse existimes. Amisimus non modò succum & sanguinem, sed colorem etiam, & speciem pristinam, Cic.
units.tr: Changed: how changed from that man (Virg.); you would not recognise that it is the same (Ter.); you would think he is another. We have lost not only juice and blood but even colour and former appearance (Cic.).

units.la: Mutilare aliquem] Emancare aliquem. Depravare hominem, Sen. Obtruncare aliquem, Cic. Admutilare aliquem, Plaut. Detruncare corpora, Liv. Circumscindere, Id. Desecare aures, Caes.
units.tr: To mutilate someone: to maim someone; to debase a man (Sen.); to cut down someone (Cic.); to mutilate someone (Plaut.); to cut bodies to pieces (Liv.); to cut around (Id.); to cut off ears (Caes.).

units.la: Mutilatus] Mutilus homo, Hor. Mancus, Cic. Depravatus corpore, Cic. Truncus, Virg. Lacer, Lucr. Truncatus, Plin. Iun. Semiputatus, Virg.
units.tr: Mutilated: a maimed man (Hor.); maimed (Cic.); impaired in body (Cic.); mangled (Virg.); torn (Lucr.); lopped (Plin. Iun.); half-pruned (Virg.).

units.la: Mutuare ] Dare mutuam pecuniam. Nomina facere. Commodare triticum, Cic. Mutuò appendere murænas, Plin. Credere aurum fidei alterius. Credere mutuitanti. Facere copiam argenti. Credere, Abs. Nunquam magis nomina facio, quàm cum dono, Sen.
units.tr: To lend: to give money as a loan; to make loans. To lend wheat (Cic.); to lend lampreys (Plin.); to entrust gold to another's good faith; to lend to a borrower; to supply silver. To lend (Abs.). I never make loans more than when I give gifts (Sen.).

units.la: Mutuari ] Mutuum sumere, petere, rogare, Plaut. Sumere mutuas pecunias, Cic. Mutuitare, ex Plaut.
units.tr: To borrow: to take, seek, or ask for a loan (Plaut.); to take borrowed money (Cic.); to borrow (from Plaut.).

units.la: Mutuatitius] Argentum mutuum, Plin. Mutuatica pecunia, Robert. Usurarius, Plaut. Æra usuraria.
units.tr: Borrowed: borrowed silver (Plin.); borrowed money (Robert.); usurious (Plaut.); usurious money.

units.la: Mutuatus] Mutuò sumptus, Plaut.
units.tr: Borrowed: taken as a loan (Plaut.).

units.la: Mutuò] Mutuè, Cic. Mutuà, Lucr. Mutuùm, Lucil. Mutuiter, Varr. Invicem, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: On loan: mutually (Cic.); mutually (Lucr.); mutually (Lucil.); mutually (Varr.); in turn (Plin. Iun.).

units.la: Mutuò (2) i.e. invicem] Cognoscunt se invicem, Plin. Vicissim. Ultro citroque data beneficia, & accepta. Communiter aliquorum, Cic. Mutuò deperiebat illam, Plaut. Consociatim, Am. In commune jacebant munera naturæ promiscuè utenda, Sen.
units.tr: Mutually, that is, in turn: they know one another (Plin.); in turn; benefits given and received on both sides; common to several (Cic.); he was mutually in love with her (Plaut.); together (Am.); the gifts of nature lay in common, to be used by all alike (Sen.).

units.la: Mutus] Infans, Hor. Brutus & elinguis, Pacuv. Magis mutus, quam piscis. (Infantia, Henric. Steph. Oris vinculum, nodus, Gell. Sunt Abstracta, quasi mutitas dicas, si imiteris Ciceronem, qui dixit surditas.)
units.tr: Mute: an infant (Hor.); dumb and tongue-tied (Pacuv.); more mute than a fish. (Infantia, Henric. Steph. A bond of the mouth, a knot (Gell.). These are abstract nouns; you may say mutitas if you imitate Cicero, who said surditas.)

units.la: Mutuus] Vicaria opera, servitus, mors, Quint. Mutuum officium, Cic. Vid. Communio.
units.tr: Reciprocal: vicarious work, servitude, death (Quint.); a reciprocal duty (Cic.). See Communion.

units.la: Myops, vid. Luscios.
units.tr: Myops, see Squinting.

units.la: Mysterium, vid. Arcanum.
units.tr: Mystery, see Secret.

units.la: Nablium]
units.tr: Nablium

units.la: N.
units.tr: N.

units.la: NAblium] Psalterium, Virg. Magadis, Iul. Caf. Sambuca, Lorin. ex Euphorion. & Suid. Naulium, Ovid. Nablium, in SS.
units.tr: Nablium: psaltery, Virg.; magadis, Iul. Caf.; sambuca, Lorin. ex Euphorion. & Suid.; naulium, Ovid.; nablium, in SS.

units.la: Næ, vid. Certè.
units.tr: Næ: indeed. See Certè.

units.la: Nænia, vid. Epicedium.
units.tr: Nænia: a funeral dirge. See Epicedium.

units.la: Nævus] Nævus est corporis macula, Cic. Nævulus, Gell. Insigne naturæ, Plin. Genitiva nota, Suet. Notaculum. Notaculo corporis dignoscimus, Minut. Felix.
units.tr: Nævus: a blemish on the body, Cic.; a small mole, Gell.; a mark of nature, Plin.; a birthmark, Suet.; a little mark. We recognise a person by a mark on the body, Minut. Felix.

units.la: Nam] Quia;quoniam;etenim;namque;enim;quippe, Cic.
units.tr: Nam: because; since; for; for; indeed; truly, Cic.

units.la: Nancisci, vid. Acquirere.
units.tr: Nancisci: see Acquirere.

units.la: Nanus] Pumilio, Plin. Pumilo, Stat. Pumilus, Id. Pomilo, Pomilus, Sipont. Salaputium, vel Salicippium, Catul. Sen.
units.tr: Nanus: a dwarf, Plin.; a dwarf, Stat.; a dwarf, Id.; a dwarf, Sipont.; a little fellow, Catul. Sen.

units.la: Naphta] Oleum vivum, Turneb. ex Grat. Oleum incendiarium. Oleum medicum, Solin.
units.tr: Naphta: quick oil, Turneb. ex Grat.; incendiary oil; medicinal oil, Solin.

units.la: Napus] Bunias, adis. Plin. Col.
units.tr: Napus: bunias, Plin. Col.

units.la: Nardus, herba] Nardus celtica. Nardi spica, Matthiol. Ozænitis, Plin. Comagene. Folium, simpl. Id.
units.tr: Nard, the herb: Celtic nard; the spike of nard, Matthiol.; ozaenitis, Plin.; comagene; the leaf, simply, Id.

units.la: Nardus, oleum ex illa] Nardinum oleum. Malobathrum, Al. Malabathrum, Plin. Hor. Nardum, Tibul.
units.tr: Oil of nard: nard oil; malobathrum, Al.; malabathrum, Plin. Hor.; nard, Tibul.

units.la: Nares] Spiritus, vel, mucoris vehicula. Cloaca cerebri.
units.tr: Nostrils: passages of breath, or conveyers of mucus; the sewer of the brain.

units.la: Narrare] Referre alicui aliquid. Recensere. Exponere rem gestam; narrationem; quemadmodum res gesta sit. Exsequi verbis. Edam quid gesserim. Renunciare. Prosequi omnia. Reddere. Dicere paucis. Oratione persequi, Cic. Exponere rem verbis, Lucr. Eloqui. Edocere ut se res habent. Dicere bonâ fide, Plaut. Expedire causam adventûs, Liv. Tradere, Plin. Ferre, Tac. Apportare. PræNarrare, Ter. Vid. Enarrare.
units.tr: Narrare: to tell someone something; to recount; to set out a deed done, a narrative; how the thing was done; to follow in words; I will tell what I did; to report; to pursue everything; to give back; to say in few words; to relate in speech, Cic.; to set out a matter in words, Lucr.; to utter; to teach how things stand; to speak in good faith, Plaut.; to explain the cause of one's arrival, Liv.; to hand down, Plin.; to bring, Tac.; to bring forward. To narrate beforehand, Ter. See Enarrare.

units.la: Narratur, vid. Ajunt.
units.tr: Narratur: see Ajunt. (they say).

units.la: Narratio] Rerum gestarum, vel ut gestarum expositio, Quint. Relatio, Justin. Relatus, Tac. Narratus, Ovid.
units.tr: Narratio: an exposition of deeds done, or of things done as they were done, Quint.; a report, Justin.; a narrative, Tac.; a thing narrated, Ovid.

units.la: Narrator] Pronunciator rerum gestarum. Certis auctoribus comperi. Relator. Caput: sine capite, sine auctore, &c. audivimus, Cic.
units.tr: Narrator: one who announces deeds done; I learned this from certain authors; a reporter. Chapter: without head, without author, and so on, we have heard, Cic.

units.la: Nasci] Suscipi in lucem, & hoc cœlesti spiritu augeri, Cic. Provenire. Suboriri, Plin. Generascere. Procrescere, Lucr. Gigni, Macrob.
units.tr: Nasci: to be brought into the light and nourished by this heavenly breath, Cic.; to come forth; to spring up, Plin.; to grow up, Lucr.; to be born, Macrob.

units.la: Naso] Nasutus, Hor. Nasatus, Cæl. Rhod. Nasica, Arnob.
units.tr: Naso: big-nosed, Hor.; big-nosed, Cael. Rhod.; Nasica, Arnob.

units.la: Natalis] Meus est natalis. Natalitius, Cic. Primigenius dies. Tempus genitale, Lucr. Genitalis hora, Plin. Genethliacus.
units.tr: Natalis: it is my birthday; birthday, Cic.; the first day of life; the time of generation, Lucr.; the hour of birth, Plin.; a caster of nativities.

units.la: Natalitia Christi] Nato Christo celebris dies.
units.tr: Christ's birthday: the day celebrated for the birth of Christ.

units.la: Natalitia celebrare] Dare natalitia, Cic. Celebrare natalem suum, Hor. Concelebrare natalem, Plin.
units.tr: To celebrate a birthday: to give birthday feasts, Cic.; to celebrate one's birthday, Hor.; to celebrate a birthday together, Plin.

units.la: Natare] Nare. Natatu ferri. Prænatare, Plin. Natatu aliquid transgredi. Vid. Innatare.
units.tr: Natare: to swim; to be carried by swimming; to swim before, Plin.; to cross something by swimming. See Innatare.

units.la: Natator] Fluctivagi nautæ, Stat.
units.tr: Natator: sailors wandering on the waves, Stat.

units.la: Natio] Gentes & nationes exteræ, Cic. Quod genus hoc hominum? Virg. Gentilitas, Amm.
units.tr: Natio: foreign peoples and nations, Cic.; what kind of men is this? Virg.; heathendom, Amm.

units.la: Nativitas] Nascentia, Vitr. Gignentia, Apul. Progeneratio. Genitura. Origo, Plin. Satus, Cic. Editio, Vlp.
units.tr: Nativitas: those being born, Vitr.; those begetting, Apul.; progeneration; begetting; origin, Plin.; seed, Cic.; publication, Vlp.

units.la: Nativus, vid. Naturalis, & Sponte nascens.
units.tr: Nativus: see Naturalis and Sponte nascens. (growing of its own accord)

units.la: Natura] Rerum mater. Artifex mundi, Cic. Rerum parens, Plin. Naturalis potestas, Amm. Conservatrix sui.
units.tr: Natura: mother of things; craftsman of the world, Cic.; parent of things, Plin.; natural power, Amm.; preserver of itself.

units.la: Natura non mutatur] Lupus, vulpes, pilum mutant, non mentem. Maculas non deponit pardus. Æthiops non albescit. Naturam expellas furcâ, tamen usque recurrit.
units.tr: Nature does not change: wolves and foxes change their hair, not their mind. The leopard does not lose its spots. The Ethiopian does not grow white. You may drive nature out with a pitchfork, yet it will always come back.

units.la: Natura cujusque] Ingenium soli, Plin. Indoles, Quint. Mos cœli, Virg. Genius, Fest.
units.tr: The nature of each thing: the character of the soil, Plin.; disposition, Quint.; the climate of the sky, Virg.; genius, Fest.

units.la: Naturâ adversante nihil succedit] Reluctante natura irritus est labor, Cic. Tu nihil invita dices, faciesve Minervâ. Invitâ Deliâ venari vanum.
units.tr: When nature opposes, nothing succeeds: labour is in vain when nature resists, Cic. You will say or do nothing against Minerva's will. To hunt against Diana's will is vain.

units.la: Natura solers] Apis nulla, nisi artifex, nascitur, Quint. Aranei statim ac nati sunt, fila mittunt.
units.tr: Clever nature: no bee is born except as a craftsman; spiders, as soon as they are born, send out threads.

units.la: A natura] E natura est aliquid. Naturæ insitum, Habitus naturæ, Cic. Ab ingenio est improbus, Plaut.
units.tr: From nature: something comes from nature; implanted by nature; a habit of nature, Cic.; wicked by nature, Plaut.

units.la: A natura hoc habemus] Ita est anticipatum & informatum mentibus nostris. Natura informationem Deorum insculpsit mentibus nostris. Insitum à natura. Innascitur (homini) cupiditas principatus. Naturâ insitum est. Naturaliter homini insitum est. Accommodatum ad naturam est, Cic. Ita naturâ comparatum est, Liv. Id natura nobis indidit. Id cunctis attribuit natura. Multa vitia nobis recepta cepta consuetudo conciliat, nonnulla natura ingenerat. Omnibus innatum. Id vitii tibi naturâ adjunctum est,Er.
units.tr: We have this from nature: thus it is anticipated and imprinted on our minds. Nature has engraved the knowledge of God on our minds. Implanted by nature. Desire for mastery is born in man. It is implanted by nature. It is naturally implanted in man. It is adapted to nature, Cic. It has been so arranged by nature, Liv. Nature has put this into us. Nature grants this to all. Long custom produces many vices in us; nature engenders some. Innate in all. This vice has been joined to you by nature, Erasm.

units.la: Naturalis] Nativus color. Congenita vastitas, Plin. Non scripta, sed nata lex. Insita animis cognitio. Ingenerata ei frugalitas. Innata probitas, Cic. Natalis & ingenita sterilitas, Col. Genuinus honor, Gell. Genitalis, Col. Generosum honestum, Perf. Lactant.
units.tr: Natural: natural colour; innate barrenness, Plin.; a law not written but born; knowledge implanted in minds; thrift engendered in him; innate uprightness, Cic.; natural and inborn barrenness, Col.; genuine honour, Gell.; genital, Col.; noble and honest, Perf. Lactant.

units.la: Naturaliter] Naturâ tu illi pater es, Ter. Physicè. Habitu naturæ, Cic. Per naturam, Gell. Genuino more, Amm.
units.tr: Naturally: you are his father by nature, Ter.; physically; by the habit of nature, Cic.; by nature, Gell.; in a genuine manner, Amm.

units.la: Natus, vid. Filius. Prognatus.
units.tr: Natus: see Filius. Prognatus.

units.la: Navarchus,inter Nautas] Dominus navis. Nauclerus. Navicularius. Naviculator, Cic. Magister navis, Liv.
units.tr: Navarch, among sailors: owner of a ship; shipmaster; ship-owner; ship's master, Cic.; master of the ship, Liv.

units.la: Navarchus, inter milites] Dux praefectusque classis. Trierarchus, Cic. Praepositus classi, Suet.
units.tr: Navarch, among soldiers: commander and prefect of the fleet; trierarch, Cic.; placed over the fleet, Suet.

units.la: Nauci homo] Simius. Nullo in numero est, Cic. Non semissis homo, Id. Matula. Fungus. Coenum. Ignavissimus. Inscitissimus. Bliteus. Frutex,Plaut. Incus. Stipes ille, Nullo numero est, Cic. Mala merx, Plaut. Caudex, stipes, asinus, Ter.
units.tr: A good-for-nothing man: an ape; of no account, Cic.; not even half a man, Id.; a jug; a mushroom; mud; a most idle fellow; a most ignorant one; a blite; a bush, Plaut.; an anvil; that block, of no account, Cic.; bad goods, Plaut.; a blockhead, a stick, an ass, Ter.

units.la: Naufragium facere] Affligere ad scopulos navem, Cic. Frangere, confringere navem, Ter.
units.tr: To suffer shipwreck: to dash a ship against the rocks, Cic.; to break, to shatter a ship, Ter.

units.la: Naufragus] Afflicta navis. Naufragia colligere, Cic.
units.tr: Shipwrecked: a wrecked ship. To gather up shipwrecks, Cic.

units.la: Navicularia] Nauticarum rerum scientia. Res nautica, navalis, Cic.
units.tr: Seamanship: knowledge of nautical matters. Naval and nautical affairs, Cic.

units.la: Navigabilis] Flumen navigabile, Sen. Navigerum velivolum mare, Lucr. Velificus cursus, Plin.
units.tr: Navigable: a navigable river, Sen.; a sea bearing ships and driven by sails, Lucr.; swift sailing, Plin.

units.la: Navigare] Ire navigio. Proficisci navi. Flumine invehi. Vela dare, facere. Ratis in mari vehitur. Cursum tenere vento secundissimo. Committere se fluctibus. Dare carbasa ventis. Dare se ventis. Dare ratem fluctibus. Embaticam facere, Cic. Venire navibus, Liv. Deferri navi ad littus, Plin. Remigare Romam, Liv. Velificare, Propert. Vir mare metitur magnum, Non. Innare fluvios. Petere vento urbem, Virg. Naviculari in stagno, Mart. Navicularium facere, Cic.
units.tr: To sail: to go by ship; to set out by ship; to be carried up a river; to set sails; a raft is carried on the sea; to keep course with the most favourable wind; to commit oneself to the waves; to give the sails to the winds; to give oneself to the winds; to give the raft to the waves; to make an embattic voyage, Cic.; to come by ships, Liv.; to be carried by ship to the shore, Plin.; to row to Rome, Liv.; to sail, Propert.; a man measures the great sea, Non.; to swim across rivers; to seek the city with the wind, Virg.; to sail on a pool, Mart.; to make a little voyage, Cic.

units.la: Navigatio] Velificatio. Cursus per mare, Cic. Praenavigatio. Praeternavigatio, Plin. Cursus sine pedibus. Iter sine vestigiis. Volatus sine pennis.
units.tr: Navigation: sailing; a course over the sea, Cic.; sailing ahead; sailing past, Plin.; a course without feet; a journey without tracks; flight without wings.

units.la: Navigatio est res periculosa] Qui non navigavit, malum ignorat. Qui non scit orare, descendat in mare.
units.tr: Navigation is a dangerous thing: he who has never sailed knows no evil. He who does not know how to pray, let him go down to the sea.

units.la: A navigatione cessare] Vela colligere, contrahere, sinuare, vertere. Funem reducere, Erasm.
units.tr: To cease from navigation: to gather in the sails, to draw them in, to furl them, to turn them. To reel back the rope, Erasm.

units.la: Navigiolum] Navicula. Scapha, Cic. Phaselus, Catul. Virg. Salust. Gaulus, Gell. Navis vectoria, Vlp.
units.tr: A small boat: a little ship; a skiff, Cic.; a light boat, Catul. Virg. Salust.; a gaulus, Gell.; a cargo ship, Vlp.

units.la: Navis] Navigium. Vehiculum. Classis, Virg. Murus ligneus, apud Plutarch. Themist. Liburna. Equo ligneo per vias caeruleas estis vectae, Plaut. Maris equus, Homer. Domus erratica, volatica. Avis lignea. Pons innatans. Charontis cymba sutilis, Virg.
units.tr: Ship: a vessel; a conveyance; a fleet, Virg.; a wooden wall, Plutarch, Themist.; a liburna; you were carried through blue ways on a wooden horse, Plaut.; horse of the sea, Homer.; a wandering house, a flying house; a wooden bird; a floating bridge; Charon's stitched skiff, Virg.

units.la: Navis oneraria] Navis geraria, Plaut. Gestoria, Gell.
units.tr: Cargo ship: a carrying ship, Plaut.; a carrying ship, Gell.

units.la: Navis actuaria] Navigium actuarium, Cef. Vectorium navigium. Navis longa, Id. Liburna, Hor. Liburnica, Liv.
units.tr: Transport ship: a working vessel, Caes.; a passenger vessel; a long ship, Id.; a liburna, Hor.; a liburnian vessel, Liv.

units.la: Navim solvere, vid. Solvere.
units.tr: To cast off a ship: see Solvere.

units.la: Naulum, vid. Portorium.
units.tr: Passage fare: see Portorium.

units.la: Nausea] Fastidiens stomachus, Sen. Nauseola, Cic. Redundantia stomachi, Plin. Iners stomachus, Ovid. Obtusus, Plin. Jun. Languens. Aversso stomacho, Arnob.
units.tr: Nausea: a loathing stomach, Sen.; a slight nausea, Cic.; an overflow of the stomach, Plin.; a sluggish stomach, Ovid.; a dulled stomach, Plin. Jun.; a languishing stomach; a stomach turned away, Arnob.

units.la: Nauseare] Nauseator sum, Sen. Fastidio stomachi laborare. Vid. Fastidire.
units.tr: To be nauseated: I am nauseated, Sen.; to suffer from a loathing of the stomach. See Fastidire.

units.la: Nauta] Navita, Cic. Nauticus, Plin. Nauclerus, Plaut. Sulcator ponti, Stat. Classicus, Curt. Vector, Sen. Equiso nauticus, Varr. Cliens undae. Oberrator sepulchri sui.
units.tr: Sailor: a navigator, Cic.; a seaman, Plin.; a shipmaster, Plaut.; a plougher of the sea, Stat.; a naval man, Curt.; a passenger, Sen.; a sea-horse of the crew, Varr.; a client of the wave; a wanderer about his own tomb.

units.la: Nautica ars] Ars bene gubernandi. Vid. Navicularia.
units.tr: The art of sailing: the art of steering well. See Navicularia.

units.la: Nauticus] Navales socii, Liv. Navicularius. Naucleriacus ornatus, Plin. Classicus, Paterc.
units.tr: Nautical: allies at sea, Liv.; a shipmaster; ornament of a ship, Plin.; naval, Paterc.

units.la: Ne, conjunctio] Ut ne : ut non. Quin. Neve, Cic. Quin ne. Quo minus. Neu, Ter.
units.tr: Ne, conjunction: that not; that not, or not; but that not; nor, Cic.; not even, Ter.; that not, lest; but not; so that not. Neither, nor, Ter.

units.la: Ne, adverbi, ne facias] Da operam ut ne. Noli putare. Abstine te a. Tolle metum, Cic. Minime feceris. Tempora dormire. Ah noli. Cave parsis, Plaut. Mitte male loqui. Missam fac iram, &c. Ter. Fuge suspicari, Hor. Parce laboori, Cic. Absiste moveri, Virg. Define querelarum, Hor. Omitte timorem, Cic. Tempera a lacrymis, Virg.
units.tr: Ne, adverb, ne facias: take care that you do not; do not think; keep away from. Take away fear, Cic.; do least; sleep in the proper time. Ah, do not. Beware of sparing, Plaut.; stop speaking ill; put aside your anger, and so on, Ter.; do not suspect, Hor.; spare the labour, Cic.; cease to be moved, Virg.; stop your complaints, Hor.; lay aside fear, Cic.; restrain yourself from tears, Virg.

units.la: Nebula] Amictus nebulae caligo, Cic. Exhalatio aere crassior ; nube subtilior, Apul. Nubes in terra. Nox in die. Aëris caligo. Roris seges. Infalubritatum pabulum , vel fomes.
units.tr: Cloud: a covering of mist, a darkness, Cic.; an exhalation thicker than air and finer than a cloud, Apul.; a cloud on the earth; night in the day; a dimness of the air; the crop of dew; food or fuel of unhealthiness.

units.la: Nebula suboritur] Caliginem inducit Deus ; Ovid. Nubes humida circumligat , Virg. Nebulæ suffundunt cœlum suâ caligine. Subtexunt cœlum nubila , Lucr.
units.tr: A mist rises: God brings on darkness, Ovid.; a damp cloud wraps around, Virg.; mists cover the sky with their gloom; clouds veil the sky, Lucr.

units.la: Nebula subsidit] Discutitur caligo, Cic. Vento & sole resolvuntur nebulæ.
units.tr: The mist settles: the darkness is dispelled, Cic.; mists are dissolved by wind and sun.

units.la: Nebulo, vid. Nequam.
units.tr: Nebulo: see Nequam.

units.la: Nebulosus] Nebulosus aër, Plin. Cœlum caliginosum, Cic. Caliginosæ tenebræ, Val. M.
units.tr: Misty: misty air, Plin.; a murky sky, Cic.; shadowy darkness, Val. M.

units.la: Nec ] Neque, ne, Cic. Ne tantillum quidem, Ter. Ne nunc quidem cùm. Ne gry quidem.
units.tr: Nor: Neque, ne. Cic. Not even the smallest amount. Ter. Not even now, when. Not even grey.

units.la: Nec, nec ] Nec Deum extimescit nec homines. Non veretur neque Deos, neque homines. Neque Deos, neque homines veretur. Non veretur haud Deos, haud homines. Non metuit homines Deosve, Er.
units.tr: Neither, nor: He fears neither God nor men. He has no regard for either gods or men. He has no regard for gods or men. He does not fear, by no means, gods or men. He fears neither men nor gods. Er.

units.la: Necare] Auferre vitam alicui. Afferre necem, Ovid. Privare luce, communi vitâ. Eripere vitam. Eripere lucis usuram alicui. Expellere è vita. Tollere ex rerum naturâ. Tollere de medio. Evitare vitam alicui. Extúrbare è numero vivorum. Violare vitam patris, Cic. Conficere aliquem sicâ, plagis. Exanimare aliquem, Id. Enecare, Col. Interimere vitam. Exanimalem facere ; exheredem vitæ, Plaut. Inferre alicui mortem, Plin.
units.tr: To kill: To take someone's life. To bring death upon someone. To deprive someone of light and of common life. To snatch away life. To take from someone the use of light. To drive out of life. To remove from the nature of things. To remove from the midst. To take life from someone. To drive out of the number of the living. To violate a father's life, Cic. To cut someone down with a dagger or with blows. To make someone lifeless, Cic. To kill, Col. To destroy life. To make lifeless. To make one disinherited of life, Plaut. To bring death upon someone, Plin.

units.la: Nec-dum, vid. Nondum.
units.tr: Nec-dum: see Nondum.

units.la: Necessaria, pl.] Iusta servis præbenda, Cic. Præbenda, pl. Gell. Requisita, Spart. Copia, Ter. Copiæ, Plin.Iun. Præbita, Suet. Paratus funebris, Tac.
units.tr: Necessaries, pl.: Things to be provided for slaves, Cic. Things to be supplied, pl., Gell. Things required, Spart. Supplies, Ter. Supplies, pl., Plin. Iun. Things furnished, Suet. Funeral provisions, Tac.

units.la: Necessario] Necessitate coguntur esse tales. Æternis causis necessitate manantibus. Fatali necessitate. Non sine multis, & magnis, & necessariis causis. Omnino. Plané : prorsus. Fataliter, Cic. Planissimè. Profectò stabile est, Plaut. Plurimis, maximis, gravissimisque de causis, Cic.
units.tr: Necessarily: They are compelled by necessity to be such. Eternal causes flowing from necessity. By fatal necessity. Not without many and great and necessary causes. Altogether. Plainly, entirely. Fatally, Cic. Most plainly. Assuredly it is firm, Plaut. For very many, very great and most serious reasons, Cic.

units.la: Necessarium charum] Imbre terra gaudet.
units.tr: A necessary dear thing: The earth rejoices in rain.

units.la: Necessaria quare,non superflua] Pellere panem satiùs, quàm purpurâ indui.
units.tr: Necessities, not superfluities: Better to put aside bread than to be clothed in purple.

units.la: Necessarius] Opus eo est. Habet ca res necessitatem, Cic.
units.tr: Necessary: There is need of it. The matter has necessity, Cic.

units.la: Necesse est] Necessum est,Plaut. Necessarium dictu, Plin. Necessitas est, flagitat. Tempus & necessitas flagitat. Moriendum certè est, & id incertum, an eo ipso die. Habet res necessitatem, Cic. Non modò oportet, sed & necesse est, Quint. Si res necessaria vocabit, Sen. Peribis, si non feceris.
units.tr: It is necessary: It is necessary, Plaut. Necessary to say, Plin. Necessity presses and demands. Time and necessity demand it. One must certainly die, and it is uncertain whether it will be on that very day. The matter has necessity, Cic. It is not only fitting but also necessary, Quint. If the necessary matter calls, Sen. You will perish if you do not do it.

units.la: Necessitas ] Necessitudo, cui nullâ vi resisti potest. Articulus temporis,Cic.In tempus amici conferre pecuniam, Id. Articulus necessitatum,Amm. Necessum intestinum, Lucr. Necessitas ultima.
units.tr: Necessity: A close tie, which cannot be resisted by any force. A crisis of time, Cic. To lend money to a friend in his need, Cic. A crisis of needs, Amm. Inner necessity, Lucr. The final necessity.

units.la: Necessitas multa docet] Necessitas magistra, rationum inventrix. Multa docet magistra fames.
units.tr: Necessity teaches much: Necessity is the teacher and the inventor of reasons. Hunger, the teacher, teaches many things.

units.la: Necessitate adigi] Necessitati parere. Vi ac necessitate coactus feci, Cic. Non posse non. Non queo,quin, Plaut. Ita res erat, faciendum fuit, Ter. Expressit hoc illis necessitas, Liv. Necessitate constringi, adstringi, cogi, Cic.
units.tr: To be driven by necessity: To obey necessity. I did it, compelled by force and necessity, Cic. To be unable not to. I cannot but, Plaut. The thing was so; it had to be done, Ter. Necessity wrung this from them, Liv. To be bound fast, drawn tight, compelled by necessity, Cic.

units.la: Necessitas ad multa cogit ] Necessitas durum telum: Legem non habet: Frangit legem. Asinus esuriens fustem negligit. Venter caret auribus. Viro egenti supervacaneus est pudor.
units.tr: Necessity drives to many things: Necessity is a hard weapon. It has no law; it breaks the law. A hungry donkey ignores the stick. The belly has no ears. To a needy man, shame is superfluous.

units.la: Nectere, vid. Nodare.
units.tr: Nectere: see Nodare.

units.la: Nedum] Tantum abest, ut voluptates sectentur; etiam curas, solicitudines perferunt. Tantum abest ut sibi aliquid attribuat; ut etiam moleste ferat,tam multos ad se ire, Cic.
units.tr: Nedum: So far is it from pursuing pleasures that they endure even cares and anxieties. So far is he from claiming anything for himself that he even takes it ill that so many come to him, Cic.

units.la: Nefandus, vid. Infandus.
units.tr: Nefandus: see Infandus.

units.la: Nefarie, Nefarius, vid. Sceleste, &c.
units.tr: Nefarie, Nefarius: see Sceleste, etc.

units.la: Nefas] Indignitas, Quint. Res infanda,nefanda, Cic. Nefandum, Ovid. Infandum facinus, Ter. Nefantia, Varr. Contra fas, legem, Cic.
units.tr: Nefas: Unworthiness, Quint. An unspeakable thing, Cic. Unspeakable, Ovid. An unspeakable deed, Ter. Unspeakable things, Varr. Against divine law, against law, Cic.

units.la: Nefas est] Nefas dictu est. Illicitum est. Non licet mihi, (vel me) facere, Cic. Piaculum est. Flagitium id sit meum, te apud me facere meâ gratiâ sumptum apud me, Plaut. Piatio est. Religiosum est, Plin. Religio est dicere, Ter.
units.tr: It is unlawful: It is unspeakable to say. It is not allowed. It is not permitted for me or me to do this, Cic. It is an expiable offence. Let it be my shame that you have done this at my favour, Plaut. It is an atonement. It is sacred, Plin. It is a scruple to say, Ter.

units.la: Negans] Abnutivus, negatorius, negativus, Sipont. Negibundus, Sipont.
units.tr: Denying: Negative, negatory, negative, Sipont. Inclined to deny, Sipont.

units.la: Negare] Nego ita esse. Inficiari aliquid. Pernegare, Cic. Nego me scisse, Varr. Nego, & negando, si quid refert, ravio. vio. Negitare, Plaut. Inficias ire, Ter. Non fateri. Infite-ri, Fest. Denegare, Propert. Vid. Abnegare.
units.tr: To deny: I deny that it is so. To disown something. To deny utterly, Cic. I deny that I knew, Varr. I deny, and in denying, if it matters, ... To keep denying, Plaut. To refuse to admit, Ter. Not to confess. To disavow, Fest. To refuse, Propert. See Abnegare.

units.la: Non negare, fateri est] Fatentis est silentium. Qui tacet, consentire videtur.
units.tr: Not to deny is to confess: Silence belongs to one who confesses. He who is silent seems to agree.

units.la: Negatio] Inficiatio. Negantia, Cic. Apophasis, Quint.
units.tr: Denial: Denial. Denying, Cic. Apophasis [ἀπόφασις], Quint.

units.la: Neglectus, us] Neglectio amicorum. Incuria rei tam necessariae, Cic. Incultus ; per incultum & negligentiam, Liv.
units.tr: Neglect: Neglect of friends. Carelessness about a matter so necessary, Cic. Lack of cultivation; through neglect and carelessness, Liv.

units.la: Negligens]Negligens sui, Sen. Negligens de aliquâ re, Plin. In aliqua re, Cic. Homo remisso animo, Cic. Remissus animo, Caes. Incuriosus discriminis. Socors futuri, Tacit. Indiligens, Plaut. Supinus, Mart. Perfunctorius, Bud.
units.tr: Negligent: Careless of oneself, Sen. Careless about some matter, Plin. In some matter, Cic. A man of lax mind, Cic. Lax in mind, Caes. Heedless of danger. Careless of the future, Tac. Thoughtless, Plaut. Idle, Mart. Perfunctory, Bud.

units.la: Negligens officii ] Omissior ab re, Ter. Inimicus suae rei. Male gerens rei, Plaut.
units.tr: Negligent of duty: Remiss in his duty, Ter. An enemy to his own affairs. Managing his affairs badly, Plaut.

units.la: Negligenter] Indiligenter. Parum diligenter. Oscitanter, remisse, otiose negotium agere. Molli articulo, & levi brachio. Solute, segniter, dissolute, jejune. Per transsennam aspicere, Cic. Supine, Sen. Temere, Caes. Per nebulam seu caliginem adspicere. Dicis causâ, Cic. Perfunctorie, Papin. Vid. Obiter. Superficialiter.
units.tr: Negligently: Carelessly. Not diligently. Too little diligently. To carry on business lazily, idly, and without attention. With a soft joint and a light arm. Loosely, sluggishly, dissolutely, shallowly. To look through a window, Cic. Supinely, Sen. Rashly, Caes. To look through a mist or fog. For mere show, Cic. Perfunctorily, Papin. See Obiter. Superficially.

units.la: Negligenter agere] Indormire causae. Deesse sibi. Alias res agere, Cic. Parum tibi consulis, Ter. Dormitare, Hor. Supinâ aure aliquem audire, Mart. Vid. Non curare, sub Cur.
units.tr: To act negligently: To fall asleep over one's case. To fail oneself. To attend to other matters, Cic. You take too little thought for yourself, Ter. To doze, Hor. To listen to someone with a careless ear, Mart. See Non curare under Cur.

units.la: Negligentia] Remissio & dissolutio animi. Indiligentia. Oscitatio. Mollitia animi, Cic. Vid. Incuria.
units.tr: Negligence: Relaxation and dissolution of mind. Carelessness. Yawning. Softness of mind, Cic. See Incuria.

units.la: Negligentia damnosa ] Neglectis urenda filix innascitur agris. Cunctatio dispendiosa est. Cunctando res amittitur.
units.tr: Harmful negligence: Fern springs up in neglected fields and must be burned. Delay is costly. By delaying, a matter is lost.

units.la: Negotiari] Mercaturam facere ; instituere. Mercaturis faciendis rem quaerere. Cauponari bellum, Cic. Res inter se contrahere, emendo, vendendo, Liv. Negotiari aliquo genere mercaturae, Col. Negotiari animas, Plaut.
units.tr: To trade: To carry on trade; to set up a business. To seek wealth by trading. To haggle over war, Cic. To make contracts with one another, buying and selling, Liv. To deal in some kind of merchandise, Col. To traffic in souls, Plaut.

units.la: Negotiatio]Mercatio, Gell. Nundinatio bonorum, Cic.
units.tr: Trading: Commerce, Gell. Auctioning of goods, Cic.

units.la: Negotiator] Mercator, Cic. Magnarius, Apul.
units.tr: Trader: Merchant, Cic. A wholesale dealer, Apul.

units.la: Negotiosus] Negotiis plenus, Cic. Vid. Occupatus.
units.tr: Busy: Full of business, Cic. See Occupatus.

units.la: Negotium ] Res mihi est cum aliquo. Qui aliquod munus efficere molitur. Causam suam curare. Provinciam suscipere, Cic. Multùm negotiorum ferunt negotia, Sen. Moles curarum, Tac.
units.tr: Business: I have business with someone. One who sets about performing some duty. To attend to one's own cause. To undertake a charge, Cic. Business brings much business, Sen. A mass of cares, Tac.

units.la: Negotium molestissimum tractare] Hydram secare.
units.tr: To handle a very troublesome business: To cut the Hydra.

units.la: Negotium idem agere] Incudem eandem tundere.
units.tr: To pursue the same business: To beat the same anvil.

units.la: Ad negotium aliquid venire] In aliam terram venire.
units.tr: To come to some business: To come into another land.

units.la: Alienis immiscere se negotiis ] In alieno choro pedem ponere. Falcem in alienam messem immittere.
units.tr: To mix oneself into others' business: To set one's foot in another's dance. To put one's sickle into another's harvest.

units.la: Negotium melius tacite conficitur] Qui sitiunt, silentio bibunt.
units.tr: A business is better done quietly: Those who are thirsty drink in silence.

units.la: Negotium celeriter confectum] Apua ignem vidit.
units.tr: A business quickly finished: Apua saw the fire.

units.la: Negotium examinare] Ruminare negotium.
units.tr: To examine a business: To chew over a business.

units.la: Nemo] Nemo omnium. Nemo omnium hominum. Nemo ex. Nemo unus. Nullus homo, Cic. Nemo hominum. Nemo quisquam. Nemo homo, Ter. Cic. Hominem esse arbitror neminem. Nemo divum, Virg. Natus nemo. Nemo alter, Plaut. Ne unus quidem adest, Cic. Ne musca quidem, Suet. Bona fortuna, pro nullus, Diomed. Charientismus est: cum interrogantibus. Nun quis nos quaesierit? resp. Bona fortuna. Nulla res: Nulla belluarum: nulli de inimicis superunt, Cic. Unus nullus, Non est qui, Apul.
units.tr: No one: No one of all. No one of all men. No one out of. No one alone. No man, Cic. No one among men. No one whatever. No man, Ter., Cic. I think there is no man at all. No one of the gods, Virg. No one born. No other, Plaut. Not even one is present, Cic. Not even a fly, Suet. Good fortune, used for "no one", Diomed. It is a charientismus [χαριεντισμός], when questioners are answered: "Has no one sought us?" Answer: "Good fortune." No thing; no beast; none of the enemies survived, Cic. Not one, none. There is no one who, Apul.

units.la: Nemo semper idem ] Jupiter aliquando pluit, aliquando serenat. Non semper arcum tendit Apollo.
units.tr: No one is always the same: Jupiter sometimes rains and sometimes clears. Apollo does not always bend his bow.

units.la: Nemo judex in propria causa ] Non licet accusare & judicare simul.
units.tr: No one is judge in his own cause: It is not lawful to accuse and judge at the same time.

units.la: Nemus] Saltus, Cic. Densitas arborum in altum exsiliens, Isid. Acherusion, Aristot. Aviarium, Virg.
units.tr: Grove: Woodland, Cic. A dense growth of trees springing up high, Isid. Acherusion [Ἀχερούσιον], Aristot. Aviary, Virg.

units.la: Nepos] Nepotulus, Plaut.
units.tr: Grandson: A little grandson, Plaut.

units.la: Nepotes, vid. Posteri.
units.tr: Nepotes: see Posteri.

units.la: Nequam] Bipedum nequissimus, Plin. Bipedum impurissimus. Homo omnium, qui sunt, qui fuerunt, qui futuri sunt, nequissimus. Certus nebulo. Nebulo certior illo nullus. Homo nequitia singulari praeditus. Delecti ad omne facinus, Cic. Nefandissimum caput. Improbus impense. Graphicus fur, &c. Ab ingenio improbus, Plaut. Homo insigniter malus, Apul. Unica luxuria fuit Sardanapalus, Fest. Filii Belial. Ipsa nequitia nequior. Sardanapalo nequior, Er. Homo insignis omnibus notis turpitudinis, Cic. Vid. Malus.
units.tr: Worthless: The most worthless of two-footed creatures, Plin. The most unclean of two-footed creatures. A man the most worthless of all who are, who have been, and who will be. A sure scoundrel. No scoundrel more certain than he. A man endowed with singular wickedness. Chosen for every crime, Cic. A most abominable head. Shamelessly wicked. A thief of a rare kind, etc. Wicked by nature, Plaut. A man notably bad, Apul. Sardanapalus was the only extravagance, Fest. Sons of Belial. Wickedness itself more wicked. More wicked than Sardanapalus, Er. A man notable for every mark of baseness, Cic. See Malus.

units.la: Neque, vid. Nec.
units.tr: Neque: see Nec.

units.la: Neque doctus, neque probus] Nec literis, nec moribus probatus. Vir est non indoctus modo, verum etiam improbus. bus. Non minùs improbus, quàm illiteratus. Pariter & improbus, & indoctus. Vir cui sit omnino nihil bonarum literarum, bonorum quoque morum tantundem, Er.
units.tr: Neither learned nor upright: Approved neither in letters nor in morals. He is a man not only unlearned but also wicked. No less wicked than unlettered. Equally wicked and unlearned. A man who has absolutely nothing of good letters, and just as little of good morals, Er.

units.la: Nequitia] Per nequitiam aliquid facere, Vlp. Versuta & fallax nocendi ratio. Malitia, per quam insidiæ struuntur alteri, Cic. Solida nequitia, Sen. Solida malefacta, Plaut.
units.tr: Wickedness: To do something through wickedness, Ulp. A crafty and deceitful way of harming. Malice by which snares are laid for another, Cic. Solid wickedness, Sen. Solid misdeeds, Plaut.

units.la: Nere] Torquere fusos, Plin. Ducere lanam, Ovid. Carpere lanam, Plaut. Carpere pensa, Virg. Pernere aliquid, Mart.
units.tr: To spin: To twirl spindles, Plin. To draw out wool, Ovid. To card wool, Plaut. To card out the tasks, Virg. To spin through something, Mart.

units.la: Nervosus ] Venosus. Venosa herba, Plin. Nerviceus, in SS.
units.tr: Nervosus ] Veined. Veined herb, Plin. Sinewy, in SS.

units.la: Nescire] Nescium esse, Haud scire. In summa ignoratione versari. Fugit me ; meam sententiam. Nihil extrico, Cic. Præterit me hæc res. Clam me est, Ter. Latet me, & mihi, Plin. Cic. Incompertum est mihi. Incompertum habeo, Liv. Juxta cum ignarissimis scio, Plaut. Albus an ater sit, nescio. Nescio, quod nescio. Natare non didici. Ne pictum quidem vidit.
units.tr: Nescire] To be ignorant, not to know. To be utterly ignorant. It escapes me; my opinion. I cannot make this out at all, Cic. This matter has escaped my notice. It is hidden from me, Ter. It is hidden from me and from me, Plin. Cic. It is unknown to me. I hold it unknown, Liv. I know it as well as the most ignorant do, Plaut. Whether it is white or black, I do not know. I know not what I do not know. I have not learned to swim. He has not even seen a painted picture.

units.la: Nescio quando] Cras post triginta dies (scil. discedet Cato ; ex Plutarch. quia semper cras se discessurum promittebat, & semper hærebat.) Vid. Nunquam.
units.tr: Nescio quando] Tomorrow, thirty days after (namely, Cato will leave; from Plutarch, because he always promised he would leave tomorrow, and always stayed on.) See Nunquam.

units.la: Quod quis nescit, ne agat ] Habenas ignarus ne tractet. Quodque parum novit nemo docere potest.
units.tr: Quod quis nescit, ne agat ] Let the ignorant man not handle the reins. And no one can teach what he knows little of.

units.la: Nescius, vid. Ignarus.
units.tr: Nescius, see Ignarus.

units.la: Nictare ] Adnictare sæpe, & leviter oculo annuere, Fest. Supercilio penè loquente signa dare. Vibrante supercilio loqui. Verba superciliis, sine voce loquentia dicam, Ovid. Dare signum oculis, Plaut. Nictari, Lucr.
units.tr: Nictare ] To wink often, and lightly nod with the eye, Fest. To give signs almost by speaking with the eyebrow. To speak with a quivering eyebrow. I shall speak with the eyebrows, words speaking without voice, Ovid. To give a sign with the eyes, Plaut. To wink, Lucr.

units.la: Nictatio] Nictus oculorum. Nutus ac renutus, Plin. Signo aliquid dicere, Ovid. Ludibundi oculi, Gell.
units.tr: Nictatio] A winking of the eyes. A nod and a counter-nod, Plin. To tell something by a sign, Ovid. Playful eyes, Gell.

units.la: Nidificare] Nidulari. Internidificare, Plin. Nidum construere, fingere, Cic. Congerere nidamenta in aliquem locum, Plaut. Congerunt aliquò palumbes, Virg. Texere nidos, Quint.
units.tr: Nidificare] To nest, to build a nest. To build nests among, Plin. To build and fashion a nest, Cic. To gather nesting material into some place, Plaut. The wood-pigeons gather together there, Virg. To weave nests, Quint.

units.la: Nidificatio] Congestus avium, Cic.
units.tr: Nidificatio] A gathering together of birds, Cic.

units.la: Nidus] Cubilia & nidi avium. Nidulus, Cic. Cunabula avium, Plin. Habitacula avium, Pallad. Nidamentum, Plaut. Domus avium, Lucr. Nidificium formicarum, Apul.
units.tr: Nidus] Lairs and nests of birds. A little nest, Cic. The cradles of birds, Plin. The dwellings of birds, Pallad. Nesting material, Plaut. The house of birds, Lucr. The nest of ants, Apul.

units.la: Niger] Nigellus, Varr. Perniger, Plaut. Meruleus, Id. Atratus, Cic. Atricolor, Plin. Furvus, Ovid. Piceus, Mart. Anthracinus, Varr. Tam atra, quàm carbo est, Ter. Pice nigrior. Clemate Ægyptiâ nigrior, Er.
units.tr: Niger] Somewhat black, Varr. Very black, Plaut. Dark-coloured, Id. Clad in black, Cic. Black as a coal-colour, Plin. Dusky, Ovid. Pitch-coloured, Mart. Coal-black, Varr. As black as charcoal is, Ter. Blacker than pitch. Blacker than Egyptian clematis, Er.

units.la: Nigrescere]Nigrum colorem trahere,Ovid. Infuscari,Virg. Nigrefieri, Sipont.
units.tr: Nigrescere] To take on a black colour, Ovid. To become dusky, Virg. To become black, Sipont.

units.la: Nigricans] Nigellus, Ausón. Obniger. Languidè niger, Plin. Subniger,Plaut. Infuscus. Infuscatus ; & propemodum niger, Col.
units.tr: Nigricans] Blackish, Ausón. Dark-black. Faintly black, Plin. Somewhat black, Plaut. Dusky. Darkened, and almost black, Col.

units.la: Nigricare] Nigrare, Lucr. Nigrere , Olivæ cùm nigruerint, Col.
units.tr: Nigricare] To be blackish, Lucr. To turn black: when the olives have turned black, Col.

units.la: Nigritudo ] Nigritia, Plin. Nigror, Lucr. Nigritas, Cels. Atritas, Plaut. Atror, Gell. Nigredo, Sipont. S. A. V.
units.tr: Nigritudo ] Blackness, Plin. Blackness, Lucr. Blackness, Cels. Swarthiness, Plaut. Blackness, Gell. Blackness, Sipont. S. A. V.

units.la: Nihil] Nil, Virg. Nihil quicquam. Nihilum : Ex nihilo, in nihilum,ad nihilum. Ne hilum.Ne umbram quidem,Cic. Minus quàm nihil. Ne ciccum quidem. Ne punctum quidem. Ne gry quidem. Nec vola,nec vestigium.Neque remi, neque venti. Æquè quidquam , Ter. Latum unguem. (Gen. 14. pulchra Periphrasis: A filo subtegminis usque corrigiam caligæ non accipiam quicquam.)
units.tr: Nihil] Nil, Virg. Nothing whatever. Nothing: out of nothing, into nothing, to nothing. Not a whit. Not even a shadow, Cic. Less than nothing. Not even a crumb. Not even a point. Not even a grain. Neither palm nor trace. Neither oars nor winds. Anything at all, Ter. Not a nail's breadth. (Gen. 14., a fine periphrasis: I will not take anything from a thread even to a shoe-latchet.)

units.la: Nihil pluris constat, quam quod precibus emitur]Emere malo, quàm rogare. Caro emitur,quod precibus emitur.
units.tr: Nihil pluris constat, quam quod precibus emitur] I would rather buy than ask. What is bought by prayers is bought dearly.

units.la: Nihil scit] Neque natare, neque literas.
units.tr: Nihil scit] He knows neither how to swim nor how to read.

units.la: Nihil credam] Plumbeum nummum non credam.
units.tr: Nihil credam] I will not trust a leaden coin.

units.la: Nihil difficile amanti] Amor docet Musicam.
units.tr: Nihil difficile amanti] Nothing is difficult for a lover. Love teaches music.

units.la: Nihil agas frustra] Frustra niti, dementiæ est.
units.tr: Nihil agas frustra] To strive in vain is madness.

units.la: Nihil dulcius, quàm omnia scire ] Dulcedo cuncta intelligendi, superat omnes suavitates.
units.tr: Nihil dulcius, quàm omnia scire ] The sweetness of understanding everything surpasses all other pleasures.

units.la: Nihil perfectum sub sole] Regula nulla fuit, quam non exceptio torsit. Nulla regula sine exceptione. Nihil ab omni parte beatum, Hor.
units.tr: Nihil perfectum sub sole] There has been no rule that exception has not torn apart. No rule without exception. Nothing is wholly happy in every respect, Hor.

units.la: Nihil proficere]Cum plurimum laboraverimus in eodem statu sumus. Pullus tuus semper parvus.
units.tr: Nihil proficere] However much we have laboured, we remain in the same state. Your chick is always small.

units.la: Nihil interest] Nihil refert quid velis,aut nolis. Parvi mea refert per te facias,an per alium.Quid interest? utrum facias. Equidem haud magno in discrimine pono. Verane sint, an ficta, nihil laboro. Utrum scripseris,an dixeris,nihil laboro. Manum non verterim. Susque deque fero, habeo. Amussis alba in albo lapide, Er.
units.tr: Nihil interest] It makes no difference what you wish or do not wish. It matters little to me whether you do it yourself or through another. What difference does it make whether you do it? I certainly do not set much store by it. Whether they are true or false, I do not care. Whether you have written or spoken, I do not care. I will not lift a finger. I take it lightly, I have it. A plain mark on white stone, Er.

units.la: Nihili homo] Nullo numero homo. Nullo in numero est. Nihil valet. Iners interrogationis genus, Cic. Nauci homo. Homo non nauci, Plaut. (Sicut Cic. Homo non semissis.) Bono usui estis nulli, Plaut. Homo non quisquiliæ, Næv. Homo non sescuncia, Pomp. Frustra est, Sal. Simius, stipes, truncus.
units.tr: Nihili homo] A man of no account. A man of no number. He counts for nothing. He is worth nothing. A lazy kind of question, Cic. A worthless fellow. A man who is no good, Plaut. (Like Cic.: a man not worth half a penny.) You are of no use to anyone, Plaut. A man not worth a pinch, Naev. A man not worth a sixth of a penny, Pomp. A man for nothing, Sal. An ape, a log, a stump.

units.la: Nihili res] Araneorum textura, opera, vestis, tela. Nihil valet. Titivillitium.
units.tr: Nihili res] A thing of no value: a spider's web, a spider's work, a garment, a cobweb. It counts for nothing. A trifle.

units.la: De re nihili rixari, vid. Rixari.
units.tr: De re nihili rixari, see Rixari.

units.la: Nihili facio]Non emam vitiosâ nuce, Plaut. Ciccum, floccum non interduim. Ne nummum quidem impenderim. Ne teruntio quidem id æstimo. Vilius id mihi est, quàm ut obulum ob id perdere velim. Isthoc vilius, Ter. Non Hettæ facio. Non flocci facio. Digitum non porrexerim. Minus de istis laboro, quàm de ranis. Vid. Non Curare.
units.tr: Nihili facio] I will not buy it even with a rotten nut, Plaut. I do not value it a crumb or a jot. I would not spend even a penny on it. I do not value it even at a farthing. It is less to me than that I should lose a halfpenny for it. Cheaper than that, Ter. I do not care for Hetta. I do not care a fig. I would not lift a finger. I care less about those things than about frogs. See Non Curare.

units.la: Nimbosus, vid. Pluviosus.
units.tr: Nimbosus, see Pluviosus.

units.la: Nimis] Immodicè, Col. Effusè. Nimio plus. Plus satis, Plus quàm satis. Plus æquo; nimio. Putidè. Ad insaniam. Præter modum. Satis superque. Nimiopere, Cic. Nimium, Virg. Nimium multùm scis, Plaut. Enormiter, Plin. Perditè & usque ad exemplum, Quint. Nimium quantùm, Præniminis, Gell. Nimium nimiumque, Apul. Supervacuò, Vlp. Immenso plus, Plin. Extra numerum modumque, Hor. Nimiè, Macrob. Plaut.
units.tr: Nimis] Immoderately, Col. Lavishly. Far too much. More than enough. More than is fitting. Foolishly. Beyond measure. To madness. Enough and more than enough. Excessively, Cic. Too much, Virg. You know far too much, Plaut. Monstrously, Plin. Recklessly, to the point of becoming a model, Quint. An enormous amount, Gell. Too much and more, Apul. Superfluously, Ulp. Immensely more, Plin. Beyond number and measure, Hor. Too much, Macrob. Plaut.

units.la: Nimis amat filium] Tenerè amat filium, Er.
units.tr: Nimis amat filium] He loves his son too tenderly, Er.

units.la: Nimis desiderare aliquid] Desiderium alterius non posse ferre.
units.tr: Nimis desiderare aliquid] To long for something too much: to be unable to bear another's absence.

units.la: Nimius]Multus in re quâpiam, Cic. Immoderatus, Tac.
units.tr: Nimius] Excessive in some matter, Cic. Immoderate, Tac.

units.la: Nimia velle damnosum] Perdit totum, qui non vult nisi totum.
units.tr: Nimia velle damnosum] He who wants only the whole thing loses the whole.

units.la: Nimia sunt nociva]Nimia omnia nimium exhibent negotium. Segetem iternit nimia ubertas. Rami nimio onere franguntur. Arcus nimis intensus rumpitur. Nimium mungens elicit sanguinem. Profundior risus lacrymas parit. Nimia familiaritas contemptum parit. Nimium festinans serius absolvit. Nimia nimiam pariunt molestiam. Vive tibi, tecumtecumque habita, nec grandia tentes. Effugit immodicas parvula puppis aquas, Ovid.
units.tr: Nimia sunt nociva] Excesses all bring trouble. Too much abundance spoils the crop. Branches break under too great a weight. A bow drawn too tight snaps. Pricking too hard draws blood. Deeper laughter brings tears. Excessive familiarity breeds contempt. Hurrying too much finishes later. Excess brings excessive trouble. Live for yourself, dwell with yourself wherever you are, and do not attempt great things. The little boat escapes the excessive waters, Ovid.

units.la: Nimia felicitas] Gygis annulus. Fortunati pileus. Aureum vellus, Aurea pecus.
units.tr: Nimia felicitas] The ring of Gyges. The cap of the fortunate man. The golden fleece, the golden flock.

units.la: Ningit] Bruma nives illinit agris, Hor.
units.tr: Ningit] Winter smears snow over the fields, Hor.

units.la: Nisi] Præter si aliter nequeas, Varr. Nisi si, Col. Excepto quod, Hor.
units.tr: Nisi] Unless you can do otherwise, Varr. Unless, Col. Except that, Hor.

units.la: Nisus] Accipiter minor, Gesn. Accipiter fringillarius, Gaz. Abert. Gesn.
units.tr: Nisus] A smaller hawk, Gesn. A sparrow-hawk, Gaz. Abert. Gesn.

units.la: Nisus, ûs, vid. Conatus.
units.tr: Nisus, ûs, see Conatus.

units.la: Nitere] Nitet ut oleum, Plaut. Micat ardor ex oculis, Lucr. Renitent, internitent gemmæ, Plin. Renidet orichalcum, Stat. Crispatur sole pelagus, Val. Arg. Pellucent littora lapillis, Prop. Enitescit cultus, Quint. Splendicant gemmæ, Apul. Coruscare. Enitet opus picturis, Cic. Rutilant arma. Splendet lumine pontus. Splendescit vomer attritus. Nitescit oleo perfusa juventus, Virg.
units.tr: Nitere] It shines like oil, Plaut. Fire flashes from the eyes, Lucr. Gems glitter back and forth, Plin. Bronze gleams, Stat. The sea glitters in the sun, Val. Arg. The shores sparkle with pebbles, Prop. Polished elegance shines out, Quint. Gems sparkle, Apul. To glitter. The work shines with paintings, Cic. The arms flash. The sea shines with light. The worn ploughshare gleams. The youth, anointed with oil, shines, Virg.

units.la: Niti] Inniti hasta, Liv. Membra levare baculo. Sustinere artus baculo, Ovid. Adniti hastis, Virg. Vid. Inniti.
units.tr: Niti] To lean on a spear, Liv. To rest the limbs on a staff. To support the limbs with a staff, Ovid. To lean on spears, Virg. See Inniti.

units.la: Niti præsidiis incertis] In caducum parietem inclinare.
units.tr: Niti præsidiis incertis] To lean on unsafe supports: to lean against a falling wall.

units.la: Nitidus, vid. Pulcher.
units.tr: Nitidus, see Pulcher.

units.la: Nitor] Splendor argenti. Fulgor armorum, Hor. Radiatio marmoris, Plin. Jubar galeæ, Stat. Nitela armorum, Solin. Refulgentia lacunarum, Apul.
units.tr: Nitor] The sheen of silver. The glitter of arms, Hor. The radiance of marble, Plin. The gleam of a helmet, Stat. The brightness of arms, Solin. The shining of ceilings, Apul.

units.la: Nitrosus] Nitrata aqua, Mart.
units.tr: Nitrosus] Water impregnated with nitre, Mart.

units.la: Nitrum] Halonitrum. Sal petræ. Sal petrosus. Sal nitri, Iun. Sal nitrum, Plin.
units.tr: Nitrum] Halonitrum. Rock salt. Stony salt. Salt of nitre, Iun. Nitrum salt, Plin.

units.la: Nivalis] Nivosa hiems, Liv. Niveus agger, Virg. Ninguidus mensis, Sidon. Auson.
units.tr: Nivalis] A snowy winter, Liv. A snowy mound, Virg. A snowy month, Sidon. Auson.

units.la: Nix] Nigor, Apul. Tacitarum vellus aquarum, Mart. Plumeæ crustulæ, nives. Arnob. Pluma, quibus foventur segetes. Brumæ pabulum. Flos brumæ. Lætamen agrorum, Siccescentes aquæ. Syrtes nivales: tumuli nivales.
units.tr: Nix] Whiteness, Apul. The fleece of silent waters, Mart. Feathery flakes, snows, Arnob. Down with which the crops are kept warm. The food of winter. The flower of winter. The manure of fields. Waters that are drying up. Snowy Syrtes: snowy mounds.

units.la: Nobilis] Nobili genere natus, Salust. Equestri, nobili loco natus, Cic. Clarus natalibus, Tac. Prosapiâ nobili editus, Amm. Veteris prosapiæ & multarum imaginum homo, Sal. Tria nomina habens (prænomen, nomen, cognomen) Iuv. Bene natus, Hor. Cerâ & æ re nobilis, Vir apprimè nobilis. Minimè obscuris natalibus. Homo minimè novus. Homo cum primis illustris. Vir antiquæ nobilitatis. Vir honesto apud suos loco natus. Summo loco natus. Domi splendidus. Majorum imaginibus clarus. Ex illustri progenitus, Er.
units.tr: Nobilis] Born of noble stock, Sall. Born of equestrian and noble rank, Cic. Famous by birth, Tac. Born of a noble lineage, Amm. A man of ancient lineage and many ancestral images, Sall. Having three names (praenomen, nomen, cognomen), Juv. Well-born, Hor. Noble in wax and bronze (renowned for ancestral likenesses). A man of very noble birth. Of no obscure parentage. Not a new man. A man among the foremost and most illustrious. A man of ancient nobility. A man born in an honourable place among his own people. Born of high rank. Splendid at home. Famous for the images of his ancestors. Descended from an illustrious line, Er.

units.la: Nobiles decet virtus] Bene natum turpe est malè vivere.
units.tr: Nobiles decet virtus] Virtue befits the noble. It is shameful for one who is well born to live badly.

units.la: Nobilitare] Restituere aliquem natalibus, Plin. Iun. Jus annuli alicui donare, Bud. Annulis aureis aliquem donare, Suet.
units.tr: Nobilitare] To restore someone to his birth, Plin. Iun. To grant someone the right of the gold ring, Bud. To present someone with gold rings, Suet.

units.la: Nobilitari] Jus annulorum à Principe impetrare, vel, obtinere. Venire in nobilitatem, Plaut.
units.tr: To be ennobled: To obtain the right of the ring from the Prince, or to get it. To come into nobility, Plaut.

units.la: Nobilitas] Nobilitas generis. Per tuam nobilitatem. Per tuas statuas, Cic. Natales clari, Tac. Prosapiæ claritudo. Amm.
units.tr: Nobility: Nobility of birth. Through your nobility. Through your statues, Cic. Distinguished birth, Tac. The fame of one's lineage, Amm.

units.la: Nobilitatio] Novitas, Salust. Novitas generis, Cic. Subitæ imagines, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Ennoblement: Newness, Sall. Newness of birth, Cic. Sudden ancestral images, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Nobilitatus demum] Homo novus. Homo à se natus; per se cognitus. Ex se nobilitatus. Nulla commendatione majorum, Cic. Homo novus honore & gloriâ, Id.
units.tr: Newly ennobled: A new man. A man born of himself, known through himself, ennobled by himself. With no recommendation from ancestors, Cic. A new man in honour and glory, Id.

units.la: Nocenter, vid. Damnose.
units.tr: Harmfully: see Damnose.

units.la: Nocere] Nocere noxam. Esse noxæ alicui, Liv. Afficere aliquem incommodo. Incommodare alicui. Arrodere Remp. Vulnus imponere provinciæ, Reip. plagam, securim injicere alicui. Injungere detrimentum alicui, Cic. Attondere aliquem. Officere alicui. Exitium afferre, Plaut. Damno esse alicui, Plin. Infensare pabula, Tac.
units.tr: To harm: To do harm. To be a harm to someone. To afflict someone with an inconvenience. To inconvenience someone. To gnaw at the commonwealth. To lay a wound on a province, to deal a blow to the state, to put the axe to someone. To inflict loss on someone, Cic. To clip someone short. To stand in someone's way. To bring ruin, Plaut. To be a loss to someone, Plin. To ravage the pastures, Tac.

units.la: Nocet aliquid stomacho] Pyrorum esus stomacho gravis. Dulcia stomachum lædunt. Acida concoctioni officiunt. Salsa noxia sunt hepati. Lac virilem stomachum offendit. Erasm.
units.tr: Something harms the stomach: Eating pears is heavy on the stomach. Sweet things injure the stomach. Sour things hinder digestion. Salty things are harmful to the liver. Milk offends a man's stomach, Erasm.

units.la: Nocere sibi ipsi turpe] Bis interimitur, qui suis armis perit.
units.tr: To harm oneself is shameful: He dies twice who perishes by his own weapons.

units.la: Nocere possunt eadem, quæ prosunt] Ægrotamus ex his, quibus valemus. Unde cibus, inde Venenum.
units.tr: The same things that can harm can also help: We fall sick from the very things by which we are kept well. Whence comes food, thence comes poison.

units.la: Nocebit tibi &c.] Fraudi erit tibi, Vlp.
units.tr: It will harm you, etc.: It will be to your detriment, Ulp.

units.la: Nocivus] Noxius. Perniciosus, Cic. Nocens, Hor. Noxiosissimum animal, Sen. Inimicus, Plin. Dispade nocentior, Er. Vid. Damnosus. Exitialis.
units.tr: Harmful: Hurtful. Pernicious, Cic. Hurtful, Hor. A most harmful animal, Sen. Hostile, Plin. More harmful than Dispas, Erasm. See Damnosus and Exitialis.

units.la: Noctle]
units.tr: At night

units.la: Nocte]. Noctu. Noctuabundus ad me venit, Cic. Multa noctu,Macrob. Sub nocte rudentium leonum, Virg. Per noctem cernuntur sidera,Plin. Nocturnus obambulat,Virg. Sub noctem, Caes.
units.tr: By night: By night. He came to me wandering at night, Cic. Much at night, Macrob. Under the night of roaring lions, Virg. The stars are seen through the night, Plin. The wanderer of the night goes about, Virg. Towards nightfall, Caes.

units.la: Nocte serena] Apricante noctu coelo.
units.tr: In a clear night: With the sky basking at night.

units.la: Nocte multa]Nocte provecta, Amm. Producere noctem vino, Mart. Multo jam noctis serum auxilium venit, Tac. Plerumque noctis processit, Salust. Intempesta nocte, Fest. Ad multam noctem vigilare ; producere convivium. De multa nocte profectus, Cic.
units.tr: Late at night: With the night advanced, Amm. To prolong the night with wine, Mart. Help came late, when much of the night was gone, Tac. For the most part the night had advanced, Sall. In the dead of night, Fest. To keep watch far into the night; to prolong a feast. To set out from the middle of the night, Cic.

units.la: Nocte tota ] In multo nox est pervigilata mero, Ovid. Noctem trahere per pocula, Mart. Perpete nocte alea ludere, Iul. Cap. Producere noctem vino, Mart. Transmittere noctem operi, Pers. Pernox est, Liv.
