units.tr: All night: The night was spent awake over much wine, Ovid. To drag the night out over cups, Mart. To play dice through the whole night, Iul. Cap. To prolong the night with wine, Mart. To spend the night at work, Pers. It is a night-long vigil, Liv.

units.la: Noctescit]Nocte opprimi, Cic. Contenebrat, Varr. Intendunt se tenebrae, Liv. Maturato sol praecedit vespere lucem, Lucan.
units.tr: It grows dark: To be overtaken by night, Cic. It grows dark, Varr. The shadows spread, Liv. The hastening sun goes before the light with the evening, Lucan.

units.la: Noctu medium] Noctis meridies, Varr. Nox intempesta, Lucr. Marcipore, Scal. Sipont.
units.tr: Midnight: The midday of the night, Varr. The dead of night, Lucr. Marcipore, Scal. Sipont.

units.la: Qui nocte ambulat, offendit]Noctu saxa volant.
units.tr: He who walks by night stumbles: Stones fly at night.

units.la: Noctivagus]Nocturnus, Cic. Tenebricola, Plaut. Vespertilio, Erasm.
units.tr: Wandering by night: Nocturnal, Cic. Dweller in shadows, Plaut. Bat, Erasm.

units.la: Noctu heluones, interdiu dormientes] Antipodes.
units.tr: Those who feast by night and sleep by day: Antipodes.

units.la: Noctua ] Lucifuga. Noctivida ales, Mart. Solem nesciens. Noctis monstrum.
units.tr: Owl: Light-shunning. A bird that hates the daylight, Mart. Ignorant of the sun. A monster of the night.

units.la: Nodare] Nodis nectere, Virg. Vincire connexis nodis, Ovid. Innodare, Sipont. Innodum torquere, Mart.
units.tr: To tie in knots: To tie with knots, Virg. To bind with knotted cords, Ovid. To entangle, Sipont. To twist into a knot, Mart.

units.la: Nodosus] Renodis capillus, Capitol.
units.tr: Knotted: Hair tied up again in knots, Capitol.

units.la: Nodus]Nodulus,Pli.Currax nodus,Grat.Nexus nodi,Pli.
units.tr: Knot: A little knot, Plin. A tight knot, Grat. The binding of a knot, Plin.

units.la: Noëma] Sententia, sententiola,Cic. Senticulus,Quint. Diverbium,Ausón. Depascimur (ut apes) aurea dicta (legendo libros) perpetuâ semper dignissima vitâ, Lucr. Dicta laudis annotamentis digna,Gell. Quae aliis declamantibus laudata sunt, Quint. Laudabilia scholastica, Scal.
units.tr: Thought [νόημα]: A maxim, a little maxim, Cic. A little sentence, Quint. A witty saying, Ausón. "Like bees, we feed on golden sayings from reading books, always most worthy of lasting life," Lucr. Sayings worthy of being recorded for their praise, Gell. Things praised by other declaimers, Quint. Scholastic praiseworthy sayings, Scal.

units.la: Nola, vid. Campana.
units.tr: Nola: see Campana.

units.la: Nolens feci] Nollem hanc injuriam tibi à me factam, Ter. Imprudens feci. Insciens feci. Nollem dixisse, Cicer.
units.tr: I did it unwillingly: I would not have wished this wrong done to you by me, Ter. I did it without thinking. I did it unknowingly. I would rather not have said it, Cic.

units.la: Nolens non multùm peccat] Involuntarium veniâ dignum.
units.tr: One who is unwilling does not sin much: What is involuntary is worthy of pardon.

units.la: Nolens volens] Ægrè quidem , sed facimus tamen.
units.tr: Willy-nilly: Grudgingly, indeed, but we do it all the same.

units.la: Nolle] Minimè velle, Cic. Negatire,Ovid. Recusat,Hor. Renutat, Lucr. In præsenti animus non est, Er.
units.tr: To be unwilling: To be by no means willing, Cic. To refuse, Ovid. He declines, Hor. He refuses, Lucr. The mind is not in the present, Erasm.

units.la: Nomen] Vocamen proprium,Lucr. Appellatio,Cic. Cognomen loci,Virg.
units.tr: Name: A proper name, Lucr. An appellation, Cic. The surname of a place, Virg.

units.la: Nomen habere] Est mihi nomen Mercurii. Est mihi nomen Auxilio, Plaut. Ísto nomine eum appellant. Hoc proprio signata est nomine, Cic. Ex vero nomine vocor Miccotrogus,Plaut. Nomen est mihi Julii, Julio, Julium,Gell. Ei morbo nomen est avaritia, Cic. Nomen habet Fabius, Ovid. Appellor hoc nomine. Sustineo nomen publicani,Cic. Victor clueo, Plaut. Audio callidus, Hor. Sic illos nomine dicunt. Dicor, Virg. Obtinere nomen,Cic. Referre, Virg. Cognomen ex aliqua re trahere, sumere, invenire, Cic.
units.tr: To have a name: My name is Mercury. My name is Auxilium, Plaut. They call him by this name. He is marked by this proper name, Cic. I am called Miccotrogus by my true name, Plaut. My name is Julius, Julio, Julium, Gell. That disease is called avarice, Cic. Fabius has the name, Ovid. I am called by this name. I bear the name of publican, Cic. I am called Victor, Plaut. I am called clever, Hor. Thus they call them by name. I am called, Virg. To keep a name, Cic. To carry back a name, Virg. To take, assume or find a surname from some thing, Cic.

units.la: Nomen dare militiæ, &c.] Profiteri nomen, Liv. Dare nomen in coloniam, Id. Ad molariam coloniam, Plaut.
units.tr: To give one's name to military service, etc.: To enrol one's name, Liv. To give one's name for a colony, Id. To a colony of millers, Plaut.

units.la: Nomenclator] Nomenculator,Quint. A memoria,Lampr. Appellare cives per monitorem,Cic. Ab aure famulus.
units.tr: Nomenclator: A nomenclator, Quint. From memory, Lampr. To call citizens by name with a prompter, Cic. A servant at the ear.

units.la: Nomina rebus similia] Conveniunt rebus nomina sæpe suis. Ex re nomen habet. Nomini suo respondens. Imperator vere sui nominis, i. Probus, Trebell.
units.tr: Names similar to things: Names often suit their things. Has its name from the thing. Answering to its name. A true emperor of his name, that is, Probus, Trebell.

units.la: Nomina impedita] Non apparet ratio argenti,Plaut. Summa rationem excurrens, Cic.
units.tr: Unclear accounts: The reckoning of the silver does not appear, Plaut. Running over the sum of the account, Cic.

units.la: Nominatim] Nomine aliquem compellare, Liv. Per nomina citare mancipia, Col.
units.tr: By name: To address someone by name, Liv. To summon slaves by name, Col.

units.la: Nominatim appellare aliquem ] Pronunciare victorum nomina. Prosequi omnes nominatim, Cic. Ciere aliquem Perciere, Plaut.
units.tr: To name someone individually: To proclaim the names of the victors. To follow all of them by name, Cic. To summon someone, to call out, Plaut.

units.la: Nominare] Nominitare, Lucr. Nomine Dei aliquem nuncupare. Appellare : appellitare. Notare rem nomine. Perhibere aliquem claro nomine. Verbum aliquod in aliquo ponere. Nomen imponere, Cic. Nomen alicui indere, dicere, facere, Liv. Dare alicui vocamen, Solin. Præno minare, Varr. Vocare nomine, Plaut. Cognomen imponere, Plin. Facere, Liv. Cognominare, Pli. Indigitare, Macr. Perhiberi aliquem probum, Ter. Vocitare, Cic. Phalereus vocitatus est.
units.tr: To name: To name, Lucr. To call someone by the name of God. To call; to call often. To mark a thing with a name. To give someone a famous name. To put a word upon someone. To impose a name, Cic. To bestow a name on someone, Liv. To give someone a name, Solin. To name by the praenomen, Varr. To call by name, Plaut. To impose a surname, Plin. To make, Liv. To surname, Plin. To name, Macr. To be called good, Ter. To call, Cic. Phalereus was called so.

units.la: Nominari] Sustinere nomen, Cic. Referre nomen avi, Virg. Vid. Nomen habere.
units.tr: To be named: To bear a name, Cic. To bear a grandfather's name, Virg. See To have a name.

units.la: Nominatio] Nominatus, Varr. Nomenclatio, Col. Nomenclatura. Nuncupatio, Amm. Usurpatio nominum, Plin. Impositio nominis, Varr.
units.tr: Nomination: A being named, Varr. Nomenclature, Col. Nomenclature. Proclamation, Amm. Use of names, Plin. Imposition of a name, Varr.

units.la: Nomine alicujus facere] Nomine alterius cuipiam gratulari, Cic. Vid. Loco.
units.tr: To act in someone's name: To congratulate someone in another's name, Cic. See Loco.

units.la: Non] Haud, Plaut. Haud quaquam. Nihil minus. Minus intellexi. Nequaquam, Cic. Nihil, Virg. Nullo pacto: nullo modo possum, Ter. Nunquam hodie effugies, Virg.
units.tr: Not: Not at all, Plaut. By no means. Not in the least. I understood less. In no way, Cic. Nothing, Virg. In no way: I cannot in any manner, Ter. You will not escape today, Virg.

units.la: Non omnia possumus omnes] Condire recte non est cujusvis.
units.tr: We cannot all do everything: To season well is not for everyone.

units.la: Non est de nihilo] Quaestio non est tribularis.
units.tr: It is not a trifling matter: The question is no small one.

units.la: Non modo, sed &] Non modo non intelligit, sed ne legit quidem. Non solum parum intelligit, sed ne legit. Non tantum parum intelligit, imo nec legit. Ne legere quidem novit, nedum intelligat. Non novit vel intelligere, tantum abest ut intelligat. Tantum abest ab intelligendo, ut ne legere quidem norit. Usque adeo non intelligit, ut nesciat vel legere. Hic in Graecis literis nihil, quid dicam intelligere, imo nec legere potest. Hic nihil in bonis literis, non dicam non intelligit, imo ne legit quidem, Erasm.
units.tr: Not only... but also: He not only does not understand, but does not even read. He understands little, and does not even read. He understands little, indeed he does not even read. He does not even know how to read, let alone understand. He does not understand, so far is he from understanding that he does not even know how to read. He cannot read Greek letters, let alone understand what I would call understanding. He does not understand the good letters, I will not say, and indeed does not even read them, Erasm.

units.la: Non sic] Non ita se habet, ex Ter. Non ita se res habet; Cic.
units.tr: It is not so: The matter does not stand thus, Ter. The matter does not stand so, Cic.

units.la: Nondum] Necdum, Liv. Dum. Nihil dum sciebat, Cic. Nulla-dum via superatas Alpes, Nequedum, Cels.
units.tr: Not yet: Not yet, Liv. He did not yet know anything, Cic. The Alps had not yet been crossed by any road, Cels.

units.la: Nonnihil. Nonnunquam, vid. Aliquando, &c.
units.tr: Somewhat, sometimes: see Aliquando, etc.

units.la: Norma] Ariadnes filum.
units.tr: Rule: Ariadne's thread.

units.la: Normalis] Normatus. Orthogonius ager, Col.
units.tr: Regular: Regulated. A field laid out at right angles, Col.

units.la: Noscere] Novi de facie aliquem. Cognoscere. Habere notitiam alicujus rei. Habere aliquid notum: notitiam veri & falsi. Habere notum perspectumque, Est mihi notum aliquid. Teneo voluntatem ejus. Intelligere in re aliqua, Cic. Nosse viae suae rationem, Sen. Callere sensum alicujus, Ter. Sentire, Hor.
units.tr: To know: I know someone by face. To recognise. To have knowledge of a thing. To have something known: knowledge of true and false. To have something known and clearly perceived. I have something known to me. I hold his will. To understand in some matter, Cic. To know the way of one's own course, Sen. To understand someone's feelings, Ter. To perceive, Hor.

units.la: Nosse bene] Nosse aliquem familiariter, Quint. Intus & in cute novi te.
units.tr: To know well: To know someone intimately, Quint. I know you inside and out.

units.la: Non nosse] Ne umbram quidem ejus novit.
units.tr: Not to know: He does not even know his shadow.

units.la: Nosler est] Nostras, Cic. Nostri gregis. Nostræ farinæ.
units.tr: Ours is: Ours, Cic. Of our flock. Of our kind.

units.la: Nostrâ ætate] Meâ memoriâ. Nostrâ & patrum memoriâ usu venit. Ut mea est memoria. Nobis pueris, Cic.
units.tr: In our age: In my memory. It happened in our memory and that of our fathers. As far as my memory goes. When we were boys, Cic.

units.la: Nota] Notula, Sipont. Indicium, Vestigium, Cic. vid. Sign.
units.tr: Mark: A little mark. A sign, a trace, Cic. See Sign.

units.la: Notis suis unumquodque agnoscitur] Cauda devulpe testatur.
units.tr: Each thing is known by its marks: The stripped tail bears witness.

units.la: Notabilis] Insignis maculis, Virg. Conspicuus colore, Col. Nobilis vitiis. Luculentus patronus, Cic. Notabilis favor, Suet. Observabilis, Quint. Celebrabilis favor, Amm. Insignitæ & acres imagines. Perinsignis pravitas, Cic. Præsignis vertice hasta, Stat. Insignis res ad laudem, Cic.
units.tr: Notable: Marked with spots, Virg. Conspicuous in colour, Col. Notorious for faults. A distinguished advocate, Cic. Notable favour, Suet. Worthy of notice, Quint. Celebrated favour, Amm. Distinguished and keen images. Remarkable wickedness, Cic. A spear conspicuous at the top, Stat. A matter remarkable for praise, Cic.

units.la: Notabiliter] Insignitè improbus, Insigniter diligere, Cic. Enormiter admittere in se, Plin. Notabilius turbans, Tac.
units.tr: Notably: Conspicuously wicked. To love conspicuously, Cic. To commit excessively, Plin. Disturbing more notably, Tac.

units.la: Notare] Denotare pedes, Plin. Insignire annum cladibus. Persignare aliquid, Designare notâ ignominiæ, Liv. Apponere notam ad malum versum; Cic. Signare humum limite, Ovid. Vid. Signare.
units.tr: To mark: To mark feet, Plin. To mark the year with disasters. To mark something as a token of disgrace, Liv. To put a mark against a bad line, Cic. To mark the ground with a furrow, Ovid. See Signare.

units.la: Notarius Publicus] Scripturarius, Lucil. Magister scripturæ, Cic. Tabularius, Ulp. Scriba, qui rationes publicas scribit, Fest. Actuarius, Suet. Censualis, Iul. Cap. Commentariensis, Paul. IC. A punctis, Frontin. Numerarius, Amm.
units.tr: Public notary: Scribe, Lucil. Teacher of writing, Cic. Keeper of records, Ulp. A clerk who writes up the public accounts, Fest. Recorder, Suet. Census clerk, Iul. Cap. Record-keeper, Paul. IC. Clerk of the tally, Frontin. Accountant, Amm.

units.la: Notatio] Animadversio. Observatio, Cic. Deprehensio, Varr. Affectatio, Plin.
units.tr: Notation: Censure. Observation, Cic. Detection, Varr. Affectation, Plin.

units.la: Notatus] Signatus, Virg. Notatissimus maculis omnium scelerum, Cic. Nummus in vultum Principis effigiatus, Amm. Nummos Alexandri habitu figuravit, Lamp.
units.tr: Marked: Branded, Virg. Stained with the marks of every crime, Cic. A coin stamped with the Prince's likeness, Amm. He stamped coins with Alexander's bearing, Lamp.

units.la: Notescere] Agnosci, Cic. Venire in notitiam. Innotescere, Ovid. Inclarescere, Plin.
units.tr: To become known: To be recognised, Cic. To come into notice. To become known, Ovid. To grow famous, Plin.

units.la: Nothus, vid. Spurius.
units.tr: Bastard: see Spurius.

units.la: Notitia] Notio veri & falsi, Cic. Scientia futurorum: de re aliquâ, Cognitio legum, Cic. In Conscientiam assumere aliquem, Tac.
units.tr: Notion: Understanding of truth and falsehood, Cic. Knowledge of future events; knowledge of some matter; acquaintance with the laws, Cic. To take someone into one's confidence, Tac.

units.la: Notus omnibus] Res nota atque omnibus pervulgata: Notissima. Penitus perspecta, planeque cognita. Decantata. In ore vulgi atque in omnibus proverbiis versatur. Spectata & cognita fides alicujus. Audita, pervulgata, & percelebrata res sermonibus. Pervagata fama. Pervagatissimus tissimus ille versus. Perfamiliaris alicui, & alicujus, Cic. Id gnarum est Neroni, Tac. Gnobilis facies: gnobilis oculis meis, Plaut. Testata res in omne tempus, Ovid. Lippis & tonsoribus, inferis & superis nota.
units.tr: Known to all: A matter known and widely published, most notorious. Thoroughly examined and plainly known. Sung about everywhere. It is on the lips of the crowd and in all the proverbs. A proven and well-known loyalty of someone. A thing heard, passed about and much talked of in conversation. A rumour spread far and wide. That most widely spread verse. Very intimate with someone, Cic. This is known to Nero, Tac. A face well known: well known to my eyes, Plaut. A matter attested for all time, Ovid. Known to the bleary-eyed and the barbers, to the dead and the living.

units.la: Novacula] Culter tonsorius. Scalpellum, Cic. Scalpellus, Celf. Scalper excisorius, &, Scalprum, Id. Culter tonsoris, Pli.
units.tr: Razor: A barber's knife. A scalpel, Cic. A small surgical knife, Celsus. A cutting chisel, and a scraper, Id. A barber's knife, Plin.

units.la: Novale ] Novalis ager, Varr. Inarata terra, Virg. Requietum arvum, Col.
units.tr: Fallow land: Land left to fallow, Varr. Unploughed ground, Virg. Land left to rest, Col.

units.la: Novare, vid. Renovare, &c.
units.tr: To renew: see Renovate, etc.

units.la: Novator ] Reparator ævi, Stat. Reformator literarum, Plin. Innovator, Henr. Steph.
units.tr: Innovator: Restorer of the age, Stat. Reformer of letters, Plin. Innovator, Henr. Steph.

units.la: Nové] Novum in modum, Plaut. Neotericè, Ausson.
units.tr: Newly: In a new manner, Plaut. In the modern fashion, Ausson.

units.la: Nova de novis rebus judicia, & successus inæquales] Eventus varios res nova semper habet.
units.tr: New judgements about new matters, and unequal outcomes: Events vary; a new thing always has varied results.

units.la: Nova placent ] Novum cribrum novo paxillo pendeat. Plures adorant solem orientem, quàm occidentem. Novitas grata.
units.tr: New things please: Let a new sieve hang on a new peg. More people worship the rising sun than the setting one. Novelty is welcome.

units.la: Novilunium] Nova luna, Cic. Nascens luna, Hor.
units.tr: New moon: The new moon, Cic. The waxing moon, Hor.

units.la: Novum quid & ignotum alicui ] In alio mundo sibi videri, atque esse.
units.tr: Something new and unknown to someone: To seem to himself to be in another world, and to be so.

units.la: Novus] Novitius, Plin. Novatus. Nullo exemplo factus: novo exemplo factus, Cic. Recens homo, Hor. Neotericus, Ascon.
units.tr: New: Newly trained, Plin. Renewed. Made without precedent: made on a new model, Cic. A new man, Hor. Modern, Ascon.

units.la: Novus homo ] Ab aliquo natus. Nitedula ex vepreculis. Repentinus homo, Cic. Terræ filius, Casau. Lumbricus, Plaut.
units.tr: Upstart: Born of someone of no account. A nobody from the brambles. A sudden upstart, Cic. A son of the earth, Casaubon. An earthworm, Plaut.

units.la: Novus nuptus] Novus maritus, Plaut. Novus vir, Propert. Recens maritus, Plin. Iun. Juvenis maritus, Tibul.
units.tr: Newly married: A new husband, Plaut. A new husband, Propert. A recent husband, Plin. Iun. A young husband, Tibul.

units.la: Nox]Nocturnum spatium, Cic. Quietis reductrix. Somni genitrix. Curarum domitrix.
units.tr: Night: The span of night, Cic. Bringer of rest. Mother of sleep. Tamer of cares.

units.la: Nox serena ] Nox sideribus illustris, Tac. Pernox luna erat, Liv. Nox siderea, Val. Argon.
units.tr: Clear night: A night bright with stars, Tac. The moon was very clear all night, Liv. A starry night, Val. Argon.

units.la: Nox sublustris] Sublustris umbra noctis. Lux maligna. Incerta luna, Virg. Lux lunæ ambigua, Am. Dubia luna, Ovid.
units.tr: Dim night: The dim shade of night. Baleful light. An uncertain moon, Virg. An ambiguous moonlight, Am. A doubtful moon, Ovid.

units.la: Noxa, vid. Crimen. Noxius. Nocivus.
units.tr: Harm: see Crime. Harmful. Hurtful.

units.la: Nubes] Nubilum, Plin. Velamentum cœli. Umbraculum terræ. Vehiculum ventorum. Refrigerium æstuantium. Pluviarum mater. Nubere] Enubere, Liv. Denubere in familiam alicujus, Tac. Convenire in manum alicui. Conjungere connubia, Cic. In luculentam familiam sponsa collocata est, Plaut. Innubere alicui, Liv. In maximas divitias desponsa est. In conditionem se dignam collocata est, Plaut.
units.tr: Cloud: Cloudiness, Plin. The veil of the sky. The shade of the earth. The carriage of the winds. The coolness of the sweltering. Mother of rains. To marry: To marry out, Liv. To marry into someone's family, Tac. To come into someone's hand in marriage. To join in wedlock, Cic. The bride was settled in a splendid household, Plaut. To marry into someone's family, Liv. She was betrothed to very great wealth. She was settled in a suitable station, Plaut.

units.la: Nubilis] Matura viro. Filia nubilis. Filia plenis annis, Virg. Filia grandis dotem poscit, Mart. Viripotens, Vlp. Virgo tempestiva viro, Hor.
units.tr: Marriageable: Ripe for a husband. A marriageable daughter. A daughter of full years, Virg. A grown daughter asks for a dowry, Mart. Able to marry, Ulp. A maiden ripe for a husband, Hor.

units.la: Nubilum] Nubilosum, turbidum coelum, Cic. Dubium & impendens coelum, Sen.
units.tr: Cloudy: A cloudy, troubled sky, Cic. A doubtful and threatening sky, Sen.

units.la: Nubilus dies] Turbidus. Nubilans, Plin. Nebulosum coelum. Caliginosus, Cic. Prænubilus, Ovid.
units.tr: Cloudy day: Troubled. Growing overcast, Plin. A cloudy sky. Dim, Cic. Overcast beforehand, Ovid.

units.la: Nubilum fieri] Pendent nubila, Virg. Nubila obducuntur, surgunt, Plin. Nubilus est coeli status, Col. Serenam mundi faciem nubes violant. Subtexunt coelum nubila, Lucr. Inglomerat noctem Auster, Stat. Contristat Auster coelum frigore pluvio, Virg.
units.tr: Becoming cloudy: Clouds hang, Virg. Clouds gather and rise, Plin. The state of the sky is cloudy, Col. Clouds violate the serene face of the world. Clouds spread over the sky, Lucr. The south wind heaps up the night, Stat. The south wind saddens the sky with cold rain, Virg.

units.la: Nucleus] Corpus nucis, Plin.
units.tr: Kernel: The body of a nut, Plin.

units.la: Nudare] Denudare aliquem. Veste exspoliare, Cic. Retegere pectus, Ovid. Devestire aliquem, Apul. Detrahere alicui vestimentum, Plaut. Exuere vestem alicui, Sen. Exuere aliquem armis, Sil. Spoliare aliquem vestitu, Cic. Connudare, Plin.
units.tr: To strip: To strip someone bare. To strip of clothing, Cic. To bare the breast, Ovid. To undress someone, Apul. To pull a garment off someone, Plaut. To take the clothing off someone, Sen. To strip someone of his arms, Sil. To despoil someone of his clothing, Cic. To lay bare, Plin.

units.la: Nudare caput] Adaperire caput alicui, Val. Max.
units.tr: To bare the head: To uncover someone's head, Val. Max.

units.la: Nudatus] Spoliatus, Cic. Suris & pene natibus apertis ambulans, Varr.
units.tr: Stripped: Despoiled, Cic. Walking with calves and almost buttocks bared, Varr.

units.la: Nude] Nudus in convivio saltavit, Cic.
units.tr: Naked: He danced naked at the banquet, Cic.

units.la: Nudipes] Nudus pedes, Ovid. Nudato pede currens, Tibul. Excalceatus, Mart. Discalceatus, Suet. Planipes, Diomed.
units.tr: Barefoot: Bare-footed, Ovid. Running with bare feet, Tibul. Unshod, Mart. Without shoes, Suet. Flat-footed, Diomed.

units.la: Nudus] Nudula animula, Spart. Apertæ suræ, Noni. Nudior ovo depili. Nudior paxillo, pistillo. Nudus tanquam ex matre.
units.tr: Naked: A little naked soul, Spart. Bare calves, Non. Balder than a plucked egg. Balder than a peg or a pestle. Naked as from the mother's womb.

units.la: Nudo quid eripias?] Corpore de nudo quis tulit exuvias. Nudus nec à centum viris spoliari potest. Nihil habenti, nihil perit, Sallust. Cantabit vacuus coram latrone viator.
units.tr: What can you take from the naked?: Who has ever taken spoils from a naked body? A naked man cannot be stripped even by a hundred men. One who has nothing loses nothing, Sallust. The empty-handed traveller will sing in front of the robber.

units.la: Nugæ] Bullatæ nugæ, canoræ. Apinæ tricæque. Hilum. Floccus. Fama putrida, Plaut. Cassa nux, Hor. Nebula. Mortualia, Plaut. Nugalia, Gell. Nugamenta, Gell. Liræ, Plaut. Ineptiæ. Crepundia puerorum, Cic. Ineptitudo, Non. Susque deque omnia. Ludus jocusque, Lucil. Gerræ Siculæ. Nugæ theatri. Verba frivola.
units.tr: Trifles: Trifles of the bulla and of song. Trifles of the apina and the tricae. A hair's breadth. A tuft of wool. Rotten gossip, Plaut. An empty nut, Hor. Mist. Funeral trifles, Plaut. Little trifles, Gell. Small trinkets, Gell. Lyres, Plaut. Follies. Children's rattles, Cic. Silliness, Non. Everything counts for nothing. Play and jest, Lucil. Sicilian gerrae. Trifles of the stage. Frivolous words.

units.la: Nugari] Ineptire, Ter. Campas dicere. Nugas agere. Nugas blatis, seu dicis, seu garris. Nugas de me conciliavit. Quas tu mihi tricas narras? Plaut. Quisquilias volantis venti spolia memoras, Cæcil. Somniare. Dormire, Plaut. Somniare ineptias, Col. Magno conatu magnas nugas dicere. Blatire, Non. Vid. Blaterare.
units.tr: To trifle: To play the fool, Ter. To talk nonsense. To tell trifles. To prattle trifles, whether you tell them or chatter them. What trifles are you telling me? Plaut. You recount the spoils of a passing wind, Caecil. To dream. To sleep, Plaut. To dream follies, Col. To speak great trifles with great effort. To babble, Non. See Babble.

units.la: Nugator] Futilis homo, Cic. Ineptitudinis cumulatissimus, Cæcil. Balatro, Acron. Institor nugarum. Nugigerulus, Sipont. Architectus nugarum, Muret. Stulta & immodica blaterans, Blatero, Gell. Nugipolyloquides, æ, Plaut.
units.tr: Trifler: A frivolous man, Cic. The utter pinnacle of silliness, Caecil. A buffoon, Acron. A peddler of trifles. A carrier of trifles, Sipont. An architect of trifles, Muret. One who babbles foolishly and immoderately, Gell. A chatterbox of many words, Plaut.

units.la: Nugatorius] Nugalis, Gell. Nugarius, Varr.
units.tr: Trifling: Trivial, Gell. Trifling, Varr.

units.la: Nullatenus] Nullo pacto, Plaut. Nullo modo. Minimè gentium, Ter. Nullâ ratione. Minimè omnium ad te pertinebat, Cic. Minimè, Sallust. Nullo genere, Petron. Quod optimo genere facere non licuit, Cic. Ne per somnium quidem, Plaut.
units.tr: By no means: In no way, Plaut. In no way at all. Least of all, Ter. For no reason. It least of all concerned you, Cic. Not at all, Sallust. In no kind, Petron. What it was not allowed to do in the best manner, Cic. Not even in a dream, Plaut.

units.la: Nullibi] Nusquam est. Nullo in loco, Cic. Nusquam gentium. Nunquam usquam, Ter. Necubi, Liv. Nec usquam aliubi. Neque intus, neque foris. Neque inter mortuos, neque inter vivos.
units.tr: Nowhere: It is nowhere. In no place, Cic. Nowhere in the world. Never anywhere, Ter. Anywhere, Liv. Nowhere else. Neither inside nor outside. Neither among the dead nor among the living.

units.la: Nusquam exire] Nusquam pedem, Ter. Ne altero quidem pede.
units.tr: To go nowhere: Not to set a foot anywhere, Ter. Not even one foot.

units.la: Nullus, vid. Nemo.
units.tr: None: see No one.

units.la: Nullus sum, vid. Periit.
units.tr: I am nobody: see Perished.

units.la: Numella] Numelli, Col. Bojæ, Fest.
units.tr: Numella: Numelli, Col. Bojae, Fest.

units.la: Numen]Nutus & potestas Dei, Cic. Deus suus & omnium.
units.tr: Divine power: The will and power of God, Cic. His own god and the god of all.

units.la: Numerare] Dinumerare stellas. Annumerare sententias, Cic. Recensere captivos, Liv. Mittere in digitos. Vid. Computare.
units.tr: To count: To count the stars. To enumerate opinions, Cic. To review captives, Liv. To place on the fingers. See Reckon.

units.la: Numeratò] In numerato relinquere, Plin. Numero definitum, Cic. Numero digerere, Virg. Numerosus] Numerosior ambitus littorum, Plin. Acer-valis, Cic.
units.tr: Counted: To leave in reserve, Plin. Defined by number, Cic. To arrange by number, Virg. Numerous: A more numerous circuit of shores, Plin. Crowded together, Cic.

units.la: Nummatus, vid. Pecuniosus.
units.tr: Wealthy: see Rich in money.

units.la: Nummi] Argentum signatum, Plin. Aurum,Plaut. Numisma, Mart. Res numaria, Cic. Res,absol. Lucr. Asses contulit populus, Suet. Vid. Pecunia.
units.tr: Coins: Silver stamped with a mark, Plin. Gold, Plaut. Coinage, Mart. Money matters, Cic. Goods, absolutely, Lucr. The people contributed asses, Suet. See Money.

units.la: Nunc] Nunc temporis numero. Nunc ipsum ea lego. In praesentia. In praesens tempus. Modo, Cic. In praesens, Gell. Impraesentiarum, Priscian. Vlp.
units.tr: Now: At the present time. I am reading these very things now. At present. For the present time. Just now, Cic. For the present, Gell. For the moment, Priscian, Ulp.

units.la: Nuncubi] Sicubi, Ter.
units.tr: If anywhere: If anywhere, Ter.

units.la: Nunciare, vid. Nuntiare.
units.tr: see Announce.

units.la: Nuncupare, vid. Nominare.
units.tr: see Name.

units.la: Nundinae] Nundina, pl. Vopisc. Panegyris nundinarum, Cic. Mercatus, Plaut.
units.tr: Market days: Market days, Vopisc. The festival of market days, Cic. Trading, Plaut.

units.la: Nundinalis] Nundinarius, Plin.
units.tr: Of market days: Relating to market days, Plin.

units.la: Nundinari, vid. Emere. Vendere.
units.tr: see Buy. Sell.

units.la: Nunquam] Nec noctu, nec diu, Titin. Ad Graecas Calendas. Ad flores ficus venias. Anno magno Platonis. Cum mula peperit. Terra citius aetherem conscendet. Scarabaeus citius mel faciet. Nunquam usquam. Prius testudo leporem capiet. Prius unda cum flamma inibit gratiam. Prius cavum a convexo disjunxeris.
units.tr: Never: Neither by night nor by day, Titin. At the Greek Kalends. You will come when the figs flower. In Plato's Great Year. When the mule bears young. The earth will climb to the sky sooner. The beetle will make honey sooner. Never anywhere. The tortoise will catch the hare sooner. Water will enter into friendship with fire sooner. You will separate the hollow from the convex sooner.

units.la: Nuntiare] Denunciare, annuntiare alicui. Nuntium deferre. Per nuncium certiorem facere. Renunciare de aliqua re, aliquid, Cic. Apportare nuncium, Ter.
units.tr: To announce: To denounce or announce something to someone. To carry a message. To inform through a messenger. To report back on some matter, Cic. To bring a message, Ter.

units.la: Nuncius] Internuncius, Cic. Loquelaris servus, Fest.
units.tr: Messenger: A go-between, Cic. A household slave for carrying speech, Fest.

units.la: Nuper] Nuperrime. Proximo, &, proxime. Paulo ante. Non ita multis ante diebus, Cic. Haud dudum; haud diu, Cic. Pro-nuper, Plaut. Nunc nuper, Ter. Ab recenti memoria, Liv. Heri & nudius tertius.
units.tr: Recently: Most recently. Nearest, and nearest. A little before. Not so many days before, Cic. Not long ago; not for long, Cic. Just lately, Plaut. Only just now, Ter. From recent memory, Liv. Yesterday and the day before.

units.la: Nuperus] Nuper rumor, Propert. Recens captum hominem nuperum & novitium, Plaut.
units.tr: Recent: A recent rumour, Propert. A man recently captured, new and inexperienced, Plaut.

units.la: Nuptiae] Nuptialis coena, Plaut. Solennia nuptiarum, Tac. Officium, abs. Iuv. Officium nuptiarum, Suet.
units.tr: Nuptiae] Nuptial feast, Plaut. Solemnities of a wedding, Tac. Duty, abs. Iuv. Duty of marriage, Suet.

units.la: Nuptias celebrare] Solennia nuptiarum celebrare, Tacit. Nuptias adornare, Plaut.
units.tr: Nuptias celebrare] To celebrate the solemnities of a wedding, Tacit. To prepare a wedding, Plaut.

units.la: Nuptialis] Conjugialia festa, Ovid. Genialis lectus, Hor.
units.tr: Nuptialis] Festivities of marriage, Ovid. Bridal bed, Hor.

units.la: Nuptus novus, vid. Novus nuptus.
units.tr: Nuptus novus, see Novus nuptus.

units.la: Nusquam, vid. Nullibi.
units.tr: Nusquam, see Nullibi.

units.la: Nutrire, vid. Alere.
units.tr: Nutrire, see Alere.

units.la: Nutritor] Altor. Nutricius, Cic. Alumnus. Terra omnium alumna, Plin.
units.tr: Nutritor] Nourisher. Foster-father, Cic. Foster-son. The earth, nurse of all, Plin.

units.la: Nutrix] Educatrix. Altrix. Alumna, Cic. Nutricula. Mater, pro nutrice, Plaut. Supposititia mater, Varr.
units.tr: Nutrix] Educator. Nourisher. Nursling, Cic. Little nurse. Mother, for a nurse, Plaut. A substituted mother, Varr.

units.la: Nutus] Ad numen mentis moventur, Lucr. Significatio vestra declarat, quid sententiatis, Lamb. Supercilium, Hor.
units.tr: Nutus] They are moved by the nod of the mind, Lucr. Your signification declares what you think, Lamb. Eyebrow, Hor.

units.la: Nux, vid. Avellana. Iuglans.
units.tr: Nux, see Avellana. Walnut.

units.la: O.
units.tr: O.

units.la: Exclaman. vid. Vtinam.
units.tr: Exclaim. See Vtinam.

units.la: O bene factum!] Optimum est. Factum optime. Jam id laudo. Diis habeo grates. Voluptatem magnam nuncias, Ter. O bene, quod. Gratia magna Jovi, (Christo, Deo,) Ovid. Bene hercle factum! Bene habet. O lepidum diem! Plaut. Bonum factum. Bonum hercle factum. Hercle rem bene gestam! Id. Dii nos respiciunt, Ter. Dii me salvum & servatum volunt, Plaut.
units.tr: O well done!] It is best. Done very well. Now I praise it. I give thanks to the gods. You bring great joy, Ter. O good, that... Great thanks to Jove (to Christ, to God), Ovid. Well done, by Hercules! It is well. O delightful day! Plaut. Good deed. Good deed indeed, by Hercules. Hercules, a deed well done! Id. The gods look upon us, Ter. The gods wish me safe and preserved, Plaut.

units.la: O si!] Utinam. O, Cic. Si, pro, O si, Virg. Ut illum, Ter. O utinam! Ovid.
units.tr: O if!] Would that! O, Cic. If, for: O if, Virg. That he..., Ter. O that! Ovid.

units.la: Ob, vid. Quare.
units.tr: Ob, see Quare.

units.la: Obaratus, vid. Debitor, debere.
units.tr: Obaratus, see Debitor, debere.

units.la: Obambulatio, vid. Deambulatio.
units.tr: Obambulatio, see Deambulatio.

units.la: Obambulare, vid. Deambulare.
units.tr: Obambulare, see Deambulare.

units.la: Obcaecare, vid. Excaecare.
units.tr: Obcaecare, see Excaecare.

units.la: Obdormire] Obdormiscere. Consopiri somno. Completitur me somnus, Cic. Sopiri, Lucr. Condormire, vel, Condormiscere, Plaut. Oppressit somnus virginem, Ter. Ire somnum, Virg. In somnum ire. Obrepit alicui somnus, Sen. Serpit somnus, Plin. Sopore somnus devinxit membra, Liv. Obsopiri, Scribon. Inserpit somnus, Stat. Labi in somnum, Petron.
units.tr: Obdormire] To fall asleep. To be lulled into sleep. Sleep overcomes me, Cic. To be lulled, Lucr. To fall asleep, Plaut. Sleep overcame the maiden, Ter. To go to sleep, Virg. To go into sleep. Sleep creeps over someone, Sen. Sleep creeps on, Plin. Sleep bound his limbs in slumber, Liv. To be lulled, Scribon. Sleep creeps in, Stat. To slip into sleep, Petron.

units.la: Obducere callum] Exsurdare palatum, Hor. Torpare, Non. Vid. Callescere.
units.tr: Obducere callum] To make the palate numb, Hor. To grow numb, Non. See Callescere.

units.la: Obdurescere, vid. Durescere.
units.tr: Obdurescere, see Durescere.

units.la: Obediens] Dicto audiens, obsequens. Parens alicui, Cic. Audiens imperii, Plaut. Parens dicto, Liv. Morigerus, Lucr. Obnoxius, Salust. Flexiles & sequaces sumus, Plin. Descendere ad omnia paratus, Cæs.
units.tr: Obediens] Obedient, compliant; heeding commands. Submissive to someone, Cic. Listening to orders, Plaut. Obedient to command, Liv. Compliant, Lucr. Subject, Sall. We are pliant and compliant, Plin. Ready to yield to everything, Caes.

units.la: Obedienter] Obsequenter, Plin. Iun. Obsecundanter, Nigit. Sine recusatione, Cæs.
units.tr: Obedienter] Compliantly, Plin. Iun. Obsequiously, Nigid. Without refusal, Caes.

units.la: Obedientia] Obtemperatio. Obsequium, Cic. Obsequentia, Cæs. Obsecutio, Arnob. Obsequela. Auscultatio, Plaut. Obedientia felicitatis mater.
units.tr: Obedientia] Submission. Compliance, Cic. Compliance, Caes. Obedience, Arnob. Obsequience. Hearkening, Plaut. Obedience is the mother of happiness.

units.la: Obedire]Obsequi in omnibus. Parere legibus. Obtemperare magistratibus. Obsecundare. Auscultare alicui Cic. Obsequentem esse. Morem gerere alicui. Morigerum esse, Ter. Morigerari, Cic. Obsequelam facere, Plaut. Accipere imperium, Tac. Audire aliquem, Liv. Aure facili annuere, Propert. Cedamus Phœbo, & moniti meliora sequamur, Virg. Obnoxius sum alicui. Imperari, Salust. Nunc ades ad imperandum (ad parendum) Cic. Morigerus sum alicui, Ter. Audiens & obediens dicto sum, Liv. Facere, Cic. Ad nutum alicujus præstò sum, Cic.
units.tr: Obedire] To comply in all things. To obey the laws. To submit to the magistrates. To comply. To listen to someone, Cic. To be compliant. To humour someone. To be compliant, Ter. To make oneself compliant, Plaut. To accept a command, Tac. To hear someone, Liv. To nod with an easy ear, Propert. Let us yield to Phoebus and, being warned, follow better things, Virg. I am subject to someone. To be commanded, Sall. Now come to command, or to obey, Cic. I am compliant with someone, Ter. I listen and obey the word, Liv. To do, Cic. I am at someone's beck and call, Cic.

units.la: Oberrare, vid. Vagari.
units.tr: Oberrare, see Vagari.

units.la: Obesus] Crassus, Ter. Gravis, Plin. Gravistellus, Plaut. Plenissimus, Cels. Adipe fartus, Plutar. Popa venter. Porcus obesus. Terga pulposis torulis obesa trahens, Apul. Alit aqualiculum. Vid. Pinguis.
units.tr: Obesus] Fat, Ter. Heavy, Plin. Rather heavy, Plaut. Very full, Cels. Stuffed with fat, Plut. Paunchy belly. A fat pig. Dragging back fleshy haunches, Apul. Nourishes the belly. See Pinguis.

units.la: Obex] Pessulus, Ter. Repagulum, Cic. Sera, Ovid.
units.tr: Obex] Bolt, Ter. Bar, Cic. Lock, Ovid.

units.la: Obstirmare animum]Obstirmatè resistere, Suet. Obstinare aliquid, Liv. Destinare animis vinci, Id. Obstinatè operam dare, Ter. Cor durare, Plaut. Indurare animum, Sen. Obdurare, abs. Hor. Catul. Obstinatâ mente perferre, Id. Durare animum, Ovid. Mordere frenum, Cic. Pertendere animo cubare vestitum, Propert.
units.tr: Obstirmare animum] To resist stubbornly, Suet. To be obstinate about something, Liv. To set the mind on not being conquered, Id. To make an obstinate effort, Ter. To harden the heart, Plaut. To harden the mind, Sen. To harden, absolutely, Hor., Catul. To endure with an obstinate mind, Id. To harden the mind, Ovid. To champ the bit, Cic. To stretch out in mind, lying clothed, Propert.

units.la: Obstirmatè, vid. Contumaciter.
units.tr: Obstirmatè, see Contumaciter.

units.la: Objectio]Objectus, Sipont. Objectatio, Cæs. Criminatio, Cic. Intentio criminis, Quint. Insimulatio probrorum, Cic.
units.tr: Objectio] Objection, Sipont. Objection, Caes. Accusation, Cic. Charge of a crime, Quint. Accusation of shameful things, Cic.

units.la: Objicere aliquid alicui] Opponere, Cic. Obtrudere, Ter. Impingam tibi ingentem epistolam, Sen.
units.tr: Objicere aliquid alicui] To set against, Cic. To thrust upon, Ter. I shall throw a huge letter at you, Sen.

units.la: Obire] Obambulare urbem, Plaut. Circumire fundum. Peragrare rura, Cic. Lustrare muros, Virg.
units.tr: Obire] To walk about the city, Plaut. To go round an estate. To roam the countryside, Cic. To survey the walls, Virg.

units.la: Obiter] Per transfennam. Striͤtim præterēundo. Uno a-spectu transfiens, Cic. In transitu, Quint. In transcursu attingere, Plin. Clausis oculis aliquid agere, Tertul. Summis ingredi pedibus. Summis labris, digitis atingere aliquid. Summis naribus olfacere. Transeunter, Amm. Suspensâ manu, Plin. Iun. Lacinia tenere. Vid. Negligenter.
units.tr: Obiter] In passing. Briefly, in passing. Passing with a single glance, Cic. In transit, Quint. To touch in passing, Plin. To act with eyes closed, Tert. To walk on tiptoe. To touch something with the tips of the lips or fingers. To smell with the tips of the nostrils. In passing, Amm. With hand raised, Plin. Iun. To hold by the hem. See Negligenter.

units.la: Obitus, vid. Occasus. Mors.
units.tr: Obitus, see Occasus. Mors.

units.la: Objurgare aliquem] Verbis vehementioribus persequi. Stomachum in aliquem erumpere. Incurrere in aliquem verbis. Male; vehementer accipere aliquem, Cic. Objurgitare aliquem, Plaut. Dicere in aliquem inclementer, Liv. Acerbè, Cic. Gravius, inclementius, Ter. Incessere aliquem asperè, Quint. Accipere clamore aliquem. Gravibus verbis ab aliquo confici, & trucidari. Corripere aliquem clamoribus, Cic. Vid. Arguere.
units.tr: Objurgare aliquem] To rebuke someone with rather vehement words. To vent one's spleen upon someone. To run at someone with words. To treat someone badly and harshly, Cic. To scold someone, Plaut. To speak harshly against someone, Liv. Bitterly, Cic. More severely, more harshly, Ter. To assail someone harshly, Quint. To receive someone with shouts. To be crushed and slaughtered by someone's heavy words. To reprimand someone with shouts, Cic. See Arguere.

units.la: Objurgatio] Castigatio verborum, Liv. Reprehensio culpæ. Incusatio peccatorum. Incessio, Cic. Culpa castigabilis, Plaut.
units.tr: Objurgatio] Verbal castigation, Liv. Reproof of a fault. Accusation of sins. Attack, Cic. A blameworthy fault, Plaut.

units.la: Objurgator] Objurgatorius, Cic. Castigator. Reprehensor delicti, Ovid. Correptor peccantium, Sen.
units.tr: Objurgator] Rebuking, Cic. A castigator. A reprover of a misdeed, Ovid. A corrector of sinners, Sen.

units.la: Oblatio, vid. Sacrificium.
units.tr: Oblatio, see Sacrificium.

units.la: Oblatrare] Allatrare aliquem, Col. Gannitibus aliquem lacessere, Mart. Latrant in me canes, Plaut. Illatrare per rimas, Lucan. Latror à canibus, Plin.
units.tr: Oblatrare] To bark at someone, Col. To provoke someone with yapping, Mart. Dogs bark at me, Plaut. To bark through the cracks, Lucan. To be barked at by dogs, Plin.

units.la: Oblectamen, vid. Delectamentum.
units.tr: Oblectamen, see Delectamentum.

units.la: Oblectare aliquem] Detinere aliquem lepore. Delectamus nos cum Musis, Cic. Oblecta otium versibus inter coenam, in balneo, in vehiculo, Plin. Occupare animum in funambulo, Ter. Vid. Delectare.
units.tr: Oblectare aliquem] To detain someone with charm. We delight ourselves with the Muses, Cic. Pass your leisure with verses during dinner, in the bath, in the carriage, Plin. To occupy the mind with a tightrope walker, Ter. See Delectare.

units.la: Oblectari, vid. Delectari.
units.tr: Oblectari, see Delectari.

units.la: Obligare vulnus &c.] Præligare, Cic. Circumligare, Liv. Circumvincire, Plaut. Circumnectere, Lactant. Colligare vulnera. Deligare in linteolo grana, Plin. Ligare vulnera, guttur laqueo, Ov. Internectere plagas. Stat. Obnectere, Fest.
units.tr: Obligare vulnus &c.] To bind up a wound, Cic. To bind round, Liv. To wrap round, Plaut. To tie round, Lact. To bind up wounds. To tie grains up in linen, Plin. To bind wounds, or to bind the throat with a noose, Ov. To interlace the wounds, Stat. To tie round, Fest.

units.la: Obligare aliquem] Alligare stipulatione. Lex omnes alligat. Adstringere conditionibus. Obstringere religione, Cic. Auctorare, Liv.
units.tr: Obligare aliquem] To bind someone by stipulation. The law binds everyone. To tie by conditions. To bind by religious obligation, Cic. To hire, Liv.

units.la: Obligare se alicui ] Obligare fidem suam. Interponere fidem inter rem aliquam. Addicere se alicui ; mancipare. Auctorari. Ego me religione obstrictum puto, Cic. Adstringere fidem suam, Ter. Fidem dare, Bud. Ad hoc sacramentum adactifumus ferre mortalia, Sen. Qui fiduciam acceperit, fidem praestare debet, Cic. (Fiduc. i. obligationem.)
units.tr: Obligare se alicui] To pledge one's faith. To place one's faith in some matter. To surrender oneself to someone; to hire oneself out. To sell oneself into service. I think myself bound by religious obligation, Cic. To bind one's faith, Ter. To give one's faith, Bud. To this oath we are compelled to bear mortal things, Sen. Whoever has received a trust must keep faith, Cic. (Fiducia means obligation.)

units.la: Obligatio ] Auctoramentum servitutis. Conditio. Lex, Cic.
units.tr: Obligatio] Hiring oneself out into servitude. A condition. A law, Cic.

units.la: Obligatus] Devinctus alicui. Obstrictus maximis beneficii vinculis. Addictum, obstrictum, deditum sibi habere. Servus. Mancipatus alicui, Cic. Obnoxius, Plaut. Auctoratus, Liv. Tenetur legibus, Id. Offrenatus unius praedae offulâ, Apul.
units.tr: Obligatus] Bound to someone. Bound by the strongest chains of a benefit. To hold someone as bound, given, and devoted to oneself. A slave. Handed over to someone, Cic. Liable, Plaut. Hired, Liv. Held by the laws, Liv. Caught by the bait of a single prey, Apul.

units.la: Oblimare limo] Oppilare ostia, Lucr.
units.tr: Oblimare limo] To block up the doorways, Lucr.

units.la: Oblinire, vid. Circumlinire.
units.tr: Oblinire, see Circumlinire.

units.la: Obliquare, vid. Curvare, Dirigere.
units.tr: Obliquare, see Curvare, Dirigere.

units.la: Obliquè ] Obliquo ictu, Hor. Inflexo ictu ferire, Plin. Tractim tangere, Plaut.
units.tr: Obliquè] With a glancing blow, Hor. To strike with a bent blow, Plin. To touch lightly, Plaut.

units.la: Obliquitas] Obliquuum, Virg.Plin.Ovid. Obsitum, Apul. Scal.
units.tr: Obliquitas] Obliquity, Virg., Plin., Ovid. Obliquity, Apul., Scal.

units.la: Obliquus] Limus signifer, Scal. Obstitus sol, Apul. Fest.
units.tr: Obliquus] The oblique sign of the zodiac, Scal. The sun obstructed, Apul., Fest.

units.la: Oblitescere, vid. Latere.
units.tr: Oblitescere, see Latere.

units.la: Oblivio] Oblivia,orum, Lucr. Obliteratio praeteritorum, Am. Infirmitas memoriae, Papin. Oblivionis campus. Lethe.
units.tr: Oblivio] Oblivion, Lucr. Obliteration of past things, Am. Weakness of memory, Papin. The field of oblivion. Lethe.

units.la: Oblivio delictorum, malorum] Amnestia, Vopisc. Lex oblivionis, Aemil. Prob. Oblivio & venia omnium factorum dictorumque in perpetuum, Sen. Plebiscitum interposuit, ne qua praeteritarum rerum mentio fieret, Val.M. Abolitio praeteritorum, Iul. Cap.
units.tr: Oblivio delictorum, malorum] Amnesty, Vopisc. A law of oblivion, Aemil. Prob. Oblivion and pardon of all deeds and words for ever, Sen. A plebiscite was passed that no mention of past things should be made, Val. Max. Abolition of past things, Iul. Cap.

units.la: Oblivio malorum ] Injuria oblivione ulciscenda. Injuriarum optimum remedium oblivio. Irreparabilium felix oblivio rerum.
units.tr: Oblivio malorum] An injury is to be avenged by oblivion. Oblivion is the best remedy for injuries. Happy is the oblivion of irreparable things.

units.la: Oblivioni traditus] Jacet in oblivione aliquid. Intermortua ejus memoria. Elapsus ex memoria. Obruit eum oblivione vetustas. Inobscurat, delevit eum oblivio, Cic. Obruit eum oblivio, Tac. Vetustate incompertum, Obliterata vetustate res, Liv.
units.tr: Oblivioni traditus] Something lies in oblivion. His memory is extinct. Slipped from memory. Antiquity covers him with oblivion. Oblivion has obscured him and blotted him out, Cic. Oblivion has overwhelmed him, Tac. Unknown through antiquity; a thing obliterated by age, Liv.

units.la: Obliviosus ] Deficitur aliquis memoriâ, Col. Subrepit illi oblivio, Plin. Dolium sc. vas pertusum. Pertuso dolio nihil infundas. Proprii nominis oblitus. Oblivio literarum, pro, Oblivioso, Plaut. Curione obliviosior, Er.
units.tr: Obliviosus] A person deprived of memory, Col. Forgetfulness creeps over him, Plin. A leaking vessel: do not pour into a leaking cask. Forgetful of his own name. Forgetfulness of letters, Plaut. More forgetful than Curio, Erasm.

units.la: Oblivisci] Oblivione conterere, obruere, delere. In oblivionem adducere. Venire in oblivionem alicujus. Capit me rei oblivio. Occidit rei memoria & recordatio. Memoriam alicujus abjicere, delere, deponere. Deponere ex memoria. Exstinguitur aliquid oblivione posteritatis. Effluit; excidit mihi aliquid. Effluit ex animo, Cic. Excidit memoria hujus rei, Liv. Exiit ab hominum memoriâ, Sen. Excidit omnis retinentia rerum actarum. Meminisse jacet, Lucr. Dememinisse, i. oblivisci, Mart. Oblivio transmisit eam sententiam, Tacit. Obliterare memoriam beneficii, Cic. Intercidit memoria. Dare aliquid oblivioni, Liv. Oblivionem alicujus rei capere, Plin. Falli memoriâ, Id. Vento & aquæ, noctisque tenebris inscribere. Vacillare. Devoravi modò nomen, Plaut.
units.tr: Oblivisci] To wear away, bury, or destroy by oblivion. To bring into oblivion. To come into someone's oblivion. Forgetfulness of the thing takes hold of me. The memory and recollection of the thing perish. To cast off, delete, or lay aside someone's memory. To drop out of memory. Something is extinguished by the oblivion of posterity. It slips my mind; something escapes me. It has gone out of my mind, Cic. The memory of this matter has slipped away, Liv. It has passed out of human memory, Sen. All recollection of past deeds has departed. Memory lies dormant, Lucr. To have forgotten entirely, that is, to forget, Mart. Oblivion has passed over that opinion, Tac. To obliterate the memory of a benefit, Cic. Memory has perished. To give something to oblivion, Liv. To take hold of oblivion of a thing, Plin. To be deceived by memory, Id. To write down on wind and water and the darkness of night. To waver. I have just swallowed the name, Plaut.

units.la: Oblocutio] Obtrectatio, Cic. Obtrectatus, Gell. Iniqui sermones. Lingua:linguas hominum vitare non possumus, Cic. Sugillatio majestatis, Plin. Morsus, Catul.
units.tr: Oblocutio] Disparagement, Cic. Detraction, Gell. Unfriendly talk. Tongues: we cannot escape the tongues of men, Cic. A slander against majesty, Plin. A biting remark, Catul.

units.la: Oblocutor] Obtrectator laudum alicujus, Cic. Detrectator, Tac. Linguæ in absentes jactator, Claud.
units.tr: Oblocutor] A detractor of someone's praises, Cic. A disparager, Tac. A boaster in slanders against the absent, Claud.

units.la: Obloqui alicui] Detrahere alicui: de absente: de auctoritate alicujus. Lacerare incesto ore virum optimum. Carpere aliquem maledico dente. De absentibus detrahendi causâ maledicè contumelioséque dicere, Cic. Rodere aliquem, Id. Detrectare laudes alicujus, Ovid. Detrectare aliquem, Tac. Obtrectare laudes, &, laudibus alicujus, Liv. Sinistris sermonibus aliquem carpere, Plin. Iun. Vellicare absentem. Mordere dente invido: falsis opprobriis, Hor. Mordere dente iniquo; dictis, Ovid. Mordere clanculum aliquem. Absenti male loqui, Ter. Taxare aliquem, Suet. Allatrare alicujus magnitudinem, Liv.
units.tr: Obloqui alicui] To detract from someone; of an absent person; of someone's authority. To tear the best man apart with a slanderous mouth. To carp at someone with a slandering tooth. To speak maliciously and insultingly of the absent for the sake of detraction, Cic. To gnaw at someone, Cic. To detract from someone's praises, Ovid. To disparage someone, Tac. To detract from someone's praises, Liv. To carp at someone with malicious talk, Plin. Iun. To pick at an absent person. To bite with an envious tooth, with false reproaches, Hor. To bite with an unfair tooth, with words, Ovid. To bite secretly at someone. To speak ill of the absent, Ter. To tax someone, Suet. To bark at someone's greatness, Liv.

units.la: Obluctari, vid. Reniti.
units.tr: To struggle against, see Resist.

units.la: Obluctatio, vid. Reluctatio.
units.tr: Struggling against, see Reluctation.

units.la: Obmarcescere] Obtorpuit jacendo. Segnis otio evasit. Quiete deses ab opere factus est, Liv.
units.tr: To wither away, grow languid: He grew numb from lying still. He became sluggish through idleness. He was made slack and idle from work by rest, Liv.

units.la: Obmurmurare] Responsare, Plaut. Remurmurare, Stat. Vid. Murmurare.
units.tr: To murmur in reply: To answer back, Plaut. To murmur again, Stat. See Murmur.

units.la: Obmutescere] Immutescere, Quint. Elinguis redditus est, Cic. Mutus fio, Ter. Linguam oculi praeciderunt, Plaut. Inclusit illi vocem admiratio, Liv. Lingua ille excidit, Plaut.
units.tr: To fall silent: To become speechless, Quint. He was made tongueless, Cic. I become mute, Ter. His eyes cut off his tongue, Plaut. Admiration locked up his voice, Liv. The tongue fell out of him, Plaut.

units.la: Obniti, vid. Reniti.
units.tr: To strive against, see Resist.

units.la: Obnixe, vid. Enixe.
units.tr: Strenuously, see Earnestly.

units.la: Obnubilare, vid. Obumbrare.
units.tr: To cloud over, see Overshadow.

units.la: Obrepere] Imagines in animos dormientium obrepunt, Cic. Correpere occulte in navim. Influere in animum alicujus, Id. Surrepit animo judicis opinio, Quint. Vid. Irrepere.
units.tr: To creep up on: Images creep into the minds of sleepers, Cic. To slip secretly onto a ship. To flow into someone's mind, Id. An opinion creeps into the judge's mind, Quint. See Creep in.

units.la: Obrigescere] Diriguit, a dirigeo, Virg. Riget lingua. Stupere, Ovid. Demori, Col. Emori, Cels. Intermori, Cic. Obtorpere, Cic. Obbrutescere. Membratim vitalem deperdere sensum. Tardescit lingua, Lucr. Siderari, Plin.
units.tr: To grow stiff: It stiffened, from dirigeo, Virg. The tongue is stiff. To be stunned, Ovid. To die, Col. To die, Cels. To die off, Cic. To grow numb, Cic. To become brutish. To lose vital feeling limb by limb. The tongue grows slow, Lucr. To be benumbed by a star, Plin.

units.la: Obrodere] Derodere, Cic. Circumrodere quid devorandum est, Id.
units.tr: To gnaw: To gnaw away, Cic. To gnaw around what is to be devoured, Id.

units.la: Obrosus] Obesus, Nev. Adesus, Liv. Ambesus, Virg. Semesa frustra, Hor. Depastus, Plin.
units.tr: Gnawed: Eaten away, Nev. Eaten at, Liv. Eaten all round, Virg. Half-eaten in vain, Hor. Grazed on, Plin.

units.la: Obruere] Adobruere aliquid. Coaggerare ova sale, Col. Superinducere terram. Strangulant sata gramina, Plin.
units.tr: To bury, cover over: To bury something over. To heap eggs in salt, Col. To spread earth on top. Weeds choke the crops, Plin.

units.la: Obrussa] Praetentatus, us, Plin. Spectatio pecuniae, Cic. Vid. Examen.
units.tr: Assay, test of gold: Testing, Plin. Weighing of money, Cic. See Examination.

units.la: Obryzum] Aurum elutum, Iul. Capit. Aurum absolutius nullum, quam e fluminum ramentis, Plin.
units.tr: Pure gold: Refined gold, Iul. Capit. There is no gold more pure than that from the grains of rivers, Plin.

units.la: Obsaturari, vid. Effarcire se.
units.tr: To satiate oneself, see To stuff oneself.

units.la: Obscene] Obscene amari ab aliquo, Fest. Obscenius, Spurce dicere. Spurcissime scribere, Sordide dictum, Cic. Indigne corpore quaestum quaerere, Plaut. Osce fabulari, Titin. Vid. Foede.
units.tr: Obscenely: To be loved obscenely by someone, Fest. More obscenely: to speak foully. To write most foully; spoken basely, Cic. To seek gain from one's body unworthily, Plaut. To talk in the Oscan manner, Titin. See Foully.

units.la: Obscenus] In obscoenis est, Cic. Fescenninus versus, Lucr. Fescennina locutio, Catul. Praetextatus sermo, Suet. Obscoenissimarum rerum auctor, Paterc. Spurcata senectus, impuris moribus, Catul. Paticus, f. Pathicus, Mart. Opicus, Plin. Iun. Oscus, Fest. Tabernarius, Apul. Spurcus, Cic. Nupta verba, Plaut. Flagitiosa libido, Cic. Tetra, Hor. Turpe verbum, Id. Foedus amor, Ovid.
units.tr: Obscene: He is among the obscene things, Cic. Fescennine verse, Lucr. Fescennine speech, Catul. Praetextatus speech, Suet. Author of the most obscene things, Paterc. A filthy old age with impure morals, Catul. Paticus, or Pathicus, Mart. Opicus, Plin. Iun. Oscus, Fest. Tabernarius, Apul. Spurcus, Cic. Improper words, Plaut. Shameful lust, Cic. Foul, Hor. An unseemly word, Id. Foul love, Ovid.

units.la: Obscurare] Offundere tenebras, noctem, rebus. Inobscurare. Luminibus obstruere. Obducere tenebras clarissimis rebus. Officit soli umbra terrae, Cic. Inumbrare, Tac. Obnubilare, Gell. Offuscare, Justin. Adnubilat virtutem pravis actibus, Amm. Sol stellas praestringit, Lucr. Serenitati nubem inducere. Obcaecantur tenebris imagines, Pl. vid. Obumbrare.
units.tr: To darken: To pour darkness and night over things. To make dark. To block the light. To cast shadows over the most famous things. The earth's shadow obstructs the sun, Cic. To overshadow, Tac. To cloud over, Gell. To dim, Justin. He clouds virtue with wicked deeds, Amm. The sun outshines the stars, Lucr. To bring a cloud over clear weather. Images are blinded by shadows, Pl. See Overshadow.

units.la: Obscuratio, vid. Eclipsis.
units.tr: Darkening, see Eclipse.

units.la: Obscure] Per nebulam, Plaut. Per caliginem cernere, Cic. Per transsennam aspicere, Id. Non distincte, Tac. Adumbratim aliqua simulata, Lucr.
units.tr: Obscurely: Through mist, Plaut. To see through fog, Cic. To look through a lattice, Id. Not distinctly, Tac. In outline, hinting at some pretended things, Lucr.

units.la: Obscurus] Perobscurus, Cic. Caecus. Opacus, Virg. Heraclito obscurior, Er. Vid. Tenebricosus.
units.tr: Obscure: Very obscure, Cic. Blind. Shady, Virg. Darker than Heraclitus, Er. See Gloomy.

units.la: Obscurus sermo, vid. Sermo obsc.
units.tr: Obscure speech, see Obscene speech.

units.la: Obscura res aegre intelligitur] Delio natatore haec res eget, ne quis mergatur. Ne Apollo quidem intelligit.
units.tr: An obscure matter is understood with difficulty: This matter needs a Delian swimmer, lest anyone drown. Not even Apollo understands it.

units.la: Obscura egent luce] De Pythagoricis rebus absque lumine ne loquaris. Interpres eget interprete, Cic. Mercurius Mercurio.
units.tr: Obscure things need light: Do not speak of Pythagorean matters without a light. An interpreter needs an interpreter, Cic. Mercury to Mercury.

units.la: Obscura, luce clarescunt] Luce dissolvuntur tenebrae.
units.tr: Obscure things become clear in the light: Darkness is dissolved by light.

units.la: Ex obscuro in apertum] Ex umbra in solem.
units.tr: From the obscure into the open: From shade into sun.

units.la: Obsecrare] Implorare hominum misericordiam. Obtestari fidem & misericordiam alicujus. Precibus omnibus aliquem orare & obtestari. Summopere, vehementer, omnibus precibus petere. Rogare magno studio, molestè, precario, Precibus & obsecratione humili uti. Obsecrare per nomen propinquitatis. Ab aliquo etiam atque etiam, pro maximâ benevolentiâ &c. majorem in modum petere atque contendere, Cic. Per ego te Deos oro, Ter. Obtestari, orare per, &c. Plaut. Petere cupienter, Id.
units.tr: To beseech: To implore people's mercy. To entreat and beg someone's faith and mercy. To beg someone with all prayers. To ask with the greatest zeal and urgency, with every entreaty. To ask with great eagerness, troublesomely, by favour. To use prayers and humble entreaty. To beseech by the name of kinship. To ask and press someone again and again for the greatest goodwill, and so on, in the greatest measure, Cic. By the gods I beg you, Ter. To entreat, to beg by, and so on, Plaut. To seek eagerly, Id.

units.la: Obsecratio, vid. Precatio.
units.tr: Beseeching, see Prayer.

units.la: Obsecundare, vid. Obedire.
units.tr: To comply, see To obey.

units.la: Obsepire, vid. Sepire.
units.tr: To hedge in, see To fence in.

units.la: Obsequi, vid. Obedire.
units.tr: To comply with, see To obey.

units.la: Obsequium] Ministerium, Virg. Officium, Propert. Vid. Ministerium. Obedientia.
units.tr: Compliance, service: Service, Virg. Duty, Propert. See Ministry; Obedience.

units.la: Obserere, vid. Conferere.
units.tr: To bolt, see To bring together.

units.la: Obfervabilis, vid. Notabilis.
units.tr: Remarkable, see Notable.

units.la: Obfervanter, vid. Diligenter.
units.tr: Attentively, see Diligently.

units.la: Observantia] Observantia est, per quam ætate, aut sapientiâ, aut honore, aut dignitate aliqua antecedentes reveremur & colimus, Cic. Observatio, Val. Max. Dignatio, Numerus. Locus. Esse aliquo loco, numero apud aliquem. Pondus. Habere pondus: magni ponderis, & aliquo pondere esse apud aliquem, Cic. Reverentia. Veneratio, Id.
units.tr: Respect, observance: Observance is that by which we revere and honour those who excel in age, wisdom, honour or some dignity, Cic. Observance, Val. Max. Esteem. Number. Place. To be in someone's place, to count with someone. Weight. To have weight: to be of great weight, and to be of some weight with someone, Cic. Reverence. Veneration, Id.

units.la: Observare] Adnotare: advertere, Plin. In oculis habere. Captare, suspensum esse quomodo &c.Cic.
units.tr: To observe: To note, to take notice, Plin. To keep in view. To watch for, to be in suspense as to how, and so on, Cic.

units.la: Observator occultus] Corycæus. Annotator, Plin. Speculator, Cic.
units.tr: Secret observer: Corycaeus. Annotator, Plin. Spy, Cic.

units.la: Obses] Pignus obsidatus, Amm. Cùm tantus Arrhabo populi R. penes Samnites esset (Cato arrhabonem dixit 600. obsides.)
units.tr: Hostage: A pledge of hostageship, Amm. When the Roman people had so great an earnest among the Samnites (Cato called the earnest six hundred hostages).

units.la: Obsides dare]Cavere alicui obsidibus.Cæs.Obsidio aliquem dare,Tac.Obsidatus pignore sobolem suam tradiderunt,Tac.
units.tr: To give hostages: To secure someone with hostages, Caes. To give someone as a hostage, Tac. They gave up their children as a pledge of hostageship, Tac.

units.la: Obsides accipere] Cavere sibi ab aliquo obsidibus, Cæs.
units.tr: To take hostages: To secure oneself against someone with hostages, Caes.

units.la: Obsidere]Præsidebat littora Oceani haud spernenda manus. Insidere anfractus silvarum, Sil. Obsidere aditus. Circumsidere aliquem. Sepire oppidum,Cic. Obsidium facere,Gell. Obsidione premere, cingere, Virg. Claudere, Lucan. Assidere oppidum,Salust. Cingere copiis. Claudere alicui fugam. Circumfunduntur hostes, Liv. Appugnare castra, Tac.
units.tr: To besiege, occupy: A force not to be despised guarded the shores of the ocean. To sit in the windings of the forests, Sil. To block the approaches. To surround someone. To wall in a town, Cic. To lay siege, Gell. To press with a siege, to encircle, Virg. To shut in, Lucan. To sit down before a town, Sall. To surround with troops. To cut someone off from flight. The enemies surround him, Liv. To attack a camp, Tac.

units.la: Obsidio] Obsessio. Circumsessio. Oppressio, Cic. Obsidium, Tac. Obsidiæ, Sipont. ap. Col.
units.tr: Siege: Besieging. Investing. Oppression, Cic. Siege, Tac. Sieges, Sipont. ap. Col.

units.la: Obsidionem solvere] Solvere obsidione, Plin.Iun. Solvere obsidium, Tac. Relinquere obsidionem, Cæs. Obsidione eximere, liberare, Cic. Plin.
units.tr: To raise a siege: To lift the siege, Plin. Iun. To raise the siege, Tac. To abandon the siege, Caes. To free from a siege, to liberate, Cic., Plin.

units.la: Obsignare, vid. Sigillare.
units.tr: To seal up, see To seal.

units.la: Obsignatio] Consignatio, Quint.
units.tr: Sealing: Signing, Quint.

units.la: Obsignator] Signator, Salust. Tabularius, Tac.
units.tr: Sealer: Signatory, Sall. Keeper of records, Tac.

units.la: Obsistere] Resistere alicui : contra aliquem. Opponere se alicui. Offerre se sceleri alicujus. Contra aliquem facere. Contravenire aliquem. Venire contra rem alicujus. Contra omni ratione pugnare. Adversarium esse alicujus. jus, Cic. Contra stare, Nev. Tendere adversus. Intercedere sententiae alicujus, Liv. Intercedere contra aliquem, Plin. Interponere se audaciae alicujus, Cic. Obviare alicui, Macrob. Vid. Reniti.
units.tr: To resist, withstand: To oppose someone. To set oneself against someone. To offer oneself against someone's crime. To act against someone. To come against someone. To go against someone's interest. To fight against all reason. To be someone's opponent, Cic. To stand against, Nev. To strive against. To intercede against someone's opinion, Liv. To intervene against someone, Plin. To interpose oneself against someone's boldness, Cic. To meet someone in the way, Macrob. See Resist.

units.la: Obsolescere] Obfuscari. Iust. Decolorari, Col. Evanescere stinguique colorem, Lucr. Vid. Exolescere.
units.tr: To fall into disuse, fade: To grow dim, Just. To lose colour, Col. To fade away and the colour be extinguished, Lucr. See To wear out.

units.la: Obsoletus, vid. Priscus.
units.tr: Obsolete, see Ancient.

units.la: Obstaculum, vid. Impedimentum.
units.tr: Obstacle, see Hindrance.

units.la: Obstinatè, vid. Pertinaciter.
units.tr: Obstinately, see Persistently.

units.la: Obstinatio, vid. Contumacia.
units.tr: Obstinacy, see Contumacy.

units.la: Obstinare, vid. Obfirmare.
units.tr: To persist, see To harden.

units.la: Obstinatus] Obfirmatus. Obstinatae voluntatis, Cic. Destinatus, Catul. Mens obnixa malo, Stat. Vid. Contumax.
units.tr: Obstinate: Hardened. Of obstinate will, Cic. Resolved, Catul. A mind stubbornly set on evil, Stat. See Contumacious.

units.la: Obstipus] Obstipum caput, Cic. Obstipa & rigida cervix. Obstipo capite aliquis, Suet.
units.tr: Bent, stiff: A head bent to one side, Cic. A stiff and rigid neck. Someone with his head bent, Suet.

units.la: Obstare] Obsistere fugienti, Ovid. Officit altitudo aedium auspiciis, Cic. Vid. Impedire.
units.tr: To stand in the way: To stand in the way of someone fleeing, Ovid. The height of the house obstructs the auspices, Cic. See Hinder.

units.la: Obstragulum] Corrigia calceamenti, Cic. Ligula calceorum, Iuv. Ansa, Tibul. Ansula, Val.M.
units.tr: Shoe-strap: The thong of a shoe, Cic. The shoe-latchet, Juv. A loop, handle, Tibul. A small handle, Val. Max.

units.la: Obstrepere, vid. Obtundere.
units.tr: To make a din, see To deafen.

units.la: Obstringere, obstrictus. vid. Obligare, obligatus.
units.tr: To bind, bound, see To oblige, obliged.

units.la: Obstructio] Oppilatio aurium, Scribon. Obturatio, Sipont.
units.tr: Obstruction: A blocking of the ears, Scribon. A stopping up, Sipont.

units.la: Obstruere] Explere rimas, Cic. Oppilare, Lucr. Obturare, Varr. Obmoliri, Liv. Obstipare, Calep.
units.tr: To block up: To fill cracks, Cic. To choke up, Lucr. To stop up, Varr. To build up a barrier, Liv. To stuff, Calep.

units.la: Obstupefacere, vid. Stupefacere.
units.tr: To astonish, see To stupefy.

units.la: Obstupescere, vid. Stupere.
units.tr: To be astonished, see To be stunned.

units.la: Obtegere, vid. Tegere.
units.tr: To cover, see To cover.

units.la: Obtemperare, vid. Obedire.
units.tr: To comply, see To obey.

units.la: Obtestari, vid. Obsecrare, orare.
units.tr: To call to witness, see To beseech, to pray.

units.la: Obtigit mihi aliquid] Cic. Obvenit mihi forte, in fortione hereditas, Id. Contigit mihi, Ter. Sortitus sum aliquid, Ovid.
units.tr: Something has fallen to me, Cic. Something came to me by chance, an inheritance by luck, Id. It befell me, Ter. I have been allotted something, Ovid.

units.la: Obtinere] Compotem fieri alicujus rei, Cic. Potiri auro, Virg. Tenere, Plin.Iun.
units.tr: To obtain, hold: To become master of something, Cic. To possess gold, Virg. To hold, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Obtrectatio, obtrectator, vid. Oblocutio. &c.
units.tr: Detraction, detractor, see Slander, etc.

units.la: Obtundere aures alicui] Onerare aures mendaciis. Callent aures meae illius sermonibus. Refercire aures alicujus. Inculcare aliquid alicui. Insusurrare crebrò cantilenam suam alicui. Inculcant se auribus nostris, Cic. Tundere aures alicujus, Plaut. Adstrepere aures alicujus, Plin. Iun. Verberare aures sermonibus, Tac. Cantilenam eandem canere. Ter. Exsurdare aliquem, Val. Max. Aures sermonibus implere, Ovid. Complere, Claud. Obtundere aures. Obruere, opprimere alicujus orationem, Cic. Ogganire alicui in aurem, Ter.
units.tr: To deafen someone's ears: To burden the ears with lies. My ears are tired of his talk. To fill someone's ears again. To drum a tune into someone's ears. To keep whispering one's song into someone's ear. They drum themselves into our ears, Cic. To beat someone's ears, Plaut. To ring in someone's ears, Plin. Iun. To batter the ears with talk, Tac. To sing the same tune, Ter. To deafen someone, Val. Max. To fill the ears with talk, Ovid. To fill, Claud. To deafen the ears. To drown out someone's speech, Cic. To whisper into someone's ear, Ter.

units.la: Obturamentum] Epistomium, Iun. Vid. Operculum.
units.tr: Stopper: A plug, Iun. See Covering.

units.la: Obturare] Obstruere, Plin. Oppilare ostia, Lucret. Obmoliri, Liv. Operculare vasa, Col.
units.tr: To stop up: To block up, Plin. To close doorways, Lucr. To build up, Liv. To cover vessels, Col.

units.la: Obturbare, vid. Inquietare.
units.tr: To disturb, see To disquiet.

units.la: Obtusus, vid. Hebes.
units.tr: Blunt, see Dull.

units.la: Obvertere, vid. Vertere, Dirigere.
units.tr: To turn towards, see To turn, To direct.

units.la: Obviare alicui] Progredi obviam, Liv. Obvium esse. Ferre se obviam alicui. Obvium volare alicui. Obviam alicui procedere, prodire, venire, Cic. Obviam exire, occurrere. Obviam se dare alicui, Liv. Obviam proficisci, Cæs. Offerre se obvium, Ter. Adversum alicui ire, venire. Adversum fieri, venire, Plaut. Occurrere, Mart. Occursare alicui. Adversum tendentem vidit, Virg.
units.tr: To meet someone: To go forward to meet, Liv. To be in the way. To bring oneself into someone's way. To fly in someone's way. To go, come or proceed to meet someone, Cic. To go out to meet, run to meet. To present oneself in the way, Liv. To set out to meet, Caes. To offer oneself in the way, Ter. To go or come against someone. To come against, Plaut. To run into, Mart. To run to meet someone. He saw him coming towards him, Virg.

units.la: Obviatio] Obviam itio, Cic. Occursus, Plin. Offensus fortuitus, Macrob. Coitio, Quint. Cœtus, Plaut.
units.tr: Meeting: Going to meet, Cic. Encounter, Plin. Chance collision, Macrob. Coming together, Quint. Gathering, Plaut.

units.la: Obumbrare] Obnubere, Varr. Adumbrare. Col. Velare aliquid extrinsecus, Tac. Inumbrat vespera universum, Id. Umbravit forum velis. Præpandere. Obtendere alicui velum, membranam, Plin. Obtendere aliquid, Tegere. Prætegere. Obducere operimentô, Cic. Prætendere manum auribus, Plin. Iun. Præstringere, Cic. Opponere manum ante oculos, Ovid. Opacat ramus humum. Caligat nubes aliquid, Virg. Obnubilare, Gell.
units.tr: To overshadow: To cover over, Varr. To shade, Col. To veil something from outside, Tac. Evening shades the whole, Id. He shaded the forum with sails. To spread over. To hold a veil or membrane before someone, Plin. To hold something over, to cover. To cover with a covering, Cic. To hold a hand before the ears, Plin. Iun. To block, Cic. To put a hand before the eyes, Ovid. The branch shades the ground. The cloud darkens something, Virg. To cloud over, Gell.

units.la: Obvolvere, vid. Involvere.
units.tr: Obvolvere, see Involvere.

units.la: Obvolutio] Circumplexus, Plin.
units.tr: Obvolutio: an enfolding, an embrace, Plin.

units.la: Occa] Pecten, Ovid. Sirpices, vel, Irpices, Virg. Crates dentata stilis ferreis, Plin. Crates viminea, Virg.
units.tr: Occa: a rake, Ovid. Sirpices, or Irpices, Virg. A harrow set with iron teeth, Plin. A wicker harrow, Virg.

units.la: Occallescere, vid. Callescere.
units.tr: Occallescere, see Callescere.

units.la: Occare] Inoccare lupinum. Pulverare. Semina farriculis adobruere, Col. Subigere glebas, Cic. Delirare; Lure, Lucil. Sipont. Deoccare. Cratire. Pectinare, Plin. Occillare, Gloss.
units.tr: Occare: to harrow in lupins. To pulverise. To cover seed with spelt-grains, Col. To break up clods, Cic. To be deluded; Lure, Lucil. Sipont. To harrow off. To rake. To comb, Plin. To harrow, Gloss.

units.la: Occatio ] Ocecatio. Occœcatio, Non. Isid. Pulveratio, Col. Deliratio, Plin.
units.tr: Occatio: harrowing. Ocecatio. Occœcatio, Non. Isid. Pulverising, Col. A going astray, Plin.

units.la: Occator] Glebarius, Varr. Occillator, Gloss.
units.tr: Occator: a clod-breaker, Varr. A harrower, Gloss.

units.la: Occasio ] Occasiuncula, Plaut. Oblatum, Liv. Casum dare praeclari facinoris, Sallust. Occasus juvat rem, Enn. Ansa, Cic. Materia benefaciendi, Plin. Cursus apertus ad laudem. Seges & materia gloriæ. Ductus. Auctoritatem peccandi afferre. Facultates, Cic. Materia campusque tuis laudibus, Plin. Ducatum sceleri præbere, Hor. Janua lethi, Lucr. Fenestra ad nequitiam, Ter. Conciliabulum damni, Plaut.
units.tr: Occasio: a small opportunity, Plaut. An offer, Liv. To give the chance of a notable deed, Sallust. Opportunity helps a matter, Enn. A handle, Cic. Material for doing good, Plin. An open course to praise. A seed-bed and material of glory. A leading. To bring authority for sinning. Facilities, Cic. Material and field for your praises, Plin. To offer a leading to crime, Hor. A gate of death, Lucr. A window to wickedness, Ter. A meeting-place of loss, Plaut.

units.la: Occasio peccandi periculosa] Canem intestina gustâsse periculosum.
units.tr: Occasio peccandi periculosa: an opportunity for sin is dangerous; it is dangerous for a dog to have tasted entrails.

units.la: Occasio boni mala] Ex malis moribus nascuntur bonæ leges. Calamitas virtutis occasio.
units.tr: Occasio boni mala: an opportunity for good may be evil. Good laws are born from bad morals. Calamity is an opportunity for virtue.

units.la: Occasio mali non objicienda] Ignem stipulæ admovere non tutum. Non monstranda sunt canibus ossa. Occasio facit furem, Occasione duntaxat improbitati.
units.tr: Occasio mali non objicienda: an opportunity for evil must not be put before people. It is not safe to bring fire to straw. Bones must not be shown to dogs. Opportunity makes the thief; opportunity alone spurs wickedness.

units.la: Occasio occasionem trahit] Lis litem serit.
units.tr: Occasio occasionem trahit: one occasion draws on another. Strife sows strife.

units.la: Occasio expectando perditur] Qui tempus præstolatur, tempus perdit.
units.tr: Occasio expectando perditur: opportunity is lost by waiting. He who awaits the time loses the time.

units.la: Occasioni attendendum ] Premenda occasio. Arripienda, quæ offeruntur. Ferrum dum candet, cudendum. Primâ facie, primâ fronte. Primus veniens, primus molet. Prior occupat. Prior tempore, potior jure. Avis apertâ caveâ evolat, Lipf. Frons occipitio prior, Cat. Fronte capillata, post hæc occasio calva. Opportunitas rei gerendæ nunquam est negligenda.
units.tr: Occasioni attendendum: heed the opportunity. Seize the chance; seize what is offered. While the iron is hot, it must be struck. At first sight, at first glance. The first comer grinds first. The first to act takes it. Earlier in time, stronger in right. The bird flies out of an open cage, Lipf. The forehead comes before the back of the head, Cat. Opportunity has hair at the front, and after it is bald behind. The opportunity for doing a thing must never be neglected.

units.la: Occasionem dare ] Ansam dare, Patefacere viam, iter, aditum ad aliquid, Cic. Materiam præbere, Ovid. Fenestram ad nequitiam patefacero, Ter. Sternere viam alicui, Stat.
units.tr: Occasionem dare: to give a handle; to open a way, a path, access to something, Cic. To provide material, Ovid. To open a window to wickedness, Ter. To pave the way for someone, Stat.

units.la: Occasionem eripere] Manubrium e manu eripere.
units.tr: Occasionem eripere: to snatch the handle out of someone's hand.

units.la: Occasione data]Occasione oblata.Occasionem nactus, Cic. Per occasionem, Liv. Oblata facultate, fortunâ, Liv. Caf.
units.tr: Occasione data: with an opportunity offered. Having got an opportunity, Cic. By way of opportunity, Liv. With a facility or fortune offered, Liv., Caes.

units.la: Occasiones à Deo oblatæ, non spernendæ] Occasiones divinitus oblatas negligere, est adversus Deum ingratum esse, Demosth.
units.tr: Occasiones à Deo oblatae, non spernendae: to neglect opportunities offered by God is to be ungrateful towards God, Demosth.

units.la: Occasionibus scire uti] Scisti uti foro. Piscari in aqua turbidâ.
units.tr: Occasionibus scire uti: you know how to use the forum. To fish in troubled water.

units.la: Ex parvis occasionibus, paucula, magna] Lignum parvum accendit magnum.
units.tr: Ex parvis occasionibus, paucula, magna: a small stick kindles a great one.

units.la: Occasus] Obitus siderum, Cic. Sol occasus (mersus) suprema tempestas esto. in 12. Tabul. Sol in noctem vergens. Sole occaso aquantur, Gell.
units.tr: Occasus: the setting of the stars, Cic. Let the sun's setting (its sinking) be the last deadline, in the 12 Tabul. The sun declining toward night. When the sun has set they are made equal, Gell.

units.la: Occidens] Insula ultima occidentis, Catul. Occasus, Cic. Sinus ultimus occidentis, Hor. Occiduus orbis, Claud. Obeuntis solis partes, Cic. Ultima cœli, Lucr. Plaga occidua.
units.tr: Occidens: the furthest island of the west, Catul. Sunset, Cic. The furthest bay of the west, Hor. The western world, Claud. The parts of the setting sun, Cic. The farthest reaches of the sky, Lucr. A western region.

units.la: Occidentalis] Occiduus, Ovid.
units.tr: Occidentalis: western, Ovid.

units.la: Occidens occiditur] Qui mortem facit, mortem debet pati. Qui gladio ferit, gladio perit.
units.tr: Occidens occiditur: he who causes death must suffer death. Whoever strikes with the sword perishes by the sword.

units.la: Occidere, id est, Horizontem egredi] Obeunt sidera, Plin. Obluit cometes, Sen. Ruit sol, Virg. Cadunt sidera, Prop. Mergitur pars cœli, Sen. Oblitescunt stellæ, Cic.
units.tr: Occidere, id est, Horizontem egredi: the stars set, Plin. The comet sinks, Sen. The sun falls, Virg. The stars fall, Prop. Part of the sky sinks, Sen. The stars fade, Cic.

units.la: Occidere aliquem, id est, vitam adimere] Interimere. Mactare aliquem, Afferre mortem ictu. Cædem facere, efficere, Cic. Afficere cæde, Liv. Perimere cæde unâ, Virg. Conficere, Cic. Perdere aliquem capitis. Interficere vitâ & lumine. Capitalis cædes hic facta est, Plaut. Occupare ense, Propert. Occisio facta est, Cic. Vid. Necare.
units.tr: Occidere aliquem, id est, vitam adimere: to kill; to take away life. To slaughter someone; to bring death by a blow. To commit murder, to bring it about, Cic. To inflict slaughter, Liv. To destroy with one slaughter, Virg. To finish off, Cic. To deprive someone of life. To take away life and light. A capital murder was committed here, Plaut. To cut down with the sword, Propert. The killing was done, Cic. See Necare.

units.la: Occidere seipsum] Afferre sibi manus. Abjicere vitam. Exhaurire sibi vitam. Consciscere sibi mortem. Orbare se luce, Cic. Abrumpere sua fata, Sen. Accersere sibi fatum ferro, Lucan. Statuere de se. Irrogare sibi mortem. Animâ sese exuere, Tac. Renunciare vitæ, Suet. Qui sibi lethum insontes peperêre manu, lucemque perosi projecere animas, Virg. Projicere diem, Stat. Transfigere se ferro, Suet.
units.tr: Occidere seipsum: to lay hands on oneself. To cast away life. To drain one's own life. To bring death upon oneself. To deprive oneself of light, Cic. To break off one's own fate, Sen. To bring fate upon oneself by the sword, Lucan. To decide about oneself. To inflict death on oneself. To strip oneself of life, Tac. To renounce life, Suet. Those innocents who by their own hand brought death upon themselves, and, hating the light, threw away their lives, Virg. To cast away the day, Stat. To pierce oneself with a sword, Suet.

units.la: Occiput] Occipitium, Plaut.
units.tr: Occiput: the back of the head, Plaut.

units.la: Occisio] Internecio. Nex, Cic. Interfectio alicujus, Lamp. Interemptio, Plin. Internectio, Fest. Ultima poena, Plin.Iun. Extrema poena, Apul. Ultimum supplicium, IC. Summum supplicium, Paul. IC.
units.tr: Occisio: slaughter. Destruction; killing, Cic. The killing of someone, Lamp. A slaying, Plin. A destruction, Fest. The final punishment, Plin. Iun. The extreme punishment, Apul. The ultimate penalty, IC. The supreme penalty, Paul. IC.

units.la: Occisus] Poenaliter interire. Poenali ferro vel gladio consumpti. Poenali morte perière, Amm. Fustibus ad exitium necatus, Amm. Merita morte perire, Virg. Internectus, Plaut. Biothanatus, Lampr.
units.tr: Occisus: to die by judicial punishment. Destroyed by a penal sword or blade. They perished by penal death, Amm. Killed with clubs to their destruction, Amm. To perish by a deserved death, Virg. Killed outright, Plaut. One who killed himself, Lampr.

units.la: Occludere, vid. Claudere.
units.tr: Occludere, see Claudere.

units.la: Occulta actiones] Furtivae operae.
units.tr: Occulta actiones: secret works; furtive operations.

units.la: Occultare aliquid] Tegere commissa, Hor. Habere aliquid tacitum. Plaut. Tacitè, Liv. Obscurè ferre, Cic. Occultè ferre, Ter. Clam aliquem facere. Plaut. Vid. Celare.
units.tr: Occultare aliquid: to hide what has been entrusted, Hor. To keep something quiet, Plaut. Quietly, Liv. To bear obscurely, Cic. To bear secretly, Ter. To do something behind someone's back, Plaut. See Celare.

units.la: Occultari factum nullum potest] Fama prodit omnia.
units.tr: Occultari factum nullum potest: no deed can be hidden; rumour reveals all things.

units.la: Occultatio] Abscondio, Plin. Abstrusio, Arnob. Latitatio, Quint.
units.tr: Occultatio: a concealing, Plin. A hiding away, Arnob. A lying hid, Quint.
