units.la: Occultator] Receptator latronum, Cic.Vlp.
units.tr: Occultator: a harbourer of robbers, Cic., Vlp.

units.la: Occulte] Abditè. Latenter. In angulo. Clam. Tecte, tectius. Occultissimè. Abscondite. Secreto. Obscurè serpit malum, Cic. Arcanè, Secretius, Col. Vid. Abditè.
units.tr: Occulte: secretly. Hidden; out of sight. In a corner. Covertly. Most secretly. Hidden away. In private. Evil creeps unseen, Cic. Mysteriously; more secretly, Col. See Abditè.

units.la: Occulte moliri malum] Monstrum alere.
units.tr: Occulte moliri malum: to nurse a monster.

units.la: Occultum, vid. Latebra.
units.tr: Occultum, see Latebra.

units.la: Occultus] Retrusus in tenebris. Retrusus, Abs. Interiores & reconditae literae. Perrecondita facultas, Cic. Tectus, Ter. Obstrusus recessus, Claud. Vid. Abscónditus.
units.tr: Occultus: sunk in darkness. Retired, Abs. Inner and hidden letters. A most profound faculty, Cic. Covered, Ter. A concealed recess, Claud. See Abscónditus.

units.la: Occumbere] Occubare, Liv. Decumbere, Cic. Sterni: stratus somno, Liv. Procumbere ictu saxi, Sil. Offenso pede, Ovid. Soluti vino procubuēre, Virg.
units.tr: Occumbere: to lie down; to fall, Liv. To sink down, Cic. To be laid low, stretched out in sleep, Liv. To fall forward at a blow of a stone, Sil. A foot having stumbled, Ovid. Loosened with wine, they fell down, Virg.

units.la: Occupare bona aliqua] Usurpare possessionem alicujus. Possidere agros, bona. Potiri regni, Cic. Obsidere praesidiis Italiam, Id. Tenere forum. Praesidiis aliquem locum interclusum tenere, Id. Insidere locum aliquem, Liv.
units.tr: Occupare bona aliqua: to seize possession of someone's goods. To take possession of fields and goods. To gain control of a kingdom, Cic. To hold Italy with garrisons, Id. To hold the forum. To hold a place cut off by garrisons, Id. To settle in a place, Liv.

units.la: Occupari negotiis] Distineri maximis occupationibus. Districtus sum. Implicatus operosis negotiis. Me Reip. procuratio multis officiis implicatum & constrictum tenebat. Negotiis plenus sum. Detineri, obrui negotiis. Impediri ab aliquā re negotiis. Habent me occupatiorem negotia. Distentus tum operā tum animo sum. Distentus est tot tantisque negotiis, ut respirare libere non possit, Cicer. Negotiosus sum, Salust. Distringor officio, causis, Plin. Iun. Distractus occupationibus sum, Sen. Negotium est. Opera est mihi. Non est operae mihi in tanto rerum discrimine legationes audire, Plaut. Liv. Egere tempore, Cic.
units.tr: Occupari negotiis: to be drawn away by very great occupations. I am taken up. Entangled in laborious business. The management of the commonwealth held me entangled and bound by many duties. I am full of business. To be held back, overwhelmed by business. To be hindered from something by business. Business keeps me busier. I am stretched both in work and in mind. He is so occupied with so many great matters that he cannot breathe freely, Cicer. I am busy, Salust. I am taken up with duties and cases, Plin. Iun. I am pulled apart by occupations, Sen. There is business. I have work. I have no time to hear embassies in such a crisis of affairs, Plaut., Liv. To lack time, Cic.

units.la: Occupare alienis negotiis] Fundum alienum arare.
units.tr: Occupare alienis negotiis: to plough another's field.

units.la: Occupationes] Negotia, Cic. Studium, Ter. Magna molimina rerum tenent numen, (i. Caesarem), Ovid. Negotiositas.
units.tr: Occupationes: business, Cic. Eagerness, Ter. Great designs of affairs hold the divine power (i.e. Caesar), Ovid. Busyness.

units.la: Occupatus ] Occupatissimus. Occupationibus implicatus, Cic. Negotiosus, Tacit. Distractus curis. Involutus, distentus, immersus, obrutus, opertus negotiis. Tot me res circumvallant; tot me pericula circumstant, circumsistunt, obsepiunt, cingunt, premunt, urgent, Er.
units.tr: Occupatus: very busy. Entangled in occupations, Cic. Busy, Tacit. Distracted by cares. Wrapped up, occupied, immersed, overwhelmed, engrossed in business. So many things surround me; so many dangers beset, besiege, hem in, encircle, press and urge me, Er.

units.la: Occurrere] Obviam ire cupiditati alicujus, Cic. Prospicere malo alicui. Praemunire ante. Providere consilio. Praestare. Anteoccupare. Huic malo consulite ac providete, Id. Vid. Obviare. Uni nemo hostium adversus prodiit, Liv.
units.tr: Occurrere: to go to meet someone's desire, Cic. To look ahead to someone's harm. To fortify beforehand. To provide by counsel. To excel. To forestall. Take counsel and provide against this evil, Id. See Obviare. No enemy came out against him alone, Liv.

units.la: Octonarius ] Octonaria fistula, Plin. Octupla pars, Cicer. Octuplicatus, Liv.
units.tr: Octonarius: an eight-part pipe, Plin. An eighth part, Cicer. Multiplied eightfold, Liv.

units.la: Ocularis] Ocularius. Ocularia claritas, Sol.
units.tr: Ocularis: of the eye. Ocular brightness, Sol.

units.la: Oculatus ] Oculeus totus, Plin. Noctividus, M. Capel. Lynceis oculis homo. Acutum cernens. Tam cernit acutum, quàm aut aquila, aut serpens Epidaurius, Hor. Perspicacior lynceo & Argo, Apul. Argus foris, domi talpa.
units.tr: Oculatus: all eye, Plin. Seeing at night, M. Capel. A man with lynx's eyes. Seeing what is sharp. He sees as keenly as an eagle or the Epidaurian serpent, Hor. Sharper-sighted than the lynx and Argus, Apul. Argus abroad, a mole at home.

units.la: Oculatis hallucinationem tribuere ] Cornicum oculos configere.
units.tr: Oculatis hallucinationem tribuere: to ascribe delusion to those with sharp eyes. To pick at the eyes of crows.

units.la: Oculi ] Lumen, Lucr. Fenestrae, Prudent. Postes, Lucr. Portae solis, Hesych. Fenestrae, animi, Cic. Lux, Ovid. Janua animi. Illices amoris. Cogitationum indices. Corporis duces. Luminis vasa.
units.tr: Oculi: light, Lucr. Windows, Prudent. Doorposts, Lucr. Gates of the sun, Hesych. Windows of the mind, Cic. Light, Ovid. Gate of the mind. Lures of love. Indicators of thoughts. Leaders of the body. Vessels of light.

units.la: Oculi immoti] Rigentes oculi.
units.tr: Oculi immoti: fixed, staring eyes.

units.la: Oculos movere ] Oculos conjicere, Convertere, contorquere aspectum aliquò, Cic. Flectere oculos, attollere, Ovid. Tollere oculos contrà, Tendere oculos, jactare, Lucr. Emittere, tere, spargere, Perf. Aspicere aliquem, Plaut. Aperire oculos. Referre aspectum aliquò, Cic.
units.tr: Oculos movere: to cast one's eyes; to turn or twist one's gaze somewhere, Cic. To lift or raise the eyes, Ovid. To lift one's eyes against; to fix one's eyes; to dart them, Lucr. To send forth, scatter, Perf. To look at someone, Plaut. To open the eyes. To turn one's gaze somewhere, Cic.

units.la: Ocyor, vid. Agilis.
units.tr: Ocyor, see Agilis.

units.la: Odiosus] Detestabilis. Putidus, Invisus omnibus. Dignus odio. Invidiosus & infensus multis, Cic. Odibilis, Lampr. Poenitendus, Col. Fastidio est, Plin. Exosus diis. Aspernabilis, Gell. Nauseosus, Plin. Odium terrae, Plaut. Marte odiosior, Er.
units.tr: Odiosus: detestable. Foul, hated by all. Worthy of hatred. Hated and hostile to many, Cic. Hateful, Lampr. To be regretted, Col. It is loathsome, Plin. Abhorred by the gods. Disgusting, Gell. Nauseating, Plin. The hated thing of the earth, Plaut. More hateful than war, Er.

units.la: Odisse] Male odisse. Odium gerere in aliquem. Flagrare odio alicujus. Abhorrere aliquem; ab aliquo. Alienum habere ab aliquo animum. Alienissimum esse ab aliquo, Cic. Magno esse odio in aliquem. Alieno esse ab aliquo animo. Omnes illum aspernabantur atque abhorrebant. Omnes, ut aliquem bestiam, &c. fugiebant. Ardent in aliquid odia alicujus, Cicer. Odium tenet, capit alicujus, Ter. Perosus sum aliquid, Liv. Exosus sum aliquid, Virg.
units.tr: Odisse: to hate wickedly. To bear hatred against someone. To burn with someone's hatred. To shrink from someone, from something. To have an estranged mind toward someone. To be utterly alienated from someone, Cic. To be an object of great hatred to someone. To be of an estranged mind toward someone. They all shunned and recoiled from him. They all fled from him as from a beast, etc. Someone's hatreds blaze against something, Cicer. Someone's hatred holds or seizes someone, Ter. I am utterly hated by something, Liv. I am hated by something, Virg.

units.la: Odisse valde] Odisse odio Vatiniano. Capitali odio ab aliquo dissentire. Magnum in aliquem odium habere, Cic. Odisse odio novercali, Tac. Septenis in diem horis odisse aliquem, Iuv. Vid. Praecedentia.
units.tr: To hate greatly: to hate with Vatinian hatred; to dissent from someone with deadly hatred; to have great hatred against someone, Cic.; to hate with step-motherly hatred, Tac.; to hate someone seven times a day, Juv. See the preceding entries.

units.la: Oderunt se uterque] Alter alterum odit. Oderunt alter alterum. Mutuum oderunt. Oderunt se mutuo. Oderunt invicem: inter sese. Mutuum inter ipsos est odium. Neuter alterum amat. Alter alterum vicissim odit, Erasm.
units.tr: They hate each other: each hates the other; they hate one another; they hate each other mutually; they hate each other in return; there is mutual hatred between them; neither loves the other; one hates the other in turn, Erasm.

units.la: Odium] Invidia. Inimicus animus. Ira inveterata, Cic. Aversatio, Sen. Rancor, Cassian.
units.tr: Hatred: envy; a hostile mind; long-standing anger, Cic.; aversion, Sen.; rancour, Cassian.

units.la: Odium ingens] Capitale, infestum, acerrimum, insitum animis odium, Cic. Vatinianum, Catul. Novercale, Tac.
units.tr: Great hatred: deadly, hostile, most bitter hatred planted in men's minds, Cic.; Vatinian hatred, Catull.; step-motherly hatred, Tac.

units.la: Odium alicui creare] Vocare in odium. Subjicere odium, Rapere aliquem in invidiam. Concitare odium in aliquem. Inflammare, augere, conflare, parare invidiam, Cicer. Conciliare alicui odium omnium, Plin. Odium facere, Cic.
units.tr: To stir up hatred against someone: to bring someone into hatred; to lay hatred upon someone; to drag someone into odium; to stir up hatred against someone; to kindle, increase, fan or prepare envy, Cic.; to win someone the hatred of all, Plin.; to incur hatred, Cic.

units.la: Odium incurrere] Convertere in se odia omnium. Subire hominum odia. Incurrere, irruere in odia. Vocari in invidiam. diam. Colligere invidiam crudelitatis ex re aliqua. Venire in odium acerbissimum multitudini, Cic.
units.tr: To incur hatred: to turn the hatred of all upon oneself; to take upon oneself men's hatreds; to run into or rush into hatreds; to be brought into envy; to draw upon oneself envy for some cruelty; to come into the most bitter hatred of the crowd, Cic.

units.la: In odio esse ] In invidia & odio esse apud omnes. In odio esse omnibus. Odio esse apud omnes. Invidiâ & odio premi. Invidiæ incendio conflagrare. Laborare ex invidia. Omnium in illum ardent odia. Invidiam habere, sustinere. In invidia esse, Cicer. Laborare odio apud aliquem, Liv. Æstuare invidiâ, Salust.
units.tr: To be hated: to be in envy and hatred with everyone; to be hated by all; to be oppressed by envy and hatred; to be set alight by the fire of envy; to suffer from envy; the hatred of all burns against him; to bear or endure envy; to be in envy, Cic.; to labour under hatred from someone, Liv.; to seethe with envy, Sall.

units.la: Odianon curare ] Odia aliquorum sorbere & concoquere, Cic.
units.tr: Not to mind hatreds: to swallow and digest the hatreds of others, Cic.

units.la: Odium amoliri] Levare aliquem invidiâ. Deonerare ex invidia. Mittere sanguinem invidiæ. Liberare invidiâ aliquem. Invidiam sedare, transferre, Cicer. In alium vertere, Quint. Exonerare aliquem invidiâ, Mart. Lenire invidiam, Salust.
units.tr: To remove hatred: to relieve someone of envy; to unburden someone of envy; to let out the blood of envy; to free someone from envy; to calm envy, to transfer it, Cic.; to turn it upon another, Quint.; to lift envy from someone, Mart.; to soften envy, Sall.

units.la: Odor] Odoratus gravis coriandri. Voluptas aliena; nam qui gerit, ipse non sentit, Plin. Odoramen, Macrob. Spiritus unguenti, Lucr. Olor (ab oleo) Apul. Col. Halitus pomorum, Col. Fragrantia. f. a. v. Odos.
units.tr: Odour: a heavy smell of coriander; a pleasure of another's, for the one who wears it does not notice it himself, Plin.; a perfume, Macrob.; the scent of ointment, Lucr.; olor (from oleum), Apul., Col.; the breath of apples, Col.; fragrance. Odos.

units.la: Odorari] Olfacere, Cic. Olefacere & odefacere (ab odore,) Fest. Olfactare aliquid, Plaut. Vestigare odore. Trahere odorem. Frui odore, Plin. Vestigare naribus, Col. Consulere nares, Mart. Obodorare, Plaut. Naribus hariolari, Lucan. Naribus auras captare, Virg. Sagio antequam oblata est res, Cic.
units.tr: To smell: to scent, Cic.; to smell out (from odor), Fest.; to sniff at something, Plaut.; to track by scent; to draw in a smell; to enjoy an odour, Plin.; to track with the nostrils, Col.; to consult the nostrils, Mart.; to sniff out, Plaut.; to divine with the nostrils, Lucan.; to catch the breezes with the nostrils, Virg.; to smell out a thing before it is offered, Cic.

units.la: Odoratio] Odoratus, Cic. Odorationum voluptates, Id.
units.tr: Smelling: the sense of smell, Cic.; the pleasures of odours, Id.

units.la: Odorus, vid. Olens.
units.tr: Odorous: see Smelling sweet.

units.la: OEconomia ] Res familiares & domesticæ. Cura rei domesticæ, Cic. Res, absol. Ter.
units.tr: Economy: household and domestic affairs; care of domestic matters, Cic.; affairs, used absolutely, Ter.

units.la: OEconomiam administrare] Administrare rem familiarem: &, rem, absol. Obire res suas; rem privatam. Revocare se ad curam rei domesticæ. Servire rei familiari, Cic. Rei operam dare, Ter.
units.tr: To manage the household: to administer family affairs; and, affairs used absolutely; to attend to one's own affairs or private business; to turn oneself back to the care of domestic matters; to serve family business, Cic.; to give attention to one's affairs, Ter.

units.la: OEconomice] OEconomica. Prudentia domestica. Privatæ rei ratio, Cic. Scientia rei familiaris, Col.
units.tr: Economical: household management; domestic prudence; a reckoning of private affairs, Cic.; knowledge of family matters, Col.

units.la: OEconomicus] Rationes familiares. Liber de tuendâ re familiari.
units.tr: Economic: family accounts; a book on preserving one's family property.

units.la: OEconomus diligens ] Diligentissimus rei familiaris, Suet. Rei operam dat, Ter. Sapit ad rem suam, Plaut. Suæ rei benè gerens, Cic. Diligens patrimonii, Sen.
units.tr: A careful housekeeper: most diligent in family affairs, Suet.; attends to his affairs, Ter.; is shrewd about his own interest, Plaut.; managing his own affairs well, Cic.; diligent in looking after his estate, Sen.

units.la: Offa, vid. Fructum.
units.tr: Cake: see Fruit.

units.la: Offendere] Offendere animum alicui. Offendere in aliquo aliquem. Concitare, contrahere offensionem alicujus. Cadere in offensionem alicujus, incurrere. Esse in offensa; offensioni alicui. Vulnerare aliquem voce. Lædere aliquem contumeliosè, ludibrio. Exulcerare gratiam alicujus, Cic. Confricare sensus judicum, Gell. Verbis odia aspera movere, Virg. Radere aures delicatas, Quint.
units.tr: To offend: to offend someone's mind; to offend someone in some matter; to provoke and incur someone's displeasure; to fall into someone's offence or run into it; to be in offence; to be an offence to someone; to wound someone with words; to injure someone with insult or mockery; to gall someone's favour, Cic.; to rub the feelings of judges raw, Gell.; to stir up bitter hatreds with words, Virg.; to grate on delicate ears, Quint.

units.la: Offendere ad aliquid ] Ad fornicem caput offendere, Cic. Oblædere manum, Plaut. Lædere oculos, Hor. Si quis in opere sauciatus noxam cepit, Col. Incidere in lapidem, Varr. Impingere se in columnam. Incursitare in, Sen. Offensare capita, Liv. Incutere pollicem limini, Plin. Infringere liminibus lumbos, Hor. Illidere foribus caput, Suet. Illidi ad scopulos, Cæs. Illidi in, Quint. Detundere digitos pedum ob lapides, Apul.
units.tr: To strike against something: to strike one's head against the vault, Cic.; to hurt one's hand, Plaut.; to injure the eyes, Hor.; if anyone was wounded at work and suffered harm, Col.; to stumble on a stone, Varr.; to run into a column; to run against, Sen.; to bump one's head, Liv.; to stub one's thumb against a threshold, Plin.; to dash the loins against the doorposts, Hor.; to knock one's head against doors, Suet.; to be dashed against rocks, Caes.; to be dashed against, Quint.; to stub one's toes on stones, Apul.

units.la: Offendi] Offensionem accipere. Offensioni mihi est. Offensio facta est animi mei perversitate aliquorum. Lædi crimine. Incurrit in offensionem & odium meum, Cic. Accipere aliquid intemperanter, asperè, Tac. Durius, Ter. Facilè fit, quod illi doleat, Id.
units.tr: Taking offence: to take offence; it is an offence to me; the offence arose from the perversity of certain people in my mind; to be hurt by an accusation; he incurs offence and my hatred, Cic.; to take something intemperately or harshly, Tac.; more harshly, Ter.; it easily happens that what grieves him, Id.

units.la: Offendiculum ] Offensaculum, Lactant. Offensus, Sen. Vita in offensu est, Lambin. Offensum. Offensio, Cic.
units.tr: Hindrance: a stumbling-block, Lact.; a stumbling, Sen.; life is a stumbling, Lambin.; a stumbling-block; offence, Cic.

units.la: Offensio, actives] Vereri offensam (ne offenderet.) Læsio, Cic. Invidia verbi. Absit invidia verbo, Liv.
units.tr: Offence, active sense: to fear giving offence (lest he offend); injury, Cic.; the odium of a word; let there be no ill will in the word, Liv.

units.la: Offensio, passive] Accipere sine offensione aliquid. Vulnus. Offensiuncula, offensa, Cic.
units.tr: Offence, passive sense: to receive something without offence; a wound; a slight offence, Cic.

units.la: Offensivus, facilè offendens] Invidiosus. Invidus. Odiosum verbum. Res ardet invidiâ, Aculeatæ literæ, Cic. Habet offensionem hæc res apud aliquos, Plin. Acriter infestat sensum res aliqua, Lucr.
units.tr: Offensive, easily giving offence: envious; grudging; a hateful word; the matter blazes with envy, biting letters, Cic.; this matter gives offence to some, Plin.; the matter sharply assails the senses, Lucr.

units.la: Offensus] Offensa voluptas populi, Saucius, exulceratus animus, Cic.
units.tr: Offended: a pleasure of the people that is offended; a wounded, galled mind, Cic.

units.la: Offerre, vid. Sacrificare.
units.tr: To offer: see To sacrifice.

units.la: Officere, vid. Nocere.
units.tr: To hinder: see To harm.

units.la: Officina ] Locus sellæ atque operis quotidiani, Cic. Fabrica, Plin. Ergasterium, Rhodig. Pistrinum operarium.
units.tr: Workshop: a place of seat and daily work, Cic.; a workshop, Plin.; a workshop, Rhodig.; a working bakehouse.

units.la: Officiosus] Officiosissimus in aliquem. Singulari officio: summo officio præditus, officii plenus. Officiorum omnium observantissimus, Cic. Qui obsequio grassatur, Hor. Munes amicis videamur viri, Lucil.
units.tr: Dutiful: most dutiful towards someone; endowed with singular duty, with the highest duty, full of duty; most observant of all duties, Cic.; one who pursues with obsequiousness, Hor.; let us men appear dutiful to our friends, Lucil.

units.la: Officium] Munus. Partes. Professio. Persona: Hanc mihi personam impositi, Cic. Munia, pl. Id. Cura, Quint. Curatio, Plaut. Sors, Liv. Officii gratia.
units.tr: Duty: service; parts; profession; role. "I have been assigned this role," Cic.; duties, plural, Id.; care, Quint.; attention, Plaut.; lot, Liv.; out of courtesy.

units.la: Officium geram, vid. Geram.
units.tr: To perform a duty: see To perform.

units.la: Officium est labor] Honos onus.
units.tr: Duty is toil: honour is a burden.

units.la: Officium non nocet ] Officium suum nemini debet esse damnosum.
units.tr: Duty does no harm: one's duty ought to be harmful to no one.

units.la: Officio dimittere ] Rude donare aliquem. Rudem accipere verò est dimitti.
units.tr: To dismiss from duty: to grant someone the wooden sword (discharge); but to receive the wooden sword is indeed to be dismissed.

units.la: Officium mutuum] Manus manum lavat, fricat. Mutuum muli scabunt. Pes pedem fulcit. Officiis mutuis respondere, Cic.
units.tr: Mutual duty: the hand washes and rubs the hand; mules scratch each other; the foot supports the foot; to return mutual services, Cic.

units.la: Officium quisque faciat suum] Defendat pampinus uvas, Virg. Spartam, quam nactus es, orna.
units.tr: Let each do his own duty: let the tendril protect the grapes, Virg.; adorn Sparta, which you have obtained.

units.la: Offundere alicui aquam] Perfundere aliquem a quâ ferventi. Circumfundere. Inundat terram aqua, Cic. Obsipare alicui aquulam, Plaut. Circumluere, Liv. Undare campos sanguine, Stat. Cingitur amni urbs, Virg. Inundatur sanguine, Liv.
units.tr: To pour water upon someone: to drench someone with hot water; to surround; water floods the land, Cic.; to sprinkle someone with a little water, Plaut.; to flow around, Liv.; to wash the fields with blood, Stat.; the city is girdled by the river, Virg.; it is flooded with blood, Liv.

units.la: Offuscare, vid. Obscurare.
units.tr: To darken: see To obscure.

units.la: Ogganire alicui, vid. Obtundere.
units.tr: To bother someone: see To blunt.

units.la: Oh] Ohe, Perf. Oho, Plaut. O. Pro Deum, vel Proh, Ter. Cic.
units.tr: Oh: ohe, Pers.; oho, Plaut.; O; for the gods' sake, or alas, Ter., Cic.

units.la: Oleaginem] Oleaginus, Virg. Oleaceus, Plin. Olearis talea, Col. Olivifer, Ovid.
units.tr: Olive-like: olive-bearing, Virg.; oleaceous, Plin.; an olive cutting, Col.; olive-bearing, Ovid.

units.la: Olens qui odorem exhalat ] Suaveolens, Catul. Odorifer, odoratus, Plin. Odorus. Bene olens, Virg. Grate olens, & grateolens, Apul. Excitatissimus odore, i. res excitatissimi odoris, Plin. Tanquam de narthecio vel myrothecio depromptus, Cic. Omnium unguentorum odor præ tuo nautea est. Tu mihi stacte, tu cinnamomum, tu rosa, tu crocum & casia es, Plaut. de vino. Quod tu cùm olfacies, Deos rogabis, totum te ut faciant nasum, Catul. Ambrosius liquor, Stat. Olidus murice, Mart.
units.tr: Sweet-smelling, giving off an odour: sweet-smelling, Catull.; odorous, fragrant, Plin.; odorous; smelling well, Virg.; pleasantly fragrant, Apul.; of most exciting fragrance, i.e. things of most exciting odour, Plin.; as if taken out of a perfume-box or myrrh-box, Cic.; the scent of all ointments is nausea beside yours; you are my storax, you are my cinnamon, you are my rose, you are my saffron and cassia, Plaut., speaking of wine; when you smell it, you will pray to the gods to make your whole self a nose, Catull.; ambrosial liquor, Stat.; stinking of purple-shell, Mart.

units.la: Olere] Olet Arabicè. Obolere,Plaut. Olet benè, Cic. Jucundè, Plin. Odorem reddere, Id. Diffundere odorem. Spirat odor,Virg. Odorem exspirare,Catul. Afflantur odores è floribus,Cic. Fragrat odor, Virg. Exhalant vestes,Stat. Spirat totam Arabiam. Spirat nectar.
units.tr: To smell: it smells of Arabia; to smell foully, Plaut.; to smell sweet, Cic.; pleasantly, Plin.; to give off a smell, Id.; to diffuse a scent; a scent breathes forth, Virg.; to breathe out fragrance, Catull.; odours are wafted from the flowers, Cic.; fragrance rises, Virg.; garments exhale, Stat.; it breathes all Arabia; it breathes nectar.

units.la: Olere, in specie] Olere crocum,Cic. Myrrham,Plaut. Olet aliquid sulfure,Ovid. Nardo,Propert. Redolere vinum,Cic. Redolere thymo. Spirare odorem ambrosium. Halare floribus horti, Virg. Fragrare hesterno vino, Mart.
units.tr: To smell of something: to smell of saffron, Cic.; of myrrh, Plaut.; of sulphur, Ovid.; of nard, Propert.; to smell of wine, Cic.; to smell of thyme; to breathe an ambrosial scent; to breathe out the flowers of the garden, Virg.; to be fragrant with yesterday's wine, Mart.

units.la: Oletare] Oletum facere, Perf. Alvum levare, exinanire, evacuare. Reddere,Plin. Alvum dejicere,Cat. Purgare,Cic. Subtrahere, Celf. Exsolvere ventrem, Id. Exonerare ventrem,Mart. Eluviem facere per ventrem,Lucil. Emittere saturitatem. Reddere onus ciborum,Plin. Excernere,abf. Sedere,Marcil.Emp. Cacare,Hor. Egerere, eluere cibi reliquias per ventrem,Turneb. Excipere ventris onus auro, Mart.
units.tr: To defecate: to make a stench, Perf.; to relieve the bowels, empty out, evacuate; to void, Plin.; to drop the bowels, Cat.; to purge, Cic.; to withdraw, Cels.; to loosen the belly, Id.; to unload the belly, Mart.; to make a flux through the belly, Lucil.; to let out one's fill; to void the load of food, Plin.; to excrete, absolutely, Id.; to sit, Marcell. Emp.; to defecate, Hor.; to void, to wash out the remains of food through the belly, Turneb.; to pay the belly's load in gold, Mart.

units.la: Oletum, vid. Excrementum.
units.tr: Latrine: see Excrement.

units.la: Oleum] Olivum,Plaut.Oleum cibarium.Oleum olivæ,Col.
units.tr: Oil: olive, Plaut.; cooking oil; olive oil, Col.

units.la: Olfacere, vid. Odorari.
units.tr: To smell: see To smell.

units.la: Olfactorium] Olfactoriolum, Hier. Fasciculus florum odoratorum, Cic. Odoramentum, Sipont. Fasciculus odoramentorum, ex Plin.
units.tr: Scent-bottle: a little scent-bottle, Hier.; a bunch of fragrant flowers, Cic.; perfume, Sipont.; a bundle of perfumes, from Plin.

units.la: Olfactus] Odoratus, Cic.
units.tr: Smell: the sense of smell, Cic.

units.la: Olfactu acri praeditus] Naso plus videt,quàm oculis,Plaut.
units.tr: Keen-scented: the nose sees more than the eyes, Plaut.

units.la: Olidus, vid. Fœtidus.
units.tr: Olidus, see Foetidus.

units.la: Olim, vid. Quondam.
units.tr: Olim, see Quondam.

units.la: Olitor, vid. Hortulanus.
units.tr: Olitor, see Hortulanus.

units.la: Oliva] Olea, Virg.
units.tr: Oliva] Olive, Virg.

units.la: Olivetum] Oletum, Cato.
units.tr: Olivetum] Olive grove, Cato.

units.la: Olla] Hirnea fictilis, Cat. Seria, Perf. Chutra, vel chytra, Cat. Testa, tr. Ovid. Hor. Cacabus figuli, Col. Pultarium, Pallad. Pultarius, Celf. Col. Calix,Ovid. Ollula,Varr.
units.tr: Olla] Earthen pot, Cat. Jar, Perf. Pot, Cat. Earthen vessel, tr. Ovid. Hor. Potter's pot, Col. Porridge pot, Pallad. Porridge pot, Celf. Col. Cup, Ovid. Little pot, Varr.

units.la: Ollaris] Ollarius, Plin.
units.tr: Ollaris] Pertaining to pots, Plin.

units.la: Ollula] Seriola, Perf. Caliculus, vas fictile, Pallad. Cacabulus, Arnob. Cucumula, Petron.
units.tr: Ollula] Little jar, Perf. Small cup, earthen vessel, Pallad. Small pot, Arnob. Little cup, Petron.

units.la: Olor] Cygnus, Cic. Cycnus, Lambin.
units.tr: Olor] Swan, Cic. Cycnus, Lambin.

units.la: Olorinus] Cygneus, Cic.
units.tr: Olorinus] Of a swan, Cic.

units.la: Olus ] Olusculum, Cic. Lachanon, Hor. Nascentia in horto. In horto sata. Hortensia. Germina hortorum, Plin.
units.tr: Olus] Small herbs, Cic. Herbs, Hor. Things growing in the garden. Sown in the garden. Garden produce. Garden sprouts, Plin.

units.la: Omen bonum] Omen secundum, Hor. Dextrum. Sili. Scæva bona, Plaut. Addicunt aves, Liv. Auspicium bonum, optimum, secundum, Cic. Auspicium solistimum, Fest. Sonivivum, Plin.
units.tr: Omen bonum] Favourable omen, Hor. Propitious omen, Sil. Good omen from the left, Plaut. The birds yield to it, Liv. Good, best, favourable auspice, Cic. Most solemn auspice, Fest. Life-giving omen, Plin.

units.la: Omen malum] Dirum, sinistrum, infaustum, Ovid. Detestabile, Cic. Scæva mala, Fest. Mali ominis obscœnitas, Arnob. Inauspicatum, inauspicatissimum, Plin. Auspicium malum. Obstitum, Cic. Avis sinistra
units.tr: Omen malum] Dire, sinister, unlucky, Ovid. Detestable, Cic. Evil omen from the left, Fest. The foulness of an evil omen, Arnob. Uninauspicious, most inauspicious, Plin. Evil auspice. Ill-omened, Cic. Bird on the left.

units.la: Omen sumere ] Capere omen. Periculum fortunæ facere, Cic. Auspicari alicui rei, Plaut.
units.tr: Omen sumere] To take an omen. To risk one's fortune, Cic. To take auspices for something, Plaut.

units.la: Ominari, vid. Vaticinari.
units.tr: Ominari, see Vaticinari.

units.la: Omittere ] Mittere. Missum facere. Prætermittere occasionem. Præterire. Relinquere. Dimittere fabulas. Transilire rem pulcherrimam, Cic. Intermittere, Ter. Transire quædam in legendo, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Omittere] To send. To let go. To let pass. To pass over an opportunity. To pass by. To leave behind. To drop stories. To skip over a most beautiful matter, Cic. To interrupt, Ter. To pass over certain things in reading, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Omnes] Ad unum omnes. Barbari & Græci. Omnes omnes. Dii hominesque senesque. Vivi mortui. Omnes qui ubique sunt. Cuncti, Cic. Omnes universi, Apul. Quicunque ubique sunt, Plaut. Universi. Pro se quisque. Ad unum, Virg. Nemine excepto.
units.tr: Omnes] All, every one. Barbarians and Greeks. All and sundry. Gods and men, old and young. The living and the dead. All who are anywhere. All together, Cic. All of them together, Apul. Whoever are anywhere, Plaut. All together. Each for himself. To a man, Virg. With no one excepted.

units.la: Omnes loquuntur] In omnium est ore.
units.tr: Omnes loquuntur] It is on everyone's lips.

units.la: Omnia]Omne, Plaut. Omnis res. Universum, Ter. Maxima, minima, omnia. Bona, mala. Digna, indigna. Fanda, infanda. Joca seriaque. Fasque nefasque. Totum & partes. Totum & universum. Initium, medium, finis. Prora & puppis. Sol & sal.
units.tr: Omnia] Everything, Plaut. All things. The whole, Ter. Greatest, least, all things. Good and bad. Worthy and unworthy. Speakable and unspeakable. Jests and earnest. Right and wrong. The whole and the parts. The whole and the universe. Beginning, middle, end. Prow and stern. Sun and salt.

units.la: Omnia tempus habent ] Musica in luctu importuna. Non semper erit æstas, componite nidos. Non semper Saturnalia. Non semper cœlum serenat, nec semper lætus ridet Apollo.
units.tr: Omnia tempus habent] Music is unwelcome in mourning. Summer will not always last, so build your nests. Not every day is a Saturnalia. The sky does not always stay clear, nor does Apollo always smile.

units.la: Omnia sunt fluxa] Oportet omnibus corydalis (alaudis)inesse cristam. Omnia sunt hominum tenui pendentia filo, Ovid. Mors etiam saxis, marmoribusque venit, Auson.
units.tr: Omnia sunt fluxa] Every crested lark must have its crest. All human things hang by a slender thread, Ovid. Death comes even to rocks and marble, Auson.

units.la: Omnia futura incerta] Non omnia eveniunt, quæ in animo statueris. Non ejusdem potestatis initium & finis est. Omne quare habet suum quia] Nunquam sceleri defuit ratio.
units.tr: Omnia futura incerta] Not everything turns out as you have resolved in your mind. The beginning and the end are not in the same power. Omne quare habet suum quia] Every "why" has its "because." Wickedness has never lacked a reason.

units.la: Omnia ablata] Cum ramento, cum pulvisculo, Plaut. Ne bolus quidem relictus. Ne rutis quidem & caesis receptis, vel exceptis, Cic.
units.tr: Omnia ablata] With the shavings, with the dust, Plaut. Not even a scrap left behind. Not even the cut timber taken back or excepted, Cic.

units.la: Omnia simul] Uno fasce completi omnia.
units.tr: Omnia simul] All gathered into one bundle.

units.la: Aut omnia, aut nihil] Aut Caesar, aut nihil. Aut Rex, aut asinus.
units.tr: Aut omnia, aut nihil] Either everything or nothing. Either Caesar or nothing. Either king or donkey.

units.la: Omni conatu ] Cum hasta, cum scuto. Remis atque quadrigis. Omnibus nervis. Omnimodè, omnimodis, Lucr. Omni modo, omnifarium, Firm. Per omnia, Col. Omnibus nervis, unguiculis, opibus. Omni certaminis genere ; omni telorum genere oppugnare. Pugnis & calcibus. Caesim ac punctim. Manibus pedibusque. Omnibus ungulis alicui rei asservire.
units.tr: Omni conatu] With spear and shield. With oars and chariots. With all one's sinews. In every way, Lucr. In every way and every sort, Firm. In every respect, Col. With all sinews, nails and resources. To attack with every kind of fighting and every kind of weapon. With fists and kicks. By cutting and thrusting. With hands and feet. To be devoted to something with all one's claws.

units.la: Omnimodus]Omnimodis, Turneb. Omnigenus, Lucr. Omnis generis, Cic. Omne genus animantium, i. omnis generis. Omnium rerum (generum) missilia, Suet. Omnium ordinum, generum homines, Cic. Omnifarius, Apul. Cujusquemodi, Lucr.
units.tr: Omnimodus] In every way, Turneb. Of every kind, Lucr. Of every sort, Cic. Every kind of living creature, that is, of every sort. Missiles of all things (kinds), Suet. Men of all ranks and kinds, Cic. Of every sort, Apul. Of whatever sort, Lucr.

units.la: Omnino, vid. Necessario, & Penitus.
units.tr: Omnino, see Necessario, and Penitus.

units.la: Omnis, vid. Quisque.
units.tr: Omnis, see Quisque.

units.la: Onerare aliquem] Onus alicui imponere. Onere premere. opprimere, Cic. Peditem super arma ferramentis coonerant, Tac.
units.tr: Onerare aliquem] To lay a burden on someone. To weigh down, to oppress, Cic. They loaded the foot soldiers with iron tools on top of their arms, Tac.

units.la: Onerare navem] Saburra gravare onerariam, Liv. In onerariam navem aliqua conjicere, Cic. Saburrare, Plaut.
units.tr: Onerare navem] To weigh down a transport ship with ballast, Liv. To throw something into a transport ship, Cic. To ballast, Plaut.

units.la: Onerosus, vid. Gravis.
units.tr: Onerosus, see Gravis.

units.la: Onus] Pondus, Virg. Pondusculum, Plaut. Fascis. Animam sub fasce dedere apes, i. sub pondere succi mellei, Virg.
units.tr: Onus] Weight, Virg. Little weight, Plaut. Bundle. The bees gave up their lives under the burden, that is, under the weight of the honeyed juice, Virg.

units.la: Onus impar viribus ] Onus Atho & Aethna gravius, Cic. Pondus vix tractabile, Stat. Injusto sub fasce viam tractat miles Romanus, Virg. Atlas coelum.
units.tr: Onus impar viribus] A load heavier than Athos and Etna, Cic. A weight scarcely manageable, Stat. The Roman soldier drags his way under an unjust load, Virg. Atlas bearing the sky.

units.la: Onustus ] Oneratus recte est, & plus justo vehit, Plaut. Praepeditus latera ferro, Id. Depressus auro, Cic.
units.tr: Onustus] Properly loaded, and carries more than is fair, Plaut. Hampered at the sides with iron, Id. Weighed down with gold, Cic.

units.la: Opacare ] Officere apricanti alicui ; alicujus luminibus. Obstruere luminibus alicujus. Platanus ad opacandum templum patulis diffusa est ramis, Cic. Nocere lumini. Impedire lurelumen, Vlp. Adimere prospectum, Liv. Lucus obumbrat templum, Ovid. Vid. Obumbrare, obscurare.
units.tr: Opacare] To stand in someone's sunlight; to stand in someone's light. To block someone's light. The plane tree is spread with wide branches to shade the temple, Cic. To harm the light. To hinder the light, Ulp. To take away the view, Liv. The grove shades the temple, Ovid. See Obumbrare, obscurare.

units.la: Opacus] Umbrosus locus, Cic. Umbrosissimum folium fico, Plin. Umbrifer, Varr. Virg. Vid. Tenebricosus.
units.tr: Opacus] Shady place, Cic. The fig's most shady leaf, Plin. Shade-bearing, Varr. Virg. See Tenebricosus.

units.la: Opera] Nunquam mihi opus deest, Cic. Tempus officii urget, Varr. Operatio. Officina, Plin. Molimentum, Liv. Opella, Lucr. Operula, Id. Exercitio, Cat. Operositas, Quint.
units.tr: Opera] "I never lack work," Cic. The time of duty presses, Varr. Labour, operation. Workshop, Plin. Effort, Liv. Little work, Lucr. Little task, Id. Exercise, Cat. Industriousness, Quint.

units.la: Operari] Operam dare alicui rei. Operam intra aliquid impendere, Col. Sumere, insumere operam. Studiose in aliquid operam dare. Texere opus. Efficere & navare aliquod opus. Multo labore & sudore aliquid efficere. Fabricari gladium, Cic. Fabricare, fingere aliquid, Ovid. Exercere ferrum, Virg. Plin. Obire rem, Cic. Facessere, Virg. Architectari. Expedire, agere, gerere, explicare, tractare negotium. Administrare. Pertexere orsa. Insistere muneri. Opus magnum in manibus habere. Pergere. Pergere explicare, scribere, &c. Cic. Persequi incepta, Liv. Moliri opus, Id. Urgere aliquid, Hor. Opus facere, efficere, Cic. Ter. Laborare arma, Stat. Facere lanam, (i. carpere, &c.) Luc. Ducere lateres e cretoso solo, Plin. Defingere panem. Deformare areas in horto, Cat.
units.tr: Operari] To take pains over something. To spend effort on something. To spend effort within something, Col. To take on and expend effort. To devote effort eagerly to something. To weave a work. To accomplish and carry through some work. To achieve something by great labour and sweat. To forge a sword, Cic. To fabricate or shape something, Ovid. To work iron, Virg. Plin. To take a matter in hand, Cic. To go about, Virg. To build. To carry out, do, explain, handle or manage a business. To weave the beginnings through to the end. To apply oneself to a duty. To have a great work in hand. To proceed. To go on explaining, writing, and so on, Cic. To pursue undertakings, Liv. To strive at a work, Id. To press on with something, Hor. To do or effect a work, Cic. Ter. To labour at arms, Stat. To make wool (that is, to card it, and so on), Luc. To draw bricks from chalky soil, Plin. To knead bread. To lay out flower beds in a garden, Cat.

units.la: Operarius] Factor, qui vinum vel oleum facit, Cat. Opera: accedes opera agro, Hor. Pall. Operator, Firm. Cui opera vita erat, Ter. Qui in operis est alicujus, Cic. Fabriles operas praebendo vitam tenebat, Apul.
units.tr: Operarius] Workman, one who makes wine or oil, Cat. Worker: you will add labour to the field, Hor. Pall. Labourer, Firm. One whose life was his labour, Ter. One who is in someone's employ, Cic. By offering his craft he kept himself alive, Apul.

units.la: Operculum] Tectorium vasorum, Cat. Cooperculum capuli, Apul. Claxendix, Plaut. Testus, us, Cat. Cortina, Virg.
units.tr: Operculum] Lid of vessels, Cat. Cover of a hilt, Apul. Lid, Plaut. Cover, Cat. Cover, Virg.

units.la: Operire, vid. Tegere.
units.tr: Operire, see Tegere.

units.la: Operose, vid. Laboriose
units.tr: Operose, see Laboriose.

units.la: Operosus, vid. Laboriosus.
units.tr: Operosus, see Laboriosus.

units.la: Operte] Tecte, Cic. Vid. Clam.
units.tr: Operte] Covertly, Cic. See Clam.

units.la: Opertus] Tectus, Ovid. Intectus, Liv. Operculati favi, Col.
units.tr: Opertus] Covered, Ovid. Uncovered, Liv. Honeycombs with lids, Col.

units.la: Opes, vid. Facultates.
units.tr: Opes, see Facultates.

units.la: Opes iniquae] Dives aut iniquus est, aut iniqui heres.
units.tr: Opes iniquae] The rich man is either unjust, or the heir of an unjust man.

units.la: Opes cura parantur] Vigilet oportet, qui cupit ditescere. Vigilare necesse est eum, qui rem cupit facere, Vigilet necessum est, qui velit dives evadere, Erasm.
units.tr: Opes cura parantur] One who wishes to grow rich must keep watch. The man who wishes to make his fortune must necessarily be watchful. He who wishes to become rich must keep vigil, Erasm.

units.la: Opes æstimare præ sapientiâ] Gutta fortunæ præ dolio sapientiæ.
units.tr: Opes aestimare prae sapientia] A drop of fortune against a cask of wisdom.

units.la: Opifex] Homo operarius. Humili arte præditus, Cic. Sedentarius, Plaut. Sellularius, Liv. Professionis ultimæ homines, Lampr.
units.tr: Opifex] A working man. Endowed with a humble craft, Cic. Sedentary, Plaut. Workshop man, Liv. Men of the lowest trades, Lampr.

units.la: Opificium] Opificina,Plaut. Artificium opificis. Ars humilis, sordida opificum. Illiberalis labor. Pictura & fabrica cæteræque artes, Cic. Ars mechanica, Firm. Sedentaria opera, Col.
units.tr: Opificium] Workshop, Plaut. The craft of a craftsman. The humble, base craft of workmen. Ignoble labour. Painting, building and the other arts, Cic. Mechanical art, Firm. Sedentary work, Col.

units.la: Opilio] Upilio, Virg. Ovilio, Iabol.IC.
units.tr: Opilio] Shepherd, Virg. Shepherd, Iabol. IC.

units.la: Opimè, vid. Effuse, Copiosè.
units.tr: Opime, see Effuse, Copiose.

units.la: Opimitas, vid. Copia.
units.tr: Opimitas, see Copia.

units.la: Opimus, vid. Pinguis.
units.tr: Opimus, see Pinguis.

units.la: Opinamentum] Anicularum deliramentum. Idolum,Cic. Vanæ finguntur species, velut ægri somnia,Hor. Quæcunque in somno videntur.
units.tr: Opinamentum] The raving of old women. An idol, Cic. Vain shapes are fashioned, like the dreams of the sick, Hor. Whatever things are seen in sleep.

units.la: Opinari] Opinione duci. Mea fert opinio. In eam opinionem veni. Autumare, arbitrari, putare. Deputare. Videor mihi perspexisse aliquid, Cic. Sedit quorundam opinioni aliquid,Amm. Censere. Credere,Ter. Videtur mihi ita, Plaut. Cic. Existimatio communis est, Liv. Reputare. Persuasum habere. Persuasum mihi est. Persuadere sibi. Sentire. Sic statuo & judico. Judicium meum est. Opinio est. Hanc teneo sententiam, Cic. Reri, Salust.
units.tr: Opinari] To be led by opinion. My opinion is. I have come to this opinion. To suppose, to judge, to reckon. To deem. I seem to myself to have perceived something, Cic. Something has settled into the opinion of some people, Amm. To be of the view. To believe, Ter. It seems so to me, Plaut. Cic. The common view is, Liv. To consider. To hold as persuaded. I am persuaded. To persuade oneself. To feel. Thus I decide and judge. My judgement is. It is an opinion. I hold this view, Cic. To think, Sall.

units.la: Opinio] Opinatio. Existimatio. Sententia. Sensus unum bonorum omnium, Cic. Opinatus, Lucr. Persuasio de se inanis,Quint. Arbitratus, Circ. Arbitrium, Suet.
units.tr: Opinio] Supposition, estimation, judgement, view. The one feeling of all good men, Cic. Supposition, Lucr. Empty self-persuasion, Quint. Judgement, Circ. Decision, Suet.

units.la: Opinio falsa] Non respondet opinioni calculus. Sacer morbus.
units.tr: Opinio falsa] The reckoning does not agree with the opinion. A sacred disease.

units.la: Opinio arrogans] Præsumpta opinio ; persuasio.
units.tr: Opinio arrogans] A presumed opinion; a conviction.

units.la: Nulla opinio perennat] Opinionum commenta delet dies, Cic.
units.tr: Nulla opinio perennat] Time erases the inventions of opinions, Cic.

units.la: Opinionem suam probare, allegato classico Auctore] Tibicine honorato fulcire sententiam suam.
units.tr: Opinionem suam probare, allegato classico Auctore] To prop up one's view with an honoured flute-player.

units.la: Opiniosus] Opiniosissimus. Opinator, Cic. Imaginosus. Imaginosum morbum patiens, Catul. Sen. Neque mores vult mutare suos, nec alienos ferre potest, Tac.
units.tr: Opiniosus] Most opinionated. A conjecturer, Cic. Fanciful. Suffering from a fanciful sickness, Catul. Sen. He wants neither to change his own ways nor can he bear those of others, Tac.

units.la: Opiparè] Recte & dapsile convivari, Suet. Dapatice acceptus, Fest. Epulari Persice. Persici apparatus, Cic. Nitidiuscule, Plaut. Prolixè, prolixius aliquem accipere, Ter. Soluto sinu, Sen. Genialiter agere festum, Ovid. Opimè & opipare instructa domus, Plaut. Pleno modio, Cic. Liberaliter. Laute diversari, Id. Magnificè & splendide ornare convivium, Id. Pascue, Apul.
units.tr: Sumptuously] To feast well and generously, Suet. Welcomed with a lavish feast, Fest. To feast in the Persian manner. A Persian style of furnishing, Cic. Elegantly, Plaut. Lavishly; to receive someone more lavishly, Ter. With loose folds (of the toga), Sen. To celebrate a festival with festive cheer, Ovid. A house richly and sumptuously furnished, Plaut. With a full measure, Cic. Generously. To lodge in splendour, Id. To adorn a banquet magnificently and splendidly, Id. Abundantly, Apul.

units.la: Opiparus ] Magnifica & lauta coena; sumptuosa, Cic. Cerealis, Plaut. Dapalis, Titin. Varr. Persici apparatus, Hor. Dapsilis, Plaut. Dapatilis; omnia dapatilia comesse, Varr, Dapaticus, Fest. Rectus apparatus, Sen. Prælautus. Liberales epulæ, Suet. Opulentum prandium, Plaut. Opiparis piscatus, Apul.
units.tr: Sumptuous ] A magnificent and lavish dinner; costly, Cic. Of grain (a meal of bread), Plaut. Of a feast, Titin. Varr. A Persian display, Hor. Bountiful, Plaut. Of a feast, Plaut. To eat all the feast-dishes, Varr. A proper display, Sen. Very elegant. Generous banquets, Suet. A rich lunch, Plaut. A sumptuous catch of fish, Apul.

units.la: Opitulari] Suppetias ferre, Plaut. Opem, Cic. Manu utraque adesse. Vid. Iuvare.
units.tr: To help] To bring aid, Plaut. To give help, Cic. To be present with both hands. See To help.

units.la: Opitulator inspearatus] Homo homini Deus.
units.tr: A helper who is unskilled] Man is a god to man.

units.la: Oportet, vid. Necesse est. Opus est.
units.tr: It behoves, see It is necessary. It is needed.

units.la: Opperiri aliquem] Exspectare aliquem. Præstolor tibi, alicui spei, Cic. Manere, Abs. Ter. Plaut. Demorari aliquem, Virg. Exspectatio me tenet. Suspensus exspectatione rerum novarum, Cic. Vid. Exspectare.
units.tr: To wait for someone] To expect someone. I await you, a hope for someone, Cic. To remain, Terence, Plautus. To detain someone, Virg. Expectation holds me. Held in suspense by the expectation of new events, Cic. See To expect.

units.la: Oppidum ] Oppidulum, Cic. Civitatula, Sen. Mandra, Mar. Rader.
units.tr: Town] A small town, Cic. A little state, Sen. A hamlet, Mar. Rader.

units.la: Oppignorare]Pignerare unionem ad expensas itineris, Suet. Oppignerare libellos pro vino, Cic. Obligare ædem ob amoris prandium, Plin. Obligare, dare aliquid pignori, Vlp. Opponere pignori. Arrhaboni aliquid relinquere, Ter. Pro pignore tradere salutem, Cic. Opponere, Absol. Iuv. Catul.
units.tr: To pledge] To pledge a pearl to cover the costs of a journey, Suet. To pledge books for wine, Cic. To mortgage a temple for the cost of a dinner of love, Plin. To bind, to give something as a pledge, Ulpian. To set something as a pledge. To leave something as earnest money, Ter. To surrender one's safety as a pledge, Cic. To offer, absolutely; Juv., Catul.

units.la: Opponere, vid. Obsistere.
units.tr: To oppose, see To resist.

units.la: Opportune] Ad diem, Tempore, In tempore, Per tempus advenire. In ipso articulo temporis. Commodè. Ad tempus. Maximis temporibus præsto esse. Suo tempore. Ad constitutum diem. Summo tempore. Percommodè. Non incommode. Peropportune, Cic. Opportunitate advenire. Tempori, Plaut. Attemperate venit. Commodum, Ter. Ex usu temporis, Tac.
units.tr: Opportunely] On the day; at the right time; in good time; to arrive in due time. At the very moment. Suitably. At the appointed time. To be present at the most opportune times. In its own time. On the appointed day. At the very last moment. Very conveniently. Not inconveniently. Most opportunely, Cic. To arrive opportunely. To suit the time, Plaut. He came at the right moment. Conveniently, Ter. According to the advantage of the time, Tac.

units.la: Opportunitas]Occasio. Tempus commodū: Tempus actionis nis opportunum. Tempestas idonea. Opportunitas tem-poris: idonea. Tempestivitas, Cic. Congruum tempus, Claud. Temporum momentum: temporum momenta captare, Liv. De cœlo servare, Cic. Opportunitatem ad aliquid habere, Id. Occasio oblata, est, venit, parta est, Plaut. Cardo, Virg.
units.tr: Opportunity] Occasion. A convenient time; a time fit for acting. A suitable season. A fit time: suitable. Timeliness, Cic. A fitting time, Claud. The moment of events: to seize the moments of events, Liv. To watch the sky (for omens), Cic. To have an opportunity for something, Id. An occasion has been offered, has come, has been won, Plaut. The hinge, Virg.

units.la: Opportunus] Opportunissima ætas. Tempestiva maturitas, Cic. Peropportuna victoria, Liv. Commodus, Ter.
units.tr: Opportune] A most opportune age. Timely maturity, Cic. A most opportune victory, Liv. Convenient, Ter.

units.la: Oppositio, vid. Contrarietas.
units.tr: Opposition, see Contrariety.

units.la: Oppositus] E contraria parte: è regione nobis sunt, Adversis stant vestigiis contra nostra Antipodes. Respondet. Adversum solem intueri, Cic. Respondet contrà, Virg. Contrapositus, Quint. Ex adverso situs, Ter. Contrarius ictus. Liv.
units.tr: Opposite] On the opposite side: they are across from us; the Antipodes stand with feet opposed to ours. He answers. To look at the sun face to face, Cic. He answers in reply, Virg. Set against, Quint. Situated opposite, Ter. A blow from the opposite side, Liv.

units.la: Oppressio] Summæ angustæ. Angustia rei familiaris, Cic.
units.tr: Oppression] Great straits. Straitened circumstances of one's household, Cic.

units.la: Oppressor] Vindex conjurationis, Cic.
units.tr: Oppressor] The avenger of a conspiracy, Cic.

units.la: Opprimere] Præmere famam alicujus, Tac. Deprimere fortunam alicujus. Comprimere scriptum, ne emanet. Obruere nomen alicujus, Cic. Supprimere famam rei, Liv. Pessundare, Plaut.
units.tr: To oppress] To press down someone's reputation, Tac. To lower someone's fortune. To suppress a writing so that it does not get out. To bury someone's name, Cic. To suppress the report of a matter, Liv. To ruin utterly, Plaut.

units.la: Opprobrare, vid, Exprobrare.
units.tr: To reproach, see To upbraid.

units.la: Opprobrium, vid. Contumelia.
units.tr: Reproach, see Insult.

units.la: Oppugnare urbem] Arietare in portas, Virg. Admovere machinas, Cic. Machinamenta & scalas promovere, Tac. Admœnire fabricas. Impugnare: Aggredi urbem, Plaut. Adpugnare, Tac. Invadere urbem, Virg.
units.tr: To attack a city] To batter against the gates, Virg. To bring up siege engines, Cic. To advance engines and scaling ladders, Tac. To set up siege works. To assault: to attack a city, Plaut. To assault, Tac. To invade a city, Virg.

units.la: Oppugnatio] Impugnatio urbis. Impetus, Cic.
units.tr: Assault] An assault on a city. An attack, Cic.

units.la: Oppugnator] Obsessor curiæ, Cic. Aquarum, Ovid.
units.tr: Assailant] A besieger of the senate-house, Cic. Of waters, Ovid.

units.la: Optabilis, vid. Desiderabilis.
units.tr: Desirable, see Desirable.

units.la: Optare] Exoptare alicui exitium. Precari salutem. Volo aliquid valdè tuâ causa. Ego illi omnia malo, Cic. Vovere. Expetissere. Jubeo te salvere. Volo vobis, quæ vultis, Plaut.
units.tr: To wish] To wish someone ruin with all one's heart. To pray for someone's safety. I want something very much for your sake. I prefer everything for him, Cic. To vow. To long for. I bid you farewell. I want for you what you want, Plaut.

units.la: Quod optamus, facilè speramus] Amantes sibi somnia fingunt.
units.tr: What we wish for, we easily hope for] Lovers fashion dreams for themselves.

units.la: Optata non semper eveniunt] Optimè cogitatum surripitur sæpissimè, Plaut.
units.tr: Wished-for things do not always come to pass] A well-laid plan is very often snatched away, Plaut.

units.la: Optatò] Peroptato datum est. Cum desiderio. Optabiliter, Cic.
units.tr: Wishfully] Granted most gladly. With longing. Desirably, Cic.

units.la: Optimates, vid. Magnates.
units.tr: Optimates, see Magnates.

units.la: Optimè accuratißimè] Oppidò quam benè, Gell. Optimè si unquam ; si quidquam. Dici vix potest, quàm præclare. Archimedes non posset melius describere. Vid. Benè.
units.tr: Very well, most accurately] Quite well indeed, Gell. Very well, if ever, if at all. It can hardly be said how excellently. Archimedes could not describe it better. See Well.

units.la: Optimum quid] Mellis medulla.
units.tr: The best of something] The marrow of honey.

units.la: Optimus] Meliorem neque tu reperies, neque sol vidit, Cic. Omnibus judicibus vincit.
units.tr: Best] You will find no better, nor has the sun seen one, Cic. He conquers with all the judges.

units.la: Optio, vid. Electio.
units.tr: Option, see Choice.

units.la: Optionem alicui dare] Optionem alicui deferre, facere, permittere. Facere potestatem eligendi, deligendi: ut eligat. Permittere ut eligat de tribus quem velit. Dare optionem eligendi. Optio tibi datur. Optio tua est, Cic.
units.tr: To give someone an option] To offer, make or grant an option to someone. To make it possible to choose, to select, so that he may choose. To permit him to choose whom he wishes from three. To give the option of choosing. The option is given to you. The choice is yours, Cic.

units.la: Opulenter] Opulentius, Liv. Opulentè ornata domus, Apul.
units.tr: Richly] More richly, Liv. A house richly adorned, Apul.

units.la: Opulentia] Rei pecuniariæ copia. Vid. Divitiæ, &c.
units.tr: Wealth] An abundance of money. See Riches, etc.

units.la: Opus] Opera. Opusculum. Labores. Manus, (pro opere) Cic.
units.tr: Work] Labour. A little work. Toil. Hands (for work), Cic.

units.la: Opus laudat artificem] Pictor tabellis commendat editis.
units.tr: The work praises the craftsman] A painter commends himself by the pictures he has put forward.

units.la: Operi quærendus est operarius] Navi nauclerus quærendusest.
units.tr: For the work the workman must be sought] For a ship a pilot must be sought.

units.la: Operis adjutores multi] Manus multæ opus levius reddunt.
units.tr: Many are the helpers in the work] Many hands make the work lighter.

units.la: Operis finis] Extrema linea.
units.tr: The end of the work] The final line.

units.la: Opus est aliquo, vel aliquid] Opus est facto. Opus est illo convento, Plaut. Opus est fieri. Dux opus est, Cic. Opus est lectionis, Quint. Opus est ut, Plaut. Opus est illam rem, Non. Vestimenta ei opus sunt, Varr. Peropus est, Ter. Usus est, Cic. Nunc viribus usus, Virg. Usus indiget horum, Id. Usus est hominem ad eam rem, Plaut. Agitandum est vigilias, Id. Omnes artes repudiandum est, Varr. Ad naturam videmus pauca opus esse, Lucr. Oportet pascere oves, Virg.
units.tr: There is need of someone or something] There is need of a deed. There is need of that gathering, Plaut. There is need to be done. There is need of a leader, Cic. There is need of reading, Quint. There is need that, Plaut. There is need of that matter, Non. He has need of clothes, Varr. There is great need, Ter. There is use for it, Cic. Now he has used his strength, Virg. Use has need of these things, Id. There is use for a man for that purpose, Plaut. One must keep watch, Id. All arts must be rejected, Varr. We see that few things are needed for nature, Lucr. One must pasture the sheep, Virg.

units.la: Opus habere, indigere] Necesse habeo scribere. Hæc longam desiderant orationem. Postulat ratio, necessitas, &c. Flagitat à me necessitas, tempus, &c. Cic. Poscit res, causa locus aliquid, Plin. Poscit usus, Cæs. Requirere. Virtus nullam requirit voluptatem, Cic. Vid. Egere.
units.tr: To have need of, to lack] I am under the necessity of writing. These matters require a long discourse. Reason, necessity, etc., demand it. Necessity, time, etc., press upon me, Cic. The thing, the cause, the place demands something, Plin. Use demands it, Caes. To require. Virtue requires no pleasure, Cic. See To lack.

units.la: Ora] Extremitas mundi, regionis. Regio vineæ, Cic Margo terrarum, Ovid.
units.tr: Edges] The extremity of the world or of a region. The region of a vineyard, Cic. The border of lands, Ovid.

units.la: Oraculum] Oracula vatum. Fatum Sibyllæ. Vaticinium. Responsum. Effatum, Cic. Effata vatum, Amm. Dictio data fuit, caveret Acherufiam aquam, Liv.
units.tr: Oracle] The oracles of seers. The fate of the Sibyl. A prophecy. An answer. A pronouncement, Cic. The sayings of seers, Amm. A reply was given that he should beware of the Acherusian water, Liv.

units.la: Orare Deum ] Precari Deos, Cic. Ad Deos, Liv. Adora-re superos prece, Ovid. Comprecari Deos, Ter. Exposcere precibus & votis pacem Deum, Deos Deasqne implorare & obtestari, Cic. Exposcere aliquid Deos. Facere precationes, Liv. Petere voto, Plin. Iun. Quærere prece divos, Lucr. Præfari divos, Virg. Supplicare, Abf.Plin. Vid. Obsecrare.
units.tr: To pray to God] To entreat the gods, Cic. To the gods, Liv. To entreat the gods above with prayer, Ovid. To join in praying to the gods, Ter. To ask for peace from God with prayers and vows, to implore and beseech the gods and goddesses, Cic. To ask the gods for something. To make supplications, Liv. To seek by vow, Plin. Iun. To seek the gods by prayer, Lucr. To address the gods, Virg. To supplicate, Plin. See To beseech.

units.la: Ora & labora ] Admotâ manu Deum invoca. Cum Minerva manum move. Industriam adjuvat Deus.
units.tr: Pray and work] Call upon God with your hand applied. Move your hand with Minerva's help. God helps the diligent.

units.la: Orare (2) sermonem præmeditatum habere ] Agere orationem. Orationem ad populum habere. Quint. Orationem dicere, recitare. Perorare causam. Dicere ad, apud judices. Agere ad populum, Cic. Agere causam apud aliquem, Plin.
units.tr: To pray (2), to have a prepared speech] To deliver a speech. To give an oration to the people, Quint. To deliver and recite a speech. To plead a case to the end. To speak before judges. To speak to the people, Cic. To plead a case before someone, Plin.

units.la: Oratio prosa] Oratio soluta, libera. Dictio oratoria, Cic. Prosa facundia, opposita versæ, Apul. Numeris fertur lege solutis, Hor. Oratoris facultas. Pedestre eloquium, Trebell. Prosaica oratio, Plin. Versuum nexu repudiato. Passa verba. Solutus loquutus, Apul.
units.tr: Prose oration] Unbound, free speech. Oratorical diction, Cic. Prose eloquence, opposed to verse, Apul. Carried along by unbound measures, Hor. The skill of the orator. Plain-footed eloquence, Trebell. Prosaic speech, Plin. Having rejected the bond of verse. Unmetrical words. Loose speech, Apul.

units.la: Oratio superba ] Phalerata dicta. Ampullas projiciunt & sesquipedalia verba, Hor.
units.tr: Pompous oration] Ornamented expressions. They throw out bombast and words a foot and a half long, Hor.

units.la: Oratio jejuna] Orationis inopia, siccitas, salebræ.
units.tr: Dry speech] Poverty of speech, dryness, roughness.

units.la: Oratio egenum non juvat] Re opitulandum, non verbis. Venter caret auribus. Qui dare vult aliis, non debet dicere vultis. Sed dicat plane dulcis amice tene.
units.tr: Speech does not help the needy] One must help with deeds, not words. The belly has no ears. He who wishes to give to others should not say, "Be warm and fed." But let him say plainly, "Dear friend, hold on."

units.la: Oratio non coharens] Scopæ dissolutæ.
units.tr: Speech not cohering] A loose broom.

units.la: Orator] Artifex, opifex dicendi, Cic. Opifex persuadendi, Quint. Declamandi magister. Vir in eloquentia præcipuus. Rhetoricoteros, Cic.
units.tr: Orator] A craftsman, a maker of speech, Cic. A maker of persuasion, Quint. A master of declamation. A man outstanding in eloquence. More rhetorical, Cic.

units.la: Orator eximius] Cicerones, Hortensii, Demosthenes ævo nostro ubi sunt ? Sirenibus ad persuadendum aptis, Er.
units.tr: Outstanding orator] Where are the Ciceros, the Hortensii, the Demosthenes of our age? Sirens fit for persuading, Erasmus.

units.la: Oratoria, vid. Eloquentia.
units.tr: Oratory, see Eloquence.

units.la: Orbare aliquem aliquâ re] Privare aliquem dolore, vitâ. Eximere aliquid alicui quod eum angat, Cic. Eximere curam alicui, Plaut. Exuere patrimonio aliquem, Suet. Fraudare aliquem voluptate, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: To bereave someone of something] To deprive someone of grief or of life. To take away from someone what troubles him, Cic. To relieve someone of care, Plaut. To strip someone of his inheritance, Suet. To cheat someone of pleasure, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Orbatio ] Orbitas. Privatio Spoliatio omnium rerum, Cic. Viduitas auxilii, omnium auxiliorum, Plaut.
units.tr: Bereavement] Orphanhood. Deprivation, the stripping of all things, Cic. Widowhood of help, of all aid, Plaut.

units.la: Orbis, vid. Mundus, Circulus.
units.tr: Orb, see World, Circle.

units.la: Orbus aliqua re] Expeculiatus, Plaut. Viduatus aliqua re, Lucr. Viduus pharetrâ Apollo. Hor. Nudatus, Cic. Privatus: Cui quid ademptum est, Fest.
units.tr: Bereft of something] Stripped of property, Plaut. Deprived of something, Lucr. Apollo, widowed of his quiver, Hor. Stripped, Cic. Deprived: one from whom something has been taken away, Festus.

units.la: Orcinus. Orcus, vid. Infernalis, &c.
units.tr: Infernal. Hell, see Infernal, etc.

units.la: Ordinare] In ordinem reponere, Col. Collocare ex ordine. Redigere in ordinem. Digerere. Dispensare, Cic. Suo quidque loco reponere. Disponere quidque suo ordine, Col. Ponere ordine vites, Virg. Concenturiare in corde sycophantias, Plaut. Instruere copias, Caes.
units.tr: To arrange] To put into order, Col. To place in order. To bring into order. To arrange. To distribute, Cic. To put each thing in its own place. To set each thing in its proper order, Col. To place the vines in order, Virg. To plot sycophantic schemes in the heart, Plaut. To draw up troops, Caes.

units.la: Ordinarie, vid. Vulgo.
units.tr: Ordinarily, see Commonly.

units.la: Ordinarius, vid. Vsitatus.
units.tr: Ordinary, see Usual.

units.la: Ordinate, vid. Ordine.
units.tr: Orderly, see In order.

units.la: Ordinatus] Ordinatior pars mundi, Sen. Ordinatissimus stellarum meatus, Apul. Ordinaria semina, quae ordinem suum obtinent, Col. Disposita vita hominis, Plin. Instructus, Vlp.
units.tr: Ordinatus] A more orderly part of the world, Sen. The most orderly course of the stars, Apul. Ordinary seeds, which keep their proper order, Col. A man's life arranged, Plin. Equipped, Vlp.

units.la: Ordo] Series artis, Cic. Ordinatio vitae, Col. Tenor dierum, Virg.
units.tr: Ordo] The sequence of an art, Cic. The arrangement of life, Col. The course of the days, Virg.

units.la: Ordo servandus] Bos currum trahit, non bovem currus. Tribulis factus serva ordinem.
units.tr: Ordo servandus] The ox draws the cart, not the cart the ox. Having become a tribesman, keep the order.

units.la: Ordinem servare] Recte atque ordine facere omnia. Ordine administrare. Referre se ad ordinem, Cic. Sequi ordinem vitae, Plin.
units.tr: Ordinem servare] To do everything rightly and in order. To administer in order. To return oneself to order, Cic. To follow the order of life, Plin.

units.la: Ordine] Ex ordine dicere. Ordinatim, Cic. Per ordinem, Quint. Ordinate, ad Heren. Ordinatius, Apul. Dispositè aliquem accusare. Via ac ratione procedit oratio, Cic. Consequenter. Regulariter, Vlp.
units.tr: Ordine] To speak in order. Methodically, Cic. In sequence, Quint. Orderly, ad Heren. More orderly, Apul. To accuse someone in an orderly way. The speech proceeds by method and reason, Cic. Consequently. Regularly, Vlp.

units.la: Ordine se res insequuntur] Alpha sequitur beta. Viam qui nescit ad mare, fluvium sequatur.
units.tr: Ordine se res insequuntur] Alpha follows beta. Let him who does not know the way to the sea follow the river.

units.la: Ordiri, vid. Incipere.
units.tr: Ordiri, see To begin.

units.la: Oretenus. Barb.] Coram inter nos conferemus. Coram ex ipso audiebamus. Sed haec coram, Cic.
units.tr: Oretenus. Barb.] We will confer face to face between ourselves. We heard it face to face from himself. But these things face to face, Cic.

units.la: Orexis, vid. Appetitus, & Bulimia.
units.tr: Orexis, see Appetite, and Bulimia.

units.la: Organa] Organa Musica, Quint. Spiritalis machina, Vitr. Organum pneusticum, Ios. Scal. Armamenta cantus, Plin.
units.tr: Organs] Musical organs, Quint. A spiritual machine, Vitr. A pneumatic organ, Ios. Scal. Instruments of song, Plin.

units.la: Organarius] Organicus, Lucr. Psaltes, Iun.
units.tr: Organist] Organic, Lucr. A harp-player, Iun.

units.la: Orichalcum] Æs coronarium, Plin.
units.tr: Orichalcum] Crown-bronze, Plin.

units.la: Oriens ] Orientis solis partes. Orientis oræ. Exoriens. Exortus,Cic. Ortus. Subortus, Lucr. Solifera plaga cœli, Sen. Plaga eoa.
units.tr: Orient] The parts of the rising sun. The shores of the east. Rising. Risen, Cic. Rising, origin. Rising up, Lucr. The sun-bearing region of the sky, Sen. The eastern quarter.

units.la: Orientalis ] Ortivus sol, Apul. Ortivus cardo, Manil. Exortivus Oceanus, Plin. Eous orbis, Ovid.
units.tr: Oriental] The rising sun, Apul. The rising hinge, Manil. The eastern ocean, Plin. The eastern world, Ovid.

units.la: Orificium] Ostium fluminis,Cic. Os vasculi,Quint. Fauces amphoræ, Col. Caput fluminis,Caf.
units.tr: Orifice] The mouth of a river, Cic. The mouth of a vessel, Quint. The throat of a jar, Col. The head of a river, Caf.

units.la: Origo ] Orsus. Primordia rerum. Incunabula virtutis. Radix. Prima adolescentia. Fons. Semen, Cic. Avaritia metropolis malitiæ, Bion. Cubilia avaritiæ. Cunabula gentis, Virg. Summus puteus, Plaut.
units.tr: Origin] A beginning. The first beginnings of things. The cradle of virtue. Root. Early youth. Source. Seed, Cic. Avarice, the mother-city of wickedness, Bion. The dens of avarice. The cradle of a nation, Virg. The deepest well, Plaut.

units.la: Origo alicujus mali] Hinc belli initium.
units.tr: The origin of some evil] Hence the beginning of the war.

units.la: Origo omnium eadem] Idem omnia pulvis. Omnis sanguis concolor, virtus nos separat.
units.tr: The origin of all is the same] All things are the same dust. All blood is of one colour; virtue alone separates us.

units.la: Orion] Jugula, vel, Jugulæ, Plaut.
units.tr: Orion] Jugula, or, Jugulae, Plaut.

units.la: Oriri] Exoritur stella, Plin. Surgit luna, Tac. Oboritur lux. Emergunt stellæ, Cic. Redeunt soles, Catul.
units.tr: To arise] A star rises, Plin. The moon rises, Tac. Light rises up. The stars emerge, Cic. The suns return, Catul.

units.la: Oriundus] Natio Macedo,Plin. Ortu Tusculanus. Oriundus ab ingenuis, Genere Andria, Ter. Oriundus liberis parentibus, Col. Turnus ab Africa, id est, Africanus, Liv.
units.tr: Descended] A Macedonian nation, Plin. Of Tusculan birth. Descended from freeborn parents, of Andros by race, Ter. Descended from free parents, Col. Turnus from Africa, that is, an African, Liv.

units.la: Oritur ] Incipit ver, febris,Cic. Cooritur pestilentia, Liv. Committitur bellum, Non. Exoritur clamor. Præluditur vitæ meliori, Sen. Cœptus est, Cic. Incipitur, Liv. Optimè incipitur à longis, Quint. Recipit res, Lucr.
units.tr: It arises] Spring, fever begins, Cic. Plague breaks out together, Liv. War is entered upon, Non. A shout arises. A prelude is given to a better life, Sen. It was begun, Cic. It is begun, Liv. It is best begun with long syllables, Quint. The matter takes hold, Lucr.

units.la: Ornamentum] Ornatus verborum. Instructus orationis. natio, Cic. Color. Venus, Quint. Pigmenta. Flosculi, Lecythi. Venustas. Lepos, nitor, gratia, lenocinium, emblemata, myrothecia, fuci, phaleræ, dignitas, cultus, polities, Eraf. Vid. Decor.
units.tr: Ornament] Ornament of words. Equipment of speech. Adornment, Cic. Colour. Charm, Quint. Paints. Little flowers, little oil-flasks. Loveliness. Charm, brilliance, grace, allurement, emblems, perfume-boxes, cosmetics, trappings, dignity, refinement, polish, Erasmus. See Decor.

units.la: Ornare] Exornare. Ornare & vestire res inventas. Domino domus honestanda est. Cohonestare. Illuminare, pingere verbis. Colorare, Adornare. Ornamentis afficere. Ornatum afferre. Ornatu ornare. Honori esse. Decorare patriam spoliis, Cic. Condecorare. Investire. Mangonizata villa, Plin. Perornare, Tac. Ornamento esse alicui. Mactare aliquem honoribus. Ornamenta congere-re.Cic. Colere aliquid,Ovid. Recolere antiquum decus,Tac. Illustrare nomen alicujus: laudibus aliquem,Cic. Comere, expolire, perpolire, venustare, picturare, Er.
units.tr: To adorn] To adorn thoroughly. To adorn and clothe found things. A master's house ought to be graced. To lend honour. To illuminate, to paint with words. To colour, to decorate. To furnish with ornaments. To bring adornment. To adorn with finery. To be an honour. To decorate the fatherland with spoils, Cic. To deck out completely. To invest. A villa dressed up for sale, Plin. To adorn thoroughly, Tac. To be an ornament to someone. To load someone with honours. To gather together ornaments, Cic. To cultivate something, Ovid. To revive ancient glory, Tac. To illustrate someone's name: to honour someone with praises, Cic. To comb, polish, perpolish, beautify, paint, Er.

units.la: Ornate] Decore, polite, splendide, luculente. Concinne, composite, rotunde dicere, Cicer. Non inornate dicere, ad Her.
units.tr: Ornately] Becomingly, polished, splendidly, brilliantly. To speak neatly, composedly, smoothly, Cicer. To speak not unadorned, ad Her.

units.la: Ornatus vestitu] Graphicus, pergraphicus. Graphice exornatus, Plaut. Luxuriosus corporis cultus, Quint. Vestitu est ad munditiem curioso. Elaboratus ad speciem incedit, Macrob. Pulchre indusiatus adolescens, Apul. Paludatus, Claud. Pavo, Adag. Atheniensis. Unde hic nobis Pavo?
units.tr: Ornately dressed] Graphic, very graphic. Graphically adorned, Plaut. Luxurious care of the body, Quint. He is fastidious about neatness in his dress. He walks about elaborately dressed for show, Macrob. A youth beautifully dressed in an undergarment, Apul. Dressed in a general's cloak, Claud. A peacock, Adag. Athenian. Where has this peacock come to us from?

units.la: Orphanus ] Orbus, abs. Quint. Orbus filius patre, Cicer. (Orbus pater, vid. est sine liberis, Cic.) Nudus a propinquis, Id.
units.tr: Orphan] Bereft, absolutely, Quint. A son bereft of his father, Cicer. (A bereft father, see is without children, Cic.) Stripped of kin, Id.

units.la: Ortus solis] Exortus, Plin. Emersus Caniculae, Col. Coortus solis. Subortus stellarum, Lucr.
units.tr: Rising of the sun] Rising, Plin. The rising of the Dog Star, Col. The rising together of the sun. The rising of the stars, Lucr.

units.la: Ortus prodit futurae rei incrementa] Urit mature, quod vult urtica manere. Protinus apparet planta futura ferax.
units.tr: The beginning reveals the growth of a future thing] The nettle stings early what it wishes to last. At once the plant that will be fruitful appears.

units.la: Os] Ora, Ovid. Os aliis animantibus ad inferendum ventri copias comparatum; sed homini Promptuarium potius rectae rationis, & suavissimae orationis datum est,Apul.
units.tr: Mouth] Mouth, Ovid. The mouth was given to other living creatures as a means of bringing supplies to the belly; but to man has been given rather a storehouse of right reason and most sweet speech, Apul.

units.la: Os, ossa] Ossei lapides, Plin. Testa, Cels. Ossum, Ter.
units.tr: Bone, bones] Bony stones, Plin. A shell, Cels. Bone, Ter.

units.la: Oscitans ] Oscitabundus. Oscitator, Henr. Steph. Qui vitio oscedinis tenetur,Gell. Scordalus,Sen. interpr. Bisciol. qui vocat Pandiculatorem.
units.tr: Yawning] Yawning. A yawner, Henr. Steph. One who is held by the vice of yawning, Gell. Scordalus, Sen., interpreter Bisciol, who calls him a stretcher.

units.la: Oscitare] Pandiculans oscitatur, Plaut. Oscitationes longas trahere, Mart.
units.tr: To yawn] Stretching, he yawns, Plaut. To draw out long yawns, Mart.

units.la: Oscitatio] Hiatus oris, Cic. Oscedo, Gell.
units.tr: Yawning] A gaping of the mouth, Cic. Yawning, Gell.

units.la: Osculari] Dare osculum. Excipere osculo aliquem. Reddere oscula manu, Plin. Impertire aliquem osculo. Delibatum digitis osculum ad os suum referre, Suet. Affigere oscula, Lucr. Contingere osculo, Liv. Fatigare dextram oculis, Tac. Conterere osculis manus alicujus, Sen. Suaviari; dissuaviari. Dare suavium, Cic. Oppangere, pangere, facere suavium, Plaut. Exosculari, Sipont.
units.tr: To kiss] To give a kiss. To receive someone with a kiss. To return kisses with the hand, Plin. To bestow a kiss on someone. To raise to one's own mouth a kiss touched with the fingers, Suet. To fasten kisses, Lucr. To touch with a kiss, Liv. To wear out the right hand with eyes, Tac. To wear out someone's hand with kisses, Sen. To kiss; to kiss repeatedly. To give a kiss, Cic. To fasten, make a kiss, Plaut. To kiss fondly, Sipont.

units.la: Osculum] Osculatio. Suavium, Cicer. Suaviatio, Gell. Exosculatio, Plin. Suaviolum, Catul. Basium, Basiatio, Mart.
units.tr: Kiss] Kissing. A sweet kiss, Cicer. A kissing, Gell. A thorough kissing, Plin. A little kiss, Catul. A kiss, a kissing, Mart.

units.la: Osor] Infensus alicui, Cic. Invisor, Apul.
units.tr: Hater] Hostile to someone, Cic. One who hates, Apul.

units.la: Ossarium] Ossuarium, Vlp.
units.tr: Ossuary] Ossuary, Vlp.

units.la: Ostendere] Ostentare. Convincit ratio ipsa, Declarare vim verbi. Exhibere, indicare. Dare specimen virtutis. Probare fidem suam, Cic. Arguere: degeneres animos timor arguit, Virg. Ratio aliquid dictat, Plin. Evincit ratio, Hor. Stare, consistere, in aliquo, Cic.
units.tr: To show] To display. Reason itself convinces; to declare the force of a word. To exhibit, to point out. To give a sample of virtue. To prove one's faith, Cic. To prove: fear reveals degenerate spirits, Virg. Reason dictates something, Plin. Reason proves, Hor. To stand, to rest, upon something, Cic.

units.la: Ostensio] Declaratio amoris, demonstratio. Significatio pudoris, Cic. Indicatura dolorum, Plin. Exhibitio chirographi, Gell. Monstratio, Ter. Monstratus urbium novo hospiti gratus est, Sen.
units.tr: Showing] A declaration of love, a demonstration. A sign of modesty, Cic. An indication of pains, Plin. An exhibition of a document, Gell. A showing, Ter. A showing of cities is pleasing to a new guest, Sen.

units.la: Ostentare se] Præ se ferre aliquid. Vultu & verbis aliquid significare, Cic. Vultu ferebat quos spiritus gestisset, Tacit. Habere, præferre studium sapientiæ, Plin. Iun. Promittit nescio quid magnum, Petron. Formatus in admirationem, Suet. Præ se gerere aliquid, Cic. Prætendere, proferre, Quint.
units.tr: To display oneself] To bear something before oneself. To signify something by look and words, Cic. He showed by his face what spirit he had stirred up, Tacit. To have and put forward a zeal for wisdom, Plin. Iun. He promises I know not what great thing, Petron. Shaped for admiration, Suet. To carry something before oneself, Cic. To hold out, to put forward, Quint.

units.la: Ostentare] Animum Achilleum spirat. Animos leonum præ se ferentes.
units.tr: To display] He breathes an Achillean spirit. Bearing the spirits of lions before them.

units.la: Ostentatio] Pompa. Jactatio popularis. Venditatio, Cic. Scena, Suet. Pulchrum est digito monstrari. Dicta phalerata, Ter.
units.tr: Ostentation] Pomp. Popular boasting. Showing off, Cic. A stage display, Suet. It is fine to be pointed at with the finger. Showy sayings, Ter.

units.la: Ostentatio prematura] Capra nondum peperit, & hœdus saltat in tectis. Triumphus ante victoriam.
units.tr: Premature display] The goat has not yet given birth, and already the kid leaps about in the house. A triumph before the victory.

units.la: Ostentatio provocat invidiam] Corvus si possit tacitus pasci.
units.tr: Ostentation provokes envy] If only the crow could feed in silence.

units.la: Ostentatio suspecta] Ostentatio mendacii suspicionem habet.
units.tr: Suspicious display] Display carries the suspicion of a lie.

units.la: Ostentator] Affectator, Quint. Salaco, vel, Salacon, (i. qui pauper est, & dives vult haberi.) Ita ambitiosus, ut omnes nos quotidie persalutet, Cic. Pauper ambitiosus, Quint. Staperda, Varr. Bellus, Mart. Plin. Iun. Laudicœna, Id. Laudicœnus, Manut. Vid. Iactator.
units.tr: Show-off] A pretender, Quint. Salaco, or Salacon, (that is, one who is poor and wants to be thought rich.) So ambitious that he greets all of us every day, Cic. A poor man with ambition, Quint. Staperda, Varr. A fine fellow, Mart. Plin. Iun. Laudicoena, Id. Laudicoenus, Manut. See Boaster.

units.la: Ostentum, vid. Monstrum.
units.tr: Portent, see Monster.

units.la: Ostiarium, vid. Census qui per eos.
units.tr: Ostiarium, see The census which is paid through them.

units.la: Ostiarius, vid. Ianitor.
units.tr: Doorkeeper, see Janitor.

units.la: Ostium, vid. Ianua.
units.tr: Ostium, see Door.

units.la: Otiari] Otiosum esse. In otio esse. Sequi otium. Otium est tempus conterere. Cessare. Cessatorem esse. Vacare ab omni curatione & administratione rerum, Cic. Agere otium, Virg. Dare se otio, Plaut. Ducere otia segnia, Ovid. Pendent opera, Virg. Sedere ferias, Plaut.
units.tr: To be at leisure] To be idle. To be at ease. To follow leisure. Leisure is time to be wasted. To rest. To be a loiterer. To be free from all care and management of affairs, Cic. To pass one's leisure, Virg. To give oneself to leisure, Plaut. To lead a life of idle leisure, Ovid. The works hang idle, Virg. To keep holiday, Plaut.

units.la: Otio torpere] Otio tabescere. Hebescere & languescere in otio. Torpere cessatione. Tardari animo, Cicer. Marcescere desidiâ & otiô, Liv. Consenescere veterno, Col. Manum habere sub pallio. Pulmonis vitam vivere.
units.tr: To grow numb with idleness] To waste away in leisure. To grow dull and languid in leisure. To grow numb through inactivity. To be slowed in mind, Cicer. To wither with sloth and idleness, Liv. To grow old in lethargy, Col. To keep one's hand under one's cloak. To live the life of a mere breather.

units.la: Otiose] Desidiose vitam agere, Lucr.
units.tr: Idly] To lead an idle life, Lucr.

units.la: Otiosus] Otiosissimus, Plin. Diffluens otio. Immunis. Feriatus: & feriatus à negotiis. In otio est; in otio deses vivit. Otium sequitur. Subrostranus, Cic. Cessator operarius, vacuus operarius, Col. Vacuus rerum, Tac. Operum, Liv. Hor. Desidiosus, Ovid. Maleferiatus, Hor. Subbasilicanus, Plaut. Reses populus, Virg. Inficiens, Varr. Nihil pensi habet, quomodo tempus transigatur. Avis sine volatu. Coelum sine roratu. Omissus animus. Omissior ab re.
units.tr: Idle] Most idle, Plin. Dissolving in leisure. Exempt. On holiday, and free from business. He is at leisure; in leisure he lives idle. He follows leisure. Loafing about the Rostra, Cic. An idle workman, an unoccupied workman, Col. Empty of affairs, Tac. Of works, Liv. Hor. Idle, Ovid. Keeping holiday badly, Hor. Loafing about the basilica, Plaut. An idle people, Virg. Doing nothing, Varr. He has no concern how time is spent. A bird without flight. A sky without dew. A spirit let go. More neglectful of business.

units.la: Otiosus bene pastus] Bos ad præsepe; in stabulo. Gravastellus, vel gravistellus, Plaut. Telluris inutile pondus. Nos numerus sumus, & fruges consumere nati, Hor.
units.tr: Idle and well fed] An ox at the manger, in the stall. Gravastellus, or gravistellus, Plaut. A useless weight upon the earth. We are but a number, born to consume the fruits, Hor.

units.la: Otium] Otium ab re. Cessatio, Cic. Otium operis, Plin. (Vacuna, Dea otiosorum, Plin.] Desidia, Ovid. Pulvinar Satanæ. Vivi hominis sepultura.
units.tr: Leisure] Leisure from business. Cessation, Cic. Leisure from work, Plin. (Vacuna, goddess of the idle, Plin.) Idleness, Ovid. Satan's pillow. The burial of a living man.

units.la: Oviaria] Lanicium, Arnob. Grex ovium, Virg. Laniger grex.
units.tr: Oviary: a flock of wool-bearers, Arnob. A flock of sheep, Virg. A woolly flock, Virg.

units.la: Ovile] Caula, Virg. Cohors ovium, Col.
units.tr: Sheepfold: a pen, Virg. A company of sheep, Col.

units.la: Ovis] Lanare pecus, Varr. Agnus fœmina, Scal. Agna, Varr. Lanigeræ pecudes, Lucr. Bela, pl. Varr. Balantum pecudes, Lucr. Lanatum pecus, Col. Ambidens, Fest.
units.tr: Sheep: a woolly herd, Varr. A ewe lamb, Scal. A female lamb, Varr. Wool-bearing beasts, Lucr. Bleating creatures, plural, Varr. Bleating beasts, Lucr. A woolly herd, Col. Two-toothed, Fest.

units.la: Ovum] Fœtus gallinæ, Col. Pullus non-dum natus.
units.tr: Egg: the offspring of a hen, Col. A chick not yet hatched.

units.la: Ovum corruptum] Ovum irritum, hypenemium, Zephyrium; quod Zephyro flante generatur, urinum, cynosurum rum. Fœtus ovi corruptus, Plin. Subventaneum ovum, Cel. Rhod.
