units.tr: Addled egg: an egg that is unfertile, called a wind-egg, a zephyr-egg, that which is produced when the west wind blows, a urine-egg, a dog-star egg; a spoiled offspring of an egg, Plin. A wind-fed egg, Cel. Rhod.

units.la: Ovum incorruptum] Ovum pullescens, animatum, Col. Oppositum, silens ovum, Id.
units.tr: Sound egg: an egg with a chick beginning to stir, living, Col. The opposite: a silent egg, Id.

units.la: Oxygala] Oxygalum. Lac crebro jactatu coactum. Sedimentum lactis a butyro separato. Acor lactis jucundus, a butyro separatus, Plin. Lac serosum, Iun.
units.tr: Oxygala: sour milk. Milk curdled by frequent shaking. The residue of milk separated from butter. The pleasant sourness of milk separated from butter, Plin. Watery milk, Iun.

units.la: P.
units.tr: P.

units.la: PAbulari] Frumentari, Cic. (Copiari, lignari, aquari, castrensia verba sunt, inquit, Gell.)
units.tr: To forage: to get grain, Cic. (To procure supplies, to gather wood, to fetch water, are military terms, he says, Gell.)

units.la: Pabulatio] Frumentatio, Liv. Sitonia, Ulp.
units.tr: Foraging: procuring grain, Liv. Supply of grain, Ulp.

units.la: Pabulator, vid. Annonæ præf.
units.tr: Forager: see the prefect of the grain supply.

units.la: Pabulatorius] Pabularis vicia. Esculentus, Col. Escarius, Plin. Annonarius, Veget. Fungibiles res, apud ICtos.
units.tr: Fodder-like: fodder vetches. Edible, Col. Fit for eating, Plin. Relating to provisions, Veget. Fungible goods, among the jurists.

units.la: Pabulum] Pastus ex se fundit petra bestiis, Cic. Porculatoris & subulci diversæ pastiones, Col. Ubi idonea pabulatio est, Varr.
units.tr: Fodder: food which the rock yields from itself to beasts, Cic. The varied feedings of the swineherd and the pig-keeper, Col. Where foraging is suitable, Varr.

units.la: Pacare] Perpacare aliquem, Liv. Vid. Tranquillare, Placare.
units.tr: To pacify: to subdue someone completely, Liv. See To calm, To appease.

units.la: Pacatè] Quietè acta ætas. Tranquillè placidéque, Cic. Quietissimè, Cæs. Tranquillò, Plin. Tranquillissimè, Suet. Placidè accubare. Pace advenio, (i.pacificus) Plaut.
units.tr: Peacefully: a life spent quietly. Calmly and gently, Cic. Most quietly, Caes. Tranquilly, Plin. Most tranquilly, Suet. To recline gently. He comes in peace (i.e. peaceably), Plaut.

units.la: Pacator, vid. Arbiter.
units.tr: Pacifier: see arbiter.

units.la: Pacatus, vid. Tranquillus.
units.tr: Pacified: see tranquil.

units.la: Pace tuâ, vid. Venia sit.
units.tr: With your peace: see let it be forgiven.

units.la: Pacificare, i. pacem tractare] Pacificatum venêre legati, Liv. Facere pacem, Cic. Pangere pacem cum aliquo populo, Liv. Patrare pacem, Tac. Componere cum aliquo pacem, Plaut.
units.tr: To pacify, i.e. to treat for peace: Envoys came to make peace, Liv. To make peace, Cic. To make peace with some people, Liv. To bring about peace, Tac. To arrange peace with someone, Plaut.

units.la: Pacificatio] Compositio. Decisio; conciliatio; concordia, Cicer. Ita res concordiâ coaluit, Liv. Conciliatura, Sen.
units.tr: Pacification: settlement; resolution; reconciliation; concord, Cic. Thus the matter grew together by concord, Liv. Conciliation, Sen.

units.la: Pacificator] Pacator, Sen. Reconciliator, Liv. Conciliator. Varr. Commeator, Apul, Internuncius, Sipont. Vid. Arbiter. Pacificus] Oleo tranquillior, Eraf. Abest à contentione, Cic. Fugiens litium, Ter. Vid. Quietus.
units.tr: Pacifier: one who pacifies, Sen. A reconciler, Liv. A conciliator, Varr. A go-between, Apul. An intermediary, Sipont. See arbiter. Peaceable: calmer than oil, Erasm. Free from strife, Cic. Avoiding lawsuits, Ter. See quiet.

units.la: Pacisci cum aliquo] Condicere alicui, Sen. Condicere locum, tempusque coëundi, Iuft. Condictus statuts,dies cum hoste, Plaut. Pactionem cum aliquo cum aliqua re facere, conficere, conflare. Pactionem pecuniarum agere. Ad pactionem & conditionem aliquam venire. Constituere mercedem funeris &c. Depacisci cum aliquo partem suam. Depacisci aliquo periculo. Adducere, perducere ad aliquam conditionem. Adstringere aliquem conditionibus. Decidere cum aliquo de aliqua re. Constituere inter se,Cic. Depacisci ad conditionem, Id. Depecisci, Muret. Struere mercedem, Cic. Constituere cum aliquo,Ter. Pangere cum aliquo de aliqua re, Plin. Iun. Pangere inducias. Conditionibus accipere populos in societatem, Liv. Emere operam alicujus, Plin.
units.tr: To make a pact with someone: to agree with someone, Sen. To agree on a place and time for meeting, Just. A day fixed with the enemy, Plaut. To make, complete or strike a bargain with someone about something. To conduct a money agreement. To come to an arrangement and terms. To settle the wages of a funeral, etc. To bargain away one's share with someone. To stake something on a danger. To bring or lead someone to some terms. To bind someone with conditions. To settle something with someone. To agree among themselves, Cic. To agree on terms, Id. To bargain away, Muret. To arrange a fee, Cic. To agree with someone, Ter. To make an agreement with someone about something, Plin. Iun. To make a truce. To receive peoples into alliance on conditions, Liv. To hire someone's services, Plin.

units.la: Pactio] Pactum, Pacta conventa, Conventum, Conventus, Conditio, Constitutum, Stipulatio, Cic. Conventio, Vlp. Condictum, Condictio, Fest. Contractus, IC. Auctoramentum, Formula, Sen.
units.tr: Pact: agreement, agreed terms, settlement, stipulation, condition, arrangement, Cic. Convention, Ulp. Engagement, Fest. Contract, among the jurists. Hire, formula, Sen.

units.la: Pactor] Conditor disciplinæ militaris, Plin.Iun. Constitutor, Quint. Conditor legum, Plaut. Sanctor,Tac.
units.tr: Pactor: founder of military discipline, Plin. Iun. Establisher, Quint. Maker of laws, Plaut. Sanctioner, Tac.

units.la: Pactus] Status. Condictus dies cum hoste, Plaut. Conventa pax, Sal. Composita hora, Hor. Statutus dies, Liv. Præfinitus: præstituta dies, Cic.
units.tr: Pactus: fixed. A day fixed with the enemy, Plaut. An agreed peace, Sal. An appointed hour, Hor. An appointed day, Liv. Fixed beforehand: a day settled in advance, Cic.

units.la: Pædagogus] Pædonomus, Alex. Neap. Custos herilis, Plaut. Formator morum, Plin. Iun. Animi formator & institutor, scil. puerilis.Col. Magister morum puerilium. Magnus bajulus, Codin.
units.tr: Pedagogue: child-governor, Alex. Neap. Household guard, Plaut. Shaper of manners, Plin. Iun. Former and instructor of the mind, namely of boys, Col. Teacher of boys' manners. Great nurse, Codin.

units.la: Pænula, vid. Penula.
units.tr: Penula: see penula.

units.la: Pætulus]Pætus, Hor. Patranti fractus ocello, Perf. Patrans oculus libidinosi. Fractus effœminati & parum viri, Marsil. Morsicantes oculi, Apul. Mollis petulantia oculorum, Petron.
units.tr: Wanton: Pætus, Hor. An eye broken by a roving glance, Pers. A wanton, lustful eye. Broken, of an effeminate and unmanly man, Marsil. Biting eyes, Apul. Soft wantonness of the eyes, Petron.

units.la: Paganicus] Pagana lex,Plin. Rusticus, Rusticana vita, Cic. Ruralis, Macrob. Rurestris, April. Ruricola bos, Ovid. Rusticulus libellus, Mart. Paganalis,Varr. Villaticus,Col. Villanus, Sipon. Vicanus homo, Cic.
units.tr: Rustic: rustic law, Plin. Country, rustic life, Cic. Rural, Macrob. Of the countryside, April. A field-dwelling ox, Ovid. A little rustic book, Mart. Pagan, Varr. Of the farmyard, Col. Village, Sipon. A villager, Cic.

units.la: Pagina ] Paginula ; pagella , Cic. Prima & fecunda cera, Suet.
units.tr: Page: a little page; a small tablet, Cic. The first and fertile wax, Suet.

units.la: Pagina inscripta utraque ] Opistographus commentarius, Plin. Aversâ & adversâ paginâ scriptus, Hermol.
units.tr: Page written on both sides: a commentary written on the back, Plin. Written on back and front, Hermol.

units.la: Pagus] Rus, Ter. Hor. Villa, Cic. Varr.
units.tr: Country district: countryside, Ter. Hor. Farm, Cic. Varr.

units.la: Pala] Infurnibulum, Grip. & Iun.
units.tr: Baking-shovel: a fire-shovel, Grip. & Iun.

units.la: Palæstra] Arena, Mart. Palæstra & Ceroma, Plin. Gymnasium, Plaut. Xystus, Stadiata porticus. Paradromis, Vitruv.
units.tr: Wrestling-ground: sand, Mart. Wrestling-ground and oiling-room, Plin. Gymnasium, Plaut. Xystus, a covered colonnade for running. A walkway, Vitr.

units.la: Palæstrica ars, vid. Pugillatus.
units.tr: Wrestling art: see boxing.

units.la: Palam, vid. Manifesté.
units.tr: Openly: see plainly.

units.la: Palam est] Liquet, constat, patet, apparet. Clara res, toto orbe celeberrima & notissima. Id solis videtur luce clarius. Clara & testata res est. Patescit res. In promptu est, & patet. Apertum est omnibus. Ante oculos positum est. In oculis & in conspectu. Perspicuum est omnibus. Controversia non est. Res ipsa loquitur, quæ semper plurimum valuit. Videre licet. Res percrebruit. In ore atque sermone omnium esse cœpit. Id ita perspicuum est, ut judicare oculis possimus, Cicer. Claret, Lucr. Clarescit, Macrob. Manifestum habeo, Sallust. Manifestaria res est, Plaut. In confesso est, Plin. In propatulo positum, Liv. Videre est, Hor.
units.tr: It is plain: it is clear, agreed, evident, apparent. A matter clear and very well known throughout the world. This is clearer than the light of the sun. The matter is clear and attested. The matter is laid open. It lies ready and open. It is open to all. It is set before the eyes. It is in plain sight. It is plain to all. There is no dispute. The thing itself speaks, which has always weighed most. One may see. The matter has become widely known. It has begun to be on everyone's lips. It is so plain that we can judge with our eyes, Cic. It is clear, Lucr. It becomes clear, Macrob. I hold it manifest, Sall. It is a manifest matter, Plaut. It is admitted, Plin. Set out in the open, Liv. One may see it, Hor.

units.la: Palanga] Phalanga, Plin. Palangæ: Palancæ: Plancæ, Scal. Chamulcus, Anim.
units.tr: Phalanx: phalanx, Plin. Palangae, palancae, plancae, Scal. Chamulcus, Anim.

units.la: Palangarius, vid. Bajulus.
units.tr: Porter: see carrier.

units.la: Palatium] Basilica, Vitr. Regia, Id. Augustale, Quint. Prætorium.
units.tr: Palace: basilica, Vitr. Royal house, Id. Augustan house, Quint. Praetorium.

units.la: Palatum] Palatus, Cic. Cœlum, Sipont. Cœlum oris, Calep. Templa linguæ humida, sudantia, Lucr. Gulam Domini debet habere coquus, Mart.
units.tr: Palate: palate, Cic. The sky of the mouth, Sipont. The roof of the mouth, Calep. The moist, sweating roof of the tongue, Lucr. The cook must have his master's palate, Mart.

units.la: Palea] Acus, eris, Cat. Acus, us, Col.
units.tr: Chaff: straw of a stalk, Cat. Straw, Col.

units.la: Paleatus] Acerosus panis. Aceratus, Fest.
units.tr: Chaffy: bread full of chaff. Stalky bread, Fest.

units.la: Palla] Stola. Crocota, Cic. Peplus, Virg. Peplum, Plaut. Cyclas, Propert. Supparus, & Supparum, Varr.
units.tr: Mantle: a robe. A saffron-coloured robe, Cic. A peplos, Virg. A peplum, Plaut. A cyclas, Propert. A supparus and supparum, Varr.

units.la: Pallere ] Pallescere, Exalbescere, Expallere, Exsanguem esse, Cic. Pallorem trahere, Col. Impallescere, Stat. Excidit alicui color, Ovid. Et redit infelix effosso concolor auro, Sili.
units.tr: To turn pale: to become pale, to grow white, to lose colour, to be bloodless, Cic. To draw a pallor, Col. To grow pale, Stat. Colour leaves someone, Ovid. And the unhappy man returns the colour of dug gold, Sil.

units.la: Palliatus] Palliolatus, Mart. Palliolatim amictus, Plaut. Scissili palliastro amictus, Apul. Reciniatus & Ricinia-tus, Fest.
units.tr: Cloaked: wrapped in a small cloak, Mart. Wrapped in a cloak thrown on, Plaut. Wrapped in a worn cloak, Apul. Wrapped in a hood, Fest.

units.la: Pallidus] Pallidulus, Catul. Vepallidus, Hor. Pallore peremptus, Lucr. Exsangui colore, Ovid. Sine colore, Cic. Mali habitus corpus, Celf. Cachectos, Plin. Luridus pallor. Excidit illi color, Ovid. Cadaverosa facies, Ter. Squalidus, Liv.
units.tr: Pale: rather pale, Catul. Very pale, Hor. Destroyed by pallor, Lucr. With bloodless colour, Ovid. Without colour, Cic. Of bad bodily condition, Celsus. Wan, Plin. A livid pallor. Colour has left him, Ovid. A corpse-like face, Ter. Filthy, Liv.

units.la: Palliolum] Palliastrum, Apul.
units.tr: Little cloak: a small cloak, Apul.

units.la: Pallium] Palliolata tunica, Apul. Bardocucullus, Ruder. Ricinum, vel ricinium, Cic. Varr. Recinus, Serv.
units.tr: Cloak: a tunic worn as a cloak, Apul. A hooded cloak, Ruder. Ricinum or ricinium, Cic. Varr. Recinus, Serv.

units.la: Pallor] Luror corporis, Lucr.
units.tr: Pallor: paleness of the body, Lucr.

units.la: Palma, pro manu] Explicata manus, Quint.
units.tr: Palm, for hand: an outstretched hand, Quint.

units.la: Palmarius] Palmaris virgula, Varr.
units.tr: Palmary: a palm-rod, Varr.

units.la: Palmes] Pampinus, Col. Suboles vitium, Id. Propago, Plin. Virg. Vitis minor, Varr. Vitis tenera in vite, Cat. Flagellum vitis, Virg. Sarmentum vitis, Col. Vid. Resex.
units.tr: Shoot: a tendril, Col. A vine sprout, Id. A layering, Plin. Virg. A little vine, Varr. A tender vine-shoot on a vine, Cat. A whip of the vine, Virg. A vine-twig, Col. See rejected shoot.

units.la: Palmipes] Plancus, Plin. Fest. Planipes, Quint. Plautus, Plotus, Fest. Pansa, Plin.
units.tr: Web-footed: flat-footed, Plin. Fest. Flat-footed, Quint. Plautus, plotus, Fest. Pansa, Plin.

units.la: Palmosus, de arb.] Palmifer, Ovid.
units.tr: Palm-bearing, of trees: palm-bearing, Ovid.

units.la: Palpare] Tentare aliquid digitis, Col. Manticulari, Apul. Sollicitare manu, Virg. Pertractare, Petron.
units.tr: To touch: to try something with the fingers, Col. To feel about, Apul. To stir with the hand, Virg. To handle, Petron.

units.la: Palpatio] Præientatus, ûs, Plin. Contrectatio, Apul. Palpator, vid. Adulator.
units.tr: Touching: a touching, Plin. A handling, Apul. Flatterer: see flatterer.

units.la: Palpebra] Pili palpebrarum, Celf. Vallum pilorum, Cic. Cilia, pl. Iuv. Gorr.
units.tr: Eyelid: the hairs of the eyelids, Celsus. A rampart of hairs, Cic. Lashes, plural, Juv. Gorr.

units.la: Palpitare] Micant venæ, Cic. Emicat cor, Plaut.
units.tr: To throb: the veins gleam, Cic. The heart leaps, Plaut.

units.la: Palpitatio] Palpitatus, Plin.
units.tr: Throbbing: a throbbing, Plin.

units.la: Paludamentum, vestis militaris] Abolla, Mart. Lacerna, Propert. Læna, Non. Chlæna, Sipont. Sagum. Chlamys, Cic. Chlamydula, Plaut. Sagulum, Liv. Sagochlamys, Trebell. Gausape purpureum, Hor.
units.tr: Military cloak: abolla, Mart. Lacerna, Propert. Laena, Non. Chlaena, Sipont. Sagum. Chlamys, Cic. A little chlamys, Plaut. A little sagum, Liv. Sagochlamys, Trebell. A purple-edged cloth, Hor.

units.la: Paludosus] Paluftris, Col. Paludifer, Aust. Philom.
units.tr: Marshy: marshy, Col. Marsh-bearing, Aust. Philom.

units.la: Palumbus] Palumbus major, torquatus, Gesn. Palumba, Propert. Palumbes, Virg.
units.tr: Wood-pigeon: the larger, ring-necked wood-pigeon, Gesn. A wood-pigeon, Propert. A wood-pigeon, Virg.

units.la: Palus, fustis] Sublica, Vitr. Cippus, Caf. Stylus, Hirt. Ficolea, (palus ficulneus) Fest. Vallus, Cic. Virg. Sudes, stipitesque praeacutos defigit, Caes. Liv. Surus, Fest. Scal. Ridica, Varr.
units.tr: Stake, club: a post, Vitr. A pillar, Caes. A stake, Hirt. A fig-wood stake, Fest. A pole, Cic. Virg. Stakes and sharp-pointed stakes driven in, Caes. Liv. A stake, Fest. Scal. A ridica, Varr.

units.la: Palus, aqua caenosa] Terra stagnata palude, Col. Locus palustris, Caes.
units.tr: Swamp, muddy water: land made a pool by marsh, Col. A marshy place, Caes.

units.la: Pampinare, vid. Putare.
units.tr: Pampinare: see prune.

units.la: Pampinus, vid. Palmes.
units.tr: Pampinus: see palm shoot.

units.la: Panacea] Panax, Col. Panaces : Panaces ipso nomine omnium morborum remedia promittit, Plin
units.tr: Panacea: panax, Col. Panaces: by its very name panacea promises remedies for all diseases, Plin.

units.la: Pandari, i. incurvari] Pandare, Vitr. Pandatione fidit contignatio, Id. Incurvescunt rami ubertate, Cic. Cedunt rami oneri, Mart. Incurvatur ceditque ponderi robur oleae, Plin. Secedit trabes pondere, Stat.
units.tr: To bend, i.e. to curve: to bend, Vitr. A floor supported by bending beams, Vitr. The branches curve with fruitfulness, Cic. The branches yield to the weight, Mart. The strength of the olive bends and yields to the weight, Plin. The beam gives way under the weight, Stat.

units.la: Pandiculari] Pandiculans oscitatur, Plaut.
units.tr: To stretch: to yawn while stretching, Plaut.

units.la: Pandiculatio ] Inter oscitandum totius corporis extensio, Fest.
units.tr: Stretching: the extension of the whole body while yawning, Fest.

units.la: Pangere] Adigere clavos in crucem, Sen. Incutere clavum parieti, vel, in parietem, Liv. Plin. Depangere, Plin. Refigere, Col. Virg. Vid. Depangere.
units.tr: To fasten: to drive nails into a cross, Sen. To drive a nail into a wall, or into the wall, Liv. Plin. To nail down, Plin. To fasten again, Col. Virg. See Depangere.

units.la: Panificium] Furnaria : Furnariam exercere, Suet.
units.tr: Panificium: a bakery; to carry on the trade of a baker, Suet.

units.la: Panis ] Pistrinarum opera, Plin. Cereale donum. Ceres, Virg.
units.tr: Panis: the work of the bakehouses, Plin. A cereal gift; the gift of Ceres, Virg.

units.la: Panis acerosus] Panis sordidus, Suet. Panis cibarius, Cic. Plin.
units.tr: Panis acerosus: coarse bread, Suet. Ordinary bread, Cic. Plin.

units.la: Panis secundarius] Panis secundus, Hor. Panis furnaceus, Autopyrus, Plin. Panis sequens, Lamp. Panis agelaeus, Cael. Rhod. Gregarius, Gor.
units.tr: Panis secundarius: second-grade bread, Hor. Oven-baked bread, or self-baked bread, Plin. Following bread, Lamp. Shepherd's bread, Cael. Rhod. Common bread, Gor.

units.la: Panis candidus] Panis triticeus, Ovid. Panis niveus, Iuv. Primarius, Quint. Panis siligineus, Sen. Panis sitanius, Plin. Similaceus, similagineus, Iun.
units.tr: Panis candidus: wheaten bread, Ovid. Snow-white bread, Iuv. First-rate bread, Quint. Bread of fine wheat flour, Sen. Sitanius bread, Plin. Bread of fine flour, Iun.

units.la: Panis bis coctus] Panis ad usus diuturnitatem excoctus, Amm. Panis nauticus, Plin. Panis rubidus, Plaut. Buccellatum, Amm. Paximas, atis, Meurs. Paxamas, & atius, Lipf.
units.tr: Panis bis coctus: bread baked hard for long keeping, Amm. Ship's biscuit, Plin. Reddish bread, Plaut. Biscuit, Amm. Paximas, Meurs. Paxamas, Lipf.

units.la: Panis subcineritius] Panis focarius, Sipont. Panis speusticus, militaris, Plin. Lipf. Panis subitus, nec bene excoctus, Plin.
units.tr: Panis subcineritius: hearth bread, Sipont. Camp or soldiers' bread, baked in the embers, Plin. Lipf. Bread put in under the ashes and not well baked, Plin.

units.la: Pannifex] Lanarius, Plaut. Artis lanificæ doctissimus, Claud. Textor lacernæ, Iuv. Textor tunicarum, Firmic. Lanificus. Lanarius artifex, Sipont.
units.tr: Pannifex: a wool-worker, Plaut. Most skilled in the wool-working craft, Claud. A weaver of cloaks, Iuv. A weaver of tunics, Firmic. A wool-worker; a craftsman in wool, Sipont.

units.la: Pannificium] Lanificium, Col. Ars lanifica, Claud.
units.tr: Pannificium: wool-working, Col. The wool-working craft, Claud.

units.la: Pannosus] Semilacer. Lacer homo, Ovid. Pannuciatus, Pompon. Scissili palliastro semiamictus, lurore ac miserâ macie deformatus, Plin. Sentus, Ter. Sordidatus, Plaut. Pullatus, Suet. Obsoletius vestitus : malè vestitus, Cic. Vestitus vix ad privati modicè locupletis habitum. Liv. Tunicatus, Hor. Pannis obsitus, Ter. Pannucius homo, Perf. Mediocriter vestitus, Ter. Fenestrata domus, Plaut.
units.tr: Pannosus: half-torn; a man in tatters, Ovid. Ragged, Pompon. Half-clothed in torn rags, disfigured by filth and wretched thinness, Plin. Shabby, Ter. Dressed in dirty clothes, Plaut. Dressed in rags, Suet. Rather poorly dressed; badly dressed, Cic. Dressed barely as a moderately well-off private man would dress, Liv. Clad in a tunic, Hor. Covered with rags, Ter. A ragged fellow, Pers. Moderately dressed, Ter. A house full of windows, Plaut.

units.la: Pannus] Pannum, Non. Ovium villi contexti.
units.tr: Pannus: a piece of cloth, Non. Woven from the fleece of sheep.

units.la: Pansa, vid. Pamipes.
units.tr: Pansa: see Pamipes.

units.la: Panthera] Varia, Abf.Plin. Pardalis, Iun.
units.tr: Panthera: spotted, Abf. Plin. A leopard, Iun.

units.la: Panurgus] Polytropus. Omnium horarum homo.
units.tr: Panurgus: versatile; a man for all hours.

units.la: Panus] Tramæ involucrum, Non. Panulia, vel, Panucla, Isid. Panula, Non. Scal. Panulla, Aug.
units.tr: Panus: the covering of a weft, Non. Panulia or panucla, Isid. Panula, Non. Scal. Panulla, Aug.

units.la: Papilio] Volatilis eruca.
units.tr: Papilio: a flying caterpillar.

units.la: Papula] Pustula, Celf. Plin. Pusula tumens, Turn. Epinyctis, Celf. Plin.
units.tr: Papula: a pustule, Celf. Plin. A swelling pimple, Turn. Epinyctis, Celf. Plin.

units.la: Papyraceus] Chartaceus, Vlp. Papyrinus, Varr. Papyrifer, Ovid.
units.tr: Papyraceus: made of paper, Vlp. Of papyrus, Varr. Bearing papyrus, Ovid.

units.la: Par] Jugum impiorum, Cic. Conjugium, Plin.
units.tr: Par: a yoke of the wicked, Cic. Marriage, Plin.

units.la: Par, adj vid. Æqualis. Par est, vid. Fas est.
units.tr: Par, adj: see Aequalis. Par est: see Fas est.

units.la: Paralysis] Resolutio nervorum, Celf. Sideratio nervorum, Scrib. Sidus, Mart. Sidere est percussa tibi Zoile lingua.
units.tr: Paralysis: a loosening of the nerves, Celf. A stroke affecting the nerves, Scrib. A star-stroke, Mart. Your tongue, Zoilus, has been struck by a star.

units.la: Paraphernalia, vid. Dotalia dona.
units.tr: Paraphernalia: see Dotalia dona.

units.la: Parare] Præparare res necessarias. Comparare insidias. Constituere, Concinnare. Struere bellum. Instruere insidias. Ornare convivium. Adornare, Machinari aliquid, Parturire, Cic. Apparare cœnam, Ter. Præstruere, Apul. Instituere dapes, Virg. Paritare, Plaut. Expedire equos, Liv. Moliri, aptare, Virg. In procinctu versari, Vlp. Præsternere aliquid, Plin.
units.tr: Parare: to prepare necessary things; to lay snares; to set up, to arrange; to put together; to make ready for war; to set snares; to furnish a feast; to adorn; to plan something; to be pregnant with a plan, Cic. To prepare a dinner, Ter. To prepare beforehand, Apul. To set out a feast, Virg. To make ready, Plaut. To equip horses, Liv. To devise, to fit out, Virg. To be ready for action, Vlp. To spread something out beforehand, Plin.

units.la: Parare se ad] Aptare se fugæ. Moliri fugam. Comparare se ad aliquid, Cic. Accingere se operi, Virg.
units.tr: Parare se ad: to fit oneself for flight; to plan a flight; to prepare oneself for something, Cic. To gird oneself for a task, Virg.

units.la: Parasitari, vid. Adulari.
units.tr: Parasitari: see Adulari.

units.la: Parasitus ] Assecla mensarum, Cic. Stultorum divitum arrosor, Sen. Coenipeta, Sipont. Assectator coenarum, quas improbitate linguae meretur, Sen. Captus nidore alienae culinae, Iuv. Amicus circa sartaginem, Plaut. Alter Melanthus (qui fuit Alex. Pherei parasitus.) Musca, Caesaris Getae assecla. Asymbolum comedens. Ollarum venator. In ventrem sumpsit confidentiam, Plaut. Parasitaster.
units.tr: Parasitus: a hanger-on at tables, Cic. A gnawer away at rich fools, Sen. A dinner-seeker, Sipont. One who pursues dinners, which he earns by the impudence of his tongue, Sen. Drawn by the smell of another's kitchen, Iuv. A friend at the frying-pan, Plaut. Another Melanthus (who was the parasite of Alexander, son of Pheraeus). Fly, attendant of Caesar's Getan. One who eats without paying his share. A hunter of pots. He has taken boldness into his belly, Plaut. A would-be parasite.

units.la: Paratus ] Paratissimus ad omnem eventum, Cic. In expedito est, Sen. Promptus ad aliquid, Cic. Succinctus ad, Quint. Praesens auxilium. Instructus ad mortem contemnendam. Ad manum servus, Cic. Praesentarius. In mundo est, Plaut.
units.tr: Paratus: most ready for every outcome, Cic. At hand, Sen. Ready for something, Cic. Girded for, Quint. Ready help at hand. Equipped to despise death. A slave at hand, Cic. Ready at hand. Ready in the world, Plaut.

units.la: Parata habere omnia ] In numerato habere, Sen. In promptu : in procinctu. Proclive, in proclivi, obvium, expositum, expromptum, in statione, ad manum, ex tempore, extemporaneum, Erasm.
units.tr: Parata habere omnia: to have ready money in hand, Sen. At hand; ready for action. Close to hand, on the slope, ready, exposed, put forward, on standby, to hand, on the spur of the moment, extempore, Erasm.

units.la: Paratus certamini ] Procinctus miles, Fest. In armis est, Cic.
units.tr: Paratus certamini: a soldier girded for battle, Fest. Is under arms, Cic.

units.la: Parce ] Parcius, Cic. Exiguè, Caes. Maligne, Liv. Perparce, Ter. Parcissime, Col. Exiguè se habuit frumentum, Caes.
units.tr: Parce: sparingly, Cic. Scantily, Caes. Grudgingly, Liv. Very sparingly, Ter. Most sparingly, Col. The grain supply was scanty, Caes.

units.la: Parce vivere] Defraudare genium.
units.tr: Parce vivere: to cheat one's genius.

units.la: Parcere alicui] Parcere nominibus aliquorum, Quint. Auribus alicujus, Cic. Comiter conservare. Honorificè tractare aliquem. Colere, Observare aliquem. Colere observantia aliquem. Observantissimum esse alicujus, Cic. Reverenter habere, Ausón. Honestè mactare. Benè ac pudicè hanc habui domi meae, Plaut. Habere dignitatem alicui, Plin. Iun. In sinu gestare aliquem, Ter.
units.tr: Parcere alicui: to spare some men's names, Quint. To spare someone's ears, Cic. To keep someone courteously; to treat someone with honour; to cherish, to regard someone; to cherish someone with regard; to be most devoted to someone, Cic. To hold in reverence, Ausón. To slaughter honourably. "I have kept her well and chastely at home," Plaut. To hold someone in esteem, Plin. Iun. To carry someone in one's bosom, Ter.

units.la: Pacere sibi] Habere rationem valetudinis. Tribuere aliquid valetudini. Defendere valetudinem. Habere salutis rationem. Indulge tuae valetudini. Praesta te incolumem. Parcere suae valetudini, vitae, Cic. Consulere suae saluti, Caes. Respice te, Plaut.
units.tr: Pacere sibi: to have regard for one's health; to attribute something to one's health; to defend one's health; to have regard for one's safety; to indulge one's health; to keep oneself safe; to spare one's health, one's life, Cic. To look to one's safety, Caes. Look to yourself, Plaut.

units.la: Parcitas] Parsimonia nimia, Ter. Rustica & inculta parsimonia. Illiberalitas. Sordes, Cic. Malignitas conferendi, Liv. Tenacia, Tenacitas.
units.tr: Parcitas: excessive thrift, Ter. Rustic and unpolished thrift; meanness; stinginess, Cic. Niggardliness in giving, Liv. Tenacity; tightfistedness.

units.la: Parcus] Parcus & tenax pater. Sordidus, Cic. Parcè parcus, Triparcus Senex. Homines miserè miseri. Miseris modis victitantes, Plaut. Præparcus, Plin. Deparcus, Suet. Perparcus, Pelli. Attentiores sumus ad rem quàm sat est, Ter. Malignus, Quint. Homo aridus, Ter.
units.tr: Parcus: a sparing and tight-fisted father; mean, Cic. Very sparing; a thrice-sparing old man; men wretchedly stingy; living on miserable means, Plaut. Very sparing, Plin. Excessively sparing, Suet. Most sparing, Pelli. "We are more attentive to money than is enough," Ter. Ungenerous, Quint. A dry man, Ter.

units.la: Parcum esse] Parcere sumptui, Cic. Parcè, exiguè facere sumptum. Claudere benignitatem, Ter. Parcere impensæ. Maligné præbere alicui, Liv. Nec ita claudenda est res familiaris, ut eam benignitas aperire non possit, Cic. Introrsus referre fines benignitatis, Sen.
units.tr: Parcum esse: to spare expense, Cic. To make expense sparingly and meagrely; to shut up one's generosity, Ter. To economise on outlay. To give grudgingly to someone, Liv. "Nor should one's means be so closed up that generosity cannot open them," Cic. To draw the limits of generosity inward, Sen.

units.la: Parelius] Sol geminatus, Gaz. Bini, terni soles, Sen. Parelia, Pl.Id. Gemini soles, Bud.
units.tr: Parelius: a doubled sun, Gaz. Two or three suns, Sen. Parelia, Pl. Id. Twin suns, Bud.

units.la: Parens ] Procreator, Genitor, Cic. Generator. Auctor generis, Sanguinis, Virg.
units.tr: Parens: a begetter, a father or mother, Cic. A generator; the author of a line of descent or of blood, Virg.

units.la: Parentalia ] Epulum funebre, Cic. Cœna feralis, Iuv. Epulæ ferales, Plin. Ad sepulchrum silicernium confecimus, Varr.
units.tr: Parentalia: a funeral feast, Cic. A funeral supper, Iuv. Funeral banquets, Plin. "At the tomb we have prepared a silicernium," Varr.

units.la: Parentare, vid. Exsequias celebrare.
units.tr: Parentare: see Exsequias celebrare.

units.la: Parentatio, vid. Exsequiæ.
units.tr: Parentatio: see Exsequiae.

units.la: Parentela, vid. Cognatio.
units.tr: Parentela: see Cognatio.

units.la: Parere, vid. Obedire.
units.tr: Parere: see Obedire.

units.la: Parere] Excludere partum, Celf. Edere partu filium, Tac. Generare hominem. Fœtum fundere, Cic. Dare liberos, Catul. Progignere, Procreare, Producere, Profundere, Cic. Progenerare fœtum. Fœtare, Fœtificare, Plin. Eniti, Quint. Eniti partum, Liv. Creat terra fructum, Quint. Citat fructum planta, Pallad.
units.tr: Parere: to expel a birth, Celf. To bring forth a son, Tac. To beget a human being. To pour forth offspring, Cic. To give children, Catul. To beget, to procreate, to produce, to bring forth, Cic. To bring forth offspring. To make fruitful, Plin. To bring forth, Quint. To bring forth a birth, Liv. The earth yields fruit, Quint. The plant yields fruit, Pallad.

units.la: Paria paribus conveniunt] Æqualis æqualem delectat. Æqualitas haud parit bellum. Deus simile ducit ad simile. Similitudo confervat amicitiam, & generat.
units.tr: Paria paribus conveniunt: equals delight in equals. Equality does not give birth to war. God leads like to like. Similarity preserves friendship and also generates it.

units.la: Paritas, vid. Æqualitas.
units.tr: Paritas: see Aequalitas.

units.la: Pariter] Perinde ac si, Cic. Vid. Æquè ac.
units.tr: Pariter: just as if, Cic. See Aequè ac.

units.la: Parma] Scutum, Cic.
units.tr: Parma: a shield, Cic.

units.la: Parmatus ] Scutatus, Cic. Parmularius, Quint. Scutigerulus, Plaut. Cetratus, Peltatus, Peltasta, Liv. Peltifer, Stat.
units.tr: Parmatus: shielded, Cic. A small-shield bearer, Quint. A shield-carrying servant, Plaut. Armed with a small round shield; a light-armed soldier, Liv. Shield-bearing, Stat.

units.la: Paroxysmus] Accessio morbi, Celf.
units.tr: Paroxysmus: the onset of a disease, Celf.

units.la: Parricidium, vid. Homicidium.
units.tr: Parricidium: see Homicidium.

units.la: Pars] Particula, Cic. Portio, Plin. Sors, Ovid.
units.tr: Pars: a small part, Cic. A portion, Plin. A lot, Ovid.

units.la: Parsimonia, vid. Parcitas. Frugalitas.
units.tr: Parsimonia: see Parcitas. Frugalitas.

units.la: Parsimonia utilis] Parsimonia magnum vectigal. Ex frugalitate ubertas. Non esse emacem, vectigal est.
units.tr: Parsimonia utilis: thrift is a great source of revenue. Abundance comes from frugality. Not being a buyer is a source of revenue.

units.la: Partes dissidentes] Factio, Caes. Pars: Partium studiosi homines. Litigatores, Cic. Secta, Lucr.
units.tr: Partes dissidentes: faction, Caes. A party; men zealous for parties; litigants, Cic. A sect, Lucr.

units.la: Partium utrique assentari] Duabus sedere sellis.
units.tr: Partium utrique assentari: to sit on two chairs.

units.la: Partium neutri assentiri] Integrum se servare.
units.tr: Partium neutri assentiri: to keep oneself whole.

units.la: Particeps] Particeps alicui rei, Curt. Particeps doloris, Cic. Consors laudis, Plaut. Compos urbis. Socius doloris, Affinis sceleris. & sceleri, Cic.
units.tr: Particeps: sharing in a thing, Curt. A partaker in sorrow, Cic. A sharer in glory, Plaut. Master of the city. A companion in sorrow; connected with crime, Cic.

units.la: Participare] Participem esse. Venire in societatem laudum, Cic. Venire in partem alicujus, Quint. Venire in sortem provinciae. In parte laboris ac periculi esse, Liv.
units.tr: Participare: to be a participant; to enter into a fellowship of praises, Cic. To come into someone's share, Quint. To receive a province by lot. To share in the labour and danger, Liv.

units.la: Participatio] Participium, Cass. Communio civitatis. Contagio belli, Cic. Participatus imperii, Spart. Capit.
units.tr: Participatio: a participle, Cass. Fellowship in citizenship; the spread of war, Cic. Sharing in power, Spart. Capit.

units.la: Particula] Portiuncula, Apul.
units.tr: Particula: a little portion, Apul.

units.la: Particulatim] Partibus, Col. Carptim, Liv. Per partes, Ulp. Partiliter, Arnob.
units.tr: Particulatim: part by part, Col. Piecemeal, Liv. By parts, Ulp. Partially, Arnob.

units.la: Partim] Ex parte gaudeo, Cic. Sed id parte curavi, ut caverem, Plaut. Vid. Tum tum.
units.tr: Partim: I rejoice in part, Cic. But I took care of this in part, so that I might guard against it, Plaut. See Tum tum.

units.la: Partim-partim] Cic. Amici me partim deseruerunt, partim prodiderunt, Plin. Flos parte flavus, parte melleus, Quintil. Interrogatio in parte expoditior, in parte difficilior, Tac. Milites pars fiducia, pars dolore, Liv. Omnes simul spernebant, simul metuebant.
units.tr: Partim-partim: Cic. My friends partly deserted me and partly betrayed me, Plin. A flower partly yellow, partly honey-coloured, Quintil. The question partly more explicit, partly more difficult, Tac. Soldiers, partly with confidence, partly with grief, Liv. They all at once despised and at once feared.

units.la: Partiri] Partes facere. In partes tribuere. Partiri in membra. Dispertiri in membra, in minima, Cic. Vid. Distribuere, dividere.
units.tr: Partiri: to make parts; to assign into parts; to divide into members; to distribute into members, into the smallest, Cic. See Distribuere, dividere.

units.la: Partitor] Distributor, Cic. Tributor. Discriminator mundi, Apul.
units.tr: Partitor: a distributor, Cic. An allotter. The divider of the world, Apul.

units.la: Partum] Collectum, Plin. Quaesitum, Ovid. Collectaneum aes, Plin. Appositum, acquisitum, Sen. Coactura, Col. Antepartum: ne antepartum demus postpartoribus, Plaut.
units.tr: Partum: collected, Plin. Sought after, Ovid. Collected money, Plin. Added, acquired, Sen. A gathering, Col. Antepartum: "do not give the earlier gains to the later claimants," Plaut.

units.la: Parta iniquè, haud diuturna] Male parta, male dilabuntur. De male quaesitis non gaudet tertius haeres. Partura] Partus, procreatio, progeneratio mularum, Satus, us,Cic. Fœtus,Col. Enixus, Genitura alitum, Generatio ovorum,Plin. Partio,Varr. Germinatio arborum.
units.tr: Parta iniquè, haud diuturna] Ill-gotten goods are ill-spent: badly got, badly lost. The third heir does not rejoice in what was badly acquired. Partura] Offspring, procreation, the breeding of mules; satus, Cic.; fœtus, Col.; a bringing forth, the generation of birds, the laying of eggs, Plin.; parturition, Varr.; the budding of trees.

units.la: Parum ] Perparum, Pauxillum, Plaut. Nimiô minus, Multò parum,Id. Paulò plus, Perpaulum, Perpaululum, Exiguè. Pusillum laxamenti,Cic. Modicè, Plin. Perhilum, Lucr.
units.tr: Parum] Far too little, a very little, Plaut.; much less, far less, Id.; a little more, very little, very slightly, sparingly, Cic.; moderately, Plin.; a tiny bit, Lucr.

units.la: Parum interest] Pluma haud interest, Plaut. Parvulum refert, Plin.Iun.
units.tr: Parum interest] A feather's weight makes no difference, Plaut.; it matters only a little, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Parum verè] Extra veritatis curriculum cursum est sæpe.
units.tr: Parum verè] One often runs beyond the course of truth.

units.la: Parum aberat, quin assequeretur] Pene scopum attigeras, Prope scopum attigeras. Propemodum attigeras scopum. Parum abfuit, ut scopum attigeris, Erasm.
units.tr: Parum aberat, quin assequeretur] You had almost hit the mark; you had nearly reached the target; you had all but attained the goal. It was a very little way off that you hit the mark, Erasm.

units.la: Parum aberat à pugnâ] Parum aberat, quin pugnarent. Minimum aberat, ut homini manus injiceret. Vix homi-nem cohibui, quò minus manus injiceret. Tantum non conserebant manus, Eras.
units.tr: Parum aberat à pugnâ] It was a very little way from fighting; they all but came to blows; he very nearly laid hands on the man; I scarcely restrained myself from laying hands on him; their hands were all but joined, Eras.

units.la: Parvus] Modicus. Corpore vesco, sed eximiis viribus, Plin. Exiguus, Tenuis, Tenuissimus,Cic. Pertenuis,Plaut. Pauxillus, Lucr. Vegrandis, Ovid. Pumilus,Apul.
units.tr: Parvus] Moderate, small. Small in body, but of remarkable strength, Plin.; slight, very slender, Cic.; very slight, Plaut.; tiny, Lucr.; very small, Ovid.; a dwarf, Apul.

units.la: Parviparva ] Molà salsa litant, qui thura non habent, Pauperis est numerare pecus.
units.tr: Parviparva] He who has no incense sacrifices with salted meal; it is the mark of a poor man to count his flock.

units.la: Parva non contemnenda] Formicæ etiam inest bilis. Capillus quoque suam umbram habet. Habet & musca splenem.
units.tr: Parva non contemnenda] Even an ant has its bile. A hair too has its shadow. A gnat also has a spleen.

units.la: Parva etiam juvant aliquid] Et quæ non prosunt singula, multa juvant. Exigua etiam scintilla in tenebris micat. Ex minimis initiis maxima.
units.tr: Parva etiam juvant aliquid] Things which do not help singly often help greatly when many. Even a tiny spark glimmers in the dark. Great things come from small beginnings.

units.la: Parva interdum prævalent magnis] A cane non magno sæpe tenetur aper. Pluvia parva magnum sæpe sedavit ventum.
units.tr: Parva interdum prævalent magnis] A boar is often caught by a dog that is not large. A small rain has often calmed a great wind.

units.la: Parvo adsvesce] Parum accipere plus est, quàm nihil omnino.
units.tr: Parvo adsvesce] To receive a little is more than to receive nothing at all.

units.la: Parvitas] Exiguitas, Exilitas, Cic. Minuties, Apul. Pumilitas gallinarum, Col.
units.tr: Parvitas] Smallness, slightness, Cic.; triviality, Apul.; the stunted size of hens, Col.

units.la: Pascalis] Pascualis ovis. Herbilis anser, Fest. Herbaticus, Vopisc. Chortinus, Plin.
units.tr: Pascalis] Of pasture: a sheep grazed on pasture; a goose fed on herbs, Fest.; of herbs, Vopisc.; of the garden, Plin.

units.la: Pascha] Dies anniversarius reviviscentis Christi. Magnus dies, Tac. Hebdomada renovationis. Quia, Christo in vitam redeunte, renovata sunt omnia.
units.tr: Pascha] The yearly day of Christ's rising to life. A great day, Tac.; the week of renewal, because, with Christ returning to life, all things were renewed.

units.la: Pascere] Servare pecudes, Ovid. Bubulcitare, Apul. Bubulcitari, Plaut. (Boves pascere.) Impascere, Com. (Compascere, vero est simul pascere.)
units.tr: Pascere] To keep flocks, Ovid.; to tend oxen like a herdsman, Apul.; to be a herdsman, Plaut. (to pasture oxen). To feed on, Com. (compascere, however, means to feed together.)

units.la: Pasci] Armenta per herbas pascebant, Ovid. Pascitare, Var. Pabulari. Impasci (i. in aliquo loco pasci) Col. Pecus carpit rura, Virg. (Compasci, vero est simul pasci, Var.)
units.tr: Pasci] They were grazing the herds through the grass, Ovid.; to graze, Var.; to be fed on; to be pastured in a place, Col.; the flock browses the fields, Virg. (compasci, however, means to feed together, Var.)

units.la: Pascua] Pastio. Pecuria, pl. Cic. Compascuus ager, Id. Bucetum, Gell. Pascuum viride, Varr. Pecuaria loca, Sipont. Pecuaria, æ, Robert. Steph.
units.tr: Pascua] Pasturage. Herds, plural, Cic.; common pasture land, Id.; grazing land, Gell.; green pasture, Varr.; pasture places, Sipont.; pastureland, Robert. Steph.

units.la: Passim, vid. Vbique.
units.tr: Passim, see Ubique.

units.la: Passio] Perpessio, Cic.
units.tr: Passio] Suffering through to the end, Cic.

units.la: Pastinare] Molliri arva ferro, Lucr.
units.tr: Pastinare] To soften fields with the iron, Lucr.

units.la: Pastinum] Pastinatio, Col. Culta nitentia. Enituit rudis campus vomere, Virg. Pectita tellus, Col.
units.tr: Pastinum] Digging of the ground, Col.; cultivated and shining fields; the rough plain has shone under the plough, Virg.; ground that has been broken up, Col.

units.la: Pastio] Pabulatio, Sipont.
units.tr: Pastio] Feeding, grazing, Sipont.

units.la: Pastor] Pecuarius. Magister pecoris, Cic. Armentarius, Varr. Ad baculum, Propert. Armenti custos.
units.tr: Pastor] A herdsman. A master of the flock, Cic.; a keeper of cattle, Varr.; one with a staff, Propert.; a guardian of the herd.

units.la: Pastoralis] Pastoritius, Cic. Pastoria pellis, Ovid. Bucolicus, Id.
units.tr: Pastoralis] Of shepherds, Cic.; a shepherd's skin, Ovid.; pastoral, Id.

units.la: Pastoralis ars] Pastoralis res. Pastoritia ars, res, Varr. Pastoritia scientia, Col. (Pastoratus, f. a.v.
units.tr: Pastoralis ars] The pastoral trade or business. The art and business of herding, Varr.; the knowledge of herding, Col. (Pastoratus, see the entry.)

units.la: Pastus. vid. Pabulum.
units.tr: Pastus, see Pabulum.

units.la: Patefacere, vid. Detegere.
units.tr: Patefacere, see Detegere.

units.la: Patens, vid. Apertus.
units.tr: Patens, see Apertus.

units.la: Paterfamilias] Paterfamiliæ, Liv. Dominus in suis ædibus: in suos, Cic. Nostri majores, Dominum patrem familiæ appellaverunt; servos, familiares, Sen. Pater domûs, Hor.
units.tr: Paterfamilias] Head of the household, Liv. The master in his own house, over his own people, Cic.; our ancestors called the master of the house the paterfamilias, and the slaves familiares, Sen.; the father of the house, Hor.

units.la: Patet aditus] Patet domus, Ter. Patent valvæ, Cic. Reclusæ fores, Ovid. Interpatet meatibus & rimis pulmo, Macrob. Patescit janua, Tibul.
units.tr: Patet aditus] The house is open, Ter.; the doors stand open, Cic.; doors unbarred, Ovid.; the lung lies open through its passages and cracks, Macrob.; the door stands open, Tibul.

units.la: Pati] Perpeti, Ferre, Sufferre, Vorare molestiam. Subire, Sustinere pœnam. Tolerare fortunam, Cic.
units.tr: Pati] To suffer through, to bear, to endure, to swallow down trouble. To undergo, to sustain punishment. To endure fortune, Cic.

units.la: Pati æquo animo] Facilè pati; non molestè. Toleranter, toleratolerabiliter, modicè, moderatè, pacatè, æquo animo, clementer, bellè, humanissimè, levissimè, patienter, mediocriter, sine dolore ferre, Cic. Modestè fert ista animus. Pati humanè, leni animo, Ter. Tolerare patienter, Quint. Rectè ferre, Plaut. Incredibili utor patientiâ, Cic.
units.tr: Pati æquo animo] To bear easily, not with vexation. To bear tolerantly, tolerably, moderately, calmly, with an even mind, gently, well, most humanely, very lightly, patiently, in moderation, without pain, Cic.; the mind bears these things with restraint, Id.; to bear humanely, with a gentle spirit, Ter.; to tolerate patiently, Quint.; to bear rightly, Plaut.; I use an incredible patience, Cic.

units.la: Patere si vis assequi] Patiar dum potiar.
units.tr: Patere si vis assequi] I will suffer, provided I may gain my end.

units.la: Patibilis ] Patibilis natura omni animali, Cic. Passivus animo, Apul. Quod passivum est, & promptum ac expositum passioni; corruptibile est, Arnob. (Passibilis.)
units.tr: Patibilis] Nature is capable of suffering in every living creature, Cic.; passive in spirit, Apul.; what is capable of suffering, and ready and exposed to suffering, is corruptible, Arnob. (passibilis.)

units.la: Patibulum ] Crux. Arbor infelix, Cic. Infelix stipes, infamis. Damnata crux, Apul. Infelix lignum, Sen. Gemoniæ scalæ. Gemonii gradus, Suet. Græcum Π.
units.tr: Patibulum] A cross. An unlucky tree, Cic.; an unlucky post, infamous; the condemned cross, Apul.; an unlucky wood, Sen.; the Gemonian stairs, the Gemonian steps, Suet. Greek Π.

units.la: Patiendum est] Accipienda & mussitanda est injuria, Virg. Superanda omnis fortuna ferendo est. Durate, & vosmet rebus servate secundis, ex eod. Tacebo æquo animo, quando virtus mea, me tacente, agit causam meam. Statutum est atque decretum omnia perpeti, quæ volet furor libidinosorum. Ore presso cervices præbebo. Hanc temporis flammam feram. Tentemus, quid patientia proficere possit. Viro forti ac sapiente dignum est, calumnias atque injurias obterere & contundere, Cic. Devorandum est, Id. Obstinata mente perfer, obdura: destinatus obdura, Catul. Durum, sed levius fit patientia, quicquid corrigere est nefas, Hor. Quod malè fers, assuesce, feres benè, Ovid. Verberat & lacerat nos fortuna? patiamur, Sen. Habendum & ferendum omne hoc est cum labore. Æquus animus optimum ærumnæ condimentum est, Plaut. Dicimus autem, Hos quoque felices, qui ferre incommoda vitæ, nec jactare jugum vitâ didicere magistrâ, Juv.
units.tr: Patiendum est] An injury must be received and kept silent, Virg.; every misfortune must be overcome by enduring it. Endure and keep yourselves for better fortune, ibid. I will keep silent with an even mind, since my virtue, while I am silent, pleads my cause. It is decided and resolved to suffer all that the frenzy of the lustful may wish. With pressed lips I will offer my neck. I will bear this flame of the time. Let us try what patience can achieve. It is worthy of a brave and wise man to trample down and crush slanders and injuries, Cic.; it must be swallowed down, Id.; bear it with a steadfast mind, harden yourself; with a fixed mind, harden yourself, Catul.; it is hard, but patience makes lighter whatever it is wrong to correct, Hor.; what you bear badly, get used to, and you will bear it well, Ovid.; does fortune beat and tear us? Let us bear it, Sen.; all this is to be held and borne with labour. An even mind is the best seasoning of distress, Plaut.; we say that those are happy too who have learned to bear the troubles of life, and not to shake off the yoke, with life as their teacher, Juv.

units.la: Patiens ] Perpessitius, Sen. Tolerans, Tolerantissimus, Cic. Benignus interpres fatorum suorum, Sen. Patientiâ præstans, Col. Perseverans, Id.
units.tr: Patiens] Long-suffering, Sen.; tolerant, very tolerant, Cic.; a gracious interpreter of his own fate, Sen.; excelling in patience, Col.; persevering, Id.

units.la: Patienter] Patientius, Ovid. Molliter ferre sapientem jubet, Cic. Toleranter, Id.
units.tr: Patienter] More patiently, Ovid.; he bids the wise man bear things gently, Cic.; tolerantly, Id.

units.la: Patientia] Tolerantia rerum humanarum. Toleratio, Perpessio diuturna, Cic. Æquanimitas, Plin. Vitæ antidotum. Ærumnæ condimentum. Malorum remedium. Gaudens duris.
units.tr: Patientia] Tolerance of human affairs. Endurance, long-lasting suffering, Cic.; equanimity, Plin.; the antidote of life; the seasoning of distress; the remedy for evils; rejoicing in hardships.

units.la: Patientia læsa ] Bonus animus læsus gravius multò irascitur. Furor læsa sæpius patientia.
units.tr: Patientia læsa] A good spirit, when wounded, is roused to far greater anger. Patience that has been often injured turns to fury.

units.la: Patina] Patella grandis, Cic. Magida, Varr. Magis, idis, Iun. Lanx, Plaut.
units.tr: Patina] A large dish, Cic.; a pan, Varr.; a dish, Iun.; a platter, Plaut.

units.la: Patrare, vid. Exsequi. Perpetrare.
units.tr: Patrare, see Exsequi, Perpetrare.

units.la: Patria ] Terra, quæ te genuit & aluit, Liv. Natale solum, Ovid. Genitalis terra, Amm.
units.tr: Patria] The land which bore you and nourished you, Liv.; the native soil, Ovid.; the land of one's birth, Amm.

units.la: Patrimonialis ] Paterna bona. Res patriæ & avitæ. Avita & patrita Philosophia, Cic. Patrius pavor, Lucr.
units.tr: Patrimonialis] Paternal goods. Property of the fatherland and of the grandfathers. Philosophy handed down from ancestors and fathers, Cic.; ancestral dread, Lucr.

units.la: Patrimonium ] Res paterna, Hor. Res patria; res patrita, Cic.
units.tr: Patrimonium] Paternal property, Hor.; ancestral property; inherited property, Cic.

units.la: Patrius] Patrius sermo. Nativus, Lucr. Natalis, Ovid. Genitalis, Amm.
units.tr: Patrius] Ancestral speech. Native, Lucr.; natal, Ovid.; native, Amm.

units.la: Patrocinium, vid. Defensio.
units.tr: Patrocinium, see Defensio.

units.la: Patronus] Amicus magnus, Cic. Rex meus. Is fundus est mihi, Plaut. Vid. Defensor.
units.tr: Patronus] A great friend, Cic.; my king; that is my estate, Plaut. See Defensor.

units.la: Patronus studiorum] Mecoenas, Hor. Musageta.
units.tr: Patronus studiorum] Maecenas, Hor.; leader of the Muses.

units.la: Paucitas ] Infrequentia. Senatus, Cic. Res parva voluptatum, Plaut.
units.tr: Paucitas] Thinness of attendance. A senate of small numbers, Cic.; a small amount of pleasures, Plaut.

units.la: Paucus ] Pauculi dies. Perpauculi passus. Parva copia poëtarum. Non ita multi, Cic. Perpauci, pauxilluli, Cic. Apparent rari nantes in gurgite vasto. Numero vix sunt totidem, quot Tebarum portæ, vel divitis ostia Nili. Pauci quos æquus amavit Jupiter, aut ardens evexit ad æthera virtus, Virg. Pauxilla ossa, Lucr. Modica pecunia, Cic. Res parva voluptatum. Tot sunt, quot ego & tu, Plaut.
units.tr: Paucus] A few days. A very few paces. A small store of poets. Not so many, Cic.; very few, a small handful, Cic. Few swimmers appear, scattered on the vast whirlpool. They are hardly as many in number as the gates of Thebes or the mouths of the rich Nile. Few are those whom the just Jupiter has loved, or whom burning virtue has raised to the stars, Virg.; small bones, Lucr.; a modest sum of money, Cic.; a small store of pleasures. There are as many as you and I, Plaut.

units.la: Paucis verbis] Paucis, Lucr. Tribus verbis, Plaut. Numero dicere. Uno verbo. Ut summatim dicam. Ut te absolvam. Vid. Breviter loqui.
units.tr: Paucis verbis] In a few words, Lucr.; in three words, Plaut.; to speak by count; in one word; to sum up briefly; to give you the gist. See Breviter loqui.

units.la: Pavescere, vid. Timere.
units.tr: Pavescere, see Timere.

units.la: Pavire, vid. Fistucare.
units.tr: Pavire, see Fistucare.

units.la: Pavitus, vid. Fistucatus. Paulatim ] Sensim. Lentè venire, Plin. Lentissimè, Col. Placidè pulsa. Ductim liquorem in me invergo. Clementer, Plaut. Pedetentim, Cic. Pedepressim, Non. Excommodo, Sen. Minutatim, Varr.
units.tr: Pavitus, see Fistucatus. Paulatim] Gradually. To come slowly, Plin.; most slowly, Col.; struck gently; I pour the liquid into myself in a trickle; mildly, Plaut.; step by step, Cic.; step by step, Non.; by degrees, Sen.; little by little, Varr.

units.la: Paulisper] Ad tempus. Ad breve, ad brevissimum tempus. Ad punctum temporis. Parumper abducere, Cic. Ad praesens, Plin. Nunc te marmoreum pro tempore fecimus, Virg. Vid. Exiguum.
units.tr: Paulisper] For a time. For a short, very short time. For a moment. To lead aside for a little while, Cic.; for the present, Plin.; now for the time we have made you a figure of marble, Virg. See Exiguum.

units.la: Paulò, vid. Parum.
units.tr: Paulò, see Parum.

units.la: Pavo]Pavus, Gell. Junonia avis, Ovid. Avis gloriosa & malitiosa, Plin. Medica avis, Varr. Multicolor, & Versicolor, & discolor.
units.tr: Pavo] A peacock, Gell.; the Juno bird, Ovid.; a glorious and malicious bird, Plin.; the Median bird, Varr.; many-coloured, both varicoloured and of differing colours.

units.la: Pavor] Pavitas, Apul. Metus loco movens mentem,Cic.
units.tr: Pavor] Fearfulness, Apul.; fear that moves the mind from its place, Cic.

units.la: Pauper] Pauperrimus,Hor. Tenuis homo. Perpauper,Cic. Inops fortunae, Tac. Modicus facultatibus, Plin. Iun. Res nostrae sunt pauperculae, Plaut. Paupertinus, Varr. Paupertas,propauperib. Plaut. Pauperculus, Id. Penuriâ pauperior. Iro pauperior, Er.
units.tr: Pauper] Very poor, Hor.; a poor man of slender means. Very poor, Cic.; poor in fortune, Tac.; moderate in means, Plin. Iun.; our affairs are rather meagre, Plaut.; poverty-stricken, Varr.; poverty, very poor, Plaut.; rather poor, Id.; poorer than penury; poorer than Irus, Er.

units.la: Extremè pauper] Homo sine censu. Extremè egenus. Infima plebs. Codrus ; de quo Iuv. Tota domus Codri rhedâ componitur unâ. Leberide nudior. Doliaris vita. (Diogenes in dolio habitabat.) Omnem facultatem indutus est. Omnia sua secum portat. Egomet vix vitam colo, Plaut. Capite census. Egestate perditus. Ne symbolum quidem habet.
units.tr: Extremely poor: a man without property rating, extremely needy, of the lowest common people. Codrus, of whom Juvenal says: "The whole household of Codrus fits in one cart." Barer than a Leberis. A barrel-life (Diogenes lived in a tub). He has put on every kind of want. He carries all his belongings with him. Plautus: "I scarcely keep body and soul together." Rated by head count alone. Ruined by want. He cannot even pay his share of the bill.

units.la: Pauper ab omnibus negligitur] Pauper ubique jacet, pauperi nullus cognatus, pauperi ne parentes quidem amici, paupertas omnibus invisa. Vulgus amicitias utilitate probat.
units.tr: The poor are neglected by all: The poor man lies low everywhere. The poor have no kinsman, and not even parents count the poor as friends. Poverty is hated by everyone. The crowd measures friendships by their usefulness.

units.la: Pauperare aliquem ] Depauperare, Varr. Mendicitatem alicui offerre, Varr. Detrudere ad mendicitatem. Ad incitas redigere aliquem, Plaut. Afferre alicui egestatem, Cicer. Redigere ad inopiam, Terent. Accidere res alicujus, Liv. Attenuare opes, Ovid. Laceravi validè rem meam,Plaut.
units.tr: To impoverish someone: To strip of property, Varro. To bring beggary upon someone, Varro. To thrust someone into beggary. To reduce someone to rags, Plautus. To bring want upon someone, Cicero. To reduce to penury, Terence. To let someone's affairs fall to ruin, Livy. To diminish one's means, Ovid. "I have badly damaged my property," Plautus.

units.la: Pauperari] Ab re perire, Plaut. Labi facultatibus. Incessit eum inopia, Vlp. Comminui re familiari. Vix aliquod pristini splendoris vestigium obtinet, Cic. Ad rastros illi res rediit, Ter. Res, opes, fortunæ ejus modicæ, affectæ, imminutæ, adesæ, attritæ, accisæ sunt, Cic. Liv. Non eadem fortuna viro, non opes antiquæ. Res ejus exiguæ. Copiolæ extenuatissimæ. Ad manticam illi res rediit. Redactus ad inopiam, ex Ter.
units.tr: To become poor: To perish in one's property, Plautus. To slip from one's means. Want has come upon him, Ulpian. To be worn down in household affairs. He scarcely keeps any trace of his former splendour, Cicero. His property has come back to the rake, Terence. His property, resources and fortune have been diminished, reduced, eaten away, worn down and cut back, Cicero, Livy. His fortune is no longer what it was, nor his wealth what it once was. His estate is small. His little stock is very slender. His property has returned to the beggar's knapsack. Reduced to want, from Terence.

units.la: Paupertas] Pauperies, Virg. Tenuitas, Cic. Res pauperculæ, modicæ, egenæ. Malæ res, Plaut. Incitæ, Id. Parva domi fortuna, Propert.
units.tr: Poverty: Poverty, Virgil. Slender means, Cicero. Small, modest, needy circumstances. Bad circumstances, Plautus. Straitened means, Plautus. A small fortune at home, Propertius.

units.la: Paupertas tuta] Pauperes à dispendio tuti. Nulla venena bibuntur fictilibus. Cantabit vacuus coram latrone viator. Paupertas securitatis parens.
units.tr: Poverty is safe: The poor are safe from loss. No poisons are drunk from earthenware. The traveller with an empty purse will sing in the presence of the robber. Poverty is the parent of safety.

units.la: Paupertas ad aliquid bona est] Docet artes egestas. Fames magistra. Paupertas sapientiæ mater. (quia aliquid excogitare cogit.) Paupertas sapientiam sortita est.
units.tr: Poverty is good for something: Want teaches the arts. Hunger is the teacher. Poverty is the mother of wisdom, because it forces a man to devise something. Poverty has won wisdom by lot.

units.la: Pausa, vid. Cessatio.
units.tr: Pausa, see Cessatio.

units.la: Pauxillatim] Pauxillisper, Plaut. Unciatim, Ter. Frustillatim, Plaut. Minutatim ætas frangit vires, Lucr. Scrupulatim, Plin.
units.tr: Little by little: For a little while, Plautus. Ounce by ounce, Terence. In small bits, Plautus. Age breaks down strength bit by bit, Lucretius. Scruple by scruple, Pliny.

units.la: Pax] Paces, Varr. Pacibus, Plaut. Laurus quietis, indicium, Plin. Otium. Toga, Cic. Malacia, Sen.
units.tr: Peace: Peaces, Varro. With peaceful gifts, Plautus. The laurel as a sign of quiet, Pliny. Leisure. The gown of peace, Cicero. Calm at sea, Seneca.

units.la: Pax litipræferenda] Felix qui non litigat. Cum licet fugere, ne quæras litem. Nemo ita amens est, ut bellum quàm pacem præoptet. Nam in pace filii patres, in bello patres filios sepeliunt, Præf. apud. Herod.
units.tr: Peace is to be preferred to a lawsuit: Happy is he who does not go to law. When you can get away, do not seek a lawsuit. No one is so mad as to prefer war to peace; for in peace sons bury their fathers, but in war fathers bury their sons, Preface to Herodotus.

units.la: Pacem quâ datur redime] Perde aliquid, ut habeas quietum tempus. Pax optima rerum, quas homini novisse datum est. Pax una Triumphis innumeris potior.
units.tr: Buy peace where it is offered: Lose something so that you may have a quiet time. Peace is the best of all things that man has been granted to know. One peace is worth more than countless triumphs.

units.la: Pax publica] Concordia regum, felicitas temporum.
units.tr: Public peace: The harmony of kings, the happiness of the times.

units.la: Peccare] Delinquere, Cicer. Delictum admittere, Ter. Culpam admittere, Liv. Commereri culpam, Plaut.
units.tr: To sin: To offend, Cicero. To commit a fault, Terence. To incur guilt, Livy. To earn blame, Plautus.

units.la: Peccare iterum] Canis ad vomitum. Sus ad volutabrum. Impingere ad eundem lapidem.
units.tr: To sin again: The dog returns to its vomit. The sow to its wallow. To stumble over the same stone.

units.la: Peccator utrinque] Iliacos intra muros peccatur & extra, Hor.
units.tr: The sinner on every side: Within and outside the walls of Troy men sin, Horace.

units.la: Peccator non effugiet pænam] Reperit Deus nocentem, tem, Lucan. Raro antecedentem scelestum deseruit poena pede claudo, Hor.
units.tr: The sinner will not escape punishment: God finds the guilty one, Lucan. Seldom does punishment, though lame of foot, fail to overtake the wicked man who goes before, Horace.

units.la: Peccatum] Peccamen, Prudent. Labes & vulnus conscientiæ. Noxa, Cic. Admissum, Lucr. Commissum turpe, Hor. Lapsus animi.
units.tr: Sin: A sin, Prudentius. The stain and wound of conscience. An offence, Cicero. A deed committed, Lucretius. A shameful deed committed, Horace. A slip of the mind.

units.la: Peccatum originale] Originale crimen, Macrob. Primigenia noxa. Capitale principum parentum admissum, Bud. Nativa labes.
units.tr: Original sin: Original crime, Macrobius. First-born offence. The capital offence committed by our first parents, Budé. Innate stain.

units.la: Peccatum alienum luere] Canis peccatum suus dependit.
units.tr: To pay for another's sin: The dog pays for its own sin.

units.la: Peccatum superiorum, pœna inferiorum] Quicquid delirant Reges plectuntur Achivi.
units.tr: The sin of superiors, the punishment of inferiors: Whatever the kings rave about, the Achaeans are punished.

units.la: Pecten] Pectunculus. Buxus multifido dente, Mart. Dens eburnus numerosus, Claud.
units.tr: Comb: A little comb. Boxwood with a many-toothed comb, Martial. An ivory comb with numerous teeth, Claudian.

units.la: Pectere ] Depectere crines, Ovid. Perpexa barba, Firm.
units.tr: To comb: To comb the hair out, Ovid. A combed beard, Firmicus.

units.la: Pectinatim] Pectinato ordine dentium, Amm. Serratim, Vitruv.
units.tr: Like a comb: In the comb-like order of teeth, Ammianus. Like a saw, Vitruvius.

units.la: Pectorale ] Tegimen, vel, tegumen pectoris, Liv. Thorax, Iuv. Sueton.
units.tr: Breastplate: A covering, or covering of the breast, Livy. A cuirass, Juvenal, Suetonius.

units.la: Pectus] Thorax, Plin. Templa mentis, Lucr. Sedes mentis, Præcordia, Lamb.
units.tr: Breast: The chest, Pliny. The temples of the mind, Lucretius. The seat of the mind; the midriff, Lambinus.

units.la: Pecuarius] Pecorinus, Sipont. Veterinarius, Arnob. Jumentarius, Apul.
units.tr: Pastoral: Of sheep, Sipontinus. Veterinary, Arnobius. Of beasts of burden, Apuleius.

units.la: Peculiaris, vid. Proprius. Singularis.
units.tr: Peculiar, see Proprius, Singularis.

units.la: Pecunia] Æs; æra, Hor. Argentum, Aurum, Plin. Lamella argenti, Sen. Copia rei nummariæ, Suet. Res, Lucr. Nervus belli pecunia. Res numaria, Cicer. Nervus rerum agendarum. Argentum hominibus, sanguis & anima, Antiphan. Vita pecunia est, Pindar. Æs signatum, Plin. Res nummorum. Pararium æs. Vid. Nummi.
units.tr: Money: Bronze; coins, Horace. Silver, gold, Pliny. A silver plate, Seneca. A plenty of coin, Suetonius. Goods, Lucretius. Money is the sinew of war. Monetary matter, Cicero. The sinew of affairs. Silver is to men blood and life, Antiphanes. Life is money, Pindar. Bronze stamped with a mark, Pliny. Matter of coins. Ready bronze. See Coins.

units.la: Pecunia præsens] Præsentarium argentum, Plaut. Numeratum, Cic. Numerata talenta, Plaut. Repræsentatione emere. Explicare repræsentatione, Cicer. Repræsentare pecuniam, Id.
units.tr: Ready money: Ready silver, Plautus. Counted out, Cicero. Counted talents, Plautus. To buy with ready payment. To explain by payment in hand, Cicero. To pay money in hand, Cicero.

units.la: Pecunia super omnia]
units.tr: Money above all things:

units.la: Mundus hic est pelagus, regina Pecunia nauta est: Navigat infelix, qui caret hujus ope.
units.tr: This world is a sea, and Queen Money is its sailor; he sails unhappily who lacks her help.

units.la: Pecuniæ quò minùs habetur, tantò minùs desideratur] Tanto quisque minùs optat pecuniam, quantò minus possidet pecuniæ, Eras.
units.tr: The less money is had, the less it is desired: Each man desires money the less, the less of it he possesses, Erasmus.

units.la: Voluptates pluris facit, quàm pecuniam] Magis avidus voluptatis, quàm pecuniæ. Avidior voluptatum, quàm pecuniæ. Minùs avidus pecuniæ, quàm voluptatum, Erasm.
units.tr: He values pleasures more than money: More greedy for pleasure than for money. More eager for pleasures than for money. Less greedy for money than for pleasures, Erasmus.

units.la: Pecuniam plus amat, quàm famam] Magis amat pecuniam, quàm famam. Pecuniæ amans est magis, quàm famæ. Pecuniæ amantior est, quàm famæ. Famam pecuniæ posthabet. Famæ pecuniam anteponit. Minùs famæ cupiditate ducitur, quàm pecuniæ. Impensiùs amat pecuniam, quàm famam. Huic potior est pecunia, quàm fama. Huic prius est lucrum, quàm honesta fama. Huic vilior est vita, quàm pecunia, Eras.
units.tr: He loves money more than fame: He loves money more than fame. He is a greater lover of money than of fame. He is fonder of money than of fame. He puts fame after money. He puts money before fame. He is driven less by the desire for fame than by the desire for money. He loves money more eagerly than fame. For him money matters more than fame. For him gain comes before honest reputation. For him life is cheaper than money, Erasmus.

units.la: Pecuniam colligere] Conficere pecuniam de vectigalibus. Redigere pecuniam ex. Facere maximam, innumerabilem pecuniam. Corrogare nummos de bonis. Cogere pecuniam, Cic.
units.tr: To collect money: To raise money from taxes. To bring in money from. To make a great, countless sum of money. To scrape money together from goods. To gather money, Cicero.

units.la: Pecuniam erogare ad aliquid emendum] Calcearium verò, Calcearii nomine dare, Suet. Meurs. Pecuniam classis nomine imperare, Cicer. Pecuniam dare calceis (& aliis id genus] emendis, Dare æs calceis permutandis. Calceis æs cum sutore mutare.
units.tr: To spend money on buying something: To give money under the name of shoes, Suetonius, Meursius. To levy money under the name of the fleet, Cicero. To give money for shoes and things of that sort to be bought. To give bronze to exchange for shoes. To swap bronze with the cobbler for shoes.

units.la: Pecuniæ obediunt omnia] Pecunia impetrat omnia. Pecunia nervus est rerum gerendarum. Et genus, & formam regina pecunia donat, Hor. Nummis omnia venalia. Pecuniosus damnari non potest. Si quid habes, viges; si nihil, jaces.
units.tr: All things obey money: Money obtains everything. Money is the sinew of affairs. Queen Money gives both family and beauty, Horace. Everything is for sale for coin. A man of money cannot be condemned. If you have something you thrive; if you have nothing, you lie low.

units.la: Pecuniosus] Nummatus, peculiatus. Benè peculiatus. Habet in sumptum, Cic. Nummosus, Gell. Valet à pecunia, Plaut. Præmiosus, Fest.
units.tr: Wealthy: Rich in coin, well-heeled. Well supplied with money. He has it for expenses, Cicero. Full of money, Gellius. Strong through money, Plautus. Prize-winning, Festus.

units.la: Pecus] Jumenta & pecuda, Cic. Pecu, pl. Pecua, Plaut. Plin. Ignavum pecus, Virg. Quadrupes, Varr. Grex triginta capitum, Col. Res pecuaria, Cic. Pecuaria, pecudum genus omne, Virg.
units.tr: Livestock: Beasts of burden and cattle, Cicero. Cattle, plural cattle, Plautus, Pliny. A lazy herd, Virgil. A four-footed beast, Varro. A flock of thirty head, Columella. Stock-farming, Cicero. Pastoral: every kind of herd, Virgil.

units.la: Pedamentum] Pedamen teres, Col. Ridica, palus, Varr. Statumen maritandis vitibus, Col. Ulmus maritus, Catul. Virga, pertica, furca, hastile, sudes, calamus in vineis, Virg.
units.tr: Stake: A smooth vine-prop, Columella. A pole, a stake, Varro. A support for setting vines, Columella. An elm as husband to the vine, Catullus. A rod, pole, fork, shaft, stake, or reed in the vineyards, Virgil.

units.la: Pedatim, vid. Lente.
units.tr: Step by step, see Slowly.

units.la: Pedatio] Arundulatio, Varr. Subligatio uvarum, Pallad. Ligatura, Id.
units.tr: Staking: Tying of reeds, Varro. Binding of the vines, Palladius. Binding, Palladius.

units.la: Pedes] Pedarius, Cic. Pedaneus, Vlp. Pedestris. Manipularis, Cicer. Commanipularis, Commanipulo, Spart. (Servus.)
units.tr: Foot: Of the foot, Cicero. Pedaneous, Ulpian. Pedestrian. Of a maniple, Cicero. Fellow-maniple, Spartianus. (A slave.)

units.la: Pedestri itinere] Pedes ibat, Virg. Pedibus ire, Cicer. Pedester profectus est, Apul. Incedere pedes, Liv. Metamur gradibus militaribus, Plaut.
units.tr: By land march: He went on foot, Virgil. To go on foot, Cicero. He set out on foot, Apuleius. To advance on foot, Livy. We measure with soldiers' paces, Plautus.

units.la: Pedetentim, vid. Paulatim.
units.tr: Gradually, see Paulatim.

units.la: Pedica, vid. Laqueus.
units.tr: Snare, see Noose.

units.la: Pediculosus] Pedicosus, Titin. Pedicularis, Col.
units.tr: Lousy: Lousy, Titinius. Of lice, Columella.

units.la: Pediculus] Pes, Varr. Serpens. Animalia capillorum, Plin.
units.tr: Louse: Foot, Varro. A creeping thing. Creatures of the hair, Pliny.

units.la: Pedissequa, vid. Ancilla.
units.tr: Waiting-woman, see Maidservant.

units.la: Peditatus] Pedites. Pedestres copiae, Cicer. Pedestris acies, Liv. Pedestris militia, Amm. Manipulares, Plin.
units.tr: Infantry: Foot soldiers. Foot forces, Cicero. A line of infantry, Livy. Foot service, Ammianus. Maniple men, Pliny.

units.la: Pejerare] Pejerare conceptis verbis, Cicer. Perjurare, Plaut. Perfidum ducere sacramentum, Hor. Perjerare, Lips. Taubm.
units.tr: To swear falsely: To swear falsely in set words, Cicero. To perjure oneself, Plautus. To regard an oath as a breach of faith, Horace. To perjure, Lipsius, Taubmann.

units.la: Pejor] Deterior, Cic. Sequior fortuna, Amm.
units.tr: Worse: Inferior, Cicero. A worse fortune, Ammianus.

units.la: Pejora nancisci] De foece haurire.
units.tr: To get worse: To drain from the dregs.

units.la: Pejùs] Deteriùs scripta, Cicer. Sequiùs, vel seccius, Tacit.
units.tr: Worse (adverb): Written more badly, Cicero. More harshly, or more sharply, Tacitus.

units.la: Pellere] Propellere, Repellere, Depellere famem. Fugare, Expellere, Exterminare, Exigere, Cic. Propulsare hostem, Caes. Protelare, Fest. Appellere, Plaut.
units.tr: To drive: To drive away, to repel, to drive off hunger. To put to flight, expel, exterminate, exact, Cicero. To repel an enemy, Caesar. To keep off, Festus. To drive to, Plautus.

units.la: Pellere vi] Expellere furcâ, Hor.
units.tr: To drive by force: To drive out with a pitchfork, Horace.

units.la: Pelles] Pelliceum, vid. Pellicium stragulum, Paul. IC.
units.tr: Skins: A fur coat, see Pellicium; a coverlet of skins, Paulus, jurist.

units.la: Pellex, vid. Concubina.
units.tr: Concubine, see Mistress.

units.la: Pellicere, vid. Illicere.
units.tr: To entice, see To allure.

units.la: Pellio] Pellarius, Firm. Bracharius, Lampr.
units.tr: Furrier: Skinner, Firmicus. Breeches-maker, Lampridius.

units.la: Pellis] Corium, Salust. Exuviae leonis, Virg. Spolium ferarum, Ovid. Tergus, Virg.
units.tr: Skin: Hide, Sallust. The skin of a lion, Virgil. The spoil of wild beasts, Ovid. Back, hide, Virgil.

units.la: Pellucere] Perlucet villa crebrius quàm cribrum, Plaut. Interlucet corona rara viris. Potes per illum videre, Virg. Interpatet rimis pulmo, Macrob. Translucet gemma, Plin. Transpicitur aliquid, Lucr.
units.tr: To shine through: The house shows light through more often than a sieve, Plautus. A thin crown of flowers gleams among the men. You can see through him, Virgil. The lung is visible through the chinks, Macrobius. The gem shines through, Pliny. Something is seen through, Lucretius.

units.la: Pelluciditas] Perluciditas vitri, Vitr. Limpitudo, Plin.
units.tr: Transparency: The clearness of glass, Vitruvius. Clearness, Pliny.

units.la: Pellucidus] Pellucidulus lapillus, Catul. Translucens, Translucidus. Pertranslucida charta, Plin. Liquidus aër, Virg. Liquidiusculus, Plaut. Perspicuus, Mart. Pellucens amictus, Ovid. Perspicibilis splendor solis, Vitr. Limpidus lacus, Catul. Clarus, Ovid.
units.tr: Transparent: A little transparent pebble, Catullus. Translucent. Paper that is quite transparent, Pliny. Clear air, Virgil. Rather clear, Plautus. Clear, Martial. A see-through cloak, Ovid. The visible brightness of the sun, Vitruvius. A clear lake, Catullus. Bright, Ovid.

units.la: Pelvis] Aqualis, Varr. Concha ærea, Amm. Concha ferrea, Plin. Sinus aquarius, Non. Trulleum, Varr. Trullium, Cat. Pollubrum, Liv. Trulleus, Arnob. Pelluvium, Fest. Trua, Varr.
units.tr: Pelvis: a water-vessel, Varr.; a bronze basin, Amm.; an iron basin, Plin.; a water-tub, Non.; a small wash-bowl, Varr.; a wash-bowl, Cat.; a basin, Liv.; a washing-bowl, Arnob.; a wash-basin, Fest.; a bowl, Varr.

units.la: Pendere] Dependere collo. Suspendere, Col. Appensum esse, Cicer. Præpendere, Mart. Pendere ex, in arbore, ab humero, Cic. Pendere de, à, Virg.
units.tr: Pendere: to hang from the neck. To hang up, Col. To be suspended, Cicer. To hang down, Mart. To hang from a tree or from the shoulder, Cic. To hang from or of, Virg.

units.la: Pendulus] Pensilis uva, Hor. Propenduli crines, Apul. Apta è lacertis brachia, Lucr.
units.tr: Pendulus: grapes hanging on the vine, Hor. Dangling tresses, Apul. Arms fitted to the upper arms, Lucr.

units.la: Penè, vid. Ferè.
units.tr: Penè, see Ferè.

units.la: Penes, vid. Apul.
units.tr: Penes, see Apul.

units.la: Penetrabilis] Vibrans oratio, Cicer. Meabilis per omnia rerum spiritus, Plin. Manabile frigus, Lucr. Oxypora antidota, Plin.
units.tr: Penetrabilis: a vibrant speech, Cicer. A spirit that passes through all things of nature, Plin. A creeping cold, Lucr. Sharp-piercing antidotes, Plin.

units.la: Penetrare] Penetrare cœlum, per cœlum, in cœlum. Permeat & transit per omnia intelligentia. Vibrant fulmina. Tranat ignis, Cicer. Permanat ad ossa frigus. Travolat vitri species foramina. Traviat ignis aliquid, Lucr. Persidit ad vivum humor, Virg. Transabit costas ensis, Id.
units.tr: Penetrare: to penetrate heaven, through heaven, into heaven. It passes through and permeates all understanding. Lightnings pierce. Fire swims through, Cicer. Cold seeps into the bones. The image of glass flies through its pores. Fire penetrates something, Lucr. Moisture sinks down to the quick, Virg. The sword will pierce the ribs, Id.

units.la: Penetrare ad cor] In venis medullisque insidere. Aculeos in animos relinquere.
units.tr: Penetrare ad cor: to settle into the veins and marrow. To leave stings in the minds.

units.la: Penicillus] Penicillum, Quint. Penis, Nav.
units.tr: Penicillus: a painter's brush, Quint. A tail, Nav.

units.la: Penitus] Prorsùm, Ter. Prorsus. In omne tempus. Planè non intellexi ænigma. Planè benè. Omnino. Funditus interiere, Cic. In totum, Quint. Ex toto, Sen. Per omnia, Col. Absolutè, Gell. Abruptè, Macrob.
units.tr: Penitus: straight forward, Ter. Quite, wholly. In omne tempus: for all time. I did not understand the riddle at all. Quite well. Altogether. They perished utterly, Cic. Entirely, Quint. From the whole, Sen. In all things, Col. Absolutely, Gell. Abruptly, Macrob.

units.la: Penna] Pinna, Col. Pluma, Virg.
units.tr: Penna: a wing, Col. A feather, Virg.

units.la: Pennatus] Pinnata cauda, Cic. Plumato corpore, Id. Plumosus. Penniger anser, Plin. Pennifer, Liv.
units.tr: Pennatus: with a feathered tail, Cic. With a feathered body, Id. Feathered. A feather-bearing goose, Plin. Feather-bearing, Liv.

units.la: Pensabilis ] Reparabile damnum, Ovid. Revocabile damnum, Amm.
units.tr: Pensabilis: a loss that can be repaired, Ovid. A loss that can be recalled, Amm.

units.la: Pensare aliquid] Quod corporis viribus deest, id ingenii dolis exæqua. Quod corporis formæ detractum, id animi dotibus natura pensabit. Tu opulentior, nos eruditiores, atque ita paria fecimus. Absentiam nostram crebris literis sarciamus. Quod hactenus cessatum est, id oportet diligentiâ recuperare. Quod illius stultitiâ peccatum est, id tuâ sapientiâ restituas oportet. Quod illius inscitia admissum est, id oportet ut tuâ prudentiâ redimas. Supplendum diligentiâ, quod ingenio deest. Quod corpori detractum, id ingenii dotibus accessit, Eras.
units.tr: Pensare aliquid: what is lacking in bodily strength, make up for with the tricks of wit. What has been taken from bodily beauty, nature will make up with gifts of the mind. You are richer, we are more learned, and so we have made things equal. Let us make up for our absence with frequent letters. What has been neglected until now, it is right to recover with diligence. What was sinned through his folly, you should make good by your wisdom. What was committed through his ignorance, you ought to redeem by your prudence. What is lacking in ability must be supplied by diligence. What was taken from the body has been added in gifts of the mind, Erasmus.

units.la: Pensat vicem, vid. Est pro.
units.tr: Pensat vicem, see Est pro.

units.la: Pensum] Justa, pl. Col. Diurnum, Sen. Angaria, Veget.
units.tr: Pensum: a due portion, pl., Col. A daily task, Sen. Forced labour, Veget.

units.la: Penu ] Penaria, Varr. Penarium, Fest. Cella penaria, Cic. Cella penuaria, Suet. Promptuarium, Cat. Apotheca, Col.
units.tr: Penu: a larder, Varr. A store-room, Fest. A larder room, Cic. A store-room, Suet. A storeroom, Cat. A storehouse, Col.

units.la: Penula] Pænula gausapina, Scortea, & Scortea, abs. Mart. Lacerna, Id. Chlamys, Plaut.
units.tr: Penula: a shaggy woollen cloak; a leather cloak, abl., Mart. A cloak, Id. A cape, Plaut.

units.la: Penuria, vid. Egestas.
units.tr: Penuria, see Egestas.

units.la: Pepo, vid. Melon.
units.tr: Pepo, see Melon.

units.la: Per se, vel per alium ] Beneficio meo. Bono literarum utemur. Per se, & suâ sponte movetur. Per literas colloqui, Cic.
units.tr: Per se, vel per alium: by my good offices. We shall use the good of letters. It moves of itself and by its own accord. To converse by letters, Cic.

units.la: Per tot annos] Inter, intra tot annos. Bidui aberam, Cic. Toto orbe diffusos Britannos, Virg.
units.tr: Per tot annos: within, during so many years. I was away for two days, Cic. The Britons, spread over the whole world, Virg.

units.la: Pera] Perula, Sen. Mantica, Perf. Manticula, Fest.
units.tr: Pera: a little bag, Sen. A wallet, Perf. A little wallet, Fest.

units.la: Peragere, vid. Absolvere, Finire.
units.tr: Peragere, see Absolve, Finish.

units.la: Peractum negotium ] Facta transacta omnia, Ter.
units.tr: Peractum negotium: all affairs done and transacted, Ter.

units.la: Peragrare] Spatiari per Ægyptum, Plin. Oppida circumvecturi, Plaut. Volitare per gentes. Res rusticas delectationis causâ invisere, Cic.
units.tr: Peragrare: to wander through Egypt, Plin. To be carried around the towns, Plaut. To fly through nations. To visit country estates for pleasure, Cic.

units.la: Percellere]Percussit illico animum, Ter. Strinxit animum, Virg. Horrore perstringi, Liv. Præstringere oculos, Cic. Perstringere, stringere, Hor. Vulnerare aliquem voce, Cicer. Percire, vel perciere, Lucr. Confutabat meum obtutum vestis flam-mida, Apul.
units.tr: Percellere: it struck his mind at once, Ter. It touched his mind, Virg. To be struck with horror, Liv. To dazzle the eyes, Cic. To graze, to touch, Hor. To wound someone with words, Cicer. To stir up or rouse, Lucr. The flame-coloured dress confused my gaze, Apul.

units.la: Percellere aliquem, vid. Exterrere.
units.tr: Percellere aliquem, see Terrify.

units.la: Percensere, vid. Enumerare.
units.tr: Percensere, see Enumerate.

units.la: Perceptio, vid. Intelligentia.
units.tr: Perceptio, see Understanding.

units.la: Percipere, vid. Intelligere.
units.tr: Percipere, see Understand.

units.la: Percontari, Percontatio, vid. Interrog.
units.tr: Percontari, Percontatio, see Interrogate.

units.la: Percontator] Rogator, Cic.
units.tr: Percontator: a questioner, Cic.

units.la: Percurrere] Percurrere aliquid cursu, Lucr. Transcurrere coelum. Transmittere cursu. Carpere prata fuga. Emetiri iter, Virg. Permetiri, Cicer. Transire campus pedibus, Lucr. Perlabi, Sil. Pervulgant sidera coelum, Pacuv.
units.tr: Percurrere: to run over something in a course, Lucr. To run across the sky. To pass through by running. To seize the meadows in flight. To measure out a journey, Virg. To measure through, Cicer. To cross the plain on foot, Lucr. To glide through, Sil. The stars spread across the sky, Pacuv.

units.la: Percussio, vid. Ictus.
units.tr: Percussio, see Blow.

units.la: Percutere, vid. Ferire.
units.tr: Percutere, see Strike.

units.la: Perdere] Ire perditum, Ter. Afferre perniciem, exitium, pestem alicui, Cicer. Dare exitio. Sepelire salutem, Lucr. Universum genus ad occisionem perducere, Col. Agnos canibus objicere. Pessum dare. Vid. Amittere, Abolere.
units.tr: Perdere: to go to ruin, Ter. To bring destruction, ruin or plague upon someone, Cicer. To give over to ruin. To bury safety, Lucr. To lead the whole race to slaughter, Col. To throw sheep to the dogs. To cast down to ruin. See Lose, Destroy.

units.la: Perditè, vid. Desperanter.
units.tr: Perditè, see Desperately.

units.la: Perditio, vid. Amissio.
units.tr: Perditio, see Loss.

units.la: Perditus] Prodita summa rerum, Lucr. Omnia ad perniciem profligata & perdita. Judicata atque damnata causa. Convicta & damnata. Amissæ ac perditæ classes. Obrutæ ac perditæ res, Cic. In perdito est, Sen.
units.tr: Perditus: the sum of affairs betrayed, Lucr. All things driven headlong to ruin and lost. A case judged and condemned. Convicted and condemned. Fleets lost and destroyed. Affairs overwhelmed and ruined, Cic. He is in a hopeless state, Sen.
