units.la: Perditus, transl.] Perditi animi homo, Plaut. Ad omne facinus promptissimus homo. Projectus ad audendum. Audax ad facinus. Expeditus ad cædem. Ad vim promptus, Cic.
units.tr: Perditus, transl.: a man of desperate mind, Plaut. A man most ready for any crime. Thrown forward to dare. Bold for crime. Ready for slaughter. Ready for violence, Cic.

units.la: Perducere] Perducere aliquid ad effectum, Pomp. Inducere ad parricidium. Neque eò deducam, aut progredi patiar. Producti simus, ut loqueremur, Cic. Conficere aliquid alicui mali. Redigere aliquem ad inopiam. Eò redigis me, ut, Ter.
units.tr: Perducere: to bring something to completion, Pomp. To lead someone on to parricide. I will not lead you so far, nor allow you to advance. We were brought forward to speak, Cic. To bring some evil upon someone. To reduce someone to poverty. You bring me to such a point that, Ter.

units.la: Perduellio] Majestatis crimen, Vlp. Crimen læsæ majestatis, & Imminutio majestatis, IC. Injuria Reip. facta, Paul. IC. Perduellionis crimen, Cic.
units.tr: Perduellio: the crime of majesty, Ulp. The crime of injured majesty and diminished majesty, IC. An injury done to the Republic, Paul IC. The crime of treason, Cic.

units.la: Perdurare, vid. Perseverare.
units.tr: Perdurare, see Persevere.

units.la: Peregrinari] Pervagari orbem terrarum, Liv. Peragrare ultimas terras, regionem, latebras. Concursare. Lustrare. Longè latéque peregrinari. In peregrinatione tempus consumere, Cic. Pererrare terras, Ovid. Percognoscere, Plin. Convisere loca oculis, Lucr. Perarare Pontum, Sen.
units.tr: Peregrinari: to roam over the whole world, Liv. To traverse the furthest lands, regions and hiding places. To wander about. To haunt. To wander far and wide. To spend time in travelling, Cic. To wander through lands, Ovid. To get to know thoroughly, Plin. To survey places with the eyes, Lucr. To plough the sea, Sen.

units.la: Peregrinatio] Legatio libera, Cic.
units.tr: Peregrinatio: a free embassy, Cic.

units.la: Peregrinatio imperitorum nihil prodest ] Cœlum, non animum mutant, qui trans mare currunt. Felis & trans mare vectus, vocem non mutant.
units.tr: Peregrinatio imperitorum nihil prodest: those who run across the sea change the sky, not the mind. A cat carried over the sea does not change its voice.

units.la: Parisios stolidum si mittas forsan asellum;
units.tr: If you send a foolish donkey to Paris, perhaps,

units.la: Si fuit hic asinus, non ibi fiet equus.
units.tr: if it was an ass here, there it will not become a horse.

units.la: Peregrinationis expers ] Hectorem imitaris, ab Ilio nunquam recedis. Sutor claudus. Cochlea domiporta.
units.tr: Peregrinationis expers: you imitate Hector, never leaving Troy. A lame cobbler. A snail that carries its home.

units.la: Peregrinator, vid. Viator.
units.tr: Peregrinator, see Traveller.

units.la: Peregrinus] Extraneus, Fest. Alieno cœlo natus. Experegrina, Ter. Externa gens. Barbarus hic ego sum, quia non intelligor ulli, Ovid. Convenæ. Alienigena. Adventitia & transmarina doctrina, Cic. Exoticum unguentum, Plin.
units.tr: Peregrinus: a stranger, Fest. Born in a foreign land. A foreign woman, Ter. A foreign people. Here I am a barbarian, because no one understands me, Ovid. Sojourners. Foreigners. Foreign and overseas learning, Cic. Exotic ointment, Plin.

units.la: Perfectè] Perfectissimè. Gell.
units.tr: Perfectè: most perfectly, Gell.

units.la: Perfectio ] Absolutio. Virtus, Cic. Exactio partus coepti, Ausson. Consummatio operis, Col. Peractio ætatis, Cic. Perfunctio laborum. Confectio belli, Cic. Finitio ædificiorum, Vitr.
units.tr: Perfectio: completion. Virtue, Cic. The bringing to term of a begun birth, Ausson. The completion of a work, Col. The full course of life, Cic. The performance of labours. The ending of a war, Cic. The finishing of buildings, Vitr.

units.la: Perfectus] Absolutus orator. Omnibus numeris absolutus. Omnes virtutis numeros continet; in se habet. Expletus omnibus suis numeris & partibus. Venit ad summum laus oratorum, Cic. Omnes numeros habet, Quint. Consummatus, consummatissimus. Exactus, Plin.Iun. Totus torus atque rotundus, Hor. Omnes numeros implet, Juv. Ad omnem legem exacta innocentia. Consummabilis, Sen. Cui nihil addi potest, vel demi.
units.tr: Perfectus: a complete orator. Complete in every respect. Contains all the measures of virtue and has them within itself. Filled with all its measures and parts. The praise of orators has reached its height, Cic. Has all measures, Quint. Consummate, most consummate. Finished, Plin. Iun. Whole, smooth and round, Hor. Fills all measures, Juv. Innocence exact to every law. Capable of completion, Sen. To which nothing can be added or taken away.

units.la: Perferre, vid. Pati.
units.tr: Perferre, see Endure.

units.la: Perficere, vid. Absolvere, Finire.
units.tr: Perficere, see Complete, Finish.

units.la: Perfidè] Perfidiosè, Plaut. Per fas & fidem deceptus. Liv. Perfidè agere] Græcâ mercari fide, Plaut.
units.tr: Perfidè: treacherously, Plaut. Deceived against right and faith, Liv. Perfidè agere: to trade in Greek faith, Plaut.

units.la: Perfidia] Punica fides. Perfidia violatæ dextræ, quæ fidei testis esse solebat, Cic. Impostura, Ulp.
units.tr: Perfidia: Punic faith. The treachery of a violated right hand, which used to be the witness of faith, Cic. Imposture, Ulp.

units.la: Perfidus] Perfidiosus, Perfidiosissimus homo, Cic. Falsificus animus. Sinister fidei. Sublestæ fidei, Plaut. Vid. Infidelis.
units.tr: Perfidus: a treacherous man, a most treacherous man, Cic. A false mind. Sinister in faith. Of flimsy faith, Plaut. See Unfaithful.

units.la: Perflatilis ] Expositus ventis, Plin. Perflabilis locus auris, Amm. Transmittit ventum vestis, Val. M. Capit perflatus, Col.
units.tr: Perflatilis: exposed to the winds, Plin. A place where the air blows through, Amm. The garment lets the wind through, Val. M. It takes in the blast, Col.

units.la: Perfluere] Permeare. Transfluit sanguis, Plin. Perpluere, Plaut. Bibula aut male cocta olla transmittit humorem, Col. Aqua transit, Vitr.
units.tr: Perfluere: to pass through. Blood flows through, Plin. To rain through, Plaut. A thirsty or badly fired pot lets the moisture through, Col. Water passes through, Vitr.

units.la: Perfodere aliquid] Præfodere, Plin. Transfodere, Liv.
units.tr: Perfodere aliquid: to dig up in front, Plin. To pierce through, Liv.

units.la: Perfretare, vid. Transfretare.
units.tr: Perfretare, see Cross the strait.

units.la: Perfuga, vid. Profugus.
units.tr: Perfuga, see Fugitive.

units.la: Perfugium, vid. Refugium.
units.tr: Perfugium, see Refuge.

units.la: Perfunctorie, vid. Negligenter. Obiter.
units.tr: Perfunctorie, see Carelessly, Incidentally.

units.la: Pergere, vid. Proficisci.
units.tr: Pergere, see Set out.

units.la: Pergræcari, vid. Prodigere.
units.tr: Pergræcari, see Squander.

units.la: Periclitari] Periclitatur rumpi vox, Quint. Venire in periculum, ne: in discrimen existimationis, Cic. De gloria & vita in discrimen vocari. Id. Venire propè exitium, Liv.
units.tr: Periclitari: the voice is in danger of breaking, Quint. To come into danger, lest: into peril of reputation, Cic. To be called into danger of glory and life, Id. To come near to ruin, Liv.

units.la: Periculosè] Capitaliter aliquem lacessere, Plin. Iun. Prope, Propius, proxime à periculo. Proxime periculum, Quint.
units.tr: Periculosè: to attack someone dangerously, Plin. Iun. Near, nearer, nearest to danger. Very close to danger, Quint.

units.la: Periculosus ] Infestus, Lubricus, Obnoxius, Scopulosus. In discrimine versatur maximo, Cic. Intutus, Liv. Pericu lo subjectus, Celf. Decretoria pugna, Quint.
units.tr: Periculosus: hostile, slippery, exposed, rocky. He is engaged in the greatest danger, Cic. Unprotected, Liv. Subject to danger, Celf. A decisive battle, Quint.

units.la: Periculosi aliquid tentare] Admovere ignem stipulæ. Ægeum navigare. Auribus lupum tenere. A transsenna cibum petere. In portu dormire. Per ignem incedere. Per extentum funem ire.
units.tr: Periculosi aliquid tentare: to bring fire to tinder. To sail the Aegean. To hold a wolf by the ears. To seek food from a crossbeam. To sleep in a harbour. To walk through fire. To walk along a taut rope.

units.la: Periculosa res] Gladius de filo pendet.
units.tr: A dangerous matter: the sword hangs by a hair.

units.la: Periculosum pugnare minorem cum majoribus] Conferre pugnam cum leone capram nolim.
units.tr: A dangerous thing, for the lesser to fight the greater: I would not care to pit a goat against a lion.

units.la: Periculum] Certamen & discrimen salutis. Procella fortufortunæ. Scopulus. Vadum. Tempestas, Cic. Altum, Lucr. Alea vitæ, Varr. Fauces mortis & hiatus, Arnob.
units.tr: Danger: A contest and a crisis for one's safety. A storm of fortune. A rock. A shallow. A tempest, Cic. The deep, Lucr. The dice of life, Varr. The jaws and gaping pit of death, Arnob.

units.la: Periculum extremum] Ancora rupta. Cum aqua fauces strangulat. Decretoria dies, Causa, Quint. De capite agun-tur comitia. De tuo corio luditur alea.
units.tr: Extreme danger: An anchor snapped. Water chokes the throat. The decisive day; a crisis, Quint. The assemblies are held concerning one's head. The dice are being thrown with your own hide.

units.la: Periculum est] Summum periculum est, ne &c. Periculosum est. Impendet periculum, Periclitantur jura. Non procul abest à periculo. Res in discrimine versatur maximo; In extremum, in propinquum adducta discrimen videtur, Cic. In periculo res vertitur, Plaut. Venit in periculum, in discrimen, Cic. Versatur in scopuloso loco, Id. Habet periculum ne &c, Col. In dubio est vita, Ter. In præcipiti est, Cels. De filo pendet hæc res. In acie novaculæ. Latet anguis in herba, Virg.
units.tr: It is a danger: It is a very great danger that &c. It is dangerous. Danger hangs over us. Rights are imperilled. He is not far from danger. The matter is in the greatest hazard; it is brought to the extreme, to the very edge of danger, Cic. The matter turns to danger, Plaut. He comes into danger, into peril, Cic. He is placed in a rocky spot, Id. There is a risk that &c., Col. Life is in doubt, Ter. He is in a precarious state, Cels. This matter hangs by a thread. On the edge of a razor. A snake lurks in the grass, Virg.

units.la: Periculum summum tentare] Omnem aleam jacere. Plurimum periclitari, Extrema fortuna stetit, Tac.
units.tr: To run the greatest risk: To cast every die. To put oneself in the greatest peril; he stood at the extreme of fortune, Tac.

units.la: Periculum evitare] Sub dentibus leti mortem effugere, Lucr. E vado emergere, Cic. In portu habere pedem.
units.tr: To avoid danger: To escape death from between the teeth of destruction, Lucr. To climb out of the shallows, Cic. To have a foot in the harbour.

units.la: Pericula sunt vitanda] Deprecatur navis scopulum. Flamma fumo est proxima. Sub omni lapide scorpius dormit.
units.tr: Dangers are to be avoided: The ship shuns the rock. The flame is close to the smoke. Under every stone the scorpion sleeps.

units.la: Periculum utrinque cavendum] Charybdin vitans in Scyllas incidit. Cinerem vitans in prunas. Dum vitant vitia stulti, in contraria currunt.
units.tr: Danger must be guarded against on both sides: Avoiding Charybdis, he falls into Scylla. Avoiding the ashes, he falls into the embers. While fools shun one vice, they rush into the opposite one.

units.la: De periculo in exitium] De fumo in flammam.
units.tr: From danger into ruin: From the smoke into the flame.

units.la: Periculum experTus cautior] Mus picem gustans.
units.tr: The more cautious for having been in danger: The mouse that has tasted pitch.

units.la: Pericula prudentiam ostendunt] In discrimine apparet qui Vir. Gubernator in tempestate dignoscitur, Cypr. Explorant adversa Viros.
units.tr: Dangers show prudence: A man's character appears in peril. The steersman is recognised in the storm, Cypr. Adversity tests men.

units.la: Periculo alieno facere] De alieno ludis corio.
units.tr: To act at another's peril: You play with another man's hide.

units.la: Perinde, vid. Itidem.
units.tr: Perinde, see Itidem.

units.la: Perire] Peritare. Si non peream, plane inteream, Plaut. Disperire, Intercidere, Occidere, Deperire, Cic. Abire in leves auras, in fumum. Devorari, Plin.
units.tr: To perish: To be lost. To be undone. If I do not die, I shall certainly be ruined, Plaut. To be destroyed, to fall to ruin, to be lost, Cic. To vanish into light breezes, into smoke. To be devoured, Plin.

units.la: Perire suis actionibus] Gladio suo jugulari. Suo sibi jumento malum asportare. Cacare sibi cum turdo exitium. Sorex suo indicio perit.
units.tr: To perish by one's own actions: To be cut down by one's own sword. To bring ruin on oneself with one's own beast of burden. To shit out one's own destruction with a thrush. The shrew perishes by its own betrayal.

units.la: Periit] Actum est de illo. Occidere occidione, Cic. Nullus sum. Occidi, Ter. Occisa haec res est. Occisissimus sum omnium, qui vivunt, Plaut. Deploratus, Liv. Sepulta fama, Ovid. Sepulta domus, Catul. Ecce autem perii, Plaut. Occidit spes omnis, Hor.
units.tr: He is lost: It is all over with him. To be lost in ruin, Cic. I am a nobody. I am done for, Ter. This affair is lost. I am the most ruined of all who live, Plaut. Given up for dead, Liv. A buried reputation, Ovid. A buried house, Catul. Look, I am lost, Plaut. All hope has perished, Hor.

units.la: Peream, vel pereat] Moriar. Non vivam. Male sit illi, Cic. Si fallo, tum me faciat quod vult magnus Jupiter. Vae aetati vestrae, Plaut. Emoriar priusquam, Id. Ut illum Dii terant, Nev. Qui illum Dii perdant, Ter. In cineres vertatur. Male pereat, Hor. Dii capiti illius generique reservent, Virg.
units.tr: May I perish, or may he perish: May I die. May I not live. May it go ill with him, Cic. If I am lying, may great Jupiter do to me what he will. Woe to your generation, Plaut. I would die before that, Id. May the gods crush him, Naev. May the gods destroy him, Ter. May he be turned to ashes. May he perish wretchedly, Hor. May the gods keep it for his head and his race, Virg.

units.la: Pereat hostis] Canis mortuus non mordet.
units.tr: May the enemy perish: A dead dog does not bite.

units.la: Peritia] Gnavitas, Sallust. Prudentia juris. Experientia patrimonii amplificandi, Cic.
units.tr: Skill: Diligence, Sallust. Knowledge of the law. Experience in increasing one's estate, Cic.

units.la: Peritus] Peritus usu. Volutatus, versatus in aliqua re. Nemo scientius versatus. Usu longo exercitatus. Usu eruditus. Perfecte planeque eruditus. Instructus a re civili. Nulla in re rudis. Callidus, cujus usu mens concaluit. Consultus naturae, Cic. Callidus usu, Ovid. Callidissimus rerum rusticarum, Col. Usu negotii diuturno firmatus, Amm. Pergnarus venerandi Deos, Apul. Prudentissimus adulandi, Tac. Valet in aliqua arte, Mart. Prudens medicinae, Col. Peritissimus de agricultura, Varr. Vid. Gnarus.
units.tr: Skilled: Skilled through practice. Versed and steeped in some matter. Most learnedly versed in it. Trained by long practice. Taught by experience. Thoroughly and completely learned. Instructed in public affairs. Untrained in no matter. Clever, whose mind has warmed to it through practice. Versed in nature, Cic. Clever through practice, Ovid. Most skilled in country matters, Col. Strengthened by long experience in business, Amm. Very well versed in worshipping the gods, Apul. Most shrewd at flattery, Tac. Strong in some art, Mart. Skilled in medicine, Col. Most expert in agriculture, Varr. See Gnarus.

units.la: Perjurium] Perjuratiuncula. Jusjurandum malum, Plaut. Perfidum sacramentum, Hor. Lingua juravi, mentem injuratam gero.
units.tr: Perjury: A petty perjury. A wicked oath, Plaut. A faithless oath, Hor. I swore with my tongue; I carry an unsworn mind.

units.la: Perjurus] Perjuriosus. Perfidus, Cic. Falsijurus. Comitiales homines, Plaut. Prodigus animae. Lenone perjurus magis, Eraf.
units.tr: Perjured: Forsworn. Faithless, Cic. Swearing falsely. Men of the assemblies, Plaut. Prodigal of his soul. More perjured than a pimp, Erasm.

units.la: Perlegere] Translegere, Plaut.
units.tr: To read through: To read through from end to end, Plaut.

units.la: Perlustrare] Recognoscere vestes. Col. Perspectare aliquid, Plaut. Perspicere aliquid, Cic. Perlegere oculis omnia, Virg. Recensere exercitum, Liv.
units.tr: To survey: To inspect garments, Col. To examine something closely, Plaut. To look carefully at something, Cic. To scan everything with the eyes, Virg. To review an army, Liv.

units.la: Permadere] Totus pluvia madefactus sum. Permadui, Col. Ad imum persedit imber, Virg.
units.tr: To soak through: I am wholly soaked with rain. I was drenched through, Col. The rain soaked down to the very bottom, Virg.

units.la: Permissio] Permissus, us. Permissa licentia. Concessio, Concessum. Facultas, Venia, Potestas, Cic.
units.tr: Permission: Permission. Granted licence. Concession, something conceded. Opportunity, pardon, power, Cic.

units.la: Permittere] Sinere aliquem respirare. Dare aliquid adolescentiæ. Pati aliquem abesse. Quiescat rem adduci ad interregnum. Largiri, Dare, Concedere facultatem aliquid agendi, Cic. Indulgere suffragio alicujus, Plin.Iun. Per me licet, Plaut. Tribuere alicui multa, Cic. Nimis liberaliter aliquem habere, Sal.
units.tr: To permit: To let someone draw breath. To give something to youth. To allow someone to be away. Let it rest; let the matter not be brought to an interregnum. To grant, to give, to concede the opportunity of doing something, Cic. To indulge someone's vote, Plin. Iun. As far as I am concerned, Plaut. To grant someone many things, Cic. To treat someone too generously, Sall.

units.la: Pernicies] Exitium urbis, Cic. Pestis, Liv.
units.tr: Ruin: The destruction of the city, Cic. A plague, Liv.

units.la: Perniciose, vid. Damnose.
units.tr: See Damnose.

units.la: Perniciosus] Pernicialis, Plin. Perniciabilis, Curt. Internecivus, Amm.
units.tr: Pernicious: Destructive, Plin. Deadly, Curt. Murderous, Amm.

units.la: Perniciosa nemini subministranda] Gladium dedisti, quo se occideret.
units.tr: Dangerous things are not to be supplied to anyone: You gave him a sword with which he killed himself.

units.la: Perorare, finem facere] Perorare orationem, causam, Cic. Finem facere sermonis, Plaut. Orandi, Ter. Concludere, Terminare orationem. Deorare, Fest. Tantum est, Plaut.
units.tr: To conclude a speech, to make an end: To conclude a speech or a cause, Cic. To make an end of a conversation, Plaut. Of pleading, Ter. To bring a speech to a close, to end it. To finish speaking, Fest. That is all, Plaut.

units.la: Peroratio, vid. Clausula.
units.tr: See Clausula.

units.la: Perpendere] Ponderare aliquid judicio. Expendere. Pensare singula, Cic. Penficulare, Gell. Ruminare, Varr. Vid. Considerare.
units.tr: To weigh up: To weigh something by judgement. To weigh out. To weigh single points, Cic. To examine minutely, Gell. To chew over, Varr. See Considerare.

units.la: Perpendicularis] Librata collocatio. Ad normam, ad perpendiculum, ad libellam respondens, Vitr. In neutram partem vergens. Normalis linea, Censor.
units.tr: Perpendicular: Exactly level in placement. Corresponding to the rule, the plumb line and the level, Vitr. Inclining to neither side. A normal line, Censor.

units.la: Perpendiculariter] Ad perpendiculam respondet ædificium, Vitr. Ad lineam deorsum ferri. Rectis lineis cœlestem locum subvolare, Cic. Rectô libramento.
units.tr: Perpendicularly: The building corresponds to the plumb line, Vitr. To be carried straight down to the line. To fly straight up to the heavenly region, Cic. By a true balance.

units.la: Perperam] Præposterè calceum induŏtum, Plin.
units.tr: Wrongly: A shoe put on the wrong foot, Plin.

units.la: Perpessio, vid. Passio.
units.tr: See Passio.

units.la: Patientia, perpeti, vid. Pati. Edurare.
units.tr: See Pati. Edurare.

units.la: Perpetrare aliquid] Patrare facinus, Liv. Committere aliquid contra legem. Committere multas res nefarias. Admittere in se aliquid, Cic. Admittere noxam, Ter. Suscipere in se facinus. Facere, edere scelus. Alligare se scelere. Adstringi scelere. Devincire se scelere. Conscisccere facinus. Concipere scelus. Obstringere se parricidio. Offendere in arrogantiam, Cic. Obstringere se furti, Ulp. Obstringi furti, Gell. Obligare se sceleris, Sen. Qui capitalem fraudem ausi, Liv.
units.tr: To commit a crime: To perpetrate a wicked deed, Liv. To commit something against the law. To commit many wicked acts. To take something upon oneself, Cic. To admit a fault, Ter. To undertake a crime. To do, to carry out a crime. To bind oneself to a crime. To be bound by a crime. To entangle oneself in wickedness. To conceive a crime. To bind oneself to parricide. To give offence by arrogance, Cic. To bind oneself to theft, Ulp. To be bound over for theft, Gell. To oblige oneself to a crime, Sen. Those who dared a capital fraud, Liv.

units.la: Perpetuare] Super aliquid dare aliquid, Plaut. Vid. Continuare.
units.tr: To perpetuate: To give something in return for something, Plaut. See Continuare.

units.la: Perpetuo, vid. Æternum.
units.tr: See Æternum.

units.la: Perpetuus, vid. Æternus. Continuus.
units.tr: See Æternus. Continuus.

units.la: Perpetua molestia] In vita nulla est intercapedo molestiæ.
units.tr: Perpetual trouble: In life there is no break in trouble.

units.la: Perplexari] Contorquere orationem, Cic. Perplexe cum aliquo loqui, Ter. Sensum obscurare, Quint. Perplexabilia verba facere. Perplexabiliter loqui, Plaut. Sepire dictis, Cic.
units.tr: To entangle: To twist one's speech, Cic. To speak in a perplexing manner with someone, Ter. To obscure the meaning, Quint. To use perplexing words. To speak in a perplexing way, Plaut. To hedge about with words, Cic.

units.la: Perplexe] Perplexabiliter. Perplexim loqui, Plaut. Contorte, implicitè, Cic. Involute, Spart. Intortius, Plin. Sinuosius dicere, Gell. Mæandri more, Vid. Difficulter.
units.tr: Perplexingly: In a perplexing way. To speak in a confusing manner, Plaut. Intricately, obscurely, Cic. Involvedly, Spart. More intricately, Plin. To speak more crookedly, Gell. In the manner of the Maeander; see Difficulter.

units.la: Perplexitas] Implicatio. Contortio orationis. Complexio mira verborum, Cic. Inexplicabilis series, Quint. Volumina vinculorum, Virg.
units.tr: Perplexity: Entanglement. Twisting of speech. A wonderful complexity of words, Cic. An inexplicable sequence, Quint. Coils of chains, Virg.

units.la: In perplexitate & periculo versari] Inter sacrum & sacrum sudare, Fest. Æstuare. Qui tibi æstus, qui error, quæ tenebræ? Cic. Inter malleum & incudem.
units.tr: To be in perplexity and danger: To sweat between one sacrifice and another, Fest. To seethe. What tide, what error, what darkness is this for you? Cic. Between the hammer and the anvil.

units.la: Perplexus] Inextricabilis. Inenodabilis, Contortus, Involutus, Cic. Inexplicitus, Mart. Perplexabilis, Plaut.
units.tr: Perplexed: Inextricable. Unknottable, twisted, involved, Cic. Unexplained, Mart. Perplexing, Plaut.

units.la: Perplexus error] Labyrinthus. Mæander.
units.tr: A perplexing error: A labyrinth. A maze.

units.la: Perplexus hæret] Hæret ei aqua. Hæret tanquam musin pice. Hærebat nebulo, quo se verteret, non habebat. Valde implicatus hæreo. Hæreo in salebra. Irretitus ac pene constrictus sum. Vehementer animi pendeo. Neque quid sequar, neque quid declinem, video. Perplexus animique consternati. In salebras incidi, Cic. Suspensus animi inter spem metumque, Liv. Decem anni incerti in pectore certant, nec, quid consilii capere possim, scio. Nullam mentem animi habeo. Incertat me aliquid. Distrahor. Differor, Plaut. Incertus est sui, Sen.
units.tr: He is perplexed and stuck: The water sticks to him. He sticks like a mouse in pitch. The rogue was stuck and had no way to turn. I am stuck fast. I stick on a rock in the mire. I am caught in a net and almost throttled. I hang in a mental turmoil. I see neither what to follow nor what to avoid. Perplexed and dismayed in mind. I fell among rough places, Cic. Suspended in mind between hope and fear, Liv. Ten uncertain years contend in my breast, and I do not know what counsel I can take. I have no settled mind. Something troubles me. I am torn in two. I am pulled apart, Plaut. He is uncertain of himself, Sen.

units.la: Perrumpere] Perrumpere agmen. Perrumpere per mediam aciem, Liv. Perrumpere castra, Plin. Per castra, Liv. Ire per gladios, Ovid. Vid. Rumpere.
units.tr: To break through: To break through a line. To break through the middle of the battle line, Liv. To break through a camp, Plin. Through the camp, Liv. To go through swords, Ovid. See Rumpere.

units.la: Persecutio] Vexatio, Cic. Insectatio fortunæ humanæ, Quint.
units.tr: Persecution: Harassment, Cic. Assault upon human fortune, Quint.

units.la: Persecutor] Vexator crudelis Reip. Cic. Exagitator omnium.
units.tr: Persecutor: A cruel harasser of the commonwealth, Cic. A tormentor of all.

units.la: Persequi] Insectari, Insequi. Exercere, Exagitare aliquem. Vexare, Cic. Fugitare, Protelare, Plaut.
units.tr: To pursue: To hound, to follow after. To harass someone. To vex, Cic. To shun, to put off, Plaut.

units.la: Perseverans, vid. Constans.
units.tr: See Constans.

units.la: Perseverantia] Perseveratio. Apul. Firma & stabilis permansio, in oratione bene considerata, Cic.
units.tr: Perseverance: Persistence. A firm and steady remaining, in a well-considered speech, Cic.

units.la: Perseverare] Perseverare constanter, in constantia. Exspectare ad extremum, Cic. Perdurare, Ter. Perspectare ludos, Suet. Manere, Hor. Durare, Virg.
units.tr: To persevere: To persist steadfastly, in constancy. To wait for the end, Cic. To endure, Ter. To watch the games through, Suet. To remain, Hor. To last, Virg.

units.la: Persona] Caput, Liv. Sextantibus collatis in capita.
units.tr: Person: A head, Liv. Sextants collected per head.

units.la: Perspectus, vid. Probatus.
units.tr: Perspectus, see Probatus.

units.la: Perspicabilis] Janua praebet per se apertum transpectum, Lucr. Bipatentes aedes, Virg. Vid. Pellucidus.
units.tr: Perspicabilis] A door offers a clear view straight through, Lucr. A house with doors open on both sides, Virg. See Pellucidus.

units.la: Perspicax] Quis est tam lynceus? Cic. Oculus aquilinus, Plaut. Milvinus, Sen. Venti oculi, Plaut. Lynceo perspicacior, Er. Vid. Oculatus.
units.tr: Perspicax] Who is as keen-sighted as a lynx? Cic. An eagle's eye, Plaut. Kite-eyed, Sen. Eyes of the wind, Plaut. Sharper-sighted than a lynx, Er. See Oculatus.

units.la: Perspicue] Clare, liquide, dilucide, plane, luculente dicere, Cic. Evidenter, Quint. Illustrissimè narrare, Gell. Dicam pinguiore Minerva.
units.tr: Perspicue] To speak clearly, lucidly, plainly, openly, brilliantly, Cic. Evidently, Quint. To narrate most illustriously, Gell. I will speak with a richer Minerva.

units.la: Perspicuitas] Evidentia & perspicuitas in oratione. Libri lumen desiderant, Cic. Fulgor, Val.M. Claritudo virtutum, Tac.
units.tr: Perspicuitas] Evidence and clarity in speech. The book needs light, Cic. Brilliance, Val.M. The brightness of virtues, Tac.

units.la: Perspicuus] Clara res. Dilucida oratio. Evidens. Illustris, splendida ratio dicendi. Explicata ratio. Explicitus, Cicer.
units.tr: Perspicuus] A clear matter. A lucid speech. Evident. An illustrious, splendid manner of speaking. An explained manner. Explicit, Cicer.

units.la: Perspicuum est, vid. Palam est.
units.tr: Perspicuum est, see Palam est.

units.la: Perstrepere, vid. Concrepare.
units.tr: Perstrepere, see Concrepare.

units.la: Perstringere, vid. Percellere, Praestringere.
units.tr: Perstringere, see Percellere, Praestringere.

units.la: Persuadere] Instillare aliquid alicui. Perducere in, ad meam sententiam. Inducere aliquem oratione ad faciendum. Flectere animum alicujus oratione. Compositae orationis insidiis fidem alicujus attentare. Dicere accommodatè ad persuadendum, Cic. Terebrare, Plaut. Impellere in, ad, Cic.
units.tr: Persuadere] To instil something into someone. To lead someone into my opinion. To induce someone by speech to act. To bend someone's mind by speech. To test someone's trust by the snares of a composed speech. To speak fittingly so as to persuade, Cic. To bore into, Plaut. To urge into or towards, Cic.

units.la: Persuadere oratoris est] Persuadebis cito, si bene dicas. Non persuadebis album esse.
units.tr: Persuadere oratoris est] You will persuade quickly if you speak well. You will not persuade him that white is black.

units.la: Persuaderi mihi patiar] Prorsus ita esse mihi persuades. Persuasus sum à. Dat se facilem, Ovid.
units.tr: Persuaderi mihi patiar] You certainly persuade me that it is so. I am persuaded by. She shows herself easy to persuade, Ovid.

units.la: Persuasio, vid. Suasio.
units.tr: Persuasio, see Suasio.

units.la: Persuasor] Suada, Bud. Flexanima oratio, Cic. Persua-strix. Malesuada vitii, Plaut. Persuasiosus artifex callidus, Amm. Vid. Suasor.
units.tr: Persuasor] Suada, Bud. A speech that moves the mind, Cic. A woman who persuades. Suada, the evil counsellor of vice, Plaut. A crafty, persuasive artisan, Amm. See Suasor.

units.la: Persuasu difficilis] Ne suadela quidem persuaserit. Non persuadebis. Ne si persuaseris quidem. Non persuasibilis sum, Quint. Non tuis depellor dictis, quin rumori serviam, Plaut. Si Suadae medulla sis, non persuadebis. Si Mercurius suadeat, nihil fecerit. Licet Gratias cum Musis adducas, non exhilarabis, &c. Mihi nunquam persuaderi poterit. Non adducar ut credam, Cic. Non sustinebit inducere in animum, Plin.Iun. Scarabaeo citius persuaseris.
units.tr: Persuasu difficilis] Not even the goddess of persuasion could persuade him. You will not persuade. Not even if you persuaded him. I am not to be persuaded, Quint. I am not turned from my purpose by your words, so that I should not yield to rumour, Plaut. Even if you were the very marrow of Suada, you would not persuade. Even if Mercury advised, he would achieve nothing. Although you bring the Graces with the Muses, you will not cheer him, etc. I can never be persuaded. I will not be brought to believe, Cic. He will not allow it to enter his mind, Plin.Iun. You would sooner persuade a beetle.

units.la: Persuasu facilis] Cui dare verba facile est, Ter. Facilis persuasu. Facilis mollescere (f. oratione,) Claud. Facilis capi. Facilis suadenti. Mollis in obsequium, facilisque roganti, Ovid. Mens facilis & apta capi, Lucan. Facilis ad credendum, Cic.
units.tr: Persuasu facilis] One to whom it is easy to give words, Ter. Easy to persuade. Easy to soften (by speech), Claud. Easy to take. Easy for a persuader. Soft to compliance and easy for one who asks, Ovid. A mind easy and apt to be seized, Lucan. Easy to believe, Cic.

units.la: Pertæsus] Pertæsum est me alicujus rei, Cic. Semet ipse pertæsus, Suet. Percipit me odium agni. Pertædescit alicujus cibi, Cic. Obsaturabere istius propediem. Cepit eum satietas hujus rei. Defatigari satietate alicujus rei, Cic. Abiit aliquid in satietatem, Plin.
units.tr: Pertæsus] It wearies me of something, Cic. Wearied of himself, Suet. Loathing of the lamb seizes me. It grows tedious to someone, of some food, Cic. You will soon be surfeited with that. Satiety of this thing has seized him. To be worn out by satiety of something, Cic. Something has passed into surfeit, Plin.

units.la: Perterrefacere. vid. Exterrere.
units.tr: Perterrefacere, see Exterrere.

units.la: Pertinacia] Destinatio pertinax, Amm. Vid. Contumacia. Pervicacia.
units.tr: Pertinacia] Persistent determination, Amm. See Contumacia. Pervicacia.

units.la: Pertinacia sequitur superbiam] Pertinacia elati animi comes.
units.tr: Pertinacia sequitur superbiam] Obstinacy is the companion of a proud spirit.

units.la: Pertinaciter] Pugnaciter, Quint. Pugnacissimè defendere, Cic. Pervicaciter perstant. Districtè, Vlp. Obstinatè, Liv. Obstinatâ mente, Catul. Destinatione pervicaci, Amm. Vid. Contumaciter.
units.tr: Pertinaciter] Pugnaciously, Quint. To defend most pugnaciously, Cic. They persist obstinately. Strictly, Vlp. Obstinately, Liv. With an obstinate mind, Catul. With persistent determination, Amm. See Contumaciter.

units.la: Pertinax] Obstinatus. Durae cervicis. Excetrâ pertinacior, Er. Vid. Contumax.
units.tr: Pertinax] Obstinate. Stiff-necked. More obstinate than a viper, Er. See Contumax.

units.la: Pertinet] Attinet ad me, Plaut. Attingit me, te, Cicer. Facit ad bonos mores, Ovid. Habet in hac re partes, Ter. Competit ei, Non.
units.tr: Pertinet] It concerns me, Plaut. It touches me or you, Cicer. It contributes to good morals, Ovid. He has a share in this matter, Ter. It is fitting for him, Non.

units.la: Non pertinet ad te] Fori tui non est.
units.tr: Non pertinet ad te] It is not within your forum (it is not your business).

units.la: Pertingere] Venae ex oculis pertingunt ad cerebrum, brum: Plin. Pertinet contagio ad lunam, vel potius ad ter-ram, Cic. Ex ædibus meis in tuas tignum pertinet, Vlp.
units.tr: Pertingere] Veins run from the eyes to the brain, Plin. The contagion reaches the moon, or rather the earth, Cic. A beam runs from my house into yours, Vlp.

units.la: Pertrahere aliquem] Pertraho ratem ad ripam, Liv. At-traho aliquem ad. Protrahere aliquem ad convivium, Cic.
units.tr: Pertrahere aliquem] I drag the raft to the bank, Liv. To draw someone along to. To draw someone forth to a banquet, Cic.

units.la: Perturbare] Perturbare animos hominum. Afferre alicui motum. Incerta omnia reddere. Tumultum injicere. Injectus à me tumultus civitati videretur, Cic. Conturbare, Id. Consternere aliquem. Confundere sensus animi alicujus, Liv. Deturbare aliquem de mente, de spe, Cic. v. Turbare.
units.tr: Perturbare] To disturb men's minds. To bring agitation to someone. To make all things uncertain. To raise a tumult. A tumult raised by me would seem to the state, Cic. To dismay, Id. To strike someone with dismay. To confound someone's mental faculties, Liv. To drive someone from his mind or his hope, Cic. See Turbare.

units.la: Perturbari] Turbari. Affici molestiâ. Afficit aliquem aliquid. In perturbationem incidere. Perturbationi animi succumbere. Commoveri. Commoveri animo, miseriis, desiderio. Commovet me inopia. Moveri. Moveri animo: Movet, Perturbat, Conturbat, Obturbat me aliquid. Magnâ animi perturbatione commovere. Permoveri iracundiâ. Conturbatum me res hæc tenuit, Cic. Inquietari aliquâ re, Plin. Iun. Percutit aliquid animum, Lucr. Confluctuari meta, Sen.
units.tr: Perturbari] To be troubled. To be affected with annoyance. Something affects someone. To fall into disturbance. To yield to a disturbance of mind. To be moved. To be moved in mind, by miseries, by longing. Want moves me. To be stirred. To be stirred in mind. Something moves, disturbs, confounds or obstructs me. To be stirred with great disturbance of mind. To be moved to anger. This matter held me in disturbance, Cic. To be unsettled by something, Plin.Iun. Something strikes the mind, Lucr. To be tossed about at the turning-post, Sen.

units.la: Perturbatè, vid. Turbidè.
units.tr: Perturbatè, see Turbidè.

units.la: Perturbatio, vid. Turbatio.
units.tr: Perturbatio, see Turbatio.

units.la: Perturbatus, vid. Turbatus.
units.tr: Perturbatus, see Turbatus.

units.la: Pervadere, vid. Transfire. Pervagatus, vid. Vulgaris. Pervagari, vid. Discurrere.
units.tr: Pervadere, see Transfire. Pervagatus, see Vulgaris. Pervagari, see Discurrere.

units.la: Pervenire aliquò] Pertendere Romam, Liv. Tangere provinciam. Pervehi aliquò. Permanare aliquò. Devenire. Perlabi. Devolare, Cic. Penetrare in aliquem locum, Quint.
units.tr: Pervenire aliquò] To extend as far as Rome, Liv. To touch a province. To be carried through to somewhere. To pass through to somewhere. To arrive. To come down. To glide through. To fly down, Cic. To penetrate into some place, Quint.

units.la: Versè] Depravatè judicare, Cic. Præposterè, Perperam, Plin.
units.tr: Perversè] To judge depravedly, Cic. Preposterously, perversely, Plin.

units.la: Perversitas] Quæ tanta perversitas in hominibus, ut, inventis frugibus, glande vescantur, Cic. Inversio, Id.
units.tr: Perversitas] What great perversity is in men, that, though crops have been discovered, they feed on acorns, Cic. Inversion, Id.

units.la: Perversus] Inversi mores, Hor. Præposterus, Cic. Sinister, Plin. Retrogradus exortus, Plin.
units.tr: Perversus] Inverted manners, Hor. Preposterous, Cic. Sinister, Plin. A retrograde rising, Plin.

units.la: Perversa omnia] Versa & mutata in pejorem partem sunt omnia, Cic. Contrarium iter mundo sidera intendunt, Sen.
units.tr: Perversa omnia] All things have been turned and changed for the worse, Cic. The stars direct a course contrary to the world, Sen.

units.la: Pervertere] Invertere ordinem. Evertere naviculam, Cic. Cic. Resupinare aulam, Iuv. Pervolvit saxa torrens, Plin. Vertere cadum, Plaut. Subvertere. Revolvere, Col. Ima summis mutare, Hor.
units.tr: Pervertere] To invert the order. To capsize a little boat, Cic. Cic. To overturn the hall, Iuv. A torrent rolls the stones over, Plin. To turn a jar over, Plaut. To subvert. To roll back, Col. To change the lowest into the highest, Hor.

units.la: Pervicacia] Pervicax contumacia, Col. Pugnacitas, Plin. Cervices, Frangere cervices, vid. Contumacia.
units.tr: Pervicacia] Persistent obstinacy, Col. Pugnacity, Plin. Necks; to break necks, see Contumacia.

units.la: Pervicax, vid. Contumax.
units.tr: Pervicax, see Contumax.

units.la: Pervincere] Pertendere aliquid, Ter. Evincere, Liv. Efficere quod cupias, Ter. Tenere propositum, Caes. Efficere propositum, Cic. Obtinere, Liv.
units.tr: Pervincere] To stretch something through, Ter. To prove, Liv. To bring about what you desire, Ter. To hold to a purpose, Caes. To carry out a purpose, Cic. To obtain, Liv.

units.la: Pervivere, vid. Provivere.
units.tr: Pervivere, see Provivere.

units.la: Pervius] Penetrabilis Nilus, Stat. Meabilis transitus, Plin. Exsuperabile vallum, Claud. Superabilis, Liv. Transitorius, Suet. Commeabilis, Arnob. Commeatus continet. Commeatus est hinc à nobis, Plaut.
units.tr: Pervius] A penetrable Nile, Stat. A passable crossing, Plin. An insurmountable rampart, Claud. Surmountable, Liv. Transitory, Suet. Passable, Arnob. It holds supplies. Supplies come to us from here, Plaut.

units.la: Pervulgata res, vid. Palàm est.
units.tr: Pervulgata res, see Palàm est.

units.la: Pessime] Nequissimè, Plin.
units.tr: Pessime] Most wickedly, Plin.

units.la: Pessimus] Maximè pessimus, Col. Nequissimus, Cic. Homo omnium, quos videt sol, scelestissimus; Scelestior nullus alter. Quantum hominum terra sustinet sacerrimus, Plaut. Insigniter malus.
units.tr: Pessimus] Most wicked, Col. Most worthless, Cic. The most criminal man the sun sees; no one more villainous. As many men as the earth bears, most accursed, Plaut. Remarkably bad.

units.la: Pessima mala] Extrema extremorum mala.
units.tr: Pessima mala] The extreme of extreme evils.

units.la: Pessulus, vid. Obex. Pessum dare, vid. Conculare.
units.tr: Pessulus, see Obex. Pessum dare, see Conculcare.

units.la: Pessum ire] Ad ima sidere, Plin. Submergi, Virg.
units.tr: Pessum ire] To sink to the bottom, Plin. To be submerged, Virg.

units.la: Pestis] Pestes, Plin. Pestilentia, Cic. Pestifera labes pecorum, Col. Lues infesta, continuâ contage populum inficiens, Lucr.
units.tr: Pestis] Pests, Plin. Pestilence, Cic. A deadly blight of cattle, Col. A harmful plague infecting the people with continual contagion, Lucr.

units.la: Pestem afferre] Afferre pestilentiam, Plin. Facere pestilentiam aliquid valet, Col. Pestem conferre, Id.
units.tr: Pestem afferre] To bring pestilence, Plin. Being able to cause pestilence, Col. To bring plague, Id.

units.la: Peste infici] Pestis incessit apes, Col. invadit, Cic. Pestilentia lacerat exercitum, Patercul. Pestilentia coorta est. In urbem incidit, Liv. Percelli peste, Col.
units.tr: Peste infici] Plague fell upon the bees, Col. invades, Cic. Pestilence tears the army, Patercul. Pestilence has broken out. It fell upon the city, Liv. To be struck by plague, Col.

units.la: Peste infectus] Contactus pestilentiâ. Afflatus peste, Sil. Infectum mare venenis, Liv.
units.tr: Peste infectus] Touched by pestilence. Breathed upon by plague, Sil. The sea infected with poisons, Liv.

units.la: Pestilens] Annus pestilentiâ infamis, Liv. Morbidus aer, Lucr. Tabificus, Lucan. Unde halitus letalis exsurgit, Amm. Pestifer aer, Claud. Pestifera ripa, Cic. Nocens coelum, Lucan. Plenus pestilentiæ, Catul. Valet facere pestilenpestilentiam, Col. Quâvis peste pestilentior, Er. Pestilentus, Gell. Pestilentiosus, Vlp.
units.tr: Pestilens] A year infamous for pestilence, Liv. Unhealthy air, Lucr. Wasting, Lucan. Whence a deadly breath rises, Amm. Pestiferous air, Claud. A pestilential bank, Cic. A harmful sky, Lucan. Full of pestilence, Catul. Able to cause pestilence, Col. More pestilent than any plague, Er. Pestilential, Gell. Pestilential, Vlp.

units.la: Petasio] Petasio, Var. Petasunculus, Iuv.
units.tr: Petasio] Petasio, Var. Petasunculus, Iuv.

units.la: Petasus] Petasunculus, Arnob. Pilei umbraculum, Sipont. Causia, Val. M. Galerus, Iun.
units.tr: Petasus] Petasunculus, Arnob. A little umbrella for a cap, Sipont. Causia, Val.M. Galerus, Iun.

units.la: Petax, vid. Rogator. Petere, vid. Rogare.
units.tr: Petax, see Rogator. Petere, see Rogare.

units.la: Pevigo, vid. Mentagra.
units.tr: Pevigo, see Mentagra.

units.la: Petitio] Petitum, Catul. Petitus, Gell. Precatio, Preces, deprecatio, Rogatus, Rogatio, Cic. Postulatus, Liv. Supplicatio, Sipont. Obtestatio, Cic. Precatus, Amm. Orata, pl. Ter. Non votis, neque suppliciis muliebribus Deorum auxilia parantur, Salust.
units.tr: Petitio] A thing sought, Catul. A request, Gell. Prayer, entreaty, supplication, asking, Cic. A demand, Liv. Supplication, Sipont. Entreaty, Cic. A plea, Amm. Prayers, Ter. Help from the gods is not won by vows or by women's supplications, Salust.

units.la: Petitor, vid. Rogator.
units.tr: Petitor, see Rogator.

units.la: Petra] Rupes, Cæs. Cautes, Plin. Saxum, Cic. Rupina, Apul. Vivum saxum, Virg.
units.tr: Petra] A rock, Caes. A crag, Plin. A stone, Cic. A rocky ledge, Apul. A living rock, Virg.

units.la: Petrosus] Petricosus, Mart. Scopulosus collis, Sil.
units.tr: Petrosus] Stony, Mart. A rocky hill, Sil.

units.la: Petulans] Effrenus, Stat. Procax, Hor. Freno opus habet. Dissolutus. Virg. Procacissimis ingeniis inter servos, Tac. Col. Audax animis, viribus.
units.tr: Petulans] Unbridled, Stat. Insolent, Hor. Needs a bridle. Dissolute, Virg. Most insolent minds among slaves, Tac. Bold in spirit and strength.

units.la: Petulanter] Effrenatè. Petulantissimè aliquid facere. Luxuriosè, Cic. Protervè alicui facere injuriam, Plaut. Licenter errare, Cic.
units.tr: Petulanter] Unrestrainedly. To do something most wantonly. Luxuriously, Cic. To wrong someone wantonly, Plaut. To wander without restraint, Cic.

units.la: Petulantia] Immoderata libertas. Juvenilis licentia. Effrenatio animi, Cic. vid. Dissoluta vita.
units.tr: Petulantia] Immoderate freedom. Youthful licence. Unbridled spirit, Cic. See Dissoluta vita.

units.la: Phantasia] Idolum. Species. Imaginationes libidinum, Cic.
units.tr: Phantasia] An idol. An appearance. Imaginings of lusts, Cic.

units.la: Phantasma] Falsa visio. Forma, Species. Visum. Somniorum visa, Visa à nocte & ratione vacua, Cic.
units.tr: Phantasma] A false vision. A shape, an appearance. A vision. The visions of dreams. Visions from the night and an empty mind, Cic.

units.la: Pharmacopola] Myropola, Plaut. Unguentarius. Pigmentarius, Cic. Magmentarius, Gloss. Medicamentarius. Herbarius, Plin. Seplasiarius, Lamp.
units.tr: Pharmacopola] A perfumer, Plaut. An ointment-seller. A dealer in dyes, Cic. A druggist (Magmentarius, Gloss.). A medicine-seller. A herbalist, Plin. Seplasiarius, Lamp.

units.la: Pharmacopolium] Myropolium, Plaut. Aromataria taberna. Iun. Seplasia, Plin.
units.tr: Pharmacopolium] A perfumer's shop, Plaut. A spice shop, Iun. A perfume-market, Plin.

units.la: Pharmacum, vid. Medicamentum.
units.tr: Drug, see Medicine.

units.la: Phasiana] Phasianus. Phasis, Mart. Scythica volucris. Iuv. Phasidis ales, Stat.
units.tr: Phasian: pheasant. Phasis, Mart. A Scythian bird, Juv. A bird of the Phasis, Stat.

units.la: Phengites] Lapis specularis, Plin. Vitrum illiquabile.
units.tr: Phengites: mica (stone for windows), Plin. Glass that cannot be melted.

units.la: Philomela, vid. Lusцinia.
units.tr: Nightingale, see Luscinia.

units.la: Philosophari Christiane] Philosophare coelum intuens.
units.tr: To philosophize as a Christian: to philosophize while gazing at heaven.

units.la: Philosophia] Studium sapientiae. Cognitio optimarum artium, Cic. Vivendi & moriendi scientia, Sen.
units.tr: Philosophy: the pursuit of wisdom. Knowledge of the best arts, Cic. The science of living and dying, Sen.

units.la: Philosophus] Magister virtutis, Cic. Doctor Sapientiae, Tac. Professor sapientiae, Quint. Idearum venator.
units.tr: Philosopher: a teacher of virtue, Cic. A teacher of wisdom, Tac. A professor of wisdom, Quint. A hunter after ideas.

units.la: Philura] Philyra, plagula papyri. Scheda, Plin.
units.tr: Philura: Philyra, a sheet of papyrus. A leaf, Plin.

units.la: Phlebotomia] Detractio sanguinis per venas, Plin. Sectio venae, Gor.
units.tr: Phlebotomy: drawing blood through the veins, Plin. Cutting of a vein, Gor.

units.la: Physica] Oratorem ne Physicorum quidem expertem volo, Cic. Physiologia. Naturae ratio. Explicatio naturae, Id. Physice.
units.tr: Physics: "I do not want an orator who is not even versed in physics," Cic. Physiology. An account of nature. An explanation of nature, Id. Physics.

units.la: Physiognomia] Peritia ex aspectu vultus de natura judicandi, Gell.
units.tr: Physiognomy: skill in judging character from the look of the face, Gell.

units.la: Physiognomus] Metoposcopus. Ex facie hominum addivinans, Plin.
units.tr: Physiognomist: a reader of foreheads. One who foretells from people's faces, Plin.

units.la: Piaculum] Piatio, Plin. (i, piaculo dignum: ut inauspicati nominis lustratione, Expiatione, averruncatione, Decalemp.) Piamen, Ovid. Piamentum, Test. Februa, Plin. Ovid.
units.tr: Expiation: atonement, Plin. (that is, something needing expiation: as by purifying an ill-omened name, expiation, averting, Decalemp.) Means of atonement, Ovid. Atonement, Test. The Februa, Plin. Ovid.

units.la: Picaria] Picariae, picis fodinae, Florent, in Pand. Piceaaria, Robert.
units.tr: Pitch-pit: pitch mines, Florent, in Pand. Pitch-works, Robert.

units.la: Picatus] Piceatus, Mart.
units.tr: Smeared with pitch: smeared with pitch, Mart.

units.la: Pieus] Picinus: picinum oleum, Sipont.
units.tr: Pitchy: pitchlike; pitch oil, Sipont.

units.la: Pictura] Graphis. Graphice. Diagraphice, Plin.
units.tr: Painting: graphic art. Drawing. Outline drawing, Plin.

units.la: Pictura, pro opere] Imago picta. Imago alicujus in tabula. Tabula bene picta, Cic.
units.tr: Painting, as a work: a painted image. The likeness of someone on a panel. A well-painted panel, Cic.

units.la: Pictus acu.] Picto plumbo chlamys, Virg.
units.tr: Embroidered with the needle: a cloak of painted lead-colour, Virg.

units.la: Picturatus] Distinctus, Ovid. Variata vestis figuris, Lucr. Stragulum magnificis operibus pictum, Cic. Magis varius quam pavo. Vestis signis ingentibus apta, Lucr. Florida, Apul. Variata figuris vestis, Lucr. Intertexta vestis pluribus notis, Quint. Plumatus auro, Lucan. Variatus acu, Martial.
units.tr: Embroidered: marked out, Ovid. A garment varied with figures, Lucr. A covering decorated with magnificent works, Cic. More varied than a peacock. A garment fit for huge figures, Lucr. Flowery, Apul. A garment varied with figures, Lucr. A garment interwoven with many marks, Quint. Feathered with gold, Lucan. Varied with the needle, Mart.

units.la: Pictus] Coloratus, Cic. Pictilis, Apul.
units.tr: Painted: coloured, Cic. Painted, Apul.

units.la: Pie] Pie sanctèque colere deos. Religiose, Cic. vid. Religiose.
units.tr: Piously: to worship the gods reverently and holily. Religiously, Cic. See Religiously.

units.la: Pietas] Tum maximè Religio & pietas versatur in animis, cùm rebus divinis operam damus, Cic. vid. Religio.
units.tr: Piety: "Then religion and piety especially dwell in minds when we devote ourselves to divine matters," Cic. See Religion.

units.la: Piger] Segnis. Tardus asellus, Virg. Cessator. Iners & desidiosus. Socors, Cic. Asino pigrior, Mart. Fugiens laboris, Cæs. Supinus, Iuv. vid. Desidiosus.
units.tr: Lazy: slothful. A slow donkey, Virg. An idler. Inactive and indolent. Careless, Cic. Lazier than a donkey, Mart. Shirking toil, Caes. Lying on one's back, Juv. See Idle.

units.la: Pigri amant laborum fructum, non labores ipsos] Ficus avibus gratæ sunt, sed eas plantare recusant. Felis amat piscēs, sed aquas intrare recusat.
units.tr: The lazy love the fruit of labour, not the labour itself: figs are pleasing to birds, yet they refuse to plant them. A cat loves fish, yet refuses to wade into the water.

units.la: Piget]Pigror. Ne pigrēre scribere. Non gravabor dicere, Cic.
units.tr: To be reluctant: to be slow. Do not be reluctant to write. I shall not hesitate to say, Cic.

units.la: Pigmentarius. vid. Pharmacopola.
units.tr: Druggist, see Apothecary.

units.la: Pigmentum] Color, Cic. Venenum, Poëticè, Enn. Medicamentum, Sen. Suasum. Insuasum, Fest.
units.tr: Pigment: colour, Cic. Poison, poetically, Enn. Medicine, Sen. Persuasion. Unpersuasiveness, Fest.

units.la: Pignorare, vid. Oppignorare.
units.tr: To pledge, see To mortgage.

units.la: Pignus] Hypotheca. Arrhabo, Ter. Fiducia, Cic.
units.tr: Pledge: a mortgage. A deposit, Ter. Trust, Cic.

units.la: Pignus accipere] Accipere aliquid pignori, Pomp. Cavere sibi pignore, Vlp. Fiduciam accipere. Cic.
units.tr: To accept a pledge: to accept something in pledge, Pomp. To take security for oneself, Ulp. To accept a trust, Cic.

units.la: Pigrè] Lentè veniunt, Plin. Gravatim, Liv. Gravatè. Languidè & cunctanter procedere, Cic. vid. Lentè.
units.tr: Slowly: they come slowly, Plin. Reluctantly, Liv. Heavily. To proceed languidly and hesitantly, Cic. See Slowly.

units.la: Pigrescere] Consenescere veternô, Pel. Torpere veterno. Virg. Torpere cessatione. Languere otio. Jacére. Frigere. Deponere studium, Cic. Torpescere socordiâ, Salust. Marcere, Celf. Lentere, Liv. Desidere residem, Paterc.
units.tr: To grow slothful: to grow old in drowsiness, Pel. To grow numb with lethargy, Virg. To grow numb through idleness. To languish in leisure. To lie prostrate. To grow cold. To lay aside zeal, Cic. To grow torpid through sloth, Sall. To wither, Cels. To slacken, Liv. To settle into inactivity, Paterc.

units.la: Pigritia] Segnities. Inertia laboris. Tarditas in rebus agendis, Cic. Socordia, Ter. Torpedo animi, Salust. Pigror, Lucr. Murcea, Dea socordiæ, Aug. vid. Desidia.
units.tr: Sloth: laziness. Inertia in labour. Sluggishness in getting things done, Cic. Carelessness, Ter. Torpor of mind, Sall. Laziness, Lucr. Murcea, goddess of sloth, Aug. See Idleness.

units.la: Pilentum] Carpentum, Liv. Lectica, Cic. Pensilibus plumis vehi, Iuv. Cameratum vehiculum.
units.tr: Carriage: a cart, Liv. A litter, Cic. To be borne on soft feathers, Juv. A vaulted vehicle.

units.la: Pileus] Pileum, Perf. Apex, Serv. Tutulus, Seal. Galerus, Suet.
units.tr: Cap: a felt cap, Pers. A peak, Serv. A tutulus, Seal. A helmet, Suet.

units.la: Pilosus. vid. Hirsutus.
units.tr: Hairy, see Shaggy.

units.la: Pilula] Catapotium, Plin. Gær.
units.tr: Pill: a pill, Plin. Gaer.

units.la: Pilum] Pilum farreacium, Cat. Pilum Græcum, Plaut. Pilum ruidum, Plin.
units.tr: Pestle: a spelt pestle, Cat. A Greek pestle, Plaut. A rough pestle, Plin.

units.la: Pilus] Villus, Cic.
units.tr: Hair: a tuft, Cic.

units.la: Pinaster] Pinus sylvestris. Strobilus, vel, Strobulus, Plin. Pinus suæ spontis, Col.
units.tr: Wild pine: Scots pine. A cone, or strobulus, Plin. A pine that grows of its own accord, Col.

units.la: Pinea] Pinus sativa, Col. Pinus in hortis, Virg. Pinus, Abs. Plin.
units.tr: Cultivated pine: a planted pine, Col. A pine in gardens, Virg. Pine, absolutely, Plin.

units.la: Pinetum] Sylva pinea, Virg.
units.tr: Pinewood: a pine grove, Virg.

units.la: Pingere] Pingere coloribus. Depingere aliquid. Exprimere, Cic. Scripsit Dianam, Plin.
units.tr: To paint: to paint with colours. To depict something. To express, Cic. He painted Diana, Plin.

units.la: Pingere exquisitè] Apelleo penicillo pingere.
units.tr: To paint exquisitely: to paint with the brush of Apelles.

units.la: Pinguedo] Pinguitudo, Varr. Sagina, Iustin. Mercimonium, quo flamma alitur, Tac. Pingue, Plin. Pinguitia, Arn. Pinguefacere] vid. Saginare.
units.tr: Fatness: plumpness, Varr. Fattening feed, Justin. Fuel by which the flame is fed, Tac. Fat, Plin. Fatness, Arn. To fatten: see To feed up.

units.la: Pinguescere] Terra leguminibus gliscit. Perglíscere, Col. Sues crassescunt purgamentis, Plin. Quo cibo tantum corpus fecisti? Phædrus.
units.tr: To grow fat: the land swells with pulses. To grow fat thoroughly, Col. Pigs grow fat on refuse, Plin. "With what food did you make your body so large?" Phaedrus.

units.la: Pinguis] Opimus bos, Varr. Curatus corpore, Cat. Curatá cute, Hor. Habitior, Plaut. Popa venter, Perf. Cerea ficedula, Mart. Unctum olusculum, Hor. Unctiusculum pulmentum, Plaut. Unguinosus, Plin. Adipatus, Cic. Pulpâ & omentô gravatus, Cresfol. Crassus ager, Cic. Uber homo, Gell. Præpingue arbustum, Col. Vasto corpore farcinosus. Terga pulposis torulis obesa trahens, Apul. Porcus puer, Pompon.
units.tr: Fat: a fat ox, Varr. Well cared for in body, Cat. Cared for in skin, Hor. Plumper, Plaut. With a paunch, Pers. A fat fig-bird, Mart. Oily vegetables, Hor. A rather greasy dish, Plaut. Oily, Plin. Fatty, Cic. Weighed down with flesh and fat, Cresc. Rich field, Cic. A plump man, Gell. A very fat vineyard, Col. Burdened with a vast body. Dragging along fleshy lumps, Apul. A fat boy, Pompon.

units.la: Pinna] Pinnula. Brachium, Plin. Remi piscium.
units.tr: Fin: a little fin. A wing, Plin. The oars of fishes.

units.la: Pinsare] Pinsitare, Plaut. Pinsere: pinsunt far pilo, Var. Expinsere far, Cat.
units.tr: To pound: to crush, Plaut. They pound grain with a pestle, Varr. They have pounded the spelt, Cat.

units.la: Pinsatio] Pistura frumentorum, quæ fit pinsente pilo præserrato, Plin.
units.tr: Pounding: the grinding of grain, done by pounding with a serrated pestle, Plin.

units.la: Pinus, vid. Pinea.
units.tr: Pine, see Pinea.

units.la: Pipio] Pulli avium, &, infantes pulli, Plin.
units.tr: Chirping: the young of birds, and even very young chicks, Plin.

units.la: Pirata, vid. Prædator.
units.tr: Pirate, see Plunderer.

units.la: Piscari] Venari pisces, Plin. Colare amnes inductis retibus, Manil. Hamare, Petron.
units.tr: To fish: to hunt fish, Plin. To strain rivers with nets set across, Manil. To angle, Petron.

units.la: Piscarium forum] Piscaria, Varr. Forum cupedinis, Id. & Apul.
units.tr: Fish-market: a fish market, Varr. A market of delicacies, Id. and Apul.

units.la: Piscator] Jaculator, Isid. Piscinarius, Cic. Fures maritimos, & Famelicam hominum nationem, fame, siti, speque pereuntem, vocat Plaut.
units.tr: Fisherman: a spearman, Isid. A fisher, Cic. Plautus calls them sea-robbers and a starving race of men, perishing from hunger, thirst and hope.

units.la: Piscatorius] Piscarius, Col. Halieuticus, Trebell.
units.tr: Fishing: relating to fish, Col. Of fishing, Trebell.

units.la: Piscatus, vid. Captura.
units.tr: Caught, see Capture.

units.la: Pisces] Squamosus grex. Aquatile pecus, Col. Squamigerum genus. Pecudes natantes, mutæ, Lucr. Nerei pecus, Næo. Squamosum pecus. Neptuni pecus, Poëtic. Plaut.
units.tr: Fishes: a scaly flock. A water-dwelling herd, Col. A scaly kind. Silent swimming creatures, Lucr. The herd of Nereus, Naev. A scaly herd. The herd of Neptune, poetic, Plaut.

units.la: Plaut. Aquarum incolæ. Navis animata.
units.tr: Plaut. Dwellers of the waters. A living ship.

units.la: Piscina] Vivarium piscium, Col.
units.tr: Fishpond: a stock-pond for fish, Col.

units.la: Piscinalis.] Piscinarius, Plaut. Piscinensis, Lucil.
units.tr: Of a fishpond: of a fishpond, Plaut. Of a fishpond, Lucil.

units.la: Piscosus] Piscosus Tagus, Mart. Pisculentus fluvius, Cat.
units.tr: Full of fish: the Tagus abounding in fish, Mart. A river teeming with fish, Cat.

units.la: Pistillum] Pistillus, Virg. Pilum, Var.
units.tr: Pestle: a pestle, Virg. A pestle, Varr.

units.la: Pistor] Artocopus, Juv. Panifex, Sipont. Fornacarius, Vlp. Pistorienfis, Plaut.
units.tr: Baker: a bread-seller, Juv. A baker, Sipont. An oven-keeper, Ulp. Of Pistoia, Plaut.

units.la: Pistorius] Pistoricus, Vlp. Pistrinensis, Suet. Pistrinalis, Col. Ad cibaria coquenda & conficienda pertinens, Cic.
units.tr: Of the baker: of the bakehouse, Ulp. Of the mill, Suet. Of the mill, Col. Relating to the cooking and preparing of food, Cic.

units.la: Pistrinum] Artoptæum, Cæl. Rhod. Coctilitia taberna, Capitol. Pistrilla, Ter. Pistrella, Donat. Pistrina, Var.
units.tr: Bakehouse: a bakery, Cael. Rhod. A shop of baked goods, Capitol. A mill, Ter. A mill, Donat. Mills, Varr.

units.la: Pistrix] Coquula. Cocula, Var. Panifica mulier, Sipont.
units.tr: Cook: a cook, Varr. A cook-woman, Sipont.

units.la: Pituita] Phlegma, Sipont. Fomentum ignaviæ.
units.tr: Phlegm: phlegm, Sipont. Fuel of idleness.

units.la: Pituitosus] Phlegmaticus, Sipent.
units.tr: Phlegmatic: phlegmatic, Sipont.

units.la: Pius] Piissimus in Deos, Cic. Pietaticultrix, de Ciconia Petron. vid. Religiosus.
units.tr: Pious: most pious towards the gods, Cic. A devout woman, of the stork, Petron. See Religious.

units.la: Pius securus] Recte faciendo neminem time.
units.tr: A pious man is free from care: fear no one while doing right.

units.la: Pix] Picinum oleum, Sipont. Piffinum oleum, Plin. Hoc picis, Scrib. (Est id, quod oleosum supernè innatat, ut serum lactis, Gor.) Pisselæum, Id.
units.tr: Pitch: pitch oil, Sipont. Pitch oil, Plin. This is pitch, Scrib. (It is that which floats oily on top, like the whey of milk, Gor.) Pisselaeum, Id.

units.la: Placabiliter] Leniter agere, Liv. Perbenignè. Suaviter. Molliter. Placatè & humanè ferre humana omnia, Cic. Placidè, Plaut. Comiter appellare aliquem, Liv. Affabilissimè, Gell. Affabiliter, Macrob. Moderatè, Lentè, Cic.
units.tr: Placably: to act gently, Liv. Most kindly. Sweetly. Softly. To bear all human things calmly and humanely, Cic. Calmly, Plaut. To address someone courteously, Liv. Most affably, Gell. Affably, Macrob. Moderately, gently, Cic.

units.la: Placabilitas, vid. Clementia.
units.tr: Placability, see Clemency.

units.la: Placare] Pacare hostes, Ovid. Mitigare, Lenire, Pacatum reddere. Delenire animos. Recolligere animum alicujus offensiorem. Mactare deos extis, Cic. Demulcere, Gell Permulcere iras, Liv. Sedare, Propitiare, Plaut. Complacare, Gell. Oblenire, Pen. Piaculare Deos, Cat. Litare sævitiæ, Apul.
units.tr: To appease: to pacify enemies, Ovid. To soften, to allay, to make gentle. To soothe minds. To win back the mind of someone offended. To sacrifice to the gods with entrails, Cic. To soothe, Gell. To calm raging anger, Liv. To soothe, to propitiate, Plaut. To appease fully, Gell. To mollify, Pen. To propitiate the gods with expiation, Cat. To appease cruelty, Apul.

units.la: Placatio] Placamenta Deum, Tac. Mitigatio, Cic. Propitiationes pericul& avertunt, Sen.
units.tr: Appeasement: appeasing of the gods, Tac. Mitigation, Cic. Propitiations avert dangers, Sen.

units.la: Placere alicui] Placebam tibi facie, dote, Ovid. Neque placitant mores, Plaut. Probare alicui omnia facta dictaque sua, Plini. Quâ in legatione ita se probavit, ut &c. Cic.
units.tr: To please someone: "I pleased you by face and dowry," Ovid. "Nor do manners please," Plaut. To prove to someone all one's deeds and words, Plin. "In that embassy he so distinguished himself that," etc., Cic.

units.la: Placere omnibus nemo potest] Ne Jupiter quidem omnibus æquus. Nihil omnibus placet præter vinum & placentam, Lips.
units.tr: No one can please everyone: not even Jupiter is fair to all. Nothing pleases everyone except wine and cake, Lips.

units.la: Placet mihi aliquid] Perplacet, Placitum est. Collibitum est. Gratum est. Arridet mihi. Habeo gratum. Probatur mihi. Videtur. Commodum est. Quantum libido tulit, Cic. Complacitum est. Allubescit, Plaut. Libet, & lubet. Volupe est, Ter. Sedit nobis consilium, Amm. Amas quòd, Her. Amat bibere planta, Plaut. Facit ad stomachum meum, Mart. Hæc scire magis juvat, quàm prodest, Sen.
units.tr: It pleases me: it is very pleasing. It is decided. It is agreeable. It is welcome to me. I count it welcome. It is approved by me. It seems good. It is convenient. As much as desire prompted, Cic. It is agreed. It tickles, Plaut. It is delightful, Ter. Counsel has settled upon us, Amm. You love that, Her. The plant loves to drink, Plaut. It suits my stomach, Mart. It delights more to know these things than it profits, Sen.

units.la: Placere sibi] Amare se in re aliquâ. Gaudet in se: Se miratur ipse. usque adeone te diligis, & magnificè circumspicis, Cic. Plaudere sibi, Her.
units.tr: To please oneself: to be in love with oneself in some matter. He rejoices in himself: he admires himself. Do you love yourself so much and look so grandly about you? Cic. To applaud oneself, Her.

units.la: Non placere sibi] Pastidio laborat sui. Displicet sibi, Sen.
units.tr: Not to please oneself: he suffers from self-disgust. He is displeased with himself, Sen.

units.la: Placidè. vid. Placabiliter. Placiditas. Mansuetudo. Clementia.
units.tr: Gently: see Placably. Gentleness. Meekness. Clemency.

units.la: Placidus] Liquidus & tranquillus animus. Submissa & lenis oratio. Perurbana oratio, Cic. vid. Affabilis. Mansuetus.
units.tr: Calm: a clear and tranquil mind. A submissive and mild speech. A very urbane speech, Cic. See Affable. Meek.

units.la: Plaga] Percussio femoris, Verberatio, Cic. Verber, Ovid. Oppuvium, Non. ex Afran. Planctus pectoris, Lucan. Percussus. Pulsus, Plin.
units.tr: Blow: a striking of the thigh, a beating, Cic. A lash, Ovid. A slap, Non. from Afran. A beating of the breast, Lucan. A stroke. A push, Plin.

units.la: Plagiarius] Plagiator, Isid. Plagiarium agit, in Basil. Feles virginaria, Plaut.
units.tr: Plagiarius] A kidnapper, Isid. He practises kidnapping, in Basil. A cat for virgins, Plaut.

units.la: Plagosus. vid. Verbero.
units.tr: Plagosus. See Verbero.

units.la: Planca] Tabulæ, Liv. Assamenta, Plin.
units.tr: Planca] Boards, Liv. Planks, Plin.

units.la: Plane, vid. Penitus.
units.tr: Plane, see Penitus.

units.la: Planeta] Stellæ vagantes, Cic. Sidera errantia, Plin. Palantia, Lucr. Erroneæ stellæ, Gell. Stellavaga, Cic. Sep:em vitalia mundi viscera.
units.tr: Planeta] Wandering stars, Cic. Erring stars, Plin. Wanderers, Lucr. Erratic stars, Gell. Star-wanderer, Cic. The seven vital organs of the world.

units.la: Planetarius. vid. Astrologus.
units.tr: Planetarius. See Astrologus.

units.la: Plangor. vid. Ejulatus.
units.tr: Plangor. See Ejulatus.

units.la: Planities] Æquora camporum, Cic. Æquora plani campi, Plucr. Plana camporum, Amm. Planitia, Vitr. Planitudo, Pol. Planus situs, Minut. Porrecta & aperta loca, Cels. Æquum campi, Liv.
units.tr: Planities] Level stretches of fields, Cic. The level surface of a plain, Lucr. Flat plains, Amm. A plain, Vitr. Flatness, Pol. A level lie of the land, Minut. Open and stretched-out places, Cels. The level of a field, Liv.

units.la: Planta] Imus pes, Plin. Ima pedis, Plin. Virg. Vestigium carnosum, Plin.
units.tr: Planta] The lowest part of the foot, Plin. The sole of the foot, Plin. Virg. A fleshy footprint, Plin.

units.la: Planta, 2, i.e. ramulus] Surculus, Virg. Surculus praecisus, Pat. Summa ex arbore detracta planta. Stirps. Germen, Virg. Semen arboris, &, plantae, Varr. Col. Calamus pomi arboris. Insitum, Plin.
units.tr: Planta, 2, i.e. ramulus] A sprout, Virg. A cut-off sprout, Pat. A shoot torn from the top of a tree; a stock. A stem, Virg. A tree seedling, and plants, Varr. Col. A cutting from a fruit tree. A graft, Plin.

units.la: Plantago] Heptapleros. Stelephuros. Ortyx, (major sic vocatur, duplex n. est.) Plin. Arnoglossa, Iun. Nervalis, Scribon. (Minorem appellant.)
units.tr: Plantago] Heptapleros. Stelephuros. Ortyx (the larger is so called; there are two kinds), Plin. Arnoglossa, Iun. Nervalis, Scribon. (They call the smaller kind so.)

units.la: Plantare] Inserere plantas radicibus. Subserere arbores, Plin. Serere pullos arborum, Pat. Immittere plantas truncis. Inserere pyrum, Virg. Pangere malleolum. Subsero vineam. Inoculare arbores. Emplastrare arborem. Supplantare vitem, Col. Stirpes committere ramis, Lucr.
units.tr: Plantare] To insert plants into roots. To graft trees under. To sow tree shoots, Pat. To put plants into trunks. To graft a pear, Virg. To set a slip. To graft a vine. To inoculate trees. To plaster a tree. To layer a vine, Col. To join roots to branches, Lucr.

units.la: Plantarium] Seminarium plantarum, Col.
units.tr: Plantarium] A nursery of plants, Col.

units.la: Plantatio] Insitio arborum, Col. Cic. Insitus. Emplastratio arborum, Plin. Col. Inoculatio arborum. Id. Adulteria arborum, vocat Plin. insitiones. Immissio sarmentorum, Cic.
units.tr: Plantatio] Grafting of trees, Col. Cic. Insertion. Plastering of trees, Plin. Col. Inoculation of trees, Id. Pliny calls grafts the adulteries of trees, Plin. The insertion of twigs, Cic.

units.la: Planus] Locus planus & aequus. Aequabilis, Cic. Plana via. Aequalis ab omni parte, Ovid. Exactus ad regulam, Vitr. ad libellam, Id. Perlibrata area, planities, Col.
units.tr: Planus] A level and even place. Even, Cic. A plain road. Equal on every side, Ovid. Squared by the rule, Vitr. Squared by the level, Id. A thoroughly levelled area, a plain, Col.

units.la: Platea] Via urbis, Cic.
units.tr: Platea] A street of the city, Cic.

units.la: Plaudere manibus] Complodere manus, Sen. Concrepare digitis, Cic. Displodere, Var. Collidere manus, Quint.
units.tr: Plaudere manibus] To clap the hands together, Sen. To snap the fingers, Cic. To clap, Var. To knock the hands together, Quint.

units.la: Plausibilis] Ad gratiam est aliquid, Liv.
units.tr: Plausibilis] Something agreeable to favour, Liv.

units.la: Plaustrarius] Traharius, Sidon. Rhedarius, vehicularius fabricator, Capit. Carpentarius faber, Sipont.
units.tr: Plaustrarius] A cart-maker, Sidon. A carter, a maker of wagons, Capit. A carpenter, Sipont.

units.la: Plaustrum] Mandra, Prob. Rader. Currus longus, Hamaxa, Iul. Cap. Veha, vel Veja, Fest. Vehia, Sipont. Oneraria vehicula Carrum. Carpentum. Sarracum, Bud.
units.tr: Plaustrum] A cart, Prob. Rader. A long wagon, hamaxa, Iul. Cap. Veha or Veja, Fest. Vehia, Sipont. Freight wagons: a cart, a carpentum, a sarracum, Bud.

units.la: Plausus] Crepitus illisae manus, Sen. Sclopus, Perf. Stlopus, Priscian. Stloppus, Casaub & Marcel. (Sonus est, qui fit ex buccis inflatis, vi repentina ruptis.)
units.tr: Plausus] The rattle of clapping hands, Sen. A sclopus, Perf. Stlopus, Priscian. Stloppus, Casaub & Marcel. (It is a sound made from puffed cheeks, burst by sudden force.)

units.la: Plebejus obscurus] Ex quercubus & saxis nati. E multis unus. Plebeji feminis pullus, Col. De faece urbis. De plebeja faece. E circulo. In multis numerandus. Quem natum nemo novit. Nescio quis. Quintae classis homo. Cujus pater cubito se emungebat, Ad. Her. De plebe Deos, Ovid. Unus multorum, Hor. Ultima plebis homo, Sen. Virimi subsellii, Plaut. Vulgus, Sal. Sine nomine vulgus, Virg. Fraterculus gigantum, Iuv. Pedarius. Proletarius, Honn. Innatus triviis, Hor. vid, Vilis homo.
units.tr: Plebejus obscurus] Born of oaks and rocks. One of many. A chick of the common folk, Col. From the dregs of the city. From the common dregs. From the crowd. To be counted among the many. Whose birth nobody knows. Someone or other. A man of the fifth class. Whose father blew his nose on his elbow, Ad. Her. Gods of the common people, Ovid. One of many, Hor. The lowest man of the commons, Sen. A man of the lowest bench, Plaut. The common herd, Sal. A crowd without a name, Virg. A little brother of giants, Iuv. A foot-soldier. A proletarian, Honn. Born at the crossroads, Hor. See Vilis homo.

units.la: Plebiscitum ] Scitum populi. Scitum plebis, Fest. Rogatio. Lex popularis. Lex tribunitia, Cic. Psephisma, Id. Plebisve scita, apud Cic.
units.tr: Plebiscitum] A decree of the people. A decree of the plebs, Fest. A proposal. A popular law. A tribunician law, Cic. A psephisma, Id. Decrees of the plebs, in Cic.

units.la: Plebs ] Populus, Vulgus, Multitudo infima, Plebecula, Multi, Cic. Plebes, ei, Salust.
units.tr: Plebs] The people, the common folk, the lowest multitude, the rabble, the many, Cic. The plebs, Sallust.

units.la: Plebs inutilis ] Sordes & sex urbis, Cic. Nihil habent insigne. Turba sunt & numerantur tantùm, Sen. Numerus sumus, & fruges consumere nati, Hor. Ignota capita, Liv.
units.tr: Plebs inutilis] The dregs and filth of the city, Cic. They have nothing distinguished about them. They are a crowd and are only counted, Sen. We are a number, born to consume the harvest, Hor. Unknown heads, Liv.

units.la: Plebere ] (1.) Contexere, Tibul. Texere fiscellam, sepes. Viere scirpeas rates. Crines in aurum nodare, Virg. Sirpare aliquid virgis, Var. Cogere nodo comas, Sen.
units.tr: Plebere] (1.) To weave together, Tibul. To weave a basket or a hedge. To bind rush boats. To tie hair up in gold, Virg. To bind something with rods, Var. To gather locks with a knot, Sen.

units.la: Plebere capite (2.) vid. Decollare.
units.tr: Plebere capite (2.) See Decollare.

units.la: Plectrum ] Pecten, Sipont. Arcum lyricus, vel lyrae. Arcus lyricinis pilis equinis intentus.
units.tr: Plectrum] A comb, Sipont. The bow of a lyre, or of a lyre. A bow strung with horsehair lyre-strings.

units.la: Plene ] res penitus perspectæ, Cic. Integrè, Id. Planè perfectæ res, Id. Ad plenum, Virg. Pleno medio, gradu. Ad numerum. Solidum solvere, Cic. Ex toto, Cels. Ex asse. Insolidum, Vlp. Plena manu, Sen. In totum, Col. In assem, Plin. Iun. Ad ambas usque aures. Cum totâ ærugine reddere follem, Iuv.
units.tr: Plene] Things thoroughly examined, Cic. Wholly, Id. Things entirely perfected, Id. To the full, Virg. With a full middle step. In full measure. To pay a debt in full, Cic. Entirely, Cels. From the whole as. Undivided, Vlp. With a full hand, Sen. Wholly, Col. For the full as, Plin. Iun. Up to both ears. To give back the bellows with all its rust, Iuv.

units.la: Plenitudo ] Statura plena, Plin. Cacumen alescendi, Lucr. Plenum, Plin. Plenitas sententiarum, Tac. Expletio, Cic. ἡ ἀκμὴ.
units.tr: Plenitudo] Full stature, Plin. The height of growth, Lucr. Fullness, Plin. Fullness of sentences, Tac. Completion, Cic. ἡ ἀκμὴ [the prime, the peak].

units.la: Plenus ] Expletus omnibus suis partibus. Completus, Refertus, Refertissimus. Conferta vita voluptatibus, Cic. differtus facetiarum, Catul. Effertus, Plaut. distentus, Hor. Ebrius, Fartus, Sen. Integer, Cic. Justus, Quint. Solidus dies, Hor.
units.tr: Plenus] Filled in all its parts. Complete, stuffed, crammed. A life crowded with pleasures, Cic. Stuffed with witticisms, Catul. Puffed out, Plaut. Distended, Hor. Drunk, stuffed full, Sen. Whole, Cic. Just, Quint. A solid day, Hor.

units.la: Plerique ] Quam plures vestrûm, Cic. Plerique omnes. Complures. Complusculi, Ter. Ferè omnes, Col.
units.tr: Plerique] Far more of you, Cic. Almost all. Several. Quite a few, Ter. Nearly all, Col.

units.la: Plerumque, vid. Vulgò.
units.tr: Plerumque, see Vulgò.

units.la: Plexus ] Plectilis. Pactilis, Plin. Nexa corona, Hor. Vitilis cista, Plin. Textile sertum, Mart. Virgea sepes, Virg. Texta de vimine cista, Ovid.
units.tr: Plexus] Plaited. Woven, Plin. A tied garland, Hor. A wicker basket, Plin. A woven garland, Mart. A hedge of twigs, Virg. A basket woven of osier, Ovid.

units.la: Plica ] Stria. In veste rugas & sinus invenit Chæremon. Plin.
units.tr: Plica] A fold. Chaeremon found wrinkles and folds in the garment, Plin.

units.la: Plicare ] Complicare epistolam, Cic.
units.tr: Plicare] To fold up a letter, Cic.

units.la: Plicatura ] Structura togæ, Macrob. Tabulas, & Tabulata vestium, vocat Tertull. Contabulationes, Apul. Tabulata congregati pallii, Tertull.
units.tr: Plicatura] The arrangement of a toga, Macrob. Tertullian calls the folds and pleats of garments tabulae, Tertull. Contabulationes, Apul. The pleats of a gathered pallium, Tertull.

units.la: Placabundus ] Lacrymosus oculus, Plin. Largus lacrymarum, Plaut. Lacrymabundus, Liv.
units.tr: Placabundus] A tearful eye, Plin. Abounding in tears, Plaut. Weeping, Liv.

units.la: Plorare, vid. Flere. Ploratus, vid. Fletus.
units.tr: Plorare, see Flere. Ploratus, see Fletus.

units.la: Pluere ] Pluviae incessunt, vel incesserunt. Depluit, Col. Impluit in aliquem locum, Plin.
units.tr: Pluere] Showers come on, or came on. It rains down, Col. It rains into a place, Plin.

units.la: Pluere lapides ] Lapidare de cœlo. Pluit lapidibus, Liv. Depluit multus lapis in terras, Tibul.
units.tr: Pluere lapides] To rain stones from heaven. It rains stones, Liv. Much stone rains down upon the earth, Tibul.

units.la: Pluma ] Lana anserina, Vlp. Plumula, Col. Pensiles plumæ, Iuv. (i. e. molles lecticarum pulvini.)
units.tr: Pluma] Goose down, Vlp. A little feather, Col. Hanging feathers, Iuv. (i.e. the soft cushions of litters.)

units.la: Plumbare ] Applumbare, Vlp.
units.tr: Plumbare] To coat with lead, Vlp.

units.la: Plumbeus ]Plumbarius,Plin. Plumbosus, Plumbatus, Id.
units.tr: Plumbeus] Of lead, leaden, Plin. Full of lead, leaded, Id.

units.la: Plumeus ] Plumatilis, Plaut. Plumaria culcita, Sipont.
units.tr: Plumeus] Feathered, Plaut. A feather mattress, Sipont.

units.la: Plumosus, vid. Pennatus.
units.tr: Plumosus, see Pennatus.

units.la: Plures, plus quàm unus ]Oculi plus vident, quàm oculus.
units.tr: Plures, plus quàm unus] The eyes see more than the eye.

units.la: Plures vincunt ] Plurium calculi vincunt.
units.tr: Plures vincunt] The pebbles of many win.

units.la: Plus ] Amplius tibi liberorum esse gaudeo, Plaut. Plus plusque sospitent dii, Id. Super mille, Suet. Tac. Plus virium, Cic. vid. Magis.
units.tr: Plus] I rejoice that you have more children, Plaut. May the gods keep you safe more and more, Id. More than a thousand, Suet. Tac. More strength, Cic. See Magis.

units.la: Plus posce, ut minus obtineas ] Iniquum petendum, ut æquum feras.
units.tr: Plus posce, ut minus obtineas] It is unfair to ask for more, so that you may bear what is fair.

units.la: Plus impendere spe lucri ] Aureo hamo piscari.
units.tr: Plus impendere spe lucri] To fish with a golden hook.

units.la: Plus quàm ] Amplius triennium. Plusculum quàm. Magis magisque, Cic. Mediâ plus parte, Ovid. Plus plusque, Plaut. Supra tres, Her. Immenso plus. Immensum quantum. Plus satis. Plus quàm satis.
units.tr: Plus quàm] More than three years. A little more than. More and more, Cic. More than half, Ovid. More and more, Plaut. More than three, Her. Immensely more. Immeasurably great. More than enough. More than enough.

units.la: Pluviæ differentias, vid. in Ianua LL.
units.tr: Pluviæ differentias, see in Ianua LL.

units.la: Pluvialis ] Pluvius ros, Hor. Pluviatilis aqua. Cœlestis aqua, Col.
units.tr: Pluvialis] Rainy dew, Hor. Rainwater. Heavenly water, Col.

units.la: Pluviosus] Pluvius cœli status, Var. Pluvialis dies, Col. Nimbosus. Imbrifer, Virg. Imbricus auster, fluctusconstans, Plaut. Imbridum cœlum, Solin. Graves imbre nubes, Liv.
units.tr: Pluviosus] A rainy state of the sky, Var. A rainy day, Col. Cloudy. Rain-bringing, Virg. The south wind bringing rain, the waves constant, Plaut. A sky full of rain, Solin. Clouds heavy with rain, Liv.

units.la: Potillator] Ad cyathos, Prop. A potione, Meurs. Pinceina, Ascon. Ascon. Minister Falerni, Catul. Servus à lagena, Fulv. Vrsin. Suppromus, Plaut.
units.tr: Potillator] A server at the cups, Prop. From drinking, Meurs. Pinceina, Ascon. Ascon. A servant of Falernian wine, Catul. A servant from the flask, Fulv. Vrsin. Suppromus, Plaut.

units.la: Poculum ] Calix. Scyphus, Cic. Toreuma. Plin.
units.tr: Poculum] A cup. A goblet, Cic. A carved vessel, Plin.

units.la: Poculum magnum ] Poculum immane, Heracleum, Cic. Anancæum, Plaut. Modiales Phialæ, calices. Puteus argenteus. Propino tibi decumâ fonte. Argenteus puteus, Plaut. Athenæ. Amystis Threjicia, Hor. Crater Philotesius, Er.
units.tr: Poculum magnum] A huge cup, Heraclean, Cic. Anancaean, Plaut. Bowls of a peck measure, goblets. A silver well. I drink to you a tenth-fountain. A silver well, Plaut. Athenae. The Thracian Amystis, Hor. The Philotesian crater, Er.

units.la: Podagricus ] Podager, Claud. Podagrosus, Plin. Articularius, Plaut.
units.tr: Podagricus] A gouty man, Claud. Full of gout, Plin. Of the joints, Plaut.

units.la: Poëma ] Carmen, Cic. Poësis, Her. Pictura tacita. Vorsa facundia, Apul. Epigramma, Mart.
units.tr: Poëma] A song, Cic. Poetry, Her. Silent painting. Turned eloquence, Apul. An epigram, Mart.

units.la: Pœna ] Punitio, Cic. Disciplina, Quint. Supplicium. Multatio bonorum. Castigatio, Cic. Dedere aliquem noxæ. Liv. Censura, Juv. Censio, Piaculum, Liv. Vindicta legis, Ovid. Luela sceleris, Lucr. Malum, Plaut.
units.tr: Pœna] Punishment, Cic. Discipline, Quint. Torture. Forfeiture of goods. Chastisement, Cic. To hand someone over for damages, Liv. Censure, Juv. A penalty, an expiation, Liv. The vengeance of the law, Ovid. The atonement for a crime, Lucr. An evil, Plaut.

units.la: Pœna sit in exemplum ] Pœna unius multorum sit metus.
units.tr: Pœna sit in exemplum] Let the punishment of one man be the fear of many.

units.la: Pœnam quæris? ] Prurit tibi dorsum? Plaut.
units.tr: Pœnam quæris?] Does your back itch? Plaut.

units.la: Pœna venit, sera licet ] Quæ peccamus juvenes, luimus senes. Lento gradu ad vindictam sui divina procedit ira, sed tarditatem, gravitate supplicii compensat. Val. Max.
units.tr: Pœna venit, sera licet] What we sin in youth we pay for in old age. Divine wrath proceeds to vengeance with a slow step, but makes up for its tardiness by the severity of the punishment. Val. Max.

units.la: Pœnas dare ] Persolvere pœnas sceleris. Pœnas sceleris à se repetere. Pendere pœnas, Perferre, sustinere. Dependere pœnas exitiô. Multari morte, bonis, Cic. Piacularem fieri ob stultitiam alicujus, Plaut. Transfigere aliquod scelus pœnâ, Quint. Dedi pœnarum satis, Hor. Exsolvere pœnas. Ter. Pœnam luere, Tac. Peccatum luere, Liv.
units.tr: Pœnas dare] To pay the penalties of a crime. To exact the penalties of a crime from oneself. To hang penalties; to bear, to undergo. To pay penalties with ruin. To be punished by death, by loss of goods, Cic. To make oneself a sacrifice for someone's folly, Plaut. To expiate some crime by punishment, Quint. I have paid enough penalties, Hor. To pay penalties, Ter. To pay the penalty, Tac. To atone for a sin, Liv.

units.la: Pœnis afficere. v. Punire.
units.tr: To afflict with penalties. See Punish.

units.la: Pœnitentia ] Pœnitudo, Pacuv.
units.tr: Repentance] Regret, Pacuvius.

units.la: Pœnitet ] Piget facti. Suppœnitet me hujus rei. Acerbè fero, Cic. Indoluit facto, Ovid. Pœnitentia cœpti me tenet, Sen. Nihil me pœnitet, Cic. Habet me miserum animi petulantia mea. Dolet hoc cordi meo, Plaut, Pœnitentiam ago sermonis mei, Tac. Resìdere pœnitentiam, Plin. l. 34. c. 14. v. Resipiscere.
