units.tr: It repents me] It grieves me for the deed. I regret this matter. I bear it bitterly, Cic. He grieved at the deed, Ovid. The regret of what I have begun holds me, Sen. I regret nothing, Cic. My wantonness of mind holds me wretched. This grieves my heart, Plaut. I repent of my words, Tac. To lose one's regret, Plin. bk. 34, ch. 14. See Come to one's senses.

units.la: Poësis ] Poetica, Cic. Poetice, Non. Versificatio, Quint. Ars musica. Studium musicum, Ter.
units.tr: Poetry] Poetics, Cic. Poetically, Non. Versification, Quint. The art of music. The study of music, Ter.

units.la: Poëta ] Poëtius, Cic. Poëtificus, Enn. Museus, Lucr. Nectit quicunque canoris eloquium vocate modis, laurumque momordit, Iuv. Poëtæ Musarum aves. Epigrammaticus, Spart. Epigrammatarius, Vopisc. Versificator, Quint. Melicus, Cic. Musarum Sacerdos, Hor. Carminifex, Owen.
units.tr: Poet] Poetic, Cic. Poet-maker, Enn. Museus, Lucr. Whoever ties words to melodious measures and has bitten the laurel, Juv. The birds of the Muses. Writer of epigrams, Spart. Epigrammatist, Vopisc. Versifier, Quint. Lyric poet, Cic. Priest of the Muses, Hor. Maker of verses, Owen.

units.la: Polenta ] Hordeum tostum, Scalig. ex Var. Byne, Iun.
units.tr: Polenta] Toasted barley, Scalig. from Var. Byne, Iun.

units.la: Polio ] Armorum artifex, Trebel. Fabricensis, Amm. Samiator, qui, ferramenta fricando & poliendo splendida facit, & aciem eorum exasperat, Turneb.
units.tr: Polisher] Maker of arms, Trebel. Smith, Amm. One who makes metal tools shine by rubbing and polishing them, and roughens their edge, Turneb.

units.la: Polire ] Perpolire aliquid. Expolire, Plin. Expolitum dare opus, Plaut. depolire cote, Interradere, Var. v. Lævigare.
units.tr: To polish] To polish something thoroughly. To smooth, Plin. To give a finished work, Plaut. To polish with a whetstone, to shave smooth, Var. See To smooth.

units.la: Politè ] Limatè, Limatius, Politius, Concinnè, Compositè, Conclusè, Circumscriptè, rotundè dicere, Cic. Ad unguem, Hor. In unguem, Celf. Ad amussim, Var.
units.tr: Elegantly] Finely, more finely, more elegantly, neatly, concisely, precisely, roundly to speak, Cic. To the nail, Hor. To the last detail, Celf. To the square, Var.

units.la: Politia ] Res publica. Respublica, Cic. Commune Siciliæ (i, communitas) Apul. Civitas, Cæf. Corpus totum Reipub. curare, Cic. id est, Rempub. Publicum, Pac. Omne publicum, Apul.
units.tr: Polity] The commonwealth. The republic, Cic. The common good of Sicily (that is, the community), Apul. The state, Caes. To look after the whole body of the commonwealth, Cic., that is, to care for the republic. The public, Pac. Everything public, Apul.

units.la: Politica ] Politica scientia. Ratio administrandæ Reipub. secundùm virtutem & legem divinam. Gubernacula. Civilis ratio. Civitatis custodiendæ sapientia, Cic. Civilis scientia, Quint. Civilitas, Apul.
units.tr: Politics] The science of politics. The method of administering the commonwealth according to virtue and divine law. The helm. Civil method. The wisdom of guarding the state, Cic. Civil science, Quint. Civility, Apul.

units.la: Politicus bonus ] Vir administrandæ Reip. peritus. Administrator præclarus. Vir civilis. Publicarum privatarumque rerum administrationi accommodatus. Qui regere consiliis urbes, fundare legibus, emendare judiciis possit, Quint.
units.tr: A good politician] A man skilled in administering the commonwealth. An outstanding administrator. A man of civic affairs. One fit for the management of public and private affairs. One who can rule cities by counsel, found them on laws, and reform them by judgments, Quint.

units.la: Politulus ] Politus. Expolitus vitâ atque cultu. Comptus Cic. Immodicè fucatus formam, Lucan. Bellulus, Bellatulus, Plaut. Bellus, Mart. Scitus, Scitulus, Cic. Trossulus, Perf.
units.tr: Affected] Polished. Refined in life and manners. Elegant, Cic. Excessively painted in appearance, Lucan. Pretty, Plaut. Handsome, Mart. Witty, Cic. Dandified, Pers.

units.la: Politus ] Lævatus, Lævatior, Gell. Lævigatior, Mart. Limatus, Cic. Rasilis hasta, Sil. Expolitus liber pumice, Catul. Pumicatus, Mart. Lubricatus lapis, Arnob.
units.tr: Polished] Smoothed, smoother, Gell. Smoother still, Mart. Filed, Cic. A smooth spear, Sil. A book smoothed with pumice, Catul. Pumiced, Mart. A slippery stone, Arnob.

units.la: Pollere, v. Posse.
units.tr: To be powerful, see Be able.

units.la: Polliceri liberaliter ] Ducere aliquem phaleratis dictis, Ter. Largiri dictis, Plaut. Lingua largiri, Id. Aures vo-bis divitare, Accius. Aureos montes polliceri. Montes & maria polliceri. Polliceri haustum lactis gallinacei. Polliciris dives quilibet esse potest. Ovid.
units.tr: To promise generously] To lead someone on with gilded words, Ter. To give with words, Plaut. To give with the tongue, Id. To make ears rich, Accius. To promise golden mountains. To promise mountains and seas. To promise a draught of cock's milk. Anyone can be rich if he promises, Ovid.

units.la: Pollicitatio, vid. Promissio. Pollicitator, vid. Promissor. Pollincire, vid. Vngere. Pollinctor, vid. Vespillo. Pollubrum, vid. Pelvis. Pollucere, vid. Convivari. Polluere, vid. Contaminare.
units.tr: Promise, see Pledge. Promiser, see Promisor. To anoint, see Anoint. Undertaker, see Corpse-bearer. Washbasin, see Basin. To feast, see Dine. To pollute, see Defile.

units.la: Pomarium ] Hortus arboribus consitus, Cat. Col. Paradisus, Sipont. Pometum, Carif.
units.tr: Orchard] A garden planted with trees, Cato, Columella. Paradise, Sipont. Fruit grove, Carif.

units.la: Pomærium ] Pomerium, Cic. Summoenium, Sipont.
units.tr: Pomerium] Pomerium, Cic. Summoenium, Sipont.

units.la: Pomosus ] Pomifera arbor, Col. Fructifer, Plin.
units.tr: Fruitful] A fruit-bearing tree, Col. Bearing fruit, Plin.

units.la: Pompa ] Deductio alicujus honorifica. Comitatus, Cic. Profequium, Fest.
units.tr: Procession] An honourable escorting of someone. Retinue, Cic. Farewell, Fest.

units.la: Pomum ] Fructus, foetus arborum, Plin. Arboreus foetus, Virg.
units.tr: Fruit] The produce, the yield of trees, Plin. Tree-born yield, Virg.

units.la: Ponderare, vid. Librare. Ponderosus. vid. Gravis. Pondus. vid. Onus.
units.tr: To weigh, see To balance. Weighty, see Heavy. Weight, see Burden.

units.la: Pone ] Retro pono aliquid. A tergo. Ante & post. Posteriorem duco vitam libertate. Posthabeo aliquid alicui, Cic. Post tergum equitatus cernitur, Caes. Secundum sequi, ire, Plaut. Poltvenio, Plin.
units.tr: Behind] To put something behind. At the back. Before and after. I count life as less than freedom. To set one thing below another, Cic. Cavalry is seen behind, Caes. To follow or go second, Plaut. Behind, Plin.

units.la: Ponere, vid. ipsius Composita.
units.tr: To put, see its compounds.

units.la: Pontem facere ] Cic. Cingere fossam ponticulo, Cic. Indere pontem fluvio, Tac. Jungere ponte fluvium, Curt. Conjunxit ponte Capitolium & Palatium. Contabulavit pontem, Suet.
units.tr: To make a bridge] Cic. To surround a ditch with a little bridge, Cic. To throw a bridge over a river, Tac. To join a river with a bridge, Curt. He joined the Capitol and the Palatine with a bridge. He floored the bridge, Suet.

units.la: Pontem destruere ] Interrumpere, disturbate, interscindere a tergo pontem, Cic.
units.tr: To destroy a bridge] To break, disrupt, or cut down a bridge behind one, Cic.

units.la: Pontifex. vid. Episcopus.
units.tr: High priest, see Bishop.

units.la: Popina ] Ganea, Suet. Taberna coquinaria, Plin. Thermopolium, Plaut.
units.tr: Eating-house] A cookshop, Suet. A kitchen shop, Plin. A place selling hot food, Plaut.

units.la: Popinari, vid. Bacchari.
units.tr: To frequent taverns, see To revel.

units.la: Poppysmus ] Poppysma, Juv. Sibilum pastoritium, Ovid. Sibilus, Virg. Sclopus, Pers. vid. Clausus.
units.tr: Whistling] A whistle, Juv. A shepherd's whistle, Ovid. A whistle, Virg. A clapping, Pers. See Shut.

units.la: Poppizare ] Sibilare ore, Virg. Allectare sibilo boves
units.tr: To whistle] To whistle with the mouth, Virg. To lure oxen with a whistle

units.la: ut bibant, Col. Sibilô signum dare, Liv.
units.tr: so that they drink, Col. To give a signal with a whistle, Liv.

units.la: Populari, vid. Vastare.
units.tr: To lay waste, see To devastate.

units.la: Popularis ] Plebejus. Concionalis clamor, Turmalis Statua, Valet in vulgus. Probatur in vulgus, Cic. Catervalis pugil, Suet. Acceptum in vulgus, Tac.
units.tr: Popular] Plebeian. A shout of the crowd. A statue in the street. It is current among the common people. It is approved by the common people, Cic. A boxer of the mob, Suet. Received among the common people, Tac.

units.la: Populosus ] Floret hominum celebritate locus. Celebrantur viæ multitudine hominum. Frequens municipium, Cic. Frequens urbs populis, Lucan. Referta hominum oppida, Var. Celeber, Ovid. Refertissimum celebritate theatrum, Cic. Forum celeberrimum tanta frequentiâ, Id.
units.tr: Populous] A place flourishes with a crowd of people. Streets are thronged with a multitude of people. A crowded town, Cic. A city crowded with people, Lucan. Towns crammed with people, Varro. Crowded, Ovid. A theatre packed with a crowd, Cic. A forum most crowded with such a throng, Id.

units.la: Populus ] Multitudo, Cic. Populositas, Arnob. vid. Plebs.
units.tr: People] A multitude, Cic. Populousness, Arnob. See Commons.

units.la: Porca. vid. Lira. Porcarius, vid. Subulcus.
units.tr: Sow. See Furrow. Swineherd, see Pig-keeper.

units.la: Porcellus ] Porcus lacteus, Col. Porculus, Plin. Catulus suis, Plaut. Fœtus suis, Cic.
units.tr: Piglet] A suckling pig, Col. A little pig, Plin. A young of a sow, Plaut. The offspring of a sow, Cic.

units.la: Porcus. vid. Sus.
units.tr: Pig. See Swine.

units.la: Pori in corpore ] Meatus articulares, Plin. Invisibilia foramina, Celf. Caulæ corporis, Lucr.
units.tr: Pores in the body] Joint passages, Plin. Invisible openings, Celf. Crevices of the body, Lucr.

units.la: Porrigere aliquid ] Tradere in manus, Liv. Ministrare, Cic. Propinare alicui partem edendam, Capitol. Contradere argumenta, Lucr. Protensâ manu dare, Ovid. Protendere dextram nanti, Id.
units.tr: To hold something out] To hand over into the hands, Liv. To serve, Cic. To offer a portion to someone to eat, Capitol. To put forward arguments, Lucr. To give with an outstretched hand, Ovid. To hold out the right hand to a swimmer, Id.

units.la: Porrò. vid. Vlterius.
units.tr: Moreover. See Further.

units.la: Porta ] Pyla, Cic.
units.tr: Gate] A gateway, Cic.

units.la: Portendere ] Præmonstrare. Præsignificare hominibus futura, Cic.
units.tr: To portend] To show beforehand. To signify future things to men, Cic.

units.la: Portentum, portentosus, vid. Monstrum.
units.tr: Portent, portentous, see Monster.

units.la: Porticus ] Porticula, Cic Peristylium, Vitr.
units.tr: Portico] A little portico, Cic. A peristyle, Vitr.

units.la: Portio ] Pars, Suet. De mensâ mittere, Cic. De coenâ mittere, Suet. de prandio, Capit. Bolus, Var.
units.tr: Portion] A part, Suet. To send from the table, Cic. To send from dinner, Suet. From the midday meal, Capitol. A morsel, Varro.

units.la: Portitor ] Lintrarius, Vlp. Ratiarius, Paul. I. C. Navicula-tor. Navicularius. Nauta, Cic. Porthmæus, Inv.
units.tr: Ferryman] A boatman, Ulpian. A raftsman, Paul the jurist. A little boat-man. A ship-owner. A sailor, Cic. Ferryman of the dead, Inv.

units.la: Portorium ] Naulum, Iud. Vecturæ quadrans, Var. Quadrans ratitus, Lucil.
units.tr: Toll] Fare, Iud. The quarter-coin of a passage, Varro. A quarter-coin of a ferry, Lucil.

units.la: Portus ] Cataplus, Sidon. Cothon. Fest. Servaculum, Vlp.
units.tr: Harbour] A landing place, Sidon. A basin for ships, Fest. A small safe place, Ulpian.

units.la: Posse ] Potis sum, ut, Plaut. Queo. Ut facultas tulit, fecimus. Quid dicere habeant. Sustinere, Cic. Non quitus sum impelli, Acci. Valere, Pollere, Liv. Habere potestatem. Est potestate. Sum praeditus potestate. Est mihi potestas, facultas, hujus rei. Est id meae facultatis. Integra est mihi potestas. Tota potestas mea est, Cic. Est potestas adipiscendi, Plaut.
units.tr: To be able] I am able, that, Plaut. I can. As far as my means allowed, I did it. What they may have to say. To hold out, Cic. I was not able to be pushed, Accius. To prevail, to be strong, Liv. To have the power. He is in power. I am endowed with power. I have the power, the means, of this matter. This is within my means. My power over it is unimpaired. My whole power is mine, Cic. There is a chance of gaining it, Plaut.

units.la: Si non possumus ut volumus, velimus ut possumus ] Destitutus ventis, remos adhibe.
units.tr: If we cannot do as we wish, let us wish as we can] When the winds fail, use the oars.

units.la: Pro posse, barb. ] Pro mea, tua virili. v. Pro.
units.tr: As far as possible, barbarous] As far as my, your, manly strength allows. See For.

units.la: Possessio ] Usus agri aut aedificii, Fest. Ditio, Cic. Arae & foci, Id. v. Facultates.
units.tr: Possession] Use of a field or building, Fest. Dominion, Cic. Altars and hearths, Id. See Resources.

units.la: Possessor ] Possestrix, Non. Auctor, Cic.
units.tr: Possessor] A female possessor, Non. An author, Cic.

units.la: Possibilis ] Fieri potest, Cic. Possibile. Cadit in rerum naturam, Quint. Ejus rei potestas mihi, vel mea est, Cic. Res viribus & potentatui tuo conveniens, Arnob.
units.tr: Possible] It can happen, Cic. Possible. It falls within the nature of things, Quint. It is in my power, or is mine, to do this, Cic. A thing suited to your strength and power, Arnob.

units.la: Possibilitas ] Potestas adipiscendi. Plaut.
units.tr: Possibility] The power of attaining, Plaut.

units.la: Possidere ] Occupare, usurpare possessionem aliquam. Potiri gazae. Obsidere praesidiis Italiam. Tenere hereditatem. Esse in bonis, in possessione, Cic.
units.tr: To possess] To seize, to take possession of something. To get hold of treasure. To occupy Italy with garrisons. To hold an inheritance. To be in goods, in possession, Cic.

units.la: Postea v. Deinde.
units.tr: Afterwards, see Then.

units.la: Posteri ] Posteritas, Cic. Post futuri. Sal. Et nati natorum, & qui nascentur ab illis. Minores, i, posteri Nepotes, Virg. Qui erunt, & qui futuri sunt, Plaut. Minorum aetas, Apul.
units.tr: Posterity] Posterity, Cic. Those who are to come, Sall. The sons of sons, and those who will be born of them. The younger generation, or posterity. Grandchildren, Virg. Those who will be and who are to come, Plaut. The age of the younger ones, Apul.

units.la: Posteriora sunt meliora ] Posteriores cogitationes sunt sapientiores primis.
units.tr: Later things are better] Later thoughts are wiser than first ones.

units.la: Posteriora prius agit ] Antidotum ante venenum.
units.tr: He does the later thing first] An antidote before the poison.

units.la: Posthumus ] Posthuma proles, Ter.
units.tr: Posthumous] A posthumous child, Ter.

units.la: Posticum ] Posticula, Apul. Pseudothyrum, Cic. Pseudothyrum palatii, Amm.
units.tr: Back door] A little back door, Apul. A back door, Cic. A back door of the palace, Amm.

units.la: Posticus ] Postica domus. Postica pars aedium, Liv. Aversa pars capitis cervix. Retrorsa manus, Plin. Retrorsa respicere, Apul.
units.tr: Back] A back house. The back part of a building, Liv. The back part of the head, the nape. A hand turned backwards, Plin. To look back, Apul.

units.la: Postliminio recipere, v. Recuperare.
units.tr: To recover by right of return, see To recover.

units.la: Postponere ] Posthabere aliquid alicui. Posteriorem ducere vitam libertate. Retro ponere, Cic. Postferre aliquid alicui, Liv. Omnia sibi postputavit prae meo commodo, Ter.
units.tr: To postpone] To rank something below another. To count life as less than freedom. To put behind, Cic. To set one thing after another, Liv. He reckoned all things secondary to my advantage, Ter.

units.la: Postquam ] Postea vero quam. Ubi audivit. Simul ac, atque, Cic. Jam revertar, si exquisivero, Plaut.
units.tr: After] Afterwards indeed, when. When he heard. As soon as, and, Cic. I will return when I have made enquiry, Plaut.

units.la: Postremus] Imi subsellii vir, vid. Ultimus.
units.tr: Last] A man of the lowest bench, see Final.

units.la: Postridie] Postridie ejus diei. Postridie quàm à vobis discessi. Postridie ludos, Cic. Posterò. Tac. Deincepiti die, Apul.
units.tr: The next day] The day after that day. The day after I left you. The day after the games, Cic. On the following day, Tac. The next morning, Apul.

units.la: Postulare] Poscere aliquid aliquem, & ab aliquo. Deposcere, Requirere, desiderare, Flagitare, Cic.
units.tr: To demand: to ask something of someone, or to ask of someone. To demand urgently, to require, to desire, to importune, Cic.

units.la: Postulatum] Postulatio, Efflagitatio, Efflagitatus, Conditio, Cic.
units.tr: A demand: a request, an urgent demand, an insistent claim, a condition, Cic.

units.la: Potare] Potitare, Plaut. Voluptate potandi fruī, Cic.
units.tr: To drink: to drink habitually, Plaut. To enjoy the pleasure of drinking, Cic.

units.la: Potare largius] Largiùs se invitare, vel alterum.
units.tr: To drink more freely: to invite oneself more generously, or to invite another.

units.la: Potare aliquem] Dare potionem, Quint. Dare potatum bubus, Col. Potandum praebere, faucibus infundere, Id.
units.tr: To give someone to drink: to give a potion, Quint. To give cattle water to drink, Col. To offer something to be drunk, to pour into the throat, Id.

units.la: Potator] Potor, Plin. Bibo, Firm. Magister bibendi, vid. Ebriosus.
units.tr: Drinker: a tippler, Plin. One who drinks, Firm. A master of drinking; see Drunkard.

units.la: Potens] Valens opibus & potentiae. In magna potentia est. Praepotens terrae marique. Homo potentissimus, Cic. Factiosus. Multipotens, Plaut. Pollens factionibus, Apul.
units.tr: Powerful: strong in resources and power. He is of great power. Mighty over land and sea. A most powerful man, Cic. Factious. Mighty in many things, Plaut. Strong in factions, Apul.

units.la: Potentes non coeunt] Mons cum monte non committetur.
units.tr: Powerful men do not unite: mountain will not meet mountain.

units.la: Potentes non patiuntur moneri] Montes tange, & fumigabunt.
units.tr: Powerful men will not suffer admonition: touch the mountains and they will smoke.

units.la: Potentes provocare ad sui exitium] Leonem stimulare.
units.tr: To provoke the powerful to their own ruin: to goad the lion.

units.la: Potentia] Opum nimiarum potentia. Ad sua conservanda, & alterius obtinenda idonearum rerum facultas. Numen Senatus, Potestas. Facultas. Fortitudo militum, vel militaris. Vires adolescentis, virtutis, Cic. Manus, Tac. Pollentia impiorum, Plaut. Vehementia odoris, Plin. vid. Robur.
units.tr: Power: power of excessive wealth; the ability to preserve one's own and obtain another's by suitable means. The authority of the Senate, sovereignty, capacity. The strength of soldiers, or military might. The vigour of a young man, of virtue, Cic. Hand, Tac. The might of the wicked, Plaut. The vehemence of a smell, Plin.; see Strength.

units.la: Potentia & amor non ferunt socium] Nec regna socium, nec taedae sciunt. Nulla fides regni sociis; omnisque potestas impatiens consortis erit.
units.tr: Power and love do not bear a partner: neither kingdoms nor marriage tolerate a companion. No kingdom can trust a partner; all power will be impatient of a sharer.

units.la: Potestas] Habere summam potestatem alicubi. Ejus numini parent omnia. Regnum senis. Nutus Jovis, Cic. Arbitrium vestri Romulus habet. Jus, Liv.
units.tr: Power: to hold supreme power somewhere. All things obey his divine will. The rule of an old man. The nod of Jove, Cic. Romulus holds your judgement in his hand. Right, Liv.

units.la: Potestas omnis à deo est] Quicquid dominatur, vim Dei habet.
units.tr: All power is from God: whatever holds dominion has the power of God.

units.la: In Potestate habere] In manu est. In regno meo est. In tuo luco & fano est situm. Intra tuas præsepes, Plaut. In te, in tua potestate, situm est. In te sita est potestas. Tota ejus facultas tua est. Penes te, me, illum, est potestas. Arbitrium tuum sit orationis custodiendæ, Cic. Penes te arbitrium vitæ necisque, Ovid. Ifleo remigio rem gero, Turneb.
units.tr: To have in one's power: it is in one's hand; it is in my kingdom; it lies in your grove and temple; within your stalls, Plaut. It lies in you, in your power; power is placed in you; all his ability is yours. The power rests with you, with me, with him. Let it be your judgement to guard the speech, Cic. The judgement over life and death rests with you, Ovid. I manage the affair with this oarage, Turneb.

units.la: Potio] Poculentum, Cic. Potulentum, Vlp. Potiuncula, Suet.
units.tr: Potion: a drink, Cic. A beverage, Vlp. A little drink, Suet.

units.la: Potiri] Tenere, Plin. Compotem fieri, Cic. vid. Possidere. Potius] Abeo potius, Ter. (Eleganter aliquando omittitur potius, sequente particulâ quàm.) Tacita mulier est bona, quàm loquens, Tac. Pot. Pro Meliore nobis fuit hostes effugere, Cic. Magis. Optandum magis, quàm sperandum, Cic.
units.tr: To gain possession of: to hold, Plin. To become master of, Cic.; see To possess. Rather: "I will go rather," Ter. (Sometimes potius is elegantly omitted when followed by the particle quam.) A silent woman is good rather than a talkative one, Tac. Rather, instead: it was better for us to escape the enemy, Cic. More: it is more to be wished for than to be hoped for, Cic.

units.la: Potus] Potura, Var. Haustus, Ovid. In medià potione exclamavit, Cic. Potatio, Plaut.
units.tr: Draught: a drink, Var. A swallow, Ovid. In the middle of his drinking he cried out, Cic. A drinking bout, Plaut.

units.la: Præbenda] æ. Præbenda, Plin. Gell. Annuum, Suet. Sportula, Cypri. Præbitiones (salis is) Vlp.
units.tr: Stipend: a stipend, Plin. Gell. An annual allowance, Suet. A dole, Cypr. Allowances of salt, Vlp.

units.la: Præbendarius] Sportularius, Cypr. Alimentarius, Capit.
units.tr: Recipient of a stipend: one who receives a dole, Cypr. One maintained at public expense, Capit.

units.la: Prebere, vid. dare. Subminist.
units.tr: To provide; see to give. Subminist.

units.la: Præbibere, vid. Propinare. Præbitor, vid. Dator.
units.tr: To drink first to someone; see to pledge. A provider; see giver.

units.la: Præcavere] Præcavere alicui, Ter. Facere aliquem cautiorem, Cuf. Præmonere à periculis. Cavere alicui. Cautionem adhibere, Cic.
units.tr: To take precaution: to be on one's guard against someone, Ter. To make someone more cautious, Cuf. To warn of dangers. To beware of someone. To apply caution, Cic.

units.la: Præcutor] Cautor, Plaut. Præa monitor, Cic.
units.tr: Cautious one: a guardian, Plaut. One who warns beforehand, Cic.

units.la: Precedere] Præcurrere aliquem, & alicui. Antegredi. Anteire alicui. Anticipare molestiam. Prætergredi castra. Prævertere aliquem. Prævolare, Cic. Præcurrere adventum alicujus in aliquem locum, Plin. Iun. Præire, Liv. Ire præ, Plaut. Anteire ventos, Sil. Antevenire aliquem magnis itineribus, Stat. Antevertere alicui, Ter. Antevolare currum, Stat. Prævenire alicujus desiderium. Præoccupare, Liv. Antecapere aliquem, Sal. Opprimere, Plaut. Occupare aliquem, Virg. Ovid. Præcellere] Præstare in arte aliquâ, Lucr. Eminere, Liv. Tenere principatum, principem locum. Primas ferre, tenere. Primas partes agere. Penes illum est principatus. Ducere familiam. In hoc uno regnat, Cic. Principatus est avibus. Primatum obtinere. Palmam alicujus rei habere, Plin. Priores partes habere, Ter. Signa ferre, Sen. Equis albis præcedere. Primum esse. Nulli secundum esse. Nullo inferiorem esse. Nulli cedere. Nemine posterior. Antesignanus. Omnes procul à se reliquit. Omnes à tergo reliquit: Longo intervallo præcellit. Eloquentiæ artem tenet. Primam laudem obtinet. Stadiis centum præcedere, Eraf. Præmia prima feres, Virg.
units.tr: To precede: to run ahead of someone or to someone. To go before. To get in front of someone. To anticipate trouble. To pass beyond the camp. To outstrip someone. To fly ahead, Cic. To run ahead to announce someone's arrival at a place, Plin. Iun. To go before, Liv. To go in front, Plaut. To outrun the winds, Sil. To outstrip someone by great journeys, Stat. To get ahead of someone, Ter. To fly ahead of a chariot, Stat. To anticipate someone's wish. To forestall, Liv. To seize beforehand, Sal. To catch someone out, Plaut. To take hold of someone, Virg. Ovid. To excel: to surpass in some art, Lucr. To stand out, Liv. To hold the leading place, the first position. To bear and hold the palm. To act the chief part. The leadership belongs to him. To lead the household. He reigns alone in this, Cic. Leadership belongs to birds. To hold the primacy. To have the palm of something, Plin. To have the first place, Ter. To carry the standards, Sen. To go before on white horses. To be first. To be second to no one. To be inferior to no one. To yield to no one. To be second to none. A standard-bearer. He has left everyone far behind him. He has left all behind his back. He surpasses by a long interval. He holds the art of eloquence. He obtains the first praise. To outrun by a hundred stades, Eraf. You will bear the first prizes, Virg.

units.la: Præceps] Præceps in aliquid animus, Liv. Præcox pugna, Enn. Præpropera festinatio, Cic. Quicquid agit, properat omnia, Plaut. Præcipitia ingenia, Curt. Proruptα audacia. Volaticus impetus. Præcipiti quâdam celeritate volubilis homo, Cic. Rapidus, Virg.
units.tr: Headlong: a mind inclined headlong to something, Liv. An early battle, Enn. Overhasty haste, Cic. Whatever he does, he hurries; he does everything in haste, Plaut. Rash minds, Curt. Reckless boldness. Impetuous rush. A man who is whirled along with a certain headlong speed, Cic. Swift, Virg.

units.la: Præceptor, vid. Doctor.
units.tr: Teacher; see Doctor.

units.la: Præcerpere] Præcerpere fructus officii alicujus, Cic. Præsumere remedium, Ter. Præcipere fructum, Col. Debitum, dotem, Vlp.
units.tr: To pluck beforehand: to pluck the fruits of someone's duty, Cic. To take a remedy in advance, Ter. To gather fruit early, Col. A debt, a dowry, Vlp.

units.la: Præcidere, vid. Abscindere. Præcipere, vid. Iubere.
units.tr: To cut off; see to cut away. To instruct; see to command.

units.la: Præcipitanter] Præproperanter, Lucr. Præproperè, Liv. Præfestinè, Plaut. Nimium festinanter. Turbulentè, Cic. Præmaturè, Gell. Tumultuariè & raptim, Amm.
units.tr: Hastily: very hurriedly, Lucr. Too hastily, Liv. Over-hastily, Plaut. Too hurriedly. Tumultuously, Cic. Prematurely, Gell. In a tumultuous and hasty manner, Amm.

units.la: Præcipitantia] Præcipitatio, Sen. Præpropera festinatio. Immaturitas & festinatio. Impetus animi, Cic.
units.tr: Precipitancy: headlong haste, Sen. Overhasty rushing. Immaturity and haste. An impulse of mind, Cic.

units.la: Præcipitantia cavenda] Festinatio improvida & cæca est, Liv. Festinatio pœnitudinis mater. Mala cuncta ministrat impetus. Offendit qui festinis est pedibus. Cunctari solet vir, qui magna molitur. Canis festinans cœcos parit catulos.
units.tr: Precipitancy to be avoided: rash haste is blind and heedless, Liv. Haste is the mother of repentance. Impulse furnishes every evil. He who hurries on foot stumbles. A man who undertakes great things is wont to delay. A hurrying dog bears blind whelps.

units.la: Præcipitare, aliquem] Dare præcipitem; in præceps, Liv. Ter. Jacere in præceps aliquem, Tac. Præcipitem agere aliquem de. Dejicio præcipitem, Cic. Deturbare præcipitem, Virg. Mittere pronum aliquem, Catul. In præceps adigere, deturbare, projicere, Virg. In caput dejicere, Lucil. Projicere præcipitem in undas, Virg. Mittere præcipitem de muro, Hirt.
units.tr: To hurl someone headlong: to throw headlong, Liv. Ter. To cast someone down headlong, Tac. To drive someone headlong from. To throw down headlong, Cic. To hurl down headlong, Virg. To send someone prone, Catul. To drive down headlong, to cast down, to throw, Virg. To fling down on the head, Lucil. To throw headlong into the waves, Virg. To send headlong from a wall, Hirt.

units.la: Præcipitare se. vid. Cadere præcip. Præcipitare, vid. Festinare.
units.tr: To throw oneself headlong; see to fall headlong. To hurry; see to hasten.

units.la: Præcipuè] Principaliter, Vlp. Cumprimis, Cic. Apprimè, Ter. vid. Singulariter.
units.tr: Especially: principally, Vlp. Above all, Cic. Very much, Ter.; see singularly.

units.la: Præcipuus] Unus multorum instar. Unus pro centum millibus, vid. Primarius.
units.tr: Special: one who is worth many. One who is worth a hundred thousand; see Primary.

units.la: Præclarè vid. Eximiè. Præclarus, vid. Excellens. Celebris.
units.tr: Splendidly; see excellently. Famous; see excellent. Celebrated.

units.la: Præcludere, vid. Excludere.
units.tr: To shut out; see to exclude.

units.la: Præco] Prædicator, Cic. Prænuntius, Ovid. Enunciativus, Sen. Curio, Iul. Clamator, & Proclamator, ex Cic. Præclamitator, Fest. Calo, Hor.
units.tr: Herald: a proclaimer, Cic. A forerunning messenger, Ovid. An announcer, Sen. A town crier, Iul. A crier and proclaimer, from Cic. A shouter, Fest. A crier, Hor.

units.la: Præcogitare, vid. Præmeditari.
units.tr: To forethink; see to premeditate.

units.la: Præcognoscere aliquid] Præcipere aliquid animo, Virg. Liv. Præsagire aliquid animo. Præscitcere, Liv. Præsagior aliquid, (dep.) Prædivinare, Prosentire, Plaut. Præscire aliquid, Præsentiscere. Subolet mihi, Ter. Præsentire aliquid. Videre aliquid, Videre animo aliquid, Multùm, plurimum videre in re aliqua, Valdè videre. Olfacere. Odorari sagacissimè. Longè prospicere futuros casus, Cic. Prænoscere aliquid venturum, Stat. Prospeculari, Amm.
units.tr: To foreknow something: to perceive something in advance in the mind, Virg. Liv. To have a presentiment of something in the mind. To know beforehand, Liv. I have a presentiment of something, Plaut. To foresee, to have a sense of something beforehand. Something tells me, Ter. To sense something beforehand. To see something. To see something in the mind. To see much or most in a matter. To see clearly. To smell out. To scent most keenly. To look far ahead to future chances, Cic. To know beforehand that something will come, Stat. To spy out beforehand, Amm.

units.la: Præcox] Præmaturus fructus, Col. Præciæ uvæ, Plin. Virg. Præcoquæ, Col. (Præcoqui fructu, item, Præcoquem, Præcoques, à Præcoquis Recto, apud Colum. reperiuntur.) Maturissimus, Id. Maturrimus, Tac. Tempestivus fructus, Cic. Prodromos ficus, Plin. Protericus, Macrob.
units.tr: Early: early ripening fruit, Col. Early grapes, Plin. Virg. Early-ripe, Col. (The forms praecoqui fructu, likewise praecoquem and praecoques, from the nominative praecoquis, are found in Col.) Most mature, Id. Very mature, Tac. Timely fruit, Cic. Early figs, Plin. Early-ripening, Macrob.

units.la: Præcox judicium] Ante barbam doces senes. Ante pilos sapit. Ingenio canus & ante canos.
units.tr: Precocious judgement: you teach old men before their beards grow. He is wise before he has hair. Grey in wit and before grey hairs.

units.la: Præcocia haud diuturna] Odi pueros præcoci sapientiæ. Quod citò fit, cito perit. Fugacia sunt poma præcocia.
units.tr: Precocious things are not lasting: I dislike boys with precocious wisdom. What is done quickly perishes quickly. Early fruits are fleeting.

units.la: Præcurrere vid. Præcedere.
units.tr: To run before; see to precede.

units.la: Præcursio] Præcursus Etesiarum, Plin. Anteversio, Prægressus, Amm. Antecessio rerum. Prægressio causæ. Anticipatio deorum, Cic. Antecessus, Sen.
units.tr: Forerunning: the forerunning of the Etesian winds, Plin. A going before, a preceding, Amm. Anticipation of events. The forerunning of a cause. The anticipation of the gods, Cic. A going before, Sen.

units.la: Præcursor, vid. Antecessor.
units.tr: Forerunner; see predecessor.

units.la: Præda] Spolium, Plin. Exuviæ. Manubiæ, Cic. Rapta præmia, Tibull. Bello parta.
units.tr: Booty: plunder, spoil, Plin. Spoils, Cic. Seized prizes, Tibull. Won in war.

units.la: Prædari] Grassari, Non. Prædas agere, agitare, Sallust. Facere prædas. Latrocinari. Infestam reddere provinciam latrociniis, Cic. Agere latrocinia, Iat. Vivere rapto, Ovid.
units.tr: To plunder: to rage about, Non. To drive off booty, to carry on plunder, Sall. To make booty. To play the robber. To make a province unsafe through robberies, Cic. To carry on brigandage, Iat. To live by plunder, Ovid.

units.la: Prædator] Prædo, Næv. Spoliator, direptor urbis. Pirata. Insidiator viæ, Cic. Catillo, Fest. Aggressor, Vlp.
units.tr: Plunderer: a robber, Naev. A despoiler, a sacker of a city. A pirate. A highwayman, Cic. A cudgel, Fest. An aggressor, Vlp.

units.la: Prædatorius] Piraticus myoparo (navis nomen) Cic. Prædacea navis. Prædatica pecunia, Gell. Prædonius, Vlp.
units.tr: Predatory: piratical; a pirate ship (name of a vessel), Cic. A raiding ship. Money gained by plunder, Gell. Predatory, Vlp.

units.la: Prædicere] Prædivinare, Varr. Prænunciare, Antenunciare, Antedicere. Dii aliquid præmonstrant & præcinunt, Cic. Prodicere diem, Var. Præfari, Catul. Sibylla prolocuta est, Lactant.
units.tr: To foretell: to foresee, Varr. To announce beforehand, to forewarn. The gods show and sing beforehand what is to come, Cic. To fix a day in advance, Var. To speak beforehand, Catul. The Sibyl has spoken beforehand, Lactant.

units.la: Prædictio] Auguria rerum futurarum. Prædicta augurum, Cic. Apotelesmata, Firm.
units.tr: Prediction: auguries of future things. The predictions of augurs, Cic. Astrological forecasts, Firm.

units.la: Prædium] Res rustica, Cic. Villa fructuaria. Colonia, Col.
units.tr: Estate: rural affairs, Cic. A farm villa. A colony, Col.

units.la: Præfari] Præfari aliquem in scribendo, Plin. Præloqui. Procœmiari, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: To speak before: to name someone at the start of a writing, Plin. To say beforehand. To introduce, to preface, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Præfatio] Procœmium, Cic. Antelogium, Plaut. Prologuium, Pacuv. Prologus, Ter. Anteloquium, Macrob. Proloquium. Principium, Fest.
units.tr: Preface: a proem, Cic. A prelude, Plaut. A prologue, Pacuv. A prologue, Ter. A preliminary speech, Macrob. A foreword. A beginning, Fest.

units.la: Præfatus] Antedictus, Amm. Supradictus, Hor. Plin. Suprapositus. Cic.
units.tr: Aforesaid: mentioned before, Amm. Mentioned above, Hor. Plin. Set down above, Cic.

units.la: Præfectus] Præsul regionum Mars, Amm. Præses Reip. Antistes ceremoniarum. Præpositus, Cic. Præsidatum regens, administrans, Spart. Præstes, Fest.
units.tr: Prefect: a Mars who presides over regions, Amm. A president of the state. A master of ceremonies. A placed head, Cic. One who rules and administers a presidency, Spart. A governor, Fest.

units.la: Præfectura] Satrapia, Plin. Præsidatus, Vopisc. Spart. Capitaneatus, Meurs.
units.tr: Prefecture] Satrapy, Plin. Presidency, Vopisc. Spart. Captaincy, Meurs.

units.la: Præferre, vid. Anteferre.
units.tr: To bring before, see To prefer.

units.la: Præficere aliquem negotio] Præponere bello, muneri. Præstare aliquem negotio Cic. Præfulcire aliquem negotiis, Plaut.
units.tr: To put someone in charge of a business] To set someone over a war or an office. To place someone in charge of an affair, Cic. To prop someone up in his affairs, Plaut.

units.la: Præfiscine] Præfiscini, Plaut. Præfiscinò, Scal. Absit verbo invidia, Liv. Bonum factum, Plaut. Bonâ salute, Cato.
units.tr: Without ill omen] Variant forms, Plaut. Scal. "Let there be no offence in the word," Liv. "Good luck," Plaut. "With good health," Cato.

units.la: Præfractè, vid. Contumaciter.
units.tr: Obstinately, see Stubbornly.

units.la: Præfractus] Rubo arido præfractior, Er. vid. Obstinatus
units.tr: Obstinate] As stubborn as a dry bramble, Er. see Obstinate.

units.la: Prægnans, vid. Gravida.
units.tr: Pregnant, see Pregnant woman.

units.la: Prægustare] Præliba̅re, Plin. Præflorare, Plin. Iun. Libare gustu, Tac. Propinare, Mart. Prælambere, Hor. Libatam gustu potionem alicui tradere, Tac.
units.tr: To taste beforehand] To take a prior sip, Plin. To take the first bloom from, Plin. Iun. To take a taste of, Tac. To drink to someone, Mart. To lick lightly, Hor. To hand someone a drink already tasted, Tac.

units.la: Prægustator] Prælambens omne quod affert, Hor. vid. Scissor.
units.tr: Taster] One who licks lightly everything that is brought, Hor. see Carver.

units.la: Præire, vid. Præcedere.
units.tr: To go before, see To precede.

units.la: Præjudicare] Quod Senatus nondum censuit, nec populus Romanus jussit, id arroganter non judico, nec revoco ad arbitrium meum, Cic. Præjudicium facere de aliquo, Cic. Prædamnare, Suet.
units.tr: To prejudge] What the Senate has not yet voted on, nor the Roman people ordered, I do not arrogantly judge, nor do I bring back to my own judgement, Cic. To pass a prejudgement on someone, Cic. To condemn beforehand, Suet.

units.la: Præjudicatus] Præsumpta opinio, Quint. Suspicio præsumpta, spes Tac. Præliator. Præventa gratia. Id.
units.tr: Prejudiced] A presumed opinion, Quint. A presumed suspicion or hope, Tac. A favour anticipated, Id.

units.la: Præjudicium] Præjudicia juris. Anticipata judicia, Bud. Præjudicatio, Quint.
units.tr: Prejudice] Prejudices of law. Anticipated judgements, Bud. Prejudgement, Quint.

units.la: Præliari cum aliquo] Prælium committere. Prælio dimicare. Decertare prælio, manu, ferro, vid. Confligere, Confligtari, Cic. Prælio contendere, confligere. Conficere præliium, Cæs. Inire, facere præliium. Decernere præliio. Dimicare acie. Ad manus venire. Conferre, conserere manum cum hoste, Liv. Serebant crebra præliia pro portis. Decernere, Absol. Tac. Descendere in arenam, Plin. Concurrere cum aliquo, Salust. Committere, Vlp.
units.tr: To fight with someone] To engage in battle. To contend in battle, by hand or by sword; see To clash, To grapple, Cic. To contend in battle, to close with. To bring a battle to an end, Caes. To begin or make a battle. To decide by battle. To fight in ranks. To come to hand-to-hand fighting. To join battle with the enemy, Liv. They fought frequent battles before the gates. To decide, Tac. To enter the arena, Plin. To run together with someone, Sall. To engage, Ulp.

units.la: Præliator] Concursator hostis, Amm. Confertor, Plin.
units.tr: Fighter] A harasser of the enemy, Amm. One who crowds together, Plin.

units.la: Præliuм] Certamen. Dimicatio. Conflictus cum adversario, Cic. Congressus, Salust. Congressio, Iustin. Coitio, Ter. Mars anceps. Acies, Liv.
units.tr: Battle] Contest. Fight. Conflict with an opponent, Cic. Encounter, Sall. Meeting, Just. A coming together, Ter. Doubtful Mars. Line of battle, Liv.

units.la: Præluceere alicui] Præferre alicui facem, tædas, Cic. Lucere facem alicui, Plaut.
units.tr: To light the way for someone] To carry a torch before someone, Cic. To hold a torch for someone, Plaut.

units.la: Præludere pugnæ] Præludere ad pugnam, Var. Præludium rei castrensis & armaturæ exercere, Amm. Proludere, Cic. Præsultare hostium signis, Liv. Primas hastas jácere, Cic. i, pugnæ seriæ præludere.
units.tr: To prelude to battle] To prelude to battle, Var. To practise the drill and arms of war, Amm. To prelude, Cic. To skirmish before the standards of the enemy, Liv. To throw the first spears, Cic. To prelude to a serious fight.

units.la: Præludium] Initium, vel proludium pugnæ, certaminis, minis, Amm. Præcertatio, ad Heren. Præludio & præcursio pugnæ, Plin. Prolusio, Cic. Velitatio, Fest. Velitaris pugna, Sallust.
units.tr: Prelude] The beginning or prelude of a battle or contest, Amm. Preliminary skirmish, ad Her. Prelude and skirmishing of battle, Plin. Prelude, Cic. Light skirmishing, Fest. Skirmishing warfare, Sall.

units.la: Præmândere] Præmollire cibum puero, Quint. Mansa nutrices infantibus in os inserunt, Cic. Mansum ex ore dare, Lucil.
units.tr: To chew for someone] To soften food for a child, Quint. Nurses put chewed food into infants' mouths, Cic. To give from one's mouth what has been chewed, Lucil.

units.la: Præmaturus, vid. Præcox.
units.tr: Premature, see Precocious.

units.la: Præmeditari] Præmoliri, Liv. Præsumere futura, Sen. Curam & cogitationem suscipere de aliquâ re, Cic. Præcogitare, ex Sen.
units.tr: To premeditate] To prepare, Liv. To anticipate the future, Sen. To take up care and thought about some matter, Cic. To think beforehand, from Sen.

units.la: Præmeditatè] Cogitatè scribere, Cic. Judicatò pronunciare, Gell. Sumptò spatiò ad cogitandum dicere. Consulto cogitatóque fit injuria, Cic. Cunctanter, Plin. Conceptis verbis jurare: consultis quoque, Plaut. Pensiculatè, Gell.
units.tr: Deliberately] To write with thought, Cic. To pronounce after judgement, Gell. To speak after taking time to think. A wrong done with deliberate thought, Cic. Hesitantly, Plin. To swear to words already framed, also with counsel, Plaut. Carefully weighed, Gell.

units.la: Præmeditatus] Meditatus venit, Plin. Iun. Pensitato, Tac. Consulta verba, Plaut. Conceptum aliquid, Id.
units.tr: Premeditated] Come well considered, Plin. Iun. Weighed up, Tac. Words considered, Plaut. Something conceived, Id.

units.la: Præmittere] Præmittere literas, Cic. Præmittere aliquid trans maria, Col.
units.tr: To send ahead] To send letters ahead, Cic. To send something across the seas in advance, Col.

units.la: Præmium] Remuneratio, Cic. Laurea desidiæ præbetur nulla, vid. Merces.
units.tr: Reward] Remuneration, Cic. No laurel is given to idleness, see Wages.

units.la: Præmonere, vid. Præcavere. Præno scere, v. Præcognoscere.
units.tr: To forewarn, see To take precautions. To foreknow, see To foreknow.

units.la: Prænunciare] Abi, prænuncia hanc venturam, Ter.
units.tr: To announce beforehand] Go, announce that she is coming, Ter.

units.la: Prænuncius] Admissionalis, Bud. Prænunciæ palæ, Cic. Prænunciativus ignis, Plin. Enunciativus, Sen.
units.tr: Announcing] Of admission, Bud. Announcing signs, Cic. Announcing fire, Plin. Foretelling, Sen.

units.la: Præoccupare] Præsumere remedium, Tac. Eripere alicui ex ore responsionem, Plaut. Quas partes mihi sumpseram, præoccupavit oratio tua, Cic.
units.tr: To anticipate] To take a remedy beforehand, Tac. To snatch a reply from someone's mouth, Plaut. The part I had taken on for myself, your speech has already anticipated, Cic.

units.la: Præoccupatio apud Oratores] Præsumptio, Quint. Occupatio & anteoccupatio, Cic. Prolepsis, Rutil. Præceptio, Plin.
units.tr: Anticipation among orators] Presumption, Quint. Occupation and anticipation, Cic. Prolepsis, Rutil. Preconception, Plin.

units.la: Præparare, vid. Parare.
units.tr: To prepare, see To make ready.

units.la: Præparatio] Comparatio novi belli. Apparatus. Apparatio, Cic. Præparatus, & Præperatus, Gell. vid. Apparatus.
units.tr: Preparation] Preparing for a new war. Equipment. Preparation, Cic. Prepared, and prepared, Gell. see Equipment.

units.la: Præpollere, vid. Prævalere.
units.tr: To prevail, see To excel.

units.la: Præponere] Præteexere, Plin. vid. Anteferre.
units.tr: To put before] To put before, Plin. see To prefer.

units.la: Præpositus, vid. Præfectus.
units.tr: Set over, see Prefect.

units.la: Præposterè aliquid agere] Ante quàm pisces ceperis, muriam misces. Antidotum ante venenum. Excorias, antequam mactàris. Farinam subigis, priusquam pinsueris. Retroagere ordinem. Rem comesâ, rationes putare. Sylva nondum cæsa est, & domum ædificat.
units.tr: To do something back to front] You mix the brine before you have caught the fish. An antidote before the poison. You flay the victim before you have slaughtered it. You sift the flour before you have pounded it. To reverse the order. To reckon the accounts after the matter has been eaten up. The wood is not yet cut, and he is already building the house.

units.la: Præposterum quid] Coryphæus chorum sequitur. Currus bovem rotat. Præfatio libro prolixior. Adhærere sanæ corporis parti scalpellum.
units.tr: Something back to front] The chorus-leader follows the chorus. The cart turns the ox round. A preface longer than the book. Applying the scalpel to a healthy part of the body.

units.la: Præposterus] Inversus, Quint. Retrogradus. Sinister, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Back to front] Inverted, Quint. Retrograde. Perverse, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Præproperè. Præproperus, vid. Præceps, &c.
units.tr: Too hastily. Too hasty, see Headlong, etc.

units.la: Præripere aliquid alicui] Præripere alicui laudem, gratiam. Anteoccupare aliquid. Contendere occupare aliquid, Cic. Intercipere regnum, victoriam, Plin. Iun. Præcipere littora, Virg. vid. Præcedere.
units.tr: To snatch something from someone] To snatch praise or favour from someone. To forestall someone in seizing something. To try to seize something first, Cic. To intercept a kingdom or a victory, Plin. Iun. To seize the shores, Virg. see To precede.

units.la: Prærogativa] Primatus, Plin. Principatus, Cæf. Summatus, Lucr. Fastigium inter alios habere, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Prerogative] Primacy, Plin. Principate, Caes. Supremacy, Lucr. To hold the summit above others, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Præsagire] Sagire, Cic. Præ[…] PræDivinare, Plin. vid. Præ-dicere, Præcognosc.
units.tr: To presage] To perceive, Cic. To divine beforehand, Plin. see To foretell, To foreknow.

units.la: Præsagium] Præsagitio. Præsensio, Prænotio, Cic. Prædi-vinatio, Præscitum, Plin.
units.tr: Presage] Foreboding. Presentiment. Foreknowledge, Cic. Foretelling. Foreknowledge, Plin.

units.la: Præsagium bonum] Auris dextra tinnijt. Oculus dexter mihi saliit, vid. Omen.
units.tr: A good omen] The right ear rings. My right eye has twitched, see Omen.

units.la: Præsagium malum] Fumum olfacere.
units.tr: A bad omen] To smell smoke.

units.la: Præsagus] Præscius venturi, Virg. Prospectator, Apul. Præscire aliquid, vid. Præcognoscere.
units.tr: Presaging] Foreknowing what is to come, Virg. Watcher, Apul. To foreknow something, see To foreknow.

units.la: Præscribere] Præscribere alicui quæ gerenda sunt, Cic. Præformare literas infanti, Quint. Præfigurare literas, Cass. Dicere legem alicui, Sen.
units.tr: To prescribe] To prescribe to someone what is to be done, Cic. To pre-form letters for an infant, Quint. To mark letters in advance, Cass. To lay down the law to someone, Sen.

units.la: Præse ferre] Non omnes sunt, quod præ se ferunt. Multi qui boves stimulant, pauci oratores. Multi thyrsigeri, pauci Phœbi. Non omne quod apparet, verum est. Non omnes, qui habent citharam, sunt citharœdi. Non omnis est coquus, cui longus culter adhæret.
units.tr: To display openly] Not all who display something openly possess it. Many goad oxen, few are orators. Many bear thyrsi, few are followers of Phoebus. Not everything that appears is true. Not everyone who has a lyre is a lyre-player. Not everyone who has a long knife clinging to him is a cook.

units.la: Præsens] Præs est, pro, præstò est, Varr. Nemo adest superstes, Plaut. Præstò est mihi aliquis. Ruri assiduus semper vixit. In oculis alicujus habitare, Cic. Superesse suis negotiis, Vlp. In medio est, Ter.
units.tr: Present] Being at hand, Varr. No one is present and alive, Plaut. Someone is at hand for me. He always lived constantly in the country. To live in someone's eyes, Cic. To be free for one's own affairs, Ulp. He is in the midst, Ter.

units.la: Præsente me, &c.] Præsente testibus (pro præsentibus) Pompon. Præsente omnibus, Næv. Non.
units.tr: With me present, etc.] With witnesses present (for the present ones), Pompon. With all present, Naev., Non.

units.la: Præsente re, vid. Repræs.
units.tr: In the present case, see Present.

units.la: Præsentia] Assiduitas amicorum quotidiana. Os: in ore alicujus versari, Cic. Interventus, Col.
units.tr: Presence] The daily close attendance of friends. To be in someone's face, to dwell before someone's eyes, Cic. Intervention, Col.

units.la: Præsentia certiora futuris] Crastinum tu sume, mihi da hodiernum.
units.tr: Present things are more certain than future ones] You take tomorrow, give me today.

units.la: Præsentia fastidimus] Optat ephippia bos piger, optat arare caballus.
units.tr: We scorn the present] The lazy ox wants a saddle, the horse wants to plough.

units.la: Præsentia agere] Consule de præsentibus. Hoc age.
units.tr: To deal with present matters] Consider the present. Attend to this.

units.la: Præsentibus contentum, in futurum non prospicere] In diem vivere. Suavia in præsentia quae essent, prima habere, neque consulere in longitudinem, Ter.
units.tr: Content with the present, not looking to the future] To live for the day. To hold first those pleasures that are present, and not to think of the long run, Ter.

units.la: Præsepe] Præsepes. Præsepium, Var. Ad præsepim tuam, Plaut.
units.tr: Manger] Mangers. A manger, Varr. To your manger, Plaut.

units.la: Præsertim] Præsertim si: præsertim quod, Cic. Præsertim cùm, Ter. & ut in re tali. Atque. Maximè, Cic.
units.tr: Especially] Especially if; especially because, Cic. especially when, Ter. and, as in such a matter. And. Most of all, Cic.

units.la: Præses] Nomarcha, Bud. vid. Præfectus.
units.tr: Governor] Nomarch, Bud. see Prefect.

units.la: Præsidatus, vid. Præfectura.
units.tr: Presidency, see Prefecture.

units.la: Præsidere] Præesse imperio, Reip. sacris, provinciæ, Cic. Cum potestate esse. Cum imperio esse, Fest.
units.tr: To preside] To be set over a command, the state, sacred rites, a province, Cic. To hold authority. To have command, Fest.

units.la: Præsides rerum sunt omnibus æqui] Deus & sol omnibus idem.
units.tr: The gods are equal to all] God and the sun are the same for all.

units.la: Præsidiarius miles] Stationarius, Vlp. Limitaneus, Bud. Tituli milites. (quasi tutuli) Fest. Sipont.
units.tr: Garrison soldier] Stationed soldier, Ulp. Border soldier, Bud. Soldiers of the titles (as if guards), Fest. Sipont.

units.la: Præsidium, vid. Propugnaculum. Tutela,
units.tr: Protection, see Bulwark. Guardianship.

units.la: Præstans Vir] Longe præstans omnibus aliquâ re, Cic. vid. Excellens.
units.tr: Outstanding man] Far surpassing all others in some respect, Cic. see Excellent.

units.la: Præstantia] Flos, Cic. vid. Excellentia.
units.tr: Excellence] The flower, Cic. see Excellence.

units.la: Præstare aliquid, vid. Efficere. Præstat, vid. Melius est.
units.tr: To perform something, see To effect. It is better, see It is better.

units.la: Præstat hoc malum non movere] Satius erat hoc ulcus non attingere.
units.tr: It is better not to stir this evil] It would have been better not to touch this sore.

units.la: Præstigiæ] Præstigia. Errore mentis, Cic. Offuciæ, Plaut.
units.tr: Illusions] Illusions. Error of the mind, Cic. Deceits, Plaut.

units.la: Præstigiator, vid. Deceptor.
units.tr: Trickster, see Deceiver.

units.la: Præstolari, vid. Opperiri.
units.tr: To wait for, see To await.

units.la: Præstringere oculos] Objicere alicui glaucoma ob oculos, Plaut. Perstringere oculos, Cic. Perstringere aciem oculorum, Liv. Sensus magicis cantibus avertere, Virg. Offundere alicui tenebras, noctem, Cic. Oculis caliginem, Liv. Terrentes tirones præstrictis luminibus, Ascon.
units.tr: To dazzle the eyes] To throw a film before someone's eyes, Plaut. To dazzle the eyes, Cic. To dazzle the sight of the eyes, Liv. To turn the senses away with magic chants, Virg. To pour darkness or night over someone, Cic. Mist over the eyes, Liv. Frightening raw recruits with blinded eyes, Ascon.

units.la: Præsultor, vid. Choragus. Præsumere, vid. Præcerpere. Sperare. Confidere.
units.tr: Leader of the dance, see Choragus. To presume, see To anticipate, To hope, To trust.

units.la: Præsumere de se magna] Multum sibi sumere, arrogare, Cic. Majores spiritus ducere. Falsam sibi persuasionem induere. Nimium sibi tribuere, Quint. Ingentes tollere animos, Virg. Sumere spiritus, Cæs. Digito se cœlum attigisse putat.
units.tr: To presume great things of oneself] To claim much for oneself, to arrogate, Cic. To entertain greater spirits. To adopt a false persuasion. To attribute too much to oneself, Quint. To raise high one's spirits, Virg. To take on spirit, Caes. He thinks he has touched heaven with his finger.

units.la: Præsumptio] Præsumpto opinio, Quint. Præsumptum, Ulp. Anticipatio, Prærogativa, Animus, Omen, Cic. Præceps confidentia.
units.tr: Presumption] Presumed opinion, Quint. Presumption, Ulp. Anticipation, prerogative, mind, omen, Cic. Headlong confidence.

units.la: Prætendere, vid. Obumbrare. Excusare se.
units.tr: To pretend, see To overshadow. To excuse oneself.

units.la: Prætentare] Palpando attingere. Obvia quæque tangere, Cic. vid. Explorare.
units.tr: To feel for] To touch by feeling; to touch whatever lies in the way, Cic. see To explore.

units.la: Præter] Præterquam. Præterea. Demptâ æternitate nihilo beatior Jupiter quàm Epicurus, Cic. Præquam, Cat. Præ se uno rudes cæteros, Gell. Excepto quod, Hor. Usque ad Pompejum (i. illo excepto) Plin. Iun. Extra unam anicu-lam, Ter. Super quàm, Liv. Salvo eo si, Ulp. Præter si, Var.
units.tr: Except] Except, besides. Besides. Jupiter, with eternity taken away, is no happier than Epicurus, Cic. Except, Cat. Apart from himself the rest are ignorant, Gell. Except that, Hor. Up to Pompey (that is, excepting him), Plin. Iun. Except one old woman, Ter. Beyond what, Liv. Saving that, if, Ulp. Unless, Var.

units.la: Præterea] Præter hæc. Ultra hæc, Plaut. Habent oculos; præterque tactum, Plin. Ultrà. Insuper. Hoc ampliùs. Tum præterea. Nihil suprà. Ad hæc. Deinde, Cic. Ad hoc, Sallust. Inde. Huic adde, Liv. Quin etiam, Plaut. Quin etiam insuper. Tum, Ter. Tum autem, Plaut. Suprà, Celsus. Adde quod, Ovid. Adstruitur his, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Besides] Besides these. Beyond these, Plaut. They have eyes, and besides touch, Plin. Further. Moreover. This more. Then also. Nothing above. To these. Then, Cic. To this, Sallust. Thence. Add to this, Liv. Nay even, Plaut. Nay even, moreover. Then, Ter. Then indeed, Plaut. Above, Celsus. Add that, Ovid. This is added to these, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Præterire] Prætercurrere urbem, Amm. Prætervehi scopulum. Declinare civitatem. Flectere promontorium, Cic. Transire, Sen. Transabire difficultates, Apul. Prælegere Campaniam, Tac. Præteritare, Plaut.
units.tr: To pass by] To run past the city, Amm. To sail past a reef. To avoid a city. To round a headland, Cic. To cross over, Sen. To get past difficulties, Apul. To skim past Campania, Tac. To pass by, Plaut.

units.la: Præterit tempus] Dies transiit. Præterfluere, Prælabi, Prætervolare, Cic. Transvectum est tempus, Tac. Menses abierunt decem, Ter. Pertransire, Plin. Transfluxêre dies, Claud. Exactis temporibus, Cic. Exemptis tribus diebus, Pall.
units.tr: Time passes] The day has gone by. To flow past, to slip past, to fly past, Cic. Time has been carried past, Tac. Ten months have gone, Ter. To pass through, Plin. The days have flowed away, Claud. With the times spent, Cic. With three days taken out, Pall.

units.la: Præteritio] Prætervectio eorum, qui ultro citroque navigant. Trajectio stellarum. Obversatio. Per transfennam prætereuntes strictim aspeximus, Cic. Transitum tempestatis exspectare, Cic. Transcursus, Plin.
units.tr: Passing by] The passing by of those who sail to and fro. The crossing of the stars. Being seen. We glimpsed those passing through the window in passing, Cic. To wait for the passing of the storm, Cic. A running past, Plin.

units.la: Præterita] Antea acta, Liv.
units.tr: Past things] Things done before, Liv.

units.la: Præterita ne cura] Quæ deciderunt, ne tollito.
units.tr: Do not worry about past things] Do not pick up what has fallen.

units.la: Præteritus] Anteacta vita, Cic. Antecedens, Ter. Antegestæ res, Amm. Proximis diebus. Prior ætas, Cic. Superanteacta ætas, Lucr. Retro aliquis, vel aliquid, Plin. Iun. Ne cujusquam retro habeatur ratio, Id. Omnes retro Principes, Paeat. Transmissus, Stat.
units.tr: Past] A life lived before, Cic. Preceding, Ter. Things done before, Amm. In the last few days. Former age, Cic. A very ancient age, Lucr. For someone or something to be looked back upon, Plin. Iun. That no account be taken of anyone's past, Id. All earlier princes, Paneg. Passed over, Stat.

units.la: Præteremittere, vid. Omittere.
units.tr: To pass over, see To omit.

units.la: Præterremeare] Prætervehi convivium flagitiosiss. Prætergredi castra, Cic. Præterequitare. Præterferri, Liv. Præter campos agimus navim, Lucr. Præterlabor tumulum, Virg. Transcurrere præter oculos alicujus, Ovid. Præteritare (& Præterbitare,) Plaut. Transvehi Tuscos. Appeninus (mons) volatu stringitur, Plaud. Præternavigare.
units.tr: To ride past] To ride past a shameful banquet. To go past a camp, Cic. To ride past. To be carried past, Liv. We drive the ship past the fields, Lucr. I glide past the mound, Virg. To run past someone's eyes, Ovid. To pass by (and to pass by), Plaut. To carry across the Tuscans. The Apennine (mountain) is grazed by flight, Plaud. To sail past.

units.la: Prætexere] Obtendere turpitudini rationem, Plin. Obumbrare crimen sub imagine erroris, Ovid. Obvolvere vitium verbis, Cæs. Palliari res tam aperta non potest, Apul. Quærere sermonem, Ter.
units.tr: To weave in front] To put a reason before a disgrace, Plin. To hide a crime under the appearance of error, Ovid. To wrap a fault in words, Caes. So open a matter cannot be disguised, Apul. To seek an excuse in speech, Ter.

units.la: Prætextus] Prætextum, Sen. Obtentus, Gell. Species, Liv. Nomine honesto prætexunt culpam, Virg. Sub umbra fœderis, Liv. Integumentum flagitiorum, Cic. Præscriptio, Cæs. Color, Quint.
units.tr: Pretext] A pretext, Sen. A cover, Gell. An appearance, Liv. With a fair name they cloak the fault, Virg. Under the shade of a treaty, Liv. A cloak for crimes, Cic. A plea, Caes. A colour, Quint.

units.la: Prætextu virtutis] Sub virtutis specie. Virtutis titulo. Sub imagine pietatis. Sub umbra pietatis, Erar.
units.tr: Under the pretext of virtue] Under the appearance of virtue. Under the title of virtue. Under the image of piety. Under the shade of piety, Erar.

units.la: Prætor, vid. Iudex. Prætorium, vid. Puria.
units.tr: Praetor, see Judge. Praetorium, see Puria.

units.la: Prætorius] Prætorianus, Plin. Prætoritius, Mart. Ducalis tunica, Vopisc. Imperatorius, Cic. Imperialis, Gul. Capit.
units.tr: Praetorian] Of the praetorian guard, Plin. Praetorian, Mart. A ducal tunic, Vopisc. Imperial, Cic. Imperial, Gul. Capit.

units.la: Prævalere] Prævalescit arbor, Col. Vincere viribus, Virg. Præposse, Tac. Superare aliquem, Cic. Superare pugnando, Ovid. Dolis, Plaut. Opprimere, Id. Præpollere, ex Liv.
units.tr: To prevail] The tree grows strong, Col. To conquer by strength, Virg. To have the upper hand, Tac. To overcome someone, Cic. To overcome by fighting, Ovid. By trickery, Plaut. To crush, Id. To excel, from Liv.

units.la: Prævaricari] Tr. Ordinem non servare, Propert. Violare legem, Plaud. Conculcare, Evertere, perfringere, convellere legem. Migrare communia jura, Cic. Egredi leges, Tac. Fraudem facere Senatusconsulto. Committere aliquid contra legem, Cic. Facere fraudem legi, Plaut. Transgredi, Ap. S. Eccl.
units.tr: To transgress] Tr. Not to keep the order, Propert. To violate the law, Plaud. To trample, overturn, break, or tear up a law. To alter common rights, Cic. To go beyond the laws, Tac. To cheat against a decree of the Senate. To commit something against the law, Cic. To defraud the law, Plaut. To transgress, Ap. S. Eccl.

units.la: Prævaricatio] Transgressio legis, officii, Sipont. Contra legem factum, commissum, delictum, Cic.
units.tr: Transgression] Transgression of law or duty, Sipont. A thing done, committed or offended against the law, Cic.

units.la: Prævaricator] Violator juris humani, Liv.
units.tr: Transgressor] A violator of human law, Liv.

units.la: Prævenire, vid. Præcedere. Prævertere. Ibid.
units.tr: To anticipate, see To go before. To forestall. Ibid.

units.la: Prævidere] Prospicere futuros casus. Providere futura, Cic. vid. præcognoscere.
units.tr: To foresee] To look ahead to future events. To provide for the future, Cic. See To foreknow.

units.la: Prævisus] Præcogitatum malum, Sen.
units.tr: Foreseen] An evil thought of beforehand, Sen.

units.la: Prandere] Prandere calidum prandium, Plaut. Pransitare, Macrob. Meridiare & ri, prandium meridie capere, ex Plaut. Anteponere bonum prandium pransoribus, Plaut.
units.tr: To dine] To eat a hot dinner, Plaut. To dine often, Macrob. To take a midday meal, from Plaut. To set a good dinner before those who dine, Plaut.

units.la: Prandium] Mensa, Juv. Pransum paratum, Var.
units.tr: Dinner] A table, Juv. A dinner made ready, Var.

units.la: Pravè, vid. Male. Pravus, vid. Malus.
units.tr: Badly, see Ill. Crooked, see Bad.

units.la: Precari, vid. Orare Deum.
units.tr: To pray, see To pray to God.

units.la: Precari bene alicui] Reditum exeunti precari, Jubere valere, Cic. Optare.
units.tr: To wish someone well] To wish a return to one who is leaving, to bid farewell, Cic. To wish.

units.la: Precatio] Preces, obsecratio, imploratio deum, Cic. Comprecatio deorum, Liv. Adoratio, Plin. Postulationes divinæ, Arnob.
units.tr: Prayer] Prayers, entreaties, the supplication of God, Cic. A joint prayer to the gods, Liv. Worship, Plin. Divine petitions, Arnob.

units.la: Preces armatæ] Dominus rogans præcipit.
units.tr: Armed prayers] The Lord, asking, commands.

units.la: Prehendere] Apprehendere manu aliquid. Reprehendere aliquem pallio, Plaut.
units.tr: To seize] To take hold of something with the hand. To seize someone by the cloak, Plaut.

units.la: Prelum, vid. Torcular.
units.tr: Press, see Winepress.

units.la: Premere] Pressare. Imprimere corpus stipiti, Plin. Perprimere, Hor. Condensare ponderibus aliquid. Prelo subjicere, Col.
units.tr: To press] To squeeze. To press a body against a post, Plin. To press through, Hor. To weigh something down with weights. To put under the press, Col.

units.la: Prensare, vid. Captare. Prensatio, vid. Ambitio honorum.
units.tr: To importune, see To seek. Importuning, see Canvassing for office.

units.la: Presbyter, vid. Sacerdos.
units.tr: Elder, see Priest.

units.la: Presse, vid. Arcte.
units.tr: Tightly, see Closely.

units.la: Pretiosus] Auro carior. Auro contra carior, Plaut. Magno pretio stat, Hor. vid. Carus.
units.tr: Precious] Dearer than gold. On the contrary, dearer than gold, Plaut. It costs a great price, Hor. See Dear.

units.la: Pretiosa indignis] Margarita inter porcos.
units.tr: Precious things to the unworthy] A pearl among swine.

units.la: Pretium] Valor. Nuncupatio, Plin. Æstimatio, Cæs. Pretiositas.
units.tr: Price] Value. A naming, Plin. Estimation, Caes. Preciousness.

units.la: Pretium indicare] Imponere pretium alicui rei, Cic. Indica, fac pretium, Plaut. Dicere pretium alicujus rei, Hor.
units.tr: To set a price] To put a price on a thing, Cic. Name the price, Plaut. To state the price of a thing, Hor.

units.la: Pretii alicujus esse] Alicujus æris, Gel. Aliquo numero habetur, Var. Pro aliquo est, Sen. Pensi habere, Salust. Pensi est mihi, Liv. Momentum habere. Plurimi id est æstimandum. Plurimi est. Æstimabilis, Cic.
units.tr: To be of someone's worth] Of so much money, Gel. Is reckoned in a certain number, Var. Stands for someone, Sen. To hold in regard, Sallust. It is of concern to me, Liv. To have weight. It is to be valued most highly. It is of the greatest. Valuable, Cic.

units.la: Pridem, vid. Dudum.
units.tr: Long since, see For some time.

units.la: Pridianus] Hesterna coena, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Of the previous day] Yesterday's dinner, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Primarius] Primanus, Tac. Principalis causa, Quint. Primitius, Ovid. Primus, Ter. Apprimus, Virg. Primarum partium. In primis Italiae civitas. Praecipuum Iur. Princeps locus. In principibus est, Cic. Palmarium facinus. Primae caveae Rhetores, Vorf. Primae cerae amicus. Primae classis, notae. Primatum obtinens. Primimipilarius, vid. Anteferendus.
units.tr: Chief] Of the first rank, Tac. The principal cause, Quint. Earliest, Ovid. First, Ter. Foremost, Virg. Of the first parts. The first city in Italy. Pre-eminent. The place of honour. Among the leaders, Cic. A notable crime. Rhetoricians of the first rank, Vorf. A friend of the first rank. Of the first class, well known. Holding the first place. Chief centurion, see Preferred.

units.la: Primarii requisiti non oblivisce ndum] Focus luculentus in aedibus.
units.tr: Primary requisites not to be forgotten] A bright hearth in the house.

units.la: Primates, vid. Magnates. Primatus, vid. Praerogativa.
units.tr: Chiefs, see Magnates. Primacy, see Prerogative.

units.la: Primigenius] Primogenitus, Hieron. Primigenitus, Bisciol. Vall. Prima naturae vocat. Primus genitus, Plin. Primigenus dies, Lucr.
units.tr: Firstborn] First-begotten, Jerome. First-born, Bisciol. Vall. Nature calls it the first-born. First-begotten, Plin. A first-born day, Lucr.

units.la: Primipara] Porcetra, sus quae semel peperit. Tiruncula canis. Primum partum enixa. Primo effoeta, Col.
units.tr: Primipara] A sow that has farrowed once. A young bitch. Having borne a first offspring. Worn out after the first birth, Col.

units.la: Primitiae] Praemetium, quasi praemessum, Fest. Praemissa, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: First fruits] First reaping, as if "sent before", Fest. Things sent in advance, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Primo] Primum. Imprimis, Cic. In primo. Primitus oritur, Var. Principio, Cic. Primodum, Plaut.
units.tr: First] First. Above all, Cic. In the first place. It arises first, Var. At the beginning, Cic. Firstly, Plaut.

units.la: Primopilus] Manut. Primipilus, Caf. Centurio primi pili, Liv. Cic. Primus Centurio, Cic. Praefui militum, Vopisc. Primipilarius, Spart.
units.tr: Chief centurion] Manut. Primipilus, Caf. Centurion of the first spear, Liv. Cic. First centurion, Cic. I commanded the soldiers, Vopisc. Primipilarius, Spart.

units.la: Primores, vid. Magnates.
units.tr: Leading men, see Magnates.

units.la: Primum quid in suo genere] Prima rerum, summa. Caput est. Ultimum id in amicitia putavit. Quod familiam ducit, Cic. Quod est potissimum, Quint. Col. In hoc cardo versatur.
units.tr: The first in its kind] The first and highest of things. It is the head. He counted that the ultimate thing in friendship. What leads the family, Cic. What is most powerful, Quint. Col. The hinge turns on this.

units.la: Prima feliciter tentare] Glaciem scindere, frangere, perrumpere.
units.tr: To attempt a first venture successfully] To split, break, or burst through the ice.

units.la: Primum experienti venia datur] Primus error veniam meretur.
units.tr: Indulgence is given to a first attempt] A first error deserves pardon.

units.la: Primus] Primus ante omnes, Virg. Primigenius, Fest. Ultimus auctor sanguinis, Virg. Primulus, Plaut.
units.tr: First] First of all, Virg. Earliest-born, Fest. The last originator of the blood, Virg. Very first, Plaut.

units.la: Primus inter suos] Coryphaeus, vid. Anteferendus.
units.tr: First among his own] The leader, see Preferred.

units.la: Principalis, vid. Primarius.
units.tr: Principal, see Primary.

units.la: Principium] Frons exercitus, Tac. Cujusque rei potispotissima pars. Priora & terga, Plin. Principia, pl. Liv. caput jecinoris, Id. Primum, Cic. Primores ungues erigit, Lucil. vid. Initium.
units.tr: Beginning] The front of an army, Tac. The most important part of anything. Front and back, Plin. The principal headquarters, Liv. The head of the liver, Id. First, Cic. He raises his first claws, Lucil. See Beginning.

units.la: Principium & finis] Alpha & O mega. Prora & puppis.
units.tr: Beginning and end] Alpha and Omega. Prow and stern.

units.la: Principiis obstandum] Omne malum nascens facile opprimitur. Satius est initiis mederi, quàm fini.
units.tr: Beginnings must be resisted] Every evil, as it springs up, is easily crushed. It is better to cure beginnings than the end.

units.la: Exparvis principiis magna rerum incrementa] De parvâ scintillâ magnum sæpe excitatur incendium. Tandem fit surculus arbor.
units.tr: From small beginnings, great increases of things] From a small spark a great fire is often kindled. In time a sapling becomes a tree.

units.la: Prior] Primas etsi utrique, priores tamen deferunt Lælio, Cic.
units.tr: Prior] Although both are given the first place, the earlier ones nonetheless award it to Laelius, Cic.

units.la: Ad priorem statum tenuem redire] Ad pristina præsepia.
units.tr: To return to a former humble state] Back to the former stalls.

units.la: Prisce, vid. Antique.
units.tr: Ancient, see Antique.

units.la: Priscus] Ipsa sua vetustate consenuit. Nimis antiquus & obsoletus. Oblivione obsoleti mores. Majorum consuetudo longo intervallo repetita atque relata. Obsoletus, Cic. Vetultus mos, Ovid. Pervetusta verba, Cic. Exoletus. Vetustate exoletus. Ex Vetustate verba, Quint. Cascus, Var.Cic. Cana antiquitas: cana morum antiquitas, Cassiod. Archaici lecti, (i. e. antiquo more facti,) Hor.
units.tr: Ancient] Grown old through its own antiquity. Too old and obsolete. Customs obsolete through oblivion. The custom of the elders, taken up again and brought back after a long interval. Obsolete, Cic. An old custom, Ovid. Very old words, Cic. Gone out of use. Faded with age. Words from antiquity, Quint. Worn, Var. Cic. Hoary antiquity: hoary antiquity of manners, Cassiod. Archaic couches (i.e. made in the old fashion), Hor.

units.la: Privare aliquem aliquâ re, vid. Orbare. Adimere.
units.tr: To deprive someone of something, see To bereave. To take away.

units.la: Privata vita] Vita segrex, Sen. Solitudo: Mihi solitudo & recessus provincia est. Umbratilis vita, Cic. Secretum, Quint. Interior & familiaris vita, Suet.
units.tr: Private life] A life apart, Sen. Solitude: solitude and retreat are my province. A shadowy life, Cic. Seclusion, Quint. The inner and family life, Suet.

units.la: Privatam vitam agere] Submittere se ad privatum fastigium. Removere se à negotiis publicis. Removere operam suam à populari cætu. Secum vivere, Liv. Subtrahere se à Curiâ, & ab omni Reip. parte. Jacere, Cic. Abstinere se urbanis, Plaut. A vulgo & scenâ in secreta se revocare, Hor. Civilibus renunciare officiis, Quint. Vitam perobscuram transmittere, Sen. Vitam in obscuro agere. Ætatem procul à Repub. habere, Salust.
units.tr: To live a private life] To lower oneself to a private station. To withdraw from public business. To withdraw one's efforts from the popular gathering. To live with oneself, Liv. To withdraw from the Senate and from every part of the commonwealth. To lie low, Cic. To keep away from urban affairs, Plaut. To call oneself back from the crowd and the stage into seclusion, Hor. To renounce civic duties, Quint. To pass a very obscure life, Sen. To live in obscurity. To keep one's life far from the Republic, Sallust.

units.la: Privatim] In privato, Liv. Inferre se in locum sine arbitris. Remotis arbitris agere, Id. Remotô liberô ab arbitris loco, Cic. Nemo hic adest superstes, i.e. testis. Extrâ turbam, Plaut. Extra ordinem, Cic. Secreto ab aliis coquere consilia, Liv. vid. Separatim.
units.tr: Privately] In private, Liv. To withdraw into a place without witnesses. To transact with witnesses removed, Id. In a place with the free man removed from witnesses, Cic. No one here is present as a survivor, i.e. a witness. Outside the crowd, Plaut. Outside the order, Cic. To plan in secret apart from others, Liv. See Separately.

units.la: Privatum commodum] In privatum versum omne, Liv. Prædam omnem in unum contulit, Lamp.
units.tr: Privatum commodum] Turned wholly to private advantage, Liv. He gathered all the booty into one heap, Lamp.

units.la: Privatus homo] Privus. Carens luce forensi; rebus urbanis; publico, Cic. Publico abstinens, Ter. Vocans, Amm.
units.tr: Privatus homo] Privus. Free of the public light of the forum; having nothing to do with city affairs or public business, Cic. Abstaining from public business, Ter. Free of, Amm.

units.la: Privignus] Privigna proles, Col.
units.tr: Privignus] The offspring of a stepchild, Col.

units.la: Privilegiatus] Privilegiarius, Vlp. Eximius. Bud. Homo immunis, Cic. Liberæ capræ ab aratro.
units.tr: Privilegiatus] One holding a privilege, Vlp. Exempt, distinguished, Bud. A man free of burdens, Cic. Goats free from the plough.

units.la: Privilegium] Lex privatis hominibus irrogata. Beneficium legis, Cic. Privata lex. Jus singulare. Beneficium Principis. Indultum. Immunitas. Dispensatio. Constitutio personalis, Ulp. Prærogativa, pro jure specialiter indulto, Vlp. Rogatio, Fest.
units.tr: Privilegium] A law imposed on private persons. A benefit of the law, Cic. A private law. A special right. A favour of the Prince. An indulgence. An immunity. A dispensation. A personal constitution, Ulp. A prerogative, meaning a right specially granted, Ulp. A proposal, Fest.

units.la: Privilegio donare aliquem] Privilegium alicui concedere, Paul. I.C. Dare immunitatem muneris. Privilegium facere. Legem privatis hominibus irrogare. Liberare aliquem opere magno. Eximere aliquem de vectigalibus. Excipere, Cic. Solvere legibus aliquem, ad Her. Dare vacationem militiæ alicui, Liv.
units.tr: Privilegio donare aliquem] To grant someone a privilege, Paul, J.C. To grant immunity from a duty. To confer a privilege. To impose a law on private persons. To free someone from a heavy task. To exempt someone from taxes. To make an exception for someone, Cic. To release someone from the laws, ad Her. To give someone a dispensation from military service, Liv.

units.la: Prius] Primò purgare, mox pinguescere, Plin. Priore loco dicere, Cic. Prius disce quid sit vivere: ubi scies, tum &c, Ter.
units.tr: Prius] First to cleanse, then soon to fatten, Plin. To speak in the first place, Cic. Learn first what it is to live; when you know that, then etc., Ter.

units.la: Priusquam] Prius quàm. Prius de probro, quàm de re. Priusque tollentur, quàm. Antequam, & ante quàm, Cic.
units.tr: Priusquam] Prius quam. To speak of the disgrace before the matter. Before they are removed, before. Antequam and ante quam, Cic.

units.la: Pro aliquo agere aliquid] Fungi alienâ vice, Liv. Pro herede aliquid gerere, possidere, Vlp. Vicem alicujus ulciscì. Officia, partes pro aliquo suscipere. Nomine alicujus solvere, Cic, Oppetere vicem alicujus, Plaut. Ego te absente tuis fungar partibus, Tuas agam partes, Er.
units.tr: Pro aliquo agere aliquid] To act in another's place, Liv. To hold and possess as heir on someone's behalf, Ulp. To avenge someone's cause. To take on someone's duties and roles. To pay in someone's name, Cic. To die in someone's place, Plaut. In your absence I will fill your part; I will play your role, Er.

units.la: Pro aliquo est, vid. Pretii alicujus.
units.tr: Pro aliquo est: see Pretii alicujus (of someone's worth).

units.la: Pro me est] A me est. A me stant judices. A nobis id facit. Cum aliquo stare. Secundo populo aliquid facere, Cic. Vnde jus stat, Liv.
units.tr: Pro me est] It is from me. The judges stand with me. He does this on our side. To stand with someone. To do something with the people's favour, Cic. Whence the law stands, Liv.

units.la: Pro posse, vulgò, Latinius, pro possibilitate, Amm.] Pro virili parte. Pro sua quisque parte, facultate, opibus, portione. Pro ratâ portione. Pro se quisque. Prout ferebant facultates, Cic. Pro copiâ, Plaut. Pro copiâ rei facere, Sallust. Salust. Pro virili portione, Tac. Pro modo virium opus, Quint. Id quod quisque valet, & potest, edit, Plaut.
units.tr: Pro posse, commonly; more Latinly, pro possibilitate, Amm.] According to one's share. Each according to his share, means, resources and portion. In proportion to one's means. Each for himself. As their means allowed, Cic. According to what is available, Plaut. To act according to the resources of the matter, Sall. In proportion to one's strength, Tac. A work done to the measure of one's powers, Quint. He produces what each is worth and able to, Plaut.

units.la: Probabile est, vid. Verisimile est.
units.tr: Probabile est: see Verisimile est (it is likely).

units.la: Probabilis] Evidens, Cic. Authenticus, Vlp. vid. Verisimil.
units.tr: Probabilis] Evident, Cic. Authentic, Ulp. See Verisimil.

units.la: Probare] Planum facere, Lucr. Convincere. Colligere. Fidem facere, Cic. vid. Demonstrare, Approbare.
units.tr: Probare] To make plain, Lucr. To convict. To gather together. To give assurance, Cic. See Demonstrare and Approbare.

units.la: Probatio. vid. Demonstratio.
units.tr: Probatio: see Demonstratio.

units.la: Probatus vir, &c.] Virtus experta atque perspecta. Homo in utraque fortuna cognitus, multis signis & virtutis &c. Spectatus vir. Spectata ejus est integritas. Probatissimus homo. Compertus, Cic. Explorata fides, Stat.
units.tr: Probatus vir, &c.] Virtue tested and examined. A man known in either fortune, by many signs of virtue etc. A man of proven worth. His integrity has been tested. A most approved man. Known, Cic. Tried loyalty, Stat.

units.la: Probè] Probiter, Var. Romano more. Integrè, integerrimè. Salva fide, lege, jure, officio, aliquid facere. Innocentissimè acta vita. Vivere sanctissimè; cum virtute, Cic.
units.tr: Probè] Honestly, Var. In the Roman manner. With full integrity, most thoroughly. Keeping faith, law, right and duty intact, to do something. To lead a most blameless life. To live most holily, with virtue, Cic.

units.la: Probitas] Bonitas, integritas in candidato requiritur, Cic.
units.tr: Probitas] Goodness and integrity are required in a candidate, Cic.

units.la: Probrose] Contumeliosè, contumeliosissimè. Maledicè, Detrahendi causa dicere. Per contumeliam. Per summum dedecus vitam amittere, Cic. Per flagitium perdere famam, Ter. Subcontumeliosè tractari. Flagitiosè & turpiter dicta. Flagitiosissimè amori alicujus servire. Cum probro & dedecore, Cic.
units.tr: Probrose] Insultingly, most insultingly. Slanderously, speaking to disparage. By insult. To lose one's life with the greatest disgrace, Cic. To lose one's reputation through shameful conduct, Ter. To be treated with some contempt. Spoken shamefully and basely. To serve someone's love most shamefully. With disgrace and dishonour, Cic.

units.la: Probrosus, Probrosum, vid. Contumelia, &c.
units.tr: Probrosus, Probrosum: see Contumelia, etc. (insult).

units.la: Probus] Approbus. Inculpatissimæ vitæ, Gell. Vitæ integerrimæ. Vir integer, innocens. Nemo illo innocentior, neque sanctior. Omnes virtutis numeros continet. Pollet virtute præditus. Vir exemplum innocentiæ. Integer, spectatus vir, Cic. Probissimus, Plin. Iun. In omnium virtutum exempla genitus adolescens, Paterc. Cato sui temporis, Lampr. vid. Bonus.
units.tr: Probus] Approbus. Of most blameless life, Gell. Of most upright life. An upright, innocent man. No one more innocent or holier than he. He holds every number of virtue. He excels, endowed with virtue. A man who is an example of innocence. An upright, proven man, Cic. Most upright, Plin. Iun. A youth born as an example of all virtues, Paterc. Cato of his time, Lampr. See Bonus.

units.la: Procacia] Procacitas lepida, Mart. Audacia, importunitas, petulantia, contumacia, Ferocia, Cic. Confidentia ingens, Ter. Cornua, Hor. Protervia, Lucr. Temeritas furiosa, Cic. Ferocitas, Id.
units.tr: Procacia] Charming forwardness, Mart. Boldness, importunity, petulance, obstinacy, ferocity, Cic. Great self-assurance, Ter. Horns, Hor. Insolence, Lucr. Headstrong rashness, Cic. Ferocity, Id.

units.la: Procaciter] Procacius Turbulenté aliquid facere. Ferociter dicta. Contumaciter ad aliquem scribere. Pugnis calcibus uti. Audacter, Cic. Proterve, Plaut. Confidenter, Acci. Proterviter, Enn.
units.tr: Procaciter] More forwardly. To do something riotously. Said fiercely. To write obstinately to someone. To use fists and heels. Boldly, Cic. Insolently, Plaut. Confidently, Acc. Insolently, Enn.
