units.la: Procax, vid. Lascivus & Protervus.
units.tr: Procax: see Lascivus and Protervus (wanton, insolent).

units.la: Procedit] Cedit res, Virg. It res bene. Fluunt res ad voluntatem, Cic. Sic fortuna rotam suam versat, v. Succedit.
units.tr: Procedit] The thing gives way, Virg. Things go well. Affairs flow according to one's wish, Cic. So fortune turns her wheel: see Succedit.

units.la: Procella] Torrens aeris. Aereum diluvium. Tempestas pelagi, Virg. Tempestas maris, Caes. Æstus, fervor, agitatio maris. Agitatio fluctuum, Cic.
units.tr: Procella] A rushing of air. A flood from the air. A storm of the sea, Virg. A storm at sea, Caes. Surge, heat, agitation of the sea. Agitation of the waves, Cic.

units.la: Procellosus] Tempestuosum mare, Gell. Turbidus dies, Plin. Tumultuosum mare, Hor. Turbulentum tempus. Turbulentissimus Tribunatus, Cic.
units.tr: Procellosus] A stormy sea, Gell. A turbulent day, Plin. A tumultuous sea, Hor. A turbulent time. The most turbulent tribunate, Cic.

units.la: Procerus] Alno procerior, Er. vid. Altus.
units.tr: Procerus] Taller than an alder, Er. See Altus (tall).

units.la: Processus juris] Via juris, ratio, norma, Cic. Formula, Plin. Processus judiciarius, I. C. Persecutio, Vlp.
units.tr: Processus juris] The way of law, method, rule, norm, Cic. Formula, Plin. Judicial procedure, J.C. Prosecution, Ulp.

units.la: Procidentia oculorum] Intus abacti oculi, Stat.
units.tr: Procidentia oculorum] Eyes driven inward, Stat.

units.la: Procidentia sedis] Procidua sedes, Plin. Bubonocele, Sipont.
units.tr: Procidentia sedis] A prolapsed seat, Plin. Bubonocele, Sipont.

units.la: Procidere in genua] Accidere, Prosternere se, projicere, sternere se ad pedes alicujus. Volutari ad pedes alicujus. Abjicere se supplicem ad pedes alicui, Cic. Advolvi pedibus alicujus, Tac. Procumbere ad genua: ad pedes alicujus. Provolvere se ad genua alicui, Liv. Provolutus ejus genibus, Tac. Exhibere se supplicem. Esse supplicem alicui. Supplicem ad pedes alicujus jacere, Cic.
units.tr: Procidere in genua] To fall to the ground, prostrate oneself, throw oneself, lay oneself at someone's feet. To roll at someone's feet. To cast oneself down as a suppliant at someone's feet, Cic. To throw oneself at someone's feet, Tac. To fall on one's knees, at someone's feet. To sink to someone's knees, Liv. Prostrate at his knees, Tac. To present oneself as a suppliant. To be a suppliant to someone. To lie as a suppliant at someone's feet, Cic.

units.la: Procire] Matrem procitum plurimi venerunt, Liv. Procare, Fest. Ambire nuptias.
units.tr: Procire] Very many came when the mother summoned them, Liv. Procare, Fest. To court for marriage.

units.la: Proclamare] Promulgare legem. Edicere comitia. Praeco praedicat aliquid. Recitare edictum, Cic. Judicare forum, Virg. Pronunciare praemium, Liv. Conclamare auctionem, Plaut. Debuccinare, Ter. Subjicere bona alicujus voci praeconis, Cic. Praeconis voce victorem declarare, Virg. Proquiritare, Sidon. Lex proquiritata (i. Publicata.) Beroal.
units.tr: Proclamare] To promulgate a law. To announce the assemblies. The herald announces something. To recite an edict, Cic. To pronounce judgment in the forum, Virg. To announce a reward, Liv. To cry out an auction, Plaut. To bawl out, Ter. To put a man's goods up to the herald's voice, Cic. To declare the victor by the herald's voice, Virg. To cry out for help, Sidon. A law proclaimed (that is, published), Beroal.

units.la: Proclamare] Promulgatio legis, Cic.
units.tr: Proclamare] The promulgation of a law, Cic.

units.la: Proclivis] Propensus ad vitia. Affectus ad munus fungendum. Natus ad aliquid, Cic. Pronus ad omne nefas: in ferrum, Lucan. Pronus offensioni, Tac. Inclinatus ad. Inclinatior ad pacem animus, Liv. Promptus ad discendum. Appositus judex juri, Quint. Sum affectus ad, Sen.
units.tr: Proclivis] Prone to vices. Disposed to discharge a duty. Born for something, Cic. Prone to every crime, to the sword, Lucan. Prone to offence, Tac. Inclined to. A mind more inclined to peace, Liv. Ready to learn. A judge suited to the law, Quint. I am disposed to, Sen.

units.la: Proclivitas] Propensio ad aliquid. Inclinatio voluntatum. Facilitas ad bona. Declinatio ad libidinem, Cic. Pronitas ad malum, Sen.
units.tr: Proclivitas] Inclination to something. Bending of the wills. Readiness toward good things. Turning aside to lust, Cic. Proneness to evil, Sen.

units.la: Proclivitas naturalis] Minervâ. Natura, Cic. Genius. Naturæ Deus, Hor. Vena, Juv.
units.tr: Proclivitas naturalis] By the gift of Minerva. Nature, Cic. Genius. The god of nature, Hor. Vein, Juv.

units.la: Procrastinare] Recrastinare aliquid, Col. vid. Differre negotium.
units.tr: Procrastinare] To put something off until tomorrow, Col. See Differre negotium (to defer a matter).

units.la: Procrastinatio, vid. Dilatio.
units.tr: Procrastinatio: see Dilatio (delay).

units.la: Procul] Longè abire. Longe gentium, Cic. Longè procul à me, Plaut. Longissimè abest. Remotus ultra Gades. Ultra Herculis columnas.
units.tr: Procul] To go far away. Far from the nations, Cic. Far, far from me, Plaut. Very far off. Remote beyond Gades. Beyond the pillars of Hercules.

units.la: Procul dubio] Dubium nemini est. Utique. Nempè. Quippe, Cic. Videlicet, Id. Sine dubio, Pompon. Sine dubietate, Amm. Indubitanter, Plin. Indubitatè, Vlp. Scilicet, Ter. Nimirum, Quint. Ex professo bonus, malus, Sen.
units.tr: Procul dubio] No one doubts it. Surely. Certainly. Indeed, Cic. Evidently, Id. Without doubt, Pompon. Without hesitation, Amm. Undoubtedly, Plin. Undoubtedly, Ulp. Surely, Ter. Doubtless, Quint. Openly good, openly bad, Sen.

units.la: Proculcare] Calce proterere, vid. Conculcare.
units.tr: Proculcare] To crush with the heel: see Conculcare (trample upon).

units.la: Procumbere] Rejicere membra fatigata, Curt. Projicere corpus humi, Liv. Deponere corpora sub ramis, Virg. Reclinari in gramine, Hor.
units.tr: Procumbere] To lay down tired limbs, Curt. To throw the body to the ground, Liv. To lay bodies down under the boughs, Virg. To recline on the grass, Hor.

units.la: Procurare] Vacare corpori, Plin. Iun. Concurare, Plaut. Munire ignem ne evagetur, Vlp. vid. Curare. Providere.
units.tr: Procurare] To attend to the body, Plin. Iun. To run about, Plaut. To guard a fire lest it spread, Ulp. See Curare and Providere (take care of, provide for).

units.la: Prodere] Edere auctorem, Liv. Efferre peccatum alicujus foris. Promere consilia alicujus. Effundo, quæ tacueram. Indicare conjurationem, Cic. Indicare de conjuratione, Cæs. Proferre aliquid foràs; in medium; in lucem; in aspectum, Cic. Per indicium enunciata res, Cæs. Effutire aliquid, Ter. Evulgare, Liv.
units.tr: Prodere] To put the author forward, Liv. To bring someone's fault out into the open. To disclose someone's plans. I pour out what I had kept silent. To reveal a conspiracy, Cic. To inform about a conspiracy, Caes. To bring something out into the open, into the middle, into the light, into view, Cic. The matter was made known by an informer, Caes. To blurt something out, Ter. To spread abroad, Liv.

units.la: Prodesse Utilitati esse, commodo. Magnos usus, utilitatem afferre. Fructum utilitatis præbere, Cic. E re esse. Non ab re esse, Plaut. In rem esse, Tac. Profore, Hor. vid. Utilis. Expedit.
units.tr: Prodesse] To be of use, of advantage. To bring great use and profit. To yield the fruit of advantage, Cic. To be to one's benefit. Not to be without profit, Plaut. To be of service, Tac. To profit, Hor. See Utilis and Expedit (useful, expedient).

units.la: Prodigalitas] Prodigentia, Tac. Prodigitas, Lucil. Profusio divitiarum, Suet. Profusa luxuries. Liberalitas dissolutior. Effusio liberalitatem imitatur, Cic. Nepotatus, Plin. Nequitia contrarium vitium frugalitati. Luxuria, Insolentia, Cic. Luxus populator opum, Claud. Largitas nimia, Ter.
units.tr: Prodigalitas] Prodigence, Tac. Prodigity, Lucil. Lavish squandering of riches, Suet. Wasteful luxury. Generosity that has grown dissolute. Squandering imitates liberality, Cic. Extravagance, Plin. Dissipation is the vice opposed to thrift. Luxury, insolence, Cic. Luxury, the plunderer of wealth, Claud. Excessive largess, Ter.

units.la: Prodigè vivere] Sumptuosius vivere. Effusè largeque donare, Cic. Profusissimè, Suet. vid. Seqq.
units.tr: Prodigè vivere] To live more extravagantly. To give lavishly and generously, Cic. Most lavishly, Suet. See the following entries.

units.la: Prodigere] Prodigè vivere. Profundere patrimonium. Abligurire fortunas suas. Effundere patrimonium : per luxuriam bona. Consumere bona. Devorare omnem pecuniam. Exhaurire immanes quæstûs. Dilapidare pecuniam. Dissipare, conficere rem, patrimonium. Comedere patrimonium, bona sua. Disperdere possessiones à majoribus relictas, Cic. Sumptus facere dapsiles. Lacerare validè rem suam. Vapulat peculium. Minùs cautè & cogitatè tractavit rem suam. Mortuâ re, verba nunc facis. Reni confringere. In deliciis disperdere. Diffunditare. Deterere, Plaut. Conturbare fortunas, Cic. Proficiscitur pecunia, Paul. I. C. Ire, redire pecuniam, dicit Vlp. Proluere opes, Tac. Eluere, Plaut. Pergræcari. Congræcare aliquid in lustris. Abuti rem patriam, Perdere. Degulare patrimonium, Plaut. Absumere, oblimare rem, Hor. Comesum, expotum, exutum, elotum in balneis, Plaut. Proterviam facere, Eras. corrigendum, Propter viam facere, Macrob. Fest. Plaut. Luxuriosè &) Exuere se paterno agro, Liv. Decoquere aliquid, Plaut. Insolenter re uti, Bud.
units.tr: Prodigere] To live prodigally. To squander one's inheritance. To lick up one's fortune. To pour out one's patrimony: to waste goods through luxury. To consume goods. To devour all one's money. To drain away enormous gains. To dissipate money. To scatter and ruin a property or patrimony. To eat up one's patrimony and goods. To squander the possessions left by one's ancestors, Cic. To make lavish expenses. To tear one's own property to pieces. His purse is being thrashed. He handled his property less carefully and thoughtfully. The thing is dead, and now you make speeches. To break one's kidneys. To ruin in pleasures. To squander, Plaut. To upset fortunes, Cic. Money goes away, Paul, J.C. Money goes out and comes back, says Ulp. To pour out wealth, Tac. To wash away, Plaut. To live in Greek fashion. To waste something in brothels. To abuse and destroy the ancestral property. To squander a patrimony, Plaut. To consume and sink property, Hor. Eaten, drunk, stripped, washed away in the baths, Plaut. "Proterviam facere," Eras. (to be corrected to "propter viam facere," Macrob., Fest., Plaut.). To live luxuriously, etc. To strip oneself of a paternal estate, Liv. To boil away something, Plaut. To use wealth insolently, Bud.

units.la: Prodigus] Prodigus sui peculii, Plaut. Profusus, sumptuosus homo. Luxuriosus, dissolutus, profusus, ac perditus nepos. Insolens. Effusior in largitione, Cic. Profusus sui, Salust. Promus magis quàm condus, Ausón. Impendiosus. Is vel Herculi conterere quæstum possit, Plaut. Effusus in luxum, Tac. Damnosus in ædificando, Suet. Ignorat quantùm ferratâ distet ab arcâ sacculus, Juv. Croesi opes prodigeret. Rei suæ inimicus. Malè gerens. Unicæ luxuriæ.
units.tr: Prodigus] Prodigal of his own property (Plaut.). A lavish, extravagant man. A luxurious, dissolute, wasteful, and ruined spendthrift. Insolent. More lavish in giving (Cic.). Wasteful of his own (Sall.). More a spender than a saver (Ausonius). Extravagant. He could squander Hercules' wealth (Plaut.). Given over to luxury (Tac.). Ruinous in building (Suet.). He does not know how far a purse is from an iron-bound chest (Juv.). He would squander the riches of Croesus. An enemy to his own affairs. Managing badly. Of luxury alone.

units.la: Prodigus fit indignus] Egebit, qui sua prodegerit.
units.tr: Prodigus fit indignus] He who squanders his own will be in want.

units.la: Prodire] Exire foràs. Exire limen, Ter. Efferre pedem. In conspectum se dare, Cic. Procedere foras, Plaut. Facessere ædibus, Pacuo. Venire in medium, Ter.
units.tr: Prodire] To go out, to come forth. To cross the threshold (Ter.). To put forward the foot. To show oneself in view (Cic.). To go forth (Plaut.). To clear out of the house (Pacuvius). To come into the open (Ter.).

units.la: Proditio] Rerum public. Proditio, Cic. Detectio, Vlp. Indicina, Apul. Indicatio, Vlp. Indicium conjurationis, Cic.
units.tr: Proditio] Betrayal of public affairs. Betrayal (Cic.). Disclosure (Ulp.). Informing (Apul.). Indication (Ulp.). Information about a conspiracy (Cic.).

units.la: Proditor] Traditor, Tac. Insidiator, Cic. Prævaricator, Vlp. Sociofraudus, Plaut. Index, Cic. Ascon.
units.tr: Proditor] Betrayer (Tac.). Ambusher (Cic.). Prevaricator (Ulp.). Partner in fraud (Plaut.). Informer (Cic., Ascon.).

units.la: Proditorius] Fraudatorius, I. C.
units.tr: Proditorius] Fraudulent (I.C.).

units.la: Proditoria epistola] Bellerophontis literæ (contra asse-rentem scriptæ.)
units.tr: Proditoria epistola] The letter of Bellerophon (written against the one who asserts it).

units.la: Producere] Proferre in medium, in prospectum, Cic. Præsentare aliquid alicui, Plin. Repræsentare, Id. Sistere, Cic.
units.tr: Producere] To bring forward into the open, into view (Cic.). To present something to someone (Plin.). To represent (Id.). To present, to produce (Cic.).

units.la: Profanare] Sacra profana habere. Profanum aliquid facere. Tollere, polluere religionem. Eripere religionem de domo Pontificis. Religiones & ceremonias sacrorum, fanorumque violare, Cic. Funestare templa, Id. Profestum facere, scil. diem, Fest. Exaugurare fana, sacella, Liv.
units.tr: Profanare] To hold sacred things as profane. To make something profane. To remove or defile religion. To snatch religion out of the house of the Pontiff. To violate the religious rites and ceremonies of sacred things and temples (Cic.). To desecrate temples (Cic.). To make a day profane (Fest.). To deconsecrate shrines and chapels (Liv.).

units.la: Profanatio] Usus profanus, Plin. Exauguratio, Liv.
units.tr: Profanatio] Profane use (Plin.). Deconsecration (Liv.).

units.la: Profanatus] Profanatum id, quod in sacrario pollutum, Var. Tegmina profana & usu polluta, Tac. Defanatus, Arnob.
units.tr: Profanatus] Profaned is that which has been polluted in the sanctuary (Varro). Profane coverings, polluted by use (Tac.). Desecrated (Arnob.).

units.la: Profanus] Omni religione solutus, Fest. Profestus homo, Gell. Procul esse profani, Virg. i. non initiati sacris, Cerd. Absint meretrices, ne quid parum sanctum occurrat, Tertul.
units.tr: Profanus] Released from all religion (Fest.). A common, ordinary man (Gell.). Keep far away, you profane ones (Virg.), that is, those not initiated into the rites (Cerd.). Let harlots be kept away, lest anything not sufficiently holy come across you (Tertul.).

units.la: Profectio] Peragratio itinerum, vid. Abitio. Equitatio.
units.tr: Profectio] A going about on journeys; see Abitio, Equitatio.

units.la: Profecto] Ne vivam, si scio. Ita vivam, Cic. vid. Certè.
units.tr: Profecto] So may I live, if I know. Truly, so may I live (Cic.); see Certè.

units.la: Profectus] Progressus in studiis. Progressio dicendi: progressio ad virtutem, Cic. Processus in literis, Suet. Postprincipia. Utilitas in postprincipiis exsistit, Var.
units.tr: Profectus] Progress in studies. Progress in speaking; progress toward virtue (Cic.). Advancement in letters (Suet.). Postprincipia. Utility arises in postprincipia (Varro).

units.la: Proferre] Proferre foras aliquid, Cic. In solem, Plin. In conspectum, Cæs. Progerere, Plin.
units.tr: Proferre] To bring something forth into the open (Cic.). Into the sun (Plin.). Into view (Caes.). To put forward (Plin.).

units.la: Professor] Interpres alicujus artis, poëtarum, juris, Cic. Exercens eloquentiam meritoriam, Tac.
units.tr: Professor] A teacher of some art, of poets, or of law (Cic.). One who practises eloquence for pay (Tac.).

units.la: Professus, vid. Manifestus.
units.tr: Professus, see Manifestus.

units.la: Proficere] Procedere in virtute: ad virtutem. Facere progressum in studiis. Progressio facta ad virtutem, Cic. Profectum facere sub Præceptore, Plin. Iun. Proficere ad bonitatem, Quint.
units.tr: Proficere] To advance in virtue, toward virtue. To make progress in studies. Progress made toward virtue (Cic.). To make progress under a teacher (Plin. Iun.). To make progress toward goodness (Quint.).

units.la: Nihil proficere] Nihil promovere, Vlp. Ne digitum quidem progredi, Cic. Parùm proficere, Id. Quàm te magis in altum capessis, tam æstus te in portum refert. Spissum est. Pro spisso evenit, Plaut. Quod tenetur, per manus fugit, Sen. Pullus tuus semper parvus. Cùm plurimùm laboravimus, in eodem statu sumus.
units.tr: Nihil proficere] To accomplish nothing (Ulp.). Not to move a finger forward (Cic.). To achieve little (Cic.). The more you strive for the heights, the more the tide carries you back to harbour. It is a tight fix; it has turned out a tight fix (Plaut.). What is held slips through the hands (Sen.). Your chick is always small. When we have toiled most, we are in the same state.

units.la: Proficisci] Contendere cursum aliquò, Plin. Cursu concontendo petere, Virg. Alium cursum petierunt. Pergere per mare. Contendere, Abs. Facere iter. Isti, & redisti. Tendere Venusiam. Longius progredi, Cic. Pergo tendere aliquò, Virg. Petere rus, Suet. Facere profectionem, Caes. Pertendere, Liv. vid. Ire & Progredi.
units.tr: Proficisci] To make for a destination (Plin.). To set off on a course (Virg.). They have made for another course. To make a passage over the sea. To strive, to press on (Abs.). To make a journey. You went and came back. To make for Venusia. To go further (Cic.). I make straight for somewhere (Virg.). To seek the countryside (Suet.). To set out (Caes.). To press on through (Liv.). See Ire & Progredi.

units.la: Profiteri] Palàm profiteri, Liv. Ego, quod facio, me omnium vestrum causâ facere, testor, Cic.
units.tr: Profiteri] To declare openly (Liv.). I call you to witness that what I do, I do for the sake of you all (Cic.).

units.la: Profiteri Philosophiam] Præcipere artem Oratoriam. Prælegere pueris, Quint. Explicare Scholam, Cic. Habeo Scholam de aliquâ re, ex Cic. Prodocere, Hor.
units.tr: Profiteri Philosophiam] To teach the art of oratory. To read lessons to boys (Quint.). To explain a school (Cic.). I hold a school on some subject (from Cic.). To teach publicly (Hor.).

units.la: Profligare hostes] Prosternere aciem. Dare stragem. Fundere exercitum. Facere cladem. Sternere catervas hostium, Liv. Stragem edere, facere. Conficere & opprimere hostes. Effligere aliquem, Cic. Fœdant & proterunt hostium copias, Plaut. Fundere copias, Caes. Prosternere hostes, Cic. Protelare, Fest.
units.tr: Profligare hostes] To rout the battle line. To inflict slaughter. To rout the army. To make a massacre. To lay low the enemy's battalions (Liv.). To make a slaughter. To finish off and crush the enemy. To strike down someone (Cic.). They crush and trample the enemy's forces (Plaut.). To rout the forces (Caes.). To lay enemies low (Cic.). To drive off (Fest.).

units.la: Profluere, vid. Fluere.
units.tr: Profluere, see Fluere.

units.la: Profluvium narium] Eruptio sanguinis è naribus, Celf. Profluvium ventris] Fluxus ventris, Plin. Fluxio, Id. vid. Alvus cita.
units.tr: Profluvium narium] A discharge of blood from the nostrils (Celsus). Profluvium ventris] Flux of the belly (Plin.). A flow (Id.); see Alvus cita.

units.la: Profluus, vid. Fluidus.
units.tr: Profluus, see Fluidus.

units.la: Profugere] Profugere à Domino, Cic. Profugere Dominos, Curt. Aufugere alicui, Cic. Transfugere ab aliquo, Id. Ad hostes, Liv. Perfugere ad aliquem, Cic. Transvolare ad hostes, Plaut. Ad transeundum hostes vocabant, Lib. Facere transitionem (ad hostes,) Hirt.
units.tr: Profugere] To flee from one's master (Cic.). To run away from masters (Curt.). To flee from someone (Cic.). To desert someone (Cic.). To desert to the enemy (Liv.). To take refuge with someone (Cic.). To fly across to the enemy (Plaut.). They summoned them to desert to the enemy (Liv.). To make a defection to the enemy (Hirt.).

units.la: Profugus] Fugitivus : Perfuga ab aliquo. Transfuga. Retractus ex fugâ, Cic. Desertor, Liv. Defector, Tac. Refugus, Id. Refuga, Ulp. Profuga castra, Claud. Fugitor, Plaut.
units.tr: Profugus] A fugitive; a deserter from someone; a turncoat. Brought back from flight (Cic.). Deserter (Liv.). Defector (Tac.). Refugee (Id.). Refugee (Ulp.). Fugitive camps (Claud.). Runaway (Plaut.).

units.la: Profundè.] Altè, Liv. Altius imprimere. Penitùs abstrusum, insitum insedit. Depressius, Cic.
units.tr: Profunde] Deeply (Liv.). To imprint more deeply. Lodged deep, implanted, sank in deeply. More deeply (Cic.).

units.la: Profundere] Refundere, Propert. Progere, Apul. Profdare rivos sanguinis pectore, Stat. Evomere, Ter. vid. Effundere.
units.tr: Profundere] To pour out again (Propert.). To pour forth (Apul.). To spill streams of blood from the breast (Stat.). To vomit (Ter.); see Effundere.

units.la: Profunditas] In profundo veritas. Altum, altitudo maris, Cic. Profunda Ponti, Lucr. Gurges, Pl. Fastigium fossæ, Var.
units.tr: Profunditas] Truth lies in the depths. The deep, the depth of the sea (Cic.). The deep of the Pontus (Lucr.). A whirlpool (Pl.). The bottom of a ditch (Varro).

units.la: Profundus] Altus fluvius, Caes. Præaltus, Liv. Interiores & reconditæ literæ, Cic. Penitus : penitas radices, Acci.
units.tr: Profundus] A deep river (Caes.). Very deep (Liv.). Inner and recondite letters (Cic.). Deep, deep-rooted (Accius).

units.la: Profusè, vid. Prodigè. & Catervatim. Profusio bonorum in copia] Cum multum est piperis, etiam oleribus immiscet, vid. Prodigalitas.
units.tr: Profusè, see Prodigè and Catervatim. Profusio bonorum in copia] When there is much pepper, one mixes it even into the vegetables; see Prodigalitas.

units.la: Profusus, vid. Prodigus.
units.tr: Profusus, see Prodigus.

units.la: Progenies] Proles illa futurorum hominum. Oriundus ab aliquo, Cic. Semen æthereum. Soboles Deûm, Virg. Propago Romana, Id. Propages sanguinis, Pacuv. Seminium, Var. Lucr. Interpr. Gifan. Monumentum generi, vel, generis, Plaut.
units.tr: Progenies] That offspring of future men. Descended from someone (Cic.). Ethereal seed. Offspring of the gods (Virg.). Roman progeny (Virg.). Progeny of blood (Pacuv.). Seed, seedling (Var., Lucr., Interpr. Gifan.). A memorial of the family or of the race (Plaut.).

units.la: Prognatus] Abaliquo prognatus, Hor. Natus: Natus ex aliquo. Cretus, Satus Hercule, Virg. Profatus, Cypr.
units.tr: Prognatus] Descended from someone (Hor.). Born: born from someone. Begotten, sprung from Hercules (Virg.). Uttered forth (Cypr.).

units.la: Progredi] Ultrà progredi. Longiùs discedere. Pergo ire. Pergo conficere reliquum iter. Perge, qui coepisti: perge aliqua. Gradum ad aliquid jacere, facere. Gradibus venire ad virtutum. Processûs efficere. Transfire ad. Tendere ad reliqua, Cic. Tendere ultrà, Liv. Provehi, Quint. Proferre gradum, Plaut. Promovere gradum, Sil. Proferre passûs, Lucr. Pedem, Hor. Promovere, Abs. Ter.
units.tr: Progredi] To go beyond. To withdraw further. To go on. To carry on the remaining journey. Persevere, you who have begun; persevere in something. To take a step toward something. To come by steps to virtue. To make advances. To pass over to. To extend to the rest (Cic.). To stretch further (Liv.). To advance (Quint.). To step forward (Plaut.). To advance a step (Sil.). To take paces forward (Lucr.). To advance a foot (Hor.). To advance (Abs., Ter.).

units.la: Progressio] Progressu maximo procurrere. Processus militum, Cæs. Processio ad aliquid. Gradatio ab uuo ad aliquid, Cic.
units.tr: Progressio] To run forward at full speed. The advance of soldiers (Caes.). An advance toward something. A gradual ascent from one thing to another (Cic.).

units.la: Prohibere] Prohibere aliquem ab injuriâ. Prohibere conatus alicujus, Cic. Prohibebere aliquem cibo, &c. à. Prohibere ne, Id. Prohibessis, i. Prohibeas, Cat. Impedire à vel ab: ne: quò minùs. Impediri aliquâ re. Eripere alicui potestatem, facultatem alicujus rei. Interpellare aliquem quin: quò minùs. Impedimento sum quò secius feratur. Obstare alicui ne: quò minùs. Non sinere. Non pati. Privare aliquem potestate faciendi aliquid. Arcere à progressu. Adimere alicui facultatem faciendi. Arcere Reditu. Non est si tres per,&c. Accusare. Denegare, negare aliquid alicui, Cic. Intercedere alicui. Vindicare aliquem à vel ab, Id. Demere potestatem, Iul. Cap. Dempsit rumoribus adolescendi facultatem, Cic.
units.tr: Prohibere] To keep someone from wrongdoing. To check someone's attempts (Cic.). To keep someone from food, etc. To prevent (Cic.). To forbid (Cat.). To hinder from, or that something not happen, or so that not. To be prevented by something. To take away from someone the power or opportunity of doing something. To interrupt someone, that not, or so that not. I stand in the way so that it is not carried more easily. To stand in someone's way, lest. Not to allow. Not to suffer. To deprive someone of the power to do something. To keep from progress. To take away someone's opportunity to do something. To keep from returning. To accuse. To deny, to refuse something to someone (Cic.). To intercede against someone. To protect someone from (Cic.). To take away the power (Iul. Cap.). He took from the rumours the opportunity to grow (Cic.).

units.la: Prohibita impotentius concupiscimus] Nitimur in vetitum semper, cupimusque negata.
units.tr: Prohibita impotentius concupiscimus] We always strive, without restraint, for what is forbidden, and we desire what is refused.

units.la: Prohibitor] Propulsator, Val. Max. Depulsor dominatûs, Cic.
units.tr: Prohibitor] A defender (Val. Max.). A repeller of tyranny (Cic.).

units.la: Prohibitus] Vetitus. Interdictus. Interminatus cibus, Hor. PræVetitus, Sil.
units.tr: Prohibitus] Forbidden; prohibited; banned. Forbidden food (Hor.). Previously forbidden (Sil.).

units.la: Projectio] Conjectio telorum, Cic. Conjectus brachii, Lucr. oculorum, Cic. Jaculatio testarum, Minut. Fel. Jactatus pennarum, Ovid.
units.tr: Projectio] A throwing of missiles (Cic.). A casting out of an arm (Lucr.), of the eyes (Cic.). A hurling of potsherds (Minut. Fel.). A flapping of wings (Ovid).

units.la: Projectus, vid. Abjectus & Expositivius. Projicere, vid. Abjicere. Prom, vid. Ergo.
units.tr: Projectus, see Abjectus & Expositivius. Projicere, see Abjicere. Prom, see Ergo.

units.la: Prolapsus] Abjectus, prostratus, jacens, Cic. Prociduus, Plin. Sublapsus, Vir. Caducus, Varr. v. Afflictus, & Miser.
units.tr: Prolapsus] Cast down, prostrate, lying (Cic.). Bent forward (Plin.). Sliding under (Virg.). Falling (Varr.). See Afflictus & Miser.

units.la: Prolatio juris, vid. Dilatio.
units.tr: Prolatio juris, see Dilatio.

units.la: Proles] Propages sanguinis, Pacuv. Amor utriusque sobolis æqualis, Plin. Ditescere dulci partu, Lucr. vid. Progenies.
units.tr: Proles] Progeny of blood (Pacuv.). The love of both offspring is equal (Plin.). To grow rich through a sweet birth (Lucr.); see Progenies.

units.la: Proles similis parentum] E squillâ non nascitur rosa. Nec imbellem ferores progenerant aquilæ columbam. Non procul à proprio stipite poma cadunt. Mali corvi malum ovum. E viperâ rursum vipera nascitur.
units.tr: Proles similis parentum] A rose is not born of a squill. Nor does a fierce eagle beget a timid dove. Apples do not fall far from their own stock. Bad crows lay a bad egg. From a viper, again, a viper is born.

units.la: Proletarius, vid. Vilis homo.
units.tr: Proletarius, see Vilis homo.

units.la: Prolixè loqui] Loqui supra clepsydram. Longum nimis loqui, Plaut. Multum esse in aliqua re. Longius prosequi, Cic. Latius, Quint. altius, Plin. Dilatare oratione. Longius excurrit oratio. Infinitè fertur ut flumen, Cic. Expatiari, Quint.
units.tr: Prolixè loqui] To talk beyond the water-clock. To speak too long (Plaut.). To be lengthy on some matter. To pursue a subject further (Cic.), more widely (Quint.), more deeply (Plin.). To spread out in speech. The speech runs on at length; it flows on endlessly like a river (Cic.). To range freely (Quint.).

units.la: Prolixum scriptum] Iliade prolixius.
units.tr: Prolixum scriptum] Longer than the Iliad.

units.la: Prolixus sermo] Asianus tumor, vid. Longus.
units.tr: Prolixus sermo] Asian bombast; see Longus.

units.la: Prolongare aliquid] Longius aliquid facere. Producere convivium, sermonem in multam noctem. Prorogare tempus alicui. Ducere bellum. Proferre vitam beatam usque ad rogum. Trahere bellum, Cic. Elongare, Plin. Protatare vitam, Tac. Protrahere moram lentâ fame, Senec.
units.tr: Prolongare aliquid] To make something longer. To prolong a banquet or a conversation into the late night. To extend time for someone. To drag out a war. To prolong a happy life up to the funeral pyre. To drag out a war, Cic. To lengthen, Plin. To prolong life, Tac. To drag out a delay by slow hunger, Sen.

units.la: Prolubium, vid. Lubentia. Proludium, vid. Præludium. Proluvies alvi. vid. Alvus cita.
units.tr: Prolubium: see Lubentia. Proludium: see Præludium. Proluvies alvi: see Alvus cita.

units.la: Promere] Promere vinum dolio, Hor. vid. Expromere, & Relinere.
units.tr: Promere] To bring wine out of the cask, Hor. See Expromere and Relinere.

units.la: Promereri, vid. Mereri. Promeritum, vid. Meritum.
units.tr: Promereri: see Mereri. Promeritum: see Meritum.

units.la: Promicare] Emicare, Plaut. Intermicat aurum squammis, Claud. Dissultat splendor aquæ per tecta, Scintillare, Plin. Sil. Radiare, Tac.
units.tr: Promicare] To flash forth, Plaut. Gold glitters between the scales, Claud. The brightness of water leaps across the roofs; to sparkle, Plin. Sil. To shine out, Tac.

units.la: Prominens] Eminentes oculi, Cic. Prominulus, Iul. Capit. Projectus venter, Cic. Propensus aqualiculus, Pers. Eminula crura, Var. Pulvinata labra, Plin. Dorsuosus, Salni. vid. Eminens. Prominentia, in picturis] Eminentiæ in pictura, Cic. Enitentiæ colorum. Splendor coloris. Tonus, Plin. Lumina, Id. Bud. vid. Eminentia.
units.tr: Prominens] Bulging eyes, Cic. Somewhat prominent, Iul. Capit. A protruding belly, Cic. A swollen paunch, Pers. Somewhat bulging shins, Var. Puffed-out lips, Plin. Humped-backed, Salni. See Eminens. Prominentia, in picturis] Projection in painting, Cic. Vividness of colours. Brightness of colour. Tone, Plin. Highlights, Id. Bud. See Eminentia.

units.la: Prominere] Projicitur rectum. Eminet foras aliquid, Cic. Excurrit peninsula, Liv. Procurrit mons in occidentem, Col. Inter digitos medius longissimè protenditur, Plin. Superexcurrit arbor, Vlp. Prominent à cæterâ acie, Liv. vid. Exserere, & Eminere.
units.tr: Prominere] To jut out straight. Something projects outward, Cic. A peninsula runs out, Liv. A mountain juts out to the west, Col. The middle finger stretches out furthest among the fingers, Plin. A tree towers above, Vlp. They stand out from the rest of the line, Liv. See Exserere and Eminere.

units.la: Promiscuus, vid. Mistus, & Communis.
units.tr: Promiscuus: see Mistus and Communis.

units.la: Promissio] Pollicitatio, Ter. Pollicitum, Ovid. Memores pollicitì nostri, Col. Promissum, Cic.
units.tr: Promissio] Promise, Ter. A pledge, Ovid. Mindful of our promise, Col. A promise, Cic.

units.la: Promissor] Largiloquus. Oratione beneficus. Lingua factiosus. Dapsilis dictis, Plaut. Pollicitator, Dig.
units.tr: Promissor] One who promises lavishly. Generous in speech. Smooth-tongued. Lavish with words, Plaut. A promiser, Dig.

units.la: Promissum] Receptum: promissa ac recepta invertit, ad séque transtulit, Cic. Vadimonium, Apul. Flagitare vadimonium, Britan.
units.tr: Promissum] Something undertaken: he reversed his promises and undertakings and transferred them to himself, Cic. A recognizance, Apul. To demand a recognizance, Britan.

units.la: Promissum solvendum] Omne promissum (de jure) cadit in debitum. Res vana & stulta, dare nihil promittere multa.
units.tr: Promissum solvendum] Every promise (by law) falls into debt. It is a vain and foolish thing to give nothing while promising much.

units.la: Promissum solvere] Persolvere, complere promissum. Præsto quod promisi. Patrare, Solvere promissa. Stare promissis. Satisfacere promissis & promissioni. Diem promissorum repræsentare. Præstare exitu pollicita, Cic. Præstare promissum: fidem promissi. Exonerare, exsolvere fidem suam, Liv. Exsolvo quod promisi, Cic. Implere promissum, Plin. Iun. Perficere promissa, Ter. Persequi dicta promissa factis, Plaut. Exsolvere promissa, Tibul.
units.tr: Promissum solvere] To pay what was promised; to fulfil a promise in full. I deliver what I promised. To accomplish promises, to pay promises. To abide by promises. To satisfy promises and the promise. To present the day of promised things. To make good on what was promised by the outcome, Cic. To make good a promise: the pledge of a promise. To discharge one's word and pay one's pledge, Liv. I pay what I promised, Cic. To fulfil a promise, Plin. Iun. To carry out promises, Ter. To follow words promised by deeds, Plaut. To pay promises, Tibul.

units.la: Promittere aliquid alicui] Polliceri aliquid & de aliqua re, Cic. Promittere de re aliquâ. Recipere alicui aliquid. Profiteri operam suam. Præstare de me possum. Dare fidem. Dicere pecuniam. Spondere se satisfacturum. Despondere alicui bibliothecam, Cic. Pollicitor tibi meam operam, Plaut. Promittis aliquem morari, Lucr. Pronunciare munus populo, Suet. Addicunt auspicia, Tac.
units.tr: Promittere aliquid alicui] To promise something to someone: to promise something concerning some matter, Cic. To promise something about some matter. To undertake something for someone. To offer one's service. I can vouch for myself. To give one's word. To name a sum of money. To pledge oneself to make satisfaction. To betroth a library to someone, Cic. I promise you my service, Plaut. You promise that someone will delay, Lucr. To announce a gift to the people, Suet. The auspices assent, Tac.

units.la: Promittere sanctè, vid. Spondere.
units.tr: Promittere sanctè: see Spondere.

units.la: Promittere præsentiam] Promittere ad aliquem, Cic. Promittere alicui ad prandium, Sen. Pignorari coenæ alicujus, Apul.
units.tr: Promittere præsentiam] To promise one's presence: to promise to come to someone, Cic. To promise someone to come to dinner, Sen. To pledge oneself to someone's dinner, Apul.

units.la: Promittere non præstare] Dare verba. Leonis loco mu-rem rem ostendere. Aures verbis divitare. Acci. Fidei tesse-ram apud me fregisti, Plaut.
units.tr: Promittere non præstare] To give words. Instead of a lion, to show a mouse. To enrich the ears with words, Acci. You have broken the token of faith with me, Plaut.

units.la: Promittere nimia, vid. Polliceri.
units.tr: Promittere nimia: see Polliceri.

units.la: Promontorium] Eminentes terræ partes.
units.tr: Promontorium] Projecting parts of land.

units.la: Promotio retrograda] Ab equis ad asinos.
units.tr: Promotio retrograda] From horses to asses.

units.la: Promovere] Proferre munitiones, Cæs. Propagare im-perium, Liv. Orationem meam vestra benignitas provexit longius, Cic. Pennas addere negotio.
units.tr: Promovere] To push forward fortifications, Caes. To extend the empire, Liv. Your kindness has carried my speech further, Cic. To add wings to a business.

units.la: Promoveri in melius] Ab asinis ad boves transcendere.
units.tr: Promoveri in melius] To move up from asses to oxen.

units.la: Promptè, vid. Alacriter. Promptus, vid. Paratus.
units.tr: Promptè: see Alacriter. Promptus: see Paratus.

units.la: In promptu] Promptum est. Obviium est, Cic. Ad manum habere, Tac. Sub manu, Cic. In procinctu, Quint. Obviam est, Plaut. Sub ictu rem habere, Sen. In mundo est, Fest. Plaut. Ante pedes est, Ter.
units.tr: In promptu] It is ready. It lies open to hand, Cic. To have at hand, Tac. Under the hand, Cic. In readiness, Quint. It is in the way, Cic. To have a thing within striking distance, Sen. It is in good order, Fest. Plaut. It is before one's feet, Ter.

units.la: Promptuarium, vid. Penu] Promulgare, vid. Proclamare.
units.tr: Promptuarium, see Penu] To publish; see Proclamare.

units.la: Promus] Condus promus, Plaut. Cellarius, Col. Procurator peni, Plaut. Penator, Cat. Siliginarius, Vlp. Oeconomus, Sipont.
units.tr: Promus] Steward of provisions, Plaut. Cellarer, Col. Steward of the pantry, Plaut. Pantry-keeper, Cat. Keeper of fine bread, Vlp. Housekeeper, Sipont.

units.la: Pronuba]Prommestria & Proxenetria, Alc. Ianitrix, Gloss.
units.tr: Pronuba] Matchmaker and go-between, Alc. Doorkeeper, Gloss.

units.la: Pronubus] Paranymphus, Sipont. Nuptiarum auspex, Plaut. Simpulator (Sponsi amicus,) Isid. Simplator, Fulgent.
units.tr: Pronubus] Best man, Sipont. Patron of the wedding, Plaut. Simpulator (friend of the bridegroom), Isid. Simplator, Fulgent.

units.la: Pronunciare] Pronunciare aptè, Plin. Iun. Efferre non indecenter, Quint. Verba proferre, Ovid. Eloqui, Plaut. Exprimere literas putidiùs, Cic. Articulare verba, Apul. Sum planiloquus, Plaut.
units.tr: Pronunciare] To pronounce fittingly, Plin. Iun. To utter not unbecomingly, Quint. To bring out words, Ovid. To speak out, Plaut. To express letters too affectedly, Cic. To articulate words, Apul. I am plain-spoken, Plaut.

units.la: Pronunciatio] Pronunciatus, Gell. Vocesipso profatu insuaves, Id. Recta locutio. Emendata cum suavitate vocum explanatio, Quint.
units.tr: Pronunciatio] Pronouncement, Gell. Voices that are unpleasant in the very utterance, Id. Correct speech. An explanation of the voice made correct with pleasantness, Quint.

units.la: Pronus] Pronum in ventrem puerorum equo imponere, Varr. Pandata manus, Quint. Plano situ testam digitis comprehensam, Minut. Fel. In planum jacet, Vitr.
units.tr: Pronus] To set boys face-down on a horse, Varr. A hand held open, Quint. Plano situ a shell held between the fingers, Minut. Fel. It lies flat, Vitr.

units.la: Proœmium, vid. Præfatio.
units.tr: Proœmium: see Præfatio.

units.la: Propagare] Prodere posteritatem. Proseminare familiam, Cic. Procudere propagando prolem, Lucr. vid. Multiplicare, Augere.
units.tr: Propagare] To hand down to posterity. To sow a family, Cic. To produce offspring by propagating, Lucr. See Multiplicare, Augere.

units.la: Propagatio arborum] Propago vitium, Plin. Propago disciplinarum, Var. Propages, Fest. Fruticatio, Plin. vid.
units.tr: Propagatio arborum] Layering of vines, Plin. Propagation of teachings, Var. Shoots, Fest. Shrubbing, Plin. See.

units.la: Propago, vid. Palmes & Progenies. Propalam, vid. Palam.
units.tr: Propago: see Palmes and Progenies. Propalam: see Palam.

units.la: Prope] Propinquè, Plaut. Haud procul: in propinquo, Liv. Proximè jamam : in proximo. Ante pedes, Cic. Proximum est, Ter. In conspectu, & sub ictu aliquid, Sen. In foribus adest. Intra januam est. Nihil propius quàm, vid. Imminere.
units.tr: Prope] Nearby, Plaut. Not far off; in the neighbourhood, Liv. Very nearly now; in the nearest place. Before one's feet, Cic. It is next, Ter. In sight, and within striking distance of something, Sen. It is present at the doors. It is inside the threshold. Nothing nearer than; see Imminere.

units.la: Propediem, vid. Brevi, & Quotidie.
units.tr: Propediem: see Brevi and Quotidie.

units.la: Propemodum, vid. Fere.
units.tr: Propemodum: see Fere.

units.la: Propendere, vid. Inclinare.
units.tr: Propendere: see Inclinare.

units.la: Propensio, vid. Proclivis.
units.tr: Propensio: see Proclivis.

units.la: Propensè, vid. Proclivitas, Libenter.
units.tr: Propensè: see Proclivitas, Libenter.

units.la: Properans] Properanter. Properare, vid. Festinus. Fe-stinanter, &c. Ovid.
units.tr: Properans] Hastily. To hasten: see Festinus. Festinanter, etc., Ovid.

units.la: Propheta] Prophetia vid. Vates, Vaticinium, &c.
units.tr: Propheta] Prophetia: see Vates, Vaticinium, etc.

units.la: Propinare alicui] Provocare aliquem poculo pleno, Had. Propino tibi hôc poculô. Poscere poculis, Cic. Inquietare aliquem poculô, Plaut. Præbibere alicui, Apul. Propino tibi salutem plenis faucibus, Plaut. Sit salubris potio, bibe salutem, &c.
units.tr: Propinare alicui] To pledge someone: to challenge someone to a full cup, Had. I pledge you this cup. To call for drinks, Cic. To harass someone with a cup, Plaut. To drink first to someone, Apul. I pledge you good health with full throats, Plaut. May the drink be wholesome; drink to health, etc.

units.la: Propinquè, vid. Prope.
units.tr: Propinquè: see Prope.

units.la: Propinquitas] Proximitas vitii & virtutis, Ovid. Vicinia, Col. Vicinitas, Cic. Confinium artis & falsi, Tac.
units.tr: Propinquitas] Nearness of vice and virtue, Ovid. Neighbourhood, Col. Vicinity, Cic. The border between skill and falsehood, Tac.

units.la: Propinquus] Proximus alicui, ab aliquo, post aliquem, Cic. Proximior, Sen. Citerior, Citimus. Vicinus alicui, Cic.
units.tr: Propinquus] Nearest to someone, from someone, after someone, Cic. Nearer, Sen. Nearer on this side; nearest. Neighbouring to someone, Cic.

units.la: Propitiare] Propitium reddere, Plaut. Piaculare Deos, Cat. vid. Placare.
units.tr: Propitiare] To render favourable, Plaut. To make expiation to the gods, Cat. See Placare.

units.la: Propitio Deo] Bona obtingunt expiatis.
units.tr: Propitio Deo] Good things befall those who have made expiation.

units.la: Propitius] Propitia fortuna. Dii propitii, Cic. Volens propitiusque sis, Cit. Dexter volensque adsit, Quint.
units.tr: Propitius] Favourable fortune. Propitious gods, Cic. May you be willing and favourable, Cit. May he be present, favourable and willing, Quint.

units.la: Proponere aliquid alicui] Referre ad Senatum aliquid de re aliquâ. Ponere ante oculos, in oculis, & aspectu. Defigere in mentibus & oculis omnium. Constituere in oculis hominum aliquid. Statuere ante oculos, Cic. Subjicere sub oculos, Quint. Oculis, Plin. Subexhibere, Arnob.
units.tr: Proponere aliquid alicui] To refer something concerning some matter to the Senate. To place before the eyes, in the eyes, and in sight. To fix in the minds and eyes of all. To set something before people's eyes. To set before the eyes, Cic. To place under the eyes, Quint. Before the eyes, Plin. To exhibit below, Arnob.

units.la: Proponere sibi, vid. Constituere.
units.tr: Proponere sibi: see Constituere.

units.la: Proportio] Convenientia partium. Apta compositio. Portio. Analogia, Cic. Congruentia statuæ ad. Plin. Iun. Symmetria. Conveniens consensus. Responsus ad Vitr. Plin. Commensus, Commodulatio membrorum, Vitr. Competentia, Gell. Ratio, Cito. Vitr.
units.tr: Proportio] Agreement of parts. Apt arrangement. Portion. Analogy, Cic. Harmony of a statue, Plin. Iun. Symmetry. Fitting agreement. Correspondence, Vitr. Plin. Commensuration; due proportioning of the limbs, Vitr. Suitability, Gell. Ratio, Cic. Vitr.

units.la: Propositio excellens, vid. Quæstio abstrusa.
units.tr: Propositio excellens: see Quæstio abstrusa.

units.la: Propositum] Propositio animi. Institutum, Cic. Destinatio, Plin. Suscepta sententia, Id. Mens, Voluntas, Cic. Animus, Ter.
units.tr: Propositum] A resolve of mind. Plan, Cic. Determination, Plin. A resolution taken, Id. Mind, will, Cic. Intention, Ter.

units.la: Propositum est mihi] Habeo institutum & deliberatum cum animo. Ita animatus sum. Nihil deliberatius illi est, quùm ut &c, Cic. Stat sententia, Ter. In animo est, Liv. Consilium est ita facere, Plaut. Certum apud animum meum constat, Liv. Definitum, decretum est mihi, Plaut.
units.tr: Propositum est mihi] I have a settled and deliberate plan in my mind. I am so minded. Nothing is more settled for him than that, Cic. My mind is made up, Ter. It is in my mind, Liv. It is my plan to do so, Plaut. It is certain in my mind, Liv. It has been determined and decreed for me, Plaut.

units.la: Proprietas] Natura herbarum, Plin. Qualitas cœli, Quint. Ingenium cœli, Plin. Indoles frugum, Liv. Virtus verbi, dictionis, Cic.
units.tr: Proprietas] The nature of herbs, Plin. The quality of the sky, Quint. The character of the climate, Plin. The disposition of crops, Liv. The force of a word or expression, Cic.

units.la: Proprietas linguæ] Genius linguæ.
units.tr: Proprietas linguæ] The genius of the language.

units.la: Proprius] Germana patria. Peculiaris, Cic. Peculatorius, Var. Vernaculus, Plin. Mancipi, vel mancupi res, Cic. Vlp. Privus Hor. Privatus. Suus. Nativus. Singularis, Cic. Id maximè decet, quod est cuique suum maximè. Specialis, Iul. Capit. Genitalis. Genuinus, Amm. Tanquam meum met genium, Plaut.
units.tr: Proprius] One's true native land. Peculiar, Cic. Pertaining to embezzlement, Var. Native, Plin. Things held by mancipation, Cic. Vlp. Private, Hor. Private. One's own. Native. Particular, Cic. That suits each one most which is most his own. Special, Iul. Capit. Innate. Genuine, Amm. As though my own self were my genius, Plaut.

units.la: Propria placent] Crepitus auctori suo benè olet. Patriæ fumus igni alieno luculentior. Patria sua cuique jucundissima.
units.tr: Propria placent] A fart smells sweet to its own author. The smoke of one's own country is brighter than another's fire. Each man's own country is most pleasant to him.

units.la: De proprio vivere] Vivere propriâ quadrâ.
units.tr: De proprio vivere] To live on one's own means.

units.la: Propter] Præ lacrymis. Per discordiam optimatum. Meô, tuô, beneficiô, Cic. Nec defendendi præ altitudine erat copia, Amm. Ex paupertate parcus, Plaut. Amoris vitio, non meô, nunc morologus fio, Id. Honoris causâ. Hominum gratiâ. Amicitiæ nomine, Cic. Ingratiam.
units.tr: Propter] Because of tears. Through the discord of the nobles. By my, your, his kindness, Cic. There was no means of defending because of the depth, Amm. Frugal through poverty, Plaut. Through my lover's fault, not mine, I now become a cranky fellow, Id. For the sake of honour. For the sake of men. In the name of friendship, Cic. Into favour.

units.la: Propterea, vid. Ideo.
units.tr: Propterea: see Ideo.

units.la: Propugnaculum] Munitio. Præsidium, Cic. Procestria, pl. Fest. Tutamentum, Liv.
units.tr: Propugnaculum] Fortification. Defence, Cic. Procestria, pl. Fest. Protection, Liv.

units.la: Propugnare, vid. defendere. Propulsare, vid. Abigere.
units.tr: To defend, see defend. To drive back, see Drive away.

units.la: Propulsatio] Repulsus, Cic. Recussus, Plin.
units.tr: Propulsatio: Repulsus, Cic. Recussus, Plin.

units.la: Prorepere] Erepere. Proserpere, Plaut.
units.tr: Prorepere: To creep out; to escape. Proserpere (to creep forth), Plaut.

units.la: Prorex] Interrex, Cic. Subregulus, Amm.
units.tr: Prorex: Interrex, Cic. Subregulus, Amm.

units.la: Proripere. vid. Erumpere. Prorsus, vid. Penitùs. Prosa orat. vid. Oratio.
units.tr: Proripere, see Erumpere. Prorsus, see Penitus. Prose (oratio soluta), see Oratio.

units.la: Prosapia] prosapies, Hon. Progenies. Propago, Virg. Propages sanguinis, Pacuv. Stemma, Paul IC. Genus, Plin. Trames generis, Gell.
units.tr: Prosapia: prosapies, Hon. Progeny. Offspring, Virg. Line of blood, Pacuv. Family tree, Paul IC. Stock, Plin. Track of descent, Gell.

units.la: Proscribere aliquem] Agere in exilium. Igni & aquâ interdicere. Interdicere igne, aquâ, tecto, Cic. Proscriptionem ferre de capite alicujus. Velle, jubere, ut aliquis in civitate ne sit, Id. Proscripturire, proscriptionem cogitare, Cic.
units.tr: Proscribere aliquem: To drive into exile. To forbid fire and water. To forbid fire, water and roof, Cic. To bring a proscription against someone's life. To will and order that someone be no longer in the state, Id. To be eager to proscribe, to think about proscription, Cic.

units.la: Proscriptio] Proscriptio de capite civis. Proscriptio capitis, Cic. Capitis diminutio maxima, quae deportationi succesßit, IC. Programma, Vlp. Bannitio criminalis, & Bannum, vulgò, Ictis.
units.tr: Proscriptio: proscription of a citizen's life. Loss of civic rights by death sentence, Cic. The greatest loss of status, which followed deportation, IC. Public notice, Vlp. Criminal banishment, and in common usage "bannum", Ictis.

units.la: Proscriptus] Capite diminutus, Liv. Cui aquâ & igni interdictum est, Fest.
units.tr: Proscriptus: Reduced in status, Liv. One to whom fire and water are forbidden, Fest.

units.la: Prospectare] Prospicere ex speculâ, Cic. Provisere, Plaut. Notare & designare oculis aliquid. Explorare fugam. & prospectare exilium, Cic. Conspicio locum insidiis. Vestigare oculis, Virg. Perspeculari de vallo, Hirt. Speculari, Cic. Per rimam arbitrari, Plaut. Aucupare, Acc.
units.tr: Prospectare: To look out from a watch-tower, Cic. To watch ahead, Plaut. To mark and single out something with the eyes. To spy out an escape, and to watch for exile, Cic. To survey a place for ambushes. To track with the eyes, Virg. To spy from the rampart, Hirt. To observe, Cic. To watch through a crack, Plaut. To fowl, Acc.

units.la: Prospectus] Despectus ex oppido in campum, Cæs. Despectatio coenaculi, vitr. Lumen, Cic.
units.tr: Prospectus: A view down from a town onto the plain, Caes. A looking down into the upper room, Vitr. Light, Cic.

units.la: Prosperare aliquem] Prosperare alicui, Plaut. Prosperare victoriam, Liv. Secundare iter, Propert. Fortunare aliquem, vel, aliquid alicui, Cic Beare aliquem, Plaut.
units.tr: Prosperare aliquem: To make someone prosper. To prosper someone, Plaut. To bring victory to success, Liv. To speed a journey, Propert. To bless someone, or something for someone, Cic. To make someone happy, Plaut.

units.la: Prosperitas, vid. Fortuna.
units.tr: Prosperitas, see Fortune.

units.la: Prosper, Prosperè, vid. Fortunatè, &c.
units.tr: Prosper, prospere, see fortunate, etc.

units.la: Prospicere] Despicere; catuli qui jam despecturi sunt, Cic. melius, dispecturi. Dies reluxit caeco, Tac.
units.tr: Prospicere: To look down. Puppies which are about to open their eyes, Cic. (better, about to open them). The day dawned on the blind, Tac.

units.la: Prosternere] Humi sternere, Hor. Stragem edere, Cic. Ad terram dare aliquem, Suet. Proruere violento turbine molem, Lucr. Corruere, Proruere. Id, vid. Caedere.
units.tr: Prosternere: To strew on the ground, Hor. To make a slaughter, Cic. To throw someone to the ground, Suet. To hurl down a mass by a violent whirlwind, Lucr. To fall down, to cast down. For this, see Cut down.

units.la: Prostituere se] Prostituere pudicitiam, Suet. Prostituere se toto corpore, Cat. Corpus quaestuarium habere, Vlp. Pervulgare se omnibus. Amori aliorum flagitiosissimè servire, Cic. Publicare vulgò, Vulgare corpus, Plaut. Corpus in vulgus dare, Gell. Quaestum suo corpore facere, Liv. Indigno quaestu conterere corpus, Plaut. Concubitus pati, Ovid. Succubare, substernere se, Catul.
units.tr: Prostituere se: To prostitute one's chastity, Suet. To offer oneself with one's whole body, Cat. To keep a body for hire, Vlp. To give oneself up to all. To serve the love of others most shamefully, Cic. To make oneself common; to give one's body to the crowd, Plaut. To give the body to the public, Gell. To make a trade of one's body, Liv. To wear out one's body in shameful gain, Plaut. To submit to intercourse, Ovid. To lie under, to throw oneself down, Catul.

units.la: Prostratus, vid. Prolapsus.
units.tr: Prostratus, see Prolapsus.

units.la: Protegere, vid, Defendere.
units.tr: Protegere, see Defend.

units.la: Protelum] Versus in arando. Versura. Col. Striga, Scal. In singulis jugis arare, Plin. Cursus continens, Liv.
units.tr: Protelum: A line of furrows in ploughing. A turning, Col. A furrow, Scal. To plough each yoke, Plin. A continuous course, Liv.

units.la: Proterve vid. Procaciter. Protervia, vid. Procacia.
units.tr: Proterve, see Impudently. Protervia, see Impudence.

units.la: Protervus] Retrectant juventus, Col. Ferox, Cic. Procax, Hor. Praeferocis animi homo, Liv. Procacissimis ingeniis, Tac.
units.tr: Protervus: Youth that refuses to be handled, Col. Fierce, Cic. Bold, Hor. A man of very fierce spirit, Liv. Most headstrong talents, Tac.

units.la: Protestari] Contestari deos & homines, coelum, terram. Testari Deos & homines. Testificor me a te rogatum, Cic.
units.tr: Protestari: To call gods and men, heaven and earth, to witness. To call gods and men to witness. I call it to witness that I was asked by you, Cic.

units.la: Protestatio] Testificatio, Cic. Detestatio, Vlp.
units.tr: Protestatio: Testimony, Cic. Denunciation, Vlp.

units.la: Protocollum] Acta publica: Auctoritas, Cic. vid. Acta.
units.tr: Protocollum: Public records; authority, Cic. See Acts.

units.la: Protrahere negotium, vid. Prolongare, & differre. Protrudere, vid. Trudere.
units.tr: Protrahere negotium, see Prolong, and defer. Protrudere, see Thrust.

units.la: Provenire, vid. Exire, & Nasci.
units.tr: Provenire, see Go out, and Be born.

units.la: Proventus] Census. Vectigal privatum. Merces. Mercedulae. Annona lactis, Cic. Reditus, Plin. Ratio calculorum, Col. Canon frumentarius urbis, Suet. Redactus, Scaev. I.C.
units.tr: Proventus: Income. Private revenue. Wages. Small earnings. The supply of milk, Cic. Returns, Plin. Account of reckonings, Col. The corn-tax of the city, Suet. Yield, Scaev. I.C.

units.la: Proverbium] Vetus verbum est, Ter. Vulgare dictum, Plin. Vetus adagium. Dicta sapienter: docta dicta, Plaut. Vetus adagio. Adagio, ambagio. Paroemia, Tar.
units.tr: Proverbium: It is an old saying, Ter. A common saying, Plin. An old adage. Wise sayings: learned sayings, Plaut. An old adage. Adage, circumlocution. Proverb, Tar.

units.la: Proverbio dicitur] Vetus Adagium est, Plaut. Vetus adagio est Var. In proverbio est. Proverbii loco dici solet. Obtinuit proverbii locum. Venit in consuetudinem proverbii. In communi proverbio versatur. Tritum sermone proverbium. Contritum vetustate proverbium. Veteri proverbio, Cic. Cessit in proverbium, Plin. Increbuit ter proverbio, Liv. Vulgo dicitur, dici solet. Ajunt, Ter.
units.tr: Proverbio dicitur: It is an old adage, Plaut. It is an old adage, Var. It is in the proverb. It is commonly said by way of proverb. It has taken the place of a proverb. It has come into the custom of a proverb. It is in common proverb. A proverb worn smooth by talk. A proverb worn by age. By an old proverb, Cic. It has passed into a proverb, Plin. It has become a proverb three times over, Liv. It is commonly said, it is usually said. They say, Ter.

units.la: Providè] Providenter, Plin. Providentissimè. Considerate Cic. Prospicienter, Gell.
units.tr: Providè: Providently, Plin. Most providently. Considerately, Cic. Foreseeingly, Gell.

units.la: Providens] Providus, Consideratus, Cic. Providentissimus, Plin. Iun. Provisor, Hor. Janus alter. Janus bifrons,
units.tr: Providens: Provident, considerate, Cic. Most provident, Plin. Iun. A provider, Hor. Another Janus. Two-faced Janus.

units.la: Providentia] Circumspectio accurata, Cic. Provisus, us, Tac. Circumspicientia, Gell.
units.tr: Providentia: Careful circumspection, Cic. Foresight, Tac. Circumspection, Gell.

units.la: Providentia melior paenitentia] Providere melius, quam poenitere.
units.tr: Providentia melior paenitentia: It is better to provide than to repent.

units.la: Providere, in futurum consulere] Prospicere in posterum: futuros casus, Cic. Animo providere aliquid, Caes. Praevidere futura. Videre. Præmunire. Prospicere ne quid fiat, Cic. Providere astu aliquid. Considere in longitudinem, Ter.
units.tr: Providere, in futurum consulere: To look forward to the future: future chances, Cic. To foresee something in mind, Caes. To foresee the future. To see. To fortify in advance. To look out that nothing happens, Cic. To provide for something by cunning. To sit down at length, Ter.

units.la: Providere sibi, Prospicere sibi, Ter. Benè, optimè, commodis ac saluti suæ Consulere. Munire se ad reliqua tempora, Cic.
units.tr: Providere sibi, to provide for oneself, Ter. To look well and best to one's own convenience and safety. To fortify oneself for the times ahead, Cic.

units.la: Provifio] Res ad vivendum necessariæ. Victus vestitusque necessarius. Cultus corporis. Victus quotidianus. Subsidia omnia vitæ honestè ducendæ. Apud. Eccles. scriptores. Alias, Dispectus rerum gerendarum, Sen. Provifio mentis, animi, Cic.
units.tr: Provisio: Things necessary for living. Necessary food and clothing. Care of the body. Daily sustenance. All the resources for living honourably. Used by ecclesiastical writers. Elsewhere: foresight in affairs to be done, Sen. Foresight of mind, of spirit, Cic.

units.la: Provisor, vid. Inspector.
units.tr: Provisor, see Inspector.

units.la: Provivere] Pervivere usque ad summam ætatem. Vincere vivendo aliquem, Plaut Pervenire: vitam perducere, ad centesimum annum. Si vita suppeditasset, consul factus esset, Cic. Perducere se ad longam senectutem, Plin. Protollere vitam in crastinum, Plaut. Annos centum conficere, complere, Cic. Edurare quina secula. Cui multi anni transmissi sunt, Sen. Excessit annos 80, Col.
units.tr: Provivere: To live on through to extreme old age. To outlive someone by living, Plaut. To reach: to lead life to the hundredth year. If his life had lasted, he would have been made consul, Cic. To extend oneself into long old age, Plin. To hold life over until tomorrow, Plaut. To complete or fill a hundred years, Cic. To endure five centuries. For whom many years have passed, Sen. He exceeded eighty years, Col.

units.la: Provocare aliquem] Lacessere ad pugnam: Poscere pugnam: in prælium. Vocare in certamen, Virg. Vocare aliquem contrà, Plaut. Evocare ad pugnam magnâ verborum contumeliâ. Excire hostem ad dimicandum, Liv. Procieo, i. e. provoco, Sipont. Procalare. & provocare & procitare.
units.tr: Provocare aliquem: To challenge to fight: to demand battle: to the fight. To call into contest, Virg. To call someone out against, Plaut. To summon to fight with great verbal insult. To rouse the enemy to fight, Liv. I drive forth, that is, I provoke, Sipont. To call out. And to provoke, and to stir up.

units.la: Provocare ultioni promptum] Irritare crabrones. Stimulare leonem.
units.tr: Provocare ultioni promptum: To stir up hornets. To goad a lion.

units.la: Provocare aliquem ad id, quô ille maximè gaudet] Equum in planitiem.
units.tr: Provocare aliquem ad id, quo ille maxime gaudet: To lead a horse onto the plain.

units.la: Prout res ac tempus se dabit] Quod sors feret, feremus æquo animo. Ut res dant sese, ita &c, Ter. Ut cunque aderunt res. Ut sese dederint initia. Fortuitò, Cic. Pro re, Lucr. vid. Iuxta.
units.tr: Prout res ac tempus se dabit: What fate brings, we shall bear with an even mind. As circumstances present themselves, so etc., Ter. As whatever the circumstances are. As the beginnings have given themselves. By chance, Cic. According to the matter, Lucr. See Iuxta.

units.la: Proxeneta, vid. Conciliator.
units.tr: Proxeneta, see Go-between.

units.la: Proximè] Proximum est tibi, Ter. Quàm proximè alter ab altero, Col.
units.tr: Proximè: It is closest to you, Ter. How closely one is next to another, Col.

units.la: Proximus] Propinquissimus, Afcon.
units.tr: Proximus: Most closely related, Ascon.

units.la: Proximus, de homine] Frater, Cic. Alter, Plaut. Eodem luto factus. Ovô prognatus eodem.
units.tr: Proximus, de homine: Brother, Cic. Another, Plaut. Made of the same mud. Born of the same egg.

units.la: Proximus quisque sibi] Omnes sibi melius esse malunt, quàm alteri. Tunica pallio propior. Genu surâ propius. Ordinata charitas incipit à seipsâ. Regula amoris proximi est amor sui ipsius.
units.tr: Proximus quisque sibi: Everyone prefers to be better off himself than others. The tunic is closer than the cloak. The knee is nearer than the calf. Ordered charity begins with oneself. The rule of love of neighbour is love of oneself.

units.la: Prudens] Prudentiâ præditus, Cic. Callidus usu, Ovid. Oculatus à fronte simul & occipitio. Oculatus ad omnia. Per dioptram ventura prospicit. Animô integer. Gerit bina crania, & innumeros oculos.
units.tr: Prudens: Endowed with prudence, Cic. Skilled through experience, Ovid. Sharp-eyed at front and back. Watchful for everything. Looks into the future through a telescope. Whole in mind. Bears two skulls and countless eyes.

units.la: Prudens maturè] Mente senex.
units.tr: Prudens maturè: Old in mind.

units.la: Prudens opinione suâ] Tertius Cato.
units.tr: Prudens opinione suâ: A third Cato.

units.la: Prudens plus metuit] Prudenti diffidentiâ nihil mortalibus utilius. Prudentis est plus metuere, quàm sperare. In audaces non est audacia tuta. Commercium cum vulpe habens dolos cave. Fortiorem te vita. Cautus timet.
units.tr: Prudens plus metuit: Prudent distrust is nothing more useful to mortals. It is the part of a prudent man to fear more than to hope. Boldness is not safe among the bold. Beware of the fox if you have dealings with its tricks. Life is stronger than you. The cautious man fears.

units.la: Prudentem oportet consilium extempore & invenire, & mutare] Gladiator in arena consilium capit.
units.tr: A prudent man ought to both devise and change his plan on the spur of the moment: a gladiator takes counsel in the arena.

units.la: Prudenter] Peritè, scientèt, peritissimè & callidissimè, Cic. Nemo dexteriùs fortunâ usus est, Hor. Rem dexter agit. Liv.
units.tr: Prudenter: Skilfully, knowingly, most skilfully and most cleverly, Cic. No one has used fortune more adroitly, Hor. He handles the matter adroitly, Liv.

units.la: Prudenter ac solerter] Oculis ac manibus.
units.tr: Prudenter ac solerter: With eyes and hands.

units.la: Prudenter vive] Audi, vide, tace, si vis vivere in pace.
units.tr: Prudenter vive: Hear, see, be silent, if you wish to live in peace.

units.la: Prudenter, ne negotium rumpatur] Ne in nervum erumpat.
units.tr: Prudenter, ne negotium rumpatur: Lest it break out into the sinew.

units.la: Prudenter id intelligendum] Cum grano, vel micâ salis accipiendum est.
units.tr: Prudenter id intelligendum: It must be taken with a grain, or pinch, of salt.

units.la: Prudenter inter pericula] Ne cinerem vitans, in prunas incidas. Ancoris duabus niti bonum.
units.tr: Prudenter inter pericula: Lest, avoiding the ash, you fall into the embers. It is good to rest on two anchors.

units.la: Prudentia] Phronesis est rerum expetendarum fugiendarumque scientia. Ars vivendi est prudentia, Cic. Dexteritas, Liv. Choraga familiæ virtutum. Judicii trutina.
units.tr: Prudentia: Phronesis is the knowledge of what is to be sought and what avoided. The art of living is prudence, Cic. Dexterity, Liv. The leader of the family of virtues. The scales of judgement.

units.la: Prudentia serò comparatur] Seris venit usus ab annis.
units.tr: Prudentia serò comparatur: Experience comes late, with the years.

units.la: Prudentia perpetua] Etiam dormiens vigilo serpentis oculus.
units.tr: Prudentia perpetua: Even sleeping I keep watch: the serpent's eye.

units.la: Prudentiâ in actionibus uti bonum] Considerate agere plus est, quam prudenter considerare. Calamitas vertenda est in virtutis occasionem.
units.tr: Prudentiâ in actionibus uti bonum: To act with consideration is more than to consider prudently. A calamity is to be turned into an occasion for virtue.

units.la: Prudentia occasionem sequitur] Naviga secundùm fluvium, & naviga secundùm fortunam.
units.tr: Prudentia occasionem sequitur: Sail with the river, and sail with fortune.

units.la: Prudentia imperitorum] Natare circa terram.
units.tr: Prudentia imperitorum: To swim around the shore.

units.la: Prudentia imprudens, vid. Imprudens prud.
units.tr: Prudentia imprudens, see Imprudent prudence.

units.la: Prudentiæ studere] Salem lingere.
units.tr: Prudentiae studere: To lick salt.

units.la: Pruina] Ros gelatus. Hibernæ arborum frondes. Gelidus humor in montibus canis, Virg.
units.tr: Pruina: Frozen dew. The wintry foliage of trees. Cold moisture on the snowy mountains, Virg.

units.la: Pruna] Prunæ vivaces. Cum vehementer pellucet carbo. Carbo candens, Plin. Vivacissimi carbones, Capitol. Carbo vivus.
units.tr: Pruna] Live embers. Glowing coals, when the charcoal shines brightly. Glowing charcoal, Pliny. Very lively coals, Capitolinus. Live charcoal.

units.la: Prurigo] Pruritus, Plin. Scalpurigo, Solin. Uredo, Plin.
units.tr: Prurigo] Itching, Pliny. Scalpurigo (itch), Solinus. Uredo (a burning rash), Pliny.

units.la: Prurire] Perpruriscere, Plaut. Verminat auris prurigine, Mart.
units.tr: Prurire] To itch thoroughly, Plautus. The ear swarms with itching, Martial.

units.la: Prußia] Borussia, Cromer. Olim. Ulmigeria.
units.tr: Prußia] Borussia, Cromer, Olim. Ulmigeria.

units.la: Prussus] Borussus, Pruthenus, Crom. Iun.
units.tr: Prussus] Borussus, Pruthenus, Cromer, Iunius.

units.la: Puber] Pubes & puber, Fest. Pubentes genæ, Virg. Pubescentia ora, Stat. Vesticeps, Gell.
units.tr: Puber] Pubes and puber, Festus. Cheeks growing downy, Virgil. Faces beginning to show down, Statius. Vesticeps, Gellius.

units.la: Pubescere] Vestiri pilo, Plin. Vestit nihi flore genas prima juventus, Virg. Juventus vestit molli lanugine malas, Lucr. Gallulascere, Non. Vernant lanugine malæ, Mart. Imbarbescere, Fest. Lanugo inserpit genis, Amm. Opacat flore lanugo genas, Paeuv.
units.tr: Pubescere] To be clothed with hair, Pliny. Now youth clothes the cheeks with its flower, Virgil. Youth clothes the cheeks with soft down, Lucretius. To grow a first beard (gallulascere), Nonius. The cheeks grow down, Martial. To become bearded, Festus. Down creeps over the cheeks, Ammianus. Down darkens the cheeks with its bloom, Pacuvius.

units.la: Publicanus, vid. Vectigalarius.
units.tr: Publicanus, see Vectigalarius.

units.la: Publicare, vid. Divulgare, Proclamare.
units.tr: Publicare, see Divulgare, Proclamare.

units.la: Publica anteferenda] Publica privatis potiora.
units.tr: Publica anteferenda] Public matters are to be preferred to private ones.

units.la: Publicè] Publicitus accipi, Plaut. vid. Manifestè.
units.tr: Publicè] To be received publicly, Plautus; see Manifestè.

units.la: Publicus] Recito literas publicas: testimonium publicum, Cic. vid. Communis.
units.tr: Publicus] I read out public letters; a public testimony, Cicero; see Communis.

units.la: Pudefacere aliquem] Inferre alicui verecundiam. Adducere aliquem in verecundiam, Cic. Lædere os alicui, Ter. Verberare oculos, Val. Max. Incutere pudorem, Hor. Confundere adversarium, Sen. Aliquid ruboris habent, Sipont. Faciam ut te pudeat. In rubórem retotum dabo, Plaut. Mutum reddere. Conturbare aliquem, Cic. Rubor ei injectus est, Val. M. vid. Confundere.
units.tr: Pudefacere aliquem] To bring shame upon someone. To bring someone into shame, Cicero. To wound someone's face, Terence. To strike someone's eyes, Valerius Maximus. To put shame into someone, Horace. To confound an opponent, Seneca. They have some redness, Sipontinus. I will make you ashamed. I will drive you to a full blush, Plautus. To make mute. To disconcert someone, Cicero. A blush was cast upon him, Valerius Maximus; see Confundere.

units.la: Pudefactus] Demisso capite. Demissis auribus. Confusus pudore, vultu, Ovid. vid. Erubescere.
units.tr: Pudefactus] With head bowed. With ears drooping. Confused in shame, in face, Ovid; see Erubescere.

units.la: Pudendus] Est pudori, Liv. Erubescendus, Hor. Pudenda inscitia, Plin. Quæ si appelles, honor præfandus est, Cic.
units.tr: Pudendus] Is a disgrace, Livy. To be blushed at, Horace. Shameful ignorance, Pliny. If you address such a person, honour must be prefaced, Cicero.

units.la: Pudet me] Dispudet, Plaut. Pudor est mihi dicere. Est mihi opprobrio, Ovid. Pallori tibi erit, Propert. Suppudet me hujus rei. Pœnitet me ineptiarum. Rubeo, mihi crede; sed jam scripseram, delere nolui. Verecundia me capit, Cic. Verecundia teneor, Liv. Verecundari neminem apud mensam decet, Plaut. Pudet me aliquid, Ter. alicujus, Cic. Pudescit illum impudicitiæ, Min. Fel. Habeo verecundiam alicujus; Liv.
units.tr: Pudet me] I am ashamed, Plautus. It is shameful for me to speak. It is a reproach to me, Ovid. It will make you pale, Propertius. I am a little ashamed of this matter. I repent of my silliness. I blush, believe me; but I had already written and did not want to erase it. Modesty seizes me, Cicero. I am held by modesty, Livy. It is not fitting for anyone to be bashful at table, Plautus. I am ashamed of something, Terence; of someone, Cicero. He is ashamed of his immodesty, Minucius Felix. I have respect for someone's feelings, Livy.

units.la: Pudicè] Digne, haud meretricie incedit, Plaut. Ubi pudicitius continerentur, quàm sub oculis parentum? Plin. Iun. vid. Honestè.
units.tr: Pudicè] Worthily; she does not walk like a harlot, Plautus. Where could they be kept more modestly than under their parents' eyes? Pliny the Younger; see Honestè.

units.la: Pudicitia] Pudor. Verecundia virginalis. Ingenuitas, Cic. Reverentia, Plin. Iun. Rubor, Iuv. Mollis frons, Quint. Mollities frontis, Plin. Iun. Infirmitas frontis, Sen. Teneritudo frontis, Cæs. Frons, Perf. Flos morum. Flos virginei pudoris.
units.tr: Pudicitia] Modesty. Virginal bashfulness. Ingenuousness, Cicero. Reverence, Pliny the Younger. Blushing, Juvenal. A soft brow, Quintilian. Softness of brow, Pliny the Younger. Weakness of brow, Seneca. Tenderness of brow, Caesar. Brow, Persius. Flower of good conduct. Flower of virginal modesty.

units.la: Pudicus] Pudicitior, Apul. Verecundus vultus, Ovid. Verecundus in aliqua re, Cic. Pudibunda matrona, Hor. Pudens animus, Ter. vid. Verecundus.
units.tr: Pudicus] More modest, Apuleius. A modest countenance, Ovid. Modest in some matter, Cicero. A bashful matron, Horace. A shamefaced mind, Terence; see Verecundus.

units.la: Pudor] Postpositò pudore aliquid referre, Ovid. Verecundia turpitudinis, Rubor, Cic. Nulla est reverentia poscendi, Propert. Ago gratias confusioni meæ, quòd, &c. Sen. Erubescentia, Sipont.
units.tr: Pudor] To relate something with shame set aside, Ovid. Bashfulness at baseness; blushing, Cicero. There is no reverence in demanding, Propertius. I give thanks to my confusion that, etc., Seneca. Blushing, Sipontinus.

units.la: Pudor est] Et inceptu turpe est, Ter. Pudor est dicere. Pudor adest nominibus, Ovid. Pārere sibi probrum, Cæcil. Pudorem deposuit, ex Hor. vid. Depudere.
units.tr: Pudor est] It is shameful even to begin it, Terence. It is shameful to speak. Shame attends names, Ovid. To bring disgrace upon oneself, Caecilius. He has laid aside shame, from Horace; see Depudere.

units.la: Puella] Adolescentula, Ter. Juvenis honesta, Apul.
units.tr: Puella] A young girl, Terence. An honourable young woman, Apuleius.

units.la: Puer de infante] Puellus, Lucil. Pupus, Var. Non. Pu-fio, Cic. Pusus, Var. Pupulus, Catul. Pignus. Puercu-lus, Arnob. Puerulus, Cic.
units.tr: Puer de infante] A little boy, Lucilius. Pupus, Varro, Nonius. Pufio, Cicero. Pusus, Varro. Pupulus, Catullus. Pignus. A little boy, Arnobius. A little boy, Cicero.

units.la: Puer grandiusculus] Grandis puer, Fest. Bupæs, Id. Catlaster, Carif. Catulaster, Scal.
units.tr: Puer grandiusculus] A grown boy, Festus. Bupaes, Festus. Catlaster, Carifius. Catulaster, Scaliger.

units.la: Puer non sum amplius] Et nos manum ferulæ subduximus.
units.tr: Puer non sum amplius] And we have withdrawn our hand from the rod.

units.la: Pueri] Liberi, Cic. Qui nondum æte lavantur, Perf.
units.tr: Pueri] Children, Cicero. Those not yet bathed, Persius.

units.la: Puerascere] Repuerascere, Cic. Fio puer, Plaut.
units.tr: Puerascere] To become a boy again, Cicero. I become a boy, Plautus.

units.la: Puerilis] Infantilis, Iustin. Bulla dignissimus.
units.tr: Puerilis] Infantile, Justin. Most worthy of the bulla (the boy's amulet).

units.la: Pueritia] Puerilitas, Var. Infantia, Plin. Prætextati anni, Id. Prætextata ætas, Gell.
units.tr: Pueritia] Childishness, Varro. Infancy, Pliny. The years of the toga praetexta, Pliny. The age of the toga praetexta, Gellius.

units.la: Puerpera] Ter. Infantaria, Mart. Parturies, Plin. Inciens, est. Puella partu laborans, Hor.
units.tr: Puerpera] Terence. Infantaria, Martial. Parturies, Pliny. Inciens, est. A girl labouring in childbirth, Horace.

units.la: Pugil] Gladiator, Cic. Athleta. Pancratiastes, Gell. Pentathlus, Plin. Pyctes, Lampr. Pycta, Plin. Quinquertio, Fest.
units.tr: Pugil] A gladiator, Cicero. An athlete. A pancratiast, Gellius. A pentathlete, Pliny. Pyctes, Lampridius. Pycta, Pliny. Quinquertio, Festus.

units.la: Pugilatus] Pugilatio, Cic. Gladiatura, Tac. Militia imaginaria, Suet Pancratium, Sen. Ars gymnastica, Plaut. Sciamachia, Coel. Rhod. Athletice, Athletica, Plin. Palaestra, Cic. Ars palaestrica, Quint. Exercitium palaestricum, Plaut. Gymnasticum, Id. Gymnas, Stat. Ludi gymnici, Cic. Lucta, Cel. Rhod.
units.tr: Pugilatus] Boxing, Cicero. Gladiatorship, Tacitus. Imaginary warfare, Suetonius. Pancratium, Seneca. The gymnastic art, Plautus. Sciamachia, Coelius Rhodiginus. Athletics, Pliny. The wrestling-ground, Cicero. The art of the wrestling-ground, Quintilian. Wrestling exercise, Plautus. Gymnastics, Id.. Gymnas, Statius. Gymnic games, Cicero. Wrestling, Coelius Rhodiginus.

units.la: Pugillares] Pugillar, Auf. Pugillaria, pl. Catul. Palimpsestus, Cic. Codicilli, Manut. Tabula cerata, Id. Charta deletitia, Muret.
units.tr: Pugillares] Pugillar, Auf. Writing-tablets, Catullus. Palimpsest, Cicero. Codicils, Manutius. A waxed tablet, Id.. Deletable paper, Muretus.

units.la: Pugio] Pugiunculus, Cic. Semispatha, Reg. Sicula, Plaut. Clunaculum, Iun.
units.tr: Pugio] A little dagger, Cicero. Half-sword, Regius. Sicilian (dagger), Plautus. Clunaculum, Juvenal.

units.la: Pugna] Manus: rem ad manus revocare, Cic. Depugnatio, Firmic, vid. Prælium
units.tr: Pugna] Hand to hand: to bring the matter back to hands, Cicero. Depugnatio, Firmicus; see Prælium.

units.la: Pugna navalis] Navale bellum, Cic. prælium, Plin. Naumachia, Suet. Classicum certamen, Paterc.
units.tr: Pugna navalis] A naval war, Cicero. A battle, Pliny. A naumachia, Suetonius. A naval contest, Paterculus.

units.la: Pugnas concitavit] Ad mucronem & manus rem adduxit.
units.tr: Pugnas concitavit] He brought the matter to sword and hand.

units.la: Pugna stulta] Andabatarum certamen.
units.tr: Pugna stulta] The contest of the Andabatae (blindfolded fighters).

units.la: Pugnare] Pugnare pugnam, Gell. Ad manus venire. Manum conferere, conferre, Cic. vid. Præliari.
units.tr: Pugnare] To fight a fight, Gellius. To come to hands. To join hands, Cicero; see Præliari.

units.la: Pugnax] Pugnacissimus, Tac. Pugnator, Gell. Promptus ad pugnam, ad omnem dimicationem. Cic. Promptus manu, Liv. Salust.
units.tr: Pugnax] Most pugnacious, Tacitus. A fighter, Gellius. Ready for battle, for every kind of combat, Cicero. Ready with the hand, Livy, Sallust.

units.la: Pugnus] Digiti in condylos complicati, Mart. Palma compressa, Plaut. Manus in pugnum compressa, Quint. Dentifrangibula, Plaut.
units.tr: Pugnus] Fingers folded into the knuckles, Martial. A pressed palm, Plautus. A hand pressed into a fist, Quintilian. Tooth-breaker, Plautus.

units.la: Pulcher] Pulchellus, Elegans, Perelegans, Putus: putissimæ orationes. Lepóre & venustate affluens. Eximia pulchritudine. Nitidus, Luculentus, Visendus apparatus. Venustus ad adspectum. Aureolus libellus. Sol aureus, Cic. Perpulcher: Scitus puer. Festivum caput, Ter. Speciosus. Lautus amicus. Non inelegans, Cic. Venustulus, Mundulus, Bellatulus, Bellus, Bellulus, Scitulus, Plaut. Purpureus, Poët. Decorus ab aspectu, Col. Liberali facie, forma.
units.tr: Pulcher] Pretty, elegant, very elegant, neat; the most polished speeches. Abounding in charm and grace. Of outstanding beauty. Bright, splendid, an apparatus worth seeing. Pleasing to the eye. A little golden book. Golden sun, Cicero. Very handsome: a clever boy. A festive head, Terence. Comely. A fine friend. Not inelegant, Cicero. Charming, neat, pretty, fine, clever (diminutives), Plautus. Purple, Poet. Graceful in appearance, Columella. Of noble face and form.

units.la: Et pulcher, & prudens] Est puer & formosus, & bene ingeniosus.
units.tr: Et pulcher, & prudens] He is a boy both handsome and very clever.

units.la: Pulchrum est) Laudaret livor quoque.
units.tr: Pulchrum est] Even envy would praise it.

units.la: Pulchra pulchris] Margaritæ conchyliis includendæ.
units.tr: Pulchra pulchris] Pearls are to be set in shells.

units.la: Pulchra grata] Amicum quod pulchrum. Omne pul-chrum conciliat sui amorem & desiderium.
units.tr: Pulchra grata] A friend because he is beautiful. All beauty wins love and longing for itself.

units.la: Pulchrum quid] Flos ævi, ætatis, &c.
units.tr: Pulchrum quid] The flower of youth, of age, etc.

units.la: Pulchra placent aliis & sibi] Fastus inest pulchris, sequi-turque superbia formam. Ovid.
units.tr: Pulchra placent aliis & sibi] Pride dwells in beautiful people, and arrogance follows beauty, Ovid.

units.la: Pulchrum cuique suum] Scruta laudat scrutarius.
units.tr: Pulchrum cuique suum] The junk-dealer praises his own junk.

units.la: In pulchris nævus evidentior] Fumus pulchriorem per-sequitur.
units.tr: In pulchris nævus evidentior] Smoke pursues the more beautiful one.

units.la: Pulchrè] Pulcherrimè, Bellè, Bellissimè, Decorè, Ve-nustè, Cum venustate, Eleganter, Præclarè, Scitè. Cic. Scitulè, Apul. Speciosè, Col. Nitidiusculè, Bellulè, Le-pidè, Basilicè, Plaut. Nitidè. Ornate, Compositè, Perele-ganter, Cic. Eximiè ornatum templum, Hirt.
units.tr: Pulchrè] Most beautifully, finely, very finely, gracefully, charmingly, elegantly, splendidly, skilfully, Cicero. Skilfully, Apuleius. Showily, Columella. Rather neatly, prettily, daintily, Plautus. Neatly. Ornately, elegantly, very elegantly, Cicero. A temple exceptionally adorned, Hirtius.

units.la: Pulchritudo] Venustas, Nitor, Concinnitas, Concin-nitudo in oratione. Species & nitor stellarum. Formositas, Cic. Elegantia, Id. Decor corporis, Sen. Gratia villæ, Plin. Iun. Venus, Quint. Almities, Carif.
units.tr: Pulchritudo] Charm, lustre, neatness, harmony in speech. The appearance and brightness of the stars. Beauty, Cicero. Elegance, Id.. Bodily grace, Seneca. The charm of a villa, Pliny the Younger. Venus, Quintilian. Prettiness, Carifius.

units.la: Pulex] Pulveris pullities.
units.tr: Pulex] The dusky colour of dust.

units.la: Pulla vestis, vid. Lugubris habitus.
units.tr: Pulla vestis, see Lugubris habitus.

units.la: Pullus Subst.] Pullulus, Apul. Quadrupedes cogno-scunt suos infantes, Plin. Recens à partu pullus, Var. Re-cens natus, Plaut. Tener equus, Cic. Vituli equorum, Virg. Novella agna, Ovid Tener fœtus, Quint. Hinnulus lepo-rum, Plin. vid. Pipio.
units.tr: Pullus Subst.] A little chick, Apuleius. Four-footed creatures recognise their young, Pliny. Newly born from the womb, Varro. Newly born, Plautus. A young horse, Cicero. Foals, Virgil. A young lamb, Ovid. A tender offspring, Quintilian. A young hare, Pliny; see Pipio.

units.la: Pulmentum] Puls, Cic. Pulticula, Col. Farratum, Iuv.
units.tr: Pulmentum] Pottage, Cicero. A little pulse, Columella. Spelt, Juvenal.

units.la: Pulmo] Pulmunculus, Solin. Spiramenta animæ, Virg. Spuma sanguinis. Instrumentum vocis & respirationis, Gorr. Cordis flabellum & ventilabrum. Cordis culcitra, Avicen. Haustor aëris.
units.tr: Pulmo] A little lung, Solinus. The breaths of life, Virgil. The froth of blood. An instrument of voice and breathing, Gorraeus. The fan and bellows of the heart. The cushion of the heart, Avicenna. The drawer-in of air.

units.la: Pulpa] Pulpamentum, Ter. Torus, Celf. Spondylus, Plin. Viscum, Apul.
units.tr: Pulpa] Meat for pottage, Terence. A swelling, Celsus. A vertebra, Pliny. Birdlime, Apuleius.

units.la: Pulpa arboris, vid. Alburnum.
units.tr: Pulpa arboris, see Alburnum.

units.la: Pulsare] Pulsare ostium, Increpare fores. Placidè pul-tas, Plaut. Insultare fores calcibus, Ter.
