units.tr: Pulsare] To knock at the door, to rattle the doors. To knock gently, Plautus. To kick at the doors with the heels, Terence.

units.la: Pulsatio] Strepitus, Hor. Pulsus, Cic.
units.tr: Pulsatio] A noise, Horace. A beating, Cicero.

units.la: Pulverulentus] Pulvereum solum, Ovid. Vaporiferum littus, Stat.
units.tr: Pulverulentus] Dusty ground, Ovid. A steaming shore, Statius.

units.la: Pulvis] Arida pulvis, Propert. Aridum lutum, Lud. Viv.
units.tr: Pulvis] Dry dust, Propertius. Dry mud, Ludovicus Vives.

units.la: Pulverem excitare] Col. Movere pulverem, Quint.
units.tr: Pulverem excitare] Columella. To stir up dust, Quintilian.

units.la: Pulvis excitatur] Volvitur pulvis turbidus atra caligine, Virg. In se volutatur incitatus pulvis. Laboravimus pulvere (in itinere,) Sen. Pulverat aliquid, Plaut.
units.tr: Pulvis excitatur] A turbid cloud of dust rolls in black darkness, Virgil. The stirred-up dust whirls about itself. We laboured in the dust (on the journey), Seneca. To cover someone with dust, Plautus.

units.la: Pulvis excitatus] Nebula pulveris, Lucr. Exhalatio terræ, Cic. Halitus terræ, Plin. Evaporatio terrarum, Sen. Nubes commoto, glomerato pulvere, Sil. Arenæ nimbi. Lucr. Vapor solis, Plin.
units.tr: Pulvis excitatus] A cloud of dust, Lucretius. An exhalation of the earth, Cicero. The breath of the earth, Pliny. The evaporation of lands, Seneca. Clouds from dust stirred and gathered, Silius. Sandstorms, Lucretius. The vapour of the sun, Pliny.

units.la: Pulvis tormentarius] Iun. Pulvis nitratus, Id. fulmineus, Lipf. Pyrius pulvis, Recent.
units.tr: Pulvis tormentarius] Iunius. Nitrous powder, Id.. Thunder-powder, Lipsius. Fiery powder, Recentiores.

units.la: Pumex] Saxum fistulosum, Vitr. Lapis bibulus. Virg. Spongia, Pallad. Lapidea spongia.
units.tr: Pumex] A porous stone, Vitruvius. A absorbent stone, Virgil. A sponge, Palladius. A stony sponge.

units.la: Pumicare, vid. Lævigare.
units.tr: Pumicare, see Lævigare.

units.la: Pumilio] Atlas, Iron. vid. Nanus.
units.tr: Pumilio] Atlas, Ironicus; see Nanus.

units.la: Punctio] Punctus nervorum. Punctura cæli, Firm. Punctiuncula articulorum, Sen. Verminatio cerebri, Sen. Compunctio laterum, Plin.
units.tr: Punctio] A pricking of the nerves. A piercing of the sky, Firmicus. A small pricking of the joints, Seneca. A worm-like gnawing of the brain, Seneca. A stabbing of the sides, Pliny.

units.la: Punctum] Punctus mundi, terræ, Plin. Minimum, Lucr. Apex, Quint.
units.tr: Punctum] The point of the world, of the earth, Pliny. The smallest particle, Lucretius. A apex, Quintilian.

units.la: Pungere] Compungere, Stimulare, Fodicare, Cic. Mucrone infestare. Punctim petere. Fodere hasta aliquem, Liv.
units.tr: To prick: to sting, to goad, to pierce, Cic. To attack with a point. To seek to strike with the point. To run someone through with a spear, Liv.

units.la: Puniceus, vid. Purpureus.
units.tr: Puniceus (purplish-red), see Purpureus.

units.la: Punire aliquem] Poenas ab aliquo petere, sumere. Afficere poena aliquem. Sceleris poenas ab aliquo ob delictum expetere. Supplicium de aliquo sumere. Uti in aliquem supplicio. Coërcere aliquem verberibus, suppliciis. Castigare aliquem verberibus. Animadvertere in aliquem. Animadvertere facinus. Plectere aliquem: culpam. Mactare malo aliquem. Multare. Vindicare acerrime maleficia, Cic. Expetere ab aliquo supplicium, Liv. Castigare bubulis exuviis, Plaut. Animadvertere ab aliquo injuriam. Edere exempla in aliquem, Ter. Exempla in te faciam, Plaut. Advertere in aliquem, Tac. Multari aliquem poena, Suet. Exigere ab aliquo supplicium, Plin. piacula, Liv. Dicere jus gladio ignaviae suae, Petron. vid. Castigare.
units.tr: To punish someone: to exact penalties from someone, to take punishment from someone. To inflict a penalty on someone. To demand penalties from someone for a wrong committed. To take vengeance on someone. To use torture against someone. To restrain someone with blows or torments. To chastise someone with blows. To take notice of someone, to take action against someone. To take notice of a crime. To punish someone for a fault. To put someone to death with a penalty. To fine someone. To avenge wrongdoings most severely, Cic. To demand punishment from someone, Liv. To chastise with ox-hide whips, Plaut. To take notice of an injury from someone. To make an example of someone, Ter. I will make an example of you, Plaut. To turn one's attention against someone, Tac. To punish someone with a penalty, Suet. To exact punishment from someone, Plin. expiations, Liv. To pronounce judgment by the sword of one's own cowardice, Petron. see Castigare.

units.la: Punitio, vid. Poena.
units.tr: Punishment, see Poena.

units.la: Punitor] Animadversor vitiorum. Vindex scelerum. Ipse se puniens, Cic. Castigator, Plaut. Censor minorum senex. Correctox, Hor. Correptor, Sen.
units.tr: Punisher: one who takes notice of faults. An avenger of crimes. One who punishes himself, Cic. A chastiser, Plaut. An old man who censures the young. A corrector, Hor. A reprover, Sen.

units.la: Pupilla] Pupula, Lucr.
units.tr: Pupil (of the eye): a little pupil, Lucr.

units.la: Pupillus] Qui tutorem habet, Scaev. Pupillus & pupilla in Tutoris potestate est, Cic.
units.tr: Orphan ward: one who has a guardian, Scaev. A ward, male or female, is under the power of the guardian, Cic.

units.la: Purgare] Perpurgare. Expurgare. Tergere vasa, Cic. Depurgare locum, Munditias facere, Cat. Emundare. Extricare agrum, Col. Repurgare. Emaculare, mundare, Plin. Putare, Fest.
units.tr: To cleanse: to purge thoroughly, to cleanse out. To wipe out vessels, Cic. To clean a place, to make it tidy, Cato. To free from dirt. To clear a field, Col. To cleanse again. To remove faults, to make clean, Plin. To prune, Fest.

units.la: Purgare rem supra modum inquinatam] Augiae stabulum repurgare.
units.tr: To cleanse a thing defiled beyond measure: to clean out the stable of Augeas.

units.la: Purgatio] Purificatio, Plin.
units.tr: Purification: a cleansing, Plin.

units.la: Purgatio, in jure idest, excusatio] Purgatio est cum factum conceditur, culpa removetur. Dissolutio criminis. Satisfactio: nec satisfactionem meam accipis, Cic. Habere expurgationem, Lamb.
units.tr: Purgation, in law, that is, excuse: a purgation is when the deed is granted and the fault removed. The dissolving of a charge. Satisfaction: "you do not accept my satisfaction," Cic. To have a clearing, Lamb.

units.la: Purgatio, de medicina] Ductio alvi, Cels. Detractio alvi, Plin. Clysmus, Scribon. Alvus: alvus corpus ac vires carpit, operique inutilem reddit, Col.
units.tr: Purgation, in medicine: a drawing off of the bowels, Cels. A purging of the bowels, Plin. A clyster, Scribon. The bowel: the bowel wastes the body and its strength and renders it unfit for work, Col.

units.la: Purgationem adhibere] Purgari per alvum. Perluit se Ibis. Ciere, inanire alvum, Plin. Perpurgant se cervae herbula, Cic. Alvum clysmo trahere, Scrib. Ducere, subducere, movere alvum, Cels.
units.tr: To apply a purge: to purge through the bowels. The ibis washes itself out. To bring on or empty the bowels, Plin. Deer purge themselves with a herb, Cic. To draw the bowels by a clyster, Scrib. To lead, lower, or move the bowels, Cels.

units.la: Puritas] puritia, Andr. Schot. Varronem sic legit apud Non. Munditia, Cic.
units.tr: Purity: purity, Andr. Schot. Schottus reads Varro thus in Nonius. Cleanliness, Cic.

units.la: Purpura] Vestitus purpureus, Cic. Vestis ostro perfusa; purpurea, Virg. Ostrina tunica, Propert. Murice tincta vestis, Hor. Conchyliata, Plin. Quisquiliata vestis, a quisquilio, Hermol. Iun.
units.tr: Purple: a purple garment, Cic. A garment soaked in purple dye; purple, Virg. A purple tunic, Propert. A garment dyed with murex, Hor. Dyed with shellfish, Plin. A garment of rags, from quisquilium, Hermol. Iun.

units.la: Purpura simiae non convenit] Haud decet simiam purpura. Dedecet simiam purpura. Indecora est simiae purpura. Haud quaquam decora est simiae purpura, Eras.
units.tr: Purple does not suit an ape: purple is not becoming to an ape. Purple disgraces an ape. Purple is unseemly on an ape. Purple is by no means fitting on an ape, Eras.

units.la: Purpura, pro colore ipso] Murex, Hor. Conchylium, Plin. Purpurae sanguis, succus, flos, fucus, ros, sanies, Id. Vitr. Vitr. Ostrum, Virg. Succus buccini, Pelagium, Tyrius succus, Plin.
units.tr: Purple, for the colour itself: murex, Hor. Shellfish dye, Plin. The blood, juice, bloom, dye, dew, or gore of purple, Id. Vitr. Vitr. Purple dye, Virg. The juice of the whelk, the Pelagian dye, the Tyrian juice, Plin.

units.la: Purpuratus] Purpureus tyrannus, Hor. Prætextatus, Cic. Coccinatus, Mart. Prætextis purpurâ togis uti, Liv.
units.tr: Clad in purple: a purple tyrant, Hor. Wearing the purple-bordered toga, Cic. Scarlet-clad, Mart. To wear togas bordered with purple, Liv.

units.la: Purpureus] Purpurarius, Plin. Puniceus, Phœniceus, Tyrius, Virg. Punicus, Hor. Conchyliatus, Cic. Coccinus, Coccineus. Cocceus, Lampr. Cocco nexus, Suet. Sarranus, Col. Blattæus, Vopisc. Ostrinus Propert. Spadix, Spadiceus, Bajus, Cerd. Russulæ fasciolæ, Capit. Roseus, Virg.
units.tr: Purple-red: dealing in purple, Plin. Purplish-red, Phoenician-red, Tyrian, Virg. Punic-red, Hor. Dyed with shellfish, Cic. Scarlet, crimson. Coccine-red, Lampr. Bound with scarlet, Suet. Sarran-red, Col. Dyed with blatta, Vopisc. Purple, Propert. Chestnut-brown, chestnut, bay, Cerd. Little red bands, Capit. Rose-coloured, Virg.

units.la: Purus] Putus, Fest. Cera pura puta. Mundus & elegans. Lautus, Cic. Permundus, Var. Sincerum vas, Hor. Eliquatus. Fonte purior, clavo. Nive candidior, Eras.
units.tr: Pure: clean, Fest. Pure wax, clean. Clean and elegant. Refined, Cic. Very clean, Var. An unmixed vessel, Hor. Strained. Purer than a spring, than a nail. Whiter than snow, Eras.

units.la: Purus putus] Sincera voluptas, Ovid. Purum argentum, Cic. Putatum argentum, Fest. Merum vinum, Plaut. Meraculum vinum, Plin. Meracus, Perf. Liquidum mel, Virg. Liquida voluptas, Cic. Defæcatus sanguis, Macr. Persolæ nugæ. Germanæ gerræ, Plaut. Argentum pusulatum, vel pultulatum, Suet.
units.tr: Pure, unmixed: unmixed pleasure, Ovid. Pure silver, Cic. Silver that has been refined, Fest. Unmixed wine, Plaut. Wine of the purest quality, Plin. Pure wine, Perf. Liquid honey, Virg. Liquid pleasure, Cic. Blood that has been clarified, Macr. Idle trifles, real nonsense, Plaut. Silver with bubbles, or with small balls, Suet.

units.la: Pus] Suppurata, pl. Plin. Tabo, Donat.
units.tr: Pus: festering matter, in the plural, Plin. Pus, Donat.

units.la: Pusillanimis] Abjecto, demisso, humili, pusillo, fracto, angusto, muliebri animo Cic. Corde gelato, Lucan.
units.tr: Faint-hearted: of a cast-down, humble, weak, broken, narrow, womanish spirit, Cic. With a frozen heart, Lucan.

units.la: Miles pusillanimis in periculis] Lepus galeatus. Asinus in pelle leonis. Initio confidens, in facto timidus.
units.tr: A soldier faint-hearted in dangers: a hare in a helmet. An ass in a lion's skin. Bold at the start, timid in the deed.

units.la: Pusillanimitas] Abjectus, animus pusillus, &c. Egestas animi. Angustiæ pectoris, Cic.
units.tr: Faint-heartedness: a cast-down, feeble spirit, etc. Poverty of spirit. Narrowness of heart, Cic.

units.la: Pusillum, vid. Parum.
units.tr: Little, see Parum.

units.la: Putamen Ovi] Calix, cortex, testa ovi, Plin.
units.tr: Shell of an egg: the cup, the rind, the shell of an egg, Plin.

units.la: Putamen nucis &c.] Culeola, vel. Culiola, f. culliola, Fest. Calyx. Operimentum juglandis. Vitium, crusta, cutis, corium, Plin. Fructus munitur vitio, Putamine clauduntur nuces, Crusta glandes, Cute uvæ. Pericarpium, Rhodig. vid. Siliqua.
units.tr: Shell of a nut, etc.: a husk, or a little husk, perhaps culliola, Fest. A calyx. A covering of the walnut. Skin, crust, hide, bark, Plin. The fruit is protected by a skin; nuts are enclosed in a shell, acorns in a crust, grapes in a peel. Pericarp, Rhodig. see Siliqua.

units.la: Putare arborem &c.] Deputare vineam, Cato. Amputare, Opputare ramos. Plin. Perputare. Attondere ulmos, Plaut. Liberare palmites nepotibus. Orbandus pampinus nepotibus. Truncam reddere arborem. Truncare vitem. Surculare. Dedolare. Detundere virgulta. Enodare falce virgas. Delumbare radices. Decacuminare pampinum, Col. Pampinare re vineam, vel vites. Circumcîdere extrema vitium, Varr. Castrare vites,stringere frondes. Fronde leuare nemus. Tondere arborum brachia, Virg.
units.tr: To prune a tree, etc.: to trim a vineyard, Cato. To cut off, to cut back the branches, Plin. To prune thoroughly. To shear elms, Plaut. To free the vine-shoots for the young growth. The vine-shoot deprived of its young growth. To make a tree a stump. To lop a vine. To cut into shoots. To dress with an adze. To strip off twigs. To cut away the shoots with a sickle. To cut away the roots at the loins. To top the tendril, Col. To prune the vineyard or the vines of their tendrils. To cut away the extremities of the vines, Varr. To geld the vines, to strip the leaves. To strip the grove of its leaves. To shear the arms of trees, Virg.

units.la: Putare 2. vid. Opinari.
units.tr: To think (2), see Opinari.

units.la: Putatio ] Amputatio sarmentorum, Cic. Detruncatio ramorum, Plin. Frondatio, Pampinatio, Obtruncatio vitis, Col. Castratio, Tonsura arborum. Recisio plantarum, Plin. Ablaqueatio, Col.
units.tr: Pruning: the cutting off of vine-shoots, Cic. The lopping of branches, Plin. Stripping of leaves, of tendrils, cutting back of the vine, Col. Castration, shearing of trees. The cutting of plants, Plin. Digging around the roots, Col.

units.la: Putator vid. Arborator.
units.tr: Pruner, see Arborator.

units.la: Putealis] Aqua puteana, Plin.
units.tr: Of a well: well water, Plin.

units.la: Putere] Putescere, Cato. Rancore inficiuntur vasa, Pal-lad. Fracescit oleum, si congelatur, Col. Rancere, ex Lucr.
units.tr: To rot: to become putrid, Cato. Vessels are spoiled by rancidity, Pallad. Oil turns rancid if it freezes, Col. To be rancid, from Lucr.

units.la: Putidus] Caro putida, Cic. Putidulus, Mart. Rancidus aper, Hor. Rancidula obsonia, Iuv. Foetulentus, Apul. vid. Foetidus.
units.tr: Stinking: stinking flesh, Cic. Somewhat stinking, Mart. A rancid boar, Hor. Rancid dishes, Juv. Fetid, Apul. see Foetidus.

units.la: Putens] Subterraneorum humorum cribrum.
units.tr: Stinking (of the earth): a sieve for underground moisture.

units.la: Putor] Rancor, Pallad. Putror terrae, Lucr.
units.tr: Stench: rancidity, Pallad. The rot of the earth, Lucr.

units.la: Putrescere] Putrere, Acc. Non. Imputrescere, Col. Flaccere, Var. Marcescere, Mart.
units.tr: To putrefy: to rot, Acc. Non. To rot without decay, Col. To wither, Var. To waste away, Mart.

units.la: Putredo] Putror, Lucr. Putrilago, Non.
units.tr: Putrefaction: rot, Lucr. Putrid liquid, Non.

units.la: Putris] Putre corpus, Lucr. Putridus dens, Cic. Putre-factus, Ovid. Rancidum cadaver, Lucr. Puter palus, Var. Saper caseus, Plin. Putida navis, Non.
units.tr: Rotten: a rotten body, Lucr. A decayed tooth, Cic. Putrefied, Ovid. A rancid corpse, Lucr. A rotten swamp, Var. Sour cheese, Plin. A stinking ship, Non.

units.la: Pyxis] Pyxidicula, vel, Pyxidula, Celf.
units.tr: Pyxis (box): a little box, or a small box, Celf.

units.la: Q.
units.tr: Q.

units.la: Quâ viâ] Quâ, Cic.
units.tr: By what way] Whereby, Cic.

units.la: Quâ, quâ, vid. Et &, item, Tam-quàm.
units.tr: Whereby, whereby, see And &, likewise As ... as.

units.la: Quâcunque] Qualibet transitum praebet, Quint. Quâquam meare, Lucr. Aliquâ evolare, Cic.
units.tr: Whichever way] Offers passage by any route, Quint. To move through by whatever means, Lucr. To fly out by some way, Cic.

units.la: Quâdantenus] Aliquâ ex parte, Cic. Aliquâ nocere, Virg. sc. parte. Aliquâtenus, utcunque, Plin.
units.tr: To some extent] In some part, Cic. To harm in some measure, Virg., i.e. in some part. In some measure, however it may be, Plin.

units.la: Quadra] Orbis, Iun. Orbiculus, Plin. Cereale solum, Virg. Circulus, Mart.
units.tr: Square] A circle, Iun. A little circle, Plin. Land for grain, Virg. A circle, Mart.

units.la: Quadrageni] Quaterdeni, Ovid.
units.tr: Forty each] Four tens each, Ovid.

units.la: Quadrangulus] Quadratus, Cic. Perquadratus, Vitr. Quadratis angulis, Plin. Conquadratus, Col. Cubicus, Vitr. Quadrarius, Cato.
units.tr: Quadrangular] Squared, Cic. Thoroughly squared, Vitr. With square corners, Plin. Squared together, Col. Cubical, Vitr. Quadrarius, Cato.

units.la: Quadrans] Quarta pars jugeri, Col. Tetrans: dividere aliquid tetrantibus, Vitr.
units.tr: Quarter] A quarter of a jugerum, Col. Tetrans: to divide something into quarters, Vitr.

units.la: Quadrat] Valet hoc in te. In omnes partes valet. Convenit ad pedem cothurnus. Habilis est ad pedem calceus, Cic. Convenit in aliquem, Id.
units.tr: It suits] This suits you. It suits in every respect. The buskin fits the foot. The shoe is suitable for the foot, Cic. It agrees with someone, Id.

units.la: Quadripartiri] Corpus in membra dividere, Sen. Carnificare jacentem, Liv.
units.tr: To divide into four parts] To cut the body into limbs, Sen. To butcher a man lying on the ground, Liv.

units.la: Quadripartitio] Quadratura coeli, Fab. Vit. Quadripartita distributio, distinctio, Cic.
units.tr: Division into four parts] The squaring of the heavens, Fab. Vit. A fourfold division or distinction, Cic.

units.la: Quadrupes] Quadripes, Iul. Obseq. Quadrupedans, Virg. Plaut. Quadrupedus, Amm.
units.tr: Quadruped] Quadripes, Iul. Obseq. Quadrupedant, Virg. Plaut. Quadrupedus, Amm.

units.la: Quadruplex] Quadripertitus, & Quadripartitus, Cic. Quadrimus. Quadriplicatus, Var. Quaternus, Virg.
units.tr: Fourfold] Divided into four parts, and quadripartite, Cic. Four years old. Multiplied fourfold, Var. Fourfold, Virg.

units.la: Quærere] Quæritare aliquem, Ter. Requirere, Conquirere, Inquirere, Perquirere, Vestigare investigatione, Pervestigare, Rimari, Cic. Vestigiis omnibus inquirere.
units.tr: To seek] To question someone, Ter. To look for, to search out, to inquire into, to track down by investigation, to search thoroughly, to ferret out, Cic. To inquire into every trace.

units.la: Quæritur] Quæritur de facto. Ambigitur inter homines. Sit nec ne magna quæstio est, De hoc omnis quæstio est. In disceptationem quæstionemque aliquid vocatur. Versatur in quæstione. Habet res ea aliquid quæstionis. In magnâ quæstione habent aliquid augures, Cic. Immensæ quæstionis est, in quo, &c. In quæstione est, quis, &c. Plin. Quæstionis est utrum, Vlp.
units.tr: It is asked] It is asked about the fact. It is disputed among men. Whether it is so or not is a great question. All the question turns on this. Something is brought forward for debate and question. The matter is in question. That thing has some question in it. Augurs have some doubt about a great question, Cic. It is a question of immense scope, in which, etc. The question is who, etc., Plin. The question is whether, Ulp.

units.la: Quæsitio] Quæsitus. Inquisitio & investigatio veri, Plin. Ne quæstioni mihi sit, jube, &c. Plaut. Conquisitio alicujus, Cic.
units.tr: Inquiry] A seeking out. Inquiry and investigation of the truth, Plin. Do not make me an inquiry; order it, etc., Plaut. The searching out of someone, Cic.

units.la: Quæsitor, vid. Indagator, Scisciator.
units.tr: Examiner, see Investigator, Scisciator.

units.la: Quæstio] Rogatio, Cic. Quærítum. Ovid. v. Interrogatio.
units.tr: Question] A request, Cic. A question put, Ovid. See Interrogatio.

units.la: Quæstio abstrusa, solutu difficilis] Archimedeum Problema.
units.tr: Abstruse question, hard to solve] The Archimedean problem.

units.la: Quæstio infinita, vid. Infinitæ rei, &c.
units.tr: Infinite question, see Of an infinite thing, etc.

units.la: Quæstor] Exquæstor, I. C. Quæstorius vir. Quæstor ærarius, Tac. Custos pecuniæ, & ærarii præfectus. Ærarii rex, scriba, Cic. Rationarius. Rationum præfectus, Amm. A rationibus, Suet. Actor summarum, Id. Procurator fisci, Capit. Dispensator, Suet. Proquæstor, Cic. Erogator, Stevech.
units.tr: Quaestor] Former quaestor, jurist. A man of quaestorian rank. Quaestor of the treasury, Tac. Keeper of money and prefect of the treasury. Treasury king, scribe, Cic. Accountant. Prefect of accounts, Amm. From the accounts, Suet. Collector of sums, Id. Procurator of the exchequer, Capit. Dispenser, Suet. Deputy quaestor, Cic. Paymaster, Stevech.

units.la: Quæstuosus, vid. Lucrosus. Quæstum facere, vid. Lucro inhiare.
units.tr: Profitable, see Lucrosus. To make a profit, see Lucro inhiare.

units.la: Quaestura] Quaestorium officium, Cic. Aurarium, vel argentarium negotium, ex Plaut.
units.tr: Quaestorship] The office of quaestor, Cic. Treasury or silver-dealing business, vel banking, ex Plaut.

units.la: Quaestus] Vocem in quaestum contulit, Cic. Aviditas lucri, ex Gir.
units.tr: Gain] He turned his voice to gain, Cic. Greed for profit, ex Gir.

units.la: Qualis ?] Cujusmodi? Plaut. Qui erit rumor ille populi? Ter. Qual est, qui donum dedit? proqualis, Plaut.
units.tr: What sort?] Of what kind? Plaut. What rumour will that be among the people? Ter. What is he who gave the gift? Plaut.

units.la: Qualis, sine interrog.] Qui vir sit, nescis, Cic. Nostis ut est pater meus, Plaut. Quod genus pastores, Var. Cujus notae, Col. Cujus generis, Cic. vid. Quid.
units.tr: Of what sort, without interrogative] You do not know what sort of man he is, Cic. You know what my father is like, Plaut. What kind of shepherds, Var. Of what mark, Col. Of what kind, Cic. See Quid.

units.la: Qualis causa, talis effectus] A puro fonte, pura defluit aqua. Consilia inania inanium. Malorum doctorum malae sunt disciplinae. Mentis bonae bona opera. Parvulus facit ut parvulus. Qualis vir, talis oratio.
units.tr: As the cause, so the effect] Pure water flows from a pure spring. Empty plans come from empty minds. Bad teachers make bad discipline. Good minds produce good works. A little child acts like a little child. As the man, so his speech.

units.la: Qualis interrogatio, talis responsio] Quale dixeris verbum, tale audies. Ut salutabis, ita resalutaberis.
units.tr: As the question, so the answer] As the word you speak, so you will hear. As you greet, so you will be greeted in return.

units.la: Quales qui praesunt, tales subditi] Qualis rex, talis grex. Qualis Hera, talis catella, vel tales pedisequae. Qualis erat mater, filia talis erat. Regis ad exemplum totus componitur orbis. Mobile mutatur semper cum Principe vulgus.
units.tr: As the rulers, so the subjects] As the king, so the flock. As the mistress, so the lapdog, or such maidservants. As the mother was, so the daughter was. The whole world is shaped after the example of the king. The fickle crowd always changes with the prince.

units.la: Qualis actio, tale instrumentum] Duro nodo durus quaerendus est cuneus.
units.tr: As the action, so the tool] A hard wedge must be sought for a hard knot.

units.la: Qualiscunque] Qualislibet, Cujusmodicunque, Quicunque, Qualiscunque, Cuimodi, Cujusque modi, Cic. Cujuscunque modi, Salust. Cujuscunque notae, Col. Qualisqualis, Triphon. I. C. Ut ut homo est, Plaut.
units.tr: Of whatever sort] Of any sort, of whatever kind, whoever, whatever sort, of such kind, Cic. Of whatever kind, Salust. Of whatever mark, Col. Of whatever sort, Triphon, jurist. However the man may be, Plaut.

units.la: Qualitas, vid. Proprietas. & Quidam. Qualiter, Qualitercunque, vid. Quomodo, &c.
units.tr: Quality, see Property. And Quidam. Qualiter, Qualitercunque, see Quomodo, etc.

units.la: Qualus] Qualum, Cato. Colum, Virg. Fiscus met, vel vimineus, Col. Saccus lineus, Plin. Sportula faecaria, Col. vid. Canistrum.
units.tr: Basket] Qualum, Cato. Colum, Virg. A wicker basket, or basket of osiers, Col. A linen sack, Plin. A dung basket, Col. See Canistrum.

units.la: Quam] Altior quam. Secus quam volunt, Suet. Non plus triennium (i. quam trienn.) Var. Ne minus singulos homines, Catul. Atque aliquanto secus, atque, Cic. Praequam, Praeut. Sed hoc pulchrum est, praequam ubi sumptus petunt, Lambin.
units.tr: Than] Higher than. Otherwise than they wish, Suet. Not more than three years (i.e. than three years), Var. Not fewer than individual men, Catul. And somewhat otherwise than, Cic. Praequam, Praeut. But this is fine, rather than where they demand expenses, Lambin.

units.la: Quam dudum ?] Quam dudum venit! Ter. Quam pridem hoc retulisti? Cic.
units.tr: How long ago?] How long ago he came! Ter. How long ago did you report this? Cic.

units.la: Quam diu] Quamdiu vixit. Quem ad finem te jactabit, Cic. Quoad vixit, Suet. Usque dum regnum obtinebit Jupiter, Plaut. Dum ætas tulit, Ter. Donec eris felix, Ovid. Usquequo, Var. Usque adeo dum. Usque ut, Ter. Tandiu quoad. Eatenus quoad, Cic. Quatenus, Fest. Quid modi. Qui modus flendi, Acc. Quo te spectamus usque, Mart.
units.tr: How long] As long as he lived. Up to what end will he toss you about, Cic. As long as he lived, Suet. As long as Jupiter holds the kingdom, Plaut. As long as age allowed, Ter. As long as you are happy, Ovid. How long, Var. Until, up to the point that, Ter. So long as, Cic. Insofar as, Fest. What manner of weeping, Acc. How far we look at you, Mart.

units.la: Quam plures, vid. Plerique.
units.tr: How many more, see Most.

units.la: Quamvis] Quamquam, Etsi, Etiamsi, Licet, Tametsi, Cic. Ter. Tametli, tamen, Caes. Quantumvis, Hor. Quamlibet, Lucr. Tamen, pro quamvis. Plaut. Bene inter vos dicatis, & mihi absenti tamen.
units.tr: Although] Although, even if, even though, granted that, Cic. Ter. Although, nevertheless, Caes. However great, Hor. However much, Lucr. Nevertheless, used for although, Plaut. Speak well among yourselves, and yet to me absent.

units.la: Quando?] Ecquando? Cic. Quando gentium? Plaut. Enunquam, Fest.
units.tr: When?] Ever when? Cic. When in the world? Plaut. Never, ever, Fest.

units.la: Quando] Cum. Dum, Cic. Ut, Ter. Unquam, Quint. Ubi, Virg.
units.tr: When] With; while, Cic. As, Ter. Ever, Quint. Where, Virg.

units.la: Quandocunque] Utcunque dulci fistula valles personure, Hor. Lambin.
units.tr: Whenever] However the valleys may resound with a sweet pipe, Hor. Lambin.

units.la: Quandoque, vid. Aliquando.
units.tr: Sometimes, see Aliquando.

units.la: Quandoquidem, vid. Siquidem.
units.tr: Since, see Siquidem.

units.la: Quanti?] Quanti libertas æstimanda est? Cic.
units.tr: At what price?] At what price should liberty be valued? Cic.

units.la: Quantivis] Quanticunque, Sen. Quanti-quanti, bene emitur, quod necesse est. Quoquo pretio coemptus sit, Cic.
units.tr: At whatever price] Whatever its worth, Sen. Whatever the price, what is necessary is well bought. Bought at whatever price it cost, Cic.

units.la: Quantivis pretii] Quantivis pretii homo, Ter. Non est id parvi, Lucr. Non nihilo æstimandum. Longissime est ab imperitorum intelligentia sensuque distinctum, Cic.
units.tr: Of whatever worth] A man of whatever worth, Ter. That is no small matter, Lucr. Not to be valued at nothing. It is set far apart from the understanding and perception of the unlearned, Cic.

units.la: Quantillum] Quantulum id est! Cic.
units.tr: How tiny] How small that is! Cic.

units.la: Quanto] Quo minus, hoc, Cic. Quam plurimam braf-sicam ederit, tam citissimum sanus fiet, Cat. Col. Quam magis, tanto, ita. Quanto magis, plus, tam magis, Lucret. m, quanto tam, Salust.
units.tr: How much] The less, this; Cic. As much as he eats of the cabbage, so soon will he be made healthy, Cat. Col. The more, the more; so; Lucret. The more, so much the more; Salust.

units.la: Quantopere] Videte quam confidat, Cic.
units.tr: How greatly] See how much he trusts, Cic.

units.la: Quantum] Quantum potui. Quoad possum. Quoad ejus facere poteris. Quatenus amicitiæ tribuendum sit. Quam velit, sit potens. Quantulum. Quantum in uno homine fuit. Ut mea memoria est. Quantum in nobis situm est. Quod auri ornamentorum militum fuit, Cic. Quoad ejus fieri potest, ad Her. Mea quidem causa liber esto, Plaut. In quantum potest, Quint. Ut scire possis, ad quo te expediat loqui, Afran. Ut ratio redditur, Plaut.
units.tr: As much as] As much as I could. As far as I can. As far as you are able. How far friendship should be given. Let him be as powerful as he wishes. As much as there was in one man. As far as I remember. As far as lies in us. Whatever gold ornaments the soldiers had, Cic. As far as can be done, ad Her. For my part let him be free, Plaut. As far as he can, Quint. So that you may know how it suits you to speak, Afran. As the account is rendered, Plaut.

units.la: Quantum? vid. Quot.
units.tr: How much? See Quot.

units.la: Quantumcunque] In quantumcunque creverunt, Sen. Quantulumcunque videbitur, Cic.
units.tr: However much] However much they grew, Sen. However little it may seem, Cic.

units.la: Quantus?] Quantillus? Plaut. Et sine interrog.
units.tr: How great?] How tiny? Plaut. And without interrogative.

units.la: Quantuscunque] Quantuslibet, Plin. Quantuvis, Lucr. Quantus-quantus, Ter. Quantuluscunque, Cic.
units.tr: However great] However great, Plin. However great, Lucr. However great, Ter. However small, Cic.

units.la: Quâqua versus] Quoquoversus. Quoquoversum, Caes. Qualibet aedes perambula, Plaut.
units.tr: Wherever] Wherever, in every direction. Wherever, Caes. Walk through any house you like, Plaut.

units.la: Quare] Cur? Quamobrem? Quapropter? Quid est cur? Quid causae? Quid causae est cur? Quî? ut quid? Cic. Quidita? Quidum? Ter. Quid ergo? Quid tibi est. Quianam arbitrare? resp. quia, &c. Quâ causâ, Plaut. Quâ de causâ, Cic. Quas ob res, Lucr. Nihil est quod pocula laudes, i. cur, Virg. Quî sic. Er.
units.tr: Why] Why? For what reason? Why then? What is the reason why? What is the cause? Is there any cause why? Why? For what? Cic. What then? What is the matter with you? Why do you think so? Answer: because, etc. For what cause, Plaut. For which cause, Cic. For which reasons, Lucr. There is nothing for which you praise the cups, i.e. why, Virg. Why so? Er.

units.la: Omne quare habet suum quia] Nunquam sceleri defuit ratio.
units.tr: Every "why" has its "because": Crime has never lacked a reason.

units.la: Quartana febris, vid. Febris quart.
units.tr: Quartan fever, see Febris quart.

units.la: Quasi] Velut. Perinde quasi. Æquè atque, Cic. Pariter atque, Liv. Quàm si. Quasi si, Plaut. Ceu, Ceu verò, Plin. Ut si, Æmil. Prob.
units.tr: As if] Just as. Just as if. Equally as, Cic. Equally as, Liv. As if. As if, Plaut. As, as though, Plin. As if, Aemil. Prob.

units.la: Quasi verò] Scilicet, Virg. Videlicet. Nihil vidi magis, Iron. Cic. Audio, (id non audio,) Donat. Si Diis placet.
units.tr: As if indeed] Surely, Virg. Evidently. I have seen nothing more, Iron. Cic. I hear (I do not hear it), Donat. If it pleases the gods.

units.la: Quassatio] Agitatio. Succussus. Terrae motus, vel terraemotus. Coagitatio pulmorum, Cic. Pulsus terrae, Amm. Vexamen mundi, Lucr. Concussus, Plin. Quassus, Pacuv. Propulsus, Sen.
units.tr: Shaking] Agitation. A shaking. An earthquake. A trembling of the lungs, Cic. A pulse of the earth, Amm. The buffeting of the world, Lucr. A jolt, Plin. Shaken, Pacuv. Driven forth, Sen.

units.la: Quatenus] Quantum attinet ad, Varr. Non qua filius, sed qua homo æstimatur, Paul. I. C. In quantum in se est, Lucr.
units.tr: Insofar as] As far as concerns, Varr. Not as son but as man is he valued, Paul. jurist. Insofar as he is in himself, Lucr.

units.la: Quatere] Concutere, Lucr. Conquassare, Cic. Motum tremulum facio exsistere, Lucr. Quassare caput, Plaut.
units.tr: To shake] To strike, Lucr. To shatter, Cic. I bring about a trembling motion, Lucr. To shake the head, Plaut.

units.la: Quaternarius numerus, &c.] Quadrigeminus, Plin. Quadrinae copulae verborum, Var. Quadriga, & quadrigae, Var. Quaternio militum, Steph. Robert (Huc pertinent, Quadrifluvium, Vitr. & Quadrifinium, Aggen.
units.tr: Quaternary number, etc.] Fourfold, Plin. Fourfold joinings of words, Var. Quadriga, and quadrigae, Var. A company of four soldiers, Steph. Robert (to this belongs: Quadrifluvium, Vitr. and Quadrifinium, Aggen.

units.la: Quercetum] Querquetum, Fest.
units.tr: Oakwood] An alternative spelling, Fest.

units.la: Quercetus] Quernus, Querculanus, Querquetulanus, Cerreus, Cerrinus, Plin. Roboreus, Roburneus, Robustus, Col. Robusteus, Vitr. Quercicus, Suet. Querneus, Cat. Querquetularia porta, (juxta quam erat querquetum) Fest.
units.tr: Oaken] Of oak, oaken, Plin. Of oak, made of oak, sturdy, Col. Sturdy, Vitr. Oak-like, Suet. Oaken, Cat. The Oak-grove Gate, by which there was an oak grove, Fest.

units.la: Quercus] Robur, Cic. Fagus glandifera, Robert Constant. Cerrus, Plin. Jovis arbor, Ovid.
units.tr: Oak] Heartwood, hardwood, Cic. Acorn-bearing beech, Robert Constant. Turkey oak, Plin. Tree of Jove, Ovid.

units.la: Querela] Querimonia, Questus, Conquestio, Expostulatio cum absente, Cic. Conquestus, Liv. Postulatio, Ter.
units.tr: Complaint] Lament, complaint, grievance, expostulation with someone absent, Cic. A complaint, Liv. A demand, Ter.

units.la: Queri] Queri injuriam, Cic. De injuriis, Caef. Queri ad populum, Plin. Iun. Queri cum aliquo, Cic. Super aliquā, &c. Cic. Conqueri aliquid, de aliquo, graviter, cum aliquo de. Querimoniam habere de. Querelam habere apud aliquem de. Subaccusare aliquem. Deplorare aliquid apud aliquem, de. Cic. Querimonias ultrò citròque jactare, Liv. Queritantes, Tac. à Queritari, Bud. Quiritare, Plin. Accusare alicujus operam, fidem, Plaut. Causari vini inopiam, dicitur plebs Romana apud Amm.
units.tr: To complain] To complain of an injury, Cic. To complain of wrongs, Caef. To complain to the people, Plin. Iun. To complain with someone, Cic. To complain about something, etc., Cic. To complain of something, of someone, gravely, with someone about. To have a grievance about something before someone. To accuse someone a little. To lodge a complaint before someone about. To throw complaints back and forth, Liv. Complaining, Tac. From Queritari, Bud. To cry out, Plin. To accuse someone's work or loyalty, Plaut. The Roman plebs is said to complain of a shortage of wine, in Amm.

units.la: Querulus] Queribundus, Sil. Omnia gemens, Sen.
units.tr: Complaining] Full of lament, Sil. Groaning at everything, Sen.

units.la: Quia] Quòd. Quoniam, Cic. vid. Nam.
units.tr: Because] That, since, Cic. See Nam.

units.la: Quicquid] Quodcunque, Cic. Si quid, Id. Quod, vel. Quid, Absol. Ter. Quicquam, Id. Quicque, Quint.
units.tr: Whatever] Whatever it is, Cic. If anything, Id. Which, vel. Anything, absolutely, Ter. Anything, Id. Each thing, Quint.

units.la: Quicunque] Quisquis, Quivis è, Cic. Quilibet, Quispiam, Cic. Aliquis. Quis nunciate, (pro aliquis) Plaut.
units.tr: Whoever] Whoever it may be, whatever sort, Cic. Anyone you like, someone or other, Cic. Anyone. "Who will announce" (for someone), Plaut.

units.la: Quid hominis? &c.] Quid tu hominis es? Quid tu homo es? Quid hoc hominis. Quis videor, Ter. Quod genus est homo, Gell. Quod genus hoc hominum, Virg. Nescio quid viri sis? Plaut. vid. Qualis.
units.tr: What kind of man? etc.] What sort of man are you? What kind of man are you? What manner of man is this? What sort of man do I seem to be? Ter. What kind of man is he? Gell. What kind of men are these? Virg. I do not know what sort of man you are, Plaut. See Qualis.

units.la: Quid illi facias?] Quid tu huic homini facias. Quid hoc homine faciatis? Quid nam dici potest? Cic. Quid cum illis agas, qui, &c. Quid facias? Ter.
units.tr: What would you do to him?] What would you do to this man? What would you do with this man? What can be said? Cic. What will you do with those who... Cic. What are you going to do? Ter.

units.la: Quid ad rem?] Quid ad farinam? Quid ad Mercurium? Quid ad Bacchum? Quid cœco cum speculo?
units.tr: What has it to do with the matter?] What has it to do with the flour? What has it to do with Mercury? What has it to do with Bacchus? What has a blind man to do with a mirror?

units.la: Quid opus tuta timere?] Quid si cœlum ruat?
units.tr: Why fear safe things?] What if the sky should fall?

units.la: Quid pro quo] Palumbem pro columbâ. Pilos pro lanâ.
units.tr: One thing for another] A pigeon for a dove. Hair for wool.

units.la: Quid tum?] Quid postea? Quid tum inde? Quid interest utrum, &c. Cic. Quid tum postea, Ter.
units.tr: What then?] What afterwards? What then from that? What does it matter whether, Cic. What then afterwards, Ter.

units.la: Quidam] Quidam de, ex, è. Cic Aliquantis largitus est, Spart. Plerique, Quint. Partim hominum, (i. quidam) Gell. Habet hic unum hospitem, (id est quendam) Plaut. Arnob. vid. Aliquis.
units.tr: Some] Some of, from, out of, Cic. He gave to some, Spart. Most, Quint. Some of the people, that is, certain ones, Gell. He has one guest here (that is, a certain one), Plaut. Arnob. See Aliquis.

units.la: Quidam, cum laude] Cujusdam modi. Qualitate aliquâ praeditus. Excellentis cujusdam ingenii est. Nescio quis, Cic.
units.tr: Some, with praise] Of a certain kind. Endowed with some quality. It belongs to a man of excellent talent. I know not who, Cic.

units.la: Quiddam] Est quiddam, Cic. Aliquid est, Plaut. Quid certe est, Virg. Aliquid magnum est, Cerda.
units.tr: Something] There is something, Cic. Something is, Plaut. Something certainly is, Virg. Something great is, Cerda.

units.la: Quidem, vid. Certè.
units.tr: Indeed, see Certainly.

units.la: Quidni ?] Quin continetis vocem ? Cic. Cur non ? Apul. Quippini ? Plaut. Quin potius quam auro expendas ? Plin.
units.tr: Why not?] Do you not restrain your voice? Cic. Why not? Apul. Why not indeed? Plaut. Why not rather spend it than gold? Plin.

units.la: Quies] quies animi, laborum. Requies. Cessatio. Vacatio militiae, laborum, omnium rerum, à. Remissio animorum. Otium, Cic. Laxamentum curarum, Plin. Iun. Quiescentia, Firm.
units.tr: Rest] Rest of mind, of labours. Respite. Cessation. Release from military service, from labours, from all things. Relaxation of spirits. Leisure, Cic. Relief from cares, Plin. Iun. Quiescence, Firm.

units.la: Quiescere] Quietem capere. Conquiescere, abs. & à bellis. Requiescere à. Remittere, relaxare animum. Relaxari animis. Levare animum. Habere vacationem alicujus rei. Acquiescere, Cic. Animos laxare à, Id. Levare curas, corpus. Relevare laborem requie, Ovid. Intermittere tempus à labore, Caes. Remittere labores, Mart. Facere pausam, Plin. Levare membra toro, Tibul. Interquiescere, Cato. Suspendere spiritum (in pronunciando) Quint.
units.tr: To rest] To take rest. To rest, absolutely and from wars. To rest from. To relax the mind. To be relaxed in spirit. To lift up the spirit. To have a respite from something. To cease from, Cic. To relax the spirits from, Id. To lighten cares, the body. To relieve labour by rest, Ovid. To interrupt work with a pause, Caes. To remit labours, Mart. To make a pause, Plin. To lighten the limbs on the couch, Tibul. To rest between, Cato. To hold the breath (in speaking), Quint.

units.la: Quiescendum aliquando] Amant alterna Camoenae.
units.tr: One must rest sometime] The Muses love alternation.

units.la: Quiete rebus opus] Planta, quae saepius transfertur, non coalescit. Quod caret alternâ requie, durabile non est. Requies sit certa laborum. (Symb. Caroli Borbonij Navarrae Regis.)
units.tr: Work needs rest] A plant that is often transplanted does not take root. What lacks alternating rest is not durable. Let rest be the sure end of labours. (Motto of Charles of Bourbon, King of Navarre.)

units.la: Quietè] Quietissimè se recipere, Caes. Tranquillè, Cic. vid. Pacatè.
units.tr: Quietly] To withdraw most quietly, Caes. Calmly, Cic. See Calmly.

units.la: Quietus] Quies, Næv. Tranquillus animus. Starius orator. Otiosa senectus. Pacatissima provincia, Cic. vid. Tranquillus.
units.tr: Quiet] Restful, Naev. A tranquil mind. A calm orator. A leisured old age. A most peaceful province, Cic. See Tranquil.

units.la: Quilibet, vid. Quicunque. Quin. vid. Imò. Ne. Quippe, vid. Nam.
units.tr: Whoever, see Whoever. Not? see Yes indeed. No. Indeed, see Because.

units.la: Quiritari] Proquiritari, Apul. Gannire, Ter. Obvagulari. Pipare. Pipulo aliquem differre. Flagitare. Occentare, Plaut.
units.tr: To cry out] To cry out in support, Apul. To yelp, Ter. To howl at. To squeak. To put someone off with squeals. To demand insistently. To make a racket, Plaut.

units.la: Quis?] Quisnam? Hor. Nam qui (pro quis) erit rumor populi? Ter. Qui finis discordiarum? Liv. Quid gentium (pro, quae gens) caret his malis? Plaut. Quid hoc iceleris, Ter. Quod argentum? Quas tu mihi tricas narras? Quos tu mihi luscos libertos, quos Sumanos somnias? Plaut. Quem deum sponsorem accepisti? Sen. Quis Deus appellandus? Cic. Ecquis vivit me hodie fortunatior? Ter. Ecquisnam, Cic. Quis tandem? Id.
units.tr: Who?] Who then? Hor. For what rumour of the people will there be? Ter. What end of discords? Liv. What nation is free of these evils? Plaut. What is this crime? Ter. What silver? What tricks are you telling me about? What one-eyed freedmen, what Sumans are you dreaming of? Plaut. What god did you take as surety? Sen. What god is to be called upon? Cic. Does anyone live more fortunate than me today? Ter. Who then, pray? Cic.

units.la: Quis, sine interrog.] Si ullus me vocabit, Ter. Quisquam gentium: quisquam omnium, Cic. Quisquam unus, Liv. vid. Aliquis.
units.tr: Anyone, without a question] If anyone will call me, Ter. Anyone in the world; anyone of all, Cic. Any one at all, Liv. See Someone.

units.la: Quisque] Quisque homo, Plaut. Infimus quisque. Optimum quidque rarissimum. Quilibet. Omnis pars. Omne genus. In omni genere artis excellere, (id est in omni arte.) Nemo non videt. Nemo est quin arbitretur, Cic. Nullus non, Suet. Nulla non luce ducentos facio versus, Mart.
units.tr: Each] Every man, Plaut. Each lowest one. Each best thing is very rare. Whoever you like. Every part. Every kind. To excel in every kind of art (that is, in every art). No one fails to see. There is no one who does not think, Cic. No one who does not, Suet. I write two hundred verses every day, Mart.

units.la: Quisque agat sua, vid. Agat.
units.tr: Let each do his own, see Do.

units.la: Quisque habet, quod agat] Nulla vitæ pars officiô vacare potest.
units.tr: Each has something to do] No part of life can be free from duty.

units.la: Quisquis es] Quicquid tibi est nomen, Plaut. vid. Quicunque.
units.tr: Whoever you are] Whatever your name is, Plaut. See Whoever.

units.la: Quò?] Quorsum. Quò-nam, Cic. Quò gentium fugiam? Plaut.
units.tr: Whither?] Whereto. Whither then, Cic. Whither in the world shall I flee? Plaut.

units.la: Quò vadis] Quò paras proficisci? Quò paras profectionem? Quò tendis Quò tenetur iter? Quonam iter est? Er.
units.tr: Where are you going?] Where are you preparing to set out? Where are you preparing your departure? Where are you heading? Which way is your journey? Er.

units.la: Quoad, vid. Quantùm. & Vsque. Quocirca, vid. Ergo.
units.tr: Until, see As much as. and Up to. Therefore, see Therefore.

units.la: Quocunque] Quopiam ire. Quoquò gentium. Quovis gentium, Ter. Quoque se vertent, Cic. Quamquam in partem, Lucr. Quoquam, Cat.
units.tr: Wherever] To go somewhere. Wherever in the world. Anywhere in the world. Anywhere at all, Ter. Wherever they turn, Cic. Although in some direction, Lucr. Anywhere, Cat.

units.la: Quomodo?] Quomodonam? Quonam modo. Quonam tandem modo? Qui convenit? Qui potest esse sapientia? Quî fieri potest? Cic.
units.tr: How?] In what way then? In what way at all? In what manner then? How does it agree? How can there be wisdom? How can it come about? Cic.

units.la: Quomodo sine interr.] Quonam modo. Quî, Cic. Qualiter,
units.tr: How, without a question] In what manner. How, Cic. In what way.

units.la: liter, Mart. Quaratione, Virg. Quo pacto, Hor. Sicuti, Lucr. Sicut. Cic. Ut, Plaut.
units.tr: ...ly, Mart. By what reasoning, Virg. In what manner, Hor. Just as, Lucr. Just as, Cic. As, Plaut.

units.la: Quomodocunque] Qualitercunque, Col. Qualiter-qualiter, Vlp. quomodo potuissem, te convenissem, si, &c. Quoquo modo, Cic. Quoquo pacto, Ter. Utcunque collibitum est, Plaut. Quicquid id est, Virg. Lucr.
units.tr: However] In whatever way, Col. In whatever way at all, Vlp. In whatever way I could have met you, if, etc. In whatever manner, Cic. In whatever way, Ter. However it pleases, Plaut. Whatever that is, Virg. Lucr.

units.la: Quondam] Olim sic loquebantur (de praeterito) Cic. Hanc tu olim accipies, (de fut.) Virg. Aliquando vocitata Syrtis, Plin. Sero, aliquando tamen, Cic.
units.tr: Formerly] Thus they spoke formerly (of the past), Cic. You will one day accept this (of the future), Virg. Sometimes called Syrtis, Plin. Late, yet sometimes, Cic.

units.la: Quot] Quid hominum est, (i. quot) Plaut. Quantum militum, Tac. Quid captivorum, Plaut. Quanti? (pro, quot) Veget. Quantos milites, I.C.
units.tr: How many] How many men there are (that is, how many), Plaut. As many soldiers, Tac. How many captives, Plaut. How many? (for how many), Veget. As many soldiers, I.C.

units.la: Quotannis] Quotquot annis, Var. In annos singulos. In singulis annis, Cic. Annua vice, Col.
units.tr: Yearly] As many years as, Var. Each year. Every single year, Cic. A yearly turn, Col.

units.la: Quotidianus] Amphemerinus, Plin.
units.tr: Daily] Daily, Plin.

units.la: Quotidie] Quotidiano, Plin. Quot diebus, Quint. Quot dies, Apul. Quotquot eunt dies, Hor. In dies. In dies singulos. Singulis diebus, Cic. Prope diem spero affuturum, Ter. Sic de Mensibus. Quot mensibus, Catu. Quotquot mensibus, Var. Quot Calendis, Plaut. Vitr. In singulos menses, Vlp.
units.tr: Daily] Daily, Plin. As many days as, Quint. How many days, Apul. As many days as go, Hor. Day by day. Each single day, Cic. I hope it will come about soon, Ter. Likewise of months. As many months, Catu. As many months as, Var. How many Calends, Plaut. Vitr. Each single month, Vlp.

units.la: Quotus] Quotumus, Plaut.
units.tr: How many-th] How many-th, Plaut.

units.la: Quousque] Quoad! Cic. Ecquid facies modi? Plaut. vid. Quamdiu, Cic.
units.tr: Until when] Until when? Cic. What will you do, and in what way? Plaut. See How long, Cic.

units.la: R.
units.tr: R.

units.la: Rabies] Rabies canis, Plin. Hydrophobia, Celf.
units.tr: Rabies] The rabies of a dog, Pliny. Hydrophobia, Celsus.

units.la: Rabiose] Rabidè, Cic.
units.tr: Rabiose: rabidly, Cic.

units.la: Rabiosus] Rabidus, Plin, Rabie stimulatus, Catul. Efferum pecus, Sen.
units.tr: Rabiosus: rabid, Plin. Stirred by madness, Catul. A savage beast, Sen.

units.la: Rabiosum fieri] Rabidi fiunt canes. Inflammantur equi rabie, Plin. Rabie ferri, Id. Venit rabies canibus, Virg. Vertitur in rabiem, Hor. Furere, Virg. Rábere, & Rabire, Cæcil. Sipont.
units.tr: Rabiosum fieri: Dogs become rabid. Horses are inflamed with rage, Plin. With the rage of iron, Id. Rage comes upon dogs, Virg. It turns into madness, Hor. To rage, Virg. Rabere and rabire, Cæcil. Sipont.

units.la: Rabula, vid. Rixator, & Advocatus.
units.tr: Rabula: see Rixator and Advocatus.

units.la: Racemari] Racemationem facere, Bud.
units.tr: Racemari: To gather grapes in clusters; to make a gathering of clusters, Bud.

units.la: Racemarius] Racemosus, Racematus, Plin. Racemifer, Ovid.
units.tr: Racemarius: Full of clusters, Racemosus, Racematus, Plin. Bearing clusters, Ovid.

units.la: Racemus, vid. Botrus.
units.tr: Racemus: see Botrus.

units.la: Radians] Radiatus sol, Cic. Radiosus sol. Radiatus stel-læ modo, Plin.
units.tr: Radians: A radiant sun, Cic. A radiating sun. Shining like a star, Plin.

units.la: Radiare] Radiat vultu Phœbe, Col. Irradiare, Sipont.
units.tr: Radiare: Phoebus shines with his face, Col. To shine upon, Sipont.

units.la: Radicari] Radicare, Sipont. Radicescere, Sen. Agere radices, Cic. Agere radices deorsum in profundum, Plin. Mittere radices. Descendit in altum radix, Col. Descendit arbor radice. Descendit radix arboris altius, Plin. Altis nititur radicibus, Cic.
units.tr: Radicari: To take root; Radicare, Sipont. Radicescere, Sen. To put forth roots, Cic. To send roots down into the depths, Plin. To send out roots. The root goes down on high, Col. The tree goes down by its root. The root of the tree goes deeper, Plin. It rests on deep roots, Cic.

units.la: Radicatus] Radicatæ plantæ, Pallad. Radicosus. Multâ crassaque radice herba. Radicatum est multis fibris, Plin. Altissimis defixus est radicibus, Cic.
units.tr: Radicatus: Rooted plants, Pallad. Rooted; grass with a thick and abundant root. It is rooted with many fibres, Plin. It is fixed by very deep roots, Cic.

units.la: Radicitus] Radicibus erupta pinus. Ab radice alta revellere: cum imis stirpibus evellere aliquid, Virg. Stirpitus radicem exigere. Cic. A stirpe, Liv. Radicitus effodere. Cum radice evellere, Col.
units.tr: Radicitus: A pine torn up by the roots. To pull up from a deep root; to tear something out from its lowest stumps, Virg. To draw out the root from the stump, Cic. From the stump, Liv. To dig out by the root. To pull out with the root, Col.

units.la: Radius solis &c.] Radiolus, Col. Crinis stellæ, fulguris, Virg. Jubar, coma, crinis, falx, gladius, villorum species, Plin.
units.tr: Radius solis &c.: A little ray, Col. The hair of a star, of lightning, Virg. Ray, mane, hair, sickle, sword, a kind of fibre-like growth, Plin.

units.la: Radere] Scarificare radicem, Cat. Desquamare summum corticem, Plin. Destringere cutem, Plin. Supperradere, Id. vid. Deradere.
units.tr: Radere: To scarify the root, Cat. To scrape off the top bark, Plin. To strip the skin, Plin. To scrape over, Id. See Deradere.

units.la: Radix] Truncus ægritudinis, Cic. Stirps, Virg. Rapum arboris, Sen. Caput vitis, extrema ejus pars, Col. i, radix Scal.
units.tr: Radix: The trunk of a sickness, Cic. Stock, Virg. The root of a tree, Sen. The head of a vine, its extreme part, Col. i, radix, Scaliger.

units.la: Ramentum] Ramenta, æ, Plaut. Projectitium purgamentum, Fulgent. Strigmentum, Plin. Destrigmentum. Rasamen, Marcell. vid. Scobs.
units.tr: Ramentum: Shavings, Plaut. Cast-off refuse, Fulgent. Scrapings, Plin. Destrigmentum. Rasamen, Marcell. See Scobs.

units.la: Rameus] Frondea tecta, Virg.
units.tr: Rameus: Leafy roofs, Virg.

units.la: Ramex, vid. Hernia.
units.tr: Ramex: see Hernia.

units.la: Ramosus] Ramulosus, Sarmentosus. Diffunditur vastis ramis, Plin. Frondosus, Liv. Arboreus: cornua arborea cervi, Virg. Frondifer, Luer. Frondifluus, Boët.
units.tr: Ramosus: Full of twigs, full of shoots. Spreading out with huge branches, Plin. Leafy, Liv. Tree-like: the branching horns of a stag, Virg. Leaf-bearing, Lucr. Leaf-flowing, Boët.

units.la: Ramosus, 2. in plures ramos distinctus] In ramos sparsus. Multicaulis frutex. Surculosi rami. Bisulcus surculus. Multifidus. In quinque (&c) partes diffusus, Plin. Trisulcus surculus. Trifurca stirps. Brachiata vinea. Bifurcus, Col.
units.tr: Ramosus, 2. in plures ramos distinctus: Scattered into branches. A shrub with many stems. Twiggy shoots. A two-cleft shoot. Many-cleft. Spread out into five (etc.) parts, Plin. A three-cleft shoot. A three-forked stock. A branching vine. Two-pronged, Col.

units.la: Ramus] Brachia arboris. Duramenta, & Duramina, Col. Tabulata arborum, ut in abiete, larice, Scamna ramorum, Plin. Ramulus, Col. Ramusculus, surculus, Plin.
units.tr: Ramus: The arms of a tree. Hard wood and heartwood, Col. The layers of trees, as in fir and larch; the benches of branches, Plin. A little branch, Col. A little twig, a shoot, Plin.

units.la: Rana, vitium linguæ] Nodus linguæ, Gell. Obligatio linguæ, Firm. Ranunculus, Gorr. Vitiosa incrementa linguæ, Col.
units.tr: Rana, vitium linguæ: A knot of the tongue, Gell. A binding of the tongue, Firm. Ranula, Gorr. Faulty growths of the tongue, Col.

units.la: Rancere, vid. Putere. Rancidus, vid. Putidus.
units.tr: Rancere: see Putere. Rancidus: see Putidus.

units.la: Rapa] Rapum, Var. (quod 40 amplius librarum vidit Cæl. Rhod.) Rapulum, Hor. Congylis, Col.
units.tr: Rapa: A turnip, Var. (a turnip of more than forty pounds, which Caelius Rhodiginus saw). A little turnip, Hor. Congylis, Col.

units.la: Rapacia] Rapicia, pl. Plin. Rapicius colis, Cat.
units.tr: Rapacia: Rapicia, plural, Plin. Rapicius colis, Cat.

units.la: Rapax] Raptor lupus, Col. Vulturius provinciæ, Reip. Cic. Harpyia rapacior. Vultureus venter, Er. vid. Raptor.
units.tr: Rapax: A wolf that snatches (raptor lupus), Col. A vulture of the province, Reip. Cic. A harpy greedier still. A vulturous belly, Er. See Raptor.

units.la: Rapere] Præceleri vi, repente, aliquid rapere. Rapere in sublime, Plin. Raptare Virg. Arripere, Corripere. Prehendere, apprehendere, Cic. Surripere, Plaut. Harpagare. Facere harpax, Id. Capere, Virg. Omnia viscatis manibus legere, Lucil. Asportare aliquid, Auferre de, Cic. Subtrahere aliquid clandestina fuga, Cæs.
units.tr: Rapere: To snatch something suddenly and with very swift force. To snatch up on high, Plin. To drag away, Virg. To seize, to lay hold of, Cic. To grab, to catch hold of, Cic. To steal away, Plaut. To plunder. To make oneself a snatcher, Id. To seize, Virg. To gather everything with sticky hands, Lucil. To carry something off, to take away from, Cic. To withdraw something by secret flight, Cæs.

units.la: Rapidus] Rapax torrens, Sen. Violentus amnis, Virg. Torrens flumen, Id. Præcipitans torrens, Cic. Tanquam torrens, Er.
units.tr: Rapidus: A rapacious torrent, Sen. A violent river, Virg. A rushing river, Id. A headlong torrent, Cic. Like a torrent, Er.

units.la: Raptim] Cursim arripui & succisivis horis. Raptim, turbulenter, temerè agere. In procinctu testamentum facere. Ex tempore, Cic. Mobiliter ad bellum agitari, Cæs.
units.tr: Raptim: I snatched it up hastily and in spare hours. To do things hastily, confusedly, rashly. To make a will in the field. On the spot, Cic. To be moved quickly to war, Cæs.

units.la: Raptor] Accipiter pecuniarum. Trahax, Rapax, Rapacida. Summanus, Plaut. Turn. Rapo, onis, Non. Viscatis manibus, Lucil.
units.tr: Raptor: A hawk of money (a usurer). Greedy, rapacious, a plunderer. Summanus, Plaut. Turn. Rapo, Non. With sticky hands, Lucil.

units.la: Raptum] Vivere rapto, & ex rapto, Ovid. Rapina, Cic.
units.tr: Raptum: To live by plunder and from what is seized, Ovid. Robbery, Cic.

units.la: Rarè] Rarenter, Var. Rarissimè conseritur panax, Col. Sparsim convoluta canitie, Plin.
units.tr: Rarè: Rarely, Var. Panax is planted very rarely, Col. Scattered with white hair, Plin.

units.la: Rarefacere] Disrarare, Col. Diluere, Ovid. Diluviem facere, Lucr. Liquare alvum, Celf.
units.tr: Rarefacere: To thin out, Col. To dilute, Ovid. To make a flood, Lucr. To loosen the bowels, Celf.

units.la: Rarescere] Rarefieri. Rarefactum corpus, Lucr.
units.tr: Rarescere: To become rarefied. A rarefied body, Lucr.

units.la: Raritas] Raritudo terræ, Col. Rara liquiditas aëris, Apul. Parcitas animadversionum, Sen. Infrequentia Senatus, Cic.
units.tr: Raritas: Looseness of the earth, Col. The thin fluidity of air, Apul. Sparingness of punishments, Sen. Thin attendance at the Senate, Cic.

units.la: Rarò] Rarius facere aliquid. Perraro. Minus in senatum venit, Cic. Rarenter, Cato. Infrequens sum Romæ, Cic.
units.tr: Rarò: To do something less often. Very rarely. He comes to the Senate less often, Cic. Rarely, Cato. I am seldom in Rome, Cic.

units.la: Rarus] Rarum quid, Cic. Infrequens Senatus, Cic. Infrequens paucitate alicujus rei, Col. Perrarae literæ, Liv. Sparsus: sparsior racemus, Plin. v. Levidensis & Liquidus.
units.tr: Rarus: Something rare, Cic. A thin attendance at the Senate, Cic. Thin through the scarcity of some thing, Col. Very rare letters, Liv. Sparse: a sparser cluster, Plin. See Levidensis and Liquidus.

units.la: Rararesʼ Rarum, Cic. Rara avis, Hor. Corvus albus. Lac gallinaceum. Phoenice rarior. Cygno nigro rarior. Albo corvo rarior, Er.
units.tr: Rare: Rare, Cic. A rare bird, Hor. A white crow. Rooster's milk. Rarer than a phoenix. Rarer than a black swan. Rarer than a white crow, Er.

units.la: Rara, chara] In omni re optimum, quod rarissimum est. vel: Optimum quidque rarissimum, Cic. Omnia praeclara rara. Voluptates commendat rarior usus. Vilescunt quotidiana.
units.tr: Rara, chara: In every matter the best thing is what is rarest. Or: each best thing is the rarest, Cic. All excellent things are rare. Pleasures are recommended by rarer use. Daily things grow cheap.

units.la: Rastrum] Rastellum, Suet. Plural. Rastra, Cels. Rastri, Ter. Rastelli, Var.
units.tr: Rastrum: A small rake, Suet. Plural. Rakes, Cels. Rakes, Ter. Little rakes, Var.

units.la: Rastris colligere fœnum &c.] Stipulam rastellis de prato eradere. Festucas in pratis per fœnisicia relictas ab radere, Varr. Rastris herba mundetur, Pallad. Rastris congregare, converrere.
units.tr: Rastris colligere fœnum &c.: To scrape up stubble with rakes from the meadow. To rake up the stalks left in the meadows by haymaking, Varr. The grass is to be cleaned with rakes, Pallad. To gather together and sweep up with rakes.

units.la: Rasura arboris &c.] Decorticatio angusta arbori non nocet. Repumicatio & politura vitium, Plin. Scarificatio, Col. Rasus, Id. Var.
units.tr: Rasura arboris &c.: A narrow stripping of bark does not harm a tree. Scraping and polishing of a fault, Plin. Scarification, Col. Scraped, Id. Var.

units.la: Ratio] Intelligentia. Mens, Cic. Animus, Inv. Intellectus, Quint. Corde vigere, Ausón. Usque adeone corde erant vacui? Arnob.
units.tr: Ratio: Understanding. Mind, Cic. Spirit, Inv. Intellect, Quint. To flourish in heart, Ausón. Were they then so empty of heart? Arnob.

units.la: Ratio quadrat. vid. Computatio recta.
units.tr: Ratio quadrat.: see Computatio recta.

units.la: Rationem reddere] Referre, deponere rationes. Referre ad aerarium rationes, Cic. Edere rationes, Id.
units.tr: Rationem reddere: To carry over, to set down accounts. To refer accounts to the treasury, Cic. To publish accounts, Id.

units.la: Rationes cum aliquo inire] Rationem ab aliquo reposcere. Putare cum aliquo rationes. Ad calculos vocare, Cic. Supputare rationem cum argentario, Plaut. Calculum cum aliquo ponere, Plin. Iun. Conferre accepta & data, Vlp. Accipere rationes à. Cic. Disputare rationes, Plaut. Conferre rationes. Ponere rationem singulorum, Sen. Summam ducere sumptûs sui & alieni, Lucil. Dispungere rationes, Vlp.
units.tr: Rationes cum aliquo inire: To demand an account from someone. To reckon accounts with someone. To call to account, Cic. To reckon accounts with a banker, Plaut. To place a reckoning with someone, Plin. Iun. To compare receipts and payments, Vlp. To receive accounts from, Cic. To dispute accounts, Plaut. To compare accounts. To set out the account of each, Sen. To draw up the sum of one's own and others' expenses, Lucil. To strike out accounts, Vlp.

units.la: Rationem reposcere] Rationem vitæ & magistratûs gesti reposcere. Interrogat aliquem judex legibus, Cic.
units.tr: Rationem reposcere: To demand an account of one's life and of the office held. A judge calls someone to account by the laws, Cic.

units.la: Rationabilis] Cum ratione, Cic. Habetne id rationem? Vlp.
units.tr: Rationabilis: With reason, Cic. Does this have a reason? Vlp.

units.la: Rationabiliter omnia age] Dignum te Deo finge.
units.tr: Rationabiliter omnia age: Shape yourself to be worthy of God.

units.la: Rationalis] Rationis particeps. Ratione utens. Mente, animo præditus. Habet mentem. Intelligens. Intelligentiæ particeps. Cic.
units.tr: Rationalis: Partaking of reason. Using reason. Endowed with mind and spirit. Having a mind. Intelligent. Partaking of understanding, Cic.

units.la: Rationarius codex] Ratio expensi, Plaut. v. Expensi codex.
units.tr: Rationarius codex: An account of expenditure, Plaut. See Expensi codex.

units.la: Rationarius, Nomen] Rationum præfectus. A rationi-bus, Suet. Supputator, Firm. Ratiocinator, Col. Tabula-rius, Sidon. Vlp. Rationalis. Rationum perscriptor, Bud. Actor summarum, Suet Qui accepti & expensi rationem habet.
units.tr: Rationarius, Nomen: Prefect of accounts. From the accounts office, Suet. A reckoner, Firm. A calculator, Col. A bookkeeper, Sidon. Vlp. Accountant. A keeper of the reckoning of items, Bud. A keeper of totals, Suet. One who keeps the account of receipts and expenses.

units.la: Ratum habere, vid. Confirmare.
units.tr: Ratum habere: see Confirmare.

units.la: Ratus] Rata acta Cæsaris. Ratum judicium, Cic. Ratissima & gratissima, Cato. Legitimæ nuptiæ, Cic. Legitimum fœdus, Ovid.
units.tr: Ratus: The acts of Caesar, ratified. A ratified judgment, Cic. Most valid and most welcome, Cato. Lawful marriage, Cic. Lawful covenant, Ovid.

units.la: Raucedo] Ravis. Rauca ravis, Plaut. Raucitas, Plin.
units.tr: Raucedo: Hoarseness. Hoarse hoarseness, Plaut. Hoarseness, Plin.

units.la: Raucescere] Raucere, Ovid. Raucum sonare, Id.
units.tr: Raucescere: To grow hoarse, Ovid. To sound hoarsely, Id.

units.la: Raucus] Raucisonus, Lucr. Ravus, Fest.
units.tr: Raucus: Hoarse-sounding, Lucr. Hoarse, Fest.

units.la: Re ipsa] Re, abs. Re vera. Reapse, Cic. Opere ipso, Sen. Ad verum exerceri. Verba in rem conferre, Tac. Rem tibi auctorem dabo. Res ipsa dicet tibi, Plaut. Res operi faciet pondusque fidemque, Manil. In re ipsa, Ter. In re præsenti, Plaut. In oculis habere, Quint. Mea dicta ex factis nosce, Plaut. Dicta factis honestare, Id.
units.tr: Re ipsa: In fact (re, absolute). In truth. Really, Cic. By the work itself, Sen. To be exercised in what is true. To bring words to the matter, Tac. I will give you the thing itself as witness. The thing itself will tell you, Plaut. The work itself will give weight and trust, Manil. In the very matter, Ter. In the present matter, Plaut. To keep before one's eyes, Quint. Know my words from my deeds, Plaut. To honour words by deeds, Id.

units.la: Re præsente, non curamus signa] Cum adsit ursus, vestigia quæris.
units.tr: Re præsente, non curamus signa: When the bear is present, you look for tracks.

units.la: Reassumere aliquid] Recolere, Rectrare, instaurare, Cic. Redauspicare, Plin. Integrare, Virg.
units.tr: Reassumere aliquid: To recall, to take up again, to renew, Cic. To take the auspices afresh, Plin. To make whole, Virg.

units.la: Reatus] Admissa culpa.
units.tr: Reatus: A fault committed.

units.la: Rebellare alicui] Abjicere, relinquere obedientiam, Cic. deficere, Cæs. Convertere se in eum, quo adjutore omnia feceris, Cic. Verte arma adversus aliquem, ex Liv.
units.tr: Rebellare alicui: To cast off and abandon obedience, Cic. To revolt, Cæs. To turn oneself against him by whose help you have done everything, Cic. Turn arms against someone, from Liv.

units.la: Rebellatio] Rebellio, Tac. Rebellium, Liv. defectio, Cic.
units.tr: Rebellatio: Rebellion, Tac. Rebellium, Liv. Defection, Cic.

units.la: Rebellator] Rebellis, Stat.
units.tr: Rebellator: A rebel, Stat.

units.la: Recalefieri. vid Calefieri. Recantare, vid. Revocare. Recedere, vid. Abire.
units.tr: Recalefieri: see Calefieri. Recantare: see Revocare. Recedere: see Abire.

units.la: Recens] Recentissimæ literæ, Cic. Musteus caseus, Plin.
units.tr: Recens: Very recent letters, Cic. Fresh must-cheese, Plin.

units.la: Recentiora meliora] Equis vetulis teneros anteponimus. Piscis nequam est nisi recens.
units.tr: Recentiora meliora: We prefer young horses to old ones. A fish is worthless unless it is fresh.

units.la: Recensere, vid. Enumerare.
units.tr: Recensere: see Enumerare.

units.la: Recenter] Sole recens orto, Virg. Quàm recentissimè, Plin. Recenti re, tempore, negotio. Dum res calet, Cic. Nihil est nisi dum calet, id agitur, Plaut.
units.tr: Recenter: With the sun newly risen, Virg. As recently as possible, Plin. With the thing, time or business freshly done. While the thing is still hot, Cic. Nothing matters except while it is hot; that is what is at stake, Plaut.

units.la: Receptaculum] Receptus tutus, Virg. Diversorium stu-dio. diorum villa, Cic. Diverticulum, Quint. Ectrope, es Varr. Turneb.
units.tr: Receptacle] A safe refuge, Virg. A lodging for the stud, Cic. A side-road, Quint. A place of outflow, Varr. Turneb.

units.la: Receptio] Susceptio causae, Cic.
units.tr: Receiving] Taking up a cause, Cic.

units.la: Receptor] Susceptor. Receptator, Vlp. Receptrix furtorum, Cic.
units.tr: Receiver] One who takes in. A harbourer, Ulp. A receiver of stolen goods, Cic.

units.la: Recidere] Relabi, Tac. Recidere in easdem tenebras.
units.tr: To fall back] To slip back, Tac. To fall back into the same darkness.

units.la: Recidere in morbum] Remorbescere, Enn. Redeunt febres, Plin. Recruduit sopoatus dolor, Curt.
units.tr: To relapse into sickness] To fall sick again, Enn. The fevers return, Plin. The pain, lulled to sleep, flares up again, Curt.

units.la: Recidet in me hoc malum] Faba cadetur in me. De meo capite aguntur comitia. Mei capitis luditur alea.
units.tr: This evil will fall back on me] The bean will fall to me. The assembly is held about my head. The dice are rolled over my head.

units.la: Recidet in auctorem, vid. auctor.
units.tr: It will fall back on the author: see author.

units.la: Recipere aliquem] Receptare, Ter. Mea domus me excepit, Caes. Excipere hospitio, Plin. Accipere in numerum, in societatem regni. Adscisccre in civitatem, Liv. Recipere aliquem civitate, in civitate, in civitatem. Aggregare aliquem in numerum. Adscribere ad amicitiam. Adscribere civitati, in civitatem. Aperire fores amicitiae. Suscipere in, Cic. Civitate donare, Sen.
units.tr: To receive someone] To entertain, Ter. My house has received me, Caes. To welcome as a guest, Plin. To admit into a company or into partnership in a kingdom. To admit into the citizenship, Liv. To receive someone into the citizenship or into a community. To enrol someone in a body. To enrol as a friend. To open the doors of friendship. To take in, Cic. To grant the citizenship, Sen.

units.la: Recipere in se aliquid] Recipio id ad me, Ter. in me, Cic. Accipio ad me litem, Plaut. Suscipere aes alienum, Cic. Transscribere in se aes alienum, Bud. Litem suam facere. Praestare periculum, damnum. Suscipere curam, culpam. Nomen suum ad translationem criminis concedere, Cic. Expromittere, IC. Sui periculi rem facere, Bud. Transferre in se alicujus peccatum. Ego isthaec videro, Ter. Valde videro, de reliquo videro, Cic. Redimere litem, Quint. Vindicem se causae offerre. Eventum judicii praestare, Bud.
units.tr: To take something upon oneself] I take that upon myself, Ter. upon myself, Cic. I take the suit upon myself, Plaut. To take on another's debt, Cic. To transfer another's debt to oneself, Bud. To make the case one's own. To answer for a danger or a loss. To take up a care or a fault. To consent to transfer the name to another's charge, Cic. To stand surety, Jurists. To make another's risk one's own, Bud. To transfer another's sin to oneself. I will see to that, Ter. I will see to it fully, I will see to the rest, Cic. To buy back the suit, Quint. To offer oneself as the champion of the cause. To answer for the outcome of the trial, Bud.

units.la: Recipere aliquid] Accipere quod datur. Accipere excusationem, Cic. Conditionem, Caes. Suscipere profectionem. Adscisccre consuetudinem. Ratum habere, Cic. Acceptare reliquationem rationum, Paul. IC. Acceptare jugum, Sil. Acceptum facere alicui, Iulian. Turneb.
units.tr: To receive something] To accept what is given. To accept an excuse, Cic. A condition, Caes. To undertake a journey. To adopt a custom. To hold as valid, Cic. To accept the settlement of accounts, Paul, Jurist. To accept the yoke, Sil. To credit to someone's account, Julian, Turneb.

units.la: Reciprocus] Reciprocata vicissitudo, Arnob.
units.tr: Reciprocal] A reciprocal change, Arnob.

units.la: Recitare vid. Proclamare & Memoriter.
units.tr: To recite: see To proclaim and From memory.

units.la: Reclamare] Reclamitare alicui, Cic. Interclamantibus multis nostri restiterunt, Amm.
units.tr: To cry out in protest] To protest loudly against someone, Cic. Though many cried out against it, our men held their ground, Amm.

units.la: Reclamatio] Acclamatio adversa populi, Cic.
units.tr: Protest] An adverse acclamation of the people, Cic.

units.la: Reclinare vid. Inniti.
units.tr: To recline: see To lean upon.

units.la: Reclinatus] Reclivus & resupinatus in manus pende-bat, Vopisc. Acclivis arbori, Plin.
units.tr: Reclined] Leaning back and hanging on his hands, Vopisc. Leaning against a tree, Plin.

units.la: Recludere, Reclusus ; vid. Aperire Apertus.
units.tr: To unlock, unlocked: see To open, open.

units.la: Recognitio] Circumspectus. Lustratio municipiorum, Cic. Lustramen, Val. Arg. Inspectio rerum suarum, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Inspection] A survey. A review of the towns, Cic. An atonement sacrifice, Val. Arg. An inspection of one's own affairs, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Recognoscere] Recognoscere decretum. Retractare causas, Cic. Remetiri dicta, facta, Sen. Recolligere actionem suam, Plin. Iun. vid. Perlustrare.
units.tr: To review] To review a decree. To reconsider causes, Cic. To retrace one's words and deeds, Sen. To recall one's own action, Plin. Iun. See To survey thoroughly.

units.la: Recolere, vid. Reassumere.
units.tr: To recall: see To take up again.

units.la: Reconciliare] Reconciliare gratiam cum aliquo, Curt. Conciliatum reddere animum alicujus. Sanare vulnus injuriae, Cic. Propitiare, propitium reddere aliquem. Redigere in antiquam concordiam, Plaut. vid Placare. Conciliare.
units.tr: To reconcile] To restore goodwill with someone, Curt. To win back a person's mind. To heal the wound of an injury, Cic. To propitiate, to make someone well-disposed. To bring back into the former harmony, Plaut. See To appease, To win over.

units.la: Reconciliatio] Reconciliatio gratiae, concordiae: Reditus in gratiam cum aliquo, Cic. Conciliatura, Sen.
units.tr: Reconciliation] Reconciliation of favour, of harmony. A return to favour with someone, Cic. A conciliation, Sen.

units.la: Reconciliator, vid. Pacificator. Reconcinnare, vid. Reparare.
units.tr: Reconciler: see Peacemaker. To patch up: see To repair.

units.la: Recondere aliquid] Reponere ac condere fructus, Cic. Servare vinum in vetustatem, Col. Seponere pecuniam in aedificationem, Liv. Penum struere, Virg. Condo esui oleam, Var.
units.tr: To store something away] To put by and store up fruits, Cic. To keep wine to age, Col. To set money aside for building, Liv. To lay up provisions, Virg. I lay up olives for food, Varr.

units.la: Reconvenire, Barb. Latine, Citare in jus, qui me prius citaverat] Resortiri judicium, Bud. Actori meo vicissim litem intendo. Actori & victori, quo agente absens damnatus sum, quaestionem, litem, judicium refero, Id.
units.tr: To counter-sue, in barbarous Latin: to summon to court one who had already summoned me] To renew the trial, Bud. I bring a counter-suit against my plaintiff in turn. I refer the question, the suit, the trial back to the plaintiff and winner, by whose action I was condemned in my absence, Id.

units.la: Reconventio apud IC.] Relatio criminis, Ulp. Mutua actio, accusatio, Cuj. IC.
units.tr: Counter-action in legal usage] A reporting of a charge, Ulp. A mutual action, an accusation, Cujas, Jurist.

units.la: Recordari] Recordari aliquid cum animo. Reminisci alicujus rei : de aliqua re. Reminiscendo recordari. Recognoscere. Repetere memoriam alicujus rei. Memoria repetere. Renovare recordatione aliquid. Renovare memoriam rei intermortuam. Recolere aliquid Replicare memoriam. Referre animum ad aliquid. Redit, incurrit in memoriam. Succurrit. In mentem venit aliquid, & alicujus rei. Redintegratur memoriam auditoris, Cic. Reprehendere aliquid memori mente, Lucr. Tangit animum memoria rei, Liv. In mentem mihi fuit. In memoriam regredi, Plaut. Repræsentare aliquid animo, Curt. Repetere præterita. Retorquere se in præteritum. In præteritum tempus animus mittendus, Sen. Recomminisci, Plaut. Occursant mihi verba, Plin. Iun. In memoriam redigere, reducere, inducere, Plaut. Ter. Usurpare memoria, Cic.
units.tr: To remember] To recall something in mind. To be reminded of a thing, or to remember a thing about something. To remember by reminding oneself. To recognise. To recall the memory of a thing. To bring a thing back to mind. To refresh a thing by recollection. To revive the memory of a long-dead thing. To call a thing to mind. To renew the memory. To turn the mind to something. It comes back to me, it occurs to me. It comes to mind. It comes to my memory. The hearer's memory is refreshed, Cic. To grasp a thing with a retentive mind, Lucr. The memory of a thing touches the mind, Liv. It came into my mind. To go back into memory, Plaut. To present something to the mind, Curt. To recall past things. To turn back upon the past. The mind must be sent back to past time, Sen. To recall again, Plaut. Words come to me, Plin. Iun. To bring back into memory, to lead back, to call in, Plaut., Ter. To use in memory, Cic.

units.la: Retardari nonsatis queo] Hæret in prioribus labiis.
units.tr: I cannot quite get it out] It sticks on the first lips.

units.la: Recordatio] Commemoratio beneficii. Memoria, Cic. Memoratus, Gell. Usurpatio, Liv. Repetentia priorum, Arnob.
units.tr: Recollection] A recalling of a kindness. Memory, Cic. Mentioned, Gell. Repeated use, Liv. A going over of earlier things, Arnob.

units.la: Recrastinare. vid. differre.
units.tr: To postpone: see To defer.

units.la: Recreare] Focillare Refocillare aliquem, Plin. Iun. Roborare, firmare corpora juvenum labore, Cic. Corroborare, Suet. Solidare stomachum, Pallad. Confirmare animum alicujus. Erigere, excitare jacentem, Cic. Ægritudinem levare, lenire, sedare, Id. Arrigere oratione, Salust. Restituere animum, Liv. Reficere se ab imbecillitate, Plin. Reficere se ad audiendum. Recipere se. Relaxatus animus somno. Confirmare se. Confirmata à morbo valetudo, Cic. Redintegrare animum, Cæf. Renovare animum à satietate & fatigatione, Quint. Refovere membra, Sil. Revocare vires victu, Virg. Suffundere vires cibo, Var. Suffulcit cibus artus, Lucr. Recuperatis cibo somnoque viribus, Tibul. Reciperare se quiete, Var.
units.tr: To refresh] To revive and restore someone, Plin. Iun. To strengthen the bodies of the young by toil, Cic. To invigorate, Suet. To fortify the stomach, Pallad. To strengthen someone's spirit. To raise and rouse one who lies fallen, Cic. To lighten, soothe, and calm grief, Id. To cheer up by speech, Sall. To restore the spirit, Liv. To recover oneself from weakness, Plin. To recover oneself to listen. To take heart. The spirit relaxed by sleep. To gather strength. Health restored from sickness, Cic. To renew the spirit, Caes. To renew the spirit from weariness and fatigue, Quint. To warm the limbs, Sil. To restore strength by food, Virg. To nourish strength with food, Varr. Food strengthens the limbs, Lucr. Strength regained by food and sleep, Tibul. To restore oneself by rest, Varr.

units.la: Recreari à metu] Ad se redire. Animum ad se ipsum revocare, colligere. Consistere animo. Respirare, à Cic. Remigrat animus, Plaut. Redire in potestatem, Cato. Revivisce-re, Var. Resipiscere, Plin. Recipere animum ex pavore, Liv. Restituere se. Var. Recipere animum sc. ex pavore, Ter. Liv.
units.tr: To recover from fear] To come back to oneself. To call back and gather the mind. To steady oneself. To catch one's breath, Cic. The mind returns, Plaut. To return to one's senses, Cato. To come back to life, Varr. To come to one's senses, Plin. To take heart again after fear, Liv. To restore oneself, Varr. To take heart again after fear, Ter., Liv.

units.la: Recreationis causa] Animi (sc. delectandi) causa, Plaut. Deliciarum causa, Cic. Reficiendi animi gratia, Plin. Fallendi temporis gratia, Ovid.
units.tr: For the sake of recreation] For the sake of pleasure, Plaut. For the sake of delight, Cic. For the refreshment of the mind, Plin. To pass the time, Ovid.

units.la: Recreatus] Iterum natus sum, si vera autumas. Jam defæcato sum animo, Plaut. Respirasse homines videbantur. Cùm ex illorum metu mortis, quasi luce libertatis recreatus revixisset, Cic. Recipi animum ex pavore, Liv. Non secus est, quàm si ab Acheronte veniam.
units.tr: Restored] If you say so truly, I am born again. Now my mind is cleared, Plaut. People seemed to breathe again. When, as if restored to the light of freedom after their fear of death, they had revived, Cic. The mind recovered from fear, Liv. It is as if I had come back from Acheron.

units.la: Recrescere] Repullulafcere (Repullulefcere, Commelin.) Col. Repullulare. Resurgit arbor. Regerminat, Plin. Pullulat ab radice silva, Virg. Regignuntur membra, Lucr. Renascuntur dentes, pennæ, reviviscunt, Plin.
units.tr: To sprout again] To sprout afresh, Col. To shoot again. The tree springs up again. It sprouts again from the root, Plin. The forest sprouts from the root, Virg. The limbs grow again, Lucr. Teeth and feathers grow again and come to life, Plin.

units.la: Rectâ] Cic. Directim pergere ad, Macrob. Prorsum Athenas ibo, Plaut. Prorsus, Cat. Protinus, Cic. Recta via, Ter. Sen. Ad lineam. Rectis lineis, Cic. In directo itineris sunt pedes, Var. vid. Perpendicum, vid. directè.
units.tr: Straight] Cic. To proceed straight towards, Macrob. I will go straight to Athens, Plaut. Straight on, Cato. Straightway, Cic. By the straight road, Ter., Sen. In a line. By straight lines, Cic. The feet are in a straight course of the journey, Varr. See Plumb-line; see Rightly.

units.la: Recta in rem] In limine diu detineri nemini volupe est. Proœmium longum audiendi cupido crux.
units.tr: Straight to the matter] Nobody likes to be kept long on the threshold. A long preamble is a torment to one eager to listen.

units.la: Rectè, vid. Benè.
units.tr: Rightly: see Well.

units.la: Rectè currere] Cursu contendere recto.
units.tr: To run straight] To race in a straight course.

units.la: Rectissimè agere] Momo satisfacere. Vel Momo judice.
units.tr: To act most rightly] To satisfy Momus. Or, with Momus as judge.

units.la: Rectitudo] Rectum : mens conscia recti, Virg.
units.tr: Rectitude] What is right: a mind conscious of rectitude, Virg.

units.la: Rector] Moderator rerum. Temperator. Administrator belli, Cic. Præses, Ovid. Prudens moderandi, Tac. Curator, Cic. Imperator vitæ & necis, Plin. Modiperator, Var.
units.tr: Ruler] A governor of affairs. A regulator. A director of war, Cic. A commander, Ovid. One skilled in governing, Tac. A curator, Cic. Lord of life and death, Plin. A helmsman, Varr.

units.la: Rector sit unus] Domus una non fert duos canes; neque duos gallos sterquilinium unum. Una arbor non capit duos erinaceos.
units.tr: There should be one ruler] One house does not bear two dogs; nor does one dunghill hold two cocks. One tree does not hold two hedgehogs.

units.la: Rectus] Directus passus, Tibul. Regularis, Plin. Prorsus limes, ad orientem directus, Fest. Simplex iter, Cic.
units.tr: Right] A straight step, Tibul. Regular, Plin. A straight boundary, directed to the east, Fest. A simple way, Cic.

units.la: Recubare, vid. Cubare.
units.tr: To lie down: see To lie.

units.la: Recudere] Conflare falces in enses, Virg. Diffingere ferrum nova incude, Hor.
units.tr: To beat again] To beat sickles into swords, Virg. To hammer iron anew on a fresh anvil, Hor.

units.la: Recuperare] Recipere urbem amissam. Pervenire ad suum, Cic. Reparare amissa, Lucr. Clarigare. Res raptas clarè repetere. Plin. Redipisci aliquid, Plaut. Postliminiò recipere, Paul. I C. Postliminio ad nos redeunt, quæ à nobis alienata sunt, Cic. Repetere res, bona, ex Cic. Evincere aliquid ab aliquo, Vlp.
units.tr: To recover] To regain a lost city. To come back into one's own, Cic. To restore what was lost, Lucr. To claim back openly, to demand clearly the goods seized, Plin.
