To get back something, Plaut. To recover by right of return, Paul, Jurist. What has been alienated from us returns to us by right of return, Cic. To reclaim goods and property, Cic. To win something from someone, Ulp.

units.la: Recuperatio] Reciperatio, Fest. Clarigatio, Arnob. Evictio, Vendicatio, actio in rem, Vlp. (Postliminium, est I. C. jus repetendi sua ejus, qui ab hostibus captus redit.)
units.tr: Recovery] Reclaiming, Fest. Demanding back by reprisal, Arnob. Eviction, vindication, an action for a thing, Ulp. (Postliminium is the right of jurists to reclaim their own goods, of one who returns after being captured by enemies.)

units.la: Recurvare] Aducum reddere, Col.
units.tr: To bend back] To make hooked, Col.

units.la: Recurvus] Recurvatus, Col. Reflexum telum, Sil. Camura cornua, Virg. In se redeuntia, Macrob. Obunca falx, Arnob. Obuncula cingula, Non. Conflexus, Plin.
units.tr: Curved back] Bent back, Col. A reflexed weapon, Sil. Curved horns, Virg. Turning back upon itself, Macrob. A hooked sickle, Arnob. Hooked girdles, Non. Bent, Plin.

units.la: Recusare] Recusare quod imperatur. Recusare de aliquâ re. Defugere munus. Refugere aliquid: à. Cic. Detrectare officium suum, Quint. certamen, Tac.
units.tr: To refuse] To refuse what is commanded. To refuse something. To shun a duty. To shrink from something, Cic. To decline one's duty, Quint. To decline a contest, Tac.

units.la: Recusatio] Detrectatio, Liv. Dedignatio parendi, Plin. Iun. Detrectatio officii, detrectator animus imperii.
units.tr: Refusal Disparagement, Liv. Disdain of obeying, Plin. Iun. Shirking of duty; a spirit that shirks command.

units.la: Recusatio fiſta] Accifmus. Accifare.
units.tr: Feigned refusal Accismus. To feign reluctance.

units.la: Redamare] Amori amore respondere. Respondere in amore iis, à quibus provocêre. Mutuò diligere. Tribuere alicui mutuam voluntatem. Mutuum in amicitia est, cùm par voluntas accipitur & redditur, Cic.
units.tr: To love in return To answer love with love. To answer in love those by whom one has been challenged. To love mutually. To give someone mutual goodwill. Affection is mutual in friendship when equal goodwill is received and returned, Cic.

units.la: Redarguere, vid. Confutare.
units.tr: To refute, see Confute.

units.la: Reddere] Retribuere debitum. Reponere alicui. Regerere, Cic. Redhibere, Plaut. Refundere quod acceperis, Vlp. Resignare, Hor. Remetire, Quint. Redonare, Hor.
units.tr: To give back To pay back what is due. To lay back upon someone. To throw back, Cic. To return what was bought, Plaut. To refund what you have received, Vlp. To unseal, Hor. To measure back, Quint. To give back as a gift, Hor.

units.la: Reddere rationem.] Reddere rationem vitæ. Respondere de suo officio alicui. Purgare se alicui de aliquo, Cic. Dare alicui rationem, Plaut. Causam dicere, Liv. vid. Excusare se.
units.tr: To give an account To give an account of one's life. To answer to someone for one's duty. To clear oneself to someone of something, Cic. To give someone an account, Plaut. To plead a case, Liv. See To excuse oneself.

units.la: Redemptio] Redemptura, Liv. (Paulò aliter sonat.)
units.tr: Redemption A contract for public works, Liv. (The sense is a little different.)

units.la: Redemptor] Assertor, Liv. Vindex libertatis, Cic.
units.tr: Redeemer A champion, Liv. A defender of liberty, Cic.

units.la: Redhostire, vid. Remunerari.
units.tr: To requite, see Remunerate.

units.la: Redigere] Redigere ad nihilum, Lucr. Ad vanum & irritum aliquid redigere, Liv. Ad nihilum recido, Cic. In cassum impensa recidit, Col. Ad irritum victoria revolvebatur, Tac. vid. Perducere.
units.tr: To reduce To reduce to nothing, Lucr. To bring something to nothing and void, Liv. I reduce to nothing, Cic. Expense comes to nothing in vain, Col. Victory was turned back to fruitlessness, Tac. See To bring through.

units.la: Redimere] Redemptare, Sipont. Redemptitare captos, Plaut. Repignerare, vel repignorare rem suam, Vlp. Reluere vestem, domum, Fest. Plaut.
units.tr: To redeem To ransom, Sipont. To ransom captives, Plaut. To pledge one's property again, Vlp. To redeem a garment or a house, Fest., Plaut.

units.la: Redire] Redire retrorsum, Plin. Redire à: ad, Plaut. Reversionem facere, Cic. Reverti domum, Ter. Reverti ad: in; Cic. Revertit ad me, Pomp. Revenire domum. Cic. Revenire ex, Tac. Revocare se; referre se ad studia pristina, intermissa. Recipere se: rursus in: ad, Cic. Revehi equo. Reddere dere se alicui rei, convivio, Liv. Revocare gradum, pedem. Recursare, Virg. Recurrere ad initia, Cic. Retroire, Plin. Dare vela retrorsum. Iterare causas relictas, Hor. Redambulare, Plaut. Repedare, Lucil. Revolare ad, Paterc. Repetere castra, Liv. Revolvi ad ; in : Remigrare ad : in : Regredi, Cic. Regredi ad, Quint. Remeare, Var. Retroferre se, Sen. Relegere iter, Stat. Remetiri mare, Virg. Relabi in. Renare, Hor. Renavigare, Cic.
units.tr: To return To return backwards, Plin. To return from or to, Plaut. To make a return visit, Cic. To go home again, Ter. To return to or into, Cic. It comes back to me, Pomp. To come home again, Cic. To come back out of, Tac. To withdraw oneself and turn back to former studies, long abandoned. To retreat back into or to, Cic. To ride back on horseback. To give oneself back to a thing or to a feast, Liv. To take back a step or a foot. To run back, Virg. To run back to beginnings, Cic. To go backwards, Plin. To set sail backwards. To repeat abandoned cases, Hor. To walk back, Plaut. To come back on foot, Lucil. To fly back to, Paterc. To pitch camp again, Liv. To flow back to or into; to migrate back to or into; to go back, Cic. To go back to, Quint. To go back again, Var. To carry oneself back, Sen. To retrace one's journey, Stat. To cross the sea again, Virg. To slip back into. To swim back, Hor. To sail back, Cic.

units.la: Redire ad intermissa mala] Relabi. Redire ad vomitum. Redire ad ingenium, Ter. Ad se & suos mores redire, Cic. Recipere se ad ingenium suum, Plaut. Revolvi in eamdem vitam.
units.tr: To return to former evils To slip back. To return to one's vomit. To return to one's old nature, Ter. To return to oneself and one's own habits, Cic. To take oneself back to one's nature, Plaut. To roll back into the same life.

units.la: Redire ad meliorem mentem] Redire ad bonam frugem, Lamp. Redire in viam. Mutare mentem, Cic. mores, Ter. vitam, Lucr. Applicare se ad frugem, Plaut. Receptus à malis consiliis, Liv.
units.tr: To return to a better mind To return to good conduct, Lamp. To return to the right path. To change one's mind, Cic.; one's manners, Ter.; one's life, Lucr. To apply oneself to good conduct, Plaut. Withdrawn from bad counsels, Liv.

units.la: Redire in patriam] Revenire domum, Cic. Reducem esse, Id. Repatriare, Solin.
units.tr: To return to one's country To come home again, Cic. To be one who has come back, Id. To repatriate, Solin.

units.la: Reditus] Reditio : Celeritas reditionis. Reversio febrium. Recursus ad pristinum ordinem. Regressus & progressus. Regressio & profectio, Cic. Reverticulum solis. Remeaculum, Apul. Receptus à : receptus pertinacis sententiæ, Liv Reciprocatio fili à culmine & rursus à terrâ, Plin. Domuitio : nec larem requiro, nec domuitionem paro, Pacuv. Apul. (domum itio, Lamb. apud Cic.
units.tr: Return A going back. Speed of return. The recurrence of fevers. A return to the former order. Going back and going forward. Going back and departing, Cic. The turning point of the sun. A place to come back to, Apul. A withdrawal to or from; the withdrawal of a stubborn opinion, Liv. The backward and forward motion of a thread from the top to the ground, Plin. Homecoming: "I seek neither hearth nor homecoming, nor do I prepare a return," Pacuv., Apul. (domum itio, Lamb. apud Cic.)

units.la: Redivivus] Qui resumpsit animam, Sen.
units.tr: Restored to life One who has taken up breath again, Sen.

units.la: Reducere aliquem] Retroducere, Mart. Inducere in viam, Viam. Deducere in viam, Cic. Reconciliare filium domum, Plaut. i. reducere, Lamb. Officii causâ aliquem ab domo prosequi, Liv.
units.tr: To lead someone back To lead back again, Mart. To lead into the way, Viam. To lead down the way, Cic. To bring a son home again and reconcile him, Plaut. I.e. to lead back, Lamb. To accompany someone from home out of courtesy, Liv.

units.la: Redundare vid. Superest.
units.tr: To overflow, see To be left over.

units.la: Refectio] Valet refectioni, Cic. Refectus, Plin.
units.tr: Refreshment It serves for refreshment, Cic. Refreshed, Plin.

units.la: Refellere, vid. Confutare.
units.tr: To refute, see Confute.

units.la: Referendarius] Supplicum libellorum magister, Bud. Ab ore Principis, Vrsin. A libellis, Suet. Proximus libellorum, Amm. Magister memoriæ, Meurs.
units.tr: Referendary Master of the petitions of suppliants, Bud. From the mouth of the Prince, Ursin. Of petitions, Suet. Next in charge of the petitions, Amm. Master of memory, Meurs.

units.la: Referire] Repetere mulam calce, Sen Resævire, Ovid.
units.tr: To kick back To kick back with the heel like a mule, Sen. To rage again, Ovid.

units.la: Referre] Reportare, Cic. Retroferre, Sen.
units.tr: To bring back To carry back, Cic. To carry backwards, Sen.

units.la: Referre par pari] Æmulari cum aliquo, Liv. Tendere odiis, Virg. vid. Retaliare.
units.tr: To return like for like To vie with someone, Liv. To press on with hatreds, Virg. See Retaliate.

units.la: Refert] Pluma haud interest, Plaut. Permultum interest. Multum mea interest. Permagni, magni interest. Magni, permagni refert. Permagna res agitur, Cic. Perminimum interest, Ter. Momentum in re aliquâ positum est, Quint.
units.tr: It matters A feather's difference, Plaut. It matters very much. It matters much to me. It matters greatly, very greatly. It is of very great, great importance. A very great matter is at stake, Cic. It matters very little, Ter. The turning point lies in the matter, Quint.

units.la: Refertus, vid. Fartus. Reficere, vid. Corrigere, Reparare. Recreare.
units.tr: To make again, see Correct, Repair, Refresh.

units.la: Reflexus, vid. Recurvus.
units.tr: Bent back, see Recurved.

units.la: Refluit mare] Reciprocatur, Curt. Resorbet mare æstum, Lucr. Fluctûs, Ovid. Alternis æstibus reciprocans fluctus alluit aggestionem littoris, Pallad.
units.tr: The sea ebbs It is turned back, Curt. The sea draws back its tide, Lucr. Waves, Ovid. The waves, alternating with the tides, wash the heap of the shore, Pallad.

units.la: Refocillare, vid. Recreare. Reformare, vid. Reparare. Emendare.
units.tr: To refresh, see Refresh. To reform, see Repair, Amend.

units.la: Reformatio, vid. Renovatio.
units.tr: Reformation, see Renewal.

units.la: Refractarius] Perduellis spiritus, Amm. Rebellis. Stat. Retrorsæ mentes, Lampr. Vid. Contumax.
units.tr: Refractory A rebellious spirit, Amm. Rebellious, Stat. Turned-back minds, Lampr. See Stubborn.

units.la: Refractarius equus] Duri oris, Ovid.
units.tr: Refractory horse Hard-mouthed, Ovid.

units.la: Refragari, vid. Contradicere.
units.tr: To gainsay, see Contradict.

units.la: Refrigerare] Ventilare & refrigerare vinum. Refrigerationem auræ captare, Col. Reficere se ex caloribus, Cic. Perfrigerare, Plin. Obsipare, aspergere alicui aquulam. Frigefactare. vel Frigidefactare, Plaut. Lambin. Refrigerari aquis, umbris, Cic. Passivè.
units.tr: To cool To fan and cool wine. To seek a cooling breeze, Col. To refresh oneself from the heat, Cic. To chill thoroughly, Plin. To sprinkle someone with a little water. To make cold, Plaut., Lambin. To be cooled by waters and shade, Cic. (Passive.)

units.la: Refrigeratorius] Refrigeratrix natura, Plin. Frigidaria cella, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Cooling A nature that cools, Plin. A cooling room, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Refrigeratus] Teporatum vitri fragmentum, Plin. Tepidus, Plaut.
units.tr: Cooled A lukewarm fragment of glass, Plin. Tepid, Plaut.

units.la: Refugium] Perfugium, Profugium, Receptaculum, Receptus, Receptator locus latronum, Nationum portus, Ara, Diverticulum insidiarum, Cic. Asylum, Virg. Suffugium, Confugium, Ovid.
units.tr: Refuge Shelter, retreat, receptacle, a harbour of robbers, a port of nations, an altar, a hiding-place for ambush, Cic. Asylum, Virg. A place of shelter or flight, Ovid.

units.la: Refutare] Elidere argumenta, vid. Confutare.
units.tr: To refute To crush arguments, see Confute.

units.la: Regalis] Regius apparatus, Cic. Regificus luxus, Virg. Basilicum facinus, Plaut. vid. Magnificus.
units.tr: Royal Royal display, Cic. Kingly luxury, Virg. Regal crime, Plaut. See Magnificent.

units.la: Regaliter] Regiè. Regificè, Cic. Basilicè, Plaut.
units.tr: Royally Like a king, Cic. In a kingly manner, Plaut.

units.la: Regelare] Zephyrus regelat brumam, Col. Zephyri minuunt frigora, Ovid.
units.tr: To freeze again The west wind brings back the frost, Col. The zephyrs lessen the cold, Ovid.

units.la: Regelari] Ætas mea vix mediâ regelatur æstate, Sen. Regelare sinantur vites, Col.
units.tr: To be frozen again My age is scarcely thawed in the middle of summer, Sen. The vines are allowed to be frozen again, Col.

units.la: Regere] Gubernare, Gerere Remp. Moderari aliquid, Cic. Alicui, Tac. Moderari frena, Iuv. Temperare Remp. Administrare. Præsidere urbi. Gubernacula tractare, tenere. Ad gubernacula sedere. Clavum, summam imperii tenere. Tenere Remp. Cic. Quo natura aurigatur, Var. Exercere imperium, Virg.
units.tr: To rule To steer, to conduct affairs of state. To govern something, Cic.; someone, Tac. To control the reins, Juv. To temper the state. To administer. To preside over a city. To handle or hold the helm. To sit at the helm. To hold the rudder and the chief command. To hold the state, Cic. By which nature is driven like a charioteer, Var. To exercise command, Virg.

units.la: Regere seipsum] Clavum tenere sui. Imperare sibi, animo, cupiditati, Cic.
units.tr: To rule oneself To hold the rudder of oneself. To command oneself, one's mind, one's desires, Cic.

units.la: Regere seipsum nescit] Vertumnô natus iniquo.
units.tr: He cannot rule himself Born under the unkind Vertumnus.

units.la: Regimen, vid. Moderamen.
units.tr: Rule, see Moderation.

units.la: Regina] Regnatrix, Tac. Iuno.
units.tr: Queen A ruler, Tac. Juno.

units.la: Regis filia] Regia virgo.
units.tr: King's daughter A royal maiden.

units.la: Regio] Ora. Pars terrarum. Plaga cœli, Cic. Tractus, Virg. Terra, Plin. Abire in ultimas terras, Cic. Civitas: tota Helvetia civitas in quatuor pagos distributa, Cæs. Turneb. Templum; templa cœli, Virg. Cœlum, Col. Cœlum, non animos mutant, qui trans mare currunt, Hor. Orbis, Ovid. Plin.
units.tr: Region A shore; a part of the lands; a quarter of the sky, Cic. A tract, Virg. Land, Plin. To go to the farthest lands, Cic. A state: the whole of Helvetia is a state divided into four cantons, Caes., Turneb. A temple; temples of the heavens, Virg. The sky, Col. Those who run across the sea change their sky, not their minds, Hor. The world, Ovid., Plin.

units.la: Registrum, barb.] Inventarium, Repertorium, Synopsis bonorum, Vlp. Index bonorum. Regestum, Bud. Rationarium imperii, Suet. Perscriptio, Cic. vid. Rationarius Codex.
units.tr: Register, barbarous word: An inventory, a repertory, a synopsis of goods, Vlp. An index of goods. A register, Bud. An account-book of the empire, Suet. An enrolment, Cic. See Account Book.

units.la: Regnare] Regnum obtinere, Cæs. Possidere, Ter. Exercere regnum, Plin. Sceptra tenere. Potiri sceptris, Virg. Potiri sceptra, Lucr. vid. Dominari.
units.tr: To reign To hold a kingdom, Caes. To possess, Ter. To exercise a kingdom, Plin. To hold the sceptre. To wield sceptres, Virg.; Lucr. See To dominate.

units.la: Regula] Canon, Plin. Normula, Sipont. Linea, Vitr.
units.tr: Rule A canon, Plin. A little rule, Sipont. A line, Vitr.

units.la: Regula infallibilis] Norma Polyeteri.
units.tr: Infallible rule The norm of Polyeteris.

units.la: Regula regat, non regatur] Amussi applica lapidem, non contrà.
units.tr: The rule rules, it is not ruled Apply the stone to the rule, not the rule to the stone.

units.la: Rejectaneus] Rejiculus dies, Sen. Abactus, Hor. Reprobus nummus, Vlp.
units.tr: Rejected A rejected day, Sen. A cast-off, Hor. A reprobate coin, Vlp.

units.la: Rejectio] Rejectio judicum, Cic. Abjectio literarum. Improbatio testium, ad Heren. Rejectus, Cæs. Regestus terræ, Col. Reprobatio.
units.tr: Rejection Rejection of judges, Cic. Discarding of letters. Disapproval of witnesses, ad Heren. Rejected, Caes. Dumped earth, Col. Reprobation.

units.la: Rejectus] Præteritus, Cic. Exauctorata & repudiata verba, Gell. Reprobatus, Scæv.
units.tr: Rejected Passed over, Cic. Words discharged and rejected, Gell. Reproved, Scaev.

units.la: Rejicere] Abjicere arma, Cic. vid. Repudiare.
units.tr: To reject To cast away arms, Cic. See Repudiate.

units.la: Relatio, vid. Narratio. Relator, vid. Narrator.
units.tr: Report, see Narration. Reporter, see Narrator.

units.la: Relaxare] Frena laxare populis, Lucan. Dare frena alicui, Sen. Effundere habenas, Virg. Remittere habenas amicitiæ. Permittere omnia, Cic.
units.tr: To loosen To loosen the reins for the peoples, Lucan. To give the reins to someone, Sen. To pour out the reins, Virg. To let go the reins of friendship. To allow everything, Cic.

units.la: Relaxatio] Remissio. Indulgentia, Cic.
units.tr: Relaxation Remission. Indulgence, Cic.

units.la: Relegare aliquem] Exilio afficere. In exilium ejicere. Pellere. Sedibus expellere, Cic. Dare in exilium, Firm. Protelare patria, Turpil.
units.tr: To relegate someone To punish with exile. To cast into exile. To drive away. To expel from one's seat, Cic. To give into exile, Firm. To banish from one's country, Turpil.

units.la: Relegatio, vid. Exilium.
units.tr: Relegation, see Exile.

units.la: Religio] Pietas erga deos. Cultus deorum. Cerimoniæ religionesque in deos, Cic. Religiositas, Apul.
units.tr: Religion Piety towards the gods. Worship of the gods. Ceremonies and religious observances towards the gods, Cic. Religiousness, Apul.

units.la: Religiosè] Religiosissimè. Summâ religione cerimoniâque conficere sacra. Piè sanctéque colere deos, Cic. Reverentissimè colit ceremonias, Suet.
units.tr: Religiously Most religiously. To perform sacred rites with the greatest devotion and ceremony. To worship the gods piously and holily, Cic. He observes ceremonies most reverently, Suet.

units.la: Religiosè consultare] Apud aram consultare.
units.tr: To consult religiously To consult at the altar.

units.la: Religiosus] Vir religionibus deditus. Qui colit religionem. Religionem colens. Summâ religione præditus. Exemplar antiquæ religionis, Cic. Numa religiosior, Er.
units.tr: Religious A man devoted to religion. One who worships religiously. Endowed with the highest religion. A model of ancient religion, Cic. Numa more religious, Er.

units.la: Relinere dolium] Promere de pleno, Plaut. Partem sumere de solido, Hor. Adtegrare vinum, Fest.
units.tr: To draw wine from a cask To take from the full, Plaut. To take a portion from the solid, Hor. To unseal a cask, Fest.

units.la: Relinquere] Reliquum aliquid facere. Prodere laudem posteris, Cic. Desistere aliquem, Apul.
units.tr: To leave To make something a remainder. To hand praise down to posterity, Cic. To desist from someone, Apul.

units.la: Relinquere assueta difficile] Canis assuetus corio.
units.tr: To leave accustomed things behind is hard: a dog accustomed to leather.

units.la: Reliquiæ] Reliquia, æ, Apul. Residua pecunia, Liv. Extima limitum, Amm. Superamenta materiarum, Vlp. Analecta mensarum, Mart. De fæce haurire, Cic. Subsecivum agri, Var. Admonitio morbi, Plin.
units.tr: Remnants: Reliquia, ae, Apul. Residual money, Liv. Outlying boundary marks of the frontiers, Amm. Leftover materials, Vlp. Scraps from the tables, Mart. To drain from the dregs, Cic. A remnant plot of land, Var. A warning of illness, Plin.

units.la: Reliquiæ alicujus magnæ rei] Colossi fragmenta.
units.tr: Remains of some great thing: fragments of a colossus.

units.la: Reliquiæ cibi] Quod satietati superfuit, Cic.
units.tr: Remains of food: what was left over after hunger was satisfied, Cic.

units.la: Reliquias colligere] Aristas colligere aliquot ex opimâ messe, nemo prohibeat.
units.tr: To gather up remnants: no one would forbid gathering a few ears of grain from a rich harvest.

units.la: Reliquum] Cæterum omne, Liv. Extremum anni, Tac. Residuum, Paul. I.C. Summa senectus, Cic. Reliqua Græcia, pro reliqua pars Græciæ, Cic.
units.tr: Reliquum: all the rest, Liv. The end of the year, Tac. What remains, Paul. I.C. The final stage of old age, Cic. The rest of Greece, that is, the remaining part of Greece, Cic.

units.la: Reliquus, qui post alios relinquitur] Relictus. Superstes, Cic. Residuus, Liv. Imperditus, Virg. Vitalis, pro superstite, Hor. Inconsumptus, Ovid. Posthumus, Apul. Super, pro Superest : Nec spes ulla super, Valer. Flacc. Reluctari, vid. Reniti. Reluctatio] Obluctatio, Firm. Renixus cartilaginis, Cels. Nisus pedum, Lucr. Remanere] Manere, Residere, Restare, Redundare in annum sequentem. Exstat memoria, Cic. Superesse, Cirg. Superare, Liv. Hærescere, Lucr. Remansio] Mansio, Cic. Remedium] Medicina dolorum, Stat. vid. Medicamentum. Auxilium. Remedium ineptum] Calceus à podagrâ non liberat. Remedio opus] Non luctu, sed remedio opus : est in malis. Remex seu Remiges] Remigium, pro remigibus, Cic. Hor. Classicus, Curt. Navales socii, Liv. Navales pedes, Plaut. Equiso nauticus, Var. Auriga carinæ, Charis. Nauta, & Navita, Cic. Mesonauta, Rud. Reminisci, vid. Recordari. Remissio, vid. Venia. Remittere, vid. Ignoscere. Remittere de suo jure] Propria vineta cædere. Remora] Ægermoræ, Lucan. Virg. Multos dies hanc epistolam habui, propter commorationem tabellariorum, Cic. Remeligo, Plaut. Fest. Remorari, vid. Retardare. Remotio] Remotio criminis. Abalienatio alicujus rei. Amotio, depulsio doloris. Propulsatio periculi. Alienatio sacrorum, Cic. Amolitio alicujus rei ex oculis, Gell. Remotus] Disjunctus : disjunctissima terra. Longè, & longissimè remotus. Remotissimus à, vel ab. Longissimè abest à. Longinquus, Cic. Dissitus, Apul. Distans, Liv. Sepositus, Mart. Removere] Moliri naves à terrâ, Liv. Remunerari] Remunerari suppliciis aliquem, Cat. Remunerari officia beneficiis. Remunerari aliquem cum simillimo munere. Referre alicui gratiam. Respondere beneficiis alicui: amore:in amore:amore amori, Cic. Respondere meritis, Hor. Referre gratiam, & gratias, Plaut. Rependere gratiam, Ovid.
units.tr: Reliquus, what is left behind after others: left over. Surviving, Cic. Remaining, Liv. Unlost, Virg. Alive, in place of surviving, Hor. Unconsumed, Ovid. Posthumous, Apul. Super, in place of superest: "nor is there any hope left," Valer. Flacc. To struggle against, see Reniti. Struggling against: resistance, Firm. A twisting back of the cartilage, Cels. A pressing of the feet, Lucr. To remain: to stay, to sit still, to stand, to overflow into the following year. The record survives, Cic. To be left over, Cic. To be left over, Liv. To stick fast, Lucr. Remaining: a staying, Cic. Remedy: a medicine for pain, Stat., see Medicament, Help. An unsuitable remedy: a shoe does not free one from gout. A remedy is needed: not mourning but a remedy is needed in evils. Oarsman or oarsmen: the oar-men for the rowers, Cic., Hor. Fleet, Curt. Naval comrades, Liv. Naval feet, Plaut. A naval horse, Var. The charioteer of the keel, Charis. Sailor and navigator, Cic. A half-sailor, Rud. To recall, see Remember. Remission, see Pardon. To remit, see Forgive. To remit one's own right: to cut down one's own vines. Delay: a hindrance by the slowness of a sort, Lucan., Virg. I have held this letter for many days because of the delay of the couriers, Cic. To delay, Plaut., Fest. To delay, see Retard. Removal: removal of a charge; alienation of something; taking away, driving off of grief; warding off of danger; alienation of sacred things, Cic. Removing something from sight, Gell. Removed: separated; the most distant land; far, and very far removed. Most remote from, or by. Far away from. Remote, Cic. Distant, Apul. Distant, Liv. Set apart, Mart. To remove: to launch ships from land, Liv. To reward: to reward someone with punishments, Cat. To reward services with benefits. To reward someone with a most similar gift. To return thanks to someone. To answer benefits with kindness; love with love, Cic. To answer merits, Hor. To return thanks and thanks, Plaut. To repay thanks, Ovid.

units.la: Refundere beneficium, Sen. Redhostire, Fest. Remunerare, pensare, persolvere beneficium. Reponere merita. Rependere officia. Parem esse beneficiis acceptis. Efficiam ut tuum ad te beneficium non sine fœnore redeat. Fœneratum hoc beneficium tibi pulchrè dices. Dispeream nisi tibi beneficium istud conduplicaverit. Statim regerere beneficium est nolentis debere. Certemus mutuis inter nos officiis. Cum fœnore reponendum cùm acceperis. Quisquis grate munus accipit, jam gratiam retulit, Er.
units.tr: To repay a benefit, Sen. To pay back, Fest. To reward, weigh, and discharge a benefit. To return merits. To repay services. To be equal to the benefits received. I shall make your benefit return to you with interest. You will fittingly call this benefit one that bears interest. May I perish if that benefit has not doubled for you. To return a benefit at once is to be unwilling to be indebted. Let us vie with one another in mutual services. Repay with interest when you have received. Whoever gladly receives a gift has already returned thanks, Erasm.

units.la: Remuneratio] Relatio gratiæ, Sen. Meritorum, Quint. Studiorum officiorumque vicissitudo, Cic. Hostimentum, Plaut. Antidotum, Vlp.
units.tr: Remuneration: a return of thanks, Sen. Of merits, Quint. The interchange of studies and services, Cic. A requital, Plaut. An antidote, Vlp.

units.la: Remurmurare, vid. Obmurmurare.
units.tr: Remurmurare, see Obmurmurare.

units.la: Remus] Pes navalis, Non.
units.tr: Remus: a naval oar, Non.

units.la: Remutare, vid. Mutare.
units.tr: Remutare, see Mutare.

units.la: Renasci] Reseminat seipsam ales, Ovid. vid. Recrescere.
units.tr: Renasci: the phoenix renews itself, Ovid. See Recrescere.

units.la: Reniti] Obniti undis, Lucr. Obsistere, Reluctari, Hor. Resistere immobilem, Plin. Obstare audaciter alicui. Repugnare valdè. Prætor improbus cui nemo interdicere possit. Excipere, sustinere impetum alicujus, Cic. Sufferre vim, nec claustra, nec custodes valent. Obluctari alicui, Virg. Subsistere aliquem, Liv. (Proobsistere alicui) Insistere, Ter. Adversus resistere, Æmil. Prob.
units.tr: Reniti: to strive against the waves, Lucr. To resist, to struggle against, Hor. To withstand immovably, Plin. To stand boldly against someone. To resist strongly. A praetor, shameless, whom no one can forbid. To receive and withstand someone's onslaught, Cic. To bear force, neither bars nor guards can prevent it. To struggle against someone, Virg. To withstand someone, Liv. (To oppose someone) To press on, Ter. To resist opposition, Aemil. Prob.

units.la: Renovare] Revocare morem. Instaurare proscriptionem. Novare. Refricare desiderium, Refricat lippitudo (pro refricatur.) Redintegrare memoriam, Cic. Innovare terrorem. Reparare, Recolere intermissa, Liv. Dare novitatem vetustis, Plin. Retractare. Retardescere. Restringere luctus. Rescindere carmina (retractare,) Ovid. Retentare memoriam, Sen. Reconflatur sensus, Lucr. Recreari incipit res, Id. Integrare inimicitiam, Pacuv. Integrascit malum, Ter.
units.tr: Renovare: to revive a custom. To renew a proscription. To make new. To rekindle a desire; the sore eye rekindles (for "is rekindled"). To restore a memory, Cic. To renew terror. To repair, to revive things that have lapsed, Liv. To give novelty to old things, Plin. To take up again, to grow fresh again, to slacken, to check mourning. To rewrite poems (to take up again), Ovid. To try the memory again, Sen. The sense is rekindled, Lucr. The matter begins to revive, Id. To renew enmity, Pacuv. The evil grows worse again, Ter.

units.la: Renovate dolorem] Refricare cicatricem obductam : vulnus : dolorem. Recrudescit vulnus, Cic. Reglliscit dolor, Plaut. Redulcerare, Col.
units.tr: Renew the pain: to rub open a healed scar: the wound, the pain. The wound breaks out again, Cic. The pain flares up again, Plaut. To make sore again, Col.

units.la: Renovatio] Restauratio, Iulian. I.C. Reintegratio amoris. ris. Instauratio ludorum, Cic. Reformatio omnium rerum in mundo, Apul. Novatio, Vlp. Novatus, Virg. Renovamen formæ, Ovid.
units.tr: Renovatio: restoration, Iulian. I.C. Renewal of love. Restoration of games, Cic. Reformation of all things in the world, Apul. Renewal, Vlp. Renewed, Virg. Renewal of beauty, Ovid.

units.la: Renumerare, vid. Annumerare.
units.tr: Renumerare, see Annumerare.

units.la: Renunciare, vid. Nunciare. Renuere, vid. Abnuere.
units.tr: Renunciare, see Nunciare. Renuere, see Abnuere.

units.la: Repandus sursum recurvus] Obuncum rostrum vulturis, Claud. Reduncus, Ovid. Resima labra, Recurvum rostrum, Col.
units.tr: Repandus, bent back upward: the hooked beak of a vulture, Claud. Curved back, Ovid. Turned-back lips, a curved beak, Col.

units.la: Reparare] Reficere opus, ædes. Restituere ædes, quæ vitium fecerunt. Reconcinnare ædificia, Cic. Concinnare, Cat. Col. Reparare in melius vetustate sublapsa, Plin. Iun. Instaurare, Fest. Restaurare theatrum, Tac. Aptare aliquid in aliquâ re, Col. Sarcire, est integrum facere, præstare, Fest. Reformare, Plin. Iun. Emendare, Corrigere, Cic. Corrigere ad frugem, Plaut. Marginare vas, Liv. Munitare viam, Cic. Instaurare vias, iter, Stat.
units.tr: Reparare: to redo a work or building. To restore a building that has suffered damage. To patch up buildings, Cic. To put together, Cat. Col. To repair for the better what has fallen through age, Plin. Iun. To renew, Fest. To restore a theatre, Tac. To fit something into something, Col. To mend, is to make whole, to supply, Fest. To reform, Plin. Iun. To amend, to correct, Cic. To bring back to honesty, Plaut. To rim a vessel, Liv. To fortify a road, Cic. To restore roads or a journey, Stat.

units.la: Repellere, vid. Abigere.
units.tr: Repellere, see Abigere.

units.la: Rependere] Repensare, Paterc. Compensare damna. Resarcire damnum. Sarcire damna, Col. Reconcinnare detrimenta, Cæs. Exsarcire suum sumptum, Ter. Impendium usque ad assem reddere, Plin. Iun. Præstare damnum alicui, Cic. Resolvere, Cato. Paria facere, Sen. Reficitur, Var. Repræsentatur labor sapientia. Bud. Recompensare, Latinis inusitatum, vid. Remunerari.
units.tr: Rependere: to weigh out again, Paterc. To make up for losses. To make good a loss. To make good expenses, Col. To make good a loss, Caes. To repay one's own expenditure, Ter. To pay back an expense down to the last penny, Plin. Iun. To pay damage to someone, Cic. To settle, Cato. To make equal, Sen. It is repaid, Var. Labour is repaid by wisdom. Budé. Recompensare, not used in Latin, see Remunerari.

units.la: Repentè, vid. Subitò. Repentinus, vid. Subitaneus.
units.tr: Repentè, see Subitò. Repentinus, see Subitaneus.

units.la: Repercussio, Philosophis recent. Plin. vid. Repercussus solis, caloris.
units.tr: Repercussio, recent philosophers. Plin. See Repercussus solis, caloris.

units.la: Repercutere] Refringitur radius solis alicui rei immissus, Plin. Referitur Pœbus opposito speculo, Ovid. A speculo in speculum transfertur imago: è spec. transfertur in speculum, Lucr. Radii solis replicantur: acies radios replicat ab, Sen.
units.tr: Repercutere: a ray of sunlight is refracted when it strikes something, Plin. Phoebus is reflected by an opposing mirror, Ovid. The image is carried from mirror to mirror, Lucr. The rays of the sun are reflected back, Sen.

units.la: Repere] Reptare, Hor. Reptabundus sequor, Sen. Perreptare, Ter.
units.tr: Repere: to creep, Hor. I follow crawling along, Sen. To creep through, Ter.

units.la: Repere genibus] Reptare per manus & genua, Quint. Suffraginibus insidentes, Amm. Genibus volutans, Virg. Poplitibus subsidendo ima clivorum pervadere, Amm.
units.tr: Repere genibus: to crawl on hands and knees, Quint. Sitting on the backs of the knees, Amm. Rolling on the knees, Virg. Sinking down on the hams to traverse the lowest slopes of the hills, Amm.

units.la: Reperire, vid. Invenire.
units.tr: Reperire, see Invenire.

units.la: Reperitur] Comparet, Liv. Est invenire, Gell. Erit ubi te ulciscar, si vivo, Plaut.
units.tr: Reperitur: appears, Liv. It can be found, Gell. There will be a place where I shall avenge you, if I live, Plaut.

units.la: Repertitius] Indagabilis, Var.
units.tr: Repertitius: discoverable, Var.

units.la: Repertor, Repertum, vid. Inventor, Inventum.
units.tr: Repertor, Repertum, see Inventor, Inventum.

units.la: Repetere] Ingeminare, Virg. Reassumere aliquid, Plin. Iterare. Referre rem judicatam. Recolere artes, ex Cic. Retractare, Identidem aliquid revocando me pronuncio, Cic. Integrare pugnam, Liv.
units.tr: Repetere: to repeat, Virg. To take up again something, Plin. To iterate. To refer a judged matter again. To revive the arts, cf. Cic. To retract, by repeatedly calling something back I affirm myself, Cic. To renew the battle, Liv.

units.la: Repetere eadem] Eadem obgannire, Plaut. Cantilenam eandem canere, Ter. Eâdem oberrare lyrâ, chordâ. Eadem per eadem dicere. Eandem incudem tundere. Obtundere de eadem re sæpius, Ter.
units.tr: Repetere eadem: to babble the same things again, Plaut. To sing the same tune, Ter. To wander over the same lyre or string. To say the same things through the same things. To beat the same anvil. To harp on the same matter more often, Ter.

units.la: Repetitio] Iteratio. Geminatio, conduplicatio verborum, Instauratio ludorum, Cic. Reiteratio, Quint. Duplicatio, Sen.
units.tr: Repetitio: iteration. Doubling, repetition of words, a renewal of games, Cic. Reiteration, Quint. Duplication, Sen.

units.la: Repetitio eorundem odiosa] Crambe bis cocta. Cavendum ne id, quod suprasemel diximus, deinceps dicamus, Cic.
units.tr: Tiresome repetition of the same things: cabbage boiled twice. Take care not to say afterwards what we have already said above, Cic.

units.la: Repetundarum damnare] Cic. Damnare de repetundis, Id. Litem alicui æstimare, Id. Bud.
units.tr: To condemn for extortion: Cic. To condemn on a charge of extortion, Id. To assess damages against someone, Id. Budé.

units.la: Replere. vid. Implere.
units.tr: Replere, see Implere.

units.la: Reposcere] Poscere, admonere debitorem. Flagitare, exigere ab aliquo promissum. Repetere alicui promissa. Deposcere aliquem ad ab aliquo. Deposcere, Cic. Deposcere in poenam, Liv. Appellare aliquem pecuniæ, & de pecuniâ, Cic. pecuniâ, Quint. Interpellare debitorem, Pompon Reflagitare aliquid, Catul.
units.tr: Reposcere: to demand, to remind a debtor. To press, to exact from someone a promise. To demand again promises from someone. To summon someone for something from someone. To demand, Cic. To demand as punishment, Liv. To appeal to someone for money, and about money, Cic. About money, Quint. To importune a debtor, Pompon. To demand something back again, Catul.

units.la: Repositorium] Thesaurus omnium rerum memoria. Receptaculum prædæ. Theca vasorum, Cic. Conditorium, Quint. Conditum, Amm. Repositio ligni, Pallad.
units.tr: Repositorium: a storehouse of all things in memory. A receptacle for plunder. A case for vessels, Cic. A place of storage, Quint. Something stored, Amm. A putting away of wood, Pallad.

units.la: Repotia] Repotria (à reportandâ sponsâ) legit ap. Hor. Landin. Repotatio, Var. Instauratitius dies epularum, Macrob.
units.tr: Repotia: a feast on the bride's return home (from "bringing back the bride"), read in Hor., Landin. Repeated drinking, Var. A renewed day of feasting, Macrob.

units.la: Repræsentare aliquem] Effingere mores alicujus. Exprimere aliquem imitando: sermones, mores aliorum. Respondere alicui. Reddidit Clodius omnes Catilinas. Verbis & sono ipso persequi & imitari aliquem. Imitari & exprimere aliquem virum. Consequi aliquem imitatione, Cic. Referre mores patris. Exscribere patrem similitudine, Plin. Plin. Iun. Refert ore patentem, Virg. Agere naufragum, Quint. Reddere exemplum & effigiem, Liv. Assimilare aliquos colores, Ovid. Adumbrare morem alicujus, Curt. Repræsentare faciem, Col. imaginem sceleris, Quint.
units.tr: To represent someone: to portray a person's character. To express someone by imitating: the speech and character of others. To answer someone. Clodius gave back all the Catilines. To pursue and imitate someone with the very words and sound. To imitate and express a man. To follow someone by imitation, Cic. To bring back a father's character. To copy a father in likeness, Plin. Iun. He brings back a man with open mouth, Virg. To act a shipwrecked man, Quint. To render an example and likeness, Liv. To assimilate some colours, Ovid. To sketch the manner of someone, Curt. To represent a face, Col. an image of a crime, Quint.

units.la: Reprehendere, vid. Vituperare.
units.tr: Reprehendere, see Vituperare.

units.la: Reprehensurus alium vitiô careat ipse] Loripedem rectus derideat. Turpe est Doctori cùm culpa redarguit ipsum, Cat. Mirum est bellum cùm culpat asellus asellum. Aliorum vult esse medicus, & ipse ulcerib.scatet.
units.tr: Let him who would rebuke another be free of fault himself. Let the straight-limbed man laugh at the lame. It is shameful for a teacher when his own fault refutes him, Cat. It is strange when a donkey finds fault with a donkey. He wants to be a doctor to others, yet he himself is covered in sores.

units.la: Reprehensio, vid. Objurgatio.
units.tr: Reprehensio, see Objurgatio.

units.la: Reprimere aliquem] Rejicere hostem ab aliquo loco. Repulsam alicui afferre, Cic. Obsistere ventis, fugienti, Ovid. Submovere mare, Sen.
units.tr: To repel someone: to drive an enemy away from a place. To deal a repulse to someone, Cic. To resist the winds, or a fleeing man, Ovid. To hold back the sea, Sen.

units.la: Reprobare] Improbare judicium, Cic. vid Seqq. & Improbare.
units.tr: Reprobare: to disapprove of a judgment, Cic. See the following and Improbare.

units.la: Repudiare aliquid] Repudiare funditus. Respuere consolationem, Cic. conditionem, Cæs. Rejicere, Recusare judicem Abrogare legem. Explodere sententiam. Repulsam ferre ab aliquo, Cicero. Abdicare & rejicere, Pompon. Abnegare comitem, Horat. Vertere pollicem, Juv.
units.tr: Repudiare aliquid: to repudiate utterly. To reject a consolation, Cic.; a condition, Caes. To reject or refuse a judge. To repeal a law. To explode an opinion. To suffer a rebuff from someone, Cicero. To renounce and reject, Pompon. To disown a companion, Horat. To turn the thumb down, Juv.

units.la: Repudiare uxorem] Remittere, renunciare, dicere uxori repudium, Ter. Remittere nuncium uxori, Cic. Missam facere uxorem, Suet. Multare uxorem matrimonio, Sen. Dimittere uxorem, matrimonium. Digressa, dimissa à matrimonio. Diductum matrimonium, à Diduco, Suet. Uxor discessit à, Cic.
units.tr: Repudiare uxorem: to send a wife away, to renounce her and give her a bill of divorce, Ter. To send a message of divorce to one's wife, Cic. To make one's wife a former wife, Suet. To deprive a wife of marriage, Sen. To dismiss a wife from marriage. Separated, dismissed from marriage. A marriage dissolved, from Diduco, Suet. A wife departed from, Cic.

units.la: Repudium] Divortium. Abruptio, Cicero. Discidium conjugum, Ovid. Discessio, Ter. Diffarratio, & diffareatio, apud Fest.
units.tr: Repudium: divorce. A breaking off, Cicero. A separation of spouses, Ovid. A departure, Ter. Diffarratio and diffareatio, in Festus.

units.la: Repuerascere, vid. Puerascere. Repugnare, vid. Reniti, Adversari.
units.tr: Repuerascere, see Puerascere. Repugnare, see Reniti, Adversari.

units.la: Repugnare iis frustra, quos vincere nequeas] In coelum ne exspuas. Contra stimulum ne calcitres.
units.tr: To resist in vain those whom you cannot overcome: do not spit at heaven. Do not kick against the goad.

units.la: Requies, vid. Quies, Quiescere.
units.tr: Requies, see Quies, Quiescere.

units.la: Requiem dare] Requiem dare ab opere, Col. Dare alicui vacationem alicujus rei, vel, ab aliquâ re, Cic. Dare alicui pausam, Lucretius. Strigare, Plinius Senior.
units.tr: Requiem dare: to give rest from work, Col. To grant someone exemption from a thing, or from something, Cic. To give someone a pause, Lucretius. To curry a horse, Plinius Senior.

units.la: Est dare spatium quietis equo in superando clivo, Muret.
units.tr: It is to give a horse a space of rest in climbing a steep hill, Muret.

units.la: Requiescere] Suspendere spiritum. vid. Quiescere.
units.tr: Requiescere: to hold one's breath. See Quiescere.

units.la: Requirere] Requirere aliquid ab aliquo. Desiderare officium alicujus, Cic. vid, Quaerere.
units.tr: Requirere: to require something from someone. To expect a service from someone, Cic. See Quaerere.

units.la: Requisita, vid. Necessaria.
units.tr: Requisita, see Necessaria.

units.la: Res] Genus, pro re, In omni genere diligens. Opus, Cic.
units.tr: Res: a kind, standing for res: diligent in every kind of thing. A work, Cic.

units.la: Res tua agitur] Tuum ferrum nunc in igni est.
units.tr: Your affair is at stake: your iron is now in the fire.

units.la: Res ipsa ostendit] Aqua quam alta sit, ipsa ostendit. Dictis fidem dabit ipsa res. Res ipsa loquitur.
units.tr: The thing itself shows: the thing itself shows how deep the water is. The thing itself will give credence to words. The thing speaks for itself.

units.la: Res difficilis] Nodus Gordius.
units.tr: A difficult matter: the Gordian knot.

units.la: Res sine usu] Frondes fructuum expertes. Avis sine volatu. Coelum sine rorato.
units.tr: A thing without use: leaves barren of fruit. A bird without flight. A sky without dew.

units.la: Res nihili, vid. Nihili. Res ridiculae, vid. Ridiculae actiones.
units.tr: Res nihili, see Nihili. Res ridiculae, see Ridiculae actiones.

units.la: Res non succedunt ex voto] Copiae meae nunc in arctum coguntur, Ter.
units.tr: Things do not turn out as one wished: my resources are now being squeezed into a narrow space, Ter.

units.la: Ad rem veniamus] In rem praesentem eamus. Quid de pusillis magna proœmia.
units.tr: Let us come to the matter: let us go to the matter at hand. Why such great preambles for small things?

units.la: Resalutare] Impertire aliquem resalutatione. Reddere alicui verbum, Suet. Salutanti mutuam salutationem reddere, Sen.
units.tr: Resalutare: to return someone's greeting. To return a word of greeting, Suet. To return a mutual greeting to one who greets, Sen.

units.la: Rescribere] Rescribere epistolae alicujus: alicui de aliquo: ad aliquid. Persolvere epistolae, Cic.
units.tr: Rescribere: to write back to someone's letter; to someone about something; to something. To answer a letter, Cic.

units.la: Rescriptum] Contrascriptum, Cic.
units.tr: Rescriptum: a written reply, Cic.

units.la: Resecare] Desecare aliquid, Cic. Recidere ornamenta ambitiosa, Hor. Rescindere vitem, Col. Deplantare semen, Var. Praesecta radix, Col. Incidere arborem, Plin.
units.tr: Resecare: to cut off something, Cic. To prune away showy ornaments, Hor. To cut back a vine, Col. To pluck out seed, Var. A root cut off, Col. To fell a tree, Plin.

units.la: Resegmen] Praesegmen, Non. Abscgmen, Naev. Recisamentum, Non. Sarmenta & superamenta, Vlp. Profectum, Var. Segmen, Plin.
units.tr: Resegmen: a cutting off, Non. A piece cut away, Naev. Trimmings, Non. Twigs and prunings, Vlp. A shoot, Var. A segment, Plin.

units.la: Reservare] Reservare se, vel aliquid, aliis temporibus: in aliud tempus: eo: ad ea tempora, Cic. Reservare sibi ad reditum; in congressum, Id.
units.tr: Reservare: to keep oneself or something back for other times: for another time, for that time, for those times, Cic. To keep back for oneself for the return, or for a meeting, Id.

units.la: Resex] Palmes subsidiarius, Praesidiarius, Col. Palmes emissarius, emissus, Plin. Custos, Id. Duramentum, Duramen, suboles vitis. Furunculus, Col.
units.tr: Resex: a supporting side-shoot of a vine, Col. A sprouting shoot put out, Plin. A guardian, Id. A hardened stem, the heart-wood, a sucker of a vine. A little sprout, Col.

units.la: Residuus, vid. Reliquus, Vltimus.
units.tr: Residuus, see Reliquus, Ultimus.

units.la: Resignare literas] Relinere epistolam, Cic. Resolvere literas, Liv. Linum incidere, Cic. (Quia lino tabellas obligabant.)
units.tr: Resignare literas: to unseal a letter, Cic. To open a letter, Liv. To cut the thread, Cic. (Because they bound their tablets with thread.)

units.la: Resipiscens emendet] Benefactis pensare delicta.
units.tr: Let him who comes to his senses make amends: to balance wrongs with good deeds.

units.la: Resipiscentia] Receptus à malis consiliis, Liv. Correctionis initium, agnoscere culpam.
units.tr: Resipiscentia: a withdrawal from bad counsels, Liv. The beginning of correction: to acknowledge one's fault.

units.la: Resipiscere] Colligere se. Nunquamne, amentissime homo, te circumspicies? Cic. Defecit illum improbitas, Id. Redire ad se. Jam aderit (tempus,) cum se ipse quoque oderit, Ter. vid. Pœnitet.
units.tr: Resipiscere: to collect oneself. Will you never look about you, most senseless man? Cic. Wickedness failed him, Id. To come back to oneself. The time will come when he will hate himself too, Ter. See Paenitet.

units.la: Resistere, vid. Reniti.
units.tr: Resistere, see Reniti.

units.la: Resistere duobus malis difficile] Ne Hercules quidem contra duos. Difficile duo contraria pellere.
units.tr: It is hard to resist two evils: not even Hercules against two. It is hard to drive off two opposites.

units.la: Resolvere vid. Dissolvere. Resonare. vid. Sonare.
units.tr: Resolvere, see Dissolvere. Resonare, see Sonare.

units.la: Respectare aliquid] Circumspectare vultus aliorum, & inde libertatis auram captare, Liv. Pendere ex aliquo. In te unum tota se convertit civitas, Cic. Respectum habere, Cic. Respectum agere, Val. Max. Respicere, spectare aliquem, Cic.
units.tr: Respectare aliquid: to look round at the faces of others and so catch a breath of liberty, Liv. To depend on someone. All the state turns on you alone, Cic. To have regard, Cic. To pay regard, Val. Max. To look back at, to regard someone, Cic.

units.la: Respectu] Comparatè. Ad rationem. Pro: pro horum temporum perturbatione. Ad: nihil ad illum, Cic. Ab: friget ab illo, Gell. Præut. Præquàm, Plaut.
units.tr: Respectu: comparatively. In relation to. For: in view of the disturbance of these times. To: it has nothing to do with him, Cic. From: he is cold toward him, Gell. Before, than, Plaut.

units.la: Respectus] Respectus alicujus: &, ad aliquid. Ratio, Cic. Reverentia, Iuv.
units.tr: Respectus: regard for someone, and in regard to something. Consideration, Cic. Reverence, Juv.

units.la: Respicere. vid. Circumspicere.
units.tr: Respicere, see Circumspicere.

units.la: Respirare[ Dncere spiritum: animum de cœlo, Cic. Trahere & reddere spiritum, Celf. Attrahere & reddere animam, Plin. Reciprocare animam, Liv. Recipere animam, Quint. anhelitum, Plaut. Prospirare, Cat. Ducere & reflare aërem. Rehalare. Reddere animam. Reducere auras naribus, Lucret. Exceptare leves auras, Virg. Bestiæ auras recipiunt naribus, & per anhelitum reciprocatas reddunt, Arnob. Reciprocare à vitali spiritu aërem, Id. Interspirare, Cato.
units.tr: Respirare: to draw breath. To draw the mind from heaven, Cic. To draw in and give back breath, Celsus. To draw in and give back the breath of life, Plin. To breathe back, Liv. To receive breath, Quint. Breath, Plaut. To breathe out, Cato. To draw in and blow out air. To breathe again. To give back the breath. To draw air back through the nostrils, Lucret. To catch the light breezes, Virg. Beasts take air into their nostrils and give it back, breathed through the lungs, Arnob. To breathe back air from the vital spirit, Id. To breathe in between, Cato.

units.la: Respirare àmetu, vid. Recreari.
units.tr: Respirare à metu, see Recreari.

units.la: Respiratio] Spiritus, Anima, Aspiratio, Adspiratio aëris, Respiratus, Cic. Reflatus, Reciprocatio spiritus, Plin. Interspiratio in oratione, Cic.
units.tr: Respiratio: breath, spirit, life, an inhaling of air, a drawing of breath, Cic. A blowing back, a return of spirit, Plin. A pausing for breath in speech, Cic.

units.la: Respondere] Responsitare: Responsum dare, reddere, Cic. Respondere alicui, &, ad aliquid, Id. Resequi, Ovid. Responsare, Plaut. Expedire, Ter. Subjicere, Virg.
units.tr: Respondere: to answer. To give or return an answer, Cic. To answer someone, and to something, Id. To follow, Ovid. To answer back, Plaut. To explain, Ter. To add, Virg.

units.la: Respondere dure alicui] Asperè alicui respondere; vehementer, inhumanè, male respondere. Graviore verbo compellare aliquem. Vehementer, iracundè agere, Liv. Inclementer alicui dicere, Plaut. Inclementer dicere in aliquem, Liv.
units.tr: Respondere dure alicui: to answer someone harshly; to answer vehemently, inhumanely, badly. To address someone with a harsher word. To act vehemently and angrily, Liv. To speak unkindly to someone, Plaut. To speak unkindly against someone, Liv.

units.la: Respondere ad literas, vid. Rescribere.
units.tr: Respondere ad literas, see Rescribere.

units.la: Responsio] Responsum, Suet. Hostimentum, Enn. Apophasis, Vlp.
units.tr: Responsio: an answer, Suet. A retort, Enn. A denial, Vlp.

units.la: Responsor] Renuncius, Plaut.
units.tr: Responsor: a messenger who brings back an answer, Plaut.

units.la: Respublica, vid. Politia.
units.tr: Respublica, see Politia.

units.la: Restat, vid. Remanere. Restaurare, vid. Reparare.
units.tr: Restat, see Remanere. Restaurare, see Reparare.

units.la: Restinguere, vid. Exstinguere.
units.tr: Restinguere, see Exstinguere.

units.la: Restio] Restiarius, Front. Funarius. Sext. Aurel.
units.tr: Restio: a rope-maker, Front. A rope-maker, Sext. Aurel.

units.la: Restitare] Insistere singulis gradibus. Insistit oratio in singulis sententiis. Resistere in gradu, Cic. Restare, Ter. Constare, Plaut. Subsistere in limine, Virg. vid. Cunctari.
units.tr: Restitare: to stand firm on each step. The speech dwells on each sentence. To stand fast on the spot, Cic. To remain, Ter. To stand, Plaut. To halt on the threshold, Virg. See Cunctari.

units.la: Restituere aliquem statui pristino] Restituere aliquem in pristinum statum, dignitatem, gratiam, possessionem; damnatum in integrum: in locum unde quis cecidit: reipublicæ. Repræsentare libertatem, Cic. Reponere aliquem in gradu, I C. Restituere in locum antiquum gratiæ & honoris. Revocare ab exilio, Plin. Facere reducem in patriam. Reducere aliquem in gratiam, Ter. Reconciliare in libertatem, Plin. Reddere, vel restituere aliquem natalibus, Plin. Iun. Eximere aliquem infamiæ, Tac. Liv. Eximere in libertatem, Id. Jus in præteritum dare, Plaut.
units.tr: Restituere aliquem statui pristino: to restore someone to his former state, dignity, favour or possession; a condemned man to his former standing; to the place from which one fell; to the commonwealth. To restore liberty, Cic. To put someone back in his rank, I.C. To restore someone to the old place of favour and honour. To recall from exile, Plin. To make someone return to his country. To bring someone back into favour, Ter. To reconcile someone to liberty, Plin. To restore someone to his birthright, Plin. Jun. To free someone from infamy, Tac., Liv. To set someone free into liberty, Id. To give law retrospectively, Plaut.

units.la: Restitutio] Venia exilii, Tac. Reditus gratiæ, vel in gratiam, Cic.
units.tr: Restitutio: pardon for exile, Tac. A return to favour, or into favour, Cic.

units.la: Restitutor] Reductor literarum senescentium, Plin. Iun. Vindex, Cic.
units.tr: Restitutor: a restorer of fading letters, Plin. Jun. An avenger, Cic.

units.la: Resultare] Resilire, Ovid. Absilire, Lucr. Respuitur imber à cornu, Id.
units.tr: Resultare: to leap back, Ovid. To leap off, Lucr. The rain is thrown back from the horn, Id.

units.la: Resurgere] Cecidi, ut honestissimè surgerem, Cic. Revirescere, Id. Assurgere ex morbo, Liv. Excitari à morte, ab inferis, ex Cic. Reviviscere ad verba. Reviviscit Resp. justitia, Cic.
units.tr: Resurgere: I fell so that I might rise most honourably, Cic. To grow green again, Id. To rise up from sickness, Liv. To be raised from death, from the dead, from Cic. To come back to life at words. Justice revives in the commonwealth, Cic.

units.la: Resurrectio] Postliminium mortis, Apul.
units.tr: Resurrectio: a return of the dead to life, the postliminy of death, Apul.

units.la: Resuscitare] Revocare aliquem ab inferis, à limine mortis, à morte ad vitam. Excitare aliquem à morte: mortuos ab inferis, Cic. Revocare defunctos, Plin. Reducere à morte, Virg. Restituere à limine mortis, Catul.
units.tr: Resuscitare: to call someone back from the dead, from the threshold of death, from death to life. To raise someone from death; the dead from the underworld, Cic. To recall the departed, Plin. To lead back from death, Virg. To restore from the threshold of death, Catul.

units.la: Retaliare aliquid alicui] Referre par: par pari referre, Ter. Referre, reddere paria, Cic. Reddere vicem, Mart. Rependere vices, Propert. Remetiri, Plin. Iun. Coërcere aliquem talione. Æquiparare talionem. Talione parem facere talionem, ex Gell. Regerere injuriam, Plin. Redhostire par, paria, ex Fest.
units.tr: Retaliare aliquid alicui: to return like for like; to repay a thing in kind, Ter. To return, to give back equal things, Cic. To give back a turn, Mart. To repay turns, Propert. To measure back, Plin. Jun. To restrain someone by the law of retaliation. To make the retaliation equal. To make the retaliation equal to the injury, from Gell. To return an injury, Plin. To return an equal retaliation, paria, from Fest.

units.la: Retardare aliquem] Multis, vel diutius aliquem morari. Tardare aliquem. Detinere & demorari aliquem. Multis aliquem tenere. In mora sum alicui, Cic. Mora sum alicui, Per me est mora, Ter. Morae sum alicui, Plaut. Commorari aliquem. Remorari ituros, Morari iter alicujus, Ovid. Facere moram certamini, Liv. Moram alicui objicere, creare, offerre, Plaut. afferre, inferre. Facere alicui moram. Interponere moram. Tenerere distinere, occupare aliquem, Cic. moram alicui facere, Luc. Delectare aliquem, Cæs. Pl.
units.tr: Retardare aliquem: to detain someone for many hours, or longer. To delay someone. To hold back and detain someone. To keep someone back for a long time. To be in someone's way, Cic. To be someone's delay, Ter. To be a hindrance to someone, Plaut. To hold someone back. To keep someone from going. To hinder someone's journey, Ovid. To cause a delay in the contest, Liv. To put, create or offer a delay for someone, Plaut. To bring or cause a delay. To make a delay for someone. To interpose a delay. To hold, detain, occupy someone, Cic. To cause someone delay, Luc. To delight someone, Caes., Pl.

units.la: Rete] Plagas tendere, Cic. Cassis, Plin. Tendicula, Viscum, Sipont. Panthera, Cerd. Indago; indagine aliquem cingere, claudere, Virg. Liv.
units.tr: Rete: to set snares (plagas tendere), Cic. A hunting-net (cassis), Plin. A small net, birdlime (viscum), Sipont. A panther-net, Cerd. A hunting-net (indago); to surround or enclose someone with a net, Virg. Liv.

units.la: Retegere, vid. Detegere.
units.tr: Retegere, see Detegere.

units.la: Reticere aliquid] Reticere, tacere aliquid de aliquo. Silentio praetermittere, praetervehere, omittere, Cic. Transire aliquid, abs. Plin. Iun. Transire, transmittere, dissimulare aliquid silentio. Agere de aliquo silentium, Quint. In silentio reponere, Plin. Iun. Muginari, Cic. Mussitare, Plaut.
units.tr: Reticere aliquid: to keep silent, to say nothing of someone or something. To pass over in silence, to skip past, to omit, Cic. To pass over something absolutely, abs. Plin. Iun. To pass over, to let pass, to conceal something by silence. To keep silence about someone, Quint. To consign to silence, Plin. Iun. To mutter, Cic. To mumble, Plaut.

units.la: Reticere te hoc velim] Vide ne cui dicas. Nemini dixeris. Vide ne dicas cuiquam. Vide ne cuipiam dixeris. Vide ne dixeris alicui. Vide ne mortalium ulli dixeris. Er.
units.tr: Reticere te hoc velim: I would have you keep this quiet. See that you tell no one. Tell no one. See that you tell anyone. See that you tell some person. See that you tell someone. See that you tell any mortal at all. Er.

units.la: Reticulum] Reticulum junceuni, linteum, Col Reticulus, Ulp. Casticulum, Fost. Casticulus, Hier. Retiola, æ, Ap.
units.tr: Reticulum: a net of rushes, a linen net, Col. A little net, Ulp. A little net (casticulum), Fost. A little net (casticulus), Hier. A little net (retiola), Ap.

units.la: Retinere] Retentare fræna, Ovid. Cic. Obtinere lenitatem: necessitudinem cum aliquo obtinere & conservare. Continere exercitum. Coërcere aliquem à progressu. Refrenare à reditu. Tardat aliquem profectionem meam. Reprimere objurgationem, Cic. vid. Detinere.
units.tr: Retinere: to tighten the reins, Ovid. Cic. To keep up gentleness: to maintain and preserve a bond of kinship with someone. To keep the army in check. To restrain someone from advancing. To hold someone back from returning. He delays my departure. To suppress a rebuke, Cic. See Detinere.

units.la: Retorquere] Retundere tela, Cic. Reflectere, Sil. Respuere tela in eum, qui miserat, Sen. vid. Intorquere.
units.tr: Retorquere: to beat back weapons, Cic. To bend back, Sil. To hurl weapons back at the one who sent them, Sen. See Intorquere.

units.la: Retorquere argumentum] Jugulare aliquem suo gladio.
units.tr: Retorquere argumentum: to cut someone's throat with his own sword.

units.la: Retractare] Retexere orationem, Cic. vid. Renovare, Revocare.
units.tr: Retractare: to unweave a speech, Cic. See Renovare, Revocare.

units.la: Retractatio] Dicere libere sine retractatione. Palinodia, Cic.
units.tr: Retractatio: to speak freely without retraction. A palinode, Cic.

units.la: Retrahere] Abstrahere ab, ad. Submovere maleficio. Revocare a scelere, Cic. Avocare, Liv.
units.tr: Retrahere: to draw away from, or to draw toward. To remove from wrongdoing. To call back from crime, Cic. To call away, Liv.

units.la: Retribuere. vid. Reddere.
units.tr: Retribuere. See Reddere.

units.la: Retrimentum] Fraces. Floces, retrimenta uvarum, Gell. Intrita folliculorum, Col. Vinaceus, & Vinacea, pl. Id. Vinacea, æ, Pallad. Col. Brisa, ex quâ prælo subjecta secundarium vinum fit, Id.
units.tr: Retrimentum: dregs, lees; the husks and residue of grapes, Gell. Crushed husks of the pods, Col. Grape-skins and pulp, plural, Id. Grape-skins (vinacea), Pallad. Col. A pressed residue (brisa), from which a second-grade wine is made when placed under the press, Id.

units.la: Retro] Retrorsum, Plin. Rursum, prorsum, Don. Conversim, Firm. Rursum, vorsum, Recessim, Plaut. Cessim, Justin.
units.tr: Retro: backwards, Plin. Again, forwards, Don. Turned about, Firm. Back and forth, backwards, withdrawing, Plaut. Withdrawing, Justin.

units.la: Retroagere] Retroire cogere, Plin. Vertere, avertere, agere in fugam aliquem, Liv. Retorquere oculos ad urbem, Cic. Caput in terga sua, Ovid. Recurvare in caput aquas, Id. Rejicere retrorsum, Hor. Reciprocare quinqueremem, Plin. Obvertere proras pelago, Virg.
units.tr: Retroagere: to force to go backwards, Plin. To turn away, to drive someone into flight, Liv. To turn one's eyes back to the city, Cic. To turn the head back over the shoulders, Ovid. To curl the waters back upon the head, Id. To thrust backwards, Hor. To row a quinquereme back, Plin. To turn the prows toward the sea, Virg.

units.la: Retrocedere] Retro iter vertere. Referre gradum, pedem, Liv. Retro se ferre, Sen. Retrogradi, Plin. Retrahere se. Revocare se. Reprehendere se, vel alium, Inhibere retro navem, Terga vertere, Cic. Torquere vestigium, Virg. Convertere terga, Caes. Remanare, refluere, Lucr. Revolare, Cic. Cursus aversos retorquere, Virg.
units.tr: Retrocedere: to turn back on one's road. To bring back one's step or foot, Liv. To carry oneself back, Sen. To go backwards, Plin. To draw oneself back. To call oneself back. To check oneself or another. To back the ship. To turn one's back, Cic. To turn one's footstep, Virg. To turn one's back, Caes. To flow back, to ebb, Lucr. To fly back, Cic. To turn backwards the courses that have been turned away, Virg.

units.la: Retrocessus] Inhibitio remigum, Cic. Redundatio stellarum, coeli, Vitr.
units.tr: Retrocessus: the checking of oarsmen, Cic. The backward motion of the stars, of the sky, Vitr.

units.la: Retrogradus] Retrorsum rediens, Plin. Recessim cedens, Plaut. Conversim retrogrediens, Firm.
units.tr: Retrogradus: returning backwards, Plin. Withdrawing, retiring, Plaut. Going back by turning about, Firm.

units.la: Retrudere] Dimovere obstantes, Hor. Dimoveri & depelli loco. Repellere aliquem a genibus, Cic.
units.tr: Retrudere: to move aside those who stand in the way, Hor. To be moved and driven from a place. To push someone away from one's knees, Cic.

units.la: Revalescere] Phœnicis instar revivisccre. Revivisccre, Cic. Ex morbi longinquitate recreari. Relevatus est morbus, Id. Ad sanitatem perduci, Celf. Sanum fieri ex morbo, Cato. vid. Convalescere.
units.tr: Revalescere: to revive like the phoenix. To come back to life, Cic. To recover from a long illness. The illness has been lifted, Id. To be brought back to health, Celf. To become well again from sickness, Cato. See Convalescere.

units.la: Revelare, vid. Manifestare. Detegere.
units.tr: Revelare, see Manifestare. Detegere.

units.la: Revera, vid. Re.
units.tr: Revera, see Re.

units.la: Reverendus] Venerandus, Val. Arg. Venerabile nomen, Ovid.
units.tr: Reverendus: to be venerated, Val. Arg. A venerable name, Ovid.

units.la: Reverenter] Venerabundè, Liv. Venerabiliter, Macrob. Reverentissimè, Suet. Dignanter, Vopisc. Dignè, Plaut.
units.tr: Reverenter: with reverence, humbly, Liv. Venerably, Macrob. Most reverently, Suet. With dignity, Vopisc. Worthily, Plaut.

units.la: Reverentia] Honorificentia, Capitol. vid. Honestas.
units.tr: Reverentia: honour, Capitol. See Honestas.

units.la: Revereri, vid. Vereri. Reverti, vid. Redire.
units.tr: Revereri, see Vereri. Reverti, see Redire.

units.la: Revirescere] Repubescere, Col. Puellascere, Non.
units.tr: Revirescere: to grow young again, Col. To become a girl again, Non.

units.la: Revivisцere, vid. Revalescere.
units.tr: Revivisci, see Revalescere.

units.la: Revocare factum, dictum] Retractare dicta, Virg. Retexere orationem, Cic. Habere pro non dicto, Liv. Resecrare, Amm. Recantare opprobrium, Hor. Exjuratli temihi per jocum dixisse, Plaut. Nolle factum. Nolle facta esse injuriam, Ter. Adjuret, nolle esse dicta, quae in insontem protulit, Plaut. Palinodiam canere scribere, Er. Aug. & Recent.
units.tr: Revocare factum, dictum: to retract words, Virg. To unweave a speech, Cic. To hold as not said, Liv. To take back (resecrare), Amm. To recant an insult, Hor. He swears that he said it to me in jest, Plaut. To wish a deed undone. To wish that an injury had not been done, Ter. He swears he did not wish the words spoken which he uttered against an innocent man, Plaut. To sing or write a palinode, Er. Aug. & Recent.

units.la: Revolvere] Amoliri aliquid de, Sisen. Remoliri pondus, Ovid. vid. Circumagere.
units.tr: Revolvere: to remove something from, Sisen. To move a weight back, Ovid. See Circumagere.

units.la: Revolutio caeli] Conversio coeli. Replicatio mundi, Cic. Conversatio universi, Sen. Vertigo coeli, Plin. Circumductus orbium, Macrob. Circinatio planetarum, Vitr. Celer volumen coeli, Ovid. Circumrotundatio, Sipont. Rotundatio circulorum in motu, Vitr. vid. Circumactio.
units.tr: Revolutio caeli: the turning of the heavens. The unfolding of the world, Cic. The turning of the universe, Sen. The whirling of the sky, Plin. The circling of the orbs, Macrob. The circling of the planets, Vitr. The swift wheel of heaven, Ovid. Circular rotation, Sipont. The rounding of circles in motion, Vitr. See Circumactio.

units.la: Revolutiones temporum] Spirae in se redeuntes. Revolutionum labyrinthi.
units.tr: Revolutiones temporum: coils returning into themselves. Labyrinths of revolutions.

units.la: Reus] Advocationem alicujus ferre (advoc. id est personas reas.) Nocens reus. Nocens.abs. Citatus audaciae reus. Affinis vitio. Affinis sceleris. Huic culpa haeret. Tenetur culpa, poena. Haeret in eo crimen. Sons, Cic. Tenetur de vi, Sen. Noxius, Sal. Obnoxius, Plau. Obnoxius crimini. Damnatus voti, Liv. debitor voti, Mart. Accusatus vid. Culpa in eo est.
units.tr: Reus: to bring the defence of someone (advocationem, that is, of persons who are accused). A guilty defendant. Guilty, simply. A defendant charged with audacity. Implicated in a fault. Implicated in a crime. Blame clings to him. He is held by blame and penalty. The charge hangs upon him. Guilty, Cic. Held for violence, Sen. Liable to harm, Sal. Liable, Plau. Liable to a charge. Bound by a vow, Liv. Debtor of a vow, Mart. Accused, see Culpa in eo est.

units.la: Reum esse] Reus sum caedis: de vi ab aliquo: A Milone nomen meum de parricidio delatum est. Delatus sum furti. Lege de vi teneri, Cic. Sedere inter reos. Causam capitis dicere, Bud. Dies mihi dicta est, Plaut. Postulatus sum caedis, Bud. Reus agitur aliquis, Ovid.
units.tr: Reum esse: I am accused of murder; accused of violence by someone. My name was brought by Milo against me on a charge of parricide. I have been charged with theft. To be held under the law on violence, Cic. To sit among the accused. To plead a capital cause, Bud. A day has been fixed for me, Plaut. I have been indicted for murder, Bud. Someone is being tried as a defendant, Ovid.

units.la: Rex] Regnator, Virg. Tyrannus, Id. Princeps Principium, Cic. Imago Dei, ex Persarum lege. Jovenati. Jo-cipium, Cic. Imago Dei, ex Persarum lege. Jovenati. Jovisi vis alumni, Homer. Ornator & Pastor populorum. Pater Reipub. ex Gr. Lipf. in Epist. Reges fulmini similes di-cit, quod dura frangit, mollibus plerumque illæsis.
units.tr: Rex: ruler, Virg. Tyrant, Id. Prince, first principle, Cic. Image of God, from the law of the Persians. Nursling of Jove. Nursling of Jove's power, Homer. Adorner and shepherd of the peoples. Father of the commonwealth, from the Greek; Lipsius in Epistles. He says kings are like lightning, because they break hard things, while they mostly leave soft things unharmed.

units.la: Rex sapiat ipse] Regium est domi habere consilium, non ab aliena pendere sententia, Eras.
units.tr: Let the king himself be wise: it is kingly to have counsel at home, and not to depend on another's opinion, Eras.

units.la: Reges sunt sapientes] Reges Deorum discipuli.
units.tr: Kings are wise] Kings are the disciples of the gods.

units.la: Reges multa vident & audiunt] Regum aures atque oculi multi. An nescis longas regibus esse manus? Hor.
units.tr: Kings see and hear many things] Many are the ears and eyes of kings. Do you not know that kings have long hands? Hor.

units.la: Reges sumus recte faciendo] Rex eris, si recte feceris. Si vis esse Rex, dabo tibi regnum, Rege te ipsum.
units.tr: We are kings by doing right] You will be king if you act rightly. If you wish to be king, I will give you a kingdom: rule yourself.

units.la: Rheda] Triga, Ulp. Quadriga, Iun. Quadrigæ, Hor. Carruca, Mart. Carrus, Cæs. Carrum, Hirt. Bijuge carriculum, Spet. Sarracum, Iuv.
units.tr: Rheda: a three-horse chariot, Ulp. A four-horse chariot, Iun. Four-horse chariots, Hor. A carriage, Mart. A wagon, Caes. A wagon, Hirt. A little two-horse carriage, Spet. A cart, Iuv.

units.la: Rhetor] Rhetoricus doctor, Cic. Magister declamandi, Quint. Traditor eloquentiæ, Fab. Victor. Sophista, Mario Victor. Cic.
units.tr: Rhetor: a teacher of rhetoric, Cic. A master of declamation, Quint. A transmitter of eloquence, Fab. Victor. A sophist, Mario Victor. Cic.

units.la: Rhetorica] Professio benè dicendi. Eloquentia forensis, popularis, Cic. vid. Eloquentia.
units.tr: Rhetorica: the profession of speaking well. Forensic and popular eloquence, Cic. See Eloquentia.

units.la: Rhetoricari] Rhetoricare, Non. Rhetorissare, Id. Rhonchissare, vid. Stertere, &c.
units.tr: To rhetoricize: to rhetoricate, Non. To rhetorize, Id. To snore (rhonchissare), see Stertere, etc.

units.la: Rhytmus] Numerus, Cic.
units.tr: Rhythm: number, measure, Cic.

units.la: Rictus] Rictus ad auras dehiscens, Plin. Rictum, Lucr.
units.tr: Rictus: a gaping mouth opening toward the air, Plin. A gaping mouth, Lucr.

units.la: Rictum diducere] Hor. Rictum distendere, Quint. Restringere dentes, Plaut. Nudare, Lucr. Diducere malas, Col. Irridենt me albis dentibus, Plaut. Labra diducere, Sen. Aperire os, Virg. Oscitat dissutis undique malis, Pers. Canem irritatam imitari, Plaut.
units.tr: To open the mouth wide] Hor. To stretch the mouth wide, Quint. To draw back the teeth, Plaut. To bare, Lucr. To draw apart the cheeks, Col. They laugh at me with white teeth, Plaut. To draw apart the lips, Sen. To open the mouth, Virg. He yawns with jaws gaping on every side, Pers. To imitate a dog that has been provoked, Plaut.

units.la: Ridere] Edere, ridere risum. Risus erumpit, Cic. Tollere risum, Hor. Corridere, Lucr. Vultum risu solvere, Val. Max. Cachinnum sustulit, & in jocos transfusus est, Suet.
units.tr: To laugh: to give out laughter, to laugh a laugh. Laughter bursts forth, Cic. To raise a laugh, Hor. To laugh loudly, Lucr. To relax the face into laughter, Val. Max. He burst into a guffaw and was turned to jesting, Suet.

units.la: Ridere nimium] Emori risu.
units.tr: To laugh too much: to die of laughter.

units.la: Rideri, vid. Ludibrio esse.
units.tr: To be laughed at, see To be a laughing-stock.

units.la: Ridiculus] Ridiculissimus, Ridiculosus, Ridiculosissimus, Plaut. Ridendus, Hor. Ridicularius, Gell. Perridiculus, Cic.
units.tr: Ridiculous: most ridiculous, full of ridicule, most full of ridicule, Plaut. Laughable, Hor. Jesting, comical, Gell. Very ridiculous, Cic.

units.la: Ridiculæ actiones] Camelus saltat. Cancer leporem capit.
units.tr: Ridiculous actions: a camel dances. A crab catches a hare.

units.la: Rigare, vid. Aspergere. Rigatio, vid. Aspersio.
units.tr: To wet, see Aspergere. Watering, see Aspersio.

units.la: Rigens] Rigidus, Ovid. Torpens, Virg. Obtorpuit manus, Cic. Callosus, Col. Torpidus stupore ac miraculo. Sopitus humerus, Liv. Abalienata morbis membra praecidunt medici, Quint. Instupens membrum, Plin.
units.tr: Stiff: rigid, Ovid. Numb, Virg. His hand has gone numb, Cic. Hardened, callous, Col. Torpid with astonishment and wonder. A benumbed shoulder, Liv. Limbs wasted by disease are cut off by doctors, Quint. A numbed limb, Plin.

units.la: Rigescere, vid. Obrigescere.
units.tr: To stiffen, see Obrigescere.

units.la: Rigidè, parùm civiliter] Ex Syngraphâ agere. Morosissimè penitare, Suet.
units.tr: Harshly, uncivilly: to act strictly according to the written bond. To punish with the utmost severity, Suet.

units.la: Rigidè procedere] Summo jure agere, Cic. Præter æquum & bonum, Ter. Gravius aliquid in aliquem statuere, Caes. Inclementius dictum, Ter. Tristius respondere, Cic. Illiberaliter factum, Ter. Præcisè, Cic. De apicibus juris disceptare, Vlp. Pro meo jure, Ter. Abscissè, Callistr.
units.tr: To proceed rigidly: to act by the strictest law, Cic. Beyond what is fair and good, Ter. To decide something more severely against someone, Caes. A harsher word, Ter. To answer more gloomily, Cic. Done illiberally, Ter. Precisely, Cic. To dispute over the fine points of law, Ulp. By my right, Ter. Abruptly, Callistr.

units.la: Rigidus] Immite edictum, Ovid. Summum jus, summa injuria, Cic. Censorium judicium, Id. Priscus pater, Catul. Abscissus, Val. M. vid. Severus.
units.tr: Rigid: a harsh edict, Ovid. The strictest law is the greatest injustice, Cic. A censorial judgment, Id. A stern old father, Catul. Abrupt, Val. M. See Severe.

units.la: Rima] Vitium ædis, parietis. Fissus, Cic. Segmen & ruptura parietis, Vitr. Spiramentum, Virg. Fissum, Cels. Fissura, Col.
units.tr: A crack: a fault in a building or wall. Cleft, Cic. A split and break in a wall, Vitr. A breathing hole, Virg. A cleft, Cels. A fissure, Col.

units.la: Rimosus] Fissus, Scissus, Col. Fisliculatus, Mart. Hiulcus, Virg. Bifidus. Bifidatus, Ovid. Plin. Fluxum pertusumque vas, Lucr. Futilis ac rimarum plenus, Apul.
units.tr: Full of cracks: cleft, split, Col. Full of little cracks, Mart. Gaping, Virg. Forked, cleft in two (bifidus, bifidatus), Ovid. Plin. A leaking, perforated vessel, Lucr. Leaky and full of cracks, Apul.

units.la: Ringi] Hirrire, Carif. vid. Rictum diducere.
units.tr: To snarl (hirrire), Carif. See To open the mouth wide.

units.la: Ripa] Margo fontis, ripæ, Ovid. Margo fluminis, Var. Labrum fluminis, Sisen. Supercilium fluminis, Amm.
units.tr: Bank: the edge of a spring or of a bank, Ovid. The edge of a river, Var. The lip of a river, Sisen. The brow of a river, Amm.

units.la: Riparius, vid. Littoralis.
units.tr: Riparius: see Littoralis.

units.la: Risibilis] Ridendi facultate præditus, Sipont. Cachinnabilis, Apul.
units.tr: Risibilis: endowed with the faculty of laughing, Sipont. Causing loud laughter, Apul.

units.la: Risus moderatus] Extra cachinnum risus. Sine dente sales, Mart.
units.tr: Risus moderatus: laughter short of a belly laugh. Wit without a sting, Mart.

units.la: Risus simulatus] Sardonius risus, Eras. ex Gr. ab herba Sardoa, quæ comesa rictus homini invito diducit, & contrahit ridentis speciem, nascitur in Sardiniâ, Virg. Alienis malis ridens, Hor. Errantesque genæ atque alieno gaudia vultu, Val. Arg.
units.tr: Risus simulatus: sardonic laughter, Erasmus, from the Greek. It comes from a Sardinian herb which, when eaten, forces the mouth of an unwilling man open and draws the face into the look of laughter; it grows in Sardinia, Virg. Laughing at another's misfortunes, Hor. Wandering eyes and joy in a face not one's own, Val. Arg.

units.la: Risui est mihi] Movet mihi risum. Risum vix teneo, Cic.
units.tr: Risui est mihi: it moves me to laughter. I can hardly hold back my laughter, Cic.

units.la: Risum excitare] Concitare, movere, captare risum. Jacio aliquod ridiculum. Commovere cachinnos, Cic. Exprimere risum alicui, Plin. Iun. Facere risum, Quint. Quatere risu aliquem, Hor.
units.tr: Risum excitare: to stir up, move, or catch laughter. To throw out some joke. To set off loud laughter, Cic. To draw laughter from someone, Plin. Iun. To make people laugh, Quint. To shake someone with laughter, Hor.

units.la: Rite] Recte latum aliquid, Cic. Ritualiter, Amm. Augustè sacréque consecrare aliquem. Auspicato renunciatus consul, Cic. Augurato, Liv. Ter, partic. apud Virg. Idem sonat, quod ritè.
units.tr: Rite: something done properly, Cic. Ritually, Amm. To consecrate someone solemnly and sacredly. A consul proclaimed under good auspices, Cic. Under augury, Liv. Ter, as a participle in Virg. It has the same meaning as ritè.

units.la: Ritualia] Libri rituales, Cic. Agenda, Plin.
units.tr: Ritualia: ritual books, Cic. Agenda, Plin.

units.la: Ritualis. Ritus, vid. Ceremonia, &c.
units.tr: Ritualis. For ritus, see Ceremonia, etc.

units.la: Rivalis] Rivinus, Plant. Corrivalis, Sipont. Commaritus, & connatio, apud Plaut.
units.tr: Rivalis: a rival, Plaut. A fellow rival, Sipont. A co-husband and a fellow-wife, in Plaut.

units.la: Rivus] Fluentum, Virg.
units.tr: Rivus: a stream, Virg.

units.la: Rixa] Contentio. Concertatio verborum. Jurgium, Cic. Abjurgium, Plaut. Convitium, Hor. Velitatio verborum. Lis, Cic.
units.tr: Rixa: contention. A contest of words. A quarrel, Cic. A wrangle of words, Plaut. Abuse, Hor. A skirmish of words. A lawsuit, Cic.

units.la: Rixa pestis veritatis] Nimium altercando amittitur veritas, Publ. Mim.
units.tr: Rixa pestis veritatis: by too much wrangling, truth is lost, Publ. Mim.

units.la: Rixari] Contendere jurgio cum aliquo. Jurgari, Cic. Jurgari verbis. Delitigare, Hor. Committere rixam, Liv. Compugnare. Velitari adversus aliquem, Gell. Labiis inter se velitari, Afran. Inimicari.
units.tr: Rixari: to contend in a quarrel with someone. To quarrel, Cic. To quarrel in words. To wrangle, Hor. To start a brawl, Liv. To fight together. To skirmish against someone, Gell. To skirmish with the lips among themselves, Afran. To be enemies.

units.la: Rixari de re nihili] De umbrâ asini. De lanâ caprinâ. Id est, utrum caper lanam habeat, an fetas.
units.tr: Rixari de re nihili: to quarrel about the shadow of an ass, or about goat's wool; that is, whether a goat has wool or kids.

units.la: Rixator] Altercator, Quint. Vitilitigator, Plin. Concertator, Tac. Rabula, Var. Ordinarius homo; scurra improbus. Litium amans, & minimè ordine vivens, Fest. Perturbator, Sipont. Cœni agitator, Aristoph. Trico, Capitol. Concitor turbarum, Amm.
units.tr: Rixator: a wrangler, Quint. A hair-splitter, Plin. A contender, Tac. A brawler, Var. A common fellow; a rascally buffoon. One who loves lawsuits and does not live in good order, Fest. A disturber, Sipont. A stirrer of mud, Aristoph. A cheat, Capitol. A stirrer-up of disturbances, Amm.

units.la: Rixosus] Litigiosus loquaciter. Concitus ad rixam, Cic. Litigator, Quint. Jurgiosus, Gell. Jurgatorius, Amm. Concertatorius, Cic. Contentiosa & pugnax oratio, Plin. Iun. Tricosus, Lucil. Litium cupidus, rixarum, Hor. Litis sator. Cane rixosior, Eraf.
units.tr: Rixosus: litigious and talkative. Stirred up to brawling, Cic. A litigant, Quint. Quarrelsome, Gell. Contentious, Amm. Given to contention, Cic. A contentious and pugnacious speech, Plin. Iun. Brawling, Lucil. Fond of lawsuits and quarrels, Hor. A sower of strife. More quarrelsome than a dog, Erasmus.

units.la: Roborascere] Roborare se. Paulùm roboris accessit. Firmitatem nancisci, Cic. Robur accipere, Col. Sumere robur corpore, Liv. Valescere, Tac. Vigescunt pedes, Catul. Virescit animi vis, Non. Robur] Vis viri. Vis in manibus. Nervus belli, animi. Firmitas animi. Duramentum, Cic. Valentia, Macrob. Manus, Tac. Virtute manuum pedumque fretus, Virg. Virus, pro virtute naturali, apud Lucil.
units.tr: Roborascere: to strengthen oneself. A little strength has been gained. To win firmness, Cic. To receive strength, Col. To take strength in the body, Liv. To grow strong, Tac. The feet grow strong, Catul. The strength of the mind grows green, Non. Robur: the strength of a man. Power in the hands. The sinew of war, or of the mind. Firmness of spirit. Hardness, Cic. Vigour, Macrob. Hands, Tac. Relying on the strength of hands and feet, Virg. Virus used for natural vigour, in Lucil.

units.la: Robustus] Exercito corpore homo, Salust. Magni sunt oneris, quicquid imponas vehunt cliteliarii, Plaut. Centauricus, Ovid. Valens colonus, Vim habet, Maximis viribus vir, valentissimus, Forticulus, Cic. Habet vires, Operosa viribus herba, Plin. Valentulus est, Plaut. Pollens corpus, Validus, Lucr. Praevalidus juvenis, Liv. Ingentium virium, Celf. Fortis manu. Valet pugnis, Plaut. Adamantinus, Hor. Plus pollet potiorque est. Lacertosus, Cic. Compacto corpore. Athleta robustior, Eras. Tenax complexus, Ovid. Pollentia potior, Plaut. Plus pollet, potiorque est, Cic.
units.tr: Robustus: a man hardened by exercise, Sall. Whatever you load on them, the carters carry; it is of great weight, Plaut. Centauric, Ovid. A strong farmer. Has force. A man of great might, very strong, a sturdy fellow, Cic. Has strength; an herb of great power, Plin. He is somewhat strong, Plaut. A sturdy body, compact, Lucr. A very strong youth, Liv. Of great strength, Celsus. Strong of hand. He is strong with his fists, Plaut. Adamantine, Hor. He is more powerful and stronger. Muscular, Cic. A compact body. A stronger athlete, Erasmus.
