A tenacious embrace, Ovid. More powerful and stronger, Plaut. He is more powerful and stronger, Cic.

units.la: Rodere] Corrodere, Cicer. Arrodere morsu, Sidon. Derodere, Plinius. Mordere frena, Cicer. Mandit equus frena, Virg. Frendere, Varr. Nucem dentibus conficere, Plin. Frangere nucem, Cic. Tondent dumeta juvenci, Virg.
units.tr: Rodere: to gnaw away, Cic. To nibble with the teeth, Sidon. To gnaw off, Plin. To bite the bit, Cic. The horse champs the bit, Virg. To grind, Varr. To crush a nut with the teeth, Plin. To crack a nut, Cic. The heifers nibble the brambles, Virg.

units.la: Rogare] Rogare precatio: aliquid aliquem: aliquid de aliquo. Petere aliquid ab aliquo. Poscere aliquid aliquem; verbo: ab aliquo. Orare aliquem. Orare precibus. Uti precibus. Precari aliquid aliquem: ab aliquo. Expetere ab aliquo, Cicer. Exposcere, Livius. Petere dictis bonis, Plautus. Postulo id a te, Terentius. Amare (i. amanter orare) Plautus. Efflagitasti quotidianis convitiis. Eblanditus est favorem. Illud unum abs te magnopere peto contendoque, Eras. vid. Obsecrare.
units.tr: Rogare: to ask, a prayer; to ask something of someone; to ask someone for something. To seek something from someone. To demand something of someone, or to demand it from someone. To entreat someone. To entreat with prayers. To use prayers. To beg something of someone, or from someone. To seek something from someone, Cic. To demand, Livy. To ask for good things with words, Plautus. I ask this of you, Terence. To love (that is, to beseech lovingly), Plautus. You have pestered him with daily abuse. He wheedled for favour. "This one thing I ask of you and earnestly entreat," Erasmus. See Obsecrare.

units.la: Rogator] Petax, Donat. Precator, Ter. Orator, Plaut. Postulator, Suet. Procax, Ter. Petitor, Macrob.
units.tr: Rogator: a seeker, Donat. An entreater, Ter. A speaker, Plaut. A claimant, Suet. Bold, Ter. A petitioner, Macrob.

units.la: Rogus] Bustum, Ovid. Bustar, Carif. Ustrina, Var. Ustor, Mart. (Apparatus mortuorum, funus dicitur; Exstructio lignorum, rogus: Subjectio igni, pyra: Crematio cadaverum, bustum: Locus, Ustrina: Operis exstructio, sepulchrum: Inscriptum nomen memoriaque, monumentum, Scal.
units.tr: Rogus: a funeral pyre, Ovid. A pyre-builder, Carif. A burning-place, Var. A burner of the dead, Mart. (The preparation of the dead is called funus; the piling of wood, rogus; the setting fire to it, pyra; the burning of corpses, bustum; the place, ustrina; the construction of the work, sepulchrum; the name inscribed and the memory kept, monumentum, Scal.)

units.la: Romanus] Romanicus, Cat. Romanensis, Salust. Romulea urbs. Sil. Romulus: Romula tellus, Virg. Romulidæ (Romana gens) Lucr.
units.tr: Romanus: Roman-like, Cat. Of Rome, Sall. The Romulean city, Sil. Romulus; the Romulean land, Virg. The Romulidae (the Roman people), Lucr.

units.la: Roralis] Rorulentus, Col. Roscidus, Var. Rorans capillus. Roratæ rosæ, Ovid. Rorifluus, Var. Rorifer, Lucr.
units.tr: Roralis: dewy, Col. Dewy, Var. Hair dripping with dew. Roses bathed in dew, Ovid. Dew-flowing, Var. Dew-bearing, Lucr.

units.la: Rorat] Rorat imbrem, Plin. Irrorat. Stillat arbor rore Col. Stillare rorem, Hor.
units.tr: Rorat: it drips dew, Plin. To sprinkle. A tree drips with dew, Col. To drip dew, Hor.

units.la: Ros] Concretura vaporum. Pluvia insensilis. Pabulum herbarum. Aleman Lyricus, Rorem solis vel aëris & lunæ filiam dixit.
units.tr: Ros: a condensation of vapours. Unfelt rain. The pasture of herbs. The lyric poet Alcman called dew the daughter of the sun, or of the air and the moon.

units.la: Rosaceus] Rhodinus: rhodinum unguentum, oleum, Pl. Roscidus, vid. Roralis.
units.tr: Rosaceus: rose-like; rose ointment, rose oil, Plin. Dewy, see Roralis.

units.la: Roseum] Rosarium, Col. Rhodonia. Rhodig.
units.tr: Roseum: a rose garden, Col. A rose bed. Rhodig.

units.la: Rosmarius] Ros marinus: marinus ros: Ros-marinum, Col. Ros maris, Ovid. Libanotis, idis. Plin. Libanotis coronaria, Iun.
units.tr: Rosmarius: rosemary, sea-dew, marine dew, Col. Sea-dew, Ovid. Libanotis, Plin. Garland-libanotis, Iun.

units.la: Rostrare] Plin. Ferire rostrò, Liv. Rostro everberat os, vel oculos alicui corvus, Quint.
units.tr: Rostrare: Plin. To strike with the beak, Liv. A crow pecks a man's mouth or eyes with its beak, Quint.

units.la: Rota] Ferrati orbes, Valer. Arg.
units.tr: Rota: iron-bound wheels, Valer. Arg.

units.la: Rotare, vid. Circumagere.
units.tr: Rotare: see Circumagere.

units.la: Rotundare] Globare. Circinare in orbem, Plin. Decircinare, Manil. Circulare, Amm. Gyrare, Plin. Corrotundari grando dicitur, apud Sen.
units.tr: Rotundare: to make round, to globe. To describe a circle, Plin. To make circular, Manil. To make round, Amm. To circle, Plin. Hail is said to become rounded, in Sen.

units.la: Rotundè] Orbiculatim flexa ossa, Plin.
units.tr: Rotunde: bones bent into circles, Plin.

units.la: Rotunditas] Rotundatio turris, Vitr. Globositas, Macrob. Circumferentia, Apul. Circinatio, Vitr.
units.tr: Rotunditas: the rounding of a tower, Vitr. Globosity, Macrob. Circumference, Apul. Circling, Vitr.

units.la: Rotundus] Rotundissima ova, Col. Globosus. Orbiculatus, Cic. Sphæralis forma, Macr. Gyratus orbis, Plin. In rotundum habitum figurata acies, Amm. Glomerosus, Col. Totus teres atque rotundus.
units.tr: Rotundus: very round eggs, Col. Globular. Orbicular, Cic. Spherical in form, Macr. A winding circle, Plin. A battle line drawn up in a round formation, Amm. Clustered, Col. Wholly smooth and round.

units.la: Rubedo] Rubor, Plin. Virg.
units.tr: Rubedo: redness, Plin. Virg.

units.la: Ruber] Rubens, Rubeus, Virg. Rubicundus, Var. Rubicundulus, Iuv. Rubellus, Mart. Rubricosus, Plin. Rubidus, Fest. Sanguinolentus, Ovid. Phœniceus, Plaut. Rubellianæ vites, Col. Carbunculans. Carbunculosus, Plin.
units.tr: Ruber: reddening, red, Virg. Ruddy, Var. Somewhat ruddy, Juv. Reddish, Mart. Red-streaked, Plin. Reddish, Fest. Bloody, Ovid. Purple-red, Plaut. Reddish vines, Col. Glowing like a carbuncle. Carbuncled, Plin.

units.la: Rubere] Rubescere, Plin. Subrubet cœlum. Ruborem trahere. Sublucent ora misto rubore, Ovid. Purpurascere, Cic. Roseo colore fulgent flores, Plin.
units.tr: Rubere: to grow red, Plin. The sky reddens. To take on a blush. Faces shine with a mingled blush, Ovid. To turn purple, Cic. Flowers shine with a rosy colour, Plin.

units.la: Rubescit aurora, &c.] Irrubuit coeli plaga, Stat. Inardescit nubes radiis solis, Virg. Suffecta nubes sole, Sen.
units.tr: Rubescit aurora, &c.: the region of the sky has flushed red, Stat. The cloud glows in the sun's rays, Virg. The cloud is suffused by the sun, Sen.

units.la: Rubiginari] Gladius situ rubiginatur, Apul. Vera rubigine consenescit, Plaut. Rubiginem trahere, Plin. Sentire, Hor. Contrahere æruginem, Plin.
units.tr: Rubiginari: the sword rusts through neglect, Apul. It grows old with real rust, Plaut. To take on rust, Plin. To feel it, Hor. To contract verdigris, Plin.

units.la: Rubiginosus] Æruginosus, Sen. Scebrum rabigine telum, Virg.
units.tr: Rubiginosus: covered with verdigris, Sen. A weapon rough with rust, Virg.

units.la: Rubigo] Robigo, Plin. Ærugo, Bud.
units.tr: Rubigo: rust, Plin. Verdigris, Bud.

units.la: Rubor virtutis color] Erubuit, salva res est, Ter.
units.tr: Rubor virtutis color: she has blushed; the matter is safe, Ter.

units.la: Ructare] Ructari aves, Var. Hor. Eructare, est saepe erugere: Erugere, est semel ructare, Fest. Eructare sermonibus caedem bonorum, Cic. Irructare in os alicui, Plaut. Obructare alicui, Apul. Redundare hesterna coena, Plin. Iun. Exhalare acidos ructus ex pectore, Lucr.
units.tr: Ructare: birds belch, Var. Hor. To belch repeatedly is often said of eructare; to belch once is erugere, Fest. To belch out the slaughter of good men with words, Cic. To belch into someone's face, Plaut. To belch back at someone, Apul. Yesterday's dinner comes back up in belches, Plin. Iun. To breathe out sour belches from the chest, Lucr.

units.la: Ructatio] Ructitatio, Celf. Ructus, Cic. Eructatio, Firm. Ructamen, Prudent.
units.tr: Ructatio: belching, Celsus. Belching, Cic. Eructation, Firm. Belching, Prudent.

units.la: Ructuosus] Ructuosos spiritus geminare. Quint. Ructatrix menta, Marr. à ructator. Os si aperiat, cacabum putes, ollamque fumantem, Cresfol.
units.tr: Ructuosus: to double one's belching breaths, Quint. A mint-belching mouth, from ructator, Marr. If he opens his mouth you would think it a steaming pot and cauldron, Cresfol.

units.la: Rudimentum, vid. Tirocinium.
units.tr: Rudimentum: see Tirocinium.

units.la: Rudis] Indocilis: anima jejuna, Plin. Imperitus rerum Hospes, Tiro, Cic. Homo recens, nuperus, novitius. Vir indoctissimus: minime doctus. Homo quidvis potius quam doctus, Plaut. Album colorem a nigro non distinguit. Nescit quid sit inter dextram & sinistram. Viam in forum ignorat.
units.tr: Rudis: untaught, a starved soul, Plin. A stranger and novice in affairs, Cic. A recent, new, untried man. A most unlearned man, not learned at all. A man anything rather than learned, Plaut. He cannot tell white from black. He does not know the difference between right and left. He does not know the way to the forum.

units.la: Rudis moribus] Agrestis, Impolitus, Inconcinnus, Inornatus, Inconditus, Invenustus, Subhorridus, Verrucosus, Rusticanus, Horridus & incultus, Cic. Merum rus, Plaut. Incomis, Macrob. Rusticitati quam deliciis propior, Plin.
units.tr: Rudis moribus: rustic, unpolished, awkward, unadorned, uncouth, unlovely, somewhat rough, warty, country-bred, rough and uncultivated, Cic. Pure countryside, Plaut. Uncouth, Macrob. Nearer to rusticity than to refinement, Plin.

units.la: Rudibus moribus] Impolitè, Vastè, Rusticè, Cic. Invenustè, Gell.
units.tr: Rudibus moribus: crudely, roughly, rustically, Cic. Unlovely, Gell.

units.la: Rudi ingenio, i. simplicius & indoctius] Crassa Minerva, Hor. Pingui Minerva, Cic. Crassiore Musa, Quint. Indoctius. Mappalia mera fecisti, Sen.
units.tr: Rudi ingenio, i.e. simpler and less learned: a coarse Minerva, Hor. A thick-witted Minerva, Cic. A coarser Muse, Quint. Less learned. You have made nothing but sheds, Sen.

units.la: Rudes ad gubernacula inepti] Remum ducat, qui nihil didicit.
units.tr: Rudes ad gubernacula inepti: let him who has learned nothing take up the oar.

units.la: Rudes loquaciores eruditis] Vacuum vas altius pleno resonat. Vasa inania tinniunt.
units.tr: Rudes loquaciores eruditis: an empty vessel rings louder than a full one. Empty vessels rattle.

units.la: Ruditas morum] Rusticitas, Plin. Enormitas rusticitatis, Diomed. Barbarismus, Barbaries, Cic. Rus: plenus ruris, Cat. Merum rus, Plaut. Simplicitas rudis, Ovid. Impolitia, Gell. Inficetiæ, Infacetiæ, Catul. Atechnia, Quint.
units.tr: Ruditas morum: rusticity, Plin. Excessive rusticity, Diomed. Barbarism, barbarity, Cic. Full of the countryside, Cat. Pure countryside, Plaut. Plain, untutored simplicity, Ovid. Lack of polish, Gell. Dullness, lack of wit, Catul. Lack of art, Quint.

units.la: Ruere] Ruinam dare, Virg. Facere, Hor. Corruere, Liv. Tecta super habitantes procubuerunt, Quint.
units.tr: To rush headlong] To cause ruin, Virg. To make, Hor. To collapse, Liv. The roofs fell down upon the inhabitants, Quint.

units.la: Rufus] Rutilus, Var. Russus, Apul. Ænobarbus. Homo æneâ barbâ, Suet. Æri similis capillus, Id.
units.tr: Red-haired] Reddish, Var. Russet, Apul. Bronze-bearded. A man with a bronze beard, Suet. Hair like bronze, Id.

units.la: Ruga] Contractio frontis, Cic.
units.tr: Wrinkle] A drawing together of the brow, Cic.

units.la: Ruga ostendit senium] Facies tua computat annos.
units.tr: A wrinkle shows old age] Your face counts your years.

units.la: Rugare, vid. Corrugare.
units.tr: To wrinkle, see To crease.

units.la: Rugosus] Facies rugosior uvâ passâ, Claud. Rugatus. Corrugatus, Col. Striata, contracta frons, Apul. Adstricta frons, Mart. Contricta fronte Catones, Petron. Cossus, à similitudine cossi, vermis lignorum, dictus; est rugosi corporis homo, Fest.
units.tr: Wrinkled] A face more wrinkled than a raisin, Claud. Wrinkled. Creased, Col. A brow striated and drawn together, Apul. A brow drawn tight, Mart. Catos with knotted brows, Petron. Cossus, so called from its likeness to the cossus, a wood-worm, is a man of wrinkled body, Fest.

units.la: Ruina] Demolitio statuarum. Excisio tectorum, Cic. Dejectus arborum, Plin.
units.tr: Ruin] The demolition of statues. The cutting down of roofs, Cic. The felling of trees, Plin.

units.la: Ruminare] Remandere, Plin. Revocare palearibus herbas, Calpur. Præteritos cibos in ore volvere, & in alvum missos iterum retrahere, Hieron. Pasto pasci cibo: Atque iterum pasto pascitur ante cibo, Ovid.
units.tr: To ruminate] To chew the cud again, Plin. To bring grass back up to the dewlaps (of cattle), Calpurn. To roll food previously taken in the mouth and to draw back again what has been sent into the belly, Hieron. Fed by food already fed on, and again fed before the food, Ovid.

units.la: Rumor] Rumusculus. Aura rumoris. Fama, Cic.
units.tr: Rumour] A little rumour. A breath of rumour. Report, Cic.

units.la: Rumor est] Rumores sparsi sunt. Rumoris nescio quid afflaverat. Nihil à te ad nos rumoris affluxit. Rumor perfertur ex Asiâ. Rumore nuntio audivimus. Rumor serpit. Perfert, affert aliquid rumor. Fama est, celebrat, nunciat, surrexit, percrebuit, emanavit, ad aures meas pervenit. Fama aliquid accepi. Affertur, Absol. &, Affertur rumor, Cic. Fama fert: ita tenet; Fama traditur, perfertur, obtinet, Liv. Fama persuasit, Tac. Vulgavit, Curt. Circumfert, Plin. Crebrescit fama, Tac. Fama in vulgus exierat, Suet. vid. Adjunt.
units.tr: There is a rumour] Rumours have been spread. Some rumour had blown in. Nothing of rumour has flowed to us from you. A rumour is carried from Asia. We heard it on the report of a messenger. A rumour creeps about. A rumour carries and bears something. There is talk, it is spreading, it is announced, it has arisen, it has grown strong, it has got out, it has reached my ears. I have received something by report. It is brought, absolutely; and, it is brought as a rumour, Cic. Report bears, so it holds; it is handed down, carried about, prevails, Liv. Report persuaded, Tac. Spread abroad, Curt. Carries about, Plin. Report grows, Tac. Report had gone out among the common people, Suet. See Additions.

units.la: Rumor incertus] Frigidus à rostris manat per compita rumor, Hor. Sine capite aliquid manat: Cujus non est auctor. Audire aliquid de aliquo sine capite, sine auctore, Cic.
units.tr: Unfounded rumour] A cold rumour flows from the rostra through the crossroads, Hor. Something flows without a head, whose author is not known. To hear something about someone without a head, without an author, Cic.

units.la: Rumpere] Perrumpere nodos, Lucret. Prærumpere retinacula, Ovid. Interrumpere. Dirimere, Cic. Dirumpere, Plautus. Distrahere rem, Cæs. Intercidere, rescindere pontem, Idem. Perfringere conspirationem. Præcidere sermonem, Cic. Incidere verba, Stat. Scindere verba fletu, Ovid. Perscindit ventus nubem, Lucr. Abrumpere somnum, Virg. Discutere morbum, Celf. Intercipere iter, Liv. Frangere diem, Hor.
units.tr: To break] To break through knots, Lucr. To snap the reins beforehand, Ovid. To interrupt. To divide, Cic. To tear apart, Plaut. To separate a matter, Caes. To cut off and cut down a bridge, Id. To break up a conspiracy. To cut short a speech, Cic. To cut words off, Stat. To tear words with weeping, Ovid. The wind rends the cloud, Lucr. To break off sleep, Virg. To dispel a disease, Cels. To cut off a journey, Liv. To break the day, Hor.

units.la: Rumpi] Inflata rumpuntur, Cic. Rumpantur ut ilia Codro invidiâ, Virg. Dirumpi, Plautus. Dirupi me pene, Cic. Dehiscunt pisces præ pinguedine: dehiscit uterus, Plin. Displosa vehicula, Displodor, Lucr. Crepant remi, Virg. Hiascunt nuces, Cat. Frangi assulatim: raphani modo (in transversum, Plin.
units.tr: To be broken] Swollen things burst, Cic. Let them burst with envy like the bowels of Codrus, Virg. To burst apart, Plaut. I almost burst, Cic. Fishes gape from fatness; the womb gapes, Plin. Carriages burst open, Lucr. Oars creak, Virg. Nuts split open, Cat. To be splintered into pieces, like radishes (crosswise, Plin.).

units.la: Runcare] Eruncare omnes alterius generis herbas; Col. Herbam è segetib. expurgare, Varr. Exherbare locum, Eligere manu herbas & exstirpare herbas, Col. Purgare locum ab herba, Cato.
units.tr: Weeding] To root out all herbs of another kind, Col. To clear weeds from the crops, Varr. To clear a place of herbs; to pick herbs out by hand and to pull up herbs, Col. To clear a place of grass, Cato.

units.la: Runcatio] Evulsio in utilium herbarum, Sipont. Botamismus, Plin. Bud.
units.tr: Weeding] The pulling out of useful herbs, Sipont. A clearing of weeds, Plin. Bud.

units.la: Rupes] Inaccessæ scopulosæque cautes. vid. Petra.
units.tr: Rock] Inaccessible and craggy cliffs. See Stone.

units.la: Rupicapra] Dama, Ovid. Capra silvestris, Gesner. Ibex, Id.
units.tr: Chamois] A deer, Ovid. A wild goat, Gesner. An ibex, Id.

units.la: Ruptio] Distentio nervorum, Celf. Convulsio distractis fibris, vel. Solutio unitatis in parte nervosa ictu citra vulnerationem, Gorr. Ruptum in corpore, Id.
units.tr: Rupture] A stretching of the sinews, Cels. A convulsion with the fibres pulled apart, Veget. A loosening of the sinewy part by a blow without wounding, Gorr. Ruptured in the body, Id.

units.la: Ruptus] Ruptus & convulsus, Plin. Diruptus, Cic. Fractus, Hor.
units.tr: Ruptured] Burst and convulsed, Plin. Torn apart, Cic. Broken, Hor.

units.la: Rurestris] Ruralis, Macrob. Rusticus: Rusticanus, Cic. Villaticus, Col. Vicanus, Cic. Paganus, Ovid. Rusticulus, Mart. Villaris gallina, Plin. Paganicus, Mart.
units.tr: Rural] Of the countryside, Macrob. Rustic; rustic, Cic. Of the farm, Col. Of the village, Cic. Rural, Ovid. A little rustic, Mart. A farmyard hen, Plin. Rustic, Mart.

units.la: Rursus, vid. Denuo. Rursus prorsus, vid. Huc & illuc.
units.tr: Again, see Anew. Back and forth, see Hither and thither.

units.la: Rustica vita] Cic. Rusticatio Rusticatus, Id, Ruratio, Apul. Aspera vita sed salubris. Rusticari] Rurari, Varr. Rurare, Plaut. Rure morari, Mart. Villicari, Pompon. Ligone philosophari.
units.tr: Rustic life] Cic. Country life; lived in the country, Cic. Country living, Apul. A hard life, but a healthy one. To live in the country] To live in the country, Varr. To live rustically, Plaut. To tarry in the country, Mart. To farm, Pompon. To philosophise with a hoe.

units.la: Rustice] Rusticius, Hor. Rusticatim tanquam, quæ urbanatim nescio, Pompon.
units.tr: Rustically] More rustically, Hor. Rustically, as one who does not know how to be urbane, Pompon.

units.la: Rusticitas, sumitur etiam pro rusticis & Agrestibus, vid. Ruditas morum.
units.tr: Rusticity is also taken for country folk and rustics, see Rudeness of manners.

units.la: Rusticus, nom.] Rusticanus quidam. Rusticulus non incatuus, Cic. Ruricola, Col. Custos simplicitatis. Homo de plebe.
units.tr: Rustic, noun] A certain rustic. A rather simple country fellow, not unpolished, Cic. A dweller in the country, Col. A guardian of simplicity. A man of the common people.

units.la: Rutilare] Rutilare, rufare capillum, Plin. Irrufare capillum, Hieron. vid. Nitere.
units.tr: To redden] To make the hair reddish, Plin. To make the hair ruddy, Hieron. See To shine.

units.la: Rutilus] Rutilatus crinis, Tac. Subrutilus, Plin. Aureus color barbæ, Ovid. Auro certans, Sil. Flammeus, Cic. Flammeolus, Col. Croceus ignis, Claud. Igneus color, Plin. Flammis florens, Lucr. Florus, Næv. Russus, Lucr. Russeolæ fasciæ, Capitol.
units.tr: Reddish] Hair made ruddy, Tac. Somewhat reddish, Plin. The golden colour of a beard, Ovid. Vying with gold, Sil. Flame-coloured, Cic. A little flame-coloured, Col. Saffron-coloured fire, Claud. A fiery colour, Plin. Blossoming with flames, Lucr. Florid, Naev. Russet, Lucr. Russet bands, Capitol.

units.la: S.
units.tr: S.

units.la: Sabbathum] Sabbatum. Sabbata, plus tantum volunt, Plin. Ovid. Lambin. Cultaque Judæo Septima sacra viro, Ovid. Ignava lux, Juv. Dies Saturni, Tibull.
units.tr: Sabbath] Sabbatum. Sabbaths (plural), they want only more, Pliny, Ovid, Lambinus. "And the seventh day, sacred to the Jewish man, is kept," Ovid. "The idle day," Juvenal. "The day of Saturn," Tibullus.

units.la: Sabbatarius, vid. Judæus. Sabulum, vid. Arena.
units.tr: Sabbatarian, see Jew. Sand, see Sand.

units.la: Saburrare] Saburrâ gravare onerariam, Liv. Onerare navem frumento. In onerariam navem aliqua conjicere, Cic. Corbitare, Plaut.
units.tr: To load with ballast] To weigh down a transport ship with ballast, Livy. To load a ship with grain. To throw something into a cargo ship, Cic. Corbitare, Plautus.

units.la: Saccharum] Mel concretum. Sal Indicus, Gor. Mel arundinum, ex Græ.
units.tr: Sugar] Honey in lumps. Indian salt, Gorraeus. Reed honey, from the Greek.

units.la: Saccus] Pero, Vitr.
units.tr: Sack] Pero, Vitruvius.

units.la: Sacellum] Sacrarium Cereris, Cic. Lararium, Lampr. Ædicula, Liv. Augurale, Tac. Auguratorium, Lips. Fanulum, Fest. Ædis sacræ appendix.
units.tr: Small shrine] A shrine of Ceres, Cic. A household shrine, Lampridius. A little altar-chapel, Livy. A place for taking the auspices, Tacitus. An augury-house, Lipsius. A little shrine, Festus. An appendix to a sacred building.

units.la: Sacer] Magno ritu sacer. Sacratissimus, Plin. Sacratus, Ovid. Sanctus campus; Religiosus locus: altaria religiosissima, Cic. Sanctior, Id. Sacratior, Plin. Sacrosanctus, Val. Max. Augustus locus, Cic.
units.tr: Sacred] Sacred with great ceremony. Most sacred, Pliny. Consecrated, Ovid. A holy field; a sacred place: most sacred altars, Cic. Holier, Id. More consecrated, Pliny. Inviolable, Valerius Maximus. An august place, Cic.

units.la: Sacerdos] Sacerdotio præditus, Cic. Sacricola, Tac. Sacrificulus, Liv. Mysta, Sen. Victimarius, Plin. Cultrarius, Suet. Presbyter Christiani ritûs, Amm. Presbyter Christianastianorum, Vopisc. Flamen, Sacerdos Ethnicorum, Var. In numerum sacerdotum venire] Venire in sacerdotium, Inire sacerdotium, Consequi, Cic. Initiari sacris, Quint.
units.tr: Priest] Endowed with the priesthood, Cic. One who offers sacrifice, Tacitus. A minor sacrificer, Livy. An initiate in the mysteries, Seneca. An attendant at sacrifices, Pliny. A knife-bearer, Suetonius. A presbyter of the Christian rite, Ammianus. A presbyter of the Christians, Vopiscus. A flamen, a priest of the heathens, Varro. To come into the number of priests: to enter the priesthood, to take up the priesthood, to attain it, Cic. To be initiated into the sacred rites, Quintilian.

units.la: Sacerdotalis] Sacrificalis apparatus, Tac.
units.tr: Priestly] The equipment of sacrifice, Tacitus.

units.la: Sacrare, vid. Consecrare.
units.tr: To consecrate, see To consecrate.

units.la: Sacrarium] Locus in quo res sacræ servantur, Isid. Sacrorum repositorium, Sipont. Sacrum vestiarium. Supellectilis sacræ cella.
units.tr: Sacristy] A place in which sacred things are kept, Isidore. A repository of sacred things, Sipontinus. A sacred wardrobe. The chamber for sacred furnishings.

units.la: Sacrificare] Facere sacra, sacrificium, res divinas, Cic. Facere rem divinam, Ter. Facere, abs. Facere vitulâ, Virg. Agnis, Plaut. Cædere agnum, Id. Victimare hostiam, Apul. Immolare, Fest. Virg. Agno immolato aram spargere, Hor. Operari deo, Tibul. Immolare diis hostias, Cic. Operari superstitionibus hostes, dixit Liv. Supplicare Deo thure & vino, Plaut. Instaurare sacra Diis, Tac. Litare victimas, sacrificium, Suet. Libare Diis thura, Ovid. Porricere (exta projiciendo offerre) aris & foculo exta, Fest. Pollucere, Cato. Perlitare, Liv. Persibare vinum in sacris, Plin. Sacrare, Virg. Procurare sacrificia, Cæs. Factitare sacrificia. Rem divinam obire. Dare operam rebus divinis, Cic. Offerre donarium, Sipont. Consecrare, Plin. Jovi dapem sine contagione profanato, Var. Decumare. Præcidere, Fest. Obire sacra. Perpetrare sacrificium, Liv. Peragere sacra, Ovid.
units.tr: To sacrifice] To perform sacred rites, to make a sacrifice, to perform divine service, Cic. To perform divine service, Terence. To make sacrifice, absolutely: to sacrifice a heifer, Virgil. To sacrifice lambs, Plautus. To slaughter a lamb, Id. To offer a victim, Apuleius. To immolate, Festus. Virgil: having sacrificed a lamb, to sprinkle the altar. To serve God, Tibullus. To sacrifice victims to the gods, Cic. Livy says: to serve the superstitions of enemies. To pray to God with incense and wine, Plautus. To renew the sacred rites of the gods, Tacitus. To offer victims successfully, to sacrifice, Suetonius. To pour incense to the gods, Ovid. To offer the entrails by casting them on the altar and hearth, Festus. To offer in sacrifice, Cato. To propitiate with sacrifice, Livy. To pour wine over the sacred things, Pliny. To consecrate, Virgil. To carry out sacrifices, Caesar. To practise sacrifices. To perform divine service. To give attention to divine things, Cic. To offer a gift at the altar, Sipontinus. To consecrate, Pliny. To give Jove a feast not defiled by profane use, Varro. To tithe. To cut off, Festus. To attend to sacred rites. To carry out a sacrifice to the end, Livy. To perform the sacred rites, Ovid.

units.la: Sacrificium] Sacrificatio, Sacrum, Immolatio, Procuratio, Res sacra, Libatio, Cic. Litatio, Liv. Piacularia sacra, Id. Operatio, Pl. Initiatio, Suet. Oblatio muneris, Arnob.
units.tr: Sacrifice] The making of sacrifice, a sacred offering, immolation, the performance of rites, a holy thing, libation, Cic. Propitiation, Livy. Expiatory rites, Id. The performance of rites, Pl. Initiation, Suetonius. The offering of a gift, Arnobius.

units.la: Sacrilegium] Sacrilegium facere, admittere, committere, Quint.
units.tr: Sacrilege] To commit, admit, or perpetrate sacrilege, Quintilian.

units.la: Sæpe] Sæpius, Sæpenumero, Cic. Sæpicule, Apul. Sæpiusculè, Plaut. Persæpe. Semel atq; iterum & sæpius. Iterum & sæpius, Crebrò, crebriùs, creberrimè. Frequenter, frequentissimè, Cic. Identidem, Plin. Iun. Creberiter, crebra, Crebre, Vitr. Multoties, Flor. Plurimùm, Ter. Pluries, Gell. Compluries, Plaut. Iterum atq; iterum. Iterum iterumque, Virg. Frequens aderat, Ter. Multa re vertitur oratio mea, (id est sæpe) Cic. Decies die uno. Centies dicere, Plaut. Millies audivi, Ter.
units.tr: Often] More often, very often, Cic. Rather often, Apuleius. Fairly often, Plautus. Once and twice and more often. Repeatedly, frequently, Cic. Frequently, most frequently, Cic. Again and again, Pliny the Younger. Often, Vitruvius. Many times, Florus. Most, Terence. Several times, Gellius. Several times, Plautus. Again and again. Again and again, Virgil. He was often present, Terence. My speech turns on this many times (that is, often), Cic. Ten times in one day. To say a hundred times, Plautus. I have heard it a thousand times, Terence.

units.la: Sæpe agere aliquid] Crebriùs aliquid agere. Crebrum esse in aliquâ re. Usurpare aliquid crebris sermonibus. Sæpe usurpatur aliquid. Usurpare aliquid in omnibus dictis minimis & maximis. Adjungitur usus frequens. Frequentare domum alicujus, Cic. Frequentantur conjugia, Tac. Crebrescunt auræ, Virg. Inculcare aliquid alicui. Abuti aliquâ re, Cic. Plurimùm esse alicubi, exTer. Crebrè egrediuntur venti, Vitr.
units.tr: To do something often] To do something more often. To be frequent in some matter. To use something in frequent talk. Something is often used. To use something in all one's words, great and small. Frequent use is added. To visit someone's house often, Cic. Marriages become frequent, Tacitus. The breezes grow frequent, Virgil. To inculcate something in someone. To misuse something, Cic. To be most often in some place, from Terence. The winds blow frequently, Vitruvius.

units.la: Sævire] Dæsævire in omnes, Claud. Grassari, Liv. Ingeminant Austri, Virg. vid. Debacchari.
units.tr: To rage] To rage against all, Claudian. To rage about, Livy. The south winds keep pressing, Virgil. See To rave.

units.la: Sævitas, vid. Crudelitas.
units.tr: Savagery, see Cruelty.

units.la: Sæviter] Sæviter alloqui aliquem, Plaut. Atrociter minitari, Cic. Districtè minari, Plin. Iun. Torvum intueri, Apul. Torvè aspectare aliquem, Plaut. Truculentissimè adspicere, Quint. Truculentius se gerebat, Cic. Truculentè, Sipont. Torviter increpare, Enn. Non.
units.tr: Savagely] To address someone savagely, Plautus. To threaten fiercely, Cic. To threaten sharply, Pliny the Younger. To look grimly, Apuleius. To look grimly at someone, Plautus. To look most fiercely, Quintilian. He conducted himself more fiercely, Cic. Fiercely, Sipontinus. To scold harshly, Ennius, Nonius.

units.la: Sævus, vid. Atrox.
units.tr: Savage, see Fierce.

units.la: Saga] Venefica, Ovid. Trivenefica, Plaut. vid. Venefica.
units.tr: Witch] A poisoner, Ovid. A triple poisoner, Plautus. See Poisoner.

units.la: Sagacitas] Animi acies, acumen. Perspicacia, Cic. Acetum, Plaut. Bonitas, solertia ingenii, Cic. Indoles ingenii, industriæ in aliquo est, Plaut. Nasus Rhinocerotis, Mart.
units.tr: Sagacity] Keenness of mind, sharpness. Perceptiveness, Cic. Vinegar, Plautus. Goodness, skill of mind, Cic. A natural aptitude; a person's bent for industry, Plautus. A rhinoceros's nose, Martial.

units.la: Sagaciter, vid. Ingeniosè.
units.tr: Sagaciously, see Ingeniously.

units.la: Sagax] Perspicax & acutus. Solertissimus ad perspiciendum. Vir in rebus agendis acer, Cic. Emunctæ naris, acutæ, Hor. Præsaga naris, Firm. Præsagis naribus canes, Id.
units.tr: Sagacious] Perceptive and sharp. Very skilled at perceiving. A man keen in doing business, Cic. Of a keen nose, sharp, Horace. A nose that foresees, Firmicus. Dogs with foreseeing noses, Id.

units.la: Sagina] Altus, us, Macrob. Assura gallinarum, Varr. Saginandi ratio, Col.
units.tr: Fattening feed] A feeding, Macrobius. Fattening of hens, Varro. The method of fattening, Columella.

units.la: Saginare] Opimare, Col. Pinguefacere pecora, Plin. Cogere pinguescere, Sen.
units.tr: To fatten] To enrich, Columella. To make cattle fat, Pliny. To force to grow fat, Seneca.

units.la: Saginarium] Vivarium suum, Plin. Sagina cellaria, Plaut. Hara, Donat. Col.
units.tr: Fattening pen] One's own animal park, Pliny. Fattening store in the pantry, Plautus. A pen, Donatus, Columella.

units.la: Saginatio] Est facilis harum avium sagina, Col.
units.tr: Fattening] The fattening of these birds is easy, Columella.

units.la: Saginatus, vid. Altilis.
units.tr: Fattened, see Fat.

units.la: Sagitta] Ferrum missile, pennatum, vid. Iaculum.
units.tr: Arrow] A missile iron with feathers, see Javelin.

units.la: Sagum, vid. Paludamentum.
units.tr: Cloak, see Military cloak.

units.la: Sal] Flos salis, i.e. sal primæ notæ, Cat. Panacea, ab Effectu, Lucr. Condimentum condimentorum.
units.tr: Salt] The flower of salt, that is, salt of the first quality, Cato. A cure-all, named from its effect, Lucretius. The seasoning of seasonings.

units.la: Salacitas, vid. Lascivia, &c.
units.tr: Lechery, see Lewdness, etc.

units.la: Salariarius] Beneficiarius, Cæs. Beneficii alicujus centurio, Suet.
units.tr: Salaried official] A beneficiary, Caesar. The centurion of someone's benefit, Suetonius.

units.la: Salarium] Annuum,Suet. Annona,Voget. Stipendium militare, Cic.
units.tr: Salary] Yearly, Suetonius. Provisions, Vegetius. Military pay, Cic.

units.la: Salax] Priapo, passere salacior. Satyrium bibit. Satyrias, vid. Lascivus.
units.tr: Lecherous] More lecherous than Priapus or a sparrow. He drinks satyr-like. Satyrs, see Lustful.

units.la: Salebra] Iniquitas loci, Liv. Inæquabilis locus, Var.
units.tr: Rough ground] The unevenness of a place, Livy. An uneven place, Varro.

units.la: Salebrosus] Confragosus, iniquus locus, Liv. Fragosus, Lucr. Fragosa oratio, Quint. Gradatus, Plin. Inæqualis mensa, Mart. Inæquabilis, Var.
units.tr: Rugged] A rough, uneven place, Livy. Rough, Lucretius. A rugged style, Quintilian. Stepped, Pliny. An uneven table, Martial. Uneven, Varro.

units.la: Sales, vid. Iocus.
units.tr: Wit, see Joke.

units.la: Salinæ] Salifodinæ, & Salis fodinæ, Vitr. Areæ salinariæ, Id. Montes salis nativi, Plin. Optimi condimenti promptuarium.
units.tr: Salt-pans] Salt-mines, and mines of salt, Vitruvius. Salt-works areas, Id. Mountains of natural salt, Pliny. A storehouse of the finest seasoning.

units.la: Salire] Sallire, Sisen. Aspergere sale, Col. Aspergere salem carnibus, Plin.
units.tr: To leap] To leap, Sisenna. To sprinkle with salt, Columella. To sprinkle salt on meat, Pliny.

units.la: Saliva] Sputum salsum, tenue, Lucr. Pituita tenuis, Celf.
units.tr: Spittle] Salty, thin spit, Lucretius. Thin phlegm, Celsus.

units.la: Salsamentum] Muriatica salsa, Plaut. Salsura, Col. Pabulum salsurae, Id.
units.tr: Salted meat] Salted pickle, Plautus. Salting, Columella. Food for salting, Id.

units.la: Salsugo] Salsilago, Plin. Salsitudo aquae, Vitr. Muria. Aqua salsa, Col. Eliquamen salsamentorum, Colvin.
units.tr: Saltiness] Brackishness, Pliny. Saltness of water, Vitruvius. Brine. Salt water, Columella. The drippings of salted meats, Colvin.

units.la: Salsus] Sallior, Solin. Præsulsus, Col. Salmacidus, Plin. Salmacia aqua, Scal.
units.tr: Salty] Saltier, Solinus. Very salted, Columella. Salmacian, Pliny. Salmacian water, Scaliger.

units.la: Saltare] Saltitare, Macrob. Saltu ferri, Virg. Dare saltum, Ovid. Uti saltu, Cic. Saliendo se exercere, Plaut. Argutari pedibus, Non. Persultare per campos, Lucr. campos, Tac. Insultare solo, Virg.
units.tr: To dance] To leap about, Macrobius. To leap with a sword, Virgil. To make a leap, Ovid. To use a leap, Cic. To exercise oneself by leaping, Plautus. To dance with the feet, Nonius. To leap across the plains, Lucretius. Across the plains, Tacitus. To leap upon the ground, Virgil.

units.la: Saltatio] Saltatus, Liv. Intempestivi convivii comes, vid. Chorea.
units.tr: Dancing] A dance, Livy. A companion of an untimely feast, see Dance.

units.la: Saltatorius] Saltatorius ludus, Macr. Saltuaris: saltuares insulæ, Plin.
units.tr: Leaping] A leaping game, Macrobius. Leaping, scattered: scattered islands, Pliny.

units.la: Saltem] Saltim, Priscian. Vel: si nullo alio pacto, vel fœnore, Ter. Minimùm, Var. Adero, sin, utique postridiè. Velim possis antè, sin minùs, utique simul. Certè. Ut levissimè dicam. Sin minùs, at, Cic. Non amplius unam noctem, Virg. Minimè, Col. Vix saltem, Quint. Tamen. Quin dicas, quicquid est, Ter.
units.tr: At least] At least, Priscian. Or, if by no other means, or by usury, Terence. At the least, Varro. I will come, or if not, certainly the next day. You could come before, or if not, certainly at the same time. Certainly. To speak most lightly. But if not, yet, Cic. No more than one night, Virgil. Not at all, Columella. Scarcely at least, Quintilian. Yet. Come on, say whatever it is, Terence.

units.la: Saltus, lusus] Ascoliasmus, Empusæ ludus, Iun. Staticulus, Plaut. Saltus, pro silva. vid. Nemus.
units.tr: Leaping, play] A sport of bagpipe-leaping, the game of Empusa, Juvenal. A stationary game, Plautus. Saltus, meaning a wood, see Grove.

units.la: Salvare. Salvator, vid. Liberare, &c.
units.tr: To save. Saviour, see To free, etc.

units.la: Salubris] Salutaris ad aliquid, Cic. Pollet contra angi-nas. Pollet in remediis aurum. Præclaram virtutem habet in viribus recreandis, stomacho mulcendo. Præcipuum contra morsus remedium: ad serpentis ictus. Mentastrum torminibus efficacissimum. Perquam commodatus stomacho succus, Plin. Valet nutriendis herbis, Pallad. Ad stomachum, ad tormina vinum myrtiten, Col. Salubris aura, Salubre cœlum, Ovid. Malvæ corpori salubres, Hor. Salubre consilium: sententia Reip: salubris. Salutaris calor, civis, stella, Cic. Bonum cœlum habet, Col. Sospes cursus, Hor. Salutifer, Ovid. Salute ipsa salubrior, Eras.
units.tr: Wholesome] Helpful for something, Cic. Effective against quinsy. Effective in remedies for gold. Has a notable virtue in restoring strength and soothing the stomach. An especially useful remedy against bites, for snake strikes. Mint is most effective for gripes. A juice quite suitable for the stomach, Pliny. Good for nourishing herbs, Palladius. Wine of myrtle for the stomach and gripes, Columella. Wholesome breeze, wholesome sky, Ovid. Mallows wholesome for the body, Horace. A wholesome counsel; a wholesome opinion of the state. A healthy heat, citizen, star, Cic. It has a good sky, Columella. A safe course, Horace. Saving, Ovid. More wholesome than health itself, Erasmus.

units.la: Salutare aliquem] Salutem dicere, impertiri alicui, Cic. Impertire aliquem salute. Jubeo te salvere, Hor. Jubeo Chremetem (scil. salvere) Ter. Persalutare, Cic. Consalutare. Salutationem facere, Liv. Sospitare aliquem, Lucil. Larga donare salute, Tibul. Sternutanti salutem solito sermone fuerat imprecatus, Apul. Dare salutem. Salutem multam dicere.
units.tr: To greet someone] To say hello, to bestow greeting on someone, Cic. To give someone greetings. "I bid you be well," Horace. "I bid Chremes (namely, to be well)," Terence. To greet warmly, Cic. To greet together. To make a greeting, Livy. To wish someone health, Lucilius. To bestow generous greetings, Tibullus. He had wished the sneezer health in the usual words, Apuleius. To give greeting. To say many greetings.

units.la: Salutare se mutuò] Salutationem dare & accipere, Matrob. Salutationi amicorum se dare. Consumere tempus salutationibus. Consalutant inter se, Cic. Salvere sibi singuli dicebant, Suet. (Jungere dextram dextræ, Virg. Interjungere dextras, Liv. sunt gestus, &c.)
units.tr: To greet one another] To give and receive greeting, Macrobius. To give oneself to the greetings of friends. To spend time in greetings. They greet one another, Cic. Each said "farewell" to the other, Suetonius. (To join right hand to right hand, Virgil. To join hands together, Livy: these are gestures, etc.)

units.la: Salutare advenientem] Cic. Salutatum aliquem venire. Salvum venisse aliquem gaudere, Cic. Salvum advenisse gaudere. Adventum alicui gratulari, Ter. Ut te fortissime Teucrum accipio, agnoscoque lubens, Virg. Venienti dare salutem atque osculum. Ferre osculum adversus illam occupa, Plaut. Facere salutationem, Liv.
units.tr: To greet one arriving] Cic. To be greeted as one who has come. To rejoice that someone has come safely, Cic. To rejoice that one has arrived safely. To congratulate someone on his coming, Terence. "As I receive you, bravest of the Teucrians, and gladly acknowledge you," Virgil. To give greeting and a kiss to one coming. Take hold of her and offer a kiss, Plautus. To make a greeting, Livy.

units.la: Salutare per literas] Scribere alicui salutem, Plin. Salutem digitis scriptam alicui mittere, Plaut. Mittere, adscribere alicui salutem. Misit ad me qui mihi salutem nunciaret. Salutem mihi tuis verbis nunciavit, Cic. Annunciare alicui salutem, Id. Dic à me illi salutem. Salvebis à meo Cicerone. Id. Mandare alicui salutem, Ovid. Referilli gaudere, & rem bene gerere, Hor.
units.tr: Greeting by letter: to write greetings to someone, Plin.; to send someone greetings written with the fingers, Plaut.; to send, to add greetings to someone. He sent to me one who was to bring me greetings. He conveyed greetings to me in your words, Cic.; to announce greetings to someone, Id.; say greetings from me to him. You will be greeted from my Cicero, Id.; to commission greetings to someone, Ovid.; to report that he rejoices and is doing well, Hor.

units.la: Salutatio] Consalutatio. Salus; ut, mitto salutem, Cic. Salve: & salve addito, Apul.
units.tr: Greeting: a mutual greeting. Salutation; as, to send greetings, Cic. "Salve," and "salve" with an addition, Apul.

units.la: · Salutator] Salutiger, Apul. Salutigerus, Plaut. Matutinum portans Ave, Mart. Communis amicus unum salutandi verbum per omnia portans, Manil. Qui salutationum publicum exercet, Sen. Salutaris porta, (à salutationibus, quæ ibi fiebant, dicta) Fest. Salutatorius, eodem sensu, Plin.
units.tr: · One who greets: bringing greetings, Apul.; bringing greetings, Plaut.; bringing a morning "Ave", Mart.; a common friend carrying a single word of greeting through every matter, Manil.; one who makes a public business of greetings, Sen.; the Salutary Gate (so called from the greetings that were given there), Fest.; salutatorius, in the same sense, Plin.

units.la: Salve] Ave Osce, Sen. Ave Cæsar victor, Macrob. Salve multùm. Salvus sis. Peregrè advenientem aliquem salvâ salute impertit aliquis. Bonâ salute advenis. Venire salvum volupe est. Porrige ad salutem brachium. Cedo manum actutum. Optimè in tempore advenis. Salve, salvus cùm advenis. Salutem propitiam mihi atque vobis nuncio. Salutem tibi propino plenis faucibus. Ut ego te lubens salvum conspicio! Plaut. Conspectus tuus est mihi multo jucundissimus. Conspectus tuus reficit & recreat mentem meam, Cic. Salvum te advenisse gaudeo, Ter. Venire salvum gaudeo, Plaut.
units.tr: Salve: "Hail, Osce," Sen.; "Hail, victorious Caesar," Macrob.; hearty greetings. May you be well. A stranger arriving is given a safe greeting by someone. You arrive in good health. It is a joy to come back safe. Hold out your arm in greeting. Give me your hand at once. You arrive at just the right time. Hail, you come safe. I bring favourable greetings to me and to you. I drink your health with full throat. How gladly I see you safe! Plaut. Your sight is most pleasing to me, Cic. Your sight refreshes and restores my mind. I rejoice that you have arrived safe, Ter. I am glad you have come back safe, Plaut.

units.la: Sambucus] Ardum (S. Aridum) miserrimum atque infelix lignum, Lucil.
units.tr: Elder: "Ardum" (or "Aridum"), a most wretched and unlucky piece of wood, Lucil.

units.la: Sanabilis] Medicabilis arte, Ovid. Genus vulneris sanabile, Cic. Recipit curationem, Celf. (Per sanare, Percurare, Plin.)
units.tr: Curable: curable by art, Ovid. A kind of wound that can be healed, Cic. admits of treatment, Celf. (To heal thoroughly, to cure completely, Plin.)

units.la: Sanare] Sanum facere aliquem, Cic. Restituere aliquem sanitati, & alicui sanitatem, Plin. Reddere alicui sanitatem. Explere curationem, Celf. Restituere alicui salutem. Reducere medicinam ad salutem. Dare salutem. Esse saluti, Cic. Præsanare, Plin. Curare reduviam, Cic. Ad cicatricem perducere vulnus, Plin. vid. Mederi.
units.tr: To heal: to make someone sound, Cic.; to restore someone to health, and to give someone health, Plin.; to give someone back his health; to complete a cure, Celf.; to restore someone's safety; to bring medicine to a healthy result; to give health; to be a means of safety, Cic.; to heal beforehand, Plin.; to treat a hangnail, Cic.; to bring a wound to a scar, Plin. See Mederi.

units.la: Sanari] Sanescit vulnus. Consanescit, Cic. Consanatur, Col. Persanavêre cicatrices, Plin. Solidantur nervi, Plin. Obducta cicatrix, Cic. Medicamentò sanum fieri, Id.
units.tr: To be healed: the wound heals. It heals completely, Cic.; it is healed, Col.; the scars have fully healed, Plin.; the sinews grow firm, Plin.; a scar grows over, Cic.; to be made sound by medicine, Id.

units.la: Sanatio] Curatio morborum, Cic. Medela, Gell. Medicatio, Col.
units.tr: Healing: the cure of diseases, Cic.; a remedy, Gell.; medication, Col.

units.la: Sanatus] Percuratum vulnus, Curt. Præsanatus vulnera, Plin.
units.tr: Healed: a wound cured through, Curt.; wounds previously healed, Plin.

units.la: Sancire, vid. Statuere. Vetare. Sanctè. vid. Religiosè. Sanctificare, vid. Consecrare.
units.tr: To sanction, see To decree. To forbid. Holily, see Devoutly. To sanctify, see To consecrate.

units.la: Sanctitas] Sanctimonia, Cic. Sanctitudo, Acc.
units.tr: Holiness: sanctity, Cic.; sanctitude, Acc.

units.la: Sanctuarium] Adytum, Cæs. In occultis ac remotis templi, quò præter sacerdotes adire fas non est. Penetralia, Virg. Stat. Oraculum, Plin. Sanctum, & sancta, Plin. Item, Sancta sanctorum, in S. S.
units.tr: Sanctuary: the inner shrine, Caes.; in the secret and remote parts of the temple, where it is not lawful for anyone but the priests to enter. Innermost chambers, Virg., Stat.; the oracle, Plin.; the holy place and the holy of holies, Plin.; likewise, the Holy of Holies, in S.S.

units.la: Sanctus] Sanctissimus vir: sanctus & religiosus, Cic. vid. Sacer.
units.tr: Holy: a most holy man; holy and devout, Cic. See Sacred.

units.la: Sandalium] Solea, a. & Soleæ, Plin. Plaut. Socculus, Plin. Pantophellos, Bud. Sicyonii calcei, Cic. Sicyonia, Pl. Lucret. Diabathra, Pl. En. Græcanicæ soleæ (sunt muliebres,) Fest.
units.tr: Sandal: a sole, a., and soles, Plin., Plaut.; a light shoe, Plin.; a Pantophellos, Bud.; Sicyonian shoes, Cic.; Sicyonian shoes, Pl., Lucret.; diabathra, Pl., En.; Greek soles (these are feminine), Fest.

units.la: Sandapila, vid. Feretrum.
units.tr: Litter, see Bier.

units.la: Sanè] Salubriter, Liv. Salubrius refrigerari, Cic. Salu-berrimè miscetur aconitum medicamentis, Plin. Salutariter uti armis. Salvè, Plaut. Saniùs, Hor. Saniter, Afran.
units.tr: Healthily: wholesomely, Liv.; more wholesome to cool, Cic.; aconite is most wholesomely mixed with medicines, Plin.; to use arms beneficially. Safely, Plaut.; more soundly, Hor.; soundly, Afran.

units.la: Sanè quidem, vid. Certè.
units.tr: Certainly indeed, see Certainly.

units.la: Sanguinare] Sanguinant pedes, Plin. Manat sanguine cicatrix, Sen. Manat culter cruore, Liv.
units.tr: To bleed: the feet bleed, Plin.; the scar oozes blood, Sen.; the knife drips with gore, Liv.

units.la: Sanguis] Sanguen, priscè. En. Var. Balsamus vitæ. Ros vitalis.
units.tr: Blood: an old form of "sanguen", En., Var.; the balm of life; the vital dew.

units.la: Sanguinem mittere] Cic. Sanguinem detrahere, Cels. Minuere, Plin. Dimittere ex capite, Tar. Detrahere ex, Col. Mittere ex, Cels. Scarificatione demere sanguinem: emittere, Col. Sanguinem incisâ venâ mittere, Cels. Incidere alicui venam, Cic. solvere, rescindere, aperire, Col. Ferire, Cels. Virg. Resolvere venas, Tac.
units.tr: To let blood: Cic.; to draw off blood, Cels.; to lessen, Plin.; to let blood from the head, Tar.; to draw from, Col.; to send out from, Cels.; to remove blood by scarification: to let out, Col.; to let blood by an incised vein, Cels.; to open someone's vein, Cic.; to loosen, cut open, open up, Col.; to strike, Cels., Virg.; to open the veins, Tac.

units.la: Sanguinem exspuere] Cels. Exscreare, Id. Sputare sanguinem, Plaut. Rejicere, Plin. Vomere, Virg. Reddere sanguinem per os, Plin. Rumices rupi, Plaut.
units.tr: To spit blood: Cels.; to expectorate, Id.; to spit blood, Plaut.; to reject, Plin.; to vomit, Virg.; to give back blood through the mouth, Plin.; "I have broken up the phlegm," Plaut.

units.la: Sanguineus] Sanguinolentus color, Ovid. Sanguilenta urina, Scribon. Subcruentus, Cels. Suffusus sanguis oculis, &, suffusi cruore oculi, Plin.
units.tr: Bloody: blood-coloured, Ovid.; bloody urine, Scribon.; somewhat bloody, Cels.; blood suffused in the eyes, &; eyes suffused with gore, Plin.

units.la: Saties] Tabo, Virg. Tabus, Carif.
units.tr: Rottenness: pus, Virg.; a putrid discharge, Carif.

units.la: Sanitas] Corporis salus. Incolumitas. Integritas corporis, Cic. Salva salus, Plaut. Valetudo commoda, Quint. Valetudinis firmitas, Plin Incolume corpus, Lucr. v. Valere.
units.tr: Health: soundness of body. Safety. Wholeness of the body, Cic.; sound safety, Plaut.; comfortable health, Quint.; firmness of health, Plin.; a sound body, Lucr. See To be strong.

units.la: Sanna, vid. Ludibrium.
units.tr: Mockery, see Ridicule.

units.la: Sanus] Benè firmus. Bellè habet. Valens, Cic. Salvus, Ter. Ter. Incolume corpus, Lucr. Sincerum, Ovid. Vegetus, Non. Vivus, Virg. Sospes, Plaut. Vacat adversâ valetudine, Caes. Corporis qualitate sanissimus, Iul. Cap. Pisce sanior, Er.
units.tr: Sound: well-built. Doing well. Strong, Cic.; safe, Ter., Ter.; a body unharmed, Lucr.; unblemished, Ovid.; vigorous, Non.; alive, Virg.; safe and sound, Plaut.; free from illness, Caes.; most sound in bodily condition, Iul. Cap.; healthier than a fish, Er.

units.la: Sanus ægrotum facile admonet] Cum rectè valemus, facile ægrotis consilia damus, Ter.
units.tr: A sound man easily advises the sick: when we are well, we readily give advice to the sick, Ter.

units.la: Sapere] Sapit illi pectus. Sapit pleno pectore, Plaut. Sapit per se, Hor. Habet mentem, Cic. Habet salem, Ter.
units.tr: To be wise: he has a sensible heart. He is wise with a full heart, Plaut.; he is wise by himself, Hor.; he has sense, Cic.; he has wit, Ter.

units.la: Sapias tandem] Ede nasturtium.
units.tr: Be wise at last: eat watercress.

units.la: Sapere alieno exemplo] Dolore alterius disce cavere tuo. Feliciter sapit, qui periculo alieno sapit. Felix, quem faciunt aliena pericula cautum.
units.tr: To be wise by another's example: learn to beware through another's pain. He is happily wise who becomes wise through another's danger. Happy is he whom other men's dangers make careful.

units.la: Sapere post factum] Novit rem factam denique stultus. Factum stultus cognoscit. Eventus stultorum magister, Liv. vid. Sero sapere.
units.tr: To be wise after the event: at last the fool learns of the deed once it is done. The fool knows the thing after it has happened. Outcome is the teacher of fools, Liv. See To be wise too late.

units.la: Sapit aliquid gustui] Sapit jucundissimè, Col. Meminit quid sapiat hoc, vel illud, Inv. Subsipit aliquid, quod non plane sapit, Var. Salivam movet, Sen.
units.tr: Something has a taste: it tastes most pleasant, Col.; he remembers how this or that tastes, Inv.; he has a slight taste of something that does not quite taste, Var.; it stirs the saliva, Sen.

units.la: Sapidè] Iucundè edere, bibere, Cic. Suavius edere, Hor. Gulosius condire, Col.
units.tr: Tastily: to eat and drink with pleasure, Cic.; to eat more agreeably, Hor.; to season more greedily, Col.

units.la: Sapidus cibus] In mensarum honore est, Cic. Suavis. In gustu tener, Plin. Salivosus. in Catal. Virg.
units.tr: Savoury food: it is in honour at the tables, Cic.; pleasant; tender to the taste, Plin.; salivating, in Catal., Virg.

units.la: Sapiens] Persapiens, sophus, catus, cordatus. Adultæ vir sapientiæ. Cui cor sapit. Sapientiâ præditus singulari. Divinâ mente & consilio præditus, Cic. Maturus animo & ævo, Ovid. Callidus rei judex, Hor. Scitum consilium, Plaut. Assecutus sapientiam. Assecutus boni summam, Sen. In quantus quantus, nihil nisi sapientia es, Ter. Magus. Corculum, Cic. Frunitus, Fest. Nestore sapientior. Omnia sua secum portat. Cui sanum est cerebrum. Sol supra horizontem elevatus.
units.tr: Wise: very wise, a sage, cunning, judicious. A man of mature wisdom. One whose heart is wise. Endowed with singular wisdom. Endowed with a divine mind and counsel, Cic.; mature in mind and age, Ovid.; a judge skilled in affairs, Hor.; a shrewd plan, Plaut.; one who has attained wisdom; who has attained the highest good, Sen.; however great you are, you are nothing but wisdom, Ter.; a sage. Dear little heart, Cic.; discreet, Fest.; wiser than Nestor. He carries all his goods with him. One whose brain is sound. The sun raised above the horizon.

units.la: Sapiens facile intelligit] Dictum puta. Sapienti sat est. Sapientem mittas, nihil ei dicas.
units.tr: The wise man easily understands: take it as said. A word is enough for the wise. Send the wise man away; say nothing to him.

units.la: Sapientissimus] Oraculorum interpres. Totus sapientia est.
units.tr: Most wise: an interpreter of oracles. Wholly wisdom.

units.la: Sapienter] Persapienter, perscienter, prudenter, ratione, magna ratione, scitè, scientissimè, Cic. Cordatè, consultè, Plaut. Consultissimè, Capitol. Non inargute, nec incallidè,
units.tr: Wisely: very wisely, very knowingly, prudently, with reason, with great reason, skilfully, most skilfully, Cic.; judiciously, deliberately, Plaut.; most deliberately, Capitol.; not sharply, nor craftily.

units.la: Sapienter dictum, Euge!] Nunc ipsa venit sapientia.
units.tr: Well said, bravo! Now wisdom itself has come.

units.la: Sapientia] Prudentia senectutis, Cic. Sal: qui habet salem, qui in te est, Ter. Cor, Jecur; En cor, en jecur, Zenod. Cratet. Bibul. Lumen mentis.
units.tr: Wisdom: the prudence of old age, Cic.; salt: one who has salt, who is within you, Ter.; heart, liver; here is heart, here is liver, Zenod., Cratet., Bibul.; the light of the mind.

units.la: Sapientia mediocris optima] Sapere est, non nimium supere, Mart. Maxima pars sapientiæ est, quædam æquo animo nescire velle, Scal.
units.tr: Moderate wisdom is best: to be wise is not to be too far above others, Mart.; the greatest part of wisdom is to be content, with a calm mind, to be willing not to know some things, Scal.

units.la: Vinum sapientiæ venenum] Sapientia vino obumbratur.
units.tr: Wine is the poison of wisdom: wisdom is overshadowed by wine.

units.la: Sapientulus] Saperda bellulus & festivus, Var. Qui solus sibi sapere videtur. Argutulus, Cic. Argutator Subargutulus, Gell. Sapientum octavus ultra peram sapit.
units.tr: A little wise man: a pretty and charming little saperda fish, Var.; one who alone seems wise to himself. A little clever one, Cic.; a clever talker, a little sub-clever one, Gell.; the eighth of the sages is wise beyond his wallet.

units.la: Sapo] Smegma, Plin. Mattiatica pila, Id. Mart.
units.tr: Soap: smegma, Plin.; a ball of Mattiacan soap, Id., Mart.

units.la: Saponarius] Saponopœus.
units.tr: Soap-maker: a soap-boiler.

units.la: Sapor] Sapientia, prosapore, Symposf. Vet. Poët. Saliva vini, Plin. turdorum, Perf. Gustulum dulce & amarum, Apul.
units.tr: Taste: wisdom; in "prosapore", Symposius, old poets; the spittle of wine, Plin.; of thrushes, Perf.; a sweet and bitter taste, Apul.

units.la: Sarcina] Vidulus, Plaut. Coactilia, pl. Apul. interpret. Joh. Bapt. Egnat. Bayf. Hippopera, (equitum saccus) Sen.
units.tr: Baggage: a travelling bag, Plaut.; packed things, plural, Apul., interpreter Joh. Bapt. Egnat. Bayf.; a horse-bag (the saddle-bag of horsemen), Sen.

units.la: Sarcinosus] Sarcinosior poëta, Apul. Mammosus pannus: mammosum pyrum Mammarum effigie. Orthomastica poma, Plin. Suffarcinatus, Plaut. In ventrem crescit cucumis, Virg. Doliaris anus, Plin. Diltentum corpus Enn. Mammatus, Sipon.
units.tr: Stuffed full: a more stuffed poet, Apul.; a breast-shaped cloth; a pear shaped like breasts, in the likeness of breasts. Breast-shaped apples, Plin.; crammed full, Plaut.; the cucumber swells into its belly, Virg.; a tub-shaped old woman, Plin.; a swollen body, Enn.; having breasts, Sipon.

units.la: Sarcire] Resarcire vestes, Cic.
units.tr: To mend: to patch clothes, Cic.

units.la: Saruclum] Sarculus, Cic.
units.tr: Hoe: a hoe, Cic.

units.la: Sarrire] Sarire, Lamb. Consarrire sulcos, Sarritor terram movere. Fossionibus excitare vineas. Fosturam facere. Bidentibus æqualiter & minutim soli terga convertere, Col. Sarculare segetes. Pulverare vineas Pallad.
units.tr: To hoe: Sarire, Lamb.; to hoe furrows together; a hoer moves the earth. To dig up vines with trenches. To make a hoeing. To turn the surface of the soil evenly and finely with a two-pronged hoe, Col.; to hoe the crops; to dust the vines, Pallad.

units.la: Sarritio] Saritio, Lamb. Sarculatio. Sartura, Plin. Sarritura, Col.
units.tr: Hoeing: Saritio, Lamb.; weeding; hoeing, Plin.; hoeing, Col.

units.la: Sarritor] Saritor, Lambr. Sartor, Plin.
units.tr: Hoer: Saritor, Lambr.; a mender, Plin.

units.la: Sartor] à sarcio] Sarcinator, Plaut. Vestitor, Lampr. Limbolarius, Plaut. Braccarius, Lampr.
units.tr: Tailor, from sarcio: a patcher, Plaut.; a clothier, Lampr.; a shoemaker of low grade, Plaut.; a trouser-maker, Lampr.

units.la: Satagere, vid. Eniti. Satan, vid. Cacodæmon.
units.tr: To strive, see To struggle. Satan, see Demon.

units.la: Saviles] Custos corporis, Fest. salutis, Quintilian. Docyryphorus, Cic. Defensor corporis, Vlp. Stipator Prætoris, Cic. Lanearius, Speculator, Suet. Spiculator, Turneb. Regiæ domus armati excubitores. Apparitur regis, Liv. Circumpedes. A pedibus. A latere alicujus. A corporis custodia.
units.tr: Bodyguards: a guard of the body, Fest.; of safety, Quintilian.; a dagger-bearer, Cic.; a defender of the body, Ulp.; attendant of the praetor, Cic.; a lancer, a scout, Suet.; a spearman, Turneb.; the armed sentries of the royal household. The king's attendant, Liv.; around the feet; from the feet. From the side of someone. From the body-guard.

units.la: Satellitium] Cohors ad custodiam corporis institu​ta, Suet. Cohors prætoria, Cic. Tac. Castra prætoria, Bud. Custodes vitæ, Lamp.
units.tr: Satellitium: A cohort set up to guard the person, Suet. A praetorian cohort, Cic. Tac. The praetorian camp, Bud. Guardians of life, Lamp.

units.la: Satiare] Exsatiare, Sil. Saturare famem epulis, Claud. Exsaturare. Afferre satietatem, Cic. Explere aliquem, Ter. Satullare, Var. Obsaturare aliquem.
units.tr: Satiare: To satiate thoroughly, Sil. To sate hunger with feasts, Claud. To glut completely. To bring on satiety, Cic. To fill someone up, Ter. To satisfy, Var. To cram someone full.

units.la: Satiari] Satiari legendo. Saturari nummis. Saturare se, Cicero. Satias me tenet hujus, Teren. Satias eum cepit amoris, Liv. Cum sat habet satias, manum de mensa tollere, Var. Satietatem ferre ex copia, Quintilian. Libidines nec expleri nec satiari ullo modo possunt, Cicero.
units.tr: Satiari: To be satisfied by reading. To be glutted with money. To sate oneself, Cicero. Satiety of this thing seizes me, Teren. Satiety of love seized him, Liv. When satiety has had enough, to take the hand from the table, Var. To bring on satiety by abundance, Quintilian. Desires can be neither filled nor satisfied in any way, Cicero.

units.la: Satietas[ Satias: ad satiatem; cum satiate, Acc. Lucr. Saturitas, Plaut. Expletio, Cic. Saties, Plin.
units.tr: Satietas: Satias: to satiety; with satiety, Acc. Lucr. Saturity, Plaut. Fullness, Cic. Satiety, Plin.

units.la: Satietas fastidium parit] Satietas fastidii mater.
units.tr: Satietas fastidium parit: Satiety is the mother of disgust.

units.la: Satis] Sat: satis superque, Cic. Affatim, Ter. Abunde, Col. Quantumvis prolationum. Largiter, Plaut. Pax, nihil amplius, Ter. Tantum, Priscian. Sat abunde. Usque affatim.
units.tr: Satis: Sat: enough and more than enough, Cic. Enough, Ter. Abundantly, Col. As much as you like of delays. Largely, Plaut. Peace, nothing more, Ter. Only, Priscian. Enough and abundantly. Enough and to spare.

units.la: Satisfacere] Satisfacere alicui rei, Cic. de aliqua re, Quint. Litare sævitiæ, Apul. id est, Exsaturare crudelitatem, Beroal. Respondere, Cic. vid Promissum solvere.
units.tr: Satisfacere: To satisfy someone in a matter, Cic. Concerning some matter, Quint. To appease cruelty, Apul. That is, to glut cruelty, Beroal. To answer, Cic. See to pay a promise.

units.la: Satius, vid. Melius est.
units.tr: Satius, see It is better.

units.la: Sativus] Delita femina, Var. stipes desertus (insitus) in agro, Tibul.
units.tr: Sativus: A woman left behind, Var. A stake left standing (or grafted) in the field, Tibul.

units.la: Satur] Saturatus. Expletus. Cibo gravis, onustus, Cic. Fessus satietate videndi, Lucr. Satullus, Var.
units.tr: Satur: Saturated. Filled. Heavy with food, laden, Cic. Weary from satiety of seeing, Lucr. Somewhat sated, Var.

units.la: Saturare, vid. Satiare.
units.tr: Saturare, see Satiare.

units.la: Saturans increpa] Ubi paveris impera.
units.tr: Saturans increpa: When you have fed, give orders.

units.la: Saturnus] Mundi splen. Sidus grave Saturni, Propert.
units.tr: Saturnus: The sphere of the world. The heavy star of Saturn, Propert.

units.la: Sauciare, vid. Vulnerare.
units.tr: Sauciare, see Vulnerare.

units.la: Saucius] Ex vulnere æger, vid. Vulneratus.
units.tr: Saucius: Sick from a wound; see Wounded.

units.la: Saxatilis] Saxetanus lacertus, Mart.
units.tr: Saxatilis: A rock-dwelling lizard, Mart.

units.la: Saxeus, vid. Lapideus. Saxum, vid. Petra.
units.tr: Saxeus, see Stony. Saxum, see Rock.

units.la: Scaber. vid. Asper. Scabere. vid. Fricare.
units.tr: Scaber, see Rough. Scabere, see Rub.

units.la: Scabies] Psora, Cels.
units.tr: Scabies: Psora, Cels.

units.la: Scabiosus] Psoricus, Plin.
units.tr: Scabiosus: Psoric, Plin.

units.la: Scabrè, vid. Asperè. Scabricia, vid. Asperitas. Scalpere, Calare, Fricare.
units.tr: Scabrè, see Roughly. Scabricia, see Roughness. Scalpere: to scratch, to scrape, to rub.

units.la: Scandalizare aliquem] Exemplo malo esse alicui, ex Terent. Exemplis laedere multos, Amm. Nocere exemplo plus, quàm peccato. Periculosam imitationem exempli reliquis in posterum prodere. Exemplum perniciosum prodere, Cicer. Mala exempla movere, Ovid. Periculum animae creare.
units.tr: Scandalizare aliquem: To be a bad example to someone, ex Terent. To injure many by examples, Amm. To do more harm by example than by sin. To hand on a dangerous imitation of an example to others in future. To set forth a pernicious example, Cicer. To stir up evil examples, Ovid. To create danger to the soul.

units.la: Scandalum datum] Offensio : occasio lapsus. Pessimi exempli factum, Liv. Exemplum malum, Sallust. Exemplum mali ; vel, mali facti, Cic. Pessimo publica aedificatae villae Metelli & Luculli, Varr.
units.tr: Scandalum datum: Offence; an occasion of falling. A deed of the worst example, Liv. A bad example, Sallust. An example of evil, or of an evil deed, Cic. The public buildings of the villas of Metellus and Lucullus, built as the worst example, Varr.

units.la: Scandalum acceptum] Offensio. Imitatio mali facti. Imitatio vitiosa. Imitatio exempli periculosa improborum, Cic.
units.tr: Scandalum acceptum: Offence. Imitation of a bad deed. Vicious imitation. The dangerous imitation of the wicked, Cic.

units.la: Scandalum accipere] Tangi exemplo alicujus Ovid. Facere aliquid, alicujus exemplo, Ter. Auctoritate & exemplo alicujus facere aliquid, Cic.
units.tr: Scandalum accipere: To be moved by someone's example, Ovid. To do something after someone's example, Ter. To do something by the authority and example of someone, Cic.

units.la: Scatebrae] Eruptio subita fontium, Sen.
units.tr: Scatebrae: A sudden outburst of springs, Sen.

units.la: Scatere aliquo] Scatere vino, Plaut. Scaturire fontibus Lucr. Sudant mella quercus, Virg. Stillant saxa guttis, Lucr. Stillo ex oculis rorem, Hor. Manare sudore, Cic. Manat picem arbor, Plin. Distillat uva, Col. Distillant per pectus aquae, Tibul. Distillant tempora nardo, Plin. Scatit terra serrarum, Lucr. à Scato.
units.tr: Scatere aliquo: To overflow with wine, Plaut. To gush with springs, Lucr. Oaks sweat honey, Virg. Rocks drip with drops, Lucr. I drip dew from my eyes, Hor. To ooze with sweat, Cic. The tree exudes pitch, Plin. The grape drips, Col. Waters trickle through the breast, Tibul. Tresses drip with nard, Plin. The earth teems with saws, Lucr. From Scato.

units.la: Scatere, absol] Scatent fontes, Cic. Prorumpit fons, Caes. Scaturire fontibus. Erumpit undae, Lucr. Erumpit liquor, Plin. Erumpit terra liquores fontibus, Tibul. Exsilit e saxo fretum, Ovid. Scatit fons, Lucr.
units.tr: Scatere, absol: The springs gush, Cic. The spring bursts forth, Caes. To gush from springs. The water erupts, Lucr. The liquid bursts forth, Plin. The earth pours out liquids from its springs, Tibul. The sea leaps out of the rock, Ovid. The spring gushes, Lucr.

units.la: Scaturigo] Scatebra fonticuli semper emicans, Plin. Latices perennes, Lucr. Caput fluminis, fontis, Virg. Capita fontium, Varr. Caput aquae. Eruptio subita amnis ex abdito, Sen. Fons perennis aquae, Plin. Fons jugis aquae, Hor. Aquae perennes, Cic. Rivus perennis, Plin. Iun. Fons vivus, Ovid.. Manalis fons, Fest. Aqua viva, Var. Fonticulus, Plin.
units.tr: Scaturigo: A little spring always welling up, Plin. Perennial streams, Lucr. The head of a river or spring, Virg. Heads of springs, Varr. Head of water. A sudden outburst of a stream from a hidden place, Sen. A perennial spring of water, Plin. A constant flow of water, Hor. Perennial waters, Cic. A perennial stream, Plin. Iun. A living spring, Ovid. A welling spring, Fest. Living water, Var. A small spring, Plin.

units.la: Scaurus, vid. Valgus.
units.tr: Scaurus, see Valgus.

units.la: Sceleste] Scelerate, flagitiose, flagitiosissime, Nefarie, Nequiter, nequissime. Improbe, improbissime. Per scelus & latrocinium, Cic. Per nequitiam, Vlp.
units.tr: Sceleste: Wickedly, villainously, most villainously, abominably, most abominably. Improperly, most improperly. Through crime and robbery, Cic. Through wickedness, Vlp.

units.la: Scelestus] Sceleratus, consceleratus, flagitiosus, profligatus ac perditus. Plenus sceleris. Scelere praeditus. Nefarius. Ille sceleratissimus, ex omnium scelerum colluvione natus. Omnium scelerum maculis notatissimus, Cic. Maximorum scelerum molitor, Sen. Scelerosus. Scelus, Ter. Scelus viri, Plaut. Maligniffimum caput, Sen. Carcer, vix carcere dignus, Lucr. Certus sceleris, Tac. Desperatissimus latro, extremae poenae certus, Apul.
units.tr: Scelestus: Wicked, utterly wicked, villainous, abandoned and lost. Full of crime. Endowed with crime. Abominable. That most wicked man, born from a heap of all crimes. Marked with the stains of every crime, Cic. A contriver of the greatest crimes, Sen. Criminal. A villain, Ter. A villain of a man, Plaut. The most malignant head, Sen. A prison, scarcely worthy of prison, Lucr. Certain of crime, Tac. The most desperate robber, certain of the extreme penalty, Apul.

units.la: Scelus] Flagitium, Ter. Facinus sceleris. Scelus atrox, indignissimum, insigne, nefarium. Scelestum facinus. Atrocitas peccati, Cicero. Capital, Plautus. Infanda res.
units.tr: Scelus: A disgrace, Ter. A heinous deed. An atrocious, most unworthy, notorious, abominable crime. A wicked deed. The atrocity of sin, Cicero. A capital crime, Plautus. An unspeakable thing.

units.la: Sceptrum] Hasta pura, Virg.
units.tr: Sceptrum: A plain spear, Virg.

units.la: Schola] Ludus literarius, Quint. Ludus discendi. Officina discendi. Gymnasium, Lyceum, Palaestra, Cic. Paedagogium, Sen. Plin. Humanitatis officina. Literaria palaestra. Musarum officina, janua. Seminarium sapientiae. Seminarium virorum. Equus Trojanus.
units.tr: Schola: A school, Quint. A place of learning. A workshop of learning. Gymnasium, lyceum, wrestling-ground, Cic. Paedagogium, Sen. Plin. A workshop of humanity. A literary wrestling-ground. A workshop and gateway of the Muses. A seminary of wisdom. A seminary of men. The Trojan horse.

units.la: Schola Poetica] Parnassus.
units.tr: Schola Poetica: Parnassus.

units.la: Scholasticus] Scholicus, Gell. Literarius, Plinius. Studiosa quaestio, Quintilian. Homo de schola. Scholastes.
units.tr: Scholasticus: A scholar, Gell. Literary, Plinius. A studious question, Quintilian. A man of the school. A scholar.

units.la: Sciatherícon] Solium, sciothericum horologium, Plin. Solarium, Cic. Solis proditor.
units.tr: Sciatherícon: A seat; a hemispherical sundial, Plin. A sundial, Cic. A betrayer of the sun.

units.la: Sciens, vid. Gnarus.
units.tr: Sciens, see Knowing.

units.la: Scienter] Sciens nihil praetermisi. Vivus & videns. Prudens & sciens ad interitum ruebam. Sciens prudensque, Cic. Prudens, Plin.
units.tr: Scienter: Knowing, I have omitted nothing. Alive and seeing. Prudently and knowingly I rushed to ruin. Knowingly and wittingly, Cic. Prudently, Plin.

units.la: Scientia] Scientiola, Arnob. Intelligentia. Cognitio, Cic. Notitia rerum maximarum, Cic. Portus miseriae ars.
units.tr: Scientia: A little knowledge, Arnob. Understanding. Knowledge, Cic. Knowledge of the greatest things, Cic. Art is a harbour of misery.

units.la: Scientia frustillata] De omnibus aliquid, de toto nihil.
units.tr: Scientia frustillata: About everything something, about the whole nothing.

units.la: Scilicet, vid. Quasi vero.
units.tr: Scilicet, see As if indeed.

units.la: Scindere] Concidere aliquid, Plin. Profecare exta, Sen. Conficere offatim, Cic. vid. Secare.
units.tr: Scindere: To cut up something, Plin. To cut out the entrails, Sen. To cut up piece by piece, Cic. See Secare.

units.la: Scintilla] Scintillula, Cic. Igniculus, Lucil. Stricturæ, è ferro ferventi scintillæ exeuntes, Virg. Non.
units.tr: Scintilla: A little spark, Cic. A little fire, Lucil. Sparks flying out of hot iron, Virg. Non.

units.la: Scintillare] Scintillas agere, Lucr.
units.tr: Scintillare: To throw off sparks, Lucr.

units.la: Scintillatio] Tremulæ radiationis vibratio.
units.tr: Scintillatio: A trembling vibration of radiance.

units.la: Scio] Dictum puta, Ter.
units.tr: Scio: Consider it said, Ter.

units.la: Sciolus] Qui solus sibi sapere videtur, Cic. Ipsa sapientia, Ter. Belluli & festivi saperdae, Var. Superat omnes argutando præficas, Plaut. Novit quid toto fiat in orbe, Perendinum ventum praedicere.
units.tr: Sciolus: One who alone seems wise to himself, Cic. Wisdom itself, Ter. Little witty herrings, Var. He surpasses all in chattering like professional mourners, Plaut. He knows what is happening in the whole world; he can predict a wind two days ahead.

units.la: Scipio] Bacillum, Cic.
units.tr: Scipio: A little staff, Cic.

units.la: Scire] Nosse, Tenere. Non ignorare. Habere, tenere scientiam. Habere in aliqua re scientiam. Scientia aliquid comprehendere. Tenere animo: causas rationemque rerum callere, noscere jura, Esse scientem, gnarum, peritum, intelligentem alicujus rei. Percallere usum rerum. Non sum nescius. Non me fugit. Constat mihi aliquid & de aliqua re. Tenere aliquid probe. Sic habetote, Cic. Habeo quid agam, Ter. Notum, apertum, perspectum est mihi aliquid, Cic.
units.tr: Scire: To know, to hold. Not to be ignorant. To have, hold knowledge. To have knowledge in some matter. To grasp something by knowledge. To hold in mind: to understand the causes and reason of things, to know the laws; to be knowing, aware, skilled, understanding of some thing. To have thorough practical knowledge of things. I am not unaware. It does not escape me. It is established for me about something. To hold something well. Thus you should consider, Cic. I know what I am to do, Ter. Something is known, open, clear to me, Cic.

units.la: Scire certo] Habere exploratum: pro certo. Est mihi pro explorato, Exploratum, exploratissimum, perspectum mihi est. Compertum habere de aliqua re, Cic. Compertum est mihi de, Sal. Comperi aliquid: de re aliqua. Manifesto comperi, & manu teneo. Comperi certis autoribus, Cic. Comperi certis indiciis, Liv. Ad plenum nosse, Veget. Constat mihi ratio impensae, Sen. Non sum animi dubius, Virg. Non me fallit animi, Lucr. Cognitum habeo. Nemini dubium. Non me praeterit, fugit, latet, fallit. Haud me falsum habet, Eras.
units.tr: Scire certo: To have as explored; for certain. It is explored for me; I have it thoroughly explored and clearly seen. To have learned about some matter, Cic. It has been learned by me about, Sal. I have learned something about a matter. I learned it clearly and hold it in my hand. I learned it from certain authors, Cic. I learned it from certain signs, Liv. To know fully, Veget. The account of expense is established for me, Sen. I am not doubtful in mind, Virg. It does not escape my mind, Lucr. I have it known. To no one doubtful. It does not escape me, is not hidden from me, does not deceive me. It does not hold me in error, Eras.

units.la: Scito] Dixi, Ter. Ne sis nescius, Cic. Ut sis sciens, Teren. Dictum est, Plautus. Haec, quae scivi, ut scires curari omnia, Insciens ne sis. Tenes? Id. Memineris tibi id praedictum.
units.tr: Scito: I have said, Ter. Lest you be ignorant, Cic. That you may be aware, Teren. It has been said, Plautus. Know that I have cared for everything you should know. Lest you be unaware. Do you understand? Id. Remember that this was foretold to you.

units.la: Sciscitari] Sciscitare sententiam alicujus: ex aliquo, Cic. sciscere, Plaut. Scitari nomen, Ovid. Requirere res novas. Anquirere. Perscrutari, Plaut. Indefessa scitatione percunctari, Amm. Vise, revise quid agat, Teren. vid. Disquirere.
units.tr: Sciscitari: To ask someone's opinion of someone, Cic. To ask, Plaut. To seek after a name, Ovid. To seek new things. To inquire. To search through, Plaut. To question tirelessly, Amm. Go and see, and revisit what he is doing, Ter. See Disquirere.

units.la: Scisçitatio] Scitatio, Amm. Disquisitio. Inquisitio, investigatio veri, Cic. Discussio, Macrob. Examinatio, Ulp. Scrutatio, Sen. Requisitio, Gell.
units.tr: Sciscitatio: Inquiry, Amm. Investigation. Inquiry, investigation of the truth, Cic. Discussion, Macrob. Examination, Ulp. Scrutiny, Sen. Requisition, Gell.

units.la: Scisçitator] Discussor rerum diligens, Macrob. Inquisitor rerum. Investigator, Cicero. Perquisitor actionum, Plautus. Examinator scrupulosus, Amm. Scrutator, Luc. Portitor, Plaut.
units.tr: Sciscitator: A diligent examiner of things, Macrob. An inquirer into things. An investigator, Cicero. A questioner into actions, Plautus. A scrupulous examiner, Amm. A scrutinizer, Luc. A toll-collector, Plaut.

units.la: Scissor cibi in convivio] Creodates, Rader. Edeatra, & Edeatres, Fest. Incisor, Crom. Scindendi obsonii magister, Sen. Diribitor, Apul.
units.tr: Scissor cibi in convivio: Creodates, Rader. Edeatra and Edeatres, Fest. Carver, Crom. The master of carving the dishes, Sen. Diribitor, Apul.

units.la: Scitè, Scitus. vid. Artificiosè &c. Scius vid. Gnarus.
units.tr: Scitè, Scitus: see Skilfully etc. Scius, see Knowing.

units.la: Scobs.] Scobis eburnea, Lanugo quam excitat tenebra, Colon. Ramentum terebrae, Idem. Serrago cervini cornu, Iun.
units.tr: Scobs: Ivory shavings; the fluff which the darkness raises, Colon. The shavings of a borer, Idem. Sawdust of deer's horn, Iun.

units.la: Scomma, vid. Dicterium.
units.tr: Scomma, see Gibe.

units.la: Scopae] Scopas, Syros vocat Var. ap. Non.
units.tr: Scopae: Brooms; Varro calls them Syros, Var. ap. Non.

units.la: Scopulae] Scopulae vestiariae, ut apud Caton. Scopulae virgeae, ulmeae, & ap. Col. myrteae extergendis intus doliis vinariis.
units.tr: Scopulae: Clothes-cloths, as in Cato. Rods of willow and elm, and, in Columella, of myrtle, for wiping out the insides of wine casks.

units.la: Scopulus] Rupes scopulosa, Lucan. vid. Petra.
units.tr: Scopulus] A rocky crag, full of cliffs, Lucan. See Petra.

units.la: Scopus] Scopus huic est. Finis, mens, consilium. Exitum propositus. Propositum, Cicero. Omnis labor aliquo respiciat, aliquò referatur, Sen. Intentio, apud Plinius.
units.tr: Scopus] He has this as his aim: end, intention, plan. To set out a goal. Purpose, Cicero. All labour should aim at something and be referred to something, Sen. Intention, apud Plinius.

units.la: Scoria] Scoriae aeris, argenti, plumbi, &c. Helcysma, scoria argenti, Plin. Recrementum plumbi, Caes.
units.tr: Scoria] Dross of copper, silver, lead, etc. Helcysma [ἕλκυσμα], dross of silver, Plin. Refuse of lead, Caes.

units.la: Scorpio] Scorpius, Ovid.
units.tr: Scorpio] Scorpion, Ovid.

units.la: Scortari vid. Libidinari.
units.tr: To whore, see Libidinari.

units.la: Scortatis] Scortatus, Apul, Meretricium facere. Suet. Publicata pudicitia, Tac.
units.tr: Scortatis] Whored, Apul. To make oneself a prostitute, Suet. Chastity made public, Tac.

units.la: Scortator] Ganeo, Cic. Amator, Id. Amatorculus. Patres conventii, Plaut. Ancilariolus, Mart. Sen. Mulierarius, Muret. Embasicoeta, Petron. Perambulans omnium cubilia, Catul. Venerivaga, à Venerivagus, habet Var. Venereus, Cic. vid. Libidinosus.
units.tr: Scortator] Debauchee, Cic. Lover, Id. Little lover. Fathers of the assembly, Plaut. Hanger-on of lovers, Mart., Sen. Womanizer, Muret. Embasicoeta [ἐμβασικοίτης], Petron. One who roams through everyone's bedrooms, Catul. Wanderer after Venus, from Venerivagus, Var. has it. Venereal, Cic. See Libidinosus.

units.la: Screare] Exscreare, Ovid. Attrahere salivam, Sen. Trochleis pituitam adducere, Quint. Bud. Gargarizare, Celf.
units.tr: Screare] To cough up, Ovid. To draw in spittle, Sen. To bring phlegm up by pulleys, Quint. Bud. To gargle, Celf.

units.la: Screatus] Gargarizatio, Plin.
units.tr: Screatus] Gargling, Plin.

units.la: Scriba] Scriptor. Magister scripturæ, Cic. Ab epistolis, Suet. A commentariis, Hieron. vid. Amanuensis.
units.tr: Scriba] Writer. Teacher of writing, Cic. Secretary of correspondence, Suet. Keeper of records, Hieron. See Amanuensis.

units.la: Scribere] Pangere aliquid, Conscribere. Conficere epistolam. Componere librum, commentarium. Scriptum relinquere. Mandare literis, scriptis, monumentis. Commendare monumentis. Prosequi scriptura, literis. Prodere aliquid memoriæ literis, monumentis. Consignare literis: literis publicis. Condere carmen. Excudere aliquid de gloria. Elimare, evigilare, elucubrare, & ti, expolire aliquid, Cic. Signare aliquid stylo, Paterc. In literas dare aliquid, Macr. tradere, mittere, Spart. Facere scripturam, Liv. (Proprie, Notarii) Stylum exercere.
units.tr: Scribere] To compose something, to draw up. To write a letter. To compose a book or a commentary. To leave something in writing. To commit to letters, writings, records. To commend to records. To pursue in writing or in letters. To hand something down to memory in letters or records. To set down in letters; in public records. To compose a poem. To coin something for glory. To polish, to keep vigil over, to labour over and refine something, Cic. To mark something with the stylus, Paterc. To put something into letters, Macr. To deliver or send, Spart. To make a written record, Liv. (Properly, of notaries.) To practise the pen.

units.la: Scribere plus licet, quàm loqui] Epistola non erubescit.
units.tr: Writing is allowed more than speaking] A letter does not blush.

units.la: Scribere in publicum] Cœlo ac terræ loqui.
units.tr: Scribere in publicum] To speak to heaven and earth.

units.la: Scribere epistolam] Scribere literas ad aliquem: de aliquare, Cic. Scribere alicui, Plaut. Scriptare, Hor. Litera peratratur, Ovid. Exarare, texere epistolam. Literis appellare, loqui. Per literas colloqui cum alio, Cic. Literas ad aliquem dare, Id. Facere literas scil. in cerâ, Plaut.
units.tr: Scribere epistolam] To write letters to someone about something, Cic. To write to someone, Plaut. To write often, Hor. The letter is carried through, Ovid. To draw up, to weave a letter. To address someone by letter, to speak to. To converse with another by letter, Cic. To give a letter to someone, Id. To make letters, namely on wax, Plaut.

units.la: Scribere dictata] Excipere dictata, Bud. Excipere aliquid notis velocissimè. Suet. Excipere alicujus orationem, Sen.
units.tr: Scribere dictata] To take down dictation, Bud. To take down something very swiftly in shorthand, Suet. To take down someone's speech, Sen.

units.la: Scribendo se exercere] Exercere stylum, Cicero. Operam dare stylo, Sueton. Stylo limare & ornare orationem, Cicero. Literarum formas propriis ductibus lineare, Martial.
units.tr: Scribendo se exercere] To exercise oneself in writing. To practise the pen, Cicero. To devote effort to writing, Suet. To polish and adorn a speech with the pen, Cicero. To trace the forms of letters with one's own strokes, Martial.

units.la: Scribere celeriter per abbreviaturas] Scribere per compendia, Solin. Notis scribere, Varr. Quantum notando consequi potuerunt, Virgil. Currat sermo licet: manus est velocior illis; Nondum lingua suum, dextra peregit opus, Martial. Litera mihi verbum est. Notis linguam superare, cursumque loquentis excipiens longas nova per compendia voces, Manil. Notis quamvis citatam exexcipere orationem. Celeritatem linguæ manus sequitur, Sidon.
