units.tr: Scribere celeriter per abbreviaturas] To write quickly by abbreviations. To write by shorthand, Solin. To write in notes, Varr. As much as they could keep up with by noting, Virgil. Let the speech run on; the hand is quicker than they are, the tongue has not yet finished its work when the right hand has, Martial. A letter is a word to me. To outrun speech with signs, catching the speaker's course and taking long words into new abbreviations, Manil. To take down even a rapidly delivered speech in notes. The hand follows the speed of the tongue, Sidon.

units.la: Scrinium. vid. Arca.
units.tr: Scrinium. See Arca.

units.la: Scriptum] Scriptio, Varr. Litera, Cic.
units.tr: Scriptum] Writing, Varr. A letter, Cic.

units.la: Scriptum severum rem definiens] Decretorius stylus.
units.tr: Scriptum severum rem definiens] A decisive pen, settling the matter.

units.la: Scripto agere] Ex syngraphâ agere. Obsignatis tabellis agere.
units.tr: Scripto agere] To act on a written agreement. To proceed on sealed tablets.

units.la: Scriptura sacra] Divini libri. Sanctæ literæ. Divinorum librorum, vel divinarum legum monumenta. Sanctæ religionis literæ, Lact. Epistola Creatoris ad creaturam.
units.tr: Scriptura sacra] The divine books. The holy letters. The records of the divine books or divine laws. The letters of holy religion, Lact. The letter of the Creator to the creature.

units.la: Scriptus] Auro literata lacinia, Apul. Scriptiles formæ, Amm.
units.tr: Scriptus] A hem embroidered with gold, Apul. Written shapes, Amm.

units.la: Scrupulose, Scrupulosus, vid. Accuratus.
units.tr: Scrupulose, Scrupulosus, see Accuratus.

units.la: Scrutari] Perscrutari, Vestigare causas, Cic. Rimari, est valdè quærere in rimis quoque, Fest. Ruspari, Id. vid. Quærere. Indagare.
units.tr: Scrutari] To search thoroughly. To investigate causes, Cic. To rummage means to search very eagerly, even in the cracks, Fest. To ransack, Id. See Quærere. Indagare.

units.la: Scrutator, vid. Sciscitator.
units.tr: Scrutator, see Sciscitator.

units.la: Sculpere, Sculptor, vid. Cælare &c.
units.tr: Sculpere, Sculptor, see Cælare &c.

units.la: Scurra] Scurra Articus. Sinnio, Cic. Morio, Mart. Caprea, Suet. Sectator assiduus, Lucil. Gelasianus, Sidon. Morologus, Plaut. Oscus. Petulans atque improbus scurra, Cicero. Scurrilis homo, Quintilian. Opicus. Spurcidicus; Plaut.
units.tr: Scurra] Attic jester. Sinnio, Cic. Morio, Mart. Caprea, Suet. Constant follower, Lucil. Gelasianus, Sidon. Morologus, Plaut. Oscus. A pert and wicked buffoon, Cicero. A buffoonish man, Quintilian. Opicus. Foul-mouthed, Plaut.

units.la: Scurrari] Morologis uti sermonibus, Plaut. Oscè fabulari, Titin. Scurriliter ludere, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Scurrari] To use buffoonish talk, Plaut. To talk in the Oscan manner, Titin. To play the buffoon, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Scurrilis] Ludibriosus, Gell. Derisorius, Ulp. Joculare & à multis derisum, Cic. Diasyrticum dictum, Spart. Lusorius, Sen. Ad jocum & risum factus, Cic. Ludicer, Ludicrus, Gell.
units.tr: Scurrilis] Mocking, Gell. Derisive, Ulp. A joke laughed at by many, Cic. Called a jest, Spart. Playful, Sen. Made for jest and laughter, Cic. Ludicer, Ludicrus, Gell.

units.la: Scurrilitas, vid. Ludibrium. Scurriliter. vid. Ludibriosè.
units.tr: Scurrilitas, see Ludibrium. Scurriliter, see Ludibriosè.

units.la: Scutum, vid. Parma.
units.tr: Scutum, see Parma.

units.la: Se & sua quisque maximè sentit] Domesticum omne afficit.
units.tr: Se & sua quisque maximè sentit] Everyone feels most keenly what concerns himself and his own household.

units.la: Se habere, est bonum] Qui se habet, nihil perdidit.
units.tr: Se habere, est bonum] Whoever keeps himself has lost nothing.

units.la: Se nemo novit] Nemo manticæ quod in tergo est novit. Se & suis quisque pro libitu utitur] Domi suæ quisque Rex.
units.tr: Se nemo novit] No one knows what is on his own back in the wallet. Se & suis quisque pro libitu utitur] Each man is king in his own house.

units.la: A se & suis ordiri] A lare ordiri. (Proverb. à ritu gentilium, qui sacrificiorum primitiar, Lari domestico offerebant) Ædibus in nostris quæ prava aut recta geruntur. In sinum tuum inspice.
units.tr: A se & suis ordiri] To begin from oneself and one's own; to begin from the hearth. (A proverb from the custom of the Gentiles, who offered the first-fruits of sacrifices to the household Lar.) What is done rightly or wrongly in our houses: look into your own bosom.

units.la: Se vincere, est invictum esse] Qui se vincit, à nemine vinci potest.
units.tr: Se vincere, est invictum esse] He who conquers himself can be conquered by no one.

units.la: Secare aliquid] Secare ac dividere animal, Cic. Concidere securi ligna, Ovid. Cædere saginam, Plaut. Cædere arbores, Cic. silvam, Cæs. Scindere quercum, Virg. Proscindere quercum ferro, Lucan.
units.tr: Secare aliquid] To cut and divide an animal, Cic. To chop wood with an axe, Ovid. To carve meat, Plaut. To fell trees, Cic. A forest, Caes. To split an oak, Virg. To cut down an oak with iron, Lucan.

units.la: Secare in frusta aliquid] Secare in partes, Cic. Discindere aliquid in partes, Lucr. Frusta facere, Col. Facere furtum ex aliquo. Faciam ut hic te formicæ fustillatim differant, Plaut.
units.tr: Secare in frusta aliquid] To cut into pieces, Cic. To divide something into parts, Lucr. To make into bits, Col. To steal from someone. I will have the ants tear you to bits piece by piece, Plaut.

units.la: Secedere, solum vel cum alio] Inferre se in aliquem locum sine arbitris, Liv. Seducere me debeo, Sen. Seducere aliquem solum, Ter. Singulos separatim seductos obtestantur, Liv. Prehendere hominem solum, Tac. Sevocare aliquem. Sevocare se ab aliquo, Plaut. Concedamus huc, sine arbitris locum capiamus. Cauto & capto loco loquendi agere. Cavere ne eo, Cic.
units.tr: Secedere, solum vel cum alio] To go into some place without witnesses, Liv. I ought to withdraw myself, Sen. To lead someone aside alone, Ter. They entreat the men taken aside one by one, Liv. To take hold of a man alone, Tac. To call someone aside. To withdraw oneself from someone, Plaut. Let us withdraw here and take a place without witnesses. To hold a talk in a cautious and chosen place. To take care lest..., Cic.

units.la: Secedere ad officia naturæ] Sext. Aurel Vict. Ad officia naturalia secedere, Secedere ad secreta ventris, Cels. Ad requisita naturæ discedere, Spart. Ire quò saturi solent, Plaut. Desurgere, Scribon. vid. Oletare.
units.tr: Secedere ad officia naturæ] Sext. Aurel Vict. To withdraw to the natural functions; to withdraw to the privy of the belly, Cels. To go off to the needs of nature, Spart. To go where the sated usually go, Plaut. To rise up, Scribon. See Oletare.

units.la: Secessio] Seductio subscriptorum. Avocatio, revocatio alicujus à vel, ab, Cic. Flexus: flexu eludere, Quint. Flexio, Cic. Secessus, Plin. Recessus collium, Mart. Seductus recessus, Ovid. Diverticula & flexiones quærere, Cic. Secretarium, Apul.
units.tr: Secessio] Enticing away of the signatories. Drawing away, recall of someone from or by, Cic. A bend: to elude by a turn, Quint. A bending, Cic. A retreat, Plin. Recesses of hills, Mart. A secluded recess, Ovid. To seek out byways and turnings, Cic. A private room, Apul.

units.la: Secius, vid. Pejus, Minus. Secludere, vid. Excludere, Separare.
units.tr: Secius, see Pejus, Minus. Secludere, see Excludere, Separare.

units.la: Secretarius] A secretis consiliis, epistolis: A secretis, Bud. Ab aure, Iun. Silentiarius & auricularius, in Cod.
units.tr: Secretarius] Secretary for secret counsels and letters. Secretary, Bud. Confidant, Iun. Silent and whispering secretary, in Cod.

units.la: Secretum, vid. Arcanum. Secretus, vid. Arcanus, Separatus.
units.tr: Secretum, see Arcanum. Secretus, see Arcanus, Separatus.

units.la: Sella] Factio, pars, Disciplina, Hæresis, familia philosophorum. Via & ratio vitæ. Certa quædam disciplinæ formula, Cic.
units.tr: Secta] Faction, party, school, heresy, a company of philosophers. A way and rule of life. A certain fixed formula of teaching, Cic.

units.la: Sectator, vid. Imitator.
units.tr: Sectator, see Imitator.

units.la: Sectura alicujus rei] Defectio stramentorum pecori utilis, Col. Conciliura, Sen. Confectio arborum ad calfaciendum, Cic. Cæsio arborum, Col. Cæsura tempestiva arborum, Plin. Scissus materiæ, Var. Succisio lignorum, in SS.
units.tr: Sectura alicujus rei] Cutting of litter useful to cattle, Col. A cutting back, Sen. Felling of trees for warmth, Cic. Felling of trees, Col. Timely pruning of trees, Plin. A cut of timber, Varr. Cutting of wood, in SS.

units.la: Secula] Falx, Cic. Falx fœnaria, Var. Falx lunata à tergo acuta, (quales pellionum, &c.) Pallad.
units.tr: Secula] A sickle, Cic. A hay-sickle, Varr. A crescent-shaped sickle, sharp at the back (such as those of furriers), Pallad.

units.la: Seculum, vid. Ævum.
units.tr: Seculum, see Ævum.

units.la: Secundarius] Secundarum partium, Cic. Secundæ notæ mel, Col. Optimis proximus, Cic. secundi meriti ager, Pallad. Secundæ sententiæ senator, Spartian. Beta, Mart. Non ineptissimus. Non inepti homines. Minimè aspernandus. Non contemnendus. Minimè vulgaris. Tolerabilis orator. Melius in pessimis nihil fuit, Cic. Haud pœnitendus magister, Liv.
units.tr: Secundarius] Of second rank, Cic. Honey of the second grade, Col. Next to the best, Cic. A field of second quality, Pallad. A senator of the second opinion, Spartian. Beet, Mart. Not the least incompetent. Men not incompetent. By no means to be despised. Not to be scorned. By no means common. A tolerable orator. Nothing was better among the worst, Cic. A teacher not to be regretted, Liv.

units.la: Secundo] Deinceps. Iterum, Cic. Iterato, Vlp.
units.tr: Secundo] Next, in succession. Again, Cic. Repeatedly, Ulp.

units.la: Secundum, vid. Iuxta.
units.tr: Secundum, see Iuxta.

units.la: Secundus] Secundus à Rege, Hirt. Secundus alicui, Ovid. Sil. Alter; quod est è tribus officiis oratoris alterum, Cic. Alter ab undecimo, Virg.
units.tr: Secundus] Second to the king, Hirt. Second to someone, Ovid. Sil. Another; which is the second of the three duties of an orator, Cic. Second from the eleventh, Virg.

units.la: Securè] Tutò, tutè, tutissimè, fidenter, liberè, Cic. Otiosè, Ter. Fidissimè, Cic.
units.tr: Securè] Safely, most safely, confidently, freely, Cic. At leisure, Ter. Most confidently, Cic.

units.la: Securitas inducit mala] Securitas calamitatis indicium, Val. Max.
units.tr: Securitas inducit mala] Security is a sign of calamity, Val. Max.

units.la: Securus] Securi animi homo, Cic. Otiosus animus, Ter. vid. Tutus.
units.tr: Securus] A man of carefree mind, Cic. A mind at leisure, Ter. See Tutus.

units.la: Securum esse] Securus sum alicujus rei, Tac. Componere se in securitatem, Id. Sedere. In tuto, in tranquillo esse. In vado res est. In portu navigare, Cic. Ter. In portu dormire. Utroque oculo, in utramque aurem dormire. Extra hutum habere pedes. Extra telorum jactum. Anchorâ non vulgari nititur. Portum tangere.
units.tr: Securum esse] I am free from anxiety about something, Tac. To settle oneself in security, Id. To sit in safety, to be in calm waters. The matter is in the shallows. To sail into harbour, Cic. Ter. To sleep in port. To sleep with both eyes and in both ears. To have one's feet outside danger. Beyond the reach of missiles. It rests on no common anchor. To touch port.

units.la: Securum reddere] Securum reddere à vel ab. Securitatem alicui præstare, Cic. facere, Liv.
units.tr: Securum reddere] To make secure from or against. To provide security to someone, Cic. To make, Liv.

units.la: Securus esto] Quietus esto de hoc. Quiesce istam rem;
units.tr: Securus esto] Be at ease about this. Leave that matter alone;

units.la: Quiesce cætera : aliud cura. Animo liquido & tranquillo es : Tace, Plaut. Per hanc curam quieto tibi esse licet. Ne curassis, Id. Bono es animo, Cic. Non est quod metuas, Mart. Fac apud te sis. Nec tu aram tibi, nec tu precatorem pararis.
units.tr: Leave the rest, attend to something else. Be of a clear and tranquil mind; be silent, Plaut. By this care you may be at rest. Do not worry, Id. Be of good heart, Cic. There is no reason to fear, Mart. See that you are yourself. Do not prepare an altar for yourself, nor a suppliant.

units.la: Secus] Alioqui, Cic. Alio pacto, Plin. Diverse, Gell. vid. Aliter.
units.tr: Otherwise] Otherwise, Cic. In another way, Plin. Differently, Gell. See Aliter.

units.la: Sed] At, ast, verum, nunc, vero. Verumenimvero, Verumtamen, Atqui, Cic. Attamen, Ter. Quin tamen, Lucr. At tandem tandem, Plaut. Caeterum, Sallust. Nam, pro Sed, Plaut. Virg. Nisi, pro Sed, apud Cic. Sal. Ter. rara usurpatio.
units.tr: But] But, yet, however, now, indeed. Truly indeed, however, and yet, Cic. Nevertheless, Ter. Yet nonetheless, Lucr. But at last, at length, Plaut. Moreover, Sallust. Nam, used for Sed, Plaut. Virg. Nisi, used for Sed, in Cic. Sal. Ter. a rare usage.

units.la: Sedare. v. Compescere. Sedatè, Sedatus, v. Modestè, &c.
units.tr: To calm. See Compescere. Calmly, calmed; see Modestè, &c.

units.la: Sedatio] Mitigatio motuum animi. Obturbare alicujus solitudinem, Cic. Quies, Propert.
units.tr: Calming] Moderation of the emotions of the mind. To disturb someone's solitude, Cic. Rest, Propert.

units.la: Sedentarius] Sellariolus, Mart.
units.tr: Sedentary] Sitting much, a stay-at-home, Mart.

units.la: Sedere] Considere in sedibus, Cic. Insidere in fellâ, Plin. Superseedere ansam, Apul. Sedere post aliquem, Hor. Obsidere domi, Ter.
units.tr: To sit] To sit down in seats, Cic. To settle on a bench, Plin. To sit on the handle, Apul. To sit behind someone, Hor. To stay at home, Ter.

units.la: Sedes] Sedes inter deos, Plin. jun. Sedes deum, Lucr. Sedes honoris. Sella Praetoris : sella aurea Caesaris. Hemicyclus auguris, Cic. Solium regale, Ovid. aureum, Virg. Semirotundus suggestus, Apul. Hemicycli schematis tribunal, Vitr. Thronus, Sipont. Sedile, unum capit, Var. Consellae (duae sellae) Catul. Exedra, vel Exhedra, Cic. Cathedra, Mart.
units.tr: Seat] A seat among the gods, Plin. jun. The seat of the gods, Lucr. A seat of honour. The praetor's chair; Caesar's golden chair. The augur's half-circle, Cic. A royal throne, Ovid. A golden one, Virg. A semicircular platform, Apul. A tribunal in the shape of a half-circle, Vitr. A throne, Sipont. A seat holding one person, Var. Two seats (duae sellae), Catul. An exedra or exhedra, Cic. A chair, Mart.

units.la: Seditio] Dissensio. Seditiosorum manus. Turbarum concitatio. Tempestas seditionum, Tempestas popularis, Cic. Consternatio, Sallust. Curt. Val. Max. Factio, Sallust. Coitio, Cic. Rebellio, Caes.
units.tr: Sedition] Dissension. A band of seditious men. The stirring up of crowds. A storm of sedition, a popular storm, Cic. Consternation, Sallust. Curt. Val. Max. Faction, Sallust. A gathering together, Cic. Rebellion, Caes.

units.la: Seditionem movere] Agitate plebem seditionibus, Plin. Excitare tumultum, Cic.
units.tr: To stir up sedition] To stir the common people up with sedition, Plin. To raise a tumult, Cic.

units.la: Seditiose] Seditiosissime dicere, Cic.
units.tr: Seditiously] To speak most seditiously, Cic.

units.la: Seditiosus] Factiosus, Plaut. Turbator, Liv. Fax patriae Catilina, vid. Factiosus.
units.tr: Seditious] Factious, Plaut. A disturber, Liv. Catiline, the torch of his country; see Factiosus.

units.la: Seducere aliquem] Seducere solum, Cic. Sevocare, Plaut. vid. Secedere, Decipere.
units.tr: To lead someone aside] To lead someone aside alone, Cic. To call apart, Plaut. See Secedere, Decipere.

units.la: Sedule, Sedulus, vid. Diligens, diligenter. Seges, vid. Fruges. ges. Segmen, vid. Resegmen. Segnis, vid. Piger. Segniter, vid. Ignavè. Segregare, vid. Separare. Selectus, vid. Electus, Eximius.
units.tr: Diligent, diligently, see Diligens, diligenter. Crop, see Fruges. ges. Segment, see Resegmen. Sluggish, see Piger. Sluggishly, see Ignavè. To separate, see Separare. Chosen, see Electus, Eximius.

units.la: Semel] Semel anno, Plaut. Semel per annum, Cic.
units.tr: Once] Once a year, Plaut. Once a year, Cic.

units.la: Semen] Sementis. Col. Satus, Cic.
units.tr: Seed] Seed-corn, Col. A sowing, Cic.

units.la: Semidoctus] Non illiteratus. Attigit literas. Tinctus literis. Primoribus labris strictim libros attigit. Leviter doctus. Leviter scit aliquid, Cic. Vir parcæ sapientiæ, Sen. Moderatè eloquens, Sext. Aurel. Vict. Literator, Plin. Eruditulus, Catul.
units.tr: Half-learned] Not unlettered. Has touched letters. Dipped in letters. He has touched books with the tips of his lips. Slightly learned. He knows something slightly, Cic. A man of slender wisdom, Sen. Moderately eloquent, Sext. Aurel. Vict. A smatterer in letters, Plin. A little learned, Catul.

units.la: Seminare] Serere fruges, Ter. Sementes facere, Celsi sementim facere, Col. Sementem facere. Spargere semen, Cic. Mandare semina terræ, Col. sulcis, Virg. Committere semina sulcis, Id. Ingerere semina solo. Interserere, Col. Proserere segetem, Lucan. Differere, Var. Insere frumentum arboribus (id est, inter arbores,) Col. Serere nuces, Plin.
units.tr: To sow] To sow crops, Ter. To make sowings, Celsus; to make a sowing, Col. To scatter seed, Cic. To commit seed to the earth, Col. To commit seeds to the furrows, Virg. To entrust seeds to the furrows, Id. To pour seeds into the soil. To sow between, Col. To put forth a crop, Lucan. To scatter, Var. To plant grain among the trees (that is, between the trees), Col. To sow nuts, Plin.

units.la: Seminarium] Hortus seminarius. vid. Schola.
units.tr: Seed-bed] A seed garden. See Schola.

units.la: Seminatio] Consitio. Satio. Satus. Sementis, Cic.
units.tr: Sowing] Planting, sowing, the sowing of seed. Seed-time, Cic.

units.la: Seminator] Sator, Cic. Seminaria (à seminarius Adj. Substantivè Flor. ut: Hispania seminaria exercitûs &c.
units.tr: Sower] A sower, Cic. Seminaria (from seminarius used as a noun, Flor., as in: Spain the nursery of the army, etc.).

units.la: Semisomnis] Semisomnus, Cic. Semisopitus, Liv. Intervigilat, Sen. Dormitio nostri pectoris vigilabilis, Var. Corybantiare, Plin.
units.tr: Half-asleep] Half-asleep, Cic. Half-drowsy, Liv. Keeping watch between sleeps, Sen. A sleep of our breast that can be roused to wakefulness, Var. To dance like a Corybant, Plin.

units.la: Semita] Callis, Trames, Cic. Diverticulum, Liv. Via compendiosa, Steph. Henric. In hortis Interordinia, Col. Paginæ, Plin. Scamna, Col. Spatia cruda inter sulcos vineti. Via pedum est visa.
units.tr: Footpath] A footpath, Cic. A byway, Liv. A short cut, Steph. Henric. In gardens, interordinia, Col. Paths, Plin. Scamna, Col. Raw strips of ground between the furrows of a vineyard. A way that was seen to be a footpath.

units.la: Semovere, vid. Removere, Seponere.
units.tr: To remove, see Removere, Seponere.

units.la: Semper] Omni memoriâ, Cic. Per omnes dies, Plin. Ætatem. Præsens, Ter. vid. Assiduè. Æternum.
units.tr: Always] For all memory, Cic. Through all days, Plin. For a lifetime. Presently, Ter. See Assiduè. Eternally.

units.la: Semper ita fuit] Post hominum memoriam. Post homines natos. Post genus humanum natum. Omni (vel in omni) memoriâ fuit usurpatum. Memoriâ majorum non secus fuit. Ex omni memoria ætatum nemo aliter dicet. Nemo superiore memoria secus sensit. Ad hanc usque memoriam. Usque ad nostram memoriam, Cic.
units.tr: It has always been so] Since the memory of man. Since men were born. Since the human race was born. It has been used within all memory. Within the memory of our ancestors it was not otherwise. Within all the memory of ages no one will say otherwise. No one in earlier memory thought otherwise. Up to this memory. Up to our memory, Cic.

units.la: Senator] Vir consularis. Columen Reip. Consilii publici auctor, princeps. Consilio princeps. Patritius, Cic. Curator Reip. Salust. Præsul regendæ Reip. Spart. In consilio Imperatoris est, Lampr.
units.tr: Senator] A man of consular rank. A pillar of the Republic. An author of public counsel, a chief. Chief by counsel. A patrician, Cic. A curator of the Republic, Sallust. A head for governing the Republic, Spart. He is in the emperor's council, Lampr.

units.la: Senatus] Senatorius ordo. Ordo amplissimus, summus. Consilium summum. Amplissimus magistratus. Patres conscripti. Orbis terræ consilium (de Senatu Rom.) Senatorius conventus. Consilium, Abs. advocare, dimittere consilium dicere, Cicero. Concilium, Virgilius. Sanctius interiusque consilium, Bud. Prætorium. Seniores, Liv.
units.tr: Senate] The senatorial order. The most distinguished, highest order. The supreme council. The most distinguished magistracy. The conscript fathers. The council of the whole world (of the Roman Senate). A senatorial assembly. A council, Abs. To summon the council, to dismiss it, to say "the council is dismissed," Cicero. An assembly, Virgilius. A holier and more inner council, Bud. A praetorium. Elders, Liv.

units.la: Senatus consultum] Senatūs decretum, Fest. Decretum senatūs, Cic. Consulta patrum, Hor.
units.tr: Decree of the Senate] A decree of the Senate, Fest. A decree of the Senate, Cic. Decrees of the fathers, Hor.

units.la: Senectus] Senecta, Virg. Senium. Ætas acta, exacta, decursa, affecta, ingravescens, grandior, Cic. Progressa, Suet. Declinata, Quint. defecta, Vlp. Anilitas cana, Catul. Tempus ultimum ætatis. Præcipitata ætas. Extremi cardinis anni, Lucan. Anitas, Salust. Mala ætas, Pacuv. Pejor pars ætatis, Lucr. (Anna Perenna, Dea, annorum præses, Ovid.) Declinata ætas, Quint. Progressa, Suet. Seniles anni, Ovid. Grandævitas, Pacuv. Granditas ætatis, Sisen. Ætas decrepita, summa. Ætas senilis mala mierx. Fatale tempus vitæ exactum. Vestibulum mortis. Vespera vitæ.
units.tr: Old age] Old age, Virg. Senility. A life lived, spent, run through, worn down, advancing, growing heavier, greater, Cic. Far advanced, Suet. Declining, Quint. Spent, Ulp. Hoary decrepitude, Catul. The last time of life. A headlong age. The last hinge of the years, Lucan. Old age, Sallust. An evil age, Pacuv. The worse part of life, Lucr. (Anna Perenna, goddess, president of the years, Ovid.) Declining age, Quint. Advanced, Suet. Senile years, Ovid. Great age, Pacuv. Greatness of age, Sisen. Decrepit age, the utmost age. A senile age is an evil thing. A fated span of life now spent. The threshold of death. The evening of life.

units.la: Senectus omnia debilitat] Ingenium quoque senectus deterit, nedum corporis vigor perpetuum duret, Er.
units.tr: Old age weakens everything] Old age wears down the wit as well, let alone that bodily vigour should last for ever, Er.

units.la: Senectus cuivis obrepit] Et tibi jam cani venient formosæ capilli.
units.tr: Old age creeps up on everyone] "And soon grey hairs will come upon even you, lovely in your locks."

units.la: Senectus vegeta] Aquilæ senecta.
units.tr: Vigorous old age] The old age of an eagle.

units.la: Senectus debilis] Effœta senecta. Effœtæ vires.
units.tr: Feeble old age] Worn-out old age. Exhausted strength.

units.la: Senectus molesta] Senectus durum onus, ipsa morbus. Non sola venit senectus. Aufert viriditatem senectus. Nec revivíscere, nec repubescere potest senex.
units.tr: Burdensome old age] Old age is a hard burden, itself a sickness. Old age does not come alone. Old age takes away greenness. An old man can neither come back to life nor grow young again.

units.la: Senectas indisciplinabilis] Psittacus senex ferulam negligit.
units.tr: Old age unteachable] An old parrot disregards the rod.

units.la: Senescens] In senium vergens.
units.tr: Growing old] Tending towards old age.

units.la: Senescere] Quem veterascentem ad gloriam videas. Exoleyit tua ætas ad ea patienda. Procedere ætate. Conse senescere mœrore, Cic. Senere, Catul. Attingere senectutem, Col. Vergere in senium, Stat. Accedit ætas vino, Celf. corpus marcet annis, Lucr. Anere, Scal. vid. Veterascere.
units.tr: To grow old] One whom you see growing old towards glory. Your age has grown too weak to endure those things. To advance in years. To grow old in grief, Cic. To grow old, Catul. To reach old age, Col. To verge into old age, Stat. Age comes on with wine, Celsus. The body wastes away with the years, Lucr. To grow old, Scal. See Veterascere.

units.la: Senex] Ætate provectus. Ætate prope acta, Cic. Defectus ætate, Vlp. Exacta ætate vir, Ter. Senectute confectus. Plenus annis, Plin. Plenus ætatis, Plaut. Annis vergens, Tacit. Obsitus annis, Ter. Obsitus ævo. Maturus ævi, Virg. Maturus ævo, Ovid. Veter Priamus, Enn. Senectus homo. Senecta ætas, Plaut. Lucr. Senectum corpus, Salust. Senectute consitus. Senecta ætate vir, Plaut. Gravis, Livius. ævo, Iul. Capit. Grandævus, Virg. Vetulus homo, equus, Cicero. Veteranus bos, Var. Cascus, Enn.
units.tr: Old man] Advanced in years. Nearly spent in age, Cic. Worn out by age, Ulp. A man of spent age, Ter. Worn out with age. Full of years, Plin. Full of age, Plaut. Verging on the years, Tac. Covered with years, Ter. Covered in age. Ripe in years, Virg. Ripe in age, Ovid. Old Priam, Enn. An old man. An old-age man. An aged condition, Plaut. Lucr. An aged body, Sallust. Weighed down with age. A man of aged years, Plaut. Heavy with years, Livy. In old age, Iul. Capit. Aged, Virg. An old man, or horse, Cicero. An old ox, Var. Old, Enn.

units.la: Valde senex] Decrepitus senex. Senectute confectus, prope jam desipiens senectute. Summa senectute, Cic. Tripes homo, Hesiod. Depontanus senex. Senium. Silicernium, Ter. Persenex, Suet. Capulo proximus. Capularis, Acheronticus senex. Mors, Plaut. Confectus ætate, senio, Cic. Sesquisenex, Var. Trisesquisenex, Næv. Pergin' capulare cadaver? Lucil. Senio senior ipso. Alterum pedem in cymba Charontis habens, Er. Senes bis pueri. Cadaverosa facies, Ter. Morticinum, Plaut.
units.tr: Very old] A decrepit old man. Worn out with age, nearly now foolish from age. At great age, Cic. A three-legged man, Hesiod. An old man on his last legs. Senility. A silicernium, Ter. Extremely old, Suet. Next to the bier. Bier-bound; an Acherontic old man. Death, Plaut. Worn out by age and senility, Cic. One and a half times old, Var. Two and a half times old, Naev. "Are you still a carcass fit for the bier?" Lucil. Older than old age itself. Having one foot in Charon's boat, Er. Old men are twice children. A cadaverous face, Ter. A corpse, Plaut.

units.la: Senex languidus] Annoso leoni vel lepores insultant. Senectus aufert viriditatem.
units.tr: Feeble old man] Even hares insult an aged lion. Old age takes away greenness.

units.la: Senex cautus] Annosa vulpes haud capitur laqueo.
units.tr: Cautious old man] An aged fox is not caught in a snare.

units.la: Senex pius] Ætate major, virtutibus major.
units.tr: Pious old man] Greater in years, greater in virtues.

units.la: Senex impius] Major ætate, major iniquitate.
units.tr: Impious old man] Greater in age, greater in wickedness.

units.la: Senes artifices meliores] Vetulus cantor canit memoria dignum.
units.tr: Old craftsmen are better] An old singer sings what is worth remembering.

units.la: Senex morosus] Senex delirus, Hor. recoctus, Catul. odiosus, Ovid.
units.tr: Peevish old man] A delirious old man, Hor. Warmed over, Catul. Hateful, Ovid.

units.la: Senex garrulus] Senectus natura loquacior.
units.tr: Talkative old man] Old age is by nature more talkative.

units.la: Senex insipiens] Vetus puer. Præter ætatem stultus. Stultus es adversus ætatem, & capitis canitudinem, Plaut. Stolo, Auf. Inter pueros senex, inter senes puer, Philostr. Nullium argumentum habet, quo probet se diu vixisse, præter ætatem, Sen. Non diu vixit, sed diu fuit, Id. Puer centum annorum, Esa.
units.tr: Foolish old man] An old boy. Foolish beyond his years. You are foolish for your age and your grey head, Plaut. A simpleton, Auf. Among boys an old man, among old men a boy, Philostr. He has no proof by which to show that he has lived long, beyond his years, Sen. He has not lived long, but has been long, Id. A boy of a hundred years, Isa.

units.la: Senex avarus] Exacta via, viaticum quærit.
units.tr: Greedy old man] Having finished the road, he seeks provisions for the journey.

units.la: Senes mori non est mirum] Bos senex non lugetur.
units.tr: It is no wonder that old men die] An old ox is not mourned.

units.la: Senum actiones graviores] Bos lassus fortius figit pedem.
units.tr: The actions of old men are more serious] A weary ox plants its foot more firmly.

units.la: Sensibilis res] Sensilis, Lucr. Quæ sensu percipitur, Cadit in sensum, Cic. Sensualis, Apul.
units.tr: Perceptible thing] Perceptible, Lucr. That which is perceived by the senses, falls under the senses, Cic. Sensual, Apul.

units.la: Sensim, vid. Paulatim.
units.tr: Gradually, see Paulatim.

units.la: Sensus] Interpretes ac nuncii rerum. Viæ quasi quædam ad oculos, ad aures, à sede animi perforatæ, Cic. Tyrannos & carnifices rationis appellat, Mercur. Trismegistus.
units.tr: Sense] Interpreters and messengers of things. As it were paths bored to the eyes and ears from the seat of the mind, Cic. He calls them tyrants and executioners of reason, Mercurius Trismegistus.

units.la: Sententia] Sensus. Sensa mentis. Iudicium, Arbitratus, Arbitrium, Omen, Cic. Animus, Plaut. Placitum, Plin. In eam partem, rationem, &c. Cic. vid. Noëma.
units.tr: Opinion] Meaning. The thoughts of the mind. Judgement, opinion, decision, omen, Cic. Mind, Plaut. Opinion, Plin. In that direction, on that reasoning, etc., Cic. See Noëma.

units.la: Sententia stetit, ita decretum fuit] Ea sententia tenuit, Plin. Iun. Eo consilio discessum est, Ter. In eam sententiam itum est, Cic. Orationis exitus is fuit, Cæs.
units.tr: The opinion prevailed, it was so decided] That opinion prevailed, Plin. Iun. By that plan they departed, Ter. They went over to that opinion, Cic. That was the outcome of the speech, Caes.

units.la: Sententiam rogare] Cic. Perrogare sententiam, Liv. Plin. Iun. Suffragium ferre jubere Cic. Mittere in suffragia senatores. Inire suffragia jubere, Liv. Ire in suffragia tribus jubeo, Plin.
units.tr: To ask for an opinion] Cic. To ask each man's opinion, Liv. Plin. Iun. To order that the vote be given, Cic. To send the senators to the vote. To order them to enter the voting, Liv. I order the tribes to go to the vote, Plin.

units.la: Sententiam dicere, vid. Suffragari.
units.tr: To give an opinion, see Suffragari.

units.la: Sententia dubia] Utroque nutans sententia,
units.tr: A doubtful opinion] An opinion wavering between both sides.

units.la: Sententiose] Sententialiter, Macr. Sententias loqui, Terent.
units.tr: Pithily] Sententiously, Macr. To speak in maxims, Terent.

units.la: Sententiosus] Sententiosum genus dicendi, Cic.
units.tr: Pithy] A pithy style of speaking, Cic.

units.la: Sentire] Sentire dolorem, Cels. Persentire. Persentiscere. Usurpare aliquid sensibus, Lucr. Percipere aliquid sensibus, Cic. Intelligere, Col.
units.tr: To feel] To feel pain, Cels. To feel deeply. To feel strongly. To make something one's own by the senses, Lucr. To perceive something by the senses, Cic. To understand, Col.

units.la: Sentis, vid. Spina.
units.tr: A thorn, see Spina.

units.la: Separare] Sejungere, disjungere, sejugare, segregare, secludere, discludere aliquid à vel ab. Cic. Sequestrare, Macrob.
units.tr: To separate] To sever, disjoin, unyoke, segregate, seclude, or shut something off from something, Cic. To set apart, Macrob.

units.la: Separatim] Separatim à reliquis. Seorsum à Collega. Singulatim gratias agere. Singillatim, Cic. Extra turbam. Per se utrumque, Plaut. Secretò ab aliis, Plin. In secessu, Plin. Viritim, Particulatim, Sen. Diversi in terrogabantur, Tac. Segregatim, Diom.
units.tr: Separately] Separately from the rest. Apart from a colleague. To thank each one individually. One by one, Cic. Apart from the crowd. Each on its own, Plaut. Secretly from others, Plin. In seclusion, Plin. Man by man, Sen. They were questioned separately, Tac. Apart, Diom.

units.la: Separatio] Separatus, Apul. Disjunctio meorum. Dissolutio naturæ, verborum. Distinctio numerorum. Dissidium conjugis, Cic. Dissidium voluptatum, Plaut. Dijugatio animarum à corporib. Arnob. Secretio ac diremptus partium, Cic. Discriminatio, Diom. Dissociatio, Plin.
units.tr: Separation] A parting, Apul. The disjoining of limbs. The dissolution of nature, of words. The distinction of numbers. The estrangement of husband and wife, Cic. The conflict of desires, Plaut. The unyoking of souls from bodies, Arnob. The secession and parting of parts, Cic. Discrimination, Diom. Dissociation, Plin.

units.la: Separatus] Disjugatus, Arnob. Segrex, Sen. Secretus, Plaut. Seclusus, seductus, Plin. Segrex equus, honor. Seorsus, Virg. Exceptitius: Exceptus, Plin. Privus, Catul.
units.tr: Separated] Unyoked, Arnob. Apart, Sen. Secret, Plaut. Shut off, led aside, Plin. A horse set apart, an honour. Apart, Virg. Set aside, taken out, Plin. Single, Catul.

units.la: Sepelire] Præsepelire, Quint. Sepulturæ tradere, Apul. Sepulchro tumulare, Mart. vid. Humare.
units.tr: To bury] To bury before one's time, Quint. To deliver to the tomb, Apul. To entomb in a sepulchre, Mart. See Humare.

units.la: Sepes] Sepes viva, Col. Sepimentum naturale, virgeum, spineum, fabrile, agreste. Septum, Var. Sepes fructilis, hirta, Col. Crates texta, Hor. Lorica ex cratibus. Loricula viminea, Cæs.
units.tr: A hedge] A living hedge, Col. A natural, willow, thorn, man-made or rustic hedge. A fence, Var. A fruit-bearing, bristly hedge, Col. A woven lattice, Hor. Armour of wicker. A small wicker breastplate, Caes.

units.la: Sepire] Præsepire aditus, Cæs. Sepimento vallare, Cic. Obsepire, Liv. Circumsepire, Paul. I. C. Prætendere sepes, Virg. Conseptus, à consepire, Cic. Munire contra feras, Plin.
units.tr: To hedge in] To block the approaches, Caes. To wall round with a fence, Cic. To hedge up, Liv. To surround, Paul. I.C. To stretch out hedges, Virg. Hedged in, from consepire, Cic. To fortify against wild beasts, Plin.

units.la: Seponere] Seponere sibi tempus ad aliquid faciendum. Pecuniam in ædificationem. Omnia postposui, ut, &c. Semovere à, Cic. Removere pudorem, Ovid. metum, Liv.
units.tr: To set aside] To set aside time for oneself to do something. Money for building. I have put everything aside so that, etc. To remove from, Cic. To remove shame, Ovid. Fear, Liv.

units.la: Septemtrio] Vertex, aut polus, arcticus, aquilonaris, Sipont.
units.tr: The north] The pole: the arctic, northern pole, Sipont.

units.la: Septemtrionalis] Septemtrionarius, Gell. Aquilonaris, Cic. Aquilonius, Plin. Arctous, Mart. Arcticus, Sipont. Boreus, Ovid. Hyperboreus Fest.
units.tr: Northern] Septentrional, Gell. Northerly, Cic. Northern, Plin. Arctic, Mart. Arctic, Sipont. Boreal, Ovid. Hyperborean, Fest.

units.la: Septimana] Hebdomada, & Hebdomas, Cic.
units.tr: A week] A hebdomad, and hebdomas, Cic.

units.la: Sepulcralis] Bustuarius, Cic. Monumentarius, Apul. Capularis, Plaut.
units.tr: Sepulchral] Of a tomb, Cic. Of a monument, Apul. Coffin-like, Plaut.

units.la: Sepulchrum] Monumentum. Monumenta sepulcrorum, Cic. Locus communis. Capulum, Plaut. Conditorium, Plin. Conditivum, Sen. Tumulus, Virg. Bustum, Ovid. Sarcophagus, Inv. Portus corporis, Cic.
units.tr: A sepulchre] A monument. Monuments of graves, Cic. A commonplace. A coffin, Plaut. A burial-place, Plin. A vault, Sen. A mound, Virg. A tomb, Ovid. A sarcophagus, Inv. The harbour of the body, Cic.

units.la: Sepultura, vid. Exsequiæ.
units.tr: Burial, see Exsequiae.

units.la: Sepultus] Conditus, humatus. Quem humus injecta contegit, Cic. Situs: hic siti sunt Acarnanes, Liv. Semisepultus, Ovid.
units.tr: Buried] Laid in the ground, interred. Covered by earth heaped over it, Cic. Laid to rest: here lie the Acarnanians, Liv. Half-buried, Ovid.

units.la: Sequi] Subsequi aliquem, sectari, consectari, consequi. Pergere eadem via: itineribus alicujus, Cic. Ire secundum, Plaut. Insistere vestigiis alicujus, Quint. Vestigia, Virgil. in vestigio, Cic. Ingredi patriis vestigiis. Persequi vestigia, Idem. Vestigiis alicujus inhaerere, Col. Eadem vestigia incedere, Sen.
units.tr: To follow] To follow after someone, to pursue, chase, overtake. To keep on the same road: in someone's journeys, Cic. To go close behind, Plaut. To tread in someone's footsteps, Quint. Footsteps, Virg. In the footprint, Cic. To walk in ancestral footsteps. To trace footsteps, Id. To cling to someone's footsteps, Col. To walk the same footsteps, Sen.

units.la: Sera, vid. Claustrum.
units.tr: A bolt, see Claustrum.

units.la: Serenat] Disserenat. Conserenat, Liv. Confectum sidus (tempestas) est, Plin. Sudum est, Cic. Tempestas arridet, indulget, Lucr.
units.tr: It clears] It clears up. It clears up thoroughly, Liv. The star has set (the storm), Plin. It is calm and fair, Cic. The weather smiles and favours, Lucr.

units.la: Serenitas] Serenum, Liv. Serena tempestas, Suet. Serena coeli, Pacati status aeris. Innubilus aether, Lucr. Sudum. Tempestas bona, egregia, serena. Temperatio coeli. Tranquillitas, Cic. Temperatura coeli, Var. Tempus temperatissimum, Cato. Apricitas, clementia diei, Col. Temperies coeli, Plin. jun. Tempestas liquidissima coeli, Lucr. secunda, Tac.
units.tr: Serenity] Clear weather, Liv. A clear storm, Suet. A clear sky, a calm state of the air. A cloudless sky, Lucr. Fair weather. Good, excellent, clear weather. The temperature of the sky. Tranquillity, Cic. The temperature of the sky, Var. The most temperate season, Cato. Sunniness, the mildness of the day, Col. The temperature of the sky, Plin. jun. The clearest air of the heavens, Lucr. Favourable weather, Tac.

units.la: Sereno caelo] Sereno, Plin. Liv. Tempestate serena, Suet. Perpurum, Horat. Lævin. Tranquillitate proficisci, Cicer. Tranquillo, Plin.
units.tr: Under a clear sky] Serene, Plin. Liv. In clear weather, Suet. Perfectly pure, Hor. Lævin. To set out in tranquillity, Cic. Calmly, Plin.

units.la: Serenus] Placidus & serenus dies, Plin. jun. apricus, apricissimus, Insolatus dies, Col. Vernans collum, Plin. Apricante coelo profectus, Amm. Tempestivus, Cic. Sudum ver, Virg.
units.tr: Serene] A calm and serene day, Plin. jun. Sunny, most sunny, a day full of sun, Col. Blooming at the neck, Plin. Set out under a sunny sky, Amm. Timely, Cic. A clear spring, Virg.

units.la: Serere, vid. Seminare.
units.tr: To sow, see Seminare.

units.la: Sericum] Bombycinum. Coum, Cerd. ex Plin. Metaxa, Iun. Lacinium silvarum, Plin.
units.tr: Silk] Silk cloth. Coan silk, Cerd. ex Plin. Metaxa silk, Iun. Lacinian silk of the forests, Plin.

units.la: Sericus] Holosericus, Lamp. Bombycinus, Plin. Coa vestis, Id. Hor.
units.tr: Silken] All silk, Lamp. Of silkworms, Plin. A Coan garment, Id. Hor.

units.la: Serica vestis] Bombyx Coa, Assyria, Plin.
units.tr: Silk garment] Silkworm: Coan, Assyrian, Plin.

units.la: Series] Ordo, Plin. Versus remorum, Liv. Striga praetorianorum, Lipsi. Classes civium, Liv. Tabulatum: tabulata ollarum in dolio, uvis condiendis positarum, Col.
units.tr: A series] An order, Plin. Rows of oars, Liv. A file of praetorians, Lipsi. Classes of citizens, Liv. A shelf or layer: layers of jars in a cask, set in place for preserving grapes, Col.

units.la: Serio] Extra jocum. Remoto joco, Cic. Omissis jocis, Plin. jun. Non nugas ago, Liv.
units.tr: Seriously] Apart from jest. With jesting set aside, Cic. With jokes omitted, Plin. jun. I am not trifling, Liv.

units.la: Serio aliquid agere] Totus in hoc sum. Tota mente in curam aliquam incumbere, Cic. Hoc agere. Expandere utrumque velum, vel omnia. Machinas admovere omnes.
units.tr: To do something seriously] I am wholly intent on this. To throw one's whole mind into some concern, Cic. To make this one's business. To spread out every sail, or everything. To bring up all one's machines.

units.la: Seria serio agenda] In periculoso negotio non est dormi-tandum.
units.tr: Serious matters must be handled seriously] In a dangerous business one must not doze.

units.la: Seria res] Seriae res. Serium, Cic. Vertere seria ludo, Virg.
units.tr: A serious matter] Serious things. Serious, Cic. To turn serious things into play, Virg.

units.la: Sermo] Locutio, Cic. Loquela, Catul. Dictio. Oratio, Cic. Eloquium, Plin. Loquutus, Apul.
units.tr: Speech] Speaking, Cic. Talk, Catul. Diction. Oration, Cic. Eloquence, Plin. Utterance, Apul.

units.la: Sermo index animi] Avis e cantu dignoscitur. Oratio vitae speculum. Sermo animi character. Ut quisque est, ita loquitur.
units.tr: Speech reveals the mind] A bird is known by its song. Speech is the mirror of life. Speech is the mark of the mind. As each one is, so he speaks.

units.la: Sermo brevis, vid. Breviloquentia. Sermo prolixus, vid. Prolixus.
units.tr: Brief speech, see Breviloquentia. Long-winded speech, see Prolixus.

units.la: Sermo jactabundus] Ampullae & sesquipedalia verba, Hor. Bullatae nugae, Perf. Nugae canorae. Jactatio, granditas verborum. Verba inflata, Cic. Dicta phalerata, Ter. Tumor magna flandi, Quint. Turgens spuma. Cava verba & in modum vesicarum tumentia, Hieron. Eloquentiae tympanum, Philostr. Genus orationis pompae quam pugnae aptius, Cicero. Omnia magna loquens, Horatius.
units.tr: Bombastic speech] Bubbles and words a foot and a half long, Hor. Bubbled trifles, Pers. Sonorous trifles. Pomp and grandiosity of words. Inflated words, Cic. Ornate sayings, Ter. The swelling of a great blast, Quint. Swelling foam. Hollow words swelling like bladders, Hier. The drum of eloquence, Philostr. A kind of speech better suited to display than to battle, Cic. Speaking everything grandly, Hor.

units.la: Sermo elegans] rotundus. Oratio teres. Cygnea hominis vox & oratio, Cic. Sermo rotatus, Juv. Phalerata dicta, Ter. Compositae lexes ut tesserulae, Lucr. Verba quae bene tangere possunt aures, & lepido fucata sonore, Lucr. Museum lepor. Museum mel, Id. Atticus sal, lepor. Verborum delectus elegantiae radix.
units.tr: Elegant speech] Rounded, polished. A smooth style. A man's voice and speech like a swan's, Cic. Rounded speech, Juv. Ornate sayings, Ter. Well-composed words like little tesserae, Lucr. Words that touch the ears pleasantly and are coloured with a charming sound, Lucr. The Muses' charm. The Muses' honey, Id. Attic wit and charm. Careful choice of words is the root of elegance.

units.la: Sermo barbarus] Oratio abhorrens a linguae Romanae castimonia, Eras.
units.tr: Barbarous speech] Speech far removed from the purity of the Roman tongue, Erasmus.

units.la: Sermo magnificus] Magniloquentia. Ad dignitatem rerum exsurgit oratio, Cic. Cothurnus, Virg. Cothurnarius stylus, Amm.
units.tr: Lofty speech] Grandiloquence. Speech rises up to the dignity of the subject, Cic. The buskin, Virg. A buskin style, Amm.

units.la: Sermo obscurus] Spinosa oratio. Tecta verba. Involucra & integumenta dissimulationis. Versutiloquae malitiae. Flexiloqua & obscura oracula, Cicero. Senticosa verba, Afran. Intorta, confragosa oratio, Plautus. Confragosa argumenta. Strophae verbosae. Ceratinae & Crocodilinae (argumentationes.) Quintilianus. Contorta Sophismata. Tortuosa disputatio, Cicero. Sententia involuta, arguta, ut Pythagorae dicta, Idem.
units.tr: Obscure speech] Thorny speech. Hidden words. Veils and coverings of dissimulation. Crafty malice in words. Ambiguous and obscure oracles, Cic. Thorny words, Afran. Twisted, rugged speech, Plaut. Rugged arguments. Wordy strophes. Horned and crocodile arguments, Quint. Twisted sophisms. A tortuous debate, Cic. A sentence involved and subtle, like the sayings of Pythagoras, Id.

units.la: Ambages allegoricae, Arnob. Scotina scripta, Bud. Perplexabile verbum, Plaut.
units.tr: Allegorical riddles, Arnob. Scotist writings, Bud. A word hard to unravel, Plaut.

units.la: Sermo dubius] Ambigua verba. Ex ambiguo dicta. Genus quoddam ambigui in oratione. Ambiguitas orationis. Verborum amphibologia. Amphilogia, & Amphibolia. Anceps & multiplex verborum potestas in ambiguis, Cic. Amphibolon, Quint. Dilogia, Ausen.
units.tr: Ambiguous speech] Ambiguous words. Said in an ambiguous way. A kind of ambiguity in speech. Ambiguity of expression. Ambiguity of words: amphibology. Amphilogy and amphibolia. The double and manifold power of words in ambiguities, Cic. Amphibolon [ἀμφίβολον], Quint. Dilogy [διλογία], Ausen.

units.la: Sermo vanus] Verbosa sine profundo sensu oratio.
units.tr: Empty speech] Wordy speech without deep sense.

units.la: Sermo benevolus] Quod bonum, felix, faustumque sit, Cic. Bene me, bene te: mihi, tibi, vobis omnibus, Bene dicatis inter vos, Plaut. Te Jupiter bene amet, Id. Bene vivas. Bona verba, Ter. Bona ominatio. Faventia, Fest. Bene ominata verba, Horat. Ora faventia, Propert. Omnibus faustis augustam adhibere faventiam, Hor.
units.tr: Kindly speech] What is good, lucky and auspicious, Cic. Good to me, good to you: to me, to you, to all of you. Speak well among yourselves, Plaut. May Jupiter love you well, Id. May you live well. Good words, Ter. A good omen. Favourable words, Fest. Words of good omen, Hor. Favourable lips, Propert. To bring favourable blessing to all good things, Hor.

units.la: Sermo obscenus] Spurcidici versus, Plaut. Praetextata verba, Gell. Impudica ac praetextata verba, Macrob. Nupta verba, quae virginem loqui non licebat. Fest. Plaut. Aeschrologia, Diom. Cacemphaton, Cacophaton, Quintil. Cacephaton, Fig. Gram.
units.tr: Obscene speech] Filthy verses, Plaut. Praetextate words, Gell. Shameless and praetextate words, Macrob. Bridal words, which a virgin was not allowed to speak, Fest. Plaut. Aeschrologia, Diom. Cacemphaton, Cacophaton, Quintil. Cacephaton, Fig. Gram.

units.la: Sermones de se habere] Bene, vel, male audire, Cic. In sermonem hominum incidere, venire. In ore omnium versari. Sermonibus omnium vapulare. Subire sermones, invidiam orationis imperitae multitudinis. Incurrere in voculas malevolorum. In sermone omnium esse, Cic. In ore est omni populo, Terentius. Sermo est omnibus, Plautus. Fabula nunc ille est, Tibul. In fabulis ejus coena fuit, Suetonius. Omnibus in triviis vulgatur fabula passim, Catul.
units.tr: To have talk about oneself] To be spoken of well or ill, Cic. To fall into people's talk, to come into talk. To be in everyone's mouth. To be beaten about with everyone's gossip. To undergo talk and the envy of an ignorant crowd's speech. To run into the little words of ill-wishers. To be in everyone's talk, Cic. Everyone has it on their lips, Ter. It is talk for everyone, Plaut. He is now a tale, Tibul. His dinner was the talk of the town, Suet. The story is spread everywhere at every crossroads, Catul.

units.la: Sermonis modus, vid. Stylus.
units.tr: Manner of speech, see Stylus.

units.la: Sero] Sero post tempus, Plaut. Serum est quaerere, Mart, Sera, pro sero, Virg. Serius, seriissime, Plin. Tarde, Cic. Tardissime, Plin. Spisse, Cic.
units.tr: Late] Late, after the time, Plaut. It is too late to ask, Mart. Late, Virg. Later, latest, Plin. Slowly, Cic. Very slowly, Plin. Thickly, Cic.

units.la: Sero venire] Ad pugnam peracta re venire. Depugnato praelio venis, Plautus. Re confecta, Cic. Post festum venire, vulgo. Nundinis dissolutis, non est negotiationis commercium.
units.tr: To come late] To come to the fight after the business is over. You come to the battle when the fighting is done, Plaut. With the matter finished, Cic. To come after the festival, common usage. When the markets are closed, there is no trade in business.

units.la: Sero sapere] Post factum sapere. Sero sapiunt Phryges, Cumani. Acceptô damnô, januam claudere. Clypeum post vulnera sumere. Consilium re peractâ inutile. Post inceptam pugnam aciem instruere. Exactâ viâ viaticum quærere. Miserum est tum demum sodere puteum, cùm fauces sitis tenet, Plaut. Sera post cineres gloria, vid. Damnô acceptô prud.
units.tr: To be wise too late] Wise after the event. The Phrygians and the Cumaeans are wise too late. Having accepted the loss, to shut the door. To take up the shield after the wounds. Counsel is useless once the deed is done. After the battle has begun, to draw up the battle line. Having finished the journey, to look for provisions. It is wretched to dig the well only when thirst has the throat, Plaut. Glory comes late after the ashes; see Damnô acceptô prud.

units.la: Serò sapiens] Epimetheus non Prometheus. Post facta Prometheus. In occipitio oculos gerens. Novit tem factam denique stultus. Rebus peractis est Cleon Prometheus.
units.tr: Serò sapiens] Epimetheus, not Prometheus. Prometheus after the fact. Having eyes in the back of the head. The fool at last learns of a thing once it is done. When things are done, Cleon is Prometheus.

units.la: Serpens] Repens animans, Luer. Reptile, Hier. Proserpens bestia, duplici linguâ, Plaut.
units.tr: Serpens] A creeping animal, Lucr. A reptile, Hier. A serpent beast with a double tongue, Plaut.

units.la: Serpere] Metabat sese serpens, Virg. Sinuatur, labitur serpens. Rapit immensos orbes per humum. Sinuant angues terra volumine. Sinuosa volumina versant, Id. Sinuatur serpens in arcus. Serpens torquet squammosos orbes, Ovid. Tractu placido reptavit draco, Claud. Inspiram se colligit anguis, Virg.
units.tr: Serpere] The serpent moved itself along, Virg. It winds and glides like a snake. It sweeps its huge coils across the ground. Snakes wind their bodies over the earth in coils. They turn their sinuous coils, Id. The serpent curls into arches. The serpent turns its scaly coils, Ovid. The dragon crept along with a gentle trail, Claud. The snake gathers itself into a coil, Virg.

units.la: Serra] Runcina, Plin. Serra major, Cæl. Rhod. Lupus, Pallad.
units.tr: Serra] A plane-saw, Plin. A larger saw, Cæl. Rhod. A saw with teeth like a wolf's, Pallad.

units.la: Serrago, vid. Scobs.
units.tr: Sawdust; see Scobs.

units.la: Serrare, i. serrâ scindere] Serrâ præcidere, Col. Desecare serra arborem, Id. Reciprocare serram per lignum, Tertul.
units.tr: Serrare, i. serrâ scindere] To cut off with a saw, Col. To cut down a tree with a saw, Id. To saw back and forth through wood, Tertul.

units.la: Serrarius] Tritor lignorum, Plin.
units.tr: Serrarius] A sawyer of timber, Plin.

units.la: Sertum, vid. Corona. Servare, vid. Conservare. Recondere.
units.tr: Sertum, see Corona. Servare, see Conservare. Recondere.

units.la: Servilis] Servituti natus, Cic. Vernilis, Tac. Servitricius, Plaut.
units.tr: Servilis] Born for servitude, Cic. Of slaves, Tac. Of a female slave, Plaut.

units.la: Serviliter] Servorum more, Liv.
units.tr: Serviliter] In the manner of slaves, Liv.

units.la: Servire] Esse à servitio alicujus, Tac. Tribuere operas alicui, Reip. Operas alicui dare in re aliqua, Cic. Servitutem colere apud aliquem, Plaut. vid. Famulari.
units.tr: Servire] To be at someone's service, Tac. To render service to someone, Reip. To give one's services to someone in some matter, Cic. To live in servitude to someone, Plaut. See Famulari.

units.la: Servitus] Triste ministerium, Virg. Famulatus miser, Cic. Gravis, Sen. Servitium, Plin. Servitudo, Liv. Servitudo, Fest. Servientia, Plaut.
units.tr: Servitus] A sad service, Virg. Wretched servitude, Cic. Heavy, Sen. Servitude, Plin. Servitude, Liv. Servitude, Fest. Servile duties, Plaut.

units.la: Servitus invita] In cavea minùs benè canit luscinia.
units.tr: Servitus invita] A nightingale does not sing so well in a cage.

units.la: In servitutem redigere ] Addicere, asserere aliquem in serviservitutem, Liv. Injungere alicui æternam servitutem, Cæs. Servitiô premere, Virg.
units.tr: In servitutem redigere] To hand over, to claim someone as a slave, Liv. To impose eternal servitude on someone, Cæs. To press with slavery, Virg.

units.la: Serus] Serior, Ovid. Serissimus. Serotinus, Plin. Tardus, Ovid. Intempestivus, Cic.
units.tr: Serus] Later, Ovid. Very late. Late-coming, Plin. Slow, Ovid. Untimely, Cic.

units.la: Serum auxilium] Bellô peracto machinas adferre. Mortuo mederi. Mortuo verba facere. Senem admonere. Deploratis vulnerib. manûs admovere. Post causam vulneratam remedium quærere.
units.tr: Serum auxilium] To bring up siege engines after the war is over. To treat the dead. To make a speech over the dead. To admonish an old man. To lay hands on wounds already given up for lost. After the wound has been inflicted, to look for a remedy.

units.la: Servus] De lapide emptus servus, Cic. De lapide noxius, Col. Qui sempiternam servit servitutem. Ætatem serviens. Servitutem colit apud aliquem. Solida servitus, pro servo. Mancipium, vel mancupium, Plaut. Ergastulus, Lucil. Ergastulum, Juv. Servus est, qui cupit aut metuit.
units.tr: Servus] A slave bought from the stone, Cic. A slave guilty by the stone, Col. One who serves an everlasting servitude. One who serves for his whole life. One who serves as a slave with someone. Solid servitude, for a slave. A slave-boy or purchased slave, Plaut. A workhouse, Lucil. A slave-prison, Juv. He is a slave who desires or fears.

units.la: Servus Domino placeat] Cujus pane vescor, ejus verba molior. Coquus Domini debet habere gulam.
units.tr: Servus Domino placeat] He whose bread I eat, his words I shape. A master's cook ought to have a gullet.

units.la: Servus ne superbiat] Servus cum sis, comam geris?
units.tr: Servus ne superbiat] Since you are a servant, do you wear your hair long?

units.la: Sessio, locus sedendi] Sellaria, Plin. Exedrion. Exedra, Cicero. Sessibulum, Plautus. Lamb. Sessimonium, Vitr.
units.tr: Sessio, locus sedendi] Seats, Plin. A sitting-room. An exedra, Cicero. A little seat, Plautus. Lamb. A seat-place, Vitr.

units.la: Severè] Virgulâ censoriâ, vid. Rigidè.
units.tr: Severè] With a censor's rod; see Rigidè.

units.la: Severitas] Austeritas frontis. Torvitas naturæ, Plin. Duritas morum, Suet. Immanitas verborum. Duritas, Durities, Cic. Immodestia heri, Plaut. Duritia imperii, Tac. Aspera censura, Patere. Obducta frons.
units.tr: Severitas] Austerity of countenance. Grimness of nature, Plin. Hardness of manners, Suet. Harshness of words. Hardness, sternness, Cic. Intemperance of a master, Plaut. Harshness of rule, Tac. Harsh censure, Patere. A frowning brow.

units.la: Severus] Severum supercilium, Ovid. Saturninus aspectus, Cressol. Subductis superciliis, Sen. Crudus, Mart. Perseverus, Tac. Acerbus homo, Cic. vid. Rigidus.
units.tr: Severus] A stern brow, Ovid. A saturnine look, Cressol. With lowered eyebrows, Sen. Raw, Mart. Persistent, Tac. A harsh man, Cic. See Rigidus.

units.la: Sevum] Sebum aliqui scribunt. Arbilla, Fest.Scal. (Arbina etiam scribitur.)
units.tr: Sevum] Some write sebum (tallow). Arbilla, Fest. Scal. (Also written arbina.)

units.la: Si] Si est, ut velis, id est si vis. Si est ut admiserit: si admisit, Ter. An, Cic. An si, Ovid. Utrum, Plaut. (Sicubi. Nuncubi, Ter. sunt Loci.)
units.tr: Si] If it is your wish, that is, if you will. If it is that he admitted: if he admitted, Ter. Or, Cic. Or if, Ovid. Whether, Plaut. (Sicubi and Nuncubi, Ter., are place-words.)

units.la: Si aliquando] Si quando: si unquam, Virg. Ut cum maximè, Cic.
units.tr: Si aliquando] If ever: if at any time, Virg. Just as at the greatest, Cic.

units.la: Sinon] Sin minùs, & Sin, absol. post, si. Sin mihi veniam dederit, &c. sin minus. Sin autem. Ni ita res haberet, Nisi, Cic.
units.tr: Sinon] But if not; and sin, used absolutely after si. If he grants me pardon, etc.; but if not. But if. If the matter were otherwise, Nisi, Cic.

units.la: Si Deus volet] Si Deus annuerit, Plin. Iun. Sperat quidem animus quò eveniat, Diis in manu est. Si Diis placet, Plaut. Modò Jupiter adsit. Si quæ viam dederit fortuna. Si quæ fata sinant, Virg. Ut pia fata volunt. Fata obstant. Si fortuna volet, fies de Rhetore Consul: Si volet hæc eadem, fies de Consule Rhetor, Iuv.
units.tr: Si Deus volet] If God consents, Plin. Iun. The mind hopes how the thing will turn out, but it is in the gods' hand. If it pleases the gods, Plaut. Only let Jupiter be present. If fortune gives a way. If the fates allow, Virg. As the kindly fates will. The fates stand in the way. If fortune wills, you will go from rhetorician to consul; if she wills the same, you will go from consul to rhetorician, Juv.

units.la: Si tu non esses] Absque te si fuisset. Absque te foret, sat scio in alto distraxissent me, Plaut. Per te stetit quò minus, Ter. Præsentia tua obstitit. Extra conspectum tuum esset, luderent.
units.tr: Si tu non esses] If it had been without you. Without you, I would surely have been torn apart at sea, Plaut. It was through you that it did not happen, Ter. Your presence stood in the way. If it were out of your sight, they would play.

units.la: Sibi vivere] Suis commodis ; sibi natus. Ad utilitatem (propriam) omnia referre, Cic. Animi causâ aliquid facere, Id. Suo stomacho vivere, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Sibi vivere] To live for one's own convenience; born for oneself. To refer everything to one's own (private) advantage, Cic. To do something for the sake of one's own mind, Id. To live by one's own temper, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Sic, vid. Ita.
units.tr: Sic, see Ita.

units.la: Siccare] Arefacere aliquid, Cat. Arfacere, Col. Assiccare in sole ficus, Vl. Torrere frigore aliquid, Var. Torrefacere. Pati in sole arescere, Col. Urere, Ovid.
units.tr: Siccare] To dry something up, Cat. To make dry, Col. To dry figs in the sun, Vl. To parch something with cold, Var. To make thoroughly dry by heat. To let something wither in the sun, Col. To scorch, Ovid.

units.la: Siccè] Aridè. Aridulè, Sipont. Retorridè natæ herbæ, Plin. Infecundè & jejunè, Gell.
units.tr: Siccè] Dryly. Somewhat dry, Sipont. Plants dried up, Plin. Barren and fasting, Gell.

units.la: Siccitas] Ariditas, Plin. Aritudo scirpi, Plaut. Macritas soli. Jejunitas humoris, Vitr.
units.tr: Siccitas] Dryness, Plin. Dryness of the rush, Plaut. Leanness of soil. Lack of moisture, Vitr.

units.la: Siccus] Siccum tempus : poculum, Tibul. Aridus cinis, Siticulosus, Hor. Sitiens annus. Siccanus, Plin. Siccaneum pratum. Retorridus. Macerrima humus, Col. Permacer, Plin. Macer agellus, Hor. Jejuna terra. Jejunio laborat terra macra, Col. Assus sol, i. siccus, Cic. Aridum sermonis genus, Id. Semisiccus, Pallad.
units.tr: Siccus] A dry season. A dry cup, Tibul. Dry ash. Thirsty, Hor. A thirsty year. Dry, Plin. A dry meadow. Parched. Very lean ground, Col. Very lean, Plin. A thin little field, Hor. Barren land. Lean ground suffers from hunger, Col. Sun-dried, that is, dry, Cic. A dry style of speech, Id. Half-dry, Pallad.

units.la: Sicut] Sicuti, Lucr. Quemadmodum. Velut. Ut temporibus illis ; ut in tantis malis. Ut par est : ut potest. Prout res postulat. Similis ut si, atque. Talis ac, Cic. Talis atque. Quam, Ter. Atque, Cic. Quasi, Lucr. Pariter atque. Juxta atque, Liv.
units.tr: Sicut] As, Lucr. Just as. Like. As in those times; as in such great evils. As is fitting; as is possible. According to what the matter requires. Similar as if, and. Such as, Cic. Such as. As, Ter. And, Cic. As if, Lucr. Equally as. Just as, Liv.

units.la: Sidera] Gemmantia sidera. Picturæ firmamenti. Astrorum chorus. Flammæ inextinguibiles. Lampadæ mundi. Circulatores rerum. Horologii mundani motores primi. Luminis nostri diribitores.
units.tr: Sidera] Sparkling stars. The pictures of the firmament. The chorus of the stars. Unquenchable flames. The lamps of the world. The circlers of things. The first movers of the world's clockwork. The dividers of our light.

units.la: Sidere] Considere, Plin. Residere, Cic. Subsidere in fundo, Col, Limus in imum confluxit, & subsidit funditus ut fæx, Lucr. vid. Desidere.
units.tr: Sidere] To settle, Plin. To sit down, Cic. To sink to the bottom, Col. Mud has flowed together and settled to the bottom like dregs, Lucr. See Desidere.

units.la: Sigillare] Obsigillare, Sen. Obsignare, Consignare epistolam, Cic.
units.tr: Sigillare] To seal up, Sen. To seal, to close a letter, Cic.

units.la: Sigillum] Signaculum, Vlp. Signatura, Suet. Cerae signaturis vacuae.
units.tr: Sigillum] A seal, Vlp. An impression, Suet. Wax tablets empty of impressions.

units.la: Signare] Consignare aliqua re. Notam apponere, Cic. Persignare. Disignare nota ignominiae, Liv. Adnotare, Quint. Denotare, Plin. Signum imprimere. Notare locum, Virg. Insignire, Tac.
units.tr: Signare] To seal something. To put a mark on, Cic. To mark thoroughly. To brand with a mark of disgrace, Liv. To annotate, Quint. To denote, Plin. To impress a sign. To mark a place, Virg. To distinguish, Tac.

units.la: Signate, vid. Expresse.
units.tr: Signate, see Expresse.

units.la: Signatio] Signatus, Apul. vid. Significatio.
units.tr: Signatio] Marking, Apul. See Significatio.

units.la: Signatus, adn.] Signata cicatrix in stirpe. Notatus, Cic. Effigiatus in aliquid, Amm. Literata urna, Plaut. i. literis inscripta.
units.tr: Signatus, adn.] A marked scar on the trunk. Noted, Cic. Stamped with something, Amm. A lettered urn, Plaut. That is, inscribed with letters.

units.la: Significare, vid. Certum reddere.
units.tr: Significare, see Certum reddere.

units.la: Significat aliquid vox, aut res] Quid haec celeritas significat? Verbum quid valet. Haec vis subiecta huic voci. Quid sibi vult istud? Cic. Haec notant & designant turpitudinem aliquam, Cic.
units.tr: Significat aliquid vox, aut res] What does this haste mean? What does the word signify? This force lies under this word. What does that mean? Cic. These words mark and designate some shameful thing, Cic.

units.la: Significatio] Significatio nominum, somniorum, scripti. Vis verbi. Notio alicui verbo subiecta, Cic. Significantia nominis, Fab. Vet. Significatus, Plin. Signatio, Tac.
units.tr: Significatio] The meaning of names, dreams, and writing. The force of a word. A notion attached to a word, Cic. The signification of a name, Fab. Vet. Meaning, Plin. Signification, Tac.

units.la: Signum] Vestigium amoris. Index, Indicium, Argumentum, Significatio pudoris, valetudinis. Insigne (Insignia) maeroris. Simulacrum, Specimen. Nota, Cic. Notula, Sipont.
units.tr: Signum] A trace of love. An indication, token, proof, or sign of shame or health. A badge of grief. An image, a specimen. A mark, Cic. A little note, Sipont.

units.la: Signa praecedunt rem] Aedificia prius crepant & nutant, quam corruunt, Sen. Aestatem loquitur hirundo. Arbor crepitu pronunciat se frangi. Aures tinniunt. Pluvia tonitrua sequitur. Post folia cadunt & arbores. Post verba verbera. Imbrem praecedit nubes. Praecedit protervia ignaviam, vid. Omen.
units.tr: Signa praecedunt rem] Buildings creak and sway before they fall, Sen. The swallow announces summer. A tree announces by a crack that it is breaking. The ears ring. Rain follows thunder. Leaves and trees fall afterwards. Blows follow words. A cloud goes before rain. Insolence goes before idleness; see Omen.

units.la: Signum unum fallit] Fuscina non facit una cocum. Non omnis cocus, cui longus culter adhaeret. Una hirundo non facit ver. Una linea non facit Geometram. Una navicula-tio non facit nautam. Una tussis non facit phtisin. Adag.
units.tr: Signum unum fallit] One prong does not make a cook. Not every man to whom a long knife clings is a cook. One swallow does not make spring. One line does not make a geometer. One short voyage does not make a sailor. One cough does not make consumption. Adag.

units.la: Silentium] Taciturnitas imitatur confessionem, Cic.
units.tr: Silentium] Silence imitates confession, Cic.

units.la: Silentium indicare] Facere per praeconem silentium, Liv. Majestate manûs facere silentium, Perf. Jubere silentium, Lucan. Favere linguis jubeo, Plin.
units.tr: Silentium indicare] To call for silence through a herald, Liv. To impose silence with a lordly wave of the hand, Perf. To order silence, Lucan. I command the tongues to be favourable, Plin.

units.la: Silentium sibi imperare] Manum ad os apprimere. Premere vocem, Virg.
units.tr: Silentium sibi imperare] To press the hand to the mouth. To press down the voice, Virg.

units.la: Silentium intempestivum noxium] Amyclas perdidit silentium.
units.tr: Silentium intempestivum noxium] Silence ruined Amyclae.

units.la: Silentium pestis amicitiæ] Multas amicitias silentium diremit.
units.tr: Silence, the bane of friendship] Silence has broken up many friendships.

units.la: Silentio interdum optimè respondetur] Silentium prudens pro responso est. Tacens stulto satis respondet.
units.tr: Sometimes the best answer is silence] Prudent silence serves as an answer. A silent man answers a fool well enough.

units.la: Silentium remunerabitur] Silentii multa bona. Silentii præmium periculo vacat. Est & fideli tuta silentio merces, Hor. Silentii tutum præmium.
units.tr: Silence will be rewarded] Silence brings many goods. The reward of silence is free from danger. There is also a safe reward for the faithful man who keeps silent, Hor. A safe reward of silence.

units.la: Silentio præterire, vid. Reticere. Omittere.
units.tr: To pass over in silence, see To keep back. To leave out.

units.la: Silere] Silescere. Obticere, Ter. Tenere silentium, Liv. Tenere se in silentio : intra silentium, Plin. Iun. Agere silentium, Ovid. Præstare, Liv. Dare, Ter. Moderari linguæ, Plaut. Premere vocem, Virg. Favere linguis, Cic.
units.tr: To be silent] To grow quiet. To hold one's tongue, Ter. To keep silence, Liv. To keep oneself in silence; to remain within silence, Plin. Iun. To keep silence, Ovid. To impose silence, Liv. To give silence, Ter. To restrain the tongue, Plaut. To press down the voice, Virg. To hold one's tongue in reverent silence, Cic.

units.la: Qui silet, consentire videtur] Silentium fatentis est.
units.tr: He who is silent seems to consent] Silence is the mark of one who confesses.

units.la: Sileantur hæc] Id venti abripiant.
units.tr: Let these things be passed over] Let the winds carry them away.

units.la: Silex] Lapis pyrites. Æternus ignis thesaurus. Lapis igne fertilis, Scal. ex Ætna, Virg.
units.tr: Flint] A pyrites stone. The treasure of eternal fire. A stone fertile in fire, Scal. from Etna, Virg.

units.la: Siligineus] Farreus, Col. Secalitius, Iun. Cerealis, Ovid.
units.tr: Made of fine wheat] Of spelt, Col. Of rye, Iun. Of grain, Ovid.

units.la: Siligo] Secale. Olyra. Arinca, Plin. Adoreum, Sen. Semen vel far adoreum, Col.
units.tr: Fine wheat] Rye. Spelt-like grain. Arinca, Plin. Emmer, Sen. Seed or spelt of emmer, Col.

units.la: Siliqua, in leguminibus] Tunica lupini. Utriculus granorum frumenti, Plin. Valvulæ fabarum, &c. Col. Folliculus adorei, Id. Lobus, Cæl. Rhod. Concha fabæ, Scribon. Putamen, Non.
units.tr: Pod, of pulses] The husk of the lupin. A little bag of grains of wheat, Plin. Pods of beans, etc., Col. The little husk of emmer, Id. Pod, Cael. Rhod. Shell of a bean, Scribon. Hull, Non.

units.la: Silua] Arboretum, Gell. Arbustum, Plin. Arbustivus locus, Col.
units.tr: Wood] A grove, Gell. A plantation of trees, Plin. A wooded place, Col.

units.la: Silvescere] Stirpescere, Plin. Degener inferitatem vitis, Id. Dumescere, Diom.
units.tr: To run wild] To put forth shoots, Plin. To degenerate into the wildness of the vine, Id. To grow thick with brambles, Diom.

units.la: Silvestris] Silvester, Cic. Sylvosus, Liv. Sylvaticus, Cat. Silviger mons, Plin. Sylvicola, Ovid. Arbores ferae, Col. Nemor vagus. Sylvicultrix cerva, Catul. Poët.
units.tr: Wild, of woods] Wild, Cic. Wooded, Liv. Of the woods, Cat. A wood-bearing mountain, Plin. Dwelling in the woods, Ovid. Wild trees, Col. A wandering grove. A wood-dwelling hind, Catul. Poët.

units.la: Simia] Simius, Mart. Cluvinum pecus, Arnob. Pitheucium, cium, Plaut. Pithecus, Gr. Humanorum operum imita- trix.
units.tr: Ape] An ape, Mart. Cluvian cattle, Arnob. Pitheucium, Plaut. Pithecus, Gr. An imitator of human works.

units.la: Similis] Simillimus Deo. Est illi similitudo cum. Accedit ad similitudinem alicujus. Habet similitudinem ad. Similitudo naturæ illius ad te pervenit. Similes inter se. Similis alicujus, alicui, ac, vel atque aliquis. Persimilis alicui. Similitudinem speciemque gerit. Accedit alicui. Respondet illi. Refert sonum. Gemina aliquorum audacia. Tergeminum Par. Geminus in furtis alicui. Germanus Thucydidis. Germanissimus Stoicis. Assimilis & consimilis alicui, Cic. Habet alicujus similitudinem, refert. Speciem ejus præbet, repræsentat. Est illi species aquæ. Aliquem mentitur. Descendit ad hyacinthum. Reddit colorem vini. Proximus vino, Plinius. Faciem obtinet alicujus, Col. Non multum abludit ab, Horat. Subsimilis, Cels. Non dissimilis atque, Cicero. Non dissimili formâ in Dominum, Tacit. Idem aliis, Lucr. Hujus notæ alia, Sen. Ad ipsam faciem; ad hoc exemplum est, Plautus. Refert ore aliquem, Virgilius. Compar alicui, Livius. Fratres vocantur res similes, Fest. Fratres montes, Solin. Sorores lodices, Martialis. Sorores sapore, Plinius. Omnia dicta factaque inter se congruunt, respondent sibi, ac unâ formâ percussa sunt, Senec. Indissimilis, Patercul. Ejusdem notæ, farinæ, furfuris. Ovo prognatus eodem, &c.
units.tr: Like] Most like God. He has a likeness to him. He comes near the likeness of someone. He has a resemblance to. The likeness of that man's nature reaches you. Like one another. Like someone, to someone, as or as if someone. Very like someone. He bears the likeness and appearance. He resembles someone. He answers to him. He echoes the sound. The twofold boldness of certain people. A threefold pair. A twin in thefts with someone. A brother of Thucydides. Most akin to the Stoics. Similar and very similar to someone, Cic. He has the likeness of someone, he reproduces it. He presents his appearance, represents him. He has the appearance of water. He counterfeits someone. He comes close to hyacinth. He gives the colour of wine. Nearest to wine, Plin. He takes on the face of someone, Col. Does not differ much from, Hor. Somewhat similar, Cels. Not unlike, Cic. Not in a dissimilar form to the Lord, Tac. The same as others, Lucr. Another of this kind, Sen. To the very face; this is the pattern, Plaut. He resembles someone in face, Virg. Equal to someone, Liv. Things alike are called brothers, Fest. Mountains are brothers, Solin. Coverlets are sisters, Mart. Sisters in taste, Plin. All sayings and deeds agree with each other, answer each other, and are struck from one mould, Sen. Not unlike, Paterc. Of the same mark, meal, bran. Born from the same egg, etc.

units.la: Simillimus] Non ovum ovo tam simile: non lac lacti. Non aqua aquæ. Ne mater quidem sua, quæ illos peperherat, internosse potuit, Plaut. Proles indiscreta suis, gratusque parentibus error, Virg. Omnia dicta factaque inter se congruunt.
units.tr: Most like] Egg is not so like egg, nor milk like milk, nor water like water. Not even his own mother, who bore them, could tell them apart, Plaut. An offspring indistinguishable from its own kind, and a pleasing error to parents, Virg. All sayings and deeds agree with each other.

units.la: Similem esse] Similare aliquid, Sipont. Simulare, Mart. Æmulari, Plin. Plurapete in Similis, & Repræsentare.
units.tr: To be similar] To make something similar, Sipont. To simulate, Mart. To emulate, Plin. See also under Similis, and to represent.

units.la: Simile est hoc huic] Harum rerum est quædam inter se similitudo, affinitas, cognatio, vicinia. His confinia sunt illa. Puro fonti quàm flumini proprior. Ejus est classis, Eraf.
units.tr: This is like that] Among these things there is a certain likeness, affinity, kinship and nearness. Those things border on these. Nearer to a pure spring than to a river. Of that class, Erasm.

units.la: Simile similibus] Pharmacis amaris amara bilis.
units.tr: Like to like] Bitter bile to bitter drugs.

units.la: Simile facit simile] Barbarus inter barbaros evasit. fit. Ignavia generat ignaviam. Studium generat studium.
units.tr: Like makes like] A barbarian became one among barbarians. Idleness begets idleness. Zeal begets zeal.

units.la: Simile gaudet simili] Mater benevolentiae similitudo. Morum similitudo amicitiae gluten. Asinus asino pulcher: Bos bovi : Cicada Cicadae : Formica formicae. Mores æstimantur ex sodalitiis, Eras. Perca sequitur. Melaxurum Fur displicet Verri. Homicida Miloni, (scil. ironicè) Graculus quaerit graculum. Jecur vescentium jecinora exhilarat.
units.tr: Like delights in like] Likeness is the mother of goodwill; likeness of manners is the glue of friendship. An ass is fair to an ass, an ox to an ox, a cicada to a cicada, an ant to an ant. Manners are judged from companionships, Erasm. Perch follows perch. A thief dislikes Verres; a murderer dislikes Milo (said ironically). A jackdaw seeks a jackdaw. The liver of those who eat livers cheers them.

units.la: Similis simVilem novit] Bestia bestiam, Fure furem, Lupus lupum Cognoscit. Furati apud furem difficile. Sophisticari apud sophistam.
units.tr: Like knows like] A beast knows a beast, a thief a thief, a wolf a wolf. It is hard to cheat a thief before a thief. To practise sophistry before a sophist.

units.la: Similem simili adducit Deus] Semper similem ducit Deus ad similem.
units.tr: God leads like to like] God always leads like to like.

units.la: Simile conducit simili] Ubi tu Cajus, ego Caja. Cascus eascam ducit. Pariter remum ducere. Pupus pupam deamat.
units.tr: Like joins with like] Where you are Gaius, I am Gaia. Cascus leads Eascam. To row together. A pup loves a pup.

units.la: Simile non tollitur simili, non nocet] Ignis igni non exstinguitur. Canis caninam non est.
units.tr: Like is not removed by like; it does no harm] Fire is not put out by fire. A dog does not bite a dog.

units.la: Similiter] Simillimè, similè. Simili modo, ratione, Cic. Similiter alicui, Plin. Assimiliter mihi obtigit, Plaut. Consimiliter, Arnob. (Simultè, Plaut. Simulter, Lambin) Pari nube. Pari voce & uno spiritu. Pari filo, jugo, momento, lance, libra.
units.tr: Similarly] Most similarly, similarly. In a similar way or manner, Cic. Similarly to someone, Plin. It has befallen me similarly, Plaut. Similarly, Arnob. (Simultè, Plaut. Simulter, Lambin) With a like cloud. With a like voice and one breath. With a like thread, yoke, moment, scale, balance.

units.la: Similitudo] Similitas, Varr. Analogia. Proportio vocabulorum, Var. Geminitudo, Pacuv. Unitas foliorum, Plin. Apes apum similes. Parabola. in SS.
units.tr: Likeness] Similarity, Varr. Analogy. Proportion of words, Varr. Likeness, Pacuv. Unity of leaves, Plin. Bees like bees. Parable. in SS.

units.la: Simplex] Simplex cibus, Mart. Inartificialis, Quint. Incompta oratio, Cic. Incoptum decus, Sen. Inconditus orator, incondita verba, Cic.
units.tr: Simple] Plain food, Mart. Unartificial, Quint. Unadorned speech, Cic. Unadorned ornament, Sen. A rough orator, rough words, Cic.

units.la: Simplex homo] Homo unius cujusdam operis. Rudis omnium rerum, Cic. Prope ad stultitiam simplicissimus, Aur. Text. Vitt. Quadratus homo.
units.tr: A simple man] A man of one particular work. Raw in all things, Cic. Very simple, nearly to foolishness, Aur. Text. Vitt. A square man.

units.la: Simplex sincerus] Vir bonus, & simplicis veritatis amicus. Antiquus homo. Antiquorum hominum homo. Apparent in eo vestigia antiqui officii. Incallidus. Simplex animus erga me, Cicero. Simplex domus, & inscia fraudum, Stat. Antiquis moribus adolescens, Plautus. Homo antiquâ virtute & fide, Terentius.
units.tr: Simple, sincere] A good man and a friend of simple truth. An old-fashioned man. A man of the old sort. Traces of an old duty appear in him. Not crafty. A simple spirit towards me, Cic. A simple house, knowing nothing of fraud, Stat. A youth of old morals, Plaut. A man of old virtue and faith, Ter.

units.la: Piso vultu habituque moris antiqui, & æstimatione rectâ severus, Tac. Inexpertus malorum, malis, ad mala, Liv. Bonus vir semper tiro. Boni facilè sunt deceptui. Inter bonos benè agitur.
units.tr: Piso, severe in face and bearing of the old custom, and in sound judgement, Tac. Inexperienced in evils, to evils, towards evils, Liv. A good man is always a novice. Good men are easily deceived. Among good men things go well.

units.la: Simplicitas] Simplicitas hominis, Mart. fabularum convivalium, Tac. vid. Sinceritas.
units.tr: Simplicity] The simplicity of a man, Mart. Of after-dinner tales, Tac. See Sincerity.

units.la: Simpliciter, vid. Vulgariter.
units.tr: Simply, see Vulgarly.

units.la: Simul] Simul duas res agere, Plaut. Uno tempore epistolas datas duas, Cic. Eâdem operâ. Unâ opera, Plaut. Quasi signô dato conveniunt, Cic.
units.tr: At once] To do two things at once, Plaut. Two letters given at one time, Cic. With the same effort. With one effort, Plaut. They meet as if at a given signal, Cic.

units.la: Simul cum aliquo] Simul esse, cubare simul tecum. Pariter cum aliquo. Pariter lætamur & dolemus. Unà : unà cum aliquo, Cic. Unà inter se, Plautus. In-simul, Stat. Junctim, Suet. Conjunctim, Cæs. Conjunctè. Communiter cum aliquo. Promiscuè uti, Cic. Uno fasce complecti, Plin. Unitè, Non.
units.tr: At the same time as someone] To be together; to lie together with you. Equally with someone. We rejoice and grieve equally. Together with someone, Cic. Together among themselves, Plaut. Together, Stat. Jointly, Suet. Conjointly, Caes. Conjointly. In common with someone. To use indiscriminately, Cic. To embrace in one bundle, Plin. As one, Non.

units.la: Simulare] Simulo me litigare. Assimulare, Cic. Induere simulationem. Alienam personam ferre. Speciem præbere euntis, Liv. Uti simulatione itineris, Cæs. Induere falsos pavores, Tac. Mentiri amorem, dolorem, Ovid. Facere se alias res agere, Cic. Ostentare verbis, Id. Componere blanditias, Tibul. Componere se ad veritatis imitationem, Quint. Facere se magnum, ferocem, plenum studii, Plaut. Habitum ac voces dolentûm simulatione induebat, Tac. Habitu præferre studium sapientiæ, Plin. Iun. Præ se ferre, gerere aliquid, Cic. Prætendere amicitiam alicujus, Tac. Specimen abeuntis exercitûs hosti dedit, Quint. v. Vultu significare.
units.tr: To pretend] I pretend to quarrel. To feign, Cic. To put on a pretence. To wear another's character. To show the appearance of one going away, Liv. To use the pretext of a journey, Caes. To put on false fears, Tac. To feign love or grief, Ovid. To make oneself appear to be doing other things, Cic. To show by words, Id. To compose flatteries, Tibul. To shape oneself to the imitation of truth, Quint. To make oneself out great, fierce, full of zeal, Plaut. He put on the bearing and voice of one grieving, by pretence, Tac. To display by one's bearing a zeal for wisdom, Plin. Iun. To show openly, to bear something, Cic. To pretend the friendship of someone, Tac. He gave the enemy a sample of the departing army, Quint. See To signify by the face.

units.la: Simulare se aliquem esse] Mentiri sexum, Col. Genus, Cic. Ducere se pro adolescentulo, Plaut. Hic se facit venustum, Catul. Consulem se ferens, Tac. vid. Venditare se aliquo nomine.
units.tr: To pretend to be someone] To feign a sex, Col. A kind, Cic. To pass oneself off as a youth, Plaut. Here he makes himself charming, Catul. Bearing himself as a consul, Tac. See To advertise oneself under some name.

units.la: Simulare tristitiam] Ad novercæ tumulum flere.
units.tr: To feign sadness] To weep at the tomb of a stepmother.

units.la: Simulatè] Per simulationem. Dissimulanter, Cic. Dissimulatim, Quint. Fícto officio, & simulata sedulitate specie fictæ simulationis. Fronte an mente, dubitatur. Dicis causa, Cic. Voce negare, mente dare vel contra, Virg. A summis labris hæc veniunt, Sen. In speciem, Liv. Simulanlanter, Apul. Dissimulandi causâ, Id. Fictè & simulatè. Ficto sermone, vultu. Simulatione & inani ostentatione, Cic. Per dissimulationem, Suet. Fronte promittere, Quint. Non ex fide, Liv. Temporis causa aliquid dicere, fingere, colere aliquem, Cic. vid. dicis causâ.
units.tr: Pretendedly] By pretence. Dissemblingly, Cic. Dissemblingly, Quint. With feigned service and simulated zeal, in the appearance of a pretended pretence.
