Whether it is in the face or the mind is doubted. For the sake of appearance, Cic. To deny with the voice and give with the mind, or the reverse, Virg. These come from the tip of the lips, Sen. For show, Liv. Pretendingly, Apul. For the sake of dissembling, Id. Feignedly and pretendedly. With feigned speech and face. By pretence and empty show, Cic. By dissimulation, Suet. To promise with the forehead, Quint. Not in good faith, Liv. To say, feign or cultivate someone for the sake of the moment, Cic. See For the sake of appearance.

units.la: Simulatio] Dissimulatio. Fallaciloquentia. Imitatio fallax simulatioque virtutis, Cic. Simulacra & imitamenta, Gell. Imitatio doloris, Tac. Prætextus, Suet. Nomen, Virg. Umbra, Liv. Color, Quint. Ostentus, Sallust. vid. Ironia.
units.tr: Pretence] Dissimulation. Deceitful talk. A deceptive imitation and pretence of virtue, Cic. Images and imitations, Gell. Imitation of grief, Tac. Pretext, Suet. A name, Virg. A shadow, Liv. A colour, Quint. A display, Sall. See Irony.

units.la: Simulator] Dissimulator artis, Quintil. Dormitator, Plaut. Ingeniosus ad comminiscendum, Cic. Curialibus moribus præditi. Aulicaster, Bud.
units.tr: Simulator] A dissembler of skill, Quintil. A sluggard, Plaut. Clever at inventing, Cic. Endowed with courtly manners. A little courtier, Bud.

units.la: Simulator officiosus] Obsecundator & omnibus sese dans, Bud. Omnes mores ejus ad venustatem valent, Plaut. Factiosus linguâ, iners opera, Id. In officium plus æquo pronus, Hor.
units.tr: Simulator officiosus] A sycophant who gives himself to everyone, Bud. All his ways tend towards charm, Plaut. Busy with his tongue, idle in deed, Id. Too much inclined to obligingness, Hor.

units.la: Simulatores plerumque perfidi] Artifices fingendi vultus, animo sunt plerumque pessimo.
units.tr: Simulatores plerumque perfidi] Feigners of looks, who are for the most part of the worst disposition.

units.la: Simulatus] Quæsitior adulatio, Tac. Compositus, Acc. Pictus Philosophus. Adumbratus, Cic. v. Affectatus.
units.tr: Simulatus] More studied flattery, Tac. Composed, Acc. A painted philosopher. Shadowed, sketched, Cic. See Affectatus.

units.la: Simulata humanitas] Blandus verbis, re non item. Honoraria opera. Malitiosis blanditiis officiorum, non veritate, sed simulatione quærere aliquid, Cic. Comitas assentatrix, Bud. Letale venenum. vid. Blanditiæ.
units.tr: Simulata humanitas] Smooth in words, not so in deed. Service done for show. To seek something by the malicious flatteries of courtesy, not in truth but in pretence, Cic. Courtesy that flatters, Bud. A deadly poison. See Blanditiae.

units.la: Sincerè] Sincera fide, Liv. Candidè: ex animo, ex fide bona. Ingenuè; integrè & incorruptè. Verissima fronte. Liquidò. Sine fuco & pigmentis. Ex animi sententia jurare, Cic. Merè, Plaut. Aperto pectore. Simpliciter & amicè reprehendere. Ex fide, Plin. Bona fide, Ter. Recto pectore, Amm. Mente, Cic. Sine dolo. (id est, sine dolo) Scal. Purè, Hor. Quod clam, hoc palàm.
units.tr: Sincerè] With sincere faith, Liv. Frankly: from the heart, in good faith. Ingenuously; wholly and uncorrupted. With the most truthful brow. Clearly. Without paint or cosmetics. To swear according to one's real opinion, Cic. Purely, Plaut. With an open breast. To rebuke simply and in friendship. In good faith, Plin. In good faith, Ter. With an upright breast, Amm. In mind, Cic. Without guile (that is, sine dolo), Scal. Purely, Hor. What was secret, now openly.

units.la: Sinceritas] Integritas hominis, Candor animi. Apertum pectus, Cic. Simplicitas nuda, Ovid.
units.tr: Sinceritas] The integrity of a man, the candour of his mind. An open breast, Cic. Naked simplicity, Ovid.

units.la: Sincerus] Sincera mens, Plaut. Apertus homo, antiquus, antiqui officii. Vir integer: quo nemo integrior. Optima & spectatissima fide vir, Cic. Homo antiqua virtute & fide, Ter. Semper tanquam in publico vivit, Sen. Candidus. Pectore store candidus, Ovid. In fronte gerens animum. Mentem habet in fronte. Antiquis moribus.
units.tr: Sincerus] A sincere mind, Plaut. An open man, old-fashioned, of the old sort of duty. An upright man, than whom none is more upright. A man of the best and most proven faith, Cic. A man of old-time virtue and faith, Ter. He lives always as if in public, Sen. Candid. Candid of heart, Ovid. Bearing his mind on his forehead. He has his mind on his brow. Of old-fashioned manners.

units.la: Sine] Absque me, te, illo, Cic. Citra, Col. Seorsum anima, Lucr. Orbus pedum, Liv. Expers consilii, Cic. Defectus aliquâ re, Plin. Viduus pharetrâ, Hor. Viduata loca pruinis, Virg.
units.tr: Sine] Without me, you, or him, Cic. On this side of, Col. Soul apart, Lucr. Bereft of feet, Liv. Lacking counsel, Cic. Deprived of something, Plin. Bereft of the quiver, Hor. Places widowed by frost, Virg.

units.la: Sinere] Sine, & line me, Ter. Missum facere aliquem, Cic. Omitte me. Dare pacem alicui, Plaut. Laudare : laudato ingentia rura, exiguum colito, Virg. Turneb. Quiesce tu, Cic. Reliquum facere, Id. Sine fine, fruatur, Apul. Gratiam facere, Plaut. Compendium, Ter.
units.tr: Sinere] Let be, and leave me alone, Ter. To let someone go, Cic. Let me go. To grant peace to someone, Plaut. To praise: "praise great estates, but cultivate a small one," Virg., Turneb. Be quiet yourself, Cic. To make an end, Id. "Let him enjoy it without end," Apul. To grant a favour, Plaut. To give a saving, Ter.

units.la: Nonsinere] Nunquam per Antonium quietus esse possum, Cic.
units.tr: Nonsinere] "I can never be at rest because of Antonius," Cic.

units.la: Singillatim] Singulatim; singuli audiunt, Duelli rem ago, Cic. Singulare prælium, Ausón. Viritim dimicare, Curt.
units.tr: Singillatim] Singly; each man hears by himself. "I am waging a private war," Cic. A single combat, Ausón. To fight man by man, Curt.

units.la: Singularis] Singulus, Var. Singulariæ literæ, Gell. Simplaris, Veget. Simplarius, Ulp. Unicus prorsùs es ad eandem rem, Plaut. Speciarius, Cæs. Peculiaris, Privata vita, Cic. Præcipuus, Cic.
units.tr: Singularis] Single, Var. Singular letters, Gell. Simplaris, Veget. Simplarius, Ulp. "You are altogether unique in the same matter," Plaut. Speciarius, Caes. Peculiar; private life, Cic. Preeminent, Cic.

units.la: Singulariter] Singulari modo, unicè diligere. Insignitè, Egregiè diligi ab aliquo. Præcipuè decorus color. Maximè, Cic. Peculiariter, Quint.
units.tr: Singulariter] To love in a singular way, uniquely. To be loved distinctly, especially, by someone. A colour especially becoming. Most of all, Cic. Peculiarly, Quint.

units.la: Singuli] Singulatim unicuique denunciabat, Cic. In viros dividere nummos, Plaut.
units.tr: Singuli] He announced it to each one separately, Cic. To divide money among the men, Plaut.

units.la: Sinister] Sinisterior pars, Var. Lævus oculus, Plaut. Exterior comes, Hor. Pallasque sinistro affixus lateri, Virg.
units.tr: Sinister] The more left part, Var. The left eye, Plaut. The outer companion, Hor. And Pallas fixed at the left side, Virg.

units.la: Sinistra manus] Læva, abs. Mala manus, Plaut. (id est, Ominosa, Scal.) Furtiva manus, Id. Scæva, Var.
units.tr: Sinistra manus] The left hand, abs. A bad hand, Plaut. (that is, ominous, Scal.) A thieving hand, Id. The left hand, Var.

units.la: Sinistra pars] Sinistera, Plaut. Sinistrum soli. Lævum, Lucr.
units.tr: Sinistra pars] Sinistera, Plaut. The left side of the ground. The left, Lucr.

units.la: Ad sinistram] Sinistra, Vitr. Sinistrorsum, Hor. Sinistrorsus, Fest. Lævorsum, Apul. Ad lævam est, Plaut. Ad sinisteram, Id.
units.tr: Ad sinistram] To the left, Vitr. Leftwards, Hor. Leftwards, Fest. Leftwards, Apul. It is to the left, Plaut. To the left, Id.

units.la: Sinistrè aliquid interpretari] Indignè ferre, Cic. Malè me id habet, Ter. Ægrè me id habet, Plaut. Aspere; adversis animis, ægrè, graviter, atrociùs, accipere, Tac. Fastidiosè accipere. Malè interpretari, Sen. Duriùs accipere hoc mihi visus est, quàm vellem. Ponere aliquid in nefario sario crimine, atque fraude capitali, Cic. Vitio vertere aliquid alicui, Id. Accipere in malam partem: sicut Cicer. dicit. Accipere in optimam partem.
units.tr: Sinistrè aliquid interpretari] To take something amiss, Cic. It annoys me badly, Ter. It grieves me, Plaut. To take harshly, with hostile minds; to take it ill, grievously, most fiercely, Tac. To receive with disdain. To interpret badly, Sen. I seemed to take this more harshly than I would wish. To place something in a wicked, criminal and capital fraud, Cic. To take something amiss in someone, Id. To take in the bad part, as Cicero says. To take in the best part.

units.la: Sinuare] Sinuare chlamydem, Stat. Laculare, Apul. vid. Serpere.
units.tr: Sinuare] To curve a cloak, Stat. Laculare, Apul. See Serpere.

units.la: Sinuosus] Sinuata chlamys, Stat. Laculata vestis, Isid. Laciniosus, Plin. vid. Tortuosus.
units.tr: Sinuosus] A curved cloak, Stat. A garment with fringes, Isid. Full of flaps, Plin. See Tortuosus.

units.la: Sinus, vid. Gremium.
units.tr: Sinus, see Gremium.

units.la: Sinus fluminum &c.] Diverticulum fluminis. Mart. &c. Divortia aquarum, Cic. Brachium maris, fluminis. Æstuarium à mari affunditur, Liv. Cornu fluminum, Serv. Curuatio & flexus undarum, Id.
units.tr: Sinus fluminum &c.] A side-channel of a river, Mart. &c. Parting of the waters, Cic. An arm of the sea or of a river. The estuary is poured in from the sea, Liv. The horn of rivers, Serv. The curving and bending of the waves, Id.

units.la: Sinus vestis] Laxitas vestis, Pomp.
units.tr: Sinus vestis] The looseness of a garment, Pomp.

units.la: In sinu habere] Fovere dextram sinu, Ovid. Inter tunicas habere, Plaut.
units.tr: In sinu habere] To cherish a right hand in the bosom, Ovid. To keep between the tunics, Plaut.

units.la: Siquidem] Quandoquidem. Quoniam, Cic. Quippe quoniam, Plin. Quatenus, Suet. Quatinus, Fest. Utpote, Spont. Quando, Pro quoniam, Lucr.
units.tr: Siquidem] Since indeed. Since, Cic. Seeing that, Plin. Inasmuch as, Suet. Inasmuch as, Fest. Inasmuch as, Spont. "When," for since, Lucr.

units.la: Sirpare, vid. Plectere.
units.tr: Sirpare, see Plectere.

units.la: Sirpea] Scirpicula, Lucr. Virgea, Var.
units.tr: Sirpea] Little rush-things, Lucr. Made of willow twigs, Var.

units.la: Sistere] Præsentare aliquid alicui, Plin. jun. Repræsentare, Col. Producere, exhibere, Cic. Adesse ad, Id. in, Vlp. Adsum præsens, Plaut. Præsentiam sui facere, Paul I.C. Exhiberi statim servum jubet. Vas factus es sistendi alicujus, Cic. Adstituor tribunali, Apul. Reddere se convivio, Liv. Apparere, abs. & apparere alicui, Plaut, Dare se in conspectum, Cic.
units.tr: Sistere] To present something to someone, Plin. jun. To represent, Col. To produce, to exhibit, Cic. To be present at, Id. in, Ulp. "I am here present," Plaut. To make oneself present, Paul I.C. He orders the slave to be produced at once. You were made a vessel for the summoning of someone, Cic. I take my stand before the tribunal, Apul. To present oneself at a banquet, Liv. To appear, abs., and to appear before someone, Plaut. To put oneself in sight, Cic.

units.la: Sitita] Sit sanè ita. Esto, Cic. Licet: per me licet, Plaut. Viceris, Ter. vid. Concedamus.
units.tr: Sitita] Let it be so, indeed. So be it, Cic. It is allowed: so far as I am concerned, it is permitted, Plaut. You have won, Ter. See Concedamus.

units.la: Sitiens] Sitibundus, Sipont. Siticulosus, Hor. Ardens siti, Claud. Sititor, Apul. Ipsa siti siticulosior, Tantalo siticulosior, Er.
units.tr: Sitiens] Thirsty, Sipont. Very thirsty, Hor. Burning with thirst, Claud. A thirster, Apul. More thirsty than thirst itself; more thirsty than Tantalus, Er.

units.la: Sitire] Sitire aquam, sitiuntur aquæ, Concipere sitim, Ovid. Ardere siti, Claud.
units.tr: Sitire] To thirst for water; waters are thirsted for. To conceive a thirst, Ovid. To burn with thirst, Claud.

units.la: Situla, vid] Vrna.
units.tr: Situla, see Urna.

units.la: Situs] Natura & situs. Positio urbis, Cic. Positura, Lucr. Positus locorum, Tac. Declinatio, Col. Statio operis, Vitr. Qualitas littoris, Col. Situm esse] Situata ad flumem Numantia, Flor. Urbs in montibus posita, Virg.
units.tr: Situs] Nature and situation. The position of a city, Cic. Position, Lucr. The arrangement of places, Tac. Inclination, Col. The station of a work, Vitr. The quality of a shore, Col. Situm esse] Numantia, situated by the river, Flor. A city placed on mountains, Virg.

units.la: Situs alias vid. Mucor, Mucescere.
units.tr: Situs, elsewhere see Mucor, Mucescere.

units.la: Situ corruptus) Obsitus situ, Paterc. Situ vetustatis obductus, Col. Squalet situ, Claud. Oblita squalore vestis, Liv.
units.tr: Situ corruptus] Covered over with mould, Paterc. Overgrown with the mould of age, Col. Squalid with mould, Claud. A garment clotted with filth, Liv.

units.la: Sive] Aut, vel, seu, Cic. Ter. Ve, Enclit. Plus minusve, Virg. Molirive moram, Var. Aliusque quis ferus, Col.
units.tr: Sive] Or, either, Cic., Ter. -ve, enclitic. More or less, Virg. Or to delay, Var. And any other wild creature, Col.

units.la: Sive-sive) Si deus, si dea es, Macrob, Cato. Si intus, si foris volent. Si ego taceam, sive loquar, Plaut. Utrum, Utrumvis, Utrumlibet, Utruncunque, Cic.
units.tr: Sive-sive] If you are a god, if a goddess, Macrob., Cato. Whether within or without they wish. If I am silent or if I speak, Plaut. Whether, whichever, whichever you like, whatever, Cic.

units.la: Soboles, vid. Proles Progenies. Sobolescere, v. Fœtificare.
units.tr: Soboles, see Proles, Progenies. Sobolescere, v. Fœtificare.

units.la: Sobrietas] Abstinentia, Quint.
units.tr: Sobrietas] Abstinence, Quint.

units.la: Sobrius] Siccus, Cic. Abstinentissimus vini, Col.
units.tr: Sobrius] Dry, Cic. Most abstinent from wine, Col.

units.la: Sobrius prudens] Sicca anima sapientissima, Galen.
units.tr: Sobrius prudens] A dry and most wise mind, Galen.

units.la: Sobrium esse] Quanquam ego bibi vinum, at mandata non consuevi simul bibere. Non ego cum vino simitu (i. simul) ebibi ingenium tuum. Dii me infelicitent, si ego in os meum hodie vini guttam indidi. Equidem me siccum & sobrium esse sentio & scio, Plaut.
units.tr: Sobrium esse] Although I have drunk wine, yet I am not accustomed to drink together with orders. I did not drink up your wit together with wine. May the gods make me wretched if I have put a drop of wine into my mouth today. Indeed I feel and know that I am dry and sober, Plaut.

units.la: Socer] Socerus, Plaut. Socrus, M. de Viro. Priscian. Næy. Acc.
units.tr: Socer] A father-in-law, Plaut. Socrus, a mother-in-law, M. de Viro. Priscian. Naev. Acc.

units.la: Socialis] Socia urbs, agmen, Ovid.
units.tr: Socialis] An allied city, an allied army, Ovid.

units.la: Socialiter] Familiariter, familiarissimè. Conjunctissimè versati sumus. Multum uti aliquo. Multum vivere cum aliquo, Cic.
units.tr: Socialiter] On familiar terms, most intimately. We have lived in the closest intimacy. To make much use of someone. To live much with someone, Cic.

units.la: Sociare, vid. Iungere.
units.tr: Sociare, see Iungere.

units.la: Sociari cum aliquo] Consociari cum aliquo. Societatem cum aliquo conflare, inire, jungere, conjungere, copulare, coire, facere, habere. Adscribere se alicui socium. Venire in societatem. Venire, intrare, recipi in familiaritatem. Contrahere familiaritatem. Applicare se ad fam. Dare se in familiaritem. Consv. societ. Dedere se penitus in famil. In consv. alicujus se immergere. Colligare se cum multis. Facere hospitium cum aliquo, Cic. Facere amicitiam & societ. Jungi societate alicui. Assumere in societ. Pangere cum aliquo societatem. Liv. Congregare se cum aliquo, Cic. Contubernium Philosophi inire, Suet. Componere societatem cum Salust. Accedere ad societ. Tac. Conflare familiaritatem, Ter.
units.tr: Sociari cum aliquo] To associate oneself with someone. To form, enter into, join, conjoin, couple, come together, make, or have a partnership with someone. To enrol oneself as a partner with someone. To come into partnership. To come into, enter, be received into intimacy. To contract intimacy. To apply oneself to familiarity. To give oneself up to familiarity. To abandon oneself wholly to intimacy. To plunge oneself into someone's company. To bind oneself with many. To make hospitality with someone, Cic. To make friendship and partnership. To be joined to someone in partnership. To take someone into partnership. To form a partnership with someone, Liv. To join oneself with someone, Cic. To enter the fellowship of a philosopher, Suet. To form a partnership with, Sallust. To come to partnership, Tac. To strike up intimacy, Ter.

units.la: Societas] Familitas, necessitudo, commercium, consuetudo, sodalitium, sodalitas, Officia sodalitatis familiaritatisque ab aliquo flagitare. Consortio, Cic. Consortium, Celf. Contubernium, Spart.
units.tr: Societas] Familiarity, close tie, dealing, custom, fellowship, comradeship. To demand from someone the duties of comradeship and familiarity. Companionship, Cic. Consortium, Celsus. Shared lodging, Spart.

units.la: Societas, Collectivum] Sodales, socii. Sodalitas, Cic. Factio, Secta latronum, Apul. Grex: in his gregibus sunt, Cic. Ter De gregalibus ejus, Cic. Comitatus, Collegium, Id. Ex suo numero legatos mittit, Salust. Familia gladiatorum, Cic.
units.tr: Societas, Collectivum] Comrades, partners. Comradeship, Cic. A faction; a band of robbers, Apul. A flock: "in these flocks there are," Cic., Ter. Of his fellow-herdsmen, Cic. A retinue, a college, Id. He sends envoys from his own number, Sallust. A troop of gladiators, Cic.

units.la: Societas inaequalis] Vulpes cum leonibus congregare. Leonina societas. Quid speculo commercii cum gladio? Commercium cum virtute non habet voluptas, Cic.
units.tr: Societas inaequalis] To gather foxes together with lions. A lion's partnership. What has a mirror to do with a sword? Pleasure has no dealings with virtue, Cic.

units.la: Societas ejusdem] De grege illo est. Ejusdem farinae; ejusdem Musae aemulus. In eodem luto haesitat.
units.tr: Partnership with the same person: He belongs to that flock. Of the same meal; a rival of the same Muse. He is stuck in the same mud.

units.la: Socius] Societate conjunctus. Sodalis. In sodalibus ejus est. Contubernalis, Consors, Comes periculorum &c. Familiaris: ex familiaribus: in familiaribus ejus est. Perfamiliaris alicujus & alicui. Gregalis alicujus. Conjunctissimus mihi est usu, consuetudine, officiis, Cic. Compar, Hor.
units.tr: Partner: Bound by partnership. A companion. A comrade. He is among his companions. A messmate, a fellow, a comrade in dangers, etc. A familiar friend: one of his intimates; he is among his intimates. Very intimate with someone or to someone. A fellow member of someone's flock. He is most closely bound to me by practice, habit and services, Cic. An equal, Hor.

units.la: Sociorum mores similes] Talis quisque est, quales, quibus cum familiaris. Noscitur ex socio, qui non cognoscitur ex se.
units.tr: Companions have similar habits: Each man is such as those he is intimate with. One is known from his companion, who is not known from himself.

units.la: Socium esse calamitatis] Eodem urgeri jugo. In eodem jacere vuletudinario.
units.tr: To share someone's misfortune: To be pressed under the same yoke. To lie in the same sickbed.

units.la: Socium esse alicujus, vid. Familiariter uti.
units.tr: To be someone's partner: see To use familiarly.

units.la: Sodalitium pravum noxium] Affricat morum suorum scabiem convictor Impurus. Claudo vicinus claudicare disces.
units.tr: A wicked, harmful fellowship: An impure fellow lodger rubs the scab of his own habits onto others. Live next to a lame man and you will learn to limp.

units.la: Sol] Jubar aureus, Corn. Sever. Phanes, Macrob. Phaethon, Virg. Fons largifluus caloris, aut luminis, Lucr. Cor coeli. Fons ignis aetherei. Phoebus, Macrob. Mundi oculus, Ovid. Auriga lucis. Flagellum tenebrarum. Astrorum Rex. Umbra lucis Dei. Dispensator temporum. Reductor diei quotidianus. Dux itinerantium. Detector arcanorum. Tenebrionum proditor.
units.tr: Sun: Golden radiance, Corn. Sever. Phanes, Macrob. Phaethon, Virg. Generous fountain of heat or light, Lucr. Heart of heaven. Fountain of ethereal fire. Phoebus, Macrob. Eye of the world, Ovid. Charioteer of light. Scourge of darkness. King of the stars. Shadow of the light of God. Dispenser of times. Daily restorer of the day. Leader of travellers. Discoverer of secrets. Betrayer of the creatures of darkness.

units.la: Solari aliquem] Solatio esse alicui, Caf. Solatio afficere, Tac. Solatium adhibere, Plin. Iun. Consolatione uti, permulcere. Consolari verbis, spe, solatio, per literas de morte. Inducere animum alicujus jacentem in spem, cogitationemque meliorem. Mitigare tristitiam alicujus. Lenire multum consolatione. Solatium alicui dare, præbere. Solatio uti. Levare luctum solatio. Allevare ærumnas distis. Recreare animos afflictos. Consolationem adhibere, Cic. Refocillare animum lugentem, Sen. Alloqui in luctu parentes, Mur. Beatti, Ter. Aspergere, offundere, obsipare, Plaut.
units.tr: To comfort someone: To be a comfort to someone, Caf. To afford consolation, Tac. To offer comfort, Plin. Iun. To use consolation, to soothe. To console with words, with hope, with comfort, by letter on a death. To lead someone's downcast mind into hope and better thoughts. To mitigate someone's sadness. To soothe greatly by consolation. To give or offer comfort to someone. To use comfort. To lighten grief with comfort. To relieve troubles with words. To revive afflicted spirits. To apply consolation, Cic. To revive a grieving mind, Sen. To address parents in their grief, Mur. To make happy, Ter. To sprinkle, pour over, Plaut.

units.la: Solatium Solatiolum doloris, Catul. Solamen mali, Virg. Consolatio, Cic. Animo ægrotanti (laborantî) medicus est oratio.
units.tr: Comfort: A little solace for pain, Catul. The solace of evil, Virg. Consolation, Cic. For a sick (suffering) mind, speech is the physician.

units.la: Solenne est, vid. More fit. Solennis, vid. Consuetus.
units.tr: It is customary: see As is the custom. Customary: see Accustomed.

units.la: Solennis dies Festum solenne, Ovid. Celebris: celeberrimus dies, Cic. Festivissimi dies, Vopisc. Status dies, Plin. jun. Stativæ feriæ, Hotom.
units.tr: Solemn day: A solemn feast, Ovid. A celebrated day, a most celebrated day, Cic. Most festive days, Vopisc. An appointed day, Plin. Iun. Stated holidays, Hotom.

units.la: Solere Solenne habent nuptæ, Plin. Assolet, Ter. Fecit sibi morem, Liv. Est illi consuetudo, Plin. jun. Sum, pro soleo, Cic. Si, ut es, cessabis. Est miseriorum, ut malevolentes sint, & invideant bonis, Plaut. Didici vera dicere, Id. Solitare, Gell. Consuetus fugere, sequi, Lucr. Ut in rebus amat fieri dubiis, Amm. Ut ferè amat, Ter. In moribus est mihi. Natura, consuetudo mea fert, Cic. Mihi sic usus est, Idem. In usu est mihi, Plin. jun. Habeo nunc morem. Meum non est, Plautus. (non soleo.) Suere; appelare svemus, Lucr. Suescere: à te quod svesti peto, Cic. Lucr.
units.tr: To be accustomed: Brides are accustomed to it, Plin. It is customary, Ter. He made it his habit, Liv. He has the custom, Plin. Iun. I am in the habit of it, in place of soleo, Cic. If you will go on idling as you are... It is the way of the unhappy to be spiteful and to envy the good, Plaut. I have learned to speak the truth, Id. To be wont, Gell. Accustomed to flee, to follow, Lucr. As usually happens in doubtful matters, Amm. As he usually loves, Ter. It is my habit. My nature and custom bring it, Cic. My practice is like this, Idem. It is my practice now, Plin. Iun. I have the custom now. It is not my way, Plautus (non soleo). To be accustomed; we call it "to be used to", Lucr. To grow accustomed: what you are accustomed to, I ask of you, Cic., Lucr.

units.la: Solers Provida solersque natura. Solertissimus ad perspiciendum. Sagax homo. Sapiens, Cic. Animo solerti res novas excogitare, Liv. Dispositu & provisu rerum civilium peritus, Tac. Industrius, Cic. Multipotens pectus habet, ubicunque usus fiet pectore expromit suo, Plaut.
units.tr: Skilful: Provident and skilful nature. Most skilful at seeing. A sagacious man. Wise, Cic. To devise new things with a skilful mind, Liv. Experienced in the arrangement and foresight of civil affairs, Tac. Industrious, Cic. He has a breast of many skills; wherever the need arises, he brings forth what is in his breast, Plaut.

units.la: Solers natura Apis nulla nisi artifex nascitur. Aranei simul ac editi sunt fila mittunt.
units.tr: Skilful nature: No bee is born except as a craftsman. Spiders, as soon as they are hatched, begin to spin threads.

units.la: Solerter Solerti animo, Liv. Industriè, Cæs.
units.tr: Skilfully: With a skilful mind, Liv. Diligently, Caes.

units.la: Solertia Ars, Ovid. Cic. Consilium. Industria. Machinatio & solertia quædam in araneolis, Cic.
units.tr: Skill: Art, Ovid, Cic. Counsel. Industry. Some contrivance and cunning in little spiders, Cic.

units.la: Solet Accidere solitum est, Cic. Sæpè ést, Ter. Amat, Tac. Amat fieri, vid. Solere.
units.tr: It happens: It is usual to happen, Cic. It often is so, Ter. He loves, Tac. He tends to happen; see To be accustomed.

units.la: Solicitare, vid. Vrgere. Solicitatio, vid. Importunitas.
units.tr: To importune: see To press. Importuning: see Importunity.

units.la: Solicitator] Suasor & impulsor fuisti, Cic. vid. Svasor.
units.tr: Instigator: You were the persuader and the prompter, Cic. See Persuader.

units.la: Solicitè] Anxiè, Salust. Scrupulosè, Quint.
units.tr: Anxiously: Anxiously, Sall. Scrupulously, Quint.

units.la: Solicitudo] Anxietas, Juv. Angor, Cura, Scrupulus, Tricæ domesticæ. Contractiuncula animi. Aculi & scrupuli solicitudinum, Cic. Hulcus cordi insidens, ex Gyr. Curæ senium accelerant.
units.tr: Anxiety: Anxiety, Juv. Care, worry, scruple, household cares. A little contraction of the mind. The stings and pricks of anxieties, Cic. A sore sitting on the heart, from Gyr. Cares hasten old age.

units.la: Solicitudinem adimere] Allevare alicujus solicitudines. Abstrahere à solicitudine. Liberare, levare curâ, Cic. Exsolvere solicitudine, Plin. jun. Vino pellere curas, Hor. Eximere scrupulum, Cic.
units.tr: To remove anxiety: To relieve someone's anxieties. To draw away from anxiety. To free from care and relieve it, Cic. To release from anxiety, Plin. Iun. To drive away cares with wine, Hor. To remove a scruple, Cic.

units.la: Solicitudo pellit somnum] Anxia mens pervigilat.
units.tr: Anxiety drives away sleep: An anxious mind keeps watch all night.

units.la: Solicitudo noxia] Cor solicitum ossium teredo. Cura facit canos, quamvis homo non habet annos.
units.tr: Harmful anxiety: An anxious heart is a worm in the bones. Care makes hair grey, though a man does not yet have the years.

units.la: Solicitus] Solicitior, Cic. Solicitissimus, Sen. Anxius. Anxiô animô. Curiosus & negotii plenus, Cic. Ipsus se comest. Animo suo sat est homo miser. Curâ macet, Plaut. Districtus solicitudine, Hor. Anxius curis, Salust. gloriæ alicujus, Liv. mentis, Ovid. Anxius alicujus rei, Plin. jun. Suam rem, Liv. Curis æger, Virg. Satagens, Sen. Fricat, scabit caput. Unguem arrodit.
units.tr: Anxious: More anxious, Cic. Most anxious, Sen. Troubled. With an anxious mind. Busy and full of business, Cic. He consumes himself. A wretched man is tormented enough by his own mind. Wasted by care, Plaut. Distracted by anxiety, Hor. Anxious with cares, Sall. Anxious for someone's glory, Liv. Troubled in mind, Ovid. Anxious about a matter, Plin. Iun. Anxious about his own affairs, Liv. Sick with care, Virg. Busy, Sen. He scratches his head. He gnaws his nails.

units.la: Solicitum esse] Sum solicitus eâ re, Ter. De eâ re, Cic. Non sum in hoc solicitus, Quint. Solicitus pro animo, Gell. Solicitus suspicione: quid-nam futurum sit, Cic. Solicitus vicem alterius, Liv. Exedi. Urgeri solicitudine. Solicitudo me stimulat, conficit, afficit. Scrupulus me angit, stimulat. Esse magnâ solitudine. Solicito & anxio esse animo. Cruciari & solicitum esse. Solicitudine me res aliqua afficit. Sustinere solicitudinem. Multa me solicitant anguntque. Afflictare se, Cic. Est mihi hæc res solicitudini. Habet me solicitudo, Plaut. Pati solicitudinem pro, Plin. jun. Anxium esse de, Quint. Ægersum ab animo, Plaut. Miserum ex animo esse. Amburet misero illi corculum carbunculus. Cruciari, agitari, versari, exanimari, differri, Plaut. Perturbari de. Angi animo, intimis sensibus, curis, de. Tangit me hæc cura, cogitatio, Cic. Affici curâ, Plin. jun. Exest, afficit me anxius angor. Scindunt curæ, Lucr. Macerari interdum, Ovid. vid. Angi.
units.tr: To be anxious: I am anxious about that matter, Ter. About that matter, Cic. I am not anxious about this, Quint. Anxious in spirit, Gell. Anxious from suspicion, wondering what will happen, Cic. Anxious on another's account, Liv. To be eaten away. To be oppressed by anxiety. Anxiety gnaws at me, wears me down and afflicts me. A scruple torments and goads me. To be in great anxiety. To be anxious and troubled in mind. To be tormented and anxious. Some matter afflicts me with anxiety. To bear anxiety. Many things trouble me and distress me. To harass oneself, Cic. This matter is a source of anxiety to me. Anxiety holds me, Plaut. To suffer anxiety over, Plin. Iun. To be anxious about, Quint. To be sick at heart, Plaut. To be wretched in mind. A carbuncle burns that poor little heart. To be tormented, driven, turned about, worn out, torn apart, Plaut. To be disturbed about. To be vexed in mind, in the innermost feelings, by cares, about. This care, this thought touches me, Cic. To be affected by care, Plin. Iun. An anxious pain eats me away and afflicts me. Cares tear me apart, Lucr. To be worn down at times, Ovid. See To be distressed.

units.la: Solicitum aliquem reddere] Solicate, Habere solicitum aliquem. Curâ & solicitudine afficere. Afferre alicui solicitudinem. Adducere in solicitudinem. Habere miserrimum molestiis & solicitudinibus, Cic. Conficere solicitudines alicui, Ter. Esse solicitudini. Excruciare animi aliquem, Plaut. Curâ animum alicujus pellere, Liv. Curam afferre, Cic.
units.tr: To make someone anxious: To make someone anxious. To have someone anxious. To affect someone with care and anxiety. To bring anxiety upon someone. To lead someone into anxiety. To keep someone most wretched with troubles and anxieties, Cic. To wear out someone with anxieties, Ter. To be a cause of anxiety to someone. To torment someone's mind, Plaut. To drive care out of someone's mind, Liv. To bring care upon someone, Cic.

units.la: Solidè, vid. Sufficienter.
units.tr: Solidly: see Sufficiently.

units.la: Solidus] Perpetuæ trabes, Cæs. Integer, Hor.
units.tr: Solid: Continuous beams, Caes. Whole, undamaged, Hor.

units.la: Solida, potiùs spectanda, quàm pulchra] Altissima flumina tacitò labuntur sono.
units.tr: Solid things are to be esteemed rather than beautiful ones: The deepest rivers flow on silently, without noise.

units.la: Solitarius] Immunis ab omnibus arbitris, Paterc. Secum vivit, loquitur. Solus est. Solitarius est. Incomitatus incedit. Solus ambulat. Communionem abnuit. Ne musca quidem adest. Agit in solitudine. Secretum agit, Suet. Privatus locus, Ovid. Seorsus, Virg. Solivagus, Plin. vid. Separatus.
units.tr: Solitary: Free from all witnesses, Paterc. He lives and talks with himself. He is alone. He is solitary. He goes about unaccompanied. He walks alone. He refuses company. Not even a fly is there. He lives in solitude. He keeps to a secret place, Suet. A private place, Ovid. Apart, Virg. A wanderer alone, Plin. See Separated.

units.la: Solitudo] Inopia & solitudo alicujus. Viduitas. Ab arbitris remotus locus, sine arbitris, Cic. Vastitas hominis, Plaut. Vastitudo, Acc. Secessus, Plin. Seductus, Sen. Anachoresis, Cassian. vid. Privata vita.
units.tr: Solitude: Someone's want and solitude. Widowhood. A place remote from witnesses, a place without witnesses, Cic. A man's emptiness, Plaut. Desolation, Acc. A retreat, Plin. A withdrawal, Sen. Anachoresis (hermit's life), Cassian. See Private life.

units.la: Solitudo studiis rapta] Amici fures temporis. Stylus secreto gaudet, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Solitude snatched for study: Friends are thieves of time. The pen rejoices in secrecy, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Solitudinem petere] Captare solirudines. Collocare se in solitudinem. Fugæ solitudinique mandare vitam, Cic. Subtrahere se. Petere secretum, Plin. Iun. Seducere se. Recipere se ad tranquilliora. Excerpe te vulgo, & in tranquilliorem portum jactatus recede, Sen.
units.tr: To seek solitude: To seek out solitudes. To place oneself in solitude. To commit one's life to flight and solitude, Cic. To withdraw oneself. To seek seclusion, Plin. Iun. To seclude oneself. To retire to calmer things. Withdraw from the crowd and, once tossed about, retire into a calmer harbour, Sen.

units.la: Solitus, vid. Consuetus.
units.tr: Solitary: see Accustomed.

units.la: Solivagus] Custode remoto, Hor. Desolatum magistro agmen, Stat.
units.tr: Wandering alone: With the guardian removed, Hor. A column left without its leader, Stat.

units.la: Solstitium æstivum] Solstitialis meta Cancri. Partes æstivæ solis, Lucr. Puncta reversionis solis, Turneb.
units.tr: Summer solstice: The solstitial limit of Cancer. The summer parts of the sun, Lucr. The turning points of the sun, Turneb.

units.la: Solstitium hybernum] Solstitialis dies, Cic. Solstitialis nox, Ovid. Brumalis flexus ægocerotis Lucr. Duo Tropica signa, Cancrum & Capricornum, portas solis vocat, Macrob.
units.tr: Winter solstice: A solstitial day, Cic. A solstitial night, Ovid. The wintry bend of Capricorn, Lucr. He calls the two tropical signs, Cancer and Capricorn, the gates of the sun, Macrob.

units.la: Solum, vid. Tantum.
units.tr: Only: see Merely.

units.la: Solvere ligata] Solvere ex catena ad Her. Resolvere nore nodos, Plin. Enodare; nodis exsolvere, Non. Abno-dare, ex Col. vid. Dissolvere. Liberare.
units.tr: To loose what is bound: To release from a chain, Her. To untie knots, Plin. To unfasten, to loosen from knots, Non. See To dissolve. To free.

units.la: Solvere navim] Solvere, abf. Solvere è portu. Solvere anchoram, oram, Cic. Solvere naves è portu, Caes. Moliri naves ab terra. Altum petere. Evehi in altum, Liv. Ancoras tollere, Var. Religare funem, Catul. Referunt me in mare fluctus, Hor.
units.tr: To cast off a ship: To cast off, Abf. To cast off from harbour. To weigh anchor, to slip a cable, Cic. To cast ships off from harbour, Caes. To push ships away from land. To make for the deep. To be carried out to sea, Liv. To lift anchors, Var. To cast off the rope, Catul. The waves carry me back out to sea, Hor.

units.la: Solvere debitum, aut mercedem] Solvere alicui: pecuniam: pro vectura; ad diem: ad denarium. Solvere, dissolvere quod debet aliquis, Cic. Solvere argentum, Plaut. Resolvere argent. Cui debet: pro, Id. Dependere mercedem, Col. dependere, persolvere aliquid alicui. Dare, enumerare pretium. Annumerare pecuniam, reddere mercedem, tribuere praemium alicui. Pendere, pensitare usuram, vectigal, pecuniam. Persolvere, numerare stipendium militibus, Cic. pendere stip. Liv. dependere, Caes. Afficere stipendio milites, Cic. Repraesentare mercedem, Suet. Exsolvere praemium, Liv. pretium, Plaut. Dinumerare alicui pecuniam, Ter. Resolvere pro vino, Catul. Solvendo sum aeri alieno, Liv. Rationem ad sestertium conficere, Vof. Scribere nummos, Plaut. (id est non praesentes, sed apud Trapezitam se obligare, Turneb.) vid. Debitum solvere.
units.tr: To pay a debt or a wage: To pay someone money for transport; on the day; to the last penny. To pay, to settle what someone owes, Cic. To pay out silver, Plaut. To repay money to the one to whom it is owed, Plaut. To pay wages, Col. To pay out, to give something to someone. To give or count out a price. To count out money, to hand over wages, to grant a reward to someone. To weigh out interest, tax, money. To pay out, to count out soldiers' pay, Cic. To pay soldiers' wages, Liv. Caes. To pay the reward, Cic. To pay out the reward, Liv. The price, Plaut. To count out money to someone, Ter. To pay for wine, Catul. I am able to pay my debts, Liv. To make up the account in sesterces, Vof. To write down coins, Plaut. (That is, not to pay now, but to bind oneself to a banker, Turneb.) See To pay a debt.

units.la: Solus] Unus. Unus solus, Plin. Nullo comitante, Mart.
units.tr: Alone] One. One alone, Pliny. With no companion, Martial.

units.la: Sola vox] vid. Vox.
units.tr: Lone voice] See Voice.

units.la: Solisumus] Inter nos dicere liceat.
units.tr: Let me say it] Let me be permitted to say this between ourselves.

units.la: Solum esse miserum est] Vae solis, sociatis inest robur.
units.tr: Being alone is wretched] Woe to the one who is alone; strength lies in those who are joined together.

units.la: Solutio] Resolutio sophismatis, Gell. Enodatio. Dissolutio naturae, Cic.
units.tr: Solution] Resolution of a sophism, Gellius. Explanation. Dissolution of nature, Cicero.

units.la: Solutio debiti] Solutio debitorum, nominis, nominum, rerum creditarum, Cic. Exsolutio, Scaev. I.C. Perscriptio, Cic. ad Att. 1. solutio. Manut. Repraesentatio.
units.tr: Payment of a debt] Payment of debts, of a name, of names, of credited things, Cicero. Full payment, Scaevola the jurist. Entry in the ledger, Cicero, Letters to Atticus, book 1. Payment, Manutius. Repayment.

units.la: Solutus, vid. Liber. Licentiosus.
units.tr: Loose, see Free. Licentious.

units.la: Somniare aliquid] Somniare aliquem, Ter. De aliquo, Cic. In somnis videre aliquid. Visa est in somnis parere. Visa est in quiete habere, &c. Visum ei est in quiete, &c. Quae ei secundum quietem visa sunt. In quiete per visum audisse. Jucundissimis uti somniis. Quo somnio facto, Cic. Consomniare ni are aliquid, Plaut. Videre somnium tale, Ovid. Cernere somnia, Lucr. Venit mihi in somnis imago amici, Virg.
units.tr: To dream something] To dream of someone, Terence. To dream about someone, Cicero. To see something in sleep. She seemed in her sleep to give birth. She seemed in rest to have... It seemed to him in rest, etc. What seemed to him in his sleep. To have heard in rest through a vision. To enjoy most pleasant dreams. Having had this dream, Cicero. To dream such a thing, Plautus. To see such a dream, Ovid. To perceive dreams, Lucretius. The image of a friend came to me in dreams, Virgil.

units.la: Somniator] Somniosus, Plin. Insomniosus, Caro.
units.tr: Dreamer] Dreamy, Pliny. Sleepless, Caro.

units.la: Somniculosè] Oscitanter, Cic.
units.tr: Drowsily] Yawningly, sluggishly, Cicero.

units.la: Somnium] Insomnium, Virg.
units.tr: Dream] Bad dream, Virgil.

units.la: Somnolentia] Diuturna quies, vitiis alimenta ministrat.
units.tr: Drowsiness] Long rest supplies nourishment to vices.

units.la: Somnolentus] Somniculosa senectus. Somni plenus. Oscitans, Cic. Dormitator, Plaut. Solem nec occidentem nec orientem vidit unquam.
units.tr: Drowsy] An old age inclined to doze. Full of sleep. Yawning, Cicero. Dozer, Plautus. He never saw the sun, neither setting nor rising.

units.la: Somnus] Sopor, Virg. Dormitio, Var. Quies, Cic. Imago mortis, Ovid.
units.tr: Sleep] Deep slumber, Virgil. Dozing, Varro. Rest, Cicero. Image of death, Ovid.

units.la: Somnus profundus] Cataphoricus somnus : altissimus, Liv. Artior, Cic. Inexcitabilis, Sen. Truculentus supor, Quint. Altus, ferreus, lethæus somnus, Virg. Inexperrectus homo, Ovid.
units.tr: Deep sleep] Cataphoric sleep: the deepest, Livy. Tighter, Cicero. Unwakeable, Seneca. Savage slumber, Quintilian. Deep, iron, Lethean sleep, Virgil. A man not woken, Ovid.

units.la: Somnus pomeridianus] Somnus de prandio, Plaut. Meridiatio, Cic. Somnus insititius meridie, Var. (Meridiari, Celf. Meridiari, Suet. Diffindere meridiem somno insititio, Var. sunt verba Actionis.)
units.tr: Afternoon sleep] Sleep after dinner, Plautus. Midday rest, Cicero. Adventitious sleep at midday, Varro. (To rest at midday, Celsus. To rest at midday, Suetonius. To split midday with adventitious sleep, Varro; these are words of Actius.)

units.la: Somnus me urget] Cic. Opprimit me somnus, Ter. Urget me sopor, Hor. Sopor occupat artus. Condit somnus natantia lumina, Virg. Inserpit somnus.
units.tr: Sleep overcomes me] Cicero. Sleep oppresses me, Terence. Drowsiness presses me, Horace. Drowsiness seizes my limbs. Sleep closes my swimming eyes, Virgil. Sleep creeps in.

units.la: Sonare] Personare. Resonare. Recinere. Sonos efficere, fundere, percrepare, Cic. Circumsonare, Ovid. Reboant tympana, Claud. Tonant tympana, Lucr. Tintinnire, Fest. Tinnire, Cic. Tintinare, Catul. Consonare, Virg. Concrepare, Proper.
units.tr: To sound] To resound. To echo. To sing back. To produce sounds, to pour out, to ring out, Cicero. To resound all around, Ovid. The drums roar, Claudian. The drums thunder, Lucretius. To tinkle, Festus. To jingle, Cicero. To tinkle, Catullus. To sound together, Virgil. To clatter, Propertius.

units.la: Sonores] Clarè recitare, Plaut. Clamosè loqui, Quint. Magnâ, clarissimâ voce profiteor, Cic. Sublatissimâ, Gell. Conclamare altiore voce, Catul. Exsertâ voce ; exsertè clamare : maximùm, solidum exclamare, Apul. Apertis tibiis, foraminibus canere, Quint. Contentâ voce : summâ vocis contentione : contentè dicere, Cicer. Exclamas ut Stentora vincere possis, Juv.
units.tr: Loudly] To recite clearly, Plautus. To speak loudly, Quintilian. I profess with a great and very clear voice, Cicero. With the highest pitch, Gellius. To shout with a higher voice, Catullus. With an outstretched voice; to cry out loudly: to shout with the greatest and fullest force, Apuleius. To play the pipes with open holes, Quintilian. With strained voice: with the utmost effort of the voice: to speak with strain, Cicero. You shout so loudly that you could outdo Stentor, Juvenal.

units.la: Sonorus] Sonax, Apul.Col. Canorum æs, Virg. Canora vox, clara. Vocalis orator. Acutus & excitatus sonus. Canorum vocis genus. Consonans : consonantiora, grandiora, (sc. verba) Cic. Resonus, Resonabilis, Sonabilis, Ovid. Ovid. Tinnulus, Quint. Sonivivus, Clarisonus, Cic. Sonantior, Plin. jun. Clamosus, Quint. Longè referunt sonitûs tintinnabula, Quint.
units.tr: Sonorous] Resounding, Apuleius, Columella. Bronze that rings sweetly, Virgil. A clear, tuneful voice. A vocal orator. A sharp and stirring sound. A tuneful kind of voice. Consonant: more consonant, grander (words), Cicero. Resonant, resonable, sonorous, Ovid. Tinkling, Quintilian. Sound-living, famous-sounding, Cicero. More resonant, Pliny the Younger. Noisy, Quintilian. Bells carry their sound far, Quintilian.

units.la: Sans, vid. Reus. Sonticus, vid. Exitialis. Legitimus.
units.tr: Guilty, see Accused. Deadly, see Lawful.

units.la: Sonus] Sonitus, Sonor, Canor, Virg. Tinnitus, Plin. Strepitus, Hor.
units.tr: Sound] Noise, resonance, ringing, Virgil. Ringing, Pliny. Din, Horace.

units.la: Sophisma] Depravatio verbi. Tergiversatio. Argutiæ, Cic. Argutiolæ, Gell. Strophæ, Plin. Versutiæ sermonum, Sap. 8. Cavillatus, Apul. Cavillationes juris, verborum, Quint.
units.tr: Sophism] Distortion of a word. Evasion. Subtleties, Cicero. Little subtleties, Gellius. Turns of phrase, Pliny. Crafty twists of speech, Wisdom 8. Quibbles, Apuleius. Quibbles of law and of words, Quintilian.

units.la: Sophista] Sophistes. Contortor legum. Cavillator. Versutiloqvus, Flexiloqvus, Cic. In deterius recta torquens, Sen.
units.tr: Sophist] Sophist. A twister of laws. A quibbler. Smooth-tongued, flexible-tongued, Cicero. Turning straight things to worse, Seneca.

units.la: Sopire] Consopire aliquem, Lucr. Obsopire, Dion. Soporare, Stat. Parere, facere, conciliare, allicere somnum, Plin. Affert somnum aliquid, Cic. Movet, inducit, Cels. Collocare in soporem, Plaut. Invitat somnos rivus, Ovid. Molior somnum, Cels. Facit inire somnum susurro, Virg. vid. Obdormire.
units.tr: To lull] To lull someone to sleep, Lucretius. To lull, Dionysius. To make drowsy, Statius. To produce, bring on, win over sleep, Pliny. Something brings sleep, Cicero. To move, to induce, Celsus. To put into a stupor, Plautus. A stream invites sleep, Ovid. I induce sleep, Celsus. A whisper brings on sleep, Virgil. See To fall asleep.

units.la: Soporus] Soporifer, Somnificus, Virg. Somnifer, Plin. Somniculosus, Cima.
units.tr: Soporific] Sleep-bringing, sleep-making, Virgil. Sleep-bearing, Pliny. Drowsy, Cima.

units.la: Sorbere] Sorbillare aliquid, Ter. Subducere succum spiritu, Plin. Obsorbere aquam, Plaut. Absorbere humorem. Exsorbere ovum, Plin.
units.tr: To sip] To sip something, Terence. To draw up juice with the breath, Pliny. To soak up water, Plautus. To absorb moisture. To suck out an egg, Pliny.

units.la: Sorbilis, vid. Liquidus. Sordere, vid. Fœtere.
units.tr: Sipping, see Liquid. To be filthy, see To stink.

units.la: Sordes] Spurcities cœni, Lucr. Impuritas, Cic. Inquinamentum, Gell. Purgamentum urbis, Liv. Eluvies, Plin. Colluvies, stercorea, fæces amurcæ expressa, Col. Illuvies locorum, Sil. Subluvies, Apul. Situs: loca senta situ, Virg.
units.tr: Filth] Foulness of mud, Lucretius. Impurity, Cicero. Pollution, Gellius. Sweepings of the city, Livy. Washings, Pliny. Drainage, dung, dregs of pressed oil-lees, Columella. Filth of places, Silius. Dirt washed away, Apuleius. Squalor: places overgrown with squalor, Virgil.

units.la: Sordidè] Sordidissimè per cloacas ductus est, Lamp. vid. Impurè.
units.tr: Filthily] Most filthily led through the sewers, Lampridius. See Impurely.

units.la: Sordidus] Sordidatus, Ter. Sordidulus, Plaut. Obsoletus sordidus, Hor. Squalidus homo, Plaut. Squarosus, Lucil. Squalore obsita vestis, Liv. Pædidus, Fest. Dentes scabri rubigine, Ovid. vid. Immundus sus, Virg. Luteus, Plaut. Fœdus odor, Plin. Spurcissimus heluo, Cic. Lutulenta & impura persona, Plaut. Squalus, Enn.
units.tr: Filthy] Dirty-clad, Terence. Somewhat dirty, Plautus. Shabby and dirty, Horace. A squalid man, Plautus. Squalid, Lucilius. Clothing covered in squalor, Livy. Dirty, Festus. Teeth rough with rust, Ovid. See Unclean pig, Virgil. Muddy, Plautus. Foul smell, Pliny. The filthiest glutton, Cicero. A muddy and unclean person, Plautus. Squalid, Ennius.

units.la: Sors] Sortitio. Sortitus. Subsortitio. Sortes, Cic.
units.tr: Lot] Drawing of lots. Allotment. Subsidiary drawing. Lots, Cicero.

units.la: Sorte] Sortitò, Plaut. Sorti cecidit, Virg.
units.tr: By lot] By lot, Plautus. It fell by lot, Virgil.

units.la: Sortiri] Sortiri ad pœnam : quid loquare : judices. Sortes ducere. Rem ad sortem revocare. Sorte agros assignare. Subsortiri Prætorem in locum alterius, Cic. Sorte dare, trahere aliquid, Virg. Tracta sorte, Suet. Ductu sortis deligere, Fest. Sors cernat, Liv. Micare cum aliquo, Var. Sortitionem facere. Sortitò aliquid capere, Cic.
units.tr: To draw lots] To draw lots for punishment: what do you say, judges? To draw lots. To refer a matter to the lot. To assign fields by lot. To appoint a praetor by lot in another's place, Cicero. To give or draw something by lot, Virgil. Drawn by lot, Suetonius. To choose by drawing lots, Festus. Let the lot decide, Livy. To play at dice with someone, Varro. To hold a drawing of lots. To take something by lot, Cicero.

units.la: Sortitor] Sortilegus, Cic.
units.tr: Diviner] A sorcerer who casts lots, Cicero.

units.la: Sospes, vid. Sanus. Sospitare, vid. Conservare.
units.tr: Safe, see Sound. To preserve, see To conserve.

units.la: Spadiceus] Spadix, Virg. Bajus, balius, badius, Var. Castaneus color, Bayf, Myrteus color in equis, Pallad. Murrheus crinis, Hor. Myrrhea coma, Tibul. v. Purpureus.
units.tr: Chestnut-coloured] Chestnut horse, Virgil. Bay, Varro. Chestnut colour, Bayf. Myrtle colour in horses, Palladius. Myrrh-coloured hair, Horace. Myrrh-coloured hair, Tibullus. See Purple.

units.la: Spado, vid. Eviratus.
units.tr: Eunuch, see Castrated.

units.la: Spargere] Spargere humum foliis, Virg. Perspergere, spargere aliquid sale, Cic. Aspergere sale carnes, & salem carnibus, Plin. Inspergere sale, Col. Superspargere, Cat. Respergere pulvere, Stat. Conspergere ante ædes, Plaut. Inspergere Circumspergere stercus, simum arbori, Col. Præspargere, vel, præspergere viam floribus, Lucr. Prospergere, Apul. Interspersus, habet Id. Incernere terram cribro, Cat. Incernere aliquid super aliquid, Vitr. Supercernere terram, Plin.
units.tr: To scatter] To strew the ground with leaves, Virgil. To sprinkle something with salt, Cicero. To sprinkle meat with salt and salt on meat, Pliny. To strew with salt, Columella. To scatter over, Cato. To sprinkle with dust, Statius. To sprinkle in front of the houses, Plautus. To strew manure or dung around a tree, Columella. To strew in advance, or to strew the way with flowers, Lucretius. To sprinkle, Apuleius. Interspersed, has Id. To sift earth through a sieve, Catullus. To sift something over something, Vitruvius. To sift earth over, Pliny.

units.la: Sparsim] Dispersè, Cic. Dispersim, Var. Carptim, Sallust. Palatim, Liv. Vagè aliquid dispergere, ad Her. Saltuatim, Sisen. Saltim, And. Schot.
units.tr: Scattered] Dispersedly, Cicero. Dispersedly, Varro. Piecemeal, Sallust. Here and there, Livy. To scatter something widely, Rhetorica ad Herennium. By leaps, Sisenna. By jumps, Andreas Schottus.

units.la: Spasmus] Convulsio nervorum, Plin. Distentio nervorum, Celsf. Nervorum conductio, Cæl. Aurel.
units.tr: Spasm] Convulsion of the nerves, Pliny. Stretching of the nerves, Celsus. Contraction of the nerves, Caelius Aurelianus.

units.la: Spatiari] Facere spatia, Cic. Prodeambulare, Ter. vid. Deambulare.
units.tr: To walk about] To take strides, Cicero. To stroll ahead, Terence. See To stroll.

units.la: Spatiosè, vid. Latè.
units.tr: Spaciously, see Widely.

units.la: Spatium] Area, Var. Areola, Plin. jun. Intervallum, Vitr. Intervallum loci, Cæf. Temporis, Cic. Tabula jugeralis, Pallad. Interstitium loci, Macr. Interstitio, Arnob. Diastema, Sidon. Tractus maris, Virg. Semporis, Paterc.
units.tr: Space] Area, Varro. Little open area, Pliny the Younger. Interval, Vitruvius. Interval of place, Caesar. Of time, Cicero. Surveyed plot, Palladius. Gap in place, Macrobius. Interval, Arnobius. Interval, Sidonius. Stretch of sea, Virgil. Of time, Paterculus.

units.la: Specialiter] Speciatim, Cic. Particulariter dicere, Firm. Particulatim, Sen. Propriè, Cic.
units.tr: Specially] Specifically, Cicero. To speak particularly, Firmicus. Particularly, piecemeal, Seneca. Properly, Cicero.

units.la: Species, vid. Figura.
units.tr: Species, see Figure.

units.la: Specimen] Argumentum, Cic. Experimentum, Suet.
units.tr: Specimen] Proof, Cicero. Experiment, Suetonius.

units.la: Specimen edere] Dare aliquod specimen indolis, Plin. Dare aliquod sui specimen, Cic. Experimentum insignis artificii dare, Suet.
units.tr: To give a specimen] To give some specimen of one's talent, Pliny. To give some specimen of oneself, Cicero. To give a trial of remarkable skill, Suetonius.

units.la: Speciosè] Ad speciem, Cic. Spectatissimè, Plin. Ad gratiam, Liv. vid. Pulchrè.
units.tr: Speciously] In appearance, Cicero. Most conspicuously, Pliny. To win favour, Livy. See Beautifully.

units.la: Speciosus. vid. Pulcher.
units.tr: Specious, see Beautiful.

units.la: Spectaculum] Theatrum. Spectaculum apparatissimum, pulcherrimum, Cic. Spectaculum lusorium, Sen. Phasma, Juv. Munus populare, Cic. vid. Theatrum.
units.tr: Spectacle] Theatre. A most magnificent, most beautiful spectacle, Cicero. A spectacle of play, Seneca. Apparition, Juvenal. A public show, Cicero. See Theatre.

units.la: Spectare] Spectat oculis devorantibus aliquem, Mart. Vitas hominum tanquam in speculo inspicere, Ter. Inspectare, Contueri duobus oculis. Contemplari oculis, Cic. Fixis oculis intueri. Nunc specimen specitur, Plaut. Intueri aliquem, & in aliquem: coram, Cic. Intueri modestè, Ter. Cernere oculis, Cic. Pascere oculos, Ter. lumina, Ovid. Figere obtutum. Intendere aciem oculorum.
units.tr: To look at] He gazes at someone with devouring eyes, Martial. To view the lives of men as in a mirror, Terence. To look into, to gaze at with both eyes. To contemplate with the eyes, Cicero. To look with fixed eyes. Now a sight is seen, Plautus. To look at someone and at someone: face to face, Cicero. To look modestly, Terence. To see with the eyes, Cicero. To feast the eyes, Terence. The eyes, Ovid. To fix the gaze. To direct the sight of the eyes.

units.la: Spectatio] Contuitus, Cic. Obtutus continuus. Intuitus, Quint. Obtuitus, Fest. Obtuitio, Apul. Inspectio rerum suarum, Plin. Inspectatio, Sen.
units.tr: Looking] Gaze, Cicero. Continuous gaze. Look, Quintilian. Gazing, Festus. Gazing, Apuleius. Inspection of one's own things, Pliny. Inspection, Seneca.

units.la: Spectator] Spectator cœlestium. Speculator naturæ. Contemplator cœli, Cic. Considerator & scepticus. Philosophus, Gell. Contemplativus. Admirator, Sen. Inspector siderum, Plin. jun. Contemplabilis artifex, Amm. Speculativus, Sipont. Spectaculum, pro spectatoris. Liv.
units.tr: Spectator] Observer of heavenly things. Observer of nature. Contemplator of the sky, Cicero. Considerer and sceptic. Philosopher, Gellius. Contemplative. Admirer, Seneca. Stargazer, Pliny the Younger. Skilled contemplating craftsman, Ammianus. Speculative, Sipontinus. Spectacle, for spectator, Livy.

units.la: Spectatus, vid. Probatus.
units.tr: Watched, see Proven.

units.la: Spectrum] Larva umbratilis, Plaut. Larvalis forma, Apul. Monstrum, Plaut. Nocte volantes umbræ, Ovid. Idolum apparebat, Plin. jun. Occursaculum. Apul. Occursatrix (Scil. avis) Fest.
units.tr: Apparition] Shadowy phantom, Plautus. Ghostly shape, Apuleius. Monster, Plautus. Shadows flying by night, Ovid. An idol appeared, Pliny the Younger. A meeting thing, Apuleius. A meeting (of a bird), Festus.

units.la: Spectrum demortui] Simulacra virûm majora viiis, Sen. Deformes animæ, Ovid. Umbrarum facies, Petron.
units.tr: Apparition of the dead] Images of men larger than life, Seneca. Deformed souls, Ovid. Faces of shades, Petronius.

units.la: Specula] Custodia, Cic. Ex speculâ prospectare. Statio. Collocatas in stationecohortes, &c. Val. Max. Conspicillium, Plaut. Vel conspicillum, Lamb.
units.tr: Watchtower] Guard, Cicero. To look out from a watchtower. Station. Cohorts stationed in their posts, etc., Valerius Maximus. Spyglass, Plautus. Or spyglass, Lambinus.

units.la: Speculari] Contemplari unumquodque otiosè. Perspicere cere aliquid cum cura & consilio omni vie ingenii contem-plari. Dispicere aliqvid, considerare. Perlustrare animo. Ponere ante oculos aliquid. Constituite vobis ante oculos. Oculos adjicere alicui rei. Contemplari intentis oculis : acerrimè. Intuere aliquid acri & intento animo, Cic. Intueri acrioribus oculis : sagaciter, Quint. Perlustrare oculis. Noscitare aliquem, Liv. Oculos per singula volvere. Servare sidera, Virg. Inscrutari aliquid altius, Macr. Noscitabundus accedo, Gell. Pervidere pulchritudinem, Plin. jun. Inspicere propius hominem, Id. Curiose arbitrabar jugulum comitis, Apul. Obtueri aliquem, Plaut.
units.tr: To speculate] To contemplate anything at leisure. To look into something with care and all the power of mind. To examine something, to consider. To survey in the mind. To set before the eyes. Set before your eyes. To direct the eyes to a thing. To contemplate with intent eyes: most keenly. To look at something with a sharp and intent mind, Cicero. To look with sharper eyes: shrewdly, Quintilian. To survey with the eyes. To recognise someone, Livy. To roll the eyes over single things. To watch the stars, Virgil. To investigate something more deeply, Macrobius. I approach looking about me, Gellius. To perceive beauty, Pliny the Younger. To look more closely at a man, Id. I was curiously eyeing my companion's throat, Apuleius. To gaze at someone, Plautus.

units.la: Speculari 2. vid. Explorare.
units.tr: Speculari 2. see Explorare.

units.la: Speculator] Excubitor, Cælf. Præfectus vigilum, Paul I. C. Procubitor ante castra, Fest. Circuitor, Virg. Stationarius, Vlp. Nictostrategus, Robert. Constant.
units.tr: Speculator] Watchman, Cælf. Prefect of the night watch, Paul I. C. Vanguard scout before the camp, Fest. Scout, Virg. Patrolman, Vlp. Night-scout [νυκτοστρατηγός], Robert. Constant.

units.la: Speculum] Specula uda ex ære, argento, suda influvio, Apul. Glacies æris. Æquor seu planities speculi, Lucr.
units.tr: Speculum] Mirrors moist from bronze or silver, sweating with flowing water, Apul. The gleam of bronze. A level surface or plane of a mirror, Lucr.

units.la: Speculum inspicere, vid. Contemplari se in spec.
units.tr: Speculum inspicere, see Contemplari se in spec.

units.la: Specus] Spelunca Caverna, Cic. Virg. Antrum, Id. Desidiabula, (loca desidiæ apta) Plaut. Successus terrarum, Arnob.
units.tr: Specus] A cave, cavern, Cic. Virg. A cave, Id. A lazing-hole (a place suited to idleness), Plaut. The hollows of the lands, Arnob.

units.la: Sperare] Spe ali, duci, niti, pendere, teneri, inflammari spe potiunt. Spe bona esse. In spe esse. In spem venire, adduci. Tenet, obtentat, consolatur me spes. In optima spe ponere, in spe habere. Habere spem propositum. Spe atque animo incubare. Spes est. Sperare bene de aliquo, ab aliquo. Confidere, Cic. Spe, & spem concipere. Affulget spes, Liv. Spem tenere, Plaut. In spem erigi, Tac. Præsumere animo, Val. Max. Spes præsumpta, Tac. Ingredi in spem. De tuo ingenio bonam spem capimus, tebrevi in virum evasurum. Colloco, figo, repono in spem. Vocari in spem. Erectus in spem. Nonnulla me spes habet. Magna me spes tenet. Maxima teneor spe. Spei nonnihil affulsit, Eraf.
units.tr: Sperare] To be nourished by hope, led on, supported, hung upon, held fast, set aflame with hope. To be hopeful. To be in hope. To come into hope, to be brought to it. Hope holds, sustains and comforts me. To place in the best hope, to have in hope. To have hope as one's aim. To lie brooding in hope and spirit. There is hope. To hope well of someone or from someone. To trust, Cic. To conceive hope and expectation. Hope shines forth, Liv. To keep hope, Plaut. To be raised into hope, Tac. To anticipate in mind, Val. Max. Anticipated hope, Tac. To enter into hope. We conceive good hope of your talent, that you will soon grow into a man. To place, fix, lay up in hope. To be called into hope. Raised up in hope. I have some hope. A great hope holds me. I am held by the greatest hope. Some hope has dawned on me, Erasm.

units.la: Spero ita esse] Aut omnia me fallunt.
units.tr: Spero ita esse] Unless I am completely mistaken.

units.la: Sperare multum successum] Sperare invidiam.
units.tr: Sperare multum successum] To hope for great success. To hope for ill will [envy].

units.la: Spes] Spes omnes. Fiducia, Cic. Specula, Plaut.
units.tr: Spes] All hopes. Confidence, Cic. A lookout post, Plaut.

units.la: Spes est] Bona spes ostensa. Addicunt aves, Liv. Est aliquid, vel aliquis in spe, Cic.
units.tr: Spes est] A good hope has been shown. The birds give favourable omens, Liv. There is something, or someone, in hope, Cic.

units.la: Spes ultima] Ancora sacra.
units.tr: Spes ultima] The sacred anchor.

units.la: Spes vana] Ægri somnia. Anguillam caudâ tenes. Inanium inania consilia. Inani spe flagrat. Pascitur vento, rore. Scipioni arundineo innititur.
units.tr: Spes vana] The dreams of a sick man. You hold an eel by its tail. The empty plans of empty men. He burns with empty hope. He feeds on wind and dew. He leans on a reed staff.

units.la: Spes frustrata] Bolus è faucibus ereptus. Spes subventanea.
units.tr: Spes frustrata] A morsel snatched from the jaws. A hope blown away by the wind.

units.la: Spes alit agricolam] Agricola semper in novum annum dives.
units.tr: Spes alit agricolam] The farmer is always rich in the coming year.

units.la: Spes longa adhuc] Messis in herba.
units.tr: Spes longa adhuc] The harvest is still in the blade.

units.la: Spe dives] Spe Croesô ditior, inopiâ Irô pauperior.
units.tr: Spe dives] Richer in hope than Croesus, poorer in want than Irus.

units.la: Spem facere alicui] Spem dare, alere, augere. Impellere, vocare, adducere Inducere in spem. Spe consolari, inflammare, Cic. Bonâ spe complere, Cæs. Inflare spem alicujus, Liv. Fovere spem alicujus, Sen. Firmare ad spem, Tac.
units.tr: Spem facere alicui] To give, nourish, increase hope. To urge, call, lead, bring into hope. To comfort or inflame with hope, Cic. To fill with good hope, Caes. To inflate someone's hope, Liv. To foster someone's hope, Sen. To strengthen towards hope, Tac.

units.la: Spem alicui auferre] Cic. Debilitare, eripere, præcidere spem. Avertere à spe. Sublata spes, Cic. Abdicunt aves, Id.
units.tr: Spem alicui auferre] Cic. To weaken, snatch away, cut off hope. To turn away from hope. Hope taken away, Cic. The birds take away the omen, Id.

units.la: Spem in aliquo ponere] Spem in fide ulterius habere. Spem collocare in aliquo, vel in aliqua re, Cic. Spes omnis in te est. In virtute tua spes residet, Cic. Spem de aliquo capere, Quint. Deponere spem in aliqua re, Curt.
units.tr: Spem in aliquo ponere] To have hope further in someone's good faith. To place one's hope in someone, or in something, Cic. All hope is in you. My hope rests in your virtue, Cic. To take hope from someone, Quint. To put down hope in something, Curt.

units.la: Spem abjicere] Præďamnare spem, Liv. v. Desperare.
units.tr: Spem abjicere] To condemn hope in advance, Liv. See Desperare.

units.la: Sperandum semper] Animus æquus optimum ærumnæ condimentum, Plaut. Animus bonus in re mala dimidium est mali, Id.
units.tr: Sperandum semper] A calm mind is the best seasoning for hardship, Plaut. A good mind in a bad situation is half the evil, Id.

units.la: Sperandum adhuc] Non statim finis apparet. Sol omnium dierum nondum occidit. Fata viam invenient. Adhuc aliquis Deus respicit nos. Adhuc cœlum volvitur.
units.tr: Sperandum adhuc] The end does not appear at once. The sun of all days has not yet set. The fates will find a way. Some God still looks upon us. The heavens still turn.

units.la: Speranda credere] Credit facilè quod quisque sperat.
units.tr: Speranda credere] A man readily believes what he hopes.

units.la: Spiculator, vid. Satelles. Spiculum, vid. Jaculum.
units.tr: Spiculator, see Satelles. Spiculum, see Jaculum.

units.la: Spina arbuscula] Rubus, Sentis, Col. Sentix, Prudent. Vepris, Col. Vepres. Veprecula. Dumus, Cic. Luna, Varr. Acacia. Polyacanthos, Plin.
units.tr: Spina arbuscula] Bramble, briar, Col. Thorn-bush, Prudent. Brier, Col. Briers. A little briar. Thicket, Cic. Buckthorn, Varr. Acacia. Many-thorned plant, Plin.

units.la: Spinetum] Senticetum, Plaut. Vepretum, Col. Vepreta, æ, Priscian. dumetum, Cic. Rubetum, Ovid. Lumetum & Lumectum, Var. Sipont.
units.tr: Spinetum] A thorn-brake, Plaut. A briar-patch, Col. A briar-patch, Priscian. A thicket, Cic. A bramble-patch, Ovid. A thicket of brambles, Var. Sipont.

units.la: Spinosus] Spinifer, Cic. Senticosus, Afran, Dumosus, Col. Vepricosus, Gell.
units.tr: Spinosus] Thorn-bearing, Cic. Full of brambles, Afran. Thicketed, Col. Full of briars, Gell.

units.la: Spiraculum] Spiramentum, Virg. Spiramenta cavernæ; in alveis apum, Col. Cavernulæ, Plin, Fauces pestiferæ (sc. orci) Virg.
units.tr: Spiraculum] A breathing-hole, Virg. The breathing-holes of a cave; in beehives, Col. Little caverns, Plin. The pestilential jaws (of the underworld), Virg.

units.la: Spirare] Halare naribus, Lucr. Rehalare, Id. vid. Respirare, Anhelare.
units.tr: Spirare] To breathe through the nostrils, Lucr. To breathe again, Id. See Respirare, Anhelare.

units.la: Spiritualis] Ad animum; cultum vel culturam animi, spectans. Mentem ad Deum, vel ad divina excitans. Homo vitæ istius contemptor & cœlestis affectator, Res animi, vel animorum. Homo divinis deditus. Divinus vir.
units.tr: Spiritualis] Pertaining to the soul; looking to the cultivation or culture of the mind. Raising the mind to God or to divine things. A person who despises this life and aspires to heavenly things. Matters of the mind or of minds. A man devoted to divine things. A godly man.

units.la: Spiritualis sensus] Interpretatio, res, vires naturæ superans. Sensus altior, quàm ut naturali vi intellectùs comprehendatur. Cœlitus infusa, non excogitata verborum intelligentia.
units.tr: Spiritualis sensus] An interpretation that surpasses the matter, the powers of nature. A meaning higher than can be grasped by the natural power of the intellect. An understanding of words poured in from heaven, not invented.

units.la: Spiritualiter interpretari] Literam ad spiritum traducere. ex Isid.
units.tr: Spiritualiter interpretari] To carry the letter over to the spirit. From Isidore.

units.la: Spiritus] Deum mentem vocat, Cic. Animos cœlestes, Virg. Architectus & auriga corporis, vid. Anhelitus Aer.
units.tr: Spiritus] God calls [him] mind, Cic. Heavenly spirits, Virg. The architect and charioteer of the body; see Anhelitus Aer.

units.la: Spiritus sanctuæ] Pneuma divinum.
units.tr: Spiritus sanctus] The divine Pneuma [πνεῦμα].

units.la: Spissè &c. vid. Densè, &c.
units.tr: Spissè etc., see Densè, etc.

units.la: Spithama] Palmus major. Dodrans pedis, Plin.
units.tr: Spithama] A greater span. Three-quarters of a foot, Plin.

units.la: Splen] Lien, Plaut. Lienis, in Retto apud Celf.
units.tr: Splen] The spleen, Plaut. Of the spleen, in the Retto passage in Celsus.

units.la: Splendens] Coruscus. Crispisulcans fulmen, Cicer. ex Poët.
units.tr: Splendens] Flashing. A crackling, jagged lightning-bolt, Cicero, from the poets.

units.la: Splendere &c. vid. Nitere. Splendidus, vid. Clarus.
units.tr: Splendere etc., see Nitere. Splendidus, see Clarus.

units.la: Splendor] Luculentitas & magnificentia, Coel. Rhod. Adhibere speciem atque pompam. Pompa triumphi, Cic. Claritudo, Salust.
units.tr: Splendor] Brightness and magnificence, Coel. Rhod. To put on show and display. A triumphal procession, Cic. Brilliance, Sall.

units.la: Splenēticus] Splenicus, Firm. Lienicus. Lienosus, Plin.
units.tr: Splenēticus] Splenic, Firm. Of the spleen. Spleeny, Plin.

units.la: Spoliare] Spolia capere, detrahere, Cic. Manus afferre bonis alicujus. Manubias facere. Depeculari, Id.
units.tr: Spoliare] To take and strip spoils, Cic. To lay hands on another's goods. To make booty. To plunder the public treasury, Id.

units.la: Spoliatio] Latrocinatio, Plin. Prædatio, Paterc. Depræda-tio, Firm. Præda, Cic. Batillatio, Fest.
units.tr: Spoliatio] Robbery, Plin. Plundering, Paterc. Pillaging, Firm. Booty, Cic. Stripping, Fest.

units.la: Spoliator, vid. Prædator, Latro.
units.tr: Spoliator, see Prædator, Latro.

units.la: Spolium]Præmia pugnæ, Virg. vid. Præda.
units.tr: Spolium] The rewards of battle, Virg. See Præda.

units.la: Spondere] Fidem suam spondere, Cic. Fide suâ spondere, Plin. Sanctè sanctissimè, affirmatè Deo teste promittere. Promittere ac recipere sanctissimè observaturum. Appromittere. Deos omnes contestans promitto. Mea af-firfirmatione recipio. Omni asseveratione affirmare. Pro certo hoc vobis polliceor. Obligare se verbo, Cic. Sacramento obligatum esse, Sen. Expromittere, Vlp. Auctores tibi sumus fore. Dare dextram fidemque. Obligare fidem alicui suam, Liv. Dare alicui firmatam fidem, Plaut. Obstringere fidem suam, Plin. adstringere, Plin. jun. De plano promittere, Lucr. Fidem interponere.
units.tr: Spondere] To pledge one's faith, Cic. To pledge by one's honour, Plin. To promise most solemnly and affirmatively, calling God as witness. To promise and undertake most solemnly that one will observe it. To promise in addition. I promise, calling all the gods to witness. I undertake it on my affirmation. To affirm with every solemn assurance. I give you this as a sure promise. To bind oneself by one's word, Cic. To be bound by an oath, Sen. To promise out, Ulp. We shall be your guarantors. To give one's right hand and pledge. To bind one's faith to another, Liv. To give a firm pledge to someone, Plaut. To bind one's faith, Plin. To bind firmly, Plin. jun. To promise outright, Lucr. To interpose one's faith.

units.la: Spondere pro aliquo] Spondere pro, de aliquo. Intercedere pro aliquo. Fidem suam pro aliquo pignori ponere. Fidem suam in aliquid interponere. Fidem meam alteri do, de aliquo. Do me vadem alicui pro aliquo. Vas fio sistendi alicujus, Cic. Fide mea fac, si isti formidas credere, Plaut. Fide jubeo pro aliquo. Fide mea aliquid esse jubeo, Vlp. Intervenio fidejussor pro aliquo, Id. Vadimonium promittere, adpromittere, Cicer. Præstare. Satisdare damni infecti, Id. Ego tibi hujus nomine fide jubeo. Recipio tibi facturum hunc. Recipio ad me, Hoc tibi meo periculo promitto. Ita mihi stipulanti pactus est.
units.tr: Spondere pro aliquo] To stand surety for, or concerning, someone. To intercede for someone. To pledge one's faith for someone as a pledge. To put one's faith into something. I give my bond for another, concerning someone. I give myself as bail for someone. I stand surety for someone's appearance, Cic. Trust me, if you are afraid to entrust him, Plaut. I stand surety for someone with my faith. I bind myself by my faith that something will be, Ulp. I come forward as surety for someone, Id. To promise a bail-bond, to undertake it, Cic. To answer for, to guarantee. To give security against loss to come, Id. On this matter I bind myself with my faith to you. I undertake that this man will do it. I undertake to answer for it at my own risk; I promise you this. Thus he agreed with me by my questioning.

units.la: Sponsa] Sperata mea. Sperata salve, Plaut. Nympha, Bud.
units.tr: Sponsa] My hoped-for one. Hail, hoped-for one, Plaut. A bride-nymph, Bud.

units.la: Sponsalia] Coëmptio. Cic. Pactionem connubialem facere, Liv. Sponsus: sponsu erat alligatus, Var. Sponsionum, stipulationum contractus, Gell. Conventæ conditio, vel conventa conditio, Fest. Conditio, est conjunctio, vel pactio nuptiarum, vel sponsaliorum, apud Suet. vid. Copula Matrim.
units.tr: Sponsalia] A marriage by purchase, Cic. To make a marriage contract, Liv. A betrothed man: he was bound by a betrothal, Varr. A contract of promises and stipulations, Gell. The agreed condition, or the agreed term, Fest. The condition, that is, the union or agreement of a marriage or betrothal, in Suet. See Copula Matrim.

units.la: Sponsalia celebrare] In manum convenire. Facere coemptionem, Cic.
units.tr: Sponsalia celebrare] To come into the husband's power (manus). To make a marriage by purchase, Cic.

units.la: Sponsalis dies] Varr. Sponsalitia largitas, in C.
units.tr: Sponsalis dies] Varr. Generous betrothal gifts, in C.

units.la: Sponsio] Sponsum: ex sponso agere, Cic. Stipulatio, Id. Consponsio, Scal. vid. Promissio, & Votum.
units.tr: Sponsio] A pledge; to sue on a pledge, Cic. A stipulation, Id. Joint pledge, Scal. See Promissio, and Votum.

units.la: Sponsione contendere, vid. Certare pignore.
units.tr: Sponsione contendere, see Certare pignore.

units.la: Sponsor] Fidejussor. Expromissor, Vlp. Adpromissor, Fest. Auctor securus. Interventor, Vlp. Manceps, Plaut. vid. Vas.
units.tr: Sponsor] A surety. A guarantor who takes over the debt, Ulp. One who promises in addition, Fest. A secure guarantor. An intervenor, Ulp. A contractor, Plaut. See Vas.

units.la: Sponsus] Spem suam vocat sponsa, apud Plaut. Speratus, Non.
units.tr: Sponsus] The bride calls her husband-to-be "my hope," in Plautus. Hoped-for, Non.

units.la: Spontaneus] Ultroneus, Sen. Voluntarius, Gratuitus, Cic. Affectata brevitas, Macrob. (Spontalis, Apul.)
units.tr: Spontaneus] Of one's own accord, Sen. Voluntary, freely given, Cic. Studied brevity, Macrob. (Spontalis, Apul.)

units.la: Sponte] Sponte suâ, tuá, meâ, Cic. Voluntario, Liv. Voluntariè, Caf. Voluntate impetrare, Ter. Suâ voluntate, nullâ vi coactus. Ultrò. Consciscere sibi mortem voluntariam, Cic. Suapte mobilitate alescit. Res ipsa per se vocifecratur, Lucr. Ab se cantat, Plaut. Voluntarius adest, Liv.
units.tr: Sponte] Of one's own accord, by yourself, by me, Cic. Voluntarily, Liv. Voluntarily, Caes. To obtain by consent, Ter. By one's own will, compelled by no force. Of its own accord. To procure a voluntary death for oneself, Cic. It grows by its own pliancy. The thing itself reveals its meaning, Lucr. He sings of his own accord, Plaut. It comes voluntarily, Liv.

units.la: Sponte miser] Accersitum malum.
units.tr: Sponte miser] Wretched by one's own choice: a misfortune brought on oneself.

units.la: Sponte nascens] Voluntaria herba. Sponte naturæ proveniens, Plinius. Suæ spontis planta. Per se radicatus, Col. Ingenio arbusta nata, Næv. id est, sponte naturæ nata, Non. Ingenui fontes, Ausón. Nativus sal, color, Plin. Nativa coma, Ovid. Inaffectatum capillitium. Ingenio flexi crines, Apul.
units.tr: Sponte nascens] A voluntary herb. Growing of its own accord by nature's way, Plin. A plant of its own kind. Rooted by itself, Col. Trees born by their own nature, Naev. That is, born by nature's own accord, Non. Natural springs, Ausonius. Natural salt, natural colour, Plin. Native hair, Ovid. Unaffected head of hair. Curls naturally waved, Apul.

units.la: Sporta] Canistrum, Virg. (Caniter, Pallad.) Corbis Cophinus, Col. Urna spartea. Scirpea, vel sirpea, Cato. Qualus vimineus, Virgil. Qualus ad calcem ferendam, Vlp. Qualum, Cat. Fiscina ex viminibus, Varr. è virgis, Virg. Cista viminea solidè & spissè contexta, Col. Panarium, à pane.
units.tr: Basket] Basket, Virg. (basket, Pallad.) Basket, creel, Col. Esparto basket. Rush basket, Cato. Wicker basket, Virgil. Basket for carrying lime, Vlp. Basket, Cat. Wicker basket, Varr. of twigs, Virg. Wicker chest closely and densely woven, Col. Bread basket, from bread.

units.la: Sportula] Sportella, Cic. Canistellum, Paul. Fest. Calathus, Virg. Calathiscus, Catul.
units.tr: Small basket] Little basket, Cic. Small basket, Paul. Fest. Basket, Virg. Little basket, Catul.

units.la: Spuere] Spuere in frontem alicujus, Sen. Crebrò spuere. Sputare. Sputator sum. Conspuere, Consputare aliquem, Plaut. Inspuere alicui, & aliquem, Plaut. Adspuitur à nutrice infans, Plin. Adspergere sputò; purgamentis oris aliquem. Sen. Edere sputum, Celf.
units.tr: To spit] To spit in someone's face, Sen. To spit often. To spit. I am a spitter. To spit upon someone, Plaut. To spit upon someone or at someone, Plaut. The infant is spat upon by the nurse, Plin. To sprinkle someone with spittle, with the refuse of the mouth, Sen. To bring up phlegm, Celf.

units.la: Spumare] Spumescere, Ovid. Adæstuat amnis, Stat. Spumas agere, Lucr. Bullare, Cat. Exspumare, Celf. Despumare, Sen.
units.tr: To foam] To become foamy, Ovid. The river seethes, Stat. To produce foam, Lucr. To bubble, Cat. To foam out, Celf. To skim off the foam, Sen.

units.la: Spumatio] Spumatus, ûs, Stat.
units.tr: Foaming] Foam, Stat.

units.la: Spumeus] Spumatus, Cic. Spumans. Spumosus, Virg. Spumifer, Stat. Spumiger, Ovid.
units.tr: Foamy] Foamed, Cic. Foaming. Frothy, Virg. Foam-bearing, Stat. Foam-bearing, Ovid.

units.la: Spurcare, v. Contaminare, Inquinare. Spurcè &c. vide Obscænè &c.
units.tr: To defile, see To contaminate, To pollute. Defiled, etc., see Obscenely, etc.

units.la: Spurius] Nothus, Quint. Varius, Lampr. Incertus, Virg. Malè conceptus infans, Ovid. Fraterculus gigantis, Juv. Insititium animal, ut mulus, Var. E furto genitus, Sili. Ex patribus conventitiis infans, Plaut. Cœli & terræ filius, Vatl. Illegitimus. I C. R. Filius vitio, Scal. Ex illuillustri familia originem, natione, non lege ducebat, Lipf. Ne Patris quidem sui nomen dicere posset. Adag.
units.tr: Bastard] Illegitimate, Quint. Of mixed origin, Lampr. Uncertain, Virg. A child badly conceived, Ovid. Brother of a giant, Juv. A hybrid animal, like a mule, Var. Born of theft, Sil. A child of irregular parents, Plaut. Son of heaven and earth, Vatl. Illegitimate, I C. R. Son by defect, Scal. He derived his origin from that illustrious family by birth, not by law, Lipf. He could not even name his own father. Adag.

units.la: Sputum] Sputisma, Vitr. Oris excrementum, Tac. Oris purgamenta, Sen. Excreatio cruenta, Plin. Gravedo, Plaut.
units.tr: Spittle] Spittle, Vitr. Excrement of the mouth, Tac. Purgings of the mouth, Sen. Bloody expectoration, Plin. Catarrh, Plaut.

units.la: Squalens] Squalidus, Catul. Arma squalent situ ac rubigine, Quint. Squaloris & pœdoris plenus, Cic. Squalore obsitus, Liv.
units.tr: Squalid] Filthy, Catul. Arms grow squalid with rust and mould, Quint. Full of filth and foulness, Cic. Covered in squalor, Liv.

units.la: Squalere] Squalore obsitus sum, ex Liv. Pœdore obsitus, Sen. Redolere situm, fœtorem
units.tr: To be squalid] I am covered in squalor, from Liv. Covered in foulness, Sen. To smell of mould and stench.

units.la: Squalor] Squales, Varr. Strigmentum, Celf. Illuvies, Ter. Pœdor, Lucr. Subluvies, Col.
units.tr: Squalor] Filth, Varr. Dirt-deposit, Celf. Filth, Ter. Foulness, Lucr. Dirt, Col.

units.la: Squama] Squamula, Celf.
units.tr: Scale] A small scale, Celf.

units.la: Squameus] Squamosus, Cic. Squamiger, Plin.
units.tr: Scaly] Scaly, Cic. Scale-bearing, Plin.

units.la: Stabilire] Duobus clavis figere. Trabali clavo figere. vide, Firmare.
units.tr: To make firm] To fix with two nails. To fix with a beam-nail. See Firm.

units.la: Stabilis] Ratus. Constat sibi, Cic. Solidus, Plautus. vid. Constans, Firmus.
units.tr: Stable] Fixed. Consistent with himself, Cic. Solid, Plautus. See Constant, Firm.

units.la: Stabilitas] Stabilitas dentium, Plin. Robur herbæ, arboris, Ovid. corporis, Livius. Tenacitas unguium, Cicero.
units.tr: Stability] Firmness of teeth, Plin. Strength of a herb or tree, Ovid. Of the body, Livy. Tenacity of nails, Cicero.

units.la: Stabulum] Stabularium, Col. Catabulum, (clausura animalium) Meurf. Caula, Virg. Bubile, Col. Mandra, Sipont. Præsepes bubus æstivas &c. Cat.
units.tr: Stable] Stableman, Col. Pen (an enclosure for animals), Meurs. Fold, Virg. Cowshed, Col. Sheepfold, Sipont. Mangers for oxen in summer, etc., Cat.

units.la: Stagnum] Lacus, Isid. Velabrum, Var.
units.tr: Pool] Lake, Isid. Velabrum, Var.

units.la: Stare] Hi stant ambo, non sedent. Rectus assisto, Cic. Insistere vestigiis, Plin.
units.tr: To stand] These two both stand, they do not sit. To stand upright, Cic. To step upon footprints, Plin.

units.la: Stare, id est, non moveri] Parietes urbis stant & manent, Cic. Stare in gradu, Sen. Tenere se loco. Tenet locum miles, Liv. Hærere, Cic. Quiescunt æquora, Virg.
units.tr: To stand, that is, not to be moved] The walls of the city stand and remain, Cic. To stand on a step, Sen. To hold one's place. The soldier holds the place, Liv. To cling, Cic. The seas are at rest, Virg.

units.la: Statim] Confestim, continuò, illico, actutum, repente, derepente, è vestigio, abjecta cunctatione. Simul cum aliquo. Pariter cum vita. Protinus, Subitò. Eodem loci & temporis vestigio. Sine mora, Sine ullâ mora. Nullam moram interposuisti, quin quàm primum, &c. Jam inde à principio, Cic. Nunc jam, Ter. Jamjam faciam. Numerò, Plaut. Rectâ, Dictum & factum, Ter. Cum dicto, Ap. Ex continenti, Iustin. In continenti, Vlp. Continenti, Amm. Nullâ morâ interposita. Mox. Repentè è vestigio. Jam jamque esse moriendum, cogitandum est, Cic. Intra punctum temporis. Stans pede in uno dictabat versus ducentos, Hor. Atque, Plaut. Exin. Virg.
units.tr: Immediately] At once, continually, straightway, forthwith, suddenly, all at once, without hesitation. Together with someone. Alongside life. Straight away, suddenly. On the same spot and at the same time. Without delay, without any delay at all. You interposed no delay but as soon as possible, etc. From the very beginning, Cic. Now already, Ter. I will do it at once. Instantly, Plaut. Right away. No sooner said than done, Ter. At the word, Ap. Without interval, Iustin. Straightway, Vlp. Immediately, Amm. With no delay interposed. Soon.
