At once, suddenly, on the spot. Now already, now at once one must die; one must think on it, Cic. Within a point of time. Standing on one foot he dictated two hundred verses, Hor. And, Plaut. Thereupon, Virg.

units.la: Statim-quum] Statim ut legeram scripsi. Ut me salutavit, statim, &c. Statim Catone absoluto, Cic. Statim quam: atque, Vlpian. Subito postquam; cum. Simul ut, atque. Simul ac primum potestas data est. Simul inflavit tubicen, Cic. Simul primum, Simul in potestate vestra erunt, Livius.
units.tr: As soon as] As soon as I had read, I wrote. As soon as he greeted me, at once, etc. Immediately after Cato had been acquitted, Cic. As soon as, as well as, Vlpian. Immediately after; when. At the same time as, as soon as. As soon as the first opportunity is given. As soon as the trumpeter blew, Cic. As soon as first, as soon as they are in your power, Livy.

units.la: Statim post] Sub eas literas; sub mentionem, Cic. Juxta hæc, Plin.
units.tr: Immediately after] Under those letters; under the mention, Cic. Next to these things, Plin.

units.la: Statim dare] Manu breviter tradere.
units.tr: To hand over immediately] To hand over briefly by hand.

units.la: Satio, locus] Stabulum, Plaut. Stabulatio, Gell. Stativa castra, Cic. Subsidium navigiis, Tac. Stativæ, Lamp.
units.tr: Place of standing] Stable, Plaut. Stabling, Gell. Stationary camp, Cic. Support for ships, Tac. Stationary, Lamp.

units.la: Statua] Signum è marmore, Ovid. Simulacrum, Cic. Opere statuario effigies, vid. Imago.
units.tr: Statue] Image of marble, Ovid. Likeness, Cic. A figure made by sculpted work, see Image.

units.la: Statuarius, vid. Cælator.
units.tr: Sculptor, see Engraver.

units.la: Statuere] Statuere modum rebus, locum, poenam, Cic. Constituere, Mart. Cernere, sancire, scisscere legem Destinare diem. Instituere heredem, Cic. vid. Definire.
units.tr: To establish] To set limits to things, a place, a penalty, Cic. To establish, Mart. To decree, sanction, enact a law. To fix a day. To appoint an heir, Cic. See Define.

units.la: Statura] Status statuæ, Cic. Spatium hominis â vestigio ad verticem, Plin. Corporatio & statura bovis. Corporatura. Incrementum, Col. Proceritas tironum, Veget.
units.tr: Stature] The bearing of a statue, Cic. The height of a man from sole to crown, Plin. The build and stature of an ox. Physique. Growth, Col. Height of recruits, Veget.

units.la: Status, vid. Pactus.
units.tr: Status, see Agreement.

units.la: Status, ûs] Conditio vitæ. Ordo Senatorius, equester, mercatorum, oratorum. Locus in quo quisque natus est. Fortuna in qua quisque nascendi initio constitutus est, institutum vitæ capere, Cic. Sors, Hor. Fastigium: civis ejusdem fastigii, Liv.
units.tr: Status] Condition of life. The rank of senators, of knights, of merchants, of orators. The place where someone was born. The fortune in which someone is placed at the beginning of birth; to take up a way of life, Cic. Lot, Hor. Summit: a citizen of the same rank, Liv.

units.la: Statum mutare, vid. Mutare.
units.tr: To change one's status, see Change.

units.la: Statu bono res sunt tuæ] In sudo sunt res tuæ. Res in vado, Ter. In portu navigare.
units.tr: Your affairs are in good condition] Your affairs are in a tight spot. Affairs in shallow water, Ter. To sail into harbour.

units.la: Stellæ] Cœli forma undique sideribus ornata. Astra, Luces, Ci. Ignes, Virg.
units.tr: Stars] The form of the sky adorned on every side with heavenly bodies. Stars, lights, Cic. Fires, Virg.

units.la: Stellæ fixæ] Sideta innumerabilia cœlo inhærentia, cum ipsius motu congruere certis infixa sedibus, quæ infixa sunt cœlo. Chorus astrorum fixis inter se distantiis radiantium, æqualique motu terras circumvolitantium.
units.tr: Fixed stars] Countless heavenly bodies clinging to the heavens, fixed in certain places, moving together with the motion of the heavens, which are fixed to the sky. A chorus of stars, shining at fixed distances from one another, circling the earth with equal motion.

units.la: Stellatum cælum] Stellans cœlum, Lucr. Sidereus polus, Val. Arg. Astrifera sphæra, Mart.
units.tr: Starry sky] Starry heaven, Lucr. Sidereal pole, Val. Arg. Star-bearing sphere, Mart.

units.la: Stercorare agrum] Cic. Lætificare agrum, Plin. Lætare arbores, Pallad. id est, lætamine excitare, Idem. Lætamine saturare prata. Agrum stercore saturare, satiare. Ingerere stercus vitibus. Pabulari oleas fimo, Col. Pingui fimo saturare solum, Virg.
units.tr: To manure a field] Cic. To enrich a field, Plin. To gladden trees, Pallad., that is, to stimulate with manure, Idem. To saturate meadows with dung. To saturate and sate a field with dung. To heap dung on vines. To feed olives with dung, Col. To saturate the soil with rich dung, Virg.

units.la: Stercoreus] Stercoraria porta, Fest. (Stercus, vid. Excrementum.)
units.tr: Dung-like] Dung gate, Fest. (For dung, see Excrement.)

units.la: Sterilescere] Exolescit ager. Nimiâ ubertate defatigari. Fatiscit solum segetibus. Fit sterilis, effœtum, Col. Effœtos agros, Virg. habet (id est, continuâ fertilitate lassos.) Exinanitur seges, Col. Defrugatur, ex Plin. Emaceratur terra satu millii. Evalescit arbor, Plin. Vanescit seges in herbam sterilem, Ovid.
units.tr: To become barren] The field grows exhausted. To be worn out by excessive fertility. The ground splits under its crops. It becomes barren and exhausted, Col. Exhausted fields, Virg. (that is, weary from continual fertility.) The crop is emptied, Col. Stripped, from Plin. The soil is wasted by sowing millet. The tree grows strong, Plin. The crop fades into barren grass, Ovid.

units.la: Sterilis] Ad sterilitatem damnatus.
units.tr: Barren] Condemned to barrenness.

units.la: Sterilis ager] Exsuctæ segetes, Var. Malignus ager, Non. Colles maligni, Virg. Vegrande frumentum, Fest. Messes quæ malæ creverunt, Ovid. Ager malus est, cum quo luctator Dominus. vid. Infecundus.
units.tr: Barren field] Exhausted crops, Var. Niggardly field, Non. Stingy hills, Virg. Very thin grain, Fest. Crops that have grown badly, Ovid. The field is bad when the master wrestles with it. See Unfruitful.

units.la: Sterilitas] Tenuitas frugum.
units.tr: Barrenness] Scantiness of crops.

units.la: Steriliter] Infecundè, Infecundò, Gell.
units.tr: Barrenly] Unfruitfully, Gell.

units.la: Sternere] Sternere lectulum pellibus. Substernuntaves nidos mollissimè, Cic. Adsternere, Ovid. Consternere cubilia, Col. Lectulus disternebatur, Apul. Pulvinorum excitare impressiones (vel compressiones) Arnob.
units.tr: To spread] To spread a little bed with skins. They spread softest nests, Cic. To spread upon, Ovid. To spread out couches, Col. The little bed was spread out, Apul. To rouse the impressions (or compressions) of cushions, Arnob.

units.la: Sternutare] Sternuere. Flatum è pectore exsurgentem cum capitis concussione emittere, Plin. Sternutamentis quati, Gell.
units.tr: To sneeze] To sneeze. To let out breath rising from the chest with a shaking of the head, Plin. To be shaken by sneezes, Gell.

units.la: Sternutatio] Adhibere ea, per quæ sternutamenta excitentur, Celf. Sternutatus, Iun.
units.tr: Sneezing] To apply those things by which sneezes are provoked, Celf. Sneezed, Iun.

units.la: Sterquilinium] Sterculinium, & sterculinum, scribit Ulp. Fimetum, Plin.
units.tr: Dunghill] Dunghill, and dung-heap; Ulp. writes it so. Dung-pit, Plin.

units.la: Stertens] Rhonchisonus, Pararrhencho, onis, vel Pararrhynthon, ontis, Fest. Pararrhinchus, Alcit. Qui naso stertit.
units.tr: Snoring] Snoring, Pararrhencho (gen. -onis), or Pararrhynthon (gen. -ontis), Fest. Pararrhinchus, Alcit. One who snores through the nose.

units.la: Stertere] Stertere naso, Perf. Rhonchiffare, Plaut. Profl are somnum pectore, Virg.
units.tr: To snore] To snore through the nose, Pers. To snore loudly, Plaut. To breathe out sleep from the chest, Virg.

units.la: Stertor, propr.] Rhonchus, Mart. Gutturis stridor, Amm.
units.tr: Snore, properly] A snore, Mart. A harsh rasping of the throat, Amm.

units.la: Stigma] Inscriptio frontis, Sen. Victurum in capite punctum, Veget. Nota publica. Cod.
units.tr: Brand] An inscription on the forehead, Sen. A mark to be borne on the head, Veget. A public mark, Cod.

units.la: Stigma alicui imponere] Stigma alicui inscribere, Sen. Inscribere aliquid in fronte, Cic. Ferrô genas altius sulcare, Amm.
units.tr: To brand someone] To inscribe a mark on someone, Sen. To inscribe something on the forehead, Cic. To furrow the cheeks deeply with iron, Amm.

units.la: Stigmaticus] Stigmatias, æ, Cic. Stigmosus, Plin. Literatus, Plaut. Literatus frontem, Apul. Samii literati, Aristoph. Deformatus stigmatum notis, Suet. Threjiciis compunctus notis, Cic. Subverbustus, Plaut. vel Subvervustus, Tertull. Inustus, Bud. Inscriptus, Lipf. Inscripti vultus.
units.tr: Branded] Branded, Cic. Marked, Plin. Lettered, Plaut. Lettered on the forehead, Apul. Samian lettered men, Aristoph. Disfigured with brand marks, Suet. Pricked with Thracian marks, Cic. Scourged, Plaut. or scourged to the bone, Tertull. Burned, Bud. Inscribed, Lipf. Inscribed faces.

units.la: Stillare] Stillat arbor guttis, vel guttas. Destillant aquæ, Tibull. Instillare oleum lumini, Cic. Stillam demittere. Guttam instillare. Guttatim fundere. Impluere in aliquem locum, Plin. Malum cùm impluit cæteros, non impluat mihi, Plaut. Stillæ decidunt in, Vitr. Casitant stillicidia, Paul. I. C.
units.tr: To drip] The tree drips with drops or drop by drop. Waters drip, Tibull. To drip oil into a lamp, Cic. To let fall a drip. To drip a drop. To pour out drop by drop. To rain upon a place, Plin. When the evil rains upon the others, let it not rain on me, Plaut. Drops fall into, Vitr. The eaves drip, Paul. I.C.

units.la: Stillatio] Stillatus, us, Ovid. Stillicidium, Destillatio, Plin. Stiricidium, cum stillæ concretæ cadunt, Fest.
units.tr: Dripping] A dripping, Ovid. Dripping, dropping, Plin. A dripping of rain, when drops that have congealed fall, Fest.

units.la: Stillatitius] Stillatus, Ovid. Stillatis guttans, Plin.
units.tr: Dripped] Dripped, Ovid. Dripping in drops, Plin.

units.la: Stimulare] Subjectis stimulis lassare, Hor. Fodicare, vel fodere latus alicujus, Id. Stimulis aliquem fodere, Cic. Stimulos adigere mancipio, Sen. Umbone pellere aliquem, Mart. Subditare stimulum, Lucr. Stimulos adhibere, adjicere, admovere, subdere, Ovid. Cic.
units.tr: To goad] To wear out with goads applied, Hor. To prod or dig into someone's side, Id. To goad someone with goads, Cic. To drive goads home, Sen. To drive someone off with the boss of a shield, Mart. To apply a goad underneath, Lucr. To apply, add, bring up, put under goads, Ovid. Cic.

units.la: Stimulatio] Stimulatus, Plin.
units.tr: Stimulation: stimulated, Plin.

units.la: Stimulator, vide. Incitator.
units.tr: Stimulator, see Incitator.

units.la: Stipare] Angustare, Sen. vid. Angustare.
units.tr: To crowd together: to narrow, Sen. see To narrow.

units.la: Stipendiarius] Tributarius alicujus, Justin. Vectigalis homo, Cic. Stipendiosus miles, veget.
units.tr: Stipendiary: a tributary of someone, Justin. a man liable to tax, Cic. a soldier on pay, Veget.

units.la: Stipendium] Vectigal, & Stipendiarium vectigal, &c. Pensitatio stipendii, I. C.
units.tr: Stipend: a tax, and a stipendiary tax, etc. A payment of a stipend, I. C.

units.la: Stipendium militare] Stipendium castrense, Plin. Jun. Martiaticum, Priscian. Manupretium castrensium laborum, Sen. Æs militare, Var. Attributum : pecunia militibus assignata nondum data. Pecunia attributa, Var. Castrense peculium, Pompon. I. e. Annona militaris, quæ stipendii loco datur, Veget.
units.tr: Military pay: camp pay, Plin. Jun. a soldier's allowance, Priscian. the wage for labour in camp, Sen. military money, Var. Attributum: money assigned to soldiers but not yet paid. Money assigned, Var. camp savings, Pompon. I. e. the military grain ration given in place of pay, Veget.

units.la: Stipulari] Stipulor te, & stipulor à te, Suet. Rogare aliquem, Plaut. vid. Pacisci.
units.tr: To stipulate: I stipulate with you, and I stipulate from you, Suet. to ask someone, Plaut. see To bargain.

units.la: Stipulatio] Stipulatus, Quint. Stipulatiuncula, Cic.
units.tr: Stipulation: a stipulated term, Quint. a little stipulation, Cic.

units.la: Stirpescere] Herbascere, Plin. Herbescere, Sipont. Obherbescere: herbam increscere, Fest. Silvescit vitis sarmentis, Cic. Obducit natura sentibus arva, Lucr. Stat sentibus ager, Lucr. Vastescit terra stirpium asperitate, Cic. Vastescunt agri, Acc.
units.tr: To grow into grass: to become grassy, Plin. to grow grassy, Sipont. to overgrow with grass: the grass increases, Fest. the vine grows leafy with its shoots, Cic. nature covers the fields with brambles, Lucr. the field stands thick with brambles, Lucr. the land becomes waste through the roughness of plants, Cic. the fields grow waste, Acc.

units.la: Stirpitus, vid. Radicitus.
units.tr: Stirpitus, see Radicitus.

units.la: Stirps] Animal loco affixum.
units.tr: Stirps: an animal fixed in one place.

units.la: Stiva] Capulum aratri, quod manibus tenet arator, Henric. Steph. Aures aratri, Virg.
units.tr: Stiva: the handle of a plough, which the ploughman holds in his hands, Henric. Steph. the ears of a plough, Virg.

units.la: Stolide] Fatuè, Quint. Stultè, Plaut. Insipienter, insulsè, incallidè, Cic. Quid dici potest obtusius? Id.
units.tr: Stolidly: foolishly, Quint. stupidly, Plaut. without wisdom, dully, unskilfully, Cic. What could be said more dull? Id.

units.la: Stoliditas] Stultitia, fatuitas, inscitia, insulsitas, infantia, stupor, Cicer. Desipientia, Lucret. Insipientia, socordia, Plautus.
units.tr: Stolidity: stupidity, foolishness, ignorance, dullness, childishness, stupor, Cic. folly, Lucr. lack of wisdom, carelessness, Plaut.

units.la: Stolidus] Stipes, asinus, Ter. Truncus, vero ex Apul. Verveceum caput, Plaut. Stolo, Ausón. Ovis aurea, Suet. Arietina mens. Vacerra, Fest. Cucullus, Plaut. Sannas, Cæl. Rhod. Delirus, fatuus, stultus, excors, vecors, Cicer. Infrunitus, Sen. Captus corde, Plaut. Perfatuus, jocus, catul. Corpus sine pectore. Coroebo stultior. Adeò nullum habet judicium, ut careat etiam sensu communi, Eraf. Plura. vid. Stupidus.
units.tr: Stolid: a stump, an ass, Ter. a trunk; but from Apul. a sheep's head, Plaut. a shoot, Ausón. a golden sheep, Suet. a ram's mind. A fool, Fest. a hood, Plaut. a dolt, Cael. Rhod. crazy, foolish, stupid, senseless, witless, Cic. mindless, Sen. out of one's wits, Plaut. utterly foolish, a jest, Catul. a body without a heart. Stupider than Coroebus. He has so little judgement that he lacks even common sense, Erasm. more. See Stupid.

units.la: Stolidi nihil curant] In nihil sapiendo jucundissima vita.
units.tr: Stolid people care for nothing: a most pleasant life in knowing nothing.

units.la: Stolidum esse] Abest à bonâ mente, Sen. Cor illi abest, Mart. Nihil planè sapere, Cic. Quæ dicta sunt in stultum, caudex, stipes, asinus, plumbeus, in illum nihil potest (f. convenire), nam superat ejus stultitia hæc omnia, Ter. Quicunque sunt, fuêre, futurique sunt posthac stulti, stolidi, fatui, fungi, bardi; solus ego omnes longè anteeo stultitiâ, Plaut. Si quando fatuô delectari volo, non longè mihi quærendus est, me video, Sen. Navigat Anticyras.
units.tr: Being stolid: to be far from good sense, Sen. he has no heart, Mart. to know nothing at all, Cic. What is said of a fool (blockhead, stump, ass, leaden) does not suit him, for his folly surpasses all these, Ter. Whoever they are, they have been, and will be, stupid, dull, foolish, fungi, bards; I alone far surpass them all in folly, Plaut. If ever I want to be amused by a fool, I need not look far; I see myself, Sen. He sails to Anticyra.

units.la: Stomachus, vid. Ventriculus.
units.tr: Stomach, see Ventriculus.

units.la: Storea] Teges canea, Col. Teges è scirpo, junco, palmâ, segetibus. Tegeticula. Segestre, & Segestria, pl. Var. Segestrum, Scal. Matta scirpea, Ovid.
units.tr: Storea: a reed mat, Col. a mat of rush, reed, palm, or stalks. A small mat. Segestre and Segestria, pl., Var. Segestrum, Scal. a rush mat, Ovid.

units.la: Strages, vid. Clades.
units.tr: Slaughter, see Disaster.

units.la: Stragulum] Stragula vestis. Stragulum textile in horto, Cic. Stragulum tori, Mart. Stragula, æ, Donat. Instratum, Vlp. Stratoria vestis, Paul. Pallium lecticulæ. Lodix, Juv. Accubitale, Vopisc. Cadurcum, Juv. Toral, Torale, & Toralium, Var. Non. Opertorium, Sen.
units.tr: Coverlet: a covering cloth. A woven covering in the garden, Cic. a couch cover, Mart. bed coverings, Donat. a spread, Ulp. a bedspread, Paul. a cloth for a couch. A rug, Juv. a couch cover, Vopisc. a Cahors rug, Juv. a bed-throw, a bedspread, and a bedcover, Var. Non. a coverlet, Sen.

units.la: Stramen] Stramentum, Plaut. Culmus, Virg.
units.tr: Straw: bedding straw, Plaut. a stalk, Virg.

units.la: Stramineus] Stramentitius, Var. (Stramentarius, ad straamen pertinens, Tac.)
units.tr: Of straw: made of straw, Var. (pertaining to straw, Tac.)

units.la: Strangulare] Suffocare, Lucr. Præfocare, Ovid. Effocare. Vi præclusis faucibus spiritum elisit, Sen. Premere fauces alicujus, faucibus aliquem, Cic. Interprimere, interstringere, fauces alicui, Plaut. Interstinguere aliquem oblisis faucibus. Oblidere fauces, Apul. Elidere fauces, Ovid. Offocare, Flor. Strangulat segetes nimia terræ lætitia, Quint. Strangulare semina, Col. Intercludere animam, Tac. Respiramen iterque animæ eripere, Ovid. Spiritum, vel animam elidere interclusis spiraculis, spiramentis obturatis, ex Cels. Ovid.
units.tr: To strangle: to suffocate, Lucr. to choke, Ovid. to stifle. With the passages of the throat shut by force, he crushed out the breath, Sen. to press the throat of someone, to throttle someone, Cic. to close the throat of someone, Plaut. to stop up the throat of someone, Apul. to squeeze the throat, Ovid. to choke, Flor. Excessive joy of the earth strangles the crops, Quint. to strangle seeds, Col. to cut off the breath, Tac. to snatch away the breath and the passage of life, Ovid. to crush out the breath or life by blocking the air passages, from Cels. Ovid.

units.la: Strangulatio] Strangulatus. Suffocatio, Plin. Præfocatio, Scribon.
units.tr: Strangulation: strangling. Suffocation, Plin. choking, Scribon.

units.la: Stratum] Stratum lecti molle, Lucr. Stratus, ûs, Gell. Substratus, Plin. Substrameu, Var. Torus plumeus, Ovid. Comminxit lectum potus, Mart. vid. Stragulum.
units.tr: Bed: a soft couch-bed, Lucr. a spread, Gell. an underlay, Plin. bedding, Var. a feather bed, Ovid. a drunkard fouled the bed, Mart. see Coverlet.

units.la: Strenuè] Arma capere strenuè. Actuosè agere. Caleres, Cic. Alacriter defendere, Plin. Gnaviter pugnatum, Liv. Naviter, Ter. Impigrè, Liv. vid. Alacris.
units.tr: Vigorously: to take up arms vigorously. To act energetically. To be hot with zeal, Cic. to defend eagerly, Plin. a vigorous fight, Liv. vigorously, Ter. briskly, Liv. see Lively.

units.la: Strenuitas, vid. Alacritas. Strenuus, vid. Alacer.
units.tr: Vigour, see Liveliness. Vigorous, see Lively.

units.la: Strepere] Strepitare. Interstrepere, Virg. Edere strepitum, Col. Circumstrepere aliquem, Sen.
units.tr: To rustle: to make a noise. To rustle among, Virg. to make a din, Col. to make a din around someone, Sen.

units.la: Strepitus] Strepitus & admurmuratio concionis, Cic. Crepitus testarum, Juv. Commurmuratio, Gell. Mugitus nemorum, Plin. amnium, Virg. Susurrus, Id. Stridor aquilonis, Cic. Inconditus clamor, Plin. Jun. Murmur, Ovid. Fremor per ora cucurrit, Virg.
units.tr: Noise: the din and murmuring of an assembly, Cic. the crackle of potsherds, Juv. a murmuring together, Gell. the roaring of woods, Plin. of rivers, Virg. a whisper, Id. the whistling of the north wind, Cic. disorderly shouting, Plin. Jun. a murmur, Ovid. a roar ran through the mouths, Virg.

units.la: Striare] Imbricatim undatæ conchæ, Plin.
units.tr: To be channelled: shells with waves tiled like roof-tiles, Plin.

units.la: Strictus] Canaliculatus, Plin. Imbricatus, Vitr.
units.tr: Fluted: channelled, Plin. tiled like roof-tiles, Vitr.

units.la: Strictim, vid. Breviter. Arctè.
units.tr: Strictly, see Briefly. Closely.

units.la: Stridere] Valido stridore impulit fores, Val. Arg. Flagitium magnum fecêre fores, Plaut. Frendere dentibus, Idem.
units.tr: To creak: with a loud creak he pushed the doors, Val. Arg. the doors made a great scandal, Plaut. to grind the teeth, Idem.

units.la: Stridor] Argutatio lecti, Catul. Strepitus januæ, Hor. Crepitus fo-rium, Plaut. Sonus raucus cardinis, Propert. Querela foriū, Ovid. Dentium inter se arietatorum sonitus.
units.tr: Creaking: the creaking of a bed, Catul. the noise of a door, Hor. the rattle of doors, Plaut. the hoarse sound of a hinge, Propert. the complaint of doors, Ovid. the sound of teeth grinding against one another.

units.la: Stridulus] Stridulum plaustrum, Ovid. Stridens serra, Lucr. Crepax mola, Sen.
units.tr: Creaking: a creaking wagon, Ovid. a screeching saw, Lucr. a rattling mill, Sen.

units.la: Strigare, vid. Requiem dare.
units.tr: To strigare, see To give rest.

units.la: Strigosus] Strigosissimi corporis capra, Col. Junceus, Ter. Uvis aridior. Exsuctus, Scal. Passos senes, vocat Lucil. Apricos, Perf. Corpora sicciora cornu habetis, Catul. Lignea conjux, Id. i. Gracilis & exsucci corporis, Sen.
units.tr: Lean: a goat of very lean body, Col. slender as a rush, Ter. drier than a grape. Sucked dry, Scal. old men dried up, Lucil. sunburnt, Pers. you have bodies drier than horn, Catul. a wooden wife, Id. of slender and sucked-dry body, Sen.

units.la: Stringere, vid. Comprimere. Strophiolum, vid. Muccinium.
units.tr: To tighten, see To compress. Strophiolum, see Muccinium.

units.la: Structor, qui fercula disponit] Fercula struens, Col. Instructor convivii, Cic. TriclinIarcha, Fulv. Analectes, Sen. Diætarius, Vlp. vid. aliter Ædificator.
units.tr: One who arranges the dishes: arranging dishes, Col. the steward of a banquet, Cic. the master of the dining-room, Fulv. the analectes, Sen. the caterer, Ulp. see otherwise Builder.

units.la: Struere, &c. vid. Ædificare.
units.tr: To build, etc., see To build.

units.la: Strues] Struix malorum, Næv.
units.tr: Heap: a heap of evils, Naev.

units.la: Struma] Tumor gutturis, Celf. Intumescit guttur aquarum certarum vitio, Plin. Gutturis propendula struma, Philand.
units.tr: Scrofula: a swelling of the throat, Cels. the throat swells from a fault in certain waters, Plin. a dangling goitre of the throat, Philand.

units.la: Strumosus] Strumaticus, Firm. Gutturosus, Vlp. Gutture turgido, Vitruv. Glandulosa cervix suis, Col. Glandulosus sus, Gar.
units.tr: Scrofulous: scrofulous, Firm. goitred, Ulp. with a swollen throat, Vitr. a pig with a glandular neck, Col. a glandular pig, Gar.

units.la: Struthiocamelus] Struthocamelus, Plin. Struthio, abs. Hieron. Isidor. jun. Passer marinus. Pœna (punica) avis, Plin. Afra avis, Acron. Avis non avis, Aldromand.
units.tr: Ostrich-camel: struthocamelus, Plin. ostrich, simply, Jerome, Isidore the younger. a sea sparrow. The Punic bird, Plin. an African bird, Acron. a bird that is not a bird, Aldrovandi.

units.la: Studere] Studere literas, & literis. Dare operam studio juris. Versari in artibus ingenuis: in studio literarum. Addiscere aliquid. Incumbere in, ad studia. Referre se ad studia, Cic. Discere aliquid apud aliquem: de aliquo: Discere fidibus, Id. Litare Musis. Dare se literis, vel ad literas.
units.tr: To study: to study letters and in letters. To devote effort to the study of law. To engage in the liberal arts: in the study of letters. To learn something. To devote oneself to studies. To return to one's studies, Cic. to learn something from someone, or about someone. To learn to play the lyre, Id. to offer sacrifice to the Muses. To give oneself to letters.

units.la: Dare operam Præceptori. Irrigari sapientiæ rore. Quatere Demosthenis arma. Petron. p. vid. Discere.
units.tr: To attend a teacher. To be watered with the dew of wisdom. To shake the arms of Demosthenes, Petron. see To learn.

units.la: Studia literarum] Mansuetiores Musæ, &c. literæ, Cic. Studia literalia, Tac. vid. Artes liberales.
units.tr: Studies of letters: the gentler Muses, letters, etc., Cic. literary studies, Tac. see Liberal arts.

units.la: Studia debilitant] Fecit amor macrum.
units.tr: Studies weaken: love has made him thin.

units.la: Studia neglecta] Exolescentes literæ.
units.tr: Neglected studies: letters grown obsolete.

units.la: Studia relinquere Repudium mittere studiis.
units.tr: To abandon studies: to send a bill of divorce to one's studies.

units.la: Studia odisse] A potiori elegantiâ abhorrere, vid. Illiteratus.
units.tr: To hate studies: to shrink from the finer elegance, see Illiterate.

units.la: Studiô, vid. Consultò.
units.tr: Deliberately, see On purpose.

units.la: Studiosus] Studiosus literarum, doctrinarum, philosophiæ, pilæ, nobilitatis, Cic. Musarum alumnus. Addictus literis, Eras.
units.tr: Studious: a student of letters, of learning, of philosophy, of ball games, of nobility, Cic. a nursling of the Muses. Devoted to letters, Erasm.

units.la: Studiosus grandævus] Serus studiorum, Hor.
units.tr: Studious old man: late in his studies, Hor.

units.la: Studiosos decet candor] Apertæ Musarum januæ.
units.tr: Students should have candour: the doors of the Muses are open.

units.la: Stulte agere] Clave findere lignum, & securi fores aperire. Eras.
units.tr: To act foolishly: to split wood with a wedge and open doors with an axe. Erasm.

units.la: Stultitia se ipsam prodit] Stultitiam celare difficile est.
units.tr: Folly betrays itself: it is hard to hide folly.

units.la: Stultitia, vulgare malum] Nihil est tam vulgare malum, quàm nihil sapere.
units.tr: Folly, a common evil: nothing is so common an evil as to know nothing.

units.la: Stultus, vid. Stolidus.
units.tr: Fool, see Stolid.

units.la: Egone stultus?] Summe ego nihili?
units.tr: Am I a fool? Am I of no account at all?

units.la: Stultorum plena sunt omnia] Stultorum infinitus numerus.
units.tr: All is full of fools: the number of fools is endless.

units.la: Stupefacere] Obstupefecit illum pudor, Ter. Detinere aliquem stupidum, Cic. Dementare, Apul.
units.tr: To astound: shame astounded him, Ter. to hold someone in a stupor, Cic. to drive out of one's mind, Apul.

units.la: Stupefactus] Omnes stupidi timore, obmutuerunt, ad Heren. Intermortuus, Suet, vid. Attonitus. Rigens.
units.tr: Astounded: all were struck dumb with fear, ad Heren. half dead, Suet. see Astonished. stiff.

units.la: Stupere] Stupescere : Stupefieri. Obstupui & visus mihi sum captus esse, Cic. Adstupere divitiis, Sen. Obstupefieri: homines ad miratione obstupefacti. Obstupescere aliquâ re, & aliquam rem, Cic. Tacita mœstitia defixit animos omnium. Pavor, stupor admiratione rei tam atrocis defixit. Liv. (cum admiratione defixit, Id.)
units.tr: To be stunned: to be stupefied, to be made dull. I was stunned and seemed to myself to be seized, Cic. to be stunned by riches, Sen. to be astonished: men stunned with wonder. To be stunned by something, Cic. A silent sadness fixed the minds of all. Fear and stupor, fixed by admiration of so atrocious a thing, Liv. (with admiration it fixed, Id.)

units.la: Stupiditas, privatio sensûs] Stupor mentis, Cic.
units.tr: Stupidity, privation of sense: dullness of mind, Cic.

units.la: Stupidus, privatus sensu] Brutus, Hor. Obstupidus. Exsensus, Gell. Sensu & vitâ carens. A sensu mentis abstractus, Cic. Res surdæ & sensu carentes, Plin.
units.tr: Stupid, deprived of sense: brutish, Hor. dulled, Gell. lacking sense and life. Drawn away from the faculty of mind, Cic. deaf things and things lacking sense, Plin.

units.la: Stupidus, trop.] Bardus, Cic. Plumbeus, Ten. Inscitus, Blennus, Fungus. Album colorem ab atro non distinguit, Plaut. Truncus, Cic. Obesæ naris, Hor. Cerebrum in calcaneo habet. Caput vacuum cerebro. Cerebrum nutat. Glauco stupidior, Eras. Grylla stultior. Non pro sano loquitur. Titubat mente.
units.tr: Stupid, figuratively: boorish, Cic. leaden, Ten. ignorant, a dolt, a blockhead. He cannot tell white from black, Plaut. a stump, Cic. of flat nose, Hor. he has his brains in his heel. A head empty of brains. The brain nods. Stupider than Glaucus, Erasm. more foolish than a cricket. He does not speak sensibly. He staggers in mind.

units.la: Stupor] Torpor, Cic. Rigior nervorum, Celf. Torpedo, Sal.
units.tr: Stupor] Torpor, Cic. Stiffness of the sinews, Celf. Numbness, Sal.

units.la: Stuprare] Stuprata per vim Lucretia à Regis filio. Stuprum virgini inferre, afferre. Expugnare puellæ pudicitiam. Afferre, inferre vim matribusfamilias. Peccare in virgine, in muliere, Cic. In matrona, Hor. Eripere, Spoliare pudicitiam alienam. Mittere vim adhibitam ingenuis. Violare virginitatem alicujus, Cic. Constuprare. Expugnare decus muliebre. Vim facere corpori alicujus, Liv. Viciare filiam. Vitium addere pudicitiæ. Imminuere pudorem, pudicitiam. Facere stuprum cum aliqua. Incestare puellam, Pudicitiam alicui pellere, Plaut. Vitium offerre virgini, Ter. Ludificatus est virginem, Id. Corrumpere virginem. Violare cubile alicujus, Catul. Puellam. Tibul. Illudere mulieri, Tac. Devirginare puellam, Petron. Imminuere virginem, Apul. Nomen virginis deintegrare, Cæcil. Virgineum nomen adimere puellæ, Ovid. Comprimere puellam, Liv. Depravare pudorem fœminæ, Capitol. Delinquere in ancillam, Ovid.
units.tr: Stuprare] Lucretia ravished by force by the king's son. To bring defilement upon a virgin. To storm a girl's chastity. To inflict violence upon married women. To sin with a virgin, with a woman, Cic. With a matron, Hor. To snatch away and strip another's chastity. To send force applied to freeborn women. To violate someone's virginity, Cic. To defile thoroughly. To storm a woman's honour. To do violence to someone's body, Liv. To corrupt a daughter. To add a blemish to chastity. To diminish modesty and chastity. To commit defilement with a woman. To dishonour a girl. To drive chastity out of someone, Plaut. To offer a blemish to a virgin, Ter. He has mocked the virgin, Id. To corrupt a virgin. To violate someone's bed, Catul. A girl, Tibul. To trifle with a woman, Tac. To deflower a girl, Petron. To diminish a virgin, Apul. To impair a virgin's name, Cæcil. To take away a girl's maidenly name, Ovid. To ravish a girl, Liv. To pervert a woman's modesty, Capitol. To offend against a maidservant, Ovid.

units.la: Stuprator] Expugnator alienæ pudicitiæ, Cic. Constuprator, Liv. Stuprolus, Val. Max. Compressor, Plaut. Vitiator, Sen. Corruptor juvenis, Propert. Prædator corporis, Petron.
units.tr: Stuprator] A stormer of another's chastity, Cic. A defiler, Liv. A little seducer, Val. Max. A ravisher, Plaut. A corrupter, Sen. A corrupter of youths, Propert. A plunderer of bodies, Petron.

units.la: Stupratus] Prostrata pudicitiâ, Suet. Corrupta virgo. Passa nefas corpore, Ovid. Præflorata mulier, Apul. Impudicatus. Impudicus factus, Fest.
units.tr: Stupratus] With chastity overthrown, Suet. A corrupted maiden. One who has suffered an outrage upon her body, Ovid. A woman deflowered beforehand, Apul. Dishonoured. Made immodest, Fest.

units.la: Stuprum, in genere] Libido. Flagitium: noctis longitudo stupris & flagitiis conterebatur, Cic. Libitium: Abrisii conjuges ad libita Cæsarum, Tac. Nequitia, Propert. Nequam, Subst. Plaut. Probrum, Fest.
units.tr: Stuprum, in genere] Lust. Shameful conduct: the length of the night was spent in debauchery and disgraceful deeds, Cic. Wantonness: the wives of Abrisius at the pleasures of the Caesars, Tac. Wickedness, Propert. A wanton, as a noun, Plaut. Disgrace, Fest.

units.la: Stuprum in specie] Stuprum per vim oblatum, voluntaria morte luit Lucretia vis; afferre vim, Cic.
units.tr: Stuprum in specie] Lucretia atoned for the defilement offered by force with a voluntary death. To do violence, Cic.

units.la: Stylus dicendi modus] Phralis. Textum orationis tenue, Quint. Character. Genus dicendi, Cic. Contextus & structura orationis oratoriæ, Bud.
units.tr: Stylus dicendi modus] Phrasis [φράσις]. A fine texture of speech, Quint. Character: a kind of speaking, Cic. The weaving and structure of oratorical speech, Bud.

units.la: Stylum exercere] Cic. Operam dare stylo, Suet. Stylo limare & ornare orationem. Exercitatione & stylo formanda est oratio, Cic.
units.tr: Stylum exercere] Cic. To devote effort to writing, Suet. To polish and adorn a speech with style. Speech must be shaped by practice and style, Cic.

units.la: Suavitia corrigere] Admordere proprium nasum.
units.tr: Suavitia corrigere] To bite one's own nose.

units.la: Suadere] Suadere, orare usque adeò, donec perpulit, Ter. Persuadere aliquid alicui velle. Solicitare aliquem spe, pretio, ad aliquid faciendum. Inducere aliquem ut, &c. Cic. Suasor sum alicui, & auctor deditionis. Magnopere censeo desistas. Ducere aliquem in aliquam sententiam, Cic. Consuadere alicui aliquid, Plaut. Consiliari alicui, Hor. vid. Persuadere, Consulere.
units.tr: Suadere] To urge and beg until one has prevailed, Ter. To wish to persuade someone of something. To entice someone with hope or money to do something. To induce someone to, &c., Cic. I am an adviser to someone, and the author of surrender. I strongly advise you to desist. To lead someone into a certain opinion, Cic. To advise someone together about something, Plaut. To give counsel to someone, Hor. See Persuadere, Consulere.

units.la: Suasio] Suasus, Vlp. Suadela, Plaut. Suada, Cic. Persuasio. Inductus, Id. Illectatio sermonum, Gell.
units.tr: Suasio] Persuasion: Suasus, Vlp. Suadela, Plaut. Suada, Cic. Persuasion. Induced, Id. An enticing of conversation, Gell.

units.la: Suasor] Suasionis opifex, Amm. Suada, Bud. Persuasor, Sipont. Persuastrix, Plaut. Solicitator, Vlp. Impulsor. Flexanima oratio, Cic.
units.tr: Suasor] A craftsman of persuasion, Amm. A persuader, Bud. A persuader, Sipont. A woman persuader, Plaut. A tempter, Vlp. An instigator. A soul-bending speech, Cic.

units.la: Suasorius] Persuasoria assertatio, Suet. Delenifica & suada facundia, Symm. Flexanimus, Cic.
units.tr: Suasorius] A persuasive assertion, Suet. Soothing and persuasive eloquence, Symm. Soul-bending, Cic.

units.la: Suasu tuo feci] Tu auctor es mihi. Te auctore suscepi negotium. Tuo impulsu feci. Te impulsore feci. Tuo inductu, Cic. Te consultore, Tuo consilio, Abs te persuasus id feci. Tuo instinctu, Te flagitatore suscepi negotium, Eras.
units.tr: Suasu tuo feci] You are my authority. At your urging I took up the business. I did it at your impulse. I did it at your prompting. By your inducement, Cic. At your counsel, at your advice. Persuaded by you, I did it. At your instigation. I took up the business at your insistent urging, Eras.

units.la: Suaviari, &c. vid. Osculari, &c.
units.tr: Suaviari, &c. See Osculari, &c.

units.la: Suavis] Mellitus: melliti oculi, Catul. Melicus sonor, Lucr. Iucundè tangit sensus. Belle tangunt aures verba. Distinctus vario lepore, Id. Jucundum auditu. Jucunda ad audiendum verba. Perjucundæ literæ. Dulcissima epistola, Cic. Volentia plebi facere, Salust. Voluptabilis adventus, Plaut. Nectareus. Nectar spirat. Nectaris flos.
units.tr: Suavis] Honeyed: honeyed eyes, Catul. A melodious sound, Lucr. It touches the senses pleasantly. Words touch the ears agreeably. Marked by varied charm, Id. Pleasant to hear. Pleasant words to listen to. Very pleasant letters. A most sweet letter, Cic. Making things pleasing to the common people, Sall. A delightful arrival, Plaut. Nectarous. It breathes nectar. A flower of nectar.

units.la: Suavitas] Gratia, Lepor, Lepos dicendi, Illecebra, Venustas, Cic. Venus, Quint. Amabilitas, Suavitudo, Plaut. Amantia, Id. Lubentia & gratia conviviorum, Gell.
units.tr: Suavitas] Grace, charm, charm of speech, allurement, loveliness, Cic. Charm, Quint. Lovableness, sweetness, Plaut. Affection, Id. The pleasure and charm of feasts, Gell.

units.la: Suaviter] Suavè olens, suavè rubens, Virg. Gratè olens, Apul. Amabiliter ludit, Hor.
units.tr: Suaviter] Sweetly smelling, sweetly blushing, Virg. Pleasantly smelling, Apul. Plays charmingly, Hor.

units.la: Sub] Subter testudine : subter radices, Virg. Infra, Ter.
units.tr: Sub] Beneath the vault: beneath the roots, Virg. Below, Ter.

units.la: Sub cælo] Sub cœli tegmine. Sud dio, sub divo, Lucr. Cic. Sub Jove frigido, Hor. Extra ostium, Ter. Exterior sis, Plaut. In propatulo, Col. Subdialis inambulatio, Plin. Hypæthræ ambulationes, Vitr. Hypæthrum, Subst. Id. Aperta promptáque cœli, Lucr. Loca retecta, Plin. Xy-stum, Vitr.
units.tr: Sub cælo] Under the covering of heaven. In the open air, Lucr. Cic. Under the cold sky, Hor. Outside the door, Ter. Be outside, Plaut. In the open, Col. An open-air walk, Plin. Open-air walks, Vitr. An open-air space, as a noun, Id. Open and exposed to the sky, Lucr. Uncovered places, Plin. A xystus, Vitr.

units.la: Sub custodiâ meâ] In meis castris, præsidiis.
units.tr: Sub custodiâ meâ] In my camps, under my garrisons.

units.la: Subauscultare] Subauscultare pariete posito. Subauscul-tando excipere voces, & quid narrent attendere. Operam dare sermoni aliquorum. Aucupium facere auribus. Gustare alicujus sermonem, Plaut. (Sermonem alicujus ex occulto clepere, Pacuv.) Auscultare ad fores : ab ostio. Clam sublegere sermonem alicujus, Plaut. Admovere aurem, Ter.
units.tr: Subauscultare] To eavesdrop by a wall placed close by. To catch voices by eavesdropping and attend to what they are saying. To pay attention to the conversation of others. To lend one's ear to others' talk. To catch someone's conversation, Plaut. (To snatch someone's talk secretly, Pacuv.) To listen at the door, from the doorway. To pick up someone's talk secretly, Plaut. To lend an ear, Ter.

units.la: Subdere se alicui] Subjicere se, Submittere fasces. Succumbere, Cic. Subire deditionem, Cæs. Sub jugum abire, Liv. Ire, Lucan. Jugum subire, Plin. Dedere se hosti, Cæs. Dedere se in deditionem, Plaut. Jugum accipere, Liv. Tradere se in potestatem alterius, Cæs. in fidem ditionemque, Liv. vid. Dedere se.
units.tr: Subdere se alicui] To submit oneself, to lower the fasces. To yield, Cic. To undergo surrender, Cæs. To go under the yoke, Liv. To go, Lucan. To submit to the yoke, Plin. To surrender to the enemy, Cæs. To give oneself up in surrender, Plaut. To accept the yoke, Liv. To hand oneself over into another's power, Cæs. into trust and dominion, Liv. See Dedere se.

units.la: Subdialis, vid. Sub cælo.
units.tr: Subdialis, see Sub cælo.

units.la: Subditus] Subjectus servitio, Liv. Obnoxius alicui, Cic. Patiens, Sen. Mancipatus. Supplex vester est judices, Cic. Obnoxiosus, Plaut. Qui in ditione, imperio, potestate alterius est, Cic.
units.tr: Subditus] Subjected to servitude, Liv. Bound to someone, Cic. Submissive, Sen. Enslaved. Your suppliant, judges, Cic. Obnoxious, Plaut. One who is under the rule, command or power of another, Cic.

units.la: Subditi non nimis angariandi] Forpicibus binis tonderi.
units.tr: Subditi non nimis angariandi] To be plucked with two pairs of tongs.

units.la: Subdulcis, vid. Dulciculus.
units.tr: Subdulcis, see Dulciculus.

units.la: Subesse alicui] Non defugere auctoritatem.
units.tr: Subesse alicui] Not to shun authority.

units.la: Subesse aliquid oportet] Fama non temere spargitur. Non temere nasci fama solet, Cic. Non de nihilo est, quod Ter. Non temerarium est, Plaut. Non ex vano est. Non necquicquam ita appellant, Liv.
units.tr: Subesse aliquid oportet] Rumour is not spread without cause. Rumour does not commonly arise rashly, Cic. It is not from nothing, as Ter. says. It is not without reason, Plaut. It is not from nothing. They do not name it in vain, Liv.

units.la: Subfrigidus] Frigidulus, Catul. Frigidiusculus, Gell.
units.tr: Subfrigidus] Somewhat cold, Catul. Rather chilly, Gell.

units.la: Subjicere] Subterjácere, Pallad. Subjectare, Ovid. Subjicere sub regem, Var. Subjicere, securi cervices, Liv. Subdere ignem, Cato. Supponere, subjicere ova gallinis, Cic. Plin. Subditare, Lucr.
units.tr: Subjicere] To throw under, Pallad. To subject, Ovid. To place under a king, Var. To subject necks to the axe, Liv. To put fire under, Cato. To place under, to put eggs under hens, Cic. Plin. To put under secretly, Lucr.

units.la: Subire] Subire sub mœnia. Succedere ad muros, Liv. Subire muro, Virg. Suggredi, Tac. Sub jactum telorum venire. Subeo rectus, Liv. Subtus ambulare, Cat.
units.tr: Subire] To go under the walls. To approach the walls, Liv. To go under a wall, Virg. To attack, Tac. To come within the range of missiles. To go upright under a burden, Liv. To walk beneath, Cato.

units.la: Subitaneus] Subitus, Repentinus, Repens adventus hostium, Cic. Repens fama allata, Liv. Subitaria res est, Gell. Tumultuarius delectus, Liv. Extemporalis, Quint. Præceps. Præcipiti genere valetudinis abreptus, Sen.
units.tr: Subitaneus] Sudden. A sudden arrival of enemies, Cic. A sudden report brought, Liv. A sudden matter, Gell. A hastily levied force, Liv. Extemporary, Quint. Headlong. Seized by a headlong kind of illness, Sen.

units.la: Subitaneus terror] Panicus terror, casus, Sen.
units.tr: Subitaneus terror] Panic terror, a fall, Sen.

units.la: Subitâ occasione uti] Ere nata consilium capere.
units.tr: Subitâ occasione uti] To take counsel from an opportunity that has just arisen.

units.la: Subitò] Desubitò, Subitum est nimis. Repentinò, Plaut. Repente, Derepente, Ex tempore, Cic. Abruptè incipere, Quint.
units.tr: Subitò] Suddenly. Desubitò. Subitum est nimis. On the spur of the moment, Plaut. At once, all of a sudden, on the spot, Cic. To begin abruptly, Quint.

units.la: Subitò nihil fit] Nemo primo quoquo die fit doctus.
units.tr: Subitò nihil fit] No one becomes learned on the first day that comes along.

units.la: Subitò exaltatus] Homo novus, Salust. de Cic. Terræ filius. Casaub. Lumbricus, Plaut. Ab aliquo natus. A vobis natus sum Consularis. Repentinus homo. Nitedula ex repreculis, Cic.
units.tr: Subitò exaltatus] A new man, Sall. of Cic. A son of the earth, Casaub. A worm, Plaut. Born of someone. I am a consular who was born of you. An upstart man. A dormouse out of the rubbish, Cic.

units.la: Subjugare] Sub jugum mittere, Sen. Subjungere sub imperium armis. Subigere armis. Redigere in deditionem ac potestatem suam. Subjicere sibi populos, Cic. Accipere ad deditionem. Facere hostes stipendiarios, vectigales, Cæs. Redigere sub imperium, Id.
units.tr: Subjugare] To send under the yoke, Sen. To subject to dominion by arms. To subdue by arms. To bring into surrender and into one's power. To subject peoples to oneself, Cic. To accept into surrender. To make enemies tributary and subject to tribute, Cæs. To bring under dominion, Id.

units.la: Sublevare, vid. Attollere.
units.tr: Sublevare, see Attollere.

units.la: Subligaculum] Subligar, Mart. Suffibulum, Var. Perizoma, Isid. Campestre, Hor.
units.tr: Subligaculum] A loincloth, Mart. A cloth worn beneath, Var. A loincloth, Isid. Breeches for the field, Hor.

units.la: Sublimitas, vid. Altitudo:
units.tr: Sublimitas, see Altitudo.

units.la: Subluere, fluendo ripas attenuare] Subedit unda scopulum, Ovid. Torrens subterfluens, Plin. Lambit littora fluvius, Hor. Stringit ripas, Virg.
units.tr: Subluere, fluendo ripas attenuare] The wave undermines the rock, Ovid. A torrent flowing beneath, Plin. The river laps the shores, Hor. It grazes the banks, Virg.

units.la: Submergere] Mergere cymbam, Plin. Supprimere navem, Iustin. Obruere puppes ponto submersas, Virg. Submersum facere, Passerat. vid. Mergere.
units.tr: Submergere] To dip a boat, Plin. To sink a ship, Justin. Ships overwhelmed and sunk in the sea, Virg. To cause to sink, Passerat. See Mergere.

units.la: Submergi dignus] In mari balneandus.
units.tr: Submergi dignus] Fit to be bathed in the sea.

units.la: Subministrare] Subministrare frumentum, vires, Cæs. Col. pecuniam, Cic. Præbere sumptum, Suppeditare sumptus, Ter. Omnium rerum abundantiam. Suggerere copiam argumentorum, Cic. Submittit sol lumina rebus, Lucretius. Ministrare arma, vires. Sufficit tellus humorem: Vires Jupiter: salices sufficiunt umbram, Virg. Subjicere aliquid alicui, Propert.
units.tr: Subministrare] To supply grain and strength, Cæs. Col. money, Cic. To furnish expense, to supply costs, Ter. An abundance of all things. To supply a store of arguments, Cic. The sun lets its light down upon things, Lucretius. To furnish arms and strength. The earth supplies moisture, Jupiter supplies strength, the willows supply shade, Virg. To put something under someone, Propert.

units.la: Subornare aliquem] Subornare falsum testem: pecuniâ, Cic. Subornare ad solicitandum, Plaut. Submittere aliquem, ad aliquem, Cic. Immittere, Sallust. Instruere aliquem dolis, Virg. Mandatis, ad aliquid, Liv. Struere, Tac. Præstruere, Suet. Apponere alicui calumniatorem, accusatorem, &c. Cic.
units.tr: Subornare aliquem] To suborn a false witness with money, Cic. To suborn someone to solicit, Plaut. To send someone secretly to another, Cic. To send in, Sallust. To equip someone with tricks, Virg. To instruct someone with orders for something, Liv. To contrive, Tac. To prepare beforehand, Suet. To set a false accuser or prosecutor against someone, Cic.

units.la: Subscribere] Subsignare aliquid apud aliquem, Cic. Subnotare libellos, (scil. supplices) Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Subscribere] To sign under something before someone, Cic. To annotate petitions, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Subscriptio] Subsignatio, Paul. IC.
units.tr: Subscriptio] A countersigning, Paul. IC.

units.la: Subsidiari] Subsidio alicui venire, currere. Supplementum scribere legionibus. Mittere auxilia Impp. Cic. Submittere subsidia. Suppetias ire, mittere, venire, alicui, Cæs. Submittere alicui auxilia, Sil. Mittere globum subsidio, Id. Constabilire subsidiis legiones, Lucr. Decurrere suppetias (pro ad suppetias) suis fugientibus, Hirt.
units.tr: Subsidiari] To come or run to someone's aid. To write up a supplement for the legions. To send auxiliary forces, Cic. To send reinforcements. To send, go or come to someone's aid, Cæs. To send aid to someone, Sil. To send a ball as a reserve, Id. To station legions in reserve, Lucr. To run to the aid of their fleeing men, Hirt.

units.la: Subsidium militare] Supplementum, Cæs. Auxiliaris miles. Auxiliariæ cohortes, Cic. Auxiliaria manus, Volcat. Adminiculum, adjumentum militare. Subsidialis manus, acies, Amm. Auxilia, pl. Tacit. Suppetiæ, Cæs. Subsidiarius miles, Liv. Subitarii milites, Id. Ferentarius, Varr. (qui auxilium fert, Turneb.) Adcensi, Plaut. (ad censum legionum additi, Turneb.) Adscriptitii, Varr.
units.tr: Military reserve: reinforcement, Caes. An auxiliary soldier. Auxiliary cohorts, Cic. An auxiliary band, Volcat. Military aid or support. A reserve band or line, Amm. Auxiliary troops, pl. Tacit. Help, Caes. A reserve soldier, Liv. Hastily levied soldiers, Id. A light-armed skirmisher, Varr. (one who brings aid, Turneb.) Supernumeraries, Plaut. (added to the legion's census, Turneb.) Enrolled men, Varr.

units.la: Substituere in locum] Substituere in vicem aliquid: deficientibus & demortuis, Col. Substituere aliquid pro aliquo. Supponere vicarium: Substituere & supponere aliquem. Supplere legiones, exercitum. Subsortiri judicem. Surrogare, s. subrogare, Cic. Submittere sarmentum, prolem pecudi, &c. Novâ progenie repleatur numerus. In supplementum gregis reservare, Col. Succenturiare, Fest. Suggere aliquem alicui, Liv. Sufficere aliam ex alia prolem. Reficere sobolem, Virg.
units.tr: To substitute in place: to substitute something in turn: for those who fail and die, Col. To substitute something for someone. To appoint a deputy. To substitute and put someone in place. To fill up legions and the army. To choose a judge by lot as a substitute. To surrogate, or subrogate, Cic. To put in cuttings, offspring for livestock, etc. Let the number be filled up with new offspring. To keep back as a replacement for the flock, Col. To supply a reserve, Fest. To supply someone to someone, Liv. To replace offspring with offspring. To renew the progeny, Virg.

units.la: Subterraneus] Subterreus, Arnob. Subsolaneus, Fest. Crypticus, Sidon.
units.tr: Subterranean: underground, Arnob.; Subsolaneus, Fest.; hidden, Sidon.

units.la: Subtilis] Persubtilis, Tenera, attenuata oratio, Tenuis aër, Acutus homo, Acutulæ conclusiones. Pressus orator, tor, Cic. Nebulosum syrma, Fulgent. Consulatus Caninii· Argutus in sententiis, Cic. Non inarguta sententia, Vlp. Deducta vox, Pompon. Macrob. Nasum deductiorem habuit, Robert. Constant. Petulus, vel Petilus; petilis cruribus, Plaut. Scrupulosa multa in voluminibus, Plin. Iun. Ænigmata Sphingis dissolvit.
units.tr: Subtle: very subtle. A delicate, refined speech. A thin air. A keen man. Rather sharp arguments. A restrained orator, Cic. A cloudy train, Fulgent. The consulship of Caninius. Acute in thought, Cic. Not an unsubtle opinion, Vlp. A drawn-out voice, Pompon. Macrob. He had a more slender nose, Robert Constant. Petulus or Petilus; thin-legged, Plaut. Many scrupulous details in volumes, Plin. Iun. He solved the riddles of the Sphinx.

units.la: Subtile quid, sed inutile agere ] Milium terebrare. Milium torno sculpere.
units.tr: To do something subtle but useless: to bore through a millet grain. To carve a millet grain on the lathe.

units.la: Subtilitas ] Tenuitas animi. Exilitas in dicendo. Acumen. Argutiæ, Cicer. Argutiolæ, Gell. Scrupulositas & nimia subtilitas juris, Vlp. Parvitas vinculorum, Cic.
units.tr: Subtlety: slightness of mind. Meagreness in speaking. Acuteness. Subtleties, Cic. Little subtleties, Gell. Scrupulousness and excessive subtlety of law, Vlp. Smallness of bonds, Cic.

units.la: Subtiliter] Tenuiter, tenuius differere: attenuatè, presse, pressius dicere. Acutè respondere, peracutè, argutè, argutissimè, Cic. Tenerrimè, Plin. Scrupulosè, Col. Minutius & scrupulosius, Quint.
units.tr: Subtly: to discuss thinly, more thinly; to speak finely, closely, more closely. To answer acutely, very acutely, cleverly, most cleverly, Cic. Most delicately, Plin. Scrupulously, Col. More minutely and more scrupulously, Quint.

units.la: Subtus] Omnia quæ supra & subter sunt, Cic.
units.tr: Below: all things that are above and below, Cic.

units.la: Subulcus] Suarius, Plin. Porcarius, Firm. Porculator, Col. Scrofipascus, Plaut.
units.tr: Swineherd: swineherd, Plin.; pig-keeper, Firm.; pig-driver, Col.; sow-feeder, Plaut.

units.la: Subvolare ] Subvolare in cœlestem locum, Cicer. Pennis efferri. A pennis petere auxiliatum, Lucr. Ex humili sede sublima evolat, Acc. Sublime abire, Liv. Vid. Sursum.
units.tr: To fly up: to fly up into the heavenly place, Cic. To be borne aloft on wings. To seek help from wings, Lucr. From a low seat it flies up on high, Acc. To depart on high, Liv. See "Upward."

units.la: Suburbium] Suburbanum, Subst. Vlp. Suburbanitas, Cic. Continentia (pl.) urbis, Volcat.
units.tr: Suburb: suburban (as a noun), Ulp. Suburban character, Cic. The built-up areas adjoining the city, Volcat.

units.la: Succedere, in alterius locum surrogari ] Succedo vicarius alicujus muneri. Succedere alicui, & in locum alicujus, Cic. Succedere in alicujus vicem, Plin. Succedere in paternas opes, Liv. Subire in locum alicujus, in partes, Ovid. Consequi in Prætura aliquem, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: To succeed, to be substituted in another's place: I succeed someone as deputy in an office. To succeed someone, and to take someone's place, Cic. To succeed in someone's stead, Plin. To succeed to paternal wealth, Liv. To step into someone's place or role, Ovid. To follow someone in the praetorship, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Succedit bene ] It res : It bene res, Cicer. Provenit recte, Plaut. Cedit res voto, Ovid. Cedit victoria alicui, Virg. Bene tibi habent principia, Terent. Vid. Cedit bene.
units.tr: It goes well: things go well, Cic. It turns out rightly, Plaut. The thing goes according to wish, Ovid. Victory falls to someone, Virg. Your beginnings are going well, Ter. See "It goes well."

units.la: Non bene succedit] Cedit male, Ovid. Male processit, Ter. Male cadit, Cæs. Male vertit res. Nimis proventum est nequiter, Plaut. Equidem proveni nequiter multis modis, Id. Offendere : Offensum esset aliquid, Cic. Huncine solem tam nigrum surrexêre mihi ! Hor. Adversâ fortunâ uti. Vid. Evenit malè.
units.tr: It does not go well: it goes badly, Ovid. It went badly, Ter. It falls out badly, Caes. Things turn out badly. It has turned out too wretchedly, Plaut. Indeed I have fared wretchedly in many ways, Id. To stumble: something had gone amiss, Cic. "Has this sun risen so dark for me!" Hor. To suffer adverse fortune. See "It turns out badly."

units.la: Successio] Successio in locum alicujus. Consequentia. Consecutio voluptatis,Cic. Sequela morborum mors,Lact. Consequium, Apul.
units.tr: Succession: succession into someone's place. Consequence. The following of pleasure, Cic. Death is the sequel of diseases, Lact. Consequence, Apul.

units.la: Successivus] Succidaneus, i. succedaneus, Gell. Successorius,Vlp. Consectarius, Cic. Vid. Consequens.
units.tr: Successive: substitute, i.e. succedaneous, Gell. Successional, Ulp. Consequential, Cic. See "Consequent."

units.la: Successus bonus aut malus] Successum, Ovid. Queruntur semper de processibus suis, Sen. Fortuna secunda, prospera, florens, adversa. Felicitas, Prosperitas. Sors atrox, tr. jucunda. Eventus. Eventum. Casus. Incerti exitus pugnarum, Marsque communis,Cic. Mars varius, Quint. Proventus felicitatis, Val. Maxim. Sors pessima rerum, Ovid.
units.tr: Successful or unsuccessful outcome: outcome, Ovid. They always complain of their progress, Sen. Good, prosperous, flourishing or adverse fortune. Happiness, prosperity. A cruel or pleasant lot. Outcome, event. Chance. Uncertain outcomes of battles and common Mars, Cic. Fickle Mars, Quint. The yield of good fortune, Val. Max. The worst lot of things, Ovid.

units.la: Succisivus] Subsecivus : Subseciva quædam tempora incurrunt,quæ ego perire non patior, Cic. Subseciva temporum,Quint. Subsecundaria & subseciva tempora,Gell. Surreptitius, Plaut.
units.tr: Spare: spare, Cic.: certain spare times occur, which I do not allow to be wasted, Cic. Spare moments, Quint. Secondary and spare times, Gell. Stolen, furtive, Plaut.

units.la: Succrescere] Increscit hulcus, &c. Subnascuntur plumæ, Plaut. Supercrescit aliquid, Quint. Grandescere, Plin.
units.tr: To grow up: the sore grows, etc. Feathers sprout beneath, Plaut. Something grows over, Quint. To grow larger, Plin.

units.la: Succumbere] Succumbere oneri. Concidere sub onere, Liv. Opprimi onere, Cic. Concidere, procumbere pondere, Virg. Cedere ponderi, Quint. Dare manus. Porrigere herbam. Lampada tradere. Vid. Dedere, subdere se.
units.tr: To succumb: to sink under a burden. To collapse under the load, Liv. To be weighed down by the load, Cic. To fall and sink under the weight, Virg. To yield to the weight, Quint. To surrender. To hold out the grass. To hand over the lamp. See "To surrender, to submit oneself."

units.la: Succus, vid. Liquor.
units.tr: Juice: see "Liquid."

units.la: Sudare] Sudore manare, Cic. Fluit, manat sudor è, de corpore, Lucr. Ovid. Emittere sudorem, Plin. Elicere, evocare. Sudor oritur, effuditur, Cels. Exsudare,Col. Desudare, Stat. Desudascere, Plaut. Assudescere, Varr. Circumsudare,Plin. Consudare, consudascere, Col. Praesudare, Stat.
units.tr: To sweat: to drip with sweat, Cic. Sweat flows and drips from the body, Lucr., Ovid. To give off sweat, Plin. To draw out, to call forth. Sweat arises and pours forth, Cels. To exude, Col. To sweat out, Stat. To sweat out, Plaut. To begin to sweat, Varr. To sweat round about, Plin. To sweat together, Col. To sweat beforehand, Stat.

units.la: Sudatorium] Assa,pl. Laconicum, Cic. Sudatio,abs.Vitr. Sudatio assa, Cels. Caldarium, Vitr. Caldaria cella, Plin. Sudatoria cella, Sen. Tepidaria, & Frigidaria, Vouver. Balnearia,(pl. locus) Cic.
units.tr: Sweating-room: sweating-rooms, pl.; Laconicum, Cic. Sweating-room, Vitr. Dry sweating, Cels. Hot room, Vitr. Hot chamber, Plin. Sweating chamber, Sen. Warm and cold rooms, Vouver. Bathing-places, pl., Cic.

units.la: Sudes, vid. Palus.
units.tr: Stake: see "Stake."

units.la: Sudum, vid. Serenitas.
units.tr: Clear weather: see "Serenity."

units.la: Sufficere ] Sufficiunt vires, Liv. Sustinere onus possum, Cicer. Sum ferendo oneri, Liv. Sum validus sustinere pondus, Plin. Suppeditare labori, Plaut. Superesse laboribus, ex Col.
units.tr: To suffice: the strength suffices, Liv. I am able to bear the burden, Cic. I am equal to bearing the burden, Liv. I am strong enough to hold up the weight, Plin. To supply for the labour, Plaut. To survive the labours, from Col.

units.la: Sufficiens ] Satis vehemens ad, Ter. Vinum affatim habemus, (Adverb. pro Nom.) Apul. Si satis consilium quadam de re haberem, Cic. Satis tempus ad quaestum faciendum, Caj.
units.tr: Sufficient: vehement enough for, Ter. We have wine in plenty (adverb for noun), Apul. If I had sufficient counsel on a certain matter, Cic. Enough time for making a profit, Gaius.

units.la: Sufficienter ] Affatim edi, bibi, Liv. Affatim diximus, Plin. Plena manu laudes nostras ad astra sustulit. Luculenter Graece scio. Plene laudare, scribere, Cic. Plenissime facere, Plin. Jun. Solide scio, Plaut.
units.tr: Sufficiently: I ate and drank to my fill, Liv. We have said enough, Plin. With full hand he raised our praises to the stars. I know Greek thoroughly. To praise, to write fully, Cic. To do most fully, Plin. Iun. I know it thoroughly, Plaut.

units.la: Sufficit ] Suppetunt verba ; omnia : suppetit mihi satis, Cic. Suppetit mihi cibus, Plaut. Consilium, Liv. Non suppeditant mihi chartae ; omissis omnibus quibus nos suppeditamur, Cic. Nihil deest, Plaut. Non deest mihi lac, Virg.
units.tr: It suffices: words are abundant; everything: there is enough for me, Cic. Food is enough for me, Plaut. Counsel, Liv. The papers do not suffice for me; all the rest being omitted by which we are supplied, Cic. Nothing is lacking, Plaut. I have no lack of milk, Virg.

units.la: Suffigere] Suppingere, Plaut. Subcuneare postes trabibus, Vitr. Subcudere clavis aeneis, Lucil.
units.tr: To fasten: to fasten beneath, Plaut. To wedge posts under beams, Vitr. To hammer in beneath with bronze nails, Lucil.

units.la: Suffimentum ] Suffimen, Ovid. Suffitus, suffitio, Plin. Incensi odores, Cic. Thymiama, Id.
units.tr: Fumigation: fumigation, Ovid. Fumigation, Plin. Burnt odours, Cic. Incense, Id.

units.la: Suffire] Suffire cellam bonis odoribus, Col. Thus: odores incendere, Cicer. Thus adolere. Vaporare templum thure, Virg. Fumificare, Lamb. Suffumigare sulphure, Caf. Suffumigare apes, Col. Suffocate domum sulphure, Scal. ex Propert. (à focus, non à faux deriv.)
units.tr: To fumigate: to fumigate the store-room with good scents, Col. Incense: to burn scents, Cic. To burn incense. To fill the temple with incense smoke, Virg. To smoke, Lamb. To fumigate with sulphur, Caf. To smoke bees, Col. To smoke the house with sulphur, Scal. from Propert. (derived from focus, not from faux).

units.la: Sufflaminare] Sustinet currum agitator, Cic.
units.tr: To check: the charioteer holds back the chariot, Cic.

units.la: Suffocare, vid. Strangulare.
units.tr: To suffocate: see "To strangle."

units.la: Suffodere ] Agere cuniculos, Cic. Specus agere, Vitruv. Subruere moenia cuniculis, Liv.
units.tr: To undermine: to drive mines, Cic. To dig caves, Vitruv. To undermine walls with mines, Liv.

units.la: Suffossio, vid. Cuniculus.
units.tr: Undermining: see "Tunnel."

units.la: Suffragari alicui, suffragio suo declarare ]
units.tr: To support someone, to declare one's support by vote

units.la: Suffragari ad Consulatum. Ornare suffragio aliquem. Ferre suffragium de salute alicujus. Sententiam dicere : ferre sententiam de aliquo per tabellam, Cicer. Dicere pro sententia, Liv. Rogatione suâ honorem & imperium ad illum defert. Pedibus ire, Cicer. Calculum album adjicere errori alicujus, Plin. Jun. Manum porrigere, Cic.
units.tr: To canvass for the consulship. To honour someone with one's vote. To give one's vote on someone's safety. To pass judgement: to give a sentence on someone by ballot, Cicero. To speak in favour of a motion, Livy. By his proposal he confers honour and command upon him. To go on foot, Cicero. To add a white pebble to someone's mistake, Pliny the Younger. To stretch out a hand, Cicero.

units.la: Suffragatio] Sententiae dictio, Cic.
units.tr: Suffragatio: The delivery of an opinion, Cicero.

units.la: Suffragium] Sententia, Punctum, Cic. Omne tulit punctum, Hor. Calculus, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Suffragium: An opinion, a vote, a point, Cicero. He carried every point, Horace. A pebble, Pliny the Younger.

units.la: Suggerere ] Si meministi, subjice, Ter. Vid. Memorare, subministrare.
units.tr: Suggerere: If you remember, prompt me, Terence. See Memorare, subministrare.

units.la: Suggestus, vid. Cathedra.
units.tr: Suggestus: see Cathedra.

units.la: Sugere ] Trahunt agni maternum alimentum, Col. Bibere suctu, Plin. Exsugere mammas, Arnob. Fellare lac, Varr. Fellitare, Solin.
units.tr: Sugere: Lambs draw in their mother's nourishment, Columella. To drink by suction, Pliny. To suck out the breasts, Arnobius. To suckle milk, Varro. To suck at, Solinus.

units.la: Sui juris] Sui juris & municipii. Dominus juris sui retinendi, vel dimittendi. Dominus rerum suarum. Nemini mancipatus, Cic.
units.tr: Sui juris: Of one's own right, and of a free town. Master of retaining or giving up his right. Master of his own affairs. Bound to no one, Cicero.

units.la: Suis viribus] Sine adminiculo progredi, Quint. Per me nixus adscendi, Cic. Sua sponte pedibus ambulare, Plaut.
units.tr: Suis viribus: To advance without a prop, Quintilian. I climbed up by my own effort, Cicero. To walk on foot of one's own accord, Plautus.

units.la: Sulcare, vid. Lirare.
units.tr: See Lirare.

units.la: Sulcus] Sulcamen, Apul. Qua aratrum vomere lacunam striam fecit, sulcus vocatur, Varr.
units.tr: Sulcus: A furrowing, Apuleius. Where the plough's share has cut a striped trench in the ground, it is called a furrow, Varro.

units.la: Sulfur] Sulfur vivum & fossile, Iun.
units.tr: Sulfur: Living and fossil sulphur, Juvenal.

units.la: Sulfuratum] Sulfurata, pl. Plin. Sulfuratum ramentum, Mart. Inducta taeda sulfure, Ovid.
units.tr: Sulfuratum: Sulphured things, plural, Pliny. A sulphured shaving, Martial. A torch smeared with sulphur, Ovid.

units.la: Sumen] Ruma, Cat. Rumen, Plin. Rumis & Rumus, Varr. (Suminata caro, Arnob. quae est suminis.)
units.tr: Sumen: Paunch, Cato. Rumen, Pliny. Rumis and Rumus, Varro. (Suminata flesh, Arnobius, which is of the sow's udder.)

units.la: Summa rei] Summa summarum haec est, Sen. Summa rerum fastigia sequi, (summatim dicere) Cic. Summa orationis, causae, Id. Operis, Hor. Periocha. Caput literarum. Argumentum epistolae. Scena totius rei haec est, Cic. Substantia orationis, Quint. Lemma, Mart. Vid. Compendium.
units.tr: Summa rei: The sum of the whole matter is this, Seneca. To follow the heights of things (to speak summarily), Cicero. The summary of a speech or a cause, Cicero. Of a work, Horace. A periocha. The heading of a letter. The argument of an epistle. The stage of the whole affair is this, Cicero. The substance of a speech, Quintilian. A lemma, Martial. See Compendium.

units.la: Summam rei petere] Invadere in arcem causae.
units.tr: Summam rei petere: To storm the citadel of the cause.

units.la: Summare, barb.] Summam facere, conficere, subducere, Colligere omnia. Summatim narrare, describere, exponere, Cicer. Summatim attingere, Lucr. Decurtare per capita, Quint. Deflorare auctores, Cassiod. Recapitulare, Sipont.
units.tr: Summare, barbarous: To make up a sum, to complete, to reckon up, to collect everything. To narrate, describe or set out summarily, Cicero. To touch on summarily, Lucretius. To abridge under heads, Quintilian. To skim the authors, Cassiodorus. To recapitulate, Sipontinus.

units.la: Summum alicujus rei] Summa navium tabulatis augent, Tacit. Vertex arcis, Lucr. Arboris, Plin. Montis, coeli, Virg. Vertex, Abs. Ab imis unguibus ad verticem. Fastigium operis, Cic. Tecti, ædificii, Vitr. Caes. Culmen rerum, Plin. Hominis, Liv. Caput, arboris, Sen. Vid. Cacumen.
units.tr: Summum alicujus rei: The tops of the ships increase the height of the decks, Tacitus. The summit of a citadel, Lucretius. Of a tree, Pliny. Of a mountain, of heaven, Virgil. The peak, Abs. From the very soles to the crown of the head. The top of a work, Cicero. Of a roof or building, Vitruvius, Caesar. The summit of things, Pliny. Of a man, Livy. The head of a tree, Seneca. See Cacumen.

units.la: Sumere, vid. Accipere.
units.tr: Sumere: see Accipere.

units.la: Sumptus, vid. Impensa.
units.tr: Sumptus: see Impensa.

units.la: Sumptus facere in rem incertam] Ollam exornas.
units.tr: Sumptus facere in rem incertam: You adorn a pot.

units.la: Sumptus supra proventum] Vomere argenteo aratur, Aureo hamo piscari.
units.tr: Sumptus supra proventum: They plough with a silver share; they fish with a golden hook.

units.la: Sumptus faciat, qui quaerit lucrum] Hostimentum est operapro pecuniâ, Plaut. Lucernâ qui indiget, oleum affundat. Lucernas oleo ne defrauda.
units.tr: Sumptus faciat, qui quaerit lucrum: Labour for pay is a loss, Plautus. Whoever needs a lamp, let him pour in oil. Do not cheat the lamps of their oil.

units.la: Supellex] Supellectilis, in Rect. Serv. Utensilia, Col. Armamenta. Arma rustica, Plaut. Impedimenta bellica, Caes. Apparatus, Cic. Paratus, Tac.
units.tr: Supellex: Furniture, in Rect. Serv. Utensils, Columella. Tackle. Rustic tools, Plautus. Military baggage, Caesar. Equipment, Cicero. Gear, Tacitus.

units.la: Super] Supra hominem, Cic. Supera caput, Lucr.
units.tr: Super: Above man, Cicero. Above the head, Lucretius.

units.la: Superare, vid. Antecellere. Vincere.
units.tr: See Antecellere, Vincere.

units.la: Superat, vid. Superest.
units.tr: See Superest.

units.la: Superbè] Sublatè, insolenter, intoleranter, arroganter. Elatè dicere, Cic. Inflatiùs perscribere aliquid, Caes.
units.tr: Superbè: Haughtily, insolently, intolerantly, arrogantly. To speak haughtily, Cicero. To write something more inflatedly, Caesar.

units.la: Superbia ] Arrogantia, Insolentia, Spiritus, Animi, Supercilium Campanum. Contumacia responsi. Tumor, sublatio animi, Cic. Jactantia, Quint. Fastus, Plin. Flatus, Virg. Torrens ambitionis. Typhus, Arnob. Typhus philautiæ.
units.tr: Superbia: Arrogance, insolence, a high spirit, a Campanian haughtiness. Obstinacy in reply. Swelling, lifting up of the mind, Cicero. Boastfulness, Quintilian. Pride, Pliny. A blast, Virgil. The burning of ambition. Typhus, Arnobius. The typhus of self-love.

units.la: Superbia noxia] Paries tumescens ruinam minatur.
units.tr: Superbia noxia: A swelling wall threatens ruin.

units.la: Superbire ] Superbire formâ, gloriâ, &c. Claud. Plin. Sumere sibi spiritus & arrogantiam, Caes. Sufflari fastu, Amm. Inflari & efferri. Efferre se insolentius. Insolentiâ dominatùs animos efferre, extollere. Turgescere, Cic. Intumescere, Quint. Tumere successu, Plin. Sufflatus adeptâ repentina potestate, Amm. Tollere animos, Sallust. Sustolli, Caes. Ejus artis fiduciâ subnixus ambulat. Inflabat animos rumor, Cic. Inflatos esse vanâ spe, Liv. Attollere supercilium. Sustulit supercilium, Petron. Ferox sum formâ, Plaut. Comam erigere. Subnixus alis me infero. Tollere cristas, cornua.
units.tr: Superbire: To be proud of beauty, glory, etc., Claudian, Pliny. To take to oneself spirit and arrogance, Caesar. To be puffed up with pride, Ammianus. To be inflated and elated. To bear oneself more insolently. To lift up the mind with the insolence of power, to exalt. To swell, Cicero. To be puffed up, Quintilian. To swell with success, Pliny. Puffed up by sudden power obtained, Ammianus. To raise the spirits, Sallust. To be lifted up, Caesar. He walks about supported by confidence in that art. Rumour inflated their minds, Cicero. To be puffed up with empty hope, Livy. To raise the eyebrow. He raised his eyebrow, Petronius. I am proud of my beauty, Plautus. To raise the hair. Relying on my wings, I swoop down. To raise the crest, the horns.

units.la: Superbire ultra conditionem] Nido majores extendere pennas, Hor.
units.tr: Superbire ultra conditionem: To spread larger wings than the nest can hold, Horace.

units.la: Superbire desinere] Remittere spiritus. Comprimere animos. Sedare arrogantiam, Cic. Exuere arrogantiam, Tacit. Factum, Ovid.
units.tr: Superbire desinere: To relax one's spirits. To check one's mind. To calm arrogance, Cicero. To cast off arrogance, Tacitus. Done, Ovid.

units.la: Superbus] Arrogans, Insolens, Arrogantiæ plenus. Inflatusanimus. Elatus animo,Cic. Nimius animi,Liv. Tumidus homo, Hor. Superbificus, Sen. Sublatus, Cæf. Tumefactus vano nomine,Mart. Sufflatus scientiâ,genere, Varr. Fastosus, Mart. Fastuosus. Inflatus opinione, Cic. Ferox fortunis,Acc. Infrunitus,Sen. Circumspectans se tanquam pavo. Pavo pulchritudine se oblectat. In cœlum exspuit, Adag.
units.tr: Superbus: Arrogant, insolent, full of arrogance. Inflated in mind. Elated in mind, Cicero. Excessive in spirit, Livy. A puffed-up man, Horace. Overbearing, Seneca. Raised up, Caesar. Puffed up with an empty title, Martial. Puffed up with learning or birth, Varro. Haughty, Martial. Pompous. Inflated by opinion, Cicero. Fierce in his fortunes, Accius. Unbending, Seneca. Looking about himself like a peacock. The peacock delights in its beauty. He spits into heaven, Adagia.

units.la: Superbus alienis plumis] Graculus Æsopicus.
units.tr: Superbus alienis plumis: The Aesopian jackdaw.

units.la: Superenatare, vid. Emergere.
units.tr: See Emergere.

units.la: Superest] Superat aliquid alicui. Redundat aliquid de, ex aliquo, Cic. Superabundant aliqua,Vlp. Superfit,Col. Superfluit. Supervacat. Supra modum necessarium est aliquid, Gell.
units.tr: Superest: Something is left over to someone, or exceeds him. Something overflows from something, Cicero. Things superabound, Ulpian. It is left over, Columella. It overflows. It is superfluous. Something is more than is necessary, Gellius.

units.la: Superficialis] Superficiarius, Bud. Personata felicitas,Sen. Bracteata,Id. Extraria lux,Lucr. Inumbratus, Celf. IC.
units.tr: Superficialis: Superficial, Budaeus. Happiness merely put on, Seneca. Gilded, Seneca. Extraneous light, Lucretius. Shaded, Celsus, jurisconsult.

units.la: Superficialiter] Primoribus labris degustare. Extremis digitis attingere aliquid. Summis labris invitare,Hieron. A limine salutare. Gustare ut canis de Nilo. De plano cognoscere, IC. Vid. Negligenter.
units.tr: Superficialiter: To taste with the very lips. To touch something with the tips of the fingers. To invite with the upper lips, Jerome. To greet from the threshold. To taste like a dog drinking from the Nile. To know by a flat view, jurisconsult. See Negligenter.

units.la: Superficies] Tergum terræ, Lucr.
units.tr: Superficies: The back of the earth, Lucretius.

units.la: Superfluere] Supervacare, Gell. Superficere. Superabundare, Vlp. Pro supervacaneo ac inutili haberi, Liv. Inanem, supervacaneum esse. Supervacaneum est quicquid usum non habet, Cic. Vid. Superest.
units.tr: Superfluere: To be superfluous, Gellius. To overflow. To superabound, Ulpian. To be regarded as superfluous and useless, Livy. To be empty, superfluous. Whatever has no use is superfluous, Cicero. See Superest.

units.la: Superfluus] Superfluens,Seu. Nimius, supervacaneus,Cic. Supervacuus, Plin. Exsuperatorius mensis, Lamp. Superficiens aqua, Vlp. Vid. Abundans.
units.tr: Superfluus: Overflowing, Seneca. Excessive, superfluous, Cicero. Superfluous, Pliny. An exsuperatory month, Lampridius. Floating water, Ulpian. See Abundans.

units.la: Superflua resecare, utilibus retentis] Inane abscindere soldo (Hor. jubet.)
units.tr: Superflua resecare, utilibus retentis: To cut off the empty husk (as Horace bids).

units.la: Superflua agere] Currentem incitare. Ignes hortari ut caleant. Doctum docere. Memorem monere. Musas hortari ut canant. Crœsi pecuniæ teruncium addere. In mare aquam deferre, Noctuas Athenas. In Ægyptum fruges. Alcinoo poma dare. Arboribus folia. Coelo sidera addere. Lumen soli mutuare. Juxta fluvium puteum fodere. Mari aquas addere. Maria hortari ut effluant.
units.tr: Superflua agere: To urge on one who is already running. To bid fires grow hot. To teach the learned. To remind the mindful. To exhort the Muses to sing. To add a farthing to the money of Croesus. To carry water to the sea, owls to Athens, grain to Egypt. To give apples to Alcinous. Leaves to trees. Stars to heaven. To lend light to the sun. To dig a well beside a river. To add water to the sea. To urge the seas to flow out.

units.la: Superior] Superior loco, Cicer. Altior, Saturn. Vid. Altus.
units.tr: Superior: Higher in place, Cicero. Higher, Saturn. See Altus.

units.la: Superior, vid. Majores.
units.tr: See Majores.

units.la: Supernè, vid. Desuper.
units.tr: See Desuper.

units.la: Superponere ] Superimponere aliquid alicui rei, Plin. Insuperponere. Supergerere. Superjicere aliquid, Col.
units.tr: Superponere: To place one thing upon another, Pliny. To lay on top, to heap up, to throw over, Columella.

units.la: Superstes, vid. Reliquus. Vivus.
units.tr: See Reliquus, Vivus.

units.la: Superstitio ] Ficta religio, Cicer. Scrupea religio, Varr. Prave detorta opinio rusticorum, Col. Metus, Valer. Flac. Virg. Superstitiosa solicitudo, Cic.
units.tr: Superstitio: Feigned religion, Cicero. Scrupulous religion, Varro. A wrongly twisted opinion of country folk, Columella. Dread, Valerius Flaccus, Virgil. Superstitious anxiety, Cicero.

units.la: Superstitionibus fidem dare ] Superstitione anili obligari, conflictari, imbui, Cicer. Operari superstitionibus, Liv. Superstitio mentes omnium occupavit, oppressit, Cicer.
units.tr: Superstitionibus fidem dare: To be bound, entangled, steeped in old-wives' superstition, Cicero. To be busy with superstitions, Livy. Superstition has taken hold of, overwhelmed, the minds of all, Cicero.

units.la: Superstitiosus] Plenum superstitionis & anile aliquid. Superstitione imbutus. Superstitio mentem ejus occupavit, Cic. Religiosus, Ter. Stultae & miserè sumus omnes religiosæ. Scrupeus. Vid. Cod.
units.tr: Superstitiosus: Full of superstition and something old-womanish. Steeped in superstition. Superstition has taken possession of his mind, Cicero. Religious, Terence. We are all foolish, and wretchedly religious. Scrupulous. See Cod.

units.la: Supervacuus, vid. Superfluus.
units.tr: See Superfluus.

units.la: Supervenire ] Intervenire, Cic.
units.tr: Supervenire: To come in between, Cicero.

units.la: Supinus ] Supinatus, Quint. Supus, Lucil. Fest. Scal. Resupinus, Plin. Resupinatus, Vopisc.
units.tr: Supinus: Turned back, Quintilian. Supus, Lucilius, Festus, Scaliger. Resupinus, Pliny. Thrown back, Vopiscus.

units.la: Suppeditare, vid. Subministrare.
units.tr: See Subministrare.

units.la: Suppetiæ, vid. Auxilium.
units.tr: See Auxilium.

units.la: Supplicare Deo] Adorare superos prece, Ovid. Vid. Orare Deum.
units.tr: Supplicare Deo: To worship the gods above with prayer, Ovid. See Orare Deum.

units.la: Supplicare homini, supplicem fieri ] Orare multis & supplicibus verbis. Vobis supplex manus tendit patria. Veiter est supplex judices, Cic. Suppliciter orare, postulare, Liv. Vid. Procidere ad genua. Obsecrare.
units.tr: Supplicare homini, supplicem fieri: To beg with many humble words. Your country stretches out suppliant hands to you. Veiter is a suppliant before the judges, Cicero. To beseech, to petition humbly, Livy. See Procidere ad genua, Obsecrare.

units.la: Supplicatio] Libellus supplex, Mart. Libellus, Iuv.
units.tr: Supplicatio: A humble petition, Martial. A little book, Juvenal.

units.la: Supplicium mortis ] Ultima poena, Liv. Cruenta mors, Ovid. Novissima exempla meritus, Tacit.
units.tr: Supplicium mortis: The ultimate punishment, Livy. A bloody death, Ovid. Deserving the newest examples, Tacitus.

units.la: Supplodere pedem, Cic.] Tundere pede terram. Pulsare humum pedibus, Hor. Pede terram crebra ferit, Virg. Calcaneis strepitum movere, Scal. Pedes allidere ad terram, Hieron. Crepitum suscitare pede, Propert.
units.tr: Supplodere pedem, Cicero: To beat the earth with the foot. To strike the ground with the feet, Horace. He strikes the earth with frequent foot, Virgil. To make a clatter with the heels, Scaliger. To dash the feet against the ground, Jerome. To raise a clatter with the foot, Propertius.

units.la: Supplosio pedum] Pulsus pedum, Virg.
units.tr: Supplosio pedum: A stamping of feet, Virgil.

units.la: Supponere aliud quidpiam ] Supponere puerum, Terent. Subdere partum, Paul. IC. Subjicere falsum testimonium, Cic. Nomen alicujus,Vlp. Gallinis pullos adulterinos,Plin. Substituere alia pro aliis,Id.
units.tr: Supponere aliud quidpiam: To substitute a boy, Terence. To pass off a child, Paulus, jurisconsult. To suborn false testimony, Cicero. To put in someone's name, Ulpian. To put counterfeit chicks under hens, Pliny. To substitute one thing for another, Pliny.

units.la: Suppositio ] Subjectio testamentorum, Liv. Subjectus, Plin. Suffectio, Arnob.
units.tr: Suppositio: Substitution of wills, Livy. Substitution, Pliny. Substitution, Arnobius.

units.la: Suppositititus] Suppositus, Cic. Subditicius liber, Quint. Subditivus servus,Plaut. Subditus partus, judex,testamentum, IC.
units.tr: Suppositititus: Substituted, Cicero. A spurious book, Quintilian. A substituted slave, Plautus. A substituted child, judge, or will, jurisconsult.

units.la: Supprimere, vid. Opprimere.
units.tr: See Opprimere.

units.la: Suppurare ] Ulcerare, Cicer. Abscedere. Pus erumpit, fluit. Suppuratio oritur, Cels. Caput fecit apostema, vel abscessus, Plin.
units.tr: Suppurare: To ulcerate, Cicero. To form an abscess. Pus breaks out and flows. Suppuration arises, Celsus. The head formed an abscess, Pliny.

units.la: Suppuratio] Hulceratio, Cels. Exulceratio interaneorum, Plin.
units.tr: Suppuratio: Ulceration, Celsus. Ulceration of the bowels, Pliny.

units.la: Suprà ] Supera paulò antè dixi, Lucr. Superius, Sipont.
units.tr: Suprà: I said above a little while ago, Lucretius. Higher up, Sipontinus.

units.la: Supradictus, vid. Prefatus.
units.tr: Aforesaid, see Before-mentioned.

units.la: Supremum tempus] Suprema, pl. Amm. Extremus spiritus, Cic. Exodium vitæ, Varr.
units.tr: The last time: the final moments (plural), Amm. The last breath, Cic. The departure from life, Varr.

units.la: Surculus, vid. Planta. Talea.
units.tr: Sprig, see Shoot. Cutting.

units.la: Surdescere] Surdum fieri, Ter.
units.tr: To grow deaf: to become deaf, Ter.

units.la: Surdus ] Surdus veritatis, Col. Captus auribus. Sensu audiendi carens, Cicer. Auditu carens. Auditus illi negatus, Plin. Exsurdatus,Sen. Cervo demissis auribus surdior. Surdior turdo, Eras.
units.tr: Deaf: deaf to the truth, Col. Hard of hearing. Lacking the sense of hearing, Cicer. Lacking hearing. Hearing denied to him, Plin. Made deaf, Sen. Deafer than a stag with drooping ears. Deafer than a thrush, Eras.

units.la: Surgere ] Exsurgere à genibus, Plaut. Erigere se, Cicer. Consurgere. Assurgere, Id. Tollere se solio, Virg.
units.tr: To rise: to rise from one's knees, Plaut. To raise oneself up, Cicer. To rise together. To rise up (to someone), Id. To lift oneself from the throne, Virg.

units.la: Surrogare. vid. Substituere.
units.tr: To substitute in place of, see To substitute.

units.la: Sursum ferri] Sublime ferri, Cic. In sublime tendere, ferri, Plin. Sublime raptus,Tac. Sublimem abire, Liv. Sublimem rapere aliquem,Ter. Petere sublime, Plin.
