Supernè tendit non in terram, Id. Ad supera ferri. Sursum versus, Cic. Altum petere, Ovid. Sursum cursitare, Cic. In summum aliquid trahere, Col. Petessere auras, Lucr.
units.tr: To be carried upwards: to be carried aloft, Cic. To stretch or be borne on high, Plin. Carried on high, Tac. To depart on high, Liv. To snatch someone up on high, Ter. To seek the heights, Plin. It stretches upward, not down to the earth, Id. To be borne to the heights. Upward, Cic. To hasten upward, Ovid. To drag something to the top, Col. To seek the breezes, Lucr.

units.la: Suc] Porca, Cat. Porcetra, Gell. Porcus fœmina, Cic.
units.tr: Sow: a sow, Cat. A young sow, Gell. A female pig, Cic.

units.la: Suscipere negotium] Suscipere provinciam. Sustinere curam, causam alicujus. Recipere onus. Deposcere sibi partes, Cic. Sumere partes aliquas, Quint. Subire defensionem, Plin. Iun. Ire in opus alienum & operam polliceri. Condicere operam; Plaut. i. e. Suscipere opus, Bud. Supponere collum oneri, Ovid.
units.tr: To undertake a task: to take on a province. To bear the care or cause of someone. To receive a burden. To claim a part for oneself, Cic. To take on certain parts, Quint. To undertake a defence, Plin. Iun. To take up another's work and promise one's services. To undertake the labour, Plaut. To take up a task, Bud. To put one's neck to a burden, Ovid.

units.la: Suscitare, Vid. Excitare.
units.tr: To rouse, see To excite.

units.la: Suspectus] Suspectissimus, Vlp. Suspiciosus: suspiciosum aliquid facere. Affinis suspicionis. Cadit, convenit in eum, pertinet ad eum suspicio. Residet in eo suspicio. Venit, incidit in suspicionem. Cadens in suspicionem. Suspectus nomine negligentiæ. Suspectior, Cic. Invidiosum judicium, Id.
units.tr: Suspected: most suspected, Vlp. Suspicious: to do something suspicious. Of a related suspicion. The suspicion falls, attaches, or pertains to him. The suspicion rests on him. He comes under, falls into suspicion. Falling into suspicion. Suspected on account of negligence. More suspect, Cic. An unfavourable judgement, Id.

units.la: Suspendere aliquem] Suspendere infelici arbore, Cic. In furcas, Vlp. Suffigere cruci, Val. Max. Interstringere gulam, Plaut. Furca figere aliquem, Callistrat. Mandare alicui laqueum.
units.tr: To hang someone: to hang from an unlucky tree, Cic. On the gallows, Vlp. To fix to a cross, Val. Max. To choke someone by the throat, Plaut. To fix someone on a fork, Callistrat. To entrust a noose to someone.

units.la: Suspendere se] Suspendio vitam finire, Suet. Injuriæ remedium suspendio quærere, Cic. Pensilem se facere. Litteram longam ex se facere, Plaut. Laqueo nodatus à trabe sublimi triste pependit onus, Ovid. Ad restim illi res rediit, Ter. In laqueum collum inserenti subvenire, Cic.
units.tr: To hang oneself: to end one's life by hanging, Suet. To seek a remedy for an injury by hanging, Cic. To make oneself dangle. To make a long letter out of oneself, Plaut. Tied with a noose, he hung from a high beam, a sad burden, Ovid. The matter came down to the rope for him, Ter. To one putting his neck into the noose, to come to help, Cic.

units.la: Suspicari] Suspicari aliquid de aliquo. Habere suspicionem alicujus rei. Suspectus mihi est. Perculsus sum hac suspicione, Cic. Suspicere aliquem, Salust. Suspectare, Ter.
units.tr: To suspect: to suspect something about someone. To have a suspicion of something. He is suspect to me. I have been struck by this suspicion, Cic. To look up at someone, Salust. To suspect, Ter.

units.la: Suspicere cælum] Suspicere in cælum, Cic. Suspectare sidera, Mart. Intendere oculos in cælum, Non.
units.tr: To look up to heaven: to look up into heaven, Cic. To gaze at the stars, Mart. To direct one's eyes to heaven, Non.

units.la: Suspicio] Suspectio, Ter. Opinio. Varr. Cic.
units.tr: Suspicion: suspicion, Ter. Opinion, Varr. Cic.

units.la: Suspiciosus] Suspiciosus in suos, Cic. Suspicax, Tac. Suspicatrix, Varr.
units.tr: Suspicious: suspicious of one's own people, Cic. Distrustful, Tac. Suspicious (feminine), Varr.

units.la: Suspirare, vid. Ingemiscere.
units.tr: To sigh, see To groan.

units.la: Sustentare se] Cic. Sustentari aliquo cibo, Col. Colere vitam inopem, Ter. Trahere vitam quoquo modo, Plin. Tolerare vitam, Cic. Se, Cæs. Suo vivitare, in 12. Tab.
units.tr: To sustain oneself, Cic. To be sustained by some food, Col. To keep up a meagre life, Ter. To drag out life somehow, Plin. To endure life, Cic. Oneself, Caes. To live on one's own means, in the Twelve Tables.

units.la: Vix agitát, Ter. Salust. Sustentare se schola, Suet. Facere piraticam, Cic. Scrutariam, Apul. Scriptum, Gell. Alimenta arcu expedire, Tac. Tolerare vitam colo, Virg. Lacte, Col. Uti alicunde, Ter. Vivere pane, Plin. De lucro, Cic. Ex rapto, Ovid. Victitare sorbilo, Plaut.
units.tr: Scarcely gets by, Ter. Salust. To support oneself by teaching school, Suet. To make a living by piracy, Cic. By scavenging, Apul. By writing, Gell. To provide food by means of the bow, Tac. To make a living by tilling the soil, Virg. On milk, Col. To make use of something from somewhere, Ter. To live on bread, Plin. On profit, Cic. On plunder, Ovid. To live on sipped broth, Plaut.

units.la: Sustentare aliquem] Sustentare tenuitatem alicujus, Cic. Famem alicujus, Caes. Tueri aliquo legiones, Cic. Tolerare aliquem sua pecunia, Plin. Tolerare equitatum, Caes. Vid. Alere. Fulcire.
units.tr: To support someone: to support someone's poverty, Cic. To relieve someone's hunger, Caes. To maintain legions with something, Cic. To support someone with his own money, Plin. To maintain cavalry, Caes. See To nourish. To prop up.

units.la: Sustentatur quaelibet res suis] Ignis cineribus alitur suis.
units.tr: Everything is sustained by its own means: fire is fed by its own ashes.

units.la: Sustentatio] Nutricatio plantarum: nutricatus herbarum. Alimonium, Varr.
units.tr: Sustenance: the nourishing of plants; the nourishment of herbs. Nourishment, Varr.

units.la: Sustentator] Columna familiae.
units.tr: Sustainer: the pillar of the family.

units.la: Sustentaculum sit firmum] Fulcrum trabe debilius ne sit.
units.tr: Let the support be firm: let the prop not be weaker than the beam.

units.la: Sustinere aliquid] Sustinere Remp. cervicibus suis: Humeris Remp. negotium humeris, Cic. Sustinere pugnam, Liv. Sustentare aciem, Tac.
units.tr: To sustain something: to bear the commonwealth on one's neck; to bear the commonwealth on one's shoulders, to bear the business on one's shoulders, Cic. To sustain a battle, Liv. To hold up the battle line, Tac.

units.la: Susurrare] Mussare, Plaut. Mussitare, Liv. Garrire in aurem, Pers. Sussurare in aurem alicui aliquid, Plaut. Stillare in aurem. Juv. Tenui murmure dicere, Ovid. Insusurrare aliquid alicui: in aurem alicui, Cic.
units.tr: To whisper: to mutter, Plaut. To murmur, Liv. To chatter in the ear, Pers. To whisper something to someone in the ear, Plaut. To drip into the ear, Juv. To speak with a faint murmur, Ovid. To whisper something to someone: into someone's ear, Cic.

units.la: Susurrus] Susurrum, Ovid. Susurratio, Cic. Susurramen, Apul. Insusurratio, Jul. Capit. Strepitus: non strepitu sed clamore &c. Cic. Admurmuratio, Id.
units.tr: A whisper: a whispering, Ovid. A whispering, Cic. A whispering, Apul. A whispering in, Jul. Capit. A rustling or murmur: not with noise but with a shout, etc., Cic. A murmur of approval, Id.

units.la: Sutor] Calceolarius. Solearius, Plaut. Diabathrarius, Id. Crepidarius, Gell. Sutates (pl. i. sutores) Plaut. Dentibus antiquas solitus producere pelles, Mart. Calcearius, Lev.
units.tr: Cobbler: a shoemaker (calceolarius). A sandal-maker, Plaut. A slipper-maker, Id. A sandal-maker, Gell. Cobblers (plural sutores), Plaut. One accustomed to stretch old hides with his teeth, Mart. A shoemaker, Lev.

units.la: Sutorius] Sutrinus, Tac. Crepidarius cultellus, Gell.
units.tr: Of a cobbler: of a shoemaker, Tac. A cobbler's knife, Gell.

units.la: Sutrina] Sutrinae tabernae, Tac. Suterna, Apul. Taubm. (Sutrinum, ars ipsa est, Sen.)
units.tr: Cobbler's shop: cobblers' shops, Tac. A cobbler's workshop, Apul., Taubm. (Sutrinum is the craft itself, Sen.)

units.la: Sutura] Compages, Plin. Commissura, Iun.
units.tr: Seam: a joining together, Plin. A juncture, Iun.

units.la: Suus cuique mos] Quot capita, homines, tot sententiae. Quisque suo sensu abundat.
units.tr: Each has his own custom: as many heads, so many opinions. Each man abounds in his own sense.

units.la: Symbolae nihil adferre] Immonem venire.
units.tr: To bring no contribution: to come without paying one's share.

units.la: Symbolam dare] Conferre in medium argenteos in aliquid, quid, Suet. Conferre in commune. In partem impensæ venire. Contribuere pecuniam. Congerere, Cic. Intribuere, Plin.
units.tr: To give a contribution: to put coins together for something, Suet. To contribute to the common fund. To come in for a share of the expense. To contribute money. To pile together, Cic. To contribute, Plin.

units.la: Sympathia] Rerum distantium naturalis cognatio. Cognatio naturæ, & qs. concentus ac consensus. Convenientia & conjunctio naturæ, Cic. Consensus rerum occultus naturalis inter se: contagio, contages, Cæl. Rhod.
units.tr: Sympathy: the natural kinship of things that are apart. The kinship of nature, and so on: harmony and agreement. The agreement and conjunction of nature, Cic. A hidden natural agreement of things among themselves: contagion, Cael. Rhod.

units.la: Symphonia] Concordia vocum discors, Ovid. Vid. Melodia.
units.tr: Symphony: a discordant concord of voices, Ovid. See Melody.

units.la: T.
units.tr: T.

units.la: Tabellarius] Tabellio. Grammatophorus, Eras. Perlator litterarum. Vid. Cursor.
units.tr: Tabellarius] Tabellio. Grammatophorus, Eras. A carrier of letters. See Cursor.

units.la: Taberna] Institoria taberna. Tabernula, Suet. Umbra tonsoris, Hor. i. taberna, Lamb.
units.tr: Taberna] A shop for trade. A little shop, Suet. The barber's shade, Hor. i. a shop, Lamb.

units.la: Tabes] Tabitudo, Plin. Marcor. Phthisis. Malus habitus corporis, Cels. Consumptio sui, Cic. Mala nutritio, Gorr.
units.tr: Tabes] A wasting away, Plin. Decay. Consumption. A bad condition of the body, Cels. Self-consumption, Cic. Poor nourishment, Gorr.

units.la: Tabescere] Tabe laborare, consumi. Lentâ tabe liquitur, Ovid. Extabescit macie corpus, Cic. Contabescere luctu. Exarescere diuturnâ miseriâ, Cic. Macerari lentis ignibus, Hor.
units.tr: Tabescere] To suffer from a wasting sickness, to be consumed. It melts away with slow decay, Ovid. His body wastes away with leanness, Cic. To pine away with grief. To dry up through long misery, Cic. To be worn down by slow fires, Hor.

units.la: Tabidus] Ad tabitudinem redactus. Phthisicus. Atrophos, qui cibum non sentit, Plin.
units.tr: Tabidus] Reduced to a wasting condition. Consumptive. Atrophos [ἄτροφος], one who does not feel his food, Plin.

units.la: Tabula] Tabella, Cic.
units.tr: Tabula] A small tablet, Cic.

units.la: Tacere] Obticere, Ter. Silere, Cic. Favere ore, Virg. Ne mutire quidem audent, Sospp. Neque mu facere audent. Enn. Mussare, Lambin. Vid. Silere.
units.tr: Tacere] To keep silent, Ter. To be silent, Cic. To hold one's tongue, Virg. They do not even dare to mutter, Sospp. They do not dare to make a sound, Enn. To mutter, Lambin. See Silere.

units.la: Tace] Quod scis, nescias. Digito compesce labellum, Juv. Tacito opus est, Plaut. Quod bonum est, id tacitus tecum taceas, & gaudes, Id. Verbum cave faxis verbero. Id.
units.tr: Tace] Pretend not to know what you know. Press your lips shut with your finger, Juv. Silence is needed, Plaut. What is good, keep quiet about it to yourself, and rejoice, Id. Take care not to let slip a word that will bring a beating, Id.

units.la: Tacebo] Ne sol quidem sciet.
units.tr: Tacebo] Not even the sun will know it.

units.la: Tacendum prius loquturo] Loqui ignorabit, qui tacere nescit. Loqui nescit, & tacere non potest.
units.tr: Tacendum prius loquturo] He who does not know how to be silent will not know how to speak. He does not know how to speak, and cannot keep silent.

units.la: Tacitè] Tacito. Silentio ferre plagas. Tacitus assentitur. Tacendo loqui videbantur, Cic. Per silentium, Ter. Inaudicere. Vasis non conclamatis abire, Cæs. Silenter. SS. Tacitè Tacitè res geruntur optimè] Ante ferit, quam flamma micet. Altissima flumina tacito labuntur sono.
units.tr: Tacitè] Quietly. To bear blows in silence. He assents tacitly. They seemed to speak by keeping silent, Cic. In silence, Ter. To withdraw without the baggage being called together with shouts, Cæs. Silently. SS. Things are best done quietly, quietly. He strikes before the flame flashes. The deepest rivers glide with a silent sound.

units.la: Taciturnitas] Fide & taciturnitate opus est, Ter.
units.tr: Taciturnitas] Trust and silence are needed, Ter.

units.la: Taciturnitas utilis] Præstat pede quam lingua labi.
units.tr: Taciturnitas utilis] It is better to stumble with the foot than with the tongue.

units.la: Taciturnus] Taciturnulus, Apul. Taciturnissimus, Plaut. Mutum forum, Cic. Elinguis curia, Plin. Lingua huic excidit, ut ego opinor, Plaut. Areopagita taciturnior. Harpocratem reddit, Statua taciturnior.
units.tr: Taciturnus] Somewhat taciturn, Apul. Most taciturn, Plaut. A mute forum, Cic. A tongue-tied senate-house, Plin. Her tongue has fallen out, I think, Plaut. More taciturn than an Areopagite. He makes himself a Harpocrates; more silent than a statue.

units.la: Taciturnus esto] Alios quod silere vules, ipse primum sile.
units.tr: Taciturnus esto] If you wish others to be silent about something, be silent about it yourself first.

units.la: Tacitus] Tacitus cursus fluminis tacita vox, Ovid. Silens dies à ventis. Dies spiritus silentis, Col. Silens cœlum, Plin. Mitis, placatus, Virg.
units.tr: Tacitus] A silent course of a river, a silent voice, Ovid. A day silent from winds. A day of still air, Col. A silent sky, Plin. Gentle, calm, Virg.

units.la: Tacitus assessor] Muta persona.
units.tr: Tacitus assessor] A mute character.

units.la: Tactilis] Tractabilis. Sub tactum cadens, Cic.
units.tr: Tactilis] Tractable. Falling under the touch, Cic.

units.la: Tactus] Contactus, Col. Contrectatio. Tactio, Cic. Tractatus, Quint. Attrectatus, Cic. Attactus, Virg.
units.tr: Tactus] Contact, Col. Handling. Touching, Cic. Treatment, Quint. Touching, Cic. A touch, Virg.

units.la: Tæda, vid. Fax.
units.tr: Tæda, see Fax.

units.la: Tædet me] Tædet nos vitæ, Cic. Tædescit me, Min. Fel. Capit me tædium belli, Liv. Pertæsum est me, vel illum, alicujus rei, Cic. Pertæsus ignaviam suam, Suet. Pertædebat matrimonii, Gell. Pertædescit, Cat. Distædet aliquem domi, Plaut. Distædet cum hoc loqui, Ter. Percipit me odium agri &c. Odium me cepit alicujus rei, Id.
units.tr: Tædet me] It wearies me. We are weary of life, Cic. I grow weary, Min. Fel. Weariness of war seizes me, Liv. I am sick of a thing, or of him, Cic. Sick of his own cowardice, Suet. He was tired of marriage, Gell. He grows weary, Cat. One is tired of being at home, Plaut. I am weary of speaking with this man, Ter. Disgust for the countryside seizes me, etc. A hatred of something has taken hold of me, Id.

units.la: Tædiosus] Tædulus, Fest. Fastidiosus, Cic.
units.tr: Tædiosus] Wearisome, Fest. Fastidious, Cic.

units.la: Tædium] Fastidium alicujus rei, Cic. Odium, Ter.
units.tr: Tædium] Distaste for something, Cic. Hatred, Ter.

units.la: Cum tædio] Fastidiosè aliquid exspectare, Cic. Morosè, Id.
units.tr: Cum tædio] To await something with disdain, Cic. Peevishly, Id.

units.la: Talea] Talcola. Malleolus, Col. Virga malleolaris, Id. Surculus utrinque capitatus, Plin. Clava. Palladius. Clavola. Præsegmen, Varr. Plantarium. Semen, Virg. Viviradix, Col. Planta quæ cum radice terræ inseritur, Plin.
units.tr: Talea] A cutting. A cutting, Col. A layering shoot, Col. A twig with a bud at each end, Plin. A club. Palladius. A small club. A piece cut off in advance, Varr. A slip for planting. Seed, Virg. A living root, Col. A plant which is set in the earth with its root, Plin.

units.la: Talio] Vices, Hor. Vicem reddere, Mart. Æquilibritas, Gell.
units.tr: Talio] Requital, Hor. To return the favour, Mart. Equal balance, Gell.

units.la: Talionis pœna] Ab alio exspectes, alteri quod feceris. Non est lex justior ulla, quàm necis artifices arte perire suâ, Ovid.
units.tr: Talionis pœna] Expect from another what you have done to another. There is no more just law than that the makers of death should perish by their own craft, Ovid.

units.la: Talis] Ejusmodi. Hujus generis. Id genus. Is. De eodem genere, Cic. Hujus notæ, Col. Ad eam faciem est, Plaut. Sic oculos, sic illè manus, sic ora ferebat, Virg.
units.tr: Talis] Of such a kind. Of this sort. Of that kind. Such. Of the same kind, Cic. Of this mark, Col. He has that appearance, Plaut. Such were his eyes, such his hands, such the face he bore, Virg.

units.la: Talia talibus conveniunt] Dignum patellâ operculum. Similes habent labra lactucas.
units.tr: Talia talibus conveniunt] A lid fit for its pot. Like lettuces have like lips.

units.la: Taliter, vid. Ita.
units.tr: Taliter, see Ita.

units.la: Tam, vid. Adeo.
units.tr: Tam, see Adeo.

units.la: Tam-quàm] Æquè quam. Item quasi, Plaut. Item atque, Varr. Item ut, Id. Item quemadmodum. Item uti, Cic. Ita ut si, Ter. Taliter, qualiter, Nart. Sic quasi. Pariter suades, qualis es. Tam atque. Proinde ut, Plaut. Sic, quomodo. Ita quasi. Quâ, quâ, Cic.
units.tr: Tam-quàm] Equally as. Likewise as if, Plaut. Likewise as, Varr. Likewise as, Id. Likewise as, Cic. Just as if, Ter. In such a way, Nart. Thus, as if. You urge in the same way as you are. Just as, Plaut. Thus, as. So as if. Here and there, Cic.

units.la: Tamdiu donec] Tantisper quoad. Tamdiu quoad, Vlp. Tamdiu quàmdiu: tandiu dum. Tantisper dum. Usque eo dum, Cic. Usque dum. Usque adeo dum. Usque adeo donec, Ter. Usque eò donec. Ut adhuc locorum feci, Plaut. Hactenus. Adhuc. Eatenus, Cic. Ad id locorum (de tempore) Liv. Eousque, Col. Eò ad, dum. Apul. Etiam dum, Ter. Istactenus, Plaut.
units.tr: Tamdiu donec] For just so long as. For as long as, Ulp. For just so long as, while. For just so long as, Cic. Until. Right up until, Ter. Until, Cic. As I have done thus far in this place, Plaut. Thus far. Still. So far, Cic. To that point (of time), Liv. Up to that point, Col. To that point, until, Apul. Even while, Ter. Up to that point, Plaut.

units.la: Tamen] Attamen. Nihilominus. Nihilominus tamen, Cic. Secius. Verumtamen. Sed tamen, Id.
units.tr: Tamen] Yet. Nevertheless. Nevertheless yet, Cic. Otherwise, Secius. Yet, Verumtamen. Still, Id.

units.la: Tandem] Aliquando. Plaut. Demum. Jam verò. Ultimò. Denique, Cic.
units.tr: Tandem] At some time, Plaut. At last. Now indeed. Finally. Lastly, Cic.

units.la: Tandem verum est factum] Hoc jam & vates sciunt.
units.tr: Tandem verum est factum] At last it has come true: even the seers know this now.

units.la: Tangere] Attingere aliquem. Contingere, Cic. Tractare, Col. Attrectare, Cic. Contrectare, Col. Perstringere, Col.
units.tr: Tangere] To touch someone. To touch, Cic. To handle, Col. To handle, Cic. To handle, Col. To graze, Col.

units.la: Tanquam] Veluti, Hor. Quasi. Quasi si, Plaut. Quasi verò, Ter. Instar Deorum, Tac. Ad instar, ad Her. Perinde ac si, quasi. Ut si, Cic.
units.tr: Tanquam] As, Hor. As if. As if, Plaut. As though, Ter. Like gods, Tac. Like, ad Her. As if, as though. As if, Cic.

units.la: Tanti] Tantidem, Ter. Auro contra vendere, Plaut.
units.tr: Tanti] Of so much worth. Just as much, Ter. To sell in return for as much gold, Plaut.

units.la: Tantum, tam multum] Ne pilo quidem minus.
units.tr: Tantum, tam multum] Not a hair less.

units.la: Tantum modò] Tantummodo. Plaut. Tantum duntaxat. Duntaxat. Modò ut: ne: non modo, sed etiam. Solum. Solos menses novem, Cic. Triduum unum. Unos sex dies, Plaut. Solis tribus ictibus, Ter. Tenus: Verbo tenus, Cic. Intra verba peccare, Curt. Omnino: Quinque omnino fuerunt qui &c. Cic. (i. tantum, Bud.)
units.tr: Tantum modò] Only, merely. Only, Plaut. Only, merely. Only, provided that; not only ... but also. Alone. Only nine months, Cic. One period of three days. Only six days, Plaut. With only three blows, Ter. Only as far as: in words only, Cic. To sin only in words, Curt. In all: five in all there were who etc., Cic. (that is, only, Bud.)

units.la: Tardare] Posterare, Pallad. Serus, vel serissimus omnium sum, advenio, Plin. Serius venire, Acc. Serò allata epistola, Cic. Postvenire, Plin.
units.tr: Tardare] To delay. To be late, Pallad. I am the latest of all to arrive, Plin. To come later, Acc. A letter brought too late, Cic. To come after, Plin.

units.la: Tardè] Lente, Plin. Spisse, Cic. Pro spisso evenit, Plaut. (tardè) Spissius nascimur, quam morimur. Var. Morose, Plin. Morosissime, Suet. Gravate, Cic. Myrmicè incedere, Catul. Elephanti citius pariunt. Pulmo citius venerit, Plaut. Incedere passu anili, desíde, inerti, tardo, suspenso gradu.
units.tr: Tardè] Slowly, Plin. Densely, Cic. It turned out slowly, Plaut. We are born more slowly than we die, Var. Peevishly, Plin. Most peevishly, Suet. Reluctantly, Cic. To walk like an ant [μυρμηκιστί], Catul. Elephants give birth more quickly. A lung will come more quickly, Plaut. To walk with an old woman's step, idly, sluggishly, slowly, with a hesitant step.

units.la: Tarditas] Cunctatio, Cic. Mora. Lentitudo, Tac.
units.tr: Tarditas] Delay, hesitation, Cic. Delay. Slowness, Tac.

units.la: Tardus] Tardus pes, Ovid. Lentus. Spissus, Cic. Morosus, Plin. Tardior quam corbita in tranquillo mari. Cochleam tarditate vincit. Formicinum gradum movet. Testudineus gradus. Tandem si podagrosis esset pedibus, jam rediisse oportuit, Plaut. Pulmoneis pedibus est. Cum pedicis condidicisti hoc grassari gradu, Id. Testudine tardior, Eras. Asello tardior, Id. Vid. Impromptus.
units.tr: Tardus] A slow foot, Ovid. Slow, sluggish. Dense, sluggish, Cic. Peevish, Plin. Slower than a freighter on a calm sea. He outdoes a snail in slowness. He moves at an ant's pace. A tortoise's step. If he had gouty feet, he should have come back by now, Plaut. He has lungs for feet. Since you learned to stride at this pace with fetters, Id. Slower than a tortoise, Eras. Slower than an ass, Id. See Impromptus.

units.la: Tartarus, vid. Infernus.
units.tr: Tartarus, see Infernus.

units.la: Taurus] Maritus pecoris.
units.tr: Taurus] The husband of the herd.

units.la: Tautologia] Bis eadem repetere ridiculum. Occidit miseros crambe repetita magistros, Iuv.
units.tr: Tautologia] To repeat the same thing twice is ridiculous. Cabbage served up again has killed off the poor teachers, Iuv.

units.la: Taxare] Facere pretium rei, Plin. Statuere quanti sit aliquid, Cic. Censere bona, praedia, Id. Æstimationem facere, Cæs. Parvi pretii deputare operam alicujus, Ter. Habere æstimationem, Cic. Vid. Æstimare. Obloqui.
units.tr: Taxare] To set a price on a thing, Plin. To determine what something is worth, Cic. To assess goods and estates, Id. To make an estimate, Cæs. To reckon a man's services of little worth, Ter. To have an estimate, Cic. See Æstimare. Obloqui.

units.la: Quæ in aliis taxas, ipse fugias] Omnia quæ vindicas in alio, tibi ipsi vehementer fugienda sunt. Quod aliis vitio vertis, id tibi non ducas laudi.
units.tr: Quæ in aliis taxas, ipse fugias] Whatever you censure in others, shun yourself. Everything you claim against another ought to be strongly avoided by yourself. What you find fault with in others, do not count as praise for yourself.

units.la: Taxatio] Æstimatio, Cic. Censio, Fest.
units.tr: Taxatio] Assessment, valuation, Cic. Assessment, Fest.

units.la: Taxator] Æstimator. Censor, Cic.
units.tr: Taxator] An assessor, valuer. A censor, Cic.

units.la: Teckna, vid. Fraus.
units.tr: Teckna, see Fraus.

units.la: Tectorium opus] Tectorium, Abs. Plin. Tectura parietis, Pallad. Albarium opus: album opus. Lorica ex calce & arena. Corium ex tectorio parietibus inducere. Crusta. Nucleus ex testa tusa in pavimenta, Vitruv. Crustatio inducta, Philand.
units.tr: Tectorium opus] Plasterwork, Abs. Plin. Plastering of a wall, Pallad. White work: white work. A cuirass of lime and sand. To lay a skin of plaster on walls. A crust. A core of crushed tile for floors, Vitruv. A coating applied, Philand.

units.la: Tegere] Tegere involucris aliquid, Cic. Contegere, Plin. Integere, Stat. Obtegere, Cac. Protegere ab imbri, Plin. Occulere, Cic. Adoperire, Col. Operire. Convelare, Plin. Velare. Subtegere, Ovid.
units.tr: Tegere] To cover something with wrappings, Cic. To cover over, Plin. To cover, Stat. To cover up, Cac. To shelter from rain, Plin. To hide, Cic. To cover up, Col. To cover, Plin. To veil, Plin. To cover from beneath, Ovid.

units.la: Teges, vid. Storea.
units.tr: Teges, see Storea.

units.la: Tegumentum] Integumentum tecti. Tegmen, Cic. Tegimen, Liv. Tegillum, Varr. Operimentum, Cat. Opertorium, Sen. Opertura, Amm. Opertus, Apul. Cooperimentum, Gell. Tegeticula, Col. Præextextum, Plin. Soliar, Varr. Solisternium, Fest.
units.tr: Tegumentum] A covering of a roof. A covering, Cic. A covering, Liv. A little covering, Varr. A cover, Cat. A covering, Sen. A covering, Amm. A covering, Apul. A covering over, Gell. A small cover, Col. A hanging, Plin. A couch cover, Varr. A rug for a couch, Fest.

units.la: Tela, vid. Linteum.
units.tr: Tela, see Linteum.

units.la: Telum, vid. Iaculum.
units.tr: Telum, see Iaculum.

units.la: Temerarius] Inconsideratus, Cic. Incogitatus, Plin. Oratio ejus in ore, non in pectore nascitur, Gell. Præsidens, Cic. Confidens homo, Ter. Scatet verbis sine ullo judicio. Incogitabilis, Plaut. Inconsulta amentia, Quint. Præceps consiliis. Cœci consules, Temerarius pluma est, vel palea, quam omnis ventus agit.
units.tr: Temerarius] Rash. Inconsiderate, Cic. Unthinking, Plin. His speech is born on his lips, not in his heart, Gell. Presumptuous, Cic. A confident man, Ter. He is full of words without any judgement. Thoughtless, Plaut. Ill-advised madness, Quint. Headlong in counsels. Blind consuls. The rash man is a feather, or a straw, which every wind drives.

units.la: Temerarius provocat peritiorem] Dares Entellum provocat: Tiro Veteranum.
units.tr: Temerarius provocat peritiorem] Dares challenges Entellus; a novice challenges a veteran.

units.la: Temeraria credulitas] Glaciei unius noctis fidere.
units.tr: Rash credulity] To trust the ice of a single night.

units.la: Temere] Clausis oculis agere. Nullo consilio agere. Sine judicio & modo. Inconsulte, Cic. Incogitato animo, Plaut. Immeditate scribere aliquid, Gell. Ex tempore dicere: subito dicere, Cic. Temeriter, Acc. Quicquid in buccam venerit loqui. Jaculari sine scopo. Impetu magis quam consilio.
units.tr: Temere] Rashly: to act with eyes shut; to act without any plan; without judgement or measure. Inconsiderately, Cic. With an unthinking mind, Plaut. To write something off the cuff, Gell. To speak extempore, to speak on the spur of the moment, Cic. Rashly, Acc. To say whatever comes into one's mouth. To throw darts without a target. More from impulse than from design.

units.la: Temeritas] Temeritudo, Pacuv. Incogitantia, Plaut. Præcipitatio, Sen. Inconsideratissima temeritas, Cic.
units.tr: Temeritas] Rashness, Pacuv. Thoughtlessness, Plaut. Headlong haste, Sen. The most inconsiderate rashness, Cic.

units.la: Felix temeritas] Atheniensium inconsulta temeritas.
units.tr: Felix temeritas] The inconsiderate rashness of the Athenians.

units.la: Temeritas noxia] Culex lychno se committens aduritur. Omnibus in rebus temeritas turpis.
units.tr: Temeritas noxia] A gnat that commits itself to a lamp is burned. Rashness is disgraceful in all things.

units.la: Temperans] Temperatus, temperatissimus, moderatus: salubri & moderato victu. Siccus, frugi, continens, cibi minimi est, Cic.
units.tr: Temperans] Temperate, very temperate, moderate: with a wholesome and moderate diet. Dry, frugal, continent, of very little food, Cic.

units.la: Temperans esto] Mature fias senex, si vis diu esse senex.
units.tr: Temperans esto] You will become an old man early, if you wish to remain old for long.

units.la: Temperanter] Castigatius vivere, Amm. Parvo vivere, Hor. Exiguo, Claud. Vid. Frugaliter. Mediocriter.
units.tr: Temperanter] To live more chastely, Amm. To live on little, Hor. On a meagre amount, Claud. See Frugaliter, Mediocriter.

units.la: Temperantia] Temperantia in victu, in prætermittendis voluptatibus, Cic. In cibis, Plin. Sophrosyne, Cic. Vid. Frugalitas. Mediocritas.
units.tr: Temperantia] Temperance in food, in forgoing pleasures, Cic. In meals, Plin. Sophrosyne, Cic. See Frugalitas, Mediocritas.

units.la: Temperantia sanitatis mater] Multa fercula, multi morbi.
units.tr: Temperantia sanitatis mater] Many dishes, many diseases.

units.la: Temperantia decet sapientem] Anima sicca, anima prudens.
units.tr: Temperantia decet sapientem] A dry soul, a prudent soul.

units.la: Temperantia prodest] Coena frugi non facit insaniam. Mater sanitatis indigentia. Multa fercula, multi morbi.
units.tr: Temperantia prodest] A thrifty supper does not bring madness. Need is the mother of health. Many dishes, many diseases.

units.la: Tempestas] Conflata ventis tempestas & imbres, Liv. Foeda tempestas cum grandine, adversa, Cicer. Saeva, turbida, Lucr. Turbidum tempus. Perturbatio coeli, Cicer. Intemperantia coeli, Col. Intemperies, intempestas coeli. Immite & turbidum coelum, Plin. Malitia coeli, Varr. Tempus anni adversum, Cic. Imber effusus nubibus, Virg. Conficitur sidus, vel signum, cum tempestas saevit, Turneb. ex Plin. Vehemens ventus, & immoderata tempestas, Cic.
units.tr: Tempestas] A storm of wind and rain, Liv. A foul storm with hail, adverse, Cic. Savage, turbulent, Lucr. A turbulent time. Disturbance of the sky, Cic. Intemperance of the sky, Col. Intemperies, unseasonableness of the sky. A harsh and turbulent sky, Plin. Malice of the sky, Varr. An unfavourable season of the year, Cic. Rain poured from the clouds, Virg. A constellation is formed, or a sign, when the storm rages, Turneb. from Plin. A violent wind and an immoderate storm, Cic.

units.la: Tempestive] De tempore coenant, Hirt. Satis tempore venire. Mature venire, Cicer. Per tempus legatur salix, Cato.
units.tr: Tempestive] They dine at the proper time, Hirt. To come at a suitable time. To come early, Cic. Let the willow be gathered in due season, Cato.

units.la: Tempestivus, vid. Praecox. Opportunus.
units.tr: Tempestivus: see Praecox, Opportunus.

units.la: Tempestuosus] Turbidum, turbulentum tempus: calamitosum coelum, Cic. Procellosum mare, Sen. Coelum Col. Totus annus hiemavit, Sen. Intempesta nox, Virg. Inserenus, Stat.
units.tr: Tempestuosus] A turbulent, troubled time; a calamitous sky, Cic. A stormy sea, Sen. A sky, Col. The whole year was wintry, Sen. A stormy night, Virg. Overcast, Stat.

units.la: Templum] Aedes sacra, Varr. Dominicum, Hieron. Sacrum, Paul. IC. Domus Dei, Tertull. Fanum, Cic. Sacrarium ritus Christiani, Amm. Monimentum, Cic.
units.tr: Templum] A sacred building, Varr. The Lord's house, Hieron. Sacred, Paul. IC. House of God, Tertull. Shrine, Cic. Sanctuary of the Christian rite, Amm. Monument, Cic.

units.la: Temporalis] Temporarius, Plin. Momentarius, Lampr. Secularis, in SS.
units.tr: Temporalis] Temporary, Plin. Momentary, Lampr. Secular, in SS.

units.la: Tempore, vid, Opportune.
units.tr: Tempore: see Opportune.

units.la: Tempus] Spatium temporis, Cicer. Aetas, aevum, Plin. Dies, Sen. Intervallum, otium, Cic. Explorator omnium. Pater omnium. Omnium sapientissimum. Omnia revelans. Edax rerum, Ovid. Usura temporis, Cic.
units.tr: Tempus] A space of time, Cic. Age, eternity, Plin. Day, Sen. Interval, leisure, Cic. The explorer of all. The father of all. The wisest of all. Revealing all. Devourer of things, Ovid. The usury of time, Cic.

units.la: Tempus est] Commodum est, Ter. Commodissimum est. Maturum est. Tempus optimum, opportunum. Tempus agit rem, Cic. Fert tempus, aetas, Ter. Res est in cardine, Virg.
units.tr: Tempus est] It is convenient, Ter. Most convenient. It is ripe. The best, opportune time. Time drives the matter, Cic. Time and age bring it, Ter. The matter hangs on its hinge, Virg.

units.la: Tempus non est] Alienum tempus est expostulandi. Tempus pus importunum, difficile, Cic. Intempestivitas partus octavi mensis, Gell.
units.tr: Tempus non est] It is an unseasonable time for complaining. An unwelcome, difficult time, Cic. The untimeliness of a birth in the eighth month, Gell.

units.la: Tempus summum] Maximum tempus est. Articulus temporis, Cic. Maturitas temporis est, Liv.
units.tr: Tempus summum] The greatest time. The crucial moment, Cic. The ripeness of the time has come, Liv.

units.la: Tempus habere, barb.] Cum plus otii nactus ero. tempus liberum. Libertas, Otiolum, Cic.
units.tr: Tempus habere, barb.] When I shall have got more leisure. Free time. Freedom, a little leisure, Cic.

units.la: Tempus omnia profert] Annus producit, non ager.
units.tr: Tempus omnia profert] The year brings forth, not the field.

units.la: Tempus exspectandum] Exspecta bos aliquando herbam.
units.tr: Tempus exspectandum] Wait for the ox sometime to find grass.

units.la: Tempus ostendet an verum] Fama loquetur anus. Veritas temporis filia. Omnium explorator tempus.
units.tr: Tempus ostendet an verum] Rumour will tell, old woman. Truth is the daughter of time. Time is the explorer of all.

units.la: Omnia tempus habent] Non semper erit æstas. Non semper Saturnalia. Felici horâ nihil optatius. In luctu Musica importuna.
units.tr: Omnia tempus habent] Summer will not always last. Not always the Saturnalia. Nothing is more welcome than a happy hour. In mourning, music is unwelcome.

units.la: Tempora mutantur] Post nubila Phœbus. Blandi post nubila soles, Sen. Nube solet pulsâ clarior ire dies, Ovid.
units.tr: Tempora mutantur] After clouds, the sun. Smiling suns after clouds, Sen. When the clouds are driven off, the day is wont to shine brighter, Ovid.

units.la: Temporis jactura maxima] Qui fallere quærit tempus, seipsum fallit.
units.tr: Temporis jactura maxima] He who seeks to deceive time deceives himself.

units.la: Per tempus non possum] Tempore excludor. Tempus est importunum, alienum, Cic.
units.tr: Per tempus non possum] I am shut out by time. The time is unwelcome and unsuitable, Cic.

units.la: Tempus recludit omnia] Quicquid in occulto est, in apricum proferet ætas.
units.tr: Tempus recludit omnia] Whatever lies hidden, the age will bring into the open light.

units.la: Tempus omnia consumit] Vel lapidem vitiat tempus.
units.tr: Tempus omnia consumit] Time wears away even a stone.

units.la: Tempore, vulgò] Sub tempus judicii, Liv. Sub horam pugnæ, Suet. Per ver, Cato. Super mensam, Curt. Sub die, Plin.
units.tr: Tempore, vulgo] At the time of judgement, Liv. At the hour of battle, Suet. Through the spring, Cato. Over the table, Curt. In the open day, Plin.

units.la: Tempore misero] Difficili Reip. tempore. Tristissimo meo tempore. Gravissimis temporibus civitatis. Duris, miseris, asperis, turbulentis, extremis, perditis temporibus, Cicer.
units.tr: Tempore misero] In a difficult time for the Republic. In my most sorrowful time. In the gravest times of the state. In hard, wretched, harsh, turbulent, extreme, ruined times, Cic.

units.la: Temporis progressu] Temporis processu, Firm. Tempore procedente, Plin. Iun. Addito tempore, Tac. Progressu ævi, Amm.
units.tr: Temporis progressu] In the course of time, Firm. As time goes on, Plin. Iun. With time added, Tac. In the progress of the age, Amm.

units.la: Tempore perit dolor] Dies adimit ægritudinem hominibus, Ter. Tempus procedens mitigat ægritudinem, Cicer. Lentescunt tempore curæ.
units.tr: Tempore perit dolor] Day takes sorrow away from men, Ter. As time goes on it softens grief, Cic. Cares grow slack with time.

units.la: Tempore proficimus] Alius de alio judicat dies, Plin. Dies diem docet. Discipulus est prioris posterior dies. Temulenter inter pocula] Ad vinum disertus, Cicer. Per vinum exortum dissidium, Plaut. Inter vina, Hor.
units.tr: Tempore proficimus] Each day judges differently from another, Plin. Day teaches day. The later day is the pupil of the earlier. Temulenter inter pocula] Eloquent over wine, Cic. A quarrel arising through wine, Plaut. Among the cups, Hor.

units.la: Temulentia, &c. vid. Ebrietas, &c.
units.tr: Temulentia, &c.: see Ebrietas, &c.

units.la: Tenacitas, vid. Stabilitas.
units.tr: Tenacitas: see Stabilitas.

units.la: Tenax sordidè] Lari sacrificat. Aquam plorat cum lavat. Emptor difficilis haud edit bonum opsonium, Euclionis sordes. Vel unguium praesegmina colligeret. Ne allii caput dederit. Euclione tenacior. Vid. Parcus.
units.tr: Tenax sordide] He sacrifices to the household god. He weeps over the water when he washes. A stingy buyer hardly eats a good dish: the squalor of Euclio. He would gather up the parings of his nails. He would not give up a head of garlic. Tighter than Euclio. See Parcus.

units.la: Tendere aliquò, vid. Proficisci.
units.tr: Tendere aliquo: see Proficisci.

units.la: Tendicula, vid. Laqueus.
units.tr: Tendicula: see Laqueus.

units.la: Tenebrae] Obscuritas, Cic. Privatus aër lumine, Lucr. Lux maligna, Virg. Oculorum praestigiae. Rerum velator.
units.tr: Tenebrae] Obscurity, Cic. Air deprived of light, Lucr. Baleful light, Virg. Deceptions of the eyes. The veiler of things.

units.la: Tenebrae densae] Cimmeriae, Ægyptiacae tenebrae.
units.tr: Tenebrae densae] Cimmerian, Egyptian darkness.

units.la: Tenebricosus] Obscurus, Liv. Tenebrosus locus, Varr. Caliginosus, Cicer. Tenebricosissimus. Tenebrae illi sunt, offunduntur, Id. Obortae tenebrae, Ovid. Caecus, Virg. Illunis, Apul. Obatrum cornu lunae. Obtusa cornua lunae, Plin.
units.tr: Tenebricosus] Dark, Liv. A dark place, Varr. Misty, Cic. Very dark. They are in darkness, are overspread, Id. Darkness has come on, Ovid. Blind, Virg. Dim, Apul. The dark horn of the moon. The blunt horns of the moon, Plin.

units.la: Tenebrio] Lucifuga, Sen. Lucifugus nebulo, Lucil. Latebricola, Plaut.
units.tr: Tenebrio] A light-shunner, Sen. A light-shunning rogue, Lucil. A lurker in holes, Plaut.

units.la: Tener] Mollis, infimâ auricula mollior. Lentus ut cera, Cic. Cereus, Hor. Edurus, Virg.
units.tr: Tener] Soft, softer than the lowest earlobe. Pliant as wax, Cic. Waxen, Hor. Hardy, Virg.

units.la: Tenerum quid] Manum requirens modestissimam.
units.tr: Tenerum quid] Seeking a most modest hand.

units.la: Tenere] Tenere dextrâ aliquid, Ovid. Manu in manu, Cicer. Attinere cultros, Plaut. Praetendere aliquid manu, Virg.
units.tr: Tenere] To hold something in the right hand, Ovid. Hand in hand, Cic. To hold back knives, Plaut. To hold something out with the hand, Virg.

units.la: Tene quod habes] Quod cuique obtigit, id habeat.
units.tr: Tene quod habes] Let each man keep what has fallen to him.

units.la: Tentare aliquem] Tentare aures alicujus verbo nefario, Cicer. Pertentare, Terent. Oppugnare aliquem pecuniâ, Cic.
units.tr: Tentare aliquem] To test someone's ears with a wicked word, Cic. To try thoroughly, Ter. To assail someone with money, Cic.

units.la: Tentare aliquid] Attentare urbem, Cic. Moliri corruptelam judicii. Solicitare animos hominum pretio, Cic. Adpugnare classem, Tac. Omnes aleae casus experiri, Amm. Omnem aleam jacere. Omnem movere funem, lapidem. Omnes adhibere machinas.
units.tr: Tentare aliquid] To attack a city, Cic. To plan the corruption of a judgement. To stir men's minds with bribery, Cic. To assault a fleet, Tac. To try every chance of the dice, Amm. To throw every die. To move every rope, every stone. To apply every machine.

units.la: Tentare impossibilia] Cancrum rectâ ingredi doces.
units.tr: Tentare impossibilia] You teach a crab to walk straight.

units.la: Tentatio] Tentamentum, Ovid. Vexatio virginum, Cic. Vexamen, Lucr. Inquietatio, Liv.
units.tr: Tentatio] A trial, Ovid. Harassment of maidens, Cic. Vexation, Lucr. Disturbance, Liv.

units.la: Tentator] Tentator novitatis, molitor rerum novarum, Sueton.
units.tr: Tentator] A tester of novelty, a mover of revolutions, Suet.

units.la: Tenuis] Pertenuis lamina. Pertenue filum, Plin. Sucrotilla vocula, Titin. Afran. i. tenuis & alta, Fest.
units.tr: Tenuis] A very thin plate. A very fine thread, Plin. A little sweet voice, Titin. Afran. That is, thin and high, Fest.

units.la: Tepefacere, vid. Calefacere.
units.tr: Tepefacere: see Calefacere.

units.la: Tepidus] Pertepidus, Vopisc. Tepens sol, Ovid. Tepens aura, Virg. Lentus ignis tepor, Plin. Egelidum ver, Ovid. Egelidi tepores, Catul.
units.tr: Tepidus] Very lukewarm, Vopisc. A warm sun, Ovid. A warm breeze, Virg. The gentle warmth of a fire, Plin. Chilly spring, Ovid. Chilly warmth, Catul.

units.la: Terebrare]Perterebrare columnam, Cic. Forare, perforare vitem, Col. Inforare truncum in medio, Plin. Circumforatus, Id.
units.tr: Terebrare] To bore thoroughly through a column, Cic. To bore or pierce a vine, Col. To bore a trunk in the middle, Plin. Bored through around, Id.

units.la: Terere] Disterere calcum in mortario, Cat. Subterere metam cum melle, Col. Vid. Atterere.
units.tr: Terere] To grind chalk in a mortar, Cato. To grind the meta with honey, Col. See Atterere.

units.la: Tergere] Detergere, Extergere, Cat. Abstergere labellum, Plaut. Defricare pumice, Plin. Circumfricare, Cat. Pertergere, Hor. Despumare, Vitr.
units.tr: Tergere] To wipe off, to wipe clean, Cato. To wipe a little lip, Plaut. To rub with pumice, Plin. To rub around, Cato. To wipe thoroughly, Hor. To skim off foam, Vitr.

units.la: Terminare] Circumscribere locum. Circumscribere aliquid terminis, cancellis, Cic. Circumsignare, Col. Determinare, Plin. Præscribere modum alicui, Quint. Proponere finem, Ter. Proponere lege. Definire locum, tempus, diem. Præfinem aliquid, & de aliquo. Finire modum sepulchris. Statuere modum alicui. Præcidere. Describere. Terminare finibus gloriam, &c. Cic. Delineare, Arnob.
units.tr: Terminare] To circumscribe a place. To bound something with limits or barriers, Cic. To mark around, Col. To determine, Plin. To prescribe a limit for someone, Quint. To set an end, Ter. To propose by law. To define a place, a time, a day. To set a limit to something and of something. To set bounds to tombs. To fix a limit for someone. To cut off. To describe. To bound glory with limits, etc., Cic. To delineate, Arnob.

units.la: Terminatur aliquid] Terminatur stomachus palato. Definit. Finitur. Annuae nobis operae ad III. Calend. Sextiles emerentur, Cic. Deficit in mucronem aliquid. In angulos exeunt folia. Leni cuneo descendit fastigiatio, Plin.
units.tr: Terminatur aliquid] The stomach ends at the palate. It defines, it is finished. The annual work is to be paid to us by the third day before the Sextile calends, Cic. Something ends in a point. Leaves run out into corners. The gable descends with a gentle wedge, Plin.

units.la: Terminus, vid. Finis. Limes.
units.tr: Terminus: see Finis, Limes.

units.la: Terra] Terra mater omnium. Terra altrix nostra. Globus terrae. Orbis terrarum. Humus, Solum, Cic. Sola terrae, Lucr. Sola terrarum, Enn. Terrenum, Col. Tellus, Virg. Tergum terrae, Lucr. Nutrix & devoratrix omnium. Sustentaculum solidescentium corporum.
units.tr: Terra] Earth, mother of all. Our nourishing earth. The globe of earth. The orb of lands. Ground, soil, Cic. Soil alone, Lucr. The sole of the lands, Enn. Earthly, Col. Land, Virg. The back of the earth, Lucr. Nurse and devourer of all. The support of solidifying bodies.

units.la: Terram rostro fodicare] Rostro terram ruere.
units.tr: Terram rostro fodicare] To dig up the earth with a beak. To dig up the earth with a snout.

units.la: Terrenus] Terrena sodalitas, Cicer. Terrestre praesidium, dium, Idem. Iter, Plin. Terrigena: terrigenæ gigantes, Cicer.
units.tr: Terrenus] Earthly fellowship, Cic. Earthly protection, Id. A journey, Plin. Earth-born: the giants, born of earth, Cic.

units.la: Terrere] Terrorem afferre, injicere, Cic. Incutere. Territare minis, Liv. Terrores jacere, opponere, denunciare. Metum objicere, incutere. Timore afficere. Proponere aliquid ad timorem, Cic. Constat custodes umbris inquietatos, Suet. Proterrere aliquem. Dare in timorem, Plaut. Conterrere, Liv. Intentare alicui formidinem, Am. Adducere. Conjicere in metum: metum inferre, Liv. Intendere, Tac. In metum trahere, Id. Formidines opponere, Cic. Facere pavorem, Liv. Metum, Tac.
units.tr: Terrere] To bring terror, to inspire it, Cic. To strike terror into. To frighten with threats, Liv. To cast terrors, to set against, to announce. To cast fear, to strike fear. To afflict with fear. To propose something to frighten, Cic. It is agreed that guards are disturbed by shadows, Suet. To frighten thoroughly. To give someone a fright, Plaut. To terrify utterly, Liv. To hold out dread to someone, Amm. To bring into fear, Liv. To stretch out, Tac. To drag into fear, Id. To set fears against, Cic. To cause dread, Liv. To cause alarm, Tac.

units.la: Terrent hic omnia] Omnia horriditati mihi erant maximæ, Nev. Ipsa silentia terrent, Virg. Terret solitudo & tacentes loci, Tac. Aura ciet horrorem membris, Lucr. Palpitantibus præcordiis vivitur.
units.tr: All things here terrify] Everything was of the greatest horror to me, Nev. Silence itself terrifies, Virg. Solitude and silent places terrify, Tac. The breeze stirs horror in the limbs, Lucr. One lives with a trembling heart.

units.la: Terribilis] Terrificus. Terriloquus. Perterricrepus, Lucr. Terrisonus, Claud. Larvalis forma, Apul. Trux classicum, Hor. Horribilis. Immanis bellua. Metuendus, Cic. Timendus, Ovid. Tremendus, Virg. Tetrum auribus, Lucr. Terret, Tacit. Horriditati est maximæ, Nev. Vid. Horrendus. Horribile.
units.tr: Terrible] Terrifying; terror-speaking. Terrifying-crashing, Lucr. Thunder-sounding, Claud. A ghostly shape, Apul. A fierce trumpet-call, Hor. Horrible. A monstrous beast. To be feared, Cic. To be dreaded, Ovid. Dreadful, Virg. Hideous to the ears, Lucr. Terrifies, Tac. It is of the greatest horror, Nev. See Horrendus, Horribile.

units.la: Terricula nocturna, vid. Lemures
units.tr: Nocturnal terrors, see Lemures.

units.la: Terriculamentum immane] Panicum, Cic. Fulgur ex pelvi. Formidatæ pennæ. Stramentitius homo.
units.tr: Huge bugbear] A panic, Cic. A thunderbolt from a basin. A feared feathered thing. A straw man.

units.la: Territus] Exanimis metu, & exanimatus, Ter. Conscientiâ peccati mutus, atque exanimatus, ac vix vivus, Cic. Territus animi. Consternatus, Liv. Timefactus. Timore perculsus, Lucr. Exterrita somno, Cicer. Cœci trepidus sub nube timoris, Lucan. Lymphatus, Curt. Hydrophobus, Plin. Attonitus, Virg.
units.tr: Terrified] Lifeless with fear, and deathly pale, Ter. Struck dumb and half dead by a sense of sin, and scarcely alive, Cic. Terrified in mind. Dismayed, Liv. Frightened out of one's wits. Struck down by fear, Lucr. Startled out of sleep, Cic. Trembling beneath the cloud of blind fear, Lucan. Crazed, Curt. Hydrophobic, Plin. Thunderstruck, Virg.

units.la: Terror] Horror. Horribilis formido, Cicer. Terriculum, Liv. Terricula, Sen. Lymphationes nocturnæ, Plin. Consternatio, Liv. Exanimatio, Cic. Cataplexis, Lucr. Hydrophobos, morbus, quo affecti aquam timent, Cels.
units.tr: Terror] Horror. Dreadful fear, Cic. A bugbear, Liv. Bugbears, Sen. Nocturnal frenzies, Plin. Consternation, Liv. Loss of consciousness, Cic. Cataplexy, Lucr. Hydrophobia, a disease in which those affected fear water, Cels.

units.la: Tertiana, vid. Febris.
units.tr: Tertian, see Fever.

units.la: Tessera] Symbolum, Veget. Signum, Sen. Conditum militare, Spart.
units.tr: Tessera] A token, Veget. A sign, Sen. A military watchword, Spart.

units.la: Testa] Testum, Petron. Testu, indecl. ex Varr. Carisf. Crusta marmorea, Vitr. Frivola, pl. Fest.
units.tr: Tile] A tile, Petron. Tile (indeclinable), Varr. Carisf. A marble facing, Vitr. Trifles, plural, Fest.

units.la: Testa ovi, vid. Putamen.
units.tr: Eggshell, see Shell.

units.la: Testa marina] Concha : conchas & umbilicos legere, Cic. Reduviae concharum, Solin. Crusta. Testa limacis. Putamen testudinis, Plin. Conchula, Col.
units.tr: Sea shell] A shell. To gather shells and cockles, Cic. Shellfish remnants, Solin. A crust. A snail's shell. The shell of a tortoise, Plin. A little shell, Col.

units.la: Testaceus] Signinus, Plin. Signinum pavimentum, Col. Crustata animalia : crusta tecta dura, molli, laevi, aspera, crassa, tenui, ut cochleae, conchae, ostrea, &c. Plin.
units.tr: Shelled] Made of potsherd-brick, Plin. A tiled pavement of crushed brick, Col. Animals with a crust: creatures covered by a hard, soft, smooth, rough, thick or thin crust, as snails, mussels, oysters, etc., Plin.

units.la: Testamentum] Cerae primae, ultimae, secundae. Suet. Tabulae supremae, Mart. Testamenti tabulae, Quint. Diatheca, Bud. Voluntas ultima, Vlp. Elogium supremum.
units.tr: Will] First, last and second wax tablets, Suet. The last tablets, Mart. The tablets of a will, Quint. A disposition, Bud. A last will, Ulp. A final eulogy.

units.la: Sine testamento] Intestatus, Intestato mortuus, Cic. Ab intestato, Afran. Intestabilis, Vlp.
units.tr: Without a will] Intestate; died intestate, Cic. From intestacy, Afran. Incapable of making a will, Ulp.

units.la: Testamentum Vetus] Priscae legis instituta, monumenta.
units.tr: Old Testament] The institutions and records of the former law.

units.la: Testamentum Novum] Novae legis institutum. Vitae & doctrinae Christi monumenta. Gestorum & dogmatum Christi codex.
units.tr: New Testament] The institution of the new law. The records of the life and teaching of Christ. The book of Christ's deeds and doctrines.

units.la: Testans] Testator, testatrix, Vlp. Legator, Suet.
units.tr: Testator] A testator, male or female, Ulp. A bequeather, Suet.

units.la: Testari] Dare, dicere, tribuere testimonium, Cic. Perhibere, Col. Reddere, Quint. Dicere pro testimonio, Cic. Pertribuere testimonium alicui, Plin. Iun. Antestari, Priscian. Attestari, alii. Vid. Testem advocare.
units.tr: To testify] To give or bear witness, Cic. To bear witness, Col. To render, Quint. To speak as a witness, Cic. To bear full witness for someone, Plin. Iun. To call to witness, Priscian. To attest, others. See to call a witness.

units.la: Testari, id est, testamentum facere] De re pupilli testari. Testamentum facere, conscribere, Cicer. Testari suam voluntatem, IC. Cavere aliquid testamento, IC. Testato decedere, Vlp. Condere voluntatem, vel voluntates. Ordinare postremam voluntatem, Amm. Testamento aliquid alicui commendare, Cic. Scribere heredem aliquem, Quint.
units.tr: To testify, that is, to make a will] To make a will concerning a ward's property. To make and draw up a will, Cic. To testify one's wishes, IC. To provide for something by will, IC. To die having made a will, Ulp. To make one's will or wills. To set in order one's last wishes, Amm. To entrust something to someone by will, Cic. To write someone as heir, Quint.

units.la: Testimonium] Testatio, Quint. Testificatio, Cic. Auctoritas, Id.
units.tr: Testimony] Attestation, Quint. Testifying, Cic. Authority, Id.

units.la: Testis] Superstes, Plaut. Id est, testis praesens, Fest.
units.tr: Witness] A survivor, Plaut. That is, a present witness, Fest.

units.la: Testis certus] Testis classicus, Fest. Testis locuples, Cic. Testis assiduus, Bud. Testis omni exceptione major, IC. Testabilis, Gell. Testis oculatus, Plaut. Pluris est unus oculatus testis, quam auriti decem. Testem advocare] Testem aliquem facere, Plaut. Ter. Proferre testes. Planum facere testibus. Testari Deum, Cic. Per superos, Plaut. Antestari aliquem, Id. Testiculari. Jovem testem laudo, Id. Conscia sunt numina, Ovid. Do idoneum & gravem testem in singulas res. Producere testes incorruptos. Excitare, adhibere testes, laudatores. Laudatore & teste aliquo uti, Testimonium veritatis ab aliquo petere, sumere. Habeo innocentiæ meæ testem. Testimonium mihi ab aliquo datur, Cic. Vocare ad partes.
units.tr: Reliable witness] A witness of the fleet, Fest. A wealthy witness, Cic. A constant witness, Bud. A witness above all exception, IC. Credible, Gell. An eyewitness, Plaut. One eyewitness is worth more than ten who have only heard. To call a witness] To make someone a witness, Plaut., Ter. To bring forward witnesses. To make a matter plain by witnesses. To call God to witness, Cic. By the gods above, Plaut. To call someone to witness, Id. To call the gods as witnesses, I praise Jupiter as witness, Id. The divinities are conscious, Ovid. I give a suitable and weighty witness for each matter. To produce incorruptible witnesses. To summon and bring in witnesses, commenders. To use someone as a praiser and witness. To seek or take the testimony of truth from someone. I have my innocence as witness. Testimony is given to me by someone, Cic. To summon to a side.

units.la: Tetricitas] Nubecula frontis, Cic. Vid. Torvum videre.
units.tr: Grimness] A little cloud on the brow, Cic. See To look grim.

units.la: Tetricus] Tristi supercilio, Lucr. Adstricta frons, Mart. Agelastus, Cic. Dejecto lumina vultu, Virg.
units.tr: Gloomy] With a sullen brow, Lucr. A furrowed brow, Mart. Never smiling, Cic. With eyes cast down, face lowered, Virg.

units.la: Texere] Contexere, Cic. Telam facere, Ovid. Pectine telam percurrere, Virg. Dentibus pectinis ferire tramam, Varr. Plauduntur vestes, Virg.
units.tr: To weave] To interweave, Cic. To make a web, Ovid. To run the weft through with a comb, Virg. To strike the woof with the teeth of a comb, Varr. The garments are beaten, Virg.

units.la: Textor] Gerdius, Lucil.
units.tr: Weaver] A Gerdian, Lucil.

units.la: Textum] Textile, Liv. Textura, Sipont.
units.tr: Woven fabric] Textile, Liv. Texture, Sipont.

units.la: Theatrum] Theatridium, Varr. Spectaculum, Suet. Scena, Cic. Proscenium, Liv. Amphitheatrum, Mart. Cavea, Plaut. Gradus, Lipf.
units.tr: Theatre] A little theatre, Varr. A spectacle, Suet. The stage, Cic. The proscenium, Liv. An amphitheatre, Mart. The auditorium, Plaut. Rows of seats, Lipsius.

units.la: Theatricus] Theatralis consessus, Cic.
units.tr: Theatrical] A theatrical assembly, Cic.

units.la: Theologia] Sermo de Deo, aut rebus divinis.
units.tr: Theology] Discourse about God, or about divine things.

units.la: Theologi] Atrienses cœli. Duces animarum.
units.tr: Theologians] The attendants of heaven. Leaders of souls.

units.la: Thermæ] Thermulæ, Mart. Aquæ, abfol. Cic. Balneæ sine balneatore. Medicinæ sine Medico.
units.tr: Baths] Little baths, Mart. Waters, absolutely, Cic. Bathhouses without a bath-attendant. Medicines without a physician.

units.la: Thesaurarius] Ærarii rex, præfectus, Cic. A rationibus, Suet. A thesauris. Vid. Quæstor.
units.tr: Treasurer] The king, or prefect, of the treasury, Cic. Of the accounts, Suet. Of the treasuries. See Quaestor.

units.la: Thesauri z are] Condere in thesauros aliquid, Plin.
units.tr: To store up treasure] To put something into treasuries, Plin.

units.la: Thesaurus] Flavissæ, Gell. pro loco. vel Favissæ.
units.tr: Treasury] Favissae, Gell., as a place; or Favissae.

units.la: Thorax ferreus] Thorax ahenus, Virg. Plumbeus, Plin. Lorica ferrea, Varr. Ænea, Cic. Ex ære, Virg. Tunica adamantina, Hor. Tunica recta, Plin. Arma: induere arma, Ovid.
units.tr: Iron breastplate] A bronze breastplate, Virg. Of lead, Plin. An iron cuirass, Varr. Of bronze, Cic. Of copper, Virg. An adamantine coat, Hor. A straight coat, Plin. Arms: to put on armour, Ovid.

units.la: Thronus purpureus] Purpurei throni honor.
units.tr: Purple throne] The honour of a purple throne.

units.la: Thurarius] Thurilegus, Ovid.
units.tr: Incense-bearer] One who gathers incense, Ovid.

units.la: Thureus] Thurifer, Plin. Thuticremus focus. Ovid.
units.tr: Of incense] Incense-bearing, Plin. A hearth burning with incense, Ovid.

units.la: Thuribulum] Acerra, Mart. Plin. Battillum, Hor.
units.tr: Censer] A small altar-pan, Mart., Plin. A little shovel, Hor.

units.la: Thus] Thusculum, Plaut. Dathiatum, vel Dathyatum. Carpheotum, Plin.
units.tr: Incense] A little incense, Plaut. Dathiatum, or Dathyatum. Carpheotum, Plin.

units.la: Tibi sape] Qui sibi silentium non sapiunt, alteri monstrant viam.
units.tr: Tibi sape] Those who do not know how to keep silent for themselves show the way to others.

units.la: Tibia]Tibiae dextrae, ap. Ter. Praecentoriae tibiae, Solin.
units.tr: Flute] Right-hand flutes, ap. Ter. Leading flutes, Solin.

units.la: Tibialia] Genualia, Ovid. Periscelis, idis, Hor.
units.tr: Leggings] Knee-coverings, Ovid. Trousers, Hor.

units.la: Tibicen]Auletes, & auledus, Cic. Choraules,Plin. Choraula, Mart. Flator. Gingrinator, & Gingriator, Fest. Subulo, Id. A sibilare. Tibicina, Plaut.
units.tr: Flute-player] Auletes and auledus, Cic. Choraules, Plin. Choraula, Mart. A piper. Gingrinator and Gingriator, Fest. Subulo, Id. From to whistle. A female flute-player, Plaut.

units.la: Timere] Timere aliquid : timeo mihi ab aliquo : timeo quid agatur. Subtimere. Timore percelli. Tremere animo, Cic. Lymphari, trepidare, Curt. Sperare,Virg. Magno esse timore. Pavere, reformidare aliquid. Horrore perfundi. Horrere minas, conspectum, Cic. Perhorrescere aliquid, Id. Horrescere, Terent. Metuere ab aliquo, Vereri ab aliquo supplicium : ne : vereor ut satis firmum sit, Cicer. Praetimet tibi, Plaut. Formidare sibi malum, Afformidare, Id. Praeformidare,Quint. Pavescere,Tac. Terreri,Plaut. Vid. Metuere.
units.tr: To fear] To fear something; I fear for myself from someone; I fear what is happening. To be a little afraid. To be struck with fear. To tremble in mind, Cic. To be frenzied, to tremble, Curt. To hope, Virg. To be in great fear. To dread, to be afraid of something. To be drenched in horror. To shudder at threats, at the sight, Cic. To be utterly horrified by something, Id. To shudder, Ter. To dread something from someone; to fear punishment from someone; to fear lest; I fear that it is not firm enough, Cic. He fears for you, Plaut. To dread harm for oneself; to be terribly afraid, Id. To dread beforehand, Quint. To be fearful, Tac. To be frightened, Plaut. See To fear.

units.la: Timide] Diffidenter aliquid attingere. Religiose commendare, Cic. Pavide, trepide, Liv. Trepidanter, Suet. Suspensa manu, Plin. Iun. Obnoxie dicere, Bud. ex Liv.
units.tr: Timidly] To touch something with distrust. To commend scrupulously, Cic. Fearfully, anxiously, Liv. Tremblingly, Suet. With a hand held back, Plin. Iun. To speak submissively, Bud., from Liv.

units.la: Timidus] Abjecto, demisso, humili, pusillo, fracto, angusto, muliebri animo. Formidinis plenus, Cic. Corde gelato, Luc. Meticulosus,Plaut. Praetrepidus,Suet. Obnoxius & trepidus,Id. Pavidus,Hor. Pavidissimus,Sil. Formidolosus, Ter. Col. Neque vigilans,neque in somnis mente potest consistere, Cic. Animus in pedes decidit. Ante tubam trepidat. Lepore, dama timidior,Eraf. Parum Vir. Vel muscas metuit praetervolantes. Corpus sine pectore. Crepitus frondium leporem terret. Degenerem trepidatio prodit. Degeneres canum caudam deflectunt sub alvum.
units.tr: Timid] Of a downcast, abased, humble, petty, broken, narrow, womanish spirit. Full of dread, Cic. With a frozen heart, Luc. Fearful, Plaut. Overly anxious, Suet. Anxious and trembling, Id. Fearful, Hor. Most fearful, Sil. Dreadful, Ter., Col. Neither awake nor in dreams can the mind hold still, Cic. The spirit falls down into the feet. He trembles before the trumpet. More timid than a hare, Erasmus. Hardly a man. He fears even flies flying past. A body without a heart. The rustling of leaves frightens a hare. Trembling reveals a degenerate. Degenerate dogs tuck their tails under their bellies.

units.la: Timidi minaces] Canes timidi vehementius latrant.
units.tr: Timid threateners] Timid dogs bark more fiercely.

units.la: Timidus miles] Lepus galeatus. Omnia tuta timet, Virg. Umbram suam metuit, Cic.
units.tr: Timid soldier] A helmeted hare. He fears everything, even safe things, Virg. He fears his own shadow, Cic.

units.la: Timida vita] Leporis vita. Lepus dormiens. Leporinus somnus.
units.tr: Timid life] The life of a hare. A sleeping hare. A hare's sleep.

units.la: Timor] Timiditas. Formido. Reformidatio. Metus. Diffidentia futuri mali, Cic.
units.tr: Fear] Timidity. Dread. Recoil. Fear. Distrust of a future evil, Cic.

units.la: Timor malè ominatur] Pessimus in dubiis augur timor.
units.tr: Fear gives bad omens] Fear is the worst augur in doubtful matters.

units.la: Timor verecundiæ custos] Ubi timor, ibi pudor.
units.tr: Fear is the guardian of modesty] Where there is fear, there is shame.

units.la: Tinctor] Insector, Plin. Offector, Fest. Colorator, Gell. Flammearius. Carinarius, Plaut. Caltularius, Douz.
units.tr: Dyer] One who stains, Plin. One who does harm, Fest. A colourer, Gell. A flame-worker. A ship-caulker, Plaut. A cloth-dyer, Douza.

units.la: Tinctura] Tinctus, us. Infectus, us, Plin.
units.tr: Dye] A dyeing, a staining, Plin.

units.la: Tinctus, vid. Coloratus.
units.tr: Dyed, see Coloured.

units.la: Tingere, vid. Intingere, Colorare.
units.tr: To dye, see To dip in, to colour.

units.la: Tinnire, vid. Sonare.
units.tr: To ring, see To sound.

units.la: Tinnunculus] Tinunculus, Columbarum amicus.
units.tr: Kestrel] A kestrel, a friend of pigeons.

units.la: Tiro] Tirunculus, Iuv. Novitius, Var. De grege novitiorum, Cic.
units.tr: Recruit] A little recruit, Juv. A novice, Var. From the flock of novices, Cic.

units.la: Tirones sapientiæ] Initiati Musarum sacris.
units.tr: Beginners in wisdom] Those initiated into the rites of the Muses.

units.la: Tiro provocat, &c. Vid. Temerarius.
units.tr: The recruit challenges, etc. See Rash.

units.la: Tirocinium] Elementa puerorum. Seminarium triumphorum. Incunabula doctrinæ, Cic. Initiamenta, pl. Sen. Rudimenta dicendi, Quint. Militiæ, Paterc. Vid. Exercitatio.
units.tr: Apprenticeship] The elements for boys. A nursery of triumphs. The cradle of learning, Cic. Initiations, plural, Sen. The rudiments of speaking, Quint. Of military service, Paterc. See Practice.

units.la: Titillare] Titillare sensus, Lucr. Prolectare sensus, Vitr. Lacessere corpus mollibus & lenibus fomentis, Sen.
units.tr: To tickle] To tickle the senses, Lucr. To entice the senses, Vitr. To stimulate the body with soft and gentle applications, Sen.

units.la: Titillatio] Titillatus, Plin. Tactu quodam corporis risus lacessitur, Quint. Scalpurigo blandiens, Solin.
units.tr: Tickling] A tickling, Plin. Laughter is provoked by a certain touch on the body, Quint. Itching that flatters, Solin.

units.la: Titubans] Lapsans gressu, ex Sil. Lapsabundus, Sen. Quassabundus Hercules ebrius, Macrob.
units.tr: Staggering] Stumbling in step, from Sil. Tottering, Sen. Hercules staggering drunk, Macrob.

units.la: Titubare] Succidui titubant gressus, Claud. Vestigia pedum extra mensuram aberrantia, Petron. Vestigia presso haud tenuit titubata solo, Virg. Vacillare ex vino, Quint.
units.tr: To stagger] Their weak steps stagger, Claud. Footsteps wandering beyond measure, Petron. The faltering feet did not hold on the pressed ground, Virg. To reel from wine, Quint.

units.la: Titubatio] Lapsans gressus, Sili. Ebrius gradus, Sen. Vestigia ebria multo Baccho, Propert.
units.tr: Staggering] Stumbling in gait, Sil. A drunken walk, Sen. Steps drunk with much Bacchus, Propert.

units.la: Titulus] Titulo tenus Consulatum gessit, Suet. Vid. Inscriptio.
units.tr: Title: He held the consulship in name only, Suet. See Inscription.

units.la: Toga] Toga virilis, pura, Cic. Abolla major, Iuv. Vid. Paludamentum.
units.tr: Toga: The plain toga of manhood, Cic. The greater abolla, Juv. See Paludamentum.

units.la: Tolerabilis] Patibilis dolor, Cic. Commodum exilium, Ovid.
units.tr: Tolerable: Pain that can be borne, Cic. A tolerable exile, Ovid.

units.la: Tolerabiliter] Tolerabilius pati dolores. Toleranter ferre, pati, Cic.
units.tr: Tolerably: To bear pains more tolerably. To endure or suffer patiently, Cic.

units.la: Tolerans, vid. Patiens.
units.tr: Tolerant: See Patient.

units.la: Tolerantia] Toleratio. Perfunctio laborum,Cic. Patien-tia malorum, Ovid.
units.tr: Tolerance: Toleration. Getting through hardships, Cic. Patience in misfortunes, Ovid.

units.la: Tolerantia mutua] Amici vitia noveris, non oderis.
units.tr: Mutual tolerance: Know your friend's faults, but do not hate him for them.

units.la: Tolerare] Ferre malum. Toleranter, tolerabiliter ferre, æquo animo, pacatè &c. Cic. Vid. Pati æquo animo.
units.tr: To tolerate: To bear an evil. To bear it patiently, tolerably, calmly, quietly, and so on, Cic. See To suffer with an even mind.

units.la: Tolerare mores alicujus] Ferre aliquem. Nobis inter nos vitia toleranda sunt,Cic. Vincere aliquem patientiâ ; silen-tio conviciatorem, Bud.
units.tr: To tolerate someone's ways: To put up with someone. Among ourselves faults must be tolerated, Cic. To overcome someone by patience; to answer a reviler with silence, Bud.

units.la: Tollere] Tollere in sublime aliquid,Plin. Sustollere, Plaut. Extollere, sublevare. Subire humeris, Cic. Tollere in col-lum, Plaut.
units.tr: To lift: To lift something up on high, Plin. To raise up, Plaut. To lift up and raise, to give relief. To take on the shoulders, Cic. To lift onto the neck, Plaut.

units.la: Tolutarius] Tolutaris equus, Sipont. Gradarius, Lucil. Asturco, Plin.
units.tr: Ambling: An ambling horse, Sipont. A trotting horse, Lucil. A pacer, Plin.

units.la: Tolutim incedere] Tolutim carpere incessus, Plin. Sinua-re volumina crurum. Gressus glomerare superbos, Virg. Ad numerum colligere ungulas, Mart.
units.tr: To go at an amble: To cover ground with an ambling gait, Plin. To swing the legs in a curve. To gather proud steps, Virg. To bring the hooves together to a beat, Mart.

units.la: Tomaculum] Tomaclum, Britan. Tomaculæ, Juv. To-macinæ,Var. Hysitium,Platin. Isitium, & Isicium,Macrob.
units.tr: Sausage: Tomaclum, Britan. Tomaculae, Juv. Tomacinae, Varr. Hysitium, Platin. Isitium and Isicium, Macrob.

units.la: Tonat] Coelum tonat,Plin. Faciunt sonitus nubila. Per-currunt nubila coelum, Lucr. Coelum tonitru contremit.
units.tr: It thunders: The sky thunders, Plin. The clouds make a sound. The clouds run across the sky, Lucr. The sky shakes with thunder.

units.la: Tondere caput, barbam] Radere alicujus caput,Suet. Rasi-tare barbam,Gell. Abradere,Plin. Attondere strictim,Plaut. Detondere capillos. Recidere comam, Mart. Tonsitare, Plaut. Silvam menti demetere, Eraf.
units.tr: To shave the head and beard: To shave someone's head, Suet. To shave the beard, Gell. To scrape off, Plin. To trim close, Plaut. To cut off the hair, Mart. To shear the beard, Plaut. To mow the forest of the chin, Erasm.

units.la: Tondere oves] Tonsitare oves,Plaut. Detondere, Col.
units.tr: To shear sheep: To shear sheep, Plaut. To clip, Col.

units.la: Tonitru] Tonitrus, Plin. Tonitruum,Cic. Fragor nu-bium. Fragor coelestis, Amm. Murmura coeli, Lucr.
units.tr: Thunder: Thunder, Plin. A thunderclap, Cic. The crash of clouds. A heavenly crash, Amm. The murmurs of heaven, Lucr.

units.la: Tonsitari] Tonsitor ter anno, Plaut. Operam dare ton-soribus, Suet. Ponere barbam, Hor. Suet.
units.tr: Shaving: A barber three times a year, Plaut. To take care to employ barbers, Suet. To lay aside the beard, Hor., Suet.

units.la: Tonsor] Rasor, Fest. Capitum & capillorum concinna-tor, Col. Pilicerpus, Sen.
units.tr: Barber: A shaver, Fest. One who neatly trims heads and hair, Col. A hair-clipper, Sen.

units.la: Tonsura] Tonsura lanæ,Var. Tonsus, us,Plaut. Tonsio.
units.tr: Shearing: The shearing of wool, Varr. A shearing, Plaut. A clipping.

units.la: Tophus] Bibulus lapis.
units.tr: Tophus: A porous stone.

units.la: Topiarium opus] Plin. Topium, Vitr. Pergula in vineis, Col. Trichilum, Virg.
units.tr: Topiary work: Plin. Topium, Vitr. A pergola in the vineyards, Col. A trellis arbour, Virg.

units.la: Topiarius] Viridarius, Vlp.
units.tr: Topiarius: A gardener, Ulp.

units.la: Torcular] Torculare,Sosip. Torculum,Var. Prelum,Col. Calcatorium,Pallad. Forum,Var.Col.
units.tr: Wine press: Torculare, Sosip. Torculum, Varr. A press, Col. A treading vat, Pallad. A forum, Varr., Col.

units.la: Torcularium] Torcularia cella, Col. Forum torcula-ris,Tertul.
units.tr: Press-room: A press-room, Col. A court of the press, Tertull.

units.la: Torcularius] Calcator uvæ,Henric. Steph.
units.tr: Presser: One who treads grapes, Henric. Steph.

units.la: Tormentum æneum] Bombarda fulminca, Lipf. Tormentum, Absol. Vopisc. Fulminea machina,Polyd.Virg. Helepolis, Vitr. Tormentum murale, Virg.
units.tr: Bronze cannon: A thundering bombard, Lipsius. A cannon, Abs. Vopisc. A thunderbolt-engine, Polyd. Vergil. A helepolis, Vitr. A siege-engine, Virg.

units.la: Tornare] Detornare, Globare. Torno facere calicem, Plin. Tudiculare, Sipont. Rotundare ad volubilitatem.
units.tr: To turn on a lathe: To turn round, to round off. To make a cup on the lathe, Plin. To turn, Sipont. To round so that it rolls.

units.la: Tornatilis] Torno rasilis, Virg. Tornatus, Lucr. Tortus, Mart. Diatretus calix, Vlp.
units.tr: Turned: Smoothed on the lathe, Virg. Turned, Lucr. Twisted, Mart. A diatreta cup, Ulp.

units.la: Tornator] Diatretarius, Cal. Rhod.
units.tr: Turner: A diatretarius, Cal. Rhod.

units.la: Torpere] Ignaviæ se dare, desidiæ. Vid.Desidere. Otio torpere.
units.tr: To be numb: To give oneself to idleness and sloth. See Desidere. To grow numb with leisure.

units.la: Torpor, vid. Stupor. Desidia.
units.tr: Numbness: See Stupor, Desidia. Sluggishness.

units.la: Torquere] Torquere capillos ferro, Ovid. Contorquere, Plin.
units.tr: To curl: To curl hair with the iron, Ovid. To twist, Plin.

units.la: Torrere] Assa, frixa, &c. Celf. Vid. Frigere. Assare.
units.tr: To roast: Roasted, fried, etc., Celsus. See Frigere, Assare.

units.la: Tortuosus] Contortus & deflexus amnis. Flexuosus auditus, Cic. Sinuosa volumina serpentis, Virg. Vorticosus amnis,Liv. Turbineus vortex,Ovid. Tortilis nervus,Plin. Contortus crinis, Sen. Cochlis columna, Pub. Victor. Mæandratus, Var. Vid. Contortus.
units.tr: Winding: A river twisted and bent. A winding sound, Cic. The sinuous coils of a serpent, Virg. A whirling river, Liv. A whirling eddy, Ovid. A twisted sinew, Plin. Twisted hair, Sen. A spiral column, Pub. Victor. Meandering, Varr. See Contortus.

units.la: Torvus] Torvioculi, Plin. Sæva facies, Tac. Horribilis, horrendus visu, Virg. Dira facies,Ovid. Rigidus vultus,Id. Vid. Severus.
units.tr: Grim: Grim-eyed, Plin. A savage face, Tac. Horrible, dreadful to look at, Virg. A dire face, Ovid. A stiff face, Ovid. See Severus.

units.la: Torvum videre] Truces oculos vibrare, Salvian. Severo & tristi vultu, Cic. Torvo vultu. Invito vultu ridere, Hor. Ficto vultu, Stat. Dejecto, Sen. Fronte contractâ, obdu-cta, Hor. Oculis infestis, torvis tueri. Oculis contortis cernere. Taurine & limis oculis tueri. Transversis hirquis tueri.
units.tr: To look grim: To shake fierce eyes, Salvian. With a stern and sad face, Cic. With a grim look. To laugh with an unwilling face, Hor. With a feigned face, Stat. Downcast, Sen. With the brow contracted or drawn, Hor. To gaze with hostile, grim eyes. To look with squinting eyes. To gaze with bull-like and sidelong eyes. To look with goat-like sidelong glances.

units.la: Tot] Tantum est, Plaut.
units.tr: So many: It is only so much, Plaut.

units.la: Totidem] Tantundem solutum est, Cic.
units.tr: As many: As much has been paid, Cic.

units.la: Totus] Totus perpetuus. Totus universus, Plaut. Totum corpus alicujus rei, (pro totâ re,) Cic. Cunctus populus: cuncta civitas. Universa familia, vita. Omnis plebs. Tantus, quantus. Integer lituus deflagravit,Cic. Perpetuæ ædes ruunt, Plaut. Tu quantusquantus nil nisi sapientia es, Ter.
units.tr: Whole: Entire and continuous. Whole and entire, Plaut. The whole body of something (for the whole matter), Cic. The whole people; the whole state. The whole household, the whole of life. All the common people. As great as. The whole lituus burned up, Cic. Continuous buildings fall down, Plaut. Whatever you are, you are nothing but wisdom, Ter.

units.la: Totum hoc est] Paginam utramque facit.
units.tr: This whole thing is: It fills both pages.

units.la: Totum melius fracto] Melius solidum, quam solidatum. Nunquam cicatrix nisi collata vulneri, placuit, quod ita coivisse gaudemus, ut non fuisse mallemus, Sen.
units.tr: Better whole than mended: Better solid than repaired. A scar never forms unless joined to the wound; we are glad it has so knit together that we would have preferred it never to have happened, Sen.

units.la: Per totum] A planta pedis usque ad verticem. A vertice, ad imos talos. Ab unguiculis ad pilum summum, ad caput, ad pedes. A capite usque ad calcem. A summo capillo usque ad calcem pedis.
units.tr: Throughout: From the sole of the foot to the crown. From the crown to the lowest heel. From the fingernails to the top hair, to the head, to the feet. From the head to the heel. From the top hair to the sole of the foot.

units.la: Ex toto] Ad assem vel denarium. Ne rutis quidem & cæsis receptis, vel exceptis, ex Cic. Quantumquantum erat, accepit. Ne tantillum quidem reliquit. Cum pulviculo. Cum totâ ærugine, Iuv.
units.tr: Entirely: To the last as or denarius. Even the cut and stripped coins being taken in or excepted, Cic. He took whatever there was. He left not even the tiniest bit. With the dust. With all the rust, Juv.

units.la: Trabs] Tignum, Hor. Transtra, pl. Vitr.
units.tr: Beam: A timber, Hor. Crossbeams, Vitr.

units.la: Tractabilis] Nihil eo tractabilius. Flexilis civium voluntas. Ad arbitrium, nutum, voluntatem alicujus se fingit, convertit. Ad nutum alicujus præsto est. Morem gerit voluntati, Cic. Morigerus in rebus omnib. alicui, Ter. Pro rota me uti licet, (figulari) vel ego huc, vel illuc vertar, quo imperabitis, Plaut. Indulgeo me alicui, Macrob. Cerâ tractabilior. Domabilis.
units.tr: Tractable: Nothing more pliable. A flexible will of citizens. He shapes and turns himself to another's will, nod or desire. He is at hand at someone's nod. He complies with someone's wishes, Cic. Compliant in all things to someone, Ter. I may be used like a potter's wheel; I shall turn here or there, wherever you command, Plaut. I indulge myself to someone, Macrob. Softer than wax. Tameable.

units.la: Tractare, vid. Tangere. Mansuefacere.
units.tr: To handle: See Tangere. Mansuefacere.

units.la: Tractare hospitem] Tractare aliquem liberaliter; liberalissime omnibus rebus, Cic. Commode, Ter. Ut abs te affecta est, Cic. Habere se, vel aliquem parce, duriter, Ter. Durius, Vlp. Male, Plaut. Ita me habuit, Plin. Accipere aliquem verbis male, Cic. Accipere haud familiariter, Plaut. indignis modis, Ter. Invitate illum usque adeo, donec quâ domum abeat, nesciat. Accipere magnifice lepidis victibus, Plaut. Accipere aliquem clementer, bene, hilare, Cic. Prolixè, Ter. Lautè, Hor. Apparatis epulis, Liv. Ampliter apponere in cœna. Accipere aliquem in prandio apud se ampliter, Plin. Apponere mensam alicui, Cic.
units.tr: To treat a guest: To treat someone generously, most generously in all things, Cic. Courteously, Ter. As you have been treated by yourself, Cic. To treat someone sparingly or harshly, Ter. More harshly, Ulp. Badly, Plaut. He treated me so, Plin. To receive someone roughly with words, Cic. To receive someone not very familiarly, Plaut. With unworthy manners, Ter. Invite him so long that he does not know how to get home. To receive magnificently with pleasant fare, Plaut. To receive someone kindly, well, cheerfully, Cic. Generously, Ter. Elegantly, Hor. With prepared feasts, Liv. To set out a lavish spread at dinner. To entertain someone at lunch lavishly at one's house, Plin. To set a table before someone, Cic.

units.la: Tractatio] Maletractatio, Arnob. Propinatio, Gell. Præbitio, Varr.
units.tr: Handling: Ill-treatment, Arnob. Offering a drink, Gell. Provision, Varr.

units.la: Tradere alicui aliquid] Porrigere alicui manum. Ministrare pocupoculum. Tradere de manu in manum. Porrigere & tendere alicui consilium, Cic. Contradere argumenta, Lucr. Transmittere alicui provinciam, Plin. Iun. Vid. Porrigere.
units.tr: To hand something to someone: To hold out one's hand to someone. To serve a cup. To hand from hand to hand. To offer and extend advice to someone, Cic. To hand over arguments, Lucr. To hand over a province to someone, Plin. Iun. See Porrigere.

units.la: Traditio] Mos traditus ab antiquis, Hor. Traditum aliquid posteris. Tradita consuetudo, Cic. Traditum aliquid in posteros. Quint.
units.tr: Tradition: A custom handed down by the ancients, Hor. Something handed down to posterity. Handed-down custom, Cic. Something transmitted to posterity, Quint.

units.la: Traducere] Traduc matrem, & omnem familiam ad nos, Ter. Transducere, Cic. Transmovere, Tac. Vid. al. Diffamare.
units.tr: To lead across: Bring your mother and the whole household over to us, Ter. To lead across, Cic. To move across, Tac. See also Diffamare.

units.la: Trahere] Cinibus trahere, Virg. Obtorto collo trahere, Plaut. Allicit magnes ferrum, Cic. Pellicit ad se, Lucr. Ducere aliquem capillis, Tibul. Magnetis more attrahere.
units.tr: To draw: To drag through the ashes, Virg. To drag by a twisted neck, Plaut. The magnet draws iron, Cic. It draws to itself, Lucr. To drag someone by the hair, Tibull. To attract as a magnet does.

units.la: Trajectus] Trajectio. Transvectio. Transmissio, Vectura, Cic. Commeatus, Caes.
units.tr: Crossing: Conveyance. Transit, transmission, passage, carriage, Cic. Supplies, Caes.

units.la: Trajicere] Transvehi navibus, Sallust. Transportari carina, Mart. Vid. Transfretare.
units.tr: To cross: To be carried across by ships, Sallust. To be transported by a keel, Mart. See Transfretare.

units.la: Trames] Limes, via transversa, Fest.
units.tr: Path: A boundary, a cross-path, Fest.

units.la: Tranquillare] Sedare mentes, Plin. Tranquillum animum, tranquillitatem facere, Plaut. In tranquillum redigere, Liv. Componere mentem, Cels. In tranquillum ex saevis tempestatibus transferre, Lucil. E tantis fluctibus in tranquillo locare, Lucr. Mulcere procellas. Mitigare aliquem, Cic. Mitificare, Plin. Mansuefacere, Liv. Evellere scrupulum alicui, Cic. Eximere, Plin.
units.tr: To calm: To settle minds, Plin. To make the mind calm and tranquil, Plaut. To bring into a calm, Liv. To compose the mind, Cels. To carry from savage storms into calm, Lucil. To place in calm from great waves, Lucr. To soothe storms. To pacify someone, Cic. To mitigate, Plin. To tame, Liv. To pluck a worry out of someone's mind, Cic. To take away, Plin.

units.la: Tranquille, vid. Pacate.
units.tr: Calmly: See Pacate.

units.la: Tranquillitas maris] Tranquillum, Plin. Status pacati aëris, Lucr. Silent venti, Sen. Quiescunt, Plin. Iun. Posuere venti, Virg. Mitescit fretum, Liv. Loca non pervia ventis, ex Ovid. Malacia maris, Caes. Pellacia maris, Lucr. Rid ent æquora, Ridet tempestas, Id. Mollities maris, Plin. Halcedonia, Plaut. Dies halcyonii, Varr. Halcyonides dies, Plin. Tractabile mare, Id. Undæ mollesc, Lucr. Flustra, pl. Fest.
units.tr: Calm of the sea: Calm, Plin. A state of peaceful air, Lucr. The winds are silent, Sen. They rest, Plin. Iun. The winds have fallen, Virg. The sea grows gentle, Liv. Places not open to the winds, from Ovid. The calm of the sea, Caes. The deceptive calm of the sea, Lucr. The waters smile, the storm laughs, Id. Softness of the sea, Plin. Halcyon, Plaut. Halcyon days, Varr. Halcyon days, Plin. A sea that can be handled, Id. The waves grow soft, Lucr. Calms, Fest.

units.la: Tranquillitas animi] Tranquillitas vitæ. Tranquilla vitæ frons. Otiosa senectus. Quietè acta ætas. Animus errore liber. Euthymia, Cic. Tranquillè placideque ducere vitam, Caes.
