units.tr: Calm of mind: Tranquillity of life. A calm face of life. A leisured old age. A life spent quietly. A mind free from error. Euthymia, Cic. To lead life tranquilly and peacefully, Caes.

units.la: Tranquillitas à negotiis] Halcyonia sunt apud forum, Plaut.
units.tr: Calm from business: The halcyon days are found at the forum, Plaut.

units.la: Tranquillus] Placidus homo, Ter. Quietus, quietissimus. Sedatus. Vacuus à turbis locus. Res pacatæ & minime turbulentæ, Cic. Pacatum æquor, Ovid. Placata procella, Propert. Inturbidus annus, Tac. Pacatus aër: pacata vita, Lucr.
units.tr: Calm: A peaceful man, Ter. Quiet, most quiet. Settled. A place free from crowds. Peaceful and not at all turbulent affairs, Cic. A calm sea, Ovid. A calmed storm, Propert. An untroubled year, Tac. Calm air; a peaceful life, Lucr.

units.la: Tranquillæ res] Inducias vacillantis fortunæ. Malacia. Vid. Superiora.
units.tr: Calm circumstances: A truce from a wavering fortune. Malacia. See Superiora.

units.la: Trans] Trans ripam, Cic. Mare, Quint. Ultra villam est, Cic. Cis Rhenum, Sallust. (id est, ultra, Sipont.) Secundum Tiberim fanum dedicavit, Var.
units.tr: Across: Across the bank, Cic. Across the sea, Quint. Beyond the villa, Cic. Cis Rhenum, Sall. (that is, beyond, Sipont.) He dedicated a shrine along the Tiber, Varr.

units.la: Transcribere] Transcribere literas publicas. Transferre literas, & lituras de tabulis in libros. Aliquem locum totidem verbis ex aliquo transferre. Describere librum ab aliquo. Exscribere tabulas, Cic. Exscribere è libris, Var. Transponere aliquid ex annalibus, Gell.
units.tr: Transcribere: To transcribe public records. To transfer letters and erasures from tablets into books. To transfer some passage word for word from one author. To copy a book from someone. To copy out tablets, Cic. To copy out from books, Var. To transpose something from the annals, Gell.

units.la: Transcurrere] Transcurrere in alia castra, Liv. Transcurrere in arcem, Ter. Transvolare in alteram partem, Liv. Transire ad, Cic. Curisitare ab aliquo ad, Ter.
units.tr: Transcurrere: To run over into another camp, Liv. To run across into the citadel, Ter. To fly over to the other side, Liv. To go over to, Cic. To run about from someone to, Ter.

units.la: Transferre] Transportare aliquid, Cic. Transducere arbores, Col. Transmovere, Ter. Trajicere verba, Cic. Transcribere nomina in socios, Liv. i. e. debita.
units.tr: Transferre: To carry something across, Cic. To lead trees across, Col. To move across, Ter. To put words across, Cic. To transfer names onto allies, Liv., that is, debts.

units.la: Transfigere] Transfigere corpus alicujus cum armis, Liv. Transverberare bestiam venabulo, Cic. Transfigere aliquem gladio, Tac. Adigere agnum ferro, Spart. Adigere ensem in pectus, Ovid. Trajicere aliquem, Cæs. Perfodere gladio aliquem, Gell. Suffodere equum, Cæs. Transfodere latus alicui, Liv. Transfadigere aliquem, Virg. Perforare ictu pectus. Ovid. Pertundere crumenam, Plaut. Infigere hosti in pectus gladium, Cic. Compegit gladium in sua viscera, Amm.
units.tr: Transfigere: To pierce the body of someone with weapons, Liv. To run a beast through with a hunting spear, Cic. To pierce someone with a sword, Tac. To drive a lamb through with iron, Spart. To drive a sword into the breast, Ovid. To pierce someone through, Caes. To stab someone with a sword, Gell. To stab a horse through, Caes. To pierce someone's side, Liv. To transfix someone, Virg. To pierce the breast with a blow, Ovid. To pierce a purse, Plaut. To thrust a sword into an enemy's breast, Cic. He drove the sword into his own entrails, Amm.

units.la: Transfretare] Perfretare, Solin. Transmittere mare, Cic. Transire mare, Id. Enavigare, Plin. Evincere fretum, Ovid.
units.tr: Transfretare: To cross the strait, Solin. To send across the sea, Cic. To cross the sea, Id. To sail across, Plin. To overcome the strait, Ovid.

units.la: Transfuga, vid. Profugus.
units.tr: Transfuga, see Profugus.

units.la: Transgredi aliquid] Cic. Transire lineas, Id. Transcendere fines, Lucr. Proferre passum ultra aliquid, Ultra lineas figere gradum. Transire intactum aliquid, ut limen, cœnum. Transferre caute vestigia per aliquid. Superferre vestigia, pedes alicui rei. Superare pede innoxio spinas, coenam &c· Supergredi, Plin.
units.tr: Transgredi aliquid: To cross lines, Cic. To cross boundaries, Lucr. To step beyond something; to set a foot beyond the lines. To pass over something untouched, such as a threshold or mud. To carefully carry one's steps across something. To step over something with the feet. To pass over thorns with an unhurt foot, supper and so on. To step over, Plin.

units.la: Transfigere cum aliquo aliquid] Transfigere controversiam. Facere decisionem, Decidere cum aliquo aliquid : de aliqua re, Conficere cum heredibus. Absolvere se (vel absolvi judicio) ab aliquo, Cic. Dissolvi me ocyus, operam ut darem tibi, Ter.
units.tr: Transfigere cum aliquo aliquid: To settle a dispute. To make a decision; to settle something with someone about some matter; to come to terms with the heirs. To acquit oneself of someone (or be acquitted by judgment), Cic. To be released from me more quickly so that I may give you my help, Ter.

units.la: Transfigere diem in re aliquâ] Sic ille dies extractus est. Hoc agebant ut dies eximeretur; duceretur tempus. Fallere horas, Eraf. Comburere diem, Plaut.
units.tr: Transfigere diem in re aliqua: So that day was dragged out. They were doing this so that the day might be taken away and the time led on. To beguile the hours, Erasmus. To burn up the day, Plaut.

units.la: Transfit hoc] Evanuit fabula.
units.tr: Transfit hoc: The story has evaporated.

units.la: Transfire] Transitum facere, Col. Transcendere, Caf. Permeare & transire omnia. Transitare, Id. Transvectum est tempus. Pervadere. Permanare ad, Cic. Perlabitur per &c. ad cor, Id. Vid. Praeterire.
units.tr: Transfire: To make a passage, Col. To cross over, Cass. To pass through and across everything. To go across, Id. Time has been carried past. To pervade. To flow through to, Cic. It slips through to the heart, Id. See Praeterire.

units.la: Transitorius] Fugitivus, Mart. Caducus, Cic. Fugax, Hor. Momentosus, Quint. Res humanae fragiles, Cic.
units.tr: Transitorius: Fleeting, Mart. Falling, Cic. Fleeting, Hor. Momentous, Quint. Human things are frail, Cic.

units.la: Transitoria omnia] Nihil semper floret.
units.tr: Transitoria omnia: Nothing always flourishes.

units.la: Transitus] Commeatus utroque continet, Plaut. Pervius usus tectorum, Virg. Transmissus à Gallia in Britanniam, Caf.
units.tr: Transitus: Passage contains both, Plaut. The passable use of roofs, Virg. Passage from Gaul into Britain, Caes.

units.la: In transitu, vid. Obiter.
units.tr: In transitu, see Obiter.

units.la: Transmigrare, vid. Migrare.
units.tr: Transmigrare, see Migrare.

units.la: Transmittere] Transmittere exercitum. Dare transitum per agros. Dare iter alicui per provinciam, Liv.
units.tr: Transmittere: To send an army across. To give passage through the fields. To give someone a route through a province, Liv.

units.la: Transnare] Cic. Tranare aquas, Quint. Transnatare, Liv. Natatu transgredi flumen, Amm. Denatare alveo, Hor.
units.tr: Transnare: Cic. To swim across waters, Quint. To swim across, Liv. To cross a river by swimming, Amm. To swim across a channel, Hor.

units.la: Transplantare] Transferre, transducere arborem, Col. Transferere, Stat. Transferre plantam, Pallad. Semina è terra in terram, Var. Differre rutam, Col.
units.tr: Transplantare: To transfer or transplant a tree, Col. To transfer, Stat. To transfer a seedling, Pallad. To move seeds from earth to earth, Var. To transplant rue, Col.

units.la: Transponere] Trajicere in alia vasa aliquid, Var. Vid. Transferre.
units.tr: Transponere: To transfer something into other vessels, Var. See Transferre.

units.la: Tremens] Tremulus, tremebundus, Cic. Trepidus, Virg. Trepidulus, Plaut. Praetrepidus, Suet. Praetrepidans, Catul. Vibrans sonus, Plin. Vacillans, Cic.
units.tr: Tremens: Trembling, Cic. Trembling, Virg. Quivering, Plaut. Very trembling, Suet. Trembling exceedingly, Catul. A vibrating sound, Plin. Wavering, Cic.

units.la: Tremere] Tremiscere, Virg. Intremere, Intremiscere, Plin. Contremiscere. Trepidare, Cic. Circumtremere, Lucr. Attrepidare. Frigutire, Plaut. Tremefacta tellus, Virg. à Tremefio.
units.tr: Tremere: To quiver, Virg. To tremble within, Plin. To shudder, Cic. To shake all around, Lucr. To shiver, Plaut. The earth made to tremble, Virg., from Tremefio.

units.la: Tremulus] Tremula flamma, Cic. Nictantia lumina flammis, Lucr. i. Micantia, Vibrantia, Lamb.
units.tr: Tremulus: A trembling flame, Cic. Flickering lights with flames, Lucr. That is, shining, quivering, Lamb.

units.la: Trepidare, vid. Timere, tremere.
units.tr: Trepidare, see Timere, tremere.

units.la: Tribuere aliquid alicui, ut Auctori] Acceptum referre alicui, Cic. Accepto ferre, referre, IC. Decus alicujus rei ad aliquem trahere, Liv. Gratiam recte factorum sibi tribuere, Tac. Transfundere ad alium laudes &c. Assumere sibi aliquid. Addicere aliquid alicui. Proprium aliquid alicui tradere. Assignare aliquid homini, sceleri, misericordiae, fortunae, civitati. Mihi salutem imperii adjudicavit, Cic. Transmovere in se verbis gloriam alieno labore partam, Ter. Affingere alicui vitium, Lucr. Damnare aliquem tarditatis, Quint. Sordium, Plin.Jun. Eam mihi debeo gratiam atque animo meo. Plaut. Crimen in aliquem ultro fateri, Suet. Vid. Imputare.
units.tr: Tribuere aliquid alicui, as to the author: To refer something to someone as received, Cic. To carry to someone's account, IC. To attribute the honour of a thing to someone, Liv. To claim for oneself the credit for right deeds, Tac. To transfer praises to another. To assume something for oneself. To assign something to someone. To hand over something proper to someone. To assign something to a man, a crime, pity, fortune, a state. He adjudged to me the safety of the empire, Cic. To transfer to oneself by words the glory won by another's labour, Ter. To attach a fault to someone, Lucr. To condemn someone for slowness, Quint. For filth, Plin. Jun. I owe that favour to myself and to my own mind, Plaut. To freely confess a crime against someone, Suet. See Imputare.

units.la: Tribulare, vid. Triturare.
units.tr: Tribulare, see Triturare.

units.la: Tribunal] Forum judiciale totius regni. Subsellia judicum. Forum, Cic. Forus, Isid. Consistorium, Amm. Jus, Ter.
units.tr: Tribunal: The judicial seat of the whole kingdom. Seats of judges. Forum, Cic. Forus, Isid. Consistory, Amm. Law, Ter.

units.la: Tribunus] Curio, Cic. Magister curiae, Plaut. Xetæriarcha, Bud. Præfectus sodalitio. Tribuum magister, Henr. Steph.
units.tr: Tribunus: Curio, Cic. Master of the curia, Plaut. Xetariarch, Bud. Prefect of a fellowship. Master of the tribes, Henr. Steph.

units.la: Tribus] Collegium. Sodalitium & sodalitas, Cic. Curia, Plaut. Corpus, Lampr.
units.tr: Tribus: Corporation. Fellowship and brotherhood, Cic. Curia, Plaut. Body, Lampr.

units.la: Tributarius] Munificum prædium, i. publicæ functioni & vectigalis collationi subditum, Bud. ex Paul. IC.
units.tr: Tributarius: A munificent estate, that is, subject to public service and the collection of tax, Bud. from Paul the jurist.

units.la: Tributum] Vectigal. Census, Cic. Publicum, Suet. Indictio, Plin.Jun. Canon in constit. Imperatoriis.
units.tr: Tributum: Tax. Census, Cic. Public levy, Suet. Imposition, Plin. Jun. Canon in the imperial constitutions.

units.la: Tributum solvere] Pendere tributum, Ovid. Conferre tributum. Pendere vectigal, Cic.
units.tr: Tributum solvere: To pay tribute, Ovid. To contribute tribute. To pay a tax, Cic.

units.la: Tributa exigere] Censum habere, Cic. Agere, Liv. Censere, Spart.
units.tr: Tributa exigere: To hold the census, Cic. To drive, Liv. To assess, Spart.

units.la: Tributorum exactor] Exactor, Liv. Coactor pecuniae publicæ, Cic. Fiscalium præstationum exactor, Firm. Custos, Cic. Antigrapheus, & Antigrapharius, Bud. Decaprotus, Modest.
units.tr: Tributorum exactor: Collector, Liv. Compeller of public money, Cic. Collector of fiscal dues, Firm. Guardian, Cic. Antigrapheus and Antigrapharius, Bud. Decaprotus, Modest.

units.la: Tricliniarcha] Triclinarius, Fulv. Vrs. Vid. Structor.
units.tr: Tricliniarcha: Triclinarius, Fulv. Ursin. See Structor.

units.la: Triclinium] Diæta hypocausta, Vlp. Triclinarium, Var. Tricliniarium, aliqui. Conclave, Cic. Vid. Cænaculum.
units.tr: Triclinium: A heated dining room, Ulp. Triclinarium, Var. Tricliniarium, some authors. A chamber, Cic. See Cenaculum.

units.la: Tripudiare] Gestire, Abs. & Gestire lætitiâ, voluptate. Exsultare lætitiâ, Cic. Ludere exsultim, Hor.
units.tr: Tripudiare: To exult, Abs., and to exult with joy or pleasure. To rejoice greatly, Cic. To play by leaping about, Hor.

units.la: Tripudiatio ] Tripudium. Solennis saltatus, Liv. Exsultatio, Plin. Exsultantia, Gell.
units.tr: Tripudiatio: Tripudium. A solemn dance, Liv. Exultation, Plin. Exultation, Gell.

units.la: Tristari] Angi mœrore. Intimis sensibus. Lacrymis ac tristitiæ te tradidisti, Cic. Contristari, Col. Tabescere luctu. Ægrescit animus, Lucr. Ægrè est mihi, Plaut. Affici, opprimi ægritudine. Dedere se totum ægritudini. Esse in ægritudine. Tangit aliquem ægritudo, Cic.
units.tr: Tristari: To be pained with grief, to the innermost feelings. You gave yourself over to tears and sadness, Cic. To be saddened, Col. To waste away with grief. The mind sickens, Lucr. I am sick at heart, Plaut. To be affected, overwhelmed by sorrow. To give oneself wholly to sorrow. To be in sorrow. Sorrow touches someone, Cic.

units.la: Tristis] Tristis frons, Tibul. Tristiculus, Pertristis, Cic. Æger animus: Ægrum cor, Quint. Lugubris vox, Lucr. Luctuosum tempus: perluctuosum. Funesta vox, Cic. Vid. Mæstus.
units.tr: Tristis: A sad brow, Tibul. Somewhat sad, very sad, Cic. A sick mind; a sick heart, Quint. A mournful voice, Lucr. A mournful time; very mournful. A deadly voice, Cic. See Maestus.

units.la: Non semper tristia] Neptunus non semper nautas exercet.
units.tr: Non semper tristia: Neptune does not always trouble the sailors.

units.la: Tristitia] Tristities, Apul. Tristitias, atis Pacuv. Tristitudo, Apul. Senium, Cic. Contractio animi in dolore, Id.
units.tr: Tristitia: Sadness, Apul. Sadness, Pacuv. Sadness, Apul. Old age, Cic. The contraction of the mind in grief, Id.

units.la: Triticum] Robus, (bi. n.) Col.
units.tr: Triticum: Robus, (bi. n.) Col.

units.la: Triturare] Tribulare, Cato. Terere fruges, Virg. Flagellare frumentum perticis, Plin. Tundere, Col. Cudere fabam. Frumenta deterere, baculis excutere, exterere pecudibus, Id. Expinsere far, Cat.
units.tr: Triturare: To thresh, Cato. To tread out grain, Virg. To beat grain with poles, Plin. To pound, Col. To beat beans. To thresh grain with sticks, to drive out with cattle, Col. To pound spelt, Cato.

units.la: Tritus, us] Tritu aurum perpolitum, Plin. Fricatus. Attritus, Plin. Allisio digitorum, Spart. Conflictio corporum, Quint. Conflictus lapidum, nubium, Cic. Collisus margaritarum. Plin. Intrigo, & Intertrigo, Var.
units.tr: Tritus, us: Gold polished by rubbing, Plin. Rubbed, worn down, Plin. A striking of the fingers, Spart. A collision of bodies, Quint. A collision of stones or clouds, Cic. A rubbing together of pearls, Plin. Chafing and inter-chafing, Var.

units.la: Triumphalis] Triumphalis via, vehiculum, Cic. Vestis, currus, Plin. Ovalis corona, Gell. Palmaris statua, sententia, Cic. Palmarius, Ter. Quod mihi duco palmarium. Victrix laurus, Virg. Victrix palma, Ovid. Victoriosus, Gell. Victorialis dies, Iul. Cap.
units.tr: Triumphalis: A triumphal way, a triumphal vehicle, Cic. A triumphal garment or chariot, Plin. An oval crown, Gell. A palmary statue, a palmary sentence, Cic. Palmarius, Ter. Which I count as my palm of victory. Victorious laurel, Virg. Victorious palm, Ovid. Victorious, Gell. Day of victory, Iul. Cap.

units.la: Triumphare] Triumphare de aliquo. Triumphum agere, habere, deportare. Ducere per triumphum, Cic. In triumpho, Plin. Ducere triumphum ex, Id. Triumphare aliquem, Plin.I. Ovare: ovans descendit in Capitolium, Cic. Ovantes, lætantes.
units.tr: Triumphare: To triumph over someone. To hold, have, or bring home a triumph. To lead in triumph, Cic. In triumph, Plin. To lead a triumph from, Id. To triumph over someone, Plin. To ovate: he went up to the Capitol in an ovation, Cic. Exulting, rejoicing.

units.la: Triumphus ] Triumphatus, Plin. Triumphalia, pl. Tac. Pompa, Cic. Ovatio (apud Rom. Triumphus minus solennis) Gell. Ovatus, Val. Arg.
units.tr: Triumphus: A triumph, Plin. Triumphal rites, Tac. A procession, Cic. An ovation (among the Romans a less solemn triumph), Gell. An ovation, Val. Arg.

units.la: Trucidare aliquem] Omni supplicio excruciatum necare, Cic. Percruciatum interficere aliquem, Cef. Ardescere jussit mucrorem, Tac. Laceratosque omnibus, quae corpus ullum pati potest, supplicis interfecit, Liv. Mactare aliquem supplicio. Omni supplicio interfici. Fame, cruciatu, supplicioque periit, Cic. A quibus hic multis acceptis, ac debilitato corpore & contrucidato, se abjecit exanimatus, Cic.
units.tr: Trucidare aliquem: To kill someone after tormenting him with every punishment, Cic. To put someone to death with extreme torture, Caes. He ordered the sword to be made red-hot, Tac. And having mangled the captives in every way the body can endure, he killed them, Liv. To slaughter someone with punishment. To be killed by every kind of punishment. He perished by hunger, torture and punishment, Cic. Having received many blows from these men, his body weakened and mangled, he threw himself down lifeless, Cic.

units.la: Trucidatio] Laniationes hominum, Sen. Laniatus. Carnificina, Cic.
units.tr: Trucidatio: Mangling of men, Sen. Mangling. Butchery, Cic.

units.la: Truculentus, vid. Crudelis.
units.tr: Truculentus, see Crudelis.

units.la: Trudere] Protrudere molem, Lucr. Agere aliquem praecipitem. Impellere naves. Urgere jacentes, Cic. Propellere, Col. Propellens alium prae se, Lucr. Adurgere aliquid, Celf. Subigere ratem conto, Virg.
units.tr: Trudere: To thrust forward a mass, Lucr. To drive someone headlong. To push ships. To press upon the fallen, Cic. To propel, Col. Propelling another before oneself, Lucr. To press hard upon something, Celsus. To drive a boat with a pole, Virg.

units.la: Truncare] Praecidere manum, Cic. Praesecare partem aliquam (corporis). Abscindere humerum. Recidere, Ovid. Desecare, rescindere vitem, Col. Vid. Decollare. Mutilare.
units.tr: Truncare: To cut off a hand, Cic. To cut away some part (of the body). To cut off a shoulder. To cut off, Ovid. To lop off or cut back a vine, Col. See Decollare. Mutilare.

units.la: Truncatio] Amputatio. Praecisio. Abscissio, Cic.
units.tr: Truncatio: Amputation. Cutting off. Excision, Cic.

units.la: Truncatus] Trunca manus, Propert. Vid. Mutilatus.
units.tr: Truncatus: A maimed hand, Propert. See Mutilatus.

units.la: Truncus, vid. Caudex.
units.tr: Truncus, see Caudex.

units.la: Trutina, vid. Libra &c.
units.tr: Trutina, see Libra &c.

units.la: Trux, vid. Crudelis.
units.tr: Trux, see Cruel.

units.la: Tu, tua dominatio. vulgo] Prisci Latini unum compellantes simpliciter dicebant: Tu, tibi, te, sive illustris persona erat. Addebant aliquando: Mi dulcissime Tiro, Cic. Lucilii virorum optime, Sen. Ergo satis Latine dices: Vir prudentissime, nobilissime, clarissime. Princeps illustris, clementissime. Sanctissime Imperator, Trebel. Imperator optime, providentissime, Plin. Invicte, Veget &c. Alter modus: Tua clementia, indulgentia, pietas, det, concedat, Plin. Iun. Etiam Latinus est. Tertius adhuc modus est, cum dicimus. Domine. absol. Tu quidem Domine providentissime vereris, ne &c. Plin. Iun. (Audiat reverentia sua, dicat dominatio sua. Item: Dicat, audiat Dominus, minus, pro dic, audi Domine; Triviales & inepte apud imperitos locutiones sunt: Siquidem ad tertiam personam, non ad secundam diriguntur.
units.tr: Tu, your lordship. Commonly The early Latins, when addressing one person, simply said: tu, tibi, te, whether the person was of high rank. They sometimes added: my dearest Tiro, Cic.; best of men, Lucilius, Sen. So you will speak good Latin if you say: most prudent, most noble, most distinguished man; illustrious prince, most merciful; most holy Emperor, Trebel.; best and most provident Emperor, Plin.; unconquered one, Veget. etc. Another manner: your clemency, indulgence, piety, grant, concede, Plin. Iun. It is also Latin. There is a third manner, when we say: Lord, absolutely: You indeed, most provident Lord, fear lest etc., Plin. Iun. (Let your reverence hear, let your lordship say.) Likewise: let the Lord say, let him hear, (minus, for "say", "hear, Lord"). These are trivial and foolish expressions among the unskilled, since they are addressed to the third person, not the second.

units.la: Tuba, tubâ canere, vid. Buccina &c
units.tr: Tuba, to sound a trumpet, see Trumpet &c.

units.la: Tuber] Callus terrae.
units.tr: Tuber] A hard lump of the earth.

units.la: Tuberosus ] Tuberosissimæ frontis homo, Petron. Tuber est totum caput colaphis, (id est, instar tuberis) Ter. Tumidum & turgidum membrum vitiosè habet, Cic. Turgiduli ocelli, Catul.
units.tr: Tuberosus] A man with a very knobbly forehead, Petron. A tuber is a head entirely struck with blows (that is, like a lump), Ter. He has a swollen and bloated limb, Cic. Little swollen eyes, Catul.

units.la: Tubicen, vid. Buccinator.
units.tr: Tubicen, see Trumpeter.

units.la: Tuburcinari, vid. Vorare.
units.tr: Tuburcinari, see Devour.

units.la: Tubus opticus] Fistula visoria. Telescopium; Dioptra.
units.tr: Tubus opticus] A seeing tube: a telescope; a dioptra.

units.la: Tueri, vid. Defendere. Spectare.
units.tr: Tueri, see Defend. Look at.

units.la: Tugurium, vid. Casa.
units.tr: Tugurium, see Cottage.

units.la: Tum ] Erat tunc excusatio, Cic. Per id tempus, Cæs. Per illa tempora, Liv. Tunc temporis, Justin. Eodem vestigio temporis. Id temporis, Cicer. Per idem tempus, Id.
units.tr: Tum] There was tunc as an excuse, Cic. At that time, Caes. In those times, Liv. At that very time, Justin. At the same moment of time. At that time, Cic. In the same period, Id.

units.la: Tum-tum ] Amici me partim defuerunt, partim prodiderunt. Omnes simul spernebant, simul metuebant, Cic. Parte flavus, parte melleus, Plin. Interrogatio in parte expeditior, in parte difficilior, Quint. Milites pars fiducia, pars dolore, Tac.
units.tr: Tum-tum] My friends partly failed me, partly betrayed me. All at once despised, at once feared, Cic. Partly yellow, partly honey-coloured, Plin. A question is in part easier, in part more difficult, Quint. Soldiers, partly with confidence, partly with grief, Tac.

units.la: Tumere ] Tumescit meto, Cic. Turgere, Ovid. Vid. Intumescere.
units.tr: Tumere] The crop swells, Cic. To swell, Ovid. See Swell up.

units.la: Tumidus] Tumens, Virg. Turgidum membrum. Extuberatus venter, Amm. Sufflata cutis, Plin. Inflatum collum, Ovid.
units.tr: Tumidus] Swelling, Virg. A swollen limb. A distended belly, Amm. Puffed-up skin, Plin. A swollen neck, Ovid.

units.la: Tumor] Tumiditas, Firm. Inflatio ventris, Col. Extuberatio, Plin. Torus venarum, Cels. Sufflatio, Plin. Contabulatio laciniæ, Apul. Flemina in genubus, Plaut.
units.tr: Tumor] Swelling, Firm. Distension of the belly, Col. Protuberance, Plin. A knot of veins, Cels. Puffing up, Plin. Folding of a garment's hem, Apul. Swellings on the knees, Plaut.

units.la: Tumulare, vid. Humare.
units.tr: Tumulare, see Bury.

units.la: Tumultuarie] Turbulente, raptim, temerè agere. Mobiliter, Cæs. Vid. Raptim.
units.tr: Tumultuarie] To act in a disorderly, hasty and rash manner. Tumultuously, Caes. See Hastily.

units.la: Tumultuari] Trepido tumultu concutere omnia, Lucr. Rebellare, Cæs. Ovid. Turbare, abs. Tac. Tragœdias excitare, Cic.
units.tr: Tumultuari] To shake everything with a trembling uproar, Lucr. To rebel, Caes., Ovid. To disturb, absolutely, Tac. To stir up tragedies, Cic.

units.la: Tumultuari ob levicula] In nugis tragœdias agere.
units.tr: Tumultuari ob levicula] To act out tragedies over trifles.

units.la: Tumultuarius, vid. Subitaneus.
units.tr: Tumultuarius, see Sudden.

units.la: Tumultus] Tumultuatio. Turba, Cic. Motus temerarius. Srepitus forensis, Id. Tempestas popularis: pacis, discordiarum. Tragœdia. Vndæ comitionum. Tenebræ Reip. Nox, caligo animis offusa, Id.
units.tr: Tumultus] Uproar. A crowd, Cic. A rash movement. The din of the forum, Id. A popular storm: of peace, of discords. A tragedy. The waves of elections. The darkness of the state. A night, a mist poured over the minds, Id.

units.la: Tumultus ex re insperatâ] Negotium ex otio.
units.tr: Tumultus arising from an unexpected matter] Business out of idleness.

units.la: Tumulus, vid. Collis, Sepulchrum.
units.tr: Tumulus, see Hill, Tomb.

units.la: Tunc, vid. Tum.
units.tr: Tunc, see Then.

units.la: Tundere] Quatere fundamenta, Virg. Contundere pilis ferreis. Obterere, Col. Vid. Supplodere.
units.tr: Tundere] To shake the foundations, Virg. To beat with iron clubs. To crush, Col. See Stamp.

units.la: Turba] Frequentia hominum. Fluctus barbariæ. Celebritas, Cic. Stipatio hominum, Plin. Iun. Vndas salutantum vomit domus, Virg. Turbula, Apul.
units.tr: Turba] A crowd of people. The surging of the rabble. A throng, Cic. A press of people, Plin. Iun. The house pours forth waves of greeters, Virg. A small crowd, Apul.

units.la: Turbas ciere ob res leves] Fluctus movere in simpulo.
units.tr: Turbas ciere ob res leves] To stir up waves in a cup (to make a storm in a teacup).

units.la: Turbare] Facere turbas, Plaut. Perturbationem, Cæs. Motus, Liv. Miscere Remp. Permiscere Græciam. Perturbare. Tument negotia, Cic. Excitare motus, Liv. Conturbare rationes, Ter. Novis rebus studere. Inconciliare copias, Plaut.
units.tr: Turbare] To make disturbances, Plaut. Disorder, Caes. Commotions, Liv. To throw the state into confusion. To throw Greece into turmoil. To perturb. Affairs are in turmoil, Cic. To excite commotions, Liv. To confound plans, Ter. To strive after revolution. To break up forces, Plaut.

units.la: Turbare omnia] Miscere cœlo terram, terræ cœlum, Liv. Maria omnia cœlo miscere, Virg. Dextra lævis transmutare, Lucr. Miscere sacra profanis.
units.tr: Turbare omnia] To mix earth with heaven and heaven with earth, Liv. To mix all seas with the sky, Virg. To change right into left, Lucr. To mix sacred things with profane.

units.la: Turbari] Perturbantur animi aliquorum: Vid. Perturb. transfer.
units.tr: Turbari] The minds of some people are disturbed: see Perturbation, transferred sense.

units.la: Turbatè, vid. Inordinatè.
units.tr: Turbatè, see Disorderly.

units.la: Turbatio] Perturbatio. Motus animi nimius. Conturbatio animum sanitate spoliat. Turbidi animi concitatique motus. Turbida mens, Cic. Æstus mentis, Lucr. Confusio, Val.Max. Confusionem in vultu gerere.
units.tr: Turbatio] Perturbation. Excessive motion of the mind. Confusion robs the mind of sanity. Agitated and disturbed movements of the mind. A troubled mind, Cic. The heat of the mind, Lucr. Confusion, Val. Max. To show confusion in one's face.

units.la: Turbator, vid. Factiosus.
units.tr: Turbator, see Factious.

units.la: Turbatur] Perturbatur animi motus. Turbidus & concitatus animus, homo. Offensus, offensior animus. Turbulenta res, Cic. Turbidus animi, Tac. Turbidissimæ actiones, Quint. Tactus dolore, Tac.
units.tr: Turbatur] The motion of the mind is disturbed. A man with a troubled and agitated mind. An offended and more offended mind. A turbulent affair, Cic. A troubled state of mind, Tac. Most troubled actions, Quint. Touched by grief, Tac.

units.la: Turbidè] Turbulentè, turbulenter, perturbatè, Cic. Tumultuariè, Amm.
units.tr: Turbidè] Turbulently, perturbedly, Cic. Tumultuously, Amm.

units.la: Turbidus] Turbida aqua, Lucr. Fæcatum vinum, Cat. Infuscata aqua, Plin.
units.tr: Turbidus] Turbid water, Lucr. Wine full of lees, Cat. Darkened water, Plin.

units.la: Turbo] Procella vehemens è nube repente erumpens, Ecnephias. Typhon, Plin. Turbo versabundus, violentus, Lucr. Aërei fluminis vortex.
units.tr: Turbo] A violent storm bursting suddenly from a cloud, an ecnephias. A typhoon, Plin. A whirling, violent whirlwind, Lucr. The eddy of an airy river.

units.la: Turbulenter, vid. Inordinatè.
units.tr: Turbulenter, see Disorderly.

units.la: Turbulentus, vid. Procellosus.
units.tr: Turbulentus, see Stormy.

units.la: Turgens] Tumentes pedes, Virg. Cadaverosa facies, (i.pulposa, crassa, & qs. carnosa) Donat. Turneb.
units.tr: Turgens] Swollen feet, Virg. A cadaverous face (that is, pulpy, thick, and so to speak fleshy), Donat., Turneb.

units.la: Turgere] Obturgere, Lucil. Inflari, Cic. Vid. Intumescere.
units.tr: Turgere] To swell up, Lucil. To be inflated, Cic. See Swell up.

units.la: Turgidus] Tumidum & turgidum membrum, Cic. Turgiduli ocelli, Catul. Invaserunt misero in genua flumina, Plaut. Intumuisse genas, Ovid.
units.tr: Turgidus] A swollen limb, Cic. Little swollen eyes, Catul. Rivers rushed upon his wretched knees, Plaut. Swollen cheeks, Ovid.

units.la: Turio] Est novissima pars surculi, quæ longius à matre prosiliit, & acumine attenuata est, inutilis ad deponendum (i.e. ad serendum.) Unguis palmitis, Col. Pullus arboris, Cat. Excrescentia cacumina arborum. Sagitta. Unguis arboris, Plin. Colis, Coliculus, Var. Festuca, Col. Vittulamen, Sap. 4.
units.tr: Turio] The last part of a shoot, which springs out farther from the mother stem and is thinned at the tip, useless for planting (that is, for sowing). The bud of a vine shoot, Col. A young shoot of a tree, Cat. Growing tips of trees. An arrow. The nail of a tree, Plin. A little stalk, Var. A stalk of straw, Col. A little rag, Sap. 4.

units.la: Turma] Alæ equitum, Veget. Alarii equites, apud Livium.
units.tr: Turma] Wings of cavalry, Veget. Cavalry of the wings, in Livy.

units.la: Turmatim] Cuneatim, Caf. Centuriatim, Non. Manipulatim structa acies, Liv.
units.tr: Turmatim] In wedges, Caes. By centuries, Non. An army drawn up by maniples, Liv.

units.la: Turpis] Turpitudine notabilis, Tac. In turpissimis habetur, Caf. Fœdus amor, Ovid. Immanis soloecismus, Gell. Vid. Fœdus. Deformis.
units.tr: Turpis] Notable for its baseness, Tac. Held among the most shameful things, Caes. Foul love, Ovid. A monstrous solecism, Gell. See Foul. Deformed.

units.la: Turpe est turpe, seu latens, seu patens] Turpe quid acturus, te sine teste time.
units.tr: Turpe est turpe, whether hidden or open] If you are about to do something shameful, fear yourself as the witness, whether the deed is hidden or open.

units.la: Turpiter] Sordidè dicere, conciotari. Inquinatè loqui. Inelegantèr dividere, Cic. Deformiter sonat, Quint. Indignè oppidum captum. Indignissimè eripere. Per ignaviam & dedecus vivere, Cic. Fœdè admissum, Lucr. Turpius ejicitur, quàm non admittitur hospes, Ovid. Sordidè gessit Consulatum, Plin. Iun. Causa agetur foedissimè, Cic.
units.tr: Turpiter] To speak meanly, to chatter. To speak in a defiling way. To divide inelegantly, Cic. It sounds ugly, Quint. A town taken shamefully. To snatch away unworthily. To live in idleness and disgrace, Cic. Committed basely, Lucr. A guest is driven out more shamefully than one who is not admitted, Ovid. He held the consulship in a squalid way, Plin. Iun. The case will be pleaded most foully, Cic.

units.la: Turpitudo] Obscœnitas verborum. Flagitium in obscœniscœnitate. Deformitas fugæ. Fœditas animi. Labes turpitudinis. Indignitas. Impuritas, Cic.
units.tr: Turpitudo] Obscenity of words. Shame in obscenity. Ugliness of flight. Foulness of mind. Stain of baseness. Unworthiness. Impurity, Cic.

units.la: Tussire] Tussi edita sputa, Lucr. Emoliri aliquid tussi. ex Cels. Extussire pus, Id. Purulenta, Plin.
units.tr: Tussire] Spittle brought up by coughing, Lucr. To soften something by coughing, from Cels. To cough up pus, Id. Purulent, Plin.

units.la: Tussis] Tussicula, Plin. Tussedo, Apul.
units.tr: Tussis] A slight cough, Plin. A hacking cough, Apul.

units.la: Tute, vid. Secure.
units.tr: Tute, see Securely.

units.la: Tutela, i. e. defensio] Tutamen, Virg. Arx. Leges sunt arx, Cic. In fide alicujus esse, Ter. Præsidium innocentiæ, in virtute, Cic. Patrocinium orbis terræ potius, quàm imperium poterat nominari, Id. Propugnaculum senectutis, societas hominum, Id.
units.tr: Tutela, that is, defence] A shelter, Virg. A citadel. Laws are a citadel, Cic. To be in someone's trust, Ter. A safeguard of innocence, found in virtue, Cic. Patronage of the whole world could be called rather than rule, Id. A bulwark of old age, a fellowship of men, Id.

units.la: Tutela, al. vid. Clientela.
units.tr: Tutela, other reading, see Clientship.

units.la: Tutor] Curator pupilli, Vlp. Patronus, Bud. Compatronus, & Contutor. Vlp.
units.tr: Tutor] Guardian of a ward, Ulp. Patron, Bud. Co-patron and co-guardian, Ulp.

units.la: Tutorem esse] Perf. Gerere tutelam alicujus, Plaut. Administrare tutelam, Vlp. Habere tutelam regni.
units.tr: Tutorem esse] Perfect tense. To hold the guardianship of someone, Plaut. To administer a guardianship, Ulp. To hold the guardianship of a kingdom.

units.la: Tutus] Tutus ab, a. Tutus ad omnes ictus, Liv. Tutus adversus pericula, Cels. Securus abs, à metu, Plin. Iun. Innoxius à, Col. Immunis sagittarum periculo, Amm. Vacuus periculo, Tac. Extra periculum est. Abest à periculo, Cic. Defecato animo, Plaut. Ancoris duabus fultus.
units.tr: Tutus] Safe from. Safe against every blow, Liv. Safe against dangers, Cels. Free from fear of, Plin. Iun. Unharmed by, Col. Immune to the danger of arrows, Amm. Free from danger, Tac. Out of danger. Far from danger, Cic. With a cleansed mind, Plaut. Supported by two anchors.

units.la: In tuto esse, vid. Securum esse.
units.tr: In tuto esse, see To be safe.

units.la: Tutiora eligere] Circa terram navigare.
units.tr: Tutiora eligere] To sail close to the land.

units.la: Tympanista] Tympanotriba, Plaut.
units.tr: Tympanista] A drummer, Plaut.

units.la: Tympaniȝare] Suet. Tympana pulsare, tundere, Ovid.
units.tr: Tympaniȝare] Suet. To beat drums, to strike the tambourine, Ovid.

units.la: Tympanum] Tympaniolum, Arnob. Symphonia, Isid. Bronteum, Cæl.
units.tr: Tympanum] A little drum, Arnob. A symphony, Isid. A thunder-stone, Cael.

units.la: Typographus] Impressor, Hermol. Excusor, vox Quint. Bibliographus, Scal. Librarius, ex Cic.
units.tr: Typographus] A printer, Hermol. Printer, a word from Quint. A bibliographer, Scal. A bookseller, from Cic.

units.la: Tyrannice] Tyrannorum more, Cic. Affectare tyrannidem, Quint. Vid. Crudeliter.
units.tr: Tyrannice] In the manner of tyrants, Cic. To aspire to tyranny, Quint. See Cruelly.

units.la: Tyrannis] Cruentum regimen, Stat. Oppressio libertatis & legum, Cic. Phalaridis imperium. Ratio non prodest, ubi vis imperat.
units.tr: Tyrannis] A bloody rule, Stat. The oppression of liberty and laws, Cic. The rule of Phalaris. Reason is no help where force commands.

units.la: Tyrannus, solus omnia regere quarens] Draco non esset draco, nisi alios devorasset serpentes, Draco non fiet serpens, pens, ni edat serpentem. Caesare & Julio Consulibus, Proverb.
units.tr: Tyrannus, seeking to rule everything alone] A dragon would not be a dragon unless it had devoured other serpents; a dragon will not become a serpent unless it eats a serpent. In the consulship of Caesar and Julius. Proverb.

units.la: Tyranni timendi & timidi] Quem multi timent, necesse estmultos timeat.
units.tr: Tyrants to be feared and fearful] He whom many fear must necessarily fear many.

units.la: U.
units.tr: U.

units.la: Uber] Ubertus. Gell. Uberrimus, Virg. Vid. Fertilis.
units.tr: Uber (fertile): abundant, Gell.; most fertile, Virg. See Fertile.

units.la: Ubera] Uber, Virg. Fontem illum sanctissimum corporis, humani generis educatorem, vocat Gell.
units.tr: Ubera (udders, breasts): Uber, Virg. Gell. calls that most sacred fountain of the body, the nurturer of the human race.

units.la: Ubertas, vid. Fertilitas. Copia.
units.tr: Ubertas (abundance): see Fertility; Plenty.

units.la: Ubertim, vid. Copiose.
units.tr: Ubertim: see Copiously.

units.la: Ubi?] Ubi gentium? Ubi loci est? Plaut. Ubi terrarum?
units.tr: Ubi? (where?): Where in the world? Where is the place? Plaut. Where on earth?

units.la: Ubi, sine interr.] Usquam, uspiam, alicubi, Cic. Ut, pro ubi: Ut quisque steterat, jacet, Plaut.
units.tr: Ubi, without an interrogative: anywhere, somewhere, Cic. Ut, for ubi: as each had stood, so he lies, Plaut.

units.la: Ubi fuero liber à curis] Ubi his malis emersero. Ubi ex his negotiis me expedivero, ubi his e nugis me excussero. Cum ex his negotiorum labyrinthis evolavero. Simul atque his me tumultibus exsolvero. Si quando licebit, memet ex negotiorum his fluctibus emoliri. Si licebit ab his curis discedere. Si continget liberari, levari. Si quando ab his negotiis me ipsum vindicavero, Eras.
units.tr: Ubi fuero liber a curis (when I shall be free from cares): When I have emerged from these troubles; when I have extricated myself from these affairs and shaken myself free of these trifles; when I have flown out of these labyrinths of business; as soon as I am released from these tumults; if ever it is permitted me to struggle out of these waves of business; if I may withdraw from these cares; if I am at last freed and relieved; if ever I shall have reclaimed myself from these affairs, Erasmus.

units.la: Ubicunque] Ubicunque gentium, terrarum sunt. Ubi ubi, Cic. Ubi ubi gentium. Quaqua tangit, amburit, Plaut. Ubilibet, Sipont. Quovis cunque loco, Mart. Alicubi, Cic. Utcunque mecum vos eritis, Hor.
units.tr: Ubicunque (wherever): wherever in the world, on earth, they are. Ubi ubi, Cic. Wherever in the world. Wherever it touches, it burns, Plaut. Ubilibet, Sipont. Wherever you like, Mart. Somewhere, Cic. However it is with me, you will be there, Hor.

units.la: Ubique] Ubivis. Passim vagantur. Terra, marique perquirere aliquem. Omnibus vestigiis indagare aliquem. Omnibus locis, usquequaque, Cic. Plaut. Nullibi non, quà libet, Catul.
units.tr: Ubique (everywhere): everywhere; they wander about everywhere. To seek someone by land and sea. To track someone by every trace. In all places, everywhere, Cic., Plaut. Nowhere not, wherever one pleases, Catul.

units.la: Ubique mediocritas tutissima] Disce modum servare. Alieno discere periculo.
units.tr: Ubique mediocritas tutissima (moderation is safest everywhere): Learn to keep measure. Learn at another's peril.

units.la: Udare, udus, vid. Humectare, Humidus.
units.tr: Udare, udus: see Moisten, Moist.

units.la: Ulcisci] Ulciscor injuriam, Cic. Ulciscor me ab aliquo, Plaut. Persequi alicujus injuriam. Persequi ab aliquo poenas judicio, Cic. Vindicare mortem alicujus, Plin. Se ab aliquo, Sen. Expiare injurias, Liv. Mactare aliquem ultioni, Tac.
units.tr: Ulcisci (to avenge): I avenge a wrong, Cic. I take vengeance on someone, Plaut. To pursue someone's wrong. To pursue penalties from someone by judgement, Cic. To claim vengeance for someone's death, Plin. To avenge oneself on someone, Sen. To expiate wrongs, Liv. To deliver someone up to vengeance, Tac.

units.la: Ulcisцitur Deus] Deus habet vindicem oculum.
units.tr: Ulciscitur Deus (God avenges): God has an avenging eye.

units.la: Ulcus, vid. Hulcus.
units.tr: Ulcus: see Ulcer.

units.la: Uliginosa terra] Glutinosa, Col. Solum tenax, Plin.
units.tr: Uliginosa terra (marshy land): sticky ground, Col. Ground that holds fast, Plin.

units.la: Uligo] Naturalis humor terrae, Serv. Marga, Plin. Locus uliginosus & palude stagnans.
units.tr: Uligo (moisture): the natural moisture of the earth, Serv. Marl, Plin. A place that is marshy and stagnant with swamp water.

units.la: Ulna] Cubitus, Cic. Cubitum. n. Plin. Sesquipes.
units.tr: Ulna (forearm, ell): a cubit, Cic.; a cubit, Plin.; a cubit and a half.

units.la: Ulterius] Ultrà progredi, quam, &c. Cic. Longius abire, Ter. Amplius, Virg. Porrectius tendere, Amm. Porrò ire pergas, Liv. Proporrò, Lucr. Sic porrò, Ovid.
units.tr: Ulterius (further): to go beyond, further than, &c., Cic. To go farther away, Ter. More, Virg. To stretch out further, Amm. To keep going forward, Liv. Onward, Lucr. Thus onward, Ovid.

units.la: Ultimò] Ultimum visuri domos, Liv. Novissimè, Postremò, Postremum, Cic. Supremò, Plin. Hic dies summus est apud me inopiæ accusatio, Plaut.
units.tr: Ultimo (at last): about to see their homes for the last time, Liv. Most recently, finally, lastly, Cic. Supremely, Plin. This day is the final reckoning of my poverty, Plaut.

units.la: Ultimus] Novissimus. In novissimis est. Extremus. Postremus, Cic. Summus, Virg. Supremus dies, Fest. Residuus. Reliquus, Cic. Claudit aciem, Sil. Extimus, Plin. Subsecivus, Apul.
units.tr: Ultimus (last): newest; among the last. Furthest, Cic. Last, Virg. The last day, Fest. Remaining, left over, Cic. Closing the battle line, Sil. Outermost, Plin. Spare, Apul.

units.la: Ultio] Vindicta, Ovid. Vindicatio, Cic. Adrastia, Amm. Nemesis, Id.
units.tr: Ultio (vengeance): avenging, Ovid. Vindication, Cic. Adrastia, Amm. Nemesis, Id.

units.la: Ultor] Vindex mali, Cic. Exsecutor inimicitiarum, Suet. Bis ultor (Mars) Ovid. Ultrix, Cic. Promptus ultioni, Tac. Qui ultionis cupidus est)
units.tr: Ultor (avenger): avenger of wrong, Cic. Executor of enmities, Suet. Twice an avenger (Mars), Ovid. Avenger (feminine), Cic. Ready for vengeance, Tac. (one eager for revenge).

units.la: Ultra] Super mediam noctem, Col. Extra modum. Cic. Amplius duobus millibus, Sallust. Justo longius, Quint. Media plus parte, Ovid. Ova non pauciora infra novena, Plin. Ex abundanti, Quint.
units.tr: Ultra (beyond): past midnight, Col. Beyond measure, Cic. More than two thousand, Sallust. Further than is just, Quint. More than half, Ovid. Eggs not fewer than nine, Plin. Over and above, Quint.

units.la: Ultrò, vid. Sponte.
units.tr: Ultro: see Willingly.

units.la: Ultrò oblata minus grata] Merx ultronea putet. Semper inhumanos habet officiosus amicos, Mart.
units.tr: Ultro oblata minus grata (what is offered unasked is less welcome): an unasked-for gift smells bad. An obliging man always has unkind friends, Mart.

units.la: Ululare] Exululare, Ovid.
units.tr: Ululare (to howl): to howl out, Ovid.

units.la: Umbræ pictorum] Reductoria in coloribus, Quint. Abscedentia in picturis, Vitr.
units.tr: Umbrae pictorum (painters' shadows): receding in colours, Quint. Receding in paintings, Vitr.

units.la: Umbraculum] Umbella. Velarium, Iuv. Cadurcum, Iun.
units.tr: Umbraculum (sunshade): a parasol; an awning, Juv.; Cadurcum, Iun.

units.la: Umbraticus homo] Murcus, (à Murcâ, Deâ ignavorum) Amm. Valtrin. Tectis ac tenebris continetur, Cic. Vid. Clanculatius. Domi desidere.
units.tr: Umbraticus homo (a man who lives in the shade): a lazybones (from Murcia, goddess of the idle), Amm., Valtrin. Kept within roofs and darkness, Cic. See Secretly; sit idle at home.

units.la: Umbrosus, vid. Opacus.
units.tr: Umbrosus: see Shady.

units.la: Unā]
units.tr: Unā] (catchword, no gloss)

units.la: Unâ] Unâ cum aliquo, Cic. Unâ inter se, Plaut. Uno fasce, Plin. Vid. Simul.
units.tr: Unā (together): together with someone, Cic. Together among themselves, Plaut. In one bundle, Plin. See At once.

units.la: Unâ opera duo perficere] Unâ fidelià duos dealbare parietes.
units.tr: Unā opera duo perficere (to accomplish two things with one work): with one brush to whitewash two walls.

units.la: Unanimis] Unanimus, Liv. Vid. Concors.
units.tr: Unanimis (of one mind): unanimous, Liv. See Harmonious.

units.la: Unanimitas] Studiorum magna consensio, Cic. Vid. Concordia.
units.tr: Unanimitas (unanimity): great agreement of pursuits, Cic. See Concord.

units.la: Unanimiter] Uno animo, Ter. Conjunctis sententiis. Consensu omnium.
units.tr: Unanimiter (unanimously): with one mind, Ter. With opinions joined together. By the consent of all.

units.la: Unctio] Unctura, Cic. Unctus, Apul. Inunctio, Perunctio, Litus, Plin. Suffectio unguentorum, Arnob. Celf.
units.tr: Unctio (anointing): anointing, Cic. Unction, Apul. Smearing in, rubbing on, Plin. Application of ointments, Arnob., Cels.

units.la: Unctus] Obunctì oculi, Apul. Delibutus, Cic.
units.tr: Unctus (anointed): eyes smeared over, Apul. Smeared, Cic.

units.la: Uncus] Uncinus, Sipont. Harpago, Plin. Unguis ferreus, Col. Dens anchorae, Virg.
units.tr: Uncus (hook): a little hook, Sipont. A grappling iron, Plin. An iron claw, Col. The tooth of an anchor, Virg.

units.la: Uncus, adj. vid. Aduncus.
units.tr: Uncus, adj.: see Hooked.

units.la: Unda] Fluctus, Cic. Fluctìculus, Apul. Moles, Stat.
units.tr: Unda (wave): a wave, Cic. A little wave, Apul. A mass of water, Stat.

units.la: Undare, vid. Inundare.
units.tr: Undare: see Inundate.

units.la: Unde] Unde gentium? Plaut. Qui bene sit, i.e. unde, Id. Qui genus? unde domo? Virg. Cujas, Cic. Cujatis, Plaut.
units.tr: Unde (whence?): whence in the world? Plaut. Who lives well, that is, whence? Id. Of what family, from what house? Virg. Whose? Cic. Whose (plural)? Plaut.

units.la: Unde cibus, inde venenum] Ægrotamus ex his, quibus vivimus.
units.tr: Unde cibus, inde venenum (the same food that nourishes can also poison): we fall sick from the very things by which we live.

units.la: Undecunque] Undelibet, ad Her. Alicunde. Aut terrâ, aut mari, Id.
units.tr: Undecunque (from whatever place): from wherever you like, ad Her. From somewhere. Either from land or from sea, Id.

units.la: Undique] Undiquesecus, undiqueversus-m, Sol. Hinc & illinc, Cic. Hinc inde, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Undique (from every side): from every side, every direction, Sol. On this side and that, Cic. From here and there, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Ungere] Inungere oculos, Plin. Perungere corpora, Cic. Superungere. Superinungere, Celf. Linere, illinere, Col. Pollincire, & Pollincere, Sen. Affricare membris unguedinem, Apul.
units.tr: Ungere (to anoint): to anoint the eyes, Plin. To smear the bodies all over, Cic. To anoint over, Cels. To smear on, Col. To rub grease into the limbs, Apul.

units.la: Ungues] Nubecula unguium, Iun. Excrementa manus, Lucan. Unguiculi.
units.tr: Ungues (nails): a little cloud of nails, Iun. The filth of the hand, Lucan. Little nails.

units.la: Ungula] Unguis bovis, Col. Cornu infimum bovis, Cat.
units.tr: Ungula (hoof): the claw of an ox, Col. The lowest horn of an ox, Cato.

units.la: Unicaulis] Unistirpis palma, unicalamus. In quibusdam omnino nullus ramus, Plin. Capitata vinea, Col. Opposita brachiata.
units.tr: Unicaulis (single-stemmed): a palm with a single trunk, a single stalk. In some there is no branch at all, Plin. A headed vine, Col. Opposite branches.

units.la: Unigenitus] Unigena, unicus filius, Cic. Ascanius. (unicus Æneæ filius.)
units.tr: Unigenitus (only-begotten): only-born, the only son, Cic. Ascanius (the only son of Aeneas).

units.la: Unio, vid. Magarita.
units.tr: Unio: see Pearl.

units.la: Universalis] Catholicus, Quint. OEcumenicus, Sipont. Generalis.
units.tr: Universalis (universal): catholic, Quint. Ecumenical, Sipont. General.

units.la: Uniusmodi] Uniformis, Macrob. Uno tenore est, Cicer. Unimodus, Apul. Unius generis, unis moribus, Cicer. Vid. Æqualis.
units.tr: Uniusmodi (of one kind): uniform, Macrob. Of one tenor, Cic. Of one measure, Apul. Of one kind and one manner, Cic. See Equal.

units.la: Uno verbo, vid. Breviter loqui.
units.tr: Uno verbo: see Speak briefly.

units.la: Unoculus, vid. Cocles.
units.tr: Unoculus (one-eyed): see One-eyed (Cocles).

units.la: Unquam, vid. Quando.
units.tr: Unquam: see When.

units.la: Unus] Unus ex, de, multis, Cic. Unus multorum, Hor. Singulus, Non. Solus ex collegio, Cic.
units.tr: Unus (one): one of many, Cic. One of many, Hor. Single, Non. The only one of the college, Cic.

units.la: Uni omnia ne committas] Ne uni navi facultates. Mus non uni fidit antro. Mus miser est antro qui saltem clauditur uno.
units.tr: Uni omnia ne committas (do not entrust everything to one): do not trust all your goods to one ship. The mouse does not trust itself to one hole. Wretched is the mouse that has at least one hole to shut it in.

units.la: Unus non potest, quod multi] Unus vir haud cernit omnia. Unus vir, nullus vir, unus nullus.
units.tr: Unus non potest quod multi (one cannot do what many can): one man does not see everything. One man, no man; one, nobody.

units.la: Uno instrumento, vid. Una opera.
units.tr: Uno instrumento: see One work.

units.la: Unusquisque] Privus, Cat. Viritim divisit agros, Cic. In viros dividere, Plaut.
units.tr: Unusquisque (each one): each man by himself, Cat. He divided the fields man by man, Cic. To divide among men, Plaut.

units.la: Urbane, vid. Facete.
units.tr: Urbane: see Witty.

units.la: Urbanitas, vid. Civilitas.
units.tr: Urbanitas: see Civility.

units.la: Urbanus, vid. Moratus, Facetus.
units.tr: Urbanus: see Polite, Witty.

units.la: Urbs, vid. Civitas.
units.tr: Urbs: see City.

units.la: Urceus, vid. Urna.
units.tr: Urceus: see Urn.

units.la: Urere] Ustulare, Pacuv. Torrere, Hor. Uredinem mittit urtica, Plin.
units.tr: Urere (to burn): to scorch, Pacuv. To parch, Hor. The nettle sends out a burning, Plin.

units.la: Uri] Calor urit artus, Lucr. Aduric sol, Virg. Peruri æstu, Ovid. Flammis, Sen. Calidum hoc est, etsi procul abest, urit male, Plaut.
units.tr: Uri (to be burned): heat burns the limbs, Lucr. The sun scorches, Virg. Burnt by heat, Ovid. By flames, Sen. Though it is far off, this is hot and burns badly, Plaut.

units.la: Urgere] Urgere aliquem aliquâ re. Urge, insta, perfice. Etiam atque etiam instare. Insectari atque adeo flagitare crimen. Imminere. Premere, Cic. Incumbere, Tac. Interpellare, Val. M. Obtundere, Apul. Tundere, Ter. Solicitare precibus, donis, Ovid. Urgere ad aliquid, Vlp. Cogere in angustum, Ter. Premit me necessitas, Cic.
units.tr: Urgere (to press): to press someone with something. Press on, urge, finish. To keep pressing again and again. To pursue and even demand an accusation. To hang over. To press, Cic. To lean upon, Tac. To interrupt, Val. Max. To beat, Apul. To harass, Ter. To importune with prayers and gifts, Ovid. To press towards something, Ulp. To drive into a narrow place, Ter. Necessity presses me, Cic.

units.la: Urina] Lotium, Cat. Saccatus humor totius corporis, Lucr. (i. colatus.) Humor obscoenus, Sen. Aqua immunda, Id. da, Id. Præfandus humor. Humoris præfandi profluvium. Humor quem profundimus, Plin. Aqua, abs. Propert. Ovid.
units.tr: Urina (urine): urine, Cat. The strained watery humour of the whole body, Lucr. (i.e. filtered out.) Foul humour, Sen. Unclean water, Id. Liquid to be voided. The flow of liquid we discharge, Plin. Water, Propert., Ovid.

units.la: Urinæ nimium profluvium] Incontinentia urinæ, Plin. Diabetes, Iun. Ureticus, Cæl. Rhod.
units.tr: Urinae nimium profluvium (excessive flow of urine): incontinence of urine, Plin. Diabetes, Iun. Urethral, Cael. Rhod.

units.la: Urina stillicidium] Substillum, Turneb. Stranguria, Plin. Urina difficilis, vid. Dysuria.
units.tr: Urina stillicidium (dribbling of urine): dribbling, Turneb. Strangury, Plin. Difficult urination: see Dysuria.

units.la: Urinam facere, vid. Mejere.
units.tr: Urinam facere: see Urinate.

units.la: Urinari] Inurinare lacui. Mergitur. Delphinus undâ, Cic.
units.tr: Urinari (to dive): to dive into a lake; it is submerged. The dolphin dives in the water, Cic.

units.la: Urna] Urceus aquarius, mustarius, Catul. Situla, Plaut. Situlus aquarius, Cato. Hydria, Cic. Cratera, Vas vinarium, vel olearium, Non. (Creterra, Fest.) Aquiminarium, Vlp. Aquiminale, Paul. IC. Matella, vas aquarium, Var. Nasiterna, Plaut.
units.tr: Urna (urn): a water pitcher, a wine pitcher, Catul. A bucket, Plaut. A water bucket, Cato. A water jar, Cic. A krater, a vessel for wine or oil, Non. A water vessel, Ulp. A water basin, Paul. IC. A matella, a water vessel, Varr. A nasiterna, Plaut.

units.la: Usitatè, vid. Morefit.
units.tr: Usitate: see Customarily.

units.la: Usitatus] Tritum sermone proverbium. Communia ac contrita præcepta. Quotidianus. In quotidiano usu positus. Tralatitium jus. Plebejus, vulgaris sermo, Cic. Popularis notæ, Col. Triviale verbum, Suet. Ordinarius, Vitruv. Circulatorius, Quint.
units.tr: Usitatus (customary): a proverb worn smooth by speech. Common and hackneyed precepts. Everyday; placed in daily use. Ordinary law. Plebeian, common speech, Cic. Of popular note, Col. A trivial word, Suet. Ordinary, Vitr. Circulating, Quint.

units.la: Usque resp. temporis] Usque ad Calendas, Cic. Usque in nostra tempora, Col. Usque adeo dum, Ter. Ad eum finem, dum, Cic. Ad id usque dum, Plaut. Usque donec, Ter. Donec, Cic. Usque quoad, Varr. Quoadusque, Acc. Vid. Tam diu, donec.
units.tr: Usque (until, of time): until the Kalends, Cic. Until our own times, Col. Until, so long as, Ter. To that end, while, Cic. Up to that time while, Plaut. Until, Ter. Until, Cic. Until which, Varr. Until which, Acc. See So long as, until.

units.la: Usque respectu loci] Usque ad pulmones, usque Romam. Trans Alpes usque, Cic. Usque eò, quò opus erit, prosequemur, ad Her. Usque illò, Plin. Ad usque columnas exulat. Crurum tenus, Virg. Inguinibus tenus in aquam se demittere, Cels.
units.tr: Usque (up to, of place): up to the lungs; all the way to Rome. All the way beyond the Alps, Cic. We shall follow all the way to wherever it is needed, ad Her. All the way to that place, Plin. He is exiled up to the columns. Up to the shins, Virg. To plunge into the water up to the groin, Cels.

units.la: Ustio] Crematio vini, secis, Plin.
units.tr: Ustio: the boiling down of wine, Plin.

units.la: Usu venit, vid. Accidere præter spem.
units.tr: It happens; see Accidere præter spem.

units.la: Usuarius] Usualis, Mart. Utibilis, Plaut. Utentior, Cic.
units.tr: Usuarius: usual, Mart. Serviceable, Plaut. More inclined to use, Cic.

units.la: Usura, vid. Fœnus.
units.tr: Usura; see Fœnus.

units.la: Usurpare, vid. Uti.
units.tr: Usurpare; see Uti.

units.la: Usurpator alieni muneris] Ædilitatem gerit sine populo suffragio.
units.tr: A usurper of another's office: he holds the aedileship without the people's vote.

units.la: Usus] Usio, Varr. Usura lucis, usurpatio. Fructus, Cic. Utilitas, Plaut. Necessitas, Cic.
units.tr: Usus: use, Varr. Enjoyment of daylight, use. Fruit, Cic. Utility, Plaut. Necessity, Cic.

units.la: Usus rerum mutuus] Dominus servo, & servus Domino indiget.
units.tr: Mutual use of things: the master needs the servant, and the servant needs the master.

units.la: Usus & abusus datur omnium] Nil agit exemplum litem quod lite resolvit, Hor.
units.tr: Use and abuse are given to all: an example does nothing when it settles a quarrel by a quarrel, Hor.

units.la: Usu altera natura] Usque adeo à teneris assuefscere multum est, Ter.
units.tr: Habit becomes a second nature: to be accustomed so thoroughly from tender years is a great thing, Ter.

units.la: Usu reddimur sapientes] Ætas homines acuit. Ætate prudentiores reddimur.
units.tr: We are made wise by experience: age sharpens men. We become wiser with age.

units.la: Res sine usu] Frondes fructuum expertes.
units.tr: Things without use: leaves without fruit.

units.la: Res diversi usus] Delphicus gladius.
units.tr: Things of different uses: the Delphic sword.

units.la: Ut, admirandi] Quàm cupiunt laudari. Quomodo mortem filii tulit, Cic.
units.tr: How (an exclamation of wonder): how eager they are to be praised! How he bore the death of his son, Cic.

units.la: Ut, causale] Uti, Cic. Effice qui detur, Ter. Quò, Plin. Quatenus, Macrob.
units.tr: Ut, causal: since, Cic. Contrive that it be given, Ter. Whereby, Plin. Inasmuch as, Macrob.

units.la: Ut similit.] vid. Sicut.
units.tr: Ut, comparative; see Sicut.

units.la: Ut te] Attatæ vel At at tate, Cavif. At tate. At te Dii Deæque quantus es, Plaut.
units.tr: Ut te: ah! Cavif. Ah! Plaut. Ah, ye gods and goddesses, how great you are!

units.la: Ut se res dant] Pro re nata.
units.tr: As the occasion arises.

units.la: Ut-ita] Ut quisque est gloriæ dignissimus, ita gloriæ est negligentissimus : ut quisque est gloriâ maximè dignus, ita gloriæ est minimè avidus. Quò quisque dignior est quò laudetur, hoc minùs laudari gaudet, Eras.
units.tr: The more worthy a person is of glory, the less eager he is for it: the more a person deserves to be praised, the less he delights in being praised, Eras.

units.la: Ut Deus se gerit] Jovi paria intonat.
units.tr: As God conducts himself: he thunders with a voice equal to Jove's.

units.la: Utcunque, vid. Quomodocunque.
units.tr: However; see Quomodocunque.

units.la: Uter] Uternam? Hor. Incertum utrâ via, Plin. Vid. Alteruter.
units.tr: Which of the two? Is it that one? Hor. It is uncertain by which road, Plin. See Alteruter.

units.la: Utercunque] Uterlibet, Cic. Utrumvis mihi licet. Utro uti volueris, pro utrovis, Cic.
units.tr: Whichever of the two: whichever you like, Cic. I am free to choose either. Use whichever you wish, for either, Cic.

units.la: Uterque, vid. Ambo.
units.tr: Each of the two; see Ambo.

units.la: Uti rebus] Uti ad aliquid. Frui, Sen. Usurpare, Cicer. Abuti, ad aliquid, Id. Est mihi ea res in usu, Quint. Fungi gaudio, Tac. Adhibere ad aliquid & alicui.
units.tr: To use things: to use for something. To enjoy, Sen. To make use of, Cicer. To misuse for something, Id. That thing is in use with me, Quint. To take pleasure in joy, Tac. To apply to something and to someone.

units.la: Uti tempore] Opportunitate uti, Cic. Occasionem arripere, Liv. Opprimere occasionem, Plaut.
units.tr: To use time: to make use of an opportunity, Cic. To seize the occasion, Liv. To let an opportunity slip, Plaut.

units.la: Uti aliqua re ad suum commodum] Insaniâ alienâ uti, optimum. mum. In rem suam vertere, Liv. Ad commodum suum convertere.
units.tr: To use something for one's own advantage: to use another's madness to the best effect. To turn to one's own profit, Liv. To bring it round to one's own advantage.

units.la: Utendum est rebus] Frustra habet, qui non utitur.
units.tr: Things must be used: he who does not use them has them in vain.

units.la: Utilis] Utilissimus. Perutilis, Conducibilis, Habet utilitatem, affert. Fructum utilitatis praebet. Fructuosus. Commodis meis aptus. Magnos usus adfert ad. Quaestuosus. Quaestuosissimus. Admodum utilis : utilis ad, Cicer. Alicui, Ter. Foecundus. Salutaris alicui. Frugi bona, Cicer. Frugi servus. Utibilis alicui, & ad aliquid, Plaut. E re tua, non ab re aucupis est, Id. Vertit id mihi in utilitatem, Lucr. Bono publico natus, Sen. Commodus, Prop. Commodatus stomacho, Plin. Opima praedia, Id. Commodum est. Ex usu meo est. Fenerat id mihi. Lucrosum id est, Ter. Is quaestus est uberrimus, Plaut.
units.tr: Useful: most useful. Very useful, convenient. It has usefulness, it brings it. It offers the fruit of usefulness. Fruitful. Suited to my convenience. It brings great uses for. Profitable. Most profitable. Quite useful: useful for, Cicer. To someone, Ter. Fruitful. Wholesome for someone. Good and worthy, Cicer. A thrifty servant. Serviceable to someone and for something, Plaut. It is for your advantage, not beside the point, is the fowler's business, Id. He has turned that to my advantage, Lucr. Born for the public good, Sen. Convenient, Prop. Agreeable to the stomach, Plin. Rich estates, Id. It is convenient. It is to my advantage. He lends me that at interest. That is profitable, Ter. That gain is most abundant, Plaut.

units.la: Utilitas] Usum habere ex : magno usui est in multis rebus. Fructus, Emolumentum, Commoditas, Commodum, Compendium, Opportunitas, Bonum, Cic. Cui bono fuit? Liv. Mihi nullum inde operae pretium, Iuven. Pretium morae, Virg.
units.tr: Utility: to have use from something: it is of great use in many matters. Fruit, profit, convenience, advantage, gain, opportunity, good, Cic. For whose benefit was it? Liv. No worthwhile reward comes to me from it, Juv. The reward of delay, Virg.

units.la: Utilitatis maximae res]Magnum ex ea re fructum tulit, Cepit emolumentum, Lucrum reporavit, sensit commodum, Commoditatem demessuit, Collegit utilitatem, Frugem accepit, Compendium paravit. Ea res illi frugifera fuit, Eras. In lucro deputo, Ter.
units.tr: A matter of the greatest utility: he reaped great fruit from that thing; he gained advantage; he recovered profit; he felt the benefit; he harvested convenience; he gathered utility; he received produce; he secured gain. That thing was fruitful for him, Eras. I count it as profit, Ter.

units.la: Utiliter] Salutariter uti armis, Cic. Vid. Bene.
units.tr: Usefully: to use arms to good effect, Cic. See Bene.

units.la: Utinam] O tantum libeat! Virg. O utinam! Ovid. O! O si! Cic. Ut illum! Ter.
units.tr: Would that: O, if only it might please you! Virg. O that! Ovid. O! O if! Cic. Would that he! Ter.

units.la: Utique] At tandem, tandem. Saltem, vel saltim, Plaut. Quin dic, quicquid est, Ter. Mortem optare incipiant, vel certe timere desinant, Cic.
units.tr: At any rate: at last, at last. At least, or at any rate, Plaut. Come, say whatever it is, Ter. Let them begin to wish for death, or at least cease to fear it, Cic.

units.la: Utrinque] Utrinquesecus, Cato. Lucr. Utrinque secus laterum, Apul. Utrobique eadem veritas est, Cic. Alterutrique, Plin. Ultro citroque, Caes.
units.tr: On both sides: on either side, Cato, Lucr. On both sides of the flanks, Apul. On each side the truth is the same, Cic. To either of the two, Plin. Back and forth, Caes.

units.la: Utrobique] Utroque versum, Gell. Utroque commeatus continet, Plaut. Ambifariam, Apul.
units.tr: On both sides: written in both directions, Gell. He keeps supplies on both sides, Plaut. In two ways, on both sides, Apul.

units.la: Utrum, nec ne?] Vise utrum; num jam redierit, an nondum. Vise redieritne domum. Vise an redierit, an non. Vise redieritne domum, nec ne? Eras.
units.tr: Whether or not: go and see whether he has already returned or not yet. Go and see whether he has returned home. Go and see whether he has returned or not. Go and see whether he has returned home or not, Eras.

units.la: Uva] Acinus vinaceus, Cic. Corymbus, Virg.
units.tr: Grape: a grape-berry with its skin and seeds, Cic. A bunch of grapes, Virg.

units.la: Uxor] Nupta Conjux & conjunx, Cic. Conjuga, Apul. Marita, Hor. Domina, Ovid.
units.tr: Wife: a married woman, a spouse, Cic. A consort, Apul. A bride, Hor. A mistress, Ovid.

units.la: Uxor prostitutæ pudicitiæ, dolore maritum conficit] Discruciat animum uxor impudica. Uxoris impudicitia discruciat animum, Eraf.
units.tr: A wife of unchaste character wears down her husband with grief: an immodest wife torments the mind. A wife's immodesty torments the mind, Eraf.

units.la: Uxor imperiosa] Juno.
units.tr: Domineering wife: Juno.

units.la: Uxoris jactat pulchritudinem] Gloriatur formosâ uxore. De uxoris formâ gloriatur, Eraf.
units.tr: He boasts of a beautiful wife. He boasts of his wife's beauty, Eraf.

units.la: Uxorem ducere] Adjungere sibi uxorem. Ducere aliquem in matrimonium, Cic. Assumere filium alicujus in matrimonium, Tac. Assumere uxorem, Plin. Iun. Conjungere sibi feminam matrimonio, Liv. Conjungere, jungere secum matrimonio aliquam, Curt. Nuptiis inter se juncti, Val. M. Maritari. Apul. Conjungere connubia, Cic. Jugare juvenem puellæ, Catul. Nubere alicui; in claram familiam, Cic. Nubit amicus, Juv.
units.tr: To take a wife: to join a wife to oneself. To lead someone into marriage, Cic. To take the son of someone in marriage, Tac. To take a wife, Plin. Iun. To join a woman to oneself in marriage, Liv. To join, to take someone to oneself in marriage, Curt. Joined to each other in wedlock, Val. M. To marry, Apul. To contract a marriage, Cic. To yoke a young man to a girl, Catul. To marry someone into a famous family, Cic. A friend marries, Juv.

units.la: V.
units.tr: V.

units.la: Vacans] Vacuus curis, negotiis. Vacuus à rebus, Cicer. Vacuum tempus, Ter. Dum sit vacuissima quæras, Ovid. Remissus ad otium & omnem comitatem animus, Suet.
units.tr: Vacans: free from cares and business. Free from affairs, Cicer. Empty time, Ter. "Seek while it is most empty," Ovid. A mind relaxed to leisure and all courtesy, Suet.

units.la: Vacare] Vacare curâ & negotio: animo: ab administratione rerum. Vacat mihi tempus è forensi dictione, Cic. Vacuum esse ad aliquid, Tacit. Otium habere, Cic. Otium mihi est. Opera est: operæ est, Plaut. Commodum mihi est, Ter. Erit tempus parandæ facultatis, Quint.
units.tr: Vacare: to be free from care and business; to be at leisure in mind; to be free from the administration of affairs. "Time is free for me from pleading in the forum," Cic. To be at leisure for something, Tacit. To have leisure, Cic. I have leisure. It is worth the trouble, it is worthwhile, Plaut. It suits me, Ter. There will be time for acquiring the means, Quint.

units.la: Non vacat] Auribus scalpendis deest otium. Vid. Occupatus.
units.tr: Non vacat: there is no leisure for scratching one's ears. See Occupatus.

units.la: Vacatio, vid. Cessatio.
units.tr: Vacatio: see Cessatio.

units.la: Vacationem alicui dare] Dare vacationem rerum omnium; à causis, Cic. Dare gratiam jurisjurandi, Plaut. Donare aliquem rude, ex Hor. Liberari curæ, tutelæ, Vlp. Voti, Liv. Solvatur legibus, quanquam leges eum non tenent, Id. Vid. Privilegio donare.
units.tr: Vacationem alicui dare: to grant someone exemption from all duties; from legal cases, Cic. To grant exemption from an oath, Plaut. To discharge someone from service with the wooden sword, ex Hor. To free someone from care or guardianship, Vlp. From a vow, Liv. Let him be released by the laws, although the laws do not bind him, Id. See Privilegio donare.

units.la: Vacca] Bos. Vitula, Virg.
units.tr: Vacca: a cow. A heifer, Virg.

units.la: Vacerra] Cavea stultorum.
units.tr: Vacerra: a cage for fools.

units.la: Vacia, vid. Valgus.
units.tr: Vacia: see Valgus.

units.la: Vacillans, vid. Debilis.
units.tr: Vacillans: see Debilis.

units.la: Vacillare, vid. Labascere.
units.tr: Vacillare: see Labascere.

units.la: Vacuum] Nihil est quod vacet corpore, Cic. Inane. Vacuum inane. Inane rerum. Locus intactus vacansque. Quacunque vacat spatium, Lucr. Cassum, Solin.
units.tr: Vacuum: there is nothing that is empty of body, Cic. Void. Empty void. Void of things. A place untouched and empty. Wherever space lies empty, Lucr. Empty, Solin.

units.la: Vacuus] Vacans, Virg. Intervacans spatium, Col. Vacat: fac vacent aedes. Plenae aedes inanitate, Plaut. Inane vas, Cic. Obinane ovum, Varr. Cassum & inane granum, Plin. Cassa nux, Hor. Vanae avenae, Virg. Ampulla inanior, Er.
units.tr: Vacuus: empty, Virg. A space left empty between, Col. It is empty: make the houses empty. Houses full of emptiness, Plaut. An empty vessel, Cic. An empty egg, Varr. Empty and worthless grain, Plin. An empty nut, Hor. Vain oats, Virg. A flask emptier still, Er.

units.la: Vacuus à crimine] Vacuus crimine, Ovid. Vacuus à suspicione: Vacat vitio, culpa. Nulla pars corporis vacat à turpitudine, Cic, Immunis mali alicujus, Ovid. Expers cupiditatum, Cic. Expers laboris, domo, more, metu, Plaut. Non cadit in eum cupiditas, suspicio, mentiri, Cic. Liber non est, qui non aliquando nihil agit.
units.tr: Vacuus à crimine: free from crime, Ovid. Free from suspicion. Free from fault or blame. No part of the body is free from baseness, Cic. Exempt from some evil, Ovid. Without desires, Cic. Without labour, home, custom or fear, Plaut. Desire, suspicion or lying does not fall upon him, Cic. He is not free who never at any time does nothing.

units.la: Vadare] Gradi per aequor, Virg. Pedibus flumen transire, Cic. Flumen vado transiri potest, Paul. IC. Vado ire, transire; vadum ingredi.
units.tr: Vadare: to walk across the sea, Virg. To cross a river on foot, Cic. A river can be crossed at a ford, Paul. IC. To go across, to cross at a ford; to enter a ford.

units.la: Vadatus] Vadimonio obstrictus, Bud.
units.tr: Vadatus: bound by a surety bond, Bud.

units.la: Vadimonium] Missum facere vadimonium, Cic. Fidejussio. Expromissio. Sponsio. Satisdatum. Testis, Id.
units.tr: Vadimonium: to release the obligation of a bail-bond, Cic. Guarantee. Expromission. Sponsion. Security. A witness, Id.

units.la: Vadimonium alicui promittere] Cic. Vadimonium facere, constituere alicui. Obstringere se alicui sponsione; praedibus. Cavere alicui praedibus. Satisdare alicui, Cic. Satis praestare, Mart. Dare vadem, Liv. Dare fidem firmatam, Plaut. Satisdato promittere, Bud.
units.tr: Vadimonium alicui promittere: Cic. To make or fix a bail-bond for someone. To bind oneself to someone by a sponsion; by sureties. To give sureties to someone. To give security to someone, Cic. To give adequate guarantee, Mart. To give bail, Liv. To give a firmly pledged word, Plaut. To promise upon adequate security, Bud.

units.la: Vadimonium ab aliquo accipere] Bud. Postulare, Id. Accipere praedes pecuniae publicae: accipere pro aliquo praedes; Vadem. Satis accipere, abs. & ab aliquo. Vadari aliquem, Cic. Vadari vadibus aliquem, Liv.
units.tr: Vadimonium ab aliquo accipere: Bud. To demand, Id. To accept sureties for public money; to accept sureties on behalf of someone; a bail. To accept sufficient security, absolutely and from someone. To have someone bailed, Cic. To have someone bailed with sureties, Liv.

units.la: Vadum] Brevia, Virg. Tac.
units.tr: Vadum: shallows, Virg. Tac.

units.la: Vecors, vid. Amens.
units.tr: Vecors: see Amens.

units.la: Vafer] Annibale vafrior, Er. Vid. Astutus.
units.tr: Vafer: more cunning than Hannibal, Er. See Astutus.

units.la: Vafra versutaque consilia] Sisyphi artes.
units.tr: Vafra versutaque consilia: the crafty arts of Sisyphus.

units.la: Vafre, vid. Astute.
units.tr: Vafre: see Astute.

units.la: Vagabundus] Vagus,Cic. Erro,Hor. Erraticus homo,Gell. Lixabundus,Plaut. Homo de via. Puer è triviis,Tibul. Circumcelliones, (quòd circa cellas vagentur) Fest. Canalicolas vocat,Fest. Obsessor fori. Ignobilis,Plaut.
units.tr: Vagabundus: wandering, Cic. Roving, Hor. A wandering man, Gell. A vagrant, Plaut. A man off the road. A boy from the crossroads, Tibul. Circumcelliones (so called because they wander about the cells), Fest. He calls them street-haunters, Fest. A loiterer in the courts. Of low birth, Plaut.

units.la: Vagari] Divagari huc atque illuc,Lactan. Mutare sedem ex sede,Plin. Pererrare ignotum orbem,Col. Frustra per multas ambages vagari. Nomadicam vitam agere,Solin. (Nomades erant populi, pascendi gregib. vacantes, eoque regiones mutantes.) Oberrare,Plin. Volutantur circa terram animi post mortem. Errare circa villulas,Cicer. Inerrare montibus,Plin. Iun. Palari,Liv. Palitare,Plaut. Vagari per forum: toto foro: in foro,Cic.
units.tr: Vagari: to wander hither and thither, Lactan. To change one's seat from one place to another, Plin. To roam through an unknown world, Col. To wander in vain through many windings. To lead a nomadic life, Solin. (The Nomades were peoples devoted to pasturing flocks, and so changing their regions.) To wander about, Plin. Souls wander about the earth after death. To roam about the villages, Cicer. To wander among the mountains, Plin. Iun. To stray, Liv. To ramble, Plaut. To walk about the forum: through the whole forum, in the forum, Cic.

units.la: Vagari est inutile] Haud temerè ditescunt,qui crebrò vertunt solum. Lapis sæpe volutus, non fit hirsutus.
units.tr: Vagari est inutile: Those do not grow rich by chance who often change their ground. A stone that is often rolled does not become mossy.

units.la: Vagire] Vagitare,Stat. Vagitum edere,Quint. Obvagire,Plaut.
units.tr: Vagire: to wail, Stat. To utter the cry of an infant, Quint. To cry out at, Plaut.

units.la: Vagitus] Vagor,Lucr. Quiritatus infantium,Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Vagitus: wailing, Lucr. The crying of infants, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Vagus] Vagula anima,Spart. Palatus exercitus,Liv. Palans,Lucr. Vid.Vagabundus.
units.tr: Vagus: a little wandering soul, Spart. A straggling army, Liv. Wandering, Lucr. See Vagabundus.

units.la: Vah! ] Papæ! jugulâras hominem. Euge! Eja!Ter.
units.tr: Vah!: Bravo! You have throttled the man! Well done! Come on! Ter.

units.la: Valde] Valdè exspecto,velim; valdè bene, diligens: valdè quàm paucos habet. Nimis valdè. Valdè opinio est de. Validissimè ravere. Vehementer. Admodum. Benè longus: benè manè: benè & naviter impudens. Malè odisse,Cic. Malè maceror,metuo,Plaut. Magnè peccare,Tac. Maximè, summè,impensè, impendio odi. Multum,multò: multò maximè exercemus: multi existimare aliquid. Incredibiliter, insignitè, insigniter, effusè, Nimiùm, Eximiè. Ut cùm maximè. Magnopere, summopere, maximopere,Cic. Multopere, magno opere, & opere magno,Plaut. Maximo te orabat opere. Apprimè utile,Ter. Oppidò ridiculus,Cicer. Oppidò quàm peritus,Gell. Ita, ut nihil magis unquam. Ita accuratè, ut nihil suprà. Immortaliter gaudeo. Mirabiliter, mirificè deditus studiis. Majorem, mirabilem in modum,Cic. Mirum quantùm,Liv. Mirum in modum, miris modis. Ampliter mentiri,Plaut. Omni modo,Plin. Omnibus modis, multis modis,Terent. Multimodis, Plaut. Per , (in compositis, ut) Peramans, pergratus, perbrevis, perhorresco, perquam puerile, Cic. Perquam fortiter. Egregiè, Ter. Insanè esuriens, Varr. Insanum magnus, Plaut. Ter felix, Ovid. Terque quaterque, Felices ter & amplius, Hor. Præter justum, Lucr. Sanè quàm. Porrò. Pergraviter offensus ; Mihi usque curæ erit quid agat. In omnes partes molestum. Post hominum memoriam magnificentissimi ludi, Cic. In immensum, Ovid. Oculitùs amare. Maximum exclamat, Plaut. Multa reluctanti, Virg. Supra quàm æstimari potest. Prope ad stultitiam simplicissimus, Sext. Aurel. Diapason. Desiderando desiderare, Hebraism. Supra modum; præter modum, singulariter, unicè. Operâ quantâ potest maximâ, Eraf.
units.tr: Valde: I wait very much, I should like; very well, diligent; how very few he has. Too much. There is a strong opinion about. To rave most vehemently. Vehemently. Greatly. Quite long; quite early in the morning; quite and vigorously shameless. To hate badly, Cic. I am badly tormented, I fear, Plaut. To sin greatly, Tac. Most, chiefly, extremely, lavishly, I hate exceedingly. Much, much more; we practise much more; many think something. Incredibly, remarkably, notably, lavishly, too much, exceptionally. As much as possible. Greatly, very greatly, most greatly, Cic. Much, with great effort, and with great effort, Plaut. He begged you with the greatest effort. Especially useful, Ter. Quite ridiculous, Cicer. Quite skilled, Gell. So that nothing more ever. So exactly that nothing beyond. I rejoice immortally. Wonderfully, marvellously devoted to his studies. Greater, in a marvellous manner, Cic. Wonderfully much, Liv. In a marvellous manner, in marvellous ways. To lie copiously, Plaut. In every way, Plin. In all ways, in many ways, Terent. In many ways, Plaut. Per- (in compounds, as): very loving, very pleasing, very brief, I shudder greatly, quite childish, Cic. Quite bravely. Outstandingly, Ter. Madly hungry, Varr. Madly great, Plaut. Thrice happy, Ovid. Thrice and four times over. Happy thrice and more, Hor. Beyond what is just, Lucr. Certainly how much. Moreover. Gravely offended. To me it will be a constant concern what he does. Troublesome in every part. Since the memory of men, the most magnificent games, Cic. Without measure, Ovid. To love with the eyes. He cries out most loudly, Plaut. Much against his will, Virg. Beyond what can be estimated. Almost to foolishness most simple, Sext. Aurel. Diapason. Desiring to desire, Hebraism. Beyond measure; beyond measure; singularly, uniquely. With the greatest effort possible, Eras.

units.la: Valdè multum] Multum:plus: plurimum:multis partibus.
units.tr: Valde multum: much; more; most; in many parts.

units.la: Vale] Vale atque salve. Vale & vive. Benè vale. Fac valeas, Plaut. Benè sit tibi, Id. Sis felix. Æternum salve, æternumque vale, Virg.
units.tr: Vale: farewell and greetings. Farewell and live. Farewell and be well. Mind that you are well, Plaut. May it go well with you, Id. Be happy. Hail for ever, and farewell for ever, Virg.

units.la: Valedicere] Dicere vale, Ovid. Dicere supremum alicui, Plaut. Dicere novissima verba, Virg. Jubeo valere aliquem, Cic. Nuncium remittere alicui. Rebus humanis valere & plaudere dixit, Apul.
units.tr: Valedicere: to say farewell, Ovid. To say a last word to someone, Plaut. To speak the final words, Virg. To bid someone farewell, Cic. To send back a message to someone. He bade farewell to human affairs and took his applause, Apul.

units.la: Valens, vid. Robustus.
units.tr: Valens: see Robustus.

units.la: Valere benè] Valere à morbo, Plaut. Uti firmâ valetudine, Plin. Iun. Salvere, vivere, valere pancraticè & athleticè. Valuistin', Plaut. Posse : nihil dolet nisi pes, possunt oculi, potest caput, possunt latera, pulmones, possunt omnia. Habere belle, & habere se bellè. Recte est alicui, Cic. Valere ab oculis, Gell. Incolumis sum, Hor. Sum opimo habitu corporis, Cic. Sum habitior, Ter. Benè habeo cibo, Plaut. Meliusculè est mihi.
units.tr: Valere bene: to be well after an illness, Plaut. To enjoy firm health, Plin. Iun. To be sound, to live, to be strong in the manner of the pancratium and athletics. Are you well? Plaut. To be able: nothing hurts except the foot; the eyes can, the head can, the sides, the lungs, all things can. To be well and to be in good shape. It is well with someone, Cic. To be well in the eyes, Gell. I am safe, Hor. I am in robust bodily condition, Cic. I am in better condition, Ter. I am well fed, Plaut. I am somewhat better.

units.la: Valere benè omnium bonorum est optimum] Valetudo est censu præstantior omni.
units.tr: Valere bene omnium bonorum est optimum: health is better than any wealth. Health surpasses in worth every possession.

units.la: Valet ad aliquid] In omnes partes valet. In utramque partem valet. Valet ad dicendum. Est palæstræ, vel gymnasii. Erit usui, Cicer. Facit : quorundam contumacia non facit ad aulam, Sen. Non faciet capiti dura corona meo, Propert. (i. non conveniet.) Aptus ad usum aliquem, quem, Ovid. Utibilis ad rem aliquam, Propert. Vid. Prodesse. Est pro.
units.tr: Valet ad aliquid: it is effective in every respect. It is effective on both sides. It is effective for speaking. It belongs to the wrestling-ground or gymnasium. It will be of use, Cicer. It serves: the obstinacy of some people does not serve the court, Sen. A hard crown will not suit my head, Propert. (i.e. will not fit). Fit for some use, Ovid. Useful for some matter, Propert. See Prodesse. Est pro.

units.la: Valeat, sensu fastidiente, &c.] Longum vale tibi dico. In rem malam abeat. Habeat, fruatur. Sinamus illum. Illum ego nihil moror. Deo hæc sint curæ. Ilicet parasiticæ arti maximam malam crucem, (sc. opto,dico.) Plaut. Vivant, qui mihi malè volunt, i. Valeant. Cum suis vivat valeatque mœchus, Catul. Sine vivat ineptus, Hor.
units.tr: Valeat, in a disdainful sense, etc.: I bid him a long farewell. Let him go to ruin. Let him have it and enjoy it. Let us allow him. I care nothing for him. Let God take care of these things. Away with the parasitic art, a great evil cross (I wish, I say), Plaut. Let those who wish me ill live, i.e. let them fare well. Let the adulterer live and be well with his own, Catul. Let the fool live, Hor.

units.la: Valetudo, vid. Sanitas.
units.tr: Valetudo: see Sanitas.

units.la: Valetudinem curare, vid. Curare val.
units.tr: Valetudinem curare: see Curare val.

units.la: Valgus] Valgius, Lev. Vacia, Turn. Vatia, & Vatius, Var. Scal. Scaurus, Plin. Scauripeda, Varr. Scambus, Suet. Varus, distortis & introrsus actis ac conjunctis pedibus, Varr.
