Cruribus distortis, Hor. Vatrax, & Vatricosus, Lucil. Vacax, Decalemp. Compernis, Plaut. Compressis genibus, Fest. Male pedatus, Suet. Pravis fultus male talis, Hor. Varica femina, Ovid. Prævarus, Cic. Curvipes, Sipont. (Flexipes, epithet. hederæ, ex Ovid.) Extritis talis, Varr. al. Extortis talis.
units.tr: Valgus: bow-legged. Valgius, Lev. Vacia, Turn. Vatia and Vatius, Var. Scal. Scaurus, Plin. Scauripeda, Varr. Scambus, Suet. Varus: with feet twisted and turned inward and joined together, Varr. With legs distorted, Hor. Vatrax and Vatricosus, Lucil. Vacax, Decalemp. Compernis, Plaut. With knees pressed together, Fest. Badly footed, Suet. Propped on crooked ankles, badly, Hor. A bow-legged woman, Ovid. Prævarus, Cic. Curvipes, Sipont. (Flexipes, an epithet of ivy, from Ovid.) With twisted ankles, Varr. Others: with ankles turned out.

units.la: Validus, vid. Robustus.
units.tr: Validus: see Robustus.

units.la: Vallare] Vallant oppida muri, Lucr. Circumvallare aliquem. Obvallare, Cicer. Circumdare vallum urbi, Curt. Circumjicere vallum, Liv. Munire vallo, Lucr. Vallo fossaque munire, Cæs. Vallo fossaque mœnia circumvenit, Sallust. Circummunire fossâ, Col. Circummœnitus, Plin. Cingere urbem fossâ, vallo, mœnibus. Circumdare fossam alicui loco, Cic. Sepire castris, castellis, Id. Interseptire aliquid operibus, Liv. Circundare, cingere muro, Virg. Vid. Munire.
units.tr: Vallare: walls surround towns, Lucr. To surround someone. To fortify around, Cicer. To put a rampart round the city, Curt. To cast a rampart around, Liv. To fortify with a rampart, Lucr. To fortify with rampart and ditch, Cæs. He surrounded the walls with rampart and ditch, Sallust. To fortify round with a ditch, Col. Fortified all round, Plin. To gird a city with a ditch, rampart and walls. To put a ditch round a place, Cic. To fence in with camps and forts, Id. To hem in with works, Liv. To gird round with a wall, Virg. See Munire.

units.la: Vanescere] Evanuerunt & exaruerunt omnes. Extenuatur & evanescit spes, Cic. Evanescere stinguique colorem, Lucr. Revanescit ardor, Ovid. Exstinguitur forma. Defloresc it formæ dignitas, Cic. Disperiret labor, Catul. Tabere, Var. Exolevit favor, Liv. Abolescit gratia, Virg. Vinea, Col. Aboleri, apud Tac. Vid. Evanescere. Disparere.
units.tr: To vanish] They have all faded and dried up. Hope is weakened and vanishes, Cic. To fade away and lose its colour, Lucr. Ardour revives again, Ovid. Beauty is extinguished. The dignity of beauty withers, Cic. Labour perishes, Catul. To waste away, Var. Favour has faded away, Liv. Grace is abolished, Virg. The vine, Col. To be abolished, in Tac. See Evanescere. Disparere.

units.la: Vaniloquentia] Vanitas orationis, Cic. Multum loquentiæ, sapientiæ parum. Mare verborum, gutta rerum.
units.tr: Empty talk] The emptiness of speech, Cic. Much talk, little wisdom. A sea of words, a drop of substance.

units.la: Vaniloquii pœna] Linguarium dato. Verba mea redimam. Damno castigabo promittendi facultatem, Sen.
units.tr: Punishment for empty talk] Give him a tongue-clamp. I will buy back my words. I will punish the power of promising with a fine, Sen.

units.la: Vanitas] Vanities, Apul. Inanitas, Cic. Inaniæ, Plaut. Futilitas, res inanes, Cicer. O quantum est in rebus inane! Perf. Inania, æ, Non.
units.tr: Vanity] Vanity, Apul. Emptiness, Cic. Empty things, Plaut. Futility, empty things, Cicer. O how much emptiness there is in things! Pers. Empty things, Non.

units.la: Vannare] Vanno, vel vannis expurgare, Col. Vannare frumentum, Lucil. Evannantur acus extra aream, Varr. Evallere, (evallo, is) Plin. Repolire frumenta, Col.
units.tr: To winnow] To winnow, or to clean out with a winnowing fan, Col. To winnow grain, Lucil. The needles are winnowed out beyond the threshing floor, Varr. To sift out, Plin. To clean grain again, Col.

units.la: Vannus] Vallus, Varr. Cribrum areale, Serv. Cribrum cereale, Sipont.
units.tr: Winnowing fan] A winnowing fan, Varr. A threshing-floor sieve, Serv. A grain sieve, Sipont.

units.la: Vanus] Vana imago, Hor. Inane somnium, Cic. Futilis, Id. Evanidus, Sen.
units.tr: Vain] A vain image, Hor. An empty dream, Cic. Futile, Id. Fading away, Sen.

units.la: Vana sunt, quæ dicuntur, ut somnium] Deinde expergiscebar.
units.tr: What is said is vain, like a dream] Then I woke up.

units.la: Vana sunt strepera, vera non item] Altissima quæque flumina tacito labuntur sono.
units.tr: Noisy things are empty, true things are not so] The deepest rivers flow with a silent sound.

units.la: Vapidus] Vinum vapidum, Mart. Vappa, Hor. Marcidum vinum, Stat.
units.tr: Vapid] Vapid wine, Mart. Flat wine, Hor. Wine gone stale, Stat.

units.la: Vapor] Halitus terræ, Plin. Aqua rarefacta. Fluor volaticus. Aëris rigator. Nubium genitor. Exhalatio nebulosa, Plin. Exspiratio terræ, Cicer. Humor terrenus, marinus, Cicer. Humor aquæ & aquatilis, Lucr. Varr.
units.tr: Vapour] Exhalation of the earth, Plin. Water made thin. A volatile flow. Sprinkler of the air. Begetter of clouds. A misty exhalation, Plin. Breath of the earth, Cicer. Earthly and sea moisture, Cicer. Watery and aqueous moisture, Lucr. Varr.

units.la: Vaporare, vid. Exhalare.
units.tr: To vaporise, see Exhalare.

units.la: Vaporeus, vid. Calidus.
units.tr: Vaporous, see Calidus.

units.la: Vapulare] Vilitare sorbilo, (scil. vapulans & suspirans.) Plaut.
units.tr: To be beaten] To be cheapened with a slurp (namely, being beaten and sighing), Plaut.

units.la: Vari, seu varri] Vara, æ, Scal. ex Varr. Bacillum furcillatum. Furcillæ, Idem. Furcæ: Furcis sublevant retia, Plin.
units.tr: Vari, or varri] A vara, Scal. from Varr. A forked stick. Forked props. Forks: forks support the nets, Plin.

units.la: Varians, vid. Mutabilis.
units.tr: Varying, see Mutabilis.

units.la: Variare aliquid] Variare & distinguere orationem. Varietate aliquid distinguere, Cic. Varium aliquid facere, Plaut. Distinguere vario colore, Ovid. Distinguere albis maculis rutilum colorem, Plin. Conspergunt viridantes floribus herbas. Anni tempora pingunt. Pingere rosarum floribus viam, Lucr. Flore vario depingere. Infuscare pullis maculis vellera, Virg. Intertexere notis ex Quint. Bullis aureis te multis velut stellis sidereis relucentem inocu-labo, Apul. Variegare, Bero. Vid. Mutare.
units.tr: To vary something] To vary and distinguish a speech. To distinguish something by variety, Cic. To make something varied, Plaut. To distinguish with varied colour, Ovid. To mark a reddish colour with white spots, Plin. They sprinkle the greening grass with flowers. They paint the seasons of the year. To paint a road with roses, Lucr. To adorn with a variety of flowers. To darken fleeces with dark spots, Virg. To interweave with marks, from Quint. I shall graft you shining with many golden studs like starry stars, Apul. To variegate, Bero. See Mutare.

units.la: Variatio, vid. Differentia.
units.tr: Variation, see Differentia.

units.la: Variatus] Distinctus : distinctæ floribus herbæ, Ovid. Distincta auro & ebore cithara. Cœlum astris distinctum, Cic. Perpictus, Ovid. Comptus, Lucan. Fixum cœlum sideribus, Lucr. Ager floribus picturatus, Stat. Pavone picturatior. Vid. Picturatus.
units.tr: Variegated] Distinguished: herbs distinguished with flowers, Ovid. A lyre distinguished with gold and ivory. The heavens distinguished with stars, Cic. Richly painted, Ovid. Adorned, Lucan. The sky fixed with stars, Lucr. A field painted with flowers, Stat. More gaudy than a peacock. See Picturatus.

units.la: Varie] Pervarie, multifariam, Cicer. Multifarie, Plin. Plurifariam, Suet. Multiformiter, Plin. Multipliciter, Firm. Multimodis, Lucr. Aliquotfariam, Varr. Variatim, Gell.
units.tr: Variously] In many ways, Cicer. In many ways, Plin. In many parts, Suet. In many forms, Plin. In many ways, Firm. In many modes, Lucr. In some parts, Varr. Variously, Gell.

units.la: Varietas] Versicolor varietas, Plin. Variantia, Lucr.
units.tr: Variety] Variety of colours, Plin. Variety, Lucr.

units.la: Varietas delectat] Jucunda vicissitudo rerum. Gaudet ipsa natura varietate. Tantam ubique vim habet varietas, ut nihil omnino tam nitidum sit, quod non squalere videatur, citra ejus commendationem, Eras.
units.tr: Variety delights] A pleasant change of things. Nature herself delights in variety. Variety has such power everywhere that nothing at all is so bright that it does not seem dull without its recommendation, Eras.

units.la: Varius] Multiplex, multiformis, Cic. Plurifarius, Suet. Pluriformis, Apul. Versicolor varietas, Plin. Versicolor pluma. Multiplicabilis, Cic. Omnium rerum ; variarum rerum missilia, Suet.
units.tr: Various] Manifold, multiform, Cic. Of many kinds, Suet. Multiform, Apul. Variegated, Plin. A variegated feather. Capable of being multiplied, Cic. Of all things: miscellaneous things of various kinds, Suet.

units.la: Varia sunt res] Non una omnium facies.
units.tr: Things are various] Not all things have one appearance.

units.la: Varia variis eveniunt] Bona nemini hora est ; quin alicui sit mala.
units.tr: Various things happen to various people] No hour is good for everyone; indeed, it may be bad for someone.

units.la: Varo, i. stolidus] Varro, Cic. Lapis : quid stas lapis? Ter. Stupor : talis iste meus stupor, nihil videt, nihil audit, Catul. Brutus, Isid. Vid. Stupidus.
units.tr: Varo, i.e. a fool] Varro, Cic. A stone: why do you stand there like a stone? Ter. Stupor: such is my stupor; he sees nothing, hears nothing, Catul. Brutus, Isid. See Stupidus.

units.la: Varus, vid. Valgus.
units.tr: Varus, see Valgus.

units.la: Vas, adis] Vadimonium, pro persona, Apul. Præs, Cic. Interventor. Fidejussor, Apul. Vid. Sponsor.
units.tr: Vas, adis] Bail for a person, Apul. Surety, Cic. Guarantor. Bail-giver, Apul. See Sponsor.

units.la: Vas, sis] Vasculum, Catul. Vasum argenteum, Plaut. Vasarium, Vitruv. Receptaculum olei, Pallad. Gemellar structile oleo recipiendo, Col. Instrumentum, Suet. Vas pertusum, vas plenum rimarum.
units.tr: Vas, sis] A little vessel, Catul. A silver vessel, Plaut. A storage vessel, Vitruv. A receptacle for oil, Pallad. A twin structure for holding oil, Col. An implement, Suet. A pierced vessel, a vessel full of cracks.

units.la: Vastare] Vastitatem efficere, inferre urbibus. Popu-lari agros. Depopulari ; depopulationem inferre. Infesta-re, re, infestum habere locum aliquem, Cicer. Evastare, Devastare, Pervastare fines, Liv. Desolare agros, Col. Vexare agros, Cæs. Vastam facere urbem, Fest. Excursionibus & latrociniis infestam provinciam reddere. Rapinis, cædibus, incendiis omnia pervertere. Excisionem, eversionem, inflammationem, depopulationem agris, tectis inferre. Exinanire agros, Cic. Perpopulari omnia. Populationem facere, exercere. Agere & ferre passim cuncta, Liv.
units.tr: To lay waste] To bring about desolation, to inflict it on cities. To lay waste the fields. To ravage; to bring ravaging upon. To harass, to hold a place as hostile, Cicer. To lay waste, to devastate, to ravage the borders, Liv. To desolate the fields, Col. To harry the fields, Caes. To make a city a waste, Fest. To make a province hostile with raids and robberies. To overturn everything with plunder, slaughter and fire. To bring destruction, overthrow, burning and ravaging upon fields and houses. To drain the fields, Cic. To ravage everything. To carry on devastation. To carry off and bring everything everywhere, Liv.

units.la: Vastari] Vastescere, Non. Efferari: homines non patiuntur terram immanitate belluarum efferari, nec stirpium asperitate vastari, Cic.
units.tr: To be laid waste] To become waste, Non. To grow savage: men do not allow the land to be made savage by the monstrosity of beasts, nor laid waste by the roughness of plants, Cic.

units.la: Vastatio] Populatio, Liv. Populatus, Lucan. Depopulatio, Cic. Expopulatio, Col. Vexatio provinciæ. Direptio urbis, sociorum. Excisio, eversio, inflammatio, Cicer.
units.tr: Devastation] Ravaging, Liv. Plundering, Lucan. Depopulation, Cic. Expopulation, Col. The harassing of a province. The plundering of a city, of allies. Destruction, overthrow, burning, Cicer.

units.la: Vastator] Populator agri, Sen. Depopulator, Vexator & direptor urbis, Cic. Eversor regnorum, Virg. Popula trix, Mart. Vastatrix luxuria, Sen. Vastifica belua, Cic.
units.tr: Devastator] A ravager of fields, Sen. A depopulator, harasser and plunderer of a city, Cic. An overthrower of kingdoms, Virg. A female ravager, Mart. Wasting luxury, Sen. A destructive beast, Cic.

units.la: Vastè] Hiulcè, rusticè dicere, Cic.
units.tr: Vaste] To speak gapingly and rustically, Cic.

units.la: Vastitas] Vastitas in agris. Deserta, inculta, relicta omnia, Cic. Vastitudo fundi, agri, Cat. Vastities, Plaut. Colluvio & eversio civitatis, Cic. Vastatio, & depopulatio, hoc sensu usurpantur à Cic. & Liv.
units.tr: Desolation] Desolation in the fields. Deserted, uncultivated, everything abandoned, Cic. Waste of an estate, of a field, Cat. Desolation, Plaut. The ruin and overthrow of a state, Cic. Devastation and depopulation; these are used in this sense by Cic. and Liv.

units.la: Vastitas, al. vid. Magnitudo.
units.tr: Vastitas, alt., see Magnitudo.

units.la: Vastus, vid. Desertus. Latus.
units.tr: Vast, see Desertus. Latus.

units.la: Vates] Vaticinator, Ovid. Fatidicus. Vir divino numine afflatus. Divinæ mentis interpres, Cic. Oraculorum interpres, Fest. Propheta, Isid.
units.tr: Prophet] One who speaks in prophecy, Ovid. A soothsayer. A man inspired by divine power. An interpreter of the divine mind, Cic. An interpreter of oracles, Fest. A prophet, Isid.

units.la: Vates, fœmina] Prophetis, in S.L. Prophetissa, in Vulg. Vid. Fatiloqua, Liv.
units.tr: Prophetess] Prophetis, in S.L. A prophetess, in the Vulgate. See Fatiloqua, Liv.

units.la: Vaticinari] Inflatu divino futura prænunciare, Cic. Oraculum edere, fundere. Augurari alicui mortem. Divinare de aliquâ re: futura. Divinitus loqui. Multa divinè præsensa & prædicta. In posterum præsentire, Cicer. Dei jussu aperit ora fatis futuris, Virg. Ominari alicui consulatum tum, Plin. Iun. Prophetizare, & Prophetare, apud Christ. Scrip. Haruspicinam facere.
units.tr: To prophesy] To foretell future things by divine inspiration, Cic. To give out an oracle, to pour it forth. To foretell death to someone. To divine about a matter: future things. To speak by divine inspiration. To have foreseen and foretold many things divinely. To foresee what is to come, Cicer. By the command of God he opens his mouth to the coming fates, Virg. To foretell someone's consulship at that time, Plin. Iun. To prophesy, and to prophesy, in Christian Scripture. To practise haruspicy.

units.la: Vaticinium] Vaticinationes & responsa aruspicum, Sibyllarum, Cicer. Prophetia, Isid. Oraculum. Præsensa & prædicta divinè. Præfensio & scientia rerum futurarum. Prædicta, prædictio vatum. Prædictio divina. A Diis profecta denunciatio, significatio. Omen: ut oratio ejus omen fati habere videretur, Cic.
units.tr: Prophecy] The prophecies and responses of the soothsayers and Sibyls, Cicer. Prophecy, Isid. An oracle. Things foreseen and foretold divinely. Foresight and knowledge of future things. Prediction, the prophecy of prophets. Divine prediction. An announcement or sign sent from the gods. An omen: so that his speech seemed to carry an omen of fate, Cic.

units.la: Vaticinus] Vaticinus furor, Ovid. Vaticini libri, Liv. Propheticus, Sipont.
units.tr: Prophetic] Prophetic frenzy, Ovid. Prophetic books, Liv. Prophetic, Sipont.

units.la: Vectiarius, vid. Bajulus.
units.tr: Carrier, see Bajulus.

units.la: Vectigal] Merces prædiorum. Mercedula, Cicer. Publicum, Suet. Lav. Vicesima, Cic. Reditus, Proventus, Plin. Annona, Col.
units.tr: Tax] Rent of estates. A small fee, Cicer. Public revenue, Suet. Lav. A twentieth, Cic. Income, revenue, Plin. Yearly provision, Col.

units.la: Vectigaliarius] Publicanus. Portitor, Cicer. Manceps, Fest.
units.tr: Tax collector] A publican. A toll-collector, Cicer. A contractor, Fest.

units.la: Vectigalis, vid. Tributarius.
units.tr: Taxable, see Tributarius.

units.la: Vectio] Vectura, Cicer. Vectatio, Sipont. Vehiculatio, Cassiub. Vehiatura, Sipont. Vejatura, veitura, Fest. Subvectio, Cæf. Subvectus, Tacit. Convectio, Amm. Vectura, Varr.
units.tr: Carriage] Carriage, Cicer. Conveyance, Sipont. Transport, Cassiub. Conveyance, Sipont. Carriage, Fest. Transport, Caes. Carrying up, Tacit. Carrying together, Amm. Carriage, Varr.

units.la: Vector, vid. Nauta. Auriga.
units.tr: Passenger, see Nauta. Auriga.

units.la: Vecturam facere] Quint. Factitare vecturam, Gell. Velaturam facere. Vecturis vivere, Varr.
units.tr: To carry for hire] Quint. To carry for hire habitually, Gell. To make a sailing trip. To live by carrying, Varr.

units.la: Vegetare] Vegere, Non. Vid. Exhilarare aliquem.
units.tr: To enliven] To quicken, Non. See To cheer someone.

units.la: Vegetari] Vigere corporibus, Liv. Vigescunt pedes, Catul. Vegere, Sal.
units.tr: To be enlivened] To flourish in body, Liv. The feet grow strong, Catul. To quicken, Sal.

units.la: Vegetus] Vegetior aspectus, Col. Vigens mens, Lucr. Cicer. Vigentis sensus adolescentulus, Col. Vivax senectus, Plin. Vividus animus, Tacit. Experrectus, Col. Experrectiores apes.
units.tr: Lively] A more lively look, Col. A vigorous mind, Lucr. Cicer. Lively senses of a youth, Col. A long-lived old age, Plin. A lively spirit, Tacit. Awake, Col. Bees more awake.

units.la: Vehemens] Ardens studium. Fervens animus. Refervens crimen. Flagrans cupiditas. Calidior & ardentior animus, Cic. Fervidi animi vir, Liv. Æstuans animus, Catul. Calida juventus, Hor.
units.tr: Vehement] Burning zeal. A glowing spirit. A glowing crime. Burning desire. A hotter and more ardent spirit, Cic. A man of fiery spirit, Liv. A seething spirit, Catul. A hot-blooded youth, Hor.

units.la: Vehementer] Ferventer loqui, Cicer. Incensè & inflammanter, Gell. Pathetice tractare aliquid, Macrob. Acriter & ardenter causas agere, Plin. Iun. Ardenti studio facere aliquid, Cic.
units.tr: Vehemently] To speak fervently, Cicer. Inflamed and burning, Gell. To treat a subject pathetically, Macrob. To plead causes sharply and ardently, Plin. Iun. To do something with burning zeal, Cic.

units.la: Vehementia] Acies auctoritatis, Cic. Acumen saporis, Plin. Asperitas sententiarum, contentionis, orationis. Acerbitas sententiarum. Mucro defensionis. Acrimonia in oratione, Cic. Acrimonia animi, Non. Brassicæ, Cat. Acritas veritatis, Gell. Acritudo succi, Vitruv.
units.tr: Vehemence] The edge of authority, Cic. The sharpness of taste, Plin. Harshness of opinions, of contention, of speech. Bitterness of opinions. The point of a defence. Acrimony in speech, Cic. Acrimony of mind, Non. Of cabbage, Cat. Sharpness of truth, Gell. Pungency of juice, Vitruv.

units.la: Vehere] Portare, scil. curru, Cic. Naves portabant Legatos Romam, Liv. Ferre aliquid per æquor, Ovid. Vectare, Gell. Subvectare cymbâ corpora, Virg. Vejari stipites in plaustro, Fest. Vehiare, pro vectare, vectitare, Sipont.
units.tr: To carry] To carry, namely in a chariot, Cic. Ships carried envoys to Rome, Liv. To bear something across the sea, Ovid. To convey, Gell. To ferry bodies over the water in a boat, Virg. Stakes were carried on a wagon, Fest. Vehiare, for vectare, vectitare, Sipont.

units.la: Vehiculum] Veha brevis, Varr. Vectabulum, Sipont. Plo-stellum, Hor. Quadrigula, Cic. Curriculum, Curt. Curriculus, Varr. Tintinnabulum & Stirpiculæ olerum, Plaut. Scal. Lamb.
units.tr: Vehicle] A small carriage, Varr. A carriage bed, Sipont. A little wagon, Hor. A two-horse carriage, Cic. A chariot, Curt. A racing chariot, Varr. A tinkling bell and little stalks of herbs, Plaut. Scal. Lamb.

units.la: Vel, vid. Sive.
units.tr: Or, see Sive.

units.la: Velare] Advelare tempora lauro. Operit pellis humeros, nox terras, Virg. Cooperire telis, Liv. Vestire corpus spoliis ferarum, Lucan. Convestire, Cic. Circumvestire, Plin. Amicire: amicitur vitibus ulmus, Ovid. Tegit nox terras caligine, Lucr. Circumtegit cœlum omnia, id. Circumtectus est corio, Plaut. Obtegere, Cic. Prætegere, Plin. Iun. Subtegere, Amm. Supervestit cupressus aliquid folio, Plin. Obserere: obsita setis Io. Obit illum pellis leonis, Virg. Obnubit mare terras, ut cœlum nubes, Varr.
units.tr: To cover] To wreathe the temples with laurel. A skin covers the shoulders, night covers the lands, Virg. To cover with weapons, Liv. To clothe the body with the spoils of beasts, Lucan. To clothe thoroughly, Cic. To clothe all around, Plin. To wrap in: the elm is wrapped in vines, Ovid. Night covers the lands with darkness, Lucr. It covers all things with the sky, id. Covered with a hide, Plaut. To cover over, Cic. To cover in front, Plin. Iun. To cover from below, Amm. The cypress clothes something with foliage, Plin. To entangle: bristly with bristles, Io. The lion's skin covers him, Virg. The cloud covers the sea and the lands as the clouds cover the sky, Varr.

units.la: Velificare, vid. Navigare.
units.tr: Velificare: see Navigare.

units.la: Velim, vid. Cupere.
units.tr: Velim: see Cupere.

units.la: Velitari] Velitari adversus aliquem, Gell. Inter se, Plaut. Velitationem exercere, Id. Primas hastas jactare, Cic.
units.tr: Velitari] To skirmish against someone, Gell. Among themselves, Plaut. To carry on a skirmish, Id. To hurl the first spears, Cic.

units.la: Velitatio] Advelitatio, Fest. Velitaris pugna, Salust. Præludium rei castrensis & armaturæ exercere, Amm. Prolufio, Cic.
units.tr: Velitatio] Advelitatio, Fest. A skirmish, Sallust. To practise the prelude of military service and arms, Amm. A prelude, Cic.

units.la: Velites] Veles, itis. Volites. Miles levis armaturæ, Cicer. Ferentarii, Salust. Adscriptitii, Accensi, Rorarii, rii, Fest. Diocmitæ, Capit. Diocnitas legit, Robert. Constant. Dimachæ, Curt. Supernumerarii, Id. Levis armatura, (pro personis), Liv.
units.tr: Velites] Veles, itis. Volites. A light-armed soldier, Cicer. Ferentarii, Sallust. Adscriptitii, Accensi, Rorarii, Fest. Diocmitae, Capit. He reads Diocnitas, Robert. Constant. Dimachae, Curt. Supernumeraries, Id. Light armature (of persons), Liv.

units.la: Velle] Volo ire parare pisces, Plaut. Fert mea voluntas. Avere. Studeo audire, Cicer. Vobis verba dare, Ter. Ardere studio alicujus rei, Cicer. Jubeo te salvere, (i. volo) Plaut. Habeo, pro, aveo. Sen. Apul. Habeo audire quid afferant.
units.tr: Velle] I want to go and buy fish, Plaut. My will carries me. To long for. I am eager to hear, Cicer. To deceive you with words, Ter. To burn with zeal for something, Cicer. I bid you farewell (i.e. I wish), Plaut. Habeo, for aveo, Sen. Apul. I am eager to hear what they bring.

units.la: Vellere] Scindere capillos, Ovid. Conscindere aliquem capillis, Ter. Rumpere capillos, Ovid. Vellicare, Quint.
units.tr: Vellere] To tear the hair, Ovid. To tear someone by the hair, Ter. To tear out hair, Ovid. To pluck, Quint.

units.la: Vellicare aliquem] Pervellere aliquem, Cic. Lædere duris pollicibus aliquem, Propert. Morsicare, Fest. Lancinare, Mart.
units.tr: Vellicare aliquem] To pluck someone thoroughly, Cic. To hurt someone with hard fingers, Propert. To nip, Fest. To mangle, Mart.

units.la: Vellicatio] Vellicatus. Laceratio, Plin. Lancinatio, Celf.
units.tr: Vellicatio] A plucking. Laceration, Plin. Mangling, Celf.

units.la: Velocitas, Velociter, vid. Celeritas, &c.
units.tr: Velocitas, Velociter: see Celeritas, &c.

units.la: Velox] Pegaso velocior. Ferri Pegaseo volatu. Cursu prævertit ventos. Vid. Celer.
units.tr: Velox] Swifter than Pegasus. Carried on Pegasean flight. Outruns the winds in speed. See Celer.

units.la: Velum] Velamen, Lucan. Velamentum, Liv. Obtentus, us, Virg. Vid. Tegumentum.
units.tr: Velum] A veil, Lucan. A covering, Liv. A screen, Virg. See Tegumentum.

units.la: Velut, vid. Quasi.
units.tr: Velut: see Quasi.

units.la: Vena] Naturalis sipho. Via sanguinis. Rivus sanguinis, Plin. Flumen, quo corpus hominis irrigatur.
units.tr: Vena] A natural conduit. The path of the blood. A channel of blood, Plin. The river by which the human body is watered.

units.la: Venabulum] Lancea venatoria, Amm.
units.tr: Venabulum] A hunting spear, Amm.

units.la: Venalis] Vendibilis, Cic. Venalitius, Paul. IC. Vendi-tarius, Plaut. Addictus pretio. Nummarius, Cic. Promercalis, Col. Est in merce aliquid, Plin.
units.tr: Venalis] Saleable, Cic. Venal, Paul. IC. Saleable, Plaut. Given up for money. Mercenary, Cic. Fit for market, Col. Something is on sale, Plin.

units.la: Venari] Venari pantheras, Cic. Venaturam facere, Plin. Sectari apros, Virg. Leporem. Sequi, persequi feras, Ovid. Captare feras, Virg.
units.tr: Venari] To hunt panthers, Cic. To make a hunt, Plin. To chase boars, Virg. To hunt a hare. To pursue wild beasts, Ovid. To seize wild beasts, Virg.

units.la: Venatio] Venatura. Venatus, Plaut.
units.tr: Venatio] The hunt. The chase. The hunt, Plaut.

units.la: Venator] Vestigiator, Varr. (Latro, Virg.)
units.tr: Venator] A tracker, Varr. (A robber, Virg.)

units.la: Venatores avari]
units.tr: Venatores avari] Greedy hunters.

units.la: Venator sequitur fugientia, capta relinquit; Semper & inventis ulteriora petit.
units.tr: The hunter pursues what flees and leaves what he has caught; and always seeks what lies beyond what he has found.

units.la: Vendere aliquid] Venditare. Commutare pecunia, Cic. Ære mutare, Col. Veno exercere, Tacit. Venundare, Plin. Nundinantur judices pretio sententias, Apul. Nundinabit nabit pudorem, Firm. Addicere, abs. &, addicere pecuniâ, nummo sessertio, Cic. Distrahere fundum, Vlp. Caseus commodus pretio distrahitur, Apul.
units.tr: Vendere aliquid] To offer for sale. To exchange for money, Cic. To exchange for bronze, Col. To carry on a trade, Tacit. To sell off, Plin. Judges sell their verdicts for a price, Apul. He will sell off his modesty, Firm. To knock down, absolutely; and to sell for money, for a sesterce, Cic. To break up an estate, Vlp. Good cheese is sold for a price, Apul.

units.la: Vendicare sibi aliquid] Arrogare, Usurpare, Adsciscere, Attribuere sibi aliquid. Jure meo mihi aliquid sumo, vendico, Cic. Aliquid pro suo vendicare. Velut proprium sibi, vel alicui afferere aliquid, Quint. Usu facere suum, Sen. Beneficii sui aliquid facere, Suet. de Claud. Vid. Tribuere alicui.
units.tr: Vendicare sibi aliquid] To claim, usurp, assume, or attribute something to oneself. I claim something for myself by my own right, Cic. To claim something as one's own. To assert something as one's own property, as if it were proper to oneself, Quint. To make something one's own by use, Sen. To make something of one's own kindness, Suet. de Claud. See Tribuere alicui.

units.la: Venditare se nomine aliquo] Imponere sibi aliquam personam. Suscipere, induere, sumere alicujus personam. Profiteri; se dicere Philosophum. Similitudinem speciemque sapientis gerere. Sumere partes alicujus, Cic. Induere speciem; simulationem alicujus, Liv. Induere hostem, proditorem, Tac. Formam alterius gerere, Plaut. Agere naufragum: orbum, Quint. Præbere speciem scurrantis, Hor. Affectare diligentiam, Plin. Occupare, usurpare aliquid, Curt. Suet. Vid. Simulare.
units.tr: Venditare se nomine aliquo] To put a persona upon oneself. To take up, put on, or assume another's persona. To profess; to call oneself a philosopher. To bear the likeness and appearance of a wise man. To take on the role of someone, Cic. To put on the appearance or pretence of someone, Liv. To put on the enemy, the traitor, Tac. To bear another's form, Plaut. To play the shipwrecked man, or the bereaved, Quint. To show the appearance of a buffoon, Hor. To affect diligence, Plin. To seize or usurp something, Curt. Suet. See Simulare.

units.la: Venditio] Venditatio, Non. Venus, vel Vænus, us. Apul. Promercium. Distractio fundi, Vlp.
units.tr: Venditio] Venditatio, Non. Venus, or Vaenus, Apul. Merchandise. The distraction of an estate, Vlp.

units.la: Venefica ] Saga, Col. Pharmaceutria, Virg. Præstigiatrix, Plaut. Præcantrix, Var. Veratrix, Apul. Thessala mulier, ex Plaut. Striges. Mulieres volaticæ, Fest. Divinipotens, Apul. epith. Sagæ.
units.tr: Venefica] A witch, Col. A sorceress, Virg. An enchantress, Plaut. A charmer, Varr. A poisoner, Apul. A Thessalian woman, ex Plaut. Striges: flying women, Fest. Divinely powerful, Apul. an epithet of the witch.

units.la: Veneficus] Præstigiator, Plaut. Artium malarum doctor, Amm. Incantator, Firm.
units.tr: Veneficus] A sorcerer, Plaut. A teacher of evil arts, Amm. An enchanter, Firm.

units.la: Veneficus, adnom.] Venenarius, Delri. Pharmacus, Petron.
units.tr: Veneficus, adnom.] A poisoner, Delri. A poisoner, Petron.

units.la: Venenare aliquid] Inficere veneno, Virg. Infecit virus fila, Plin. Spargere venenum, Cic. Linere venenis ora. Tingere veneno, Ovid. Suffusa lingua veneno, (à suffundere) Id. Illitum veneno dolium, (ab illinere) Liv. Medicata tela veneno, (à medicari) Sili.
units.tr: Venenare aliquid] To infect with poison, Virg. He infected the threads with poison, Plin. To scatter poison, Cic. To smear the mouth with poisons. To dye with poison, Ovid. A tongue suffused with poison (from suffundere), Id. A jar smeared with poison (from illinere), Liv. Weapons medicated with poison (from medicari), Sil.

units.la: Venenatus] Venenosus, Cic. Virulentus serpens, Gell. Viriosus, Apul. Viriosus, Serv. Potens animal leti, genitumque nocere, Lucan. Medicatus boletus, Suet. Veneni-fer, Ovid. Delibutus veneno, Hor. Sanie, Cic. Inest illi virus, Ovid. Infectus aliquo, Stat.
units.tr: Venenatus] Poisonous, Cic. A venomous serpent, Gell. Venomous, Apul. Venomous, Serv. A creature powerful to bring death and born to harm, Lucan. A drugged mushroom, Suet. Poison-bearing, Ovid. Steeped in poison, Hor. Dripping with matter, Cic. The venom is in him, Ovid. Infected with something, Stat.

units.la: Venenum] Virus,Cic. Tabes veneni,Ovid. Tabes mortifera, Id.
units.tr: Venenum] Poison, Cic. The deadly rot of poison, Ovid. A deadly rot, Id.

units.la: Veneno aliquem occidere] Veneno necare, tollere. Venenum præbere, spargere, Cic. Præripere veneno fata, Flor. Veneno vitâ concessit, Tac. Toxico me morti dabo, Plaut. Miscere toxicum, Ovid.
units.tr: Veneno aliquem occidere] To kill someone with poison. To kill or remove by poison. To give or scatter poison, Cic. To snatch away fate by poison, Flor. He yielded his life to poison, Tac. I will give myself to death by poison, Plaut. To mix poison, Ovid.

units.la: Venerandus] Venerabilis, Ovid. Verendus senex, Claud. Reverenda canities, Id. Augustum caput, Ovid. Venerabundus, Liv.
units.tr: Venerandus] Venerable, Ovid. A reverend old man, Claud. Respected grey hair, Id. An august head, Ovid. Full of reverence, Liv.

units.la: Venerari] Veneratione prosequi,Paterc. Advenerari,Sil. Devenerari,Ovid. Vid. Honorare.
units.tr: Venerari] To honour with reverence, Paterc. To revere greatly, Sil. To revere from afar, Ovid. See Honorare.

units.la: Veneratio, vid. Observantia.
units.tr: Veneratio: see Observantia.

units.la: Venia] Remissio, Indulgentia, Vacatio, Impunitas, Cic. Ignoscentia, Gell.
units.tr: Venia] Remission, indulgence, exemption, impunity, Cic. Forgiveness, Gell.

units.la: Venia sit] Venia sit dicto, Cic. Bona venia: bona cum venia me audiatis. Date mihi hanc veniam: ad ignoscendum. Pacem ac veniam peto. Pace tua: magistri dixerim, Cic. Bona gratia,Vlp. Cum bona gratia, Cic. Salva gratia, Quint. Salva reverentia; vel ut Mart. Cum salva reverentia personarum. Honore dicto,Plin. Salvo honore. Honos auribus sit habitus, Curt. Salvo jure amicitiae: salvo officio, fide, lege, Cic. Salva magnitudine tuâ Domine, Plin.Iun. Propitiis auribus tuis,Sen. Et mihi quæso ignoscite, si appello talem virum sæpius, Cic. Honor præfandus est, Id. Per pacem te alloqui liceat,Plaut. Per gratiam,& amicitiam ab illo impetravi,Id.Salvâdignitate tuâ jocabor. Liceat mihi dicere. Nulla mala vestra gratia hoc à me dicatur. Quod sine invidia ejus dictum velim. Modo cum bona gratia à vobis audiar.
units.tr: Venia sit] Let it be pardoned, what I am about to say, Cic. With your good pardon: hear me with good grace. Grant me this pardon for forgiving. I ask for peace and pardon. With your leave, I would call him master, Cic. With good grace, Vlp. With good grace, Cic. With all due respect, Quint. With due respect, or as in Mart. With due respect for persons. With the honour preserved, Plin. With due honour. Let honour be given to the ears, Curt. With the right of friendship preserved; saving duty, faith, and law, Cic. With your greatness, Lord, preserved, Plin.Iun. With your ears kindly disposed, Sen. And I beg you to forgive me if I so often call such a man by that name, Cic. Honour must be spoken first, Id. May I address you in peace, Plaut. I obtained this from him through favour and friendship, Id. With your dignity preserved I will make a joke. Let me be allowed to say. Let nothing bad be said by me with your favour. Let it be said without any envy of him. Only with good grace may I be heard by you.

units.la: Veniam petere] Petere veniam errato. Pacem à Deo petere. A Diis pacem & veniam petere,Cic. Petere veniam in præteritum,Tac.Pacem exposcere,Virg.Pacem venialem poscere,Amm.Honore dicto aliquid referre,Plin.Isti in bonam partem interpreteris velim. Si quid peccavi, ac potius quia peccavi,ignosce. Velim,si qua offensiuncula est animi tui perversitate aliquorum, des te ad lenitatem, vel propter &c. vel etiam honoris mei causa. Sit erranti medicina confessio,Cic.
units.tr: Veniam petere] To ask pardon for an error. To ask peace from God. To ask peace and pardon from the gods, Cic. To ask pardon for the past, Tac. To demand peace, Virg. To seek a pardonable peace, Amm. To refer something with due honour, Plin. I would wish you to take that in good part. If I have sinned, or rather because I have sinned, forgive me. I would wish, if some small offence has arisen in your mind through the perversity of some men, that you incline yourself to gentleness, either on account of ... or even for the sake of my honour. Let confession be the remedy for one who has erred, Cic.

units.la: Veniam dare, vid. Ignoscere.
units.tr: Veniam dare, see Ignoscere.

units.la: Venire] Advenire domum, Plaut. Pervenire aliquo ad, in, Cic. Permanare aliquò. Perlabi supra solis orbem. Perlabi ad, Lucr. Ventitare domum alicujus. Devolare. Advolare, adesse ad judicium. Devenire ad, Cic. Devenire in, Hirt. Adventare, Cic. Aditare ad, Enn. Ventare, Fest.
units.tr: Venire] To come to the house, Plaut. To arrive somewhere at or in, Cic. To spread through to somewhere. To glide past above the orbit of the sun. To glide to, Lucr. To visit someone's house often. To fly down. To fly to, to be present at a court. To arrive at, Cic. To come into, Hirt. To draw near, Cic. To go to, Enn. Ventare, Fest.

units.la: Venire in, vid. Periclitari.
units.tr: Venire in, see Periclitari.

units.la: Venire ad, vid. Devenire.
units.tr: Venire ad, see Devenire.

units.la: Venire ad finem] Attingere calcem. Vid. Absolvere.
units.tr: Venire ad finem] To reach the heel, the goal. See Absolvere.

units.la: Veni] Adesdum.
units.tr: Veni] Come here.

units.la: Veni tu desiderate] Exorere sol.
units.tr: Veni tu desiderate] Come, you longed-for one: rise, sun.

units.la: Venter] Alvus, abdomen, Cic. Profundum, Scal. Dolium pertusum, Fest. Ingluvies, Ter. Pantices, Plaut.
units.tr: Venter] The belly, abdomen, Cic. A deep pit, Scal. A leaky cask, Fest. Gluttony, Ter. The paunch, Plaut.

units.la: Ventris causa quidvis pati] E flamma cibum petere.
units.tr: Ventris causa quidvis pati] To suffer anything for the belly's sake. To seek food from the flame.

units.la: Ventilabrum] Capisterium, vel Scaphisterium, Col.
units.tr: Ventilabrum] A winnowing shovel, Col. or a winnowing fan, Col.

units.la: Ventilare] Ventilabris frumentum jactare, Col. Subjactare ventilabris, Var. Excernere flatu frumenta, Col. Evannare levissimum foras extra aream, Var. Eventilare. Vento separare, Col. Vannare frumentum, Lucil.
units.tr: Ventilare] To toss grain with winnowing shovels, Col. To throw under the shovels, Var. To blow grain apart, Col. To winnow the lightest chaff out of the threshing floor, Var. To separate by wind, Col. To winnow grain, Lucil.

units.la: Ventilat aura aliquid] Sal. Permulcet flatu austri spiritus aram, Cic. Inspirantes ramis arborum auræ, Quint. Incursat in arborem ventus, Sen. Retrodat capillos aura. Sinuantur vestes flamine, Ovid. Aura dulcis spirat. Adspirant auræ, Virg. Undantem chlamydem quassando aliquis facit, Plaut.
units.tr: Ventilat aura aliquid] Sal. A breath of the south wind softens the altar, Cic. Breezes breathing through the branches of trees, Quint. The wind rushes at the tree, Sen. The breeze blows back the hair. Garments are rippled by the blast, Ovid. A sweet breeze blows. The breezes breathe upon, Virg. Someone shakes the billowing cloak, Plaut.

units.la: Ventosus] Spiritalis. Spiritale genus machinæ. Pneumaticus, Vitr. Pneusticum dolium, Decalemp.
units.tr: Ventosus] Spiritual. A spiritual kind of machine. Pneumatic, Vitr. A pneustic cask, Decalemp.

units.la: Ventrosus homo] Ventricosus. Ventriosus, Plaut. Promisso ventre, Col. Ventre projecto, projectiori, Suet. Prominulo, Iul. Capit. Ventre propenso, Perf. Homo cum collativo ventre, Plaut. Venter, abs. Panticib. laxis lanius, Mart. In ventrem crescit.
units.tr: Ventrosus homo] Big-bellied. Potbellied, Plaut. With a projecting belly, Col. With the belly thrust out, more prominent, Suet. Prominent in the belly, Iul. Capit. With the belly leaning forward, Perf. A man with a full belly, Plaut. Venter, absolutely: a butcher with loose paunches, Mart. He grows into his belly.

units.la: Venturus] Veniens: In annum venientem curas extendere, Virg. Futurum tempus. Appropinquante morte, Cic.
units.tr: Venturus] Coming. To extend cares into the coming year, Virg. Future time. With death approaching, Cic.

units.la: Ventus] Aëris fluxus, Plin. Fluor aëris, Arnob. Aëris fluens unda, Vitr. Agitando percitus aër, Lucr. Flatus, Cic. Spiritus, Col. Flabra, pro vento sumit, Suet. Flamina spirant, Ovid, Auræ, Id, Anima, pro vento, Virg. Æolus, ventorum Deus. Aëreum flumen, diluvium. Aëris de loco in locum migratio. Humiditatum exsiccatio. Putredinum expurgatio. Scopæ mundi. Discussor nebularum.
units.tr: Ventus] A flow of air, Plin. A flux of air, Arnob. A flowing wave of air, Vitr. Air stirred by agitation, Lucr. A blast, Cic. A breath, Col. A breeze, Spiritus, Col. Flabra, used for wind, Suet. The breezes blow, Ovid. Breezes, Id. Breath, used for wind, Virg. Aeolus, the god of the winds. An airy flood, a deluge. The migration of air from place to place. The drying of moisture. The purging of putrefactions. The brooms of the world. The dispeller of clouds.

units.la: Ventus secundus] Ventus secundans, Tac. Ventus favens, Ovid. Ferens, Virg. Animas secundas, vocat Lucr.
units.tr: Favourable wind: "favouring wind", Tac.; "favourable wind", Ovid.; "bearing wind", Virg.; Lucr. calls it "favourable breezes."

units.la: Ventis secundis navigare] Aquilone secundo ferri.
units.tr: To sail with favourable winds: to be carried along by a favourable north wind.

units.la: Venum dare] Proponere aliquid venale, Cic. Prostituere voces foro, Ovid. Proscribere venale aliquid. Hastæ subjicere. Hastâ posita bona præconis voci subjicere, Cic. Addicere bona in publicum, Cæs. Auctionari aliquid. Auctionem vendere. Vendo bona constituta auctione, Cic. Auctionem facere, Plaut. Producere servos. Præbere servos venales, Ter. Inscripsi ædes illico mercede, Plaut. Transcribere aliquid. Proponere auctionem, Quint. Prostat aliquid pretio, Ovid. Venum ire omnia illi in animo hæserat, Sallust.
units.tr: To sell off: to put something up for sale, Cic. To offer words for sale in the forum, Ovid. To post something as for sale. To put up for auction. To put goods under the auctioneer's hammer, Cic. To sell goods to the crier's voice, the auction having been held. To give goods over to the public, Caes. To auction something. To sell at auction. To sell goods after an auction has been set, Cic. To hold an auction, Plaut. To bring slaves out for sale. To offer slaves for sale, Ter. I have put the house up for sale straight away for a price, Plaut. To transfer something. To advertise an auction, Quint. Something is offered for sale at a price, Ovid. He had fixed in his mind that everything should be sold off, Sallust.

units.la: Venus] Stella Veneris, Cic. Lucifer, Plin. Phosphorus, Mart. Jubar, Apul. Fest. Noctiluca Venus, Lævin. Hesperus, Cic. Vesper, Catul. Vesperugo, Plaut. Hesperugo, Sen. Mundi genitalis calor.
units.tr: Venus: the star of Venus, Cic.; Lucifer, Plin.; Phosphorus, Mart.; the brightness, Apul., Fest.; Venus the night-shining, Lævin.; Hesperus, Cic.; Vesper, Catul.; Vesperugo, Plaut.; Hesperugo, Sen.; the generative warmth of the world.

units.la: Venustus] Ipsa Venere venustior, Er, Vid. Formosus.
units.tr: Charming: more charming than Venus herself, Er. See Formosus.

units.la: Vepres &c. vid. Spina.
units.tr: Thorns, etc.: see Spina.

units.la: Ver] Verculum, Plaut. Perfida nubiferi veris inconstantia, Lucan. Pratorum pictor.
units.tr: Spring: a little spring, Plaut. The treacherous inconstancy of the cloud-bringing spring, Lucan. The painter of the meadows.

units.la: Veracitas, vid. Veritas.
units.tr: Truthfulness: see Veritas.

units.la: Verax] Verus. Veritatis custos. Habet fidem. Fidei plenus vir, Cic. Veridicus, Lucr. Cic. Ex vero ductum cognomen, Hor.
units.tr: Truthful: true. Guardian of the truth. Holds to faith. A man full of faith, Cic. Speaking the truth, Lucr., Cic. A surname derived from truth, Hor.

units.la: Verberare] Verberitare, Fest. Verberibus accipere aliquem, Cic. Cædere verberibus, Ter. Pulsare hominem. Percutere manu, Cic. Obverberare baculo, Apul. Tundere latera, Cic. Multare verberibus, Tac. Ferire aliquem, Plaut. Obtundere pugnis pectora, Firm. Depavire, vel depavire aliquem, Fest. Infligere plagam alicui, Cic. Plagam imponere. Flagris ferventem facere. Sauciare virgis ad saturitatem, Plaut. Ad satietatem trucidare, Liv.
units.tr: To beat: to beat with blows, Cic.; "verberitare", Fest. To strike with a rod, Ter. To strike a man. To hit with the hand, Cic. To strike round about with a staff, Apul. To thump the sides, Cic. To punish with blows, Tac. To strike someone, Plaut. To pummel the breast with fists, Firm. To beat someone soundly, Fest. To inflict a blow on someone, Cic. To lay on a blow. To make someone smart under the lash. To flog someone to satiety, Plaut. To butcher to satiety, Liv.

units.la: Verberatio, vid. Plaga.
units.tr: Beating: see Plaga.

units.la: Verbero] Flagrio. Mastigia. Literatus, Plaut. Irrigatus flagris. Gymnasium flagri. Ulmorum Acheruns. Plagiger, Cic. Plagosus, Id. Polluctus virgis. Caesus virgis sub furca, Id. Flagellis ad mortem caesus. Peruftus funibus latus. Sectus flagellis, Hor. Bucaeda, Plaut. Quasi oftreatum tergum ulceribus gestitat. Carnificum, vel carnificinum cribrum. Tribunus vapularis, Id. Fractor ferularum, Sidon. Vibicibus livedinis totam cutem depictus, Apul. Reduviae flagri. Conservum lassitudo, Titin.
units.tr: Scourger: a flogger. A whipping-boy. A schoolmaster, Plaut. Soaked with whips. A gymnasium of the lash. An Acheron of elms. Bearing the blows, Cic. Full of blows, Id. Beaten with rods. Beaten with rods under the yoke, Id. Flogged to death. A side scorched with cords. Cut with whips, Hor. A bucaeda, Plaut. He carries his back as if it were clotted with ulcers. A sieve of executioners, or of executioners' making. A tribune who is beaten, Id. A breaker of rods, Sidon. His whole skin painted with weals of livid bruises, Apul. Rag-whips. The weariness of a fellow-slave, Titin.

units.la: Verbi causa, vid. Exempli causa.
units.tr: For example: see Exempli causa.

units.la: Verbositas &c. vid. Garrulitas.
units.tr: Wordiness, etc.: see Garrulitas.

units.la: Verbo tenus] Verbo promittere, Cic. Sum verna verbo, Plaut. Voce, Virg. Loquelariter, Cic. Oratione benefi-cus, Plaut. Vid. Pollicitari, Promittere.
units.tr: In word only: to promise in words, Cic. I am a slave in word only, Plaut. By voice, Virg. Speaking eloquently, Cic. A benefactor only in speech, Plaut. See Pollicitari, Promittere.

units.la: Verbum] Vocabulum, Vox, Dictum, Cic. Dictio, Quint.
units.tr: Word: a term, a voice, a saying, Cic. A word, Quint.

units.la: Verbum elabitur, vid. Elabitur.
units.tr: A word slips out: see Elabitur.

units.la: Verba aspera] Senticosa verba.
units.tr: Harsh words: thorny words.

units.la: Verba sine re, frustra] Ubi opus est factis, inutiles sunt sermones. Ubi factis opus est, verba non sufficiunt. Verbum sine factis vanum.
units.tr: Words without deeds, in vain: where deeds are needed, speeches are useless. Where deeds are needed, words do not suffice. A word without deeds is empty.

units.la: Verba inania] Verba sine penu & pecunia.
units.tr: Empty words: words without provisions and money.

units.la: Verbum verbo exprimere] Cic. Exprimere ad verbum de Graecis literis. Exprimere verbum e verbo, de verbo, Id. Totidem verbis transferre. Verbum pro verbo reddere. Verbum verbis reddere, Id. Verbum verbo reddere, Hor. Verba de verbis trahere, Quint. Ad verbum excerpere aliquid ex scripto alieno, Suet.
units.tr: To render word for word: Cic. To translate Greek literature word for word. To render word from word, Id. To carry over in just so many words. To give word for word. To render word by word, Id.; Hor. To draw words out of words, Quint. To excerpt something word for word from another's writing, Suet.

units.la: Vere, a ver] Vernatione, Verno, Plin. Ineunte vere, Cic. Cum hirundine prima, Hor. Incipiente vere.
units.tr: In spring: the springtime, springing, Plin. At the beginning of spring, Cic. With the first swallow, Hor. As spring begins.

units.la: Vere, a verus] Verissime. Revera. Re ipsa. Ex veritate, Cic. Verum, Ter. Vero, Plaut. Ex vero nomine, Id. Ex bona fide, Plin. Iun. Bona fide, Sen. Historica fide, Ovid. In veritate, Quint. A vero & recto sensu, Cic. Ab re nominarunt. Ab imo pectore verae voces eliciuntur, Lucr. Veridice, Amm. Incorrupte, incorruptius judicare. Ex animi sententia. Convenienter, Cic. Liquido jurare, Ter. Tangens aram assevero, ex Cic.
units.tr: Truly: most truly. Really. In fact. From the truth, Cic. Truly, Ter. Indeed, Plaut. By the true name, Id. In good faith, Plin. Iun. In good faith, Sen. In historical faith, Ovid. In truth, Quint. In the true and plain sense, Cic. They named things from the reality. True voices are drawn from the depths of the breast, Lucr. Truthfully, Amm. To judge uncorruptly, more uncorruptly. From the opinion of one's mind. Fittingly, Cic. To swear clearly, Ter. Touching the altar I swear solemnly, from Cic.

units.la: Parum vere] Extra veritatis curriculum cursum est sæpe.
units.tr: Not quite truly: it is often a course run outside the track of truth.

units.la: Verecunde] Verecunditer, Non. Pudenter vivere: aliquem appellare; Cic.
units.tr: Modestly: modestly, Non. To live chastely; to address someone, Cic.

units.la: Verecundia] Erubescentia, Sipont. Vid. Pudicitia.
units.tr: Modesty: blushing, Sipont. See Pudicitia.

units.la: Verecundia grata] Verecundi bene audiunt.
units.tr: Modesty is pleasing: the modest are well received.

units.la: Verecundia ornat juvenem] Verecundia in adolescente bonum signum.
units.tr: Modesty adorns a young man: modesty in a youth is a good sign.

units.la: Verecundus] Frontis integræ homo, Papin. Molli admodum fronte, Quint. Verecundiæ particeps. Virginali verecundiâ homo. Pudens adolescens. Pudentissimus. Pudorem & pudicitiam colit, Cic.
units.tr: Modest: a man of unblemished brow, Papin. With a very soft brow, Quint. Sharing in modesty. A man of maidenly modesty. A bashful youth. Most bashful. He cultivates shame and chastity, Cic.

units.la: Veredarius] Equorum permutatione veloci vehens. Cursus publici celeri mutatione vectus, Amm. Ancarius, vel Angarius, Lucil. Brutiani, Fest. id est. Cursores publici, Scal. Gerones literarum, Fulgent. Armillatus cursor, Pegasarius, Bud.
units.tr: Post-rider: one who carries by swift exchange of horses. Public transport conveyed by quick change, Amm. Ancarius or Angarius, Lucil. Brutiani, Fest., that is, public couriers, Scal. Gerones of letters, Fulgent. An armlet-wearing courier, Pegasarius, Bud.

units.la: Veredus] Vector, Apul. Celes, Cæl. Rhod. Cursualis equus, Cassiod. Qui cursus publici causa præbetur.
units.tr: Post-horse: a carrier, Apul. A swift horse, Cael. Rhod. A running horse, Cassiod. One provided for the sake of the public post.

units.la: Verenda] Pudibunda membra, Lampr. Pars nostri pudibunda, Ovid. Inguen, Liv. Genitale, & Genitalia, Plin. Genitales partes corporis. Genitalia loca; naturalia loca, & Naturalia, abs. Col. Locus, Petron. Partes illæ, quas pudor communis, quas naturalis verecundiæ lex abscondere jubet: quas inter aures castas sine venia nefas est, ac sine honoribus appellare præfatis, Arnob. Pars, qua discernitur homo mas an fœmina sit, Var. Res Veneris, & Genitales res Veneris, Lucr. Res illæ, Arnob. Obscœnæ partes, Ovid.
units.tr: Private parts: shameful limbs, Lampr. The part of us that is shameful, Ovid. The groin, Liv. Genitals, Plin. The genital parts of the body. Genital places; natural places, and "naturalia", abs. Col. A place, Petron. Those parts which common shame, and the law of natural modesty, bid us hide, and which it is wrong to name among chaste ears without apology, Arnob. The part by which one is distinguished as male or female, Varro. The matters of Venus, and the genital matters of Venus, Lucr. Those things, Arnob. Obscene parts, Ovid.

units.la: Vereri] Vereri aliquem, alicui, aliquid de aliqua re, Cic. Vereri aliquid ab aliquo. Revereri alicujus adventum, Ter. Subvereri. Suspensus sum metu, vel exspectatione alicujus rei. Reformidare vulgi reprehensionem, Cic. Affor-midare ne pereat, Plaut. Contineor auctoritate alicujus; Cicer.
units.tr: To fear: to fear someone, to be afraid of someone, of something, about some matter, Cic. To dread something from someone. To await someone's coming with dread, Ter. To be afraid of something. I am held in suspense by fear or expectation of something. To dread the public's censure, Cic. To be frightened lest he perish, Plaut. I am restrained by someone's authority, Cic.

units.la: Verisimile est] Veri & vero simile est. Probabile est. Proxime ad verum accedit, Cic. Vero proximum, Hor. Veritati proximum. Possibile est, Quint. Vid. seqq. & Possibilis.
units.tr: It is likely: it is like the truth and truly like. It is probable. It comes very close to the truth, Cic. Next to the truth, Hor. Close to the truth. It is possible, Quint. See what follows and Possibilis.

units.la: Verisimilis ] Veri similis. Vero simile videtur. Verisimillimum mihi videtur. Probabilis causa. Credibilis conjectura, Cic. Vero propius est, Tac. Res credula, (passive) Ovid.
units.tr: Likely: like the truth. It seems like the truth. It seems most like the truth to me. A probable cause. A credible conjecture, Cic. Nearer to the truth, Tac. A credulous matter (passive), Ovid.

units.la: Verisimiliter ] Probabiliter dicere. Credibiliter confingere, Cic.
units.tr: Plausibly: to speak probably. To invent credibly, Cic.

units.la: Veritas] Verum. Veriloquium. Vera ratio. Fides, Cic. Rem loquitur, Plaut. Distat à re ipsa atque veritate, Cic. Veracitas, Sipont. Nihil absonum fidei, Liv. Filia temporis, apud Gell.
units.tr: Truth: the true thing. True speech. Sound reason. Faithfulness, Cic. It speaks the matter, Plaut. It differs from the thing itself and from the truth, Cic. Veracity, Sipont. Nothing discordant with faith, Liv. Daughter of time, quoted in Gell.

units.la: Veritas clara ] Luce meridiana clarius. Mero meridie clarius.
units.tr: Clear truth: clearer than the light of midday. Clearer than undiluted noon.

units.la: Veritas ipsa] Sibyllae folium. Sibylla effata est.
units.tr: Truth itself: a leaf of the Sibyl. The Sibyl has spoken.

units.la: Veritas simplex] Simplex veritatis oratio. Veritatem sine dote quaere.
units.tr: Plain truth: the plain speech of truth. Seek truth without a dowry.

units.la: Veritate nihil efficacius] Veritas invincibilis, nam victa etiam vincit tandem.
units.tr: Nothing is more effective than truth: truth is invincible, for even when beaten it conquers in the end.

units.la: Veritatem dicere] Melius dices: Verum dicere, Plaut. Vera dicere, praedicare, Ter. Haec ex oraculo Apollinis Pythii edita tibi puta; nihil potest esse verius, Cic. Delphis tibi responsum dicito, Plaut. Veritatis arci insidere.
units.tr: To speak the truth: better, "verum dicere", Plaut. To speak true things and proclaim them, Ter. Take this as if it were pronounced by the oracle of Pythian Apollo; nothing can be truer, Cic. Tell yourself the answer given at Delphi, Plaut. To sit on the citadel of truth.

units.la: Vermiculari, id est, vermiculis infestari]Vermiculantur arbores, Plin. Verminare, Sen. Scatere vermibus, Col. Exspirant vermes cadavera. Effervent vermes, Lucr. Animantum copia tanta, exos & exsanguis tumidos perfluctuat artus, Id.
units.tr: To be wormy, that is, to be infested with worms: trees are wormy, Plin. To be full of worms, Sen. To swarm with worms, Col. Corpses breathe out worms. Worms seethe forth, Lucr. Such a multitude of creatures swarms through the swollen limbs, bloodless and boneless, Id.

units.la: Vermiculosus] Verminosus, Plin.
units.tr: Wormy: full of worms, Plin.

units.la: Vermina, morbi genus ] Tormina, Cic. Tormines, pl. m. Non. Torsio, rosio stomachi: Rosio intestinorum. Ileos, vel Ileus. Dysenteria, Plin. Strophus, Celf. Cordapsus. Volvolus, Rhodig.
units.tr: Gripes, a kind of disease: colic, Cic. Gripes, plural, Non. Twisting or gnawing of the stomach: gnawing of the bowels. Ileus or ileos. Dysentery, Plin. Strophus, Celf. Cordapsus. Volvulus, Rhodig.

units.la: Verminosus, qui morbo intestinorum laborat] Torminosus, Cic. Iliosus, dysentericus, Plin. Torminib. afficior, Plin. Intestina mihi torquentur, Celf. Vermino, Scal.
units.tr: Wormy, one who suffers from a bowel disease: griped, Cic. Ileac, dysenteric, Plin. I am afflicted with gripes, Plin. My bowels are twisted, Celf. Vermino, Scal.

units.la: Vermis] Vermen, Lucr. Animans exos & exsangue, Id.
units.tr: Worm: a worm, Lucr. A creature bloodless and boneless, Id.

units.la: Vernare, vid. Florere.
units.tr: To be in bloom: see Florere.

units.la: Verrere] Converrere, pugare stabulum, Col. Scopare, Cel. Rhod.
units.tr: To sweep: to sweep up, to clean out a stall, Col. To sweep, Cels. Rhod.

units.la: Verruca] Myrmecion, Cels. Verrucula, Col.
units.tr: Wart: a wart [μυρμήκιον], Cels. A little wart, Col.

units.la: Versare, vid. Vertere.
units.tr: To turn: see Vertere.

units.la: Versatilis]Versabilis homo ad omne momentum, Amm. Versutus, Lamb. Versuta rota figuli. Versutior quam rota figuli. Pro rota illo uti licet, Plaut. Versabundus turbo, Lucr. Volubilis, Cic. Actuosus histrio, Fest.
units.tr: Changeable: a man changeable at every moment, Amm. Crafty, Lamb. A potter's wheel that turns quickly. Quicker than a potter's wheel. One may use him as a wheel, Plaut. A whirling top, Lucr. Revolving, Cic. A busy actor, Fest.

units.la: Versicolor] Discolor, Apul. Discolorius, Petron. Discolora vestis, Martian. Omnicolor, Lucil. Multicolor, Plin. Bicolor myrtus. Ovid. Albis maculis bicolor equus, Maculis bos insignis. Capreoli sparsis pellibus albo, Virg. Variae lynces, Id. Varia loris latera, Plaut. Maculosa cutis. Pantherina mensa. Apiatus: Mensa apiata, crispa, densa grani congerie. Plin. Varietate macularum conspicua mensa, Sen. Variegatus, Apul. Interalbicans. Leucostictos, Plin. Maculis internigrantibus albae, Stat.
units.tr: Many-coloured: of different colour, Apul. More varied in colour, Petron. A garment of various colour, Martian. Of every colour, Lucil. Of many colours, Plin. A two-coloured myrtle, Ovid. A horse two-coloured with white spots; an ox marked with spots. Roe-deer with skins sprinkled with white, Virg. Varied lynxes, Id. Flanks striped with straps, Plaut. Mottled skin. A panther-patterned table. A table of spotted wood, crisp, dense with a heap of grain, Plin. A table conspicuous for the variety of its markings, Sen. Variegated, Apul. Between-white. Leucostictos, Plin. White with blackish spots within, Stat.

units.la: Versificari] Versificare, Quint. Versus fundere, facere, conficere. Versibus aliquid scribere, dicere. Numeris persequi aliquid, Cic. Versus scribere, componere, Hor. Deducere carmen & tenuare, Propert. Poëtari, Enn.
units.tr: To versify: Quint. To pour out, make or compose verses. Cic. To write or speak something in verses. Cic. To set something down in metre. Hor. To write or compose verses. Propert. To spin out a song and make it fine. Enn. To write poetry.

units.la: Versificatio, &c. vid. Poësis, &c.
units.tr: Versificatio, etc.: see Poesis, etc.

units.la: Versipellis] Bispellio, Vlp. Anguillae instar lubricus. Duodecim artium magister. Getae versutior, Vid. Astutus.
units.tr: Versipellis: Vlp. a sly fellow. Slippery as an eel. Master of twelve arts. More cunning than a Getan. See Astutus.

units.la: Versipellis aeque] In eodem ludo doctus.
units.tr: Versipellis aeque: Learned in the same game.

units.la: Versus] Metrum, Col. Vorsa facundia, Apul. Vid. Poësis.
units.tr: Versus: Col. metre. Apul. turned eloquence. See Poesis.

units.la: Versutia, vid. Sophisma.
units.tr: Versutia, see Sophisma.

units.la: Versutus, vid. Versatilis, & Astutus.
units.tr: Versutus, see Versatilis and Astutus.

units.la: Vertagus] Vertragus, Henr. Steph. Turn. Vertraha, Gratio. Canis venaticus grandior & agilior.
units.tr: Vertagus: Henr. Steph. Turn. vertragus. Gratio vertraha. A hunting dog, larger and swifter.

units.la: Vertebra] Vertibulum, Lactant. Verticula, Lucil. Verticulum, Gloss. Gotfred. Spondylus, Plin.
units.tr: Vertebra: Lactant. vertibulum. Lucil. verticula. Gloss. Gotfred. verticulum. Plin. spondylus.

units.la: Vertere] Versare, Quint. Obvertere navem. Convertere, Cic. Torquere in varias partes, Plin. Circumrotare machinam. Convibrare linguam, Apul.
units.tr: Vertere: Quint. to turn round. To turn a ship about. Cic. to convert. Plin. to twist in various directions. To spin a machine round. Apul. to shake the tongue about.

units.la: Vertere in rem suam, vid. Utire ad suum commodum.
units.tr: Vertere in rem suam, see Uti ad suum commodum.

units.la: Vervex] Vervex sectarius, Plaut.
units.tr: Vervex: A sectarian sheep. Plaut.

units.la: Verus] Justus dominus alicujus rei, Cic. Ipsissimus, Plaut. Ex vero nomen tibi erit, Ovid. Vid. Verax.
units.tr: Verus: Cic. the rightful owner of something. Plaut. the very own. Ovid. From the truth your name will come. See Verax.

units.la: Veraloqui, vid. Veritatem dicere.
units.tr: Veraloqui, see Veritatem dicere.

units.la: Vera bona meliora fucatis ] Melius pallens aurum, quàm fulgens orichalcum.
units.tr: Vera bona meliora fucatis: Pale gold is better than shining brass.

units.la: Vesania, vid. Delirium.
units.tr: Vesania, see Delirium.

units.la: Vesanus, vid. Amens. Stolidus.
units.tr: Vesanus, see Amens. Stolidus.

units.la: Vescus, vid. Macer.
units.tr: Vescus, see Macer.

units.la: Vesci, vid. Frui.
units.tr: Vesci, see Frui.

units.la: Vesica] Vesicula, Lucr. Uterculus, vel utriculus apum, Plin.
units.tr: Vesica: Lucr. a little bladder. Plin. the little womb or little bag of bees.

units.la: Vesicam levare, vid. Mejere.
units.tr: Vesicam levare, see Mejere.

units.la: Vesicula in pisce] Vesica vento plena, Aut, Vela vento plena. Folliculus.
units.tr: Vesicula in pisce: A bladder full of wind; Aut: a sail full of wind. A little sac.

units.la: Vesper] Vesperus. Vespera. Vespertinum tempus, Cic. Vesperum tempus, Plin. Serum diei. In serum aliquid trahere, Liv. Præceps in noctem diei tempus, Curt. Dies in noctem vergens, Sen. Vesperatus dies, Id. Nocturnus, (Nomen.) Stat. Lucernarium, Aug. Primæ tenebræ.
units.tr: Vesper: Vesperus. Vespera. Cic. evening time. Plin. the evening time. The late part of the day. Liv. to drag something into the late hours. Curt. falling headlong into the night, the time of day. Sen. the day sinking into night. Id. an evening-like day. Stat. Nocturnus (as a noun). Aug. lamp-lighting time. The first darkness.

units.la: Vesperascit] Vesperat, Gell. Advesperascit, Cic. Invesperascit, Tacit. Declinat in vesperum dies, Col. Inclinat se Sol. Præceps in occasum est Sol, Liv. Sol est in occasum, Col. Tabescit dies, Plaut. In serum protracta dimicatione, Suet. Dies inclinatus in tempus pomeridianum, Cic.
units.tr: Vesperascit: Gell. it is growing towards evening. Cic. it draws on towards evening. Tacit. it grows late towards evening. Col. the day declines towards evening. The sun sinks. Liv. the sun falls headlong to its setting. Col. the sun is setting. Plaut. the day wastes away. Suet. a fight drawn out into the late hours. Cic. the day inclined towards the afternoon.

units.la: Vesperi] Vespere. Pervesperi, Cic. Vesperâ primâ, Cæs. Vesperascente die, Tac. Vesperascente cœlo, Æmil. Prob. Serò, Cic. Obscurâ luce, Virg. Ante lucernam, Vopisc. Sub noctem, Hor. Vespertinis matutinisque perunctos, Plin. Inclinato sole, die.
units.tr: Vesperi: Vespere. Cic. late in the evening. Caes. early in the evening. Tac. as the day grows towards evening. Æmil. Prob. as the sky grows dark. Cic. late. Virg. in dim light. Vopisc. before the lamp is lit. Hor. at nightfall. Plin. those washed in evening and morning. With the sun inclined, in the day.

units.la: Vespertilio ] Animal volucre biforme, Non. Nycteris. Avis non avis, Cæl. Rhod. Mus alatus, Gesner. Monstrum avium.
units.tr: Vespertilio: Non. a winged animal of double form. Nycteris. Cael. Rhod. a bird that is not a bird. Gesner a winged mouse. A monster of birds.

units.la: Vespertinus] Vesper, ra, rum, Plin. Hora vespera. Serotinum tempus : serotina hora, Sipont.
units.tr: Vespertinus: Plin. evening, adjective. An evening hour. A late time; Sipont. a late hour.

units.la: Vespillo] Vispillo, Apul. Vespa, Fest. Humator, Lucan. Funerarius, Firm. Pollinctor, Plaut. Sandapilarius, Bud. Libitinarius, Vlp. Uctor (f. cadaverum.)
units.tr: Vespillo: Apul. vispillo. Fest. vespa. Lucan. an undertaker. Firm. a funeral man. Plaut. a corpse-washer. Bud. sandapilarius. Vlp. libitinarius. Uctor (perhaps for cadaverum, a carrier of corpses).

units.la: Vestibulum ] Prothyrum, Vlp. Propyleum, Cic. Præstega, æ, Rebert. Tit.
units.tr: Vestibulum: Vlp. prothyrum. Cic. propylaeum. Rebert. Tit. praestega.

units.la: Vestigare, vid. Indagare. Odorari.
units.tr: Vestigare, see Indagare. Odorari.

units.la: Vestigium ] Signa pedum, Lucr. Viarum indicia, Lucil. Virg.
units.tr: Vestigium: Lucr. the marks of feet. Lucil. Virg. signs of the roads.

units.la: Vestire aliquem ] Amicire, Suet. Tunicare, Varr. Induere alicui vestes, Ovid. Ornare aliquem, Propert. Adornatum forum magnifico ornatu, Cic. Vestem præbere, Plaut.
units.tr: Vestire aliquem: Suet. to put a cloak on someone. Varr. to dress in a tunic. Ovid. to put clothes on someone. Propert. to adorn someone. Cic. the forum adorned with magnificent display. Plaut. to provide clothing.

units.la: Vestis ] Vestitus, vestimentum, indumentum, Cic. Tegumentum corporis, Liv. Vestiarium, Sen. Velamen corporis, Col. Cultus, Liv.
units.tr: Vestis: Cic. clothing, garment, covering. Liv. a covering of the body. Sen. a wardrobe. Col. a covering of the body. Liv. dress, attire.

units.la: Vestis ostendit animum] Discincta vestis, discinctus animus. Ostendit vestis quales intrinsecus estis.
units.tr: Vestis ostendit animum: Loose clothing, loose mind. Your clothes show what sort of people you are inside.

units.la: Veteramenta] Senecta anguium, Plin. Vetustas rerum, Liv. Vetustas anguium exuritur, Ovid.
units.tr: Veteramenta: Plin. the old skin of snakes. Liv. the age of things. Ovid. the old skin of snakes is burnt.

units.la: Veteramentarius, vid. Cerdo.
units.tr: Veteramentarius, see Cerdo.

units.la: Vetare] Prætor sanxit edicto, ne. Prohibere, Cic. Prohibere & vetare quin, Id. Prohibere minaciter, Plaut. Arguere: arguit imponi mensis animalia, Ovid. Arcuit, leguntquidam. Vid. Interdicere.
units.tr: Vetare: The praetor forbade by edict that. Cic. to prohibit. Id. to prohibit and forbid that. Plaut. to forbid with threats. Ovid. he forbids animals to be placed on the tables; some read arcuit. See Interdicere.

units.la: Vetare sub pœna] Sub pœna mortis, vel capitis denunciare, Suet. Sancire pœna, capite, aliquid. Sancire pœna observantiam, Cic. Publicis exsecrationibus sancitum est, Cic. Sub exitii denunciatione statutum est, Amm. Impero facite, nisi quidem vos vestra crura, aut latera nihili pendi-tis. Nisi tuis cruribus capitique fraudem capitalem creare velis, Plaut. Capite cavere, Plin.
units.tr: Vetare sub poena: Suet. to declare under penalty of death or capital punishment. To sanction something by penalty and by the head. Cic. to sanction observance by penalty. Cic. it has been sanctioned by public curses. Amm. it was decreed under threat of ruin. Plaut. I order you to do it, unless you think your legs or sides worth nothing; unless you wish to bring capital ruin upon your legs and head. Plin. to beware on pain of life.

units.la: Veterascere] Veterare, Celf. Vetustescere, Col. Inveterare, & Inveterascere, Cic. Exolescunt amictus, Tac. Exolescere vetustate, Quint. Patitur aliquid vetustatem, Sen. Capit longissimam vetustatem aliqua res, Col. Accedit ætas vino, Celf. Senescit fama, vitium, Liv. Laus, Cic. Forma. Ovid. Caseus, Plint. Senet phaselus, Catul. Consenescere, Cic. Obsolescere, (f. usu vel tempore) Id.
units.tr: Veterascere: Celf. veterare. Col. vetustescere. Cic. inveterare and inveterascere. Tac. clothes grow old. Quint. to grow old through age. Sen. to admit age. Col. a thing takes on the longest age. Celf. age comes to wine. Liv. a reputation or fault grows old. Cic. praise. Ovid. beauty. Plin. cheese. Catul. the boat grows old. Cic. to grow old together. Id. to become obsolete through use or time.

units.la: Veterator] Circumforaneus homo, Suet. Circulator, Cic. Sycophanta, Plaut. Calophanta. (qui blando sermone decipit) Id. Holophanta, vel Halapanta, Fest. Bovinator, Gell. Planus. Nebulo, Cic. Saccularius, Vlp. Æruscator, Gell. Æsculator, Gloss. Agyrtes, Rhodig. Vid. Deceptor.
units.tr: Veterator: Suet. a wandering market man. Cic. a circulator. Plaut. a sycophant. Id. a calophanta (one who deceives with smooth talk). Fest. holophanta or halapanta. Gell. a bovinator. Cic. a plain nebulo. Vlp. a saccularius. Gell. an aeruscator. Gloss. an aesculator. Rhodig. an agyrtes. See Deceptor.

units.la: Veternus] Lethargus. Morbus lethargicus, Plin. Noctu diuque se continuans sopor, Cels. Perpetuus sopor, Hor. Marcor & inexpugnabilis dormiendi necessitas, Cels. Cataphoricus somnus, Paul. Ægin.
units.tr: Veternus: Lethargy. Plin. a lethargic disease. Cels. a sleep continuing night and day. Hor. perpetual sleep. Cels. torpor and an unconquerable need to sleep. Paul. Ægin. cataphoric sleep.

units.la: Vetitum, vid. Interdictum.
units.tr: Vetitum, see Interdictum.

units.la: Vetitus, vid. Prohibitus.
units.tr: Vetitus, see Prohibitus.

units.la: Vetula, vid. Anus.
units.tr: Vetula, see Anus.

units.la: Vetulus, vid. Senex. Vetus.
units.tr: Vetulus, see Senex. Vetus.

units.la: Vetus] Vetus auctor, hostis, societas, Liv. Veter olla, Var. Veterior senex, Plaut. Veterrimus Poëta, Cic. Pervetus, Vetustus, Pervetustus, Pristinus, Id. Vetulum vinum, Col. Cana fides, Virg. Prisca, Id. Veteranus hostis, Liv. Senex memoria, Cic. Antegenitale experimentum, Plin. Veteris monetae. Memoria hominum antiquior. Vid. Priscus. Antiquus.
units.tr: Vetus: Liv. an old author, an old enemy, an old alliance. Var. an old pot. Plaut. an older old man. Cic. the most ancient poet. Id. very old, aged, very ancient, original. Col. old wine. Virg. grey faith. Id. ancient. Liv. a veteran enemy. Cic. an old man in memory. Plin. experience before birth. Old coinage. Older than human memory. See Priscus. Antiquus.

units.la: Vetustas ] Antiquitas generis. Senectus orationis, Cic. Memoria: Unanimitatem memoria dejugat, Pacuv. Tabes annorum, Liv.
units.tr: Vetustas: The antiquity of a race. Cic. the old age of speech. Memory: Pacuv. memory dissolves unanimity. Liv. the wasting of years.

units.la: Vexare aliquem] Exagitare, raptare. Vexare fortunas alicujus, Cic. Divexare aliquem, Gell. Lancinare, Catul. Laniare, Carpere, Ovid. Incessere dictis, jaculis aliquem, Id. Provocare aliquem, Cic. Prolectare aliquem probris, Plaut. Inquietare aliquem, Col. Vid. Irritare. Exagitare.
units.tr: Vexare aliquem: To harass, to drag about. Cic. to harass someone's fortunes. Gell. to harass. Catul. to tear to pieces. Ovid. to tear, to pluck. Id. to assail someone with words and darts. Cic. to provoke someone. Plaut. to entice someone with insults. Col. to disquiet someone. See Irritare. Exagitare.

units.la: Vexare nimis] Ad vivum radere. Ad vivam cutem tondere.
units.tr: Vexare nimis: To shave down to the quick. To shear to the living skin.

units.la: Vexari] Mitti ab Herode ad Pilatum.
units.tr: Vexari: To be sent from Herod to Pilate.

units.la: Vexatio] Vexamen, Lucr. Tentatio morbi, Cic. Laceratio, Laniatus, Cic. Laniatio, Sen. Vexatio & direptio sociorum, Cic. Aggressura, Vlp. Vid. Inquietatio.
units.tr: Vexatio: Lucr. vexation. Cic. an attack of disease. Cic. tearing, mangling. Sen. mangling. Cic. the harassing and plundering of allies. Vlp. an aggressura. See Inquietatio.

units.la: Vexatio dat intellectum ] Aromata cum teruntur vehementius fragrant, Lipsf.
units.tr: Vexatio dat intellectum: Lipsf. when spices are crushed more vigorously, they give off a stronger fragrance.

units.la: Vexator] Aggressor, Vlp. Vid. Irritator. Persecutor. Vexillifer] Vexillarius, Liv. Signifer, Cic. Aquilifer apud Romanos, Caes. Signarius, Veget. Draconarius, Vopisc. Vexillum] Signa, Cic. Signa militaria, Hor. Via] Iter, Cic. Itiner, Varr. Orbita, Quint. Limes, Fest. Iter viae, Lucr. Via publica] Via tritissima & celeberrima, Sen. Via illustris & lata. Via militaris, Cic. Via consularis, praetoria, Vlp. Via difficilis, finis optatus] Artium & virtutis radices amarae, fructus dulcis, Isocrat. Via eundum est] Callem ne desere. Viam parare] Aperire viam. Apertis fontibus fluunt rivi. Viarum index columna] Mercurialis statua. Viarius] Cic. Vialis, Plaut. Itinerarius agger, Amm. Agyieus Apollo, Hor. (ἀγυιεύς, quòd viis praesit, quae ἀγυιαὶ dicuntur.) Viatica coena] Coena adventoria, Mart. Item viatica coena dicebatur, quae dabatur peregre abituris. Adventitia coena, Suet. Viaticari] Æstivè viaticati sumus, Plaut. Instrui viatico. Sumptum itinerarium exigere, Lampr. Viaticum] Viaticulum, Vlp. Legativum, Id. Vasarium, Cicer. Sumptus itinerarius, Lampr. Auxilium viae, Virg. Æsopicum onus, in Paroemiis, pro pane viatorum. Viaticus] Viatorius, Plin. Itinerarius, Lampr. Expeditionalis, Spart. Viator] Vians, Solin. Peregrinator, Cic. Peregrinabundus, Liv. Vibex] Orbita vinculi sentitur, Plin. Tumex, Iof. Scalig. Plaga ex retuso telo, Celf. Nodi plagarum, Stat. Offerumentas, Plaut. Per jocum vocat plagas, quod offerantur tergo. Vibrare hastam, &c.] Crispare, Concrispare hastam, telum, Amm. Concutere hastam, Sil. Caesariem capitis, Ovid. Quatere hastam, securim, Cic. Quassare hastam, Ovid. Caput, Plaut. Ventilare aureos manu, Apul. Vid. Iacere. Vibratio, vid. Iaculatio.
units.tr: Vexator: Vlp. an aggressor. See Irritator. Persecutor. Vexillifer: Liv. a vexillarius; Cic. a signifer; among the Romans, Caes. an aquilifer; Veget. a signarius; Vopisc. a draconarius. Vexillum: Cic. standards; Hor. military standards. Via: Cic. a going, a journey; Varr. an itinerary; Quint. a track of wheels; Fest. a boundary; Lucr. the course of a road. Via publica: Sen. the most worn and most frequented road. Cic. a broad and famous road, a military road; Vlp. a consular road, a praetorian road. Via difficilis, finis optatus: Isocrat. the roots of arts and virtue are bitter, the fruit sweet. Via eundum est: Do not desert the narrow path. Viam parare: to open a way. With the springs opened, the rivers flow. Viarum index columna: a statue of Mercury. Viarius: Cic. vialis; Plaut. an itinerary embankment; Amm. Apollo Agyieus, Hor. (Greek ἀγυιεύς [agyieus], because he presides over the streets, which are called ἀγυιαί [agyiai]). Viatica coena: Mart. an arrival dinner. The viatic dinner was also the name given to the meal offered to those leaving abroad. Suet. an adventitious dinner. Viaticari: Plaut. we have been provided for the summer. To be equipped with travel provisions. Lampr. to exact travel expenses. Viaticum: Vlp. a little provision; Id. a legation; Cic. a vasarium; Lampr. travelling expenses; Virg. the help of the road. An Aesopian burden, in the proverbs, for the bread of travellers. Viaticus: Plin. of travel; Lampr. itinerant; Spart. expeditionary. Viator: Solin. a passer-by; Cic. a traveller; Liv. a wanderer. Vibex: Plin. the mark of a cord is felt. Iof. Scalig. a weal. Celf. a blow from a blunt weapon. Stat. weals of blows. Plaut. offerumentas; he jokingly calls the blows that, because they are offered to the back. Vibrare hastam, etc.: Amm. to brandish a spear: crispare, concrispare hastam, telum. Sil. concutere hastam. Ovid. caesariem capitis. Cic. quatere hastam, securim. Ovid. quassare hastam. Plaut. caput. Apul. to wave golden things with the hand. See Iacere. Vibratio: see Iaculatio.

units.la: Vicarius] In locum alicujus suppositus, Varr. Vicem agens Rectoris. Secundi loci Rector, Amm. Absentis partibus fungens, Sen. Proconsul, Proquæstor, Cic.
units.tr: Vicarius: Varr. placed in the position of someone. Acting in the office of a ruler. Amm. the ruler of the second place. Sen. discharging the duties of one who is absent. Cic. a proconsul, a proquaestor.

units.la: Vice, vid. Pro aliquo. Loco.
units.tr: Vice, see In place of someone; instead of.

units.la: Per vices] In orbem.
units.tr: Per vices: in turn, in rotation.

units.la: Vicinia] Vicinitas & confinium, Cic. Vicinium,Ser. Vicinum,Plin. In vicino sunt terræ.
units.tr: Vicinity: nearness and neighbourhood, Cic. Also vicinium, Ser.; vicinum, Plin. The lands are nearby.

units.la: Vicinus] Proximus vicinus, Hor. Bonus, Mart. Vicinus meus est, manuque tangi potest. Senex de proximo. Hæ è proximo. Hujus è proximo, Plaut. Accola, Virg.
units.tr: Neighbour: a close neighbour, Hor. A good neighbour, Mart. "My neighbour is, and can be touched by hand." An old man "from nearby." These women "from nearby." Of this man, from nearby, Plaut. A dweller nearby (accola), Virg.

units.la: Vicinus, ad nom.] Vicinumque pecus grandius uber habet, Ovid. Vicinalis usus, Liv.
units.tr: Neighbouring, adjective: "And the neighbouring herd has a larger udder," Ovid. Neighbourly use, Liv.

units.la: Vicissim, vid. Mutuò.
units.tr: Vicissim, see Mutually.

units.la: Vicissitudo, vid. Alternatio.
units.tr: Vicissitude, see Alternation.

units.la: Vicissitudo est rerum omnium] Felix turbinem prospecta. Nemo tam divos habuit faventes, crastinum ut possit sibi polliceri, Sen. Humanarum rerum circulus est, qui rotatus, semper eosdem fortunatos esse non sinit, Herodot.
units.tr: Vicissitude is of all things: "Happy is the one who watches the whirlwind from afar. No one has had the gods so favourable that he can promise himself tomorrow," Sen. "The cycle of human affairs is a wheel which, once turned, does not let the same people remain fortunate," Herodot.

units.la: Vicissitudo rerum grata] Amant alterna Camœnæ, Virg.
units.tr: Pleasing variety of things: "The Muses love alternation," Virg.

units.la: Victima scil. Ethnicorum] Piaculum, Hor. Libamen, Cic. Libamentum, Stat. Offerumentum, Plaut.
units.tr: Victim, namely of the heathen: an expiation, Hor. A libation, Cic. A libation-offering, Stat. An offering, Plaut.

units.la: Victimarius] Immolator, Cic. Cultrarius, Suet. Liturgus, Plin. Iun.
units.tr: Victim-slaughterer: an immolator, Cic. A knife-man, Suet. A sacrificial attendant, Plin. Iun.

units.la: Victitare, vid. Sustentare.
units.tr: Victitare, see Sustain.

units.la: Victitare bene] Fungi epulis, Ovid. Vid. Epulari.
units.tr: To live well: to feast at banquets, Ovid. See To feast.

units.la: Victor] Domitor Hispaniæ, Cic. Debellator alicujus, Stat. Confector ferarum, Suet.
units.tr: Victor: a conqueror of Spain, Cic. A vanquisher of someone, Stat. A slayer of wild beasts, Suet.

units.la: Victor dabit leges] Conditiones accipiant victi, non ferant.
units.tr: The victor will dictate laws: let the conquered accept terms, not dictate them.

units.la: Victoria sine jactura] Victoria intacto milite parta, Amm. Exercitu incruento, Sallust. Incolumi, Hort. Sine sanguine quæsita victoria, Tacit. Sine vulnere & cæde suorum. Sine sanguine, Cæs. Palma, Cicer. Trophæum, Horat.
units.tr: Victory without loss: victory won with the soldiers unharmed, Amm. With an army bloodless, Sallust. Unhurt, Hort. A victory won without bloodshed, Tacit. Without wound or slaughter of one's own. Without bloodshed, Caes. Palm, Cic. Trophy, Hor.

units.la: Victoria plerumque utrique parti damnosa] Flet victor, victus interiit.
units.tr: Victory is generally harmful to both sides: "The victor weeps, the vanquished perishes."

units.la: Victoria labore comparatur] Amat victoria curam.
units.tr: Victory is won by labour: "Victory loves care."

units.la: Victoriæ incertæ præferenda constans pax] Tutior pax certa, quam sperata victoria.
units.tr: Steady peace is to be preferred to uncertain victory: "A sure peace is safer than a hoped-for victory."

units.la: Victoriosus] Victrix laurus, Virg. Palmata tunica, Liv. Vid. Triumphalis.
units.tr: Victorious: "a victorious laurel," Virg. "A palm-embroidered tunic," Liv. See Triumphal.

units.la: Victus, Adj.] Victus & subactus sum. Excidit è manibus alicui victoria, Cic. Infra dolorem vel voluptatem esse, Sen. Frangi cupiditate. Non frangant te mala, Cic. (NB. formentur ex his phrases Nominales.)
units.tr: Vanquished, adjective: I have been conquered and subdued. Victory has slipped from someone's hands, Cic. To be below pain or pleasure, Sen. To be broken by desire. "Let misfortunes not break you," Cic. (N.B. nominal phrases are formed from these.)

units.la: Victus dolor] Galli victi silent, victores canunt, Cic.
units.tr: Vanquished grief: "The vanquished Gauls are silent, the victors sing," Cic.

units.la: Victus, ûs, vid. Alimentum.
units.tr: Victus, -ūs, see Nourishment.

units.la: Vide!] Papæ! Hem! Hoc vide, Ter. En ut pullat propudium! Babæ! Plaut. Vah consilium callidum! Ter.
units.tr: Look!: Wow! Ha! "Look at this," Ter. "Look how the shameful creature stirs!" Babae! Plaut. "Ah, what a clever plan!" Ter.

units.la: Videndi studio] Videndi causa veneo, Cic. Visendi studio ruit juventus, Virg. Ire ad videndum. Visere eo, Ter. Venio visere ad fanum, Plaut.
units.tr: With a desire to see: I go out for the sake of seeing, Cic. Youth rushes eagerly to see, Virg. To go to look. I am going to visit, Ter. I come to the temple to see, Plaut.

units.la: Videre] Videre oculis, Cernere, Conspicere, Adspectu aliquid sentire. Percipere aliquid oculis. Ante oculos mihi versatur, obversatur, Cic. Usurpare aliquid oculis, Plaut. Conspicari, Contueri aliquid, Cic. Contui, à Contuor, Plaut. Lucr. Nullam hic intuor cornicem, Plaut.
units.tr: To see: to see with the eyes, to discern, to behold, to perceive something by sight. To take something in with the eyes. It flits before my eyes, is before me, Cic. To take in something with the eyes, Plaut. To behold, to gaze upon something, Cic. Contui, from contuor, Plaut. Lucr. Here I see no crow, Plaut.

units.la: Videre aliena, sua non] In alieno plus, quam in suo videre. Lamiam agere: quæ domi clausos habebat oculos, foras proditura vero eos assumebat. Domi talpa, foris lynceus.
