units.tr: To see others' faults but not one's own: to see more in another's than in one's own. To play Lamia: she kept her eyes shut at home but, when about to go out, took them up. At home a mole, abroad a lynx.

units.la: Videre statim quid sit]. Ex fronte perspicere.
units.tr: To see at once what something is: to read it from the brow.

units.la: Non videre clarissima] Caligare in sole.
units.tr: Not to see the very clearest things: to be dazzled in the sun.

units.la: Videre acute]Plures plura vident. Plus vident oculi quam oculus.
units.tr: To see keenly: "The more see more things. The eyes see more than the eye."

units.la: Vidua] Viduata conjux, Sen. In viduitate relicta, Liv. Vacua, Tac. Vacans, Suet.
units.tr: Widow: a bereaved wife, Sen. Left in widowhood, Liv. Empty, Tac. Vacant, Suet.

units.la: Viduus] Viduus vir, Plaut. Cœlebs: diceris quater factus esse cœlebs, Mart.
units.tr: Widower: a widowed man, Plaut. A bachelor: "You are said to have become a bachelor four times," Mart.

units.la: Viere] Nectere coronam, Hor. Texere sertum, Sen. Plectere, Lucr.
units.tr: To weave: to bind a garland, Hor. To plait a wreath, Sen. To braid, Lucr.

units.la: Vietor] Doliarius, Plin. Doliorum cupparumque factor, Pallad.
units.tr: Cooper: a maker of casks, Plin. A maker of casks and tubs, Pallad.

units.la: Vigens, vid. Vegetus.
units.tr: Being vigorous, see Lively.

units.la: Vigere, vid. Vegetari.
units.tr: To flourish, see To be lively.

units.la: Vigil] Custos, Cic. Excubitor canis, Col. Vigilarius, Sen. Capsarius, Paul. IC. Incensor, Apul. (qui signum dat noctu face accensa.)
units.tr: Watchman: a guard, Cic. A watchdog, Col. A night-watchman, Sen. A chest-keeper, Paul IC. One who gives the signal at night with a torch, Apul.

units.la: Vigilans] Vigil canis, Hor. Pervigil, Plin. Abstinentissimus somni, Col. Inconnivus. Pupillis excubantibus, Apul. Vigilax gallus, canis, Col. Sagax anser, Ovid.
units.tr: Watchful: a watchful dog, Hor. Ever-wakeful, Plin. Most abstemious of sleep, Col. Not sleeping. The pupils keeping watch, Apul. A wakeful cock or dog, Col. A keen goose, Ovid.

units.la: Vigilanter] Vigilatè, Macrob. Expergitè custodi, Apul. Vid. Diligenter.
units.tr: Watchfully: wakefully, Macrob. Guard alertly, Apul. See Diligently.

units.la: Vigilantia] Vigilia. Pervigilatio, Cic. Pervigilium, Lucr. Pervigilia, Iustin. Insomnia, Cæcil. Nocturna inquies, Plin. Excubatio perpetua pro dignitate & salute amicorum, Val. Max.
units.tr: Vigilance: wakefulness. Keeping vigil, Cic. Vigil, Lucr. Vigils, Iustin. Sleeplessness, Caecil. Nocturnal restlessness, Plin. Constant watch for the dignity and welfare of friends, Val. Max.

units.la: Vigilare] Vigilare ad multam noctem, de nocte, Ter. Vigilias agere, Cic. Vigilias agitare, Plaut. Pervigilare noctem, Cic. Pervigilium agere, Suet. Evigilare noctem, Tibul. Excubare in muris, pro muris, Liv. Pro castris excubare, Salust. Privat me somno ægritudo. Somnum non vidi, Cic. Multas noctes peregi insomnes, Apul. Noctem vacuus somno peregi, Ovid. Intervigilare, Sen.
units.tr: To keep watch: to be awake late into the night, Ter. To keep vigils, Cic. To keep vigils, Plaut. To spend the whole night awake, Cic. To hold a vigil, Suet. To watch through the night, Tibul. To stand guard on the walls, Liv. To keep watch before the camp, Sallust. Grief deprives me of sleep. I have not seen sleep, Cic. I spent many nights sleepless, Apul. I passed the night without sleep, Ovid. To stay awake, Sen.

units.la: Vilescere] Evilescere, Suet. Revilescere, Sen. Jacent pretia prædiorum, Cic. Retro abiit pretium agrorum, Plin. Iun. Detrahitur pretium metallis, Plin. Depretiatum est aliquid, Paul. IC. Ex inopia gravi frumenti, satias facta est, Salust.
units.tr: To become cheap: to become worthless, Suet. To come back to value, Sen. Land prices fall, Cic. The price of land went back, Plin. Iun. The price of metals is lowered, Plin. Something has been depreciated, Paul IC. From a grievous shortage of grain, a glut came about, Sallust.

units.la: Vili] Vilissime constat, Plin. Vilissimo, Bud. Tenuiter, tenuissime aliquid æstimare. Benigne, Bene emere, Cic. Melius emere, Cic. Minimo, Plaut. Quadrante lavari, Hor. (i. e. minimo pretio.)
units.tr: At a very low price: to be sold very cheaply, Plin. At a very low price, Bud. To value something very slightly. To buy kindly, to buy well, Cic. To buy better, Cic. For a minimum, Plaut. To wash for a quadrans, Hor. (i.e. at the lowest price.)

units.la: Vilipendere] Æstimare unius assis, Catul. Nullius æstimare, Apul. In minimis, in extremis res aliquas ponere, Cic. In ultimis ponere, Plin. Vile habere aliquid, Salust. Pro nihilo ducere, habere, putare. Pro nihili mihi videtur. Parvi ducere, Cic. Parvi facere, æstimare, Plaut. Putare, Catul. Nihili, parvi, floccipendere, Ter. Floccifacere, Cic. Nullo loco habere, numerare. Neminem præ se putare, Id. In levi habere, Tacit. Parum habere, Liv. Hujus non facio, Ter. Ternuncii non facere. Nihili facere, Plaut. Pili
units.tr: To hold cheap: to value at a single as, Catul. To value at nothing, Apul. To put things in the least and lowest place, Cic. To place in the last rank, Plin. To hold something cheap, Sallust. To regard as nothing; to hold, to reckon. To think no one of oneself. To think little of, Cic. Parvi facere, Plaut. Putare, Catul. To make nothing of, to think it worth a floccus, Ter. To make a floccus of, Cic. To count in no place, to reckon. To think nobody of oneself, Id. To hold in light regard, Tacit. To have little, Liv. I do not care for this man, Ter. To make nothing of, Plaut. Not to care a hair,

units.la: non facere, Catul. Nauci non habere, Enn. Pro matulâ habere aliquem, Plaut. Pro stercore habere, Id. Manum non verterim, Cic.
units.tr: not to care a whit, Catul. Not to count it worth a nut, Enn. To regard someone as a mere pot-herb, Plaut. To regard as dung, Id. I would not lift a hand, Cic.

units.la: Vilis] Vile frumentum. Pervilis annona, Liv. Annona pretium non habet, Cic. Vile pretium alicujus rei, Mart. Minimi æris est, Vlp. Laxior annona, Liv. Benè, pulchrè conciliatus, Plaut. Orichalco contrà non est carus. Modio falis emptus, Id. Benè emptus, ex Cic.
units.tr: Cheap: cheap grain. A very cheap grain supply, Liv. Grain has no price, Cic. A cheap price for something, Mart. It is of the least value, Ulp. A looser grain supply, Liv. Well and handsomely acquired, Plaut. Not dear compared with brass. Bought for a measure of salt, Plaut. Well bought, from Cic.

units.la: Vilis homo, vel aliquid] Ad numerum tantùm facit. Albus an ater fit, ignorant. Ubilibet non defuturus. Calcata quæstio, Sen. Numerus, Hor. Nullo in numero Oratorum fuit, Cicer. Umbraticus, Sen. Minorum gentium Philosophus. Extra numerum est, extra pretium, extra ordinem. Fœneus homo. Natus è mari. De lapide emptus. Infimus & sordidissimus omnium. Semissis homo, Cicer. Infimâ de gente, Hor. De viâ homo. Trioboli homo. Infimatis, vel infimas. Ego infimatis infimus accumbam, Plaut. Quadrantarius, Sen. Fricti ciceris emptor, Hor. Ultimæ professionis homo, Lampr. Nullius coloris homo, Plaut. Ne patriæ quidem nomen dicere possit. Terræ filius, Cic. Cærite cerâ dignus, Hor. Terræ juvenes, Id. Inutile terræ pondus, Cic. Proletarius civis, Non. Cibarius homo, Varr. Trivialis scientiæ magister, Quint. Tenuis locus. Tenui, sordido loco ortus, Liv. Humilis homo, locus, ars, ortus, oratio, Cic. Treffis agaso, Perf. Gregalia poma, Sen. Gregarius miles, Cic. Catervarius, Suet. E trivio, Catul. De circo, Atti. Cyclicus scriptor, Hor. In multis numerandus, Cic. De triviis verba, Sidon. Contempta ars, verbum, Cic. Parvus dictu; Parva dictu animalia, Quint. Ignobilis locus, magister. Abjectus homo, gemitus, oratio, verba, Cic. Ignobilissimus & despicatissimus, Gell. Ultimæ plebis. Vitiosis pomis vilior. Cassâ nuce vilior. Algâ vilior.
units.tr: A cheap man or thing: he counts only as a number. Whether he turns out white or black, nobody knows. He will not be missing anywhere. A worn-out question, Sen. A number, Hor. He was in no rank of orators, Cic. A shadowy fellow, Sen. A philosopher of the lesser sort. He is outside the number, outside price, outside rank. A usurer's man. Born of the sea. Bought from a stone. Lowest and most squalid of all. A half-as man, Cic. Of the lowest stock, Hor. A man from the road. A man of three obols. Lowest, or the lowliest. "I, the lowest of the lowest, will recline," Plaut. A quadrans-man, Sen. A buyer of fried chickpeas, Hor. A man of the lowest profession, Lampr. A man of no colour, Plaut. He could not even say the name of his country. Son of the earth, Cic. Worthy only of Caere's wax, Hor. Youths of the earth, Id. A useless weight of earth, Cic. A proletarian citizen, Non. A food-seller, Varr. Master of trivial learning, Quint. A humble place. Born of a humble, squalid station, Liv. A humble man, place, craft, birth, speech, Cic. A shabby groom, Pers. Common apples, Sen. A common soldier, Cic. A hanger-on of the crowd, Suet. From the crossroads, Catul. From the circus, Atti. A cyclic writer, Hor. To be counted among the many, Cic. Words from the crossroads, Sidon. A despised craft, word, Cic. Small to speak of; small animals, Quint. An ignoble place, teacher. An abject man, groan, speech, words, Cic. Most ignoble and despised, Gell. Of the lowest common people. Cheaper than spoiled apples. Cheaper than a shell-less nut. Cheaper than seaweed.

units.la: Vilia facile fiunt] Fungus unâ nocte nascitur.
units.tr: Cheap things come about easily: a mushroom springs up in a single night.

units.la: Vilia ne cura] Quæ infra nos, nihil ad nos.
units.tr: Do not worry about cheap things: what is beneath us is nothing to us.

units.la: Viliora malult] Vinum cùm adsit, acetum bibit.
units.tr: He prefers cheaper things: "When wine is at hand, he drinks vinegar."

units.la: Villosus, vid. Hirsutus.
units.tr: Shaggy, see Hairy.

units.la: Villus, vid. Floccus.
units.tr: Shag, see Tuft.

units.la: Vimen ] Viminalia, pl. Plin. Vimenta, pl. Donat. Vi-burnum, Virg. Stamina contorti junci, Colvi.
units.tr: Withy: withies, plural, Plin. Twigs, plural, Donat. Viburnum, Virg. Threads of twisted rush, Col.

units.la: Vimineus ] Viminalis salix, Col. Virgeus, Virg. Virgatus calathiscus, Catul. Vimine textum serpiculum, Col.
units.tr: Of withy: a willow of osier, Col. Willow-like, Virg. A basket of rods, Catul. A little basket woven of osier, Col.

units.la: Vinacea, vid. Retrimentum.
units.tr: Grape-skins, see Refuse.

units.la: Vinaceus ] Vinalis fortitudo, Macrob. Vinarius lacus. Vineaticus fructus, Col. Vinosus succus, sapor, Plin.
units.tr: Wine-like: wine-like strength, Macrob. A wine-vat. Vineyard fruit, Col. Winy juice, flavour, Plin.

units.la: Vincere hostem aliquem] Devincere aliquem bello. Consequi victoriam gloriosam. Reportare, adipisci victoriam: parta victoria, Cic. Patrare victoriam, Tac. Debellare aliquem, Plin. Frangere aliquem praelio, Cic. Superare aliquem pugnando, Ovid. Transgredi aliquem collatis signis, Plin.
units.tr: To conquer an enemy] To defeat someone in war. To win a glorious victory. To win or obtain victory: victory having been won, Cic. To achieve victory, Tac. To subdue someone, Plin. To break someone in battle, Cic. To overcome someone in fight, Ovid. To get past someone with the standards drawn up, Plin.

units.la: Vincere se ipsum plus est, quam alios] Fortior est, qui se, quam fortissima vincit Moenia; nec virtus altius ire potest, Ovid.
units.tr: To conquer oneself is more than to conquer others] He is braver who conquers himself than who conquers the strongest walls, and virtue can rise no higher, Ovid.

units.la: Vince, si potes] Palma in medio est posita, Ter.
units.tr: Conquer, if you can] The palm is set in the middle, Ter.

units.la: Vincibilis] Superabilis ulli non est, Ovid.
units.tr: Conquerable] Not to be overcome by anyone, Ovid.

units.la: Vincire aliquem] Ligare in catenas, Quint. Colligare manus, Cic. Constringere catenis, laqueis, Cic. Indere alicui catenas, Plaut. Innectere vincula, Hor. Injicere vincula, Cic. Circumdare, adstringere vincula, Ovid. Instringere captivum vinculis, Quint. Destinare: Destinatis ejus membris, Apul. Arcae in aquam demittendae, destinandae firmiter, Vitr. (i. e. alligandae, Philand. Catenare, Cic. Injicere catenas alicui. Quadrupedes constringere, Vid. Ligare.
units.tr: To bind someone] To tie in chains, Quint. To bind the hands, Cic. To bind with chains or nooses, Cic. To put chains on someone, Plaut. To entwine with fetters, Hor. To throw on fetters, Cic. To surround and tie fast with bonds, Ovid. To fetter a captive with chains, Quint. To fasten: with his limbs fastened, Apul. A chest to be lowered into the water and firmly fastened, Vitr. (i.e. tied, Philand.) To chain, Cic. To put chains on someone. To bind four-footed animals, see Ligare.

units.la: Vinctio] Conjugatio capitum, (f. in vitibus.) Colligatio causarum, societatis, Cic. Nexus, Ovid.
units.tr: Binding] A joining of heads (f. in vines). A linking together of causes or of alliance, Cic. A knot, Ovid.

units.la: Vinctus ] Carcer, (pro homine carcere digno) Ter. Carcerarius, Donat. Custodia, Suet. Post terga revinctus, Virg. Catenatus. Retorta tergo brachia, Hor.
units.tr: Bound] A prison (said of a man deserving prison), Ter. A jailer, Donat. Custody, Suet. With arms bound behind the back, Virg. Chained. With arms twisted behind the back, Hor.

units.la: Vincula, orum] Mandare aeternis vinculis: abripi in vincula. Cic. Catenae, Id. In manibus gestant copulas, Plaut. i. e. vincula, Lamb. Nervo vinctus, Plaut. Custodia; dare, tradere, in custodiam; includere in custodias. Asservari privatis custodiis, Cic. Militari custodia haberi: haberi in custodia, Tac. Teneri in custodiis, Salust. Custodia libera, liberalis, Cic. Vinculum] Vinctus, us. Cestus,ti,Var. Ligamen vitium, Col. Nexus, Claud. Nodus, Cic. Copula irrupta, Hor. Laqueus, Firm. Torus, quo vitis arbori alligatur, Col.
units.tr: Chains] To commit to eternal chains; to be dragged off to chains, Cic. Fetters, Id. They carry shackles in their hands, Plaut. i.e. chains, Lamb. Bound with sinew, Plaut. Custody: to hand over or give into custody; to shut up in prisons. To be kept in private custody, Cic. To be held under military guard, or in custody, Tac. To be held in prisons, Sall. Free custody, liberal custody, Cic. Cic. Bond] A binding or band. A girdle, Var. A tie of a vine, Col. A bond, Claud. A knot, Cic. An unbroken link, Hor. A noose, Firm. The collar by which a vine is tied to a tree, Col.

units.la: Vindemiare vineam] Vindemiam colligere, Plin.Iun. Vindemiam facere, & Uvas legere, Varr.
units.tr: To harvest the vineyard] To gather in the vintage, Plin. Iun. To make the vintage, and to pick grapes, Varr.

units.la: Vindemiator ] Vindemiator, Hor. Vindemitor, Ovid. Vindemator, Porphyr.
units.tr: Vintager] Vintager, Hor. Another form of the same word, Ovid. Another form, Porphyr.

units.la: Vindex, vid. Ultor.
units.tr: Avenger: see Avenger.

units.la: Vindicare] Asserere aliquem: Ovid. Asserere manu causa liberali, Ter. Asserere in causa liberali, Cic. Donare libertate servos, Id. Manumittere aliquem, Plaut. Vindicias dare secundum libertatem, Liv. Servos suppliciorum metu Dominorum benignitas una vindicta liberavit, Cic.
units.tr: To claim] To claim someone as one's own, Ovid. To claim in a suit for freedom, Ter. To claim in a free-birth case, Cic. To grant freedom to slaves, Id. To manumit someone, Plaut. To give provisional possession in favour of liberty, Liv. The kindness of masters freed slaves from the fear of punishment by a single act of release, Cic.

units.la: Vindicatio, vid. Ultio. Liberatio.
units.tr: Vindication: see Vengeance. Liberation.

units.la: Vindicta, vid. Ultio.
units.tr: Revenge: see Vengeance.

units.la: Vindicta cupidus] Canis lapidem rodens. In lapidem saeviens canis.
units.tr: Eager for revenge] A dog gnawing a stone. A dog raging at a stone.

units.la: Vinea ] Vinetum: novella vineta fodienda trigesimo quoque die, Col. Masculetum, Plin.
units.tr: Vineyard] A vineyard plot: young vineyards to be dug every thirtieth day, Col. A plantation of male vines, Plin.

units.la: Vinealis] Vineatica falx, Var. Vinearius colis, Col. Vindemialis fructus, Macr.
units.tr: Of the vineyard] A vine-pruning sickle, Var. A vineyard-tiller, Col. Vintage fruit, Macr.

units.la: Vinitor] Cultor vineae, Cic. Pampinator, Col. Consitor uvae, Ovid. Vitisator, Virg.
units.tr: Vine-dresser] A tiller of the vineyard, Cic. A pruner of vine-shoots, Col. A planter of grapes, Ovid. A vine-planter, Virg.

units.la: Vinum]Vinolentia,& Vinolentus. Vid.Ebrietas.Ebriosus.
units.tr: Wine] Drunkenness and drunken. See Drunkenness. Drunkard.

units.la: Vinum ] Temetum, Plaut. Merum, Ovid. Lac senum. Lac veneris. Coagulum hilaritatis. Venenum terrae, vocat Androcides. Speculum animi.
units.tr: Wine] Strong wine, Plaut. Undiluted wine, Ovid. The milk of the old. The milk of Venus. The curdling of merriment. The poison of the earth, so called by Androcides. The mirror of the mind.

units.la: Vinum plus nocet, quam gladius] Bacchus Marte fortior, plures sepelit.
units.tr: Wine does more harm than the sword] Bacchus, stronger than Mars, buries more men.

units.la: Violare aliquid, vel aliquem] Profanare sacra, sacerdotes, Liv. Temerare sepulchrum, Id. Conscelerare domum, Cat. Foedare sacella turpitudine, Cic. Incestare thalamos, Virg. Mactare jus civitatis supplicio. Afferre vim patriae, parentibus. Vim facere, inferre, adhibere alicui. Vim suscipere contra aliquem. Per oppressionem aliquid eripere alicui. Violentiae impetu opprimere. Vi agere: vi agitur res, Cic. Contemerare manus magistri, Mart. Funestare aliquem, Catul. Violare
units.tr: To violate something or someone] To profane sacred things and priests, Liv. To defile a tomb, Id. To pollute a house, Cat. To foul shrines with filthiness, Cic. To defile marriage beds, Virg. To punish the rights of the state with death. To bring violence against one's country or parents. To use force on someone, to inflict or apply it. To take up force against someone. To snatch something from someone by oppression. To crush by the onslaught of violence. To act by force: a matter is done by force, Cic. To touch impurely the hands of a teacher, Mart. To bring death upon someone, Catul. To violate.

units.la: Violare pudicitiam, vid. Stuprare.
units.tr: To violate chastity: see To debauch.

units.la: Violatio alicujus] Violatio templi, Liv. Profanum, Plin. i. e. Profanatio.
units.tr: Violation of someone] Violation of a temple, Liv. Profanation, Plin. i.e. profanation.

units.la: Violatio pudicitiæ] Violatio pudoris fœminæ. Rupta virginitas, Quint. Vitiatio, Sen. Devirginatio, Scribon. Compressus, us, Plaut. Ludibrium, Curt.
units.tr: Violation of chastity] Violation of a woman's modesty. Broken virginity, Quint. Defilement, Sen. Deflowering, Scribon. A forced embrace, Plaut. Mockery, Curt.

units.la: Violator] Violator juris. Ruptor fœderis, Liv. Temerator, Amm.
units.tr: Violator] Violator of law. Breaker of a covenant, Liv. Desecrator, Amm.

units.la: Violator pudicitiæ, vid. Stuprator.
units.tr: Violator of chastity: see Debaucher.

units.la: Violenter] Violentius, Vlp. Vi ac necessitate coactus, Cic. Vi subigente, Lucr. Per vim actum. Per potestatem auferre aliquid alicui, Pro potestate agere, Cic. Per oppressionem eripere, Ter.
units.tr: Violently] More violently, Ulp. Compelled by force and necessity, Cic. With force driving, Lucr. Done by force. To take something from someone by power. To act with authority, Cic. To take by oppression, Ter.

units.la: Violentia] Vis: vim & manus alicui inferre, Cic. Oppressio, Ter.
units.tr: Violence] Force: to bring force and hand against someone, Cic. Oppression, Ter.

units.la: Violentus] Violentissima tempestas, Cic. Impetuosus, Plin. Imperiosus. Urgens malum. Fatalis ac necessarius casus, Cic.
units.tr: Violent] A most violent storm, Cic. Impetuous, Plin. Imperious. Pressing evil. A fated and necessary chance, Cic.

units.la: Vipera] Excetra. Aspis, Cic. Prester. Cerastes, (i. e. Serpens cornutus,) Plin. Echidna, Ovid.
units.tr: Viper] Excetra. Asp, Cic. Prester. Cerastes (i.e. the horned serpent), Plin. Echidna, Ovid.

units.la: Viperinus Vipereus, Virg. Viperalis, Apul.
units.tr: Viperous] Of a viper, Virg. Viper-like, Apul.

units.la: Vir, vid. Maritus.
units.tr: Man: see Husband.

units.la: Vir gravis, vid Gravis.
units.tr: Serious man: see Serious.

units.la: Vir es] Virum te judico. Macte, Cic. Laudo, Ter. Nolster esto, dum te poteris defensare injuria, Plaut. Tanto major! Tanto augustior! Plin. Iun. Euge & belle, Pers. Vid. Euge.
units.tr: You are a man] I judge you a man. Well done, Cic. I praise you, Ter. Be our own, as long as you can defend yourself from injury, Plaut. So much the greater! So much the more august! Plin. Iun. Well and fine, Pers. See Well done.

units.la: Virens] Viridis, Cic. Viridans, Virg. Præviridans, Macrob. Perviridis; herbidus color, Plin. Herbeus oculus, Plaut. Vivus cespes, Hor. Vivax gramen, Ovid. Viridicatus, Cic. Porraceus, Plin. Galbus color, Turneb. Prasinus, Bayf.
units.tr: Green] Green, Cic. Greening, Virg. Very green, Macrob. Thoroughly green; a grassy colour, Plin. An eye of grass-green, Plaut. Living turf, Hor. Lasting grass, Ovid. Greenish, Cic. Leek-coloured, Plin. A yellowish-green colour, Turneb. Leek-green, Bayf.

units.la: Vivere] Virescere, Col. Viridantur ab undis grana, Ovid. Viridari ab herbis, Grati. Evirescere, Var. Intervirere, Claud. Vernant agri, Mart. Herbescere, Cic. Viriditatem alicujus imitari, Plin.
units.tr: To grow green] To become green, Col. The grains turn green from the waves, Ovid. To be green with herbs, Grat. To grow green again, Var. To green through, Claud. The fields are in spring, Mart. To grow grassy, Cic. To imitate someone's greenness, Plin.

units.la: Virga ] Flagrum, Liv. Flagellum, Var. Ferula, Iuv. Plin.
units.tr: Rod] A whip, Liv. A scourge, Var. A cane, Juv. Plin.

units.la: Virgetum] Virgultum. Arbustum, Virg. Virectum, Isid. Area virgea. Frutetum, Col. Fruticetum, Hor. Frutetosus tractus. Frutetis obsessus ager, Col. Frutetosus locus, Plin.
units.tr: Thicket] Brushwood. A plantation of shrubs, Virg. A place for brushwood, Isid. A brushy area. Brushwood, Col. Thicket, Hor. A brushy tract. A field beset with thickets, Col. A bushy place, Plin.

units.la: Virgeus] Virgeum pabulum. Frondeus, Ovid. Frontetosus, Col. Sarmentitius cinis, Id.
units.tr: Of twigs] Twiggy fodder. Leafy, Ovid. Bushy, Col. Ash of twigs, Id.

units.la: Virginal, locus, in quo sunt virgines & fæminæ] Gynæceum, Ter. Gynæconitis, idis, Vitr.
units.tr: Women's quarters, the place where virgins and women are] Gynaeceum, Ter. Gynaeconitis, Vitr.

units.la: Virginalis] Virgineus cultus habitus, Ovid. Virginarius, Plaut.
units.tr: Maidenly] Maidenly dress and bearing, Ovid. Of maidens, Plaut.

units.la: Virginitas] Virginei pudoris flos intemeratus, Cic. Integritas, Id.
units.tr: Virginity] The unspoiled flower of maidenly modesty, Cic. Integrity, Id.

units.la: Virginitatem amittere] Zonam solvere, Catul. Substernere alicui suam pudicitiam, Suet. Cognovit adultera virgo virum, Ovid. Notitiam habere viri, ex Cæs.
units.tr: To lose one's virginity] To loosen the girdle, Catul. To lay one's chastity under someone, Suet. A virgin adulteress has known a man, Ovid. To have knowledge of a man, from Caes.

units.la: Virgo] Filia, Virgo integra, Plaut. Nescia viri, Ovid. Pura sum, comperce quæso attrectare me. Tam à me pudica est, quasi soror mea sit, Plaut. Integra à viro, Ter. Virgo signata, Lucr. Virgo puer, Paul. Virgo maritus, P. Chrysolog.
units.tr: Virgin] A daughter, an unwed virgin, Plaut. Ignorant of a man, Ovid. I am pure; spare me, I beg you, from being handled. She is as chaste with me as if she were my sister, Plaut. Untouched by a husband, Ter. A sealed virgin, Lucr. A virgin boy, Paul. A virgin husband, P. Chrysolog.

units.la: Virgo corrupta] Imminuta virgo, Scal. Præflorata, Apul. Cui erepta virginitas, Virg. Cui libata virginitas, Ovid. Solvit pudorem, Virg. Passa virum, Tertul. Habet viri notitiam, ex Cæs. Non virgo.
units.tr: Corrupted virgin] A diminished virgin, Scal. Deflowered, Apul. One from whom virginity has been snatched, Virg. One whose virginity has been tasted, Ovid. She has lost her modesty, Virg. She has suffered a man, Tertul. She has knowledge of a man, from Caes. Not a virgin.

units.la: Viridarium] Viridium, Philand. Viridiarium, Pompon. Viretum, Virg. Virectum, Serv.
units.tr: Pleasure-garden] Another form of the word, Philand. Another form, Pompon. A grassy grove, Virg. A grassy place, Serv.

units.la: Viridis, vid. Virens.
units.tr: Green: see Green.

units.la: Virilis] Masculinus, Fest. Masculabilis, Juv.
units.tr: Manly] Masculine, Fest. Fit for a man, Juv.

units.la: Viriliter, vid. Fortiter.
units.tr: Manfully: see Bravely.

units.la: Viritim aliquid agere] Singulatim quærere ex aliquibus. Singillatim dicere. Singuli audiunt, Cic. Singulare prælium conserere, Ausón. Duelli rem agere, Cic.
units.tr: To do something man by man] To inquire singly of some. To speak one by one. Each hears, Cic. To fight a single combat, Ausón. To conduct a duel, Cic.

units.la: Virtus] Probitas. Integritas vitæ, Cic. Animi dos speciosa.
units.tr: Virtue] Uprightness. Integrity of life, Cic. A splendid dowry of the mind.

units.la: Virulentus. Virus, vid. Venenatus. Venenum.
units.tr: Virulent. Venom: see Poisonous. Poison.

units.la: Vis, vid. Robur. Violentia.
units.tr: Force: see Strength. Violence.

units.la: Vim vi repellere] Clavum clavo pellere.
units.tr: To repel force with force] To drive a nail with a nail.

units.la: Vis cavenda] Bovem volentem ducito.
units.tr: Force to be avoided] Lead the ox that is willing.

units.la: Per vim] Obtorto collo, aut gula arripere. Vid. Violenter.
units.tr: By force] To seize by the twisted neck, or by the throat. See Violently.

units.la: Viscatus] Viscata & hamata beneficia, Sen. Plin.Iun. Viscosus. Viscidus, Sipont. Piceatus, Mart. Lentus: Lentum & visco simile, Plaut. Sequax bitumen, Plin. Tenax bitumen, Ovid. Tenax cera, Virg.
units.tr: Sticky] Sticky and hooked favours, Sen. Plin. Iun. Viscous. Sticky, Sipont. Pitched, Mart. Clinging: clinging and like birdlime, Plaut. Sticky bitumen, Plin. Tenacious bitumen, Ovid. Tenacious wax, Virg.

units.la: Viscera] Exta, Cic. Fibrae, Virg. Praecordia, Plin. Vitalia, Lucan.
units.tr: Entrails] Innards, Cic. Fibres, Virg. Midriff, Plin. Vital organs, Lucan.

units.la: Viscum] Viscus merus est vestra blanditia, Plaut.
units.tr: Birdlime] Your flattery is pure birdlime, Plaut.

units.la: Visibilis] Aspectabilis. Cadit sub sensum: sub aspectum & oculos. Cadit in conspectum: in sensum videndi. Res subjecta sensibus. Quae sub aspectum veniunt, Cic. Quae subjiciuntur oculis, Liv. Spectabile corpus, Ovid.
units.tr: Visible] Capable of being seen. Falls under the senses: under sight and the eyes. Falls within view: into the sense of seeing. A thing subject to the senses. Things that come under sight, Cic. Things placed beneath the eyes, Liv. A visible body, Ovid.

units.la: Visitare] Visere aliquem; Revisere, intervisere aliquem. Visendi causa venire, Cic. Visere ad aliquem, Lucr. It visere ad eam. Ego hinc ad vos provisam, Ter. Salutatum aliquem vadere, Quint. Salutatum venire. Convisere aliqua loca, Cic. Portare matutinum Ave, Mart. Anquirere in aliquem quomodo vivat, Cic.
units.tr: To visit] To go to see someone; to revisit or look in on someone. To come for the purpose of seeing, Cic. To go to see someone, Lucr. He goes to visit her. I will come to you from here, Ter. To go to greet someone, Quint. To come to pay respects. To visit certain places, Cic. To bring a morning greeting, Mart. To inquire of someone how he lives, Cic.

units.la: Visitatio] Lustratio municipiorum, Cic.
units.tr: Visitation] An inspection of the towns, Cic.

units.la: Visitator, vid. Inspector.
units.tr: Visitor: see Inspector.

units.la: Visus] Sensus oculorum: sensus cernendi, videndi. Adspectus, Cic. In offensum lumen oculorum, Pallad.
units.tr: Sight] The sense of the eyes: the sense of seeing. Look, Cic. Light striking the eyes, Pallad.

units.la: Vita] Aetas. Spatium aetatis. Breve tempus aetatis. Spatium vitae. Cursus, (f. vitae) Cic. Aevum, Enn. Degere aevum, Cic. Mortalitas, Suet. Fore aliquem finem hujus lucis. Capitis res est, Plaut. Actus vitae, Sen. Curriculum vitae exiguum. Cursus vivendi. Usura vitae: usura lucis. Propagatio temporis, Cic. Traductio temporis est quasi explicatio rudentis, Id.
units.tr: Life] Age. A span of age. A short time of life. A span of life. Course (f. of life), Cic. Age, Enn. To pass one's age, Cic. Mortality, Suet. To bring someone to the end of this light. It is a matter of life and head, Plaut. The course of life, Sen. A brief running course of life. The course of living. The usury of life: the usury of light. The lengthening of time, Cic. The passing of time is like the unwinding of a rope, Id.

units.la: Vita brevis] Brevis vitae isthmus.
units.tr: Brief life] A narrow isthmus of life.

units.la: Vita hominis] Lucerna in vento posita. Peregrinatio perpetua.
units.tr: Human life] A lamp set out in the wind. A perpetual pilgrimage.

units.la: Vita nostra est comoedia] Vita scena est, in qua personam agit quisque suam.
units.tr: Our life is a comedy] Life is a stage, on which each person plays his own part.

units.la: Vita haec omnibus chara] Vivendi cupiditate incensi sumus omnes. Post hanc vitam exspectat nos alia] Superata tellus, sidera donabit.
units.tr: This life is dear to all] We are all fired with the desire to live. After this life another awaits us] Once the earth is overcome, it will give us the stars.

units.la: Vita functus] Superiori memoriā cives, Cic. Sorani sancta memoria. Astris post obitum mistus, Amm. Beatus: Quem cum Beatum, & Fuisse respondisset Præfectus, intellexit mortuum, Perf. Beatulus, Id. Vocat beatos clamitetque felices, Mart. O terque quaterque beatos, queis &c. contigit oppetere, Virg. Felices quibus est fortuna peracta jam sua, Id. Morte functi, Ovid.
units.tr: One who has departed this life] Citizens remember him with honour, Cic. The holy memory of Soranus. Mingled with the stars after death, Amm. Blessed: when the prefect answered that he was, and had been, blessed, he understood that the man was dead, Pers. Little blessed, Id. He calls them blessed and cries out that they are happy, Mart. O thrice and four times blessed are those to whom it has been granted to die, Virg. Happy are those whose course is now fully run, Id. Having finished life, Ovid.

units.la: Vitam pro aliquo ponere] Sanguinem pro aliquo profundere, Cic. Profundere vitam pro patria. Reddere vitam pro Rep. Id.
units.tr: To lay down one's life for someone] To pour out one's blood for someone, Cic. To pour out one's life for one's country. To give back one's life for the republic, Id.

units.la: Vitalitas] Vitalitas in corde durat. Vigor animi, Plin. In ore vigor, Ovid. Vivacitas. Col.
units.tr: Vitality] Vitality lasts in the heart. Vigour of spirit, Plin. Vigour in the face, Ovid. Liveliness, Col.

units.la: Vitare aliquid] Subtrahere se labore, Col. Devitare aliquid, vel aliquem. Declinare contentiones: à malis. Fugere laborem, Cic. Fugitare aliquid, Plaut. Refugere tela, periculum. Subterfugere militiam. Cavere à veneno: cavere malum, Cic. Cavere sibi ab aliquo, Ter. Cavere scabiem pecori, Cato. Vid. Evitare.
units.tr: To avoid something] To withdraw oneself from toil, Col. To shun something or someone. To decline quarrels, from evils. To flee labour, Cic. To dodge something, Plaut. To escape weapons or danger. To slip away from military service. To beware of poison: to guard against evil, Cic. To beware of someone, Ter. To keep the scab from the flock, Cato. See Evitare.

units.la: Vitatio] Fuga honoris, laboris. Declinatio malorum, Cicer. Vitiare, vid. Corrumpere. Stuprare. Vitiatio, vid. Violatio. Vitiator, vid. Stuprator. Vitiatus, vid. Corruptus. Vitilitigator, vid. Rixator. Vitiose, vid. Male.
units.tr: Avoidance] Flight from honour or labour. Escape from evils, Cic. To spoil, see Corrumpere, Stuprare. Spoiling, see Violatio. Spoiler, see Stuprator. Spoiled, see Corruptus. Quarrelsome litigant, see Rixator. Faultily, see Male.

units.la: Vitiosus] Mendosa facies: mendosi mores, Ovid. Insignitus, Plaut. Insignis, Ter. Criminosus, Cic. Vid. Corruptus.
units.tr: Faulty] A blemished face; blemished manners, Ovid. Marked, Plaut. Notable, Ter. Guilty, Cic. See Corruptus.

units.la: Vitiū] Synonyma non habet: Differentias vide in Janua & Atr. LL.
units.tr: Fault] It has no synonyms. See the differences in the Janua and the Atrium of the Latin language.

units.la: Vitium] Vitium in tecto: habet hæc res vitium, Cic. Vitiositas in corpore, Macrob. Quid morbi vitiique in mancipio sit, Vlp. In toto nusquam corpore monda fuit, Ovid. Labes corporis, Lucr. Macula seculi, Cic.
units.tr: Defect] A defect in a building: this thing has a defect, Cic. Faultiness in the body, Macrob. What disease or defect there is in a slave, Ulpian. Nowhere on his whole body was he clean, Ovid. A blemish on the body, Lucr. A stain on the age, Cic.

units.la: Vitrarius] Muret. Vitriarius, Sen. Specularius, Vlp. Qui
units.tr: Glassmaker] Muret. Glass-worker, Sen. Mirror-maker, Ulpian. One who

units.la: flatu vitrum in varios habitus format, Sen. Phallovitroboli, seu Phalloveretroboli, Capit.
units.tr: shapes glass into various forms by blowing, Sen. Phallovitroboli, or Phalloveretroboli, Capit.

units.la: Vitrum] Vitrea, pl. Plin. Vitreamina, Paul. IC. Hyalus, Virg. Vasa vitrea, Col. Vitreus calix, Mart.
units.tr: Glass] Glass things, pl., Plin. Glassware, Paul. IC. Glass, Virg. Glass vessels, Col. A glass cup, Mart.

units.la: Vitta] Vitta crinalis, Ovid. Reticulum, Var. Capillare, Mart. Involucrum, Var.
units.tr: Hair-band] A hair-ribbon, Ovid. A net, Varro. A hair-net, Mart. A wrapping, Varro.

units.la: Vittatus] Vittata navis, Plin. Lemniscata palma, Cic.
units.tr: Ribboned] A ship decked with ribbons, Plin. A palm-branch bound with ribbons, Cic.

units.la: Vituperabilis, vid. Damnabilis.
units.tr: Blameworthy, see Damnabilis.

units.la: Vituperare] Reprehendere, reprobare, improbare, culpare aliquid. Ponere in culpa, in vitio, in crimine aliquid. Communi vituperatione reprehendere aliquid. Adducere in vituperationem. Vocare in crimen aliquid, Cic. Dare vitio aliquid alicui, Cic. Donat. Culpitare jusjurandum alicujus, Plaut. Ducere in crimen, Tac. Vertere in crimen, Liv. Accusare voluptatem, dolorem laudare, Cic. Damnare libros suos, Quint. Laudato ingentia rura, Virg. i.e. improbato, Turneb.
units.tr: To blame] To find fault with, condemn, disapprove of, censure something. To place something under blame, under a fault, under a charge. To rebuke something with common censure. To bring into disrepute. To call something a crime, Cic. To impute a fault to someone, Cic. Donatus. To find fault with someone's oath, Plaut. To bring into disrepute, Tac. To turn into a charge, Liv. To accuse pleasure, to praise pain, Cic. To condemn one's own books, Quint. Praise the vast countryside, Virg., that is, disapprove, Turnebus.

units.la: Vituperatio] Reprehensio culpae. Improbatio testium, Cic. Notatio censoria, vel censorum. Maculam effugere, Id. Culpatio, Gell. Suggilatio, Plin.
units.tr: Blame] Rebuke of a fault. Disparagement of witnesses, Cic. A censorial mark, or of the censors. To escape the stain, Id. Censure, Gell. Disparagement, Plin.

units.la: Vituperator] Reprehensor Academiae, Cic. Vid. Carptor.
units.tr: Critic] A critic of the Academy, Cic. See Carptor.

units.la: Vivarium] Theriotrophium, Var. Leporarium, Id. Roborarium, Gell. Herbarium elephantum, P. Victor.
units.tr: Animal park] A place for keeping wild beasts, Varro. A hare-warren, Id. A place for keeping stock, Gell. A herb-garden for elephants, P. Victor.

units.la: Vivax] Vivacissima celeritas, Gell. Vivacissimus ingenio, Vopisc. Vividus, Tac. Vivens favilla, Ovid. Vivata potestas cernendi, Lucr. Fest. Vivum exemplum, Cic. Vegetus. Actuosa virtus. Spirans, Id. Animosa signa, Propert.
units.tr: Lively] Most lively speed, Gell. Most lively in talent, Vopisc. Vivid, Tac. A living spark, Ovid. The living power of seeing, Lucr. Fest. A living example, Cic. Vigorous. Active virtue. Breathing, Id. Spirited standards, Propert.

units.la: Vivè] Vividè, Caes. Vivi capti. Vivus combustus est, Cic.
units.tr: Vividly] Vividly, Caes. Living captives. He was burned alive, Cic.

units.la: Vivere] Vitem dicimus vivere. Arbor viget, Cic. Vivescere, Plin. Ducere vitam, spiritum: ducere ad tempus spiritum. Spiritu coelesti augeri, vivere ac spirare. Dum spirare potero: dum anima spirabo mea: ducere animam de coelo: Animari, viget Deus. Frui vita & communi spiritu. Agere, ducere, traducere, propagare, degere, vivere vitam, Cic. Vivere vita, Pl, Agere. Degere, abs. Agere, degere aetatem. Propagare tempora. Esse, commorari, manere in vita, Cic. Manet mihi vita, Virg. Agitare, transfigere vitam, Sallust, Prorogare vitam, Col. Aetatem, Plin. Vitam sapienter instituere. Exigere vitam, Ter. Exigere annos, ævum, Virg. Numerari inter vivos. Vivere è natura. Colere vitam cum virtute, Cic. Colere ævum, Lucr. Esse in rebus humanis, Paul.IC. Superare: Puer Ascanius, superatne? Virg.
units.tr: To live] We say that a vine lives. A tree flourishes, Cic. To grow to life. To draw breath, to draw in the breath of life: to draw breath for a time. To be increased by the heavenly Spirit, to live and breathe. As long as I can breathe; as long as I breathe with my own soul; to draw the breath of life from heaven; to be quickened: God flourishes. To enjoy life and the common Spirit. To pass, lead, spend, prolong, pass one's life, Cic. To live a life, Pl. To spend, to pass the time. To spend one's years, to pass one's age, Virg. To lengthen one's days. To be, to dwell, to remain in life, Cic. Life remains to me, Virg. To pass or spend one's life, Sallust. To prolong life, Col. One's age, Plin. To order one's life wisely. To pass one's life, Ter. To pass years and age, Virg. To be counted among the living. To live according to nature. To cultivate life with virtue, Cic. To cultivate one's age, Lucr. To be among human affairs, Paul. IC. To survive: Is the boy Ascanius still alive? Virg.

units.la: Vivere, respectu annorum] Vivere annum: ad annum centesimum. Producere vitam ad annum centesimum, Cic. Prolatare vitam, Tac. Vivere centum annis, vel annos, Plin. Vivere mille annorum, Plaut. Vitam ad plura secula deducere, Gorop. Vid. Provivere.
units.tr: To live, with respect to years] To live a year: to the hundredth year. To prolong life to the hundredth year, Cic. To extend life, Tac. To live a hundred years, or years, Plin. To live a thousand years, Plaut. To lead life into many ages, Gorop. See Provivere.

units.la: Vivere in diem] Cic. Vivere nullo consilio, Propert. Praeter propter vivere, Cato. Vivere temere inconsulteque, Sen. De talibus mortuis: Non vixit sed fuit, Id.
units.tr: To live from day to day] Cic. To live without any plan, Propert. To live roughly, Cato. To live rashly and without counsel, Sen. Of such dead men: he did not live, but merely existed, Id.

units.la: Vivendo vincere aliquem] Plaut. Suppetit superstes uxor vitae mariti, Id. Superstes sum alicui, Ter. Utinam te non solum vitae, sed etiam dignitatis meae superstitem reliquissem, Cic. Superstitare, Plaut. Ut mihi superstitet.
units.tr: To outlive someone] Plaut. The surviving wife remains to the life of her husband, Id. I survive someone, Ter. Would that I had left you surviving not only my life but also my dignity, Cic. To survive, Plaut. So that he may survive me.

units.la: Vivificare] Animare plantam liquore quotidiano. Animantur ova, Col. Animam alicui reddere, Ter.
units.tr: To quicken] To give life to a plant with daily moisture. Eggs are quickened, Col. To restore breath to someone, Ter.

units.la: Viviradix, vid. Talea.
units.tr: Living root, see Talea.

units.la: Vivus] Vivens pectus, Ovid. Vitalis, Plin. Incolumis, Spirabilis animus, animatus, Cic. Vitaliter animatus, Lucr. Vivus & spirans. Animans, Cic. Vivax in poenam, Plin. Superstes, Virg.
units.tr: Living] A living breast, Ovid. Vital, Plin. Unhurt, Cic. A breathing, animated spirit, Cic. Vitally animated, Lucr. Living and breathing. Animate, Cic. Living for punishment, Plin. Surviving, Virg.

units.la: Vix] Ægre me tenui, Cic. Vix ægre inveniemus, Plaut. Male me continui, Ovid.
units.tr: Scarcely] I scarcely held myself back, Cic. We shall hardly find it with difficulty, Plaut. I restrained myself badly, Ovid.

units.la: Vocabulum, vid. Verbum.
units.tr: Word, see Verbum.

units.la: Vocalis, vid. Sonorus.
units.tr: Vocal, see Sonorus.

units.la: Vocalitas] Claritas vocis, Cic. Claritudo vocis, Gell.
units.tr: Vocal quality] Clarity of voice, Cic. Clearness of voice, Gell.

units.la: Vocare aliquem ad se] Advocare sibi aliquem: ad signandum, Cic. Advocare ad, Ter. Accersere, Plaut. Arcessere ab: ad. Accire in regnum, Cic. Accitare, Lucr. Acciere, Diomed. Ciere nomina singulorum, Tac. Citare mancipia per nomina, Col. Inclamare aliquem, Quint. Alicui: nomine aliquem, Liv. Inclamitare aliquem, Clamore flagitare, poscere, Plaut. Clamare aliquem, Mart. Provocare: provocatur paedagogus, Plaut. Devocare de provincia ad triumphum, Cic. Advocitare, Fest. Quis me jubilat? vicinus tuus antiquus, Var.Scal.
units.tr: To call someone to oneself] To summon someone to oneself: to sign, Cic. To summon to, Ter. To fetch, Plaut. To fetch from or to. To summon into a kingdom, Cic. To call repeatedly, Lucr. To summon, Diomed. To call the names of individuals, Tac. To summon slaves by name, Col. To call someone aloud, Quint. To call someone by name, Liv. To call out to someone, to demand, to clamour for, Plaut. To shout for someone, Mart. To summon: the attendant is summoned, Plaut. To summon from a province to a triumph, Cic. To summon repeatedly, Fest. Who is calling me? Your old neighbour, Var. Scal.

units.la: Vocatio] Invitatio hospitum : invitatio ad aliquid. Vocatus, us, Cic.
units.tr: Summons] An invitation of guests; an invitation to something. A calling, Cic.

units.la: Vociferare. vid. Clamare.
units.tr: To shout, see Clamare.

units.la: Vocitare, vid. Nominare.
units.tr: To call, see Nominare.

units.la: Volare] Volitare, Cic. Meant aves, Plin. Circumvolare campum, Cic. Circumvolitat hirundo, Virg. Pervolare, Iuv. Pervolitare loca omnia, Virg. Involitant comae humeris, Hor. Ferri volatu, Catul. Labi pennis, Virg.
units.tr: To fly] To flit about, Cic. Birds fly, Plin. To fly round the field, Cic. The swallow flits about, Virg. To fly through, Juv. To fly through all places, Virg. Hair flutters on the shoulders, Hor. To be carried on the wing, Catul. To glide on wings, Virg.

units.la: Volaticus] Volatilis bestia, Cic. Volucris, Plin. Volatile pecus.
units.tr: Winged] A flying beast, Cic. A winged creature, Plin. A flying flock.

units.la: Volatus] Volatura, Var. Meatus avium, Plin. Cursus per aërem, Virg.
units.tr: Flight] A flying, Varro. The motion of birds, Plin. Course through the air, Virg.

units.la: Volens, volenter, vid. Lubens, lubenter.
units.tr: Willing, willingly, see Lubens, lubenter.

units.la: Volites, vid. Velites.
units.tr: Skirmishers, see Velites.

units.la: Volo] Voluntarii milites, Liv. Evocati milites, Caes. Auxilia voluntaria Regum, Cic.
units.tr: To wish] Volunteer soldiers, Liv. Veterans called back to service, Caes. Voluntary auxiliaries of kings, Cic.

units.la: Volubilis] Incitatum in orbem coelum, Cic. Subrotatus aries, Vitr.
units.tr: Revolving] The heavens turned in a circle, Cic. A ram rotated, Vitr.

units.la: Volucris, vid. Avis.
units.tr: Bird, see Avis.

units.la: Volvere aliquid] Volutare, Plin. Supervolvere, Col.
units.tr: To roll something] To roll about, Plin. To roll over, Col.

units.la: Voluntarie, voluntarius, vid. Sponte, spontaneus.
units.tr: Voluntarily, voluntary, see Sponte, spontaneus.

units.la: Voluntas, ut est actus] Arbitrium, Arbitratus, Nutus; Libido, Animus, Cic.
units.tr: Will, as an act] Judgement, decision, nod; desire, mind, inclination, Cic.

units.la: Volvox] Volucra, Col. Uruca, Convolvulus, Plin. Involvulus, & Involvolus, Plaut. Ips, Sipont. Ices, ab Ix. Rhodig. Byturus, vel Biurus, Cic. Campe, Col. Multipeda, centipeda, milepeda, Plin.
units.tr: Volvox] Volucra, Col. Uruca, Convolvulus, Plin. Involvulus and Involvolus, Plaut. Ips, Sipont. Ices, from Ix. Rhodig. Byturus or Biurus, Cic. Campe, Col. Multipeda, centipeda, milepeda, Plin.

units.la: Volupe est] Titillari, voluptate capi. Duci & delectari aliqua re: in aliqua re. Facile haec audio: Facile: facillime hic sum. Gratum est mihi, Cic. Teneri studio alicujus rei: ludis, spectaculis. Oblectari aliqua re, Id. Oblectat me aliquid, Plaut. Multum est in aliqua re aliquis, Caes. Capi locis, Virg. Duci aliqua re, Lucr. Aliquid insit, quod capiat ignaros, Cic.
units.tr: To be pleased] To be tickled, to be captured by pleasure. To be led and delighted by something: in something. I hear these things easily; I am most easily here. It is pleasing to me, Cic. To be fond of a pursuit: of games, of shows. To be delighted by something, Id. Something delights me, Plaut. Someone is much taken up with something, Caes. To be captivated by places, Virg. To be led by something, Lucr. Let there be something in it that catches the ignorant, Cic.

units.la: Voluptarius, Subst.] Voluptatum artifex. Delicatus adolescens, Cic. Malthinus demissis tunicis ambulat, Horat. Quibus in solo vivendi causa palato est, Iuv. Omnia ad voluptatem refert. Voluptatibus corporis omnia metitur. Est in voluptate semper. Fastidii delicatissimi homo, Cic. Provocat Mæcenatem deliciis, Apitium cænis, Sen. Deliciæ hominis, & deliciæ, pro delicato, Iuv. Otio ac mollitiis penè ultra fœminam fluens, Paterc.
units.tr: Pleasure-seeker, noun] A master of pleasures. A delicate young man, Cic. He walks about with drooping tunics, Hor. Those for whom the reason for living lies solely in the palate, Juv. He refers everything to pleasure. He measures everything by bodily pleasures. He is always in pleasure. A man of the most delicate fastidiousness, Cic. He challenges Maecenas with delicacies and Apicius with dinners, Sen. The darling of a man, and a darling, of a delicate man, Juv. Flowing with leisure and softness almost beyond a woman, Paterc.

units.la: Voluptas] Voluptas corporis pestis capitalis, Cic. Delectatio. Jucunditas: dare se jucunditati. Deliciæ. Deliciolæ, Id. Mala mentis gaudia, Virg. Gaudium extorsi. Lassus gaudio, Petron.
units.tr: Pleasure] Pleasure is the chief ruin of the body, Cic. Delight. Enjoyment, gratification: to give oneself up to enjoyment. Delights. Little delights, Id. The evil joys of the mind, Virg. Joy wrung out. Weary with joy, Petron.

units.la: Voluptatem habere] Voluptuari, Apul. Voluptari, Lipsi. Compleri, perfundi, frui, gestire voluptate. Voluptatem capere animo, percipere, habere. Magnam delectationem habere. Delectari cogitatione: in aliqua re. Est mihi cara res voluptati. Recreari literis, Cic. Pro delectamento habere agere aliquid, Gell. Permulceri lætissima voluptate, Col.
units.tr: To have pleasure] To take sensual delight, Apul. To delight oneself, Lipsius. To be filled, steeped, enjoy, and rejoice in pleasure. To take pleasure in the mind, to perceive it, to have it. To have great delight. To take delight in a thought, or in some matter. This thing is dear to me as a pleasure. To be refreshed by literature, Cic. To hold something as a delight to do, Gell. To be soothed with the most joyful pleasure, Col.

units.la: Voluptuosus, vid. Delectabilis.
units.tr: Voluptuous, see Delightful.

units.la: Vomica] Vomica erumpens, Cels. Abscessus, Apostema. Manans; adapertum hulcus, Id. Erumpens hulcus, Plin. Vomicus morbus, Sen.
units.tr: Boil] A boil breaking out, Cels. An abscess, an apostume. Oozing; an opened sore, Id. A breaking ulcer, Plin. A festering disease, Sen.

units.la: Vomere] Vomitare, Col. Nauseare, vel nauseam facere, Cic. Quod ingurgitaverat, refudit, Plin. Devomere, Gell. Non rediturus qua intraverat cibus, Sen. Vomitu revertitur, quicquid bibit, Id. Rejectavit noctē caseum, Spart. Superiorem alvum dejicere, Cato. Revomere, Virg. Convomere aliquem, Iuv. Vomitu aspergere.
units.tr: To vomit] To keep vomiting, Col. To cause nausea, or to make one nauseated, Cic. What he had gulped down he brought back up, Plin. To vomit out completely, Gell. Food that will not come back out by the way it went in, Sen. Whatever he drinks comes back in vomit, Id. He vomited up his cheese in the night, Spart. To purge the upper bowel, Cato. To vomit up again, Virg. To vomit upon someone, Juv. To spatter with vomit.

units.la: Vomitio, actio] Vomitus: facere, sistere, inhibere vomitum. Rejectus cibi, Cels. Rejectio, Plin. Orexis, Id. Nausea, Cic. Vomitus & purgatio alvi, turpia redundantiæ remedia, Plut.
units.tr: Vomiting, the act of] Vomit: to induce, stop, or check vomiting. Rejection of food, Cels. Rejection, Plin. Orexis, Id. Nausea, Cic. Vomiting and purging of the bowels, the shameful remedies for excess, Plut.

units.la: Voracitas, vid. Edacitas.
units.tr: Voracity, see Greediness.

units.la: Voraginosus] Verticosus, Vorticosus, Liv.
units.tr: Full of whirlpools] Full of eddies, whirling, Liv.

units.la: Vorago] Vertex: contorta in se aqua, Quint. Vortex, Virg. Torta vertigo, Propert. Turbo in aquis, Stat. Gurges exæstuat voragine, Virg. Barathrum, Id. Voratrix terræ, Amm.
units.tr: Whirlpool] A vortex: water twisted in on itself, Quint. A vortex, Virg. A twisted whirl, Propert. A whirling in the waters, Stat. The gulf seethes in a whirlpool, Virg. The abyss, Id. A devourer of the earth, Amm.

units.la: Vorare] Ligurire, vel ligurrire, Hor. Lurcare lardum. Pompon. Lurcare cum aliquo, Var. Lurcari, Lucil. Tubur-cinari, Plaut. Ingerere. Ingenti aviditate distentum ventrem oncrare. onerare, Sen. Hiatu oris cibum capere, Cic. Obstrudere, obsaturare, Fest.
units.tr: To devour] To lick up, or to lick, Hor. To gobble up bacon, Pompon. To feast greedily with someone, Var. To gobble, Lucil. To guzzle, Plaut. To stuff in. To load the belly, distended with immense greed, Sen. To take food with a gaping mouth, Cic. To stuff full, to glut, Fest.

units.la: Vorax] Edax hospes,Cic. Edax vultur, ignis,Ovid. Pamphagus, Id. Vid. Edax.
units.tr: Voracious] A greedy guest, Cic. A ravenous vulture, or fire, Ovid. Eating everything, Id. See Greedy.

units.la: Votum] Sponsio,Cic. Sponsio voti qua Deo obligamur.
units.tr: Vow] A pledge, Cic. A pledge of a vow by which we are bound to God.

units.la: Votum solvere] Virg. Votum dissolvere, reddere, Cic. Persolvere, Propert.
units.tr: To fulfil a vow] Virg. To dissolve a vow, to render it, Cic. To pay it in full, Propert.

units.la: Vovere aliquid alicui] Voverunt se Dianæ vitulum immolaturos. Vota facere Deo. Vota suscipere, nuncupare. Sponsio voti, qua Deo obligamur, Cic. Suscipere Deo vota pro aliquo, Plin.iun. Vovere votum, Liv. Concipere vota, Ovid. Obstringere se religione voti. Devovere aliquid alicui, Cic.
units.tr: To vow something to someone] They vowed to sacrifice a calf to Diana. To make vows to God. To take up vows, to declare them. A pledge of a vow by which we are bound to God, Cic. To undertake vows to God on someone's behalf, Plin. Iun. To make a vow, Liv. To conceive vows, Ovid. To bind oneself by the obligation of a vow. To devote something to someone, Cic.

units.la: Vox] Vox clara, suavis, sonora, canora & suavis, Cic. Clarisona, Catul. Limpida, Plin. Liquida, Lucr. Liquata, Macr. Articulata, Apul.
units.tr: Voice] A clear, sweet, sonorous voice; a melodious and sweet voice, Cic. Clear-sounding, Catul. Limpid, Plin. Liquid, Lucr. Melted, Macr. Articulate, Apul.

units.la: Vox sola] Assa vox: assa voce canere, Scal. Vox mera, Var.
units.tr: Bare voice] A voice alone: to sing with the bare voice, Scal. A mere voice, Var.

units.la: Vox plena] Cic. Vox toto organo instructa, Quint.
units.tr: Full voice] Cic. A voice furnished with the whole instrument, Quint.

units.la: Vulgare, vid. Divulgare.
units.tr: To make common, see To divulge.

units.la: Vulgaris] Plebejus, popularis, pervagatus, vernaculus, gregarius, compitalitius, Cic. Compitalis, Suet. Gregalis, Sen. Ad multos pertinet, Cic. Vulgata verba, Plaut. Plebeji feminis pulli, Col. Vulgus servorum, (id est, vulgares servi) Ter. Vid. Vsitatus.
units.tr: Common] Plebeian, popular, widespread, vernacular, of the herd, of the crossroads, Cic. Of the crossroads, Suet. Of the herd, Sen. Pertaining to many, Cic. Common words, Plaut. Plebeian chicks, Col. The common crowd of slaves (that is, common slaves), Ter. See Usual.

units.la: Vulgariter] Simpliciter, incondite dicere. Vulgariter, populariter. Usitato more agere. Usitatis verbis uti. Nullo apparatu dicere. Sine fuco & pigmentis. Pingui Minerva agere, Cic. Crassa Minerva, Crassiore Musa, Quint. Pervulgate loqui, Gell. Inartificialiter, Quint. Non in ambitionem compositum cubile. Ad naturam vivere, Sen. Ut natura fert facere. Aperte rem ipsam modo locutus, nihil circuitione usus es, Ter. Sine ambage: ambage nulla antegressa, Amm.
units.tr: Commonly] To speak simply and without polish. Commonly, popularly. To act in the usual manner. To use ordinary words. To speak without ornament. Without rouge or paint. To work with plain Minerva, Cic. With thick Minerva, with a coarser Muse, Quint. To speak in common fashion, Gell. Unartfully, Quint. A bed not arranged for show. To live according to nature, Sen. To do as nature bears. You spoke the thing itself plainly and used no circumlocution, Ter. Without ambiguity: no ambiguity having gone before, Amm.

units.la: Vulgo] Vulgo & passim. Fere. Plerumque. Communiter, Cic. Plurimum, Plin. Ordinarie, Sipont. Isthæc fiunt, Plaut. Vulgus servorum facit. (pro servi vulgo faciunt.
units.tr: Commonly] Commonly and everywhere. Nearly. Mostly. Generally, Cic. For the most part, Plin. Ordinarily, Sipont. These things happen, Plaut. The mass of slaves does it (for slaves in general do it).

units.la: Vulgus] Vulgaritas, Arnob. Sordes & sex urbis populus, Cic. Popellus, Hor. Multitudo, Salust. Multi, Cic. Turba, Non. Ignota capita, Liv.
units.tr: The common people] Commonness, Arnob. The dregs and lowest part of the city's population, Cic. The rabble, Hor. The multitude, Sall. Many, Cic. A crowd, Non. Unknown heads, Liv.

units.la: Vulnerare] Sauciare ferro, Col. Facere, infligere, imponere plagam mortiferam. Vulnus alicui infligere, imponere, Cic. Impingere, Plaut. Facere alicui vulnera in tergo. Saucium facere, Ovid. Vultus gladio turpare, Lucan. Tangere jactu usque ad ossa, Propert. Adigere vulnus, Tac. Violare corpus vulnere, Virg. Convulnerare aliquem, Plin. Consauciare, Suet. Infligere alicui securim, Cic.
units.tr: To wound] To wound with iron, Col. To make, inflict, or deal a deadly blow. To inflict a wound on someone, Cic. To strike, Plaut. To make wounds on someone's back. To make wounded, Ovid. To disfigure the face with a sword, Lucan. To touch to the bone with a thrust, Propert. To drive in a wound, Tac. To violate the body with a wound, Virg. To wound several people, Plin. To wound severely, Suet. To inflict an axe on someone, Cic.

units.la: Vulnerari ] Accipere vulnus; plagam luculentam. Excipere plagas cicatrices. Injecta est ei plaga maxima, Cic. Vulneribus confici, Liv. Ingestis vulneribus concidit, Tacit. Vulnere per inguen accepto, Sen. Recipere corpore ferrum, telum, Cic. Jugulo accepit ensem, Virg.
units.tr: To be wounded] To receive a wound, a severe blow. To receive blows and bear scars. A very great blow was dealt him, Cic. To be worn down by wounds, Liv. Struck down by the wounds inflicted, Tac. With a wound received through the groin, Sen. To take the iron, the weapon, into the body, Cic. He took the sword in his throat, Virg.

units.la: Vulneratio] Sauciatio, Cic. Profectus, Apul.
units.tr: Wounding] Wounding, Cic. Advance, Apul.

units.la: Vulneratus ] Saucius, Cic. Sauciatus, Col. Lacer membris undique, Lucr. Lacer crudeliter, Virg. Collaceratum corpus, Tac. Exsinceratum tergum, Plaut. Æger ex vulnere, Liv. Plagosus, Apul.
units.tr: Wounded] Wounded, Cic. Wounded, Col. Torn limb from limb on every side, Lucr. Cruelly mangled, Virg. A body torn to pieces, Tac. A back flayed, Plaut. Sick from a wound, Liv. Beaten, Apul.

units.la: Vulnus] Plaga, Cic.
units.tr: Wound] A blow, Cic.

units.la: Vultur] Vulturio, & Vulturius, Plaut. Caucasea, volucris, Virg. Avis palatina, Propert. Avis magna, Plaut.
units.tr: Vulture] Vulturio and Vulturius, Plaut. The Caucasian bird, Virg. The palatine bird, Propert. A great bird, Plaut.

units.la: Vulturinus] Vulturius jactus, Plaut.
units.tr: Vulturine] A vulturine throw, Plaut.

units.la: Vultus] Sermo mentis, Cic. Habitus oris, Lucr. Os pudibundum, Ovid.
units.tr: Countenance] The speech of the mind, Cic. The bearing of the mouth, Lucr. A bashful face, Ovid.

units.la: Vultus serenus] Vultus renidens, Val. Flacc. Frons erugata, Plin. Frons exporrecta, Ter.
units.tr: Serene countenance] A beaming face, Val. Flacc. A smooth brow, Plin. An open brow, Ter.

units.la: Vultus tristis] Severus, Cic. Trux, Tac. Obductus vultus, Ovid. Caperata frons severitudine, Plaut. Frons adducta, Ovid. Obducta, Juv. Contracta, Hor. Frons matutina, adstricta, Mart. Vultuosa, Apul. Parum laeta frons, Virg.
units.tr: Sad countenance] Stern, Cic. Fierce, Tac. A clouded face, Ovid. A brow wrinkled with sternness, Plaut. A brow drawn down, Ovid. Clouded, Juv. Contracted, Hor. A morning brow, drawn tight, Mart. Grimacing, Apul. A face not very cheerful, Virg.

units.la: Vultu & verbis aliquid significare] Significationem dare alicujus rei. Quod animo sentiebat, & vultu promptum habuit & lingua. Clamant supercilia malitiam, Cic. Vultu ferebat, quos spiritus gestisset. Manifestus erat tacitæ cogitationis, Tac. Vultu aliquid promittere, Quint. Prodere crimen vultu, Ovid. Ostendo me ægre pati, Ter. Erumpo gaudium, Id. Profiteri ac præ se ferre aliquid, Cic. Profert mores oratio, & animi secreta detegit, Quint. Lætitiam vagis sermonibus simulare, Tac. Setæ promittunt atrocem animum, Iuv. Vid. Simulare.
units.tr: To signify something by face and words] To give a sign of something. What he felt in his mind he had ready in both face and tongue. Their eyebrows proclaim malice, Cic. He showed by his face what spirit he had within. He was clear about his silent thought, Tac. To promise something by the face, Quint. To betray a crime by the face, Ovid. I show that I suffer with difficulty, Ter. I break out in joy, Id. To profess and openly display something, Cic. Speech reveals character and uncovers the secrets of the mind, Quint. To feign joy with idle words, Tac. Bristles promise a savage spirit, Juv. See Feign.

units.la: X.
units.tr: X.

units.la: Xenium ] Xenia, ( mittebantur hospitibus) Vitr. Aphoreta, plur. Mart. Sortes, Suet. Mart. Vid. Honorarium.
units.tr: Xenium] Xenia (they were sent to guests), Vitr. Aphoreta, plur. Mart. Sortes, Suet. Mart. See Honorarium.

units.la: Xylinus. Xylon, vid. Gossampinus &c.]
units.tr: Xylinus. Xylon, see Gossampinus etc.

units.la: Xystus, vid. Palæstra.
units.tr: Xystus, see Palaestra.

units.la: Z.
units.tr: Z.

units.la: Zea] Spelta, Gorra. Semen, Plin.
units.tr: Zea] Spelt, Gorra. Seed, Plin.

units.la: Zelare] Nihil amplius vindicare, quam impietatem in Deum. Zelo divino moveri. Ardenter propugnare, tueri gloriam Dei, honorem, cultum supremi Numinis. Studiosissimum esse divini honoris. Sum acris vindex violatæ religionis, pietatis, &c.
units.tr: Zelare] To avenge nothing more than impiety against God. To be moved by divine zeal. To defend ardently, to guard the glory of God, the honour and worship of the supreme Deity. To be most eager for the honour of God. To be a fierce avenger of violated religion, piety, etc.

units.la: Zelosus, vulgo ] Zelotes, in SS. Ardens propugnator religionis, honoris divini. Ultor acerrimus violatæ religionis, pietatis.
units.tr: Zelosus, vulgo] Zealous; (Zelotes, in SS.) an ardent defender of religion and of the honour of God; a most fierce avenger of violated religion and piety.

units.la: Zelotypia ] Rivalitas, Plin. Suspicio amoris, Corrad. Vid. Invidia.
units.tr: Zelotypia] Rivalry, Plin. Suspicion of love, Corrad. See Invidia.

units.la: Zelotypus Se [illegible, ~6 letters] amare, Æmulus, Cic.
units.tr: Zelotypus] [text illegible, about six letters] to love; Aemulus, Cic.

units.la: Zelus] Ardens Dei colendi impetus.
units.tr: Zelus] An ardent impulse to worship God.

units.la: Zephyrus] Favonius, Sen.
units.tr: Zephyrus] Favonius, Sen.

units.la: Zoilus] Obtrectator studiorum alicujus, Cic. Homero-mastix.
units.tr: Zoilus] A carper at someone's studies, Cic. Homeromastix [Ὁμηρομάστιξ].

units.la: PAg. 1. Omissum est aliquid, quod supplendum ita: Abacus in triclinio] Mensa vinaria, Varr. Mensa Delphica, Rhod. ex Porphyrio. Repositorium, Plin. Abacus calculatorius] Abacium, Mensa Pythagoræ &c. Minora ipsi lectores eruditi emendabunt. Ut quod pag. 417. Lorica, indusium ferrum, pro, ferreum, dicitur, & similia.
units.tr: p. 1. Something has been omitted, which should be supplied thus: Abacus in triclinio] A wine table, Varr. A Delphic table, Rhod., from Porphyrio. A shelf, Plin. Abacus calculatorius] An abacus, the table of Pythagoras, etc. The learned readers will correct the smaller matters themselves, such as what is said on p. 417: "Lorica, indusium ferrum" for "ferreum" (a coat of mail, a shirt, "iron" for "of iron"), and similar errors.
